incident_description: This is what I have typed up to email to attorneys. Can you tell me if this is good or not?   On Tuesday evening, my 10-year-old nonverbal son with Down Syndrome and Autism nearly severed his fingers with a Ninja Blast portable blender. I had bought it a year ago to make smoothies for my mother after her stroke, but she passed away before I had a chance to even use it. My kitchen is under renovation, so my appliances are all out of their normal place. This blender hasn't been out of the cabinet in a year, so when my son saw it, I assume it caught his interest, being new to him. I was preparing his evening medication with him standing beside me, and within an instant, he had picked up the blender and simultaneously turned on the blades with his hand inside. It happened so fast I couldn't even register what was happening. To my knowledge, it hadn't even been charged in the past year as it has been stored away in the cabinet. It did not have the lid on, so I also did not understand how the motor could turn on. Seven extremely traumatic hours later, two ER sedations and stitches, I arrived back home at 3am and crawled into bed to try to make sense of what happened. In my research, I discovered that this particular model lacks a safety latch to prevent the blades from turning on when the lid is open. Every blender and Ninja I have ever owned did. I am absolutely devastated that this happened to my son. He has endured so much in his life...being born with Down Syndrome and a heart condition, being adopted from China at 3, heart repair resulting in pulmonary hypertension at 4, epilepsy, leukemia at 7, which he fought bravely and is now in remission. He already has so much medical trauma that it is almost impossible to even succeed at basic well-child care for him. This should have never happened.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (severed fingers requiring ER treatment), but such occurrences are unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
Product Involved: Whirlpool WFE540H0ES Electric Range Oven

Incident Date: 09/06/2025

Location: [REDACTED], Colorado 

On the evening of 09/06/2025, I was using my Whirlpool WFE540H0ES electric range oven to bake food when a dangerous incident occurred. While the oven was operating at a regular baking temperature, I suddenly saw a bright orange flame inside the oven, accompanied by loud crackling and popping noises similar to a welding arc. Within seconds, sparks began flying throughout the interior of the oven.



The food inside was untouched and not burned, which indicates that the source of the problem came from the oven itself, not the food or any spills. While this was happening, the bottom of the oven began to melt, and a hole approximately 2 inches by 1 inch burned completely through the metal base of the oven cavity.



I immediately attempted to turn off the oven using the control panel, but the entire display panel shut down on its own, and the oven powered off suddenly. Despite the shutdown, flames continued to burn briefly inside before eventually extinguishing on their own. The fire produced heavy, acrid, chemical-smelling smoke that quickly filled the house and triggered all of our smoke detectors.



Out of caution, we switched off the breaker manually, though the circuit breaker did not trip automatically despite the severity of the incident.



While there were no burns or direct physical injuries, the heavy smoke exposure caused health issues for multiple members of the household:

 Both my husband and I experienced significant respiratory irritation, resulting in frequent coughing and throat discomfort.

 The strong odor and harsh fumes caused headaches for my husband and 3 year old daughter the following morning.
justification: The incident caused respiratory irritation and headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). Such electrical malfunctions are rare but possible (likelihood 3).

As a result, the entire apartment was filled with heavy smoke and became uninhabitable.
Because of the damage, I had to temporarily leave the apartment. I hired professional cleaners to wash the walls, remove cabinets, and clean or remove smoke-damaged furniture, curtains, mattresses, carpet, and clothing. The entrance door, which was damaged by the fire department when they forced entry, had to be replaced by a contractor immediately. The balcony door was also forcibly opened by the fire department and still requires repair.
At present, I am arranging for contractors to repaint the walls and ceilings and to redo the wood floors so that the apartment is properly restored and safe for my child. In addition, I purchased a commercial air purifier, which the doorman has been operating daily to help air out the apartment. Until all repairs and repainting are completed, I cannot allow my young child to return to live there safely.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant property damage and making the apartment uninhabitable, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I just received a pressure cooker that I ordered and I believe its an unsafe product. One of the first things youre supposed to do is to run a test by filling the pot 2/3 full of water and running a cycle. The pot is never supposed to be filled more than 2/3 full of anything. I noticed that the measurement lines in the pot are in 5ths not 3rds, so there is no clear indication of where 2/3 full is. So then I thought I would just use the cup measurement lines on the other side of the indicator and do a calculation. Since its a 12 quart pot, which is 48 cups, 2/3 full would be just under 32 cups. When I poured 32 cups in, it came up to a mark that said 20 cups. So the measurement lines are way off. Since pressure cookers can be very dangerous if used improperly, Im returning it without using. But I am afraid that imprecise or inaccurate measurements could be dangerous for someone else. The manufacturer gave me very unsatisfactory excuses when I called.

The workers had some items on top of the range, which burned due to this issue.  The technicians were able to extinguish the fire without any injuries.  The technicians also agreed to replace the range-top and they did.
 
 
The consumer, her husband, and their renter, all bumped the range knobs at different times and accidentally turned it on.  Each time, they caught the issue before any property damage occurred.
 
 
5/26/2025: The consumer called the manufacturer and spoke to different representatives. Who happened to be the same person but used a different name each time. She asked for a refund.  The manufacturer offered her a 15% discount on the purchase of a new range.  The consumer said she should not have to purchase a new range at her expense.  She also said that people cannot be expected to lock their range after each use and that children could be in heightened damage because of this issue.
 
 
 
NOTE:  The range was purchased 11/1/2023, delivered to the home in 3/2024 and used a few months later.  When the phone representative informed her that the range was out of warranty, the consumer noted that the service person said it was still in warranty. 

Warranty shouldn't have anything to do with a defective/hazard stove. Note: the customer service person on the phone called me a racist. [REDACTED] was his name. On previous calls he used the name [REDACTED] also

Recall on LG slide and ranges with front mount knobs. Model number LSEL6331F
Unintentional contact with turn burners. (Using a microwave above, body will have contact with knobs and burners will turn on.)

Purchased during the Thanksgiving day sale 2023. Had it delivered in March 2024. Had it
installed either in July/August 2024. The contractors, while working by the stove,
unintentionally bumped the knobs and turned the stove on.
They did not realize it until smell of smoke was in the house. The damage was so bad that a
new top had to be replaced. The contractors paid for that.

Decided to do some research on the stove and found out that problem happened to a lot of other owners. There is also a recall on this model. 

I called LG customer relations at 800-243-0000. Talked to someone there and they told me
that [REDACTED] would call and make an appointment for service.
Appointment was made, but nobody showed up the first time. Wasted a whole day waiting for
them. Finally showed up on the second request. All he did was show us where the lock button
was on the stove. Told him I wasn't happy with just having a lock button. I cannot guarantee
that renters will be using the lock button after every time they use the stove. It is a fire hazard
and I do not want it in there. He told me to call the 800-243-000. So I called and it sounded
like I was talking to the same person I had talked to before. I asked him what his name was,
but I couldn't quite understand what he was saying. So I asked him to spell his name. I heard
computer clicking and he didn't answer me for about 10 seconds. I said, don't you know how
to spell your name? So then he spelled out his name, which was [REDACTED]. Went through

incident_description:
Product Information
		Product: LG Gas Range / Oven
		Brand/Manufacturer: LG Electronics USA, Inc.
		Retailer: Lowes
		Purchase Date: January 1, 2025
		Delivery/Installation Date: January 15, 2025
		Serial Number: 407KMYH15010

Incident Description
I purchased an LG gas range from Lowes on January 1, 2025. It was delivered and professionally installed on January 15, 2025. Since the first use, there has been a persistent strong gas odor whenever the oven is in use. This odor does not occur when using the cooktop burners.

I reported the issue to LG several times beginning in January 2025. Initially, I was told this was normal for a new appliance. In June 2025, LG advised me to run the self-cleaning cycle with windows open to burn off the smell. This did not resolve the problem.

In July 2025, LG acknowledged the problem and said they would assign a warranty service provider. Despite repeated escalations, no service has been provided. Their system has produced false service confirmations (e.g., listing my own email address as the providers contact, showing appointments that never occurred, and marking service completed when no technician ever visited). To date, no repair or inspection has been completed.

The oven continues to emit a strong gas odor every time it is used.

Safety Concern
		The smell is consistent with natural gas, raising concerns about leakage or incomplete combustion.
		LG has not inspected or repaired the unit despite acknowledging the warranty.
		I am concerned about the risk of fire, explosion, or carbon monoxide exposure.
		This is not an isolated problem with customer service  the appliance itself may be defective and unsafe.

Injury/Property Damage
		No injuries yet, but continued exposure to leaking gas poses a health and fire hazard.
		Household members have avoided using the oven due to the odor and safety concern.

Resolution Attempts
		Multiple calls and escalations to LG (phone, social media, Presidential Escalation team).
		LG has not provided service despite over 7 months of complaints.
		LG has instructed me not to hire my own repair provider, claiming it would void the warranty.

Requested Action
I am reporting this to CPSC because LG has failed to address a potentially dangerous defect in a consumer gas appliance. I request that CPSC investigate whether this issue indicates a broader product safety hazard affecting other LG gas ranges.
justification: The incident involves a persistent gas odor indicating a potential safety hazard, but no injury or property damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
What happened?
I purchased a Ninja Air Fryer Toaster Oven from Amazon on December 2, 2024. In July 2025just 8 months laterI discovered significant rust forming inside the cooking area, specifically underneath the heating element tray where food drippings and steam naturally accumulate. The product was used strictly as intended: air frying, toasting, and baking small meals. No harsh chemicals, soaking, or misuse occurred.

This rust poses a food safety hazard because its located where heat, moisture, and food contact happen. Rust particles can break loose during cooking and contaminate food. Ingesting rust can be harmful, especially for children, elderly, or those with compromised immune systems.

When I contacted Ninja, they refused to replace or repair the unit, even though its well within the standard 1-year warranty. Customer service gave conflicting and confusing information:

    At first said they could not help.

    The next day claimed it was registered but had no warranty.

    Suggested bizarre troubleshooting steps like reading numbers off the electrical prongs and doing a video call to prove the damage, despite already having clear photos.

    One representative implied the rust was my fault without any evidence.

The unit is still functional but unsafe, and the companys refusal to address a clear material failure leaves other consumers at risk.

Who was using the product?
I, an adult, used the product for normal household cooking.

How was it being used?
Used per instructionsair frying vegetables, meats, and baked goods. No submersion in water or harsh cleaning agents.

Were there any injuries?
No injuries yet, but the potential exists for ingesting rust particles if unnoticed in food.
justification: The incident involves a product defect posing a potential health hazard, but no injuries have occurred yet. The likelihood is high given the described conditions and usage.

incident_description:
We purchased a Keurig coffeemaker at Walmart in Murray, KY on July 4, 2025, and registered it online on the day of purchase.

Less than a month later the machine wouldn't brew and began to dump boiling hot water out the bottom and onto our counters while still plugged in, which is both a burn and a shock hazard making the product unsafe. Luckily we were able to unplug the machine before anyone was injured. Since the machine was unusable we decided to file for the one year warranty we had signed up for when registering the product. I called the company and was told by the agent that I could use a duplicate receipt from the Murray Walmart as proof of purchase, so I drove the 60 mile round trip to Walmart to generate the receipt. 

We submitted the documentation as required and were rejected via a form email - probably no live person even reviewed the claim. My guess is the company is implementing cost cutting measures by refusing to honor warranty even when they've sold a dangerous product. They should be focusing on getting these dangerous items off the market instead of telling consumers they're stuck with something that might shock or injure someone. There's a post on the Keurig [REDACTED] saying they had the same problem with their machine, so I wonder if this company sold a large number of these unsafe products.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffeemaker that posed burn and shock hazards, but no injuries occurred as it was unplugged in time.

However, each time I call, Samsung representatives on the phone insist that the oven is functioning normally because I used the self-clean cycle.

This is unacceptable. U.S. safety standards exist to protect consumers, and those standards apply during all modes of operation, including self-cleaning. The fact that Samsung continues to disregard these safety limits is deeply concerning.

I have video evidence, which I sent to Samsung support, showing the oven handle reaching unsafe temperatures. Despite this, Samsung continues to make excuses and denies that there is a problem. Most ovens on the market do not come close to exceeding 149F on their handles, even during self-clean cycles. I simply want a safe oven in my homeone that wont pose a burn risk to me or my children during normal cooking activities.

Companies should not be allowed to violate established U.S. safety regulations. I am requesting that Samsung take immediate responsibility by offering a replacement or refund. If this issue remains unresolved, I will be filing formal complaints with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), the retailer (Home Depot), and my states consumer protection office.

Shortly after installation, I discovered a serious safety issue: the front control knobs are very sensitive and can be unintentionally turned just by brushing against them. As a result, a burner was accidentally activated while I was near the range, without me realizing it. This caused a visible burn mark on one of my small appliances and could have led to a fire or injury.

Two Home Depot technicians visited my home on July 12, 2025, and directly observed the unintended burner activation. One technician even called a manager during the visit and told me verbally that a return would be authorized due to the safety concern. However, the return was later denied, and I was told by Home Depot that I needed to contact GE directly. I am reporting this because I believe it reflects a serious design flaw that could affect many other consumers, especially households with children.

Here is what happened:
The product is a GE electric range, model GRS600AVWW, with front-facing knobs, purchased new from Home Depot. My wife, the homeowner, was using the product under normal conditions in my kitchen. The incident occurred when she brushed past the stove without touching the knob intentionally and a burner turned on by itself.

There were no injuries in this case, but a small appliance (a steamer) was damaged from the unintentional activation. The product presents an ongoing risk of fire or serious injury, especially if unnoticed or if flammable items are nearby. I am especially concerned for families with small children who may be at even greater risk due to this design.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (burn mark on a small appliance) but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the observed sensitivity of the knobs and potential for repeated incidents.

incident_description:
I own a Frigidaire FFEF3016VS 5 electric range. On 07/16/2025, the outer glass panel of the oven door suddenly shattered without warning. The oven had not been used in over two days and was completely cool. I had just moved the oven slightly to unplug and replug it after a control panel issue. Please investigate this incident and consider whether this model needs to be recalled or further examined for consumer safety.

Manufacturer: Frigidaire / Electrolux

incident_description:
What happened that made you want to report?
In June 2025, my household purchased a Hisense side-by-side refrigerator model HRS290P5FSE from Lowes. Upon delivery and setup, the unit failed to cool properly in the refrigerator compartment. After more than 18 hours plugged in and empty, the internal temperature remained in the 50s Fahrenheit, despite the digital panel falsely displaying 34F. We verified this using multiple calibrated thermometers and confirmed food safety temperatures were never reached.

Lowes replaced the defective unit with another refrigerator of the same model and production batch (same batch number on the serial). Within the first 24 hours, the replacement refrigerator began leaking unprompted water into the ice chute and dispenser tray, even though the ice maker was off and the water had not been used. Soon after, a mechanical knocking noise began inside the unit, coming from the ice-making area. These symptoms strongly suggested a defect in the water inlet valve, sensor system, or internal cycling motor.

These are back-to-back product failures from the same manufacturer and model, with safety and reliability issues that could pose electrical risks, foodborne illness dangers, or mechanical damage due to faulty components cycling inappropriately.

What type of product(s) were being used?
Hisense HRS290P5FSE  20.9 cu. ft. side-by-side refrigerator with water and ice dispenser in the door.

Who was using the product(s)?
My father, a senior citizen with medical needs, and I were the primary users. The product was installed in a residential kitchen and was meant for normal home food storage and water/ice dispensing.

How were the product(s) being used?
The refrigerator was installed per manufacturer instructions, leveled, connected to a water supply line, and left empty to allow the internal temperature to stabilize. The first unit failed to cool adequately. The second unit was used in the same way  empty and monitored for cooling. The ice maker was never turned on, and the water dispenser had not been used, yet water pooled internally, and mechanical cycling noises began within 12 hours of installation.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
While there were no physical injuries, the defects posed serious risks of food spoilage, electrical hazard due to water intrusion, and possible malfunction of internal motors or fans due to repeated cycling or moisture exposure. Additionally, stress and anxiety were caused by managing appliance failures for an elderly household member on a special diet and strict medication schedule.

How did any injuries occur?
No direct physical injuries occurred, but unsafe food temperatures and internal water leakage created circumstances where injury, illness, or damage could have occurred if we had not vigilantly monitored temperatures and noticed the issues early. Water in the ice chute could also have presented a shock hazard if it had reached internal electrical components.
justification: The incident involved product failures posing risks of food spoilage and electrical hazards, but no actual injuries occurred.

I took it out of the oven with my oven gloves on, and it exploded in my hands sending shards of glass everywhere.  One shard went into my ankle and caused a lot of bleeding.  It was a huge mess.  I did not bump the glassware or drop it or set it on any surface; it just exploded on its own.

incident_description: I received a new oven/stove and was told that it is normal to smell when first using as they are coated with oil and it needs to burn off. The smell did not go away and I had the company come look at it. They said it could take up to a month and to keep using. The smell did not go away, air quality was poor, windows had to be opened, and I could not be in the house. The stove was extremely hot to touch and I burned my finger turning it off. They came back out and it turned out it was not built right at the manufacturer. According to my understanding of what I was told, the heat is not escaping, the vent is in the wrong place,  the inside is concave, the wires and insulation is over heating. I am being told I have to work with Whirlpool and not the company that sold it to me. I will need to replace with the same model, however I have not verified this with Whirlpool as they have not approved the return yet. They put it before the "board" to determine what to do.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and poor air quality, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the manufacturing defect and recurring issues.

incident_description:
Defective Hamilton Beach Compact 20 oz. / 0.6 Liter Gooseneck Electric Kettle.  This product trips the breaker, and appears water is getting into the electric components.  This was given to me as a gift and the initial one we got had that problem after several week of use.  That one was subsequently replaced with the same kettle and the second one also had the same problem after about 3 weeks of use.   This is definitely a fire hazard and could have caused a fire or electrocution if the outlet was not on a GFCI breaker. 
The product was used properly per user manual and only once every couple days. 

After having the problem with our kettle, I found numerous reviews on Amazon with exactly the same problem.  
There are also reviews right on the Hamilton Beach website that note the same problem

So far Hamilton Beach has not been helpful either acknowledging the problem or offering us a full refund.

incident_description:
I am reporting a safety and functionality failure of an LG French Door Refrigerator, Model LFDS22520S.ASTCNA0, Serial 008MRKU2J373, purchased in 2020. The unit experienced complete compressor failure on June 1, 2025.

LG acknowledged the issue is due to a known defect in their linear compressors, previously addressed in a class action lawsuit ([REDACTED]). Despite this, LG has failed to resolve the issue promptly. I have been without refrigeration for more than 8 days, resulting in food spoilage, unsanitary conditions (gnats, odor), and risk to household health.

LGs refusal to replace the unit or expedite repair despite acknowledging the defect constitutes a risk to consumer well-being and may affect a broader population of consumers. I am requesting that CPSC review LGs failure to provide timely corrective action for this known product defect.

incident_description: We have a new Signature brand SKSGR360S 36-inch Gas Pro Range with 6 Burners.  The front door of the oven has a handle that appears fixed to the front door, but as the door is opened, the handle begins to hinge out and away from the door surface, creating a gap.  I was standing off to the side of the oven, and grabbed the side of the door to close it and as I raised the door, two of my fingertips were crushed between the front door and the now-retracting handle base.

Upon further inspection, I discovered significant charring, melted insulation, and a second regulator switch burned beyond repair.

incident_description:
Description of what happened:

I am escalating this again for the second time.

This is a formal update to my prior CPSC report [REDACTED] regarding my defective Samsung Gas Range.

That unit had major defects and was exchanged by BrandsMart for a replacement unit on June 30, 2024 (under their exchange policy).

I have had several incidents of accidental turning on the range by the slightest touch. I contacted LG they confirmed that my range was not on the recall list but sent me the sticker that gives you instructions on where to place the sticker, and how to use the Control Lock or Lock Out feature on their range.  first of all the sticker is no good if you have  activated the control lock and while you are sleeping  or out of the house the power goes out even for a second, the control lock deactivates , there is no warning, the clock does not start flashing, no warning sounds, nothing. incident_description:
We purchased a Ninja Foodi XL Pro AirFryer Oven (model DT201) in September 2023. We have followed all usage and cleaning guidelines. Last week, the unit started making loud a loud rattling/grinding noise when in use. It also does not shut off when cooking is complete or when the power button is pressed. The only way to turn it off completely is to unplug  the unit. We have tried it several times and in several different settings, but the issue is the same. At this point, we have left it off and unplugged because were concerned it may start a fire. 
I read several reports online of other consumers having a similar issue so I contacted Ninja customer service on 6/5/25. We are outside of the one year warranty so they will not repair or replace the unit. The rep said that if we had continued use and there was damage from use (such as a fire, etc.) then replacement falls under different guidelines. The suggested repair was to buy a new base, which is an entirely new unit without the included trays.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance with potential fire risk but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
On Friday, May 31st, 2025, my Samsung refrigerator (still under warranty) suddenly stopped working. A few hours later, it started emitting smoke and caught fire inside the lower back area of the unit. We were home and immediately unplugged the fridge .

I contacted Samsung support the same day. On Tuesday, June 3rd, a technician came and inspected the unit. He confirmed the fridge had burned internally, and declared it non-repairable. Samsung has since told me to wait while engineers evaluate the case.

As of today, Ive been without a refrigerator for 7 days, and Samsung has not provided a replacement, refund, or resolution. The fact that a relatively new refrigerator (still under warranty) can overheat and ignite poses a serious fire hazard, especially in a home with children.

I am filing this report because this is a potential product safety issue, and I want to prevent others from facing similar risks.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
COSORI CP159-AF Air Fryer appliance caught fire while turned off and unattended. Causing flame and smoke damage to counter top, cabinet and ceiling/walls of kitchen in a single family residence,  occupied by two adults and a juvenile. Product had been last used 60-90 minutes prior to fire occurring. No reported injuries.

This was a replacement unit provided by the manufacturer as part of their 2023 voluntary recall campaign.

However, recently, a serious safety hazard occurred. The oven turned on by itself and began heating without any operation or input (this was around 1.5 years into use).. It started to smoke and burned items that were stored inside. Fortunately, we were home and were able to cut the power in time.
Had no one been home, it could have easily caused a fire. This incident has made us feel that this oven is no longer safe to use.
justification: The oven malfunctioned, causing smoke and burning stored items, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Subject: Safety Concern Report: KitchenAid Gas Cooktop Model KCGC506JSS00 (Serial Number: DD4203603)

Dear U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission,

I am writing to bring to your attention a serious safety concern regarding my KitchenAid gas cooktop, model KCGC506JSS00, serial number DD4203603. This issue not only affects my appliance but appears to be a recurring problem across similar KitchenAid models, based on feedback I have encountered.

The primary issue involves the burner controls, which can unintentionally turn on with even the slightest contact, such as brushing against them while walking by. 

In these instances, one of two outcomes occurs:
1.	Gas flows without ignition/combustion.
2.	Gas flows and ignites unintentionally.

These incidents happen without deliberate user input and create an environment susceptible to severe hazards, including fire, explosion, or exposure to gas leakage. This poses a substantial threat to users' safety and well-being.

I have contacted KitchenAid to address this issue but feel it is necessary to escalate this matter to your agency to ensure public safety. KitchenAids response was to remove the knobs. 

I urge you to investigate whether this appliance, and potentially other models with similar designs, meet current safety standards. If necessary, I request that corrective actions be taken to prevent unintentional activation of gas flow or ignition.

Thank you for your attention to this critical safety matter. Please let me know if further details or actions are required from my side.
Sincerely,
justification: The incident involves unintentional gas flow and ignition, posing risks of fire, explosion, or gas exposure, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bosch Benchmark Series 24" Dishwasher (Model #SHX89PW75N) from Home Depot #6678 in Livermore, CA in December 2024, with delivery delayed multiple times and completed in April 2024.

Timeline of Issues:

Shortly after installation, the unit failed due to a motherboard issue, which was replaced under warranty. Immediately after that, the dishwasher began tripping GFCI outlets and emitting visible internal sparks/fire when connected to a standard outlet.

A licensed electrician confirmed the homes wiring was correct and GFCI-protected at the panel.

Certified Technician Diagnosis:

A BSH-certified technician from [REDACTED] visited my home and diagnosed the dishwasher as having internal short circuits and being unsafe and beyond repair.

I was told the technician submitted a report to BSH, and I followed up repeatedly with their support team.

Contradictory Information:

When I later called BSH support, I was told the report states the unit is reparable, directly contradicting what I was told during the technicians visit.

I have requested a copy of the technician's report but have not received one.

Efforts to Resolve:

I contacted BSH, Home Depot, and the technicians office multiple times.

I also initiated a credit card dispute with [REDACTED].

I asked BSH for either a replacement unit or a refund due to the unresolved and unsafe condition.

Unresolved and Unsafe:

At present, I have a non-functional and potentially dangerous dishwasher in my home. Ive received no meaningful resolution or transparency from the manufacturer or retailer.
justification: The dishwasher is emitting sparks and has internal short circuits, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
My Samsung refrigerator (model RF28HDEDBSR) has a recurring issue with the ice maker freezing up. This causes it to stop producing ice and leads to fan and sensor errors, specifically codes 14E, 25E, and 32E. Ice builds up inside the unit and blocks airflow, sometimes preventing the fridge from cooling properly.

This problem requires me to manually thaw the ice maker every couple of months to keep it working. It's not due to misuse or wear  it's a design flaw that many other owners report online.

The failure risks food spoilage, water leakage, and possible electrical strain or fire hazard from the overworked components. Samsung sells a repair kit to fix this known issue, but refuses to cover the cost because the fridge is out of warranty, despite it being a design-related failure.
justification: The issue causes food spoilage and potential electrical hazards, but no direct injury or death is reported.

The burners on my Dacor stove were inadvertently ignited by my dog setting the cabinets on fire filling the house full of soot and smoke. My husband who was working upstairs responded to the fire alarms and was able to contain the fire but not without material damage. The stove is a Dacor 36" gas model # HGPR36S/NG. ML2-TC10SAIT-SS from Wayfair on December 10, 2022. In the last ten days, the electronic panel occasionly became unresponsive, making it impossible to turn the unit off or on. Tonight, the panel was being fussy while I was using the broil/convection function. When I was finished using the unit, the microwave turned itself on and was running all on its own, after I had left the kitchen. Luckily, I saw the light on inside and the timer on the display panel counting down from the other room and was able to inplug the unit to turn it off. It leaves me to wonder if this has happened before without my knowledge. When the panel is unresponsive, I am unable to use my appliance as it's intended. incident_description:
While gently hand-washing a gifted to me IKEA UPPHETTA French Press Coffee Maker, I suffered a sudden, traumatic injury that changed my life. The glass carafe completely intact, with no chips, cracks, or visible damage, was unexpectedly punctured the palm of my left hand near the base of my thumb. The wound was so deep that blood spurted from it, and I entered a state of physical shock, barely able to stay on my feet. I had to self-administer emergency care before being rushed to urgent care by my brother for stitches.

Despite the external wound being closed, internal nerve damage was later diagnosed, requiring surgery and leading to ongoing numbness, pain, and a loss of function in my hand. Simple daily tasks are now a challenge. The emotional toll has also been significant  I live with constant anxiety about using glass kitchenware and performing basic household routines.

I am submitting this report because I believe no one should endure what I did from a product used as intended. The fact that such a severe injury could occur during normal cleaning of a product that appeared safe and undamaged is deeply alarming. This French Press poses a hidden design danger, and consumers deserve to be protected.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury requiring surgery and causing ongoing pain and loss of function, fitting severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the unusual nature of the injury from an intact glass carafe.

incident_description: We have a GE Profile Model PDW9980N20SS Dishwasher (approximately 2008 vintage). During the last wash cycle, the internal heating element failed to turn off at the end of the cycle. We were home and noticed the smell of burning plastic. By the time we discovered the problem, the counter above the dishwasher was very hot and the internal plastic spinner inside the bottom of the dishwasher was partially melted. These older GE dishwashers that are subject to this failure should be recalled and taken out of service.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a serious safety issue with a childrens product: the Pura Kiki original straw, manufactured by Pura Stainless.

This product is marketed for babies and young children, but after minimal use, the valved tip of the straw detaches or falls apart after being bitten, posing a significant choking hazard. I have personally experienced this issue twice with two separate straws from the same pack.

After several minutes, it activated the broiler element, while still displaying bake and 350, and began overheating the element. As the food I was cooking needed to be in the oven for 30 minutes, and was in a paper ish container (it was a frozen lasagna, that can be baked or microwaved, so it was in that type of 'pan'), the container had dried out and was very neat the point of catching fire when I smelled that my food was burning and checked on it. All of this happened in less than 5 minutes, so the broiler element was significantly hotter than its normal 500. I'm confident in that assessment based on how burned my lasagna was too. It was blackened in excess of  of an inch thickness. 

Had I not been close at hand, this very easily, and very quickly, could have turned into a kitchen fire. Upon research the error message, and the switch from bake to broil, I found this is a common nature of failure with this control panel, which is used across multiple models of oven, across multiple brands.

incident_description:
Toshiba ML2-EC10SA
S#: 347D099500115051100081

ORDERED FROM: AMAZON
Order placed September 24, 2021  
Order # [REDACTED]   $199.99

FIRE: 04/10/2025

I have owned this Toshiba microwave for several years, having purchased it after my previous Toshiba model failed. I was attracted to its multifunctionality, but I found that I seldom utilized those features as they didn't perform as expected. Its main function, the microwave, was satisfactory and above average. 

Recently, when using the unit added some extra time, we guessed this was just us pushing the button too often. But the unit was adding extra cooking time on its own. For instance, if we set it for 2 minutes, it would sometimes extend the time by an additional 30, 60, or even 90 seconds. 

FIRE
Then came the alarming incident. Last night, my wife was heating a small pillow when she stepped away. The microwave unexpectedly added more time while she was out of the room.

When she returned, the microwave was still operating and adding additional time. The pillow was smoking and potentially on fire, and the kitchen was filling with smoke. Fortunately, she managed to remove the entire unit from the house. Had she been a few moments later, the situation could have escalated, especially since the microwave is positioned beneath a wooden cabinet.

I also remember that the microwave had turned itself on and added time after a power outage, but I guess this was due to the power outage at the time. Now, Im reconsidering those incidents. 
As I begin to research this issue, Ive come across reports suggesting that the '30-second button' can get stuck. This is difficult to detect since it is flush with the unit. 

After taking some additional photos, Ive decided to dispose of this microwave. I felt it was important to share this warning with others about a potential fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with potential for escalation, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a KitchenAid dishwasher (Model KDTM404KPS) + installation from Home Depot. 

Due to installer negligence (the installer ran the unit without inspecting it adequately) and/or a product defect that would have been caught by proper inspection during the installation, the internal spray arm came loose and melted onto the heating element during the first cycle, filling my home with toxic plastic fumes, and blasting my wife in the face upon opening the dishwasher. 

This caused immediate eye and respiratory irritation for my wife and exposed my family of 6 to harmful vapors. 

The installer started the dishwasher right before he left and said "don't touch it - let it finish the cycle before using it."  When my wife later opened the dishwasher after the first cycle, she was blasted in the face with melted plastic vapor that mixed with the steam. 

My wife immediately called me after this event and I told her to keep the dishwasher closed until I got home to take a look. I opened and inspected the dishwasher to find a loose screw on the inside-bottom of the unit, along with the main spray arm off to the side. Upon inspecting the spray arm further, I noticed it had been melted onto the heating element - this is what caused the strong chemical blast into my wife's face upon opening the unit after the wash cycle kicked off by the installer. 

My wife's eyes, airway, and face were painfully irritated for approximately 30 minutes. She opened the windows in the house to help clear the chemical vapors, which lasted for about 8 hours (into the evening after the event). She did not seek further medical attention.

Vaporized plastic exposure to mucous membranes and airways is toxic and likely carcinogenic - there is no safe toxicity limit established for most common consumer-grade plastics used in products in their vapor form when exposed to human tissue in the eyes, face, and airway. 

I have photographic evidence and a recorded report from a technician sent by Whirlpool after the event documenting the loose screw and melted spray arm.
justification: The incident caused immediate eye and respiratory irritation to the wife and exposed the family to harmful vapors, but no long-term medical attention was required.

incident_description:
What Happened:

For over three years, I suffered from chronic stomach problems. Doctors were unable to diagnose the issue and believed the symptoms were psychosomatic, prescribing antidepressants. However, the pain persisted and worsened over time.

About a month and a half ago, after throwing out a bag of trash, I experienced a sharp pain in my abdomen. Two days later, the pain became severe, and I was unable to eat or drink. I was admitted to the emergency room. An ultrasound revealed a foreign object lodged at the end of my small intestine. After further testing and a colonoscopy, doctors discovered a plastic bread bag clip had been stuck in my digestive system, likely for more than three years. It had caused damage to my ileum and intestine.

The clip had gone undetected because of its size and thin plastic design. It was not felt in my mouth and could not be detected by standard imaging methods until severe symptoms appeared. Doctors confirmed that the clip allowed partial stool passage, which is why it remained in my body for so long without being expelled naturally.

Product Information:

The item was a plastic bread bag clipa common product used in food packaging. It is not biodegradable and poses a significant ingestion risk. Based on my research, similar incidents have occurred in the U.S. These clips were patented in 1954 and have never been redesigned to improve safety. They are still made from thin plastic that is easy to swallow and not detectable when chewing.

Why This Product Is Dangerous:

This type of clip:

Is made from non-biodegradable plastic

Is too thin to be noticed if swallowed

Can remain lodged in the digestive tract for years

Can cause serious intestinal damage, infection, or even death

Outcome:

I now have medical documentation and support from the hospital doctor who treated me. Had the clip not been discovered and removed, I could have suffered an intestinal perforation or worse.

What Should Be Done:

This product needs to be redesigned using a thicker, biodegradable material and include safety guidelines. I am currently seeking legal representation to hold the manufacturer accountable.
