Kitchenaid Electric stove dials on stove out front get turned on and caused a fire. They are extremely sensitive to any movement by the stove if brushed gently it will turn on unknowingly and Kitchenaid just tells you to babyproof by buying covers yet NO warning about this feature and engineers should make it more safe for adults I do not have children and should not have to "baby proof" my home is ridiculous. I spent 1700 dollars on a stove that is not safe. Model # KSEG700ESS
Store SKU # 1001292816
justification: The incident describes a fire caused by sensitive stove dials, indicating a clear hazard but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
While cooking chicken on a medium heat setting, the screw cover that secures the handle to my Ninja brand frying pan suddenly exploded. The metal piece detached with force and shot across the kitchen, accompanied by a very loud popping noise. Thankfully, I had just turned away from the stove and was not hit by the flying part, but the outcome could have been serious if someone had been in the line of fire.

There was nothing unusual about the cooking conditionsno high heat or visible warping. The pan was on a standard stovetop, and I had been using it as instructed. The temperature was not excessive, and the food was cooking normally until the sudden failure occurred.

This incident raises serious concerns about the structural integrity and safety of the pan, particularly the handle components. Im reporting this in case others have experienced similar issues or are at risk of injury.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous failure of the frying pan handle, but no injury occurred as the user was not hit by the flying part.

incident_description: knobs accidentally turned on LG ThinQ stove resulting in fire.   Was caught quick enough that it did not burn the house, but did burn a cutting board on the stove.  My specific model is not listed in the LG recall but it should be.   Model LSEL6335*E
justification: The incident resulted in a fire that burned a cutting board but was caught before causing more damage, indicating no injury or death.

incident_description: While preheating my oven to 400 degrees F, I heard a crash and noted that the outside tempered glass had shattered. The oven is a Frigidaire FFEF3054TD. There were no noticeable defects in the glass before it shattered. The internal glass remains intact. While there was glass everywhere, no one was injured fortunately. I have read online that this is not an uncommon occurance so I wanted to report mine.
justification: The incident involved shattered oven glass but no injuries, and the description notes this is not uncommon.

incident_description: While using a Copper Diamond pan by Lexi Home cookware, a metal cap near the handle shot off like a projectile and flew 25 feet away.  It caused a deafening loud pop, ringing our ears for 5 minutes.  If the piece would have hit someone it would have cause serious bodily harm.
justification: The incident involved a projectile that could have caused serious bodily harm but did not result in injury.

incident_description: The inner glass of our Whirlpool double oven spontaneously shattered while baking a meal at 425 degrees.  The fragments and tiny shards were everywhere inside of the upper oven and fell down into the bottom oven when we opened the door to assess the situation. This unit was installed less than 3 years ago in a brand new construction home and the manufacturer seems to have no interest in determining what could have caused the issue.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous shattering of oven glass, causing debris but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I was utilizing the product, and it became extremely hot to touch, and once opened, the steam was extremely hot; I only used this product four times because on the last use, I was burned on my hand and wrist.
justification: The user sustained a burn injury from the product, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident occurred on the fourth use, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I am reporting a serious safety hazard involving an Aicok Air Fryer (model AF-02B, received as a gift in 2022). While the appliance was turned off and after use, it internally overheated, triggering smoke detectors in my home approximately 20 minutes later. The unit was emitting heavy smoke, the basket was stuck, and when forced open, the internal components were found melted and charred, with visible damage to screws and wiring.

This incident posed a significant fire risk and could have resulted in property damage or injury. The air fryer showed no external signs of being operational at the time of the overheating.

Despite contacting the company multiple times, they have refused to take appropriate action to address the issue, refund, or replace the unit.

This product presents a serious safety defect and is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved significant overheating and smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Outer Glass on Frigidaire Electric Oven model FFEF3054TSR  spontaneously shatters and could potential injure anyone close to the oven.  It appears from internet data that Frigidaire knew of this issue and did issue a recall.
justification: The incident involves spontaneous shattering of oven glass, which could injure anyone nearby, and there is evidence of a recall indicating a known issue.

incident_description: I own an Amana stove mod # agr5330ba53, it has a defective flame sensing package, if the burner knob is slightly moved gas will be released from the burner without an ignition source being present. This happened as someone reaching into the microwave above the stove accidently leaned on the burner knob just slightly but enough for the gas the start flowing, this is just before the knob reaches the ignite position. Gas started to fill up the kitchen before anyone noticed and an hour later we had to evacuate the house once we smelled the gas. Gas should never flow unless an ignition source is present, maybe this is a MFG. way to cut costs. The ovens main burner will not flow gas unless an ignition source is present, should be the same for the stove top. I have reached out to Amana for them to correct the problem and there response was to purchase knob locks or something like that. I shouldn't have purchase anything to mask a defective appliance. This is an extreme hazard and could have turned out much worse. Thank you for your time.
justification: Gas leakage without ignition is a severe hazard that could lead to explosion or poisoning, though no injury occurred this time.

incident_description: Bumping into stove can activate knob and turn on flow of gas. This can happen while reaching for microwave or cleaning stove.
justification: Bumping into the stove can lead to a gas leak, which is an incident with potential for harm but no immediate injury reported.

incident_description: My ovens glass door exploded, starting from a crack in a corner and then the entire glass gradually shattered. It had been turned off for 10min after 30min of use. It is a Samsung freestanding electric range, the model number is likely NE63A6311SS. The product was purchased 10 months ago. Luckily I was eating away from the oven when it broke.
justification: The oven's glass door shattered but no one was injured as the person was away from the oven when it broke.

incident_description: LG Electric Range.  Model LSEL6335FE.  I was using the stove which was purchased last October and put into service in December 2024.  I turned on the left back burner and the front left burner turned on high in addition to the back burner.  I almost caught my clothing on fire . . . I was very fortunate that did not happen.  We then tried the other burners and the same thing happened . . . the other burner would turn on in addition to the front left burner.   I contacted LG last week and finally heard from a repair person and he informed that there were at least 5 parts LG recommended having replaced for this problem and one of them was backordered with no known delivery date.  This is clearly a known problem at LG and exceptionally dangerous.  There should be a recall on this product immediately.   People will get injured and houses will burn down if there is not.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could have caused injury or fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding a defective stove I purchased just three months ago. The appliance has become a serious safety hazard in my home, and I am deeply concerned for the well-being of my family. While cooking recently, the stove caused a significant malfunction that resulted in a large hole being burned through the bottom of my metal pot. This was not only damaging to the cookware but also created a fire hazard, as the incident nearly caused an electrical fire. Additionally, my husband almost had a heart attack from the shock of watching the explosion on the stove. If he was any closer, he wouldve sustained serious injuries.
Given that the stove is only three months old, I do not feel comfortable using it anymore. I have contacted the customer service department, where I spent over an hour explaining my situation and requesting a replacement. However, I was advised by a representative named [REDACTED] that the only option available is for GE to send a technician to attempt a repair. The soonest technician can come is in five days, which is far too long to wait, especially considering the potential dangers this appliance poses. I am also extremely concerned about the safety of my children, as I work outside the home and cannot be there to supervise them when they cook. I cannot in good conscience allow them to use a stove that is clearly unsafe. I must emphasize that this is a safety issue, and I am not willing to accept a repair attempt on a brand-new appliance. I respectfully request that you intervene in this matter and facilitate the immediate replacement of the stove. As an additional concern, I cannot afford to eat fast food daily while waiting for the stove to be replaced, which further complicates this situation. I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and look forward to your assistance in ensuring that my family can cook safely once again. Thank you
justification: The incident caused property damage and a near-injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was using an Oster 2-slice toaster (Model TSSTTRJB07) in my kitchen when I heard a loud pop and saw a spark come out of the unit. The toaster immediately shut off, and it caused both the GFCI outlet to trip and the circuit breaker to shut off power. No injuries occurred, but this was a serious electrical fault. The outlet was inspected and works fine after being reset. The toaster appears to be the source of the short. Im reporting this in case its part of a larger issue.
justification: The incident involved a serious electrical fault with no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the fault.

incident_description: plug over heats gets to hot to even unplug
justification: The plug overheating is an incident that could lead to injury if not addressed, but the description does not mention any injury occurring.

incident_description: I came home to a burning plastic smell in the kitchen.  I traced the smell to the kitchen cabinet below the kitchen sink. Specifically at the Bosch manufactured electrical junction box for my Bosch dishwasher.  The junction box was so  hot that it could not be touched. I immediately switched off the corresponding circuit breaker then opened up the junction box.  I was amazed that the terminal where the wires are connected were charred  and melted along with the insulation around the wires.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous electrical malfunction that could have led to a fire or injury, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We were taking a pizza out of the oven and the glass of the inside oven shattered
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering, which is a notable event but did not result in any injury.

incident_description: My husband was cooking bacon in a cooks brand pan when one of the bolt covers shot off, flying across the room. The bolt edge is now misshaped and the cover is unable to be put back on.  No one was injured although there could have been serious injury if the hot bolt cover hit him or our infant.
justification: No one was injured, but the incident involved a potential hazard with the pan's bolt cover.

incident_description: I own an LG Stove and I have found the stove top ON more times than I can count - if I had to estimate - at least a dozen times or more since we've owned it. At first I thought someone had left the stove on ?!? I just happened to hear there was a recall on LG ranges because they've caused house fires - NOW I put 2 and 2 together - Oh my goodness- it scares me to think it could come on and all they want to do is have you order a sticker to put on your stove or put a setting on. My stove IS on the recall list - I was never notified and I have my product registered on their website! AND all they want to do is give you a sticker to put on your stove, how does that help and who wants a sticker on the stove! On the sticker on their website there is a QR code - that is suppose to take you to a video of how to put on the control lock/lock out function.  I scanned it and it only takes you to a product page where I tried to search but was unable to find a video. What happens when someone other than myself uses the range and forgets to lock it. A sticker and a setting does not keep my house from catching fire because LG made a faulty product! This is NOT GOOD!
justification: The stove turning on unexpectedly poses a fire hazard, which is a serious incident but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
In May of 2024, I began experiencing recurring symptoms including fatigue, headaches, and nausea, which persisted over the course of a year. These symptoms affected both myself and members of my household and led to missed workdays and concerns about our overall health. It wasn't until I read an article about CM and your burners must be all blue did I suspect something.  A technician confirmed that the appliance was leaking carbon monoxide (CO). Following this, I contacted the appliance manufacturer, who sent a technician to evaluate the unit. The technician initially noted a gas leak and confirmed the carbon monoxide leak after I insisted on the findings provided by the gas company.

I have since had medical tests to evaluate the impact of long-term CO exposure, and my household has incurred both health concerns and increased utility bills due to the ongoing gas leak. We are also in the process of fertility evaluations and are concerned the exposure may have had an effect.
justification: The incident involved long-term CO exposure leading to health concerns and medical evaluations, indicating injury.

incident_description:
I am using an LTE 4815 electric stovetop range.  
I bought a fire resistant pasta board to store items on top of the stove for extra buffet food items and I use that board every day.  It lays on top of the burners.   The stovetop buttons to turn on the electric burners are not made with any stop-gap mechanism that keeps the buttons in the off position.  If someone brushes against the buttons or a child comes up to the stove, they can turn on the stovetop cooking burners.   
I removed a jar from one of my cabinets in the kitchen adjacent to the stove burner buttons and indavertently and brushed against the button that turns on the cooktop. I did not realize at the time that the cooktop burner was on because the board was on top of the stove.

Because the buttons do not lock about an hour after I turned on the burner, I started to smell smoke.  The board was fire resistant so it did not ignite, but my home filled with black smoke from the heated board and my fire alarms turned on.

I went to the website for LG to look up information on the stove and found that the stove had a recall because there have been many instances of fires starting for the reason that the burners can be turned on with no effort.  I could have had a fire in my home.  Here is the recall notice I found, but I was not informed about this issue until I looked at the website and found it myself.
https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2025/LG-Recalls-Electric-Ranges-Due-to-Fire-Hazard

My home could have caught fire and I live in a multi family building.
justification: The incident involved a near-miss fire hazard due to easily activated stove buttons, resulting in smoke but no injury or fire.

incident_description: Kenmore upright freezer was failing to keep items frozen.  Upon further inspection of the outside of the freezer, it was found to have a severe burn marks along the back underside of the freezer.  Upon further inspection of the inside of the freezer, it was found to have severe burn  and melted plastic near the coils.
justification: The incident involves equipment damage (burn marks and melted plastic) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: At [REDACTED] this morning, our oven door exploded with glass flying out into the kitchen and on to the floor.  We have a Frigidaire brand with the Model Number LFIF3054TFA, and Serial Number VF73408728.  Our power was out last night, so the oven was positively not on.  I woke up to a loud "crash" sound, and saw all the glass on the floor.  Our oven was cold to the touch.  There were no injuries because everyone was asleep and not near the oven, thank goodness!  But I have 5 children who peer into the oven regularly and if this had happened while they were close, I can't imagine the damage it could have done to their eyes or face.
justification: The oven door exploded, but no one was injured as everyone was asleep and not near the oven.

incident_description: The wheels on the bottom rack of my dishwasher keep melting making it unsafe to use.
justification: Melting wheels pose a safety hazard but no injury is reported, and the issue is likely to recur based on the description.

incident_description: Our brand new Frigidaire stove randomly turned the elements on and caused a fire. We were not using the stove at the time. We have video evidence that all burners were off but the element light was on. Friday evening we were outside playing with our kids when we heard all fire alarms going off in our house. We ran inside to see smoke coming from the stove and flames. The flames were burning our microwave which is located above the stove. The flat top was completely on fire and the microwave was melting.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a malfunctioning stove, resulting in property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I was getting ice form our Samsung large capacity refrigerator and fill a large cup of water with the ice for my 10-year daughter. My daughter said, daddy look the is a piece of a large point object and her cup of water looked a little cloudy like there were crumbs in her water. Come to find out that piece of point hard plastic came from the ice maker itself and Pices if the turning mechanism from the inside of the ice maker tray broke apart leaving the cloud of other small piece of plastic in my daughters' water along with the hard piece of plastic that was in my daughters' cup. The only reason my daughter did not swallow or ingest the large piece of sharp plastic. It was caught on the bottom of my daughter's straw when she was trying to drink her water.
justification: Incident involving plastic pieces in water, but no injury occurred as the sharp piece was caught before ingestion.

incident_description: I purchased a new stainless steel LG gas range. Within a week or so after purchase, I was baking bread at 400 degrees F. I noticed the exterior strip of stainless steel on the outside of the oven, knob area, was extremely hot. We clocked the exterior temperature at over 175 degrees F. I contacted LG, they stated it is within spec, that it can reach up to 180F and still be considered within spec. I have a small child at home (2 years old) and I believe even with careful monitoring, this oven is not safe for households with small children. Manufacturer (LG) was no help.
justification: The exterior of the oven reaches high temperatures, posing a burn risk, especially to small children, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My appliance is part of a nationwide recall but my serial number is not included in the recall. It is doing what the other serial number models are doing and I think it should be included in the recall. It accidently turns on when someone rubs the power knobs on the stove.
justification: The incident involves the appliance turning on accidentally, which is an operational issue but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Using my whirlpool stove top with a heavy pot full of food the steel great slips off the base. The steel grate is not attached to the base and therefore slides easily. This has happened several times to me while cooking over the last 10 years.
justification: The incident involves a pot slipping off the stove grate, which has happened several times over 10 years without reported injury.

incident_description: This Frigidaire electric range (Model: FFEF3054TSU, Serial: VF30907203) came with the new home I purchased from [REDACTED] in May 2023. On April 22 2025, while the oven was not actively in use, the outer glass on the oven door spontaneously shattered. No heavy impact occurred, and the appliance had only been lightly used for normal household cooking. At the time, no one was touching the oven, but the shattering glass posed a risk of injury to nearby people, including children. Fortunately, no injuries occurred, but glass pieces were scattered across the kitchen floor, creating a significant safety hazard.
justification: The oven door glass shattered spontaneously, posing a risk of injury, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: The control panel starts beeping and lighting up like someone is operating it all on its own. The self clean cycle has came on by itself, burners have been turned on, oven door locked, etc. It's completely random and very dangerous. I purchased my range from Lowe's and have a protection plan. I have filed 4 claims. Each time the control board has been replaced. Months later, the same issue occurs.
justification: The malfunctioning control panel poses a direct risk of injury due to burners turning on and the oven door locking unexpectedly, and the issue has recurred multiple times despite repairs.

incident_description: Lg electric stove, one of the burners does not turn off. While the other burners are on, I've contacted Lg but will not help
justification: A burner not turning off is an incident with potential safety risk, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: GE Stove door exploded outside glass part at a stove that was only at a little under 300.
justification: The stove door exploded, which could cause injury due to flying glass or burns, but no injury was mentioned.

incident_description: SAMSUNG REFRIGERATOR.  FIRST ISSUE WAS ICE MAKER.  THEY "FIXED" IT, BUT NOW IT DRIPS WATER AND THE REFRIGERATOR IS NOT KEEPING FOOD COLD.
justification: The refrigerator is malfunctioning but there is no mention of injury or death, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description: I bought a Bosch 30 inch MODEL HG18056UC 5 burner gas oven. After doing a self cleaning, I noticed there were chips in the interior enamel.  Also chip of enamel dug into my thumb while rinsing oven. The metal is now exposed.  I called Bosch who informed me it was cosmetic and not a manufacturer's defect. I feel this is a danger to our health because of the exposed metal.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (chip dug into thumb) and potential health concerns due to exposed metal, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description: The glass window on my oven door shattered, spewing glass all over the kitchen floor.  There was no one home at the time. The oven was not in use and hadn't been used in about 2 weeks.  It hadn't been exposed to high temperatures, like a self clean cycle, in over a year.  Frigidaire electric range, FFWF3054TSC.  serial # VF73312585.  The door had never been banged or hit in any way.
justification: The oven door shattered, causing an incident with no injury as no one was present.

incident_description: We were baking bread in our oven and standing right in front of it talking when out of nowhere the outer glass exploded and sent glass all over the kitchen floor. The glass was very sharp and I stepped on a shard and drew blood.
justification: The incident involved an injury from stepping on glass shards, which drew blood, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the oven glass exploding.

incident_description: GE Induction Cooktop model PHP9030DJ5BB lock feature disengages after power outage.  This poses a safety hazard for consumers that have pets.  We had a dog get his paws on the cooktop after a power outage but noticed it in time to avoid any problems. It is preferred the lock feature stay in place after a power outage.  The lock feature on our GE wall oven MODEL JTS5000EWES also disengages after a power outage posing a hazard for small children's curiosity.  This has been the case for 2.5 years since we remodeled our kitchen and just came back to light since acquiring a new puppy.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard with no injury, and the likelihood is high given the recurring issue over 2.5 years.

incident_description: I purchased a Cuisinart Deluxe Convection Toaster Oven Broiler in August of 2022 for my daughter.  In November of 2024, we discovered that the plug was melted onto the back of the unit where the heating unit is located.  We reached out to Conair, Cuisinarts parent company to advise them this dangerous design flaw and were told that it was our fault for not maintaining a two inch distance between the unit and the plug on the wall.
justification: The incident involved a melted plug but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: GE   Microwave Oven
justification: The description only mentions a GE Microwave Oven with no incident or injury reported.

incident_description: We are reheating a leftover pizza for 250F in our GE double oven. Our oven is clean no oil buildup and not used often. All of a sudden we heard a spark and the oven started burning and the fire seemed to have started from the electrical in between the double oven to the top oven and even burned the bottom of the top oven
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injury was reported, making it a severity level 2. Electrical fires in ovens are uncommon but not unheard of, hence an occurrence likelihood of 2.

incident_description: GE Microwave Model PEM31SF3SS - Door interlock switch is defective and the unit's Magnetron runs by itself non-stop when the door is closed. There is no fan, lights, or control panel indications and only a very low, imperceptible hum so it's not obvious it is operating by itself. The unit gets extremely hot on the inside and I believe it is a fire hazard, especially if it is mounted overhead in a wood kitchen cabinet. It is designed to be installed this way with the optional trim kit GE-JX827SFSS. I have also reported this issue to GE Appliances.
justification: The defective microwave poses a fire hazard, especially when installed overhead, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Our KitchenAid oven failed while cooking a loaf of bread. We heard loud buzzing sounds from the over, and through the door you could see sparks, smoke and flames. It looked and sounded like welding. We shut off the breaker to make it stop. After cooling down and inspecting further, the heating element completely failed and burned through. It also arc welded a hole in the bottom pan in the oven.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and flames but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the description of the failure.

incident_description: Mr. Coffee 4-in-1 Single-Serve Latte, Iced, and Hot Coffee Maker with Milk Frother, SKU: SAP_2175542. The product's instructions list to pour a cup of water into coffee maker's water reservoir, turn the coffee maker power to on and that after making coffee, the product automatically turns off. The frother has a separate heating element and its own power button, which also automatically turns off based on a short timer. In the morning, my wife poured water into the coffee maker's water reservoir and the water immediately starting steaming. We found that the coffee maker and frother were extremely hot and had apparently been on for a long time. There had been no water in the water reservoir. The frother's heating element was also on. The power buttons have lights indicating that they're on and were not lit up to show they were on. We were the only ones in the house awake. We're unsure how many hours the coffee maker had been on.
justification: The coffee maker and frother were left on unintentionally, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I am reporting a serious and recurring safety issue with our Frigidaire oven. This is the second time in less than one year that the ovens glass door has shattered spontaneously and violently. The first time this happened was June 2024. I contacted Frigidaire and opened a claim. However, I was told that "maybe one of my kids had accidentally hit the glass which caused to explode". 

Most recently, we turned the oven on to preheat, and within 30 seconds, the glass door exploded without warning. The sound was deafeninglike a gunshotand glass shards flew across the kitchen. Thankfully, my children were not present at the time. If they had been, this could have resulted in severe injuries.

We experienced the exact same incident last summer, and reported it to Frigidaire. However, they failed to take any responsibility or offer support to cover the cost of replacing the glass door. This response is unacceptable, especially given the clear and present danger this product poses.

I am deeply concerned that this oven is not safe for consumers. The force and unpredictability of the glass shattering make it a serious hazard, particularly in households with children. I fear that someoneespecially a childcould be seriously harmed or worse if this continues to happen.

Is there a recall in place for this model? If not, there absolutely should be. I urge your office to investigate this product before it causes a catastrophic injury.

As it stands, we no longer have a functioning oven, and we are unwilling to repair it again given the ongoing risk. We simply cannot trust this product in our home any longer.

Please take this report seriously. I truly believe lives could be at risk if this issue is not addressed.
justification: The oven door shattered violently twice, posing a clear hazard, but no injuries were reported this time.

incident_description: My 10 month old daughter was using PrimaStella Silicone spoons that we purchased six weeks ago . We had used them for normal baby feeding, no extreme or abnormal use. I found the green spoon in two pieces after my 10 month old daughter dropped it. As I examined it, it crumbled into a third piece. I initially assumed it was a fluke until two days later, she dropped the orange one and it was torn and missing a piece. Another piece tore off easily while I was inspecting it. I still have not found the missing piece from the orange spoon, and I am worried she may have swallowed it. If she did swallow it, we do not know yet if it has caused injury. Thankfully, she did not choke, but I am deeply concerned these spoons may be made with defective silicone and pose a choking hazard. We stopped using them immediately. My daughter only has two teeth and was not using them as teethers so they should not deteriorate like this after such minimal use. I am seriously concerned about the safety of this product.
justification: The incident involves a potential choking hazard with no confirmed injury, but there is concern about the child possibly swallowing a piece of the spoon.

incident_description: Frigidaire oven (model #FCRE305LAFJ) outside glass door shattered all over my kitchen. The sound that it made was like a gunshot. My adult daughter was standing just outside of the glass spray and was not hurt. Frigidaire said the stove was past the one year warranty and they wouldnt pay for the replacement when clearly this isnt normal for a 2.8 year old stove.
justification: The oven door shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: item is a Frigidaire model FFEF3054TSR electric range.  I had moved the stove to clen behind it; while I was cleaning I heard a loud "bang" and found that the front glass on the door had shattered.
justification: The incident involved the glass shattering but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My brand new KitchenAid dual fuel range's glass door exploded for no reason.  I had it replaced and the same thing happened five days later.  I've had this oven for three weeks and had two exterior glass windows shatter on their own.
justification: The incident describes repeated glass shattering without injury, indicating a significant product defect but no harm to individuals.

incident_description: I had set the lower oven on Bake at 400 for 30 minutes to burn off any manufacturers chemicals on my newly installed GE Profile Double Oven Freestanding Range with doors open for ventilation. About an hour later, the alarms began to sound. Our alarm monitoring company called to tell us to evacuate due to carbon monoxide. The alarm company phoned the Fire Department for us while we evacuated. The Fire Department measured the CO level coming from the top oven and found the levels to be over 250 ppm. They reported that this was the highest level of CO output that they had ever seen. We were told by the Fire Department not to use this appliance at all. They ventilated the house using fans and found CO levels throughout the house including the most distant rooms from the source.
justification: The incident involved high levels of carbon monoxide requiring evacuation and fire department intervention, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Cooking bake glass crack purchased from Target, Crack inside the Range Oven Causing a Fire in the Kitchen And Personal Injuries and Property Damages
justification: The incident involved a fire causing personal injuries and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: I was using the clean oven selection on my frigerdaire oven when about an hour into the two hour session i hear a loud crashing and found shattered glass from my oven door all over the floor.
justification: The oven door shattered, causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

We called the fire department and they removed the back panel of the oven and found that the wrap insulation was smoldering. I want to report this because the oven has been properly used and maintained for only 1.5 years  and this should not have happened and it could have been tragic. incident_description:
Samsung refrigerator, which has caused significant damage to my home. The unit is a 4-door French door model equipped with a dual ice maker, including the smaller cube ice maker located in the upper left section of the refrigerator.

Over time, the small cube ice maker began to freeze over and malfunction. Despite regular maintenance and following Samsungs recommended troubleshooting steps, the problem persisted. Eventually, the ice maker became so frozen that it blocked the normal flow of water within the unit. This caused water to leak internally throughout the refrigerator and then externally, where it pooled and seeped out onto the kitchen floor.

My husband, self and children have all slipped on the water that seeped out of refrigerator onto the floor. Thankfully the slipping did not cause serious injury. 

The leaking water caused damage to my hardwood floors and baseboards, requiring professional repair. The floors warped, and the baseboards began to swell and separate from the wall. This incident not only created an unsafe environment but also resulted in unexpected repair expenses and loss of use of my kitchen during cleanup.
justification: The incident caused property damage and created a slipping hazard, but no serious injuries were reported.

incident_description: Ice maker cube developed hairline crack, from normal use, and leaks water inside freezer that pools inside the unit or passes through the dispenser which may damage property or cause personal injury due to the increased risk of trips and falls.
justification: The incident involves a leak that may cause property damage or increase trip hazards, but no injury is reported.

Upon investigating we find the knob turned on just enough that it is leaking gas.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to accidental knob activation, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
April 4, 2023
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
RE: Product Malfunction and Personal Injury Claim
To Whom It May Concern:
On March 6, 2023, my KitchenAid range ceased to preheat properly. I was attempting to heat the oven to bake a loaf of bread when the main oven would not increase beyond 425F. When I tried to turn the oven off and re-enter the desired temperature, I discovered that the registered temperature had dropped to 375F. As it was later in the day, I unplugged the range in an attempt to reset the system. The next day, I experienced the same issues, although the bottom oven unit was working at a lower functioning capacity. The top burners were also working properly.
I proceeded to call Whirlpool on March 7 to schedule service, as this product was under the 1-year manufacturer's warranty. A Whirlpool representative from Alabama asked me several questions about the unit's functionality issues, and an appointment was subsequently set for March 13, 2023.
On the morning of March 10, I began cleaning food particles off the top left side of the range before heating water for tea. None of the heating burner/oven functions were engaged at this time. As I wiped the top right metal edge of the range with my dominant right hand, I noticed a slight tingling feeling in my elbow, similar to the sensation of hitting your funny bone. Suspecting that I might have slept awkwardly on my arm, I continued cleaning the unit.
When I wiped between the counter and where the range met, where food debris had accumulated, I suddenly felt an immense electrical charge rush through my arm and up through the right side of my head. I became disoriented and immediately sat down. My partner, alerted by what happened, noticed my speech was slurred. When she asked how I felt, I told her I wasn't well. She suggested going to the emergency room, which I initially declined as I wanted to see if the symptoms would subside. After about an hour, I attempted to stand and walk around, but my legs were very wobbly, and I felt uncoordinated. My forehead felt cloudy and congested. At this point, I realized I had likely been electrocuted.
My partner drove me to the emergency room, and during the journey, I experienced pinging sensations on the right side of my brain, difficulty swallowing, and shooting sensations of cold, numbness, and twitching up my right arm. I spent several hours in the emergency room before being released in the mid-evening. Upon discharge, with my symptoms confirmed by medical staff, I called Whirlpool to request an urgent call from someone on their executive team. I was told someone would reach out within 48 business hours.
A technician named [REDACTED] from [REDACTED] arrived as scheduled on Monday, March 13, in the morning. I explained the issues with the unit and requested that he perform a voltage test while the unit was cold/not engaged. [REDACTED] agreed, and I stepped away to take a phone call. When I returned, he confirmed there was electrical voltage registering and asked me to turn off the circuit breaker as a safety precaution.
Upon pulling the unit out for inspection, he showed me where a circuit board displayed damage as if it had been "fried" in the rear of the unit behind a panel he unscrewed. He checked if he had a replacement part in his truck and proceeded to repair that component. After this, he ran code checks on the top display and discovered that the bottom heating element was also damaged, as well as some components on the top control board.
After completing all necessary repairs, I requested that he document everything he diagnosed as well as the voltage reading. I retained the damaged rear circuit board and bottom heating element, which I still have in my possession. I called [REDACTED] the following day to request a copy of the findings and repairs made by [REDACTED]. The language in the report wasn't as clear as I had expected, so I requested an amendment, which was subsequently made.
At this point, 72 hours had passed since my call following the emergency room visit, and I still had not heard any follow-up from Whirlpool. Eventually, [REDACTED] from the safety department contacted me to inquire about the incident. I explained my account as detailed above, but he disputed certain aspects of my recounting based on his documented conversation with [REDACTED]. A claim form was emailed to me with an offer of $3,600 to replace the defective appliance.
I have since followed up with my medical provider to seek neurological care. My next appointment is scheduled for June 9, 2023. I am experiencing lingering symptoms, including extreme fatigue and nerve sensations in my right arm throughout the day. My lifestyle has been dramatically disrupted because of this hazardous product your company sold to me.
I have  formally filed a claim to address my medical expenses and damages incurred up to now and any that may arise in the future as a result of your faulty product. In addition, I am also submitting a formal claim for physical, emotional, and mental damages related to your hazardous product.
Kind Regards,
[REDACTED]
Phone: [REDACTED]
Email: [REDACTED]
Claim Reference:[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injury (electrocution) with lingering symptoms, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific circumstances of the malfunction.

incident_description:
On numerous occasions our new 36 GE Pro Cafe gas range has ignited with the slightest bump by people walking by, leaning against or by our large dogs passing through the
kitchen. I have resorted to removing the knobs and storing them beside this very expensive gas range in my newly remodeled foothills home.  There are no aftermarket locks that fit these knobs. And, the range is not designed with any sort of locking option that can be engaged  to prevent accidental ignition according to the manufacturer when I asked.  I went to the store where I bought the range.  They had one hooked up on display.  I was able to demonstrate how quickly and easily these ranges will turn on and ignite with the slightest bump by someone  walking by.   Any household with children, elderly, and pets is at risk of this range being turned on and burning without realizing it until the house is on fire.
justification: The incident describes a significant risk of accidental ignition with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death is reported.

LG 6.3 cu. ft. Smart wi-fi Enabled InstaView ELECTRIC Slide-In Range with ProBake Convection, Air Fry and Air Sous Vide, in Stainless Steel

incident_description: I own a Bosch dishwasher.  The power cord junction box that is provided by many of the Bosch dishwashers started to emit a burning smell.  This junction box is included with the dishwasher and was installed by Lowe's.  An electrician removed the cover and the neutral was severely burnt and he told me that i was lucky there was not a house fiire.  A simple search will many examples of burnt boxes exactly like mine.  I did find recalls issued on the Bosch website specifically for the powercord, however, when I called Bosch the only thing they could offer is to send a technician.  Interestingly, many reported that this happens about 2 to three years into the life of the product so by then it is out of warranty.  The estimate to replace is $1100.00.  I was very surprised at the lack of concern.  You can purchase this junction box from Home Depot.  While it has 4.4 stars, there are 22 individual images of burnt boxes in the reviews some from Jan of this year 2025.
justification: The incident involved a burnt power cord junction box with potential for a house fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Before this incident began, it had been 10 minutes since anyone had touched the refrigerator. I heard the refrigerator started dispensing ice making noise and thought it was ice dropping. I left the kitchen and went to my office for about 20-30 minutes. When I came back to the kitchen it smelled like something was burning and discovered that the ice maker was dispensing ice on its own. When I opened the refrigerator and removed the ice maker, there was smoke in the ice maker area. I tried to turn off the ice maker, tried to reset two times and finally we had to unplug the refrigerator because it would not trying to dispense ice. This was a Friday night and Samsung technician came to our house Monday and said the refrigerator was not repairable. He also took photos - which I have - where you see components were melting. Had I not been home, this would have started a fire. This incident comes after Samsung has fixed my ice maker 5 times since we purchased it 4 1/2 years ago. We still have the refrigerator but it cant be used. This happened on 4/4 and as of today 4/12, Samsung still has not resolved this issue and I still dont have a refrigerator.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator that could have started a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

After using the oven to cook food at approximately 430F, the oven door suddenly shattered when I opened it. The glass from the door exploded and scattered everywhere. Fortunately, no one was injured in this incident, but the glass shards could have potentially caused serious injuries to anyone nearby. The product was being used properly and as intended in a home setting. The incident raises significant safety concerns about the structural integrity of the oven door glass when exposed to high temperatures.
justification: The oven door shattered, posing potential injury risk, but no one was harmed.

incident_description:
Kenmore 30" drop-in smooth top range.  1. Left two burners couldn't be turned off when knobs were at "off" setting.  It happened about 6 times a month, starting from about 5 years ago.  I usually could manage the knob to stop the burner from heating up totally.  2. Sometimes left front burner got too hot than the level I set for cooking and caused food burnt even I was just nearby preparing food to cook. Today, April 1, 2025, the front left burner wouldn't shut off no matter how I tried, we ended up running to the power panel to shut the range off to cool it off.  
3. The front right big burner has two functions: single (the smaller diameter burner which size is equal to the back small burner size), and dual (the inner small burner size plus outer rings burners make a big burner size equal to the left big burner).  When we turned on the dual function, we noticed the outer ring turned on only, but the inner small burner not on. However, when we turned on the single function, the small burner was working, and kept on.
justification: The incident involves burners not turning off properly and getting too hot, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Purchased a new Whirlpool refrigerator and kept hearing loud Popping since day 1. We reported it to the Lowe's store where purchased, we were reassured that's it's normal because she had the same one and hers did it too. We didn't agree, because we have never heard a refrigerator do that before. So, now after 5 years the refrigerator begins to not hold the cold in the freezer and the in the refrigerator, also started smelling  something coming from the refrigerator. We went to Lowe's with our paperwork, only to find out that we no longer have warranty. We purchased the 3 year extended and the product has a one year. Found out, you actually do not get the four years; the one year manufacturer runs at the same time as the extended. So, only 3 years if what you get as far as warranty. Didn't help us!  As the person, who Lowe's  recommend as a repair service to come check the refrigerator. They said, they didn't have one, but there was a couple in town. She didn't know if they would travel out of town to where we lived.  We finally called a repair person out of Albuquerque to come check the refrigerator. We explained the situation to him. He said, the loud popping was not normal, maybe small noises when cooling. He checked the temperature in the freezer. He found out that only one side of the freezer was freezing. It was actually building up ice on that side. (It's a frost free) He continued to remove the inside freezer panel. He found that it was burning and melting the inside. (fire hazard) The refrigerator could not be repaired in this condition. He said, he could try to refill the refrigerant (because it had been leaking out) enough to keep it going until we could get a new refrigerator, but he wouldn't recommend with the fire danger. He recommended we get a new refrigerator asap. He couldn't guarantee this refrigerator would make it much longer.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I am using a Samsung slide in electric range (NE59N6630SS) with a rear control panel. The product is five years old (purchased July 2019). The control touch panel for the oven has started to activate on its own. Random oven features simply start turning on - could the broiler, the self cleaning feature, the warmer, or any other feature. When this happens, I also am unable to turn it off and the buttons are completely unresponsive to me as if I am locked out. This seems to mostly happen when Im cooking, and the only way to stop it is to turn off the breaker. Obviously, I am concerned that this could also happen when Im sleeping or away from home, and could easily start a fire.
justification: The malfunctioning control panel can lead to uncontrolled heating, posing a fire hazard and potential injury risk, especially if it occurs when unattended.

incident_description: Knobs on Frigidaire gas range turn too easily. While reaching into the microwave over the range the knobs were unknowingly moved to the on position by a house sitter. The sitter left the home and when I returned an hour later the home was filling with gas. This required a call to the local gas company to make sure the gas cleared safely to prevent an explosion.

I closed the oven and left the room and about 30 minutes later, the glass door exploded.

But it was worse than expected with the lightbulb bursting and scattering glass shards all over the inside of the oven after running the oven for 40 minutes at 375 degF the first time the oven was used the week after purchasing. This is a safety hazard and should not be sold to consumers as is. Fortunately, no one was injured as the door was closed, but there were glass shards on the food that was baking at the time.

This stove is dangerous to have in a home, I understand it is a factory defect and they do not want to respond

incident_description: While using my Whirlpool Gas Range (Model WFG114SWB0) (SN VE22404820) in my home I noticed the front of the range became very hot to the touch. In addition, i could no longer control the flow of gas to the range using the knob as it had become stuck. At this time I realized a fire has started underneath the lid of the range. I immediately pulled the range away from the wall and turned the gas supply vale to the off position to stop the flow of gas and extinguish the fire. Upon further inspection, I noticed the gas supply tube to the burner had cracked and caught fire at the location of the crack. No injury occurred.
justification: The incident involved a fire and gas leak but no injury occurred, and the issue was promptly addressed.

incident_description: I have a GE cafe gas range and am having issues with the gas burners going out during the simmer mode.   This issue occurs when the oven door is opened then closed.  My concern is having a gas leak exposure if unaware of this happening while cooking.  This can be very hazardous if the burner impacted is not turned off when the issue occurs.  The gas will continue to run through the burner. This has been occurring since the range was new.  I have had numerous service calls from the applicance store with no resolution. The technician tried to fix but was unsuccessful.  To go further, I also contacted GE who provided a tech to review issue.  The technician realized there was a design flaw in the vents in the front of the oven where air would pull through when door was opened and closed causing the gas to go out on the stove top.  The resolution is to remove all the simmer function from the range to alleviate the design flaw causing the issue.  This is not acceptable because cooking will always need a simmer capability.
justification: The incident involves a gas burner going out during simmer mode, posing a potential gas leak hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: My cosmo oven glass exploded while broiling some salmon. The oven was being used within normal everyday use. It was on max broiler temperature of 550. The glass exploded and came out of the bottom onto the ground. I was barefoot and stepped on the glass as well as my dog. Seems like a major safety issue to me.. incident_description:
We have a Hamilton Beach Brew Station Coffee Maker Model 48464 or 48465 (almost identical). The device has a water reservoir and a self-contained
coffee reservoir, where brewed coffee can be kept warm for preset number of hours until dispensed from reservoir into coffee mug.
When I awoke in the morning I started a morning routine to make fresh coffee. There was residual coffee in the "coffee" reservoir. The device was
powered (plugged into wall outlet), but had been in OFF mode since previous morning's brew cycle had ended. When I lifted the lid, condensed water
dribbles back down into the water reservoir (as it usually does). However, when the water dripped back into the water reservoir, the open lid shot
steam back out, as if the device was in brew mode. I felt the out side of the coffee maker and found that the lower half (where the water reservoir is)
was very hot. When I removed the self-contained coffee reservoir from the appliance, I found the left over coffee to be at room temperature. This
meant that the "coffee" heating element was NOT on, but that the "water" reservoir heating element (brewer coil) was on (and HOT). When I
mentioned the incident to my wife, she stated that the coffee maker had the same problem one week earlier.
I suspect that this malfunction could be a fire hazard and/or an injury (burn) hazard. I did read another consumer complaint that sounded like their
same device had similar issue (Incident Report | 5/18/2020 | [REDACTED]).
justification: The incident describes a malfunction causing steam and heat, posing a burn hazard, but no actual injury occurred. The issue has recurred, indicating likelihood is high.

"I bought a LG Range, model #LSEL6333F from Lowes and was delivered / installed mid-Jan 2025. Since I have been using the range (less than 60 days), I've been burned twice by the vent in the rear of the stovetop and once from the oven's metal framework along the front of the range-top above the control knobs while having the "oven cleaning" function in operation and  the large front burner on high setting.  When I contacted LG Customer service online on 4 Mar 25, I was texted that they would get back to me within 24 to 48 hours.  I could not find a customer service Phone number to LG on their website, but Lowes gave me the number to LG customer service (833-378-0003).  On 6 Mar 25,  I called the LG Customer Service number given to me by Lowes.  On 7 Mar 25, I finally got a call from the LG Escalation TM to discuss my issue.  LG Rep would only agree to schedule a service technician visit / inspection.  They dispatched a service technician who admitted his inability to correct the hazardous operation of the stove.  Instead he referred to the owners manual stating it would be hot during operation.  LG would not authorize a return / exchange with since there was no repair required.  LG accepts that the Self-Clean Oven feature is hazardous according to the owners manual.  Nothing was mentioned about a LG recall on the range due to the front-mounted knobs on the ranges being easily activated by accidental contact by humans or pets, posing a fire hazard.  This is validated by the Consumer Product Service Commission as of 6 Feb 25 citing 86 reports of unintentional activation involving more than 28 fires, 8 injuries, 3 pet deaths, and five fires caused extensive property damage totaling over $340,000.  LGs recall solution is to provide a decal warning to owners/ users.  Unacceptable for sub-par safety operation in my opinion.  LG obviously produces a hazardous product and is evidently willing to let the Buyer beware.  NO more LG products for me and I encourage others to not buy LG Products."   

Lowes told me to contact LG.  LG told me to contact Lowes.  The tech and Escalation Team rep both told me to read the owner's manual which stated that the oven door and frame would get hot and not to touch it during the self clean cycle.  It did not state that it would burn flesh...like mine or a child's.  Nor did I have an owner's manual until after the product was purchased and delivered.  Otherwise, I would not have purchased it.  It would appear that LG knew about the hazard but failed to protect the public or warn the public beforehand that the range would harm them.

A suit has been filed in New Jersey Federal court a class action suit against LG on this and in para 97 cites that LG knew or should have known that the misrepresentations and omissions with the intent that consumers, including Plaintiff, would rely upon them (LG) when purchasing the Defective Product.

incident_description:
We purchased a LG 6.3 cu. ft. Smart Wi-Fi Enabled Electric Single Oven InstaView Range with Air Fry in Stainless Steel (LREL6325F) from Costco (P/No. MEz57157118) in 2024 (and have had it for about 1 year. I noticed that that burner acted funny before (all of a sudden it would heat up to hot although I had not touched the control dial) but that's when I was making pancakes or sauteing something and those I easy to burn. I assumed it was something that I did. It was using the left front burner with the 3 ring burner sizes. It is labeled UltraHeat Power Boil but that function (according to the manual) is only supposed to work when you set it to "High.") 
On this occasion, I was making stew which requires simmering for about 1.5 to 2 hours using the front left burner (which has the 3 rings).  I had it on a low setting and it was simmering without any issues for about 1.5 hours. I would check on it every 10 minutes to stir it (using my [REDACTED] watch timer to remind me) and adding water as needed. I was also using the built in timer for the overall cooking time and came to stir it after 1.5 hours timer was up and realized the meat wasn't tender enough and needed more time. So I stirred it and added 20 minutes on the stove timer without adjusting any of the temperature settings. As before I had my [REDACTED] watch timer set at 10 minute intervals. But before the 10 minutes were up, I heard violent bubbling and started to smell something was burning. Sure enough the pot with the strew was boiling violently and the bottom was burnt. It was still set on the low temperature setting (I took pictures). If I had not been in the kitchen checking on it regularly, who knows what would have happened. Luckily, my children weren't home at that time. This experience confirmed for me that there is something wrong with the stove and is a fire hazard. Luckily, no one, but my burnt pot and ruined stew, got hurt. This stove is a major fire hazard. 
I saw on [REDACTED] that others have had the same issues with the Ultra Heat Power Boil burners. See here: [REDACTED]
And that some LG Stove Ovens are also being recalled. I think this model should be looked at too. We have decided we won't be using that burner because it is too risky.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that caused a pot to burn, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Hi, I have a GE PROFILE OVEN acquired through my builder in March of 2022. It was one of the kitchen appliances included in our new built home. I rarely used the oven because I stayed in a different address until late 2023 and even when I completely moved in our new home I mostly used the stove. There were multiple incidents.  The first incident was on October 8, 2024.  I came home around lunch time and found the oven lights on. I opened the door, it was burning hot inside. I immediately pressed cancel but it didnt work. I got out and switched the breaker off and back on. When I checked, the lights are still on. So, I switched the breaker off and called GE customer service who connected me to consumer relations because it is a safety issue.
A Bodewell technician (also GE) came in. I paid $147.85 for the oven light switch replaced on October 10th. He could not explain why it happened.  The second incident was on December 24th, the same thing. I found the oven lights on, interior is very hot and the breaker didn't trip. The same Bodewell technician came in on December 30th and this time he said there are three parts that need to be replaced-  1. the oven lights on switch, 2. the control panel and 3. the board. They were charging for $543.80 after the 25% discount they offered.  I asked what could be the reason it is happening, and he said there are three reasons: overuse, power outage and product defect. It was rarely used and looks brand new and there was no power outage. Therefore it is product defect. I called GE consumer relations, I complained that it is a safety issue and ask them to replace the oven. They declined because it was out of one year warranty and said they will just replace the parts without charge. So they ordered the parts and I had to wait till January 27th for the third appointment which they canceled because they said there was no technician available. For the next appointment, a different technician came in. He replaced all three parts, tested the oven for less than a minute and left. The following day, I eagerly prepared to bake some bread and mixed all ingredients. I preheated the oven and after a minute I heard a big pop! The oven was dead. It was late so I called GE the following day, upset, demanding they replace my defective oven. Again they declined. We scheduled another technician but they booked it on February 5th, the day we were set for a trip. Previously, I made it clear to them I wanted my oven fixed before we go on that date. The fourth appointment was on February 25th day after we arrived from our trip. The third technician tried to pull out the oven but he said he couldn't access it. His advice is to do a rewire because he was not familiar to the new code connection. He thought the oven was installed by the builder. Right away I called the builders customer relations officer to go to my home to clarify things. The three of us, face to face discussed the matter. The builder customer relations officer made it clear that it was JB Hunt, under GE Back then who installed the connection, therefore its GEs responsibility. The Bodewell Technicians advice is for me to hire an electrician to unhook the wire and pull out the oven, he will do a separate appointment to diagnose and hopefully fix it. Then for the third appointment the electrician will be back to reinstall the oven and wiring. The fourt appointment, the Bodewell technician will be back to check if the oven will work! And how is this guaranteed to work and the problem not repeating?
Appliances are supposed to last for more than two years, especially when they are rarely used, aren't they? Under California Lemon Law the appliance needs to be replaced under the following requirements: -The appliance has a defect that affects its safety, value or functionality -The manufacturer is given a reasonable number of repair attempts -The appliance has been out of service for more than 30 days -The defect was not caused by the consumer I have all four. Good thing there were no injuries but if I didnt come home on time during the first two incidents, fire can happen because the breaker did not trip off. Fire not only in my home but in my community. I dont want to take another risk. General Electric must replace the defective oven, and refund my payment for the price of $147.85.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue recurred multiple times despite repairs.

incident_description:
Consumer Product Safety Report
Date of Incident: Approx.. February 10, 2025

On approximately February 10th, 2025, while using a Mr. Coffee Stovetop Kettle (Stainless Steel, Silver, 15.00x15.00x10.00 inches, purchased from Walmart in late 2024), the product caught fire in my kitchen. The plastic components, including the handle and lid, ignited and produced 2-3 foot flames. The fire was extinguished, but the event posed a significant fire hazard and led to exposure to toxic fumes.

Details of the Incident
What happened that made you want to report?

The tea kettle unexpectedly caught fire while boiling water, an action for which it was designed.
The plastic handle and lid ignited, producing flames 2-3 feet high.
The fire posed a serious risk of property damage and personal injury.
Toxic fumes from the burning plastic filled my home, causing lingering health effects.
What type of product was being used?
Mr. Coffee Stovetop Kettle (Stainless Steel, Silver)

Who was using the product?
The tea kettle was used by me and my household members for boiling water.

How was the product being used?
The kettle was used almost daily before the incident.
On the morning of the incident, the kettle was placed on the stovetop with water in it.
The kettle was not left alone for an extended period.
Flames were noticed when my wife alerted me to the fire in the kitchen.

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
I suffered headaches from exposure to the toxic fumes.
The home environment was contaminated with harmful smoke from burning plastic.
There was potential risk of severe burns or property damage if the fire had not been quickly controlled.

How did the injuries occur?
Toxic fumes from burning plastic filled the house, leading to health effects.
Exposure to smoke inhalation caused persistent headaches for about a week.

Manufacturer Response
Gibson Homewares, the manufacturer, attributed the incident to improper care, suggesting that the kettle may have boiled dry.
They acknowledged my concerns but refused to take responsibility, offering only a replacement kettle.
They claimed that no other reports of similar incidents had been received.
My request for a formal investigation and accountability was not addressed satisfactorily.

Conclusion & Request for Investigation
This incident highlights a severe product safety issue. A stovetop tea kettle should never ignite under normal use, even if water evaporates. This suggests a design flaw or use of flammable materials in critical components.

I request that the CPSC investigate this product for fire hazards and toxicity concerns to prevent future incidents. Consumers should be warned, and the product should be recalled or modified if found unsafe.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Throughout this whole time the refrigerator's built-in digital readout was showing 0 degrees in the freezer section and 37 degrees in the refrigerator section. With that knowledge I knew where my symptoms of spoiled food poisoning arrived from. Luckily in my case it was  just a case of the runs but as you know, it could have been deadly for me or anyone relying on the refrigerators own digital readout. With that said, my conscience regarding consumer safety couldn't let this go unnoticed any longer.

incident_description:
Oven Fire Issue

1.	 First noticed odd burning smells in approximately November of 2024.
2.	Smells were more pronounced around Thanksgiving
3.	Burnt food smell was eliminated as there was no burnt food.
4.	Burnt oven smells were eliminated as oven was clean.
5.	Oven self-clean system was employed also.
6.	Started noticing ash fragments in the drawer below the oven.
7.	As more ashes were found, over time, the decision was taken to call our home warranty provider to determine the source and cause of the ashes and the status of the oven.
8.	The 2-10 Warranty Company sent an appliance serviceman who evaluated the problem, but did not remove the oven from the cabinet. He determined that a hole of approximately 8 inches in diameter had burned through the wood that separates the oven from the drawer below the oven. He concluded that the oven was at fault and recommended that the oven be replaced.
9.	A second appliance company service man evaluated the problem but did not remove the oven from the cabinet. He concluded the problem, in his opinion, was due to the wood used in the cabinet.
10.	On 2/6/25 a service man, from ABC Appliance Repair, evaluated the problem and did remove the oven from the cabinet. He speculated that the spacers designed to separate the wood from the oven might not have been utilized during installation and may have been the source of the problem. However, when he pulled the oven from the cabinet he determined that the spacers were properly in place. He examined the wood and the burn hole and stated, in his opinion, that the wood used to separate the oven from the drawer was not consistent with City code and was the cause of the burn hole.
11.	On 2/6/25 I spoke with [REDACTED], the General Manager, from Signature Homes, the builder of our home. He stated that Signature Homes has built hundreds of homes, utilizing the same cabinet maker and same wood as our home and that this type of wood has never caused a fire. He said the same wood is used in the cabinets in his personal home.
12.	On 2/11/25 I spoke with [REDACTED] from the Rogers, Arkansas Inspectors office. He stated that there is no City code pertaining to the type of wood to be used to separate an oven from a drawer and that he would be happy to testify that, in his opinion, the oven was at fault. He also referred me to [REDACTED] from Consumer Affairs and said he felt [REDACTED] would want to know about the oven issue.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and ash fragments, but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was contained without escalation.

incident_description:
2/9/2025

Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC)
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814
Subject: Formal Complaint Against LG Electronics  Hazardous Electric Range Recall and Insufficient Resolution
Dear Consumer Product Safety Commission,
I am filing this formal complaint regarding a severe safety hazard posed by LG Electronics recalled electric range models and their unacceptable response to the recall. The defective front-mounted control knobs on these stoves have led to accidental activation, creating a serious risk of fire, burns, and injury, yet LG has failed to offer a proper remedy for consumers.
Incident Details & Injury
I purchased an LG LSEL6331F | Serial Number 209MMYF0K946 electric range from Home Depot on 10/1/2022 and I have repeatedly experienced the dangerous accidental activation of the burners due to the excessively sensitive front-mounted knobs.
Last summer, in July 2024 one of the burners turned on unexpectedly, which resulted in my friends cat suffering severe burns to its paws, requiring urgent veterinary treatment and medical expenses. I also sustain a serious burn on my left hand when the stove was inadvertently turned on when someone brushed up against the knobs. I have also experienced multiple other instances where burners were activated unintentionally, posing a serious fire hazard in my home.
LG's Inadequate Recall "Solution"
Despite the serious documented risks, LG's official recall remedy is wholly insufficient:
	LG is not offering repairs, refunds, or replacements.
	Instead, they are sending a warning label and advising consumers to use the "Lock Out" feature manually after each use.
	This fails to fix the underlying defect, shifts responsibility onto the consumer, and is an unacceptable excuse for a safety recall.
Why Immediate Action is Needed:
Given the number of documented fires and injuries associated with these models, I urge the CPSC to take stronger action against LG. Specifically:
1.	Require LG to issue full replacements, refunds, or a proper repair solution for affected consumers.
2.	Investigate LGs inadequate recall response and whether they are in violation of consumer protection laws.
3.	Warn consumers that LGs recall fix does not eliminate the fire hazard, increasing their liability for future incidents.
I am also filing a complaint with my State Attorney Generals Office and will be pursuing legal options if LG continues to avoid responsibility. Given the growing number of reports of fires, injuries, and property damage, I urge the CPSC to escalate this matter immediately before more people get hurt.
Please confirm receipt of this complaint and advise on the next steps. Thank you for your attention to this urgent consumer safety issue.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to a cat and a serious burn to a person's hand, indicating injury (severity 3). The description mentions multiple instances of accidental activation, suggesting the likelihood is high (4).

incident_description:
In March 2017 we obtained an electric range from Home Depot. We immediately started having problems with the back-left burner becoming extremely hot when the oven was on but the burner itself was off. Myself and other family members have accidentally touched the burner and have obtained burns. This is a design flaw that can lead to serious injury and/or death since it is also a fire hazard.

After burning myself last year I finally decided to report the range to Whirlpool. On March 12, 2024, I sent the following email to Whirlpool (whirlpool_customerexperience@whirlpool.com):

Hello:
Model Number:  WFC150M0EW0  
Serial Number:  R70761680
Date of Purchase: March 2017
Dealers Name: Home Depot
There is a design flaw with the oven that makes using it very dangerous. The oven vents out through the back-left burner such that a pot of water will boil on the burner when the burner is OFF but the oven is on. I am very surprised the oven has not been recalled due to this design defect.
I have burned myself numerous times accidentally on the back burner when the burners were completely turned off and the oven was on because the burner gets too hot; it is easy to forget sometimes to avoid the burner when the oven is on but the burner is off because it is very unusual for burners to get so hot when they are off.  I've also accidentally melted/burned items that were too close to the burner while the oven was on and the burner was off. I have to continuously warn people who use the oven to not touch the back left burner and to make sure nothing is near it so that nothing burns or catches fire.  It is a fire/safety hazard and I am really annoyed with constantly having to worry about it.  I have never had an oven do this before.
Please let me know what can be done about this situation. The oven should be recalled since I can't be the only one experiencing this issue and it is dangerous.  Feel free to call me if you need more information.
Thank you.

In response to the above, I received the following email reply from Whirlpool on April 8, 2024:

Thank you for contacting the Whirlpool Consumer Correspondence Team. We sincerely apologize for the delay in responding to your previous email.
Your particular model and serial number do not fall under any current recalls listed with Whirlpool.
We regret that our Whirlpool Consumer Correspondence team is unable to assist you further with this matter.
If you have any concerns regarding the safety of using this product, we kindly request that you contact our Consumer Care Team by calling (866) 698-2538, Mon - Fri: 8 a.m. - 6 p.m. EST.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
Whirlpool Consumer Correspondence Team
www.whirlpool.com
(866) 698-2538

I contacted the consumer care team at the number provided on 2/7/25 and again explained the situation and that I feel the range is dangerous. A woman who answered took my information and then put me on hold. She never returned to the call and I was left holding for at least 20 minutes before I gave up holding and hung up.

I am getting ready to purchase a new range even though I cannot afford to do so because it is too dangerous to continue using the Whirlpool range I currently have. This model should have a recall and consumers compensated for the oven or provided with a way to prevent the dangerous heating up of the back-left burner. I have used many ranges (electric and gas) over the years and I've never had a range with a burner that gets hot enough to boil water when it is off because of how the oven vents when on.
justification: The incident describes multiple instances of burns from touching the hot burner, indicating injury (severity 3), and the issue is described as recurring and dangerous, making occurrence likely (4).
