The yellow-green oval on the design returned a result of 1.0 mg/cm^2 (on the other hand, the light blue oval on the blue design returned a result of 0.7mg/cm^2. The main users of these plates were a child under 6 years old and their family. The plates were being used to serve and eat food from. The only associated injury I know of related to this plate is this case of lead poisoning. I am worried that others may be poisoned because there are a myriad of listings selling the product secondhand online.
justification: The incident involves lead poisoning from plates used by a child under 6, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to widespread secondhand sales and potential for more cases.

incident_description: The LG Range LDG4315ST	has no safety feature to ensure that there is an active flame once the gas valve for a range top burner after the gas supply is activated and the control knobs are very easy to bump by accident by clothing or by pets etc bumping or walking across the controls. If this happens the gas will flow unchecked leading to unsafe air or worst case gas explosions.  We have bumped the knobs several times and had a pet walk across and turn on the gas supply with no flame. Similar electric stoves from LG have now been recalled for similar knob activation issues, but with electric stoves most of the dangers can be avoided by not leaving anything on the stove. This is not the case for a gas stove where hazard is not excess heat, up until the point there is an explosion. We now always remove the knobs when a burner is not in use.
justification: The incident describes a potential for gas explosions, which can lead to death, and the likelihood is high due to frequent accidental activations.

incident_description:

The label states, "This product contains Stainless Steel (Iron, Chromium, Nickel, Manganese) Formaldehyde, Octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane". Why is this company allowed to sell a product that has Neurotoxins and carcinogens in it?

UPDATED ON 1/27/2025: [Manganese can cause neurological effects, including memory loss, attention problems, and motor skill issues. It can also cause behavioral changes, such as irritability and social withdrawal. Repeated exposure to manganese can cause permanent brain damage, similar to Parkinson's disease. Prolonged exposure to manganese can cause permanent lung damage. Manganese exposure can damage the kidneys, affect the liver and cause anemia, and can impact reproduction. 


Chromium can cause various health effects including respiratory irritation, skin ulcers, lung cancer, stomach ulcers, and damage to the kidneys and liver.


Formaldehyde which leaches into drinking liquids, can cause irritation to the gastrointestinal tract, causing symptoms like stomach upset, nausea, and inflammation, particularly at high concentrations; long-term exposure to significant levels may be linked to increased cancer risk. Ingestion of large amounts of formaldehyde could lead to severe damage to the stomach lining and potentially life-threatening complications. 



Octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane can have adverse effects on the female reproductive system, including changes in the ovaries and uterus, particularly at higher exposure levels. There is a potential for decreased ovary weight, atrophy, and vaginal mucification (the process of epithelial cells changing into mucus-secreting cells).]
justification: The product was not used, so no injury or incident occurred, but the presence of harmful substances raises concerns.

incident_description:
I am reporting this issue because my Samsung stovetop, which has front-facing knobs that turn on too easily, caused a potentially dangerous situation in my home. Despite Samsung acknowledging this defect through a voluntary recall, the issue led to permanent damage to my stovetop and could have resulted in a serious fire or injury. The lack of accountability and transparency in Samsungs response has only added to my frustration, and I want to ensure this is properly addressed.

The product in question is a Samsung gas range with front-facing knobs that have been recalled due to their tendency to turn on with accidental contact. These knobs are extremely sensitive, making it easy to turn the burners on unintentionally.

The stovetop was being used in a standard home setting. On December 13th, during a family gathering, someone unknowingly bumped a knob while placing a [REDACTED] cookie tray on the stovetop. The stove and oven were not in use that evening, and we had followed all of Samsungs safety recommendations prior to this incident, including regularly checking the knobs, ensuring they were off after cooking, and even removing them when the stove was not in use due to prior accidental activations. However, during this event, we had company over, and the knobs were left on the stove.
One person was physically injured as they removed the burning tray from the stove, as well as the incident posing a serious fire hazard. The plastic tray melted completely, turning into liquid on the stovetop. We were lucky that we smelled the burning plastic in time to prevent further damage or a fire. The stovetop itself was permanently damaged, and one of the knobs is now not functioning properly. Given how easily this could have resulted in a fire or serious injury, it is unacceptable that Samsung has closed my claim without resolution despite the known defect.

This incident highlights the ongoing danger of this product, even after Samsungs recall efforts. I am requesting that Samsung take full responsibility and replace my damaged stovetop and defective knobs at no cost. I also urge Samsung to handle claims related to this issue with greater transparency and efficiency to prevent further potential harm to consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in physical injury and significant property damage, with a high potential for a serious fire, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the known defect and previous accidental activations.

I pressed cancel and the clock started showing the time, but the magnetron was still humming. I opened the door and the magnetron stopped. I closed the door and the magnetron started again and the food started to sizzle.

The microwave control panel is not turned on (it just shows the time), there is no program set or running, the interior light is off, and the carousel is not turning. Even the fan that cools the magnetron is not running; only the magnetron is active.  It can be confirmed that the magnetron is engaged by putting food in the microwave and closing the door. The magnetron, and only the magnetron, will turn on and heat the food. Pressing cancel has no effect. Opening the door turns off the magnetron, but it turns back on when you close the door. 

This is a FIRE HAZARD as the microwave has failed in an "ON" state. I have unplugged the microwave and will replace it with a different manufacturer's appliance as I don't trust GE any longer (failed ice maker and water solenoid in the GE refrigerator, failed wash pump, control board, touchpad, door sensor, and drain pump in the GE dishwasher (all different years over 8 years), and now a stuck on magnetron in the GE microwave). Description of Incident:
While using the T-fal 3.5L Deep Fryer with Oil Filtration System, I attempted to pour peanut oil from the oil container using the built-in spout. During this process, the lid of the oil container detached unexpectedly, causing approximately one gallon of peanut oil to spill onto the counter and under the stove. This design flaw created a significant fire hazard, as peanut oil is highly flammable and could have ignited had the stove been on at the time of the spill.

Hazard Description:
The lid of the oil container does not secure tightly enough to withstand the normal use of the spout, leading to a high likelihood of accidental spills. Given that this product is specifically intended for use with flammable oil, the inability of the container to reliably prevent spills poses a serious risk of fire and injury.

Injury Details:
No injuries occurred during this incident. However, the potential for a fire or burns was substantial. Cleaning up the spill was time-consuming and required extensive effort to remove oil from the counter and under the stove.

Recommendation for Resolution:
The product design should be reviewed to ensure the lid secures tightly during use, particularly when pouring oil. Any features that compromise the safety of handling flammable liquids should be re-engineered to prevent similar incidents in the future.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the spill created a significant fire hazard, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: I used the self-cleaning feature on my  Bosch double oven 800 series for the first time ever ten days ago. My top oven was not overly dirty or greasy but I wanted to clean it,  and followed the simple directions in the manual. About an hour into the process  I heard an incredibly loud crash. The internal glass panel on the oven door exploded and shattered into hundreds of tiny shards inside the oven. I immediately turned off the cleaning feature and let it cool down before carefully opening the door.  Some shards of glass fell out onto my floor but most of the shattered glass was contained inside the oven. I was not injured but was badly shaken. It could have been a lot more dangerous if the outer glass panel of the oven door had also shattered since I was standing across from my oven at the kitchen sink when the explosion occurred.  I contacted the store I bought my Bosch oven from and was told that, because my oven was no longer under warranty, I would have to pay over $800 for replacement parts which included new glass and a new oven door.  When I pointed out that this was either a manufacturer's defect or flaw in the glass and Bosch should be held accountable, regardless of whether the warranty was still good, the store contacted Bosch on my behalf. Bosch's response was an immediate rejection.  I then contacted the VP of Consumer Services at Bosch through email but have not heard back.  This dangerous situation of shattering glass and damaging internal ovens due to self-cleaning has happened too many times to people when I researched on the web.  Bosch and other companies need to be held accountable and, at the very least, put warning on the ovens and in their manuals about the potential hazards of using the self-cleaning feature. My hope is that Bosch stands up to its good reputation and credits me for the damages done to my oven.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of the oven's internal glass panel, but no injuries occurred. Research indicates this is a recurring issue with Bosch ovens.

incident_description:
I am a fire investigator for the [REDACTED].  We had an oven / range fire on December 26, 2024.  The summary is as follows:

1.	Called to a house with a stove fire.
2.	We arrived on scene, and Police and homeowners had used ABC extinguishers.  Not sure if that actually put the fire out, or the fuels were consumed.  Regardless, fire was out upon our arrival.
3.	Because of the heat still coming off and out of unit, we disconnected the natural gas line and pulled the unit out of the house, and into their back yard.
4.	The oven door was locked, but with a little prying, we were able to get it to open.  We found a pan that once had either a wooden or plastic handle.  This handle would appear to be what was on fire. 
5.	With a little prying, we were also able to lift the stove top up.  Nothing appeared out of place other than the pan found in the oven.
6.	Interviewing the residents revealed that they had just used the oven to bake a dish.  She had left the door open, and was not aware that the pan was placed inside the oven.  She then used the self clean feature.  This was done by pressing a button on the control panel.  This locked the door electrically.  Then the fire occurred, and they were not able to open the door to put out.  
7.	The residents are new to this house, having lived there for only 1 to 2 months.  They do not have renters insurance, and they owned the oven / range.  The land lord arrived, and they do have insurance.  The only fire related damage appeared to have been contained to the oven / range.  No other damage was noticed inside the kitchen or the rest of the house.  The only damage was dry powder from the ABC extinguishers and smoke smell.
justification: The incident involved a stove fire with no reported injuries or deaths, and damage was limited to the oven/range.

incident_description:
I would like to report a serious and dangerous small appliance malfunction that occurred with a Cuisinart 14-Cup Food Processor (Model DFP-14BCN).

We purchased this food processor just under 6 years ago.  On average, we use it once every other week.  We have had no problems with it in the past.  The appliance sits on a marble countertop with plenty of space around it.  It was plugged in as usual, but it was clearly turned off at the time of the malfunction.  It had last been used 24 hours prior.

During the afternoon of January 6, 2025, the food processor suddenly turned on.  The blade spinning noise was heard by multiple people in the house who went to the kitchen to investigate.  A few seconds later, the appliance started to emit heavy gray smoke and the scent of burning plastic.  We quickly unplugged it and placed it outside in the snow.  While moving the appliance outside, it was noted that the underside metal components were glowing red and sparking.

Afterwards, we checked the standard electrical socket that the appliance was plugged into in the kitchen wall and found no damage or abnormalities.  There was no lightning outside or any other obvious external cause.  No other electrical devices in the house were affected, and no house circuit breakers tripped.

To be frank, if we had not been home at the time, this event could have easily started a house fire.  Luckily there were no injuries.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction with potential for fire, but no injuries occurred and the issue was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,

We bought 4-Door Flex with Family Hub 27.9-cu ft 4-Door French Door Refrigerator with Single Ice Maker (Black) model RF28M9580SG/AA from Lowes for $3,704.05 on 08/14/2017.  We been having nothing but trouble with the ice maker, which started within 2 years of buying. The ice maker keeps over freezing and completely icing up the whole mechanism and harness.  We would constantly have to disable the refrigerator and to defrost it.  In addition, the unit also started to produce mold and mildew.  By the time this started, the warranty was already up. Additionally, the issue was not a hardware issue, but a defect in Samsung refrigerator which they wanted us to pay for them to resolve.  We finally just disabled the ice maker and bought an ice maker.  I am now seeing that the power consumption of the refrigerator started to increase.  I also ran a self-check, but Samsung's self-check says nothing is wrong refrigerator.  It was normally around 46.46 kWh - 54.96 kWh, but in May it began to rise.  It rose from 65.87 kWh to 98.13 kWh as of December 31, 2024.  This made me concerned as to why this was happening.  I was also hearing a louder humming sound coming from the refrigerator, which made me make sure the condenser coil was clean of dust, but no luck.  I also checked behind the triple & metal cooling to make sure it was not frozen.  It was little but was not bad.  I then checked the ice maker, which to my shock, the whole area was frozen even though the ice maker was still disabled.  Therefore, I disabled the refrigerator and unthaw the whole ice maker again.  In addition, I made sure to actually pull out the Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly this time, in the hope it would stop it from causing this issue.  To my dismay, it did not.  So even though the ice maker is disabled, and the Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly is pulled out, the ice maker compartment is still getting iced up.  I think this is a fault in the Samsung refrigerator and I want to bring it to your attention.  I have uploaded some images of the issue but if more is required, please let me know.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator causing inconvenience and increased power consumption, but no injury or death.

incident_description:
My wife and I have been loyal customers of Samsung for several years, and we were excited to purchase the Samsung Electric Range, Model #NE63T8311SS/AA, from Lowes in Delta Park, Oregon, in 2021 as part of our kitchen remodel. However, I am writing today to express my concern over ongoing safety issues we have encountered with this appliance.

While we have generally been satisfied with the performance of the range, we have experienced repeated problems with the front control knobs, which we have found to be highly sensitive and prone to being accidentally bumped. On multiple occasions, these knobs have been unintentionally turned on, leading to the stove burners activating without our knowledge. On one occasion, a plastic cutting board was partially placed on the stove top when a knob was accidentally turned, causing the cutting board to melt and enough smoke to set off our smoke alarms. This incident posed a serious safety hazard, and it is a situation we are very concerned about.

Additionally, one of the knobs recently became loose, and I had to glue it back in place because the knob doesn't fit securely. While we understand that there was a recall on these ranges related to the faulty front knobs, the solution provideda plastic clip for the knobshas proven to be both ineffective and unsightly. The clips frequently fall off when touched, and in some cases, they don't even work properly at all. This temporary solution has not addressed the core safety issue, and the range has continued to present a risk to our home and family.
Given the nature of these ongoing problems and the safety concerns they pose, we are requesting a full replacement of the unit. This range has become a liability in our kitchen, and we believe a replacement is the most effective solution to ensure our peace of mind and safety. We chose this range specifically for our new kitchen, and it is disappointing that it has failed to meet the standards we expected from Samsung.

We kindly request that you review this situation and provide us with a prompt response regarding how to proceed with the replacement. We look forward to a resolution and appreciate your attention to this serious matter.

incident_description:
On December 8, 2019 I purchased a Samsung refrigerator, model number RF263BEAESGAA, for $1,547.00 at Home Depot. I began experiencing issues with the refrigerator during the summer of 2023; the ice maker failed to consistently make ice and kept freezing into a solid mass along with the fan located in the fridge compartment would intermittently emit loud noises 

Around May of 2024, my family and I noticed that the refrigerators  temperature felt consistently warmer than usual. On May 28, 2024, while searching online for information about these ongoing issues with Subject Refrigerator, I learned of the class action against Samsung (along with numerous other product defect related lawsuits against Samsung) regarding the very same problems we were experiencing with our own appliance.
While reading about the litigation, I discovered that Samsung was offering a service call and replacement part, free of charge, to remedy this known defect. I immediately called Samsung, provided my appliances information, and was given a ticket number as confirmation of my upcoming service appointment for the repair and installation of the replacement part.  

Soon after this call, I received a text message from a Samsung representative named [REDACTED] who requested that I send her photos of the refrigerators  ice maker unit.  I tried to upload the photos on the portal website provided by Samsung in its second confirmation email, but I was unable to complete the upload due to errors on the site. After being contacted by Samsung representatives [REDACTED] and [REDACTED], I was finally able to text photos of the fridge and the receipt on June 3, 2024 

Throughout the following weeks, I frequently visited the Samsung customer service portal to check the status of my service request. Each time I visited this site (even on the day of the July 26, 2024 incident) I was met with the same message , which stated: Dear customer, your request has been received and we are in the process of reviewing the submitted documents. You will only be able to access the portal, to send additional documentation, once the documents have been reviewed. Here at Samsung, we pride ourselves in providing customer service nothing short of excellence. Please feel free to reach out to us for status updates or any additional inquiries.

	I continued to check the portal throughout the months of June and July of 2024. In mid-July, my 5-year-old son and I began experiencing bouts of vomiting and diarrhea whenever we would drink something out of the fridge. It got to the point that every time  my son would have a glass of milk, he would vomit violently. On July 26, 2024, I decided to deep clean the Subject Refrigerator and began removing the refrigerators contents. It was then that I discovered that the back panels were iced up. Additionally, water was dripping down the back of the main compartment into the vegetable compartments and pooling under the trays. As I pulled open the trays, water gushed out onto my kitchen floor. Obviously alarmed, I called the phone number listed on my Samsung work order. I explained the current situation to the representative and asked him about the status of my pending service request. To my utter surprise, the representative informed me that my service request was closed out. I asked how it could possibly be closed out since nobody had yet contacted me to schedule the service. According to the website, my documents were still being reviewed. The representative answered that Samsung closed out the request since they could not find a technician available that would complete my service. 
	 I have never heard of a company cancelling out its own work order to remedy a defective product that posed a health and safety hazard. Samsung knew of this products defect, accepted my claim, and was in the process of scheduling a service call for my unit. According to their own portal, my claim was still active. Yet Samsung decided to close out my request and refuse to follow through on the repair without even contacting me about their inability to complete the process. Due to Samsungs negligence in mishandling my repair request, the defective component failed and caused this major issue. I expressed my shock to the Samsung representative and explained that it was currently 105 degrees in my area; thus, I needed my refrigerator repaired as soon as possible. He assured me that he would give me a ticket number to have someone respond to me within 48 hours, who would then arrange a date to inspect the Subject Refrigerator. I reminded him that the last time I followed this procedure, my request was closed out without any notice.  Additionally, since the Subject Refrigerator was flooding and inoperable, I needed to have the service, repair, and/or replacement provided as soon as possible. The Samsung representative gave me the number of the local appliance repair technician to see if I could get them to come to my home earlier due to this emergency situation. 

I immediately called the technician but they informed me that I would be required to pay for the service call and any repairs out of my own pocket. I called Samsung back and they confirmed that they would be charging me to pay for any service calls, fees, and repairs despite the fact that this emergency was caused by their own defective product and their failure to follow through on their previous (and free) service call. When I requested that they provide either a replacement refrigerator or credit toward the purchase of one, Samsung refused. As a result, I had to purchase a small emergency refrigerator, ice, and subsequently a new refrigerator unit. Additionally, all my food in the refrigerator and in the freezer were spoiled and had to be thrown away, approximately $500.00 worth of frozen and fresh food. I have since been attempting to resolve this issue with Samsung but despite filing a [REDACTED] complaint and exchanging numerous phone calls and emails with customer service representatives, I have been unable to do so. Samsung denies that their representative told me during my call on July 26, 2024 that my May 28, 2024 repair request was cancelled on their own volition. As Samsung records all of their calls for quality control purposes, they should be able to find the recording of this conversation. To date, Samsung has only offered to send a technician out to look at my refrigerator, which has been stored in my garage and rendered inoperable since the July 26, 2024 incident.
justification: The incident resulted in vomiting and diarrhea for the individual and their child due to the refrigerator's malfunction, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) as such defects are known but not universal.

I ran into the kitchen and saw smoke billowing from behind the dashboard/panel where the knobs are located.  It smelled like electrical fire and we immediately called our Home Warranty Service ([REDACTED]).  On 26 November 2024, [REDACTED] sent [REDACTED] (2 technicians) to service the oven.  They (the technicians) ran diagnostics test and checked the wiring behind the stove.  Upon completion on their testing they said they did not see anything wrong.  The next day (November 27th) we used the stove top without incident.   Thanksgiving morning (28 November 2024), we (spouse/myself) used the stove went to cook Turkey sausages to cook in the oven.  The turkey sausages were on a  parchment paper-covered pan.   The oven was set at 365 for 30 minutes. In 15 mins., or less the sausages were charred and the  blackened parchment paper crumbled to the touch.  I have never known parchment paper to be reduced to ashes even at 425 degrees or broiling. We reduced the heat to 175 degrees and placed some cornbread in a [REDACTED] glass/dish to warm up.  7-10 minutes later, the cornbread was ash and the heat coming from the oven felt as if the temperature had not been reduced at all.   The oven seems to be heating up at an accelerated temperature and we immediately turned the oven off and unplugged the appliance to avoid a potential fire hazard. incident_description: I was using the Ninja Professional Plus Kitchen System to make smoothies.  I smelled an unusual smell that smelled like something burning. One drank the smoothie; the other said it did not taste good.  When I smelled his smoothie, it smelled like the same burning smell I smelled while making them.  I put water and a few ice cubes in the Ninja smoothie container, put it in the base, and turned it on.  I was shocked to see the water turn blackish with sediments of a black substance.   I am very concerned because one of my sons drank the smoothie that had this substance.  I kept the smoothie container that has the water and black substance, hoping it would be analyzed to determine what it is.   The first week of November, when this occurred,  I immediately contacted the Shark/Ninja company.  The customer representative I spoke with told me they were going to expedite a return call to address my concerns and that I should hear back within two days.  I did not hear back that week.  The following week, I contacted the company again.  Again, I was told they would expediate a response and that I should hear back within two days.  It has now been four weeks, and I have not heard back from anyone at Shark/Ninja.  My concern is that something from the machine entered the container and contaminated the contents of the smoothies I prepared.  I am very concerned that this substance may have entered other food that I have prepared in the unit.  I am also very concerned that this could happen to someone else.  I offered to send my unit and the container that has the water and black substance to Shark/Ninja, but they have been unresponsive.  During the second call, they did offer to send me another unit, but I would never take a chance using this appliance again.  I hope that someone can help determine what this black substance is and whether it could harm my son's health.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a serious safety concern regarding the ice maker in my Samsung refrigerator, Model RF23M8590SR/AA. This issue involves plastic fragments being dispensed with ice, posing a potential health hazard.

Recently, I discovered small plastic fragments in the ice dispensed from the refrigerator. Upon inspection, I found that a plastic component between the ice and the metal crushing arms had broken off. This has happened before; a larger plastic piece broke months ago, but I discarded it and continued using the ice maker as it appeared to function normally. However, this time, the broken plastic was ground into fragments about the size of half a pea, which were dispensed with the ice.

This problem appears to be a design flaw and is not isolated. I found a forum post on Samsungs website where another customer reported the same issue of plastic fragments in their ice. Despite this recurring defect, I have seen no recall or safety warning issued for this product.

I believe this situation warrants immediate investigation by the CPSC. The issue not only endangers the health of consumers but also reflects a potential failure in the products safety design. I kindly request that the CPSC review this matter, determine the extent of the risk, and consider whether a recall or safety advisory is necessary.

Please let me know if additional information or documentation is required to assist with your investigation. Thank you for your attention to this serious matter.
justification: Plastic fragments in ice pose a potential health hazard, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
On 28 September 2024, I purchased from Lowes in Canton, Ohio, and was delivered the Whirlpool range model number WFG535S0LZ, and was professionally installed on 05 October 2024. Upon the trial of my new range, I noticed that one corner of the range was really hot when I preheated the oven. I immediately shut the oven off and tried to see what the issue was. I had then noticed that the oven door was not properly shutting. So I called Whirlpool and set up a service visit. Platinum Factory Service visited my house on 28 October 2024 and replaced the hinges on the range. Afterward, the technician stated that the whole range is defective and is out of specification. The technician then sent the photos to Whirlpool and stated that replacement unit is needed. I contacted Whirlpool a week later and they stated that they call me a week later. A week went by and I contacted Whirlpool again and still did not commit to a replacement, that I needed to work with Lowes for a replacement because Whirlpool stated that is was shipping damage. So I immediately contacted Lowes customer care to remedy the issue. The Lowes had to contact Whirlpool, albeit while I was still on the phone with Lowes, and thats when Whirlpool stated that It was a defective unit and that I needed a replacement. Whirlpool then ordered Platinum Factory Service to deliver a new range. On 17 November 2024, Platinum Factory Service notified me that Whirlpool no longer wanted to provide a replacement. 
In short, Whirlpool sold a defective range/oven that is extremely dangerous and could pose a fire hazard to my house, and is unwilling to replace the unit, violating the Consumer Product Safety Act as well as the state-level Ohio Consumer Product Safety Act.
justification: The incident involved a defective range posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We bought a condo which included a Bosch Side by Side, built in refrigerator and ice maker.  The prior owner bought the unit new and never occupied it, so the refrigerator was turned on, but never used in day-to-day service.  The problem I am reporting is that the ceramic water line to the ice maker has disintegrated, causing minute ceramic debris particles to flow into the water that is becoming ice.  The ice is unusable and unsafe.  The line is surrounded by foam insulation from the manufacturer, so it is not accessible and cannot be replaced.  The disintegration of the line is a defect that was not caused by misuse.  There is no access to the line and no situation of operating use of the line that could cause line to fracture and disintegrate the way it did.  The problem was discovered by an independent repair technician.  The problem was masked by other defects in the freezer, which included a disconnected (severed) wire that should have powered a fan in the freezer.  Because the fan did not work, the ice maker never functioned because there is a temperature controller that prevents operation of the ice maker when the ambient temperature in the freezer exceeds a preset temperature.  A BSH approved servicer attempted to repair the fan problem and after several unsuccessful repair attempts, declared the unit to be not serviceable.  I sought a replacement of the refrigerator.  Bosch advised me that the unit was out of warranty, but they would offer me $1,484.85 against the purchase of a new $9,899 replacement unit.  Since the replacement unit cost and installation far exceeds BSH offer, I sought an independent repair.  That repair person was able to fix the wiring issue and restore normal fan function, but then discovered that the ceramic water line was disintegrating and that it could not be replaced and represented a safety hazard as pieces broke off and flowed into the ice.  We have not used the ice and so have not been injured, but anyone with this refrigerator and this problem would not know that foreign bodies are flowing into the ice and so this is a danger to consumers.  I have other Bosch products, and have a Bosch refrigerator in another dwelling, and typically Bosch makes a quality product.  I am confounded by how this issue happened and why this refrigerator presented with problems that neither repair person had seen in their careers.
justification: The incident involves a defective water line contaminating ice, but no injuries have occurred as the ice was not consumed.

incident_description:
Purchased Jenn Air Noir Gas Range in June 2021.  It was delivered in October 2021.  The knobs appeared to be metal, however, the stem that attaches the knob to the stove is plastic.  The stem extending from the range is metal.  As the range stem is steel, it gets very hot while using the stove causing the plastic knob stem to splay/strip/melt due to heat.  I contacted ABT while the range was under warranty and new knobs were sent.  However, the new knobs also had plastic stems which subsequently melted and splayed causing the same issue.  Recently, my 17-year-old niece used the stove, when she finished she turned to the knob to the "OFF" position.  Unbeknownst to her the stove was still on as the plastic knob stem had melted and was stripped. While it appeared that the knob was turned to the "OFF" - it was still on.  I have spent hours on the phone.  I contacted the JennAir safety department and I was sent one replacement knob.  To-date, I have replaced 5 knobs. 

A technician from Diamond Factory Service was sent out by the JennAir Safety Team and I was informed that JennAir had been notified of this safety issue and that Product Managers have been onsite during service calls and personally witnessed said hazards.  It was said that Jenn Air product engineers/managers routinely ignored known safety hazards that they refuse to address safety issues despite known fire and gas hazards.  Using plastic parts against metal stems is inherently defective.  An oven not closing also constitutes a hazard.  

This range has defects that pose serious safety hazards and should be recalled. The knobs and oven closure mechanism are both defective and should be replaced.  Alternatively, If I cannot safely use this appliance without risk of injury or death, I would like a refund.  I would be open to a replacement provided the replacement does not contain the plastic interior parts.
justification: The incident involves a stove that fails to turn off due to melted plastic knobs, posing a fire and gas hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Reason for Report:

I am filing this report due to a persistent defect with the door handles on my Amana refrigerator, model AS12175GRSO4, which poses a significant safety hazard. This issue has occurred repeatedly over several years, despite the companys knowledge and multiple replacement attempts, yet the defect remains unresolved.

What Happened:

Since purchasing my Amana model AS12175GRSO4 refrigerator, the handles have consistently developed deep cracks, particularly in the plastic component that attaches the handle to the refrigerator door. This defect has manifested multiple times, leading me to report it directly to Amana. While they initially acknowledged the issue by replacing the handles several times, each replacement has developed the same cracking problem without prolonged use. We intentionally avoid using these handles due to the known risk, opting instead to open the refrigerator from a notch at the top of the door. Despite this precaution, the handles continue to crack and deteriorate.

The plastic portion of the handle, which covers the area connecting to the door, eventually breaks down and detaches in sharp shards. The first time this happened, my daughter nearly stepped on these shards in the middle of the night, which could have caused serious injury. I have found small pieces scattered on the floor, indicating that the plastic cracks across multiple sections of the handle and can detach unpredictably. Currently, my refrigerator handles have developed severe cracks, and I am concerned that pieces may soon detach.

Safety Hazard and Companys Response:

This ongoing defect, combined with the risk of sharp plastic fragments detaching, represents a serious safety hazard, especially during night-time or low-light conditions. The company, Amana, has been made fully aware of this hazard on several occasions, yet has failed to provide a safe, long-term solution. They have refused to replace the handles further or offer any alternative design that could avoid this issue, despite my repeated requests. Their lack of action despite knowing the risk of potential harm suggests a disregard for the safety of their customers.

Although no injuries have occurred yet, the risk remains substantial, and I am filing this report in hopes of finally addressing this defective component before it leads to harm.
justification: The incident involves a persistent defect with potential for injury, but no actual injuries have occurred yet, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the repeated failures.

incident_description: A Jenn-air range model JDS1750FS1 was installed by a certified installer.  The range is very dangerous.  The 2 front burners are 4.25 inches wide and 17,000 BTU. incident_description:
Introduction
At precisely 7 AM on a seemingly serene Sunday morning, an unusual and alarming occurrence shattered the peaceful atmosphere of my household. While the majority of my family enjoyed the blissful slumber that only a weekend can provide, my youngest son and I were jolted awake by a thunderous explosion emanating from the kitchen. This report chronicles the events that unfolded and the subsequent implications on our culinary endeavors.The Incident
Upon hearing the deafening bang, my son and I exchanged bewildered glances that could only be interpreted as a shared understanding of impending chaos. We raced to the kitchen, adrenaline pumping, only to discover that our Frigidaire glass stove door had spontaneously shattered into a million glittering pieces. Remarkably, the stove was off, unutilized, and decidedly cool to the touch. Investigating the Phenomenon
In my quest for answers, I turned to the all-knowing entity we call the internet. Much to my astonishment, I uncovered a nationwide trend: the Frigidaire glass stove doors were apparently revolting against their mundane existence. Reports indicated that these doors were shattering like they were auditioning for a role in a dramatic film, leaving countless families in a state of culinary disarray. The Diet Dilemma
While one might surmise that a spontaneous kitchen explosion could serve as a divine intervention in my ongoing battle with weight, I must firmly reject the notion that my appliances should take matters into their own handsor, in this case, glass shards. As I embark on my journey to replace the stove door, I am faced with the pressing issue of how to feed a family of six without the luxury of a functioning stove.Alternative Culinary Solutions
In light of this unexpected predicament, I propose the following strategies to keep my family nourished:Microwave Marvels: The trusty microwave stands ready to assist. Frozen meals, leftover pizza, and popcorn can provide sustenance, albeit with a side of guilt for not utilizing the stove.Grill Mastery: If weather permits, I can channel my inner grill master. A backyard barbecue may not only salvage our meals but also provide an opportunity for family bonding over charred hot dogs and burnt burgers.Salad Extravaganza: Embracing a healthy diet (ironically, aided by the exploding stove), I can pivot to gourmet salads. Who knew that lettuce could be so versatile? Cold Sandwiches: The classic sandwich reigns supreme. With a variety of deli meats, cheeses, and toppings, I can craft meals that require zero cookingperfect for the chaos of a shattered kitchen.Conclusion
In conclusion, while the spontaneous explosion of the Frigidaire glass stove door was an unexpected and alarming event, it has inadvertently encouraged creativity in our meal planning. With a bit of ingenuity and humor, my family will navigate this culinary crisis until the stove door can be replaced. Rest assured, the kitchen appliances have not won this round!
justification: The stove door shattered but no one was injured, and the incident is part of a known trend with Frigidaire stoves.

Their warranty is non-transferrable, and requires the consumer to pay a $150 shipping fee, and manage the shipping of the product to a qualified technician for repair, when the warranty is in effect. Individuals hard of hearing or in other areas of the home while the unit is in use may not hear the popping sounds of the arcing and fires may occur quickly and easily.

incident_description:
Dear Sir/ma'am:
I bought a new Samsung refrigerator on 5/26/24 and it was delivered on 5/31/24 (Model# RF23BB86004MAA - 04 and Serial number 1HM643AX300041L). Since 9/1/24 we have been having issues with the fridge not making ice cubes. 

I contacted Samsung for the first time on 9/10/24 for help and I was directed to read the manual and since we have reverse osmosis filters, I was told that the lack of water pressure was due to our filter. I called the reverse osmosis installer, and they came to the house and checked the water pressure and the pressure from the filters to the fridge was correct. On 9/18/24 I called Samsung again and this time I was recommended to buy Samsung DA67-02270A Cap-Support Filter. I bought the caps and waited over a week to receive them. I received them around Friday September 27th. The caps didn't fit our unit (the caps are not made for our fridge model). I decided to go buy a fridge water filter and install it with the hope that the fridge made ice. That weekend we went out of town and came back Sunday 29th and the freezer had defrosted, and the fridge top part was in the mid 60's, but the panel was showing that the inside temperature was 36 degrees. We had to throw away all the food that went bad. My son received a liver transplant in August, and he needs to keep his medications and insulin refrigerated and we had to dispose of those as well.
I contacted Samsun again Monday 30th. Samsung sent a contractor on Tuesday October 1st to make a diagnostic of the issue. The technician found that the evaporator and condenser were not working. incident_description:
I own a GE Profile Ice maker, model UNC15NJII. That's the model number on the receipt, but the model plate inside the unit says UNC15NJBII. I bought it in April 2020 from Home Depot. It is a built-in ice maker installed under an island in our kitchen and is regularly cleaned and the ice is used for consumption all the time.

On Sep 25th 2024 I did a routine cleaning and noticed a fine gray substance in the bottom of the ice bin and along the lip that the ice slides over as it is produced. At first I thought this was mold or similar, and scrubbed it up with an abrasive sponge and paper towels. I could not get all of the gray material off the bin; there is still a "stain" of a gray line running around the perimeter of the bin near the bottom. However when I restarted the ice maker and observed the first pieces of ice falling from the hopper, I noticed black material suspended in the ice nuggets. I assumed again this was mold that may have somehow made its way into the machine. I unplugged the machine to try to further investigate. When that ice melted, I wiped up the black stuff, and realized on my paper towel that it was sparkling like some kind of metal. I got a magnet and confirmed it was metal shavings. Similarly, the very fine gray material that I had on a paper towel was also magnetic in nature. 

I tested this myself several times. When starting the ice maker with an empty bin from an empty tank, the first ice will have the most coarse shavings, and progressively the ice gets more clear, with the worse ice settling to the bottom of the bin where people are less likely to scoop it in most situations. However, the very fine gray metallic powder did coat the entire bin, which makes me suspect that the metal is always present, just to different degrees of fineness.

It is not clear for how long this ice maker has been embedding metal in the ice, whether coarse or fine, but it was an alarming discovery. The ice auger assembly is sealed and I didn't want to pop it open and void my warranty. So I contacted GE, who told me it was out of warranty for this type of failure, but that they'd send someone to look at it for free as it was considered a safety issue. The following Monday, a tech from a local authorized GE servicer ([REDACTED] Appliance) came by and reproduced the issue himself, again using a magnet to observe the metal shavings that were embedded in the ice.

After the tech left, he spoke to GE who advised that he would need to replace several parts in the machine at my expense. The parts alone were almost $3,000, nearly the cost of a new unit, and the tech suggested I pursue a claim through my Home Depot extended warranty instead. In the meantime I contacted GE's social media to let them know about the issue, with photos and videos. GE's social media team offered me a $400 coupon to help recover some of the parts cost. I refused that, and insisted it was a serious safety issue that should be investigated. Ultimately, they have agreed to replace the unit with a slightly newer revision. However I do not know whether the new unit has changed anything about the design, and I'm very concerned that GE Profile ice makers may have a design flaw that is resulting in the widespread consumption of metal particulate in water ice.

I cannot say for certain whether direct injury has occurred. I did get an MRI recently and, as far as I know, my stomach didn't explode with shrapnel, but I'm genuinely concerned for anyone who may consume the first ice of a batch when the shavings seem to be more coarse. I also suspect that machines that have been in service for longer may well show significantly more wear to the internal assemblies and thus more metal may be present.
justification: The incident involves metal shavings in ice, but no direct injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:

incident_description:
I am writing as a consumer of a Samsung smooth top electric slide in range/oven. Model NE63T811AA   (which I purchased online on the Samsung website, boy was that a mistake!) I bought this oven September 28, 2023, it was delivered to my home October 3, 2023. I was about to leave my home on November 13 and I heard crackling on the top of my stove and a silicone pad from my microwave was on top of the glass and caught fire and we don't even know how the stove got turned on!  I put a claim into Samsung, they sent technicians out, they cleaned off the top of the stove (not completely since two spots are now permanent) and I told them the stove is faulty because as soon as your body leans against a knob, it turns on!  

I did some research, and noticed online there's a class action suit against them for this very reason and still they would not exchange the appliance! I wrote emails, I contacted different departments of Samsung and nothing! I even contacted the [REDACTED] and they tried to work it out with Samsung and still nothing.  In addition, I had another fire on 8/27/24! My 17 yo son brought the groceries in and put the bag on top of the stove for a moment, must have leaned on a knob and again a fire! I called 911, the fire department came since my whole kitchen and living room were filled with smoke and I wanted to have it documented for Samsung. All I had asked was for them to replace my stove with one that has the knobs on the rear of the unit. THEY WILL NOT DO IT!    Oh, and one thing I forgot to mention They put out a voluntary email August 21 admitting that the knobs are too easily turned on and they would send out free knob locks or knob covers, depending on the model! I received the locks in the mail and they are just little plastic pieces that go over the top so that you can't turn the knob. I don't know about any of you,  but when I spend $800 on an appliance, I don't want to have to put a piece of plastic over the front to fix a mechanical mistake that the company is aware is a MECHANICAL DEFECT ON THEIR PART! 

An inspector came out, was on the phone with Samsung for 20 min,  took some photos of the damage, and they won't even send somebody out to try and fix the damage on the glass top. Once again they have closed my claim! I bought a Samsung stove because I have their refrigerator, their microwave and several televisions and thought that they were a good company and would stand behind their product!! Boy was I wrong!
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by the stove turning on accidentally, leading to property damage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

We found out about the fire because the next day, Tuesday, September 3, 2024 we witnessed their semi-annual kitchen hood test & inspection. Our Battalion Chief that witnessed the inspection looked up the business on [REDACTED] and found the picture. The Battalion Chief reported the fire to me. On Wednesday, September 4, 2024 I spoke with the business owner about their fire.
[REDACTED], owner of [REDACTED], told me that the oil in the electric fryer started to boil. The fryer was set at 300 degrees Fahrenheit. [REDACTED] stated that her husband [REDACTED] reached over the fryer to turn the knob to off. [REDACTED] stated that the temperature and off knob just spun and did not turn off the fryer. [REDACTED] stated that her husband then unplugged the fryer and that is when the oil caught fire. [REDACTED] used an ABC fire extinguisher to put the fire out.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was extinguished without injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the described equipment malfunction and human error.

incident_description:
SHARP SMC1452CH Carousel 1.4cuft 1100 watt Microwave purchased mid-2020 from Lowes. Home Improvement.   At least twice in past year magnetron continues to operate and heat food after timer stops after turntable stops and after interior light goes out creating risk of fire if user is  unaware of continued heating in the dark microwave or has left the area.   

Microwave was set on half power and 4mins to reheat 2nd portion of pre-packaged cardboard tray of [REDACTED] chicken cobbler.  Saran Wrap was over unsealed original clear food covering and cardboard tray.  Started micro left area for 9 mins and returned to micro still buzzing loudly, timer had stopped, time of day displayed and interior was dark.  This time was able to take video of magnetron buzzing, dark interior and pressing keypad STOP button several times without result.   Video also shows door opening with Saran Wrap covering raised by steam at 3inch height over food tray with lots of steam and/or smoke rolling out of micro.   Photo of food tray shows original clear cover and sticker melted away/ burned off due to heating malfunction.  
Not in video: Closing the door caused the magnetron buzzing to restart yet keypad had not been pressed, interior was dark and turntable did not rotate.   Interior bulb lights normally before and after malfunction.  

Micro must be unplugged and wait couple mins so the keypad functions again.  It appears the internal electronics and/or door latch malfunction intermittently.

Second issue: Since purchased new in 2020 the micro door is difficult to pull open as the latch is very tight.  Latch is so tight the microwave pulls forward an inch or so each time door handle is pulled.   This creates risk of burns due to spills when a heated liquid is inside micro.
justification: The microwave malfunction poses a fire hazard and risk of burns, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
In November of 2022 I purchased FRIGIDAIRE Gallery 27.8 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator in Black Stainless Steel (Model#:GRFS2853AD1). About 9 months later in August 2023I noticed that this refrigerator gave me a warning that the freezer's temperature is higher than it supposed to be and since it was under 1 year manufacturing warranty, I call Frigidaire, and they made an appointment with a local technician. 
The first technician came sometime in late August or early September and after checking this refrigerator, he said that this unit has a sealant leak and since he has not a license to do that type of work, someone else will come later. And about 2 weeks later a new technician came. He said that this unit had a leak somewhere but was not able to identify where it was leaking, so he filled the unit with a refrigerant and added some type of leak detector and said that he would come later to check it again, but never showed up. But since the refrigerator was working correctly, I was not worried about it until of June 2024 when I had the same issue again.
I called Frigidaire and told them that the issue reappears and since it was not fixed properly the first time, they should fix it and the lady from support services said that I have to not worry, and they will send a new technician to fix it properly this time.
The first technician came in June of 2024 and said that there is a leak somewhere he is not able to identify, and he will send a report to Frigidaire and someone from Frigidaire will contact me within 2 business days. After 3 days of waiting, I called Frigidaire again to find out what they should do and the lady said that the technician did not provided them with a detailed explanation and what parts needed and they will send another technician. 
Sometime in July there is another technician came and he said the same thing that he is not able to identify where is a leak is and another technician with a license to fix sealed units will come and fix the problem.
On August 27, 2024, another technician came ([REDACTED] from [REDACTED]) and said that the unit has internal leak in the cabinet itself and he will not be able to fix it, he said that since refrigerant is a flammable I am not able to use this refrigerator anymore and disconnect it. I asked him to send me details and he text me the following notes:
"[REDACTED] Found internal leak in cabinet. Pressure tested to 150 PSI and bubble checked every external joint. No bubbles presented. Previous company added dye for leak detection - no dye visible in freezer or in rear cabinet. Contacted Frigidaire and was notified this is not covered under the sealed system warranty - warranty is 1 year. NOT REPAIRABLE."
I called Frigidaire the same day to find out what are the next steps, and the lady said that they have not received the notes from the technician and someone from Frigidaire will contact me from 24 to 48 hours.
Since I have not received any phone call, on August 30, 2024, I call them myself and the person from Frigidaire said that the unit is not under the warranty and Frigidaire will not do anything.
I would like to report a fraud from Frigidaire and for unsafe product with possibility of fire, since leak was never found and as [REDACTED] technician said refrigerant is Flammable, so all these 2 years my family was live in unsafe environment with possibility of Fire.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning refrigerator with a potential fire hazard due to a refrigerant leak, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Today (8/27/2024) my LG electric stove top (Model: LRE30755ST, SN: 602KMDS00066) was being used on a low setting with a large pot of stock on it to simmer for a few hours, lid closed.  Next thing I know the stock is boiling over so I remove the pot from the burner.  The setting of my burner was set to 1.4 (very low on these units) but the burner was continuously on and not cycling on/off as it normally does, very hot.  I attempted to turn the burner off from the control panel but that did not work so I went to my circuit breaker to trip the breaker open while I dealt with the mess.  After some time, I tested to see if this was still an issue by closing the breaker again but the burner immediately turned back on without me pushing the on button on the control panel. 

This is the second time I've experienced this.  The first time, back in 2017, was a very similar situation described above.  During that time I came across a recall that LG had for this issue (see: https://www.lg.com/us/public-notices/general/lg-electric-range-recall-for-repair).  They scheduled the stove to be repaired free of cost and the technician replaced a circuit board on the back panel of the stove.  I was told this would fix the issue but it seems that it only actually delays this from happening again for some time. I've now experienced this twice and am thankful I have not had a house fire or something severe happen.   Please note that no injuries occurred during either time but easily could have considering it wouldn't take much if someone were to panic trying to clear the stove while it is still on.  

The reason I'm making this report is because there doesn't seem to be any attempt from LG to actually fix the issue but rather just swapping out a part until it happens again.  The recall information in the link above instructs consumers to stop using it until the free in-home repair can be done but I've had the repair done and the issue still occurred again.  My understanding is that this repair was a replace in kind and that no design changes or other fixes were made to the board.  I can't believe a company would simply replace the hardware without correcting the issue knowing full well that this is a huge safety risk for it's consumers.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that could lead to injury or fire, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
My husband and I bought a brand newly built house in June 2023 that came with a new Frigidaire dishwasher. [Product identification tag shows manufacturer as Electrolux Home Products, Inc., Charlotte, NC 28262; Serial # TH30978187; Model # FFID2426TS6A]. We began using the new dishwasher starting at the end of August 2023 when we moved into the house. We regularly smelled an odor of burning plastic when using the dishwasher but could never identify the root cause, which was not evident. In the past 7 to 10 or 12 days, the dishwasher began leaking from the base of it when operating. We tried to troubleshoot and were unable to determine the cause. Today, our home's builder came out to help troubleshoot the dishwasher. He found that water was leaking from the dishwasher when it was operating, and observed water falling on the floor (after the dishwasher's front low kick plate was removed). After further testing, the builder and I noticed that one section of the heating element inside the dishwasher at the base of the appliance, was touching and in direct contact with the dishwasher's interior plastic in one section, had melted the plastic, and the heating element was fused to the plastic. This is a very dangerous condition and could have caused a fire. As it is, the leaking water from the dishwasher, has caused water damage to a section of our new home's hardwood floors, causing a section of the floor to swell up, lift, and separate from other boards. With our Builder, we cut off the power to the dishwasher and the water supply line and have stopped using the dishwasher effective today and henceforth. This Frigidaire brand dishwasher manufactured by Electrolux Home Products, is a danger anywhere it has been sold.
My husband did a [REDACTED] search today after we discovered this issue, and found that Electrolux was sued under a class action in U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina on or around November 15, 2012 by lead Plaintiffs [REDACTED] and that, "...Electrolux designed, manufactured, and marketed dishwashers...that contain a serious and dangerous defect, putting many of its customers in harm's way."
As consumers with no prior knowledge, ownership or use of a Frigidaire dishwasher prior to purchasing this new house in June 2023, we are shocked that there is prior legal precedent about dangerous Electrolux dishwashers from 12 years ago.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous condition with the dishwasher that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the prior legal precedent and the described malfunction.

I contacted Samsung in chat, one person said I could exchange the unit at Lowe's. I called Lowe's and spoke with the manager, who said Samsung would need to give me an RA number in order to return. Lowes didn't give me anything with the 2 day return window, and told me I'd have to buy their extended warranty to return it and lose the price I paid as it is not transferable. I have seen similar issues with this brand/model since having an issue, that didn't show up before I purchased. Samsung had a post as far back as 2016, yet deleted the comments about the refrigerator not cooling. Reddit is full of the same complaints. I don't have the money, nor the space to buy a new refrigerator again. Samsung claims they can send someone out tomorrow instead of a week from yesterday, (somehow, they magically had someone available), I have requested this person wear a mask in my home, as I am immunocompromised. Samsung went back on their initial word that I could exchange, and now say I must wait to see what the technician says. This refrigerator doesn't keep a constant temp at all. I have added two temp probes to measure the air temp.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain proper temperature poses a risk to perishable goods, but no injury or death is reported. Similar complaints suggest this issue is likely to occur.

incident_description:

incident_description:
I chose to report my case for many reasons, but two in particular. First, since Samsung has finally announced only a recall on one style of their cooktop stoves, I believe consumers have the right to know that Samsung is aware that this design flaw is not limited to the stoves with the knobs on the front of the oven exclusively. My stove had them on the back panel, and they were the source of the fire that destroyed my entire home. 
The second reason I am reporting this situation is that even though I was not in the house at the time of the fire, I suffered profoundly. I waited things out, thinking they would get better once normalcy returned to my life, but none of my post-traumatic stress, depression, emotional/physical stress, or anxiety has improved. I have developed ADHD from this traumatic event and OCD. Furthermore, I have medical problems still being investigated, with the possibility of having a relationship between them and the exposure to the smoke and the carcinogens in the air at my home after the fire. Additionally, my daughter, who was 18 at the time, has experienced her own set of emotional demons over this day.
On Monday, August 15, 2022, my daughter and I were getting things packed for her first year of college. She was leaving in just four days to attend the welcome weekend. I tell you this because my tiny home had trunks and boxes stacked wherever we could find a place for them so that we could load the car more easily. So, you can picture it better; my quaint home was 990 square feet, with a cape cod design. The floor plan was two bedrooms upstairs; one was my daughter's room, and the other was my office. Downstairs was the living room on one side of the house, and off the other side of the home was a dining room and kitchen that was opened 98% of the way, with only a little breakfast bar separating the two rooms. Down the small hallway was a bathroom and a bedroom. There was also a flight of stairs in the hallway that went to the basement and garage. 
In my dining room was an [REDACTED], set to "on guard" / "away." I had a [REDACTED] in the downstairs bedroom, which I used as a baby monitor for my granddaughter, who visited earlier that morning. I had [REDACTED] monitor the rooms in both the living room and my office upstairs. I was informed by a few firefighters and the fire chief that the first 911 call was from a security system or my [REDACTED]. I did not know that was possible, but I do know that my [REDACTED] noted the sound of an explosion and recorded the audio of the fire bellowing in my home.
Before the day of the fire, the stove was bought at Lowes nine months earlier. I still have the stove in my possession because I firmly believe it needs to be investigated further, and Samsung needs to be held accountable for the pain and suffering they have caused me, along with how they have destroyed my future! Additionally, a few weeks before the fire, this new stove's LED screen began to glitch for an unknown reason. Now, finally, here are the details of what happened that day. That morning, my daughter and I watched my granddaughter, who was one year and three months old at the time. She stayed for a couple of hours, and then she went home. My daughter and I were exhausted after chasing her, so we decided to nap. When we got up late afternoon, we noticed that the electricity must have gone out briefly because all the clocks were blinking. (The fire marshal verified this information) My daughter ate leftovers that required no reheating, so the cooktop was not used, and I decided that I was going to run some last-minute errands for college things. My daughter and I left our home with our cat, exotic parrot, German Shepherd, Australian Shepherd, Border Collie, and Shokri and drove 4.7 miles to the store. That's when I got a phone call from my neighbor who said smoke was coming from my house. "A LOT OF SMOKE!" My daughter and I got right back in the car and headed home. Halfway back, we were passed by firetrucks heading to my house from another municipality. By the time I reached my street, we were gone only 30 minutes total from when we first left, but there were already seven fire companies missing animals, and the house was a complete loss. 
This fire was investigated extensively, and there was no disputing that the stove was the cause. No one can say for sure how the stove caused it since I know I did not use it, nor did my daughter. One investigator said it was on. The other said he thought it was bumped by one of my large dogs jumping up at the stove and pushing something into it. Either way, the stove, an inanimate object, had destroyed my past, present, and future.
justification: The incident resulted in significant emotional and physical stress, along with potential long-term health effects from smoke exposure, but no direct injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a serious safety concern with a Samsung dishwasher, as well as multiple product failures from the same manufacturer. I have attempted to resolve this issue directly with Samsung, and through the [REDACTED], but have not received a satisfactory response addressing my safety concerns.

Key points of my complaint:

1. Safety Hazard: My Samsung dishwasher's bottom rack is melting during the heated dry cycle, posing a potential fire risk and safety hazard.

2. Multiple Product Failures: I purchased a Samsung refrigerator, dishwasher, and TV simultaneously. All three products began experiencing issues shortly after the standard one-year warranty expired.

3. Inadequate Response: Samsung has refused to address the safety concern or consider the exceptional circumstance of multiple product failures from the same purchase period.

4. Customer Service Issues: Samsung denied any accommodation or goodwill service for out-of-warranty products, despite the unusual nature of the situation and the potential safety risk.

5. Lack of Escalation: I was informed that there are no further escalation options beyond the initial customer service representative.

I have photographic evidence of the melting dishwasher rack, which I can provide upon request. I am deeply concerned about the safety implications of continuing to use this appliance, as well as the apparent quality control issues affecting multiple Samsung products.

I am seeking assistance in:
1. Addressing the immediate safety concern with the dishwasher.
2. Investigating whether this is a widespread issue affecting other consumers.
3. Encouraging Samsung to take appropriate action to resolve these concerns.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response and any guidance you can provide.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a melting dishwasher rack posing a potential fire risk, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Whirlpool needs to immediately recall and provide safe replacements for their microwave Model WMC50522H. 
It poses a fire risk.  After using the microwave, I noticed a humming sound as if the microwave was running.  However, the clock was showing the current time, the cooking timer was not on, and the microwave light was not on as it is while heating food.  I opened the door and the humming stopped.  I heated a food item by setting a cook timer and pressing start and it heated appropriately for the set time (with the light on, turntable rotating, and cooking timer counting down).  Upon removing the food and shutting the door, the humming sound started again.  I placed food in the microwave and simply shut the door (without pressing a cooking timer or start) and immediately the food started heating and smoking despite the microwave only showing the clock, lights off, and turntable not moving.  The microwave was not set to heat food, but it was heating food.  Now, the only way to prevent the microwave from running is to keep the door open. This is not a good option as the light remains on and becomes warm  (plus, who wants to leave their microwave door open when not in use?).  Whirlpool needs to fix this problem immediately and offer replacements.  A quick [REDACTED] search shows that this is not an isolated problem and others have experienced the exact same issue.  Please remedy asap.  Thanks!
https://www.whirlpool.com/kitchen/cooking/microwaves/countertop/p.2.2-cu.-ft.-countertop-microwave-with-1,200-watt-cooking-power.wmc50522hz.html
justification: The microwave poses a fire risk and can start heating food without user input, which is a significant safety hazard. While no injury is reported, the potential for harm is high.

incident_description: The recently announced recall on [REDACTED] electric ranges with front-mounted control knobs [REDACTED] should include gas models as well.  I have had a Samsung gas range (model NX58M9420S) for 6 years, and we frequently accidentally turn burners on or, worse, turn the gas on without it being ignited, just by bumping the front-mounted knobs.  The knobs appear to have the same design as those on the electric models. While this has not resulted in a fire or injury in my home, I see no reason the current recall should be limited only to the electric models when the same issue exists on the gas models.

incident_description: On multiple occasions, I have unintentionally turned the knob to the on position on our Samsung gas stove. Sometimes it is only on enough to where gas is being released, others it is turned enough to release gas and start the igniter. The burner has produced fire some of the times the igniter was started. This happens quite often by simply bumping into or leaning on the knob. It has also happened with our teenagers. If the igniter is not started, there is no sound and natural gas is released into our home until the knob is turned to the off position. The only reason we know it is happening is the blue light that comes on around the knob. If this ever happens when there is no electricity,  such as during natural disasters or other power outages, we may not be aware that natural gas is being released in our home. This could lead to carbon monoxide poisoning, fire, and death. So far we have been lucky and noticed when the stove has been turned on unintentionally and no injuries have occurred.
justification: The incident involves unintentional gas release with potential for severe outcomes, but no injuries have occurred so far.

I try not to cook on it and will never buy a Samsung again.  You need to replace these stoves.  At the hospital we wonder why you would make such a product.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung 30 Inch 6.3 Cu. Ft. Slide-In Induction Range with Self Cleaning, in Black Stainless, in November of 2022.  Model Number is NE63B8211SG. 
 Our house was being renovated at the time, so scheduled the delivery for January of 2023.  Withing the first month, we had 2 fires, where a stovetop burner was inadvertantly turned on, and also a 3rd fire a few months later.  Shortly after delivery of the new range, during construction, a worker had placed some cardboard on the stovetop to protect it from dust and paint.  He evidently had brushed up against one of the front-mounted control knobs, activating one of the burners.  We had moved to the back of the house for some work, when we all smelled smoke, and the smoke alarm went off.  We ran to the kitchen and the fire was blazing!   We immediately put it out.  Thinking it was our fault, we did not report the issue.  And yet, a few weeks later, I had purchased a stovetop protector matt to cover the stovetop and protect it from anything set on the glass top.   It too ended up catching fire!  So we made sure not to put anything on top of the range.  However, a few months later, my girlfriend laid some curtains out on the countertop next to the range, close enough that when yet again, one of the burners was inadvertant activated, another fire ensued.  We are so fortunate that our home did not burn to the ground during one of these incidents.
justification: The incident involved multiple fires caused by inadvertent activation of burners, but no injuries or deaths were reported.
