incident_description:
On January 27, 2021, I purchased a JennAir refrigerator at a cost of $9,399.00 from Build.com.  This JennAir refrigerator was a panel ready refrigerator meaning it did not come with the refrigerator doors or the freezer door.  I purchased JennAir refrigerator doors and a JennAir freezer door to this refrigerator at an additional cost of $1,999.00.  These were all JennAir doors.  I had the refrigerator installed by a certified JennAir technician.  The model numbers are as follows:
	Refrigerator - JF42NXFXDE   	Doors (3) - JBFFS42NHL
I have attached a copy of the JennAir installation instructions.  The technician that I used to put the doors on followed the JennAir instruction sheet and used JenAir supplied X6 phillips head screws (4 on each side). The refrigerator was not delivered until approximately May 14, 2021 and was installed sometime in June 2021.
The freezer door (pictures of which are attached) which is made of stainless steel is a very heavy door and the handle is at the very top of the door as seen.  I am providing you with a video of my wife opening both the refrigerator doors and the freezer door.  You can see that the refrigerator doors open very easily (with 1 finger).  However, the freezer door must be pulled very, very hard to get it open.
On July 4, 2024, a 10 year old boy who was at my home to celebrate the 4th, pulled the freezer door open to get an ice cream and the freezer panel actually came off and almost fell on his foot.  If it had, more than likely it would have broke or crushed his foot.  I don't know if JennAir has had other complaints about this problem.  I asked them and they would not disclose that information.
The outside stainless steel freezer panel is held onto the inside permanent freezer panel by 4 small wood screws (x6)  on each side as you can see from the photos.  These are very small wood screws and when the boy pulled on the door the screws stripped out of the wood and fell in front of him.  I am attaching pictures of the freezer panel after it fell off of the permanent freezer panel.  You can see from the pictures and the installation instructions that these small screws are JennAir's way to attach the outside stainless steel panel to the freezer's permanent panel.
I have now put the panel back on by using bigger wood screws on each side.  In addition to the 4 screws on each side that JennAir provided, I added 4 additional wood screws on each side by drilling new holes through the metal flange and then drilling additional smaller holes into the wood so the new screws can bite into the wood.  I have added wood glue to the tip of each screw.
Whoever designed the connection method of the outside heavy stainless steel panel to the inside permanent panel by using 4 small wood screws on each side made a mistake.  All of these "panel ready" freezer doors made by JennAir use the same fastening method.  There are 4 slots in the metal flange for the technician to put in the 4 JennAir screws.  These slots were made by JennAir.  The screws were provided by JennAir.  The doors (both refrigerator and freezer doors) were made by JennAir and sold as JennAir accessories to be added to the refrigerator.  Without these panels, there would be no doors at all.
I have talked to JennAir and there response is that they will not address this situation.  They are taking a "hands off" policy.
I have repaired my freezer door myself since they would not.  My concern is other people may experience the same issue but might not be as lucky as the 10 year old boy at our house.  You should also know that we keep very little frozen items in the JennAir since we have two refrigerators with freezers outside in addition to a chest freezer.

ATTACHMENTS:
1.	PHOTO OF REFRIGERATOR WITH ALL DOORS ON
2.	PHOTO - JENNAIR INSTRUCTIONS FOR INSTALLATION OF FREEZER PANEL (REFERENCE TO THE X6 WOOD SCREWS)
3.	VIDEOS (2) OF MY WIFE OPENING BOTH THE REFRIGERATOR DOOR AND THE FREEZER DOOR (NOTICE THE DIFFERENCE)
4.	FIVE PHOTOS OF FREEZER PANEL AND SCREWS AFTER IT FELL OFF 
If at all possible, I would really like to know the outcome of your investigation into this problem.

Very Truly Yours, [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a freezer door panel detaching and nearly injuring a child, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I am a fire investigator and was called to investigate a past fire incident concerning an over the range microwave appliance.  The occupant had returned home and noticed a burning plastic smell in the apartment.  They then found a small fire in the microwave, which was not in use at the time.  They described that when they opened the door to the microwave, the issue stopped.  When they shut the door, the microwave made a buzzing or humming sound and started burning again.  They opened the door back up to make it stop and then called maintenance.  They later determined that it was electrical arcing/sparking.  They recalled that the microwave had arced in the past as well.  They stated that the microwave was last used by their babysitter to warm up a bottle approximately 20 minutes before they got home and noticed the smell and fire inside the microwave.  

I visited the apartment to investigate the issue on 6/18/24.  I observed soot and heat damage on the glass turntable in the microwave that had caused several sections of turntable to crack and break off.  The plastic roller that the turntable sets upon had an area that had burned away.  There was soot staining on the bottom of the microwave compartment, and minor soot deposits on the back wall of the cooking compartment.  It appeared that the fire occurred between the glass turntable and the bottom of the cooking compartment.  There was no evidence of any food or other materials in the microwave or in the fire debris in the bottom.  The only materials present were parts of the microwave.  I also found the microwave to be relatively clean and without excessive grease or food remnants.  

The occupant plugged the microwave back in and I observed that it appeared fine when the door was open.  When the door was closed, the microwave made a humming sound and then electrical arcing was observed on the bottom of the cooking compartment near one of the glass shards from the damaged turntable.  The microwave was unplugged and there was no further activity.
justification: The incident involved a small fire and electrical arcing in a microwave, causing damage to the appliance but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I purchased a cast iron hot plate from Amazon, listing here: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07VLK8G99?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details 
This unit is a serious safety hazard. I used it to boil 4 cups of water in a pot with the heat turned all the way up and in the 11.5 minute it took to reach a rolling boil, the entire housing of the unit had become too hot to touch. The entire housing of the unit is made from sheet metal which rapidly conducts the heat of the cast iron top, raising the temperature of the housing almost as high as the cooking surface. After just 11.5 minutes of use I couldn't touch the metal housing anywhere at all and I could only touch the plastic temperature dial for a second before it became too painful to maintain contact. Had I continued using the hot plate the temperature dial would've inevitably become so hot that attempting to turn the unit off using the dial with bare hands  would've caused burns.

This hotplate also has no internal fan, meaning it's enclosed and poorly ventilated metal body acts as an oven-like enclosure, trapping it's radiated heat inside itself and cooking the internal electrical components. I believe that, with enough regular use, these conditions will cause the insulation on the internal wire harness to melt or break down enough to become either a fire or electrical hazard.

I also believe that using this hot plate on a wood surface/countertop may cause pyrolysis in the wood, lowing it's ignition temperature, due to the high heat the unit radiates downward on a regular basis, potentially posing a fire hazard due to it's poor heat management.
justification: The hot plate poses a burn hazard and potential fire risk, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
(ApproxÃÂ2015):  The consumer called the manufacturer after receiving information about a recall.  He said the firm sent him a strip of tape to apply to the product.  The concern was that steam from the oven could get into the electrical components/control and cause it to malfunction.

The consumer is not sure of the purchase date but believes that he may have purchased it shortly after the CPSC Recall# 09-333, and the product may have been made during the time frame listed in the CPSC Recall.

(6/2024):  The consumer received a letter in the mail for Recall# 24-235.  He responded and their rep. told him that they would pay him $50 to haul the product away.

The consumer said that the manufacturer should provide a more substantial resolution, considering the safety hazards this product presents.

One of the smaller burners on his range also no longer works.  When he called the firm about this matter, he was told that it would cost around $700 to fix the burner and that was not worth it.

The consumer is on a fixed income and this recall does not offer any real assistance to him.

To Whom This May Concern: 

My statement about the date of receiving the recall notice must have been later than my earlier recollection, because the date of manufacture appears to be November of 2015. According to the Frigidaire representative that I talked to on the phone, there is a solid state panel containing circuit boards housed in a patrician between the back oven wall and the rear wall of the range. 

The issue was that the vented moisture was migrating into the electronic panel and causing failure to the temperature controllers. Indeed he sent me a roll of aluminum duct sealer tape, which I was instructed to apply to all joints where the moisture was being vented to the ambient air in the kitchen, which I completed as instructed. 

After my retirement, we decided to update our home to be more elderly friendly, meaning that we installed new kitchen cabinets with 100% roll out shelves for easy access to contents. At that time we purchased high quality appliances, dishwasher, smooth toped range and refrigerator. Knowing that our income would be drastically reduced, we purchased top of the line equipment to last us through our elder years! 

This safety recall notice which we received a depreciated value refund of $50. In the form of an electronic gift card and a reimbursement of up to $60.00 for the haul-away of the old range. 

This is not acceptable to us, as we are not able to replace the range, on our very tight income along with health issues that we have to pay for ongoing. 

I believe that this company's engineers designed a faulty piece of equipment and as such should be required to make it safe for owners or replace it, at no additional cost to the customer. Frigidaire knew back in 2009 that their design was a real problem, yet continued to build their ranges without making necessary changes to eliminate this faulty design.
justification: The incident involves a product malfunction and recall, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Electric cooktop sensors & switch malfunction causing the burners to heat to uncontrollably hot setting regardless of the switch setting (low to high). So hot, that the unit doesn't shut off by itself, but relies on the home's electric system to trip the breaker (my breaker was tripped on June 5th). Children & elderly are most susceptible as they won't be able to react to a burning pan when they pour the olive oil like I did. Jenn-Air is aware and offered a 25% discount, but refused to consider a recall. The technician that Jenn-Air sent to investigate, named [REDACTED] with [REDACTED], was so familiar with this issue that he did not need to take anything apart or even look under the counter. He stated the sensor itself wasn't malfunctioning, but it the switch's response to the sensor was the malfunction where it "sticks" so that it doesn't shut off the heat when it needs to. The heat isn't supposed to be on for just a few seconds and then turns off until the sensor calls for more heat. It's interesting how he knew right away like this happened so many times before. Jenn-Air's safety department originally dispatched [REDACTED] to investigate for a safety issue, but since no recalls have been issued, this was not considered a known issue. I had the option to pay to repair it so that I can be safe again. I reported this outcome to Jenn-Air only to be told a 25% discount would be issued for my next purchase and that no recall will likely be considered. They didn't express concern that the young or elderly could inadvertently cause a kitchen fire.
justification: The malfunction poses a significant fire hazard, especially for vulnerable individuals, but no actual injury or death was reported in this incident.

incident_description:
Electrocution and explosion hazard on General Electric Gas oven/stove model JGBS66EEK1ES. Gas oven/stove has Line and Neutral wires improperly installed at factory to the ignitor/spark module.  This miswire caused two dangerous conditions, that would have been mitigated, had the unit been properly assembled at factory. The violet Line wire was plugged into the Neutral position on the spark module, with the white Neutral wire plugged into the Line position on the module. The rear cover holding this module was removed for inspection and cleaning. The wire connected to the NEUTRAL position of the spark module became unplugged, resting inside the chassis. The cover was reinstalled without noting this loose wire, and an attempt was made to ignite the stove from the knob. This energized the disconnected Line wire, which contacted the oven chassis/ground. This created the first hazard, electrocution thru the body of the oven. As the oven was on a AFCI circuit breaker in the house, it did trip properly. The second hazard was that with this line wire disconnected, the spark module was inop, and turning the knob further allowed gas flow without ignition. 

If this spark module was wired properly, the wire that became disconnected by removing the rear cover, would have been a NEUTRAL wire, carrying no voltage. This would have prevented the electrocution hazard, and the spark module may have potentially remained functional, using the ground wire as a return path, preventing freeflowing gas without a spark. This may still have tripped the AFCI/GFCI breaker, which would alert the user to a problem. 

The positioning of the spark module allows for (if appropriately installed) NEUTRAL wire to catch on the panel below it on removal. 

This wiring reversal was verified by comparing it to the wiring diagram taped to the rear of the appliance, and voltage tests.

UPDATED ON 5/29/2024: [After correcting the problem identified in this report, (reversed neutral and Line wires) the gas stovetop has a more powerful ignition spark. Before the cover was initially removed for cleaning, and throughout the life of the unit, the burners would often fail to light until the knobs were turned almost past the ignite portion of the knob. I used to have to turn the knob back to the ignite range and it would often "flare up" on first ignite. Now the burner will light right away at the BEGINNING of the ignite portion of the knob. This is much safer as there is a lower gas flow and flame.

I did not contact the manufacturer as it is out of warranty, after business hours, and from past experience in contacting their support, they would not have been capable of recording a serious safety report. ]
justification: The incident describes a hazardous miswiring that could lead to electrocution and gas leakage, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: LG range child lock reset to unlocked state during brief power outage, causing a fire. The child lock had been set to prevent the burners from being turned on by the dog or othur kitchen activity. The front mounted  knobs are incredibly sensitive and a light push will allow them to turn. Power went out briefly causing the child lock to switch off. Dog bumped into the knob shortly after the power outage while no one else was downstairs which turned a burner on. A plastic container of sugar near the burner melted onto the burner and caught fire, causing nearby items to also flame up. Fire was put out before it spread further into the kitchen. Since then the power outage reset issue has been replicated multiple times. If the child lock is set and the power goes out for even a second, the child lock turns off. If a burner knob is turned into an on position while the power outage resets the child lock, the burner will automatically come on when the child lock resets after the outage. The knobs are so sensitive that lightly leaning over the stove  or bumping them with a cabinet door will push them in and turn them. The push to turn function offers very minimal resistance making it easy for them to be turned by accident. Both of these issues cause a fire risk and a safety hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in a fire but was contained without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue is replicable and the knobs are highly sensitive, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: Our oven turned itself on on the middle of the night again... the third time this week, and just the most recent of dozens of previous times! We woke up from the smell of burning, and the entire house was filled with an acrid smoke that burned the eyes. A burner has spontaneously turned itself on and heated the stove, where a small plastic bag containing bread had been set the night before, melting the plastic and burning the bread black. No one had been in the kitchen or was using the oven. This defective appliance nearly burned our house down! We already disliked this double-oven/stove combo product, and have had several issues including the glass top surface crack, as well as the wildly oversensitive control panel buttons that will turn the oven and/or stove on or off when one is standing over the front of the range and just slightly leans forward. After a handful of similar incidents we have learned to obsessively check whether the appliance is off and the lock button engaged, for fear of fire. Unfortunately, the lock button cannot be used to prevent additional cooking functions from engaging if one of the dual ovens or one of five burners is on, and will shut off all functions. Another annoyance is that we cannot even use the timer function by itself (without the oven or stove heating) while appliance is locked, so even if we do not use the range to cook one evening, we still have to compulsively check that the control panel is locked if weve used the timer at all. In addition to this phantom cooking, the ventilation at the top rear of the product releases such steaming air from the oven that anything or anyone near the side or back countertops can be damaged (melted, burned, or caught fire) or injured (barstool seating at split level height). We can no longer keep anything remotely near our stove, nor have hightop barstool seating for ourselves or guests to sit. Finally, the door handle of the lower oven, when opened, hits the floor and the height a person must stoop to in order to lift out the hot contents is completely absurd even for a short person; this cannot possibly be safe or intended! There is an obvious risk of the glass door shattering from the impact of the handle hitting the floor, as well as a user being scalded/burned while removing items from the lower oven. Everything about this product is poorly designed.
justification: The incident involved acrid smoke that burned the eyes and a risk of fire, indicating potential for injury.

Not to mention the amount of money lost due to having to throw away spoiled food. I ordered the Samsung - 17.5 Cu. Ft. French Door-Counter Depth Refrigerator-with Ice Maker-Stainless Steel. The business committed to provide a reliable, working fridge/freezer combo that would keep my food at a safe temperature, however, that has been far from the case. The fridge/freezer combo worked for about 6 months until I noticed that the freezer on this component suddenly goes in defrost mode and thaws all frozen food and does this about 2-3 times every other month or so, that I have noticed, possibly even more. incident_description: I bought two Thyme & Table 12x18 Acacia Wood Cutting Boards from Walmart less than a month ago and I use them not only to cut and prepare food on but to also cover my sink openings in my kitchen for extra counter space. I spit my food out and that is when I noticed a fairly large chunk of wood. Thats what I bit down on. Upon further inspection I noticed several small sliver style pieces in the rest of my salad. I inspected the cutting board and there was several chucks and slices of wood missing from the top of the cutting board. If I had been preparing food for my family instead of just myself, which is normally the case, then one of my children could have choked on a piece or broke their teeth or worse! I was using a normal kitchen knife, Ive even used butcher knives before and never had anything like this happen on any cutting board or butcher block Ive ever owned. Luckily its just my tooth and Im not in any major pain just some discomfort from a sharp edged tooth rubbing against my tongue. I wasnt using it in any manor other than what its intended for and this shouldnt have happened. Clearly Ill be discarding the board and possibly the other one as well but consumers should be aware that these boards are not as well made or as hard  as they first seem.

incident_description:
One of our U.S. military occupants at Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, Japan staying in our on-base senior enlisted apartments stated they were reheating food in a GE PVM 9179K1SS Convection Microwave in a plastic container, setting the timer for 1 minute and 30 seconds. Occupant was in the bathroom at the time, and heard the microwave beep, indicating the food was ready. They checked the food and discovered it was still cold. The occupant then returned the food to the microwave and selected the reheat setting and went back to the bathroom.
2. While in the bathroom, the occupant described smelling something burning but could not identify what it was or where it was coming from, prompting the occupant to open the bathroom door. The occupant noticed white and black smoke coming from the microwave but did not see flames. They opened the door, removed the food, and set it on the counter, believing the removal of the food would resolve the issue.
3. The local smoke detector activated.
4. Occupant then opened the window and attempted to wave the smoke away from the detector. While doing so, the building/facility fire alarm system activated, indicating (to them) that it was a larger issue than what was observed, and withdrew the room, closing the door behind her.  The microwave caught fire.  Highly likely that the origin of the fire was in the microwave, behind the control panel.  Highly probable that the cause was due to an electrical short or arc.    Fire sprinkers in the building activated.  Immediate fire damage to the kitchen at the point of origin, which was the microwave and cupboards above and adjacent.  Fire damage was external to the food cooking cavity.   Additional smoke damage to the kitchen and room as well.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to the kitchen and smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Background:
The Fullstar Vegetable Chopper arrived a day before on March 7, 2024. Before purchasing the Fullstar Vegetable Chopper, I conducted extensive research over a course of months on various models (can confirm based on search history) where I assessed safety and user friendliness. I selected the Fullstar Vegetable Chopper due to its raving reviews on safety and popularity. The intention of buying the product was to help decrease cooking time, which turned out to be the worst decision of my life.

Saving myself 10 seconds of chopping time has resulted in a life altering event that has now impacted my body, personal life, functionality of my right-dominant hand,employment, and graduate school.

Packaging issue: 
As I began to open the packaging I realized that there were many red flags in terms of packaging.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung refrigerator model #RF30KMEDBSR/AA on 11/23/2016. It was installed in early 2017  because of the holidays. Within the first year, the ice machine froze over, started leaking and no longer produced ice. 
We also noticed that our produce and dairy products were spoiling too fast. Because the ice maker is located in the refrigerator portion of our fridge, the frozen ice maker made the fan work overtime and the temperature would consistently stay over 40 degrees, instead of the 37 degrees for which it was set. We used our homeowners warranty to have it repaired. 

This pattern continued multiple times in 2018, 2019 and 2020. Each time we used our home warranty for repairs. Each time we had to throw away all dairy, fruit, produce and meat because the temperature would spoil food.

In 2021 our home warranty was expired and our ice maker/fridge stop working. We had to throw away food. 

I decided to contact Samsung directly on 7/31/2021 and they sent a repairman to fix. They tried to  tell me it was out of warranty so I needed to pay for repair. After much argument they agreed to pay for the repair. Again I had food spoilage. On 1/1/2022, I again contacted Samsung for a repair due to the same issue. They again sent a repairman 3 weeks later. All food spoiled again.

During this time, a friend found a Samsung fridge complaint page. I  discovered that there were multiple lawsuits against Samsung due to my EXACT complaint on my same model/year.  In one of the lawsuits, Samsung admitted they were selling a defaulted product, so they agreed to repair it 3 times, then offer a 50 % refund of your purchase price if out of their 1 year manufacturer warranty. But, they would only give the refund after 3 attempted repairs. Of course, by then most refrigerators would be out of the 1 year warranty! 

So basically, when I purchased a new refrigerator in early 2017, Samsung knew they were selling a defective product! They implied that it was a great refrigerator and it would work properly. 
Unfortunately, I didnt discover this information until 2021, so Samsung  did not have an official complaint from me until their warranty expired. 

On 8/26/2022, I contacted Samsung to schedule a repair since my fridge/ice-maker malfunctioned again multiple times during the year. Samsung attempted to schedule a repair, but could not get a repairman to even come out to repair it because they knew it was a defective product. 

I asked for a refund for replacement and was offered $1070. Replacement cost was $1900 on sale, so I decided not to take that low amount. I did not realize I could also get food replacement refund, so I did not ask for it at the time but told them about my spoilage. 

Due to major health problems and my husband loosing his job, I did not have the time or energy to call Samsung in 2023, but the problem continued by this time on a weekly basis. We not only lost food, we lost expensive medications because I could not verify the safety of the product with fluctuating temperatures. 

In 4/3/2024, I called Samsung again because of the problem. In June 2023, we purchased a counter top ice-maker because of the frequency of the problem. But, food continued to spoil well before their expiration dates and had to be thrown away on multiple occasions during 2017-2024. 

Samsung asked for my receipt during my April 2024 phone call and I was able to send it to them (after much research). My purchase price in November 2016 was $1959.52 plus $200 installation and connection lines. 

They then told me they could only offer me $832 because they used my receipt for refund price (less than 50% of original cost) despite the fact that during the conversation the supervisor admitted to the defect, told me they are still selling the faulty product but working on a new design, admitted to the multiple lawsuits and told me the replacement cost was $2400. 

He also stated that they were only allowed to replace food loss if the complaint was within 5 years of purchasing the product. He would be able to offer me the original $1070 if I did not give them my receipt. 

After a 2 hr and 7 min phone call and speaking to 4 people, Samsung agreed to give me a refund for $1070 max and no food refund. 

My refrigerator broke down so many times from 2017-2024, I lost count. Since I got it we have wasted thousands of dollars in food/medications because the temperature fluctuations above 40 degrees. Samsung is still selling the faulty refrigerators that they admit has a defect, yet they imply that the product works as it is advertised.

Had I discovered the lawsuits/[REDACTED]page sooner, I would have immediately asked for a refund instead of using my home warranty for repair. 

Unfortunately, I was not able to afford a new refrigerator during this time or I would have replaced it. I have had major GI health issues requiring complex surgeries/hospitalizations and wonder if it was because I ate spoiled food?

Samsung is still selling the same product. How?
justification: The incident involves repeated food and medication spoilage due to a defective refrigerator, with potential health implications from consuming spoiled food.

incident_description: Started load of dishes and towards the end of the wash cycle, load noise was heard followed by smoke and flames coming from the controls on front of dishwasher.  Fortunately my wife was home and extinguished the fire.

incident_description: My  carbon Monoxide dector began to alarm so the fire department was sent to my home by  my [REDACTED] service representative said firemen detected a reading of 28 and began a search to find the source and discovered that the element(s) on my Whirlpool Gold Series double oven gas range was the source stating that the elements were the reason and promptly disconnected the stove from the gas line  At the time of the incident I has just finished making some jam and both the front burners were being used one element to cook the fruit and the other to heat the water for processing.  The alarm sounding prevented what could have been a contrastrophy from happenine.  I could have lost my life had that alarm not alerted me to an issue.
justification: The carbon monoxide alarm prevented a potential fatality, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: KitchenAid dishwasher Model: KUDE60FXBL3 caught fire mid cycle with smoldering and arcing. The was a loud pop and within a minute audible crackling from a nearby speaker was heard from the arcing occurring in the dishwasher. When we went to investigate, thick smoke was discovered pouring out the top of the dishwasher, and a horrific electrical burning smell was detected.  The door to the dishwasher was opened to stop the cycle, and the electrical breaker was switched to "off".  Smoke continued to emit from the inside vent on the door of the dishwasher. The front cover has since been removed to reveal char marks, soot, and damage to what I think is the control panel. The pop we heard was some sort of explosion that created a bulge in the cover of this part. When this cover was removed evidence of the fire was seen. Upon internet research, we discovered there was a class action lawsuit for this issue; not a recall. We were never aware of this potential problem. Had we been asleep or not home, there most definitely would have been a tragic accident. KitchenAid/Whirlpool has not responded. The dishwasher was functioning normally prior to this event.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, which could have led to severe consequences if not addressed promptly, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
cooktop started sparking and popping under glass like fireworks, could see electricity jumping. Could hear popping and smell burning.
Immediately turned off breaker. After letting cooktop cool down it would not come back on.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire Model FCFE3083AS Electric Range from Home Depot which was delivered on Jan 6, 2024.  We have been using it without incident since it was installed.  Yesterday, I was baking a ham in the oven.  The temperature was set to 350 degrees.  I put the ham in the over at about 12:00.  At about 2:30, the interior glass to the oven door shattered and showered glass all over the inside of the oven.  My wife imeediately shut the oven off, and after it cooled, vacuumed up the glass.  There were no injuries, but there could have been if someone had been in the kitchen or checking the oven at the time the glass shattered.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured, though there was potential for harm if someone had been nearby.

incident_description: I have an air fryer Power XL Mfg Empower Brands LLC Model ID1501a 120 volts.  This is my third one in a year and a half.  What is happening is that in order for it to go on, sometimes you have to bang the front of it very hard.  I think it might be getting too hot and needs to cool down, but I feel it is a safety issue.  Also under the basket, all of the coloring is gone bloatches of rust and circles and peeling under the basket, as when I clean it this is how I noticed all the rust and peeling.

incident_description: I own a $500 device called a "Venty" from Storz & Bickel. (https://www.storz-bickel.com/en-us/venty). This device is a "medical grade" hot air generator for vaporizing dry herbs. I've had the device since December of 2023. I was using the device on the night of March 19th, 2024. The Venty was powered on and the temperature was set to 180C. After approximately 90 seconds of the Venty sitting up right and powered on, I noticed a burning smell in the room. I looked over at the Venty and observed smoke coming from the vents on the side of the device. I quickly grabbed the device and pressed the orange power button the side to power it off. The device turned off but the whole unit was extremely hot to the touch to a point where I could not hold it in my hand. I removed the Venty from my home and allowed it cool off before inspecting further. After sufficient amount of time to cool, I unscrewed the top portion from the heater and here's what I observed: The top piece was difficult to remove, I found that it was fused to the bottom piece due to the plastic melting from the overheating. Any dry herb in the device were burnt to ash. The plastic that holds the ceramic ring above the heater was completely melted and the ceramic ring above the heater was leaning and disformed. The O-ring was also deformed and discolored. A horrible smell was emitting from the device and permeating throughout house. Fortunately, no injuries were sustained but I am extremely worried that had I not acted quickly, I could have been injured by the Venty catching fire, melting, and / or causing damage to my property and home.
justification: The incident involved a device overheating and emitting smoke, but no injuries were sustained.

incident_description: Fire in a freezer of an Electrolux refrigerator with the model #FFR1814QB9B. The products Serial number is BA70811940
justification: The incident involves a fire in a freezer, which is a significant event but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: I just purchased a Cuisinart TOA-65 toaster/oven/airfryer. I noticed really hot air coming out the vent on the back so got out a thermocouple thermometer. When on the 450 degree airfry setting, after a few minutes the air coming out the vent on the back was 220 degrees F. This seems to be a fan forced airflow. I looked up the UL safety spec (UL 1026) and it said a maximum of 110 degree temperature rise was allowed. I also looked up the operating temperate specs of a [REDACTED] electrical outlet (the appliance may be placed in front of a kitchen counter outlet), and it was a lot less than 220 degrees. Common [REDACTED] wire used in homes is only rated up to 60 degrees C (140 F). People reported both on Amazon reviews and the Cuisinart [REDACTED]support group of melted outlets behind this appliance. I am returning the appliance to Amazon, as I don't want to risk damage to my home or my personal safety. I don't know if this is just something about the specific unit I have is defective or if this is a design defect of all TOA-65's. No injuries occurred and no damage occurred to my home, but potentially melting an outlet is not something an appliance should do.
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard with no actual injury or damage, but with evidence of similar issues reported by others.

incident_description:
I purchased a Dacor Cooktop and discovered one of the two low-flame capable burners has an unstable flickering inconsistent flame that oscillates as the igniter attempts to light gas as it fills the room.

This poses a risk of explosion because the gas flows but the flame won't light.   I contacted Dacor and they gave me instructions to clean with alcohol and [REDACTED].  I carefully cleaned the removable parts.  This made the problem worse the lower burn stopped flicking altogether after cleaning only sometimes there is an oscillating unstable flame.  I emailed Dacor/Samsung again that I would try a second time which I carefully cleaned, and now the burner at high is a serious risk of a gas explosion the gas turns on and the igniter clocks the room is filling with gas, if I jiggle the knob it seems to light the high flame mode.  Now for the low setting there is 100% chance of a gas explosion because the room fills with gas and the burner at low setting will never light as the igniter clicks away.

This is safety risk to family and the general public consumers.  It may have been caused if or if over time dust got in or an insect entered unit or if a pot bubbles over.  This is a design flaw at the low flow burner setting.  I informed Dacor there is a safety hazard and requested they recall this low flame models due to explosion risk.  Dacor/Samsung's reply is that the design of the unit changed and because its out of warranty they will do nothing regardless of any consumer product safety issue.  I suspect over time if dust or an insect enters the unit or if a customer's pot overflows there is a blockage internal to the unit which puts customers at risk for gas inhalation and gas explosion.
justification: The description indicates a serious risk of gas explosion, which could lead to death, and the issue is persistent and unresolved.

incident_description: As a consumer of the Samsung French Door Refrigerator with Family Hub RF265BEAESG, I am deeply disappointed and frustrated by the numerous issues I have encountered with the appliance. Today marks yet another instance of the refrigerator's malfunction, adding to a series of problems that have persisted throughout the second year of ownership. Despite experiencing similar issues multiple times before, reaching out for assistance yielded no meaningful help or resolution from Samsung or its representatives. The recurring failure of the cooling system, premature breakdown of interior components, and persistent water leakage from the back of the refrigerator have caused significant inconvenience and damage to my home. It is evident that these issues are not isolated incidents, as many other consumers have reported similar experiences with the same model. Given the recurring nature of these problems and their potential hazards, I strongly advocate for Samsung to recall the RF265BEAESG refrigerator and take immediate action to address these issues comprehensively. Additionally, I expect to be compensated for all damages incurred as a result of the faulty refrigerator and the lack of adequate support from Samsung. As a loyal customer, I implore Samsung to prioritize consumer safety and satisfaction by rectifying these issues promptly and effectively.
justification: The incident describes appliance malfunctions and inconvenience but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I received an Ember mug for Christmas 2023 and used it according to directions approximately 6 times. On January 22, 2024 I picked it up off the charging coaster where it had sat undisturbed for a period of around 2 weeks and found it had significant corrosion and looked burned on the bottom of the mug and on the charging coaster. I reached out via email to the Ember company to report the damage and after two months received a reply. They accused me of putting the mug in the microwave and that's what the caused the damage. The mug did not leave the charging coaster. It was never put into the microwave. They did not offer a replacement mug, merely a discount on a new one.

incident_description:
The consumer used the left rear burner (if facing the stove) for approximately 15 minutes.  He turned the burner off and the control screen normally flashes to indicate that the surface was still hot.

A few minutes later, he returned and the soup was still cooking the burner continued to get hotter with time.  He tried to turn it off, but it would not turn off.  He tripped the breaker to stop the range from heating.


A few hours later, he tried the range again.  However, as soon as he turned the breaker back on, that same rear, left burner began to heat up and he had to trip the breaker to turn it off.  He turned on 2 other burner and was able to turn them off.

After searching the Internet for the problem he found a recall notice.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer about this matter and was told that his model is not included in a recall.

The problem is similar to what is identified in CPSC Recall# 13-031, but his model number is not included.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that could not be turned off, but no injury or death occurred. The problem is similar to a known recall issue, indicating a possible but not certain likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the knobs get really hot to the touch when the oven is turned on, and two of them get extremely hot. The consumer measured the tempeture on one of them and it read 165 Fahrenheit. The consumer also notes that the unit makes a very loud noise when the oven is on.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to arranged for a service technician to inspect the unit. Once in his home, the service technician installed a new seal around the door. The new seal did not solve the problem.

The consumer states that the cooktop is used two to three times per week whereas the oven about once weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

incident_description: The microwave tray that comes with the microwave/convection oven is defective.  The trays wheels wear down, causing the metal to start sparking, creating a fire hazard. I have included a photo that shows the black burn mark left behind on the wheel.

justification: The bowl shattered, throwing sharp glass fragments, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our concern:  that we have ingested a toxic substance from our defective dishwasher, and that it is causing health problems.   The new Asko dishwasher we purchased, still under warranty, seemed to be working fine, but shortly we noticed there was a grimy black residue building up on the filters.  I cleaned the filters with hot soapy water, and also white vinegar, but they seemed permanently stained. (See the photos)   There is no smell to the residue.   After a time, we noticed it covering the stainless steel tub, as well.  We would take a clean white paper towel and wipe the tub, and it would come away black.  After awhile, we noticed that the black residue had stained all the dishwasher racks, and other interior components, and also was  on all of our dishes, pots and pans, plastic containers, etc.   If it was a smooth surface, we were able to wash it off.   But if it was slightly porous, it stained the ceramics and plastic, and made it impossible to get clean.  We tried running multiple cleaning cycles with citric acid, as recommended in the owner's manual. Nothing helped. We called for a service technician to come. He found nothing  wrong. Then we got an error code- the circulation pump. Another tech came. He tested the pump, checked the dishwasher, declared there was nothing wrong. Except neither tech could explain the black residue. They said change detergent. We did. Nothing helped. We called again for service. This time the tech recommended changing out some hoses. He said maybe the hoses were defective and possibly disintegrating. The senior tech advisor from Milestone, the distribution company, also recommended changing out the circ. pump since she had the tech run a diagnostic, and saw the error code again for the circ. pump. These parts were replaced.   The tub itself is cleaner, but there is still black residue remains on everything.  We tried running multiple cleaning cycles again, as recommended by the technician, with no luck.  We called Milestone, with concerns about all the rest of the dishwasher components which were covered with black residue...because even if the replacement of the circ pump worked, how were we to get the black residue off of every interior component???   And, we were wondering if the black residue could then contaminate the new circulation pump?   Milestone was not helpful.  We asked for refund of the machine.   Because even  with the new pump and hoses, the black residue and stain remains on everything.  And it is not just stained, but still comes off if you wipe it with a dry clean paper towel.   All technicians say they have never seen anything like this before.  We are concerned that the residue may be harmful/toxic.  We have been ingesting it for months. Since the machine is still under warranty, the distribution company after much effort, and after seeing videos which demonstrate how pervasive and extreme this black residue is, has agreed to give us a full refund.  They checked with Asko, and their contact there had never seen anything like it in 20 years and has no idea what it is.  In order for us to get the refund, we have to give back the machine.  But we want to find out if we have been subjected to toxic substances.  I have been having recurrent headaches, gastrointestinal issues, insomnia and  exhaustion.  I don't know if this is related -- but it makes me very uneasy.  We are hoping for an investigation and analysis as soon as possible, in case our health has been affected and we need treatment of some sort.  We were told by the retailer that we have a very limited amount of time to get a refund, which is contingent upon on us returning the defective unit.   Our fear is that the manufacturer may just discard the unit, and not investigate this health and safety issue properly.   We also don't know how to ensure that they will  inform us of the accurate results of their investigation, if they perform one. We have videos that we could send as well.
justification: The incident involves potential ingestion of a toxic substance causing health issues like headaches and gastrointestinal problems, indicating injury.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:

I am a Sears customer who purchased a refrigerator and warranty. Sears has engaged in deceptive and fraudulent practices and has refused to honor the terms and obligations outlined in their warranty.

In 2018, I purchased a Kenmore 795.5183 refrigerator from a Sears Department Store. At the time of purchase, the refrigerator was equipped with a manufacturer's warranty. Within the first year of purchase, I began to have problems with the unit. Sears would come out, attempt a patch/fix on the refrigerator and then it would malfunction again, or some feature on it would stop working. Before the manufacturer's warranty expired, I began purchasing a yearly Warranty from Sears to cover the refrigerator. The Warranty included repairing the unit or replacing the unit if it could not be repaired. Since 2018 I have experienced multiple breakdowns and malfunctioning of the unit yearly. Technicians have been sent to my home nearly 20 times to work on this lemon of a unit. Sears sent 2 outside contractors to address th issues and report back to them as well as their own technician. The technicians have ordered approximately 10-15 replacement parts and to date, the unit is still not functioning and leaking through my kitchen floor into my basement causing mold and wood rot
In August of 2023, what had become a customary process, the refrigerator malfunctioned and stopped working. I lost food and Sears sent me a nominal food loss draft which did not nearly cover the cost of the amount of food lost. Since August, my refrigerator has not worked properly. The water/ice maker has not worked in over 7 months. The refrigerator side shuts down completely, meaning the refrigerator side or the freezer side stops functioning and or the ice maker stops working. In February 2024, the refrigerator began leaking. It leaks so much that it's leaking into my basement damaging the floors beneath the refrigerator and causing mold damage as outlined above. The water is leaking directly onto electrical cad wiring
The last technician was a Sears technician who still did not resolve the issues with this faulty unit. Each time a technician sets an appointment, either I or my sister will take a day off from work, to wait for the technician to arrive, and not repair the unit.
Last November, Sears sent one of their technicians. He had been there several times before to no avail. I had been requesting a new replacement for the longest as it was absolutely absurd that this unit was constantly malfunctioning. After inspecting the unit in an attempt to repair it, the Sears technician agreed that a replacement unit was necessary. He further advised that he was going to make that recommendation to Sears. I spoke to him after he left my home, he advisd that he submitted the work order for the replacement unit. In approximately December 2023/January 2024, I reached out to Sears to inquire about the status of the replacement. The representative that I spoke to confirmed that I was in line for the replacement. The representative further advised that I would receive an email in 1-2 days with documentation to be completed which would initiate the replacement protocol. Days and weeks passed and I never received the email. I reached out to Sears in February 2024 inquiring about the status of the replacement. This representative advised me that despite their prior confirmation that a replacement was warranted, the technician who recommended the replacement allegedly did not correctly complete the paperwork and that it would be necessary for me to start the process again. That meant, a technician would have to come out to my home yet again and attempt to fix this unit that another technician stated needed to be replaced. Why do I have to bear the burden of the alleged improper completion of paperwork by their "experienced" technician? If it was completed incorrectly by the technician, why didn't Sears reach out to the technician and instruct him to complete the paperwork properly? When did they discover this paperwork was allegedly completed incorrectly, before or after they confirmed that a replacement was approved? How can they approve the replacement then fail to honor that approval? Meanwhile, my floors, subloor and floor joists are wet, moldy and wood rotten. This constant leak is also a fire hazard! Furthermore, my refrigerator as of the date of this letter still is not functioning. All of the above failures and misleadings are indicative of the deceptive and fraudulent practices engaged by Sears.
The same Sears technician who began servicing the unit in November 2023, and who informed me a replacement unit was needed, came to my home on February 16, 2024. He observed the leaking and did what he always does, ordered random parts and scheduled me for yet another appointment on March 1, 2024. The parts were delivered about a week before March 1. (Please see proof of delivery annexed hereto as Exhibit C.) I took off from work yet again for this issue to be resolved. I received text messages and emails regarding the appointment. The last text I received from Sears in regards to my appointment was at 5:35 PM on February 29, 2024 confirming same. However, at 8:02 AM on March 1, 2024, I received a text from Sears, stating that my previously confirmed appointment scheduled for that day had been rescheduled to March 15, 2024. (Please see appointment notifications annexed hereto as Exhibit D.)
I immediately called Sears and advised them this again is unacceptable as (1) I had taken the day off from work to have this painstaking recurrent issue resolved (2) this constant leaking was causing severe damage to my home, making conditions unsafe and hazardous and (3) the problem needed to be remedied already.
The first representative I spoke to told me that my appointment was back on for March 1 and assured me that the technician would call me within an hour to provide me with his arrival time. After not hearing back from the technician, I called Sears throughout the day and spoke with NINE different representatives. I requested to speak with a supervisor but never spoke with one. Finally at approximately 2:30 PM, another wasted day without resolution, the representative advised that the technician had just ordered additional parts that day. Why weren't these parts ordered before the day of the appointment and what about the other 2 parts that were already ordered and sitting in my home waiting for someone to install them? The representative basically said I don't have a choice but to wait until March 15, allowing more water damage to my home. The condition of the non working leaking refrigerator did not change from February 16 to March 1, 2024, so why the additional ordered parts?
Sears never ever fixes the problem with this appliance. They don't get to the root of the problem and instead allow the issue to fester, at the risk and peril of my life, home and peace of mind. This unit is beyond repair by the words of Sears' own technician however, despite that, the company is sending him back to my home again for yet another attempt at "repair" which will be to no avail.

Sears is committing fraud with their cyclical practice of constantly ordering non descript parts, setting, confirming and cancelling appointments, and never addressing the true underlying issue. As such, Sears has breached their contract with me and their warranty/replacement duties by failing to adequately repair the unit and ultimately by failing to replace the unit despite their own technician's recommendation that they do so. Nearly 20 repairs for one unit in 6 years is completely unacceptable. Allowing my home to continually sustain damage, mold and wood rot is unacceptable. Failing to honor the terms of the warranty contract via the provided replacement provision is unacceptable. The warranty contract indicates that the appliance would be replaced if it was deemed irreparable. It has been deemed irreparable by their technician, but they continue to attempt to initiate repairs on an appliance the "technician" stated needed to be replaced.
Sears has failed to fully honor the warranty. Sears has breached their contract with me and I demand that they honor the contract, replace this lemon unit and repair the damage caused to my floors. They are putting my home at risk for fire, mold and thereby risking my life!!! This is horrendous and egregious on the part of Sears. Please be advised that I am filing Complaints with the [REDACTED], State of New Jersey and Federal Trade Commission. This matter is of dire urgency due to the water rotting wood in my home and leaking onto wiring which can cause fire! I do not understand how it is possible or legal for Sears to continue to sell and fail to honor appliance warranties!

 
Please be guided accordingly,
justification: The incident involves significant property damage and potential safety hazards (mold, electrical risks) but no reported injuries or deaths.

After talking with [REDACTED] at Customer Service whom spoke with his tech support team,  I  was told that the plastic particles may have been from the manufacturer mold and have not had any problems related to this. incident_description:
I purchased the Keurig K-Slim + Iced Single Serve Coffee Maker from Amazon.com. The very first time that I took it out of the package, after following the initial setup instructions, I attempted the brew over ice feature, using a Keurig branded K-cup coffee pod. 

The machine burst into smoke, following which it produced a very small amount of what appeared to be coffee, then turned off. 

I tried once more to make sure it was not a malfunction, and the same result occurred, with significantly more smoke. This was definitively smoke, not steam. 

I immediately unplugged the unit and contacted customer support. Customer support, despite telling me this was an emergency, rerouted my call several times and repeatedly told me that all staff were busy and that they could not take my call. 

I sent this message to your attention while on hold to Keurigs specialist team and as of 7:01pm EST, I am still on hold with them, having not been given any indication as to how to proceed, despite the confirmation that this situation is indeed an emergency.
justification: The machine produced smoke but there was no injury reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: The Joy air fryer made by Galanz has a problem with the time and temp setting changing by itself while using it has happened all the time. incident_description:
My Bosch 800 Series dishwasher lost power.  It was installed in October 2023.  Bosch service representative immediately found burned electrical connections inside the power cord junction box (Bosch Model SMZPCJB1UC).  Bosch service stated that he finds burned junction boxes frequently.  Online search for the problem shows dozens of smoldering and melted junction box failures.  All connections were landed and tightened according to Bosch instructions.

Service representative recommended that junction box cord get replaced with a under- sink plug and conventional cord "to be safe".
justification: The incident involves burned electrical connections, which could lead to fire or injury, but no actual injury or death was reported. The service representative's statement and online reports indicate this is a common issue.

incident_description: My dishwasher had been running fine with no sign of trouble when it started belching smoke from the door.  After researching and finding that the common cause is a faulty control module I opened the door panel and found the damage too great to be able to be repaired with a new board.  The control board is severely scorched, the wires got so hot they melted into the sound proofing layer, one [REDACTED] plug had fused itself to another component.  Most disturbing is that despite all this damage, the thermal fuse still has continuity.  It should have blown.   Had it proceeded farther, I could have been killed from burning plastic vapors.
justification: The incident involved severe damage and potential for fatal consequences from burning plastic vapors, though it was caught in time.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE Range through home depot. Model Number JB735SPSS . Serial Number 31413825. I plugged in the appliance for the first time. As soon as I plugged it in, there was a spark and electric smoke at the back of the appliance. I heard a loud buzz at the circut breaker and went to investigate. It too smelled of electric smoke and the breaker had tripped.
As I shut the breaker, I recieved a slight shock.
Upon further examination, I determined that the plug to the appliance had been negligently and improperly wired to the appliance by the manufactuer. There was a color coded cord that that attaches to the appliance- a black wire attaches to a black wire, a white wire to a white wire, and a red to a red. However, the manufactuer negligently connected the black wire on the plug to the white wire on the appliance and the white wire on the plug to the black wire on the appliance.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight shock (injury) due to improper wiring, but the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely as it appears to be a manufacturing defect.

incident_description: Brand new Black and Decker toster oven nearly causes house fire. After recently purchasing a toster oven from Walmart, a dangerous defective timer mechanism caused the unit not to turn off after the timer had counted down. I used the oven 10-20 times before the failure occurred. It was about 1 month old at the time. I typically cook small pizza in the oven. I set the timer to 8 minutes. The timer controls the power going to the heating elements and turns it off after it makes a ding. When the timer failed, it got stuck one second before it was supposed to ding, causing the 8 minute pizza to cook until a small fire began in the oven and my smoke alarms went off. I was able to turn the oven off by applying a slight amount of pressure to the timer knob, pushing it past zero and causing an audible ding and the de-powering of the heating elements. The issue persists and the oven must now be carefully monitored throughout the cooking cycle. After searching [REDACTED] it seems this is a very common problem with these toster ovens. Timer mechanisms must be built reliably to turn power off.
justification: The incident involved a defective toaster oven that caused a small fire, but no injury or death occurred. The issue is described as very common, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a brand new ninja creami 11 in 1 from Costco on 3/6/24. I used the product for the third time on 3/13/24 to process some ice cream. The blade skimmed the inside of the container during mixing which resulted in long, 2-4", plastic shavings being mixed in with my ice cream. I followed all instructions properly. I did not notice the shavings until about half way though eating my ice cream. This resulted in my consuming some shavings, some of which became lodged in my throat requiring an intense amount of heaving to become unloaded.  I was able to isolate more shavings by placing the remaining ice cream in a metal strainer and running hot water over it, melting the ice cream, but leaving the shavings behind. It would appear from my internet research that this is common occurrence. I have two small children who luckily were not injured as a result of this. Had they ingested the plastic shavings that I did it would have likely been much more difficult for them to heave them up. In addition the length poses a concern as they may home become entangled inside the body resulting in the need for surgery to be removed. It would seem that this product should likely be recalled and not sold on the open market as it poses a serious health risk to all people and particularly small children consuming the food products created.
justification: The incident resulted in injury due to plastic shavings being consumed and lodged in the throat, requiring intense heaving to dislodge. The description also indicates this is a common occurrence, suggesting a higher likelihood.

incident_description: Frigidaire Oven w/air fryer.  Model Number: GCRG3060AF, Serial Number VF01079809. Anytime the air fryer is used the exhaust vent dispenses heat directly below the controller panel to the oven, rendering the control panel useless with no way to shut off oven for several minutes until it ultimately fails with the error code 666 typed in automatically and followed by a FAIL error and then thank god the oven shuts off. This happens all the time in air fry unless i dampen the metal surrounding the controller keypad with water from a wet paper towel and then point a fan directly at the water. This cools the overheating controller by removing the heat caused by the exhaust vent directly below the controller. When the water beads evaporate from the fan i add new ones with a wet paper towel and do this over and over (usually 5 times) until i am finished cooking with air fryer. Oven mode will sometimes do this if i go over 400 degrees.  This is clearly a failure by design to exhaust the heat in the oven away from the controller panel which when overheated becomes rendered useless with no way to shut of the over because the buttons do not work. This is very dangerous and their are several complaints on [REDACTED] website from other owners experiencing the same issue. [REDACTED]. This problem has been happening since January 2020 to the present time.

It is disturbing to note that Whirlpool Corporation has had numerous similar incidences reported to SaferProducts.gov for many years.

Additionally, the use of the stove leads to a noticeable gas odor permeating throughout the kitchen. This has necessitated the continuous use of a carbon monoxide filter adjacent to the stovetop, underscoring the potential health hazards posed by the unit.

Given the severity of these issues and the fact that my model has been erroneously excluded from the recall, I urge the Commission to take immediate action. It is imperative that the manufacturer, ZLINE, be held accountable for releasing a potentially dangerous product and failing to adequately address the defects through its recall process.

I seek a thorough investigation into this matter and request an appropriate remedy, which may include but is not limited to, a full replacement or refund. The safety and well-being of consumers should be of paramount concern, and it is distressing that such a serious issue has not been properly resolved.

Please let me know if there are any supporting documents that I can provide.

service appointment was made for December 27, 2023 with [REDACTED] No repairman showed up. I again contacted Frigidaire customer
service and again told them about the fire in the stove. I requested a different
repair service company because of my inability to contact G&G Appliance
about the missed appointment. Another repair service call was scheduled for
January 4, 2024 with [REDACTED] . The repairman came and said the
fire was caused by grease. I showed him the burnt pot and he said he
smelled grease. I told him that I had already used the steam cleaning and
self-cleaning features and the stove was clean. He turned the air fryer on at

incident_description:

subsequently cut into, my shin. The hinge mechanism was never smooth, but this was
the first time it bound and then released without warning.

After treating my injury (which is now a permanent and sensitive scar), I inspected
the dishwasher to find a very sharp edge and point on the upper front corner of the door.
This condition was created by several poor design and manufacturing practices which
lead to an overhang of the plastic control panel and a protruding sharp edge and point.

While it may seem like an unlikely combination of events that led to my injury, upon
further inspection of other similar brand new, KitchenAid dishwashers, I found this
sharp edge and point condition is quite common. It is also a design that is used on
many models of Whirlpool dishwashers still on sale today.
justification: The incident resulted in a permanent and sensitive scar, indicating an injury (severity 3). The sharp edge is common in similar dishwashers, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: I purchased two 16 ounce Philadelphia Eagles Glasses 1/23/24 from Fanatics.com.  The product description states, Dishwasher Safe.  That is one of the main reasons I bought the glasses.  But after I put the first glass in the Dishwasher, the Philadelphia script, Eagles script, Eagle, silver line, and green line decals are dismembered with some completely missing.  I will attach photos, but have to return the glasses.  In small type on the box is this statement, "Glassware Is Top Shelf Dishwasher Safe."  I placed the glass in the top shelf of my Dishwasher.  This damage and the release of potentially harmful substances should not have happened to a Dishwasher Safe item.  That is false advertising to misleadingly promote an item to be Dishwasher Safe, when in fact it is NOT Dishwasher Safe, and potentially harmful substances were detached from the glass.  I did not want to put the other glass in the Dishwasher for fear that harmful materials would come off the glass.  This is a consumer safety issue.  If it happened to me, it could happen to anyone.  Fanatics sells and manufacturer Logo Brands makes a wide range of 16 ounce glasses featuring decals of many sports teams.  That means there is a potential that those products are NOT Dishwasher Safe.  I tried to locate the decals missing from the glass, but could not find them in the Dishwasher.  These are small decals, which if detached from the glass can very possibly be ingested by a consumer.  This can be harmful.  Both on Fanatics website and Logo Brands website, these glasses are marketed as Dishwasher Safe.  It could be that the glasses I received were defective (which is unsafe).  Or it could be that these glasses are NOT Dishwasher Safe.  I believe this warrants further investigation.  Through chats, emails, and finally after I demanded a number to call a Fanatics Customer Service Supervisor, I was able to get explanations.  An email from a Fanatics customer service representative stated, "Unfortunately, the Philadelphia Eagles 16oz. Pint Glass Two Pack is not dishwasher safe like the site states.  We are working to get the information updated/removed as soon as possible."  The supervisor told me he will monitor to make sure the Dishwasher Safe statement is removed from the online product description.  So Fanatics admitted in writing that the product it promotes as Dishwasher Safe is NOT Dishwasher Safe.  Meanwhile, the only response I received from Logo Brands showed little concern.  As I did with Fanatics, I asked for confirmation from Logo Brands that these glasses are Dishwasher Safe.  I can provide the entire email text, but for now, here is the response from a Logo Brands customer service representative, "I would say that most of our glasses are dishwasher safe, but like any product there can be a problem during manufacturing and errors can occur."  Logo Brands does not seem willing to even consider the possibility that one or any or all of their products are not Dishwasher Safe.  So I am filing this report.  I hope the CPSC pursues this investigation to determine if what happened to me was because of a defective item (a safety issue) or a product claimed to be Dishwasher Safe that is in fact NOT Dishwasher Safe (also a safety issue).  If these glasses are not safe to be washed in the dishwasher, then they should NOT be marketed as Dishwasher Safe.
justification: The incident involves potential harm from detached decals, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I own a Whirlpool refrigerator model number WRB322DMBM00, serial number K64404587. The freezer drawer, located at the bottom of the refrigerator, has a light switch is activated by a white plastic tab that hangs down from the top center at the front of the freezer. The edges of this actuator are extremely sharp and I have cut the back of my hand a number of times when reaching for items stored on the top shelf. I am on blood thinners so this has resulted in significant bleeding as this sharp piece of plastic is not visible when standing in front of the refrigerator. This is a safety hazard. I looked at similar newer Whirlpool brand refrigerators at Lowe's and found the design of this switch actuator has been improved by mounting the switch horizontally in the front frame of the freezer, made the actuator wider and rounded the edge. This makes the switch clearly visible and eliminates the danger of lacerations by rounding the edge.

I contacted the manufacturer by filling out a request by on their "contact us" form at whirlpool.com on 01/28/24 and provided all these details. I received an auto reply confirmation email with the subject line "We're Here to Help" confirming all the details and comments I submitted, but to date was never contacted by Whirlpool.
justification: The description reports repeated injuries (cuts with significant bleeding) due to the sharp plastic tab, indicating an injury severity level. The likelihood is high (4) as the user has been cut multiple times.

incident_description: We purchased a Samsung refrigerator (model number RF28T5021SG) on May  23, 2023 from Best Buy.  The refrigerator was working as normal until November 2023, when my wife noticed the temperature inside felt a little warm.  We put a thermometer inside the refrigerator and realized the temperature was over 60F even though the thermostat on the door of the fridge was reading 34F.  We had to throw out a full refrigerator and freezers worth of groceries, including a lot of pumped breast milk that we didn't feel was safe for our infant after being at an unsafe temperature for an unknown period of time.  A repairman came out to look at the unit on 11/30/2023 but by that time it was working as normal again.  He checked some settings on the refrigerator and said he would be in contact in a weeks time to check on the unit.  We kept on eye on the temperature after that and had another incident around February 9, 2024, when the refrigerator again went about 60F, even though the thermostat on the inside of the fridge was still registering 34F.  We again lost a full refrigerator and freezer full of groceries along with more breast milk for our child.   When cleaning out the fridge this time, I noticed lots of food with mold on it suggesting the temperature had been dipping for while.  We're very lucky that our child didn't eat any of this and get sick, because the built in thermostat on the fridge never got above 34F suggesting everything was safe.  We were only able to tell there was issue by using a separate thermometer that tracked maximum temperature recorded each day.  We have started trying to contact Samsung about fixing the issues but are being told the warranty period expired in January 2024, even though the unit was not purchased until May 2023 and they state a one year warranty on the purchase.
justification: The incident caused significant financial loss and potential health risk due to spoiled food and breast milk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Having had a new (1-1/2 year old) Frigidaire Refrigerator fail last month, I got to talking to the repair person, who explained he has been seeing compressors fail frequently since the switch to R600, which is butane. Anecdotally, I began to wonder if R600 (butane) was implicated in what seems to me as an increase in home explosions. (What can I say, I was an ICU Burn Nurse for 30 years, I think about this stuff.) I realize the overwhelming number are probably attributable to archaic gas lines, but it did make me wonder. And, I only have access to my own observations, which are often skewed and no substitute for nationwide data.

I had filed a complaint with CPSC regarding the failure, the company's refusal to take responsibility, etc. and I had mentioned this concern at the end of the complaint. CPSC e-mailed a reply and suggested I file a complaint at this e-mail address, so I leave the research in your capable hands. 

I want to make crystal clear that my refrigerator did not do anything except stop working. I just wondered, after my conversation with the repair person, if the problem could be wider than just compressors failing and actually concern overheating, fan failures and then explosions. Also, manufacturer date is a guess since the form would not accept Don't Know or N/A in that spot, but it was manufactured before 4/13/2022 when I bought it new.
justification: The refrigerator stopped working without causing injury or damage, but there is concern about potential wider risks like overheating or explosions.
