incident_description:
CPSC,

In short, my new GE CAFE refrigerator cannot keep its temperature under 40. It may cool down to 34 but the differential allows the refrigerator to heat up, in many cases, above 40 before it starts cooling again. It seems that this is GE's way of trying to save energy or save on compressor wear. Either way it meant loss of food and I believe, in some cases where people do not use a thermometer, food poisoning. I understand that Samsung is involved in a lawsuit right now for this very issue.

The below paragraphs reference log files located on my website at [REDACTED]

I bought a GE CAFE refrigerator in late December of last year. I installed it on 12-23-23, set it for 37 degrees, waited 24 hours, then loaded the refrigerator with food. Shortly after then I noticed that my food, mainly smoothies were not cold. I set the refrigerator to 34 and put in a cheap refer thermometer that I used for my old refrigerator. For a couple of days I noted that it would never get below 40. I started testing the temperature with my [REDACTED] and it showed that, even though the refrigerator display showed 34, the actual temperature in most cases was over 39 and many times over 40, 45 and as high as 52

I then switched to a [REDACTED] logging meter on 1-9-24 and started logging the temperature in 5 minute intervals for 24hrs. It showed that the refrigerator has at least an 8 differential/hysteresis setting from the set point of 34. I lost all my vegetables the next day. I emptied the new refrigerator back to my old one. I contacted GE and a tech came out on 1-23-24. His data he showed me had the same high numbers 45, 48 and higher. He contacted his tech support and I over heard that the temperature differential could be as high as 10. Even though the tech on the phone said it is a fairly normal, I insisted is was not so the tech at my house ordered e new board(he really did understand the issue).

While I was waiting for the new board, I logged my old 2001 [REDACTED] refrigerator and its differential is 3 and has no problem keeping the temp under 37(Check Graph). I received the board and got the OK from the GE tech to install the board myself. I installed it on 2-1-24, waited 24 hours, then began logging temps again. Although the refrigerator worked better, it was still not able to hold the temp under 40 while the set point was 34(34 degrees is the lowest setting). I did 3 24hr tests, one at 34, one at 37 and one at 40. All results were very poor. This refrigerator will not keep the temperature at or below the set point. The logs here: [REDACTED] show the results. Please show these results to a tech that understands [REDACTED] logging values. I also have all the number data that makes up these graphs. I also included the [REDACTED] results for comparison.

In all test cases, once the refrigerator reached its set temperature, the actual control display temperature will show that "set point" temperature no matter what the real recorded temperature was. I find this very misleading and I would say that most people who have these refrigerators do not know that they are probably over temp for FDA recommendations for safe refrigerator temperature.

I just emailed the GE tech saying the problem is not fixed. I suspect that GE will drag me and their tech through the mud on this. I do not believe GE can provide me a refrigerator that can keep a temperature under the set point of 37 because of how they want to control their compressors. I would like my money back now instead of doing this months long walk of never getting a refrigerator that works for me.

Are we allowing refrigerator companies to have and average for a set point? If that is the case then the average of 47 and 27 is 37 meaning they could allow the refrigerator to heat up to 47 before cooling and call it good. You can see that with my logs. Unfortunately I see why regulation comes into play with stuff like this.

I would welcome CPSC or anyone else to come and test this refrigerator. They have been to my house to test another appliance.

Am I stuck with a refrigerator that cannot cool properly? What is my recourse? How are these companies being allowed to do this?
justification: The refrigerator fails to maintain safe temperatures, leading to food spoilage and potential food poisoning risks, though no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description:
The New Range Problem:

Product Image GE 30 in. 5.0 cu. ft. Gas Range with Self-Cleaning Convection Oven and Air Fry in Stainless Steel.    Store SKU # 1005649087   Internet # 314138082    Model # JGB735SPSS    [REDACTED]

It has:
	Four large slots on the metal cover at the bottom of the oven.
	A big hole under the metal cover that directly leads to the exit big hole at the back of the stove.     
	Another bigger hole at the back of the stove that directly leads to the inside of the stove.
	There are no mesh or ventilable barrier between the entrance and exit holes.

As a result:
Mice, small animals and various bugs can freely access the inside of the stove and oven. These creatures may carry bacteria, viruses and various pathogenic microorganisms. They can easily contaminate the food and utensils in the oven, and spread diseases. Most importantly, they can bite the wires in the stove, which will cause a terrible fire!  If this continues, it will pose of a huge threat to the health and safety of all users.

Our experience: 

In January 2021, my family bought this stove from Home Depot. After using a few times, we often found dirty secretions and mice droppings in the oven. 

We have used various stoves for over 30 years. Since moving into the current house in 2003, we have used two gas stoves and never had such an issue. We really did not know, then, how it could have happened?

On July 2022, after wiping off the mice droppings in the oven, I turned on the Self Clean for the first time. Suddenly, the stove was on fire, and a large amount of black smoke and burning smell came out of the stove, so I turned off  Self Clean immediately to avoid danger.

In order to find the dead mice and clean it thoroughly, I opened the metal plates at the bottom of the oven and back of the stove. There were numerous mice feces and secretions scattered inside, especially in the white asbestos-like insulation above at the back of the stove. Due to configuration of the stove, I was unable to open more parts. So I needed help and had to contact GE. 

Experience with GE:

From July25, 2022 to now, GE (appliancesupport@geappliances.com) and I emailed each other 26 times. However, they insisted there were no new design defects and all problem came from the mice.  They repeatedly emphasized that the one-year warranty of the range has expired. In sum, they simply pushed me away and refused to help at all, whether it be a stove exchange, refund, recall, or at least sending someone to investigate the issue. 

GE Appliances Support said:

incident_description: Breville Smart Oven Pro Model BOV845 BSS batch #2136.  This toaster oven tripped our kitchen GFI twice within 3 weeks.  After the second tripping of the GFI, I used a voltmeter and determined that the outer case of the Breville was fully electrified, and, as I understand it, would have delivered a shock to myself or my wife if it weren't for the GFI.  I returned the product to Breville, who examined it and wrote back:  "During the inspection, our technicians discovered unforeseen damage that was not initially evident. This required additional materials and labor to address properly. Even after doing so, safety concerns were still evident and resulted in unrepairable scenario of your unit."  In other words, it seems that this Breville product was so dangerous that even Breville's own technicians said they couldn't fix it.

incident_description:
We were using the ELLA'S baby food maker steamer and food processor. We noticed 2 design flaws for this unit. First, the steam pump will back flow water back to the water tank with the food particles intact. This will cause bacteria growth and mold in the water lines. Assuming the heating element is working correctly and at proper temperature there is a chance that bacteria will enter the babies food when processing food or by gravity tilt, bad water will flow into the babies food after steaming has occurred.
Second, pending certain foods being blended, the blade has a chance to chip or shread itself into shavings. This is dangerous. We didn't notice this on our unit but others have online. You will have to inspect the food each use to make sure the blade didn't chip or get shaved off into the food.
justification: The design flaws could lead to bacterial contamination or ingestion of blade shavings, posing a risk of injury to the baby.

incident_description: Submersible Bird-Bath Heater.  I purchased this type of product, Lollyes, Model BSV-HP003/P, 70-watt heater, made in China, in mid October 2023 via Amazon.  While in use in a water-filled birdbath in late January 2024 it started to trip the GFI outlet that powers exterior electrical devices.  As I searched for a replacement on Amazon's site I noticed many similar products have received poor reviews ( 1 star) because they also had a similar short-circuit problems.  The heater I described above has a 3-wire plug, but several models have only a simple 2-prong  power plug.  After my experience and reading reviews I believe strongly that these types of products require a thorough review for potential short circuits and faulty wiring.  Without a GFI, this type of product is a serious shock hazard.  An ohmmeter connected between the power pin the the third-wire (green) pin measured a resistance of 20,000 ohms.  That value means a "leakage" of about 5.5 milliamperes,  which could cause death.
justification: The product poses a serious shock hazard with potential for death, and similar products have frequent reports of short-circuit issues.

incident_description:
I own a Frigidaire electric oven. 
Serial number:VF11213600
Model number: FFEF3054TSP
On Tuesday January 30th, 2024 I (31 year old woman) was in my kitchen and preheated my oven to 425 degrees which Ive done many times before. Once preheated I placed my bread pan into the oven, closed the oven door, and set a timer for 25minutes. My 3 year old daughter and I then went outside to play in the yard. After 25minutes we came back inside, I opened the oven door and I took the cover off my bread pan. Once the cover was off I closed the oven door and set a timer for 10 minutes so my bread could continue to bake. My daughter and I went back outside to play in the yard. Once the 10 minute timer was done, we came back inside. When we got into the kitchen I saw that the front glass panel of my oven door had shattered and exploded glass shards all over the kitchen floor. I immediately shut the oven off, got my daughter somewhere safe and started inspecting the area. The force at which the glass shattered was evident because I found glass shards on my counter tops and dinner room table. Once I took a picture of the oven and glass all over my kitchen floor; I began to clean up. I am reporting this because I [REDACTED] my specific model and found reviews on home depot where this exact thing has happened to other people who own this exact oven. In some cases the oven wasnt even on. This is extremely dangerous. I have a 3 year old daughter and we love to bake together.  She also loves to watch our baked goods through the oven window as they bake. I keep thanking God we went back outside to play. If her little face would have been by that glass door watching our bread bake when it exploded she would have been severely injured. I have called Frigidaire and made a complaint but they didnt seem to be concerned.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no reported injuries, but the potential for severe injury was high.

incident_description:
My Whirlpool electric range model WFE525S0HZ0 overheated food and filled the house with smoke. Bake temp was set to 450 degrees F. to toast bread. After allowing the oven to pre-heat, the food was inserted. Two to three minutes after inserting the food, the house filled with smoke released from the burning food in the interior of the oven. No injuries or damage to the house occurred due to smoke detector alarming, direct supervision of the oven, and actions taken by the user which included turning off the oven, opening the oven door, opening the house windows, and letting the oven cool off and the smoke clear.

After letting the oven cool down, I attempted set the bake mode to 350 degrees F., allowed the oven to pre-heat, then inserted a fresh set of bread. While observing the oven cooking the food, the bread began to overheat within a minute after closing the door. I removed the food before it began to burn. The ambient heat from within the oven felt much higher than usual.  It appeared that the broiler element was red-hot and may have been stuck in the on position which caused the food to overheat. It appears that this caused the inside of oven to reach a much higher temperature than the 350 F. which was reported on the control panel. The product documentation indicates that the broiler element is used during the pre-heating cycle and should turn off after the oven has come up to temperature. The broiler element remaining on leads me to believe that the product failed to switch off the element after the pre-heat cycle and caused it to overheat. My safety concern is that the product failed in an unsafe configuration and the temperatures inside the oven were much higher than the reported 350 F.
justification: The incident involved an overheating oven that filled the house with smoke, but no injuries or property damage occurred due to prompt user action.

We are still negotiating with support.

Samsung refrigerator, model RF22K9381SR

Who was using the product
Myself and my husband.

How were the products being used:
We were using the refrigerator and freezer to keep food. 

Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened?
No, but there was illness.

[REDACTED]

incident_description: On December 19, 2023, I turned my Bosch dishwasher on, and in just a few minutes I started smelling like something was burning. Tracked the smell to the dishwasher and noticed flames in the lower left corner. Called 911 immediately. The fire department came right away. Meanwhile, poured a couple of cups of water in that corner and the fire luckily went out. The firemen removed the dishwasher and stored it in my garage. There was no damage to any cabinetry. The only damage was on the dishwasher, where a piece of plastic was completely burnt and even made a hole all the way to the inside of the dishwasher! This indicated that the fire started in the dishwasher. The next day, I called Bosch and told them what happened. They opened a safety case and a technician came the next day to assess the situation. The technician confirmed that the fire must have started in the dishwasher, but could not tell how that happened since there are no electrical parts near that spot. He called Bosch and they asked him to send pictures and a report. He did that right in front of me. Eventually, Bosch called me and said that since it has been a bit over a year since I bought the dishwasher, it is not covered by the warranty and I have to go through my Lowe's extended warranty.  I argued that this is not a warranty case but a serious safety case. They said they understood, but I have to go through Lowe's anyway. I was amazed by how they did not care to figure out what caused the dishwasher to spontaneously start a fire. Lowe's did stand behind their extended warranty and gave me store credit that covered the price of a new ([REDACTED]) dishwasher and its installation. The Bosch dishwasher was hauled away. I still thought I should bring this safety issue to your attention.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher but resulted in no injuries or damage beyond the appliance itself, indicating a moderate severity with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
Product: KitchenAid 25.8 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator in Stainless Steel with Platinum Interior (Model Number KRMF706EBS01)

Issue: Repeated mold growth, water leakage, and potential food contamination

Summary:

This report details my experience with a faulty KitchenAid refrigerator, highlighting concerns about product safety and consumer protection. Since its purchase in 2018, the refrigerator has experienced:

Mold growth: Persistent mold appeared in the ice maker area within 3 years. This mold spread to stored fruits, vegetables, and dairy products, raising health concerns for my family.
Faulty temperature control: We identified a faulty sensor related to temperature regulation as the likely cause of mold growth.
Manufacturer inaction: Despite repeated attempts to address the issue through [REDACTED] (the manufacturer's authorized service provider), the problem worsened.
Additional damage: Water leakage from the fruit and dairy drawers is now damaging our wooden floors.
Inadequate customer service: The manufacturer only offered a 15% discount on a new appliance despite the severity of the issue and the expired warranty.
Concerns:

Health hazard: Mold contamination in food poses a serious health risk to my family and potentially other consumers.
Product defect: The faulty sensor suggests a design or manufacturing flaw that may endanger other users.
Poor service: The lengthy troubleshooting process and insufficient compensation demonstrate a lack of concern for consumer safety and satisfaction.
Financial burden: We incurred costs for a temporary refrigerator and deep freezer due to the unusable state of the original unit.
Request:

I urge the CPSC to investigate this issue and take the following actions:

Launch a formal investigation: Assess the potential health risks associated with mold growth and leakage in this model.
Issue a public safety advisory: Warn consumers about the potential dangers of the KRMF706EBS01 model and instruct them on necessary precautions.
Hold KitchenAid accountable: Demand a recall or repair program for affected units to ensure consumer safety.
Review manufacturer practices: Assess KitchenAid's customer service and warranty policies to ensure fairness and protect consumers from defective products.
Supporting Documents:

I am attaching copies of purchase receipts, service records, photos of the mold growth and water leakage, and communications with [REDACTED] and KitchenAid.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I urge you to take immediate action to protect consumers from the dangers associated with this faulty refrigerator.
justification: Mold growth and water leakage pose health risks and property damage, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I have reached-out to Frigidaire in the past.

After many threats, they replaced the original cooktop (~$1,300.00), which was turning itself on and eventually caught fire. They chose NOT to collect the unit that turned itself on and caught fire.

It cost me ~$400 to have a wider cut-out created in my quartz countertop to accommodate the replacement cooktop.

The replacement then did the same thing; turned itself on and caught fire. Many more contacts ensued with Frigidaire telling me to contract for service and pay the bill, but they would give me 20% off of parts. I had the cooktop analyzed, informing Frigidaire the FMEA found:

"The component potentiometers for your dual-burners have faulty, potentiometers with traces which, literally, corrode-away causing the dangerous failure in the performance of your cooktops"

Frigidaire took no action, so I ordered parts and had the cooktop repaired. This cost me ~$700.

Now the same thing has happened - this company KNOWS these units are catching fire, knows the burners turn themselves on "high," while unattended; this time a nearby towel went up in flames! My house has been filled with toxic fumes, four times, now.

It is unacceptable that this company sells these dangerous units; declaring they have zero responsibility once the limited warranty period expires! I still have an >30 year old [REDACTED] cooktop installed in my home; it has never turned itself on nor caught fire...
justification: The cooktop turning itself on and catching fire poses a significant risk, as evidenced by the towel catching fire and toxic fumes filling the house, but no injury or death is reported.

In both cases the stoves were Samsung Model NE63A6511SS and appear to be manufactured approximately one month apart.
justification: The incident involved fires caused by combustibles contacting stove knobs, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Fellow Stagg electric kettle which suddenly started violently spouting boiling water during the boiling process during which the electric base would be completely drenched in boiling water. Water would be spouted up to 1 foot away from the kettle. I reported this to the manufacturer immediately, recommending a recall due to this extreme danger of burning and electric shock, however they did not seem to be interested and blamed me for a user error instead.

As it turns out, this issue is due to a manufacturing error. I found that the filling lid for my kettle has a set of venting holes which were misaligned during the manufacturing process, and the kettle cannot relieve enough pressure through the venting holes in the filling lid during the boiling process, I had recommended to the manufacturer to recall the product and redesign the product with a set screw that would prevent any misalignment of these vent holes. However, they do not seem to be interested. I urge you to immediately force a recall of this product. 

As I found out, I am not the only person with this problem as you can for example, see a [REDACTED] thread on this topic: [REDACTED]

Judging by the age of this thread, I must assume that the manufacturer has been aware of this problem for a long time.

I burnt myself with the hot water coming out of the kettle.
justification: The incident involves boiling water spouting violently, causing burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is a known manufacturing defect, making occurrence likely (4).

It seems the design is bad and definitely unsafe for propane use. I am unsure of what the performance would be or is with natural gas. I believe a recall investigation for safety is warranted.

incident_description:
This is an induction unit with capacitive-touch buttons. Burners are turning themselves on randomly, sometimes while the stove was unattended. We are not leaving any cookware on it unattended because it is clearly a major fire hazard otherwise. When it doesn't turn on randomly, it works great (99.99% of the time).

The first time this happened on around November 15th, I was standing near the range and heard a single beep, and both right burners turned on spontaneously to power setting 8. Luckily I was standing right there and turned them both off.

The second time on November 30th, my girlfriend was cooking dinner. She started pasta boiling on the front right burner, and went to the bathroom. She came back to BOTH right hand burners on, and the rear right burner at power 7, and the front right (pasta) burner had changed itself from P to 4. This scalded and warped a cast iron pan on the rear right burner and filled the house with smoke. I happened to come home at this point, and witnessed her turn both burners off and attempt to turn back on the pasta burner. The pasta burner would not turn on and instead showed an error message.

Since then, the stove has turned the burners on to random power settings on its own multiple times. Power setting "8" is the most common, but other power settings also occur.

This induction range is likely capable of turning a cast iron pan into liquid metal in under 15 minutes at the highest power setting.

Frigidaire has been extremely unresponsive to fixing this stove. To date, I have called Frigidaire customer service 4 times and emailed twice over the course of 6 weeks. Each call I have been promised a call back within specific time frames. To date, I have not received a single call or email back from Frigidaire besides an automated "we received your email" message.
justification: The incident involves burners turning on randomly, causing property damage and potential fire hazard, but no reported injuries or deaths.

This particular jar requires proper screwing onto the base with the blade and should be mounted upside down in the blender. Failure to completely secure or mount the jar correctly prevents the blender from initiating the grinding process. Unfortunately, during the grinding process, the jar unscrewed itself from the base. In an attempt to prevent spills and avoid spraying spices, my wife attempted to secure the jar manually and stop the blender. However, the jar dislodged from the base, resulting in severe lacerations to her middle and ring fingers. The injury caused significant blood loss, immense pain, and dizziness.

Swift action was taken, and my wife was immediately taken to an urgent care facility where she received nine stitches to mitigate further blood loss. Despite being prescribed painkillers, she endured constant pain and disrupted sleep for several weeks. Subsequently, she underwent a procedure at [REDACTED] Hospital to remove the stitches and realign the tissues, as they were not properly positioned due to the substantial blood loss. It took an additional month for her to recover and regain the ability to use her right hand for basic activities. Since the incident, her right-hand ring finger has not functioned normally, and she experiences intermittent pain.

I am prepared to provide medical treatment records and doctor's findings as needed by your office. It is noteworthy that the product details indicate that if a jar is not mounted or screwed properly, the blender is designed to detect this and should not initiate its functioning.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations requiring medical treatment and long-term recovery, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). incident_description:
A fire erupted in my KitchenAid stove, which was purchased/installed in new construction in the late summer of 2016.  The oven had been on preheat mode for approximately five minutes when a muffled noise emitted and suddenly a large orange flame could be seen through the entire oven box window.  There was no food in the oven at the time, the oven was clean, and it was on pre-heat mode for approximately five minutes.  The pre-heat mode had been set to 400-degrees, but it had only attained approximately 300-degrees at the time of the incident.

My wife immediately turned off power to the oven at the unit.  I watched the flame for a period of time that probably was no more than a minute or two.  When I perceived the fire would not extinguish itself, I readied the kitchen fire extinguisher and prepared to open the oven door.  Just as I was about to open the door, the fire seemed to diminish so I waited.  Eventually, the flame disappeared, but considerable smoke was emitting from the rear vents on the stove.  I turned on the overhead exhaust fan, which vents to the outside, and that kept the smoke from further infiltrating the house.  The air that was venting with the smoke was extremely hot, so I was unsure whether the fire was completely out or was continuing to burn behind or underneath the oven.  Eventually though, both the air cooled and the smoke subsided, so I was confident that it was out.  I then went outside and turned off the breaker to the oven, which was on a dedicated switch.  The breaker did not seem to me to have tripped.  

When I was able to open the oven door I saw that the fire had burned through the steel pan on the bottom of the oven box and left a yellow residue to the right of the hole as if under pressure.  If you like, I have pictures of the hole and this residue available.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no injuries or deaths, but significant property damage.

incident_description:
Per the homeowner.- she left the residence around 1300 hours, returned four hours later, and noticed that the dishwasher was still running. She stated that the dishwasher had never run for this long. She opened the dishwasher door around 1730-1745 hours, and smoke immediately came out. 
Initially, the smoke was grey and rapidly turned black. The homeowner called 911 and cut the power at the main electrical panel.
The dishwasher is a General Electric (GE) Monogram series ZBD6880K00SS, serial number RG70724B. The homeowner stated that the house was built in 2014 and that all of the dishwashers in the housing tract had the same units. A recall search on the GE website has several dishwasher recalls, but none after 2006. The same search on the CPSC website returned no results.
Origin and Cause Examination
The fire was contained inside the dishwasher's door. Soot deposits were inside the door frame (between the inner and outer skins) and on the door's locking mechanism. The metal around the lock mechanism was discolored and may have a clean burn from soot deposits being burned off or heated to a point where they were consumed. The door was not disassembled, damaged, or altered by responding fire crews or the on-scene fire investigator. 
For NFIRS reporting, the fire is classified as accidental. Without disassembly and analysis by an electrical engineer, the specific ignition sequence or cause cannot be determined. 
The concern in this fire is that the initial failure sequence did not shut down the dishwasher. The homeowner said she tried to turn the unit off at the control panel, but the system was not working. The initial fault, or the subsequent fire, did not turn off the timer and heating element. Had the homeowner left for an extended period, a high probability exists that the fire in the dishwasher door would have spread to the counter above the dishwasher and subsequently involved the kitchen or the entire home.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher fire with no reported injuries, and the likelihood is unlikely given the specific circumstances and lack of widespread recalls.

incident_description:
Microwave caught fire; Thermador's poor safety record-keeping & follow-up led to long delays 

Our Thermador microwave's internal components caught on fire as we prepared dinner. There was a loud electrical buzzing sound and smoke that smelled like burning electronics and rubber.

We quickly stopped the cooking cycle, and removed the trim siding to unplug the cord, which released a plume of foul smoke (see attached screengrab, with red circle added around rising smoke).


This was the second time a Thermador microwave oven caught fire in our home. The first time, the fire department needed to come and remove the unit from our house, because its components would not stop burning (see attached photos). Thermador then arranged for the unit to be picked up and transported to their laboratory for a safety inspection, and they arranged for a product replacement out of safety concerns. 

This recent time, we again contacted Thermador / BSH Group. The priority cases representative [REDACTED] indicated that standard procedure in such a situation is still to arrange for an in-laboratory inspection and replacement. She tagged the case as a safety and priority issue, and arranged for a home visit by a technician.

The Thermador technician [REDACTED] came and tested the unit, and he watched it catch on fire again in front of his own eyes (see attached video). He said that this was not an uncommon problem for those microwaves.

The technician stated that he was preparing a report with photos, to help arrange for the in-laboratory review and microwave replacement. He said to wait to hear back from the department responsible for safety issues with a resolution. 


But apparently there were no guardrails in place at that department to flag priority safety cases for post-visit follow-up action. We waited, but we did not hear back.  After two months with no follow-up, we contacted Thermador to find out the status of the process.

We then needed to fill in a second representative, [REDACTED], about the situation. And Thermador's record-keeping about the units it distributes was so poor that we needed to email that representative the very same documentation the company had previously emailed us about the unit because she did not already have it or have access to it.  Two weeks later, the representative called back to ask basic information about the company's own product, like whether that model of microwave was a combo unit.

(This suggests to us that Thermador -- incredibly -- may not maintain a comprehensive central database of its own product safety activities or the replacement products it distributes and installs into consumers' homes, depriving the company's own product safety personnel of that important information.

This confusion from the representative about Thermador's product line may also be due in part to Thermador's apparent badging of [REDACTED]-manufactured microwave ovens as Thermador microwaves, according to the [REDACTED] certification mark report discussed in the "product details" section above. That could presumably lead to confusion and lack of product knowledge in a company seemingly using a larger, cheaper competitor's products as its own.)

At that point, we had back-and-forth communication with the representative, to arrange for a laboratory safety inspection and unit replacement. But the representative suddenly stopped replying. We simply got radio silence. After a lengthy period with no response (even longer than her previous delays in responding to messages), eventually we learned from another employee that the representative, who was our point-of-contact in the company, had been transferred to a different department.  Apparently, company policies did not require her to continue communicating about the priority safety cases that she had been assigned once she got a new role in the company ÃÂ even if simply to reply to consumers about her change of position and any hand-off of the cases. Allegedly we should have been left a generic answering machine message asking us to call the company, yet we received no response to multiple email messages continuing to try to follow up.

A third Thermador representative created a new case ticket and we were supposed to get a timely response, which we still have not yet received.

(We'll be glad to provide copies of email messages, call logs, etc., as useful to the CPSC.)


In sum, this mix of:

* lax safety-related case management, 

* poor record-keeping by the company about its product safety actions, including as to its replacement units,

* serious organizational incompetence concerning product safety cases, and 

* the apparent frequency of microwaves catching on fire (according to their own technician), 

draws a disturbing picture for us of the Thermador / BSH product safety environment.

This puts the lie to Thermador / BSH's usual reply on SaferProducts.gov danger reports that "BSH Home Appliances Corporation takes product safety issues very seriously."

We strongly suggest that CPSC investigate these significant failings in product safety handling at Thermador / BSH Group.
justification: The microwave caught fire twice, but no injuries were reported. The technician indicated this was not an uncommon problem, suggesting a likely recurrence.

Went online for help with this and discovered that I had been sold a refrigerator in 2018 that was already involved in a class action lawsuit for this exact issue. Realized these refrigerators might also have an issue with maintaining appropriate temperatures so I bought two refrigerator thermometers and was astonished. Setting the fridge at 36, the thermometer read 40. I left the thermometers in and have observed widely different temperatures, both below and above what the fridge is set at. I am getting nowhere with either Costco nor Samsung and I know I have been sold a refrigerator with more than one design defect in the ice maker but I have always trusted the refrigerator to keep an appropriate temperature and now I am worried we have been repeatedly exposed to food that has been stored at unsafe temperatures.

incident_description: I own a Samsung French door refrigerator model RF263BEAESG\AA. At the end of December 2022, the ice maker in the fridge portion of the appliance was completely iced up and was not producing ice. It could not even be pulled out. When the ice maker freezes up, it also causes ice to build up behind the twin cooling plus unit where the evaporator coils are that then control overall cooling to the fridge. As a result, the fridge stops cooling and food can be held inside at unsafe temperatures. Water also pools under the crisper drawers that can cause mold due to lack of evaporation. I had to remove all food to turn off power to the fridge and let the fridge completely defrost with the doors open. At the beginning of January, the ice maker was fixed per Samsung but the tech told me the issues with freezing behind the twin plus cooling unit would continue. In September 2023,  I noticed my drinks were not as cold as they should be. Ice had once again completely built up behind the panel. On October 12, 2023, I removed all perishable food and set in a cooler. I then turned the power off to the fridge to let the ice defrost completely. On October 13, the ice had defrosted, but I also noticed mold had developed from the lack of cooling between the glass and panel for the water filter. I cleaned it out, and restarted power to the fridge. While the fridge is successfully cooling to date, the fact that it will continue to build up ice, prevent cooling, and create mold or other unstable environments for food is unsatisfactory.
justification: The incident involves repeated equipment malfunction leading to potential food spoilage and mold growth, but no direct injury or death is reported.

Food spoiled, turned black and had to discard. Installed remote thermometers to monitor temps and bottom never got near top temp, food spoiled and after 2 service attempts, spoke with Whirlpool tech direct and was told that is the way the refrigerator worked, there is nothing more they can do.
Contacted Michigan Attorney General, then Whirlpool Executive made contact and after another service fiasco in which the service individual was told by Whirlpool Tech to remove the rubber seal at the rear of the third self. I was told the seal was never intended to be there when manufactured, I however checked with Whirlpool parts and it IS part of the shelf, but the next day it was still 34 top 48 bottom. When confronted with my investigation, Executive then made decision to supply another refrigerator, however THESE REFRIGERATORS WITH A SINGLE COOLING SYSTEM ARE ALL JUNK and there is no way for the fresh food section to maintain a constant temp top to bottom, so a replacement was out of the question.
I rejected any offer from Whirlpool as I made my point in the company agreeing that the refrigerator(s) are faulty, so retained the junk and made a deflector and a compartment seal to direct the cold air down and have maintained a temp for both top and bottom of the fresh food section in the mid 30's.
After seeing [REDACTED] being hung out to dry, thought I'd make contact and prove that Whirlpool manufactures the same junk, as do others with a single cooling system.
Was on vacation and the unit had the same refrigerator as ours, installed the thermometers and low and behold, 36 top shelf, 51 bottom. All the same JUNK. They should be removed from the market.

incident_description:
Samsung RF28HMEDBSR/AA Refrigerator - purchased new about 5 years ago.  It has inconsistent, unsafe temperatures in the freezer and fridge. 

I've noticed high temps occasionally over the years, but in the past few months, I've noticed exceptionally high disparities.  The freezer is set to 0F and the fridge at 34F. The display always shows this is the temperature, but the actual is often much higher. Most often the fridge is at 40F, and the freezer at 10F. However, at least a few times a week, the freezer will be in the mid 30Fs and the fridge in the mid 50F. I take these measurements after the doors have been closed for at least an hour, such as first thing in the morning.

The ice maker also freezes over frequently and drips water under it and out of the dispenser. Ice has to be chipped out of the dispenser to clear it.

It has a 'power cool' feature - when this is manually enabled, it does cool down to below the set temperatures (the fridge will get into the 20Fs). This can only be enabled for a short period of time before it turns off automatically. Usually after this, the fridge stays at a reasonable temperature for a few days.
 
My family has not gotten sick from this yet, that we are aware of, but we have had a lot of food that has spoiled sooner than it should have.
justification: The incident involves unsafe temperature fluctuations leading to food spoilage but no reported injuries, and the issue occurs frequently based on the description.

incident_description:
I am writing to file a complaint against Samsung concerning a refrigerator (Model No: RF28R7201SR) purchased on December 20, 2019. Despite being under warranty, the unit has malfunctioned four times since its purchase, causing significant inconvenience, financial strain, and unsafe food storage.

When the refrigerator breaks, we lose complete control of temperature and the ability to adjust any temperature settings. The issue causes food spoilage, and the food must be removed for the service technician to fix the broken door. The refrigerator has the same repeated problem that occurs yearly where the wiring harness breaks and the ice maker door starts opening and closing repeatedly. When the ice-making door is opened, it leaves an opening in the refrigerator, creating an unsafe refrigerator environment. It cannot be shut off, and all the controls lose functionality. Even the refrigerator light will not turn on. 

One of the most distressing incidents occurred when a crucial repair took approximately seven weeks. During this period, my family and I were forced to rely on alternative means to store perishable goods, which was both inconvenient and costly.
I have made numerous attempts to resolve these issues directly with Samsung, including making ten phone calls, one of which lasted for five hours on Monday, October 9, 2023. No tangible solutions have been provided despite the lengthy discussions and numerous assurances. My efforts to secure a repair appointment have been fruitless, and the poor responsiveness exacerbates the situation.

On October 13th I opened a case with the [REDACTED] since I was not getting a resolution with Samsung directly. I asked them for higher compensation than what was offered so I could purchase a reliable refrigerator. So far, after multiple emails since Oct. 16th, they are trying to schedule another service appointment. They have acknowledged that the refrigerator is of a defective design. I would expect to get at least ten years of life out of a refrigerator. Their behavior has been a complete waste of time, disrespectful, and unsafe to my family. We are already in the process of purchasing a new refrigerator, and now they want to send a technician after all this time. How long is this going to take another month?

Moreover, Samsung offered a partial compensation of $1,106.89 for the ongoing issues. However, despite their assurance, no payment has been received to date. Adding to the disappointment, they have not responded to an email that they requested, further demonstrating a lack of responsibility and customer care.

Furthermore, Samsung advised me to seek a refund from Assurion for the extended warranty purchased. However, this does not address the core issue of the safety of the faulty refrigerator and the irresponsible customer service provided by Samsung.
This ordeal has been incredibly frustrating, and the lack of action from Samsung has left me feeling neglected and undervalued as a customer. I hope that by bringing this matter to the attention of the Better Business Bureau, other consumers can be spared the ordeal that I have been through.

I am requesting a full refund for the refrigerator and the extended warranty, alongside a formal apology from Samsung for the undue stress and inconvenience caused and the unsafe appliance they have sold me.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I am willing to provide further information if required and am hopeful for a satisfactory resolution.


Yours sincerely,

This caught my eye and never thought to check. To my surprise, I put a thermometer in the main part of the fridge and the temp shown was 43 degrees. It's supposed to be at 37. There's no telling how many food items spoiled over the years and caused possible food poising issues. I recall many times have stomach issues and did not make the connect that it could be from my fridge and spoiled food. 

This is clearly a danger to consumers and needs to be addressed. There needs to be a recall. I spent a lot of money for a product that is clearly deflective.

incident_description:
The machine had been not brewing full cups of coffee so I purchased the Keurig descaling solution to descale it.  I followed all instructions, and the machine still failed to brew cups of coffee.  I then unplugged and drained the machine using the two drain tubes in the back, and then refilled the reservoir with the descaling solution to descale again.  When I turned on the unit to descale once more, it indicated "heating" on the display screen.  Not after long, i noticed smoke being emitted from what I would call the overflow nozzle, a small rubber dump tube into the top of the reservoir.  I then quickly unplugged the machine and brought it outside, not before it filled the office with a toxic smoke, presumably caused by the inside of the boiler burning off.

If I had not been attentive to the unit, this could have easily caught our break room on fire, if not our entire building.  

We have attempted to contact the manufacturer, but they are unwilling to resolve the issue amicably.  We believe this machine is unsafe, and has the potential to cause bodily injury and  property damage.

We would like to lodge a formal complaint into this unit due to the issue above, and the company's lack of concern for the safety of their consumers.

incident_description:
Re: Zline gas range/ oven Model RG30: Existing Recall RGRECALL-00449439-Case # [REDACTED]

New email from Zline dated 9.14.23 that there are still product problems- is CPSC aware of this?
Background:
I received the recall notice via email from Zline dated 12.29.22 about the voluntary recall of their product. At the time I did not feel safe keeping the equipment, and now even less so since on 9.14.23 I received a new email from the manufacturer about problems. I have forwarded this today to info@cpsc.gov. 

I am super unhappy that over 9 months later I am getting an email from the company Zline, months after the repair was performed, that the product still has problems and that consumers should be sure to use their fan and make sure the carbon monoxide alarm is working. Seriously? I am 100% not comfortable with this process or the outcome and I want to return this product and get it out of my house as soon as possible. I am concerned that the CPSC even allowed a manufacturer driven repair approach without any (visible) external monitoring. Each and every range/ oven should have had an inspection by a third party to confirm that there is/ was not carbon monoxide being emitted, and probably some kind of ongoing oversight. In any case, I urge the CPSC to take stronger measures with safety issues, and also to require manufacturers to accept and manage returns. I personally request a return, and for Zline to pick up the product and make sure it does not end up in someone else's home. Thank you
justification: The incident involves a product recall due to potential safety issues, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung refrigerator, model # RF27T5241, back in August of 2022. I kept finding flakes of some sort coming out of the water and settling at the bottom of our cups and glasses. At first I thought that maybe I didn't flush out the system enough when I first set it up. but no matter how much water I ran through it, the flakes continued to show up. I bought a couple of new water filters for it thinking that maybe it had a bad filter in it. I replaced the filter, and we still had the same problem. I finally called Samsung and reported it to them and they sent someone out to my home. The man they sent out the first time, paid more attention to the girl he was talking to on the phone than he was to the issue. He first said, what I was seeing were bubbles. After I showed him that those so called bubbles were settling at the bottle of the glass, he indicated that the particles I was seeing had to be calcium deposits coming through my water supply. I advised him that this is the 3rd refrigerator I have had in this home, and we never had any such issue with them. I also stated, that the water filter in the refrigerator should have caught the particles. He denied that and said that the filters don't always catch everything. He asked if I replaced the filter with a Samsung filter, and I advised him that I did. He obviously did not believe me and (without turning off the water supply as the manual indicates), he pulled out the filter, water started flowing out everywhere, and then he slammed the filter back in. So he still insisted it was just calcium coming through and left. I had to replace that new filter because dark water began coming out of the filter. Not to mention that the filter was not placed back on correctly and water was leaking all over the place. I reported all of this to Samsung, and they sent someone else out, who more or less did said the same thing as the first one. Again, I called Samsung because there was no way we were going to drink that water or use the ice from it. When I spoke with someone from Samsung that time, The lady on the phone advised me that if she sent someone out, I would have to pay for it because my 1 year warranty was up in April. I advised her, that I bought the unit in August not April, and if they have it registered to someone else, the unit must have been sold before, taken back to Lowe's, and resold to me. She then stated that someone else will come to the house and check it out again. So the 3rd person came to the home and guess what? He found that there were some damaged parts inside the water filter system and it wasn't calcium coming through the line. The next day, I received a call from Samsung, and was told that they were going to send me out a new unit. I asked if I could get a refund instead because I really didn't trust their product if it has issues this early in the game. The gentleman stated, that the unit will be brand new and last me for years, and not to worry because it will be under a new warranty. So, they sent Lowe's out with another unit and this one turns out to be worst than the last one. We received this one on 06/10/23, and at first, everything worked fine. But right around the 1st of July (the day before we left for our vacation), we noticed that some of the ice cubes in the bottom tray, were stuck together and it didn't seem to have made much more ice. I thought by the time we returned from vacation, the tray would be full again. But when we returned, it didn't make anymore ice. We also noticed that some of the items in the freezer were getting soft. So I called Samsung and reported it to them. They had me unplug the unit, wait several minutes, and then plug it back in. I did that and the temperature inside both the top and the bottom of the refrigerator were lower than they should be. So, I was instructed as to how I could reset the correct temperature on both the top and bottom, then told it could take up to 16 hours before everything was back to normal again. Well, I had to repeat that over and over again on the phone with them until I got fed up with it all. It was apparent, that the compressor was not working correctly. Again, I asked for a refund, but was denied. I asked if they were going to send a new unit, and I was denied that too. Now, we're are about to July 21st without a refrigerator or freezer working properly, and I was told that they will send somebody out to look at it. On the 24th, a man came out to look at it, and sure enough, the compressor was out. I asked if Samsung was going to send out another since we had food going bad, and he indicated that he was going to order the parts for it. I asked how long does that take, and he stated it takes at least a week, but Samsung is a little slower than most of them. As soon as he left, I called Samsung and advised them of what was going on, and could I please have a refund or an exchange, as this now seems like an emergency. And again, I was denied. They can't offer an exchange or a refund, until after the unit has been repaired (like they are going to refund or exchange anything after it's up and running again). I also mentioned (because during calls and waiting times, I did some research, and found that this model is the same as the RF27T5201, except the 5241 model has the dual ice makers, have been on your recall lists since 2020), that the unit has been on a recall list, and it should be handled ASAP. I asked them how soon can I expect to have something going because we need something now. I was then told that as soon as the repairman completes his report, and we receive it, which takes up to 48 hours, then Samsung will make a decision as to what will be done. There isn't anything else the can do until then. So here we sit in the middle of the summer 100 degree weather without a refrigerator. About a week later, I called the repair shop and asked if the parts came in yet, and I was told that the parts had been received, but the only person qualified to work on it could not get out to my home until the following Thursday (it was on a Friday when I called, so that meant it would be another week). Well, the following Thursday, the repairman came by. All he really did (that I could see), was shoot some Freon into the system. The repairman stated that the unit wasn't properly filled correctly from the factory. Then I waited about a week before calling Samsung back because one of the people that I first spoken with when I called about these issues, told me to make a list of all the food that gets spoiled because Samsung will give me a food voucher to replace it all. I advised my other half as to what I was told, so she began making a list. Now, we usually only shop once a month because we are on fixed incomes, so at the time this all began, we had already done all of that shopping. The unit was very full both top and bottom. When I spoke with an agent from Samsung about having a list, he asked me to send the list to him, and I did. I figured with all the meats, seafood, and poultry alone would be an easy $250.00. Then most likely another, at least $200.00 with everything else we had in there. The agent offered me $200.00. I told him he must be out of his mind. He said that's all he can offer because Samsung doesn't cover this and that and the other (like everything else we had to replace was going to be free). I brought up again that with all we have been through with both of their refrigerators, I would still prefer a refund because even after this one had been fixed, I do not trust Samsung's refrigerators. Again, he said all he could do was give me $200.00. I was so upset with him, that I told him that was not acceptable, in fact, all he did was insult me and I could not deal with him any further and I hung up the phone. But as to how the refrigerator is working now, well, the temperatures on both the top and bottom (because I purchased my own thermometers), have been going up and down and not keeping a constant temperatures. I think that I better start saving my money to buy a new refrigerator to replace this Samsung unit.

The hot plate on the machine that keeps the pot warm was very hot to to touch and would burn someone, which is possible given that the machine was not activated by the user and showed nothing on the display/LEDs indicating it had turned on.  The machine had clearly failed "on", the display was blank and it was unresponsive to button pushes.  

I replaced this machine with an identical unit through a warranty return.  The replacement coffee maker did the exact same thing after a few uses.  

This appears to be the same problem reported on report number [REDACTED] by a different consumer.  A cursory review of some retail websites with consumer reviews indicates that this failure mode has been happening on this model.  Additionally, given that I encountered it on two different machines (one purchased locally, one shipped from Sunbeam) that were acquired in mid-2023 it may be widespread.
justification: The incident describes a machine that can burn someone due to malfunction, and similar issues are reported by other consumers, indicating a likely and injurious problem.

incident_description:
I am reporting two incidents spanning apx 4 months, because despite several emails to Bertazzoni Customer Care, Customer Service, After Sale Service and what turned out to be the Marketing Division, the only reply was from Marketing.  I emailed customer support at Bertazzoni on April 14, 2023 regarding a cooling fan, whereby a wire was rubbing into the blade, causing cuts to the blade and the wire, hence it's failure.  I wrote to Bertazzoni that this should have been picked up in their inspection process because the fan was very loud.  We have never owned anything like this and simply assumed that's the way a Professional model sounds, however I received no reply.  The cutting of the wire certainly could have caused a short, this being a clear indication of "Faulty Wiring" and not a component failure. 

The second incident was when the small side oven blew up at 330 deg. F, as the unit was reaching a temperature of 350deg. F, (I place an oven thermometer in the unit, as this doesn't have one). I was standing in front of the unit, when I heard a loud rocking boom, and turned to see a bright white light in the electric oven.  I immediately turned off the oven, opened the door and smoke billowed out.

We had the same repairman out and he indicated it was due to the Baking Element (coil).  After he removed the floor plate from the oven, you could see where the insulation was burned through to the bottom spanning a distance of apx 11" long and 2.5" wide. His helper indicated he just viewed a safety video where this type of fire can continue to burn, even after the unit is unplugged. Upon doing my own research, it is written that the primary cause of this incident is "Faulty Wiring". Needless to say I was very shaken, knowing this unit may be compromised and now feeling unsafe using the primary oven which is much larger. As of this writing, we are waiting on this component as it is out of stock and on a 4 week back order. The part is ordered through Bertazzoni. 
 I should add the unit is one year out of a 2 year manufacturers warranty, (3 yrs old), however, as previously mentioned, this isn't product failure. In my opinion, the reason I haven't received one reply is that no one wants to touch this with a 10 foot pole, so the saying goes.

To complete the questions, I was not hurt, I am the primary user. This model is manufactured for home use, not commercial.
justification: The incident involved faulty wiring and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
For the past month, my family has been purchasing groceries from [REDACTED] and we have noticed a recurring issue with the quality of the products, particularly regarding the milk. We've observed that the milk consistently goes bad within just a few days of purchase. Initially, we attributed this problem to [REDACTED], as the internal temperature of our Samsung refrigerator, as displayed on its LCD screen, was consistently at 34 degrees Fahrenheit. It seemed plausible that [REDACTED] might be selling spoiled milk. Additionally, we found that the cheese we had purchased from [REDACTED] had rapidly developed mold and emitted a foul odor. Consequently, we opted to explore alternative grocery shopping options, believing that there might be a lapse in quality control at [REDACTED].

Around a week ago, our 16-year-old daughter fell seriously ill. She woke up in the middle of the night, experiencing severe vomiting and diarrhea. As parents, we initially suspected she might have contracted the Norovirus or a similar stomach bug, as we had exclusively consumed food prepared at home and hadn't eaten from outside food sources. Our daughter's recovery took approximately five days before she was fit enough to attend school again, having missed her first day of school. It's noteworthy that while neither parent experienced any illness, the potential highly infectious nature of the Norovirus led us to consider the possibility of food poisoning. It's important to highlight that our daughter maintains a vegetarian diet, which differs from our own, and she had been consuming distinct food items. During the time of her illness, she had been consuming food from our primary storage area, while we, her parents, were consuming frozen food from the freezer.

A few days later, the mother had a bowl of cereal and promptly noticed that the milk had also gone sour. This milk had been purchased just three days prior from [REDACTED], a part of the [REDACTED] chain, and the expiration date was still a week away. This discovery prompted us to realize that there was more to this situation than we had initially thought.

In an attempt to understand the root cause of these issues, we placed a thermometer in the fridge on the middle shelf. Although the fridge's LCD panel continued to indicate a temperature of 34 degrees Fahrenheit, the thermometer registered a significantly higher temperature of 54 degrees Fahrenheit. To eliminate the possibility of temperature variations at the front of the fridge, where the doors open, we relocated the thermometer to the back. Throughout the day, the readings consistently ranged between 53 and 54 degrees Fahrenheit. Despite our efforts, utilizing the "power cool" button adjacent to the LCD panel yielded no positive results.

Our Samsung fridge, which was acquired in late 2015, has been a recurring source of trouble. Over the years, we've been compelled to defrost it once or twice annually due to the accumulation of ice around the evaporator coils, causing the fan to emit disruptive noises. Each defrosting cycle produces over a gallon of water from the evaporator coils. This consistent issue has made the fridge a persistent headache, and now we find ourselves with an expensive appliance that is unusable and unsellable. Continuing to use this fridge poses a direct danger to the safety of our family.

In response to these circumstances, we have been forced to discard all the contents of the fridge and subsequently purchase new groceries, storing them in an icebox. Unfortunately, we are left with no functional refrigerator aside from an older mini fridge situated in our garage.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious illness (vomiting and diarrhea) of a family member, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The recurring issue with the fridge and spoiled food suggests a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description:
My wife's Blendjet 2 started running on it's own yesterday, couldn't be shutoff for 10+ minutes, overheated, smoked and melted the casing!

My wife had used her Blendjet 2 for breakfast Saturday August 26th as per normal, cleaned it out and left it on the kitchen counter near the paper towel holder with the lid off but the main container still attached.

Over two hours later we were in the garage getting ready to leave the house and came back inside to get something and heard a whirring sound that we tracked down to the Blendjet running on the kitchen counter with the blades turning.  We pressed the button to turn it off and it sped up to normal mixing speed!  So we pressed the button again and it slowed down but didn't stop.  We repeated this process numerous times with similar results and were unable to stop the motor and the spinning blades.  We tried holding the button to reset it, nothing worked.  The lights flashing were sometimes red but nothing would turn it off.  

Not sure what to do we put it down on the counter away from other things hoping the battery would die soon.  A few minutes later my wife yelled out to me in the garage that the Blendjet 2 was smoking!  I grabbed it and took it out onto the driveway away from the house and cars.  I took off the clear plastic container part assuming there would be an automatic safety shutoff to protect users from the spinning blades, and it still didn't stop!

By now it was getting pretty hot to hold and so I dropped the base with spinning blades on the driveway to try to break it and stop it which didn't work.  We then thought to try to video it and managed to capture the last second of it running with the blades spinning as it rolled around on the sidewalk.  

After it finally stopped I tried to pick it up and it was too hot to hold.

I took a picture of the melted casing.  

My wife never dropped this Blendjet 2 or submersed it in water.  

Had this happened just a few minutes later, after we had left the house, this Blendjet 2 could have easily caused a fired which could have destroyed our house!

We also sent this report to the manufacturers customer support department.
We are not looking for a replacement.  We only want to warn others of this dangerous situation and the failure of at least two safety features on this Blendjet 2 (auto shutoff after 30 seconds, and a shutoff when the container is not attached).

incident_description: Went into our kitchen, smelled a very strong odor of gas. incident_description: I purchased a Samsung 3-door Refrigerator in April 2020. The unit was within normal working parameters until April 2022. I began noticing ice build up in the vents at the back of the refrigerator section. This build-up did not affect any part or operation of the unit at this time. At the end of April 2022, I noticed my deli drawer at the bottom of the unit was stuck, it wouldn't move. Thanks to a layer of ice that formed, the drawer was going nowhere. I also noticed that food was going bad quicker than it normally would. The temperature from the top shelf reported 55F when the panel read 37F. Each week, I would remove the deli drawer and break out the layer of ice that had accumulated before drying it out. At the end of May 2022, food stored in the unit began to spoil within days of purchasing. A gallon of milk had spoiled within a day. In June of 2022, I had my first repair bill for it for $350. Samsung had scheduled the repair from a company on their authorized lists. Upon arrival, the repair person knew within moments of the issue, as they described this situation as the most common one they face: a faulty temperature sensor. This sensor messages the coolant system telling it if the fridge needs colder or to stand down. This fluctuation from the sensor's failure caused ice build-up that blocks the air vents, which raises the internal temperature. The fix was immediate and had no further issues until March of 2023. The ice build-up was back and I began removing it every two weeks. I reached out to Samsung asking for the repair to a device they replaced less than a year ago, but was told there was no authorized repairfolk in the {REDACTED] area so I would have to schedule my service and then file a claim to see IF the warranty of only the sensor would be covered (but there may be other 'issues' discovered'). At the time, the ice removal was not a huge issue so I did nothing In May of 2023, my food began to spoil within days of purchasing, again. Contacting Samsung, I was told there was now an authorized repair company that could schedule the appointment but I would have to pay $425 upfront to schedule it. I never had to do that with the first repair and this new appointment is essentially fixing the original repair's problem. Furiously, I decided not to continue the conversation with Samsung and attempt alternative routes. I concluded that if the sensor was the simple fix, then I could do it. After days of reviewing several videos and articles on the subject, as this issue with Samsung's units has been going on since 2017, I felt confident enough to screw off a panel, remove the ice build-up, and replace this sensor piece. The operation went text-book well. I was closing up the operation when I had not realized that the final 2 screws were not catching the receiving end for fastening. Realizing I placed the wrong screws in, I began removing the first incorrectly placed screw when a high-pressure burst of gas spewed out around the screw. I had punctured the coil which circulated the refrigerant gas. Unknowing the toxicity of the gas, I closed the unit doors immediately and removed my roommate and myself from my townhouse. After spending a wasteful 20 minutes with Samsung support on ascertaining how toxic this gas was, I discovered that we were in no danger by my research for an MSDS sheet on the gas. My issues are these: how are these products still being produced when they knowingly have continuous errors in their temperature sensors? If they claim they didn't, then their research department should be fired.  [REDACTED] knew that this has been an issue since 2017. The only logical conclusion is that Samsung has designed these units to fail on purpose. FOR EXAMPLE: why is there a vital tube behind a screw hole? Why need two different length screws when you could have designed it only to have one, eliminating the chance a consumer would be confused, [REDACTED] even a repairperson could get confused. I don't think I'm an Einstien-level genius, but as a licensed architect, I understand the purpose and why things are built the way they are. This product was designed to fail. That failure has costed me with lost food, pointless repairs, and poses a hazard to my health. This is not only unprofessional of Samsung but unethical. I am blown away that this has been allowed.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous gas release but no injury occurred, and the issue is a known recurring problem with the product.

I took the first picture at 9:05pm from a distance, due to being barefoot, and you can see that the control/display panel showed everything was off and only the time was showing.  The external smoke colored glass was shattered.  Once I had my shoes on, I started walking around the kitchen and I stood back because I kept hearing the external shattered glass popping as pieces were still being projected onto the floor.  I slowly approached from the left side and felt the ovenÃÂs intact clear glass and it was very hot.  I then tried to partially open the oven door to let the heat out, but the shattered glass kept popping and falling so I re-closed the door.  I believe opening the oven door helped relieve any pressure heat in the oven and the island saved me from getting hit by the flying glass.  Medium to very small pieces of different shaped glass were to the left and right of the oven, up on the countertops, thrown behind the butter dish, and down the hallway to the spare bedrooms, in addition to being behind the family room chair near me.
  
I texted our apartment manager, [REDACTED], and called their emergency line where [REDACTED], the maintenance lead, and [REDACTED] showed up around 10:00pm.  The clear glass on the oven was still hot even though the oven showed turned off and just had the time.  They started cleaning up the glass and around 11:00pm the clear glass was still warm to the touch.  [REDACTED] then decided to shut off the apartmentÃÂs main circuit panel to the oven.
  
I have read there have been unexplained explosions of glass and that the Consumer Product Safety Commission says safety glass should break into nuggets and not shards.  But these pieces of glass were very sharp, and some were like arrows.  I have two independent witnesses that help clean up the broken glass and they had to double up the garbage bag due to the sharpness of the glass pieces.  If I had been hit by these shards of glass at the high velocity speed it broke, they would have punctured my eyes, sliced my face, skin, neck etc.  I was by myself, and I could have been badly injured and unconscious bleeding for an hour and half before my husband came home from work. 
   
The display/control panel did not show anything was turned on, yet this oven got extremely hot to cause this explosion and rapid velocity spray of the external smoke colored glass.  I read how they blame people for resting things on the glass, or damaging the glass, or a crack in the glass that grew, or how people use the glass to shut the metal shelves and more.  This was not the case with our oven. None of those reasons explain why the oven was hot for three hours while showing it was off.  Plus, this is a two-year-old oven, barely used, by two very meticulous and careful adults with no children in the apartment.
 
Something needs to be done before someone is hurt.  If I had been within range and the island hadnÃÂt been between the oven and I, then those high velocity shards of glass would have easily placed me in the hospital.  Glass powerful enough where it shoots out, smashes against an island, and then flies 4 feet to the sides behind butter dishes, against backsplashes, and down hallways is powerful enough to have caused severe damage to me or someone else.  

I can send pictures if you can tell me how/where I can do that, if this system doesn't allow me to upload them. 
 
I look forward to a reply on how these ovens that are turning on/staying on with no notice, heating up so intense that it causes glass to become high velocity projectiles or potentially can cause a fire are going to be corrected.

But we contact GE again because we were worried for our kids and our own safety and not satisfied with the resolution giving by the third party tech. incident_description:
I have owned my Bobby Flay cookware for about 6 years. I was cooking a hamburger patty in the small pan on my kitchen stovetop on May 11, 2023 at about 5pm when all of a sudden something like a gunshot went off in my kitchen. I was standing right next to the stove, chopping vegetables. It was so loud I covered my ears and heard ringing. I wasn't sure what had happened, but I could tell it came from the stove. As I went to go turn off the burner, it happened again and I could hear that it was happening in the pan itself. On the countertop, I found a round piece of metal. I moved the pan off the burner and took the splatter guard off the pan, removed the hamburger, looked to see if I could see any metal on it and found none on the outside of the burger, so I put it in the micro to continue cooking. As I inspected the pan, I could see that it was a piece of metal from where the handle attaches to the pan that had somehow become dislodged and became a projectile. I could only find one piece, but not the other. As I sat down to eat my burger, I bit into the other piece of metal. It had literally shot into the middle of my hamburger meat!
     I have never had cookware bullets flying around my kitchen! I am so glad that my daughter had not been cooking that day or that I did not get hurt. I'm also glad my micro didn't blow up from cooking metal! But I feel the need to report this to anyone and everyone I can, as what happened was EXTREMELY dangerous! Please do a recall or something on these pans. I can't help but think "What would have happened if I had the matching glass lid on that pan" that day, or no cover! Super scary! I threw away the metal pieces, but have taken a comparison picture of the broken pan and unbroken pan so you can see where the problem is. Now I have to replace all of these pans, as well, since I am afraid of this happening again. As you can see from the photos, the pan on top is missing the tops of the metal caps, while the bottom pan still has them.

incident_description:
I purchased a Wolf CI304C/B induction cooktop. When this unit was turned on and used to heat cookware, the cookware emitted a sound that forced anyone in the room to leave. This happened consistently, on multiple occasions, with several varieties of highly-regarded induction-compliant cookware. Using a phone app, this sound was measured at 19,688 Hz, with an estimated intensity of at least 93 dB at normal working distance. (Given frequency roll-off, it's very probably higher than that.) Note that 85 dB is the generally-recognized level at which long-term exposure causes hearing loss.

Since most adults can no longer hear at such high frequencies, this is not a commonly reported issue. That means this problem is specifically A DANGER TO CHILDREN WHICH WILL CAUSE HEARING LOSS, and one which their parents generally cannot perceive!

I'm an electrical engineer, and I spent nine years of my career designing switching power electronics similar to induction cooktops in many respects. The pans ring, just by the nature of induction heating. However, the fact that the cooktop operates within the human hearing range is a design choice by the manufacturer, and it is this design choice that is at the root of this hazard. No specific unit defect would have this result; the entire product line is a threat to public safety. As a licensed engineer, I am ethically obligated to report threats to public safety. So here I am.

I reported this problem to Wolf, who said, "We do not have actual decibel ratings for most of our products but I assure you we are within market standards." This implies the problem is likely to exist across the entire industry, not just within Wolf. A friend measured the sound from a [REDACTED] induction cooktop and found the same ~20 kHz spike, though we were not able to effectively compare decibel measurements.
justification: The incident describes a consistent hazard causing potential hearing loss, particularly to children, due to high-frequency noise from the cooktop.
