incident_description:
Today I experienced a terrifying and dangerous situation with my household Frigidaire oven/range unit. Our house came with Model # FFEF3054TSH, Serial # VF83504619 and we use both the stove-top/range and the oven portions of this unit in typical fashion, just cooking meals for two (nothing fancy). We had not had any issues or damages to either the cooking surfaces or the interior or exterior of the unit prior to this dangerous situation. The unit I am reporting was not in use during its spontaneous explosion, and had been out of use for over twelve hours prior. On May 1, 2023 at around 4:00pm CST I was opening mail at my kitchen counter when I heard a loud explosion. Out of the corner of my eye I watched the tempered glass window from the front of my oven blow off and scatter throughout my kitchen and living area. I realized quickly that the explosion I heard was the glass being blown out and broken from the front of my oven. 

While I am grateful that the only injuries sustained during this incident occurred to my fingers while cleaning up the shards of tempered glass, the event was scary and the fact it occurred completely spontaneously, when the unit was not in use and had not been used in over twelve hours prior makes it a dangerous product. I am lucky that I was home and able to prevent my pets from walking across the glass and cutting their feet, but not every consumer will have or has had this same luck and people are at risk when purchasing, using, or having this product from this company. When researching the situation online, it is very apparent that my household is not the only one to have this issue with Frigidaire oven glass exploding, and we are also not the only ones to be denied reimbursement, assistance, and the opportunity to file a proper complaint with the company. In fact, this seems to be an increasingly common issue with this specific company. I have not been allowed to file a complaint, and now I am torn between paying hundreds of dollars to repair the glass on a unit that I no longer trust to operate (or exist) safely, or spend even more money purchasing a brand new oven/range unit from a company with better safety reputations and customer service. Either way, this spontaneous explosion has created a significant financial setback for my household, and we are angry that the company responsible for ensuring the safety of their product is refusing to make it right. Not only would I like to report a dangerous product, I would like to report a dangerous company who couldn't care less about the safety of consumers or about taking responsibilities for their own faulty product. 

I am happy to provide more information as well as images depicting the damage. I do consider myself lucky, but I am still negatively affected by this occurrence and I want to help make sure it doesn't happen to others. Again, there are so many news reports, forums, reviews, and more available that highlight this same issue with this same company. It could have been so much worse. Please put a stop to these dangerous products being available on the market. Now that I know how Frigidaire handles dangerous and faulty products and customer service, I would never recommend them for anyone or anything, ever.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts from glass shards) and the description indicates this is a recurring issue with the product.

incident_description:
I am writing regarding extensive mold lurking in the lids of Nespresso's Nomad Travel Mugs. 

My husband and I have three Nomad mugs, two 18 oz., and one 13.5 oz. All three mugs have pop down tops with a center that depresses allowing for 360 degree drinking. We've had health annoyances and coffee that would curdle for one of us, but not the other on some days. When the coffee curdled again we decided to look into the lids. Prior to this, we have followed the directions that require only that the product is  soaked if not washed immediately, and if placed in the dishwasher that the lid is washed in the "open" position so water can flow through the cup. When we discovered mold in all three cups, I first pressure washed two of the three cups (cups A and B in the images) with the sink faucet before soaking in water and vinegar, then disassembling disassembling the lid as much as can be done (with the inner "pop" lid and outer spring removed, but the innermost spring locked inside). The third lid (lid C) was disassembled and soaked without any pressure washing, so the image shows even more of the mold and coffee left hiding in what appeared to be a "clean" mug.

Once soaked in vinegar and water overnight, I tried pressure washing each of the inner springs in the lids again and used bottle top brushes of different sizes and stiffness to try to clean the inner springs of the visible remnants within them. The photo of the inner springs is attempting to show you that there are still coffee and mold remnants stuck below that spring. Even the parts of the inner spring that look clean can be lifted and then scraped below with a toothpick to remove more residue. 

Which leads me to this:  these lids pose a serious health risk to consumers; they must be recalled.  The instructions do not tell consumers how to even clean as far as I was able to; they were disassembled by force and without direction. But more importantly, they ultimately cannot be FULLY disassembled. That inner ring that cannot be removed, that is tucked into the center ring, that every ounce of beverage passes through, harbors mold. I have called Whirlpool several times and told them I believe the design to be defective and dangerous and asked for my money back. I told service I believe the drying cycle drives steam and/or water past the gasket, melting the adhesive on the control panel and this allows water in the form of steam, vapor or liquid to enter the control module cavity, corroding it and shorting it out. Whirlpool customer service told me the 3rd party service co. must come to repair it regardless and they will keep repairing it until the service manager declares the unit to be "nonrepairable". They have a long case file on my complaint listed under my name, address and telephone number, I was told. Frankly, I have washed more dishes than this dishwasher has. This cannot be coincidence since it keeps happening in the same place and way across two similar models. incident_description:
I was using a Dash Rapid Egg Cooker this afternoon to make hard boiled eggs. The Rapid Egg Cooker is a small appliance that plugs into the wall, but it also has a power button for turning the appliance on. I was using the product for the first time after it had been in storage for a few months, and I placed it on my kitchen counter and plugged it in while I measured water and arranged the eggs in the accompanying plastic tray. Before adding water to the product's hot plate and pressing the power button, I noticed that there was a bit of dust or debris on the hot plate's surface, and so I tried to quickly brush it off so that it wouldn't burn onto the surface. However, unbeknownst to me, the product was already switched on, even though I had not pressed the power button, and even though the hot plate was dry. I burned two fingers due to touching the hot plate; luckily, the burns appear to be minor, first-degree burns. I only noticed afterward that the Rapid Egg Cooker's indicator light was on, and found that pressing the power button did nothing: it's not possible to turn the unit off without either unplugging it or allowing it to become hot enough to automatically turn off.

Upon consulting the manual, I noticed this warning: "ATTENTION: Do not unplug the unit while cooking. If you unplug the unit while cooking, it will still be turned on when you plug it back in. If the unit does not detect water on the Heating Plate, it will automatically shut off and reset itself in a few seconds." I do not know whether the hot plate had been unplugged while it was cooking, but this evening, I tested a hunch. I did manage to successfully cook eggs after the incident, so I had observed the product turn off after the water boiled off. So, I took the unplugged, cold cooker, and pressed the power button. Upon plugging the cooker in, it was on. It took over a minute - a far cry from a few seconds - to automatically shut off. This means that any accidental motion that could push the button (for instance, bumping into another object while the product is in storage) can cause the cooker to start immediately without intentionally pressing the power button, greatly increasing the likelihood of this type of injury.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns (injury), and the design flaw makes it likely to occur again if the cooker is bumped or mishandled.

incident_description:
I own a "30 in. 5.4 cu. ft. Induction Electric Range with Self-Cleaning Oven in Smudge-Proof Stainless Steel with Air Fry" by Frigidaire that I purchased in May of 2022. The oven has buttons to operate the burners rather than physical switches. Two times now I have heard beeping coming from the oven, and when I went into the kitchen I have found that the oven had registered inputs from the buttons despite no human or animal being anywhere near the stove. In the most recent incident, at roughly 3am on March 23, I was awoken by beeping coming from my kitchen, and came downstairs to find that the oven had started a one minute timer and turned the oven light on.

In the previous instance, the oven turned a burner on to the highest power setting. (There happened to be a clean non-stick frying pan sitting on top of the oven when this happened - I believe the oven needs to detect the presence of a pan in order to turn on.) On the highest power setting an empty pan would vaporize it's non-stick coating within minutes (if not seconds) and plausibly even melt the pan. Furthermore, if the oven had other flammable items in the vicinity when this happened, it's easy to imagine it starting a fire. Fortunately I made it into the room within 30 seconds and was able to turn off the burner (and remove the pan) before this happened.

I've turned off the oven at my home circuit breaker and don't plan to leave it energized when not using it, due to what I perceive to be an extreme fire hazard from an oven that can randomly turn itself (or its burners) on at any time, and am contacting Frigidaire.

I purchased T-fal frying pans from Walmart in Shelby Twp, MI.  One about a year ago and the other one about 4 years ago.  I was using them to fry eggs, brown hamburger etc with a gas stove. When I took a picture of the two emblems, I also noticed that the one pan also has little yellow markings across the whole cooking area and they are all crumbling off as well.  I'm not sure if we have injuries from this situation, as we have been internalizing this teflon and paint material for some time now.  I notified T-fal company by email and they said this:     Dear [REDACTED],


Thank you for your email via https://www.t-falusa.com. 

Please note based on the pictures provided we could not determine a manufacturing related cause and thus it would not be subject to replacement under the terms of our warranty. This determination was reached by the discoloration from overheating.

Cookware with non-stick coatings should be used on low to medium heat settings, because due to the superior quality of our cookware, the cookware will heat up quicker and retain the heat longer. Overheating of the non-stick coating will cause the non-stick properties to break down. As a result, you will find that foods are sticking to the cookware. Another indication that your pan has been overheated is that your cookware has turned a brown or rusty color. If the pan has warped, buckled, flaking , cracked, rippled, layers have separated or there is some other gross defect, we would recommend not using the pan any longer.
 
Overheating of the cookware is not covered under the terms of the warranty.
 

If you have any additional questions, please call 1-800-395-8325 and provide the consumer service agent with reference number [REDACTED]. Representatives are available from Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 5:00 pm EST.

 

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]

T-fal Consumer Service

This is a severe safety issue and I would like our unit fixed so the hot indicator light does not go off until the temperature is below 100 degrees Farenheit. incident_description:
I gave birth to my son on [REDACTED]. His birth weight was 9.1lbs. We came home from the hospital a few days later on Sunday 2/12/2023. The days between birth and going home, I breastfed my son. On Sunday 2/12/2023, the day we arrived home, I began using the Brezza to formula feed every 2-3 hours in tandem with breast feeding and pumping. We began exclusively using the Brezza on Sunday 2/19/2023 and stopped breastfeeding. While using the Brezza, my son's weight either decreased or was slow to regain to his original birth weight each time we measured his weight. On Friday 2/24/2023, our pediatrician advised us to manually scoop the formula and increase the formula amount (increase the ratio of formula to water). That day, we measured out the dosage the Brezza was dispensing and learned it was less than half of the amount of powder recommended on the back of the formula package. After manually measuring and increasing the powder amount, he gained over 8oz in 48 hours putting him back on track to regain his original birth weight.

Pediatrician visits:
Monday 2/13/23 = 8.24lbs * First visit (routine wellness)
Wednesday 2/15/23 = 8.13lbs Weight check
Friday 2/17/23 = 8.22lbs Weight check
Friday 2/24/23 = 8.24lbs *2 Week visit (routine wellness) stopped Brezza, began manually scooping formula
Monday 2/27/23 = 8.78lbs Weight check

The injuries that happened are to be determined. At the 2 week check up, my son was supposed to regain all the weight lost and return to his original birth weight. Because of the Brezza dosage error, he did not. During the time we were using the Brezza, he slept poorly, and had unrest during his wake hours.
justification: The infant experienced weight loss and unrest due to incorrect formula dosage, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such errors are not common with proper device use.

incident_description:
I purchased a Cuisinart brand tea kettle (Cuisinart CTK-SS17N Aura 2-Quart Teakettle) from Amazon on January 3, 2023 (Amazon.com order number: [REDACTED]). I was traveling most of January, and have used the tea kettle relatively few times. Last night (Friday, Fed 25, 2023), I used the kettle to boil water for tea. I was in the kitchen when the kettle whistled and removed it from the burner almost immediately. I put tea bags in the cups and then began to pour the boiled water into the cups. As I was doing so, the metal part of the flap (the part that whistles fell out) fell out of its plastic casing and caused boiling water to go everywhere. When I looked closer, I saw that the plastic in the flap had melted (see uploaded photo). I have asked Amazon for a full refund. They have refused and offered only a partial refund "in keeping" with their policies. It seems like a full refund should be in order in this case, where Amazon sold a product with a hidden and dangerous defect.   

I'd like [REDACTED] to talk with Amazon about the need to (1) give their customer service reps some leeway in this type of circumstance (which they seem to lack), and (2) as a policy, give full refunds where a product is shown to have a hidden and dangerous defect. Thank you for raising this with Amazon - I hope its a simple one for a reasonable person with authority at Amazon to resolve. Unfortunately, I was unable to speak to such a person.
justification: The incident involved a product defect causing boiling water to spill, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a sauce pan that has tipped several times on my stove top due to "holes" in the grating. In addition, food prep bowls have also tipped when placed near these holes.

I have had a pan tip on two different occasions and a mixing bowl tip while pouring hot liquids into. The grids are too sparse in several areas of the top as I have photographed. If a pot containing hot liquids or oils tips forward, someone will experience 3rd degree burns possibly over half of the front of their body.

UPDATED ON 2/17/2023: [Samsung has updated their range tops and have fixed this problem. However, they do not have any fixes or replacement grids for this type of unit.  So it looks like they know about the problem but have designed new grids so that they are NOT compatible with the version I have.

Thus I hope we can get a recall!!!]

UPDATED ON 3/13/2023: [Yesterday, the 8th of March, 2023, I had another spill on my stove from a sauce pot that slipped through the front gap of my stove. I was moving the pot off a burner to cool. Even after filing the report, you'd think I wouldn't make this mistake but I've never encountered a stove with such a large gap where a pot can tip. This makes at least the 4th time I have had a spill related to the defective design of this cook top. A week or two ago I was contacted as a follow-up by Samsung to see if I wanted to purchase a new electric stove. I asked them to repair my cook top or send me to a repair shop that could modify the grate. No response.]
justification: The incident describes multiple occurrences of pots and bowls tipping due to a defective stove design, posing a risk of severe burns, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description: Frigidaire slide-in gas range, model number:FGGH3047VFB, serial number:  VF03796564.We purchased this model in September 2020 from an authorized Frigidaire vendor. For two years, the appliance worked fine. We used the oven's self-cleaning feature two times during that period. the second time we used that feature after Thanksgiving 2022, the self-cleaning feature issued two error codes ( F027, F022) which we subsequently learned affected the pc control board and another board. We cancelled the self-clean feature and attempted to open the oven door after an hour had elapsed. The locking feature on the door did not disengage and after several attempts at resetting the oven by disconnecting the electricity, the oven door remained locked. We called customer service and were informed that the warranty had expired (we knew this but didn't expect the appliance to fail after two years operation and very infrequent use of the self-cleaning feature). Through research we found that technicians and vendors advised not to use self-cleaning features on ovens of many manufacturers because the electronic components could not withstand the intense heat generated from the self-clean cycle.   Because this is a gas stove and the intense heat generated during the self-clean cycle, this stove presents a serious safety hazard to unsuspecting consumers who may, in good faith, purchase this model appliance not realizing the dangers in operating defective devices. We would think that given this unit is only two years old Frigidaire would want to stand behind its product and replace it. Instead, we had an authorized service technician come out, diagnosed the problem as the two electronic boards were not communicating with each other, and advised they had to be replaced. Our service call cost and that of the boards totaled $585.00. We paid $1,200.00 for the appliance which now retails for $1,024.00. The boards arrived, the technician installed them and the thermo fuse, plugged in the electricity and the oven controls did not work. In consultation with Frigidaire who then advised that the wiring harness should be replaced, we went along with the "black box" practice of replacing the next item on the troubleshooting list. We were then told that the harness which was to have been delivered before the 12/22 appointment would not be delivered in time for the appointment to be kept. Now we are facing the reality of not having a functional range for the holidays. We do have a cooktop but one cannot bake on the stove top.  In sum, such appliances should not be equipped with a self-clean feature especially since the designs now incorporate electronic components and software to regulate how they perform.  That intense heat is deployed beyond the capacity of the electronics to survive and endangering the homeowner is irresponsible.  That these appliances are still being configured with this kind of feature is bordering on the criminal given that the incident reports date back more than 10 years.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven with no reported injuries or deaths, but it presents a potential safety hazard due to the defective self-cleaning feature.

incident_description: My GE dishwasher Model #GDF510PSM4SS (approximately 2-1/2 years old) suddenly leaked all over the kitchen floor.  Upon troubleshooting I found the rubber hose elbow at the discharge of the wash pump had completely deteriorated.  In researching the replacement part at [REDACTED] , I found that hundreds of angry customers had reported the same problem on recently purchased dishwashers, with an average satisfaction rating of 1 star.  Some reported major damage to their wood floors, or even to their finished basement below.  GE has been aware of this problem,  but has done nothing to prevent its recurrence.  They require replacement of the entire pump assembly ($100) and refuse to make the rubber hose elbow available.  This would seem to indicate that any replacement pump assembly would still use the flawed hose elbow, and that the problem would repeat within two years.  Please note that the customers that have complained are only the tip of the iceberg, being those customers who are handy enough to fix their own appliances and order replacement parts.  The average consumer would simply call a repairman and pay the bill without understanding that there is a defective part causing a problem with their dishwasher.  Such flooding is a major safety hazard, as the electrical connection to the dishwasher is less than an inch off the floor.  Unexpected flooding of a kitchen floor is not only a slipping hazard, but could result in electrocution or electrical short-circuit fire risk.  Other models believed to use this same part, besides the GDF510 series,  include the GDT535 and GDP615 series. GE needs to initiate a recall of all washers using this part, engineer a replacement hose elbow that does not degrade in detergent, and as a minimum, supply this part at no cost to the consumer.

incident_description: I was using my whirlpool oven and noticed over the past three days, items were hotter than expecting or even burned. Yesterday, less than 7 minutes after placing cookies in the pre-heated oven at 400 degrees, smoke was billowing out of the oven and my parchment paper was on fire and cookies black. When I pressed the cancel button which is how it is supposed to turn off, it said "fault detected" but didn't turn off. It didn't give a repair code. It was still reading that it was set and on to 400 degrees. It was so hot that the top of my oven, the glass burner cooktop, would burn my skin if I touched it. I could not get the oven to turn off and had to turn the breaker off.  Then, the oven would not power back on. 40 minutes after I shut it off at the breaker, I set a candy thermometer on the stove top and it was 109 degrees, with the windows open and cold air blowing on it. Today I had a local repairman with 25 years of experience take a look. None of the safety switches triggered. Because it has a self-clean option that would bring it to 1,000 degrees, he thinks it was at least 1,000 degrees given how badly the items looked and how quickly it happened. I took a video of his diagnostics. He set it to 250 degrees, and within a minute his temperature measurement indicated it was almost 400. He turned it off for safety and did not continue to see how high it would get. He said there are two safety switches in the oven that are a redundant protection to prevent the oven from doing this, and neither were working. The temperature sensor was slightly off, but only by about 20 degrees, so that was an issue that needed to be repaired, but not causing this issue. I may be using the wrong terminology, but it was the motherboard or brains of the oven that was broken, including both emergency safety turn-off switches. He said the oven temperature was unregulated, and would continue to rise as much as possible without stopping. It was so hot, that the adjoining countertops and shelves were hot. I think this could have caused my house to burn down if it had been a different situation, or I had left the kitchen for a moment, or was cooking something containing oil.
justification: The oven malfunctioned severely, posing a fire hazard and potential for injury, but no actual injury or death occurred.

10/2022 The retailer was contacted, they advised her that they contacted the company and after much duration that the issue she was having was cosmetic not a safety issue and would send out a touch up pen repair kit.  Caller feels that this range is unsafe and should be reported.

She then sent the pictures and has not heard back from LG for three weeks now. She called me a week ago and said she sent pictures to someone internally at Home Depot that might help but I still have not heard back. 
This is is a safety defect. I looked online and viewed others that had this same issue with their blue ceramic oven. Not all of them were LG. With expansion and contraction with heat, I foresee this issue to continue:- I'm disappointed in Home Depot and LG for not responding and recognizing this is a problem, and being silent hoping it will go away. Who is liable if someone consumes one of these shards. And shame on these companies that make their automated customer service so difficult that one has to tum to the store you bought it from for help. 
Thank you and sorry it took me so long to respond to this letter but I was holding out hoping someone might care.

incident_description: Maytag Electric Range Model MER8700DS heating element catches fire, explodes and vaporizes the metal in the bottom of the oven resulting in a large hole.  My wife and I had been cooking a turkey in the oven, at 325 degrees for about 3 hours when she came to get me and stated that she thought she saw flames coming from the bottom right side of the oven.  I went to the oven and looked thru the glass window and did not see any flames.  About 10 minutes later we were sitting in our living room with the rest of the family when we lost power in the house momentarily and all electronics reset themselves (our town loses power frequently and we were not concerned).  About 5 minutes later, while still gathered in the living room, the power went out momentarily again and immediately turned back on. When the power came back on my wife heard a bang while I simultaneously heard a very loud, deep "humm" that lasted about 1 second or so which I assumed had come from the television speakers in the kitchen. Soon after this my wife went to check on our dinner and again informed me that she saw fire in the bottom of the oven.  I went to the oven and looked thru the glass window. This time I did see blue colored flames rising up about 1" high and emanating from between the right-hand side of the oven and the floor of the oven cavity. I then examined the left-hand side of the oven and observed the same blue flames there at the bottom as well.  I assumed at that moment that the heating element was burning out and it would need to replace it.  I shut the oven off using the control panel and we removed the food.  We continued to utilize the stove burners and the clock was still working at this time. The next day pulled the stove out from between our kitchen cabinets and unplugged it. I then opened the oven to remove the bottom pan of the oven that covers the heating element. As I reached inside the oven cavity I saw an oval shaped hole measuring approximately 1/2" x 3/4" located in the bottom rear of the cavity.  I removed the screws holding the bottom of the oven to the frame, flipped it over and observed a tear drop shaped scorch mark along with "metal spatter balls" emanating like rays of sunshine from the scorch mark.  This was all accompanied by a tan residue flowing out from the pointed end of the teardrop shape.  It looked like a comet with a tail.  From my years of working in a metal fabrication and welding shop I recognized this pattern.  In my opinion, the hole in the metal had been welded and vaporized by an electric arc rather than melting due to overheating of the heating element.  I next turned my attention to the  heating element itself.  The portion of the heating element below the hole in the pan was contorted and blown in half from the inside with charred, ragged, melted tares extending approximately 3" outward from the right hand-side of the fracture and 1" from the left-hand side of the fracture.  I also observed that along almost the entire length of the heating element was severe pitting, charring and fusing of the heating element metal with the outer coating.   I realized that I was very fortunate not to have been electrocuted when I touched the control panel to shut off the oven. Fortunately, no-one was injured at this time. The range is unplugged and I will be contacting Maytag to report this. I'm also hiring an electrician to examine my homes main electrical panel to determine if it needs to be repaired. At this point I don't know the cause of the malfunction but it needs to be investigated and resolved before someone gets seriously injured.
justification: The incident involved a fire and explosion in the oven, but no one was injured, which aligns with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such malfunctions are not common but have been reported.

He charged me $336.01 including $89.00 for the identical clamp which Bosch is refusing to reimburse on the grounds that the problem was my fault.

incident_description: My teen son and one of his friends, just arriving home from school one afternoon, went into the kitchen in search of food while waiting on me before we all headed out together. My son moved a large cupcake carrier with lid off the bar counter in order to make room for the leftover pizza box his friend had just retrieved from the fridge. His friend grabbed 2 slices and heated them up in the microwave, each kid still chewing on pizza as we were driving down the road a minute later. Not even 5 minutes later we had parked at the bike shop when my alarm company called me. They let me know my fire alarm was reporting an incident and asked me if they needed to send the fire department. I was in shock, there was no way there was an issue, we literally just left. I told them not to send anyone yet, left the kids at the bike shop, and raced the not even 5 minute drive back home. I should have known better, that fire alarm doesn't go off unless something is truly happening. I live in a townhome and when I pulled up I was already able to see my house was full of smoke from the windows, my dog's face pressed eagerly in the window closest to the door. I hit fire panic on my alarm app, yes! Send right away!! At the same time I was running to the door and let my dog out, telling her to jump in the [REDACTED] (she did, good girl). The neighbor to my right wasn't home, but on my left was, a mom younger than me with her 4 year old. I banged on her door and was able to yell inside to her to get outside asap. Then I ran back to my place, I couldn't see any flames, but the smoke was so thick I couldn't see much further than a few feet in front of me either, but our cat that had been with us, my son, since the divorce when he was 5 was still inside. I covered my face and tried to go through the house, but couldn't stay long between the burn in my chest and my eyes, made my way out to my neighbor yelling at me to get out. The fire department finally showed up after what felt like forever, but they were really just right around the corner. They put on the whole show with the masks, dragging out the hoses, raising the ladders.... haven't seen so many of my neighbors in can't remember how long. Thankfully the hoses did not get turned on. The firemen had asked if I knew where it was starting from and I had answered no clue. Well, before they turned on the water, one guy cameout with a melting, little flames here and there gooey blob, dropped it on the road and they put it out, telling the others to cut the water to the hoses. It was the cupcake carrier. It had gotten moved over on top of the stove and the stove was accidentally turned on when the kids leaned up/over to heat up the pizza. I had recently been debating about suspending my alarm services to save some money with all the costs rising and I am so grateful I didn't, and I won't. I knew those knobs were easily turned on, we'd done it before, but I've been extremely careful that nothing gets left on the stove, due to the possibility of what "could happen". I've had my new Samsung appliances about a year now and this was the 1st time we left an item on the stove. If it wasn't for my alarm company and the early detection I  would've lost at the very least half my home and my neighbor's home, the one that wasn't home shares the wall with my kitchen. We did lose our kitty. Too much smoke for his little lungs, my heart breaks everytime I think of him. The firefighters suggested the child locks for the dials, I've been so busy I haven't had a chance to order them yet and it's been a month. My son came home from a visit to his dad's last night, threw his stiff down, and came upstairs to say hello and tell me about his visit. A few minutes later we smelled smoke. I asked him where he threw his stuff down and we sprinted downstairs. A strap from his bookbag had fallen onto the stove which he had accidentally turned on, smoke was filling the downstairs and the alarm went off, again. At least this time we were home and on it, and didn't lose a family member, even if it was a furry one. Ordering the covers right now, which is how I came across this website. Feel as if everyone should be warned. One little slip up, and I had been so careful!
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a pet due to smoke inhalation and significant property damage, indicating a high severity level. The recurrence of a similar incident shortly after suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I bought a Samsung Counter Depth 4-Door Refrigerator (Model RF24FSEDBSR) and extended warranty from Lowes on August 19, 2014. This purchase totaled $2836.52 for what I had been told was a high-end and reliable appliance.
Throughout my ownership of this refrigerator, the ice maker has not maintained proper function. Oftentimes, the icemaker freezes itself and stops producing ice. The issue became such an intrusive part of ownership that we turned it off and bought a countertop ice machine at a cost of $154.37. In addition to our issues with the applianceÃÂs ice maker, we have experienced erratic temperature control within the refrigerator part of the appliance. Noticing food spoilage within the refrigerator, we bought two digital refrigerator/freezer thermometers at a cost of $23.66, to check the refrigeratorÃÂs temperature at shelf and door locations. These devices often report significant temperature differences from the temperature presented on the outside panel of the refrigeratorÃÂs door, with the internal temperature often reaching 44 degrees or higher. It has been a challenge to store many types of products, specifically dairy, within this appliance without them spoiling prematurely.
After performing initial research on the issues weÃÂve experienced, we learned Samsung has acknowledged both issues through Service Bulletins provided to their technicians.
When we bought the refrigerator, we put great faith in the Samsung brand and the implied warranty behind any such large appliance. Instead, this appliance clearly has a design defect causing known and proven problems with the icemaker and temperature regulation, and never should have been made available for sale to the public. This appliance may be beyond its express warranty period, but it's time that Samsung stands behind its name, appliances, and the implied warranty included with each sale. Not doing so is clearly severely limiting the safety, use, and value of the appliance, including endangering my family through exposure to improper food temperatures.

incident_description: My All-Clad bonded stainless steel cookware purchased between December, 2012 and February, 2020 all became dangerous to use and clean due to a condition that exists in the bonded material used in the vessel component of each piece. This bonded "sandwich" of aluminum core material between two layers of stainless steel degraded over time. During this degradation, the aluminum core slowly sheds leaving the double edges of thin stainless steel exposed to the user during cooking and cleaning. I discovered through an accident that the material had become dangerous to handle by me, my family, and anyone who may use the cookware. While cleaning the saucepan in the sink, I ran a dishcloth around the inner sides of the cooking surface and began bleeding from a cut on my wrist and thumb. The cut did not require medical attention because while it was deep  enough to bleed, it was not seriously deep. The source of my injury needed to be investigated, and that is when I found my skin rolled up in the edge of the pan between the two layer of stainless steel and occupying the space that once had contained the aluminum layer of the cladding. I owned a complete set and several additional pieces of this cookware, the set was a gift from my wife for Christmas, and the additional pieces were purchased through the All-Clad store on the Amazon site. I had discovered that all pieces of this cookware had this defect, and had become problematic. I attempted to use the manufacturers website to obtain remedy for my products and my request was ignored. I replaced my cookware and disposed of the dangerous pieces in early 2021. Today I was notified as a member of a "Class" about settlement for this defect. The settlement is not acceptable to me, because it does not remedy the danger of the product, nor does the manufacturer acknowledge the defect. The claims indicate that the cause for this condition is dishwasher detergent, which is not the case in my circumstance. All pieces of this cookware had razor sharp edges after only hand washing. This bonded material is dangerous because of the nature of dissimilar metals, the methods used to shape the pieces in manufacture, and the way the edges are exposed to the user. I also learned through this settlement offer that the manufacturer has discontinued this line of cookware. I have never received a product recall, and will never buy anything from this brand again.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut that bled but did not require medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the defect affected multiple pieces of cookware and posed a consistent risk during use and cleaning.

incident_description:
A Pyrex Dish exploded in my oven!

I love to cook! I use the Pyrex Snapware so much that this last set was a gift set that was purchased from Costco. Preparing for Hurricane Ian, my family came to shelter at our home.  The dish was washed after being removed from the package one or two days prior to the incident. I had a few things in the oven and this particular dish was for dessert so it went in the oven last. It was filled with the ingredients for bread pudding that were marinating on the countertop for over an hour so, it was at room temperature when it was placed inside the oven at 375 degrees with the other items being cooked. I typically cook the same item at 350 degrees but, because there were a few things in the oven, I raised the temperature. Within 15-minutes of placing the dish in the oven, we heard a loud explosion! It sounded like, and we initially thought that it was a transformer blowing with Hurricane Ian on the way. 
The explosion was contained so, there were no injuries except to the oven itself, and the other meal items that were in the oven at the time. 

I reported it to Costco by phone a day later when the initial shock wore off and they asked me to come in to file a report and bring the container, which I did.  Costco forwarded my concerns to the vendor. A few days later, the vendor Instant Brands, contacted me.
The exchange with the vendor was very amicable at first and they offered to pay for any damages. I thought I was saving lives by bringing this to their attention but, the side-stepping led to my researching online and finding that this is a known issue. Additionally, I became alarmed by the offer they made which included issuing a W-9 form, in other words, it would go down in their books as an employee/contractor-type payment and not an insurance claim that needed to be reported.
justification: The Pyrex dish explosion caused no injuries but damaged the oven and other items, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents are known but not extremely common.

incident_description:
I bought a General Electric (GE) gas range in November 2020 for my mother. The model number is JGB660YP1FS and the serial number is TR202232P.  I purchased it from Home Depot online.   The appliance was delivered in late November or early December 2020 to a vacant apartment being renovated.  My mother moved into the apartment two months later at the end of January 2021.  My mother is in her 80s and disabled.  She is bedbound and physically unable to stand walk or perform most activities without assistance.  She does not cook anymore.  Home care aides attend to her they do the cooking.  The cooking is almost always done only on the stovetop. The oven has rarely been used for cooking since the range was purchased.  To the extent that it has been used, it has been under normal conditions.   For four months, from August to December 2021, my mother was away from her home in a hospital and nursing home rehabilitation facility.  During all of those time periods, the appliance was not used at all.
In the pre-dawn hours of Saturday, August 27, 2022, when my mother was alone and in bed, she heard a strange noise coming from the kitchen area, which startled her.  When the home care aide arrived later in the morning, she saw broken glass on the floor by the appliance and more glass continuing to break off from inside the oven.   She called me and I came over.  I saw hundreds, maybe thousands of chunks of glass that the aide was sweeping up. The aide needed to use a vacuum cleaner to remove the smallest shards so that no one would step on them (including my motherÃÂs cat) and get cut. The aide and I carefully opened the oven door and saw that the inner glass pane had almost completely cracked and fallen apart.  There was still a section of glass remaining, which continued to break off.  It looked like it was "raining" glass.  Eventually almost all of it broke off.
On August 29, 2022, I contacted GEÃÂs Consumer Relations Department, told them about the incident and was assigned Case Number [REDACTED].
In my opinion, this incident is due to a manufacturing defect, since the oven has not been used or barely used since the appliance was bought almost two years ago. incident_description:
Something scary just happened with my Instant Pot Vortex air fryer.  I reported this to the manufacturer as well.

I turned my air fryer on and set the time and temperature.  Then I walked away doing other things, waiting for the beep saying it was ready for food.  This is the normal way to operate this air fryer, you preheat it and it beeps when it is ready (and the timer begins.)   Even if you walk away, the oven eventually preheats and the timer starts (and the air fryer turns off when the timer is done.)  There is no way to "keep it running" indefinetely.

So anyway 20 or so minutes later, I realized the beep never happened.  The air fryer still said "on" and was still preheating.  The scary thing is the cord was hot and when I unplugged it, the plug was hot.  Hot enough to blister you. Certainly something that could cause a fire.

It's almost like the heater turned on and just stayed on, but there was nothing inside to take all the heat!  And since it was stuck in pre-heat mode, it kept getting hotter and hotter and hotter.  When I say the plug was hot enough to blister, I'm not kidding.  If I had not found it when I did, there would have been a fire.
justification: The air fryer malfunctioned, overheating to a dangerous level with potential to cause injury or fire, but no actual injury occurred.

This weekend the washer was off and after determining the breaker and switch were ok I searched on [REDACTED]. I found this link [REDACTED] you can see he also had an overheating issue.  He attributed this to an object in the macerator but I donÃÂt think that was the root-cause.  My macerator was free to spin. incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung French Door refrigerator in 2017 for a new build. It was installed a year later. In 2020, the icemaker stopped working properly, freezing up solid and requiring us to make attempts to break apart the ice to get it to start working again. After contacting Samsung, I was told that because it was out of warranty I'd have to pay for its repair. After many calls to different appliance companies to find a repair service, Samsung arranged for one to come from an hour away and I paid $270 for the repair on June 19, 2020.

In May 2022, I noticed the refrigerator icemaker seemed to be getting worse again, making slushy ice and sometimes a bit of water would come first. This had been gradual so I believe it started much earlier, though it we accepted the "wetter" ice. But by May, there was an occasional louder fan noise that it was inconsistent. I began to look for more information online and found out that this was a known issue with these refrigerators going back to 2006 and two related repair/service bulletins were issued through 2017 and 2018. I also learned from other consumers that this was accompanied by swings in temperature. I believe this is from the compressor working overtime likely from the fan freezing over from the icemaker. I began to check my refrigerator's temperature on a regular basis, moving an analog freezer thermometer that I keep in a large freezer in the garage to my Samsung kitchen fridge. While the door settings showed it should be 37F in the fridge and 0F in the freezer, it was instead reading at between 22-26 degrees in the fridge and 6-8 degrees in the freezer. 

On June 8, 2022, I contacted Samsung after noticing that the now slushy ice from the icemaker was accompanied by loud fan noises from the back of the refrigerator. It would occasionally stop, always when the door opened, but then would start up again sometimes so loud that it kept me up at night (my bedroom is about 30 feet away). I have video of this occurrence. I told them about the temperature issues as well and my primary concern related to the noise from the compressor indicating it was in danger of failing. I was also concerned about possible overheating of the compressor.
I was told they would repair the icemaker for free as a warranty repair. When I asked if this would address the compressor, temperature issues, etc. I was told "no".

Three appointments later, the tech finally arrives to repair the icemaker. [First appointment made for 6/10/22 by Samsung was cancelled by the tech saying they weren't available then. Second appointment made for 6/13/22 by the tech resulted in a no-show. Third appointment made on 6/28/22, the tech arrived.] The tech was let in by a cleaning lady because he did not use the doorbell and just banged on the door (a [REDACTED] doorbell video caught all this). I found him by the fridge after he'd claimed he'd just finished installing the new icemaker. He asked me if he could dump the ice out so it could "start fresh". Later it occurred to me that this meant that the ice tray with the auger was still the old one. But I could see that the main unit had been replaced since he left the plastic film on it which I later peeled off. I asked him if this would also fix the temperature issues and he said "Yes" because the rest - indicating the compressor - was working overtime to get the job done. I asked about a receipt for the repair and the tech said that someone from his company would email it to me. I recorded this conversation.

I mentally noted that he had never pulled out the fridge from the wall, or replaced the motherboard (accessible only from the back) or checked the compressor for ice.

About 5 hours later, we checked the icemaker. It was full of ice. The auger, however, wouldn't turn and deliver the icemaker. We dumped the ice and tried again about 45 minutes later. Although there were some ice cubes in the bucket/auger area, no motor could be heard when the ice lever was pushed and no ice was delivered. The next morning, we noted that the temperature in the freezer was now -10F. Yes - negative 10 degrees Fahrenheit. The refrigerator was still around 22 degrees. 

We emptied the fridge and have now moved it to the garage and left it unplugged. I am concerned about a potential fire hazard with the temperatures swinging so far from the settings. I am concerned about the high electric bills I've received over the last few months and how much of it is due to this fridge. 

And I am especially concerned that since September 2021, I have suffered numerous debilitatingly severe cases of diarrhea finally leading to a diagnosis in March 2022 of Lymphocytic Colitis. I've been on a steroid treatment since March 2022 which I began to taper off of and symptoms have been returning. I am concerned that this is because of consuming food undergoing the freeze/thaw from the refrigerator.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator leading to potential health issues (Lymphocytic Colitis) and safety concerns (fire hazard), but no direct injury or death is confirmed.

Brinks model 44-2020 electrical appliance shut off timer. The model appears to be functioning normally with indicator lights, but will fail open. 

Failure was seen with multiple appliances well within product specifications. No tungsten devices were used.

I have a second timer that doesn't have this issue.


Description of Risk of Harm 

The device in question is designed to shut off the flow of electrical current based on a pre-set timer. Nevertheless, the relay will fail open, meaning that the electrical current will be hot, even if indicator lights appear to be working normally. There is risk of electrocution if the user incorrectly believes that the current has been turned off based on an off indicator light. Also, there is a fire risk, as cooking devices that may be attached to the timer will not turn off at preset times. There are no warnings on the packaging and/or instructions for this type of potential situation. There is only a max wattage threshold for resistive devices and a max wattage threshold for tungsten based devices.
justification: The device failing open poses a risk of electrocution and fire, which could lead to injury or death, and the likelihood is high given the description of the failure mode and lack of warnings.

incident_description:
This is regards to a Ooni Karu 12 Pizza Oven.  The leg assembly do NOT lock into place.  I received this oven for Christmas, December 2021 and have used it over a dozen times in the span of time.  On Friday, 5/20/2022 I was making pizzas in my back yard.  The oven was set on a level, metal table and I was making my 5th pizza I was making that night, the dough stuck to the pizza stone, when I tried to get the pizza peel (fancy word for big metal spatula) under the pizza, it nudged the oven back.  The rear leg folds in toward the front of the oven - meaning that when the oven was nudged backwards, the leg folded toward the front.  The legs do NOT lock into place by any means (dimple lock, pin, retardation mechanism).    There are 2 legs in the front - the fold toward front of the oven, so when you push the oven backwards, the reach the maximum extent of the opening.  Since the rear leg ALSO folds toward the front, it collapses into its closed position.  This happened to me with hot coals burning in the rear compartment as per normal operation, but the back leg closed, the coals fell out onto the concrete ground, splashing embers into my mulch garden bed.  I suffered a moderate burn to my arm getting the oven back into place before running inside my house to grab my fire-resistant BBQ gloves and pick everything up.  Then I got a hose and watered the garden to put out the smoldering leaves and coals.  

When I contacted Ooni I have received conflicting responses which prompted me to contact the CPSC.  I provided videos replicating the rear leg folding in on concrete, travertine, and metal.

One message from Ooni stated "I can confirm, that the legs should extend and lock in to place. Have you had the issue from the beginning or perhaps it occurs unexpectedly?"

The next message from Ooni then stated ""I've reviewed the videos that you've sent with the team, and the legs do seem alright. Realistically, the legs folding in while the oven is in use shouldn't happen. The legs themselves don't lock into place, however, once they are fully open on a flat surface, the weight should keep them splayed out."

I do not have faith in their response but will continue to try and work with them.  I can recreate the rear leg folding down on multiple a flat surfaces,  concrete, travertine, a metal table.  The legs would either have to do one of two things when a parallel force is presented in the direction the legs "splay" out.  The legs would either slide against the surface they are on, dangerous if the oven is elevated as it could then fall; or the feet of the leg would create enough friction against the surface to resist said force, and then close.  Both scenarios are bad - what should happen is the feet provide enough friction, and the legs are prevented from closing -  a gravity lock, self locking hinge, or even just a match friction dimple would work.
justification: The user suffered a moderate burn while trying to stabilize the oven, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
Electrical safety hazard regarding FoodSaver Model FM-3945.  Want to bring to your attention an electrical safety hazard regarding my FoodSaver. The power cable insulation (16-month-old, moderate usage) has worn away leaving exposed electrical conductors.  If one reaches under a plugged-in unit to pick it up, contact with the energized conductors can be made, creating an electrical shock hazard.

Report Update:
The statement that the product does not present a hazard or unreasonable risk of death is inaccurate. The underside of the food processor has exposed electrical conductors, brought about by normal product usage, energized to a potential of 120 VAC when plugged in. Keeping in mind that a significant number of older homes do not have electrical GFCI protection, an individual could pick up the food processor by the underside, come in contact with the exposed "hot" conductor with one hand while touching a metal appliance (range or cooktop) with the other hand or bare arm (or even a stainless-steel kitchen sink - in some homes copper plumbing can provide a ground for the electrical system) completing an electrical path to ground through the body. The result being electrical current will flow through the body, potentially causing cardiac arrest which could result in injury or even death. Additionally, having damp hands will increase this risk.
justification: Exposed electrical conductors pose a risk of severe injury or death due to potential electrical shock, especially in older homes without GFCI protection.

Had it been night time, I might have gone to sleep and been asphyxiated and then my house blown up when some electrical device turned on.

incident_description:
Hello,

I'm writing this email in regards to the issues of my Samsung French Door Refrigerator.

Refrigerator Information: 
Model #: RF25HMEDBSR/AA
Serial #: 0AFJ4BBGA02362K
Purchase Date: 11/27/15
Purchase Price: $1997.49
Dealer: New England Appliance (Braintree, MA.)

This was the original email I sent to Samsung regarding my refrigerator issue:
The fridge had problems approximately 1-year after installation.  We had a service company fix the ice maker at least two times, each time changing the draw and some electrical component.  The ice maker has never worked correctly since then.  We constantly have to defrost the unit as it just forms a giant block of ice.  Currently we can't remove the draw as it is totally frozen (encased).  We have to remove everything from the refrigerator in order for this to thaw out.  In addition, we now have the entire back of the refrigerator unit forming ice behind the rear panel encasing the coils.  We've had to thaw this out on a bi-weekly basis!  The air will not circulate within the refrigerator, although the fridge is cold, we can't keep milk in there as it goes bad.  I have tried calling 4 service vendors in this area, NOBODY will work on these refrigerators.  They told me that the problem will come back a week after they leave, so it's not worth them servicing these units.  The only remedy is to constantly de-thaw the fridge and ice maker on a continuous basis.  This is extremely frustrating as we paid nearly $2000 for this unit.  For comparison, we still have an old [REDACTED] refrigerator in the basement that is 20-years old and runs perfectly fine!

After Samsung received that email, they did send a repair service to change the icemaker unit.  However, they would not address the freezing panel/coil issue and stated a new ticket would need to be made.  After numerous email exchanges with the NJ BBB and Samsung, Samsung ultimately stated they would not do anything for this issue as it is out of warranty.
 However, this has nothing to do with a warranty issue, but rather a design defect issue! These Samsung service bulletins below acknowledge there is an issue with my model along with numerous other models.  
(05/24/17) Service Bulletin # [REDACTED] (for the ice-maker issues)
(10/05/17) Service Bulletin # [REDACTED] (for the rear panel/coil freeze-up issues)
Samsung KNOWS this refrigerator model has design defects and yet refuses to fix the problem, recall the unit, or compensate me for a refund.  I must manually unplug my refrigerator every 2-weeks for 24-hours in order for all of the ice to melt.  We have lost hundreds of dollars of food, milk, and most importantly medicines due to high temperatures within the refrigerator (50-degrees actual with thermometer).
This is a well known problem, currently there are 109,000 members of a [REDACTED] group with the identical problems that I'm having.  Samsung has been repairing some and refunding others, but there is no rhyme or reason to how this is done, totally hit or miss!
I'm respectfully requesting compensation for this appliance as the issues have been going on for so long, and nobody can or is willing to fix them correctly.  I'm looking forward to hearing from you regarding this matter.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator causing food and medicine spoilage, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I've a GE free standing electric range w/ a glass top at my apartment. This model of stove has a hot cooktop indicator light on the surface so when it's still "hot" to the touch it is illuminated. I went to clean some flour off of the top surface of a burner, after using the stove ~20+ minutes prior, and despite the hot cooktop light being off I sustained 2nd degree burns on my right hand. After speaking with my primary care physician I was requested to visit the ER at my local hospital where I was treated for first and second degree burns. I was referred for an additional appointment the following day with the hospitals wound clinic. As an engineer the fact that someone could be burned this severely while the hot cooktop indicator is off is appalling. After doing some research I found that the user manual of the stove calls out that the hot cooktop indicator turns off at ~150F.  [REDACTED] states that 1st degree burns can occur at 118F and that 2nd degree burns occur at temperatures of 131F. The fact that GE has designed their stove with a hot cooktop indicator that shuts off at 150F is a risk to the public and in my opinion demonstrates negligence on the part of GE. Burn risks could easily be limited by using a sensor in the stove that turns off below the threshold for injury.   The GE appliance is Model JB860EJ3ES.

incident_description:
Here is the list of problems we have experienced with our Samsung refrigerator.
We purchased it 3/21/2018; (took delivery) April 10th, 2018. 
I believe that in 2019 (August) we came back from a trip, and found our freezer completely defrosted. We lost hundreds of dollars of food. The freezer door was securely shut, and no one had been in the home while we were gone.
I called Samsung service, and was given some kind of reset code that seemed to work.
At the time, I was unaware of the massive problems and manufacturing defects with Samsung refrigerators and ice-makers, and didn't document the call, but it should appear in their records.
Around the same time, we started having water come out of the icemaker when we were trying to dispense ice.
Then, the icemaker started freezing up, and we had to start chipping ice out of the maker on a regular basis.
Then, we started having water and ice at the bottom of the fridge under the specialty drawer.
Then started having food at the back of the fridge freeze up, as well as in the vegetable drawers. Again, wasted food and money, over and over again.

In mid 2021, the problem was so severe we couldn't use the icemaker, and I started researching online and found that Samsung refrigerators are known for having manufacturing defects related to the icemaker and temperature regulation (documented in their service bulletins to technicians).
In October 2021, Samsung serviced our icemaker and replaced it. The technician also said the temperature problem and ice in the fridge (at the bottom and also behind the plastic panel where the "twin" coolers are located) was caused by a defect in the motherboard, and he replaced that as well.

About a month after that service, I started noticing that food seemed to spoil faster, and that alternated with food freezing unexpectedly. I put digital thermometers in the fridge and freezer, and have been regularly photographing the temperatures each morning, and then re-setting the thermometers. The temperatures in the fridge fluctuate wildly: from as low as 29 to as high as 54. They rarely  are in the food safe range of 40 degrees or less (except when they are below freezing for no apparent reason--freezing our food). This morning's temperature was showing 44 (after the fridge being unopened for more than 12 hours), with a high of 52 degrees, and a low of 40 degrees. Meanwhile, the temperature on the front of the fridge ALWAYS shows 38 degrees for the fridge and 1 degree for the freezer, no matter what the actual temperature is inside the fridge. I have changed the position of the thermometer to various locations in the fridge, and the results are similar no matter where placed.

Before I started using the digital thermometers, and since October 2021 when the motherboard was replaced, we've had multiple instances of feeling ill after meals, including vomiting and diarrhea. We DO NOT eat out or eat food prepared outside the home because of COVID-19 concerns. We wash all incoming food and produce with a mild soap solution.  I'm a health care provider, and immediately thought that we could have food-born illnesses because ot the timing and symptoms. Our food prep and kitchen practices are exceptional and careful as we have a family member with a chronic illness. In retrospect, I suspect that these episodes of illness correspond with temperature fluctuations inside the refrigerator. Now that we are aware of the temperature fluctuations, we don't store dairy products, eggs or any proteins in the fridge, and have had to purchase a second smaller fridge to store those items.

This is, without a doubt, the WORST appliance I have ever owned. It has numerous well documented manufacturing defects and faults, and Samsung, as a company, has failed to do a recall.
As a result, we've lost hundreds (thousands?) of dollars worth of food, suffered food-born illness, and had to purchase a second fridge because of the unsafe temperature swings inside the fridge.
Oh, and the replaced ice-maker is now starting to have the same problems it had initially: water coming out, ice accumulations inside the maker itself, and requiring removal of built up ice so that it doesn't freeze shut.
justification: The incident involves food spoilage, financial loss, and food-borne illnesses due to refrigerator malfunctions, indicating injury (severity 3). The recurring nature of the issues suggests a high likelihood of occurrence (4).

As I stated, I live alone, no one was interacting with this thing.  I hadn't used the cook top in over a week.
I could not get them to stop snapping, so I went in the basement and shut off the circuit breaker switch to that appliance.  I left it off for a few days, reengaged the circuit breaker switch, it wasn't snapping.
2 days after this, again, for no reason whatsoever this GE Profile was snapping.  I couldn't cook with it, as all burners would be acting like they were trying to light.
This is a KNOWN problem with these GE stoves, I've found hundreds of complaints online for exactly this.
Why has there not been a recall???

The visit from one of their so-called "technicians" was quoted at $500 just to get them to show up, most likely from [REDACTED], and my income is SSDI, why am I paying for GE's failures as a company?  I didn't break this cook top, neither did the hundreds of others who are stating the exact same experiences.
Then I got their outrageous Buzzer.
Here is the item that should have forced a Recall immediately:  In the center is a switch, with On/Off for the Child Safety "Lock," if it's On, the burners can't be turned on or engaged, you have to turn it to Off to cook with.  Also, much like GE's other notorious appliances, for no reason whatsoever they accompany this useless switch with an ungodly loud buzzer.  That even a Deaf woman can hear and feel!  It's that loud.
Well on my cook top, as with hundreds of other reviewers have stated, this stupid buzzer started going off whether turned to On or Off if you tried to start a burner.  The burners will start while it's set to Off, but the buzzing does not end.
You can not cook because the buzzing is so loud, that it's impossible.
And again, I'm Deaf, so imagine the rest of the world having to hear this.
In addition, there is a red light under the glass when it's set to On, for Child Safety Lock On.  Well along with the obnoxious buzzing, the red light stays lit no matter if you have it set to On or Off.
This is an absolute danger.  
You can't tell if the Child Safety Lock is engaged or not because the red light does not turn off.
You can not cook because of this horrible buzzing sound coming from the cook top.
I was not cleaning, nothing overflowed, I did not spill anything when this started happening.
Now I have a cook top taking up half my kitchen I can't use!  I'm scared of it exploding.
I removed all burners and knobs, so I could open this up and remove the damn buzzer.
Well underneath the front right burner, the one for pots of soup and such, under that burner is all black and burned, almost like it had been on fire.
I am a Deaf, Disabled woman and for the past 5 months, I have not been able to make any food with this piece of trash cook top.
I have had to unplug it and turn off the gas at the line to get it to stop clicking and/or buzzing, I am also scared it's going to explode as I see many people on here mentioning.  A handful of times, I've smelled something burning coming from the cook top, but no one is using it or had used it when I smelled this.
There are hundreds of complaints about this same model.  It should have been recalled.  Why are all of GE's appliances outfitted with a useless, loud buzzer that breaks for no reason, then GE has the audacity to BLAME the consumer.
I didn't break this cook top, spill anything, manhandle it, spray anything on it, it's just a cheap piece of trash cook top that they charge $2,000 for, and that's ridiculous.  This thing is DANGEROUS and it's total junk.  It should be recalled.

incident_description:
We bought a Bosch microwave, believing Bosch to be one of the best manufacturers.   But, after a short time of use, it let out a lout crackling and zapping noise.  I was pretty sure that I recognized the sound as a circuit, arcing out.  I figured that it was the capacitor, or the radar unit, and called the warranty in as a covered repair.  I had them note the noise on the repair ticket.  And, we waited a couple months, which was expected, due to supply chain and COVID related staffing issues, nationwide.
The repairman noted it as a door short that occurs when someone opens the microwave door in the middle of a cycle, disrupting the timer, and three switches, in the door that have to balance a very particular way....  
In checking reviews and complaints, published across the web, it seems that this is an absolutely common occurance with the model.  And, that the repairmen, in their cases, would also, reliably blame it upon a switch in the door of the microwave.
I' for one, and having owned some of the cheapest microwaves on the market, have never had one that would have such a rule, not to open the door, to interrupt the cycle.  In fact, it has always been a feature.  And, there is no mention of any such requirement, in any of the manuals.
Happily, we only smelled cooking wqire insulators, and our microwave only stopped heating, after an all clear by the repairman.  It seems that most reviews include a violent tripping of the household breakers.  
We have since set another appointment for a repairman to come out to our house, and work on the unit.  But, I might implore you to take a closer look at this model, as I believe it to be a hazard.  And, it is likely in violation of any number of rules of proper procedure, both in manufacturing, and in service.
It might be noted that the unit was only six weeks old at the time.  And, this is apparently a terribly common issue.  We have not been offered a replacement.
Whatever the case, I don't want my house to burn down.  I just want to heat a meal.
Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning microwave causing electrical issues but no injury or death, and it is described as a common occurrence with this model.
