I was using our 18 month old microwave to boil a cup of cold water and instant coffee in a microwave safe mug, when I smelled melting plastic and opened the door to find a hole in the inside door. (I have attached 3 photos as documentation.) I had the microwave on for 2-3 minutes. A microwave door shouldn't melt after only 18 months of use by two adults.  

I tried reaching out 5+ times to Toshiba/Medea via their customer service reps: I would have been very happy with just a replacement door, a refurbished or used unit. But all they did was tell me that my 12 month warranty was expired and there was nothing they could do. This is not a microwave that broke. It MELTED. This is hazardous...why did the door melt? Clearly a defect of some kind.

One rep told me to use the "[REDACTED]" to find a repair shop. Is this 1980? There is no "[REDACTED]" and no one repairs microwaves. Clearly he was sending me a canned response that hasn't been changed in 25 years. Or just being sarcastic and dismissive...can't tell. 

I very politely asked the reps to escalate this to a supervisory level, but none would reply back or do so. This is no way to treat a possibly hazardous defect and risky situation to a customer.
justification: The microwave door melting is a hazardous defect, but no injury or death occurred, only property damage.

incident_description: I have mistakenly turned a burner on for a Frigidaire range unit on a number of occasions. The burner is easily turned on when leaning onto the front of the control panel (e.g. reaching in an upper cabinet or microwave). This is incredibly unsafe and has led to me discovering it on 60-120 sec after the fact, on one occasion with an item on the stove beginning to melt.
justification: The incident involves a burner being accidentally turned on, leading to a potential hazard, but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
The dishwasher was in use, when the consumer noticed the smell of burning wires.  He immediately stopped the operation of the dishwasher.

A little while later, he removed the dishwasher door and found that the power wires (and the copper) melted completely.  The control panel was singed and the 2 main power wires melted completely through and separated from their connection.  None of the items that were placed in the dishwasher to be cleaned were damaged.

He tried to call the brand name company, but could not get a live person.  He was only able to reach a department, where he could schedule an appointment.

The consumer read about a class action suit settlement on these dishwashers and contacted, who he think is the manufacturer (which was listed in the settlement).  The staff at the law firm he spoke to, said that his model was not included in the settlement.  Nothing else transpired.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing burnt wires and a singed control panel, but no injuries or damage to other items occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her dishwasher plug overheated in the outlet and feels that she experienced the same problem as the company's previous recall. Caller stated that an E15 error was displaying on the unit while in use.  Caller stated that she called an electrician and he came out and found that the plug had caused a fire in the breaker box, this could have caused a house fire, the plug was repair but the error still remains.  

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that someone would be sent out on 12/20. She stated that she also file a report with their recall department.
justification: The incident involved an overheated plug and a fire in the breaker box, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
(11/28/2021) The consumer has a safety concern about the product. She stated that the area outside of the control panel gets very hot when the oven is in use. The oven was set for 425. 

Also the right side panel gets very hot. The consumer measured the heat with a meat thermometer. The thermometer indicated 162.3 degrees.

The consumer burned her finger on the range but no medical attention was require.

(12/06/2021) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that it will be a week and a half before they can send someone out to check the product.

Third party tech sent by Whirlpool recorded external temperatures ranging from 120 degrees on control panel to 190 degrees on exterior door with internal temp correct at 425 degrees.
justification: The consumer burned her finger, indicating an injury, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description: We purchased a new frigidaire gas oven 3 years ago. From the start we noticed that the burner control dials were sensitive to be moved by the slightest pressure. Also that the two outermost controls on each side were unshielded by the oven door and were easily accidentally turned on by brushing up against them with a part of your body or by an object. Often these accidents did not result in any notable click from the igniter or a sparking of the burner as the dial spun past that range. This early morning (2:00 A.M.) as I walked through the kitchen, on my way to go to bed upstairs, I or an object I was carrying brushed up against a knob and turned on the gas. At 9:00 A.M. we discovered that the middle floor of our home was filled with gas. We quickly opened doors, windows, turned on exhaust fans and of course turned off the burner on the stove.  Fortunately no one was sleeping on that floor and the door to the lower level, where the utility room and burning pilot lights were located, was closed. Otherwise we could have been killed in a major explosion.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with no injury or death, and the description indicates that accidental activation of the burner is a recurring issue.

incident_description: GE Range JGB660SP1SS - Less than a year old started smelling gas when using the oven.  GE repairman said it was gas not getting ignited and did a valve adjustment.  3 months after repair the gas smell is back.  Clearly it's a safety issue with this model.
justification: Gas smell indicates a potential safety issue but no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I went to put a Samsung electric smooth stop stove bottom drawer in and sliced open 2 of my fingers open from the metal on the sides of drawer
justification: The description mentions a clear injury with two fingers being sliced open, which falls under severity level 3.

incident_description: I would like to report a manufacturing defect affecting the control knobs of Samsung gas ranges. The knobs are plastic and break easily which makes very hard to ensure that the burner is shut completely off.  All five of my knobs have broken and only two are usable.  The poor design and barely functional knobs are dangerous. I contacted Samsung and they are unwilling to offer a replacement
justification: The broken knobs make it difficult to ensure the burner is off, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I own a Samsung refrigerator with a known defect. While purchased in 6/2014, it started failing in 6/2017. Each time, I have lost entire refrigerator's worth of food, after eating unsafe food due to internal temp of 47-48 degrees (food deemed unsafe above 40 degrees). I have paid to have it fixed 4 times and it has failed again. Samsung claims this is a warranty issue. It is in fact a known defect. They did not honor the federal Magnuson Moss Lemon Law and are not standing behind their un safe product.
justification: The incident describes consumption of unsafe food due to refrigerator failure, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The repeated failures and lack of resolution make recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: While broiling for just a few minutes, I heard sounds in my oven. I opened it to find that my 2 and a half year old GE range had exploded and the inner glass on the door was shattered. The glass was flying around in there and it was a miracle that I was not hurt.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven with shattered glass, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: The cooktop turned on by rubbing up against the dials causing oil in a pan to catch fire
justification: The cooktop turning on accidentally caused a fire, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On January 13, 2022, at approximately 6:15 pm I was about to finish up making a batch of homemade spaghetti sauce. I was using a 4-quart Kirkland Signature series pot (model no. 1119345?) and had it on the stovetop over a low simmer - the sauce had been simmering for approximately 3 hours. As I walked into our homeÃÂs kitchen to turn the stovetopÃÂs gas burner off and remove the bay leaves from the sauce, I noticed that the lid for the pot had shattered and that there were pieces of glass were found sitting on top of the spiderweb-cracked lid, on the stovetop, and below the lid in the spaghetti sauce. No one heard any noise from the adjacent living room to indicate anything had happened with the cookware.

There are no injuries to report from this incident; but, the introduction of shattered glass into a food product is alarming. I saw where a previous recall was issued for a similar Kirkland pot lid (Recall No. 13-708).

I was cooking and the owner of the product. This product was purchased by me from Costco within the past two years; but, I am unable to locate the online receipt from Costco for anything purchased more than s year ago to know exactly when it was purchased.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass in food but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) based on the recall history and lack of prior similar incidents mentioned.

incident_description: Purchased a new Samsung microwave. After installing in a new building it was found running days later with no operator input. Contacted Samsung several times and nothing has been done to resolve this issue. Also found others complaining of the same issue in reviews.
justification: The microwave running without operator input poses a potential safety hazard, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was cooking food on my electric stove. I had the control set to medium heat, the liquids in the pot started to boil vigorously. I adjusted the control to low. I could see the burner cover glow more brightly. there was a loud "bang" that came from the back of the stove. The noise scared me, I turned off the burner control and asked my husband to disconnect the circuit breaker in the service panel just in case there was a fire. Contacted Better Living Hardware, asked if there was a recall on the stove. I was told "no". Instructed to call Jersey Appliance for repair services. Jersey Appliance replaced Infinity(?) switch, replaced "harness". Stove still does not work. Contacted LG Electronics when I learned that LG recalled 161K ranges in 2012 for the same problem. Waiting for LG to send rep to inspect stove, January 20 2022..
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and potential electrical issue, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I ordered an Ultrean 6 Quart Air Fryer, Large Family Size Electric Hot Air Fryers XL Oven Oilless Cooker with 7 Presets, LCD Digital Touch Screen and Nonstick Detachable Basket,UL Certified,1700W (red) in May of 2021. Last week, my son was removing the basket/drawer, and the lower pan dropped off the basket. He had been cooking in it at 400ÃÂ°, so the pan was very hot, but he managed to dodge the hot pan. I told him to be sure not to hit the release button as he was removing it, and he told me he hadnÃÂt. Last night, he was removing the pan full of fajita filling, and it fell off the basket once again. Once again, the pan was 400ÃÂ°, and this time the pan contained hot fajita marinade that had drained down during cooking. Fortunately, my son wasnÃÂt burned. My husband and I both took a look at the pan/basket, and the pan disengaged from the basket while if we held it a certain way or shook itÃÂwhich we do all the time so the food cooks evenly.
justification: The incident involved a hot pan falling multiple times but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) as it happened twice under normal use.

incident_description: I Turned my Kenmore oven on to self clean mode and it never turned off. Had to turn it off  after 7 hours of it being on and found it melted the top part of the oven door because it got too hot. The bottom seal around the door was also black.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and caused damage but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I used the slicing blade attachment for the Black & Decker FP1600B 8 quart food processor.  I used it to slice potatoes and was careful to not put any pieces that were too large through the chute.  While we were eating, my husband noticed a sharp shard of plastic in his potatoes and upon inspection of the processor found that the lid had chipped off in 2 places.  We never found the other shard and hope one of our kids didn't eat it.  This happened because the blade assembly is loose so the blade wobbled and chipped the lid.
justification: A plastic shard was found in food, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Refrigerator leaks water inside and underneath causing potential slipping and has ruined sections of my hardwood flooring.
justification: The refrigerator leak caused property damage (ruined flooring) and poses a slipping hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: I was in the other room and heard a sound as if something fell. I walk into the kitchen to find the outer door of my double oven shattered suddenly.
justification: No injury or harm occurred, only property damage (shattered oven door).

incident_description: KitchenAid dishwasher model KTDM404ESS1 - when running smelled a burning smell coming from the dishwasher for approximately a week when during one cycle the circuit breaker tripped.  Taking off the front panel revealed that the part of the control board where the wiring harness was attached was burnt up and the wires had overheated burning the 'rubber mat' underneath the front panel.  Thankfully no fire but have seen reports of this happening to other KitchenAid dishwashers soon after the five year warranty expires (ours lasted 5 years and 9 months).
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and damage to the dishwasher's control board and wiring, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I put a frozen pizza in the oven and it started smoking. I opened up the oven and there was flames coming from the bottom along with popping sounds. I had to call 911.
justification: The incident involved flames and popping sounds, requiring emergency services, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Breville BOV900BSS countertop convection oven glass shattered with explosive force distributing 400 degree glass over kitchen counter, floor, and oven interior.
justification: The oven glass shattered explosively, posing a significant hazard, but the description does not mention any injury.

incident_description: I noticed a burning electrical smell coming from under my sink.  We thought it was just a one time thing until it happened again when running our Bosch dishwasher. We called Bosch for service but after multiple call backs and hours of hold, they reported they had no contractors available in our service area and would forward our issue to a manager.  While waiting for a response, we investigated under our sink and found that the junction power box connecting our dishwasher had actually caught on fire and was charred.  We removed the junction box/power cord unit and called Bosch to report our findings.  We are currently waiting to hear back.
justification: The incident involved a charred junction box under the sink, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On May 12, 2014 , I have purchased a Samsung refrigerator from Best Buy showroom in Fort Wayne Indiana . Its model no. is RF31FMESBSR and SN is WG5143BD301838R. I have had Authorized repair services Wisemans as well as Brookmill to come out and repair the ice maker. Today My service guy came to fix my refrigerator again. He brought out the back panel because we have had a sudden drop of temp on the unit again it is broken and he was unable to get my icemaker open. This is my third repair on the units cooling system and ice maker. I am in the process of of obtaining all my service records but at this time I feel that with the repairs that have been done I feel that Samsung should return the total cost of my refrigerator. This not a warranty issue it is a design defect that Samsung has known about and has failed to correct. This Unit holds my perishable groceries
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning refrigerator requiring multiple repairs, but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description: does not cool, freezes and fills with water, makes noise, ice maker freezes and does not work
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning appliance with no indication of injury or death, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: Today, my 28 month-old Mr. Coffee Easy Measure 12 Cup Coffee Maker spontaneously flickered on and off, so I pressed the power button, it flickered again, I turned it off, it flickered, and so on. Meanwhile, the little water remaining in the reservoir from the morning's brew sputtered as it heated, and the warming element and rest of the unit got hotter and hotter, so I unplugged it. I plugged it in again, and the LED displayed "EC5". I unplugged and plugged it in again, and the flickering cycle repeated. Today's experience is a repeat of what happened a couple weeks ago, after which I unplugged it and let it sit unused until 3 days ago, and it worked fine, until today. I [REDACTED] "Mr. Coffee error code" and discovered what appear to be dozens of comments on mrcoffee.com describing similar experiences for this model, in response to each of which is offered a gratuitous reply and no solution. I think this coffee maker is a potential fire hazard, and it doesn't look like Sunbeam Products is going to do anything about it.
justification: The coffee maker exhibited malfunctioning behavior and overheating, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: We ate spoiled food and lost our 8year olds insulin due to defective Samsung fridge. Our fridge was 11 months old when unbeknownst to us, temperatures were in the 50s. Once the freezer defrosted we knew something was wrong and tested the fridge which by then was obviously room temperature. Samsung techs ÃÂfixedÃÂ our fridge after a fight for support  for a less than year old fridge, but the repair lasted 12 hours. We went with no fridge for months because we had to fight for a refund. Food spoilage is a serious issue, especially for type 1 diabetics and those will health issues. Not to mention the loss of medicine.
justification: The incident involved spoiled food and loss of insulin, which is critical for a type 1 diabetic, but there is no mention of actual injury or death.

incident_description: I own a Samsung French door refrigerator with water/ice maker. Getting ice buildup inside the fridge and control panel. Also, have mold on my wall.
justification: Ice buildup and mold indicate an incident with no injury, and such issues are likely to occur with refrigerator malfunctions.

incident_description:
Samsung refrigerator model RF28HMEDBSR does not display correct temperature for refrigerator or freezer. Refrigerator was being used according to the provided manual and was previously in good working order. 
This caused my family (2 adults and 1 child under 2years) to become ill. Upon putting a thermometer in the fridge itÃÂs showed the interior temp was 65 when the control panel showed 36 degrees for the refrigerator and -3 degrees for the freezer. The freezer was 45 degrees. 
Samsung was contacted and they did not offer to correct or diagnose the issue despite the refrigerator being under warranty. There are numerous stories under the BBB stating other consumers have had this issue with no resolution from Samsung.
justification: The incorrect temperature display led to illness in a family, indicating injury (severity 3). Multiple reports suggest this issue is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Plates that are advertised as ÃÂmicrowave safeÃÂ explode in microwave after 50 seconds. This happened with three plates.
justification: Plates exploding in the microwave is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a Black and Decker Double Flip Waffle Maker WMD 200 B  from JCPenny on Nov. 26, 2021. I used the waffle maker for the 3rd. time at my Son in Law and Daughter's house. on Dec. 22, 2021. I was at a gathering of 6 people including myself. I was seated at a card table with the waffle maker. The other 5 people were around in front of me. When the light indicated the waffle maker was ready, I put a normal amount of batter in the waffle maker, engaged the latch, waited 10 seconds, rotated it, an added a similar amount of batter to the empty side, and engaged the latch. 
About 1 and a half minutes later (time uncertain), The top of the upper chamber blew open and I felt a force hit my chest. The waffle maker lid had broken where it meets the rotation part of the waffle maker. The rim of the waffle maker didn't have any excess batter. Using a rag, I was able to turn the waffle maker and remove the lower waffle.
We were all shocked to say the least!  Later, after I removed my shirt, I was stunned to see shards of plastic fall from my shirt with some still embedded in my shirt.
If I had had the waffle maker on a kitchen counter, a higher height, the blast would have hit me in the face.
The Incident occurred on Wednesday, Dec. 22, 2021 ~ 5:30 pm. In Tucson AZ.
I believe this was a dangerous event and warrants immediate attention
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning waffle maker causing physical impact and minor injury (shards embedded in shirt), but no serious harm or death.

incident_description: Samsung refrigerator- temp noted on fridge at 36 degrees. When did handheld temp gun, this returned a temp of 50 degrees. This is an unsafe temperature for food. The fridge is not giving correct temperature which can lead to food borne illnesses, which for some with compromised immune system could kill them.
justification: The fridge displays incorrect temperature, posing a risk of foodborne illness, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: I have had issues with the ice maker in my Samsung RF263BEAESR refrigerator. I has ice buildup and is unable to make any ice cubes. After installing a temperature monitor, it is also unable to maintain temperature at the desired setpoint. This is a health issue. It is also pooling water on the bottom of my crisper and creating sheets of ice that need to be removed daily. I contacted Samsung first on this issue on November 10, 2020. I heard nothing after a service appointment was made. I contacted them again on Dec.10, 2020 and they again claimed someone was coming out. This was also a no show. I contacted them a third time and they cancelled that call as well and told me that there was no one in my area to service this machine. These refrigerators have known defects and are currently in a class action lawsuit (see attached) for them selling this exact refrigerator model with known defects. They are unable to repair this defect so I am now insisting on a full refund.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain temperature and ice buildup poses a health risk due to potential food spoilage, but no direct injury is reported.

incident_description: Oven is emitting dangerous amounts of carbon monoxide
justification: The oven emitting dangerous amounts of carbon monoxide poses a significant health risk, potentially leading to injury or death if not addressed.

incident_description: I placed an Anchor Hocking glass baking dish in the oven with 6 rolls to bake at 350 for 13 minutes. At around 12 minutes I peeked in the oven to see if they had browned yet, they had not so i closed the door and decided to wait until the 13 min mark about 2 minutes later I heard a loud sound from the oven and to my complete horror when I opened the oven door there were pieces of glass everywhere  and still making sounds so i closed the door quickly and turned the oven off.  If i had opened the oven door to check on the doneness of the rolls as it exploded, i can only imagine what could have happened, as i am a nurse and have seen a lot. This could have not only blinded me but also burned and possibly could have killed me in the case a shard had penetrated my carotid which is not out of the realm of posssibilities and if i had been taking it out and holding it something fatal could  have happened and to my utter dismay find almost 17-18 pages on this site with complaints about the same Anchor Hocking glass baking dish that states that it is made for baking and sold as such. I am so lucky to not have been seriously injured or blinded or disfigured or burned. This is beyond my comprehension.
justification: The incident involved a glass baking dish shattering in the oven, but no injury occurred despite the potential for serious harm.

incident_description: GE Over the Range Microwave Model #JVM3160RF5SS tripped a circuit breaker.  After resetting the circuit breaker, the unit instantly began making a vibrating/buzzing noise, even though the unit was not in the "ON" position or operating.  I soon began to smell the very distinct smell of electric (burning plastic) and smoke came into the kitchen.  I quickly unplugged the unit and turned off the main power to the house.  The smoke and burning smell were alarming to me.  An electrician came to our house to make sure the problem was not wiring.  It was in fact from the microwave.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell, causing alarm but no injury or death. The issue was confirmed to be from the microwave, not the wiring.

incident_description: We have a Samsung gas range, model NX58M9420S.  The knobs that control the burners extend forward at an angle.  When you bump into the or slide by, they rotate and turn on the gas.  This happens to us a lot. Sometimes we are alerted by the igniter, and sometimes by the smell of gas.  Anyway, this is not safe. I suggest a recall which would involve replacing the knobs with some of a different shape, not susceptible to accidentally engaging gas flow.
justification: The incident involves accidental gas flow activation, posing a hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I have twice used a Mug Warmer (model  BWD-700, MFG: BESTINNKITS) and it reached a temperature well above the 140 degrees- Fahrenheit the manual stated it would reach. I received a slight burn on one finger from the surface. My husband, who works in electrical power protection, used a thermal reader to detect the products temperature. It was 396 degrees Fahrenheit.  The device is used to keep hot beverages warm when the beverage container is placed  on the surface of the device.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight burn (injury), and the device's temperature was significantly higher than stated, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: Our Samsung refrigerator's ice maker constantly builds up ice and drips water from the front of the ice maker tray. The refrigerator does not maintain a cold enough temperature because the ice cubes are wet when they are dispensed. I have very expensive medication that needs to be refrigerated and I am concerned about the safety of the medicine and obviously the food  stored at unsafe temperatures. Ice maker has been replaced twice under extended warrantee and now is leaking again for the third time. I'm beginning to think the problem is not with the icemaker.
justification: The refrigerator's malfunction poses a risk to medication and food safety, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Bosch dishwasher power cord recall provides to customers a power cord replacement which is also defective and provides a fire hazard.
Bosch dishwasher:
Model: SHX68T55UC/01    -   FD930601073.

As part of a recall announced in 2017, Bosch sent to my house in November 2017 a technician to replace the power cord on my dishwasher. The power replacement includes a junction box which is connected to a wire coming from the circuit breaker panel. 

On January 3rd, 2022 we noticed a plastic burning smell coming from behind the dishwasher when operating. After turning off the power to the dishwasher, we inspected the junction box and found that the terminal block in the junction box had overheated and was the source of the burning smell. The junction box terminal block as well as the wire connected to it had started to overheat and burn.
The initial feedback from Bosch (provided to me over the phone and restated by Bosch in all similar complaints) is that a loose connection could trigger this type of overheating and burning. However, connecting securely a wire to a junction box is electrical installation 101 and I am doubtful that an electrician sent by Bosch would not care of setting those connection securely. In addition, one finds dozens of such reports on the internet and in the CPSC safety reports database. 
So, the junction box that Bosch replaced as part of their recall just started to burn out. Is the junction box as defective as the initial junction box they replaced (which I believe it is), or did the technician left a loose connection after replacing the junction box? In both alternatives, how can I trust Bosch to provide me with a safe and reliable solution to this problem? How come their junction box is not UL listed? I have called Bosch support, requested to talk to a supervisor and have been waiting for several days for a call back. The fact is Bosch junction box replacement under their recall almost burned my house but they donÃÂt seem to care.
justification: The incident involved a defective power cord replacement causing overheating and a burning smell, posing a fire hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I own a Samsung Refrigerator that the ice maker continues to freeze up and when this occurs the ice maker is dysfunctional. When this occurs, mold begins to build up along with think layers of ice with the inside. This is a known defect with Samsung, yet it is a cumbersome process to get resolution.
justification: The incident involves a dysfunctional ice maker leading to mold and ice buildup, which is a known defect but does not cause injury or death.

incident_description: Wife started the microwave and heard a very loud noise coming from the microwave.  I went to start it again and wanted to record the noise but them flames shot out of the inside of the microwave and continue to burn until I shut the microwave down.
justification: The incident involved flames shooting out of the microwave, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was cooking a ham for Christmas dinner and my Frigidaire oven exploded internally, without warning. I was standing about 4 ft. From it. My wife and her Mother was upstairs with our twins and they ran down to the kitchen to see what had happened and to make sure I was ok. I explained to her that the oven exploded and was not working nowÃÂ
justification: The oven exploded but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: The interior light on my Kenmore refrigerator did not turn off when the door was shut. The light housing overheated and began melting the top of the refrigerator. Fortunately, my wife noticed the smell of burning plastic and we removed the light bulbs.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting but no injury or death occurred, and such electrical malfunctions are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description: Rivet cap exploded while cooking. It sounded like a gun shot and hit me with a blast of steam. It is a stainless steel frying pan sold under the kenmore brand name.
justification: The incident caused injury due to the steam blast and explosion, but death or severe injury is unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: Had just purchased an anchor hocking 1 cup glass measure the day before and ran it through the dishwasher and place in cabinet.  Removed the next day and placed on countertop.  Cracked two eggs into the glass and lowered a wire whisk into the glass to whisk the eggs when the glass shattered violently into many razor sharp shards flying up to a radius of about 8 feet.
justification: The glass shattered violently, posing a risk of injury, but the description does not mention any actual injury occurring.

incident_description: While using this Espresso maker, twice it was not shut off and was wound to be out of water yet still heating. After 30-60 minutes the smell of burning plastic led us to the still energized Espresso Machine. The upper plastic on the machine was hot and could not be safely touched with a finger.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and hot plastic, posing a burn risk but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Stove top burner grates on gas cooking range unsafe. Burner grates are manufactured with a slippery, non stick material , and top of burner grate is uneven causing pan/pots to wobble and slip off grate while cooking. Very high potential for scalding or burns to anyone cooking. I have tried various pans with non skid bottoms but all pans slip very easily off grates onto floor or side of stove.
justification: The description indicates a high potential for scalding or burns due to pans slipping off the grates, which constitutes an injury risk.

incident_description:
Caller stated that microwave powers on spontaneously by itself.  This has been ongoing over a month.
The manufacturer was contacted and they sent a technician out for inspection, however, they advised that they would report back to the company about the issue but the company has not resolve the issue.

Caller feels that the product has a failure and the manufacturer is aware of the issue but is not assisting.  Caller is concerned that this microwave is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The microwave powers on spontaneously, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description: We were drinking coffee out of our new green canteen coffee mugs when suddenly we heard cracking sound. My husband's cup top had split on one side of spout, as I looked down at mine, the entire spout area melted and dropped into my coffee. We had washed them by hand before use and of course because the bottom is metal a microwave was not used. The coffee was cool enough to drink and came right from our coffee pot. I called the company twice and [REDACTED] got back with me. I called Joanns and because I did not have my receipt, they could not help so I emailed their office with my safety concerns and they said because I didn't buy it online I would have to go to my local store.

incident_description:

By the time the Fire Department arrived, approximately five to ten minutes after they were called, the fire had extinguished itself. Once they finished their inspection, they informed the consumer that the fire was strictly due to her oven range and not her electrical system.

The consumer contacted the retailer and the representative she spoke to informed her that they could not assist her as the unit was no longer under warranty. The consumer tried to explain that she was just trying to report the fire but they did not take a complaint.

The consumer states that, prior to the incident, the cooktop was used three to four times per week whereas the oven once weekly.

The consumer is unsure if she will keep her unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We purchased an LG slide-in gas oven and range from Appliance Connection on August 10 of
2020 for $2,024. It arrived in September of 2020 and we installed it in November of 2020. It is
a double oven and the top oven has never worked. It doesn't get up to temp and shows an error
message. The first time I tried it, when I opened the door the flames blew out and singed my
face. The next time I tried it, it seemed to be working so I looked into it carefully. Nothing
happened so I looked a little closer and delayed flames blew out again, this time singeing my
hair, face and arm. In February of2021 I reached out to Appliance Connection who told me I
needed to speak to the Manufacturer. I first contacted LG Electronics on 3/16/21. I supplied the
proof of purchase and the serial numbers (There were 3 on the front of the oven). They told me
to try turning the oven off and on. I'd obviously already done this, but I tried resetting the
breaker as well without luck. After a lot of back and forth we pulled the oven out and found
additional serial numbers on the back. On 4/19 they again requested the model, dealer, proof of
purchase and serial numbers which I provided again. On 4/20 I finally received confirmation
that they had assigned a reference number to my case, [REDACTED], and I should be
sure and answer my phone and texts and await contact for the next steps. It also asked AGAIN
for my proof of purchase, which I uploaded. Around 5/3 I still hadn't heard from anyone so I
reached out via their chat. At that point in time they told me someone would get back to me in
2-5 days and assigned me a chat reference, [REDACTED]. On 5/11 I still hadn't heard
from anyone so I chatted again and after about 30-45 minutes they told me that they hadn't been
able to locate a service tech in our area and had referred it up the chain and gave me a new
reference number, [REDACTED] and said that someone would get back to me in 2-5
days. On 5/15 I received an email saying, "(Action Required - Please see below to upload your
proof-of-purchase with LG) Following up to your recent conversation with LG Customer
Service, your proof-of-purchase is required to proceed in processing your case. Please use the
link below to access LG's document portal and upload a legible digital scan or photograph of
your original proof-of-purchase to LG Customer Service" I forwarded this email WITH
screenshots this time of my proof of purchase to their Customer Service email and I have
uploaded the proof of purchase AGAIN. I have still not heard back, still can't use the oven. It's
dangerous and I just want someone to come out and fix it.
justification: The incident resulted in singed face, hair, and arm, indicating injury (severity 3). The repeated malfunctions suggest a likely occurrence (4) of similar incidents.

incident_description: Over the Christmas holidays, my family and I discovered a serious fire/health risk involving a Samsung electric stove( model No. NE58K9500SG/AA). Both incidents, within days of December 25, 2021, involved contact with the front burner knobs with the waist area of the user( first my granddaughter, next my wife) which caused the stovetop burner elements to go into full "on" by accidental contact. Ironically and , almost, unbelievably, the very first power level "both on some of the burner elements is "HIGH")(HI), as opposed to "LOW". The first warning each user had that the burners had been turned on was the smell and heat emanating from the burner elements. No one was injured, but they could easily have been burned(severely). It takes a simple demonstration to prove that these knobs are far too sensitive to the slightest pressure9 usually by a person's waist as they lean over the stove (perhaps to open a cupboard above the stove. I quick Internet [REDACTED] search revealed at least one other description of this product hazard( almost exactly like our experience). please
justification: The incident involved accidental activation of stove burners with potential for severe burns, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is high given the described sensitivity of the knobs and similar reports found online.

incident_description: I purchased a high-end toaster oven/air fryer from a reputable retailer. I read the manual thoroughly, and the first time I turned the oven on, it exploded and sent shattered glass flying through my kitchen. There had not been any obvious defects with the oven prior to the explosion. We were working through the initial setup "Before First Use" steps as specified in the manual; specifically, we wiped down the interior of the oven, inserted the crumb tray, plugged it in, and set it for "pizza" which, according to the manual, was supposed to walk it through a 20-minute pre-use cycle to burn off a protective coating from the heating elements. After it completed the "preheat" phase of this cycle, it exploded. When I called Breville's customer service to report this dangerous incident, the representative informed me that the shattered glass was caused by the weather. To be clear, the oven had been in its original packaging and unopened shipping box under our Christmas tree for several weeks prior to first use, and first use occurred in the kitchen of our climate-controlled home. I am unable to view the serial number or other identifying details on the oven without exposing myself to broken glass.
justification: The incident involved an exploding toaster oven causing shattered glass, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was using a Cuisinart food processor, model # EFP-14DC.  I had the grating disc in place and was grating a block of mozzarella cheese using the pulse function on the food processor.  The machine seemed to be laboring so i removed the cover and checked to make sure the cheese hadn't balled up.  Everything appeared to be ok so I replaced the cover and pressed the pulse function again and the processor started working.  Almost immediately, the cover broke off and several pieces of the cover and the bowl flew across the kitchen.  The processor had stopped as soon as the cover broke but not before the pieces flew about.   The plastic pieces were approximately 2.25 to 2.5 inches long and each had sharp points on both ends.  One of the release buttons on the cover and a spring also had come off.  I was not injured and no one else was in the room but I feel that the potential for a serious injury, particularly to eyes, could have occurred if a person had been in the path of the broken pieces.  I have always used my Cuisinart food processor with the assumption that the machine would not operate if the cover or the blades were not correctly in place and this safety measure protected the user from any possibility of injury.  I feel that the safety measures failed and that is why I am filing this report.
justification: The incident involved a food processor cover breaking and flying pieces, but no injury occurred. The potential for injury was noted, especially to eyes, if someone had been in the path.

incident_description:
We had purchased a Samsung Refrigerator that has had problems from the beginning, ice maker freezing, back panel freezing, etc.  I am sure you are aware of these know defects as it has happened to many others. 
The problem right now, TODAY, is that Samsung sent out a repair person to help fix some problems. On November 16 a repair person came and replace our ice maker. It did make ice but unfortunately something was wrong with the controls and the bottom ice maker constantly ran even in the off position...literally maniacally making ice.  When turned on, only the top unit worked and water constantly leaked from the dispenser.  The back panel froze up worse than ever within a week of this repair.  Samsung sent out another repair person Wednesday, Dec. 22.  The guy was here for almost two hours before he even touched anything.  I was so concerned with his ability that I finally called the company to ask if he was qualified and they assured me that he was and had been on the phone asking for help.  He finally took out the ice maker and within minutes told me that there was coolant leaking.  He tried to blame the last repair person, but honestly, our unit still ran before this guy came.  He called Samsung and they said it was non repairable and would contact me.  Within minutes of this happening the temperature began rising.  Before he left a loud noise started.  I made him listen to it.  He tried to tell me that he did not do anything to it, yet it was not making that noise before he started.  Then he said it was just the refrigerator starting up.  I have lived with this fridge long enough to recognize every single sound, good and bad. and this was bad!  He assure me that the only thing that wouldn't work was the top ice maker.  He stated that the water line, bottom ice maker, refrigerator and freezer would be fine.  Within a hour the temp had hit 60 degrees and I began losing everything, freezer included. By evening it was at 80 degrees. I had food supplies for Christmas dinner to feed 20 people plus a regular full freezer with meats, seafood, vegis, etc.  I have lost it all.  However, that is not the worst part.
The coolant began permeating the entire unit.  All food is destroyed as it has taken on the fumes from the coolant.  I thought I could salvage some ice, yet when I got water from the dispenser and tried to drink it, both tasted like the coolant.  The fumes are so bad that when we open the unit, we immediately get nauseated and headaches.  I have my 80+ parents living with me with major health issues and daughters with some other family members with medical concerns as well. This is an emergency situation.  This unit needs to be removed immediately as the toxicity id dangerous.
Samsung will not return my calls or emails. [REDACTED] had assured me that you would take care of this but I cannot reach him,. I got another rep on the phone who tried to tell me maybe he could prorate a refund which is totally unacceptable as this was entirely due to the damage caused by your service, not to mention that the original problems were from know defects. I have been encouraged to contact the local media as they recently did a news release on these issues. My goal is not to become a major news item. I just want my refund plus the cost of my lost food and this unit REMOVED from my house.  If we wait any longer there will also be medical bills if my family continues to have to inhale this.  I am considering sending some of them to a hotel for safety if you would prefer to add that to the cost of the expenses.  Please, I am begging you.  Resolve this today so that we can both end this.  I spoke with [REDACTED] again today, December 28, who again told me they will only give me a very minimal refund which would not even cover the cost of a new refrigerator, much less the same size as the one we had.  They will not help dispose of this.
justification: The incident involves exposure to toxic coolant fumes causing nausea and headaches, which qualifies as injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe outcomes from refrigerator repairs are not common.

incident_description:
March 2021 homeowners purchased a GE Profile Dual-Fuel Range Model P2B940SEJSS. Although multiple issues with range since purchase, 2 issues prompted this reporting. (1) flames approximately 8"(+) high from burner. Since the Service Rep came over, the burner delivers gas and does not ignite normally, but if left on long enough, erupts in what looks like a ball of fire. We (family members) no longer turn this burner on or try to use use it because of risk of fire starting and/or person getting burned). The underside of burner is blackened which shows the flame pattern (and may indicate intensity of  the fire). (2) the oven racks are coated with a substance that comes off as a powder residue when rack is slid. Risk is the powder residue being ingested by getting into the food. We do not slide the rack and cover food to avoid food contamination. Rack issue has been known since March 2021. The burner issue that poses risk of fire first happened in September (and did not get resolved).  We have been trying to get the GE Range returned  as a defective item and get a refund for many months. Since there have been multiple issues since purchase,  chose to enter the month of the most recent incident (burner issue) in #2 below. The day is the estimate.

Report updated 1/27/22:
As of today January 27, 2022, we have specifics about the causes of the still unresolved issue. These are items I thought may be more helpful and of interest to CPSC - especially in that the latest indicator is the GE Range we purchased was built with an incorrect part (i.e., are any more out there like ours?).

Picture 20220127_130643 (item on the right) 
(This is one of the reasons I prepared report [REDACTED].) A finding - The  tube that delivers gas to the front-left burner (the power burner) had a break in it (see bottom end of tube near the attachment). Gas coming out of the break in the line was igniting and flames were coming out in an uncontrolled fashion from underneath the burner rather than through the burner. This part was replaced January 11, 2022 and the flames do go through the burner now. However, the flames continue to be uncontrollable (flame picture 20220127_082445).

Picture 20220127_130643 (item on left) 
Today the Service Rep replaced the burner value in an attempt to fix the uncontrolled flame issue. This did not work. Because all parts for the front-left burner have been replaced to date, the Service Rep contacted the GE Technician. Per the GE Technician, the three orifices (gold circular looking items on picture on left) for the outer burner need to be N109 and the one orifice on the inner burner needs to be N63. On our Range, the three orifices for the outer burner are N114 not only on the original part for this Range but also on the replacement part GE sent and the Service Technician installed on an earlier visit. 
All attempts today by the Service Technician to order the correct part from GE (three N109 and one N63) failed - something about it not being in their system. To sum it up - this Range was built with an incorrect part based upon what the GE technician indicated today.
justification: The burner issue poses a risk of fire and burns, but no injury has been reported yet. The powder residue from the oven racks also presents a contamination risk.

incident_description: We own a Matag gas range we purchased in February, 2019. This range has 5 control knobs across the top front portion of the range that turns on the gas & starts the burners. Over this period we accidentally brushed the knobs which turned on the gas without knowingly doing so. There is a grey area between the knob off position & when the burner is ignited. When the knob rotation reaches the the ignition point the range will emit a clicking sound & the burner will ignite.   This grey area is approximately about 45 degrees of rotation. If you accidentally strike the knob at a 45 degree downward  angle & at the same rotation that the knob rotates it turns the gas on. If the knob stops in the grey area (described above) it will emit gas and the burner will not ignite nor will the range emit a clicking sound. When this happens the gas is emitted into the room making a very serious situation especially if you happen to leave the room. The safety device on the knobs requires the operator to press down & rotate the knob at the same time. The problem is that the downward spring tension on the knob is insufficient so the accidental 45degree motion will override the spring tension on the knob allowing the knob to stop in the grey area allowing gas to emit into the room. This is a very serious problem which could allow an explosion or carbon monoxide poison.
justification: The incident describes a serious safety issue with the gas range that could lead to gas leaks, posing risks of explosion or carbon monoxide poisoning, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased a home in October of 2020. To prepare the home for sale, prop owners did significant renovations, including purchasing all new LG kitchen appliances. This item is present in both photos of the home listing and in our documentation from the purchase of the home, as these appliances conveyed with the home. While cooking a meal in the oven, my husband and I noticed blue enamel chips in the bottom of tour household electric range interior of the oven portion (LG model: LSE4613ST /00 serial number: 001KMQG01084 manufacture date: January 2020). We searched extensively and did not observe any damage. We assumed that this was a remnant of manufacturing and cleaned it up, however; we retained those flakes. We did not notice any further issues until October 2021. Approximately around October 2, while cleaning the oven, my husband and I discovered more blue flakes matching the ovenÃÂs interior. We immediately called LG and they agreed to send a technician for diagnostic purposes. We continually reiterated that we purchased our home with this oven, so we did not have the original receipt, just the documentation with the oven on our bill of sale for the home. We were assured that that would not be a problem. The technician visited and coordinated with LG after seeing the pristine condition of the oven and the glass flakes that were falling from an unknown source in the ovenÃÂs interior. We were told by both the technician and LG customer service that this was absolutely a safety concern and were advised not to use the oven. Subsequent to the technicianÃÂs visit on October 7, LG made the determination to provide us with a refund or replacement from their Return Authorization (RA) department. At this point, the discussion stalled, because LG began asking us to provide original receipts and advised us that our documents from the purchase of our home were not sufficient for a refund or replacement without this product being under a recall. Without any way to obtain the original receipt, we have had no choice but to utilize this oven that has been deemed a safety hazard to us by the company that manufactured it. There are numerous phone conversations laying out the process for us to replace our defective product, however; LG changed what we were being told about their policies after it was apparent that this product would need to be replaced or the cost of it refunded to us. We are at a standstill with this company and are hoping that this is an issue we can have corrected to avoid any ill health effects to our family from ingesting this glass falling from an unknown source in the interior of our oven. In addition, it should be documented in recordings during our initial callas on Monday October 3 that LG disclosed to us that we were not the only ones who had experienced this phenomena.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with potential health risks from ingesting glass flakes, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
We purchased a Bosch dishwasher on 9/1/15.   We realized on 9/21/21 that it was severely leaking.  We had to cut they drywall 12 inches from the floor due to growth of black mold.  The insulation was treated with bleach and the drywall was discarded.  We contactd Bosch and they offered suggestions for an approved repair company.  We chose Mr appliance and she confirmed the leak from the tub area.

Report Updated 10/13/21:

The question I want to change is "could anyone get hurt from this issue". I answered no, but the more I thought about it, the answer should have been yes. My wife has been diagnosed with asthma. Black mold could affect respiratory functions in people with low immune systems and asthma. I don't have asthma, but my chest was tight and I experienced slight discomfort after I cut out the moldy drywall and discarded it.

Report Updated 1/31/22:

Mr. Appliance which is an authorized Bosch repair center came to our house on two visits. The first visit, the technician thought the leak was from oversudzing. She told us how to rectify, but a pump was bad and needed to be replaced (at our expense). On October 11, 2021 the technician from Mr. Appliance came out to install the new pump. I had set up the dishwasher and ran it with no soap to show the technician the major leaking coming from the right upper side of the unit. At that time the technician determined there was a tub leak. The technician said she would update her report. In the pictures I submitted, you can see there is a great deal of water accumulating in the bottom. The water is not soapy. I know because I had to use a baster to suck the water out of the bottom as evident from the original pictures. There were never any bubbles.
justification: The incident caused respiratory discomfort and potential health risks due to black mold exposure, particularly affecting individuals with asthma.

incident_description: The large burners on my GE electric range are intermittently and unpredictably overheating and glowing red when the knob is set for only low or moderate heat.  This is a potentially lethal defect, as it could cause a fire.  We intend to replace the infinite switches; however, my concern is that a cook who is unaware of this defect could leave a pot simmering on a low heat, the burner could malfunction, and the food could burn and catch fire in a matter of minutes, especially if it contains oil or fat.  I no longer feel it's safe to cook dishes that need to simmer for several hours, as standing by the stove for that amount of time to monitor whether the burner is going to overheat is impractical.  This range is only 4 years old.  I've owned other electric ranges, one as old as 17 years, that have never demonstrated this defect.  I suspect that GE has implemented a cost cutting policy in manufacturing the infinite switches that has placed profit over consumer safety.  The infinite switches should have a fail safe mechanism that ensures they cannot glow red hot unless the cook has set the knob for high heat.  This has been happening for several weeks, today both of the large burners malfunctioned when I was making dinner.
justification: The defect could cause a fire, posing a lethal risk (severity 4), and the issue occurs intermittently and unpredictably (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Turned my 3-year-old Whirlpool convection oven on to 350 degrees to preheat while preparing cake batter. This range has a "hidden" bottom heating element underneath the bottom surface of the oven. The oven heated to the set temperature. Approximately 3 minutes after placing the glass cake pan into the oven, I heard a snapping, popping sound. Fortunately, I was standing next to the oven to hear it. When I opened the oven door, I could see bright orange flames and hear sparks underneath the bottom of the oven. I turned the oven off and the snapping stopped. I pulled the range away from the wall and unplugged it. Nothing had dripped into the space under the floor of the oven. I removed the back panel and all the wiring at the cable terminal was intact and tight. The short circuit must be coming from the wiring or electrical board components inside the oven housing. Had I not been standing next to the oven to hear the problem as soon as it occurred and been there to turn it off, I fear it would have caused a major house fire. We are supposed to be able to "program" bake times and walk away from items while they are baking. I don't know that I will feel secure again leaving the kitchen while something is baking. I will not buy another oven where the heating element is NOT within the main oven area.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to immediate action.

I sanitized the CF5 placed all connections and lid on the fermenter, and started to pressurize with the spunding valve by keeping it full open at first, and closing the valve until it released CO2 at 10 psi.

There were no injuries from this close call, however the interior of machine electrical systems were discovered burned by GE repair on Sept 2, 2021 when diagnostic visit was completed.  House fire was averted because surge protector shut off power but was severely damaged as result of dishwasher electrical failure. The GE recall repair in 2011 only put a [REDACTED] on the problem, did not fix the cause of the fires.  WednesdayÃÂs repair was another [REDACTED].  A fix would require a door redesign to prevent condensation from entering the electrical controls of the machine.  There is currently a big hole in the door stainless interior panel where the door latch is located that encourages condensation to enter the door electrical connections.  I would bet there are house fires around the United States where my dishwasher model was the cause of the house fire but evidence would have been destroyed in the fire.  Fires would have been attributed to a house electrical connection problem and not having been generated by the dishwasher failure.  This is true if the machine had been directly plugged into an electrical socket.  My house close call fire was saved because a surge protecter between the machine and electrical socket protected my house from the electrical fault of the machine. I checked the internal temperate using a thermometer and it was above 40 degrees even though the refrigerator thermometer  is reading 37. Temperatures above 40 are not safe to store food.

incident_description: We have a Samsung Refrigerator with French doors.  The icemaker freezes up and the pullout drawers are freezing.  I have to defrost the Refrigerator at least 2x a week. Because of the excessive heat problem we limited the use of our oven.  We are concerned that this excessive heat could cause a fire.  We paid over $4,000 for the oven.  It is not just an inconvenience but also is a real safety concern.

incident_description: I purchased a Black and Decker microwave oven model EM720CB7 on April 30, 2020. incident_description: Our new Samsung refrigerator/freezer malfunctioned three times, allowing the stored food temperatures to reach dangerous levels.  The unit was purchased on June 21, 2021; it failed on July 14, 2021, July 22, 2021, and August 14, 2021.
justification: The refrigerator malfunctioned multiple times, posing a risk to food safety but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Samsung refrigerator inside back panel freezes up every year causing it to not cool properly so foods were not cold or frozen. It freezes up every year. We defrost it for days after each time this happens losing whatever perishables we have in the fridge and freezer. My fiance and I use the refrigerator. It was being used to keep food cold and frozen. There were no injuries. This is not a warranty issue, it is in fact a design issue. After [REDACTED] the issue we found hundreds of people had the same problem with Samsung refrigerators.
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with the refrigerator causing food spoilage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The problem occurs annually, indicating a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: Samsung refrigerator went out of food safe temperature, tempature display reads as normal while fridge is sixty degrees.
justification: The refrigerator malfunctioned but there is no mention of injury or death, only a potential food safety issue.

incident_description: We (family of 4, 2 adults, 2 kids) own a Samsung fridge, model RF261BEAESR, that suffers from manufacturing defects-- that also affects thousands of other people and many other Samsung fridge models. The defect occurs due to the back wall/ice machine freezing over which in turn prohibits the fridge from cooling to a safe temperature. We recently had to throw away hundreds of dollars of food that spoiled because the fridge temperature was actually 15+ degrees warmer than the fridge door said it was. Thankfully no one in our family got sick and we were alerted to the temperature not being right because we had fish in there that spoiled and smelled so bad that it stunk up our entire house and fridge-- and is still lingering months later. Since then we have been unable to use our fridge for food because it continues to not cool to the proper food safe temperature and we are seeking resolution (refund) from Samsung for wide spread defective refrigerators.

incident_description: Purchased a Samsung refrigerator.Due to design defects it does not maintain food at a safe temperature. The evaporator coils freeze over and cooling stops or is significantly reduced.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain safe temperatures poses a risk of food spoilage, but no direct injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: We had an Anchor glass loaf pan shatter in the dishwasher, even though it was listed and marked as dishwasher safe. The pan had been sitting on the counter until we consumed all the bread loaf we had made, which also meant there shouldn't have been any known sudden thermal changes (except by the dishwasher cycle). Injuries could have occurred when cleaning up the shattered glass or if shattered glass had gotten in to other "clean" dishware.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher-safe pan shattering, but no injuries were reported, only potential risks during cleanup.

incident_description:
FRIDGE DOES NOT STAY COLD. FOOD CONSTANTLY SPOILING.  HAZARD TO MY FAMILY.

incident_description: Samsung Refrigerator has been fixed twice. We have lost so much food due to unsafe temperatures. We now have our floors buckling because of water damage, as well as our wall.  Our family was using the product (husband, wife, and toddler). My toddler SLIPPED on the water on the floor that came out of the floor due to water sitting under my floor. She could have fallen in.

incident_description: We purchased our Samsung refrigerator on 11/7/2015 at Best Buy for $1950.44. This is not a warranty issue it is a design defect. One of the design flaws is the digital temperature to show that it is cooling at 34 degrees, when in fact, we placed a thermometer in several different places in the fridge, it was 54 degrees! We monitored it for several days and it did not get below 54 degrees. This is 14 degrees about the maximum safe temperature, which is a violation of our health and safety. We lost hundreds of dollars in food. This is a design flaw that causes the coils to freeze up so the sensor fails and the fan stops working. The second design flaw that we have been having to cope with (for several years) is the back freezes up. We have to transfer perishable food to other fridges and unplug it so it thaws every two months. We have not been able to use our ice maker for years as this causes it to freeze up even more. Third, it is leaking water to the bottom trays.
justification: The refrigerator's design flaws led to food spoilage and inconvenience, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Baby  seen in my pediatric gastroenterology practice for poor weight gain, failure to thrive.  Family had been using Baby Brezza to mix formula.  Family was not aware that settings had to be adjusted for the formula type and baby had been receiving diluted formula for the first 6 months of his life.  Once this was identified, baby gained weight quickly.  Though no specific harm to this patient, potential consequences of diluted formula in infancy are severe hyponatremia and electrolyte disturbances, malnutrition, developmental delay due to malnutrition.
justification: No specific harm occurred to the baby, but the incident involved incorrect formula preparation, which could have led to severe consequences.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that while he was using the microwave to bake a potato, after 5 mins into baking the unit burst into flames. He stated that he noticed flames emanating from the interior of the unit, he immediately unplugged it and use water to contain the flames.

The manufacturer was contacted and a service technician was sent out to inspect the damaged unit. They informed him that they are able to give a rebate towards a purchase new unit.

Caller stated that he had replaced the original unit for the current microwave.

Caller feels that this microwave is a fire hazard and should be reported.

Report Update:
This was a replacement for the same model of a General Electric microwave oven which also was
defective. The previous microwave oven turned on by itself and would not turn off until it was
unplugged. Fortunately I was home when it did this because if I had not been home, it would have
caught fire and destroyed my home. Even after a few minutes before I was able to unplug it, it was
beginning to emit a burning smell.
Thus, both General Electric microwave ovens were defective and represent potential life threatening
hazards. They should be recalled and/or taken off the market.
justification: The microwave burst into flames, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(08/16/2021) The consumer stated that she was boiling water in one of the pots. As the water was about to come to a boil, the rivets from the pot blew off and shot across the room.

No one was injured.

The consumer stated that she checked the rivets on the other pots. Those rivets seems loose also.

incident_description:
We purchased a Samsung Refrigerator a few years ago. This
appliance has a manufacturers defect with the inside temperature
along with a faulty icemaker that causes bad leaking. The outside
computer screen tells us one temperature, but the actual

manufacturers defect, and we should be fully refunded at this
point.
justification: The incident involves spoiled food consumption leading to food poisoning, which qualifies as an injury, and the issue is ongoing with a known defect.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool gas oven range model WGG745S0FS. The knobs on my gas range dont need to be pushed in to be turned on. Just bumping them will turn them on. My husband warmed up chicken in the microwave (which is above it) and bumped the knob turning it on slightly not realizing it. He warmed up his chicken, went to the room for a couple hours and then went to sleep leaving the gas on all night. I got home to my whole house smelling of gas. It had been on for approximately 14hrs before I came home from being out of town and turned it off. My husband was still asleep at the time. It has always turned on easily but I always turn it off. I was not home and this was too much of a close call! We had painters over recently and they bumped the stove turning it on 4 times, 2 of which burned the plastic that was covering it.

incident_description:
I've had my fridge for @ 3 years.  Last week I noticed that there was condensation in the vegetable/pastry boxes.  I thought water must have spilled.  I lined them with paper towels.  2 days later I went to make a sandwich and the bread tasted odd, it was moldy.  I went into boxes and noticed the condensation was back and there was now mold.  I ended up throwing out the food.  
I contacted Samsung and was told that product was out of warranty and that all they could do was place a service call and I'd have to wait for repair company to contact me.  I talked to supervisor and explained to him that mold is a very serious health issue, especially since I babysit my grandkids  and that it should be handled immediately. He responded there was nothing he could do except provide me with contact info to service provider.  I called for over 2 hours and there was no answer.  After @20 on hold line would disconnect. I called samsung back and explained the issue and [REDACTED] attempted to call himself and had same results. 
He asked me to check the temperature panel and it's not working.  I'm extremely concerned about my health,  I'm a senior citizen and I can't use my fridge.  What I'm I supposed to do?
There has been many issues with this unit for months, specifically with the ice making. I paid  close to $3,000 for this fridge, it should be in proper working order for several years.  It is a defective design and sansung is aware of it, but refuses to do anything about it.
justification: The incident involves mold growth due to a malfunctioning fridge, posing potential health risks, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I own a Samsung French Door fridge with design flaws that allow the digital temp display to show normal safe temperatures yet in the refrigerator temperatures are 10-15 degrees F. higher. My children and I are never aware the food is bad till we consume and get sick, our health and safety is at risk because the refrigerator coil freezes, the fan stops working and the air temps in the refrigerator rise unknowingly. There have been multiple design defects with ice makers in French Door units with freeze up and leaking issues too. Samsung sold this model and about 28 others knowingly and willingly for many years with no concern for its customers health and safety
justification: The description indicates that the fridge's design flaws have led to food spoilage and illness, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The issue is described as recurring and affecting multiple units, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven with Natural Convection, Stainless Steel, TO1760SS
None of this is a joke. 
I think the only reason why no lawsuits is because item is cheap, just hurts the poor, and doesnÃÂt kill just is a severe burn risk in many ways. Also, for those unconcerned about safety it is in a small category of inexpensive high wattage, small toaster-ovens. 

Why dangerous?
1) Leak from toaster heats knobs which get as hot as inside of toaster. Steam visible on knobs while heating.
2) Door does not open completely, so easily tips forward toward user and worse hot rack slides out toward user when tips.
3) Poor or zero tactile and audio feedback for off, and hard to turn-off.
4) Worse, just passed the off position is a permanently on position. So easy to accidentally keep on. Fire hazard. They even know it, and warn in big letters what to do in case of fire. Only indicator is subtle light, and very subtle in daytime since it dims (not kidding) when inside reaches set temperature.
5) Small, but BPA containing product poorly labeled.
6) Rack is in contact with glass. I could not maintain any space, even with effort. This is probably why negative reviewers report that glass shatters.

The main risk is obviously that heat leaks through backs of knobs to a a virtually unlimited temperature (maybe limit is 450 degrees F, I did not do an experiment) AND easily tips toward user spilling hot rack, and falling. Also, I think Amazon censored my review because I said it should not be sold. They did however answer my phone call, took a report, and processed a return.
justification: The description indicates severe burn risks and potential fire hazards, which can lead to injuries.

incident_description: Le Creuset Tea kettle constantly splashes boiling water wildly from the spout after heating water to boil. It doesnÃÂt seem to matter how high or low the burner is (I have tested on both gas and glass stovetops) or if I hang the spout far off the burner or not. I, a healthy and physically coordinated person have this occur whenever I hear water for my coffee, tea, ramen, etc. I have not been injured but I can see massive potential for injury, especially if someone with muscle weakness, dull reaction time, tremor, or any similar impairment attempts to use this kettle.

incident_description: Within the first month of owning the Samsung Household Electric Range I've had multiple stovetop incidents where the burner turns on  accidentally and burned  things on top of the stove. The consumer said she read the ownerÃÂs manual from cover-2-cover and there is no information in the book, indicating that nothing can block the condenser or touch it.  The consumer claims that the rep. (name unknown) at the firmÃÂs Independent Living Center (in approx.. 2018) told her that they were aware of the problem, but had not done anything to address this issue.

She has lost food on several occasions.  She also has problems with her sense of taste and smell.  Therefore, she is at a higher risk of eating food that could possibly make her sick.

NOTE:  She did not have the model and serial number available at the time of this report, but may add more details when she receives the report.

incident_description: I am a pediatrician.  Parents of a newborn baby report they own a Baby Brezza machine (similar to a coffe maker, it 'brews' individual formula bottles for babies).  Apparently the machine is able to hold a water volume larger than an appropriately proportionate amount of powdered formula mix - which can result in the preparation of formula that is inappropriately diluted.  This apparently happened on two occasions during the night, and the father didn't realize it until after the bottles had been fed.  This is gravely concerning from a nutritional standpoint for sure, but also from a safety standpoint.  In the first 4 months of life especially, babies are reliant on a milk source for all of their nutrition, and each feeding serves a crucial role (during this time, babies must gain weight at 1/2 to 1 ounce each day).  From a safety standpoint, during the first 6 months of life the kidney function in babies is immature, and it is crucial they receive a proper electrolyte balance in any fluid they consume.  Blood sodium levels in newborns are prone to fall significantly with rather modest consumption of fluids containing suboptimal electrolytes (which can result in brain swelling and seizures).
justification: The incident involves inappropriate dilution of formula, which poses serious health risks to newborns but no immediate injury or death was reported.

incident_description:

We have been calling LG and they booked us another repair weeks out. Those temperatures are not safe for edible food. The milk spoiled prematurely and the meat is supposed to stay under 40.

incident_description: About a month ago I had purchased a set of metal measuring cups from a Neighborhood Walmart for the purpose of measuring out ingredients and pouring pre-measured sauce on my meals. On the day of the incident, I had filled one of the measuring cups with sour cream and seasoning to pour on top of my salmon. Afterward, I washed the measuring cup and felt something sharp go into my thumb. At first, I thought I had somehow received a splinter from the seasoning, but upon closer inspection I had noticed that the splinter was shiny and metallic, meaning it had chipped off the measuring cup. This could have easily gotten into my meal, or someone else's had I been cooking for others, and caused oral and/or internal injuries. It should be noted that this was not the only issue I had experienced with the measuring cups, but the only one of hazard.
