DANGER!!!  FIRE HAZARD.  I bought a LG Range / Microwave combination from Costco in late September 2020 (last month).  The microwave LMHM2237 is fine.  The LG Model LTE4815 Double Oven Range is a fire hazard.  
        It is fairly easy to inadvertently bump the stove top "burner" knobs that activate the stovetop burners and unknowingly heat up anything sitting on top.  
          That happened to me twice about 2 weeks apart.  Both happened in the past 3 weeks.  The first incident, I sat a piece of plywood on top the COLD range to protect it while I removed the old microwave above it.  I carried the old microwave to the garage and was gone for less than 5 minutes.  Fortunately a friend was visiting, observed smoke coming from the stovetop and make a short video of the smoking wood before turning off the burner.  I dismissed that one as a "one of" and blamed myself.  
         Then, it happened a second time when I sat a plastic bin used to haul groceries from car to kitchen on the COLD stove top.  I unknowingly bumped the far left burner knob and fortunately was present moving items from the bin into the refrigerator when I saw the glow of the burner coming through the bottom of the bin and resulting boiling plastic and smoke.  It was a mess to clean off the stovetop but only because I was present there was no flames.
        The range would be excellent except it may burn your house down or injure your kids or you.  Consumer Product Safety Commission and/or LG should recall the range and [REDACTED], and others should stop selling it until this significant safety hazard is fixed.
justification: The incident describes two occurrences of fire hazards due to inadvertent activation of burners, resulting in smoke and damage but no injuries.

incident_description: Last night, after I was done cooking dinner, I called my family to the dinner table. My son, 6, sat at the kitchen table, and I put his plate of food in front of him. We were still waiting for his dad, my husband, to come down, and I was still setting the table. I went to our kitchen cabinet to grab a drinking glass for my son. He uses the same IKEA drinking glass every night of which we had (past tense because I threw them out last night) about 6. I reached in the cabinet, and grabbed the glass as one does. Just as the glass and my hand cleared the front of the cabinet, but before I could put it down on the counter to fill it with water, the glass exploded. No, I do not mean that it broke, cracked, or shattered. It exploded like a bomb! Thank goodness my son was at the kitchen table and not trailing behind me as he often does, or that my husband had not just arrived to the kitchen. The glass exploded with such force that we found shards in the hallway to the dining room, at least 20 feet away. My arm was covered in fine glass, like sand, and I had several places on my hand that were bleeding (nothing serious), caused by glass shooting out with enormous force. Shards were in my hair, down my shirt, and in the nice dinner on the stove that I had just made. And glass even made it's way over to the kitchen table where my son was sitting waiting for his glass of water. It honestly makes my heart stop to think of how much worse this situation could have been. My husband is a physicist. He tells me that the glass was defective and under enormous stress. I still don't understand how this could have happened. Imagine if my son had been holding that glass! We have had these IKEA glasses for about 3 years (a guesstimate). I unload the dishwasher every AM, and this happened around 6 PM at night, so there was no change in temperature or other environmental factors. The glass did not hit the shelf on the way out. I had not even put it on the counter. All I did was pick it up and it exploded, like a bomb, in my hand. It was very frightening and I am so worried that this could happen to someone else, god forbid a child. It seemed a prudent idea to report it.

1) After the popper had completed popping the popcorn, when I flipped the popcorn removable popping plate and cover over to allow the popcorn to be contained in the cover for eating I burned both hands. 2) When I flipped the removable popping plate over, the heater element in the bottom portion of the popper remains fully energized.  I could have dropped popped popcorn or residual oil used to make the popcorn directly on the energied element and caused a fire.  In addition, there was nothing to prevent me from  contacting the heater element during the removal of the popping plate.

The second time I used the popper I used the melted butter feature in the popper.  During the popping process, the melted butter ran down the popper cover and landed on the energized heater element under the removable popper plate.  This created a significant amount of smoke and was an obvious fire hazard when the popper plate was removed and adequate oxygen reached the smoldering butter on the element.

Based on these (2) incidences I have not used the popper since.  

When I filed a complaint with West Bend on 11/28/2019 regarding the unsafe aspects of the popper, I never received a response from the company.
justification: The user experienced burns and a fire hazard, indicating injury and potential for severe harm.

incident_description:
We purchased a Samsung French 4 door stainless steel refrigerator on 10/30/2015 for our new home. Model: RF28HMEDBSR/AA  Serial: 065L43BG503572W

Since then we have had a multitude of issues.  We have had the ice maker leek water, produce watery ice, ice jam up internally, as well as a frost layering the top of the ice maker unit that needs to be removed on a weekly basis.  It is not safe for it to be necessary to remove ice chunks from the ice compartment by hand. 

The thermometer is defective, fridge reads 35 degrees On the external display,  but when the temperature is taken through thermal reading is in the the 60s. This is EXTREMELY dangerous to store milk, eggs, as well as medications in a refrigerator that does not provide accurate temperature readings.  We found  thawed food in the freezer in May 2020 even though the freezer stated that the temp was -4 degrees.  All freezer food was ruined and over the next week the fridge temp rose as well.  Ice maker no longer produces ice at all.  The unit runs loudly.  After unplugging for a week and then restarting, the freezer temp does not budge from room temperature of 70 degrees and fridge is only able to get to down to 64 degrees.  My family has experienced nausea, vomiting, stomach pains, and excessive diarrhea for several months leading up to May 2020 when the fridge quit working completely.  We are confident that this is due to the consumption of spoiled food.  It was not apparent at first, but over time we realized that the milk etc did not feel very cold in the refrigerator. That is when we started taking the temps and recording the issues. 

This is unsafe for food storage. I am filing this complaint against Samsung as this is a wide spread issue on many of their refrigerator models and they are knowingly continuing to sell defective and unsafe products. There is a group of over 28,000 customers with theses same issues including mold spores in refrigerators, medical & hospital stays due to mold.

I have contacted Samsung directly and have been lied by several reps telling me that ÃÂthere are no known issues.  Samsung has a blatant disregard to the safety of their customers.  All affected Samsung refrigerators should have been recalled by now. Samsung has known about these manufacturing defects since 2006.  There are service bulletins dating back to 2006.  Samsung.  I have come to the reputable [REDACTED] for assistance with this disappointing experience with Samsung.. Samsung is continuing to manufacture and sell defective products that do not work properly and are unsafe for consumers. I have high hopes that thAt [REDACTED] will issue an investigation and demand a product recall.

incident_description: We purchased a Samsung refrigerator, model # RF28HFEDTSR/AA, in late June 2016. We have had many problems with the fridge including both icemakers not working and not dispensing water or ice properly. While researching how to fix the fridge, We were alerted to the fact that the temperature display is inaccurate. We have had to throw away a lot of food before its expiration date. We assumed it was due to our local grocery store. After placing fridge thermometers and testing with an infrared thermometer it was clear that the fridge nor freezer did not cool properly. The fridge section varies from 38-56 degrees and the freezer section varies from -10 to 26 degrees. Several times the fridge section stopped cooling entirely due to ice on the fan. Samsung did send a repairman out who verified the fridge section was 42 degrees and the freezer was 26 degrees. The repairman did replace both icemakers, both temperature sensors, the water inlet valve/filter housing and the motherboard. In less than 4 days the fridge was 45 degrees. The temperature variances continue. Theses are known design defects. There are service bulletins concerning these problems that were issued before our refrigerator was manufactured. Even with brand new parts the refrigerator is unable to maintain temperatures that are safe for food i.e. less than 40 or 0 for fridge and freezer respectively. We really feel that these refrigerators should be recalled as there is no fix to make them safe for food storage
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain safe temperatures leads to food spoilage, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung side by side counter depth refrigerator at the end of June 2015 from a store called HH Gregg.  We started to wonder if this unit was cooling properly because we were having stomach issues, so I purchased 3 thermometers to place inside of the fridge and another one inside our freezer.  The outside door panel was set at 34 degrees, which is the lowest I could set it at.  I set the freezer at 0 degrees and sometimes it is around 10 degrees.    
My fridge's inside temperatures register in the 40 and 50 degree range and then drop back into the upper 30's. It does this all day.  I am concerned about things going bad and have noticed certain foods are spoiling or going bad before their expiration dates.  

I filed with the New Jersey BBB and the New Jersey Attorney General in Feb. 2020.  A lady named [REDACTED], from Samsung's Office of the President, then contacted me shortly after.  Samsung sent out [REDACTED] at the end of Feb. 2020 to attempt to repair this refrigerator.
 First repair visit:   the repair guy told  me it was a sealed system issue and another repair guy would be out the fix on another day.

Second Repair visit:  Another repair guy came out and said all he needs to do is vacuum the condenser and blow it out.  (The repair guy showed me what he did and how to do this.)  This unit has this condenser located underneath, since it is a counter depth fridge.  I also asked the guy why my ice cubes freeze together in the ice bucket.  He said he would order a part and be back on another day.

Third repair visit:  The second repair guy returned and replaced part on the outside of the freezer door ice dispenser.  I guess the outside dispenser on the freezer door was not sealing, warm air was then allowed to enter the ice bucket, melt ice cubes which would then freeze together.

Now It is July  28, 2020 and I my inside fridge temperatures are still in the 40's and 50's.  She asked me to send her a photo of my sales receipt, so I did and she confirmed receiving it.

Emailed [REDACTED] multiple times.  Finally, on August 28th she emails me and tells me she does not have my receipt on file, so I email her a copy of my sales receipt again.

I have emailed her multiple times and she will not respond at all.  I have since filed once again with the NJ BBB and NJ Attorney General.  Have not heard anything from anyone.  

Samsung has made thousands on these defective fridges which are not cooling food properly.  They also have very poor customer support and seem to not want to be bothered by their defective products.  

Their defective refrigerators are a health and safety risk.
justification: The refrigerator's malfunction poses a health risk due to potential food spoilage, but there is no direct report of injury or death.

incident_description:
The last week of June my GE Induction range Model PHS930SLSS started to stop working.  The burners would turn on or off by themselves, or not come on at all but the oven worked.  They sent parts, the repairman came out, took the parts back and told me to unplug the stove every time it did this. Then, the burners stopped working again, and the oven. Well, at least before the oven worked.  Have 2 roast ready to put in the oven and it doesn't work. It cost us $23 for breakfast yesterday and $56 for dinner. And, this is just for one day.  We have not had a stove since the last week of June. EXTREMELY UPSET!  Read online that GE has a problem with the wiring at the back of the stove that can catch on fire.  They replaced parts, and still it has the same problems; so they replaced the stove this week.
 
Used stove yesterday and thought maybe it was me touching wrong buttons, but I wasn't and I knew it but tried to rationalize the situation.  Tried to use right front burner but it did not come on so used left. Yes, I know the pan has to fit the circles and it has to be an induction pan.

Using left front burner, and it would change from low or medium to high and/or back; or shut off completely.  I was frying eggs, had it on medium, turned my back without touching anything and it shut off; or the most dangerous was it kept turning the burner sync on by itself and would stick and took several tries to shut off.  I believe the technology in it is not perfected or the parts are just defective or it's just a plain bad product. So, I gave it the benefit of doubt yesterday, but made sure I kept locking it.

This morning, cooking eggs again, it would not really cook on medium so I turned it up, watched it and went back to medium, and turned around, it shut off by itself; turned it back on and the burner sync went back on by itself, so I pushed the burner sync button to make sure whether it was on or off, but it was off.  I'm afraid to use the oven.  Not sure what will happen.  Our house could burn down or our electrical system could blow out. It is not fit for the use intended.  2 months without a stove or oven; food spoiled, had to eat out and can't afford it.  Paid over $2400 and it's dangerous.

  My husband is a veteran that's had 2 strokes.  I do not need this.  Others on the internet have had the same problems.
justification: The stove's malfunctioning poses a potential fire hazard and has caused significant inconvenience and financial loss, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Our 2012 Bosch 500 series dishwasher caught on fire while it was running. This model is not part of the Bosch power cord recall. When we opened the dishwasher door there was no indication of fire and there was some water in the bottom because the cycle had not finished. Smoke was coming out between the top of the dishwasher door and counter.  We had to use a fire extinguisher to stop the fire and the smoldering would not stop until we pulled the dishwasher completely out of the house. There was a lot of smoke, and the smoke had a plastic like smell that burned our eyes. We cut power to the dishwasher with our circuit breaker before removing the dishwasher. My husband recalls that he thinks the switch to either the dishwasher or garbage disposal had tripped. Also, when we was pulling out the dishwasher, he saw sparks. The fire from the motor area burned the plastic, neighboring wires, insulation wrapping the dishwasher and part of the wooden cabinet which formed one side of the rough out. Based upon our photos, it looks like the fire started in the motor or perhaps even more likely the wires leading to it. I have photos which I sent to Bosch. My Bosch file number is [REDACTED]. Bosch did not give me any money and did not send anyone to inspect the machine. I sent photos and supplied all the information they requested. I hope Bosch takes this incident seriously because I actually really liked our Bosch dishwasher until it nearly burned down our house. I phoned Bosch several times and sent a series of emails. I received a lot of inconsistent responses from Bosch: they rejected my Sears receipt (yes I have it from Nov 2012 in its entirety) because Sears uses it's own item number and not the specific Bosch model on the receipt. Then I was told that we shouldn't have un-installed the dishwasher in order to have a technician look at it. This of course was absurd since our house was filled with smoke.

I did not receive any compensation from Bosch. I did not have technician see the machine. I had no contact from their safety or product development or quality departments et al.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke and eye irritation, but no serious injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My husband and I purchased a Samsung Refrigerator ÃÂ Module # RF263BEAESR on June 11, 2013 for our new home.  Within a few years, we noticed that the ice maker, every couple of weeks, would stop producing ice.  My husband would need to remove the ice tray and take a knife (or other sharp object) and chisel away a buildup of ice in the ice maker.  This was annoying and tedious, yes, but at the time, it did not seem like a fridge that was, otherwise, working fine. 

Last year, we noticed our refrigerator making a very loud noise.  We noticed that when we opened the door, this noise stopped.  After researching a bit online, we determine that the reason it turned off when we opened the fridge door was because upon opening the door, the fan stops, thus the noise was not being produced.  Again, when looking further in to it, we found people posting online that the inside of the back panel tends to freeze up in this model (and other Samsung models) and the ice is hitting the fan (hence, the noise we heard).  We watched several You Tube tutorials as to how to rectify this situation.  We went through the process of removing all of our belongings from the fridge and letting it defrost for several days.  Then, we plugged it back in.  It appeared that the problem had been solved!  However, this has continued at least five times since then.  The most recent occurrences have been much more frequent: in May 2020, end of June 2020, and July 2020.  The process of having to defrost our fridge, move all of our food to a spare fridge and/or coolers for several days, is quite bothersome and is something we should not have to do.  Again, we have researched and found that this is a known problem (as well as the ice maker issue) with Samsungs.    

The problem we have experienced now, however, is that our fridge is no longer cooling as it should.  We have our fridge set at the lowest temperature, 34?.  We started to notice that our food did not seem as cold as it should.  When I put a thermometer in the fridge, it says it is 45? (despite it being set at 34?).  When researching what an adequate and safe temperature is for a fridge (to keep food safe) I learned that it should be at or below 40?.  We are now having food spoil, including milk, eggs, and meat.  I am currently pregnant and this is not safe for myself or my husband and small child to be ingesting food at this temperature.
justification: The incident involves food spoilage due to a malfunctioning refrigerator, posing a health risk, especially to a pregnant woman and a small child, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
This is about gas range Whirlpool wfg510S0aw.

The issue was that the oven would not light up in a random fashion. Upon troubleshooting, it appears that the ignition wire was not properly insulated (see attached photo). When we stored a baking sheet inside the drawer, it would sometime connect with the un-insulated wire and the frame, thus causing a short circuit, thus preventing the oven from lighting up.

I believe that it's a safety issue, because the oven should light up all the time and not release un-ignited propane. There is a safety mechanism that cuts off the gas when the oven fails to light up, but I would opine that the appliance should not rely on that safety mechanism.

In addition, I do not believe that the internals of the appliance (see attached photo) should be accessible to the consumer during normal operations

I would suggest two changes:
1) I would have QA make sure that the wires are properly insulated

2) I would have the internals of the appliance inaccessible by consumers. If that is a manufacturing defect (missing panel), I would have QA insure that the panel is present. If by design there is no protection panel, then I would recall the entire line of product.
justification: The incident involves a safety issue with potential gas release but no reported injury or death, and the occurrence is likely due to the described conditions.

Approximately 1 minute later, we heard a loud pop and noticed that the entire glass door on the front of the oven had exploded. Glass was all over the counter and on the floor. incident_description:
LG LD57551ST dishwasher purchased in 2013.  Normal use.  Dishwasher was mid-cycle.  Fortunately spouse was home.  Smelled very strong electrical fire odor.  Quickly went throughout house to smell out the source.  Found it in the kitchen where the dishwasher was venting.  Stopped dishwasher and opened to see if anything was stuck or burning.  Because this dishwasher does not have an exposed heating element she was confident it was not a melted utensil nor did it smell like burning plastic.  The odor was stronger and smelled more serious.
Researched the problem and found multiple reports of other consumer with burned wires and circuit boards at the top right of the dishwasher front panel; one consumer said they called the fire department to extinguish.  Our did not catch fire but who knows if it would have if someone was not home to stop the cycle and unplug the appliance. Followed instructions to remove inside panel of the door and found the same problem.  Wire harnesses with melted protective coating, brittleness around wire connection to circuit board, and severe darkening around the area on the control board.  Too extensive to just replace a control board without having to replace multiple wire harness assembly parts as well. 
Contacted LG service on their [REDACTED] social media channel to report problem.  No response.

I recently remodeled my kitchen and finally have room for them and began using them.  After using the 5qt 2 times for pasta, the enamel began to crack on the bottom and chip off of the side. Every surface was hot, and the black plastic above the door came loose, pieces came off and it continued to make operating sounds. I shut door, grabbed stepstool and unplugged it from outlet in cabinet above. incident_description:
Was using a NuWave Air Fryer Brio 6-Qt

My girlfriend pulled the basket out after our fries were done.
The release "button" on the outer basket was somehow triggered and released the outer basket containing the hot oil. The oil sprayed on us and caused burns. 

I get that warnings are important, but they are a weak safety control. In my opinion, these warnings are also too vague to put the user on notice about the basket separation hazard.

It is wayyyyy too easy to inadvertently release the baskets and the warning appears to be inadequate on user manual. We are both smart people and my girlfriend went to culinary school for 2 years and this was NOT AN OBVIOUS HAZARD.

The only warning I found in the manual was "use caution when shaking basket" and on page 8 warning #9 "extreme caution must be used when moving unit containing hot oil or other hot liquids"


There were no warnings about the inadvertent separation.
There was no pictogram showing we could be splashed with hot oil.

If we had a cat or a kid nearby it would have scalded them badly. We were lucky we were adults who just got sprayed on our legs -  it sucked a lot but aside from skin discoloration and the need to use ice packs we were fine a week later. 

I was horrified. Here are some simple solutions:
(1) how about a red release button so people are more conscious of the release potential
(2) how about a lock or button cover to prevent the thumb from accidentally releasing
(3) a specific warning would be useful about the need to not slip and hit the button and to keep the basket on a level surface.

I have emailed this to Costco and Customer Service. Hopefully this changes before someone else gets burned more badly.
justification: The incident resulted in burns requiring ice packs and caused skin discoloration, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Frigidare Gas Stove Model FPGS3085KFH       Ser # NF40227050

I want to advise you of a very serious safety issue with a Frigidare gas range that results in a serious explosion hazard.
I am a retired electrical engineer. Last year we purchased a Summer house in Ohio that is 7 years old. It has the Frigidare range cited above. We recently had a problem with the oven main burner coming on but not igniting, thus filling the kitchen with gas. This puzzled me since I know that gas appliances have safety valves to prevent that.
Historically, gas appliances had pilot lights that heated a thermocouple. If the thermocouple did not sense the heat from the flame, it would not allow the main gas valve to turn on. Later, a continuous pilot light was replaced with a spark igniter and a pilot light that only turned on when the appliance was used, but it had the same thermocouple for safety. Both of these systems were very safe.
When I investigated why our kitchen filled with gas and later discussed it with the repairman, I found that this range has an entirely different system which, I believe, has a serious design flaw. There is no ÃÂpilot lightÃÂ of either type or spark igniter. Instead there is an igniter with a heating element that gets hot enough to ignite the gas. The gas valve senses the current to the igniter and if there is none, such as with a broken igniter, it will not turn on. When the igniter is new it all works fine. The design defect is that as the igniter ages it does not get hot enough to ignite the gas but the current to it is still great enough to turn the gas valve on. Hence, the gas is on and fills the room or the house depending on how long it is before the problem is discovered. 
I believe this issue is serious enough to warrant a recall.
justification: The incident describes a serious explosion hazard due to a design flaw in the gas stove, which could lead to death if the gas ignites.

incident_description:
This report involves an electrical shock hazard from a GE built-in oven (Model #JRS06SK2SS) and is the second failure of this unit.  I am not the owner but have first-hand knowledge of both incidents.  The owner of the home is an elderly woman whose son [REDACTED NAME] is my friend.  [REDACTED NAME] contacted me in March of 2019 and asked if I could inspect his mother's stove after she claimed to be shocked while making contact with it.  During my inspection, I measured approximately 120V AC using a voltmeter.  I disconnected power to the oven at the breaker and advised my friend to contact GE and to file a complaint with CPSC.  I can confirm that GE was contacted but am unsure at the time of this writing whether CPSC was notified.
A GE repairman came to the home within a week, replaced some unidentified component on the oven but refused to provide [REDACTED NAME] with any receipt or documentation.  
The second incident occurred recently and I visited the home on 8/12/20 and measured 113V AC using the same voltmeter.  This measurement was made by placing the negative probe on the stainless steel sink and the positive probe on either the stainless trim on the oven door or on one of the stainless screw heads inside the oven at the bottom surface near the door.  (picture attached to this record)

THIS IS AN URGENT SAFETY MATTER

I am a former [REDACTED] and would greatly appreciate some follow-up to this matter.  I am concerned that other consumers may have already been hurt or killed by this potential defect especially those with pre-existing heart ailments.  You can contact me directly or [REDACTED NAME] using the information provided in this report.
justification: The incident involves repeated electrical shock hazards with potential for injury, especially to vulnerable individuals, and has occurred twice with measurable voltage present.

incident_description:
Electric range malfunctioned in early morning of July 7, 2020 when no one was in the kitchen, started self-cleaning cycle, producing heat and smoke enough to set off house smoke alarms. Family members who were sleeping were awakened and consumer called local Fire Department because of unknown consequences and risk of fire. I shut off all electrical circuits in the house. Fire crews were able to remove extremely hot stove from kitchen but had to break drywall behind the stove to make sure nothing was burning or smoldering. Wood and insulation were OK. Stove remains outside but consumer is unable to open the oven door. Inside the house, fire crews had to bring in blower apparatus to help clear the noxious smoke; in fact it took several days for the odor to clear.
My great concern is that if no one had been at home, the stove might have continued to heat, in spite of possibly having shut-off fuses, and start a fire in the home, or produce enough heat to activate interior fire sprinklers. This would have ruined all furnishings, books and artwork, personal items and clothing, etc. causing terrible financial ss. A fire in the home would have threatened neighbors in the area, which is a rural and dry Southern California valley that has seen fires destroy homes in the past ([REDACTED], Dec 2017).
I will be seeking damages from GE, even though the manufacturer's warranty was one year only, on the grounds that a manufacturing defect was the likely cause of this incident, and such an incident as this is a danger to personal and property safety and must be disclosed in the public record as a hazardous event. The stove was purchased new, was less than 2 and a half years old, and was maintained in excellent condition and cleanliness.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and risk of fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My Hamilton Beach toaster oven's glass window just exploded all over me!  When I checked on Amazon where I bought it I also found numerous other reports of the same thing happening to others!  This is so dangerous!!!

We've had a Samsung over-the-range microwave for 3 1/2 years since moving into our home.  During this entire time, the microwave randomly and without assistance turns itself on.  In addition, many times the buttons won't respond to touch when attempting to turn on/turn off the unit.  

I've considered this an inconvenience to a great extent but after reading other consumer's posts about the dangers of this microwave such as fires, smoke. damage, I fear it may start a fire and damage my condo and others in the building.

The Model is MC17F808KDT.  Serial Number:  J7CZ7WOF20025R, manufactured Feb 2014.

Please recall this microwave before it causes irreparable damage.
justification: The microwave's malfunction poses a potential fire hazard, which could lead to property damage, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
FIRE HAZARD -OVERHEATING:  BOSCH refrigerator Model #B11CB50SSS/08, Serial Number FD951000007. Purchased 2016

Refrigerator had been working without incident. On August 4 the appliance was turned off from the fuse panel as soon as power loss occurred due to a storm. After power was restored and old food removed from the refrigerator, the refrigerator was turned on at the fuse box. After 3 hours, the refrigerator was opened to determine if cooling temperature had been reached- it was then discovered that the inside of the refrigerator was too hot to touch -the power was immediately turned off at the fuse box and the fire department called. The fire department found the inside of the refrigerator to be 148 degree Fahrenheit. The fire department checked the fuse box and other appliances and did not find any other issues or storm related damage.
A licensed electrician also examined the fuse box, the all-house surge protector and refrigerator electrical outlet and all were in 100% working order. It was determined that the refrigerator motor overheated and did not shut off or give an alarm of overheating.
Note that I regularly vacuum around the refrigerator so there has never been a dust build up, and the refrigerator is always used in accordance with manufactures instructions. It is a newer appliance and prior to the overheating incident had been in working order. 
PLEASE PURSUE THIS FINDING- IF THE OVERHEATING HAD OCCURED DURING THE NIGHT WHEN THE HOUSEHOLD WAS ASLEEP  MAJOR FIRE WITH FATALITIES COULD HAVE OCCURED.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator overheating to dangerous levels, posing a significant fire hazard, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

My wife had the presence of mind to go down to the basement and turn off the circuit breaker.  Smoke then subsided.  This morning, August 10th, I removed the outer panel of the front door and found the master control board partially melted and charred.  Attached wiring was also charred for a few inches adjacent to the control board. There is still a residual smell of burned plastic in our kitchen.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injuries or deaths were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the detailed description of the damage and residual effects.

incident_description:
We used the Kitchenaid KCM222CU 14-cup electric coffee maker to make 10 cups of coffee. While pouring the coffee over our sink (because the glass carafe normally drips), the top plastic ring connecting the plastic handle to the glass came off. Thankfully nobody was hurt. However, if this had come off while removing the pot from the appliance or while pouring over the counter then we could have had severe injuries from 10-cups of scalding hot coffee and/or broken glass if the carafe fell.

The plastic ring can be press-fit back onto the silicone ring on top of the glass portion of the the carafe; however, we no longer trust this coffee maker. I could not find an applicable recall on KitchenAid.com or CPSC.gov for this defect.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing hot coffee to spill, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the potential for similar malfunctions under different circumstances.

We are having an independent Frigidaire appliance repair company coming out to document this and I have also notified Lowes as well.  My plumber believes this is a faulty regulator as a result of poor manufacturing but advised to have a Frigidaire Certified installer come and document this.

incident_description:
So I bought this brand new model stove made by GE, mostly for the whole oven air fryer feature. Special ordered it from LoweÃÂs, paid $1600.00 for it. It was delivered and installed on 6/13. About three days after I started using it, I noticed a serious design flaw in the touch panel that controls the burners and the entire stove.  When cooking, I accidentally dropped a tiny bit of oil on the panel and was terrified to find I then couldnÃÂt turn the burner off. Thought it was a fluke until it happened a few days later when I opened the oven door and some of the steam which came out immediately condensed on the control panel, again rendering it unresponsive. Then I really began to investigate and found that no matter what liquidÃÂoil, spaghetti sauce, water... same results. Even worse, the liquid can change the burner settings when it hits it. So a pot that is on a low simmer can be turned to high if a small bubble bursts and the liquid lands on the screen. Bottom line....cooking is messy and a touch screen control panel that becomes unresponsive OR reacts incorrectly due to a drop of moisture on the screen is a BAD IDEA! Anyone who has ever tried to answer a phone call on their touch screen Phone with a little bit of water on their hands knows exactly what I am describing. 

I then called GE customer service on 6/22 and filed a report about a serious safety issue. I was told someone would look into it and get back to me. So as of 7/30, I had yet to receive a call back. I finally called them and was told they would be happy to send a repair man to verify what I was reporting, then try to replace the panel, then if that didnÃÂt fix it, they would consider replacing the whole stoveÃÂWITH THE SAME MODEL! I have offered to email them my video showing the issue but no, they want me to go this whole ÃÂattempt repair, nope, repair didnÃÂt work, hereÃÂs the same stove againÃÂ route while continuing to use a dangerous appliance??? 

So, now since I waited for GE to call me back, IÃÂm was out of my 30 day return window with LoweÃÂs. GE wonÃÂt stand behind their product and admit there is a serious design flaw that will likely lead to someone getting seriously hurt in a cooking fire. The LoweÃÂs manager, after seeing my video demonstrating the design flaw in the touch control panel, agreed to take the stove back as the product is DANGEROUS!  So, I am now filing this complaint now in an effort to ask the CPSC to stop manufacturers from selling stoves with this dangerous and flawed design and to let you know that based upon the questions I was asked today about my concerns, GE does NOT take a customer complaint about a potentially dangerous product seriously unless someone has already suffered a fire or bodily harm. 

Can you imagine if a pan of oil catches fire and you canÃÂt even turn the burners off? Or worse, what if your circuit breaker is in the basement and you have to run down two flights of stairs to try and turn the stove off to stop the fire? 

The model number is PSS93BP1TS and it is a GE Range with Air Fryer oven.

justification: The incident describes a serious design flaw that could lead to a fire, but no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

I have a Samsung refrigerator, Model # RF261BEAEWW/AA.

Since June 4, we have tried and tried to get it repaired., and we understand it has known issues with cooling. 

We recently had it repaired, and we have a thermometer inside the fridge to make sure it is working.
