I purchased a separate thermometer to find out the temp is actually too high and unsafe even though the display on the fridge says it is what I set it at.  This is a dangerous design flaw that has sickened my family with spoiled food as well as lost food due to early spoilage.
justification: The refrigerator's malfunction has caused food spoilage and illness in family members, indicating injury due to the incident.

incident_description: Last night, we just sat down to eat dinner. We used the Samsung oven and our air fryer to make dinner, not the stove. . We smelled smoke and got up to find the source. The pot holders were in flames they had a metal pan sitting on them with food. The air fryer basket with food was sitting on edge of stove and the corner was melted on it. We picked the pot holders up and threw them in sink with water. Smoke was choking us we opened doors and windows. The glass top on the stove has the print of the hot pad on it. Somehow someone bumped the knob getting their food and the burner came on without us knowing. The pot holders were burnt black and one fell apart .
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: At 2 am dog alerted us, walked into barn and saw the plastic cover on our VacMaster Pro 350 fully engulfed in flames on top of table.  The unit was plugged in, but was powered off.  The area that the plastic cover was burning is where the heat sealing strip is located, appears that for some reason the heat strip turned on and didn't shut off and overheated and started the fire
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death was reported, and such equipment malfunctions are rare.

incident_description:
(07/16/2020) The consumer stated that the bottom oven of her double oven range came on by itself.
The oven had been making a beeping sound earlier. 

The consumer also stated that the control board on the range has been repaired four times.
justification: The oven turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, and the repeated control board repairs suggest a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: Samsung refrigerator is not keeping food at a safe temperature.
justification: The refrigerator not maintaining safe temperature is an incident with no reported injury, and such failures are possible but not certain.

incident_description:
In 2014 I purchased a Samsung French Door Refrigerator at Best Buy. This product has known defects. It has been repaired twice already. In 2016 we paid to have the fridge repaired by Sears (order#[REDACTED]). In 2019 we filed through the NJ BBB and Samsung sent Dish to service the unit (ticket# [REDACTED]). The first service was to repair the ice machine, which had stopped making ice. The second repair was to solve a problem that was causing ice buildup behind the back panel of the fridge, which ultimately caused a fan to stop. As a result, the internal temperature in the fridge rose to dangerous levels, despite the external display incorrectly indicating that the temperature was normal. (The display read 34 degrees while a thermometer placed inside the fridge was at 44+ degrees.) This posed a health risk to my family and resulted in food spoilage/waste. 

Now the ice maker has stopped making ice AND the ice build up behind the back panel has caused to fan to stop again. These are product defects, that are well documented in Samsung service bulletins. There is also a [REDACTED] group with over 24,000 members that shows the widespread impact of these product defects: [REDACTED]. There is also class action lawsuit against Samsung regarding this issue. 

It is moral failure that Samsung has not recalled these fridges. This is a health issue. It is only a matter of time before some gets sick or dies. Samsung, please contact me ASAP to let me know when I can expect my full refund.
justification: The incident describes a health risk due to incorrect temperature readings leading to food spoilage, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Electric toaster (4 slots) - while plugged in and in use there was a glow, arcing sound that then a loud pop that blew out the toaster. I unplugged it. There were remnants of insulation and such blown out of the toaster. Toaster is 4 months old.
justification: The toaster malfunctioned with visible and audible signs of electrical failure, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I had a Rovsun air fryer and my husband was going to use it to make himself something to eat Tuesday July 28, 2020. The air fryer caught fire from inside the product. My husband and I got ahold of the air fryer and tossed it out the back door. As the fryer was on fire and melting, as we grabbed it, it dripped burning plastic onto my carpet and now it also has burned plastic into it. The fryer is a total loss. I have pictures of the item. My house could have burned because of this. Luckily we got it out. Now we have a bad smell in our house from it.
justification: The air fryer caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries, and the situation was controlled without further escalation.

incident_description: I was called to investigate the origin and cause of a fire that occurred in a resdence in Naperville Illinois. The family had replaced their gas rang 3 months prior. The family purchased a samsung range from Lowes. https://www.lowes.com/pd/Samsung-5-Burners-5-8-cu-ft-Self-Cleaning-True-Convection-Slide-in-Gas-Range-Stainless-Steel-Common-30-in-Actual-29-8125-in/50266969 The oven caught fire after 3 months. The fire was caught in time and an extinguisher was used. the range is heavily damaged.
justification: The fire caused significant damage to the range but was extinguished without injury or death.

incident_description: While my oven was pre heating, I began to slowly open the door to put in my pan and the glass on the front of the oven shattered. Didn't just crack or slowly break, it exploded and glass flew everywhere.
justification: The oven glass shattered explosively, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore Elite fridge (Model No 10651773510) from Sears in 2017. In three short years, the ice maker has stopped working. We had a Sears Repair person examine it and the issue lies in a manufacturing defect on the freezer door.  Per *regular* door use, a cluster of wires at the bottom of the door has broken in half.  The damage is irreparable and would require a door replacement or new fridge.  We certainly aren't paying for a new, expensive door only to have it break again in three years. Nor do we feel we should have to buy a new fridge.  But what started as an inconvenience (no ice) has now become a hazard in my kitchen. We have a 6yo and two pets and when the freezer door is open, several broken/open wires are exposed. 

I imagine this issue will start cropping up more and more with this model.  It is outrageous that such a 'young' and modern fridge has not only failed us but now poses an electrical issue-threat to my family.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a manufacturing defect causing exposed wires, posing a potential electrical hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My kenmore electric range 2 front burners will get stuck in the on position even when the knobs have been turned off. I have to pull out the range and unplug it from the outlet for it to turn off.
justification: The burners getting stuck in the on position poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My KitchenAid gas cook top  KCGS556ESS. The knob on front of cook top was slightly pushed over and turned on during cleaning after dinner. The cook top gave no indication of it being on. My family went to bed for the night and woke up the next morning and the house was full of gas fumes. The safety features did not work. the gas had been running for 7 hours in a closed house. I noticed it because I went to get my husbands coffee and I heard the hiss of the gas coming out of the eye.
justification: Gas leak for 7 hours in a closed house poses a significant risk of explosion or poisoning, though no injury occurred this time.

incident_description:
In April 2020 we purchased a new Frigidaire gas range.  Model FFGF3054TBE.

Since then, we have had several (six or seven) incidences of us accidentally "bumping on" the burner knobs.  This occurs by accidentally brushing up against the knob and turning it to an on position, without realizing that this has happened.  In our incidences, the burner did not light.  At some point later, we have smelled the raw gas and gone to investigate and turn it off.

We previously had a similar Frigidaire range that apparently had a much safer knob design.  This problem never happened at all in the previous 6 years that we lived here with that older stove.

The issue with the knobs on this new model is one that Frigidaire is aware of from complaints by other consumers, but they have so far refused to offer a fix, saying only that the design "meets standards."
justification: The incident involves accidental gas release without ignition, posing a hazard but no injury, and it has happened multiple times.

incident_description: The heating element of our GE Electric Range (Model JS760SLSS) exploded sending sparks and flames out and burning holes in our wooden floor.  A flying part of broken heating element also cracked the glass door on the oven.  A repairman said the circuit board on the range was broken.  We have had this range less than 2 years and this is second one we have had.  The first range broke after a month and was replaced by local appliance company from which we bought it.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned floor, cracked glass) but no reported injuries, warranting severity level 2. The recurrence with a second unit suggests possible likelihood (3).

incident_description:
Model # RBS160DM2WW
Serial # LR258346R

While cooking over the front left cooktop heating element an occupant was electrocuted when removing a metal pan from the surface.  Earlier in the week another occupant using the rear left heating element found the front right element to be warm to the touch when not in use.
justification: The incident resulted in electrocution, which is a severe injury, and there is evidence of a recurring issue with the cooktop.

incident_description:
I was using a spatula made by Cuisinart while grilling.  There was a bee flying near me and as I attempted to use the spatula to knock the bee from the air, the handle and the spatula separated, sending the metal portion flying through the air.  It hit my house and bounced off hitting my 2.5 year old son in the hand causing a large cut on his finger.  

If this had hit him in the eye or head the results could have been catastrophic.
justification: The incident resulted in a large cut on the child's finger, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such specific circumstances are rare.

incident_description:
As a new homeowner, I discovered my dishwasher was under this recall: https://store-pacto3wrn2.mybigcommerce.com/ge/recall/dishwasher_2012/?_ga=2.205036436.505496420.1595870690-1243323204.1591595330

A service was scheduled to replace the heating element.  The part was late and I had to reschedule with the service company.  About a week after this service was complete, an electrical fire began inside the door of the dishwasher, filling the kitchen with nauseating fumes.

After reporting this to GE, another service was scheduled to repair the electrical components.  The part was late again and I had to reschedule with the service company.  The technician reported that the component was beyond repair.

Now, after all this, representatives from GE are now telling me that "This recall work, or the free repair you are referring to was completed earlier this year. With this said the recall portion has been completed and the free repair or rebate option that the recall offers is no longer available" and also "the additional issue you experienced with the smoke coming out of the control area was not directly related to the recall and is a separate issue"
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and nauseating fumes, which could cause injury, but no death was reported.

incident_description: On March 13th my daughter purchased a Best Choice Products 5.5qt 6-in-1 Digital Family Sized Air Fryer Kitchen Appliance w/ LCD Screen and Non-Stick Fryer Basket Black for me through Walmart.com..  Until now the product worked perfectly. I was cooking 6 frozen fish fillets about 10 mins. Cooking 3 at a time I was on my second batch. I had walked outside for 7 minutes came back in and my kitchen was smokey and the air fryer was on fire. The reason I know it was 7 minutes because the air fryer was still going and had 3 mins remaining. As you can see by the pictures the area it caught fire was the wiring inside the fryer.
justification: The air fryer caught fire, causing smoke in the kitchen, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kitoart meat grinder attachment for a [REDACTED] stand mixer on August 7, 2019 from Amazon (https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B07RWYW74H/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1).  We used this product extensively and without incident until July 24, 2020.  On July 24th, after grinding up approximately 4lbs of boneless turkey breasts, we found a small, approximately 1/4 inch metal shard in the sink while cleaning the grinder.  The sharp is extremely sharp and, with jagged and ponted edges.  There was an approximately 1/2 inch break in the grinding screw mechanism, which is larger than the shard that we found.  We confirmed that the metal shard was not the only missing piece from the break in the grinding screw mechanism.

We have discontinued use of and preserved the meat grinder and the shard as well as having taken pictures thereof.  We will need to discard the meat ground that day as well as any meat in our freezer that we had ground previously with the product.  This will result in a loss of at least $50 for us in terms of the meat that we will need to throw away and $63.99 for the purchase of the meat grinder.
justification: A metal shard was found in the meat grinder, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This is with regards to Chef's Choice International electric kettle #680 and S/N 42207

I was picking up the kettle with hot water in it and the handle broke off at the base scalding me.  The handle was made of thin ABS plastic and had cracked/fatigued at the screw mounting point and let go completely without warning.   I have photos and the parts preserved.  

I immediately wrote to both Chef's Choice International and their parent company, The Legacy Companies to let them know of the safety issue and have not received a response from either one, which made me worry that others might be scalded or burned.   Luckily, there was not much water in the pot when it broke off without warning.

Sadly, if Chef's Choice had used a more robust/appropriate plastic for the handle -- something like glass-reinforced PA 6/6 or Zytel (pennies more per unit), there wouldn't be a problem.
justification: The incident resulted in scalding, which is an injury (severity 3). The handle failure is described as a sudden and unexpected event, suggesting a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: in wiping out the inside of the emeril laagasse air fryer 360, i received a deep cut on the sharp edge of the metal support for the lower shelf (position 5).  i was wiping out the bottom of the unit and while wiping the bottom on the right side my finger brushed along the right edge and was cut by the sheet metal support.
justification: The description indicates a deep cut from sharp metal, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: two year old LG gas range was producing high levels of carbon monoxide when my carbon monoxide alarm went off I called 911 and was taken to the hospital. The fire dept called the gas company. The gas company found high levels of carbon monoxide and shut my gas stove off, because the oven was leaking  carbon monoxide. I had felt sick for several days, before the alarm went off. I was using the oven at 250 Fahrenheit to roast beef, when the alarm went off. I felt really sick, I was nauseated, I had a headache And my breathing was labored. I was put on oxygen in the hospital. Combustion is spilling into the diverter.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hospitalization and oxygen treatment) due to carbon monoxide poisoning, but the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given proper appliance maintenance and monitoring.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool electric range :
Model Number:  WTW4815EW
Serial Number:  R64613472

This range was purchased in November 2016.

Two burner controls have failed.   In both cases the controls failed such that the burner was stuck on high.   Fortunately, I was there to notice.

In some cases a pot is left on to simmer.   Had this been the case, I might have had a kitchen fire.

This range model should be recalled and Whirlpool should payoff repairs.
I have contacted Whirlpool about this safety concern and they have merely responded with "sorry for you poor experience."
justification: The burner controls failed, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description:
In March 2020, about 3 days after being issued a stay at home order in Ohio, my less-than-four-year-old microwave (Whirlpool over the range microwave (WMH31017AS))began catching things on fire.  I was not using anything new in the microwave.  It ignited a paper towel and a paper plate on 2 separate occasions.  I had regularly used these same brands of these items since I got the appliance. They were not new packages.  The day before I used a paper towel from the same roll with zero problems.  Thankfully I was right there and saw it happen and was able to put the fires out with water.

I called their customer service where I was advised to turn the power level down. WHAT? The power level must be changed every time you use the microwave.  What if I forgot and walked away?  I could have burned my house down. Ridiculous.  

I have had the appliance unplugged since I do not feel safe using it and I will be replacing.
justification: The microwave caused fires on two separate occasions, but no injuries occurred as the user was present and able to extinguish the flames.

incident_description: Timer began to buzz whenever it was turned on, and a burning smell and sparks started to come out of it.  It's a fire hazard.
justification: The timer malfunctioned with sparks and a burning smell, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
We had a GE Profile dishwasher installed in our new house in Dec. 2007.  There was one recall in Sept, 2012 and just this month, July our dishwasher overheated and nearly started a fire.  Fortunately I happened to come into the kitchen and I smelled something burning.  The dishwasher was extremely hot as well as the counter top. The element burnt the inside cavity of the dishwasher. We, my husband and I immediately turned off the breaker.

I know the dishwasher has a long chronological date however there is just my husband and myself in the household, we are retired and we travel a lot.  This dishwasher gets very little use and this should not have happened.  Due to this defect which is unsafe and could have ended up worse, ie a fire, we have to turn around and buy a new dishwasher.  I don't think that is fair and reasonable.  GE should replace it at no cost to us because it malfunctioned.  Not something we did.

I called GE and they said they would give us a new one for $539.31 installed.  I challenged them on this even asking for a supervisor [REDATED] and they basically said they couldn't do any better.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and nearly started a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The bottom metal panel (below the buttons) came unattached and is now a sharp piece of metal sticking out from the unit that I've now cut my hand on twice. We tried gluing it back but it won't stay. My guess is the glue product wasn't sufficient to handle heat from the stove.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (cut hand twice) due to a sharp metal panel, and the issue is likely to recur as the panel cannot be reattached securely.

incident_description: SAMSUNG REFRIGERATORS HAVE A DEFECTIVE PART THAT CAUSES ICE TO BUILD UP FROM THE DRAIN TO THE INTERIOR WALL, UP TO THE FAN MOTOR.  THE REFRIGERATOR THEN DOES NOT COOL BUT THE FREEZER STILL WORKS WHICH THEN CAUSES THE FOOD INSIDE THE REFRIGERATOR TO SPOIL.  THIS IS ALL OVER SOCIAL MEDIA AND I WAS ABLE TO FIX IT AFTER BUYING A NEW PART.  SAMSUNG REFUSES TO FIX THEIR DEFECT.  I GOT FOOD POISONING FROM EATING FOOD OUT OF MY REFRIGERATOR AS I DID NOT KNOW IT SPOILED DUE TO NOT BEING COLD ENOUGH.
justification: The incident caused food spoilage leading to food poisoning, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The widespread reports on social media suggest the issue is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Was cooking Raman noodles. Transformer burned out caught on fire. House filled with smoke. Turned off breaker. Removed microwave. Identified transformer as faulty unit.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury was reported, and the situation was controlled by turning off the breaker and removing the faulty unit.

incident_description: My Samsung refrigerator is freezing on the back wall causing temperatures to exceed 47. The ice maker is completely frozen and does not produce ice. Ice has formed under crisper tray and is leaking water on to floor under refrigerator.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator causing water leakage and freezing issues, posing a potential slip hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
GreetGreetings,

I have an Samsung Refrigerator RF4287HARS SN 10204308100776, that has been having ongoing issues with the Ice Maker and the Cooling Temperatures. My ice machine was fixed the first time, but it started to build up ice inside and as of today I have to chip it away every few weeks otherwise ice would not be able to produce. I've been noticing my food begun to spoil more quickly and never thought of any issue with the fridge. I bought a thermometer and now can clearly see that its operating above 50 degrees when the digital temperature is set at 34.  Food safety is most important and after I realized that the set point display temp did not correspond to the unsafe higher temps inside my refrigerator I started my quest with the U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission. I've reported this fridge to the https://saferproducts.gov/. My kids and I have been ingesting warm milk and nearly spoiled food for months perhaps even years now with occasional sickness that we are unaware of.

I've asked Samsung to come out to repair but they will not pay the bill for the labor when it is a known defect on their end. I have tirelessly contacted Samsung on numerous times to troubleshoot and try to resolve the problem at the lowest level but they are unable to provide any solution.
justification: The incident involves potential injury due to ingestion of spoiled food and occasional sickness, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) as the issue has persisted for months or years.

incident_description: I have a Samsung Refrigerator, purchased 10/31/2015. It has a digital temperature display. I have always trusted that it was the temperature in the refrigerator. Last week for the first time I put 2 thermometer in the refrigerator, a digital and analog. Both registered 9 degrees more than on the display, 46 degrees! Who knows how long the refrigerator has been in the unsafe zone. I have had stomach issues for the last two years, could that be the problem?
justification: The refrigerator's temperature display was inaccurate, potentially leading to unsafe food storage conditions, but no direct injury is confirmed.

incident_description: My desired income is a refund for the amount of purchase.  I originally bought the Samsung Refrigerator RF24FSEDBSR/AA two years ago when we moved to TX.  Since then I have had numerous messes of melted ice coming out the front and inside the door, molded foods from inconsistent temps (I use separate thermometers to regulate), and have been buying ice for over 6 months because the ice maker will not work without freezing up or making ungodly noises.  I cannot even currently pull the ice drawer out.  This is a design flaw, not a warranty issue and I would like to be able to replace it with something reliable.
justification: The incident involves product malfunction causing inconvenience and financial loss, but no injury or death.

incident_description: Our refrigerator no longer keeps food cold and the freezer hasnÃÂt worked for months. It is a Samsung French Door refrigerator with known defects. I donÃÂt know if I have been eating food that has been bad previously because the temperature indicator said it was cold. However, after being away a few days I came back to find my fridge had significant mold. I threw all my food out. When I complained about the temperature before they gave me some tips to make it cold again and it would work temporarily. However what appears to happen is that when we have a power outage due to a storm the fridge doesnÃÂt reset so I have no idea how long food has been in there at a warm temperature that then gets cold again putting my family at risk.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain proper temperature poses a risk of food spoilage, but no actual injury or illness is reported.

incident_description:
Product is a Breville Smart OvenPro BOV845BSS purchase new 09/16/19.
Had just toasted 2pieces of bread & removed them from oven & closed oven door at which time the entire glass front on the door shattered sending glass into the oven, onto the counter & floor.

Photos are available.
justification: The glass door shattered, causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Bosch dishwasher junction box caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the junction box, which is an incident with no reported injury.

incident_description: We have had constant issues with the ice maker for probably the last six years.  There are several issues including: water constantly dripping out of the water/ice maker chute to the floor (laminate floor damage from this now), ice maker CONSTANTLY freezing up (jammed up, completely iced over, not producing ice, etc) , ice randomly falls out of the chute, ice never has been made properly (always partially chopped ice when set on cubes). Not necessarily food safety issues, but definitely major issues.  We had also been noticing a lot of condensation and water dripping inside the refrigerator on the back panel.  (I don't recall when we first started noticing this, but it has been quite awhile.) After reading many other complaints online of others having issues with their Samsung units not keeping proper temperatures (too warm), I started to become a bit concerned, especially since we store expensive medical supplies (allergy serum) in it that must be maintained at refrigerated temps.  When I arrived home from vacation on July 3, 2020, I found a can of refrigerated biscuits (expiration date of August 2, 2020) had exploded open while we were gone.  This led me to believe that there was likely a temperature fluctuation issue and I immediately purchased a thermometer so we could test the internal temperature of the refrigerator.  As I suspected, the set temperature and internal (actual) temperatures differ.  In fact, the internal temperature is in the ÃÂdanger zoneÃÂ for food.  This is unacceptable and completely unsafe!  Our set temperature is set to 37 F.  On July 5, 2020, the internal thermometer recorded the temperature at about 41 F.  On July 6, 2020, the thermometer recorded the temperature at 47 F.  I have a degree in Food Science and based on my knowledge and years of professional experience, I know this is extremely unsafe!  The alleged defect not only renders the refrigerator unusable, but also poses a safety risk to me and my family because it leads to food spoilage and the risk of foodborne illnesses.  The risk of illness is further enhanced because this refrigerator is falsely displaying a temperature on the exterior reader (or the setting) that the inside of the fridge is at a standard cool temperature when, in fact, it is not.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator leading to potential food spoilage and risk of foodborne illnesses, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I am reporting an incident with a Maytag Dishwasher. On July 10 after loading the dishwasher, and selecting "Normal Wash", The dishwasher completed the wash cycle, and apparently exploded. There is a 2 inch in diameter hole blown out the front of the unit, and the top and front are black with soot.
I was not present in the kitchen when the event happened, but the damage indicates that it caught fire.
justification: The dishwasher exploded and caught fire, but no one was present in the kitchen, so there was no injury.

incident_description: Plastic holding ball bearings on left and right slides of the top rack is disintegrating allowing the bearIngs to fall into the bottom the bottom of the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involves mechanical failure without reported injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
When one is cooking something or leaning against the stove, there is the potential to touch the control knobs and turn the range burners on.

The control knobs are in the front of the stove and are super sensitive.  The consumer has leaned against the stove while cooking or cleaning the range and unknowingly found the burners on.

The consumer also had relatives in her home on different occasions, who boiled water and experienced the same problem. The oven also goes on if the stove is touched in that area.

No one has been injured and the range does not appear to be included in a recall.
justification: The description indicates incidents of burners being turned on accidentally, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
The SIEMENS DISHWASHER I own SL84A605UC/33  FD860500025 started to billow smoke from the front door  during a normal wash cycle. 
Upon inspection of the electrical wiring, it was noted the control board failed and blew a hole through the plastic package.  luckily the counter top is not flammable, otherwise the fire could have spread. However the cabinets are wood.

The fire started because of a shorted motor relay. The relay is made in China and of very poor quality.
With the poor quality of the printed circuit not being able to support the motor current, this is a serious design flaw. The copper trace thickness does not meet basic electrical engineer safe designs for sufficient skin depth at 60Hz AC.
Due to these unreliable parts this dishwasher is unsafe.
I have pictures of the burnt parts.

I contacted Siemen/Bosch and while they had similar control board problems with other dishwashers they refused to discuss this matter. They said it was not part of the recall but admitted there was a safety problem with their power wiring.

I am a registered professional electrical engineer MD. License number [REDACTED]

[REDACTED]
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke due to a control board failure, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Bosch series 800 dishwasher junction box shorted and burned. If located near paper my home would have likely caught fire.i called Bosch and they blamed the installer.  This is not logical - dangerous design.  I have pictures but this site does not accept file uploads.
justification: The incident involved a shorted and burned junction box, posing a fire risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Samsung refrigerator is pooling water under the deli tray and foods continue to spoil and mold. The humidity in the refrigerator is high. Foods also freeze due to the change in temps.
justification: The refrigerator malfunction causes food spoilage and freezing, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: While cleaning inside of lid a small metal shaving came off the screw part of the  middle of lid.
justification: A small metal shaving came off during cleaning, which is an incident but caused no injury.

incident_description:
Our Duo 8 Qt instant Pot was in the process of warming up to make soup when I Thought I heard beeping from the other room in the house But was not positive as (I was vacuuming) As I did not expect anything to be beeping.  Suddenly the vacuum went off and I heard the rapid beeping.  I walked into the kitchen following the sound of the beeping and to check the plug Of the vacuum thinking it had come unplugged.  At this time I saw flames coming out from under my Instant Pot and black putrid smelling smoke filling the corner of the kitchen.  I instantly grabbed a kitchen towel to smother the flames, pulled the plug out of the wall and removed the instant pot to the edge of the garage to let it cool off.  When I turned it upside down, the entire bottom was burnt out of the IP.  I went back into the kitchen and took some pictures of the granite counter top and the cabinet showing the soot going up the cabinet and on the countertop.

When the fire started it apparently sent a surge in the plug because it blew out the plug that the vacuum was plugged into which was the next plug along that same wall.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the Instant Pot, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Bosh dishwasher model # SHP865WD5N POWER CORD CAUGHT FIRE INSIDE JUNCTION BOX
justification: The power cord catching fire is an incident with potential for injury, but the description does not mention any harm.

incident_description: Haier refrigerator recalled due to fire hazard. My RV with that refrigerator burned down. No one was there so it completely burned with all our camping/hunting equipment. We did not receive any recall notice until now.
justification: The refrigerator caused a fire that destroyed the RV and equipment, but no injuries or deaths occurred as no one was present.

incident_description:
Oxo Good Grips Pizza Server #11194300

The pizza server is advertised as stainless steel with a beveled edge. However this "beveled edge" is a razor sharp knife edge, sharper than most kitchen knives.  There is nothing on the website and no mention on the packaging that the server has a sharp edge.

While washing it for the first time, my husband severely cut his finger. Almost all of the finger pad has been sliced off. Then while I was putting it back into the packaging to return it, I also cut my finger on the edge.

Imagine if a child picked this up -- they could have severe damage or even lose a finger. 

This product needs to be recalled ASAP.
justification: The incident resulted in severe finger injuries to two individuals, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood of occurrence is high given the sharp edge and lack of warning.

incident_description:
This is in regards to a Samsung French Door refrigerator RF25HMEDBSR/AA which we purchased new and have had ongoing issues with the ice maker and the refrigerator fan both icing over and causing food to spoil. Every few weeks we need to defrost the refrigerator so the fan can be de-iced otherwise our refrigerator temp is well above 40 degrees and our food spoils.  
Because the ice maker doesn't function, we had mold growing in there and finally just turned the entire ice maker off.
justification: The incident involves recurring issues with the refrigerator causing food spoilage and mold growth, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I bought a Samsung refrigerator (model RF23HTEDBSR/AA in January 2016.  I contacted Samsung in 2017 when the ice maker kept freezing up and the refrigerator temperature rose to unsafe food temperature storage (60s).  They had repairman replace the ice maker and motherboard.  The same thing happened again in 2019 and Samsung again paid for the replacement of ice maker and motherboard.  The same issue happened again in May/June 2020.  I contacted Samsung and customer service told both my husband and I that the problem could easily be fixed by raising the front legs of the fridge.  He send instructions and while on the phone we adjusted the legs as instructed.  On July 3, 2020 the same thing happened again.  I noticed the digital display was blinking 39 degrees.  I [REDACTED] what that meant and it meant the fridge temp was above 59 degrees.  We thawed the fridge again and the same problem happened again July 7.  Unlike before, I could not get the fridge to go down to a safe food storage temp. On July 10, the freezer started to increase in temperature.  Currently the temperature in the fridge is 75 and the freezer is 72.  This is unsafe as the digital display does not indicate the actual temperature in the fridge and freezer.  As a result, I believe the other night when I got sick, it was from eating something from the fridge that hadn't been stored at a safe temperature.  The same thing happened to my husband the night before.
justification: The incident describes repeated failures of the refrigerator leading to unsafe food storage temperatures, resulting in illness for two people.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung French style 4 door refrigerator. The ice maker in the refrigerator portion started icing up and became non functional in less than 1 year. It was replaced under warranty 1 time but continued to freeze up over and over. Once the ice maker is frozen the refrigerator continues to ice up on the back wall Twin-Cooling system which freezes food against the back of the refrigerator, making it unsafe to consume. Once the back wall is frozen solid the drain freezes up too that forces water and ice under the crisper drawers, which affects the temperature of food stored in the drawers now sitting on an ice flow. When it gets full of water and can hold no more, it flows out onto the floor creating a fall risk. There are numerous Samsung service bulletins out to repair technicians about this know design defect. It is not a warranty issue which consumers hear ad nauseam when requesting assistance for these problems. This affects appliances dating back to at least 2009 and yet Samsung continues to sell the same defective refrigerators to unknowing consumers. The last stage of this flawed product is the ice maker fails in the freezer compartment, then the freezer itself fluctuates temperature regulation, periodically raising enough the contents start to thaw and/or then refreeze - another consumer safety issue. There is an LED display on the outside of the refrigerator that is to reflect the internal temperatures. It is no where close to being accurate as verified by placing thermometers inside the compartments. Another failed safety component, as I have become sick eating food I thought was cooled to a safe edible temperature. Numerous telephone calls, chats online, text message, reports to Better Business Bureau, New Jersey Consumer Affairs, Missouri and New Jersey Attorney Generals and finally the Federal Trade Commission have not address the problem for me, however it seems there are a few lucky people that are getting full refunds of purchase price.
justification: The incident involves food safety issues and illness from consuming improperly cooled food, indicating injury (severity 3). The widespread and recurring nature of the defect suggests a high likelihood of occurrence (5).

incident_description: Frigidaire FFEF3054tsh electric range was not in use.  Set a pan on the cooktop and the outside oven door glass exploded sending glass fragments all over the kitchen
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding oven door glass) but no reported injury.

incident_description: I had a dish in oven cooking at 425 degrees as I do at least weekly when it sounded like a shotgun went off in my ear.  The whole glass outer surface of my wall oven had exploded into hundreds of pieces on the floor and much of it was popping and jumping around on the floor after it exploded for about 10 minutes.  The handle was lying in the midst of the glass.  The hot glass on the inside of the over door was fine as was the glass dish I was baking the meat in.  All things inside were fine and unharmed.  My floor is pitted and I keep finding glass in three rooms of my house it exploded so far out. Had anyone been standing in front of it they would have been seriously hurt.  It was not all peeble sized and rounded as they claim.  Some of it was shards.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and potential for injury, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Removed shelf from my Whirlpool refrigerator to clean it. The shelf slipped from hand , fell to the floor. The glass shattered into many small pieces , each about 1/4 to 1/2 inch . The distribution field of the pieces of glass was as much as 11 feet . 

Fortunately no one was close by except me so no one was injured. However the distribution of the broken glass would no doubt injured a child or pet .
justification: No one was injured, but the incident involved broken glass that could have harmed a child or pet.

incident_description:
The pressure cook had been on for approximately 1 hour, when the consumer began to turn the lid and it flew off of the pot and fell into the sink.  The pressure cooker was on the counter next to the sink at the time.

The contents in the pot flew out and landed on the consumer and her 23 month old son.  The consumer sustained burns to her right wrist and stomach.  Her son was burned on the left side of his face, left shoulder and parts of his back.

The consumer immediately called 911 and was taken to [REDACTED] Hospital.  The son was treated and released later that night.

The consumer suffered 3rd degree burns and the son suffered 2nd & 3rd degree burns.

The consumer went to a doctor approximately 2 - 3 days after the incident.  She had infections and was placed on antibiotics.

The consumer has never had any problems with the pot before. She estimates that it was used approximately 2 - 3 times per month, prior to the incident.

The consumer contacted an attorney and was advised to call CPSC.
justification: Both the consumer and her son sustained significant burns (2nd & 3rd degree), requiring medical treatment, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: I have a kitchen aid built in oven and it is 6 years old. On June 20, I roasted some vegetables and a few of them fell on the bottom of the door. I let the oven cool down and picked the vegetables after a couple of hours. when I picked up the vegetables and I tried to wipe the part where the vegetables fell, that oven part was so sharp that it made a dee cut on my middle finger on right hand. The cut was so deep and the skin was hanging on the side. The bleeding was excessive. So my daughter took me to the emergency department at [REDACTED] Hospital. The doctor gave me three stitches since the bleeding was so bad and cut was very deep. I have called the whirlpool and filed the injury report with them.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut requiring stitches, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Such injuries from sharp oven parts are unlikely but not impossible (likelihood 2).

incident_description: I purchase a new set of Circulon cookware. The handle on the saute pans which are usually a silicone type product, get hot and burn your hand. The rubber material AND the metal rings on the end become too hot to handle. I had a set previously where this never happened. Furthermore, you can see steam coming out of the end of the handle.

incident_description: My Samsung refrigerator failed to hold a safe temperature 3x. The door displays an incorrect temperature. I purchased a third party thermometer to keep inside and it the refrigerator was upwards of 50 degrees leading to food spoilage.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain a safe temperature led to food spoilage, which could potentially cause foodborne illness (injury).

incident_description: The Samsung 28 cu ft French Door refrigerator (RF28HFEDTSR/SN 065P43BF401062L) with cool select pantry and duel ice makers has a defect in the top ice maker that is inside the refrigerator itself.  The ice maker completely freezes up and stops making ice. You cannot get the ice bucket out without using a heat source such as a hair dryer to melt the ice or you have to scrape the ice away.  I tried scraping the ice and ended up tearing up my knuckles and bruising them. The ice bucket is cracked in multiple places and cannot be used at all. I have researched issues with the Samsung refrigerators and have found thousands of complaints from consumer plus a class action lawsuit against Samsung.  I contacted Samsung and was initially told to call an approved Samsung repair center near me. I called a repair company and was immediately told that the ice makers for the Samsung refrigerator model I have has a defect and that there is a service bulletin issued on what is required to fix the issue.  The cost of parts alone are over $500.00.  I was told to call Samsung and request an accommodation to cover the parts & labor for the repairs.  When I did call them, I was told that I was not eligible for any accommodation because I had not contacted Samsung directly and had not already had a service repair of any type done of the refrigerator.  Even if I needed to have the refrigerator repaired before now, I would have just called a local repair person. I would not have called Samsung.  No consumer should have to use a hair dryer or an ice pick to remove built up ice on the outside of an ice bucket in a refrigerator.  Samsung should either recall the product(s) or provide NO Charge repair accommodations.  I have spent hours talking to person after person at Samsung and no one seems concerned.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (torn and bruised knuckles) and the defect is widespread with thousands of complaints and a class action lawsuit, indicating high likelihood.

incident_description:
I own a Samsung french door refrigerator. I have always had problems with the ice make freezing, however, it has recently come to my attention that Samsung has known of this defect in addition to having knowledge that the refrigerator does not keep the temperature in a safe range defect, since 2006.

I put a thermometer in my refrigerator for 24 hours and discovered it is well over the 40 degree temperature that it is set.

I think it is reprehensible that Samsung has put our physical well-being in jeopardy, in addition to all other owners. We have had incidents of stomach issues, that could not be explained.

I have owned the refrigerator since 2016. I have had many items that have gone bad before they should have but never suspected the refrigerator as the temperature has always read 40 degrees.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain safe temperatures has led to unexplained stomach issues, indicating injury, and the issue is likely given the long-standing defect and multiple reports.

A few minutes later the disposal turned on by itself. I turned it off and scratched my head a bit wondering how it turned on by itself. Then it did it again a few minutes later. I opened the cabinet door and saw smoke. I immediately unplugged the disposal to shut it off. I noticed burn marks on the disposal plug, but none on the incinerator plug into the wall outlet.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burn marks, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury occurred.

What held the handle of the bowl together is one small screw mounted in a plastic thread. With minimal use, the thread for the screw broke and the handle fell apart.
justification: The broken handle allows unsafe operation of the food processor, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
I have a Bosch dishwasher where the power cord caught on fire.

I have called Bosch and they told me it is not affected by their current recall, so I'm guessing that their recall needs to be expanded before someone else has a fire due to their substandard power cord design.

Unfortunately, they gave me a lot of runaround to address this issue of their product catching fire, because it wasn't associated with the particular models / years included in the recall. 

What they realize but don't want to admit, is that their power cord is fairly universal to their units and is packaged completely separately from the dishwasher, and so when you order a dishwasher from a store, the power cord they send with the dishwasher could have been in stock for a long time, and could be one of the units that was made poorly and will catch fire. 

Bosch's concern appears to be minimizing the extent (and associated cost) of the recall, and placing a much lower value on people's property and human lives. They know there are still a lot of these fire hazards out there.
justification: The power cord caught fire, indicating an incident with no reported injury, and the description suggests similar incidents are likely due to a widespread design issue.

incident_description: We have a Samsung RS25H5111BC refrigerator (side-by-side) that we purchased in 2015. A year or two into owning the fridge, we noticed the food just didn't feel cold. The temperature would fluctuate, but some days it just didn't feel right, even though the external display read a constant 36 degrees. It also made a horrible noise that sounded like an airplane taking off. Eventually we got a fridge thermometer, and we found out that our fridge was maintaining a temp ABOVE 50 degrees constantly. We looked online to see what could be causing this since our freezer seemed to be working just fine. We discovered that this is a constant problem with Samsung refrigerators, so we opened up the panel in the fridge and found the elements COVERED in ice. We defrosted it, and the temp seemed to return to normal. But within a week or so, it began to creep up again. We opened it up, and it was frozen again. We have been defrosting the fridge every few weeks for years, and the temp will not go below 40 degrees now. It's very upsetting that we were unknowingly eating food that wasn't maintained at proper temperatures (and having digestive upset at the same time, mind you). The external display does NOT match the internal temperature. This is clearly a product defect considering the thousands of people who also have this problem and are unable to repair it.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator leading to food spoilage, but no direct injury is reported, only digestive upset.

incident_description:
The control knobs on this stove stick out to a point that are very easy to come into contact with.  A sight brush against the knob causes it to turn on.  The closest heat level to the Off position is the hottest.  Since purchasing it in March 2019 we have had numerous accidental turn-ons. It was purchased at the Kahului, HI Costco store.  I read several owner comments who complained about the controls. But the rating was very high. I have reported this problem to Costco, I sent a complaint to Samsung appliance division and I checked their factory parts department to see if they had recessed knobs to fit my stove; they did not.
My personal feeling is the knobs are designer overkill. They look nice but are impractical and unsafe. 
The reason I am sending this complaint is that tonight was the last straw. While preparing the evening meal one knob was brushed and burned part of the meal on the stove. I'm very surprised that children don't cause the burners to turn on.
My email is [REDACTED]
Thank you
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes numerous accidental turn-ons and a burned meal, indicating a clear hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: I bought a Bosch Dual Fuel Range (Serial #950500172) in 2015, which was  installed in my home in [REDACTED].   Starting within about two years, we would turn on the left  or right front burner, and the ignition would simply click (along with all the other burners) with the gas coming out.    We would stop, wait awhile; sometimes if we turned on another burner the one we wanted would work.   Sometimes none of the burners would work, or only the rear ones.    Authorized technicians came over the summer of 2018 to clean and then replace ignition system (at considerable cost), but the problem reappeared early that fall and then each summer since.    When humidity is high, the front and other burners cannot ignite, and we must wait for the front burners to dry out via the rear burners.   This is extremely dangerous, since gas comes out while the ignition is not working.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning ignition system that releases gas without ignition, posing a potential hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: My Samsung refrigerator temperature gauge says my refrigerator is at 38 degrees, after many years of throwing out dairy products that did not reach their expiration date ,I put a digital thermometer in refrigerator and to my horror the real temperature was 59 degrees. incident_description: I recently purchased a set of Pyrex brand food storage bowls with snap on lids. They are sold as use from refrigerator to microwave or oven. I just placed a bowl in my microwave to reheat leftover couscous with peas. The cook time was set for 2 minutes. About 40 seconds into it I heard a very loud explosion and realized the sound came from the microwave. I immediately opened the door to stop the timer. Not only had the Pyrex exploded, the interior of the microwave now shows faint gray discoloration throughout which was not there prior to the explosion. The entire bowl had exploded. incident_description:

It would be hot enough to cause pain after less than a second...Called a tech out. He said it was normal. Took his word for it. 3. It took several attempts before the controls responded and the oven shut off.
4. We applied a quality heat sensor gun to the external back panel and the SURFACE temperature OF THE CONTROL PANEL  read 363ÃÂ° Ferenheight

I finally had to lock the oven to keep it from turning on.
6. I cautiously unlocked the oven 3 weeks later (after not being able to use it at all) and the ONLY control that would work was the off/lock button. 
We have contacted Samsung multiple times and gotten multiple excuses or the run around.. supposedly in FL they have no technicians.. 
This stove is a safety hazard for multiple reasons

***F I R E risk to whatever wall it backs up to.

***GAS LEAK risk . Gas can cause a person...or pets to become severely I'll. (bad knobs) 

***E X P L O S I O N risk (slight bump of a knob a little too far without ignition of evaporator...gas leak... Explosion = injury, loss of home, or fatality) ... This stove NEEDS TO BE RECALLED BEFORE IT COSTS LIVES.
justification: The incident describes a burn injury from the hot control panel and highlights multiple ongoing safety hazards, including fire and gas leak risks, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Turned on the oven clean function for my upper oven around 1030am 6/23/2020. Came home this evening around 10pm opened oven for to check how the cleaning went. There were large shards of glass all over the door.
justification: The incident involved glass shards in the oven door but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer is concerned about the safety of the product and stated that it should be recalled.

(01/04/2020) The consumer used the product as instructed. About one hour into the process, the product exploded. The explosion caused $2500 worth of damages in the kitchen.

No injuries.

incident_description: On June 30, 2020 I turned my lower oven on to cook. Within 5 minutes smoke bellowed out with a horrendous smell. Range was unplugged but for approximately 15 minutes smoke was still coming out and we could see fire in the back of the range. I immediately called Sears Home Servicing to arrange an appointment to have a repairman come.  It was scheduled for July 1, 2020.  He took the back panel off and yes you could see where the wires burned.  He then said it was due to grease in the back even though the range was only 4 1/2 months old.  I explained that very little besides pizza and bread were cooked in the lower range and no way could that account for what he said was there.  He admitted that some grease is placed there by the manufacturer to assemble it.  Then he proceeded to say it was wired wrong in the wall unit but I explained to him that I did wire it, Sears did when installing it.  The repairman plugged it in to see what happens and sure enough the heating element started smoking and firing again.  He called his boss and told him I did not want anything to do with this range as I felt even with extensive repairs I could not trust it to do it again.  I was told a representative from Sears would decide whether I could get a new range. Also it would take 3-7 days to decide whether with the warranty I could receive another range.  After reading reviews on the Samsung range there were numerous complaints about the heating element catching fire and if we had gone outside to do our chores the house may have burnt down and with our animals inside. I just want a new range and not a Samsung so that I can feel safe in my own home.
justification: The incident involved smoke and fire from the oven, posing a significant risk but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The outside glass door shattered spontaneously while cooking and the handle broke.  There were four children in the kitchen while it happened.  There was hot, shatter glass everywhere.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass door and broken handle, posing a risk to the children present, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My Thor Range Model Number HRG3080U18 Serial Number 03353 has been making my electrical breaker for my stove outlet pop. Long story short, I went to repair the oven and what I found was completely shocking. The igniter (glow bar) got so hot that it melted the gas burner, causing it to flow upward and short out against the igniter! What an insane fire safety hazard! You could burn your house down with a failure like this! The crazy thing is that I am not the only person that this has happened to. Doing a quick search tonight I found another individual who had this SAME EXACT THING happen to them who posted a review on [REDACTED]. This product is absolutely not safe to be in someone's home and should be recalled immediately!
justification: The incident describes a significant fire safety hazard that could lead to property damage or injury, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
While cleaning side by side refrigerator with a water and [REDACTED} dampened cloth, water drained down a hole that is supposed to be sealed by this silicon type material. 5 mins after cleaning smoke started coming from under the fridge. After further investigation and I discovered that the hole that is supposed to be sealed sits right on top of a electrical component called the compressor. A small amount of water dripped down onto the compressor and ignited a fire. This hole is where the water dispenser lines come up through the bottom of the fridge.  After all was said and done I thought to myself that this could happen to anyone just cleaning this type of refrigerator. I have video and pictures of my findings. I've contacted Electrolux and I haven't received any response.

Frigidaire FFHS2622MSJ
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by water dripping onto an electrical component, but no injury or death was reported. The description suggests this could happen to anyone cleaning this type of refrigerator, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
The oven was not in use and we smelled a very strong gas smell. My husband and son immediately pulled the stove out and checked for leakage with soap and water at the connection in the back of the stove. No leak was found however they immediately closed the propane tank connected to the home.
I called HOME DEPOT, who transferred me to GE repair. the oven is 11 months old. 
We were scheduled out 10 days to have the oven looked at. I repeatedly explained the severity of the gas smell and was told there was nothing they can do and call back tomorrow.
Monday 6/15/2020 I called back first thing in the morning, after waiting over an hour on the phone, I again wad told there was nothing they can do.  I explained the severity of the gas leak and the rude individual then stated that I needed to have clearance to come in the house and to call the fire department to clear their repair man from any safety issues.
I asked what about the consumer's safety? the person [REDACTED NAME] then told me to call Consumer Affairs to report a safety issue. I called consumer relations and spoke to [REDACTED NAME] . She requested if there was any personal injury or property damage. She also offered to provide us with a check for $60 allowing us to buy a burner for our inconvenience? [REDACTED] then said scheduling is closed and they would definatley call us first thing in the morning to have someone come in sooner.
Today is 6/17/2020 and I not only never received a phone call back, I called the number again and after waiting for an hour the representative in repair stated I had to call dispatch and they opened at 9:00 am.  I am on hold again for over an hour waiting for any answer.  
Why would I want a stove repaired that leaks gas?  we paid $650 for a stove with a $160 five year extended warranty. 
We want a safe oven and our $160 extended warranty refunded.
justification: Strong gas smell was detected but no leak found, and no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kitchenaid dishwasher control board overheated, causing it to melt and smoke.

incident_description: Microwave was feeling hot inside even though it had not been used.  The next day I noticed it was glowing underneath even though it had not been used.  I unplugged it and pulled it out and noticed two burn spots on the counter over an inch in diameter.
justification: The microwave exhibited hazardous behavior (glowing, burn spots) but no injury or death occurred.

justification: The incident involved a burning smell and damage to the dishwasher's logic board, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Cuisinart toaster oven (Model TOB-40N) in 2019. I had it for less than a year and in December/January I found that the toaster would turn on by itself. I typically unplug it when it is not in use, but even after removing my toast or bagel, in the short time it takes me to put it on a plate and add a topping, the toaster over would turn on and off by itself. I found this to be dangerous, because the auto shutoff didn't seem to work. Because it was within the warranty period, I contacted Cuisinart to report the problem.  They offered to send me a replacement toaster, same model; I accepted. Now, less than six months later, I am experiencing the same problem again.  This time, the toaster turned on by itself, despite being in the OFF position, while I was out of the house.

This product seems defective and I am surprised there isn't a recall.
justification: The toaster oven turns on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Our GE Profile Dishwasher overheated and ruined some of our dishes. The heating element would not turn off. We did not have the heated dry selected on the cycle. We were simply trying to run a cleaning cycle.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and damaged dishes, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I own two KitchenAid Ranges/Ovens Model No.  KSSGG700ESS1, Serial Nos. R64721581 and R64318813.  This stove is very easy to turn on the gas burners.  You can actually turn them on just by bumping into them.  I called KitchenAid and was told this is normal for this design.  I have lost my sense of smell and it has been at least 3-5 times my adult children have come in the house and say that they smell gas. The burner could be moved from off position to the slightest on position by an easy touch.  Thank God nothing has happened due to this but this can turn into something serious. I had purchased these plastic covers and had them installed but I have a lot of problems trying to open them to use the stove and eventually just took them off.  Is there anything that can be done about this?  Please advise.

We have been dealing with issues with our Samsung appliances since we bought them in 2016. The refrigerator's ice maker freezes up, does not produce ice, leaks to the point it causes damage, and does not maintain safe food temperature. The stovetop range also does not keep correct temp and the dishwasher fails to dispense the detergent, thus failing to clean anything. This is a 6 year old fridge that we've always taken excellent care of, and it is Energy Star rated (so expected to last at least 12 years). Samsung is taking no responsibility, saying the product is out of warranty, though I have since learned that this is a known product defect.
justification: The incident caused significant financial loss and emotional distress due to spoiled food and lost breastmilk, but no physical injury or death.

incident_description: I am a Primary Care Pediatrician practicing in Longmont, CO.  A 2.5 month old baby I care for in my practice was failing to gain weight for several weeks.  I admitted him to the hospital for Failure to Thrive.  After extensive evaluation, it was discovered that the source of his poor weight gain was improper mixing of his formula via the Baby Brezza machine the parents were using at home.  Per the Nutritionist's calculations, the machine was mixing the formula at 60% of the appropriate caloric strength, so he was receiving quite dilute formula.  This is exceedingly dangerous for a young infant, as it can lead to complications such as severe electrolyte imbalances and seizures in addition to restricted growth.  Per the parents' report, there was another baby on the hospital floor at the same time with the same issue with this machine.  It appears there have been many complaints and similar medical complications reported due to this machine working improperly in the past few years.  Please recall this product immediately before any further harm is done to young children.
justification: The incident resulted in a baby failing to thrive due to improper formula mixing, which can lead to severe health complications, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased this from a store and re-packages products and re-sells them.  He contacted the manufacturer and told them about the problem and they provided a replacement butter tray.

incident_description: I had pressed the START button of my dishwasher and went into another room. After about 5-10 minutes, my lights kept flickering on and off and I was hearing a very loud grinding noise. My husband went to investigate and found the dishwasher smoking heavily and there was a bad burning smell. It took awhile to get the door off of the dishwasher to remove from the house and when we removed the front panel, we saw the wires and plastic were black and melted.

incident_description: Our Samsung refrigerator is making our family sick. It doesnÃÂt keep a cold temperature and our food is spoiling. Our ice maker is frozen and doesn't make ice. incident_description:

The metal air vents located on the top rear of the range have not been deburred or filed smooth and are razor sharp. I went to remove the plastic from the back small burner and burned my fingers touching the center piece of the burner coil.  The back burner was not on.  None of the burners were being used just the oven.  There seems to be a lot of heat coming up from the oven at that back burner location only.  So much that the burners gets very hot.

incident_description:
Ice Maker from GE Refrigerator model number: TBX22PIYARWW caught on fire overnight.
Clear signs of burning damage on the ice marker part: blackened and melted plastic. See pictures attached. Freezer side walls were also damaged. Refrigerator and freezer were being used normally. Luckily there were not further damages to the house or to anyone.

This has been going on for a year now and sears still can't fix, in spite of replacing numerous parts

incident_description:
Three times since we purchased our toaster on May 9, 2020 the toaster got into a dangerous state.  Each time the incidents occurred we were toasting bagels.  After several minutes we noticed smoke coming out of the toaster and the toaster had not automatically stopped.  Clicking the 'Cancel' button had no effect - the elements stayed on and the bagels continued to burn.  The only way I could get the toaster to stop was to unplug it.  The toaster itself became *extremely* hot to the touch, and there was a distinct smell of burning toaster parts (perhaps plastic, rubber, or metal).

After the toaster cooled down it appears the problem is that the metal piece the bread or bagel sits on gets dislodged easily and stuck on the inside of the toaster itself.  This must prevent the toaster from turning off and popping up the bagel/toast.  We had an older model that also had the metal piece dislodge occasionally, but it didn't prevent the toaster from turning off (it just made it hard to get the toast out).

I feel this is an extremely dangerous appliance.  If we had walked away or been distracted, there is no doubt the bagel would have caught on fire (it was very close).  I also am made to wonder what would happen to the toaster unit itself if it were left on indefinitely.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous malfunction with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

VERY dangerous - we had guests 2 weeks ago that did not know this -- they placed a hot casserole on the upper rack and it collapsed on the right onto the lower rack -- the contents of the casserole burning her arm.

incident_description: I bought an electric 12 cup Toastmaster coffee maker with a swing out basket from Dollar General ( https://www.dollargeneral.com/toastmaster-electric-coffee-maker-12-cups.html ). I ran a brew cycle using only water as the manufacturer recommended and had no problem. However, when I tried to brew coffee in it, the coffee did not flow out from the basket fast enough and overflowed the filter, nearly spilling out the top of the basket. I thought the coffee was just taking a long time to brew and decided to utilize the pause feature (meaning, the coffee is supposed to stop coming out of the basket while you poor a cup) but the coffee continued to flow from the basket. I wasn't expecting that so I opened the top and saw that the reason my coffee carafe was only half full was because it was all still in the brew basket. I emptied the carafe and basket and proceeded to attempt cleaning the grounds out of the basket by pouring water through it with the carafe in place. The water barely came out of the bottom, letting me know that the basket design was defective. It does not allow free flow of the liquid from the basket to the carafe, nor does the flow stop when you remove the carafe allowing the plunger to spring back into place. It appears that the weight of the wet grounds, combined with the heat of the coffee, causes the rubber stopper and/or spring to fail. This is dangerous in so many ways. First, you have the overflow hazard, then there is the burn/spill hazard when trying to utilize the pause feature. Then there is the added hazard of an electrical short if the liquid enters the bottom of the appliance when the carafe is removed.
justification: The incident describes a burn/spill hazard and potential for electrical short, indicating risk of injury.

There is some type of electrical internal failure that gives off a toxic smell.

Most importantly, because there is no model number anywhere on the oven, we were told by Maytag (the manufacturer) that we will not be able to replace the glass because we are unable to locate a model number.  

The failure to apply a sturdy and durable model number to the oven is a huge oversight and misstep by the manufacturer.  What a let down for the consumer.  What is the result?  That we must replace this oven.  The consequences are that 1) an otherwise perfectly functioning oven will be added to our landfills and 2) we as a consumer need to spend money and time on getting a replacement oven.  This is especially challenging during this economic crisis.

The first time I used the oven I set it on 425.  I accidentally grazed the left side of the metal vent that runs along the back of the range.  It was unbelievably hot  - burning hot!  I assumed there was something wrong.  I contacted Albert Lee who spoke with Whirlpool.  Whirlpool advise them there was nothing wrong with my range.  Then I called Whirlpool myself thinking there was an error.  I was informed that they would send someone out to look at it but if nothing was wrong we would pay the service fee.  I told her it didn't matter.  It needed to be looked at.  
The service man came the following week.  I was very disappointed with outcome.  I was advised by the technician that he had been to other calls regarding this slide in model.  He had been on service calls where the oven actually scorched the wall behind it. We did try to put a review on the Whirlpool website for the oven, and also on the website where we bought this item, but both have removed the review.  

Our purpose was to alert others of this dangerous situation.

incident_description:
I have a GE electric range
model JBP30WA2WW
s/n FT208584G
I was using the oven to bake a chicken and went outside for a short time.  When I came inside the house I heard a beeping sound coming from the kitchen.  I found that it was coming from the range.  The display on the range showed F2 and the range was very hot.  I immediately turned the oven dial to Off.  I opened the oven door and felt a blast of very hot air.  I looked in the oven and noticed the broiler element was glowing bright red.  I know I had the dial set to bake when I put the chicken in the oven.  The broiler element continued to glow red even though the oven dial was still in the Off position.  I twisted the oven dial around both ways and the broiler element did not go off.  The oven was extremely hot.  Unable to figure out how to turn off the broiler, I ran to turn off the circuit breaker.  It appears the controls failed in the On state instead of an Off state, which is very scary and extremely dangerous.  It likely would have caused a fire, if it continued for the full time the chicken was to bake.  If I had not been close by, the consequences could have been catastrophic.  This range has an automatic start feature and we have used it numerous times, not realizing a failure like this could happen while we are not home.  I canÃÂt imagine that we are the first this has happened to in all these years.  Has there been a recall on this range that we missed?  If not, there should be before this happens to another person.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a suite of Frigidaire kitchen appliances in January, 2020. Immediately, we (me, my son, my daughter and my tenant) noticed that the gas range knobs, if bumped inadvertently, even slightly, will allow gas to flow without the ignition being triggered. This has happened many times - literally several times every week - when merely brushing it with a hand or hip when walking past or leaning against it to access the microwave. If one of us does not notice slight tilting of the knob and leaves the kitchen, the room fills with gas. This is an EXTREMELY DANGEROUS DESIGN FLAW and, according to MANY online product reviews, is experienced by many customers.

Frigidaire referred me to [REDACTED]. The appliance serviceman refused to acknowledge the problem. When [REDACTED] came out to inspect and I refused to take ÃÂthere's no problemÃÂ for an answer, he went to his truck and got a device that senses gas. I duplicated the slight turn of the knob and we waited a few seconds. After a couple of seconds, the meter light went on indicating gas was detected. I said ÃÂLook! It detected gas!ÃÂ The repairman said ÃÂNo, itÃÂs residual gas from previous attemptsÃÂ [to demonstrate the problem]. I said that if there was that much residual gas it would have lit up immediately and I asked him to repeat the test again.

HE REFUSED TO REPEAT THE TEST FOR GAS FLOWING BEFORE THE IGNITION WAS TRIGGERED.  I again asked him to retest the range for a gas leak. He then said he had another appointment, his company was calling him and he had to leave. He told me he was reporting to Frigidaire that there was no problem. I told him that was not accurate and he said I could call Frigidaire if I disagreed. He was dismissive and clearly not interested in accurate diagnosis of the problem due to the referral relationship with Frigidaire.  

Today, I spoke to [REDACTED], a supervisor at Frigidaire, who said Frigidaire would not repair or replace the range and she refused to acknowledge that gas flowing, silently, before the ignition is triggered is dangerous or a design flaw. She told me I could purchase after market clips from Lowes to prevent the knob from being pushed. However, if the clips fail, and I have no means to test for gas flow, then Frigidaire will just claim their warranty of merchantability is invalidated by an after market alteration.    

This range has a defective design because the knobs are positioned on the front of the unit where a  mere brush of a hand, hip or stomach when leaning against the unit to access the microwave, can cause gas to silently flow.  If the knobs were positioned on the lateral surface in front of or behind the burners, it would not be possible to inadvertently brush the knobs causing gas to flow without the ignitiion switch being triggered.  The design of the range will endanger anyone living in the home and could result in life threatening, unintended combustion or death from gas inhalation.

I am requesting that Frigidaire replace this range with one that has knobs positioned on top of the range surface. 
video links: [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Thank you
justification: The incident involves a dangerous design flaw that allows gas to flow without ignition, posing a significant risk of gas inhalation or explosion, though no injury or death has been reported yet.
