I never banged against the oven door, nor used it to hold a pot, nor misused it in any other way. The explosion happened without any warning and it was very shocking. The tempered glass used for this range must have been defective.
justification: The incident involved a sudden and unexpected shattering of the oven door, causing shock but no reported injury.

incident_description: Bought baby Brezza formula pro advanced. Have been using it a couple days. Machine appears to add extra unmixed water at the end of making a bottle.  Formula appears to be less concentrated and more liquidy than when we hand make it. Baby has become extra fussy, been eating less, and started having diarrhea. Machine is not mixing the bottle properly and is dangerous to our sons health.
justification: The baby is experiencing health issues (fussiness, reduced eating, diarrhea) due to improperly mixed formula, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We purchased a Kenmore Double Wall Oven through Sears in 2014.  We NEVER use the self-clean feature on the oven as many reports have indicated that the temperatures are too hot and potentially damage the electronics.  The oven is five years old, and the walls have expanded resulting in the oven racks falling through to the bottom.  A Sears technician came out to service the oven, and he indicated that the actual walls are warped/expanded which is the cause of the grates falling through to the bottom.  I have had several hot pots fall through when I have tried to remove the pot resulting in significant burns from the splashed, hot gravies/food.  The expansion of the walls is a serious safety flaw and clearly not the result of any negligence or misuse by the owner.
justification: The incident resulted in significant burns from hot food splashing, indicating an injury (severity 3). The repeated occurrence of hot pots falling through suggests a likely frequency (likelihood 4).

incident_description: We purchased a suite of appliances from Home Depot July 4, 2016. Three of the appliances were Samsung products-French Door refrigerator with ice/water in door, over the range microwave and dual oven stove. Due to delivery delays and then service tech flooding kitchen when installing dishwasher it was October before we had a functioning kitchen. The Samsung microwave caught on fire the 4th time it was used. After multiple calls to Samsung we finally received a refund. Samsung French Door refrigerator with ice/water in door had water coming from under fridge and in the middle drawer in May 2017. We had been on a weekend trip and thought it could be due to ice maker being full and could not dump more in bin. It only did that once however it has been freezing over since then.The ice maker has been replaced twice. It continues to freeze over. It has frozen over 4 times since May 26,2020. It has frozen up 2 days in row this week. Ice Maker grows mold where ice comes of maker and on rubber chute in door. Refrigerator started making loud noise around the ice maker. Noise stops when door is opened. Due to the noise I started checking the internal temp of the unit. The door temp shows 36/37. Internal temp ranges from 41-45 and has gone as high as 50. I have had to thrown away food that had spoiled after just 1 day in fridge. I have taken meat back to grocery store that was spoiled thinking it was fault of grocery store-I now know it is due to fridge. I now freeze meat when I purchase it even if I plan to cook it the next day. Bagged salad goes bad after 1day. I am a cancer survivor with a compromised immune system. Two years ago I started having severe stomach, digestive and bowel issues. I have had many tests and procedures by my oncologist and gastro dr trying to find cause of condition. I am letting them both know about the internal temp of fridge to see if that contributes to my condition. The ice maker is a frustrating inconvenience. The noise goes from loud to a low hum. The internal temp is a major health concern for me and my family. I have filed compliant with NJ BBB and have received phone call and emails from Office of the President at Samsung. I have requested a full refund of purchase price + sales tax. The ice maker issue is a known product defect that goes back to 2006/2007 yet they continue to sale units with the known defective ice maker.
justification: The incident involves repeated appliance malfunctions leading to spoiled food and potential health risks, but no direct injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung refrigerator and have had multiple issues with it especially within the last two years. Currently the temperature gauge that is on the door is not accurate for the temperature inside the unit for the food. I also have issues with the ice maker freezing all the time and and leaks water outside the ice maker and now is growing mold because the temperature is not cold enough to sustain the ice maker and foods in the refrigerator.  It also freezes up behind the back panel weekly and leaks water under the crisper drawers and is turning moldy because the temperature is incorrect.

incident_description:

incident_description:
The consumer used a plastic cup and filled double layer plastic bags with 3 cups of ice.  Once she was done with using the ice, she poured the remaining ice cubes in a flower pot, so that it could water a plant.  Sometime later, she noticed something sticking up in the plant and discovered that it was a piece of plastic (approx. 3" x 1-1/2")..
     *  The consumer has never used glass to scoop ice out of the freezer.

The consumer removed the bin that catches the ice in the freezer and examined the plastic auger.  There was one piece that was broken and it fit the piece that was found in the flower pot, just like a jigsaw puzzle.  The auger has a frosted color and looks similar to ice.  

Same day of the incident, the consumer contacted the manufacturer.  Initially, the firm wanted to charge her to send a technician out, but the consumer had a protection plan and noted that she should not be charged.  The consumer was referred back to the warranty service company.  The consumer called the warranty company.  The firm sent her a replacement bin.

The consumer is extremely concerned that slithers could have fallen off of the auger and injured her or her family.

(dates unknown) In the past, the consumer experienced a problem where the ice was not being crushed as it should when that feature was used.  She contacted the firm and they sent out a technician.  He ran hot water over the part.  The consumer followed up with the firm further and a new replacement part was sent out to her.


The consumer did a search for the issue of the freezerÃÂs auger breaking, online, and she found numerous reports through [REDACTED].  One man even brought this issue to the news and made videos of this problem.

The firm's rep's have told her that her information would be passed on to their engineers.  The consumer wanted to speak with the firm's Engineering Dept., but she has not been able to, even after several calls/requests.

I would like ta add The broken piece that I found looks like ICE or GLASS, is the plastic used to make the auger defective? The auger should be made of a different color than ice or glass. If it is made of a very bright color such as RED OR ORANGE OR ANYOTHER color that sticks out, the person using it may be aware of a PROBLEM.

My last GE ice bin had a metal worm mechanism to push the ice through the chute. THAT IS WHAT GE NEEDS TO DO TO FIX THE PROBLEM. What are the chances of pieces of that breaking off?

I just saw on SAFERPRODUCTS.GOV other people have had the same issue as mine dating back to 2016. What is going to be done about this?
justification: The incident involved a broken plastic piece from the auger found in a flower pot, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is high due to multiple reports of similar issues.

incident_description: We purchased Samsung Refrigerator Model RF28HMEDBSR/AA.   Eight months later the icemaker stopped working.   We contacted support and did the steps they recommended.  It would fix it for a few months and then right back to icemaker freezing up.  The refrigerator leaks down the back and into the drawers, and does not keep safe temperatures.   Contacting Samsung has not resulted in resolution.  They have Service Bulletins to address these issues but claim they aren't aware of the problem.  They have no record of our contacting support and claim it is out of warranty, although it is a Manufacturing Defect and not a warranty issue.   We currently have to freeze 1/2 gallon containers in our big freezer and place them in the refrigerator to cool it down and still temperatures are above 40 degrees.   We regularly have to throw out food that has spoiled long before the sell by dates on the packaging.   We have to soak up the water that has leaked below the drawer compartments daily and mold grows regularly.   This is hazard to our health.  As senior citizens we have limited resources to replace this appliance.   Samsung knows this is a problem and yet they continue to manufacture and sell refrigerators will this same Design Defect.  We have requested a full refund for this appliance, as they have done with others, and they have refused.  These refrigerators need to be recalled and refunds issued to consumers.  Samsung needs to be forced to stop selling these defective refrigerators.
justification: The incident involves health hazards due to spoiled food and mold growth, indicating potential for injury, and the problem is likely to recur based on the description.

incident_description:
This email involves poor performance with the following Samsung fridge.

RGF298AARS series, Serial number: C78743CSB0188R
Purchased 3/7/2010

Complaints: Ongoing issues with drawers, ice build up below crisper and in ice maker and poor temp control

This product has caused me work and continual monitoring due to over icing and not keep consistent temps. I have found out that in talking to others with the same concerns that there is a design defect and two class actions in the US and Israel!
I purchased a new Samsung refrigerator in March 2010 model number RFG298AARS. Even though it is an older model, it has had many issues that Samsung has refused to resolve. I first noticed some loud grinding noises near where the ice maker is located inside the refrigerator section. Then the ice maker itself started to form ice all around the unit, causing it to seize up and not work properly. Then one day I had trouble opening the long pantry door on the bottom of the refrigerator section. This has been a continual issue and causes me to clean, wipe down, and remove the ice build-up frequently. If not properly done, it leads to a substantial leak inside the fridge along with poor temp control for food storage. I have to monitor items in the back due to over freezing and other items such as milk as temps get too low.

I have also had issues w/the shelving as they are not strong enough to handle condiments on the door.
All pictures are attached to see the maintenance issues with this unit.

I tried searching online to see if there was a solution to the problems I was having, and I then found that there have been thousands of complaints by other Samsung refrigerator customers with the same exact issues I was having. I was also made aware of a class-action lawsuit against Samsung currently in mediation regarding these issues. It is clear that Samsung has knowledge of a common, widespread problem with their refrigerators. 

I contacted Samsung to address and still wanted to reach out as my complaints and issues follow others that have had the same concerns. I have heard many accounts from other Samsung customers that any repair attempts ultimately do not work, and their units have to be serviced multiple times and eventually replaced altogether. Because of this, I was not willing to pay to have the unit serviced knowing that I would almost certainly have to replace it anyway. I also do not feel it is right for Samsung to continue to charge their customers to service a knowingly faulty product. I would like a refund for this product due to continual maintenance and headaches.
justification: The incident describes ongoing issues with the refrigerator causing inconvenience and maintenance, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:

We know from reading other owners complaints that if we spend money trying to repair this unit, it will most likely not remedy the problem.  I am a 100% disabled veteran. My wife and I are over 65. incident_description: I purchased a Samsung Refrigerator, model RF263BEAE, and it's ice maker never worked correctly.   The ice maker continues to freeze up.  I would defrost the ice maker and it would freeze back up within 2 weeks if not sooner.  About 9 months ago I finally turned off the ice maker and decided to buy bagged ice, I thought this would at least help the hassle of defrosting once every two weeks.   This did not help, the ice maker is now so frozen that it's pushed out the housing so the door does not close properly. incident_description: We have a Samsung refrigerator, Model #RF31FMESBSR that we purchased in 2014.  We couldn't figure out why our milk, fruit, meats and other parishables were going bad before the sell by dates and liquids seemed cool, but not cold when the temperature was set at 38 degrees (which is what the display showed)  We lowered the temperature and monitored it for several days with a digital thermometer.  The range was between 45 and 60 degrees.  Our food was spoiling and during this time with the Coronavirus, we could not go out all the time to get fresh food.  We stocked up on several items that all had to be thrown out.   In addition, the panel on the back of the fridge and the coils were frozen with ice coming through the hole.   My main concern was my food going bad.   I contacted Samsung asking for a service call, and they were not only rude, but indicated there was nothing that could be done by them because it was out of warranty.   We finally had to purchase a new refrigerator and we moved the Samsung in our garage for the time being.  The freezer portion still works but that is it.  I have done my homework, followed many social media sites with thousands of people have the same issue.  This is a safety issue.  This is not a warranty issue, it is a known design defect. The sensor that shows consumers what the temperature is inside the fridge is sending false and misleading temperature readings.  This is allowing people to think their food is being kept at a safe temp, when in fact it is not.  My son got extremely ill from drinking milk that went bad because of this defect.  Samsung needs to acknowledge their design flaws that allows the digital temp display to show normal safe temps yet in the refrigerator temps are actually 10-20 degrees higher.  In addition to these issues, the ice maker would no longer made ice and was frozen shut and could not be removed.   I did all the resets, unplugged and let defrost, then plub back in only for it to work for a day and then again freeze up.  Mind you this only allowed the ice maker to work again...the temps were still much much higher then what was indicated on the panel.  I have read that many consumers have been complaining about these issues and it needs to be resolved. On of the social media sites indicates that Samsung has refunded over $3MM to consumers because of these known defects, yet they wouldn't even send out someone to try to repair ours.  Some of these refunds were for refrigerators that were purchase way before ours so I'm not certain why they are discriminating against me.  If they are not going to offer me a FREE service call including any parts that might need to be replaced, then we should be refunded for the purchase of this faulty refrigerator, we should also be reimbursed for all of the food we lost.
justification: The incident caused food spoilage and illness due to false temperature readings, but no death was reported.

When the fan stops the temperature rises to unsafe levels, but the temperature on the door does not reflect, because the temperature sensor is by the frozen coils, not where the food is stored.  I was sick for days from eating spoiled chicken breast that I did not realize was being stored at 50 degrees.  The refrigerator was report it was 36 degrees. Samsung will tell you the warranty is up and you have to pay for service even though it is a $3000 product that only last just over 1 year.

incident_description:
We have bought the fridge at the end of the 2013, we received it at our new house (we moved to TX for a job) at the end of January 2014, that's when Home Depot was able to deliver it.  Within a year or two, the electronic panel went out, we could not tell the set temperatures by pressing on it, it was halfway lit up. What never occurred to us is that the panel is only responsible for setting the temps, not necessarily what is actually inside of the refrigerator. We have had milk spoiling too fast, fruits and vegetables freeze up and then go mush. I thought maybe the grocery store is selling defective groceries so I tried to pick a better firmer product, but it kept going bad. This year, with pandemic and all, we started hearing noises that would stop when you open the refrigerator doors. Turns out the back wall was completely covered in ice. My husband took out the inside panel (i wish i took pictures) and the whole wall was covered in ice. I then went to google to see what was that and I have discovered many other consumers experiencing issues just like I am. I also found a [REDACTED] group that I joined called "[REDACTED]" with [REDACTED] members as of [REDACTED]. Every single one of them is experiencing issues with their Samsung refrigerator, to the point that the moderator started sharing tips on how to ask Samsung to repair/refund for the defective product. Many of them have successfully received repairs/refunds from Samsung. Over $3M have been refunded since June of 2019.
So we defrosted our fridge by letting it sit open for a few hours, hoping this would be the end. Comes April of 2020 we started to hear the fan noise again. When the back wall gets covered in ice, the fan blades are hitting the ice creating this awful noise, as it turns out. This is where I reached out to Samsung and was told that due to the age of the unit (purchased at the end of 2013, received at the end of January 2014) Samsung can only send a repair man at my expense. Then I filed with NJ BBB, a few emails back and forth, the answer I got is basically the same, due to unit age, Samsung cannot offer anything. The fact that this defect affects so many consumers and yet, nothing is done, appalls me to say the least. Samsung customer support even tried to tell me there are no reported issues with my model, when I know for a fact my brother (we purchased same models together) had already had a repair for the compressor when his fridge was about 3 year old, and that same model is also listed in 2017 class action suit with people commenting how their back wall freezes over and they have had the Samsung repair guys coming out and fixing it temporarily. 
I wanted Samsung to offer a one time courtesy fix which they absolutely refuse to do. Reading and talking to other customers, all their fixes are only temporary, therefore, I am refusing to pay $$ to just temporarily fix the issue. And I dont think it is right for Samsung to make us pay for their defects that they are completely aware of and even issued at least 7 service bulletins and refuse to own their mistake. 
To this day you can walk to any home appliance store and buy a defective unit. 
I have also continued to talk to Samsung Customer care and got 2 tickets that were supposed to be reviewed by their highest customer accommodations department, to only find out a week later that they just cancel the tickets with some fabricated lame excuses without ever trying to reach out to me in any form of fashion. 
All I want is to have a refrigerator that does its only job of keeping food at safe temperatures.   

I am completely shocked to find out that such a major home appliance company won't stand behind their product and be allowed to continue to sell its defective appliances to US consumers.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator causing food spoilage and inconvenience, but no injury or death is reported.

Every time I opened the door after the repairs  I was anxious and would check the thermometer to make sure I was not eating spoiled food and get sick again. I know how important it is to maintain safe temperatures.  In  April 2020 refrigerator started freezing. Tech said would cost $700 to $800 to repair with no guarantee it would work. Called Samsung. incident_description: I have a Frigidaire cook top that is approximately 3 years old. On Sunday, May 24, 2020 I was using the large burner on the stove and went to turn it off. The burner valve would not budge. It seized up. I could not turn the burner off. I had to go to my garage and get a pair of pliers to turn it. Prior to turning with the pair of pliers, I turned off the other burner I had on as an abundance of caution. I called out a repairman the next day. When he came out he advised me that these burner valves have graphite in them and when they get to hot they seize up over time. The burner valve that seized up was the one to the largest burner with the most BTU's on the cook top and it is located right in front of the burner valve. Luckily for us, we were very logical in the way we turned it off. Had it happened to someone else, it could have become a catastrophic event.

incident_description:
We purchased a Samsung Refrigerator Model # RF28HMEDBSR/AA in 7/2014. We have had nothing but problems with this refrigerator. Over $1200 in repairs to replace part after part, but nothing works. The latest issue involves inaccurate and unsafe temperatures in the refrigerator. incident_description: I was using my instant pot which have used many times over the last year and a half so I know how to use it correctly. I had filled it with some meat and turned on the saute function. Within a few seconds I saw some what I thought was steam rising. But quickly realized it was smoke and smelled awful. My meat was not even sizzling so I lifted up the instant pot and saw that the bottom portion of plastic had melted and was filling my house and lungs with toxic plastic fumes. It caused some damage to the surface that was on. I am just lucky that I was standing right there. I hate to think what might have happened if I had walked away. Instant pot has recalled some models for this very reason however clearly they have not resolved the problem as yet another model is having the same issue.

incident_description: In April of 2020 I purchased a set of flatware manufactured by Cambridge Silversmiths, at Walmart in [REDACTED].  I brought the set home, washed it and put it into use.  Within a few of weeks of having the flatware my significant other was using a spoon and he cut his mouth.  I claimed it was the spoon that did it.  I did not believe it, until my daughter and I both had the same thing happen to us while eating ice cream.  Realizing that the flatware was unsafe I pulled all of it out of my drawer.  Having done that, I ordered flatware from a company I knew was not going to be a problem to replace the flatware.  I also, reached out to Cambridge Silversmiths to let them know what had happened.  The representative apologized and offered to replace the flatware with the same kind of flatware.  I was not interested as I believed there to be a design flaw.  The company did not offer me a refund of any kind but did sent me a pre paid postage return label.  I have pictures of the design but I did not save the original packaging or the receipt from Walmart because in all my years I never expected to have dangerous spoons.  I filed a complaint with the BBB and am now sending this because I am really concerned.  Luckily, the three of us did not have to receive any medical attention.  But what if this happens to a very small child.  It is concerning that this product is out there.  I have agreed to send the product back to the company.  But I am concerned that they aren't going to do anything about it, because the representative stated that it is rare that this happens.  It didn't seem rare to me because every single piece of flatware in the set seemed to all be the same.  40 pieces.  One in 1000 maybe is rare, but all 40, didn't seem rare to me.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts to the mouth) to three individuals, though no medical attention was required, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as the issue affected all 40 pieces of flatware in the set, indicating a systemic problem rather than an isolated incident.

incident_description:

incident_description: Upon cleaning the top inside of our Frigidaire, 30 inch, electric range, oven door, my wife ripped her left index finger on a very sharp edge and had to seek medical attention on 5/9/20. incident_description:
The consumer got the range from his landlord and was told that it was not second hand.

At some point, the consumer began to notice that he could be eating supper and noticed his eyes were burning.  His wife also experienced a burning in her eyes.  Initially, they were not aware of what was causing the problem.

2020:  The consumer noticed that there was a gas leak from the range.  At one point, the oven stopped coming on, when it was turned on.  The consumer identified that gas was being emitted from the oven, but there was no mechanism on the range/oven to indicate that there was a problem.

The  oven emitted gas and nothing was shutting it off.  There was no correlation between the oven being cold and the oven's temperature.

The consumer called the mfr. and was directed to their Repair Department.  The consumer asked the Repair Manager ([REDACTED]), "Do they have separate lines for the oven and range burners or do they have a manifold?"  The manager said that they have a manifold.

He then asked [REDACTED] if there was a gas solenoid (manual valve) to address this issue.  [REDACTED] said no, there was a disc in the unit for this problem.  Initially, the consumer said he wanted them to come and look at it, but changed his mind.  

The consumer has contacted the firm several times and wanted to speak with someone who can speak about the design details of this range.

The top burner of the range has a screw valve.  The pilot of that valve doesn't work very well.  The consumer has experienced incidents of turning the valve on, but the burner did not light.


The gas in the burner is at a large diameter instead of a central group orifices.  He burned the hair on his arm on one occasion.

Gas flame flares, "licks & spits."
The consumer has discontinued use of the oven.
justification: The consumer experienced burning eyes and a gas leak, indicating potential health risks and physical injury (burned hair on arm).

incident_description:

I have requested communication via email because both my husband and myself have full time jobs. They will not give any info in their emails except that they have called. Here is the problem.

I was preparing Thanksgiving dinner and we went to remove the middle grate and it was stuck. We had a hard time getting it out. incident_description:
To whom it may concern: 
I am reaching out to you in complete desperation. My entire kitchen is outfitted with Samsung appliances that are just over 3 years old, and we have had preposterous issues with them from the start. Although we are still under warranty until August 2020 thanks to the purchase of an extended warranty, these are 100% design flaws and it is extremely obvious these are not warranty or age-related.  We have a dangerously large puddle in front of our refrigerator and dishwasher, every day. We have dark brown, concrete floors and the water is not always easy to see. I have had 3 of my 4 family members slip on the water, landing on the concrete floor as well as one friend of my children. We have noticed that our food seems to spoil at an unrealistic rate, so we have installed a simple additional thermometer inside of the fridge, and have seen it regularly 20 or even 30 degrees warmer than the fridge settings are programmed to. We have a continuous pile of ice buildup inside of the ice maker which we have had to replace twice. There is a constant glacier that builds up, under the crisper drawer at the bottom portion of the fridge, pouring ice sheets and water onto the floor when the door is opened. The ice maker is continuously dripping water from where? We are unable to see it, but it has sealed our freezer door shut several times, tearing the rubber seal around the freezer door and requiring replacement. The shelves are not dependable and have broken many times, causing items to tumble out of the fridge as soon as someone opens the door. This is all very unsafe!! We noticed that in the last 3 years we have been ill multiple times, and my daughter and myself were tested for allergies, assuming something near our home was causing a problem-only to discover we have had food poisoning repeatedly. How is this company still selling faulty appliances? The dishwasher drains on to the floor and continues to smell like sewer inside of the unit. Dishes are not cleaned, even though they have been scrubbed thoroughly before being placed into the appliance. The continual puddle on the floor has caused a massive breakdown of my flooring which now must be repaired, as well.  
I have reached out to Samsung as well as the BBB in NJ (because I was told it is their HQ state) requesting a full refund so we can buy appliances that are useable and can be trusted to be safe.  I have had numerous repair people into our home to fix the endless headache from these appliances to no avail. I have contacted an internationally acclaimed attorney regarding a lawsuit, should we not find a resolution with Samsung. 
I join thousands of other Americans in asking that Samsung be held accountable for their negligence with these products. Please advise me on my next necessary step. 
Thank you for your help.
[REDACTED]
justification: Multiple family members and a friend have slipped on water from faulty appliances, resulting in injuries, and repeated food poisoning incidents have occurred due to spoiled food.

incident_description:
Item: Maytag French door, freezer on bottom, refrigerator
Model #: MFF2557KES
Serial #: 10132472JL
Short Name: Appliance Fire
Incident: Refrigerator compressor controller-relay caught fire during normal, residential use. No extraordinary circumstances existed: temperature, pressure, humidity, power load, and demand on the appliance were all unremarkable. 
Narrative: While in the adjacent room to my kitchen, I smelled the distinct, acrid odor of burning plastic. I followed my nose into the kitchen where I heard my refrigerator compressor attempting to spool up while also hearing the sound of arching electricity. I pulled the refrigerator away from wall to look for any sign of distress at the outlet, but found no indication of a problem with the wall socket. I did encounter a much more concentrated odor of burning plastic coming from the back of the unitÃÂs cabinet. I immediately turned the power off at the circuit breaker. I unplugged the unit from the wall and removed the rear access panel to investigate the problem and search out any damage. I cleaned all dust from the surfaces. I briefly plugged the unit in and witnessed the compressor relay housing emit a growing flame along with the sound of arching electricity. I again unplugged the unit and called for service. The service rep stated he had never seen that condition before. 
Assessment: Compressor relay failed in a hazardous, unacceptable manner. 

Editorial: If I had not been home at that exact moment, there is a very real chance my home would have been destroyed and my wife severely injured or killed.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with potential for severe consequences, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
At 5:00 PM, 27 April, 2020 my daughter [REDACTED] opened up the main stove on the 48 inch Blue Star (RNB486GSS, Serial Number 1703602) and was blown back by gas which also burned her eyes.  The light and convection was on in the main oven of this 48 inch range. 

[REDACTED] heard a pop, felt heat and had gas hit her eyes and was knocked back and fell over into the refrigerator door which is directly to her left and suffered yet another serious concussion.  She left early to bed and was unable to /still is unable to function normally to date (This was some 2 weeks ago and is another serious concussion).

NOTE:  (My daughter had a serious concussion last year in 2019 and suffers from debilitating headaches, concentration, vision, and cognitive function.  She is a senior at [REDACTED] University and is trying to graduate with this injury which was due to the product failures identified by the company.

The vendor and the local distributor did not contact me with a recall, notice or backfit.  No notice has come to myself, the owner of the stove, further , while the serial number range is in the window in your [REDACTED] the above model is not in the notice (RNB486GSS), Serial Number 1703602. 

I was a GS14-801 senior Federal Safety and Reliability Engineer for DoD, NRC, and DOE.  The FRACAS system failed here.  Their is gross black oxide on the igniter.  (I left this in situ - does anyone want to document this further, would you want to document the As-Is installation?)  It seems that air currents can be addressed with a cowling or an interlock over to the thermistor, etc..  There is a lot of volume in this oven and this is dangerous. The fryer was also powering on without being prompted and the heating element was on while the fan was not, which could start a fire if left unattended for any length of time. (for instance while one is sleeping) We can't now, without concern, even move away from it unless its unplugged from the outlet. I believe the public should be warned before someone gets seriously hurt, or a serious fire occurs.

incident_description:
Introduction:  Reading in January issue of [REDACTED] an article "How to Complain Well..." reminded me of how when I complained to Fisher & Paykel who made my DCS stove, they referred me to an authorized repair company, Jersey Coast Appliance, whose technicians made several visits to my home to repair a burner on the stove but actually made it worse and then could not repair it properly.  And then, Fisher & Paykel provided an alternate authorized repair company after I complained to them, Jersey Appliance, who ended up repairing it to what they described as the "best that could be done."  I was left with a kind of crippled burner knob.  But at least they stopped the gas leak that was not fixed by the first repair company.  
Details to the best of my memory:   We purchased a DCS Stove RDU 33610, dual fuel, self-clean oven Serial #UPP431281 which was delivered on February 20, 2012 costing $5,475.00.   The first thing I noticed was the very loud noise when the oven is on.   A call to the manufacturer resulted in them telling me it is normal.  It is still loud to this day.  The second thing began in 2016.  The front left burner would not stop clicking when turned on.  A call to the manufacturer resulted in receiving the name of an authorized repair company, Jersey Coast Appliance in Toms River, NJ.  I called them on June 9 and they sent a technician on June 15 to repair it.  He checked the burner and acknowledged the problem, saying it needs a part.  I don't know what he did in examining the burner but after he left we noticed a gas odor.  So we didn't use that burner again and waited 3 months until I called them on September 6 to find out if the part came in.  On September 9 the tech returned and acknowledged gas smell and said it was leaking.  He said it needed a new valve.  By the way, while he was working on my stove, he appeared to not know what he was doing.  He was sweating and sparks were flying out of the burner all over the kitchen!  I called them again on September 30.  They said they couldn't get the valve.  The tech returned on October 5 and tried again to fix it, apparently with a new suddenly materialized valve.  I noticed and complained to the Tech that now the knob was pushed in and not turning smoothly.  The tech wrote that he straightened the valve stem and acknowledged it was still stiff and left it like that.  I called his office to complain speaking with a woman named [REDACTED] who said she would "look at the paperwork and call back on Monday".  On October 7 she called back saying the tech "never touched the knobs" which was not true.  My husband called them back asking to speak with a manager.  Three days later on October 10, and again on October 17 we were told that the service manager would call.    We were fed up. On October 25, we called the manufacturer and spoke with a "[REDACTED]" who gave our information to the Customer Relations Department to complain about their authorized repair company, Jersey Coast.  They said they would call Jersey Coast who never did anything about it.   We then obtained the name of another authorized repair company, Jersey Appliance, Monroe, NJ.  On November 14, 2016 we received a call from their employee, [REDACTED].  We were told that the valve part plus labor would come to $263.58.   (We had already paid $139 to Jersey Coast!!!)    We were also told that he had to call the manufacturer for information on how to fix the stove!  From what I remember I was at some point told that the valve was "obsolete" and that they fixed the stove so that it would not leak gas but nothing could be done to make the knob work smoothly the way it did before and the way the other knobs still do.  One of the people at Jersey Appliance, I believe his name may have been "[REDACTED]",  mentioned something about a "bent or dislocated valve"  and referred to a Valve #210586.  I was told to speak with "[REDACTED]" at the manufacturer.  [REDACTED] said he would get a "consultant" to call me.  Someone named "[REDACTED]" said she would create a Customer Relations "file" and "rectify" the situation.  This went on between the manfacturer and Jersey Appliance for months.  On December 5, 2016 we spoke with "[REDACTED]" at Jersey Appliance who said "[REDACTED]" was busy and could not come to the phone.  [REDACTED] was supposed to call us to tell us how they were going to rectify the problem.   On December 29, we called the manufacturer and spoke with "[REDACTED]" who pulled up the file.  She said she saw "[REDACTED]" notes in the file which indicated [REDACTED] is dealing with Jersey Appliance.  [REDACTED] put me on hold while she talked to "Tech Support" because she didn't know who "[REDACTED]" was!  [REDACTED] then told me that the file was "closed" because no parts were available.  I protested.  [REDACTED] then said she would "email [REDACTED]" to give me a "call back."  [REDACTED] said she marked it "urgent."  On January3, 2017 received message [REDACTED] says "wrong part #".  On January 5, 2017 we tried to call her.  A "[REDACTED]" answered the phone and transferred me to "Fisher & Peykel Customer Relations Team."   A "[REDACTED]" requested proof of purchase  which I emailed to her at the address given me: [REDACTED] with File Ref #[REDACTED] in subject line as requested.   We received a reply email with Case #[REDACTED].  On January 16, 2017 a tech from Jersey Appliance installed a part.  And we paid $308.78.  The knob is no longer pushed in.  But it is still a bit stiff.  There are no leaks.  It is fixed as best as they can do.   this is what we were told and we have been living with it.   The oven remains loud when in use.  The REASON I have written this to you is because [REDACTED] advised me to do so after I commented on their article,"How to Complain Well..."
justification: The incident involved a gas leak and poor repair service, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We installed a Frigidaire 5 burner LP cooktop, model FFGC3626SSE,  in our new home October 23, 2019 and began using the cooktop November 1, 2019.  After a month of use we noticed that the stems of the plastic control knobs were cracking.  Upon further inspection, we noted that all 5 control knobs were cracked to a degree.  The problem became so serious that the metal clip inside the plastic stem was no longer held in place and would spin independently of the knob.  My wife called me at work around January 15, 2020 because she could not get a burner to turn off due to the control knob spinning freely.  The plastic stem held long enough to turn the burner on but failed when my wife attempted to shut the burner down.  Had the knob been turned past the ignition position allowing gas to flow without igniting and then failed, the result could have been an explosion.  As a stopgap, I tightly wound the plastic stems with electrical tape to control the cracking and then called Frigidaire customer service.  Frigidaire agreed to send 5 new control knobs which were the same style as the original.  We received a package of the new burner knobs around January 25, 2020 (the packing label was dated 1/23/20) and began replacing the knobs that were critical.  Within a couple of weeks, the new knobs began to crack as well
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning control knob that could have led to a dangerous situation, but no actual injury or explosion occurred.

incident_description:
GE Side by Side Refrigerator / Freezer, (Model # GSHS6HGDBCSS, and other similar models); has a potential deadly safety issue with the ice maker:

(1) Refrigerator ice bucket cover, crushing housing and dispenser auger plate 
WR17X11497 , and
(2) Refrigerator ice maker auger assembly 
WR17X11939 

are  made of plastic. The plastic can, and does, crack and break; dispersing pieces of sharp, rigid plastic into the glass held under the dispenser. The potentially deadly pieces of clear plastic are not easily distinguishable from the crushed or cubed ice. 

I had several pieces of broken plastic fall into my glass, held under the dispenser. One piece was a couple of inches long; and the other pieces were about a half inch in length. These are  sharp and rigid pieces of plastic that broke loose. 

Even after ordering and replacing the components above; I still found a couple pieces of small sharp pieces of plastic in my glass. Not sure if these additional and subsequent pieces of plastic were left over from the dispensing hole; or if the replacement components broke again.

These pieces of plastic are small enough, rigid enough, and sharp enough that they can lodge in a person's throat or intestines and possibly result in choking or death.

Extremely Dangerous!!!
justification: The description indicates potential for choking or death due to sharp plastic pieces in ice, which is a severe risk.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung 26 CF French Door Refrigerator on February 1, 2015 (Model number: RF263BEAESR, Serial number: JKJ44BBFC00565R). I have since then experienced multiple problems with the appliance that has required service calls and repairs listed below.

The refrigerator required a service call and repair on August 15, 2017 due to standing water under the produce and cool select pantry drawers, as well as the ice maker freezing over. The back panel was removed and found to be frozen over. This visit the temp sensor was replaced. 

Since the 2017 service call, the refrigerator continued to freeze over requiring a manual defrost. The manual defrost was required every 3-4 months to resolve the standing water and frozen ice maker that would continuously return. 

The refrigerator required an additional service call and repair on January 17, 2020. The technique to manually defrost the refrigerator was no longer effective as the refrigerator was now making a loud, churning noise. The serviceman that came to repair the refrigerator stated that the noise was due to the fan blade in the back of the refrigerator making contact with the thick, frozen ice that was built up underneath the back panel. At that time, the fan was no longer able to turn at all due to the increasing thickness and amount of frozen ice under the back panel. The serviceman deemed that the ice maker required replacement. The following parts were replaced on February 1, 2020: Ice Maker Service Kit (DA82-02697A) and Cover Assembly Eval-Ref (DA97-12609C). 

The refrigerator required an additional service call and repair on February 19, 2020. The loud noise from the fan blade, standing water and freezing over of the ice maker had returned. The serviceman cleared the drain in the evaporator.

The refrigerator required an additional service call and repair on March 11, 2020. The loud noise from the fan blade, standing water and freezing over of the ice maker had returned. The serviceman returned a completed a manual defrost. 

I have initiated a new service call as of March 20, 2020 for the same, persistent issues. In addition to the noise, standing water and frozen ice maker, two family members became sick after eating lunch on March 23, 2020 from the refrigerator. I purchased a thermometer to test the temperature inside of the refrigerator and the thermometer has continued to read 54 degrees each day since. 

The service company that has been attending to the refrigerator is no longer able to provide additional service visits as they have deemed the refrigerator status to "beyond repair." 

As this is our sole refrigerator, my family is now challenged with the current COVID-19 pandemic to maintain a stocked refrigerator with food that is safe to eat. This ongoing situation needs to be resolved among Samsung to compensate its consumers who are experiencing ongoing defects with a problematic product. Samsung is aware of this issue and recognizes the problems as "known defects."
justification: Two family members became sick from eating food stored in the malfunctioning refrigerator, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I own a Viking VGIC365-gss range which developed a significant set of gas leaks, even when turned off.  

All of the leaks were in a single aluminum gas line, part PB020039.  which comes directly off the gas manifold, before going to the valves that are opened by the stove knobs for the oven and thus are under gas pressure any time the stove is connected to a gas line.  

The line goes from the top of the range down to the bottom of the oven and is near the front corner of the range, where food can drip into the cavity that houses the aluminum line which is very close to the stainless steel surface of the range.  The humidity in a kitchen and or food drippings into the cavity can aggravate galvanic corrosion or regular corrosion causing pinholes in that gas line.  The aluminum line was perforated in multiple places from corrosion.

The part number has been changed to a stainless steel line, part PB020217, I am guessing I was not the only one that ran into this issue, but given that its a gas appliance with open flame a recall would seem prudent. 

I did cal I did call Viking to to replace the line and report the safety issue.

I can provide the faulty part or pictures of the part directly to you.  I will not be reinstalling it.....
justification: Gas leaks from corrosion in the aluminum line pose a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported in this incident.

incident_description:
On Thursday, March 12, 2020 around 10am, I started the "Normal" cycle wash with the "Heated Air Dry" cycle option on our Maytag dishwasher. After about 45-60 minutes, my children and I suddenly heard a loud "clicking" sound coming from the appliance. From our kitchen table, we turned to see a huge plume of white-ish smoke coming from our dishwasher, in the middle of the kitchen island. The clicking sound continued and I ran over to the dishwasher and opened the dishwasher door. A very large amount of smoke came billowing out from the vent on top of the dishwasher door and smoke from all around the sides of the dishwasher door. The clicking sound continued and so I immediately pushed "cancel" on the unit. The sound and smoke continued. I ran into our garage and flipped off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher and all island outlets. I ran back inside and our entire kitchen area was full of smoke that smelled like an electrical fire. The clicking sound continued for another minute or so and the smoke also continued to billow. After a minute or so, it stopped and the smoke continued for another few minutes. The entire unit smelled so strongly of electrical fire, we kept trying to fan the air and smoke outside.

At 11:30am or so, I contacted Maytag and opened a case number with their Safety Department. They took our information and requested that a company ([REDACTED]) come out on Tuesday, March 17th to complete a diagnostic of the dishwasher to determine what exactly took place.

On Tuesday, March 17th a technician from [REDACTED] came to our home and inspected the dishwasher. The technician immediately commented on the burnt electrical smell, despite the dishwasher being moved into our garage back on March 12th due to the smell. He opened the dishwasher door and discovered the entire circuit board was burnt and clearly had been on fire. He stated that he had no idea why the unit had started on fire and he took two photographs of the unit. He said that it would cost almost as much as a new dishwasher to make a repair and he did not see any point in attempting to do so, given the terrible smell and condition of the dishwasher.

On Friday, March 20th I called the Safety Department at Maytag, in order to follow up with the status of our dishwasher. I was informed that Maytag has no obligation to repair or replace the item and it is not currently involved in any recalls. Because our dishwasher is past the warranty date (one year), Maytag does not need to provide any replacement or compensation of any kind. I was told that Maytag would offer us a depreciated value of the item ($339) or 40% off the MSRP of a new Maytag brand dishwasher, out of their own "good will."

This is extremely concerning as our Maytag dishwasher started on fire on it's own, without any known cause. We traditionally start the dishwasher at night, before going off to bed, which would have resulted in most likely a catastrophic house fire. We sleep on the top floor of our home, with two adults and four children. I am terrified to think that this incident is not alarming for the Maytag Corporation and a similar incident may occur in another home at any time.

Clicking continued and smoke pouring out of vent and around dishwasher door. Ran and turned off circuit breaker. Came in and clicking continued for a bit, then stopped. TONS of smoke.11:30am - called Maytag and opened case number. Technician scheduled to come out on Tuesday, 3/17 between 8am-12pm.

incident_description: A plastic wheel on the bottom rack of the dishwasher popped off and rolled inside next to the heating element. I didn't know it had popped off until I smelled a burning smell and the kitchen filled with smoke. I opened the dishwasher to find thick smoke and the wheel burning.

incident_description: KitchenAid Oven's roll-out rack rolls out when the oven door is opened.  When reaching for one of the other racks, the roll-out rack comes in contact with the the user causing arm burns.

incident_description:
Our Samsung refrigerator has had issues from the beginning. The ice maker freezers, the cooling system then freezes. This causes the temperature inside to rise. The display panel does not show the correct internal temperature of the unit. Over the weekend my daughterÃÂs stomach began to bother her. I realized the yogurt she had eaten was beginning to spoil from the temperature in the refrigerator rising to 50F. We have had over $550 worth of food spoil in the last week and half in this refrigerator. Samsung promised a repair which has been a no-show since their scheduled appointment on Saturday 2/8/2020. I also lost nearly 100 oz of breastmilk I had worked hard to pump for my infant. 
Concerns-
*Faulty product a fire risk.
*Ice maker does not work and water drips out of the dispenser door constantly, causing mold and moisture issues to surrounding surfaces such as flooring and walls. 
*Requires frequent defrosting. 
*Control panel does not show correct internal temperature, causing food borne illness and food spoilage. 
 This can be dangerous for anyone who has to store medication in the fridge, breastmilk, formula, and food borne illness.
justification: The incident caused food spoilage and a stomach issue due to spoiled yogurt, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurring issues with the refrigerator suggest the likelihood of recurrence is high (4).

incident_description:

When the consumer checked his kitchen, he noticed that his toaster turned on by itself overnight and it was so hot that he was unable to turn it off by its ON/ OFF button. The consumer unplugged the unit from the wall, and discontinued its use.

The consumer plans on keeping his toaster for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

incident_description:
Samsung Refrigerator: RF4287HARS

1. Does not hold or display proper temperature
2. Ice Maker freezes over
3. Food is spoiling due to temperature issues
4. Metal soda cans explode sending metal shards everywhere due to temperature misalignment in drink drawer

incident_description: The electronic panel on my Maytag MDB8949SBB3 dishwasher ignited yesterday. It started smoking and smelled strongly of an electric burn. Upon dismantling the panel, I found that the wires had burned. The unit is no more than 6 years old and the panel on it has already been replaced so the panel itself is even newer than the unit. Thankfully I was home at the time and was able to turn off the power at the breaker before any further damage was done.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire hazard but no injury occurred as the power was promptly turned off.

incident_description: Bought a Samsung refrigerator in 2016. Within the first year we had Samsung repair our frozen over ice maker under the one year warranty. Then over the next two and a half years we were forced to defrost our fridge ourselves because the ice maker was frozen solid and the back of the fridge was making a horrible noise with a strange burning smell. Upon investigating the horrible noise, we removed the back panel and found the fan was hitting a huge chunk of ice that had formed under the panel. If we didn't do this our home could have caught on fire! There was mold and dripping water coming from the screw holes. We had to remove everything from the unit defrost it and wash with bleach four times in that two in a half year time period. Finally, we bought a digital thermometer to monitor the interior refrigerator temperature. Even though the reading on the outside display of the fridge registered 37 degrees the interior temps ranged from 46-50 degrees. No wonder why I had so much food spoilage! But the most dangerous thing was how my husband's health was being compromised. He has had 5 surgeries over the last year because of an ongoing infection. When he came home after each surgery he was on IV antibiotics that needed to be stored at 36-40 degrees. They were not, and we didn't know that. I was furious that Samsung could be responsible for multiple surgeries and a possible leg amputation due to improper temperature storage of his antibiotic. I called Samsung to correct the issue and they said it was not under warranty. I explained my situation, and they did not care. I filed with the BBB and after another run around with Samsung they finally agreed to a courtesy one time repair, after two weeks we had slushy ice and improper interior temperatures. Called Samsung back and received a full refund and some food loss reimbursement. I know there are thousands of other consumers affected buy this life threatening dysfunctional refrigerator. Life threatening because there have been fires reported also. I am aware of a second class action law suit, that we all know is useless. Samsung has deep pockets, they don't care about their consumers health and safety, they wont to issue a recall. I see you have received many complaints about this very issue. The CPSC needs to do the right thing, PROTECT THE CONSUMERS.
justification: The incident caused injury (multiple surgeries due to infection) and had potential for severe harm (fire risk, improper medication storage). The issue appears widespread based on the description.

incident_description: While preparing something in the oven, one side of the handle fell off.  When my husband went to try and put the handle back on, the glass of the oven door shattered all over the place.  Thankfully he was wearing shoes and didn't sustain any injuries.  It very well could have caused injury if a small child was standing there or even my small dog.
justification: The incident involved the oven handle falling off and glass shattering, but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents can happen with faulty appliances.

incident_description: I was cooking on my glass stove top starting off at 3/4 heat on.  Once it got hot enough I turn it down, I know I went to turn it down again because it was still cooking and not on simmer.  It was close to no heat and before I knew it my food was burnt, the element was red hot.  I had guests down and if we were not right there to stop it I hate to think of what could of happened.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Advocate:

I recently purchased a house with this gas range installed and inspected by home inspector
(passed.} I called Frigidaire to report a safety concern and the woman I spoke listened to what I
explained was occurring and said it works as intended/designed. I asked her if there were any
known safety issues and/or recalls, she put me on hold to check, came back and said there
wasn't any record of any issues.

Since living in the home the last several months, we have come home about 6 different times to
a strong gas smell, as a burner had (unknowingly} been on all day. If you ever so lightly (and
unknowingly) brush against one of the burner knobs {that stick out about 2 1/4") the burner will be
on. You do not hear any clicking sound, there is no light indicating a burner is on, you don't even
have to push the knob in to engage the burner. There is absolutely nothing to indicate a burner is
on. We are in the habit of inspecting to make sure the line on the burner is straight up (the off
position) but even if it is ever so slightly not straight up, the burner is engaged filling the house
with gas all day long. I work full time and have a 1.5" commute, so that gives it about 10 hours to
be filling the air with gas. The last time, I was so freaked out that I called our energy provider,
Xcel, for help, but since I wasn't home at the time, the only thing they could do was shut off the
gas line from the outside of the home. I cannot tell you how much stress this has created for me.
Thank God the Xcel Energy tech that came out to the house to turn the gas back on, performed
an inspection inside and outside to make sure there were no other leaks. There were not. He told
me about the hazards of this particular gas range model and suggested that I buy safety knobs to
go over each burner switch (which we did.) Thank God we are not smokers-this could have been
fatal.

When I called your office to ask if there had been a recall or any complaints, I was told there
wasn't anything on file. This was rather shocking to me. I implore you to check out this gas range
model. I cannot believe that no light indicator, no sound, nothing of any kind to alert you that a
gas burner is engaged and on is not a safety concern. Please consider this as an official complaint.
J would hope that it would justify further investigation from your agency. If there is another
avenue I need to take to accomplish this, please advise. Thank you.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with a gas range that could lead to gas leaks, but no actual injury or death has occurred. The occurrence is likely as it has happened multiple times.

incident_description:
"I received the Ninja Foodie for my birthday on April 26, 2019. The item was purchased by my husband, [REDACTED] at
Target for the special birthday. On May 6, 2019, I used the Ninja Foodi 301, Model# OP301 107 (6.5 quart, serial number A 11JJ202Z4K3) to prepare a beef stew for dinner, when the unit exploded and sprayed the hot contents all
over my abdomen, causing second degree burns over most of my abdomen. Per the instruction manual, I ptaced
the ingredients in the pot, secured the pressure cooking lid to lock, and turned the steam valve to the "seal" position. I turned on the pressure cooking option and watched as the unit displayed the loading screen indicating the cooker was building pressure and heat. Steam started to escape the machine, yet everything was in the locked and sealed position. Concerned, I turned the valve to vent to release all of the pressure and steam from the machine. After the steam stopped coming out, I powered off the machine by selecting the power button and unplugged the machine. r then went to retrieve the owner's manual. While standing in front of the machine reading the owner's manual, the lid exploded off like a bomb sending hot liquid all over my abdomen and kitchen. By pure dumb luck, my children were not in the kitchen at the time of the explosion and were not harmed. This item had been used successfully three times prior this incident. I have been left with permanent heat sensitivity and scarring all over lower abdomen."
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns and permanent scarring, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) because the product had been used successfully three times prior to the incident, indicating such failures are not common.

incident_description: On 2/19, I was using a Dash air fryer produced by storebound. Shortly after turning it on, it began putting off a strong burning odor similar to what would be expected of an electrical fire. Upon noticing the odor, my husband and I also heard a loud popping sound. We immediately unplugged the air fryer, but unfortunately it heated up to such an extent that my husbandÃÂs hand was burnt unplugging it, and the fryer cracked our 2 year old quartz countertops, causing $2,200 worth of damage. I was also able to locate two other consumers via product reviews who had similar issues with cracked countertops. [REDACTED] quartz countertops were cracked due to the air fryer over heating, and [REDACTED] countertops were cracked by the product.  I spoke with [REDACTED] at Dash about the issues, but unfortunately he dismissed the damage left by this product, claiming that the company had never heard of a similar issue with this product. This claim, however, was completely false as both [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] referenced speaking to corporate and having their concerns similarly dismissed. [REDACTED] from storebound (Dash) claimed that it was impossible for the base of the unit to have heated up to such an extent due to the fact that the heating element is located in the upper half of the appliance. While this may be true, the electrical components are located in the base of the air fryer. Upon unplugging the unit, my husband burnt his hand on the base of the fryer moving it, and the countertops were extremely hot. Based on these facts, in conjunction with the odor similar to what would be associated with an electrical fire, I assume that these units are prone to faulty wiring or some form of failure of the electrical components which are housed in the base of the air fryer. I have kept the product for reference and would be happy to submit it to the CPSC for further inspection. I believe this product to be dangerous. Not only did it cause costly property damage to our home, it is also a potential fire hazard and is capable of causing severe bodily harm due to the extensive heat that is produced upon malfunction.  I am also extremely disappointed that Dash cares so little about the well being of their customers that they would choose to lie about the safety of their products rather than investigating and resolving the apparent electrical malfunctions inherent to these appliances that are capable of causing extensive damage and bodily harm.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burn) and significant property damage, with multiple similar reports indicating a pattern.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dishwasher was in use for about 45 mins when it started to emit smoke from the control panel.  She stated that she powered off the unit, her spouse screwed the door panel off and switched off the circuit breaker to contain the fire.  The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that a service technician would be sent out.  

2/27 The technician came out and informed that the electrical wiring had been severely burnt.  He stated that there was an estimated repair cost of $500.  However, it was not guaranteed that this would solved the problem.

Caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.

incident_description:
We had a small electrical fire in the kitchen which turned out to be due to our Amana (Whirlpool) range being sold without a protective panel which would have housed electrical contacts.  One of the erroneously exposed electrical contacts at the bottom/rear of the range apparently came into contact with the back of the plug while it was plugged into the wall.  The heat from the resulting energy transfer melted part of the rubber plug housing, caused a wire to completely sever and melted some of the nearby parts and a pile of ash was produced. Luckily no injuries or further damage.

I went to a home improvement store to get parts and, while there, looked at some similar Amana ranges.  All of the ranges in the store had protective panels protecting the electrical contacts which ours did not.  I called Whirlpool for the part and they quoted a price but I reminded them that the part was never included and should have been, they agreed to ship the panel.
justification: The incident involved a small electrical fire with no injuries or further damage, and the issue was identified as a missing protective panel which is not a common occurrence.

incident_description:

The consumer's mother-in-law was in the kitchen and when she attempted to open the ovenÃÂs door, it make an unusual sound.  The mother backed up a few steps, while the oven door was opened and the exterior glass that covered the entire outer door, shattered.  Pieces of glass were still connected to the edges of the oven door.  The inner glass remained intact.  The mother did not sustain any injuries.

The oven was barely used, except to warm food.  The glass was tempered and the pieces of glass were not jagged or sharp.

incident_description: I have a newer Frigidaire Gallery smooth top oven. Had a wire on the control board burn clear off. Melted part of the control board. Ordered a new harness and control board and seemed to have fixed it. Now my shelves are falling off the slides in the oven. Not safe to have shelves with food on them falling into the bottom of your oven.

justification: The description mentions the potential for burns from the hot rack, which constitutes an injury, and the issue is described as happening easily, making it likely.

incident_description: Built a new home in 2008, Frigidaire Appl. installed. December1st 2019, oveb over heated due to a failed sensor. Oven over heated and caught my cabinet on fire. Called Frigidaire and was told to get a appliance repair company to service it.Which I did and was told that the sensor had failed . Called my warranty company and they sent out another service repair company. Was told that the sensor had failed causing over heating and caused the fire. Called Electrolux and was told that I would have to have one of their appliance repair (Frigidaire) to inspect and verify that the fire  was caused by the failed sensor. He pulled the oven (built in) and verified and took pictures of the fire damage. Was told that even though it was out of warranty , due to the faulty sensor, they would cover the damages. Was told today 2-25-2020, that they are not responsibility because it is out of warranty, it is my responsibility. Frigidaire (Electrolux) Mod. # PLEB3059FCD  Ser. # NF83011550 . Seems they were using the same sensors on other models, didn't include the other model numbers. So, who is responsible for this, my house could have burned down. But they refuse to take responsibility for using a faulty part. I have been given nothing but the run around try to get this resolved.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a failed sensor, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Used air fryer as directed to cook chicken wings. Upon removing the basket assembly, the pan unexpectedly detached. As the pan detached, and fell, tumbling, and splashed extremely hot grease onto my leg.
I suffered several burns on my left leg.
While these burns are painful, the are not an emergency.  However, I can easily imagine a situation where the same might happen while a small child is nearby, causing serious injury.
justification: The incident resulted in burns (injury), and the description suggests a plausible scenario where this could easily happen again, especially with children nearby.

She stated that there was a piece of glass growing that dispersed from the stem causing laceration to her throat.  She stated that her throat became severely swollen, she could hardly speak .

She stated that her throat was still hurting so she visited her ENT doctor the following day and was diagnosed of throat abrasion.

incident_description:
Samsung Consumer Products 									February 18, 2020
Address: Unknown, sent via Samsung website complaint	

Dear Sirs:
My wife and I purchased a new Samsung Electric Slide-In Range in October 2019.  It has worked fine, but we immediately noticed two (2) problems with this Range (Model No. NE58K9430SS/AA).
1.	The timer alarm is very soft. Unless you are standing very close to the oven you cannot hear the alarm.  If you are in the next room, you will not hear it.
2.	The front mounted knobs are VERY easy to accidentally turn on without knowing.  This has happened to us several times while cleaning up or moving from side-to-side looking for something in the overhead cabinets above or along side of the stove.  Luckily, since we are aware of the problem we watch.  However, we had an incident on February 3, 2020 that was nearly a catastrophic event.
 On February 3, 2020 we had a contractor in our home making revisions to our kitchen overhead lighting.  We had covered the stove top with a heavy towel to protect it from falling debris and paint.  It was about 4:30 PM and my wife and I were leaving for an appointment, leaving the contractor in the house with instructions to lock up when they were done.  Apparently someone bumped the leftmost knob (controls Left Rear Burner), and because the stove top was covered, the red glow of the burner was not visible.  A few minutes later the contractor noticed an odor and noticed the towel was smoking and immediately removed the towel and threw it in the sink and turned on the water.  We were lucky someone was in the house to notice the smoke and extinguish the fire.  Attached is a photo of the burnt towel.
In the aftermath, the burner had a heavy residue on it from the burnt towel material.  I have been able to remove the majority of the residue, but not all.  However the glass top is visibly dulled/scratched where I had rubbed to remove the burnt on residue.  So now I have a NEW range/stove with a scratched top because of your poor design.
THIS IS A SAFETY ISSUE!  I am sending a copy of this complaint to the ÃÂUnited States Consumer Product Safety CommissionÃÂ.  Only quick thinking by my Contractor avoided a potentially catastrophic fire event.
I would appreciate a response to this complaint.
justification: The incident involved a near-catastrophic fire due to accidental activation of the stove, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Yesterday evening I ran the self cleaning cycle on the upper oven of our LG Gas Double Oven, Model LDG3035ST.   This morning when I went into the kitchen I cut my foot when I stepped upon a piece of glass by the oven.  When I looked at the oven door I saw that part of the glass panel in the oven door had cracked into small fragments, a few of which were on the floor.  The door, and thus the oven, was now useless until a replacement door could be installed.  I contacted LG.  I was told that it was possible that LG would replace or repair the door as an out-of-warranty courtesy.  I am waiting to hear back from them.  This oven was purchased in late 2014, and this was approximately the third time I had run the self cleaning cycle.

The self cleaning cycle is a feature of this oven.  The fact that it destroyed my oven in the process of cleaning itself is distressing and, I believe, an indication of a manufacturing or an engineering problem.  All I had to do to initiate the process was remove the oven racks, which I did, and press the button to start the cycle.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut foot from broken glass, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is considered possible (3) as it happened during a standard cleaning cycle but is not a frequent event.

incident_description:
My husband and I have a Bosch dishwasher, that suddenly stopped working. We contacted Bosch customer service, who gave us the name of a Bosch approved service provider in our area ([REDACTED]) and we had that provider out. After looking at the dishwasher, [REDACTED] determined it was a faulty cord, and advised us this is an active recall issue in our exact dishwasher model. The cord was completely charred - THIS COULD HAVE STARTED A FIRE IN OUR HOME, AND IN FACT, OTHER MODELS WITH THIS ISSUE HAVE STARTED FIRES, HENCE THE RECALL. While the [REDACTED] service provider was still at our home, my husband and [REDACTED] again called the Bosch customer service, and they advised us our model's serial number was outside of the recall, but we can still submit a claim if we provide purchase and service receipts. They emailed my husband with a list of items needed for such a claim and all such items were submitted. THIS EMAIL DOES NOT SAY PHOTOS OF THE DISHWASHER OR SERVICE ARE REQUIRED, NOR DID [REDACTED], THE BOSCH APPROVED SERVICE PROVIDER, KNOW ANYTHING ABOUT TAKING PHOTOS. I have this email and can provide it. As such, no photos were taken at the time of service. About a week later, we then received a call from Bosch customer service that we needed pictures of the cord prior to the service being done for this to be covered. Of course at this time, it was too late to get such photos, and their customer service denied our claim. This repair was half the
cost of a new dishwasher. When asked, the customer service department would not even provide a written explanation of why our claim was denied, or even just a written statement that our claim was denied. Their recall has already been expanded once, and I believe it needs to be expanded again given our issue. This dishwasher could have killed me and my family, and Bosch is not even going to cover the cost of this repair. I'm so upset that this is happening, and
even more upset to know that if this happened to us, there are other families that also likely have this issue and their homes could start on fire at any time due to this faulty cord from Bosch. - [REDACTED]
justification: The faulty cord could have started a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred, making the severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the recall and similar incidents reported.

incident_description:

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him that they are aware of the problem thus suggested he send the unit back for repair for US67$ out of pocket.

The consumer states that the toaster oven is used once or twice daily.

The consumer plans on keeping his unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The toaster oven turns on by itself and won't shut off unless unplugged, posing a potential hazard but no injury has occurred.

incident_description:
On Thursday, November 28, 2019, the Anchor Hocking glass baking dish I was using exploded and shattered sending glass flying further into my oven and all over my kitchen. The blast sent shards of glass into my face and all over the oven and kitchen floor. My oven was destroyed. I was baking sweet potatoes in the oven. I followed the recipe. It called for cubing the potatoes and baking them in a glass dish in a 400 degree oven, turning them a few times over the course of an hour. When I opened the oven for the second turning (with a wooden spoon), the glass baking dish spontaneously shattered and exploded. Glass shards were sent everywhere, including deeper within the oven, my kitchen, my wood floor, my kitchen mat. The heat of the blast hit my face and I fell back. I was not hurt, but was very upset and shocked. Glass fragments were everywhere. My oven was destroyed, glass melted into my floor, penetrated my oven mitts and slippers, and ruined a kitchen mat. My sweet potatoes were also ruined, so we did not have them at Thanksgiving. The Anchor Hocking Glass Baking dish was only 2 years old and it was the second time I had used it. It was clear glass, oblong, 3 qt capacity, 13 in by 9 in.  There were no scratches or chips in the glass. It exploded spontaneously and without cause. 
I called Anchor Hocking to report the accident caused by the exploding glass baking dish on Monday, December 2, 2019. Anchor Hocking took down all my information and said they would get back to me in a day or 2. They never did. I called again on December 11, 2019 and December 16, 2019. I kept getting the run around.  On December 19, 2019, I received and email from Anchor Hocking that my claim for a replacement oven was turned over to [REDACTED].  On January 2, 2020 an inspector from [REDACTED] came over to inspect the damage, collect the glass shards, take photos.  On February 17, 2020, I received an email that my claim has been denied because Anchor Hocking/[REDACTED] found that the glass baking dish was NOT defective. incident_description:
In October 2012, I purchased a Samsung refrigerator, this was to replace a [REDACTED] one I had. The model #RF4287HARS. It was manufactured in March 2011. From the beginning, I was having issues with the ice maker. I called Sears out to check it out. The repairman told me I needed a new ice maker & it would cost around $600.
