It also started leaking into the dispenser of the door, meaning that when you went to get ice from the door & hit the button to get ice, water would come out first. Water also started leaking down into the bottom of the freezer at the bottom of the whole unit, creating the freezer door to stick, having to defrost it when it's a no defrost unit. Since I have not been able to afford a new refrigerator, I have just been living with it, not knowing there has been issues with this product with other people, lots of other people. 
On Thursday, January 16,2020, the ice maker was just pouring out water from the ice maker, I pulled the box that ice would be in out & found the ice maker burning hot & smoking. It was a blessing that I was home that day, if I had not been, I can only imagine that the unit would have caught on fire & destroyed my house & possibly killing my pets as well as this was what would have been the middle of my work day.

incident_description:
3 problems:

1)While using both the oven and burner for several hours cooking a holiday dinner, the knob for the burner became stuck.  Had to forcefully turn knob to get it to shut off, required pliers.  Contacted manufacturer with safety/warranty concern and after several emails back and forth they stopped responding to me and never resolved.  Has happened several times after unit is used for 2-3 hrs.  this happened within warranty, range was 6 month in use, no resolution or acknowledgment from manufacturer.

2)The broiler stopped staying lit, would slowly leak gas into the oven, which would ignite into a fireball when the door was opened.  Repair technician explained the igniter was failing, which skewed the voltage used by the gas valve.  The igniter still glowed, and gas would still flow, but not enough to keep the burner lit.  this began to happen once unit had been in service for 2 years, just out of warranty.

3)  Meanwhile, the sound of the oven burner igniting got louder and louder until it became a thumping whoosh, a large quantity of gas igniting almost a like small explosion. While baking, a very loud buzzing noise came from nowhere and the lights in the oven dimmed.  Obviously something wrong, happened to be standing there luckily and immediately shut down the oven.  Oven would no longer operate, closer inspection revealed the igniter and burner to be severely degraded and melted.  the buzzing noise seems to be from arcing electricity, the steel around the igniter has been melted by a very high temperature, and the igniter was effectively welded to the burner. I can only guess... but it appears that the igniter gradually melted a hole in the burner tube over time, which caused excess flame from the burner on the igniter, which in turn caused the igniter coil to corrode.  When the element failed, it had an electrical arc which melted everything and made the loud buzzing.  I am only reverse engineering what I think happened, but obviously there was some sort of fault that seems to me easily could have resulted in a fire or explosion.  Did not trip the 20 amp breaker.  Note: the incident date provided is for this most recent problem.
justification: The incidents describe multiple safety hazards with the oven, including gas leaks and potential fire risks, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

Range, first floor, leak at appliance, oven passing gas with control in off position, meter on, tape not applied." Abt

incident_description:
Dear Madams & Sirs from the Safer Products Commission,

Below you will find an email that I sent today to Frigidaire's customer support service, with a summary of my experience with one of their products.
-----------------------------------------------

Hello,

This email serves as notice for Frigidaire that I will be passing my experience with your appliance and your customer services to KYÃÂs State Attorney General, the Consumer Product Safety Commission and the Better Business Bureau. A copy of this email will be sent to those parties, along with my recorded calls with your customer service.  

On December 2nd 2019, I reached out to Frigidaire to report a fire hazard with one of your Microwave units :

Frigidaire Gallery
Model # FGMV175QFA
Serial # KG64111695

Earlier that day, my wife had loaded a bag of popcorn in the microwave, and after a few seconds, sparks started flying inside, and small yet violent fire started raging inside the microwave. Thank goodness we were standing right there, and we were able to put the fire out.

I explained the situation to your customer service rep and they assured me that theyÃÂd have a ÃÂspecialistÃÂ take a look. I made my request very clear, that my primary concern was NOT to have this unit repaired or replaced, my main concern was to have Frigidaire show interest in the safety of their products by conducting an investigation and identifying the root cause. 

Frigidaire proceeded to send an appliance repair person with the order to ÃÂSand and paint the unitÃÂ. 
I explained to the technician that thatÃÂs not what I was trying to achieve and I refused the repair. One of Frigidaires technicians on the phone mentioned that this was due to ÃÂUser negligence, since in Page 12 of the manual itÃÂs stated clearly that you should not operate the microwave with the mounted metal grateÃÂ ÃÂ This is a totally false statement. After carefully reading your manual (which I had done before operating the microwave, since it came with the house we had just moved into, and I thought It was unusual for a metal grate to be inside the microwave. ThereÃÂs only a few references in the manual with recommendations on how to store the grate, but there is no mention in the manual to not operate the microwave with the grate mounted) .

I followed that visit with another call to your repair center, I was given a different case number. One of your agents [REDACTED] ensured me that sheÃÂd do her best to escalate my issue. 
A few days ago, she called me back, ensuring me that theyÃÂd arrange for a ÃÂtrue specialistÃÂ to come investigate the issue 

This morning at around 10:00am, a tech [REDACTED] from the company [REDACTED] came to our house with the instructions to assess the repair of our unit. He spent about an hour on the phone with FrigidaireÃÂs tech support, doing his best to convey to your Techs that our intent was for them to investigate. He was told by Frigidaire that the only action that theyÃÂd approve would be to ÃÂSand and paintÃÂ. 

I have also attempted several times to create a ticket on FrigidaireÃÂs website (https://www.frigidaire.com/Owner-Center/Contact-Us/) neither the chat nor the ÃÂemail formsÃÂ are working properly (I tried 3 different computers, 4 different web browsers). 
[REDACTED] was extremely patient and helpful. And his ÃÂunofficialÃÂ assessment of the root cause coincides with my suspicions ÃÂ this is based on a rather rudimentary understanding of physics and electronics. But the cause seems to be a combination of material fatigue of both, the mounts for the grates and the paint at the back of the grates. The grate seems to cause wear on the paint, exposing the metal, then under certain conditions, the arcs can reach the plastic mounts, which get heated up, causing a fire inside. 

As a father of a family with two small children, it is hard for me to believe that a company like Frigidaire has shown absolutely no concern in the safety of their products, despite several attempts from my part to make them aware of this. 
I have lost my confidence in FrigidaireÃÂs customer service and so I will now search for other means to accomplish my goals.

[REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the microwave, which could have led to injury, but no actual injury was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as it requires specific conditions to occur.

incident_description:
The range was used in the kitchen as our method of cooking.  Two separate incidences occurred during the first three weeks after we installed it.  The first time, simply passing by too close to the front mounted left most burner control knobs caused it to turn on.  This resulted in something left on the stove top to catch fire.  Thankfully, one of us was home and extinguished the fire.  

The second incident was similar in that this time is was the right most burner knob that was turned on by brushing against the front of the stove as a result of incidental contact brushing by the stove as I walked by.  This time the burner again came on, but nothing caught fire because the stove top was bare.  

I have since spent $135 to buy replacement safety knobs (interesting that they were readily available for this make and model on line),  This is clear indication that others are having the same issue.

I contacted Fridgidaire and was told that there was no problems with this oven related to incidental burner turn on and they refused to pay me for the new safety knobs.
justification: The incidents resulted in a fire but no injuries, and the issue occurred twice in three weeks with readily available safety knobs indicating a known problem.

incident_description: placed a small bowl with 1-2 tablespoons of butter in microwave to soften, after 5 sec the panel on lower right hand (composite) was on fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injury was reported, making it a minor incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description: Several similar Whirlpool refrigerator models have a defect that causes electrical wires to become severed, causing a fire hazard and preventing the refrigerator from working properly. There are two of these products in our home and both are exhibiting the same issue. The wire bundle connected to the freezer door rubs on a sharp edge each time the freezer door is opened, eventually exposing the wires and cutting them. Our refrigerators were manufactured in August and November of 2017 and the newer one is worse. Another consumer documented the same issue at [REDACTED] and five other consumers found that report useful (i.e., had the same problem). In our case, when the wires were severed, the ice maker stopped working. I called the Whirlpool Customer eXperience (sic) center at 800-253-1301 on 1/6/2020 to identify the hazard and they offered to send a repair technician out at my expense to give me a price quote to fix it. I realize that the refrigerator only had a 1 year warranty, but I'm worried that other consumers think the issue is minor and "just live with" the inconvenience of not having a working ice maker on a $1,300 refrigerator. While these are relatively small wires, they are in close proximity to the highly flammable "dust bunnies" that commonly live under most refrigerators.
justification: The defect poses a fire hazard due to exposed wires near flammable materials, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
Oven was installed 8/20/13. We purchased house in 2017. In February 2019, heated up oven. Opened oven door to put in product, slowly closed oven door, outer glass on door shattered. New oven glass Kenmore OEM part was then installed. February 2020 heated oven up and again went to put in product and slowly closed door and again oven door glass shattered. Pieces go everywhere. Very dangerous and thankful no children or pets were present. Also, very damaging to hardwood floor each time. Found several similar cases with same oven model 790. 
Contacted kenmore and was told there is no recall and is no longer under the one year warranty. Transferred to 7 different departments with one that did not even realize kenmore and sears are one in the same. They told us we would have to contact Kenmore. Nobody at Kenmore/Sears seems to think this is an issue of concern. They want to send a repair call at owners expense to replace the glass again. Very fortunate that we did not sustain serious injury.  At this point I would never ever purchase another Kenmore product. Satisfaction and cook at this time are laid off.
justification: The incident involved shattered oven glass causing potential injury, though none occurred, and similar cases have been reported.

incident_description: My GE glass cook top exploded and shatter while cooking dinner on 1/20/20 leaving a one inch hole and a Y formation cracking over 3 of the elements and uneven jagged edges from the crack. I reported the incident immediately to GE as it was still within warranty. They were hesitant in honoring my warranty but changed their minds when I threatened to report them to Consumer Affairs.
justification: The cooktop exploded and shattered, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the oven that was installed in the home a few years before she purchased the home is having problems.
The cleaning cycle was ran at the shortest recommended time of 2 hours and she discovered that after it was completed that the while she was wiping the interior, the porcelain finish was cracked and it had formed needle shaped glass falling from the top of the unit.  She is concerned that this can fall into food content while using the oven.

(12/23) The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that because she was not the original owner and they are unaware of how the unit was treated before she got it, they were unable to assist her.

Caller feels that this oven is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves a cracked oven finish with potential for glass to fall into food, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: This is in regards to the Bosch Dishwasher recall in late 2017 concerning the chance of fire due to the power box/cord.  Our dishwasher is a Bosch SHP65T55UC/02 Ser. # FD931003437.  This unit was covered by the recall and subsequently retrofitted with the recall kit by the Bosch approved appliance repair company in our area, [REDACTED], Joliet, IL 60431.  On this past Monday, Jan 6, the dishwasher just stopped working with the appearance of no power.  Called out our preferred appliance repair company who diagnosed the problem as a defective power module.  He returned yesterday with the part and replaced it.  Upon further inspection and now looking at the power box (subject of previous recall) was shocked at the burning and scorching of the box and wires.  He stated that in all likelihood this blew out the power module and saved us from an all out fire.  The circuit breaker did not trip since this was a slow overload.  Bosch was contacted and offered to send out a new power box but declined to pay for the damaged circuit board, a not insubstantial about (~$430 w/ installation). I have pictures detailing the damage. It seems the recall did nothing and the problem still exists  What guarantee do we have that this will not occur again?
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the power box and wires, posing a fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: A Pioneer Woman wooden handled food whisk has a nail in the handle which can and did fall out in the food bowl, which I then ate and chipped a tooth. This nail could potentially get lodged in the throat, paler, stomach or intestines.
justification: The incident resulted in a chipped tooth (injury), and the description notes potential for more severe harm, though not certain.

incident_description:
(02/01/2020) The oven had been in use for about 30 minutes. The consumer saw smoke coming from the back of the control panel. The consumer unplugged the unit, removed the panel and saw several parts that were burnt black.

One of the heating elements was replaced about  1and 1/2 years ago.
justification: Smoke and burnt parts indicate an incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Running the dishwasher as usual, started to smell plastic burning, saw smoke at dishwasher and we shut it down immediately. Checked the heating element to see if there was any obstructions. Found none, restarted and noticed smoke seeping from the control panel, it is now shutoff and disconnected.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was promptly addressed.

incident_description: I was cooking vegetables in a stainless steel sauce pan until I realized the cookware had boiled dry. When I lifted the pot, the aluminum base fell off and landed in the floor, and liquid metal poured out. I was cooking in socks, but not shoes. The molten aluminum landed on the tile floor and splashed on the side of my foot. The side of my left foot is burned. I pulled my sock off as quickly as I could to get the liquid metal away from my skin. There are black fibers from my sock stuck on the burns. I'm going to the doctor in the morning. The pot says Betty Crocker on it.
justification: The incident resulted in burns requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such incidents are unlikely (likelihood 2) given proper cooking practices.

incident_description:
On December 4, 2019 I used for the first time the self cleaning oven. I followed the instructions on page 56 and 57 of the manual. The default setting is 3 hours which I used. The doors and front drawers of kitchen cabinet on each side of the range were damaged by the heat coming out of the oven during the cycle.

I called the manufacturer they sent a technician from DISH Samsung authorized service provider on December 7, 2019. He told us that the default 3 hours is too long.  He recommends to all his clients not to exceed 90 minutes because the oven reach 700 degrees Fahrenheit. In the manual nothing is mentioned about 90 minutes. But according to page 14 it says DO NOT TURN THE APPLIANCE OFF WHILE AN OPERATION IS IN PROGRESS. THIS MAY CAUSE A SPARK AND RESULT IN ELECTRIC SHOCK OR FIRE.
Every customers that purchased this range should be notified immediately to avoid damages. This information should be added to the manual for customers protection: Remove all doors and drawers beside range to avoid damages.
Samsung sent me an email on December 20, 2019 stating at this time the claim is being closed as this is not considered to be a mechanical defect.
justification: The incident caused damage to kitchen cabinets but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) as the issue stems from a common user action with inadequate warnings.

incident_description: I have a Samsung Refrigerator Model #RF28JBEDBSG/AA which was not cooling causing food and medicines to spoil even though the door temperature read 36 degrees and the ice dispenser continuously freezes up. Called 1-800-Samsung and was given a trouble ticket number. Was told that although the 1 year warranty was up that they would grant a "one-time warranty allowance" for parts and labor. I would have to pay the repair and they would reimburse me. The representative whose name was [REDACTED] gave me the name and number of an authorized Samsung repair center in my area and I scheduled the repair for 2 January at the cost of $95. A technician pulled up in a Samsung van wearing a Samsung shirt and came in and after I told him what the unit was doing he diagnosed the problem in 5 minutes. He removed the Evaporator Cover which was caked in ice. I was amazed at what I saw and said "Boy that's bad". He commented that this was a common problem. I asked him specifically if Samsung was aware of this problem and he said "Oh yes, they are aware". He had the parts on hand and replaced the Evaporator Cover, Defrost sensor and defrosted the ice maker unit with a steamer and was done in 30 minutes to the tune of $353. I paid the man and the next morning filed for my reimbursement by calling Samsung. I was given another ticket number and email address to send my scan of the workorder. I asked how the reimbursement was going to come and the representative named [REDACTED] said "usually by check". I sent the invoice and received an email from Samsung the next day saying "We are sorry to hear that youÃÂre experiencing an issue with your Samsung Refrigerator and that youÃÂve received a warranty ruling you do not agree with. We know it is frustrating for any product to fail, whether in-or-out of warranty. We certainly never like to hear of any of our products failing at any age. Samsung believes in building quality products and we apologize all of your expectations of us have not been met. We value our relationship and are committed to providing the highest level of service simply because our customers deserve it." I immediately contacted Samsung and was told that "the ticket says if the problem was the cooling system condenser they would reimburse parts and labor." I elevated the problem to four different customer service representatives who said they couldn't authorize the reimbursement ending up with [REDACTED] who said he could do nothing else and he was the highest customer service person I could speak to. I paid over $2300 for a refrigerator that should have lasted more than 3 years. This is not a warranty issue this is a safety issue. We were eating food and taking medicines that were not preserved.  There should be a safety recall issued for this refrigerator because it does not cool nor operate as it was designed and consumers are goin to get sick from eating spoiled food.
justification: The incident describes spoiled food and medicines due to refrigerator failure, which could lead to health issues (injury). The technician's comment about this being a common problem suggests the issue is likely to recur.

incident_description:
I purchased a brand new Samsung RF263BEAESR/AA refrigerator in 2013 with an extended warranty from Sears.  Over the past 3 years I have had continuous problems with my Samsung Refrigerator not producing ice, freezing up in the rear causing the fan to stop and stop cooling, and water puddling under the crisper. I called Samsung and they said there was nothing they could do about this because it was out of warranty. After having done research I realized this is a common issue that affects over 20 models and this was not acceptable.

January 26, 2019 I sent complaint to the BBB regarding this issue and on January 28, Samsung set me up with an out of warranty service repair ticket. The authorized Dealer [REDACTED] came to my home on February 8, 2019 and repaired my refrigerator. Less than a month later my refrigerator started to freeze up again and [REDACTED] team came out again on March 07, 2019. He, defrosted the rear, replaced the ice maker and some other components as well as sealing compartments. In July my ice maker stopped working and in September the back panel freezing started again. I contacted Samsung on November 8 to see if they would rectify this situation via chat. They offered me a repair at my cost and I declined because I have already had it fixed 2 times and should not have to pay for a defect. After almost 2 hours they informed me they will escalate this to the higher level team that I am requesting for a refund for the refrigerator. On November 8, [REDACTED] from Samsung emailed me and said they wonÃÂt be able to process a refund since my unit has not been deemed defective, to qualify for a refund my unit needed to have at least 2 complete repairs and at the moment it only has one, please call back if I wanted to proceed with the service repair but will have to cover the charges. 
I re-opened my case with the BBB on November 11 because I went through the 2 repairs as mentioned and Samsung is denying I had a second repair done at all. On November 21, [REDACTED] from SamsungÃÂs Office of the President stated that I was previously misinformed on their policies and because of the age of my unit, it will not qualify for any accommodations. 
This is far beyond a warranty issue it's a defective design that is now endangering me and my family. I had to start throwing away food every few days because the refrigerator does not stay cool, I consistently purchase ice and use coolers as a backup when the refrigerator stops cooling completely. The ice maker is non-functional and frozen shut. Now there is mold appearing under the crisper as well. Samsung is well aware of this defect and only chooses to refund selective customers. My model is one of over 20 models listed in a class action suit filed in New Jersey in 2017 as well as SamsungÃÂs Company issued Service bulletin in May 2017.  Even though my refrigerator is 7 years old, models as new as 2018 have the same exact issues.
justification: The incident involves a defective refrigerator causing food spoilage and mold, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Oster Toaster Oven Model TSSTTVF815 PN:160493 Prong Numbers H014 and GAZ developed a defective timer.  This is critical because after using the toaster oven the timer turns off as it should but then immediately goes beyond off and TURNS ITSELF BACK ON in the keep warm position which is actually the temperature at which you were cooking.  If the consumer does not immediately remove the cooked item it will continue cooking and burn possibly starting a kitchen fire.  If the consumer turns it off again it will begin ticking and turn itself back on.  The only way to turn it off is to unplug the toaster over.  The timer keeps going even with out electricity .

I did report this to Oster and because it was beyond warranty they referred me to a service centers in Wisconsin and Indiana both of who said that it could not be repaired.  No one seemed concerned that it was a fire hazard.  I know that their have been other complaints because I saw them on line.  I suggested that it should have been recalled but got no comment.
justification: The defective timer can cause the toaster oven to turn back on, posing a fire hazard, but no actual incidents or injuries are reported in the description.

incident_description:
I own a Bosch dishwasher that stopped working on 12/31/19.  I contacted a repair technician and electrician. They diagnosed the problem as a faulty electrical cord to the dishwasher. They believe that the power cord overheated causing the contacts to break. Went I went online, I learned that Bosch had a CPSC ordered recall for exactly this issue. I contacted Bosch regarding the recall and was told that my unit was not covered because it was produced after January 2015.  However, the unit was purchased and installed in 2014.  The recall covers exactly my unit, and I believe their information on serial number and date of manufacture is wrong. When I explained the situation, they said they would not address or cover any repairs even though it is the same issue as the recall. While I intend to get this fixed privately, I am concerned that the scope of the recall may be too narrow and that someone could get injured or hurt under similar circumstances. 

Model number is SHX68T55UC/02 which is a covered model
Serial number is 9407
justification: The incident involves a faulty electrical cord that could potentially cause harm, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: GE Refrigerator Control Board mounted on the rear of the unit caught fire.  We were originally drawn to the unit due to the door open alarm sounding while the door was closed.  During that time, we heard a "sizzling" sound coming from the back of the fridge, followed by a plume of smoke rising from behind.  We were able to pull the unit out and remove the electrical cord from the outlet, which stopped the sizzle and burn activity.  We cleared the house of smoke / electrical fire smell and removed the cover to find the control board blackened.  Photos were taken.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled by unplugging the unit.

incident_description: We had a Bosch dishwasher (Model SHVM78W53N) installed in April 2018. In November 2019 it suddenly stopped working. We had the original installer come back and he discovered that a part in the dishwasherÃÂs junction box had melted causing the dishwasher to stop working. There have been recalls for this same reason on similar Bosch dishwashers but we were informed by Bosch that our model was not included in the recall. I believe that this model of dishwasher also poses a fire hazard to the ones that have been recalled. Thankfully our dishwasher tripped the breaker but if it had not, a fire could have been the result. I have contacted Bosch and they are unconcerned about the potential hazard that their product could present even though other models have been recalled for this same problem.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned without causing injury or fire, but a fire hazard was possible if the breaker had not tripped.

incident_description: I was making blue berry waffles. I made the batter with blue berries. Before plugging the Black & Decker Double Flip (with duel cooking plates) product to the outlet to use for the first time, I read the product instruction book thoroughly, including the safeguards section, season the waffle irons as instructed, then wiped away any excess oil. I plugged in the product, then when the green indicator light turned on, I poured the first amount (3/4 cup) as directed in the instructions. I locked the product as designed and instructed. After 10 seconds (per the instructions), I turned it over to pour the batter on the other side. I locked the product as instructed, waiting 10 seconds, before turning it over to the side with the first cooking waffle. The first cooking waffle started to steam. At about one minute and a half later, it started to make a noise and was steaming very much. I backed away and the device exploded and jumped off the edge of the counter hitting the floor. No one was injured. It unplugged itself when it fell to the ground. I left it alone until it cooled off. I took two picture of the area shortly after the product exploded. I noticed that the plastic lock and one of the two handles snapped off and was left on the counter. I took additional pictures of the product after it cooled.
justification: The device exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the electric range burner knobs when brushed against slightly turns the unit without their knowledge.  She stated that a blanket was placed on the unit to prevent the glass from scratch while installing a microwave, the unit came on catching the blanket on fire, she took it outside to contain the flames.  She stated that there has been more than one incidents with the range coming on.

Caller stated that the company was contacted and a technician was sent out, she was informed by him that she should remove the knobs when not using or place plastic cover over it.  The company advised her that the range was made with sensitive knobs. She stated that she contacted them most recently 1/8 and was advised that they are unaware of these incidents which she does not believe.

Caller stated that she has seen numerous reports about these ranges on the internet.  She stated that these ranges are a fire hazard and should be recalled before she has a house fire.

*Also caught dish cover on fire + melted it
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with the electric range, causing a blanket and dish cover to catch fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Mainstay Toaster for $15 4 slicer bought at Wal-Mart January 2020. 

The toaster on the right side caught fire and this was even after having it on the lowest setting. 

It could have caught my kitchen on fire !!!
justification: The toaster caught fire, which is an incident with potential for significant harm, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: This was a new purchase of a Haier gas range. The first time the oven was used, The roasting pan had been sitting on the 3rd position in the oven, the rack collapsed when taking a 15 lb roast out of the oven spilling the juices in the pan all over the oven door, lower cabinets to the right and kitchen floor barely missing my leg.   In a second incident the rack that was placed in the 2nd position didn't hold the weight of a 17 lb turkey after the oven was pre-heated.  Out of necessity, The turkey had to be cooked on the bottom of the oven.  In a 3rd incident the rack on the 2nd position collapsed on to the bottom of the oven when a heavy cake pan was placed on it.
justification: The incident describes multiple occurrences of oven rack collapses causing spills and inconvenience, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Fire Agency dispatched to incident address for report of smoke in the structure. Engine crew located charred plastic container on top of stove top. All controls were in the off position at time of discovery. Occupant reported last using stove previous day and that they had experienced intermittent episodes of burners randomly turning on several times previously.

Fire was contained to stove top, smoke throughout second floor of structure, fire department assisted with ventilation, secured and isolated electric range from power and advised occupant to have repaired/replaced.
justification: Incident involved smoke and a contained fire with no reported injuries, and the issue of burners turning on intermittently suggests a possible recurrence.

incident_description: My LG refrigerators light did not turn off when the refrigerator door was closed.  The light is supposed to turn off when the doors close or after being on for 7 minutes so not to overheat.  My daughter discovered the problem when opening the refrigerator and there was a bad burning smell. It has melted much of the plastic cover to a point that I could not remove the cover in order to remove the light bulbs.  There is NO switch to turn off the light.  We unplugged it, and had to pry the pieces off, which was very difficult without being burnt or cut because it was extremely hot.  But not wanting to loose all of our food, we didn't have a lot of time. Some of the food containers had also begun to melt and much food was ruined.  What really concerns me is that if it hadn't been noticed, it would be a fire hazard.  It had even begun to melt the top of the refrigerator.  There should be a safety switch that turns off the lights when overheated - or it should operate as stated that it turns off after 7 minutes.  There is also no way to turn it off manually.  Had this happened a week earlier when we were out of town, I am afraid it would have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore Elite refrigerator Model 106.5177 or model 465177*51*. The wires leading from the main unit to the freezer door became broken and wire is exposed that could cause a shock hazard or short circuit. I have read and heard from others that have the same problem. 

Calling Kenmore resulting in a service technician telling us that the door had to be replaced for $1200. The refrigerator was only 1.5 years old and cost $1400.

I believe that this is a design flaw and a recall should be issued. 

It is extremely unfair to the consumer to have to be responsible for this unsafe and expensive condition and repair.
justification: The exposed wires pose a shock hazard or short circuit risk, but no injury is reported. The issue is described as a common problem, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I have a GE side-by-side refrigerator, model GSC23LSRC SS, serial number GH415160. It was put in use in my house in May of 2005. Never had any problem until yesteday evening Dec 23 2019. My wife heard some noises in the kitchen, and when she was near the refrigerator she smelled burned plastic. We did not see anything burning, so thought nothing of it. About 15 minutes later, there was another sound that was very noticeable, and stronger burning smell from the refrigerator. I laid flat on the floor, looking into the bottom of the refrigerator through the plastic grill, and saw a flame on the bottom side of the fridge. I quickly unplugged the refrigerator. I have not used it since then, and intend to dispose of the refrigerator. We are buying a new refrigerator.
I believe this refrigerator GE Profile family model is pretty popular back then, and think maybe many are being used today. I have read somewhere there was a class action lawsuit against GE for this refrigerator in 2013. I just learned about this lawsuit after this incident. I thought the responsible government agency should know about the potential fire hazard of this refrigerator and the like models. I still have the refrigerator, until Dec 30, when HomeDepot will deliver new refrigerator and take a way this dangerous appliance. It was a good thing we were home at that time. I don't want to think what could happen if we were not home.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury or death, and the likelihood is possible given the reported class action lawsuit and the model's popularity.

incident_description:
Model: JB250DF5WW
Serial #: GH238579Q

This product is defective. The problem occurred before the warranty expired, but it was dismissed as a one or two time event. It is a very noisy range in use ÃÂ surging. Since then, the problem has progressively gotten much worse. 

This is the problem. The burner switch, larger burner, is set to 4. The electric coil / burner flares to high, high heat and turns bright red. Food, if not removed from the burner, would burn quickly. This occurs on all burners. ItÃÂs less frequent on the smaller burners which are used less. Pan size appears to be irrelevant. 

This problem is escalating and presents a fire hazard. As conscientious cooks, we never leave the range unattended as the burner may flare at any time. The range is used everyday, and we must use lower and lower temps. In fact, items will boil even when burner is set to low / 1. This is clearly unacceptable and a defective product. GE is responsible for this.
justification: The defective product presents a fire hazard and requires constant monitoring, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Samsung Electric Oven/Range sparked and flamed in the rear where the majority of the electrical connections are. Caused a small fire and smoke.
justification: The incident involved a small fire and smoke but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. Such electrical malfunctions in appliances are possible but not extremely common.

incident_description: Whirlpool Slide-in Electric Range Model GY399LXUS02 turned oven on by itself.  Unable to turn oven/range off via the keypad --  had to turn range off at the circuit breaker.

incident_description: I am writing to report a serious concern with our GE profile refrigerator, model PSHS6PGZBESS.   My complaint focuses on the fridge's ice maker.  The ice maker has an auger in the plastic ice tray, which rotates to stir, break up and release ice from the fridge.  Our auger, which looks like a big clear plastic corkscrew, cracked and released sharp shards of clear plastic into my drinking cup.  I, fortunately, did not consume any sharp pieces of plastic to my knowledge and observed these shards at the bottom of my cup.  I am concerned, however, that this product defect can cause harm to other consumers.   It is abundantly predictable that a clear plastic auger that is tasked with churning and breaking up frozen ice cubes will break over time.  It is equally predictable the resulting shards of plastic from the auger will land in someone's drinking cup, potentially be consumed, and cause injury.  GE could easily use a metal auger at an increased cost and eliminate this risk to the consumer.  I feel that this is an unacceptable and hidden risk to GE's customers that could cause serious harm or potentially death.

incident_description:
I recently purchased, and then returned, a waffle maker:

Chefman 
Model RJ04-AO4

WAFFLE MAKER
120V-60 HZ  700W

CONFORMS TO UL STD.1803

ETL LISTED YS
INTERTEX 3103807

DATE CODE 1902
ACCESS CODE 3001512
======
I returned it because it is a burn hazard and should be removed from the marketplace until its design is modified.

This is a waffle-maker of standard clamshell design, but there is no handle on the lower shell.
It seems perfectly fine and opens just by releasing the latch--until you cook a waffle. Then the waffle acts as a glue between the upper and lower shells, and releasing the latch does not open the waffle-maker. If you grab the lower half to pull it open, you will get burned, and with no handle on the lower half, there is no safe way to open the device. 

I managed to get a butter knife under the latch and lever the sections apart, but I had to pick the hot waffle-maker up off the counter to get the knife in there. Because it does not open easily once the waffle is cooked, this thing is a burn hazard.
justification: The waffle maker's design poses a burn hazard due to the lack of a handle on the lower shell, making it likely to cause injury during use.

incident_description:
GE Profile Gas Range Oven Model "PGB910SEM4SS", Serial No. AT212815P.  Purchased from Home Depot on Special Order, circa 2009 during a kitchen remodel package.  The defect is that a main product sales feature, the "self-clean cycle" locks the range anywhere from one (1), two (2) to four (4) hours at extremely high temperatures, during which the entire range becomes not only dangerously hot to the human touch, causing burns, but causing the range knobs to melt (also known as "binding") due to the excessive and unabated heat the oven generates when the "self-clean" cycle is used.  

Further, the excessive and unabated heat generated when the broiler or high (400 degree) baking temperatures are selected, have burned my fingers when touching anything on the stovetop.  Even if the knobs are replaced, use of the self-clean cycle or any high temperature oven activity will repeat the same danger.  As narrated in the video, it is extremely dangerous to consistently check these knobs to ensure they are in the "off" position and that there isn't any gas escaping at my cooperative (for both my and my fellow shareholders' safety).  

The defect occurred over a period of years and cannot be confined to one particular date for statute of limitations.  Every time the "self-clean" cycle is activated, it presents an new and ever-increasing danger, besides the existing danger of the knobs.  I am a single owner user and as you can see, the range oven is well maintained at all times and still sparkles in every area except the burnt area of the knobs (near the oven heat vents).  (Except, the oven light just went out a day, ago... no worries).  Thank you for your attention to this matter for it is a serious concern.

[REDACTED]
justification: The description reports burns from touching the hot range and melted knobs, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurs every time the self-clean cycle or high temperatures are used, making it likely (4).

incident_description: We recently purchased a KitchenAid Model KCG5550ESS01 gas cooktop for a new house we are building.  We selected this appliance because it is very similar to a KitchenAid gas cooktop we purchased approximately 6 years ago for our current house. We were disturbed to learn the old and new units work differently in a material way.  With the older unit when a burner knob is depressed and rotated to any position (ignite, low, medium, high or any point in between) the igniter continues to function until the burner ignites whether or not the knob continues to be depressed and regardless of whether the knob has been rotated to the ignite, low, medium or high positions.  With the new one the igniter stops functioning once the knob is no longer depressed whether or not the burner is ignited.  If the knob is rotated to "ignite" it functions property, but if the knob is rotated past "ignite" to another setting (and there is nothing to prevent that from happening) the igniter quits functioning but the gas continues to flow. To compound the problem, the lettering on the unit identifying the various positions of the knobs is so dim that you almost have to strain to read it.  In other words, only a very attentive adult, familiar with the design characteristics of this unit, can operate it safely.  An inattentive adult, one not familiar with the characteristics of the unit or a child can easily turn the gas on to a burner, inadvertently turn off the igniter and because the gas continues to flow cause a fire or explosion.  At our request KitchenAid sent out a technician who said the unit was operating as designed.
justification: The design flaw in the cooktop could lead to gas leaks and potential fire or explosion, posing a significant safety risk, especially to inattentive users or children.

incident_description:
The range was included  in CPSC Recall# 09-333 and has been serviced for this issue in accordance with the recall.  The consumer estimates that it has been serviced at least 3 times over the years.


The consumer has experienced all 3 problems stated in the recall:  All 4 of the burners have jumped to a higher temperature unexpectedly.  Different burners have turned on unexpectedly.  Some of the burners could not be turned off and the consumer had to either unplug the range or trip the breaker  The consumer has contacted the manufacturer each time and they sent the replacement parts out to her (usually overnight) and scheduled a technician to service the range.  Every time the repair was the done, the problem returned.  The length of time that it took the problem to return varied.

After it was fixed it continued to freeze up and water would pool under our deli drawer and mold was growing in the bottom. Smoke started to fill the kitchen when it was shorting out and melting.  Occurred when just my son was home in the house.  He called me at work indicating that the dishwasher was pouring out smoke. incident_description:

Both first floor smoke alarms went off.  When I put my hand on this area of the stove, it was too hot to actually touch.  It took over 30 minutes for it to be cool enough to touch. incident_description:
Viking Range was fined for ranges that turn on by themselves (article dated 4/17/17) for 15 models sold between 2007 & 2014. 

We have a Viking Range that was purchased in 2017 when our home was under construction. It is Model # VGCC548*; Serial Number 012417C*. 

On 11/9/19 the oven ignited by itself in the middle of the night; our fire alarm went off & woke us. The house was filled with smoke; we have to flip the circuit breaker to turn the oven off. It was super-heated & left marks on our brick back-splash. It also melted the igniter & safety features of the oven, as well as the mechanisms for the sliding racks. I phoned Viking the next day to report the issue & was told to call a service provider to have the oven fixed, but Viking is not liable because our serial number wasn't under their recall list. She further stated that there have been no complaints with my particular unit, to which I responded, 'please log this as an official complaint', which she didn't. 

I called Lakeview Service, which is the provider recommended by Viking and they came to our home on 11/13. The specialist that serviced the oven said it looked exactly like the previous problems that occurred as part of the recall program and this was a major safety issue, although the part in the oven read as the updated version. 

Clearly, Viking has not remedied the faulty part issues that caused this. I called them back after the service tech left and & they're blanket answer again was "that's not one of the recall ranges", albeit the exact circumstances around the previous problem were evident. The customer service person stated to send her the service notes from the technician and she'd send to management but doubted it would be covered. She refused information about the manager to whom the information would be sent; I emailed the service notes; no feedback as of yet. 

Viking needs to be revisited about this issue, as there's no such thing as a coincidence. Although my unit may not be under the recall provision, the exact circumstances occurred, which can lead one to logically conclude the manufacturing defect has not been remedied. Had we not been home and the fire alarm not gone off, I'm unsure the result that would have occurred to our home, our animals, and our possessions. It's quite a frightening thought.  

As a businessman, I'd venture to guess they did a cost/benefit on the number of instances versus cost to fix and did nothing in the hopes that they could squash the whole issue and castigate anyone who called in the future as not being under the recall provision.
justification: The oven ignited by itself, causing smoke and property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Wife went to use the Bosh Dishwasher on the afternoon 11/12/2019.  It had run Monday night to completion that we could tell.  On that Tuesday afternoon my wife noticed that the water was pooled in bottom of the dishwasher and that the control panel was dark.  I investigated:
1. Sucked the water out of the bottom and checked the filter if it was clogged (was not)
2. Attempt to reset via 'start' button for 5 seconds produced no results
3. GFCI outlet nor main panel breaker had tripped (wet dry vacuum used same outlet as dishwasher normally is in without problem)
4. Unplug and plug back in had no results
5. (Left unplugged) and opened power cord to dishwasher junction box.  The middle junction was blackened in places where the load, neutral and ground wires are connected.  The neutral wire was completely melted and no longer connected.

Nobody was injured during the incident.

Only the junction box was damaged that we can tell.  We are awaiting a technician to some diagnose the problem further per a call into Bosch.  At this time we are not certain of the cause or if the dishwasher itself has any other damage or what caused this.

The plug in cord per the label is 14 gauge.  The junction box label requires 14/3 or 12/3 wiring.

Called Bosch on 11/12/2019 and found out about a similar recall for power extension cords but was told our model was not in any active recalls.

Dishwasher was installed in March 8, 2017 and has worked fine since then.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with no injuries, and the issue appears to be isolated to the junction box.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung French door refrigerator, model RF323TEDB. This model is currently part of a class action lawsuit because of its inability to maintain safe temperatures. I have had four separate repairs on this unit since its purchase in 2012. The repairs were all related to the ice maker freezing over and the water lines getting clogged. I did not realize that the ice maker freezing over was causing the fan to be less effective at circulating the cold air. Today a repair tech came out for the fourth repair. While he was here, he checked the internal and external temperatures of the unit. The external back of the unit had experienced some rust due to a cold spot on the back that was condensing and then dripping. The tech measured a considerable temperature difference between one part of the back and the rest of the back of the unit. He determined this to be a manufacturing defect due to insufficient insulation. More concerning, however, was that when he measured the temperature of the interior of the unit, no part of the fridge was colder than 48 degrees. This was in spite of the fact that the display panel of the fridge was showing that the fridge was set to 36 degrees and that the fridge should have, in fact been 36 degrees. No amount of tinkering will fix this issue as the display is programed to show one temperature regardless of the actual temperature of the unit. I have a documented visit to the doctor from March of last year where my two of my children were so sick they needed to be medicated to stop vomiting. My husband, older son, his girlfriend, and my mother were also affected. We fear the erratic temperature of the refrigerator may be to blame. 

I have contacted Samsung about this issue, including details about my children's illnesses, the multiple attempted repairs on the unit, and the opinion of the most recent repair tech that this problem is not a fixable problem but is in fact a manufacturing defect. Samsung will not agree to pay for any repairs or the original cost of the unit. They repeatedly tell me that it is outside of the warranty period. However, this is not a wear and tear issue. This is a defect in the design and could not have been fixed regardless of age.

incident_description: Our refrigerator had a sustained electrical fire in the inverter circuitry that connects to the compressor tank. At 10:00 pm on October 30, 2019 I was in my kitchen to turn off lights. Immediately upon entering the kitchen I could smell smoke that was indicative of an electrical fire. I alerted my wife, and we started searching for the source. At that time there was no active fire for us to track down, but the smoke odor was strongest near the fridge. The fridge then activated its cooling motor and I immediately heard a sizzling sound from the underneath the fridge. I looked through the grate and saw a sustained 2-3 inch high electrical fire. I reached behind the fridge and unplugged it and the fire immediately stopped. I rolled the fridge away from the wall in its designated place and started inspecting the rear to be sure that there was no risk of it restarting while it was unplugged. Once I was sure it would not start again, I started looking for a possible cause. Eventually, while inspecting it I saw a drop of water land directly onto a electrical connector box for the inverter next to the compressor tank. I followed the source of the dripping water to an access port position directly above the inverter for the water hose that goes to and from the water filter. Inspecting this port on the inside of the fridge, I found that the foam sealant was no longer adhered to the interior housing of the fridge and water from condensation or other sources inside the fridge was leaking through this port and dripping directly onto the wiring for the inverter. Given the known wet nature of refrigerators, and the lack of design foresight in putting a hose port directly above some critical wiring, and then using insufficiently water-proof sealant to close that port, this appears to be a design destined to fail. Our fridge is ~3 years old. My hope is that our luck in being home and in the room when this started and catching it early can prevent more significant fires in other homes that have this refrigerator model.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but was caught early with no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The design flaw suggests a likely recurrence if unaddressed.

incident_description:
Product: Samsung French Door Refrigerator
Model: RF31FMESBSR
Serial Number: W65143BD401254B
Purchase Price: $2699.99 + 8.0% Sales Tax = $2,915.99
Purchase Date: 05/21/2013

PROBLEM STATEMENT:
Samsung has over 20 models of refrigerators with a known defect that causes their refrigerators to operate at UNSAFE temperatures.  The defect causes the fridge section evaporator to freeze over so much that the ice build-up hits the circulation fan, a causing loud, unsettling noise.  This ice over the evaporator also prevents the proper circulation of cold air inside the refrigerator, causing the temperature to rise to unsafe levels for proper food storage.

ADDITIONAL DETAILS:
Our family has been having stomach issues off and on for the past few years.  Not enough to go to the hospital, but a lot of feelings of queasiness, discomfort, and diarrhea.  At first, we thought that it may have been due to food quality, so we start buying more premium brands and all organic product.  When that didn't help, we started a food log to try to establish a pattern to rule out food allergies.  However, we could not find any consistencies.

However, after I saw on my local news about defective Samsung refrigerators, we did more research and found that there are thousands of people experiencing the same issue.  We were shocked to discover that this is not a warranty issue - this is a known factory defect issue with zero fixes on over 20 models and is currently in class action court.

I then purchased a refrigerator thermometer and recorded the inside temperatures at random intervals.  I have been recording for a few days now and refrigerator temperature is consistently higher than the indicated temperature on the display panel.  The refrigerator is set to 38 Degrees Fahrenheit (DF), but the actual temperature is above the safe zone averaging around 45 DF.  It gets worse - after the evaporator freezes up again, I see temperatures between 50-60 DF.  When the evaporators get extremely frozen over and the fan hits the ice, the inside temperature feels like room temperature.

The defect defects are: 1) The evaporator coils freeze, which prevents cold air from circulating properly - increasing the inside temperature to unsafe levels, and 2) the temperature reading of the refrigerator is false/misleading, which causes consumers to believe their food is safe when it is not. 

Ultimately, the design defects are causing my family (and other unsuspecting consumers) to think their food is safe to consume, even though the temperatures are at UNSAFE levels for days, weeks, even months!

SAMSUNG RESPONSE:
Samsung has not been forthcoming about this issue. Many people I have spoken to have had Samsung try to dismiss their claims by saying this is a warranty issue when this is a known factory defect issue. Samsung has tried to get customers to PAY for repairs that are ultimately temporary and futile because there are ZERO fixes for any of the 20+ affect models - ZERO FIXES!

DESIRED RESOLUTION:
I would like Samsung to provide me and my family a FULL refund of the $2,915.99 purchase price of the refrigerator due to it harming my family because of its design flaw and factory defect causing it to operate at unsafe temperatures and misleading us with a false temperature reading.

I would like for Samsung to also provide refunds/restitution to harmed consumers for their full purchase price including the removal, destruction, and recycling of all defective Samsung refrigerators.
justification: The incident describes unsafe refrigerator temperatures leading to food spoilage and family members experiencing stomach issues, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue is widespread across multiple models, making occurrence likely (4).
