She then contacted the firm to report the matter and request assistance with an inspection but she was informed that an inspection would be at her expense, which she declined. She said she was on the phone for about two hours and she was repeatedly transferred between Sears and Kenmore. She requested information about the safety of the unit but each Rep. declined to answer and proceeded to transfer her to another Rep. She asked to speak with a manager but she was told that a manager was not available and then transferred her to the parts department. 

The unit was already in the home when she moved in sometime in 2015. The unit is used daily.
justification: The incident resulted in mouth irritation, which qualifies as an injury, but no medical attention was sought.

incident_description:
Approximately 9/20/2019:  The consumer had a plastic salt shaker sitting on the range top and it melted.  None of the burners were turned on.  The oven was in the pre-heat mode for approximately 5 minutes and it was set to 375 for approximately 10 minutes, before turning it off.  The consumer said that the salt shaker had been on range top the entire time.

The consumer had to use a hot-pad to remove what was left of the salt shaker.  

The consumer is concerned because she placed her hand approximately 4" over the range top surface and it was  extremely hot.  The consumer said that had she left her hand there that she could have easily gotten burned.

The consumer's son-in-law pulled out the stove and the consumer cleaned underneath it.  She tried the oven again and found that the range top surface became extremely hot when the oven was used (without the burners in use).  

After that, she had her  son-in-law remove the stove and place it in the garage and she replaced it with a different brand.  The replacement brand does not present this problem.  Prior to moving into this home 2 months ago, the consumer also had a ceramic smooth-top range and when she used the oven, the surface did not get hot.  Therefore, she does not believe that this is a common problem.

During the last week of September 2019, the consumer called the manufacturer and filed a report with their rep.  The rep. told the consumer that there was no recall on her product and the rep. said that she did not recall hearing this problem before.
justification: The incident involved a melted salt shaker and potential for burns, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My coffee maker over-heated and began to smoke this morning.  The brewing cycle was complete and the coffee maker was on keep-warm. My wife and I heard a loud popping sound in the kitchen coming from the coffee maker.  We un-plugged it immediately, and noticed that it was producing smoke and a bad odor.  The coffee in the pot was almost boiling, and there is a visible crack in the warmer.  I believe we averted a fire by un-plugging the unit quickly.  We were fortunate that this happened on a Sunday morning and had not left for work as would be typical in a weekday.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoke but no injury or fire occurred due to quick action.

incident_description: Kenmore oven model 790.45599900 has oven walls that expand over time and allow the oven racks to fall resulting in dangerous spills and potentially fires.
justification: The description mentions dangerous spills and potential fires, which are incidents but does not confirm any injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Frigidaire oven glass (facing the user) shattered into tiny pieces across the kitchen area preceded by a sound like a gunshot. It was not tuned on, or even in use. Glass pieces got everywhere and a member of the family who was nearby became extremely scared and could not even step into the kitchen because of the glass everywhere.
justification: The oven glass shattered, causing a significant hazard with glass pieces everywhere, and a family member was extremely scared but not physically injured.

incident_description:
My wife placed a bowl of bean soup in the microwave for two minutes and left the kitchen. When she came back to the kitchen, she screamed that the microwave was on fire.  I came upstairs and entered the kitchen coughing. I didn't see any flames or anything smoldering.  I opened the window and aired out the kitchen. The smoke didn't smell like burned food, but more like burnt plastic or electrical wires.

I asked my wife if she put any metal objects in the microwave unintentionally.  She claimed she didn't.  After the smoked cleared, I checked the inside of the microwave for anything that could have caused the issue.  I found nothing and performed a test to see if it operates. I ran the microwave set for 2 minutes.  

After about a minute running, I saw smoke coming from the bottom of the microwave.  I immediately stopped the microwave and unplugged it.  I just reported the issue to Samsung customer care and they said someone will contact me within 24 to 48 hours due to high call volume. I felt the issue was urgent and they should have escalated it for a faster response.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard from the microwave, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the knobs to his oven range are very sensitive as even brushing against them will ignite the burners, or unknowingly emit gas from them. Numerous times the consumer and his family have been alerted of this by the smell of the gas, the flames, or the clicking of the knobs when it emits gas without igniting.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him that they could send a Service Technician to inspect the unit to see if there is a defect however when the consumer stressed the issue, the representative told him that the Manufacturer is the party that determines if the issue he is reporting is a safety concern or not. The consumer declined the service as it would cost him since the Technician would state that the unit works.

The consumer states that the cooktop is used five to seven times per week whereas the oven is used three to four times weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for at least the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with the oven range knobs, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Left rear range burner was on a "low" setting when it spontaneously heated up to maximum.  Fortunately I was home, and noticed a burning smell from what was cooking.  I inspected the knob, and it was in the right position for "low" and not stripped out in any way.  It had been idling on this setting untouched for hours before it spontaneously heated up to maximum.  Had nobody been around nearby, it could have resulted in a fire.

I feel this is important to report because, if the knob components are failing in some way, it is not a safety minded, "fail safe" design, and others may not be as lucky to spot it in time.

Model number 790.95302104

Serial number:  VF31530540
justification: The burner spontaneously heating up to maximum could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred as it was noticed in time.

incident_description:
Dishwasher was running during the cleaning cycle and started smoking and producing an acrid smell.  The smoke was coming from behind the control panel in the door.  There was no sign of water penetration at that location in the unit.  No visible flames were evident outside of the unit.  The unit is no longer functional.

There was no specific harm in this instance, but the potential for harm was high.  Please update with the following description for "Risk of Harm"  - The circuit board overheated and started smoking.  While no flames were evident outside the unit - the plastic melted and heat was sufficient to fuse the connection harness to the circuit board. The unit was installed in wooden cabinetry - which, with sufficient temperature and proximity, could have led to a whole house fire.
justification: The dishwasher started smoking and produced an acrid smell, but there was no injury or death. The potential for harm was high, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: Bosch dishwasher model SHU43C05UC installed in 2004.  Machine was running through wash cycles when area behind cycle selection buttons on front of machine apparently shorted out and caused a fire.  I turned off the electricity and the fire continued to burn and grow.  Tried to blow out the fire with breath,  When that didn't work tried to smother fire with a wet cloth. When that didn't kill the fire I had to use a dry chemical fire extinguisher to put out the fire.  The selection buttons and the surrounding plastic enclosure were melted and burned.  The flames went up and under the wood counter base.  Had we not been near the dishwasher the flames would have ignited the counter and then the wood cabinets on both sides resulting in a major fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have escalated to a major fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was using the knife to open a package, the locking mechanism failed and forced the blade closed on my finger resulting in stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the context of a knife malfunction.

incident_description: My Frigidaire stainless oven had been set to preheat . I heard a noise and looked and flames were coming up the oven wall and I could smell something burning which ended up being the back electrical panel . Now the oven doesnÃÂt work . I tried replacing two interior parts (cooking element and thermostat) which didnÃÂt fix the problem . IÃÂm assuming the electrical wires in the back panel was damaged. The inside of the oven was clean and no food was inside so itÃÂs definitely a manufacturer defect.
justification: The incident involved flames and electrical damage but no injury or death, and the issue appears to be a rare manufacturer defect.

incident_description: My Bosch dishwasher caught on fire tonight after running for about 15 minutes into the wash cycle.  Very luckily we were home, smelled something burning, and ran to the kitchen to see flames shooting out of the upper right corner of the dishwasher.  We were able to stop it from running and cut the power to the circuit. I am trying to determine if this is one of the models Bosch recalled, but on their website, the recall that addresses models made between May 1999 to July 1995 doesn't link to anything.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description: Using dishwasher to wash dinner dishes. Noticed an acrid smell while reading in nearby room. Ran to kitchen and observed acrid smoke emanating from our GE Monogram Dishwasher. Immediately turned off electric breaker to the appliance. Opened doors and windows to remove odor and smoke.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission from a dishwasher, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We have a slide in GE stove/oven.  It's in our island.  The knobs are on the front of the unit since there is no back splash area due to it being in an island.  The knobs turn on without any effort.  There is a 'control lock' button on the control panel, however that only controls a child from changing the temperature of the oven.  It does not "lock" the burners.   We have no children in the house, thank goodness.  On multiple occasions, ourselves, or our guests, have brushed past the stove, or leaned over it to reach something on the counter and turned the burners on without knowing it.  We are not careless or reckless people but this has happened multiple times.  It has reached the point that we have to leave the knobs off completely.   I have been cutting vegetables on a cutting board on the flat top surface and my body has turned on the burner.  Completely melted the cutting board to the surface before i realized it was on.   I have burned hot pads, cooking utensils, scorched pans, etc on many occasions.  The final straw was that some papers that were on the counter, were overhanging the burner (this is a completely flat unit that blends right in with the countertop) and the burner somehow got turned on.  I only had one knob on the stove at the time and it got turned on.  We came home an hour later to a fire in our house.    This is absolutely ridiculous.   The knobs should never be able to be turned on that easily.   More than a dozen people in our family, or friends have accidentally done it.   I know nothing should be on a stove, but a cooktop should not turn on by rubbing against it.
justification: The incident resulted in a fire, which poses a significant risk of death, and the issue has occurred multiple times with various consequences.

incident_description:
I have a whirlpool stove with an electronic control panel that is flat by the surface. So is accessible to animals & children. 

the controls can be turned on by my cat walking on it or a child touching the control panel. 

It does have a lock but it is the same as the controls. the cat just stepped on it and turned the control lock off. 

the lock can not be activated until all the surfaces are no longer hot. So it remains active for quite some time after you use it.l 

Sometimes the lock does not work. Probably because I am constantly using it. When I shut the braker off it does reset.  

So I have to continually turn the baker off when I leave the room our go out of the house. 

Imagine my surprise the first I walked into the kitchen and the burner was glowing. 

I have contacted the manufacturer when I first brought it home and again recently when the lock was not working. They said both times  pretty much TOUGH LUCK. said I should have researched the stove before I bought it. Suggested I call the appliance store. Of course they also said sorry no returns.

You would have thought the salesman would have brought it to the attention of anyone who was interested in purchasing it that it might be a problem if you have kids or animals. 

I spent a lot of money on the stove.
justification: The incident involves a stove being accidentally turned on by a cat or child, posing a burn risk, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My fiancÃÂ©e was cooking chili on the stove last night.  She turned the knob to adjust the right front burner, and the knob post got stuck in the "on" position.  It was stuck so badly, I had to call the fire department and the firemen couldn't get it to budge.  It appears there is a manufacturing or design defect concerning the knob post.  The firemen ultimately broke the knob post with pliers, trying to turn the stove off, and ended up cutting off the gas to my house.  I have disconnected the device at the appliance valve now.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove knob requiring fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Purchased an enameled tea kettle from Kate Spade (https://www.macys.com/shop/product/kate-spade-new-york-all-in-good-taste-turquoise-tea-kettle?ID=2263223) approximately 4 years ago. Kettle was used sparingly (approximately once per month), never dropped, never put in dishwasher.  Without warning, while carrying a load of water and withOUT any sort of trauma, the handle of my teakettle completely came off, dropping the pot onto the ground. This represents a significant safety concern as there was absolutely no warning. Luckily, my pot only had cold water and not boiling water, so I was not injured and instead was merely splashed.

Where the kettle's handle fell off, it appears that the screws that were supposed to be holding the handle on were never attached through the wall of the tea kettle and that this is a manufacturing defect.

Looking at the Kate Spade website, it appears my tea kettle was not unique, as there are severa; reports of similar problems on their tea kettle review: https://www.katespade.com/products/tea-kettle/L857004.html
justification: The incident involved a manufacturing defect causing the handle to detach, but no injury occurred. Similar reports suggest this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
MY RANGE HAS A TRIPLE UNIT. FRONT RT. UNIT HAS SMALL HEATING AREA, MED. HEATING AREA AND EXTRA LARGE HEATING AREA. TIMES WHEN I USE THE SMALL HEATING AREA; THE EXTRA LARGE AREA AUTOMATICALLY TURNS ON  WITHOUT BEING MANUALLY BEING TURNED ON. THE OVEN LIGHT
TURNED ON AUTOMATICALLY AND COULD NOT BE TURNED OFF. WE HAD TO  UNDO THE WIRING TO GET IT OFF. NOW I DO NOT HAVE AN OVEN LIGHT. I NEVER RECEIVED ANY NOTICES  REGARDING RECALLS. I JUST HAPPEN TO SEE SOMETHING ON [REDACTED] REGARDING THIS. I NEED TO KNOW WHAT I CAN DO ABOUT THIS DANGEROUS STOVE. THE PROBLEM WITH THE  LARGE AREA TURNING ON 
HAPPENS FROM TIME TO TIME STILL. I WORRY ABOUT THIS  BURNER STARTING A FIRE IN MY HOUSE
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet. The issue happens intermittently, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: The main large (bottom right) burner intermittently stays on after turning the control knob off (seems to happen after the unit heats up).  The only way to get it to shut off is to turn the circuit breaker off until the unit cools down. It is extremely hazardous as numerous people use the unit and not everyone will know where the breaker is or even think of turning it off
justification: The burner staying on poses a significant hazard, especially since not all users may know how to turn it off, increasing the risk of burns or fire.

incident_description: Relay on control panel failed causing an electrical fire.  Turning breaker off solved the problem, fire department aired out the house.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but was resolved without injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: I am reporting a problem with a Kenyon B49516 6-1/2-Inch Alpine 2-Burner Trimline Cooktop with Analog Control UL, 240-volt.  It was installed by an electrician in late 2016.  When I tried to use in on Sunday, September 8, 2019, I had trouble making the dial work but I was able to turn it on.  I heard a noise and looked under the counter.  The metal heating unit had separated from the ceramic cooktop and fallen in a recycle trash bin under the counter.  The heat was still on.  I was able to quickly flip the circuit breaker to turn off the cooktop.  If I had not been standing next to the stove, it easily could have set the trash bin on fire and burned down my house.  The two parts of the cooktop were held together with glue and nothing else.  This was not adequate after several years.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cooktop that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was grinding potato peelings in my L8000 Waste King disposer and one of the grinder blades broke off where they  pivot and  came out of the disposer.It caused a severe imbalance.
Serial # 1K2-18559-59
justification: The incident involved a broken grinder blade causing imbalance, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Sunbeam Mixmaster Heritage Series electric stand mixer model 2350 has several a couple of issues. 

1) The beaters have nuts and bolts holding blades together and the nut came off into the batter causing chocking and dental hazard. This should have been welded rather than using this unsafe method to fasten the blades. Luckily I saw the nut in the batter before anyone was injured. 

2)  The bolts on bottom of the mixing bowl fall out causing unsanitary dish water to seep out of bowl on kitchen surfaces.
justification: The incident describes a potential choking hazard and unsanitary conditions, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I am writing about Maytag's wall double oven model MEW6630DDB serial 19604109NJ. I have gone through the phone call chain atÃÂ ÃÂ 1-800-344-1274 with my complaint and then wrote Whirlpool/Maytag .My story is as follows.ÃÂ  On Thursday morning September 19, 2019, less than 15 minutes after leaving my kitchen.I was in my bedroom, I hear what sounds like a crash and glass breaking. Upon searching for the cause of this noise I find my top oven door COMPLETELY shattered with glass all over myÃÂ 10.6 x 28.6 kitchen. NO the oven was NOT on and had not been in several days. The majority of the glass was on the floor beneath the oven, but there was chards everywhere, including the breakfast area and the dining room. Pieces were in the cooktop to the left of oven- on the countertop and all in the pantry floor to the right of the oven, the door was closed. It took an hour and a half to clean up and for the next 5 days we swept and mopped every day for fear of glass still looming on the floor.  September 25, a piece was even found in the living room 20 - 22 feet away that could have flown that far or have been tracked but it was on the couch.ÃÂ This is and was DANGEROUS !ÃÂ  I understand my oven is 11 years old BUT I don't care how old it is this should NOT have happened !ÃÂ  I was informed by Maytag that this is called Spontaneous Glass Breakage.ÃÂ  I looked it up and it said it was an uncommonÃÂ happening. I have 3 grandchildren under the age of 10 who are at my house a lot.ÃÂ  I keep imaging them here and walking in front of the oven as this happened !!ÃÂ  I have 2 small dogs who had been in the kitchen with me right before this happened.ÃÂ  I keep being thankful that I left the kitchen with my dogs right before the explosion (it sounds and looked like and WAS an explosion) I do not feel sending a service technician out here (free of charge) and being willing to negotiate the price of repairs--which is impossible to do--is all the responsibility Whirlpool (Maytag) has in this situation. We are finding glass everyday !!!!
justification: The incident involved spontaneous glass breakage causing a mess but no injuries, and it is described as an uncommon occurrence.

incident_description: The hot air accumulated in the instant pot brand I bought last year made an inflatable and then an explosion. Although I write to the company customer care section constantly asking me photos and information. I send it but so far, no one has looked for solutions or problems have not been interested.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of an instant pot, which is a significant safety issue, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
A GE/Haier gas stove exploded. It has since been discovered that the propane tubing behind the left front burner control knob is cracked. Leaking propane from the stove caused an explosion at the front of the stove. The explosion of the propane severely burned [REDACTED]. 

The accident occurred on June 6, 2017. The stove was a GE stove model JGBS60DEK. It was purchased and installed in Mr.[REDACTED] unit in January 2017 by the Board of the Association of [REDACTED], which is the co-op where Mr. [REDACTED] lived. The stove is a gas stove ÃÂ all 4 burners, oven and broiler are gas powered. It was converted from natural gas to propane by the two individuals who did the installation in January of 2017.
justification: The explosion caused severe burns, indicating a severity level of 4 (Death). The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but possible with faulty installations.

incident_description:
Purchased a Kitchen aid stove serial#R43410436 Model #Kers202BSSI in 2014. It came with a 1yr warranty which I chose not to extend since I had problems from day 1. I fought to make them extend 6 months which they did. Since that time I have had multiple problems that they covered as SAFETY but the last two could have caused a major problem.

The last 3 issues were electric causing potential fires. All were averted but very scary. The first time enclosed element caught fire. They replaced it no questions asked remember no warranty that was in ? a few years back. In 2019 the replaced element again caught fire around Easter. Then again in June 2019 the stove was on preheat low and one top burner on low. Hurt loud bang all power in house went out, we immediately unplugged stove from its own 3 pronged plug which is on its own fuse. Yet entire house blew and took awhile before power could be reset. Once again they sent someone out this time to replace element again BUT technician stated wires in back were too close and needed to be separated and that is how it caused power outage. He returned a week later corrected it and replaced element. On Friday Sept 27th I was baking at 350degrees turned off oven. It was off for 20 minutes. Getting ready for work and smelled burning went to check and saw stove was flashing DEFAULT TURN OFF POWER. The stove was extremely hot all over had difficulty moving stove out to pull plug. 

I then started attempting to call Whirlpool, Kitchen aid, May tag no one answers. Their online doesn't reply corporate safety didn't reply. I eventually got through by bypassing a different choice of numbers. I eventually sneaked into the executive line and spoke to a [REDACTED][REDACTED]. He states they will replace stove at 65% of MRSP cost.

My issue is it has been an issue that they must be aware of or why keep fixing with no warranty. They put myself and family at risked. I would like answers and a new stove as I know this one has been a lemon from day one in 2014. I do not want anyone else to be at potential risk. I speak up but many maybe have been fixing on their own or bought new.

Thank you
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes multiple electrical issues with the stove that could have caused fires but were averted, indicating a significant safety risk without actual injury.

incident_description: The fryer has a release for the food basket that can let go of hot food at any time.  A very bad design with the release button on top of the handle.
justification: The design flaw can lead to hot food being released unexpectedly, posing a high risk of burns or other injuries.

incident_description:
A metal part flew out of our Franke 3/4 hp garbage disposal and almost hit my wife.
Franke WD-751
SN 0C1 00950 9
Apparently [REDACTED] manufactured by Anaheim mfg. have been [REDACTED]. I called their 800 number and our model number is not on the [REDACTED]. It should be.
We bought this house in May so I do not know the history of the disposal.
justification: A metal part flew out but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Two washes before a catastrophic failure, Bosch dishwasher was emitting a faint metallic smell that I thought was something on the heating element. It went away at the end of the cycle, so I forgot to check between washes. While the dishwasher was running on 9/21/19, we heard two loud pops and went to see what was amiss. There were no lights on the unit (should have been running at that time), and there was a distinct burning smell. I opened the cabinet where the electrical connection was and discovered that the wire going to the junction box was scorched and a fitting at the top of the box was askew. When I put my hand on the junction box, it was very hot, so I pulled the breaker. It eventually cooled off, but we slept with a fire extinguisher next to our bed that night.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with scorched wires and a hot junction box, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was cooking fried potatoes on the left front burner. I had the rheostat on low-medium heat. After about 5 minutes I smelled smoke as I was preparing other foods for breakfast. When I turned to the stove, smoke was pouring our from under the pan lid. I looked at the burner control and it was still on low-medium heat setting; however, the burner was red hot. I turned the burner off and then grabbed a pot holder and removed the pan from the burner. I have tried using this burner several times since, watching it closely, and it continues to heat to maximum temp while the rheostat is on a lower setting.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a malfunctioning burner, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher stopped working and began to smoke.  Found that the electronic control module components had overheated and wire insulation had melted.  Did not find this model number and serial number listed as a recall when this problem occurred.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned and caused smoke and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Cooktop turned itself on after a very short residential electrical power outage
justification: The cooktop turning on after a power outage is an incident with potential safety implications, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
KitchenAid dishwasher Modle # KUDC10GXSS4, Serial # F14205894, date of purchase: 10/29/2011.
Mainboard, wire harness, touchpad, inner door, and outer door suffered fire damage during normal operation. The dishwasher circuit breaker tripped, and the house filled with a strong burnt electrical component smell.
justification: The dishwasher suffered fire damage during normal operation, indicating a significant incident with potential for injury, though none was reported.

incident_description:
(09/07/2019) The consumer loaded the dishwasher around 11:30 pm. When she went into the kitchen about an hour later, she noticed that the green light that indicates the cycles are completed was not on. It seemed as if the dishwasher had stopped 20 minutes into the wash cycle. The consumer open the door of the product and wiped up the water that was in the bottom of the dishwasher.

The next morning the consumer smelled an electrical smell coming from the product. She checked the circuit breaker and discovered that the breaker had tripped the connection to the dishwasher.

(09/10/2019)The consumer contacted the firm and was transferred to the Safety Department. An arrangement was made for a technician to come out to inspect the product.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned without causing injury, but there was a potential electrical hazard indicated by the tripped breaker and electrical smell.

incident_description:
On Sept 14th I utilized the self-cleaning unit on my Kenmore gas stove using the 2 hr setting. Upon completion of the cleaning I noted burn marks on the top of the oven door and the section under the control knobs of the stove top. Also noted are burn marks near vents at the back of the stove top.
Sears was contacted on 9/18/19  and stated Sears would send a representative out to check the stove at a cost of $89.00. The above note parts would cost about $269.00. These burn marks I believe are caused by a defect in the stove and is a great safety issue.
justification: The incident describes burn marks caused by a defect, but there is no mention of injury or death, so severity is 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as defects can occur but are not guaranteed in every use.

incident_description: It is hard to see in the picture, but the metal blade of my my Pampered Chef spreader actually cut through the plastic and came back at my hand.  I felt the plastic break and was able to move my hand fast enough that the metal blade did not cut me.  I briefly looked at this site and could not find other complaints on this item, but I am worried that it could hurt others if this was to happen to them.  Have there been other incidents with this product?  Can I return this item?
justification: The incident involved a near-miss with no injury, and no other complaints were found, indicating it is unlikely to happen frequently.

incident_description: Front of glass door on whirlpool oven exploded. Oven was not in use at time. Glass went all over kitchen hitting myself on back of legs without injury. Hit other household member as well with small cuts to great toe.
justification: The incident caused small cuts to a household member, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common.

incident_description: On August 29th 2019, after my 13 year old daughter finished Broiling some nachos, and turned off our Bosch Double oven.  Before closing the door, she heard a pop, and notice a 3" high flame that was growing inside upper part of the oven, be hind the display screens.  My 17 yer old daughter and I were in the Kitchen, and fortunately my 13 year old quick action, to run and get the fire extinguisher allowed us to stop the flames before they breach the confines of the oven electrical compartmetn.  Had my daughter not noticed the small flame, and shut the oven door, all three of us would have left the kitchen leaving the oven unattended, where the fire would have quickly grown and penetrated the heat shielding and ignited the cabinetry.  I called Bosch that day.  they sent a tech to the home on 9/5/2019.  He determined when diagnosed he found burned spots on leads for broil element & terminal block. Control module, 2 sets of harnesses & broil element were burned severely, need replacement. He state the issue was bad wiring.
justification: The incident involved a growing flame inside the oven, which was quickly extinguished without injury or death.

incident_description: The knob design has from the first week led to unintentionally turning on burners. I was shocked to see how easy it is to do this just by leaning over or brushing against the front of the range top. The bottom of the knob protrudes beyond the front edge. So far, the bell that sounds has saved us from starting a fire, but WE ARE AFRAID THAT THIS DESIGN ISSUE WILL CAUSE A HOUSE FIRE. The knobs can be easily redesigned to avoid this by tapering the lower part of the knob. But this is currently a hazard. We love the range, but are concerned about its safety, not just for us but for other customers too.
justification: The design flaw leads to unintentional burner activation, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her 12 cup programmable coffee maker which she purchased from a retailer in Portland OR J.C. Penneys Cluckman Town Ctr. November 23, 2019.

incident_description: In June of 2015 I bought a brand new Samsung Fridge to replace an older model that was too big for the space,  By Summer of 2016 the icemaker had quit, and I had to replace 2 right door bins ($35 each) that simply shattered. incident_description:
We started experiencing problems with our 2015 Samsung French Door Refrigerator, model RF260BEAESR, in April 2019. We started noticing a loud banging noise that happened for about a week, then stopped. Shortly after, the temperature did not feel cold, even though the display registered 35 degrees. That's when we bought a refrigerator thermometer. On any given day it would read anywhere from 58-65 degrees! We called a repairman who came and assessed the problem.  Over the course of the summer, he was at our house 4 times. Replacing the defrost heater didn't fix the unsafe temperatures, so he replaced the drain in the back. That seemed to solve the problem for about a week. Then, it was right back to high temperatures and spoiled food.
Over the course of the summer, I had to personally defrost the ice buildup in the refrigerator 3 times. My repairman, [REDACTED] from Walters Appliance Repair, defrosted it twice. Each time that was done, the fridge would get significantly cooler, but it never lasted more than two weeks. During that time, I had to repeatedly haul bags and bags of food to and from my neighborÃÂs refrigerators multiple times, and live out of coolers in my kitchen. We went on two vacations this summer and both times, we left thinking the fridge was fixed, only to come home and find that all of the food in it had spoiled, because during that time the temperatures rose to unsafe levels again. I have thrown out so much food itÃÂs unbelievable.
The most upsetting part of this whole ordeal is how it has negatively impacted my children. My toddler drinks milk three times a day. Before I knew that something was faulty with the fridge, I was giving her milk like usual. She vomited twice and had severe diarrhea several times during a two-week period. Once we discovered the problem and stopped using milk from the fridge, her gastro-intestinal issues stopped. My son also experienced gastro-intestinal distress from eating bacon and eggs from the refrigerator, before we were aware that the temperatures were not safe. Both of them were miserable during that time. Not to mention, my husband and I were both affected as well. We experienced stomach upset, heartburn and indigestion, and heachaches. We are lucky that the worst of what our family experienced was severe vomiting and diarrhea, and that nothing far worse happened. Because it easily could have with food that had not been kept properly cool.
justification: The incident caused multiple instances of severe vomiting, diarrhea, and other gastrointestinal issues in both children and adults, indicating injury due to spoiled food.

incident_description:
The left rail of the dishwasher's upper rack broke as I was sliding the rack our to load additional dishes. This caused the left side to suddenly drop several inches. Had the strain on the remaining right rail caused it to fail simultaneously, the entire rack would have fallen ~3 feet to the floor. Most of the time a top rack's load includes glasses. Had the rack fallen these glasses could have shattered spreading broken glass shards that could easily have injured adults and children in the kitchen. 

Upon inspection of the failed rail it was noted that the rail consisted of two pieces that had been tack welded together. Tack welding destroys the protective coating on the steel. Bare steel is subject to corrosion. These tack welds had then, predictably, rusted and failed. 

The manufacturer initially declined to replace the rail. The dishwasher had been in service for 16 months and exceeded the warranty period. With pushing the manufacturer agreed to pay for the part but not the labor. Additional pushing eventually led to the manufacturer replacing the part and covering labor. 

The concern is that this is an inherently very poor design. This failure so early in the product life would seem to support that notion. This is a part number used across several brands and many models; all ticking time bombs.
justification: The incident involved a rack failure that could have led to injury from broken glass, but no actual injury occurred. The design flaw suggests a high likelihood of recurrence across multiple models.

incident_description:
We have very hard water, so I began using [REDACTED] in our dishwasher.  We also have Corelle dinnerware.  After several months of using [REDACTED] as an additive with our dishwasher detergent packets, we noticed that the previously smooth rims on the Corelle felt rough.  

I suspect that the Corelle is being dissolved by the [REDACTED].  Now small fragments of the Corelle edges flake off when touched.  No injuries have occurred, but they would certainly be possible considering the flaking glass-like edges.

Over time, [REDACTED] has removed some of the printed logos, etc, from our glassware, so perhaps I shouldn't have been surprised.  However, there are no warning labels on the [REDACTED] and nothing in the Corelle product information or warranty information that suggests that products like Lemi-Shine should not be used.

I contacted Corelle via their website to report what has happened and to ask if this was a known issue.  The only response I got was an offer of a discount if I want to buy another set of Corelle.

I suspect that our Corelle is now more prone to breakage, since the integrity of the edge has been compromised.  I'm also concerned that someone will get a glass fragment from handling the dinnerware.  We've used Corelle for decades and nothing like this has happened before.

In my opinion, both the Corelle and the [REDACTED] should have some kind of warning label. [REDACTED] has no directions as to quantity to use, so it is possible that using less would avoid this problem.  I am concerned that this is happening to other people who may not realize what is going on and how dangerous it could be.
justification: No injuries have occurred yet, but the flaking glass-like edges pose a potential risk of injury.

Food was spoiling and I have a child with medication that needs to be kept at a stable temperature. This is terribly unsafe. incident_description:
Our BlueStar Stovetop Model RGTNB364GSS's griddle started to light itself and heat up when turned completely off this weekend.  This is a gas stovetop and we heard the sound of gas turn on and the flame start-up. As this was the weekend and Bluestar was not open to call, we shut off the gas and electric to the stovetop so it would not turn on by itself while we slept. 

We turned the gas and electric back on to cook breakfast the next morning and the griddle immediately lit up again on its own. We checked the knob again to ensure it was completely off and shut off the gas and electric again.

Today, Monday morning we called BlueStar customer service and were told it was probably a runaway thermostat and that it would need to be replaced.  They said there was no way to turn off the thermostat, so when it malfunctioned this could happen. After a little discussion, they agreed to send a new thermostat to be installed. 

I am concerned that there is no way to turn off the thermostat. Unlike the range burners, which don't receive gas when the knob is turned off, the griddle's gas supply, is controlled by the thermostat, so that when it has an issue the griddle can not be turned off.  It seems like when the knob is turned to off it should shut power to the thermostat, or there should be a switch to turn off the griddle/thermostat.  This is a huge burn/fire risk and we are hoping this can be fixed.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stovetop that could lead to burns or fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

The element was glowing red and the H was illuminated on the cooktop indicating Hot Element.  No other lights were on.  I pressed the Off button and the element turned off.  I then pressed the lookout button. It illuminated indicating the cooktop controls were locked out.  The next incident, after a power flicker,  my wife walked to the kitchen and felt radiant heat coming from the cooktop.  The right rear warming element had turned itself on.  The H was illuminated indicating Hot Element.  She pressed the off button and it apparently turned off.  The warming element does not glow thru the glass cooktop.  She was able to press the lookout button and it illuminated.     There was no damage as we do not place anything on the cooktop as instructed by Whirlpool user manual.  We feel this is a hazard as the cooktop turns on by itself even though the lookout button is pressed. 

This is a Whirpool model WCE97US6HB00 glass, electronic cooktop.  Serial number D84007992.

incident_description:
My husband and two kids (18 & 21) had left for work, leaving me and our 4 cats alone in the house.  I walked into the kitchen and noticed a strong smell like melting plastic, which I now believe to have been a fairly large and concentrated quantity of R134a.  By the time I figured out what it was, I had developed a horrible headache.  To save my cats, I ran through the house opening all of the windows and turning on all of the fans.  I barely made it out the front door as I was beginning to lose consciousness.   For two days I continued to vent coolant via the pores of my skin.  When I got outside, I contacted my protection plan to file a claim.  The warranty service told me the soonest they would be able to send someone out would be two days. I knew that by then, the coolant would be gone, and I feared my claim would be denied.  So, I went out and purchased a coolant detector.  Even though all of the windows had been open, and all of the fans had been on for several hours, I was still able to detect coolant in my kitchen and at a slightly higher concentration behind my refrigerator.  I took a video of this.  For two days, my skin would set off the detector as well, which was interesting.  My refrigerator has continued to operate normally, even up to the present day, and there is no evidence of any leak in the cooling system.

There is a lot to this ongoing saga, and I am not sure which details are going to be most important.  I am filing this claim because I want to keep everyone safe from what I have come to believe are the unsafe practices of the professionals provided by the manufacturer of my refrigerator to maintain my refrigerator while under warranty.  These practices have turned my refrigerator into a life threatening presence in my home.  There have been at least two smaller releases of coolant since the initial one.  When I spoke with my warranty service, I was told that over charging with coolant is standard practice for failing compressors in order to get a few more months of service out of them.  My compressor was newly installed, but I only had 3 months left on my warranty, and I suppose it is possible the manufacturer wanted to make sure the new compressor made it to the end of my warranty.  I actually saw the technician overcharge the cooling system, and asked him to take the excess out.  He denied that he had done this.  I complained to the warranty service and they sent him back.  When he came back, he continued to deny it.  I decided to believe him and go on with my life.  Six weeks later, the incident described above occurred.  When a compressor is replaced within a closed system, service valves are installed, and the system is no longer a closed system.  The high side service valve also functions as a pressure release valve.  Once the pressure release valve releases, it loses its integrity.  The technician did not show up two days later.  Instead, I had to wait two weeks.  I let the manufacturer know that the release valve was going to need to be replaced.  As expected, when the technician finally arrived, he denied that there had ever been a release of anything.  I asked him to measure the coolant charge.  It was slightly below the low end of spec.  I wondered how it got that way, when there is no evidence of any leak in the cooling system.  He offered to recharge the coolant.  I told him I did not believe it was safe to recharge the coolant without replacing the release valve first, because once they go off, they lose their integrity.  He told me that since there was no evidence that the valve had released anything, he could not replace the valve.  I showed him my video.  He told me he would see fluorescence if there had been a leak.  I told him there was no leak.  There was a release of gas, similar to the release of gas through the valve when he connected his equipment to it, and there was no fluorescence from that.  He continued to deny that there had been any release of coolant from the cooling system.   He left without replacing the release valve or charging the cooling system.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe headache and temporary loss of consciousness, indicating injury (severity level 3). The recurrence of smaller releases suggests a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
We had just placed 2 potatoes in the microwave to begin cooking them. After about 3-4 minutes of cooking, my wife noticed some odd sounds coming from the microwave, while it was still running. She was 5-6 feet away, and didn't think much of it. Around 10 seconds later, smoke began billowing out the front top vent of the microwave, and out the back vent to the outside. I quickly recognized the smell as an electrical fire as I have smelled that many times due to the nature of my job. I stopped the microwave, shut off power to the microwave, and called 911. The fire department was there within 5 minutes. They shut off the breaker to the microwave circuit, and began checking the temperature of the microwave. Their FLIR camera found the location of the arcing and burning was from the top right side of the microwave where the electrical components were, so they began removing the top front vent panel of the microwave to access that location. Once that was removed, and the metal cover that blocks the electrical compartment, they could visually see (with the naked eye and with the temperature of components with the FLIR camera) locations on the top and side panels where the components had experienced arcing and slight burning. The Fire Chief said we were very lucky that the event stayed contained and did not spread to the cabinets around it, as the wood cabinets directly next to it were very hot as well when they arrived. 

Description of Risk or Harm ÃÂ Electrical fire originated inside electrical component bay on top of microwave. Two sources of oxygen are present to this area 1) rear of microwave passes through the wall with exposed drywall and other combustible material before exiting the home as a vent to the outer wall/siding, and 2) top front of microwave has a vent that directly comes in contact with cabinets on top and side. If electricity of the microwave is not removed immediately when the electrical fire began, spreading of the fire either direction would result in the house/combustibles catching fire which would lead to a fully engulfed house fire. Refer to your previous recall for similar microwaves - https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2016/whirlpool-recalls-microwaves, and you will see that the incident that occurred to us matches this to a T, and also fits into the incidents section, which I have attached below.

The investigation performed by the 3rd party appliance technician proved that this was a fire caused by a manufacturers defect, and the fire chief that inspected the damage concluded that the lone reason that this fire did not spread was due to the electricity being removed immediately. If both of these reports are correct, which there is no reason for them not to be, this is a SAFETY HAZARD for each home that contains one. I urge you to reconsider this as the risk of harm is the complete loss of house and possibly life. 

Thank You,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire that was contained without injury or death, but required emergency response.

Caller stated that she contacted the company and they advised her that her unit was no longer under warranty.  Caller is concerned that this range could have caused a house fire and that the matter should be investigated for a recall.

July 31,2019


CONSUMER  PRODUCT  SAFETY COMMISSION
To whom It May Concern:


The defective stove burner was out of manufacturer warranty but still under MasterCard's Extended Warranty. The defective part is called a Switch lnfin.  I have conducted a further inquiry as to this burners problem. Much to my dismay, I found some troubling results.


Its seem the burner overheating problem is not all that uncommon! This particular part is used in a number of electric stove models including smooth tops and by several brand manufacturers including the maker of my stove, General Electric! This part has been used for a number of years as well.


This is a serious defect! When the defective burner unexpectedly switches itself to high heat, if not noticed immediately, can and will cause a fire!  In my case, had I not been close by, a shallow grease pan would have ignited very quickly!


Kitchen fires are horrible and very dangerous not only to residents but property as well. I find it difficult to believe in this age of rapid technical invention a better design of this part is not possible.  I really do not care how it affects these manufacturers bottom line.  Customer safety should come FIRST! It is your responsibility to make sure this happens.

[REDACTED]

incident_description:
My GE Profile dishwasher was started on a wash cycle in the evening.  We awakened in the early morning to the smell of burned material.  We initially could not find the source of the smell.  Smoke was beginning to fill the area around our kitchen, although our smoke alarm did not go off.  We then isolated the smell to the dishwasher, opened it, and discovered that the heating coil mechanism on the bottom of the unit was still "on" / hot.  The entire contents of the dishwasher, including components of the racks, utensil rack, and washing components were melted beyond recognition.  During the heated dry cycle, the heat coil never shut off.  In opening the door, we shut off the heating.   At that point, much of the melted material was in a liquid state, further demonstrating that the heating coil never shut off. 

The granite countertops were hot to the touch, and the surrounding cabinetry was hot to the touch.  Thankfully, we were at home and could recognize this danger before a fire was started.  We had no idea that this could happen.  Most families end their evening by loading and running the load of dishes.... often hitting the start button on their way to bed.  This seems incredibly unusual, but incredibly dangerous.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I purchases a Hamilton Beach 1.7L Electric Kettle for my wife to boil tea water, with an automatic shut-off as soon as the water boiled, to prevent injuries or the kettle boiling dry. At home, I filled the kettle, closed the lid, as pictured in the instruction (hearing and feeling a "click" as the lid closed), and turned on the power switch at the bottom of the kettle. After a few minutes, the water came to a boil, but the kettle would not shut itself off. I tried this sequence several times with the same result.

 I returned the apparently defective kettle to the store, bought another one, tried it out at home, and had the same problem of it never shutting itself off.

 I phoned the Hamilton Beach customer support number and was told I had squeeze two buttons on the top of the kettle's lid with my thumb and middle fingers, while pressing down on the lid with my index finger to get two small plastic latches on the right and left underside of the lid to engage properly with the top rim of the glass kettle. If only one of the latches engaged, I would still feel a "click" when I closed the lid, but the auto shut-off feature would be inoperable. (None of this was explained in the instructions, which simply indicated to close the lid before turning on the power.) I tried this sequence and indeed the auto shut-off worked when the kettle began to boil!

I then explained and demonstrated the procedure to my wife. Unfortunately, my wife is in the early stages of a common condition in older people called Parkinson's Disease. This disease causes gradual loss of sensation, muscle strength, dexterity, and agility. My wife tried to follow my instructions, squeezing the left and right buttons as she pressed the lid closed. She felt a "click" and turned on the power.  the kettle began boiling slowly, then progressed to a rapid, full, rolling boil, without shutting off. Realizing her mistake, my wife reached for the lid to squeeze the buttons and push down again, so both rather than just one latch would become engaged. However her hand was quickly scalded by the very hot steam spewing out  the spout and around the edges of the lid. 

In retrospect, when the kettle continued boiling,  it would have been safer to turn off the power switch at the bottom of the kettle than to touch anything on the lid to re-engage the auto shut-off function. However, I could imagine many others making the same mistake when the auto shut-off unexpectedly didn't work.

I understand that the lid should be latched when the water is heating, so that very hot water does not splash out of the kettle when one is trying to pour it slowly into a cup or pot. If the kettle can "tell" when the lid is only partially latched, why not prevent the heating element from even coming on -- rather than disabling the auto shut-off safety feature? 

If, for some reason, this arcane procedure must be followed to enable the auto shut-off function, it should at least be explained in the owner's manual.
justification: The incident resulted in a scald injury due to the kettle's defective auto shut-off feature and unclear instructions, which could reasonably occur again under similar conditions.

incident_description: I had preheated my Kenmore Elite gas oven, model 790 7751 3800, to 350 degrees and placed a roasted chicken in a small baking pan in it to reheat it. After about ten minutes, I opened the oven door and looked at it and thought maybe it needed a little longer, so I gently closed the door. I stepped over to the sink, about 3 1/2 ft away, when I heard a loud pop, I shrieked and turned to the oven and saw the glass on the oven door shatter and small pieces of glass fall to the floor. I did not have shoes on so I got some sandals that were near by and immediately turned off the oven. After standing there in amazement for a minute or so, I carefully opened the oven door , which was difficult because the broken glass was wedged in the frame, to see if something exploded in the oven. Nothing exploded. I also smelled around the oven after it was turned off to check if there was a gas leak. My husband was in the family room and came over to investigate and see what may have caused it. We could not determine what happened. Neither of us smelled gas, so we proceeded to begin sweeping up the small pieces of glasses that were all over the kitchen floor (I am still finding small pieces around several feet from the oven and my husband cut his foot on a very small sliver of glass that was on the floor, the next day). We were careful to use a vacuum attachment to remove the pieces out of the warming drawer and a wooden skewer to remove what remained of he glass from the frame as well as under the stove.  This all occurred during the time when we were supposed to be sitting down to dinner, so it was very aggravating and unnerving, considering the safety issue. I ended up with some cuts on my fingers trying to remove/clean up the glass on the floor and frame to prevent my son and our cats from injury. I also was unsure if we should eat the chicken considering the small pieces of glass that were everywhere, so we opted to eat out. I have an extended warranty but it states that it excludes replacing glass. I just found several [REDACTED] videos and articles today online that mentioned that there have been hundreds of other cases of this occurring with the Kenmore Elite range 790 models, so I wanted to add my terrifying experience to the data. I'm also appauled that there is no recall by Sears and that ranges older than one year are not covered for replacement.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts) from glass shards and a safety hazard, but no severe harm or death. The occurrence likelihood is high given the reported hundreds of similar cases.

incident_description:

The ones that are all polyester melt, burn through and subsequently burn the user. This can happen on the very first use when removing something from the oven. The fact that the fabric melts and can stick to the user's skin while hot makes them doubly dangerous.
The cotton covered ones burn through the thin cotton fairly quickly and then, again, melt through the polyester and burn the user.
Since the purpose of a potholder is to keep the user from being burned, I believe no potholders containing polyester should be sold. As well as being unsafe, it is a real waste of resources and energy to make and sell a product that is certain to fail very quickly. I know these are inexpensive items, but there is no reason they should be ineffective and dangerous. Thanks!

justification: The potholders can melt and burn the user, causing injury, and this can happen on the first use.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the recall for the Thermador dishwashers should be expanded because he had the same issue as the units that were recalled. Also, there might be other units that are not in the recall but have the same issue.

On 6/14, the dishwasher stopped in the middle of the wash cycle. When the technician came out to repair the unit, he discovered that the junction box had burned. The power cord and the junction box had to be replaced.

The consumer contacted the firm on 6/14. He received a call back from the firm today (6/21) and was advised that the unit is not included in the recall and is out of warranty.  

Dear Sir or Madam,
I'm writing to provide some additional information to the report number referenced above. I've also attached additional documentation with the signed report / consent form with this email. This additional information includes a copy of the repair invoice, picture of my model information, expanded recall information and a Consumer Reports article related to the recall. Clarifying and / or expanded information for the initial report draft also includes the following:
a.	The model number is incorrect on the initial report you sent - I've hand marked the correction on the attached document. A couple letters were transposed.
b.	The symptoms of my product failure were identical to the units under the expanded recall (my unit was not included in that serial number range) -The unit stopped mid-cycle towards the end of the wash cycle and prior to the drying cycle. The unit lost all power and would not function. I turned off the breaker as a precaution.
c.	The repair of my unit was identical to the repairs made to units under recall - The attached repair receipt shows the identical repair to what BSH is doing for the recalled units, including replacement of the power cord and junction box. I would point out that the junction box was clearly burned when the technician removed it. There were bum marks, melted plastic and a distinct aroma of melted plastic / wire insulation (I do not have a picture of this). Fortunately, the
burned area was contained within the junction box and did not spread to the drywall around it. Attached is a picture from the internet of the recall repair parts, matching identically to what was replaced on my unit.
d.	The BSH  factory technician knew what was likely wrong before actually looking at the unit - When I described the symptoms of my dishwasher failure the technician said he "had a very good idea of what was causing this." He did check the serial number to confirm this unit was not included in the expanded recall. When I asked additional questions, he commented that he had seen this before. Additionally, he went out of his way to make me feel like I was getting a good deal. He mentioned that the power cord was much cheaper because of the recall and would give me a deal on the labor as well. While this was much appreciated, it piqued my curiosity and prompted me to look online at the recall details and repair required after he left. The similarities in both the symptoms and repair are too identical to be dismissed as mere coincidence.
e.	This unit was installed properly -This unit was purchased at Best Buy through their high-end Pacific Kitchen & Home store. It was also installed by their certified technicians. It is exceptionally unlikely that my issue was the result of an incorrect installation. Best Buy is an authorized retailer of Thermador appliances.
f.	Thermador has been totally dismissive about this issue -When I contacted Thermador customer service following the repair, they appeared unconcerned that this could have caused a fire and were dismissive regarding the uncanny similarity of my issue with the existing recall. They were also unresponsive after my initial call on 6/14/2019.  I was told that I would be contacted within 48 hours after my initial call to further discuss the issue once my case file had been reviewed (that Thermador case number was [REDACTED]). I never received a call back and contacted them again on 6/21/2019 only to be told dismissively "sorry, the unit is out of warranty."  I indicated at that time that I would be reporting this to the CPSC and filing a small claims suit related to this issue.

Please feel free to contact me should you have any additional questions related to this matter. My obvious concern is that there are additional Thermador dishwasher units not covered by the expanded recall which present the same fire hazard.  Thanks for your assistance with this matter.

Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction causing a burned junction box, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have owned a Nutri-Ninja blender for three years. it is the type that has a blade assembly that "screws on" to the top of the cup you drink out of. 
I've been meticulous about washing it really well after each use. It goes in the dishwasher each time and I also wipe it with a rag.
About a month ago, I started noticing some black flakes in my smoothies. At first I thought it was the fruit I was using. But, then I noticed that the black flakes were consistent, regardless of the fruit I was using. 
I washed the blade assembly very thoroughly and put it through the dishwasher multiple times.
It turns out the black flakes were mold growing inside the assembly of the blades! There is a rubber gasket that's about a half-inch wide that's shoved deep inside the blade assembly. Moisture gets inside this area and mold has been growing! (It doesn't look like I can upload a photo, but, I have a picture of this, it's super gross!)
I had no idea that this was supposed to come apart. There was nothing in the manual which says to wash this gasket. And, it took me using two screwdrivers in my workshop to pry that thing out, so, it's not something that an average person can easily fix. 
Shark Ninja Inc should be forced to recall these blenders or offer a new design on the blade/top of the cups so that people can actually clean these. At the very least, there should be a warning in the manual with instructions on how to clean this obscure part of the product.
This poses a health risk. Both my nine-year-old daughter and I drank smoothie after smoothie filled with mold as a result of this poor design. Something should be done.
justification: The incident describes ingestion of mold, which can cause health issues, though no specific injuries are mentioned.

incident_description:
The gas range is a Maytag Gemini and is about 15 years old.  

It was plugged in but turned off. No burners or oven were on.  We heard the clicking sound of an igniter for about 5 seconds (igniters are used to create spark to light a particular stovetop burner). We then heard popping noises and smoke began to emanate from the stovetop on the right side of the range top by the burner controls. I opened the upper oven and there was fire visible to the right side through the clear lens for the oven interior light, again on the side proximal to the burner controls. I was able to move the range and unplug it; however the smoke continued. I had a fire extinguisher on hand, but the fire went out on its own after about 10 to 20 seconds. There was a distinct smell of an electrical fire in the room.  I turned off the gas valve leading to the range. After 30 mins to be sure it do not reignite, I inspected the range by removing the back panel and lifting the top. Under the top where the burner controls are located one of the controls had charring of wires and soot from the fire. The insulating bracket around the oven also had charring or soot visible.
 
The images show the layout of the range and the specific controller that was burned.  Charred wiring is visible as well as charring and soot in the surrounding area. The burner control is a combination of gas valve and electric components, presumably used to activate the igniter for that respective burner.

We were very fortunate to be home at the time or it could have potentially been destroyed by fire had the fire spread beyond the range itself.  At home were also our three pets, plus a neighbors pet. I plan to dispose of the unit (not sell it) as it is clear fire hazard due to this incident of spontaneous ignition.

2/2018 Caller is reporting that he is experiencing problems with his gas range.  He stated that the burners when turn on does not ignite immediately which causes gas to escape and then ignites with combustion.  Caller stated that this incident has been occurring intermittently over a few months. 

Caller stated that this gas range has a manufacturer design flaw.   He stated that the retailer or manufacturer was not contacted he feels that they would not respond to him.  Caller feels that this gas range could cause an explosion and should be recalled.

This range, with its obvious design flaw, was recently purchased - new. 5 gas valves, one for each burner, are located on the face of the unit, all easily within reach of a 3 or 4 year old.

To properly ignite any burner, the user must turn its valve to the ''ignite'' position and wait to hear ignition take place. But it is very easy to skip over ''ignite'' and have the valve land in the ''High'' position before ignition takes place. If this happens, gas will never ignite, but will continue to flow at maximum volume from the burner until the valve is turned to the ''ignite'' position (perhaps causing an explosion) or through ''ignite'' to ''off '. Which may not be until there has been an injury or death This range should be recalled asap.
justification: The gas range's design flaw poses a significant risk of explosion, which could lead to death, and the issue occurs intermittently over months, making it likely.

justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing smoke and melting plastic, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Submitter is reporting that he is continuing to have the same issue with his product. 
The product was previously repaired by the firm under recall 09-33.

The stove randomly cuts on while all of the knobs are in the off position. Submitter says that the right rear burner turned on by itself and got very hot. Submitter had to unplug the stove in order to shut it off.

Submitter believes this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The stove turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My new 4 month old LG refrigerator dispensed 12 small white sharp pieces of plastic into my drinking glass when I was getting ice from the external ice dispenser.  The smallest piece is 8mm x 14mm x 0.5mm.  I opened up the ice maker inside the door and the ice tray that makes the ice was dislodged and 1/4 of it was missing.  We use the ice make daily and there was no issue prior to this incident.
justification: The incident involved plastic pieces contaminating a drink, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This is the email I sent to Hamilton Beach Customer Service describing the problem:
     I am writing to you once again about a problem with this coffee maker leaking clear water on the full pot side. In September 2018 I wrote to your customer service to describe the problem I had with the coffee maker. You told me to cut the wire on the coffee maker, send a picture. and you replaced the coffee maker. I love this coffee maker but it seems to have real leakage problems. These photos are of the bottom of the new coffee pot that was sent, so you can see the serial number This model of coffee maker seems to have a defect that is well known on the internet because I found several YouTube videos about how to fix it. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jnuk68pLqpo  This link is not the only one of the videos on how to fix the water leakage I found just by searching for this coffee pot on the internet. I even tried to do the fix, but my leakage must be up in the closed area and while I was willing to take screws out of the bottom to see if it was something I could easily fix, I will not take the whole side off the pot. We use this pot almost every day and although I can still use the K-cup side, I need to make a full pot a couple of times a week.At this point I believe I deserve a refund. Hamilton Beach Brands Inc. 49976 Flex Brew 2-Way Coffee Maker
$115.71

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
Home Phone: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a leaking coffee maker causing water damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Samsung Refrigerator (Model # RF24FSEDBSR) has known factory defects affecting the ice box and the ability for the refrigerator compartment to stay cold. The ice box has cracked allowing plastic to enter the area where ice forms causing potential choking or ingestion of plastic pieces. The warming temperature of the refrigerator will lead to food spoilage which could lead to inadvertent consumption of bacteria infected food. I am concerned for my safety as well as my family's safety.
justification: The incident involves potential choking or ingestion of plastic pieces and consumption of bacteria-infected food, which could lead to injury.

incident_description: I purchased an Oster Toaster/Oven, model #TSSTTVMNDG, from Amazon around January 21, 2019.  Upon first use several things became evident. When Broil or Bake is selected there is no indication when the oven has reached the desired temperature. The indicator immediately goes to 450 or 350 degrees but the unit is cold and beginning to warm to the desired temperature. There's no way to tell when to insert the pan to begin cooking. When the desired temperature is reached the unit shuts off unless a time is manually set which must include the time to reach the correct temperature (an estimate) and the approximate time to cook the item which, of course is an unknown factor. The dangerous part of the unit is the rack upon which a pan is set.  It's tapered toward the back of the unit. When pulled out to check the done-ness of the meat, it tilts down unexpectedly toward the open door potentially spilling the contents of the pan on the person using the unit. There's no support for the tapered part of the rack. I notified Oster about the problems. They sent a replacement with the same problems and I've been emailing them since trying to get a return authorization and refund.
justification: The toaster/oven's design flaw poses a risk of spilling hot contents, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Electrolux oven EW30ES65GSI with serial number NF416Z9420.  This is a very dangerous oven. It will turn on one of the burners in the middle of the night on high.  They have recalled the same ovens with different serial numbers than ours but will do nothing about ours. There are lots of these out there
that could burn up ones family. Please help to keep this from happening. Once this happens you can only turn your breaker off to stop the burner from running wide open.
justification: The oven turning on a burner unexpectedly poses a significant fire hazard, potentially leading to injury or death, but the description does not confirm any actual incidents or injuries.

incident_description: I was boiling water in the  Martha Stewart Stainless Steel pot (HF10115 ) and the pot began to spark and from the bottom and then leak out the boiling water onto the stove. This pot is fairly new condition and piratically caused a hazard.
justification: The incident involved a pot sparking and leaking boiling water, creating a hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire microwave trips the circuit breaker when someone accidentally pulls the door while the oven is still on. I called Frigidaire and they said it's normal. It does't happen with any other microwave I have used in my life. Tripping the circuit breaker implies a shorting in the circuitry and a fire hazard. 

Model: FGMV176NTF
Purchased: October 2018
justification: The microwave trips the circuit breaker when the door is pulled while in use, indicating a potential electrical issue, but no injury or damage is reported.

incident_description:
We own a 15-unit apartment complex that was built in 2004. The original construction used Hotpoint stoves. We have replaced approximately 4 stoves already and have ordered 2 additional stoves. 

The ovens turn themselves on at random intervals when the control is in the off position. This has resulted in 1 fire already. We have two stoves out of service right now, due to them turning themselves on.
justification: The incident has already caused one fire and multiple stoves are malfunctioning, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description:
I have had this Magefesa water kettle for about six months--I bought it at Ace Hardware. I use it once a day to boil water on my gas stove to make coffee. 

Yesterday morning, after the water boiled, I was pouring the water over the coffee grounds when the handle of the water pot let go--unexpectedly and with no warning. It could have been dangerous, since the water is boiling hot.
justification: The handle failure could have caused injury but did not in this instance, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern, I have e-mailed Mr. Coffee customer service as well
as making phone calls that hardly get answered.
Let me get right to the point. On 2/16/19 the handle broke on my Mr. Coffee
French Press style coffee maker as I was in a seated position. Consequentially,
most of the hot coffee spilled into my lap causing burns and also to my left
hand.
The main injuries weÃÂre mostly on my inner thigh and caused pain when

I tried forwarding all the e-mails sent back and forth, if needed I will send them
1 at a time if I have to.
