incident_description:
Caller stated that the knobs of the range is easily turned when someone brushes against it.  Once it started a fire, a few times the gas escaped into the home for several hours.  She stated that a cleaning crew was at her house while she was away, she  came home to find that the gas had been on for hours.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that they are unable to fix the sensitivity of the knobs.

Caller feels that this unit is a safety hazard and should be reported/recalled.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks and a fire, posing significant safety hazards, though no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
The mold or mildew is inside the door panel and cannot be easily cleaned

The consumer indicates that she saw black flakes floating in her cup of water. The consumer checked her refrigerator and noticed that there is mold in the door panel where ice and water is dispensed.

The consumer states that since October 2018, she has had ongoing chronic sinus infection, difficulty breathing, fatigue, headaches, and dizziness, and believes the refrigerator is the cause.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative she spoke to informed her that they could send a Service Technician to inspect the unit however they would not pay for the service if the mold was not due to a defect in manufacturing.

The consumer plans on keeping her refrigerator for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The consumer reports health issues potentially linked to mold exposure, indicating injury (severity 3). Mold in appliances is a known issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
My landlord purchased a basic gas range for my home.  When using the stove the first time, I turned the knob to light it.  After a few seconds I realized that the knobs were not made like every other stove I have used - meaning the ignition is usually immediately next to the off position.  This one is opposite.  All 4 burners have the ignition at 180 degrees from the off position.  Getting to that point releases gas (between off and lighting).  If a child turns the knob (or someone accidentally does) gas will fill the room quickly before anyone realizes it.  Clicking sound of the lighter does not occur until the 180 degree point.  I am shocked that this range is legally on the market.

GE JGBS30REKSS
justification: The design flaw in the gas range could lead to a dangerous gas leak, posing a risk of fire or explosion, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Cooking on electric stove top. Put water in pot and turned heat to 8. At boil, turned down to 4 and put half bag of peas in, then covered and went to living room. After 5 minutes, I smelled burned metal, ran to kitchen to find pot melted to element (white hot, not red hot). Turned off burner and moved pot to unused burner, leaving a trail of molten metal. I've never seen an infinite control switch fail in such a way...
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove causing property damage but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Bought a Cuisinart DTC-975BKN Programmable 12 cup coffee maker.  I had read other reviewers Amazon complaints that it tends to spill over and has caused burns.  I thought it was user error, so I read the directions carefully but it happened to me too.  The coffee maker does not safely brew more than 8 cups.  The coffee maker kept spilling over, then the third time used, just stopped working.  Amazon exchanged it, and the replacement did the same thing.  

I got second degree burns all over my left hand trying to catch it before it made a big mess.  Other Amazon reviewers reported the same thing.  

I contacted Cuisinart, and after many many email exchanges, their best offer was to have me ship the coffee maker to them, have them examine it, and if they determined that it was defective, they would send another replacement.  I told them I thought it was a defect in design, not in manufacture, so an examination would not help, and they design needed to be improved to make it safe.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, indicating an injury, and multiple reports suggest the issue is common.

incident_description:
The product of reference is Aroma Housewares. Model #AWK -210SB Gooseneck Kettle. The kettle sits on an electric hot plate configuration to heat the water placed within. The attachment of the handle is the concern. It is not mechanically attached. And I apologize but I believe is some kind of electronic weld, if you will. 
IÃÂve already sent a request previously (5 times ) to the manufacturer through their website, but I have had no response. THIS IS MY REPORT TO THE MANUFACTURER. I have your lovely gooseneck kettle for less than one year. When using it, full of hot water, the handle popped off (it was not attached by a screw to make sure there was what I would call a belt and suspenders in design) while I was transferring it full of ÃÂboilingÃÂ water to pour into my French press. You can tell how the unit was attached, the upper two nodules (of this perceived weld) barely had anything connected. This is a product defect. I am fortunate that I was not scolded with hot (boiling) water as most of it came out onto the floor. And I am fortunate that my dog was not injured either.  When it fell it couldÃÂve easily damaged the floor but it did not, it broke its own fall and dented the base and part of the plastic piece of the base cane apart as well. I am requesting a new kettle from you, the manufacturer.  By the way in your description of the product to talk about safety. I would be concerned about using the word safety when the handles of these units can pop off. 

First of all, IÃÂm fortunate I was not hurt, and was hopeful that the manufacture would care enough to contact me concerning this matter. If I wasnÃÂt quick enough to jump out of the way, this hot boiling water could possibly had burnt me  significantly , broke small bones in my foot or severely hurt a pet or small child who frequently our at our feet, not to mention possible property damage. And hereÃÂs an opportunity to (I hope) make the Manufacturer pay attention to safety that they tout so much on their website. ItÃÂs honestly a simple manufacturing defect, it happens. But they should recognize the errors and Rectify any issues or concerns of consumers have
justification: The handle detachment incident occurred without injury, but the potential for severe burns or other injuries was high, making it a significant safety concern.

incident_description: I purchased the Gozney Pizza Oven, ROCCBOX (www.gozney.com) from Williams Sonoma March 8th. I used it for the "FIRST TIME" yesterday, May 14th, with great and not-so-great results. My first pizza came out great. After letting the oven cool down, I attached the manufacturer's Carrying Strap, lifted the unit off the table top, and the handle gave way; one side of the handle tore away from the main strap. The unit weighs approximately 20 kg. The main strap is designed to be wrapped around the oven & held in place with Velcro. The handle is sewn to the strap. As a result of the handle failure, the oven fell. Thankfully, neither I or anyone else was hurt!! But, the Ceramic baking surface within the oven is broken into 3 pieces and who knows what other damage the unit may have sustained. I have taken photos of the incident so that you may see the results from the strap failure, if they are desired. There is obviously insufficient stitching securing the handle to the main strap, it is no wonder it failed during it's first usage!!
justification: The incident involved a product failure causing damage to the oven but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the evident design flaw in the strap.

incident_description:
We ran the dishwasher earlier in the day and noticed a burning plastic smell while the dishwasher was running but were not able to figure out where it was coming from.  After dinner while cleaning up, we filled the dishwasher and started the dishwasher (Maytag Dishwasher model: MDB4949SDM2) running and were sitting around the kitchen table talking.  After a while we started to smell the burning plastic smell preparing dinner and we were going to start looking for the smell when we noticed black smoke coming out from under the trim around the top of the door where the controls are located.  We heard several pops and sizzles followed by the display flashing and then the circuit breaker tripped.  we felt the door and the control area of the door was hot.  The smoke reduced but continued for several more minutes.  The circuit breaker was turned off and we ended up pulling the partially washed dishes out of the dishwasher.

On 13 May 2019, we called our insurance company and reported the incident.  Our insurance company indicated that we should report the incident to Maytag customer service.  Maytag Customer service transferred us to their Safety Department and they are sending out a factory service rep to look at the dishwasher to evaluate the dishwasher and repair it if possible.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical issues but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
We moved into this home in August 2018.  From the first time we used the cooktop, we noticed dangerous issues.  Unless cooktop is locked, simply setting an item on the cooktop can cause it to turn on/off or adjust the temperature setting of any of the burners.  This has proved to be dangerous on several occasions.  I had a dish sitting on the cool cooktop,  I set a pot onto the stove to prepare for cooking something at a later time.  I went about my business, only to smell something burning.  The pot had turned on one of the burners and heated up my dish to the point of making a "crackling" sound,  The was extremely hot and now has permanent burn marks on the bottom.  I worry this will happen when I am leaving the house and I will not catch it!  The controls on this cooktop are easily set off and dangerous.  There are similar reviews of this issue on the GE Appliances web page for this item if you were to buy it new.  Others have found the same dangerous issue.  
Model JP5030SJ1SS / Serial VF712285Q.
justification: The cooktop's malfunction caused a pot to overheat, resulting in burn marks but no injury, and similar issues are reported by others.

incident_description: A family was relying on the Baby Breeze to mix powdered formula for their infant.  When they presented for their babyÃÂs well child check it was noted that the baby had lost significant weight.  When parents returned home they realized that the Breeza was not mixing correctly leaving diluted formula which was bejng fed to their infant. Once the mixer was no longer used the infant quickly regained weight.
justification: The infant suffered significant weight loss due to diluted formula, indicating harm (injury) from the malfunctioning device.

incident_description:
In January 2018, the handle of my Bodum espresso maker caught on fire. I put it out quickly and was angry about the poor design. 
Today, May 11th, 2019 I finally used it again, despite being careful to keep handle out of the way of our gas stove flames, but it caught on fire again and melted so it is no longer useable.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury, and it happened twice under similar conditions, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Our Jenn-Air gas cooktop exploded. Model JGD8430ADF.
justification: The description mentions an explosion, which implies a significant incident with potential for injury.

incident_description: While using pan on gas stove on rivets popped off and metal shot off.  Luckily no injury
justification: The incident involved a pan malfunction but resulted in no injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
The coffee mug warmer was being used in the normal fashion set to a temperature of 190 degrees.  It contains a touch pad to set the temp and to turn the unit on and off.  When the unit is off the on/off icon is red; when the unit is on, that icon becomes white and the set temperature (in this case 190 degrees) flashes white also.

After drinking most of the coffee over the course of about one hour, I touched the on/off button and the icon turned red.  After at least an hour later, I picked up the cup to find it was still quite hot and the burner was still emitting heat. I was not injured or burned as the contact was brief.

This event occurred on 4 May [REDACTED], and a similar event occurred about two weeks earlier.  After the first event I contacted Cosori who offered to replace the unit.  I continued to use it in the meantime away from family just to be safe and to confirm the original event was repeatable.

Although I was not injured, the unit allows setting a temperature up to 220 degrees and could thus result in a serious burn.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning coffee mug warmer that did not turn off as expected, but no injury occurred. The issue was repeatable and could potentially lead to burns at higher temperatures.

incident_description:
Our KitchenAid Artisan 5-qt. Stand Mixer with Sku#: 06373165 Size: 5 QT is dangerous.
The motor has difficulty mixing even slightly stiff batter and the motor whines. The pin near the connection between the head of the mixer and the stand slips out (not completely) and you need to slide it back in so that the head doesn't fall off. It's a miracle that I noticed it slipping out and was able to slide it back in. With the pin out the entire head (which probably weighs around 40 lbs.!!) can fall off and it could be deadly!!  But the most dangerous of all is the fact the bowl becomes lose from the place that you screw it in on the bottom of the stand and can fly off in the middle of mixing!! That could cause a really really serious injury.
I was trying to stabilize the bowl that was becoming slightly dislodged while mixing and my hand almost got crushed between the bowl and the machine!!!
justification: The description indicates a near-miss incident with potential for serious injury or death due to mechanical failure, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Keurig K-elite is about 5 months old.  Set to turn on automatically at 6am so water is hot for morning coffee.  Automatically turned on this morning and began pumping hot water without any buttons being pushed or any warning, continued until it emptied reservoir - overflowing 8 oz cup that was in the machine and machine catch basin, flowing out over counter.  Water was hot, fortunately reservoir was not full.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing hot water overflow without injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his electric stove that was already in his home when purchased during 2015 as a safety hazard.

Sometime around beginning of November problems began when the stove began heating up when it was turned off and rising to higher and could not be adjusted to the lower temperatures.
He is reporting this issue as a fire safety hazard and he is asking that his unit also become recalled for safety reasons.
There are no injuries being reporting 
He has contacted the manufacturer who referred him to this hotline
justification: The stove is malfunctioning and poses a fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
(02/24/2019) The consumer stated that his wife had ice in a glass with soda. When she drank the soda, she got a piece of plastic in her mouth. After pulling the ice maker apart, the consumer discovered that the plastic came for the ice maker. The shield in front of the auger had broken and pieces of plastic was in the ice.

There were no injuries.
justification: The consumer found plastic in the ice but there were no injuries, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: THe burner on our Samsung gas range would not shut off.The knob was frozen. this is while the burner was on . There was no indication of any problems before. in fact we lit the burner as directed no problem then about 20 minutes later we tried to shut the burner off but the knob wouldnt turn. I even tried pulling knob off and turning the shaft but it started to twist it would not turn. I had to turn the gas line valve going to the range off.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but was safely resolved by turning off the gas line, with no injury or damage reported.

incident_description:
After I made a pot of coffee, The Krups Savoy coffee maker I have, overheated and partially melted the plug and there were some small flames coming out of it as well.  I immediately unplugged it.  Thank goodness I was in the kitchen when it happened.

This is obviously a very dangerous thing to have had happen.
justification: The coffee maker overheated, melted the plug, and produced small flames, but no injury occurred as the user was present and unplugged it immediately.

incident_description: Amazon Basics electric kettle malfunctioned, burned the plastic around the unit and filled the house with smoke.  Unit is supposed to have automatic shut off.  Fire department called to clear house of smoke.  They agree it was an appliance malfunction.  Cooktop that kettle was sitting on is now unusable until melted plastic can be removed.  I have photos of the pot and still have the pot for evidence
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning kettle causing smoke and property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: When we were baking, we noticed to oven light wasn't turning off when the door was closed. We ignored it, finished cooking, and went to bed. My daughter went down later to get a snack and noticed a burning smell. She opened the oven and found it still hot, even though it was turned off. When she closed the door, sparks and embers flew out. She had to extinguish them around the kitchen. I woke my husband, so that he could pull it out and unplug it. We then found soot marks on the cabinetry, and the button and wires melted.
justification: The incident involved sparks and embers, requiring extinguishing, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: While using a KitchenAid brand oven with model number  KFED500ESS, one of the knobs controlling the heating elements broke off while attempting to turn the knob to the off position. This prevented me from safely turning off the oven heating element, and could have resulted in injury or property damage. After turning the element off using a wrench, I looked at the knob to identify why it broke and it appears that the knob is made of a very thin plastic, which broke under the heating-cooling stress of being near a high-temperature area such as the spot above the heating elements of an oven. This is a danger, as KitchenAid has defective control knobs on their ovens which can prevent the users from safely turning them off if the knob were to suffer a failure. The age of this oven is only 14 months, and was pruchased new from the store, previous ovens I have owned have never suffered a failure such as this even when going beyond 10 years of frequent use.
justification: The incident involved a broken knob preventing safe oven shutdown, but no actual injury or property damage occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue is linked to a specific defect in the product.

incident_description: Whirlpool microwave oven melted the plastic cover located in the inside roof of the microwave while popping popcorn. The plastic was hot and melted causing a string of melted plastic to get on to the popcorn bag which was grabbed and melted plastic burnt hand. There is now a hole on the inside plastic cover and can no longer use the microwave.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from melted plastic, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description:
We recently purchased a new home that included the Frigidaire Self Cleaning Range Model: ffgf3054TSB 

This range looks exactly like the one listed in the recall list with the model: Frigidaire Gas Ranges Model # LGGF3043KFM .

We experienced exactly the same problem as described in the recall from 2012. This resulted in a minor explosion within the oven that blew open the door and an alarm from our CO detector. The local fire department filed an incident report and ordered the stove shut off.
justification: The incident involved a minor explosion and CO alarm activation, indicating potential for injury but no reported injuries.

incident_description: My LG Gas Range ultra burner continues to extinguish while on a low setting.  It is only after noticing the smell of gas in my home that I am aware of the issue.  The oven is less then four months old and has had the issue almost since the day I received it.  I have had 3 service calls from LG and yet the problem persists.  Although the oven is well within the 3 year warranty and clearly a safety hazard (the service man himself has recommended I do not use the oven!), LG refuses to replace the oven or issue a safety recall
justification: The incident involves a gas leak hazard with no reported injury, but the repeated occurrence and service calls indicate a persistent issue.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her microwave dom May 5, 2007 - was purchased from retailer possibly 10 years ago,.
The microwave has arced on several occasions beginning just after purchased then around one week ago it caught fire after arching with flames around six inches high with flames contained inside. 
The caller's husband threw a pot holder over the flames and smothered them then she threw baking soda over the extinguished flames.
No injuries 
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but she may contact them
justification: The microwave caught fire but was contained and extinguished without injuries, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description:
Samsung elec. glass top range     ne58k9430------ne58m9430

I purchased this range in sept. of 2018 from Best Buy in Honolulu  Hi.

This product has a dangerous design flaw. Last Saturday, for the fourth time since I purchased this unit, I returned home to find one of the on- off knobs on high and a dangerously hot kitchen. This has happened three times previous to this incident. It is caused by the design and placement of the range knobs. These knobs are very large and protrude out in front of the range. Because of this, a person walking close by and brushing a knob can accidentally turn the knob to high. This is the fourth time this has happened in the 6 months I have owned this range. I consider this to be a potentially very dangerous situation. I talked to Samsung about the very serious matter several days ago and i was told that they were sorry but there were no other knobs available.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the range knobs turning on accidentally, creating a dangerously hot environment, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Waffle Maker model WM 45024 by Kalorik.
Severely Burned 4 finger tips first time used.
product is very unsafe where batter is poured in, no labels stating do not touch or hot.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to four fingertips, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The lack of warning labels suggests this could happen to others, making occurrence likely.

incident_description: My cooktop came on all by itself.  Even with the lock option on.  It could have started a fire if something were on the cooktop like an oven mitt.
justification: The cooktop turning on by itself is an incident with no injury, but it poses a potential fire hazard if flammable items are left unattended.

incident_description: My husband was using the chef knife from our Calphalon knife set that we received in June of 2015 as a wedding gift and as using to slice a calzone the blade dismantled from the handle completely and flew backwards. I have never seen this happen with any knife IÃÂve used in the past. While looking into this knife set it looks as if there was a recall I was not aware of in 2017. IÃÂm nervous to use any of the other larger knives in this set after seeing no sign this would happen with this one.
justification: The knife blade dismantled but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The Tupperware brand microwave pasta cooker is oblong, approximately 12"x7"x5". The lid fits loosely on top with nothing to secure it to the base of the product during use, it also has holes one one end to act as a steam vent and for use to drain the water from pasta once cooked. I used this product according to the manufacturer's directions to cook a single portion of pasta, and I used oven mitts when I took the cooker out of the microwave after the pasta, holding it with the steam/ drain vents away from me. As I moved toward the sink, the water splashed back toward me, came through the space between the lid and the product base and caused a blistering burn on my abdomen. 

I have used this product for a few years, and this is the second blistering burn I have had while using the product according to the manufacturer's directions. The first occurred about a year ago, causing redness over an area that was approximately 6" in diameter, with a blister covering most of that area. The most recent incident happened on 4/23/2019, and has a smaller burn area. 

My concern is that this product is marketed as a convenient way to make pasta and could be used by more fragile populations (children or the elderly) for whom a burn could be devastating.
justification: The incident resulted in a blistering burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the user reports this is the second such incident in a few years.

incident_description:

incident_description:
My LG electric range LRE3083ST has a malfunctioning burner: when the back left burner or the middle back warming burner is turned on, the front left burner also turns red, heats to high, and the HS (hot surface) indicator light turns on. If the back burners are on low, the front burner turns to low as well. It cannot be turned off unless the back burner is turned off. This began as an intermittent problem a few months ago, and now it happens every time we use the back burners. This is a safety issue. I have not burned myself, but there is risk of fire or burns from this malfunction. 

A second problem is that the oven fails to heat correctly, whether on "bake" or "convection bake." It heats consistently lowly when set at 350, measuring only 200-300 on my analog oven thermometer, even after an hour "at temperature." (I am reading the temperature through the oven door, so it's not due to heat loss with an open oven door.) When I increase the heat to 400 or 425, sometimes it climbs to 275, but at other times it has overshot to 500. 

I contacted LG and, with some tenacity, got a response from the LG Executive Services Team that I could repair it at my own cost or receive a 15% rebate off the purchase of a new unit. I am not happy with that response because this is clearly a safety problem, not wear/tear. As a homeowner, I have purchased plenty of replacement appliances when the older one fails. This is different.

The unit was manufactured October 2014 serial # 410KMVP0F423. I do not have proof of purchase because the unit was in the house we bought 18 months ago.
justification: The malfunctioning burners and inconsistent oven heating pose a clear safety risk of fire or burns, though no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
On March 22, 2019 while loading the aforementioned dishwasher top rack for cleaning during the early morning on March 23, 2019, the top rack two front support "bosses" failed without warning throwing some glass ware onto the ceramic floor causing said glassware to shatter on the floor. This is the second instance of this type of failure the other having occurred in October 2017 while the tray was being pulled out for unloading. In this instance only one of the top rack's bosses failed since the owner was able to quickly grab onto the rack thus preventing the rack's contents from spilling on the floor. In doing so, the owner's finger suffered a minor cut. In the current failure, only minor scrapes and scuffs on the finger and hand with no open wounds.

Luckily for the owner an extended warranty was purchased along with the KitchenAid Dishwasher and the top rack was repaired on Monday March 25, 2019. Whirlpool customer service was contacted on
Friday evening to no avail. Owner was placed on hold for an extended time interval. Consequently the phone conversation was ended by the owner. On Saturday March 23, 2019 contacted Whirlpool customer service and informed them of the catastrophic top rack failure. They were also advised of the previous failure and extended warranty coverage. Contacted [REDACTED] customer service who eventually made arrangements for the Monday repair.

Top Rack failure was very similar to that which occurred in October 2017. The support bosses apparently failed by them being pulled away from the material substrate. This is shown in Figures (8-16} where the part location that was on the bracket showed material separation. Repairs in both instances were made using the same Whirlpool part Wl0546503 Mfd. date 09/14/2019 for current failure compared to that part that failed that had been Mfd. on 10/11/2017. 

Note that Whirlpool warranty covers rack failures for a period of S years. Last 4 years are for parts only.
The implication here is that Whirlpool apparently knew that the racks apparently did not last. Now the question remains is what happens after 5 years? The MTBF for both failures is about the same. May 2016 to October 2017 for the first failure and October 2017 to March 2019. Accordingly, Whirlpool apparently has no desire to prevent future failures by either changing materials or design. Both the new bracket and older brackets apparently share the same design and material. Other Whirlpool dishwashers have apparently a more robust design and or material since KitchenAid does not universally used these parts across their entire dishwasher product line.

Note that this dishwasher was a replacement for a 6 year old one that previously had a burned up circuit board that took over 2.5 years to fail based upon the overheated electrical insulation odor that was present after each wash cycle. Kindly note that owner was certified Weapons inspector after training at [REDACTED] high reliability soldering school so owner surely is aware of what overheated electrical insulation smells like. Repair to replace the board was well over $300. Whirlpool offered a $300 rebate on a new dishwasher. All paperwork was filed via certified mail and to date Whirlpool's response as to the whereabouts of the rebate fell into an abyss of silence. The owner has had other Whirlpool kitchen and laundry products fail and I am wondering just why there is no remedial action by consumer product safety commissions to remedy the situations.

In conclusion, owner feels that Whirlpool Dishwasher is a ticking top rack failure time bomb. It had two failures and replacement parts appear to be that which had been initially installed and failed twice. Previous failure parts were sent back to Whirlpool for analysis. To date we have not received any analysis information. 

Question to the CPSC is what will be your actions to correct the situation before someone really gets hurt from this defective product. Having a Whirlpool warranty to correct top rack failures truly does not protect the customer from the obvious safety issues with this dishwasher. Do we have to wait for corrective action to be taken when someone is really hurt because of this top rack failure? Kindly provide an answer. Please note that based upon the MTBF limited data, it is anticipated that another top rack failure will occur within the 5 year warranty and surely when the warranty expires.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts and scrapes) from broken glass, and the description indicates a recurring issue with the dishwasher's top rack failing, suggesting a likely chance of recurrence.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Cooktop Model FEC30S6ABF Serial NF74823198.  During normal operation, the front main element stopped cycling and remained on. The unit failed to turn off when placing the heat control dial to the off position.  If the element does not cycle it emits very high temperature that would likely in a matter minutes could cause any thing on the cooktop to catch fire and longer exposure could cause the cooktop to become brittle or internal component begin to melt causing fire hazard or an electrical short with same result.  The circuit breaker had to be used to turn the unit off as stated the dial control no longer was in any control of the element. Subsequent attempts to use one of the other 3 elements of cooktop was also not an option. When engaging one of the other elements, which seemed to function correctly, also powered the main front element as well and was stuck on high without being able to turn off once engaged.  The internal circuitry is done poorly in my opinion.  Parts fail eventually, knowing that the limiters will fail and the hazard of one element staying on all the time should dictate internal wiring precluding turning on one element from physically allowing any other elements to be powered as a simple safety precaution.  If all 4 elements were to engage without cycling, the risk of fire I think would almost be certain.
There is a recall for similar cooktop types as my model made by Electrolux(Frigidaire) during the same time frame mine was manufactured for a very similar problem, but were not included in the recall. Obviously they should have expanded in my opinion.
justification: The incident describes a high risk of fire due to the cooktop element not turning off, which could lead to injury. The likelihood is high given the description of the malfunction and the recall history.

incident_description:
Re:  LG Dishwasher Fire

On March 3, 2019, during a dishwashing cycle, our LG dishwasher (model LDF6810ST) started a fire that filled our home with smoke and could have caused extensive harm to life and property had we not been nearby. The dishwasher began popping, and smoke poured out of it in larger and larger amounts.  Fortunately, I was in the kitchen at the time, and my wife was nearby.  We were able to quickly use our fire extinguisher to extinguish the electrical fire inside the dishwasher door.  By that time, our house had filled with smoke and we had to open many windows and doors fully to clear it out.  By the time we put out the fire, we could not safely breath in our home.

This situation was frightening, and could have had terrible consequences for our home, ourselves, and our pet. We were able to minimize the property damage by acting quickly, but the experience was shocking. 

I emailed LG the details above on March 4, 2019.  I then called LG on or about March 5, 2019, and asked to speak with their executive office for complaints given the seriousness of the product failure.  At my suggestion, the individual I spoke with in LG's executive office scheduled an inspection of the dishwasher at our home.  She also told me that someone from LG's product team would be contacting me to discuss the incident.  She also offered me 15% off a new LG dishwasher.  I rejected this offer out of hand, which I felt was offensive and inappropriate under the circumstances.

The inspection occurred on March 8, 2019.  An LG inspector came to our home and inspected the dishwasher.  He confirmed that the cause of the fire was that the electrical circuits in the door to the dishwasher had started an electrical fire.  Although the individual I spoke with in LG's executive office promised that someone on LG's product team would contact me after the inspection, LG never contacted me to compensate us for our losses, or even to understand more about the fire caused by LG's product, a product defect that could threaten the lives and property of other LG consumers.

The inspector failed to remove (or even unplug) the dishwasher.  Therefore, when several days ago we turned the the circuit breaker for the power to the dishwasher back on, the product again began to smoke and smelled like an electrical fire.  We had to race to turn off the breaker to avoid a second fire.  Why would a company leave an unsafe product in a home after inspecting it, rather than removing it?  This additional failing of LG's product-safety compliance program is unfortunately emblematic of LG's overall failure to take this matter seriously (including their failure to contact me to gather more information about the fire after I twice put them on notice of the incident--by email and in the above-described phone call with LG's executive office).

I request that you investigate this matter and inform me of the action you take as a result of your investigation.  Other consumers need to be aware of the risk of this product.  I also ask that you request that LG contact me to discuss this matter, as they promised me they would do (but never did).  I do not understand why a company whose product caused a fire in a residence would not contact the consumer to, at a minimum, gather more information and cover the consumer's losses (which are small compared to the damage to life and property that could have resulted).  It seems reckless not to do so.  For this reason, I also believe the CPSC should investigate whether LG's product-safety compliance program is sufficiently robust to protect their consumers.

Regards,
[REDACTED}
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported, placing it at severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the repeated electrical issues with the dishwasher.

incident_description:
I bought a GE oven from The Home Depot a few months ago. 

serial #: tl217241p
Model: jgb720sej4ss

From day one, when you turn the oven on, you smell gas for a few minutes.  

Exposure to natural gas through gas leaks can be harmful. It may lead to explosions and pose serious health hazards that are sometimes even fatal. Small gas leaks accumulate over a period of time and add a significant amount of pollutants that stress the immune system and other bodily functions. According to the National Library of Medicine, "If a natural gas leak has occurred and is severe, oxygen can be reduced, causing dizziness, fatigue, nausea, headache, and irregular breathing." Gas leaks can cause serious harm to plants, thus affecting the environmental ecosystem as well.

Though it's under warranty, GE won't come and repair or replace the oven.

Upon further inspection, 4 of the 5 knobs had the same damage, the knobs' plastic  mating to the steel range posts had cracked completely through.  We were fortunate that we discovered the other breaks, as we could have easily found ourselves unable to shut off lit burners, or with the gas on but unlit with the knobs indicating that the burner was off.  Samsung is aware of this problem, it has been amply discussed on their own product support forums, and they have dismissed this obvious safety issue as a "cosmetic problem".  This is a hazard that could easily have been prevented or remedied, and the list cost of the knobs approaches the cost if purchasing the stove.  Samsung appears to be permitting this safety hazard to continue to avoid bad press and generate revenue from equally shoddy replacement parts.

incident_description:

incident_description:
The consumer has a safety concern about her Kitchenaid cook top. On 3/3/2019, the consumer stated that she had a power outage. When the power came back on, two out of five burners on her cooktop were on. The cooktop was not in use when the power went out. The consumer was also advised that turning the circuit breaker off and on resets the circuit board. She was also advised that they did not consider the incident a fire issue.

 The consumer contacted the Safety Department again to advised them that the product is unsafe and wanted a refund and the product removed from her home.

The consumer still has the product but is waiting for Kitchenaid to contact her to arrange for the removal of the cooktop.

incident_description:

She stated that this has been ongoing since  installation, although she was not really aware of what was happening.  She stated that she read online numerous reports of this incident. Caller feels that this is a safety hazard especially if there are children in the home and should be reported.

He stated that the unit would not automatically turn off causing the incident, the microwave eventually stopped but they were unable to open the door. Consumer is concerned that this microwave is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description:
My KitchenAid Gas Kitchen Range Gas is a serious gas leak hazard!
I own a new KitchenAid Gas Kitchen Range 6.25cu 5-burner. Model: KSGB900ESS. There is a very serious issue with the way the gas range knobs are located and engineered. The knobs are round, about 2 1/2" wide and 1 1/4" deep. The way the knobs stick out makes it inevitable that walking by the range will cause them to turn slightly. The detent in the off position does not prevent this movement even with the lightest of brushing by.
Here is the issue. That slight movement, even a fraction of an inch, cause the gas to turn on without lighting it. It is not noticed by any sound or haptic feedback so now you have gas leaking into your house. Now the smell will eventually come to your attention but if not or if you leave the house that gas buildup could cause and explosion. I believe this is a serious enough issue that a manufacturer recall/repair is needed.
justification: The description indicates a serious gas leak hazard that could lead to an explosion, which poses a risk of death or injury if unnoticed.

I told them it was unsafe and they said it was user error. I asked them to replace it with a different safer product and they said, no.

incident_description: Despite the "Loc" feature being turned on at all times when our gas range is not in use, the burner knobs turn on unintentionally at the slightest bump. On many occasions this has happened, and thankfully we have to this point realized when the gas was coming from the burner on most occasions fairly quickly. However, one occasion we did not realize for quite some time and all ended up with severe headaches. This is a HUGE safety concern. If we do not catch the gas turning on like this, we could go to bed and our house fill with gas. This is totally not acceptable! I have reached out to LG regarding this safety concern, and was told that unless we received physical injuries or property damage, there was nothing they could do. LG knows there is a problem; I have researched this particular model of range and found that hundreds of others have had similar experiences as we have had, and others have ended up having fires as a result of this faulty model of LG gas range. As a parent, I cannot sleep soundly at night knowing that this range is so dangerous. I find myself constantly checking the range & knobs just to make sure that gas isn't coming out of the burners. Again, this is happening while the so-called "Loc" feature is on.... also would like to note that with the "Loc" feature on, barely turning the knobs counterclockwise causes gas to come from the burners as well (this occurs without even pushing the knob in... you are supposed to have to push the knob in and then turn clockwise to get the gas to turn on when the the Loc feature is OFF... gas should not be coming out period when Loc is on nor when counterclockwise. Obviously this is either a design flaw or defective ranges). Waiting for a serious personal injury or property damage is not an acceptable response from LG!! The extreme headaches from the gas was bad enough! My family's safety is number 1 to me. It's a shame that LG does not care about its customers' safety.

Upon the attempt to open again to remove the second food item, the oven had a big spark, and a made loud and continuous buzzing sound, that of an electric shock. Fire ensued but after closing the door, the circuit breaker tripped, burning pieces of metal fell from the top of the oven to the food on the oven rack. We left the door closed until the fire stopped. 

After the oven cooled off, we inspected it and saw that the metal holding the top heat element was burnt and broken. We saw pieces of metal broken on top of the flatbread we were cooking and other pieces that were shot towards the oven door made a small dent in the glass and the edge of the oven door.

This situation could have resulted in large fire as the oven is mounted on wooden kitchen cabinets or body injury considering that the metal that was shot out was so hot that it left chip in a glass and damaged the edge of the door, both designed to withstand very high heat. Should a piece of such metal get in contact with the skin at such velocity and heat, the injury could be devastating.
justification: The incident involved a fire and hot metal pieces that could have caused severe injury, though no actual injury was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as such events are not common with proper maintenance.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range with Convection. Color; Bisque. P/N or Model No. from back of Range: 316492239.  Purchased approximately February, 2013 from Sears store. 
On Saturday, March 9, 2019, the circuit board across the top back of my range Short-Circuited. I heard static and several flashes of Flame came up the back of the range. This happened after I had been using the range at 450 degrees for approximately 1 hour and then pressed the Stop "button" to turn off the oven. 
The Range screen immediately started flashing an Error Code, F10 I think, and the letters ERR and emitting a loud beeping sound.
When the firemen came they immediately pulled the range away from the wall and unplugged the power cord. They confirmed that the problem was definitely the circuit board. The back metal panel over the circuit boards was still extremely hot to the touch. The problem was not the power cord. 
I contacted Sears Consumer Services on March 11th. They did not seem interested in the fact that one of their Kenmore ranges had short circuited and potentially could have easily started a major fire in the kitchen and home. We were extremely lucky it did not start a fire After I left the kitchen. My husband is a double amputee and we would have had great difficulty removing him quickly from his back bedroom to a safe distance rom the house.
justification: The incident involved a short-circuit and flames but no actual fire or injury occurred, and the situation was controlled without harm.

incident_description:
A GE Profile Series Front Control Slide-In Gas Range was delivered by Jim's Appliances, Boise, ID, to my home on December 18, 2018. It was  connected to the gas line in my kitchen by a licensed plumber on 12/19/18. Subsequently, during a clock replacement service call, a technician from Jim's Appliances noted that the gas valve for the broiler was not working. Another was ordered by service at Jim's Appliances and replacement of the defective valve was done on March 20 at 9am. After the new valve was installed the technician tested it and all other gas-related functions. He left, and a short time later I smelled a hint of gas. Figuring it was residual odor after the gas to the stove was turned back on, I checked the burners in the stove and broiler by briefly turning them on, then off. The odor went away and did not appear to return. I considered lying down for a nap but decided to go to a neighbor's instead. About an hour later I returned home. When I opened the front door I was hit by a strong, acrid smell. I suspected it was coming from the stove, possibly the broiler burning off some factory residue. When I opened the oven it was hot although all of controls were in the off position. I had not left it on, I knew that, but I couldn't figure out what was causing the oven to be so warm. I left it for a few minutes to see if it would cool off. Maybe, I thought, the newly connected wifi (the technician had me connect it when he was there earlier so the clock would keep time) had started the oven while I was gone. I had not touched the app, and there was no reason for this to have happened, but I don't understand such things so that was one of my considerations. I called my neighbor to ask her to come over to help me figure out what was going on, she didn't pick up. While I was waiting to call her back, I looked at the oven again and heard a sound that resemble that of a pilot light flickering. This range doesn't have a pilot light though, so I was still at a loss as to what was going on. I could not see a flame or any source of the heat that was still being generated. I also noticed that the air in my house had begun to take on the look of a sheer blue veil and I felt a bit foggy myself. I called my neighbor again about 10 minutes later and she told me to get out of the house. I met her in street and asked her to open my front door to check for a smell. Once she got a whiff, she had me call 911 for Fire & Rescue. I also called the service technician and requested that he return to the house. 
The FD arrived within minutes. The technician not long after. Apparently FD called [REDACTED] Gas and their man arrived next. 
According to Boise FD, my house was filling up with carbon monoxide and their was a fire burning in the manifold inside the range. The seal on one of the gas distribution pipes going to one of the burners was leaking and the flame from the oven or broiler had been drawn back to the manifold, igniting the gas when I turned the burners on before I left the house.  The gas to the then the entire house was turned off. The gas tech pressure checked the lines in my house and found all of them to be in good working order. The service technician tightened the Control Valve that had been leaking .The situation appeared to be under control and the firefighters, gas tech and service tech were about to leave when the gas tech decided to check the Control Valve one more time. It was still leaking even though it had been tightened multiple times by [REDACTED], the service repair technician. The gas to the range was turned off, for good this time. The Boise FD filled out a report. The [REDACTED] Gas technician left me with a Notice of Hazardous Condition regarding a Defective Control Valve. The service technician from Jim's Appliances also mentioned the range's Defective Control Valve when he called GE while he was still here. 
The range was removed from my home March 21, 2019, by Jim's Appliances. I received a check for the full amount, including taxes and my cost of initial installation. 
I am filing this report because I am deeply concerned about this range and what appear to be several flaws in it's design and/or parts. But for the fact that I decided to visit a neighbor rather than take a nap, I might well have succumbed to carbon monoxide poisoning. Whether or not my house would have gone up in flames or as a result of a gas explosion is not in my purview. I leave it to those who read this to make that decision.


I am hopeful that by filing this complaint an investigation into the possibility of a dangerous Defect in the Control Valve on the GE Profile Series 30 Slide-In Range will be undertaken. The outcome for me could have been very different and I want to make sure no one else is put into the same dangerous situation as I was.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak and carbon monoxide buildup, which could have led to severe injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Gold oven [manufactured / home built around 2001/2002] was used early in the day Feb 21, 2019 to cook chicken at 350 degrees F, was turned off by me when done. After I left home at 2:30pm that same day, the oven turned itself on [no one home], created intense heat, and was likely minutes away from starting a kitchen fire when I got home.
I left home at 2:30pm to teach 2 lessons [my job], arrived home at appx 4:05pm to my home filled with smoke, chemical stench, and the oven blazing hot, the broiler coils lava red, and smoke coming out of the oven. The house was filled with a fine smoke and irritating smell that caused coughing for several hours. The oven had turned itself on while I was away, and was heating to what I estimate to be over 1000 degrees F. The oven showed self-cleaning mode and 'locked'. However, the door was unlocked, smoke was coming out and singed the top of the oven door, and WOULD NOT TURN OFF! I tried several times with the off button, the temp button to lower the temp, but it would not turn off. Talked with a friend who told me to run to the breaker box and turn off power to the oven/range, which I did. I kept the breaker off, and it is still off. Whirlpool sent a factory technician [Fields Factory Service, Orlando, FL] to check this out. Interior components of oven were severely damaged. When the technician turned on the power to the oven, the oven again turned itself on -- was already warm by the time he made his way into the kitchen, without having touched the oven control panel. Once again, it had turned itself on. He discussed that with Whirlpool, who did not authorize repair [I assume due to the extensive internal damage caused by the malfunction]. The breaker power remains off, and I am trying to resolve with Whirlpool Safety Team.
I am fortunate that I came home when I did and that the two pets inside the home were still alive. I firmly believe that the intense heat building in the oven, from the malfunction while I was not home, was minutes away from starting a kitchen fire while I was away. Whirlpool is not cooperating with replacement of the unit as of this writing on March 24.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual fire or injuries occurred.

incident_description: While following the directions on some [REDACTED] for making jerky I left the door slightly ajar while the oven was dialed to 200degres F. The directions indicated that the cook time should be approximately 1 hour. Luckily I checked after 30-40 minutes and found that my oven was very over heated .The knobs on the front of the oven were melted and one cupboard next to the oven had a charred door. This oven is clearly a fire hazard if the door is left open even a crack. In looking at the LG information that I could find, many cases of melted knobs were discovered. The very least that the Manufacture should do is send all purchasers a warning that never should the door be ajar and all future products should have a red flag warning in the operators manual. In addition the door on new products should carry a sticker with the same warning. Notification to the LG web site left me sure that this problem would not be corrected and they would not even pay for the melted knobs to be replaced. While my wife would like a new kitchen this is not a good way to get one. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted knobs, charred cupboard) but no injury or death, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) given the reported cases of similar incidents with the same oven model.

incident_description: Tonight while using my LG lmv1683sb microwave oven. I noticed something black dripping from the top plastic plate inside the microwave. Not thinking much of it I wiped it down and continued. After about 30 seconds I noticed flames coming from that same spot. I stopped the microwave and after waiting until I felt it safe to open the microwave I saw a hole in that place from the drip and the flames. This was very terrifying, my home could have burn down and being disabled may not have noticed in time. Because of fire being inside of microwave my smoke alarm didn't go off.
justification: The incident involved flames inside the microwave, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My wife and I purchased a Viking oven form Gerhard's Appliances in Doylestown, Pa. on December 1, 2018. Within two weeks the door hinges broke keeping the door from closing. I complained and insisted that Gerhard replace the oven.They refused stating that it could be fixed. A couple weeks later the door was repaired. Immediately afterwards, the flames on the stove began to act erratically, blowing sideways instead of upwards. I continued to insist that I wanted a new oven, but Gerhard's refused again stating it was a Viking problem. Viking sent out a repair man from [REDACTED] Appliance. The repair man said nothing was wrong with the oven. I emailed videos and pictures to Viking and they acknowledged that there is a problem. They sent another repair company out, [REDACTED] Appliance, who did the repairs on the door. Again the repair man found nothing wrong. It wasn't until we were cooking something in the oven that we noticed that when the internal fan kicked on, the flames on the stove went out leaving unlit gas to escape into the kitchen. We noticed that the higher set flames were distorted and again operating erratically. I contacted [REDACTED] Appliances and Viking and and a repairman came out on March 20, 2019. He acknowledged the problem and contacted Viking. Viking told him that they are aware of the problem, but there is no current fix. I informed Gerhard's of this and again demanded that they take back the oven, and again they refused. Stating it is passed the return period. Today, Viking informed me that they have a fix for the problem, but it will take several weeks to get repaired. I informed Gerhard's of this and told them if this repair does not work, I want my money back. Gerhard's refused. Now, for the next several weeks I am using an oven that can blow up my house, but Gerhard's and Viking don't care.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that could potentially release unlit gas into the kitchen, posing a risk of explosion, but no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: The Oven in my kitchen has been releasing CO for the last three months. A gas technician came yesterday and detected a CO concentration in the house of 28-30. He stated that it is very dangerous. I have been living in this house since January and my roomates and I many times requested some control mainteinance control since every time we turn the oven on it smells gas so badly. After several requests in the last two months the house company decided to let a maintainance guy for the gas. While he was detecting for gas concentration in the air, he actually revealed high concentration of CO. Unfortunately, my roommate didn't ask for something official and written to prove that. That's my concern. In conclusion, my roommates and I have been exposed to CO at least for two months in an indoor space.
justification: High CO concentration was detected, posing a serious health risk, but no immediate injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
While using the Frigidaire microwave, our circuit breaker trips if you open the door of the microwave while it is running. The door of the microwave is misaligned. It has been misaligned since we purchased the microwave but other than being difficult to open & close it had not caused any other issues until recently.  In addition, 3 or 4 other neighbors in our newly developed neighborhood are also experienced the same problem.  All of our homes were built around 2017 by the same builder who used the same Frigidaire vendor.  

The point of the safety switch on the door is to keep the microwave from operating when the door is misaligned or partially opened.  No-one wants to be exposed to microwave energy while heating up their coffee.  Microwave energy is harmful to humans.

The model no. is FGMV175QFA
Serial # KG71320601
Manufactured in March of 2017.
justification: The microwave's misaligned door causes the circuit breaker to trip when opened during operation, posing a potential safety risk but no reported injuries.

This is an ongoing problem.
The consumer is reporting a second issue at this time that there are metal shavings coming out in his cubed and crushed ice.
He is reporting this as a safety hazard because if not noticed and the person drinks the liquid the ice is in there could be severe internal consequences.
He said that this may have been happening much before it was noticed because he also found metal shavings built up under the ice area. 
There are no known injuries at this time
He was contacted the  manufacturer who referred him to CPSC.
He states that due to the safety hazards, the less than two years age of the unit he would ask to have the refrigerator replaced with a different model.
justification: The incident involves potential safety hazards (electrical and ingestion of metal shavings) but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: I have a GE Profile Dishwasher.  It has a delay cycle feature of up to 8 hours.  I was leaving for greater than 8 hours so I set the feature for 8 hours to start.   When I returned, the dishwasher did not turn on as expected.  I opened the front door and noticed the dishwasher did not cycle.  I closed the door then pushed the start button to start the process.   About 5 minutes into the cycle I noticed smoke coming from the top of the dishwasher.  I opened the front door to the dishwasher, to stop the cycle.  I touched the front of the door and could feel it was hot.  So I went and opened the inside panel of the door, removed the panel to try and keep the fire contained.  I was able to contain the fire.  The circuit board and the electrical connection to the circuit board were melted.  I removed the connector to the circuit board (it was melted to the board) and shut the power off to the appliance.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a small fire, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
I placed items in oven to bake, approximately 20 minutes later I was alerted by a loud alarm. I ran to the kitchen to find it was coming from my stove.  I saw smoke coming from in back of the stove, when I pulled it from the wall, fire erupted from upper back grid. My kitchen was filled with smoke and after I blasted the fire it flashed back at least twice. I then pulled the pull from the socket gave the stove one more blast, grabbed my two year old grand son and ran out the door. I called 911. The firetrucks came and assessed the situation and  told me I could go back in. The food in the oven was not burned nor was it effected at all. Burned marks can be seen on back of the stove and the metal at top of the back is discolored.  The wires inside the stove (Coils) can be seen to be burnt. IT was an electrical fire.  I am lucky that i was at home at the time and not in my back, front yard or even upstairs in my room or the bathroom. My grandson could have been killed or harmed. He suffers from severe respiratory and skin allergies. I call the company and the sent someone over three days later. He determined that a relay switch stuck open, got too hot and caught on fire.  I was told I would have to wait another week for them to make a determination. I was told I have three choices: (1) get the switch fix. (2) get a voucher, (3) get a new samsung stove.  But I don't feel safe with a samsung stove. No one should buy one unless they can sit and watch it while they cook. 
I see their phones, microwaves and stoves are catching on fire all over internet. I see that no recalls are out and nothing is being done. I see where samsung is giving folks like me a difficult time and making statements like "these are only a few incidences out of the many we have sold" I think that someone or some child is going to be severely burned or killed before anything is done here.  They are not going to voluntarily recall as they should, so shouldn't you? I already spoke to the military exchange where i bought the stove, I spoke to Consumer Reports and I will speak to Attorney General in [REDACTED] about this.  I am a 40% disable Vet, I anticipate having to purchase my own stove as I don't want another samsung and i suppose that is what they are going to offer me. This is not fair. This is not safe.  I depend on my military retirement to supplement my income. I work 12hrs per week. I now have to divert my money to pay for food as I can't cook. This is not fair.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with no injuries, but potential for severe harm was present, especially to the allergic grandson.

It has done this on numerous occasions. It will not cool down even when reduced to a 4 or 2 setting (LOW). The only way to get it to stop becoming hotter and redder is to turn the burner off completely and wait a few minutes. It has done this multiple times and will even jump from the 2 or 4 settings (when I have something set to simmer or warm). If I turn away from the stove for even a moment to chop something or get something from the refrigerator it can mean whatever I am cooking is burnt. It is a fire hazard. This stove is less than 2 years old!
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a fire hazard and has occurred multiple times, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Our Frigidaire Gas Oven/Stove, Model Number: FGGF3035RFC Serial Number: VF64000633. The unit has been in home for about a year and half approximately. We purchased it new from Sears.  Over the course of usage, we noticed that if you brush into the furthest knob to the right closest to our sink, the knob actuates too easily and release unburned gas in the home. 
This has happened a few times but is noticed quickly and shut off because user is still cooking in kitchen.  Today unfortunately, my elderly grandmother had accidentally brushed into the unit and left the gas open on full for unknown amount of time. The knob that was on full was the middle knob. This morning the gas smell was so strong I avoided the crisis before any further damage could be done. I shut the knob off and ventilated the home quickly and contacted customer support for Frigidaire.  They have no records of complaints for this unit for this problem, nor do they have a solution they offer to fix their unit. Instead they referred me to Amazon to purchase a child safety knob like device as a solution from a third party vendor.  I think this is very irresponsible for Frigidaire as well as I am having hard time believing their side of the story that this has never been a complaint or brought up to their attention. I did a modicum of research which lead me to a small google search and found another person in [REDACTED] who had similar problems with lightly brushing into their gas stove unit. I told them I will be pursuing and making a complaint to whatever business or avenue I can to prevent someone from losing their life, loved ones or even their home.  I am not asking for a new unit, or a refund for our unit, I'd just like the company to investigate the problem and warn other's and offer a proper solution to save lives.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to easily actuated knobs, which could lead to serious harm but no injury occurred this time.

incident_description: I have had this General Electric Range for about 6 years, brand new from building this home. A few days ago I had put some fries in the oven to bake as I normally would, set the timer and went to the living room with my infant. About 10 minutes into cooking, I noticed bright orange flashing from the kitchen (I can see my stove top from the couch) so I put the baby down and rushed to the kitchen where the oven was shooting out bright orange sparks/flames. The coil at the bottom had shattered into 3 pieces and was shooting electric sparks from the open ends of the remaining connected pieces. If I had not seen the incident, it could've gotten worse, or it could've just shut down, I'm not sure, but I did want to warn anyone else with this model, in case of a reoccurring issue.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical malfunction with potential for fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My ice dispenser on my Frigidaire refrigerator jammed, so I removed the ice tray/container (this is a normal procedure as this fridge has a removable ice tray for filling large containers).  When I placed my hand on the icemaker to try and clear the jam, my finger came in contact with a coil underneath the icemaker that, unbeknownst to me, was extremely hot.  My finger was instantly burned before I felt the pain and pulled it away.  It left a very painful blister on my finger.

There are no markings on the icemaker to warn of hot surfaces, and the area where the hot coil is located is not guarded from inadvertent contact.  It is even possible to contact this area with the ice tray/container still in place.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful blister, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the hot coil is accessible during normal use without warning.

incident_description:
About 4 years we purchased a Mr Coffee brand electric coffee grinder from Target. We used it regularly to grind coffee and never had any problems until February 25. It was left plugged in on our kitchen counter. At about 10pm I was in bed when my wife heard a grinding noise from the kitchen and went to investigate. The coffee grinder was on fire, emitting thick black smoke and flames which had just caught the cabinet above it on fire. Fortunately, I was able to put it out with a fire extinguisher, and pulled the plug on the coffee grinder and it stopped. It must have switched on by itself and ground until it overheated and caught fire. There was minimal damage, considering, only about $1000 worth of materials, and about $3000 worth of labor from a contractor to repair it. If we had not caught it when we did, it certainly would have caught the house and burned down as we slept.

I saved the coffee grinder, and took many pictures from every angle. I emailed the Mr Coffee company through their contact us form, but have not heard anything back from them for a week. Looking online, it did not seem like this was a common problem, but at least two other people reported the same thing happening on various websites.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

Both an electrician and a certified Frigidaire repairman said that the Relay on the compressor was the source of the fire. Frigidaire customer service apologized for our inconvenience, but did not seem at all concerned about the product over a lengthy back and forth email exchange and offered only a 30% discount on parts if we wanted it repaired.

incident_description:

Serial #: VF82216955
justification: The range turned on automatically and caused a smell of melting plastic, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: We have a Kitchenaid double oven, Model number KEBC207KBL05, serial number XT1711296, that was installed when we built our home in December 2006.  The oven was set to reach 350 degrees on Saturday evening and the outside door glass suddenly exploded, sending small fragments of glass into our living room, down halls, into our appliance center, all over our kitchen at distances as far as 40 feet away.  It sounded like a gunshot and to say it scared us to death is an understatement.  Had my grandchildren been standing there it could have blinded them.  My husband and I didn't suffer serious injury but we too were covered in glass sustaining minor knicks and cuts.  After researching this I have learned that it is more common than I knew.  I have contacted Kitchenaid and have a service repairman coming out to inspect the oven on Wednesday.  Whirlpool Corporation Safety Department had the nerve to say that the manual says to keep children away from appliances when I mentioned that my grandchildren could have been injured had they been here.  Ridiculous.
justification: The incident caused minor injuries (nicks and cuts) and had potential for severe harm (blinding), but no death occurred. Research indicates this is more common than initially thought.

incident_description:
Products are being used in kitchen to prepare breakfast, lunch and dinners. Major safety concerns are (1) lids do not fit the pots or skillets, when cooking grease bubbles over the edge of the too small lids and grease comes over the edge of the skillet towards the burner. (2) pots and smaller skillet are "handle heavy and tip the pot or skillet to sit unevenly on burner. (3) handles on lids are metal with a rubber time piece slipped over the metal, problem is the metal gets very hot and the rubber piece does not cover properly to place fingers to remove lid for food adjustment and or removal. If a child was to try and "help Mom or Dad cook" this could lead to a dropped lid, splashed cooking oil and burned fingers for the child. I received this set of cooking ware at Christmas, Name of Mfg:Chef's Mark
Made in China and distributed country wide. I have not contacted the Mfg or the company it was purchased from. I find this product extremely unsafe with a potential to burn anyone using this product and potentially a fire hazard. Let me know who I talk to next.
justification: The description indicates potential for burns and injuries due to poorly designed cookware, with a high likelihood of occurrence during use.

incident_description: Microwave was being used to reheat (warm up) a cup of coffee.  It was put in for less that 20 seconds and the closest plastic shelf holder sparked and then flamed.  When I opened the door of the microwave there was smoke and melted plastic smell and the plastic shelf holder was melted.  I have a picture on my phone.

incident_description:
My Whirlpool gas range has knobs that are so easily turned that I keep having gas leaks in my kitchen. It seems when I put things in my microwave above it or in the cabinets on the side, a slight push begins the gas flow but the igniters don't click in, probably takes a full 1/2 inch turn for them to start.  One time I came home after 45+ minutes and the house was full of gas. Other times I have caught it within 10 mins or so.  I have called Whirlpool and was told this is the correct design.  They sent out a tech who confirmed this is as engineered.  

I feel very fortunate that I have been able to air out the house and realize the situation before anything horrible happens.  I presently have masking tape on the knobs, but this seems very serious as a design flaw.  I feel nauseated and have headaches each time it happens.
justification: The incident involves repeated gas leaks causing headaches and nausea, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as it has happened multiple times and the design flaw persists.

incident_description:
TURNED OVEN ON TO PREHEAT . LOW BUZZING AND POPPING NOISE WAS HEARD AFTER ABOUT A MINUTE. FLAMES AND SMOKE WERE COMING OUT OF THE REAR VENTS WHERE ELECTRONIC CONTROLS ARE LOCATED. ONLY WAY TO STOP THE FIRE WAS TO UNPLUG THE STOVE AND FAN OUT THE FLAMES.
QUITE A BIT OF SMOKE AND SOOT WERE IN THE AIR AFTERWARDS. CIRCUIT BOARD SHORTED OUT AND CURRENT WAS NOT CUT OFF UNTIL UNIT WAS UNPLUGGED FROM THE WALL- A CLEAR SAFETY CONCERN HAD THE STOVE BEEN ON AND WE WERE NOT HOME TO ACT QUICKLY.

incident_description:
I took my Pyrex clear glass bowl from the cupboard, placed it on the counter top and added salad greens and dressing, then brought the bowl to the dinner table.  As we were eating dinner and salad, the bowl suddenly exploded into hundreds of pieces of glass and several large pieces, see attached pix.

This bowl was given to me at Christmas 2017 and was the largest of a set of four Pyrex bowls.  The large one was the one that exploded, it has never been in the oven, microwave or freezer.  I have read where these have been known to explode when heated or transitioned from hot to cold or cold to hot but this bowl was at room temperature when in the cupboard and during our use for the salad.

Shards of glass landed in our food, on the table, floor and in our laps.  Obviously our meal ended abruptly as we started cleanup.  When it exploded, it made quite a loud noise and happened faster than anyone could react.  We are so lucky glass didn't fly into our eyes.

There is no apparent reason why this type of glass explosion should happen and I am writing to you in hopes you have the power to work with Pyrex in preventing this from ever happening again.  These glass bowls should all be recalled.
justification: The bowl exploded, causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased this mini waffle maker in November 2018, so it is only about 3.5 months old at this point.  I use it about 2 times per day.  I noticed yesterday that it is malfunctioning and it could be a fire hazard.  The top half of the iron heats and the bottom does not.  The problem is that the waffle iron relies on both top and bottom to get hot to trigger the device to turn off the light and stop the iron from working to get any hotter, once it reaches the required temperature.  Without the bottom half heating up to help trigger the stop, the top half never stops getting hotter.  The plastic on the top got so hot, the last time I used it, it has heat burn marks.
justification: The waffle maker malfunction poses a fire hazard and has caused heat burn marks, but no injury has been reported.
