incident_description:
The dishwasher completely quit working. A new load of dishes was ready to run but the unit would
not start and no indicator light would come on.
Some background:
 Unit was acting up for month or so with green light not coming on at end of cycle, no lights or
buttons working, or blue light coming on but buttons not working and cannot cancel. Turning
off circuit breaker and then on had been fixing the problem every time.
 On Saturday evening Jan 19, the circuit breaker ÃÂfixÃÂ did not work.
 I removed the front metal panel. Looking at the control module at the upper right, the problem
was easy to see. The 4-wire plastic connector housing at the lower left of the control module
was burned, positions #2 and #3, #3 seemed the worst (black wire) and positions #1 and #4
seemed fine
 From Left to Right, wire colors are #1 Blue (w/white stripe), #2 Blue (w/red stripe), #3 Black,
#4 White
Safety concern:
 I believe the connector as designed by the manufacturer is the problem
as it is undersized to handle the electric current for the heater and motor. As such, arcing
occurs at the metal junction between male and female part of each connector.
 This seems to be a chronic problem with dishwashers and in particular with the
model which I have.
 Potential hazard is fire.
Follow-up:
 Dishwasher now works perfectly and dishes are super clean and no film on dishes.
 My thinking is that the water is now hotter as the resistance in the burned terminal was
limiting current to the heating element.
 I believe high water temperature is the best solution to prevent film and crud buildup.
Action Recommended:
 believe there should be a recall to replace the connector on the wiring harness so that the
female metal part is a standard spade type connector and not the existing design which is
unusual and undersized.
 I have attached pictures showing the actual burned connectors removed from my unit I have
also attached a picture from the internet (IMG_7389.jpg) which is similar to my unit, although
mine was not burned quite as severely. I have also attached a pictures of the type of connector
I used to repair my unit.
This report copied from consumers account sent in on hardcopy model asking for submission.
pictures have been forwarded with request to upload to this report
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning dishwasher with a potential fire hazard due to a burned connector, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was using a Black and Decker Toaster Oven Model # TO1950SBD in my kitchen. I prepared some food with it and the food was removed before the timer dinged based upon the appearance of the food through the glass. The food was handed to the person who wanted it but then I couldn't turn the timer off, and it was running red hot. So I unplugged it to let it cool off to see if I could get it to reset itself, but unfortunately as soon as I plugged it back in it went straight to red hot. I cannot get the timer to work, and I cannot get it to regulate the temperature any longer. I am afraid to use it again. Luckily nothing was damaged and nobody got hurt.

incident_description:
Brand Hamilton Beach Brands, Inc.
Product: Countertop Oven with Convection and Rotisserie (31100)
Model: 31100
Series: A4431ce
When turning on the toaster oven to a set time the timer will go to the off position and no longer ring when done and will continue on to the stay on position. After putting the timer knob back to the off position and walking away the timer again went back on to the stay on position the only way to shut it off is to unplug it from the outlet. I reported the incident to Hamilton Beach Brands, Inc. they stated that it is no longer under warranty. Please note I was not looking for a replacement I was reporting to the a dangerous appliance.  After further investigation of my own I took the timer out of the toaster oven and examined it. It appears that the plastic piece that pushes down on the electric contact melted to it making it so it will not longer reset the timer properly therefor it will continue to run to the stay one position. I never used this toaster over beyond the limit of the timer on most occasions it was only used for 20 minutes. In my opinion I was lucky I didn't leave home that day it may have started a fire.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance that could potentially cause a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high given the described failure mode and user's experience.

incident_description: On 11/06/2012 I bought Whirlpool Dishwasher. We will see what they decide, but this model should be including on the same recall notices for their dishwashers. It has all the same symptoms as their current recalls concerning the power cord.

.

incident_description:
I installed the dishwasher the night before and ran it once without incident. The next day as I was shaving my wife called out my name and I ran into the kitchen to find her lying on he floor near the dishwasher with her eyes red and tearing. She appeared to be dizzy and disoriented.  She said she just passed out. She said she opened the dishwasher because the light was white to indicate it is finished and she breathed in the vapors which overcame her causing her lungs and throat to burn and she passed out and fell to the ground. 

 I opened the dishwasher and the fumes were overwhelming burning my eyes, throat, and nose. It resembled the smell of nitro methane top fuel dragster exhaust. I let the fumes clear out then removed the lower rack. I found plastic melted onto the exposed heating element as well as a plastic piece of the upper rack on top of the filter the same color as the melted plastic. The pieces came from the upper rack roller end stop and the folding finger holders. Opening the dishwasher 5 hours later the smell remains but is no longer overwhelming. 

 The use of poorly secured plastic parts above an exposed heating element is a poor design which can lead to inhalation poisonous gases and possible consequential injury from falling.  I believe that this is caused by a common dishwasher design flaw.  Having an open heating element.  Even if all the parts in the washer were metal there is still a risk of a person in a rush putting a bowl with a plastic wrapper or alike in the washer. I think there should be some government regulation preventing the use of an exposed heating element in a dishwasher to protect consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (dizziness, disorientation, and burning sensations) due to inhalation of toxic fumes, but no death occurred. The likelihood is possible (3) as the design flaw is common but not every use leads to such incidents.

incident_description:
Potential fire hazard from Miele Gas Oven with Self Cleaning 

I am contacting you regarding a potential fire hazard with our Miele Gas Oven. 

Two years ago we did a kitchen remodel and purchased a Miele HR1134G all gas range and installed DuPont Zodiac Quartz countertops and backsplash.

During one of the service visits for our range, the Miele authorized repairman said it would be a good idea to self clean the oven while still under warranty. We ran the self clean feature at the middle setting (there are 3 available) and near the end of the cycle the backsplash developed 2 dark brown spots about 4 inches wide and about 6 inches high.  There are also small cracks in the middle of each spot.  We called DuPont and they said the polymers must have been scorched and there is no way to repair it.  The backsplash was so hot we were unable to touch it for more than 2 hours after the self clean finished.  The DuPont rep stated he was surprised the wall did not catch on fire.

Miele claims the range was working within specs and we should make a claim with our homeowners insurance.  They take no responsibility for what happened.

We talked to a couple of DuPont installers and they both said that the stove shouldnÃÂt been installed right up against the backsplash.  Neither Miele in their multiple visits to our kitchen before, during or after completion, nor the backsplash installers had any concerns about this being a potential hazard.  

There are no warnings, cautions or any other discussions in either the Miele installation or user guide about a potential fire hazard with installing this stove right up against a wall. 

I have contacted Underwriters Laboratories and have submitted a Market Surveillance Report form with them.
justification: The incident involved scorching and cracking of the backsplash due to the oven's self-cleaning feature, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

Caller mailed in an update to the report stating, "Just wanted to emphasize that I recovered 5 pieces of hard plastic that appear to be fan blades (see photo) but that is appeared that at least 8 blades were missing from the fans. The posterior fan had all blades missing (see photo). The fan blade pieces probably landed in food something although I can't be sure any landed in my Christmas cookies. However, I felt I could not take the change of serving them to my grandkids. I just threw them out. Also, this company had a problem similar to this in 1992 which was reported to CPSC and Hamilton Beach did a voluntary recall at that time. Although not the same model number as now, Hamilton Beach models 230 & 232 hand held mixers had broken cooling fans and broken fan pieces contaminated food & caused injuries in 15 incidents (Per news from CPSC - release # 92-043). I don't think this company had done due diligence in re fans/fan blade."
justification: The incident involved plastic pieces breaking off and potentially contaminating food, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is possible given the historical context of similar incidents.

incident_description: I moved into a condo in June and have occasionally been using the LG oven MODEL LRG3095ST / 02. I noticed that the covering of the microwave handle had melted as well the knobs on the range but it wasn't until the new cabinet veneer next to the stove began to curl that I realized it was happening when I was using the oven. There seems to be a great deal of hot air pouring out from right below the control panel when the oven is on - enough so that the metal handles of the cabinets closest to the range become warm and the solid-state oils inside the cabinet melt to liquid state. I contacted LG at 1-800-243-0000. They initially seemed quite concerned and motivated to check this out. They told me not to use the oven any more and they would escalate the matter to Upper Management as a safety issue and would contact me within 24-48 hours. It has been more than a week since I first contacted them although I have called several times since as they assured me that this was a priority. Every time I call they put me off a few more days and I am starting to worry that they will not address my issue. In the meantime I am not sure what to do and wondered if this was an issue with this model.
justification: The incident involves property damage (melted handle, knobs, and cabinet veneer) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
GE MIcrowave Model # JVM316ORF255  Serial # GD284950A  Manufactured 2014
This is an over the range microwave. The lights under the unit have overheated and the insulation around the socket shell has disintegrated. I had a GE appliance repair man look at the unit but was told there was a charge for repairs. I believe that failed insulation on an electrical appliance is not bound to a one year warranty but rather a safety issue.
justification: The incident involves overheated lights and disintegrated insulation, posing a potential safety hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: The product is a General Electric brand electric range, model number JB655SKSS. There is some kind of vent that comes out just underneath the control panel on the range. You can't see this vent unless you bend over to look underneath the control panel, and as I was cleaning under the control panel with a cloth, the edge of the vent opening, which is very sharp metal, sliced open the top of my right ring finger, just at the knuckle. This is a very dangerous design.
justification: The incident resulted in a finger injury due to a sharp vent edge, indicating a moderate severity. The likelihood is possible as the hazard is present but requires specific actions to encounter.

incident_description: Appliance is shooting sparks from the bottom vent
justification: Sparks from an appliance can cause injury if someone is nearby or touches the appliance.

incident_description: My complaint is with the Oster Triple Station Buffet Server.  I cut my finger while washing the bottom of one of the buffet trays.  The edge of the tray is too sharp.
justification: The user reported a cut finger from a sharp tray edge, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Caller reported that while the double oven range was in use , her daughter opened the door to base the turkey and the oven rack fell down spilling grease from the container everywhere.  Fortunately no one was hurt.  She stated that the oven racks are fitted until the oven is heated which seems as if the oven expands causing the racks to fall.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that the unit was no longer under warranty.

Caller is concerned that these oven racks are a safety hazard and should be recalled.

This was not the first time the racks fell - if we had not seen it fall down it could have created a dangerous fire.
justification: No one was hurt, but the incident involved spilled grease and potential fire hazard, indicating a safety concern.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his spouse opened the oven door and the outer glass shattered into several pieces while the oven was not in use.

The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that the unit was out of warranty, he explained that the incident was not a matter of warranty but material defect (a design flaw).

Caller stated that he has read several reports on this incident and that he is concerned that the product has not been recalled for this issue.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered oven glass) but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to multiple reported incidents suggesting a potential design flaw.

incident_description:
This 85 year old consumer purchased a gas range from a retailer in California. That was installed October 25th, 2018.
The caller states that she rarely used the range but that she used it for the first time around the end of October 2018 at which time she became very ill but she thought it was because of something she had eaten.
She used it rarely during November and until Christmas and each time she became very ill then on Christmas Day she used it most of the day then December 26th, 2018 she could barely get up she was so ill.
She has been feeling ill since this range was installed in her home then contacted the gas company December 27, 2018 over 500 ppm.  The gas company employee immediately helped her open doors and windows, then red tagged her range and explained to her that she could not use the range and if she had been using it every day since she may not have survived.
She was medically checked Kaiser's Marino Valley walk in clinic where they checked her levels then advised her that just as she had been feeling a bit better the past few days she will continue to regain memory, cognitive thinking as she is not exposed to the carbon monoxide anymore.
She contacted the place of purchase December 27th, 2018 after the gas tech left and a representative is scheduled to come to her home to look at the range.
justification: The consumer suffered repeated illness due to carbon monoxide exposure, requiring medical attention, but no death occurred.

incident_description: My husband took my blue Pyrex dish out of the oven & before he could get from the oven to the table which was about 3 feet it Exploded in his hands. It burned his hands & left  burns in the kitchen floor in several places. We were finding shards of glass under the frig, the breakfast bar & the hutches for weeks. This happened aprox Dec.17-21-2017.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the hands and property damage, indicating an injury severity. Pyrex explosions are uncommon but documented.

incident_description: My gas Range went on by itself and it would not shut down. All the knobs were on off. The only way to shut it down was to unplug and disconnect the gas.when reconnected , it proceeded to heat up on its own, without the ability to shut it off again.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas range that could not be shut off normally, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: I purchased an Avanti 23 inch gas oven in July of 2016. After about 1 year I noticed the oven exterior was beginning to melt. After I called customer service they sent someone to fix it and when they arrived, they didn't have the "parts" and would haver to order them. I have still not had it fixed and no one art Avanti is willing to help. it has continued to melt and I believe the oven is unsafe and unable to properly contain the gas heat. After reading reviews, I am. to the only person with this issue, the product is clearly unsafe.
justification: The oven's exterior melting indicates a safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
My toaster failed to pop up and continued heating the toast to the point of ignition, presenting a fire hazard. I contacted Hamilton Beach, manufacturer of the toaster, after reading of recalls of their products for the same issue. When I supplied the model number, they indicated that it was not one of the current recall toasters. I explained that I would be filing a report with you. 

Hamilton Beach 4-slice toaster
Model 24121
Series B0351BI
justification: The toaster malfunctioned and presented a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: This Good Cook cheese grater was being used in the kitchen to grate from a block of parmesan cheese, as it often is. It snapped without apparent wear or warning at the bottom (hand-side) of the plastic frame around the metal grater itself. The edge of the bottom (hand-side) of the metal grater was exposed.
justification: The grater snapped unexpectedly, exposing a sharp edge, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Electrolux electric range model PLEF398CCB: Smoothtop range burners will not turn off after use, and during use will go to maximum high heat continuously.  This has occurred on all four burners at various times within the last year or so.  In order to shut off burners, range main breaker has to be turned off.  Sometimes, after "resting" for a while, and resetting breaker, burners will shut off.  Other times they will not shut off at all.  Turning burner knobs on and off numerous times will usually shut burner off.  This malfunction poses a serious risk of burn injury or fire.  I learned that this model was subject to a recall and contacted Electrolux/Frigidaire.  They agreed that this model was part of the recall and requested the serial number.  The serial number is printed on a plastic label fixed to the door frame, and after many years, the serial number is only partially legible.  I gave Electrolux as much of the serial number as I was able to make out, but they REFUSED to rectify this dangerous condition unless i could give them a complete serial number.  They would not even tell me exactly what the problem was, but indicated that the control knobs, as well as other electrical components needed to be replaced.  They refused to give me the part numbers for the replacement parts required, and stated that the repairs had to be done by a registered repair person sent by Electrolux.  Again, they refused to send a repair person without a complete serial number.  The Electrolux representative agreed that this problem was in fact dangerous from both a burn and fire perspective, but still refused to repair.  I took photos of the ID label and sent them to an email provided by the representative; I got no response.  The incident date of this report is only the most recent instance.
justification: The malfunction poses a serious risk of burn injury or fire, and the issue has occurred multiple times on all burners.

incident_description: On 2/3/2019, I preheated my oven per instructions on the label for [REDACTED] Bacon. After the oven was preheated, I lined the glass pan with aluminum foil. Then I placed five strips of bacon onto the foiled pan. Then I placed the bacon into the oven for 15 mins. Then I removed the pan of bacon from the oven and placed it on top my glass top stove. The pan exploded. Glass went everywhere and it almost injured me.
justification: The pan exploded, causing glass to go everywhere, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller says that while leftovers where warming up there was a loud pop sound. When they went to investigate the glass turn table inside the microwave had shattered. Product was in use for about 1 minute when the incident occurred. 

Caller contacted the manufacturer and informed him the product is no longer in warranty. 

Caller believes this product is a laceration hazard.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass turntable but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon but not frequent.

incident_description:
We have owned the cooker for 1 year.  My wife washed the glass lid and placed it on edge like a dish in the drainer.  Later she went back to the drainer to move the lid, and when she picked up the lid by the handle the lid burst sending out thousands of shards.  She was blessed to only have a few small cuts, and a mess to clean up in the kitchen.
  To clarify: the lid had not suffered any sharp blows, it was no sudden change in temperature, and it was no known chips or cracks before the incident.
Please, try to get a recall on these things before someone really gets hurt.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (small cuts) and a mess, but no severe harm. The occurrence is unlikely as the lid burst under normal handling conditions without prior damage.

incident_description: Our Dishwasher was not cleaning the dishes properly. Upon investigation  it was discovered that the heating element had burnt a 2 inch wide by 8 inch long hole in the base of the dishwasher. This could have caused a fire,  Also water dammage.
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused property damage (hole in the base) and posed a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased an oven mitt from Dollar Tree in November or December 2018. The first time I used it to remove a pan from the oven on December 17th, I felt heat and found a large hole had burned thru the mitt. I was fortunate to not have been injured as I was only holding the pan for a very short period and immediately put it down when I felt the heat. I sent a message via their website and a tweet to Dollar Tree as it is their licensed product and received no response. I included a photo of the product showing the issue as well. This product is dangerous and should be removed from their stores and from any home that purchased it. I have kept the product as well.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (burned-through mitt) but no injury occurred, as the user immediately put down the hot pan upon feeling the heat.

incident_description:
I purchased 5 RTIC 20 oz. tumblers for Christmas gifts. They look great and everyone was happy with them but today my lid crumbled apart when I was popping the top open. I have dangerous, sharp shards in my beverage and the lid is like a saw blade. I'm sure this is just a defective lid but [REDACTED] at RTIC tells me that is my problem to purchase a replacement their defective lid. This item is less than 90 days old! If you read through the reviews for this item on Amazon, there is a pattern with the negative reviews that all mention the lid coming apart. 

These lids need to be recalled and replaced,
justification: The incident describes a defective lid that crumbled into sharp shards, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
We own two homes, one in [REDACTED] and one on [REDACTED] in [REDACTED].  Over the holidays we spent our time in [REDACTED].  On Thursday, January 10th I went up to the lake home. Upon entering the home I found that a couple of breakers had cut out, and the refrigerator was 'dead'.  Upon inspection, after resetting the related breaker, I found that only the internal lighting and some of the indicator lights on the control panel were working. The refrigerator is protected by a dedicated surge protector, which was 'green' and operational at the time.

I spoke with an LG representative, who said she would like to do some smart testing with me at the refrigerator?  I declined and emphasized that their refrigerator had blown breakers and I had no interest in this approach, as a matter of personal safety.  They will be sending a technician. She indicated that the problem may be related to a 'field panel', as I understood, or the compressor, as the unit was room temperature upon discovery.

The unit has only been operational around 10 months, and is brand new. It was purchased for new construction, and was not installed for use until April or May, 2018.  It's a French door refrigerator, LG model #LFX28968D /00, Serial Number #706TRBS1L685. Additionally, a Sears repair technician was recently to our [REDACTED] home and told us he 'wouldn't bring an LG product into his home?'
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator causing breakers to trip, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Turned on Stove Top and place a pan of water on stove and element popped and through flames up around my hand and caused third degree and 1st degree burns to palm of hand and fingers
justification: The incident resulted in third-degree and first-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Stove-related burns are possible but not extremely common (likelihood 3).

incident_description: I bought 6 of these cups over the course of the last 6 months. The last cup I purchased was 2months ago. A few weeks ago every single straw ripped at the valve. My baby was 13 months old at the time and must be biting the straw with more force. However, in order for the straw to release liquid the straw needs to be bit so the plastic needs to be able to hold up to baby teeth. The straws ripping in 2 pieces is a MAJOR CHOKING HAZARD! Because this happened with 6 straws I checked amazon reviews to see if others have had similar issues. They have, this is not a fluke. This product needs to be recalled. It is extremely unsafe. I contacted the company a few weeks ago to let them know and have gotten a standard response back that does not make me confident that they are taking my feedback seriously
justification: The straws ripping poses a major choking hazard, but no actual injury or death was reported in the incident.

incident_description: My toddlers were able to bite the rubber tops off from their Tommee Tippee sportee sippee cups.  They looked like they were chewing gum.  I was concerned that they could have choked on them.  One would think their toddler was safe, sitting watching [REDACTED] with their sippy cup and no small choking hazards within their reach.  Ours were using theirs to drink water.  I called the Tommee Tippee product support line, and they said it was my fault, because I should have purchased their cups with hard tops.  The product packaging states these are for "12 mos +".    Toddlers have teeth at 12 mos +.  It's not on me to anticipate this design flaw.  They need to fix it or market these to infants without teeth.
justification: The incident involved toddlers biting off rubber tops, posing a choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was warming some food in the Wolfgang Puck electric roaster on the Brown/saute setting. The glass lid was on the entire time. It was warming for about 20 minutes. I then took the food out, & shut off the electricity to it, & unplugged it. I put the glass lid back on top of the roaster after unplugging it. In about 10 minutes as the roaster was cooling the glass lid shattered. It was not touched, moved, or in any way jarred. The glass lid just shattered. The glass pieces were drawn into the roaster as if the roaster developed a vacuum with the lid on it.
justification: The glass lid shattered without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description: Started dishwasher prior to going to sleep.  Approximately 2 hours later had a strong smell of smoke within the home.  Located the source of smoke from the dishwasher.  Removed dishwasher door panel and found insulation material was melted and wiring and harness that enters control module was charred and melted.  Severe smoke and heat damage to localized area around control module with minor smoke damage extending outside of door panel.  Fire self extinguished within the door compartment.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher and localized smoke damage, but no injuries or fatalities occurred.

incident_description:
This report is about a GE JBP67 Radiant Range that I purchased in June 2007.  Here is what happened with it at the end of 2018/beginning of 2019:  
When I turned the rear burners on the stovetop to a low setting, they automatically increased the heat to a high setting (even when the knob was set at "1").  This happened 3 times in the last couple months.  It has burned items in pots and pans.  Luckily, none of the fires have spread into my house.
justification: The incident caused burned items but no injuries or property damage beyond the pots and pans, fitting severity level 2. The issue occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Electric plug on PhilipÃÂs Airfryer Model HD9230 Serial Number 1738 melted during use
justification: The incident involved a melted electric plug but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using the Air Crazy West Bend popcorn popper when a hole formed in the side of the device due to it melting through the plastic. There was a smell of something melting (rubber?) at the same time. At the time, I was popping popcorn and it was not running for very long (maybe 4 minutes). The smell has happened a few times before while popping popcorn but this was the first time an actual hole has formed in the side of the popper. It may be related to a bit of popcorn that got stuck in the one of the metal air holes in the opening where the un popped popcorn is deposited. I tried to remove it and some fell into the interior of the machine. That was a while back. I used the machine many times since and it usually worked as normal.
justification: The incident involved a hole forming in the popcorn popper due to melting plastic, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Turned the dishwasher on at 10pm when going to bed.  Came to kitchen at 7am and dishwasher was still running with smoke coming from top.  Appliance repair person discovered control board had overheated and was burned significantly.  Wires attaching to control board also were burned and melted.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore microwave caught fire, not in use at time. Fire destroyed microwave, damaged refrigerator exterior.  Smoke damage in kitchen.
justification: The microwave caught fire causing property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: gas indoor stove range control knobs are plastic steems and are broken due to  heat from oven. cannot turn on are off the burners are oven.
justification: The broken control knobs prevent proper operation of the stove, posing a risk of uncontrolled gas flow or inability to turn off the burners, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Oven racks have been falling recently - the last time 12/27/18.  So far, no one has been injured.
The product is a Kenmore Elite Microwave/Wall Oven Combination, purchased 5/6/2012.
M/n 790.48903000, s/n NF251823229.  I've noticed many similar complains and, in particular, 
#20180528-56265-2147387695, posted on 6/19/18 - same model number.

incident_description: Dishwasher control panel caught fire.
justification: The dishwasher control panel catching fire is an incident with potential for harm but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: i was washing crockpot lid with warm soapy water and rinsing with same, and the lid exploded--sending glass all over floor, counter, sink, and all over my shirt and jeans and exposed wrists and hands and face.   I may or may not have glass in left eye--can't tell.  the glass was small, and some was so tiny it stuck in my skin without drawing blood.  there was no dramatic temp change--crockpot had been used the night before, and i was re-washing since the crockpot itself had been left to soak overnight.  there was a loud pop when it exploded.  glass flew two feet at least.  the lid was not struck with anything prior to explosion.
justification: The incident resulted in potential injury with glass fragments on the face and possible eye involvement, though no severe bleeding or confirmed eye injury was mentioned.

incident_description:
Hover Cover Magnetic Microwave Splatter Guard. "securely stores in your microwave so it is always ready for use"  Trademark of EPD, Distributed by Allstar Products Group.  Hawthorne, NY 10532.

Received 12/21/2018 as gift and has been stored and used in the microwave since.  Today 12/28/2018  my husband used the microwave with the hover cover in it's stored space attached to the roof of the microwave.  He noticed a "brightening and sparks" in the microwave and stopped it. We found the hover cover had one of the magnets melted and what he saw was a fire starting.  (photos available) .  Luckily he was watching the microwave or our whole house with 4 people in it could have had a major incident.  It appears this product has been reported in the past and same issues are reported in the product reviews on other websites.  Very dangerous, should not be on the market.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a potential fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Circuit board on GE Dishwasher (Model # GLD6964R10SS/ Serial # RS836468B) caught on fire during operation.  The incident occurred in the middle of the night and mid-cycle for the dishwasher.  Smoke from the burning plastic was billowing out of the machine and fortunately we were home and were able to react to the fire detectors.  The machine was continuing to run and had approximately 40 minutes left on the cycle.  The machine could not be stopped or reset without cutting the power to it from the circuit breaker box.  

Upon investigation, nothing foreign caused the short.  Plastic around the circuit board housing was melting and causing the smoke.  The board itself is mostly black due to what appears to be a short.  The metal heat shield was also blackened as a result.  Damage to the premises was burnt plastic smell throughout.  Damages to residents includes smoke inhalation of toxic burnt plastic smoke and stress caused by the incident and potential impact to young children ages 6 and 3.  Windows and doors had to be left open overnight in frigid temperatures to allow for fresh air to clear the smoke.  

This appears to be the same issue (water condensation causing a short) that is the subject of the recall https://www.geappliances.com/ge/recall/dishwasher_2010/.   This model number, however, has not been recalled.  GE sent a technician to investigate and his report was only that a ""thermal event @ control module" occurred.  GE has made no effort to remedy this problem based on my subsequent discussions with their customer relations team other than to offer a limited discount on a GE dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved smoke inhalation and stress, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as it's a known issue but not widespread for this model.

incident_description:
After my 3rd [REDACTED] gas stove was returned, I did some research and decided to go with a Whirlpool model WEG750H0HZ0  serial  R81811625 based on the slide in photo/reviews I read.  PC Richards delivered the stove some time mid-February 2018.  Here are the problems that I consider a safety issue:
1.  Even though you need to "push in SLIGHTLY" to turn the gas jets on, IT IS NOT SAFE ENOUGH!
A guest came into my home at 1:30am, went directly into the kitchen to put away or get something from the refrigerator.  His duffle bag he was carrying, must have somehow pushed in SLIGHTLY & TURNED  2 knobs as he was walking into the kitchen.  NOT enough to hear the click, click ignitor, but enough to let gas escape.   My bedroom is 15 feet from the kitchen.  My door was ajar only 4".  I woke up at 5am to the 'SMELL OF GAS' in my bedroom.  I was terrified to go out of my bedroom door because I had a motion light in my hallway, (thinking when the light came on it would cause an explosion).  I took the chance and the smell of gas was heavier as I stood up, in the hall, livingroom, kitchen and bathroom.   I opened all of the doors, windows and after most was out of the house turned on the ceiling fans.  The knobs on ALL gas stoves with ALL manufacturers NEED to be PUSHED IN  (just like trying to open a child proof medicine bottle) in order that this does not happen to others.

In addition the engineer who designed the grates for this stove should be FIRED.   Using a compass, E.W.N.S.  the bars that go from E to W are full or at least 3/4 full.  Over the gas jet, there is a N.S. SHORT BAR ONLY 3" in long.  This short bar does NOT hold a percolator coffee pot as the base of the pot is about 4" and it "wobbles" over the grate. It is NOT secure.  I had accidently bumped the pot (fortunately it was not hot) and knocked it off the front jet.  It fell onto the floor, spilling all the coffee, grinds and broke the glass top when it hit the tile floor.

There is absolutely NO reason ON THIS EARTH that I have to spend $5k or $10k to get a "designer" stoves to make sure it works properly!!!!  In addition, the manufacturers are screwing the consumers.  A typical range is 30" wide.  Yet if you want a BIGGER oven, you have to pay more money for it.  Yet the SMALLER ovens, cost less, but they have to "build" an inner wall to make the oven smaller, so why does the bigger oven cost more?  In addition, each and every stove, most all manufacturers have taken away the 'big drawer' at the bottom of the oven and have given you a small 6" space, yet the oven space is the same on all units.   I would like to know why the manufacturers like [REDACTED], [REDACTED] and others ARE having issues with their oven temperatures and trying to jamb it down the consumer's throat to "USE" the convection oven vs the STANDARD oven - why because they know they have a problem with their heating element using the standard oven?
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to accidental activation of stove knobs, posing a serious safety hazard but resulting in no injury or death.

incident_description: I saw smoke coming from under my Bosch dishwasher while working in the kitchen and immediately went to the garage and threw the circuit breaker.  When I took off the cover to the electrical hookup panel on the bottom right side of the dishwasher , the wire nuts and wires were burned and disintegrated. We have had this dishwasher for approx 13 years .  When I went to CPSC I found the model and serial number were part of a recall which we never received a notice of.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. Given the recall and age of the dishwasher, recurrence is likely.

incident_description:
I purchased a Hamilton Beach 2-slot toaster at the local Fred Meyer store.  When using the toaster, I discovered that it does not pop up when done but continues to cook and ultimately burn the item in the toaster.  The pop-up when done feature fails to work.  
The Hamilton Beach model number is:  22790 and the Series is A2781B1.

I did a Google search for Hamilton Beach recalls and found that this toaster was recalled in 2008 and again in 2011.  The pictures of these two recalled toasters is identical to the one I just purchased.  It seems the toaster problem has not been fixed from previous recalls and has simply been put back on the market.

The only thing I can do now, is throw it out and call it a total loss.  I didn't save my receipt as I have never owned a bad toaster before.  

Can you help with this?  Recall this toaster please and if there is anyway to recover my $39 that would be great, too.  Thanks.
justification: The toaster's failure to pop up could lead to burnt items, but no injury or death was reported. The issue is likely to occur given the history of recalls.

incident_description:
Fire in a un-plugged Crock-Pot Pressure Cooker
Model: SCCPPC600-V1
justification: The description mentions a fire incident with no indication of injury or death.

incident_description:
On July 18, 2018 I contacted Cuisinart Customer Service because my coffeemaker (Model: DCC-3200W) was leaking water from the bottom of the coffeemaker. The product was still under warranty and they sent me a replacement product. Not even 6 months later, the replacement coffeemaker is having the same problem - even worse. ( So two coffeemakers, same model, both leaking water from the bottom.) 

When water is placed in the reservoir for overnight auto-programming to make coffee in the morning; as it passes through the system, somewhere water leaks out. This time 14-cups of water leaked onto my counter, onto the wood floors, behind the stove and its outlet and drench everything else on the countertop.  It is causing a safety issue as when it leaks, because first, if you don't know the water everywhere is hot, you burn yourself, when you clean it up (like I did this morning). Secondly, if you don't notice it right away (as in this morning), the electric cord where it goes into the unit sits in the water. Furthermore,  you can smell a burning scent as it is dripping on the inside of the coffeemaker and getting onto the internal heating element. The original date of my problem started in February of 2018. I notified the company in July 2018, replacement sent out on July 19th and now the replacement product has the same issue (January 2019).
justification: The incident involves hot water leakage causing burns and potential electrical hazards, indicating an injury risk (severity 3). The recurrence with two coffeemakers suggests the issue is likely (occurrence 4).

incident_description:
Started dishwasher like we normally would, smelled burnt rubbber, minute later smoke came out of the dishwasher. Observed black smoke from the door handle, immediately killed power.. whole house was Smokey. Awful!

Model : ZBD0710K03SS

Serial : VG766764B

Pictures available of sections that caught fire

incident_description:
Stove burners turn on unintentionally whenever the knob is ever so slightly brushed. Sometimes it will ignite; sometimes gas will just leak out, and until the odor is detected, it is difficult to know that the gas has been turned on.
 Knobs can be accidentally bumped to release gas without lighting the burners. They're in front & low; this can also happen if you are reaching towards the back of the unit to clean it.  I think that my dogs have turned this unit on as well.  I can't imagine how dangerous this is if small children are in the household.  I have had to resort to removing the knobs when not in use.  No solutions from LG were offered.
justification: The incident involves unintentional gas release and potential ignition, posing a significant risk of injury or death, especially to small children or pets.
The heating elements turning on spontaneously poses a burn hazard, but no injury is reported in the description.

I grabbed the handle on cup and developed 2 degree burn, the handle is burning hot enough to melt skin, where is the fluids and cup are warm to touch. I have never had a coffee cup like this. I have picture s

incident_description: Was pouring milk into a nuby sippy cup. The one that lights up when you tap the bottom of it. As I filled the cup it instantly exploded all over my hands and face. There was a black cloud of hot air that filled my lungs and my throat and eyes immediately started burning. I also got a mild burn on my right hand. About an hour later my breathing was very shallow and hurting to the point I had to go to the ER. At the er I received relaxers for my throat and breathing treatments.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and respiratory issues requiring ER treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such events are rare but possible with faulty products.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting her range for posing a burn and fire hazard. While searching online she came across recall # 18-218 and noticed she is experiencing similar issues but her serial # is not included in the recall.

In August of 2017 she preheated the oven on bake to 350 degrees and noticed that the oven became extremely hot after a few minutes. She indicated that the unit failed to shut off and she had to turn off the circuit breaker. The oven door knob was extremely hot that she could not touch it and it had burn damages.

She contacted a technician and had the unit repaired. The boiler igniter switch and the access panel were replaced.
 
A month later she had a similar incident and she contacted the tech again. The tech replaced the gas valve and control panel.

During the past month the unit is having additional issues. She states that the oven is now failing to heat and stay on. While in use the oven and fan turn off but the gas is still emitting. The home fills up with gas. She also indicated that the stove top burners are heating to different temperatures.

She left voicemails to the firm's recall hotline (800-449-8691) last week but she never received a call back. She plans to contact the firm's customer service to request assistance with repairs.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak and burn hazards, posing a risk of injury, and the recurring issues suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
We used this Dehydrator several time during each Christmas season to make Christmas Beef jerky This year we had it catch on fire and do some damage to our garage, thankful I was in the area to catch and put out or our home could have burned down and possibly killed people. I checked and saw this recall and called Cababe's who said it was too old to do anything about...???? But they did say they would send a $100 Gift Cert ( not enough due to the possibility of destroying my home).

In my conversation with them (Call center) they saw where I purchased it from them, and they knew it had a recall but at no time did they notify me and alert me to this problem, they had my address, email and knew but fails to protect me

The recall says to replace or refund which they did neither... they took the chance with our lives nothing would happen and it would go away.

incident_description: My Hamilton Beach Immersion Blender began breaking up and eventually became unusable. Shards of brittle plastic fell off of it, and some likely went into my food. This happened from about August through November of 2018, when I replaced it with another brand that seems better designed and safer (Kitchen Aid).

incident_description: This is regarding an Electric range with an electric cooktop.There were no injuries. We purchased this Range March 1, 2018. All was well with the Range until we noticed pitting on the gasket surrounding the cook top. We put a warranty claim on this issue. Today December 17, 2018 I received a phone call From LG. I was advised by the LG representative that this pitting was probably caused by contact with hot cookware or a scraper. He advised me that the rubber gasket was designed to prevent liquids from getting below the cook top and reaching the heating elements and cause an issue with damage or possible fire. This gasket is 2.5 inches from the heating element. It is a small margin of error to not have hot cookware moved 2.5 inches while cooking. Now we have a pitted gasket that may allow liquids to penetrate down to the heating elements. We don't feel comfortable or safe with this issue.
justification: No injuries occurred, but there is a potential safety issue with the pitted gasket allowing liquids to reach heating elements, which could lead to damage or fire.

incident_description: Was using the self clean feature on my LG range, LRE3083ST, I have used this several times in the past with no issues. During this cleaning noticed a strange smell and upon investigating after the cycle was over and oven cooled i saw where it had burned away part of the sealing on my cabinet and discolored my granite counter. This only happened on one side. I contacted the company and have sent documentation to them about this hazard and I am currently awaiting to hear back from them.

incident_description: I was cooking beef stew in my oval CrockPot for about 2 hours on high when we heard a loud pop.  When I went to stir the stew about 30 minutes later, we found the lid was shattered into tiny pieces. My husband tried to lift the lid off, but the handle came right off and pieces of glass fell into the food.
justification: The incident involved a shattered lid and glass falling into food, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that his stage left burner has been overheating. When cooking on Medium, the consumer notes that the burner turns red hot, at times ruining the food content. The consumer has not noticed this behavior from the remaining three burners however he has ceased use of the burner in question because of safety concerns.

The consumer states that prior to the incident, the oven was used three to four times per week whereas the cooktop was used daily multiple times.

The consumer is unsure if he will be keeping his oven range for at least the next thirty days.

Update:
Both 8-inch burner switches (significant) show evidence of arcing.  When the control knobs are removed there is soot on both the knobs and the switch.

The 6-inch burner switches appear normal.

After contacting MFG, response was warranty had expired and they were no longer responsible.

incident_description: Purchased Oster 6-slice countertop oven (model TSSTTVSK01 on 10/06/2017.  On 11/15/2018 we used it with the timer feature and saw the on light go off when we were done. The only way to keep it turned off is to unplug it.  Fortunately we were home and noticed the problem fairly quickly or we likely would have had a fire.

incident_description:
In June of 2018, I replaced my former Black and Decker digital convection toaster oven with this new, out of the box, Black and Decker countertop convection toaster/oven (Model TO1640B).  
I purchased this current oven at BIG LOTS on North 72nd St in Omaha, NE in 2013.  (I stored it a few years because I thought my former toaster oven was failing, but discovered a button stuck on it, and once that was corrected the oven lasted another 5 years). 
After some months of using this current oven, it became apparent that there was some design flaws that gave me concern of its safety and potential fire hazard.
Two main problems have occurred repeatedly over the past few months, and it wasn't until recently that the oven was discovered ON and Very hot after having supposedly shut off over an hour prior.
This occurs in one of 2 ways:
1. If you are wanting to toast or heat and item for less than 10 minutes (as in a 2-3 minutes to toast an item and fail to turn the dial for the toast/timer far past 20 and then counter clockwise to the 2-5 minutes, the unit will stay on at whatever temperature the dial setting for TEMP is at, and will remain on for an infinite time. (this happened most recently on Sunday December 30, 2018, though it has happened on other occasions prior).  with this incident an piece of bread still remained in the oven and upon smelling the burning some long hour or so later, it became evident the oven was still ON.
Even though the appliance has a note to turn past 20 before setting the time, this seems haphazardly dangerous and has no safety measure to assure an operator has done so.  The oven will operate in the ON once the dial deviates slightly from the OFF point on the dial.

2. The second way this oven inadvertantly remaining ON unknown to the operator is that if you manually turn the TIMER/TOAST dial to the OFF point, it does not stop there, it will continue past the OFF point and turn the oven back in the ON status.  You do not have to turn it counterclockwise to the point where it says STAY ON for the oven to be turned back on with out noticing.  You think you have turned the oven OFF because an audible bell dings when you get to what you would think is OFF, except the dial doesn't have much of a safe check to keep you from overturning it.  I want to emphasize that you can just slightly over turn it counter-clockwise and it will turn the oven back on.  
Rotate it another half inch counter clock wise and you will reach the STAY ON point of the control.
The big problem here is you don't have to turn it all the way to STAY ON point for the oven to return ON, it only has to be just slightly a jar the OFF point.  
I keep my oven in a large appliance garage.  The door is open and has very adequate ventilation around it and above to operate safely.  A problem occurred when the unit was presumed off and the door was shut to the garage.
 It's not a safe appliance and I have removed it from my kitchen.
I spoke with Black and Decker consumer services regarding my concern and that do not intend to take any action over the matter.  I have asked that my complaint be brought to the attention to there product engineers and follow up with me.  There has been no correspondence what so ever.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to design flaws, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was given a coffee mug as a gift. I've had this mug for several months and have used it without incident for drinking coffee. Yesterday, I put the mug in the microwave for the first time to heat up some milk. I ran the microwave for 1 minute 30 seconds. When it was done, I grabbed the mug by its handle and was burned. I used a pot holder to take the mug out of the microwave.  The milk in the mug was not very hot but the handle and the body of the mug was extremely hot. I waited for it to cool down, then poured out the milk and then looked at the bottom of the mug to see if it wasn't considered microwave safe.  The stamp on the bottom said it was both microwave and dishwasher safe. Today I have a red mark on one of the fingers I used to try to pick the cup up with, and some small blisters are starting to form.

The reason I am reporting this is because the cup is dangerous to use in the microwave. I'm not happy about being burned, but I'm more concerned about these cups being on the market and being considered microwave safe. If there's a burn danger there should be a warning on the cup. I've used lots of stoneware in microwaves. If they are safe for use, they stay reasonably cool when heating up liquids-especially handles that don't come into contact with the hot liquids.

The stamp on the bottom of the cup says it was made by Royal Norfolk and imported by Greenbrier International Inc.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and blisters, indicating an injury, and the likelihood is possible given the misleading microwave-safe label.

incident_description:
I purchased a JGC1536BS Jenn-Air gas cook top range in July of 2017.  The unit was installed by the vendor installation firm.  Almost immediately after using the unit I noticed a situation when using the front left burner.  The issue is, when you have a pot or pan on top of this burner with the burner in use, the dial knob gets extremely hot to the point it now longer function.  When turning the knob to the right to turn it off, you quickly notice how hot it is and it gets stuck in lowered position which causes the ignitor to continue to try and light a flame when the gas is off but the know is stuck in the lower position which is the ignitor on position.  The natural instinct is to lift the know in or to get it out of ignitor mode. Because the know is stiff due to the excessive heat, you pull up strong and then the know pulls off the stove and now is in your hand.  When doing so, you can get burned while lifting it and then you instinct is to release it from you hand so than to reduce the impact of a burn at which point you are know juggling it while burning yourself. The know is heave and you tend to try and keep it from hitting the cook top, counter or floor to avoid damage and the result is a burn on your hand, arm or other part of your body. 

I called Jenn-Air service a number of times. The first time, Jenn-air sent a tech out and the tech determined that the pot I was using was too close the knob.  I did not agree because the pot was centered on top of the burner.  I agreed to continue to use it and told the tech I would call back if the issue were to happen again.  The issue did happen again and this time it happened to my daughter.  I called Jenn-air back and there sent another tech.  Jenn-air also connected me with their safety department at which point I made a formal complaint.  no one called me back from safety so I call them back.  I spoke to a person and they said they would discuss with the tech coming out the second time  

When the tech came the second time, I showed him an example of the situation with a pot on top of this burner even pushed further away from the know and now not centered on the burner (which is not an optimal uses case) and the same situation occurred.  The tech when out to his vehicle and came back with a device to measure the temp of the know.  The tech also agreed the know was not working properly because it was too hot and he agreed that the temp reading of the know was outside safety requirements.  He called Jenn-air while on site and they said I was not using the cook top properly.  

This is no doubt a design flaw which makes this device unsafe and it does not perform as advertised.  

Multiple family members have been burned with scars as a result and the device is only partially usable.  

Jenn-air refused to do any further investigation.
justification: The incident describes multiple family members being burned with scars, indicating an injury severity level. The issue occurs consistently when using the front left burner, making the occurrence likely.

incident_description:
This regards an LG gas stove cook top, model LCG3091ST.

The safety issue is that the burner control knobs easily break with normal usage and one such breakage jammed the burner gas on before it was ignited and couldn't be turned off until I got a pliers and was able to turn it off.  Quite a bit of gas had been released at that point.  If I hadn't had pliers handy it could have been very dangerous, more so than it already was.

Details:
We purchased it in 2014 and had it installed in our kitchen.
The problem is that the knobs that operate the burners are poorly designed plastic and they break off with normal usage.  We have had to replace *at least 5* of them over time with the first breakage happening within about 9 months of purchase and installation.  One of the broken knobs left some part of the knob in the control jamming it in an "on" position without the gas being lit.

Given that I have replaced at least 5 of them over time it is clear that they are poorly designed and our experience is not an isolated incident.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a broken knob, which could have been dangerous but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
LG Electric Range Mod LRE3023FW, Serial# 303MMNT01519, MFG Date: 3/2013 Monterey, Mexico

The above product that I own which was purchased new from a Tupelo, MS dealer has presented a dangerous FIRE HAZARD for the following reason: This unit has four (4) cooking elements and one (1) warmer element. The danger that has developed is that when manually turning the back left element on, the left front element also automatically turns on and stays on until the left rear unit is manually turned to the off position.  Also when manually turning the warmer element on which is located at the rear center of the stove, the left front element automatically comes on and stays on until the warmer element is manually turned to the off position.  The left front element  has the highest wattage and therefore heats to a much higher temperature.  This presented a very dangerous situation recently when a skillet of food had been cooked on the left front burner element and the element was then turned off manually as the manual switch indicated that it was turned off.  A second pan of cooked food was then placed on the back center "warm" element and then the warm unit was turned on to the number 4 position in order to keep the pan of food warm. The warmer unit was the only element turned on and I went outside the house for a few (about 10)minutes and heard the smoke alarm inside the house.  I ran in and saw the pan on the left front element ablaze and the whole house was filled with dark thick smoke and it was difficult to breathe. I immediately extinguished the fire and removed the burning skillet. I then confirmed that the only element showing in the "ON" position was the warmer element which I turned off. Luckily at this incident, there were no bodily injuries or expensive property damage. I have re-confirmed several times that when either the left rear or warmer element manual controls are turned to the "ON' position  the left front element automatically comes on and stays on until the left rear or warmer elements are manually turned to the off position.  I believe that this situation definitely presents a very potentially hazardous threat to life and property and should be investigated and remedied immediately for this particular make and model of LG Electronics electric free standing range. Thanks, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The malfunction is reproducible, indicating a likely occurrence.
