incident_description: Our GE Profile dishwasher caught on Fire while washing dishes.  Model number PDW8200J03BB; Serial number VG813932B.  While washing dishes my wife and daughters were upstairs and smelled smoke and came and got me in the garage.  Smoke was coming out to the top of the dishwasher and it smelled like an electrical fire.  We immediately dialed 911 and I shut off the power to the dishwasher at the wall switch and at the breaker.  After opening the door the smoked was coming out the opening of the latch.  I covered it to snuff out the fire.  The door was extremely hot to the touch around the top behind the control panel.   The fire appeared to stop once the power was killed and snuffed out.  However, the house was filled with the fumes of the fire which smelled very chemically like burnt electronics and plastics.  This smell of the fumes made everyone feel sick and gave us each a headache.  It trigger a migraine for my wife that lasted a week after the fire.  The smell has lasted for weeks despite having opened all of the windows.  The migraine came back again for several days after we returned from Christmas break having been out of the house for 12 days.  We had a GE service technician come out and he said that the connector to the control board had caught fire.  He said this was the same defect that he had seen on other dishwashers had been recalled for but our particular model was not on the recall list (I have pictures if needed).  The unit was un-repairable due to the fact that the replacement parts are no longer available.  This could have burned our house down and forced my family and I to breath in toxic chemicals.  This model needs to be added to the recall list so that others are not injured.
justification: The incident caused physical harm (headaches, migraines) due to toxic fumes, and the fire posed a significant risk of severe injury or death.

incident_description:
At 2 am my wife woke me and said she thought something burning inside the house.  We discovered that our GE Profile dishwasher heating element was still on and had melted most plastic items inside including both racks.   I unplugged the unit to stop the heating elements and let it cool down, then removed the unit to see if any of the cabinets were burned.  Fortunately there was no signs of the wood cabinets scorched or burned.

However the granite counter top was too hot to keep you hand on it.  We feel very fortunate that it did not catch the house on fire.

This is a GE Profile Dishwasher model number PDW9700N00II & serial no. AR735087B

We are concerned to learn this has happened to other models before.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that caused significant damage to its contents and heated the countertop, but no injuries or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Any accidental bump to stove-top controls can VERY easily open valve; approximately half of the time, initiating igniter (easier to notice, but filling kitchen with gas is equally dangerous).
 Has caused three flash fires the worst of which ignited a sheet of aluminum foil which burst into flames and actually adhered to my clothing.
justification: The incident describes flash fires and a sheet of aluminum foil igniting and adhering to clothing, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
Life or death safety Issue with new LG refrigerator.ÃÂ ÃÂ Purchased a new refrigerator which was delivered on 1/21/19 a little over 24 hours later after following the manufacturerÃÂs instructions on the water and ice maker with extra safety precautions I was choked by a piece of plastic that broke loss from the top cover and fell into the ice maker but fortunately was able to get it out.ÃÂ ÃÂ 

The plastic scratched the back of my throat causing it to swell and become sore.ÃÂ ÃÂ I went into other stores to look at their floor models to see if it was just my unit but looking at other models from 2018 they have the same type of ice maker and the same problem existed.ÃÂ ÃÂ Models before 2018 used a different plastic and did not have the same issue.ÃÂ ÃÂ 

I worked as a mechanical engineer in production and felt that the manufacturer should know so I contacted them first on 11/24/19, but felt that they are not taking it serious enough. They mailed a replacement part which had the same defect. They have finally offered to buy the refrigerator back, but this will not ensure others are not injured or die from it. I have not returned the call due to the weekend and ensure that I have a replacement refrigerator in place when they take theirs.  They have had enough time to inform the public so that they understand what they need to look for so that no one will get injured or killed.

LG did take the top cover and the ice maker during the two service calls.  However, I still have the piece that choked her.  Examining other ice maker top covers at other stores you will find burrs on them as well.  Enough vibrators or impact to the top cover will cause them to fall into the ice maker.
justification: The incident resulted in a physical injury (scratched throat) due to a defective refrigerator part, and the issue is present in multiple units, indicating a systemic problem.

incident_description:
This 69 year old caller is reporting that he purchased a food processor sometime maybe in 2015 and had no problems with it until around June/July 2018.
The unit was always kept unplugged and in a cabinet if no in use, however in June 2018 the caller's wife took it out of the cabinet then plugged it in and it immediately began smoking then caught fire.
The caller grabbed the plug and unplugged it then threw it outside which extinguished the flames.
He couldn't estimate the flame size, it happened very quickly but it was hot enough in those few seconds to scorch his counter top.
He said that he was able to restore the counter top to its original appearance with a well trusted scrubbing cleaner.
There are no injuries
He contacted the manufacturer who sent him a form to populate with information but he said that the form asked for his social security number and birthday which he did not feel comfortable providing to a company he was complaining about.
He will keep the unit for 30 days as requested on the incident report.
This unit was recalled with release# 17-050 and remedy was received by caller approximately one year ago.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, and the product was already recalled, indicating a known issue.

incident_description:
(11/12/2018) Guests in home accidently brushed against the stove knobs. The consumer woke up the next morning to the smell of gas. But luckily, she was able to turn on the light switch without causing any harm.

The consumer's concern is that the knobs are being made where you don't have to push them in to turn them on. 

The consumer also stated that she had the same problem with a [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] stove, but will download forms from the Saferproducts.gov web site and file a report.
justification: Guests accidentally turned on the stove knobs, leading to a gas leak, but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description: My refrigerator was being used a normal amount, not opened and closed very often. It was purchased in June of 2013 and this morning I woke up to an acid-like smell in the air. I thought maybe someone in the house had lit a candle the night before. I did not notice any smoke at the time. I performed my normal morning routine and then was heading out of the house to go to work and heard the sound of popcorn popping. I walked into our kitchen and noticed a flickering light against the wall behind the refrigerator. When I looked behind it I noticed flames shooting out of the back of the appliance. I pulled it out away from the wall and unplugged it. The fire was coming from the lower left corner of the back side of the refrigerator. Near the compressor. I called the seller and they gave me the number for Frigidaire and I called them and they said there weren't any recalls and of course the warranty is only 1 year long. They offered to help me locate a repair tech in my area but, that is not going to happen.
justification: The incident involved a fire from the refrigerator but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We had turned on our dishwasher after Sunday morning breakfast.  Near lunch time, the dishwasher had stopped running, and we thought it had completed the cycle.  There were no panel lights, and the basin inside was still full of water.  I checked and found that the circuit breaker had tripped, and reset the breaker, but still no indicator lights on the dishwasher control panel. Troubleshooting led to finding that a fire had occurred in the OEM electrical connection box under our sink.  

Dishwasher is a Bosch SHX65T55UC/02, serial FD950300169.  We were very close in number to recalls involving the cord, but were outside of the affected serial number range.  We contacted Bosch and they sent a technician out at their cost, and Bosch determined "improper installation" by Sears (where we bought the dishwasher and installation).

As an electrical engineer, this is a terrible design, and we were fortunate to not only be home at the time, but also that our circuit breaker did its job in interrupting the fault in progress.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher's electrical connection box, but no injury or death occurred, and the circuit breaker functioned correctly to prevent further damage.

incident_description:
Frigidaire and Electrolux ICON Electric Smoothtop Cook tops and Slide-In Ranges 
Model Number: PLES389ECH
Serial Number: NF80222152
Purchased: New 06/2008
From: Morris Home Appliance Macon Ga



So My mother who is 76y/o has the stove model number listed above

She purchased it around feb 2008 and it has been a great addition to the family.

I must add my mother does a large amount of cooking especially baking professionally baked homemade cakes.
Well on yesterday she initiated the self cleaning function on the range like she does on a regular schedule following all directions by manufacture

Horribly, near the completion of the self cleaning the range begin to smoke from the control panel with a smell quite different from the cleaning. The stove had caused an electrical fire somewhere under the panel area.

This mortified me because she initiated this at bedtime

Oh no! [REDACTED], I understand your concern about your mother's range. I will be glad to review your situation with you.

May I please start with her first and last name, full physical address, and telephone number?

to conclude I was awakened to her and my 90y/o father frantically trying to disconnect the stove from its electrical source until finally we had to flip the breaker inside the main power box in the house

It seems that a very large connector inside of the control panel had caught fire and was incinerating all wires and plastic connectors in that area.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but resulted in no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) since such events are not common but are documented.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the heating element in the oven erupted in flames while it was in use.  He stated that it was approximately 30 mins after the contents was placed in the oven that the incident occurred.  They tried to contain the flames by using a fire extinguisher but that didn't work.  His son quickly used the circuit breaker to switch the power off.  The fire destroyed the interior of the unit.  The fire department was called and a fire report filed.

Caller feels that they experienced similar problems of recall #09-189.  

Caller stated that he did not contact the manufacturer as yet.
justification: The incident involved a fire that destroyed the oven's interior but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Our KitchenAid dishwasher was approximately 12 years old. During an ordinary wash cycle, I heard the unit arcing inside (Popping/ripping noise). I opened the door, which shut off the unit, and I turned off the circuit breaker (which had not tripped). After disassembling the dishwasher door, I found a seriously charred wiring termination at the main control panel. If I hadn't been nearby, the unit would very likely have caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved a serious electrical fault that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The electric water kettle does not automatically turn off when the water comes to a boil, as it is supposed to. We exchanged the kettle for the exact same model thinking the first one was faulty, however, the second one does not turn off automatically either.
justification: The kettle not turning off poses a potential safety hazard but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The gas range was in normal use, with the oven on but no burners going. My wife was in another room and heard buzzing and popping sounds, and entered the kitchen to find the range smoking and with flames coming from the back left corner. She grabbed the fire extinguisher but the flames had subsided by that time. I arrived home from work about 3-4 minutes later and pulled the range out to disconnect the plug and turn off the gas service. I could see smoke and what appeared to be electrical arcing marks at the back left side where the electrical power cord entered the unit. 

The next morning I removed the unit back and could see that the entire wiring harness was melted, plastic harness connectors had melted, and various wires were severed by the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire and electrical damage but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: On several occassions over past 5 years our Frigidaire Self Cleaning Range model FEFB78DQL serial number VF70120266 has had front left burner would continue heating when turned down or when off.  We had to turn it on and off several times to get it to shut off.  This has led to burnt food and ruined pans.
justification: The burner malfunction caused burnt food and ruined pans, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the cooktop portion of her oven range turns on and off by itself repeatedly after use even though the knobs are in the locked position. The consumer states that sometimes it takes her two to three minutes jiggling the knob in order for it to stop turning on and off. The consumer indicates that on one occasion, the oven range damaged a pot because she was not aware the unit was on.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative she spoke to informed her that the oven range was not under any recall thus she would be responsible for any labor and parts if she chose to have a Service Technician inspect the unit.

The consumer states that the cooktop is used once daily whereas the oven was used twice weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping her oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning cooktop causing property damage (damaged pot) but no injury, and the issue occurs frequently during daily use.

incident_description:
12/12/18  I put our Whirlpool built in oven on the #2 cleaning cycle for the first time since we moved into new home 4 years ago.  About an hour into the cycle I heard a loud boom and  as I ran into the kitchen hot glass was being rocketed out of the bottom of the shattered oven door and was flying all over kitchen.

Whirlpool Gold Series household electric range
Model # - WOS92ECOASO2
Serial # - D45019865

There were no injuries by the grace of God as I had just left the chair facing the oven a few minutes before the explosion.

I called Whirlpool customer service and the rep said my warranty was for only one year and since there was no fire , smoke or arcing - this was not a safety issue.  She ask me  a series of  questions for the safety team and said they would determine if I would get a call back within the next 24 to 48 hours.
She said since this is not a safety issue - we would have to pay for all repairs  or new oven.

Even if we get the glass door replaced - the question around the safety of the self cleaning system is an issue.
We are very discouraged with the response from Whirlpool.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of the oven door, but no injuries were reported as the person had moved away just before the event.

incident_description:
The problem started approximately 2 - 4 months ago.  The wife turned the burner off after cooking and sat down for dinner  Twenty minutes later, the consumer went into the kitchen and found the burner on high.  He checked and saw that the control knob was in the off position.

The consumers discontinued use of that burner, but they have mistakenly used it once in a while.

The left front burner only has the problem.  The consumer noted that he and his wife normally use the right burners, because they are right handed and there is more counter space on that side.

They have not been any injuries and no property damage, but since they became aware of the problem, they closely monitor the use of the range.

The consumer went to the local retailer where it was purchased.  He was referred to a Sears number and then he was redirected to Kenmore Customer Care.  He also spoke with those companies more than once, prior to being referred to the CPSC Hotline, today.

The consumer is concerned about the potential fire safety issue for his family and believe that this should be addressed by the mfr.

No one at Sears or Kenmore offered to take additional details from the consumer even though he mentioned  CPSC Recall# 09-333 and said he felt this presented a safety hazard.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injuries or property damage occurred; the issue is monitored but still occasionally used.

incident_description: I'm concerned because I just purchased a Whirpool gas range. I used the oven for the first time and all the outside surfaces got extremely hot including the knobs to the burners and the oven door handle. I don't have children but I think it poses a great risk of burns by simply touching any part of the stove.  Model WFG320M0BB2 (Serial # VE839 23958)
justification: The stove surfaces getting extremely hot poses a burn risk, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I purchased a Dynasty gas range in 1997 ( model DRGSC-30-4 ): the oven igniters are too far away from the burners. When I turn it on it takes a while to ignite and when it does there is a small explosion. It has been this way since I bought it but not as bad in the beginning. I checked the recall on this model and saw where my model was recalled from  stores that sold them from 1998. The company handling the recalls told me that my model was mfg. in 1996 and was not on the recall list even though my serial number ( 181296-SS ) appeared in your recall notice. Please let me know if my range is or is not a valid recall unit. Just because it was mfg. in 1996 should not be a reason to keep it from being a recall. I would think that the earlier models would have the same recall problems as the ones sold from stores in 1998.

Please advise. I donÃÂ t feel very safe with the range at this point.

Sincerely,
justification: The incident involves a gas range with delayed ignition and small explosions, posing a safety hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Last year I found my LG range didn't stop heating after reaching the set temperature. I found out it was part of a recall. I called LG and had it repaired. However while cooking for Christmas Eve the oven did it again.  This time it set something in the oven on fire.  
I am on the phone with LG again. They want to send another repair tech. However I am not confident that they can repair the range in a way that it will be safe long term.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven due to a malfunction, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The top edges of the supports that hold the handles to the fridge and freezer are extremely sharp. If you hold on that bracket and not the handle itself you could get cut like our daughter did. A guest almost cut themselves in the same way.
justification: The description mentions an injury (cut) and a near-miss, indicating both actual harm and a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Flame and sparks came from GE cooktop 
Model PP7030SJ1SS
Serial HH&18480Q
I turned it off.
Inspection underneath reveals burn marks on housing of control boards.
I am not using it as it is unsafe
Trying to get GE to respond. No luck so far
justification: Flame and sparks indicate an incident with no reported injury, and burn marks suggest possible recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description:
The range has a built-in grill which is ignited by a center knob. It should be ignited by turning the knob all the way to the left. A clicking sound is emitted and the ignition is via a glow plug and it glows very hot to ignite the gas burner.

While performing regular cleaning of the range, if the knob is wiped and the knob is moved slightly past the "off" position, the glow plug will turn on and try to fire the gas burner. No noise is noted.

The grill is usually covered by a stainless steel plate covering the grill so the activated glow plug is unnoticed. 

After a few minutes, the stainless steel cover becomes hot without any indication. The surface becomes a burning hazard. I've received numerous first degree burns by touching the surface that I had assumed was cool.
justification: The incident describes first-degree burns from touching a hot surface, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurs during regular cleaning, making it likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I had cooked chicken at 325 degrees for 30 min. I took the chicken out and then raised the oven temp to 425 degrees to cook my next dish. After the buzzer went off indicated it had reached the proper temperature, I opened the oven to put in the dish and the glass on the oven door shattered. I had glasses on, heavy oven mitts and a heavy canvas apron on. If I had not had these things on I would have been injured.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, but no injury occurred due to protective gear.

incident_description:
On 1/2/19, i preheated my oven to 350 degrees and later bumped up the temperature to 400 degrees.  I was heated up some taco shells.  I opened up the oven door to check on the food and the glass outer door shattered and glass started popping from the door.  

I have a KitchenAid Built in Electric Convection Oven -  Model No. KEMC308kSS01 / Serial No. XR3502585.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering, but there was no mention of injury, so severity is 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
Opened door inserting fingers behind the handle of the microwave where fingers encountered a strip of stamped steel that was detached from the adhesive backing.
Finger was lacerated, 10mm long, with bleeding.  Washed, applied ointment, and applied bandage.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring first aid, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such injuries can occur but are not frequent.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting her range for posing a fire hazard. She is aware her range was included in recall # 13-031 and she had an incident with the unit on July 20, 2018. She then contacted the firm and received the recall repair. However, she believes the unit has not been rectified. 

On December 6, she was baking a cake in the oven and had set the oven to 350 degrees. She also had a pot on the front left burner. After approximately 30 minutes of use, her daughter advised her that flames were emitting from the oven. She used a fire extinguisher to put out the fire. The unit has been unplugged and has not been used since the incident.

She contacted the firm and reported the incident. She was told that a technician would go out and inspect the unit. They also informed her that the unit did not need to be plugged in during examination. However, when the technician arrived he told her the unit had to be plugged in. She refuses to plug in the unit because she is worried an incident will occur. She told the firm she would plug in the unit if they provided a letter taking responsibility of any future incident that occurred but the firm refused.
justification: The incident involved flames emitting from the oven, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was extinguished without further issues.

incident_description: Our family had just turned our oven on to preheat it for dinner. Within five minutes, there was a very loud, explosion like sound. I had been standing two feet in front of the oven and felt debris hit my legs and feet. I looked down and the front glass window of our oven had exploded and shattered into lots and lots of little pieces. Thank goodness I had been wearing pants and slippers so I received no injuries, but most of all, thank goodness our two toddlers had not been near the oven. It was terrifying to even think of what could have happened.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing debris to hit the person, but no injuries occurred due to protective clothing.

incident_description: I put a dish into my Frigidaire Professional gas oven yesterday evening around 6:30 PM. The oven had not been used the entire day at that point and was cool. I did not use the oven, the food was being stored in the oven until I was ready to heat it on the stove about 24 hours later, today at 6:30 PM. The oven had not been used at all in the intervening time and the stove had been used at breakfast, roughly 10 hours prior.  When I removed the dish from the oven it was hot. I used an instant-read thermometer to test the food inside the dish and it was 147 degrees fahrenheit. I verified again that the oven knobs were all in the "off" position and that nobody in the house had used the oven. Now two hours later the oven is still quite hot, all knobs are in the off position and there is no reason the oven should feel hot.
justification: The oven heated unexpectedly without being turned on, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
On Christmas my wife was cooking in the kitchen when all of a sudden I heard a panic yell. I ran in and our microwave was having a spark fire that was turning into a fire on the inside. I opened the door to put it out where one of the sparks hit and burnt my finger. I took it outside away from our house. To prove it to Panasonic I turned it on again and took video and pictures of it happening and cleared again at my own risk. The microwave was heating butter in a clay bowl. There had never been any aluminum or metal products in the microwave and it literally was on FIRE! I contacted Panasonic and a couple emails later this was their (Panasonics) final response
 Mr. [REDACTED],

 

Based on the pictures you sent us, the unit is not economical to repair. Please discontinue use and dispose of the unit. 

If you buy a new Panasonic Microwave I will reimburse you 20% of the purchased price, not including shipping.

This offer is valid until February 4th, 2019. If you decide to accept the offer, send me the Bill of Sale for the new unit, the serial number, and new model number.

Once received the reimbursement will be processed.  A check will be mailed to you.  Please allow 5 business days to receive after processed.

 

Regards,

 

[REDACTED]

First, where is the explanation of what actually happened!? Second, they want me to buy another one of their products without any sort of safety response to this microwave catching pn firem Third, this microwave is $170 and I got it as a Christmas present 2-3 years ago. I have had a microwave for 10 plus years that was like 50 bucks that never did this. After further investigation I found out this has happened to other people and kind of the same response from Panasonic. So with a $170 microwave catching on fire, my finger burnt their response is buy our product again and we will take off 20-30 dolllars. May I add NOT INCLUDING SHIPPING as they state
Their product is a safety issue I wanted reassurance it was a fluke or something like that and a replacement. Yet, i got that.
justification: The incident involved a microwave catching fire and causing a minor burn injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description: Was preparing a meal using the manual food chopper made by Zalik.  Have used other foof choppers before, but this was the first time using this one. Wife purchased two from Amazon.  The chopper worked fine, but then it was time to clean it. The sharp thin metal cutting blades are incased in a 3.5 inch by 3.5 inch plastic frame.  The various size cutting blades snapped down into the top cover of the chopper.  I was using the medium size.  To remove the blade you must pry it up. The amount of force require cause me to slip off the edge of the plastic and slice open my thumb.  Three cuts and one very deep. Did not go to doctor.  Treated both thumb myself.  I said both thumbs because after wrapping thumb up and putting on a rubber glove to complete clean up, I ended up cutting other thumb just picking up blade assemble.  The plastic frame does not provide enough picking up surface to protect your hands.  Talk to another friend and she said the same thing happen to her.   My recommendation is for the manufacture remove locking tabs for blades and attach a thin lifting tab to them.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts, including a deep one, requiring self-treatment, indicating an injury without medical intervention.

incident_description: On 12/24/2017, our GE Profile Microwave Oven's glass cracked into many pieces cause some to fall out onto our stovetop.   The unit was not in use when this happened.  It had been used over 1/2 hour, but was off at the time that this happened.   My husband was the only one in the kitchen and thank God he was not hurt because glass was all over the floor.  My adult son was nearby and came to see what happened because it made a loud noise.   Since this happened we have had it taped close and put covering over it to keep anyone from using it.
justification: The microwave's glass cracked, causing a hazard, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she is just getting back into her home after a fire that occurred in her Kenmore range.  There was damage to her kitchen cabinets as well as damage to the stove.

(06/20/2018) The consumer stated that she turned on the self-cleaning feature before leaving for work but advised her daughter that the feature was on.  Her daughter advised her that during the self-cleaning of the oven, there was a carbon monoxide warning from the smoke detectors that had just been put up two weeks prior. Her daughter left the house and called the fire department.

It was later determined by the insurance company that the fire was caused by items in the storage bin that is under the oven. The consumer stated that she had lids for pots, warming stones and other items in the bin.

The consumer stated that nowhere in the owner's manual for the product does it advise consumers to remove items from the storage bin before using the self-cleaning feature. 

(12/03/2018) The consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that there is no recall on the product. The consumer was also advised to contact CPSC.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries or deaths, and the occurrence likelihood is considered possible given the described scenario.

incident_description: Dishwasher stopped working.  In the course of trouble shooting power cord was unplugged and replugged back in.  Shower of sparks emitted causing a fire.  Cord quickly pulled out.  Outlet and plug/cord charred.
justification: A fire occurred due to sparks from the power cord, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My husband purchased the 9 cups Bialetti Moka Express 3 weeks ago.  
We have used this type of coffee maker before and never had any issues.  
Somehow with this new one my husband cleaned the coffee maker and he didnÃÂt realize that the filter fell off of it.  That has never happened before. 
He started making coffee and the coffee grinds went up blocking it, and it exploded on his eyes, face and chest. 
This happened on Thursday, January 10, 2019 at 10:30am.  He took a cold shower to clean his eyes from the coffee grinds and we run to urgent care.   They treated him, and sent us to the burn center at the hospital and to an eye clinic afterwards. 
It was horrifying.  My husband was in extreme pain.  He has superficial burns in his eyes and around his eyes.  He has not been able to go back to his normal routine.  
Something needs to be done about this product.  ItÃÂs extremely dangerous.  That filter should not come off easily.  It needs a better and safer design. It needs more control before more tragedies happen.
justification: The incident resulted in superficial burns and required medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: A fire occurred in our kitchen on Jan. 20, 2019. This happened as a result of the knob on our stove being accidentally bumped and turned the stove on. This is at least the 4th time this has happened, this one resulted in injuries to my daughter. I've researched and this has been a common problem with Samsung ranges, and to date it appears that they have not taken responsibility for the obvious design flaw.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to a child and has occurred multiple times, indicating a recurring issue with the stove's design.

incident_description:
On Sunday evening, December 16, 2018, our Frigidaire oven had been on at a 425 degree setting for 30 minutes (including the pre-heat time). My wife was baking salmon and asparagus for our dinner with our daughter that evening.   Suddenly, my wife and I heard a crashing noise, and found that the glass door in the oven had shattered.  Being safety glass, it crinkled rather than explode.  There were plenty of shards everywhere.  The next day we called Sherman's Appliance store in [REDACTED], since that's where [REDACTED], our builder, had purchased the appliance.  
We moved into the home August 28, 2018, so expected the item would be covered under the one year warranty.
justification: The oven door shattered but no injuries were reported, only property damage.

incident_description: I was cooking food in a 9 x 13 Pyrex brand glass casserole dish.  The oven temperature was 325 degrees F.  The dish was inserted into a cold oven so the oven and the dish warmed together.  30 minutes into the cooking process, I heard a loud thump inside the oven.  Inspection revealed the dish had shattered leaving sharp glass shards throughout the bottom of the oven.  I removed what remained of the dish to a hot pad on the kitchen counter.  A few minutes later, the dish exploded again showering the kitchen with glass shards.  The glass shards were of various sizes from large chunks to grain of sand sized particles.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass dish but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are possible but not common, hence an occurrence likelihood of 3.

incident_description: The latch on the top failed under pressure and the unit literally blew its top.  A pice of the latch flew out and hit the back of my left hand hard enough to cause a bruise and swelling.  Guess IÃÂm lucky, it could have hit an eye!
justification: The incident caused a bruise and swelling, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such mechanical failures can happen but are not frequent.

incident_description: The glass door of my gas range oven exploded and shattered during use. Pieces of glass were spreading from kitchen all the way to the living and dining rooms.
justification: The glass door exploded and shattered, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: The door of the refrigerator fell off when it was opened. It appears as if the hinges were sheared.
justification: The refrigerator door falling off is an incident that could potentially cause injury if someone is nearby, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
There is a Electrical Shock Hazard and thus a LIFE SAFETY ISSUE with the LMV1813SB over the range microwave.

The hazard is that the threaded portion of the under unit light socket is hot/energized even though the light is not switched on. I have verified this case with a meter and it shows 120Vac between the socket's threaded portion and its reflector.

Normal & safe design practice is for the socket to be grounded (not hot, not energized).

What Happened:  While changing the under unit right side light bulb, I was shocked.  While threading the light into the socket, I was touching the threads of the light bulb and the other part of my hand touched the reflector.  I immediately felt an electrical shock. 

Had another part of my body provided the current path, the outcome could be more dangerous than the shock sensation and resulting jerk.  In some cases it could be deadly.

Replacing the bulb as I did is not unexpected:
- Changing the light bulb should be expected
- Given that it is a somewhat awkward potion to change the light bulb, it is reasonable to expect that the user may contact the threads which contact the energized portion of the socket as well as contacting the reflector which is at ground.
- It is not unexpected that another portion of one's body may be grounded to a stove below it or to another ground potential.  This would result in current flowing through the body core and potentially flowing through the heart.

I contacted LG and they indicated that the instructions say to wear gloves when changing the bulb (who does that).  They indicated they would look into it further.
justification: The incident involved an electrical shock, which is an injury, and the description notes the potential for more severe outcomes including death.

incident_description:
PROBLEM:  Control knobs for range top burners are easily turned on unintentionally, leading to a significant risk of burn injuries and house fires. 

INCIDENT:  On several occasions, a person leaning toward the counter (to reach an upper kitchen cabinet, etc), has unknowingly and accidentally pushed in one of the burner the knobs and turned a stove-top burner element on with their body.   This has led to the burner(s) turning on unintentionally without warning, which one one occasion, melted plastic objects on and near the stove, and starting a small fire of combustible material, which if not contained, could have led to loss of the entire house/structure.  

BACKGROUND:  The range-top burner control knobs are lightly spring-loaded and turn when pushed in slightly with minimal pressure.  Due to their location, it is easy to inadvertently push them in with the front of your body (near the person's waist).  

SOLUTION:  One possible solution would be to retrofit these controls with a strong spring requiring more pressure to push in, to release and then turn the control knobs.

This is an inherent design flaw of this widely available new glass-top electric range, installed in 2018.

EFFECTED MODELS:  The Model # is Samsung NE58K9430SS.  A slightly upgraded model (Samsung NE58F9500SS) also has the same inherent design flaw.  Sold by Home Depot, [REDACTED], and others.
justification: The incident has led to a small fire and could potentially cause burn injuries or more severe consequences, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence is likely given the design flaw and multiple reported incidents.

He contacted the senior technician by phone and was told that "you can not open the microwave door during cooking or it will trip the breaker"

Them instruction manual for the product (Kenmore 790.8033*) states under the heading "interrupting cooking"  "You can stop the oven during a cycle by opening the door."

Sear technician said he could not fix the problem because the senior technician said this normal behavior.

Checking on the internet by googling " micro wave trips house breaker " shows this problem to be wide spread.

This product is in the category of personal blenders which generally include three main components: an ingredients cup, a cover with an integrated mixing blade, and an electric motor. Furthermore, the majority of these integrated lid/blade mechanisms tend to be black in color and camouflage their presence on a counter or inside a dark cabinet.  

I implore the CPSC and manufacturers (e.g. Ninja) to implement simple safeguards to reduce the likelihood of injury. Ninja specifically produces personal and counter top devices containing sharp mixing blades yet donÃÂt include a protective cover to prevent users (and children)  from inadvertently contacting the blades.
.

Today, I called the Frigidaire Company and spoke with [REDACTED] at Customer Service. She checked to see if there had been a recall on our model. She said there had not. But, in looking on the internet there was a recall for the same oven for the same issue in 2012. We are concerned that our oven has the same defect as the ovens recalled in 2012, as our story sounds exactly the same as those that were recalled.

After our frightening experience last night, we felt the need to report it. We were told by Frigidaire Customer Service to contact a repair company, (at our expense) to find out what the issue is.

Her original warranty expired in August 2011.  She purchased a new protection plan for $322.13 - $500.00 limit coverage. Sears is aware it needed repair. 

She paid out of pocket - $322.15 + $79.92 -Total $402.07

She paid Consolidated Electric $204.01. Total cost - $606.08

The oven is definitely defective

The oven is in perfect condition.  It is well taken care of and not over and continuously used. The oven looks brand new.

Attached is a picture of outside and inside the oven.  You can see it is definitely new. 

She filled out the report form.

If any question, please call me at [REDACTED]. 

Thank you for your help.

Sincerely, [REDACTED]

If she was not home to shut off the oven it could have caused a fire.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injuries or damage occurred, and the issue was resolved by turning off the breaker.

incident_description:
Caller says that on thanksgiving for the past three years, her racks in the oven fall while cooking. Caller believed that it was the weight of the turkey but this year she cut the turkey in half before cooking it and when she pulled the rack out to check on the turkey that rack fell. Caller says that any amount of weight on those racks make them unstable and prone to fall.

No injuries.

Caller believes this is a burn hazard.
justification: The incident involves unstable oven racks posing a burn hazard, but no injuries have occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer turned her oven on and within one minute, the inside was engulfed in flames coming from the bottom vents. The consumer turned the oven off and also switched its circuit breaker. The consumer opened the oven door and sued wet towels to help the flames subside, a process which took approximately five minutes.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; a Service Technician is scheduled to inspect and possibly repair her unit on 11/07/2018.

The consumer indicates that, prior to the incident, the cooktop was used at least twice daily whereas the oven was used twice weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping her oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved flames in the oven but no injury or death occurred, and the consumer managed to control the situation.

incident_description:
The consumerÃÂs wife was cooking and when she was done, she turned off the burner however the burner stayed on until the consumer switched the breaker off to the unit. When looking at the unit, the affected burner is the front and left one. The consumer switched the breaker on and the unit would not turn off. A few days later, the consumer switched on the breaker and it seems to be working properly now however he does not trust the unit will not malfunction again.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation however he was given the runaround. He was provided several service shopsÃÂ numbers however when he contacted the shops, he was informed that they no longer work for LG.

The consumer indicates that the same incident occurred on the same burner on 08/28/2009; the oven range repaired when he contacted the Manufacturer and they sent a Service Technician on 08/31/2009.

The consumer states that the oven is used approximately once or twice weekly whereas the cooktop is used two to three times per day.

The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue has happened before, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
During a normal cycle, something happened with the electronic control board of our KitchenAid dishwasher. Areas around the control board were scorched and/or melted, and the dishwasher no longer works.  There was a strong smell of electrical burning in the house, and the circuit breaker was tripped.

The dishwasher was purchased and installed in December 2012. The model number is KUDS30IXWH7; the serial number is F23309215.
justification: The incident involved electrical damage and a tripped circuit breaker, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I recently ran out of Sodastream carbon dioxide gas to make seltzer. To save money I decided to try a device called a
Sodamod (http://www.sodamod.com/) that uses non-food grade paintball gas refills from sporting goods stores. This gas is contaminated with benzene which also causes headaches (https://bit.ly/2JBvXLH). I filled a 12 oz [REDACTED] paintball canister with paintball CO2 at Dick's sporting goods and successfully used my Sodastream unit. The gas, together with [REDACTED] antihistamine caused severe migraines which improved after stopping both. So together both the [REDACTED] and the CO2 gas were multiplying effects. I'm improving after stopping both. This type of adapter is popular and has three versions available. Style 1: amzn.to/2P302K1, Style 2: amzn.to/2P3KnKq, Style 3: amzn.to/2yI8ZhG . They aren't safe and should be banned.
justification: The incident resulted in severe migraines due to contaminated CO2 and antihistamine use, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the use of such adapters is popular but not universally harmful.

incident_description: On November 24th, I removed the 2 quart Pyrex dish from the cabinet and placed it on the stove.  I then transferred pot pie filling from my pot to the dish. It sat there as I preheated the oven to 400 degrees.  I then placed the dish in the oven on the metal rack. I set the timer for 25 minutes. When the timer read 16 minutes, I heard a loud explosion from the oven. When I opened the door, shattered glass and boiling pie filling were everywhere including on the pot pie next to it.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish exploding, causing a mess but no reported injury.

incident_description: I got this mug from Disney on Ice. The first time washing it, I stuck my hand in and it cut me up, I ran my finger around the rim and it has a sharp edge on the inside. I contacted the company who distributes it and they sent me a new one, assuring me the original was defective. I just received the new one and it is just as sharp as the original. These are not safe for kids if they aren't safe for an adult to handle. My hand had much tighter skin than my mouth- let alone, a child's.
justification: The incident describes a physical injury from a sharp-edged mug, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence with a replacement mug suggests the issue is likely to happen again.

incident_description: I was home toasting a bagel in a black and decker toaster model TR1278B type 1 and I was watching the toaster. I noticed  the right side elements dim from a dull orange showing they were on to near black showing they were no working, at same time the left side heating elements increased the orange glow to a light orange showing a intensity in energy. the toaster then produced a small blue flame.   I turned off power strip the toaster was on and the fire did not go out, I pulled out the bagel and it was not on fire.  the flame increased so I put a cup of water on it and it went out. the bottom of toaster shows on label intertek 3073283 made in china. it also says applica consumer products. sticker says QC 8 06 passed
justification: The incident involved a small fire in the toaster but was quickly extinguished without injury or significant damage.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased a glass casserole dish a few years ago made by Anchor. We've used the dish many times without incident. On 11/11 I made a beef taco casserole dish recipe by [REDACTED] that I've made many times, including in the subject dish. It exploded in the oven about halfway through the bake. The oven was set at 400, which the recipe calls for. The oven was fully preheated before the dish was inserted and the dish was at room temperature in our kitchen cupboard. I have a photo of the exploded dish in the oven.
justification: The glass dish exploded in the oven, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
November 9, 2018 at approximately 6pm my oven exploded and went on fire, scorching my kitchen cabinet.

Upon the General Electric technician examining the gas oven on November 14 , it was quite noticeable that only the burner area facing the igniter was black and damaged with holes from the explosion.   Instead of the General Electric technician being  accountable for the fire of my oven.  The GE technician used the word "corrosion" for fire damage of the gas burner, and quoted me $300 for the fire damage of the gas burner.   For gas standards I would expect a more durable material for a burner ( such as copper) This malfunction- explosion should have never occurred.   

Luckily no one was near the Gas oven range.  This is a safety issue,  and needs to be escalated to revise the standards for Gas Appliance manufacturing.
justification: The oven exploded and caused fire damage to the kitchen cabinet, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
The glass shattered when using the self cleaning feature of my GE range model JGS750SEFSS for the first time. I followed the instructions in the manual, and started the self clean cycle for 3 hours. About 45 minuets later I heard a pop in the oven and notices that glass had shattered in the oven. I stopped the self cleaning immediately. I am so thankful that I was standing by the oven when it happened, otherwise I fear that my house would have burned down. 

I did a little research and found that this issue has been reported all over the country back to at least 2015. This has the potential to be a big product liability case and could cause death and injury. I would hope that someone can put a stop to GE selling these dangerous products. An alternative would be to have them create a repair program to eliminate the danger of exploding glass. Nobody wants and exploding oven!

Also, this happened a few days before Thanksgiving and I will not be able to use my oven at all.

Purchased: September 2016. Oven door shattered on November 2018 the first time we used the self-cleaning feature.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no injury or death, and the issue is reported to be widespread, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: The GE microwave over the stove was installed in my new home when I purchased it about 6 years ago. It has never been used because it is too high for me. I am only 5 feet tall. I use a small countertop model. On November 14, 2018 in the evening I noticed flames through the glass door of the microwave. I opened the door and the flames were coming from the ceiling of the microwave, and the inside was burning bright red. I closed the door and watched to see if I needed to call the fire department. I am 81 years old and live alone. The fire went out on its own. I unplugged it the next day after it cooled. I called GE who was only willing to sell me a new microwave. They had nothing to say about a fire. I have since had an electrician out to check my electricity. He said the fire came from inside the microwave and that there were lawsuits pending from GE microwaves catching fire while not in use. There was nothing wrong with the electricity in my home.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injury or death occurred, and the fire extinguished on its own.

incident_description:
The induction stovetop turned itself on to its highest power setting without the control knobs being moved away from the off (straight up) position.   Turning the knobs would then sometimes change the setting, but never could turn it off.
If a pan had been left on the burner and we weren't home, the house could easily have burned down.

After turning it off at the circuit breaker I turned it back on to see if that helped.  The stove started beeping and the digital burner displays showed "Er" and then started flashing and again turned on the highest settings (Powerburst).   I turned it off at the breaker for good.
I have videos of the misbehavior.

Fortunately I purchased the 5 year extended warranty from BestBuy and they are supposed to come repair it.  However, given what is obviously a design flaw, the stove must be considered an ongoing hazard.

I looked online and see that there was a previous recall of similarly designed control panels.   Apparently they haven't really fixed the design, and this model should be recalled as well.   I would like to get my money back and buy a different brand without this hazardous history.
justification: The stovetop malfunction could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I bought 2 pot holders. This is what they look like after a on time use. As soon as I put them on the grates in the oven they melted. Consumer beware. The stock number was 6 39277 02567 8. I tried to complain about it at the distributor Greenbrier International, Inc. (which is owned by Dollar Tree)
[REDACTED] store but was told to contact Greenbrier
but if I wanted a refund she would give me 50 cents when I had a receipt that showed I payed $1.00. So BUYER BEWARE; YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR applies but this is CLEARLY WRONG!!! I told the manager in the store but it didn't phase him in the least. I wanted him to know that he is selling a dangerous product. They are still on the shelf and in all the Dollar Tree stores. I've been on hold for twenty minutes but thought I'd get better feedback by posting this.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (melted pot holders) but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) as the product is still on shelves and similar incidents are probable.

incident_description: There is 120 V between this appliance case and earth ground.  Measured with voltmeter.  Discovered after being shocked when touching another appliance that was at ground.  This appliance has a two prong plug which means it does not blow the GFI circuit if there is a ground fault.
justification: The incident resulted in a shock, indicating an injury, and the lack of GFI protection makes recurrence likely.

incident_description:
I purchased a slide in GE glass top range model: JS750DFBB, Serial No: ZG235145 on 02/07/17 from Spencer Tv & Appliance in Glendale Arizona. On or about 09/28/2018 very early in the morning I went into the kitchen and was astonished to see the glass on the oven door on the floor, it was still in one piece. We stored the glass in a safe place in hopes that could be repaired. Thanking that the glass was comedic and was safe to use my wife decided to use the oven. Being a heavy casserole dish and she was able to open the oven door with one hand and then with the oven door was down used the free hand to steady the dish to slide it to the oven, at that point the door spring closed and caught her two forearms causing second-degree burns. 

At this point, we realized that the glass was not just cosmetic but was part of the counterweight design of the door. I immediately called a licensed repair service to fix the problem. [REDACTED] came out on 10/05/2018. He removed the oven handle and added a double sticky tape to the bottom of the glass and all seemed great, of course, I had to pay the $100.00 service fee. The repair lasted two days, then in the morning the glass was on the floor, called the repair service out again. The repairman said if it falls off again there was nothing he could do. It seemed to him that it was a design flaw. Yes, it fell off again!!!! After a battle with GE Consumer Relations ([REDACTED]) GE did come out with their certified repairman an did repair it using the double-sided tape. they gave us a 12-month warranty, however, we are afraid to use the oven wondering if it will fall again hurting someone's feet or legs or another burn.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated failure of the repair suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I set the oven to self clean on the Precise Clean option. I had removed the racks and nothing was in the oven. Approximately 30 minutes later the inside glass exploded.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass exploding during a self-cleaning cycle, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The temperature controls will not shut off on our Kenmore Elite Stove. One of the burner we haven't used for a couple of years due to that happening and another is now malfunctioning intermittently.
We have had to unplug the stove to shut the burner off.  As a result, we never use one of the burners.
The control dials are on the front of the stove and if a child would turn it on, it could result in the stove being on high for periods of time we would be unaware of.
justification: The malfunctioning stove poses a risk of unintended heat exposure, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE Cafe dishwasher 11/2008. On November 6, 2018 I ran a load of dish, just as I always every night before go to sleep. Around 4:30am I woke up with a burn smell all over the house. We checked everything and when we got closed to the dishwasher the lights were saying done as usual but my husband burned his hand in the granite it was very hot the bottom of the small appliances on top of the granite were also very hot. We immediately unplugged the dishwasher. When we open the door a lot of smoke came out and everything inside was melted beyond recognition and glued together. The burned smell stayed in my house I had to keep the house open with the cold outside to ventilate and get the smell out. I unsuccessfully tried to contact GE over the phone then I emailed GE on 11/13/18 and they replied on the next day and scheduled an technician to come to my house on 11/17/18 for assessment. The technician assessed as damages not reparable and I should contact GE for a solution. I called GE today and since there is no recall for this unit and is passed the warranty they only thing they could offer me was a rebate to buy a new equivalent model which I would need to spend almost 1000 in another GE product. Not happy with that, I insisted this is a Hazard issue and should be looked further. GE supervisor said they are aware of the issue on these units meaning there is an issue they say mechanical but honestly is a manufactured issue on these units but since it is not a hazard so there is no recall. Everyone that reported the same issue so far it happened in different time of use so that seems not to be the trigger. Also everyone got lucky they got to it before the problem escalated. Do we need to wait someone get really hurt or have their house burned before this gets seriously looked at and the units be recalled? 

Damage assessment: 
- all dishwasher safe plastics were melted beyond recognition including my blender cup 
- most plastic dishwasher parts were melted beyond recognition - e.g. silverware basket totally gone lost all my silverware glued to it.
- could not move lower tray - wheel damage and plastic stalactites fusing everything together  
- GE technician reported damages not reparable offered a rebate and we would have to do an out of pocket of almost $1000.00, not counting on the items lost in the dishwasher. Silverware aprox $300.00,  blender cup $50.00, other dishwasher safe items $40.00.
The dishwasher is a GE Cafe model # CDW 9380N20SS serial # RR785976B
justification: The incident caused property damage and a minor injury (burned hand), but no severe injuries or deaths.

incident_description: The coffeemaker had been turned on manually to brew a pot. About 1 hour after brewing, I heard a crackling noise. It was still plugged in , keeping the carafe warm at the time. I investigated the noise, found the pot to have dark, acrid smoke coming from it (from the hot plate part) and I unplugged it. The smoke and odor of burning plastic continued to build so I grabbed the unit, threw it in the sink and put the fire out with water.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning plastic but no injury occurred, and such malfunctions are unlikely but possible with electrical appliances.

incident_description:
I was in the backyard with my son while he was drinking through an aluminum slurpee straw from 7-eleven.  We were walking back in the house when he tripped and still had the straw in his mouth. I turned to pick him up and he pulled the straw out of his mouth. He tried to scream but the only noise he made out was more of a gurgling. The straw had went through the rear of the roof of his mouth and there was blood spilling everywhere. He was gasping for air but there was so much blood he couldn't get a breath. I took him to the ER for treatment because I couldn't get the bleeding to stop and I didn't know how much more blood he could lose before it would be fatal. 
Marketing a potentially fatal product specifically to attract the eyes of children no matter how innocent a straw might seem, is purely negligent and a disregard for consumer safety.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring emergency medical treatment due to significant blood loss and breathing difficulty.

incident_description:
My client owned a Medelco 8 cup glass stove top coffee percolator, model #PK008. The glass percolator was on the back right burner of the stove while she was cooking dinner on 10/14/2016. She noticed that the burner under the percolator was on. She turned off the burner and went to remove the percolator. The plastic handle was not hot to the touch. She lifted the percolator off to place it on the butcher block next to the stove, at which point the inside plastic parts including the plastic percolator basket and basket stand became liquefied plastic and erupted out of the glass percolator.
The liquefied plastic splashed onto her hands, causing third degree burns to her right right hand and fingers, as well as scarring and other injuries.
The product is manufactured by Medelco, Inc. It was previously sold under the brand name "One All" and now under the brand name "Cafe Brew". The company operates its manufacturing business out of a facility at 54 Washburn Street, Bridgeport, Connecticut 06605.
User reviews on numerous online retailers, including Amazon, cite incidents of the percolator's plastic parts melting. These user reviews reporting that plastic parts "melted" date back to at least January 2012. Some user reviews include photographs showing the melted plastic parts.
justification: The incident caused third-degree burns and scarring, indicating a severity level of 3. User reviews dating back to 2012 show multiple reports of melting plastic parts, suggesting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description: The oven racks in my oven shrunk or the walls of the oven expanded. Whichever, the racks now do not fit and fall down.
justification: The incident involves oven racks falling due to size mismatch, which poses a potential hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Aicok air fryer- IÃÂve had this air fryer for less than a year . Tonight after using it and washing it out, I put the pan back into the fryer. After about 10 minutes I smelled something burning.  The air fryer was not turned on, but the heating element was operating and making the pan hot, Again, the fryer was not turned on and the fan was not working, but the heating element was operating. Upon removing the fry pan, I found two screws in the bottom of the basket ,apparently they had dropped from the fryer ÃÂheadÃÂ. 
I fear that if we had not been home, there could have been a fire.
justification: The air fryer malfunctioned with the heating element operating while turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Problem reported about a year ago.  Manufacturer acknowledged the safety problem and  agreed to replace microwave vent via Dan Marc Appliance WO 683673.  Piece was replaced on January 10, 2018.  The replacement did not last one year.  Both pieces of the vent housing have broken away and pose a serious safety hazard as the vent is over a four burner gas oven and is not secure. The vent housing can fall out onto a pot and of frying pan on the below gas oven. Please help me.
justification: The vent housing poses a serious safety hazard as it can fall onto a gas oven, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore electric stove/oven March 2017 (model 790.93013) and last night we were 10 minutes into a turkey getting braised when a spark appeared to come from the stove and the breaker tripped. I looked it over for obvious signs and with observers turned on the breaker again. After about 20 seconds a significant spark, almost a flame, jumped out of the upper left of the control panel and again fliped the breaker.
It is out of 1 year warranty but obviously a significant concern especially if the breaker had not done it's job.
justification: The incident involved significant sparks and a tripped breaker, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue recurred after resetting the breaker.

incident_description:
My Kenmore electric range/oven has a faulty "off" sensor for the oven. When I turn the oven and set it to any temperature, it heats to that temperature and beeps, but continues heating and never stops. If I leave it for five to ten minutes after beeping, the temperature inside has climbed to 600 degrees. If I never turn it off on the control panel, it continues heating until it reaches a critical temperature and starts making long "danger warning" beeps, and the only way to shut it off is to use the circuit breaker.

The temperature sensor is still accurate, because I have put two other oven thermometers inside to check. The problem is that it beeps when it reaches the desired temperature, but does not tell the heating element to turn off. When I press the "off" button on the control panel, the heating element turns off and stay off. So the only way I can cook in the oven is to manually turn the heat on and off every few minutes.

The danger is that if I do not manually turn it off within a few minutes, it burns the food inside, leading to smoke and possible fire. This is a very serious fire hazard.

My cousin has a similar stove made by Whirlpool (which makes Kenmore) that just had the same problem, so I am reporting it in case others have had this faulty problem too.

Brand: Kenmore
Model No. 790.92803013
Serial No. VF11248452
justification: The faulty oven sensor poses a serious fire hazard due to uncontrolled heating, but no actual incident or injury is reported yet.

incident_description: I own and LG Oven, Model # LDE3017ST, S/N 101MMAZ00096. The burner will not shut off. It stays on at the highest level.
justification: The burner not shutting off is an incident that could lead to overheating or fire, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
0n 22-Nov-18 we were using the GE ProfileÃÂ Series 30" Built-In Double Convection Wall Oven (Model Number = PT9551BL1TS) and the outer window of the top over shattered.  This caused several pounds of glass shards to be spread all over the kitchen creating a safety hazard.  In addition, the food items in the oven had to be tossed for fear of glass contamination.

Both ovens were on at the time - top oven at 350 degree F; bottom oven at 325 degree F.  Then the door just shattered.

The oven was installed on 11-Jul-2018 and has functioned normally even as high as 500 degrees F.

While no one was in the vicinity of the oven, the shattering of glass could have injured adults and children.  We choose to report this so it may be tracked with other incidents of a similar nature.
justification: The oven glass shattered, creating a safety hazard and potential for injury, but no one was injured in this incident.

incident_description: The right front burner comes on by itself, we have to turn the knob several times to get it to turn off.  This has been happening for several months.
justification: The burner turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, and it has been happening frequently over several months.

incident_description: DeÃÂLonghi espresso Machine Cup Plate has sharp edges .  I was washing the cup plate with a sponge and my side of my hand was cut deep causing extreme pain and perfuse bleeding none stop for 45 mins and then when I arrived to the emergency ward it continued to bleed for 35 mins more at hospital.  Accident happened 11/11/18. My right hand was was given 3 stitches.  I could not sleep for 2 nights due to the pain and suffering.  I felt sick for 3 days and am recovery .  Sticheches will come off within 2 days.  IÃÂm still feeling pain on my 3rd day.  This cup plate to the expression is dangerous for anyone and will cut anyoneÃÂs fingers or hand.  Very dangerous.  Needs filling down immediately.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut requiring stitches and caused significant pain and bleeding, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Put a 1 Quart Pyrex container in the microwave for one minute and 20 seconds and it EXPLODED! Shattered glass went all over the microwave.  The container had pasta in it. Container has MICROWAVE SAFE cast into the bottom of it.  This product should be recalled.  The problem appears to have been around for eight years.  Why is it still being sold?
justification: The incident involved an exploding container causing damage but no reported injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common despite the claim of an ongoing issue.

incident_description: The oven walls have warped with normal use and the oven rack will no longer fit in the slots - it often falls while cooking, and has dropped a few times when we leave anything heavier than a cookie sheet on it. This has been happening for months and just gotten worse. I see many other people with the same oven having the same issues - it seems to be defective and easily causes burns when you don't expect it.
justification: The incident describes a defective oven that causes burns, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue is recurring and affects multiple users, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
When using our Blue Star 30ÃÂ Natural Gas Wall Oven over the last 2 years we noticed our CO detector located on the 1st floor of our home would begin showing the presence of CO (numbers would climb from 0) and actually  alarm if the oven was On for more than 3 hours.  For the first many months we just thought it was do to the combustion of natural gas and since the majority of the time the oven is utilized for less than 1 hour ignored the concern.  Recently however I was preparing to get the oven ready for a good cleaning.  When removing the bottom plate that is over the burner I noticed the plate under it which I believe is formed specifically to equally distribute the heat from the burner throughout the oven was separated from the bottom plate and actually laying on the burner tube.  Further investigation revealed that this formed plate and the bottom plate were held together with what appeared to have been 8 rivets.  The rivets had all failed and were found on the very bottom near the burner tube.  This permitted this formed plate to fall unto the actual burner tube and I believe prevent correct and complete combustion.  I also believe the rivets failed do to the stress of the expansion and contraction of the formed plate during heating and than cooling.  Model # BWO30AGS.  Serial # 1106183.

Not as much as a safety concern (at least I donÃÂt think so) I also noticed the convection oven fan was not turning when powered On.  It just hummed.
My wife has been assuming that when she turned the fan switch On that it was operating.  After removing the fan from its housing in the rear of the oven I found a blade on the fan blade behind the plate (not the blades in the oven compartment) had several blades either warped from heat or bent from an unknown reason causing the blade to make contact with one of the motors supports brackets thus preventing it from turning.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven leading to CO detection but no reported injuries, and the issue is possible due to repeated use over time.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she placed her oven on self clean mode.  After the unit had completed the task she noticed that the heat at melted the top part of door handles under the knobs.  She stated that if the oven clean had not stop when it did there would have been a house fire.  She does not feel that the oven is safe to use anymore.

Caller stated that she contacted the retailer who advised her that her model was not included in a recall and to contact the agency to report the incident.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet but she will do so at a later time.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted door handles) and a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: An Anchor brand 5 QT baking dish exploded in my conventional oven when I was baking chickens at 350 degrees. The dish was shattered into many pieces of shards of glass. This ovenware was purchased sometime in the past 16 months from the Target in Allentown, PA.
justification: The baking dish exploded, causing shards of glass, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
We own Duralex Picardie tumblers (drink glasses) from Williams Sonoma, but twice now we've had problems with the tumblers 'exploding' with remarkable force and sound. 

This weekend I knocked an empty one onto our kitchen counter (so it didn't 'fall' other than its own height), and it exploded with a loud bang into 100+ pieces, almost none of them bigger than a half-dollar coin. It was shocking and took about 30 minutes to thoroughly clean up all the pieces. I was very glad that neither our children nor our dog were home at the time. 

I'm attaching photos showing how much glass was produced from this 'explosion'. 

The first time this happened to me, several years ago, I thought it was just a fluke, but that time it sent me to the emergency room for a scratch on my eye from a flying shard of glass.

And I just [REDACTED] and found many other reports of people amazed at how one of these Picardie glasses had shattered for them.

incident_description: While charging my SodaStream  (home carbonation machine) this evening, the bottle and machine blew up without warning. The bottom blew out of the SodaStream bottle being filled, and pieces of the machine flew out across the kitchen. I noticed the bottle I was using has an expiration date, and it says not to use past the date (it doesn't say why). To be honest, I hadn't noticed the expiration date (or at least had forgotten about it if I had), so perhaps using an out-dated bottle was my bad.  Who knew bottles could age in a kitchen cabinet!  I don't know if that is the reason it exploded, or if other fail safes failed). My machine and bottles have been in storage since 2016, and I've only recently pull them out for use again.  My plastic bottles and C02 were stored in my kitchen cabinet, the machine stored in a shelf in my garage. I've been using the machine all summer. I notice the past half dozen fills were slow to buzz, but I assumed it was because I was running low on Co2. I'm really clueless to what happened, but thankful I was not hurt by the debris, only startled; sad that my machine is now toast.  If the explosion was due to the bottle, might I suggest SodaStream place a clear warning such as  "Bottles used past the expiration date have an increased risk of bodily injury."  But really, should there be a risk at all?  Regards, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing damage to the machine and kitchen, but no injuries were reported.
