incident_description: I purchased new Bosch dishwasher model SHE3AR72UC/22 from Best Buy this January of 2018. The wiring through my wall for the old one (which I also installed myself in the mid '80s) has only two wires (line and neutral). I decided to ignore the grounding warnings and connected the two wires to the screws on the machine that are plainly marked L and N. I noticed later that when I grabbed my stainless steel sink and touched the washer at the same time I was feeling a slight electric buzz so I decide that I should ground it just to be safe. I did not kill the breaker for this. I was surprised that when I touched the attached wire to ground there were sparks and I could be lightly shocked having skin between the ground and the end of the wire. Something's not right. After some consideration, I decided to switch the L and N wires so that they are connected to what should be the wrong screws as they are labeled. Now, even without the ground wire connected, there is no shock between the sink and machine, and there is also no sparking or juice at the ground when I do connect it. My point is that if a responsible person made all these connections with the power off before turning it on, he or she would not know that there was a constant feed of electricity flowing to ground which is a short but not enough to trip a breaker. I believe that many of the recalled dishwashers with overheating cords causing fires may have the same reversed connections that I found on this new machine which isn't even included in any recall yet. I cannot find anywhere that this is a known cause of these fires.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock and potential fire hazard due to incorrect wiring, indicating a risk of injury.

We purchased a Samsung range for our kitchen on October 13, 2016.  It is an electric range - model # NE58K9430SS - for which we paid $1219 at our local Home Depot.  Since purchase we have had several close calls related to fire.  The knobs to control the cooktop are located on the front of the unit.  The knobs are very sensitive to touch and have been turned on without our knowledge with the slightest touch while cleaning or passing by.  Once we actually left the house without realizing the cooktop was on and returned to find the cooktop bright red and so hot that the overhead vent fan turned on in response to the heat.  Fortunately we had not left any pans or kettles on the stove.  The most recent instance occurred on October 7, 2018.  The burner was on without our realizing it and this caused a nearby pizza box to catch fire.  Again, we were fortunate to have been able to get the box outside before the fire spread.  These are two examples of several instances when the cooktop was on when we did not intend it to be.

In reviewing information online and in speaking with Samsung, it is clear that this is a known issue that has caused many other consumers similar problems and safety concern.  I received a call from Samsung on October 10, 2018 in response to a live chat and an email in which I expressed concerns about the unsafe functioning of this range.  The Samsung representative acknowledged this is a known problem.  Her only suggestion was that we use child-proof door handle covers on our stove knobs.  Given the sensitivity of the knobs, the use of the child-proof covers does not prevent the knobs from being activated.

We no longer feel that this range is a safe appliance for our home.  We feel that Samsung needs to take action to prevent a tragedy in their customers' homes.
justification: The incident describes multiple close calls with fire due to unintentional activation of the cooktop, but no injuries or deaths have occurred.

We were unable to start the dishwasher cycle without shutting off the circuit at the circuitboard.  The dishwasher is a Whirlpool that have been recalled because of a heater motor problem in 2005. We participated in the recall and had the part repaired on18 July 2005 but didnÃÂt know about the class action lawsuit. 

In checking the websites there are many reports of the circuit boards bursting into flames or exploding but there has been no recall on the circuit boards.  The model number of our dishwasher starts with G you too and the serial number is FR3801705 it was purchased on 13 November 2004 and installed on 16 November 2004.

 I just want other people to know about their propensity for these circuit boards to explode and/or burst into flames. We often left the house with the dishwasher running. Not going that we couldÃÂve come home to a burned down house.   I feel there should be some action taken by either the consumer product safety division of the government and/or the manufacturer who has been advised of this previously according to the attorney for the class-action lawsuit for the defective motors and by various news agencies that have reported this.  The manufacturer, whirlpool, has our information as they mailed us a copy of the first recall back on 8 July 2005.

We did have the fire department come to our home to ensure there was no active fire or hotspots.  The firemen were present when I removed the face of the dishwasher and exposed the circuitboard where we discovered it had melted.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher circuit board exploding and producing smoke, but no injuries or active flames occurred.

incident_description:
LG oven LRE3083st burners staying on. When the back left rear burner is turned on, the front left burner also comes on on high and will not turn off. Similarly, when the warming burner (center rear) is turned on the front left burner comes on on high and will not turn off. I put water on to boil on left rear burner, and almost burned myself when I came back to lift the pan off, as the front left burner was on high. Luckily, I did not burn myself. 

It happened first intermittently, but now is ongoing. I checked the LG website and was surprised to see that this range was not on recall, since it has the same issues that those recalled did.
justification: The incident describes a malfunction causing burners to stay on, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Kitchen aid toaster oven model KCO253CU.

This is the second failure of this oven I have had.  The first one failed and would not come on, defective switches.  It was replaced the replacement lasted about a year when it failed.  I had had problems with it not always turning off when the timer ran out but was able to have it go off by switching to toaster from bake.   This time it went off but after we finished supper my wife asked why the oven was on.  It had come on by itself and the only way I could get it off was to pull the plug.  I plugged it in this morning with all switches in the off position and it came on.  I will be cutting the cord and scrapping it will not buy another.  Kitchen Aid used to be one of the better quality appliances until they outsourced to china.  They have gone downhill fast since then.
justification: The oven malfunctioned by turning on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: I was using a 12 cup Cuisinart brand percolator in which the top is made of a plastic substance. Connair's Cuisinart after becoming old this plastic perking top breaks with no knowing of when and where it may break. One morning as my wife was making coffee it busted free and went over our countertops. If we where standing there we would of been severely scorched and burnt from this happening. I've written to the company and they said they would not replace and the plastic substance is on endless backorder. They didn't seem to care. Product # PRC 12 Model 60509B Serial number. This in my opinion should taken off the shelves immediately.
justification: The incident involved a plastic part breaking and causing a spill, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue is known but not frequent.

incident_description:
Product was turned on for about 1 hour and was in the drying cycle.

Caller says that there was smoke and flames coming from the product around 10:30pm. Husband attempted to open the door and burned his finger in the process. (Wife provided medical treatment). Once the door was open the product was still on and would not stop running. Caller says that she had to trip the breaker in order to get the product to stop. The fire stopped when the breaker was tripped and the product was turned off. 

Callers house was filled with smoke and the fire department had to come place fans all over the house to help with the smoke inside of the home. Caller believes this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved injury (burned finger) and significant property impact (smoke, flames, fire department response), but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Cooktop "Professional" Series

Model No. FPEC3085KS

Last night (09-27-2018) a horrible burning smell came out of the cooktop.  When I looked in the cabinet below, we could see FLAMES in the metal box under the control knobs.  I used a kitchen fire extinguisher to put out the fire.  We turned all the knobs to "off,"  but one element remained on  - even though all the knobs were in the off position.  I cut the power at the breaker box.  When I flipped the breaker back to "on," the same element came on, even though all the knobs were still in the off position. 

This cooktop is a fire hazard and should be recalled.  Had no one been home, there would have been a serious fire.

This is an ongoing issue with Frigidaire.  They had to recall cooktops in 2009 and 2010 for this exact problem --  burners turning themselves on and starting fires- yet this model was not recalled.  This is a life safety issue.
justification: The incident involved flames and a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. The issue is known and has led to recalls in the past, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Our dishwasher was being used as normal in the kitchen. It started leaking water from underneath. Upon inspection, I noticed that the heating element had sagged down into the tub and melted a hole through the plastic to the outside. It was not designed with enough support to prevent this. I reported it to the company and they offered a 30% discount on parts. It could have burned my house down. I am not the first person to report this and they have done nothing to protect their customers that own this fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Came home to find home smoke alarms going off and smoke filled rooms with light ash in a few places.  Smoke was coming from inside of the GE Profile Dishwasher.  Upon inspection we found the plastic utensil compartments completely melted on the bottom of the Dishwasher along with some other plastic internal parts and a plastic cutting board and other melted plastic items.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (melted dishwasher parts and items) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Our Whirlpool gas range came with our home. We purchased it this year, brand new. I was cooking dinner with our oven set to 375 degrees. My son walked by the oven (he is two) and patted the door. He normally walks by, and touches things either saying ÃÂhotÃÂ or ÃÂcoldÃÂ. This time he screamed. So I touched the glass myself. It was extremely hot. I couldnÃÂt leave my hand there for more than a second. I immediately contacted our contractor who referred me to whirlpool. Whirlpool sent a contractor out today, and according to him, after only having the oven for maybe 15 minutes, itÃÂs normal. He states our door only got 135 degrees ÃÂwhich is well below the UL standard of 180 degreesÃÂ. He did not leave the oven long enough because when I felt the door of the temperature he got it too, it was no where near as hot as when my son and I burned our hands. This is clearly dangerous and many people have reported this issue before with this model. Some ovens heat up, while others donÃÂt, so clearly some are defective and whirlpool is doing nothing about it! My brother in law also has this oven, turned it up to 400 and his door stayed cool to warm. He said he could leave his hand sitting on the door no problem. 

Another safety issue with this appliance is the easy to open broiler fold down door. Extremely dangerous for both adult and children.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to both the child and the parent, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) as multiple reports suggest this is a recurring issue with the model.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung Gas Range that when I put the Range in the self cleaning cycle the HEAT coming out from under the control panel is so severe, it causes the control panel to melt. I had this Gas Range repaired two times in six month. I had Samsung  come out to take a look at this problem, and they say there is no problem. The service men that came out all said for me NOT to use the self cleaning cycle, but they all will NOT put it in writing.
This is a manufacturers defect that they will NOT admit
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing the control panel to melt, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Burner fail to turn off after being switched off and the temperature setting can increase unexpectedly during use, posing burn and fire hazards.
justification: The burner failing to turn off and temperature increasing unexpectedly can lead to burns, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: My wife had used the Pioneer Woman Crockpot made by Hamilton Beach earlier in the day.  It had cooled off and as she started to washing the glass top of the pot it shattered causing pieces to fly into her face and eyes.  Her glasses protected her eyes and fortunately no glass embedded in her face.  This is a safety issue with Pioneer Woman cookware.  There has been other safety issues with other items manufactured for this company too.
justification: The glass shattered but no glass embedded in her face and her eyes were protected by glasses, indicating no injury occurred.

incident_description: My 4 year old son was drinking from his Contigo cup (most closely resembling the AUTOSPOUTÃÂ® Straw Gizmo Flip - Blue) recently and fortunately he noticed something in his mouth. He spit out the rubber piece shown in IMG_20180902_092852772.jpg. This piece came out while he was drinking and is clearly a choking hazard.  This should be investigated from a perspective of potentially issuing a recall, due to the risk to children.
justification: The child noticed and spat out the rubber piece, indicating no injury occurred, but the incident highlights a clear choking hazard.

incident_description:
I am very scared with the FIRE in my kitchen.  The GE Over the Range Microwave caught FIRE.
The fire was quick to spread and burned the entire microwave, the cabinets beside and above it.
The entire kitchen is "black and the house smells smoke.
The fire department powered down the entire house.
The fire was advancing to the attic, when the fire fighters were able to put it out.
There is major financial impact, as at least, my insurance deductible of a few thousand dollars and the fact that the insurance will up the renewal rate.
Please, any advice on how to best proceed?
Thanks.
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a significant fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I purchased Black+Decker electric griddle model GD2011B from a Target store in Roseville, MN on 3/11/18.

The box for the griddle clearly advertises "Fully immersible base without probe makes clean-up effortless."

But the instruction book cleaning instructions say "DO NOT IMMERSE THE UNIT IN WATER." and the bottom of the griddle also says "DO NOT IMMERSE IN WATER."

This product has Intertek / ETL file 2003398.

I am more inclined to believe the manual and markings on the product than the box. This means that people just looking at the box will put themselves in danger by immersing the griddle.
justification: The conflicting instructions could lead to incidents of misuse, but there is no report of actual injury or death.

incident_description: Outside glass exploded. Caller says that the oven had not been used for over 6 months and the glass randomly shattered. The oven and range were not in use and it happened out of nowhere. Caller says that the glass is supposed to be tempered to prevent any kind of injury incase this happens but there were big shards of broken glass all over the kitchen floor.  Caller believes this product is a laceration hazard.
justification: The glass shattered without causing injury, but the presence of large shards indicates a potential laceration hazard.

incident_description: I have this Samsung cooking range with model number NE58F9500SS and found out that is causing a danger in the kitchen because the range top knobs turns too easily.  The knobs are at adult hip height and turns on with the slightest contact -- a simple brush against the stove and a burner turns on. For us this resulted in a burning some of my placemats that was on the glass top and there are other few instances that might have caused a fire if we didn't see it.  -- this is a serious issue that Samsung needs to address.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned placemats) and poses a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Electric Smooth Top Slide in Range Model # PLES 389ECI.
Over the years there have been several occasions where the eyes come on with LITTLE to NO contact!! We already had one fire which thankfully we were able to contain because someone was IN the kitchen when it happened...but yesterday it happened again, for about the 34th time and we donÃÂt know HOW this is happening?!?! Thankfully my son walked in and saw the eyes blazing RED and turned it off!! If you SNEEZE in the direction of the oven,the knobs come on!!! I see there was a recall for this oven,what do I need to do?
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the range turning on unexpectedly, leading to a fire on one occasion. No injuries or deaths are reported, but the potential for harm is significant given the history.

incident_description: I purchased a set of Anchor Hocking glass food containers with blue plastic lids from MenardÃÂs in St. Paul, MN this past summer (about two months ago). These are the kind of bowls that are meant for food storage and are generally used instead of plastic tupperware-style containers. This morning I placed frozen blueberries and refrigerated yogurt in the container and placed the lid on the bowl. I got to work about 40 minutes later, ate the yogurt (the blueberries had thawed), and left the empty bowl with the lid on it on my desk, about 12 inches away from me. About 15 minutes after I finished the food, I heard a loud pop and looked up to see that the glass bowl had exploded, spontaneously, sending glass shards to a distance of about three feet. I was not injured. I have a picture of the glass shards that remained on my desk. Please consider a safety recall before someone gets injured. I will be discarding the rest of the set immediately.
justification: The glass bowl exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I came home with my toddler after a playdate.  Was making him a sandwich and placed my hand on the dishwasher panel.  It was so hot it burned my hand.  I knew something was wrong as the dishwasher had not been run since yesterday afternoon.  I grabbed a potholder to open it up.  the heat kept coming out of it.  I tried to turn it off by the buttons on the front, but to no avail.  Went downstairs to turn the breaker off.  After it had cooled down, we emptied it.  Upon emptying, we realized how hot it actually got as it melted most of our plastic toddler items.  I  want others warned about this dishwasher, because it looks like it was not part of the initial recall of ge profile dishwashers.  I also sent a copy of the pictures to ge so they can know
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and significant property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: This flatware will eventually snap off at the plastic and break from the metal.  It caused severe burns to my hand when the fork broke in half and my hand hit the plate and hot food flipped all over me.
justification: The description reports severe burns from the fork breaking, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the product's design flaw leading to breakage.

incident_description:
Junction box on Bosc Dishwasher model shp68t55uc caught fire and melted connections.  Seems similar to issue with this recall, but model not included on list.

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2018/BSH-Home-Appliances-Expands-Recall-of-Dishwashers
justification: The incident involved a fire and melted connections, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Right front burner on Frigidaire range oven comes on spontaneously. 
Frigidaire sent new burner switches which were installed by a qualified technician. This did not solve the problem as the burner continues to come on spontaneously continuing to result in a dangerous fire hazard. I contacted Frigidaire to report the fact that their proposed solution did not fix the problem. I was told by Frigidaire personnel that they would do nothing further as these switches were the only parts authorized to resolve the problem. 
The product recall was for this specific problem with this specific product. Their ÃÂ fixÃÂ did not work and they are telling me that I have to live with this dangerous situation.
justification: The burner spontaneously turning on poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: I was using a Rival Popcorn Popper Kitchen Appliance (model #RV-932) and the product began to smoke, burning the unpopped seeds in the bottom interior of the appliance. This product also produced enough heat to melt the clear plastic cover and had jammed and caused popcorn to nearly burn one other time. It was less than a year old!
justification: The appliance caused smoke and melting plastic but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: We bought the GE Cafe 30" Stainless Steel Gas Sealed Burner Cooktop (CGP350SETSS) on May 2017, and installed by professional on our countertop. In Sep 2018, I was cooking dinner as usual, by using the tri-ring burner in the center of the cooktop. Suddenly a huge BANG scared me. There was explosion and smoke raised at the control panel knob area. It smelled like burning wire. In case for future explosion and fire damage, I shut down the gas valve, and unplugged the cooktop. I can not see what's inside the cooktop, but it had strong smell. The gas company inspector came and detected gas leak at the cooktop.
justification: There was an explosion and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On September 20, 2018 in the early morning; I decided to have a cup of espresso.  I filled my Krups Espresso Machine with the proper amount of water.  Then added a modest amount of ground espresso to the filter holder.  Then I turned the machine on.  My 5 year old daughter and 3 year old son were curious as to what I was doing.  I picked up my son and my daughter stood next to me watching the machine work.  I explained to them that I was making Espresso.  The hot espresso began to slowly trickle into the glass carafe.  As my children and I watched and I continued to explain what was happening..something very unexpected happened.  A booming sound followed by hissing steam as the carafe exploded into hundreds of pieces.  Glass, espresso and ground espresso covered my kitchen counter, floor and walls.  Hot coffee sprayed onto my children and I.  My son was nicked by a small piece of glass.  We all were in shock as to what could have happened.

The broken glass only caused a minor cut on my son's leg.  Amazingly none of us were seriously hurt!  If we had been standing a foot closer...one of us could have lost an eye!  This should NEVER have happened!
justification: The incident resulted in a minor cut on the son's leg and hot coffee spray, indicating an injury but no serious harm.

incident_description: Suddenly, my oven glass door came shattering into tiny shards of glass. My two year old was just two feet away from the oven when it happened. No improper use was done and this was totally traumatizing. HotPoint agent casually apologized for the incident and said it's not their responsibility because it's after one year of use. The oven is just about 6 years old. Seriously this is completely unsafe, and should be dealt with with more accountability.
justification: The oven glass shattered unexpectedly, posing a significant risk to the nearby child, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Microwave sparking inside due to original microwave rack rubbing in two places on back inside of microwave.  Also light intermittently not coming on and microwave stating close/open door.  I had to remove the original rack out of microwave to prevent the sparking.
justification: The microwave sparked due to a rack rubbing inside, posing a fire hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Turned on my dishwasher, within 1/2 hr it started smoking, opened it an the heating element had melted right down throu the bottom of the tub!! If I had not been home it would have burnt my house down
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned severely, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On September 22, 2018 a dishwasher installed in the kitchen of one of our residences begin to smoke.  The facility was evacuated. No injuries reported. The 120Volt power wire coming into the circuit board showed signs of arcing and beading of the electrical wire.  The concoctor had burned off.  Damage was contained to the circuit board.
justification: The incident involved smoke and evacuation but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. Electrical issues like arcing are uncommon but not rare, hence likelihood 2.

incident_description: I have a Samsung over the range microwave, model ME16H702SES serial 078N7WOGB00268N manufactured Nov-2015, purchased 1/27/2016.  The unit was on and cooking 4 large potatoes for a few minutes, when it lost power and started producing a strong smell similar to burning plastic.  The unit tripped a dedicated, grounded 20A circuit breaker.  We removed it from where it was mounted in the kitchen, after ~15 minutes the unit was still producing a strong smell and was quite warm to the touch on the top, in an area that would have been in contact with the bottom of our wood cabinets.  If it was any worse we would have called the fire department. Contacted Samsung, they were not interested in helping or understanding the potential fire risk unless we were willing to pay for a service call which was likely to be more than the cost of the unit new.  We were not interested in having the unsafe unit in our house even if repaired, since I believe it should not have failed in this way.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, producing a burning smell and overheating, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
I smelled smoke and the microwave was pouring out smoke while not in use.
The electronic pad was also black and not working.
I have unplugged this item for safety reasons and plan on throwing away.
justification: The microwave emitted smoke and had visible damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Frigidaire has a recall for a series of its stoves ( https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2009/Frigidaire-and-Kenmore-Smoothtop-Electric-Ranges-Recalled-Due-to-Fire-Hazard )

My glass top stove is doing the same EXACT thing, but isn't included in the recall.  My model is fec30s6abf.  

The burner is staying on even after we turn it off.  It stays on the HIGHEST setting.  

I see many others posting on various website stating they have my exact model and it's doing the same exact thing too!

As described in their existing recall for other stove tops:

Name of product:
Certain Frigidaire and Kenmore Elite Smoothtop Electric Ranges

Hazard:
Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.
justification: The stove's failure to turn off poses a fire and burn hazard, but no actual incidents or injuries are reported in the description.

incident_description:
Microwave oven failed in a dangerous way by generating microwaves continuously (demonstrated by being able to boil water in a glass), though possibly not at full power, even though by all indications it was "off".

The interior lamp was not lit, the platter was not rotating, the fan was not running, and the digital display showed the clock rather than something related to cooking. It did make a humming noise, but not as loud as during normal operation (when the fan would be running). The user interface was not responsive. The appliance got hot enough before the problem was discovered that adhesive used to secure a large plastic vent piece on the front of the appliance melted; and the vent piece fell onto the floor.

"Rebooting" the appliance by unplugging the power chord then plugging it back in didn't restore it to a normal state; as soon as it was plugged back in, it started cooking again without any proper indication, and the user interface was still unresponsive.

This condition seemed to start after the microwave was used to heat a cup of coffee, rather than spontaneously.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned dangerously, posing a burn and fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: While cooking on the Kenmore electric range suddenly cooking element start to heat up uncontrollably making coil red and unsafe to use. No respond to control knobs.
justification: The electric range malfunctioned, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This husband and wife are reporting that the knobs on the consumers gas range which control the electric start are extremely dangerous because they can be turned just by brushing against them.
The fire does not light however the fire does not light which releases gas into the air.                                                                                                                                      
The callers have had to evacuate the home over 2 times
The caller has contacted the manufacturer who informed them that this unit is not recalled then provided them with two phone numbers and neither could be contacted.
Manufacturer did provide the caller with [REDACTED] May 10th, 2018 and then May 29th,, 2018 [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involves a gas range releasing gas due to faulty knobs, requiring evacuation but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Come home after being out all afternoon and noticed heat coming from the dishwasher. When I opened the dishwasher a blast of very hot air came out. I immediately sensed something was wrong and flipped circuit breaker controlling the unit. The were numerous items inside the dishwasher that were cracked & melted. There is no doubt whatsoever that had we left for a longer period of time that there would have been a strong potential for a fire. I would have assumed that at the very least a Thermal Breaker inside the unit should have shut it off, but it appears to have not taken effect. Will go out tomorrow morning and buy a new dishwasher - I would never be able to sleep or leave home for a lengthy period of time knowing this fire hazard is in my home.

Type - GE Profile Dishwasher
Model - PDW7880J15SS
Ser# - RL860343B
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that caused overheating and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I put in a load of dishes and turned my dishwasher on. After a while, I smelled fumes. Upon entering my kitchen, I realized the fumes were coming from the dishwasher. I shut it off and opened it. And noticed that the heating ring located at the base of the dishwasher had melted away the plastic connecting pieces that held the ring in place. The whole house smelled horrible and I was horrified at the thought that this could have started a fire. I have not turned it on since because I fear what will happen. I literally fear for my life, that it'll burn my house down.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that emitted fumes and melted plastic parts, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Double Wall Oven (WOD51ECOAB00) intermittently turns off then on.  While it's cooking, the oven turns off for no reason and the LCD panel goes dark.  After a minute or two, the LCD panel turns back on and the oven changes from cooking mode to preheat mode.  I've had technician's out twice and they won't do anything until they can replicate the problem.  I have dozens of reported incidents on this model from the internet so it's not uncommon.  Whirlpool won't do anything until it shoes as a recall.

Ironically, this same issue was a recall in 2004 (8 years prior to my model).  In that recall, it was a defective fan that caused the thermal fuse to flow.
justification: The oven intermittently turns off and on, causing inconvenience but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I have an LG double oven Gas Stove, purchased in Nov. 2015. I have had a problem with it igniting just by brushing against the knobs.  I had a service call from the maintenance Dept from Conns Stores in Nov 2017 before the warranty expired.  The serviceman checked it and that it was within norms,  I am NOT happy with this as it is very dangerous and the accidental ignition is more of a problem as the stove has gotten used more. The service repair man told me to put rubber pads inder the knobs if I wanted it stiffer.  Later in the year I spoke to a company rep and was told there were no other claims of this type. The knobs are now such that they ignite at the slightest brush and if they don't ignite they turn on just enough to leak gas fumes. We all have to constantly check the knobs when we pass thru the kitchen. This was a very expensive stove and I am very disappointed.

I did not put rubber pads under the knobs as I felt this would alter the original product.
justification: The stove ignites or leaks gas at the slightest touch, posing a clear hazard, though no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: Cutting Blade on a DLC-1SS has a tab that broke off into food being chopped. My wife found when trying some of the food. The part that broke off is about the size of a tooth. After further inspection of the blade 1/2 cracks were obvious on both both plastic forms where the blade protrudes. I have photos if you want them
justification: A small part of the blade broke off into food, posing a potential choking hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I received a Ninja Blender Model: BL642 for a birthday present from my mother on 9/11/2018.  On 9/16/2018 at approximately 5:00 pm, I proceeded to open the Ninja Blender box and packaging for the first time.  I opened the top of the box and removed the top piece of Styrofoam.  I did not see any warning labels or instructions on how to un-package the product. I removed the blender carafe (72 oz. pitcher) from the surrounding Styrofoam packaging.  The carafe was packaged with blade assembly inside and the lid on.  The blade assembly had no sheaths or protective covers on the blades.  There was no warning label stating that the blade assembly was not attached or anchored to the carafe.  The carafe lid was not locked into the carafe upon initial removal from packaging.  I tilted the carafe, including blade assembly and lid, a little over 90 degrees from upright position to inspect the drive mechanism on the bottom of the carafe.  As soon as I titled the carafe, the lid and the blade assembly fell out of the carafe.  I was not aware and it was not made obvious to me through the packaging that the blade assembly is not anchored to the carafe.  As I witnessed the lid fall off, I reflexively tried to catch it, not realizing or anticipating that the blade assembly would follow it out of the carafe.  The blade assembly impacted my left hand on the way to the floor.  I felt a shock of nerve pain shoot upon my arm at the instant the blade assembly made contact with the inside of my left middle finger.  I immediately felt and saw blood gush out of the wound.  The blade assembly had produced a significant laceration diagonally across the first joint from tip of my middle finger.  I immediately grabbed some paper towels nearby, held the wound above my heart, and applied pressure with my other hand.  My wife took me to the emergency room at the closest hospital and I received 6 stitches to my finger.  Since receiving this injury, I cannot feel the tip of my finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant laceration requiring stitches, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the packaging and handling process.

incident_description: Whirlpool under the hood microwave oven started up by itself.  I could not shut it off.  None of the controls worked.  I could not find the plug which was buried behind a lot of jars in a kitchen cupboard above the microwave.  I had to turn off a circuit breaker in the basement in order to get it stopped.  If we had not been home, this could have overheated and started a fire.  We did not get the microwave repaired because we can not trust it in the future.  We replaced it with another brand of microwave.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Re: Panasonic microwave oven - emitting smoke; outsides hot enough to burn skin; burned rubber and metal smell

While boiling a cup of water two days ago, a smell of burning rubber and metal began to emanate from the microwave oven. A harsh smoke also began to come from the microwave, and there was an unusual electric sound.  

Even after stopping the cooking cycle, the outsides of the oven were hot enough to burn skin. We were fortunate to have just enough room behind the oven to unplug it from the outlet. 

The smoke and smell still continued for a period of time, and it was several minutes before we felt the sides of the oven were cool enough to remove it outside, even using heat protective gear (heavy duty cooking mitts).

We contacted Panasonic support through their website chat the next day. After detailing what happened, their representative told us to take the microwave to their standard "authorized Panasonic Service Center."  

When we explained that Panasonic's responses to reports on SaferProducts.gov usually claim that the Panasonic product safety team wants "to obtain the unit for examination and testing", the representative escalated us to tier 2 support.

A tier 2 representative called us later that day to gather additional information. Then a member of Panasonic's consumer product safety team, [Redacted], called us the next day.

[REDACTED] told us that this was not a safety issue, but was instead only a service issue.

We again explained that the smoke of what was apparently burned electronics or rubber seemed like a health and safety concern, as did the extremely hot outsides, which could have burned through the skin of someone hurrying to move a smoking microwave oven to an open window or outside the home.

Yet [REDACTED] again insisted that this was "just a service issue", not a safety issue. He would not make arrangements for the product to be evaluated by the company's safety personnel.

We brought to his attention that many statements by Panasonic Corporation of North America to the Consumer Product Safety Commission, in response to incident reports, claim that Panasonic's policy is to obtain the unit for examination and testing, or evaluation. (See Appendix 1 below.)

This situation is disturbing, as it indicates that many of Panasonic's responses to the Consumer Product Safety Commission may not accurately reflect their real-world practice. 

It may not actually be "company policy [for] Panasonic [to] contact[] the consumer to request the unit be returned for an evaluation" -- or at least company policy as implemented or enforced in real life, unless the consumer escalates to the CPSC.

This is even more troubling because Panasonic usually relies on this response (that they are waiting to receive the microwave oven or were unable to obtain it from the consumer) to avoid providing comment on why the product failed and what steps they will take to protect other consumers.

The CPSC should take action to ensure that Panasonic's statements to the CPSC reflect the actual company practice that consumers will face when they report such an issue directly to the company.

incident_description:
We bought a Bosch dishwasher in 2015. Last month it started displaying a E09 code. We found out that it was for a control board, (under warranty) or heating element, (not under warranty). We continued to use the dishwasher, even though it didn't dry the dishes. We contacted Bosch and they indicated the control board or the heater/motor assembly were faulty. A Bosch authorized repair service came out and replaced the control board and said it was fixed. We ran the dishwasher and the code returned. We opted not to replace the heater due to the expense and were going to buy a replacement. In the meantime, we still used the dishwasher and dried the dishes by hand. On August 27th, 2018, we ran the dishwasher right before bed and opted to leave the door open for the dishes to dry. Upon opening the door, we started hearing electrical arcing and popping noises. Being an electrician and recognizing what the noise was I immediately unplugged the appliance. I contacted Bosch on August 28th by email have and yet to hear anything back. My concern is that with a stainless steel tub and an electrical short, this could have caused a fatal shock. Either that or if we hadn't heard it, there is a good possibility of the short causing a fire. This needs to be addressed before someone gets injured or killed.
The model number is SHE68T52UC/02
The number under it is FD93090007
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and potential for shock or fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Upon attempting to extinguish a lit wooden skewer (-my only source of fire having been my gas stove which I used to light an evening dinner candle) and running the sink water to do so, as I placed the skewer under the water, a backlash of flames engulfed me and my pet bird whom I was holding.  As the bird flew off to safety afar and my hand and arm were burned, I shuddered at what had just happened as I stood in my kitchen alone at night!  I then medicated my burns with hydrocortisone, combed my slightly singed hair, attended to the bird, and retired for the night.
     Prior to sleep, I then searched the internet and found that InSinkErator and the US CPSC had announced a recall of  single-outlet SinkTop switches manufactured by Mentor, Ohio-based Teemark and distributed by InSinkErator.  These garbage disposal switches were recalled due to a fire hazard in March 2018 though "no injuries had been reported."  Verifying that my model was one recalled (i.e. 74300), I somehow slept into the next day and shopped then to purchase two fire extinguishers -in cans- to replace my old expired extinguisher.  The next day, September 6th, I went to our local Fire Department to explore their perspective on the situation and my experience.  They had not heard of the problem but considered it of considerable concern and worth investigating.
    My concern is for basic safety and hazard remediation.  This event could have been my demise and that of my pets and home.  No-one would have know the cause.  I am not abdicating until this product is on your highest priority recall list-and perhaps not even then!   Please alert the public to the apparent dangers and then, to the availability of safe replacement modules.  Perhaps this should be elevated to a class-action issue but this is your determination.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the hand and arm, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) because the recall suggests this is an uncommon issue.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Mr.[REDACTED], President and CEO 
GE Appliances 
4000 Buechel Bank Rd 
Louisville, KY 40225

I am writing to share with you my safety concerns about the appliances that we own, made by GE.  [REDACTED]

Carelessly manufacturing parts to allow for this to happen is a threat to the safety of your consumers. I am requesting a reimbursement in the amount of $260.66 for the expense of the safety valve. 
I appreciate you looking into this matter and expect that you will take the necessary measures to prevent these dangerous occurrences from happening to other GE consumers. [REDACTED] Please do whatever you can to be certain that your appliances are safe for your consumers, well beyond the limited life of their warranty. 
 I can be reached by mail at [REDACTED]; by telephone at [REDACTED]; or by email at: [REDACTED]. Thank you. 
Sincerely, 
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
This is a report alleging that an LG range (please see attached) incorporates a burner top grill design that subjects cooking pots to fall off the stove.
While in the process of using the subject LG five burner gas range surface burners, one of the pots containing boiling water fell off the top of the stove and onto the floor to my right dispensing the hot water in a great mess. Fortunately, I was positioned to the left of this event at that time thus avoiding personal injury. Also fortunate was that my grandchildren were in another room at the time.

Ordinarily a pot falling from a stove range top would not be news to anyone; in this circumstance it is because the subject pot of water being heated was seated over the corner burner located there and appropriately on a cast iron grill platform theoretically provided to support the pots or pans while positioned thereon.

During a subsequent analysis of the event, it was determined that the manufacturer of the LG range had failed to provide pot-platform support at each front corner of the perimeter of the range top.

In order to further define the grill-top configuration, if one were to take a pot and while viewing it from the top imagine that it was resting on a grill where one quarter of the bottom surface area of the pot was unsupported because there was no grill components beneath it that image would describe the defective design of the subject LG range grill system.
Another image of familiarity; observe a checkerboard and imagine that the outside half of the corner squares have been cut away and then try balance a checker's chip on those defective "squares."

Perhaps now with the above concept in mind it can be recognized that a pot would always have to be overly centered toward the middle of the range top by the consumer to have some degree of safety from a pot cascading off the top of the stove (without warning). This cautionary measure would first presume that the consumer was aware of the hazard in the first place. That knowledge would not however eliminate the hazard. Given the frequency of use and the lifetime expectancy of a household range, it is probably safe to opine that such an event as mine will befall more people than not using this product.

Hopefully, the CPSC finds this report of value.

[REDACTED] , PE (Retired)
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a pot falling off the stove, but no injuries occurred as the user was positioned away from the event and children were in another room.

incident_description:
Product: GE Self-Cleaning Radiant Range Model # JBP78 (WOB4WW)
Serial # VA2 75855Q

WE have had this range for a number of years and have had not issues. Last night, however, I was using the oven and the element on the bottom of the stove caught fire.  I turned the oven off, but the element continued to burn. Power continued to be fed to the element despite the oven was turned off.   Luckily, I was in the kitchen at the time and my husband was able to use pliers to pull the hot element out of the stove. He then turned the power off to the stove.  We have since discovered by checking on line that this is not an isolated incident.  The power continues to flow through the element after the oven is turned off.  If I had not been in the kitchen at the time, the element would have continued to burn and the stove could have caused an electrical fire in the house.  Luckily, the only damage was the burnt out element.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury or death, and the issue is known to occur in other cases.

incident_description: I had purchased a Cuisinart electric coffee maker DCC-2800 about 4 years ago. The item is in a weekend home so is not used daily. I noticed there was some leakage in front of article and for some time I thought it was spilling coffee. The issue was intermittent at first.Yesterday I picked up the machine and discovered the entire metal plate on the bottom was corroded and half missing. I believe this could be dangerous and called Cuisinart customer service. The service agent was rude and only was concerned if there was an injury . I informed her there was a stain on my countertop but that was not primary concern, which was the unit was a potential hazard. She indicated it was no longer under warranty and there could be no follow up without a report. I told her I had sent photos to customer service and was primarily concerned regarding a safety hazard, bottom line, they  only would take a report if there was an injury or damage. Fortunately I asked to speak with the supervisor who took a damage report ( indelible black stain on Formica countertop.) I kept explaining that that was not my major concern and asked if they had seen the photos I sent. They said it was a separate department for e mails and I would hear from the insurance company within two weeks.... but onlynabout the countertop. Since the call I checked reviews on other models of Cuisinart coffee makers and there are similar report of corroded bottom plates which cover the electric unit. Why are these products not recalled? The safety aspect needs investigation.
justification: The incident involves a corroded metal plate on a coffee maker, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Similar reports suggest the issue is not rare.

She took the soup off the stove and placed it in the sink with ice around it so that she could call the suicide hotline.  Then her smoke alarm went off & told her to call 911

The gas company has come to her home, turned the gas off and unplugged her stove rendering it unusable.
She is seeking a new stove from the manufacturer due to this one being purchased only two years from an Essex Junction, Vermont retailer.  9 months after the purchase on Sept of 2017, the gas company replaced the right front burner because it had partially melted.

incident_description:
We purchased a Samsung refrigerator with french doors and in the door Ice/Water in 5/2017 (Model#: RF28JBEDBSG).  It has a manufacture date of March 2017 with a S/N: 07Y743AJ304729B.  It ran great from May 2017 until around Jan 2018. In March 2018, we reported the freezing up of the ice maker drain and surrounding area.  It would freeze up to the point where the auger would not turn, and then I would use a hair dryer and towels to defrost the ice maker area. This cycle would repeat every a few weeks starting late 2017 and early 2018.  It was always a huge water mess in the kitchen.  In March 2018, I called Lowe's Protection Plan, and they were able to get a company to come replace parts ([REDACTED]). Research at the time on Google searches, Samsung forums, Lowe's reviews, etc showed that this fix would work so that the problem would never come back, or it would return over and over again with weeks/months between failures.  We did have some slight freezing up start again mid summer 2018 (this summer). With travel and busy schedules, we were not around to keep a close eye on the timing of the failure.  We had a total freeze up in July, and I have reported the problem again mid to late August 2018.  They will again replace the parts (Ice Maker, Auger, and Y-Clips). 

Initially, I was concerned with the headache this would be for me in the future having to call Lowe's every few weeks, and I asked that they replace the unit. As I thought about the situation, I remembered a couple times where my son came into the kitchen a bit quicker than normal to find himself laid out on the tile because of water at the refrigerator door due to melted ice from the frozen ice maker area. We applied ice to the lump on the back of his head for a bit, and I checked his eyes for signs of concussion. He seemed to be fine, and the ice took down the swelling.  We observed him the remainder of the day.  I also, experienced a slip (I did not a fall) when I had to use crutches for 6 weeks earlier this summer.  I did have to put weight on my leg a bit to prevent a fall, but ice seems to have fixed that pain. The Dr. I was seeing for my acl/tibia did not think too much damage would have been done. So, after reflection on this problem, and dealing with Lowe's and Samsung (Sellers) support... I determined they do not plan on fixing these problems with a permanent solution when these issues are reported. They are banking on people just dealing with the problems until the units are out of warranty, and then the Sellers can move onto other problems once the warranty time has elapsed. 

My major concern at the moment is to have proper fixes and safety in place for elderly and kids (mostly) that could really get hurt badly when a melted ice/water mess is not noticed in time due to this faulty design.  If the sellers know that the problems come back multiple times after the first two failures, then they should take the faulty units out of homes and businesses.  If after the first repair the problem does not arise again, then it should be allowed to work properly.  However, if the problem happens a second time, I would love for the Sellers to error on the side of safety and fairness.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung oven back in mid September of 2017. I spilled a gallon of milk in my kitchen and it subsequently went under the oven. I took the warming drawer out and went to clean it up. There's a 2 flat pieces of metal that run under the oven. They are both extremely sharp, so much so that I accidentally ran my finger over the side of it, and it sliced my finger open and almost razored off my side of my pinky. The edges aren't finished and pose a significant risk to people cleaning under their oven. Not only that, the exposed sides of the drawer are not finished either and extremely sharp too. My children could easily hurt themselves if they try to come play with the oven while I'm doing dishes or what not. This is a design flaw by Samsung that poses risk to everyone who's purchased this oven or maybe all ovens. There's no warnings, and I contacted Samsung, and all I received was "Are you okay", no I'll replace the unit or refund your money to purchase a safer item. They offered to have someone come look at it but they said they wouldn't be able to fix it because that's the way it was designed. What worth is that? They had zero sympathy and felt like they were just covering their bases by contacting me. I asked for a manager and they told me it's how it's designed and I should contact a professional when servicing my oven. I wasn't servicing it, I took the drawer out that's user accessible to clean under the oven.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (sliced finger) and poses ongoing risk, especially to children, due to sharp edges on the oven.
