When I returned home there was a strong smell of burning plastic in my house.  The lights on the front panel that normally display the time and oven temperature were dark, but they would flicker on if I pressed certain parts of the control panel (this didn't seem to be associated with any particular button, more like just the upper left hand region of the panel).  The panel itself had a region about the size of a quarter that was upraised and had spiderweb cracks in it.  None of this damage was present before I left for work this morning.  None of the clocks in the house were flashing, so this wasn't a power outage or power surge.  No other appliances in the kitchen were affected, and there were no scorch marks by any of the outlets.  This appears to have been completely spontaneous and restricted to the oven.  This could have very easily started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit in the oven panel with potential fire risk but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Started Kitchen aid dishwasher - model number KDFE304DSS0 Serial number: F42812441(purchased Sept. 2014), several minutes into the cycle the dishwasher turns off because it has tripped the circuit breaker. The dishwasher is on its own circuit so I reset breaker and tried to restart the dishwasher. The circuit breaker trips again and retrips each time I tried to reset. Called a certified Kitchen aid repair service company and requested an appointment. Service person arrives exams the dishwasher shows me blackened wires on the wiring harness that connects with control board. I have pictures of blackened wiring harness and blackened connector to the control board. If my circuit breaker had not tripped the wiring would have started a fire!
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to blackened wires, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Purchase LG range with control on outside instead of top .  Realized right away how easily the controls are turned on as they do not require push-in and turn....just turn.  If you brush up against them they turn on.  Had a dish towel on edge of stove after wiping off top and must have turned burner on as smelled smoke soon after and discovered the towel on fire.  Happened again when i had a casserole holder on top as i was making casserole in oven.  The holder for transport is straw. The control again was touched and on causing the holder to start to burn.  Luckily, again, i was there to smell the burning.  I was told by a supervisor at HOME DEPOT, after complaining to them, that LG said it was a"model design problem" and i should use lock for cleaning so dials will not move.  That suggestion is great, I use whenever oven or stove top not in use.  However, one must ALWAYS remember to lock after use and LOCK does not help when using one burner and another heats up with SLIGHTEST touch.  If you have one pot just sitting on stove, with finished product, and suddenly it starts boiling, when you thought it was OFF.  I know have two small grandchildren and worry if someone is cooking, they can easily turn on the control.  They need a push in and turn dial for all ..... at least !!!
justification: The incident describes repeated occurrences of burners being accidentally turned on, leading to potential fire hazards, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Approximately three weeks ago, our Kenmore cooktop, Model #790.44229101, Serial Number:  NF40722446, spontaneously ignited at approximately 1:40 a.m. CST.  I was not feeling well and was still awake.  I smelled smoke and was on my way to the kitchen when I heard the smoke alarm.  I hurried to the kitchen and discovered a fire on my stovetop.  A stack of paper plates and several other items were in flames and the kitchen was filled with smoke.  I extinguished the fire before any damage could be done to our home's structure and before anyone on my family was injured.  My husband and I made numerous attempts to turn the stove off.  Each time we turned it off, the rear right burner would reignite This cooktop was manufactured in February 2014; and, we purchased it on 4/10/16.  We purchased it as a discontinued floor model and were NOT offered the option to purchase an extended warranty.  If this event had occurred 8 hours later, we would have lost our home and, potentially, our children.  Our two youngest would have been home while my husband and I were at work.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or structural damage occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was a specific malfunction of a discontinued model.

incident_description: Last Saturday, Aug 11, my wife was cleaning top surface on Viking stand alone gas ranges, model VGCC5366BSS. After she was done, she left kitchen area. Sometime later, Ive noticed a burning smell coming out of the kitchen. After inspecting the ranges, I've realized the oven was on, specifically the broiler heating element. The internal temperature gauge was showing  a temperature above the maximum 550 F. I've tried to use the oven control knob to shut the oven off, but it had no effect. The igniting element was constantly producing spark, the light next to the knob was on and the oven was getting hotter. Not being able to shut down the oven, we've decided to cut off the gas supply line and power to the ranges. Once the gas was off, the oven broiler flames went down.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Frigidaire refrigerator / freezer model FRT18B4AW6 (serial # BA30429784) produced a flame and very bad odor when cycling on.  Discovery process:  We were unable to identify the bad odor in home, so called fire department thinking it could be start of electrical fire.  Firemen traced source of odor to 15 year old refrigerator in basement.  We moved refrigerator away from wall, and saw flame at connection to compressor as it cycled on.  Unplugged immediately.  Back and bottom of refrigerator were clean and free from debris.  Firemen said we were extremely lucky to discover this problem as it could have caused extensive property damage and possibly death.

Called manufacturer (Electrolux) the following morning to report the concern.  CSR was indifferent toward my report of product being a fire hazard, and only suggested I call a repair service.  Asked to speak to supervisor and tech support, and CSR said I was not allowed to speak with them....only repair technicians are permitted to talk with their tech support team.  Really disappointing that Electrolux has such a casual attitude toward consumer safety.

As a side note, refrigerator / freezer provided 15 years of reliable performance, and both sections were still holding set temperatures as the problem developed.  I do not expect a product like this to last forever, but never imagined it could fail in such an unsafe manner.  To be more precise, it actually became very unsafe while it was still running.  Refrigerator has since been replaced.
justification: The incident involved a flame and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the refrigerator had 15 years of reliable performance before this failure.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bosch dishwasher in 2016 and required a repair in July 2017.  The required repair (electrical junction box issue) was very similiar to issues covered in the Bosch product recall in a similiar model.  In fact, my serial number (FD950200192) was the serial range just outside the recall (recall range [REDACTED]).  
The recall states "The dishwasher power cord can overheat and catch fire" - I have pictures showing the idetical issue with my dishwasher.
I contacted BSH on several occasions and my claims were rejected.
justification: The incident involved a potential safety issue (overheating power cord) but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
My Bosch Dishwasher was NOT included in the updated recall, but it overheated and melted the switch/junction box it is connected to under the sink.  Bosch denies it has to do with the dishwasher, but my electrician says the braided wiring from the dishwasher power cord was to blame.  

The current recall needs to be looked at and expanded again.  I'm not the only one that has experienced this issue if you look at people's comments on CR's article on the issue:
https://www.consumerreports.org/dishwashers/maker-bosch-expands-dishwasher-recall/
justification: The incident involved overheating and damage to the switch/junction box, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his tea/coffee water heater that was purchased 3 or  4 years ago and caller never had a problem with it until the first week in July year 2018.
Sometime during the first week in July the caller was preparing to heat water for his coffee/tea and the unit did heat then click and appeared to be fine until he turned it off and prepared to pour water for his drink and then noticed that the water was still boiling and never shut off with the click as it should have.
The caller is reporting this incident as a burn and fire hazard
There are no injuries being reported  
The caller has no idea how to contact the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning water heater posing a burn and fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the refrigerator light bulb stayed on causing the plastic housing to melt and the contents to become warm.  He stated that there seem to be a failure in the control board, this was the second incident.

Caller stated that he contacted the manufacturer, they advised him that his model was not included in a recall and to contact the agency to report the incident.

Caller feels that this refrigerator is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing property damage (melted housing and warm contents) but no reported injuries or deaths. The recurrence suggests a possible likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
The submitter set the unit to a normal wash cycle and while he was in the living he smelled a burn odor. He walked into the kitchen and noticed it was coming from the unit. He indicated that the lights on the control panel were off. He opened the door and noticed water on the bottom. He also saw flames near the side of the unit and immediately contacted the fire department. He used a fire extinguisher to put out the fire. The fire fighters arrived shortly after and they removed the unit because there was still a fire risk. 

The submitter said there are burn damages inside the unit, on the side and the floor was damaged while the unit was hauled outside.

He contacted the firm and reported the incident (M-18-237243). He was told that his unit was not recalled and they would not assist with any replacements or compensation for property damages. 

The submitter also contacted his home insurance company and filed a claim. They have issued him a check but they told him his monthly premium will be going up and he is not sure whether he will return the check to them.
justification: The incident involved a fire with property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Munchkin Click n Lock insulated straw cup. My son had a piece of the straw in his mouth. He must have chewed it and it broke off. This is a choking hazard.
justification: The straw broke off and posed a choking hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
GE Microwave Model JVM1950SR1SS

Microwave was off and not in use for several hours.

Around 10PM I was woken up by a single popping noise coming from the Kitchen.  I noticed the microwave was glowing and appeared to be on fire.

The microwave melted the glass plate along with the plastic stirring ring and enamel lining in the microwave prior to me being able to remove power and stop the fire.

GE did send out a tech the next day.  The tech condemned the unit (since it was unrepairable).
The tech DID NOT try to find the cause of the problem.  He did not open up (besides the door), turn on, or investigate past the cosmetic condition of the unit.

If I were not home, I am sure my condo would have had a major fire in it.  My product was an unsafe unit.

GE does not acknowledge any problems with these units and only offers a $25 gift card towards the purchase of a new unit.
justification: The microwave caught fire, causing damage to the appliance but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I was using my 30" Kitchenaid glass gas cooktop with downdraft to make dinner when it exploded. I had 2 burners turned on with pots on them. Went to put a third pot on another burner and when I turned the burner on, the cooktop made a loud boom and exploded. Shattered glass went everywhere.
The gas company came out and checked and there were no gas leaks coming into the house. Product is approximately 6 years old...this should not happen whether it's a day old or 10 years old.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and shattered glass, but there was no mention of injury or death, and no gas leaks were found.

incident_description: My Whirlpool gas range oven/stove exploded while it was off.  The glass from the front window exploded, flew about 10 feet out, and hit my 1 year old son who was in the kitchen with us.  The glass did not completely shatter like it was supposed to as there were many large shards of glass.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a child due to flying glass shards, but no death was reported.

incident_description:
This is a complaint about the "Martha Stewart Collection, Cutting Boards, Bamboo Set of 3". I puchased this product in December 2018.

After approximately 2 months of use - portions of wood fell off the back of one of the cutting boards. I was not concerned until today, a large portion of wood came off the front of the cutting board and splinted. This was while i was cutting carrots. If I had not noticed the wood splinting, this would have been ingested by a member of my family and potentially been very dangerous.

I bought this product from Macy's and have noticed that several customers have reported similar incidents.
justification: The incident involved a product defect causing wood splinters, but no actual injury occurred, though ingestion could have been dangerous.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung refrigerator model RF263TEAESR.  Just after warranty expired, problems began with the fan freezing and ice began to form and then melt inside the refrigerator.  Not being able to afford repair, I went online to get ideas on repairs and discovered many other owners with the same problem.  I read the fix was to unplug and defrost for a few days and then the fan would work and again cool the refrigerator, This is difficult and time consuming and required food to sit out for several days or at best in a cooler. After 2 times I cannot do that any more.  I chip ice off the vent every few days , but it is very little help.  I have the temperature set at 34 degrees and I just purchased a thermometer because it seemed everything was warm and  the thermometer is at 50-60 degrees depending  on where I put it.   I have been sick for several weeks with unexplained diarrhea and weight loss and I believe it because bacteria is growing in my food.  Samsung is aware of this problem and should do a recall.
justification: The refrigerator malfunction led to spoiled food and subsequent illness, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The issue is common among other owners, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description: LG gar range Model # LGR3061ST Cook top grates are not supported in the 4 corners. The overall spacing of the support is too course allowing cooking pans to tip spilling on floor--or feet. I have had several near misses catching the pan before it went on floor, one time suffering minor burn to hand, and three actual events where pan and hot food went on floor.
justification: The description reports minor burns and multiple instances of spills, indicating injury and incidents.

incident_description: When using my processor to chop some vegetables i heard a strange noise sounded like metal i shut the machine off removed blade and found the blade broke off a piece at the rivet. I discarded the processed food so as to not get anyone injured if consumed.
justification: The blade broke but no injury occurred as the food was discarded to prevent harm.

incident_description: Bosch Dishwasher modelshp65tl6UC/09 SN FD970100284 SUFFERED A WIRING FIRE IN THE CORD BETWEEN THE DISHWASHER AND  THE POWER SOURCE WITHIN THE CONNECTION BOX ON THE TERMINAL BLOCK. THIS HAPPENED AS THE DISHWASHER WAS IN THE PROCESS OF WASHING DISHES. Please note the serial number on this washer is outside the range of the published defective SNs of 9208 - 9403..
justification: The incident involved a wiring fire but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting the glass used for the shelves in her refrigerator.
July 3rd, 2018 she took the shelf out of her refrigerator and had it laying on the counter top when it slipped it hit her floor and shattered. she said that there is not one piece that is larger than 1/8 of an inch. 
The glass shattered so wildly that it is at every area of her kitchen.
The glass itself is what she is reporting as a laceration and injury hazard because she said that an appliance should not have anything that shatters or disbursed in the matter that the glass shattered.
She said that if a child was anywhere near this incident they may have been cut in so many different pieces.
She would like for the glass to become more of a tempered matter so that it would not shatter this way.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no reported injury, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as glass shelves can break but not all instances lead to shattering.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his range left front burner started turning on by itself about 8 months ago , however, he noticed it this morning when he went in the kitchen that the burner had come on without anyone using the unit.  He stated that he did not try to power it off because the unit was already off, he stated that it eventually turned off by itself. 

The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that his unit was not included in the recall.

Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: flame goes out when cooking and gas still on.
justification: The flame going out with gas still on poses a risk of gas accumulation, which could lead to an incident but no immediate injury.

incident_description: electric element in our smooth top frigidair range wont shut off .
justification: The electric element not shutting off is an incident with no injury, but poses a potential fire hazard if left unaddressed.

incident_description: I heated water the Hamilton Beach Cordless Electric Kettle MOdel 40882E as I have done previously. When I pouring the heated water, some of the hot water leaked out of the seam between the base of the kettle and the kettle, scalding my arm.
justification: Hot water leakage caused a scalding injury, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The incident is possible but not frequent (likelihood 3).

incident_description: The 20 oz. blending container separated from the blade unit during operation.   The contents of the blending container were shot all over the kitchen as the container spun off the blade unit.
justification: The incident caused a mess but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as such mechanical failures can occur with some frequency.

incident_description: The stove knob bezel was peeling/flaking. It surrounds the stove knob, when you turn the knob, the piece that was flaking was sticking out and cut the finger. The metal covering to the bezel is a very thin metal tape, which would cut your finger like it was a razor blade.
justification: The flaking metal bezel caused a cut, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Cooks coffeemaker (12cup) from exclusive JC Penney was purchased with your magazine rating/recommendation. The
product made great coffee...but there is a SERIOUS design flaw in the way they attached the handle to the carafe.
Common sense for SAFETY would have mandated a twin METAL BAND design that would have prevented the top portion of the plastic handle from breaking, which it did, spilling 12 cups of scalding hot liquid all over the
counter & me. The mfg. should initiate a product safety RECALL before someone winds up at the ER for burns!
justification: The incident resulted in injury from scalding hot liquid, and the design flaw suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
(07/07/2018) The consumer purchased the product on July 5th. When it was delivered on July 7th, he noticed a scratch on the glass top after the movers had slide the range in place. The consumer rejected the new range.

When the movers tilted the range upwards to slide it back out, the exterior glass on the oven door blew out. Glass shards flew about 12 feet per the consumer. 

There were no injuries.
justification: The incident involved property damage (scratched glass and shattered oven door) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I am reporting a safety issue with my Frigidaire gas range (Model FGGF3032MFH; Serial VF50439150) which was purchase in June, 2015. On several occasions, the gas control knobs for the surface burners have been brushed against and started the gas without turning on the igniter. This can cause them to light explosively when they are intentionally turned on.  
After one particularly dramatic incident, I contacted Frigidaire to see if the recognized the problem and was told that this easy to turn on control knob was in fact a feature of the range added because people complained that the burners were too hard to turn on.
I have used gas ranges all my life, and this is the first range I have ever used that has this particular hazard.  Frigidaire recommended that I might want to add one of the many child safety covers to prevent this accidental gas release.  We do not have young children in our house - this is a problem that affects all of these ranges in all locations.
Please investigate this problem and consider working with Frigidaire to recall and replace the knobs.

incident_description: Two elements have turned on while the stove was turned off and will not shut off.  We have had to shut off the breaker to the stove completely.
justification: The stove elements malfunctioned but were safely deactivated by turning off the breaker, preventing injury.

incident_description:
The submitter is reporting her range for posing a fire hazard. She recently came across recall # 13-031 and noticed her range was having the same issue. She believes her range should be added to the recall.

The submitter said the range changes to different temperatures unexpectedly during use and it fails to shut off. She claims there have been several incidents and she's had to cut off the circuit breaker to shut off the range.


The submitter contacted the firm and reported the issue. She also requested a repair and for the firm to investigate if her model should be added to the recall. However, the firm refuses and advised her if she wanted the range inspected or repaired it would be at her own cost.
justification: The range poses a fire hazard due to unexpected temperature changes and failure to shut off, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I received  an Instant Pot as a birthday gift and last week we had an incident involving the instant Pot.  We had it on to cook and my husband notice smoke coming out from it and he unplugged it and moved it away from my counter and there he saw that the countertop was burned from the instant pot.  We then heard about the recall and we are inquiring about a replacement and refund for the countertop that was damaged by the recall instant pot.

We look forward to hearing from you soon.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burned countertop, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Knobs on LG oven can be turned onto easy June 30th 2018 had a gathering someone barley bumped into over the top burner turned on burned a box of straws 

August 4th Jcpenny Delivered Replacement microwave for above our oven/range I had laid a sheet down so nothing would get damaged the knob again was barley touched and had turned on burner and sheet caught on fire
justification: The incident involved a burner being accidentally turned on, causing a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Good morning.
We  expierienced problems with our 1 year old LG gas stove.
LG Canada refuses to recall LSG5513 ST due to very serious safety issues.
We used our stove in self clean cycle when we noticed that our kitchen cabinet was in process of getting damaged from exsesive heat that came from top rear grill air vent.
LG Canada to cover up the problem provided us with false information.
They refused to assist us.
Knobs design  and burner valves need changes. By accidentally touching the knobs it opens gas flow that fills up the room. It happened to thousans of customers.
It happened to our family 5 times .
Our family do not feel safe by having this unit in our condo. Somebody is going to be hurt and LG  is neglecting responcibility.
Hope you can help.
Thank you.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a safety issue with the stove causing potential gas leaks and excessive heat, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We noticed a plastic burning smell about 9pm, looked every where and searched the entire house but did not find the source.  Went to bed, woke up the next day, getting ready to go to work, when we got to the main floor we noticed the same smell had gotten much stronger, but again we were unable to find what was causing it.
We went to work, and it was about 2 hours after we left the house that our smart smoke detectors went off notifying us on our phone that there was smoke in the main floor, we immediately called 911, and drove home.  We entered the house with the fire fighters, there was a strong smell of burnt plastic, and smoke all over.  After examining the house the fire fighters concluded that even though the range was not on, somehow the electric panel of it got some how short circuited and a small explosion occurred on the back of the panel, damaging the wall, but we were lucky that the fire did not spread to any where else and eventually died on its own, leaving the electrical panel all bubbled up from the heat.
We were extremely lucky, but I was surprised that once I called Frigidaire to report this incident they did not care to send someone to investigate the actual fault of the appliance.  The reason I'm reporting it here is to bring awareness and notify people of the potential hazard that they might have at their home, and not be aware of it.  Not everyone would end up as lucky as we were.
justification: The incident involved a small explosion and fire damage but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Being used for normal household cooking.  The cook top burners will sometimes not shut off when the knob is in the off position. The cook top burners will change the temperature to max when a lower - normal cooking setting is set, i.e. 4/5.  This has been happening for at least a year now.
justification: The cook top burners malfunctioning poses a risk of overheating or fire, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Wall oven front panel shock hazard.  measured voltage is 122V.

GE model # PT7050 SFSSS
justification: The presence of a shock hazard with measured voltage indicates a potential for injury, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: The oven was not on and my 9 year old daughter hear something "exploding" in the kitchen.  She walked in and the front outer glass of the oven had completely shattered and bursting out into the kitchen floor.  The glass was at least 5 feet out all around the oven.  Oven had not been on since the morning.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering without injury, and the oven was not in use, indicating a rare occurrence.

incident_description:
Hi have a Jennair Dishwasher Model JDB1275AWY.  This dishwasher failed with the heating element on causing the unit to overheat.  If the machine is in the off state and the dishwasher door is closed, the heating element will turn on and continue to heat up until it reaches extremely high temperatures until it melts plastics and can combust wood.  

In my case my wife burned her had removing metal tongs from the dishwasher not knowing the dishwasher had a thermal event.  Additionally the unit melted down and deformed metal cups ([REDACTED] Brand), [REDACTED] spatulas and miscellaneous bowls and other utensils.  

Whirlpool knew this was a possible event that could happen but because my unit was 10 years old, Whirlpool figured that this was merely normal wear and tear.  If weren't home this unit could have easily started a fire and burned down my home.
justification: The incident caused injury (burned hand) and significant property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high given the potential for fire and the manufacturer's awareness of the issue.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung French Door, Bottom Freezer Refrigerator (Model # RF26J7500BC) in July 2015 from Home Depot for approximately $2,000. It worked satisfactorily for approximately one year, and then I noticed the ice maker stopped working and water was leaking from the door.  I looked online and realized that almost everyone who purchased this model had similar issues.  You have to ÃÂdefrostÃÂ the unit with a hair dryer to loosen the ice build-up almost every month, which solves the problem temporarily.  The dispenser allows water to leak down the door to the floor and the ice is ÃÂmushy.ÃÂ  The dispenser flap also sometimes runs continuously, even though no one is pushing the dispenser for water or ice.  Unfortunately even with towels and rugs on the floor to catch the water leak (my hardwood floor had already been ruined) I recently fell in a puddle of water injuring my back, and incurring thousands of dollars in medical bills.  From all of my internet research, it appears that even having a Samsung authorized repairman come to fix the problem is a waste of money, as those that have done so, continue to have the same problem.  A few years back, Samsung even issued a technical manual to its repairman admitting to them that there was a design defect in this model.  Company executives knew about this problem and continued to sell this refrigerator to ÃÂ causing a dangerous hazard to the public.
justification: The incident resulted in a back injury and significant medical bills, indicating a severity level of 3. The widespread reports of similar issues suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
L was cooking on the front left large burner and I heard a pop/crack noise. I turned around to look & saw smoke coming out of front left and left front side of stove. I picked the pan up and it was flaring at 7 o'clock, the rest of burner black. We turned it off at the breaker & are afraid to use it since.

I called Sears and they didn't mention a recall. When I did, the CSR person said "it's old".  I said "it is doing what recalled models did".

All she could say was pay for repairman to come..$89
justification: The incident involved smoke and flaring but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as stove malfunctions can recur but are not daily occurrences.

incident_description:
I have  Krups BW750 electric teakettle.  The unit has a base separate from the carafe and the carafe is removable.  The teakettle has an automatic, temperature controlled switch that shuts it off when the water in the carafe reaches the boiling point.Until today, it functioned as expected but this morning,  The unit did not cut off when the water reached boiling.  I let it continue for nearly an hour to see if it would shut off. . . it did not. More than half the water in the pot had boiled away and I suspect that, if I had let it go, it would have boiled dry.

Last year, I reported an identical incident involving a [REDACTED] brand product.  (See:  Report No. [REDACTED].)  The bases for the Krups unit and the[REDACTED] unit are identical except for the label and a metal trim strip.  In fact, they are interchangeable.  The Krups carafe is metal and the [REDACTED] carafe is glass.  but they too are interchangeable.

It seems to me that these units have a common manufacturing source and that the defect originates there.

In my opinion, this constitutes a fire hazard.
justification: The teakettle did not shut off as designed, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
As I was preparing an Italian dinner, there were 3 burners on.  Shortly thereafter, , smoke started coming from underneath the cooktop.  I opened my cupboard directly underneath the electric cooktop and there was a lot of smoke and burnt smell.  It is my belief that the cooktop shorted out with the 3 burners on.

We discovered at the electrical box that the plastic cover that holds the cords together had melted.
I quickly told my husband to shut the circuit off.

Now I am afraid to use the stove for fear of causing a house fire.  When I called Sears Repair, they advise to check if it had been recalled and it had not.  Then they advised I report this to CPS.

It is a Kenmore Elite Cooktop.  Model Number 79045319410.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burnt smell but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the electrical malfunction.

incident_description: Kenmore Dishwasher was finishing cycle (I think) and heard loud popping and crackling sounds and smelled electrical smoke and saw smoke coming out of front of dishwasher.  Opened dishwasher and smoke continued to come out of vent in dishwasher and latch area.  Turned off circuit breaker and smoke continued to come out of holes.  Crackling stopped.  Front of dishwasher was extremely hot and inside of door was extremely hot.  Removed front door cover and saw burnt plastic, burnt wires and burnt insulation.
justification: The incident involved electrical smoke and burnt components but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher power cord caught fire and burned out the terminal connector.  Bosch Model SHX45P05UC/60 FD900500094.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher's power cord but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We own a Cusinart DLC-7P processor. For quite some time I have noticed cracks in the metal blade. To my knowledge it is still intact but I was alerted by a friend about the recall on the blade. Please send a safe replacement blade.
justification: Cracks in the blade pose a potential hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Cook Top will come on regardless of the position of the control knobs. Contacted the manufacturer and they provided repair which lasted for a couple of years. The problem is now re-occurring with increased frequency. I contacted the manufacture and they refused to remedy the situation. I was advised to simply purchase a new cook top if I deemed the current unit unsafe. In my opinion, this is both a fire and health safety risk that should be addressed. If the company is not willing to address the issue, the public should at least be aware of the risks.
justification: The cook top malfunction poses a fire and health safety risk, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
My Electrolux refrigerator/freezer started to "spit" out pieces of Styrofoam  while dispensing ice last  year. I pulled the ice cube bucket out and removed any  debris and rinsed it out. Than last week, I gave my daughter some "crushed" ice from the unit and as my  daughter was  chewing it, she  screamed and began to cry. I ran to her and she pulled out an extremely sharp piece of white  plastic from her mouth. I want to  say that I'm not exaggerating when I describe the plastic as intensely sharp, more  so than the  end  of  an ice pick. I than pulled the  ice bucket out and saw that  there was NUMBEROUS pieces of the same white plastic in the ice. One piece is large enough to lock the spinning part inside from turning. I have photos and have kept the entire bucket out without removing any of the plastic  inside. I continued to call Electrolux and they responded by saying  "it's out of warranty"  and that I would need to hire a repair person. I continued to explain this is not a warranty issue but a design flaw and safety hazard. I told them I needed someone to contact so that my attorney could speak to them. Their reply was horrific. They say,  verbatim, "if you have an attorney, they will know who to contact." I emailed Electrolux as well, only to receive a similar response, to contact a repair person.

Today, I met with my attorney, and they suggested I complete this  process before they contact Electrolux. I feel the design of their system should not allow for stryrofoam or plastic to enter the dispensing system. It's a real danger. 

My 5 month old son passed away just a few months ago and the state is now prosecuting against the caretaker. I  do not want to lose the only child I have left. The plastic could have  easily been swallowed  and lodged in my daughter's throat.  She could have died. I'm absolutely disgusted by the response from Electrolux. I  hope  you can   bring  this to their attention so that they  respond and take a more responsible action to address this.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the daughter from sharp plastic pieces in the ice, and there is a clear risk of severe harm or death if such incidents recur.

incident_description: The burner control knobs to our gas range turn so easily that twice my cat has turned a knob while cruising the kitchen counters and we have awoken or come home to a house filled with gas fumes. There have been many incidents in which a knob was turned by accidental bumping during cooking and gas began to leak into the kitchen, but until now these have happened while we were awake and at  home and detected it quickly. When it happened at night, gas flowed into our house for up to three hours, and I feel certain that we could easily have been harmed or killed if my son had not woken up and alerted me that he smelled gas in the upstairs portion of our house. The second incident happened when we had left the house for an hour but left windows and screen doors open. We could smell the gas from the street in front of our home.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks that could lead to harm or death, but no actual injuries or deaths have occurred yet.

incident_description: My husband and I smelled something burning - it smelled electrical or like plastic was melting on a heating coil. The smell was getting worse and we were alarmed because we could not immediately locate its source. The smell was the most intense in the kitchen and we realized it had to be the dishwasher that was running. We turned off the dishwasher, opened the door, turned off the power to the dishwasher at the fuse box, and my husband unscrewed the dishwasher door panel. We were shocked that the black metal housing of the motherboard was melting! We are very relieved we were not sleeping at the time and that our house did not burn down!
justification: The incident involved a melting motherboard in the dishwasher, which could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: During unboxing of a Tramontina stainless steel cookware set my wife was scratched by the edge of a lid for the cookware.  Examination found metal wire shavings protruding from the edge of the lid.  The protrusion was very thin metal ~0.5cm in length, probably left over from the milling process without being properly polished.  There were 3 other metal wires around the lid.  The wire did not break the skin, but they pose a hazard if the thin wires were to fall off into food and be ingested.
justification: The incident involved a scratch from metal shavings but no broken skin, indicating no injury. The presence of multiple shavings suggests a possible recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description: My wife and I had originally purchased a Cusinart DGB 700 grind and brew coffee maker 2 yrs ago.  With the original  coffee maker approximately 6-8mo after purchase I heard a loud clicking sound after brewing a pot of coffee and noted profuse amounts of smoke and burning plastic smell coming from the machine.  This was reported to Cuisinart, who replaced the machine and we sent it back to them for analysis.  The replacement machine broke approx 1 yr later due to a faulty grinder.  The re-replacement of said machine and a similar incident to the first machine this morning after brewing a pot of coffee.  The hot plate portion of the machine was glowing red when I removed the pot of coffee from the machine.  Increasing amount of smoke and burning plastic smell were noted as well.  This seems to be a pattern of hot plate overheating with significant fire risk.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the coffee maker overheating, emitting smoke and a burning smell, indicating a significant fire risk but no injury reported.

incident_description:
A Top burner turned itself on and would not shut off while using the oven.. This is a potential fire hazard.   This is the second incident, I have had with this electric range.  The first incident did cause a small kitchen fire that was contained to the items on the stove top itself. (Report No. 20180723-54BC0-2147386618 , incident date July 21, 2018) 

This second incident occurred August 1, 2018.    This time I was able to capture a video of the incident,  to better document what happened. 

There all ready exists a recall for this issue, which includes the model # of my Electric range, but my serial # is out of the range.  Electrolux Customer Service did not offer any assistance in  remedying my appliance. 
https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2009/Frigidaire-and-Kenmore-Smoothtop-Electric-Ranges-Recalled-Due-to-Fire-Hazard

My purpose for submitting this second report is to 1) demonstrate that this issue extends to other units not included in the original recall and 2) to better document the occurrence . 

Details for this incident:
I prepared to cook 1 pound of sliced bacon, and laid out the strips on two cookie sheets.   Turned the oven on and set it 400 degrees. Set the timer for 17 minutes. when the oven was around 330 degrees, I slid booth sheets into the oven.  About 7 minutes later, I noticed one burner came on and would not shut off.   If anything had been on the glass top it would have burnt. 

SEE VIDEO 
Video shows that status of the Electric Range 7 minutes after putting food into oven. (timer started at 17 minutes).  Stove is just reaching its set point of 400 degrees.  This is point where I noticed the burner has turned itself on and will not turn off.   Burner switch appears to be affected by steam. 

There is one thing I do not understand.    According to Customer Service, the serial number of my unit indicates it was manufactured in 2009,,,, but yet there is a label on the range with clearly says March 9, 2007 ..   Why would the dates conflict?   Could my oven have been manufactured in 2007?
If my range was mfg'd in 2007, then it should qualify under the existing recall. 
 
SEE ATTACHED PHOTOs
Photo shows Model / Serial / and a date of March 09, 2007
justification: The incident describes a burner turning on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. This is the second occurrence, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: Lg electric range cooktop will power on and turn the burner on by itself. This has happened several times without me powering the unit on.
justification: The cooktop turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, but it has happened several times, indicating it is likely to occur again.

incident_description:
Re:	glass cover (lid) of Oneida stainless steel 5 quart dutch oven (pot)  62400-5,   photos attached

Purchased from Kroger less than 10 years ago as part of a 10 piece cookware set

4-20-2018  In the evening, I put beans covered with water in the pot covered with lid to soak at room temperature overnight.  In the morning, I tuned on the electric stove top burner and slowly cooked the beans for a few hours, stirring about every 20 minutes.  I then added cooked meat, tomatoes, liquids, celery and spices and turned the burner up from simmer to low (2 out of 10) and continued to cook and stir the soup.  It came to a low boil.  About an hour later, I removed the lid and held it with my left hand and stirred the soup with my right hand.
THE LID EXPLODED IN MY HAND, I WAS LEFT HOLDING ONLY THE HANDLE!
THERE WERE TINY PIECES OF GLASS AND GLASS DUST ALL OVER THE KITCHEN.

I am so thankful that my grandchildren were not present, they had recently visited, and none of the pets were in the kitchen as they often are when I am cooking.  Also I was wearing glasses which gave me some eye protection.  I had only 3 tiny pieces of glass imbedded in my skin which I was easily able to remove.

An internet search revealed that many others have experienced glass cookware spontaneously exploding, often when simply setting in a cupboard at room temperature.  It seems that items that do this are  tempered soda-lime-silicate glass, made in China since 1998. Consumer affairs .com lists dozens of incidents of Oneida glassware exploding. Sadly, although several people have been seriously injured, Oneida is not the only manufacturer that continues to sell tempered soda-lime-silicate.  Most older bakeware was made from annealed borosilicate in the USA.  This type is more likely to break if it is dropped or bumped and when it does break, the glass is in shards.  Oneida claims that their tempered soda-lime-silicate has equal to or greater thermal shock resistance than annealed borosilicate glass bakeware. 
 
I do not want a replacement glass cover lid for my 5 quart dutch oven because it is not safe to use.  I never want to have another experience like the one described above.  I do not want the glass cover lids for my 3 quart sautÃÂ© pan ([REDACTED]) or my 1 ([REDACTED]) and 2 ([REDACTED]) quart saucepans. I saved the handle and rim of the shattered lid. Please send me a prepaid postage label and I will return the remains of the shattered lid and the other 3 lids to you.  I do not see that Oneida makes a stainless steel lid.  If they do, I would like stainless steel replacement lids for all 4 pans.  If they do not, I would like a refund of $10 per lid so I can try to find a suitable substitute and $10 to help cover the cost of the ruined soup ingredients, totaling $50.

Thank you for your attention to my report and request.

I called Oneida's contact number on 4-23-18 and was told to email them with my story, which i did the same day. Today is 5-1-18, more than 1 week later, and I have received no response, not even that they received my email.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (3 tiny pieces of glass embedded in skin) and could have been more severe if circumstances were different.

incident_description:

incident_description: We purchased a Kitchenaid downdraft duel fuel range. The burner knobs are located on the front and will release gas when brushed against. Our dog brushed a knob releasing gas into the room. Had we not been home, an explosion would have occurred when the gas came in contact with the fireplace pilot light ten feet way. When Kitchenaid was contacted their solution was to remove the knobs. Not a good long term solution.
justification: The incident involved gas release due to accidental knob activation, posing a serious explosion risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Information provided to your representative was that on at least two occasions strong gas odors were present in the home emanating from the GE gas range. The first time we noticed this happening was in February 2018 after one of the two adults present in the house must have inadvertently brushed against the front of the stove while in the kitchen. Until we walked back into the kitchen area of the house, we did not know it had happened and that gas was escaping. It happened a second time as well. The regulators operating the gas controls are very sensitive to touch and require only minimal pressure to begin releasing gas. We contacted GE Customer Care to report our concern and a service rep was sent to our home on July 16, 2018. While here, he contacted GE tech support who told him that was how the range was designed to operate (Ignition happens after the gas comes on and the control goes past the low and high settings) so there was no problem. The response was not satisfactory to us nor to our home inspector who felt it could be a dangerous situation. We re-contacted GE Customer Care and they had a second service rep come on July 24, 2018 to examine it. The rep felt that the regulators were very sensitive to touch and that even though that is how the unit was made, it could be dangerous at some point. Again, GE tech support told him that was the design of the unit.
justification: Gas leaks occurred multiple times due to sensitive controls, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Range Oven was set at 350 degrees to preheat for cooking a meal.  Lower oven element stayed bright red and caught fire, sparking and popping.  My wife turned off the oven, however element continued to glow bright red with fire emitting.  Only when she called me in my office and followed my instructions to turn off the house breaker to the Range did the element extinguish.  I contracted Whirlpool this morning and described incident.
I offered Whirlpool the unit for investigation if they would provide a replacement.  This freestanding Range was purchased new by me from Lowes when our house was built in mid 2004.  No work has been done on the Range.

[REDACTED]

I contacted Whirlpool. Whirlpool stated that the product needs to be serviced, prior to any decision being made.

The Whirlpool representative stated that the product is operating as designed.  The Whirlpool representative stated that the handle can get as hot as 200 degrees.
This product should be removed from the consumer market.
justification: The incident involves a product issue with no reported injury, but potential for harm due to high temperatures.

incident_description: Kenmore flat top stove heats to very high temperature although the knob is turned to a low temperature. Burner does not always cut off when the knob is turned into the off position. Problem is typically front large burner on left of stove (facing stove). I have called Sears, but they say this model is not included in the current recall. I am trying to be preventive in this causing a fire or injury.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a risk of fire or injury, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Purchased a GE CookTop Model JP3536DJ1BB June 20, 2017. While scrambling eggs on the center burner tonight, I heard a loud pop and saw where a triangular piece of the glass top had blown off. Before my eggs were finished cooking, I heard another loud pop. Upon removing my frying pan from the burner, I noticed that the entire center burner was horribly cracked in multiple directions. I assume the frying pan kept this glass from being blown across the kitchen. I called GE and was told that this is not normal and they would send a repair person for $99 + labor + parts......otherwise known as an unknown amount. Luckily neither myself nor my dog were injured by the shattered glass. Please advise as to if this should be acceptable for an appliance. I think not.
justification: The glass cooktop shattered but no injuries occurred to the user or their dog, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: Ovens front right burner turns on full blast and Inhave to turn the breaker off in the house to turn the oven off every time I use it.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven burner requiring breaker shutdown, posing a hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: My spouse and I live in a new residence built 18 months ago, in December, 2016.  About 8-9 weeks ago, we began having problems with the garbage disposal switch in our kitchen.  One evening, we were watching TV and suddenly, the disposer started working spontaneously; namely, without the start switch being depressed.  We immediately turned it off (using the switch).  Subsequent to that mishap, the switch would sometimes work normally, but sometimes we could not turn the disposer off, despite our depressing the switch numerous times. We called an electrician, who attempted to fix the switch, but it was not replaced.  The "fix" lasted only 2-3 days.  We have resorted to pulling the plug from the bottom of the disposer control box when the switch does not operate properly, until our electrician returns.  This morning, he called to inform us about the recall, which prompted this filing.  We have unplugged the unit until this can be resolved.
justification: The garbage disposal malfunctioned spontaneously but no injury occurred, and the issue was managed by unplugging the unit.

incident_description:
THE UNSAFE INCIDENT WAS A FIRE.
THE POTENTIALLY UNSAFE CONSUMER PRODUCT IS A 'MAGIC CHEF' OVER/UNDER FREEZER-REFRIGERATOR DESIGNED WITH WHAT APPEARED TO BE A "FAULTY RELAY." THE AREA OF INITIATION OF THE FIRE WAS WITHIN THE SUBJECT APPLIANCE (LOOKING AT THE BACK OF THE APPLIANCE), THE RELAY WAS LOCATED WHERE THE SUBJECT DEVICE CONNECTED TO THE ELECTRICALLY GROUNDED COMPRESSOR. THE UNSAFE FAILURE OF THE RELAY IS AT ISSUE. THE FIRE WAS NOT CAUSED BY THE RESIDENTIAL POWER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a faulty relay in a refrigerator, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was using a oblong anchor hawking glass baking pan with chicken breasts and stuffing in my oven at 350 degrees. After about 5 minutes I heard a pop and looked into the oven and the baking dish blew apart.
justification: The baking dish broke but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My red Paula Deen Porcelain Lined Cast Iron Skillet cracked and the porcelain came off and got into our food.  This is SO dangerous.  Tell me what I need to do.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that her dishwasher was in the heated/ dry cycle when her husband noticed that smoke was being emitted from it. By the time the consumer got to the kitchen, the unit had caught into flames that rose five to six inches. The consumerÃÂs husband opened the unit and the flames went out as steam was released. The consumer switched the breaker that supplies power to the unit. The dishes were not damaged however parts of the dishwasherÃÂs exterior plastic have heat damage.

The consumer states that prior to the incident, the dishwasher was used four to five times per week.

The consumer will not keep her dishwasher for the next thirty days as she plans on replacing it and does not have space to store it.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries or deaths, and the dishwasher was used frequently before the incident.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his spouse placed the timer on the microwave and walked away about a few mins later she heard a loud pop and noticed that there was smoke which developed in flames inside the wall of the unit.  He used the fire extinguisher to contain the flames.  Caller has since removed the unit and stored it outside.  The unit was already installed in the new home when he purchased it in 2014.

Caller stated that there was minor smoke damages to the cabinets.  6/11/18 The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that a service technician would be sent out.  6/13 Technician came out and advised that the microwave could not be repaired.  The technician after speaking with the company diagnosed that it was user error.

Caller is concerned that the microwave is a fire hazard without using it for heating or cooking purposes.  They had only used the timer on it which caused the incident.

incident_description:
While lifting the handle of a recently purchased All Clad 4 Square Waffle Maker Model #WD700462 SKU, 011644007072, which was connected to a safely grounded outlet, the user received an electrical shock while lifting the waffle maker handle and then touching another metal object on the kitchen counter. He subsequently continued to feel tingling and numbness bilaterally throughout both hands and "out of it" thereafter. 

We are reporting this incident in an effort to avoid other consumers from this potentially life threatening situation. Please follow up on this and let us know what to do with this product. We may be reached at [REDACTED] . The incident occurred Saturday, 7/28/18 and the user in this incident is [REDACTED] . 

We have called our primary care provider for support on next steps.
justification: The user experienced an electrical shock with symptoms like racing heart, dizziness, and numbness, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I was blending liquids and fruit, while pushing down on the cup to "seat" and activate the unit, the cup exploded off the base, my hand hit the moving blade and was lacerated.

Once the caller closed the microwave it would begin to run again even after the timer was on zero. After this first incident, the microwave has continued to run after each time it has been in use. The caller says that the microwave has even spontaneously cut on by itself and continuously ran. This has happened maybe 20-30 times since august 2017. In order to get the microwave to stop running the caller has to shut off the breaker. Caller says that before she leaves the house she has to shut off the breaker because she is afraid that the microwave may cut on while not home.

4/6/18 Caller contacted Samsung and they would not speak with the caller. Informed caller to contact CPSC.

Caller believes this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The microwave malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Samsung stove was not being used, however a family member reached beside the stove to turn on a coffee pot and leaned against the stove unknowingly turning on one of the eyes causing a small fire.
justification: The incident involved a small fire caused by accidental activation of the stove, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Whirlpool Gas Range (model WGG745SOFS02: serial # D72317056) on or about July 15, 2017.  The locks that require the burner knob to be pushed inward prior to turning on do not work effectively.  The gas has been turned on by my people walking past the stove brushing against it .  Every gas stove I have had prior to this model required deliberate action to push in the knob and turn it.  I have never before had a knob turn accidentally.   There have been several occasions we did not notice the knob had been turned until we smelled gas.    My wife has found comments in reviews of the item with the same complaint.  Whirlpool tells me that this is not a common complaint and there is no known repair.  We have had issues with this in the year that we've owned the range.
justification: The incident involves gas being accidentally turned on multiple times, posing a risk but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I am reporting a serious safety concern with a Sears Kenmore Elite series gas range I purchased in March of 2018. The range has 5 knobs on the front of the range that control 5 corresponding burners. I have had at least 4 different instances where the knobs have been bumped accidentally and the gas turned on without lighting the burner, causing gas to leak into the house. One instance the gas was left on all day and I can home to a house smelling of gas.

The knobs are like most gas ranges where the knob must be pushed in and then turned to turn on the gas and ignite the burner. On this particular range the knob "Push" part of the knob is very short and turns very easily. On previous gas ranges I have owned the knob had to be pushed in a lot before it would turn and also required substantial effort to push and turn. This is not the case with this range. The knob pushes and turns far to easy and does not require much push distance before turning. Thus, a small child could easily walk up to the front of the range and turn on a burner or just the gas. The knobs are within reach on the front of the range.

I believe this condition could cause an explosion in my house.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks due to easily turned knobs, posing a serious safety risk but no reported injuries or deaths yet.

incident_description:
Hazardous Incident: LG Gas Range

I am 70 years old and in my lifetime, I've cooked on a number of stoves, including
some pretty primitive camp stoves, but this, hands down, is the most
DANGEROUS stove I've ever used. The problem is the design of the burners,
including a 12-inch gap at the front of the stove between the only two metal
prongs reaching forward---if the center grill is removed-to support pots and
pans.

I got the stove in early December 2017 and almost immediately noticed a
problem with pots and pans tipping, especially if they were not at least 8 inches
across the base. At one point, a kettle I'd used for years SAFELY, tipped suddenly,
spilling its contents all over the stove and counter, but I blamed myself, thinking I
just wasn't used to the stove.

The tipping problem gets VERY DANGEROUS if the center flat grilling section is
removed, as it inevitably will be for washing-exactly what I did on the morning of
February 11, tossing it into the sink while I finished cooking. I then moved a pot
of hot water (fortunately not yet boiling) from a back burner to the front burner
and turned loose of it, only to have it tip suddenly, spilling scalding hot water all
over my abdomen from the waist down, with particularly heavy burns around my
waist line where the waist ban on the pants I was wearing caught and held the
water against me. Additionally, the scalding water hit my upper legs, especially
my right leg. I can't recall whether I caught the pot or if it only partially tipped and
then was caught by the stove, but it did not fall completely off the stove.
I immediately found myself in severe pain-ultimately with huge patches of
blisters--but had the wisdom to immediately remove the scalding hot clothing and
pour ice water on the burns, followed by cold towels until my daughter could
transport me to the emergency room at Los Alamos Medical Center. There, they
determined I had first and second degree burns over roughly 8 percent of my
body, although I think it was a bit higher, as the next day, I found some additional
burns on my lower right leg and foot.

In response to this incident I have gotten rid of pots and pans that I HAVE USED
SAFELY ON A VARIETY OF STOVES FOR DECADES, and while I'm trying to be
cautious, I live in fear of a reoccurrence. A beautiful new stove that should be a
joy instead has become a nightmare.

Of note, LG sent me some other burners, which only somewhat rectify the tipping
problem in that some horizontal front prongs are bit further forward, but the
safety issue that occurs with the flat meat grill removed persists, and in response
to that, I have a rule that when it's off the stove, the stove is NEVER turned on
except for perhaps the back burners because, bottom line, no matter what, it
leaves about a 12 inch gap between any burner supports.

I was a science reporter covering los Alamos National laboratory for 13 years for
2 major dailies, and it's obvious that LG engineers have not properly taken
Newton's law of Gravity into consideration. Of note, neither my daughter's
relatively new gas range nor my neighbor's brand-new range have similar tipping
problems. Their stoves provide adequate and safe support at the front burners.

It is my belief that all LG Gas Ranges of this design need to be recalled or their
burners replaced with ones that rectify the tipping problem, and that would not
be the replacement burners that LG sent me. They need a whole new design that
provides support CLEAR ACROSS THE FRONT OF THE STOVE for all pots and pans
set there and whether or not the flat grill is in place. Or at the least, that grill
needs stamped on it: CAUTION: Do not use front burners with this removed!

Signed,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in first and second degree burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests that the tipping problem is frequent and dangerous, especially when the center grill is removed, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
This complaint is submitted as a safety concern in regards to the hazardous wiring installation practices of a range power cord from my local Lowe's Home Improvement Store. 
Whirlpool range (model #WFE320M0EW) purchased (order # [REDACTED] for $465.64) from Lowe's of Central Tampa store #0564, and was delivered on 2/3/18 by [REDACTED] and [REDACTED]. The range appliance cord was improperly installed to the unit, causing multiple hazardous issues.  They also did not install the anti-tip bracket according to the manufacturers installation instructions. The points of concern are as follows:
1- Did not install Anti-tip bracket.  Several employees told me they do not install those, including the store manager.
2- The white tag labeled "Remove tag. Use nuts with power cord" was left in place and not removed by 2 different installation techs.
3- The power supply cord strain relief was not installed causing the individual wires to make contact with the sheet metal.
4- The "metal ground strap" was not removed per the 4-wire connection installation instruction recommendation.
I discovered this problem on 4/24/18 and contacted the store Asst Mgr [REDACTED].  He had the delivery/service manager [REDACTED] contact me. I explained and emailed photos of the problem and he attempted to send out the same team that did the original improper install. I felt it was unacceptable to send out the same persons and asked for someone else.  He sent [REDACTED] the same day.  [REDACTED] appeared to not have the proper training and experience in addition to the first crew. He attempted to connect the wiring improperly as well.  When I explained what the problem was he said he understood the hazardous nature of the way he was about to wire it but said he didn't have the correct parts. It was clear to me that he was not competent to do the install correctly and I asked him to leave and to have the store manager, [REDACTED], contact me.  After attempting several calls to [REDACTED] I reached him. He had a copy of the photo's and I attempted to describe the issues, but he was more concerned on how to "resolve the issue" so he could end the phone call.  I informed him that I hired a professional appliance installation company which came on 4/25/18 and properly installed the range appliance cord and anti-tip bracket according to the installation instructions. [REDACTED] agreed to credit me up to $100 towards the installation of the wiring and leveling of the unit, but refused to credit me for the anti-tip bracket install. I am being billed by, and am awaiting the invoice from Roberts and Company, LLC., who completed the final install. I feel that Lowe's is engaging in dangerous improper installations and don't feel the management has taken this seriously. I also tried to file a complaint with Lowe's Corporate, which said a complaint of this nature gets forwarded to the store manager for resolution.
justification: The incident describes hazardous wiring and improper installation practices that could lead to injury, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung range on 12/28/17 from Home Depot in Cordele, GA. The Model is Samsung NE59J7630SW/AA. The serial number is 0C8S7DCJB00494Y. On 7/8/18 at approximately 7:15pm, I was cooking on the cooktop. When I was across the room with my back to the range, I heard what sounded to be a loud explosion from the range area. (It sounded like a gunshot). When I turned around, I saw the front glass on the range had shattered into many pieces. Only a few had fallen down, but there were thousands cracked. The oven was NOT on at the time and had not been on that day. There was no heat anywhere on the oven door or around in-- only where the cooktop was on. NOTHING had hit the oven door at any time and I was thankfully not standing at the range at the time it happened. This was a very frightening experience and later the glass began to fall down as I have awaited resolution with the 1 year warranty with Samsung and Home Depot. (Samsung is NOT standing by their warranty at this point, claiming that it was the result of something hitting it.) This was NOT the result of something hitting it and should be considered a hazard, as there was apparently a defect in the glass.  I have seen online where this occurs with various company range products and is being monitored. I am very disappointed in the failure of Samsung to stand behind its product; however, I am concerned for the public that there may be a larger issue which could cause harm to others.
justification: The incident involved a frightening explosion-like sound and shattered glass, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I've had my Juice Machine by Mr. Coffee for several years and decided to use it, as I had some small [REDACTED] grapes and wanted to get some juice to make jelly.  I put less than 1/8 a cup of fresh grapes in it, plugged it in, turned it on, and POW!  The machine exploded while it was still plugged in. The base was flipping around on the counter; the round top & metal base blade were spinning; large & tiny chunks of plastic were hurled throughout my kitchen, into the dining room, and down the hall into the utility room!  It finally unplugged itself from the wall when the base fell to the floor.  It is a miracle my eyesight was not taken from me.  For several hours after it happened, I had a loud hum in my ears that turned into sounding like I was under water.  Now, I just have an extremely high pitched constant sound. I have had some tinnitus in the past, and it kind of sounds like that only much higher.   I took a bath to remove all the tiny pieces of plastic stuck to my face, neck, and body and washed my eyes with an eye rinse.   I'm still finding tiny little pieces of plastic on my neck, face, and arms.  On Monday, I may go to see my eye doctor to make sure nothing is still in my eyes.   I have no idea what caused it to do what it did.   I have owned many Mr. Coffee products and have always been very happy with them.
justification: The incident caused physical injury (tinnitus, potential eye damage) and significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such explosions are not common with properly functioning appliances.

incident_description:
The consumer left the freezer door opened slightly for approximately 2 hours.  When she returned a side mounted light in the freezer was burned and melted.  The casing for the light, the interior side wall of the freezer and the ceiling of the freezer were all melted and discolored yellow.

The consumer has never had any prior problems with this refrigerator.  Some of her food that was closest to the light was burned and the plastic containers for some of the food was also melted.  The consumer placed masking tape over the switch that turns the freezer light off, when the door is opened.  Therefore, the light always stays off.  

There were no injuries.

2/25/2018:  The consumer called Sears (800-469-4663) and was transferred to their Customer Care Dept.  However, that department is closed on Sundays, so the call was disconnected.

2/26/2018:  The consumer called Sears (800-469-4663) and she was transferred to their Recall Dept., but the rep. in that dept. said there was no recall on her refrigerator and gave her a number (Tel:  888-536-6673) to another dept.  The rep. at that number transferred the consumer to their Repair Dept.  The rep. in that dept. told the consumer that there would be a service charge to send a tech. out and to see how much the repair would cost her.  The consumer said she did not want that option and was calling to file a safety report.  The rep. said that they could not take a report at this dept. and referred her back to Customer Care (888-536-6673).  The rep. at that number wanted to send her back to the Repair Dept.  The consumer said she already spoke with the repair dept. and service dept. and did not want to go back to them.  

The rep. then offered to check for a recall.  The rep. said that there was a "general recall" for ice building up in the upper left hand side of the freezer and a problem with the fan motor.  The rep. said that the consumer would have to pay for a service call.  The consumer said this was not useful and did not resemble her problem, so she would not pay for tech. to come out for a problem she did not have.  The rep. then referred the consumer to the CPSC Hotline.  The consumer asked if a report could be filed, but the Sear's rep. never indicated that they could or would file a report.

The consumer said that she specifically told several people within the firm that she was calling to report this issue.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted freezer components and food containers) but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the description of the issue and the consumer's actions to prevent recurrence.

incident_description:
In December of 2016 our family received emergency medical attention due to carbon monoxide poisoning  as a  result of high wind back draft in the wood stove that had been properly installed according to manufacturer instructions in our home.  The readings near the stove were over 400 ppm the day we got sick according to the local fire department's instruments who had responded to our call.  That prompted a friend to lend us a professional grade carbon monoxide detector  made by [REDACTED], so we  could monitor the levels with detailed accuracy and find a solution to the problem.  As a result of having this detector in our house we discovered that the LP gas oven range we bought in January of 2016, a Whirlpool Gold Series model WFG715H0ES0, was emitting carbon monoxide.  The CO level was measured at 9 ppm on a day that we did not have the wood stove burning. From that point on, we monitored the levels when we turned the oven on. The levels reach their highest point when we operate the oven in the 350-400 degree range, the most common baking temperature.  The levels will jump up to the 70-80 ppm during the initial heat up and level off at about 17- 23 ppm. We contacted the store where we purchased the range from and Whirlpool gave them their own calibrated carbon monoxide detector to test the oven.  However, the test was very controlled and not based on normal use.  The oven was placed on 500 degrees and their detector was then used.  It was never tested at the 350-400 degree Fahrenheit range where the problem was most pronounced. We operate our oven nearly everyday for at least 2-3 hours, depending on what I am making.  We must open our windows every time we turn on our oven to get below the 20+ ppm range regardless of the season, which wastes our heat in winter and cool air in summer.  We can start feeling the effects of the CO when it reaches 8 ppm, the symptoms include headache, nausea, light-headedness, lack of concentration, and drowsiness. Whirlpool made no offer to amend the situation and they stated by phone that carbon monoxide level from our oven is safe until it reaches 800 parts per million. We know from experience that the ill effects of CO begin to occur long before that and respected medical studies show the same. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), exposure should be no more than 26.1 ppm for 1 hour or 8.8 ppm for 8 hours.  It's been over a year since the repair man was here to test the stove and it has increasingly gotten worse. The repair man suggested we either buy a new range or vent the oven.  At the time, the oven range was only a year old and we paid $900 for it and because the oven range is not on an outside wall, venting would be just as costly as a new oven, not to mention the modifications we would have to do to our kitchen. I grew up with a natural gas range and have had them most of my life, and I am in my 40's and I have not ever experienced this kind of issue.  My mother still has the same oven we had growing up and a gas cook top, but we do not experience ill health when visiting her.
 
Thank you in advance for looking into this matter for our safety and the the safety of other families who are unlikely to be aware of the hazard present in this and similar models of gas oven ranges from this manufacturer.


Sincerely,


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes carbon monoxide poisoning symptoms (headache, nausea, etc.) from prolonged exposure to CO levels exceeding WHO safety guidelines, indicating injury.
