incident_description:
On Wednesday, 4 July 2018, while preparing our family's July 4th meal, an Anchor Hocking glass measuring cup exploded in my hand, for no apparent reason.  I took the cup out of the cabinet and ran it under the tap.  When I first put it under, the water was still cool.  It gradually warmed up to hot, but our water heater is not set too high.  So, it's not like the water was boiling -- it wasn't even too hot for my hands -- but while I was holding the glass measuring cup under the tap, it suddenly exploded, sending tiny shards of glass all over my kitchen and into my hand!  This was a brand new measuring cup, which had been used maybe 2-3 times before this happened.  It had not been dropped and had no cracks or chips.  I had to finish cooking my meal with multiple band aids and gloves on my hand!  It took two days and a lot of effort using tweezers and a magnifying glass, but I finally got all of the pieces of glass out of my hand.  
I'm filing this report because 1) It's not like I put a cold measuring cup into boiling hot water.  Like I said, when I first started running the water from the tap, the water was still cool.  It gradually warmed up to hot.
And 2) Aren't these glass measuring cups supposed to be tempered glass, able to withstand boiling temperatures and even the oven???  So, how on earth did it shatter under running tap water??  3) After doing a quick search online to try and figure out why this happened, I noticed there are, literally, hundreds of similar reports about Anchor Hocking and [REDACTED] glass dishes shattering unexpectedly.  Supposedly, they changed the formula for the glass from using borosilicate glass to using soda lime glass.  And they say they did this so their glass dishes wouldn't break so easily if dropped, but that's stupid.  If I drop a glass dish on the floor, I EXPECT it to break.  That's just life.  But when a glass dish that is supposedly designed for use in extreme temperatures explodes under running tap water, that's a real problem.  Who cares if it falls and breaks?  We can't have glass shattering into our hands and food!  It's a miracle a shard didn't go into my eyes because I was bent over the sink at the very moment it exploded.  Something needs to be done about these dangerous products!
justification: The incident resulted in injury from glass shards, and similar occurrences are reported but not widespread.

incident_description:
I purchased the Farberware XL Electric Skillet Model #G779  UPC 6922495797798 from Walmart in Lindon, Utah within the last 30 days.  When I finally opened and used it I was cooking steaks and when I lifted the lid to turn the meat hot steam water ran down my left arm and side because there is no seal around the rim.  I thought at first it was spilling over the lip but every time I lifted it the water ran down.  So I tested it with tap water over the sink and water was coming out the edge and not over the lip.  Luckily I did it before the water got so hot that it would have burned me badly.  

I tested all the many lids I had like that and non of them leaked.  I bought a second skillet exactly like it at the American Fork Utah Walmart and it does the same thing.  I called the number 1-855-451-2897 on the box for FarberWare and it went to Walmart customer service.  The lady who took my call said she would send the information to their safety department and I could return the skillets to the store.  I was going to ask for proof of my call and all of a sudden I was sent to take a survey.  She didn't take my information or anything.

I am trying to prevent serious injury here.  What if my grandchild was standing by me and hot water had burned them?  I don't think many incidences of this should have to happen before anything is done.  One incident is too many.
justification: The incident describes a potential for injury due to hot steam and water leakage, which could lead to burns, though no actual injury was reported this time.

incident_description: Anchor Hocking Laurel EmbossedÃÂ Collection bakeware 8X8 baking dish exploded in my oven.  Prior to baking, the dish was room temp and the brownie batter was room temp.  Per baking directions, I had greased the bottom inside the dish.  The dish was filled with batter and placed in the center of the oven at 325 degrees for 50 minutes.  About 40 minutes into baking, I heard a loud explosion sound but had no idea where it came from.  A few seconds later, there was a second explosion.  I realized it was coming from the oven and carefully peered in.  The dish had completely exploded into millions of glass shards.  I have checked online and found multiple reports of similar incidents.  Even incidents where they have exploded in people's hands while they were removing it from the oven.  Thank God my 9 year old granddaughter was not removing it when this happened!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of bakeware with potential for injury, but no actual injury was reported in this case.

incident_description:
My daughter was using a Power AirFryer 3.4.  She had put french fries in it and used the pre-programmed french fry setting.  Less than 5 minutes after the fries were put into the machine a fire started from the machine.  Within minutes the fire had spread and destroyed the whole kitchen.

The product was completely and totally melted in the fire.  The device is supposed to have a shut off mechanism if it gets too hot.  There was no warning or smoke that was visible before the fire started.

The smoke detectors didn't go off until the fire had spread throughout the kitchen.  The product was less than a year old and was not dirty or overfilled.  
 
The fire adjuster said that he thinks that something on the counter caught on fire due to the heat from the machine.  The machine was on for less than 5 minutes and cooks with hot air.  I do not believe that this is how the fire was started.  

There were flames at the back of the machine and a puff of smoke came out of the top of it after the fire had already started.
justification: The incident involved a fire that destroyed the kitchen but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This afternoon (3/18/18) I heard an explosion and shattering noise coming from our kitchen. I ran in and was baffled by where exactly the noise came from because nothing was running - not the dishwasher, nothing on the stove, nothing in the oven, etc. I opened the dishwasher which was NOT running and had not been running in over a week. 

There were shards of glass everywhere which resulted from the glass lid of a Cuisinart saucepan which was placed inside two days before and remained untouched. The lid had exploded by itself. And the glass continued to shatter and crack off by itself as I was looking at it.

Attached is the photo of the lid and the bottom of the pan for model number. I had purchased it approximately two months ago.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass lid causing damage but no injuries, and such occurrences are unlikely.

incident_description:
The submitter said the front left burner has an inner burner which is smaller. The inner front left burner turns on by itself when the rear left burner and the middle rear burner is turned on. The submitter said this started happening last week. 

The submitter and her family moved back in the home a few weeks ago and didn't have any other safety issues before. 

The submitter's husband contacted the firm last week to report the issue and he was told that the unit was out of warranty so the firm would not assist with repairs. He was offered local repair shops. The submitter found recall # 13-031 and noticed the safety hazard was the same issue with her unit. She was upset the firm did not advise her husband of the recall and she believes the firm should include her model in the recall. She spoke with [REDACTED] who said a supervisor would call her back within 48 hours.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a potential safety hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the front and right burner turned on by itself. The consumer immediately switched off the circuit breaker.

The consumer contacted Frigidaire and explained the situation. The representative she spoke with informed her that the unit was included in a recall; a Service Technician was scheduled to repair the unit.

02/16/20018 ÃÂ The Service Technician installed all the parts that were sent to the consumerÃÂs home, and proceeded to advise the consumer to switch the circuit breaker back on. Once electricity was supplied to the oven range, the unit turned on by itself again. The Service Technician left and informed the consumer they would get back to her.

02/26/2018 ÃÂ The consumer received a voice message from Electrolux indicating that the issue with her oven range was due to the board and that if she wanted to have her unit fixed, it would have to be at her expense.

The consumer states that the cooktop is used once or twice daily, whereas the oven is used three to four times per week. 

The consumer states that her oven range was remedied four years ago as it was recalled because the burners would spontaneously turn on. The consumer plans on keeping her oven range for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The burners turning on by themselves is a safety incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Started my dishwasher at 2am.  Woke up shortly before 5 am to smoke. Dishwasher was on fire.  Blew out the fire and the smoke filled the house.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Kenmore Model # 721.85033111 used microwave, took out item, about 2 minutes later loud noise like jammed ice maker, smelled smoke, unplugged.  Plugged back in 15 minutes later, still smoked.  This is above the stove mounted microwave and it is not that old.  Is there a recall on this?
justification: The microwave emitted smoke and a loud noise, indicating a malfunction, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
GE Dishwasher model: GDWF100V40WW, Serial Number: FZ777573B.

Dishwasher being used normal. Didn't clean dishes. Ran twice without cleaning dishes. Water filled drained out melted pump housing. After pulling the dishwasher out I found melted thermal protector plastics substance all over components and melted electrical wire from wall. Disconnected unit. Fire could have occurred. Kitchen hardwood floor ruined.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted components and ruined floor) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: On Tuesday morning at 4:36 am , we where woken up to the sound of something breaking. we went into the kitchen where the glass on the oven door was scattering everywhere. At this point a took a picture and a brief video of it, it was still breaking and fallen out at this time.  Later on in the morning I made a claim to Home Depot protection plan. They are the ones who I have coverage with for my appliances. The range was bought in 2015. On Wednesday 7/4/2018 technician came out and said he would order part. I called the service provider who came out to find out when part would be coming in. I was informed my claim was denied by home depot due to " physical damage". This was 7/5/2018. They don't believe me.  I called Frigidaire directly and to find it if a defect , I was told no recall and there was nothing they could do,  If my dog or granddaughter was standing there they would of gotten hurt by the scattering of glass. It concerns me that something so dangerous like this could happen, and nobody cares. model #FGEF3035RFA, serial # VF60236909 Frigidaire Gallery smooth top.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass breaking, which could have caused injury but did not, and the likelihood of such an event is considered possible based on the description.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she was preparing bacon on her stove for approximately 15-17 mins she had just flipped it over, she walked away for about a min when she returned she noticed that the kitchen was engulfed in smoke.  Caller stated that she reached for the skillet with the lid  while removing it the lid opened exposing the flames which erupted and caused her hair to burn.  She received minor burns to her face.  No medical attention was received.

Caller stated that the stove had increased temperature which caused the incident to occur.  She contacted the manufacturer and they advised her that the unit was out of warranty and was unable to assist her.

Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

Injury information:  Long hair on side of face ignited burning neck both sides where hair was- facial hair ignited. Right thumb also received flesh burn.  I treated minor burns with [REDACTED] ointment  
Incident occurred 3-23-18
justification: The caller sustained minor burns to her face and thumb, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident involved a stove malfunction, which is a possible but not highly frequent occurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
The consumer states that the microwave was in use cooking popcorn. Approximately one-minute and a half after the unit was turned on, it burst into flames. The consumer states that there is scorching underneath the wood cabinetry.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer, under Case Number: [REDACTED], and explained the situation. A Service Technician inspected the microwave, and deemed it inoperable and irreparable. The Service Technician took photographs. The Manufacturer agreed to replace the unit for 247.00$, which included shipping and removal of the original microwave; the consumer is unsatisfied with this as this was the purchase price of the original one.

The consumer states that the unit was used approximately three to four times per week prior to the incident. The consumer plans on keeping his microwave oven for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The microwave burst into flames causing property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she noticed that the oven was coming on by itself around the first of March. It stayed on for about a minute, then went off. The same thing happened again on 3/21. 

(03/21/2018)The consumer stated that she contacted GE and advised them of the problem. They are dispatching a technician but not until April 3rd.
justification: The oven turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: We have an LR Range Model # LDG4315BD we purchased in Summer 2017.  The gas knobs do not lock well and it takes LITTLE effort to push and turn gas on.  Just brushing up against them you can unknowingly turn the knob on.  We have accidentally turned the gas on at least 7 times since we have owned this product to where we needed to air the house out for safety reasons.  There are numerous online postings on this issue asking for LG to remedy the issue.   This is a serious issue that needs to be addressed!
justification: The incident involves accidental gas leaks due to easily turned knobs, posing a safety risk but no reported injuries.

incident_description: Bought several glass mugs from Walmart. On two separate occasions, I was heating water in a microwave when the glass mug cracked. Obviously, these mugs are not meant for tea or coffee, as they can't seem to handle heated water without cracking.
justification: The incident involved cracked mugs but no injury, indicating a minor operational issue with product suitability.

incident_description: I own a Keurig K Compact and when the machine is left on it will brew on its own, no button needs to be press. This malfunction in the product is a safety issue since hot liquid can be dispensed on its own.  This has happen on several occasions with June 16 being the last, I notified Keurig via their website and have not received a reply.
justification: The machine dispenses hot liquid on its own, posing a burn risk, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Samsung refrigerator. Ice machine. We are now finding small slivers of white plastic in our ice. I have pictures.

Model Number RF26VABBP

I contacted Samsung. The call center instructed us to purchase a new "ice bucket." 

Not satisfied with their response.
justification: The incident involves finding plastic slivers in ice, which is a product issue but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
(05/2018)The consumer filed a safety concern in reference to his gas range. He stated that if he leans against the knobs on the stove, the burners come on. This consumer stated that this happens often, especially if he is reaching for the microwave which is above the range..

The consumer contacted LG, who referred him to a service repair company. 

When the consumer called the repair company and explained what happens with the unit, he was advised that there is nothing that can be done about the problem.
justification: The incident involves burners turning on unintentionally, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
(0617/2018) The consumer stated that she was cooking ribs in the slow cooker. She set the timer on low at about 7 a.m. The consumer left home for about an hour. When she came back around 1pm, she noticed a big hole in the glass lid. The lid has shattered and the glass was mixed in the ribs.

The consumer threw the product away.

The consumer filed a complaint on the Hamilton Beach web site on 6/17 but have not received a response.
justification: The glass lid shattered but there was no injury reported, only property damage.

incident_description: Cooktop control knobs are too sensitive and are often turned on by brushing up against the knobs while cooking, or even our dogs searching for leftovers on the counter.  I have walked into the kitchen many times to find a burner bright red with no one in the vicinity.  I feel fortunate that this has not caused any serious injuries at this time, the scariest incident happened in the middle of the night put when I awoke due my dogs barking and could feel the heat from the stove at the top of my stairs as I went to explore the cause of their barking.  As I had found before, a large element was on high.
justification: The incident involves frequent unintended activation of the cooktop, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description:
stovetop grills have rubber feet on bottom. they continuously fall off. this creates an unstable cooking surface. 
Frigidaire stove model # LGGF3043KFW
purchased 6-7-2017
justification: The rubber feet continuously falling off creates an unstable cooking surface, which is an incident but has not resulted in injury.

incident_description:
The submitter was getting ready to use the oven and she had the oven door open. She walked by and cut her left calf. She was taken to the emergency room at [REDACTED] Hospital ([REDACTED]) and she required five stitches.

She contacted the firm and reported the incident. She was told that her unit was not recalled. However, she found many reports online and informed the firm that the issue is a problem. She requested a replacement but they refused and offered a repair. The submitter also found recall # 15-142 and noticed the recall was for the same safety hazard.

She indicated that the stainless steel trim below the range control panel are extremely sharp and could injure more consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of the same safety hazard and the sharpness of the trim.

incident_description:
The submitter turned on the oven to preheat at 350 degrees and approximately 5-10 minutes later the oven's outer glass shattered to pieces. He said he heard a loud explosion and felt glass hit his legs. The inner glass is still intact.

The submitter indicated that the range was already in the home when he moved in sometime around 2009 and he believes the range was purchased from Sears.

The submitter contacted the firm the following day and reported the issue. He was told that his range was not recalled and they would not assist with free repairs or replacements. He advised them that he has an ill family member who requires a strict diet and he needs an oven to prepare the meals but they refused to assist. 

The submitter called the firm again today and received the same response from the firm.
justification: The incident involved the oven's outer glass shattering, causing glass to hit the submitter's legs, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description:
My Viking Gas Range turns on by itself unattended.  I found it on when I woke up in the morning.  There was a pan and top that was heated inside.  It continues to turn on at random times.  I used to be able to move the knob to medium broil and the oven went off.  Now I can't control it and it just turns on and off without touching it.  A service repair man advised that I shut the oven off at the breaker.
I feel this is a safety hazard and would like a repair ASAP via a recall (or a replacement range)
There was a prior recall on same issue below:
"There have been 75 reports of gas ranges turning on by themselves with three reports of minor burn injuries and four reports of minor property damage resulting in one payment of $850".

Viking Range information:
Model Number:  RDSCD2305BSS
Serial Number: 121012C10065536
justification: The gas range turns on by itself unattended, posing a safety hazard, but no injuries or property damage are reported in this specific incident.

incident_description: Stove model  FFLMC55GCC  keeps turning on and will not let me turn it off.   We have to turn the breaker off to get the stove off.      This happened the other night during the night  It got so hot that an alarm went off and woke us up.     I have ruined on fry pay because it was sitting on the eye when it came on.      This has happened several times lately  We now leave the breaker off when we are not at home.
justification: The stove malfunction caused property damage and a fire alarm, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Model FFHS2611LWMA Frigidaire Refrigerator icemaker electrocutes my wife thru the on off arm of th ice maker.  I used a [Redacted] multimeter to test for voltage and I got a reading of 120 Volts on the arm of the ice maker.  I immediately turned off the breaker to the refrigerator and took the ice maker out.  I was able to achieve continuity thru the power wire and the ice maker arm.  I will keep this product in my possession for inspection by you guys.
justification: The incident resulted in electrocution (injury) but was promptly addressed, making recurrence unlikely.

incident_description:
Caller reported that the frying pan while in use dispersed the cap of the rivet which became a projectile to the other side of the kitchen.  She stated that there was a loud noise like an explosion but she was not aware of where the noise emanated from until later when she discovered the object near the kitchen sink.  Caller feels that if a child had been present it could have caused serious injuries.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller is concerned that this frying pan presents a safety hazard to users and bystanders and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a projectile from a frying pan but no injuries were reported, though potential for injury was noted if a child had been present.

incident_description: On the evening of 4/23/18 at approximately 9:00 pm I set my 2 YEAR OLD Kenmore dishwasher on a 2 hour delay wash cycle. (I like to run the dishwasher at night so it does not interfere with showers, laundry, etc during the day time hours.) At 11 p.m. I heard the dishwasher start. I went to bed. At approximately 2 am (4/24/18) I was woken up by my daughter claiming that our dog startied barking, woke her up, sheÃÂs hearing weird noises and there is a horrible smell in our house. I told her it was probably the dishwasher running and it was fine. She insisted that I get up and check. When I get up to go to the kitchen I smell something that smells like plastic burning and figured something had fallen on the heater coil of the dishwasher. When we get to the kitchen - there is a haze of smoke and the smell is overwhelming. I open the dishwasher to find that nothing has fallen or is melting on the coil but there is about an inch of water in the bottom of dishwasher. I run to the bathroom and before I can come out my daughter is screaming that water is all over the kitchen floor. As I come down the hall back to the kitchen (I had left the dishwasher door open) I see sparks then flames shooting out of the dishwasher door and thereÃÂs a sizzling sound coming from the door! The door is so hot that you cannot touch it - just the handle. I call my parents for help and my dad comes down and disconnects the washer from electricity. I called Sears to see if thereÃÂs any warranty/protection for this- was transferred to their repair who told me ÃÂsorry about your luck and sorry this happened to you, we can send a repairman out to fix it and hereÃÂs Kenmores recall # - you can call to see if itÃÂs been recalledÃÂ - to calling kenmores recall number to be told no it hasnÃÂt been recalled. When the dishwasher was disconnected- there was nothing wrong with the wiring - it was the motherboard/control panel that caught fire. I have no doubt that had our dog not woken my daughter up- the dishwasher would have caught fire and our home would have been lost - worse yet - we would have died. This dishwasher was only 2 YEARS OLD!
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, posing a significant risk to life and property, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Betrodd Gas ranges double oven is a gas leak Danger. I purchased 2, for 2 separate houses. For both the renters turned the knob and the knob broke off. Same place on both Betrodd ranges. That means that the flame was stuck to on.. Open flame.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak and open flame due to broken knobs, posing a hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
On June 11, 2018, our GE built in microwave/convection oven (JEB1095) spontaneously exploded resulting in glass all over the kitchen, adjoining room and all over our son's face and chest (and an unusable and unsafe microwave) This is the SECOND time this has happened to us in two years.  Much to our dismay, we were required, by GE, to pay for the repair two years ago even though this was a clear product defect and no fault of our own.  I implored GE to find another solution in anticipation that this would happen again.  I even warned that it could happen while one of my children was standing in front of it. I was assured by the GE technician that this was a fluke and wouldnÃÂt happen again, and yet, itÃÂs exactly what did happen.

On June 13, 2018, I called Customer Service and spoke with a representative named [REDACTED].  She has not returned any of my numerous follow up calls.  

A few days after speaking with [REDACTED], I was contacted by a man named [REDACTED] who informed me that he was from Corporate.  We have had two phone conversations and they have been frustrating, to say the least, as I donÃÂt believe he is operating in good faith. 

[REDACTED] has made me an offer to replace my built in with a counter top model.  I tried to explain that the model he is offering is different in kind, size and replacement value (much less) to the one that I currently have. He was dismissive, unmoved and rude in his reiteration of the offer and unwillingness to consider my history or facts.  

When I mentioned that I might want to change the color and understood that it might be an additional cost to me, he offered to sell me the very model that would be a comparable model to the one we have now but at 50% the $1600 MSRP cost (Advantium - PSB9100).  In effect, rather than making us whole and doing the right thing after two glass explosions, GE is once again, trying to get me to pay to fix their defective and dangerous product.

In all my conversations with [REDACTED], he simply hasnÃÂt cared to make us whole or even ask if our son was injured when glass exploded all over his chest and face.  I asked [REDACTED] for his managerÃÂs name, and he refused, multiple times, to give me any other way to appeal.  He refused to entertain any other suggestion that I made in order to make our situation more just.  The fact that this has happened to us twice, and that my son was in front of exploding glass this time, was of no consequence to him.  

[REDACTED] has given me a deadline of July 10th to accept his offer or presumably, he is withdrawing it.  These hardball tactics are not what I expect to be used against a customer who has twice had to deal with such a dangerous product.  

I have plenty of documentation, including pictures from the two incidents, showing the damage, the email exchanges and the money we have already paid out to replace this dangerous product once already.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the son (glass on face and chest), and the recurrence (twice in two years) indicates a likely defect.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her range knobs 
She lives in a Condo development with two buildings built in 1805 and 1910 these two building were connected around 2007.  
She and her husband moved in around 2007 and the appliances were already in the condo.
She noticed very, very early that the knobs on her range are turned extremely easily, however she realized May 28th, 2018 that the range turned itself on and the fire department advised her that this fire reached 1000 degrees. This is after switches were replaced a year ago.
She did contact the manufacturer who advised her that they will send her new switches and moisture barriers because there may be an electrical short.
She is waiting for the delivery of these items so that hopefully she will be the repair she has been waiting for. 

I added photo and information on CPSC website
justification: The incident involved a range turning itself on and reaching high temperatures, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung refrigerator less than 3 years ago for approximately $1,800.00. The refrigerator will not cool the food to a safe temperature. Regardless of what it is set to, the internal temperature averages between 47-54 degrees.
justification: The refrigerator not cooling to a safe temperature is an incident with no injury, but it poses a risk to food safety.

incident_description: The lid blew off of my digital pressure cooker while under pressure.  It blew off, hit the ceiling and the entire contents were spread about on the walls and floors throughout my kitchen.  No one was hurt because we were in the other room, but this could have caused harm to myself and my 15 month old son.
justification: The pressure cooker incident caused property damage but no injuries, as no one was present in the kitchen at the time.

incident_description: Our fire dept responded to a CO (carbon monoxide) alarm call in a dwelling and the whole house was approx. 60 ppm of CO. Long story short, we isolated it down to a cooking pot, as the owners were cooking spaghetti sauce on a natural gas stove that evening. The pot involved was an 8 quart ANOLON ADVANCED , Hard Anodized Nonstick, TQQQ04. I've tried looking on the net about this pot reaching high temps and creating CO or other by products. I am troubled by the fact that a house can be filled with CO from cooking using certain pots, etc. The gas company rep. said they get alot of calls like this during Thanksgiving. No one was injured in this incident thankfully. I see a problem that has possibly been overlooked.
justification: The incident involved a CO alarm and elevated CO levels, but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The gas company rep's statement about frequent calls during Thanksgiving suggests this is likely to occur again.

incident_description: Stove was purchased in November 2017. At first I didn't realize that sound I was hearing upon turning on oven was dangerous. It was a small boom and I thought it was the grates expanding. In February my husband heard it and said it was delayed ignition and quite dangerous. I called Samsung for service but when the repairman came out it did not do it. So he didn't replace any parts and he said to video it. After further complaints about safety Samsung agreed to replace stove. An exchange is in process now but it is taking weeks. Yesterday I used the oven and there was a distinct gas odor and a loud boom.  I am not going to use oven anymore.
justification: The incident involves a dangerous delayed ignition and gas odor, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Our dishwasher starts smelling like a bad electrical fire. I smelled it from the next room. I went in and smoke was pouring out of the front ride side of the panel. The lights were no longer working on the panel but the dishwasher was running. The front cover was slightly warped near the top right section. I opened the door to stop the dishwasher. We turned off the power at the breaker. Upon opening the door, there was evidence of smoke having escaped from the top vent area of the door. Even after opening windows and turning on fans, there is still a bad odor in the house.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical issues but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The stove design includes burner knobs which are above the level of the cooking surface. This has resulted in the burner(s) being turned on accidentally when setting something on the stove surface. It has happened numerous times. Melting or catching on fire has resulted. Looking at other stoves on the market they all seem to keep the knob profile below surface level. The knob needs to be depressed before turning but that is exactly what happens when something is set on it. The knob is then easily spun to on, by the weight of the object.  The model is GE    JS750DF3BB
justification: The incident involves burners being turned on accidentally, leading to melting or catching fire, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: At 10 am the fridge made two sharp electrical short sounds and then smoke poured out of the bottom of the fridge. My husband ran into the kitchen to turn off the breaker and saw active flames from under the fridge. He pulled it out rapidly and was able to blow out the fire. He then disassembled the back of the fridge to find where the flames were coming from. He noted they originated from the side of the compressor. He plugged it in once more to confirm and it immediately lit on fire again. We then got a new fridge.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: While folding laundry upstairs tonight, we smelled smoke coming from the first floor - we were on the second floor.  We ran downstairs to the kitchen and toward the smell.  It seemed to be coming from the dishwasher.  We had a load running.  The entire cabinets around the dishwasher smelled of smoke.  We realized it was in fact coming from the dishwasher and opened it up.  We checked to see if the heating element had plastic or something on it, but it did not.  We took everything out and saw nothing on the inside of the dishwasher.  We looked under the dishwasher and saw nothing.  The powercord was fine.  As I went to close the dishwasher, I smelled a horrible smell coming from the DOOR of the dishwasher.  We didn't know what to do, so we unplugged the dishwasher and let it sit for about 20 minutes.  We went back to check on it and found that one area of the door under the control panel was still warm.  So we decided to take the door apart.  When we did, we found the black box inside the door with all the wires going to it was black with soot and melted.  It was also the exact smell we had smelled upstairs earlier.  Clearly the black box/motherboard of the dishwasher had caught FIRE during the cycle and by the grace of God, we caught it in time and stopped the dishwasher before it could become a full blown house fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard in the dishwasher, which was detected and addressed before causing injury or significant damage.

incident_description: The timer on this Black & Decker toaster oven will hang up intermittently and cause the oven to stay on rather than time out. There are two timers, one for the oven and one for the toaster. The timer on the toaster hung up up when I left for work one morning and my wife was out doing yard work. By the time she came inside, the toaster had almost started a fire.
justification: The toaster timer malfunction caused a near-fire incident, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite range, purchased as a floor model in March 2017.  The burners do not require you to push in before turning and you simply just turn the knob.  It has happened on a few occasions that the gas gets turned on and no burner and you can smell the gas.

Last week Sunday, it was a hot muggy day and the a/c was running.  My son was inside sleeping and I went in about an hour and half later to check on him, immediately as soon as I opened the door, the whole house was full of gas.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak that filled the house, posing a significant risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We experienced a serious issue with the power cord of our FAGOR (Electric Multi-Cooker) pressure cooker appliance. Model: 670041460, Made in China. This product utilizes a low quality undersized hard-wired power cord, and without proper strain release, actually caught fire at the cord entry to the appliance. It is a shame that a company such as FAGOR to allow production of such low quality short-lived and quite dangerous products. These products should NEVER utilize hard-wired flimsy light gauge zip-cord as power cords especially by a product rated to consume 1000 watts at 120VAC. Instead, utilize highly flexible 14 gauge round cable with extra length strain relief with at least IEC 320 C13/C14 or better connections. Power cords can then be easily changed or disconnected during storage. ALL products designed in such a way desperately NEED a national recall.  Do not allow dangerous junk sold to the consumer.  Do not purchase FAGOR or any other brand that produces products in such a manner.
justification: The power cord caught fire, indicating a serious incident but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was making a cup of coffee in my Keurig B31 coffee maker and at the very end of the brewing cycle, the water began spewing out faster, blowing a large hole through the pod and hot scalding water, along with all the coffee grounds in the pod came flying out and burned my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from hot water and coffee grounds, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Last evening 24 June 2018 my dishwasher started to smoke apparently from the door.  There was a strong smell of burning plastic.  I checked on the GE website to see if this model had been recalled and it had been. This morning I called the GE recall hotline 866-918-8760.  I waited from 930 to1015 am on hold till an agent picked up.  One of my concerns was, since I had registered this dishwasher with them and had a service contract, why didn't they notify me?  The agent said they had in 2012 and I had responded and it had been taken care of.  I asked why then did it start to smoke?  The answer was we're in "phase 2".  What does this mean?  Wait till it catches fire and I call?
I can't spend another 45 minutes on hold with GE for clarification.  I am hoping you can help.  At least others may be spared a potential fire in their homes.  I also think that a 45 minute wait on hold suggests a lack of seriousness on GE's part.  The agent was very polite and helpful except for the "phase 2" thing.  Perhaps I misunderstood. My [REDACTED].  My diswasher model number is GLD6760N10SS, serial number TM731998B.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and had a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The recall history and delayed response suggest this issue is likely to recur.

incident_description:
The product used was an Anchor baking set.   This wagas the first use.  The product is listed as oven safe however after removal from oven the platter exploded throwing glass fragments everywhere.




https://www.bedbathandbeyond.com/store/product/anchor-reg-value-pack-3-piece-glass-baking-set/1016063290?skuId=16063290&mcid=PS_googlepla_nonbrand_bakeware_online&product_id=16063290&adtype=pla&product_channel=online&adpos=1o3&creative=224484706032&device=c&matchtype=&network=g&mrkgadid=3140839805&mrkgcl=609&rkg_id=h-d526264942155ab9ca01c9223e397074_t-1529361466&gclid=CjwKCAjwsJ3ZBRBJEiwAtuvtlD4L6jwoBm237CbMR21fMdp2BTLX_E3KnC7na2cCBzyoe33emtpQRhoCqhwQAvD_BwE
justification: The platter exploded, causing glass fragments to scatter, which is an incident but no injury was mentioned.

incident_description:
I was reaching into the microwave, which is located above the oven. I accidentally touched the oven with my waist. The contact with the switch was very slight, but it turned on and incinerated the gas. My shirt almost caught on fire. I am very concerned with this oven model. I cannot believe that it got approved by the government and is being sold to the public. There is no safety mechanism that stops gas from escaping. It is very easy to turn switches accidentally and it could possibly create a very dangerous situation. The house could be filled with poisonous gas or there could be a very deadly explosion. The risk is even higher for households with children. All it takes for a kid to create a life-threatening situation is to easily turn the switches. The following is the oven information. Brand: Frigidaire. Model: FFGF3015LWG. Serial Number: VF64621783.

There was another incident with this oven during which our apartment almost caught on fire. When we moved in, we stored an apron in the compartment under the oven. There was a sign that says "do not use for storage," but it was very poorly visible. We were not able to see it and proceeded to store flammable materials in the compartment. Turns out that there is no screen separating the oven burner from the compartment and there are open flames in it when the oven is being used. The first time we tried to use the oven, the fabric items caught on fire. Black smoke started coming from underneath the oven and took us by surprise. Thanks to our quick reaction, we were able to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.

I hope the government takes appropriate measures to remove these dangerous ovens from people's homes and compensate them appropriately.
justification: The incident involved a shirt almost catching fire and a previous fire incident with black smoke, indicating potential for injury. The likelihood is high due to multiple incidents and the described design flaws.

incident_description:
After about 8 years of use my oven racks no longer stay in place and fall down.  I am very concerned me, my husband or my child may be burned by hot food, as we cannot afford to buy another new oven for this reason.  I contacted Frigidaire customer service who is not taking any responsibility, but stated in the response that the oven cavity could have expanded.  The want ME to purchase new racks they offer with no guarantee they will work.  There are several track positions and the distance at the top is smaller than that at the bottom, so again, they rack they want me to buy may work on one rung, but not another?  I think this oven should be recalled and a new one provided before someone is seriously burned.  Please check into any history this company is ignoring as I find it hard to believe I am the only person having this problem.  

Wall Oven Model Number:  GLEB27S9FBD
Serial Number:  NF90625946
justification: The oven racks falling pose a burn risk to the user and their family, which could result in injury.

incident_description: My instant pot purchased in December 2017 and used approximately a total of 8 times, self-destructed. I used it for the last time, to cook some artichokes for a family dinner the night of June 21st.  I turned off the Instant Pot when it was finished cooking but didn't unplug it. The next day after being in the kitchen all morning cleaning up, the Instant Pot showed no signs of any trouble. Sometime later in the early afternoon, I smelled smoke, upon investigation; I discovered the Instant Pot spewing acrid smoke.  The whole bottom of the Instant Pot had melted off and pooled in a smoldering mass of plastic and burning wires. The fumes where so bad, we had to wear masks with wet clothes underneath in order to enter the house and attempt to clean up the mess.  We had to leave the house for several hours with all the windows open and fans pushing the inside air out.  Even so, our home still smelled to the point of causing stinging eyes, headaches and coughing. Had this incident occurred during the night and gone undetected, IÃÂm not sure we would have survived the toxic smoke that filled our entire house.  It was so bad that over 24 hours later, and cleaning all surfaces in the kitchen and adjoining rooms, it still is not cleared enough to spend more than a few minutes at time in the kitchen. It would appear that it will take several days or longer to have limited use of the kitchen. The Instant Pot also damaged the surface that it was on which may need to be replaced and professionally cleaned.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and health symptoms like stinging eyes, headaches, and coughing, but no severe injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he used his electric can opened to open a can. When the can opener had rotated three-hundred sixty degrees and was at the starting point, it shaved off a piece of metal into the can. The consumer used the can opened once again to determine if the incident was a one-time matter however it was not as the same thing happened with the second can he opened. The consumer believes this poses a safety hazard as the piece of metal that falls into the can be ingested without the knowledge of a person eating, and causing serious internal injury to them.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke with informed him that they had received complaints for the same model electric can opened however not of the nature he described.

The consumer states that he used the electric can opener twice.

The consumer plans on returning the unit for a refund.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with potential for injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: On the evening of March 10, I was awakened by an acrid, burning smell in my home.  There was visible smoke in my kitchen and I traced the source to my Kenmore Dishwasher.  I usually run the dishwasher at night.  After disconnecting the power, I took off the front panel to investigate.  I found a portion of the control board along with several wiring harnesses attached to it charred and partially melted.  I took photos to document the damage.  The dishwasher apparently shut itself down in mid-cycle, but from the looks of things, it could have developed into a fire.
justification: The incident involved visible smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On the day in question my wife was heating up a cup of coffee in the Sharp Insight-Pro drawer microwave. Suddenly there was a strange noise and the microwave stopped working and the display panel went dark. Shortly thereafter my wife noticed smoke issuing from the top of the microwave near the display. I went and turned the power off at the breaker (it had not been tripped by the incident). Even with no power to the unit the smoke continued to increase. When it was obvious that there was a fire inside the unit, I unscrewed it from the cabinet and with my wife's help we carried the unit out onto an outside concrete porch. Smoke continued to increase in volume and it was apparent that the fire was still active and increasing in intensity. With the aid of a power driver I was able to unscrew all the cabinet cover retaining screws and slide the  cover off. The back of the microwave area was in flames. I extinguished the flames with a garden hose and waited for the unit to cool down before inspecting it.
I do have video of the unit smoking while on the patio and my wife got video of the flames and burned up electrical connections. I was unable to upload the video since the "add files" was not working.
justification: The incident involved a microwave malfunction leading to smoke and fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: In October, 2018,  the Insinkerator Single Outlet Sinktop Switch, Model 76703, purchased in 2014, was plugged into an electrical outlet box below the sink, which outlet box caught on fire.  The fire department was called to make sure the fire was out.  The next day our electrician replaced the electrical outlet box, although he did not see anything particularly wrong with the box.  Now, we know, due to the recall notice received today, the the fire was cause by the Insinkerator switch overheating.  The installation of the new outlet cost $115.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an overheating switch, requiring fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
InSinkErator STS-SO Single Outlet Sink Top Switch
Model 76703
Date Code 1206
Numerous incidents

Over the last several years, when engaging this switch to activate my under-sink garbage disposal unit, the switch unit activates the corresponding GFCI outlet that the switch is plugged into, hence disconnecting power to the disposal unit. This has occurred at least 100 times, causing me to have to manually reset the GFCI outlet each time, in order to eventually use the disposal unit. I did not know why this was happening repeatedly.

Over the years this repeated activation of the GFCI outlet has caused me to have to replace the GFCI outlet several times, at a cost of $15 for each replacement GFCI outlet. I could not figure out why this was happening.

Fortunately no further damage occurred (apparently because of my use of the GFCI). But this has caused an annoying burden and cost to me. It would have been nice to know about this earlier, saving me $45 in GFCI replacement costs.

I can supply photographs upon request.
justification: The incident involves repeated activation of a GFCI outlet without injury, causing inconvenience and minor financial cost.

incident_description:
We have owned a GE CafÃÂ© Double Oven Gas Range Series Model No:CG5990Set3SS, Serial No. V2111/802P since 2013. About two months ago the igniter on the main oven or lower oven exploded and shorted out the main panel.
We first contact GE about service and we were told that there was NO GE service available in our area. So we contacted an independent local service company.
The service company found that the lower oven glow igniter was damaged.
They ordered the parts including a new igniter and circuit control board and came to our home today. When the service man installed the new igniter, it also exploded.
He contacted GE and they told him we needed another part.
Afterward I went online and found that GE has had numerous problems with the igniter on their GE CafÃÂ© Ranges. There has been no recall that I can find. Why?
This range cost $3,000. It should have lasted longer than 4 years. We are going to have to spend more than $500 to fix it.
I also found online a report of the failure of this type of igniter in stoves, I wonder why?
I would like to complain that first an exploding igniter in a natural gas stove is extremely dangerous. My wife and I are retired and we do just general cooking and we maintain our appliances.
justification: The incident involved an exploding igniter, which is dangerous but did not result in injury or death. The occurrence likelihood is possible given the reported issues with this model.

incident_description: The coffee maker leaks water. Random leaks have happened about 9 times since the product was purchased. Caller has noticed that the cord sometimes is sitting in a puddle of water because of the leaks. Caller believes this product is a slipping and shock hazard.
justification: The coffee maker leaks water frequently, creating a slipping and shock hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I turned on our Cuisinart coffee maker model 10808 this morning to brew our coffee. About 90 minutes later I began to hear a popping sound and observed the warming plate turning bright red (hot) and smoke began coming from the unit. I immediately unplugged and removed the coffee maker from our home. 

This is very disturbing to us as I just happened to be home when this occurred; I will often brew the coffee and then leave the rest for my husband who gets up later. I have no doubt we would have had a kitchen fire with damage to our home if I had not been present when this issue occurred.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
On Feb 4, 2018 my Cuisinart Convection Toaster Oven caught fire.  The fire was behind the control panel and smoke and flames were coming out the top of the unit.  I got it unplugged and out of the house where my wife deployed a fire extinguisher.  There were no injuries, but our cabinets and kitchen were inundated with an electrical/fire/smoke smell.  The oven was a loss, we used up our fire extinguisher, and the patio was a mess after the extinguisher was deployed.  

On Feb 5, 2018 I contacted Cuisinart and relayed the information above and all ID numbers on the product.  They volunteered to replace the product, supplied information on a replacement oven, and asked that I send the oven to them, which I agreed.  I said it was important I learn what happened as I have another Cuisinart oven and I need to know if it is safe.  

On Feb 7, my wife contacted Cuisinart about a replacement and they changed what was promised on Feb 5.  Now having no confidence in Cuisinart to provide me with information on the product, I opted not to return the oven.  

On Feb 13, I received a letter from [REDACTED] , Claims Manager with Conair the parent company of Cuisinart.  Now having a record of their request for the oven, I mailed it to them on Feb 26.  I again noted the need for information on the safety of this product as I have another one of them.  Since then we have heard nothing from Conair or Cuisinart.  Not sure how important this is to Cuisinart, but as it could have burned down our home, and we have another one of these ovens, it is important to us.  Can you help get some answers from Cuisinart or Conair?
justification: The incident involved a fire with no injuries, but potential for significant property damage, warranting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described event and similar incidents reported.

incident_description: Was not in use. My 7 year old son came running outside yelling something is on fire.  When I ran into the house, smoke detectors were going off and it was smoky and smelt as if something was burning,  I ran into kitchen and saw the inside of microwave ingulfed in flames.  I proceeded to open the door and use a fire extinguisher.
justification: The microwave was engulfed in flames, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I used the self clean feature on my Samsung range model number Ne59j7630sg for the first time and it got so hot that it shut down the control panel and the oven remains locked. I flipped the breaker and also unplugged the appliance and it didnÃÂt reset the range like customer service thought it would. I also held the off/clear button for 3 seconds as I was told to do with no result.  This is a fire hazard not only because of the heat inside the oven but also because it stresses the electrical components of the range. It seems to be a common issue with Samsung ranges but they will not issue a recall.
justification: The incident describes a malfunction causing excessive heat and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Toaster oven was plugged in but had not been used for a couple of weeks. It came on without timer at some point today and I was only aware because of a smell that smelled like something electrical burning
justification: The toaster oven malfunctioned and produced a burning smell, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that on May 16th, 2018 her dog was cut severely enough on their dishwasher that he severed his Achilles Tendon requiring major surgery.
She is reporting this because she has read reports that children have also been cut pretty badly on this product.
The consumer's pet was sitting down with his back against the closed dishwasher and when he got up his leg brushed the unit and he was cut 
The dishwasher came with the home when purchased in 2011.
She was informed when she moved in that the appliances were three years old
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer, however she does intend to contact them.
justification: The dog suffered a severe injury requiring major surgery, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it's a rare incident involving a pet.

incident_description:
I purchased a new Samsung refrigerator from Best Buy on December 28, 2014.  Here is the product information:

Model Number: RF26HFENDSR/AA

Serial Number: 0AF24BBFA07249D

On April 20, 2018, upon opening the right-side refrigerator door, the top door hinge suddenly failed and the door collapsed.  I managed to catch it with both hands, prop it up, and close it, thus preventing it from falling off completely and crashing to the floor along with food, glass jars and bottles, etc.  Had I not caught the door just in time, it most certainly would've caused great damage to the door, the floor, and possibly bodily injury to myself and anyone else in the immediate area.  My greatest concern is that my 3 year-old daughter sometimes opens the fridge door and the accident could've been much worse had the hinge failed when she opened it with possible severe injury and even death!

On April 21, 2018, I brought this incident to the attention of Best Buy Geek Squad Protection hotline but to no avail.  They said it's out of warranty (Best Buy 3-year warranty recently expired on 1/28/18) and directed me to Samsung as the manufacturer of this product.  I then called Samsung at 877-438-3774 and spoke to customer service rep "[REDACTED]" at approx. 9:00 AM MST.  After gathering the necessary info, [REDACTED] proceeded to inform me that the 3-year manufacturer warranty on parts was expired and that my only recourse is to pay for a service technician to come out and fix the defective part, or call the Samsung parts dept., order the part, and attempt to fix the issue myself, essentially saying "you're on your own".  This proposal was unacceptable to me so I then spoke to a customer service supervisor named "[REDACTED]" who essentially told me the same thing.  The reference number for the call is [REDACTED].

To be clear, this is not an ordinary parts issue due to normal wear and tear like the seal on the door coming off or anything like that.  This is a CONSUMER SAFETY ISSUE due to a MANUFACTURER'S DEFECT IN THE PART.  I have photos to prove it.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator door hinge failure which could have caused injury but did not, and the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the defect.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting a combination microwave and oven that has racks falling into the oven.  The unit was in home when purchased in 2011.  No problems with unit until sometime around March 2018.
The consumer is reporting this as a burn and injury safety hazard, he and his wife are afraid to place a casserole or other dish on the racks because if the rack falls with the dish then it could spill hot liquid on whichever is using it at the time.
He contacted the manufacture and spoke with a helpline who when they had no answer for him advised him that there was no one above them for him to speak with and that there is nothing they could do to help him and his wife.
There are no injuries being reported .
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with potential for injury, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description:
I was preheating the oven to 350 degrees when the oven door suddenly exploded sending glass all over the kitchen and countertops. The explosion also knocked the handle off one side of the oven door. This is the second time the incident has happened, the first was in 2012.
At that time it was still under warranty and the oven door was replaced after many weeks.

It's a SEARS, Kenmore model number 790.36902901. It was delivered in January 2011.

There are over 300 incidents of the same "explosion" listed on various consumer websites with this same make and model number.
justification: The oven door exploded, sending glass everywhere, which poses a significant injury risk, though no injury was mentioned in this specific incident. The occurrence likelihood is high given the 300+ reported incidents with the same model.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that the refrigerator electrical wiring at the rear of the refrigerator had a fire that melted  the electrical harness which caused the unit to halt from cooling.   He stated that he had contacted a repair person and when he came out he notified him of the incident and that he had not seen this before.   

 Consumer stated that he contacted the fire Marshall and they  informed him that they would like to inspect the incident. 5/27 A fire personnel came out and examine the damages. Consumer stated that there was a recall on the motherboard about a design flaw.


The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised to send pictures of the incident .  He was informed that the despite that there was an incident the unit worked because the fire was contained.
justification: The incident involved a fire that caused damage to the refrigerator but was contained without injury or death, and the unit continued to function.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his electric range he purchased November 14, 2016 and had no problems until sometime around June 21, 2017 when he entered the kitchen and saw that his right rear burner was on and bright red although no one had been in the kitchen before this time.
He turned the range off.
This incident repeated itself Saturday morning June 24, 2017.
The caller contacted the manufacturer who said they were transferring him to Safety but then the call failed.  
This same thing occurred with a second call to the manufacturer.
He then contacted the retailer who is sending a repair tech June 28, 2017.
There are no injuries being reported.

As reported the stove top came on by itself.  This happened because the brain of the computer shorts out from power surges.  This happens often in the caller's area.  The tech that fixed by replacing the whole panel on the stove told caller this happens now and then.  Maybe they should have some kind of safety device that would prevent this from happening.  This could have burned down caller's house.  This is a scary incident!  Can something be done so this will not happen again.  Thanks,  [REDACTED]
justification: The burner turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injuries, but it poses a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
These consumers are reporting their electric stove due to safety hazards over the past few years. They have had to replace the left front burner because once turned on it would not turn off approximately three years ago.  
The caller replaced the circuit board the Spring of 2017 because it was displaying an F10 code and now it is still occasionally displaying the F10 code and giving them safety problems.  The F10 does not stop beeping until the callers are able to cool the oven and the only way they can cool the oven off is by unplugging it or flipping the breaker then opening the door.
Stove was purchased from an Ohio retailer in 2007.
The callers are reporting this as a severe safety and burn hazard.
There are no injuries being reported.
The caller did contact the manufacturer who referred her to CPSC
She is asking that this range be recalled and replaced.
justification: The incident involves safety hazards with no reported injuries, and the recurring F10 code issue indicates a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Metal pieces from inside the disposal broke off. I turned on the disposer and heard terrible noises so I turned off and found the pieces inside.
justification: Metal pieces breaking off is an incident but no injury occurred as the user turned off the disposer upon hearing unusual noises.

incident_description:
Caller was cleaning her refrigerator. Took the glass out to clean it over the sink. While the caller was holding the glass over the sink and running water over it the glass shattered. Caller has a few minor cuts to the hand. No medical attention was required.

Glass was at room temperature per manufacturer instructions.
justification: Caller sustained minor cuts but did not require medical attention, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the oven was in use broiling on high for approximately 30 mins, smoke started to emit from the side and top of the oven door and then flames erupted on the interior of the oven which caused the glass door to shatter and melt.  She used water to contain the flames, there was an error code F10 beeping on the control panel alerting them that the oven was overheating.  

Consumer stated that the control panel has been replaced 3 times for the past 3 years. Most current September 2017.  The retailer was contacted  and she was advised to contact the manufacturer and report the incident she was transferred to the agency.  (6/7/18) A service technician was sent out and she was advised that because of the fire it is a cosmetic issue and cannot replace the door,

Consumer feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and a shattered oven door, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: When I was removing a pie from my GE electric oven, I accidentally bumped the top of the oven door with my leg. This resulted in a second-degree burn which I treated myself. Two days later the service technician determined the temperature of the top edge of the oven door to be 165 degrees. He also stated that the upper part of the front of the door was hot enough to burn a child. Upon contacting GE I was told that they met UL standards and "the front and sides of a range can vary from 152 to 212 degrees F., depending on the materials."
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn, indicating an injury, and the technician confirmed the oven door can reach burn-inducing temperatures.

incident_description: I prepared lemon chicken as usual. I have made this dish for over 15 years the same way. I placed the chicken in the oven in an Anchor Hocking glass casserole dish. Five minutes later I heard an explosion in my kitchen and smoke began to fill the oven, kitchen, living room and family room.  I immediately turned off my gas stove. When I opened the door of the oven, I saw that the glass casserole dish had exploded in my oven. There was olive oil and chicken broth and broken glass all over the bottom of my oven. The 5 pieces of chicken were sitting on the remainder of broken glass on the oven rack. This is a Fire Hazzard!  I can only imagine if I had not been in a room close to the kitchen when this happened. My whole home could have burned down. Not to mention, if my teenager or any family member had removed this faulty casserole dish from the oven with the defect that HAS BEEN KNOWN to THIS company for years, a severe oil burn, or laceration could have happened. There have been many complaints regarding this same issue with Anchor Hocking. I find it unusual that there has been nothing done about these SAFETY issues with HUNDREDS of Complaints.  ANCHOR HOCKING has explained the exploding glass as a safety mechanism or faulty care by the consumer. My casserole was less than 1 year old.  There was NO extreme temperature changes and NO damage to my casserole prior to using. I now am afraid to use my Kitchen Aide oven that is saturated with oil near the gas igniter. I have saved the glass from the casserole dish for testing if needed. I also have many pictures.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass dish causing a fire hazard and potential for injury, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Bosch dishwasher.  This was one of the dishwashers that was previously recalled.  I had the recall work completed, which involved a cord replacement.  On June 3rd, while the dishwasher was running, the lights flashed and there was a burning smell and the dishwasher stopped working.  Since the dishwasher was over eight years old, I figured the control panel had died and the dishwasher had reached the end of its effective lifespan.  On June 4th purchased another Bosch dishwasher.  When I had the dishwasher installed on June 15th, the installer was going to use the existing cord.  I asked the installer to use the cord that came with the new unit and when the installer removed the old cord, the inside of the box, supplied as a recall replacement, was burned.  The contacts were totally burned/melted and it looked as though the unit had been on fire.  The installer stated that he had never seen another dishwasher junction box that had looked that bad.
justification: The incident involved a burned cord and junction box, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the installer had never seen such severe damage before.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the can opener shreds metal while using it to open cans.  He stated that after opening 3 cans of food he noticed that there were tiny metal s in the contents of the food.

Caller stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they were not able to find the item in their database.

Caller feels that this can opener is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves metal shredding into food, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We use the range several times per day. After about two years in service, the right front burner began intermittently getting excessively hot.  The problem became more frequent to where now the burner does not shut off at any temp setting, I.e. I can set the burner to low and it never shuts off until I turn the switch off.  This is on a dual burner element and happens whether using one or both burners in that position.  I can boil water in about two minutes on the lowest setting.  This is a serious hazard for burns and fire.
justification: The burner's failure to shut off poses a serious hazard for burns and fire, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
This refers to a gas leak in a Samsung range (Model NX58H9500WS Serial# 0BR47DDGA00822R.) This range is being used with propane . We noticed a propane smell on & off for some time and called our propane company to investigate in Oct 2017. The technician found a leak in the Gas Safety Valve Assembly (Part # DG94-00449A ) of the range and replaced this part. We again noticed a gas smell and  in Feb. I purchased a leak detector and found a leak in the same part. This time we called an appliance repair person who confirmed the problem and again replaced the same part  on Feb 12 2018. We immediately detected a leak again in the same part and contacted Samsung directly who was kind enough to send a Samsung tech ([REDACTED]) to examine the range. He again replaced the  same part on Feb 23 and while he was there I used the meter and showed him that this part still leaks. [REDACTED] called Samsung corporate who advised that it would be referred to the engineering dept. [REDACTED] called me back on March 1 and told me that:
ÃÂ	The engineering dept was not able to tell him if this gas leak is normal or safe
ÃÂ	When asked he said he ÃÂthinksÃÂ the the range is safe to use and that it is normal for this part to leak gas.
According to my gas meter the leak is consistent at >80ppm and often >160 and even >320ppm  These reading are without using the range. There is a distinct smell of gas noticeable under the range 
If you use the oven or burners even from a brief period  the leak from the Safety Valve assembly reads >640ppm on the leak detector which is the maximum indication on the meter. The attached video was taken after 1 burner was turned on for about 3 seconds then turned off.  I have videos to show the meter reading and the exact spot on the Gas Safety Valve where it is leaking.
I do not believe a gas leak of this degree is normal and have asked Samsung again to look into this and was told it was escalated to Samsung corporate but have not heard back from them
FYI This part (Gas Safety Valve Assembly (Part # DG94-00449A ) is used on multiple models of Samsung ranges
justification: The gas leak poses a significant risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Elite 40" Dual Fuel range, (model 79075503200) which was purchased on 04/09/03, recently malfunctioned.  On Saturday, 3/3/18 I was on my second floor at home cleaning all morning.  Around 1:30 in the afternoon I heard what I thought was the oven timer going off - quite odd considering I hadn't been cooking at all that day.  When I came downstairs, the display showed an error "F3" and the display was foggy.  I tried turning the timer off to no avail.  Then I touched the range and noticed quickly that it was hot to the touch.  When I opened the oven, I realized the top coil was on max and it must have been on max for many hours.  Seconds later the smoke detector went off.  Because I couldn't manually turn the oven off I went to the basement and cut the breaker.

When I called Sears' customer service, I was informed that I had performed the exact fix that they would've suggested (turning off the breaker).  I was also told that this model has had these types of issues in the past.  I informed the rep that turning the breaker off and then back on was fine (though it wasn't in my case, because when I did the oven turned right back on again), but the safety hazard in this matter needed to be addressed.  After bouncing around from department to department (and setting up a Sears Home Repair call for that following Wednesday for $89), I was ultimately disconnected and never did speak with someone about the safety hazard.

On Wednesday, 3/7/18 the Sears Home Repair rep inspected my range and informed me that the electronic range control panel had "blown" and there wasn't a repair because the part is no longer made.  He also informed me that just two months earlier he'd had to make the same diagnosis on the exact same model.

Today, 3/9/18, I made several attempts via chat to discuss the product safety hazard of this product.  Again, I was bounced around with no department wanting to address my concerns.  When I asked to speak with someone about my product safety concerns - after the rep had checked for recalls on this range - the number I was given was for the CPSC.

Had I not been home, the oven would have been on high unattended for days.  I'm normally not at home during the weekends, and I shudder to think about the consequences.

While I'm disappointed I'm currently without a working oven at the moment, I'm more concerned that this expensive piece of equipment could malfunction as it did.  I believe this is a very serious product safety hazard, and should be addressed as such.  An oven should not independently turn on - and stay on - for an indeterminate amount of time.  Considering how hot to the touch the range was (and was for four hours after I cut the breaker) I cannot imagine how hot it would have been unattended for days.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.
