incident_description:
I have had a Cuisinart  EPC1200PC pressure cooker for a few months that I had received as a present.  Cooking was fast and healthy.  This unit has an internal pot and an outer shell.  The internal pot is removable and dishwasher safe.

When food is finished, it is well over 212 degrees fahrenheit due to the pressure.  One cools it down slowly or quickly, then opens it to release the pressure.  One can then serve the food.  It will stay warm as long as one likes.

The danger zone for food is between 40 and 140 degrees.  Once food cools to 140, bacteria begin to grow rapidly.  (Some would be more conservative and say 160.) Most are not going to stick a thermometer in there and wait.  Most will try to put it in the fridge sooner.  Botulism and Salmonella can be deadly.

The problem is that the design makes it impossible to remove the inner pot safely.  Imagine sticking . your arms out at shoulder height and lifting a 16 lb weight about a foot and a half and then setting it down.  It can be done. It can hold about 20 or more lbs.  Now consider that the space between the inner pot and the outer pot is one quarter inch high.   That means you somehow need to flatten your fingers to lift it.  The outer rim only sticks out about a quarter inch.  So you have to crush your fingers and keep them plastered to the teeny rim of the inner pot to lift it.  Did I mention that the inner pot can be close to 212 degrees and the outer pot even hotter?  So crush your fingers between two boiling pieces of metal and lift up to 25 lbs of sloshing boiling liquid.  

There is no way to do this safely.  Most people would grab a potholder.  But the potholder won't fit in that 1/4 inch slot.  You need to crush your fingers than wrap the potholder around them but now it's more to be put in there and you'd need to hammer your fingers down to paper thin size. 
 
Sounds pretty crazy, no?

I assumed I was missing some part.  THere would be something to grab the inner pot without fear of burning one's self.  One that would let one move 20 lbs of sloshing liquid slow enough so a gallon of boiling liquid  didn't pour all over oneself.  Perhaps it would even allow for some mechanical advantage so one didn't need to have 25 lbs pulling with arms at 180 degrees to the floor.  Maybe there was a lid to the inner pot and one could cover it before it cools down preventing bacteria from falling in.   Even so, the container must sit at room temperature for several hours before on can lift it.

So I wrote Cuisinart.  I asked how they recommended I get the food out before it was in the food safety zone.  I was told that I had to file a claim with their legal department.  I wrote back stating I would promise not to sue--I just wanted to know if I was missing a part.  Once again they refused tp respond and asked me to fill out a claims report.

I didn't ask for money.  I didn't want money.  I just wanted advice.  Now I recognize that know the unit is dangerous.  And they don't want this dangerous unit in the hand of someone wanting that the public should be protected..

I just noticed the newer version of the product...it features special safety handles so one doesn't need a "tea towel" to lift 20 lbs of boiling liquid sloshing and carrying at arms length and parallel with the floor.

It should be recalled.  There is no way to use it safely and the fact that they've redesigned it demonstrates they know it.
justification: The description details a design flaw that makes it highly likely users will burn themselves while attempting to remove the hot inner pot, indicating a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
Dear Sir or Madam:

On November 14, 2017, I purchased a new LG gas range model LSG4513ST, serial number
707KMHW03681. The range was purchased at ABC Warehouse, 15477 Hall Road, Macomb
Township Michigan, 48044 (receipts attached).

I am convinced that this range is a potential killer and poses an extreme threat to my family's
very life, as well as the threat of extreme injury!

Your range has caused several instances of inadvertent gas buildup within our house with
corresponding threat of asphyxiation, and/or potential explosion or fire, a potential silent killer!
The basic fault is the location and design of the gas burner control knobs on the angled face of
the stove top. Minor brushing of these knobs with one's body during use or work on the stove
top has in multiple events opened the gas burner to gas flow without ignition. When this occurs,
it is not obvious from position of the knobs, sound, or odor, and is easily overlooked. Upon
leaving the kitchen, we have in several instances, become aware of substantial gas build-up
within the house due to this condition. Luckily my family did not retire for the night with this
condition or we would not now be alive to write this letter.

A similar problem is the inadvertent ignition of a stove top burner while one's arms are above
the stovetop. This results from mistaken burner ignition due to the position of the burner control
knobs, the very minor pressure necessary to turn the knob to ignition, and the speed of ignition.
This type of unwanted ignition has very nearly caused burns to us and our clothing. In my
opinion, it is very likely that someone will be burnt very seriously when their clothing catches on
fire.

These conditions of inadvertent gas release and inadvertent burner ignition has now occurred
multiple times in just two months of use, despite our knowledge of this issue and attempts to
guard against these conditions, checking, double checking, and triple checking. While we have
been extremely diligent in trying to guard against and check for these conditions, it is not
humanly possible to adequately guard against these conditions, even with obsessive checking.
Nor do we want to spend our lives checking the range and in fear of disaster.

Most recently after preparing dinner, and what we felt was careful checking, we became aware
of an extremely strong odor of gas throughout our house, again! We found gas flowing from two
burners that we inadvertently opened without ignition in the manner described above. We
immediately ventilated our home but believe we were literally minutes away from a substantial
catastrophe. We believed that we had adequately checked for inadvertent gas flow, but
obviously had not. Someone had used the stove without enough checking, and this simple
mistake could have easily ended our lives. This range is a killer!

We must ask for a full refund of the purchase price for our range and the additional secondary

incident_description:
On 5/22/18, our Kenmore Elite Model 79046719602 oven door exploded. This was absolutely a terrifying experience and I have no words for the terror and panic it caused, much less the trauma by glass exploding in my face, on my body, in my feet and in my hair. Shards of glass were stuck in our cabinets by the force. We spent hours cleaning and will likely continue to find glass everywhere leading to I'm sure future injury with additional glass being stepped on by our family.
justification: Glass exploded causing trauma and potential future injuries, but no death reported.

incident_description:
It is a 5 quart copper cookware kettle with a lock down lid. When your using the kettle and put on the lid to move it away from the heat or drain the water.You need to put the lid on and both handles snap down to secure the lid, except when you do that they snap down and trap your hand in against the wall of the kettle. We just bought it and my wife has had it happen three times already. I tried it and if your careful and snap it down properly it is easy to understand how it happens. The only option is to smack down the handles, risking it tipping or sliding out of your control and spilling the whole contents, which would be exposing yourself to a worse scenario than smashing or pinching your hands against the hot kettle.
 So far her Burns and abrasions haven't required a trip to the doctor, but it will happen to someone. We are returning the product back to vendor. Any questions please feel free to contact me.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and abrasions, indicating an injury (severity 3), and the description notes it has happened multiple times, making it likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Gas oven has over heated multiple times, beginning in August 2017, September 2017, January 2018.....with the last incident on May 12, 2018.  Repair tech took infared readings after one of the repairs.  Oven was at 350 degrees and the front user panel registered 254 degrees with the back reading 260.  Samsung has indicated this is caused by using the back burner while the oven is on (not true), not using the overhead exhaust ( not indicated in the user manual) and a bad temperature sensor.

I haven't been seriously burned because you can't touch it long enough to get burned!
justification: The oven has overheated multiple times, but no serious injuries have occurred, only potential for burns.

incident_description:
On May 4, 2018, while cooking eggs, the cap covering the rivet that holds the handle to the pan, exploded sending the cap flying and striking me in the stomach.

Bed & Bath, the seller had me contact "Table Top Unlimited" ref#[REDACTED]. I spoke with service rep. [REDACTED] and was told that there had been a few reports of this and she would need to contact the manufacturer. After a few days, they contacted me and right away disclaimed that this had ever happened and that the results were from too high of heat on the unit.

incident_description:
I purchased a 3 QUART SAUCEPAN under the Betty Crocker name. On or around Feb, 2018, I was boiling water with the saucepan and left it running without realizing that there was no water left. When I went to retrieve the saucepan to move it from the kitchen through the dining room to the garage to stop the smoke accumulating all over the house, the BOTTOM FELL OFF THE SAUCEPAN with the separated bottom layer of the pan dropping onto the floor very close to my leg and feet as well as metal from the saucepan spreading all over and damaging a section of my tiled kitchen flooring as well as a huge section of my dining room floor from the little round aluminum balls from the saucepan scattering when the bottom layer of the saucepan separated from the pan. While the bottom layer fell onto the floor, the edges of the pan started catching fire. 

The company- Formula Brands is not willing to acknowledge the problem and below is their response:

 " warping and separation of an impact bonded base on a cookware (sauce pan/pot) only begins to occur at a temperature of 590C/1094F. If there is substance in the pot, the temperature of the pan/pot cannot exceed 125C/250F. The silver colour of the stainless steel will also change colour, depending how long the pan/pot is left heating with nothing inside; a blue or rainbow tinge along the bottom of the pan will appear if it has been left heating for a little while. If left heating empty for a long time, it will change to a brown/bronze colour. If your sauce pan is a dark bronze colour, then I am sorry to advise you that your flooring will not be covered as the manufacturer is not responsible for misuse. However, if your sauce pan is a stainless steel colour, then please send in your sauce pan to my attention, as I will arrange to have it investigated by an independent 3rd party testing lab that will provide us with an analysis report". 

Their so called independent 3rd party testing lab is in Hong Kong with company name :
[REDACTED]

Yes, from the pictures that I had sent by email to the company, they already surmise that the color is bronze/brown and by asking me to send them the pot, they are appearing to address my complaint knowing that the pot is likely bronze/brown in color and that they will not cover the damage as they can restate again that it is a case of misuse. The issue is not just a case of misuse but the fact that the saucepan was manufactured to such poor standards (the bottom soldered to the saucepan instead of welded) that there is the potential for serious damage to the consumer should the bottom fall onto a person's feet or leg or any part of their body resulting in serious burns and bodily harm. There is nothing on the packaging that warns the consumer that there is the potential for this to happen. I have had this happen in the past to other pots by accident and have never had the bottom fall off the saucepan. 

I see Formula Brands saucepan is sold under different names in stores such as [REDACTED] and others under the brand name Betty Crocker, I believe [REDACTED] and others that I am not aware of. 

The damage to my flooring is approximately in the  $2000 plus range as such an incident happened as a result of the saucepan being manufactured to such poor standards that the bottom separated from the saucepan under high heat and there were no warning signs whatsoever on the packaging that this could happen. If I had known that, I would have just left the saucepan on the stove until it cooled off and then trashed it and most importantly, had I known that the bottom would separate, I would not have purchased the saucepan in the first place.

If Formula Brands' position is that there is nothing wrong with their saucepans, they should pay for a metal inspection and testing lab in the US to check and examine their product  and not their Hong Kong based ÃÂindependent 3rd Party testing labÃÂ.  Additionally if the result of the testing shows that there is nothing wrong with their saucepan -  they should put a warning sign that the bottom layer could potentially separate from the saucepan when heated beyond a certain temperature. 
Or if the result of the tests shows a poorly manufactured saucepan that could potentially cause severe harm to the consumer, the products manufactured under the same  standard and quality should be recalled. 

I have another saucepan I purchased at the same time from the store that I would be willing to send to a metal manufacturing company in the US to seek their opinion of the quality of the product.

I would ask that Formula Brands or General Mills that provide licensing authority to market the product under the name Betty Crocker pay for the testing.
justification: The incident involved property damage (flooring) and a near-miss with potential injury, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood is possible as misuse of cookware is not uncommon, but severe outcomes like this are less frequent.

incident_description:
Our LG Dishwasher, Model LDS4821ST  Serial number 012KWCF02515 caught fire after it's control board burned out.

We notified LG and they could care less.  

From what we have found on the web, this is a common occurrence and even some house fires have resulted. Also, an LG factory authorized repair service located on the LG web site told us, this is a common problem.

We think the dishwashers should be recalled and replaced.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident with no reported injury, and the problem is described as common.

incident_description: My Kenmore electric range had an electrical fire that started in the control panel. This occurred while I was using it.  I was baking frozen French fries that I have baked numerous times before, same brand, temp, etc.  After 10 minutes I checked them and they were burnt (normally cook for 25 min). I removed them and hit "stop" on my range at which time the control panel had an electrical fire. I was able to unplug the appliance before further damage or injury occurred.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but no injury occurred, and the user was able to prevent further damage.

incident_description:
Before and after the examination I spoke with this witness in person. This witness was asked to describe their experience with the fire. The following in substance is the information obtained as a result of that voluntary interview: 

ÃÂI put a load of dishes in my dishwasher was laying on my couch and smelled something awful & then walked into my kitchen and saw flames coming out the top of the dishwasher and counter. I then tried to put it out but the smoke was too thick so I got my kids and animals out and as I was on the phone with the fire dept. I saw sparks shoot out the front of my dishwasher then fire department showed upÃÂ
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Over the range Frigidaire microwave oven made by Electrolux starts when the door is opened even when there is no time left.

So, not only does the open door, cutoff feature not work; the oven turns itself on when you open the door.

I can't think of a more dangerous scenario.
justification: The microwave turning on when the door is opened poses a direct risk of injury due to unexpected operation, and the likelihood is high given the described malfunction.

incident_description: Star Wars 6 can mini fridge cooler purchased at Best Buy around May 2017 caught fire while in use 7/1/2017. Injury and surrounding damage avoided by some very smart and alert teenagers who immediately unplugged it. Had it been unattended I fear severe damage and tragedy.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury occurred due to quick action, placing it at severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but possible with faulty appliances.

incident_description: Consumer went to light gas range and it exploded and sent glass and parts throughout the room.  Glass was found on all sides of kitchen and debris field was only limited by walls.  Glass cut consumer on hand.  After explosion gas was still burning around the area of the burner that the consumer attempted to light.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury from glass cuts, and the explosion caused significant damage, but there was no death.

incident_description:
While grasping the handle and opening the toaster oven-grill with her left hand to remove what she was cooking, my wife received a second degree burn on her finger from the front of the toaster oven door.  There are three causes:
1.  The handle is too close to the door; 
2.  As you lower the door with the handle, the metal pole that the handle is attached to rotates, causing your finger to rotate towards the hot door. 
3.  As there is no insulation on the oven door, it becomes hot enough to cause second degree burns after even a brief touch.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The described design flaws make such injuries likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
We plugged in the hot plate and it works on heavy duty timer which turns the hot plate off and on we only have it on for roughly 3 h at a time.
We use it for Saturday the sabbath . So sabbath morning it turned on and it was on for 30 min my kids where sitting in the kitchen and all of a sudden it exploded and my kids got shards and chunks on there cloths and hair and thanks got it was just minor cuts and my wife as she is a nurse practitioner  took care of the wounds
justification: The hot plate exploded causing minor cuts to the children, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Our Jenn Air Electic range has begun to beep, beep, beep and then turns the oven on by itself when no one has touched it. Shut the unit down by turning off the power. Wait a while, turn the electricity back on- it does it again. Turn off the oven, 5 minutes later it beeps beeps and the oven comes on with no one near it.
justification: The oven turns on unexpectedly, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or damage is reported.

incident_description:
This morning our Aroma Kettle exploded with a loud bang. It wasnt in use but my wife place our kid's lunch bag near it and it may have pressed and held down the button for heating.

It was deafening, very scary and could have injured someone if someone was closer to the kettle as it sent a strange metal looking powder around which might have be hot or dangerous.

The kettle was less than a year old. Model no AWK-108. See photo to get serial number (not clear which number it is).

In all transparency, we did recently (a few weeks ago) also moved the kettle to a different plug inside the kitchen as it was always triggering a safety Ground Fault Circuit Interrupters of a plug with GFCIs. 
Nothing seemed wrong with the kettle. It worked on other plug in the kitchen. In hindsight, this seems like a very bad idea that we just ignored it was triggering the GFCI but it worked fine for weeks. 

Perhaps this safety (interruptor) should really be on the Kettle more than the plug itself.

So we are a bit unsure what caused this. We think it worth putting the word out regarding our safety concern with this product.
justification: The kettle exploded but no one was injured, though it could have caused harm if someone was nearby.

incident_description: A ceramic tall mug made by California Pantry was being used to heat up milk to make hot chocolate. The mug states microwave safe & dishwasher safe. This is a setting that has been used many time to duo the same thing in the microwave for the same period of time (1 1/2 minutes). This occurrence caused second (2nd) degree burns to the inside palm of hand as well as many fingers. The hand was examined & treated for second degree burns & medication, wrapping was needed in order to heal the burn process.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring medical treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:

I had started the recipe on high then turned it to low per the in instructions for the recipe.  After about an hour I began to smell a strong burn smell from inside the pot. (Not the wiring) This was in spite of the amount in the pot, the liquid and the fact it was on low.  It was at a high boil in spite of being turned down.  It was very hot.  I ended up finishing the pot roast in the oven.  There was definitely the potential for a fire.  After removing the contents to another pan I noticed the ceramic crock had a crack all the way through and there was some of the liquid which was dripping from the crack into the metal case which. It was likely the strong burn smell.  I noted the crack went from the bottom of the crock all the way through but curiously inside the metal liner where the heating source is.  

I called Maxi-Matic as I don't feel this should be normal.  They told me since it was out of its year warranty they could not do anything.  And, I could send it to them for testing at my expense.  It probably weights 10 - 15 lbs.
If I had not been home, this would have caused a fire.  It was overly hot.  

Elite Slow Cooker
Model MST 900R
PDC 2215
Intertwined 312629
justification: The slow cooker malfunctioned with potential for fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the gas range/oven had been emitting gas odor for approximately 1 month, she stated that they were not aware where the odor was coming from.  She stated that gas company came out for an annual check and discovered that there was the odor and when they test the CO level it was extremely high.  She stated that they red tag her stove and advised her not to use it until she requested a technician came out for a repair or replacement.

Caller stated that she contacted the manufacturer who advised that they needed the technician's report to proceed.

Caller stated that she would like a replacement for her range/oven from the manufacturer.  She feels that this unit is unsafe and should be recalled.

Service Master affiliated with American Home Shield sent check to replace stove.

Purchased an upgraded stove from Lowes on Great Oaks in San Jose.  Driver too old stove- told him it was red tagged.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with high CO levels, posing a serious risk, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We bought a Mr Coffee coffeemaker in July/Aug 2016 at Kroger in Columbus Ohio. 

It has sat on the kitchen counter used about once a day since then. Never fallen off the counter or had anything weird happen. Only used it to make regular black coffee with grounds from the store. Kept it reasonably clean. 

Today I made a couple cups of coffee in the afternoon. A couple hours later I heard the coffee maker making noises like it was still turned on. The little green light on the on/off button was not on, though. So I touched the button the way you would to turn it off, just to check. 

Sparks flew out of the button area in my face and up my arm-- my husband saw the light from around the corner. Not a couple of sparks. A ton, like a welder. 

It tripped the circuit, too. We unplugged it and contacted the company who has asked me to ship them the faulty machine. But I think you should know, too. 

This was a relatively new kitchen electronic, used as designed, and it electrocuted me when touching the on/off switch. Seems like a pretty bad flaw in a coffee maker. 

The model number is SK13 and the numbers on the plug were DG and H224. I don't know what that means but the company asked for it so maybe that's helpful. 

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injury (sparks flew in the face and up the arm), but such occurrences are unlikely given proper use and maintenance.

incident_description: I own a GE electric free-standing oven range. Today, the glass on the inner oven window exploded. The oven was being used normally. There was no previous obvious damage to the glass, and it had not been hit or the door slammed.
justification: The oven glass exploded during normal use, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: I was using the product to cook an omelet, as described in the product instructions.  Approximately 3/4 of the way through the cooking time, the latch suddenly came undone, the lid popped up and hot eggs blew out of the machine and onto the counter and floor.  I was standing on the other side of the kitchen, so I did not sustain any injury.  However, if I had been closer to the machine, I could have been burned by the hot eggs.

incident_description: Purchased a electric range from Best Buy 8/11/17 Model LSE4613ST.  When delivered, the delivery man brushed against the knobs and the cook top of the range inadvertently went on burning all the wrapping.  The oven was replaced with a new range of same kind.  I have owned the range now for 8 mos and have had several episodes of the knobs inadvertently going on just by leaning near the range. No one knew this had occurred and the box went up in flames, melted the microwave, and cabinet doors above.  This is a major design flaw and had I not been home to smell the burning fire, my house could have  gone completely up in flames.  The knobs are not secure and very quickly can turn on by simply brushing next to them.  I reported this to LG and to BEST BUY and no one is c concerned even though they know there is a design flaw here.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Electric Stove model 790.95043503 with a "runaway" cooking surface - it would not turn off and I had to flip the circuit breaker to cut the power to the entire stove. After about ten minutes I heard a click in the back of the stove and I was able to turn the power back on to the stove and the cooking surface remained off. where I was told that my model number was not in the system for recall. They informed me that I should report the issue to CPSR 

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2009/frigidaire-and-kenmore-smoothtop-electric-ranges-recalled-due-to-fire-hazard
justification: The stove malfunctioned but was controlled without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: I had just started my dishwasher, Kitchen Aid, and after approximately 5 to 10 minutes I heard loud popping and when I turned around there were sparks and  small flame coming from the top of my dishwasher. I immediately went to cancel and shut down to open door, it wouldn't take the cancel. But thank God the circuit breaker tripped and shut down. There was smoke coming out. It was a horrible smell and a lot. Thank God I was in the kitchen when this occurred. My 84 yr old mother and 89 year old dad, who is on hospice reside with me.  She didn't even hear the popping from the next room. The smoke did affect my mother who has asthma, but thank God her inhaler took care of it.  Took a while to get smoke out from kitchen, dining, living room area since this is all open together. This was so dangerous. It did cause some scorching to my counter top edge which is wood.  I did call Whirlpool and they had a tech come out to check. The harness went on fire. Damaged inside of door and control panel. Burned plastic and insides. They have agreed to pay 50% of a New dishwasher from there site on line and the installation and removal of the damaged machine. They gave me a reference number good for 30 days.

incident_description:
We received a replacement blade from Cusinart for our DLC-7 model food processor in mid 2017.
The blade quality is somewhat different along the cutting edge, and with limited usage, it has developed an irregular and jagged edge on it. You can  not dry it with a towel without the towel sticking or catching on the barbs on the edge. While drying it on March 7 2018, the blade caught on the towel and was jerked out of my hand,  and I sustained a 2 inch long laceration on my hand that required surgical repair. We never had any issues like this with the original-now recalled blade. Cusinart is going to send me another replacement blade. Hopefully it will be different quality.
justification: The incident resulted in a 2-inch laceration requiring surgical repair, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue appears specific to a defective replacement blade, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
We own the Capresso H2O Plus Electric Water Kettle (http://www.capresso.com/water-kettles/h2o-plus.html) and have owned it for approximately one year.

This morning I boiled a full kettle to make coffee. When the water had come to a boil, I lifted the kettle and tipped it to pour. As it began to pour, the top of the handle separated from the kettle and it tipped over and rapidly dumped almost the entire kettle of boiling water.

I was scalded a bit on the hand and foot by small splashes, but was fortunate not to be severely burned and extremely fortunate that one of my kids or my dog was not next to me.

This is product extremely dangerous.

I reported the issue to Capresso and they were dismissive, concerned only with whether I could demonstrate if the kettle was under warranty.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (scalding) from boiling water, but no severe burns or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it's a specific product failure.

incident_description:
I purchased a BergHOFF Ostend Cookware Set from Gilt.com in January 2017, and I have been experiencing the below problems with the set since January 2017. When I got the cookware, I washed it and put it away. I didn't use it at all for a few weeks, when I used one pot. The smell was terrible - it's sort of a burning plastic smell. At first, I thought I somehow forgot to wash the cookware before I used it and something was burning off the bottom because it was new or whatever. So the next time I used the cookware (it was that same pot, which is really the only one I needed from the set), the smell was there again. It's a terrible lingering smell and from fumes. It seems to linger for hours, and it makes us feel sick for a good number of hours afterward.

So I decided there was something wrong with that particular pot and didn't use any of the cookware for a while because, like I said, I really only needed that one pot. I looked on Gilt's site and saw that the set was nonreturnable, so I wasn't happy about what I thought was that one problematic pot, but I assumed the other two were fine, though I had no particular reason to use them at the time.

Months pass and I try to use another piece of the cookware. Same problem. And then a few days ago my boyfriend used yet another piece and same problem. The smaller pots are actually worse and the fumes and smell even bothered my eyes a lot this time. At that point I was pretty irritated because I paid for this set and it's useless. And who knows what effect breathing those fumes has. I emailed BergHOFF and they asked me if I'm using a gas stove (I am). And, in a series of emails yesterday, they've told me (1) they know of this problem and they think the higher heat on the gas stove is causing the issue, which they claim "1-2 customers" have reported, (2) all they are willing to do is exchange my set for a new version of the same set, and they expect me to pay shipping for that, and (3) they would have been willing to swap it for another set but they don't have any, and (4) they can't give me my money back because they are just a fulfillment center.

Can you believe this? These people are making and selling a product they admit they know has a problem with releasing who knows what kind of fumes when people use it, and they are telling me the best they can do it send me another of the same set and I have to pay shipping for that. That's ridiculous. BergHOFF has totally disgusted me with their total lack of regard or concern for the health issues this product is causing. I hate to even think what could happen if someone with respiratory problems used one of these pots. BergHOFF should be considering the risks this cookware poses and reporting it to the CPSC themselves, but they can't even be arsed to do a simple exchange or refund for someone actually affected by it.
justification: The incident describes physical symptoms (feeling sick, eye irritation) caused by fumes from the cookware, indicating injury. The likelihood is possible as the issue is known to affect some users but not all.

Board burns, contact become loose , copper foil melts & becomes unattached. Meanwhile temperature soars to harmful dangerous levels that could seriously harm or kill a person. Why? Micro control processor does not lock the oven door in an F10 Runaway condition. Also there is NO back up or redundant safety cutout with a consealed manual rest for the technician when the condition occurs! THE ONLY SAFE WAY TO STOP THE RUNAWAY AND KEEP YOUR HOME FROM BURNING DOWN IS TO TURN OFF THE MAIN UPSTREAM BREAKER!!!
justification: The incident describes a dangerous thermal runaway scenario with potential for serious harm or death, indicating high severity. The likelihood is considered possible due to the lack of safety mechanisms.

incident_description:
While unpacking Nd assembling for first time my new Cuisinart FP-12N Elite,

incident_description: Using an All-Clad copper core 1.5 qrt saucepan on a gas cooktop my wife was melting butter. As she was about to put in the eggs the saucepan exploded - the bottom stainless steel cap that covers the copper blew off with an explosion and the saucepan jumped 18 inches into the air and landed on the ceramic cooktop surface and cracked and broke the glasss. The pan was about 12 years old. The force was strong enough to make deep indentations in the steel cap that match with the 5 supports of the metal grate it was resting on.

incident_description: I have  a frigidaire smooth top stove, model # ples399ecd, that just turned on by itself and will not turn off.  It nearly burned my house down.
justification: The stove turning on by itself and nearly burning the house down indicates a significant hazard, though no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using my Cuisinart food processor to grate raw zucchini. Immediately after I started using it (switched to the "ON" position, grating disc in place on the motor shaft, work bowl and lid in the closed and locked position for proper operation) I heard a cracking sound, then a short creak. When I removed the processor work bowl, I discovered that the plastic on the motor shaft had failed, fracturing all the way through: back to front and top to bottom of the shaft. I was not injured, but a few jagged pieces of plastic from the shaft are missing. I'm not sure where they went, given how fast the motor shaft spins. This is a failure such that I can no longer safely operate this product. I use this processor frequently, but not for any "tough" jobs. I treat this product with kid gloves, so this hardware failure is an unpleasant surprise. It's Cuisinart model DLC-5BC. Color silver, 7 cup capacity, 120 V., 60 Hz., Max. 5 Amps. (This model was also included in the earlier 2016 product recall, involving failure of the chopping blades at the rivets.)
justification: The incident involved equipment failure without injury, and the model has a history of recalls, indicating possible recurring issues.

incident_description: On February 21 I was frying a brat in a 9.5 inch Gotham Steel pan when all of sudden there was a LOUD bang (sounded like a gun shot) my husband and I both looked at each other trying to figure out what happen I then notice one of the rivets that fastens the handle to the pan was not bright like the other (we found out later it was a cover over the rivet) I found that object 20+ feet away from the stove where I was standing It didn't hit anyone lucky or any serious object but it could of and could of been more serious than what it was  I have called the company or I thought it was company and they want pictures to give me a new one  I don't want a new one  I think it is dangerous to humans, objects and pets I have asked them instead of pictures and a new pan if they would issue a call tag and take this pan and investigate WHY this happen  If it happened to me it could of happen to others   ALSO it sticks and doesn't do as they advertise  Thank You  I was not frying on high heat as this pan burns easily so it was on low-medium heat

incident_description: Kitchen Aid dishwasher.  Have owned for 5-6 years.  Began washing dishes in the evening.  Heard loud pop sound in kitchen.  Found acrid black smoke coming from dishwasher door.  Turned off electricity to dishwasher.  Evaluation the next day by a technician found soot and melted plastic in the control panel inside the dishwasher door, primarily involving the area where wires connected to the computer control panel.
justification: The incident involved smoke and damage but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such electrical faults are not common but possible in older appliances.

incident_description:
Chefman Electric Kettle with Tea Infuser. 
Did not shut off.  Made 0.9L of boiling water, filled tea infuser, dropped into pot at 210 degrees.  Pot made the tea, stopped boiling, poured myself a mug of tea and left pot on to keep warm.  About 20 minutes later tea pot was boiling rapidly, splattering, and the bottom of my kitchen cabinets and wall was dripping with water from the steam.  It did not shut off until I unplugged it.  Very dangerous, plastic handles were so hot I had to use a oven mitt.  Was bought at Target as Xmas gift for me.
justification: The kettle failed to shut off, causing boiling water to splatter and steam to damage cabinets, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
In the fall of 2017, the consumer noticed that the oven rack in the smaller-top oven had the potential to tip over when it was pulled out.  The rack is used on the In the number 7 track position, the steel oven rack can act like a seesaw and fall down. There is a track that the oven rack sets in, but there is nothing on the track to keep the rack level and secure it, when it's pulled out.  

All of the other track positions in the oven, use the track above them to prevent this from happening.  There is nothing but the top of the oven itself to stop the rack from falling, when it's in that #7 position.  

The consumer's wife was cooking approximately a week ago.  Grease from the dish that was being cooked at the time, spilled on the floor and inside the oven and onto the oven's glass pane., when that rack was pulled out.  The wife was standing on the side of the oven, so she avoided injury.

1/23/2018:  The consumer called the manufacturer and reported the issue to them.  The rep. transferred the consumer over to a manager for ovens.  That person told the consumer that the #7 position is not intended to be used for cooking.  However, the consumer pointed out that the oven's owner manual showed a picture and provides instructions where the rack can be used in the #7 track position.  The manager repeatedly indicating that one of the lower tracks should be used.    Nothing else transpired out of the conversation.

The consumer said this presents a burn and fire hazard and the problem can occur regardless of the size of dish that is placed on that rack.

The consumer is aware of the problem, so he & his wife try not to use that track.  However, some foods are required to be cooked on the broil setting and that is the track/#7 position that the owner's manual recommends.

The range/oven did not appear to be included in any CPSC Recall.
justification: The incident involved a potential hazard with no injury reported, and the consumer is aware of the issue to avoid using the problematic rack position.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the pressure cooker was on for approximately twenty minutes when she noticed that steam had not stopped coming from the lid and handle of the unit. The consumer took the pressure cooker off the stove and noticed that the bottom of the food was burnt.

A few minutes after the consumer turned on the pressure cooker once again, she noticed steam coming mostly from the handle that would not subside. The unit was on for about twenty-minutes as well. The consumer removed the unit off the stove and as she placed it on the sink, the lid popped off, spilling the contents everywhere.

The consumer states that the unit has only been used twice. The consumer plans on keeping her pressure cooker for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved steam leakage and food burning, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:

I have not used the not used the dishwasher since that incident.cident.

incident_description: My daughter and I were cooking on the gas stove.  She turned the knob to turn the gas on, but the housing on the knob that slips over the valve switch on the stove broke and the knob came off in her hand.  The gas was coming from the burner, but it was not ignited.  I was standing there, so I was able to use my fingers to grab the valve and turn it closed.  Since then, two more of the knob housings have cracked.  I am concerned that someone, especially an elderly person, may have this happen, turn on the gas, have the knob come off, and then be unable to turn it off again.  It takes some finger strength to do it, and it is not easy to slip another knob off it's valve stem and unto another since there is a metal sheath that may or may not come off with the knob.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a broken knob, but no injury occurred as the gas was turned off promptly. The likelihood is rated as likely (4) due to the repeated failure of knob housings and potential difficulty for some individuals to turn off the gas.

incident_description:
My husband was standing next to the stove, putting something in the lower cabinet to the right of it away. He stood up and the oven exploded next to him.  The oven was cold. The oven was not touched. We heard a small explosion, then he found himself in the middle of a spray of glass that went at least 6 feet away. The glass continued to hiss and sizzle.  
While I am grateful he was not hurt, It makes me sick knowing this happened only hours after our grandchildren went home from visiting.
justification: The oven exploded but no one was injured, which fits severity level 2.

incident_description: Our Bosch dishwasher's power went out, went online, saw the recall; dishwasher was not one of the recalls.  Called for a repairman.  The power cord at the Bosch junction box burned out.  This appears to be the same problem the recalled dishwashers are experiencing.  The repairman agreed.  I have a blown out parts.
justification: The incident involved a power cord burning out, but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar issues have been noted in recalled models.

incident_description:

incident_description: Kitchen Aid water kettle, model # KEK1722ER handle separate (broke) away from kettle with hot water in kettle.

incident_description: We were running our GE dishwasher and noticed tremendous smoke coming out of the front of the dishwasher.  We unplugged it so no further damage was done.  When GE came out and opened the dishwasher you could see that the control panel had caught fire.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and the control panel caught fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
This is a GE gas range with a gas oven and gas burners.
model number PGS920SEF3SS
Serial number TF195320P

On two of the five range top burners, when placed to the lowest flame setting, the flame will go out.  When the nob is then adjusted back to a medium or high position, raw gas will be flowing from the burner straight into the house.  This is a very dangerous situation to have raw gas flowing.  We've had several situations where the gas "leak" is not noticed for a minute or two, during routine cooking.  

Furthermore, to turn off that burner, one must turn the burner past the "ignite" setting, which will potentially spark the gas.

Of note,  after setting the oven temperature, the gas oven will not ignite unless you "crack" a stove burner to release some gas from a burner.

There are videos of GE range owners on Youtube with this exact same problem.

thank-you!
justification: The incident involves raw gas leaking into the house, which is dangerous but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: I was cooking on the two front burners of the GE ProfileÃÂ 30" Built-In Gas Cooktop with Sealed Cooktop Burners and Right-Side Controls, product number JGP336WEVWW and the entire glass cooktop exploded into thousands of pieces. The pieces flew at speed across the room, reaching more than 25ft from the Cooktop's location. There was also a loud bang associated with the explosion.

incident_description:
In July of 2015 I purchased a Frigidaire 30 in double oven from Lowe's. The oven was received and installed properly.
 After 2 years of use, the interior walls of the oven were not built properly causing them to expand with more exposure to heat. This led to the racks in the oven falling. It is a faulty product that should have been recalled. 
The company told me that my 1 year warranty has expired. I explained that this is a faulty product that was not built properly they continued to tell me that they are not responsible and that my manufacturer warranty is out of date.
 After the company told me that they would not do anything due to my product being out of manufacturer's warranty I
contacted Lowe's because I purchased an extended warranty through them. They sent Jeff's Appliances out of Shelton to
assess the problem. They said that they product could not be fixed. They called the service department of Frigidaire directly
who told them that they know of the problem and it can not be fixed. They did not ever issue a recall. They stated that the
problem was not fixed until the next model was built In 2016/2017. Lowes stated that they would refund me the cost of the
oven. The problem then lies that all of the ovens that were in that price range did not fit in the cut out of my cabinets. The

Including Installation and a new extended warranty. I also had to cut my newly refinished cabinets. Lowes corporate
refunded the cost of the Installation. I am still infurated that an oven is still being manufactured that is completely faulty and
almost caused my mother to be severly burned on Thanksgiving when the rack fell with our turkey on it causing a huge
mess and a potential injury. I am also extremely frustrated that I had to pay the difference in the cost of the ovens when I
shouldn't have had to replace a 2 year oven in the first place if the manufacturer took responsibility

incident_description: I was using a Fagor Splendid pressure cooker to make beef stew.  This is about the 6th time I have used this appliance.  Everything seemed to be operating as usual.  It had been under pressure for the time specified in my recipe.  I removed it from the heat to cool.  Suddenly the "operating valve" (used to release pressure) blew off breaking into two large pieces and at least one small sliver.  The valve is made of plastic.

The lid will not even stay on this mug, they advertise it as being able to be shot and knocked over by a cat, but if you shake it in the least bit the lid rockets off spraying hot liquids everywhere, walls, ceiling, fridge, stove, my eyes my arms, my chest. incident_description:
Device: Rosewill Electric Hot Water Boiler and Warmer, 4.0 Liter Hot Water Dispenser, Stainless Steel / Black RHAP-16002

The device boils and keeps water warm to 212 (or 185) degrees, for instant access to hot water. I used the product successfully for 2 weeks. Then I went to use it and the stream of water would not turn off. I pushed the various buttons and got no response, meanwhile scalding water falling all over my hands, running down my counter top, and puddling all over the floor. The only way to stop the fast stream of scalding water was to unplug the device. The water damage ruined supplies that were in my cabinets and shelves, but I'm most concerned with what could have happened if small children had been around...that's a LOT of hot water spewing everywhere. Near boiling water was on my counter and floors of an approximate 4-6 feet wide width. Rosewill was unresponsive, but I have done my own testing and recreated the malfunction twice.
justification: The incident involved scalding water causing injury and significant property damage, with potential for worse outcomes if children were present.

incident_description:
I was lifting the crock pot by the side handles when one broke off. The hot contents spilled out to one side burning my hand. A few months later the other handle broke off. Really poor quality.

It's a Rancher Slow Cooker
model CP1170
Continuum Sales and Mktg.
Great Neck NY

incident_description: Samsung Gas Range model NX58J5600SG/AA less than 6 months old was being used to cook dinner.  After cooking was done, we found that the knob to turn off the gas burner was stuck and could not be turned off and the burner continued to burn gas.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern:
I am sending you these pictures of our Cuisinart DCC-1150 coffee pot (after 4 years of use) as I am 
concerned with the safety issue here. We were experiencing water on the counter under the coffee pot so my husband 
took the bottom off to investigate the problem and this is what he came up with. We did purchase another DCC-1150 as a replacement, but now I do not dare to leave it plugged in because of this safety issue. The pot has a timer to start the coffee at a certain time. Well, this just can't happen if you don't trust leaving it plugged in. (The instruction manual actually says: "Always unplug from outlet when not in use and before cleaning.")

My husband, an aerospace engineer, said that if proper materials were used, there would not have 
been corrosion to such a degree and there would have been less of a safety issue. We did send an email to Cuisinart asking 
that my complaint be forwarded to their engineering department, but a return email "scolded" us for removing the bottom plate as they could no longer provide a replacement (although the unit was out of warrantee).
We felt it important to disclose this problem to you as lives and houses could be in jeopardy.
justification: The incident describes a safety concern with the coffee pot due to corrosion, but no actual injury or damage occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue was identified before any harm could happen.

incident_description: On October 8, 2017, my husband decided to make oxtail soup for the family after church. He put the oxtail soup in a pressure cooker to cook. After about an 1 hour to 1 an a half hour he went to check on the soup and the lid malfunctioned and flew off and burned and exploded on him. My husband has second and third degree burns on his face, chest, arms and down his legs.

incident_description: I set my oven to a temperature of 335 degrees and placed food in it to cook, as I normally would.  Shortly after, I noticed a strange smell similar to melting plastic, and went to check the oven. When I opened the oven door, I could tell the temperature was far hotter than what it was set at.  My smoke alarms also went of immediately after opening the door. I checked the temperature with an external thermometer, and also by setting the oven to 500 degrees, at which point it immediately beeped, indicating that the temperature had already reached at least 500 degrees.

incident_description: I bought a smooth top oven for my 82 year old mother 12/30/2016.  The oven door handle just came off 01/03/2018. A potential burn/ injury hazard .  I got new part (just handle no new bolts included).  My husband replaced it and now it has fallen off again  less than a month later.(left side).  The threads are stripped in the handle.  I have contacted Frigidare several times.  I would think this handle should be recalled.

incident_description: I had been using this toaster oven for approximately 10 months. Due to this short timer issue, when baking potatoes (to save energy) I would have to restart the timer a few times until they were done. Within 10 minutes I heard my smoke alarm go off in my kitchen and discovered the toaster oven was smoking and  the flames shot out. The manufacturer's website does not have contact information so I felt the need to report it to the Consumer government agency.

incident_description: My sister bought a light up straw cup from Walgreens for my 8 year old. My two year old found it and popped off the battery cover. The cover was not secured with any kind of screw and I found a battery in his mouth. This is very, very dangerous!!! In past years, my sister has bought similar cups from Walgreens (the kids love them and love the flashing lights), but the battery cover was always secured with a screw. PLEASE change back to the safe light up cup from past years!! A child can easily die from a loose battery cover. I was very, very lucky that I noticed before he swallowed the battery!

incident_description: Maytag MMV4205FW1 microwave interlock switches failed at 6 months and again 6 months after repair.  Unit will either not determine that the door is open or closed and allow the unit to run, or the unit when closed will power up without any user interaction.
justification: The microwave's interlock switch failure poses a risk of unintended operation, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: We ran the dishwasher before we went to bed (about 11pm) as we usually do. The (granite) counter was hot, the cabinets surrounding it were hot, everything inside was untouchable, it was all so hot. incident_description:
I have a GE Profile Dishwasher: Model: PDW9280N00SS, Serial Number TM922574B.

We woke up around 4 a.m. on 2/10/18 to the smell of smoke and smoke alarm set off.  We came downstairs to find smoke billowing out of our dishwasher.  When we opened the dishwasher we discovered that all plastic parts of the dishwasher had melted, such as the arms at the bottom, the wheels and most of the racks.  Some of the plastic was smoldering and smoking.  The melted parts had dripped all over the vessels in the dishwasher.  It was so hot that it felt like the interior of a broiler or hotter and even with oven mitts, handling the dishes was impossible.  We switched off the circuit and waited for it to cool.  When it did, all the plastic had congealed destroying the entire contents of the dishwasher.  Some of the plastic had burnt, hence the smell.  All the plastic parts of the dishwasher had partially or completely melted.  It took nearly a week for us to get the smell out of the house, despite us leaving all the  externally venting exhaust fans on continuously and leaving some of the doors open, until it became unbearably cold.

We are now without a dishwasher and have lost an entire night's load, which includes our glasses, cups, plates, silverware, cookware and several serving ware, which are now destroyed.  We are going to have to repurchase all of them and a new dishwasher.  More importantly, this was a major fire hazard and had I not woken up and switched off the dishwasher we may have had a major fire.  Our children's bedroom was directly above the dishwasher and we shudder to think what might have happened.

We since contacted GE and were directed to their Monogram Preferred / Special Programs and Recalls.  They sent a technician out who said that (a) the dishwasher is unsalvageable; and (b) we were very lucky that the cabinets around the dishwasher did not catch fire.  However, they want us to pay for a new dishwasher and they have so far not reimbursed us for the destroyed vessels and damage.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and a major fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: This is a GE Monogram Dishwasher - I filled it as I normally do and started the load.  I left and three hours later when I returned, my house was filled with a horrible smell and smoke.  When I opened the door, it was still full of water and had apparently been running the entire time.  The bottom spinner was melted and the control panel on the top of the door showed signs of fire.  I disconnected the power and my husband removed the door panel.  The kitchen had small black particles on many of the surfaces.

incident_description:
147 Route 31
Appliance Fire
October 9, 2017 13:47:45
Hunterdon County Incident Number [REDACTED]

Alert:

	On Monday, October 09, 2017 at 13:47 Station 21 (Raritan Township), Station 49 (Flemington), the Flemington-Raritan Rescue Squad, and Raritan Township Police were dispatched to Fire-Box [REDACTED]; 147 Route 31, the Walmart  in Raritan Township for a reported cooler fire. 

Weather Conditions 

	At the time of the alert the temperature was approximately 73*F, humidity of approximately 93% and winds from the south west of 2.7mph. There were rain showers throughout the day. 

Fire Department Response

	At 13:56 [REDACTED] arrived on scene and advised of 'nothing showing' from the exterior of the structure. At 13:57 police unit 2123 advised that the fire was out. Units from the Raritan Township Fire Dept. entered the structure to check the cooler unit for extension and secure power by way of the breaker panel to the unit. Damage was contained to the front upper left corner of the cooler.
 

Origin and Cause 

                The origin and cause investigation into the incident at 147 Route 31 was conducted by Fire Marshal [REDACTED] from the Raritan Township Dept. of Fire Safety.  Scene photographs and witness statements were also taken.
	The fire was located in a freezer/cooler unit, in the front upper left corner. An electrical component was located in the immediate area of origin and was heavily damaged.  This part was latter identified as part of the door heater. The fire was initially noticed by an employee, [REDACTED], who notified 911 and utilized an nearby fire extinguisher to successfully control the fire. 

                The cooler unit is a Schott Gemtron Cooler, Model #: 859GE410LT, BOM #: 54HP42969LTG3BK, Work #: M567900/CO15966 with a date of 04/04/2009. 

Conclusion 
	The fire at 147 Route 31 was out on arrival of the fire department, with no extension beyond the door heater and no smoke damage to the structure of food. The location of the fire was the cooler, with the cause being the door heater. Research of the assembly showed no active recalls. It appears that wear and tear on the door along with high humidity and moisture on the door were contributing factors in its malfunction.
justification: The incident involved a fire in a cooler unit, which was quickly controlled by an employee with no injuries or deaths reported.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore Model 790 electric wall oven was on at 375 degrees to bake a chicken pot pie.
After half an hour of heating I began to open the lower oven door to check the status. 
As I did so - the door handle became unattached on the left side. 
The handle remained attached on the right side - and swung down hanging perpendicular.
What to do?

I proceeded to open the oven door a few inches to see if the inner corner screw was loose or missing.
As i did so there was a loud explosion. The glass front of the lower oven door shattered. 
The safety glass went all over the kitchen floor as far as 12 feet.
Some bits of glass also landed on a counter top 5 or 6 feet away.
If anyone had been looking thru the looking glass when this blast occurred it is likely their eyes 
and their face would be at risk.
 
It was fortunate I was standing to the side of the oven as i tried to open the door.
None of the glass hit me.
The inner glass of the oven did not break - only the outer decorative glass.
Afterwards I confirmed that the screw holding the door handle was very loose.
It appears that when a screw becomes loose the decorative glass front can drop or move.
It is foreseeable that this design flaw creates an unreasonable risk.

We purchased this Kenmore double oven in 2007. It worked as intended for 10 years.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of glass but no injuries occurred, and the issue appears to be a rare design flaw.

This Thanksgiving when carving a turkey I notice a curved crack spontaneously appeared on the handle as I was using it. On New Year's Day I was carving a roast, and the crack increased and a triangular piece of plastic fell off the handle from the vibration of the knife, exposing the motor. 
I knew this knife had never been dropped, so I looked at reviews of this knife on Amazon.com, and couldn't believe that dozens of other people had exactly the same problem, sometimes the first month of use, sometimes after a year or a few. The posted pictures are exactly the same as the crack and triangular piece that came off.
I contacted Cuisinart  which is now apparently Conair, and they emailed back "sorry, it's out of warranty." I emailed that they knew of this potential safety/engineering problem and have ignored it for years. They even ask people to send them $10. to ship the defective item if it is under warranty back to them to get a replacement. Then the replacements apparently have the same problem.
I don't know if anyone has been injured, but I don't want to take a chance by holding a live, vibrating handle with the piece missing over the motor. 
This item needs to be recalled once and for all. Cuisinart used to be a responsive company, but since Conair took over, they ignore engineering and defective unit issues that can cause harm.
justification: The incident describes a defective product with potential safety risks, but no actual injury is reported. The issue is likely to occur based on multiple user reports.

The Pyrex Easy Grab 2 Qt. Casserole baking dish has been  used multiple times in a gas oven at 350ÃÂ°F making the same cake (ÃÂat least 5 times with the same cake recipe), since the date of purchase.  It has never been dropped or miss used.
     My wife was baking a cake in the Pyrex Easy Grab 2 Qt. Casserole baking dish.  It is quite a useful baking dish, as we are teaching our children how to bake and seeing is a great teaching tool. The cake had been in the oven at 350ÃÂ°F for about 25 minutes in the Pyrex Easy Grab 2 Qt Casserole baking dish.  She opened the oven door no more than an inch, when she heard what sounded to her as an explosion.  She immediately closed the oven and called for me.  
     I am a US NAVY SEAL Chief, in my assessment of what I found in the oven, it was indicative of a catastrophic and explosive shattering of the Pyrex Easy Grab 2 Qt. Casserole baking dish. Casserole baking dish had happened after my wife or children had open the oven, they would have had serious lacerations to the face, torso and hands.  Safety of my Family and consumers is what has prompted this report.
justification: The baking dish shattered explosively but no injuries occurred, though potential for serious harm was noted if the oven had been fully opened.

incident_description: I was cooking stuffed peppers in the Power Pressure Cooker XL. The level of liquid was well below the recommended max level. After it finished cooking, I released the steam vent. When I did, hot sauce was spewing all over my kitchen counter, cabinets and floor. Luckily I had a few kitchen towels close by to put on top of the valve to contain the spraying hot liquid and avoided a serious burn. However the clean up was awful and I have not used the unit since.
justification: The incident involved hot liquid spewing but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is high given the description of the event.

incident_description: I own a Bosch dishwasher, model numberSHP65T56UC/01, FD941200651. On Friday 3/2/18 the dishwasher stopped working completely as it was receiving no power. On Sunday 3/4 we pulled it out to find that the junction box and connecting wires were black and charred. They had clearly burnt up. We were very fortunate that this didn't ignite an actual fire in the house. Upon researching online I came across the recall notice for Bosch (https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2018/BSH-Home-Appliances-Expands-Recall-of-Dishwasher) but my serial number range (9412) is slightly outside the stated recall range (which only extends to 9403. This recall clearly needs to be expand to later models.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned with charred wires, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
This caller purchased his range in 2007 from retailer  in Murfreesboro, TN in 2007.
He had no problems with the unit until around January 2017 when he noticed that the right rear element was coming on by itself.  He contacted the manufacturer who repaired the unit.
January 24, 2018 he noticed that the indicator light for right front element is remaining on as if the element is on but the element is not getting hot or becoming red.
He is reporting this incident as a hazard because the indicator light and element send messages electrically and since this light is on he understands that the wiring could become hot or the element could turn itself on and catch fire and/or burn persons using the range.
There are no injuries being reported at this time
He has not contacted the manufacturer at this time but he does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involves a potential hazard with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the history of similar issues but no immediate danger.

incident_description: I was making a cup of coffee using my Keurig B31 coffee maker. While I was waiting for it to brew it just kinda exploded and sprayed hot coffee grounds and hot water all over me, the wall and the floor. I got burned in the spots it hit me but wasn't seriously injured. After that incident it stopped working. It doesn't brew a cup of coffee and the power does not even come on.  I didn't know if it has a fuse that needs to be changed.  I didn't know that it could cause a safety concern until it presented itself with one.
justification: The incident resulted in burns from hot coffee grounds and water, indicating an injury (severity 3), but such explosions are unlikely based on the description (likelihood 2).

incident_description: We moved in about 4 1/2 years ago and the dishwasher was new. In the last 3-4 months we have noticed a very strong burning smell, like burning plastic, every time the dishwasher is running on the heated dry cycle. We have checked multiple times over the past few months to verify no plastic items are on or around the heating element. We are not sure if there is a possibility of fire at some point due whatever is causing the burning smell. At times the smell is such that it can irritate our throat and cause a headache if we donÃÂt open windows in the kitchen to ventilate the area more than normal.
justification: The burning smell and irritation indicate a potential health hazard and fire risk, but no actual injury or fire has occurred yet.

incident_description:
We have owned the Pamper Chef bamboo top salt shaker/grinder (item model number 2198) for several years. Recently we noticed a coiled piece metal in our food, but didn't know where the metal came from. The second time we found metal was immediately after using the grinder.  The spring located just above the grinder turned out to have deteriorated and was falling internally into the grinder, which was the source of the metal. Luckily we caught the metal on both instances and stopped using our grinder, but this faulty design is extremely dangerous and could cause great harm if the rusty spring metal were swallowed. 

Of special note, the bamboo grinders have been discontinued and a more modern version has replaced them, but with the same design flaw where the spring is in direct contact with the rock salt just above the grinder. The company even sells replacement springs as a kit without any consumer safety information or warnings that the springs may fail.  

We did contact Pampered Chef about the defective and dangerous design. They forwarded the issue onto the Field Services Risk Management department. They also replaced the grinders with identical product that still contains the spring in contact with the salt.
justification: Metal pieces were found in food due to a deteriorating spring, but no injury occurred. The issue is likely to recur given the design flaw and lack of warnings.

incident_description:
My husband and I were making bread in the KitchenAid Tilt Head Artisan Mixer with Glass Bowl on March 31, 2018.  The mixer was purchased on January 27, 2018, and had been used about a dozen times to make bread, cakes, etc.  With no warning, and while the machine was mixing the bread dough with the dough hook mechanism rotating, the glass bowl became unscrewed from the plastic ring that attaches to the bottom of the glass bowl; the ring with the bowl is then fitted and turned onto the base of the mixer to hold it in place.  
After the glass bowl became unscrewed while the mixer was mixing the dough, the bowl tilted to the left and was banged into the upright portion of the mixer several times, breaking it into two jagged pieces.  
I could not safely reach the switch on the left to turn it off because the jagged pieces of the glass bowl were moving near the switch.  So I reached to the right to unplug the mixer, as I did so the two jagged broken halves of the bowl flew apart, one flew onto the kitchen counter; the other half flew at me as I was unplugging the machine.  Luckily it did not hit me but landed on the floor and shattered into hundreds of glass shards which flew all over the kitchen. This all took less than 5 seconds. 
I have photos of the disastrous results of this failure, and I would like to stress this is how the mixer is designed for normal use. The plastic ring is not adequate to hold onto the glass bowl while the mixer is rotating contents.  I found many reviews online by other consumers who had similar problems with the plastic ring coming off during use of the mixer.  Extremely dangerous design.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous failure of the mixer, with broken glass flying but luckily not hitting anyone, indicating a potential for injury.

incident_description: refrigerator stopped working, but the two lightbults at top of refrigerator remained on and melted, destroyed the entire upper part of the refrigerator interior
justification: The refrigerator malfunction caused damage to the interior but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have a 2 cup Pyrex glass bowl containing a potato stored in a refrigerator.  I removed the bowl and place within the microwave for 1 minute and 15 seconds.  After heating up my food, I removed the bowl and walked to over to my desk.  I removed the lid and begin eating my potato.  Yes, plain and tasteless.  After about 10 seconds the bowl shattered all over my desk with a nice loud pop noise.  My coworker heard the noise and walked over to inquire about the noise.  I was surprised and lucky that none of the flying glass entered my eye, as I was sitting a foot away from the soon to be fragmentation bomb.  I laugh called my coworker over to laugh as well and carefully cleaned up the mess.
justification: The incident involved a shattered bowl but no injury, and such occurrences are unlikely as proper handling can prevent them.

incident_description:
Beverage / wine cooler stopped cooling after approx. 6-months of use.  I contacted the company (EdgeStar) inquiring about warranty service on the unit.  EdgeStar requested that I, as the consumer, inspect a compressor relay area (if I was comfortable - I was).  They requested that I access the compressor relay area and remove the cover, remove the relay and shake it to " see if it rattled ".  Upon removal of the cover I notice that the wiring to the relay was burnt / melted ( I did NOT remove the relay ).  Per EdgeStar's request I submitted photographs of the damage.

Subsequently, EdgeStar requested that the unit be returned to them and that a replacement unit would be shipped.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with no reported injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
Electrolux EW 23BC85KS3       S/N  4A 22617656

Refrigerator forms ice on outside back of refrigerator. Ice makers stops working. Mother board replaced. Foods in freezer not staying frozen. Uneven temp temperature in freezer. Racks in refrigerator rusting from humidity levels. Food freezing and thawing and refreezing. Ice that forms on back outside refrigerator rusting metal and causing drywall to get wet causing mold.

Called Electrolux have spoke to a [REDACTED] and emailed [REDACTED]. I was told that they would repair unit with a pad on back of refrigerator or that they would give me a 50% off a new refrigerator. I feel that a bandaid pad is not fixing the problem with a poor design flaw. The 50% off another refrigerator to replace the $3200 refrigerator I already bought would cost me $5000.00 in total plus the repairs I have already spent. I also feel that I am not the only consumer to have made this complaint to Electrolux. Electrolux knows this was a bad, poor, flawed refrigerator. This is a health hazard inside and out.  

 I ask for a replacement of like kind to settle the problem.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning refrigerator causing food spoilage and potential mold, but no direct injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
My Delonghi toaster model CTH2003B Serial # 90317 S900042 caught fire a few weeks ago. The unit was in perfect order and cleaned (no crumbs or pieces of bread at bottom). Fire was coming out of all sides. 

I called firm and at first they seemed to not care (offered me a 20% discount on another unit). Then, when I made an issue of it noting they should want to find out why it caught fire, they sent me a FedEx return label to ship the item back to them (which I will do shortly) saying "Once your unit has been inspected, we will contact you with a resolution."
justification: The toaster caught fire but no injury or death was reported, and the manufacturer's response suggests such incidents are not common.

incident_description: On December 20, 2017, I was using a 4-1/2 inch Parer knife made from Calphalon to cut pears. The knife broke at the handle and just missed cutting my fingers. This was part of a set that was given to me as a gift about one year ago. I had contacted Calphalon back in March to possibly replace this set of knives based on recalls that the company stated had this exact problem. I sent the knives back, only to have them returned to me with a message saying they were not affected by the recall. When I once again contacted the company on December 20, after this incident happened, I sent them photos of what the knife looked like after it broke and explained that if one of their knives can break like this when slicing something as soft as pears, it should be on the recall list. I never heard back from them. I tried two more times to contact them to try to rectify the situation, in hopes of getting the knife replaced and for the company to investigate whether this knife is a safety concern. Again, I never heard back from them. In my last email to them (December 29, 2017) I explained that I would be contacting you. It also should be noted that Calphalon has stated on their web site that no matter how their knives are used, they should not break at the handle. The model number on this knife is 0862516. I can send you the pictures I sent Calphalon if you would like them. It is my hope that this product can be investigated as a potential safety hazard.
justification: The knife broke but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is rated as possible given the recurrence of similar issues.

incident_description:
LG cooktop burner won't turn off. Burner turns on by itself and goes to highest temperature.
Burner will then shut off and then comes back on to highest temperature.
Burner had to be disconnected to prevent issue from recurring. 

LG has recalled many of these same type ranges.
It appears LG did NOT sufficiently extend the effectivity list for all models with this issue.
My model range has an SB suffix which "excludes" it from the recall though it has the exact 
issue of the recalled models.

My LG cooktop model is: LRE30755SB.
SN: 602KMBV00245.
justification: The cooktop malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death was reported, and the issue is known to occur in similar models.

incident_description: My Ikea drinking glass just spontaneously exploded in my kitchen cabinet. It shattered so hard it left shards embedded in the other shelves. The glasses were a set of 4, and they are made in Bulgaria with the batch number 21412
justification: The glass exploded causing damage but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Hamilton Beach Electric Kettle overheats.  One serious occurrence.  The kettle is intended to bring water to a boil and turn off.  I left room and discovered kettle still 'boiling.'  The water was not over capacity or empty.  I immediately took pot off of power base and realized the intense heat of the pot handle.  

Model 40998, 40998c K46 120v~ 60Hz 1500 W

The consumer is not sure if her husband swallowed any of the glass. Her husband stated that he felt pressure in his throat.
