incident_description:
I was using my Kitchen Aid Stand mixer to make naan. The dough was just coming together and the speed was either 2 or 3. I moved away and the next thing I knew the top/head/motor of the KA was at my feet, the dough hook still rotating. The bowl was still attached to the base. When I investigated I realized that the motor had completely ripped off of the base. (The silver pin still in tack, the hinge still attached to the base but broken off at the top of the hinge and a hole in the bottom of the motor where it had been attached to the base.)

I have contact Kitchen Aid and they are sending me a replacement and I am supposed to the send the broken one back to them,

I thought I should contact you so that you can be aware that this product failure happened. If I had been two feet closer I could have been seriously hurt. The motor weighs a ton.  

Model No: KSM150PSWH  Serial No: W10793218  Purchased by State Farm as a replacement from the one I lost in a house fire in February 2011.

I have photos.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as it appears to be an isolated case.

incident_description: On 12/09/2017, I had finished cooking stuffed bell peppers in my Rival Crock Pot model 3060.  Approximately an hour later I washed the glass lid, dried it and placed it on the kitchen counter because the ceramic was still soaking in the dishwater. 30 minutes later I heard a loud pop coming from the kitchen. I discovered a completely shattered crock pot lid.
justification: The incident involved a shattered crock pot lid with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. Such occurrences are uncommon but not unheard of, warranting a likelihood of 2.

No one was injured.

justification: The bowl exploded, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:

incident_description:

The consumer tried to turn the oven off but got a F1 error message. She hit the power button but still could not get the unit to go off. The top coils of the oven were red but the bottom coils were off.

The consumer pulled the unit from the wall. The consumer had to disconnect the range at the breaker to get it to go off. The consumer stated that it took about three hours for the range to cool down.

(01/23/2018) The same thing happened again the next day when the consumer plugged the unit back in.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that the range had not been recalled. She was referred to CPSC to file a report.

incident_description: I have owned a Kenmore Toaster Oven/Broiler Model 238-48449 for about 10 years. It has performed as expected, with light usage ÃÂ average of less than once a week. Last evening I noticed an unusual smell coming from the kitchen, and found that the oven was running at full power. The entire outside of the unit was scorching hot ÃÂ so much that a nearby plastic container was melting. The knobs to control the toaster were all on off at the time. I disconnected the cord from the wall socket. Nothing else in the kitchen was affected. My concern is that if this had happened when no one was in the house, it might have caused a fire. Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with potential fire risk, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: While placing our Kitchen Aid Wall oven in self cleaning mode, the interior layer of glass shattered.
justification: The incident involved the oven's glass shattering, which is an equipment failure but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: Purchased a new Kitchen aid refrigerator on 9/22/17 and it was delivered and put into service on 10/20/17.  The model number is KRSC503ESS01 mfg 10/17.  The week before Thanksgiving in November of 2017 my family got deathly ill and we assumed it was the flu as the flu has been going around.  Got better went on vacation and felt fine.  Came home and continued to have just a day or so a week where one of us would have gastro symptoms.  Then week before Christmas another major bout that we thought was flu again.  January comes and still not recovered completely from this illness and found out one evening that the leftovers that were put in fridge at noon were hotter at 6pm than had they been left out all day.  At same time opened veggie drawer and lettuce was frozen solid.  Upon cleaning out that drawer which had never been completely empty since installation, it was discovered that the back wall had an ice sheet the entire width of the fridge and as deep as veggie drawer.  This is the wall where the vent is for the air to come from freezer to fridge.  Purchased thermometer and it was 50 degrees F in fridge.  Called for service on a two month old fridge and repair man said "unlucky fridge".  Have comprised immune system and unable to eat out for past 17 years.  Tried to get them and the retailer to swap out a defective machine and was told NO.  The safety dept. at Kitchen aid for lack of better terms could care less.  Fridge requires two parts one of which is backordered but they were able to locate.  I am beyond belief that with something so major on something two months old they will not replace.  Something needs to be done as this continual food poisoning as it was getting warmer over the time period could have caused death to me or a family member.  Never have I considered in my 60 years of calling an ambulance but was very close to that on two occasions.
justification: The incident caused repeated gastro symptoms and potential food poisoning, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the recurring nature of the issue and the compromised immune system of the affected individuals.

incident_description:
I purchased the Picardie Glass Tumbler, 16 oz., Set of 6 from Williams Sonoma in September 2017. I wanted a glass set that could be used cold or hot, and read the description carefully to make sure before the purchase. The description of this product states that "Use to serve both hot and cold beverages."

However, one glass explode while I was making my tea, and the other explode while my husband was hand washing it with just hot tap water. I tried to reach out to William and Sonoma about the incident, they were very inefficient in replying to me that I just gave up. I then wrote a review warning customers about this glass set, yet William Sonoma did not publish my review saying it didn't meet their website guidelines. Last time I checked, this product still has a 100% approval rating on their website. 

I think this product poses a safety hazard and customers should be warned about it.
justification: The incident involved glass explosions during normal use, posing a safety hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer reported that the range was not in use when he heard a loud noise and discovered that there was smoke emitting from the oven, he opened the oven door and more smoke dispersed from the unit .  He  stated that the unit was burning because of the wiring.  He unplugged the unit to prevent a house fire.  

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised him to contact the recall department, the recall department advised him that there was no recall and that he should notify the agency of this incident.

Consumer feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description: The blade on my Cuisinart model  DFP-14BCNY 14-Cup  #60706cs  comes detached from the stem when slicing. The blade comes to the top of the lid and has gouged out the top from hitting the lid. If I wasn't quick to stop the machine the bade could crack the top.  I have been in communication with Cuisinart several times. The machine has been sent back twice and the problem is still not fixed. Cuisinart has issued a call tag for the third time I will be sending the machine back to them. I have asked for a refund. I do believe that there is no current fix for this machine. It appears to be an issue with the stem and blade not keeping contact.  I have owned another Cuisinart food processor that was 35 years old with no difficulty. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a blade detaching and damaging the machine, but no injury is reported, fitting severity level 2. The issue is recurring, making it likely (4) to happen again.

incident_description: Upon opening the door to my Samsung model RF268abwp  refrigerator, i noticed the top shelf was shatered but still together.  I removed it and put it on the counter.  I tried to figure out how it happened but have no idea.  I left it on the counter for a few days then when i tried to moved it it broke into a million pieces.  I cut myself trying to pick up some of the pieces to throw away.  I had to use a dust pan on my counter to "sweep" up all the peices however they were very every small and sharp. I thought the glass shelf was made of tempered glass but apparently it isnt or it is defective.   I called Samsung to see it they have had other complaints and also to see if they would replace the shelf (out of warrentee) and they said they havent had any complaints but when i look online at third party comments i see many people complaining.  I told them that but they said that they dont use those comments.  I asked how to make a report and they said they have it but there is no specific department i could talk to to be sure it is documented.  They are not going to replace the shelf. this shelf could have fallen appart as i took it out of the refrigerator which would have been tiny shattered pieces all over the refrigerator.  I did get cut and was very concerned if i got all the pieces as it was all over the counter.

incident_description: I received the Hamilton Beach Set n' Forget Programmable 6 Qt Slow Cooker for Christmas and used it for the 1st time yesterday. I went to stir the contents and noticed that the crock doesn't fit well and moves around inside the base. I grabbed the handle to hold it in place and as I stirred and came in contact with something that burned one of my fingers. It was aluminum lip at the top of the base. On my other slow cookers the crock extends over this so it isn't exposed. This one doesn't. I've never had to handle a crock pot with an oven mit while cooking something and will definitely not ever serve anything directly from the crock pot. It poses a risk to anyone unknowingly coming in contact with that part of the base and is not safe product. If I am able to return it I will.
justification: The user suffered a burn injury from contact with an exposed hot part of the slow cooker, indicating a clear safety issue with the product design.

incident_description: When using the mandolin for the second time, to dice a yellow onion, the knife blades began to detach from the portion that holds them to the mandolin.  One blade completely separated and became mixed with the diced onion pieces.  A second blade clearly became loose.  The thought of a small sharp knife blade mixed with food was enough safety concern to have me bring this to your attention.
justification: The incident involved a safety concern with a detached blade in food, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he used the self clean feature for the first time and it melted the plastic door frame of the oven. The knobs on the front of the stove were also melted. The oven is no longer operable since the plastic door frame is melted it will no longer keep heat inside the oven. The caller is still able to use the stove top.  

Caller stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they sent him to CPSC because the oven is 1 month out of warranty.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted oven parts) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description:
The hazard I wish to report concerns the Bodum glass coffee press. The main hazard is that the press, during regular use, is subject to extreme thermal stress when boiling water is poured into it, and in some cases is over stressed and fails.

Also, the glass craft is not secured into the cage, and can fall out while pouring. In both cases, the glass will shatter, leaving small glass slivers and pieces on the counter top, where food is prepared.

The first email attached is Bodums' response to my initial complaint, as well as my initial complaint. The second email
starts off with a more detailed description of the problem including the basis of a stress analysis indicating the over stressed condition.

Also included is a photo of a typical failure, this one due to thermal stress alone.  Please note that these products are similar to the product that Bodum previously recalled, the [REDACTED] coffee press, and has a similar defect. Also note that Bodum states that the product is subject to microscopic defects, not visible to the human eye, which could cause failure during normal use. Also note that Bodum does not include any warnings about these dangers on their products.

The first failure occurred when I poured boiling water into the craft. Boiling water, glass splinters, small glass cups, and
grinds were spread over the counter top, cabinets, and floor. The entire area had to be wiped with cloths which had to be thrown out due to the glass. Then the area had to be dried, vacuumed, and the wiped again. The glass chips were so
small, there is little assurance they were all removed.

Your assistance assistance is greatly appreciated.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves glass shattering during normal use, posing a risk of injury from glass slivers, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I use a Bosch Tassimo T47 coffee maker.  The issue is with the  milk creamer pods that come in the Tassimno Gevalia Cappucino Decaf beverage.  They do not function properly.  They get jammed in the machine and when the machine is forced open spray hot liquid on the user.  I contacted Tassimo and they offered no solution.  Their website is filled with similar comments.

incident_description: My Mr. Coffee Keurig single cup brewer machine is melting the plastic inside the water reservoir and that polluted melted plastic is going into the water that goes into the coffee cup. This also means that most likely the hot water is coming back up into the brewer and could cause a burn or explosion. This is very unsafe and needs to be taken care of because most people don't look down into the bottom of the water reservoir. I only looked because I was trying to clean mine and pods kept bursting.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard with the coffee machine, including melted plastic contamination and risk of burns or explosion, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: A brand new, empty, Anchor Hocking glass measuring cup (2 cup size)  shattered 20 minutes after being set on a granite counter top. The glass measuring cup was in a car for 30 minutes that was being driven ( 2 degree outside temperature) and then the cup brought inside and set on a granite counter top. Room temperature was 62 degrees. The shards of glass were scattered an all directions at least 4 feet from the cup.
justification: The glass shattered but there was no injury, only property damage.

incident_description: Our LG Electric Range Model LRE30453ST has a malfunctioning burner that will not turn off.
justification: A malfunctioning burner that won't turn off is an incident that could lead to overheating or fire, but no injury is mentioned.

Sunbeam products co.

incident_description: The toaster oven has a timer knob that has settings for 0, which is off, 1-60 which is on and stay on. incident_description:
I was filling the pitcher of my iced tea maker with ice from my refrigerator door and noticed ice falling to the floor.  When I looked at the bottom of the pitcher, I noticed that an ice cube had broken through the glass, and glass shards were all over the floor.  I put the broken container in the sink and quickly cleaned up the glass before anyone was able to walk into the kitchen.  No injuries were sustained.

I am writing because my husband and I are concerned about the glass pitcher on this item.  This pitcher was not used outside of the manufacturer warnings and should not have broken with normal use.  Upon the first use, my husband and I were both surprised that the glass used on the pitcher was so thin - especially on the bottom.  However we (wrongly) assumed that because this iced tea maker was more costly than others on the web site, the glass must be stronger or of better quality.

We do not feel that an ice cube falling from a dispenser should have enough impact to crack or break through glass.  While no injuries were sustained with this incident, an injury could have easily occurred.  Since I did not hear the glass break, I could have easily stepped on broken glass.  I also could have easily cut myself on the bottom of the pitcher or while cleaning up the shards from the floor.  In addition, if a consumer happened to crack the glass with an ice cube, then continue to make tea (which adds hot water to the pitcher while it brews), the pitcher could easily shatter.  I do not believe the pitcher is tempered, which is a larger concern if children or pets are around when the pitcher breaks.
justification: The incident involved glass breakage but no injuries occurred, though potential for harm was noted.

incident_description:
The frypan has a metal shroud attached to the bottom of the pan which surrounds the thermostatic controller when plugged in. The shroud is easily contacted when adjusting the temperature control dial. (Less than a finger width of clearance.) With the unit set at275 degrees F, we have contacted the shroud, while attempting to adjust the temperature setting. We have experienced burned fingers in the process. An infra-red temperature reading of the shroud indicated 360 degrees F with the control set at 275 degrees F. Further investigation revealed the pan itself varied from 205 degrees F to 347 degrees F when set to 275 degrees F. 

The shroud situation is dangerous and could be compounded if the user were a child, invalid or elder. 

The lack of temperature control could easily cause any number of unsafe scenarios. Especially at higher settings where grease fires or catastrophic explosive steam events could manifest.

It should be noted that we have only suffered burns from the shroud and are only pointing out that a poorly functioning thermostatic controller might represent even more serious injury potential.
justification: The description reports burns from contacting the hot shroud, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to the easily contacted shroud and poor temperature control.

It has happened a few times since purchase approximately 2 years ago.  We have recently had a lower temperature than normal suspected so we installed an analog thermometer in the oven.  We monitored a consistent low temperature than the control readout said, usually about 30 to 50 degrees colder.  After about 30 minutes it would be at the proper set temperature, this happened quite often during the holiday baking time frame.  Several times it spiked to over 550 when set at 325.  The last time this happened I noticed the upper broiling element was on high.  I shut it off several times and each time the element came back on and the oven controller showed it was operating at 350 degrees.  We shut it off and let it cool for 1 day.  I turned it on the next day, set the temp to 375, readout said it was 375, analog thermometer said 330.  It slowly climbed to 350 in 20 minutes then the temperature rose to 375 and then to 400 in a few minutes.  The top element didn't turn on this time.  I shut it off and wrote to Samsung and then to this website.
justification: The oven's temperature spikes and erratic behavior pose a risk of fire or burns, but no injury or death has been reported. The issue has occurred multiple times, indicating it is likely to happen again.

incident_description:
Dear CPSC Representative,

Calif. Dept. of corrections and rehabilitation (CDCR) changed the hotpot we are allowed to purchase to the one above.

All of us noticed that these hotpots developed small white round deposits all over the metal base inside the pot.  They're 1/16" to about 1/4" diameter. incident_description:
This evening the oven was turned on to cook dinner, 400 degrees F. 
17 minutes into the bake cycle we noticed smoke filling the house, pressed [Timer] to stop the running timer, and then the [Clear off] button to stop the baking. The digital display still read 400, so it looked normal, and returned to displaying a clock. Dinner came out blackened, and the coated paper bowl cracked at a touch as it had become brittle due to overheating.
As we discussed how this happened, and re-read the directions on the package, I noticed the oven coils continued to glow yellow-orange-hot. I rushed over to the oven, pressed [Clear] again, and then [Bake] but it acted frozen and would not respond to the key presses.
I then rushed to the power panel to turn off the circuit breaker.
I grabbed my thermal camera, and took pictures of the oven, because it was clearly in a runaway condition, and overheating out of control. I read temperatures around 660 deg.F, which I got a picture saved of, and some parts showed O.L., Over Limit, exceeding the camera's upper limit of 716 deg. F.

This clearly did not meet the definition of "FAIL SAFE" and it appears we averted a house fire.
justification: The incident involved an oven overheating and nearly causing a fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

Having a horrible smell, I immediately opened the window and turned on the exhaust fan.  I hit the "stop" button, but the F10 continued to flash.  My husband turned the breaker off and I looked up the F10 code in the owner's manual and it is a "runaway temperature". incident_description:
I own a lake cottage in Meredith, NH and have a HotPoint White Free Standing Electric Smoothtop Range/Oven. It was purchased in August of 2002, but as this is a second home it is rarely used and in excellent condition.

On Friday, 10/06/17, I turned on the range to cook something and there was no heat. I tested each burner and the oven. No heat. I knew it was getting power because the lights and clock were on. I did a google search and read that people experiencing a similar problem had experienced resolution by flipping the breaker switch on and off, so I tried this but it did not change anything.  I read further and learned that while the lights and clock only require 120V the stove top & oven heat require 240V - so I decided to wait until the next morning and call an electrician.

On Saturday, 10/07/17, I had an electrician come to see if perhaps the outlet was not supplying the required 240V - but he found that was not the problem.  I asked if he knew anything at all about repairing appliances and he said he could take a quick look to see if it was anything obvious.  Upon removing the panel he immediately showed me what the problem was and I was shocked to hear him explain to me that I was very fortunate I had not experienced a fire. I have a photo of what he found that I am hoping I will be able to attach to this report somewhere. The appliance is now unplugged - I called HotPoint to report what the electrician had found and was given the number (800) 386-1215 and told to call Monday morning to report this.

Further internet searches have uncovered similar problems people had with HotPoint RB757 model ranges, but I couldn't find anything with my model number RB787.  I don't know if it is because of it's age? But it sounds to be the same problem people were having with RB757 being a fire hazard.

My appliance  is RB787WCWW, the serial number is either DD241432R or DD241932R, one of the number is hard to read and could be a 4 or 9. I have a copy of the receipt dated 8/13/02. It was delivered and installed on 8/17/02.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance that posed a fire hazard but did not result in any injury or death.

incident_description:

A Whirlpool/KitchenAid certified technician came to our house.  He spoke directly with Whirlpool and was told that it was "simply cosmetic" and the company could send out a touchup paint to fix the problem.

incident_description:
On February 7th, 2018 at approximately 3:30 PM PST, I was operating an Espresso/Coffee Machine (DeLonghi BCO330T, Serial Number 72825).

I firstly began using the machine by adding water in the top reservoir of the unit, waiting about three minutes for the water to heat up, then I added almond milk to a frothing cup and heated up the milk with the unit's steam wand. 

Shortly after, I grabbed the espresso portafilter and added coffee using the measuring spoon included with the unit, enough to fill it at half capacity or for two shots of espresso coffee.

I began by priming the brew head to clean it. I then inserted the portafilter into the brew head, ensuring that the filter basket was properly inserted into the portafilter and that it it was flush, as I normally do when I operate the machine. I twisted the handle counter clockwise into the machine and ensured the handle was pointing to the arrow on the machine, so it lined up properly. 

I began the espresso brewing process by turning the switch on the side of the machine upwards and espresso began to brew and fall into a glass cup that was provided in the box for use with brewing espresso. 

As it was brewing, the unit had already poured enough coffee for one shot of espresso, and being accustomed to the machine, I knew it would take about a minute or two to finish brewing the full two shots of espresso, so I walked less than five feet away from the machine to another side of the kitchen and nearly two seconds after I walked away I could hear pressure build up in the machine, then suddenly heard a boom similar to a grenade exploding.

I stood there realizing and shaking by what seemed to be an explosion. I understood that I was lucky to have walked away for a moment as I could have been killed or seriously injured by the explosion's debris (the portafilter that flew from the blast of pressure, the hundreds of pieces of glass from the glass cup as well as the burning hot espresso grounds and coffee) which flew all over the room, the dining room, and the living room. 

I began by trying to clean up the mess and cut my finger with the broken shards of glass, so I consulted a cleaning lady and had her come clean up the debris which flew all over the room and previously prepared food and other kitchen items. 

I am writing this so appropriate measures can be taken to prevent this from happening to anyone else. I was left with a scene that looked like it came out of a Hollywood movie. Moments after the incident happened I contacted DeLonghi's customer service and spoke with a woman named [REDACTED] from Coffee Machine support and not only was my story not believed, but [REDACTED] asked me twice to plug in the machine again and attempt to brew a new batch of espresso, while she was on a video conference call with me although my repeated attempts to tell her that I was not comfortable with going through the experience again as I was almost seriously injured.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut finger) and had the potential for severe injury or death due to the explosion-like event.

Glass pebbles poured out of the closed oven door. The heat went off and the oven went through its normal cool down cycle and unlocked the door.

incident_description: My Whirlpool range model #FC310S0 SERIAL NUMBER R20914201began acting weird about 2 years after I moved into my new (never lived-in)  home in 2013--range was already installed.  One of the front burners began heating up bright red when it control was on low and no heat when it was on high. Wiring was burned and corroded. One homeowner had her stove top ignite. This is obviously a malfunction in the stove/range.

justification: The client sustained severe burns requiring emergency hospitalization, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I bought a Presto Dehydrator on August 17,2017. It was on my kitchen counter working on beef when it made a noise and then fire started to come out of the sides of the unit. This is the unit

mounted above it. The problem we are having is the gas range burners being turned
on when my wife puts something in the microwave. She is 5'2" and in order to reach the item in the microwave, she brushes up against the range burner knobs and they turn on. Sometimes just the igniter, and other times the gas lights. I am 6'0", so I don't have this problem. Did GE test their range below their microwave using only tall people?
There are no lock detentes on the knobs, so it is also very easy for our grandsons to turn on the burners. This is definitely a safety hazard. 
I know our concern is not unique, as I see it is the number one complaint listed on the GE oven/range.

incident_description: The knobs on our new [REDACTED] Electric stove are large and bulky, protruding out from the front of the stove.  They operate by pushing them in and turning them.   Unfortunately they are easy to push in by leaning on them, and turn very easily.   As a consequence we have turned on burners many (dozens) times just by working at or around the stove.   Once while unloading groceries, a bag which was placed adjacent to the stove burst in flame, I  threw it in the sink to put it out.  To make matters worse, the high heat burners are at the front of the stove so if you are working on the back burners you can accidentally turn them on...and they're intense!   Seems like this is an old school flaw Samsung should know about, or that they should have detected in a product safety review.   They were remiss.   The knob should pull out, if anything, I'd rather turn a burner off than burn down my house.   THIS IS A SERIOUS PROBLEM!

incident_description: We purchased our Samsung oven in March of 2017 and installed it around the end of March, 2017. This oven is a serious fire hazard. It is a slide-in range with the burner knobs on the front of the unit. You barely have to push the knobs in to turn the burners on and, as such, a simple brush up against the knobs turns the burners on. Due to this problem we have accidentally melted a cutting board, caught a pizza box on fire and, on two occasions we have unknowingly turned the oven on while grabbing a glass from a shelf above the oven and the burner was left on all night long. We have tried to get the situation rectified by Samsung and have called the customer service hotline and the warranty line. Both people that we spoke to said that this was a KNOWN issue with this particular model of oven and both people said that there was nothing that they could/would do to rectify the situation. We were also told that unless someone has a documented burn from the oven there is nothing they can do and that we need to 'be more vigilant about the knobs.' If this happened every now and then, we would try to be more vigilant but it is a FIRE HAZARD and happens frequently even when trying to be vigilant. In customer service we were told that there was nothing they could do. We asked to be escalated to a manager who told us the same thing. In warranty, they said all they could do was send us out the same knobs resulting in the same issue and there was nothing they could do. When I asked about replacement they said that wasn't an option. We are at the point that we will be out of pocket the money ($1200) we spent on this oven in order to get an oven that is safe for our family if Samsung won't stand behind their product and that is just WRONG. Also, in our online research this is a HUGE and KNOWN issue as several threads, websites and documentation of this issue with this model. Samsung seems to prefer a house fire, burn victim or worse before they are willing to stand behind their product.
justification: The incident describes frequent accidental activation of burners leading to fire hazards, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

This letter is to inform you of a potential safety defect in my GE 30ÃÂ Free-Standing Gas Range, model JGB428SERSS.

On at least six occasions, we have found that one of the burner control knobs had inadvertently been turned on enough to open the valve, perhaps by bumping into the knob, but not enough to ignite the flame.  Yesterday, after we left the condo at 5:00 PM for an evening out, we returned at 10:15 PM to immediately notice the smell of gas upon entering the condo. I understand that the intent of the push-to-turn design on the valve is to prevent accidental opening of the gas valve, or opening by a small child.  It is my assessment that it is just too easy to push the valve in to allow it to turn.

incident_description:
I have a GE gas stove that is less than 2 years old and professionally installed in a new construction home.  We had researched the stove (December 2015) and determined it would be a good purchase. 
 This Thanksgiving, the lower stopped heating for some reason.  My neighbor is a retired GE repairman and determined the ceramic ignitor was defective.

I ordered the correct factory replacement part and installed it.  As I was installing the lower cover for the bottom oven, I noticed the tin heat shield was melted.  There was about a 1 inch tear in the metal above the ignitor.  The ignitor stays on while the gas bar is heating.  It appears the ignitor is super heating the tin heat shield and making the metal molten.  Is has caused the metal to droop and finally tear open.  The tear now makes it easier for the metal to super heat and melt.  I believe the drooping metal is what caused the ignitor to fail and crack.

I feel this is a design flaw on the part of GE.  I have since researched my model of oven and found several other people are having this same issue.  My concern is this is a fire hazard and this model should never have been approved for sale.  I have had several homes over the last 30 years and never had this type of issue.  In fact, those stoves lasted over 10 + years with no issues.
justification: The incident involves a defective stove part causing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Gas Range burners blow out during use, causing gas to leak into the home, creating a health hazard and explosion risk.

On multiple occasions while using my Kenmore Gas Range, the burners blow out on their own. There is also no lock out on the knobs that control the burners, allowing them to be engaged by bumping them, and releasing gas. There have been 7 occasions that the burners have blown out and released gas into my home. The first occasion was in 2012 (6 months after purchase and install by Sears.) The burner blew out while cooking and released gas into my home over a 15 hour period, killing my dog from the fumes. 

The subsequent occasions were all caught within minutes, until 1/21/18. This evening the burner blew out and released gas into my home for 9 hours, and i was able to vent the home after becoming ill from the smell.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a dog and caused illness to the homeowner, indicating severe health hazards and a risk of explosion.

My wife was cooking 2 nights ago, the knob failed, and the burner was active for 20 minutes: the time it took me to get home from work.  I consider this a fire safety hazard.

I am employed by a large aerospace firm and my job is testing structures, often to failure.  I can confidently state this is a design issue.

incident_description:
Dear Sirs, 
I write this letter to bring to your attention what I think are dangerous flaws in the design of gas stoves currently in use.

To operate these stoves (mine in particular, a Maytag model MGR5765 QDW) one turns a dial counter clockwise. When the dial turns about 30 degrees an ignition spark is started and gas begins to flow. The burner lights.

However, if one turns the dial quickly to an through the ignition function no spark is produced, but the gas does flow and does not ignite! A child might do this or someone in a hurry ot distracted. In 10 to 20 seconds enough gas escapes to make a small explosion. But if minutes go by there will be a large explosion. If many minutes go by etc., etc.

And now comes the second dangerous flaw. when one smells gas the normal reaction for most people will be to turn the dial to OFF. But when the dial passes through the ignition position it will produce a spark and the gas WILL EXPLODE.

I have to wonder if you or the manufacturers or anyone is aware of this situation. It would seem to me that if the igniter could be altered so a not to spark when turning the burner off that might be a partial solution.

In any case, gas must not flow until spark is on, stable and proven...
Spark must not occur during shut off.

I hope I have explained this clearly. If not I would be Happy to discuss it further.  

Yours Truly, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The description details a scenario that could lead to a gas explosion, which poses a risk of death, hence severity level 4. The likelihood is possible (3) as it requires specific user actions but is not extremely rare.

Just as I finished and was walking back to the kitchen I heard a loud bang. My glass top had exploded sending large chard's of glass into my kitchen, living room, dining area and hallway. There were also small pieces of glass in the same area. If I had been in the kitchen when this occurred I could have been seriously injured.

He turned the knob of the burner that was coming on and witnessed a big flash coming from the back of the stove. It blew the breaker. incident_description:

This has happened to my husband & I many times.  Thankfully we have smelled the raw gas in time to turn the burner off, or have not been too close to the burner when it lights.   Either scenario is a safety concern.  I have tried calling and writing the company, with no reply. 

I now have wire clips attached to the knobs so they cannot turn on accidentally!  And I check and recheck the knobs constantly.

incident_description:
Approximately 1- 1 1/2 hours after beginning the the self clean cycle on my Frigidaire Gas Range Model # GLGF388DS Serial #VF51020957 I smelled & observed heavy black smoke coming from the top of the oven. I observed either flames or very bright red looking like flames in the oven, observed that the control pad was not lit i.e. time & temperature set panel & it was singed with black soot around the outside of the panel but worse were the flames that were shooting out from the back top of the oven. I quickly poured some water on the flames & then used our fire extinguisher to stop the fire.  The fire department was called but luckily we had successfully put the fire out before the fire department arrived.  The oven door remained locked & when we unscrewed the back panel we saw where the flame was as well as the destroyed wires making the stove inoperable.  We were very lucky that I was right near the stove when
I smelled the smoke, had a fire extinguisher & only had to buy a new stove.  I reported this occurrence to Frigidaire & they claim that they have no record of a similar incident & it was out of warranty & that they would not come to my home to inspect the stove.
I feel that people should know never to leave your home or go to sleep while running the self clean cycle & if possible stay close by your stove in the event of fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was successfully extinguished without injury, but caused significant damage to the stove.

We had on one occasion returned to a house full of natural gas when one of the stove knobs was accidentally bumped.

incident_description:
I have a GE five burner gas stove, GE Monogram Model ZGU385NSM2SS Serial No. TA700797Q.  I was using four burners on it cooking 4 roasts for several hours.  When I went to turn the burners off, the interior of the knobs had melted (to a soft point) and one of the knobs kept spinning and would not turn the gas off.  It was in the evening, and I was all alone, so I really did initially panic. I was thinking that I could not turn the flame and/or gas off.  After a few minutes I realized that I could use another not that had not completely melted to turn off the burner from the knob that melted.  Once the knob cooled, it hardened back but was cracked and not able to use any longer for the stove.  

Several months later, I ordered a new knob for $50 and told GE about the problem but they basically blew me off.  

I do feel like the knobs melting in the inside is a hazard to the users because of the inability to turn the burner off when they melt and crack.  

I decided to report today because I was just cleaning my stove and took off all knobs to re-examine, and I did notice that my replacement knob has two screws now and is made a little different that the other knobs which makes me feel that they are aware of the problem but are ignoring it.  I also noticed that three of the other four knobs have cracks from melting and re-hardening.  

I do feel that the interior of the knobs should be made out of metal or a plastic that can withstand heat from several pots - it is a 5 burner stove, so it does put off when it is used to cooking several pots at one time.  I feel like this defect/inferior product could be a potential hazard to the user.

I just wanted to soften the butter, so I set the timer for 15 seconds and turned it on.  I immediately began to hear crackling noises, and I smelled smoke.  When I turned around, I saw smoke and flames emerging from the right, inside wall of the oven.  Because the unit was plugged into an outlet behind the oven, there was no safe way to unplug the oven.  I reached over from the side and turned off the oven.  Fortunately, it stopped.  A hole was burned in the right (looking at the unit from the front) inside wall of the unit.

incident_description:
I was burned when a Blendtec blender lid flew off while pureeing hot squash. The lid repeatedly flew off and I was very careful to secure it and not overfill. I was using the Twister jar with the rubber lid with vent (not the Twister apparatus). 

I received first and second degree burns on my neck, arms and torso and will have some scarring. It did hit my face as well but I was fortunate in this regard. I'll have scars on my shoulder and possibly chest. Had very bad blistering from the wounds. 

The round lids seem more susceptible to being forced off by centrifugal force than the five side ones, although the design could be improved. I am very concerned that someone could get seriously injured. I was fortunate that my face didn't get hit worse. 

I contacted Blendtec and they sent me two of the same autoform saying they'd get back to me, usually within 24 hours and they completely ignored me.

It really concerns me that they didn't even call me or ask questions about what happened. It was really painful and I am really angry that I paid a lot of money for a product that is not safe. Their lack of response is inexcusable and irresponsible. The jars are dangerous for consumers.

They market them explicitly for processing hot foods. Mine even has a button programmed for this and really, they shouldn't be doing this. Their lids don't secure in a way that doesn't put consumers at risk.

I'm not sure what kind of authority you have, but thank you for reading this.

Regards,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in first and second degree burns with scarring, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the reported design flaw and lack of response from the manufacturer.

incident_description:
This morning I received second-degree burns when the bottom of my coffeepot spontaneously fell out, inundating my feet with scalding coffee. I'm wondering if I have an actionable case.

Details: At 6:15 a.m. I arose and went downstairs to get my first cup of coffee, as is my habit.

The Cuisinart Brew Central 14-cup Programmable Coffeemaker (model CBC-6400PC) had turned on automatically at 5:30 a.m., as usual, so the coffee was hot and ready. 

As I lifted the full glass pot from the coffeemaker and moved it toward my adjacent cup, the bottom of the glass pot broke out, and the hot coffee was released all at once onto my feet. I did not bump the pot against any other surfaces. There was no impact with anything.

I was wearing socks, and the hot liquid remained in contact with my skin until, in panic, I hurried into the bathroom and submerged each foot in the toilet in turn.

Both feet received second-degree burns, which were diagnosed and treated at a PeaceHealth urgent care center around 9:30 this morning. The left foot, of which I've attached a couple of pictures, suffered much greater damage.

Until it heals, which the doctor said would be possibly two weeks, I'll be unable to wear shoes and therefore unable to go outside or partake of my daily hikes or frequent bike rides or rounds of golf.

The pot that broke had no previous apparent imperfections and had been used and washed normally since we bought it from Costco on June 1, 2016.

The break in the glass followed the pot's lower metal band partway and also separated in a clean line along the bottom edge of the pot, as the attached photos show. I'm no engineer, but it seems that the nature of the break indicates a weakness in the glass rather than any accidental impact.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The spontaneous failure of the coffeepot is unlikely (likelihood 2) given the lack of prior issues.

This must be expedited to either fix it, or inform whirlpool it MUST be replaced since it's still under warranty. I refuse to smell that noxious poison again. My nostrils are burning and my head is killing me. This is toxic.

incident_description:
Whirlpool microwave WMC50522as is partly stuck on, creating a fire hazard. When the appliance ends a cycle, the turntable and fan stop, but the microwave heater is still operating. When in this mode, the microwave heater runs whenever the door is closed. 

This happened last Christmas, but we assumed my wife didn't program the cook power correctly. However, since then we have notice that when cooking a less than 100% power, the heating doesn't cycle. So you are always cooking at 100% power. Today, the oven is worse in that anytime the door is closed, it heats (but no fan or turntable).

Because there is no control on the heat, a simple 10-second cycle could turn into hours if someone gets distracted and doesn't notice. This could cause the internal circuits or the food to catch fire. 

I am in the process of reporting to Whirlpool.
justification: The microwave's malfunction creates a fire hazard, which could lead to injury or property damage if not addressed, though no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: This is regarding a GE Dishwasher Model GDWF160V40SS purchased from Home Depot in 2012. On the early evening of November 7, 2017 (6:00pm EST) I ran the dishwasher. In the early morning I went to work, not checking the dishwasher. However, on my return at 4:00 pm 11/8/2017 I went to unload  the dishwasher which was extremely hot and shelled of something melting. I discovered that the heater was still on, had melted the silverware basket and warped melted some plastic cutting boards and storage containers, and would likely have caught fire if I had been away from home for a few days as the melting basket was dripping right on the heating element. The only way for me to turn it off was to switch the circuit breaker supplying power to the dishwasher to off.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted items) but no injury or death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions to occur.

incident_description: At 2:30 a.m. on 12/21, my  husband noticed a HORRIBLE smell in the entire 1st floor of our house.  It was coming from the dishwasher, which he had started at 11am. incident_description:
DESC: Frigidaire Stove/Oven (electric)
Model # FFEF3003NWC
Serial # VF70822370
Date of Purchase: March 22, 2017

Date of Incident: Sept 23, 2017 at 6:30 PM
Date I started writing this report: Oct 2, 2017
Today's Date: Oct 9, 2017

To tell you I am upset is an understatement.

History:
After my son returned from Afghanistan with injuries suffered  when his vehicle was blown off the road by an IED.  I moved him, his wife, and his two children into my other home located at [REDACTED]. He was given an 80% disability which was then upgraded to 100%. He also has PTSD because this happened 3 times. Please understand my son is a combat Marine who ÃÂknowsÃÂ the difference between a spark and what he described as an [REDACTED] rifle shot. 

Incident:
On Sept. 23rd my son was cooking spaghetti on a Frigidaire range 6 months old, which I purchased on March 22, 2017 from Lowes in Palm Coast. He was boiling approx 1 gal of water and was walking back and forth from the kitchen when there was an explosion. (not a spark or pop as I was told the service record indicated) My son dropped to the floor. The pan along with the water was blown off the stove and hot water went everywhere. The kettle was found 2 feet from the stove on the floor. He shut off the circuit breaker to the stove and called me. 

His 5 month old baby was 15 feet away with his wife. His 4 year old was playing in the living room 10 feet away. There is no wall between the kitchen stove and the living room. It is an open floor-space  home with only a counter between kitchen and living room. This could have been a disaster but fortunately no one was injured, because no one was in front of the stove. 

I called Lowes service dept and told them what happened. They told me they couldn't do anything until a serviceman came out. They gave me G & M  Appliance Repairs number and helped scheduled a serviceman to come out Wednesday between 9-5, because they said they were quite busy after the hurricane Irma.  A nice serviceman came out named [REDACTED] and after looking at the damage and examining the stove he said he wouldn't use it again and that a Safety Report needed to be filed. The element exploded from inside outward. A large amount of white soapy cream covered the bottom steel cone as well as the stove top. The serviceman said he would let his boss know. 

After a couple days I called Lowes to see why nothing happened and was told by Lowes that they haven't heard from the service company yet. I called G & M and spoke to [REDACTED], who told me they were waiting on Lowes. When I called Lowes I was told it was turned over to G&M and they needed to do the paper work. After 2 more days of pleading to get something done I finally was told by G&M that Lowes said it was repairable and that Lowes would  not give authorization to replace the stove because it ÃÂsparkedÃÂ. . Which was not cause to have the stove replaced. I was told to contact Lowes again, if i felt it needed replaced..which I  did, and was told by [REDACTED] to contact Frigidaire because of the discrepancy in the way it was worded because Frigidaire will NOT allow the word explosion used in the report. The report was changed and now said the stoves top element ÃÂsparkedÃÂ and so it was considered repairable.  I asked her who told her it sparked and she replied G&M. So I called them and spoke to [REDACTED] again who read me the report which said it exploded and caught fire. I then called back lowes who now agreed that the report said it exploded and caught fire, but, could not use that wording in their report to Frigidaire. Both Lowes AND the service company agreed that the report from the service tech wrote 'exploded' but I was being told that since the word exploded caouldn't be used it was changed to 'sparked'. Frigidaire said they could not replace the unit all because a burner sparked ! 

Then I called Lowes back and spoke first to [REDACTED] explaining the incident, and was then connected to her  supervisor [REDACTED] 888-775-6937 who I again explained what happened. She told me that they were not allowed to write the word explosion or fire and that a spark did not justify replacement. I then called Frigidaire again at 800 374-4432 and after waiting 43 minutes was connected to [REDACTED]. All this person would say was the service report said 'sparked' so it was company policy that if it was repairable that nothing further could be done. She listened to what happened but said its repairable unless the field serviceman says it is not. I told her what the serviceman said and her reply was that since it wasn't written down that way, there was nothing she could do. After running in circles for a week I told them to repair it ASAP and that I would write a safety report and ASKED to whom I should mail it. She said she didnt know and that I should contact the seller.  Back n forth passing the blame while since the day it blew up my sons family are still using hot plates. What ever happened to good service? 

I called lowes back Monday Oct 2, 2017 again speaking with [REDACTED] at G&M and was told she was waiting for my call to confirm I wanted it repaired.. I told her that since I was being told it could not be replaced, only repaired, and cooking on portable stove tops for another month was out of the question. That of course I wanted it repaired. [REDACTRED] said she would order the parts and have it repaired. That was a week ago and the stove is still sitting there not being used until the serviceman says its OK.

This has been the worst (by far) service I have ever received.
To have the person at G&M tell me that she was waiting to see if I wanted to keep the stove was demeaning. It was her serviceman that told us not to use it and that he recommends replacement.
Lowes telling me that words like explosion and fire could not be written down was outrageous. 

I spent several hundred dollars on a stove that exploded. 
I asked about the liability of having further incidents on a repaired stove and was told that they are not liable for safety issues...  What?

Being bounced back and forth between Lowes and G&M while each blams the other is ridiculous.
G&M saying they were waiting to see if Lowes would replace it and Lowes saying a spark or pop didnt justify replacing and that its G&M fault for not repairing it needs to be resolved.

The stove needs to be either replaced or fixed and if fixed a written service work order that specifies that its now safe to use. I would like this done ASAP.

G&M said I should file a Safety Report, but no one gave me any further information.. Loews said I should contact Frigidaire, which I did and after 3 different people was connected to [REDACTED], a supervisor.. ext [REDACTED]. Everyone just kept passing the buck.! 
 
NO ONE told me how to file a report or to whom I could send it !

Here it is Monday Oct 9 and G&M says there is nothing they can do, they are still waiting on parts.
Why did I purchase a 2 year service contact ?  Never again. 

I have 6 pictures of the after effect and damage caused to stove top.

Signed,

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an explosion of a stove element, but no injuries were reported despite the potential for harm.

incident_description:
I am a consumer advocate attorney who represents a client who sustained first and second degree burns on or about February 26, 2017 as a result of using Nordic Ware's 9-inch "Leak-Proof Springform Pan".

The wholesaler, Northland Aluminum Products, Inc. dba Nordic Ware, ("Nordic Ware") imports and private labels an "off the shelf" spring form pan from Germany from the manufacturer WMF Americas Group ("WMF").  

My client purchased the item from Amazon.com on January 31, 2017.

The Use and Care Instructions included on the back of the package provides only the following: "1. Before initial use and after subsequent uses, wash with hot soapy water. 2. Before each use, brush with solid vegetable shortening and dust with flour or spray with unsalted vegetable shortening with flour in the spray. 3. Metal utensils, scouring pads and abrasive cleaners should not be used on non-stick surfaces."

On February 26, 2017, my client used the "Leak-Proof" pan for the first time and followed all instructions when baking a French pastry called "kouign-aman", a butter-croissant style cake.  

After baking the cake as called for in the recipe at about 400 degrees for approximately 25 minutes, she cautiously removed the hot "Leak-Proof" pan from the oven when butter poured out of the bottom of the pan at the sides and directly onto my client's exposed right thigh causing first and second degree burns.

The burns from the leak caused immediately swelling, redness, raised blisters, and excruciating pain.  

My client initially self-treated by cleaning the wound, dressing it with antibiotic ointment, and applying a dressing.  She continued to experience pain and drainage from the wound.

The following day, on February 27, 2017, she presented to [REDACTED].  She was examined by a PhysicianÃÂs Assistant with chief complaints associated with ÃÂLeg swelling, Burn and Burn Injury.ÃÂ  Notes indicate that she was burned from hot liquid while cooking something and after liquid spilled from the pan and dripped onto her leg.

Upon examination, it was noted that abnormal erythematous lesions with scattered blisters to the right anterior mid to distal thigh measuring an area 9cm x 5cm.  The largest blister measured 2cm x 1cm.

My client's diagnoses included the following:

1.	Burn of first degree of unspecified site of right lower limb.
2.	Burn of second degree of right thigh.

She received a three inch [REDACTED] bandage and gave explicit wound care instructions.  

As a result of the incident and her significant burns, my client has suffered pain, swelling, and disfigurement/scarring on her right leg.  Due to her injuries, she suffers embarrassing scars.  She can no longer wear shorts, skirts, or swimwear without revealing the remnants of her gruesome injury.

incident_description:
Kitchen gas stove. If the control knobs for any of the 5 burners are accidentally bumped they can rotate (ccw) enough to allow gas to escape, without igniting the gas. If not detected or noticed, gas will continue escape and cause a very dangerous situation, or worse!
In our case the gas leak was detected and we had to open windows (in the winter) to air out the room. 
But what if the knob gets bumped, is not detected, and you are leaving the house? This situation could be devastating!

It should be noted that there are already several posts listed on various "product review" pages that describe the problem and date back at least 6months along with calls to the manufacturer who has stated that this is the design and they see no problem with it.
justification: The incident describes a potential gas leak scenario that could lead to a dangerous situation or death if undetected, and there are multiple reports of this issue.

If it happens once, okay, maybe my mistake. Twice, hmmmmm. Third time, whoa, I know I'm not crazy. Our only problem was forgetting to unplug it after the last use.
I tried reaching out to Oster, apparently the parent company is Jarden Consumer, on Dec. 19th but have yet to receive any kind of reply. I'm not even looking for a refund or replacement of any kind. Just wanted to warn anybody who will listen that this can be a serious problem. Maybe this is an isolated incident and if so that is good and I will dispose of it properly. But I will be looking forward to your reply to see if this has happened before.

incident_description: We bought the Whirlpool range Model # WEG730HODSO, Serial # R52427789, on 7/24/2015         from Hudson Appliance Center at 454 Pearson Rd Paradise Ca 95969. I spoke to whirlpool and was told that the allowable limit for bare/painted metal surface is between 152 and 194 degrees.  This does just not sound right.  If the stove was allowed to be 194 degrees that would burn someone upon touching the surface.  Whirlpool is not willing to do any more, but I have a hard time believing that even 172 degrees is safe.

Thanks,

incident_description:

We noticed that the smell came from our GE Profile dishwasher (Model Number PDW7880N00SS; Serial number starts with AM).  After closer inspection we observed the top of the dishwasher had a scorched mark and had burned the underside of our kitchen cabinet.

I removed the inner panel and saw that the wiring harnesses had both burned through and a component had been melted beyond recognition.

incident_description:
kenmore elite gas cooktop 36":
  Cooktop burner controls and base surround plate will cause 1st thru 3rd degree burns to anyone touching the base plate or control knobs when in contact with human fingers, hands or flesh.

incident_description: I was watching television tonight when I heard to loud pops I went in the kitchen and family room to investigate I thought someone was banging on the wall  or actually outside banging on the window .  I happened to look at the bottom of my refrigerator which is a side-by-side Kitchen Aid model 2013 and noticed at the bottom of the freezer door a flame and I smelled fire.  I blew the finer out and it appears the wiring harness for the freezer at the base of the refrigerator shorted out the door was closed and no one was even touching the refrigerator when this happened . I open the freezer door and noticed sparks coming from the same area at the base when I open the door as the wiring was shorting so I close the door and turn the circuit breaker off for the night so I could sleep peacefully without worrying about the house burning down .  Had I not been home at the time it's quite possible that the wiring harness could've melted or ignited plastic and started a fire in the kitchen which could've eventually cause my house to go up in flames or someone to die within it I was very lucky .  Now I don't know what to do I'm sure this will be quite expensive and I plan to call to donate tomorrow voice my serious concerns over their product and expect immediate repair  or replacement.  I am very concerned about this product and extremely uncomfortable even leaving it on and I have several steaks and other foods in the refrigerator that I could lose a few hundred dollars in value from this incident but again I feel lucky because it could've been a disaster  had I not been home heard the noise smelled the smoke and seen the fire pit deal with it immediately. 9/1/2017 10:30pm

incident_description:
Potential problem with Whirlpool Free standing range model: WFE510S0AS0
Our range is a little more than two years old. We just did a clean cycle and just as it was ending we heard a loud POP. After checking the range out I found that the left two burners no longer worked. Since the range is out of warranty I took it apart to see if I could find the problem. I found that one of the main feed wires to the burners had burned through and shorted to the range metal frame. Actually burned a hole in the metal (see photos). The cause of the problem is that the wires are squeezed to the metal frame by the back of the range. As the unit gets very hot during the clean cycle it melts the wire insulation causing a short circuit. I fixed the broken wire and the burners work fine again. I covered the entire metal area near the wires with electrical tape to add extra insulation.
I reported this problem to Whirlpool today as I believe it is a design flaw that can result in a fire or electric shock hazard.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and wire damage, but no injury occurred. The issue was fixed, but the design flaw could lead to future incidents.

incident_description:
In June we purchased a new GE gas stove from Best Buy in Blaine, MN.  
Model # JGBS60DEK2WW
Serial # 131601P
This stove has the control knobs for the top burners in front of the stove with a safety feature that will not allow you to turn the burners on without first depressing the knob then turning the knob all the way counter clock wise to the left as far as it will go.  Once you turn it as far as it will go, the igniter starts to click lighting the burner.  You then turn the burner clockwise to the desired heat setting.

The locking system is working as designed and the igniter is working as designed.  The problem is, if you are reaching above the stove to get something out of the microwave, cupboard or if you are cleaning the top-back of the stove and you lean into the stove and slightly twist your body from right to left, you inadvertently turn the stove on but you are not turning it far enough for the igniter to kick in so you begin filling the kitchen with gas.

This has happened to us at least a dozen times so far and there have been 4 incidents where we did not catch it, filling the house with gas.

The stove we replaced worked in much the same fashion except the moment the gas was turned on, the igniter kicked in alerting the user that you had just turned on the stove.  If the user did not hear the clicking, it started the burner so all you did was burn some extra gas you would have preferred not to.

I called GE and spoke with two different people and explained the situation.  Both said there was nothing they could do because the stove was operating the way it was designed.  The case number they gave me was: [REDACTED]

I called Best Buy in Blaine, MN and they said also, there was nothing they could do but sell us a new stove.

This, in my opinion is a design flaw and needs to be fixed before someone dies.

I will be buying a new stove tonight but someone should do something about this.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that leads to gas leaks, which could be dangerous but has not yet resulted in injury or death.

This allows water to escape during the regular operation of the dishwasher.  Water hits the top of the door on the inside of the dishwasher and runs down both sides of the door on to the floor.  This is a safety hazard as it creates a slip/fall hazard and has the potential to cause an unsafe electricity situation.  2 service calls have yielded no resolution to this matter.  Awaiting the 3rd service call with little hope of resolution as the last technician stated that the lock/latch is not strong.  

As this dishwasher is located in a summer home, we do not consistently reside at the home.  This is our 3rd trip to this summer home this year, and we have called for service on each trip.  The dishwasher has not functioned properly since it was purchased in April of this year.

incident_description:
Our Kitchen Aid dishwasher ( Model # KDTE204DSS) was purchased 27 October 2014 from Ferguson Enterprises in Newport News, VA.

On 24 Dec 2016 we woke up and noticed that the granite countertops were extremely hot to the touch and when we opened the dishwasher steam and super hot air came gushing out.  Everything  plastic was completely melted. ( ie. kids sippy cups, [REDACTED], measuring cups etc).  The repairman told us he sees this frequently and that the control board went bad and the dishwasher had stayed in the heated dry mode all night.  What a scare to think of a house fire on Christmas Eve with all my kids and grandkids in the house!  I have since done some research and found that this was not an anomaly and that the control units have caused a large number of fires but yet nothing has been done and there has not been a recall.

The final straw was this Christmas when I discovered wet carpet in a closet while getting holiday decorations out.  We called a plumber and he traced the water back to the dishwasher.  The water had been leaking for some time apparently from the diverted motor seal.  We never had any water visible - it spread laterally along the subfloor.  We now are dealing with over $10,000 of damage while they tear up and replace the tile floor, replace cabinets and wallboard all damaged by the leak!  All for a shoddy and inferior 10 cent part.  Again the repairman and the water mitigation company told us that this is something they see all the time.  Why?  When a company has been made aware of a problem and there is a clear danger to the public why are they not held accountable.
   
I had to write you about this because the thought of some other family being injured or killed because of a dishwasher fire would be on my conscience.  I have written to Kitchen Aid as well and will look forward to hearing back from both bother you  I can no longer use this product with any confidence and would like to see it replaced as well as a public recall or repair of known defective parts. 

Thank you.
justification: The incident involved property damage and potential fire hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire stove in my residential kitchen that is a galley series.  It is used for residential cooking only.  It has been a great appliance until recently.  In the early morning hours of August 7, 2017, at approximately 0430 AM, the stove preheated itself to 350 degrees un-commanded, all the while my family were all in the bed asleep.  Just to give a quick background of myself, I am the Fire Marshal for the City of Jacksonville, AL with 18 years on the job.  This is not the first time that this has happened with a Frigidaire stove within the city limits of Jacksonville in the past 15 months.  My department has responded to five working kitchen fires due to Frigidaire stoves cutting them selves on, un-commanded by the owners, and causing residential kitchen fires. Now that this same scenario has happened to me, I see this as a systemic problem.  I now do not leave my stove plugged in while it is not in use.  I do not trust it while no one is home.  If it did an un-commanded preheat once, my opinion is that it will do it again.  The model # of stove that I have is: LGEF3045KFD.  The serial # is: VF10246284.  I have called both Electrolux and Frigidaire regarding this issue and they do not have any comments and show no concern on it.  They also stated, "we do not have any recalls on that model and have no information to give you."  This issue needs to be addressed, sooner rather than later.  Regarding the fires in other stove appliances within the city, they have all been reported to CPSC.gov.  This report is regarding my personal appliance in my residence.

The submitter said after struggling for some time she was able to open it but the top exploded and hit her in the chest. The submitter described the incident similar to opening a champagne bottle. The submitter said the top flew off hitting her in the chest and the contents went everywhere. The submitter said had pains in her chest from the incident but she did not seek medical attention. 

The submitter said she used the unit again about 2 weeks ago and she has been unable to open the blender. She said she is scared to force it open because of the last incident. She said her husband has also tried opening it but he was unsuccessful. The submitter believes the product is unsafe and should be examined.

The submitter indicated that when she has used the unit in the past it would be a little hard to open but now it has become extremely hard and unsafe to open.

The submitter plans to contact the firm and notify them of her safety concerns.
justification: The incident caused chest pain but no medical attention was sought, indicating an injury without severe consequences. The recurrence of difficulty in opening the blender suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description: My Oster Toaster Oven Model TSSTTVF817 timer failed and continues to run after reaching OFF.  It continues on to STAY ON which resulted in the oven being on all night.  It does not stay OFF when it is supposed to.
justification: The toaster oven's timer failure resulted in it staying on all night, posing a potential fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Our LG Electric Range is 3.5 years old. Eveytime I self clean is gets extremely hot and the stone counter tops and cabinets as well as the back wall behind the stove is so hot you cannot touch it.  Yesterday September 2 2017 I set the self clean and after an hour the stove turned off completely.  I assumed the breaker tripped and went to the panel and reset it.  When I did that there was smoke that came from under the front of the controls and blue and white sparks and withing a matter of seconds the back of the stove lit up with red and orange flames.  We called the fire dept and when they aarived they had to break though our wall because it was so hot to make sure there was not an electrical fire.  The Range  itself itself shorted out and cause the fire that shot out the back of the Range.  This Range is dangerous when in the self clean mode and should have a recall completed.  Now we have to buy a new range.
