incident_description:
While using the Elite Maxi-Matic electric kettle we noticed a strong odor of burning plastic.  When we looked at the bottom of the kettle we could see that it had melted a hole in the bottom plastic of the kettle and also in the base.
We did a web search on this product and discovered a review on Amazon saying virtually the same thing.  
We called the manufacturer's customer support phone number and the representative said they we not aware of any problems with this product.  I emailed them pictures of the melted plastic. 
They offered to replace the kettle, which we did not want.  They said we would have to go back to Kroger to get a refund, which we will do.  
We bought this kettle 9 months and we used it every day.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and melted plastic but no injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is high as similar issues were found in online reviews and the product was used daily.

incident_description:
Samsung electric range has poorly designed knobs that are easily &  Accidently turned on, causing stovetop fires.  I found the community on Samsung website who all say Samsung won't recall or replace the stoves because they are still operational.  
My first stove fire occurred December 24th this year,  after I (unknowingly) accidentally bumped into the stove knobs on front of the stove. Now I'm scared to death to keep this stove in my house!  Samsung has no fix for this dangerous problem.
justification: The incident describes a stovetop fire caused by accidental activation of poorly designed knobs, indicating a clear hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
I was using a 2 cup glass measuring cup made by Anchor.  I had cold butter in it and I was attempting to break it up with a table knife so that it could melt it in the microwave oven.  Suddenly, the whole thing shattered.  

I was very surprised at how fragile this measuring cup was.  It was a newer measuring cup, less than a few years old.  I have Pyrex measuring cups that I have had over 40 years, so I am not hard on my kitchen equipment.  I have done this same thing with my old measuring cup many times with no problem.

I was not injured, but very easily could have been. Glass was all over the counter and floor.  This product is made from cheap glass and not durable enough to hold up with normal kitchen use.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of a measuring cup but no injury occurred, though the potential for injury was noted.

incident_description:
I pureed a soup in the NutriBullet 900 Series Blender.  When taking off the lid of the blender, it exploded like a bomb and caused 1st and 2nd degree burns across my chest, arms, neck and face.  I went to the ER immediately and they cared for my extensive burns.  That was a week ago - since then, I've had to do daily wound cleaning and dressing changes (at the ER or a wound clinic or with a nurse).

I have since found several other stories online in which other people (even a 4 year old boy in Florida!) suffered horrible burns like mine.  There are no warnings on this blender about putting hot liquids in it.  Unlike a [REDACTED] coffee cup, there is nothing that reads NO HOT LIQUID.  

In our litigious society, I am quite shocked that this company doesn't have such basic warnings about hot liquids...especially since I have seen multiple stories online about other burn victims.

This company should be required to add language in large bold letters to each NutriBullet device that reads NO HOT LIQUID.

It has been a very painful ordeal (second most painful event for me next to childbirth) and I don't want anyone else to ever suffer this pain.

I cannot work.  I cannot pick up my 2 year old daughter.  My burns hurt and itch.  I have limited mobility.  Please do something to ensure that others are warned about this kitchen device - no hot liquids should ever be placed in it.  The manufacturer must be required to add these warnings immediately...and a recall would be beneficial as well.
justification: The incident caused 1st and 2nd degree burns requiring ER treatment and ongoing care, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
In the past three months, I've purchased two food storage containers at my local Kroger grocery store in Shelbyville, KY. Both of these containers have exploded, under different circumstances, without having been dropped or damaged in any way. Both containers had been used less than five times each.

The containers don't seem to bear any identifying information except that they have a gray handle with Smarter Lock on it, and the letters KGG on the bottom. The glass containers were square with a diagonal division down the middle to form two compartments.

In the first case, I took the container from the fridge to the microwave, removed the lid, and cooked on high for three minutes. It exploded apart.

In the second case, which was more worrisome to me given that no heat had been applied, I removed the container from the fridge and ate my sandwich from it, and then set it down on my desk at work. I hadn't touched it in 5-10 minutes when it simply exploded, raining shards of glass everywhere. Thankfully I wasn't holding it at the time, but all I can think of is what if I, or someone else, had been holding either of these containers when they shattered!
justification: The containers exploded under normal use conditions, posing a potential injury risk, but no injuries were reported in the incidents described.

incident_description:
Purchased two Pyrex 9.5 Fluted Clear Glass Pie Plate on Thursday 12/7/2017 from
Meijers Grocery located in Fraser MI.  On Sunday, 12/10/2017 I proceeded to
make the following meat pie.

Placed one package of [REDACTED] pie crust in each one of the new pie plates.
Added 1 1/4 lbs raw ground beef that had been mixed with 3 TBLS of [REDACTED] Onion Mix.
Layered 12 ounces of raw (not frozen) hash browns on top of meat.
Layered 1 cup of sharp cheddar cheese on top of raw hash browns.  
Covered with the remaining raw [REDACTED] pie crust.
Baked in preheated 350 degree [REDACTED] oven for approximately 65 minutes.  Left
both pie plates in oven for additional five minutes and then carried over to
dinner table.

Completed eating all but one piece of meat pie from one of the pie plates and  had one full meat pie completely cooked remaining.  My daughter-in-law picked up the full
meat pie and was carrying over to set unto my kitchen island.  As she carried it to set it down the Pyrex 9.5 Fluted Clear Glass Pie Plate EXPLODED IN MID AIR.  Glass
and meat pie went everywhere. Glass exploded all over the kitchen island, under the fridge, stove, even into my disposal.  There was no escaping the explosion.
The glass cut my daughter-in-laws hand.  

When I checked the internet later that evening,  I found there are many reported incidents of exploding Pyrex.  Pyrex needs to come with a warning label identifying the dangers of using these glass products in the home until they can formulate a safe glass.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury from exploding glass, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of multiple reported incidents.

justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing a melted hole and plastic dripping onto food, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite wall oven Model #790.48089000 Serial #NF11224762 Manufactured March 2011
While using the oven set to BAKE at 400ÃÂ°F, oven started beeping and displayed F10 ERR error code.  Noted that the broiler element was bright red, the oven was extremely hot and the food inside was beginning to blacken.  Oven controls would not respond when attempting to turn the oven off. After 5 minutes, error code F10 ERR came back in and the broiler element was bright red again.  The controls again failed to respond and had to open the supply breaker to turn the oven off.  Had this happened with nobody home, a fire would have occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased a Le Creuset classic stainless steel tea kettle in November of 2016.  Every time we used it for several months, we had the same problem:  every time the water in our kettle boiled this happened: when we started pouring into a cup, the hot water would spurt out of the spout, as if the spout itself were superheated.  It splashed out, partly into the cup, partly onto the countertop.  We quickly learned not to hold the cup with our hand.  I looked on line and found many descriptions of the same problem.  It seems to me someone could easily be burned by the hot water.
I contacted Le Creuset but they were not very helpful.  I returned the kettle to the retailer and bought a different brand.

The home depot did offer to refund the $200 extended service plan we purchased but told me that I would have
to deal directly with Samsung on the defective oven refund.
In the end Samsung offered $1862 for a refund provided that I cut the power cord to the oven and signed a
document stating that I would not re-sell it, and of course disposal of the defective oven was my problem. Told
Lilly that I would have to contact Home depot before I decided how to proceed. The home depot said a $200

In total we would get $1862 + $200 = $2062 back. We paid $2113.12 to the Home depot on 9/2/17, for a

incident_description:
Product: Fridgadaire Refridgerator Model No. LFUS2613LF3; Serial No. 4A11617670
Purchased on 10/8/2011.

I opened my fridge last week (8/11/17) to find that the light bulb was out.  This was the original light bulb.  When I stuck my head inside the fridge to remove the bulb, I found that the bulb had completely melted through the ceiling of the fridge!  The bulb was completely intact, but the heat from it melted the fridge!  I am very concerned about this, because it could have started a fire!  I have pictures to support this occurrence.  I have emailed Fridgadaire, but have not received a response.  When I searched online to see if others have reported similar instances, I found there were many people with the same complaints!  Apparently, Fridgadaire will not assume responsibility for this, and will replace the parts (part of the ceiling?) but the consumer (me!) will have to pay for a licensed Fridgadaire repair person to come out and fix it.  What?!?  This is a huge safety concern, and could have started a fire!
justification: The incident involved a melted light bulb and fridge ceiling, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I had a GE gas range model JQB760SEF2SS purchased 6/21/2015.  This range has not been used very much.  I turned on the self clean function for the first time on 12/9/2017. The oven was only lightly soiled and the range top has never had any notable spills so there was no accumulation anywhere of food spills or grease.   After about 3 hours into the 4 hour cleaning cycle, there was heavy  smoke. I was able to turn off the gas, disconnect the range and pull it away from the cabinets and move it towards a door to the outside of the house.  At that point, open flames were visible  underneath the range top, between the top of the oven and the stove top.  I  called the Amesbury Fire Department, the range was still burning when they arrived and they were able to extinguish the flames.  

The gas and electrical connections underneath the range top, to the burners, were completely burned out and the stove is a total loss.  

If I had not known how to disconnect the range or had been unable to do so and to move it, the gas could have exploded and burned down the house.   Many homeowners would not have the knowledge, skills and strength to promtly disconnect and move the range under those conditions. 
It was terrifying.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have led to severe consequences, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: My [REDACTED] guest was cooking this morning & the range top burner on the front left side would not turn off.  He had to turn it off at the breaker.  As soon as I got home,  I flipped the breaker & the burner immediately came back on.  I tried several exercises to get it to turn off and nothing worked & it was stuck on high. I unplugged the oven as I need to use other electricity in the kitchen, but now I can't cook.  Thank God this did not happen next week @ Christmas when my granddaughters will be here. Also, it goes on without notice and if that had happened in the middle of the night while sleeping w anything near the burner it could have been disastrous.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, though there was potential for disaster if left unattended.

incident_description:
The gas valves on our range are extremely unsafe. The way they are positioned and the way they
operate causes them to open if bumped. This has happened many times. This morning, after
being outside for a time, I returned to find the entire house filled with gas. I had to open the
doors to ventilate. Apparently the last person leaving the house bumped the stove on the way
out, causing the burner to turn on without igniting.

I have reported this to the manufacturer and seller they said they will not do anything about it.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with gas leakage but no injury or death occurred, and it has happened many times indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
We purchased an Electrolux Double Oven along with a 30" Cooktop in October 2011 for $4,090.04 from our local appliance store.  I have been in contact with Electrolux customer service for several years now, addressing my concerns which are as follows:
Specific to the Double Ovens:  The fuse box has to be reset after each self cleaning as it is placed too close to the heating element.  I am charged $85.00 for each visit, therefore I self clean the oven.  In May of 2015, I had several graduation cakes that were ruined as the bottom oven's heating element had failed.  That cost $268.49 to replace.  To date, I cannot get my baking goods to bake evenly.  One end is under-done while the other end is very dark.  I have pictures should you wish to review.  
Specific to the Stove Top:  I have issues with one of my main burners remaining on at all times.  In December 2015, we "catered" our daughters wedding.  I was cooking pasta on the burner and it never shut off.  We ended up switching the breaker which obviously shut everything off and cooled down overnight before we switched the breaker to the on position.  I have pictures of this as well when all the burners are in an "off" position yet the one burner is bright red.
Electrolux promotes customer service opinions and states they are very important.  Interesting, on January 19, 2016 I sent a letter to their CEO, [REDACTED] in Charlotte, NC, stating my concerns.  I have an email on March 9, 2016 from Electrolux stating they never received the letter.  I have a copy of the USPS tracking number that clearly states acceptance of the letter delivered on January 25, 2106 at 4:41pm.  I have several emails throughout time, dealing with [REDACTED] at Electrolux, explaining my concerns however they seem to have no regards to the issues at hand.
The best Electrolux will do is to offer 50% off any parts necessary for repairs.  I am requesting reimbursement of both the Double Oven and Cook Top as it is liability and far more inexpensive then reimbursement of a damaged home.
justification: The incident involves repeated equipment malfunctions (oven and cooktop issues) causing inconvenience and financial loss, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: After cooking on the stove top and in the oven for a short period of time, the oven was cooling down then the front oven door outer panel shattered while we were eating.
justification: The oven door shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I am reporting a very dangerous episode that occurred in my kitchen I had purchased a red copper Grill and was making an omelet, I have done this several times in the same fashion scrambled  the eggs placed them in the product closed and secured the lid set my timer for 1.50 minutes and then proceeded to flip the grill to cook eggs on the other side and again set the timer for 1.50 minutes about 45 seconds into the process a sizzling began to erupt as tho pressure was building up and suddenly the top blew open and the eggs flew off into the floor. Needless to say I wasn't standing in front of the incident or I would have been burnt by the hot egg. This happened and I thought well maybe I didn't secure the latch so a few weeks later I did the same exact thing and sure enough it built of pressure blew open the grill and once again the egg flew out of the grill and onto the floor. I called Red Copper and they couldn't explain it because I couldn't remember where I purchased it. I have used this for omelets and pancakes but never have I seen anything explode such as this.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous episode with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred as the user was not in front of the grill when it exploded.

incident_description: Ice cream scoop was in sink.   Poored pasta water into collendar.   Scoop exploded.   Ends shot off and metal end cap struck me in the forhead.  This caused me to spill Bolling water all over the kitchen.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (metal end cap struck the forehead) and spilled boiling water, indicating a moderate severity.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her icemaker started dispersing large pieces of plastic from the unit into the ice.  She stated that her children noticed it and that this could result in a choking hazard.  The company was contacted and they advised her that there was no recall and referred her to file a complaint with the agency.

Caller is concerned that this icemaker for the refrigerator is unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves a potential choking hazard from plastic pieces in ice, but no actual injury has been reported.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she was informed by her 25 yr old daughter that the refrigerator caught fire and burnt the contents inside.  Caller was informed that the smoke had engulfed the room and her daughter opened the refrigerator's door and the contents were in flames.  The contents was thrown in the sink and water was used to contain the fire.  She was not sure what had caused this incident to occur.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this refrigerator is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, causing damage to its contents, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer placed a frozen biscuit in the toaster oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit. Approximately ten minutes later, the consumer heard a loud noise coming from the kitchen. When the consumer checked, he noticed the toaster oven door had blown off, with shattered glass everywhere in his kitchen floor, and some as far as his living room floor. The consumer immediately unplugged the toaster oven; the frozen biscuit had yet to defrost.

07/10/2017 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him they would send him a shipping label so he can send the toaster oven back so they can investigate the matter.

The consumer indicates that the same thing happened with a second toaster oven he purchased for his daughter several years ago.

The consumer is unsure if he is going to keep his toaster oven for at least the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involved a toaster oven malfunction causing property damage but no injuries, and the consumer reports a similar past incident.

incident_description: Glass door on built in Kenmore Elite oven shattered.  It is only 1 1/2 years old, while baking for Thanksgiving Day the door glass shattered.  Very scary I have 3 small children at home, my daughter was in the kitchen helping and almost was hit by shattered glass.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no reported injuries, though it was a close call with a child nearby.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dishwasher was in use and he noticed that there was water leaking into his basement.  He contacted the plumber and he discovered that the heating element had burnt a hole in the bottom of the unit.  He believes this has been deteriorating for over sometime to cause this incident.

The company was contacted and he was informed that his dishwasher was not part of a recall and to report it to the agency.

Caller feels that this product is unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: Water leakage caused by a burnt heating element in the dishwasher, but no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I was mixing cake batter with my Kitchenaid stand mixer. I forgot to tighten the attachment knob, so the metal attachment hub cover fell off into the bowl while mixing the batter. The metal cover hit the flat beater and flew sideways out of the bowl. I was standing in front of the mixer, so the metal cover didnÃÂt hit me. A small piece of plastic came off of the flat beater. I donÃÂt know if it ended up in the batter or where it went. I think it could be dangerous if the metal cover hit someone or if someone hurt their teeth when eating the baked cake.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure but no injury occurred; likelihood is possible as it could happen if the attachment is not secured properly.

incident_description:
Kitchen Range Manufacturer: Samsung
Serial number: NE59J7630SS
Purchase date: 12/3/2016

My wife was cooking corn-on-the-cob on the right front burner. After taking the food into another room we heard what sounded like a shotgun going off in the kitchen. When we went back to the kitchen we found that the left front burner glass top had exploded. Samsung would not repair it under warranty.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded glass top) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Internal fire in freezer section of Whirlpool Refrigerator
justification: Internal fire in a refrigerator is an incident but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: I have a stove Frigidaire model: VF91942869. It started to turn on spontaneously and I can't turn it off. The only way is to unplugg it. I saw is a recall regarding this issue but the serial number I have on mine is not on the list. The problem I'm having is absolutely the same like all the other ones covered by the recall. Is very dangereus if no one is at home when it happens.
justification: The stove turning on spontaneously poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported in the description.

incident_description: I was making pureed door for a neighbor in need. While whisking potatoes, the shaft teeth broke off into the food. It would have been tragic if not noticed as the pieces were sharp.
justification: The incident involved a broken whisk contaminating food, which could have caused injury if not noticed, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: Viking Range that cost $8K turned on by itself and caught fire.   Would have burned my house down had we not been at home, and gotten the Fire Department's assistance.  Viking is taking its time getting back to me.   I would NOT buy another Viking stove.
justification: The stove caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred as the fire was contained.

incident_description:
Purchased a new Maytag dishwasher on 8/1/2017. Installed on 8/15/2017 During the third or fourth use we noticed an electrical smell coming from the unit. Upon opening the door, there was a two to three inch section of the lower heating element that had burned and melted.

I contacted Maytag to report this and ask for a replacement as I deemed this one hazardous. They informed me that the warranty only allows for service and repair. i then asked for a refund as this machine is a fire hazard and i do not want it simply repaired. I received the same answer.

Upon further research, it appears that Maytag had this same issue around 2010. That resulted in 12 fires and the recall of 1.4 million dishwashers. It seems it may be happening again.
justification: The dishwasher exhibited a hazardous condition (burned and melted heating element) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher interior including spray arms covered and filled with black fungus/mold that is not cleaned or removed during wash cycles.
justification: The presence of black fungus/mold in the dishwasher is an incident that poses a hygiene risk but no immediate injury is reported.

incident_description: I was using an Oster 231 knife from the kitchen block set to slice bacon.  The knife broke at the handle, it is a metal handle with black plastic in the middle. the plastic failed, causing me to almost have a serious injury.
justification: The knife broke but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Yesterday, I toasted an english muffin in the White Black And Decker toaster oven (BLACK+DECKER 4-Slice Toaster Oven, White, TRO420) which I purchased about a year ago. The toaster oven was definitely turned off and the over door was opened. I grabbed the toast and left the house and returned home the next day as I stayed overnight at a different location. The toast oven was completely on at full toaster heat with the door open and the knob past off. I felt relieved that a fire was not started. I've read on Amazon that many other reviewers experienced this same situation. The product should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toaster oven that could have caused a fire but did not, and similar issues have been reported by other users.

incident_description: The microwave turns on by itself and heats up very hot.  This is not just the exhaust fan turning on but the oven is heating, the light is on and the turntable turning.  Pushing the cancel button or any other button does not stop it.  One has to open the door or unplug it to stop it.  This has the potential to start a fire and I believe it should be recalled.  The brand is Magic Chef, model number:  MC0160UB, and serial number:  DJ08101550.  It was built in January 2008.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I was sitting at the kitchen counter this morning when the outside pane of glass in the oven blew out sending shards of glass throughout the kitchen. The oven and the stove top were not in use during this time. The last time I used the oven was 5:30pm the night before. I have never used the self- cleaning feature.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass pane blowing out, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: WHILE MY KENMORE ELITE STAND MIXER IS PLUGGED IN IT WILL ME IN THE OFF POSITION AND THEN IT WILL TURN ON BY ITSELF. THEN THE SWITCH STOPPED WORKING AND THE LIGHT JUST FLASHES WHEN YOU TRY TO TURN IT ON
justification: The mixer turns on by itself and has a malfunctioning switch, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that while using the device to remove the cover from a glass jar it snapped off becoming a projectile which hit his grandson in his stomach.  He stated that the child was not injured but it could have hit him in the face.  He stated that he had only used it twice before the incident.

Caller contacted the company and they advised him to take pictures of the device and submit it for a claim, he was offered a replacement but he declined due to the safety hazard.
justification: The child was not injured, but the incident involved a projectile, indicating a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
(05/17/2016) The consumer stated that she was closing the microwave door. Suddenly the door of the microwave door fell off. When the consumer inspected the unit, one of the metal tabs that holds the door is bent (bottom tab).  

The consumer stated that this is a safety issue.

The consumer will send pictures of the unit.

(05/17/2016) The consumer contacted Sears Home Warranty and was advised that the unit was not covered. The consumer also called Sears Home repair and was transferred back to Sears Home Warranty. The consumer was transferred to dispatch to schedule a repair.  

No injury.
justification: The microwave door fell off but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: When any of the knobs are bumped into or leaned against, the switch controlling the heating element turns automatically and activates the heating element. the activation of this knob/switch should require a two step process of push and turn of the knob. However, this range requires only a slight push of the knob for the knob to rotate automatically, resulting in the range accidentally turning on. This has happened on multiple occasions.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning switch that can accidentally activate the heating element, posing a potential hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description: My Bosch diswasher was running a cycle and caught on fire.  Our smoke detector woke us up from sleep, and we were able to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries were reported as the occupants were able to extinguish the fire.

incident_description: Upon cleaning my blade, I discovered a crack in the housing that holds the blade. I fear that the blade will come out of the housing. I will no longer use this appliance.
justification: The incident involves a cracked housing that could lead to the blade coming out, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The Kenmore Elite above range microwave (Model 721.86013010) has a handle that starts to peel its "stainless steel" coating - probably due to heat from the range. When it peels, it creates a sharp edge that can cut a person. I purchased a unit in 2013 and the first time it peeled (2015), the defect did cut a member of my family. I replaced the handle. The same problem has occurred again (no cuts this time as we were aware of the potential issue) and I need to replace the handle again.
justification: The incident resulted in a family member being cut by the sharp edge, indicating an injury (severity 3). The problem has recurred, suggesting it is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Kenmore elite stove model 79099113301 right front burners turns on itself while not in use and will not turn off got so hot before I knew it was on it melted the plastics on the coffe pot 8" away from it and burnt my hand I contacted the manufacturer sears and they didn't want to hear it
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the described malfunction and lack of manufacturer response.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his smooth-top electric range that began remaining lit sometime around February/March 2017.
He finished cooking then turned the element off, however the element would not stop heating and did not turn off until he went downstairs then turned it off and on again.              
This problem repeated itself a few times after  this time and required that he or his wife flip the breaker off then on again each time.
October 13th, 2017 the caller's wife had been cooking, she turned the element off and the breaker off and back on as she and her husband had been doing for months, however the element did not turn off.  She tried again but decided to leave the breaker off. 
The caller and is wife are no longer using the range and they are reporting it as a potential fire and burn hazard and they are also asking that it become recalled.
While they were searching for the model and serial number they realized that their range has one model and serial number on it but the product registration book has a completely different model and serial number.  
He contacted the manufacturer and asked for help but has been unable to locate anyone to speak with them or help them identify the correct model and serial number and he believes that they have no interest.
There have been no injuries
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range posing a fire and burn hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
Unintentional turning on top burners on Electric stove causing fire. A simple accidental bump of the hip to the control knob will turn the top burners on unintentionally. This had started a fire in our Kitchen when a guest leaned over the stove to get a slice of pizza and bumped the control knob which turned the burner on.

The burner had been found on unintentionally 3 times previously but we had not understood how that was happening prior to the fire.

I contacted Samsung customer service 3 times to try to talk with someone in their product liability team and all three times my transaction number case was closed without any conversation from their team.

We currently remove the knobs from the stove when not in use to avoid another fire.
justification: The incident caused a fire, which is a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported. The occurrence likelihood is high as it happened multiple times and required preventive measures.

incident_description:
I was using the self-clean option on my KitchenAid Double Oven Gas Range (model KGRS505X), which was installed in April 2011. I selected the regular self-clean option, a four hour clean. With about 1.5 hours left on the timer, I was in my basement checking on laundry and noticed debris on the surrounding area. Once I entered the laundry room, saw flames coming through from the ceiling above and realized it was from the oven. I ran upstairs to turn off the self-clean. The fire continued and smoke built up. We used a home extinguisher to contain/put out the flames. With a call to 911, the fire department arrived. The fire was extinguished, the oven was removed from my home, and the oven and surrounding area were inspected by the fire department.  It was noted that there was no debris surrounding or under the oven or anything inside to cause the malfunction which resulted in a fire. 

We are left with a hole in our kitchen, from where the oven was, that burnt through the floors into our basement. And no stove.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Brand new blender. I took it out of the box and the product was so difficult to put the plastic container on the blender motor that I was going to return to the store.When I turned it sideways to put back into the styrofoam packaging, I turn the blender container on its side and the inside blades do not lock, so they bounced out and made a large laceration and I had to be rushed to emergency for stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in a large laceration requiring emergency stitches, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Power cord/ electrical cords in back panel caught fire and melted wires and terminal
justification: The incident involved a fire and melted wires, which is a significant hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Both of my oven doors on my Capital Cooking Range have shattered during the self clean mode.  The ovens were full of exploded glass.  I was provided two new doors from the manufacturer and one arrived shattered in shipping and the other shattered again during self clean cycle. Here is the range:
http://www.capital-cooking.com/products/connoisseurian-series-60-dual-fuel-range-5/
justification: The incident involves repeated shattering of oven doors during use, posing a clear risk of injury from broken glass.

incident_description: DETAILS ---- I recently put a pot of water on my glass GE stove top and stepped into the doorway of the adjacent room. About 2 minutes later I heard this deafening boom. I turned toward the kitchen and the entire stovetop had exploded and sent shards of glass, some of them 6 inches long, across the kitchen and into the dining room, up to 20 feet away.  I had my back toward the oven and I received small lacerations to my legs and feet. Had my granddaughter been in the kitchen at the time, it would have seriously maimed her or could have killed her outright. After contacting the GE chat line, I was told I had a ten minute wait time.  I was number 1 in the queue.  After waiting 35 minutes, GE canceled my chat.  Apparently they do not wish to discuss this problem. My next stove top will definitely not be a General Electric product.  After reading the testimonials of others, I realized that mine was not an isolated incident.  This stove was a top end Profile series product.   It had been impeccably maintained.
justification: The incident caused small lacerations to the legs and feet, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description mentions this is not an isolated incident, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: Hefty disposable aluminum baking pan by Reynolds.  Large mass of glue on bottom of pan melted and started fire in oven leaving entire house covered in soot.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven causing soot damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire dishwasher which has a heating element that has melted a hole in the bottom of the inside area. We had been noticing a hot plastic or electrical smell for a couple of weeks, but couldn't locate the issue and thought that it might be just the water heating up in the washer. A couple of days ago I noticed a stream of water coming out from under the dishwasher. When the washer had finished its' cycle I opened it up, pulled out the bottom rack and noticed that the heating element was warped, downwards and had melted a hole in the bottom of the plastic housing.
justification: The dishwasher's heating element caused damage but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: In August 2017 I purchased a new LG 30" freestanding gas range (LRG4113st).  During the short time since I bought it, twice I noted the gas on with no known reason.  I initially blamed myself.  However --  and more frightening -- I have twice since accidentally turned on the front right burner as I walked by.  The second time, the wrapping on a gift nearby caught fire, and although I quickly extinguished it, these two accidental lighting episodes leave me scared spitless that either I or someone else will have a far greater accident.  Clothing easily catches on the oversized and angular knobs.  It requires almost no pressure to push the knobs in and turn them.  Playing with the knobs to see what was going on, it is clear that it is exceedingly easy to turn on all four burner knobs with an easy swipe of fingers -- no distinct push and turn is required.  The fact that the knobs are squared at the corners and are large apparently contributes to clothing catching the knobs easily.  That a 'catch' can result so easily in a 'light' is frightful.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to accidental burner activation, causing a minor fire that was quickly extinguished without injury.

incident_description:
We were using the oven on our Frigidaire range when the right rear burner turned itself on and proceeded to heat to high.  The switch war already in the off position and thus I was unable to turn off the burner.  I had to switch it to Low, just so I did not have a red hot burner on the top.  

I unplugged the range and looked up to see if people had a similar issue.

I was able to identify that a recall was issued in 2009 that described the exact issue and posted to the CPSC website.

My model number: PLEFMZ99GCB was included in the information and my serial number: VF74738003 was within the designated range.  

The contact information showed a phone number and website to report issues.  The website now redirects to the main Electrolux website.  The phone number now says they do not have weekend hours.  

I called the main Electrolux product line and eventually spoke withe someone regarding the issue.  They put me on hold to look up the recall and now tell me that the model number is not on the recall list.  I advised her that it is on the CPSC website and she just restated it was not on her list.  I asked to speak with a supervisor who advised me she wasn't sure "what I thought I saw" online, but my model was not on their recall list and they couldn't do anything.  She advised if I wanted to continue the issue, to call the other number on Monday.

It is disturbing that they do not have a complete list of their own recalls.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven burner that turned on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I took a round glass Pyrex container full of soup out the refrigerator, placed it in the microwave, and heated it for two minutes. The soup was at room temperature so I heated it for another two minutes. At that point the soup was medium hot while the container was almost unbearable to the touch. I ate the soup on my wooden desk and left it sitting empty. After four hours, at room temperature and without being disturbed in any way, the container shattered in a spectacular manner. It was literally a small explosion sending glass shrapnel more than 4 feet away and giving me a small cut above my left knee. I left the remaining glass untouched so I could take pictures later. An hour had passed and quiet but audible ticking sounds started coming from the glass at an interval of about 10 seconds. These glass Pyrex containers are labeled as microwave safe but given this incident I am now certain that they are anything but safe.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut from glass shrapnel, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description:
Our flat top electric Frigidaire stove caught fire in the back of the unit on the 3rd of December 2017. The unit was not being used to cook with at the time. Popping noise was heard coming from the unit prior to the flames.


Frigidaire Stove
 (Electrolux )
Model FFEF3048LSM
SER# VF32367142

Caught fire on 03 Dec 2017
Manufactured 23 week of 2013
justification: The stove caught fire but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description: The Mainstay coffee mug (fall series with orange and green pumpkins decoration) says on the bottom it is dishwasher and microwave safe. I have heated coffee several times and the cup and handle gets very hot, burned my hand. It is not microwave safe.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury due to the mug getting excessively hot in the microwave, contrary to its safety claims.

incident_description: I was cooking on bake and noticed the broiler was somehow on high. I should have known better but moved the roast to a lower rack even though the oven was still on bake and not broil. Eventually the oven must have overheated and a fire started behind the control panel. Sparks and flames could be seen coming out of the top, rear of the stove. We turned off the stove breaker. When it cooled down, I opened the back of the stove and saw the controller board was burnt up. I found many people post online that this was a common issue with this model stove. Model 790.94193310. My stove is just out of warranty but I felt I should report this safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a fire and sparks but no injury or death, and the issue is reported as common for this stove model.

incident_description:
1/2017:  The microwave had been on for approximately 15 seconds, when a flash,  smoke and a burning plastic odor, emitted from it.  The door became stuck and could not be opened by the use of the handle.  The consumer used a screw driver to pry open the door.  A the time of the incident the consumer was using the microwave feature.  The container and the contents (soup) had clear plastic wrap over it, but neither food or the container were damaged.

1/12/2017:  The consumer reported this incident to Sears and they arranged for it to be serviced free of charge.  Pictures were taken and the technician came out a 2nd time for further evaluation.  The consumer was given Work Order number:  [REDACTED].  The firm tried to tell the consumer that there was foil in between the door, which caused the problem.  The consumer said that was not true.  The consumer cleaned the scorch marks discontinued use of the microwave oven at that time.  The firm was not willing to do anything further to address this issue.


10/22/2017:  The oven feature was on for approximately 60 minutes, when the consumer noticed a plastic burning odor.  He later realized that the front of the microwave door was rippled and warp.  He opened  the microwave and discovered a big burn spot on the bottom center.  However, nothing was in the microwave at the time.


10/23/2017:  The consumer called Sears and their rep. checked to see if the item was recalled, but it was not.  The Sears rep. then provided the number to the CPSC Hotline and advised the consumer to contact our agency to report this 

No injuries and the product did not appear to be included in any CPSC recalls.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning odors but no injuries or damage to food or containers, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of similar issues suggests a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that this would be the fourth time the oven range's front and left burner malfunctions:

- The burner would not come on. A Service Technician replaced a part under the oven and repaired the burner on 09/05/2016.

- The burner would not heat up. A Service Technician replaced a switch on 07/14/2017.

- The consumer was cooking when she heard a loud pop, and the burner stopped working. A Service Technician replaced the terminal block element on 09/17/2017.

- 11/10/2017 - The consumer was cooking when the burner and the one behind it made an explosion-like noise and flames shot up from them. Though the flames were not as high on the back burner, they were five to six inches high on the front and left one. The consumer used baking soda to put the fire out. A Service Technician is scheduled to inspect the unit on 11/15/2017.

The consumer states that the oven range is used approximately two to three times per day whereas the oven is used once or twice weekly.

The consumer is unsure if she will keep her oven range for the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involved flames and an explosion-like noise, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that his oven range turns on with a simple brush against its knobs, many times unbeknownst to the person that walked past it.

The consumer has been in communication with the Manufacturer numerous times regarding the same issue.

03/28/2016 - A Service Technician inspected the unit however after inspection, he informed the consumer that there was nothing that could be done as this is how the unit is designed.

The consumer states that the cooktop is used once or twice daily whereas the oven is used approximately once weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The oven turning on unintentionally poses a risk of incident but no injury has been reported, and the issue is known to occur frequently based on consumer usage.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung electric range model #FTQ3531WUX when I build my house in 2011.  Within the past six months the front two burners do not regulate properly.  Most of the time they go and stay at the high heat setting.  At the very least this causes frequent burning of food and has a high potential to be a fire risk.  The initial incident date and the purchase date are approximate dates.
justification: The issue causes frequent burning of food and poses a fire risk, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: We purchased a new home with appliances made by Fridgedair purchased by our Builder Fortress Homes.  At about one year after moving into our new home, I woke early in the morning and while letting while feeding my cats in the basment I noticed huge puddles and flooding under our kitchen floor above the basement.  I thought a pipe had burst but after pulling away the insulation and inspecting the subfloor in the basement I see the water is coming out in between the floor boards from our kitchen not from pipes.  I immediately place buckets under each leak and run upstairs to find where it originated.  We run our dishwasher around 9pm every evening and during one of the cycles the heating element on our Fridgedair Gallery dishwasher Serial Number:TH53284409 Model #:FGBD2438PF7A had warped and had melted a huge whole in the bottom of the plastic tub.  As there were no clamps in that area installed by the manufacturer the heating element was able to come into contact with the tub bottom thus burning a hole and flooding our wooded kitchen floor and basement.  We had to purchase dehumidifiers, floor fans, and microbial spray to prevent mold growth.  We had to purchase a new dishwasher even though this one is only a year old.  If this had continued to be on our kitchen could have caught on fire as the element was hot enough and close enough to the electrical box on the bottom of the appliance to have burned our house down while we slept.  I have read there are class action lawsuits in Illinois against [REDACTED] and Fridgedair and cannot believe this dishwasher is still be manufactured and sold to consumers who could be in danger or out of major expenses because of negligence on the Electrolux and Fridgedairs part.  Someone needs to hold these people accountable and they need to reimburse the consumers for damages and appliances.
justification: The incident caused property damage and potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the described defect and similar reported cases.

incident_description: I purchased a cast iron grill from Walmart. It is Ozark brand. The instructions say that it can be used on a stove top or on an open fire. I was using it on my stove top (for the first time) and after being exposed to the heat for less than 2 min, I heard a loud bang that scared me and my fiance. The grill had broken in two. The blast was loud enough to shake the electric heat sources on my stove loose. If I had been close to it, I have no doubt it would have caused bodily harm. There are absolutely no warning labels on the product.
justification: The grill broke violently but caused no injury, though it had potential to harm if someone was closer.

incident_description: Kenmore 790 Series Gas Range oven glass exploded and shattered when auto clean function was used.  There have never been any problems previously.  Range was purchased 12/2008 and has been used frequently.
justification: The oven glass exploded during use, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
West Bend Slow cooker Model 84367

On 11/26/17 I had prepared a full [slow cooker] full of soup to take to a family gathering. It had been cooking on high. Went to lift it up off counter and into a towel lined laundry basket sitting directly beside [slow cooker]. As I lifted it over the basket and started to lower it down, the right side handle broke causing half the soup to mostly spill into the basket saving me from getting badly burned. Some did splash on my arms and clothing, but under other circumstances this could have had disastrous results. This [slow cooker] has gotten light use and always has been taken care of. I was shocked when this happened.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns from soup splashing on arms, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: After about 6 months of use (purchased new), our GE electric oven (model #JB755EJ3ES) began burning everything in just a few minutes of turning the oven on to 350 degrees. An appliance repairman came to look at it under GE's direction and tested it. He set it to 350 degrees and when he opened the oven to check it with a thermometer, it was already up to 750 degrees and the stove was not showing any error codes. This could have resulted in a fire or at least smoke damage had something been in for a normal baking time. The repairman ordered a new thermostat (I believe) and a new oven control panel, but the control panel was back-ordered for a month. GE customer service [Incident: [REDACTED]] was able to expedite the order (after we had been a month without our oven) and the part was finally installed on 11/27/17.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no actual fire or injury occurred, though there was potential for damage.

incident_description:
I was roasting vegetables and noticed they were taking longer than usual. I then noticed an odor and saw flames coming from behind my oven. The control board has burned areas on it. The stovetop and broiler still function, the oven does not.

Frigidaire Convection Oven.
Model #: LGEF3033KQE
Serial #: VF13162972
justification: The incident involved flames and damage to the oven's control board, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: When we pulled our dishwasher out from the cabinet to investigate a water leak, we discovered that the rubber thermal insulation of the exterior walls of the dishwasher had melted, deformed and detached from the back and sides of the dishwasher.  We feel fortunate that we did not have a fire.   I have pictures but the ADD FILES button is not functioning for me.
justification: The incident involved damage to the dishwasher but no injury or fire occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
My mother in law bought a Ninja NJ100 series express chop food processor (NJ100GR 30).  On opening the product to set this up, prior to any use, the blade slipped and cut the back of her hand below her thumb knuckle, severing an extensor tendon (I believe the extensor pollicis longus tendon).  Fortunately we were able to see an ortho hand surgeon quickly and this was surgically repaired within a few days.  She is working on rehab now and should regain full functioning of the thumb, but has not yet - currently she cannot extend the thumb.  
The product contains a flyer that says "caution: open with care, contains loose SHARP blades." but this seems insufficient as one is already opening the product before one can see this and it is among several other pieces of paper one may not know to look at prior to inspecting the equipment.  My mother in law is very competent and watches our two young children during the day, I feel strongly this accident was not due to any negligence or aberrant behavior on her part.  As a physician I feel obligated to report significant safety incidents I know about as I would with any drug I gave.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring surgical repair, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the product's design flaw and the potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: Top oven was off, bottom oven was being used.  My wife opened the fridge a few feet away and the glass on the top oven shattered.  It is the inner layer of glass, it did not explode everywhere but when we open the top door it spills out of the door, and when we opened the bottom door glass fell everywhere.  A small amount of glass somehow fell out when it broke and my 1 year old almost stepped on some of it.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injury occurred, though there was a close call with a 1-year-old nearly stepping on glass.

incident_description: We just recently moved into a home that has GE appliances.  We closed on the home Aug 8th, but did lots of remodeling in the home and never used the oven until yesterday, Thanksgiving day.  While cooking the turkey, the inside glass of the oven shattered.  Thankfully, dinner was not ruined and I was able to cook the turkey to completion.  Or else, this would have been a disaster for our company!
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured and dinner was not ruined, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
About 3 hours after starting the self-cleaning feature of my KitchenAid model KEBS207SBL02 electric double wall oven, the inner glass shattered on the top oven. It created quite a mess the day before our  Thanksgiving gathering.

This oven is approximately 9 years old.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass) but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. Given the oven's age, such failures are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a gas cooktop to replace one I had that had a failed switch that allowed gas to flow without the flame being lit.  On the NEW cooktop, it is very east to turn on the gas without the flame being ignited.  Over 1/2 of the time, if I turn the gas on quickly, the gas flows freely without the flame being lit.  If I let the gas flow for a while, and then turn the knob to the off position, it sparks, ignighting the gas that had accumulated around the burner.  With this arrangement, it is not that hard to imaging a small child turning on the burner and filing a building with gas, causing a serious explosion.

The cooktop I am replacing has an auto-reignition feature that significantly reduces risk of gas flowing from the burner without the flame being lit.  As an engineer who designs electronic equipment, I find it hard to believe that including the auto-reignition feature would add more than $10 per unit produced if it were an every unit item.

The cooktop I recently purchased is KitchenAid Model# KCGS550ESS01 Serial Number D62317092.

Can you explain why, at a minimum, auto-reignition, or a similar safety feature is not required on all gas ranges and cooktops?    As far as I am concerned, this is an obvious design defect of this unit.

I will be returning this unit to the store next week.  It is too dangerous to keep this appliance in my home.
justification: The incident describes a high risk of gas accumulation leading to a potential explosion, which could result in death. The likelihood is high as the issue occurs over half the time when the gas is turned on quickly.

incident_description:
We were cooking dinner. Had turkey in oven at 350 degrees for about 3 hrs before cooking on stove top.  Were using all 4 burners when two burners were "out of control" and got extremely hot.  Seemed to be much hotter than ever before and could not be controlled.  We could turn the burner off or on but on was "red hot" only.  One of the pots on stove was uncovered and had liquid gravy that seemed to explode and spewed hot gravy on wall, floor and nearby appliances.  
We could smell something burnt.  When we pulled stove out we could see where the wiring had burned.
justification: The incident involved uncontrolled heat and a gravy explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Fire department responded to the report of a fire in the kitchen.  Homeowners reported that their microwave oven had turned itself on and blue flames and/or sparks were seen coming from the holes near the top right edge inside the oven.  Homeowners unplugged the oven and threw baking soda into the microwave oven to extinguish the plastic "splash lid" left in the oven that had caught fire.  The only contents in the oven at the time of the incident were a plastic splash lid and the microwave oven turntable.  FD investigation did not find any fire extension to the house, though there was light smoke throughout the 2 story structure.

Owners had advised that they had been having recent problems with the microwave oven.  Problems included the oven tuning off before cooking time was complete, and continuing to run even after the door was open.  The oven had been serviced 4 days prior to this incident, with the service tech claiming the issue was due to a door sensor.  A part was replaced at that time, "in less than 5 minutes" according to the homeowners.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave with no injuries reported, and the fire was contained without extending to the house.

incident_description: Electrical cord caught fire
justification: An electrical cord catching fire is an incident with potential for injury but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his spouse reported to him that while she was using the oven for approximately 1 1/2 hours at about 375 degrees , she noticed flames erupting from the rear of the unit, she powered it off and the flame dissipated. He stated that when arrived home he switched the circuit breaker off.  They have not used the range since the incident.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised him that someone would be in touch after they sent them the range serial number.

Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: Flames erupted from the oven, but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that while using the cookware to cook eggs it exploded blowing the cover and dispersing the contents all over the room.  Fortunately no one was injured. The retailer was contacted and they advised him that they are aware of the problem and is working to fix it.

Consumer is concerned that the company is still selling these unsafe products that could cause serious injuries to consumers.  He was advised that they would be refunded the purchase price of the product and that he did not have to return it to them.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of cookware but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The retailer's awareness and ongoing issue suggest the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description: Please be advised that the top rack failed this morning almost with catastrophic results.  The washer completed its cycle and the top rack was being pulled out for emptying when without warning the right side gave way.  Luckily for Kitchenaid, my 71 year old reflexes held onto the rack preventing it from spewing glass on our new kitchen ceramic floor. The only injury was a slight blood prick and abrasion to the side of the middle finger. Was able to gingerly empty the rack free of glassware and ceramic cups without incident. Observation of failure area showed that the two side rail support lugs failed one apparently by straight shear and the other actually pulled out from the plastic bracket. Was able only to salvage the pulled out lug. Note that this washer is a replacement for a Kitchenaid Dishwasher that had failed due to a severely overheated circuit board.  Filed all of the paperwork and yet to receive any monetary compensation from this call action suit.  The washer had been installed in May 2016.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight blood prick and abrasion, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description:
Lower oven door handle came loose and fell and glass explosively shattered onto my feet and the floor.
Sears Kenmore Elite oven Model #790.48809100
justification: The oven door handle came loose and glass shattered, but there is no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: Our microwave was not being used at the time when it spontaneously burst into flames. Had we not been home and acted quickly to turn off the circuit breaker, which by the way had not tripped, and extinguished the fire quickly we could have lost our home!!! We contacted the local Sears to notify them of the problem with their defective product in able to initiate an investigation of the cause. They werenÃÂt interested. We made 3 successive calls to higher level of Sears and the Kenmore Corporation. None of which were interested enough in the safety of their costumers to take a report or to take the defective product to be looked at by their Engineers to determine the cause of the spontaneous fire and catastrophic failure of their equipment. Therefore I feel strongly that other consumers need to be advised that this is a potentional problem or defect in the this model . The model number is 565.60502990. Serial # 9T2K009404. If you need any further information please feel free to contact me at[REDACTED]. I also have photos if you need them for further evidence.
justification: The microwave burst into flames but was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: The glass top surrounding the gas burners on our Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Slide-In Range spontaneously shattered today while we were using the cooktop. There were no previously visible cracks in the glass, nothing was dropped on it, and no undue pressure was applied. It just suddenly shattered and caved into hundreds of sharp jagged pieces.
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: On November 22, 2017, my toaster that was sitting on top of my stove caught fire from underneath. Thus causing a lot of damage to my home & stove/oven
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: A burner on my Frigidaire electric range stuck on high even though the knob was turned down to low. It almost started a fire by filling the house with smoke. This stove already had the recall done once to it. I am very unhappy.
justification: The burner malfunction caused smoke but no injury or fire, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence despite a prior recall suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
Received 3rd degree burn from steam from coffee maker while it was brewing.

This coffee maker vents steam from the top when it is brewing by design.   In the black plastic there are words molded-"CAUTION - HOT SURFACE".    But, black on black lettering is not very visible.   And, the surface itself is never hot, it is the stream coming from it, which isn't very visible.

The situation was;  the coffee maker has a water reservoir on the right side.   I was making coffee,  it stopped brewing and I noticed the reservoir was empty.   I got some water to refill and opened the lid of the reservoir.   The lid is hinged on the Left hand side to it opens to the left.  When I tilted the lid to the left, it then comes to rest on the surface where the steam is vented.   As I brought the lid over, this is when the steam that had been escaping burned my little finger.

I think this is a reasonable situation and I was not reckless.   I needed my coffee and refilled the reservoir when I noticed it was empty.  Other coffee makers do not vent steam so I didn't think of this as a usual hazard.  I had a blister from this--a true third degree burn.   I have been applying scar treatment for weeks now but still have a red mark on my finger.   I am concerned for others who may somehow lean across the top of the maker to reach for something in addition to the situation I had happen.
justification: The incident resulted in a third-degree burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the design flaw and lack of clear warning.

incident_description: Mircowave oven started operating without any buttons being pressed.   In the past, we've seen situations where this microwave would not turn off after the timer had ended.  The only way to turn the microwave off was to unplug it.
justification: The microwave operates unexpectedly, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Using upper oven normally on our GE double oven range when the glass in the upper oven door shattered.  It appears there are 3 glass panes.  The middle pane shattered raining glass to the floor through the vent holes on the bottom of the door.
justification: The glass shattered but there was no mention of injury, only glass falling to the floor.

incident_description: I was cooking a dish the other day and while it was cooking, the rivet popped off and hit backsplash of kitchen wall. No one was injured, but do not feel comfortable using the pan.
justification: The rivet popping off caused an incident but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but can happen with faulty equipment.

incident_description: About a half hour after using oven and range, glass on outside of oven door shattered.
justification: Glass shattering on the oven door is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought a Bosch dishwasher and about 6 months after we had it, it stopped working.  Upon inspection I realized that the electrical cord had burnt up on the ends, severing the connection.   I had to clip off the burnt section of wires and reconnect.   I saw that there is a recall for over heating power cords on Bosch dishwashers at www.boschdishpowercord.com but my model is not listed in the recall.  I am concerned that my dishwasher has the same problem as the other recalled models and is a fire hazard waiting to happen. My model # is SHX3AR72UC/22.
justification: The dishwasher's electrical cord burnt up, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The dishwasher door was open and down and I was standing along side of the top edge. I leaned forward  and reached for a dishtowel on the counter and the top of the door tore my leg open through my corduroy pants.  It was a big triangular flap cut. It bled immediately and I had to put pressure on it and get to the emergency room.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring emergency room treatment, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
MIcrowave Food Cover Meltdown

Purchased 2 microwave food covers, know widely as a Hover Cover.

Contains magnets that allow the cover to be attached and stored on the ceiling of the microwave.

I did not witness the actual meltdown, but the magnets on the one we were using are melted and much of the plastic around it..

THIS presents a Fire and a food safety hazard.

I contacted the EBay sellr, [REDACTED] and this was the reply.

Hi, friend, so sorry for the problem you mentioned.
We will surely report them to the supplier, please understand.
In this case, could we refund $10 to you and you don't need to post them back to us?
Not bother you to return, helping you to save the postage and hassel of the post.
  
Also, I noticed that they had at least one negative feedback in the last month where the buyer 
said, "It caught fire inside of my microwave"  I believe this is the same product.

It also appears that the ones on TV and the ones on EBAY are identical in appearance, so I bekleive they all come from the same manufacturer.

HELP,  This is a serious problem!!!!!
justification: The incident describes a melted microwave cover with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Incident Description Wolf Gas Range and Oven Model R364G

Bought home in 2011, and prior owner bought the home new from a builder so all appliances were new.  We have never been able to use the broiler feature, without fear. A delayed explosion goes off every time, and we rarely use the Broiler because of it. What happens is when we turn the setting to Broil, the glow plug turns orange right away, then, 60 to 90 seconds later, a whoosh sound, then an explosion, with the door popping open a bit, with some flames.  I called a Wolf Certifed appliance repairman when this happened, he said that the igniter needed to be replaced.  I have had the igniter replaced by a Wolf certified technician and the issue has not gone away.  My hand was burned last night when the oven had a delayed explosion.

Clearly this oven needs to be replaced and not repaired as the repair did not fix this dangerous problem with the oven.  We are very afraid to use our Wolf Range for fear and anticipation of the explosion, and/or getting burned again by the delayed ignition of the broiler.
justification: The incident involves a delayed explosion causing burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue occurs consistently when using the broiler, making the likelihood almost certain (5).

incident_description: Product:  Rival Toaster   used to toast an English muffin.   Muffin was placed in toaster.  Setting was too short.  Changed setting and pushed down again. Toaster caught on fire. Flames were shooting up from toaster coming out at the top at the slots.  No injury was caused and no damage to anything.
justification: The toaster caught fire but no injury or damage occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The lights inside our refrigerator did not shut off.  I didn't notice the problem until I opened the refrigerator and discovered that my milk and juice were very warm.  It was warmer than room temperature warm.  I realized that the lights on the refrigerator would not shut off when the doors were closed.  I had smelled something "hot" earlier in the kitchen.  It was definitely the refrigerator.  The heat from the lights had caused the plastic housing/prongs that hold up the lighting fixture to melt.  In addition, the plastic casing above the lights have bubbled up due to the intense heat.  I believe this is a serious fire hazard.  

I had to manually push the buttons that turn the refrigerator lights off and on MANY times before the lights would actually turn off.  Something is wrong with the electrical lighting system of this refrigerator to cause the lights to stay on when the doors were of the refrigerator were closed.  Currently, the refrigerator is working correctly, but I am afraid that it may happen again and possibly cause a fire. The bottom freezer section was not affected by this issue.

As a result of this malfunction, I had to throw away all the items in the refrigerator section of this appliance since they were not kept at the proper cooling temperature for many hours.

The refrigerator is an LG Model No. LFD22860SW
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light that caused food spoilage and posed a fire hazard, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Over the weekend my range, Frigidare Gallery malfunctioned and caught on fire at 1am.  The smoke activated the smoke detectors and I found the two of the stove top burners on.  When I turned them off, they turned on again. The top of the stove was starting to burn inside the panel as if there was a short.  I was able to turn off power to the range and there was minimal damage.  I reviewed your site and leaned that this range was recalled un recall number [REDACTED].

When I contacted Frigidare, they advised that the model number of my range was not part of the recall.  I advised them that the recall listed serial numbers and my range matched the serial numbers on the recall and had the same problem. 

I've gotten nowhere we them and have tried three departments only to be sent to another person.

Can you advise me if this range is part of the recall.  If it's not it should be since it has the same defect and could have burned the house down

model    LG EF30572FE

Serial number     VF12461607

Thanks!!!!
justification: The stove malfunctioned and caught fire, but there was no injury or death, only minimal damage.

incident_description: Dishwasher running normal cycle began to smell burning rubber/plastic. Investigated found smell coming from dishwasher control panel. Panel was hot to touch. Turned off power to dishwasher.  There were no injuries and no damage to surrounding cabinets. Incident occurred 7/31/17
justification: Incident involved a burning smell and hot control panel but no injuries or damage, indicating a minor operational issue.

incident_description:
Our dishwasher's heating element never turned off after the cycle finished running. We came down to the smell of burning plastic. The silverware was beginning to melt the silverware container, a tupperware lid had completely melted and was in the drum of the dishwasher, across the heating element, plastic kids silverware was melted to the silverware container, other plastic dishes and cups were misshapen.

After we opened the door and ensured the cycle was done running, the heating element cooled down (after a long time). when we re-closed the door, without running the cycle, the heating element turned on again. I had to turn off the circuit breaker.

We were leaving on vacation the next day, and we were lucky we ran the dishwasher that night as we typically start the dishwasher as we leave the house.  I am confident that had we run the dishwasher the next morning, our home would have suffered a major house fire.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and a high risk of fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
When I pulled the coffee pot out of the unit the handle came apart. I grabbed the pot with my left hand to prevent complete spillage as grandchild beside me. As a result burned left hand with what spilled out.
Black and decker sdc750
justification: The incident resulted in a burned hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as handle failures can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
Kenmore range/oven, model number:790.93750102
does not turn off. Broiler heating element stays on continuously.
justification: The broiler heating element staying on continuously is an incident that could lead to overheating or fire risk, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: We have a Frigidaire stove model FEFL79DBL.  The front elements on the glass cooktop will only cook on high and sometimes will not turn off.  In investigating the issue I found a website which said models with serial numbers VF122 through VF831 were recalled for the exact same thing.  Our serial number starts with VF70.  I called sears and they said it was not part of the recall and I should call Electrolux.  I called them and they told me it was not on the recall list even though the serial number fell into that range and I should call a technician to have it repaired at my own expense.  I asked for a supervisor and spoke with [REDACTED] who told me she had my complaint and that they couldn't do anything because it was not on the recall list. I asked her what would happen with my complaint and she said "Nothing."  I asked for her supervisor (so far over an hour on the phone) and she told me her supervisor, [REDACTED], would tell me the same thing.  Apparently these people are considered corporate managers but they sound as if they are about 20 years old.
