She said they were the Electrolux managers but not of any specific division in the company.  This company is designed to give you the runaround and not help you.   They ignore the danger a defective range could cause and DO NOT stand behind their products.
justification: The stove has a malfunction that could potentially cause harm, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
On Nov. 3, 2017 three rounded corner rectangular dishes with plastic covers fell out of a kitchen cabinet onto the hardwood floor and exploded into thousands of shards of glass.  Dishes were Pyrex.  IÃÂve never used in oven.  Lids say safe in dishwasher, refrigerator, freezer and microwave.  Cabinet is low to floor, glass shard cut my leg. ItÃÂs ok. No medical treatment needed, but glass pieces everywhere.  Thousands of pieces.  These 3 containers had been sitting in cupboard were clean.  As I tried to take them out of cabinet somehow they slipped into the floor breaking into shards of glass. Very dangerous.

Purchased the set of Pyrex storage containers at Costco several years ago. Lids say: Pyrex 8212- UPC made in U.S. A.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut leg) but no medical treatment was needed, and the likelihood is possible as similar incidents can occur with glassware.

incident_description: The glass heat shield on the front of the oven shattered explosively outward. The oven was not on at the time, but the broiler function had been used recently (within the past 30 minutes). The glass pieces flew up on to the countertop and across the kitchen. It was safety glass, so there were no sharp edges, but if anyone had been directly in front of the oven, the force of the glass could have injured their eyes or face.
justification: The incident involved an explosive shattering of the oven's glass heat shield, but no injuries occurred as no one was directly in front of the oven at the time.

incident_description:
The rack(s) in the top oven of my LG double wall oven that had two loaves of bread baking suddenly and without warning fell down spilling the bread out of the oven and propelling the racks outward as well.  Fortunately I had on oven mitts and was able to stop the racks from falling off the oven door (where they had come to rest) and coming in to contact with my torso.

Upon checking, I found that NONE of the racks, including racks that fit perfectly in the lower, less used oven would rest securely on the shelving guides.  It appears the oven walls have bowed outward which is very distressing since the oven was only purchased and professionally installed in March of 2017.  I did use the self-clean function approximately one week ago for the first time and used the minimum time setting (3 hours).  The cleaning completed without incident but I did encounter difficulty reinstalling the oven racks back in to the oven after the cleaning cycle and cool down.  I was able to get the racks in and verified they glided in and out smoothly so believed there was no problem.
justification: The incident involved racks falling and spilling bread, but no injury occurred as the user was protected by oven mitts.

incident_description: The oven was warming up to 300 and an electrical fire started in the back bottom corner inside the oven.  A small 1 inch hole was melted before it was put out.
justification: An electrical fire occurred but was quickly contained, causing minor damage with no reported injuries.

incident_description:
The toaster oven heating element does not turn off after toasting has completed.  When the Function knob is set to Toast and the  Start/Stop button is pressed, the red light indicates the toaster is on and the elements heat up to toast your bread.  Once the oven beeps indicating toasting is complete, the indicator light turns off, however the upper heating elements do NOT turn off.  Even after turning the Function knob to OFF, the element is still burning.  At this point, the only way to turn off the oven is to cut power by unplugging it.  

This is incredibly dangerous because the oven indicates that it's off when it really isn't.  It has happened intermittently several times now and we don't realize it until we can smell the smoke generated by the extremely hot element that never turns off.

We cannot use this unsafe product any longer.
justification: The toaster oven's heating element not turning off poses a fire hazard and has happened intermittently, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I am a reporting an incident regarding a Cusinart Compact-Smoothie Blender, which we have had for 2 years. When making a smoothie, one of the 4 blades came off during the blending process. My husband would have drunk the blade if he hadn't noticed one of the small blades was missing from inside the blender. He used a colander to find the blade in his smoothie. He very easily could have drunk the blade in his smoothie and this would have been an incredibly serious health issue.
justification: The blade came off but was noticed before ingestion, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: The top shelf in my Kitchen Aid freezer exploded and sent shards of tempered glass onto me and as far as 10 feet away from the appliance.  There was a loud sound - like a gun shot - and then glass rained down on me.  The Kitchen Aid french door refrigerator/freezer is just barely 3 years old.  There had been problems with the appliance early on: first the ice make had to be replaced and then the entire front door of the freezer had to be replaced because it was determined that the door had no insulation.  When I contacted the customer service department regarding the exploding shelf I was told that "stress" can make tempered glass explode.  I believe that the "stress" came from improperly constructed glass or from the earlier problem of no door insulation.  I asked that Kitchen Aid replace the several tempered glass shelves.  They refused.
justification: The incident resulted in injury due to glass shards, and while the issue is serious, such occurrences are unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: We own a GE Profile Range with double oven and last week the glass in the oven literally spontaneously exploded out of the front.  The glass exploded clear across our kitchen and contaminated the inside of the oven as well.  We are very lucky no one was injured or near the unit at the time of explosion.  The oven was not on nor was it damaged, it is a fairly new unit and was purchased 5 years ago when we built our home.  GE is refusing to replace the unit even though they told me there are aware of the problem and there are hundreds of report of this happening across the nation.  The inside of the unit is contaminated with glass shards and cannot be safety used but GE still refuses to replace the unit.  I want to share my story with others so they are aware of the dangers of this unit and need to have GE replace the unit as it is their responsibility and it cannot be safely used.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing damage but no injuries, and GE acknowledges hundreds of similar incidents.

incident_description: My  8 years old Kennemore over the stove microwave get burning hot on the inside bottom when not in use.
justification: The microwave getting burning hot when not in use poses a burn injury risk, especially to a child.

incident_description: Microwave over heated and emitted burning smell with no burn food inside
justification: The microwave overheated and emitted a burning smell, but there was no injury or damage reported.

incident_description:
My GE Monogram Dishwasher caught fire last night.  I have extensive smoke damage in my house, but thankfully we were home so we were able to prevent it from doing further damage, destroying my house or heaven forbid any injuries to our children.  I called to GE to schedule service and they scheduled us for next week.  However, I think looked up the produce and found that there was a recall from October 2010 because of fires exactly like what happened to us.  
It's Model No. ZBD0710K10SS, Serial No. AL857043B
justification: The dishwasher caught fire causing extensive smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught on fire when running. Lots of smoke. Front control panel erupted in flames.
justification: Dishwasher caught fire and produced smoke, but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description:
I bought an Oster countertop oven model TSSTTVXLDG-003 at Walmart

There is no safety stop in the oven rack. As a result, when I tried to pull the rack out just a bit to remove a dish I was baking, the entire rack slid out and the hot dish landed broken at my feet.

 There is also no safety stop built into the oven door hinge.  If you open the door, it drops to the counter and as the oven is rather large, it hits the glass door onto the countertop edge.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard with the oven rack and door, leading to a broken dish but no reported injury.

incident_description: All 3 oven racks fall when putting items on it due to not being wide enough
justification: The incident describes racks falling, which is an operational issue but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: I was pulling a pizza out of the lower oven on my two-month-old LG double-oven range and the glass on the top oven shattered, with glass going everywhere. I had been using both ovens but turned the top oven off a few minutes earlier. I didn't bump anything, the top oven door just shattered.
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I have owned a Cuisinart TOB-40 Toaster Oven for about 5 years. The last few weeks the door has started opening difficult. Today after cooking toast twice when I went to open the door the second time it was once again hard to open and then completely shattered all over the place. Luckily I was not hurt by small glass fragments that went everywhere. I was able to clean up all the small chunks and slivers of glass up after about an hour. Had this been a child or the oven was at eye level it could have seriously injured someone. I have notified Cuisinart today and they are sending me a replacement oven but not sure I really want another one of this similar model now a TOB-40N. There is already a recall on this over for electric cord. Not sure if the newer model will fix the door and glass breakage or only correct the power cord issue.
justification: The incident involved the toaster oven door shattering, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is considered possible due to the reported difficulty in opening the door and the existing recall on the product.

incident_description:
(10/22/2017) The consumer stated that the broiler element would not turn off. The consumer also stated the unit is about 11 or 12 years old. 

On Sunday, while his wife was using the broiler to bake banana bread, an error code came on. The consumer is not sure of the code (maybe E2F3). His wife removed the bread which was scorched.

The consumer tried to turn the broiler off but it would not go off. He had to turn it off at the circuit breaker. The consumer waited for about a minute and turned the circuit breaker back on. 

The broiler came back on by itself with no indication that it was on.
justification: The broiler malfunctioned but no injury occurred, only property damage (scorched bread).

incident_description:
Dishwasher power cord caught fire. On Nov. 17, 2017, I started the dishwasher with a moderate load on the ÃÂdelicateÃÂ cycle.. After approximately 20 minutes, I began to smell a strange chemical odor in another part of the house (upstairs, in a bedroom). I went around sniffing, trying to discover the source of the mysterious odor. I followed the scent downstairs to the kitchen. It smelled like burning plastic, but I couldnÃÂt see any smoke. The smoke detector did not activate. 
I traced the odor to the dishwasher, which was still running. I stopped the cycle by opening the dishwasher door. The smell was not very strong inside the dishwasher but outside of it toward the floor. By that time my head was pounding and the smoke smell had increased. I opened windows for fresh air, and waited next to the dishwasher with a fire extinguisher. The smell gradually dissipated but not completely until the next day. Several hours later, my husband pulled the machine from the cavity and removed the lower panel. He found a damaged power cord which had burned at the point where the junction box combines the cord to the machine wiring. He replaced the cord with  a new one purchased from Home Depot, and scraped away most of the burned bits. Although the  dishwasher works now, we will not use it unless we are in the same room so that we can take action in case of another fire
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and caused physical symptoms (headache), but no serious injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While drinking a smoothie I made with our Ninja Blender, I bit down on something hard that turned out to be half of a metal ring. After investigating, the piece of metal broke off from a washer that is a part of the blade in our blender.
justification: The incident involved biting on a metal piece, which could cause injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I had some tamales steaming on the stove in a covered pan. My mother-in-law and I were in the living room and the fan to the microwave/range hood turned on without anyone in the kitchen! I went over and turned it off and on a couple of times to "test" it. I left it off and was keeping a eye on it. Approximately 3 hours later it started beeping like buttons were being pushed, again no one was in the kitchen. At that point do to fear of fire we shut off the breaker to that section of our house. As a fire investigator this is very scary. I called GE there is no recalls on this product yet. It was made June 2012 so it is not very old for a built in appliance
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with potential fire risk, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I used a Pyrex glass roasting pan that I purchased in October, 2017.  I roasted a beef roast at 325 degrees F.  I then used the pan on an electric stove top to make gravy.  I poured the gravy in a gravy boat and placed the Pyrex pan on a cool burner on the stove top.  The pan exploded 30 seconds later sending shards of glass everywhere.
Please pull Pyrex cookware from the market.
Thank you.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex pan, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
In 2016, I purchased a Samsung kitchen product, refrigerator with built in ice maker, Samsung model number RS25J500DSR. 
A few months later, as I was dispensing ice, the plastic ice bucket/dispenser shattered, leaving a mess of ice and plastic shards in the freezer compartment.

I replaced the ice bucket. 6 months later, it shattered again. More mess of ice and sharp plastic shards. 

Yesterday, November 8, 2017, it happened again with the same sharp shards and ice. 

My concern is that Samsung was very clear that this was just MY problem. No help at all.

My other concern is that if I had young children, dispensing their own ice water, they could have ingested the water and swallowed the sharp plastic shards. 

Samsung needs to be forced to man-up and replace all of these refrigerators/ ice makers without delay.
justification: The incident involves repeated shattering of the ice bucket, posing a risk of injury from sharp plastic shards, though no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I was baking yams in the largest pan. After I took the pan out of the oven and set it on top of the oven, it exploded. Shards of glass scattered all over the kitchen, as far as seven feet away. I am very lucky that I wasn't hurt and especially lucky that a shard of glass didn't end up in my eye! I used the product the way it is supposed to be used. I had it for about four years and hadn't had problems before this. It was the largest pan of this set: Pyrex Easy Grab 8-Piece Glass Bakeware and Food Storage Set.
justification: The incident involved an exploding pan causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she was only using the timer on her over the range microwave and it caught fire.  She stated that the flames started to emanate from the interior of the plastic part of the unit after the unit was placed on timer for 30 mins and then another 5 mins, the incident occurred during the last 5mins of the timer.  She stated that her neighbor removed the flaming plastic part and placed a wet towel on it to contain the fire.

The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that it was not included in a recall and to report it to the agency.

Consumer feels that this microwave is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported, and the fire was contained without further damage.

incident_description: I purchased new Thermador Model: PRL304GH, which is their 30 in Pro Harmony Range. I am concern there is safety and potential burn and fire hazards. Since they claim it meets safety standards, I am not entitled to a refund. The company representative explains it is safe for the back of the stove to heat up 25 degrees hotter than the temperature (e.g. Oven bake 500 degree = back of stove 525 degrees.) When cooking in the oven over 300 degrees, the knobs become hot to touch. Also, I am concerned about the fire hazard. Even when the installation instructions are followed, how can the back of the stove  heating up to over 525 degrees be safe when wood ignites at 525 degrees, [REDACTED] cement board is safe only to 200 degrees, and Drywall at 125 degrees? I am concern my new wood cabinets will become igitner wood, and the walls behind the stove pose safety hazard. Also, the electronic panel is between the oven and stove top, which appears to be a safety electrical hazard with the intense heat too. I do not understand how this is a safe exterior stove operating temperature for residential use. Also, I do not see how this meets safety product codes when whole stove is hot, including the knobs to touch. This is a concern in household uses for children and people with sensory deficits.
justification: The description raises concerns about potential burn and fire hazards, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: We bought a Fridgidaire Fridge on 4/25/16.  Today I was washing the lowest glass shelf that has the vegetable and fruit drawers underneath it.  I took the glass shelf out of the fridge and was washing it in the sink in warm soapy water.  The glass shelf exploded.  I use the word exploded because that is exactly what happened.  It shattered in thousands of tiny pieces in the sink, countertops, and floor.  I am so thankful I had shoes on and that no children were around.  I'm 43 years old and have washed glass shelves from fridges many, many times and never has a shelf shattered on me.  This glass shelf is not safe to be in a fridge.  It's dangerous.
justification: The glass shelf exploded but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Running dishwasher at 8:30 am on 10/23/2017. Electrical fire started in wiring on the lower right side of the washer door. Destroyed dishwasher, burned kitchen cabinets and cracked granite counter from the excessive heat. This was a Bosch shu43c07uc/14 model that was purchased in 2003. Was also subject to a fire hazard recall in 2009. We had the washer supposedly fixed relative to the recall at that time but the unit  went up in flames on 10/23/2017.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire causing significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire wall oven outer glass shattered while baking.
While baking we heard a large pop like noise.....upon investigation we found the oven outer glass shattered in to thousands of pieces.

No one was directly in front of the oven at the time of the breakage and there were no injuries.

We tried about a dozen parts stores to buy a new replacement glass ....however we were told the glass is not available and we would have to replace the entire door.

We inquired about door replacement and was told the part would cost over $200.00 if it was available however, the part was out of stock at the manufactures level and is not being manufactured any longer. We continued to search globally for replacement parts however none could be found.
We also tried to purchase glass at local glass vendors but they were not able to provide the special type of glass needed

We wound up replacing the complete oven at a expense to us of $2394.96. Clearly there is something wrong with this picture. In addition to this being a safety issue we were forced to replace the complete oven due to the manufacturer not able to supply parts for this unit.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured, and the incident required a full oven replacement due to unavailable parts.

incident_description: Oven will not turn off. Had to go to the electrical panel and turn it off there. When you flip the panel switch back on the oven goes back on. This is NOT good!
justification: The oven malfunction poses a risk but no injury occurred; the issue is possible to recur without intervention.

incident_description:
OVENS THAT DON'T TURN OFF

Kitchen Aid KGRK806PSS00 will not turn off

The problem with the Kitcheaid Switch Membrane is well known by the manufacture but so far they refuse to recall or redesign the part.  It is very common for the OFF BUTTON to stop funtioning on both the gas and electric stoves that have this part.

This is a serious safety issue, and Whirlpool / Kitchenaid should come forward and recall the item and replace it with a working one.
justification: The description indicates a known issue with ovens not turning off, which is a safety concern but does not mention any injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Gas Stove/Oven knobs on 30" LG Gas Oven/Range was leaking natural gas at night.  My wife woke to the smell of natural gas smell and immediately knew it was the stove.  The knobs are so sensitive that just brushing against them will engage the natural gas even if the igniter isn't triggered.  This has occurred many time when working or cleaning in the kitchen but had never gone unnoticed until now.  

These knobs should be recalled and have some sort of pressure lock where you need to press the knobs in to turn them on, not just turn them.  Electric ranges have these and I'm very surprised the gas ones do not.  

This is a very unsafe product, especially if you have young children, pets or simply have a lot of traffic through your kitchen.  LG customer service has of course tried to state that their produce meets or exceeds all standards, but apparently none of them use their own products at home.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to sensitive knobs, posing a risk but no injury occurred. The likelihood is high as it has happened multiple times unnoticed.

incident_description: The dishwasher keeps leaking all over the floor from when we first got it.  It is about 2 years old.  It keeps backing up and has dirty water stuck in the bottom.  It keeps giving error messages.  About a month ago, it got so hot (builtin), it buckled the strip of granite on the countertop and it cracked. (We have Granite Transformations).  Yesterday, it gave another error code and just now an "LE".  It was extremely hot so I turned it off.  Found out online, that it can catch on fire.
justification: The dishwasher has caused property damage (cracked granite) and poses a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description: Purchased a KitchenAid 10/12 cup coffee maker. Model KCM111, serial # WF70919498. When pouring coffee into a cup, scalding steam came up through the opening where the cover is attached to the handle and burned my hand. Thankfully not a serious injury, but still painful. Sent email complaint to manufacturer, when response implied that this was not a "common occurrence" I felt the issue would not get the investigation it needed. I wanted to make sure a "watchdog" group would be made aware of this.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful burn injury, but not serious. The manufacturer's response suggests it is not a common occurrence.

incident_description: oven racks on Sears Kenmore double oven model 790.47773406, serial # 84323983 fall down and have been doing so for the last two years
justification: The oven racks falling down is an incident but there is no mention of injury, so severity is 2. The issue has been ongoing for two years, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I was cooking chicken, rice and vegetables in my crock pot on high heat for 6 hours as recipe indicates. It has about 10 minutes left I was looking over the crock pot to see in when the lid exploded in my face. The center of the lid blew out and sent glass flying into my face, hair all over my counter and floor as well is into the food. There were small and large pieces of glass everywhere. We spent several hours trying to clean up all the little pieces of glass as well as pick a piece of glass out of my hand. We have pictures as well as the crock pot this was only the second time it was used. There was over $80. In food in the crocknpot that had to thrown in the trash
justification: The incident resulted in injury (glass in the hand) and significant property damage (exploded crock pot and ruined food).

incident_description: Bought a new Toastmaster griddle. Using it for the first time. Noticed one side wasn't cooking the food. Turned it up a half notch. Started to smell something awful burning. Thought it must be the cord. Unplugged it. Smell was getting stronger. Crouched down to look under the hot griddle and saw the heating element sitting directly on the quartz countertop burning it. It had not been attached to the unit. It was redhot and smoking. After we moved it and turned it over the heating element was burned through and white powder and pieces of the cable heating element were all over.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning griddle causing property damage (burned countertop), but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We had a house fire due to a faulty design in the knobs on our Samsung 30" Slide-in Double Oven Flex Range model NE58K9850WG.

I came home from grocery shopping put my grocery bags on the counter and walked out of the kitchen. Within just a few minutes I heard a noise of something crashing and thought it was my son in the den down one level. As I got up to check on him, I heard more crashing and discovered ceiling tiles and spice racks crashing to the floor as my stove was on fire along with the microwave and cabinets around the stove.

The fire destroyed our kitchen but luckily we were home and able to locate our fire extinguisher and put the blaze out.  When ServPro was working to restore our kitchen, cleaning up and removing items twice more the stove turned on starting a second fire.

The insurance and Samsung technician examining the stove both agreed the knobs turned too easily without much effort and that it was possible that I bummed the knob when putting my groceries down. Than the ServPro team likewise bumped it twice turning it on starting the second fire.  They need to redesign the knobs so more force is required to push the knob in before turning. They also need to add a lock feature to the knobs in addition to the one for the oven.

We lost a pet Bengal due to complications from smoke inhalation.
justification: The fire caused significant property damage and resulted in the death of a pet due to smoke inhalation, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is possible, as the incident happened once but could recur due to the faulty knob design.

incident_description: t-fal C112SC Signature large size glass pot lid exploded & shattered! Loud noise & Glass all over my kitchen! I bought this set a year ago. I've had this same set of Signature pots & pans befor before & used it for many years with no problem. What's going on! Scary & dangerous! I'm going to share this in a review on Amazon where I bought it. Time to switch back to metal lids. My cat was next to me when it happened & he freaked out & ran across the room. I'm stil shocked!
justification: The incident involved a pot lid exploding and shattering, causing a loud noise and glass debris, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Approximately 9 pm, on October 23rd, we noticed a burning smell coming from the kitchen. We quickly went to see what was potentially on fire. After going into the kitchen, we could see light smoke coming from around the dishwasher. We turned it off, and opened the door. Upon inspection, the heating element inside of the dishwasher had apparently overheated and warped down touching and burning the plastic tub. Their was still some water present in the on the surface of the tub. Had there not been, by the look of the plastic, it could have ignited the plastic tub risking the loss of our property and potential life. After a brief search online, It appears that this is a known problem with similar models. After Inspecting the product, and for consumer safety and protection, it needs to be reviewed and recalled. The potential risk to property and life merits a review of this product and the dangers associated with it. I have notified the manufacture of this risk, and will document my reporting this incident.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and light smoke from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred. The potential for property damage and life risk was noted, but not realized in this instance.

incident_description: I used my Crate and Barrel Rabbit Style wine opener to open a bottle of wine on Sunday, October 22, 2017.  this involves pushing down and pulling back the lever.  The push down inserts the screw, the pull back removes the cork.  As I was finishing the pull back the lever fractured in my hand, and the broken lever lacerated the lower joint of my thumb, which bled profusely.  I staunched the bleeding with normal first aid procedures but it was a painful wound which could have been dangerous given the profusion of arteries and nerves in that part of the body.  On 10 23, I reported the incident to Crate&Barrel's customer service website and got a reply asking me for order details.  I replied that it was a gift and could not supply them.  C&B replied on 10/24 they couldn't help me without the order details.  On 10/24 I replied that I considered this a product defect and asked them to forward our exchange to their legal department.  I haven't heard back.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful laceration that required first aid, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such product failures are not common.

incident_description:
Samsung Refrigerator Model RF30HBEDBSR serial 06p043bf701009w

Ice maker "exploded". The ice contained 4 sharp metal objects and 4 or 5 plastic nuts (washers?) These were presumably part of the mechanism.

This has been reported to Samsung. Awaiting response.
justification: The incident involved an ice maker explosion with metal and plastic parts, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: KitchenAid Gas Range - turned on by itself. Electrical control panel glitch where we couldn't turn it off. Had to cut power to the range.
justification: The incident involved a gas range turning on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I decided to test my dinner dishes for lead in the glaze and bought a test kit from the hardware store.  The dishes tested strongly positive.  I bought a different kit and retested - still positive.

The dishes are made by the Lynn Chase Foundation and are an active pattern manufactured abroad, but I do not know where.  They are sold by Neiman-Marcus, Scully and Scully and perhaps other high-end retailers.  The design name is Jaguar Jungle. 

The dishes are very beautiful and are expensive.  I notified both retailers and the Lynn Chase Foundation.  I got a response from Scully and Scully telling me that Lynn Chase had informed them that their dishes were all tested before importation and were safe.  None of them actually responded to my issue and essentially ignored my concerns.

Based on the positivity of my tests at home, I do not feel these dishes are safe and would like you to know about this.  I understand colorful glazes often have lead, but I think the public should be warned when the glaze is on a dish someone will eat from.  

Do you have an opinion re this?  Am I being over-concerned?  I did also test some old dishes I have from the 1960s (American) and they were also positive.  Dishes I have from Italy and Tunisia (not vintage) were negative. One from France (vintage) was positive.  Other American ones are also positive, but vintage (Bauer and Fiesta).
justification: The incident involves potential lead exposure from dishes, but no actual injury or death is reported. The likelihood is possible as lead in dishware is a known issue, especially with vintage or imported items.

incident_description: I purchased an Oster toaster/convection oven about 6 months ago.  I made toast yesterday, and shut the unit off.  The timer dinged and the power light went off.   When I went back into the kitchen 15 minutes later, walked by the oven and felt heat.  The timer dial had rotated to "Stay On" and the unit had turned itself on.  I could hear faint ticking of the timer. Turned toaster oven back on for 5 min., watched lower knob, it shut the unit off, yet continued to tick, it moved the knob to stay on and turned the unit back on.  I notified Oster via online yesterday.  their response was that "they would contact me within 3 days".
justification: The toaster oven malfunctioned by turning itself back on, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I have a Whirpool Gas Sealed Burner Cooktop (Model: GLT3057). My wife used the cooktop on Saturday afternoon, July 22, 2017. After she had turned off the burner, the igniter in the cooktop started clicking automatically. She checked the knobs to ensure that they were properly turned to "off," which they were, however, the igniter continued to click. After about 15 seconds of this, sparks started emitting from one of the igniter knobs and made popping sounds. Then, flames started emitting from the knob. After a few seconds, the flames and sparks stopped, the igniter stopped clicking, and smoke started to rise out of the knob. It also had the smell of burnt plastic. She then immediately turned off the gas to the cooktop, unplugged the electrical component, and haven't touched it since.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks from the cooktop, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My GE Profile dishwasher has always seemed to be extremely hot -burning up plastics that were supposed to be dishwasher safe and the upper rack has burned up many of the posts until they fall off -black!  I cannot find where my particular model of dishwasher has been recalled, however I see many of different model numbers that have been recalled for the same issue of overheating! I have had to purchase (over $150!) a new upper rack and am starting to be concerned about the new rack burning up as well or my house catching fire possibly. Do I have ANY recourse for this matter?  My dishwasher was installed in my new home in 2008 and has had this issue from the beginning.
justification: The dishwasher's overheating has caused damage to plastic items and the upper rack, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: The samsung oven is a major fire hazard. The burners are able to turn on very easily by just lightly bumping them. I came down last night before I went to bed to find the front burner and bridge burner on high and it was very hot in my kitchen. I am constantly bumping into the knobs and the burners turn on. I finally this morning took the knobs off. This is a severe fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard with burners turning on easily, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Was heating a cup of water in the microwave and it lost all power and stopped working.  When I opened the microwave door, sparks came out of the door lock openings.  I had a person check the house electrical connections and those are working fine.  The microwave is not working at all and I have it unplugged to make sure it does not cause a fire.
justification: The incident involved sparks and microwave malfunction but no injury or death occurred, and the microwave was unplugged to prevent further issues.

incident_description: On Tuesday October 24, 2017 I had a fire at my home which was apparently caused by a faulty whirlpool electric stove. Approximately 2 weeks prior I noticed that the top right eye was on but the stove was not in uses. I took me 3-4 times to turn the switch on and off to finally get the eye turned off. Then on another occasion I was sitting in my nook which is adjacent to the kitchen where the stove was located and my wife asked me if I had turned on the cooking eye to the right front of the stove. I told her I didn't and I turned the switch on then off and the stove went off. Then on Tuesday October 24, 2017 I was in another room and smelled something cooking or burning. I walked toward the kitchen and observed a pot on the stove in flames. I immediately went to the stove pushed the pot off the left eye then attempted to shut it off but it was in an off position. I then reached down to the plug and pulled it out of the wall outlet.The fire resulted in the local fire department to respond and subsequently put out the fire. My family and I did not received and injuries other than minor smoke inhalation. I have searched the internet for other instances similar and found a few in which whirlpool stoves have come on by themselves
justification: The incident resulted in a fire and minor smoke inhalation, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurring issue with the stove suggests a possible likelihood (3) of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that her oven racks have become warped causing the contents to burn user when it is in use.  The racks being uneven creates a safety hazard.  She stated that she was using the oven when the shelf collapsed and the food contents burnt her arms, first aid was administered.


Consumer stated that she noticed this defect about 6 months ago, however, the incident occurred  approximately 1 month ago.

(5/26/17) The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that there would be a service charge for examining the unit.
justification: The incident resulted in burns requiring first aid, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Glass shattered on oven door on Kenmore 790 electric range. This is the second time this has occured. The oven was not in use. Previous incident was October 2016.
justification: Glass shattered on the oven door, but no injury was reported. This is the second occurrence in several years.

incident_description: I was cooking a pizza in my Kenmore Electric Range 790.46789902 with the temperature at 425F. I went to open the oven door to take the pizza out, and felt the handle give more than it should. I saw the left side of the handle had come separated from the door where the screw was. As I pulled a little more, the entire front panel of glass on the oven exploded. It burned and cut my skin and clothes, as well as the floor where it fell. When my dog heard the explosion, he came running and stepped on the glass, cutting his feet as well. None of the injuries resulted in a trip to the doctor or hospital, but it could have been a lot worse.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and cuts to the person and their dog, but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the oven handle failure and subsequent glass explosion.

incident_description: Frigidaire Gallery side by side refrigerator/freezer, model PLRS267AZ B6 purchased 6/5/2002.  Refrigerator side had stopped cooling recently (temperature regulation was off).  Unusual noises had been noticed for a few weeks.  While cleaning out the refrigerator, it was found that plastic trim from the backside of the bottom glass tray had become dislodged and fallen into an opening in the left side of the refrigerator (left side when facing the refrigerator) towards the bottom of the box.  This opening is designed to facilitate airflow from the freezer which cools the refrigerator side.  Because all the drawers and shelf items were in the refrigerator, this hole and the trim that fell into it could not be seen until we began cleaning.  It was found that the end of the trim was melted and charred so it may have come in contact with electronics in the refrigerator or the condenser fan.  This is clearly a fire hazard and we are fortunate the refrigerator did not catch on fire.  This could certainly explain why the refrigerator side of the unit was not cooling properly.  While this is probably a rare occurrence, it still seems that this vent/hole should have had some kind of screen over it to prevent things falling into it.  What if a jar or other container had fallen in?  Or liquids leaked into it?  Either way, it was a very dangerous situation that could have led to property damage or loss of life due to fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, and the description suggests it is a rare occurrence.

incident_description:
My wife was using the Black & Decker toaster oven to toast a piece of bread. She assumed the toaster would stop when the toast was done. It failed to stop, and kept toasting. Eventually, the bread caught fire. Luckily, our nanny discovered it, and was able to unplug the toaster oven and stop the fire.

This model has a 'toast' timer knob with a poor design, insofar as it must be turned past the 4 minute mark and then back down, if the desired time is less than 4 minutes. There is mention of this in the manual, and in extremely small type on the face of the toaster. However, the type on the face is easy to miss, particularly for an appliance that should be as easy to operate as a toaster--my wife said she never knew that was required. (And how often will consumers fail to read the whole manual?)

This poor design and poor notice might not be so serious if, as I assumed, the consequence of failing to turn the knob past 4 minutes were that the unit would simply fail to activate, or perhaps that the time of operation would not precisely match the desired time. For the consequence to be that the unit toasts indefinitely seems a serious fire hazard. This seems all the more likely to cause problems given that most items only need to toast 2-3 minutes (in my experience, 2 for a piece of toast, 3 for an english muffin). 

In other words, consumers may be exposed to this potential hazard every time they are engaged in the most common use of the product--toasting bread or an english muffin for 2-3 minutes.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a design flaw, but no injury or death occurred as the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description: I was using my Cuisinart SmartPower Premier Blender Model #CBT-500W (TX)/CBT-500WC (TX) to make pesto.  I briefly heard a strange noise while using the blender but since it promptly went away, I didn't think anything of it.  A few minutes later when I was pouring the pesto out of the blender and into a container, I saw a white chunk of something.  I thought it was an unprocessed clove of garlic and almost dismissed it.  I decided to fish it out and discovered it was a piece of the white plastic that houses the blades.
justification: A piece of the blender's plastic housing broke off, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I have used this appliance for about 2 or 3 years. Last week while opening my canned corn some metal pieces shaved off. I went ahead and poured from the can thinking I could avoid getting any metal in my dish. However later when I opened one more can I cut my finger so decided to throw out the entire dish I was making. However, I had given part of it to friends and they ate it before I warned them to throw it out. They know to let me know if they have stomach or bowel problems. Needless to say I am worried about them. I saved 3 of the cans I opened for inspection if needed. It is a Hamilton Beach  model # 76606.  I think it needs to be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger and potential ingestion of metal shavings, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue occurred with multiple cans.

incident_description:
when oven or broiler is on the handles to pilots get very hot, so hot the top of stove melted our
tea pot.  When oven is on cannot touch the knobs which are on the front of stove cannot be touched without pot holders.  Very dangerous we have burnt our fingers.

Purchased the Frigidaire, propane gas range.  
Model # FGGF3054MFJ    Serial # VF45197214  was purchased from Home Depot 2015

Since purchased
justification: The description reports burns from touching hot stove knobs, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue is described as recurring when the oven is in use, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
While using a Power Cooker Pressure Cooker as called for by the instructions the top exploded off and I received
substantial second degree burns to my arm and chest. As a result of my injuries. I have suffered scarring and had to
receive medical care, and have incurred medical bills.
justification: The incident resulted in substantial second-degree burns requiring medical care, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I got an electric shock when I touched the front edge of the range. I found that an electrical connector (1/4" pushon
spade connector) to one of the heating elements had deteriorated after a long time of overheating and the connector disintegrated. A small pile of ash had accumulated in the stove under the connection from the burned away wire insulation. Then the wire came loose from the element and fell against the metal body of the range ... thereby electifying the entire range. Further inspection found another heating element's wire creatign anothe rash pile and ready to fail the same way. Then I found out that GE had already recalled a number of their ranges for this same problem ... but not this model. GE says this 2010 range (model JB640D) is out of warranty and not repairable and is only offering to give me a discount if I buy a new range from them.
Since this problem is happening two times in this one range and they have a history of similar failures with other models that are constructed the same way, I suspect this will be a big safety concern as this model ages.
justification: The incident resulted in an electric shock, indicating an injury, and the description notes a history of similar failures, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I bought a Bella M-60B23G 6qt pressure cooker and the second time using it. The unit gave an error code of E2 so I left the room for literally 5 minutes to get the user manual. When I came back in I smelled a weird chemical smell and looked at the pressure cooker. It was melting! The bottom was smoking so I flipped it over (the lid was removed at the time) to find the bottom black plastic melting. After flipping it over I was looking at the bottom  and I noticed more smoke coming from the other side. The inside metal (aloy aluminum I assume) melted and dripped onto my countertop, which melted a burn into my countertop from the dripping metal coming into contact with my countertop. My countertop is a composit material and the spot left is a discoloration that felt bumpy as the top layer of the counter was burnt through. Good thing I was able to recognize there was something wrong early or it most likely would have caught fire. I am in the process of contacting the company. I bought this item from Target.
justification: The pressure cooker malfunctioned, causing melting and smoke, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Ran a load through the dishwasher and when I opened it up, the spray arm was partially out of the bottom of the dishwasher, and the plastic was melted.  This, to me, is a fire hazard.  My son had the same thing happen to him with his Fridgidaire dishwasher.  These dishwashers should have to be replaced no matter when purchased or no matter if a person is the original purchaser or not.  VERY DANGEROUS!!
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard with no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The mention of a similar incident suggests the likelihood is possible, warranting a 3.

incident_description: When top oven set at 425 for baking a pizza - explosion heard and glass inside glass exploded everywhere in mammoth pieces - also appears element break
justification: The incident involved an oven explosion with glass shattering, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Frigidaire Flat top electric range serial # VF24675911 control panel burst into flames. there was no warning or smell, it just caught fire in the control section.
justification: The control panel burst into flames without warning, indicating a significant incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our Frigidaire smooth top electric stove was off. There was a plastic bag and a business card on top of the stove. I was in another room asleep. I woke up to smell plastic burning. Got up and found the stove element lit up. The plastic bag melting and smoking severely, and the card on fire. I went to turn the knob but found it was off. I turned it anyway. No position would turn off the burner. I put out the fire and moved the plastic. Which burned the tip of my finger. I moved the hot stove to pull the 220volt plug. It arced when I pulled it from the wall. The stove finally turned off. I was Left with a house full of smoke and burned plastic smell throughout. Minor burn from the plastic on my finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn injury and significant property damage, but no death or severe injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it involves a rare malfunction of the stove.

incident_description:
A fire started in the heating element of a Kitchen Aid electric range oven.  Shortly after turning the oven on, a buzzing electrical type sound was heard and then a small flame was seen on the heating element in the oven.  The oven was turned off and the flame extinguished.  

After the incident, the consumer saw that the heating element appeared to have been welded in four places and the fire came from one of those weld points.  The consumer was concerned the heating element had been broken prior to his purchase of the range 7-8 years ago, and it had been poorly welded back together for sale.
justification: A fire occurred but was quickly extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove top and a tripped breaker, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer has a safety concern about the knobs on her LG range.

(08/03/2017) The consumer stated that she was reaching for a spice in the cabinet about the stove. Her hip accidently touched the knob. The burner came. Another time she was in the kitchen and there was a pan of hot oil on the back burner. The consumer brushed up against the knob and the back burner came on causing the oil to start burning.

The consumer stated that she also laid a spoon on the burner. When she smelled the burning spoon, she realized that she had turned the knob on accidentally.

The consumer also stated that the burners are too close together.

The consumer stated that she normally keeps the oven open when broiling meringue. This stove does not allow her to do so.

incident_description: On 10/12/17 my daughter was wiping the front cover of the dishwasher, as she swiped across the bottom of the dishwasher it sliced open her finger severely, and required emergency treatment including stitches and surgical glue to close the wound. The stainless steel wraps under the front door, but has a raw edge that is extremely sharp.

incident_description: The serving wear set was being used to cut a birthday cake at a birthday party. The cake was a typical birthday cake with no hard fillings or other obstacles. The handle of the knife easily snapped off at the ceramic base. This was the FIRST time we had used the serving wear set. As the handle snapped from the base of the knife, it slipped in my husband's hand, lacerating his palm and thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration to the palm and thumb, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:

incident_description: This LG electric range has controls that, when accidentally bumped, turn on the stove top heating elements. I have noticed on a few occasions the heating element was on after my wife or a guest have brushed up against the knobs and was able to catch it quickly.  Recently I was not so lucky, my wife brushed up against one of the knobs prior to taking my dog for a walk and came back to my house filled with smoke. On top of my stove was a bag of cheese that melted and the smoke carried the oils from the cheese to my ceiling that has to be professionally replaced.  I highly recommend not buying this stove. I can't imagine having a stove like this with young children in my home.  My wife has removed knobs to avoid incidental contact.

incident_description: Cleaned top oven successfully.  Waited several hours and started cleaning bottom oven.  After several minutes the glass in the door shattered.
justification: The glass in the oven door shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using our glass top oven/cooktop. I had 2 burners on and the oven on. After I had these on for about 30 minutes I heard a pop from the rear of the unit. I then saw flames coming from the back of the electrical panel on the top of the oven. I pulled the oven out, unplugged it and put the fire out with a towel.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly controlled without injury.

incident_description: I was preparing to make carrot cake, when I was almost done with mixing the ingredients, turned on the oven picked BAKE then I put it on 350F, closed the door of the oven. I was finishing up with mixing the last ingredients of the cake all the sudden I jumped away scared and terrified from a boom sound of the glass explosion, my 19 months old son was close to the oven since it was placed on top of the counter, he started screaming and crying after what happened. justification: The incident resulted in a glass shard entering the child's eye, causing injury and distress, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Dualit 2 slice chrome toaster ASIN # B00009NROG ÃÂ fire risk

There is a fire risk with this toaster and it should be recalled. Interestingly, the manufacturer is aware of the risk and has taken inadequate steps to address the issue. The problem occurs when the built in timer malfunctions and sticks which causes the toaster to remain powered on constantly. This poses an obvious fire risk although I did not experience a fire and no injuries were caused. The problem with my toaster occurred in May 2017 ÃÂ the product was purchased in October 2014. A replacement part is easy to find online as are numerous reports of premature failure of timers and concerns about potential fire risk. Interestingly the replacement part has a warning of fire risk on the knob ÃÂ ÃÂUnplug after use ÃÂ fire riskÃÂ that was not on the original part - see photos below of new and original knob. This shows that manufacturer is aware of the issue. But this warning is inadequate as it is totally impractical in any busy household to unplug a toaster every time it is used. Also, by the time you purchase a replacement your original timer without the warning will have failed exposing you to fire risk. This product needs to be recalled and the timer redesigned with a built in fail safe so that if it sticks it powers down automatically.
justification: The description mentions a fire risk but no actual fire or injury occurred, and the issue is known to occur frequently based on reports.

incident_description:
Roasted vegetables in brand- new Kitchen Aid Dual Fuel range using convection roast function at 475 degrees.  After completing oven cooking, turned oven off.   Excessive steam from a vent under cooktop front panel caused burner control knob on front panel to become excessively hot and unusable.  We called for a service technician through Kam Appliances from whom we had purchased new oven.  Service technician was able to replicate issue and measured knob temperature to be as high as 170 degrees.  Kitchen aid was notified by technician and, reportedly, was told that "oven is operating as designed" and that they are aware that the knob may actually become as hot as 190 degrees.  Consumer was told to wear oven mitt when using hot dial.  Kitchen Aid also sent technician new knobs which did not fit and were useless. 

As an elderly person with grand children, I am concerned about safety and, if I use the oven, can not turn it off if I am cooking something on the stove top.   Only after completing my stove-top cooking, can I turn off the oven knowing that the heat coming from that vent can cause potential harm when standing near that vent.  This is an unsafe range.
justification: The incident involves excessive heat from the oven vent making the control knob dangerously hot, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
The product is a Samsung Electric Range Model NE58F9500SS -  Slide in range with knobs and LED control panel on front of range. Though the instruction manual indicates you are to push the knob in to turn on the element, the outer most knobs turn on with little effort i.e., you brush against the knob while reaching for something in an upper cabinet and the range turns on.
We've experienced the above several times and had a contractor back into the knob while working in the kitchen, also resulting in unknowingly turning the cook surface on. It's not a stretch to be concerned that a child or pet could also easily activate the range. When the cook surface is turned on it does not issue a warning beep. A small "hot surface" indicator on the cook surface is the only indication that the cook top is on. The instruction manual does include the warning, "Do not lean on the range as you may turn the control knobs inattentively.", however it takes minimal contact for the cook top to be turned on. To avoid accidentally turning the cook surface on, we've removed the knobs.
justification: The incident describes repeated unintentional activation of the cook surface, posing a risk of burns, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description:
(09/16/2017) The consumer stated that if the knob is bumped a little bit, gas is released in the house. The ignition should be on just before the gas is turned on, but this did not happened. The consumer was making a pizza so he did not smell the gas initially. 

The consumer called the fire department who came and pulled the stove from the wall. They tightened the fitting behind the stove because there was an undetectable gas leak.
justification: Gas leak occurred but was detected and addressed without injury, fitting the 'Incident, No Injury' severity level.

incident_description:
(09/11/2017) The submitter stated that her daughter turned the stove on to 300 degrees. Within five to ten minutes there was a terrible gas smell. 

(09/11/2017) The consumer called GE. She was advised that there was nothing that could be done because it was the end of the day.

The consumer called ConED. They came out right away. They detected a gas leak in the stove. The stove was tagged by ConED.

(09/12/2017) The firm was called. The consumer was advised to turn the stove on so that the problem could be detected when the technician got to the home. The consumer stated that they could not stay in the house because of the smell.

(09/19/2017) A technician came out to check the stove. He was able to detect the gas leak. Parts were going to be sent out but they were the wrong parts. The correct parts for the stove was unavailable.

The consumer asked GE to replace or remove the stove but was advised that they can only try to repair the product. 

All family members were affected by the gas smell.
justification: All family members were affected by the gas smell, indicating potential health impacts.

incident_description: KitchenAid Microwave model KHMS147HSS started with NO USER INPUT and was running by itself! We cannot get the Microwave to turn off!! We have to leave the Door open! As soon as we close the door it turns on. We have reset the breaker - killed all power to it, but as soon as we turn the breaker on, the microwave starts!
justification: The microwave operates without user input, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I have a General Electric Refrigerator Model GSH22JGDD BB that has a Componx Inc. Ice Maker  Model #-197D2303G080.  I dispensed ice cubes from the door and added water. I drank from the glass and a piece of plastic went down my throat. I looked in the glass and there were other shards of thick plastic indistinguishable from ice. I looked in automatic ice maker and the plastic screw that moves the ice was made of the thick plastic and there were other shards that had broken off the screw. I rushed to the emergency room at Mercy Hospital in St. Louis on Ballas Road and the doctor tried to remove the shard but was unsuccessful. He told me to return home and hopefully it would pass through my system. It had been two weeks and I assume I have successfully passed the broken piece of the plastic screw.
justification: The individual ingested a plastic shard, required emergency medical attention, and experienced ongoing concern for two weeks, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The front large burner of my electric stove would not go down in temp when I tried to turn knob from High to  lower temperature.    It stayed on high and the cook top became very hot.  A plastic spoon on the top even became too hot to pick up.  This is not only dangerous because of the burn hazard, (grease spattered and water spattered the second time this happened). but also a fire hazard exists.  I also observed that there was a snapping noise on the control panel where that switch is located.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove burner that poses a burn and fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While using our two year old Bosch 500 series dishwasher the electrical junction box provided started on fire.  Luckily it popped the circuit breaker and we were home and able to contain the situation.  Did some research online and found that Bosch has a recall on these boxes but not for my particular model.  Found numerous examples for my model that we're having the same problem. In almost all examples it is the common white wire in the connections that start the connection box on fire.  I contacted Bosch they agreed to have someone come out and diagnose the problem at their cost but all repairs for the dishwasher would be at my cost. They contend that the junction box is not part of the dishwasher it is part of the installation, even though they provide the connection box with their dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the junction box but was contained without injury, and similar issues are reported frequently for this model.

incident_description: I recently purchased an electric LG range/cooktop.  The knobs on the cooktopare angled and too easy to accidentally turn on simply by leaning into the front of the stove.  I have accidentally turned it on over one dozen times for months now.   I called the company to report the problem and they advised I purchase child safety guards for the knobs, so they are well aware of the defect.  I have read several other reviews that report the same problem.
justification: The incident involves accidental activation of the cooktop, which poses a burn or fire hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My 9x13 Pyrex dish exploded 10/8/17 when I attempted to take it out of our dishwasher.  It had run its cycle the night before and was no longer hot, my dish had a handle on edge and I just grabbed it and pulled and immediately it exploded shards everywhere spanning a 3-5 foot radius.  I screamed for my husbAnd to secure dogs and kids and clean me a way out as I was barefoot and my right arm had 6 bleeding spots and my left hand had a shard centered in the middle superficially but painful.   This is beyond unacceptable I keep picturing what would have happened if my daughter (5) had been standing next to me.  I spoke to pyrex who is replacing dish (with a metal one) and is giving me $50 credit towards purchase on their website.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple bleeding injuries from glass shards, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but do occur.

incident_description:
On August 3, 2017, I got up in the middle of night and found my stove burner on, despite not having cooked dinner that night. It was a curious event but I didnÃÂt think think much of it just continued to check it whenever I left and before bed to be cautious.
On September 14, 2017, I was at a doctorÃÂs appointment and was alerted of a fire at my home. A fire investigation concluded with the determination that the the stoveÃÂs dial was turned to approximately 11 oÃÂclock position on the same burner that had previously had issues. The stove had not been used for almost a couple hours at the time of the fire and was not on when I left the house (I had checked all knobs and touched the burners before leaving because of what had happened the month before). The house was a loss and is uninhabitable until it is rebuilt and seven pets died from smoke inhalation and temperature.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of seven pets and the house being uninhabitable, indicating a severity level of 4 (Death). The occurrence likelihood is considered possible (3) given the previous unexplained burner issue.

incident_description: We found a small bit of broken food processor blade in food that had been processed. Close inspection of the blade showed that in fact two pieces of metal had broken off the blade. Each broken piece was from near a rivet in the blade. The food processor was a Cuisinart, model DLC-5 TX (Type 25), serial 51020EK. We discarded the broken blade.

incident_description:
I set my Kenmore 790 electric range oven to preheat to 450 degrees and a few minutes later I heard a strange noise that turned out to be the middle layer of glass of the oven door shattering.  I immediately turned off the oven.  There were sharp, pea sized pieces of glass inside the oven, in the storage drawer below, and on the floor nearby.
Most notable is that the outermost layer of the door and the innermost layer of the door show no signs of damage, but the middle layer of glass is completely shattered.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, but no injury occurred, and the incident was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
LG Microwave Model Number LMHM2017ST 

The microwave suddenly started on fire Nothing was in it and it was not turned on. There were flames inside the microwave. Luckily we were home and we were able to jump up and open the microwave which stopped the fire.
justification: The microwave caught fire unexpectedly, posing a significant hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred as the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description:
ADVERTISING - BOX AND INSERT OF THIS "ELITE STAINLESS STEEL CORDLESS ELECTRIC KETTLE" IS GROSSLY MISLEADING. THE INTERIOR OF THIS PRODUCT IS PLASTIC AND WHEN HEATED OFFGASES AND THE AIR HAS A PUTRID BURNING PLASTIC SMELL AND THE WATER SMELLS LIKE PLASTIC ALSO.
