incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that her gas range/oven has a failure.  She stated that she is was on her way to leave the home when she heard a clicking noise and realized that her oven had powered on itself.  They attempted to cancel the operation several times but each time it powered back on.  Her spouse eventually turn off the gas and disconnect the unit.

Consumer stated that when this incident occurred it made the room extremely hot.  (6/19/17) She contacted  the retailer and she was informed that the range is out of warranty and she should report it to the agency.

Consumer feels that the range/oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that turned on by itself and made the room extremely hot, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: On several occasions, our gas range (KitchenAid Superba Model# KGRT607HBS9) turned the oven on or turned itself off without user input. Many times, once the oven was on, the electronic controls were frozen such that pressing the 'Cancel/Off' button did nothing. The oven would not respond. For the last 6 months, we have engaged the 'control lock' feature to prevent further incidents but have been largely unable to use our oven.
justification: The oven malfunctioning without user input and failing to respond to controls poses a safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I was scrubbing the plate with normal pressure under running water in the sink when the bottom suddenly broke out in an almost perfect circle. It cut a piece on the top of my thumb when it broke, cut could have cut worse if my hand was under it when it broke. The aftermath was two round pieces, the bottom and rim of the plate, both with very sharp edges all the way around.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the thumb, which qualifies as an injury, but there was no death or severe harm.

incident_description:
The clean oven indicator was touched accidently and unknowingly while setting the clock @ 10:00pm on the 29th April 2017.

At 1:00am on April 30, 2017 the smoke alarm went off and the apartment was filled with smoke.

Also the knobs on the front of the range for the surface burners turn on when a human body accidentally bumps into them. They have already changed once, still very unsafe.
  
No victim just a complaint

Incident information "The self cleaning ' indicator was obviously accidentally touched at 10PM on 04-30-17 @ 1:00AM our smoke alarm woke us up to a smoke filled home.  I could open the door also.  This is a serious matter!  The oven door was not locked!

My relationship to victim:  No victim whirlpool just need to change the design
justification: The incident involved smoke filling the apartment due to accidental activation of the oven's self-cleaning function, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have an older Mr. Coffee Expresso Maker model ECM250. While steaming milk today when I turned the knob to switch to the brew mode, the plastic shaft on the knob snapped in two leaving the unit in the steam mode. This is a safety issue as even when I unplugged the unit to be able to turn it "off", the steam continued as the pressure does not dissipate quickly. I had to gently loosen the top to allow the pressure to release. That is not safe as a burn could result from the steam. A plastic part should not be used for a part that is constantly subject to the torque on this item.
justification: The incident involved a safety issue with potential for burns due to steam release, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My Cuisinart TOB-40 Toaster Oven Broiler developed a possibly dangerous problem: the bottom front heating element recently and very rapidly became warped.
justification: The heating element warping is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential hazard.

incident_description:
Used our Oster Toaster Oven model # TSSTTVFDXLPP-033 to cook dinner last night. Meal appeared ready 2-3 minutes before timer was to shut off unit so I manually advanced the timer to the stopped position and unit shut down. What I did not immediately notice was that the timer continued to "tick" (mechanical timer). After dinner I found the timer had advanced the control knob to the "Stay on Continuous" position and the oven was reheated to 425F. I returned the knob to the OFF position and again it went to the continuous on position. I have tried numerous different settings of the timer and non make the timer stop at the off position, continues to the continuous on setting. This unit is a little less than 1 year old. After this occurred I searched the web and found other reviews mentioning this problem back in 2015. Jarden Consumer Solutions is not open on weekends so will report this to them Monday.
Fortunately we did not go out after dinner or we could have returned to a sad story with a house burned to the ground. 
Have never seen a timer like this before where the continuous on setting is not at the same end as the maximum time setting eg. you go to 60 min. then slightly more to achieve the continuous on setting.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning toaster oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: NuWave2 induction  cook top blew flames out while using. Big electric flash before flames, unplugged and stopped using immediately afterwards
justification: The incident involved flames and an electric flash, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Crock Pot brand slow cooker was plugged in on the kitchen counter at Church.   It was set to low. After an hour or two someone thought it was not turned on because the light was not lit.  The pot felt warm to the touch but we turned it up to high to be sure it was cooking.  A half hour later we checked again and the digital control panel was melting and smoke coming from the wires.  The counter under the Crock Pot was scorched but did not catch fire before we unplugged the machine.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning Crock Pot causing smoke and scorching, but no injuries or fire occurred.

incident_description: As part of a complete kitchen remodel in 2013, we bought an entire suite of Kitchenaid appliances. The Kitchenaid Architect 30-in 6.2 cu ft Self Cleaning Freestanding Induction Range in stainless steel (Model KIRS608BSS0, and S/N R34312238) has been a nightmare from the very beginning.  The repairs have been too numerous to count.  Today, however, I have become fearful of using my induction range.  I was cooking, in an induction pan I've used many times, on the right rear burner.  About 10 minutes after turning the burner on, I saw a very bright arc form between the surface of the cooktop and the pan, with a simultaneous loud popping noise that brought everyone running to see what had happened.  The burner shut itself off, and stopped working.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical arc and loud noise, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My dishwasher caught fire. I opened the front and found that the electric board had caught fire. The design is poor. Not only did the electric board catch fire, but the wires leading up to the board have melted into the plastic casing over time. Poor design apparently has the area so hot that it's melting the wires and perhaps also causing the board to overheat and catch fire.

I've gone online and this is a COMMON problem of some Kitchenaid/Whirlpool dishwasher models. MANY complaints. I'm surprised these have not been recalled. I'm grateful I was home.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire due to poor design, but no injury or death occurred. Online complaints indicate this is a common issue with certain models.

incident_description: On 09/27/17 my Frigidaire oven door exploded sending glass throughout the kitchen, giving me two minor cuts.  This is the second time this has happened.  The first was on 06/19/17.  Frigidaire replaced the door and it was installed by Jensen Appliance on 07/21/17.  When I called Frigidaire on 09/28/17 they told me there was nothing they could do, and suggested it was my fault.  I called KGMH (channel7) and they did a news report/video the evening of 09/28.  Today the parent company, Electrolux, called to schedule a repairman to come determine if the explosion was a result of "a malfunction or misuse"  They maintain the temepered glass meets all governmental standards.  However, it shouldn't be shooting out of the oven explosively.  It appears to me that the glass is glued in 2 places to the frame.  A screw goes through the glass from the back, and then into the handle.  If the screw becomes loose, pulling on the handle releases the glass.  These explosions are not news to Electrolux.  My concern is that if two glass shards drew blood on me, what if they went into a child's eye, or a nearby pet?
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts) and has occurred twice, indicating a recurring issue with the oven door.

incident_description:
Smoke and fire from dishwasher while in use. Door and control panel untouchable, very hot.
Pulled plug to reduce and eventually stop smoke.
GE Profile
Mod # PDW7880J15SS
Ser # ZL74311B
justification: Smoke and fire from the dishwasher indicate a clear incident, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
((06/10/2017) The consumer stated that his son baked a pizza. After he took the pizza out, he turned the oven off. The oven would not shut off. The consumer had to shut the range off at the breaker.

The consumer turned the breaker back on a couple of hours later and noticed that now the front right burner cannot be adjusted. It only runs on high.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven and burner, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her range was placed on oven clean mode which melted the top of the oven door and the knobs.  She stated that she had changed the cleaning time to 2 hours instead of 3 and approximately 1 1/2 hours later she noticed this incident, the heat was extreme to the point the door melted into the oven.  She stated that she was able to switch off the power.

The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that the range was out of warranty, she stated that she informed them that it was not a warranty issue but a safety issue.

Caller feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted oven door and knobs) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The submitter set the dishwasher to a wash cycle. Once the cycle ended the submitter put away most of the dishes inside the dishwasher and closed the door. The submitter said the dishwasher appeared to be off. The submitter then went to bed.

At approximately 3:30 am, the submitter woke up to a strong burn odor and noticed it was coming from the dishwasher. The submitter said the lights on the dishwasher were off but the exterior of the dishwasher and the countertop around the dishwasher was very hot to the touch. The submitter then shut off the circuit breaker. The submitter indicated that the sprayers, the silverware tray and the some of her dishes inside the dishwasher were melted.  

The submitter then contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The submitter was told that her dishwasher was not recalled and they arranged for a technician to examine the dishwasher.

A few days later the technician examined the dishwasher and advised the submitter that the incident occurred because the heating element did not turn off when the dishwasher turned off. The technician also took photographs and communicated his findings with the firm.

The submitter contacted the firm again and they offered her a discount for another GE dishwasher. However, the submitter does not feel safe buying another GE dishwasher and has requested a partial refund instead. The submitter indicated that his is a replacement and the original dishwasher was affected by a recall. 

The submitter believes the dishwasher should be recalled because it poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing a fire hazard and property damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer turned the oven on WARM for about eight minutes when her smoke alarm went off. The consumer went to the kitchen and noticed that the food was on fire. The consumer put the fire out and turned the oven off. The consumer walked away for less than five minutes and when she returned to the kitchen, she noticed the oven light was still on and her food was again on fire. The consumer noticed her food was on fire again as the top coil never turned off; the glass container inside the oven shattered. The consumer switched the breaker off.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer to schedule for a Service Technician to inspect her unit on 06/19/2017; after inspection the Service Technician informed the consumer what part needed to be ordered.

06/20/2017 - The consumer contacted Consumer Relations and was informed that the Service Technician told them the problem with the oven range was not hazardous so they would only be able to pay for parts and not labor.

The consumer states that she used the cooktop approximately four times weekly, whereas the oven was used approximately three to four times per week.

The consumer is unsure if she will have her oven range for the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and property damage (shattered glass) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: During regular use of our GE Profile dishwasher, after completing a "normal" cycle without the use of the "heated dry" feature, the washer heated up hot enough to melt many plastic items within. The plastic dripped onto the heating element and filled our house with toxic smoke. The next day the washer door was inadvertently closed (no cycle running) and it began to heat up again, creating more fumes. We had to turn off the breaker to get the heating to stop.
justification: The incident caused property damage and toxic smoke but no reported injuries, warranting severity level 2. The recurrence is unlikely as it required specific conditions (no heated dry, plastic items inside).

incident_description:
Caller stated that the electric range powers on by itself at nights and they are unable to power it off, he has to use the circuit breaker to switch it off.  He stated that this incident has been ongoing for 2 weeks.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.


Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The electric range malfunctioning poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description: We have the Smooth stovetop as stated on the previous recall in 2012. Our serial number was not included, however, the oven either wont get hot enough or gets too hot and wont cool down sometimes for a hour. It is totally unpredictable. When I cook, i dont know if the food will be coked properly or if it is going to burn. The oven gets dangerously hot to the point that we have to cut it off and unplug in fear of a fire The model # is LRE30453ST /01 and the serial number is 010MMRQ00886. We purchased from Home depot in I believe was 2011. This has happened numerous of times and not just today.
justification: The description indicates a recurring issue with the oven's temperature control, posing a risk of fire but no actual injury or death reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that during the past couple of weeks, on two different occasions the dishwasher did not shut off after running its cycle; the consumer had to shut it off manually. The consumer reports a burning smell when he opened the dishwasher. The dishwasher is also not washing the dishes properly, making the consumer run the same dishes more than once.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the representative he spoke to informed him his unit is not included in a recall and hence they could not assist him since it is out of warranty.

The consumer states that the motor of the dishwasher has been replaced thrice, a water pump has also been replaced, as well as the shut off/ on clamp. The unit has been serviced five times.

The consumer states that the dishwasher is used once or twice daily.

The consumer plans on keeping his unit for at least the next thirty days.

6.13.17
CPSC:
The consumer signed the form, made a copy and is returning it to you with this update:
- While attempting to use the machine, it has a foul smell that continues to emanate from the unit.
-  There is a black film build up on all of the internal washing parts inside where the dishes are placed.  The collection gasket-basket has some film on it.
-  We cannot use the machine at all.  It is mechanically unsafe.
This far, the consumer has not heard from Sears or anyone they represent.  The consumer thanks you very much for what you are doing and he hopes resolution comes quickly.

Thank you.
[REDACTED] [REDACTED]
justification: The dishwasher exhibits multiple malfunctions and a burning smell, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite combination microwave and wall oven model #49113.  Purchased in 2016 (February) delivered March 31, 2016 but did not move into new home and start using until November 15, 2016.

The microwave started up on its own when I was not home.  I returned home very late from an out of town trip to find the microwave running.  I have security cameras in my home and one happened to be facing the kitchen door to the outside and also captured the microwave turning on by itself.  Fortunately, the startup of the microwave and when I walked into the house was no more than a couple minutes and I was able to turn it off and cut power to the circuit before a fire could begin.  Needless to say, this is a fire hazard.
justification: The microwave turned on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Was making dinner on the LG stove top and turned the burner down to low and left the room. Smelled something and went back in and the liquid was boiling ( it had not been when I left) Turned the burner off and it would not turn off or turn down it was just getting hotter . The temp control stated that is was off but hot (h5?). Was afraid to go turn off the breaker in case I fell and the house caught on fire, so kept switching full tea kettles until my partner came home. He turned the breaker off and we waited 20 minutes and turned it back on. The burner immediately went on though it stated it was off, was bright red and hotter than I have ever seen any of them. We turned the breaker off. 
I did some research and found that LG had a recall of over 160,000 ranges for the same problem, however our model number was not included in that recall. Contacted LG and was told as a courtesy they would do a repair and got authorization after supplying a receipt of purchase and serial number, however there service has not happened after numerous call, chats and emails.
I truly believe that the heat of this could cause a fire.  Stove was purchased at Best Buy Model is LG Electric Double Oven LDE3017ST
justification: The stove malfunctioned and could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The issue is likely to recur given the recall history and unresolved repair.

incident_description: The left rear burner on the stove started up on its own with no action on my part. It happened several times. So I unplugged the stove.
justification: The burner starting on its own is an incident but no injury occurred, and it happened several times indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
I purchased a Imusa 9-Cup Coffee Percolator from my local Kmart about 2 or 3 months ago. After a month or 2 I noticed the clear plastic viewing bulb on top of the percolator had melted.

I know that some plastics release chemicals when heated. Some of these chemicals can be harmful to people.

Previous to this last percolator I had the same model, where the plastic coffee basket had melted. In this incident  I forgot the percolator on the stove and it overheated. my fault bet glad it did not catch on fire and burn down my house.

Thank You,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a melted plastic part but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is moderate given the user's history of similar incidents.

incident_description:
While cleaning my Cuisinart DLC-2A/DLC-2 AC Mini-Prep Plus food processor, I noticed that a piece of plastic was
hanging from the blade assembly. Further examination showed that the plastic holding the blade was cracked at
several places. This is a hazard because pieces of plastic or the blade could come off during use, and injure the user.
justification: The cracked plastic on the blade assembly poses a direct risk of injury if the blade or plastic pieces detach during use.

incident_description:
On September 26, 2017 at 10:25 PM multi-family apartment complex located in [REDACTED] had a fire in the kitchen.  The occupant had heated up a plastic cup of water which contained pasta shells in the microwave for approximately 30 seconds.  The tenant noticed the odor of smoke emitting from the microwave and she turned microwave off.  The tenant noticed flames inside upper cabinet of the microwave and used a fire extinguisher to attempt to extinguish the fire. Ultimately the fire spread and she and two roommates exited the apartment.  The fire sprinkler system activated and ultimately extinguished the fire prior to the fire departments arrival. 

Detective [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] with the State Fire Marshal's Office investigated the fire and the fire was determined to have originate in the inaccessible portion of the microwave toward the top left side of the microwave.  All other causes including the duplex receptacle were able to be eliminated as having caused or contributed to the fire.  The fire damage sustained to the cooking area of the microwave cabinet was limited to minor smoke discoloration.  The upper internal area of the microwave sustained extensive fire damage which spread to the wooden cabinets.  The fire was extinguished quickly and the majority of the damage was isolated to the upper section of the microwave cabinet and the fire spread upward and horizontally toward the electrical control panel.
justification: The fire caused property damage but no injuries or deaths, and was quickly contained by the sprinkler system.

incident_description: Main Control Board Relay caught fire while using oven.
justification: The incident involved a fire but there is no mention of injury or death, and such events are uncommon but not unheard of in appliance use.

incident_description:
The evening of June 20, 2017, shortly after starting a load of dishes, smoke and an electrical-fire smell started coming from my dishwasher.   I opened the dishwasher, which was early in the wash cycle.  I turned off the breaker switch, then I removed the dishes and drained the water.  The next day I called to schedule a service appointment.

On June 26, 2017, a qualified service professional from Harry's TV & Appliance, 11110 N.Pennsylvania Avenue, Oklahoma City, OK 73120, telephone number 405-755-4000, came and inspected the dishwasher.  He stated the fire had destroyed the controls, console, latch, insulation, wire harnesses and the fuse.  The estimated cost to repair is $724.  The technician emphasized that after replacing the clearly damaged parts, he might be able to determine the cause of the fire, which could require further repairs or might result in a determination that the dishwasher was beyond repair and not safe to use.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire in the dishwasher causing damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: One of the burners automatically turned itself on.  The range was not being used at the time and no one was in the kitchen.  I heard the chime, went into the kitchen and saw one burner had turned on.  I turned it off.  It has happened twice in the space of several hours. Luckily, I was at home when this happened and I could turn it off.  This could be a fire hazard if it happens at night or during the day when no-one is at home.
justification: The burner turning on by itself is an incident with no injury, but poses a potential fire hazard if unattended.

incident_description:
GE Dishwasher (Model #: PDW8980N00SS, SER #: SM834045B) malfunctioned almost causing a fire. The GE Dishwasher was left turned off with unit in the closed position, and we awoke in the middle of the night to something burning. We discovered the unit filled with smoke and it had melted all of the plastic material inside  including the rack, basket, lower mechanisms, and a few baby food ware items. It had also damaged the houses electrical. After speaking with the electrician he informed me that the GE Dishwasher/heating element had malfunctioned and that it would have continually heated until a possible fire or until burning all of the electrical. We also had a GE Service Technician inspect the Dishwasher and he also determined that heating element had failed, which was likely due to a faulty circuit board. When I asked if there was a recall for this GE Dishwasher (Model #: PDW8980N00SS) he said no, and also said that he couldn't say if one was needed because he would potentially get in trouble/lose his job if he told me that this was a serious issue. This really concerns me not only for the safety of my family but also for the safety of other families that may have this model GE Dishwasher in their home. 

I truly believe that a recall is need for this model GE Dishwasher (Model #: PDW8980N00SS), and after speaking with GE's customer service Representatives and Managers they seemed to not care for the safety of the consumers. I urge you and your team to investigate this issue and if needed I will be happy to offer any further assistance that might be needed.

Best regards,
[REDACTED]
Phone #: [REDACTED]
Email: [REDACTED]
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, causing smoke and damage but no injury or death.

incident_description: My wife went to reheat her coffee (because with kids, you never get to enjoy a hot cup of coffee) and set it for exactly 28 seconds. She never grabbed it out of the microwave once it beeped, and it appears the heating mechanism never shut off. The mug and coffee were literally on fire! Our microwave did this once before a month or so ago - kept heating even after time stopped and even after the door was open! I thought it was a one-time glitch, but turns out there's a larger problem. So blessed that we caught it when we did. Had we left to go for a walk, run an errand, etc. it would've been disastrous!
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing a fire, but no injuries occurred. The issue has happened before, indicating a recurring problem.

incident_description: The the door of the oven/range I just purchased becomes so hot that one's hand would be burned by touching it for more than a fraction of a second. Immediately after the oven was delivered and installed I tested it by heating to 385 degrees F. I touched the door to see how hot it was because I have a toddler in my home. The door was far too hot to be safe. A child could easily burn her hand on the door.
justification: The oven door becomes dangerously hot, posing a burn risk, especially to a toddler, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
warming a sandwich for 60 sec and the outer glass on the microwave door shattered unexpectedly!

Had used the microwave one hour earlier with no problem!
justification: The microwave door glass shattered unexpectedly, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Today was the second time my Krups XP 1000 exploded, when the first explosion occurred, it was a mess,coffee stains and glass everywhere,I took pictures and called Krups, Pretty much their standard answer, coffee to fine or compacted too much. I just cleaned up my mess and stuck it under my counter and put my old coffee maker back in service, on 09/18/2017 my old coffee maker died, Got the Krups out and made coffee, i stayed out of the kitchen till coffee ready, This morning while at my kitchen table on my computer the coffee maker exploded, instantly Deja Vu,
justification: The incident describes a coffee maker exploding twice, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: At 1:20am I heard a crashing sound. Upon looking nothing was evident. Later the same day I opened a lower kitchen cabinet and glass spilled everywhere slivers and shards. My 9 x 13 glass Pyrex baking dish exploded on the shelf in the middle of the night! It hadn't been used for weeks and had no damage. I researched and found this is not an uncommon problem. Why is it still being manufactured? I did find that [REDACTED] manufactures bakeware w/borosilicate - I'm trying that.
justification: The incident involved a glass baking dish exploding, causing glass shards to spill, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Broiler was turned on to preheat. After a few minutes, there was a small explosion that blew insulation out of the oven vent onto the cooktop. We immediately turned the broiler off using the control pad. 

Upon opening the oven door to check for additional damage, a second small explosion occurred as the open door allowed air to enter and the remaining gas to ignite.

No injuries occured as a result of either explosion.

I found a recall for the same model number on the CPSC website, but with a different range of serial numbers. My concern is that the range of serial numbers subject to the recall doesn't cover all of the defective units, and other consumers may be at risk of a gas explosion in their kitchen.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved explosions and potential safety risks, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Have a pan- gotham steel products -  that had an issue when cooking hashbrowns   with it.  The rivet for the handle inside the pan literally blew off- firecracker force-

Called the customer service number -1-888-326-0978 and was asked to fill out a  form and sent 9.99 back with the  product for replacement. I did not accept this and they then  gave me a number 1-800 423-4248 (emson?)  to call but had to leave a message.

I have pictures of this and am concerned for others that if they are startled could seriously burn themselves.Please let me know if you want these pictures.

The company does not respond very well and not well accessible to quickly resolve this.
justification: The incident involved a handle rivet blowing off with significant force, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung Microwave.  The microwave was delivered and installed in July 2017.  About a week or so ago, I woke up one morning and noticed this discoloration on the front of the microwave. I attempted to clean with [REDACTED] and realized it was a permanent discoloration. I opened the microwave door and noticed the interior door had an oval side burn hole at the bottom and a couple of inches above it the rack showed evidence of being burnt too. --- I have had a [REDACTED] Microwave in the same location for going on 20 years with no problem. I know what you can put in the microwave and what you cannot. I use the microwave exclusively to heat up water for tea in the morning, [REDACTED] microwaveable breakfast, [REDACTED], bake potatoes and reheat leftovers in microwave safe dishes, ---- There is no plausible explanation to explain why this microwave caught on fire.
justification: The microwave showed signs of burning and discoloration, indicating a fire incident, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased an electric LG Range (Model LRE30453SB) on 11/5/11.  On August 9, 2017, I was putting a bag of brown sugar into my cabinet next to the stove.  I bumped the metal side of the stove with the bag.  The oven door cracked loudly and then exploded into my kitchen.  Glass traveled more than 10 feet in my kitchen.  The oven door was never bumped; the oven was not on.  The cook top was off but still warm.  The glass shattered into tiny shards that cut my fingers.  The glass was everywhere and the inside of the door completely exposed.  This could have been disastrous had my family been in the kitchen with me.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (cut fingers) due to the oven door exploding, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Metal shavings in food while using th weston #10 manual meat grinder. I purchased this product from the Johnson restaurant supply store on 9/14/17.  I used this product to grind clams for stuffed clams.
Upon cleaning the product I discovered little metal chips on the kitchen counter. I returned to product to Johnson and they encountered the same unsafe condition. (I threw  out 1 1/2 dozen stuffed clams) Upon investigation in  the store it was discovered the chinese made product had a grinding plate in which the hole were not completely drilled through. In  addition the metal was soft. They offered me a German manufacture which was high carbon steen heat treated, ground, and polished. It was to large as a result the store refunded my money.
justification: Metal shavings in food pose a contamination risk but no injury was reported, and the issue was identified before consumption.

incident_description:
The consumer states that about one minute after she turned her kettle on, she heard a buzzing sound coming from it, as well as the cord arcing. The consumer then noticed a burn hole in the middle of the cord. There was smoke and black soot as well. The consumer unplugged the unit.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative she spoke to informed her that they would send her a replacement kettle by another brand.

The consumer indicates that prior to the incident, she used the unit daily for approximately five minutes each use. The consumer plans on keeping her kettle for at least the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involved a buzzing sound, arcing cord, and burn hole, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We purchased a new home and there was a new stove/oven range that had recently been installed in the home.  We could tell it was brand new because it still had the stickers attached and the manual was placed next to it.  Within a day or two of living in the home we had several close calls where my 16-month-old son was able to turn the stove on and could place his hand right into the front flame.  We were able to stop him before he could get hurt but the stove height is incredibly low.  We NEVER had this problem in our previous home.  There is no resistance in the knobs to turn on the stove.  I understand that child-proofing is necessary to completely protect children from turning on a stove but what if a person doesn't have children and you go to visit their home?  It's scary how quickly my son was able to turn on this stove and put his hand right into where the flame was.  We have removed the knobs from the stove.  I think this product is completely unsafe.  The oven door doesn't close all the way and you can easily slide Adult fingers between the frame of the oven and the door.  I can't believe this is on the market.  I'm thankful my son was not hurt but I can't wait until someone was hurt before I shared my concerns.  There needs to be more resistance to the mechanism that turns the stove on.  Also, the oven door should close all the way.  This product is so unsafe it scares me.
justification: The incident describes a close call with no actual injury, but the likelihood of recurrence is high given the stove's design flaws and the child's demonstrated ability to activate it.

incident_description: The GE Freestanding oven almost caught fire.  I came home and the oven had come on by itself.  It smelled like it was on fire and was too hot to touch, The wiring on the back was melted and burning. The wall behind the stove had started getting black spots from the heat. The cabinets around it were too hot to touch.  Flipped the breaker off to get the stove to turn off and unplugged the stove.  It made a spark and heard a loud pop when I unplugged it.  Got an oven mit and pulled the stove out of the space by the handle.  Put fans on everything to make everything cool down.  It would have been a fire at any minute if I had not come home in time.
justification: The oven malfunctioned severely, causing overheating and melting wiring, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We have an issue with our NXR DRGB-3602C, purchased from Costco on 8/2/2015.

In June 2016, the oven igniter had to be replaced (under warranty) by an appliance repairman contracted by NXR/Duro.

On 7/16/2017, we (the consumer) turned the oven on for baking. As it was preheating, we opened the oven door to adjust the oven racks. While the oven door was open, large sparks suddenly started to emit from the floor of the oven, all around the metal plate that covers the igniter. This was followed by a loud bang, so loud that it was interpreted as an explosion. We quickly closed the oven door, turned off the oven, and ran outside. No one was hurt and the sparks stayed within the oven.

This issue was escalated to Costco on 7/18/2017, who then discussed the issue with NXR. NXR's response was that since the product was still in warranty, they would send someone to replace the igniter again. They stated that there was no safety risk with this oven part, and that besides replacement of the igniter they did not feel additional action was necessary. We are not completely confident that it will not cause harm should a similar incident occur again.

incident_description: On the evening of June 25, 2017, I was making dinner for my family and a couple of dinner guests. I was at home with my husband, two friends, their infant daughter, and our one-year-old, four-year-old and eight-year-old. I had biscuits and zucchini in the oven at 425 degrees, and was cooking on the stovetop as well. After about six minutes, I heard a loud popping. I saw what I later realized was smoke. At the time I thought I was just seeing the shadow of steam. I was cooking on the stovetop, using the oven and the microwave and thought maybe the breaker blew. My husband reset the breaker and it immediately started popping again. He saw sparks go to the breaker too. He made sure everything was off. I pulled out the oven and saw that my wall was scorched and the back of the oven had scorching as well as if flames had gone from the back of my oven. Our oven is only three years old and I've now seen many others with similar experiences. The model is Samsung Household Electric Range NE595R1ABSR. I contacted Samsung support via Twitter and am awaiting to hear back. I'm concerned as I also have a Samsung microwave (it's my only cooking tool right now) and I've seen other consumers with fires from these units.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with visible scorching and sparks, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My 8-year-old daughter was getting ice from our refrigerator's ice maker when a large shard of plastic fell into her cup. We investigated and found that part of the ice maker had cracked into several pieces. We emptied the bin and we think we removed all the plastic pieces. We purchased this refrigerator new 6 months ago.
justification: The incident involved a plastic shard falling into a cup, but no injury occurred, and the issue was addressed by removing the plastic pieces.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her dishwasher is emanating a toxic odor which she feels is unsafe.  She would like to return it to the company.  She stated that she has never experienced anything like this in all her years purchasing dishwashers.

Caller feels that this odor might get into her utensils and cause health effects.

The submitter's daughter was making scrambled eggs and after a few minutes the smoke alarm went off. The submitter said there wasn't smoke but she smelled a chemical and burn odor. The submitter checked the eggs and noticed they were burning but the fire was on low heat. The submitter discarded the eggs and placed the pan in the sink. The submitter then noticed that the red paint on bottom of the pan was burning off. The submitter indicated that this was the first time the pan was used and it was the smallest pan of the set.

She then checked the biggest pan of the set which she used on August 4 and she noticed that the paint on the bottom had come off. The submitter contacted the retailer who she said is the importer of the product and informed them of the incident. She was told that she could return the pans and obtain a refund, which she did. She was also offered a 10% discount which she refused. The submitter believes the firm did not address the safety hazard with concern and she believes the pans should be recalled.

The consumer states that the oven in question was used three to four times weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping his double-oven range for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

07/31/2017

incident_description: I purchased a whirlpool induction double oven range in December 2014.  In March 2016 my stove made a loud pop and smoke came out the back vent.  It gave me error codes EC0021,E0300 and M0430.  I could not use the range top or oven.  It took over a month to fix it.  Then in August 2017 the range top started changing the burner settings.  I would turn it down and it would go to the highest setting.  The stove top is touch controlled.  It gave me a f40 code which was to call customer service.  Then the oven stopped working totally.  I have not been able to use it since 8/24/2017.   I have since found Whirlpool has stopped manufacturing this stove. the stove is 3 years old and not useable.  To fix it will cost over 1000.00.   I think Whirlpool should have to make some type of assistance to purchase a new stove or replace it totally.  Appliance repair tech said it is a design flaw because the computer control module is place between the ovens and stovetop which the heat burns up computer and destroys it.  He said it will continue to do this because of where it is located.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove with no reported injuries or deaths, but it caused significant inconvenience and financial loss.

incident_description:
This LG electric range has controls that, when accidentally bumped, turn on the stove top heating elements.   The first incident that I witnessed occurred during the installation process in early June 2017.  The installers bumped one of the controls and the element began to heat up.  It was quickly noticed and turned off before any damage could occur.  
The second incident occurred Sept. 8, 2017 when painters accidentally bumped the control.  This time the drop cloth over the stove caught on fire and smoke filled the room.  It was extinguished and there was no damage to the house, but the glass cook top sustained small pit marks.
justification: The incident caused a fire but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as it happened twice in a short period.

incident_description: I was cooking chicken at 350 degrees in my Pyrex glass pan. And the pan exploded in my oven! It shattered all the glass.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex pan exploding in the oven, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Top water supply hose to Frigidaire  FDB2410 is about 1 inch too short.  After about a year or two it wiggled itself free of the clamp and flooded the area beneath the dishwasher and tripped the GFCI breaker on the box under the sink.  Had to rewire the area given the flood and paid for a service call to verify that the design is defective.
justification: The incident caused flooding and required repairs, but no injury or death occurred. The description suggests this issue is likely to recur due to the defective design.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung Gas Range on 11.09.2009. It has barely been used due to a knee injury and two subsequent surgeries. I tried using the Self Cleaning feature for the first time on 06.20.2017.  After less than an hour of a three hour cycle, the product began smoking and the control panel went out. It even set off the smoke detectors in my house. When I Googled the problem, it turns out there are reports of this happening since at least 2011, and I'm lucky I did not have sparks or a fire. 
https://www.shopyourway.com/questions/1148115
Samsung gave me a hard time about the repair, and I had to upload the receipt to show the purchase date multiple times on their website. They then told me I was "Lucky" they would repair it at no charge. How am I lucky when the product has a one year warranty? I consider that a legal obligation, not luck. Given the issues with their washers and their phones, a case needs to be opened with their gas and electric ranges too.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas range that produced smoke and disabled the control panel, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Knob on gas stove has been frequently bumped causing gas to turn on silently, and without lighting, while reaching for the built-in microwave above it or reaching for dishes stored above. This causes the kitchen to be filled with natural gas. If someone is in the house after this happens, then the smell of the gas alerts us to the situation.  However, if the knob is bumped on and we leave the house, the entire house could be filled with gas, causing a very dangerous situation.

This has happened at least 10 times, but fortunately there has not been a fire or explosion (yet).

The spring rate in the knob is extremely low, allowing the knob to be pressed and slightly turned by just casually leaning against the knob. With three engineering degrees in the family, we all agree this is an easily-fixed design issue that if not fixed, can lead to injury or loss of life.

This has been happening ever since purchasing the stove over five years ago.
justification: The incident describes a high risk of gas leakage leading to potential explosion or asphyxiation, which could result in death. The issue has occurred frequently (at least 10 times) and is likely to continue without intervention.

incident_description:
On Sat Sept 16, 2017 I attached the filter holder to a Krup XP 1000 expresso maker but did not rotate it firmly into the locking position -- perhaps 10% short of the normal locked position. I used a finely ground Columbian coffee that I tamped down about 3/4 full. The coffee came out without a problem and was almost finished, just bubbles coming out, when there was a loud explosion. Boiling coffee and glass shards were sent flying in every direction including over me and my wife. Luckily I had just turned my back to get a coffee cup, and both of us were wearing long sleeves and pants. Neither of us were injured. The filter holder had blown out of the coffee maker straight down onto the carafe shattering it. If I had been standing watching/waiting as I normally do it is likely that I would have been seriously injured. Coffee was all over the 8 foot ceiling. I would strongly suggest that you put a VERY STRONG WARNING about the need to make sure that the filter holder is rotated as far as it can go. I have used this machine for 2 years without incident and tested it again after the explosion and it works fine. But older people might not have the arm strength to push the filter holder into the proper position or might just be lazy like me and not notice that it was not rotated into position before turning on the machine. 

So Krups knew about this problem in 1994 but still havenÃÂt corrected itÃÂ. weird. There is no warning or instruction regarding this potential problem in the manual and I nearly lost an eye.... they should be punished.

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/1994/cpsc-and-krups-announce-action-on-espresso-makers
justification: The incident resulted in no injuries but involved a dangerous explosion of boiling coffee and glass shards, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description: The Insinkerator air activated sink top switch caught fire during normal use with Insinkerator disposal unit.  No injuries, but could have caused a house fire
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but possible.

incident_description:
After turning off my Samsung Stove I heard loud popping and banging sounds and then the back of the unit caught on fire. It looks like the circuit board was the item that started the fire. Instructions were to let it self-clean 3-5 hours, but turned it off after approx. 30 minutes because the fumes were unbearable. Now, hours later, it's still bad, with all windows open and fans running. I have a sore throat from being in the kitchen for half an hour. We called the store and asked them to come pick it up because based on this experience, I have no confidence that the fumes will dissipate easily or quickly. If this kind of out-gassing of the insulation material needs to happen, it should happen at the factory, not in people's homes.
justification: The incident caused a sore throat, indicating minor injury, and the fumes were severe enough to require immediate action.

He felt that there was a problem but when he started doing the research via phone calls etc. he told me there was some bad news:

2) The front fascia have been documented to get up to 180 degrees F

incident_description: I turned the upper convection oven on to pre-heat to bake at 425. I started chopping some veggies at the island and I heard a loud explosion and glass pieces started tumbling out of the upper oven.

 You have to pull the plug out of the outlet on the wall to get it to stop.

incident_description:
We moved into a new condo six weeks ago. It came with all new GE appliances. The range is a electric ceramic top model with a 12" burner on the front right of the cook top (GE Model: JB700EJ2ES, Serial No.: AH272460Q).

We were boiling some water to cook some corn on the cob. After about 15-20 minutes at the highest setting (boiling water and cooking the corn), the metal front that wraps down from the ceramic top to the oven door (see attached picture) became very hot - so hot you could not touch it for even a second. My wife actually burned her stomach reaching into the microwave over the stove. I called GE and the technician came out. It was his conclusion that it was normal operation. He called some engineer who said that on a 36" high stove, the temperature is allowed to reach 191 degrees. I know with water heaters, 120 degrees at the point of use will scald a person. The technician did lift the cook top and said everything was connected properly. There was no insulation between the burner and the metal front that was getting hot.

It is hard for me to believe that an area of a range, not involved with the heating or cooking of food, is allowed to get so hot that a significant burn could occur with a mere touch.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the wife, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the described conditions and lack of insulation.

incident_description: The burner on my Cuisinart DGB-700BC grind and brew 12-cup coffeemaker has failed twice causing the burner to overheat.  The first time was in July 2016 and I replaced the machine under warranty.  Just recently, the burner on the replacement failed, again causing the machine to overheat

incident_description: I purchased a GE slide-in range on 8-22-17 and it was installed on 8-27-17.  I used the oven only twice, and on 9-12-17, while I was out shopping, the front door shattered (outside glass panel only; inner panel appears intact), spreading glass over the entire kitchen floor, and area 15 ft by 8 ft.  The clear glass broke into small pebbles, but the black glass with the see-through perforations broke into random sized, jagged pieces.  It is fortunate that I was not in the kitchen at the time this hapened because I take prescription blood thinner, and in spite of wearing a med-alert alarm, if I suffered a number of cuts, would probably have bled to death before emergency personnel could arrive.  I am also grateful that no friends and children were in my home at the time, or they could have suffered serious injuries if they were in the kitchen when the door shattered.  I have tried to add the photos I took, but this part of your form does not seem to be working.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door causing glass spread but no injuries, as no one was present in the kitchen at the time.

incident_description: I purchased an LG Electric Range model # LRE30451ST on 8/24/07.  It is listed as a recall item with the remedy of repair.  The problem is that I have had it repaired twice before (11/16/12 and 8/17/16) and it has started doing the same thing.  The issue is that the burners unexpectedly turn on high and don't shut off.  This is dangerous and the repairs have not corrected the problem; only delayed them from reoccurring.  The company should be required to replace the defective appliance.

incident_description: On September 10, 2017, I was running our Whirlpool Gold Dishwasher. I left the room and went upstairs. My family all smelled a very strong burning electrical odor throughout our entire house. I ran downstairs and the strong odor was coming from the dishwasher. It started making crackling noises, so my husband immediately turned it off, then ran down into our basement to shut off the electricity to the appliance. The hot electrical odor was very overpowering. We first dragged the built in dishwasher out, then disconnected it from the water supply and power before dragging it outside still filled with dishes and water. The dishwasher had gotten so hot, it had warped the oak veneer glued to the plywood side of the cabinetry housing it.
justification: The incident involved a strong burning odor and crackling noises from the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a new condo with new appliances. The gas range/oven included is a new Whirlpool model WFG505M0BS0. When using the oven, the ventilation duct heats the back panel of the range to a very hot temperature. I used an infrared thermometer and measured temperatures of 152 degrees F in numerous locations, as well as 194 degrees F in another location. 

To clarify, when I refer to the back panel of the range, I mean the panel with the electronic controls and the back of the stove which abuts the wall. 

The back panel becomes burning hot with every use, and depending on how long the oven is in use, it becomes hotter and hotter. 

Additionally, there are other owners in the condominium who have the same model Whirlpool range and they are experiencing the same thing. We have contacted Whirlpool and they have sent a technician out multiple times, who reports that the oven is working within manufacturers specifications. However, it seems as though this temperature is too hot and within range to cause burns.
justification: The back panel of the range becomes burning hot with every use, posing a burn risk, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description:
My wife was baking two potatoes in unit using sense mode. When the clock showed 2:00 she opened the door to check the to see if they were done. 

I just happened to be standing next to her and noticed that the unit WAS STILL RUNNING.
I was able to quickly pull her hand from the machine and close the door. The unit WAS STILL RUNNING even after the interruption!  I quickly hit the off button and it stopped.

Fortunately the unit must have been the between power cycles since it did not burn her, but it could since she did not notice that it WAS STILL RUNNING!

After that, if the unit was off and I opened the door the internal light would not turn on right away, then it would click and the light would turn on. This would happen about 50% of the time. My wife then mentioned that it would not start the previous day and the display told her to close the door even though it was closed.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning unit that could have caused injury but did not, and the issue occurs frequently based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: We were using the stove and oven preparing dinner when smoke and flames and popping sounds arose from the back of the range.  My husband quickly pulled the range away from the wall and unplugged it, as the smoke and unmistakable smell of an electrical fire spread through the house.  An inspection of the rear of the range revealed several burned areas--wires leading to the element, light, and elsewhere--as well as melted plastic connectors.  While we don't leave the stove unattended while in use, it is not unusual for us to go into the yard while something is in the oven.  Thankfully this was not the case Monday evening as we would likely have been dealing with a house fire.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with potential for severe damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Espresso maker detached the brewing basket from the machine, exploding steam, hot water, hot coffee and the brewing basket from the machine with great force. Had anyone been standing near, it would have injured them severely
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of hot materials, but no actual injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the potential for such malfunctions.

incident_description: Monigram GE Model No: ZDP48L6RD2SS/Serial No. HD2046357 Stainless Steel 48ÃÂ Range. The Range has 6 burners and a grill.  I am dissatisfied because the Grill Burner comes on spontaneously creating a life threatening and hazardous condition. We have come home from vacation on more then one occasion to find the burner on. This began to happen intermittently approximately three (3) years ago. Now it is a daily event.
justification: The grill burner coming on spontaneously is a hazardous condition that could lead to injury or death, but no actual harm has been reported yet.

incident_description: I left the house while my children were home being watched by the oldest sibling. When I arrived at home I smelled burning plastic. I figured out that it was the dishwasher. The entire corner metal lining of the dishwasher was caved inward, the rack wheels were melted, and the spinning device at the bottom was melted. I am so glad that my house did not start on fire. GE Monogram Model #ZBD6880N00SS.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted dishwasher components) but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: On the evening of September 10, 2017 Carpinteria-Summerland Fire responded to a 911 call at 5956 Via Real #3 Road, Carpinteria, CA. 93013. The fire was from a Frigidair stove Model No. FEFLZ87GCA,Serial No.VF73780816. According to the resident, the stove top was not in use and the switch was in the off position. There was an item that was on the stove top that caught fire and caused damage to the stove, cabinets, and microwave. Inspection of the control panel indicated that the on/off swith was in the off position.
justification: The incident caused damage to property but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Stove top - on going issue - upper left burner turns on by itself. Unplugged and reset now when used will not turn off. Tried contacting SEARS/Kenmore and got the run around. Have to keep the breaker off to ensure no fire when not in use.
justification: The stove burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
(08/20/2017) The consumer filled the dishwasher and set it on normal . After the dishwasher was running for about five minutes, it made a strange noise. Flames and smoke were coming from the top of the dishwasher's door. Also, there was the smell of burnt plastic.

The consumer called the fire department, who came out to her home. The fire was out when they got there but the unit was still smoking. The firemen unplugged the unit and waited a few minutes to make sue that the unit was safe. They also advised the consumer to call them back if anything else happened.

(08/21/2017) The consumer called Sears and was passed around to different departments. She was finally given the number for the CPSC Hotline.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The control knobs of the range are on an angle with a depress feature to stop them from being turned on by simple touch. I came in the house approximately 20 minutes after I had been in the house and put groceries in refrigerator directly opposite the range/oven. I found one of the stove elements on and hot enough that it had discolored wood trim on the cabinet adjacent to the range/oven. No one else had been in the house and some groceries had been on the top of the range approximately 30 minutes before for a brief time while the bags were being unloaded and items stored in pantry. This assures me that the cooking elements on top were not already on from prior cooking several hours earlier that day. I don't recall brushing against the control panel of the range/oven but I was able to do some testing and if I bend over in a manner consistent with putting item in lower levels of the refrigerator opposite the range and my butt will be on the control knobs. If I move the knobs can roll to an ON position with little effort. By luck I entered my house and felt the heat and smelled an odor of heated wood not unlike burning wood in a fire pit. I quickly determined that one of the cooking elements was in HI heat position and the wood of cabinet nearby was browned from the heat and had very high temperature a that moment. I have great concern that there was a condition that would have lead to a fire if I had not found it when I did.
justification: The incident involved a stove element being accidentally turned on, causing heat damage to nearby wood trim, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: This microwave was purchased in July 2014 and installed in November 2014 by Lowe's.  We had a problem earlier in which microwave would not turn on and were advised to open and shut door several times.  Now microwave sparks, does not turn off when press button, and also turns itself on when we aren't even in the kitchen.  We are concerned it may start a fire and have unplugged it.
justification: The microwave exhibits dangerous behavior like sparking and turning on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Our microwave started by itself.  We heard a buzzing vibration coming from it.
It did not appear to be running, (turntable not turning, light off)  but when
we opened the micro door, the buzzing stopped, and the turntable was hot to
the touch.  We had cooked peas about 20 minutes earlier, so we thought it
might be just still warn from that (although it seemed much hotter than we'd
expect).  In order to eliminate this possibility, we placed a quart of cold
tap water in a glass dish.  A few minutes of buzzing later, we opened and
found that the water had raised to 150F degrees.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and such incidents are unlikely to happen frequently.

incident_description: Our Kenmore oven door exploded and shattered into countless all tiny pieces as we were opening the door to place frozen fish in to cook. We heard a sound from the broken pieces on the floor and looked down at the pieces and noticed some of the pieces were actually moving.
justification: The oven door exploded but there was no mention of injury, only the observation of moving pieces.

incident_description: While my dishwasher was in use, towards the end of the wash cycle, the dishwasher started making "popping" noises and black smoke started to pour out if the latch used to open the dishwasher door. The noise stopped after 5-10 seconds but smoke continued to pour out of the machine. I did open the door to see if something was on the heating element causing the smoke. I could see flames inside the door to the dishwasher. The flames were contained to the inside of the door between the front amd back panels. The door is white and I could clearly see flames for a few seconds before I went to turn off the circuit breaker, which had already tripped before I got to it. The smoke stopped c a short time later. The only damage was to the dishwasher. There were no injuries or property damage as a result of this incident.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but resulted in no injuries or property damage beyond the dishwasher itself.

incident_description: Cleaning oven after it cooled from use by wiping with a sponge. While wiping the inner rim of the pizza drawer to clean off some melted cheese, the edge sliced through the sponge and deep across my wife's middle finger. There was considerable bleeding, pain and discomfort from the injury and required 15 minutes of direct pressure to stop the bleeding. Long term effect is not yet known.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut with considerable bleeding and pain, requiring first aid, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:

Kenmore ELITE Consumers BEWARE:

I would like for you to be aware of an incident that occurred yesterday. Americans like things clean and tidy, and upon
taking out the refrigerator glass shelve to clean it off in the sink because something had spilled on it, when my daughter went to put a WET CLOTH on it to wipe it off, the WHOLE THING EXPLODED in her HANDS ÃÂÃÂ not just crack , I MEAN small pieces of glass exploded inches away from her face and chest . She received small pieces of glass in her arms drawing a small amount of blood. She could may been blinded ... Why hasn't anyone demanded a class action suit before this BLINDS OR MAMES SOMEONE????

-There is obviously a manufacturing defect in the glass OR another theory is SOMEONE could be making this KNOWING
