justification: The daughter received small pieces of glass in her arms drawing a small amount of blood, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I opened my LG microwave (Model LMV1813ST) to find the inside of the unit melted and melted plastic hanging down from the top of the inside.  I have since unplugged the unit and emailed LG.  The unit was manufactured on May 2013 and is Serial Number 30STATG6E169
justification: The microwave showed signs of damage (melted plastic) but no injury or death occurred, and the unit was unplugged to prevent further risk.

incident_description: I have cooks companion perfect weight cookware. I purchased it on Evine.  Some of the pots have an applied metal hollow handles that are supposed to be cool to touch when using.  I grabbed the pot expecting the handle to be cool, and burned my hand.  After a year of use and washing, water got inside the handle and heats up when you use the pots.  This is dangerous and I was not expecting it.  I feel this is a safety issue and the handles should be replaced.
justification: The user suffered a burn injury due to the handle heating up unexpectedly, indicating a safety issue with the product.

incident_description:
GE brand microwave oven   model number HVM1540DP1WW manufactured JUNE 2011 serial number LV201627B.
When I was at home microwave starts working by itself. When I try to turn it off the buttons did not work and I disconnected power plug from the power outlet. After 10 min I plugged in and microwave starts working (EMPTY MICROWAVE) again. I called GE  and they tried to charge me for testing, driving, labor and parts, parts only cost $206 plus tax, the defective part was Keypad front panel assembly.
After talking with manager they sent me a free parts and I changed it by myself, I am a mechanic.
The microwave works now. I made a research online and decided to inform everyone because this issues can cause a fire - life danger. GE had no recalls for that appliances but should have had now. I recorded a video clip how microwave started working by itself.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and operated by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(06/23/2017) The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in the wash cycle. Smoke was coming from the door. Power was lost in the product. The consumer stated that her husband pulled the unit from under the counter. He removed the front cover from the door. The connections in the door were burnt and the plastic was melted.

(06/27/2017) The consumer contacted Kenmore . She was advised that she would be charged to have a service technician come out to look at the unit. The consumer was advised that the product was not on the recall list.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burnt connections but no reported injuries, warranting a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the description of the malfunction.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore electric range, model 790.92303011.  Yesterday morning, I was sitting at the kitchen table about 15 feet away, reading the newspaper, when the outer glass panel on the over door violently and spontaneously exploded, spewing glass up to 6 feet away.  The oven was not in use and hadn't been for about a week, and there was no one near it.  If someone were standing in front of the oven they could have easily been injured by the flying glass.
I contacted Sears customer service and was told that they could send a technician to make the needed repairs, but because the range was out of warranty, there would be a service charge of $99 and an additional charge for parts.  I find this completely unacceptable for a manufacturing defect that could easily lead to serious injury.
justification: The incident involved a spontaneous explosion of the oven door glass, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I put a k cup into the keurig dispenser. I put it into the cradle, after it heated up I turned the button to dispense the coffee. It was taking a little longer than normal and not really dispensing liquid. It started making an odd noise and then I heard a loud pop and hot water exploded everywhere, including on me. Luckily I had pants on, but I could easily have been burned if my skin was exposed. If there was a small child or pet standing in front of it, it would have been a really bad situation.
 
GE Cafe Series Caf with Keurig K-CUP Brewing System 22.2-cu ft Counter-Depth French Door Refrigerator with Ice Maker (Stainless Steel) ENERGY STAR 
MODEL: CYE22USHISS
justification: Hot water exploded, posing a burn risk, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description: Kenmore 74033 Gas Range -  I have reported this before.  It is easy to bump the front controls and unknowingly slightly turn on the gas.  There is too much travel in the control that it will release gas long before it turns far enough to reach the ignition phase. Luckily the windows were open and we caught it before big trouble.
justification: The incident involves gas release without ignition, posing a hazard but no injury occurred, and the issue is described as easily repeatable.

incident_description:
Two issues:
Issue 1:  Touch pad is too sensitive.  You only need to touch it with your clothes and or a fabric to active the functions.  This has happened on numerous occasions.

Issue 2:  (most dangerous)  While reaching for the above range microwave my body depressed and turned the cook top dial knob on without my knowledge.  Upon smelling smoke, I returned to the kitchen to find a wood platter beginning to ignite.  Accidentally activating the dial knobs has occurred numerous times, but this is the first time with potential catastrophic results.

My recommendation is for Sears corporation to replace the knob push spring with a much stronger spring.  The original equipment spring requires no resistance at all.
justification: Issue 2 describes a situation with potential for injury due to accidental activation of the cook top, evidenced by a wood platter igniting. The occurrence is likely as it has happened numerous times.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that the refrigerator glass shelves shattered a few months after purchase, she ordered and replaced it and the same incident happened again a few months later.  She stated that the smaller glass shelf shattered a few days ago. The company was contacted to order a replacement.

Caller stated that she thought her spouse had done something the first time but when it continued to happen she realize that something was wrong with the shelves.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that these shelves are unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves repeated shattering of glass shelves without reported injury, indicating a safety concern but no harm.

incident_description: Our GE Profile dishwasher had recently finished a full cycle and was off.  My son unloaded the dishwasher and then left the house.  When he returned home the dishwasher heating cycle had apparently turned on (there were no dishes in it at the time) because he could smell burning plastic and the dishwasher was very hot.  The insides had melted (this includes the part that spins the water on the bottom, the main lower basket and the silverware basket.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted dishwasher components) but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The knobs keep breaking on this range.  I've called and complained.  I've tweeted them.  They finally blocked me.  

I cant turn the gas off on my stove anylonger!!!!   I've replaced the knobs 6 times in 7 years at a cost of almost $100 each time.  

They MUST fix this!
justification: The incident involves repeated knob failures on a gas stove, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
The dishwasher had completed the wash cycle and was drying the dishes. I was working in the yard and came in for a drink of water. I noticed all the lights on the dishwasher were off except the "clean" light. I leaned against the counter above the dishwasher and noticed that it was extremely hot. 

I opened the dishwasher and was hit by a blast of heat. I could not touch the racks or dishes with my bare hands. I used a pot holder to try and slide out the bottom rack but it was stuck. I then noticed a knife on the bottom of the tub. I then realized that the utensil basket had melted and more utensils were protruding through the bottom of the basket. This was what caused the rack to be stuck in the closed position. I raised the rack and picked it up and out of the dishwasher. I then observed that the rubber had melted off the bottom rack.

I emptied the dishwasher and closed it.  A short time later I observed the heat was back on again but none of the lights on were lit and would not turn off unless the door was open. If I had not been attentive this defect could have possibly caused a fire in my residence.
justification: The incident involved extreme heat and potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Dishwasher was run when family went to bed.  Woke up to smell of smoke and the dishwasher had  black 'burns' coming out from the top of the door, soot all over, and smoke in the air.  Tripped the fuse box and dishwasher was no longer responding.  Smell of burnt plastic from the heating element and the dishwasher did not drain completely.  

GE stainless steel profile dishwasher model GLD6560L00S
justification: The incident involved smoke and burns from the dishwasher, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I went to check my cusiniart products for the recalls that was issued in december 2016.  I noticed mine wasnt in the recall; however, upon inspecting my blade in the Mini-Prep Plus that I have, the blades are the kind that are not riveted.  My blade's plastic that surrounds the blade is separating and I am afaid it will come apart as the ones in the recall.
justification: The blade's plastic is separating, posing a potential hazard, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The knobs on the range are too sensitive. I can walk by and brush them and the gas comes on, but thenignotor does not. There have been several times when we've smelled gas because of this. The interlock on these know is incorrectly designed. Further I have seen other reports of this on this site and numerous other sites on the internet. This is fire hazard plain and simple. This is a brand new stove in a kitchen we just had remodeled.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard due to sensitive knobs causing gas leaks, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Can opener does not open can on first rotation. Multiple rotations produces metal shavings.
These cans must be discarded.
The cutting wheel is worn and needs to be replaced.
Hamilton Beach was contacted and said the wheel cannot be replaced on this model.
It can be replaced with the removal of 6 cover screws and one set screw for the cutting wheel and remove the drive capstan. 
After calling Hamilton Beach 800-851-8900. I was told the cutting wheel was not replaceable and it was not repairable. I was given a code for a 40% discount on their web site. They would add $11.49 for shipping. This brings the total to around $33.

This product is $28 at Walmart.
https://www.walmart.com/ip/Hamilton-Beach-Smooth-Touch-Can-Opener-Model-76606/5924593
 Making the discount useless.
It a shame that they will not sell new cutting wheels. It make this product disposable.

Users that do not see the metal shaving could be in trouble.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning can opener producing metal shavings, posing a potential hazard if unnoticed, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidaire professional smooth top electric  free standing range. I came home from work to find the front left element on. I tried to turn it off and it would turn off for one second and then come right back on again on high. The only way I could turn it off was  unplugging the unit. This was over 2 weeks ago. Frigidaire 'customer care' was absolutely no  help whatsoever and were in fact repeatedly rude and unhelpful. Frankly impossible would be a better word. Google search indicated this is a known problem. Frigidaire authorized service technicians were not helpful either. They came out but the only service they  provided was to plug the stove in. Yes, the burner came on and would not turn off. They unplugged the stove and they left but not before they charged me $90 for that "analysis."  I needed an expert "authorized service technician" for that?  I am still waiting for the repair allegedly because the part is back ordered.  I could have lost everything that day because of the element turning itself on. Its a fire hazard. The stove cost over a thousand dollars. I purchased it through AAFES (Air Force and Army Exchange). I don't know where AAFES acquires their merchandise. I am troubled and frustrated by the complete lack of concern and response from the entities involved. I am a disabled veteran and right now the only way I can cook is on the BBQ. People should think twice about purchasing a fire hazard.

Frigidaire professional model  FPEF 3081MFF
                                  SERIAL VF43810814
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased this Frigidaire stove in 2008. Within months I noticed that the settings were unstable, it would readjust automatically. Eventually, LF burner stopped working, RF dual burner would go to high and I couldn't turn it off. When I called Frigidaire to ask if they had a recall on this product they said no. so, after the problem caused a lots of damage to food and cook wear, and being in fear of serious consequences, I began unplugging it when not in use. About a year ago I decided to check once more to see if a recall had been placed on my stove and discovered that in fact there was, in 2009, after my initial inquiry. I wasn't notified. I called Frigidaire to report the problems that I was having and arrangements were made, repair was completed. The problem has now reoccurred. RF dual burner stays on continuously so, I can no longer use my stove. (Major inconvenience!) I believe these stoves should have been replaced with a safer model rather than repaired. They are dangerous and could cause loss to property as well as human life.
justification: The stove malfunction caused damage to property and posed a potential risk, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: 2nd exact microwave that the grill unit malfinctions and turns on when not set and and idoesnt turn off with timer. 2nd one exact model nearly set my house on fire and melted plastic
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and nearly caused a fire, indicating a significant incident but no reported injury.

incident_description: I plugged my waffle iron in. The light did not turn on to indicate that it was on. So I unplugged it and re plugged it into the wall and my husband touched it. He jumped slightly and stated that it just shocked him. I immediately unplugged it and check for a recall.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (shock) but no serious harm, and such electrical faults are uncommon with proper appliance use.

incident_description:
(02/2017) The consumer stated that the unit leaks gas when the oven is turned on at times. The consumer stated that there is a buildup of gas in the bottom of the unit. The consumer stated that there is an internal explosion each time that this happens. 

The consumer stated that Electrolux has sent someone out four times to repair the issue. The issue still occurs after each repair.

The last time that the internal explosion happened was on Monday, June 5th.

(06/05/2017)The consumer was contacted by the firm and was advised that someone will be out to repair the unit. He was also advised that they will continue to repair the unit until they deem the unit as non-repairable.

The consumer is concerned about his safety.

No injuries have occurred.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks and internal explosions, posing a significant safety risk, but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description:
07/12/2017
Consumer contacted manufacture via email. Manufacture rep [REDACTED] responded via email and advised consumer at her cost she can purchase a knob cover for each knob from retailer or LG authorized dealer.  LG admitted in the email that they knew of this problem and were working on resolving the problem!!


07/12/2017
Consumer stated there are six knobs on the front of her electric range five knobs for range top and one knob for oven, with the slightest touch(rub/bump) of the knobs they can easily be turned on.  There have been multiple episodes when the range top has been accidentally turned on.

She stated there was a burning smell coming from her kitchen, she noticed one of her range top knobs was on with a newspaper atop burner.  A fire was in progress.

She confirmed her standard poodle dog is able to turn her oven and range top knobs on several times in the pass, but yesterday (07/12/17) there were items inside the oven which a dog had turned on.. 

She feels this is definitely a fire and safety hazard for her family.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to easily turned knobs, with a fire in progress but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
(07/24/2017) The consumer stated that the range was making a popping noise. It was also sparking and 4 inch flames were coming from the back of the unit near the upper half. The range had been in use for about twenty minutes.

The consumer turned the power off at the circuit breaker. He blew on the flames to put the fire out.

The  damages were contained to the unit.

No injuries.

(07/24/2017) The consumer contacted the firm. He was advised to have someone to inspect the range and contact the firm directly.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparking but was contained with no injuries, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the junction box provided by the factory melted due to a fire while the dishwasher was in use. The consumer was not in his home at the time of the fire however when he troubleshot the unit, it indicated the problem described.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that his specific unit is not included in a recall however because they had received several complaints for dishwashers not affected by recalls, they would repair his unit free of charge.

The consumer states that the dishwasher is used three to four times per week. The consumer plans on keeping his unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The submitter said she turned on the oven to the bake setting and she put the temperature to 350 degrees. The submitter said she put a chicken in a glass baking dish and placed it into the oven. She also put the timer to 40 minutes. Approximately 20 minutes later, the submitter smelled a burn odor and while she was walking downstairs the fire alarm went off. The submitter noticed smoke coming from inside the oven and she noticed that the oven was extremely hot to the touch. The submitter believes the temperature of the oven was a lot higher than 350 degrees. The submitter pushed the "Off" but the oven failed to shut off. The submitter then opened the oven and removed the baking dish with the chicken. The submitter indicated that the bottom heating element inside the oven was extremely bright orange. The submitter said the baking dish was extremely hot to the touch and the bottom of the dish turned black. The submitter said about 45 seconds after she put the baking dish down it exploded into the pieces. The submitter said the glass cut her on the back of her left leg. She did not seek medical attention. The submitter's husband told her to cut the circuit breaker and when she did the range turned off.

The submitter contacted the firm yesterday and informed them of the incident. The submitter was told that the range was not recalled and they could not assist her with a repair or replacement. 

The submitter believes the range poses a fire hazard and should be recalled. She indicated that she found other reports online for this model having similar incidents. 

The submitter said she uses the oven 3 times a week and she uses the stovetop daily.
justification: The incident resulted in a glass explosion causing injury (cut on the leg), but no medical attention was required. The submitter uses the oven frequently, increasing the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The control knobs for the range are extremely easy to engage. Numerous times in just a few short months, the knobs have been bumped, leaving gas to leak in the house for extended periods of time. It is only upon entering the room that you smell the gas, and realize the stove buttons have been Twisted a bit. Two other times, when reaching past the stove into a cupboard, the knobs have been bumped with a hip of an adult, just enough, to engage the igniter, lighting the burner while someone was reaching over the stove.
justification: Gas leaks and unintended burner ignition pose a risk of fire or explosion, but the description does not mention any actual injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I have a Jenn-Air electric range with ceramic glass cooktop. While cooking, the range exploded sending glass all over the kitchen and dining room.  I had my entire family including all grandchildren visiting our lakehome in northern Minnesota at the time and fortunately they had just left the area.  Also, 30 seconds prior to the explosion I had been standing directly in front of the cooktop and most certainly would have been hit with multiple shards of glass.  The potential for serious injury should be noted in their use and care manual but it is not found anywhere.  I have cooked on it for 12 years and never had any difficulty in any way prior to this.  I have a Jenn-Aire ceramic glass cooktop in our Twin Cities home as well and I am now concerned that the same thing could happen with that one.  Jenn-Air's only response is that they will send someone to "tell me what happened" and that I would be responsible for all parts and labor for repair.  It is beyond repair and we plan to buy a new appliance so that is not the issue.  The future potential for danger to myself and others who have ceramic glass cooktops is the issue and it should be a real concern to all but it is definitely not a concern to Jenn-Air.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage but no injuries, and the user reports no prior issues over 12 years of use, indicating rarity.

incident_description:
Accidentally Turning on Gas

This has happened multiple times, but most recently Saturday August 19th.  I got up in the morning and smelled spoiled beef.  We had just purchased a side of beef and had repacked it the day before.  The trash had not been taken out - so I was not alarmed by the smell.  I double checked the freezer temperature and took out the trash.  Several hours later I returned to the kitchen and could still smell the beef.  I then looked at the stove, and one of the knobs was turned on slightly, no ignition or flames, just enough to emit the gas.

We had gone to bed around 9 pm, and it was afternoon before we discovered what was causing the smell. (16 hours the gas had been on)  We opened windows and aired out the kitchen.  Nobody was injured.

This isn't the only time this has occurred, but had assumed an over zealous  cleaning of the stove.  But now as part of the cleaning routine, the knobs are double checked to be placed in the off position.  This has happened at least 4 other times in the past

We did notice that unlike stoves in the past, where you had to push in the knobs rather far, in order to turn on the burner, this stove barely requires any push of the knob to allow the gas to be turned on.

I have spoken with a Kitchen AId company customer service representative - who told me the stove is working as designed.  "If you turn the knob, you should get gas"  My issue isn't with the expected function, but how easy it is to accidentally turn on.  She said they have no other reports of these accidents.
justification: The incident involved gas leakage without injury, and it has occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Kenmore Side by Side refrigerator 106.5113.  The wires to the icemaker and water dispenser are at the bottom hinge area of the door.  The ice maker stopped working so I called Sears service and a technician came out.  He stated that the refrigerator had a design flaw beceaseu the wire was continually being pinched by the door as it opened and closed.  The wiers eventually were severed and in doing that exposed a hot wire to the ice maker, this is a potential fire and safety risk to usersThis could have injured someone if it was touched.  The wires will continually be severed as the door opens and closes so the entire dispenser will fail. This is a manuafacturer defect and should be recalled so there are no injuries.  My guess is that they did not have this refrigerator in use long enough to determine that it was a hazard. Now that it is known it should be taken care of.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw leading to severed wires and exposed hot wires, posing a potential fire and safety risk, though no injury occurred.

incident_description: My Kenmore 795.77573600 light bulbs didn't shut off when doors were closed and completely melted the cover.  Now the light sockets are blow out and won't work. The submitter believes the firm is falsely leading consumers about the issues with their products so that consumers are forced to purchase another range.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but was quickly controlled without injury, and the issue was resolved by the submitter.

incident_description: My mother-in-law has a Frigidaire Range Model#FGGF3032MFE. Her Carbon Monoxide detector went off several times. After questioning her as to what she was doing when it went off. She was cooking on the stove top each time. I replicated her action and after an hour a half or boiling water on the stove top the CO detector went off. I contacted Fire Dept who responded and confirmed elevated levels of CO. They checked the stove top and confirmed high level of CO being produced by range. I contacted a repairman who checked for gas leaks and burners which he did not find. Burners displayed a blue clean burn. I contact Frigidaire tech support which was no help whatsoever. It could be a serious issue being ignored. I have several videos I would like to forward with CO meter borrowed from local Fire Dept which show the issue. It occurs when a pot is placed on the quick boil burner. CO meter show it emitting over 200ppm. I'm sure this is going unnoticed by many consumers.
justification: Elevated CO levels from the stove pose a health risk, confirmed by the Fire Dept, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
Filled my Contigo Autoseal Transit Travel Mug, 14oz - Stainless with hot coffee, and screwed on the lid.  A few minutes later, I pressed the button on the mug to depressurize the container before attempting to drink.  The hot coffee sprayed out from under the edges, seams, and side slots on the mug lid.  (Note: This lid is on top of the travel mug lid and is used to lock and unlock the button that allow users to drink from the travel mug.)  Most of the spray came out of the sides and out of the slots on the sides of the lid.  The spray went approximately 3 inches around the mug and was about 1.5 tablespoons of very hot liquid.  I was burned on my chest and had, which required home treatment for several burns that were very painful, though no blistering.  

This type of explosive decompression and spray of hot liquids is very dangerous on several points:

1. Users having the real possibility of unexpectedly receiving serious burns to exposed skin and tissues - possibly blinding someone.
2. Unexpected explosive decompression and spray of hot liquids causing injuries to the user or other people in close proximity to the user. 
3. Unexpected explosive decompression and spray of hot liquids causing injuries to the user or other people in close proximity to the user causing them to react suddenly and possibly cause an accident or injury to themselves and other when operation a vehicle or equipment.
justification: The incident resulted in burns requiring home treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this type of failure is a known issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
Smelled electrical burning coming from the area around our Bosch dishwasher. Looked in the cabinet adjacent to it to try and locate the source. Located Bosch Junction box for the dishwasher. That is where the smell was coming from. The wires going into the box were black from heat and had soot on them. Called Bosch. They told us to call Service Care and they would pay for the diagnostic charge. Service care came out and opened the box. It was badly burned inside. Could have caught our house on fire. Service care said it would be an additional 251.00 to repair and Bosch would not pay it that we would have to. Sent email to Bosch with a picture of the box. Bosch said it was due to a faulty installation. Called Sears where we bought the unit and paid for them to install it. They sent the installer out who had done the installation.
He said the following in writing:
Upon inspection I found a burnt connection where the common wire connects inside the junction box. When I removed the wires on the factory installed side of the box the metal connector block for the hot wire was loose and slid out of the plastic block. When I disconnected the wires from the house side they were all tight. There was obviously a breach of the plastic between the hot and common wire inside the block where the connection was made. this could only be a fault of the factory or parts from the factory. The photos taken show the faulty connection between the hot and common connection block that happened over a period of time. A hole was burned between the hot and common wire in the plastic wall inside the connection block. It was the result of the metal block that connects the hot wire not being secure in the plastic block.

I sent this information to Bosch as well. To date I have not received a response from them. My wife called them on August 9th. They said it was a faulty installation by the installation person. There are many instances of this same thing happening to others. We are still trying to pursue this with Bosch and Sears (installer).
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to faulty wiring, but no actual injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely as it was due to a specific manufacturing or installation fault.

(5/9/16) The consumer turned on the right front burner to medium heat for about 1 minute. The consumer then opened the oven door and noticed that the flame went out. The consumer states that this is a persistent issue since she purchased the range. The consumer decided to test all the burners and noticed when the burners are on low heat and the oven door it opened the flame will go out. However, when the burners are on high heat level and the oven door is opened then the flames get lower and once the oven door is closed the flames get higher.

justification: The incident involves a persistent issue with the burner flame going out when the oven door is opened, but no injury or harm is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased this range in Jun of 2014. It worked correctly at first. After using the broiler several
times we observed damage to the control panel of the unit. As it was under warranty, we
requested a technician to come out. He replaced the control panel. Shortly after the warranty ran
out our oven would not light. I had a third party repair company diagnose the problem and fix it.
It was a faulty igniter and another part. This "other part" was responsible for a gas smell being
emitted from the oven upon lightning. Recently we have observed severe damage to the control
panel and I had to argue with Whirlpool to a) not buy their extended warranty and b) not be
charged for this repair. They agreed. During the course of the diagnosis by their certified
technician the following problems were noted: 1) Control Panel damaged (for the second time)
2) Oven Sensor registered 25 degrees higher than expected and needed to be replaced 3) A
related wiring harness damaged by heat that needed to be replaced 4) The convection fan not
working. This is being replaced 5) The gas regulator for the stove needs to be replaced for orange
flames instead of the standard blue. My dealings with the repair technician were substandard. I
was blamed for both the damage to the control panel and the problem with the orange flames.
After pointing out flaws in his logic he called Whirlpool in both cases. It turns out there is a
known issue with the heat vent which causes the control panel to melt (This was never disclosed
to me even after multiple contacts about this very issue). In the case of the orange flame, the
stove was not dirty but needed a new gas regulator. Dealings with their customer support have
not been much better. They refuse to replace the unit which I believe to be both poorly designed
and an out right lemon under the law. I have included pictures of the damage as well as a heat
gun indication of the control panel temp AFTER their fix was installed. I believe this unit is
dangerous above all else. Please help me rectify this situation with a replacement range.
justification: The incident involves repeated equipment failures and safety hazards like gas leaks and overheating, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
Fire hazard -- there was smoke noted inside my GE Profile Refrigerator, Model PWE23KMKES, serial number GG502393.  It is a French door model with a lower freezer compartment.  My granddaughter opened the door of the refrigerator and the refrigerator compartment was filled with smoke.  There was condensate on most of the food products and the temp was 39 degrees and falling.  The food was all removed and taken to another refrigerator/freezer in the garage.    Later, after unplugging the appliance, we noted the deli tray would not open.  When more force was applied, the deli tray was freed to open.  The plastic interior had a hole burned in it and the tray could not open because it was fused to the back wall by the burning plastic.  

I'm convinced that if we had not been home, there would have been a resulting fire.  I took pictures of the hole in the back panel.  It was large enough to place my hand through the opening.  If we hadn't unplugged the unit, there would have been a risk of a fire.  If you want pictures of the interior affected, please request and I will send pictures. 

I tried to speak with people at GE to see whether there has already been a recall on that product and gave up after several attempts.  Their website did not list a recall on this product.
justification: Smoke and burning plastic indicate a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On July 15, 2017, I had an alarming and dangerous incident.  I cooked a salmon patty in my Pyrex glassware dish at 450 degrees for 15 minutes.  I removed the dish from the oven, and before I had the chance to put it down, the glassware violently exploded in my hand, sending shards of glass flying toward my face and throughout my kitchen and the adjoining hallway.

My stove, countertop, kitchen floor, hallway floor were covered in large pieces of shattered glass and small shards of it, everywhere. Fortunately, I was wearing my reading glasses, which I believe protected my eyes from injury.  

I attempted to clean up the mess, but the glassware was still hot and burned my fingers and hands.  The heat also caused it to adhere to my kitchen floor, making it very difficult to remove.  On six separate occasions since the incident, I have stepped (in my stocking feet) on remaining pieces of glass that were missed during the clean-up.  

My fully-cooked meal, other pieces of glassware in the vicinity of the incident, my oven mitt used for clean-up and the nearby sponge had to be thrown out, in case they had shards of glass in them that I could accidentally ingest at a later date. Clean-up took about 20 minutes or so.  I had to recook a meal in alternate cookware, clean the counter diligently, and sweep and mop my floor.  All of this cost me time, money, expensive food, material goods, upset, burned fingers and hands, and a singed kitchen floor.  It frightened me greatly and has made me feel unsafe in my own house.

I am appalled that Pyrex is aware of this explosion issue in their now-altered Pyrex dishes, yet continues to defend their products.  I no longer have faith in their company or products and will make certain my loved ones are aware of the hazards involved in using these glassware dishes.  

Thank you for following up on my complaint.
justification: The incident caused burns to fingers and hands, and multiple instances of stepping on glass shards, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but can occur with improper use of glassware.

After the warranty expired I began having episodes where the oven handle was becoming loose from the oven door.  I eventually had to frequently refasten but sometime, the handle fell off on one side. Then both handles fell off.  On one occasion, both handles fell off and the oven door layers split over and the front glass layer fell hard on my shin. I certainly did not abuse my glass out the oven door - the defective handle assembly did!  I fear the use of this range again for these reasons. I support a recall to force Sears to back their defective product and be fair with their customers.  I have my original receipts and a useless range sitting in my kitchen.

incident_description:
On December 15, 2013, my client, 32-year-old [REDACTED], suffered serious injuries while operating a newly purchased NinjaÃÂ Master PrepÃÂ Professional blender in the kitchen of the apartment she shared with her husband [REDACTED], and 16-month-old son [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] bought the blender approximately two weeks before [REDACTED]ÃÂs injury. Before her injury,[REDACTED] had never used the blender.
 	
The blender came with two containers for blending, chopping, and mixing ÃÂ a large ÃÂPitcherÃÂ and a small ÃÂBowl.ÃÂ Each container had its own blades and its own ÃÂSplash Guard.ÃÂ An interchangeable ÃÂMaster PodÃÂ powers the blender in either configuration when users press the on/off pulse button. (See uploaded User Guide.)

The Pitcher assembly includes an interlock system that prevents Master Pod activation unless the Splash Guard is affixed securely to the Pitcher, effectively shielding the spinning blades from user contact.

Inexplicably, the Bowl assembly does not have any similar safety system. 

If an inexperienced user attempting to assemble the blender in its Bowl configuration inadvertently presses the on/off pulse button after inserting the blades through the Bowl Splash Guard into the Master Pod, the exposed blades will activate, inflicting serious injuries.

Shortly before noon, [REDACTED] was attempting to feed [REDACTED], who was particularly fussy that morning. He was crying inconsolably; he would not eat his minestrone soup. She had an idea that if she pureed the soupÃÂs vegetables and pasta, [REDACTED] might be more inclined to eat his lunch. She decided to try this using the new Ninja blender.

She retrieved the blender components from the counter, poured [REDACTED]ÃÂs soup in the blender Bowl, and attempted to put together the blades, Splash Guard, and Master Pod to complete the assembly.

She must have inadvertently pressed the on/off pulse button on the Master Pod, because suddenly, without warning, the exposed blades started spinning in her hand, inflicting severe laceration injuries to her right hand, index finger and middle finger.

[REDACTED] contends the blender was defective primarily because the blender Bowl configuration did not have an interlock system ÃÂ like the Pitcher configuration ÃÂ to prevent the exposed blades from spinning and inflicting injury when a user inadvertently presses on/off pulse button.
justification: The incident resulted in severe laceration injuries to the user's hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the lack of an interlock system in the Bowl configuration makes such injuries possible for inexperienced users.

incident_description:
On July 16, 2017 i purchased a Kenmore upright freezer model #253.22042410.  The freezer was delivered two days later on the 18th.  Later that day my wife and I went to the garage to put some food in the freezer.  When my wife went to open the freezer, it started tipping over on top of her.  Luckily I was there to catch the freezer.  If I had not been in the garage with her, it would have fallen on top of her and probably caused serious injuries if not worse.  If it had been one of my grandchildren they would probably be dead.  The problem was caused because the magnets holding the door closed were so strong that the door would not open, so when you pull on the door handle, you can literally pull the freezer over.  I lowered the adjustment feet, to the maximum that they can be lowered so that the freezer now tilts backward and can't fall forward.  However, the instructions state that the freezer must be leveled.  I ignored the instructions for safety purposes.  Once the feet were lowered the freezer would not fall forward, but it still will not open.  When you pull on the handle to open the freezer, you can literally drag it across the floor.  The magnets are that powerful.  A 200 lb. freezer with food in it and you can drag it across the floor. I contacted customer service and they sent out a technician to look at the freezer and determine that it needed to be replaced, which it did.  The second freezer was delivered on July 27th.  The delivery personnel removed the old freezer and put it on the truck.  They then unloaded and unpacked the the new freezer and put it into place in my garage,  I tried to open the freezer and the same problem existed with the door.  Also when they plugged in the freezer, it didn't run.  They had to take the second freezer, load it back onto the truck and put the original freezer back, at least it runs.  On Aug. 15, a month after the original freezer was ordered, Sears delivered a third freezer, and went through all of the same motions to put the new freezer into place.  When I went to open the third freezer, the same problem existed.  When I pulled on the door handle, the freezer did not open, it just slid across the floor with me.  Since the original freezer was already on the truck, I told the delivery personnel to just leave the third freezer and i would talk to the store manager. 
So now we have a fourth freezer ordered with no anticipated delivery date.  
In my opinion there is something inherently wrong with this model that needs to be resolved before someone gets hurt.
justification: The incident involved a freezer tipping over, which could have caused serious injuries or death, but no actual injuries occurred due to immediate intervention.

The burners have to be turned to the high setting in order for the igniter to start the flame.   Currently, the burners spew high amounts of gas and air at the same time, which causes the problem.  The consumer removed the burner cap and looked underneath it and viewed the base.  This is a 17K burner.  Underneath that cap, there are instructions: "add choke and screw for LP gas.ÃÂ  The consumer reviewed his ownerÃÂs manual and saw that this information was not referenced in the manual.  The consumer went on-line and searched for more information on this "choke and screw" verbiage for his brand of range.  He did not located information on this verbiage for his range, but he did find this verbiage mentioned with General Electric ranges.  The consumer was also able to view the schematics of the rang/oven on-line.

By then, he had already spoken with the mfr. several times about this issue.  He asked the mfr. for this (choke and screw) part, but they did not have any information about it.  He was referred to their Parts Dept., but the rep. in that department was not aware of this part or verbiage.  They were aware of a "complete conversion kit".  The consumer asked for a breakdown of what would be in the kit, but he could not identify if the part he needed would be included.

The consumer made several more calls to the manufacturerÃÂs Customer Care Division, but there were no new developments.  He then left a message with [REDACTED] , who is the president for the mfrÃÂs North American Div.  On 4/18/2017, he also sent a physical letter to Mr. [REDACTED] expressing his concerns.


The consumer found a Training Bulletin (32-05) with more information on this "choke and screw" feature, dated 3/2005, which indicated that there may be an erratic flame that could cause injury if this part was not applied to the burner.  This choke and screw part is essentially a #10" screw (metric) that is  has a 7/8" hole, where the gas is emitted.  The choke appears to reduce the hole by half of that size.

Based on the consumer's communication with the company, he has not been able to determine if they actually manufacture the part.   The consumer is willing to pay for the part, but indicated that the part should have been installed on the range/oven, when he purchased it or provided with the unit at the time of purchased.

I have never used the self cleaning feature of the oven.  The oven door has never been compromised or disturbed in any manner.

While preheating the oven to 350 degrees on dinner time. The oven door glass shattered and glass flew all over the floor and inside of the oven while the temperature was around 200 degrees.

This unexpected shattering of glass is not safe for adults, children, or pets.
justification: The oven door shattered unexpectedly, posing a safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Jenn-Air M170W Built-In Microwave Oven
My son (24 yr old) started the microwave and it worked normally at first but then stopped with time left on the clock. He was attempting to heat some chili in a glass Pyrex bowl (something we have done many many times before). The microwave had not been used within the previous hour. He hit cancel and then started it again but this time although the timer counted down, the inside light didn't come on, the turntable didn't start, and no other noise came from the microwave (fan, etc) so he hit the cancel button. While he was asking what happened to the microwave and what to try next, he smelled smoke like an electrical fire shortly followed by visible flames coming from behind the control panel.

We quickly put out the fire with a fire extinguisher, which limited the fire damage to inside the microwave but of course made a big mess in the kitchen. I removed the microwave and took off the outer case. The switches and plastic switch stack inside the control area are what started on fire and burned.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire in the microwave, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The outer layer of the glass oven door exploded.
The range is a GE 30-inch, purchased May 2015.
Product code is JB640DFBT.

The oven was in use at the time.
justification: The oven door glass exploded during use, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I was using a cutting board on top of the cooktop.  I didn't have anything turned on.  I heard a click, and the back right burner went on.  It would not go off, no matter how we turned the dial.  I turned it off at the circuit breaker.  I researched it and found a recall for this range in 2009.  We were never informed.
justification: The burner turned on unexpectedly but was turned off without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: The product is an Emerilware non-stick frying pan.  While I was frying a hamburger, a metal grommet  popped off and into the food.  It was visible in the frying pan because it was just a burger, but if it was something bigger, it would have not been noticeable in the food and it would have been swallowed.
justification: A metal grommet popped off into the food, posing a potential hazard if unnoticed, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
Please allow me to introduce myself:
My name is [REDACTED]
I Wal Mart grill Model #  GRD 20. This grill is absolutely UNSAFE and should not be sold.
Please let me explain and please refer to the pictures. As you can see the temperature of this grill heats to 400.
I went to  cook some pancakes on this grill, and when I put my hands under it to turn its position my fingers  got
extremely burned, and I was in excruciating pain. Thank God my neighbor is a nurse and she  put on [REDACTED] and bandages to relieve the pain.

I bet you wont even bother to address this problem but in case you do
I can be contacted at
Phone # [REDACTED]
Thank You
justification: The user suffered severe burns requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The Cuisinart-Conair recall of Food processor blades (2016-2017) prompted a close inspection of my mini-prep food processor, also manufactured by Cuisinart.  This small processor has a model number DLC-1TX, Type 21.
The two part standard (but small) blade has this number stamped on one of the blades: SHARP FP-099TX.
Inspection of the hollow ring housing the blade(s) reveals several cracks in the plastic that extend through the plastic completely. This small appliance has been only lightly and infrequently used through the years, always hand-washed and allowed to air dry in a semi-arid environment.  This kind of breakdown should not be occurring. I am afraid the blade will come completely out of its housing,  and I will discontinue use of it.
justification: The cracked plastic housing poses a risk of the blade coming loose, but no injury has occurred yet. The likelihood is possible given the visible damage and prior recall.

incident_description: Grating blade for Cuisinart DLC7-E. After I registered for the recall for the cutting blade I went through all of my blades to check for rivets. The fixed stem grating blade had 3 rivets which held it on. These were missing and thankfully we were not aware that they had been lost into our food. I called the companies consumer help line and I was appalled to hear that I could purchase a new blade from them. They were not concerned that my family and friends could have been injured. You need to inform the public about this danger. The recall should be for all blades with rivets.
justification: The incident involved missing rivets in a grating blade, posing a potential hazard, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher failed to turn off the heating element at the end of wash cycle resulting in potential fire hazard
justification: The dishwasher's heating element failing to turn off poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: 6-8 incidents of dishwasher heater staying on long past the dry cycle. Appears our model is on recall list
justification: The dishwasher heater staying on past the dry cycle is an incident with no reported injury, and the model being on recall list indicates this is likely to occur.

incident_description: I purchased my Cuisinart toaster oven (TOB-40) 3 years ago. About 1 year ago I noticed the front coil had a small warp to it, however I did not think much of it at the time. Today the warp has become significantly worse and was actually touching the bottom crumb tray and caused a small fire inside of the toaster oven. I immediately looked online and have come across numerous complaints over the past 4 years regarding this toaster oven. It is very dangerous and should be recalled nationally due to his long history of safety issues.
justification: The incident involved a small fire but no injury, and online complaints suggest this issue is likely to occur.

incident_description:
In January 2017, I purchased a GE stove from Lowe's in Rio Rancho NM. Since then, I get a massive pressure headache, eye swelling, and other neurological symptoms when the oven is in use. These symptoms last for days and some "may be permanent' according to my doctor. I have followed the manufacturer instructions to get rid of the toxic smell but it has not worked and, not to mention, makes me feel horrible. I have even tried to run the oven with adequate ventilation to no avail. 
I thought, at first, that maybe it was not due to the oven and have seen many doctors, specialists, and 2 neurologists to help me rule out other possible illnesses. I am even being sent out of state to a special specialist, in October, for further testing. 
While searching the internet,  I have also come across numerous others complaining about the same symptoms in relation to their new ovens. This is scary confirmation and I have since removed the oven from my house.
I am an athlete and I pride myself on being active and busy. This GE Oven has taken this away from me. Now just putting on my shoes gives my brain a painful reminder of my current state. I am hoping that my report will bring to light a big problem in industry today so others do not have to suffer as I am.
justification: The incident describes severe neurological symptoms and potential permanent damage, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the user's report and similar complaints found online.

incident_description: The Frigidaire oven model PLEB27S9DCA was warming to a temperature of 400 degrees when there was a shorting, electrical sound. Smoke started from the electronic display. The LED display lit all components and flashed. Flames started coming out of the electronics with thick black smoke. I turned off the circuit break and the fire stopped. It was limited to the electronics. I removed the oven to get it out to prevent a possible re-ignition. We are the original owners of the oven.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the oven's electronics, but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was contained.

incident_description: Frigidaire refrigerator caught on fire. Defrosting turkey juices drained through improperly sealed tube opening onto the compressor starter.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire due to a technical issue, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Used the sensor button on microwave for a potato. Microwave did not stop, potato caught on fire causing glass plate to crack and plastic motor drive to be damaged. Control panel needs to be replaced. This model was already involved in a recall just not my serial number. Whirlpool was contacted and will repair unit free of charge but will not admit a safety problem.
justification: The incident caused property damage (fire, cracked plate, damaged motor drive) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Bought a Monogram Direct Air Convection Built in Electric Double Wall Oven. It was installed on June 1, 2017 by a professional appliance installer. 

The first use of this oven was Saturday Night June 3, 2017. After cooking a baked chicken for dinner, we wanted to try out the self cleaning mode to keep the upper oven spotless. About 1 hour into the self cleaning of the upper oven exploded with a loud noise. Glass was everywhere, fine shard pieces of glass are in the upper oven, bottom oven, and all over the floor. 
Absolutely furious that this is an acceptable design by GE Monogram and come to find out extremely common.
justification: The incident involved an oven exploding during self-cleaning, causing glass shards to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I started my 9-year old GE Profile dishwasher at approximately 10 pm at night, and then went to bed. At approximately 7 am the following morning I noticed that the counter above the unit was very warm. When I opened the unit I discovered that the heated drying cycle was still active. Temperatures in the interior of the unit were hot enough to melt plastic - silverware had melted through the plastic silverware basket and started to melt into the plastic tub; plastic container tops in the top rack had completely melted and dripped down onto dishes in the lower rack.

Heat continued to pour out of the unit until I turned off the circuit breaker.  After letting the unit cool and removing it from under the counter it became clear that insulation on various connectors had become discolored due to the heat.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (melted plastic and discolored insulation) but no reported injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
On June 7th, Commerce Fire was dispatched to [REDACTED], for a residential structure fire, with fire behind dishwasher. Upon arrival, occupants had evacuated and were outside,  light smoke showing from [REDACTED] side of home blowing to the south.  Two fire fighters made entry into home with a co2 extinguisher and  found smoke through out home. Dish washer in kitchen had been pulled out from under counter top and flames and smoke coming out of rear of dishwasher.  Fire fighters used extinguisher and extinguished flames.  A PPV fan was placed at front door to ventilate, main breaker to electrical panel was turned off, water supply was turned off at dishwasher, and then dishwasher was removed from home and placed on the back deck. Ventilation continued and a thermal imaging camera was used to verify fire had not extended to other areas.  Fire Marshal arrived and took photos for report.  Female homeowner stated she was home using the dishwasher when smoke began to appear.  She moved the dishwasher away from the wall and began to see flames, called 911, evacuated her and her children from the residence and shut the front door on the way outside.  She stated she had been smelling an electrical smell off and on from dishwasher for the last couple weeks.  She stated her Husband checked it and didn't believe there was any issues.  Fire and heat damage to attached cabinets and part of wood floor.  After ventilation was complete FD cleared the scene without incident.

Model: Bosch Super Silence 42dBA
Model # SHX7ER55UC/50
Serial# SD6P5B013010266999017697
justification: The incident involved a residential fire with no injuries or deaths, but caused property damage.

incident_description: As I was baking my stove/oven began popping and sparking. There was no error code and no warning. Smoke  starts billowing out of the back of the stove and sparks fly from underneath. After removing the panel to the glass top stove (and cutting off the breaker) the internals of the stove are melted, this includes metal that now looks like solder. My fall has scorch marks and the stove is useless. I'm fortunate my home didn't burn down.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the stove and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The Circulon pot glass lid made a booming sound like an explosion and shattered in to numerous pieces. It not only destroyed what was cooking inside the pot, but also tiny glass pieces got in to the dishes that were prepared and lying nearby. Fortunately,. 

This Circulon pot was purchased at Macy's.
justification: The incident involved a pot lid shattering, causing damage to food and nearby dishes, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We purchased this electric teak kettle some 3-4 yrs ago. It has had very little use. The model # is KP728R and it is a chocolate brown plastic unit. I walked by it the other day and just happen to touch the unit and it was extremely hot and it had not been in use for days. The on/off switch was set to OFF. I asked my wife if she had used it and she replied in the negative. I left it plugged in and the next day I touched it again and it was again, extremely hot as though it had just been used to boil water. Worried that it may cause a fire I unplugged the unit. We will not use it again as we are afraid that it cold short and cause a fire.
justification: The kettle was extremely hot without being in use, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: My LG LDE3037ST range did not turn off the oven infrared burner even though it did not indicate that the burner was on.  After removing power from the range the problem reset and the range was operational again.  Since this is not a "defective part", it seems this problem is intrinsic to the design and probably a safety issue.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven burner without injury, and the issue was resolved by resetting the power.

incident_description:
The consumer indicated that this is a replacement range because the range they purchased in 2012 had the same safety defect and after it was repaired twice they requested a refund. She said the replacement is a similar model but it is not the same model.

The consumer's husband used the control knob to set the right rear burner to a 3-4 heat level and he began to cook bacon. The consumer's husband walked away for 3 minutes and when he returned the rear burner was extremely red and hot. The bacon was burned and close to catching on fire. The consumer believes the rear burner heated to a higher temperature on its own because the burner should not be that hot when it's on a 3-4 heat level.

The consumer said the burners heat to different temperatures unexpectedly and it has been intermittently for the past 3 years but today was the most severe incident. She indicated that the left rear burner is the only burner that does not display this issue. The consumer said she began calling Sears to report this issue approximately 6 months after she purchased the range and she has complained multiple times over the past 3 years.

The consumer contacted Sears today and informed them of the incident. The consumer asked for them to investigate the issue since this is the second range that has this safety defect and she said they seemed unwilling and they advised her unless the range was unusable they wouldn't go out to repair it.
justification: The incident involved a safety defect causing a burner to overheat, leading to burned food and a near-fire situation, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My electric range started to turn on automatically. First it would be only momentarily, but today I woke up in the moring with one of the surfaces completly RED. Thankfully I didn't let a pan on top of it otherwise the story could have been so differently. I bought the stove at Sears, call them and told me I had to call the manufacturer, but they could fix it for a fee. I think they should be responsible for the product they sell. I just sent a message to the manufacturer. But I think they should have let people know of this, it is a FIRE HAZARD.

KENMORE ELECTRIC RANGE
MODEL 790.92803010
Serial vf02464650
justification: The electric range turning on automatically poses a significant fire hazard, though no injury occurred this time.

incident_description:
I bought a Whrilpool Gas Range, Model Number WFG710H0AH 0 Serial Number R21410291. I've had had problems with this range since I bought it. The oven won't light unless you manually light it with a match and even then it will go out and leak gas. Whirlpool has sent out someone to fix the problem about 3 or 4 times, each time they told me it was fixed and each time it would work for a few months then go right back to the same thing. I have been removing the bottom draw and lighting it there, but now it just goes out and still leaks gas.

I've told them its a hazard leaking the gas and it not lighting. They didn't want to send anyone out but I kept insisting and they finally did. The problem has never stopped.

The range is about 4 to 5 years old and barely used due to the gas leak problem.

It seems like our house has to blow up before someone fixes this problem.
justification: The gas leak and failure to light pose a significant hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
(11/28/2016) The consumer stated that he smelled gas right after the product was installed.  The consumer contacted the firm. A technician came out. A part had to be ordered. After the part was installed the consumer was advised that it is normal to smell gas.

The consumer stated that he takes a while for the oven to ignite
Also, flames occasionally comes from the vent on the top of the stove.

(07/09/2017) The consumer stated that his wife turned on the oven to preheat to 500 degrees. After about ten minutes, she opened the door. When she opened the oven door, six inch flames shot out of the oven. The flames singed her eyebrows, arms, eyelashes  and her hairline.

The consumer stated that flames shot out before when she preheated the oven to 350 degrees but the flames were not as high.

No medical attention was required.

(07/10/2017) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that the product was not on warranty nor on recall.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (singed eyebrows, arms, eyelashes, and hairline) but no medical attention was required, and similar incidents have occurred multiple times.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the rack inside the oven falls three to four times out of every five uses. How long it takes for the rack to fall after the oven has been turned on depends on what level inside the unit the rack is located on.

07/14/2017 - The consumer contacted the retailer and explained the situation. She was advised to purchase new racks as it would fix the problem however when the racks were purchased, the problem persisted.

The consumer states that the oven is used approximately five to six times per week between thirty minutes to two hours.

The consumer is unsure if she will keep her oven for the next thirty days.
justification: The incident involves a rack falling frequently but no injury is reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence is almost certain given the high frequency of the issue.

incident_description:
i recently purchased a GE gas,convection range from Home Depot,model #JGB720SEJSS Andora,after having the range for a few days,we were using the oven and broiler,for a lengthy amount of time,we realized there is a heat shied installed in the back of the cooktop area,which i think protects the digital componants,like the timer and controls in the back of the gas range above the cooktop area,this heat shield gets extremely hot,and without know how hot it really can get,i myself got burned several time,while using the stove.I think this is extremely unsafe for children and the elderly using the stove.Outside of the actual burners there should be no place on that cooktop that should get that hot,to burn someone,i contacted Home Depot about the situation and they blew me off and said to contact GE,i called several time and never got a reply from them.I really think this is a very dangerous situation,and i felt i should report it.

                                               Thank you

incident_description:
Cuisinart toaster over model MOB 40.
Heating element sags, touches bottom of oven, burns out.
Many incidents of this. 
Some are reported here...
https://www.saferproducts.gov/Search/Result.aspx?dm=0&m=TOB-40&srt=0&t=2
Shock hazard.
Fire hazard.
Yes, ours failed yesterday after two years of service.
It went out with a spark and a hissing noise and overheating.
