incident_description: I was saute/cooking in the pressure cooker. It was not pressurized. It was open as I was not finish adding product. Suddenly I heard a whoosh sound. Then the base was glowing. Next fire began to blow out of the plug port. I unplugged it and it went out.
justification: The incident involved a fire starting from the pressure cooker, which could have caused injury but was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
We have a new ge stove that came with the new condo. It's really a nice stove. Unfortunately the low temperature on the stove is not low. It's more of a medium high. If you are trying to cook a sauce on low, you will burn the sauce as well as the pan. Unfortunately when I lifted the lid the sauce was boiling and splashed onto my index finger, burning my finger.  This also happened to my wife, however she did not burn herself.
    Low temperature dial is not a low and am concerned that others may experience the same. I hope this will help prevent further issues.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the finger, and the issue with the stove's temperature control makes recurrence likely for others.

incident_description:
The plastic handle on the glass lid of the crockpot broke off while being (hand) washed.
That caused the glass lid to fall into the sink rack.
If this would happen while using the crockpot, the glass lid could fall and break into the food in the crockpot. Or splash scalding liquid on the person using it. If it fell on your foot it could cut, or break a toe.
justification: The incident could result in injury from broken glass or scalding liquid, but no death is mentioned. The likelihood is possible as it depends on usage conditions.

incident_description:
((06/28/2017) The consumer stated that the oven had not been in use since the night before. The consumer was putting a pan in the cabinet which is two cabinet doors away from the stove. The outer glass of the oven door exploded and sent glass about 15 feet into her living room. The glass from the oven door was popping on the floor.

The consumer stated that glass hit her on the left side of her face . Glass also cut her arm between her shoulder and her elbow. The consumer washed her arm with soap and cold water but got a burning sensation about five hours afterwards. 

The consumer contacted the poison control center because she thought she had a chemical burn. She was advised to keep washing her arm. The burning stopped later after the consumer took a shower.

(07/01/2017) The consumer contacted the firm. The consumer was advised that the firm had never heard of the type of incident before. The consumer was referred to a service company but was advised that the repair would be at her expense because the unit was out of warranty.
justification: The consumer sustained injuries from glass cuts and a chemical burn sensation, requiring medical advice but no hospitalization.

incident_description:
Potential Fire Hazzard

The whirlpool range gas stove, the knobs turn on very easily, if I reached over the stove, walk by or mistakenly touch the knobs.  The knobs touched lightly turned the gas on and I have to turn it off.  The knobs touched slightly turns on without the gas unknowingly, caused leaked gas and explosion.

I don't usually have breakfast, decided to get breakfast, turned on the stove and a very loud band.  All I saw was fire completely covered the area where the gas leaked over the entire stove.  I was thrown back from shock after the fire cleared.  I looked at the knobs and saw that the knob on the right end of the stove was slight turned on, which apparently leaked gas from an unknown time.

I complained to Master's Limited in Bermuda, where I purchased the stove only 5 months old under warranty, to no avail.  The Manager suggest it's not a defective under warranty, I disagree.

This is a potential fire hazard, I could be dead today had the leaked continued without knowledge and who  would have known it was a gas leak?

The knobs have no safety mechanism to prevent turning on.  What will happen, if a child mistaken touch the knobs?   The results fire or unknown gas leak and an explosion.

How do you prevent this from happening in a resident home, it's not possible.

Kindly consider product recall, design a safety knob to prevent easily turning on or there's serious risk for fire and explosions from this unsafe product.

Kind regards.
justification: The incident involved a fire and explosion due to a gas leak, causing the individual to be thrown back from shock, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: The oven was on at 350 degrees for about 10 mins when the front glass shattered.
justification: The oven glass shattered, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I've burned myself while pouring boiled water from Proctor Silex Hot Pot, 32 Oz. Electric Hot Pot-45805.  Medical treatment was not necessary.  The hot pot has vents on the top, immediately adjacent to the handle.  When pouring, steam exists the vents and contacts the user's hand.  I don't understand how the product made it past the manufacturer's safety test, or how it obtained UL approval.
justification: The user sustained a burn injury from steam while pouring boiled water, but no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the microwave was getting hot around where the bulb is located. The consumer took the front off for inspection and noticed that the front panel is cracked due to the heat; the surrounding bulb area also has parts melting.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that because his unit has never been recalled and is no longer under warranty, there is nothing they could do to assist him free of charge.

The consumer states that he uses his microwave approximately five times a day.

The consumer plans on keeping his microwave for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The microwave showed signs of overheating and damage, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have an Elite Platinum Electric Tea Kettle by Maxi-Matic.  I filled the carafe and started the unit to boil the water. At the end of the cycle when I lifted the carafe off of the base unit, I found that there where 2 melted plastic blobs on the base unit.  Upon further investigation I found a whole melted on the carafe bottom that was exposing internal wiring.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric kettle that caused melting and exposed wiring, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
the glass door on my electric range exploded and glass shattered all over the inside of the oven and when I opened the oven door.  This was a new range and the oven had only been used twice before.  I was baking a potato at 425 degrees, and after 20 minutes, heard a loud popping noise coming from the kitchen.  When I opened the oven door, there was glass flying everywhere inside the oven and onto the kitchen floor.  I quickly closed the door and turned off the oven.  It continued to pop and explode for another 10 minutes or so. 
When it stopped, i opened the door and glass was all over the bottom of the oven.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering inside the oven but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
GE built-in microwave oven caught fire, reportedly when timer function was activated - not cooking. Model JVM1540SM5SS  Serial No AA2103966 L, date of manufacture January 2013, install date approximately Dec 2014 (?) 

Damage limited to the oven itself, primarily melted interior plastic parts in top of cooking area, plus minor smoke damage to surrounding cabinetry.
justification: The incident involved a microwave fire causing damage to the oven and minor smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I recently purchased an 18 piece set of Pyrex storage containers and a set of Pyrex mixing bowls through Amazon from World Kitchens LLC. I used the rectangle dish to freeze yogurt as the product indicated it was freezer safe. It was in my freezer 2 days before we ate the yogurt and sat the rinsed dish in the dishwasher. The dishwasher was not started. The next day, with the dishwasher interior at room temperature and the door closed, the dish LOUDLY and spontaneously exploded all over the inside of my dishwasher as my husband sat reading the newspaper at our kitchen island. There were shards of glass everywhere.  My husband and elderly Mother both are on blood thinners. What if this had exploded in their hands instead??  I must emphasize, this dish was sitting undisturbed and at room temperature when it spontaneously shattered. It had never been exposed to heat, only cold. I've asked for a refund from Amazon. It is extremely irresponsible and negligent of  this company to allow this product on the market given the number of horror stories I'm now reading online about similar product failures.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous product failure with potential for injury, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore stand alone electric ceramic top range that I purchased in 2008.  Last evening, a minute or two after I took my dinner out of the over and turned it off, the front glass panel shattered into many sharp pieces.  I didn't see it happen, but it was quite loud.  I have pictures, if needed.  To my knowledge, nothing had scratched or damaged the glass.  I live alone so no one else would have damaged it either.
justification: The glass panel shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer states that when coffee is being served, steam escapes from the hinge of the coffee pot and burns your fingers and hands.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; the Manufacturer replaced the carafe.

The consumer indicates that the unit is used once daily.

The consumer plans on keeping the carafe for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involves burns to fingers and hands, indicating an injury (severity 3). The unit is used daily, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: 10" Cuisinart skillet. Frying hash browns on medium heat when a metal disc (end cap) from inside the pan handle shot across the room. Considering the trajectory and speed: if it had hit a living entity it would have caused serious injury/death.
justification: The metal disc could have caused serious injury or death if it hit someone, but the incident itself is unlikely to recur frequently.

incident_description: The above range microwave started blowing bulbs constantly so much as causing the glass cover to break. I thought I had received bad bulbs so I switched to a led bulb and purchased a new glass. Yesterday, the express option just started going on its own. The microwave was continuously running. At this point I had unplugged it.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The issue is likely to recur given the described behavior.

incident_description:
(04/25/2017) The consumer that he was toasting bread. After the bread popped up, the consumer assumed that the unit shut off. About two or three minutes his wife noticed that the toaster did not shut off. The consumer noticed that the unit was getting very hot. Inside of the unit was red. The consumer could smell the plastic housing on the outside of the unit. 

The consumer shut the unit off.
justification: The toaster malfunctioned and overheated, but the consumer noticed and turned it off without injury.

incident_description:
The submitter used the juice extractor on April 9 at approximately 7pm.

On April 10, the submitter said he used the microwave to heat up milk for his daughter. The submitter and his family got ready and left the apartment as part of their Monday morning routine. He said the juice extractor was still plugged into the wall along with the microwave. The submitter said the microwave was not damaged from the fire and the outlet was not burned.

A few hours later the submitter was notified that his apartment caught fire and he rushed to the scene. The submitter said once he arrived the fire department had put out the fire. He said the fire investigator provided him with the fire report (incident # 2017-004438) which states that the fire was caused from the juice extractor and the cause of ignition is unintentional.

The submitter said his dog was in the apartment when the fire took place and his dog has smoke inhalation. The submitter made an itemized list of items lost during the fire and he states that it is approximately $50,000. 

On April 11, the submitter contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The firm requested a copy of the fire departments report and he sent the firm a copy. The firm also told the submitter to leave the fire scene untouched. On April 17, the firm sent out [REDACTED], with SEA Limited to examine the fire scene. She could easily have suffered a laceration to her arm or leg which could have resulted in a laceration to the radial or femoral artery. 

There is a warning on the lid, but it is a small 1 inch square sticker, light grey sticker on dark grey plastic. The lid does lock in place, but I don't think it's unusual to remove the lid from a blender. There should be some form of friction or locking mechanism, the blade assembly should not slip out as easily as it does.

I just wanted to share this story maybe it would help. Maybe the Manufacturers should warn people that have Cats to use extreme care. Looks like we will dispose of the unit and purchase one that has knobs. WE are contacting an Electrician to find out the feasibility of installing an on off switch under the counter.

incident_description:
This complaint is about a "Joyce Chen 22-9938, Pro Chef 14 Inch 10 Piece Excalibur Non-Stick Wok Set" that I purchased on July 1, 2017 from Amazon. (https://smile.amazon.com/dp/B000684DUE/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_dp_T2_unMBzbJYP5NAG)

As a volunteer firefighter and a professional distiller, I am very familiar with fire/burn hazards, and I state with confidence that this is a dangerous product that should not be used. The company should issue a recall immediately. On only the second use, all three rivets holding the handle on failed. There was only 8oz of food, so it was not a weight issue. I was frying tofu, and when they failed, the body of the wok went flying across the stove, scattering hot tofu everywhere, including on my hand (leaving several burns). Had there been more oil in the wok, this could easily have started a grease fire and/or caused severe burns.

Upon closer inspection of the rivets, they are made of soft metal and can be easily deformed with a small pliers. Although the gauge of the rivets is sufficient for the sheer load, the secondary heads are far too weak for the tension load when the wok is manipulated via the long handle. Indeed, the rivets failed so completely at the secondary heads that there is no visible evidence left that the rivets were ever even closed. The weakness of these rivets is a critical design flaw.

Though painful, the burns that I suffered when the rivet failure caused the product to rapidly disassemble were only superficial wounds. The next person might not be as fortunate. It is only a matter of time before this wok causes a fire or serious injury. Please issue a recall before this happens.
justification: The incident resulted in burns (injury) and the description suggests a high likelihood of recurrence due to a critical design flaw.

incident_description:
On Sunday, April 23, I was at home when I started to smell something burning. I had turned my dishwasher on a few minutes earlier and thought maybe something dropped to the bottom and was burning.  I opened the door of my three-year-old Bosch dishwasher and checked around and saw that nothing was on the bottom.  I closed the door and heard a ÃÂpopÃÂ and smoke began billowing out of my dishwasher! All of the controls on the door had gone black, too. I got my fire extinguisher out just in case and checked around the sides to make sure I didnÃÂt see flames.  Smoke was pouring out from underneath my sink as well so I was really concerned about a fire.  After about 20 minutes, the smoke dissipated and I felt safe again.   Monday, I called Prestige Appliance, where I purchased the dishwasher, and set up a service call for April 27. When the repairman pulled the dishwasher out, the right back side was black with soot, as was the wall behind it. At this point, I expected that they would offer to replace the appliance, but he said they were only authorized to repair. I politely told him that I expect nothing less than a replacement.  He called Bosch and started a file to reference the situation and told me that Bosch would contact me in the next few days.  Before he left, I asked him if I had done anything wrong to cause the appliance to literally burn up? He assured me it was nothing I had done, and that there had been a recall a few years prior due to a short electrical cord. I asked him if this was the case with my dishwasher and he assured me that there was plenty of cord on mine. 

On Tuesday, May 2, I had still not heard from Bosch or Prestige Appliance, so I called both, getting the run-around about how Prestige sent the information but Bosch didnÃÂt have it. Meanwhile, today is May 4th and I called Bosch customer service and was told that they are still reviewing the situation and that they should get back to me within the next few days. (more placating)  

I am very concerned that Bosch does not want to take my dishwasher and inspect it to find out why it nearly caught on fire. I believe that this situation is very serious and there could be others that may be at risk due to a defect in this product. I decided that it was important to report it to you since it seems that Bosch isn't taking it seriously.

incident_description:
Hello,
I purchased a Samsung 5.8 cu. ft. Slide-In Electric Flex Duo Range with Dual Door (model NE58K9850WG/AA) last fall.  It is an oven with a smooth cook-top and burner knobs on the front at roughly counter height.  Very shortly after installing it, we noticed that it was very easy to accidentally turn the burners on.  The knobs do not have to be depressed to work, and have very little resistance to turning or tactile feedback when they are.  Until you feel the heat or see a burner turn red, the only indication that someone has accidentally turned a burner on, is that a light around the knob quietly illuminates.  Almost immediately after it was installed, everyone in my family, including the adults, began having incidents of accidentally turning burners on. We implemented rules about being careful around the oven, not reaching over it for things, and not setting anything on the cook-top.  However, it is all to easy to set things on a smooth cook top "temporarily" when counter space is full, and unfortunately, this past weekend, as my family was leaving for an all-day school-related trip, one of us (probably one my sons) accidentally brushed up against one of the knobs and turned a burner on as we were walking out the door.  Several things had been placed on the cook-top at the time.  A small fire smoldered in our house for 10-12 hours until a family member came over than evening to feed our dogs and found pervasive smoke and soot damage throughout the house.  Our dogs luckily were fine, but both the insurance adjuster and our fire restoration contractor said our house would have burned down had we not had tiles on the wall behind the oven.  We will be out of our house for 4-6 weeks, and the damage (not including hotel lodging and other incidentals) is estimated to be at $30k-$40k. Within a few short months, we--otherwise prudent people--had numerous close calls with this oven, ultimately resulting in a serious house fire.  I feel it is an unreasonably dangerous product. Thanks,  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage and potential risk to life, though no injuries or deaths were reported. The likelihood is high as multiple close calls were reported before the fire occurred.

incident_description:
There is a serious design/safety flaw in the burner knob assembly on the front of the LG Stainless Steel Freestanding Double Gas Range - LDG4315ST. With minimal pressure, the knob can be turned unintentionally. Sometimes the burner ignites, while other times gas flows without igniting.  During my first week of use, this happened numerous times, particularly when reaching over the  stove top to wipe down rear display.  This stove presents a major risk of burn injury or fire. LG must develop a fix and issue a recall to prevent injuries to consumers.

Apparently I am not the first consumer to experience this problem. I purchased the range from ABT in Glenview, Illinois. Several reviews on their web site also note this problem. A check of the LG and Consumer Reports web sites also contain several reports of this problem. I have included excerpts below of the reviews I found on these sites that reported this problem, not including any that were obvious duplicated. 

ABT Reviews

The dials for the stove have no safety lock and turn on ALL THE TIME when cleaning it.

My only real complaint is that the knobs do not lock. This makes it a little difficult to clean the stove without turning on a burner.

We are happy with the product, but it has one design problem: it is easy to turn on a burner accidentally by leaning on the front of the stove, something that's hard to avoid.

Front controls turn on too easily when just reaching over cook top . Gas was on , we didn't realize until fumes filled the room

 The gas knobs that control the stove top burners are very easy to turn on with just a bump or touch. Reaching up to cupboards above the stove can cause the knobs to turn on if they are touched, even slightly, by a hip or belly.

Cons: The burner control knobs are very easy to move; since they are on the front you can bump them and turn it enough for the gas to release. Our cat likes to get up on the counters at night and hit one of the knobs just enough to turn the gas on (but not ignite). We woke up to a kitchen full of gas, a little scary! We started taking the knobs off at night after that for a while, thankfully it hasn't happened again. But I do bump them and turn them on occasionally while working at stove. 

Only concern is that the burner knobs can be "bumped" into the on position. 

 Plus if you accidentally lean on the knobs they can be turned on.

Lastly, the burner knobs are right at hip level. We had a friend lean against it and turn on the burner by accident. 

The angled design of the control knobs are positioned so that reaching up into the microwave can turn on a burner flame and all. I did this the first day fortunately not burned. A cleaning person did the same thing while cleaning the microwave.

LG Reviews

The only downside (needs improvement): burner knobs are not locked so the kids can turn them on easily; LG should work on this for safety reasons.

 Consumer Reports Reviews

I have a concern in that the control knobs, even with the detents to hold them in the off position, are easily bumped to the on position when operating the oven controls. I have had 3 occasions where the burner lit as I was leaning over toward the oven controls and I had hardly touched them. And the other day, one had turned on just barely allowing a minute bit of gas to flow without lighting and without me noticing. I walked into the kitchen and smelled it, and noted the knob. 

With minimal pressure, the knob can turn and ignite, and sometimes not ignite. This happened numerous times passing by the range and brushing the knobs with my hip. My wife has turned on the front burners when leaning against the knob panel to reach a pan on one of the back burners. Our dog has jumped on the front of the range and turned on the knobs. One instance was when I went out shopping and returned home to a house full of gas! Most recently, we were in another part of the house when we smelled food cooking/burning. When I ran to the kitchen, I heard the igniter clicking and the burner had ignited under a frying pan on the back burner. The UltraHeat burner tends to go out when on the low setting. We must leave the knobs off when not in use.

The problem is that it is too easy to accidentally turn on top burners. We take the knobs off the range controls to avoid problems.
justification: The incident description reports multiple instances of gas leakage and unintentional burner ignition, posing a significant risk of burn injury or fire, though no injuries are explicitly mentioned.

incident_description:
The appliance in question is a Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp 1.7-Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle which we received as a gift in December, 2015. It has been used at least 4 times per day and almost every day since that time. The unit has an electronic temperature control module which operates a relay in the base of the unit ÃÂ when operating properly, you can hear the relay click each time the controller wants power to be applied to or removed from the heating element.

For the last couple of months and with increasing frequency, the relay in our unit will get stuck in the "on" position. Regardless of the selected temperature setpoint, the unit will then heat to a boil, and if left unattended would boil dry. The controller has electronic "boil-dry protection," but if the controller cannot power down the heating element to prevent exceeding the temperature setpoint, neither can the controller power down the heating element to prevent meltdown and potential ignition of the plastic base after boiling dry. IMHO, this "stuck" condition therefore presents a fire hazard.

Cuisinart warrants this product for three years, BUT discourages warranty claims by requiring the customer to pay not only actual shipping cost to return the defective product, but also a fixed (and probably excessive) charge for shipping the replacement to the customer.
justification: The kettle's relay getting stuck presents a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I have a Bosch SHX7ER55UC/44 dishwasher, S/N 9109, P/C 00581. The unit was subject to a recall for the power cord, and Bosch previously sent a technician (from Mr. Appliance, Epping NH, ÃÂ[REDACTED]ÃÂ) out to replace the cord set (on 8 December 2015). The technician applied a green "R" sticker on the top edge of the door and on the cover of the junction box. The (no cost) invoice stated ÃÂReplaced power cord kit per Bosch recall unit tested okÃÂ and under material listed the part ÃÂPower Cord - 12010137 ÃÂ BSHÃÂ. The unit had been working without issue since. This morning (5 May 2017) it was noticed that dishes were wet, and the unit had not fully drained from a cycle started last night. It was then noticed that the unit would not turn on. This evening, I pulled the unit out from under the counter, unplugged the power cord from the unit, and checked for voltage. There was 123V from the hot to ground, but only 3V from the hot to neutral. I turned off the circuit breaker, and opened the power cord junction box. The terminal in the power cord junction box (which the Bosch-authorized Mr Appliance technician had previously worked on) had clear evidence of overheating. The insulation was melted off the neutral on the line side, part of the plastic terminal was melted, there was char inside the box, and odor of electrical fire. While the hot and ground were firmly attached, the neutral on the line side had some play in what was left of the terminal. Had the wire not loosened enough to create the power loss to the unit, a catastrophic fire could have resulted.
justification: The incident involved significant electrical overheating and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On 6/24/17 my KitchenAid gas oven range model KSGB900ESS (purchased September 2015 and installed 12/29/2015 during a kitchen remodel) caught on fire while cooking in the oven at 500 degrees. The fire was electrical in nature (according to the fire department), and was caused by a malfunction in the wiring in the back of the unit (between the back interior oven wall and exterior wall -- there is a space there, and vents are on the top of this area). First smoke filled the upstairs, then started roiling up through the vents. Within a couple of minutes, flames shot out of the vents. I attempted to put baking soda on the flames to extinguish them but this did not work. The fire department was called and they determined it was electrical, within the unit itself. There is no apparent damage to the wall outlet into which the oven was plugged. Damage is minimal due to quick response on my part and the fire department. Insurance claim (Travelers Insurance) covers only the cleaning and repairs to kitchen itself (minimal), but does not cover the oven/range because it was a mechanical failure. An 18-month old oven should not be failing electrically, especially not at temperatures at which it is designed to operate.

Also, the knobs that turn on the burners are located vertically on the front face (i.e., they stick out from the oven). In the 18 months we have had this unit, they have accidentally been bumped and  TURNED ON -- with gas leaking into the kitchen -- as it only requires MAYBE 1-lb. of pressure to push in and turn the knob. This is clearly a safety hazard, as any small child or pet could turn this gas on and create a potential hazard.

I believe this model has serious design and safety flaws which should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an electrical malfunction, but there were no injuries or deaths reported. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible due to the described design flaws and the fact that the incident happened within 18 months of purchase.

I opened the door of my Miele single electric oven and suddenly, the glass exploded and flew all over the kitchen. I was left with the handle in my hand. One shard of glass hit my face about 1 inch from my eye. 
The only explanation for this is that possibly, I pulled the door down quickly and the handle broke away from the door. It is a bad design to have the handle set into the glass rather than the metal frame above the glass.
Miele said that glass is not under warranty. Yet they paid for the glass while they asked us to pay for the service call. They are lucky as am I, that glass did not get into my eye. Someone else may not be as lucky.
justification: The glass explosion caused an injury (shard hit the face near the eye), but no death occurred.

incident_description: dishwasher caught on fire. control board smoked   model mdb7100aw    it was on recall list in 2007. had no money to replace at time. failed in 2017.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and smoked, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
My husband and I special ordered a GE double wall oven from Home Depot less than a year ago. Yesterday, I tried to use the self-cleaning feature for the first time. I read the manual, then started the cleaning cycle. Ten minutes into cleaning, I heard a loud POW, almost like fireworks or a small caliber handgun. I walked back into the kitchen to discover the glass in my upper oven exploded inside the oven. 

Being "safety glass" it should have broken into pebbles. It didn't. It broke into sharp shards all over the inside of BOTH ovens (not sure how glass fell into the lower oven, but it surely did!) When I opened the door (after it cooled enough to unlock) to take pictures for warranty issues, shards immediately fell to the floor, imbedding in my linoleum floor like daggers.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction (glass shattering) but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This following incident occurred with a GE Profile dishwasher MN: PDW7700G00WW and SN: VA774228B.

The incident below is particularly concerning because it appears to be an identical fault described in a GE recall number 12-244 issued August 9, 2012 but my unit is not covered.  This recall pertains to the same model number as my unit but the serial number of my unit eliminates it from the existing recall. 

Approximately two hours after completing a dishwashing cycle I was alerted to the smell of burning plastic coming from the dishwasher. The dishwasher indicated that it was off but the front panel was extremely hot. After opening the door an I received burns on my arm from the extreme hot air that was escaping.  Nearly all plastic dishes had either completely melted and fell onto direct contact with the heating element or were severely deformed.  No front panel controls would result in the heating element from shutting off.  Only turning off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher allowed the heating element to shut off.  If nobody was present in the home when this fault occurred it would have undoubtedly resulted in a fire. 

With the dishwasher in service mode I was able to repeatedly initiate the fault by switching the heating element on.  It appears that once the heating element is switched on it will not turn off until power is removed via a circuit breaker.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the arm and potential for a fire, indicating an injury severity (level 3) and a likely recurrence (level 4) given the fault can be repeatedly initiated.

incident_description: My daughter was making dinner in the oven just bought it 2/27/2016 with a pyrex dish always use them when all of a sudden y granddughter ran up stairs to get e i came down and the pyrex blew up and broke the glass on the oven door dont understand what happened i now afraid to use my oven bought a replacement glass from GE Consumer Affairs dont know what to do.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded and broke the oven door glass, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:
At approximately 0530 today My family and I were  having dinner at the Cheesecake Factory and our tea glass exploded.  It was not a freshly poured glass. My little girl received a small superficial laceration.  An employee, or I assumed a manager, took a picture of the glass.  

9309 SWWashington square road
Tigard, Oregon 97223
justification: The incident resulted in a small superficial laceration to a child, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Glass explosions are uncommon but not unheard of in restaurants (likelihood 2).

incident_description: I had been using this Hamilton Beach Glass Kettle for approximately two years before it exploded into pieces on June 14, 2017. I was walking from the third floor of my apartment building to the six floor, and was transporting the kettle using a polyester basket. All of a sudden following a muffled thud, the kettle broke into pieces onto the hallway floor. The hallway had carpet floor so it is not possible for a glass to break by falling from 7 inches above the ground. My doorman had to come and clean it up in order to avoid any potential injuries.
justification: The kettle exploded but no injuries occurred, and such incidents are unlikely given the description of the event.

incident_description: I was using the Capresso brand electric kettle, model h20 plus. The glass pot of the kettle fell away from the handle as I was pouring boiling hot water. The pot shattered on the counter spilling boiling hot water all over my right leg. Because of this I now have a very big second-degree burn on my leg and got glass in my foot.  My sister in law who had the same kettle said that hers broke in the exact same way. I see that this product was recalled back in 2005 for this very defect but it seems the issue has not been fixed
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn and glass injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the same defect was reported by another user and the product was previously recalled for this issue.

incident_description:
Sharp Microwave oven model KB6524PS caused much smoke during normal use.  The unit is 3 years old and I had called Sharp within 4 months of purchasing to report loud humming that would happen randomly.  I was advised that this happens from time to time and that it was normal and not a warrantable condition.  

The noise has been becoming more frequent and recently the noise is present with smoke now that fills my kitchen.  I called the help line and they said that this happens from time to time and that it is not something to worry about.

I would like everyone to know that you should not do business with this company.  Any company that gives out advice or does not care that their product is probably going to either catch fire internally or cause excessive smoke is not good for consumers.  

There is another complaint on here that the company responded to and claimed that there was never a safety issue since the fire/short circuit was contained within the unit...That's the equivalent of saying, "Hey, our jet aircraft engines have a high degree of failure so when they do fail, the problem is contained within the unit so know one gets hurt".

Consumers can be the judge of this one...These are the facts and anyone who has one of these units knows exactly that what is described here is the truth.
justification: The incident involved excessive smoke during normal use, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer states that the cooling agent in the back of the unit is causing the unit to leak water underneath. She said she has fallen twice and her son has fell from the water on the floor that leaked from the unit.

(November 2016) She said the second time she fell she hit her head on the lower handle of the unit and caused her to get a large knot.

The consumer then contacted the firm to inform them of the incident and her safety concerns. They filed a claim (reference #[REDACTED]-[REDACTED]) and advised her that they would give her a replacement. The consumer received a letter from [REDACTED], a paralegal with the firm confirming a replacement unit and $250 compensation for damaged food in the fridge.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (falls and a head injury with a large knot), but no death was reported. The likelihood is possible given the description of repeated falls.

incident_description:
I was cooking in a pan with a lid, on the right burner of my Samsung oven range (model NE59J7630SS).  I took off the lid and set it down on the unused left burner, so I could mix the food..  A minute later I heard a loud pop,  and the glass, around where the lid was lying, exploded from my cook top.   There are tiny shattered pieces, as well as large sharp pieces, and several long cracks going across.  I was not hurt, but one of my daughters stepped on a tiny and very sharp piece of glass and pulled it out of her foot.  

When I contacted Samsung about the incident, nobody ever showed interest that this had happened nor did they want to know details of how it happened.  It was their job to basically say that it wouldn't be covered due to "physical damage."  It didn't matter to them that the reason there was physical damage was because it exploded!  I must have spoken to probably 5 different Samsung people and they all told me the same thing and would take no responsibility for the incident.  The oven was 1 year and 5 months old, so technically was out of the warranty period.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (a cut from glass) to a child, but no death or serious harm. The likelihood is unlikely as such explosions are not common.

incident_description:
The consumer's wife grabbed cereal from the cabinet above the range and sat down to eat. A few moments later the consumer's wife smelled a strong odor of gas. She noticed that the knob was slightly turned and the burner was emitting gas. 

The consumer said they have had 2 similar incidents and do not feel safe using this range. The consumer believes the igniter should come on first and not the gas. The consumer indicated that he contacted Lowes after each incident and they informed him that gas ranges are designed this way. The consumer was referred to the firm and they send out a technician to inspect the range. 

A safety inspector with the firm inspected the range and found that the range is operating normal (Report # [REDACTED]). The consumer then contacted the firm and they advised him that they couldn't assist further and informed him that the range should be attended at all times.

The consumer believes this design is dangerous and there should be a recall. 
He would like to request a replacement because he does not feel safe using this range.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak but no injury or death occurred, and the range was found to be operating normally by the inspector.

incident_description:
(05/11/2017)The consumer stated that that unit starts up by itself as soon as the door is opened. He has to unplug the unit. As soon as he plugs the unit back in, the door opens.

The consumer went to a Sears store and was referred to the CPSC Hotline
justification: The unit malfunctioning poses a potential hazard but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Kenmore electric range model 790 caught fire in the vicinity of the top control panel. No surface burners on, had been preheating oven to 325 degrees for approximately 20 minutes when top of panel began arcing and a fire started, coming from behind panel and scorching wall. Fire stopped when electric breaker was manually turned off. Stove was purchased new from Sears October 2011. No previous problems/indications of a fault with stove. Online search reveals that there have been numerous such fires related to panel controls--extremely hazardous! Sears has not responded to my email re the fire. These units definitely need to be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, but the potential for harm is high given the hazardous nature of the fault.

incident_description: I was toasting bread sticks in the toaster oven. They were on the toast setting for less than 3 minutes. I took them out of the oven, turned off teh oven and closed the door.  As I turned to put the pan on the island, the door of the microwave exploded in shattered glass and continued making popping sounds.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding microwave door) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
While coworker was making coffee noticed that the outside of the microwave was very hot.  as they sat down for a coffee break the microwave kicked on by itself, display started counting down from 8 -0 one number every 4-5 seconds and then continued to heat until it got to hot and stopped.  once it cooled down it restarted again and did the same thing 2 more times.  We unplugged it as the magnetron continued to heat, shut off and restart.  We asked our local appliance repair man to look at it and see if it would do the same thing for him and start by itself.  He closely monitored it and after an hour or so it started the heating, cooling off and restarting cycle.  After a few cycles the magnetron failed and he returned the microwave to us with his findings.  We are all still looking for a reason why this could start by itself.  Hopefully someone will be able to diagnose the reason for this happening.
Thanks!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave but no injuries occurred, and the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely as it was a specific equipment failure.

incident_description:
In December or 2016, I was using my Little Pro Plus Cuisinart Food processor.    The cutting blade broke into the food.   It broke at 2 of the 4 rivets.

I submitted this under the recall.  6 months later, I received a blade.   It is for a full sized unit. 
I called and they told me, that it was too bad because I had evidently given them incorrect information and my unit was NOT under RECALL - even though it had broken it the exact manner that the recalled items were flawed.   I was free to purchase a blade from them if I wished for $17.95.

NO THANK YOU
justification: The blade broke into the food, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This caller's mother purchased an apple corer approximately two months ago (November 2016), she will furnish a picture of this product with return of her report.

On Friday, January 6, 2017 her mother began to core and apple but when she pushed down on the handles to core the apple, however when she pushed down at the handles the blade remained at the top of the apple causing both of her hands to scrape on the blade.

The right hand at her thumb has a line cut on it but the left and by the thumb looks like someone cut it with a knife.

The caller's mother contacted her by phone to get her opinion of whether or not she should go to the emergency room because she had filled two towels with blood.  

The caller advised her mother to have her father drive her to an urgent care nearby.

The urgent care put six stitches in her hand and told her that she had cut vein.

The caller will enter the information regarding product model and name of the urgent care before returning the incident report.

The caller has contacted the manufacturer both by phone and email. She spoke with [REDACTED] then [REDACTED] but has had no reaction from the company.

Frontline Products 480-557-5892
1st call  ~ 1-11-17 told he would get a call back same day.  Nothing

He called again on 1-16-17 [REDACTED] asked caller to send an email which he did - no response

He called again 1-24-17 [REDACTED] told caller [REDACTED] should have called him back on 1-16-17 if not before.  Caller has an email trail that [REDACTED] was copied on by [REDACTED].

Caller was told that he was not the first person to call with this product problem.
[REDACTED]@flpaz.com
customerservice@flpaz.com
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring stitches and medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention that the caller was not the first to report this issue suggests the occurrence likelihood is higher.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore electric range,  made by Frigidaire, that came with my new construction home. The oven was registered in March of 2016. In November of 2016 the glass on the inside of my oven exploded. It was fixed at that time. Today April 27 2017 the same thing happened again. The glass inside my oven shattered everywhere.
justification: The oven glass shattered twice, indicating a recurring issue, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Slight bumping of stove knobs turns them on.  No less than 6 times this has happened placing groceries on the stove top, or placing fruit in a fruit bowl.  The knobs can bump onto high or low.  High is noticeable immediately via smoke and fire, low is more tricky.  I discovered fresh fruit burning 45 minutes later after it bumped onto low.
justification: The incident involves repeated occurrences of stove knobs being turned on accidentally, leading to potential fire hazards, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: This gas range has knobs that turn on if barely touched.  We have had several incidents.  Our painter covered the stove with a tarp and leaned over it to paint the wall; the tarp caught fire.  On several occasions we have walked by the stove, barely brushing against the knobs, and the gas turns on - sometimes with and sometimes without the flame.  Last week we opened the front door to a wave of gas odor; our dog managed to nudge one of the knobs and the gas leaked for over an hour.  I'm lucky because I do not have small children, however, I need to remove the knobs to be safe in my own home.  This product is a safety hazard. LG refuses to acknowledge that there is an issue.  I should not have to look at a beautiful $1500 range in my kitchen without knobs for fear of my home catching fire or blowing up.
justification: The incident involves multiple occurrences of gas leaks and a fire hazard due to easily activated knobs, posing a significant risk of property damage and potential injury.

incident_description: This is a kitchen tool used in the prep work work for cooking. It chops, blend, purees food products. The blade assemble u it is degrading and falling apart and away from the metal blade. Soon the blade will fly completely off and probably through the plastic wall of the prep bowl
justification: The blade assembly is degrading and likely to fly off, posing a risk of damage or minor injury but not severe harm.

incident_description: The coffee maker had just brewed coffee when my mother went to shut it off. Upon pressing the power switch, an audible pop was heard, and my mother had been shocked by the appliance. Inspection of the switch revealed melted, black edges of the translucent red switch. There was no contact with water visible on the switch.
justification: The incident resulted in an electric shock, which qualifies as an injury, and the melted switch indicates a serious electrical fault.

incident_description:
Came home to find the front door of my range shattered and sitting on the floor next to the range.
Oven had not been used for 2 days.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered door) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My microwave kitchenaide khms155lss - 4 started turning itself on on its own and posed a serious risk to my home.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a risk but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Item # 920125L5, Anchor glass container

This item was in my refrigerator for one day with spaghetti noodles and sauce.  The day after making it, I put it in microwave to warm up.

While eating the spaghetti, i crunched on something hard.  It was a long shard of glass that was obviously chipped from the lip of the container!
justification: The incident involved a glass shard in food, which could cause injury but did not in this case.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the compressor was replaced on November 30, 2016 because the unit was not cooling.

The consumer stated that she noticed in February that the unit stopped making ice. The consumer called for repair again. An appointment was scheduled for dispatch but the unit started working again. The appointment was canceled. 

Around February 28th, the unit stopped making ice nor was it cooling. Another dispatch was scheduled. A repairperson came out on 3/9. The consumer stated that the technician added Freon.

(03/10/2017)  The consumer stated that around 12 noon,3:30pm and around 5pm, she ate some food from the refrigerator. The consumer noticed later that the unit was not cooling at all.
 
The consumer stated that later on 3/10, everything in the refrigerator was thrown out.

(03/11/2017) The consumer stated that on Saturday she woke up about 7am. She was throwing up and had diarrhea.

No medical attention was required.
justification: The consumer experienced vomiting and diarrhea, indicating injury, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description: My Hamilton Beach K39 electric teakettle has an automatic cutoff switch that turns off heat when water in the kettle comes to a boil.  Intermittently, the automatic cutoff switch does not work and the kettle threatens to boil dry.
justification: The kettle's failure to cut off heat could lead to overheating or damage, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
Using the independent timer function on Sears microwave oven to control simmering time for a chili-pot cooking on the kitchen stove. While folding clothes in the family room, adjacent to the kitchen  I smelled an unusual odor.  The odor grew more awful so I got up to investigate.  Looking around the kitchen I saw flames flickering through the microwave oven door.
I immediately pressed the microwave STOP button, grabbed the lid off the simmering chili-pot and opening the microwave door, placed the stainless steel, chili-pot lid over the glass turntable snuffing out the flames.  The microwave fan was running full speed but not responding to the control button.
The house was filled with smoke and awful noxious odors.  
I opened the large patio sliding glass door to start ventilation, turned on all of the ceiling fans in adjacent rooms, opened the windows in the master bath and my office.  Outside was very windy with wind watches and warnings all across the High Desert.  I added a portable tornado fan from the garage in the main hallway, raised the garage door one foot then leaving the door from the garage to my office open, creating a clear unobstructed ventilation path from the front of the house through the kitchen and family rooms out the back patio door.  When cooled the plastic three wheel turntable was melted beyond repair.  As a result we are afraid to use the microwave again and the turntable is beyond repair.  The odor is beginning to fade.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Turn Broiler on and the heat escapes the oven and burns you if you touch the handle and melted my display screen and if you have pots on the stove it heats the pots up to a burning touch without burners on. Cannot turn the broiler off fast enough due to the fact it is melting the display screen.
justification: The description indicates burns from touching the handle and pots, which qualifies as injury. The issue occurs when the broiler is on, making it likely.

incident_description: The refrigerator light burned out and as I replaced it, I discovered that the plastic had been burnt and melted about the bulb.  The bulb used was a 40 watt appliance bulb and the max rating is 40W.  I could not believe it.  I went online with Frigidaire and got no satisfaction,  They told me I could install a shield but the refrigerator is too old for them to do anything.  A shield is one thing, but I can't understand how this issue could be overlooked! An issue like this should not happen.  How does a small wattage bulb get so hot  that it melts the plastic?   However, I tried explaining THIS IS A SAFETY ISSUE and it's obviously a design flaw but it fell on deaf ears.   After doing some research, I have found others with the same issue. I would attach pictures if I could.
justification: The incident involves a safety issue with a design flaw causing plastic to melt, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Oven box on Frigidaire Professional slide in range has expanded.  Oven racks do not sit securely in slots and collapse. Oven door became wedged by collapsed racks and unable to be opened. Safety concerns are fire with food spilled on bottom of oven, and burns while trying to remove wedged racks and get door open.
justification: The incident describes safety concerns like fire and burns, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased  through a fund raiser at my grandson's elementary school a salad dressing maker.  It is called Salad Emulsifier Dressing Maker, distributed by Cobble Creek, Landsdale, Pa. (That is the only address information on product container).  It is made in China.
It is for making your own salad dressing.  You add the contents to the clear plastic container, and attach the top, which twists on about half a turn.  It has a stirring blade that is attached to the lid, which has a mechanism that you pull like a spray bottle, which in turn causes the internal blade to spin, thus stirring the contents of your salad dressing.  
     During the very first use, I noticed a "click" and discovered that a sliver of plastic from the top of the container that holds the lid on broke off and fell into the dressing mixture.  I cleaned everything off and tried to use it a second time, without any contents.  This time addition small slivers of plastic broke off again.  I can only imagine if ingested, that these slivers could cause serious internal damage to someone.
     I still have the product.  I had found the distributor on-line a wrote a very negative review of this product.  I have not heard from them.  It seems this item is defective.  I surely can not be the only person who has experienced this.  I've had the item for several months and was going to trash it but thought this product needs to be reviewed and the public, in the interest of their safety, alerted of the defect.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a defective product with potential for harm, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I returned home yesterday evening to the smell of burnt plastic and metal in my kitchen. I was able to localize the smell to the location of my Kenmore Elite Electric Double Oven. When I opened the door to the top unit, I immediately was hit with the same smell of burnt plastic and metal and could see that there had been a small fire in oven. There were obvious burn marks on the perimeter of the door and the top of the oven and smokiness inside of the oven. The oven had not been on that day or for two days prior to that. I do not know what prompted the unit to catch on fire, but am obviously concerned that it may happen again, especially because there are small children in the home. I contacted Sears for help, but they were not at all helpful.
justification: There was a small fire in the oven with visible burn marks, indicating a significant incident but no reported injury.

incident_description:
turned self cleaning oven to clean per manual instuctions and latched door and light came on indicate cleaning (end of 2015)
When cleaning was complete door unlatched and light went off automaticaly
Upon opening the door the exterior side of the door (Room side) glass exploded and shards of glass blew across room cutting me.
Called GE but they said not their problem and call a repair company   we did  
Repair people intalled new glass on exterior side of door and noted to me that it  appeared that the face plate holding the two glass windows was torqued to tight by manufacture therefor extreme heat possibly warped the plate causing glass to shatter.  Cost was approx 150.00 and we presented this to GE for reimbursment but they said not their problem

Nov 2016 we attempted again to clean the oven and again followed the maint manual directions
Cleaning lite came on and latch on door locked door 
After lite went out and latch released itself I opened door and found that the inside glass was shattered
Again we went to GE and they again said not their problem   We calledseveralprofessional appliance repair co for estimate.  estimate range for glass, installation and service call was over 300.00
the repair man suggested we call GE and tell them that it was his opinion that the metal plate holding the glass in was installed incorectly and the heat caused the glass to crack.  We found it more prudent to purchase a new range oven that cost 400.00 rather than spend over 300.00 for a fix

Again GE replied that it was not their problem
justification: The incident resulted in injury from glass shards and occurred twice under similar conditions, indicating a possible design or manufacturing flaw.

incident_description: I had removed the chicken and came back to close the lid when I got a terrible shock. I got a voltmeter and discovered the cookers frame was 124VAC tried to contact Ronco customer support for three days, finally on day four I contacted them and they said return it to to Amazon, After I told him what happened, he informed me just to return it.
justification: The incident involved a severe electric shock from a cooker, indicating a significant safety hazard that could cause injury.

incident_description:
I smelled gas in kitchen and called power company. Power company identified gas coming from gas range and shut off supply and advised an appliance service check appliance. Appliance repair
 identified all 4 gas burners were leaking gas. $388 for repair. My concern is other consumers may not detect problem before it is too late.
justification: Gas leak was detected and addressed without injury, but the potential for harm to others is likely if undetected.

incident_description: Using a handheld cutter called the clever cutter to cut vegetables while making soup. While eating the soup a small plastic piece was found in the soup. The piece had fallen from the side of the cutter. This piece was a choking hazard as well as possibly causing a cut mouth or broken tooth.
justification: A small plastic piece was found in the soup, posing a choking hazard and potential for minor injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: My son grabbed the side of my oven and sliced 2 fingers open. After looking at it there is unfinished metal on the of the oven door
justification: The description states that the child sliced 2 fingers open, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: LRE30453ST largest burner stays on after turning off the switch.
justification: The burner staying on after turning off the switch is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential hazard.

incident_description: Breville small appliance oven. Caused my 20-amp outlet to catch fire. The electrical cord to this appliance gets super hot. I am not using it any more. i did contact the manufacturer, and posted my review/issue on Amazon, where I bought it roughly 3 years ago.
justification: The incident caused an outlet to catch fire, indicating a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I stored mashed sweet potatoes in the cup-size Pyrex bowl and placed it in the office fridge.  At lunchtime I took out the bowl from the fridge about 30-40 minutes before my lunchtime and set it on the table where my assistant and I eat lunch.

Thirty-forty minutes later I removed the potatoes from the Pyrex container and placed the potatoes in another (non-Pyrex) microwavable dish which contained the rest of my lunch. I heated my lunch.  The Pyrex dish remained on the table and away from  the microwave oven.  At no time did I put the Pyrex inside the oven.

My assistant then heated her lunch, and we sat down to eat.  About five minutes after we began eating we heard an explosion. The Pyrex dish had "exploded" and shards were all over the table.  We  were not injured, but shaken because of the possibility that one of the shards could've flown into our eyes. 
I will no longer buy Pyrex glassware.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish causing no injuries, but potential for harm was present.

incident_description: I was sitting across the room at my kitchen table eating lunch when there was a loud sound and something flew across the room. My microwave door had shattered. Thankfully I was across the room and nobody else was around. The projectile landed on the floor by me, but if I had been standing in the kitchen I could have been seriously injured by any of the glass that flew out or fell.
justification: The microwave door shattered, creating a hazard, but no one was injured as the person was across the room.

incident_description:
Please refer to Samsung refrigerator complaints that you already have, and ours is the same.  We have the problem of the back panel fan not working, ice buildup on the panel, moisture and wetness in both meat and vege drawers.   Mold growing behind drawers.  Temperature fluctuates because it is not defrosting.
We purchased it in 2013 from Howard's Appliance in Alhambra, Ca., and they are not helpful at all, and claim they had no knowledge of any such problem.  The model RF24FSEDBSR was manufactured 4/2013.  We
Just had it repaired, $390, and the repairman told us that it probably happen again.  HE was familiar with the issue on these sAmsung refrigerators.   There was lots of mold growing behind the drawers, so we do not feel very safe now with this appliance.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator leading to mold growth and temperature fluctuations, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
My Maytag dishwasher caught on fire, I was told by my repairman that the motor inside the dishwasher was the cause of the fire.

Made by Maytag
Model # mdbh969aww3
Serial # f12405009
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but there was no mention of injury or death, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I prurchased an LG French Door refrigerator in September 2015.  Model # LMXS276265.  This afternoon , March 17,  2017, I got some ice from the icemaker.  When I drank from the glass, I almost bit down and swallowed a screw.  As you can imagine ,  I was startled.  Afted some deliberation, I checked the ice maker and found a missing screw from the bin.  I checked the screw that was in my glass and verified it was the missing screw. I called LG customer service and told them what happened.  After a couple of transfers, the representative said the refrigerator was out of warranty; however, they would send me a replacement bin at no charge.  I had to electronically send a copy of my receipt.  I am filing this issue to see if other consumers have experienced similar problems.
justification: The incident involved a screw in the ice, but no injury occurred, only a startle. The likelihood is unlikely as it's a specific manufacturing defect.

incident_description: My wife was cooking dinner using Tristar power pressure cooker xl. The product indicated it was done and all directions were followed to release pressure. While releasing cover the contents exploded all over leaving my wife with second and third degree burns on her hands, arms, chest and stomach
justification: The incident resulted in second and third degree burns, indicating an injury severity level. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely as the product was used correctly but malfunctioned.

incident_description:
I became aware of the recall about Kitchen Garbage Disposals yesterday and want to add the Model and Serial Number, I checked the list provided and it is not listed; it is a Kenmore Model Number 58770351410 Serial #2F401842S-59
On February 21, 2017 I was using the above appliance and heard a metal clanking sound, I turned it off, explored the unit and found a portion of a blade inside.
A Sears technician came to my home the next day and discoverd two blades had broken off and could not be repaired. He placed an order for a replacament and per his information it was still under Warranty since it had been in use only 15 months.
Since February when the incident occured I have made 6 telephone calls to Sears regarding the replacement, and as of yesterday was informed it had only a 12 month Warrenty. My patience resulted in no use of a disposal  for nearly 8 weeks.
I still have the metal portions of the blades from the appliance and the unit is still in the sink. I was not injured.
Since this particular unit was not on your list I wanted to report it so it could be added.
Hopefully I might receive a replacement.

incident_description: Burn hazard: Coffee maker maze buzzing sound and then smoked, smelled like burning plastic, and caught fire internally.  Is seems the hot plate assembly shorted or there was an arc in the electronics.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire internally but there was no mention of injury or death, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Front right burner stays on and can only be shut off by turning the breaker off.  Huge safety issue
justification: The burner staying on poses a significant safety risk, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The circuit board on our Kenmore Elite dishwasher, purchased at a local Sears, caught fire last night.  My wife, who was in another room of the house, said she heard some popping noises and when she got to the kitchen she saw flames coming out of the top of the dishwasher. She immediately unplugged it and that stopped the fire/issue.  The dishwasher was running, my wife was doing a load of dishes, at the time of the incident.  The house still smells like burnt plastic. 

I just had the circuit board replaced by Sears Home Services in December 2016. The previous one was also acting up i.e. turning on by itself, not turning on at all. 

I hate to think what could have happened if my wife had not been home.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was quickly unplugged, resulting in no injury or death. The issue appears to be related to a faulty circuit board, which is unlikely to recur frequently.

incident_description:
The product is the Evaco Whistling Kettle No. 20020-B.
Company address: Evaco, 285 Bel Marin Keys Blvd, Unite C, Novato, CA 94949-5763
800-7822738. Email: evacoimp@aol.com
The warranty for this tea kettle does not cover kettles boiled dry or subjected to excessive heat.

On Sunday, May 21, 2017 I boiled dry our tea kettle dry over excessive heat, both things that should not have happened. 
1) I had the heat too high
2) the whistle did not go off alerting me that the water was boiling.

Unfortunately, a flaw to these tea kettles (this is the second one I have owned) is that the whistle will not work unless the lid to the teapot is fitted snugly down on top of the kettle.

Because a recent guest had most likely taken the lid of the teapot off, there was not an adequate seal to have the whistle go off.

I picked up the tea kettle from the electric burner, noted that there was no water in it, and turned toward the middle of the kitchen. The bottom fell off the tea kettle, and layers of molten metal (tin?) hit the floor and splashed in small to 2" globs all about the floor of the kitchen, an approximate 6' radius. The hardwood floor in the kitchen burned underneath the molten metal.

Luckily one one splash landed on me which gave me a severe burn.

Even though I used the tea kettle as directions said not to by using excessive heat, it's a tea kettle and situations like mine are bound to happen because the whole point of a tea kettle is to put it on heat and boil water.

A better warning should be made to consumers, such as: Excessive heat will cause the bottom to fall off and molten metal will splash down causing possible physical burns and fires as a result.

Please have this company produce a safer Whistling Kettle, fix the flawed lid which stops the tea kettle from whistling, and issue warnings to what will happen is the tea kettle is overheated.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe burn to the user, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the conditions leading to the incident (excessive heat and faulty whistle) are not uncommon in typical use.

incident_description: My Kenmore dishwasher was running when I smelled something electrical burning.  I heard sizzling and snapping and when I went to investigate, flames were shooting out from the front right of the control panel.  I tried to cancel, but nothing happened so I ran and turned off circuit breaker and grabbed fire extinguisher....Kenmore model 665.17389300, ser. FR3106279.
justification: Flames and electrical burning indicate a serious incident, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The glass door of my Whirlpool electric range exploded and threw shattered glass all over the kitchen floor.  The range had not been used for 4 days nor the oven.  Having talked with the Safety team at Headquarters in Benton Harbor, MI, I was told they could not do anything about it.  It is at my expense to have it repaired.  The range is 23 years old and NEVER have had anything go wrong with it until now.
I am concerned as to the safety of the tempered glass oven doors because I was told this can happen at any time without any reason.  I have small great-grandchildren frequently and what if this would have happened when they were here?   Consumers need to know about this.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded glass door) but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely given the age of the appliance and lack of prior issues.

incident_description: Our Samsung electric range, model FER300SX, three years old, was in use in our kitchen when we heard a loud popping noise, and the electrical circuitry in the back of the top part of the stove caught fire. There was a brief flame, and then we turned off the oven, allowed it to cool, and pulled it out to unplug it. When my husband took off the back panel, there were blackened wires in the cavity near the circuit board in the back. I have been trying to get Samsung to respond to this (rather dangerous) problem for four days now, but I cannot get a response.
justification: The incident involved a fire and damaged wiring but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I have owned my Kenmore stove/oven for about 8 years. I used the oven in the morning with no problem. About 3 hours later, after it had completely cooled down I heard a loud crash from the kitchen. The front glass of the oven door had exploded all over the kitchen. It reached as far as the hallway and the living room. Good thing I was not in the kitchen when it happened. I saw online that Kenmore refuses to initiate a recall and they say that damage to the oven door by the consumer is the cause. Well, I want to inform your organization that is NOT the truth. This oven has been well cared for and has never been, slammed, bumped, scratched or forced closed. In order to have Sears replace the glass to the door they want $300-$350 dollars for the part and installation. The glass door panel costs $75.00 when purchasing directly from Sears online. There is no reason for Sears/Kenmore to initiate a recall when they are able to recoup half the cost of the range by just replacing the glass door panel. 

Model No: 790.92903010
Serial No.: VF02555407
justification: The oven glass exploded but no one was injured, and such incidents are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung 4 door French Door refrigerator. The door bins (2 of them) on the right upper door (facing the refrigerator) broke within a few days of each other. The bins fell on my feet, which was not pleasant. I'm concerned about these bins breaking and falling on children or pets. I have two small children and two small dogs. If they had been under me when I opened the doors they would have been seriously injured.

The disturbing part is that the bins were not overloaded in any way. There were not gallons of milk on them, rather they were primarily loaded with half full bottles of salad dressing. I estimate a total of about 5lbs was on each bin when they broke. It looks to me like the material used becomes brittle over time, then cracks and causes the failure. 

My refrigerator model and SN are:
RF32FMQDBSR/AA
W76643BFB02225A
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bins fell on feet), and the likelihood is high (4) given the concern for children and pets under similar conditions.

incident_description: On Monday, 5-29-17 I was preheating my Kenmore Range, Model 79092903010.  When it reached approximately 250 degrees, the outside glass of the oven door exploded and shattered all over the kitchen.  I immediately shut off the oven.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Oven, Model # 790.94173310 that came with a vacation house that we built in Nov 2014.  

The oven is rarely used as this is a vacation home for my family.  While baking cookies on May 29, 2017 at 350 degrees, the inside oven door glass shattered. Thankfully, no children were in the kitchen to open the door when this occurred.

A RECALL NEEDS TO BE ISSUED ON THIS PRODUCT !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

incident_description:

justification: The incident involved the oven glass exploding, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Dishwasher was started as normal.  As the cycle continued, a strong smell of burning plastic and smoke was noticed.  The dishwasher was stopped.  The fire department was called because of the smoke and strong odor that was present.  
The house was filled with the odor which made two adults and two children nauseous and light headed.

justification: The incident caused nausea and lightheadedness in four people, indicating injury (severity 3). Electrical fires in dishwashers are uncommon but not unheard of (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
Frigidaire gas range has very weak gas valve detents and gas valve is easily turned without pushing in.

Recently when leaning forward to open a nearby cabinet the left most gas valve ignited and almost lit off my shirt.  We have on occasion smelled gas and found valves partially opened, this can happen by just brushing into them unknowingly.

We have owned other gas ranges and did not have any similiar experiences owning them.   The burner valves used in this model stove are too easily overcome.
justification: The incident describes a near-miss with potential for injury due to easily turned gas valves, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: While baking fish in my over for approximately 45 minutes, the outer oven door cracked and spread small pieces of glass on the kitchen floor.  I was standing two feet away from the stove.  I was not cut by the glass.  Thank goodness my cat was not nearby.
justification: The oven door cracked and spread glass, but no one was injured.

incident_description: Went to preheat oven and the moment we hit preheat sparks started flying out the back and flames ignited.  Upon further inspection it was the circuit board in the back was on fire.
justification: The incident involved sparks and flames from the oven's circuit board, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On Saturday, May 20, 2017, I was using my Samsung Electric Range Model # FE-R300SB. I was only using the two front burners for about 10 minutes when I hear a loud pop. I look down and I see that the glass on the oven door is completely cracked into tiny pieces and parts of it is shattering onto my kitchen floor at my feet.
