I have never had an issue with this range before until that day.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, but no injuries were sustained. The likelihood is unlikely as the user had never experienced this issue before.

incident_description: In November of 2016 I bought a Kenmore Gas Stove Model 790-74323313.  This stove has burners that turn on when anyone is near the stove.  I was making toast next to it and apparently leaned on it.  I did not know it was on until a family member smelled gas.  I have put a carbon monoxide monitor next to it.  It has gone off once.  Usually we catch it before the monitor sounds.  The burners are very very easy to turn on and this can be dangerous.  The burner on the right front is very big and flames come out over the edge of the stove -not good with small children - so we don't use it.
justification: The incident involves a gas stove turning on unintentionally, posing a risk of gas leakage and potential carbon monoxide exposure, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Cooking a pizza with oven set to 425 degrees. Pizza was done in less time than expected. When turned the oven off, the oven element didn't go off. Unplugged the stove.

When re-plugged the stove back in (hoping the computer would reset) the lower oven element (bake) came back on even though I didn't press the button to turn the oven on.

incident_description:
Preheated wall oven to 350 degrees. When ready. opened door and put food in. Carefully closed door - did not slam it or otherwise. Started to walk away. About 15 seconds later, glass oven door exploded scattering small sharp pieces of glass over kitchen and 2 other nearby rooms. Luckily my back was towards the oven. Probably would haven gotten these in my eyes. Also, My 2 grandchildren had just left the kitchen.

Oven is a Kenmore 790.47789406, purchased from Sears about 6 years ago.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding oven door) but no injuries occurred, as the person's back was turned and grandchildren had left the kitchen.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung slide in range last November. Because I want to keep the glass top nice by setting casseroles atop, I kept a kitchen pad on it when not in use. 
Right after Christmas, while teen granddaughters were here, one of them yelled, "[REDACTED], something is on fire." I rushed to the stove and picked up the pad atop the burner area. It burst into flames. Granddaughter said she wasn't cooking anything nor had she turned a knob. It was long after our meal. We had gone to other parts of the house.
All this was a puzzle. So, I asked if she was near the stove, "Yes" she was. 
I recreated what had happened by doing the following. I let my mid section touch the control knobs and moved slightly to the right. Immediately the same burner came on. It and the 'bridge' that connects one burner to another so a large area can be used to cook at once. 
I went on line and realized this is the complaint I had read about before I made the purchase. Prior, I couldn't imagine such a thing. 
I called HHGregg who sent a tech to the house. I showed him what had happened and how. His only remedy was for me to remove the knobs and attach them only when I needed to cook. 
Since then, this has happened several times. Always the same left burner perhaps because I am so 'right handed' and tend to stand slightly to the left. I have a picture of the last time it occurred. 
So, I can no longer keep the knobs on the stove. I'm 73,  live alone and because of this, I live in fear if the house goes 'pop' in the night. I second guess myself wondering if I remembered to take the knobs off. Is the house on fire? Do I smell smoke? 
This is a terrible design flaw. I wish I could get my purchase price back. I have thought of trying to take a loss and sell it to someone else but would never do it without a warning of a potential fire hazzard. So, I do the best I can and live with it.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a design flaw, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high as it has happened several times and poses a recurring risk.

incident_description:

02/03/2017

incident_description:

incident_description: Burner control knobs on gas range require very little pressure or resistance.  Just brushing up against them turns them on.  Two occasions this past week (3/2-7-17) while cleaning the stove top and having my hand over the burners I accidentaly brushed against the knob and the burner ignited and singed the hair on my wrist.  On several times past two weeks I didn't notice I had accidentally turned the knobs on until I smelled gas in the room.  Since nothing can be done to fix this sensitivity problem I can only conclude this is a manufacturing defect.  This problem grows more dangerous for the elderly who may become less cognizant of surroundings.

incident_description: My GE dishwasher smells of fire when running the heat cycle. The heat cycle will not shut off, causing any plastic to melt. I'm sure if I did not catch this, a fire would have started.

incident_description: I was washing a load of dishes in my dishwasher, as usual.  While it was running, I heard a pop and smoke started coming out of the control panel.  When I pressed cancel, the button sparked.  I opened the door, and thankfully that stopped everything.  There was absolutely nothing on the bottom, nothing on the heating element.  The problem was the control panel.  I am writing this complaint to you, because I am concerned about what the outcome could have been if I was not standing right there to stop it.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks but no injury or death, and the situation was controlled without further escalation.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung refrigerator freezer model RF26HFENDSR BUIL IN OCT 2014.

The defrost of the fridge is defective in design. It freezes the drain tray and drain. The result is pooling water around the fridge. This pooling water creates a shock hazard as well as a potential slip and fall.

The internet is full of people who have shared the same story. I against my better judgment added wire to conduct heat from the heater on the fridge to the tray in an attempt to fix the problem. It did work for some time but it has failed to be the remedy.

The design is faulty and a clear safety issue.
justification: The pooling water creates a shock hazard and slip-and-fall risk, which could lead to injury. The issue is ongoing and widespread, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: On Sunday 4/16/17 I was cooking Easter dinner and my Carbon Monoxide detector went off, my alarm company called me and said they were dispatching the Fire Dept to my house.  I have a Kenmore gas range and it released Carbon Monoxide Poisoning, the levels were so high it took the Fire Dept over an hour to get the levels back down, if I didn't have a CM Detector it would have been deadly.  I saw on the internet about the recall on past Kenmore gas ranges however my stove is not one of the models on this recall.  I called Kenmore and they said sorry your stove is out of warranty. you will have to repair it at your own expense.  I feel this is a defect in their product and they should stand behind their product.
justification: The incident involved potentially deadly carbon monoxide poisoning, but the presence of a detector and quick response prevented injury or death, making the actual severity level 4. The likelihood is rated 2 as such incidents are uncommon but possible with gas appliances.

incident_description: Sauce pan has a silicon sleeve grip over the stainless steel handle. Over time the sleeve grip on the handle becomes loose and rotates freely regardless of pressure that is applies on the handle. The pan size is 2 quarts, I was boiling potatoes on a gas stove top and when it came time to drain the boiling water I was carrying the pan to the sink with my hand on the silicon grip on the handle when the handle and pan rotated in the pan grip, turning the pan upside-down and dumped boiling water. The boiling water just missed my leg and my grandson that was standing next to me.
justification: The boiling water was spilled but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: Whirlpool refrigerator model gd5thgxk501 serial #sm2925581 built 07/02. Unit started smoking and caught fire on 5/21/17. Unit had no problems or repairs done prior to that. The relay box connected to the compressor was burning. Luckily we were at home when it happened. Opened the unit to turn it off. Lights are circulation fan were still running. It did not trip the circuit breaker. Unplugged the unit to stop the fire. Initial contact at whirlpool said there was no recall for this unit and it should be ok to use. I told her no it can't be used and she transferred me to their safety department who dispatched a local repair company to inspect it. Unit needed a new relay, compressor and wiring harness. Whirlpool said they wouldn't pay to fix it due to it's age and offered to but it from me for $175.00
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was contained without significant damage.

incident_description:
LG Glass top Oven

Model # LRE3083ST/00

Serial # 308MMES01196

Burners heat up even when not turned on from the on/off knob

Burners do not regulate temperature correctly and heat up even on lowest settings
justification: Burners heating up uncontrollably can cause burns or fires, posing a significant injury risk.

incident_description:
Purchased Sears Kenmore dual electric convection oven 11/15: Model # 790.48443410
Serial# AF54001251 and used both upper and lower ovens (though rarely because also resided in another location half time) without issue. On 3/26/17 I used the lower oven to cook a casserole. I removed the dish and closed the oven door. About 30 minutes later I heard a sound and turned to see the left side of oven door handle was dislodged and hanging down. There had not been any door handle loosening issues noted previously. As I was walking towards oven to investigate there was a LOUD "pop" and the entire outer glass panel exploded into fragments that shot out all over the kitchen (including into my prepared food) and husband cut his foot on one of the fragments! I am always very careful and gentle with my electronics, appliances and equipment so was VERY disappointed that Sears blames the consumer instead of replacing the glass panel at their expense. The screw that hols the handle in is quite short and only 3 threads actually hold into the handle. The glass part shouldn't even be included in the far upper and lower parts of the exterior door because this design flaw makes the glass too vulnerable to stress fracture. As soon as the handle dislodges the glass panel must flex with the lack of total support and it fractures. Really unacceptable and unsafe to have glass explosion in your kitchen with kids, pets and all others in the area. I would like to see this item recalled because of this unsafe the design flaw. Sears sold me 4 new bolts for over $25 "that have been changed" and they don't even work for the left side of the handle because the washer is too wide and the interior of oven has a raised area that disallows washer from sitting flush.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut foot (injury) due to glass explosion, but the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely given the specific design flaw described.

incident_description:

incident_description: We purchased a new Kenmore drop-in range back on October 6, 2016 (Model # 790. 42509312 - Serial # AF 63301230). Yesterday my wife turned on the front right burner and instantly heard a loud pop and saw a flash at the same time coming from under the top burners. incident_description: Our Kenmore Stove oven door exploded and glass went all over our kitchen. Both the stove top and oven were not in use at the time.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
On 3/7/2017 I attempted to warm a "hot cross bun" muffin in my GE microwave oven. I set the timer for 15 seconds; after 10 seconds the muffin ignited into a fire and the microwave plate it was setting on exploded into pieces. Luckily I was nearby and immediately opened the oven, smothered the flames with a pot lid, closed the oven and pulled the plug from the electrical outlet. The fire created a foul odor and heavy smoke that penetrated the air of my home.  The muffin became a 2 x 2 inch sized cinder; the smoke discolored the plastic interior of the oven and the ceiling blade cover melted. 
This microwave (GE Model JVM6175RF1SS - Serial # MD221537B) is only 2 years old and was purchased January 30, 2015 as part of the appliance package provided in a new home by the home builder .  Since the appliance came with only a 1 year warranty, I purchased an extended warranty through GE's Warranty Service Corporation Assurant. The warranty/extended warranty has been continuously maintained since 01/20/2015. 
On 3/8/2017 I notified Assurant of the fire/damage and they arranged for a GE service tech to service/examine the microwave on 3/9.  In his examination he determined that the oven was not repairable and told me to keep the oven unplugged until replaced by GE/Assurant.  I have received an email message from GE Claims stating that they have no culpability or responsibility to repair/replace the appliance since the fire was due to "negligence" on my behalf.  I have sent a letter of protest to the warranty department but have not received a response.   
On examination, the service tech reported that he believed sparking occurred around shelf clips in the oven that in turn caused the fire.  This is not due to my negligence and I believe the oven malfunctioned yet GE denies responsibility; I now have to spend money I do not have to purchase a new oven.
justification: The incident involved a fire and property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the described malfunction and similar incidents reported.

Please advise if CPSC can assist me in getting Frigidaire to repair the hazardous condition.
Thanks, 
[REDACTED]

incident_description: Refrigerator lightbulb has overheated, scorched, and burned a hole in the top of the refrigerator. Model #FRS26H5DSB2 FRIGIDAIRE Side-by-Side Refrigerator.  I feel very apprehensive about putting another lightbulb in, have verified that the wattage was correct, and now have no light to use in my refrigerator, and am very concerned about the ability to properly function, insulate, or avoid a faulty electrical system fire from my refrigerator.

incident_description: I was using a Pyrex brand 9 by 13 baking pan in my oven at 400 degrees. I started to open the oven door to look in and check on the food and there was a very loud exploding noise. The baking pan exploded and a large piece of it hit the inside of my oven door shattering the glass on the inside of the oven door. incident_description: We purchased from Sears a new Kenmore Elite electric double-wall oven Model # 790.48459411 in December, 2016 for our remodeled kitchen. In all instances, when trying to broil chicken, beef, or fish in our top oven, the oven generated so much smoke and grease that our fire alarms (located about 20 feet away between two rooms) would go off. We contacted Sears, and their experienced technicians came to our home and essentially replaced all of the electrical components in our oven and the heating coil. After this was completed, we placed a 1 inch steak on a professional broiling pan in the top oven at 550 degrees, and lowered the rack position to 4 according to the Sears manual for this oven and in less than  4 minutes in the oven (without even opening the door of the oven) the smoke being blown out of the top of the oven was so dense that our fire alarms went off once again. The Sear's technicians noted this on their report. The steak in less than 4 minutes had thrown grease all over the oven walls, had an excessive amount of smoke in the oven when we opened it, and was cooked well-done in less than 6 minutes without even turning the steak over. We asked Sears to replace the oven, telling them that the oven runs too hot for us to control it. They declined to do so, and told us we needed to reschedule another appointment with the technicians, and assured us in an email that the oven would be fixed. The same technician returned this month (May, 2017) to try to repair our oven. He told us there was nothing further he could do to correct the problem and told us to put foil  over the meat when broiling to cut down on the amount of grease and smoke. Inside the oven it tells you not to use foil, which I reminded him of. Then he suggested that we lower the broiling temperature to 500 degrees and once again follow the directions in the Sear's manual for broiling a 1 inch steak. Again, we placed the steak on the same broiling pan in the top oven (which my wife had already cleaned), but this time lowered the rack to the #2 position, which is a "baking " position and after 6 minutes opened the oven to turn the steak over and grease was flying everywhere (even on me), The smoke generated once again caused our fire alarms to go off. But I continued the process, and after 4 minutes broiling on the second side of the steak, we removed the steak to see that the exterior of the steak is charred and the interior of the steak is completely rear (uncooked). We have broiled chicken at the lower temperature of 450 degrees and the same issues. The oven is so hot, that the amount of smoke generated is so severe  that we can smell the odors in our second story bedrooms. The amount of grease thrown all over the oven worries us that the oven could potentially catch on fire. Again, we asked Sears to replace the oven, which they have declined to do. We have used the oven less than a dozen times in 5 months. Who would want to cook with this oven knowing that the fire alarms are going to go off each time, and that they will have to clean the excessive amount of grease all over the oven each time. The last encounter we had video of which I can supply in a separate cover. There is no doubt that this oven is too hot to handle. One of last solutions the technician gave us was to simply bake everything in our oven, rather than use the broiler. The technician has now told Sear's management that the oven needs to be replaced and can not be repaired, and Sear's has still declined to remove the oven. It's interesting, that when we purchased the oven in Dec., 2016 that the rating given by Sear's on the oven was a 5 star. If you check it today, they do not rate it on their web-site. I wonder why?
justification: The incident involves excessive smoke and grease causing fire alarms to go off, but no injury or death has occurred. The issue is persistent and likely to recur based on the description.

incident_description:
March 12, 2017

Sir:

This letter is to inform your agency about what maybe a serious health risk associated with a
product produced in Thailand.

On February 19, 2017, I purchased a TV tray from the Target store located in Falls Church,
Virginia - a copy of the sales receipt is enclosed. The TV tray is described in the enclosed
"flyer" which came with the product. The flyer states: "Durable Top wood surface wipes clean
quickly and easily." The tray does not have any visible coating or paint.

The flyer displays the tray in what appears to be with a walnut finish. The TV tray I purchased
did not have any visible coating. In fact, the surface appeared to be that of unfinished wood. The
problem I encountered arose when I stained the tray's surface with a walnut stain on Monday,
March 5, 2017. The use of the stain apparently reacted with what must be a coating intended to
make it easier to clean the tray's surface. The application of the walnut stain may have caused an
invisible and odorless gas to be produced. This caused me to experience a breathing problem
which is still evident today. I had to remove the tray from my apartment in order to stop
breathing the gas. As I write this letter, I still feel some minor breathing problems from the side
effects from the gas.

If this is a common problem with this product, it could prove to be very dangerous to people with
respiratory conditions. I trust your agency will look into this product to prevent possible harm to
others.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a breathing problem caused by an invisible gas, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it appears to be a rare reaction to a specific product modification.
