justification: The incident involved a small fire and damage to equipment but no reported injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: Enjoying outside event. Daughter, 2 years old, running with Munchin Miracle 360 sippy cup (pink)  in left hand, carrying like "football"--she fell to the ground, falling directly onto the lip of the cup.  the lip of the cup caused a deep laceration on her face / chin--which immediately bled everywhere--lots of blood.  No other noticeable injury, only to left lower face/ chin area.  Immediately held pressure and proceeded for emergency care.  Stopped at fire house to obtain gauze and place temporary dressing.  Proceeded to Kid Med in Short Pump, as it was closer than the hospital I worked.  daughter given numbing cream, then held down and sutured laceration closed-- requiring 8 stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep laceration requiring stitches, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Such specific injuries from sippy cup falls are uncommon (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
The oven racks fall with any amount of weight. It first happened with a roast turkey. The juice in the roaster splashed up and burned my arm. It next happened with a pan of lasagne and yesterday the rack fell with a Dutch oven roast   I cooked the roast with one side of the rack resting on the oven floor 

The oven is a Kenmore Elite model 790. Manufactured in Canada March 2011. 

This issue with the racks began in the past year. Apparently the oven walls have expanded from the heat, is my guess. 

There is another issue with the oven.  During the oven cleaning cycle, about midway through, the heat sensor turns off the oven. This first happened during the warranty period and the repairman showed us how to remove the panel and reset  the oven switch.   I'm wishing now that I would have returned the oven then.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from splashing juice, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue with the oven racks has occurred multiple times, making the occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description:
I have owned the Frigidaire smooth top Model FFEF3018LQB since 11/6/2010.
Last night I turned the oven to 350 to preheat and went downstairs to the laundry room. Within minutes I heard a loud popping noise,. I ran back upstairs to find the control panel shooting flames up the wall behind the stove. Luckily my husband was in the basement and able to shut the circuit breaker down immediately.  I am very lucky that my husband was home at the time as who knows how much more damage there would have been had I had to run downstairs and cut the circuit breaker. As it is there is smoke damage to the wall and the burnt plastic smell doesn't want to leave my house. I do not see a recall on this model. I did call the number given on the 2009 recall of another model as it showed that they were there until 9:00 P.M. The company recording states they are open 9-5 Monday through Friday. I will call on Monday. However, judging from the responses other people on this cite have gotten from Frigidaire I don't hold out any hope that it will do any good.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke damage but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
GE range model C2S980SEM1SS

Gas control knob has a plastic stem with a metal sleeve inside. The plastic stem has fatigued allowing the metal sleeve to spin inside of it. 

My wife left the gas control knob showing the off position, overnight.   unburned gas filled the house leading to a very dangerous situation.
justification: The incident involved unburned gas filling the house, creating a dangerous situation, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire refrigerator, new, from a local store and one night it began smoking and ignited. This was a small fire on the backside near the bottom. I discovered later that it was an electrical component (relay box?) that connected to the side of the compressor. It appears that there is a white plastic tube that carries water to the ice maker and water in the door. This tube was fine but any liquid spilled in the refrigerator could (and apparently did) travel down the tube and drip on the relay box causing it to short out and catch fire. I have pictures showing the tube and components, a picture of the relay box that caught fire, a picture of the model and serial number information, and I still have the physical part that caught fire. I contacted the manufacturer and they didn't express much interest in the problem. What really bothered me was that it just kept burning and if we were asleep at the time I wonder how far this could have escalated.
justification: The incident involved a small fire caused by an electrical short, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Came home from work and outer window on range was shattered. There were a few pieces on the floor but majority intact. It is making cracking noises. I haven't used the oven since Christmas!
justification: The window is shattered but no injury or death occurred, and the oven hasn't been used recently, indicating a low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The heating element in my GE Dual Fuel oven burst into flame. it burned for about 2 minutes, with a full flame. after I shut off the oven and let it cool down, I used tongs to touch the metal. it broke off and little pieces of metal fell into the oven.

GE calls the "heating element failure" and I have to pay to replace the part. I don't know if the flame damaged any other part of the oven.  there are other instances of this happening in comments on the internet.

please note, I was warming up the broiler. nothing spilled onto the heating elements. the oven was pretty clean. it was the upper piece, so less exposed to food dripping on it. 

Why is this not under a recall? Why is this considered "normal" failure? my previous oven was 40 years old and I never had a problem with the element exploding into flames.
justification: The incident involved a heating element bursting into flame, but no injury occurred. The occurrence likelihood is possible as similar incidents are reported online.

incident_description:
On or about March 16, 2017 I entered my kitchen to find the Right front eye of my Frigidaire smooth Surface Range  Model No. FGES3065KFB Serial No NF00921880 on high temperature and the controls were off.
After several attempts to contact Frigidaire Support Center I was told my range was not on the recall list and I would be responsible for repairs. Since, it was out of warranty. ( Purchased May, 2010. However, should I suffer damages to my home I could file a claim. I told the representative that it was a design error. That nothing should fail in the on position. Also I had more than thirty years experience in the chemical and explosives industry and we designed equipment to fail in a safe position.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with no reported injury or damage, but potential for harm if left unchecked.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidaire gas stove in November 2017.  I recently called customer service to complain about the burner knobs turning freely without pushing in causing gas to escape without noticing.  
The knobs turn approximately 3/4" before the ticking begins to let you know you are lighting the burner.  They sent an outside technician to look at the issue who confirmed this is a problem and that he has received this complaint many times.  I then received a follow up call from the corporate office to inquire about how the service call was received.  Both my husband & I expressed our concerns and were told there was nothing that could be done.  They suggested we go to the dollar store and purchase child safely cap covers.  This is not acceptable, I advise that this appliance is unsafe and could cause harm to my family and a hazard in my home.
justification: The gas stove issue poses a potential hazard with gas escaping unnoticed, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: Product is a household dishwasher used once daily. After a smoky odor was noticed, I was initially unable to determine it's cause, and the appliance appeared to be working. The following day, the appliance failed (would not power-up). I disassembled the unit and found that a small fire on the PC board had occurred, causing permanent irreparable damage. This also caused some of the case plastic to melt. I was not aware of the fire when it occurred, and it was self-extinguishing. The electrical failure did not cause the 15 amp circuit breaker to trip. Further examination of the PC board found that no fuses exist despite the presence of AC line voltage. I have kept the PC board in case further investigation is requested. There were no injuries. Damage was limited to the dishwasher itself. Product is a General Electric dishwasher, Model GSD5560G03SS, Serial #AH864064B.
justification: The incident involved a small fire and damage to the dishwasher, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
(01/30/2017) The consumer stated that he had put a roast in the oven. All of a sudden the coil inside of the unit started to arc and burn. The consumer tried to shut the unit off. The lights on the pad went off, but the coils kept burning. 

The consumer had to shut the unit off at the breaker. 

The consumer went online and saw on YouTube that the same thing had happened to others.

The consumer called Sears Recall hotline and was advised that his unit was not listed.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
03/18/2017
Consumer stated she was cooking two potatoes in her air fryer 370 to 400 degrees for about 20 minutes. She stated she opened the drawer to turn the potatoes she heard a loud pop. She unplugged the air fryer and that's when she saw a glow at the bottom of the air fryer. She removed air fryer from kitchen to outside front walkway. She stated the air fryer burst into flame 30 seconds later. She put the flame out by using two buckets of water.


03/20/2017 
Consumer stated she spoke with rep [REDACTED] at [REDACTED] and was advised to mail product to quality department to receive a full refund
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions to occur.

incident_description:
Last December my wife was using our LG Microwave oven when it began to emit acrid odor (burning smell).  She turned off the unit and inspected the food product which was still cold.  She started the microwave a second time and smelled the same odor.  At this point she let the microwave rest for an hour and then attempted to heat something again only to smell the same order after a few seconds of operation.  At this point she turned off and unplugged the microwave and left it for me to inspect.

I'm a mechanical engineer and working in the field of forensics.  Part of my job description also includes fire investigation.  

Upon inspection of the microwave I found evidence of a high resistance connection one of the microwaves thermal cutouts.  The ABS base of the thermal cutout is melted and the crimp connection on ones side is welded on.  Note, this connection was not welded at the time of manufacture, instead the welding happened as a result of the incident.  

LG Model Number: LCS1112ST /01
Product Code: MS1142X.CS1EBBY
Serial Number: 310TABN3M005
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave emitting a burning smell but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I own a Cuisinart Convection Toaster Oven, model TOB-60N.  I noticed this morning when I moved the oven to clean the counter that the plug had melted to the back of the toaster oven.   There is no visible warning on the oven that the back panel could get hot enough to melt the plug.  IÃÂm certain I am not the only consumer who uses a counter height plug to power the oven, and to unknowingly push the oven as close to the wall as possible.  This is a serious safety issue!   Pictures are attached.   Please advise.
justification: The incident involves a melted plug but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) as the issue could affect many users unaware of the back panel's heat.

incident_description: Started the dishwasher like normal, we started smelling burnt plastic and checked the kitchen. Smoke was coming from the dishwasher.  I opened it and it seemed as though the inside of the door was burning.
justification: Smoke and burning plastic were observed, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We purchased the Crock-Pot casserole slow cooker and used it twice.  The first time we brought it to a party and set it on the counter on the "warm" setting.  We noticed that it was extremely hot to the touch and decided that it wasn't safe to have where people would be reaching over it.  The second time we used it, we put some food in it and set it on the "warm" setting and left the house for a few hours.  When we returned, we found a huge crack in our quartz right under the Crock-Pot.  We filed a claim with the company and sent it in for testing.  They said that it was operating properly and that it isn't insulated.  I told them that someone is going to get seriously burned from this thing and they said that you have to use your best judgement when using it.  I have since read in reviews on Amazon.com that people have been burned by it.  One woman stated that she received a second degree burn from it.  We feel this item is very dangerous and should be recalled.
justification: The incident describes potential for burns and property damage, with reports of second-degree burns, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) based on multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: A few years ago I purchased the Cuisinart Toaster Oven/Broiler Model TOB-40.  I notices lately that the bottom removable crumb catch pan had a burn mark on it and when I looked inside the toaster oven the rear heating element was actually bent down toward the pan.  I really like the toaster oven and when I went on line to purchase a new one I noticed that the reviews said this problem has happened to other people.  It is definitely a fire hazard and I feel this toaster should have been recalled.  I took pictures of the problem but cannot seem to attach them to this message.
justification: The description indicates a fire hazard with burn marks but no actual injury or fire incident reported.

incident_description: The gas oven stop heating. Upon inspection I found the igniter had blown a hole through he heat shied. If the glow igniter did not fail a fire may have occurred.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (igniter damage) with potential for a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: Normal use of dishwasher caused a large spark near bottom left of the dishwasher on the outside upon closing the door.  It happened yesterday and again today.  While unloading dishwasher today, we noticed that there was water in the bottom and that it didn't drain after the last wash cycle.  After draining water and trying to reset device, can not get it to run a full cycle.  There are reports of similar incidents that even caused fires with models made between March 2006 to August 2009.  Unplugged device and called manufacturer.
justification: The incident involves sparks and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sparking occurs when using product. Source of spark can be seen when you look through the door. It is occurring by the plastic piece on the front left of the microwave. One of th epieces that  holds up the metal grill.

I see your recall but think that the serial number range may not be correct.

My serial number is TR53557577. The manufacture date is August 2015.
justification: Sparking is observed but no injury or damage is reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Our Samsung refrigerator was heating up and melting part of the light bulb socket (where it screws in). When we contacted Samsung support they said there were no known problems with our model number, RFG295AARS. We assured them that this was in fact a problem and explained that it is only noticeable if you take the plastic cover off and detach the light socket as it is hidden from plain sight. This was happening on both light bulb sockets. After sending photos, Samsung said they would send someone out to look at it free of charge in order to document and evaluate if this was of larger concern to the company. Next, I was contacted by the outsourced service representative who insisted it would be a $75 charge. Apparently Samsung did not relay that it was a fire risk and should be inspected free of charge. We went round and round with Samsung, which ultimately never ended the problem being investigated. Today, a couple of months later, one of the bulbs exploded, sending shards of glass out toward my wife who was unloading groceries.  Then it started sparking and the burning the metal under the light bulb. Luckily, I was nearby and was able to pull the refrigerator out, unplug it, and put out the fire! It is clear that Samsung model number RFG295AARS has undetected problems putting owners at risk!
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb that sent glass shards toward a person and caused a fire, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
We bought an Amana gas stove about 7 years ago that had a self-cleaning feature.

Last Saturday, April22, 2017, we put the stove on self-cleaning mode- we had done this before, but not very often.

We later noticed that the self-cleaning appeared to be taking a long time; we began it at 1 in the afternoon, and it
was still going at 5.

I ran a quick errand at about 5, and was gone for about 45 minutes. When I returned, a wooden butcher block we kept on top of the stove to hold a set of knives had caught fire. The flames were 18 inches high, and the stove's digital control panel had melted. The stove's oven door was also locked shut.

In addition, the smoke alarm in the house was sounding, and the entire first floor was full of smoke when my daughter and I entered the house.

I put out the fire by grabbing the butcher block with a large towel, and tossing it out into the yard.
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: While gently opening the oven door the handle released from its screw on one side and caused the whole glass face of the oven to shatter. My mother, husband and myself were standing in the blast zone. I received cuts to my bare feet. I am very thankful that my 1 year old daughter was not in the area and that she was not the one to pull on the oven handle. The amount of pressure I had placed on the handle was VERY minimal. This experience was nerve-racking for new parents. Sears and Kenmore's customer service was not concerned in the slightest that this is a potential hazard. They claimed that in order for the oven to shatter like that we had to have hit it hard with something, which is false. There are no recalls on this range per Sears, but if you search the internet many other people have had this issue with glass faced ranges.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts to bare feet) and could have been worse, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
Using the wall oven for normal baking, and noticed 2 hours later the fan was still running. Checked the oven, found it was still heating. The oven had been turned off, and the indicator panel showed it was off. Tried resetting, no change. Shut off main breaker.
Next day, tried turning breaker back on (supervised). A few hours later, the oven spontaneously started heating - got very hot. Turned off circuit breaker again and kept off, called Bosch for repair. They sent a tech, but Bosch refused to repair the unit/replace the part, saying it was too old. I told their reps I was concerned this was a serious fire hazard, "nothing they could do."
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: While cooking on electric range top the burner would only set to high - even when a lower setting was indicated on control knob; this led to burnt food and pans. On several occasions the control knob was set to "off", but the burner would remain on high. This is an extreme fire hazard and will be reported to local and State Fire Marshall's Office. Frigidaire/Electrolux has a recall for exactly the same unsafe condition but claims my model is not included.
justification: The burner malfunction poses an extreme fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported. The issue is likely to recur based on the description.

incident_description:
On multiple occasions, while cooking food in my Kenmore (mode 790.48789901) electric built in oven,  the oven racks (and hot food!) will fall from their slots and hit the Oven bottom spewing hot food all over the oven, and me. This usually happens, upon moving or touching the pan inside. On  one occasion,  the racks and food  fell while the door was closed, shattering the glass pan inside, and contents all over the hot oven. What a mess!, and dangerous mess to clean up. This seems to happen when the oven is used for an extended period of time, or at higher temperatures, 400* or higher. On more than one occasion, I have been splashed with hot food when this happens, causing minor to slightly moderate burns on my arms, and/or hands, and even my chest. 

This has happened for many months now and I have been researching the issue, and trying to determine the cause of this issue. We even had a repairman out for another issue, he felt the Oven walls were likely warped. 


Upon calling the company, I learned that no recalls were issued on the appliance. When I asked if there were other complaints about this Oven and this issue I was told yes. Many. I asked how many were needed before the company issued a recall, the person  did not know. I also searched the product online and found many other consumers had  the same complaint. Someone is going to get seriously injured.
justification: The description reports multiple incidents of minor to moderate burns from hot food splashing due to oven rack failures, indicating injury severity (level 3) and a likely occurrence (level 4) given the frequency and similar complaints from other users.

incident_description:
LG Electric Range Model LRE30453ST manufactured October 2011 in Mexico bearing the Serial # 110MMRQ0G542 . The controls for the electric range top burners intermittently fail to turn off or turn on the heating elements on the glass stove range top.
Spoke with LG consumer products division  - they say that my range is not part of the previous recall for LG Ranges with a similar issues from 2005 and 2006.
They do not feel that there is safety issue with my product, but are willing to repair it for $380.
justification: The electric range's controls intermittently fail, posing a potential hazard, but there is no report of injury or death.

incident_description:
Microwave oven randomly turned itself on and off throughout the day. The timer showed "0:00" and the light did not turn on, so the only way to know that the oven turned itself on was the sound of the fan. 

Once discovered, I pushed the stop button, but it did not stop the operation. I opened the door, which stopped the oven from operating. The glass plate had a large circular crack with black burn marks around it, and black marks were on the floor of the oven underneath that spot.

The exterior of the oven was very warm to the touch.
I unplugged the oven and will no longer use it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave with no reported injury, but potential for harm if not addressed.

incident_description: On May 8, 2017 in the evening, my Kenmore Electric Range had the glass on the oven door explode.  The oven was off and had been off for over an hour after cooking at 325 degrees.  All the glass exploded leaving glass all over our kitchen floor.  My husband and I were both within a foot of the oven door at the time.  Neither of us had touched it.  We were lucky to not be looking into the oven door at the time of the explosion.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported despite the close proximity of the individuals.

incident_description: I had two rectangular baking dishes in the oven with meat loaves in each. I removed the first when the baking time was done. I inspected the meat to make sure it was cooked through. It was fine. I was just about to remove the second dish from the oven when we heard the explosion. The second dish exploded in the oven. The boiling hot meat juices dropped to the oven bottom. Thank goodness I was not reaching for the dish when it exploded. I could have easily sustained burns or cuts. We had to throw out the meat loaf as it was covered in tiny glass bits. The oven bottom had broken glass everywhere, walls splattered. My husband was able to remove the first layer of stove bottom plating to pick up glass and clean the surface. But, he was not able to remove the next layer of metal above the heating elements. There are still chunks of glass below. We can no longer use the bottom drawer, glass could fall into the items.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing damage and potential for injury, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
On 3-1-17 I purchased a Kitchen Aide dishwasher from Lowes in Elk Grove, California.
Store #1148. 
A family of 5 has been using this dishwasher including small children ages 8 and 3 years old.
We began noticing gray stains on the dishes etc.
Finally we realized that the plastic from the dishwasher racks was melting onto the dishes.
We have the dishes as evidence.
This is very concerning as to the health risks this could cause. We have all been eating off of the contaminated 
dishes.
I have contacted the manager [REDACTED] at Lowes and he was not very helpful.
I feel we deserve a new dishwasher/ dishes etc, and damages for all our troubles.
Please help us get justice.
Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves potential health risks from contaminated dishes, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: After using the microwave, the door was closed and the microwave began to run without any buttons being pressed. The interior light and fan were off, but there was an audible buzzing that stopped when the door was opened. It spontaneously resumed again each time the door was closed. The plate inside was getting very hot. With the door open, the microwave was unplugged and plugged back in. This time, the microwave spontaneously began running with the door open. The microwave has been unplugged since the incident. It is ~18months old, thus out of warranty. But since it failed in a way that could have been very dangerous for my family and/or home, GE is offering an ~20% discount on a new product. Given the potential consequence of this product failure, this response seems insufficient. I've seen numerous other reports of similar GE microwave models failing in the same way (including an attempted class action lawsuit in the Michigan US district courts, Case No. [REDACTED]). So I'm not inclined to roll the dice again until GE determines the cause of this problem.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned dangerously but no injury occurred, and similar incidents have been reported, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
This kitchen blender has a hollow pitcher handle with an opening at the top into which food migrates during blending. The handle isnÃÂt user-openable, so the lodged food remains inside, rots, and molds. When the blender is used again the food inside the top of the handle can then remigrate into new food that is blended, introducing contaminants into mixture. The manufacturer sent me a replacement pitcher, but the same thing happened during the first usage. 

I spoke to the companyÃÂs customer service today and they acknowledged that the pitcher had been redesigned in a newer version of the product so that the handle no longer has the opening, but the unsafe product is still being sold at Costco and other retailers, and many thousands of the defective product have been sold.
justification: The incident involves contamination of food due to a design flaw, but no injury or death is reported. The issue is likely to occur given the widespread sale of the defective product.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid Oven glass door exploded.  Model KEBS107SWH purchased August 2008.

We were just heating up the over to 350 degrees to bake a cake.  Glass door exploded.  Nobody was hurt, but it was terrifying.

We have contacted Kitchenaid to tell them.
justification: The oven door exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury. Such occurrences are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: I just returned home this evening to the odor of scorching ceramic. While we were out, my dog had jumped up, resting his paws on our new LG electric range, and inadvertently turned on the stove top, which had a ceramic mug sitting on it. The burner was turned to high and the mug was blackened from the heat. This could have burnt my house down; thank goodness we were gone for only an hour. I have owned this range for merely a week and this is the third time a burner was turned on by accident. The other two times, I leaned against the knob and it came on. I caught it, however, because a sound plays when a knob is turned on. That doesn't help when dogs are left alone.  These knobs turn way too easily, especially given their location (instead of being on the back of the appliance, the knobs are on the front side above the oven) and accessibility to dogs that counter surf and to small children. I am only now reading reviews of this appliance and I see others share my complaint.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, and the occurrence is likely given the repeated accidental activations and design flaw.

incident_description: I was loading the Kitchen Aid dishwasher model numberKDTE104ESS1 and my leg hit the side of the open door. There is a very sharp edge on it and it cut deeply into my leg. This also happened with my wife a couple of weeks ago and cut the top of her foot.
justification: The incident caused a deep cut to the leg, indicating an injury, and it has occurred twice recently, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: Monday night I put 5 cut up red potatoes on my Rachael Ray Yum-O Baking pan in an oven set at 375 degrees.  10 minutes into baking my daughter and I smelled smoke and my husband found out that the oven was on fire.  Luckily my husband was there to help me put out the fire.  Upon further investigation after getting the fire out we saw that the rubber stoppers on the pans burned up in the oven.  Its very frustrating that what you would think is heatsafe and fireproof isnt.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injuries were reported, only material damage.

incident_description:
In May 2016, I purchased a Samsung Oven, Model #NE58F9500SS and Serial #J1967DCH500720B.  On several occasions since then, the stove top range (heating elements) has been turned on accidentally by merely walking and slightly brushing up against the range knobs.  This causes the range-top to be heating up without supervision and for long periods of time until noticed later.
On April 21, 2017, during a dinner party attended by about 20 people, I removed a large casserole from the oven and placed it on the range-top for serving guests.  None of the range-top elements were used during the preparation of the casserole, just the oven.  During the time when guests were serving themselves from the casserole placed on the range-top, a guest accidentally brushed against one of the knobs and caused a heating element to be placed into a high/heat position.  The casserole dish exploded sending shards of glass at my guests and across the room.  Luckily, no guests were injured, but the risk of injury to them was extremely high.  (My granddaughter had just finished serving herself and had turned to walk away.)
I am concerned with this oven as the knobs are easily accessible to anyone walking nearby and can easily be brushed up against.  I must note that no one in the family is obese.  I am thin and brushed up against the stove several times in the last year.
justification: The incident caused no injuries but posed a high risk of injury due to the easily triggered knobs, and similar incidents have occurred multiple times.

incident_description: Our Viking range has a griddle which is now turning on by itself. There is a recall on certain Viking ranges but I was told my unit is outside the date range and not covered.
justification: The griddle turning on by itself is an incident with potential safety implications, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Oven refused to shutoff or respond to stop button or opening door. Unit is built-in under cabinet model so power cord was not accessible. Unit was finally shutoff by a neighbor by shutting off breaker. It had been running for 2 hours and was extremely hot and smoking.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and became extremely hot and smoking, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Cuisinart coffee maker model DCC1100 serial #01202- 1 hour after coffee brewed and hot plate in warming mode, control panel blanked, heating element over temped and started burning plastic and insulation. I was in room when this occurred and was able to unplug coffee maker before further damage could occur. There are two thermal fuses to heating element wiring neither of which opened.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing overheating and burning plastic, but no injury occurred as the user unplugged it in time.

incident_description: When using the oven the top element never shuts off leading to an overheating error.  Even when the error is displayed the element never shuts off.
justification: The oven's overheating error poses a risk of incident without immediate injury, and the issue is likely to occur based on the description.

incident_description: I have my gas turn on and was told my stove was a hazard and to tell my property management. I did such and they said i would get a new stove and 2 months later i get lies and the run around. I have two small kids AND if you turn on the oven it goes boom and the door flies open. Also smells like a gas leak
justification: The stove poses a clear hazard with potential for explosion and gas leaks, endangering the resident and two small children.

incident_description: Tappan electric range glass oven door exploded sending glass 6' onto kitchen floor from oven door.  A few pieces of glass found 17' away in dining room.  This unit is approximately ten (10) years old, it has never been abused in any way. Thankfully no one in kitchen at the time.  Oven had not been used in 4 days prior to incident.  Two loud crashes heard from upstairs. Self cleaning feature had only been used twice, years ago, because the fumes were intolerable.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding oven door) but no injuries or deaths, and the likelihood is unlikely given the specific conditions described (old unit, rare use of self-cleaning feature).

incident_description: Prepping vegetables when knife fell apart, flinging the blade to the floor and cutting the top of my foot.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the foot, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: While attempting to blend frozen mangos in my Blendtec 570 blender, a jagged chunk of the wall of the blender jar broke out and was thrown across the room at high velocity.  Thankfully no-one was in the path of this projectile, but it had the potential to inflict mortal injury if someone had been.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous projectile but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description:
This report is regarding a recent model Keurig 2.0 coffee maker product.

The design of the Keurig 2.0 coffee maker involves two thin hollow metal tubes that water passes in and out of the kcup through. These tubes have a tendency to clog resulting in building pressure inside the kcup. When the pressure reaches to great of force, the coffee maker begins spraying scolding water and scolding coffee grounds out all sides, several feet in distance. 

In my case, no injuries resulting however had I been standing next to the product it would have resulted in burns.

I have followed all cleaning instructions, never used off brand kcup items in the brewer, nor has the machine ever been misused. A quick check of the web reveals this is well known problem with other consumers having been burned.
justification: The incident involved no injuries but had potential to cause burns, and similar incidents are reported by other consumers.

incident_description:
Kenmore range serial number VF73148328 model number 790.96002601

Front right burner turns on spontaneously, heats above the degree set (turns to high despite being set to low), and refuses to turn off - have to unplug the stove to turn it off. 
This issue has caused a small kitchen fire (damaging the linoleum which I will have to replace) when the burner was set on low to caramelize onions and spontaneously went to high heat causing the onions to burn and catch fire.
This burner will not turn off when used, causing us to have to unplug the stove for several minutes in order to "reset" it. As a result we do not use the burner.
The issue has also caused minor burns when this burner has spontaneously turned on while the stove top was being cleaned. This issue has also caused a situation where the stove must be unplugged between uses in order to reduce the risk of house fire. 
This has been an ongoing issue for the last year (First incident was in March 2016)
justification: The incident has caused a small kitchen fire and minor burns, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The issue is ongoing and has occurred multiple times, making the occurrence likelihood 4 (likely).

incident_description:
We were awakened at about 5am to a loud noise in our home. Upon investigation we saw flames and smoke coming from our microwave. The microwave was not in use at the time. the door of the microwave was open and the loud noise we heard was probably the door blowing open.We had experienced no previous problems with the microwave. We extinguished the fire with a fire extinguisher and the fire department arrived and removed the microwave from our home. They also tried to evacuate as much smoke as possible from our home and checked the walls and did an air quality test before we were allowed to reenter our home. We are still dealing with the smoke issue in our home and of course we had to replace the microwave and trim kit. Fortunately we did not have cabinet damage as we were able to put the fire out so quickly. 
This was a spontaneous fire. Had we been out of town we would have sustained tremendous property damage. We were lucky. No one was injured.
justification: The incident involved a spontaneous fire causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
In November 2014 I bought a Kenmore glassstop range.  I noticed how fast it cooked and initially thought it was because a newer model.  I had to continually turn down the heat and watched how fast it was cooking.  Things often burned.  The oven had the same problem.
I finally looked on line and saw manny entries from people having the same problems as far back as 2009.
Even my next door neighbor has the same problem.
It appears the problem is with the infinite switches.  Some Kenmore ranges had recalls to correct the problem.  The last recall date I see is in 2009.  All these years later and the problem continues. How can these ranges continue to be manufactured without the problem being fixed.

There is no recall on my range and Sears will not repair unless I pay.  My model number is 790.94203310

For the incident report, I listed the date purchased.  It has been an ongoing problem.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the range's performance causing food to burn, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: The lights on our LG Model #LFC25760SW are staying on even when the doors are closed AGAIN. This is the second time this fault has occurred since we purchased the unit in approx. 2007. Sometimes the lights come on when the doors are open, sometimes not. Sometimes they stay on when the doors are closed, sometimes not. When the lights stay on they get so hot that they have begun to melt the housing they are in - you can see the plastic deforming and the white color going brown. They have spoiled food in the top of the refrigerator. Everything I've found online from other people who have experienced this indicated that this is due to a faulty design and a bad relay. Bottom line this product is a piece of junk and I will NEVER buy LG again. I am prepared for the standard cut and paste response from LG that I've seen to other complaints on this site. I'm also aware of a class action lawsuit filed in New Jersey against LG for this exact problem.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator light causing food spoilage and potential fire hazard due to overheating, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: We were pre heating the bottom oven of our LG electric double oven range model LDE3037ST and before it was done pre heating we heard a loud noise, then a crash sound. On opening the lower oven door we found shattered glass all over the inside of the oven. It turns out the inside glass had shattered, most were small pieces, but some small enough to cut a person, in fact did cut as we were cleaning up. We are now not sure that we can clean the oven enough to remove all the glass and make it safe for cooking.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from glass shards, and similar incidents are unlikely but documented.

incident_description:
There have been several incidents of our recently acquired LG stove being accidentally turned on and releasing gas. In each case, a burner was turned on via inadvertently brushing up against the control knobs.  In some cases we observed this as it happened; most recently on two occasions, we noticed the burner was on due to smell of gas.

This is not a one-off situation.  It has occurred at least a half-dozen times since we purchased the stove a few months back.

I believe the likely cause is the design (size, location and/or type) of the range controls on the front panel. 

Specifically, a) the front controls have very big knobs, b) the knob springs are very weak, and c) the front panel with the knobs is diagonal (making the knobs very easy to bump into when reaching near the stove).


The make of the range is LG, the mode is: LSG4513ST
justification: The incident involves gas release due to accidental stove activation, posing a hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Caller purchased all new appliances and all are fine with the exception of the dishwasher which can be opened by his 18 month old baby who can open the unit while it is running.
He is afraid that she may become burned by the hot steam and the water.
He said that it does not open with the force of the water running while it is washing dishes but if the baby pulls the door it does come open.
He is reporting this as a severe burn and potential scald hazard
There are no injuries being reported at this time
He has contacted the manufacturer and spoke with [REDACTED] who advised him that this is the way the unit is built and that there is nothing that can be done.
justification: No injuries reported, but there is a clear hazard with the dishwasher opening during operation, posing a burn risk to the child.

incident_description:
The consumer used the left front burner for a few minutes to boil water and she used the oven for approximately one hour at 350 degrees. She then turned everything off and states that the fan was still running. She later returned to the kitchen because the fan was still running and she noticed the oven was off but the stove top was not cool. She left and returned 30 minutes later because the fan was still running. She noticed the stove top was hot  but the control knobs were on the "Off" position. The consumer unplugged the range and waited a few minutes. When she plugged it back in she noticed that the left front burner immediately turned on. The consumer has left the range unplugged.

The consumer contacted the firm today and informed them of the incident. The consumer was told that the firm has not received reports of this nature and they told her the range was out of warranty so they were not able to provide a free repair. The consumer was also told that the firm would have to send their own technician to examine the range and determine whether the problem is a manufactures defect. 

The consumer indicated that the plastic front panel was replaced because it was scratched but there haven't been any mechanical repairs.

The consumer said there was a prior incident when the a burner turned on by itself but she doesn't recall the incident. 

The consumer uses the unit once a day.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner turning on by itself, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is 'possible' as it has happened before but is not a frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer states that he heard a beep sound followed by a bop sound. The consumer came into the kitchen to find that the microwave had caught fires with flames on the inside reaching out from the back of the unit where the vents are located. The unit was not on. The consumer was able to put the fire out with a kitchen towel however he had to take the unit out because of all the smoke it was emitting; the consumer had to air his home because of the smell of burnt plastic.

The consumer states that prior to the incident, the microwave had been used that same morning to heat up coffee.

04/10/2017 - The consumer contacted RCA and informed them what happened. The representative he spoke to asked the consumer to send them photographs for evaluation; after their evaluation is complete, he would be contacted. The consumer's Case Number is: [REDACTED], and his Work Order Number is: [REDACTED].

The consumer states that prior to the incident, the microwave was used approximately three to four times daily.

The consumer plans on keeping his unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

The consumer states that this microwave was a replacement to the original one of the same model number, which was causing the same problems. The retailer provided the replacement.
justification: The microwave caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but the consumer was able to extinguish it without injury.

incident_description: Product is a GE 36" Sealed Gas Cooktop (serial # AD706778Q, model PGP976).  It was purchased 5/2014.  On April 30, 3017: the control lock which is a dial to unlock the cooktop and prevent unwanted use, spontaneously started to smoke, sparked, and combusted into flames although the stove was not in use. The [REDACTED] Fire Department came to the scene of the fire.  No person was harm, and the fire was fully managed.  Please note, the cooktop was not in use at the moment of combustion.  The Fire Department noted that there were no signs of a grease fire. The smell of the combustion resembled an electric fire.
justification: The incident involved a cooktop spontaneously combusting, causing a fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: There is a Hotpoint oven model# RB757WH4WW in the house that we rent. The outer glass door exploded at about 6:30 in the morning. The oven had not been on since the previous night. The oven is about 4 years old. Luckily we were all in the bed when this happened, but there was glass all over the entire kitchen.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no one was injured as they were in bed.

incident_description: First time using Nostalgia Electrics Hot Air Popcorn Maker; followed instructions EXACTLY and unit's shell melted.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage (melted shell) but no reported injury, making it a severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it's a first-time occurrence with exact instructions followed.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the oven range has a crack on the left side that runs from the front to the back of the burner.

The contacted the Manufacturer and a Service Technician was dispatched. After inspection, the Service Technician informed the consumer that the unit was defective. The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and was informed that the repair was not covered under its warranty, and extended warranty.

The consumer indicates that she uses her oven range twice daily. The consumer plans on keeping her oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involves a defective oven range with a crack, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: We bought this Maytag dishwasher on 5-5-14, so its not even 3 years old, we did not buy the extended warranty-wish we had now, because yesterday morning i started the dishwasher like i do every day, and we heard 2 pops, and then the dishwasher started smoking. We turned the breaker off, and opened the door-smoke everywhere, it has started on fire. After it cooled down, we took the front panel off, and the plug where it attaches to the brain of the unit was burned, and the wires melted together. This thing could have burned our house down, if we would have went outside to do our farm chores 10 minutes earlier we may not have had a house to come back to-A newer machine should not do this-so now we have to replace it and it cost $772-and now we are out a machine. The Model number is MDB8959SBS3-very upsetting.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his oven caught fire while in use.  He stated that he opened the oven door and a fire ball escape and he noticed that the contents was on fire.  He used the fire extinguisher to contain the flames.  There prior incidents or service calls.

Caller stated that after he powered off the unit he powered it on later on to see what could have caused the incident.  He noticed that there was a crack at the bottom of the interior of the oven, it was large enough for him to see the heating element.

(1/16/17) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that the unit was no longer under warranty and there were unable to assist him.  The retailer was contacted and recommended a service technician who advised him that the lifespan on the unit is approximately 15 years, caller stated he only had it for 5 years.

Caller feels that the oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The oven caught fire but the caller managed to extinguish it without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Our Bosch dishwasher shorted out due to a defective power cord. It charred and burned the electric box before tripping the circuit breaker.  The same power cord was involved in a safety recall, but Bosch failed to recall and refused to cover the repairs because it wasn't the identical model number in the CPSC recall.  The repairs cost $261.55.  This defect is a serious fire hazard.   A picture is attached to the email.  The recall was 16-003.
justification: The dishwasher shorted out and caused damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I have a Bosch dishwasher.  Water somehow gets into an electronics cavity. After 2 visits the service man cannot accurately and verifiably identify the source of the leak. Bosch is not interested in pursuing this. They just deny warranty repairs. I don't know if other units have this flaw but it's a fire and electrocution issue.
justification: Water entering the electronics cavity poses a potential fire and electrocution hazard, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I had GE Profile stainless steel dishwasher model PDW8280N20SS, it was used daily until the day of incident where we smelled burnt plastic smell all around the home at 6:00 am, when checked the heater element stayed on after the cycle completed (malfunction in controller circuit) and has melted sprayer, filter mesh around it and silverware holder.

I bought this upgraded model for its more safer features, I also had to replace control board on the GE profile refrigerator in first 2 month due to mfg issue.

It seems GE neglected to provide a breaker circuit for this kind of issue that can lead to fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing damage to the dishwasher but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Just bought this pan today and cleaned it like the instructions said.  I stacked the glass lid vertically in my dryer rack in the sink and before I new it I had shattered glass everywhere.  I got cut on my L hand and the back of my right ankle.  Of course I feel like I have glass shards in me feet -- I was barefoot.  It was very difficult to clean up -- apparently the glass is not tempered or shatter proof in any way.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts to the hand and ankle, and potential glass shards in the feet, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I was cooking a pork chop in this microwave grill pan which I had used several times successfully before.  However, on this incident, I put the pork chop in the pan and placed it in the microwave.  I set the microwave for three minutes.  The microwave is 1000Watt.  At two minutes, my smoke alarm went off and my microwave was billowing black smoke.  When I opened the door, the pan was on fire, flames shooting and black smoke everywhere!  There is no question that the smoke alarm saved me from a house fire.  After this incident I searched the web, and this is not the first incident of this product catching fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Hello, I purchased a set of glass storage containers from Glasslock. The name of the product is "Oven Safe". It is advertised as oven and microwave safe. However while using it to microwave rice when the glass container shattered. I contacted Glasslock and informed them as to what a happened. I provided them with photos of the broken container. 

I checked [REDACTED] reviews of the product to find this has been occurring for years. There are many positive reviews of this product but I believe the number of one star [REDACTED] reviews shows a pattern of these containers exploding into sharp pieces in the microwave. Many of the reviews have photos that look just like the ones I took. I put in a link below to the reviews. 

There are also reviews stating that the glass unexpectedly shards and glass ends up in the food. One person stated that they contacted Glasslock about this and that the company would not replace the item. These glass shards are a different issue from the microwave problem.

I discovered that the model of container I purchased is made by Glasslock Europe. However the American version that is sold on[REDACTED] and other retailers has the same safety issue's as the European one. 

Glasslock did not acknowledge if they have heard of this happening before. I don't know how they could not have heard of it when it was so easy for me to find reports. These products should not be listed as microwave safe.

I can provide photos if it would help. 

Thank You
[REDACTED]

[REDACTED]

http://glasslockusa.com/product-category/oven-safe/
justification: The incident describes injury potential from glass shards in food, and the occurrence likelihood is high based on multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description:
(01/23/2017)The consumer stated that she was reheating a dish of food in the unit. About three minutes later,the consumer came back to the kitchen and heard a popping sound coming from the microwave. The consumer unplugged the unit. When she open the microwave oven door, smoke filled the house

The inside of the unit has melted. The cabinets above the unit are scorched. 

(01/24/2017)The consumer contacted the firm. A technician from Williston Park TV and Radio Repair was dispatched out on 1/30. When the technician came out he open the door of the microwave, took pictures and left. He also advised the consumer that she would hear from  Samsung.

(02/02/2017) The consumer received a call from Williston Park and was advised that Samsung rejected her claim because whatever the consumer was trying to heat up caused the fire.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted microwave, scorched cabinets) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The consumer set the oven to bake at 350 degrees and placed the dish inside. The dish had bread stuffing. Approximately 10 minutes later, the consumer heard a loud explosion and noticed that the dish exploded. The consumer states that the dish was advertised as oven safe. The consumer indicated that this was the first time she used the dish. The dish shattered into pieces and the consumer threw away the pieces of glass.

The consumer then visited the firm's website and filled out their contact form; advising them of the incident. The firm advised the consumer to send them the pieces of glass but she no longer had them. The consumer was told that the glass was made of soda-lime and would shatter into large pieces but the consumer stated that the pieces were both large and small. They also suggested that the dish could have been cracked prior to the incident but the consumer said it was not cracked. The consumer was also advised that the dish is discontinued but she is concerned that it is still in the market and it should be recalled.

The consumer also visited Safeway's website and filled out their contact form; advising them of the incident. The consumer stated that she never received a response from Safeway.
justification: The dish exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is rated as possible given the consumer's experience and the dish's discontinuation.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his electric range which came with his manufactured home November 2006.
This caller is reporting that on Friday, March 10, 2017 his electric range after the baking/bottom element caught fire while oven was preheating.
Flames were as high as three inches high and burned the element in half.
He uses the oven very rarely but wanted to heat precooked meatballs                                             
The caller states that he thought she saw a light and then thought maybe he had left the oven light on but then saw that there were flames so he turned the oven off then threw a wet towel he had been wiping the counter off with which extinguished the fire.
He ordered a new element Monday, March 13, 2017  but then thought that he should contact the manufacturer which prompted him to contact the manufacturer Friday, March 17, 2017 after reading that the part was manufactured in Mexico.
The manufacturer informed him that it was not a knockoff part and that it was their product.
There are no injuries being reported
Bottom Element is Part# 316075104
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description: Fire in the back of the stove, which burned insulation off most of the wiring.  Started with a loud sound like an explosion, the stove literally moved.  Fire burned itself out before the fire company arrived.  Fire originally shot out of vents on the rear of the appliance.  We pulled the stove out from the wall and cabinets or they would have caught fire as well.
justification: The fire caused significant damage to the stove and wiring, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The glass lid on a pot exploded while heating water. The water had just begun to boil with chicken breasts inside. 

I ordered the pots in April of 2012 from Amazon. The pot was part of a set: T-fal C836SC
justification: The glass lid exploded during use, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: This morning I plugged in my Capresso coffee grinder - the outlet is known to be good/property wired. WITHOUT the coffee grinder button being depressed, the grinder sparked and let out a loud pop immediately after being plugged in. It left a dark ring on my butcher block counter, which wipe away with some determination.
justification: The coffee grinder sparked and caused a loud pop, leaving a mark on the counter, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: GE adora Dishwasher model: ghda676n00ss at rental house caught fire.  Luckily renters were at home and were able to put out the fire.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident, but no injuries were reported as the renters were able to put it out.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting that her electric range glass oven door exploded.
She purchased this range  December 2012 from an appliance sales retailer in Ft. Myers, Florida and had no problems with it until March 16th, 2017.
The morning of March 16th, 2017 the consumer placed her range on the cleaning cycle then after approximately one hour she heard a sound like an explosion or very loud crash.  She and her husband rushed to the kitchen where they saw glass all over their kitchen and viewed that the inside door had exploded with the glass coming out through the bottom of the outside glass.
The range was immediately turned off.
She is reporting this incident as a severe hazard of laceration injury.
There are no injuries being reported at this time.
She contacted the manufacturer who advised the caller that this situation had been a problem with this model. the only thing they could do is schedule repair at the consumer's expense of $311.29 which she has scheduled but which she believes is totally unfair.
She has filed a claim with FTC.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door causing property damage but no injuries, and the manufacturer acknowledged it as a known issue with the model.

incident_description: The Sabbath mode (190ÃÂ°F) malfunctioned, almost causing a house fire, scorching our food and the manual thermometer. The thermometer read 550ÃÂ°F. We are not sure how much greater temperature was, as this is the upper limit of the device. We believe this is a fire hazard. See thermometer, exhibit A.
justification: The malfunction caused scorching and posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We have had an ongoing issue with our LG Gas range for years now. Every so often we have found a burner knob is partially turned and gas is leaking out. We cannot be certain whether this is from bumping the knob or from a failure to shut off completely. Like others have also reported I have also found it seems there is a flaw in the knob design which causes the part of the knob that surrounds the metal stem on the switch to be both soft and pliable and as such prone to cracking and breakage.

I had read through a number of prior complaints at CPSC online today following what really became the last straw just yesterday when our range had apparently been leaking gas while we were away and had our dog closed up alone inside the house. It was possible the gas had been on four or more hours and it certainly took a few hours for a us to air out. This really is a legitimate safety concern.

I am truly disappointed the manufacturer does not even seem to address any of these similar complaints with any sort of permanent solution, or really any useful advice at all. Many customers online complain that the customer service agents only pass the call over to the parts department. Also, if you look at the response provided to CPSC it is always word for word the exact same "prepared" statement that offers no help.

It would be more helpful if the manufacturer could instead provide some practical solutions, even if they will not issue a recall. And suggesting to replace the knobs is only acceptable advice as long as the replacements do not suffer from the same inferior design flaws. Customers deserve a practical, lasting solution.
justification: Gas leakage from the range poses a significant safety risk, especially with prolonged exposure, though no injury or death was reported in this incident.

incident_description: Whirlpool range. Can lean on stove and knob will turn to allow gas on   Came home to a gas filled house because I had reached into cabinet above range before leaving for work. Seems this is a poor design. Now have put poker chips behind knobs so have to remove to push in and turn to use stove. Whirlpool is sending a repairman to see if in proper workhorses. Just poor design. Front handle does not protect from pushing in knobs and turning on gas if someone leans against stove. Had caught this happening several times while hanging in kitchen and smelled gas prior to worse incident of coming home to smelling gas in attached garage after on all morning.
justification: The incident describes a gas leak due to poor stove design, which could be dangerous but did not result in injury or death. The issue has occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I own 3 Cuisinart food processing machines.  One is subject to the recall and I had ordered the new blade through the established process.
The other 2 machines are not covered by the recall but also exhibit unsafe conditions with the blades. A 4 year old Cuisinart Mini Prep DCL 3 ACHC has a blade encased in plastic with no rivets.  The plastic is cracked, the metal blade is partially sticking out of alignment from the plastic and bits of plastic and metal are missing.
A 2 year old Cuisinart [REDACTED] has a blade encased in plastic with no rivets.  The plastic is cracked and a bit of plastic is missing.
The instructions for each machine do not state that the blades must be inspected before and after each use to be sure customers don't ingest bits of plastic and metal.  Meals are not often prepared in our home and the machines are used only 3 or 4 times a year, at holiday gatherings or family events like graduations.  We are careful to follow instructions on use and cleaning of all of our appliances.
I first tried to report this unsafe situation to the recall line at 877-339-2534.  They referred me to the company general customer service dept at 800-726-0190 and the representative was not at all concerned that there were unsafe products.  Her only interest was that I understood that I could buy a new blade, but because the machines are past the one year warranty and not covered by the recall there was not any other option.  I tried a second time to warn that customers need to know they can also be hurt by blades not covered by the recall, and there was no interest.  I asked for a supervisor and was told no supervisors were available.
I plan to discard all 3 machines as I am appalled by the lack of quality and the lack of concern in how the unsafe blades are being handled by Cuisinart.  I will retain them for a short while in the event you would like to examine the problem blades.
justification: The incident describes unsafe conditions with the blades but no actual injury has occurred, and the machines are used infrequently.

incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED] and I am a Kitchenaid consumer.  I built my executive level home in 2011 and completed our kitchen with all brand new Kitchenaid professional level appliances.  

The kitchen is 6 years old in July.  Three weeks ago we went on vacation and when we came home we noticed a "burnt" odor in the air and we also noticed that our under counter beverage center, model number KRUG24LWBS21, serial number EK12300443. had quit working.

We accessed the Kitchenaid repair site and scheduled a repair tech to come out and look at it.  He showed us the back and all the plastic parts inside had melted from an overheating situation.  This was a defective part not due to any maintenance issues with the unit.  I am attaching pictures of the melted parts and "ashlike" residue that was covering the inside of the rear of the unit.

To be clear.  This unit malfunctioned, and almost caught on fire.  This is obviously a design issue and I believe this unit should be recalled.  The drain pan and other parts should be made of metal and this unit should have a thermal protection that would shut off the power in this situation.  It cost me $400.00 to repair the unit.  I realize it is out of warranty and I am not looking for compensation for the repair.  I was told by the repair tech that it was all okay now and safe to use the unit.

Please note, if this unit were to malfunction again and we have any damages we will certainly pursue every avenue for compensation as you now are aware of this design issue.
justification: The appliance malfunctioned and nearly caught fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Maytag Dishwasher
Model: KUDE 40CVBL2
S/N    : F00601129
Purchased in 2010


WE HAVE NOTICED PIECES OF PLASTIC BREAKING OFF AND FALLING ON THE FLOOR UNDER THE FRONT DOOR OF THE UNIT.  I looked under the front door and noticed that a long piece of plastic that runs under the door has become brittle and is twisting and breaking off in small pieces due to high heat. 
There is also wiring that runs along the bottom of the door that goes into a junction plastic box.
The wiring is melting and there is black coloring on the junction box.  This looks like a fire waiting to happen and I will no longer use the dishwasher in this condition.  There are many other Maytag washers that have been recalled due to fire concerns.  I called Maytag customer service and they said it was not on their recall list and could not offer any remedy for repair or replacement.
justification: The incident involves plastic breaking off and melting wiring, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: I was cooking onions on a 10" skillet over medium heat, and all of the sudden there was an explosion that sparked and sounded like a gunshot ÃÂ incredibly loud and jarring, causing my husband and I to hustle out of the kitchen. When it seemed nothing else was exploding, we came closer and discovered a metal disc from the frying pan had exploded itself off where the handle connects to the pan. incident_description: On Easter Sunday I was boiling water in the 6 quart Paula Deen pot. As the water was heating up I started hearing a popping sound. When the water came to a full boil I removed the lid and placed it on a trivet on my counter. About 2 minutes passed and I heard a explosion. The glass on the lid had shattered into a million pieces. The most disturbing part was that the handle became a flying projectile with shards of glass on it. I only received a nick on my hand but it could have been a lot worse had my family arrived for dinner and there were more people, including children, in the kitchen.
