incident_description: Frigidaire range was reaching set temp of 350 and it started beeping, flashing error on digital screen and threw sparks out of the back of the oven.  Oven would not shut off.  Had to pull oven away from wall to unplug to turn oven off and stop beeping.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a malfunctioning oven, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We were using a metal pan with a glass lid on a gas stove on medium heat to cook green beans in water.  My 45-year old daughter picked up the glass lid by the plastic handle.  The glass instantly shattered.  Note:  Photos available.  Two other adults were "eye witnesses" to the event.

Note:  Daughter is a PhD Nutritionist, registered dietician, and author of a cookbook--lot's of cooking experience.
justification: The glass lid shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I have numerous Anchor and [REDACTED] glass storage bowls.  One in particular, an Anchor 1.75 quart bowl has been "disintegrating" around the rim.  It's as if the glass is flaking away.  It is meant to be dishwasher safe (as are all of these), yet only this one is chipping away.   God knows how much may have gotten into food.  I've reached out to Anchor twice now and they continue to ignore me.  I've saved the bowl but stopped using it.  It's COMPLETELY UNSAFE!
justification: The glass bowl is disintegrating, posing a potential hazard if glass fragments contaminate food, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I was cooking on the stovetop with high heat.  I then noticed a smell and heard a sound, and when I checked underneath the pot, the pot was stuck to the cooktop a bit.  When I got the pot to separate, I noticed the stovetop glass was melted and the whole cooktop had cracked.
justification: The incident caused damage to the cooktop but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The surface burner control valves only need to be depressed 1/8" to turn on the flow of natural gas.  Since the unit is the electric spark lighting variety, the knob has to be in a relatively small area to cause ignition.  When reaching into the matching microwave or the cabinet above, it is not difficult to depress the valve the 1/8".  Twisting to reach for something could and has turned the knob and cause the natural gas to flow.  To turn the knobs on a ccw turn is made, which if not turned too far turns on the Hi gas and ignition.  Turned too far or very little and nothing happens but the flow of gas.
      This has occurred four times with this unit.  After the 1st occurrence Sears was advised and made a couple of suggestions, but no service.  For my families safety I purchased a natural gas detector.  The next occurrence it worked fine, setting off a alarm when it detected the gas.  The next two times it did not, and with the slow build up of gas it wasn't noticed until strong levels reached the other rooms of the house.
     The knob activates the flow anywhere from 1/8 to almost 1/2 inch.  1/8 is defiantly too small.  In my opinion something like 3/8 inch would eliminate our problem and also make it more child safe.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage without injury, occurring multiple times with a likelihood of recurrence due to design flaw.

incident_description:
I own a Samsung - 5.8 Cu. Ft. Self-Cleaning Freestanding Gas Range - Stainless Steel
Model: NX58F5500SSSKU: 9171082 that I bought from Best Buy July of 2014.  I have used this range many times as well as the oven.  I used it two nights ago to bake for about 15 minutes and then I shut it off.  I did not do anything different than I have in the past.  The range has not been damaged nor hit by anyone.  My dog and I heard a loud noise as we were coming down the stairs this morning and it was the oven glass door exploding.  The glass shot out across to the dishwasher door which faces the oven.  That was enough force to make the glass fly about 4-5'.  The glass is supposed to be designed to break into small nuggets so that it does not cause serious harm, however, the glass broke into a combination of nuggets and shards.  My dog walked into the kitchen after me to see what was happening and stepped onto glass.  I also accidentally got tiny glass shards into my hands as I was trying to get him out.  This product is not safe.  Had anyone been in the kitchen, myself, my son, or my dog, we could have seriously been harmed.  We do not wear shoes in my home and we wear a lot of shorts in the Texas heat.  This glass could have cut us and cause lacerations serious enough to seek emergent care.  Luckily I was able to take care of my dog's paws and my hands without difficulty.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries to both the dog and the owner from glass shards, but no serious harm or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common with properly functioning ovens.

incident_description:
The appliance bulb has melted the top of my refrigerator in. It has a large whole with the melted plastic hanging with a brown ring around it. This Refrigerator Model JSI-26 / FRS6R4EWC 
made in Mexico.
The Serial Number is:4A70307285.
justification: The incident describes property damage (melted refrigerator) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I have a Cuisinart food processor that I was using to prepare guacamole.  A 1"+ piece of metal broke off the riveted blade in the guacamole.  Fortunately I found the piece before I served it.
This happened about a month before the Cuisinart blade recall.  I sent the information for the large blade (which had not broken) and mentioned that the smaller blade had broken. I finally received the replacement blade for the larger processor (3 months after the claim).  There was no replacement for the smaller blade.  I called customer service and was told the smaller blades were not recalled.
I can't imagine that the smaller blade defect would be less dangerous. Accidentally swallowing a 1" piece of metal could do some harm.  The fact that it is small makes it more dangerous
justification: A piece of metal broke off the blade but was found before serving, so no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible given the defect and recall context.

incident_description:
Black & Decker Toaster oven caught fire & nearly burned my kitchen cabinets. 
The control timer is DEFECTIVE!!!
When turned "OFF" it goes a tiny bit further to "STAY ON"!!!
This is INSANE !!! It's counter-intuitive.  
One automatically turns a control button all the way OFF and the "ding" means  it's off.  
BUT THIS STUPID PRODUCT HAS A TINY MARK THERE THAT MEANS "STAY ON" !!!!'
This may work in China but not here.   
It has happened to me TWICE.  

THEY THOUGHT they fixed it by adding the "ding" to alert user of the "stay on" feature, but
Just the opposite occurs!! In this culture the "ding" means "ok it's off"
Instead the house is on fire. 

MAKE THEM CHANGE IT!!!  Otherwise a sweet product
justification: The toaster oven caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using an Anchor Hocking blue rectangular baking dish size 8x11" to bake a pork tenderloin. I took it out of a 425 degree oven and set it on a granite countertop and seconds later it popped and shattered, spraying glass everywhere. No one was badly hurt.
justification: The baking dish shattered, spraying glass everywhere, but no one was badly hurt, indicating a minor injury risk.

incident_description: MY PYREX GLASS BAKING DISH EXPLODED IN THE OVEN.  I was baking stuffed merlitons (squash) in the oven at 350 degrees.  The medium sized rectangular dish was room temperature (it had NOT been in the refrigerator or freezer) when I placed it in the oven.  After 30 minutes of baking, I turned the oven off and left the dish in the oven (oven door was closed).  Approximately 5 minutes later I heard glass breakage, similar to dropping glass on a hard floor.  I looked inside of the oven and the baking dish had shattered leaving shards and small pieces of glass in the oven.  My Thermadour oven is less than 3 years old.
justification: The incident involved a glass baking dish shattering in the oven, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The corners of my Frigidaire electric oven range including the baking compartment door and the lower smaller compartment below are so extremely sharp around and underneath that they have gashed my leg skin-deep 2 times with serious and permanent scars to my legs to the extent that I can no longer wear my dresses without opaque pantyhoses. The third injury was not as bad as the other 2. One of the 2 bad ones happened on Thanksgiving. I have never seen any product so poorly and dangerously finished. If your feet ever get partially under the range while you are standing next to it, good luck if you are able to escape without injuries and scrapes from the sharp edges at the bottom. You need to send someone out to my house to see for yourselves because it is indescribable. I am a practicing attorney and I was treated by my husband who is a medical doctor. I am still very upset about the permanence of my injuries and the fact that I remain terrified on a daily basis to use or come near my oven range or let my children come near it. It's almost as you could not avoid getting gashed around or near it, however hard you tried. They happened when I had the door open while loading the baking area.
Incident Description:Please see above.
Product: Electric Oven Ranger
Product Description: Frigidaire Electric Range
Injury Info: Injury, First Aid  given to me by my husband who is a medical doctor.
justification: The description details multiple injuries, including serious and permanent scars, caused by sharp edges on the oven range, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I have a two and a half year old GE Monogram range, model ZDP486NDPSS.  Yesterday, my wife opened the smaller of the two ovens and noted that the top oven element had fallen, getting very close to the rack.   From my inspection, the root of the problem appears to be faulty tack welds between a metal plate forming the top of the oven cavity, and the metal bracket which supports the actual heating element.  Its electrical connections are unaffected. It seems to me that this failure, if it occurred during use of the oven, could easily result in physical contact between the element and food, potentially resulting in a large amount of smoke release and potentially a fire.  I have photos of the issue
justification: The heating element falling could lead to smoke or fire, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Kenmore electric range 790.92183011

Had used the oven to bake a dish to 400 degrees. The oven was off and not being used. Approximately 20 minutes after use, the front glass exploded all over the floor with nothing touching it. We have pictures if you need to verify.
justification: The incident involved property damage (glass explosion) but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as spontaneous glass explosions are not common.

incident_description:
I own 3 Cuisinart food processing machines.  One is subject to the recall and I had ordered the new blade through the established process.
The other 2 machines are not covered by the recall but also exhibit unsafe conditions with the blades. A 4 year old Cuisinart [REDACTED] has a blade encased in plastic with no rivets.  The plastic is cracked, the metal blade is partially sticking out of alignment from the plastic and bits of plastic and metal are missing.
A 2 year old Cuisinart Essential FP8 has a blade encased in plastic with no rivets.  The plastic is cracked and a bit of plastic is missing.
The instructions for each machine do not state that the blades must be inspected before and after each use to be sure customers don't ingest bits of plastic and metal.  Meals are not often prepared in our home and the machines are used only 3 or 4 times a year, at holiday gatherings or family events like graduations.  We are careful to follow instructions on use and cleaning of all of our appliances.
I first tried to report this unsafe situation to the recall line at 877-339-2534.  They referred me to the company general customer service dept at 800-726-0190 and the representative was not at all concerned that there were unsafe products.  Her only interest was that I understood that I could buy a new blade, but because the machines are past the one year warranty and not covered by the recall there was not any other option.  I tried a second time to warn that customers need to know they can also be hurt by blades not covered by the recall, and there was no interest.  I asked for a supervisor and was told no supervisors were available.
I plan to discard all 3 machines as I am appalled by the lack of quality and the lack of concern in how the unsafe blades are being handled by Cuisinart.  I will retain them for a short while in the event you would like to examine the problem blades.
justification: The incident describes unsafe conditions with the blades but no actual injury or death has occurred. The likelihood is possible given the machines are used 3-4 times a year.

incident_description: I turned the appliance dial as far to the left as possible to the OFF position and happened not to unplug it from the outlet like I normally do.  When I returned home, and neared the appliance, I noticed the plate was hot even though it was in the OFF position.  This is dangerous and consumers and the manufacturer need to know and fix this problem so it doesn't lead to a fire in someone's home.

Plastic shards (and possibly ground/crushed plastic) have been found in the bottom of glasses and even in the garbage disposal unit after ice remnants are dumped into the sink prior to the glass being placed in the dishwasher.

We have not determined any injury but the potential for injury exists from accidentally ingesting plastic pieces, chip and shards of plastic.

incident_description:
The door, temperature control knobs, stove top, and backsplash get extremely hot to touch when in operation. Technician indicated this is common for this oven and advised not to use the cook top and oven at the same time. To reduce the amount of heat being transmitted through the heat vent, the technician advised using a "fan" and the temperature on the stove top registered over 140"F! Concerned about the risk of burns not only for my elderly mother but for children as well as adults.

We bought this oven for my elderly mother in 9/2016 who was not able to use the oven for several months and when she started to use the oven, she felt she almost got burned by the knobs as well as the oven door, and the "backsplash". Contacted Lowes, as it was still under warranty, who sent out a technician and was advised as above and that the surrounding areas should not get above 130'F but that it was "normal".

Contacted Whirlpool on 4/19/2017 talked to a "[REDACTED]" and after explaining my concerns, she advised me that she could schedule another technician out to evaluate, but, I would be charged if everything is found normal.  Therefore, Whirlpool DOES NOT stand behind their product. No supervisor was available and she was advised that an attorney will be retained if any injury/death occurs due to this appliance and I would hold them accountable. This is an UNSAFE PRODUCT,  WFG320M0BW, DO NOT BUY. Better yet, don't buy any Whirlpool product!

So now, I will have to advise my mother to use "hot pads" whenever she's using the oven! Along with NOT using the stove top and oven at the same time, and to obtain a "fan" to disseminate the heat produced by the oven! Crazy!!!

I have contacted Cuisinart by email (with pictures) and by phone, but they said they wouldn't do anything about it because it is out of warranty. incident_description:

Do not know if they will now break off completely while using it.  I have stopped using the machine.  My larger concern is that I have given several of them as gifts.

incident_description:
(01/2017) the consumer stated that her husband was taking a casserole out of the oven. The casserole was on the middle rack which slanted and fell to the bottom of the oven.

incident_description:
!The new Samsung electric stove that we bought in September and installed with the new kitchen in November has
a design flaw- the knobs are too sensitive and turn if bumped into or leaned against. It happened on 3 occasions
and we were unaware that the burners were activated, so we had 3 fires already, 2 fires damaged the glass cooktop,
and third fire damaged the oven door, and also burned the pots and pans that I was storing in the oven. Samsung
sent a technician who suggested that I remove the knobs when the stove is not in use. I explained to him that this
stove is a fire hazard, that my husband who is 78 years old and cannot walk steadily can easily bump into the knob
again, but technician sent a report to Samsung stating that there is nothing wrong with the stove and that I simply
complain that the knobs are too sensitive. I checked the online forums and found that several people also complain
about this issue. Samsung refuses to acknowledge the flaw, stating that the fires were caused accidentally by me
and therefore the warranty does not apply. I begged them to listen to me, but they said that the only way for me to
receive a refund is for the technician to say that it is not repairable. The technician that came today said that he
cannot do anything about the knobs, that this is a design flaw, but as far as his position allows him the most that he
can do is to try and replace the cooktop and oven door if Samsung approves this repair.
I am afraid to live with fire hazard, and want this stove out of my house. I had an [REDACTED] stove for 10 years, the same
type as Samsung and never had any issues with it.
justification: The incident describes multiple fires caused by the stove's design flaw, resulting in property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I was using my crockpot approximately 3 hours and when I went to add some more items noticed the lid was completely shattered.  I tried to pick up the knob on top of the lid and it came off in my hand.  Glass had fallen into the contents so I just picked up the whole pot and threw it out.
justification: The incident involved a shattered crockpot lid and glass falling into the contents, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using the broiler of the top oven in my KitchenAid built in double wall oven. I was toasting English muffins on a cookie sheet. After removing the muffins and closing the door I  heard a strange crackling sound. I opened the oven to see what it was and a large shard of glass flew out of the oven followed by smaller splintered glass pieces. About one fourth of the door fell away leaving a large sharp piece of glass hanging crooked on the oven door. The piece of glass that shattered was the inside piece. I have had this door serviced because it would form condensation and leave water drips between the glass. It was serviced while under warranty, it is now less than 21/2 years old.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore 790 oven in the kitchen. On April 11, 2017, I went to remove a pizza from the oven. When I pulled on the handle, it fell off one side and the glass oven door shattered. Parts of glass shot so far as to get on our dining table and under the couch in the living room. I called Sears the next day to see about replacing the door and someone is coming Monday, but when I just looked to see if this has happened to others, I found it seems to be quite common and thought I should report it.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering and glass spreading, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(01/08/2017) The consumer stated that she had cooked bacon in the oven at 400 degrees. A half hour later, she heard a crash and a tinkling sound. She look at the oven door and saw that the glass in the outer door of the oven had shattered.  The oven door is buckled outward. 

(01/09/2017) The consumer contacted the firm. The consumer gave them the information about the incident. She was advised to contact Home Depot for repair service because she had an extended warranty.
justification: The oven door shattered but there was no injury reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that after her spouse used the microwave and closed the door it kept running, he opened the door and closed it several times to stop the operation.  However, there was a flame that shot from the top to the bottom of the unit like a blow torch, he immediately unplugged it to switch the power off.  He stated that this was the first incident but this was a replacement for his original microwave that had a similar problem.  He stated that the flames caused burnt marks to the unit.  They feel that this could have caused a house fire.

Caller stated that the manufacturer was not contacted as yet but they feel that this is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved flames and burnt marks, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We are renting the house we live in.  The Frigidaire Professional series built-in microwave PLMBZ209GCA turned on by itself and started electric fire.  We smelled the electric burning and discovered that the microwave was on (with nothing in it).  We opened the door and the fire was still burning for a while, coming from underneath the glass plate, melting the plastic rotation device.  
After the fire burned out, the electric panel is still on and appears working.  
Since we never use microwave, and never used this one in two years living in this house, we were shocked.  Until the incident we have never heard of appliance turning on by itself.
But after searching, found many similar reports.  
Luckily, we were at home to catch it on time and nobody was harmed.
justification: The microwave caught fire but no one was harmed, indicating a severity level of 2. Similar reports suggest this is a possible occurrence.

incident_description: We ran the dishwasher in SmartWash as always and the control panel caught on fire and smoke filled the kitchen.  We called Sears and they apparently didn't care.  Good thing I was home so our house didn't catch on fire.
justification: The dishwasher control panel caught fire, creating a hazardous situation, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer's wife put a drink in the microwave and set the timer for 50 seconds. The consumer states that the microwave continued to run after the 50 seconds and caused the drink to explode. The consumer believes it ran for an extra 3 minutes. The consumer states that the microwave continued to run even after he opened the door. The consumer states that the fan shuts off when the door is open but the motor continues to run.

The consumer indicated that this has been happening intermittently for the past 6 months. The consumer states that he emailed the firm approximately 6 months ago after the first incident occurred to inform them and the consumer has not heard back from the firm.

The consumer indicated that the serial number is worn off. 

The consumer believes the microwave is dangerous and should be recalled and replaced.
justification: The microwave malfunction caused an incident (exploding drink) but no injury was reported. The issue has been occurring intermittently for 6 months, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
My BLACK & DECKER toaster oven was found to have exploded in my kitchen while not in use with
glass and twisted metal all over the counter top.
justification: The toaster oven exploded, causing damage but no reported injury.

incident_description: Like several other consumers, my LG French door refrigerator is defective and the interior lights do not shut off when the doors are closed.  I purchased the appliance in 2007 and believe it has been a reoccurring problem for a while, as I found the plastic panel over the interior lights melted about a year or two ago.  I was puzzled, of course, and the melting could not be explained.  Finally, even though it took me a while, I discovered the problem with the interior lights this morning BEFORE it caught fire and BEFORE I left the house for work for the day.  Had I not discovered it, my house, along with my pets, might be gone by now.  Judging by LG's response to the issue, they really do not care about the danger so I believe it useless to contact the company, especially since my appliance is 9 years old.  I have removed the light bulbs and plan to disconnect the wiring in the hope that the danger will be resolved until I can buy a new refrigerator.  Needless to say, I do not plan to buy another LG appliance of any type.
justification: The incident involved a defective refrigerator with potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high (likely) given the recurring nature of the issue and the potential for fire if not discovered.

incident_description:
In December of 2016, I purchased from Bed Bath & Beyond a 4 piece carbon steel wok, made by Infuse. 
We have yet to use this product, however this morning the glass lid completely shattered, thank goodness it was in the box, as it would have hurt my dad. 

In doing research, it looks like self-shattering glass lids for woks are common now a days.
justification: The glass lid shattered but no one was injured as it was still in the box.

incident_description: This morning my Fagor Rapid Express pressure cooker malfunctioned and blew the gasket and went off like a bomb. I believe I would have been severely injured if I had been in the kitchen at the time. The contents of the faulty cooker consisted of only pinto beans and water. I have been using pressure cookers for more than 35 years and I truly believe that this brand should be recalled and taken off the market. Fortunately for me I will be cleaning pinto slime and crust off of every surface in my kitchen for weeks to come instead of doing rehab in a burn unit. I am feeling very grateful tonight.
justification: The pressure cooker malfunctioned but no injury occurred as the user was not in the kitchen at the time.

incident_description:
I was preparing lunch for my husband and me, and had two dinner plates simply sitting on my Formica kitchen counter ready for sandwiches.  The plates were not warmed in the microwave or in the oven and they were not taken from the freezer or the refrigerator, when suddenly there was an explosive noise one of the plates simply  broke apart. It shattered into thousands of little glass pieces, and spewed shards all over my kitchen and into my dining room like projectile missiles! It was very frightening! The dinnerware is not even a-year-old yet, and has no chips, cracks or breakage. 
 I'm afraid to use the dinnerware anymore.
justification: The plate shattered but no injury was reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: This is a Kenmore Elite electric smooth top range model 790.46713603 manufactured in 2006.  One of the burners will not turn off unless the circuit breaker for the power supply is turned off.  With only the breaker turned on, the burner goes to full power without the control being turned on thus creating a burn/fire hazard.
justification: The burner not turning off creates a burn/fire hazard, which is an incident but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Cooking [REDACTED] mac and cheese for 16 minutes per instructions.  Kitchen smelled like electrical burning.  Pulled microwave out about an inch thinking it needed more free air circulation and the sides were too hot to touch. My husband tried pulling it out by under side and burned his hand. Way too hot for outside casing. Fire hazard and burn hazard .
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the husband and identified a fire hazard, indicating a moderate severity and possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I had just begun to prepare dinner on 3/13/2017 and had preheated my oven to 375 degrees. It had just beeped alerting that preheat was complete. I opened the door, placed a cookie sheet with meat inside and closed the door. No more than 1 minute later, a loud explosion noise came from the kitchen. I ran to the kitchen to see what had happened - the inside glass panel of my oven had shattered all over the inside of the oven. When I opened the door, glass broke off and fell out all around the stove. I immediately turned off the oven and left the door cracked for cooling.

This is a WIRLPOOL STOVE MODEL NO: WFE510S0AS0 SERIAL NO: R40415073

I have read the online reports that talk about user error but I am 110% positive that is NOT the case here. It is just my husband and me, no kids at home and I am the ONLY one who uses that stove. I am very careful with my property and know that nothing could have been done to damage that glass in the slightest. My husband and our boys work at an automotive glass factory so I am WELL aware of the micro-flaws that are allowed to pass inspection.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered oven glass) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We have a Frigidaire gas range and oven, Model FPGS3085KFA. On the top of the range are four burner control knobs. The knobs are turned counterclockwise to turn the burner on. The first marked position is "Lite". When placed there, the gas is flowing and an ignition spark occurs, creating a flame on the burner. However, the gas starts flowing a bit before the "Lite" or ignition point is reached. On two occasions, in October of last year and March 2nd of this year, the knob was unknowingly turned slightly during cleaning and or removing a utensil from another burner, but this turning of the knob was not noticed. The knob did not reach the "Lite" or ignition point, but unlit gas started to flow. It was not audible unless you placed your ear down close to the burner. Gas from the appliance filled the kitchen and other parts of the house on both occasions. Fortunately, we were able to ventilate the house before an accidental ignition / explosion took place.
justification: Gas leakage occurred without ignition or injury, but the potential for a severe incident was present. The issue has happened twice in a short period, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
(12/17/2016) The consumer indicated that he set the dishwasher to a normal wash cycle before going to bed, as usual. Approximately 20 minutes later the consumer walked into the kitchen and noticed a burn odor. The consumer realized the burn odor was coming from the dishwasher and unplugged it. The consumer noticed that the power cord was warm to the touch and he noticed that the metal prongs were melted. The consumer indicated that there is water sitting inside the dishwasher. The consumer indicated that he cannot plug the dishwasher because the metal prongs are melted.

The consumer searched online and came across recall # 16-003. The consumer contacted the firm to inform them about the incident and his safety concerns. The consumer was advised that his dishwasher was not included in any recall and they offered to send a technician to inspect the dishwasher. The consumer did not make an appointment because the next available appointment they had was 10 days away. The consumer indicated that he plans to contact a local technician. 

The consumer believes the power cord overheated.

The consumer didn't notice any burn damages inside the dishwasher. 

The consumer indicated that the dishwasher is used every 2-3 days. 

No prior incident.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with a melted power cord, but no injuries or damages beyond the appliance itself.

incident_description:
The oven, which was installed 3 weeks ago, was cycling through it's high heat self clean cycle.  About 2 hours into the cycle, the inner glass of the oven window shattered and spilled onto the floor and the bottom of the oven.
KitchenAid model KOCE500ESS
justification: The oven glass shattered during a self-cleaning cycle, causing damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Bubba Brands Bubba. 18oz Thermal Mug Model HR-1.  Screw on cap has very soft silicone plastic o'ring seal.  When tightening the o'ring stretches and buckles out producing a 1/8" to 1/4" gap in the seal.  When the mug is tipped with a hop liquid the agitation causes and increase in the vapor pressure inside the mug.  The 160 degree hot coffee in my case was then spewed upward onto my nose and glasses.  Had I not been wearing glasses I would have sustained severe eye injury.  Subsequent operations of the cap showed that the malfunction was frequent and occurred at random positions around the cap making the leak unpredictable.

I started closing the service port and holding the cup on its side over the sink each time I filled it to determine if it had sealed.  As soon as I could I acquired a suitably sized butyl o'ring that seals every time without leaking.  

I contacted Bubba to tell them about the hazard and their response was "You have voided your lifetime warranty by installing unapproved parts."  Thank you, Bubba.  It's so nice to know you care.

Mug was purchased at a Walmart in [REDACTED].
justification: The incident resulted in hot coffee spewing onto the user's nose and glasses, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The malfunction was frequent and unpredictable, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
The submitter's daughter was baking cookies and had the oven on a bake setting with the temperature at 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Approximately 30 minutes later, the submitter's daughter heard a loud explosion and noticed that the oven's outer glass shattered. The submitter's daughter was not injured from the initial explosion but she stepped on a piece of glass and sustained a small cut on her right foot. The inner and middle glass is still intact. The submitter indicated that the glass shattered into pieces, with some pieces as large as half an inch and some where smaller shards.

The submitter contacted the firm the same day and informed them of the incident. They arranged for a technician to examine the range and waived the $100 service charge. 

There are no prior incidents.

The oven is used five times a week.

The submitter indicated that the range was already in the home when she moved in sometime in 2005.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut from stepping on glass, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Given the oven's frequent use (5 times a week) and the lack of prior incidents, the likelihood is rated as unlikely (2).

incident_description:
My GE Profile range cooktop has cracked twice! I bought it 6 months ago and the first crack resulted in small glass shards all over the countertop and floor. Today I was heating some tortillas and another hairline crack (about 1 inch) appeared over the burner, along with the smell of burning wires. If any liquid gets through the crack the glass cooktop can explode!

GE is sending another repairman to fix it next Tuesday (4-17-2017). 

I am afraid of using an oven cooktop that appears to be defective in manufacture with a risk of explosion.
justification: The incident involves a defective cooktop with potential for explosion, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The oven was on the bake setting, at 350 degrees, for approximately 1 hour, when the consumer noticed a hot odor.  The consumer was cooking a roast and had aluminum foil on top of the  pan.  He checked the oven and found that the broiler had turned on by itself and the aluminum foil and the top of the glass baking dish had begun to emit smoke. 

The consumer turned the oven off by using the control and removed the dish.  He left the door open for approximately 15 seconds.  The consumer then turned the oven back to the bake setting (350 degrees) and the broiler came back on immediately.  The consumer turned the oven off for approximately 60 seconds or more.  He then turned the oven back on to the bake setting (temperature down to 260 degrees) and the broil feature immediately came on.  The consumer turned the oven off.

He then turned the oven to broil (the high setting) and the oven came on.  He then turned the oven off completely and allowed it to stay off for 5 - 7 minutes.  He turned it back on to the bake setting (350 degrees).  None of the oven lights came on, but the consumer said that the heat in and from the oven was extensive, so, he believes that the temperature was higher than 350 degrees.  He continued to increase the oven's temperature and when he go to 475 degrees, the oven lights came on to indicate that the oven was on.  He then turned the oven down to 350 degrees and finished cooking his roast.  When his roast was finished, he turned the oven off.  During the final cooking time, he heard a constant clicking sound from the oven, but was not sure exactly what caused it.  There were no injuries.

The consumer and his wife checked the Internet and saw numerous complaints online referencing the exact same problem, with this manufacturerÃÂs range.  The consumer saw that some owners replaced the control panel to address the problem, but others had replaced the control panel 2 or 3 times and the problem continued.  He saw incidents for fires and property damage, which claimed to be related to this issue.

3/13/2017:  The consumer called his local retailer and their rep. apologized.  The rep. said that he could order a replacement control panel for the consumer, but the consumer is concerned that there may still be a safety issue with the unit.  He is not sure how he will proceed at this point.

3/13/2017:  The consumer called the firmÃÂs Customer Service Dept. and shared his concerns.  He asked if the oven was under recall.  The rep. checked, came back and told him no.  The rep. gave the consumer the number to the CPSC Hotline so that he could report this issue.

The consumer had never experienced any problems with this oven before.

The problem is similar to the ones described in CPSC Recall# 09-333, but his unit does not have a smoothtop surface.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and potential fire risk, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The knobs for stovetop are on front of unit. When a person works near stove and bumps a knob, the burner turns on maximum heat with no sound and no warning. Gets red hot, could easily catch clothes on fire or burn anything flammable that was resting on stove top. We have had stove two weeks, and this has happened 6 times already. Feel very threatened by this.

We did call LG and talked to person in Korea who said a service person would be sent to check.
justification: The incident describes a high risk of burns or fire, which could lead to injury, and it has already occurred 6 times in two weeks, indicating almost certain likelihood.

incident_description: Wall Oven Convection Combo  - Internal Glass Exploded in middle of night during a cleaning
justification: The internal glass exploded, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Trio Elite three-door refrigerator from a Sears store on 9/20/2007.  Recently, we opened the refrigerator to find the light housing in the refrigerator compartment had partially melted due to overheating from the light bulbs and/or electrical wiring under the light cover.  This presents a significant fire hazard and risk to property and persons due to the fire hazard.  At no time during a product's reasonably expected service life should plastic parts melt due to heating from light bulbs, especially in a chilled environment.
justification: The incident involves a significant fire hazard due to overheating, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I bought Samsung 30 in. 5.9 cu. ft. Electric Range with Self-Cleaning Convection Oven in Stainless Steel Model# NE59J3420SS on September 10, 2016. By Feb 17, 2017 my wife noticed that Samsung Oven Glass Main Top melted. So we reported this issue to Samsung at least twice and on the third attempt the customer representative told me that the melt is considered a physical damage which voids the oven warranty and so we are on our own.
justification: The incident involves a product malfunction (melted oven glass) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Cuisinart food processor does not turn on after 2nd use.  I think a piece of the blade got stuck in the motor, and I threw out the food just to be safe. Item recalled, purchased at Wayfair.com
justification: The food processor malfunctioned without causing injury, and the item was recalled, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: When we use the main oven of our Kenmore Elite Double Oven Range Model 790.9750 to cook anything heavy (dutch oven, roast, turkey) the rack collapses on one side and the food drops precipitously.  Initially I thought this was due to the rack being installed incorrectly but finally realized that the wall of the oven are bowed out so that the rack does not engage securely.  When the oven is cold you can shift the rack to one side so that it disengages on the other side.
justification: The incident involves the oven rack collapsing, which could lead to food dropping, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: While using my oven to cook potatoes, the area of below the oven floor where you can see flames through what look like vent holes caught fire.. After the oven fire was put out and cooled off, MY husband was able to lift up the over floor plate. HE said it looked like the heating element overheated and caught fire. MY husband said there was melted plastic wiring.We have never used anything,but glass and metal baking pans in our oven. The oven is less than 2 years old  and shouldn't have done this. OUr home could've burned down if we hadn't  been able to put out the fire. Something needs to be done. This oven is unsafe! Amana Stove and their other products should be recalled befor they kill someone.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, but potential for significant property damage.

incident_description: after shaking I set it down on the counter and the glass bottom shattered
justification: The glass bottom shattered, which could potentially cause injury from broken glass.

incident_description:
(01/2017) The consumer stated that his smaller food processor has the same issue as the recalled Cuisinart food processor. The blade is cracked at one of the rivets.

The consumer contacted the firm but was advised that there is nothing that they can do because the product was not recalled.

The consumer also stated that he saw another report with someone have the same problem with their Mini Plus.
justification: The incident involves a cracked blade in a food processor, which poses a potential hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: For a few weeks our dishwasher had been making a rumbling sound after it finished its wash and rinse cycles and moved into the drying cycle.  On March 14 after it went it to the dry cycle the unit began smoking - the motor or motherboard, we think, fried and possibly caught fire.  The unit was smoking so bad that smoke filled the kitchen.  I immediately turned off the unit and turned the breaker off that fed the dishwasher.  We have completely disconnected the dishwasher and will be purchasing a new one.
justification: The dishwasher smoked and filled the kitchen with smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Tools of the Trade (Macys) 8 qt. pot was being used to cook soup on stovetop.  Pot was simmering on low flame for about an hour.  I approached it and began to lift the handle on the lid.  At that moment, the handle separated from the glass cover causing the cover to shatter into hundreds of glass shards.  The crackled glass cover remained in tact and I was able to remove it from the pot before all the glass shards fell into the soup.  However, since a number of glass pieces fell into pot, soup had to be discarded.  I have pictures of the cover.
justification: The incident involved a pot handle breaking and glass shattering, but no injury occurred. The soup had to be discarded due to glass contamination.

incident_description: Cusinart DFP-14BCN (type 33).  I received the replacement blade.  But I still have a problem.  We put the Workbowl Cover (lid) on (using the slicing disk).  The lid closed tightly.  We used the plusher to feed celery into the top hole and that's when the problem occurred.  The plunger hit the slicing blade and the plunger was mangled. The bowl is slightly cracked at the base.  The lid is cracked.  If the slicing disc or the lid were not on properly, the machine should not have been operable.  I would like replacement parts for (1) Workbowl Cover, (2) Pusher and (3)  Bowl.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage (mangled plunger, cracked bowl and lid) but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Cut finger using the TEKNO copper knife for the first time after purchase. Bottom portion of blade at end of the handle protrudes too far out from the handle itself. The portion mentioned is not rounded off which simple visual inspection will prove.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The design flaw in the knife makes similar injuries likely if not addressed.

incident_description: While cooking or walking by the knobs turn on and the center display has come on or changed to turn on the oven several times... Got the same complaint from my adult daughters and husband when they were cooking on the stove as well... Oven turns on easily and is not child safe with a 5 yo in the home... The oven cleaning cycle has come on several times... The cooktop has come on several times...
justification: The oven and cooktop turning on unexpectedly poses a risk of burns or fire, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: We own the Kenmore elite refrigerator model #: 795.77553600. We purchased it new from sears in 2005/2006. One day I noticed a burning smell... it smelled like melting plastic or burning wires. It took me a day or two to place the smell. The refrigerator light was getting very hot and melting the roof of the refrigerator. I took out the light and melted piece in order to stop the burning. This happened about a year ago and I didn't think much of it until researching recalls on our refrigerator. I don't believe ours was involved in the recall I found, but was produced After this recall, with likely the same issue.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and melting plastic but no injury or death occurred. The issue was identified and addressed by the user.

incident_description: I opened my refrigerator, a Kenmore Elite mode #795.77572600 to find the light cover hanging down.  I thought it just came loose.  Upon further inspection, I realized it was melted and the lights were on.  I tried to activate the door switches, but the lights continued to stay on.  The heat was intense enough to melt a hole in the top of the refrigerator above the metal heat shield.  The light sockets were charred.  I know this issue has already been identified, but  I never received notice in the 2011/2012 time frame.  That is the time I bought the house where the refrigerator was.  I am attempting to resolve with the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light that caused melting and charring, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Cuisinart DLC-10, with a recently recalled and replaced blade, new blade is now missing serration 'teeth' after making hummus 3 times. I have before and after pictures if needed. Basically, the recalled, replaced blade is doing the same thing as before, dropping sharp metal into my food.
justification: The incident involves a defective blade dropping sharp metal into food, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Ongoing issue with a Whirlpool gas range model #WFG371LVS, S/N R13423335

The burner Controls are placed on the front of the range and can be slightly turned on by brushing up against them. This opens the gas valve but does not light the burner. The result is gas leaking into the room until finally detected by someone who wonders what the odor is. We complained to Whirlpool about this unsafe condition and were told to buy a parts kit from them or go to [REDACTED] for a child proof fix.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage which poses a significant safety hazard, though no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
(electric range oven fire)
Large amount of flame (roughly 6-10 inches in height) coming out of the back of the oven  .  Immediately shut oven off and called customer service.  Purchase date spring 2012, incident February 26th  2017.  After doing a bit of research, we have come across numerous Consumers reporting identical situations with this exact Samsung product.  Due to the severity of the potential harm this may cause,  along with the large volume  of other consumers with the exact same problem, we have been told to report this product as potentially hazardous to a third party...

Samsung FTQ353IWUX 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Range - Convection
Samsung model number: FTQ353IWUX
Samsung serial number: 189JDDB400283N

My wife heard a buzzing noise, followed by a loud pop after simply turning the stove on to cook a pizza for our small children....
justification: The incident involved a significant flame from the oven but no injury was reported, and similar incidents have been reported by numerous consumers.

incident_description: We have a GE Profile Dishwasher that caught on fire.  It caused smoke and water damage.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire causing damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Jenn-Air cooktop JGD3536BB00  serial # D61813152 

Newly purchased cooktop was professional installed in approximately October 2016.  Insd son was preparing to cook and when he ignited the cooktop it exploded causing damage to a light fixture and the cooktop itself.

Unk cause, insd suspects possibly a gas knob was "bumped" and allowed it to leak gas into burner area.
justification: The incident caused damage to property but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I was in my kitchen when I heard a sound coming form the drip coffee maker. It was the sound of the coffee in the holding pot boiling. Then I smelled wires burning. I ran over to unplug the machine. It had shorted out. 

Upon examination, a hose that runs from the water tank to the heating element split right at a clamp point. This allowed water to flow into the electronics compartment. 

I have no doubt this would have caused a fire had I not been present.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I put in a claim in December 2016 regarding the cracking of the blade on our cuisinart food processor, to cuisinart, after learning about the recall on television. 
I have called several times regarding when we will receive the replacement blade. I was told this morning it will be in July now!! I find this unsatisfactory, and when I voiced my concern to cuisinart, I was offered a cook book for compensation!!!! We have not been able to use our food processor for 3 months now, and this has been a huge inconvience to us. We have decided to purchase a new processor, but NOT a cuisinart, since they are not willing to make a decent compensation for us.
We find this to be extremely inconvient for us in our daily household cooking preparations, in which we had no fault in this situation, 
We hope you can do something about this unfair situation by the cuisinart company.
Thank you.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a product defect and poor customer service, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Oven Broiler turned on by itself and would not turn off. Had to disconnect gas from appliance.
justification: The oven broiler malfunctioned but was resolved without injury by disconnecting the gas, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: The microwave self-starts and adds cooking time without buttons being pushed. It is a fire hazard and I am very concerned about the safety of it since self-starting microwaves are known to cause fires in homes.  This has happened on more than one occasion.
justification: The microwave self-starting poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred yet, and it has happened multiple times.

incident_description:
The consumer woke up from his dog barking and when he opened his bedroom door he noticed smoke. The consumer walked in the kitchen and noticed flames. The consumer states that one of the burners were on and a cutting board with a slice of pizza was on top of it. The consumer then put out the fire.

The consumer believes that his dog was trying to get the slice of pizza and turned the control knob, subsequently turning on the fire. The consumer believes the design of the control knob is not safe and the firm should fix this defect.

The consumer believes the control knobs should be pressed down then turned for the fire to start and his knobs turn on with a slight movement. 

There are no prior incidents.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death, and the likelihood is possible given the described scenario with the control knobs.

incident_description:
The consumer used the unit to brew approximately 4 cups of coffee and shortly after the coffee finished brewing the consumer heard a popping noise. When the consumer turned around she noticed thick smoke emitting from the base of the unit. The consumer immediately removed the coffee pot and unplugged the unit then put it outside. The consumer did not notice external damage but she believes there may be internal burn damages.

The consumer indicated that she read multiple reports online for similar incidents with his model. The consumer believes the unit presents a fire hazard and should be recalled. 

There are no prior incident.

The consumer indicated that she uses the unit five times a week and brews four cups of coffee.

The consumer has called the firm but she has not been able to speak with anyone because the lines are busy.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission but no injury or external damage, and similar incidents have been reported online, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that his dishwasher while in use for approximately 20 mins, he heard a noise which sounded like an electrical arcing.  He noticed that black smoke was dispersing from the door , he opened the door and the unit had cancel the operation because the control panel had melted.  This incident tripped the circuit breaker as well. He disconnected the unit and remove it from under the counter top.

Consumer stated that he purchased another dishwasher and the defective unit was hauled away.  He is concern that this product is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the defect was isolated to one unit.

incident_description:
Attorney Gen & FTC referred this caller to CPSC after his 3 year old son woke him up after a bad dream and while attending to his child he realized that his one story house was filled with smoke.

The caller began walking the house to find what could be on fire then realized that his refrigerator had flames coming out of the bottom of it.  He disconnected the refrigerator which extinguished the flames then opened the windows and doors to rid his home of smoke. 

He remained up for hours then returned to bed and when he awoke later he plugged the refrigerator back in but it immediately began throwing flames from the wiring in the bottom as well as shooting sparks from the same location.

The caller is reporting this product as a fire and burn hazard.

There are no injuries 

The caller has contacted the manufacturer and he was referred to CPSC.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries, and the recurrence of flames upon reconnection suggests a possible but not certain likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Microwave that is less than 3 years old.  For the past 2 weeks, it has been coming on by itself.  There is no time left on the screen, and no one is near the microwave.  Last night, I was in bed reading a book and heard it go on.  My husband was watching tv in another room and had no idea it had come on by itself.  We have been unplugging it when not in use, but I'm afraid we will forget to do this all of the time. 

When it comes on by itself, it will not let me turn it off by punching the display, I have to unplug it.

I called the 1800 842 1289 customer serv number and they will not assist because I'm out of the 1 year warranty.  Sears, where I purchased the microwave will not help either because I'm out of warranty and did not purchase an extended warranty.

As a consumer, I expect a microwave to last longer than this one has and I expect it to be safe and not to come on by itself.  We have pets in the household, as well as we are concerned about our home.  We will be taking this one to elec. trash waste hauler so that no one is endangered.
justification: The microwave turns on by itself, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The consumer used the front left burner for a few minutes and when she turned the control knob to the "Off" position the element failed to shut off. She tried turning it on and off multiple times but the element remained red and very hot. The consumer's husband arrived 10 minutes later and he pulled out the range and unplugged it.

(02/15/2017) The consumer contacted the firm to advise them of the incident and they informed her the range is not recalled. She said they were unwillingly to provide repairs or assistance free of charge.

The consumer believes the range should be recalled for a fire hazard.
justification: The burner failed to shut off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he turned his oven on for about an hour at 350F. Approximately fifteen minutes after the oven was turned off, its outer glass exploded.

The consumer indicates that the cooktop is used approximately once or twice daily, whereas the oven is used two to three times weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The oven's outer glass exploded, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a LG range in January , 2009, Serial 810KMUZ 10758 Model # LRG303575T. A major safety flaw has not been corrected with the knobs that control the gas flame. The original knobs that were supplied with the range contain a plastic that becomes brittle and cracks off after three months of usage. If the knob is slightly nudged in passing, the gas will turn on unknowingly and could potentially cause a house explosion. The position of the knobs is also poorly located. At waist level, it is easy to bump when walking past the range. I called LG at 1 (800) 243-0000on Tuesday, February 21st at 3.50PM and spoke with [REDACTED] and [REDACTED]. Both LG representatives refused to address the safety issue and refused to send replacement knobs. 
Please order LG to send me safely designed replacement knobs at their cost.
justification: The incident describes a safety flaw that could lead to a gas leak and potential explosion, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
(01/12/2017) The consumer stated that the range was in the self-cleaning mode which takes about 3 hours. Near the end of the three hours, the consumer heard a noise. He had to wait for the range to cool down before he could open the oven door. When he opened the oven door, he discovered  that the glass of the inner door had shattered.

(01/12/2017) The consumer contacted the firm in reference to the incident. He was advised that there was no a recall on the product.

incident_description:

No injuries.

incident_description: While using the fryer the units control head separated from the heating element
justification: The control head separating from the heating element is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Used my oven to warm up some bread, turned it off, but the oven stayed hot even though the displayed showed it was off.  Then the oven continued to heat up to the highest temperature, around 500 degrees and would not turn off.  I turned it back on and then back off, but it still stayed at hottest temperature.  I had to go the basement to turn off the circuit breaker, because the oven was too hot to move to pull the plug.
If I had gone out of the house after using the oven, I assume my house would have burned down by the time I got home.  There should be an overheating switch that automatically shuts off the power.
Doing a quick search on the Internet, there are several reports of the same model not turning off, so clearly there is a problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred. Internet reports indicate this is a known issue with the model.

incident_description: I opened the refrigerator this a.m. and noticed that it was hot inside. Then I noticed the light hanging down, and you could smell a burning motor smell. I noticed that everything was hot in the refrigerator. The light was on and would not go off, it melted the light fixture. It got so hot I had to throw everything out. I looked on line and noticed that several people have had this same issue. It is a Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator causing heat and damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: After eating dinner I was wiping the top of my electric range when the front oven glass door shattered on my feet.  I never used the oven it was not even on.  This scared me and never experienced anything like this before in my life.   We remodeled our kitchen 4 yrs ago and installed sears 790 convection electric glass top range.  This was an expensive range and can't believe this happened.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass door shattering, which scared the individual but did not result in any injury.

incident_description: On the morning of 2/27/2017, I was cooking bacon inside my Samsung oven range for,about 10-15 minutes. Once the bacon was cooked, I had shut off the unit, but within 10 minutes I started smelling a wierd smell and then noticed smoke,coming from the top of the unit. The insulation under the glasstop of the samsung oven range somehow caught fire and caused smoke throughout our home that led us to feel dizzy and nauseated. We reported the product safety issue to Samsung support and they sent out a technician on 3/1/2017. Samsung escalation ticket # is [REDACTED]. Upon inspection by the onsite technician, he could see that the fire started under the glasstop in the insulation; however, a samsung tech support person he called in over the phone later overrode his diagnosis and indicated it was a due to a cosmetic issue inside the over range and that they would not repair or replace. The diagnosis from the tech over the phone (I remind you: done remotely over the phone) was incorrect and conflicted with what the onsite technician saw. This was a product safety iasue that caused mental and emotional distress to me and my wife, not to mention we inhaled smoke and had to call the local fire department. Samsung has improperly diagnosed the issue and has denied responsibility.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke inhalation causing dizziness and nausea, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My wife was using our  Cuisinart Smart Stick blender with its whisk attachment. Suddenly one of the wires detached at one end resulting in a 18 inch long whipping wire. It did slash through a nearby plant before she got it under control. Could be dangerous. Didn't know how often this has occurred but wanted it on record. 

I have pictures if that would be helpful
justification: The incident involved a detached wire causing potential danger, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I own a Frigidaire Range/Oven Model fef368gch.  I was simmering a pot roast on the front right burner  and left the kitchen to do other work while it simmered for several hours.  Upon returning to the kitchen, the entire house was filled with smoke as the burner never switched down to simmer and remained on high, burning off all the liquids.  After cleaning up the incident, I returned the same pot to the same burner and put it on simmer to watch.  It did the same thing.  This is a definite fire hazard.  Other Frigidaire models are recalled for the same thing.  I believe this model should be also.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard due to a malfunctioning burner, which filled the house with smoke but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: My ice maker in my Frigidaire freezer stopped working and seemed to be jammed with ice - I reached in to remove some ice and slide out the ice bin and burned my right hand badly when it touched the metal part where the ice falls.    It blistered and now a month later the last of the scabs are healing and I have a 3" scar down my hand.    I had to be out of town for work but now that I am back I called Frigidaire customer service # on the inside of the unit and the customer service put me on hold and came back said she did see other complaints about this same thing on my model.   I left her all my info and she said thank you for reporting.  I asked if they would send someone out to fix it since it seemed very dangerous and I had not turned it back on since the burn and she said at my cost I could do that but she had looked on CPSC and they were not doing a recall so not their issue.   I was surprised they wouldn't want to help  handle it since they have other reports of the same thing and nothing should be that hot in a freezer.    I figure my only other resort is to file a report here so that other consumers might be warned it is an issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury with lasting effects (scarring), and there are other reported complaints of the same issue, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description: January 22nd 2015, I was preparing beef stew in a Farberware  7-N-1 Pressure Cooker that I purchased from Walmart, manufactured by Midea. I heard the pressure cooker beep, notifying me that the cooking cycle had ended. I then ensured the pressure release valve was positioned according to the included directions to release the all the steam from the beef stew that had been cooking. The reason I purchased this pressure cooker over the various others was the lid lock safety feature, in which the lid automatically unlocks only after all the extremely hot steam and intense pressure has been removed from cooker through an exhaust valve. Once this was complete, I went to remove the unlocked lid and the scalding hot content exploded onto my body severely burning my chest, stomach, hand, and tip of nose. I felt a searing pain to the skin on my nose, left thigh, chest, stomach, and left hand and I instinctively and immediately removed my clothing containing the scalding hot contents only to find the skin on my body had been violently burned away. This is a dangerous and defective product that is not safe. It caused me 2nd and third degree burns on my body and I am now left with ugly scars for life!
justification: The incident resulted in severe second and third-degree burns, which are serious injuries.

incident_description: I was baking potatoes.  There was a loud and bang!  When I looked the window glass had completely shattered

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her gas range purchased from New York from retailer in 2009. 
Incident three times in 7 years.
Caller has been corresponding back & forth about her plastic knobs crack and come apart.
The manufacturer has replaced the knobs but they replaced them with other plastic knobs which also cracked and broke.
They now have steel shaft knobs that don't come off, they don't become brittle and crack.
She has asked for the steel knobs but she has been advised that they replaced the original plastic knobs and will only sell her the steel shaft knobs.
She is reporting this as a severe burn, injury hazard due to the plastic knobs being affected so negatively by the heat and once they break off the only thing left is the metal.
She is asking for CPSC assistance to report this unit as a safety hazard and to obtain the knobs with the metal/steel shaft which is not affected so quickly by the heat.

I am appalled at the lack of response and concern Cuisinart representatives showed me. 

Model CBT 500 (TX)
Serial: 80917 j  S

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore 27" Self-Clean Double Electric Wall Oven (Model #790.48673.900), purchased Apr-2014. Yesterday, while heating up the oven, the glass in the upper oven door shattered. Fortunately, the glass layer was a middle layer, so I did not have glass all over the oven or the kitchen. As this was a middle glass layer, there was no wear and tear, no scratches, no damage of any kind to the glass layer. It was tempered glass, it did shatter into small pieces.

Calls to Sears customer service were unsuccessful; they refused to come do an inspection to confirm a manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
This is about my Frigidaire Electric Range Model# LGEF3043KFN, Serial# VF43109707. which we bought from Lowes on 10/1/2014.  After I used the self-cleaning for the first time, the outside glass exploded on February 18th. 

Since I have never used this feature, I pulled out my manual and followed the instructions.I had pulled out all the racks, wiped up the bottom as instructed. When I set the cleaning time, I changed the cleaning from 3 hours to 2 hours because I felt that the range wasn't that dirty.  The door locked and it started cleaning.  After about 2 hours, the oven beeped, like the manual said it would.  All the lights were off, showing the cleaning had stopped.  Knowing it would still be too hot to do anything with, I left the kitchen and while sitting in the leaving room, about 15-30 minutes later, I heard a big explosion from the kitchen,  I went in and there was glass everywhere with a big hole in the middle of the oven door.  The inside door glass was still whole, it was just the outside glass that was broken.  I was just thankful that I wasn't in the kitchen at the time, or I would of been hit with this glass.  We bought this range from Lowes and luckily we bought the extended warranty (5 years).  It took them almost 1 month to respond.   The guy told us this is happening to a lot of ovens after the self-cleaning. He had no idea as to why. We are now in wait time to see if he can get the whole door. If not he will be replacing the glass.  This worries me greatly.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the oven door glass, but no injury occurred. The technician indicated this is a common issue with this model after self-cleaning.

We had to cut the power to the range at the circuit breaker to have it turn off.  The burner was not used after that.  Sometime after 11:30 pm on Sunday, March 26 and prior to 2:30 am on March 27, the burner turned itself on again and would not shut off.  We had turned the circuit breaker back on so that we could cook in the interim of the events.  Fortunately, my husband, who had fallen asleep while reading awoke and found the burner turned on and again shut the circuit breaker to the stove.

Caller stated that the product was tested at their lab ([REDACTED]) and they discovered that the units explodes less than 10 mins.

Caller stated that they have photographs of these incidents and test videos. He stated that the company settled the case but has not issued a recall on the product.

incident_description:
I purchased the Progressive Prep Solutions Multi Slicer today.  I removed the packaging and noted the removable label on the blade stating to be careful of the sharp blade.
After washing the items, I put my vegetables in the slicer and was very pleased with the performance and quickness of the slicing.  I then sauteed the vegetables not seeing anything wrong.  About halfway through my meal I started to choke when I felt something sharp in my throat.  I was able to cough it up and remove it and found it was a "needle like" sliver of white plastic.  I went back to the saute pan and found four more of them.  As far as I know I did not ingest any other pieces but after looking them over I could see they were shaved off the food glide that holds the vegetable when you are slicing the item and apparently there is no stop to not allow you to start slicing the plastic against the blade..I never even knew it happened until I felt it in my throat.  this product sliced great but needs to be modified to not allow the glide to unknowingly contact the blade.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (choking on plastic shards), but no death occurred. The likelihood is possible as it happened once during use.

incident_description: Pressure cooker malfunction resulting in injury.  At approximately 5:50pm, I was cooking dinner in the Power Cooker Plus (Tristar) pressure cooker.  I have used it many times and I am very familiar with pressure cooker usage.  When the meal was done, I manually released the pressure using the valve.  Believing the pressure to be fully released, I attempted to turn the lid.  The lid is advertised as a safety lid that should not turn if there is any pressure.  However, the lid did turn and, as it did, the scalding hot contents of the pot erupted and shot out of the pressure cooker.  I saw another consumer say this effect was similar to a volcanic eruption.  That is the best description I can find.   Food was everywhere and I was hit in the stomach with scalding hot fluid.  I was burned with blistering 2nd degree burns across my abdomen even through 2 layers of clothing. My burns are significant, as are the accompanying blisters, with incredible pain.   At the very least, the safety lid malfunctioned.  It turned and open easily, despite the fact that the contents were obviously under pressure.  This is an unreasonably dangerous product.  (Note: I have pictures of the unit and the injuries, but I am having trouble with the photo uploader on this site).  Date of purchase provided is an estimate.  I bought it in the past year.
justification: The incident resulted in significant second-degree burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The malfunction appears to be a rare occurrence given the user's familiarity with the product and its advertised safety features (likelihood 2).

justification: The glass dish exploded, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
On March 18, 2017, we prepared three chicken breasts for cooking.  We pre-heated the oven to 350ÃÂ°, lined a 9x13 Pyrex Easy Grab glass baking dish with aluminum foil, placed the chicken breasts in the dish, covered the dish with aluminum foil and placed the dish in the pre-heated oven.  

Approximately one hour went by and we heard a loud noise coming from the oven.  We opened the oven and found that the Pyrex glass dish had exploded in our oven.  The glass dish had shattered and was in tiny pieces all over the oven. (We have saved the glass shards for research purposes, if necessary.)  

The dish was approximately one year old.  The oven temperature was double checked with an oven thermometer to ensure we had not made any errors. The temperature was accurate.  

We went on-line and read that numerous people have had this happen, but there appears to be no recourse or recalls on this defective product.  People have been injured because the dish has exploded in their hands when removing the dish from the oven.  Another lady had her oven door practically blown off.  A dish exploded after being removed from the oven and sitting on the counter to cool, sending flying glass shards all over the room.  These are just three examples out of thousands.

According to the on-line article "Exploding Pyrex", approximately 19 years ago (1998), the Corning Company not only sold the formula for making the glass, but also the Pyrex name. The new company "World Kitchen", has altered the formula of the glass components that go into the glass to make the Pyrex products.  Pyrex made prior to 1998 was made from a material called Borosilicate glass - it was indestructible.  The Chinese altered the formula and switched from using borosilicate glass to tempered soda lime glass, which is an inferior glass compared to borosilicate glass.  The company is apparently not an American company and has avoided any repercussions due to a "fine print" disclaimer. 

If you buy a Pyrex dish, the label on the front says oven safe, freezer safe, microwave safe.  The Pyrex reputation was established years ago -- when you purchased a Pyrex product, there was a sense of trust -- not so any more.  Americans are still purchasing the Pyrex dishes based on the past reputation that no longer exists.

There apparently have been numerous complaints to the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) but nothing has been done to appropriately warn the American Consumer.  This is where we are hopeful that CPSC will take appropriate action and expose this dangerous product and remove this product from being sold in America.

We consider this to be a serious issue and only desire the safety of others.  

Thanking you in advance for your assistance.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish causing property damage but no injuries, and online reports suggest this is a common issue.

incident_description: We have a cuisinart coffee maker (DCC - 750 series; 120V AC 60 HZ 1025 W serial # 31209A)  bought from Boscovs about 3 years ago. Today I heard a popping sound. The coffee pot was not on at the time. All of the sudden, I smelled a strong acrid stench and smoke was pouring out of the back. The smoke seemed to be coming from underneath and filled the house. We immediately uplugged the machine and rushed it outside. If I hadn't noticed this I am afraid my house could have burned down. We looked to consumer report to see if others had run into this problem. It seems that hundreds of people have had this same issue and yet Cuisinart is still selling this coffee maker. It also seems as if you CPSC has been contacted repeatedly. I don't understand how nothing has been done. Please contact me at ASAP to tell me what can be done ([REDACTED]).
