incident_description:
On February 08, 2017 at approx. 07:42pm Fire Department was called out to my house.  Oven was "On" I was preparing Dinner.  My house was engulfed in fumes from the Fire that started within the Interior of the Oven walls.  Inside the Oven no fire was visible.  Fire Depatment gutted out the inside of the Oven; Racks, etc.
Oven overheated and burned downward through the cabinet.  

Per Fire Report "Faulty Oven" Possible issue with the Thermostat inside the Oven.  

On February 09, 2017, I notified GE Electric of the Fire at 1-800-626-2224 due to I have a Service Contract with them.  I spent approx. 45 mins explaining what happen.  I was given a other number to call.  GE Relations and told me my Wall Oven Unit is on the "Recall" list and not to worry ALL is covered; Property Damages and Personal Damages.  GE Relations referred me to Electric Insurance at 1-888-456-7445.  Electric Insurance sent out an Inspector [REDACTED] on February 11, 2017,  As I greeted Mr. [REDACTED]  at the door he informed me he was here to inspect an Mircowave?? I informed him it was a Wall Oven Unit.  Mr. [REDACTED]  inspected, took pictures and video stated "It wouldn't have matter what temperature the Oven was "On" this is a Defected Oven.  On February 13, 2017, Electric Insurance also sent out a Service Tech to inspect.  As I greeted the Service Tech at the door he informed me he was here to inspect Microwave, I informed no it's a Wall Oven Unit.  As the Service Tech from MasterTex inspected and took pictures he also stated "interior fire inside Oven walls, defected Oven". On 02/16/2017, GE Service Tech came out as I greeted him at the door he stated he was here to repair a Mircowave I made him aware it was a Fire in my Wall Oven Unit.  He contact the main office and they had NO record of my report of the Fire within the walls of the Wall Oven Unit.  Service Tech inspected and notified the office it would be approx '$800.00 to repair and also advised if taken that route to repair instead of replacing th Oven with a New he would NOT make the repairs.
I called Assurance my service contract with GE and notified them of the findings.  They had NO reports of Fire within my Oven only a fire in my Microwave???? On 02/28/2017 no one has contacted me and the Oven is still pulled out of my walls along with the Mircowave.  I emailed GE corporate office and got a called from [REDACTED] at [REDACTED] he stated he was sorry for all I had went thru and assured me all would be taken care of ASAP and due to my Mircowave sitting on top of my Wall Oven Unit with the Fire and Smoke GE were going to replace BOTH my Microwave & Wall Oven Unit FREE of charge. He also assured me he would personally over see my case.  I asked him "what are you sure?" And he assured me "yes" both Wall Oven Unit & Mircowave would be replaced with a new one.  On 03-11-2017 I received and email from Mr.[REDACTED] advising me he made a mistake and he was confused upon calling me.  He stated NO NEW Mircowave would be replace.   As of present no one from GE, GE Relations or Electric Insurance has contacted me.  I made ALL aware my Wall oven Unit is safety hazard due to its on the floor pulled out by the Fire Department and the wired are still connected to the Wall due to the Wall Oven Unit doesn't have a plug it's just electrical wires.  I have been living miserably ever since this happen.  At time of incident I was over whelmed with Smoke inhalation. II wasn't able to stay at my house for days due to the Smoke fumes.  I stayed at my Mom house.  My house was consumed by Smoke and tinted by the dust of the smoke. My white ceiling fans are tinted by the smoke, my drapes are dingy.  My closet and clothes reep of smoke and the A/C ducts.  GE is now telling me my Oven is NOT on the Recall List.  In assistance in this matter would be greatly appreciate.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing smoke inhalation and property damage, indicating injury and significant disruption.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE Profile Dishwasher in 2006 Model# PDW8880L00SS - Serial # AL738998B and 3x now the heating element/panel has malfuctioned causing dishes and other items to melt or catch fire in the dishwasher.  When the dishwasher is done running its cycle the heating element continues to heat and won't shut off without having to shut off the breaker.

I had purchased an extended warranty when I first purchased the unit and the warranty company sent out someone to replace the panel and the heating element inside the dishwasher within the first 5 years and now again the same issue is happening (03/26/17).  So that means twice now the panel/heating element have malfunctioned and needs to be replaced again (a 3rd time).  I started the dishwasher before I went to bed on 03/25/2017) and then I heard the smoke alarm going off at 2 am (03/26/2017) and I ran to put out the sizzling meltdown and the overheated dishware which could only be handled with a pot holder and then had to shut down the breaker since the dishwasher was blowing very very hot air even though it was not on and it was shut off.  

I have never heard of a panel/heating element going bad 3 times in 11 years.  Each time it's happened thankfully I was at home but I lost dishware that either cracked from the heat or melted plus all the very toxic fumes coming from inside the dishwasher.  The dishwasher was smoking so bad and with all the toxic fumes enough to set off the smoke alarms.

I need either GE to replace the faulty panel/heating element and/or replace the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating element causing dishes to melt and emit toxic fumes, posing a risk of fire and injury.

incident_description:

I put two Taquitas on a paper plate in the microwave and set it for 1 minute.  Within 30 seconds flames came shooting from the top interior of the microwave, caught the paper plate and all on fire.  Fortunately I had a towel in my hand which I immediately put in water and doused the fire in the microwave. But it took several minutes to put out the fire. 
If I was not standing right by the microwave oven at the moment the fire started, the whole kitchen and house could have caught on fire -

incident_description:
On January 23rd 2017...My daughter baked enchiladas in the glass pan.  Ate them and an hour later went to pick up the cooled pan from the counter to put away leftovers and the pan shattered in her left hand.  It cut her middle finger causing 5 stitches and not only cut her ring finger, but severed a tendon in that finger.  She had stitches and was quickly put on the schedule the next day to have surgery to fix the tendon or else her finger would never be straight.  
She was with 3 other roommates at college when this happened and they never saved the pieces from the pan.  I think they were so shook up with all the blood and my daughter crying they just got her to the hospital and cleaned up later, not thinking (which I'm not even sure at 53 years old I would think to save the pieces).
We filed a claim w/Oxo with injury pictures, dates, receipt pictures and pictures of the box in which pan was in.  They took about 2 months, then last week denied the claim, saying since we didn't have the broken pieces, they had to deny.  I don't want to get an attorney involved, but I'm scared for anyone else that uses these pans.  The pan was clearly cooled off or my daughter wouldn't have picked it up.  We also told Oxo we have a $2,500 deductible and they said the most they could do was $38 to replace the pans.  
As it turns out our insurance company (Keystone Blue Cross/Blue Shield) has denied all of our claims (now up to $12,000) saying she was out of network and we just retained an attorney to file an appeal to the insurance company.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring stitches and surgery, but no death occurred.

This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

incident_description:
12/17/16

To Whom It May Concern,

Defective electric range complaint by:

On December of 2008 I purchased a Kenmore Elite electric range.  Model # 79096643700 from the Sears store in Prescott.  Approximately 2 years ago the fire alarms in my house went off as I was baking.  Flames and smoke were coming from the back of the top part of the range.  An F10 error appeared on the screen. Someone else may not be so lucky, they may be burnt or their house may catch on fire.

I contacted Sears customer service to register a complaint and asked them to get back to me.  I haven't heard a word from them.  I certainly hope for the sake of others that you look into this matter.  I am not risking the chance of this happening to me again.  I am not repairing this stove again.

Purchased GE Cafe CGS990SET3SS from Home Depot June 2014.  The lower oven has failed twice from the deflector shield melting on the igniter glow bar, burning out the glow bar.  The second event fried the control panel digital glass touch panel.  This is an ongoing problem and we have continued to replace parts.  We are on the second igniter glow bar and second deflector heat shield. 

This is a safety hazard as GE instructed us to disconnect the gas and not to use the appliance.  The first event was December 2015, second February 2017.  Incidents with pictures have been recorded with GE incident # [REDACTED] and [REDACTED].  We have paid for parts and GE has covered installation labor.

I believe it is a matter of time before this defect causes injury.  I found many similar complaints on appliance forums.

incident_description: We came home late, preheated the oven to cook tater tots.  Put the tater tots in the oven and walked upstairs.  By the time we sat down, we heard a loud pop.  We thought maybe the sheet bent in the heat.  Our eleven year old began screaming, "The oven exploded!  Help!"  We went downstairs and could smell burning.  Smoke billowed all around the ceiling in the kitchen and living room.  My husband checked to see if the tots were on fire.  They were not.  He turned it off.  Then, pulled out the oven and unplugged it with gloves.  The fire was in the back of the oven and it left black scorch marks on the drywall behind the oven.  I checked the GFCI and it did not trigger.  The breaker was fine.  Called Samsung.  They sent out two "certified technicians" on Thursday.  They opened the oven, gasped and started speaking in Korean.  They took a few pictures of the inside.  Then, one pulled the oven out and began unscrewing the back panel.  The other asked to use the bathroom.  By the time the first guy finished, the second guy was done taking pictures of the back.  They were in and out in under 7 minutes.  I asked, as they were rushing out, if they had seen this before.  The one who spoke better English (or at least pretended to) said that he had.  I asked it if was like the Samsung washers and phones, they laughed and nodded.  They said they needed to have an engineering report done and they'd call me back.  I asked how they were going to do that off of pictures of melted wires (he told me I couldn't see the panel because it was just melted wires).  They played dumb and pretended not to understand.  They tried to get me to sign something.  I said I wanted to read it.  He pressured me to just sign it.  I signed it, but added a clause on the form.  Today I contacted [REDACTED] on LiveChat on Samsung.com and she said that I had to call their Executive Customer Relations Department and gave me their 800 #.  I called and [REDACTED] that the ECRD is outbound only.  She said she couldn't do anything and that I was responsible for the $1000 part due to a block installation issue.  I asked how an exploding appliance that nearly caught my wall on fire was my fault.  She said she had no authority and I was transferred to [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] told me that the engineering report (which she didn't have to send to me) said it was an engineering issue.  I asked how they made that determination when all the wires were melted, they only had a picture and no one took apart the appliance.  I told her I wanted a new replacement because I didn't feel safe using this appliance.  She then said that we must have installed it incorrectly and did we hire Home Depot or someone to install it?  I told her it was a drop in range my husband, an IT Senior Network Engineer, could plug in by himself.  They said that in a few days we could get another call and they would have to do some investigating.  I have 7 children and a home daycare.  I have been without an oven or stove for 8 days.  I cook multiple times a day for my family and business and am very inconvenienced.  I am horrified that a company would have an appliance, made in 2012, that we purchased in 2013, explode and catch fire and try to bill me for near what we paid for it to begin with.

incident_description:
There are dials on the front of the gas range, which are used to turn the gas on. One presses the dial down and turns on the gas and then turns the dial to the igniter setting.  Once the igniter comes on, the temperature is at its highest setting.  One can then turn the temperature down from that point.

12/2016:  Unknowingly, the consumer's cat walked across the range and touched one of the dials, which turned the gas on.  The consumer stepped out of the home for approx. 8 - 10 minutes, but when he returned, his home was filled with gas.  He immediately opened the windows and doors in the home to get rid of the gas and turned the dial to the off position.

On a different day, the consumer touched the control dials to test them and found that all were extremely sensitive.  The slightest touch can cause a dial to turn, which causes the gas to come on.  However, the dial may not have been turned far enough to light the igniter.

1/2017:  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they contacted one of their service companies for him.  They would not give the consumer the contact information for the service company.  They said that they would get back to the consumer.  The rep. called the consumer back and indicated that there were complaints that the dials were too difficult to turn, so the manufacturer redesigned them.  The rep. made arrangements for a service tech. to inspect his range.

2/6/2017:  The tech. came to the consumer's home and installed new gas valve burners per the mfr's instructions.  However, when the consumer inspected them, he did not see any difference between them and the ones that were replaced.  The consumer believes that the replacement valves would present the exact same problem and he said that the tech. agreed with him.  The consumer also noted that the tech. said that the valves that came with the range were supposed to be the re-designed ones, which addressed this issue. The tech. ([REDACTED]) was from Stafford Repair Company, Tel: [REDACTED].
The consumer was given Ticket #[REDACTED].

The consumer believes that the knobs are too easy to turn and could present a gas and a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to sensitive dials, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high as the issue was not fully resolved and the dials remain sensitive.

incident_description: GE Ice Dispenser Bin Plastic Auger broke (cracked and plastic pieces came off) on my side by side refrigerator/ freezer made by GE (General Electric). The plastic on the ice Auger broke (cracked) off nearest to the dispenser opening and 1 piece of the 2 pieces that had broken off the auger ended up in my drinking glass when the ice was being dispensed out.  When I was drinking, the 1 piece of plastic made contact with my lips, mouth opening, when drinking from my glass, which caused me to notice something was not right and stop drinking.  I then inspected the glass and ice located inside. This is when I noticed I had a 1 piece of plastic in my cup.  The other piece of the broken plastic I found was still inside the ice bin and I found it when I inspected where the plastic had come from.  It seems to me, the plastic could possibly not be strong enough and it is possibly more prone to breaking than when some manufacturers used metal Augers in the ice dispensers.  Someone could possibly, if the plastic piece was small enough choke on the plastic.  Also, someone could bite down hard on this plastic and cause some kind of dental issue.  Luckily, this did not happen to me, thank goodness, but it did really make me think when the problem happened.  It seems reasonable to think that maybe this part should be redesigned to be stronger so no one has to have the experience that happened to me.
justification: The incident involved a broken plastic piece contacting the user's lips but did not result in injury, and the likelihood of occurrence is considered possible given the description.

incident_description: My oven caught fire while being used to bake  a cake. It caught fire at the back in the electrical board . It is a Frigidaire brand Model Number FPEF3081MFE ,serial number VF42355766 . Luckily I was there and was able to extinguish the fire almost immediately . The oven is approx 3 years old and in good general condition.
justification: The oven caught fire but was extinguished immediately with no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
GE Adora gas range (Model JGB720EEJ1ES) with 2 issues:

1. Very hot on the upper rear of the range when using broiler--service technician (GE authorized) tested it at 480 Degrees (and still rising) with infrared sensor before shutting it down for safety reasons. This is the second range with this problem--the first one was serviced by a different GE authorized tech for the same issues, then replaced because problem couldn't be resolved. Both service technicians voiced concerns regarding fire hazard and potential to damage the range's circuit board and advised us to keep the range pulled out away from the wall until problem could be resolved.

2. Excessive smoke and fumes when first used, to the point of burning eyes, coughing, having to open windows for a few hours to disperse. The smoke came from front of range and even more from the back of the range. Service tech stated that the smoke from the rear could be from burning insulation around the vent duct.
This problem actually occurred with 3 ranges, all the same model--the 2 mentioned above, and a previous one that was the original range we received but was replaced because it wasn't the color we ordered. I don't recall using the broiler on that original range so don't know if it had the heat problem.

(GE is replacing our range with a different model due to repeated problem with this model.)
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard and excessive smoke causing discomfort but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence across multiple units suggests a likely occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description: Krups FBC4 Toaster Oven will not turn off.  Should operate by setting temperature (manually or with one of the presets on the bottom rotary knob) and timer and, at the end of timing, shut off automatically.  Now, when unit is plugged in, lower heating elements are energized regardless of being on or what temperature is set.  Unplugging the unit is the only way to turn it off however the elements are immediately on if the unit is plugged in again.  It does not appear that setting the temperature has any effect, elements seem to be full on without being regulated to the temperature setting.  Having heating elements that will not respond to switches or timer is a heat and fire safety hazard.
justification: The toaster oven's heating elements being constantly on poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
We are a manufacturing facility. We use single burners to heat up wax or glue in small quantities. In our lab a  burner caught on fire. It was immediately unplugged. After inspecting the burner and pot, we noticed that the coil on the burner was damaged, which created a hole through the pot where it was placed. Due to the petrolatum leaking from the hole, it started a fire about 2 to 3 feet high. It burned itself out within seconds. Thankfully no one was too close to the burner or flame. There was also a sudden loud surge of electricity and the contents within the pot splattered all around within a 3 foot radius.

We use single burners in multiple departments within our building we have pulled all single burners from this company and replaced them. We chose to do so after reading reviews that we were not the only consumer who has had issues with these.

We have reported this incident to the company Proctor Silex/ Hamilton Beach. They asked us to send them our defective unit before they can do anything. 

The model number is 34101Y Series number A2941BW is our defective unit we had 21 additional units that have been pulled.
justification: The incident involved a fire and electrical surge but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the issue was contained quickly.

incident_description:
I have just become aware of high levels of lead detected in the paint used on the glass sippy cup that my child has used daily for over a year and I am HUGELY concerned.

This is the product:  https://www.buybuybaby.com/ÃÂ/green-sprouts-by-i-plaÃÂ/3255277

I have contacted the company, but in light of the fact that they rescinded a voluntary recall (http://sanfrancisco.cbslocal.com/.../parent-tests-prompt.../), I am concerned that they will not take swift and definitive action, so I am appealing to you to intervene.
justification: The description indicates potential exposure to high lead levels over a prolonged period, which poses a significant risk of injury to the child.

incident_description: I have used my Pyrex lasagna pan hundreds of times.   I had to go to the emergency room with a glass shard in my eye (and had a massive mess to clean up) when the pan exploded in my hands last night as I removed it from the oven. These pans are dangerous!  They are completely unpredictable.  STOP SELLING THEM!    RECALL THEM!
justification: The incident resulted in a glass shard in the eye, requiring emergency room treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG dual oven gas range which was delivered on January 1st.
The ultra high burner would not ignite and had a dangerous flare up when manually lite.  Service call replaced a missing part in the burner cap, but the burner was still slow to ignite and continued to flare up intermittently. This burner is one of front burners and can cause injury if you do not stand back.
Second issue is the knobs.  they are on the front of the unit and do not lock.  My microwave is located above the stove and when I leaned slightly against the knobs they turn on just enough to fill the kitchen with gas fumes.  The most dangerous issue for me was the noxious fumes emitted by the lower oven.  They continued after 4-5 uses and when I checked the lower oven it was covered in soot.  Nasty black soot that you would find in a wood burning fireplace or campfire when the wood does not completely burn.
justification: The burner flare-ups and gas fumes pose a clear risk of injury, and the soot emission indicates a hazardous malfunction.

incident_description:
I was using a Panasonic NB-G100P toaster oven that is 5+ years old. After toasting, the unit is supposed to automatically stop cooking. The unit continued to cook. I turned the unit off, and the unit continued to cook with the power turned off. The only thing that stopped the unit from cooking was to unplug it. I attempted to plug it back in, and the unit began cooking again WITHOUT the power being turned on.

Unit does not appear to have a serial number but has 505241 stamped on the bottom.
justification: The toaster oven malfunctioned by continuing to cook even when turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: We were using the Veggie Spiral Slicer to slice a zucchini over a bowl.  At dinner my son bit down on metal while chewing his food and it turned out to be one of the blades from the slicer.  It had fallen out of the slicer and fallen into our food.
justification: The incident involved a blade from the slicer falling into food, which was bitten but did not cause injury.

incident_description:
This report is regarding a KitchenAid under counter dishwasher, model #KUDS01DJSS0 (the user guide also lists the number 8269908A on the front cover); serial number FL4239840, type 577-0.  We did not purchase this dishwasher; it was installed by the prior owners of this house.  My guess is that the dishwasher is around 10-12 years old.  

The evening of Tuesday, February 21, 2017 the dishwasher was loaded, filled with detergent, and turned on to run with the "normal" cycle setting.  Approximately 15 minutes after the unit was turned on it began to make a strange grinding noise; about 10 seconds later smoke appeared from the top right corner of the control panel and 2-3 seconds later we could see flames coming out from the same corner of the control panel with sizzling/popping noises.

We keep a fire extinguisher in the kitchen, so as I called 911 for the fire department my husband managed to extinguish the fire before it affected anything else in the kitchen.  Thankfully no one was hurt.  The fire department arrived about 5 minutes later and helped verify that the fire was indeed out, and helped get the dishwasher disconnected from the power source/wiring to ensure an electrical fire would not start up again in the unit.

Needless to say this was a scary incident and if the dishwasher was running when we were not at home and this happened I would hate to think of what might have happened to our house.  While I never run the dryer when I'm not at home I will now NEVER run the dishwasher when I'm not at home either.  And I will never buy the brand KitchenAid.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, and the fire was quickly extinguished without further damage.

incident_description: heating element seemed to have overheated and warped causing the bottom sprayer arm to hit it and melt, as well as the heating element to burn a hole in the bottom of dishwasher and flood 3 rooms in our home.
justification: The incident caused property damage (flooding in 3 rooms) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: While making dinner and slicing chicken, the blade on my 8" chef's knife came detached and I sliced my finger.
justification: The description states that the person sliced their finger, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Knife blade broke off from handle while cutting vegetables.
justification: The broken knife blade could cause injury if it flies off or is mishandled, but the description does not mention any injury occurring.

incident_description:
The consumer put a bag of popcorn in the microwave and set the timer for 2 minutes. Approximately 3 seconds later, the consumer states that he heard a pop and noticed flames inside the microwave. The consumer opened the microwave and used a rag to put out the fire. The consumer states that the microwave has burn damages inside and the popcorn bag did not have burn damages.

The consumer contacted the place of purchase (Lyle's TV & Appliance) and informed them of the incident. The consumer was offered a replacement of the same model and the store will haul away the old microwave. The consumer states that the store is awaiting a shipment of these microwaves and they will call the consumer when they have a delivery date. 

The consumer indicated that he overheard a store employee saying that another consumer who purchased this model microwave from their store had a similar incident. 

The consumer contacted the firm today and informed them of the incident. The consumer was asked to send pictures of the inside of the microwave to [REDACTED]@sea.samung.com and they will call him back in 4 hours after they review the matter (Transaction # [REDACTED]).

The consumer indicated that he used the microwave about 3-4 times a week since he purchased it and there is no prior incident.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injuries were reported. Similar incidents have been reported, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Electronic controls on stove all began to spark, first periodic the continuous.  Electric burn smell with gas stove.  Shut off stove at breaker
justification: The incident involved sparking and an electric burn smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I self cleaned the Whirlpool over model  WOS51EC0AB and 1 1/2 hours into the cleaning cycle, the glass in the inside window just shattered while I was in the next room. Small little shards fell through the bottom of the oven. The oven was in perfect condition and I am puzzled as to why it just shattered.
justification: The glass shattered during the cleaning cycle, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
My wife was running our dishwasher when we heard a buzzing noise . When I went in to check the noise fire was coming out of the upper right side . I immediately opened the door and extinguished the fire . Luckily we were home when this occurred or our house could have easily caught fire . This failure is completely unacceptable for a high end kitchen-aide dishwasher or any other home appliance .The appliance did not kick a circuit breaker to cut power . I expect someone to contact me with an except able resolution .   Model # KUDS01FLSS3  SER # FR1723018

  Thank You
  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher, which was extinguished without injury, but posed a significant risk to property.

incident_description:
KITCHENAID DOUBLE OVEN EXPLODED WHILE COOKING.
GLASS SHARDS EVERYWHERE
MODEL NUMBER kemc308KBL04
SERIAL xt0904345
justification: The oven exploded, causing glass shards to scatter, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
On Sunday afternoon on January 29th my brother, [REDACTED], placed food to heat in a Black & Decker countertop over (a Toast-R-Oven) model and about 30 seconds after he turned on the unit fumes poured out the vents and a fire ignited inside. This appliance is several years old. (I think it is about 2 years old, but he believes it is closer to 5 years old so I using his estimated date).  My brother told me he purchased the counter top oven in new condition at a local store in Hastings, Nebraska. He said he cannot recall the name of the retailer right now, but suspects it was Walmart where he frequently shops. I carefully looked over the unit after the incident and could not find a serial number or a UPC code anywhere on the exterior.

I turned off the electricity and turned down the unit. The fire lasted inside the oven for about 3 minutes before dying out.  It was a fire (not a spark) and it blazed inside the product but did not consume the food item. I did not open the door, and fortunately the flames did not spread into the kitchen. However, a noxious odor and smoke permeated the area for several hours. I had contacted Black & Decker's website about 2 weeks earlier when I noticed a lot of smoke coming from the appliance and the heating element growing very white inside. Their customer service online chat/text service had referred me to an online vendor, support@spectrumbrands.com but I had not contacted that email since my brother had resumed using the unit and did not consider it unsafe to use. I had noticed it seemed to emit a smoky odor during use.  I did report the problem to the spectrumbrands email immediately on Sunday but have not yet received a response.

I wanted to contact you now because I am concerned about the safety of the product. The oven quite literally burst into flames in front of me on Sunday afternoon. Fortunately, I did not open the door- if I had, I think we would have had a potentially serious kitchen fire. We have since discontinued using the unit and it is available for technical inspection if desired.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the oven but no injuries or property damage occurred, and the fire was contained within the appliance.

incident_description:
Electric flat stove top malfunctions. Burner flares to high even when knob is set to simmer. At times, burner does not turn off and electricity must be turned off at the breaker box until it cools down.

Frigidaire model  # FEC32S6ABF Serial # MF73221148.
justification: The malfunctioning stove poses a risk of overheating and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I purchased as new a DeLonghi EO-1270 toaster oven in November 2015.  January 2017, after running a toasting cycle, the unit turned off as expected.  However, a few minutes later the unit turned back on by itself, and became extremely hot.  As the unit had turned off, it was unattended, and its "On" state was not detected until a burning smell was detected in our home.  Had we left the home, we would likely have returned to a fire.  On inspection, the timer had rotated to the "Off" position, as expected, but over several minutes, continued to rotate to the "On" position.  This behavior is repeatable.  This failure mode has been noted by other consumers in the Reviews section of Amazon.com.  THIS PRODUCT SHOULD BE RECALLED.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toaster oven that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Toaster Oven just a couple years when the far bottom heating element warped out of shape.  It is now making contact with interior metal of oven.  After reading the 20+ other similar reports of this happening on this model (as well as dozens of others from reputable review sites), I will no longer be using this toaster considering many consumers have been electrically shocked and/or fires have started in this model due to this situation.
justification: The description mentions electrical shocks and fires, indicating potential for injury, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: We were using our Bosch dishwasher model SHU43C05UC/17 on Sunday 2/12/2017 on the Pots and pans cycle.  It had approximately 20 minutes until the end of the cycle when the control panel caught on fire.  Flames were coming out of the front of the unit completely melting the panel.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing significant damage to the control panel, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Outer door glass shattered on Kenmore freestanding range.
justification: The shattered glass is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: J.C. Penny's 2.5qt stainless steel sauce pan/pot was being used to make rice. Suddenly, with no warning, one of the metal disks covering the end of a rivet in the pot popped off hit my girlfriend's face at a relatively high speed (the rivets are used to affix the handle to the pot body). The rivet cover disk was very hot. No serious injury occurred, but there was redness on the skin where the disk impacted and pain associated with the event. This event seems similar to recall numbers [REDACTED] and [REDACTED].
justification: The incident caused redness and pain, indicating an injury, but no serious harm was reported. The event seems isolated, making recurrence unlikely.

incident_description: We have a side by side Frigidaire Refrigerator Model #GLRS642EBA refrigerator that we purchased new in 2008 or 2009.  We noticed a strong odor coming from the refrigerator side.  The ice also tasted funny.  We replaced the water filter and completely emptied both the freezer and refrigerator.  We could still smell the odor.  We washed everything down with baking soda and water per the owner manual and still could smell the odor.  My husband then looked inside the refrigerator and noticed that the light bulb in the ceiling had burned a big hole in the roof of the ceiling.  It was a 40 W appliance bulb as per manual and it was burned into the ceiling as well.  We cannot get the smell out of the refrigerator.  The hole goes clear through the insulation.  We have been sick as a family makes me wonder if it not from drinking ice with the fumes of burnt plastic.
justification: The incident involves a burnt plastic smell and potential exposure to fumes, leading to family illness, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I know that the Caphalon knives have already been recalled but I thought I should report my incident before I returned the knife.  I did not know this was something that should have been reported when it happened.  I was using an 8" Chef's Knife to cut vegetables when the tip broke off.  There were no injuries.
justification: The knife tip broke off during use, but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My 6 quart Philippe Richard Pressure Cooker Exploded and flew off my stove on the floor, spewing hot steam and turkey breast across my entire kitchen, ( Ceiling, cabinets, floors) What a mess! Thank God we were far enough away from it we didn't get hurt. People need to know how dangerous this product is!
justification: The pressure cooker exploded causing significant damage but no injuries, as stated the individuals were far enough away to avoid harm.

incident_description:
(02/22/2017) The consumer stated that he was using the utensil to slice carrots. He had sliced thru a few carrots when his left fore finger inadvertently came in the path of the descending cutting blade. The consumer chopped off the tip of his finger.

The consumer went to an urgent care center for medical assistance. The tip of his finger could not be re-attached.

The consumer stated that the instrument should have a safety mechanism to prevent amputation of body parts.
justification: The consumer suffered a finger amputation, which is a significant injury requiring medical attention.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that he is experiencing problems with his toaster oven. While in use the toaster does not complete its cycle it goes to off but keeps running.  The unit has to be unplugged to stop it.  The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised to cut the cord and return it but he feels that this is a manufacture defect and should be reported.

Consumer feels that this toaster should be recalled because it poses a fire hazard.

After completing the "toaster" cycle, the appliance does not turn off.  Instead, it continues onto the "stay on" cyde.  Very dangerous because it remains on, when it should have turned off automatically.
justification: The toaster oven fails to turn off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
purchased a Samsung Gas Range.  When it was delivered the installer told me to run the 
oven at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.  After 30 minutes I turned off the oven and my hand
brushed against the stainless steel strip that runs behind the stove control knobs.  It was
hot.  I then touched it to see how hot it was.  It was so hot that I could not maintain contact
for more than a second.   I called my brother and asked him if his range does the same.
He said he never uses the oven REDACT but would try it out and call me back.  He did and he said
he had the same results.  I called Home Depot to report a defective range.  They called
Samsung and verified that the range was defective.  Home Depot has picked it up.
justification: The incident involved a hot surface causing discomfort but no injury, and the issue was reported and verified as a defect.

incident_description:
(11/26/2016)The consumer stated that she had used the oven all day the day before. The next morning the consumer noticed that the left knob was loose and thought that using the oven had caused the knob to come loose. The consumer took the knob off and noticed that it was burned on the inside. The consumer removed the knob.

The consumer stated that her husband removed the top of the range and noticed a naked wire.  The wires go from one knob to all of the other knobs. The naked wire connects the knob that is loose.

(12/1/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. The consumer advised them of the incident. The consumer was advised that nothing could be done about the range. 

The consumer contacted the firm's corporate office. The consumer was advised that the warranty for the product had run out and nothing could be done about the range. She was offered a repair visit at a cost to her.
justification: The incident involved a loose and burned knob with a naked wire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Was running the dishwasher. It had been set on the timer to run. As we came home the dishwasher was running and burning we opened the door and it continued to run. The walls on our cabinets were hot.  The front panel and inside had started to burn and melt. Dishwasher was removed from the home and taken apart due to the fire.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction causing burning and melting, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Oven front door exploded when the oven was turned off. The oven had been used but was not hot at the time. This was the outer glass and not the inner glass.
justification: The oven door exploded, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire dishwasher Model # FGBD2445NQ  SN# TH22087651
Noticed water leaking in basement below the dishwasher. Pulled the dishwasher out and started a wash cycle to find the leak. Water was coming out near the bottom of the tub on the left side,  when facing the dishwasher, and the tub was deformed. Took the lower rack out of the dishwasher and saw that the heating element was warped and touching the plastic tub and had burned a hole in it, causing the water leak. Also the sprayer arm was caught on the heating element and was melted, there was melted plastic hanging down from the sprayer arm. 
Called Frigidaire and was told there was nothing they could do.
I really believe this could be a possible fire hazard. I did take photos of the dishwasher.
The unit was purchased new and delivered on 06-08-2012.
My name is [REDACTED],
Phone # [REDACTED].
Thank you
justification: The incident involves a dishwasher leaking water and a warped heating element causing damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Cooktop would randomly turn on full power.  Circuit breaker needed to be turned of to shut of.  After factory repair, while using cooktop, unit "blew up" on the inside with a large flash & popping the breaker.
justification: The cooktop malfunctioned with a large flash and popping the breaker, indicating a significant incident but no reported injury.

incident_description: On my Kenmore model 790.46709603 Electric Range, the oven outer door glass shattered on its own.  The oven was not turned on and was cool at the time.  I was standing about 15 ft from the oven when it shattered sending thousands of broken glass pieces through the kitchen.
justification: The oven door glass shattered unexpectedly, but no injury was reported despite the glass scattering.

incident_description:
Regarding Whirlpool Gas Range

Model WFG530S0EB0
Serial # R50610283

The knobs on our gas range can accidentally be turned on unknowingly by merely bumping against the front of the range.  Gas will start to fill our kitchen and permeate into the remaining areas of the house because we aren't aware a knob has been bumped.  This happens frequently.  The range should have knobs that push in to turn the burners on.  The potential for an explosion to occur from a knob being bumped accidentally is great with the design flaw with this appliance.

I contacted the manufacturer and they won't do anything to fix the problem.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that could lead to gas leaks, posing a risk of explosion, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Our LG Microwave, model LCRT2010ST, suddenly started to turn on every time the door is opened. It did that without warning, having functioned OK up to this point. If our 4 year old granddaughter would have been the one to open it she would not have known to shut the door.
justification: The microwave turning on unexpectedly poses a risk, especially to a child, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
We have a frigidaire gallery stainless steel French door refrigerator with water/ice dispenser on the door. The underside of the front panel of the water/ice dispenser is razor sharp. In a freak accident my 11 month old severely cut 3 of his fingers grabbing onto it while daddy was holding him. We rushed to the emergency room and are now having to see a plastic surgeon for care to determine the extent of the damage. 

This truly was a freak accident and could've happened to anyone. Consumers should be careful when cleaning the area to not cut themselves. Frigidaire should put a cover of sorts on the underside of the panel. My parents have the same fridge in side by side and their panel is plastic.
justification: The incident resulted in severe cuts requiring emergency room and plastic surgeon care, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
During various times of the year (2016), the consumer and her husband have attempted to open the oven door, but the handle has completely detached from the oven.  Sometimes it has been one side of the handle and at other times, it has been the entire handle.

When this has happened, the consumer's husband has reconnected the handle back to the door, by re-inserting the screws into the oven door.

(12/9/2016)  The oven was set to 350 degrees for approx. 30 minutes the outer glass on the oven door shattered.  The consumer was a few inches away from the oven at the time.  Pieces of glass shot out several feet away from the oven.  There were no injuries.

The consumer Is still locating glass in various parts of her kitchen.

There were no injuries.
The range oven has never been serviced for any reason.
  
The consumer's range does not appear to be included in the Recall 0-333.
justification: The incident involved the oven door handle detaching and glass shattering, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Our GE Profile Microwave caught fire Thursday night, March 2nd. My wife was simply putting butter in a microwave safe container into the unit to melt it. When she hit the start button, the right side of the microwave caught fire. She yelled to me, we shut the unit off but the fire continued. I opened the unit and was able to extinguish the fire. I then removed the microwave from the cabinet it was set in and got it to the garage so it would pose no further risk to our home.
I called GE Consumer Relations Friday morning and they took all my info and asked me to send photos which I did right away. I asked the representative to confirm by email that she did receive the photos and she said that she would. Well, even after a followup email to her, I still never got this confirmation. I'm guessing I'll be able to contact them come Monday but I did try to call today but their CR department is closed on weekends.
Additionally, doing some online research, this is not the first GE microwave to catch fire. There have been a number of issues where the microwave caught fire without the microwave in use, and several I saw when it caught fire when the homeowners weren't even in the home, causing major damage. I'm just glad we were home when this happened as we had no damage other than the microwave itself.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was extinguished without injury or damage to the home, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
I was cooking dinner and set the preheat button to 425.  The buzzer went off but it didn't turn off.  I pushed the clear button and a code of F 1 appeared.  I pushed clear again and F 3 appeared.  The buzzer kept going off and the clear button would not shut it off.  I opened the oven door and it was way too hot to be the temp I had set it for and the heat was coming from a red hot broiler element but I had not set the oven to broil.  I reached to try the clear button again and noticed the surface element I was reaching across was hot.  I had not been using that element.  I looked and the knob was in the off position.  I set the element I was using to off but the light showing if there was an element on did not turn off.  I immediately turned the breaker off for the range. My husband checked to see if the manual would tell us what the codes represented and determined the computer/wiring had malfunctioned. Because the range was purchased in January of 1998 we decided that we would purchase a new range instead of having it repaired.

Earlier in the day I had mentioned to my husband that we needed to replace the light indicator for the oven temp because it was so light I couldn't read it anymore.  It had progressively become dimmer.  When I mentioned this to the salesperson at Sears he said that was most likely an indication that the range was beginning to malfunction.  We did purchase a new range.

After we got home we wondered if there was a recall on the old one.  I didn't locate one.  I did feel very lucky that I was in the kitchen and had the sense of mind to turn the breaker off.  This could have been a real fire hazard.  What if I had left the room.  Our house could have caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such malfunctions are not common but can happen with older appliances.

incident_description:
I used a burner on the gas range to heat a pan, then put the pan in the oven to finish it. I thought I had turned the burner off because no flame was visible.

I went to bed after dinner but was awoken by my carbon monoxide alarm about 4 hours later. It indicated a CO level >50ppm.  There was a petroleum smell and  I followed it to the kitchen where I noticed the range burner was on and warm.  I turned the burner off, opened the windows, and the CO alarm stopped sounding.

The next morning I looked at the burner and noticed that the inside was coated with soot. I tried lighting the burner, turning it almost off, and noticed that it remained warm and gave off a petroleum smell even though no flame was visible.  It seems that if the knob is between "Off" and "Lite" there is a small flame within the burner assembly that is not visible.
justification: The incident involved a gas burner left on, leading to a CO alarm activation but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a set of Scanpan pots and pans from Amazon in May of 2016.  A few weeks ago, I noticed a crack in the handle where it attaches to the pot, around the hole the bolt goes through.  The crack is about 1/4" wide and goes all the way through the metal.  I called Scanpan customer service and asked for a warranty replace/repair.  They told me (via email) that their warranty only covers the interior lining of the product, not the handle.  I believe this is a serious safety issue.  If I was trying to carry a pot of boiling water to the sink to drain it, and the handle broke, I could be seriously injured.  

The product did not break, but it is obviously defective.  I'm afraid they might have a problem with their manufacturing process.
justification: The handle is cracked but no incident or injury has occurred yet, though there is potential for injury if the handle fails during use.

incident_description:
The consumer states that her unit is not included in the recall but she believes her unit should be included because her blade looks exactly like the blade on the recall.

The consumer states that the model # for the part that houses the blade is "AFP7" and the model # for the part that houses the motor is "FPB5BK (TX5)." The consumer could not find one model number for the entire unit.

The consumer called the firm's customer service and expressed her safety concerns. The consumer was advised that she could not receive the replacement blade because her model was not recalled  and they could not assist her. 

The consumer then went to the firm's recall site (recall.cuisinart.com) and went through the questions. The consumer states that her model was not listed but she selected the first model # on the drop down menu and she filled out the contact form ([REDACTED]). The consumer states that she left a message in the comments section requesting the firm to include her unit in the recall because she believes it could also present the same safety hazard.

The consumer's daughter received this unit as a wedding gift sometime in 2006.
justification: The consumer raised a safety concern but no actual incident or injury was reported.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his dishwasher purchased during the Autumn of 2004 from a retailer in Indiana.
He had no problems with the unit until Monday, January 2, 2017 when his wife started the dishwasher, called him because she smelled an odd odor.  He came upstairs immediately but in that time the dishwasher was emitting black smoke with blue flame coming from the front.
The flames were around two or three inches coming out of the unit.
The caller said that blue flames identify electrical fire.
There are no injuries being reported
He contacted the manufacturer the same day and he was referred to their website for an online web session.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with flames, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Our Maytag Dishwasher door caught fire and black smoke began to fill the kitchen. It was stopped by shutting off the circuit breaker in the basement. The dishwasher had to be removed from the house due to the smell. I still have it in the shed.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and produced black smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Vivitar mini portable cooler (model: 82123BK-TA) a couple of years ago. We use this cooler in our bedroom to hold bottled water. At 5:30 am today I awoke to a burning smell. As I walked around the house trying to locate where the smell was coming from, I was unable to find the source of the smell. A few minutes later, I returned to my bedroom at the same time that my husband was waking up yelling "Fire!" and at that moment I heard a whoosh as a huge flame engulfed the top of the cooler. We secured a towel and threw the towel over the cooler to put out the flame as smoke filled the bedroom and the smoke alarms were triggered.
justification: The incident involved a fire that caused significant damage and triggered smoke alarms, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Fire inside dishwasher during heated dry cycle in the middle of the night caused extensive damage to dishwasher (melting parts of the dishwasher basket, cutting boards, utensils and knife handles), rendering it completely inoperable and seemingly quite dangerous. Many utensils, plates, cutting boards and knifes had to be trashed. Rancid melted plastic smoke stayed in the house for a long time.
justification: The incident caused extensive damage to property but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Our refrigerator spontaneously dispenses ice which has both caused people to slip and fall and warped our wood floor due to melted water.
justification: The refrigerator's ice dispenser causes slips and falls (injury) and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
I was installing a new Whirlpool electric range.  I was removing plastic film that protects new product, and was severely cut by the inside edge of the warming drawer.  The whole inside edge of this drawer is knife sharp  
Whirlpool Model WFE515SOESO
justification: The description mentions a severe cut from a sharp edge, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I am writing to inform you that our Whirlpool electric range is a safety hazard. I would like to know if our model # WFE710HOASO has been recalled. If it hasnÃÂt, I believe it should be.  The range was new when we purchased our home in April 2014. In June of 2015, we reported an oven fire to Whirlpool due to the lower heating element bursting into flames. I was fortunate to be standing by my range at the time so I quickly turned off the oven and the electricity from the circuit breaker. On March 1, I began preheating my oven on the bake setting. . I soon smelled a ÃÂhotÃÂ odor coming from the oven even though there was no food in it. I looked in and found the broiler was on. I made no mistake when I turned on my oven, I turned it to the bake setting, as I had done regularly for 3 years. I immediately turned off the oven and waited for a few minutes and then set it to bake at 350 degrees a second time and the same thing happened (went to broil). The danger is that the temperature the oven reaches on broil with the oven door closed is extremely hot. When someone isnÃÂt aware that the oven is even close to this temperature (because it was set to 350) this is a dangerous situation and a hazard! 
In addition to this new problem, the heating elements on the stove top do not regulate properly and have been malfunctioning for over a year. The heating elements can become extremely hot without changing the setting on the stovetop. An example of this is three nights ago we had some soup on the stove keeping warm on the lowest setting while we ate. The soup was on the stove on the lowest setting for about 10 minutes when suddenly it began to boil rapidly. I removed it from the heat and singed my arm on the very hot burner- this has happened monthly since the heating element fire in June 2015.  This should never happen on a low setting without touching the dial!
justification: The incident involves both a fire hazard and an injury (singed arm), indicating a severity level of 3. The recurring nature of the heating element issues suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: Frigidaire mdel LGGF3043KFV, serial VF63601022 purchased end of Nov. 2016 and used sparingly since.  On March 5 2016 put potatoes for baking in oven at 400 degrees.  One hour later I put a pot of water on to boil and when I turned the knob for the burner I burnt my hand as the knob had heated.  I called Frigidaire on 3/6 and explained what had occurred, their respond was it "was a stainless steel stove and the knobs are steel, the oven vents just below the knobs creating the overheating condition."  There is no warning in the manual or advertisement for this product. This is obviously a design flaw for which Frigidaire takes no responsibility, had this been one of my grandchildren or anyone's child a serious burn could have resulted.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the likelihood is possible as the issue is a known design flaw.

incident_description: My Anchor Hocking baking dish EXPLODED on Sunday after eating dinner. My family cooked chicken breasts in this glass container, ate the chicken, the dish was cooled, I washed the dish as much as I could but there was some baked on cheese so I filled the dish with the leftover dishwater to soak. We then went to the dining room to play a board game. Maybe 30 minutes later, we heard a loud sound of glass exploding and a waterfall. The dish spontaneously exploded glass ALL OVER THE KITCHEN.
justification: The glass dish exploded, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I purchased a Caphlon Cutlery set, knives.  I was using one and the handle just broke right off.  I have been meaning to contact someone regarding this, but didn't know where to start.
justification: The handle breaking off is an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Knife broke when my husband was using it.  A chunk of the blade broke off.
justification: A knife breaking during use is an incident, but the description does not mention any injury.

incident_description: During the use of the calphalon knife the tip of the 4 1/2" parer knife broke. These knives were expensive and not worth the money. I have been very disappointed in them. Not sharp at some parts of the blades and then sharp at other parts causing me to cut my fingers several times.
justification: The user reported cutting their fingers several times due to inconsistent blade sharpness, indicating injury.

incident_description: The Kenmore Elite model number 665.16263402 began emitting smoke/fumes from the top right corner of the door approximately 15 to 20 minutes into the cycle.  After cutting power to the dishwasher and allowing things to settle, there is now a white streak of chemical debris running from the top right down the inside of the door.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke/fumes and left chemical debris, indicating an incident but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Model #RBS305PDQ16 WHIRLPOOL Built-In Oven, Electric S/N XP4908322

The bottom trim on the oven is unfinished and razor-sharp. This trim lacerated my son causing  a lifelong scar,  extreme medical expenses, and lost wages due to us missing work (more than 12 stitches). 

This is a very similar situation to a recall they had last year on the same unfinished typed metal (different location, same end result)
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring more than 12 stitches, indicating a significant injury (severity 3). The mention of a similar past recall suggests this issue is likely to recur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Caller stated that his dual gas range turns on accidentally if brushed against the knobs, which causes the gas to escapes in his home.  (10/26/16) He contacted Sears and complained but they are unwilling to assist him.  He stated that this incident has been ongoing since installation.  He stated that he has had more than 40 incidents.

Caller feels that this range is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves gas escaping due to accidental activation, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported. The occurrence is almost certain, with over 40 incidents reported since installation.

incident_description: 5years ago we purchased a kitchen package from Lowe's all Samsung appliances. I am contacting you because of the issues we had. 11 months the dishwasher quit was told by the Samsung warranty would be cheaper to buy new we did did different brand.  We have had 3 repairs on the refrigerator already.the main concern is our stove caught fire in the electronic components blazing if we hadn't had a fire extinguisher our home would have burnt. We have phoned Samsung but got nowhere. I feel these are unsafe products and poor quality. I
justification: The stove caught fire, which could have resulted in death if not for the fire extinguisher, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is low as it's a single reported incident among multiple appliance issues.

incident_description: We were using a baby bottle sanitizer in the microwave in which it requires 5 minutes of run time.  We have used this sanitizer with both of our children without any issue.  The sanitizer is made completely of plastic, the bottles inside the sanitizer also made of plastic.  The microwave was turned on and my wife left the kitchen then she heard an odd popping noise.  While she was tracking the noise she saw a fire inside the microwave.  She then grabbed a fire extinguisher and put the fire out.  Looking at the inside of the microwave it appears that the fire started on the right side.  The bottle sanitizer did not have any markings on it.  She then unplugged the microwave from the wall.
justification: A fire occurred in the microwave, but it was quickly extinguished without injury or death.

incident_description:
We have a cusinart chopper [REDACTED] which has a recall on the blade.  We registered two months ago and today I was told that there is a back order for the new blades.  We were told not to use the machine so we have an expensive piece of equipment that cannot be used for who knows how long due to defective manufacture of the blade.

secondly we have a cusinart mini chopper SN#20918 Model DLC1 S on which the collar that holds the blade in place is broken on one side and cracked on the other.  When we called Cusinart about this they responded that it is not on recall and we will have to purchase a new blade for this machine.  It appears that they make defective equipment and will not take responsibility unless forced  to do so.
justification: The incident involves defective equipment that cannot be used, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
(11/28/2016) The consumer stated that she was making a protein shake in the blender. When she turned it on she heard a pinging sound which she thought was the ice cubes that she had placed in the blender.

The consumer drank the shake and felt something toward the back of her throat. She was able to remove a piece of the blade the back of her throat. The consumer looked at the unit and saw that the blade had cracked at the base and had come off. The broken piece was about an inch and a half long.

The back of the consumer's throat was scratched just a little bit but not enough for medical attention.

(12/1/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. The firm requested the unit and all of the pieces so that they could to do an inspection for defects. 

The consumer was refunded for the product.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor injury (a scratch in the throat) but did not require medical attention.

incident_description:
I own a Panasonic NN-SN686S in Stainless Steel with a dial and have had it for several years. Yesterday I used the microwave on standard settings with a glass, microwave safe Pyrex bowl inside with butter in it. 

The microwave caught on fire internally after 30s of active cook time. The interior panel on the right side of the microwave was bubbled and burnt black when I opened the microwave after unplugging it and waiting for the flames to subside. 

The microwave is out of 1-year warranty so the company will not replace it.
justification: The microwave caught fire but there was no injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description: I was about to make hummus in my Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus when I noticed that the blade housing did not get fully clean after my previous task. Upon inspection, I noticed that the plastic housing holding the blade was cracked in several places where the blade is inserted. I stopped using it immediately, having been previously affected by the recall for the blade of my 9-cup processor.
justification: The incident involves a cracked blade housing, which poses a potential hazard but no injury occurred as the user stopped using it immediately.

incident_description: I purchased a Kitchen Aid Artisan Stand Mixer (Model: KSM150PSWH, Serial #: WU0519544) in August 2008 at London Drugs in Vancouver. About 6 months ago I was using the mixer on high speed, whipping egg whites for a few minutes. There was a loud bang type of noise, a large spark and the breaker tripped. I thought it was a problem with the wiring in my 100 year old house. (But it was VERY SCARY.) Two days ago I was making cookies and sparks began to fly out of the back of the head of the mixer and the breaker tripped again. This time I realized it is a mixer problem. This poses an electrical and fire safety hazard for the user. I searched online and found a post about another consumer reporting the exact same problem. The mixer just before the most recent electrical issue,  developed what seems to be some kind of gear problem. I called the Kitchen Aid help line about the gear problem and since the machine is off warranty, they offered me a "Customer Loyalty Discount", to purchase a new machine. A can buy the same mixer locally here from Canadian Tire for less money, on sale. After the sparking and breaker incident, I realize this machine is not safe to use. I wrote about the issue on Kitchen Aid's FB page - they replied, saying that I had already been in contact with Customer Service and the best they could do was offer me the same Customer Loyalty Discount. This is a safety issue, which they do not show any concern about. They have not shown any interest in understanding the source of the problem, nor of protecting consumers who use this mixer and experience similar problems. This could have caused a house fire - and all Kitchen Aid has done is to offer me a discount to buy another mixer from them. I told them I will not be buying any more Kitchen Aid appliances! I think this matter should be looked in to, and the problem identified, consumers made aware, and affected mixers recalled. Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a serious electrical hazard with potential for fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
After preheating our electric oven (Kenmore Model 790.42531311 / Serial AF42602363) my wife -
1) opened the door;
2) the handle came off (on the left side); &
3) the outer glass fascia SHATTERED, scattering glass bits throughout the kitchen.

The above happened Friday 2/10/2017.  The unit was delivered new 7/1/2015.
justification: The incident involved the oven handle coming off and glass shattering, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was heating up butter using the Kohl's food network nonstick ceramic coated stainless steel skillet. Just as I was about to add the eggs, the rivet top made a large explosive sound and flew out of the pan and hit the counter on the other side of the room.
justification: The incident involved an explosive sound and a flying rivet top, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My adult daughter was doing dishes after our evening meal, on February 11,  2017.  She put the tempered glass lid of the 12" Presto Electric Skillet, in the dishwasher.  When she did so, it shattered.  The lid was not hot, as it had cooled to room temperature while we ate our dinner.  She did not bump the lid against anything.  I would guess that the skillet lid was only about 3 years old. 

Fortunately, no one was hurt, but it was a scary experience.
justification: The tempered glass lid shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: Our microwave oven spontaneously turned itself n and started making loud noises and sparking.it was not bent used. Fortunately, we were home to catch this before it caught fire.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was caught before causing injury or fire, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Top rack of dishwasher collapsed onto bottom rack. Upon inspection, the plastic pieces that hold the wheels that slide open and closed had broken off. 

Kenmore Elite dishwasher. Model 12773 K.
justification: The top rack collapsing is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: we have a cuisinart ch-4 food chopper. purchased x-mas 2012. it use is 3-4 times a year. we have noticed that the housing holding  blade is cracked. we thought we should report this do to other cuisinart food choppers being recalled.
justification: The housing holding the blade is cracked, which could lead to an incident, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: We purchased a new Whirlpool Double Oven Range two weeks ago. Within the first few days we found numerous occasions where the knob on the stove was partially turned to the left letting gas escape into the Kitchen.  One one evening the smell was very strong when we walked into the kitchen. After several moments we realized that it was coming from the stove. We had to turn on the ceiling fan to help dissipate the fumes. We know that, on some occasions, one of us apparently brushed up against the knob causing it to turn on. We do not know what happened the  evening the entire kitchen filled with fumes. This is obviously a defect in the product as we have had a stove in this same position for the past 35 years without a single incident.
justification: Gas leakage poses a significant risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death occurred in this incident.

incident_description: Cuisinart Smart Stick hand blender, model #CSB-76.  Exact location of serial number is unclear, but it is probably either 70807 or E143681.  The 3/4 inch long plastic collar surrounding the blade shaft just above the blade itself disintegrated into the food while pureeing well-done steamed cauliflower.  An hour-long phone call to Cuisinart was fruitless.  I was told they would not provide a replacement blade part as the item is out of warranty.  However, they could not even verify which number is the serial number so I have little confidence in their assessment that it is "out of warranty".  Regardless, however, of warranty duration, this is a safety issue.  (I am certain that my food processor from the 1990s is out of warranty, but they are still doing a massive recall when those are disintegrating into food.)  I understand a warranty limitation covering the motor, etc. in my hand blender, but this isn't that kind of issue.  If it just stopped working I wouldn't be notifying Cuisinart and requesting a replacement.  The problem here is that I almost fed my baby food with hard pieces of plastic in it.  Cuisinart should not be so cavalier about this and dismiss my call.  Look where that got them with the food processor blades.  Unbelievable.
justification: The incident involved plastic pieces disintegrating into food, posing a potential safety hazard, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: On 2/28/2017, I walked into my kitchen at 4:00am in the dark and stepped in a pile of glass.  I thought the cats must have somehow knocked over coffee beans.  However, when I turned on the light I saw a pile of glass underneath my  Frigidaire gas oven.  It was completely shattered for no reason.  I rarely use my oven and this was a complete shock.  I contacted Frigidaire and they sent me a link to an oven repair place.  This glass shattered for absolutely no reason.  The glass is defective.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have been using the Soda Stream system for 3 years now.  I recently bought 2 new Soda Stream bottles from Target.  I had put the required amount of water in the bottle and attached it to the Soda Stream machine.  I pumped it 2.5 times and suddenly it exploded. Shards of plastic went everywhere in my kitchen, It cut my hand in several places and the sound was so loud that I lost temporary hearing in my right ear.  It was INCREDIBLY scary.  I have used this system for years and it has been great.  Now I am petrified to try it again.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries (cuts and temporary hearing loss), which qualifies as a severity level 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the user had been using the system safely for years prior.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she has been experiencing ongoing problems with her oven.  The oven interior has expanded causing the racks to collapsed during use or when not in use.  

(12/2016) The manufacturer was contacted but she was advised that the oven is not included in a recall.

Caller feels that this oven is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The oven racks collapsing is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: Kenmore oven front protrudes out all around the glass in door.very dangerous. The knob on the panel for the left front blew out ..sparks then smoke came from panel when I tried to turn burner on. The knob isn't controlling the burner. Blew my breaker box.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the oven panel, indicating a hazardous situation but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Second time. Kenmore range, model 790.97473805. 

Was cooking French fries in oven - 375 degrees F for about 20 minutes when the glass door of the oven exploded, sending shards of hot glass flying as far as 20 feet from the oven. Took about 3 hours to clean up all the glass and it still rains glass from the door every time I touch the oven.

The first time my oven door exploded was November 2015. In that instance I found glass 37 feet from my oven. The exploded glass hit my kitchen island so hard that the glass damaged the wood finish.

The oven is subject to normal use and care. We bought expensive appliances and take exceptionally good care of them. There was absolutely no abuse of this oven.
justification: The incident describes property damage (exploding oven door) but no mention of injury, aligning with severity level 2. The recurrence suggests it's unlikely but not rare.

incident_description:
We purchased all new Samsung appliances for our new construction home that we are building  here in Ohio. My husband was battling cancer and we have been living at our home in Florida. .  So we were building this home from a distance.
I purchased the microwave in September, so it could be installed with the cabinetry. I cannot locate the sales receipt for that appliance.
I have contacted Best Buy and Lowes, which is where we bought most item. Neither place can find a record
Of the transaction. Because we were dealing with purchases in Ohio and Florida, I can't locate the sales slip.
My husband died in Florida on January 18.
I moved into this house on 1.24. I used the microwave, but none of the special features or settings. I just punched in the cook time. Eleven days later the microwave burst into flames while I was heating  an enchilada. The food did not catch on fire, it was a melted plastic panel on the in side of the unit.
The fire department and an independent contractor both felt it was  caused by a defect in the Samsung Microwave .The fire went out , lots of smoke  everywhere. No one was personally injured. I won't know until it is replaced if there is damage to the walls
Samsung Model Number ME21H706MQG
Serial Number OALB7WTH801402W
 Thank you. [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
I will send pictures under a separate email
If that would be helpful.


Sent from my iPhone


Sent from my iPhone
justification: The microwave burst into flames, causing significant smoke and potential property damage, but no personal injury occurred.

incident_description: On 2/15/17 the interior glass of our Whirlpool Oven shattered while in the self clean mode.  This oven is new and this was the first time we used the self clean mode.  The oven did not receive, to our knowledge any prior damage.  The oven had been in this mode for about 1 hour prior the the glass breaking.  We have been using this oven since 11/1/16, when it was installed, new.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering during use, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This dishwasher has very sharp edges on the top inside corner of the door's edge, and when folded down to load or unload, poses a substantial risk of cuts, scrapes and contusions bad enough to warrant stitches: it can slice a layer of skin clear off.
