I have sustained two such injuries while briefly brushing past the folded down door, once on each corner.

Duct tape was placed over the sharp edges, however, this product poses a serious hazard to any household, especially those with small children and should never have been offered in this form.  It should be discontinued until a better and safer design can be created.

The product was purchased from Lowe's Home Improvement in 2015.  
The product information is: KitchenAid MOD: KDTE254ESS1 SER: F54418555 Type 582-2
justification: The description reports injuries severe enough to warrant stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the user sustained injuries twice from brief contact.

incident_description:
My CE electric stove/oven exploded and there was glass everywhere. It was not In use. The glass panel covering the entire oven door exploded.

There are a lot of complaints on the internet and GE says that a hair line crack in the glass can rupture and explode anytime In the future. Perhaps this Is NOT a good design. The moment these products leave the manufacturing process they are moved, pushed. bumped on their way to the distributors  etc.  There is a great potential to explode.  Now what.  I was told by GE that I cannot use the oven without  replacing the entire oven door. That means paying for a new door  shipping & handling and hiring  an appliance technician to install. OR, I can purchase a new stove.  All of these options come close to the cost of a new stove. This appliance should have something else breakdown before the glass starts exploding. GE should make It CLEAR  to consumers that the design of this glass oven door panel is unsafe and will probably explode and should no longer make this design.
justification: The incident involved an oven door explosion causing glass shattering but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The high number of similar complaints suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I came home on Feb 14, 2017 to find that the glass on my oven door had shatteted and landed all over the kitchen floor as well as in the dining room.  The oven was not in use and had not been used in a while as I don't have a lot of people to cook for.  This could have been catastrophic jad anyone been in the kitchen at the time and especially if it was a child or pet!  
Afterwards, I read online that the company GE has been aware of this problem with the glass for several years yet they're stoll selling them.  This is of major concern to me so I wish to report it.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass) but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as the oven was not in use and the issue seems specific to certain models.

incident_description:
I bought a Cuisinart Convection Oven, model # 10B-260N1 to replace another.
I registered the oven online with Cuisinart but when I check my products. Since
they did not respond to my email concerning why my product is not listed as
registered, I did not bring up this safety concern. My previous counter top ovens
had a magnet type device to latch on to the center rack when opening the door.
This oven has 2 hooks; one on each side. They are shaped like a finger box
cutting tool. When the door is closed, they hook onto the rack; when the door
is opened, they pull the rack out. However, these hooks are dangerous in that
when cleaning the door, if one is not careful, one can cut a finger every easily.
 I've nicked myself several times even though I'm aware of these hooks.The manual
does not mention these hooks as safety warnings.
justification: The user reports nicking their fingers several times while cleaning the oven, indicating minor injuries.

incident_description: I own the Cuisinart (model DGB-700BC) 12 cup grind and brew coffee maker. On the day of the incident, I brewed coffee and left the coffee maker on to keep the coffee warm. It has an auto shutoff feature so I usually leave it on without worry. About an hour after I brewed my coffee, I heard the coffee pot moving around and I thought it was my husband moving it. As I walked to the kitchen, I noticed a smell of burning plastic. When I got to the kitchen, I saw the coffee pot bouncing on the coffee maker's warming plate and smoke emanating from around the bottom of the machine. I immediately unplugged the coffee maker and placed it outside. I had to open all of the doors and windows in my house to air out the smell. The smell caused me to gag and gave me a headache and nauseous feeling for the rest of the day. After this incident, I searched online to see if other customers have reported similar incidents. There are many reviews online of people reporting the same experience that I had. Cuisinart has offered to replace my coffee maker since it is still within the limited warranty period. I have had this coffee maker for 1 year and 1 month and for $180 I expected it to last longer and not attempt to burn my house down. I am worried I will have the same experience with the replacement since customers have also reported that their replacement coffee makers also burned out. I think this item is a fire hazard and needs to be recalled in order for Cuisinart to investigate the issue of this particular model's affinity to start smoking. I am honestly surprised this item has not already been recalled given the number of reports of this coffee maker smoking and burning out. It seems to me like Cuisinart has chosen to ignore the complaints in the interest of profits.
justification: The incident caused physical symptoms (headache, nausea) and posed a fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: Pyrex baking dish 9"x13" was being used in my oven on 425 degrees to bake chicken breasts. 20 minutes in to a 30 minute recipe the baking dish exploded into millions of pieces with a very loud bang. When I opened the door I saw glass pieces everywhere and chicken juice and glass on the bottom of the oven.
justification: The baking dish exploded, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: The Ge oven I have had for 5 years glass door shattered. I placed the oven in a self cleaning mode and the glass shattered. I barely cook and use the oven so this should not happen.
justification: The oven glass shattered during use, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We had been away on vacation for several weeks. When we returned, we found that our Frigidaire range/stove was malfunctioning in a dangerous way. The stove and all its knobs were clearly turned to" off" (no, we did not leave the
Stove on!), but the large front left burner was flaming red hot, hotter than I had ever seen it! I tried to "turn off" the burner by wiggling the appropriate knob, but the burner get kept getting hotter and hotter. Because I could not get the burner to turn off, my husband had to go down and turn off the breaker to power down the stove. We left the breaker off all night.

When we got up in the morning, I asked him to reset the breaker so we could see what happened. Again, the knobs were all in the "off" position. As soon as the breaker was turned on, the burner again became a flaming red hot, and it could not be turned off. We just turned off the breaker and unplugged the stove!

This is extremely dangerous, and we are just thankful that this stove did not burn our house down while we were away!!!
justification: The stove malfunctioned dangerously but no injury or death occurred, only potential for property damage.

incident_description: just got done cooking dinner in my wolf oven. shut the oven off and about 10 minutes later the glass door shattered
justification: The oven door shattered, which could potentially cause injury from broken glass.

incident_description: Was cooking dinner on the stove and it caught fire.  Fire department was called out but we had put the fire out.
justification: The stove caught fire, but it was extinguished without injury, qualifying as an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Our microwave oven, LG model LCRT2010ST purchased 1.5 years ago from Home Depot, started on its own with nothing in it.  We called LG customer service and were told to unplug the unit, wait 30 sec, replug it and push STOP to reset the control panel.  We did this but the problem recurred.  In a variant of the problem, the unit also periodically started over the past two days when the door was simply closed but before the keypad was pushed. We recontacted LG but they were not helpful.  Our warranty expired a few months ago, so we are out of luck.

There was no power outage associated with this behavior.  

We are disposing of the microwave because it is a fire hazard.  The unit is a counter top model that we had installed in a cherry cabinet in our kitchen.  Had this oven started on its own while we were away, it could have started a house fire.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned without causing injury, but posed a potential fire hazard, warranting disposal.

incident_description: I want cooking dinner tonight and had just turned around to get some some additional ingredients to add to what I was cooking on the oven top when I head this VERY loud explosive sound. When I turned around the oven door on the oven had blown open. It opened it all the way as if you pulled it down to put something really big into it. The glass was still intact but the explosion was so loud my ears are still ringing. I don't feel safe using this appliance any longer. If I had been in front of the door, I would have had some bad injuries. Thankfully I was not. Later we now discovered even though the oven was turned off it continued to stay on at the temperature (350 degrees) our dinner was cooking.
justification: The oven door blew open with a loud explosion, but no injuries occurred. The incident could have caused injuries if someone had been in front of the door.

incident_description: This was a Christmas present so I really do not have details about where it was bought . I have used it one time and I saw a piece of metal in my food.
justification: A piece of metal in food is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our Kitchen Aid stovetop blew up shattering the glass of the exhaust hood and sending shards of glass and ceramic 25 feet down the hall and into other rooms.  How my daughter, who had simply tried to turn on a gas burner was not shredded is a miracle. She suffered a small cut but emotionally was truly shaken.
justification: The incident caused physical injury (a small cut) and significant emotional distress, warranting a severity level of 3. Such events are rare but possible, hence an occurrence likelihood of 3.

incident_description: I was starting to use the microwave. While setting the minutes on the microwave the panel surrounding the keypad and clock fell and scratched my right hand.
justification: The incident resulted in a scratch, which qualifies as an injury, but no further harm was reported.

incident_description: KNIFE HANDLE BROKE WHILE USEING PREPARING FOOD.  SAFETY HAZARD OF CUTTING HAND.  BLADE CAME OUT OF HANDLE AND HANDLE BROKE AT INSERTION POINT.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard with potential for injury, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that for about a year now, the microwave will start on by itself at least once or twice a month immediately after the consumer shuts the door. The consumer states that once she opens and closed the microwave door it will shut off. The consumer states that she has only noticed it turn on once after use, never more than once.

The consumer states that for the past month the unit starts beeping approximately two minutes after she has already removed her food out of the microwave as if indicating that the food is ready. Although this does not occur every time, the consumer estimates it happens about once every three times the microwave is turned on.

The consumer states that she uses her unit on average at least once a day. The consumer plans on keeping the unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The microwave turns on by itself occasionally and beeps after use, but there is no report of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that range come on if the knobs are touched accidently but the gas does not ignite. This causes a gas smell in the home.

The consumer stated that it has been an issue since he purchased the product. The most recent incident happened about two week ago.


The consumer contacted the firm. He was advised that there is no recall on the product.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage without ignition, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury. The issue is recurring, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: While preheating the oven to 350 degrees F the oven door was opened in a regular fashion.  Upon opening the door, the front door glass burst outward and shattered toward the person opening the glass and onto the floor.  We keep a hand towel on the front handle of the oven semi covering the glass.  This towel as well as wearing long pants and socks prevented any injury from occurring to the person opening the oven door.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but no injury occurred due to protective measures like a towel and clothing.

incident_description: My wife was baking a pie in our Kenmore double oven. The ovens have double pane glass and the outer glass of the upper oven exploded. Luckily she was not injured as she had her back to the oven. First she heard cracking then it threw the safety glass onto the floor, and surprisingly, ejecting some glass into the sink and across the counter. It literally exploded.
justification: The oven glass exploded but no one was injured, as the person had her back to the oven.

incident_description:
Samsung has a serious safety problems with its electric range Model # FE710DRS and are doing nothing about it.  This was an expensive electric double range, $1,329.00 plus taxes and extended warranty.  
After successfully using its ÃÂsteamÃÂ cleaning cycle many times I noticed several spots that would not come clean and decided to use the regular ÃÂcleaningÃÂ cycle which takes more time.
During that cycle we noticed a strange smell but the instructions say that normal due to high heat used during this cycle.  I let the oven cool and wiped it out with a towel dampened with plain water.
Two days before Christmas I set the oven to 350 degrees preheat and prepared to bake a chicken.  Within five minutes I heard a loud explosion within the oven, I was standing 2 feet away when this occurred.  Thick black smoke began rolling from behind the range and into the kitchen.
I ran to our electric circuit (fuse) panel and turned the breaker to the oven off.  We pulled the smoldering oven away from the tiled backsplash (tiled all the way down to the floor) to find it was so hot it scorched the tile.  We also found the oven melted the counter top on one side! 
I called SamsungÃÂs 800 number.  We talked daily for two weeks while they ÃÂresearchedÃÂ the problem.   They even sent a repairman to access the damage.  He said the oven needed two control boards and a new wiring harness installed to further access damage as other parts also showed scorching damage.  This would cost over $550 in parts (plus labor) and effectively means the range is a total loss.  I was told that Samsung corporate will get back to you.
After countless phone conversations over a two week period (many of the calls were Samsung calling me) a curt representative called to say that it was no longer under SamsungÃÂs initial 12 month warranty and they will not cover repair or replacement.  If they had told us in the beginning we could have replaced the stove sooner.  We used a microwave oven and a hot plate to cook during the holidays.
I researched this model on the internet and found its serious safety complaints.  WeÃÂre not alone with our fire caused by this model range.  I canÃÂt believe a large company with an obvious safety problem would act in such a manner.
Samsung currently has many problematic appliances on the market.  Everything built by humans and can have problems.  How a company handles those problems builds their future market.
For the safety of families Samsung should recall this model.  We could have lost everything due to their faulty appliance and they donÃÂt even care!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion and fire hazard with no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple similar complaints found online.

incident_description:
I have a set of CorningWare Etch casserole dishes, purchased in Tempe, AZ Feb 1, 2012.  

On January 23, 2017 I took a casserole dish from the cupboard, placed chicken thighs in the dish, covered it with the lid and placed it in the oven at 300F.  About 5 minutes later I heard the sound of glass breaking.  Since there was no one in the kitchen at the time, both my husband and I were confused by this.  

Upon investigation, we discovered the lid of the casserole dish had exploded in the oven.  Fortunately, the mess was confined to the oven, and the drawer below.  We were able to clean up the mess and dispose of everything once the oven had cooled.  

The potential for this to cause serious injury has made me reluctant to use the remaining pieces of this set.
justification: The incident involved a casserole dish lid exploding in the oven, but no injuries occurred. The mess was contained within the oven and cleaned up safely.

incident_description:
The very heavy metal refrigerator door handle of the Fisher Paykal Refrigerato fell off and nearly hit one of our family members on the foot.

Fisher Paykal Refrigerator
Serial Number: AUQ843068
Model #: 522BRE

The refrigerator handle fell off. This handle is heavy and it is metal. It also has sharp ends.
Fortunately the handle did not hurt my daughter's foot or damage my floor.
Fortunately a small child did not encounter a dangerous injury. This handle is long and it looks like a weapon. If it falls onto a small child's head or an elderly person's foot it could cause serious injury or worse. 

This product should be recalled if it is still being manufactured. It is very dangerous.

Fisher Paykal will not take any responsibility for this hazard and they are unresponsive
to my requests for resolution. They say the refrigerator is 8 years old and this is what happens after the one year warranty. I find that response to be irresponsible.
justification: The heavy metal refrigerator door handle fell off but did not cause injury, though it had the potential to cause serious harm.

incident_description: Elite Platinum electric kettle by Maxi-Matic Product: Kettle Model: EKT-200 Number 0815 electrical short melted bottom of kettle and plug in base. While operating I smelled melting plastic and kettle was source. This is second incident with this kettle. I had to return for exchange the first one due to water leaking out of kettle base.
justification: The incident involved an electrical short and melting plastic, but no injury was reported. This is the second occurrence with the same kettle model.

incident_description: Our Cuisinart Burr Grind & Brew Coffeemaker, DGB-700 BC, burnt this morning.  It had brewed 10 cups and had some coffee in the pot on the warmer.  It made gurgling noises and started to smoke.  It smelled like burned plastic.  We unplugged it and it kept smoking from under the warmer plate and then the other areas for several minutes after it was unplugged.  There was visible smoke in the kitchen and the counter under it was hot.
justification: The coffeemaker emitted smoke and had a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Whirlpool model #GU2500XTPS3 Serial #FS2812861 began smoking out the top of the unit.  Unit would not shut down until the breaker was thrown.  Strong electrical burning smell from the unit.
justification: The incident involved smoking and a burning smell, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
1) Found sharp, jagged piece of plastic 1/8" x 1/2" inside ice cube dispensed from ice maker into my drinking-cup. Lucky to have seen it before I swallowed it and was injured. Under warranty Whirlpool replaced ice maker at no charge.

2) Year later found sharp, jagged plastic 1/8" x 7/8" inside ice cube dispensed from newly installed ice maker. Lucky to have seen it before accidently drinking it.

3) After many phone calls over the passed few months - Maytag/Whirlpool 1-800-688-9900 and Whirlpool's designated service co., via factory service 1-410-451-4104, Maytag trust keepers, Benson Harbor 1-866-526-7969, Maytag's online survey complaint, and also finding add'l sharp pieces in ice cubes, I find customer service to be oblivious to the danger this defective ice maker presents, along w/ great inconvenience it causes me. 

I request a satisfactory solution to correcting this problematic ice maker that has the potential to cause choking - especially in my grandchildren.
justification: Sharp plastic pieces were found in ice cubes multiple times, posing a risk of injury if swallowed, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
3 month old GE Stove JGBS60REKSS has dangerous burner knobs. Merely brushing against the knobs can turn burners on releasing gas.Usually, I've smelled it and turned it off. It has happened often enough that I routinely check the knobs before leaving the house. 

The other morning I was cooking a pan of eggs on the back burner and had a deli package of cheese by the front burner. I must have brushed the front knob, but was busy & distracted and didn't notice the gas smell. The flame from the back burner must have ignited the front. There was a sudden sound and burst of flames. I was right there, didn't get burnt and it was okay.

I worry that the same thing could happen when I'm not at the stove, possibly when something is cooking for a long time on the simmer burner. 

I feel that GE should replace the knobs with others that require some effort to turn on.
justification: The incident resulted in a burst of flames but no injury, and the user has taken precautions to prevent recurrence.

incident_description: Waring Convection Oven would not turn off.  On/off light indicated off when we were finished baking but after two hours when we went back to the kitchen the oven was still on and extremely hot to the touch and both elements were bright red.  We tried to turn it off at the on/off button but oven continued to heat at max temp.  We unplugged it and are not using it now.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but was unplugged before causing injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
I was given this coffee maker as a Christmas gift Dec 25th, 2013 by my daughter. As a college student on a budget she remembers buying it at Big Lots in Chandler AZ.  Warner and Alma School roads.

We awoke to our kitchen on fire 3:30 a.m.on Jan 23rd.2017.  The Coffee maker completely melted down after it burst into flames and filled our home with toxic black smoke. I have a fire extinguisher to put out the flames, it cracked our granite counter and burned the cabinet.  at 4 in the morning, I went through the attic and every cabinet to insure the fire hadn't snuck into the attic. A week of an ozone generator and ran for the week to remove the smell, washed the soot off everything. it was awful

I thought it was a [REDACTED] product and sent them photos. They returned my email quickly and explained it wasn't their product. The investigator said he knew of this Signature Gourmet and was normally only sold through Walgreen's.  We were able to find the recall notice online from 2009 that the unit would burst into  flames. The company is now out of business.   Big Lots is often selling discount and closeout items.  I can't believe they would make a simple recall check before selling in their stores, 4 years after it was recalled and discontinued from the manufacturer.  Another 5 minutes and I could have lost my home.   How can you help me?
justification: The coffee maker caused a fire, resulting in property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Oven glass external door exploded & shattered
justification: The oven glass door exploded and shattered, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
1/13/17 bought a sharp model R-551ZM microwave. it worked great! for about 2 weeks. 1/31/17 i heated 1 cup of coffee, and it went well. when i tried to heat a second cup, immediately after the first, the interior light did not come on, and the front control panel was not lit. i smelled something that was electrical, maybe melting plastic... you know it when you smell it. my brother took it out of the cabinet and i unplugged it, then plugged it back in. it instantly got hot in his hands, on one side and the bottom. too hot to hold. we unplugged it and returned it that day, to sam's club. brought home the same model and used it for about 10 days. the same thing happened yesterday. the exact same thing!!! i was home alone with my 75 year old mother. i was able to get it out of the cabinet and it was too hot to touch on the side that is behind the control panel.  we plan to take it back to sam's club, but they didn't really care that there is a problem. i called sharp, too, and they didn't seem to care. told me to call back and ask for customer satisfaction.  i would be satisfied if i didn't feel like i was going to burn to death. i would have a hard time trying to get my disabled mother out, if this thing starts a fire. 

this happens to one unit, it's bad luck. it happens two times within two weeks, there is a problem with the manufacturing of this device.  the date of manufacture, on each, is oct 2016.
justification: The microwave became dangerously hot but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue happened twice in a short period, suggesting a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: I used the self clean mode for the first time on my GE Profile wall oven that is less than a year old. The entire inside glass of door shattered. It shattered in shards instead of smooth pebbles that is supposed to be industry safety standards.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Washing my [slow cooker] and it hit the back of the sink and exploded with glass flying all over my kitchen and even into the next room cutting my left hand with deep lacerations needing 13 stitches.  I could understand if hitting the sink and counter from a close range if it cracked and broke but it was like it exploded.  There had to be some type of defect to cause the severity of shattering of the base of the crockpot.  It was at room temperature and no known cracks, etc.
justification: The incident resulted in deep lacerations requiring 13 stitches, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: I have a GE electric glass top oven that when I turned it on to warm up the whole front glass door exploded and blasted glass everywhere. I was at sink and my pets were standing in front of oven when it exploded they appear to be OK I screamed it was really scary! I contacted GE they said they will send someone out to look at it to determine if it is a safety issue or not and it isn't under warranty.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported to the person or pets.

incident_description:
I made chili in my Cuisinart electric pressure cooker. I understand how to use it and had used it before. When the chili was done, I released the steam/pressure with the release valve until it was no longer steaming. I released the valve a second time to check that all pressure was released. I twisted the lid to open it (and I did not have to force the lid) and boiling hot chili exploded all over my arm, chest and our brand new kitchen. It was under so much pressure, the contents spewed onto the ceiling, cupboards, and across the room as well. I immediately began first aid as I am a RN, but still sustained deep second degree burns requiring weeks of medical care and ending in large scarring on my forearm. 
Emails (x3) and phone calls (x2, where I spoke with a representative) resulted in no contact for the company. I am concerned others will be injured as well!!
justification: The incident resulted in deep second-degree burns requiring weeks of medical care, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the user's experience and the device's apparent failure despite proper use.

incident_description:
Last night I was cooking chicken thighs in a rectangle Pyrex Glass Baking Dish. I heard a noise and opened the door to find the dish had exploded. 

This is really really dangerous and something I had never thought could happen. I was blessed that it happened before I opened the door!
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, which is a dangerous incident, but no injury occurred as the person was not in the immediate vicinity when it happened.

incident_description: This electric range has large knobs on the front, right about waist height.  It is installed near a corner of the counter tops in our kitchen in an area where the coffee maker, food processor and toaster are located.  In other words.  an active area where a lot of moving back and forth takes place during meal preparation.  It is very easy to brush the knobs with a turn of the hip and turn burners on.  The knob is silent in its operation so there is no warning that a burner is about to glow red hot.  The possibilities of catching something on fire or being burned are real.  This is our second stove of this same model.  The first was returned under the lemon law rules due to a problem with the clock not keeping time.  The first stove also would turn on unexpectedly by brushing past the knobs.  We installed that stove in the fall of 2015.  The second one was delivered summer of 2016.  We told our Sear's salesman who was able to replicate the problem on the show room floor by brushing past the knobs.  It happened several times on the first stove until we removed the knobs when not in use.  The second one has had the same problem and it has happened several times since it was installed,  Including today.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue where burners are accidentally turned on, posing a real risk of fire or burns, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range
Model #: 79092202017
Purchased: 02/25/2013

While using the broiler to toast English muffins, a very loud buzzing sound occurred (which was heard throughout the house) and flames shot out of the oven. Oven door was immediately shut and broiler turned off. Smoke filled the kitchen and smoke alarms went off. Inspecting the oven for the cause, the range broiler element was melted and broken apart approximately three inches from where it connects at the back of the oven. The inside of oven was covered in a burnt film.
- A replacement range broiler element (Part #: 316203301) was installed. 
- Upon plugging the range back into electrical outlet, a fire immediately occurred in the top/back portion of the range in the oven control panel area.
- The range was immediately unplugged and the fire continued to burn for another minute and then went out.
- Disassembly of the top/back panel was done to view damage and the control panel was blackened and burnt where the flames were.
-- No further attempts to repair this range were attempted as it no longer seemed to be a safe appliance.--
Reviewing recalls for Kenmore Electric Ranges showed similar incidents with other models, just not the model we have ... which is why I am reporting this now.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries or deaths were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the immediate fire upon reconnection and similar recalls for other models.

incident_description:
I turned my oven on to 350 degrees.
It was empty.
About 10 minutes into the warming cycle 
I started hearing a pop pop pop crackle sound and heavy black smoke started spewing from behind the range.
The smell of an electrical fire and black smoke was thick throughout the house.
After evacuating and

The wiring of the range was toasted and had melted.
The range is a complete loss.

incident_description: Frigidair cooktop stove Model FEC30S6ABF - one of the ranges does not turn off when switched off. It requires turning off at the circuit breaker. This has happened intermittently since 2011 and has gotten worse over the years. It used to turn off when repeatedly turning the knob all the way around from low to high to off. Most recently his spouse had placed something on the range which was wrapped in butcher paper, she reached for something and brushed against the knob without her knowledge.  She then noticed that there were flames emitting from the burner where she had placed the object.  He stated that he immediately use a lid cover to extinguish the fire. Consumer feels that this range is unsafe and should be reported.

incident_description:
Product: GE XL44 oven
Model Number: JGBS21HED3WW
Serial Number: SD??3258P

Problem: The knobs for the burners are too easy to turn on resulting in unburned gas leaking if knob is bumped.  This has happened twice since I moved into the house I am renting. One time, I knocked it while cleaning the stove top (not the knobs), and another...I'm not sure how, but it was terrifying to come into my home an hour later and find the entire upstairs smelling of natural gas. 

Other gas stoves I have had in the past are not so easy to turn the knobs on to let the gas out. To light my current stove you have to turn the knob all the way to the left, whereas other stoves light when the knob is *barely* turned to the left. 

I'm just really worried that it's way too easy to accidentally leak gas. :o/

incident_description: Purchased Snapware Total Solution 18-pc Glass Food Storage Set from Costco in 2016. First noticed a chip off of edge/lip of container and noticed shard of glass in container.  Threw it out as a fluke as Pyrex should never chip! This has now happened 4-5 times with this set where glass chips/shards are breaking off, sometimes staying in lid. Often times you don't find it until you are eating food. Upon researching other reviews, there appear to be similar reports on Amazon.com. Thankfully I have not consumed a piece of glass yet and am throwing out the set and attempting to return to Costco.
justification: Glass chipping has occurred multiple times, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: Sometime in early 2000's I purchased a Thermador cooktop model PCS366US along with other appliances when I redid my kitchen. Since then I have replaced several spark electrodes (part number Bosch 415124) since they crack easily and they need to be in one piece in order function properly and to use the gas burners safely.  As they are fragile porcelain and frequently crack in half they were in need of expensive labor and replacement charges yet now it has gotten to the point where I can not have service on the cooktop because the part is no longer manufactured by Bosch or anyone else and I have gone through extensive search for a replacement parts and none are available. At one point the gas flame was able to be turned on using a match and the burner would function just fine, however inconvenient that was at least it was possible. Now it has gotten to the point where of the electrodes has now completely broke off and nothing is in it's place therefore deeming that burner useless. I can still turn on a flame with a match but then it becomes a safety concern because the absence of the electrode has a safety feature that has the unit click and the clicking signifies a gas leak, this was intended to be a safety feature so ignoring it is not a good idea. And it is only a matter of time that all the electrodes will break off. Last I checked, there was one of these electrodes available on ebay for aprox $180, although this part is normally between $10-15, I would have taken a chance making the purchase but I would still have a problem the next time around because as I mentioned, this is a fragile porcelain part. Is there any regulations in the industry to prevent the need to replace appliances due to discontinuance of parts? These appliances are not inexpensive that, they should be changed out every decade.
justification: The incident involves a safety concern due to a broken electrode causing a gas leak warning, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: I have a set of 12 Ikea glasses, 12 oz Pokal, made in Bulgaria. I was in my kitchen when I heard a loud sound of shattered glass. I could not immediately find the breakage. incident_description:
We have had several issues with our Ninja 3 in 1 Cooking System. The first issue occurred a few weeks ago when the machine turned on by itself. The machine was set to Off since we were done using it. There was no food in it at this time. When we came back to it later we realized it was hot and was heating on a high setting although the dial was set to Off and the display screen was blank. 
The second incident involved the machine restarting the cook time instead of turning to the auto warm setting. We set the timer to cook overnight for eight hours at approximately 7 p.m. When we woke up at 6 a.m. we saw that the timer had restarted and was showing that there was an additional 4.5 hours of cook time left. 
The third incident occurred yesterday January 18 2017. We were cooking with a friend so we both started our crock pot timers at the same time. Several hours later we noticed that the timer on our unit was behind so the food was going to cook for longer than it should even if the machine turned to auto warm at the end of the timer. 
We do not plan to use this machine any longer because we are concerned that it is a fire or a burn hazard since it turns on by itself and the cook setting does not turn off. 
We contacted Shark Ninja about the problem on January 6 2017 via email (They asked for us to send additional information such as the model number. After they received that information they replied back on January 19 2017 and stated that they could not assist us. They told us to contact the Customer Service Department at 18776465288. 
We called the Customer Service Department on January 19 2017. They stated that they have not heard of the problem but when we searched online we found several online complaints regarding the machine turning on by itself. These complaints were posted on amazon.com and saferproducts.gov. The customer service representative offered to send a new unit at a discounted price of 87.00 with free shipping. While we were on the phone with him we let him know that Walmart had the unit on sale for 89.10.
justification: The incidents describe malfunctions that could pose a burn or fire hazard, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
We had the authorized service company (Anova) out last night to look at our Freestanding Viking Range and the problem appears to be far worse than we had originally thought.  After thorough analysis, it turns out that, since the oven was delivered, the spark wire for the oven intermittently sparks through the insulator against the oven wall rather than in the spark module.  This is why the gas in the oven comes on when there is no spark.  This also poses an extreme hazard as there are thousands of volts flowing through the case of the oven, with the case of the oven acting as ground.  This can cause electrocution or fire and is extremely dangerous.  After this finding, it was concluded that the oven cannot be used.  Anova inspected everything and all connections, wires and insulators appeared fine, it was actually sparking through the big black insulator on the wire.  Anova took a video and I am assuming they will send it to you, if not, we have one we can send.  

Secondly, the circuit board that controls the oven is corroded.   Liquid leaked from the top surface and caused the broiler to self-ignite, the cleaning cycle come on for no reason, and the burners to stop working.  According to the Consumer Product Safety Commission, this is the exact problem the recall was supposed to fix, and it obviously didn't.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with potential for electrocution or fire, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

Whirlpool Built-In Single Electric Oven, Model #RBS305PDB-CRACKED INTERIOR GLASS OVEN WINDOW

I had to buy a new Whirlpool Built-In Single Electric Oven, Model #RBS305PDB, to replace the existing  inoperative Whirlpool Built-In oven. This oven has 1) AccuBake Advanced Temperature Management System 2) Self-Cleaning Oven with Auto Self-Clean Latch 3) EZ-Touch 300 Electronic Controls with Control Lockout and 4) Large Oven Window

1) Selected temperature (oven had been temp calibrated) does not produce the expected results.  Therefore, we had to adjust the temperature different than a recipe recommended. 

2) The biggest and most dangerous & serious issues of this oven is the Self-Cleaning/ Lockout Latch feature. 
       a. When using the Self-Cleaning feature the surrounding cabinets & counter area became extremely hot to the point where I could not touch them.  

       b.  The ovens interior glass oven window cracked after using this Self-Cleaning feature.  I followed the directions of use for Self-Cleaning.  Now I have a broken, fairly new built-in oven.

I purchased my Jenn-Air Electric Downdraft Range on December 16, 2016 and it was installed a few days later.  About one month later, on January 22, 2017, after preparing a dinner and having the oven on at 425 degrees, we were finishing dinner when we heard a strange, loud popping noise coming from the oven.  Not daring to open the oven, I could see through the oven door that glass was shattering inside the oven.  Over a period of several hours, the inner glass continued to shatter and fall to the bottom of the oven.  The next day, my 11 month old Labrador Retriever was in the kitchen and discovered some small shards of glass on the floor beneath the oven. She ate a couple of small pieces before I could get to her and then vacuum up the remaining glass that had somehow come out of the oven on to the floor.  I have not opened the oven door at all since we heard the initial popping sounds, so I am not sure how the glass escaped the oven.  I estimate that there was about 1/2 tsp to 1 tsp of glass on the floor.
I contacted Ferguson Enterprises, Inc. where I bought my range and they contacted Whirlpool, the manufacturer of the Jenn-Air Range.  Whirlpool is refusing to replace my month-old range that I paid $3,413.25 for, but wants to send a repair company out to look at it and try to fix it rather than replace it.  I think this is unacceptable and am very concerned about the safety of this oven!!!  The repair company tells me that the glass piece that they believe is needed is on back order and they did not give  me a time frame of when it would be available if I was to have it fixed.  Please help!

incident_description:
This is about:

     AMBIANO 5 QT. Programmable Slow Cooker

     Model Number LY-5000DE

     Distributed By ALDI Inc., Batavia, IL.

The support structure on the bottom side of the unit consists of three(3) very small feet. Modest pressure applied to the left or right rear rim of the unit will cause the unit to tip.I used the word modest to give a sense of the situation, but it shouldn't matter as a unit like this full of hot materials should absolutely not tip at all under any circumstance.
 
Further, I filled the unit with 6 Qts of 57 degree tap water and chose the High setting which causes the unit to stay on for 6 hours.

The temp. of the water at 3 hours had not reached a temp of 150 degrees F which is below safe food temp.

During this time the surface or outer skin was at times higher than the internal temp.

By the sixth hour the internal temp had finally reached 195 degrees and the external temp. exceeded 166 degrees. 

As we understand it, thermal burn can start as low as 140 degrees. This is, of course, dependent of exposure time. It seems that 166 degrees would be of danger to small children and pets.

The ceramic pot appears to be suspended above the heated base unit. This would seem to account, in part at least, for the lengthy heating time of the contents and the high surface temp.of the outer skin of the unit.

Thank you!
justification: The incident describes potential thermal burns due to high surface temperatures, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the conditions for burns are present but not guaranteed.

incident_description:
I was using the slicing blade on my Cuisinart food processor.  Suddenly the machine shuddered and I can only describe what happened inside the bowl as an implosion.  The stem had broken--therefore pieces of its plastic, a spring, and of course the slicing blade flew around the bowl.  The bowl contained the debris but was itself broken.

The stem on this model is curved, and the slicing and shredding blades have a weight on them to counterbalance the curve in the stem.  I believe it is this curved stem that is the cause of the implosion.  All food processors I have looked at since the incident (including Cuisinart models on the market now) have straight stems.  I believe this model was unwisely engineered and then made on the cheap, though not sold on the cheap.,

Customer Service at Cuisinart was interested only in selling me replacement stem and bowl.  They never acknowledged my concern about the safety of their product.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure causing debris to scatter inside the bowl, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On the night of December 21, 2016- (our second time using the Farberware 4 Liter Deep Fryer experienced no problem the first time we used the deep fryer) we decided to deep fry breaded shrimp in the Farberware 4 Liter Deep fryer. We filled the unit up to the maximum level line with [REDACTED] Vegetable oil. As per the instructions we set the temperature setting to 350 degrees and turned the unit on.
Soon after, a sickening smell/odor (like burning metal) spread throughout our entire house ÃÂ My eyes began to burn, my head began to hurt, and I felt nauseated. My wife who has asthma was sitting well away from our kitchen in our living room and complained that it was hard for her to breathe.


We turned the unit off and tried to get rid of the sickening odor, but to no avail. We could not get rid of the odor throughout our entire house.  The next morning, I checked the set of  [REDACTED] FPR 10air filters (which I had installed on December 9, 20 16) located at the far end of our house. The air filters bad turned black (see enclosed picture). I went to Home Depot, purchased another set of air filters, and replaced the discolored black [REDACTED] FPR 10 air filters.

My wife and I left the house for the holidays. When we returned I checked the new air filters.
This time the set of [REDACTED] air filters had turned charcoal gray.
Before replacing another set of [REDACTED] FPR air filters, we called for our heating and air service man. Two days later, he came out and witnessed the 2 sets of discolored air filters. The sight of the discolored air filters puzzled him. He checked our heating and cooling unit. He found nothing wrong. (We were charged $67.29 for a service call). He could not determine what could have caused the air filters to discolor. He suggested we call an air quality expert for help. I have kept both sets of discolored air filters. I have reinstalled another set of [REDACTED] FPR air filters (FPR 10) on January 9, 2017. There has been no discoloration. To this day, my wife is still having trouble with her breathing.

Since the time of our bad experience with the Farberware 4 Liter Deep fryer my wife has had problems breathing and has experienced an asthma attack. She visited the pulmonary specialist once ( December 28, 20 16) and was given a prescription which has done very little to help her breathe better and has had a second prescription called in. She continues to cough and use a prescription inhaler. The Pulmonary specialist saw the pictures of the air filters and commented on them stating that "it was very interesting".

Before I replaced the second set of [REDACTED] air filters and determined to fmd out what could have caused the [REDACTED] air filters to discolor- I contacted [REDACTED] on January 7, 2017 and asked for their opinion. [REDACTED] answered me on January 10, 2017. I have enclosed their answer find their response to be very interesting. In the response from [REDACTED], an air specialist stated that the cause for the discoloration was a heavy metal captured by the air filters; He also stated that this could be signs of a Teflon coating burning off the coils of the unit which could and is hazardous to one's health. He also stated that Farberware is known to coat internal parts with Teflon. He also stated for us to stop using the Deep Fryer.

On the last page of the Farberware 4 Liter Owner's Manual there is a word of caution paragraph that clearly states that the deep fryer may give off an odor and emit smoke-- also stating that this is normal.

Enclosed you will find pictures of the discolored air filters and our response from [REDACTED].
Also, in the reviews of the deep fryer a customer states that they have experienced the same problem the second time just as we have experienced the problem the second time we used the deep fryer.
justification: The incident caused health issues including breathing problems and asthma attacks, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurred on the second use and is corroborated by another customer, suggesting it is possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
The unsafe product is a Kitchen-Aid 30" Gas Range (http://www.kitchenaid.com/shop/major-appliances-1/ranges-2/slide-in-3/-[KSGG700ESS]-408407/KSGG700ESS/).
On several occasions (10 or more), myself or a family member has brushed against the range (for normal purposes such as accessing the microwave oven above, reaching into a nearby cupboard, or simply working on the counter space near the appliance) and accidentally turned one of the knobs thereby turning on the gas. Only after eventually smelling gas do we realize that the gas is on. 
As mentioned above, this has happened on several occasions to the point that I believe it is not just a random mishap. If I remember correctly, on one occasion, I came home to the smell of gas believing that I or someone may have bumped the knob(s) before leaving for work, and not knowing how long the gas has been on, I was extremely scared for the safety of my family and pets. 
This just happened again promoting this report. I am going to search for safety covers but believe I have bought some in the past and they did not fit.
Not sure what to do next.
justification: The incident involves accidental gas leaks due to knob activation, posing a potential safety hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The Kenmore unit 790 92303012 caught fire when we turned the unit on.
Flames were high and could not be put off until we killed the breaker and vented the whole are.
After unplugging the unit and pulling the unit out we noticed that the electronic board at the top of the unit had caught fire.  Behind our unit we had tile and above we had the microwave so nothing else caught fire otherwise there would have been extensive damage.
The units had burned out the last prong on the unit was charred from the fire it looked like the thermal switch was the culprit in this instance also.

incident_description: We purchased a Whirlpool micro/oven wall unit 10/2011 to complete a kitchen remodel.  Model mmw7530wdw01.   The baking oven was used very little.  Upon selecting the oven clean mode and walking away....suddenly, minutes later the outer oven door glass exploded.  This occurred 8/8/16.  I've tried unsuccessfully to locate a replacement part for this $2300.00 boat anchor I currently have sitting in my garage to no avail and now I recently found out they no longer supply the part that I had ordered.  At first I was told that the Whirlpool warehouse was out of stock and that the projected delivery date was 10/13/16; I called the parts dealer and was then told to expect it around 12/31/16.  Again, I called back after Jan.1 and was told that the part was no longer available?  I am currently waiting on a refund from the parts dealer.   After numerous checks online, I see that every other part for this unit is available along with a glass replacement for a unit that came in black and in stainless steel but No glass is available for the micro/oven they manufactured in white!  Not only will I boycott ALL Whirlpool appliances but I am currently speaking with an attorney that is willing to file a class action regarding their defective product as soon as a list of possible plaintiffs is complied.  I think that it is utterly ridiculous that a company as large as Whirlpool can suspend parts that have had a problem with breakage throughout the country and I'm sure abroad and have not been required to have a recall on these defective items or at least make the replacement/repair part available.  Thank You.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass exploding, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
I purchased an electric range (Model No. JB630DF4BB; Seriel No. HF248713Q) in May of 2016.  On New Year's eve I set the over to clean according to the instructions, and in approximately 1.5 hours, the exterior glass to the over shattered all over the kitchen floor and surrounding areas.  I've been in touch with GE and they sent a repairman who explained that since it is out of warranty the service call and part will not be covered.  I explained that the same thing happened to one of my coworkers several years ago.  He told me to contact the GE representative to discuss it.  I've just heard back from the GE Rep. and she stated that she forwarded the information to the Safety Department and they determined that it was not a "safety issue" and it would not be covered.  I tried to explain that this wasn't just a thermostat gone bad but that glass shattered all over a room and luckily no one was in the room at the time (especially a small child) or someone most definitely would have gotten hurt.

Any assistance you could provide would be greatly appreciated.

Mariann
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no injuries, and the likelihood is considered possible based on the description of a similar past incident.

incident_description:
Glass on Microwave Oven Door Shattered:
This microwave was a replacement microwave oven provided (and installed) by GE during a service call to my residence approximately one to one and a half years ago. The first microwave oven (was less than a year old) and was malfunctioning but under warranty and was replaced.  The replacement oven was manufactured in December of 2014.  

On January 23, 2017 my wife went to use the microwave to reheat food.  This was in the morning and the microwave had not been used since the following night.  She proceeded to open the door of the empty microwave when the glass on the front door shattered into tiny little pieces.  Some of this glass exploded outward and into the kitchen.  The microwave was an above the stove style mounted oven and therefore right about eye level.  Little shards of glass went everywhere including into my wife's face, neck and chest area.  She quickly flushed her eyes with water and we subsequently went to an eye specialist that morning for an eye exam as a precaution.  Please note that when I cleaned up the glass I found pieces approximately 15 feet away from the microwave.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (glass shards in face, neck, and chest) requiring medical attention, but no death occurred.

incident_description: Purchased anchor hocking measuring cup approximately three (3) years ago and stored in kitchen cupboard. Then, approximately 1 1/2 years later I heard sound of glass shattering. incident_description:
I received a Travel Mug for Christmas. Name of Mug ÃÂ Contigo auto sealÃÂ. Contract information: www. GoContigo.com or 1-888-262-0622. It came with warning instructions ÃÂhot cantents can create internal pressure resulting in discharge of hot vapor. Always press button with mug in upright position away from face to properly release pressure before drinking.ÃÂ  They do not provide a place to complain.
I had used the mug a couple of times prior to my accident. I always pushed the pressure bottom and a little air would come out. This morning 1/1/17, I filled the mug with hot coffee and let it stand a couple of minutes. When I tried to use it about a cup of steaming coffee spilled out all over my face and hands. The inside of my mouth was scalded. Plus I had to clean up a major mess.
I am 78 years old and usually very careful. But I started to think about what would happen if I had been driving in a busy freeway, or if my 99 year old mother had used this mug and had been seriously injured, or if a child had been burned while using this mug, or someone not wearing glasses would have been blinded. I live at 6,000 feet elevation and steam is not the same as at sea level. The warning is not sufficient to protect the public. I feel that a momentary lapse of caution should not subject a person to serious injuries due to using this time bomb. I am filing this complaint as a public service to protect other potential victims. All of this products should be taken off the market.
justification: The incident resulted in scalding injuries to the face, hands, and mouth, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the user followed instructions but still experienced the issue, suggesting a design flaw.

incident_description: On May 5, 2016, I was assembling our Ninja Master Prep Professional blender when it activated in my hand. I had it plugged in and was assembling the blade onto the machine part prior to putting it in the blender canister when it activated. It caused a very severe laceration to my right hand (dominant) palm and caused lacerations to my palmar arch artery, two nerves to my fingers, and a tendon going to my thumb. It would be very easy for another person to do this given that the blade did not need to be safely placed in the canister or locked in for it to activate.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations to the hand, including damage to an artery, nerves, and a tendon, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this could easily happen to others, making the occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
I want to report a scalding Hazard. I think I have the right model. It is a 5 burner range model LRG 3061 BD made by LG and purchased at Lowe's. 
I had a pot of boiling water on the right front burner and went to move it to the left front burner, it was heavy so I slid it from the right to the left burner, in the middle of that move the pot tipped forward and spilled onto my stomach and the front of my pants. I was able to push the pot back onto the level part of the range and only had minor burns on my stomach area. When I looked to see what had caused the spill I found that the middle burner iron grid does not have an iron grid that goes all the way to the front or the rear of the cooking area. The right and left burns do have a support grid on them so when you slid from one to the other the pot goes over the area without support and tips to the front toward the user. I was lucky but this frightened me. My grand children often help me cook. Had one of them been there they could have been badly burned. 
This hazard needs to be addressed.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw and potential for recurrence, especially with frequent use.

incident_description: I was making supper on my Samsung range model number FTQ3531WUX 30 I was using the oven as well as the cooktop As I started to go upstairs I heard a loud pop and turned around to see what it was Smoke was pouring out from the back of the stove and there was a strong electrical smell I ran downstairs and turned off the circuit breaker My son who is a electrical maintainance tech came up and took the back panel off The middle relay is melted and blackened He said I was really lucky I didn't have a fire and that it was a design flaw Upon going online and researching several sites this seems to be a real common problem The stove I have was  manufactured in Nov of 2010 but I am sure I didn't purchase until 2011 If this can prevent 1 family from losing their home or worse yet their lives it will be worth the filing of this report
justification: The incident involved smoke and a melted relay but no injury or fire, indicating a significant malfunction without harm.

incident_description: We purchased this Frigidaire Gas Range in March of 2012 and early on realized that it seemed like it was very easy to open the flow of gas by just brushing past or bumping the knobs for the burners.  It has happened occasionally through the past few years but we always caught it and turned the knob off.  On Friday January 20th my husband came home from work and found a strong smell of gas in our apartment and one of the stove knobs slightly turned on.  He immediately opened doors and windows and thankfully had not turned on any switches upon arrival home.  The gas smell cleared over the next couple of hours. I had been the last one to leave the house about 7 hours earlier and must have brushed past the stove as I left turning the knob so gas was accumulating in our home for 7 hours.  It could have been deadly to my husband and to the family that lives in the apartment below us.  The knobs on this range should not turn on and allow gas flow with such light pressure.  I have read online that others have the same complaint about this range.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to easily turned knobs, posing a serious risk but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I write to report an unsafe product and lack of internal controls for monitoring such hazardous products by the product' s manufacturer, retailer, and builder-installer. On November 20, 2016, I turned on the oven unit of a new Kenmore Range Model #79032603311 (Serial #AF43003397) in order to bake cookies for Thanksgiving when I smelled gas emanating from the stovetop burners. The oven was installed in a home constructed in 2014 for a home we purchased in October, 2016, so the unit was certainly less than two years old, and perhaps less than a year depending on state of sale and installation by the builder. We immediately turned the oven unit off and called our local utility, Ameren, to investigate a possible gas leak. 

After conducting an investigation of our home (including turning gas off at line valve), the Ameren technician determined that the oven was "releasing gas after ignition" at approximately "I 0,000 ppm at boiler tube when oven is on." (Ameren Notice of Code Violation of Hazardous Condition #[REDACTED], original on file with consumer). We then contacted Sears Home Services, and provided the model and serial number to them. They dispatched a Sears service technician to examine the range unit on November 22, 2016.


The Sears service technician confirmed that the defect was with the product and recommended that Sears replace the unit because it was emitting gas (he confirmed that his gas sensor would have been generally more sensitive than that used by the Ameren technician) (Technician ID [REDACTED], Service Order# [REDACTED], original on file with consumer). The technician spoke with his superior and recommended replacement of the unit because he could not identify the precise source of the leak.

He directed me to call 1-888-536-6673. I did so for two reasons: first, to alert Sears that a potentially dangerous product was on the market; second, to have Sears replace a product with a known defect. Over the course of the next two days, despite describing the hazardous condition of the range unit, I was directed to various Sears departments both in the U.S. and with overseas call centers variously described as "Consumer Solutions", "Retail Customer Care", "Warranties", "Sears Home Services" and others. Each telephone agent expressed no interest in the fact that there was a product defect and instead seemed most interested in identifying an alternative number that I would have to call so that, it seemed, that specific person would not have to deal with either our consumer complaint or the fact that a dangerous Kenmore product was on the market and may potentially pose danger to life and property in other homes.


After two days, my wife and I detern1ined that Sears lacked I) the internal controls necessary to effectively deal with a report of a hazardous product (the hazard having been identified with documentary evidence by a utility technician and a Sears-designated specialist) and 2) the interest in addressing, in any way, a consumer in possession of such a unit that was effectively new. We replaced the range at considerable expense but felt it was necessary to address a considerable risk to our lives, property, and children.


Sears' lack of internal controls is confirmed by the events that followed our attempts to notify it of the hazardous range. On December 9, 2016 and December 30, 2016, we received individualized sales letters stating "Thank you for choosing Sears to repair your Range. Now that it's fixed, we wanted you to know that we can also help protect it against future breakdowns" and encouraging us to pay between $68.43 and $77.16 for a "Master Protection Agreement." So, even though the Sears product technician confirmed the leak with the range during his visit on November 22, 21 06 and recommended that the unit be ÃÂreturned to store of purchase" and replaced by Sears, it was processed through Sears internal systems as a fixed range. We encourage the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission to investigate Kenmore Classic Range Model Number 79032603311 , ensure that other defective units do not pose threats to life or property in other homes, and to hold Sears accountable for its lack of product safety internal controls.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak from a defective oven, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.
