justification: The incident involved equipment failure and a mess, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On 01/13/2017 my wife and I were baking chicken in two separate bake ware dishes of the same size but different brands at the same time. We were baking at 400 degrees.  The oven door was opened during cooking simply to turn the dishes from inside the oven for even heating.  When she closed the oven door, the Anchor Hawking dish exploded in the oven sending broken glass everywhere inside the oven. No one was injured as the oven door was shut prior to the explosive shattering.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no injuries occurred as the oven door was closed.

incident_description:
As I walked away from the stove of boiling water the vent went on by it's own and a few seconds later there was a very loud popping sound.The electrical currant ceased. What seemed to be a minute later we smelled heavy plastic burning and found the undercarriage melted.

We have since removed and replaced the microwave with a very similar model, same make.  I would like you to know that all but 2 (two) models that we viewed now have a metal lip or banier between underneath of the door.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave causing a loud noise and melting, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Viking Dishwasher Model# DFUD042 I Serial# 063701408195 control board caught on fire (see attached pictures).
It could have caused a house fire- this happened overnight while we were sleeping. Awful smoke I burning smell.
There is a recall on Viking Dishwashers already but this unit did not make the cutoff. Might have to extend the recall
beyond the current manufacture date to go back further, as this is an serious issue that goes back beyond the
current scope. The control board and plastic casing actually caught on fire and burned. Thank goodness I was able
to turn off the main breaker to cut off electricity to the unit or my kitchen or worse my house could have caught on
fire.
justification: The dishwasher's control board caught fire, posing a significant risk of a house fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher was in operation washing a load of dishes when it started emitting noxious fumes of a burning smell. Dishwasher tripped circuit breaker and stopped operation. Further investigation disclosed that the circuit board literally melted and became charred.
justification: The dishwasher emitted fumes and the circuit board melted, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: KitchenAid Model KODE500ESS purchased July 15, 2015, from HH Gregg in Naples, FL.  Installed by technicians provided by HH Gregg.  On January 9, 2017, used the self-cleaning feature for the first time in the upper oven only.  Used the shortest cycle available (3.3 hours).  About 1.5 hours into cleaning, there was a tremendous blast.  Went into the kitchen and found glass everywhere as well as smoke.  Could not access the oven as it was too hot.  Turned off circuit to oven and called Fire Department.  Fire Department made the determination that the unit is defective and that it should be removed immediately.  This is not an isolated incident with this model number.  KitchenAid is refusing to do anything about it.
justification: The incident involved a significant blast and glass shattering, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Samsung dual oven electric range heating element does not respond to oven setting and heats up excessively. Oven element does not stop heating unless oven is turned off. Problem persists even after oven was serviced by factory authorized technician. The service technician temporary fixed problem by resetting the range (switching electric breaker on and off) but oven again burned food after using it several times.The last time it happened, food burned to a crisp, smoke filled the house and smoke alarm went off by the time my wife rushed to turn off oven and remove charred food.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned food and smoke) and potential safety hazards, but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I received my Black and Decker food processor model FP6010 for Christmas.  I was using it to dice carrots on 1/16/2017.  After I finished dicing I removed the FP6010-14 blade and noticed that some of the orange plastic which was covering part of the blade appear to be missing.  I have pictures that I can email.  I have contacted Black and Decker for a replacement part.
justification: The incident involved a damaged blade with missing plastic, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Dishwasher caught on fire during normal use.

I was running my dishwasher to clean dirty dishes.  Soon my house lights dimmed and my dishwasher door started to sizzle & smolder. Then flames came out of the door panel.  I unplugged the dishwasher before it could light the counter on fire. PTL I was close by.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was unplugged before causing further damage, resulting in an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Stove top right front burner will not shut off.  Items near stove had gotten very hot.  Had we not noticed, there would have been a fire.  We went on line to find the problem and fix it ourselves. We bought a switch from Sears Parts Direct.  The switch came and it was the wrong one.  The switch came and it was not the right one.  Sears Parts direct will not allow us to return this 96.95 part that is the wrong part in the beginning.  Then we went on the Sears Parts Direct to complain and get help.  A window popped up on the screen and asked if we needed help.  We replied to a person by the name of [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] told us to buy a 180.88 burner.  We received the burner but found that it did not fix the problem.  They refuse to take the burner back.  OK, now we are out 277.83 and have a stove that is a fire hazard.  We went on line one more time to check for recalls.  We have found that their IS a recall on this product for this exact fire hazard issue.  We are very upset that [REDACTED] did not tell us about the recall from the United Sates  Consumer Product Safety Commission.  This Commission stated that because of the recall, Sears is required to send a repair person to our home and fix the issue for FREE.  We will be contacting SEARS again and request that the stove be repaired free of charge and request the return of our 277.83 that is owned to us because they failed to send the correct part, and failed to tell us about the recall.
justification: The stove's failure to shut off created a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred. The issue is likely to recur given the recall and repeated failures to address it properly.

incident_description: Product has been used for over 10 years as kitchen double oven.Once or twice during the year it is cleaned by engaging the electronic controls it has. On January 15,2017 during the coarse of cleaning the interior glass panel shattered.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of an interior glass panel during cleaning, with no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Last night I turned our electric oven on and set the thermostat to 400 degrees.  After being on for only 3 - 4 minutes I seen smoke coming out of the vent. When I opened the Oven door the oven was full of thick black smoke and the Lower Heating Element was on fire ( 3 -5 inch flames) and had burnt in two pieces.  I closed the oven door and turned the oven off this extinguished the fire.  Once the Oven cooled we realized that the heating element coming from the power source had acted as a cutting torch causing a hole the size of a 50 cent piece to be burnt out of the bottom of the oven.   The oven was clean and there was no liner or aluminum foil in the bottom of the oven.
     I believe this is a malfunction. In other ovens I have owned in the past when electric heating elements burn out it automatically turns off the power source.  If I had not been there I believe this would have resulted in huge fire. 
I contacted Frigidaire to report the incident but of course I could only speak to a Customer Service person who knows very little about Electric Ovens and how very Dangerous this is.
I would not want this to happen to anyone else that is why I am contacting CPSC.  Below is the Stove information and I hope to hear from a representative from CPSC soon.  Sincerely [REDACTED]
FRIGIDAIR ELECTRIC RANGE ES300
SERIAL# VF62345271
MODEL# FEF366ESC
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but was quickly extinguished without injury, indicating a malfunction with potential for greater harm if unattended.

incident_description: I was using a cuisinart pan with the lid and heard a loud pop. The lid completely shattered into a million pieces while food was simmering on the stove.
justification: The lid shattered, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I was using a Cooks by JcPenney Electric Griddle purchased in 2010.

I was using the griddle at a temperature of 300F when my outlet sparked and made a  loud popping sound.  I unplugged the griddle and moved the plug to another outlet.  I continued to use the griddle at a temperature of 250F.  I then went to flip my food when I was shocked through my metal spatula when it made contact with the metal of the griddle plate.  I immediately unplugged the unit.

At the time I was also using the fan on my over-the-range microwave and an[REDACTED] (wifi radio)  on the same circuit.  There were no other appliances plugged in or running.  The microwave and [REDACTED] had no issues and continued to work.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock through a metal spatula, which constitutes an injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was isolated to the griddle and not recurring with other appliances.

incident_description: I recently  purchased a ninja professional 1500. Today I was using my blender and I tipped the container upside down to pour the last of my smoothie into a glass. The blade came flying  out and sliced my hand open. I went to the emergency room and had to get several stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury requiring emergency room treatment and stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: blade came out while I was pouring smoothie sliced two fingers on right hand lost fingernail on both
justification: The description indicates a blade injury resulting in sliced fingers and lost fingernails, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The electrical part of the oven malfunctioned in the middle of the night.  No one was using the oven nor had turned it on.  We woke up to the smell of plastic/ rubber burning.  The top of the oven where the broiler is located was very hot and lit up. The compartment that house the fire at the bottom was also lit up but not hot. We tried to turn the oven off using the control panel but nothing was working.  We had to pull the stove from the wall to unplug it. When we unplugged the stove the oven went off.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no one was injured, though there was a risk of fire.

incident_description:
I am writing to advise that I can turn on oven but I can't turn it off or reduce temperature.
I have to unplug oven to turn it off. I feel that this is unsafe being that I am a retired fire fighter.
I unplug it before we go to bed at night. This is model 79094353700. Kenmore.
I was baking chicken at the time.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that cannot be turned off normally, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Performing self cleaning function on our Kenmore Model #790.46702603 oven and had the glass door explode, sending hot glass flying all over our kitchen.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing hot glass to fly, but no injury was mentioned.

incident_description: I believe there is an issue with the Yeti Rambler. I have a 20oz model, and the issue is when you put hot liquids in (190F coffee) and put the lid on, the heat from the liquid makes the lid swell, and makes it very difficult to remove. The issue here is that it makes it very likely that the hot liquid will spill when you're trying to remove it. The reason you'd try to remove it is that the liquid is too hot, so you want it to cool down more quickly by removing the lid. To make matters worse, this is likely to happen while people are on their way to work in the morning, which could be life-threatening. I recently nearly spilled it all over myself while driving (I was stopped), and thought back to the famous [REDACTED] hot coffee case. Someone could easily burn themselves and possibly wreck and kill someone because of the engineering defect in the lid. At the very least I would issue a warning to folks, if not a full lid replacement. Thanks!
justification: The incident describes a potential for hot liquid spills that could lead to burns or accidents, with a near-miss example provided, indicating a risk of injury.

incident_description:
Fridgidaire Professional Series gas Stove/Oven 
Model FPGF3081KFA
Section of flat electronic panel that sits at back of stove stops working. Specifically, the column of 3,6,9,Cancel stops working, which means that you cannot turn the oven off. The Cancel button turns the oven off and without it, you need to unplug the oven to turn it off. We have replaced the back panel twice and it has stopped working again. We do not use any cleaners on the panel or put steaming pots in contact with the panel. I called Frigidaire and their customer service was completely disinterested in helping.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove panel that prevents turning off the oven without unplugging, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: Frigidaire Gas Range with Self Cleaning Burners model GLGF2386FCH oven turned on by itself on very high temperature. We were woken up by smoke detector in two rooms away going off and when the oven door was opened a thick black smoke with a heat draft shot back at us. The control panel was not working so had to switch of the electric supply from circuit breaker. This is clearly an product defect and could have set my house on fire if we were not around.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and produced thick black smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My sons lower lip got stuck underneath the plastic red hair part on the top of the cup. My son was screaming and crying and we were trying to get the cup off of his lip. His lip would not slide out we had to pull roughly on the cup to get his lip out and it took a piece of his lower lip off. His lip was bleeding and I immediately applied ice. The bleeding stopped shortly after and he doesn't need any medical attention. It was very scary for him and I and I don't want this to happen to anyone else.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (a piece of the lip was torn off and bleeding occurred), but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
Jenn Air Model JGS8750BDB
Was baking crab cakes in the oven, took them out after 10 minutes and they were burnt.  Realized that while I had set the oven to 350 it was way hotter I'd say around 600 degrees.  We turned off the oven and after about 20 minutes I realized the oven was NOT OFF and still at that 600 degrees.  My husband closed the gas line to the oven and we waited to burn off the rest of the gas.  

We haven't been able to cut the electricity to the stove as the plug is behind the oven and we can't get the oven out.  We're having to leave the door open because it still gets warm in the oven.  At night we are cutting the power at the breaker (which also has the refrigerator on that fuse).  

I have to wait 3 more days for repair man to come out as per Jenn Air (now Westinghouse) has that scheduled.  I'm going to try tomorrow to get him out here earlier.  

The oven is only 7 years old.  The whole thing was quite scary and still is.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with no reported injuries, and such occurrences are relatively uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: My Kenmore Elite 30" free standing electric range caught fire at the back of the electronics panel where the selections are made and the time is displayed.
justification: The incident involved a fire at the back of the electronics panel, indicating a clear incident but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased our microwave in July 2015. We have used our microwave regularly until yesterday, 1-10-17. We were using it to pop a bag of popcorn in the usual, recommended fashion. Suddenly we heard a loud sound and there was a flame inside the microwave on the cardboard panel wall. There was no metal in the microwave to create a spark. This incident occurred during completely normal use. We are no longer using the microwave, obviously. I decided to search Amazon reviews on this product's page containing the word FIRE. Apparently, this has happened to others in the exact same spot as ours. There seems to be an issue with that cardboard panel because user pictures of the burn marks look nearly identical to ours.
justification: The incident involved a flame inside the microwave during normal use, but no injury occurred. Similar incidents reported by others suggest this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Maytag built in dishwasher
model MBD8951BWB
serial number 10610928LR
Purchased in 2009
Heating element remain on even though wash function was completed.
I found the dishes so hot the next morning you could not touch them.
Based on the control panel the dishwasher was off but the heating element was still on.
I had to pull the fuse on the house circuit to shut the heat element off.
I tried restarting the dishwasher but heating element won't shut off.
Dishwasher got so hot the lower spray arm melted due to the excessive heat.
This is a potent fire hazard the unit should not fail leaving the heating function stuck on.

Due to the age of the unit we will replace it but concern with other people who have this model.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning heating element that poses a fire hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On January 16, 2017 my toaster over caught fire.  It is a Black & Decker.  At the time of the incident, my wife was making toast in it.  She was watching TV and noticed a bright image in the corner of her eye.  As she turned to her right she could see the device on fire.

She rushed over and unplugged it and then called 911.  She was told to vacate the property.  The first responder was a police officer who entered our home into the kitchen.  A few minutes later the fire department arrived and took charge of the situation.
The only damage the property sustained was smoke.  The house is fine and my wife is OK.
justification: The toaster caught fire, but no injuries or significant property damage occurred.

incident_description:
I have a GE Profile dishwasher. Approx 10 years old.
We use it about once a day on average.
About 2 weeks ago, when the dishwasher was started, after about 15 mins of operation, thick smoke started pouring from the dishwasher door. There was a strong smell of burning electrical wire. All the lights on the control panel began flashing. 
At this point we have turned off the circuit breaker to that area. If not, when the dishwasher door closes, the thick smoke returns.
justification: The incident involved thick smoke and electrical burning smell but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Was running the dishwasher, it started to smell like it was burning. I opened it up, and the element was hissing and popping. There was a class action lawsuit against the manufacturer of this dishwasher for faulty control panels that caused the heating element to overheat and catch the dishwasher on fire, or at least melt the inside, yet I don't see any recall on the product.
justification: The dishwasher exhibited signs of overheating and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: Double Oven Gas Range. GE Cafe. Model CGS990SET3SS. Bottom Oven would not heat. The igniter/glow bar is located beneath the bottom heat deflector. This is a thick metal deflector. The igniter/glow bar melted the metal of the heat deflector and the molten metal dripped onto the igniter/glow bar shorting it out. There is a hole in the thick metal deflector. Upon looking at blogs on the internet this has happened numerous times. This is a fire hazard and a material design flaw. I can replace the igniter/glow bar and heat deflector, but I believe the same hazard still exists. Help us!
justification: The incident describes a material design flaw causing a fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Turned on a gas burner on the cook top. The flame was not as it should be. One other burner had a similar flame. The two rear burners appeared to be okay. The indicator lights for the lower warming drawer were on and couldn't be shut off.
We noticed a burning odor. Smoke was visible coming from control panel. Smoke was also noticeable in the oven. The smoke smelled like burning electrical wires.
We disconnected the stove and moved it outside.
justification: The incident involved visible smoke and a burning odor, but no injuries were reported, and the situation was mitigated by disconnecting the stove.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Smooth Top Range Model # PLES389ech   SN NF74619647 
Range was turned off and cooktop had not been used in days.  Plastic cooking item was on the stove and left front burner turned on melting the plastic, breaking the cooktop and causing smoke damage and chemical damage to my home.
justification: Incident caused property damage (melted plastic, broken cooktop, smoke/chemical damage) but no reported injury.

incident_description: I have a Haier Microwave Oven that was manufactured on April of 2015,  Model # HMC935SESS,  Serial # HMC935SESS-150400566 that started to catch on fire.  The wrapping that the discharge capacitor has around it started on fire.  No damage to our home only because we smelled something burning and turned the microwave off.  I called the company and they did not seem to be as concerned as I am.  I still have the microwave and could show someone outside how it catches on fire when used.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was turned off before causing injury or property damage.

incident_description: I wanted to make you aware of the fire hazard danger that exists with this OTR microwave. This was a brand new unit in our new built home 2 1/2 years ago. Recently my wife called me while I was away from the house because it was making strange noises.  No one was using the unit, there was no time on the display, the inside light was off, she could smell something burning and the inside of the oven was extremely hot. she could not even touch the inside walls or the turntable. I had her unplug the unit and investigated later upon returning home.  I put a small pat of butter on a paper plate inside the oven, closed the door and plugged it into the power outlet. The unit appeared to be off, but I could hear the magnetron running and the butter was melted. While the door was open, the magnetron was still engaged and running. I opened and closed the door several times in rapid succession, and the control panel went dark (off).  The unit is now unplugged permanently, but this is a MAJOR FIRE HAZARD. Had my wife and kids been sleeping when this happened, my family could have suffered major injuries or have been killed.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Please see attached Incident Report along with pictures emails and receipts for new racks and Factor Catalog.


Around Mid April 2016 I self-cleaned the oven of my Frigidaire 30" Slide-Gas Range Model No.FPGS3085PFA. Let it be noted that the oven racks were removed from the oven prior to self-cleaning. After the self-cleaning I cooked a roast which was approximately 15 pounds and the oven rack in my range collapsed. It was extremely dangerous trying to get the roasting pan out of the hot oven and trying to get the rack out of the hot oven because it was wedged in. Frigidaire customer service was contacted after this incident by my husband, [REDACTED]. He explained that there must be a design flaw with the oven possibly during the cleaning that the walls of the oven expanded and the racks no longer fit. I have confirmation of that email if needed. Frigidaire's response was that the range was out of warranty. The range is currently only 2 1/2 years old. At the time of the incident it was not quite 2 years old. They proposed that we purchase new racks at a 50 percent discount. My husband did not believe that this would solve the problem. Moving forward to December of 2016, I again was cooking a roast and again the rack collapsed, spilling gravy all over the oven and setting off the fire alarm. This was an extremely dangerous situation the rack which collapsed was lodged between the wall of the hot oven and the oven door would not open, it had to be forced open. After, this incident the next day I again self-cleaned the oven, again without the oven racks in the oven. When I went to put the oven racks back in the oven they did not fit at all. They collapsed without a pan or baking sheet on them. Again, I contacted Frigidaire customer service via email, explained the problem and their only solution was for us to purchase new racks at 30% discount. I chose to do this, the racks were specifically picked out of the Frigidaire Factory Parts Catalog. The order was reviewed and priced by customer service prior to me placing the order with the parts department. The racks came they did not fit. I contacted customer service suggesting that they send a service rep to my home to inspect the range with the new and old racks. If I was shome hot not putting them in the oven correctly I would pay for service, if the new and old racks were deemed not to fit then Frigidaire would pay for service and come up with a solution to this problem. Possibly, replacing the range. Frigidaire did not respond to this suggestion. They did however, contact me after I emailed them several times and now they are offering a different rack (I need two) which they claim fits my oven. I am not sure when I initially contacted Frigidaire customer service that this solution was not offered to me. At this time I want a full refund for the racks I purchased and/or want the racks that fit which I have not received yet or a new range, I also would like to mention that this range is discontinued, I am not sure if that matters. And also there are quite a few complaints I found only with other consumers having the same problem. Regards, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with the oven rack collapsing, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Our Bialetti Brikka stovetop espresso maker has TWICE overflowed while on the burner, which has resulted in boiling hot coffee spewing out and down onto the gas range. Luckily, we have not been burned, but could have been if we'd been standing closer to it or had it on the front burner. 

This coffee maker has a design flaw that leads to the fluid rising up out of the pot. The handle has also become repeatedly loose, resulting in the pin that falling out. This poses a danger to any consumer who is lifting it or holding it while it contains hot coffee. It's very dangerous and I believe the manufacturer should recall it.
justification: The incident describes overflow and a loose handle, posing potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Kudc10fxss7 dishwasher electric panel burned and emitted electrical burned smell in kitchen.  Tripped electric breaker and stopped working.  Wires melted together in panel and burned groove in sound barrier and insulation in  dishwasher door.
justification: The incident involved electrical damage and a burned smell, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My new Kitchenaid dual fuel Range, an electric oven with gas cooktop, malfunctioned on 3 occasions, resulting in a fire in my oven on one occasion and bread burned to a crisp on another occasion.  On all 3 occasions, the oven was set on the normal baking setting, not Convection. The Range is Kitchenaid Model No. KSDB900ESS0.

I purchased the Range in mid 2016.  During the summer, the unit tripped off at approximately 300 degrees while preheating and an error code appeared.  A factory authorized Technician looked at the Range and indicated that he tripped the breaker and the unit worked fine. He speculated that a power outage may have been the cause, even though the unit attempted to heat up before the automatic shut down and error code. 

Two additional malfunctions occurred in early January 2017.  On one occasion, the oven was set to 400 degrees to reheat vegetables with puff pastry topping on the middle rack in [REDACTED].  I opened the oven after heating the serving for approximately 10 minutes and the entire dish was on FIRE with flames touching the roof of the oven.  I closed the oven immediately but the smoke was so dense that both upstairs and downstairs smoke detectors were triggered.  I promptly reopened the oven and placed a lid on the flaming food in order to trap the flames and smoke.  I removed the Corningware from the oven after the oven cooled.  We attempted to clean the Corningware, but permanent burn marks remain.
  
The oven was set at only 180 degrees on the other occasion, in order to keep french toast warm while I cooked multiple batches on the gas cooktop.  Each batch of french toast takes approximately 5 minutes to cook.  When I opened the oven to insert the second batch of french toast the first batch was thoroughly charred, black on the top and sides, and smoking.  Note that  the first batch was in the oven only 5 minutes at a purported temperature of 180 degrees.  I removed the charred french toast from the oven and immediately got an error code, either FGE1 or F6E1, referencing excessive temperature and advising that a Technician should be contacted.
  
I contacted Whirlpool Customer Service, who advised me to trip the breaker to the Range until a Technician could look at the Range due to safety concerns.  A factory authorized Technician was dispatched to check my oven on January 13, 2017.  The Technician acknowledged that the oven had experienced excessive heat, based on white marbling on the black plastic cover protecting part of the circuit board and similar white marbling on plastic protecting wires to the gas cooktop control units on the front of the Range.  The Technician called Whirlpool and then performed a series of tests of the oven temperature.  The Technician indicated that the broiler elements appeared to be working but that the bottom elements repeatedly cut off unexpectedly.  The Technician also noted that the actual oven temperature readings were inconsistent with the temperature setting on the Range.  The Technician indicated that he needed to order and then replace both the upper and lower heating elements as well as the circuit board. 
      
I explained to the Kitchenaid Customer Service representative as well as a Kitchenaid safety specialist that I was uncomfortable with the oven in my home under the circumstances, especially the significant fire in my oven that was due to an oven malfunction.  I also suggested that, from a safety standpoint, Whirlpool would best serve its customers by replacing my Range in order that Whirlpool could test the unit to determine the source of the defect.  The representatives appeared unwilling to replace the unit in order to afford Whirlpool the opportunity to test my oven to determine the root cause of the multiple malfunctions that resulted, on one occasion, in a significant fire in my oven.  Similarly, the factory authorized Technician indicated that I needed multiple events documented before Whirlpool would even consider replacing the Range.
  
In summary, the TechnicianÃÂs findings are consistent with my concern that excessive baking temperatures involved either operations in the self cleaning or broiler mode instead of the baking temperature set on my oven.  Moreover, it would appear that Whirlpool either fully aware of the source of the defect that caused my oven to catch fire and is simply unwilling to replace or recall them or, alternatively, Whirlpool does not know the root cause of the defect but is nonetheless unwilling to ensure the safety of its customers by removing and testing a defective oven.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven and significant property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
In November, 2016, the door to my Kenmore oven door spontaneously exploded 45 minutes after I had turned the oven off. I had been baking chicken for 45 mins at 350 degrees. The oven has a double glass door. It is the exterior glass door, not the interior, which exploded.

I'm told the interior door can be damaged by consumers who use the door to push racks into the oven. I don't do that. In any case, it's the EXTERIOR door that exploded, not the interior.

Purchase Date: 02 01 2011            

Model #:  790.92909011                  

Serial #: VF10455967     

PRS Unit:  8227    

Service org: SEARS  

My mom had a Sears service contract on all of her appliances through Sears for decades until she passed away last year. The Kenmore oven was purchased at the local Sears Hometown store in Weatherford Texas in 2011.

I let that coverage lapse after her death but then I purchased a Sears home warranty a year ago that covered the appliances. My Sears Home warranty refused to cover the oven, saying it's a "structural" issue, not a mechanical problem. After sending me from one department to the next over the past months, Sears suggested I contract the manufacturer--but they can't tell me who the manufacturer is. I've called Electrolux and Frigidaire and their customer service representatives deny that they're the manufacturers.

If you do a Google search of "exploding oven door," you will discover link after link of consumers who have had reported the same issue. For example:

http://6abc.com/home/consumer-alert-ovens-exploding-in-homes-across-country-/1060683/

https://consumerist.com/2016/02/04/why-are-so-many-people-reporting-kenmore-oven-door-explosions/

https://www.google.com/amp/chicago.cbslocal.com/2015/07/08/2-investigators-glass-oven-doors-shattering-without-warning/amp/?client=safari

http://www.winknews.com/2016/10/24/exploding-oven-doors-menace-consumers-in-swfl-elsewhere/

In every case, Sears has denied liability and blames consumers for mistreatment or damage to the oven door that resulted in the door combusting on its own. 

This is oven presents a safety hazard as well. There are sharp black shards of glass as well as the safety glass that were projected into the area of the room where I had been standing 20 seconds earlier. 

I have numerous photos documenting the oven post-explosion. (They look exactly like the ones you'll find on a Google search.) I've tried uploading them to your site numerous times but it won't let me.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, which is a safety hazard but no injury was reported. The occurrence likelihood is high based on multiple similar reports.

incident_description: My stove caught on fire as I was preparing dinner on Sunday 1/22/17.
justification: The stove caught fire, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that she was using both the cooktop and the oven when she smelled something burning. The consumer immediately turned off the oven range. The consumer pulled the unit from its location and noticed that there were flames coming from the metal protection cover on the back of the unit. The consumer let the flames subside.

The consumer unscrewed the metal protection cover and noticed that the wiring inside it had burnt.

The consumer indicates that prior to the incident, the cooktop portion of the oven range was used approximately once or twice daily, whereas as the oven was used once daily on average. The consumer plans on keeping the oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved flames and burnt wiring but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the frequent use of the appliance.

incident_description:
Purchased a GE ModelSG400621Q which was installed on October 16, 2016.

Right dual burner was on and started to emit sparking and blew the circuit breaker. Waited a while and reset the circuit breaker and again it sparked and blew the circuit breaker.

I went to the website regarding the issue and apparently GE is aware that it is common for this to occur because they did not put enough cover or insulation around the knob to prevent water from shorting it out.
justification: The incident involved sparking and circuit breaker trips, indicating a safety issue but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Cuisinart model TOB-40 toaster-oven-broiler. Purchased 2/7/2012.  Returned first one right away because front-lower element was clearly overheating and would burn food.  Replacement worked OK, but the same front-lower element slowly warped and displaced vertically a full inch to where it blocks the bread rack and will set food on fire when used normally.
justification: The toaster oven's overheating and warping element poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
My frigidaire smooth cooktop range turns itself ON.  Also, when it is turned ON, it will not turn off.  Also, when it is turned ON it will change its temp setting.  This has been going on for years, but only this week has gotten so bad that we had to turn off power to the unit at the breaker box for fear that it would cause a fire.  Several pots and pans have been damaged due to this malfunction. And now we must replace the whole unit.  I have researched this and found that over 200,000 similar units from the same maker have been recalled for the same reason.  I do not understand how this unit was not included in the recall.  
model # FEC30S6ABF
SER # NF80621670
FEB 2008
justification: The malfunctioning cooktop poses a fire hazard and has already damaged property, indicating a significant safety risk.

incident_description: General Electric Arora Range, Model JB745DF3WW, purchased June 2015. When turning on the oven, there was a brief fire and smoke from the Range Control Board area. The oven was immediately turned off, circuit breaker turned off, and the range was unplugged. Components and wires are melted on the back of the control board. GE technician has investigated and I am currently awaiting resolution.
justification: There was a fire and smoke incident causing damage to the range, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The glass top of our slow cooker shattered (after cooking our dinner) into tiny pieces of glass without any type of action such as dropping it, hitting it against an object, etc.  When I went online to view any information about this product, I read several negative reviews from other consumers that had the exact same thing happen to them as well. Obviously, this is a dangerous product with the glass lid shattering with no provocation. Fortunately, no one was injured.

The slow cooker is manufactured by a company called Elite  (I could not find any information online about this company as far as an address or phone number.  The only information online was the retailers that sell this product.) We had purchased this product at Kohls department stores in July 2016 and only had used it no more than 1/2 dozen times.

Elite Platinum Slow Cooker 8.5 quart  Model# MST900V
justification: The glass top shattered without provocation, posing a danger, but fortunately no one was injured. Multiple similar incidents reported by other consumers indicate a likely occurrence.

incident_description: The knobs that turn on the gas stove burners turn on when slightly bumped by anyone that brushes up close to the stove. Even with the knowledge that they turn on easily, I have bumped them on at least 40 times, and have burned towels twice. LG sent knob replacements, which made no difference. The knobs are at an angle in the front of the stove. They have no resistance to prevent them from turning on by mistake. This stove is a terrible fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the stove knobs turning on easily, leading to burned towels but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
We have a GE side by side refrigerator Model PZS25KSECFSS.  The ice maker has a plastic auger (part# WR17X11263) that has broken twice in 14 months.  The ice chips of pieces of the plastic auger until it doesn't even work anymore.  Beside the broken part, there is potential risk for swallowing or cutting your mouth on the small chips.  I chew on ice chips alot and have had a small piece of the broken auger in my mouth (11-30-2016).  This could have cut me, could have choked on it or broken a tooth.  You can't tell the diffence because they look just like the ice chips.  I did not get hurt but someone else could.
Also, broken pieces have ended up in our garbage disposal from dumping glasses out (12-1-2016).  It didn't break ours this time but could next time.  This auger should not be made from plastic.
justification: The incident involves a broken plastic auger that could cause injury but no actual injury was reported, and the likelihood is high given the recurrence and potential for harm.

incident_description: In the process of using the Electrolux smooth top electric range, model PLEF398DCJ, the right rear burner failed to go out after turning off the control.   We tried to turn the control on then off, but this failed to turn off the burner.   We turned off the breaker controlling the 240 volt supply to the stove, turned the power back on and the burner stayed off.   The cook stove should not be designed in such a way that the burner is allowed to fail in an 'on' condition.   This is unsafe
justification: The burner failed to turn off, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was using my frigidaire range purchased 02/21/2014
Model number LFEL3017LWD Serial number VF40437591 Bought at  lowes when it started smoking really bad after shutting the oven off the control panel at the top where the time is started sparking and then caught fire after looking into it I have found multiple people who have also had the same problem and when I contacted frigidaire over the situation they told me that there was nothing they could do
justification: The incident involved a range smoking and catching fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The heat venting out the top edge of the oven melted the adhesive on my laminate cabinet door above the oven, and made the door handle on the door too hot to touch.  The service man from the appliance store where I bought the oven said he thinks the problem is that the venting is at the very top of the oven, and there is virtually no deflection of the heat coming out.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted adhesive and hot handle) but no injury or death.

incident_description: I was microwaving food in a Pyrex 6 cup 1.5L rectangular baking dish when it suddenly exploded as it was cooking.  The food in the dish was not cold.  The lid was not on the dish.  There was both liquid and solid food in the dish.  The food had been microwaved about two minutes at the point of explosion.  I was not injured nor was the microwave damaged but the dish was in a million pieces, many of them very small sharp shards.  The dish was purchased three years ago as part of a set of Pyrex but has not been used more than a few times as it is at our vacation home.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no injuries or damage to the microwave, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: Control panel on range sparked, smoked and emitted electrical burning odor.
justification: The incident involved sparking and smoking from a control panel, indicating an electrical issue, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Microwave wall unit caught fire & was not being use at that time. About 8pm while in dinner room we heard explosion in kitchen. I found Microwave on fire (sparks coming from the light inside of micro, smoke & running in On mode) as it being used. Main electric cord was pulled from wall, unit on right side was very  hot. Service man stated the unit needs main PCB on magnetron.
justification: The microwave caught fire and caused an explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:

Thankfully I was not seriously injured, which was a miracle, because I was standing right next to it. And it was nothing to do with the gas line, which also was a blessing. When my husband called there were no recalls on that model. I would not want this model to do this to anyone else. Because it easily could. Glass went over the entire kitchen. I have tried to communicate with Frigidaire thru various emails with no response. Thank You.

incident_description:
A bad blade is not the only problem with Cuisinart food processors.

I have model DLC-8, which I received as a gift two or three years ago. Soon after, the blade broke and the company sent me a new one. Now that replacement blade is subject to recall. I have contacted the company to receive another one.

More recently, just before Thanksgiving, the plastic latch that connects the lid to the bowl snapped off.

I owned a Cuisinart for nearly 30 years and never had a problem. This new one is nothing but trouble. It appears that Cuisinart's manufacturing standards have fallen. Why?

I so regret that I gave away my old processor. This new one is junk.
justification: The incident describes product malfunctions (broken blade and snapped latch) but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) given the user's repeated issues and recall.

incident_description: We received a very high power bill on a house we are selling. Upon investigation we discovered that the oven broiler had been running for several weeks and all the controls were set to off. The only way to turn the unit off was at the circuit breaker. GE customer service failed to properly investigate and settle my claim. The oven is a safety hazard and nearly burned the house down. It got so hot the cooking racks rusted and deformed. The interior of the oven blistered.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a safety hazard and caused property damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased an ice cream scoop and when scooping ice cream that was VEry cold, the metal of the scoop cut my finger. Upon observation, I saw that there are areas that the metal is very thin - just enough to slice your finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the finger, which qualifies as an injury, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the thin metal design of the scoop that can easily cause cuts.

incident_description: The outer glass panel on my Sears Kenmore Electric Oven Shattered when I opened the oven door.
justification: The glass panel shattered, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Kenmore oven Model 790 41022802.  The 24 inch rack does not fit securely  and falls to the floor of the oven when baking or roasting.  This has happened several times, nearly burning me.
justification: The oven rack falling is an incident that has nearly caused burns, indicating potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description:
1. What happened to prompt your Report?
My wife ran the self-cleaning feature of our ~16-month-old oven for the first time. Approximately two hours into the procedure, she attempted to turn on the oven light (which she discovered the oven refuses to do during self-cleaning), and the inner pane of glass in the door shattered. (I can only assume that her presence caused some very minor shift in pressure/vibration/etc that was the proverbial straw that broke the camel's back.) Some of the glass fell out the bottom vent onto the floor, though much of it remained in the oven. Upon opening the door (after the oven had cooled), more glass fell onto the floor, as well as between the door and oven, between the gasket, etc.


2. What type of product(s) were being used?
KitchenAid 30" Single Wall Oven with Even-HeatÃÂ True Convection (KOSE500ESS00)


3. Who was using the product(s)?
My wife was using the oven.


4. How were the product(s) being used?
The automatic self-cleaning cycle was being run.


5. Was there a harm or risk of harm, such as an injury, illness, or death? How did the harm or risk occur?
There was (and is) risk of harm from glass particles being stepped on or ingested (either by pets or infants eating off the floor, or by anyone from food prepared in the oven in the future).
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no reported injury, with a low likelihood of future harm from glass particles.

incident_description: My Whirlpool microwave is turning on by itself, I had to unplug the unit for it to stop. Created a smoke smell during this process.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself and creating a smoke smell indicates a malfunction, but there was no injury reported.

justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: On December 2, 2015, I bought a microwave (Kenmore Elite, model No.: 790.80373310 and serial number: KG54261192). Four times my wife accidentally turned on a burner on our stove top by leaning against one of the knobs while she cooked or reached up to the microwave. Three times we smelled the gas leaking much later. One time the burner lit.
There is no way to lock the knobs, so we have to keep the knobs removed from the stove.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks and a burner lighting accidentally, posing a risk but no reported injury.

The consumer indicates that he uses his food processor five to six times a week.

The consumer plans on keeping his food processor for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The consumer sustained a laceration to his finger due to a cracked metal ring on the food processor, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I made coffee as usual, and went outside of kitchen for s few minutes and heard an explosion, I came inside to find coffee, grounds, and broken glass, and plastic everywhere.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing damage but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I had used the food processor to shred some potato. While eating, I bit on a small piece of white plastic. Didn't cause any real injury and I didn't think much of it other than I couldn't think where it had come from. A few days later, the news was reporting about the recalled blades. I must point out that although my processor has a blade like the one in the recall, it wasn't the blade I was using to shred. But, the story made me look closer at the blade. I could see that the white plastic shaft had failed and shed parts into the food.

I then looked at the other blade liked the one described in the recall. My blade has the four rivets and there are indeed cracks in the metal at two of them.

I have obviously stopped using both blades, so no longer have a food processor. I'm concerned that my model # isn't on the recall since I have the defective blade. I'm also concerned that the other blade failed at the shaft and there has been no mention of that risk.

I'm hoping you can assist me in obtaining two safe blades and also considering if the recall doesn't include all the products it should.
justification: The incident involved ingestion of plastic but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the blade defects.

incident_description:
The touch pad is no longer working. The machine would sometime come on by itself making beeping noises like it was making selections for cycles and then eventually the touch pad just stop working. 
We had our home warranty company come out and replace the touch pad the week of 11/1 and one week later the touch pad stopped working again.
We were then advised by are home warranty company that there was a recall on this part causing this to go back and to potentially cause a fire. 
www.cpsc.gov/recalls/2011/ge-recalls-dishwashers-due-to-fire-hazard
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning touch pad with a recall due to potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(11/13/2014)Consumer stated she was using the dishwasher on normal cycle for about 30 minutes when she heard a loud and smelled a burning odor.

She was sitting in her kitchen and noticed there was a lot of black smoke coming from the dishwasher. She opened the door to power off cycle to dishwasher. Her spouse also cut off power to dishwasher from the circuit breaker panel.

She stated there is damage (black soot) to the door exterior and countertop above dishwasher.

She also stated this is the first time this has happened.

Picture Attached...

I know how to use knives correctly.

incident_description:
I have an electric built-in double oven. The exterior glass door of the lower oven burst and shattered into hundreds of little pieces. (The interior glass of the oven door remains intact.) The oven was off and had not been used in 48 hours. No one was home at the time of the incident although I believe I came home shortly after it happened. The glass on my kitchen floor made a sizzling sound for 30 minutes.

The force must have been strong given the distances the glass flew. I had a dish towel and dish mat hanging on the oven door which directed the majority of glass directly below the oven on the floor.

There were no apparent reasons for the glass to burst. Had a child, adult or pet been standing in front of the oven at the time of the incident, they would have been pelted with flying glass.
justification: The incident involved a burst oven door with no injuries, but potential for harm if someone had been present.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart involved in the current recall, which got me to look at my other Cuisinart products, both of which have blades for which the plastic casing on the blade is cracked.  I wrote to Cuisinart and they say these products are safe to use even though I sent a photo of a broken and cracked blade.
justification: The description reports cracked blades but no actual incident or injury, fitting severity level 2.

come flying off if the processor Is used any longer. Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus Processor
Model# DLC-2AMGSLT
Product Code 0  86279 04876 9
No Injuries to date. I have ordered another blade. Used in our home for normal food processing

incident_description:
One basic drinking glass from Ikea exploded on the table. It was used just 5 minutes ago, and it was filled with room temperature drinking water.

The water spilled down on table and chairs, and the glass just disintegrated into tousands of pieces all over the place.
Nobody touched the glass while exploding.
justification: The glass exploded but no one was injured, only causing a mess.

incident_description:
Product is a "Joseph Joseph Lotus Non-Scratch Folding Steamer Basket" sold by Bed Bath & Beyond in stores and on-line. Product was purchased in store in DeWitt, NY. It is a replacement for the same product which failed after one use (silicon foot melted after contact with inside of cooking pot). That failed product was replaced in store with an identical item.

Vegetable steamer was placed into pot, water was brought to temp, vegetables were steamed. After removing the steamer basket from the cooking pot while doing dishes, it was noted that one of the three silicon feet was missing. The vegetables had already been consumed. The missing foot was not found - it is assumed it had been ingested.
justification: The missing silicon foot was assumed to be ingested, but there is no report of injury or harm, only a product failure.

incident_description:
We have a new home with a Whirlpool oven model # WOS51EC0AS02 installed within the cabinetry. On December 27, 2016 my daughter was walking past the oven and slid into the corner of the oven on the lower right side. The corners of the oven door and the vent deflector below the oven door are both EXTREMELY sharp stainless steel. As such, my daughter sustained a serious laceration on her left heel that required an Emergency Room visit and 18 stitches. 

Since the incident, I have inspected several neighbors/friends ovens only to discover how unusually sharp ours is. This model of oven poses a significant safety hazard to adults, children and pets. 

I have reached out to Whirlpool and they have scheduled an inspection of the oven. However, since this poses, in my opinion, such a real and significant safety concern, I felt it was best to inform this commission.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious laceration requiring emergency medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the sharp edges being a consistent hazard.

incident_description: I have a Bosch  self cleaning double oven that was installed new in March of 2011.  I very rarely use the bottom oven. I was cooking a roast in the lower oven while using the top oven as well.  I turned the oven off after 30 minutes at 500 degrees as this is how I cook a roast beef.  the oven was off for about 15 minutes when the inner door glass shattered, showering glass all over the floor
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass) but no reported injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with proper oven use.

incident_description: Our Sears Kenmore Elite model 790.98022800 front right burner did  not turn off even though the display said it was off.  I just happened to notice well after we finished using that burner and turned it off that it was getting hotter instead of cooling down. It was then bright red and burning at the highest level. We could not shut it off.  I had to shut off the circuit breaker.  I am thankful that I noticed it! I have been researching the issue for the repair options when I saw the recall on the other models.  This is serious. They need to expand this recall before someone is seriously injured or killed.
justification: The burner failed to turn off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: panasonic microwave inverter.  Microwave had grey smoke coming out of sides and bottom.  Electrical smell and flames while it was running. If I had not been present and turned it off there would have surely been a kitchen fire.
justification: The microwave emitted smoke and flames, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred as it was turned off in time.

incident_description: LG Electric range, model LRE30451SW has been recalled for burners that do not turn off however my range also has a problem with the oven. The temperature cannot be regulated and once turned on the oven heats to excessive temperatures burning the food and nearly causing a grease fire. This occurs no matter what temperature the oven is set to. I checked the temperatures with a separate oven thermometer to verify.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that overheats, posing a burn and fire hazard, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: We purchased a Kenmore smooth top oven range several years ago. Within two years, the left front burner started acting up. Since it was outside of the warranty time, and we didn't have money to repair it, we just stopped using it. The trouble began when I turned it on, and it didn't turn on. I tried turning it on and off a couple of times and it finally came on. The next issue was that it would not go below high heat. I would turn the dial down but the intensity of the heat stayed high. I turned it off, but it did not turn off. I tried several times to turn the knob different ways to turn it off, but to no avail. I finally was able to turn it off after several tries and the heat was so intense it melted the side of my refrigerator that is next to the oven, and burned my arm. Because the burner is in the front, I had a hard time reaching over the intense heat to turn the knob. I had to wrap my arm in a towel to keep trying to turn it off. I almost called the fire department for fear that it would never shut off. I have avoided using it ever since unless we desperately need to use it. The couple of times I have had to use it, we encountered the same exact issues. I recently found out that there have been recalls on this issue and these ovens. My serial number matches, but my model number does not. The serial number is VF75051333 and the model number is 790.94349700 so sears will not cover it. I strongly believe this model number should be added to the recall list as this is a dangerous and serious issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a burned arm and property damage, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue recurs when the oven is used, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: I baked a cauliflower casserole in an 8x8 glass Pyrex pan. It baked for 20 minutes at 425 degrees. Afterwards, I set the pan on top of the oven to cool. It sat for about 30 or 40 minutes and then the glass pan shattered. It sent glass shards everywhere and into several dishes of food that I had cooling on the counter, causing me to have to throw them away due to glass in the food.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass pan and contaminated food, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Purchased Sunbeam Mixmaster November 18th and used it to make holiday cookies.  The beaters are keyed in place with what appear to be oval metal tabs.  At the end of making the third batch of cookies I noticed the beaters clanging...and did not think anything of it since it was a relatively thick spritz cookie dough.  Yesterday I pulled out the mixer again to make a pumpkin pie (very thin batter).  The beaters started clanging immediately. When I pulled the beaters out, I noticed that the metal keys on one beater were completely missing. There's a very high probability that the keys broke off and fell into the dough while I was making that last batch of cookies.

incident_description: I am reporting an incident with our 4 year old Samsung Refrigerator (Model RSG307AARS).  My son was opening the refrigerator door and also touching the freezer door, when he was shocked. I have verified that this was 120V AC.  The problem originates with the refrigerator door (right side).  At the top are two wires that go from the chassis/frame through a channel in the hinge into the door.  Upon removing the hinge cover, it was evident that the two wires were severed.  The wires include a power and a ground.  So, the fact that they were severed applied voltage to the door and simultaneously removed the protective ground.  Once my son touched both doors, he completed the circuit providing the path to ground through him and into the freezer door which is properly grounded.  It is worth noting that I have not disassembled the door to determine what caused the wires to sever.  Also, once I disconnected the cable at the hinge connector, the applied voltage goes away.  So, I am confident this is the problem.  As an electrical engineer and former UL engineer, I know how dangerous this is, especially having the voltage applied to both hands with the energy passing through the chest of my son.  I am concerned that there may be other incidences of this that are waiting to happen.  Samsung has been notified but after 48 hours has yet to respond with a technician to investigate further.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock to a child, which is an injury but not fatal, hence severity level 3. Given the described wiring fault, similar incidents are possible if not addressed, hence occurrence likelihood 3.

incident_description:
Electrolux model EI30GS55JS gas range Serial # NF41228446 

Front right burner is defective resulting in unburnt natural gas being released out of the burner leading to explosive hazard and gas poisoning in the kitchen and house.  This occurs when the front right burner knob is turned through the Med-Hi position.  When the burner is turned from Off to Hi, the burner igniter triggers, the burner outputs gas, the flame lights, the flame level is High, and operates correctly.  When knob is turned to Med-Hi, the gas output from the burner decreases so low that the flame often goes out entirely or is below the flame level of the Low knob position.  This is a major safety hazard in that the flame often goes out when the burner knob is in the Med-Hi position area.  When the knob continues to be turned from Med-Hi area to Med area, the gas output from the burner increases.  If the burner flame went out when it was turned to Med-Hi, the burner is now outputting unburnt natural gas.  This is a major safety hazard because now unburnt natural gas is flowing from the burner into the room resulting in an explosive and poisoning hazard.  If the flame happened to not go out when the knob was turned from Med-Hi to Med, the flame level increases.  If the knob continues to be turned to Med-Low, the flame level decreases to a Med-Low level, operating correctly.  If the knob is turned to Low area, the flame level continues to decrease to a low level, operating correctly.

Now going the other direction, if the flame is still lit and the knob is turned from Low to the Med-Low area, the burner outputs more gas, the flame level increases, operating correctly.  If the knob continues to be turned from Med-Low to Med area, the burner outputs more gas, the flame level increases, operating correctly.  If the knob continues to be turned from Med area to Med-Hi area, the burner outputs less gas, the flame level decreases often to the point of going out.  If the knob continues to be turned from Med-Hi to High position, the gas output of the burner increases.  If the flame went out when it was turned to Med-Hi, the burner is now outputting unburnt natural gas at the high setting.   This is a major safety hazard because now unburnt natural gas is flowing from the burner into the room resulting in an explosive and poisoning hazard.

When a pan or pot is sitting on the grate over the burner, it blocks easy viewing of the burner.  With the major safety hazard described above, the operator doesn't even know the flame has gone out when cooking and adjusting the temperature.  We can be using a fry pan on the burner with it set to Hi, turn the knob down to Med, and not even realize that the flame went out when it was turned past Med-Hi and now the burner is outputting unburnt natural gas into the kitchen.  To make it even more dangerous, upon realizing this, if one turns the burner to the Off position, it passes through area on the knob that causes the electric igniter for the burner to activate.  This then ignites the unburnt natural gas causing a flash flame to occur with the unburnt natural gas in the area of the burner.  This has burnt the hair on my arm on one occasion.  

The appliances was purchased on 10/7/15.  The defect was reported to Electrolux on 8/4/16.  Electrolux has had 6 scheduled service visit to repair the appliances under warranty on 8/9/16, 8/16/16, 9/20/16, 11/7/16, 11/11/16, and 12/9/16.  The defect was demonstrated and reproduced by the Electrolux service technician.  Electrolux has made adjustments and replaced parts on the appliance with no resolution to the defect.  I have requested repair of the defect or reimbursement of the purchase price 10+ times to Electrolux.  They are now being deceptive claiming the appliance is no longer under warranty since the one year warranty period has passed since the 10/7/15 purchase date.  This is despite the defect being reported to Electrolux and three of the scheduled service visits occurring well within the one year warranty period.  To add to it, in order to not be liable, they will no longer communicate with me on resolving the defect via any electronic or written means despite doing so with dozens of emails from 8/4/16 to beginning of December timeframe.  They will now only communicate via voice.  Despite weeks since the 12/9/16 sixth attempted service visit, they have not scheduled a seventh visit to repair the defect.  They continue to be deceptive and illusive on resolving this major safety defect with natural gas.
justification: The incident involves a gas range releasing unburnt natural gas, posing explosive and poisoning hazards, and has already caused a burn injury.
