(11/26/2016)The consumer stated that he and his family was in the family room. They smelled smoke. He went into the kitchen and saw smoke coming out of the bottom of the refrigerator. When the consumer pulled the refrigerator from the wall, he saw flames coming from the right bottom of the unit.

The consumer unplugged the unit. By the time he got a fire extinguisher, the flames had fizzled out.

The consumer called the fire department, who came out. They removed the unit from the house They inspected the unit and suspected that the fire started in the condenser.

(11/26/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. He was advised that the unit was out of warranty. He was provided with a list of electrician to contact at a cost to him.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the refrigerator, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer was cleaning her refrigerator when she noticed that the plastic light cover had melted. The consumer states that the plastic light cover is about the size of a dollar bill. The consumer indicates that the light bulb was replaced around the same time she noticed the its cover had melted.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative she spoke to informed her that they would have to send a Service Technician to inspect her unit. The Service Technician inspected the refrigerator but found nothing wrong. The refrigerator is no longer under warranty so the consumer must pay out-of-pocket to replace the plastic light cover. The consumer bought an extended warranty with the retailer and will find out if this part is covered.

The consumer plans on keeping the refrigerator for at least the next thirty days in case an investigations ensues.
justification: The incident involved a melted plastic light cover with no reported injury or death, and the refrigerator was found to be functioning properly upon inspection.

incident_description: Bought LG oven in December 2008.  Oven began randomly overheating in 2011.  I thought it was just user error or that I had mis-set it.  Then, I was cooking at 350ÃÂº and the smoke alarm went off -- I came in from the other room to find my cookies were on fire in the oven and f9 displayed on the display.  In researching what could be wrong, found the product recall that was issued in 2012.  No one had ever notified me, despite having bought it at Best Buy and registering the purchase.  I notified LG.  Tech was sent a MONTH LATER and the product was "repaired."  Cooking meat in the oven less than a week later, it again incinerated the pan and meal.  Using oven thermometer -- oven went up over 700ÃÂº!  Called LG again -- waited another 3 weeks.  Oven was "repaired" -- did the same thing and another tech was sent.  All together I went more than 3 months without an oven.  Thought it was finally fixed.  This weekend -- ON CHRISTMAS while cooking the ham, the oven went up to 800ÃÂºF ruining dinner.  It happens out of NO WHERE -- smoke filled the house and the display read F9.  Thank god I was home and paying attention.  This could kill someone.  Called LG --- at first they tried to say I was "out of warranty" and tried to arrange for me to pay.  I argued and 58 minutes later, I was given to the recall department and she gave me a case number and informed me that she submitted it for approval and I will receive a call back if it is approved within 48 business hours.
justification: The oven repeatedly overheats to dangerous levels (700-800°F), causing fires and smoke, posing a significant risk of injury or death if unattended.

incident_description:
cover on calphalon  3.5 qt exploded glass.
are you going to replace? i got receipt
[REDACTED]
send me box to return
i will report this to consumer product safety commission
CALPHALON DOES NOT ANSWER THE PHONE.
THEY'RE APPARENTLY TOO CHEAP TO SUPPLY GOOD CUSTOMER SERVICE.
justification: The description mentions an exploded glass cover but does not report any injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
On Sunday evening 12/18/2016 I was preparing to bake pasta in my Pyrex 9x13 glass dish, purchased 11/15. 
I had cooked the pasta and drained it and spooned it into the Pyrex dish on my counter. The dish had not been heated or cooled, it came out of my cabinet. I turned around to get the jar of sauce to put over the pasta before I put it in the oven. Before I turned back to the dish the whole dish exploded with the pasta and cheese inside. It ttotally startled me, it was like a gun went off.  Glass went everywhere in my kitchen, in my vent and disposal. It took hours to clean and it was a complete miracle that there where no injuries. We reported the incident to Pyrex and they offered us a new dish, like I would want that! 
This was a horrendous experience and could have caused incredible damage and injury. I have 4 young  grandchildren. I can't even fathom what I would have done if they were in my kitchen. I know how to handle cookware, I taught teach injury prevention to child care providers for many years. 
I researched Pyrex dishes exploding and it's apparently been happening for many years. Why is this product not recalled?!
I used Pyrex for over 40 years, never again. Unbelievable.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish exploding, causing significant mess and potential danger, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I had purchased these Tomme Teppee cups for my grandchildren.Shortly afterwards the inserts were recalled as mold was stuck in the middle.I was then sent clear inserts and now have noticed that mold is in them.This is very dangerous and disturbing.Why are these inserts not made so that one can take them apart to clean them and dry them out.I now have five cups which are useless as I refuse to allow my grandchildren to drink from them with  mold.I would like replacement cups that do not have an insert that can get moldy.
justification: Mold in the cups poses a health risk, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We purchased an electric Macaroni & Cheese cooker called "Mac & Cheese Nation" at the Tuesday Morning retail outlet.  It is the Model MAC-1E distributed by a company called SmartPlanet.  Its web site is www.smartplanethome.com and the label on the bottom of the product claims that it conforms to UL STD. 1026 and CSA Std. C22.2 No. 64.  It also has the statement "Intertek 3123002" and "Made in China."

The first time we used it we added water according to the directions and plugged it in.   It started to boil quite quickly -- and then all the water started pouring out of the vent slots in the bottom -- running all over the wiring and heating element.  This is a very dangerous fault.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous fault with boiling water leaking onto wiring and heating elements, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I desperately need your help.

I purchased a Samsung gas range, model number NX58H5600SS, serial number OBGG67DDG704739B, from Lowe's Home Improvement in Chino Hills, CA on November 13, 2015. I also purchased a five year EPP Major Appliance Protection Plan at the same time. Lowe's reduced the price of this range, as a courtesy to me, due to two prior Samsung deliveries having scratches on the ranges after opening the crates at my home. The Lowe's assistant store manager, [REDACTED], told me at that time, that Samsung would make the store absorb the loss of the damaged ranges. That was Samsung's policy. I don't understand, why a retailer like Lowe's, continues doing business with Samsung. Their policy does not make "good business sense."

My problems all started after I used the self-cleaning feature October 4, 2016. To my surprise, after the oven cooled down, the bottom of my oven was completely shattered. I reported the problem to Samsung the morning of October 5, 2016. I had to email customer service a copy of my receipt and photos of the damage before they would even consider helping me. Originally, Samsung told me my range was out of warranty due to the date of my range.

They agreed to have [REDACTED], Lynwood, CA come out and repair may oven after providing Samsung with proper documentation. [REDACTED] was the tech that came out. He was very surprised that Samsung even agreed to fix the damage. He told me that Samsung automatically considers self-cleaning issues to be customer error, regardless of what happens. He also said that Samsung doesn't tell the public their policy, they just deny coverage. He went on to explain by using this feature, the seals fail and the mechanism that controls the heat also fails. They fail due to the high temperature that is used when cleaning the oven. Self-cleaning features are big selling points when purchasing a new range. Samsung should be making full disclosure of their policies to the public. Excluding coverage is dishonest and an unfair practice. The consumer needs to be protected

Samsung did however send out the parts to repair my oven including a new oven door. Unfortunately, after [REDACTED] opened the box with the new door in it, we immediately found a three-inch imperfection across the front door. Originally, I reported the damaged door as having a scratch and not an imperfection. I don't know the difference. I'm a consumer and not an expert on damage control. It was under the protective plastic covering packaged by the manufacture. It was obvious that Samsung shipped a damaged door from their factory. The box that the door was in was in perfect condition. Therefore, the door was shipped that way.

Since the door was damaged, [REDACTED] packed up the box and told me that he would calibrate my oven when he came back with the new door. I agreed. However, [REDACTED], Lowe's appliance manager, didn't want me to use the oven until it was calibrated. He was afraid of a potential fire. Since Samsung's smart phones and washing machines were catching fire, he was concerned for my safety. He didn't know if my oven was the beginning of another new Samsung problem.

When [REDACTED] reordered the oven door, Samsung denied it. They told their service company, [REDACTED], Lowe's appliance manager, and myself that they do not warrant cosmetic damages. After I called Samsung again, they told me to call [REDACTED]. [REDACTED], the office manager was rude, nasty and disrespectful. He told me to fight with Samsung myself. It wasn't his problem. He also insisted that [REDACTED] calibrated my oven when he came out the first time. He wouldn't even listen to an explanation of what happened in my home. He further told me that he would call the next day and he never did. For Samsung to be using a service company like this, only tells me that they do not really care about their consumers.

Samsung insists that they only send out "PERFECT PRODUCTS" AND ARE NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CONDITION OF THE PARTS THAT ARRIVE AT YOUR HOME. They told me if I wanted my oven fixed, I would need to pay $350.00 for a new door and a $160.00 service call. Since I did not accept delivery of the damaged oven door, it was now my responsibility to fix the problem myself. Being forced to accept delivery of a damaged oven door with a three-inch imperfection is ludicrous.

I've made 13 telephone calls to Samsung and [REDACTED], Lowe's appliance manager, made about the same. They refuse to replace my oven door. This all happened within the 1 year parts and labor warranty. There is no reason why I should have to pay to get my oven door replaced. The "PUBLIC" needs to made aware of Samsung's policies. When calling Samsung, they either cancel your request for assistance without talking to you or they hang up on you during your conservation. They do not call you back either. Their Executive Customer Service Department is not any better. Calling Samsung is a complete waste of time.

I am so angry with Samsung's business practices, I have written to the investigative reporting teams of Channels 4 and 7 in the Los Angeles area. I am also asking them for their assistance to help me resolve this issue between Samsung, Lowe's and myself. I am disabled, on a fixed income of Social Security, trying to make ends meet. They are treating me unfairly. Samsung should be Investigated.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated help.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a damaged oven door and potential safety concerns, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This consumer purchased his electric range on October 8th, 2014 and had no problems other than a touchpad being replaced August 2016.
His wife was running the self cleaning option on November 27, 2016 when the inner glass to the oven door exploded sending glass shards all over the inside of the oven.
There are no injuries being reported
Monday, November 28, 2016 the caller forwarded pictures to the manufacturer and was provided with a date of December 6, 2016 for the techs to come to his home to estimate damage.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On 12/24/16, we were sitting in the living room watching TV,  when we heard a large pop from the kitchen. Upon investigation, we saw that the glass in the oven door was shattered.  The range was not in use,  there was no odors, and no heat was on.  We only had the range for 3 years and it shatters?
justification: The oven glass shattered unexpectedly, but no injuries or further incidents occurred.

incident_description: I have a 2 yr old ge range that is in a second home in [REDACTED] and rarely used.  On Christmas Eve I prepared a turkey breast, cooked bacon, then set my oven to self clean.  After approximately 40 minutes a electric wire burning smell along with smoke permeated our home.  I checked on the oven and upon walking in the middle class of the door exploded in pro a thousand pcs.  I turned off the function, the breaker and brought in a fire extinguisher as I had no idea what to expect.  After 30 min I was able to unlock the door and upon opening all of the glass slid out from the door like a glass slot machine.   I contacted ge and they will not replace the oven because it is out if warrantee.  There has to be something wrong as I rarely use the oven and this was the first time I used the self clean function.  Now I'm expected to pay for what is an obvious mfg defect.
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction causing smoke and glass explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The Cuisinart DLC-10E food processor 4mm slicing disk (part number FP-104) was being used to slice cabbage to make cole slaw. I noticed that the slicing disk was making noise and, upon inspection, I saw that the rivets that attach the metal slicing disk to the plastic stem were loose. The plastic stem was cracked where the rivets attach to it and the plastic from the stem was loose in the food processor. There are three rivets that hold the plastic stem to the slicing disk and two of the rivets have been compromised, rendering the blade unsafe and unusable. No injuries were sustained, but the potential for accidental ingestion of plastic from the stem or being hit by it exists.
justification: The incident involved a compromised food processor part with potential for harm but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I read about the Cuisinart blade recall. I have two Cuisinarts. Examining them both, both have cracked blades. The [REDACTED] blade was covered by the replacement. The DLC-2A which is also cracked was not covered by the recall. It should be as it shows the same cracking that caused the other riveted blades to require replacement. 

No injury or damage, but potential is present as in the larger recalled blades.
justification: No injury or damage occurred, but cracked blades present a potential hazard, similar to the recalled blades.

incident_description: Cooking on small t-fal pan suddenly metal cups covering screws of the handle inner side of the pan exploded, making very loud noise, piece found 3 feet away. Luckily no one hurt.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of a pan handle component, causing a loud noise and debris, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
While using my kitchen aid oven on Sunday the outside oven door glass shattered and sent glass across the kitchen, hitting my son in a couple places. The oven had only been on for 20 minutes and was only at 250 degrees. 2 weeks prior, the hinges on the oven door were replaced by a service technician from Sears. This was the first time we used the oven since it was fixed.
The oven is about 13 years old and we have never had a problem with this until the hinge started locking up. 
The inside glass did not break.

No one I know has ever had this happen to them!

We have a technician from Sears coming to the house tomorrow to check it out. Should we allow them to work on the oven again?
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the son from shattered glass, but no death occurred. The likelihood is rare as it's an unusual occurrence and the first time it happened after oven repair.

incident_description: I have the Cuisinart Baby Food Maker & Bottle Warmer. I used it to steam and process carrots for my baby. Upon rewarming them up, in a microwave safe dish, the carrots started to spark due to metal in the microwave. The blade of the food processing part released metal shavings into the carrots.
justification: The incident involved metal sparking in the microwave but no injury was reported, making it a minor incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
I have the Martha Stewart 10-piece stainless steel cookware which is the subject of recall 16-067.

This evening, while cooking a pan of squash, the 7-inch lid for one of the pans shattered.  While the lid remained intact the entire glass part of the lid broke into a thousand little pieces (safety glass).

No one was injured.
justification: The lid shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was lifting a 9x13 baking dish out of my kitchen cabinet.  The cabinet has slots and is surrounded by inside walls.  The temperature of the cabinet was about 72 degrees F.  As I started to lift the dish, it exloded in my hand.  It did NOT bang against anything.  It was NOT dropped.  It exploded!
justification: The baking dish exploded in the person's hand, which could reasonably cause injury.

incident_description: Using oven to bake a roast and 5 minutes into cooking the glass door exploded.
justification: The glass door exploding is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I was checking my blade since Bed Bath and Beyond sent me an email stating I own or have purchased a food processor on the recall notice for [REDACTED]. I checked my Hamilton Beach food processor and discovered it has the exact same blade as what was recalled and also has the four rivets. 

One of the rivets is broken off, which I have never noticed before today. No one has been injured, but I think it's worth further investigation. 

Model Hamilton beach model 70700
Serial B1179w

I also have photos if necessary.

incident_description: Our gently and well cared for Kitchen Selectives 1.5 quart Slow Cooker Model # SC-15 flashed / exploded on our kitchen counter top after it was moved 1inch.  We unplugged the unit immediately.  When we lifted it off of the counter top there was a black flash burn mark on the counter top and also on the bottom of the unit where the power cord connects. The explosion caused the power cord to separate from the unit as if someone had cut it off leaving a stub of copper wire.  In addition to a potential shock hazard, this unit could have caused a fire.  If we were not home at the time we could have lost our home.  There was obviously a defect / short circuit in the power cord where it connected to the unit.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: my sears kenmore dishwasher model 665.17022401 serial number FS1305738 started on fire as it was operating on 12/23/16.  Flames were coming out of the unit and the plastic began to burn.  The unit was unplugged and the fire stopped.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: The oven has begun to bow in the middle so that the racks aren't held up. As a result, while I was cooking dinner, the rack fell, spilled oil and started a fire in my oven. I was able to put it out, but in the end I had to let it burn its way through the oil.
justification: The oven rack failure caused a fire, which was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she is experiencing problems with the icemaker, plastic pieces tends to break off in the ice posing a choking hazard to users.  She stated that the icemaker has been broken twice and that it does not operate properly.  She stated that she has replaced it twice at her expense.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this icemaker is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: Plastic pieces breaking off in the ice pose a choking hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
We loaded our dishwasher with a typical load of dishes just before going to bed for the evening. We used a normal wash cycle with a heated dry. We went to bed. Just before going to sleep, I smelled smoke in the house. I ran downstairs to the kitchen and opened the running dishwasher. An acrid black smoke what smelled like burning circuit-board was belching out of the washer door latch. The inside of the door was quite hot to the touch. The door continued to remain hot until I shut down the circuit breaker for the washer at our main box. Besides some inhaling of the tarry smoke, no injuries were sustained (THOUGH I WOULD HATE TO THINK IF THIS HAD HAPPENED AFTER WE WERE ASLEEP). The house continues to smell like burned phenolic resin 5 days after the event.

We read about the 2010 recall on our model washer the next day. We called the GE hotline to report the incident. They indicated that, based on our machines history, the recall "fix" had already been performed for the previous home owner.

The GE service tech was out to the house 5 days later. He went inside the washer door and discovered that a wire harness attaching to the main controller board was quite burned, as well as the controller board itself, a Computime 663C, GE model no 165D7305G003. Surrounding plastic was also melted. The tech offered to replace/repair the burned parts for free. He could not guarantee that the controller board would not flame up again. We turned down the repair and will replace the washer.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injuries were sustained, aligning with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the specific circumstances and the recall history of the dishwasher model.

incident_description:
I own many Breville products and have given two of their smaller convections to both of my older children.  I purchase these products for their perceived quality.  Unfortunately my oven door spring broke and has now rendered my oven unsafe and unusable. This is clearly a design flaw on this model and repairs should be covered by extended warranty.  Paying excessive $100 charge to replace defective and poorly designed spring is unacceptable.  I like the item and products, but this problem and design issue is a challenge.  Absent a satisfactory response of free repair or replacement from Breville, I will be forced to publish incident informal to their major distribution channels.
I believe this is both a fire and safety hazard to my home.
justification: The incident involves a broken oven door spring, which is described as a safety hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Maytag gas stove from Sears applicable center in Pearland, TX. Sears professionally installed the stove. Within 2 months the clear coat on the top of the stove began to come off the paint. We contacted Sears who agreed to replace the top. Within 2 months the clear coat again began bubbling and coming off the stove, within  few months the black paint began to come off in spots. We were told that the 1 year warranty was up. We are not sure if the stove is safe to operate with flames and peeling paint.

The next issue is the stove has knobs located in the front of the stove, when the oven or burners are used, the knobs get hot and a child could get burned.

We have only used this stove to cook in a single family household. We have used the self cleaning oven 1 time. We have never used abrasives to clean the stove as directed.

This stove is not safe to use around our grandchildren or disabled people nor is it safe to operate for possible fire hazard.

This stove should be recalled as a hazard.
justification: The stove's peeling paint and hot knobs pose a potential burn hazard, especially to children and disabled individuals, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I have a 3-cup Cuisinart food processor (DFP-3) that has a cracked blade.  The blade has metal shards that are about to fall off and looks just like the larger recalled units.  Cuisinart has refused to replace this blade and has told me the unit is safe to use.  The unit clearly poses a laceration hazard and should be added to the Cuisinart recall!
justification: The cracked blade with metal shards poses a laceration hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: An article about the Cuisinart food processor blade recall said the CPSC would like reports of blade breakage. My DLC-10E Cuisinart blade shattered while processing hummus in February 2016. I did not file any complaint, but ordered a new blade from Cuisinart's website. After waiting over a month with the status of Backorder, I cancelled my order. In June I placed another order, and received a new blade that is constructed differently; presumably they had fixed the problem. The blade cost $52 which Cuisinart will not reimburse, but will instead send me a replacement blade per the recall program. I don't need a second blade, but I guess I should have asked for a replacement back in February.
justification: The blade shattered during use, but no injury was reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: I have a cuisinart DLC2 min prep food processor that has two obvious cracks at the rivets in the metal blade however I just called cuisinart and they informed me despite this obvious defect my machine is not "covered by the recall" but they would gladly sell me a blade for about 20$ I think this blade is about to fly apart and presents the same hazard as with all the other riveted blades that were recalled. Not sure why CPSC did not include this machine in its recall...
justification: The food processor blade has cracks but no incident or injury has occurred yet, though there is a possible risk of the blade flying apart.

incident_description: I was using my food processor to chop and heard a metallic sound banging around in the processor.  When I inspected it, the bottom part of the blade had broken off.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade in a food processor but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On Dec. 25, 2016 we detected a strong odor of gas in our home. I contacted the Fire Department and a crew was dispatched to the house, which we had already evacuated. The crew detected a concentration of gas in the living quarters which would have sustained an ignition / explosion. The source of the gas was a burner on a newly purchased gas range / oven, which had moved from the off position to a point which allowed gas to pass to the burner, but had not allowed the ignitor to spark.

Once in the past, my wife had leaned over the gas range to reach something and the burner turned on and did ignite. This situation was better than having the gas flow to the burner without being ignited. I feel hat the design of the burner controls (dials) or the gas valves (do not turn off securely) are defective and will eventually result in fires, explosions, injuries or deaths.

The manufacturer (Whirlpool) was contacted and stated that they would report this incident to you, but I advised them that I would also make a first person report. Whirlpool's safety department indicated that a service technician would check out the unit on Thursday, Dec. 29 between 0800-1600.

I feel that this matter requires immediate attention.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with potential for explosion, but no injury or death occurred. The recurrence is possible given the defective burner controls.

incident_description: My mini prep pluses not listed in a recall and the plastic around the blade is all cracked and could separate at any given moment
justification: The cracked plastic around the blade poses a potential hazard but there is no indication of injury or death in the description.

incident_description:
I want to report an incident with the Cuisinart Food Processor, the same one that recently launched a recall due to the disintegrating blade.

Earlier this year my wife bit into some food that she blended with the food processor and felt a sharp piece of metal. Fortunately she felt it before it cut her mouth open.

We bought a new blade on Amazon and did not report it at the time. Seeing this recall announcement reminded us that we needed to report for the safety of others.
justification: The incident involved a potential injury from a disintegrating blade, but no actual injury occurred as the metal piece was detected before causing harm.

incident_description: I reheated a cup of coffee for 30 in the microwave. When taking it out, the handle was so hot I got 2nd degree burns on three fingers.  The mug says Microwave and  dishwasher safe. The brand is Royal Norfolk- Greenbrier international
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree burns on three fingers, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Elite Dishwasher model number 665.16263402 caught on fire while we were sleeping.  We were able to detect something was wrong and open the breaker in our home panel.  Following simple online repair procedures I was hoping it was a fuse replacement; however when I opened the dishwasher cover plate I found Whirlpool P/N 8564546 circuit board caught on fire and melted through the back cover and three of the connector plugs.  

I attempted to call Sears Home Services at 1-800-549-4505 when I found information online that there may be a recall on these models.  Sears was not willing to do anything about it without the consumer paying for an evaluation of their faulty product.  This is concerning considering if we weren't home to open the breaker; we may not have had a home to come to.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred as the fire was contained by opening the breaker.

incident_description: Staples spoon cut approx 1/2 inch of tongue - sharp edge causing blood to be released.
justification: The description indicates a cut causing bleeding, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
This Pyrex Baking dish measured about 6inches X 10inches and was approximately 2 inches deep. The dish was brown glass and was many years old. My husband was baking a pork loin roast in it. He baked it at 400 degrees for 40 minutes. He decided to turn on the broiler for about 2 minutes. The broiler unit was about 6 inches away from the roast. 

On completion, he turned off the oven and extracted the dish placing it on a cold burner on the stove top. After approximately 45 seconds the dish exploded with a loud cracking sound showering glass in all directions 4 to 6 inches. The pieces were shards and of course hot. Picking them up became doubly dangerous because of their shard like edges, splinters and due to the heat. No one was injured by the explosion, but I did burn a finger trying to pick up one of the shards.

It was a startling event, needless to say, and could have had much more dire consequences had some one been close when it exploded. Concerned because I'm not sure what triggered the event. We have other pieces of Pyrex of similar vintage. I know the broiler use is discouraged, but it was for such a brief duration. Not many folks remember manufacturers recommendations 20 or 30 years down the road.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burned finger) from handling hot glass shards, and the likelihood is unlikely given the specific conditions required for the dish to explode.

incident_description: Photo of Cuisinart Food Processor recalled 4-rivet cutter blade showing crack at rivet.
justification: The description indicates a recalled product with a defect (cracked blade), which poses a potential hazard but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
(11/14/2016) The consumer turned the oven on to preheat to 350 degrees. She was getting a pan out of the cupboard. She heard a pop. The pop was the glass on the door of the oven. The glass on the exterior of the oven door had shattered. Nothing was in the oven at the time. The oven had been on for less than five minutes.

(11/16/2016) The consumer contacted the firm to advised them of the incident. A report was taken and the consumer was advised that someone would get in touch with her within 24 hours.

 No one contacted the consumer.
justification: The glass on the oven door shattered, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her convection oven glass door shattered while in use.  The incident occurred after the toast was completed which she was alerted by the timer sound.  She then heard a weird noise and then she noticed the glass shattered but stayed in place.

Caller stated that she tried to contact the manufacturer, however, it was long wait time.

Caller feels that this toaster is a safety hazard and should be reported.

12/7/16  Oster advised caller's model was exclusive to Wal-Mart.  Caller gave them her report no: and will ship until back to them directly after they after they ship replacement under 5 yr warrantee.  It too several calls to get Oster.  Finally able to get help after providing numbers on the plug.
justification: The glass door shattered but stayed in place, causing no injury, and the incident was resolved under warranty.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite refrigerator model 795.77544600 was in normal use.  Internal refrigerator light started to flicker intermittently when the door was open, as if the bulb was starting to go, then would work fine.  Recently In the middle of the night we noticed a glow from between the french doors and found that even though the doors were shut, the light had stayed on causing the internal light fixtures to burn and housing around the light an items on the top shelf to melt.  Door switch was functioning properly to sense door closed (otherwise it would alarm).
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator and items inside but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was baking Christmas cookies last night and as I went to open my oven door, the glass layer on the outside of the door just exploded everywhere...all over my kitchen floor!  I sat there in disbelief.  I couldn't believe what just happened.  The oven was only on 350, and I didn't even have it on for that long.
justification: The oven glass exploded but there was no injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
I read about the Cuisinart blade recall. I have two Cuisinarts. Examining them both, both have cracked blades. The DFP-11 blade was covered by the replacement. The [REDACTED] which is also cracked was not covered by the recall. It should be as it shows the same cracking that caused the other riveted blades to require replacement.

No injury or damage, but potential is present as in the larger recalled blades.
justification: No injury or damage occurred, but potential is present due to cracked blades.

incident_description:
We have a Proctor Silex Electric Tea Kettle that is apparently defective.
The device will rapidly boil water but sometimes the auto shut off fails to shut off.

Three days ago the kettle even turned on by itself!  

We can no longer trust this device for fear of it causing a fire in our house.

It is Type K30 Kettle.  Other numbers on the bottle: K4097  and A3151CE.
justification: The defective kettle poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: DLC-10E--BLADE THAT SLICES (IS ON A LONG WHITE PLASTIC STEM)...IT BROKE...PIECES OF PLASTIC ARE IN THE FOOD UNKNOWINGLY,
justification: Plastic pieces entered food, posing a risk, but no injury reported.

incident_description:
On approximately December 4th I was mixing Christmas cookies, using my Culslnart DLC2009 to chop pecan halves,
when the side of the clear mixing container cracked. In addition to that the top of the lid to the mixing container began to crack at the safety lock point. I did use It again later to cream sume butter, but when I held the safty lock lid down (as it would not mix without me doing so), the plastic broke even further & it is now unusable. When I went online to report this Incident, there was a recall on the blade. I am not certain If the blade lifted up whlld chopping the nuts or if it was simply inferior plastic materials which caused the damage, but the food processor no longer can be used with te broken lid & mixing container. Please note: this Is my second Culslnart Food Processor & my first one I purchased in about 2012, had a problem with the plastic mixing container cracking also. I think it creates an unsafe situation becuse the plastic could crack become weak & break Into pieces while In use.
justification: The incident involved a cracked mixing container and lid, rendering the food processor unusable, but no injury was reported. The recurrence of similar issues with previous models suggests the likelihood is high.

incident_description:
Blade on mini chopperessor fracturing
I have photos but your site won't let me upload them
justification: The description mentions a blade fracturing, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart model  DLC2011BC. In July, 2014, I noticed the metal blade was cracked at the rivets and pieces of the metal were missing. At that time I bought a new blade and discraded the old blade. Though I assume the metal pieces were lost in the processing of food, no one was injured as a result.
justification: The incident involved a cracked blade with missing metal pieces, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I bought a frigidaire cook top model fpec3085ks 2 1/2 years ago which worked well until 11/16. The cook top turned itself on at 2 am and melted a food steamer I left on the cook top. Yes I know not to smart of me. I could not turn the burner off no matter what I tried and ended up flipping the breaker. I called customer support and was told this is not their problem as they only offer a 1 year warranty.  So in short I almost lost my house by fire I lost a $850 cook top and a $250 food steamer. I will spend a lot of time posting this warning on every blog, review board and web site that will listen. Do not by from this dishonest company that knowingly sell dangerous products. If you don't believe me just goggle "frigidaire cook top turned itself on" you will find this is not an uncommon occurrence. Thanks for reading.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted steamer and cooktop) and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
while performing a self clean mode on our Kitchenaid KEBS208SSS dual wall oven, the inner glass of the top unit emitted a large BANG , almost like an explosion. We checked the oven and saw that the inner glass panel was split into thousands of fragments of glass. The force was so strong that chards of glass were pushed thru the steel mesh gasket while the oven door was still locked. glass pieces were found on the floor as far as eight feet away.
we stopped the self clean process and allowed the unit to cool.
 hours later we cleaned up the glass pieces with a shop vac.
Contacted KItchenaid...very concerned however would NOT cover repair because unit was 7 years old.
 not willing to accept ownership of a defect in their product.
shameful
justification: The incident involved a significant glass explosion but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was using my Cuisinart food processor to make the filling for a sweet potato pie. As I poured the pie filling into a bowl, I noticed a dark fleck of metal in the mix. I saw a similarly shaped piece missing on the underside of the food processor blade. I managed to remove the metal piece from the filling but I was not comfortable eating the pie and threw it out to avoid injury. I have been trying to find a replacement blade and was unsuccessful. I saw the recall notice and finally realized why I couldn't find a blade. Honestly, the most frustrating part of this has been the difficulty from not being able to use my food processor.
justification: The incident involved a metal fleck in food but no injury occurred, and the issue was mitigated by discarding the affected food.

incident_description: I was given a gift of All Clad LTD pots and pans set. A month later the product started to change. The outside layer of the pots and pans started to warp and become very sharp. My family and I have sustained injury from using them, and we have damaged our cooktop as well. The pots have caused our hands to bleed from use. We followed all of the care instructions, we washed by hand with a gentle soap and soft cloth and use our electric cooktop, so no high heat is used. We have well water that is pure water. Once we noticed the problem with the cookware we sent an email to the company. They responded by saying me as the consumer must have placed them in the dishwasher, or used acid to wash the pots and pans. We also were acccused of cleaning them with drano. The company claims to have a lifetime warranty, but they will not replace my pots. They have told me for safety reasons to discard my pots because they are causing harm. Company claims they cannot do anything for me because they are not in their eyes defective. If they are not defective, why do I have to discard them.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bleeding hands) and property damage (cooktop), but no death was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as the issue appears to be specific to this set under certain conditions.

incident_description:
Piece of metal broke off bottom of blade, got into food.  No injury.

Cuisinart DLC-7FPC
justification: A piece of metal broke off into food, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: My Cuisinart blade broke off and I found pieces of metal in the hummus that I had made in the device.
justification: The blade breaking off is an incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On November 30,2016 I was using my Food Network Large Capacity Convection Oven and Rotisserie.  I had thought that it was a great space saver and energy efficient option for cooking and baking.  I had used it a few times before and had had no troubles with it. I was carrying my one year old daughter in one arm and reached above the oven to get something from the cupboard.  Her hand was brushing the outside of the oven, which I thought nothing of, although she became cranky.  A few minutes later I noticed that her fingers were red and a small blister was forming.  I ran her hand under cold water and went in search of what could have burnt her.  I found that the metal strip behind the handle was scorching hot. There was no warning on the oven or in the manual for the oven.  My daughter ended up receiving medical attention for her fingers, two of which ended up blistering.
justification: The incident resulted in a child sustaining blisters requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart mini food processor and the blade is cracked. After watching good morning America and the recall I am following the recall instructions.
justification: The blade is cracked, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have a Moulinex La Machine II food processor and it has the same blade cracks as reported in the recent [REDACTED] recall.  There are cracks in the blade at 2 of the the four rivets on the bottom and there are cracks starting around 3 of the four rivets on the top blade. Looks to be a very similar design from the TV news reports.  There has not been a failure of the blades at this time.
justification: The food processor blade has cracks but no failure or injury has occurred, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: After 1 year of light use the blade of my Cuisinart Dfp-14bcn has cracked and lost a couple small pieces. Thankfully no lnow injuries have occurred but I only noticed after seeing the recall. Larger pieces were broken through and lose near most of the rivets on the blades. Injury was imminent.
justification: The blade cracked and lost small pieces, but no injuries occurred. The description indicates injury was imminent, suggesting a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: Our cuisinart blade has a crack through a rivet.
justification: A cracked blade poses a potential hazard but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The consumer heard a loud explosion and when she walked in the kitchen she noticed glass everywhere. The consumer indicated that the glass pieces were several feet from the unit. The consumer states that the outer glass exploded and the inner glass is still intact. The unit was not being used when the glass exploded and the last time it was used was on Thanksgiving, 11/24/2016. The consumer indicated that she used the unit to heat up food and does not use the unit to cook food.

The consumer contacted the firm (800-243-0000) to inform them of the incident and the consumer was advised that the unit was out of warranty and they could not assist her.

The unit is used once a day.

There are no prior incidents. 

The consumer indicated that she plans to purchase another unit from a different manufacturer. 

The consumer is really concerned with the safety of the unit and believes if someone was near the unit when the glass exploded they could have been seriously injured.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing glass shattering but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as the unit is used daily but this is the first such incident.

incident_description: This report regards a Kenmore Elite model 790.9912,serial # VF53157197. I was heating up oil in a fry pan on the large element. I started on high but soon after moved to 3.5 heat setting. What i did not know was that the very inner element stayed on high. I was wondering why the last batch of egg rolls I was cooking was coming out burnt when cooked in the middle of the pan. I tried to turn off the the element and it would not turn off. I repeatedly tried to turn it off to no avail. I had to throw the breaker to eventually to get it to go off. I  did some research and found your website with a recall of the Kenmore Elite 790 back in August of 2009.One of the model #'s for the recall was 790.99012 not the 790.9912  that I have, which I find weird since I bought it in 2005 during the time these recalled ranges were made. How does the paint color designation code change the recall or is it just a time frame tool? I believe that the recall should be expanded to all Kenmore Elite 790's that experience the same problem. How many service calls has Sears taken for this problem in the last 7 years and because there is not a specific recall on a specific model they have no obligation to report the problem to you. I am taking the time to report this to you and also did the research to find the exact problem I was experiencing.How many other people would do this, probably a small percentage. Most people would just call Sears and say "Oh well, it is ten years old". Of course I also called Sears to have them come out as we all need a range or oven at some point that will not burn your house down. I called the Sears recall resource center and they said my range is not covered but that the service man would double check, but I am not holding out much hope. Sears will be out tommorrow
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove element that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The exterior glass of the oven door exploded as I was opening the hot oven. Shards flew all over the kitchen, thousands of them. Kenmore Gas Range Model 790.3690.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, causing shards to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
After hearing of the Cuisinart Food Processor recall last week I went to check our Cuisinart food processor.  The model number on the bottom says it is a model BFP703 or BFP703C (I will attach a photo showing the model and serial number).  The recalled models do NOT list this model as being recalled.  

However, it has a similar looking blade and what is horribly alarming is that the bottom of my blade also has the four rivets and, one section of the blade's base is missing....just like the pictures of the recalled blades.  I find myself getting sick every time I try to think of where that missing section of the blade indeed is.  I am attaching a picture of the bottom of my blade.

in any event, I am writing  because it is clear that model number BFP703 should be included in the recall as well.
justification: The description indicates a potential safety issue with the food processor blade, but no actual injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I was heating some slightly cool water in an Anchor Hocking 16 oz. glass measuring cup in the microwave. I had the microwave timer set for 2 minutes. After one minute, the measuring cup exploded in the microwave with considerable force. It shattered into many very sharp pieces of glass. Fortunately the door was still closed, so no one was hurt. 

I bought this measuring cup at Target a couple of weeks ago. I had not used it in the microwave before.
justification: The glass measuring cup exploded but no one was injured as the microwave door remained closed.

incident_description:
While stirring a pan of food on the right back burner of my four burner gas range.  I must have leaned into the rangeÃÂs right front burner knob and moved to the left, causing the right front burner to spontaneously ignite, nearly causing the sleeve of my long sleeved shirt to catch fire. The knobs on this range pose two potential safely hazards.
# 1) They turn on much too easily- very little if any resistance when pushed in & rotated.
# 2) These knobs become very hot when the oven is in use, particularly if the broiler setting is on.
justification: The incident involved a near-miss with potential for injury (shirt sleeve nearly caught fire), but no actual injury occurred. The description indicates the knobs are easily turned and become hot, making recurrence likely.

incident_description:
I was using the back right burner on my Electric  Kenmore glass stove top(Model#790.9661.2407)
I used it for about 1/2 hour. All other burners were turned off. I had a plate on the front right burner.  I picked up the plate and it was burning hot. I dropped the plate because it was so hot. The hot light was not on for the front right burner. The back center burner was also hot. Hot light was not on either. So 2 burners turned on by themselves and both hot lights were not on even though the burners were hot.
justification: The incident involved burners turning on by themselves without indication, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I had puchased a Black & Decker toaster over (BLACK+DECKER TO1303SB 4-Slice Toaster Oven). I unwrapped it and removed all of the packing and packaging materials on it. I placed the oven on my granite top counter, plugged it into a socket, and put in 4 slices of toast. I selected toast on the oven and picked a medium level of browning on my toast. The glass fogged up as soon as I turned the dial to start the toasting. After about 3 minutes, I saw smoke leaking out of the oven and I opened the door and saw flames above the toast (the toast itself was not on fire), as if the filament had caught fire. The I pulled the plug from the socket and closed the oven door. After a few seconds the fire went out but my smoke alarm went off. I opened the windows to let the smoke out and subsequently opened the toaster oven. The toast was blackened, obviously. However, there were scorch marks on the inside and on the outside (see photos). I now own a kitchen fire extinguisher.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the toaster oven but no injuries occurred, only property damage and smoke.

incident_description: I was crushing gingersnaps with the metal blade for use in a pie crust when the machine started making a strange noise. I opened it and found a 1" chunk of blade had broken off and chipped other parts of the blade.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade but no injury occurred, and such equipment failures are possible during use.

incident_description: A piece of the metal blade on my Cuisinart food processor broke off. An entire section between 2 rivets broke off in one piece as I was processing cookies to make a crust. The model is DLC-2007N.
justification: A piece of the blade broke off during use, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: A few weeks ago I found a small piece of metal in a dish of pasta I had prepared using my Cuisinart food processor. I assumed it came from the can of beans I used - maybe it had been inside the can. Fortunately, I was not injured and did not ingest the fragment. When the Cuisinart recall was announced, I checked our blade and discovered that the piece of metal I had found had actually come from the bottom of our blade. Our blade is a part of the recall.
justification: The incident involved finding a metal fragment in food, but no injury or ingestion occurred, aligning with severity level 2. The recall suggests such incidents are possible but not certain.

incident_description: In addition to the current blade recall for riveted blades on specific models of Cuisinart food processors there is also a blade defect on the mini processor listed. The blade on this model is embedded in a plastic hub. This hub on our processor is cracked in two places and thus creates the potential for the entire blade to become separated from the hub at high RPMs.
justification: The cracked blade hub poses a risk of the blade separating at high RPMs, which could lead to injury if the blade detaches during use.

incident_description: The Blade broke off during use.
justification: The blade breaking off is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I bought a Cuisinart 14-Cup food processor (model DFP-14BCN) in October 2013 in the U.S. (I currently live in Canada.) 

A few months ago, I had just made salmon mousse in it and was just putting it on the table for my children when I saw some rigid shapes in the mousse. I discovered that they were broken shards of the blade, which had cracked and come apart at the rivets. I had just served the mousse to my kids. Obviously, this was very upsetting.

I called Cuisinart's consumer line about this in August but did not hear back, and I just read about the recall for this blade defect, so I'm reporting it to you this time and will try sending the information to Cuisinart again. I'm also attaching photos.

The jagged edges of the blade also apparently left scratches on the inside of the work bowl, which I hadn't immediately noticed. I'm unhappy that I did not hear back from Cuisinart when I first contacted them, and I will contact them again today to ask that a new blade and workbowl sent to replace the defective/damaged ones. I will check back with you again if I still don't hear from Cuisinart. (I know you're aware of this issue because there is now a recall, but I thought you should know about yet another instance of the defective blade.) Thank you, [REDACTED] 

*IMPORTANT: If you need to contact me about this, please use email [REDACTED] . If you need me to call you, email me and we will arrange a time. (I will be travelling in the coming months.) Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a defective blade in a food processor, which could have caused injury but did not result in any reported harm.

incident_description: My GE Profile Stainless Steel Dishwasher heating element did not turn off, melted all my dishes, and nearly caught my kitchen counter on fire. The only way to turn off the heating element was to turn off the breaker.
justification: The dishwasher's heating element malfunction caused significant damage to dishes and nearly started a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
There is presently a product recall on Cuisinart Food Processors that have a riveted blade.  The recall site states that if there are no rivets on your blade, then it is safe to continue use.  I have a Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus Food Processor, Model DLC-2A.  Prior to the recall for the food processors with the riveted blades, I had noticed that mine which is not riveted is cracked in multiple places near where the blades insert and on multiple sites on that blade piece.

There has been no injury regarding my blade but clearly it could easily happen given the multiple cracks.  Of note, is that I have only used the processor for grinding herbs and fully cooked carrots.  As well, it has never been in a dishwasher.

I called your number as listed on your site yesterday 12.15.2016 and was told I would be able to attach pictures of my blade to this report.

In the area below for the incident report, I will have to guess when I first noticed the blade in this condition.  I was just planning on replacing the unit for another brand assuming this was a singular quality control issue.  As a physician, when I saw the recall for the riveted blades, I wanted to make sure you are alerted to the fact that the non riveted blades are most likely affected and would cause the same injuries as noted in the current recall.  Of great concern is the statement on the recall site that if you don't have a riveted blade, they are safe to use.  When you see the pictures of mine, you will understand why I am writing this. I tried numerous times to call Cuisinart but continued to get either a loud busy signal or a message that there was unusually high demand and to call later.  "Calling later" has not worked.  

Thanks for your work with protecting consumers.
justification: The blade is cracked but no injury has occurred, though the potential for injury is present given the multiple cracks.

incident_description: I own a Hamilton Beach food processor, purchased in the late 1980's with the same S-blade that was just recalled on the [REDACTED] product. My s-blade, I now notice is also missing a rivet. I believe it must have been consumed. I brought it to the attention of the company this week and they sent a response denying that they made such a product. I have model number, pictures and even a video to prove that it still works. I threatened them with going to this site but they didn't seem to care. I'm looking for them to replace my blade. Is there anything your organization do to help me?
justification: The incident involves a defective product part but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the nature of product recalls and common issues with older appliances.

incident_description: Riveted blade of Cuisinart DLC 7-Pro has multiple nicks where metal has been chipped out. A triangle of steel also was chipped out next to one of the rivets.
justification: The description indicates damage to the blade but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as blade damage can occur with use but isn't guaranteed.

incident_description:
Assembly grill (part #109 on schematic) broke off PVM1870SM3SS-GE-MICROWAVE.  Plastic tabs on bottom broke and tabs for screws on top broke.  Assembly fell onto stove top.

Having this assembly fall onto a pot of boiling water or hot pan with oil would tend to flip them off the top of the stove towards where the consumer would be standing.

I found two similar complaints on the CPSC website for this model number.

Parts diagram can be viewed at http://www.appliancepartspros.com/microwave-parts-for-ge-pvm1870sm3ss.html
justification: The incident involves a part breaking off and potentially causing harm, but no actual injury is reported. Similar complaints exist, indicating a possible issue.

incident_description: The glass lid of a Crock-Pot Cook & Carry shattered when the appliance was in use.  No one was touching it at the time.
justification: The glass lid shattered during use, but no one was injured as no one was touching it at the time.

incident_description: I was using the Cuisinart Velocity Ultra 1HP blender model SPB-650 and the blade assembly came unscrewed from the plastic jar while the motor was engaged. I was pulsing cookie crumbs for a dessert and the blade assembly came completely unscrewed from the bottom of the jar, the motor was still turning and the blades were engaged. It spilled cookie crumbs all over the blender base and kitchen and I could have been injured by the blades because they were still rotating. The plastic bottom of the blade assembly where it contacts the motor base became damaged and was shredding plastic threads because it was turning in the base when it shouldn't be. I am certain the blade assembly was properly tightened and secure on the jar because this same issue happened to me last week when I attempted to make a smoothie and it leaked almond milk all over the counter when I tried to blend. I assumed I hadn't tightened it correctly the first time it happened. But this time I am certain this is a design flaw and not user error. I will be contacting Cuisinart for a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a blender blade assembly coming unscrewed during operation, posing a potential injury risk but no actual injury occurred. The recurrence of the issue suggests a likely design flaw.

incident_description: My 1-cup glass measurer exploded in the sink with no exposure to any sudden temperature changes (nor is any other glass thing that I own) and no knocking or bumping up against anything. I had used it 4-5 hours earlier when making cookies to measure out the oil needed, placed it in the sink, put cool water in it to soak, and left it alone. I have no idea what caused it to shatter like it did. I'm just glad that no one in my house got hurt.
justification: The glass measurer exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury. Such spontaneous breakage is rare but not unheard of.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her electric built in oven she purchased from retailer during the month of April 2007 in Kennesaw, Georgia. dom 2007

This caller purchased a Kenmore built in electric oven March or April 2009 years ago which she was preparing to clean November 6, 2016.

She opened the door and the entire glass in the oven door blew up in her face, however she states that she is not injured.

She contacted Sears and is stating that she was transferred to the Philippines and that they just want to schedule a repair tech to charge her approximately $79.00 and tell her what she already is aware of.

She now has visited Sears in Kennesaw, Georgia and spoke with [REDACTED] who informed her that there was nothing she could do to assist this caller.

The caller is sending a picture of the model and serial number from the unit.

There are no injuries being reported, however the caller would like to report that if a child had been sitting nearby there could have been severe injuries.

She is reporting this incident as a laceration and potentially blinding hazard.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass blowing up, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
This is in regard to an exploding oven door panels on our Bosch electric wall oven, model number HBL8450UC, serial number 921200345, purchased new, and installed on January 28, 2013.

On December 14, 2016 at approximately 5 pm, we were preparing to place a cake into our preheated 350 degree F oven.  The door was in the fully open position and my wife was walking toward the oven with raw cake batter in a pan to place it in the oven when the incident occurred.

With a loud bang like a firecracker, the inner glass panel of the door exploded.  Glass pieces were blown through the vents of the door panel onto the kitchen floor and inside the oven cavity.  Pieces of glass were found up to four feet from the oven front.

The hot shards on the vinyl flooring were swept up immediately.  The circuit breaker was turned off.  After allowing the door panel and residual glass shards in the oven and door to cool, the door was removed to the garage and the visible glass was swept up.  The appliance warranty company was contacted and a case number assigned.

At this point, we are waiting for the service company, LH Brubaker of Mechanicsburg, to call back.

This oven was installed in a newly built house in 2013 and lightly used.  We have used the self-cleaning feature only twice, once when it was initially installed.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door panel with no reported injuries, but potential for harm due to flying glass shards.

incident_description: A pan of scalding/boiling water exploded into the kitchen over a 12 foot area covering the ceiling, walls, floor and light fixture.  It seemed to take forever to boil getting to the small bubble stage, but never poiling.  I left the area to attend to some laundry on the other side of the room and while there heard a loud bang.  Nothing had fallen so I cautiously went back into the kitchen to inspect where I found water everywhere.  There was about an inch left in the pan that had contained a little over quart.  The pan an [REDACTED] stainless 2qt. saucepan had not moved on the burner, was not stuck, not damaged and not burned on the bottom.  The burner was the small burner on the power boil unit.  Anyone in the kitchen or standing over the stove most certainly would have been badly burned.  The noise sounded like a bomb going off and was traumatic.  I believe a sudden intensity of heat from the burner may have been the problem, the burner ordinarily cycles from higher heat to less heat.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of boiling water, but no one was present in the kitchen to be injured.

incident_description:
While having dinner Saturday night, November 19, 2016, our Kenmore Model 721.86012010 began to operate.  I tried to stop it by pressing the off button without result, opened the door without result and was forced to pull the plug from the outlet to get the microwave from operating.  During this episode there was a microwaveable food cover inside the oven which was melted to the turntable.  I was not able to find a recall on this product nor was the local Sears store able to suggest a fix other than to throw it out and buy a new one.  This was an expensive combi unit which makes me believe it either needs to be repaired by Sears or replaced by Sears.  This unit was purchased in 08/12/2012.  

We were lucky to be home when this incident occurred or I suspect we may have had a major fire.  It is no longer possible to trust this unit so it remains unplugged and out of service until a repair can be made.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury or fire occurred, though there was potential for a major fire.

incident_description:
We purchased a Samsung dishwasher (Model DW80F600UTB) from Lowe's on 9/3/2014.  Since then we have had 3 repairs and now it's happened again. Repairs were on 1/9/2015, 2/24/15 and 10/5/2015. 

The dishwashee just starts running while the door is open. Nobody is near the dishwasher. Both my husband and I have witnessed this. You cannot cancel the cycle, it just keeps coming back on. We have to turn off our circuit breaker to avoid a fire. 

Now it happened again on 12/10/2016. 

First two times Lowe's sent a repairman out and third time Samsung actually sent their own person. This dishwasher has been a lemon. 

Please investigate. 

Thank you.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioning poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: DLC2011 Food processor blade broke during use. Metal fragments discovered in food.
justification: Metal fragments in food pose a potential injury risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: While using my microwave, the handle (which was sold as stainless) chipped off.  The handle is actually covered in "stainless steal contact paper".  When it chipped, it cut my finger and caused it to bleed. In addition, the chips fell into my food which I was cooking on the stove.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut and bleeding, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such material defects can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description: The rivets that hold the blades in place on this food processor broke off, while my wife was using. No injuries happened but did not find rivet pieces did not realize it broke until later when washing.
justification: The incident involved broken rivets but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as such mechanical failures can happen with usage.

incident_description: Although turned off with the door closed, the microwave turns itself on at odd hours of the day and night and then remains on indefinitely.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: (Kenmore electric range model # 790.46589503 August2009)  On 9/24/16, I went to open my oven door (it was room temperature) to stick a pan in there.  When I grabbed the handle to open it, the glass door shattered.  This glass broke into thousands of tiny pieces.  Some went in my feet, hands, arms causing slight bleeding and marks.  The rest went all over the kitchen.  3 months later I am still finding shards of glass.  This oven was not on, it was not hot, I've had no previous problems with it.  When I called Sears to file a complaint and see if it was still under warranty, the customer service woman did not believe me that it had happened.  She said she has had her position for several years and has never heard of a door exploding.  I told her it did and offered to send pictures.  Either way, she said if it was during the first year it would fall under manufacturer defect, but after that first year it is a "user error."  I did not pic shards of glass off my body for a "user error."  I was extremely unhappy with how it was handled.  When I said I was going to file with the BBB or wherever you file safety complaints she got frustrated even more with me.  This is not how you do business, Sears/Kenmore! VERY UNHAPPY!
justification: The incident caused slight bleeding and marks from glass shards, indicating an injury, but no death or severe harm. The rarity of such incidents is suggested by the customer service representative's disbelief.

incident_description:
12/12/16 we completed cooking dinner and turned everything off on the stove/oven.  Awhile after dinner, we noticed the hot surface light illuminated but weren't overly concerned since everything was "turned off".

The next morning we awoke to find the the surface light still illuminated and the left rear burner hot. Again, all the burner knobs were in the off position. We are beyond fortunate that the house didn't burn down around us while we slept.  The only way shutoff the burner was to use the breaker switch at the home electrical box.

I originally reported this same  issue back in May '14 after having the stove repaired. I don't know what it will take to force the manufacturer to resolve this issue once and for all. Catastrophic loss of life and property?

A google search reveals I am not alone with this safety issue and my stove. Please help!!

Fridgidaire smooth surface oven.  Serial #    VF71947917         Model FEFL79GSA
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that remained hot despite being turned off, posing a fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was using my Cuisinart Mini Prep Food Processor (Model DLC-2ABK/DLC-2ABKC) to process salad dressing.  I stopped the machine to add another ingredient, then put the lid back on and pressed one of the buttons to continue processing and it would not turn on.  It acted like the blade was stuck on something so I opened it up, moved some of the ingredients around and tried again, and again it wouldn't operate.  I finally opened it up, took the blade out and noticed that one of the rivets holding the blade on had completely come off and one part of the blade was still in the bottom of the machine.  I discarded the blade and the salad dressing.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning food processor with no reported injury, only equipment failure and food wastage.

incident_description: The blade on my Cuisinart Food Processor Model DLC-4CHB has cracked and broken after using only four times.
justification: The blade broke during use, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
When checking my food processor to see if cuisanart recalled mine I discovered my blade was riveted with 4 rivets and was cracked.
Worried that it is also going to break in my food preparation
It is Model BFP 703
justification: The blade is cracked but no incident or injury has occurred yet, though there is concern about potential future breakage during use.

incident_description: I have the Cuisinart Prep 7 - 7-Cup Food Processor Model DLC 2007. The blade (which is now considered unsafe due to the rivets) does not stay in place while being used. The clear container itself also broke while in use when the handle cracked and the metal piece inside no longer aligned properly as it should. I would need a new blade and clear container to use this product properly or a reimbursement to cover the cost of a new one.
justification: The incident involves equipment failure (blade and container) but no reported injury or harm.

incident_description: Blade is cracked where it connects to spindle. I have pictures.
justification: A cracked blade poses a potential hazard but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: No injury. Blade broke.
justification: Blade broke but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I saw the recall for the Cruisart Chopper on Good Morning America. So went to check my chopper and it was not on the recall list but I noticed my blade was cracked in two spots. So I wanted to let you know that maybe these blades are not the best either.
justification: The blade is cracked but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Because of the recent Cuisinart recall my wife checked our Cuisinart MINI-PREP PLUS DLC-4CHBWB and found the plastic holding the blades in place is cracked in two locations. I couldn't find it on the recall list so I called Cuisinart at their 877-339-2534 phone number. For two days it rang busy. When I finally got through, it was a recording stating due to the high volume of calls please contact us on the internet. I did that and entered the Cuisinart model number above. I got a screen saying it wasn't on the recall list, "You may continue to use it". 
I won't use it as I believe it constitutes a safety hazard and the blades may come detached at any moment.  I am shocked that Cuisinart doesn't have a person answering these calls to discuss other products that might be faulty. If you would like a photo of the blades on our Cuisinart I would gladly forward them to you.    

This site is not allowing me to upload 4 digital images of the Cuisinart blades and the cracked plastic housing for the blades. I have the latest firefox download and am operating off of a iMac. If you can forward a regular e-mail address I can forward the images to I will do so.
justification: The cracked plastic housing poses a potential safety hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The metal blade on my food processor broke while in use. I heard it break and upon examining it, discovered that a piece of the metal blade was missing. I found the blade fragment in the food, which was uneaten.
justification: The blade broke during use, but no injury occurred as the fragment was found in the uneaten food.

incident_description:
Yesterday, I filled out a report for the widely announced recall of Cusinart Model DFP-14BCN. In the course of putting the unit away, My thumb was pressed against Cusinart Cutting Blade, DLC-044TX 4mm which was sitting in a plastic bag in the drawer where the food processor was routinely stored.  My thumb was badly cut by the preceding blade, even though I had placed it in a Ziplock 1 Quart Freezer bag since I recognized how sharp this blade was.

The cut to my thumb required 7 stiches to stop the bleeding and reattach my thumb tip.  I feel the Cusinart Cutting Blade, DLC-044TX 4mm should be sold with a hard clear plastic sleeve so a consumer handling the blade or placing the main unit in a drawer is protected.
Since, the manufacturer has such a particularly dangerous  Cutting Blade, DLC-044TX 4mm people owning this unit now should be supplied a protective sleeve for this blade.  The main chopping blade that was part of the recall due to metal fragments breaking off, normally sits in the chopping container/bowl so it does not present a hazard to a user when they reach for the handled chopping bowl
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring 7 stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the inherent danger of the blade and the described storage method.

incident_description: I have metal shavings off the blades of my Cuisinart food processor.
justification: Metal shavings indicate a potential incident with the food processor, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer made tea and poured it in the tea cup. The consumer sat down on her couch and began drinking her tea. Approximately 4 minutes later, the handle on the tea cup fell apart where it connected to the tea cup. The consumer indicated that the tea spilled over her left hand, left leg and onto her bottom. The consumer states that her left leg and bottom are very red and it feels numb.
