The consumer plans to contact the firm to inform them about the incident. 

The consumer indicated that she purchased 6 more of these tea cups and they were sold individually. The consumer uses the tea cups daily.

The consumer noticed that the handle is glued onto the cup versus being molded and she believes the glue is not reliable. The consumer believes this presents a safety hazard because it can happen with the other cups.
justification: The consumer suffered burns and numbness, indicating an injury, and the issue is likely to recur given the design flaw and daily use.

incident_description: I heard about the recall, checked the blade for any discontinuity, and it appears damaged. My mother cooks a lot with it and I want to make sure she is given the proper blade before using it again.
justification: The blade is damaged but no injury has occurred yet, indicating a potential incident without harm.

incident_description: A few months ago, my husband noticed pieces of the bottom of the blade on my Cuisinart food processor missing. I had made dozens of cookies  and froze them to sell for the holidays, chopped nuts , use my processor a lot for all types of foods. I went online  and purchased another blade,and threw away my old blade, I had to also throw away at least 50 dozen  of cookies that were to sell as I am not sure where those pieces of steel went.
justification: No injury occurred, but there was an incident involving a damaged food processor blade and loss of cookies.

incident_description: As I was making my children their smoothies I noticed that their was something bizarre in the food processor.  When I turned the food processor off,  pouring the kids smoothies into glasses as I looked for the mystery item,  I found an entries chunk of the blade that dislodged between the rivets.   I immediately took my children's smoothies away, other small chunks appear to be missing and the blade is cracked in multiple places. I do not know how long it has been in this state or how much of the blade my family ingested.
justification: The incident involves potential ingestion of metal fragments, which could cause injury, though no immediate harm is reported.

incident_description:
I own a Cuisinart Food Processor that is older than the advertised date range of the current Cuisinart recall, which is due to a riveted metal blade that can develop cracks and break.

I am reporting this out of concern that some owners of older Cuisinart food processors with defective and dangerous blades will not seek or will not obtain a new blade through the recall.

My blade unit also has cracks in the metal at each of the four rivets securing the lower blade. There are between one and three cracks at each rivet. The combination of cracks on this blade extends across about 90% of the blade. Although the metal blade is cracked, none of the blade has broken off.

I purchased this food processor in 1987. However, the advertised date range for the recall is July 1996 to December 2015.

The model number of the food processor is DLC-10S TX (Type 25). It is labeled the Cuisinart PRO Classic Food Processor, made in China. The blade is marked Metal Blade FP-100TX and it is also marked Cuisinart DLC-10.

For the Cuisinart recall form on the website, I selected model "DLC-10S" and my unit was considered eligible for the recall. There wasn't an option to select model DLC-10S TX. The website form did not ask for the date of purchase.
justification: The blade has cracks but has not broken off, indicating a potential hazard without actual injury occurring.

incident_description: Thinking I had a [REDACTED] food processor, I checked mine out today. It is a Hamilton Beach food process, so not part of the recall. But it has a riveted blade and I noticed that one of the rivets is broken off, so it appears that it's not just [REDACTED] having this issue. I didn't notice it before, nor was I injured, but it certainly looks like is a problem not restricted to [REDACTED}.
justification: The incident involves a broken rivet on a food processor blade, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: While using my Cuisinart DFP-3 the stainless steel blade shattered leaving metal shards in my food.  This occurred twice with two different blades.  This model is NOT part of the current recall.
justification: The incident involved a blade shattering, which poses a risk of injury but none was reported in the description.

incident_description: I had the exact thing happen with the Cuisinart blade August 2015, while I was making hummus. I Heard an unusual grinding noise while the chickpeas were blending and stopped the process and there was a piece of the blade in my hummus. I pulled the blade out and a big chunk of the blade had fallen apart and fell into the hummus. I am glad I checked and didn't serve the hummus!! I meant to call about it but never did and ended up ordering a new blade from Amazon because I thought my Cuisinart was too old to have anything done.
justification: The incident involved a blade breaking during use, but no injury occurred as the user noticed and stopped the process.

incident_description: Using my Cuisinart Mini-Prep Processor DLC-2A Series, for my morning smoothie, the blade broke off and punched a hole into the bowl and landed at the bottom of the bowl. I have pictures if needed. This Cuisinart is not on the recall list. I previously emailed Cuisinart and received a reply saying that because my unit was older than 18 months, they would not do anything about it. I'm not sure what my recourse is since this model is not on the list, but if the blade had actually shot out of the bowl I could have been hurt as I was standing right in front of it.
justification: The blade broke off but did not cause injury, though it had the potential to do so.

incident_description: I have one of the recalled Cuisinart food processors.    we recalled an incident where we used it to cut pepperoni and found pieces of the blade shredded in the meat and threw it out.
justification: The incident involved finding pieces of the blade in food, which was discarded, indicating no injury but a clear product failure.

incident_description: The metal blade on my food processor Cuisinart E-11 broke while I was using it.
justification: The blade broke during use, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: Metal blade broke between rivets on the underside of the blade.  Metal blade ended up in meatloaf, but was caught before any injuries occurred.
justification: The metal blade broke and ended up in food, but was caught before any injuries occurred, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: Our metal blade on our Custom Prep 11 Cuisinart food processor cracked and a small piece came off into the dough I was making.  Luckily we noticed it before someone ingested it.
justification: A small piece of the blade broke off into the dough, but it was noticed before ingestion, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: A recall was implemented for the Cuisinart food processor.  Mine is a Pro 10.  The blade has the four rivits which qualify to be replaced.
justification: The description indicates a product recall due to a potential issue with the blade, but no injury or incident is reported.

incident_description:
This is related to the Cuisinart recall.  I have a Cuisinart that is affected by the recall (four steel rivets on blade, noticeable cracking of steel) and I will get a replacement blade.  However, I also have another Cuisinart that is not included in this recall, and I noticed cracking of that blade as well.  In this case, it is the plastic housing that is cracked in multiple places and could splinter off during use.  There have been no injuries related to this in my household.

I will be contacting Cuisinart about this other blade issue, but I wanted to let you know that other blades not included in the recall may be damaged as well.
justification: The incident involves a cracked blade with potential to splinter, but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description: I used my Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus to chop some herbs for stuffed shells.   While eating dinner, my husband bit down on something hard in the stuffed shell which only has soft ricotta cheese and herbs in it.   He spit it out and it was a small white piece of plastic.   We were shocked and couldn't believe it came from the cheese.   We thought about how we made the shells and checked out the Cuisinart.   The plastic around the blade had deteriorated and parts were coming off during chopping.   While he hurt his tooth and it was sore for a few days, luckily it did not require dental work.   I looked into purchasing a replacement blade but it was $15 and I decided it was too much $.  I put the mini-prep aside in a storage closet and pulled it out today after hearing about the new Cuisinart recall.   But the current recall doesn't involve this model as it's focused on blade pieces coming off.   I remember the date as my child's friend ate dinner with us and I was incredibly thankful the kids didn't chomp down on a hard piece of plastic.  It was the week before Halloween as they were trying on their costumes.   I didn't think to report it until now.   I can send pix.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (sore tooth) but no dental work was required, and the likelihood is unlikely as the plastic deterioration was specific to this one-time event.

incident_description: I was checking my recently purchased Cuisinart food processor against the recall list. Although my mod # FP11 was not on the list, I noticed the four. Rivets holding the blade to the plastic hub were rusting and one had a crack in the metal from the rivet hole. This crack can result in metal failure and metal pieces in food prepared by the processor. This model number needs to be added to the recall list!
justification: The description indicates a potential safety issue (rust and crack in the blade) that could lead to metal pieces in food, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
The plastic that holds the blade in place is cracking in several places.
Cuisinart Mini- prep DLC-1 it has no rivets but still should have been recalled.
justification: The cracking plastic poses a potential hazard but there is no mention of injury or death, only a safety concern.

incident_description: We have a Cuisinart Mini-Prep Plus Model #DLC-2ABC/DLC2ABCC. The plastic that holds the blades in place is breaking and starting to come apart.
justification: The plastic breaking could lead to blade detachment, posing a risk of injury if not addressed, but no injury is reported yet.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart Classic Pro Food Processor DLC 10.  There are 4 bolts on the blade.  There is a crack in the blade under two of the bolts.
justification: A cracked blade in a food processor poses a risk of failure during use, which could lead to an incident but no immediate injury is described.

incident_description: In response to the notification of a recall, the product (food processor) was examined and a tiny crack was discovered that extends out from one of the rivets on the bottom of the blade.
justification: A crack was found in the product, indicating a potential safety issue, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Report is for a Cuisinart Food Processor. Model number DLC-2007N.

On the day of the incident a metal shard from the food processor blade was found in the processed food. The shard had broken off around a rivet on the underside of the blade. Upon further inspection I found there were cracks around other rivets.

I have a secondary blade from an older model and inspected it as well after the incident with the first blade. The secondary blade also had cracks around several of the rivets, though no shards had broken off.

The food processor has only ever been used for soft foods, within normal operations as directed by the manufacturer, and the blades have never been used for anything else than their intended purpose.
justification: A metal shard was found in processed food, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Cuisinart  food processor Model DLC 10STX type 25 . Recall announced 12/13.2016.  My machine has cracks at all four rivets on the subject recall blade
justification: The incident involves a recalled food processor with cracks, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Cuisinart Toaster Oven TOB 60 260 caught fire
Flames came out the top through door
No injury 
Burned wall
justification: The toaster oven caught fire and caused property damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: When I inspected my Cuisinart DCLXP food processor I discovered that 2 of was completely cracked through around 2 outer rivets and you could see light through the crack. Barely holding on to center piece. I wouldn't doubt that used at the highed speed that it fly apart and penetrate through its bowl and cause serious injury.
justification: The description indicates a potential for serious injury if the food processor is used at high speed, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The Cuisinart Food Processor blade -(model #DFP-11) I have been using has a metal piece missing where the blade is attached to the plastic housing and the blade has stress lines coming from each of the 4 rivets. I use the processor on an average of 5 times a week. I am reporting no injuries due to the blade.
justification: No injuries were reported, but there is a potential for future incidents due to the damaged blade and frequent use.

incident_description:
4 CUP WORK BOWL Mini Prep Plus (chopper)
CUISINART
BLADE CRACKED
justification: The blade cracked, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I have a cuisinart food processor. From what I see on the recall models, mine is not on the recall list, how ever, I feel it should be. I was using that slicing blade to make scalloped potatoes. All of a sudden, the machine starting shimming across the counter. I shut it off, and took the blade off. The edge was damaged and bend over. You can see visually the damage on the blade. I am surprised that one of the teeth didn't break off and end up in my food. I've tried calling tP12he company but no success. I tried using the on line site, but the page could not be found, using the link posted. I ended up using a customer care site, and they said I would receive an confirm ton e-mail shortly which I submitted last night, which I did not receive. I feel this blade should be recalled for any consumer. My model number is FP-12 series. The slicing blade # is FP 12ASD slicing disc.
justification: The incident involved a damaged blade but no injury occurred, and the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description:
The oven was installed in the home, while it was being built, but it had never been used.  

The consumer was home the day before the incident and attempted to set the clock, but it did not keep the correct time.  When he came into house the next day, he discovered soot all over the house.  There was substantially more soot in the kitchen area.  The cabinet around the oven was partly burned and partly charred.  It cost $8000.00+ to repair the damage to the cabinets, because they had to be stripped down and redone.  

The problem occurred near the controller, which is located on the upper oven.  This caused the burning to cabinets and the soot damage to the home.

Initially, the consumer contacted the dealer, but he got the run-around for approximately 2 weeks.  He was referred to different stores and different phone numbers, but no resolution was offered.

The consumer submitted a builderÃÂs risk insurance claim, because the home was still under construction.  A repairman came out and investigated the damage and determined that he oven was not repairable.  He wrote a report and gave the consumer an estimate of the cost.  The consumer then hired someone to do the repairs.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they sent their own technician to examine the oven.  The technician came up with the same conclusion.

The builderÃÂs risk insurance paid a portion of the damage cost (approx. $4900.00).  The consumer purchased a different manufacturerÃÂs double oven.

The consumer claims that a manufacturerÃÂs rep. told him that they would reimburse him for the cost of their oven (approx. $2700.00). The consumer never received the payment for the oven.  He has received a check toward the damages ($2002.00+) from the mfr.

10/17/2016:  The consumer was told by a manufacturerÃÂs rep. (name & number unavailable)  that they would have to come out and pick up the old oven and the people who picked up the oven, would give him a check for the oven.

10/17/2016:  The consumer contacted the company that is supposed to pick up the oven and their rep. (name & number unavailable) told him that they did not have a check for him.

His lending company provided a construction loan.  This process is being dragged out and the incident caused by this oven may be a contributing factor.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned and charred cabinets, soot damage) but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Our gas range top. If you accidentally turn gas on by rubbing a knob. It can bypass the ignition point and remain on unlit.
Then a smell of gas and you go to turn it off. This is where it becomes a safety hazard. Depending on how long gas was
emitting will determine the size of explosion you are about to experience. You cannot turn the gas off without passing the igniter point which sets off a spark and ignites the escaped gas.
justification: The incident describes a potential gas leak that could lead to an explosion, posing a significant safety hazard with potential for severe injury or death.

incident_description:
I have a GE Adora 30-inch Self-Cleaning Freestanding Electric Convection Range (Black), JB710DTBB.  It was purchased at Home Depot around October 20, 2011.
This morning, December 12, 2016 at approximately 5:00AM, I set the stove to 300 degrees. 
I placed 4-slices of bacon in a Calphalon skillet to cook, on the middle rack, mid-way the cold oven. Around 5:45AM there was this strong odor of burning meat. I opened the oven door and black smoke  billowed from the oven. I could not distinguish the bacon in the pan. It looked like tar burning.  I removed the pan from the oven and used tongs to try and remove the bacon. There was no
distinct pieces, just thick sludge melted into the pan. The oven door interior glass cracked. 

I cut off the circuit to the range to avoid any more problems.  I turned on the exhaust and two ceiling fans to clear the smoke.  After an hour the smoke alarm stopped.  There is still heavy smoke lingering in the kitchen, and additional smoke throughout the house. 

I TRIED TO UPLOAD PICTURES, HOWEVER, THE SYSTEM WOULD NOT ALLOW THIS FUNCTION.
justification: The incident involved significant smoke and damage to the oven, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Blade of disposal came flying towards my face when I was disposing of soft cat food.
justification: The blade flew towards the face but there is no mention of injury, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: T-Fal non-stick induction pan.  Was frying scrambled eggs over low gas flame.  Very loud pop was heard, caused animals to run away, and upon investigating, rivet head (one of two) holding handle on separated and partially detached.  Could have become projectile, but did not detach fully.  No injury.
justification: The pan's rivet head partially detached, posing a potential projectile risk, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
In the middle of the night I smelled something burning so I got up to investigate.  Our GE Dishwasher Model # PDW8280N20SS SN FR7677325B was overheating to the point it melted all of the plastic in the upper tray and the lower arm had melted and drooped onto the heating element and was burned brown.  The silver ware was so hot it melted through the holder and molten plastic has dripped down onto the base of the tub.  The top counter above the DW (granite thank goodness) was almost too hot to touch.  The only way to turn the heating element off was to flip the circuit breaker.

Only by the grace of god did we not have a house fire as a result of this product's failure.  As far as I can tell it is not part of the current recall of GE Profile DW's.  We will contact the Mfr on Monday morning and based on their willingness to replace all damage caused by their product, we will chart a course forward from there.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and caused significant damage but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Our microwave was not in use but became so hot that it busted the glass turntable inside.  We did not realize what the noise was until my husband went to use the microwave about half an hour later and when opening the door saw the turntable had broken into several pieces.  I was going to clean it out but could feel the extreme heat coming from it.  We closed the door back b/c the glass was breaking and heard a loud buzzing sound so we opened the door again and unplugged it.  Once it cooled off some I was taking pictures and realized it had actually gotten so hot that it melted part of the glass turntable.  Thankfully, we were home when all this happened or else I feel like our home would have burnt down that night.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I was using a Kirkland Signature pan and heating it up getting ready to cook an omelette. I sprayed it with [REDACTED] and when it was heated up I went to move the handle out of the way. When I did this, the bottom of the pan fell off releasing melted metal. The metal destroyed parts of my stove, my kitchen floor, parts of my living room floor, two rugs, and caused severe burns on both of my feet from trying to jump out of the way. I have been trying to resolve this with Costco and Meyer Corp. with no success. I have been harassed and asked ridiculous questions from Meyer over 4 months , like do I soak my pan or do I use lukewarm water to clean my pan....etc. etc. The bottom line is this is a defective line of cookware that is no longer being sold because it explodes and spews molten hot metal. Only two small nails hold the bottom on.
justification: The incident caused severe burns and significant property damage, indicating a high severity level. The description suggests the product is defective and no longer sold, implying the likelihood is low but not impossible.

incident_description: Oven temperature does not regulate itself.  Once the oven reaches the preheat temperature, it continues to stay on and exceed temperature indicated on front panel.  Example:  oven was set at 350 degrees and continued to heat up to 500 degrees (as indicated two separate thermometers placed inside the oven) before the repair technician noticed and shut it off.
justification: The oven's failure to regulate temperature poses a risk of overheating, but no injury or death was reported in the incident.

incident_description: The product is a Westinghouse 3 outlet, light sensing countdown timer, purchased at Target in Oswego, IL. We plugged our outdoor christmas lights into it, and set the timer for "Dusk Dawn." In the morning, with the sun already up, we wondered why the lights were still on. Upon closer inspection, we found that the unit was smoking and had melted a hole through itself. We unplugged it immediately.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and melting product but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Hello,

I purchased a Bosch 500 series Dishwasher from Lowe's (model #SHP68T55UC/07 and serial number FD96080064) on 8/24/2016.

On 10/3/2016, the junction box and power supply that came packaged with the unit caught on fire and melted the box. Subsequently, the electrical fire and smoke damaged my kitchen cabinets.

Luckily, I was home and smelled the burning plastic so the damage was relatively minimal. However, had I not been home, the fire could have been catastrophic.

I had a licensed electrician troubleshoot and repair the problem. He said there was a problem with the junction box and that a plastic junction box and power supply should have never been used. To correct the safety issue, he replaced the melted junction box with a metal one.

I contact Bosch about the problem and they dismissed it as an installation issue without providing any other information or reasoning.

Your website will not allow me to upload photos (it gives an error), so please find the pictures and receipts in my Dropbox folder at:

https://www.dropbox.com/sh/9o41zuuq933cai0/AADOAssVcaglmuqNosQTvrVGa?dl=0
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire causing damage to kitchen cabinets, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The LG Range Model LDE4413ST is a dangerous fire hazard. The overly sensitive knobs at waist height can easily turn on inadvertently when slightly brushing up against them or reaching overhead. And when the double burner knobs are brushed against either way, they are automatically on high heat. Even when these knobs are not pushed in, they will turn on the stovetop. 

On August 30, 2016, I left my house and returned 45 minutes later to a smoldering pile of ashes on my stovetop and a smoky house. One of the knobs were unintentionally bumped without anyone noticing. The tea canister that was on the stove burned to ashes, along with destroying the stovetop, burning part of the countertop, and causing smoke to go throughout my house. ItÃÂs a good thing I arrived home when I did, because our house might not be standing today.
We informed LG that day about what happened, and they sent a third party out a couple days later to assess the damage. We were in contact with [REDACTED], a claims specialist, and he told us ÃÂThis is not your fault. We will take care of it.ÃÂ But since that conversation, we have tried to contact LG numerous times, but keep getting the run around. [REDACTED], a Sr. claims manager, finally told us that they wonÃÂt take responsibility and that we need to claim it on our home ownerÃÂs insurance. 

I have read numerous other complaints of LG ranges doing the same thing, electric as well as gas. This dangerously flawed LG range could have burned down our house. It could kill people. Is it going to take somebody dying to get this product recalled? ItÃÂs a shame that LG is allowed to sell these ranges that are obviously unsafe.
justification: The incident caused property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The description indicates this is a recurring issue with the product.

incident_description: I turned on my Frigidaire Gallery electric range oven to 325 degrees to warm up some leftovers in glass/[REDACTED]pans.  (Model #GLEF378AQB, Serial #VF13013618, bought new in 2001 by the previous owner of my home.)  In 30-45 minutes, I heard hissing and popping coming from the oven and when I opened the oven door to see what was happening, the food was a charred mess, the glass/pyrex pans were black with soot, and there was black smoke coming out of the pans.  I could not understand what I was seeing, but I immediately turned off the oven!  I then went to deal with the smoke detector going off - opening windows, turning on ceiling fans and microwave exhaust fan above the stove.  I was able to gingerly remove the smoking hot glass/pyrex plans without burning myself but then realized that the oven was not going off!  The oven coils in the bottom were still burning red hot!  I could not get the oven to turn off!  I was not sure I could pull the oven out away from the wall by myself to get it unplugged, so considered calling a neighbor or the fire department for help.  But then I remembered that I could run down to the basement and turn off the breaker to the range in our electrical fuse box.  Problem solved - but no working stove anymore as it could no longer be trusted and was now a fire hazard.  I later realized that what must hage happened was that the oven burner coils had never stopped burning red hot when the oven reached its preheated 325 degrees - it had just kept burning!  Looking online, I discovered there had been an earlier recall for Frigidaire ranges for the very problem I experienced but ALSO for stovetop burners turning on spontaneously and/or not being able to be turned off!  Alas, my calls to Electrolux and Frigidaire have been TOTALLY unsatisfying as they say that my particular model and serial number combination was not included in that earlier recall.  (The serial number does fit into the range as does the purchase date.) Again, looking online it is clear that many others have been experiencing these very same problems with their Frigidaire electric ranges from before the recall, through the recall, and up to the present time.  AND, folks who have gotten the "free recall repair" continued to have proboems -- the fix did NOT fix the problem.  So, in addition to the electric range not being trusted any longer, any "free repair" can also not be trusted.  Something needs to be done.  At a minimum - the public needs to be warned of this very real fire hazard in their homes.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the outermost glass of his oven range's door exploded. The unit was not on and nobody was in the kitchen. The consumer's wife came into the kitchen when she heard popping noises similar to popcorn popping and noticed that the glass door was still shattering at a distance of up to eight feet approximately. The consumer checked to see if the unit had turned on by itself but the unit was cool everywhere.

The consumer states that the oven range is used approximately once or twice a month. The last time the oven was used was two weeks ago.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that they had not heard of this issue occurring with other consumers; they will not be able to provide any assistance free of charge since the oven range is no longer under warranty.

Because of the upcoming festivities, the consumer will repair the unit. The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The glass door exploded but no one was injured, and the oven was not in use at the time.

incident_description: Our Maytag dishwasher had an electrical fire inside the door.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire, which is a significant hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On Thanksgiving, November 24,2016, while cooking a 20lb turkey in my Kenmore Elite Double Wall Oven the lower rack unexpectedly fell resulting in the turkey and liquid falling/splattering all over the open door and interior walls. After two more attempts with different racks and locations the rack continued to fall. We finally were able to get it to stay in place but we could not move the rack or even put any pressure on it  as it would fall again.
I contacted Sears to report this serious incident and an appointment was made for November 30, 2016,  to have it inspected/repaired. During the course of my conversation with the customer service representative she informed me that there is a problem with my oven model with the interior wall warping causing the racks to fall.
On November 30th the service technician inspected the oven and did inform me the walls were warped and was common with this model that he informed me Frigidaire actually made for Kenmore.
He ordered two "modification brackets", which I am to install on the racks to resolve the problem. 
I feel that this is not the correct course of action for such a serious safety issue with this unit. A more permanent corrective action plan should be put in action to resolve this safety concern.
justification: The incident involved a rack falling repeatedly, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: This is the second safety concern for the same product that was reported in 2015 to CPSC.gov.  The Document # if l11520474A - Report #02150224-39A8D-2147435110 -  The Frigidaire Smooth surface range has a radiant element that comes on without warning; no one is turning the knob.  This was a problem that was repaired in 2015 and is now happening again; same element that was repaired.    The exact burner has once again turned on by itself over the past week a number of times.  This is becoming a true fire hazard that is dangerous.  Within 5 days 2 plastic grocery bags have melted on this cook range sending fumes through my home and setting off fire alarms.  This range top turned on by itself.  We were stunned both times.  This is not a fluke; it is a fire hazard that is brewing once again.  We are notifying your agency once again to investigate further problems with this range that is still being sold in the USA.  Please refer to my first report and your document #'s
justification: The incident involves a recurring malfunction causing a fire hazard, with no reported injuries but potential for significant damage.

incident_description: The consumer indicates that she tried turning her oven on but it would not turn on. A couple of hours later, the consumer noticed that the oven turned on by itself. The consumer turned the oven off immediately. The consumer states the oven no longer works however the stove does work.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or harm occurred, only inconvenience and potential safety concern.

incident_description: On report # 20121107-3591A-1282233 date 11/07/2012 I reported a very dangerous incident with the mentioned stove  which during the morning it was found on. After the report Electrolux on ticket [REDACTED] Rev D  a visit was done and services # [REDACTED] control # 59033; service #6387336 control #59839  was performed on the mother board ES-1000Range Control. I asked for an exchange of a new stove to what they said NO. I had worries about possible future incidents. I was not far away from the reality, less than four years around mid October 2016, the same incident happened but this time I was washing dishes and suddendly I percive a smell of burning, when I turn my face the area where the stoves control are was smoking and the stove turned on by itself, the same experience. Thank God I was present and reacted inmediately to unplug the stove. Knowing that the guarantee has expired I called Frigidaire and told me sorry but guarantee is over. I called US consumer in order to get  advise which they send me paperwork for the report. Due to health issues I was not able to submit report papers before, and now I am doing the report via internet. This is a very dangerous experience because Thank God I was at home; but just to think what could of happened if I was not present and the entire kitchen, wood cabinets and things on top of stove caused a fire... It is imperative, that these products are not available to continue used by customers, because they are risks for health, safety and inclusive death. I am requesting for Electrolux to recognize the product was a danger and should have exchange the product. I still have the damaged and dangerous stove in my kitchen.
justification: The stove malfunctioned and turned on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We have a LG electric double oven, purchased from Nebraska Furniture Mart in 2014, that has an extended warranty. We have had the appliance repairman from the warranty company Assurant Solutions company, come on numerous occasions, at least twice for the same problem, glass in the oven door, exploding and shattering into shards of glass. If this was the appropriate glass for an oven door (tempered), then It would explode Into nuggets. When you contact LG, you are given the runaround, and last statement from LG representative was to "Just be careful" when re-installing for the 3d time, scheduled for Dec. 8, 2016. There is no acknowledgment that LG Is responsible for this problem.
justification: The incident involves exploding glass in an oven door, which poses a risk but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I called Keurig Green Mountain today report an incident with my mini brewing system.
Basically, if I had not walked back into my office while the machine was malfunctioning, I think the office would have been burned down.
The motor continued when there wasn't any water left in the reservoir; it kept "brewing" but started to smell like an electrical motor does when it goes haywire.  
I unplugged it and at that time, the spewing of hot steam and water came out like the reports said online, and it started to really stink as though all the wiring had melted inside the unit.  5 hours later it still smells in my office.

After discussing this with customer service rep #1 on call #1 took all my information for a rebate coupon to be mailed so I can go purchase another.  However, the serial # I gave her off my machine wasn't part of the recall so she couldn't help any further, and then gave me me another # to call.
1.866.901.2739.

Call #2 today to customer service rep [REDACTED] at this number,  In the end, she said no, sorry the best they could do was to give me a discounted price of $79.99 and I would have to purchase another one, because of the warranty expiration.  Are you KIDDING??  No replacement of this unit, serial #31.3002.0647779.  This could have gone horribly wrong.  I can't believe Keuring won't stand by their products and do right by their customers.  I could have been burned in the face or worse, burned the office down.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning brewing system that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Switch for door closure overheated & melted twice.
justification: The switch overheating and melting is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Dishwasher was set to run a normal cycle around 9PM and we woke up 3hrs later to the smell of plastic burning. The lower spray arm was out of place and resting on top of the heating coil with plastic dripping into the bottom. Plastic cups on the TOP rack were melted, 
There wasn't any water to be seen in the dishwasher and it was very hot inside and no steam as would be expected at the end of a wash cycle. 
Dishwasher never ran a wash cycle, food was baked on; it was set to not run a dry cycle.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing plastic to melt, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: My Frigidaire FGHC2331PF6 refrigerator was causing a GFI to continuously reset. Upon inspection of the rear of the fridge, it became apparent that an electrical fire had taken place.
justification: An electrical fire occurred, but there is no mention of injury or death, so the severity is 2. Electrical fires in appliances are possible but not extremely common.

incident_description: I purchased this Frigidaire gas range in June 2016. It was delivered in July. I love it. My 18 months old grandson can turn the gas knobs on. He does not have to push. This is dangerous. I have always owned a gas range and raised 3 sons. This never happened on any other range. Very disappointed
justification: The gas range knobs can be easily turned by a child, posing a potential hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
As soon as we started using food processor today, it made a grinding sound, as if a spoon was caught in the garbage disposal. We couldn't figure out what was making the sound and finished using it. We were pureeing fruit and when we poured it out, there was a sliver of metal left in there. Looked at our chopping blade, thinking the blade itself broke, and discovered that it came from the bottom. Like the others, it was a section between two rivets. (There are a total of 4 rivets on the bottom.) Called Cuisinart and they are sending a free replacement blade.  

We have only used our food processor on very simple tasks and probably only 10-15 times since purchase.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning food processor with a metal sliver found in the food, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My glass top burner only heats to high and won't turn off. This is the front right and back left burners. Both large burners.
justification: The burners not turning off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or damage is reported in the description.

incident_description: My wife was scalded using the Nutribullet blender. On November 27, 2016, she was making carrot soup. She sautÃÂ©ed the carrots with onions and spices, added liquid, and simmered for approximately 30 minutes. She then removed the soup from the heat and let it cool before transferring it to the Nutribullet. She began blending the soup, but heard a loud pop and the heated soup exploded violently from the unit. My wife had her hand on the top of the cup. She managed to close her eyes before being hit by the liquid, but she had her hand on the top of the unit, and she immediately felt severe burning on her face and arms. I took her to the hospital, where we spent hour and she was several, largely ineffective, pain medications. She was then transferred, via ambulance, to another hospital with a specialized burn clinic, where she finally received effective pain treatment. She was diagnosed with 1st- and 2nd-degree burns on her face and arm, including a 2nd-degree burn on her eyelid, and prescribed medicated creams to apply to her burns. The doctors told her her it will take her eyelid will likely require at least four months to heal.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st- and 2nd-degree burns requiring hospital treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe incidents are not common with proper use.

incident_description:
My husband and I were standing in the kitchen of our home on Wednesday, November 23, 2016, when we heard what seemed to sound like a crack and the glass front of our oven door shattered into a million pieces.  We contacted Sears customer service and they finally connected me to their 3rd party insurance company that took the report and sent a technician to my home on December 1, 2016 to take pictures of the damage.
I did incur small cuts to my hand from the shattered glass.  The oven had not been used at all in several days prior to the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts to the hand, indicating an injury (severity 3), but such events are unlikely (likelihood 2) given the oven had not been used recently.

incident_description:
11/13/2016 - The consumer was trying to use the oven however it kept tripping the circuit breaker. The first time the circuit breaker tripped was approximately ten minutes after the oven was turned on, then approximately five minutes later, and ultimately immediately after it was turned on. The consumer placed insulation between the electrical wiring and the metal panel and the unit is working properly so far. 

11/14/2016 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that somebody would contact him with information.

The consumer indicates that he uses the oven approximately two to three times per week. The consumer indicates that approximately a year ago he experienced the same issue with his unit; the consumer states that he personally and temporarily corrected the issue. The consumer believes that the removable metal panel that covers the electrical wiring inside the unit is the issue since they are too close and no insulation is between them, thus causing sparks to occur. 

The consumer plans on keeping his oven range for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven tripping the circuit breaker, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My son has always use they sippy cup called sip and grip and he was laying in bed drinking it with me as he started chocking luckly i was able to get the part out of his mouth and it was small part of sippy cup rubber lid
justification: The child choked on a small part of the sippy cup but was unharmed due to quick intervention.

incident_description: small frying pan about 8 inch diameter, looks very well made, thick stainless steel.  Betty Crocker is the maker.  I was standing at the stove frying a hot dog.  I walked to the cupboard to get something. Suddenly there was an explosion, like a rifle going off and I felt something go whizzing by my head.  Had no  idea what had happened.  Thought perhaps a kitchen light had exploded.  I had turned the stove off, but another explosion followed.  Loud enough to be dizzying.  Later I found that tops of the rivets from the handle of the pan had exploded and went flying across the room.  Very dangerous.  I tried to find the Betty Crocker website or the maker of these pans, but cannot find anything on line.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of a frying pan handle, but no injury was reported despite the close call.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the electric range cooktop cracked while it was in use.  He stated that his spouse heard a noise while it was on and then she noticed that there was a crack on the right side of the cooktop.  The manufacturer was contacted and they were advised that they were unable to assist with the matter.  He feels that the company should be held liable for this faulty product because it is a safety hazard.


Caller stated that he had read numerous complaints online about the same problem with the range.
justification: The cooktop cracked during use but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The caller mentioned numerous similar complaints, suggesting the issue is not rare.

incident_description:
Consumer is reporting that her double wall oven had a failure which could be similar to recall# 04-576.  Hazard: The ranges and wall ovens have faulty wiring, which can melt and cause the oven to short circuit. The appliance can then stop working and pose a shock hazard to consumers. 

Consumer stated that they noticed that there was electrical outage and the light came back on, however, they noticed white smoke emitting from the vent of the top oven, her spouse then opened the bottom oven and noticed that it had turn itself on and emitted sparks when he opened it.  The circuit breaker was used to switch the power off.

They contacted the company and a service technician sent out on 10/5 and they advised her that they needed to test the product she requested a document which would make them liable if there was a safety issue, before switching the power back on.  The service technician did not test  the product and had to leave.  She stated that they hired an electrician to make sure her wiring was intact, this was.  Since then she has contacted the company to let them know that they can have the product to test it outside of her home.

Consumer feels that this oven is unsafe and should be reported.

As of 11/16/16, manufacturer (GE) has offered a replacement product which is priced higher than what consumer can purchase at a retail location.  This is unsatisfactory to them.  Therefore, the consumers have ordered a new oven from a retailer.

GE should be required by law to test all defective products reported to them to determine why a safety issue occurred to prevent this from happening to other consumers and any possible injuries.  Her oven never should have turned itself on!  This is obviously a huge manufacturing defect.  Consumer should not be forced to test this product in her own home if she has legitimate concerns for the safety of her family and her home.  Numerous times she offered GE to pick up her oven and test it in their own controlled environment.  Consumer was informed that they would not do this.  If she was not home at the time of the incident to turn off the circuit breaker, her circumstances might have been different.

Consumer provided GE with the enclosed letter from electrician she hired as well as photos of the oven which show black marks on the left side where sparking occurred.  They still refused to work with consumer on an agreeable compromise in this matter.  GE's actions in this matter prove that the safety of their consumers is not a top priority.
justification: The incident involved electrical hazards and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was removing an item from a cabinet next to my electric range when the glass on the oven door shattered completely.  I don't remember even touching it but I must have because the next thing in knew, I was surrounded by glass pieces and there was nothing left to my oven door.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: We were cooking a 22 pound Thanksgiving Day Turkey. I opened the oven door to check on the turkey. Upon moving the turkey the oven grille the turkey was on fell approx 6 inch's on the right side of the oven. Only the right side. Hot juices/grease spilled out into the oven causing an oven fire. Hot grease also shot out hitting my face and arm. Fortunately the oven went out by itself in 4 or 5 seconds, just before we were going to hit it with the fire extinguisher. I immediately put cold water on my face and arm. We had a dozen people in our home and everyone was quite shocked/stunned. After shutting the oven off and proceeding to clean the grease out of the oven which included removing the bottom cover where the oven burner is located. We were able to continue cooking our dinner. This involved relocating the oven grille which the turkey would now sit on to the far bottom shelve. We now had recognized that the far top and far bottom oven widths were quite different than the middle rack measurements. Upon experimentation we found when the oven rack is located on any of the middle shelves, it would fall down when applying pressure from the top of the rack. The oven walls apparently have bowed outwards during the course of time, thus making use of the oven potentially hazardous. This situation could have been much worse. As it turned out my burns were minimal and the fire extinguished itself. Now what am I suppose to do about using my oven when wanting to cook?? Upon "Googleling" this on the internet It was apparent other people have had the same issue.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns and a small oven fire, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this is a recurring issue with the oven, making future occurrences likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Whirlpool Double Oven Stainless Steel Model # WOD97ES0E5 Serial # D63109781 interior oven glass exploded and sent shattered glass throughout the upper and lower oven and out onto kitchen floor.  

The oven was purchased on October 11, 2016 and installed October 31, 2016.  The event took place the day before Thanksgiving on No. 23, 2016.  The oven had been used approximately 6 times prior to the event.  

There had been no scratching of glass, or bumping it.  The self-clean feature had never been engaged.

The glass was supposed to be "tempered" but some glass did not stayed in full shards. 

Glass is in the frame of both doors.  A first attempt to obtain warranty service failed as the replacement 
unit was scratched.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injury was reported, and the issue occurred after minimal use without misuse.

incident_description: This complaint refers to KitchenAid dishwasher model KDTM404ESS.  The control panel is on the top of the door.  It overhangs the sides of the door and is sharp.  It sliced my daughter's leg, resulting in a bloody gash, about 1.5 inches long.  KitchenAid made the top piece too long.  It overhangs the sides of the door, has a sharp edge, with an edge that seems unfinished.  When the door is open, it can slice your skin.
justification: The description reports a bloody gash from a sharp edge, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I have a Nutri NinjaÃÂ® Blender System with Auto-IQÃÂ Model BL682 which I purchased from Bed Bath and Beyond.  I previously had their Model BL740 which has the same problem.  The blender blades has a hard plastic casing and a rubber o-ring to give a proper seal when using the blender for the NutriNinja cups.  The debris from blended food becomes lodged between the rubber ring and the hard plastic casing of the blade housing resulting in build up of decaying food, mold, and a putrid odor.  I contacted the manufacturer asking if there is a way to easily remove the rubber ring for proper cleaning and they informed me that the rubber ring should not be removed.  This leaves the consumer with the problem that food debris will become lodged there posing a health hazard.  I have looked online and found many posts from people with similar problems and they ultimately removed the rubber ring using a knife or other tool and found a large amount of rotting food matter.  The instructions that come with the product for cleaning (fill blender with soapy water and run it on the blender) only cleans the blade and does nothing for the debris that is stuck between the rubber ring and the hard casing.
justification: The incident describes a health hazard due to food debris buildup, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her gas range purchased from a retailer and delivered on August 23, 2016 in New Jersey.
She had no problems with the range until October 10, 2016 when what sounded like smoke alarm sounded and at that time she turned around, saw the display and saw that the left side was showing error messages then showing 'Cancel" however she could not stop it. 
She had contacted a technician regarding another issue and he advised her that the problem was the computer and that was why the alarm was sounding and the range was not performing as designed.
This technician ordered the computer October 10, 2016 then returned to her home on October 21. 2016 and installed it.
The caller is reporting that after this repair her stove knobs become very hot.
She was advised by the manufacturer that she should not use the stove top and the oven at the same time.
She is reporting this incident as a safety hazard due to burn potential.
There are no injuries to report
The caller also reports that the four knobs above the oven used to turn to control heat to the burners remain very hot when she is baking in the oven and cooking on the stove top.
She contacted the manufacturer who she states advised her not to use the oven at the same time that she is using the burners.
She spoke with the Georgia Consumer Protection Fraud Bureau November 9, 2016 and was advised that she should contact the CPSC.

Burner knobs registered between 145 degrees & 165 degrees.  Manufacturer, Frigidaire, claims that is in their specs, despite that caller cannot hold fingers on knobs for more than a few seconds, when oven or broiler is in operation.  They are not interested that caller can & did burn fingers.  

And as to their "specs" who, as a consumer, has access to that information?
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with burn potential but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
When mother was using the oven and turned the front burner on the back left burner came on by itself.  Within minutes flames emitted from the back of the range.  She was able to turn off the unit and the flames dissipated.  The following day a similar incident occurred while the front burner was in use the rear burner came on, her mother turned the front burner off and the rear burner powered off.

Caller stated that mother related to her that she has had several incidents with the range.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and repeated malfunctions, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
After I used the deep fryer and switched it off (the electrical cord was no longer attached) I noticed that the fryer started making noise. As if it was warming up. I look at the oil and saw that it was bubbling. I stepped away to organize something for my cooking (fortunately), heard a loud noise and the fryer exploded, covering my patio with oil. I was lucky not be close to it.
Obviously, this is a very concerning matter. Not just for me but for other users.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage but no injury, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description:
The consumer states the design of the top of the stove poses a safety hazard. The consumer indicated there are gaps on the grates and allows things to fall inside. The consumer believes the firm is aware of the safety flaw and is the reason why there newer models do not have this design.

The consumer contacted the firm to express her safety concerns (Transaction# [REDACTED]) and told her they would send a technician. However, the consumer is not having technical failure with the range, her concerns are with the design of the grate.

Pot of water got bumped fell forward off the stovetop, spilling its contents.

Not yet injured
justification: The incident involved a pot of water spilling due to the stove's design, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is high as the design flaw is inherent and similar incidents could occur frequently.

incident_description:
On a Kenmore Elite Trio (bottom freezer drawer) refrigerator, the lights were not turning off once the doors are closed. This results in the bulbs and the housing overheating, to the point that you can smell smoke/burning and the plastic enclosures where the bulbs screw into are discolored yellow/brown from the overheating/burning.

This has happened twice now in the last six months on this model (795.77719700) that was purchased in 2008. Both times the problem came to our attention when we opened the refrigerator to see that it was dark inside, and that the light bulb enclosure was very hot to the touch and we could smell burning. After the bulbs cool down and the sockets cool down, putting the bulbs back in results in everything seeming to function well, except for the fact that we placed a phone with the video recording into the fridge and saw that the lights were staying on when the doors were closed.

Not sure how this problem has never made it onto the recall list, given the obvious concern for a potential fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves overheating and potential fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred, and it has happened twice in six months indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: The rack in this oven range is no longer supported by the side walls of the oven itself.  Any small amount of wait on the oven rack will make the oven rack fall down on one side or the other.  This has led to a significant burn on my wife's hand.  An internet search for this model number range and this specific issue has yielding specific results totaling over 110.  I am shocked this range has not been recalled yet.  When I called Sears I was directed to call Kenmore customer service.  The Kenmore customer service number led me back to Sears.  It appears that Sears customer service representatives are aware of this issue and have been instructed to tell the consumer to "call the manufacturer."  I called Sears 3 times and explained the issue to 3 separate representatives and each time I was told "call the manufacturer."  Range model # is 790.98023802.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant burn injury, and the issue is reported to be common with over 110 similar cases found online.

incident_description: While preparing my Thanksgiving meal and heating precooked items, my sister and her husband who were assisting me in the kitchen called me from the back and stated that there appeared to be fire or  something blazing up from the left side of the bottom of the oven under the bottom panel.  I opened the door to find that there was a small fire present for which I used baking soda to smother the blaze.   I later realized that the oven was no longer heating from the bottom, only the top element was working.  I called whirlpool on Monday to discuss this matter, informing them that this was my third whirlpool oven I have purchased new, and I have never had a problem with an element before.  I asked if there had been a problem with this model and the heating elements, she stated no and said there was no warranty on the part.  She also recommended that I call a service person to come out and check the oven for cost.  It was only after searching the web did I realize that a similar incident involving this same model, purchased from the same company (Lowes,) had occurred and it would be wise to complete a report as well.
justification: A small fire occurred in the oven, but it was quickly extinguished without injury, and the issue was reported to the manufacturer.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Electric Range glass oven door exploded when it was just over a year old. I was making pizza at 400 degrees. There was a loud explosion and the shards of glass flew everywhere. Sears was not going to replace the glass, but eventually did even though it was no longer under warranty. The technician confirmed it was the brackets holding the glass in the door that had failed. I was told not to use the self-cleaning feature since the high temperatures cause damage to the stove. 

Now 3 years later, the glass on the oven door exploded again. We were making pizza again. I am terrified that it might happen again. I have seven kids. If one of them had been peeking in to see what was baking, they could have been seriously injured, if not blinded. My husband called Sears and was transferred around and told it was no longer under warranty. I spent over an hour being sent back and forth between departments. Sears would not discuss repairs or a credit for a new range. I am not willing to risk a third explosion. It is a miracle no one was hurt the first two times. The range cost about $900, since I had wanted a self-cleaning oven.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door with no reported injuries, but with clear potential for serious harm, especially given the presence of children.

incident_description: The glass in our GE oven door shattered.  The oven was cold and no one was in the kitchen when this happened.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, which is an incident, but no one was injured as the kitchen was unoccupied.

incident_description: My new Frigidaire freestanding range model #BGGF3045RFC serial #VF63127409 has burner knobs which stick out too far in the front of the range and are too easily pressed and turned on. As a result of this, several times I have smelled a gas odor and upon checking found the controls turned enough to allow gas to escape the burners. The more alarming result happened when I reached to the back of the stove to clean and inadvertently turned on the front power burner and barely jumped back  and turned off the burner before my clothing could catch on fire. This also happened twice when I was stirring a large pot simmering on the back burner--the front burner was turned on by my body as I reached over it and luckily, I was not burned.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak and near-miss fire hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: 18 month old Bosch oven Model SHX68TL5UC/02 door inner glass exploded. It was 40 minutes into clean cycle. No one injured. Just a mess
justification: The oven door glass exploded during a clean cycle, but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer put the oven on the bake setting and set the temperature to 375 degrees. The consumer states that he set the oven timer to 21 minutes. The consumer went outside and when he returned to the kitchen a few minutes later he noticed the whole kitchen was filled with smoke. The consumer noticed that the broiler was on (top heating element) and he noticed the control panel displayed the oven temperature at being 500 degrees. The consumer states the "Off" button did not work and he had to shut off the circuit breaker.

The consumer indicated that he waited a few hours for the oven to cool down and turned the circuit breaker back on. Immediately after the consumer noticed the broiler turned back on but the control panel did not indicate that the oven was on.

The consumer then contacted Sears and informed them about the incident. The consumer was told by the Rep. (name unknown) that he would be transferred to the department that could assist him with arranging for a technician to inspect the range. After the consumer was transferred the other Rep. (name unknown) advised him he would need to call 800-638-2772 who would start the report. The consumer was not aware he was being provided the # to the CPSC Hotline. The consumer may contact Sears again to inquire about a repair.

The consumer believes his wife had a similar incident sometime in January 2016 and the oven shut off after she pressed the off button.

The consumer indicated that sometime in 1995 the glass cooktop was replaced due to a chip and the door seal was replaced.

The consumer believes the range poses a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved smoke and malfunctioning controls but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that while using the oven to bake at 400 degrees approximately 20 mins into the operation she heard a loud noise and the panel illuminated.  Smoke and flames started to emit from the rear of the unit.  She stated that she used a fire extinguisher to contained the flames and the contacted the fire department.  The fire department came out and advised her that the range needed to be replaced and that she could obtain a report from them.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that a service technician would be sent out on 10/21 for inspection to see what caused the fire.

Caller is concerned that if she was not present this oven could have caused a house fire and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was contained without injury, and the fire department confirmed the need for replacement without further damage.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that he used his approximately one year old toaster oven on Tuesday, November 2, 2016 to heat food, ate, cleaned up turned the oven off around 5:00PM then checked to be sure it was not warm.
He went to bed then began his day on November 3rd, 2016 when he heard an odd noise then observed that the door to the toaster oven was on the other side of his kitchen and realized that the door had blown off with the glass to the door shattering to the other side of the kitchen & all over the floor.
He is reporting this incident as a severed injury and laceration hazard
He contacted the manufacturer and he was advised that they would be shipping a replacement toaster oven to him and that he should return the exploded one to them.
justification: The incident involved property damage (toaster oven door exploding) but no reported injury, hence severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common.

incident_description: Sparks fly out of the right side of the microwave on the inside making it a fire hazard whenever it is turned on.
justification: Sparks inside the microwave indicate a fire hazard, which could lead to an incident but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
Rival crock pot #5025 is being recalled for handles falling apart on the outer heating tub. I have this pot and the handles have broken. However, the data code for my pot is not on Rival's approved recall list. Hence, they will not replace the outer tub. Obviously, the problem extends beyond the date codes that are on Rival's list.

Date code for my product is 13802.
justification: The handles breaking is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: The microwave started on its own and did not turn off by pressing any of the buttons on the control pad. Stopped it by unplugging it. Fire hazard.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was stopped without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: The microwave was being used to heat three sausage patties on a microwave safe plate when the panel on the inside right side of the microwave caught on fire.
justification: The microwave caught fire, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This unit developed a defect. It worked fine for about 9 months. Now the heating element in the unit does not shut off when the water reservoir empties allowing the heating unit to continue to run. Started to smell burning plastic smell. Likely a fire would have occurred had I not unplugged the unit. 

Now the power switch does not allow you to turn it off either - so you have what is essentially a coffee maker with no water running with the heating element on. Bad situation.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning heating element that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The oven was turned on to 325 degrees to bake cookies.  Appx. nine minutes later the door was opened to check on the cookies and they were still raw.  Moments later there were large sparks behind the stove and "F10" displayed on the digital readout and a beeping sound was heard.  "CANCEL" was pressed numerous times to no avail.  The oven instantly became extremely hot and the cookies began burning/smoking.  The circuit breakers were manually tripped and the problem was stopped.  A lot of smoke was inside the stove from the burning food and a very strong burning plastic smell was emanating from the oven control panel area where the sparks were seen.  The stove was pulled from the wall and unplugged.  The home was aired out and fortunately there was no fire or smoke damage. In my opinion, if someone had not been standing right next to the stove when this happened, due to the rapid overheating of the stove, a fire would have erupted.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction and smoke, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I have had the same hand held mixer for several years. I last used the mixer on Thursday during Thanksgiving dinner without incident. While mixing cookie batter yesterday, the mixer erupted into flames while in use. There are front vents on the mixer where the flames came through. Immediaetly unplugged the mixer and the flames extinguished and placed the mixer outside. No injuries were sustained during this incident.
justification: The mixer erupted into flames but was quickly unplugged and extinguished, with no injuries reported.

incident_description: I was baking a cake at 350 degrees when the glass on my stove exploded.  The racks were in place; the stove had not been jarred or closed harshly in any way.  The stove has been in use for under one year as  I purchased the home only 9 months ago.  The installation, however, has been over a year and I'm afraid the manufacturer will not honor the warranty and this may be a costly repair.  Please, any assistance that can be offered will be greatly appreciated.
justification: The glass on the stove exploded, but there was no mention of injury or death, only concern about warranty and repair costs.

incident_description: After cooking a meal in the oven (set to 400 degrees), I closed the oven door and the outer glass panel for the door shattered.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I opened the door of my oven to see if the rack was in the right location for the cake I was about to bake, and the glass door exploded and shattered throughout my kitchen, hitting me. The oven was not turned on at the time, and had not been used for several weeks prior, since we had been out of town on vacation and just returned. Not all the glass fell to the ground, so I tried to cover what remained with heavy plastic to prevent injury to my family or my cat, and in doing so, cut my finger on the shattered glass that remained in the door.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger from shattered glass, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Oven glass exploding without prior use is rare, hence the low likelihood.

incident_description:
The machine was switched on with cold oil in it to prepare it for cooking that night, but there no food in it as of yet.  After roughly 15 minutes, a "burning plastic" smell was first noticed.  Upon approaching the machine from the front on the counter in which it sits, there was some mild but concerning smoke coming from behind the machine.  Upon checking the back of the machine, there was electrical sparking/arcing coming from the magnetic power cord anti knock over socket on the back of the unit.  The unit was then disconnected from the wall outlet ending the arcing.

No Injuries or property damage occured by this incident.
justification: The incident involved electrical sparking and smoke but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
Product: Frigidair Gas Range/Oven
Model: FGF316WGSH Serial: VF11403603

Oven turns on overnight or while occupants are away unexpectedly and themostat is set to OFF position.

Apartment was vacant for a month, oven went on unknown to anyone. When apartment was entered, it was very hot in kitchen.

The oven thermostat: (EAP Number: EAP2339203) was the cause. This is not a result of wear, but rather a defect in fail safe engineering.

I am seeking a replacement thermostat and hot surface ignitor which prematurely buned out due to the abnormal on/off cycles as complete restitution for this potentionally dangerous thermostat. I can ship this part to you for your inspection and you will find the switch closed in off position
justification: The oven turned on unexpectedly, creating a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The defect in the thermostat suggests this is a possible but not certain occurrence.

incident_description:
(10/30/2016) The consumer stated that he was brewing a cup of coffee. He heard a crash. The cup had vibrated out of the machine and fell on the floor. The consumer brewed another cup of coffee to see what happened.  This time the consumer saw the cup vibrate off of the machine. 

No injures.

The consumer stated that there are reviews for the product online stating that the same thing has happened to others.
justification: The incident involved a cup vibrating off the machine but resulted in no injuries, and similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
My wife noticed that there was smoke coming from the microwave oven.  It was not in use at the time.  She immediately grabbed the microwave oven to unplug it from the wall socket.  The socket was partially melted where the microwave was plugged into the wall.  She took the microwave oven outside of the house.  In her words, if no one was home, it would have most certainly led to a fire.  She said that the exterior housing of the microwave was hot enough to feel through a long sleeved shirt.  The microwave has a manufacture date of June 2013, so it's not like it's an extremely old unit.

We wanted to contact the CSPC because we are concerned that others may not be as lucky and not at home if this type of failure occurs in their own unit.  As it stands, I will need to replace the socket as the only part of my house that actually suffered any damage.  The first floor of the house filled with acrid smoke, but that has been vented.  I have not actually taken the cover off to see any blistering of the power wires coming to the socket.

I have contacted the manufacturer of the unit to allow them to be aware of this particular failure mode.  They have promised to contact me within 24 hours from their response team.  I feel as a concerned citizen, I want all parties to know that something about this particular design can cause it to fail dangerously and catastrophically.  Others may not be as lucky to be home if this were to happen; or worse, they may be sleeping.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the age of the microwave and the described failure mode.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that his microwave was on for approximately one minutes when he smelled smoke emitting from it. The consumer immediately opened the microwave door and noticed flames coming out of a hole on one of its sides where a steel bracket holds the microwave rack. The consumer was able to put out the flames by blowing them out.

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that his microwave is not part of a recall so he would have to pay out-of-pocket to have it repaired.

The consumer indicates that his microwave is still plugged in. The consumer states that prior to the incident, he used his microwave approximately four to five times daily. The consumer plans on keeping the unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury, and the microwave is still in use with frequent prior usage.

incident_description:
During a routine dishwashing cycle at approximate 9pm on 11/19/16, our 10 year old GE dishwasher, model PDW9880N00SS, began to smoke and fill the kitchen and lower area of the home with electronic smouldering smoke. No flames were observed, but the control panel area of the dishwasher was very hot from the event and showed evidence (sight, smell, touch) as the location of the smouldering event. There is burnt residue all over the top of the dishwasher door beside the control panel. The latch area is black and sooty as well.

This was not related to the heating element or anything in the dishwasher at the time. There were no meltable of flammable objects in the wash cycle.

The control panel appears to have shorted out, causing the smoulder and smoke. This appears to be the same flaw as reported in other GE Profile dishwasher models of similar design. The explanation there was water getting into the control area from the door latch opening, which seems the likely culprit in this case as well.

As far as I know, no recall for my model currently exists.
