My report is similar, if not identical to, report # 20131021-5B40D-1363124 on this site for the exact same model.

I represent a townhome community of 90 homes that were outfitted with similar appliances. This is a grave concern for other homes in our community. Resolving the problem and either getting a recall in place, or understanding why that should not happen, is paramount.
justification: The incident involved smoke and smouldering but no injury or death, and similar issues have been reported in other units, indicating a likely recurring problem.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore ceramic cooktop (Model 790.45409410) from Sears in October 2015. At the end of October 2016 (about 2 days after the warranty expired) the large left burner turned on spontaneously, which I only discovered because of the smell of burning plastic and metal. After getting no response from the controls, I switched off the breaker. When I reset the breaker, the burner turned on again. A repairman inspected the unit and ordered a new control board, but when he disassembled the unit, some of the metal contacts and plastic plug sheaths were melted, so we elected not to replace the board by jury-rigging the plugs and contacts. Although there's supposed to be a high-temperature safety cutoff at the supply side of the control board, clearly it did not work properly since the board was hot enough to melt metal.

Just lucky we were home when this happened, or there could have been a major fire, and several pet dogs and birds could have been killed by the fumes, if not by fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cooktop that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased our Kenmore Elite Oven Model #79041023801 in 2009. Over the last few months I noticed the oven racks seemed loose especially the middle one. 

Last month when I went to pull the middle rack to check on the food, it slide off the track fell down to bottom of the oven and the hot food splattered all over my oven, floor and even burnt my foot.

I called for my yearly annual Sears service checkup because we have all of our "wonderful" products on extended warranty with Sears. The Tech confirmed that the oven liner has bowed out and doubts that Sears has this part on hand because this is such a rare issue! 

WHAT? I found hundreds of similar complaints online for this specific oven!!

He said Sears will probably offer us some money (pro-rated based on the age of the oven) and we will have to buy another oven and shell out some cash to cover the difference!!!!

If I don't buy another oven, I'm screwed because he said the warranty will be voided on this one. 

SO, I have to pay for Sear's faulty product and their lack of admission?
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from hot food splattering, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the numerous similar complaints found online.

incident_description:
Purchased the LG 30" Freestanding Double Oven Gas Ranges (LDG4323ST) to replace our current stove.  
We found quickly throughout the day that we had to constantly check the knobs for the range to determine if they've been pushed on.   
My wife or children would use the over the range microwave and with the slightest of push from leaning forward would move the knobs on the range to allow gas or ignite.   We have experienced the knobs to ignite burners while cooking/stirring pots on the two back burns almost causing an accident or catching fire.  My concern elevated when the men working to complete my kitchen remodel, was grouting the back splash tile and leaned against the range which ignited causing him to get burned.  
Investigating why this is happening, what I can see is the controls are mounted to a front plate which is on an angle (not horizontally flat or vertically up and down like many other ranges) with large knobs that when pressed against with the front plate angle will cause the knobs to turn.  I have contacted both LG and hhgregg voicing my safety concern.  LG has dispatched two servicemen to inspect the range.  One used video to display how quickly and easily these knobs can be accidentally turned, which he sent to the LG Korean facility.  The other explained that with no downward force the knobs do not turn and are working properly.  Both explained how I should purchase safety covers to be installed on my knobs.  Which I explained that I did not purchase a $1,000 device that needs to be modified because of design and safety reasons. 
We have since had multiple incidents where we've found the range to be on with not knowing for how long.  
My fear is that (like other reviews and incidents I've read) something will happen that will cause injury to a family member.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to a worker and multiple near-misses, indicating a clear safety hazard.

incident_description: ITEM Oster Countertop Oven Model TSSTTVXXLL  I was cooking chicken cordon blue - (Frozen prepared version from [REDACTED]) on a flat pizza type pan.  I had preheated the oven. Once the oven hit the desired temperature - I inserted the chicken on the pizza pan and set the timer to the appropriate cook time -  about 36 minutes (well past the 20 minute point).  When it was done cooking.  I removed the product from the oven. Moved the timer counter clockwise to the zero point.  The red light indicates the oven is off.  Later while dining - I mention that I think I hear the oven running.  We check - the oven is hot and on.  My husband moves the timer back to zero and comments that he didn't hear the bell ding.  He twists it past the 20 minute point and back to off - no bell.  He turns off the oven.  Later we hear the oven running.  We check and the oven is on again.  We fuss with the timer again - past the 20 minute point going clockwise then back to zero (no bell ding).... then we notice that when we move it to zero - no bell dings, but the oven is off, you can still here the timer ticking though...... and it is slowly working it's way to the ALWAYS ON position and it turns the oven on again.  We reset the oven to zero (past the 20 min and back to zero) ... oven is off ..we watch it as it continues to tick and turn it self on again.. to the ALWAYS ON position.  We move it to zero, unplug it.... plug it back in 10 minutes later - same problem.  We unplug it and go to bed for the night.  The next morning. We twist it past 20 minutes in a clockwise manner, then roll it back to zero (no bell ding) plug it in and yep the timer is ticking and slowly as time passes... it moves to the ALWAYS ON button and it is on again.  Repeated a couple other variations but inevitably it turns itself back on if it is plugged in.  In my opinion, this is a huge fire hazard.
justification: The oven repeatedly turns itself on despite being turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I prepared a cup of coffee with a Keurig coffee maker. I heard a loud noise, turned around and saw that the Keurig was smoking and spewing coffee grinds all over the kitchen--up the walls, down on the floor. Then I noticed through the transparent window on the appliance that the inside of the equipment was red hot. I quickly disconnected the appliance. I contacted the company immediately, but they have never responded.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction and property damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire dishwasher model# fgbd2445nf1a in July 2013. On 11/21/2016 I noticed water all over my hardwood floors in the kitchen. Upon further searching I found out the heating element in my dishwasher had warped and melted through the bottom of the dishwasher and caused the water to run out onto floor.
justification: The incident caused water damage but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: While cooking dinner in the Tfal 10.5 inch stainless steal pan, I heard and felt a bullet like explosion. My right ear lost hearing for about 2-3 minutes as I stepped back and turned off the heat immediately trying to assess the situation. About 4 feet away on the counter top I found a piece of metal shrapnel in the shape of a circle. After removing the food from the pan I found that the rivet had exploded off the inside of the pan by the handle. the remaining steal is extremely sharp and jets out into the pan where the rivet is no longer.
justification: The incident involved a pan rivet exploding, causing temporary hearing loss but no permanent injury.

incident_description: I had placed a bagel in my 2-slice rival toaster 16041 and set to 3.5 minutes as I always have with this toaster.  While it was toasting for some reason the outside coils for extremely hot causing the outside of the begal to catch fire.  Luckily I was two feet away doing dishes.  Meanwhile the inside of the bagel is hardly toasted.
justification: The bagel caught fire due to overheating, but no injury occurred as the person was nearby and able to respond.

incident_description: My KitchenAid double wall oven, model # KEBS2077SSS, serial # XW3504799 - the interior glass panel exploded during the self-cleaning cycle. Unfortunately it's Thanksgiving week...we ran the self clean on the upper over first, that worked fine. Then we ran the self-clean on the bottom oven, and near the end of the self-clean cycle, the interior glass panel exploded into a million little pieces that started shooting out around the edges of the door, onto our hard wood floor in the kitchen - the little glass pieces were so hot they burned spots into the finish on the wood floors. This was very difficult to clean up and we finally placed large pieces of cardboard on the floor to catch the small glass pieces that kept dropping out around the edge of the door as the glass cooled. The explosion shot glass pieces two or three feet out onto the floor, thank goodness we were in the next room and no one was injured or burned.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding glass panel and burned floor) but no injuries, as stated in the description.

incident_description: Consumer using electric oven cooking in the oven portion of the unit. Unit stopped working/ cooking, flashed an error message on the digital display and began to smoke and emanate a burning smell from the rear of the unit. The unit was removed from its place and the rear was examined. The top rear portion of the unit containing circuitry and electrical parts showed burn marks and heat damage to wiring and parts. Consumer was home and quickly unplugged the unit from its power source discontinuing any further damage.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning smell but no injury or death occurred, and the consumer took prompt action to prevent further damage.

incident_description: While cooking in oven and cooktop (1 burner) sparks, smoke, and flames began coming out of the rear of the stove. The breaker was turned off and the stove was pulled out away from the wall. Once the breaker was off the Sparks and flames were less and the flames were blown out. Unplugged stove from receptacle. Removed the rear panel and found the control board melted and burned. Wall behind stove was scorched.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and flames from the stove, causing damage to the stove and wall, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Regarding a Frigidaire FPEC3685KSA Cooktop installed in our kitchen.  On Saturday, Nov 12, the cooktop was being used to boil water.  It started making grinding noises, and smoke began pouring out of it from below.  We shut off the burner control, and it continued to smoke, until the breaker was opened.  The house was filled with electrical fire smoke.  We will be replacing the unit and would like to provide this information for your trending purposes.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific malfunction described.

incident_description: On Sunday, Nov. 13, 2016 my dishwasher overheated for the second time this year. After shutting it off I closed the door and is heated up again. It was turned off! My husband researched this problem and found out there have been many recalls on GE dishwashers. Our model number was not recalled. We would like to know why this model was not recalled. PDW9280N20SS, serial number FR18415B.
justification: The dishwasher overheated but no injury or damage was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Purchased a new Cuisinart Model DCC-1150 Coffee Maker to be used in an office by 5 people.  The FIRST time we used it the carafe leaked hot coffee from the poring spout which ran down the pot and dripped hot coffee on the user.  I called Cuisinart and was advised that since this coffee pot is being used by a business, the warranty is void.  Due to the hazardous issue with this carafe, we are no longer  using it.  I can understand that a warranty would have a shorter limitation if it is being used in an office environment, but that should be no excuse for one that is hazardous and new out of the box.
justification: Hot coffee leaked and dripped on the user, causing injury, but the issue was identified and the product was discontinued after the first use.

incident_description:
Whirlpool microwave caught on fire. My wife used fire extingisher we had near the kitchen thank God. Fire was extingished. She checked and the circuit breaker did open up. We have opened a safety claim with the whirlpool corporation. 
Turns out they have a recall on this unit

Wmh53520cs-0
Ser no. TR 34311556
justification: The microwave caught fire but was extinguished without injury, and the unit is under recall indicating a known issue.

incident_description: I plugged in a Sunbeam Hot Shot water heater model number 6131, put in some water, and hit the start button. I turned my back on it but all of a sudden smelled an acrid smell. I turned and saw smoke coming from the device. I quickly unplugged it and moved the device to the sink in case it broke out in flame. I could feel a real hot spot on the left side of the heating chamber through the protective plastic outer cover. When I turned and looked at the device the white light that indicates the device is heating the water was not on. This was before I unplugged it
justification: The incident involved smoke and a hot spot but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled without escalation.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore Smoothtop range in Nov 2012.  Just 2 days ago, when my husband turned on the convection oven, the range short-circuited.  It caused all the lights in the house to strobe like a fun house and a Horrible arching sound generated throughout the whole house.  I was upstairs and could hear it.  By the time I got downstairs, my husband had the back door open, airing out the kitchen  It was filled with acrid, electrical smelling smoke.  The circuit breaker tripped to protect us.  After the smoke cleared and we felt safe, we removed the back of the range.  We saw melted wires and the plastic box that the wires ran through in the bottom of the panel was totally melted.  There was also soot on the panel causing us to believe that a flame-out had occurred.  Thank goodness the whole range did not catch fire.  We took pictures just in case anyone needs to see them.  We think this range needs to be investigated.  There is no reason for this to have happened.  We had not moved the range in over a year.  Have any other incidents like this happened with this range?
Kenmore Model # 790.92803015
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical malfunction with smoke and potential fire risk, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
My wife and I purchased a LR Electric Range, Model# LRE30755ST, Serial # 605KMEM03212 on [REDACTED]. On 10/23/2016 we were preheating the oven to bake a pizza. When we opened the door there was a large flash and a lot of smoke - We shut off power to the range and when it cooled we noticed that there was a hole inside at the bottom of the range. I contacted LG on 10/24/16 and informed them of the problem. After several calls they agreed to send out a technician who came out on 10/28/2016 and diagnosed that the unit was not repairable. The technician stated that within a sealed section of the unit, there appeared to have been an electrical arc which welded a hole in the bottom of the range and there was nothing he could do to repair it. I followed up with numerous calls to LG all of which resulted in their telling me the range was out of warranty and that there was nothing they would do either to repair, replace or provide me a credit towards the purchase of another range. 
I realize the unit is 10-years old, but the fault lies with the unit and this problem could have caused a fire. I think LG needs to recall these units so other consumers are not put at risk.
The problem was not caused by operator error or an act of God - It is a faulty piece of equipment that was already placed on a recall list for faulty burner problems
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical fault that could have caused a fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was creaming softened butter and sugar in my Cuisinart DLC-X Plus Food Processor - I was using the "pulse" feature when a very loud noise occurred. The chopping blade had broken in half and under high speed flew partially through the plastic bowl. the lid was also nicked by flying metal shards.The blade pieces also gouged each other. The noise was so loud, I still have ear pain 2 hours later. I can see that there are stress cracks around the rivets at the bottom of the blade.
justification: The incident caused ear pain and potential hearing damage, indicating an injury, and the blade failure suggests a possible manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
July 13, 2016
Dear President [REDACTED],
I am writing to you in hopes that you can help me solve a problem.  
I had purchased a Whirlpool 456 Accubake Oven System from ABT electronics over 6 years ago.  I have my daughter and her 3 year old son living with me. It is an extremely dangerous oven that will shut off and spew gas. The first time my husband experienced it, he was shocked. It is a deceiving situation because it won't do it for months and out of the blue, it happens. My husband [REDACTED] is in IT and is convinced it is a defect.
I have had various licensed appliance workers out and they have replaced parts - still happens. Also I had a gas man here and checked the hook up and it is fine - but he said he has the same stove and oven and it does that to him.
I spoke to ABT - they referred me to Whirlpool. Their attorney told me that all they could do is send another repairman out and I would have to pay for parts. They would not replace. I do not understand that?
If I actually thought that would work but it is in the defect.  I had ABT's repairman out at one time also, already. 2RMI2R Parts.
I had been sick so I did not have the energy to pursue this any further then but am feeling better enough to write to you in hopes you can help this situation resolve. I want my family safe ( I worked in a burn unit at one time) and I know this is not a safe responsible remedy. I know I need a new oven. I had reported this to Consumer affairs back in the day so there is a record. I know I need a new oven to replace the one that has been dangerous since day one.  I want Whirlpool to replace the oven (different style, or $ back).
Thank you for your time and thank you for being President of the [REDACTED].

Respectfully,
[REDACTED]
justification: The oven spews gas unexpectedly, posing a danger, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Wolfgang Puck Pressure Oven in late 2014.About 5 days ago, the unit started to turn itself  while unattended. This happened 4 times. I report it to the manufacturer Kitchen Tek LLC (877.359.9747).I was told that the 1 year warranty had expired and that I should buy a new oven. They do not seem to care but it is dangerous.
justification: The oven turning on unattended is a hazardous incident but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Range (Model 790.92903010) purchased in 2013 at Sears in Springfield Oregon. Today, I preheated it to 350 on the Convection Roast setting. It beeped, indicating that it had reached temp. A few minutes later I stepped over my dog (who was laying in front of the oven) and opened the oven door. When the door had been pulled open just a few inches, there was a loud BANG and glass flew into my kitchen and onto my dog as the glass outer door exploded. Nobody was hurt, but it doesn't sound like Sears is willing to pay for this. I am furious, because this keeps happening to this model of oven, and this is not a thing that should need to be covered by warranty. This is a thing that should never happen.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to fly, but no one was hurt.

incident_description: I was cooking a lasagna in an Amana brand oven when the inside glass door exploded in the oven.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Glass on outside of the oven door exploded as my 3 year old was walking past it. Glass from one end of my kitchen to the other and into my living room. My child was covered in little pieces of glass and dust from the glass. No injuries noted at this time. We did not use our oven or stove tonight.
justification: The incident involved glass explosion with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but possible with glass components.

incident_description: While baking pizza in our Kenmore oven (model# 79045599901) the glass on the oven door exploded.  We had opened the oven door and the handle came off so we tried to open the oven to get the food out and the glass exploded sending hot glass throughout the kitchen and dining room.  We were grateful no one was injured.  I called Sears where we purchased the range 6 years ago and inquired about repair and recall information.  I was told the representative would submit an inquiry about a recall.  After researching the model number and exploding glass oven door, many incidents of exploding oven doors were listed online.  How has Kenmore been allowed to not notify and recall this product?  They built and sold a common household product that through normal wear and tear may shoot shards of hot glass throughout your home.  How is this possible they have not recalled this product or notified their customers of this safety hazard?  They may as well strapped dynamite to the oven door and say it may explode after a few years if you use your product as intended.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door causing hot glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported. Online research indicates this is a recurring issue, suggesting a likely occurrence.

incident_description: The glass lid on my wife's pan shattered while she was cooking rice.  She was in the living room when she heard a loud pop.  She went to investigate and found the lid totally spider webbed into small pieces like safety glass breaks.  I have pictures of the lid before I discarded it.
justification: The glass lid shattered but no one was injured as the wife was in another room when it happened.

incident_description: I prepared stuffed peppers and put them in the baking dish. I used the " [REDACTED] Healthy Family Cookbook" recipe. I placed the prepared dish into a preheated 350 degree oven for 30 minutes. As I put my hand on the oven door to remove the peppers I heard a loud BOOM. I looked through the window on the oven door and saw glass & stuffed peppers all over. It took FIVE HOURS to clean this mess.
justification: The incident involved a loud explosion and a mess, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I used this product to cook beef stew. While simmering, I removed the cover and put it on top of the cooktop which I normally do every time I am cooking. I put the cover on the top of cooktop which is not being use. After few seconds the cover suddenly burst and shattered into tiny pieces and also shattered our glass cooktop. I am lucky I just got small cuts to my fingers and the shattered glass did not went in my eyes. This product should be recalled as it could cause serious injuries or worst blindness to anybody.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts to the fingers, indicating an injury, but no severe harm or death occurred.

incident_description: Glass in range/oven door exploded.  Nothing hit the door.  It just exploded for no apparent reason.
justification: Glass exploding is an incident with potential for injury, but no injury was reported in this case.

incident_description: As my Whirlpool oven was in cleaning mode, the interior glass shattered. This is the first time I've used the cleaning mode in this oven. I have only had it 1 yr and 2 weeks.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering during cleaning mode, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Dual fuel gas range control panel / circuit board (replaced in 2014 by the manufacturer) is exhibiting same issues as the original - Random error codes on the LCD screen / failure of control panel.  The last time (in 2014) we were told that excessive heat from too much cooking caused the failure.  As our cooktop burners are gas, I am concerned with any failure of the control panel.
justification: The incident involves a control panel failure with no reported injury, and the issue has recurred after a previous replacement, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
(07/2016) The consumer stated that the oven have been turned off after baking. The oven came back on by itself. The consumer had to turn the stove off at the breaker. The same thing happened again in August and September.

(10/22/2016) The consumer stated that his wife baked cookies. She turned the oven off after the cookies were done. His wife left the home and came back an hour later. The oven was still on and the cooktop was hot. The consumer tried to turn the stove off again but it would not go off. The consumer advised his wife to turn the stove off at the breaker.

(10/25/2016) The consumer contacted the firm to see if there was something that could be done. The consumer was advised that the range was not on the recall list.
justification: The oven malfunctioned multiple times, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(11/2015) The consumer stated that she had not used the oven for several days. She was standing at the kitchen sink. All of a sudden there was a pop. Glass from the exterior door shattered and flew over the room. 

(11/2015) The consumer contacted GE. She was advised that she would have to get the door replaced or buy a new one because it was out of warranty. The consumer was also advised that they had not heard of the issue before.
justification: Glass shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The issue seems rare as the manufacturer had not heard of it before.

incident_description:
GE above the range microwave oven . Model #JVM7195SF1SS Manufactured February 2015.
It sits 18" above the GE range. GE recommends 13-16". heat is causing the metal film wrapped plastic handle to peel. The metal film edge is razor sharp and cut my hand while opening the door. it has already been replaced once in the past 6 months, and is already peeling again. the microwave is a little over a year old.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury from a razor-sharp metal film edge, and the issue has recurred despite previous replacement.

incident_description: The side walls of the oven have warped out under normal use and the racks fall with any weight applied on them when installed in any of the slots other than the top.  Scalding hot liquid or metal pots and baking sheets bounce/ splash who knows where.  Burnt my hand on a pot that lurched forward onto the opened oven door.  It's happened to multiple ovens and I'm not sure why the model hasn't been recalled.  Here's a laundry list of others who have had the same problem.  https://community.sears.com/Discussions/Single_question_detail/All/Allquestions/The-oven-racks-in-Kenmore-Elite-(Model-79031043302)-Fall-Down-and-have-caused-burns .  Sears charges a fee to have it examined/ replace, which is bullshit when their product is flawed and highly dangerous.  The form below asks for a date but it's continuous because any time I bake anything I'm at risk.  How has this not been recalled?!
justification: The incident describes burns from hot pots due to faulty oven racks, indicating injury (severity 3). The problem is widespread and recurring, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
(09/22/2016) The consumer stated that she had apples in the pressure cooker. She let the pressure off and tried to open the product. The consumer stated that the steam was out and as she tried to open it, the cooker exploded. The consumer stated that the steam and apples blew out and burned her left arm.

The consumer went to the ER at [REDACTED] Hospital in [REDACTED]. The consumer had to go to the Trauma Unit. The consumer had second and third degree burns.
justification: The consumer suffered second and third degree burns requiring ER and Trauma Unit care, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool range that often shuts down and shuts off my breaker.  This happened numerous times over  the summer but after a short while I could flip the switch and turn it back on.  Just today I turned on the oven clean and once it got too hot it flipped the breaker switch again.  I contacted Whirlpool but they said it is out of warranty and I would have to pay for them to send a service tech out to see what the problem is.  Because I didn't word my complaint right she said there isn't a safety issue.  What if I weren't home and something worse happened
justification: The incident involves frequent breaker trips without injury, indicating a recurring issue with potential safety concerns if left unaddressed.

incident_description: Two to racks collapse when anything is put on them, and I mean anything.  I do believe this could be a serious burn issue or even fire issue if there were liquids of any kind in the pans. The oven racks worked fine the first year, the last two times I used the self clean option is when I started having the problem.  It seems the oven has expanded since the last few self cleanings were done. I have tried moving the racks around by switching them but to no avail they still collapse.
justification: The collapsing racks pose a burn or fire hazard if liquids are present, but no actual injury or incident is reported yet.

incident_description: Our Giada de Laurentis lasagna pan was in use when the handle broke off, holding a large amount of hot food. Luckily, we were not injured. The product was recalled in 2013, but we were not made aware.
justification: The handle broke off while in use, posing a risk, but no injury occurred. The product was previously recalled, indicating a known issue.

incident_description:
This morning our GE microwave oven started on its own without any action on my part.  It is a GE Microwave/Convection Oven Model PVM1790SR1SS.  My wife and I heard a humming noise and at first we thought it was coming from the refrigerator.  Then we noticed a burning smell. We observed that the microwave control panel display was blank so then we checked the oven which was cold.
I then opened the microwave oven door and the humming noise stopped.  The interior side walls of the microwave oven were HOT!  I then unplugged the microwave to ensure it would not restart.
justification: The microwave started on its own and produced a burning smell, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
On 11/12/16 at approximately 7:00pm my husband and I returned home from dinner out,  to find our house full of electrical type smoke. We called the fire department immediately. They found that our dishwasher door had a fire and had caused the extreme smoke damage and minor kitchen damage. I had turned the dishwasher on to run while we were out to dinner with out of town guests. The firemen chief said had we been gone longer our house could have been caught/engolfed in fire within a very short time.
Brand: GE Profile
Model # PDW8400J10WW
Serial # MH762446B
Appliance Park 40225
165062P014

Marigene Lasorsa
justification: The incident involved a fire causing smoke damage and minor kitchen damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We own a Maytag Gemini oven and range combo.  The model number is MER6872BAS.  The serial number is 18487235CJ.  Yesterday my 2 1/2 year old son stuck a spatula into a gap in the front underside of the range.  The spatula touched the electrical contacts for the hot surface indicator light.  Sparks flew, part of the spatula melted, and the breaker blew.  Luckily the spatula had a plastic handle so he was not electrocuted.  I'm not sure what the purpose of this hole is.  I think this is a dangerous design and want to make sure that nobody else is hurt in the same way.
justification: The incident involved sparks and equipment damage but no injury, warranting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description:
Our Frigidaire range has an issue with 1) burner not turning off when knob is turned to off, 2) burner sticks on high regardless of where knob is turned.  We learned there was a recall on Frigidaire ranges, but our model number is not included in the recall.  We have the exact problem the recalled models have.  It is extremely frustrating that Frigidaire refuses to take action.  We are unable to continue to use the range due to the fire hazard, and will have the financial burden of purchasing a new one.
Model #FEFL79GCA
Serial #VF71543485
justification: The range's burner malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet. The issue is likely to occur given the described behavior and recall context.

incident_description:
Sporadically, one of the burners does not turn off and seems to get stuck at high heat. The only way i have been able to turn it off if from the breaker.
This same burner also sporadically goes on maximum heat although it is set in medium or lower.

I just replaced the switch with a part recommended from the manufacturer and it also does not gradually heat the burner as it is supposed to. The heat is either very low or maximum heat.

This is certainly a fire hazard. I have had two cooking pots destroyed when the heat was set to low sim because the heat switched to maximum.
justification: The burner's malfunction poses a fire hazard and has already destroyed cooking pots, indicating a significant risk of property damage.

incident_description: Deep cut on hand while cleaning Electrolux stove surface just below touch pad. Model number e13ogf55gsg , serial number vf03140072.  Stainless steel edge has very sharp burr on thin sheet metal decorative surface between touch pad control and cook top surface.
justification: The description mentions a deep cut on the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The sharp burr on the metal surface suggests this could happen frequently during cleaning (likelihood 4).

incident_description: We have a Kenmore double oven purchased in 2012. Model #790 48879901, Serial #NF23519819. On 9/24/16, the bottom glass door on our oven exploded. I had just heated a pizza at 375 degrees, then about 10 minutes later we heard the explosion. Glass flew all around the surrounding rooms to our kitchen, and also ricocheted off the cabinets and landed in the dining room behind the kitchen. The sound of the explosion was incredible! No one was in the kitchen thankfully. I have contacted both Sears and Kenmore and both are no help since the oven is out of warranty. It is unimaginable what could have happened if one of my 3 children were standing in front of it when it exploded. Please help us in any way you can. I'm frightened to have it in my house with no way of knowing if the other door will suddenly explode. No appliance should explode in someone's home.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no one was injured. The incident could have been severe if someone was nearby.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while using the microwave it would not power off, smoke started to emit for the wall of the unit.  She had to use the circuit breaker to switch the power off.

The manufacturer was contacted and a service technician came out a few days later and noticed that the unit had melted and did not have any parts to repair it.  He informed her that they would be sending out someone, however, they have been out twice and she is still waiting to get the right parts.

Caller feels that this unit is a fire hazard and should be reported
justification: The microwave emitted smoke and required circuit breaker intervention, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she is experiencing problems with her ceramic top range which was replaced in 2/2013.  The left front burner would not turn off, the circuit breaker was used to switch it off. She stated that she contacted the retailer but they advised that the range was no longer under warranty.

Caller stated that the original stove had the same problem as well.

Caller would like this matter to be resolved quickly by the company because it is a fire hazard.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet. The issue has recurred, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the oven outer glass door exploded while the unit was not on.  She stated that no one was home when the incident occurred, they came home and found that glass pieces were shattered everywhere on the kitchen floor, counter tops and adjacent room.

The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that they would sending out a replacement glass on 10/25 and a service technician would be coming out on 10/26.  Caller stated that  informed her that they would be charged an installation fee.

Caller feels that this oven glass door in a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: No one was home when the oven glass door exploded, so there was no injury, but the incident caused property damage.

incident_description: This relates to a KitchenAid dishwasher Model No. KDTM404ESS1, Serial No. F6128849.  The problem relates to the control panel which is at the top of the door, i.e., when you close the door you do not see the controls.  The control panel protrudes slightly from the ends of the door and on the interior corners has a curved edge which is not flush with anything under it.  That is, it creates somewhat of a "scoop."  When the door is open to either fill or empty the unit, that corner, or scoop, is at the top edge of the open door.  On several occasions, my wife has cut her leg on this edge.  I did so yesterday and by the afternoon began to develop cellulitis.  I am current on 10 days antibiotic for the infection which is quite painful.  When my wife first cut herself, we complained to KitchenAid and the representative indicated that they had never had such a complaint.  That representation is dubious since the CPSC has an incident reported from 2012.  I checked at the store where we purchased the dishwasher (Ferguson's) and all KitchenAid and JennAir dishwashers appear to have this defect.  Bosch dishwashers do not.  This design defect hits the leg approximately 6 to 7 inches above the floor.  It obviously presents a hazard to young children who might be in the vicinity of an open door one of these units.
justification: The incident describes injuries (cuts leading to cellulitis) caused by the dishwasher's design, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to multiple reported incidents and the design defect being present in multiple models.

incident_description:
SAMSUNG MICROWAVE PURCHASED WITH NEW STOVE FOUR WEEKS AGO, AFTER USING LAST WEEK
THE MICROWAVE CAUGHT FIRE AND MELTED THE INSIDE-THE STORE REPLACE WITH A NEW ONE THIS SATURDAY
justification: The microwave caught fire, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description: We had a whirlpool range replaced in our house because the previous whirlpool product was catching fire back in 2014. The range/oven was put into the house in 2014.  We went to cook something in the oven this evening and a very strong chemical smell started to spread throughout the home/kitchen.  We opened the door to the oven, and the smoke alarms immediately went off and the chemical smell was intense and there was a noticeable liquid bubbling around the bottom of the range glass window on the inside. My husband touched the outside of the oven with a leg and came away with potential burn.  The entire outside of the oven door was hot to touch and could possible give 2nd to 3rd degree burns to our children.   The inside part of the glass window is now removable and at any moment if the oven door is opened will fault out and shatter.  I have called whirlpool and spoke about this issue, I was told it was outside the warranty timeframe and would need to pay for a repairman to take a look.  It is a full/complex safety issue, as we are concerned that a child or an adult can obtain burns from the outside of the oven as well the possibility of the glass window shattering.  Additionally, we are unsure of the potential harmful effects of the chemical now burning in the oven for our children.
justification: The incident involves a potential burn injury and a risk of glass shattering, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the ongoing safety issues with the oven.

incident_description:
I hear a Exploding Sound, and realize The Top of my Cuisinart Top have Exploded in Tiny little pieces of glass.
Product was being For Cooking.
No injury was Sustained. If anything Just Scared me, want to use any more glass Top Cookware.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass top but no injuries were sustained, only fear and a decision to avoid glass cookware in the future.

incident_description: This Electric Kettle was bought from a seller on eBay. The manufacture advertise that the kettle would turn off automatically when the water was hot and ready, after several days useing the kettle it quit turning off when I attempted to lift the kettle by the handle my hand got burn.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury due to the kettle's failure to turn off automatically.

incident_description:
We recently purchased an LG electric range model# LDE4413ST.
We have noticed it is very easy to accidently turn on the burners of the stove top just by leaning against the knobs. This past weekend, we had guests over for supper. My wife took a glass baking dish out of the oven and placed it on the stove top. At some point, someone leaned against the knobs, turning on one of the burners to high. My wife noticed this, turned off the burner and began moving the dish off the burner. When did so, the glass baking dish literally exploded. Glass was in all of our supper including side dishes that were on the counter next to the range. My wife sustained minor glass cuts on her feet and the dinner was ruined. Due to the extreme safety issue with this product, we are now removing the burner knobs unless we are using the stove top.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (glass cuts) and property damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the ease of accidentally turning on the burners.

incident_description:
While using Cuisinart Immersion stick blender I was dislodging stuck food with my finger. Blades accidentally  activated by the gentle torque on the stick. I sustained multiple lacerations, 4 fractures and a severed tendon. 
ER attending stated this was the third injury of this type caused by Immersion Blender he had seen this week.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple lacerations, fractures, and a severed tendon, indicating a severe injury (level 3). The ER attending's statement suggests this type of injury is not rare, supporting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
Kenmore Refrigerator Model 253 60082412 Serial # 4A63224289, sold by SEARS. Door handle of top freezer and refrigerator compartment constitute a serious safety hazard, handles are protruding almost 3 inches at the junction of each door, they have sharp corner edges, every member of my family has bump their heads, elbows and fore arms when retrieving items from freezer or refrigerator, continuous injury to our elbows fore arm and particularly our   heads may result in serious trauma to the brain, my wife and I have suffer scalp wounds, the door handles could cause wide open wound in the scalp that my require stitches. This Kenmore item should be recall , door handles are defective and badly design.
Have complained to Sears to have the item return or  exchange  for another model to no avail. Since Sears has refuse to cooperate, I have taking steps to dispute the charges with the credit card that according to them will take about six weeks.
justification: The description reports injuries such as scalp wounds and potential for serious trauma, indicating a severity level of 3. The frequent occurrence of these injuries to multiple family members suggests a likelihood of 4.

incident_description: Loading a dishwasher, the door is in the open (or down position). The edge of this appliance on both top corners is very sharp. I have cut myself twice, and I am an adult. If a child were to walk around this, they could be injured worse.
justification: The description mentions cuts from sharp edges, indicating injury, and suggests potential for worse injury to children.

incident_description:
I was roasting squash covered with foil in a roasting pan at 350F in the oven. 
After 40 minutes I heard a loud pop and saw the glass was in many pieces and falling inside the oven.
Luckily there is a clear outer piece that covers most of the door, so the hot glass stayed in the oven and
did not hit me. 
This is a brand new range that has been in use since September 16, 2016.
GE 30" Range
Model JB250RK1SS   Serial  RG219757Q
justification: The glass shattered but the outer piece contained the fragments, preventing injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung Microwave from Sears on 10-04.  It wasn't installed until the end of October.  On 11-03-16, my sister was microwaving oatmeal in a bowl when I heard a pop and there was a flash of light.  When I looked into the microwave, there was flames inside on the right side of the microwave.  I shut the microwave off.  Luckily, the fire was smothered out.  I unplugged the cord and had the fire department come and check it out as there was a hole burned through the side of the microwave that touches my cabinet. incident_description:
Product: GE Over-the-range 1.6 cu. ft. microwave oven 
Model: JVM3160RFSS 
Serial: GD282802A 
Manufactured: April 2014. Assembled in China. 

Incident: This microwave oven was installed over a gas cooking range. It operated normally for 18 months. On November 2, 2016, while heating food, the glass on the door spontaneously shattered. The door was not subjected to mechanical impact. 

Design issue: When a microwave oven is used above a cooking range, the range burners cause cyclical heating of the microwave door. Possibly the cycles of heating and cooling over time weaken the heat-tempered door glass, resulting in eventual failure by spontaneous shattering. 

On this model, the input vents of the microwave exhaust fan are located near the back. This location makes them less effective for venting hot air. This is a product design concern that merits careful investigation.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous shattering of the microwave door glass without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) due to the design issue causing cyclical heating.

incident_description: I purchased a GE Profile gas range in June of 2016 (Model #PGB911SEJ2SS) from Home Depot.  I don't cook or bake, so I didn't realize the front vent, which is located just below the large knobs, blows out at such high temperatures it actually will burn your skin if you touch any metal above it...including the knobs!  My 4 year old grandson was looking into the oven when he placed his hand on the front, right above the vent and it burned his skin.  This is a dangerous design flaw to place the vent on the front of the oven, right below the knobs of the stove top.  The metal plate around the knobs, the knobs and the oven door heat at high temperatures when baking.  GE claimed underwriters Laboratory gave a their seal of approval on this model, which is a lie.  I called and opened a case with UL and the investigator stated if there is not a sticker on the appliance or paperwork, they did not certify it passed their standards.  The investigator also looked up this model and he doesn't have record of it.  I told this to GE and everyone I spoke with said the same thing (like robots) that GE's appliances are certified by UL and pass their heat standards.  GE's consumer relations department told me they could do nothing about the oven and for me to hire a lawyer due to my grandson being burned!  I couldn't believe they didn't want to investigate this model for this design flaw! They need to recall these ovens that have the vent on the front.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to a child, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is assessed as possible (3) given the design flaw and the potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: Dishwasher was running on Heavy Wash cycle when my wife noticed me of a bad smell coming from the dishwasher. The controls were all still lit and functional. I checked the heating element expecting some plastic dish ware was melting on the element, but found nothing and noticed the smell was in the door, not the wash basin. I pressed cancel and the dishwasher cycled through the drain process and shut off. Upon disassembling the control panel, I found the two wiring (110V hot and neutral) connectors to the door switch had melted and charred. All wires and connections looked and felt secure in the spade terminals. It appears to me that the door switch failed, shorting out and burning the switch, connectors and wiring. It surprised me that the most used switch on the unit would have such a large electrical load run through it... This switch should be controlling a relay to handle the load, not the load itself. It is a poor, and dangerous design.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical failure but no injury occurred.

I purchased an LG range, model LRE3083, on October 10,2016.  It was delivered and installed on 10/18/2016.  This range is dangerous. They were not able to answer that question and told me to "use caution and when someone gets burnt to call back and fill out a product liability claim".  Not happy with that response.  So, I called consumer safety line and spoke to a woman who helped me understand the guidelines for being UL listed.  For this part, because I believe it is plastic, a temp up to 180 would Be considered OK.  I utilized a infrared heat thermometer to check the temperature when the oven had been on at 400 for 1 hour.  The readings I received were from 198.3, 195.5, 195.9, 193.8, and 200.3 degrees. The heat gun is accurate to plus or minus 2 degrees.  It is well above 180 and is extremely dangerous.  I am working with the retail store to see if they can take it back.  They will be out on Wednesday to do their own test. incident_description:
The consumer indicates that three hours after he had gone to sleep he was awoken by security personnel from his building indicating that a neighbor had complained of the smell of gas and they had concluded it came from his apartment. The consumer went to his kitchen and noticed that one of the knobs on his oven range was on even though said oven range had not been used. The consumer believes his wife must have accidentally brushed against the dial when she was in the kitchen.

The consumer states that the electronic ignition of his oven range is at the end of the dials and not at the beginning like most other oven ranges; this poses a safety hazard to consumers since one can easily brush against a knob and turn the unit on unbeknownst to that person. The difference with a knob that has an electronic ignition at the beginning is that a person can hear the "clicking" of it and become aware that they accidentally turned the unit on. 

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that in order for the knob to turn one must push against it. The consumer noted that although this is true, the knob requires very little force to push and turn. The consumer filed a report with the Manufacturer: [REDACTED], 

The consumer states that, prior to the day of the incident, the oven range was used approximately four to five times per week; the consumer uses said oven range with the same frequency to date. The consumer is unsure if he will keep his oven range for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

On October 24,2016, the bulbs in the back of the refrigerator melted the plastic and wiring controlling the interface that in turn controls the lighting, water and ice. Fortunately, the lighting no longer working prevented the refrigerator from catching fire as we slept in our beds. Upon further research we found that other consumers were not as fortunate as their units caught on fire. We contacted the manufacturer and they did not seem concerned. They further stated they had not heard of this issue occurring with other consumers. However, with just minutes of research on the Consumer Reports website we found numerous reviews where consumers had the same problem with their refrigerator. My husband and I don't have children so our refrigerator is not left open for extended periods of time as was suggested by the manufacturer. 

Due to their lack of concern and their inability to stand by their product, we will never purchase another Frigidaire product.
justification: The incident involved melted plastic and wiring, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: It started with a pop and crash in the kitchen. Upon investigating, we found the lower oven door of our double wall oven was shattered and glass was raining down on the floor. The peculiar thing is the glass panel that broke was contained inside the oven door (interior to the door). The panel on the outside and the panel on the inside of the door are intact. The broken glass came out through the vents in the bottom of the door. By repeatedly opening and closing the door, we have discharged most of the shattered glass. But small amounts continue to trickle out. Also of note: neither oven was in use, nor had been in use for 24 hours. The lower oven has only been used once or twice, ever. The last time it was used was many months ago. In addition to the danger involved with the initial shattering of the glass, the continuing trickle of residual glass makes our kitchen a dangerous place.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass creating a hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Whirlpool glass top range.  When the large burner is used for a period of time (15 to 20 minutes) the front edge and entire right side of the cook top gets extremely hot.  Hot enough to burn someone.  A small child could be seriously burned.  Whirlpool says this is normal and it is how the unit works.  They claim the edges can reach 170 degrees.  I do not believe this is safe. 

Model Number of the appliance is: WFE515S0ES0
justification: The description indicates the cooktop gets hot enough to burn someone, especially a small child, which constitutes an injury risk.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Microwave that I purchased a couple years ago. It has not been used very much,  because I stored it after I bought it because I was remodeling my kitchen. This past week-end, when I used it, one of the plastic clips holding the metal rack in place caught on fire. I am guessing that the metal rack may have touched the metal wall causing arcing. I called Sears and they told me that it would cost $247.00 plus parts for a technician to come out and look at it. I think that is rediculous, considering how new the microwave is, and the little use that it has had. The Model Number is 790.80353310. The Serial Number is KG 34219001. Thank you.
justification: The microwave's plastic clip caught fire due to arcing, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I plugged in a brand new Sharp microwave and turned it on to make sure it actually worked before mounting it to the wall. It immediately began smoking, thick grey plumes coming out of it. Then my husband googled it and there are several reports of this model (R-1214-T) catching on fire and/or smoking. This was 3 years old, but had never been used. It was stored inside of our house in the basement bar area, waiting for us to finish moving in. I knew a return would be a painful process so I took it to the local repair shop thinking it would be a $50 maximum repair. I was wrong, and ended up being quoted $250 to repair the $400 unit! When I called SHARP to report it, they stated that there's always a percentage of failures and that online reports are not a real representation of the total # of failures, so there was no need to alert the public. They also stated that they would not repair or replace the unit due to the age, regardless of the unit being brand new and a known defective design. I'm hoping that this report will alert the USCPSC that this design is known to cause fires due to an overpowered transformer. I would request that you require SHARP to alert consumers of this fire hazard and offer to replace the defective component with the appropriately powered transformer as soon as possible.
justification: The microwave smoked but did not cause injury or death, and there are multiple reports of similar incidents indicating a possible design flaw.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught fire.
justification: The dishwasher catching fire is an incident with no reported injury, and such occurrences are relatively uncommon.

incident_description: Oven was set on 375 and using the timer. There was a loud pop and electrical noise. Smoke and Fire was coming out the back of the control panel.
justification: The incident involved smoke and fire from the oven's control panel, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased Whirlpool gas range, Model WFG540HES0 Serial R54339104, a 5 burner slide in range last Dec.  I began noticing gas odor occasionally.  I called Whirlpool today,10-24-16. to report that the 2 center knobs could be opened to allow gas to escape without pushing the knob in which is normally the function for turning the stove on.  These 2 knobs could be move by a brush against the stove, a light touch, which allowed gas to escape. Which to me is a safety issue as this could be done as one passed and did not notice the gas. Why would only 2 of the knobs not work properly?  I called Whirlpool and the response was that there was no recall and that the issue I outlined was normal.  I do not think that is correct; I see this as a safety issue.
justification: Gas leakage due to faulty knobs poses a safety hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

Baking chicken at 375 degrees.
The glass in the oven door exploded.
Shooting glass into the dinning room.

incident_description:
Safety Issue - Product: Samsung 2.1 Cu.Ft. Over-the-Range Microwave (Model # ME21H706MQS/AA).  

Problem - this item was purchased new and installed recently (October 11, 2016) - it was installed in my rented condo - my tenants reported to the management company that shortly after it was installed that the microwave was "smoking and has a large hole in the side" where the microwave device is housed.  They sent me a picture of the damage caused by an internal blow out thru a metal cover on the right side of the microwave.  I will be happy to send you a copy of the photo as proof of the serious nature of this product flaw.

This is a definite safety issue and could have caused personal and/or physical damage to the tenants and/or the condo.  

I am sending this to you so other owners of this device will be forewarned.
justification: The microwave had an internal blowout causing smoke and damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My Kenmore under counter dishwasher's upper tray is poorly supported by fragile small plastic wheels mounted on side brackets. These wheels have detached from their attachments on the side brackets. When the tray is pulled out for loading or unloading, the front tilts downward possibly causing anything in it to fall out. This appliance is only 3 years old and is only run twice a week.
justification: The incident involves a dishwasher tray that may cause items to fall out, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I recently purchased a whirlpool stove model number WFG540HoESO, serial # R62267220. My son was reaching over to stove to the microwave when he leaned against the stove and the stove turned on. The controls are way to sensitive and could have caused a serious accident. This happened to me as I was reaching to the microwave as well. Either the issue needs to be fixed or the stove recalled since this is a safety hazard.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard with the stove turning on unintentionally, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: was using this toaster to toast a couple of slices of bread...set it on low..as I just wanted them a little crisp...was gonna go back a get them latter as I was doing something else at the time...well a couple of mins. latter the smoke detector sounds....so I go into the kitchen and the thing is on fire and the melted plastic has the top of the counter on fire also..and the bottom of the cabinets were ready to go...at first I was gonna use the dry chemical fire extinguisher that I keep by the smoke alarm...but then seen the sink had water in it...pulled the plug...wet a towel so as try to catch the melted burning plastic from hitting the floor (vinyl)  but still some did burn holes in that ...tossed it in the sink..then took more wet towels to cool the counter top..another couple of seconds and I think the counter would have gone up as it had burnt though the protection
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
Was making espresso this afternoon for my wife and I. As I walked back to the machine to check on the progress, the filter basket came loose from the machine, striking and shattering the glass carafe below it. I was sprayed with extremely hot coffee, grounds and small glass bits, some of which stuck into my skin above my right hip. My kitchen was covered in coffee, grounds and glass shards and splinters from the carafe. 

The machine is a Mr. Coffee, model BVMC-ECM260. Looking through previous reports, I see this is not the first time Mr. Coffee has released an espresso machine suffering from this defect; another model was recalled about 20 years ago for the exact same problem.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from hot coffee and glass shards, and the defect has been reported before, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: While cooking dinner in the oven our Samsung electric rang/oven started on fire. The fire originated in the control panel not the cooking area. The fire appears electrical in nature.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven's control panel, which is a significant hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Twice I've opened dishwasher and have cut my finger on the edge of the machine above the handle.
justification: The description reports a cut injury from the dishwasher edge, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident has occurred twice, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his spouse was using the oven at a low broil temperature for approximately 2 mins, when she closed the door she heard a loud noise and noticed that the oven glass door had exploded shattering glass pieces to the floor.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this oven door is a safety hazard and should be recalled
justification: The oven door exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her oven came on spontaneously by itself In the broil mode, she was unable to power it off.  She stated that her son removed it from the wall and unplugged it , the heat burnt 3 holes in the rear of the unit.  The cabinets and countertops became overwhelmingly hot from the incident.  She stated that when her spouse came home he plugged it back in just to see if the incident was a fluke but the same problem re-occurred.

(10/8) The manufacturer was contacted through email but she did not receive a response.

(10/12) She contacted the company and spoke to an agent who informed her that the incident occurred because of a "run off" meaning that the oven was filled with grease.  She stated that her oven was spotless.

Caller stated that they researched the problem online and noticed that there were many complaints.
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction causing heat damage and potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My Kenmore Model 100.8920890A Electric Stand Mixer occasionally starts on its own even when turned off.  Only removing the plug from the wall stops it.  The interlock that should inhibit running when the head is lifted doesn't stop it either.  The local Sears store in Lima Ohio refuses to fix it and also their national service center.
justification: The mixer starting on its own poses a potential hazard, but there is no mention of injury or death in the description.

incident_description:
We bought a West Bend Microwave model #EM925AJW-P1. 
It keeps running even when the time is up and the door is open. 
All buttons including the stop button work but when you open the door it spontaneously switches on. We often have kids in our home. We are afraid of them burning themselves so we removed the microwave from our kitchen.
We contacted West Bend and gave them the serial number. They informed us it is not under a recall notice and they won't refund any of our money nor replace it. 
We just bought it last year, but they say because it was MANUFACTURED more than a year ago the warrantee is no good.

(My hands and forearms tingle like a sunburn from putting it inside to get the bowl of soup out that was in it.)
justification: The microwave continues to operate when the door is open, posing a burn risk, and the user reports tingling hands and forearms, indicating injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that she was using the toaster oven when it caught on fire approximately five or six minutes after she had turned it on. There were flames as high as one foot. The consumer unplugged the toaster oven immediately and a few minutes later she poured water on it.

The consumer dismantled the unit and kept some of its parts before discarding the others.

The consumer indicates that she used her toaster oven at least once daily.
justification: The toaster oven caught fire, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the garbage disposal started to smoke and emit flames, after power it off the flames dissipated.  The unit was in use for about 10-15 seconds when the incident occurred.  The unit was uninstalled and stored.

The manufacturer was contacted through email.

Caller feels this product is a fire hazard and should be reported
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames but no injury, and the issue was resolved by turning off the unit.

incident_description:
My daughter and family moved into newly refurbished home. Brand new inside and out and the kitchen is totally renovated with Frigidaire appliances.  I was using the oven to bake a casserole for family meal time and noticed not only the interior oven reaching 350 to 400 degrees (whatever recipe called for) the complete exterior surfaces were also the SAME temperature; oven handle, knobs, outer vents, outer oven door, outer oven glass door, lower broiler drawer and handle. Did not realize the oven handle and door would be 350 to 400 degrees as well and went to remove item from oven and received second degree burns to my hand.  

We called Frigidaire Customer Service to schedule service to address excessive exterior heat issue.  We waited 10 days for a technician and was told, "Sorry, there is nothing we can do.  This is how they are manufactured and I can't fix it."  Called Frigidaire to address and their only solution is to continue sending service men to address the issue.  I have filed claim with Risk Management as well.  

Please be aware that this particular model is extremely dangerous to have if small children are around.  Gate off the the oven if possible.  This model will burn you if you are remotely close to oven door, handles or knobs.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, indicating an injury, and the issue is inherent to the appliance's design, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire cooktop.  If the front right burner is used it will flair up to high even if on low.  If turned off when flairing up it flairs up while off. The dial has to be turned on and off several times to stop it from being on when turned off.  This was noted right after the warranty was up.  Frigidaire stated there was nothing to be done on their end.  I have since learned there is a recall on other models for the same thing.  Mine is Model FEC30S6ABF.  Serial  NF70111971.  This was purchased in 11/2007.  Please consider this in the recall.  It is a huge safety issue and has almost caused fires in our house, has caused severely charred cookware and burnt food.  This has been happening since 2008.
justification: The cooktop's malfunction has caused charred cookware and burnt food, indicating an incident but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The carafe has a plastic handle attached to it.  There is a metal band around the entire bottom of the carafe, which connects to the plastic handle.   However, there is a little plastic hook at the top of the handle, which could break and allow the top of the carafe to spill  hot coffee on the holder.

During one instance, some of the coffee spilled out of the carafe, while the consumer was holding it.  Fortunately, there was no injury to the consumer, but he believes that this presents a substantial hazard.

The consumer has been extremely cautious when using the coffee maker and he plans to return it.
justification: The incident involved a spill of hot coffee but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the consumer's report of a substantial hazard and their cautious behavior.

incident_description:
I have a GE oven model#JBP72K0K1CC that was purchased new with my condo @10 years ago which I have used infrequently over the years. On Sunday, October 16, 2016 I baked a frozen pizza @ 325 degrees for about 25-30 minutes in my oven then I turned the oven off leaving the remaining pieces in the oven & left the room & a short while later I heard a loud popping sound & when I went back into the kitchen & opened up oven door the inside glass had exploded covering the interior of the oven & falling into the broiler draw & dropping all over the floor. Upon searching the internet to get information about the instances of this happening which seems to not be all that uncommon I tried to find out if there was a recall or any warning from General Electric with regards to exploding oven doors which there seems to me to be no such thing on General Electric's part & honestly since I live alone in a retirement community & rarely use use my oven at all this has come as a great shock & as there are many elderly in my condo community who have the same oven & I'm concerned about the danger this defect potentially will pose with the other @ 200 residents. After contacting General Electric the only option that they offer  is to buy a replacement door @ $67.75 then charges for service to make the trip to repair it is an another $99.95 & there is an additional charge for labor which they couldn't quote since it would depend upon however long it will take to repair so without the labor charges it already totals @ $167.70. It seems to me this is excessive considering that the glass exploded for no apparent reason especially in light of the fact I rarely if ever use my oven, and frankly I could've been injured badly if the oven had been on or opened it while it was exploding. I'm hoping that by filing this report I might be able to get some guidance on how to proceed with this matter & how to alert my neighbors of this serious danger this presents to them as well. 
Thanks for your kind consideration & I look forward to hearing from you soon!
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven glass, which could have caused injury if the oven was in use or being opened at the time, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I have a Kitchenaid KUDS30IXWH dishwasher that was purchased in February of 2012. Recently, I heard a noise from inside the washer, followed by smoke. I called for service, and the service tech confirmed it was a fire in the control board. They wish to repair the unit instead of replace, but i am very concerned with this as we still do not know what actually caused the issue.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a fire in the control board, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Rack inside Kenmore Elite Electric Range model 790 fell down causing hot liquid to spill.
justification: The incident involved a rack falling and spilling hot liquid, which could cause injury but none was reported.

incident_description: We purchased a Frigidaire oven Model Number FFEF3013LBH Serial Number VF53412766 on 8/11/2015 from Menards in Mankato, MN.  Shortly before the one year warranty was about to expire, I was taking a hot item out of the oven when the entire oven door fell apart.  The handle and top vent on the door fell off and each of the 2 panes of glass went in separate directions.  I burned my arm in the incident.  I contacted Frigidaire and they sent out a repair person.  The repair person informed me that ordering new parts to repair the oven would be "a waste of my time".  He bent the thin metal framework that held the glass back into shape and taped the glass back into that framework.  He then pieced the oven door back together and screwed it back together using its original parts.  I advised him that we have a small child in the house and that this is a major safety risk.  I specifically requested a new oven, refund, or a viable solution that would not put our family at risk.  He advised me that there was nothing he could do and left. This was days before the warranty was set to expire, and was clearly a measure to avoid addressing the issue until after the warranty did expire. Since that point in time, the oven door has once again fallen apart during use, this time burning my husband's arm.  We now have an oven that we are unable to use and aren't sure what to do with as it will be an imminent danger to anyone who uses it.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to both the user and her husband, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The oven door has repeatedly failed, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:

I certainly hope that any of their other customers that purchased these glasses do not get sick or worse. I still have the glasses if anyone wants to see them.

incident_description: Pyrex needs to go back to its roots using the borosilicate glass instead of the cheap chinese [REDACTED]  soda lime glass. My baby girl could have been seriously injured last night as I had a brand new 13X9 Pyrex dish explode. She was within seconds of having hot grease and glass blown all over her. Let me tell you what an ugly conversation this would be for someone at your legal department had this happened. I thank God she had just stepped away from the stove. And yes it was Pyrex because I have the matching dish that I am going to trash in my cupboard. I will never again purchase this crap. I guess it will take someone becoming seriously hurt before this company takes notice. SMH
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish exploding, which could have caused serious injury but did not due to the child stepping away in time.

incident_description: I used the Pampered Chef ice cream scooper and left it in my sink,  I poured hot water in my sink and the scooper exploded.  I had severe ringing in my ear and the metal that flew out of the sink dented my refrigerator.  Upon calling the company they said it no longer is on warranty but as a curtsy we will send u a new one.  I told them that I am not looking for a replacement but bring to your attention a consumer safety issue.  I warn everyone that has it throw it away.  It is not worth your health.
justification: The incident caused severe ringing in the ear and property damage, indicating an injury and potential safety hazard.

incident_description: I purchased a Vacucraft hot beverage cup, made out of bamboo with a rubber sleeve from Bed Bath and Beyond.  However, when I put hot beverage in the cup, the outside of the cup was so hot, I could not touch it, even with the sleeve.  I believe that this cup is unsafe for safe, even as directed with hot beverages.  I visited the Vacucraft website and used their contact us form to let them know about this issue.  I received an automated reply, but never got any follow up.  I intend to return the cup to the store from which I purchased it, but I believe that this product needs to be taken off the market, it is too dangerous.
justification: The cup becomes too hot to touch, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported in this incident.

incident_description: Oven rack falls
justification: An oven rack falling is an incident but typically does not result in injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while cooking on his range the rear of the unit started to emit black smoke flames.  He was using the range for about 15 mins when the incident occurred.
