He stated that he heard an electrical noise , then an odor of burnt plastic which was followed by smoke and a shot of flames.  He immediately switched off the power to the unit from the circuit breaker.  The flames dissipated after the power was switched off.

Caller stated that he had smelled a burning odor for a few seconds, intermittently a few days before the incident when the range was placed in use.
The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.
Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury, and the caller had previously noticed warning signs, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: middle glass of oven door  randomly shattered into pieces while cooking a pie.  Oven has been in use since 3/2014.  without issues.   Inner glass not damaged and no glass entered the cooking compartment.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but no injury occurred and no glass entered the cooking compartment.

incident_description:
Hello,

Frigidaire french door refrigerator. 

The ice maker is located in the refrigerator compartment and is separated from the cool side with a foam strip. The strip allows moist aire to enter the freezing side and build up ice on the parts and pieces. This stops the fans from moving and coats the electors and wiring in ice. It causes ice to melt out of the door creating the potential for mold. When thawed the ice allows water to enter electrical portions of the appliance. 

Frigidaire as attempted a repair on this unit and failed. They replaced the last until but refuse to take this one back. 

I am concerned for my health and safety with the defective and hazardous appliance in our home.
justification: The description indicates a potential for mold and electrical hazards, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
This involves an Electrolux Home Products, Inc., over-the-range microwave oven (model number EI30BM55HSB) manufactured February 2010.

My wife was removing food from the microwave oven when the plastic vent/grill affixed directly above the microwave oven's door fell onto her arm, then onto our stove top below.  Fortunately there were no injuries.  But had this vent/grill fallen into a hot pot of water an injury may have occurred, or onto an unattended stove top a fire may have occurred.

The vent/grill, made of plastic, is attached to the microwave oven with two (2) screws and two (2) plastic tabs.  All four (4) attachment points are made of plastic and appear to have deteriorated causing all four (4) to fail.
justification: The vent/grill fell but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the deteriorated plastic attachments.

incident_description: I put a casserole into a Pyrex casserole baking dish at room temperature. I then put it into the oven at 375F. Five minutes later there was a loud bang. When I looked into the oven, I saw that the entire back corner of the casserole dish had broken off, ruining the casserole and leaving my oven full of broken glass.
justification: The incident involved property damage (broken dish and ruined casserole) but no injury or death.

incident_description: Purchased a Kenmore Refrigerator from sears 08/16/2015 and the refrigerator began to overheat and continued to run hot, until the it burned the outlet in the wall and compressor burned up. Technician came to my house to service the appliance, but after look over, alerted me that he would not repair the refrigerator that it is running hotter than it should be, and is a fire hazard.
justification: The refrigerator overheating and posing a fire hazard constitutes an incident, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I was microwaving bacon on the plate for 3 minutes. It says that it will get hot in the microwave, but it is safe to use, and I've never had an issue before. When I opened the microwave to take the plate you, it was extremely hot, so I set it back down to get a pot holder. Seconds later I heard glass shattering and a small pointed piece of the plate flew past me and landed on the kitchen floor. The plate had shattered in the microwave and I narrowly missed being hit by a small but sharp piece that was projected across the room. The plate stayed hot for so long that I had to leave one piece in the microwave when I left 30 minutes later.
justification: The plate shattered, projecting sharp pieces, but no injury occurred. Similar incidents are possible with improper microwave use.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her food processor purchased from retailer in Massachusetts as part of her wedding registry sometime around May/June 2011. 
She began using the food processor possibly in July 2011.

On December 28th, 2013 the caller had used her food processor then saw that a piece of the blade had broken off then contacted the manufacturer sent her a replacement blade.

On August 29th, 2016 she had prepared her 19 month old daughter's dessert and she didn't finish all of the contents of her bowl and when the caller's husband was cleaning up he saw a 1/4" in length and 1/8th of an inch wide piece of the blade in his daughter's bowl. One side of the piece of the blade was pointed and the other side was not.

She believes that possibly the only thing that saved her baby from injury was that she wasn't eating the dessert with a spoon she was rather sipping it with a straw.

She is reporting this as a severe safety hazard citing that her child could have swallowed a piece of the blade if she had continued eating.

There are no injuries being reported

She has not contacted the manufacturer with this most recent incident but she does plan to contact them.
justification: No injuries were reported, but a piece of the blade was found in the child's bowl, posing a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
EXPLODING PYREX!!!

okaaay, so we were eating dinner, lasagna baked in a 9 by 13 glass pan made of pyrex. We had the dish out of the oven for at least an hour and it was cool, and it just exploded into a million pieces all over the table! WHAT THE HECK!! Glass and lasagna all over...we had to throw dinner out and scrub the kitchen. We threw away the bread and butter and had to dump the drinks. The thing just exploded! I am not exaggerating. We had little glass silvers in our hands and we feel like it is in our hair. We had our glasses on so no eye injury. The thing had cooled a bit and was sitting quite peacefully on my table.  So much for the pyrex hype! It is very dangerous. A little internet research revealed this was happening to a lot of people, over the last 10 years or so. Beware! My pan was brand new.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish exploding, causing glass shards to scatter but no reported injuries, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as similar incidents have been reported over the years.

incident_description:
Mr. Coffee coffee maker BVMC-SJX36GT begins to brew immediately when delay brew is selected.
Clocks and start time selected are correct.
justification: The coffee maker brews immediately when delay brew is selected, which is an operational incident but does not cause injury.

incident_description:
We bought a Whirlpool Microwave Model Number WMC30516AW0 from HH Greg on 5.10.16.  On 8.31.16 the microwave began throwing blue sparks when turned on.  We took it back to HH Greg and the manager on duty replace the mircowave with the same model at no charge. On 10.11.16 the second microwave stopped cooking food.  I was heating a steamable bag of broccoli and after 5 1/2 minutes the bag was still icey, but when I touched the interior and exterior of the microwave in the location the first microwave was throwing blue sparks, it burnt my finger tips.  I feel confident if I were to have cooked something longer the microwave would have caught on fire.  I contacted HH Greg and they stated it is a manufactures defect and I should call Whirlpool.  I then contacted Whirlpool, explained the situation and are now waiting on a phone call within 24 to 48 hours to talk with someone about replacing the unit with a different model. There is something electronically wrong with this model.  

Incident Date:  8.31.16 and 10.11.16
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burnt fingertips) and potential for fire, indicating a significant hazard with possible recurrence.

incident_description: A glass 8x11 baking pan exploded in the oven as I was cooking a spaghetti squash.  The squash had cooked for about 20 minutes at 350 degrees when I heard the pan explode.  Both the pan and the squash were put in the oven when the oven was cool and in the process of heating up.
justification: The incident involved a glass baking pan exploding in the oven, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED], I am Brazilian and I travel to United States every year in my vacations. 
In December 2013 I went to New York to spend the Christmas with my family. I bought and Emeril's frying pan at Macy's and started to use it normally (I liked it so much that in the other years that I went to Miami and Orlando I bought two more).
In September 23rd, my 20 years old daughter was cooking with the frying pan and it exploded, making a noise so loud that looked like a gun shooting.
I was in the living room and I got so scared that I started to scream my daughter's name but she couldn't answer because she got deaf for a few seconds. My daughter got shocked and paralyzed because the noise was really loud. 
When I got in the kitchen we started to look where it came from and we realized it was from the frying pan because we found  the "screw" that holds the cable to the frying pan at the floor. Then we found out that the pressure at the "screw" made it exploded.
I don't know what to do now because the accident could have been way bigger if the "screw" had hit my daughter's eyes.
I don't have the invoice any more so I could exchange it at Macy's and at the frying pan there isn't the manufacturer's name, it only says that it is from Emeril's brand.
I am writing to warn about the danger of this product and also to ask help so I can get in touch with the manufacturer because, as I said, I have two more products like this in my house and I would like to know if is safe using them.
I look forward to contact you so you can tell me what to do.
Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a loud explosion causing temporary deafness and shock, but no physical injury was reported.

incident_description:
Approximately May 2012 this caller purchased an electric range for her son & daughter in law from retailer in Hawaii and she reports that the callers had no problems until July 2016.

Sometime within the first two weeks in July 2016 the caller's daughter in law placed food in the oven set at 350 degrees but she doesn't know for what time length.

She left the room then heard an explosion maybe 10 or 15 minutes later which prompted her to return to the room and saw that the glass of the oven door had exploded and glass was as near as the range and as far as two feet away from the range.

She is reporting this incident as a severe injury hazard especially if a child or pet had been in front of the range or to her daughter in law if she had still been standing in front of the unit.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer July 13th, 2016 and said she was given one after another with no help until she was provided with a resolution line who referred her to the repair line who offered her a repair for the glass in the oven door at her expense of $100 plus parts and labor.

She is upset about the manufacturer's lack of commitment and is asking that the repair be completed at manufacturer expense or if she has already paid for repair that manufacturer reimburse her.
justification: The incident involved an oven door explosion causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
SEARS KENMORE RANGE MODEL NUMBER 790.923.02014
This is not my model #  This # is on the tag of my oven. Sears told me that I should use 790.923.02010. I AM GETTING RUN AROUND FROM SEARS, KENMORE I AM FED UP LIKE MANY!!!!!
SEARS REP PLACED A TEMPERATURE GAGE ON THE STOVE. IT MEASURED 180 DEGREES. THE SPECS LIMIT IS 160 DEGREES. THE SELF CLEANING OVEN AT THAT POINT WAS ONLY ON 45 MINUTES AND I SHUT IT OFF ABOUT 20 MINUTES BEFORE HE CAME. TWO DAYS BEFORE I HAVE THE SELF CLEAN ON FOR TWO HOURS. MY NEW TENANTS CAME WHILE IT WAS ON DURING THE LAST 15 MINS. MY HUSBAND WAS THERE TOO. THE RANGE TOP OF THE RANGE, THE WHITE PART NEAR THE DOOR WAS EXTREMELY HOT. 
I AM CALLING CHANNEL 7 NEWS, 7 ON MY SIDE.
I called the Frigidaire as instructed and they said that their serial # starting FFGR (4 letters). That this number 790.923.02010 is not theirs.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven with excessive heat, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I was using the oven for baking. I turned the oven off when I was done. I left the kitchen. Some time later, my husband asked me if I had something in the oven because he could smell something burning. I went into the kitchen and saw that the digital clock and display screen was showing the oven was off. However, the heating element was bright orange and the oven was extremely hot. The heat could be felt to the touch on the outside of the oven and whole stovetop area. We were unable to turn the oven off. The only way it would shut off is after we unplugged it. 

This happened late in the evening. We are so thankful that we didn't go to bed before we noticed this. We have two small children.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but was caught before causing injury or fire, though the potential for harm was high given the extreme heat and presence of children.

incident_description: I had my Kenmore model 790.47782401 oven set on 350, and it had been on for about 1 hour.  I opened the door to check my meatloaf inside, I was within 1 foot of the door.  It exploded, literally, in my face and all over me!  My oven is a wall oven, so it is eye level with me, and I was literally covered in glass all over me.  There was glass all over my kitchen, dining room, and carpeted area out of dining room...literally glass blew out at a distance of 20 feet or more away!  Amazingly, I didn't get any in my eyes, I had shut them just before it all hit my face, I had it in my hair, all over my clothes, arms, etc.  Thank goodness my child wasn't in the kitchen with me as he often is!  I could have lost an eye or both eyes for that matter!!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of glass but resulted in no injuries, though the potential for severe harm was high.

incident_description: Kenmore wall oven Model 79047769405.  Glass on door completely shattered.  Was not in use and nothing touched it.  Have seen all safety precautions and did nothing to cause it.
justification: Glass shattered without use or contact, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer states that she was cleaning and noticed that the base of the coffeemaker had burn damages. The consumer indicated that she does not know when the base melted but she noticed it today, 9/7/16. 

The consumer then contacted the firm (800-726-0190) to express her safety concerns. The consumer was advised that the coffeemaker has a 3 year warranty and they could not provide any repairs since it was purchased approximately 5 years ago. The consumer indicated that the Rep. (name unknown) refused to allow the consumer to send a picture of the damages or send the coffeemaker so it could be examined by the firm. The consumer told the Rep. that the coffeemaker could have caught on fire and the Rep. advised her that there is a safety feature that would have prevented it from catching on fire.

The consumer indicated that she received the coffee maker as a gift about 5 years ago. The consumer states that she uses the coffeemaker daily. The consumer indicated that the coffeemaker cost approximately $200.
justification: The coffeemaker showed burn damages but no injury or fire occurred, and the safety feature was confirmed to prevent fire.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that she was in her living when she heard a noise coming from her kitchen. When she went to check, she noticed her microwave had started on its own. The consumer indicates that it took her approximately one minute for the unit to understand the CANCEL command as every time she pressed said button an F2 prompt would be displayed. Approximately eight hours later, the unit turned itself on again. This time it would not shut off at all when the consumer pressed the CANCEL button so she had to unplug the unit. 

The consumer states that she seldom uses her microwave, approximately once every three months, as she possesses another unit that she uses mostly.

The consumer does not know if she will have the microwave in the next thirty days since she plans on replacing it but is unsure when.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue is unlikely to recur frequently given the consumer's infrequent use and plans to replace the unit.

incident_description:
(9/1/16) The consumer's wife turned on the oven to bake at 350 degrees and approximately 15 minutes later, the consumer's wife noticed that the metal frame was extremely hot to the touch. The consumer noticed for approximately a month the oven had been overcooking food or cooking at a faster time than it usually would. The consumer then turned off the range and unplugged it. The consumer states that the control board has burn damages.

The consumer then searched online for trouble shooting and found that the problem could be the sensor probe. The consumer ordered a replacement on [REDACTED] and states that the supplier was Electrolux.

(9/7/16 approximately) The consumer installed the part and turned on the oven to see if the oven would overheat. The consumer states the range became extremely hot after a few minutes and he noticed an error code on the control panel. The consumer states that the error code was F10, which means a runaway temperature fault. The consumer searched online and found that he needed to replace the electronic control board.

The consumer ordered a replacement on www.amazon.com and states that the supplier was Electrolux.

The consumer received the part and noticed an extra part was included. The consumer states the document stated it was a "special electrical filter designed to improve the performance of the system" and the consumer believes the firm provides this additional part because they know the ranges are overheating. The consumer believes the firm should issue a recall on the ranges and inform other consumer about the potential fire hazard.

The consumer contacted the firm's warranty customer service dept. (800-944-9044) to express his safety concerns and the consumer was transferred to the Recall Department. The consumer was told that his range was not recalled and they would send his comments to a superior.
justification: The incident involved an overheating oven with potential fire hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: My GE drop in store's broiler element caught on fire and literally melted half of it melting parts of my stove, and burning my new ceramic tile. Liquid parts of the broiler element  dropped to the bottom and burned my tile. I was burned a little while trying to contain the fire. I saves parts of the broiler element melted pieces when the time dried. I'm ok but my stove is melted in several areas and threw tile in from of it is burned, and definitely not usable AT ALL, I'm so stressed I'm afraid to go to sleep in case somehow it starts again. Any consumer that has this stove is in immediate danger!
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burn) and significant property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The description suggests a likelihood of recurrence is high given the stress and fear expressed.

incident_description:
The following happens with this microwave if it is operated for more than 5-6 minutes in one cooking cycle:
1) If you happen to open the door while the oven is running, the oven will not turn off.
2) When the oven finishes its cooking cycle; when I open the door the light will not turn on.
3) If we try to start another cooking cycle, the oven will no run and it displays that the door is not closed when actually the door is closed.
I looked inside the micro and this oven has [REDACTED] limit switches used for the door and light safety switches.  I work in the Nuclear Power Field, the company I work for received a letter from [REDACTED] instructing us to stop using their limit switch in a radiation environment. I consider this a radiation environment also and a hazard to the oven operator.
I did contact Whirlpool about this issue they take my information, pass me to another office and place me on hold. That office takes my information, passes me to another office and places me on hold. This is were I end up on hold.
justification: The microwave malfunctions pose a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
GE Profile Refrigerator Model PCF23MGWA CC

A circuit breaker blew and the clothes washer and the above appliance ceased to function.  There was no evidence of additional loads on either appliance.  After resetting the circuit breaker the clothes washer functioned but the GE Profile did not.  After waiting a period the GE Profile was plugged back into the outlet whereupon it started briefly only to be followed by several popping sounds and the smell of acrid smoke.  Removing the back plates revealed a scorched cover and several charred wires and parts.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage and smoke but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: My stove cook top cracked in February, 2016 due to overheating oven.  Cook top replaced and nothing further by Sears.  October 3, 2016 while I was baking some biscuits my electric panel on my cook top started shooting out electric sparks and was on fire.  Lots of smoke, flames and sparks but thankfully we are okay and thanks to my dad installing a fire panel behind the stove my home didn't catch fire.  Stove purchased April, 2015 so no warranty.  Just paid off last month over $600 now we are faced with buying another stove.   This is a major safety issue and we don't want anyone losing their home or life due to this issue.  Neither Sears nor Kenmore are willing to do anything about it.
justification: The incident involved a stove malfunction causing sparks and fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred due to safety measures in place.

incident_description: During normal use Keurig Mini coffee pot shot out hot water and burned arm and wrist of daughter.  Second degree burns with blistering.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns with blistering, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The Emerson household microwave oven (model no MW8773SL, manufactured April 2006, S/N 60404290 GG) was plugged into an outlet, not in use, and no food/items were inside the microwave oven at the time of the incident. The microwave oven spontaneously started running. Luckily I had witnessed the microwave turn on, so I went to stop the microwave from running. The microwave did not turn off when the "STOP" or "RESET" buttons were pressed. I unplugged the microwave before further damage could result.

I placed a cup of water inside the microwave so that it had something to heat when I tested it. The microwave turned back on instantly when plugged back in, and was again unresponsive from the touchpad. Video of this test was taken.

As a result, I have safely disassembled the unit for parts, but I have kept the controls/switches.

My opinion is that either a switch or relay keeping the microwave oven off had failed, allowing the microwave to turn on independently of the control board.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was promptly unplugged, preventing injury or damage.

incident_description: Oven was in self cleaning process and approximately 2 hours into cycle (5 hr cycle) heard glass shattering while in another room. Entered the kitchen to find glass in oven door had shattered. Shards of glass found on the floor below the oven door, as well as across the kitchen floor.
justification: Glass shattered during oven self-cleaning cycle, posing a risk of injury from shards but no injury reported.

incident_description: I was cooking on my cook top and it exploded, sending glass shards everywhere.  There is a baseball sized hole in my ceiling above where the explosion occurred.  My brother was standing near and was cut by the glass.  I was standing a couple of additional feet away and have glass shards on my body and my left eye was sore after.
justification: The incident caused injuries (cuts and eye soreness) but no death, and cooktop explosions are uncommon.

incident_description: Electronic Panel on top of Dishwasher went on fire and melted
justification: The electronic panel caught fire and melted, indicating a significant incident but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This is the same knife as in Recall number: 12-163. I believe that the company may have redesigned the knife due to the previous recall and subsequently have actually made it as equally dangerous.

It is impossible to open with one hand as advertised. Once the initial resistance is overcome while opening it, it opens extremely rapidly with great force. I had one knife that I sent back to have the clip replaced and noted this issue as well. I was informed that the clip had been redesigned and that the opening mechanism had also been redesigned. I received a replacement knife and was unable to open it with one hand. While using both hands to open it, the knife opened so rapidly that it popped out of my hand and somehow lacerated my right index finger resulting in the need for two stitches. There are numerous reports of issues with this knife in the reviews on the Gerber Website. My initial review is dated 8/31/16. I have copied a link to the knife below.

http://www.gerbergear.com/Knives/Assisted/Instant_31-002184
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring stitches, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The numerous reports of similar issues suggest the occurrence likelihood is high (4).

incident_description:
The lid of the pressure cooker broke away from the body with a loud boom. The lid was thrown through the air and broke my light fixture in the dining area about 4 feet away and landed on the floor of the kitchen. Plastic from the cooker and the food were stuck in the ceiling and kitchen floor. The tops of my cabinets had food land on them. Things fell so fast and hard it ripped up pieces of the flooring. 

Because the lid broke my glass fixture, glass chards rained down into the floors and cabinet top.
Luckily my 7 year old was in the family room, and I was in the office so no one was harmed.
justification: The pressure cooker lid caused significant property damage but no injuries, as no one was in the immediate area.

incident_description:
The consumer's wife was cooking, using the rear right burner for approximately 30 minutes when she noticed that the rear left burner turned on unexpectedly without being switched on. The consumer indicated that the rear left burner has not been working for a few months. The rear left burner fails to shut off.

The consumer indicated that the mother board was replaced sometime in 2014 because the elements were not turning on and he contacted Sears for a repair.

The consumer states that the range was already in the home when he moved in sometime in 2010.

The consumer has noticed that the right front burner is heating to different temperatures

The consumer plans to contact the firm.

The consumer has reviewed recall # 09-333 and is aware that her model is not included in the recall. However, the consumer believes her model should be added to the recall because her range is experiencing the same hazard.
justification: The burner turned on unexpectedly, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
we have a two year old electric oven with smooth cooktop that was turned on and then caught fire. the fire was extinguished with a fire extinguisher but cook have gotten out of control. 
the oven was a Kenmore-model 79094193310, serial no- vf41761228
justification: The oven caught fire but was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the coffeemaker while it had completed brewing the coffee, spontaneously came back on and started emitting smoke from the bottom of the unit.  They had unplug the unit to prevent a fire hazard.

Caller stated that she read several reviews online about the product and feels that the company should recall this dangerous product.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.
justification: The coffeemaker emitted smoke but was unplugged before any injury or fire occurred, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Dear [REDACTED],

September 23, 2016

I am writing this letter to inform you about the potential danger of one of your products. The item in
question is The Pure Intentions Stainless Steel 2 Qt. Saucepan with Glass lid.

On Saturday, September 17, 2016 my mother was cooking some peas in the saucepan, when we
heard a loud noise, which sounded like a gun shot. I was sitting in the kitchen when it happened. My
mother and I took the saucepan off of the burner and looked it over in an effort to determine what
happened. Everything looked fine and now the noise was a "mystery".

On Sunday, September 18, 2016 my mother was eating some of the peas she had cooked in the
saucepan the day before and found a small round metal object in the peas. We then began
speculating what the object was and where it came from. We then thought about the saucepan that
she cooked the peas in and the "mystery" was solved. The object came from inside of the
saucepan. It was one of the two attachments that holds the handle on.

My mother has cooked peas and other items in this saucepan many times before and everything
was fine. We were very fortunate that the glass lid didn't break and that my mother wasn't standing
over it, if it had. Second, the object could have been hidden under the peas and she could have
swallowed it and that could have caused some major health issues. I'm so glad my mother was
watching what she was eating and saw it before it ended up in her mouth.

Needless to say, we have discontinued use of this saucepan. At this point I'm not sure of the date
the saucepan was purchased, however I do know it was purchased since we have been living in
[REDACTED]. We have been in [REDACTED].  almost three years. I'm also pretty certain we purchased it
from Macys. I'm in the process of finding the receipt, but wanted to let you know about this
immediately.

For your reference, I have attached pictures of the saucepan, the object and where it came from.
Also, for your information this object is similar if not identical to the metal disc on the "[REDACTED]" that was recalled by the Consumer Product Safety Commission on
December 29, 2015.

[REDACTED], Thank you for your attention to this matter and if you have any questions or require
additional information I can be reached on [REDACTED] or the address noted above. I look forward
to hearing from you soon.
justification: The incident involved a detached metal object in food, but no injury occurred as the object was noticed before ingestion.

incident_description: My Oster table top microwave came on by itself while I was not at home. My set my security alarm system off and I was only 15 minutes away. So when I got home the microwave was still running and it was very hot inside and the outside off it to. Even the cord to it was hot. After I cut it off it started to make a humming noise so I unplugged it. If I hadn't got home when I did this home would have been up in smoke. Will never buy this Oster product again.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and overheated, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Maytag Dish Washer Model MDB7130AWW  S/N 27948984ZW purchased 02/10/2002 caught on fire 10/02/2016.  Fire was in the door - wiring harness and control board consumed as well as the front plastic on the door. Damage to cabinet top above the dishwasher.  Heavy black smoke was generated from this fire. All warranty registration was filled out at time of purchase, if a recall was issued, no recall was ever received.  Owner was home at time of fire and was able to put it out, house would have burned if owner would have been away. Appliance was being operated by the home owner.
justification: The incident involved a fire with significant damage but no reported injuries, and the owner was able to extinguish it.

incident_description: I put a piece a tortilla in a 4 slice toaster oven and within seconds it bursted into flames, and did not go out.The flames extended outside the oven door and  I unplugged the unit from the wall and extinguished the fire with a fire extinguisher. The oven is totaled and has to be replaced.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions (tortilla in toaster oven).

incident_description:
08/26/2016 - The consumer indicates that the refrigerator was not cooling. He placed a thermometer inside the refrigerator and it eventually read 74 degrees Fahrenheit. The consumer then noticed that the light cover was melted. The consumer removed the light from the refrigerator.

09/01/2016 - The consumer contacted the retailer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to informed him that his unit was not included in a recall so there was no assistance they could provide.

The consumer plans on keeping the light and the refrigerator for the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The refrigerator malfunctioned (melted light cover, not cooling), but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(09/01/2016) The consumer stated that she turned the oven on to heat at 350 degrees. She went downstairs to put in laundry. She smelled gas though out the house. She went over near the stove and opened the oven door. She could hear a clicking sound. The oven was still cold but she could smell the gas. The consumer turned the stove off immediately. 

The consumer did not call the fire department or gas company.

The consumer stated that this is not the first time that the incident happened.

The consumer stated that a new igniter was installed the first week that she got the product.
Also, the self-cleaning mode of the oven never worked.

The consumer will contact the firm.
justification: Gas leak incident with no injury, but it has happened before and poses a significant risk.

incident_description: LFC25760ST French Door refrigerator the interior light stays on and does not turn off. This has caused food to spoil, the light cover to melt, and blackening of the area around the lights. The bulbs were so hot that oven mitts needed to be used to remove them. Research on the internet shows that this is an ongoing issue with LG's French Door models. I called LG to find out what part needs to be replaced and they would not tell me and instead wanted to send an LG technician over, at my expense. With the blackening of the top of the refrigerator, it is a matter of time until a house burns down.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator light causing food spoilage, melting, and potential fire hazard, indicating a significant safety risk.

incident_description:
I was preparing to bake a pizza so set the large oven to heat at 400 degrees by pushing the oven button and turning the dial to 400 degrees.  About 5 minutes into the preheat, I heard a very loud banging noise.  I turned to see that there were bright sparks flashing inside.  Then, a foul odor came from the oven.  I immediately ran to turn off the oven.  After doing so, sparks and banging continued for another 2 seconds.  The interior of the oven is covered in a white ash and is still emitting a bad odor.  

If i wasn't near by it could have caused a fire in the home.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a foul odor from the oven, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Our client was cooking when her pressure cooker exploded. She was covered in steaming hot water and suffered gruesome burns over her arms, stomach and breasts.
justification: The client suffered gruesome burns over multiple body parts, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
Three years ago I purchased three sets of Corelle dinnerware.  I have used Corelle in the past and have had no problems.  About five weeks ago, I heard a crash in the cabinet where the dinner plates were kept.  One of the plates had broken into numerous sharp shards.  I assumed that it was a flaw in that one plate and that I had stacked them so it broke.  I took a picture because it was so strange.

About three weeks ago, we had set the table for dinner.  Fortunately no one was at the table yet.  One of the dinner plates exploded into sharp shards that shot several inches.  I believe three others of our family members were in the room and saw it happen.  We cleaned up tiny, sharp shards of Corelle on the table, the floor and the tablecloth.

I contacted Corelle and informed them about the issue, but their response was that my plates were purchased three years ago and all they could do was replace them with plain white.  That is not what I wanted.  I want them to recall the plates or be required to have a warning that they can spontaneously explode.  When I looked on the internet, other people have had the same problem, some people were injured..
justification: The incident involved plates breaking into sharp shards, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was using the Norpro Jelly Strainer Stand to strain my grapes because I was canning grape jelly. I tried several bowls to set it on (it has 3 long metal legs that fit over the edge of the bowl) before finding one that seemed like the strainer was steady on. The box says the product can be used with different size bowls because the legs bend. I used a bowl similar to the one in the picture. As I was carefully ladling the boiling hot grape pulp in to the strainer, it slipped/tipped over onto my arm.  I had to hold still, while the grapes were burning my arm,  until my husband could grab it so that more of the boiling grapes didn't pour down the front of me. I received 1st, 2nd and  3rd degree burns. I purchased this at my local Wilco Farm Store. Afterwards I looked up the reviews on [REDACTED] and saw that the wobbly legs are an ongoing problem. I contacted Norpro and they claim that this was the first time they had ever heard of a problem with this product.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st, 2nd, and 3rd degree burns, indicating a significant injury. Reviews suggest the wobbly legs are a recurring issue, making the occurrence likely.

incident_description: This is a side by side refrigerator. The self defrosting coil failed to shut down and and managed to burn holes through both sides of the freezer compartment. Smoke permeated the kitchen area.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burn holes and smoke) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: On multiple recent occasions I've utilized my Tassimo Coffee Brewer and coffee has been spewed out onto myself and/or the kitchen counter. The last incident my young child was almost burned by the hot coffee.
justification: Hot coffee spewing poses a burn risk, and the child was almost burned, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
GE Profile dishwasher burned up and is destroyed. The dishwasher was empty and not in use. It had not been used since that morning. 
In the early evening I smelled something like electrical burning in the kitchen but did not locate where the smell was coming from. A couple of hours later my husband noticed the smell and discovered that our granite countertop above the dishwasher was too hot to touch. 
The dishwasher was not turned on, there were no dishes inside it, no water inside it, yet it was too hot to touch. The electrical panel on the dishwasher read 93 minutes and was not counting down. The start/reset button on the panel would not work, nor would any other touch button on the panel. We went outside to the electrical circuit panel and turned the power to the dishwasher off. After switching it back on, the reset button worked, the dishwasher sounded like it was attempting to drain (there was no water in it) and then it shut off.
We brought a fan into the room to help cool the dishwasher and countertop off.
The next day I opened the dishwasher to discover that the entire bottom rack had melted, the blade in the bottom of the tub that moves the water around had also melted. The dishwasher is completely ruined.
justification: The dishwasher was destroyed due to an electrical malfunction, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: The coil on my frigidaire dishwasher that is under 4 years old came dislodged from the metal clamps that are supposed to keep it in place.  It was resting on the plastic bottom of the dishwasher.  It burned marks into the bottom of the dishwasher causing holes that melted clear to the underside of the dishwasher making holes where the water poured out.  It essentially caught on fire.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted dishwasher) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Purchased in February 2016 a Hamilton Beach percolator model #40621R/A46318VBV.  In July 2016, started to brew some coffee, the glass knob blew off breaking into pieces.  Had to pour out the coffee for fear that glass was in the coffee.  Contacted Hamilton Beach only to be told if I return the product at my expense they would examine it and then informed me if they would replace it.  Hamilton Beach sent me a UPS mailing label via email with instructions to drop and UPS store and I refused due to my health challenge.  In another email, I stated I would contact the Illinois Attorney General office and FCC for further investigation which I did.  Hamilton Beach sent another email offering to replace the same percolator or another one equal in price or lessor price because the model I had was out of stock.  So I visited the site only to discovered that this model has been out of stock for quite sometime because I had previously visited Hamilton Beach in January 2016 for the same percolator and then it was out of stock online but was available in a store and this made me think that they already knew that the model was defective and was not stocking anymore in stores.

Hamilton Beach knew the product was defective because they stated in the email please don't discard or give to any other agency for investigation.  Hamilton Beach knows that the products that are manufactured in CHINA have major defects and yet still sell them in America.  On 9/27/2016 I received the replacement but my concern since the product I selected was of lesser price and I was due monies and they have refused to do so.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction (glass knob breaking) but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the description of the product being defective and out of stock, suggesting known issues.

incident_description: I made sure the gliding rack is in correctly in cold oven cavity. I heat the oven broil hi. I broil on a half sheetpan full of chicken parts. I turn the chicken and push in the gliding rack and the hot oven seems to expand and the shelf fall off the rack with the chicken at an angle towards the front. The hot chicken juice hit my leg as well as the bottom of the oven.  I replaced the gliding pan with one of the other 2 regular shelves the oven came with and does the same thing. Seems like when oven is hot the cavity walls expand and do not hold the pans in place. I am an Executive Chef for a living and this is not correct. I called Samsung. It is out of warranty and want to send an authorized samsung repair person at a cost of $160 plus to me to look at it. This has happened 3 times now when the broiler is on.
justification: Hot chicken juice hit the chef's leg, causing injury, and the issue has occurred multiple times when the broiler is on.

incident_description: Baby Brezza Formula Pro. Have been using machine for few months to make formula for my baby. Formula has been made to average of 98 degrees which is considered safe by FDA for babies to consume. On 9/18 the bottle seemed hotter than usual. Started testing with a thermometer. Machine has been malfunctioning and heating water to as high as 109 degrees in the water tank. Heated water and formula after mixing out of the machine in the bottle still had temperatures of over 100. Contacted company to resolve issue with no success. They state this is normal. I don't see how over heated water is normal and safe for babies to consume.
justification: The machine malfunctioned by overheating water, posing a potential risk to the baby, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
GE Profile PT970sr3ss 

Came home and microwave was running by itself. Had to open the door to get it to stop. The keypad works but will not stop the microwave.

Lots of complaints about this issue and GE says it is not on a recall. 

This product is unsafe and I feel GE should repair it since this is a fire and safety hazard. 

This unit was manufactured April 2013
justification: The microwave running by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Aroma Professional Digital Glass Electric Tea Kettle, Model AWC-155DI.  Lid assembly is made from cheap plastic parts that fall apart after a few weeks of regular use.  The lid falls when pouring off causing boiling water and/or steam to rush out. I have sustained minor steam burns but feel the potential is there for more serious injuries.
justification: The user sustained minor steam burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue occurs regularly with use, making it likely (4) to happen again.

incident_description:
(08/31/2016) The consumer stated that she smelled something burning in the dishwasher. The next morning when she went to use it, the unit did not work. The consumer's husband took the door cover off and saw that there was black on the control panel. He opened the control panel and saw burnt components on part of the panel.

(09/01/2016) The consumer contacted the firm to advised them of the issue . A service person will be dispatched on 9/13.

Update:  Repair man came on 8/13.  Ordered 3 parts new harness wires, control panel, and control board.  Repair company called later in the day on 8/13 and is unable to get harness wires.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with burnt components, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG Oven Range in June-2012.  I've used the self-cleaning function once before.  On 09/25/2016, I turned on the self-cleaning on our LG LDE3015ST Oven Range.  After under an hour (of the four-hour process), we heard a very loud bang from the oven.  In hearing this, we pulled the plug and waited for the oven to cool down.  Once it cooled down, we realized that inner glass of the oven door had completely shattered.  This glass goes between the oven glass and the door (which also has glass). We were home during the process so that we were able to unplug the power before it continued for another 3 hours at extremely high temperatures.  Because this was the middle glass, there was no way that the glass experienced damage type of previous damage as a result of direct contact from us.  No one was hurt in the incident.  I contacted LG through email letting them know what happened with the model/year/serial number and asking for replacement of the faulty glass.  I received the following: 
{In response to your concern, I regret to inform you that we can only provide you the list of our authorized service center in your area so you can have the unit repaired since the unit is no longer under warranty. You may also try to contact our Out of Warranty Repair Service so you can get other service options...}.  After doing some research, it appears that there have been other incidences like mine during the self-cleaning process.  I would highly recommend NOT using the self-cleaning process or always making sure someone is home to turn off the power if you decide to use it.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang and shattered oven glass during the self-cleaning process, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
The icemaker in our Electrolux French door Counter depth refrigerator with ice/water in door dispensed the thermosensor as well as some styrofoam into a glass of ice.  
When I removed the ice container and was trying to see the problem, the exposed wires from the icemaker came in contact with my hand and shocked me.  Shortly after that the entire unit lost power.  
I was shocked by the incident but did not go immediately to the doctor.  I was thankful that I was here and none of my children were electrocuted or hurt by the defective appliance.
I contacted Electrolux immediately but was simply told the unit was out of warranty and they tried to sell me an extended warranty.  They did not inquire about my shock or the unit or express any concern.
I read about some similar problems with a previous electrolux icemaker but was informed there was nothing wrong with mine and it was not under recall.  Since I was shocked by the exposed wires, I disagree vehemently.
I spoke with the consumer department at electrolux again today and again was told the unit was not under warranty and they would be happy to sell me an extended warranty.
justification: The incident resulted in an electric shock, which qualifies as an injury, but no medical attention was sought.

incident_description:
For the report of a hazardous incident and safety concern 
submitted to the CPSC by [REDACTED], September 6, 2016.

*Please describe the hazard incident or safety concerns

I purchased a Calphalon "small slotted turner" on May 20, 2016 and used it for the first time on May 26 to prepare a fried egg on a non-stick pan. The egg stuck to the pan and it took a few attempts to unstick and flip it over. Upon tasting the egg, I immediately felt a burning sensation on my tongue, and disposed of the egg. On inspection, the turner had melted at the leading edge, the coating had split, and the edges were ragged.

In addition to the burning sensation, my tongue became extremely discolored and coated.
Since the symptoms did not disappear, I consulted an otolaryngologist (ENT) on 6/2/16 as well as my dentist. Results of lab tests indicated a yeast infection. Treatment began
6/7/16 and continued for three weeks. Although the yeast infection was resolved, I continued to have tongue discoloration and to experience burning, tingling, bitter taste and dryness in the mouth. Subsequent visits to ENT specialists in June and July (6/20 and
7118) yielded no specific diagnosis of, or cure for, these symptoms, but only the hope that neuropathic symptoms (damage to tongue nerve endings) would subside. I did not touch coffee, orange juice, carbonated beverages or beer, wine, or spicy foods during this entire period to avoid irritation to the tongue. About 8/26/16, three months after the incident, I began gradually to resume drinking weak coffee, eat mildly spicy food, etc. This has mostly worked out, but as of this date, 9/6116, I still experience some symptoms but in a milder form than before.

Although this spatula came in packaging that stated it was made of "heat-safe silicone," it turns out this is false. The company itself told me, through the insurance agent assigned to deal with my case, that the spatula was made of Nylon N200GL. They asked me to send the spatula to them so that they could test it for defects. Instead I sent it to an independent testing company whose report summary was "The black spatula body was composed of a nylon resin, in contrast to the 'heat-safe silicone' indicated on the packaging. The grey insert in the spatula handle was composed of PDMS (silicone)." In other words, the intention was to deceive customers into thinking the entire spatula was made of silicone when only the decorative insert on the handle was made of silicone.

This misrepresentation is significant. The danger of nylon utensils (and the relative safety of silicone materials) has been a source of concern to various organizations. One article
"The Dangers of Nylon Kitchen Utensils" [REDACTED] points out that melting is not the only problem. Utensils contain hidden dangers if they melt. "Diaminodiphenylmethane, also known as DDM or methylenedianiline, is a chemical sometimes used as an epoxy hardener. Traces of this chemical are used in some nylon kitchen utensils, particularly black nylon kitchen utensils." And further, "A certain form of DDM is listed as carcinogenic by the CDC." This particular article references studies from the CDC on the chemical DDM. Under the Center for Disease Control's
Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR} many articles are listed.
This is a succinct one: http://www.atsdr.cdc.g,ov/toxfagsffF.asp?id=lOOO&tid=210. A more complete report is: http://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/PHS/PHS.asp?id==999&tid=21 0. And also http://www.atsdr .cdc.govff oxProfilesffP .asp?id= 1 001 &tid=21 0

My concern goes beyond the pain that I have suffered from the injury and the anxiety I have about its future consequences. In submitting this complaint, I hope that others will be spared such an experience and that the company will desist from using these materials and lying about them.

(The above contains no personally identifiable information and may be included in the
Public Data Base)
justification: The incident caused injury (burning sensation, tongue discoloration, and a yeast infection) but no death, and similar incidents are unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: The door panel and control panel get red hot, so much so that the technician did not even want to touch it.  We also tried to cook an egg on the control panel, as you would a hot sidewalk, and indeed it fried.  I have a video and pictures (which I was not able to upload to this site, though I would if someone from CPSC contacted me).  This Kitchen Aid oven (KSGG700ESS) is a safety hazard for anyone having children or others as the exterior becomes so hot, it is untouchable.
justification: The oven's exterior becomes extremely hot, posing a burn risk, especially to children, though no injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
Collapse of upper dishwasher rack

Kenmore Elite UltraClean Dishwasher model 665.1276
Purchased new from Sears 12/03/2013

There are two light-gray plastic rollers on each side of the dark-gray upper rack. The upper rack rides in tracks mounted to the dishwasher side.  The rollers are secured to the rack by two plastic roller-retention stabs at each roller. Each roller-retention tab is roughly 2mm square and about 10mm long (eyeball estimate) and has a protrusion to keep the roller from coming off.

As the upper rack was being slid out to remove cleaned dishes, it collapsed without warning. Inspection revealed three of the four rollers had suddenly come off the upper rack assembly due to failure of the plastic tabs that held the rollers in place.

The upper rack was not loaded with excessive dishware. We only use it for smaller items - and usually half of the objects are plastic. The roller-retention tabs failed under remarkably light loading. Pictures were taken of the damaged components and part numbers molded on the piece were noted.
justification: The incident involved the collapse of the dishwasher rack without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The failure under light loading suggests a possible design or material flaw, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: Slow cooker set to low, left house for day trip and returned three hours later.  When we returned the slow cooker was not operating, and on closer inspection the bottom of the control panel was melted.  There was evidence of smoke around the perimeter of the control panel.  When I typed in the model number to look for what size to replace the slow cooker with, I saw there was a recall already in place.
justification: The slow cooker malfunctioned, causing melting and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We were using a relatively new spatter prevention screen on our stove and it burst into flames about 12 inches high. The screen is intended for use to cover pans to prevent spatter when cooking. We were using it to cover a pan in which we were cooking steak. Our stove is gas. We were able to extinguish the flame using water at the sink. If we had not seen the fire immediately, the house could have been on fire. The device is clearly not suitable for a gas stove and may not be suitable for any stove. After the fire we could see where the screen was melted that there is a layer of fabric  between two layers of screen.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was quickly extinguished without injury, but had potential for significant harm.

incident_description:
(08/21/2016) The consumer stated that metal parts and white plastic spacers fell out of the ice bin into the ice bucket and mixed in with the ice, which is a safety hazard. 

(08/22/2016) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that his product was out of warranty. The consumer was referred to a supervisor who advised him that, out of courtesy, the part would be replaced. 

(09/06/2016) The consumer contacted the firm and spoke to a different supervisor who advised him that the part would not be replaced.
justification: Metal parts and plastic spacers fell into the ice, posing a safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: After warming something up, I went to another room and my daughter and I could smell burning. Upon returning to the kitchen I opened the door and the inside was burnt where the door and the cooking area connect. We had to unplug it so it would turn off.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and minor damage to the appliance, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: I placed an iron Dutch oven with beef stew in it onto the oven rack of my LG dual oven range (serial number is:  410MMGR0B511)  and the rack slipped off of the support on the side of the oven and fell to the bottom of the oven.  This happened when I tried each sliding rack on each support in each oven.  Although nothing bad happened, there could have been a spill of hot stew all over me.  This is a really dangerous situation.  I think that the oven racks should be a tiny bit wider so they do not fall off of the support by slipping sideways.  This is probably an engineering problem.  I have written to the company, also.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased the above referenced coffee maker in anticipation of relocating to the beach after my husband's retirement. However, we decided not to relocate until I retired last month, and therefore, kept this item in the carton to provide ease in moving. When we unpacked it last weekend, as we were moving in, we placed the pod in as directed and were surprised with a shower of water all over the counter.  Thankfully, we were not near the coffeemaker and did not get burned. We cleaned up the "explosion" and made sure that we had inserted it correctly and tried again, but the same occurred. We are certain that the pods were inserted properly since we have one of these at our office and it works in the same fashion and has never given this problem.  We would, therefore, like to return this for a credit or for an exchange of a similar coffeemaker, perhaps a [REDACTED], without the pod, since this seems to be the culprit.  We could then continue to enjoy our favorite Gevalia coffees since they, too, are available [REDACTED].

We talked with another couple in our new neighborhood and were advised that they, too, had a similar problem with their Tassimo T20 and were able to return it to the store where they purchased it and were allowed to exchange this for one with k-cups in lieu of the pod. We shall await your direction. We still have all the packaging and complimentary colored inserts unopened in packages, which would be returned along with the coffeemaker.  We you please issue a return authorization and if you would be so kind, provide a return label for this item.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing a water spill, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
My GE 36" Built-in Gas Cooktop produced an explosion and a 6" fire flame erupted from underneath a Control Knob.  Model No. JGP970BEKIBB.  Serial No. GH717664Q.  Purchased April 2, 2005.

This safety Hazard in the Cooktop appears to be caused by a  possible design flaw that can cause an electrical arc between the wiring and gas supply tube creating this fire hazard.
When this explosion/fire happened the circuit breaker tripped at the basement electrical panel.

If there was any item near this explosion/flame a major fire could have developed and possibly burning my house down.

My wife was cooking on the range yesterday and turned off the RF burner and was walking away when the explosion happened.  The flame came from the RR control knob and the burner which was just turned off was the RF burner.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and fire from a gas cooktop, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Frigidaire Cooktop Model FEC30S6ABF. The right front burner will not shut off at times.  The temperature is inconsistent.  For example the burner knob can be on 2 and all of a sudden will heat up to high and will not cut off even when the knob is turned to off.
justification: The cooktop burner malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his electric range that he purchased from a retailer in Minnesota on July 4th, 2016 with delivery July 8th, 2016.
The caller noticed immediately that the top portion of the range becomes what he describes as unrealistically hot.  He said that it even hurt his hand to touch it.
He is reporting this incident as a burn and potential fire hazard.
There are no injuries being reported.
He contacted the manufacturer the third week of August 2016 but was simply read a notice that the rang top and casing could become extremely hot.
The caller states that nothing on his range alerted him to this occurrence.
justification: The incident involves a burn hazard and potential fire risk, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the unit sparks and the four metal prongs that hold the shelf spark as well when in use.

The consumer states that a contractor inspected her microwave and said everything was plugged in correctly however when he used the unit he noticed the issue as well and advised the consumer to contact the retailer. The consumer contacted the retailer immediately however they said they could not assist her.

The consumer indicates that she ceased use of the unit after a few days of if being installed.

The consumer plans on keeping the unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The unit sparks when in use, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The outer glass blew out on our Kenmore Electric Range, model 790  9270  9280  9290 last night.  Never having heard of this before, i did an internet search and have learned that despite over 350 similar Kenmore outer glass explosions, Sears says it is likely customer fault for mistreating oven door.    Reports also say all You folks do is collect statistics.

Really?  i am a retiree, 65 years of age.  Have cooked nearly all my life and have owned and operated well over a dozen different ovens over the years.  Never had a problem with oven glass before.  For Sears to suggest this happened because owners cause this to happen is ludicrous.

It has to be a flaw in the glass making process.  It is the outer glass that shattered.  Outer glass does not touch the oven racks.  

You folks need to check into date these glass pieces were made.  i have a feeling something went wrong with the process on a day/week that caused the flaws, and despite tens of thousands of other units not having this problem, many do have this flaw.  i predict many other consumers will be contacting You in the coming years, reporting the same issue.  

How many people have to have this happen before You decide this is an issue and Sears should be held accountable?   Probably won't help me, as i intend to junk our exploded range and purchase a different brand.
justification: The incident describes the outer glass shattering without injury, and similar incidents are reported to be common (over 350 cases).

incident_description: I have a DCS electric wall oven model WOSU30 which is 2 1/2 years old. When not in use the oven is always in the off position (for "type of cooking" and "temperature) and locked. Every time we have a power surge and the power comes back on, the oven goes into the "On" position and sometimes it is on warm, broil, or 350 degrees. This has happened quite often, and at first we thought that we didn't put the oven in the "lock" position and touched a knob by accident, but this was not the case. DCS indicated that I would have to have a private service company come out and evaluate if it is a manufacturer's defect or not. We have a concern that for an oven to go on by itself because of a power outage will create a fire hazard if this occurs when no one is home.We have now turned off the circuit breaker for the wall oven so that it doesn't turn on when we are not home.
justification: The oven turning on after a power surge poses a fire hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: I have a Keurig 2.0, at the completion of the brewing cycle, the unit is supposed to purge the remainder of hot liquid with a purge of air. Mine has stopped working in this way, and as a result, the pod is left full of 195 degree water, creating a potential burn hazard. This occurs when removing the pod, hot  (195*) water pours out.
justification: The incident describes a potential burn hazard due to hot water spillage, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I was making a cup of coffee in my Kuerig machine and it all the sudden started smoking. The smell was terrible, smelled like plastic burning. I unplugged the machine quickly and it continued smoking and was clearly on fire inside the machine. We took it outside to the driveway where it continued to burn. It was some sort of electrical short but it was scary how quickly the machine started to burn. I'm glad I was home and watching the machine while this happened.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the coffee machine but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. Electrical shorts in appliances are possible but not extremely common, hence likelihood 3.

incident_description: Our Farberware slow cooker caught fire on the kitchen counter top.  The power cord has a 90* clamp that causes the power cord to bend 180* in the wrong direction.   As a result of bending back and forth in use the wire opened and exposed the hot wire.  The fire burned a small mark on the counter top.  If we had not been in the kitchen I believe the fire would have grown.    I have pictures of the appliance, the wire and damage to the counter top.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no injury, and the likelihood is high due to the faulty design of the power cord.

incident_description: On September 17, 2016, I was baking a batch of cookies in my Kenmore range/induction stove/convection oven at 350 degrees Fahrenheit.  When I went to open the door to check the consistency, the oven door exploded, sending shards of glass everywhere in my kitchen/dining room. I have taken pictures of the aftermath, along with replacing the range that exploded.  I have kept the Kenmore range - its serial number is VF03836034.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door causing damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Slide in Electric Range model number 790.41019801. I was baking and removed my dish from the oven. In doing so the handle disconnected on one side. My husband came in to look at it and screw it back on and the outer panel "exploded". Glass went everywhere. My dishwasher was open 5 feet away and glass was on the inside. We have no idea why this happened. I am glad my husband wears glasses or he may no longer have sight. Glass flew all over.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven panel causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This unit is a safety hazard!

The consumer indicates that she had food in the oven that was supposed to be there for one hour. Approximately thirty minutes later the food was burnt and smoke was being emitted from the unit; there was a distinct smell of burnt wires. The consumer also noticed an F10 error code displayed on the panel. The fire alarms in her home went off. The consumer tried turning the oven range off but it would not do so; she eventually had to switch the breaker off.

The consumer has used the stovetop since then but the oven overheats and does not turn off.

The consumer states that she uses the stovetop once or twice daily while the oven is used once or twice weekly.

The consumer plans on keeping  the unit for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.

There were electrical sparks emitting from back of range!
justification: The incident involved smoke, burnt wires, and electrical sparks, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We purchased our 2nd GE Slate Over the Range microwave on 02/05/2016 to replace the defective microwave
(same manufacturer, brand, and model) we had previously had a fire hazard Incident with. We reported the 1.it
microwave to CPSC. The new microwave was installed in our kitchen on approximately 02/20/2016. By 04/20/2016 this new microwave was doing the exact same thing, it would turn on all by itself and run, but with no inside light showing it was operating and the turntable did not turn. It would only make a humming noise. We stopped using the microwave and completely unplugged it by 04/30/2016 because it did this multiple times and without any clear pattern or reason. It was extremely unsafe to even leave it plugged in. It could and did turn on at all hours of the day or night. We did have a GE authorized repairman look at the unit. He deemed it was unrepairable, and he showed us that the microwave had burn marks that indicated some type of sparking or arcing had taken place. We have not decided IF we will accept the same model or a different model from this manufacturer. When asked, they denied knowing of any other problems.
justification: The microwave exhibited unsafe behavior, including turning on by itself and showing signs of sparking or arcing, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The GE Slate over-the-stove microwave was installed in April 2014. By the end of Oct. 2015, it was turning on and
running for hours without any person turning it on. Consequently, the unit ran several times and we weren't aware
of it because the Inside light did not come on and the turn table didn't go around. It barely made any noise ÃÂ· just a
hum- when it would start by Itself. In fact, the last time we were able to use it the unit turned on by itself several
times that day. The last time It ran for more than an hour because we didn't know it was on. By the time we found it,
out cabinets were extremely hot to the touch. We had aGE approved service technician look at it, their
recommendation was to replace it. They said the circuit board was bad. It did have burn marks on the inside of the
microwave cabinet, just like the newer model we just bought. No one was injured. But, the unit did run without
anyone turning it on, and it could have caused our cabinets to catch fire if we had not realized the unit was running.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
While cooking at high temperature, the door to this oven flung open forcefully.  I heard a popping sound and then the door flung open.  When I went to close it, it closed momentarily and then opened again, and it was apparent that whatever mechanism the oven has to keep the door closed, was broken.  Likely that is the popping sound I heard.

Having done further research about the model, it seems like this is a common issue: the spring that holds the door closed weakens and then breaks at some point.

If that breakage happens while cooking, it's pretty dangerous.  I ended up with a minor burn on my arm, but with children or anyone who cannot move quickly, that could have been much worse.  Also, the oven is designed to operate even for hours at a time, so a fire is also a significant risk should the door open and oven continue to operate... which was the case for me.  Luckily I was there to immediately turn it off.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn (injury), and the description indicates this is a common issue with the oven model, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: I have a Hotpoint oven. Recently it started by itself. I had to unplug the oven. If I plug it in, it begins working without a stop, even if the knob is at off. The model no. is RGA724EK6WH & the seriel no. is DA107800R
justification: The oven turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
My GE microwave, model WES1450DS1BB, starts on its own with no numbers on the screen.  Opening the door stops it.  Unplugging helps, but after one time opening the door, the problem occurs again.  This has happened repeatedly today.
The only way to completely solve this is to leave the microwave unplugged.
justification: The microwave starts on its own, which is an incident but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: I was cooking chicken wings at 400 degrees. about 20 mintutes in, I heard a big bang. The interior glass inside oven exploded.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass explosion but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. Oven glass explosions are possible but not extremely common, hence likelihood 3.

incident_description:
During our home remodel a few years back we purchased all new Whirlpool appliances from our local Lowe's store. One of the appliances purchased was a gas oven/range.

One day about six months after installing the range, I accidentally bumped into one of the knobs with my leg while reaching across the cabinet next to the range to pick up a plate to take it to the dining room. After about 15 minutes, we started to smell natural gas in the dining room. I jumped up and ran into the kitchen to find one of the burner knobs on the range turned very slightly, at first glance the position of the knob didn't appear to be turned on. I leaned down and could hear gas coming out of the burner associated with the knob that was slightly turned. Normally you would think that if the knob was turned far enough for gas to be disbursed from the burner that the ignitor would have started clicking before. I turned the burner off.

After an hour or so I got to thinking about how dangerous that could have been if I'd bumped the knob when leaving the house and not even known it. We have pets in the house and other gas appliances with electronic ignitor (i.e. water heater that is in a vented closet in the kitchen and an HVAC unit in the hall leading to the kitchen. What if I had left for work and the gas had been leaking into the room for hours when the hot water heater or HVAC ignited and could have blown the house up.

I went back into the kitchen to replicate how the issue could have occurred. So I turn one of the burners slowly and sure enough, you can turn it a reasonable amount with gas being disbursed before you turn far enough for the ignitor to start clicking. And on other ranges, it seems you have to press fairly firmly in order to move the burner knob from the off position into a position for it to light. That doesn't appear to be the case with this range. It takes very little effort to turn the burner before lighting. That must have been why it lighted so easy when I lightly brushed my leg against it leaning over to pick up the plate.

I jumped online and discovered that there were pages and pages of complaints in product reviews about the same issue for this Whirlpool gas range model.

Since the initial incident, this has happened many times since we installed the range. We're all in the habit now of walking back to the kitchen a few times every time we leave to check and double check the burners to make sure someone didn't accidentally bump into one of the knobs. And when we go out of town and have visitors come in to feed our pets, before we leave, we turn the gas off to the range and pull the power plug, to prevent something from happening while we're gone.

Another concern is the ignitor on the over itself started malfunctioning. About 8 out of 10 times the oven is used, when you turn the oven on via the electronic control you hear the oven ignitor start to click over and over as the gas valve in the oven turns on. If the oven doesn't ignite after about 5 seconds, the gas valve automatically shuts off and the ignitor stops clicking.  After about a minute the cycle starts all over. Most of the time the oven does actually light right at the end of the 5 seconds of the ignitor clicking, but because the sensor that detects the oven burner on doesn't have time to heat up, it abruptly shuts down. So after this happens half a dozen times, when the oven does finally light there is so much gas built up in the oven that you hear a loud swoosh and low boom sound as the gas within the oven lights. This is also scary.

We're so scared of it that anytime we use it we have to take turns staying in the room to watch it to make sure it lights every time.  We're about ready to buy a different range that we're not scared of, but wanted to pass along our experience with this unit so hopefully something can be done before someone is severely injured or killed by one of these gas ranges.
