Whirlpool Corporation
Benton Harbor MI, 49022

Model: WFG510S0AW 0
Serial: [REDACTED]

Note: There is also a number near the "Whirlpool Corporation" name that is "W10454305A".
justification: The incident describes a gas leak scenario with potential for explosion, which could lead to death, and the issue has occurred multiple times, indicating high likelihood.

The next incident happened in December 2015 when I used the self- cleaning operation of the range and the panel was again burned and then replaced. The panel burned once again in April of this year but I did not request a service call: I instead wrote a certified letter to Sears Headquarters in Illinois and requested a response to this reoccurring problem. We were frustrated about this because, never at any time, did they look to see why the burning was happening. They just continued to replace the part. When headquarters did not respond to my letter, I followed up with an email on May 18, 2016. At the same time, I requested another service call to replace the burnt part. They replaced that part on June 10, 2016. During that visit, the technician did also replace the gasket in case that was causing the problem.

Unfortunately, due to a great deal of entertaining, we had to use the self cleaning again and again the panel burnt. On July 19, 2016, l spoke with a [REDACTED] and a [REDACTED] at headquarters to discuss this continuous problem. It was discussed at that time that maybe the panel could be replaced with a metal panel. Today, July 22, 2016, the service technician, [REDACTED], came and was told that the specs cannot be changed on the unit so the panel could not be changed to a metal or black plastic. It would have to remain white. Another part has been ordered.

I followed up with another call to headquarters and spoke with [REDACTED]. I requested another range in exchange for this one. We definitely believe there is a manufacturing defect that is causing this burn issue when the temperature gets hot. They said I would have to have 4 continuous calls for the same problem in a 12 month period; and for 2016, we only have 21!

We are looking for a replacement stove based on the fact that nothing should be burning when you operate any part of a stove. However, Sears appears to be more caught up with the number of visits per problem, rather than the safety of a unit. We do understand that there are guidelines to follow under the warranty; but we feel this problem should not be happening at all and should not be treated as a warranty problem. It is a manufacturing defect.

Attached you will find receipts for the calls for this issue, the letter I wrote to headquarters and a copy of the email that was sent. We are also including a picture of the panel.

We would appreciate any help you can give in this matter. We have met a "wall".

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves repeated burning of a panel during self-cleaning, causing cosmetic damage but no reported injuries, and the problem recurs frequently.

I called KitchenAid Customer Service again and they sent me a different model replacement:  model [REDACTED], serial # [REDACTED]. incident_description:
My wife and I own a Bosch Dishwasher model SHE68T55UC serial number FD941200047 which we purchased on June 27, 2015.  Two weeks ago it started working erratically and then stopped working altogether.  So my wife called Bosch customer service and made an appointment for a service call.

When the service technician arrived, she ran her checks and in the process determined that power was not getting to the machine. This particular dishwasher uses an unconventional line connection.  Instead of a 115 ac three prong plug or a UL approved standard junction box with hard-wired wire nut connectors, Bosh provides a plastic junction box with a proprietary pigtail to the dishwasher and a terminal board with screw terminals to connect the ac supply line. 

When the technician opened the junction box, it was readily apparent that the terminal board between the pigtail and the ac line had failed.  She could not immediately replace it because she did not have one in stock.  She commented that ÃÂThis junction box had been the subject of a recall by Bosch,ÃÂ and that ÃÂWe carry them on the truck because we replace a lot of them.ÃÂ  She also told us how to contact Bosch to make a claim for a replacement unit but that she wasn't sure the recall applied to our model machine.

When my wife called Bosch as instructed to by the technician, she was told that the recall did not apply to the model machine we own, that the machine is out of warranty and that the failure is due to a faulty installation not a defect in the design of the junction box.  When my wife tried to speak with a manager, the customer service representative became  very evasive and refused to provide a last name and contact information for a manager.  She was told that Bosch would contact her the following day.  Bosch has yet to respond to her request to speak to a manager.

I am both an electrical engineer and an amateur radio operator.  I have supervised electronics technicians for over 17 years.  I assure you that there was nothing wrong with the installation.  In fact the technician complimented the anonymous installer on a job well done.  I am certain that the terminals were torqued to a reasonable degree and that the wires were not loose and not likely to loosen to the point where an arc would happen.

I am writing to you to report that Bosch has NOT corrected the problem.  As you can see from the enclosed photo, this is a serious problem which could have resulted in a serious fire in our house.  It did not cause the breaker to trip but the charred insulation and terminal board was hot enough to cause a fire to ignite.  The evasiveness of the Bosch Customer Service Representative and the refusal to have management contact us implies strongly that Bosch is trying to cover up a serious product safety issue.  I make this report to disclose this dangerous design weakness in the interest of those who have bought this machine and are unaware of the potential disaster that is lurking under their kitchen counters.  I hope the information will help you take action to force Bosch to provide a recall solution that eliminates this extreme fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a faulty junction box that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high as the technician mentioned replacing many such units.

incident_description:
We purchased a Bosch dishwasher for $1,000.00 last year.  We read the reviews and it states the unit is very quiet.  This is true.  However, what we did not see were the possible health threatening issues it has:

  *  It smells any time there is even one or two dishes in the dishwasher (We even rinse them off before we put them in).  Not just a little smell, it will stink up the entire house.  After calling Bosch, they suggested using a cleaner (we did) and not leaving dirty dishes in the dishwasher (really?!) I actually spray bleach in the dishwasher between cycles (we run the dishwasher 2-3 times per week) to help with the smell, although it doesn't really help much.

  *  Our biggest health concern:  Mildew/mold grows inside.  We left town for a few days.  We we came back and opened the door, there were strings of gray mildew/mold growing from the top spinner.  There were only a couple of rinsed cups in the top rack.  This cannot be safe.  

My opinion is that because this dishwasher does not have a dry cycle, the inside is always wet and warm contributing to the smell and mildew/mold issue.  I may be wrong of course but something not right is going on.  This should not be happening.

I have contacted Bosch multiple times for assistance and they do not want to do anything to help us.  I seriously feel like this could be dangerous to our health and would love some feedback.

justification: The incident resulted in severe burns requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such mechanical failures can occur but are not frequent.

incident_description: Kitchen range glass door exploded when no one was near it.
justification: The glass door exploded, but no one was near it, so there was no injury.

incident_description: We bought a LG gas range, double door.  The glass door exploded during non use.  We contacted LG at web chat, spoke with [REDACTED] who stated that no warranty covers glass shattering.  The oven is stationary, during non use, the bottom glass door shatters.  How can we use this product when during NON USE it exploded?  What will happen when it is hot?
justification: The glass door exploded during non-use, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My wife was baking Friday 08/19/2016 when we heard a loud noise and the glass door had exploded and broke
justification: The glass door exploded but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: I just finished cooking dinner & shut the top of stove burners off - the front, left large burner continued cooking & would not turn off.  I had to turn the stove off via the fuse box.  Turned back on via fuse box & it still staying on.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, making it an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Last month I came into my kitchen to find my over-the-range
microwave self activated it's lamp and exhaust fan.  I was unable to turn off
either feature, except by opening the microwave oven door.  I pulled
the power cord, and upon repowering the microwave function normally,
except the lamp and fan are not powered by switch activation and don't 
function.  
Although I used the microwave and it seemed to function normally, I now
realize the turntable is inoperative.  I question the microwave.
My concern is the electrical issues related to this series of failures.
Fires often begin when electricity is misdirected.
I checked some internet comments regarding my problem and many
others seem to have had similar issues.
In some cases, the PCB is the failing components common connection.
Other narrative describes the damage found upon inspection of the failed PCB's,
including melted solder terminals and burned boards
justification: The incident involves electrical malfunctions in a microwave, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We own a GE side by side refrigerator.  Recently, the ice-maker's plastic auger broke, and a sharp, thin  piece came out with the ice into my wife's cup.  She makes a smoothie for breakfast every morning. The plastic is not detectable with the ice and she ground up a piece of the plastic and ingested a few pieces before she figured it out. She came to me alarmed that something was stuck in her throat.

I worked backward and found the shards of the plastic still in this ice bin.  I removed and took pictures of the broken pieces (attached).
justification: The incident resulted in ingestion of plastic shards and throat discomfort, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I had been preparing a gift for a friend and set it on my countertop, partially on the range. I had not used my range that day nor had I used it the day before so I am 100% sure non of the burners were hot. I left my apartment and came back to firetrucks outside and was informed there was a fire in my unit and that all my things were destroyed. When maintenance took me up to my apartment he assured me that I shouldn't feel bad because this has happened before in the building. He said the ranges are just far too easy to turn on and can be turned on easily without noticing. He stated that the leasing office had been touring a vacant unit and in the course of the tour the oven was turned on. They didn't tour that unit for a week and upon return discovered the oven had been on high for the entire time. All countertops and cabinets needed to be replaced. These ranges are FAR too easy to turn on. You should never be able to turn on your stove without noticing. Imagine if there were kids or animals that are able to climb on countertops?
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries or deaths, and the description indicates a recurring issue with the ranges being easily turned on.

incident_description:
Prior to the incident the microwave was used to re-heat several food dishes over a 5-8 minute period. About 10 minutes after we sat down to dinner, the following occurred:

The microwave inadvertently turned itself "ON" and began heating with the door closed. In an attempt to stop unit the "STOP" button was depressed and the door was opened. Unit continued to operate and I had to pull the AC power plug to stop unit completely. The contents in the unit included a glass carousel dish and a plastic plate cover. As a result the damage inflicted to the dish included several glass chips that had embedded themselves into the plastic cover which was badly melted from the overheating. Subsequent to this incident. we checked for product recalls and found several Kenmore microwaves manufactured through Dec. 2007 for the above failure mode. Our unit was manufactured in March 2008, and for the sake of a few months. I strongly suspect that internal components were probably identical to previously manufactured units. In a telephone discussion with Sears, they claimed no liability for this type failure because our model
was not on the recall list
There were no injuries from this incident, however I have a concern about exposure to radiation after my wife had opened the door initially to stop the unit.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned causing property damage but no injuries, and similar incidents have been reported in recalled models.

incident_description: Oven racks in my stove keep falling because the oven liner expands when the oven is on.  The sides of the oven liner expand to the point where they can no longer support the oven racks.  On several occasions, hot pans with liquid in them have fallen.  This is a serious burn hazard. The oven is Kenmore Elite model number 790.98023801
justification: Hot pans with liquid falling poses a serious burn hazard, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a 30" gas cooktop. The model is: Whirlpool  30" Gas C- Top  (WCGS51USODB)
Serial No. is (D62309778. The grates on flames are two peice. The mounting design is defective. When a heavy pot or pan is placed on it, if moved a bit, the grate slips off the mounting dimples creating a very dangerous situation. A few days after the install, my wife started complaining about this and one day, the grate slipped and burnt her arm. Luckily she pulled back real quick , but suffered a burn anyways. I later noticed that the grates just slip off with a slight pressure and are very unsteady. Called Whirlpool, the tech agreed it was not right and stated he could not do anything about. Whirlpool offered to take the cooktop back and reimburse me, but refused to pay for the re install of anything else I would buy. They treated us very rudely with no empathy. 

Regardless, this appliance is very unsafe and dangerous. A pot of boiling water can tilt and fall on anyone in the vicinity and cause major burns.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the user's arm due to the defective grate design, and the description indicates a high likelihood of recurrence with potential for more severe injuries.

incident_description: I own a GE Profile series electric 30" Slide in Range. On several occasions family members have placed items on the stovetop and very lightly brushed the front control knobs and turning on a burner in the process. I did it for the 3rd time now just yesterday. A light brush across the front facing burner control knobs will activate a burner without your knowledge.
justification: The incident involves unintended burner activation without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The repeated occurrences suggest a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: GE Microwave turned on by itself multiple times, Running for a 1 minute time period during each occurrence Showing a key pad error code.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no injury, and the keypad error suggests a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her smooth top electric range oven that she purchased  from retailer in Colorado July 23, 2010.

She reported this range to the retailer 2012 - 2013 and repairs were made via warranty replacing the entire top control panel.

She reported it to CPSC via incident report# 20151106-9C948-1529006 because the controls began readjusting the heat on the burners and a control valve. 

She is reporting this range again because July 6th, 2016 she had heated popcorn chicken at 325 degrees convection bake for 15 minutes then turned the oven off, went to another room however approximately 25 minutes later she heard a very loud sound  that did sound like glass was included.

She at first ran to the garage thinking that her husband may have fallen with something glass involved, however when she turned around she saw that all three levels of glass in her oven door had exploded sending glass pieces and slivers as near as remaining in the framing to at least five feet across the kitchen floor.

She asked her husband to come inside to help clean the kitchen up and take pictures which she will submit via email to attach to this report.

There are no injuries being reported.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Electric range model number 790.9417, manufacturer Fridgaire from Sears in October 2015. In March 2016 the glass door exploded and shattered in a million pieces. The product was still covered by warranty and they replaced the glass door. Fast forward another 5 months and the same thing happened again. The glass door shattered after the oven was used for baking. They are coming again to replace the glass door as the product is still covered by warranty but have not offered any reasonable explanation as to why this happened.
justification: The glass door shattered twice, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
I have a GE Monogram Refrigerator. The model number is Zisb480DXA and the serial number is GR031563.  This product costs many thousands of dollars new and has had a number of repair issues that I have already paid for.  I found the issue of mold when I had to pull a 700 pound refrigerator out from its enclosure in order for the GE service techs to come and fix a separate problem with the refrigerator. The fix has been completed on this separate problem but the mold is an open issue.    

Condensation from a poorly engineered water line up the back of the refrigerator has created about a 4 foot tall by 1 foot wide at the top and 2 foot wide at the bottom black mold issue on the sheetrock.  This mold extends slightly into my hard wood floor.   This in my opinion is a health issue and a search of the web finds many others with the same problem.  

There is a tech service bulletin from GE on this and the fix is to install 3 heaters on the back of the appliance to stop the condensation that causes mold.  

As of this writing I have called GE and have been unsuccessful in getting GE to pay for these parts and the labor to install them, though I am waiting on one more supervisor call back.  I feel that GE should be required to issue a recall on this problem and fix it at their cost.  

Thanks for your assistance.
justification: The incident involves mold growth due to a design flaw, posing a potential health risk but no immediate injury or death reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Electric Range (Model 790.42531311) from SEARS just two years ago, in 2014. 

Last night, I gently opened the door to check on food when - suddenly - the outer glass panel simply shattered into a thousand pieces on the floor. The shattered glass - with its tiny, sharp edges - was everywhere. Much of it still is - in nooks and crannies - around the kitchen that escaped the vacuum cleaner and broom. 

I have 2 kids, 2 dogs, and 3 cats.  So far, no one has been injured.  Thank goodness no one was peering into the glass when it shattered.  Sever injury could have occurred.  This product is defective!
justification: The glass shattered but no one was injured, though the potential for injury was high.

incident_description:
Sears - Kenmore oven/range-- free standing  - Electric
Model # 911-63278790
Serial # 7r278078Q
glass door in oven shattered 
Not at home and oven was not in use at the time
justification: The glass door shattered, but no one was present or injured, and the oven was not in use.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her Kenmore Electric Range purchased April 19th, 2016 delivered April 22nd, 2016 but not used for five weeks after delivery.

In mid May 2016 the caller read the manual with regard to 'seasoning' the oven by heating it, however there was an extremely strong odor emitting from the unit while she was trying to do this so she turned it off but she and her husband had to leave the house because the odor was so strong.
She contacted the manufacturer to complain also mid to late May 2016.

The first service technician came to her home July 14th, 2016 and he took the range apart from the top, from the back and the front and agreed that the odor was exceptionally bad.
He said he had to schedule another technician then told her they should be out to her home that same day because he had an injured hand and could not complete some tasks.
The technician was scheduled for that same day, however, the caller couldn't tolerate the odor from the range and had to leave the house so she cancelled to reschedule.

July 22nd, 2016 the second technician came to her home, checked the oven and ten minutes later he advised her that she was "smelling heat" and that he smelled nothing.

She said that between the two technicians and her without them the oven has had approximately nine hours of 'seasoning' or 'burning off' and it still has a strong odor coming from it.

She is reporting this as a strong health hazard due to the odor the range is emitting.

She said that CPSC has one report from January 2012 for the same hazard for a range.
justification: The incident describes a strong odor causing discomfort but no reported injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) based on the consumer's report and one prior CPSC case.

incident_description:
Product Name : Great Value Foam Cups
Quantity : 51
Size 8.5 FL OZ (251.4mL)
Along the side of the package is the code:  11 WD 07/20/16 08:41 AM
Along the bottom of the package is the code:  8RP5WM

On Tuesday, August 9, 2016 I used a Great Value Brand 8.5 FL OZ Styrofoam cup to pour some coffee. When I poured the coffee into the cup, it collapsed and folded inward. The inward collapse of the cup in my hand caused the coffee to rush over the side of the cup, spilling abruptly onto my left hand and over my left wrist. The amount of hot coffee which overflowed was sufficient to run down both sides of my left wrist. The injuries sustained as a result were both 1st and second degree burns, followed by an infection within a matter of two to three days. I am now under the Doctors supervision for the burn and the complications / infection. The Doctor and Nurse could plainly see how the accident happened and the doctor advised me that the product is dangerous and that it would be a good idea for me to report it to your agency to prevent others from being injured.
Now after having been injured, and looking closely at these cups, I have noticed that the strength, and even the amount of materials put into the product  is far less than that of the two brands of cups I normally purchase and use on a regular basis. The density and the quantity / the mass of material is far less than the [REDACTED] or [REDACTED] brand of the same size and type. The weight of these cups is less and the structure is much weaker than the stronger, better quality [REDACTED] brand or [REDACTED] brand cups which I am accustomed to. Not only are they a lesser quality product, they are not suitable for the advertised purpose.
1. When the weight of the coffee reached about 2/3 full,  the cup very abruptly collapsed and folded in my hand.
2. The heat of the liquid may have been a factor in the collapse since the cup is so weak that a temperature change could reduce the strength of the cup, which seemed to, by my observation, to have occurred. In other words, the heat may have played a factor in the collapse of the already inadequate materials used to produce the cup.
3. The cups are not adequate in density / thickness and can collapse while serving hot liquids.

If you will examine the Great Value 8.5 OZ cups and compare them to the other brands, and the standard they meet, it will be clear that the Great Value / Walmart brand should be removed from the shelves and the cup should be either discontinued all together, or at the very least, for the protection of the consumer, redesigned. A consumer who is used to the thick strong [REDACTED] cup, or the equally thick strong [REDACTED] cup, would likely expect the same quality from a Walmart / Great Value brand cup. Since the other two store brands would seem to have set the standard for generic / store brand quality, the consumer might be caught off guard by the very weak Great Value cup and more injuries such as mine will very likely occur over time to others who are not familiar with the flimsy, weak structure of the Great Value Cups!  I often serve hot chocolate and tea to friends and family in the [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] brand cups and I am relieved that I have learned this about the Great Value cups before injuring someone other than myself with such a not only poor quality, but dangerous and defective product. I will certainly not be using any of these in the future!

I request that these Great Value 8.5 OZ Foam cups be called to the attention of Walmart Corporation for voluntary recall. The company should redesign the cups, using better materials of greater integrity with sufficient density and strength to be used for hot liquids as advertised on the cup.

 I request that the consumer product safety commission examine the cups listed below (or at least current stock from any Walmart Store) matching the product description, for examination and recall. 
Product Name : Great Value Foam Cups
Quantity : 51
Size 8.5 FL OZ (251.4mL)
Along the side of the package is the code:  11 WD 07/20/16 08:41 AM
Along the bottom of the package is the code:  8RP5WM
justification: The incident resulted in 1st and 2nd degree burns and subsequent infection, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a bosch 30" single wall oven  - model HBL8451UC
The surface of the oven overheats with use - self-clean, bake  or broil
The glass alone can reach 158F (i measured with a surface thermometer for evidence), the control panel gets even hotter.
I believe this is a burning hazard. I have 3 children under 4 and their skin can burn at 120F.

I was told by a technician on a prior occasion that this is not a malfunction of my oven but a model problem related to the fan (to be verified), and that the company is aware.

I think this product should be recalled.

I have contacted bosch today regarding this particular issue.  I have to wait 2 weeks for a technician to verify the existence of the issue so bosch can think of ways to repair the current appliance... I don't think that is an adequate answer if the problem is known. People can get burnt.
justification: The oven's surface reaches temperatures high enough to cause burns, especially to children, indicating a clear hazard.

incident_description:
Product description: GE Microwave Oven, model number JES1142SPSS, purchased January 2014 at Lowes.

Incident summary: Turns on when unattended. No damage or injuries occurred.

Incident details: On at least three occasions, this oven has turned on by itself when unattended (family asleep or away from home) and did not shut down until unplugged. When my wife contacted the manufacturer, they seemed unconcerned but offered to send out a service representative for $179 (much more than the oven cost). We were able to get a refund from the retailer. The oven is still in our possession.
justification: The microwave turned on by itself multiple times but caused no damage or injuries, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: GE Spectra electric stove JBP80C0F2CC bake element blew up and went on fire
justification: The stove element blew up and caught fire, indicating a significant incident but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Microwave oven starts to heat up itself after closing the door. Originally it happened in March 2016 and then it stopped working. Every time, I closed the microwave door, it started to heat up. I left the door open for a day and then microwave started to work fine again. The same incident happened again in June and then microwave completely died. I called sears repair service and they decided to change the magnetron. Microwave started to work again until today. I started to smell burning plastic in my kitchen. After little investigation , I found out that the smell was coming from the microwave. Inside of microwave was really hot. If I leave the door open it stops heating up but as soon as the door is closed microwave starts to heat up. I am concerned that this microwave can cause fire if same thing happens at night when me and my family is asleep.
justification: The microwave's malfunction poses a fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury if left unattended, especially at night.

incident_description:
On Tuesday, August 9, 2016, I received an electrical shock when I turned off my Cuisinart toaster oven. The original Cuisinart TOB-40 toaster oven was purchased August 24, 2012. It had a 3 year warranty. Within the second year of use, one of the front bottom elements became warped. After the warping became severe, we contacted Cuisinart. The company sent a replacement oven in November 2014. We had to pay for shipping the original unit back to Cuisinart, $35.48. 

The front bottom heating element warped extensively on the replacement unit prior to the end of the second year of use. On August 9, 2016, when I turned off the toaster oven, I received an electrical shock. 

After this incident, I researched reviews on various sites where this toaster oven is sold and found numerous consumers reported problems with the heating elements warping. Some reported this resulted in fires and shocks.
justification: The incident resulted in an electrical shock (injury), and multiple reports indicate similar issues, making occurrence likely.

incident_description: Burner plate would not turn off even when the unit is turned off. Had to pull the plug out from the wall behind the cooking range to shut it. Range is now unusable and a major safety hazard.
justification: The burner plate not turning off is a safety hazard but no injury was reported, making it a severity level 2. The issue is likely to recur given the description.

incident_description:
(07/31/2016) The consumer stated that he was leaving for the day. He came back into the house and smelled burning plastic coming from the refrigerator. He opened the refrigerator and discovered that the interior light was on and smoking. It was also hot to the touch. The light assembly had melted. The consumer disconnected the power to refrigerator.

The consumer also stated that the problem is that the interior light does not go off when the refrigerator door is closed. 

(08/02/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. He advised them of the incident. A report was filed-#[REDACTED]. A repair visit was set up to assess the problem at no charge to the consumer.

The consumer researched the product and found out that this is common problem for this model.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and melting light assembly in a refrigerator, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred. The consumer's research indicates this is a common problem for the model.

incident_description:
When the igniter for the oven is turned on, it does not ignite.  Sometimes it takes 3 or 4 tries, before the oven comes on.  The problem started a year ago and has been consistently happening since that time.



The consumer contacted a [REACTED] technician to come out an look at the oven.  The consumer previously had a [REDACTED] range and this tech. serviced it in the past, so she felt comfortable having his look at this one.  A tech. came out in 6/2016 and said that he has seen this problem before and other technicians have mentioned it as well.  The tech. told the consumer that there is a problem with the air-flow to the igniter, which causes the delay for the igniter.  The tech. said that there is a fine piece of metal in the igniter components, which is paper thin.  They bend this metal to help with the air-flow, which is what he did for the consumer.

After the repair, there was some improvement, but the problem continued to occur.

The consumer is concerned that this could present a carbon monoxide hazard or a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven igniter with potential safety concerns, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
The microwave turns on by itself and runs continuously.  The problem has happened numerous times.  The consumer plugs the microwave into the outlet when she wants to use it and unplugs it when she is finished.

The problem started back in 2010.  However, the consumer has contacted the firm 3 times so far.  The microwave turned on, while the tech. was at her home and he relayed this information to their technical department.  The problem has been confirmed to be caused by a failure in the microwave's smart board (control system).

The smart board has been replaced twice by the mfr.  The first time she reported the problem, the mfr's technician indicated that the wiring in the microwave was wrong.  The technician ended up rewiring the microwave and replacing the smart board.  This was done back in early 2010.

2013:  The same problem started happening and a mfr's technician came out and replaced the smart board again.

2014 & 2015, The same problem started happening intermittently, but it eventually corrected itself.  The consumer notified the mfr., but since the problem stopped, it was concluded that a technician did not need to come out.

2016:  The same problem started again and the consumer contacted the mfr.  However, this time, their rep. told her that the microwave is beyond the warranty period.  The mfr. has informed the consumer that the microwave can be fixed, but she would have to pay for it to be repaired.  The consumer is not willing to cover the cost, because of the safety hazard.  The mfr. offered her $50 towards the purchase of another product, but she does not want another microwave by this mfr.

The consumer believes that this could cause a fire if she was not home when this happened.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred. The problem has been recurring intermittently since 2010, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: We put dishwasher on as we normally have done. Towards the end of the cycle we smelled smoke and noticed it was coming out of the top of the dishwasher. I originally thought maybe a plastic lid fell on the heating coils that dry the dishes. I removed all of the dishes from the dishwasher and the bottom slide out rack and found nothing. The inside of the door was very hot to the touch. I put the washer back on and intense grey/black smoke started pouring out of the top. Upon examination it was coming from an opening at the top middle of the door directly under the handle. The smell is of burning plastic/wire. I immediately unplugged the washer and will be calling GE tomorrow.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning smell from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: front left burner will not shut off.  open recall from Kenmore on known issue 09-333,  but Kenmore is refusing to repair product because the model number is not under this recall,  although the serial number is listed for repairs
justification: The burner not shutting off is a known issue but no injury or death has occurred, and the recall dispute suggests it's a recurring problem.

incident_description:
I purchased a Josephjoseph.com M-Cuisine Microwave rice and grain cooker this summer.  While cooking whole grain rice in my microwave, the unit melted down and made acrid smoke after about 10 minutes.

The instructions instruct to add 1/3 cup of rice and 150 ml of water.  We then noticed that a small additional piece of paper had been added to the box.  This paper had "Updated cooking instructions for whole grain rice only".  The updated instructions instruct using 450 ml of water for 1/3 cup of rice, a tripling of the amount of water.

I called the company to discuss with them.  I asked why the units had not been recalled; they indicated that this was considered but rejected.

I am concerned that someone will have a serious fire due to using this unit according to the included instructions.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction causing smoke but no reported injury, and the company's decision not to recall increases the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: This oven has exuded a faint smell of burning wire since purchased new from Sears in 2011. Sears sent a technician out twice who replaced a control board but the problem was still occasionally there. The oven always seemed to run hot and we would set it lower than the recipe recommended. The last time we used the oven it ran so hot the entire range became too hot to touch (of course the food burned to a crisp) even when the temp was lowered to 200 degrees. It seemed to go as hot as cleaning mode even though the temp was set to 350. There was a strong smell of burning wire but not sure if that was from a short or from the range being so hot it was cooking the wires
justification: The oven malfunctioned, causing excessive heat and a burning smell, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We have a 30" Kenmore Elite Gas Convection Self Cleaning Range Model #790-79363406.  My husband and I were not in the kitchen (thank goodness) and my husband heard a popping sound and then a sound like alot of pills or something hitting our tile floor.  We went in and the glass door had shattered in a lot of tiny pebble-like little pieces.  It was continuing to shatter as we watched it.  The oven had not been used for 3 days prior to this shattering.  The oven was not on during the shattering.
justification: The glass door shattered without any injury, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description:
(3/19/16) The consumer states that he was using the oven for about 3 hours on the bake setting and the oven was set at 450 degrees. The consumer states that the oven was turned off for a little while then the oven was turned back on and set to bake setting at 450 degrees. However, the consumer states that the oven did not heat to 450 degrees and it remained at 250 degrees. The consumer then turned off the oven and shut off the circuit breaker. The consumer pulled the range from the wall and he removed the cover panel so he could inspect the circuit breaker and the consumer noticed there was a burned wiring harness. 

The consumer states that there was a similar incident that occurred approximately 2 years ago. The consumer states that the oven was being used when suddenly flames and sparks were coming from the oven. The consumer had an extended warranty through Lowes and contacted Lowes to have the range repaired. The consumer states that the technician described the incident as a run away oven. The consumer states that the circuit board, a wiring harness and front control panel was replaced. The consumer was advised that the firm was notified regarding this incident. 

The consumer contacted Frigidaire to inform them about the incident and the consumer was advised that the range was not under warranty and the consumer would pay for any repairs. The consumer was also advised that the firm did not have record of any prior incident with the range. The consumer believes the range poses a fire hazard and should be recalled. The consumer has purchased another range because he did not feel safe repairing the range.

The consumer contacted Lowes to inform them about the incident but the consumer was advised that the extended warranty expired and they would not be able to assist the consumer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with burned wiring, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Cusinart smart stick CSB-75R blade broke twice in last 8 months of purchase. Both times while blending baby food. First time blade had a crack. Second time blade shattered in pieces. Concern is if this goes unnoticed, may cause injury.
justification: The blade broke twice without injury, but there is a concern for potential injury if unnoticed.

incident_description: Went to open pressure cooker. Turned the valve to release the pressure and it did not release. Attempted to repeat this step with no change. Went to turn the lid and open the cooker. Pressure cooker contents burst and burned me.
justification: The incident resulted in burns, indicating an injury, and the occurrence is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bosch 500 Series Gas Cooktop on Oct. 18, 2012.  It's Model Number NGM5664UC/03.  Serial Number 920900017.  The layout of the cooktop has five burners -- two on each side, and one in the middle rear.  The control panel metal plate with knbos is in the middle front of the cooktop.

I began noticing that the control panel metal plate grew very hot when the cooktop was in use.  It gets so hot that if my hand accidentally touches the plate for more than a few seconds, the skin would be burned.  I called Bosch to complain about this in March 2016.  They sent out a technician on March 29, who told me that the cooktop has a known knob/range defect of conducting heat to the control panel.  He ordered some foam to put underneath the metal cooktop frame, and returned in May to apply it.  However, the foam did nothing, so I called Bosch to complain again.

Their technician returned on May 17, wrote up a report and said nothing could be done to fix it.  After several frustrating calls to Bosch, I got no help.  So on June 2, I filed a complaint with the Los Angeles County Department of Consumer and Business Affairs.  The investigator looked into the issue, and Bosch agreed to send out a third-party vendor ([REDACTED]) for a second opinion.

The [REDACTED] technician came out July 8.  He measured the temperature of the control panel when the burner was on a medium flame at 128 degrees.  He said if I had turned the flame up to its maximum, the temperature would have gone even higher, but there was nothing he could do to fix the problem.  Bosch considered the matter closed, and offered me a little more than $500 to buy back the cooktop.  I declined their offer.

incident_description: XL44 gas Range Series # DF22199P Model # JGBP28TED2WW. incident_description:
Frigidaire Electric Stove/Oven.  While using the baking function, there was a loud POP, and then another POP and then the power went out in the entire home.  The internal house breaker did its job by popping, but after resetting it, power was still out.  I checked the main external house breaker, and it had Popped!  So, I reset it and power was restored.

Upon investigation online, I found hundreds of people that had the same problem.  The ECB board, part number 316207529 blew!  Inspecting the ECB, I found (as most other people) found black burn marks in between the two circuit boards that make up the ECB.  Not only is this dangerous whenever a electrical device causes a 240 circuit breaker to Pop, it seems that this is quite a common occurrence.

Why hasn't there been a recall for this stove/oven?  My Model number for the stove/oven is:FEFL78CBC 

Plus the replacement part is selling for between $100-$250!  With the average being toward the $175 range.  This is about 33%-50% of what a new stove/oven costs!  A complete rip off.  Its looks to me that Frigidaire is making $$$ off of selling replacements for a DEFECTIVE part that they should be responsible for.

Aloha and be well,
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I was using my Kitchenaid 36" glass cooktop with downdraft. I had two burners operating for several pans for approximately one hour (off and on as needed.). After completing my last cooking task, I turned the burners off.  Within about 30 minutes, I noticed that the indicator light was on and checked the appliance. Indeed the left front burner was hot and while I stood there it came on (burner turns reddish when heating) and then I heard a wire shorting sound (sizzling/clicking) from the area of the knob on the cooktop. I turned the knob, wondering if it was not turned to a full click but it was surely in the 'off' position. I turned it on and then off several times and the shorting sound continued in both positions and the burner remained on. 
Interestingly this is the second Kitchenaid appliance of the same type which has done this. We just replaced our other cooktop in March 2015 for the same reason. I contacted Kitchenaid about the problem with no reply. Since this cooktop is nearly 4 months out of the warranty, I'm guessing they don't care. 
My greatest concern is that this is a fire hazard. Had I not been at home when it occurred, my home may have been set ablaze by a faulty appliance.  Or worse, had my family been at home sleeping, we may have all been killed by this faulty appliance.  
It seems reasonable that one cooktop could go out in this way and it could be a fluke, however, twice with the same appliance from the same company seems like a manufacturing process problem and I feel that Kitchenaid should address that problem.
justification: The incident describes a faulty cooktop that could pose a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Purchased a Sumsung electric range model number NES8F9500SS in November of 2015, had it delivered in April of 2016, and just got it installed in June 2016 (kitchen remodel), so weÃÂve only been using it for two months.
Within a day of the installation, I walked by the range and noticed that a burner was on even though no one was cooking.  I asked my spouse if she turned it on, then pieced together that she had heated a cup of water in the over-the-range microwave/hood vent unit.  She tried opening the microwave again and found that because of her short stature, her midriff contacted the range knobs as she reached to place items in and out of the microwave, and that is what had turned on the range.
Over the next few weeks the range top was inadvertently tired on several times, twice with a dishtowel while cleaning the counter, a couple more times while operating the microwave, and another time which we couldnÃÂt decide how it turned on.
Last week we had a gathering at our home for my wifeÃÂs work team.  I had the entrees lined up in slow cookers beside the range top, and a glass serving platter with a serving spoon and stainless steel tongs sitting on the rant top.  With five minutes of inviting folks to enjoy the buffet, I had a gentle ask why the range was on.  He was right, the heating element under the serving platter was on and heating the platter.  I turned off the knob, grabbed a dish towel and removed the heated serving spoon and tongs, then the glass serving platter exploded sending shards of glass up to twenty feet in all directions.
Thankfully, no one was injured, even in the cleanup.
No one had any idea how the heating element knob got turned on, but it is no muster.  The range knobs are on the outboard of the unit and are so easily operated that there is no way that it meets the two movement safety requirement for residential stove knobs.
The knobs can be easily operated by a person brushing up against them which poses a serious fire and safety risk.  This unit should be recalled before some is injured or killed.
justification: The incident involved repeated unintended activation of the range knobs, posing a fire and safety risk, but thankfully no injuries occurred.

I opened the cabinet, and the larger of my nesting set of Pyrex bowls (Pyrex Smart Essentials with lids) had apparently exploded.  
It had been in the cabinet, along with the other bowls with it, for at least several days so this wasn't a sudden temperature change related issue.
The bowl is one of a set of four Pyrex bowls I purchased within the last year from Kohls.  They came as a boxed set with lids.  I purchased three of these sets, one for each of my sons, and one for myself. 
Had I been near it when this happened, I could have had a piece of glass explode into one of my eyes. There were bits of glass all inside the cabinet and the force of the explosion was strong enough to open my cabinet doors.
Since I was not near the cabinets, I was not immediately injured.  However, I did get several shards of glass in my fingers while trying to carefully clean up the broken glass.
These bowls are extremely dangerous and need to be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries from glass shards during cleanup, and the potential for severe injury was present.

incident_description: A Frigidaire refrigerator, less than 5 years old, has developed a short in its wiring harness that causes it to trip the Ground Fault Circuit Interruptor receptacle it is plugged into. The Frigidaire authorized repair technician says it is a short in the internal wiring harness, which is not accessible without disassembling the fridge beyond what was intended for service. He and I believe the only way for such a short to occur in a fridge that never moves is if the wiring harness was improperly installed when the refrigerator was built -- a latent manufacturing defect. But more importantly, the fact that the short is tripping the GFCI receptacle indicates that, by definition, the fridge currently has a potentially lethal ground fault. If the fridge was not connected to a GFI -- and there is no electrical code requirement that for a fridge to be GFI protected -- if someone touched the metal cabinet of the fridge while stepping in a puddle barefoot, or reaching into a sink full of water, that person WILL receive a shock, and there is a very real statistical likelihood that that person would die. I have notified Frigidaire customer service to the highest level I could as a consumer, and the appliance tech has notified Frigidaire through his channels as well. They don't seem to care. -- Model # LGHN2844MF0 -- Serial # 4A12115256 -- Purchased at Lowe's in Concord, NH on 9/4/2011. Appliance Repair Company is North Country Appliance Service (603) 787-6677. (the owner) was the technician on the job.
justification: The refrigerator has a potentially lethal ground fault, posing a risk of death if someone touches it under specific conditions, though no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
This is regarding a Kitchenaid Range KFGG500ESS five burner gas range that was bought from www.homedepot.com on July 7th 2016. After the oven was turned on for thirty minutes or so, I have noticed the front stainless steel panel (housing the knobs) was extremely hot to the touch. I called Home Depot and they arranged for a replacement of the range in question. The new range arrived and it showed exactly the same signs. I called Home Depot again and this time, they sent out a tech to diagnose the problem. The tech arrived while the oven was heating up. I took the surface temperature of the front panel at 135 F. The tech told me that Kitchenaid has a spec where the bare metal can get upto 160 F and he left noting that the appliance was working per design. I kept the oven ON after his departure and the surface temperature of the front panel exceeded 160 F. At this point, I called Home Depot again and explained the concern. They rescheduled another visit with the Kitchenaid tech. When the second tech came in I had the oven at 500 F for about 40 minutes. The tech has a temperature probe (contact heat thermocouple). Using his device, we have recorded temperatures in excess of 285 F in the exposed surface between the front panel and the oven door. The stainless steel panel housing the knobs recorder a temperature in excess of 190 F using the same testing device. I explained to the tech that the surface temperatures of the exposed metal are a safety hazard to my two and four year old kids in the house. The service tech measured the temperatures of the inside of the oven and found them to be close to the set temperature. Based on that he concluded that the appliance is worked as designed. I expressed my concern about exposed metal surfaces on the front of the oven that are extremely hot to the touch. He said it is per design and failed to give me any documentation when I pressed him about how hot the surface can get before its deemed unsafe. 
Per design, there are vents between the front stainless steel panel (housing the knobs) and the oven door. These vents come into play when the oven is turned on. These vents are made out of black metal type material. These vents are very susceptible to the touch (just like the front panel housing the knobs). You can barely touch these surfaces for two seconds without suffering a serious burn. I have expressed this concern to the techs and Kitechanid hot line numerous times but they insist this is per design. I believe such poor design is  a detriment to my family's safety. I have pictures of the temperature readings in case you need them for reference.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard with hot surfaces that could cause burns, especially to children, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

My concern is that at times, my elderly mother is here. Between her and my children, neither set are aware of the difference in temperature. I have 4 boys, and yesterday each got up and had a bowl of cereal with milk that did not have proper refrigeration. They are all suffering from stomach upset due to this faulty product. I can only imagine what would have happened if it had been the meat that was consumed. After looking through online for solutions, I have come to realize that this is not a problem unique to me.
