incident_description: Frigidaire refrigerator/freezer caught on fire during the night. We woke up to soot covering both the fridge and freezer and a terrible smell of burnt plastic and chemicals. Frigidaire unfortunately is not interested in making this right or even taking responsibility since the fridge is outside of their one-year warranty. The fridge is less than 5 years old. According to a repair technician who came out to diagnose where the fire started for insurance purposes, the unit was "found burned in freezer are. Fire started in freezer from defrost heater."
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Entered home to smoke and noxious odor.  Identified source as dishwasher.  Immediately cut power to the dishwasher.  Opened dishwasher door to large quantities of noxious smoke.  Electrical fire observed at dishwasher control board.
justification: Electrical fire observed at dishwasher control board poses a risk of injury or property damage, but no injury was reported in the incident.

incident_description: Electrolux wall oven. My first time using fresh clean, the oven door glass shattered into big shards.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: On Jujly 19, I was cooking a casserole at 400 degrees. In the last five minutes of the 40 minute cook time, I opened the oven to add an additional ingredient. When I did, the entire inside glass panel shattered into hundreds of pieces.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injury was reported, making it a non-injury incident with possible likelihood based on common oven-related incidents.

incident_description: Our Maytag gas double oven Model # MGR6772BDW started on fire under the stovetop control knob while unit was off.
justification: The incident involved a fire starting under the stovetop control knob while the unit was off, indicating a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: We were baking a dish at 400 degrees in our Kenmore model# 79095352803 after 50 mins. It was done and we left the oven at 400 to cook a pizza next. We started to eat, after about 15 mins. We heard a very loud pop. I went to investigate, I realized the oven was still on and looked inside. The entire inside glass door was shattered. My son was the one who was going to cook the pizza, I'm thankful that he wasn't checking on the pizza with his head near the glass. We don't use the oven very often, maybe 2 times a month. We have had the oven for about 5 years, but it is in excellent condition. This is a safety issue and should be recalled. Consumers like me don't believe this is normal wear and tear.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no injury, and the oven is used infrequently (2 times a month).

incident_description: General Electric (GE) over the range microwave oven model number JVM6175SFSS. Surface lights would not turn off. GE service repaired the microwave under warranty. Was in use less than 8 weeks. Service technician found wiring for light bulbs was shorted to microwave chassis at reflector for lights. Repair was to cut wire and splice back together. Reference GE Customer Cares case number [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a malfunction (lights not turning off due to wiring short) but no injury occurred. The issue was repaired under warranty.

incident_description: Cook top burners continue to blow fuses.  It is a four burner with two dual burners and a down draft vent.  It is a Kitchen Aid Cook Top. After repairing two burners, the hot surface light did not work to warn someone that the burner was still hot.  The latest incident was yesterday when a fuse blew and another burner went out.  After that, the unit was buzzing so we had to turn off the breaker.  We turned the breaker back on and one of the burners would come on without being turned on and the only way to turn off is at the breaker.  This will be the fourth time we had the repair guy out to fix something.  I spoke with the manufacturer requesting a new cook top but they would not help other than sending someone to repair the unit.  I finally forced the manufacturer to extend the warranty for another year.  The cook top was purchased in July, 2015 and has only been installed since November of 2015.  This is a dangerous unit because the hot surface warning indicator does no function with all burners, now the unit comes on without being turned on and the burners continue to blow fuses with a very loud pop when they blow
justification: The cook top has multiple malfunctions including burners turning on without input and failing hot surface indicators, posing a burn or fire hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: The oven was not being used at the time of the incident.  We were home at the time, and heard a loud sound from the kitchen.  Upon entering the kitchen we discovered that the front panel of glass of the oven door had shattered.  Pieces of glass were on the floor, and some had gone several feet from the oven. The two inner panels of glass that provide insulation were intact.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no injuries reported, and such events are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her oven glass door exploded shattering glass pieces all over her floor after she had finished using it, this happened about 30 mins later.  (6/2016) The company sent a replacement door but she declined the offer, requesting that she get another stove.  Caller is concerned that the company might not reliable in providing a replacement that may duplicate the incident.

Caller feels that this oven is a safety hazard and that the company should replace this product.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass shards to scatter, but no injury was reported. The incident suggests a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: I used the Elite Platinum electric kettle twice.  The second time, when the water came to a boil, the glass cracked around the base and boiling water poured down my kitchen cabinet.
justification: The incident involved a cracked kettle and spilled boiling water, but no injury was mentioned.

incident_description: I have a kenmore wall oven, model#: 790.40459802. I opened the oven door and the oven exterior front door glass exploded. The door glass part number is 318051525. I called Kenmore and was told that a technician can come to my home and give me an estimate (charge, $150.00). Price for the part is $204.00. The price for both charges is the price of the oven. I advised the Kenmore representative to please make a note of our conversation because I will be filing complaints. They looked up my information under the telephone number [REDACTED]. Please assist me in having this company replace the piece of glass thst should have never exploded while I was simply opening the oven door. Thanks.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass exploding, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
I made a huge pork roast in crock pot yesterday, figured it would make several meals for my large family while we vacation far from a grocery store at our cottage. Well ... we came home to tons of shattered glass falling into the roast. I called crock pot 2d & they said that the latches should never be hooked bc overheats & breaks glass. But it WASN'T latched! They will send me new unit but I need to send old one back!!! And no compensation for $30 roast w $6 BBQ sauce. I'm so ticked. Plus I need to return the bad unit, which means dealing with all this broken glass as we pack to return home. 

In addition, I don't know what we'll eat between now & tomorrow. Kinda low on food. 

I hope there is a way to submit pictures.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass in food but no reported injuries, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the issue was specific to the unit's malfunction.

incident_description: The Gotham Steel Cookware set becomes bowed and spins easily/rocks on top of stove. very dangerous when pan contains hot liquids, especially oils.
justification: The cookware's instability with hot liquids poses a significant risk of burns or spills, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the inner oven glass door exploded and glass pieces fell onto the contents in the oven.  He stated that if this had occurred any sooner it could have caused injury to his spouse.

(6/6) Caller stated that he contacted the manufacturer but they are only interested in replacing the glass in door, he is concerned that this is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass door exploding, but no injuries occurred. The caller expressed concern about potential future injuries, indicating a possible safety hazard.

incident_description:
I have put my family in danger for the very last time due to this toaster oven.  This product is dangerous and will no longer be used in my home. The timer does not shut off. I've had occasions where my food has burned beyond recognition or when I think I've turned it off it continues to heat up to the point of danger.  The case of the toaster oven heats up and I have been protecting my counter tops by placing it on a wooden cutting board. 

 Why has this product not been recalled?  Does someone have to lose their life or their home before action will be taken.  The unit is going into the trash today.  I often will send items to the local mission if I'm no longer using them.  There is no way that I would put someone else in danger.  

I've read other similar complaints. This unit will cause a fire if not attended to.

Thank you,
Barbara Puleri
justification: The toaster oven poses a fire hazard and has caused food to burn, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Elite Electric Oven model 790.48363410 on 05/31/2015. Twice since this purchase date, we have had to have the electronic panel replaced because the oven would turn on and off on its own. According to the repair technician, this is a known issue of this model and it is not unique to just my oven. It is concerning that an oven could turn itself on without any user input. This is a major safety issue, and I believe this model should be investigated for a possible recall.
justification: The oven turning on and off on its own is a safety issue but no injury or death has been reported, and the issue is known to occur frequently in this model.

incident_description:
I have an infantino baby food blender. It was purchased as a gift when my son was born in September 2015. I have been using it several times a week for 4 months now. I have followed all care instructions correctly (eg hand washing after each use... I have never put it in the dishwasher). 
Today I blended up some food for my baby (soft food... Peas & meat) & fed him the food. He ate every bit. After I had fed him I took the blade out to clean the parts & found that the plastic center tube of the blender bowl was broken & shards of plastic were missing!!! The only place these could have gone were into the food which my baby ate! 
I called our Tricare triage nurse who advised me to take my baby to be checked out at the ER. He had to have an x-ray etc & was prodded & poked but we have been told he is ok & should pass the small bits of plastic okay. 
Clearly though I am very shocked & upset about this!
justification: The baby ingested plastic shards, required medical evaluation, but was deemed okay, indicating injury without long-term harm.

incident_description:
(2/1/16 estimated) The consumer used the dish to cook meat in the oven. The consumer set the oven to bake at 400 degrees and let the meat cook for about an hour. After removing the dish from the oven the consumer and her husband ate. Approximately an hour later, the consumer washed the dish and states that the dish was cool prior to washing it. The consumer then placed the dish in the sink to dry and a few minutes later she heard a loud explosion. The consumer noticed multiple shards of glass everywhere in the kitchen as far as 15 ft. from the sink and the consumer states that she had shards of glass in her hair.

The consumer states that the dish was used 6 times a year (estimated).

The consumer had a similar incident with another Pyrex baking dish and filed a separate report.

(6/27/16) The consumer called the firm and the automated system indicated that they were experiencing a high call volume. After being on hold for 10 minutes the consumer hung up. The consumer then visited the firm's website and filled out the contact form.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding, causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(6/25/16) The consumer used the dish to bake hors d'oeuvres. The consumer states that the oven was on the bake setting at 350 degrees and the dish was in the oven for 25 minutes. The consumer removed the dish from the oven and transferred the hors d'oeuvres to a serving dish. The consumer left the kitchen to pass out the hors d'oeuvres and returned to the kitchen about 25 minutes later. The consumer placed the dish on top of the stove and left outside to attend to her guests. When the consumer returned to the kitchen about 15 minutes later the consumer noticed shards of glass were everywhere in the kitchen and about 18 ft. from the stove. 

The consumer states that the dish was used once a month (estimated).

The consumer had a similar incident with another Pyrex baking dish and filed a separate report.

(6/27/16) The consumer called the firm and the automated system indicated that they were experiencing a high call volume. After being on hold for 10 minutes the consumer hung up. The consumer then visited the firm's website and filled out the contact form.
justification: The incident involved a broken dish with no reported injuries, and the consumer had a similar prior incident, indicating a possible pattern.

incident_description:
I was baking 4 salmon fillets in a clear 3 qt. Pyrex baking dish. The recipe called for 425 degrees 15-20 min. After 20 minutes I removed the dish from the oven and sat in on top of the stove to cool. Within about 30 seconds, the Pyrex dish burst apart, leaving glass all over the stove and floor. Fortunately there were no small children in the room at that time.
The sides of the dish broke into large and the bottom broke apart in more of a honeycomb pattern of pieces about 3/8 to 1/2 inch in size. The entire dish was completely destroyed.
justification: The Pyrex dish burst apart, causing damage but no injuries, indicating an incident with no harm to people.

incident_description:
Using a new Hario V-60 tea kettle I received as a gift for the last several weeks, I noticed that if I allow the kettle to "boil" at all for any length of time, it spits boiling water out of the elongated spout and onto surrounding surfaces or potentially off of stove top onto floor.  Not just droplets, large water "jets" come out of the spout with velocity and land close to a foot away for the center of the burner element used.

To duplicate, you would only need to use any Hario V-60 filled with enough water to make a large cup of coffee, however, the more water in the kettle the worse the problem becomes  Allowing to full rapid boil is necessary, but this should be a foreseen circumstance as no one babysits the kettle as it heats nor should they be required to do so.
justification: The kettle spits boiling water with force, posing a burn risk if someone is nearby, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Elite Gas Range Model 790.x Fron Glass Window exploded.
Glass shards were propelled across the room several feet posing a hazard.
Luckily no one was in the vicinity at the time.
justification: Glass exploded and posed a hazard, but no one was injured.

incident_description: Kitchenaid Microwave oven model KCMS145JSS - S/N FGRO402408 turned back on after I took my food out and shut the door. I didn't notice it for a few minutes when I smelled smoke. I tried to hit the "Stop" and Cancel keys and about anything else I thought might work, but nothing worked. Worried it would cause a wall fire I unplugged it and put it outside in the trash. It has worked great for about 15 years, but to think it could have caused a house fire is most worrisome. I used to work for KitchenAid/Whirlpool and hopefully they are on top of this problem.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: We purchased the Baby Brezza Formula Pro for our baby about 4 months ago. We have been using the machine for 11 weeks following all instructions on use and care. The machine is very dangerously shorting the amount of formula that our daughter is to be receiving. It took her being extremely fussy, not pooping, and not sleeping for us to think to compare a handmade bottle to a baby brezza bottle. When comparing we weighed an empty bottle, dispensed 2oz of formula made by the baby brezza and weighed the bottle again and calculated the difference. We then did the same with a bottle made by hand using the formula scoop provided in the formula can. The difference was significant and shocking. Please look into this issue and research this on your own. Watered down bottles can be very dangerous for a newborn as you are already aware. I fear for the parents that do not think to evaluate what is being dispensed.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning product that could lead to underfeeding, posing a risk to infant health, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: First time using the waffle maker, I got burned since the outside of the waffle maker was as hot as the inside.
justification: The user sustained a burn injury from the hot waffle maker, indicating an injury severity. Burns from hot appliances are a common occurrence.

incident_description:
The tempered glass on the front of a GE "Above the Cooktop" Convection Oven, Model: JVM1790SK, Serial No:FR905387, shattered.

The oven had never been used.  GE is claiming that tempered glass used in their ovens shatters, and that the cost of replacement must be borne by the consumer.  GE has refused to acknowledge how dangerous this situation is, and has stated that tempered glass shattering despite an oven never being used is not atypical and within the scope of the appliance's design specifications.
justification: The tempered glass shattered but there was no injury reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
My husband and I were eating supper and the MIDDLE glass on our oven door shattered for no reason. The Oven was not in use and for that matter is rarely used. 
I do not use the self cleaning feature. 
The glass fell down between the other windows in the door to the floor.
The outer and inside windows are still in tact.
 I took photographs of the problem, Called Whirlpool and of course they had nothing to do with the issue, and tried to sell me an extended warranty. The stove is only three years old.
justification: The glass shattered without causing injury, and the oven was not in use, indicating a low severity incident with no harm.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while her oven was in use, she was closing door after taking out the baked contents, the outer oven glass door exploded shattering glass all over her feet and on the floor.  There were no injuries.  (7/5) The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that the range was no longer under warranty and they could send out a service technician at her expense.

Caller stated that there has been numerous reports on these incident yet the company is not willing to do anything about this safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The mention of numerous reports suggests the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description: In February 2016, I bought a KitchenAid gas range.  I noticed since then that exterior surfaces became extremely hot after the oven had been on for a while.  The heat on the horizontal surface just above the oven gets so hot, it could burn someoneÃÂs skin and I fear for the safety of my grandchildren when they visit.  I contact the manufacturer, Whirlpool, which sent a technician to my home.  The technician was knowledgeable, professional, and very familiar with this safety concern.  The technician ÃÂ THEIR TECHNICIAN informed us that the excessive heat is due to a design defect; that the product was configured with an updraft for the oven instead of a downdraft, a mistake in his opinion.
justification: The incident involves a design defect causing excessive heat, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I was using the SodaStream  - I believe it is the Splash Play model -  to charge my water. Normally, after pressing the button to charge the water, 3 loud buzzes are heard, and the water is charged. I was pressing the button to release the CO2, and suddenly, the top of the machine flew off and a brass piece flew out of the machine, just missing my eye. I contacted the company, but have not resolved anything with them yet. I tried submitting a review of this product on their website, but they would not publish it, stating my review "did not meet publishing guidelines."
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
GE MODEL:JVM1540DM5WW
SERIAL #:LZ211915L
Manufactured June 2012
Microwave began operating by itself. Opening the door didn't turn it off, only unplugging it turned it off, however, plugging it back in immediately caused it to start running again. This continued for the next 5 unplugging's and replugging's, finally after about the 5th time- after leaving it unplugged for an hour or so, the microwave acted normal again and did not turn on upon plugging it in. It reverted to normal behavior and operation.
justification: The microwave operated unexpectedly but no injury or damage was reported, and the issue resolved itself after multiple attempts.

incident_description:
(06/10/2016) The consumer stated that she was washing the blade and noticed a piece missing. She looked in the food that she had chopped and saw a 1/2 piece of metal from the blade.

(06/10/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. She spoke with [REDACTED] -Customer Service. The consumer was advised that a new blade would be sent. The consumer was advised not to send the broken blade to the firm. No report was taken.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade with no reported injury, and the firm responded by sending a replacement.

incident_description:
The consumer's daughter was using the oven on the quick bake setting. Approximately 10 minutes later the consumer's daughter opened the door to turn over the chicken nuggets when the outer glass shattered. The consumer states the inner glass is still intact.

The consumer then contacted the firm to inform them about the incident and the Rep. (name unknown) advised her that 3 other consumers reported a similar incident. The consumer states the Rep. told her the range was out of warranty and not recalled. The consumer indicated that the Rep. did not offer any further assistance. 

There are no prior incidents. 

The consumer uses the oven daily.

The consumer plans to purchase another range and may not keep the range for 30 more days.
justification: The outer glass shattered but no injury occurred, and similar incidents have been reported by other consumers.

incident_description:
I was using my Kohl's brand ceramic non-stick pan, when one of the rivets that attaches the handle to the pan exploded and flew off.  It seemed like it was a result of steam (or something else) building up and bursting the rivet.  It flew across the room, and could easily have seriously hurt someone.  It made a very loud noise and the rivet flew at a very high rate of speed.  
The pan was a Kohl's ceramic non-stick pan, 9 inches, with the number 7105 on the back.  It was white on the inside, silver on the outside.
This was definitely a dangerous and hazardous condition.
justification: The rivet exploded and flew at high speed, posing a serious injury risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: My Jen air stove glass shattered into nugget size glass when turning on self clean mode. Purchased new door turned on self clean oven again. Inside glass shatter again. Model numberjes9750aaw serial number 18898494eg
justification: The incident describes glass shattering during self-clean mode, which is a hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a GE Profile Dishwasher, Model No. PDW9980L00SS. It was not being used, although some washed dishes were inside it.

I woke up one morning last week and went into my kitchen and the counter above the dishwasher was hot to the touch. I opened it and a plume of smoke from plastic filled my kitchen. Everything inside the dishwasher had melted, including all the plastic parts of the dishwasher, and including a plastic cutting board. Apparently, the heating element came on by itself.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing smoke and melting plastic, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have an Oster Convection Toaster Oven. The door gets extremely hot while in use. Fingers have been burned when they come into contact with the door. The handle on the door is not far away enough from the door, so it becomes very easy to accidentally touch the door when opening, burns result.
justification: The description confirms burns from contact with the hot door, indicating injury (severity 3). The ease of accidental contact suggests this is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
My ninja blender cut my son's face. My husband was carrying the blender to the refrigerator to put ice in it. As he raise the unit towards the ice maker, the bad launched out, causing it to slice open my son's face. [REDACTED]
 I have outstanding medical bills of around $2672. Future medical bills are projected to be $10,000. Ninja kitchen is responsible for this. My heath insurance will not pay because they say it is 3rd party responsible. My son is entitled to pain and suffering as well. I submitted a link for an online calculator with an amount that is figured as a settlement in this case. Ninja offered me $7,500. That will not even cover the current medical expenses along with future expenses, not to mention the pain that my 3 year old son endured and the HUGE SCAR ON HIS FACE!  

This company is negligent, if you got to the Ninja Kitchen Facebook page, you will see all the posts on there about injuries. Ninja conveniently hides them, until they are called out and then they allow the posts to be visible again. My son is not the only one to suffer an injury. The blade needs to be locked in, the post it sits on needs to be longer, or held in place with a magnet or pin.

Someone from the safety department called me from his personal cell phone top discuss this matter with me. He admitted that this was not misuse of the product, the pitcher was not designed to be a stationary object. It has a handle and was designed to be carried. He said he is aware of how lose the blade sits in the pitcher, but they are at a loss of what to do, since it is so sharp and they don't know how to latch it in and make it safe for people to reach in and unlatch it.  He said this approach seemed like the option with less risk of getting cut.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury to a child, including a facial scar and substantial medical expenses, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported injuries and admitted design flaws by the manufacturer.

incident_description:
I have a single serving blender to make smoothie. Was driving one and got black plastic in the smoothie. It came for the bottom cap of the blender.
It is a GE/Walmart Model 898679
justification: Black plastic in the smoothie indicates a foreign object contamination, which could cause injury if ingested.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his refrigerator that he purchased in 2007 from a retailer in California. 
He noticed a burning odor during the very early hours on June 21st, 2016 then began investigating until he found that it was coming from his refrigerator light area.
The light had remained on during the night while the refrigerator door was shut and had melted the plastic around it as well as turning the light sockets black.
The caller had to use gloves to remove the bulbs would not turn off.
The heat melted the finger tips on the gloves.
There are no injuries being reported.
He is reporting this incident as a potential burn and fire hazard.
He contacted the manufacturer June 21st, 2016 but was referred to CPSC.
No existing recall for this product was found.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and melted plastic, but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
(06/20/2016) The consumer stated that the right rear burner came on by itself. The consumer was not able to turn it off. The consumer had to disconnect the range at the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that this happened before with the same burner.

(06/24/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. She was advised that the product was out of warranty and not recalled. The consumer was offered a service call at a cost to her.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury was reported, and the issue was previously noted, indicating a recurring problem.

incident_description:
This is what I sent to Cuisinart customer service:

"I was gifted the food processing machine Model#CFB-11ZBCPC Serial#41205 S approx 8 months ago. I use it chiefly to make purees in preparation of our family meals.

Last night, about 4pm, I was making a puree of freshly-picked tomatoes--from my garden--including fresh herbs, garlic cloves and a can of tomato sauce and a little water. After 10 seconds of the machine being on, there was a giant bang and I saw a hole in the side of the Cuisinart clear plastic container/bowl; the blade had broken in half and part of it went through the side of the container. It had hit the stove and part the processor accessory case against the wall, behind the appliance.

I was standing right in front of it (making dinner) with my three children next to me, one of which is nine years old, and her head is about level with the appliance. If that blade had broken off just a nano-second earlier, it would have gone through her head, or my stomach.

We were all in shock, as this has never happened before. My mom had a Cuisinart for 15 years and it never anything did this. Today, I compared the thickness of this blade to her model (15 years old) and mine is far thinner and appears to be made of some kind of aluminum, not steel.

After a minute, I grabbed my phone and took pictures of the splintered pieces of plastic, the broken blade and the tomato sauce all over and was on the phone calling your customer service. The man on the phone was very aloof and did not seem to grasp the seriousness of the situation. He talked about replacement parts, but I informed him that I don't want another machine that will break apart again, and put us in such danger. I asked him if you were receiving complaints about this issue; he said "no". He put me on some kind of manager "24-hour call back list" which I have not had a call back from, as of yet.

The claim that no one else was complaining turned out to be a lie. I looked up this model online and found dozens of complaints (publicly listed) about the blade snapping half--even in processing soft items--and flying out the side of the container, just using the machine as the manual says it can be used. (And no, I did not list them here; I am certain your staff knows how to use Google)

Due to the number of public, visible complaints, it seems to me that Cuisinart is ignoring a serious danger to the consumer, knowingly putting out products that have two huge flaws.

Please tell your product development team, engineers and lawyers that:

1. the blade needs to be stronger (not so flimsy) so it wont snap in half
2. the plastic container/bowl need to be stronger to withstand the seemingly inevitable blade malfunction.

I do not want a replacement product that will once again put my family in danger again. I will not use it if I think the thin, cheap blade will snap in half. Any replacement parts offered must be stronger; the blade must be thicker and made of steel. If the motor is too powerful for the blade to handle, why did you put out an appliance that might fail?

Please get back to me quickly. I make food for my family three times a day and I use a food processor of some kind at least 4 times per week; I currently have no food processor and am having to work around it and alter the menu.

If you want me to send you the photos or the broken blade & bowl mailed to you as proof, let me know. I have also sent a copy of this email to a number of consumer affairs/safety watchdog individuals. If I do not hear back from your company in 24 hours I will write a consumer affair article on this model with the full breadth of the tale included and email it to as many media outlets as possible.

The public should be informed of the danger of this model, and God forbid it kills someone's little girl, and you knew about it, and could have prevented it.

Please immediately act to take this model off the shelves and inform the public of a nation-wide recall to replace these defective blades.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction of a food processor, but no actual injury occurred despite the potential for severe harm.

incident_description: I am reporting this since it is the third time this has happened with this range. The knobs on this GE range are very sensitive. If I cross something over them they will turn on without any pushing down. The knob is designed so that you are suppose to "push in" then turn. Unfortunately you do not need to push in which means they easily turn on without knowledge. We have had two fires due to this issue and I'm concerned we won't catch the next one before it escalates. Both times we were placing a box on top of the range while not using the range. This motion of putting something on top of the range turned the knobs on. This has happened twice where the knob goes to "high" and the box ignites. Although putting a box on top of a range is not it's normal use (as a counter) this is a physical fire hazard and should not happen. The top of our range is glass so the surface is flat. We have inadvertently turned on our range numerous times by bumping it or leaning across it. Twice now we've had fire. I believe there should be a "fix" for this with knobs that are more secure. I would happily purchase a replacement to keep us safe.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the range knobs causing fires, which is a significant hazard. Although no injuries are reported, the potential for severe consequences is high.

incident_description:
My dishwasher caught fire while in use. We turned on the dishwasher before going to bed, we went to bed and wasn't fully asleep then we heard a noise in the kitchen and went to investigate and the dishwasher had flames shooting out of it. The flames were extinguished with a fire extinguisher we keep in the kitchen. 

After containing the incident, I did investigation and saw my dishwasher was under a voluntary recall from back in January of 2009. I purchased my home in July of 2013 and did not change any appliances. I was not aware of any recalls active for dishwashers.

The dishwasher make is a Bosch. It is model number SHU43C06UC /17. The serial number is FD8412 01556.

After some research online, there seems to be a large gap of affected units that have not been fixed and accounted for as of October of 2015 - something like 75% of affected units havent been fixed. I'm sure there are thousands of other consumers in the same situation as I am - purchasing a home with an defective dishwasher and not knowing about it. 

I'm sure if we weren't able to respond swiftly with the appropriate way to extinguish, the damage would have been severe and possibly fatal.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no injury. The recall status suggests this is a possible but not rare occurrence.

incident_description:
I was cooking an omelet over medium heat when I heard a VERY loud bang.
Something hit the coffeemaker and refrigerator.
I turned off the heat and investigated.
In the well where the glass carafe nestles was a round piece of metal.
Looking into the pan I saw where the rivet cover blew off of the pan.
Luckily the only casualties were the glass carafe and a small dent in my fridge.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang and damage to property (coffeemaker and fridge) but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My Kenmore oven door shattered across the kitchen floor as it was baking a ham at 380 degrees. 
There was no knick or scratch in the glass or problem with the door previously.  We bought this home in 2014 and the oven was here when we purchased the house. It is a convection oven with a ceramic glass top. 
There was a child walking in my kitchen at the time just inches away from stepping in front of the  door when it shattered. Glass hit the child in the chin and caused bleeding. 
I have never seen anything like this before, not had the friends and neighbors that I contacted about the situation. 
I have, however, seen many many reports online of similar incidents happening. 
I have pictures taken to document the incident if they are needed.
justification: The child was injured by glass shards, which caused bleeding, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents are reported online but are not common.

incident_description: I was making lemonade in my Farmstand Becerage dispenser when I went to lift it up onto my granite countertop the bottom of the dispenser just barely tapped against the granite and broke off falling down to my knee and lacerating it causing me to get 9 staples. The weight of the dispenser is 20 pounds without liquid in it! It is very very dangerous. Had one of my children been standing there it could have cut their foot off. Or if a child were to try and dispense themselves a drink out of it and pull it down on them it could kill them! This product is way too heavy to be made out of glass and then filled with liquid. The weight of the broken glass was unbelievable.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring 9 staples, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to the product's design flaws and potential for similar accidents.

incident_description: My oven for the 2nd time will not turn off.  I baked a pan of food turned my oven off went up stairs my dogs started barking and barking I smelled smoke and the pan was burning the oven was off however it was on inside.  This happened once before and I unplugged it and plugged it back in and all was fine.  Tonight not the case I tried to turn it off even though it was off but it just got hotter I pulled it away from wall and unplugged it.  I waited two hours and tried again however it was off but still on.  It was red hot and was very scary it could have burned my home down thank god I was home and my dogs let me know.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sharp Drawer Microwave (model KB6524PS) from Pacific Sales (Escondido, CA) on May 28, 2014 that included a one-year warranty. I did not purchase the additional extended warranty assuming an $800 microwave would last beyond 2 years without major issues. On July 9th at 5 pm, I was microwaving, meatballs for my two daughters (19 months and 3 years old), after 30 seconds I hit the open button and as the drawer opened large sparks flew out of the microwave. I was startled and shouted for my girls to get back. I then hit the close button and more sparks flew and the microwave shut down- all lights and power went off and will not turn back on. This appliance it at child head height- I consider this concerning since sparks were flying. I hopped online and noticed that there are an abundance of comments all over online sites- [REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and independent electronic blogs of consumers complaining of sparks, fire, melting components on this model. I didn't believe this could be true and if so, Sharp must be aware and very willing to help. I have spoken with them four times now and each time they have denied any negative reviews or issues with smoking or sparks on these drawer microwaves. A representative, [REDACTED], who said that just like any electronic there is the '1 percent' of any product that is defective and that was my microwave. I spoke to another representative, [REDACTED], whom confirmed all the negative reviews online from other consumers but there was nothing she could do and that she completely understood how I felt having children at home with a fire hazard. Sharp will not acknowledge or assist with replacement of my microwave, even though they are fully aware that this model is fire hazard (ticking time-bomb) in thousands of households across the country and world. They refuse to acknowledge, recall, repair or work with consumers because 'they sell very well'. I refuse to allow Sharp to conceal a huge liability when children's lives are in jeopardy.

I want Sharp to acknowledge and provide support for all consumers claiming any sparks, melting or smoke with these microwaves- apparently this is frequent and needs to be addressed in order to prevent death or harm to children and adults. I would also like a full reimbursement to re-purchase a microwave that is not a fire-hazard for my family, a new replacement of the existing microwave, or a different microwave that will not pose any safety risks to my children and will fit in the kitchen cabinet built specifically for this model. Sharp needs to be held accountable and stand up for their name and products. They should not wait for a fatality or lawsuit to stop them from concealing consumers complaints of a safety hazard in their homes and knowingly misguiding consumers.
justification: The incident involved sparks flying from the microwave, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was cooking, using my Cuisinart 10" skillet (model # 722-24) over medium heat when I heard an extremely loud "pop."  I asked my children (standing nearby) if they were OK and my daughter said, "Mom, look at the pan."  I saw that the rivet, attaching handle to pan, had popped open.  We were fortunate that the rivet did not dislodge and hurt anyone, though I continued to have ear pain for hours after the incident.  

Called Cuisinart and they want me to return the skillet to them and they will send a replacement.  From what I've read, this is not the first incident with their skillets.  Extremely dangerous - a recall is in order here.
justification: The incident caused ear pain (injury) and the description mentions similar incidents, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
GE CAFÃÂÃÂ SERIES SLIDE-IN FRONT CONTROL DUAL-FUEL RANGE WITH BAKING DRAWER
C2S985SETSS - There is nothing to indicate a gas burner is lit and in use. Due to low flame levels when burners are on low the flame is hard to see. If you do not look at the knobs it is easy to overlook the fact the burners are still on. We have had multiple instances where a burner has been left on and have had some close call with children.
justification: The description indicates a potential hazard with burners being left on unnoticed, leading to close calls with children, but no actual injury or death reported.

incident_description:
Responded to a reported fire in the kitchen. Homeowner had arrived and found dishwasher on fire. Wife had left the house approximately one hour earlier and the dishwasher was off.
Damage was contained to the kitchen cabinets surrounding the dishwasher.
Dishwasher was a Viking Professional series but the model and manufacturer plate were not legible. 
Heavy fire and heat damage to the bottom of the tub and rear of dishwasher.
The homeowner does not remember how old the dishwasher is, but it appears at least 5 years old.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, and the damage was contained to the dishwasher and surrounding cabinets.

incident_description:
We were mixing raw salmon and pre-cooked vegetables in a 4 quart Pyrex mixing bowl. 
The veggies and salmon had been mixed well together to make salmon cakes. 
It was at least ten minutes after any temperature changes had been made in the bowl and the bowl had not been touched in at least 3 minutes and the bowl untouched exploded on the counter top.
The food was ruined and glass went everywhere. 
The explosion was very loud. 
Glass flew 8 ft.
justification: The incident involved a bowl exploding, causing food to be ruined and glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(4/28/16) The consumer used the oven self cleaning feature for the first time. A few hours later the consumer noticed that the oven's control panel was completely blank and the door was locked. The consumer noticed that the oven was very warm to the touch. 

(4/29/16 Approximately) The consumer contacted Specialty Appliance to have the oven inspected and the consumer was referred to Whirlpool. The consumer then contacted Whirlpool and arranged for a technician to inspect the oven. 

(5/1/16 Approximately) The technician inspected the oven and advised the consumer that two fuses were blown out. The technician told the consumer that one of the fuses controls the fan which cools down the oven. When the technician pulled out the oven to conduct the inspection the consumer noticed that the cabinets surrounding the oven were scorched.  The consumer states that the fuses were replaced. The consumer states that the repairs were conducted under the warranty.

The consumer indicated that he requested a replacement oven and he is communicating with the firm. The consumer does not feel safe using the oven. The consumer states that the firm has not agreed to provide a replacement.

The consumer arranged with the store to have the oven delivered and installed on 6/27/15.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with scorched cabinets but no reported injuries, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is possible as similar incidents with appliances can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description: Tea was being brewed in the french press.  Once the brewing time has elapsed, I lifted the french press to pour the liquid into a container.  That's when the glass carafe fell through the metal frame of the coffee press.  The glass carafe shattered and hot liquid burned my right upper thigh.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from hot liquid, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description: I have LFX25980st LG Refridgerator Ice maker that broke a piece of plastic from the inside of the ice maker unit and fell into the ice of the drink.  Over time, the ice maker broke because the plastic piece was not spinning the auger motor of the ice bin.
justification: A piece of plastic broke off and fell into the ice, but there was no injury or harm to a person.

incident_description: We purchased a GE gas range with bottom broiler (instead of a storage drawer). We used it for several weeks and noticed that it ran too hot, was fume-y and smoky. Last night while baking bread (at 425, the highest temperature we have used), it scorched our vinyl floor, filling our house with horrific smoke and fumes.
justification: The incident caused property damage (scorched vinyl floor) and filled the house with smoke and fumes, posing a health risk.

incident_description:
I'm writing concerning my GE electric range, model #JB630DF4WW, that was purchased from Home Depot on 04-19-15. I did not purchase the extended warranty offered by Home Depot.  I have contacted GE and they are sending someone to check the damage.

On June 30, 2016, I was getting a glass pitcher out of the cabinet adjacent to my range.   The pitcher bumped the oven door and immediately the glass front fell to the floor at my feet.  The pitcher was not broken, so I know it was a slight bump.  Fortunately, I wasn't injured except for a small cut on my foot.  It only required minor first aid. The oven was last used four days prior to this incident.   I had never heard of this happening, but when checking on line, it appears this is not an isolated problem.

My concern is that mothers often have small children playing in the kitchen with pots, pans, wooden spoons, toys etc.  It seems very possible one of these objects could strike the range door causing the glass to break and injury a child or pet.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (small cut on foot) requiring first aid, and the description suggests this is not an isolated problem, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
General Electric states that 183 degrees is an acceptable temperature for the exterior control panel on a electric stainless steel double oven.  They claim that Underwriter's Laboratory says that is an okay temp.

OSHA and California feel that anything over 135 degrees will cause 2nd degree burns.  I used a new infrared thermometer and got readings of 172 degrees.  Too hot to touch.

A major concern is that the double oven, bought in 2013, is placed inside a wooden cabinet.  Very high potential for a fire.  G.E. has sent a repair service and they replaced the upper oven door hinges and the insulating rope on the interior of the upper unit door.  G.E. feels that 183 degrees is reasonable because it was UL tested and approved.  I am stating that it is a fire hazard and has great potential to burn someone badly.
justification: The incident describes a high temperature on the oven's exterior, posing a burn risk and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire has occurred yet.

incident_description: I was heating soup in a [REDACTED] bowl in the microwave, as I have many times previously without incident.  It was taking much longer than usual, as it was heating the soup, but not as hot as usual in the same amount of time on high power, so I had to keep heating it.  Finally, the microwave quit in the middle of a cycle and the outside display screen showed a series of 8's.  When I opened the door, I smelled a burned smell that was not the soup, and saw smoke coming out of the top of the microwave.  Then I saw a flame in the little box where the light bulb was, and heard buzzing, like an electrical live wire sound.  I screamed for my husband and by the time he came, the flame had died out.  The flame lasted for around 30-45 seconds.  It did not appear to do any damage other than the microwave became inoperable.  When my husband pulled the microwave out from its built-in cabinet in order to unplug it for safety reasons, he burned his hand when he touched the OUTSIDE of the microwave on the top.  Although the microwave was 3-1/2 years old at the time of the incident, it was not used much until one year before the incident.  (We built our retirement home a few years before moving into it in late June 2015.  Prior to that, the microwave had only been used for a few weeks while we were on vacation in 2013 and 2014).  It is not overused, as there are only 2 adults and no children living in the household.  We have not had any problems with any other appliances since moving in, so it would not appear to be due to anything with our wiring.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burn) to the husband, and the microwave malfunction was an isolated event with no prior issues.

incident_description: The microwave starts when you shut the door. It will not turn off unless you open the door. None of the buttons work. It is less than a month old. Used maybe 4 x a day.  If you search on twitter hundreds of hits, common problem with many brands for years!
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a risk of unintended operation, but no injury is reported. The issue is common and frequently reported, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a GE range on 8-30-2014, I use the range during the summer months only.  Today I was baking muffins, turned the oven off and within 15 minutes the oven glass shattered.
justification: The oven glass shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Dishwasher was running and the control panel caught on fire.
justification: The dishwasher's control panel caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
(05/30/2016) The consumer stated that his wife was cooking on the front right burner. After she finished cooking, she tried to turn the burner off. While she was working with the knob to turn the burner off, there was a popping sound. The burner would not go out.

The consumer had to disconnect the stove at the circuit breaker.

The consumer ordered a replacement part that controls the heat to the burners. When he turned the stove back on after installing the part, there was a loud popping and a spark. The burner still did not work.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner and sparks, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(6/13/16) The consumer was using the right front burner for about 4 minutes on heat level 4 when she noticed sparks and immediately shut off the burner.

(6/14/16) The consumer called the store where she purchased it and informed them of the incident. The consumer states they apologized for the incident and did not provide any further assistance. 

The consumer then contacted Frigidaire and informed them about the incident. The consumer was advised that the range was not recalled and to contact the store where she purchased it. 

The consumer states that about a year after purchasing the range the two rear burners stopped working. About 4 months ago the consumer noticed that the left front burner began to get weaker.

The consumer believes the range poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved sparks but no injury or death, and the occurrence likelihood is based on the consumer's report of multiple burner issues over time.

incident_description:
Hazardous Incident AND Safety Concern; Re: LG LDG4315ST Gas Range

There is a serious design/safety flaw in the knob assembly on the front of the range.  With minimal pressure, the knob can turn and ignite, and sometimes not ignite.  This happened numerous times passing by the range and brushing the knobs with my hip.  My wife has turned on the front burners when leaning against the knob panel to reach a pan on one of the back burners.  Our dog has jumped on the front of the range and turned on the knobs.  One instance was when I went out shopping and returned home to a house full of gas!  This past Saturday, July 2, we were in another part of the house when we smelled food cooking/burning.  When I ran to the kitchen, I heard the igniter clicking and the burner had ignited under a frying pan on the back left burner.  The dog was apparently trying to reach food that was still in the frying pan.

I have contacted LG about this matter and they sent a technician to our home on June 2, 2016.  The technician verified my concerns to LG but could not get any committal toward repair from LG.  I followed up with LG and they claim to have no report from the technician.  Now, LG is sending another technician on Friday, July 15, 2016; essentially to do the same thing, verify that it is an irreparable design problem.  LG claims to have no complaints about this model.
justification: The incident involves repeated unintended gas ignition, posing a fire hazard and gas leak risk, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Using maytag gas cook top model# mgc7536ws00 to cook lunch and one of the burner valves that wasn't being used started to smoke, spark and flames were shooting upward from under the valve knob. The electrical circuit for the lite function was shorting to the aluminum valve body for burner valve. The short was severe enough it started to melt the aluminum on the gas burner valve. I was able to unplug the unit prior to gas being potentially exposed to the electrical short preventing a fire or gas explosion. The electrical harness for all 5 lite switches and that one burner valve require replacement.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous electrical short and potential fire risk, but no injury or gas explosion occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: On November 9, 2015, we purchased an entire kitchen suite of Samsung appliances  including a French door refrigerator, microwave oven, dishwasher and electric range.  After only a few months, the refrigerator's ice maker no longer worked and I had to contact Samsung for replacement of the entire ice maker unit.  For the past 2 months, my microwave oven is no longer functioning properly and I have contacted Samsung support numerous times.  Their service contractor, Lakes Electronics, sent a repairmen out 3 wk. ago but he was not sure what the problem was and left without doing anything.  After 2 wk. the microwave again stopped working completely, losing its total power and display.  I again called Samsung who after 5 days faxed the service order over to Lakes Electronics.  Lakes called me and said the first opportunity a technician could service the microwave was in 10 days from then!  Mind you, all this time, the microwave was not operational.  I again called Samsung yesterday to tell them of my dilemma and while on with customer support, we ran the microwave to discuss in detail what it was doing.  Not only is it not running on full power and then loses total power and display, when I felt the right side of the microwave, I burned my finger pads, it was that hot.  Customer support told me to unplug the microwave to avoid its catching fire or blowing up which we did!  She also typed copious notes into their system for the technician and also told me a product specialist would call me back to lend assistance.  I have never heard back from Samsung's product specialist and am totally dismayed about my purchase of these 4 new kitchen appliances, the refrigerator, microwave, dishwasher and electric range.  After less than 6 months to have 2 major breakdowns of these appliances tells there is no reliability of them.  While they are still under warranty, I am still not happy with these appliances.  I requested a new microwave oven from Samsung yesterday and was told that the technician would have to deem this appliance unreparable in order for a new microwave to be given to us.  This is totally unacceptable that I have had this brand new appliance for 6 months of use and it is a fire hazard and non-operational.  I am hoping Consumer Affairs can lend assistance to us in getting a new microwave oven.  Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from the microwave and poses a fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the repeated malfunctions and safety concerns.

incident_description:
The inside glass in our Whirlpool range door just exploded after cooking.  We have a WFE540H0ES that we purchased last year (within warranty, but I haven't contacted Whirlpool yet).  I was not home at the time, but here is what happened according to my wife:

1. Baked a pizza at 500 degrees for 30 minutes.
2. Cooled the oven down to 425 degrees.
3. Cooked another pizza for 15 minutes.
4. Turned the oven off.

Ten minutes after turning the oven off, after the food had been removed, and while the door was closed, the inside pane of glass shattered and fell into the storage drawer with some falling out onto the floor.
justification: The incident involved the glass shattering but no injuries were reported, and such failures are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
I had just cooked breakfast in a Cuisinart small skillet and took the final pancake out of the pan, then moved the pan further back on the stove. All of a sudden, I heard a loud 'pop' that sounded like a gunshot, and something hit me in
the shoulder. However, I had horrible pain in my ears, and was holding both ears due to the pain from the loud sound. I had immediate 'ringing' in the ears and a red mark on my shoulder where I had been 'hit.' I had no idea what had happened and started looking around the room to see what had happened. I spoke with my friend and she asked me to check the walls and windows for bullet holes. (It had been THAT LOUD.) Then she asked me to take a look at my pan. She had heard about a recall on pans that had parts that went flying while cooking. I looked, and sure enough, one of the rivet covers from the inside of the pan (that holds the handle in place) was missing. I could not find it anywhere, though. I immediately called Cuisinart to discuss the incident with them. They had no resolution and said someone would call me back in 2-3 days. They did not call back; About an hour after my call, I was walking through my living room and found the rivet cover that had flown off the pan. It had traveled over 15 feet from the stove to its resting place in the living room.
justification: The incident caused pain in the ears and a red mark on the shoulder, indicating injury, but the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the rarity of pan rivet failures.

incident_description: This oven came on by itself when my power came back on after a brief outage - and it was on at the highest temp and would NOT shut off from the on/off button. incident_description: Our GE oven door (the window) gets extremely hot during use. Our 1 year old touched it and was burned, which prompted our inquiry with the mfr. They told us the window is legally allowed to reach 172 degrees. This in itself is ridiculous. When you have children in the house you're instructed to lower your water heater to 120 degrees to prevent scalding - why is something at a child's face level in the most-used room in the house allowed to get 52 degrees hotter?! The GE customer service rep first told us not to leave children unattended while using the oven. Duh. Then she said we should have done more research before we bought the oven. Who in this day and age would think to ask whether their brand new oven door could cause burns?! After several days of back and forth with the mfr, we got frustrated and bought a laser temperature guage. It read 209 degrees on the door. Only after I emailed the customer service rep a photo of this did she offer to send out a service tech. The man - who was employed by GE - was extremely rude and condescending. I said that even 172 degrees was an unacceptable temperature. He pointed at one of the burners and said "Well how hot do you think THAT gets? Do you have a problem with that?" He told us he would have to leave his temp guage on the oven door for 20-30 minutes in order to allow the glass to heat all the way up. Lo and behold, his guage read 173 within 10 minutes, and he promptly pulled the probe off and ended the test early, saying that the oven was within specs and it was pointless for us to try and fight this. Livid, I emailed the customer service rep back and told her what had happened. All we wanted was to get this dangerous unit out of our house and away from our kids before more injuries happen! This has dragged on and on and on. I finally contacted the corporate office of where we purchased the oven (Menards). We are well past their return policy, and they don't even carry GE appliances anymore. But they immediately apologized for our baby's injury and are giving us a full store credit to use toward a new oven of our choice. GE should be ashamed. We were made to feel like bad parents for being angry about this. The threat is removed from our house, but I have to wonder how many dangerous units are out there.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to a child, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) given the oven's design and common household use.

incident_description:
On 5/27/16, I inspected my ice maker bucket because over the last 2 to 3 days, my family experienced slowed ice delivery.  Upon pulling the bucket out, two piece of the plastic auger were found.  The two pieces were matched to the auger and two small pieces were determined to be missing.  
In order to find the missing pieces, the ice was removed and placed into a cooler to allow the ice to melt and the emptied bucket was inspected.  One of the two pieces was found at the bottom of the bucket.  The melted ice was then strained through a 1mm mesh strainer.  Unfortunately, the second small piece was not found and is still missing.  The portion of the auger where the missing piece originates was measured.  If still intact, the missing piece is estimated to be 7mm x 2mm x 4mm in size and likely has sharp edges.
The opening and chute leading out of the bucket was inspected and the opening appears to be close enough to the bottom for a small piece of this size to likely be pushed out and into a cup when dispensing ice.  Since the plastic is clear, it is unlikely that a consumer would see a small piece of broken plastic.  It would also be unlikely that a small piece would be detected by a consumer especially if it were to fall into crushed ice and the ice consumed.
On 5/27/16, GE Customer Relations was emailed via their website to inform them of the incident and to discuss the safety risk at hand.  Since three weeks went by with no contact, I contacted them by phone on 6/17/16.  The representative took note of the incident and recommended a technician be sent out to inspect and repair the ice bucket and auger respectively.  The decision was made to save the $99 service fee and I inspected the ice crusher and the bucket once again throughout.  No foreign material was found.
At this time, there have not been any known injuries, but the potential for a consumer to be injured by a broken piece of the auger is too high to for there brittle plastic augers to be installed.  Please assist getting these removed from the market before consumers are injured.
justification: The incident involved broken plastic pieces in the ice maker, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood of injury is possible due to the potential for sharp plastic pieces to be consumed.

incident_description:
I was standing at the kitchen counter, a step away from the LG Gas Range.  My wife reached across to kiss me and  we both heard the range ignite and turn on the front right burner on high.  It looked like her sweater was in the flame, but she  pulled away quickly enough to avoid a fire.  I then reached over and turned off the knob on the gas range, which turned on when her sleeve brushed across the knob.  It takes incredibly little effort to turn the valve knobs on, and we put up signs around the kitchen to remind us of the hazard.

The valve which the knob operates was one of a set of new replacement valves that an LG range repairman had installed on 5/9/2016 to replace the valves that I had reported as faulty in a prior report to the CPSC (report no. 20160420-6B4AF-2147420077).  The LG repairman was at my home from their Phoenix AZ office.  He also said that LG told him that LG warehouses had "worked through" the old stock and replaced it with new valves that required more of a physical push on them before they would turn.  These valves were portrayed as a new style that corrects for the problem described in my prior report (and a virtually identical report, no. 20160311-11F22-2147420995).  I told him after they were installed that they act identically like the faulty valves I reported.  He said he was told they were a new design, but the part number was identical to the prior valves. It is very poor practice to use the same part number for a re-designed part; it would be unable to control its inventory and assure the old parts were never accidentally put into the inventory.  Any company that does this contradicts the statement LG made in response to my prior CPSC report: "Our process not only rigorously tests to insure the quality of product leaving our factory, but we also carefully monitor how our products perform in use. LG takes very seriously the concerns of our customers and uses such feedback on an on-going basis to evaluate and improve our products."  Using valves of the same part number, portrayed as new design, combined with the fact these valves operate identically to the ones they replaced, the evidence is very powerful that LG misrepresented itself to me, and to any other owners of the same range.  It is also evidence that LG, in fact, did not carefully test the  gas range before sending it out the door to the supply stores. It is also noteworthy that LG never informed the CPSC that it had performed this replacement as a solution to its range defect.

I propose that LG be ordered to stop producing and marketing all gas ranges in the United States until it can prove to CPSC that it has improved its design practices, its part supply practices, and its representation to CPSC and the American Public that it is indeed a safe company to deal with.

I also want CPSC to order LG to recall these ranges and redesign the valves for these ranges, all of them, not just mine.
justification: The incident involved the gas range igniting unexpectedly, but no injury or fire occurred due to quick action.

incident_description:
Bosch Built-in Oven/Microwave Combo was purchased March 2015 from Lowes in Cary, North Carolina. In May 2016, while the oven is turned OFF, the broiler came on by itself. The oven alerted (beep sounds) me, and when I touched the oven handle and panel, it was VERY VERY hot. I immediately turned the power breaker off to cut off any power to the oven. I left the oven OFF and immediately called BOSCH. BOSCH stated they would have an authorized dealer diagnose the issue. Initial dealer that investigated the issue stated it was the "communications board". He had asked me to turn the oven on to help him diagnose. He said I could use the oven, but "be careful". A few days later, more burning smell from the oven (I called the fire department) and cut off the power to the oven again. Fire department did not identify the cause of the smell. incident_description: My son was using the Tommee Tippee Sippee Cups for 8 months, from around 8 months of age until 16 months of age. We specifically chose this cup because we really enjoyed the baby bottles from the same brand and had read great reviews about the product. Unfortunately around 13 months of age, my son began to get sick very frequently. We would clean his play area, disinfect his dishes and cups, wash his bedding and still no change. He did not attend daycare and was not around any other children or adults who had been sick. After about a month of being sick with cold like symptoms, he came down with his first case of pneumonia which resulted in several trips to the doctor as well as the ER, inclusive of x-rays. Only one and half weeks after completing his antibiotics, my son contracted a second case of pneumonia which resulted in additional doctors visits, another trip to the ER and a second round of x-rays. Needless to say, it was a very scary and very difficult 3 months. My husband and I took turns sleeping each night to make sure our son was breathing and to watch his temperature as it rose to dangerous levels. We took time off work, tended to his every need and continued searching for the culprit. It wasn't until I came upon one mothers viral online post about her TTommee Tippee Sippee Cup and the mold issue, that I then considered these cups could be the problem. I had been cleaning and disinfecting his cups daily. I would hand wash them with soap, soak the lids with soap, rinse everything very well and hang it all to dry. My husband immediately cut open one of the valves from inside the Tommee Tippee Sippee Cup and sure enough we found mold! We had been rotating these two cups among his other cups, but these were the "go-to" and as it turned out, they were also the culprit. As soon as we disposed of the cups and had our son drinking from straw cups only, he began to get healthy. It has now been 4 solid months and he has not been sick once! I plan to take action against the company for not catching this flaw in their design. There is absolutely no way to properly sanitize these valves and many children have paid the price (both physically and financially) for the company's negligence. Even though we have fantastic insurance, I am still paying off those doctors and hospital visits which has resulted in thousands of dollars out of pocket. I would pay anything to get my son healthy, but he shouldn't have been sick in the first place.
justification: The child suffered from repeated pneumonia and required multiple medical interventions, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue appears to be a known design flaw affecting multiple children, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description:
Our home oven/range, about five years old, Whirlpool model GFG471LVS3 with serial number R20511768 is the probable cause of our [REDACTED] Carbon Dioxide alarm waking us at 04:45 on 13June2016. The oven and range had been used the evening before and all burners and the oven were in the off position when dinner was removed from the unit. 
The beeping of the alarm woke us at the above noted time, and my wife said that the range top, including the knobs in the front, were hot to the touch. The kitchen was extremely warm and the oven and all burners were in the OFF position. Upon opening the oven door, she felt as large rush of hot heat as the door was opened.
Our local fire department was called and the engine crew investigated, finding increased CO levels, and decreased oxygen levels. House was aired with opening windows and levels rechecked some time after being aired, and levels were within normal limits,  Oven and burners were turned on again, and although the oven was set to 350 degrees F, it went up to 400 when it was shut off, following the study of CO and Oxygen levels. At that time CO was once more elevated, and Oxygen lower.
Local gas company was asked to investigate. The man that visited from WPS agreed with the firemen that there was some type of glitch in a gas valve in the oven. We were advised not to use it, and to either repair or replace the range/oven unit. We have ordered a new stove and will not get another Whirlpool.
