incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range Model 790.9021: 
Range top burner controller fails and burner to jump to max heat while controller setting remains set at mid-range heat. It can be reset by turning controller to off position and then turning it back on to desired mid-range temperature. This behavior has continued over the last few months.
justification: The burner controller failure is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential hazard if not addressed.

incident_description:
Purchased Cuisinart DGB-700BC Grind-and-Brew 12-Cup Automatic Coffeemaker December 2015, this morning the machine was being used to make coffee as usual. After making the coffee it keeps the coffee pot warm, it appears the heating element may have shorted out and set fire to the other electrical components inside the machine.  The machine was on fire.

We took it outside immediately.

No injuries sustained.

The house still smells strongly of electrical smoke. 

Contacted Cuisinart today to request a replacement of a different model, am not confident that they will replace it as other reviews online state that they are unreasonable.  Many reviews online with this exact scenario. Scary.
justification: The coffeemaker caught fire but no injuries were sustained, and online reviews suggest this scenario is common.

incident_description:
The exterior glass door of my oven exploded.  I had warmed up potatoes and vegetables in a 350 degree oven.  My husband was cooking the remainder of the  meal on the grill outside.  He stated that the meat was taking longer to cook than expected and it would be a few more minutes.  I returned the vegetables to the oven to keep warm.  The oven was turned OFF at this point.
I turned to leave the kitchen and heard a very loud POP.  Followed by the sound of glass hitting the tile floor.  I honestly thought my husband may have walked through the closed glass sliding door.
The glass from the oven door was from one end of the kitchen to the other.  After the initial pop, the glass continued to crumble to the floor until all of the exterior glass was broken.
If a child had been in the room, or if I had been bent down removing plates from the warming drawer, serious injury would have occurred.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass door exploding, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such events are not common.

incident_description: Heating element did not shut off in dishwasher. Melted items. Caught and turned off fuse to prevent further damage.
justification: The heating element malfunction caused damage to items but was caught before injury occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore elite model# 795.77543600 Refrigerator by Sears Roebuck.

Interior light does not turn off when the doors are shut. Due to this the light box and the cover melted causing fire hazard. I have called Sears and was told to report this to your agency.

To avoid fire, I have removed the light bulbs from the light box. 

There has been similar complaints about Kenmore elite refrigerators in the past. I found out about these when I searched solution for my case. Looks like Sears went to consumer's house and fixed the problem without a charge.

I would like Consumer Product Safety to mandate Sears to fix my refrigerator interior light problem asap.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard due to a malfunctioning light, but no injury or death has occurred. The likelihood is high given past similar complaints and the potential for fire if not addressed.

incident_description: The glass door spontaneously shattered and covered my kitchen floor with a million pieces of glass.  I checked online and found MANY complaints about the Kenmore ovens from Sears doing this...this should absolutely be a recall.  I bought this house 2 years ago and the appliances are only a few years old...now I have to buy a new oven.
justification: The glass door shattered, posing a potential injury risk, but no injury was reported in the description.

incident_description:
I had owned the machine for about 8 months and had used it many times without incident. On this occasion, I pumped the machine as stated in the instructions 3 times but it did not buzz as it had in the past.  I pumped it two more time and it still did not buzz.   
I started to remove the bottle as per the instructions and it exploded like a bomb severing my dominant right hand between the thumb and forefinger.  The gash was so deep and open that you could see down  to the bone.  Shards of the thick plastic bottle went flying a significant distance and I was very lucky that my 10 year old daughter standing a few feet away was not injured. 
My husband who was in the room at the time rushed me to the ER.  Due to the severe trauma to the bone and tissue, I was told that emergency surgery needed  to be performed within the next two days so as to not lose use of my hand or thumb.
Soda stream refuses to take responsibility for the malfunction of the machine.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury requiring emergency surgery, but no death occurred.

incident_description: The oven portion of the smooth top Frigidaire Crown (model FEFB65ASC) spontaneously came on by itself and would not shutoff with the button on the unit. The hazard was contained by de-energizing the entire unit by manually tripping the circuit breaker and removing the power source. Incident occurred during the day when home owner was nearby and alert (not sleeping); Otherwise, the incident could have caused structural damage or harm to personal health. I was notified by representative of Frigidaire at the 1-888-360-8556 that this defective unit was not part of an existing recall for models with similar issues.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but was contained without injury, though it had potential for harm.

incident_description: On the morning of 06/03/16 the outer glass on the oven door of our 7 month old GE 30" Free-Standing Electric Range unexpectedly shattered.  At the time the oven had not been used for approximately 12 hours.  Prior to this there was no evidence of physical damage to the door.
justification: The oven door glass shattered unexpectedly, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
Pan is labeled "Zwilling Henckels Gas Ceran Halogen electro induction 18/10 Stainless Steel 3 ply material made in Vietnam."

While cooking zucchinis one of the rivets holding the handle on exploded, with a loud report, sending the cap of the rivet across the room at high velocity, like  a bullet. Fortunately no one was injured. 

I'd guess water got inside of it, turned to steam when the pan was heated, exploding the top of the rivet. 

I can provide a photograph.
justification: The incident involved a rivet exploding with high velocity, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
(4/15/16) The consumer's husband used the right front burner for about 15 minutes, at a heat level of 4. The consumer's husband then turned the knob to the "Off" position but the burner failed to turn off and got even more red/ hotter. The consumer's husband then shut off the circuit breaker. The consumer's husband waited for about an hour and then he turned the circuit breaker back on. When the consumer's husband walked back in the kitchen he noticed the right front burner was cherry red and noticed sparks under the glass and near the control panel. The consumer's husband then pulled the range out from the wall and unplugged it. 

(4/15/16) The consumer then searched online and came across recall # 09-333. The consumer confirmed that her model and serial # was included in the recall.

(4/18/16) The consumer contacted the firm's recall hotline (888-360-8556) and informed the Rep. (name unknown) about the incident. The consumer was advised that the range was recalled and they would order the parts to repair the range (per the recall remedy). The consumer asked the Rep. if the firm would repair any other parts damaged from the incident and the Rep. told the consumer that they would not cover damages from the incident or anything outside the remedy. The consumer asked the Rep. why she was never notified about the recall and the Rep. said that they called the consumer to notify her about the recall. The consumer states this is a lie. The consumer said the next time she called the firm another Rep. (name unknown) said they sent the consumer a letter to notify her about the recall, however, the consumer said she never received a letter.

The consumer states that the parts arrived at her home on 4/26/16. The consumer states that the technician was supposed to arrive on 4/29/16 but they called to reschedule the repair to 5/2/16.

(5/2/16) The technician examined the range and conducted the repairs per the recall (repaired the switches and control unit). The technician advised the consumer that the dual heating element was damaged but that it was not covered under the recall and he could not repair it. The consumer called the firm and spoke with [REDACTED], a supervisor and she told the consumer that the technician is only authorized to conduct repairs under the recall. The consumer was advised that the technician would need to call the firm to explain the subsequent damages then get transferred to Support for further guidance. [REDACTED] told the consumer that the firm has not been covering any subsequent damages outside the recall. 

The consumer said there are no prior incidents.

The consumers had to pay all damages to their stove because of what the recall caused when it "the stove" failed to turn off.

Frigidaire refused to reimburse the consumers of any of the over $400 they had to pay to repair the damages cause by the recall part.  That's a nice rip off scam Frigidaire has going on
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that posed a fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: I was baking a potato in my GE gas range.  The oven has been in the home since 1992.  I went in the other room to read a magazine and then heard a loud boom and glass breaking.  I went into the kitchen to see that my oven door had exploded.  The glass was still popping on the ground even after the explosion.  Thankfully I was waiting until my potato was closer to being ready before finishing the rest of the meal, or I would have been standing directly in front  of the oven.  The glass exploded pretty far, I am also thankful that my dog was not injured by the glass. Contacted GE, they sent a technician.  Technician said "you got twice the life out of the unit." It still works but we don't have the glass available, and we can't offer anything on a new one.
justification: The oven door exploded, but no injuries occurred to the person or the dog, and the incident was isolated.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool over the range Microwave model GH7155XHS-1, Serial Number: FGP4127833, that starts on its own and continues to run.  I had to unplug it to turn it off.  It seems to generate heat in the inside of the microwave intermittently.  I have very concerned about it starting a fire if I am not at home.
justification: The microwave starting on its own and generating heat intermittently poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
We bought a GE Cafe Gas Cooktop in May 2015 and had an issue within a month; the unit was replaced by the store we purchased from. A few months later, we started to see some weird things happening to the Cooktop and one day my wife was about to get burn and hurt from high flames and big explosion from one of the burner causing the burner top to fly and hit and damaged the hood and the back splash and half the burner areas to turn black.
We contacted GE and a technician was dispatched to look at. The tech looked at it and order some parts and advised me to contact GE Customer Service since it has safety issues. I contacted GE Customer Service and they told me to speak with the GE Safety Department due to the nature of the issue. And, that is where I started to get a run around. The service call ticket was closed and they refused to take any actions.
I posted my comments on GE's Facebook and they were all removed by GE.
justification: The incident involved high flames and an explosion that could have caused injury, though no actual injury was reported. The issue was recurring but not frequent, as it happened twice over several months.

incident_description: I was heating water for tea in the morning when I was shocked.  I put my hand outside of the heating element base to secure the base while lifting the pot of heated water off the base to pour into mugs.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock but no reported injury, and such occurrences are possible with improper handling of heating elements.

incident_description: On Tuesday, May 31, 2016 at approximately 8:15pm I heard a loud pop coming from the kitchen.  When I investigated the sound I found the bottom window of my double over had exploded sending glass all over the kitchen.
justification: The oven window exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: After making salsa in a Ninja kitchen blender, model NJ600 (not included in your recall) I removed the lid and began pouring the contents into a bowl I was holding in my left hand. The blade assembly fell from the blender onto my thumb, causing a sever laceration that severed the extensor tendon. Urgent care sutured the cut and referred me to a hand surgeon. I just spent six weeks in a splint to see if the tendon would repair itself without the need for surgery. I have limited use of the thumb at this point and a determination about surgery is pending.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration and tendon damage requiring medical intervention and potential surgery, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: My little boy was using these Tommee Tippee cups and I saw an article online a few months ago so decided to cut one of my inserts open and sure enough there was mold growing in it and I had only been using it right around 6 months. I contacted Tommee Tippee and they said they could send me new inserts but I said I wanted new cups so didn't get anything.
justification: Mold was found in the cup insert, but no injury was reported. The issue is likely to occur given the description of mold growth after 6 months of use.

incident_description: I purchased 2 Tommee Tippee Sippee cups in March of 2016. After a few uses and washes I noticed water or milk would be stuck on the inside valve after both hands asking as well as running it through the dishwasher. I would have to pound it on the side of the sink to release some of the moisture. At one point milk had curdled inside the valve and came out in a chunk after being run through the dishwasher. At this point I threw both cups away.
justification: The incident describes a product issue with no reported injury or harm, only inconvenience and disposal of the cups.

incident_description: When we bought our first transitions tommee tippee sippee cup we took it home and boiled all the pieces first thing . We took them out and let them air dry . Then once more hand washed them . I then served his milk in the tommee tippee sippee cup. Once finished I rinsed the cup and hand washed the cup . I set the product out to air dry. Once air dried I stored in the cabinet for next use . The next feeding came around I pulled the sippee cup out to begin to fix his milk and the cup had a HORRIBLE smell . I began to look in the cup and the valve had mold all over it ! I did not use the product at that time anymore. I simply set the cup aside. A big disappointment for his first sippee cup.
justification: Mold in the sippee cup poses a health risk but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I started purchasing your Tommee Tippee Sippee spill-proof cups when my daughter turned about 6 months old. I first saw mold claims on facebook. After opening the white piece under the lid I found mold in mine as well. It didn't seems to be as bad as the ones pictured on facebook but any amount of mold is bad for a small child.
justification: Mold was found in the product, posing a potential health risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Outer glass of Whirlpool microwave spontaneously exploded. Unit was not in use, no one was in the room, and the unit had not been used in a week. Unit was plugged in.
justification: The microwave glass exploded but no one was present, resulting in property damage without injury.

incident_description: This range is located in our rental property and was being used by our tenent.  He was using top of electric kitchen range when the outer glass on the oven door suddenly popped and burst into tiny shreds of glass.  Oven was not in use.  no injuries
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass bursting, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Tommee Tippee Sippee Spill-Proof Cups
The white removable spill proofer grew mold inside and made my son sick.
justification: The incident resulted in the child getting sick, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: Tommie tippee cup was recalled die to mold and my son has really bad allergies.
justification: The recall due to mold exposure and the mention of severe allergies indicate potential for injury, but no explicit harm is confirmed.

incident_description: The sippy cup I bought had mold on the inside of the detachable thing after it was used several times
justification: Mold presence indicates an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We turned our GE Profile dishwasher on to wash dishes.  About halfway through the cycle, smoke started coming out of the top of the dishwasher, along with a very bad burning plastic/electric smell.  We immediately stopped the dishwasher cycle by opening the door and the smoke continued coming out and smelled very bad.  We called an appliance repairman who told us to immediately turn the breaker off for the dishwasher, because the top panel electric display was still on and showing lights indicating time elapsed in the wash cycle.  We did this and let the smoke dissipate, and determined it had been coming out of the top control panel.  We are going to replace the dishwasher with GE rebate due to recall.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death, and such electrical faults in appliances are uncommon but not rare.

incident_description:
(05/09/2016) The consumer stated that the outer glass of the oven door exploded. The oven was set for 350 but had not reached 350 degrees. Less than five minutes later, the glass door exploded.

(05/09/2016) The consumer contacted Maytag Service. She was advised that the oven is out of warranty and the consumer was responsible for the replacement of glass.
justification: The oven door glass exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
05/01/2016 - The consumer indicates that she was cooking in the oven for approximately twenty minutes. When the consumer went to check on her food and started to open the oven door, its outside glass exploded. The consumer turned the oven off and cleaned the shattered glass that was all over her kitchen floor. Fortunately, the consumer was not injured. 

05/02/2016 - The consumer contacted the retailer and they referred her to CPSC.

The consumer plans on keeping the unit for at least the next thirty days.

The consumer states that she had prior issues with the oven door handle coming off but this was addressed by the consumer herself by tightening the bolt.
justification: The oven door glass exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I have the tommee tippee spill proof cup that is being recalled for mold in the white valve. I had notice ever time I would clean the cups that water would still be in the valve and there would be a smell. I had stopped using the cups. I am so glad I seen this recall on the Today show.
justification: The incident involves a recalled product with mold issues, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore elite double wall oven purchased from sears 7 years ago.  The other day I was baking bread and heard a pop didn't pay much attention.   I returned to the oven to take the bread out noticed a thin line was running across the very bottom of my oven glass door.  

I hoped to see a recall but WOW nothing.  I will be calling sears to see what can be done but WHY would tempered glass crack.  Oh, and I am the only one using the oven so excuses on what I could have done will not work.
justification: The incident involved a cracked oven glass door with no reported injury or harm, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: Feeling sick for days: burning eyes, sore throat, coughing, headaches, fatigue. Thought it was pollen, allergies. Then tried to turn on super boiler burner on LG gas RANGE but middle burner came on instead and I couldn't' turn it off. It stayed on  no mater what I did. It was Sunday so called gas company. Took hours but when they finally came said gas leak in stove and turned off gas. Took 2 days for repairman to come. He checked for leaks but showed me that all 5 knobs had a plastic part cracked that made it impossible to turn any of the burners off completely. It cost $450 for replacement knobs and they are made of the same cheap plastic part that is very vulnerable to cracking and resulting in same hazard. This is a $1900 stove. I was sickened by the fumes, but could have died from breathing these fumes. This knob design flaw is a fire, explosion, injury hazard and should be recalled immediately. Researching replacement knobs, I literally read hundreds of this same complaint on a dozen sites. When I called LG to express my concerns all they would do was give me a number for a business that has been trained to fix their product. All they cared about it their profits.
justification: The incident involved exposure to gas fumes causing sickness, which qualifies as an injury, and the design flaw poses a recurring hazard.

incident_description: On March 4 2016 I purchased a tea kettle from AMAZON.com,but I didn't use it till few days ago when this incident occur.I boiled water for hot tea,and when poured the water from the kettle the lid came out,and whole steam blow on my hand,making burn mark ,and last night same thing happened again with my wife.She burned the whole hand,we both got marks on the hands.We got pictures to proofed.The product doesn't have any safety  direction ,or safety device.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to both the user and their wife, indicating an injury severity. The recurrence of the incident suggests a likely occurrence due to the product's lack of safety features.

incident_description:
We purchased our Jen air dual-fuel stove in 2008 At the time of purchase we were very excited to have the dual-fuel option, and to have a smaller oven on the top- so we did not mind spending the $$$$ on what we thought would be a great stove.  Within the first 6 months of using the stove we noticed the glass windows of the oven doors were getting dirty with food remnants, and spills - there is no way to clean inside the doors. They are sealed in such a way that you can not get any normal cleaning utensil in there to clean.This can get pretty unsightly.  After having the stove for about a year, one night after washing dishes- we put a wet pot on top of one of the burners. ( burners are off) all of a sudden all of the burners started to make a clicking sound, about every second. We could see all five burners flickering along with the noise. We could not get it to stop, so we unplugged the stove to get it to stop.  About a year later the noise happened again, this time there was no water involved. Again had to unplug the stove to make it stop. Then year 3 of having the stove..RUST!  Wow, after three years there is rust on the front of the bigger oven. This really compliments the incredibly gross glass door.
Now, going on year 8 of having the stove, I am steaming corn on the right burner - also have chicken cooking in the over. I turn off the burner with the corn, within a few seconds clicking noise starts. I turn the burner back on and then shut it off to see if would make it stop. Still the clicking noise every second -then all of a sudden every half second. Then sparks shooting out the sides of the stove top - a lot of them!  I saw a flame burst under the burner and did not hesitate for a second to grab the fire exsinguisher and blast it. .. There goes dinner. And the stove! We want this out of the house. Completely Unsafe!! Seems like this could of just randomly happened! 
There a more than  just a few reviews on similar issues with this stove - and some people are wanting to get it fixed ?  This is a horrible model. Should absolutely get recalled.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a flame burst, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Cooking pea soup, Left front burner was set to 1.8. after an hour soup started boiling. Found burner glowing red like on hi setting. hit the stop button to shut burner off and it stayed on.
Had to turn off breaker in panel that feeds the range. Tried it the next day by restoring power, same thing, burner on high.
justification: The burner malfunctioned and remained on high despite attempts to turn it off, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Last evening the oven door on our Maytag Range exploded into a million pieces all over the kitchen. The oven was not on at the time. Our son was heating something on a burner on low heat.  Our 4 hear old grandson had just left the kitchen. Thank God no one was injured.  I immediately called Maytag. Their response was, it's out of warranty. I told they they needed to do something.  They said they would send someone out to look at it but it would cost about $120.00. I told them I shouldn't have to pay for them to have someone look at something that could have injured us. I then went online and found over 300 complaints from people with the same experience with Maytag, [REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED] and all claimed the company would try to make it their fault. Like they bunped it or dropped something on it. This cannot be allowed to continue. You must do something to help consumers.  We are in our 70's and have paid over $700. for this range and cannot afford to buy a new one. These manufacturers need to be held responsible for these dangerous incidents and replace the faulty stoves.  They need to rethink the way they are making them in order that they not pose a safety hazard for unsuspecting consumers. Thank you for any help you can give.
justification: The oven door exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm. The presence of over 300 similar complaints suggests the occurrence is likely.

incident_description: A frying pan with sauteed cooked vegetables was on the Kenmore right front burner. I moved it to the back left burner and turned the heat to low, then pushed the simmer button. After that there was a HUGE bang/pop and a flash of light with a burnt smell. I felt the electrical charge and immediately turned off all the burners. I think it It blew the circuitry for the stove. After doing some research online, I found out that this is a common problem for Kenmore ranges. In looking at the back of the stove, there is some soot behind and over the front of the control board.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang, flash, and electrical charge but no injury, and the problem is described as common for Kenmore ranges.

incident_description:
(4/14/16) The consumer set the dishwasher to a wash cycle. Approximately an hour later the consumer walked in the kitchen to feed her dogs and noticed smoke coming from the door handle. The consumer also noticed a burn odor. The consumer believes the dishwasher had finished the cycle. The consumer opened the door and noticed black smoke coming from inside. There wasn't any water inside, near the bottom. The consumer then shut off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer went online and came across recall # 12-244 but her serial # does not fall within the recall. The consumer plans to contact the firm.

There are no prior incidents. 

The consumer indicated that she uses the dishwasher daily.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burn odor but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The dishwasher is used daily, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: When using food dehydrator for one day, the trays melted model FD1005wHGenB RONCO BRAND
justification: The incident involved melting trays in a food dehydrator, which is a malfunction but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
(04/11/2016) The consumer stated that the unit was not in use. He was getting ready to heat up something. As he walked toward the unit, the outer door of the microwave exploded. 


(04/11/2016) The consumer called the firm to advised them of the unit. A report was taken and the consumer was given  a ticket number [REDACTED].

There were no injuries.
justification: The microwave door exploded, but there were no injuries reported.

incident_description:
(05/11/2016) The consumer stated that the coffee maker was not turned on but been used earlier in the morning.  When the consumer's wife went to reheat the left over coffee, which should have been cold, she found out that the coffee maker had never turned off. The coffee maker should go off automatically. His wife unplugged the unit and plugged it back in. There was an error code of 04. The unit was unplugged and plugged in again three times. The consumer got the same error message.

(05/12/2016) The consumer contacted the GE but was advised that there was nothing that they could do because the model was not included in the recall.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned but no injury or harm occurred, only inconvenience and a minor operational issue.

incident_description:
Rival toaster was placed on kitchen counter and plugged into the wall, subject walked across the kitchen to get something, when they turned around to walk back over to the toaster, the toaster on fire with flames coming out of the top. Subject immediately unplugged the toaster and safely put out the fire. Thankfully no injuries were obtained and the fire did not spread. If the subject would not have been in the same room immediately after plugging the toaster in, or the toaster was left plugged in prior, this fire would have consumed the residence and lead to a total loss for a family of 6, as all other family members were at work and school. 
Locally their was a house fire last year in which lead to a total loss for another family, which was caused by the same toaster. The local Fire Commissioner was contacted and he confirmed that it was the same toaster as ours, the Rival, and they reported the incident through the Consumer Product Safety Commission.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, and the fire was quickly contained without spreading.

incident_description: I purchased a home with the GeminiÃÂ® 30" Double Oven Freestanding Gas Range by Maytag in it two years. I have used this range without incident until yesterday. I baked and turned the oven off upon leaving the house. When I returned a hour later the lower oven was on full blast and the entire unit was too hot to touch - almost red hot. It would not turn off despite hitting cancel multiple times. I called my handyman who had to use hot pads and rags to pull it from the wall and unplug it. When plug back in the lower oven heats rapidly to a high temp. The wall, counters and surrounding areas were warm to touch. it took 15+ minutes for unit to cool. I'm so lucky I came back when I did - it def would have caused a fire. My handyman guessed the control unit was bad but why it comes on when not prompted is a mystery and incredibly dangerous. I'm wondering if others have had this problem and if there is a recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I preheated my oven to 450 degrees.  I put a Pyrex Amethyst Glass baking dish with a breast of chicken in the oven for approximately 12 minutes.  When I went to check on the chicken's temperature, I used a pot holder in each hand and as I was taking it out of the oven the glass shattered into hundreds (maybe thousands) of tiny shards.  There were large pieces of glass left in the oven.  Nothing was left in my hands and the pot holders had many tiny shards of glass.  Glass went everywhere.  I was in shock and didn't realize until minutes later that my toe was bleeding.  (It wasn't a serious cut.)   I'm very conscientious in the kitchen and this was a disturbing incident.  I'm hesitant/scared to ever cook with glass again.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (bleeding toe) and significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but can happen under specific conditions.

incident_description: Kenmore/Frigidaire/Electrolux wall oven door model #790.48803100.  We have had a pane of glass on the wall oven COMPLETELY shatter.  When it happened, it was during cooking of normal routine.  A loud pop and there was glass shattered all over the floor while the oven was still going.  There is obviously some kind of structural weakness within these glass panes of this specific line of oven doors.  This is a SERIOUS hazard as anyone could have been standing in front of the oven when it burst.  There have been multiple reports by other consumers (example: please check [REDACTED] in your files) with the same incident occurring and the similar refusal of SEARS/KENMORE/FRIGIDAIRE/ELECTROLUX to do anything about it besides try to sell everyone an extra warranty and overcharge to fix the part.  This is outrageous and a serious issue which these companies are ignoring.  I have taken pictures of the oven door with shattered glass if needed.  I urge you, our government entity, to help myself as well as many others with this ongoing issue.
justification: The incident involves a shattered oven door glass during normal use, posing a serious hazard with potential for injury, though no injury was reported in this specific case. Multiple similar reports indicate this is a recurring issue.

incident_description:
Not too long ago we experienced a faulty light in the refrigerator compartment. Sears came out and replaced the fixture AND replaced the master control panel on the back. This was necessary because on our arrival home we discovered the melted lighting fixture and warm food inside our refrigerator, any longer and a fire would have been inevitable.
The other day, we opened our freezer door to experience the top drawer slide snap apart and collapse the drawer. The freezer bulb blows out frequently, with unknown reason. In addition, the plastic guides on the drawers inside the refrigerator have also failed.

Tried again to start the dishwasher but it was dead.

circuit board had caught fire during the night.

Transistor Q2 appeared to have failed as it was scorched.

The cable harnesses to the circuit board were melted.

The circuit board was severely burnt, both front and back.

The flexible ribbon cable that passed underneath the board had melted and 2 of its metal traces had fused themselves to the plastic circuit board enclosure and burned right through it.

Molten plastic had dripped down to the bottom of the plastic casing and left a plume of soot upwards and throughout the top of the casing.

I presume that the dishwasher's thermal cutoff (located in an opening on the top side of the plastic circuit board casing) had sensed the heat from the fire and cut the power to the dishwasher before the fire spread.

After opening the dishwasher to investigate, the kitchen was filled with an acrid burning plastic smell that lasted several days.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher's circuit board, but no injury or death occurred, and the thermal cutoff prevented further damage.

incident_description:
On Thursday, March 17th, my family and I began to cook dinner. We decided to make a sauce using our Cuisinart Food Processor model DLC - 5. We usually use our food processor when preparing dinner. While we blended up our sauce, one that we've made several times before, our processor began to make a sharp thumping noise. We stopped it, checked it, didn't see anything unusual, and tried it again. It made the sound again, so we shut it off to check around the machine and at the sauce inside. The sauce looked blended so we proceeded on with dinner. 

After dinner, we took the bowl off the processor off the base and as we went to clean it, we found a dark object in the bottom mixed in with leftover sauce. As we pulled it out, we realized that it was a piece of the S blade. When we pulled out the blade to look it over, we realized that on the bottom of the blade there are several rivets to hold the blade on. The blade had cracked along the thin edging where the rivets were. The piece we had identified in the bottom of our food processor bowl, mixed in with our food, was a piece that had broken off between two of the rivets. The sharp thumping sound we had heard, has been identified as the sound the blade was making as it spun around loose inside our food. It caused scratches and a huge dent inside the plastic of the processor bowl. 

At any point during our meal, this metal blade could have been consumed by our family, including our young children. The blade between the rivets can crack and break off and is extremely dangerous. We, as consumers, had no idea that was even possible. 

I contacted the company in April and did not hear back. I contacted the company again May 12th and we've exchanged many emails. The customer service is terrible. It takes about a day to get replies and every reply is from someone different so the emails are not cohesive. In one of the last emails, they told me I'd have to buy a replacement blade. I refused, because I don't believe we are at fault and we should not have to replace it. I also, do not want a blade with rivets on the bottom now, knowing the danger it poses to our family. 

Today, May 16th, I called customer service. It says in their emails that when you call, they will not know about the emails. As I explained my situation, the customer service representative said "So what do you want us to do about it?". When I told her I'd like my food processor replaced with one that does not have rivets on the bottom of the blade. She told me they couldn't do that, they could only replace the blade. She offered no remorse or apology. I asked to speak with a supervisor. She informed me that due to the volume of calls, she'd need to take my name and number and I would have to wait for a customer service supervisor to call me in 24 hours. 

Their Facebook page is full of negative feedback and other products that have broken or become dangerous, including a coffee pot that burst into flames. Many posts have not gotten any responses from customer service. This is a terrible way to conduct service. 

When I googled " Cuisinart Food Processor Blade Breaking" I came across many webpages with people that are dealing with the same situation for various models. It's extremely dangerous. I hope that you can help, since the company is unwilling to protect people.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade in food, posing a risk of injury if consumed, and similar issues are reported by others, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
My Bosch dishwasher stopped working; the control panel would not light up.   I opened up the dishwasher's junction box and discovered evidence of a fire: the central plastic component had burnt and partially melted;  insulation on the wires had burnt out and there was soot in the box.

I had a Bosch technician visit and he indicated that one of the supply wires was loose, even through the screw which clamps the wire had been fully tightened.   

Bosch blamed this as an installation error and wants to charge me for repairs.  I do not agree and am continuing to escalate with them.

Upon close inspection of the junction box, the root cause of the problem appears to be a design flaw which allows the supply wire to be slipped into its receptacle *outside* the clamp that is supposed to hold it.   (The clamp is a tiny piece of metal in the receptacle which moves when a screw is tightened.)   Therefore an installer would tighten the screw and get the impression that the supply cable is being held in place firmly, when in fact it remains loose.  The loose contact then causes the wire to overheat, causing a fire.

The symptoms match the junction box problem that's been widely reported online and has been the subject of a recall.  However my dishwasher model is not included in that recall, and it appears that the root cause has not been fixed.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a design flaw, but no injury or death was reported. The likelihood is high as the issue is widely reported and matches known problems.

incident_description:
Hello,

I purchased Ninja BL770 from Best Buy in November 2015. While the product is very good. The serious design flaw is that the blade can fall out while emptying the blended/processed contents from the jug.  This is because the blade is not locked into place. I understand that it is expected that the consumer removes the blade before emptying. We have been using the Ninja BL770 for 5 months now and every time the blade falls out. Twice now it has caused injuries because the blade falls on the thumb or finger. Today the blade fell out and caused a deep gash on my thumb. I had to use 2 bottles of hydrogen peroxide and 1 bottle of isopropyl alcohol to contain the bleeding. While the would is deep it cannot be stitched due to its location. 
This is a very serious flaw in the design of this product that the blade is not locked and can fall out. For years the blender industry has trained its users with locked blades - while it is possible to get accustomed to "unlocked" blades from Ninja, I worry that users like me are getting injured while using this product. 

Thank you
justification: The incident describes a deep gash requiring medical attention, indicating injury (severity 3). The blade falls out frequently, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
While preheating our Frigidaire Gallery Smooth top Electric Range ( Model #FGE3055MWD, Serial #VF32487149) at 4:00 pm, on Friday, March 4, 2016, to 400 degrees, in less than 2 minutes (did not even finish preheating ) we heard a sudden loud amp type noise then a louder pop and saw flames burst in the oven.

The flames filled the oven and were seen through the glass window of the oven door. We feared that the flames were going to crack the glass window of the oven door and spread throughout the kitchen. 
But before we could call the Fire Department, the 220 line tripped off and the flames slowly began to diminish in the oven. We did not open the oven door, but smoke and a burning smell filled our home. To be safe we also unplugged the oven.

**See Attached Sheet with complete Incident Report information and a copy of the sales receipt.

Currently, we own a Frigidaire Gallery Smooth top Electric Range Oven. On Friday, March 4, 2016 at 4:00pm, while preheating the oven, we heard a sudden loud amp type noise then a louder pop and saw flames burst in the oven. The incident happened 2 minutes after turning the oven on (did not even finish preheating).

The flames filled the oven and were seen through the glass window of the oven door. We feared that the flames were going to crack the glass window of the oven door and spread throughout the kitchen.
But before we could call the Fire Department, the 220 line tripped off and the flames slowly began to diminish in the oven. We did not open the oven door, but smoke and a burning smell filled our home. To be safe we also unplugged the stove.

It was a miracle that no one was burnt and the kitchen walls were fine. A family member was just about to place a cookie sheet in the oven.
If they had just a minute prior, they would have been severely burnt as they opened the oven door when the flames burst.

After several minutes I called B & B Appliance where we had purchased our range on June 30, 2013, and spoke to [REDACTED] about our oven fire in our Frigidaire Range (Model # FGEF3055MWD, Serial# VF32487149) to see if they could help us. [REDACTED] at B & B Appliance referred us to Frigidaire Customer Service (888 451-7007) and told us to call her back on Monday morning and let her know what happens.

I immediately called the Frigidaire Customer Service Representative and was told by [REDACTED], that there was nothing they could do for us because there was no extended warranty and no recall on our specific Frigidaire model. I was asked if I would like to purchase a one-year warranty on the rang, but the new warranty would not cover the previous fire.

I explained that the extended warranty should not apply to a defective Frigidaire range. 

But I was told that if I wanted Frigidaire to sent a repairman to check out our faulty range that we would be responsible for the total cost of the service call and repair.

I told them that I did not want a defective range repaired that had a severe electrical fire, only inspected and service fee covered by Frigidaire so that they could document the fire in their Frigidaire Gallery Smooth top Electric Range Series and warn other consumers who own this specific model of the potentialdanger of an electrical fire.

I got nowhere.

On Monday, March 7, 2016 I called B & B {216 261-5600) and asked for [REDACTED] but my call was taken by sales representative, [REDACTED], and was told that there was nothing that they could do since the range is over a year old, but he could file a report with Frigidaire. In our telephone conversation he stated, "I was aware of a problem with the heating element in Frigidaire electric ovens. (This information was never disclosed when my husband and I were purchasing a Frigidaire range from B & B Appliance.) I will call Frigidaire for you and see what I could do."

On Tuesday morning, at 9:00am, [REDACTED] called me at home and said, "I opened a file# [REDACTED] on your model with Frigidaire Customer Service and without an extended warranty, you are responsible for all service calls and repairs."

I again called Frigidaire Customer Service and spoke with [REDACTED] with the hope of getting our oven inspected without a service fee, but she refused to take responsibility for building and manufacturing a faulty product and not caring about the electrical fire hazard and safety and wellbeing of their customers. I was unable to speak with her supervisor or anyone else regarding this matter.

After researching Frigidaire ranges after our fire, I found below a link with reviews of many consumers who have had the same dangerous problem with their Frigidaire ranges:

https://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/frigidaire range.html

I had no success with Frigidaire Customer Service (800 944-9044), just as all of the consumers at the above link have reported.

I would greatly appreciate your help with getting this problem of a manufactured defect resolved with our Frigidaire Gallery Range.

Respectfully submitted, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved flames and potential danger, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
On Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2015, I was cooking a turkey, ham and several casseroles at 350.      
 I was using a relatively new Pyrex 10 x 15 pan (purchased at Fred Meyers) for the bread 
stuffing. About 25 minutes into putting it into the oven, I smelled food burning. Opened up the 
oven to discover that the Pyrex baking dish had exploded, scattering glass shards of every size 
throughout  the oven, on top of the other uncovered food, and down into the crevices of the gas 
vents. The entire dinner was ruined since glass is not a recommended dietary component.
Cost of food lost for Thanksgiving dinner and having to replace food, as well as a new baking dish, 
is $220.
The product clearly did not meet the standard of care. I emailed the broken dish, stuffing  and 
all, to World Kitchen (Pyrex) as requested along with documentation and photos. Not surprisingly, I 
have heard NOTHING from these people.
What should be most concerning to the State of Oregon attorney general and to the corporate 
officers of Fred Meyers (because all claims are denied by WK), is that the explosion and 
penetration  into other nearby foodstuffs posed a tremendously serious health and safety risk to 
individuals.

After nearly 2 months of stalling and hearing nothing from WK, I began to research similar 
incidents and found that PYREX dishes quite commonly explode  - and injure - people now that the 
company has switched to using soda-lime glass instead of borosilicate, as had been used for years.

I want the cost of my food reimbursed and the cost of purchasing another baking dish -- a safe one. 
And I want you to notify consumers about this incredible danger that PYREX poses -- too many of us 
think of the old Pyrex product and don't realize the newer ones are NOT THE SAME!
justification: The incident involved property damage and food contamination but no reported injuries, and similar incidents are described as common.
