incident_description:
I purchased a G.E. Profile Dishwasher approximately 2006. Have had no problems with it till a few days ago ( 4/23/2016) . Woke up in the morning to find the dishwasher heating element never turned off from previous evenings wash. There was no fire, the surrounding area was very HOT. I went online  to see how to fix the problem. Where i discovered that the G.E. Profile dishwasher had multiple recalls for the same problem i am having. The heating element not turning off. My dishwasher model #PDW928ONOOSS and serial # FM718154B did not show up on the recall list. I find this very disconcerting when in fact it is the same problem i am having with with dishwasher. I have not yet notified G.E. of the problem for the fact that since its not on recall list they will be less than helpful.
I realize it's about 10 years old , but up to now its been a reliable product. It's not safe to use and i do not want to put money into product that has recall issues.
justification: The heating element malfunctioned but did not cause a fire or injury, only creating a hot environment.

incident_description: Viking range griddle turned on by itself and the cutting board on top caught  on fire. Smoke and fire damage to the area.
justification: The incident caused fire and smoke damage but no injuries or deaths were mentioned.

incident_description:
The Microhearth Grill Pan for Microwave Cooking sold by Amazon.com can catch fire. I purchased one in March and used it a few times over 3 days, always following directions. The lip around the lid caught fire, which is made of plastic. Again I follow instructions to the letter. I posted a review with pictures, and if you look at other reviews other people have had it catch fire. I contacted Amazon, but that was weeks ago and this product is still being sold by them.

This is the product url:  http://www.amazon.com/Microhearth-Grill-Pan-Microwave-Cooking/dp/B004FGAVEK/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1461174258&sr=8-1&keywords=microhearth+grill

I also posted a review here with pictures: http://www.amazon.com/gp/customer-reviews/RHR9AETCZF79P/ref=cm_cr_getr_d_rvw_ttl?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B004FGAVEK
justification: The grill pan catching fire is a significant incident, but there is no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she and her husband started feeling sick about two weeks ago. They would get severe headache, muscle weakness, nausea, vomiting and dizziness. The consumer's husband also had a high fever.

The consumer could smell propane gas in the over after she would use the oven to bake. On 4/7/16, the consumer was baking and strong propane gas fumes filled the house. The consumer had to ventilate the and leave the area for a bit.

The consumer contacted Sears right away. They sent out a technician on 4/8/16. The technician identified the problem to the ignitor and regulator. The technician stated that the oven does not ignite after pre-heat and leaks a lot of gas during that time. The consumer was informed that the unit was igniting after releasing a lot of gas and that could have cause an - the consumer believes he said it could have been very bad. The  technician ordered a new regulator and ignitor. The consumer is supposed to receive the parts this week.

The technician is returning back on 4/15/16 to install the new parts. The technician informed the consumer that they can continue using the stove top. The consumer was not comfortable using the stove top and cut off all gas to the unit.

The consumer had a 225 gallons of propane gas deliver on 3/21/16. The consumer stated that the supply usually lasts at least 2 months. Instead, within 3 weeks, the propane gas was completely empty when they checked on 4/10/16.

The consumer and her husband are feeling better after cutting of the gas to the unit.

The consumer has a master protection plan so there was no charge for any of the service or parts. 

The consumer's unit appears to be included in recall # 15-142 but for different hazard than the one that they experienced.

4/15/2016  Technician replaced regulator and ignitor.  This did not fix problem so he ordered a BakeBurner and setup an appointment for 4/20/2016.

4/20/2016  Technician replaced the BakeBurner.  He showed the consumers the new BakeBurner was different than the original BakeBurner which came with the oven.  3 holes have been added to the new one to make sure it ignites.  (holes added by the manufacturer NOT technician)  He took pictures of the new and old BakeBurner and called in a report on it.
justification: The consumer and her husband experienced symptoms of gas exposure, including severe headaches and nausea, indicating injury (severity level 3). The issue was identified and addressed, but the likelihood of recurrence is possible (3) given the nature of gas leaks.

incident_description: I was making a cup of coffee in my Keurig Single Cup brewer Sunday evening. We keep it clean and well taken care of, and it was the first time it had been used that day. My 3 year old daughter likes to stand on a stool and watch it, so she was (I was cleaning the breakfast bar) and all of a sudden I heard this noise like a steam explosion and she started screaming. I turned and she, as well as the refrigerator and the counter, was covered with coffee grounds. The Keurig had exploded hot water and coffee grounds! She did have red marks from the water, but thankfully they went away and she was not injured. Several other important nearby documents were ruined, however, including a vehicle title and some paperwork for my husband's business.
justification: The child had red marks but no lasting injury, and the incident involved property damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such explosions are not common with well-maintained Keurig machines.

incident_description:
Range knobs slant downward and range sticks out past standard depth counter about  two inches.  This makes it easy to accidentally turn a knob on without realizing it.  This has happened to us several times, and the last time we had no idea how long the gas had flowed from the burner (unlit).  The very strong odor was the only thing that alerted us.  This is very unsafe.  

Take note that there is an identical report at 20160311-11F22-2147420995.  

This is completely unacceptable, and your design team should know better.  A simple button to turn off all burner gas flows, as you did for the oven burner, would solve the whole risk problem.  I am surprised LG hasn't been sued for this design flaw.

I am looking for a solution, and I don't know what it is.  I wait for a quick response with a solution.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage without injury, and it has happened several times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a gas range - Kitchen Aid Model KGRS505XSS01 and SN D10233389. Many times over the past few years, the knobs for the burners have turned on by accident after I reached in the cabinet above it and my abdomen brushed the knobs. I would just turn them off, no problem. Recently, however, I became aware that it a safety problem, because the knob turned on, but not far enough to make the electronic sparker click, so I was unaware it had turned. It was not until I smelled gas from the other room that I tried to find the source and noticed the knob was on. The room was full of gas by that time. I contacted Kitchen Aid to see if they had any retrofitting solution for this problem, and they told me they did not. I am writing you to report the safety hazard of this range in hopes that it can be corrected to prevent a disaster before it occurs.
justification: The incident describes a gas leak due to accidental knob activation, posing a safety hazard without immediate injury, but with potential for serious consequences if unaddressed.

incident_description:
The range was in the home when the consumer moved in - 9/2012. 

For approximately the last year, the right front burner began turning on by itself.  In the first incident, the consumer found that a dish towel that had been left on that element, was burned.  In that incident, the damage was limited to the towel itself.  The consumer has not left anything on top of the range since that incident.  When that element turns on, it goes to the ÃÂhighÃÂ setting.  When this happens, the consumer has to unplug the stove.  This appliance has a double oven and most of the time, this occurs when the upper oven is in use, but it also happens when both ovens and the range are in the off position.  

The consumer stated that they could later identify when the burner comes on, because the ranges makes a beeping sound.  The frequency has increased and lately, the problem has been happening twice a week.


3/14/2016:  The consumer called the mfr. after reading about the Recall# 09-333, but the rep. told him that the recall applied models made during earlier years.  The rep. also told the consumer that his range was outside of the warranty.  The consumer spoke with 1 rep. (name unknown) and asked to speak with a supervisor.  He was transferred to [REDACTED], who offered him 10% off of a replacement part.

The consumer is considering replacing the rage because of the safety hazard.

Since the consumer moved into the home, the range has never been serviced and he has never had any problems outside of this burner issue.
justification: The incident involves a burner turning on by itself, causing a burned towel but no injury, and the problem occurs twice a week.

incident_description:
(01/19/2016) The consumer stated that she was in the kitchen. She heard a pouf. She open the oven door and saw the oven had come on. 

(1/20/2016) The consumer called the electric  company who sent someone out to check the unit. Nothing was found.

The consumer called GE to ask if there were any complaints about the oven coming on by itself. The consumer was advised that they had not received any reports.

(04/10/2016) The consumer stated that the same thing happened twice with the oven. 

The consumer contacted the landlord to check the unit. He advised the consumer to unplug the unit because he researched on line and found that others had complained about the same issue.

(04/12/2016) The consumer stated that she plugged the unit in so that she could use it. The oven came on again by itself.
justification: The oven turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The issue occurred multiple times, indicating a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the kettle has several temperature settings and he used the kettle on various settings. The kettle usually beeps and turns off. 

In early march, the kettle failed to turn off on boil setting. From then on, the kettle is stuck in the "on" position. He has to unplug the kettle each time to shut off the kettle.

The consumer contacted the firm in regards to the issue. The firm sent out a replacement kettle. The consumer was asked to send back the faulty kettle.
justification: The kettle failed to turn off, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(04/2015)The consumer stated that the element light comes on and stays on. Also, the right front burner heats up when any of the other burners are in use. Initially, the right burner would only be warm. Now it gets hotter and hotter.

(04/18/2016) The consumer contacted repair service for the company. The consumer was advised that the product was not under warranty and he would have to pay for repair.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that heats up unexpectedly, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I own a GE self-cleaning gas range model RGB790CEK8CC. It was purchased in 2008. On more than one occasion, the knob for the top burner got slightly depressed and turned. As a result, gas was spewing from the burner into the kitchen. This could have been a very serious situation. It appears as though the knob/valve does not need to be depressed very far before the knob will rotate to the on position. Since this is a non-pilot light range, if the knob is not in a position to activate the igniter, unburned gas emanates from the burner creating a potential explosive situation. I suggest you investigate this.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage without injury, but with potential for serious harm, and has occurred multiple times.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dishwasher displayed similar problems of recall#12-244.  Hazard:An electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element can pose a fire hazard.  The unit was placed in use when it overheated and became extremely hot to a point the content inside melted.

He contacted the recall hotline but his serial number was not included.


Caller feels that this dishwasher should be included in a recall.

The submitter added he still has the unit, and unsure what to do with it..Its like new..
justification: The dishwasher overheated and melted contents, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her smooth top electric range that was in Florida home when she  moved into it in January 2011.

She thought that the front right and left burners were just a fluke when it never remained at the temperature it was set to and so just never used it very often.

Sometime during 2013 she noticed that the back right burner began changing temperature from the temperature she had set and at that time she was renting, not buying so she contacted the landlord who never had it repaired.

She began just watching the temperatures of these three burners as she cooked to be sure to adjust the temperature.

The house was offered for sale and the caller went to closing November 2015.

With each of the prior incidents the caller was able to turn the burners off then March 17th, 2016 the front left burner came on by itself and she could not turn it off until she turned every burner off then she could turn it off.

She is reporting this recent incident especially as a fire hazard.

There are no injuries being reported.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner with no injuries reported, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with potential safety hazards.

incident_description:
08/15/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer indicates that the cooktop had been used. Several hours later she noticed that the igniter to the left and back burner was on because of the ticking noise coming from it.

The consumer unplugged and plugged the unit back and the same ticking noise from the same burner came back on. After several days, the unit seemed to be working properly.

12/15/2015 (Approximate) - The consumer indicates that her husband had used the cooktop. A couple of hours later, the right and front burner came on by itself.

12/25/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer contacted her third-party warranty company, American Home Shield, and explained the situation. When the insurance company sent over a Service Technician from Magic Appliances, they refused to repair it citing water damage.

01/10/2016 (Approximate) - After further inspection from another firm that American Home Shield sent over (Active Appliances), they let the warranty company know that the damage was not due to misuse of the unit so a repair was agreed upon. The Electrician also informed the consumer that this is a known problem with cooktops.

01/15/2016 (Approximate) - A Service Technician from Magic Appliances repaired the unit.

The consumer indicates that she uses her cooktop approximately five times daily.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

The consumer plans on keeping the unit in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cooktop with burners turning on by themselves, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My 14 year old daughter was making a smoothie. It was our first time using the blender. She poured most of it out and took the lid off to get the final bit out. The blade came  out and lacerated her thumb. She damaged the tendon , had multiple stitches and will need a cast for 6 weeks!
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (laceration, tendon damage, stitches, and a cast), but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it was the first-time use of the blender and involved an unusual action (removing the lid while the blade was accessible).

incident_description: My daughter, age 14 months, put her hand on our closed wall oven, and cut off the tip of her finger on the area where the stainless steel part of the door meets the bottom of the glass. The cut was severe enough to require the immediate attention of an urgent care physician to stop the bleeding.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe cut requiring urgent medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe injuries from oven contact are not common.

incident_description: While the Magtag microwave exhaust fan was in operation,the exterior glass component of door spontaneously shattered.  The oven was not in use for cooking purposes.
justification: The glass shattered but there was no injury or cooking in progress, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: When leaning over to clean the range you accidentally contact the burner control valve causing burner to ignite leading to serious injury. If the burner valve is accidentally turned by contact, natural gas leaks without ignition.  The slide-in gas range IS VERY DANGEROUS, was recently installed in my home and is a Kitchen Aid Model #KSGG700EWH0 manufactured under Whirlpool Corp. Benton Harbor, MA.
justification: The description mentions a serious injury caused by accidental contact with the burner control valve, which aligns with severity level 3.

incident_description:
I purchased a Home Basics 150ml stove top espresso maker this week.  The manufacturer is HDS Trading Corp in North Brunswick, NJ; their website is http://www.hdstrading.com and the part number is EM00327.

When I put it on my stove over low gas heat, the handle melted off and fell into the burner, and the knob on top began to soften and melt.  If my roommate hadn't spotted it, there might have been a fire.  The plastic on this item is in no way heat resistant, and will burn.

I have photos of the damage if desired.
justification: The incident involved a melted handle and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Our GE Monogram dishwasher was running. We left the house and when we returned, we smelled something burning. We isolated the issue to our dishwasher. When I opened the dishwasher, I noticed that the coil had gotten so hot that it melted the plastic racks and the rotating disk where the water comes from as well. Our model number is ZBK6880K15SS and the Serial Number is TL952673B. We noticed that there had been a recall on several similar dishwashers, but ours was not on the list of those recalled. Our incident is exactly similar to the description for those dishwashers that were recalled, so it seems weird that ours was excluded.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted components) but no injury or death, and similar incidents have been reported in recalled models, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: I recently had a pyrex baking dish shatter while I was trying to wash it. The dish had been used to hold salmon that had been smoked on a grill, cooled and refrigerated for several hours.  It was then set out at room temperature for an hour or so before being placed in a 250 deg oven for ~ 20 minutes, it was then set out at room temperature to serve dinner and sat for several hours before being washed. There was absolutely no thermal shock or bumping of the dish. it just literally EXPLODED in my hands while I was washing it. Literally thousands of glass shards went all over my kitchen.  Fortunately the bulk of the pieces fell into a washtub in the sink.  Luckily I only incurred a small cut and no one was otherwise injured even during cleanup which was treacherous, especially since occurred at a party with more than a dozen guests present.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut (injury) but no serious harm, and the likelihood is unlikely as such events are not common with proper handling.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while she was using the microwave convection oven to heat chicken broth for approximately 2 mins the glass door shattered.  She stated that she noticed that there was melted hole in the inner glass.  Caller stated that the convection part of the unit had stopped working 6 months ago and she had to use the microwave part of it.

The retailer was contacted and she was advised to contact the agency and report the incident.

Caller feels that this unit is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a shattered microwave door but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her electric range purchased from retailer in Connecticut August 2011.

The caller states that the range never actually regulated the temperature very well but she said she could adapt timing until Sunday, April 10th, 2016 when she set the oven to preheat while she was cooking on the stovetop.

The oven never heated but did make a pop then sizzle before black smoke began coming from behind the range.

The caller turned the oven off then when her husband returned home approximately an hour later they pulled the range out and it has remained pulled away and turned off since.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer Monday, April 11th, 2016 and was advised only that they would send someone out for the standard fee.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range that emitted black smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We have a Whirlpool Range (model WSE510S0AW0 and serial # R22419589) and while preheating the middle tempered glass just shattered!  This seems to be a defect as the oven is only used a few times a week.
justification: The tempered glass shattered, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Our GE dishwasher model GLD6908R19BB caught on fire.  My wife was in the kitchen at the time and saw black smoke coming from the dishwasher.  She opens the door and saw flames inside.  She immediately closed the door and tried to use the dishwasher controls to shut down the machine, but it did not work.  She shut off the electrical power supply to the dishwasher on an external switch.  We called GE.  They sent a technician to inspect the unit.  The electronic components of the control unit and the insulation of the electrical wires were melted.  GE informed us, that the dishwasher cannot be repaired.  It is a total loss. They told us, that their engineers did not consider this a safety issue. This potentially deadly situation was only prevented through my wifeÃÂs luckily being in the kitchen at that time and reacting quickly and correctly in the emergency.  GEÃÂs responses were to offer us to buy a new dishwasher at an inflated price, and if we donÃÂt take it, the case is closed by them.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injury occurred due to quick action.

incident_description: glass lid exploded, shattering all over kitchen and cutting me in 3 places
justification: The glass lid exploded, causing injuries in three places, which qualifies as an injury incident.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her four burner w/one warmer smooth-top electric range purchased from retailer March 2001 in Kentucky.

She had no problems with the range until sometime in 2014 when the front right burner began turning on by itself and could only be turned off by tripping the breaker off.

The caller has been keeping the breaker turned off and only turning it on when she is going to be cooking and near the range so that she can keep an eye on it.  After cooking she has been tripping the breaker back off.

She has been trying to convince Sears to repair the range at their expense because of the nature of the fire safety hazard existing with the over $2,000.00 range but they will not repair the range unless the expense is the consumers.

There are no injuries being reported.

The caller is asking that this range become recalled with free repair at manufacturer expense.
justification: The burner turns on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported and the consumer is managing the risk by controlling the breaker.

incident_description: Samsung over the oven microwave would not respond to STOP/CLEAR and continued running after only 30 seconds of use.  I opened the door and the interior was hot to touch but after a few more attempts to shut off, the power went completely out.  The interior light did not come on when the door was opened and the digital clock was out.  I assumed it threw the circuit breaker and I did not attempt to restart it as I was concerned that the unit was unstable and hot.  After spending the next 35 minutes upstairs, I came down to find it running and something was definitely burning.  I opened the microwave door and part of the inside door panel had melted onto the interior. It was extremely hot and would not shut off manually so I had to unplug it from within a cabinet above the unit.  I have reported it to Samson and they have a ticket number ( 5114039195) associated with the report.  I looked on line at the incidences of various makes and models that have been reported spontaneously starting while families were sleeping or away at work with entire kitchens burned.  Please look closely at the number of occurrences and find a means of more closely inspecting the dangers these appliances pose before approving passing their safety standards.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing overheating and melting, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
My problem is the same as described below.
My electric range the front burner was not able to be turned off and had to shut off all electric to the stove before I could get it shut off.    I called sears and theyplaced the switch with a 60.00 co pay. That was about a month ago.  This weekend while cooking the front left burner started the same thing.  I called Sears and we could not get it to duplicate so they elected to do nothing about it and tried to collect another 60.00 co pay.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range burner that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I found my dishwasher spewing water from underneath and a strong smell of something burning. The appliance had been run through a cleaning cycle about 7:30 AM and would have finished around 8:30 AM. At approximately 10:15 AM I was in another room and heard strange noises in the house so I investigated and found hot water coming from under the dishwasher. I checked the sink to make sure there was no water in it and then immediately went to the basement and shut off the water supply and electrical current to the dishwasher. The smell from the dishwasher (electric burning type smell) was so bad I chose to just remove the appliance from my home immediately instead of calling anyone to see about a possible repair. I used a 16 gallon shop vac to vacuum the water and ended up with probably 4-5 gallons of water from the floor the dishwasher was on. There was also water in the basement that had leaked through the floor. Had I not been home this could have caused substantial damage to my home.

GE ADORA DISHWASHER
MODEL # GHDA674N00BG
SERIAL# ZL809103B
justification: The incident involved water leakage and a burning smell, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
On about March 30, 2016 during operation of the dishwasher noticeable amounts of smoke and smell of electronics overheating were emitted from the appliance even though it continued to operate. Upon opening the dishwasher, smoke continued to be emitted from the small (approximately one inch by two inch latch closure opening at the top center of the door for about ten minutes. The device was separately disabled via breaker since every time the door was closed the appliance began operation again and smoke once again became visible along with the smell. The front panel of the door was too hot too touch about 6 to 12 inches from the top of the door and about the same distance toward the center from side to side.

Upon commencing of repairs, the control module ASM GE P/N 165D7305G004 (manufactured by Computime LTD as P/N 663C and reprogrammed by GE) was discovered to have burned through the wiring harness connector in the center of the module and the module showed significant burn through, thermal cracks and charring of the case at both the front and the back.
justification: The incident involved significant smoke and overheating but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the detailed description of recurring smoke and overheating issues.

incident_description: Dishwasher turned on, 4.5 hours later lights indicated still drying.  Opened door and smoke and heat were released.  Smoke detector in adjoining room set off.   The plastic spray arm melted onto the heater and was charred.  The silverware holder as well as a plastic container and a plastic microwave cooking dish had partly melted.
justification: The incident involved smoke and heat release with melted plastic parts, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(2/29/16 estimated) The consumer set the dishwasher to a wash cycle. Approximately 2 minutes later the consumer noticed smoke coming from the control panel. The consumer opened the door to stop the cycle and shut off the dishwasher but the smoke continued to emit from the control panel. The consumer then shut off the circuit breaker and shortly after the smoke stopped.

(3/1/16 estimated) The consumer searched online and came across recall # 96-133. The consumer then contacted the firm's recall hotline (800-874-9481) and the Rep. (name unknown) informed the consumer that his dishwasher was not recalled. The consumer was not sure if his serial number started with "FA" or "FR" and provided the Rep. with both serial numbers but the consumer was told that his dishwasher was recalled. The consumer was told that someone from Sears would contact him within 24 hours to arrange for a repair, free of charge.

The consumer has not received a call as of today, 3/7/16.

The consumer has not noticed any burn damages to the dishwasher but he has not looked inside the control panel. 

The consumer states he uses the dishwasher twice a week. There are no prior incidents.
justification: Smoke emission from the dishwasher indicates an incident, but there was no injury or damage reported.

incident_description:
(12/2015) The consumer stated that each time that she uses the product, she get second degree burns when accidently touching the outside surface.

The consumer stated that she was burned on three different occasions

No medical attention was required.

The consumer would like for proper labeling to warn consumer about the outside surface.

(04/05/2016) The consumer contacted the manufacturer about the issue. She was advised that the product is design intent. She was also advise to only touch the cool-touch handle.
justification: The consumer sustained second-degree burns on multiple occasions, indicating injury (severity 3), and the issue occurs each time the product is used, making it likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Bottom elements become warped and catch fire. Numerous complaints online were found once I searched the problem. Oven does not turn off for toast once this happens.
justification: The incident involves elements catching fire and the oven not turning off, which poses a clear risk of injury.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator light does not turn off, melts plastic casing, and heats food on top shelf.
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing property damage (melted plastic and heated food) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: The oven was on for approximately 15 minutes at 350 degrees.  It began to over heat.  We tried to turn it off and then turn it down to 300 degrees.  The bottom heating element would not shut off.  Tried to turn it off, but even though the display indicated it was off, the heating element did not shut off.  Turned off the circuit breaker.  When the circuit breaker was turned back on the heating element turned back on. We have to shut off the circuit breaker to keep it off.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, only an operational issue requiring intervention.

incident_description:
Sharp Carousel microwave oven Model R-309Y purchased
12/2013 @ Lowes. Microwave keeps running even when door open & Stop
Cancel button pressed. Morningstar Farms bacon kept cooking/scorched even though microwave off.
Very dangerous with kids in household; fire hazard as well.
Sharp support zero help & Sharp not acting accountable.
justification: The microwave continues to operate with the door open, posing a risk of injury or fire, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Fire in LG dishwasher (Mdl: LDS5811ST/02).   My wife smelled smoke, then saw smoke coming from the closed door of the dishwasher. Dishwasher was turned off at the time and not in use. She put out the fire with a fire extinguisher, then turned off the breaker to the unit. The kitchen, dining room and living room were filled with smoke. If this had happened at night when everyone was asleep this fire could have resulted in the loss of our home and possibly loss of life.

I called LG and spoke to [REDACTED], who would not give her full name, but instead gave her number, [REDACTED].  She told me that there was nothing she could do because the dishwasher was out of warranty. I suggested to her that LG should want to know the cause of the fire, as there were other instances of LG dishwasher fires reported online here: http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/lg-dishwasher-c472065.html

[REDACTED] further suggested that I call a repairman. She stated that she had never heard of an LG dishwasher spontaneously catching fire. I am very concerned about the lack of concern expressed by LG to what could have been a potentially tragic incident.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have resulted in injury or death if not promptly addressed, and similar incidents have been reported online, though they are not common.

incident_description: While unpacking - picked up glass container and it exploded and cut hand
justification: The incident resulted in a cut hand, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: A KitchenAid dishwasher ignited to fire during a normal wash cycle.

incident_description:
LWFD fire company responded for the report of an activated CO alarm with no illness.  Upon our arrival, occupants were standing outside the wood frame, raised ranch, single family home.  Investigation revealed an activated CO detector on the hallway ceiling outside the sleeping quarters, but 0ppm readings on the 4-gas meter throughout the home, including the lower level where the natural gas-fire water heater and furnace are located.  
Interview of the owners revealed that the oven had been turned on at the time of the CO detector activation, but they had turned it off.  They purchased the natural gas-fired Whirlpool range (stove/oven) in March, 2016 from the Menards in Bolingbrook, IL.  The appliance was delivered by Menards but installed by a handyman they use regularly.  A few days after installation the occupants were smelling gas when using the oven.  They called NICOR Gas Company, who sent out a technician and told the them that he didn't find any gas but he did find abnormal levels of CO.  The owners called Whirlpool, who sent out a technician that told them the reason for the CO was because the owner had placed a sheet of tin foil on the bottom interior of the oven to protect it from food drippings.  The owners removed the tin foil and continued to use the range.  
Further investigation by LWFD revealed no tin foil on the bottom of the oven and that the oven was properly installed with an apparently new yellow stainless steel flexible gas appliance connector.  The tip-over safety device had even been properly attached to the wall behind the range.  LWFD turned on the oven and almost immediately began getting CO readings on the 4-gas meter.  These readings reached as high as 120 ppm, then dropped and remained between 35 ppm-45 ppm for some time before dropping.  It was noticed the oven had reached its set temperature.  LWFD raised the temperature setting, the oven "fired", and the CO readings immediately began to rise again.  LWFD turned the oven off, turned the gas off to the appliance, removed the appliances electric power cord from the wall outlet, and notified the owners to not use the range and contact Whirlpool.
justification: The incident involved a CO alarm activation with no reported illness, and CO levels were detected but mitigated without injury.

incident_description: This report concerns a GE Monogram dishwasher, Model ZBD6880N00SS, Serial Number ZM764927B.  We were awoken the morning of the event at 3:00 AM to a home full of smoke and fumes which seemed to be burning plastic.  After frantically searching the house for the most obvious possible sources (stove, oven, heater) we noticed that the counter top above the dishwasher was extremely hot and the smoke was coming from beneath the enclosure.  We opened the dishwasher and were hit by a gust of heat and billowing smoke and fumes.  The control panel showed that the unit was in the ON position and HEATED DRY, although we had not turned on the dishwasher before going to bed.  We tried repeatedly to turn off the machine using the control panel but it would not respond.  We finally ran outside and turned off the circuit breaker that controlled the dishwasher circuit.  The bottom pan of the dishwasher was filled with melted plastic (much of it from components of the dishwasher itself) and the plastic was covering and in direct contact with the heating element.  We scraped as much of the molten plastic away from the elements as possible as it continued to burn and emit noxious fumes. We were able to evacuate the smoke using our vent hood, exhaust fans, and air conditioning unit, although this took quite some time.  The granite counter top remained very hot to the touch for a good while after we disconnected the power to the unit as were the surrounding kitchen cabinets.  Had this occurred when we were not home I fear that combustion would have occurred and we may have lost our house.  We contacted GE about the event and were offered a partial discount on a new unit.  We feel that this model is inherently dangerous as the control panel failed and the circuit closed with no human interaction.
justification: The incident involved significant smoke and heat but no injuries were reported, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required specific failure conditions.

incident_description:
Model Number 790.96011407

Since we moved into this house three years ago, the front large burners have been unpredictable. Sometimes while already cooking on low or medium, the burner would turn on high without me adjusting the dial. I would have to turn the burner off and wait a few minutes and then turn the burner back to low or medium again. 

During these incidents, the burner will get super hot and sometimes ruin whatever I am cooking if I don't catch it in time. If the pan is large enough to cover the burner, you can't tell that the burner has kicked up to high until your food is burning. Sometimes I couldn't turn the burner off at all without first turning the knob on and off over and over many times back and forth to get the burner to switch off. 

The first time or two this happened, I thought I was mistaken or maybe had missed a spill that was causing it to misread but nope, it is just a short in the system! For three years this has been happening until last weekend when I couldn't turn the burner off at all. Nothing I did would turn it off. I had to go to the breaker box and cut the power to the range. The range has been sitting dead since then until we can figure out what to do. We did try to turn the power back on just to see if it fixed it but as soon as we did the burner turned right back to high until we flipped the breaker again even with all the burners in the OFF position!!! It has ruined some of my good pans from the heat being too high for them and it has ruined a couple of meals. Not to mention, this is a fire hazard. It's unsafe to use. I no longer have a working oven. Thanks, Kenmore, a.k.a. SEARS.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard and has damaged property, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description: We have a Frigidaire gas range and the corners of the door when opened are very sharp, my wife has gashed herself virtually in the same place 2 times now. She's had this happen when the loading the oven with a dish.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (gashing) and has occurred twice under similar circumstances, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I was baking at 350 degrees for about 30 minutes when I heard a big pop and opened the door to find the inside glass completely shattered. This Kenmore elite model #79048353410 was installed early January 2016, so is not even 3 months old
justification: The incident involved glass shattering in an oven, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: My Bosch dishwasher (SHU8805UC/U12) started smoking while my son was at home.  He opened the front door and the smoke was coming out of the front door near the top.  Six days later, I removed the front panel of the dishwasher to find that the small Siemens control module (where the on/off, cycle buttons are located), was badly burned.  It defect burned through the printed circuit board and through the housing of the power module.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke but no injury occurred, and the issue was identified as a burned control module.

incident_description: Coffee maker exploded causing 2nd degree burns to face, neck and chest.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that approximately a year and a half ago he was awaken mid-night by a humming sound coming from his kitchen. The consumer went to the kitchen and this is when he noticed that the microwave was on with the front panel flashing '000;' the unit had turned itself on. The consumer tried turning off the unit through its front panel and it would not respond. The consumer had to unplug the unit in order for it to turn off. The consumer indicates that he never tried opening the microwave door because he believes this would have been a mistake.

The consumer is unaware how long the unit had been on for but he states that he touched the top of the microwave and it was extremely hot.

03/28/2016 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to documented his concerns and informed the consumer that he would hear from them within twenty-fours hours.

The consumer states that prior to the incident, he used the microwave on average once or twice daily. The consumer ceased use of the unit approximately one year and a half ago because of the safety issues.

The consumer plans on keeping the unit in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred; the incident is unlikely as it happened once over a year and a half of regular use.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the stove becomes extremely hot when in use. If she turns on the front burners to cook, the entire top plate of the stove gets extremely hot. If the consumer is using the stovetop and the oven, her smoke alarm will go on. In order for the consumer to use both the stove and the oven, she has to leave her kitchen windows open so as to not trigger the smoke alarms in her home.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the issue she was having. The representative she spoke to arranged for a Service Technician to inspect her unit.

10/08/2015 - The Service Technician inspected the consumer's unit. After inspection, he indicated the unit is working as it should be.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer again. They sent another Service Technician over. This Service Technician indicated that the issue has to do with the design of the unit as the vents to the oven blow up and onto the knobs of the unit, making it extremely hot to touch.

The consumer indicates that even the microwave and its handle that is located above the range get hot when the latter is in use.

The consumer indicates that she uses her stovetop and oven six to seven times a week. Because of the issue with the overheating, the consumer has never been able to self-clean the oven.
justification: The incident involves overheating and smoke alarms triggering, but no injury is reported. The issue occurs frequently (6-7 times a week) based on consumer usage.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his electric range purchased from a furniture retailer in Baton Rough, Louisiana around February or March 2006.

The caller had no problems with the range until March 8th, 2016 when the caller was baking cake set at 'bake' while his wife was using the stove top to warm other food.

They had been cooking for approximately 30 minutes when they heard a loud pop, fire shot out of the top oven vent, the stove top and the oven stopped working and cannot be turned back on.

The caller is reporting this incident as a fire hazard.

There are no injuries being reported at this time.

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

The caller has requested that this model become recalled with free repair at manufacturer expense and if he has had to pay for repair that he become reimbursed at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described event.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the blender was in use for approximately 5 mins, he noticed sparks emitting from the bottom right sight side of the blender and there was a burning odor.  He then noticed that it had developed into a black smoke.  He immediately unplugged it and remove it outside.  He had the blender for over a year and there was no prior incident. 

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Consumer feels that the blender is unsafe and should be reported.

This incident with Ninja BL770 occurred today while making a smoothie.
Ingredients being processed:
3 medjool dates
2 bananas 
Mango 
Coconut flakes 
Dried lime
Dried lime zest & orange zest
Quart of cold water

Because the consumer had brought the dates about an hour before starting to make this smoothie, they had not been soaked. Thus, he ran the blender on high speed for a couple of minutes to emulsify them with about 4-6 ounces of cold water.
Then added the bananas, dried lime sections, emulsified them on high.2-3 minutes.
Next, added the flesh from a decently ripe mango and a little more cold water. Emulsified on high 1-2 minutes.
Added remain of the cold water. Blended medium less than a minute. Tasted.
Decided not thick enough.
Pour out most of the smoothie to allow him to blend-in coconut flakes. After starting the flakes to blend, decided to add dried zest (lime & orange).
Added those ingredients; started blending on high. Because he had not ground the zest before adding it to the smoothie, the consumer figured he needed to run the blender a little longer than he would have otherwise.
It had been running 2-3 minutes when either sparking or the odor from the blender caught the consumer's attention from where he was standing at  the kitchen counter about 5-6 feet away.
The blender was still running.

The consumer immediately investigated. He had noticed on other occasions that the blender seem to get really warm. But, it had never shutdown; or, otherwise gave indication of overheating.
However, since he had ran it longer than usual, his initial thought was maybe it was beginning to overheat.
While the blender was still running, he saw what he believe was sparking coming out of the left rear side.
The consumer immediately turned the blender off and unplugged it.
At  this  time,  smoke  - noxious  smelling  like  'burnt  plastic'  - was billowing out of the blender.

Took the pitcher off.
Turned the blender over; and saw where the plastic center section had begun to melt.
There was still a lot of smoke being generated. 

Remove the blender base to my outside landing.

Decided to take pictures with his cell phone; and then, with digital camera.

Also, took pictures where the blender had been setting. There was substantial black dust on the pad I had had under it.
The consumer cannot say that all the black dust was from this incident because the reason the pad was under the blender was its history of making that black dust when used.

Attached are two pictures, The consumer has retained 10 other pictures.
If you need additional information about this incident, please contact me.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the blender, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(2/1/16) The consumer's husband woke up and noticed a strong burn odor. The consumer's husband opened the dishwasher and noticed the odor was stronger inside. The consumer's husband also noticed that the dishwasher was extremely hot and a plastic utensil inside the dishwasher was melting. The dishwasher was "Off" and none of the buttons were lit. The consumer's husband did not notice any burn damages to the dishwasher. 

The consumer states the dishwasher was used 4- 8 hours prior to the incident.  

The consumer states there are no prior incidents.

The consumer was searching online and came across recall # 12-244. The consumer states that her dishwasher is similar to those recalled dishwashers and her dishwasher also has a defective heating element. The consumer believes her dishwasher should be included in the recall. 

The consumer called the firm's recall hotline and heard on the prompt that the dishwashers with stainless steel interiors are not included in the recall. The consumer states that her dishwasher has a stainless steel interior.
justification: The incident involved a strong burn odor and a melting plastic utensil, but no injuries or damages were reported.

incident_description:
An electrical wiring problem started a fire inside of the freezer compartment. The area in the freezer appeared to involve the wire for the interior light. By the time I realized what the problem was, the rear interior portion of the freezer had burned and melted causing the light to dangle. The fire filled our kitchen with toxic smoke. The fridge was on a dedicated outlet so I was able to shut the power off to the unit quickly.

Electrolux is the manufacturer and the brand is Frigidaire Professional. Model # is PHT189HSM4, SERIAL # BA80611174
justification: The incident involved a fire and toxic smoke but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Text of Submitter's Letter (excerpted):

We would like to report a recent serious problem with our Frigidaire Gallery Series 27" FGMC Black Microwave/Electric Wall Oven combination which we purchased from Sears for $1703 less than six years ago.

First the handle came loose on the oven door. Then, upon simply opening the oven door, the oven door glass exploded. Literally, exploded. Glass and pieces were sent across the kitchen floor and into the bottom tray of the oven. Sharp jagged pieces remained sticking out from the bottom of what was left of the glass door. We were lucky no one suffered any personal injury during the shattering or in the clean-up. See enclosures for photographs of the situation.

We contacted Electrolux North America and were told they would not pay for the costs we incurred for a new door and its installation nor did they seem concerned over any dangerous situation caused by their product.

We want to make sure no other family, especially with young children, face this situation.
justification: The oven door exploded, sending glass across the kitchen, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while the dishwasher was placed into cycle approximately 10 mins later she smelled a burning odor.  She noticed smoke emitting from the bottom right of the dishwasher, she stated that she placed a camera under it to video the incident.  Caller stated that the video showed wires burning red.  She stated that just before the cycle went into heated dry it was powered off.

(3/15) The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that the dishwasher was no longer under warranty, there was no property damage and there was no recall they could not assist her. 

The submitter added that after message to manufacturer on Facebook, they have offered 2 discounts on parts, but still will not pay for repair.

Caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning wires but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: I have a samsung microwave, and when you open the door it seems to be running. The light, and fan turn on. (the turntable is broken so iit doesnt turn on. I want to make sure that it isnt actually cooking when it is on. I put a bunch of tinfoil in the microwave, and opened it very slightly so it would run, and nothing happened. I also tried this with water and the water didnt heat so i am pretty sure that  it is not actually runnning but i would rather be safe than sorry.
justification: The microwave appears to malfunction by activating the light and fan when the door is opened, but no actual cooking occurs, posing no immediate injury risk.

incident_description: Fire crews responded to a report of a residential structure fire. Upon arrival, fire crews located a fire within the oven of a natural gas stove. The property owner discovered flames coming from the oven while the appliances was preheating to cook dinner. The fire was contained to the interior of the oven.
justification: The fire was contained to the oven with no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Kitchen-aid microwave starts on its own.  Model number.  KHMS155LSS.
justification: The microwave starting on its own is an incident but no injury is reported.

incident_description: On 3/27/16 we were cooking a ham in our Kenmore glass top stove model: 790 929 030 13.  We were using the oven at 325 and at some point changed the temp up to 375 to accommodate some potatoes.  The ham was cooking for several hours.  We took out the ham and were cutting it up and the potatoes were still cooking.  We heard a pop/bang, and looked over and saw that the inner pane of the 3 pane oven door had shattered.  When we opened the oven door to take out the potatoes glass fell on to the floor and in to the oven and the bottom oven drawer.  No one was touching the oven when this occurred.
justification: The oven door shattered, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
At approx. 10:30/11:00am, the upper oven was set to 350 degrees and had been ÃÂonÃÂ approx. 90 minutes.  The consumer was in the next room, when she heard an explosion.  The consumer went into the kitchen and found that glass in the "lower" oven door had shattered.  The lower oven was not in use at the time of the incident.  The lower oven had been used earlier that day, but it was completely cool at the time of the incident.

This oven has 3 panes of glass (an outer glass, middle glass and an inner glass).  The middle glass shattered, but the outer and the inner glass remained intact.  There is stainless on the door, which surrounds the glass.  The glass broke into tiny pieces small as pebbles and others were larger and stuck together.  There were no injuries.


2/21/2016:  The consumer called the mfr. and spoke with their repair department.  An appointment was scheduled for a tech to come out and look at the range on Wed-2/24/16.   The consumer was told that she had to pay $99.95 for the service call and cover parts and labor.

2/22/2016:  The consumer followed up with the mfr. and spoke with Chanbria, (Tel:  800-386-1215 x. 3683).  The consumer was assigned a case # [REDACTED].  Chanbria waived the $99.95 service charge call and offered approx. 25% off of the parts.  The consumer told her that was a start, but she did not want to pay anything.  Chanbria told the consumer that she was not authorized to offer any further discounts and indicated that the consumer could discuss her concerns with the technician that is scheduled to come out on Wed-2/24.  The consumer asked why more could not be offered more, because this was clearly a defect.  The consumer said that Chanbria indicated that they did not have anything on record.  Nothing else transpired.

The consumer believes that this presents oven presents a safety hazard and that there is potential for a similar incident with the upper oven door.   Chanbria told the consumer that she could discuss this concern with the technician, when he came out.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of oven glass but resulted in no injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer states that his home warranty company, Home Warranty of America purchased the microwave. The consumer believes the microwave was installed sometime in December 2014.

(2/28/16) The consumer heated up some food, then he removed it from the microwave and after closing the door he noticed a humming noise coming from the microwave. 

The consumer noticed that this happens each time he uses the microwave. After searching online the consumer read that the humming noise could be the magnetron (heating element) that continues to stay on. The consumer placed a bowl of water in the microwave and closed the door. The consumer states he did not set the timer. After 20 second the consumer removed the bowl of water and states that the water was very hot. The consumer has unplugged the microwave. 

The consumer is concerned that the microwave could be emitting high levels of radiation and also poses a fire hazard.

The consumer contacted Home Warranty of America and arranged for a technician to examine the microwave on 3/3/16.

The consumer does not plan to contact GE since the microwave is out of warranty.
justification: The microwave exhibits a malfunction (humming noise and unintended heating), but no injury or fire has occurred. The issue is possible but not yet confirmed as a widespread hazard.

incident_description:
The recessed handle on my Bosch dishwasher has broken and been replaced repeatedly in the 6 months since I have purchased it.  Online reviews indicate that this is a widespread problem with this model and that Bosch is refusing to admit there is a structural problem, only agreeing to replace the plastic handle insert until the 1-year warranty runs out.

When the handle breaks, it creates sharp shards that create a cutting risk.  When the handle crumbles completely, as they all eventually have, they create an opening for water to enter the electronics and create a fire hazard.
justification: The broken handle creates sharp shards posing a cutting risk and a potential fire hazard from water ingress, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The widespread nature of the problem and repeated failures suggest an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The caller stated that his electric griddle caught on fire.

The caller stated that they were warming up the griddle when they noticed sparks and flames coming up from underneath the griddle. It appears that the element is cracked. There is white residue around where the element is cracked. 

The caller unplugged the griddle right away. 

The caller contacted the manufacturer on 3/14/16 in regards to the incident. They are providing a replacement griddle. The caller was asked to cut off the plug and send it back to the firm for them to review.
justification: The griddle caught fire but was unplugged immediately, and no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The bake feature of the oven was turned on to warm rolls. I turned the oven off and took the rolls out. Several hours later I was preparing to leave and walked past the oven and I noticed it was extremely hot; I first checked the top display of the oven to make sure it was off there was no indication anything was on; so I opened the oven door, the broiler element of the oven was on. I double checked the panels and pressed the off buttons and it wouldn't shut off. I had to unplug the oven to get it to turn off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to injury but did not, hence severity level 2.

incident_description:
The consumer states the range was delivered on 10/13/13.

(01/24/16) The consumer was in the basement and heard a loud noise. The consumer went to the kitchen which is on the main level and noticed the oven's outer glass had cracked. The consumer states the outer glass is completely cracked and about 10% of the glass fell on the floor. 

(1/25/16) The consumer called the firm to inform them of the incident and to arrange for a repair. The consumer has an extended warranty. The consumer states the technician is scheduled to arrive today (1/28/16). 

There are no prior incidents.

The consumer believes the range poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a cracked oven glass with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as there are no prior incidents and the issue was promptly reported for repair.

incident_description: We purchased a LP gas range a little more than a year ago. Since owning it I guess 33 to 40 times the burner knobs have turned on, without turning on the igniter, by simply bumping them or brushing against them.  Allowing gas to leak into the house. The safety catch does not seem to be doing its job correctly. We have always caught the problem in the past.  Today I returned from work to a kitchen filled with gas. I turned off the burned knob and opened doors and windows to clear the gas.  It had been running all day.  I feel this is a manufacturer defect with huge safety concerns.  In 25 yrs. of owning gas ranges, I have never had this situation. Could you see what can be done to protect an unsuspecting owner.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to a faulty burner knob, which poses a significant safety risk but has not resulted in injury or death.

incident_description: The Bodum model 5500 electric tea kettle/water pot completely melted the plastic near the heating element on base of the unit without warning while I was boiling water.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore range model #79092803010 that I purchased on 2010. I opened the oven door and the glass exploded all over the kitchen floor. Fortunately I was wearing slippers or it would have cut my feet. The oven was cold and hadn't been used for 2 days. This is so dangerous! What if my small grandsons would have been there? This seems to be a problem with hundreds of other people experiencing the same thing. There should be a recall on this product!!
justification: The glass exploded but no one was injured, though there was potential for harm. The issue is reported by many others, indicating it's likely to occur.

incident_description: I was preheating my electric Samsung oven (model NE595N0PBSR) using the convection setting at 400 degrees. After about two minutes there was a loud pop, then flames and smoke billowing from the unit. The heating element had caught fire and incinerated itself, reducing it to metal pellets on the oven floor. Luckily I was in the room and could deal with it though the heat singed my eyelashes (it was still that hot even after the flame was out). I am told the heating element can be replaced but I am worried about the safety of my family and my property with this appliance in the house.  The unit is not new, but it is not even three years old and has been kept clean and in good repair.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, causing minor injury (singed eyelashes) but no serious harm. The likelihood of recurrence is possible given the appliance's age and condition.

incident_description: Turned on the oven this morning to pre-heat, burned myself as I adjusted the oven shelves because the broiler turned on.  The broiler will not turn off, even when the oven is turned completely off.  The only way to get the broiler to turn off is to disconnect the power supply.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the broiler malfunction poses a recurring hazard.

incident_description: I was cleaning a glass shelf from my refrigerator with soap and warm water and it shattered and went flying everywhere (10+ feet away). Fortunately I only received one small cut on my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in a small injury (cut on the hand), and glass shattering during cleaning is a possible but not frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
Product = GE Profile Range 
JGS968TEK1WW
ZH293549Q

The oven came on by itself and heated without any limit. Smoke alerted me to the situation.
There was no indication of the oven being on. The display panel showed only the time.
I pressed "Cancel/Off" and nothing happened.
The display panel was functioning.
I pressed "Bake" and the panel showed the normal start up indications. 
At no time did a temperature appear in the display as would normally be the case. 
The cabinet fan was NOT on during this time. Thus the oven was silent and I initially did not realize it was on until I was actually in front of the stove and felt the heat. 
I was able to shut the range down by shutting off the gas line outside.
It seemed to me that if not found, the oven would have continued to over-heat and would have eventually ignited the surrounding cabinets. 
An ozone smell continued from the unit until it cooled enough for me to disconnect it from the electric power. 
A clean clay pot used for cooking was in the oven at the time. It was totally burned. Thus I would assume the temperature in the oven significantly exceeded the clean cycle temperature.
justification: The incident involved significant overheating and potential fire hazard, posing a risk of injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I was taking a pan from the oven and closed the oven door suddenly the glass front on my Frigidaire oven shattered all over the floor. As I was cleaning it up a piece of the glass cut my finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I was running my nearly 11 year old Frigidaire oven on a self clean cycle as I've done 4 or 5 times in the past and this time the outer glass exploded 3 hours into the cycle sending glass about 10 feet across the kitchen. I'm worried that the glass was faulty since it broke into some very sharp shards. A lot of the pieces seemed to be shaped like pebbles as I believe it should have but there were  quite a few rather large, long and pointy ones that worried me. My 3 year old was making faces and looking at get reflection in the door about 5 minutes before it happened.  I think at least there should be a warning on the stove. This could have been a horrific ending if she were looking at her reflection as it exploded with the size and shape of some of the shards of glass.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass exploding, but no injuries were reported despite the potential danger.

incident_description: We had a horrible experience with our Thermador oven.  Our upper oven exploded during the self-clean cycle.  I called Thermador customer support and they explained the situation.  The customer support stated that they will solely cover the diagnostic but will not cover anything further as this oven is out of warranty.  I am surprised that Thermador would not take the safely of their oven seriously and work to ensure that the glass in the oven is working as it is intended throughout the entire life of the oven.   I was told that because my oven is over 12 years old it is not ThermadorÃÂs responsibility.  I would think that Thermador would want to continue giving the best customer service experience and stand by their products no matter their age.  Exploding ovens is not something that a company should be proud of, and not something a consumer expects.
justification: The oven exploded during the self-clean cycle, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a Viking Dishwasher (Model VDB450SS, Serial No. 081910D00018347) for my home and subsequently registered the product.  I was never notified of a recall on my unit (Recall date: April 10, 2012; Recall number: 12147) which states"[c]onsumers should immediately stop using the recalled dishwashers and contact Viking's hotline for a free in-home repair."

I discovered the recall on or about January 25, 2016, when my unit's electrical circuit ceased operation and I inquired about service.   I called the recall hotline, (800) 241-7239, was assigned Customer ID No.  [REDACTED], and was promised a repair kit would be delivered to my home within 15 business days.    On March 1, 2016, I call back to the hotline to report that the repair kit still had not arrived, and I was advised that the issue was "escalated" and that the another kit would be sent because they could not trace the 1st one.   On March 24, 2016, I again called the hotline because no repair kit has been received.   I was told that the company answering the hotline reported the matter to Viking and while I was placed on hold, they tried without success to reach Viking.  I left my cell number and demanded a call back.

The failure of Viking to timely address the recall is unacceptable.

Please let me know how the CPSC can assist.  My family of 4 has been without a dishwasher for 2 months now.
justification: The incident involves a failure to notify and repair a recalled dishwasher, causing inconvenience but no injury or death.

incident_description: On March 23, 2016, my GE Quiet Power 3 Dishwasher door latch melted from the dishwasher overheating, making it impossible to open the door after a full cleaning cycle.  This item has been recalled in 2012.  Model # GLD4400N10BB, Serial # AR765622B
justification: The dishwasher door latch melted due to overheating, causing an incident but no injury, and the item was previously recalled indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Turned on oven to 350 degrees and placed chicken and veggies on pan inside. Went into another room and closed door to call my mother. Next thing I new my husband pulled open the door and yelled didn't you hear the smoke alarm going off and me yelling from the basement ?  I said no I was on the phone with the door shut. The oven had gotten so hot that it had burned the food and had ash residue in the bottom as if it was on cleaning cycle. The oven would not turn off at the control and so he had to pull the circuit breaker in the basement. The oven control was flashing F1. We let it cool off and plugged it back in and tuned breaker back on. It proceeded to do the same thing. Turned the breaker off once again and unplugged. Contacted local appliance repair shop and they noted it might be an issue with the EOC. My husband cleaned the contacts on the EOC and the oven started working again. I turned it on today and It doesn't work at all. This oven is so unpredictable. I am afraid to even try to turn it back on without my husband being present. Had he not unexpectedly came home on that day, I have no debt that my kitchen would have caught fire and I may not have realized it until it was too late. I also want to mention that the side oven is rarely used because it smells like burning rubber every time we try to use it. The Kenmore Elite 40" Ceramic Glass Range (2001) model number: 79099503990 is dangerous and needs to be recalled!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We purchased a new Keurig coffee maker, from a local store, on 12/21/15.  The product was first used on 12/25/15 and was used once a day until 3/3/16.  One week prior to the incident, there was a faint smell of something burning in the house, but the problem could not be pinpointed.  On the morning of March 3rd, the Keurig coffee maker would not turn on.  As the machine was about to be unplugged, it was noted that the end of the power cord was melted.  After unplugging the cord, it was obvious that there was burning that had occurred. The outlet itself had a black burn mark, and the wires behind the outlet were burned back approximately 3 inches.  It was at that time that I did an internet search on Keurig and found that we were not the first to experience this issue.  Keurig was notified immediately of the defect.  They claimed they had no prior knowledge of this ever happening with one of their machines and would have FedEx to my home within the hour to pick up the defective machine; this is where red flags went up.  There are dozens of posts regarding this unit starting fires, some in which the entire house burned.  There are even more posts from customers that are on their 5th and 6th Keurig coffee makers because they stop working.  Keurig knows there is an issue, and it's a serious safety issue, yet their response is to sweep it under the rug, collect the defective machine and send the customer a new one in hopes that they will keep their mouth shut.  Well, that does not work for me. If a company is knowingly putting people in harms way and refusing to do anything about it, I will make sure the proper people know.  They did tell me they were going to send an engineer to my home to inspect the machine and outlet, but as the scheduled day approached, they changed their minds.  We are now at a stand still, and in the meantime, millions of people have these units in their homes and offices and have no idea that they could potentially be in danger of losing everything.  These machines are defective and need to be recalled before someone gets hurt.
justification: The incident involved a melted power cord and burning outlet, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: The oven mitts that I purchased for my daughter melted onto a hot cookie sheet the first time she used them.  She was not injured but these are obviously a safety hazard if they do not provide the protection as intended.
justification: The incident involved oven mitts failing to protect as intended, but no injury occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with similar products.

incident_description:
The internal glass in the door of my built-In oven, Model Number 79048783900, installed February 11, 2014, exploded on Saturday March 19, 2016, leaving safety glass all over the floor of our kitchen.

There was no apparent damage or external cause for the incident.

Though numerous examples of this incident appear to have occurred (see links below), Sears Service has no answer for it, other than they will send some body to repair it at my cost.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass explosion causing safety glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that approximately six months ago, the three racks inside started falling down when something is placed on top of them.

The consumer states that his wife has gotten her fingers and her forearms burned on numerous occasions, which have been treated with a first aide kit by family members and herself.

The consumer states that the oven was used several times per week until they ceased use of it because of the safety hazard it poses.
