justification: The consumer's wife has suffered burns on multiple occasions, which were treated with first aid, indicating an injury severity level.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the can opener is advertised as leaving smooth edges once a can is opened. The consumer states that his wife cut her thumb with a can when she opened it once and they had to dispose of the can. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised to return the product to the retailer.
justification: The consumer's wife cut her thumb, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: When using one of the sauce pots from the cookware set (boiling water on stove top), there was a loud bang and one of the small metal rivets shot off.  I see there is a recall for the frying pans from the cookware set for the same issue, but no recall yet for the pots.  Not sure why this is, since they both look to be made the same way with with the same metal rivets.  Seems like that last recall was dangerously narrow.
justification: A rivet shot off but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The recall for similar cookware suggests this issue is likely to occur.

incident_description:
I have a gas cook top and electric slide-in oven with down-draft by Jenn-Aire.

The knobs to control the gas cooktop are unstable. Several times someone in my family has bumped against them while cooking and ignited a burner. Many times this has happened as someone was simply walking by and not cooking, left the room and returned later to the smell of gas in the kitchen.
justification: The unstable knobs have led to unintended gas ignition and gas leaks, posing a hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description: When we turned on our GE Profile dishwasher (model PDW9280J00SS), Serial number TG870036B,) one evening, we smelled a very sharp burning smell, like burned plastic.  When we opened up the dishwasher door, black smoke was pouring out of the small hole at the top of the control panel.  Further, the metal near that opening was almost too hot to touch.  We presumed that something had happened with the electric control panel in the dishwasher, so stopped it from running and turned off the circuit breaker
justification: The incident involved smoke and overheating but no injury or death occurred, and such electrical faults are uncommon but not unheard of in appliances.

incident_description:
I am reporting what I think is a serious safety issue with a gas cook top that I purchased in 2013.  It is a Frigidaire model FGDS3065KWF.  This is a dual utility unit with an electric oven and a gas cook top.  From its first use, we have had problems with the gas burners being blown out whenever the oven is in operation, allowing raw gas to continue to escape.  This also happens whenever the oven door is opened.  

Apparently, there is a fan that ventilates the top side of the oven that creates a negative pressure in the cavity below the gas burners.  If the burners are adjusted toward the low side, the flames can be completely sucked down, extinguishing them.  We have to keep a close eye on the burners whenever cooking while the oven is in operation.  This also requires us to set the burners higher than we want to keep them from blowing out.  The fan exhaust also blows out the front of the unit, just above the oven door, which seems to create turbulence over the burners as well.
justification: The incident involves gas burners being extinguished and raw gas escaping, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Electric glass oven
justification: The description 'Electric glass oven' suggests a potential incident scenario, such as burns or breakage, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: Was cooking dinner. I had used the broiler for maybe 10 minutes on high. I then turned the oven off, a minute or two later the glass on the front of the oven door just shattered to the floor. Glass was sizzling and popping in the air because it was so hot.
justification: The oven glass shattered but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: When operating the oven under normal conditions at 475ÃÂ° for 20 minutes the keypad melted.  The keypad is located above the gas range and the vent is located directly underneath that so when the oven vents all of the heat rises up in front of the keypad causing the whole panel to get excessively hot and consequently, melting the command keypad controls for the oven. I received second degree burns to my R hand, index and middle finger. I was treated by my husband, an emergency first responder. The oven range model No, is listed as Kenmore Gas Range 790.7231, 7233 P/N 316901016 Rev C. purchased in 9/2013 The range receives light, household use only and oven intermittent or infrequent use at normal temperatures. (Since melting, the keypad now inadvertently sounds the timer and flashes error code F11, according to the manual means keypad short.)  Since the incident, it has been necessary to unplug and re-plug in the range in order to use it: we cannot afford a new one at the moment so this has been more than a burden and safety issue with two infant children in the house, to pull the range out, plug it in and unplug it after every use. Thank you for your attention to this matter.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the described conditions and intermittent use.

incident_description:

Please call me,

incident_description:
Ever since we bought this LG Electric range 6 months ago we have had repeated problems with the cooktop turning on accidentally when we are working in the kitchen.  The knobs are large and protrude from the front of the stove at hip height.  They are easily bumped and turned on without us realizing it.  We have learned to be very careful and not put anything on the stove except what we are cooking.  Regardless, we have repeatedly often almost been burned by turning and unexpectedly finding a blazing hot burner with nothing on it.

We have limited counter space.  When we are not working in the kitchen, we sometimes place pots and pans on the cooktop to dry.  Today there was a pot on it drying on a dishtowel.  When my husband returned from the grocery store, there was almost no space on the counters.  He put one grocery bag on what little space there was on the counter and the other on the cooktop, being careful not to bump the knobs.  He went out to bring the other groceries in from the car and was gone only seconds.  He returned to find the groceries and the dish towel engulfed in flames and the smoke alarm screaming.  Luckily, he was able to sweep everything into the sink and douse the flames with water.  Upon further inspection it appeared what happened is what has frequently happened before.  Despite his care not to bump the knobs, the left-most knob got bumped when he turned away from the stove, without him realizing it.  Unfortunately, that knob, when it is bumped a little, turns to "Hi."  More unfortunately, that knob turns on the front left burner to "Ultra-Heat" which heats to high in a matter of seconds.  We are just fortunate that he returned so promptly, before the wall and ceiling in the kitchen ignited. 

This it the last straw for us.  This electric range is a fire and burn hazard and needs to be recalled to either be replaced or modified to allow for safe use.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury, and the description indicates this is a recurring issue that happens frequently despite precautions.

incident_description:
Outer GE oven glass door shattered unexpectedly while warming up pizza.
Model number JGBS18DENWW purchased in 2009 from PC Richards. I have never seen this before. EVER. No the glass was not previously damaged. I should have know better when I had 2 previously owned GE ovens at the same time break down at exactly 8 years with the same gas leak problem. GE has this down to a science. They know exactly what will break and when. I'm very upset. Now I worry for the 2 GE microwaves I currently have above my 2 GE ovens.
justification: The oven glass door shattered unexpectedly, but there was no injury reported.

 Classic Stainless Steel Easy Grip Apple Slicer Fruit Cutter Corer and Divider

incident_description:
Text of Consumer's letter dated February 10, 2016 addressed the President of Sears Holding:

RE: REFERENCE I# [REDACTED]

Kenmore Stainless Steel Dishwasher

Model# 58716073200

Serial# TH22990872

I am writing this letter to explain my disappointment with your company. On Saturday, February 6, 2016, I attempted to load my Kenmore Stainless Steel dishwasher and my middle two fingers, left hand, got trapped and was almost amputated in the opening of the dishwasher. I was unable to remove my fingers, I had to call the police and EMS to have my fingers remove. My fingers were wedged in the opening for more than 15 minutes. Can you imagine the amount of PAIN? As a result of this injury my fingers are now swollen and I have numbness and tingling to them.

I contacted your company on February 8, 2016 and explained my injuries and ask your customer service staff about claims and replacement of my unit. To date, I have not received a single call regarding my injuries. My wife made several calls and she was told a supervisor would be contact me. To date I have not been contacted. I hope this is in no way how you treat a loyal customer and not a reflection on the direction Sears is going.

I am very upset at the lack of resolve in this matter. My fingers has been numb and swollen for 5 days. I am requesting that you immediately contact me to replace your defective dishwasher. I am sure there has been numerous reported incidents about this particular Kenmore dishwasher. The opening framework is very dangerous and prone to injury.
justification: The incident resulted in injury with swollen and numb fingers, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the defect and the reported injury.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Oven directly shorted out. Electrical flashes were seen inside oven. Cooling fan behind over pushed sparks and smoke out front bezel. Direct shorting caused lighting in house to flicker. Breaker had to be manually tripped at circuit panel.

Upon inspection, terminal block caught fire. All wiring from block continuing into oven is burnt/melted. No external wiring was damaged not house wiring. No internal fuses failed. No heating elements are burned out. I believe issue most likely caused by onboard computer fault.

incident_description: Came home and found the lid to my Crock Pot Slow Cooker shattered.  It was still sitting on top of the crock pot.
justification: The incident involved a shattered lid but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description: I was injured by the "s" blade of the Ninja Mega Kitchen System 1500 Model BL773CO F15 Spring, while doing a refund on it at my job with Costco Wholesale.  I received 3 stitches in my left thumb and butterfly bandages on my left middle finger.  This model was sold on March 3rd 2016, used and then returned on March 11th 2016.  While putting all components of the system back into the box after verifying all of the product was present; protocol for a refund-the "s" blade sliced open my left thumb and left middle finger by reaching into the bowl to grab the shaft of the blade, instead the "s" blade cut me to the point of bleeding continually until I got to the health clinic for medical care and they took medical measures to stop the bleeding.  This unit is past the one recalled from those sold between March 2012 and September 2015.  When sharing my injury with friends I learned that this has happened to some of them and also to my sister.  Why is this product still available to the public?  It should have some sort of protective sleeve or blade protector.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring stitches and medical care, and similar incidents have been reported by others, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I was cooking fish in my Kenmore Elite oven and the interior glass exploded and cracked completely. I was cooking the fish at 400 degrees. I called Sears about this and ordered a new piece of glass from them. I asked Sears if this is common and could this happen again. They replied, yes it has happened and it could happen if you use your oven too much. I asked them is a technician could come out to make sure the oven is safe to use and they replied yes but would have to charge me the service call because there is not warranty on the oven. Sears won't stand behind their product.
I, myself or someone else in my family could have gotten seriously injured from this. If the glass chips/slivers would have fallen onto our food and we ate the food not knowing we could have consumed glass. Also, the g\exterior glass could have exploded too and flown everywhere. 
This is very dangerous and needs to be addressed. I'm nervous now to use my oven.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass exploding, which could have caused injury but did not in this case. The likelihood is rated as possible since Sears acknowledged it has happened before.

incident_description:
This caller's daughter moved into apartment complex late last Summer 2015 and while the caller and his wife were assisting her with cooking he noticed a safety issue with her electric range in January 2016.

The left rear burner there is a tube that allows hot air from the oven to come up through the center of the left rear burner.
He states that the safety hazard he is reporting is that there is no warning that the very back of the range can become extremely hot.  Also placing a pan or pot on the left rear burner while the oven is on causes the pan/pot to heat and potentially melt.

He is reporting that with this large hole creates a burn hazard when this heat is released if someone were to touch this area.

Another important fact is that the current design wastes a great deal of energy by letting the oven heat escape through the rather large tube installed between the oven top and the left rear burner.  For example, this design allows great amounts of heat to escape the oven, reducing the effectiveness of oven cooking and making it nearly impossible to cook oven meals at temperatures stated in the recipe.  As an example of how unreasonable this is, it takes an hour to heat the stove to 450 degrees because of the great escape of hot air allowed by the tube design.  Also, imagine how often the air conditioner will kick on to cool the kitchen when the oven is releasing so much heat into the room.  Also see attachments showing parts involved.

There are no injuries being reported at this time.

The caller contacted the manufacturer around the second week in January 21st, 2016 and was advised that this is the design and that there have been no injuries.
justification: The description reports a safety hazard with potential for burns but confirms no injuries have occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG gas range in September, installed in November.  From day one if you brush against the knobs, the gas comes on.  You don't have to push them in.  There is no clicking sound, so the
gas doesn't ignite, but escapes in the room.  The only way I know the gas is on is the odor of the gas.
I have been outside the house and come in after 30 minutes,  and smell the strong odor of gas.  I have contacted the manufacturer and they tell me there is no fix for this problem.  I have turned knobs on LG ranges on display and you have to push them in to get them to come on.  I have asked The Home Depot to make it right and they refuse.  LG won't fix it.  At this point I'm afraid there is going to be an explosion, because if I'm not here and the gas is no, no one will know it.  This has happened not only to me but to my daughter who lives here.  I really feel this is a hazard and an accident waiting to happen.  What can I do now?  There are no re-calls on this range that I can find.  Model No. is
LDG4315ST.  It's supposedly their top of the line range.
justification: The gas range's faulty knobs allow gas to escape without ignition, posing a significant explosion hazard, though no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Coffeemaker caught on fire. Coffee maker was plugged in but not on when it caught on fire. This caused a serious safety hazard at our home that could have caused death or serious injury.

Glass shards went everywhere, including into the dishwasher, causing knicks into the cabinets and hardwood floors.

incident_description:
Re: Kitchen Aid electric combination range with convection microwave on top and regular oven on bottom. Newly installed by builder's vendor 7/2015.

Situation: On 3/4/16 while roasting vegetables in the lower oven we heard a loud bang. We got up to find that the interior glass oven window had exploded inward into the oven, with some glass ejected onto and across the kitchen floor.

Result: The entire interior oven glass shattered and dispersed throughout the oven floor. There was also micro glass residue dust in the oven, and glass pellets and a few sharp shards ejected onto and across the kitchen runner carpets and floor.

Note: We had NOT caused any micro fractures to the glass by closing the door hard, impacting it with the oven racks, dropping something on it, etc.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (shattered glass) but no reported injuries, and the likelihood is deemed unlikely based on the provided data.

incident_description: We have an LG over-the-range microwave - model LMV1683ST - manufactured in January 2013. Last night my two young children and I were trying to pop a bag of popcorn for a snack before bedtime. I placed the bag into the microwave and pressed the POPCORN button.  Something we have done many times before.  The microwave had been on for about one minute and the popcorn had just started popping when I noticed the microwave flashing orange with flames of fire. I immediately made my way to the microwave and pressed the STOP button.  When I opened the door of the microwave there was some smoke inside and as the smoke cleared I noticed a hole in the top of the microwave that had been burned through. The smoke was from the melting plastic and the hole was about the size of a quarter dollar coin. I immediately stopped using the microwave and unplugged it from the wall outlet.  I then monitored it with a fire extinguisher in hand for several minutes to be sure there was no additional fires. The microwave is now no longer usable. I contacted the manufacturer, LG, and was told that because my microwave was outside of the 1 year warranty period (even though it is less than 3 years old) they would not cover it. The cost to fix it is more than the microwave is worth brand new. So essentially because of a defective product - I also previously had issues with some numbers on the key pad working that LG would not fix - I am out several hundred dollars to buy a new microwave and get it delivered and installed. This product is very dangerous! I am just happy that I was home and in the kitchen when this occurred or the fire may have spread and this could be much worse.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On Tuesday March 8, 2016 around 6:30AM (PST) our Viking Professional Gas Double-Wall Oven control panel burst into flame. The household electrical panel breaker had to be shut off to control the situation.  The household electrical panel breaker must remain off or the unit will catch on fire again and again.  Choking smoke from this electrical fire and burning filled the house.  The smokey smell of the burnt wiring remains to date though the house is repeatedly being aired out.  Control of the oven(s) was lost and they heated to their max until the gas was shut off.  Luckily someone was at the house at the time of this occurrence or an extremely serious fire would have occurred. Luckily we were all awake at the time of the occurrence or this situation would have resulted in multiple fatalities.
justification: The incident involved a fire and potential for multiple fatalities, indicating a high severity level, but the likelihood is reduced due to immediate intervention.

When brewing was complete, she went to take the cup sitting on the base of the unit, the base dislodged, the unit shook, and hot liquid from the brewer and the cup spilled onto her hand. incident_description:
My son has been using Tommee Tippee cups for the past year and a half. He started getting sick in November. We treated his coughing as a cold but it wouldn't heal. We finally took him to the doctor Feb 22, 2016 to have him looked at and he was diagnosed with respiratory airway restriction. He was given an inhaler. A few days later I saw on Facebook that a father had a child who was ill and he opened the valves on his Tommee Tippee cups and found mold. I was shocked. I opened my valves on three of my cups and sure enough, they were covered in mold. I called Tommee Tippee Careline and they offered to replace the valves and told me to return to the doctor to see if my son's issues could be from the mold. I did. And my son was prescribed another inhaler. The doctor said my son's illness could have been from the mold spores. I called the Careline back hoping they would pay for my son's treatment, in the very least and was told they would not. Without indisputable proof that his illness was from the mold, they wouldn't do anything other than replace the valves. 
I am convinced my otherwise healthy three year old became ill from the mold in these cups. We stopped using the cups, and he's starting to recover. The fact that this company cares so little for the actual health of its customers (they say they do but obviously it's just lip service) tells me this product needs to be recalled, in the very least, until they can guarantee the safety of our children.
justification: The child suffered from respiratory airway restriction and required medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her electric smooth-top range  purchased from retailer in Ohio November 18th, 2014.

January 23rd, 2016 she and her 7 year old granddaughter were baking when she accidentally bumped against the oven noticing that it was extremely hot and felt as if it could burn her.

She contacted the manufacturer who scheduled a repair tech who came to her home Monday, February 1st, 2016, inspected the range then advised the caller that because she had not purchased a self cleaning oven that her unit was not insulated and was cosmetic.

The consumer states that she purchased the range to be safely used for cooking and not for cosmetics.

There are no injuries being reported.

She sent an email to the manufacturer February 1st, 2016 after speaking with the repair tech but has not received a response.

She is asking that this range be inspected by the CPSC for consumer safety and that it become recalled as a potential hazard for injury due to burns.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a potential burn hazard. The likelihood is possible as the issue was identified during use.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her electric range purchased at home supply store May 2nd, 2013 in Kentucky.  
She had no problems with her range until Friday, January 22nd, 2016 when she was in her family room and heard a loud noise coming from the kitchen.

She went to the kitchen and saw that the outside glass of the oven door had exploded and thrown glass as far as three feet or more and as near as just in front of the unit.

The oven or range had not been used since around 6:00AM that same morning.

There are no injuries being reported

She has contacted the manufacturer who advised her that the unit is not recalled, she has no warranty and that she must pay for the repair.

She is asking that this model/serial number be recalled with repair at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the event without prior issues.

incident_description:
01/30/2016 - The consumer was cooking and approximately two or three minutes after she put the lid at an angle on the pot, the lid exploded and shattered into pieces.

The consumer indicates that the unit has been used once or twice prior to the day of the incident.
justification: The lid exploded but there is no mention of injury, so severity is 2. The incident occurred after limited use, suggesting it is unlikely but not rare.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting her smooth top electric range oven, purchased February 2006 in Rhode Island.

The caller had no problems with the unit until February 4th, 2016 when she placed a turkey in the oven, set it at 350 degrees then after only fifteen minutes she heard a crackling sound.
She returned to the kitchen then saw that 4 - 5 inch flames were coming from the front and control panel caught fire.  The caller opened the oven door and the flames extinguished themselves.

She scheduled repair with [REDACTED] who came to her home, witnessed that the control boards are burned and panels are burned and the unit is not actually worth repair.  

She is reporting this range as a potential fire hazard.  

There are no injuries being reported

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the knobs on the stove when turn on had a clicking sound, he then noticed that the rear knob started to emit flames.  The fire extinguisher was used to contain the fire.  The fire department was also called out and the gas was turned off.

2/11/16 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that a service technician would be sent out 2/12/16, the technician came out and reported back to the manufacturer.

Caller feels that the range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a stove emitting flames, which was contained without injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the immediate fire hazard and need for emergency response.

incident_description:
A Sears Kenmore electric range, Model 790.9260, Serial No. VF 11854810 purchased June 1,2011, on two occasions allowed the oven to exceed the set temperature.  The second time, November 23, 2015, it heated to the point of allowing the food to burst into flames when the oven door was opened.  It was set to 300 degrees, and 15 minutes later the house smoke alarms went off and when I entered the kitchen heavy smoke was coming out around door and under the display panel. I hit the stop button and opened the door, which is when the flames occurred, and an oven thermometer showed its maximum of 600 degrees with the glass broken. The normal allowable temperature a consumer can set is 550 degrees.
I knew enough to close the door, so I was not hurt and there was no damage to the house. The smoke dissipated
after the doors where open for while.
Attached is my letter to Sears Holdings.
Sears did provide a small refund against the next range and Iam not looking for further compensation.
The design obviously allows the oven to exceed the maximum cooking temperature and rise Into the cleaning temperature without the automatic door lock activating.
justification: The incident involved the oven overheating and causing flames, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
I TURNED ON MY ELITE PLATINUM ELECTRIC PRESSURE COOKER AND 5 MINUTES LATER IT CAUGHT ON FIRE BURNING IT AND MY STOVE THAT IT WAS SITTING ON.
THE FIRE DEPARTMENT RESPONDED, MY HOUSE WAS FULL OF BLACK SMOKE FROM THE MELTING PLASTIC.
AFTER IT WAS PUT OUT WE DETERMINED THAT THE THERMOSTAT INSIDE THE BOTTOM OF THE UNIT SHORTED OUT AND CAUGHT FIRE.
WE'VE MADE NUMEROUS ATTEMPTS TO CONTACT THE MANUFACTURER (MAXI-MATIC) LOCATED IN CALIFORNIA. WE'VE SENT PICTURES OF THEIR FAULTY UNIT, MY BURNED STOVE, AND ALL THE BLACK SMOKE DAMAGE. 
THIS WAS THE 4TH TIME I HAD USED THIS UNIT. IT WAS PURCHASED IN DECEMBER 2015.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:

and learned quickly it overheats. Smooth top and self cleaning oven which I am told not to use but to use EASY Off Instead by the Samsung technician, not once but twice. Samsung called them after I finally got through to Samsung. A new stove almost $2,500 with Installation that was sold as self cleaning is NOT. 1st the pot stuck to the cook top it gets too got. It happened again after it was replaced at our expense, Samsung would not honor the warranty we purchased.  I have repeatedly called HHGREGG and Samsung and get the run around. The technician said Samsung has not figured out how to control the temperature. Oven locks up in self cleaning mode and they have to come and fix it. TO not use it. He told me 2x. Cooktop heats up and 2 pots stuck to it. I found many complaints online with the same problem. They say it locked up, explodes, caught on fire and burned a house down. I have a bedridden daughter living with us that I take care of 24/7/365 she was exposed to mold and carbon monoxide in her house, close to the kitchen, and I am not willing to risk her life or cause her more harm. I asked for this stove to be exchanged soon after purchase and for nothing but the run around, still do. How can I get that stove replaced because right now I can only use the cook top and very carefully. It seems Samsung has a heat control issue with this model. Thank you. When this happens, the gas does not shut off and gas continues to flow into the air. incident_description:
This caller is reporting his over the range microwave with dom March 2007 purchased from retailer  around 2008-2009 in Ohio.

Around January 24th, 2016 the caller's wife was planning to re-heat some food but when she turned the microwave on she and her caller who is her husband noticed smoke coming out of the vent, the husband turned the unit off and unplugged it.  

He took it to his garage, turned it on to check it but it immediately burst into flames inside the unit and behind the control buttons.

He contacted the manufacturer sometime around January 26th - 27th, 2016 then scheduled a service tech.

The service tech came to his home the very end of January or first week in February 2016.

After the service technician checked the microwave out he stated that the transformer and the magnetron were at fault and that even if the unit could be repaired that the odor of burning plastic and electricity would not dissipate. 

He stated that he would submit his report and the  manufacturer would contact them.

The manufacturer did not contact the caller within a couple of days so he and his wife contacted them.

They were informed that because of the age they would offered a $288 microwave unit for the price of $320 which would include removal of the old unit, delivery and set up of the new unit.

There are no injuries being reported
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames from a microwave but no injuries were reported, making it a non-injury incident. Such occurrences are unlikely but not rare for aging appliances.

incident_description:
The consumer does not remember where he purchased the dish from. The consumer believes he purchased the dish about 7-10 years ago.

(2/7/16) The consumer used the dish to roast a chicken. The oven was set at 475 degrees. The consumer states the dish was in the oven for about 20 minutes when he heard a loud explosion. The consumer then opened the oven and noticed pieces of glass were everywhere inside the oven. The consumer states the entire dish shattered to pieces. The consumer threw the pieces of glass in the trash.

The consumer had used the dish to make chicken multiple times over the years and never had an incident. 

The consumer plans to contact the firm. 

The consumer states the oven was not damaged.
justification: The dish shattered but there was no injury or damage to the oven, indicating a minor incident.

incident_description:
10/15/2016 (Approximately) - The consumer put some coffee in the microwave. When finished, he removed the coffee mug from the unit and closed the microwave door. Approximately two or three seconds later when the consumer turned around and started walking away, the unit turned on by itself. The consumer immediately pressed the STOP button but this did not work. The microwave only stopped when the consumer opened its door. When he closed it again, the unit did not turn back on.

The consumer indicates that altogether the same incident has occurred five or six times with him and his wife in the same manner. The consumer is very concerned because he does not know if the unit has or possibly can turn on without prior immediate use by itself, especially when nobody is home.

02/09/2016 - The consumer indicates that the same incident happened except this time, he opened and closed the door four or five times and the unit would not shut off at all. After four or five minutes of dealing with this, the unit finally shut off when he closed the door.

The consumer plans on unplugging the unit. The consumer indicates that he uses his unit five to ten times a day per day.

The consumer contacted the brand firm and explained the situation. The representative he spoke to asked him what was displayed on the microwave panel and the consumer informed them that the same thing that is always displayed when the unit runs by itself: the clock. The consumer provided product and contact information. He was informed that he would receive a call back.

Shortly after, the consumer received an e-mail from the brand firm indicating that he cut off the power cord from the unit and to mail it back to them. The e-mail also asked that the consumer e-mail them photos of the unit's product information. The e-mail states that the consumer would then after receive a replacement microwave. The consumer plans on following orders.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported in the incidents described.

incident_description: Within minutes of running the dishwasher and then heading upstairs, we smelled an electrical burning smell. We raced to the kitchen to find smoke billowing from the dishwasher. After unplugging the machine and letting it cool down, we realized that the source of the smoke was just behind the buttons. We disconnected the machine and found that the circuit board had burned a hole through all of the board, plus the housing and mount, and was burning through the front of the dishwasher door.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I purchased an LG Electric Range (LRE30453ST), on January 14, 2012.  The ranges has required replacement of the circuit boards and heating elements on five occasions since 2012.   The most recent incident nearly burned my house down.  The range had an "F9" error code, which is an indication that the oven is over heating.  The estimated temperature of the over is 700 - 1,000 degrees.  The oven would not shut down because the digital control panel melted, and I was unable to touch the unit because of the extreme external surface temperature.  I had to turn the unit off as the circuit breaker.  The unit needs to be recalled because fire safety concerns.
justification: The incident involved a severe overheating issue that nearly caused a fire, posing significant fire safety concerns, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My child has been drinking out of Tommee Tippee sippy cups for approximately 2 years. We found mold in two of the spill proof valves last week even though we followed the manufacturer cleaning instructions!!! We immediately threw away all the valves! Then this week we saw an article stating mold has been found inside the spouts of these same sippy cups! We immediately stopped using them. We have 10 cups that we can no longer use. They were so expensive!! Not to mention our child has been fighting sickness for many many months! This is probably why!! We have calls into our doctors.
justification: The child has been fighting sickness for months, likely due to mold exposure, indicating an injury. Mold in sippy cups is a recurring issue, making occurrence likely.

incident_description: In the summer of 2015 I purchased a baby cup aka a sippee cup made by Tommee Tippee.  My daughter transitioned from a bottle to water in this cup successfully.  I followed the detailed instructions on how to clean this cup and sterilized it periodically.  In October 2015 my now 19 month old daughter started getting repeated nasal and chest congestion which included a terrible cough for which she had a chest xray done to rule out pneumonia.  Her illness continued almost constantly till this date.  A friend forwarded me a photo taken by a fellow parent of the inside valve of this cup which the consumer is unable to access.  It was infested with black mold.  My friend immediately advised me to inspect my cup as mold may also be present and be the cause of my daughters continuous ailments.  I pryed the valve open with a wire cutter and after about 15 minutes I got it open and found a large amount of black mold on the inside.  These cups should be recalled immediately.
justification: The incident describes a child suffering from repeated nasal and chest congestion due to mold in a sippee cup, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Product has an enclosed single piece valve that is impossible to open and access the inside allowing liquid to remain even after through cleaning and shaking resulting in mold growth. No amount of santization after allows dor the complete cleanliness of the product.
justification: The product design flaw leads to mold growth, which could cause health issues if ingested, indicating a potential for injury.

incident_description:
12/05/2015 - The consumer was cooking lunch when the front and left burner got stuck on HIGH and would not shut off despite attempts. The only way the consumer was able to turn off the burner was to switch off the circuit breaker supplying electricity to the range. When the consumer switched the circuit breaker back on, the front and left burner turned back on, despite the knob being in the OFF position. The circuit breaker was switched off overnight and switched back on the morning of 12/06/2015. Approximately twenty minutes later, the consumer noticed that the same burner had turned back on again on HIGH. The consumer switched the breaker off and has kept it that way with the exception of when she has to cook.

12/06/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the situation. She was informed that her range was not included in any of their recalls and so they would not be able to provide any assistance free of charge since the product was also out of warranty.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that posed a safety hazard but did not result in injury or death.

He stated that the smoke alarm went off and while he was trying to unplug the dishwasher it was overwhelmingly hot, he was finally able to do so.

incident_description: On January 5, 2016 I started my Farberware Crock Pot that I purchased from Walmart. Model #104554. 90-120 minutes later the crock pot exploded and my kitchen then caught on fire. Pieces of the crock pot were scattered all over the house. If someone had been in the kitchen when it happened it may have killed them. I have tried numerous times to contact Farberware. They say they only put their name on it. They are not responsible for it. I have been directed to several different companies after that but nobody will claim the product. I have a fire report that stated it was not an electrical fire. It started in the crock pot. I feel like this product is unsafe and Farberware is putting other consumers at risk because they do not want to take responsibility for a product that they put their name on.

incident_description: Last evening I turned the oven on to preheat and a few minutes later after I had gone into another room, I heard a pop. I went to the kitchen and saw arcs of electricity, great puffs of grey smoke and flames roaring out of the back of the stove. I turned the oven off and sprayed water on the wall in back of the stove because I was afraid it would ignite and burn the house down. I called 911 and told them the flames were out but I wanted a fireman to check to be sure the stove would not later start a fire.The firemen pulled the stove away from the wall, unplugged it and told me not to use it again The stove is a Kenmore electric smoothtop range purchased 12/11/07 from a Sears store in Waterville, ME
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the stove, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire Electric Glass-Top Stove/Oven Model # FEF366DCE. When I awoke this morning, I went into my kitchen, turned on my light and before I even saw it, stepped onto a bunch of broken pieces of glass.  I turned to find my oven exterior door had shattered all over the floor into many small pieces and some sharp shards of glass. The glass extended all the way across my large kitchen at least 5 feet away from the oven.  I had socks on, so I only got two small cuts on the bottom of my left foot and none on my right, but did receive some minuscule cuts on my hands when I tried to clean up the mess. Several big pieces of glass were still stuck in the door, but was cracked into many pieces and when I touched it to try to clean up the area, it shattered as well all over the floor and in the drawer under the stove. I don't know how or why this glass shattered, as I have not used the stove or oven in the past 2 weeks, since I live alone and have been making sandwiches in my toaster oven or salads. I haven't turned the oven on at all in over 3 months since I have a convection toaster oven that I use for everything. I didn't bump the door or stove, haven't cleaned it recently, I've never used the self-cleaning feature, nor have slammed the door or rested anything on the door. It happened without any exterior cause that I am aware of.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (small cuts on the foot and hands) from broken glass, but no severe harm or death.

incident_description: Frigidaire professional series, smooth-top range, with a defective heating element that spontaneously heated as described in previous product recall of nearly 200,000 units back in 2009.  My unit is newer than those in the recall and as a result, I was told Frigidaire can do nothing to assist even though this is the exact same problem and a well documented issue.  Multiple heating areas came on without power being turned on to them which resulted in a small fire from a storage container that was resting on the stove-top.  If any controls are turned to "on", there is an immediate cracking sound, followed by a loud "pop" and sparks/flames can be seen beneath the glass top.  Had I not been present at the time that the fire occurred, there is no reason to believe that it wouldn't have engulfed the home as there were hand-towels also in the area that would have aided in the fire's growth.
justification: The incident resulted in a small fire and potential for significant property damage, indicating injury risk, and the issue is documented but not widespread.

incident_description:
I severely sliced the palm of my right hand while attempting to slice a potato to make potatoes au gratin. It require 9 stitches and was so deep that much of the area did not heal with skin, but with scar tissue. 
This happened nearly 2 months ago, and the sliced area is still tender and bulges out.  This appears to be a permanent condition as is it is all scar tissue and there has been no change fort the past 2 weeks.
The product is called a "Mandoline" by "essentialhome" (TM). There are no markings on the product indicating how to use it, and if there were instructions that came with it they must have been lost. When I was at the Urgent Care to get the stitches, the doctor remarked that she had seen several others who had come in with bad cuts from the same product.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring stitches and causing permanent scar tissue, and the doctor noted multiple similar cases from the same product.

incident_description: After seeing posts on social media about mold found in the Tommee Tippee Sippee Cups, I decided to open one of the spouts of my child's cup. Sure enough, there was some gunk, possibly mold growing inside of the spout. I had just run the spout through the dishwasher, with the "sanitize" option selected. There was no mold, gunk, or whatever visible. It wasn't into we broke open the spout, that the gunk was found. I'm wondering if this could be why my twins have been getting diarrhea! It can't be safe for Babies to drink from these cups, if parents can't get them clean the way any normal person would clean them.
justification: The presence of mold in the sippee cups has potentially caused diarrhea in the twins, indicating an injury.
