incident_description: On 02/25/16 I was preparing dinner for my family using the Power Pressure Cooker XL.  I had selected the soup option and set the timer for 25minutes.  When the timer went off notifying me that the cooking was complete, I turned the pressure release valve allowing the pressure to escape.  I let this action continued for over 15 minutes until the valve dropped and no other pressure released.  I then went to turn the lid to remove when  the pressure from the cooker exploded causing hot scalding soup to erupt all over my kitchen and myself.  I received second degree burns on my left hand and right breast.  My doctor prescribed Silvadene to help with the healing process and deter infection, but will  be going for a would check to ensure it is healing properly.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity level 3). Pressure cooker explosions are possible but not extremely common, hence an occurrence likelihood of 3.

incident_description: Kitchenaid double oven glass exploded during first use of self cleaning cycle.  Glass was not damaged prior to the explosion.  Shards of glass went across the room at the time of the explosion and we were cleaning glass for weeks afterward.  Kitchenaid would not replace the shattered glass.  We are making a second inquiry to request replacement.  Kitchenaid is fully aware of the danger of the exploding glass and the fact that the explosion could cause serious injury or worse.  This product needs to be recalled and at a minimum, the defective glass should be replaced.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven glass that scattered shards across the room, posing a risk of injury but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer states that after approximately a year of use, the front and right burner had been sparking but not lighting. The burner has been replaced three times but it never fixed the issue permanently. The first and second time that it was repaired, the unit worked for a couple of months, after it ceased lighting once again. The lighting issue seems to have been fixed the third time that it was repaired on 03/16/2015. After the repair, the consumer sporadically noticed the glass atop the burner was turning black. 

Approximately on 10/30/2015, the Fire Department went to his home because the carbon monoxide alarm went off. The Fire Department determined that the stove was the culprit. They told the consumer the reason why the carbon monoxide alarm did not go off any sooner is because the home was usually kept with windows open since it was Summer. 

The manager, [REDACTED], from Reliable Repair took his lead technician to inspect the consumer's range and both determined that the same burner is not burning the gas properly, thus releasing carbon monoxide above average levels.

The consumer indicates that the unit is now one week out of his extended warranty and so he cannot receive assistance without paying out of pocket.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove releasing carbon monoxide, a serious safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My wife bought a Top Chef automatic drip coffee maker from Family Dollar in the last part of 2015.  Two weeks ago it developed a melted burn hole by hot plate and upon investigation, found the power wire to water pump had shorted out causing arching.  We quit using it and bought  a [REDACTED] model from Walmart which is working fine.  I have a photo of the hole but couldn't get a clear shot of wire.  This is a product made in China and cannot find a way to contact manufacture.
justification: The coffee maker developed a melted burn hole due to a short circuit, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The Tommee Tippee sippy cup contains a spill proof valve that cannot be taken apart and cleaned thoroughly. Because of this no matter how much I bleach or boil, it grows mold. I use the cup as directed only using pulp free juices and water, I shake all the water out after washing and let it air dry completely. I even go as far as to try to blow excess water out , and still my sippy cup valve has molded. Many parents are reporting this same problem in North American and in Europe.
justification: The incident involves mold growth in a sippy cup, which can lead to health issues if ingested, hence severity level 3 (Injury). The widespread reports from multiple regions indicate a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Dishwasher was not working on Thursday, Feb 25;  my husband began to investigate on Friday, Feb 26 and noticed scorch marks on the wall around the outlet.  Due to time constraints he did not investigate further until today, Feb. 27.  He found the wall outlet partially melted and the plug partially melted with one of the prongs damages.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher and electrical damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We purchased a subzero IT-30CIID refrigerator last October from Paul's Appliances in New Jersey, It was delivered without an anti-tipping bracket. My contractor installed the unit shortly after. On February 7th, 2016m while i was taking food out from the freezer and putting into the refrigerator, the unit tipped over and fell on me. I suffered cuts and bruises. Thankfully my wife and 1.5year old daughter was not present or they could have suffered major injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts and bruises, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) given the specific circumstances of the missing anti-tipping bracket.

incident_description:
GE Profile - Electric Stove. Model  JP989BK1BB - Serial # TM2 55451Q
Bought the stove but didn't use it right away. As our 20 yr old GE stove stopped working on thanksgiving day. bought this stove. but got the part for our old stove so we used it. moved this one into another room. a couple of yrs later, my mom passed and I got rid of her old 20 yrs + working GE double oven stove and moved the new one into the spot.
I barely use the stove as I never cook. I make some tea, fry a little.
 First the right large rear burner on my GE Profile stove did not shut off but the red light was on. I played with it a bit and turned the know a lot and finally it shut off. Now 6 months to a yr later, my nephew moves in and is cooking with the stove a lot. Same thing with the rear right burner, on with the red light and won't shut off. he has to unplug it. wait a while, hr or so, and when we plug it back in, it is fine. now the left rear large front burner, stays on low heat but switch is off and no red light. this is more dangerous. it was on all day. I made tea in the am and when I came home at 6 pm it was on. we could not get it to shut off. we unplugged it for a bit and it was still on. we unplugged it over night and it was fine in the am. but I am calling a repair man as this is dangerous.
justification: The stove burner staying on poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Normal use of Kenmore 790.9611 stove. Often, the front left burner will not function correctly in the following ways: 1) after turning dial to a "high" setting the burner will briefly warm up and then turn off. The Element On light remains on, but the light above the dial is off, 2) when trying to use a low heat, the burner will either not turn on or will burn on high, turn the dial to Off and then back to a low heat solves this sometimes, 3) burner will remain on high and will not turn off. When this happens, we have to turn the dial to Off/High/Low/Off or any combination, it takes a few minutes but the burner usually shuts off. These events have worsened over the last two years. For 2016, we have already had this happen at least 10 times.
justification: The burner malfunctions but there is no mention of injury or death, only operational issues.

incident_description: While cooking a pork roast (small) on a cookie sheet lined with aluminum foil at 450 degrees, the inside oven glass shattered at approximately 16 minutes into cooking. The oven was properly preheated to 450 and the pork roast was seared on all 4 sides for 10 minutes prior to entering the oven.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering, but there was no mention of injury, making the severity level 2. Such occurrences are rare, hence likelihood 1.

incident_description: Pitcher was being used to make tea.  After glass pitcher with metal diffuser inside, I turned to get something off another counter, and it shattered.  This pitcher had been used several times before, there was nothing different in how it was being used this time (followed the instructions).  I received minor cuts to my arm.  Luckily I had turned or the glass would have hit my face.
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts to the arm, indicating an injury (severity 3). The pitcher had been used several times without issue, suggesting the likelihood is unlikely (2).

incident_description: My husband and I were in the bed asleep and I was woken by a loud glass shattering noise. I thought someone was breaking in the house, we got up to check and saw nothing. I decided to cook a cobbler and went to open the cabinet to get my Anchor 4 cup measuring cup out and noticed it was in a million pieces. I have never used it and nothing was hot or cold around the cup. It spontaneously burst.
justification: The incident involved a measuring cup spontaneously breaking, causing no injury but creating a disturbance.

incident_description: On 12/27/2016 my Whirlpool Gold Series range, which was less than a year old, exploded, like a bomb, while I was making breakfast for my family.  I had been using a burner and had it turned down low and I started the broiler so I could put the pan in to brown the frittata.  I started the broiler and then went to the pantry to get the bagels and as I was putting the bagels in the toaster, my range exploded.  It blew over a foot away from the wall, the oven door flew open, knobs blew off, it blew the trim off of my cabinets.  Whirlpool decided to replace the range, sight unseen with a new range, same make and model.  When turning the broiler on in the new range, one of two things happen, neither being the expected broiling feature.  1.) The broiler will ignite and then the flame goes out after approximately 40 seconds.  There is no indication that it shut off.  The display still reads as if the broiler is on. 2.) The broiler will ignite and anywhere between 30 seconds to 2 minutes later, a fiery red flame starts shooting out of the broiler orifice in the back of the oven.  Whirlpool has been less than responsive throughout this whole process. I had to post on social media (Facebook) in order to get someone to return my phone call about this.  I believe there is a potential safety issue for other consumers.  here is a link to a video that shows what the new range does: [REDACTED]
justification: The range exploded violently, causing significant property damage and posing a clear risk of injury or death, though none were reported in this instance.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore Elite Oven combo model number 790.4890 in 2011. For the past 6 months, the oven racks fall off the sides when something is placed in the oven. We've changed the racks around and tried different fixes but they keep falling. About a month ago, I had a casserole in the oven and went to check on it and the rack just fell and I was burned on my arm. 

We have contacted numerous customer service people at Sears and no one will help us. They will send a repair person, but at a cost for us. I think because this is a safety hazard, we should not be charged. Since this has happened, we looked up this model on the internet and there have been numerous complaints regarding this identical issue. 

I am asking for an investigation and help with this issue before I am burned again.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the issue is recurring with multiple complaints reported, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Caller stated that there was a loud noise, oven emitted sparks and smoke while preheating.  She stated that she noticed that there was burnt hole at the back wall of the oven.  The breaker was used to switch the power off.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that the oven is a fire hazard.
justification: The oven emitted sparks and smoke, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The left rear burner of the range spontaneously turned on. When I turned the dial to the "on" position, the numbers in the display were changing but not in a consistent manner with the dial, it was more random. When I turned the dial back to the "off" position, the burner remained on.  So I pulled the range out from the wall and unplugged it. 

About an hour later, hoping it would reset itself, I plugged the range back into the outlet and the dials all beeped and each display was lit for a couple seconds, then the display for each of the other 3 burners went off, while the display for the left rear burner stayed on displaying "Err". It wasn't getting hot, so thought it was OK to leave plugged in and I just wouldn't use that burner until we had it serviced.  

About 2 hours later, the burner spontaneously turned on again. I again unplugged the range from the wall outlet and have not used it since.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue was managed by unplugging the range.

incident_description:
This is the product I'm reporting: http://www.anchorhocking.com/prodd_5790_cat_7_2_qt_bistro_pitcher_w_white_stopper.html

I was making tea with this pitcher. I'd been using it about a month for this purpose. The pitcher was in no way damaged.  I was pouring hot water into the pitcher to steep the tea and the pitcher exploded. The pitcher was less than a foot in front of me as I poured the water from the tea kettle into the pitcher. The boiling water and glass shot out towards my body. I suffered 2nd degree burns across my stomach and down my right leg covering my thigh from my hip to my knee.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the pitcher exploding under normal use conditions.

incident_description: The first time I tried to remove the wine bottle stopper I recieved a puncture wound to my finger caused by a metal burr or shard that was protruding from the lower edge of the ball portion of the stopper.
justification: The description mentions a puncture wound to the finger, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Broken plastic on the inside of Gas Range Burner knobs are causing a issue knowing when gas burners are off.  This is a LG stove model lrg30357st
justification: The broken plastic on the burner knobs could lead to difficulty in determining if the gas is off, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: GE Advantium Oven caught fire while attempting to use the speed cook setting.  Just after starting the speed cook setting, smoke started coming out of the unit.  It smelled like an electrical fire.  We've only had the unit 1 yr 6 months and is no longer under warranty.
justification: The oven caught fire and emitted smoke, indicating an incident with no reported injury.

incident_description: I was making chili in my Rival Crock Pot (Model 5070) and I had been cooking it for a couple of hours.  Suddenly I heard a loud pop!  I saw that the lid had cracked into many pieces.  Looked like the way a windshield shatters.  The pieces were small, about a little less than a half in inch square. There were also a few thin shards on the top of the crock pot.  I was not cut, but what if this had happened when I was stirring the chili with the lid in my hand?  Of course I had to throw out all that chili and start over in my smaller pot.  I was not aware that this could happen, then I looked it up on the web and found that there have been 20 or so other cases.  This is a really dangerous problem.  When my husband was truing to help me clean it up, a lot of the glass wound up on the counter and the floor! What a mess. If I had small children around or a little dog  they could have been cut.
justification: The incident involved a cracked lid with potential for injury but no actual harm occurred, and similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description: The right front burner is burning fire red hot in the off position.  Have unplugged and replugged unit from outlet and same result, tried to reset by pressing the low to high indicator on dashboard but the right front burner unit stays fire hot.  This could cause surrounding damage if unattended.  This could result in human safety issue, as range unit is burning in the off position fire hot red.
justification: The burner is malfunctioning and could cause surrounding damage or a safety issue, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Description of hazardous incident and safety concerns:
During normal use of operation, on 12/7/2015 it was noticed that the porcelain oven liner in our GE
Monogram range which was put in use in March 2014, was flaking off in 2 areas and leaving small glass
shards on the bottom of the oven. They are very sharp and vary in size from approximately .5" long x
.OS" wide down to small grains (see pictures of samples and some areas involved). When wiping these
areas one of the pieces penetrated the cloth and stuck a finger like a sliver. Since then we now wear
gloves to protect our hands when cleaning as each time the oven is used new porcelain slivers are found
scattered around the bottom of the oven- not just adjacent to the 4 current areas (two new since
12/7/2015) where the porcelain has flaked off.
In addition to our hands, we are extremely concerned that the glass shards will contaminate our food
baked in the oven due to the fact they are found throughout the oven floor as noted above. We have
stopped using the convection bake for fear the fan will distribute the slivers even to the upper racks.
GE was notified on 12/8/2015 of the problem. Many discussions since that date with a GE
representative has only resulted in them claiming it is nothing more than a "cosmetic issue" and they
deny our safety concerns and also the fact that we are forced to wear gloves when wiping out the oven.
We did not do anything to cause the problem as we have not applied anything to the porcelain other
than the manufacturers recommended materials. In fact we have not even used the self- cleaning
function since installation and do not know what effect that high temperature would do to the suspect
coating. The porcelain coating is obviously defective yet they refuse to acknowledge that fact. The
range is still under warranty but we've been told by an appliance tech that the liner is non replaceable.
justification: The incident caused injury (a finger puncture) and poses ongoing risk of injury and food contamination.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she and her family  received CO poisoning from the range.  She stated that she had been feeling ill and then her husband started to feel ill the date of incident. The CO alarm went off,the fire department was called, and who in turn  called for the Hazmat team.  Hazmat called for EMS who conveyed her and her family  to the Detroit Receiving Hospital emergency. They were treated and released, where  they had to stay in a hotel.  She had noticed these health  symptoms for about  2 weeks prior, which included headaches, eventually followed by intermittent vision loss flashes followed by blurry vision, hearing impairment and chest pain.  She suffered  confusion the day of incident.

10/2/15   The gas company  came out for inspection and declared that the CO came from the gas range. The gas company  left a pink slip, stating that the range is dangerous and hazardous, and is not to be repaired, but replaced by the manufacturer.

The corporate offices of the store chain (where the range was purchased}  was contacted on 10/2/2015 about the incident, and someone phoned  her back on 10/06/2015, informing her that  a claim number (REDACTED) was in process and that she should send all reports and medical  bills to her.  Also, the representative stated that she was going to contact the manufacturer of the stove, so they could arrange for pick-up  of the stove for testing.  On,11/6/2015, she received a call from the representative for the store chain, not to contact her anymore, and that  all contact,medical bills and reports should be forwarded to the manufacturer. On, 11/5/2015, same date, a representative from  the manufacturer phoned  her, informing her that he was from Risk Management, and he also handles medical bills and reports. Claimant informed  him, that  the corporate rep. for the store chain, requested that she not contact her anymore, that he (representing the manufacturer), would be handling the incident moving forward. Per the rep for the manufacturer, he would give her a call. The manufacturer generated a claim number.  On 11/11/2015,the claimant faxed the manufacturer copies of the Fire Dept./Hazmat/EMS report ,Gas Company report, and Medical Bills and receipts received up to that point.  As of 02/24/2016, Electrolux hasn't arranged for pick-up of the stove for testing, therefore, no compensation for stove or medical bills has been received.

Caller feels that this range is dangerous and should be investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in CO poisoning with multiple health symptoms requiring hospital treatment, indicating injury.

incident_description: While using our Kenmore range on the bake setting our broiler element turned itself on.  I tried to turn off the oven, but realized that the control panel had started on fire.  We immediately unplugged the oven and put the flames out.  This range is not safe.  This was not a neglect or overuse issue.  There is no reason that the electrical connections should start on fire.  Our range is kept clean and only occasionally used.  If not addressed by the manufacturer I'm afraid that this range will continue to start house fires that put families in danger.  When I contacted Kenmore they refused to comment on whether they were aware of the design flaws in this range.  They told me they only way they would investigate was if I paid to have a service technician come to my home to inspect the range.  The customer rep explained that they would not do anything because the warranty on the range had expired.  I explained that I believed this item should be investigated for recall, but she refused to take any information from me.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly controlled without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the described design flaw and lack of manufacturer response.

incident_description: We recently stumbled across Recall number: 12737 when trying to report a problem with a different small appliance and felt we needed to report this as we have the exact same model Frigidaire Gas Range with what sounds like the same problem, but a slightly different serial number and ours was purchased in April 2012, intead of March of 2012. Ours was also purchased from Lowes, same price point, same issue with the top oven burner/broiler having ignition delay that would lead to a strong gas smell, buildup and then a bit of a pop as it ignited finally that we had reported to the company shortly after it was installed.  We were told that there was nothing to worry about and all gas ovens did this to some extent and we were being overcautious and as long as it was lighting they wouldn't even send a technician because basically "people were always worried about this and they would send techs and then there was nothing wrong and then they'd have to charge us for it and we would be angry".  Skeptical, but unsure, we took their word for it and decided to keep a close eye on things. About a year later we called back in as I had used the self clean function (very careful to follow the instruction manual as we were already a little leery of the oven) and after the cleaning cycle was completed the top burner and broiler function would no longer light. Unfortunately, we were several days out of warranty (I don't remember exactly how much, but less than 3 weeks-it was the end of april or first week of may) and of course since the warranty had expired they could do nothing for us other than to send a tech out and bill us for whatever repairs were necessary. When I stated that this was an issue that I had brought to their attention much earlier and been told was "nothing and overreaction" they mysteriously could find no record of that call.  Now seeing Recall number: 12737 I am wondering if our problem was more dangerous than we realized and it sounds like the same issue.  We have not since been able to get it repaired due to financial concerns and are starting to smell gas more often emanating from the top burner area when we turn on the oven and are concerned it is becoming more dangerous. Frigidaire is unwilling to take any repair responsibility. Please let us know how to proceed.
justification: The incident involves a gas range with ignition delay and gas smell, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
Frigidaire electric range purchased around 2008.   When shutting off the oven I saw a large amount of smoke coming from a plastic container that was set on the stove top. The plastic container was melting and starting to burn, at which point I noticed the burner surface was red and the display for the burner was spontaneously changing settings.   The dial for the burner in question was in the off position. Once the plastic container was moved from the stove dripping some burning plastic, I went to the garage and flipped the oven breaker.   My wife stayed with the Frigidaire oven to make sure nothing else happened while I was in the garage.    
This Frigidaire oven model has a recall for the same problem but our serial number falls outside the ranges covered by the recall by nine numbers.    All Frigidaire was willing to do was sell me an extended warranty for $419.    It is very disturbing that my stove is doing the exact thing that the recall covered and the manufacturer doesnÃÂt care.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove causing smoke and melting plastic, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the metal disc that covers the pan's rivet heated and shot off. The consumer stated that the disc hit the wall on the other side of the room. He has not been able to find the disc.

The consumer went into Macy's. They informed him that this was not purchased from them because the number did not match the recall.

The consumer purchased the pan as an individual item and not a part of a set. The consumer has been using the pan for over 1.5 years. 

The consumer stated that his pan has the same hazard as the ones recalled under # 16-067.
justification: The metal disc shot off but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
(11/26/2015) The consumer stated that she was baking bread stuffing in the dish. The setting of the oven was set at 350 degrees. About twenty-five minutes after she put the stuffing in the oven, she smelled food burning. She opened the oven and discovered that the baking dish had shattered. The sides of the casserole had exploded. Particles of glass was on the floor of the oven. There were also large shards of glass in the oven. 


(11/26/2015) The consumer emailed the firm. She received a response on 11/27 advising the consumer to send in every piece of glass including food that was stuck to the glass. The consumer also sent photos.

The consumer sent several inquires to [REDACTED], the Consumer Response Representative. The contact phone number is [REDACTED].Her email address is [REDACTED]. The consumer was advised that the product was received at the lab. The consumer was advised that she would be contacted when results are received form the lab.

The consumer added Pyrex glass from shattered dish was found at 3 levels inside conventional gas oven, and all food, including turkey and ham, and other casseroles had to be tossed because of glass particles throughout the oven.

The consumer also added the manufacturer sent her a letter saying the 4 quart Pyrex dish had  been braised and chilled prior to baking. The consumer noted the information was false, and her 10x15 dish holds only 16 cups and it went directly from room temperature to the oven. The consumer also noted nothing was chilled or braised in the process, and [mfrs] are flat out lairs.
justification: The incident involved a shattered baking dish causing damage and food waste, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have a pan from Cooks by JCPenney Home Collection. It is stainless steel with a copper bottom. I was cooking with it last night and heard a very loud popping noise, similar to a gunshot. I was temporarily deaf in one ear and very startled, but the brass bottom of my pan blew/bubbled/popped out. I have used this pan many times before and have never seen or heard anything like this in my life.
justification: The incident caused temporary deafness and startlement but no lasting injury, and such occurrences are rare based on the description.

incident_description: I microwaved for one minute food and the bowl shattered while I was eating. It is sold as microwave safe and oven safe to 425 degrees
justification: The bowl shattered during use, indicating an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Our stove is a Kenmore smoothtop electric range with rotary knobs and a digital display (more details below.) 

We were using the front left burner to cook. The temperature was on low (2 out of 10 on the dial.) We had the burner on medium heat for 5 minutes, then turned it down to low for the remaining 6 minutes of cooking. After 4.5 minutes on low, the temperature of the burner element increased on its own and became extremely hot, to the point that we had to take the pan off of the heat to keep our food from burning. We turned the knob to Off, but the burner continued heating and the element was red. We jiggled the knob to make sure it was off. After about 2 minutes, the burner turned off. It then turned on again with no action on our part. It continued to cycle on and off about 5 times before we were able to shut off the circuit breaker to the stove.

We are very concerned about the temperature increasing unexpectedly, then about not being able to turn off the burner without going to the breaker box. Fortunately, we were in the kitchen cooking when this happened. There was a real possibility that this could have caused a fire, or that someone could have been burned. 

We looked online and found a recall that was similar to what we experienced, but the combination of  manufacturer, model, and serial number do not match the recall.

The recall: 
Frigidaire and Kenmore Smoothtop Electric Ranges Recalled Due to Fire Hazard
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
August 27, 2009
Release # 09-333
http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2009/Frigidaire-and-Kenmore-Smoothtop-Electric-Ranges-Recalled-Due-to-Fire-Hazard/

Our range is a Kenmore, model 790.96122408, Serial VF64180141
The serial number is in the range of recalls for Frigidaire, but doesn't meet the Kenmore model number. 
We tried calling on Saturday night (2/20/16), when this occurred, but it was after hours. I called Sears recall today (800-449-9810), but they did not find our model number on their recall list. I then called CPSC and was told that I needed to file a report because my model number did not match the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could have caused a fire or burns, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Glass oven door shattered upon first use of the self-cleaning oven in our 4 month old range. As we investigated this on the internet it appears this has been a problem for many with GE and [REDACTED] brand ovens since at least 2011. 
Our range model was a: GE JB630-DF4WW
Purchased: October 2015.  Oven door shattered in February 2016 the first time we used the self-cleaning feature.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no reported injury, and similar issues have been reported by others, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
I'm writing to inform you of a tragic mishap due to a manufacturing defect. My wife has had a Cuisinart 350 watt smoothie blender (Mod. CPB 300, Ser. 01023), for over two years which she has used almost every day. 
On the morning of Sunday August 16, 2015 she made her smoothie as normal. However, shortly after start up she heard an unusual sound and turned to find that the plastic blender cup had unscrewed from the blade holder and the ingredients were spewing all about the room. The powerful motor continued to run and the blade was exposed. The blade is positional (only goes into the blender one way) but has no safety interlocks what so ever. She, bowing to her instantaneous reflex came into contact with the blade with her left palm and was severely lacerated, severing 4 tendons and 4 or 5 nerves. I immediately transported her to [REDACTED] ER in [REDACTED]. where she received emergency care to include: 17 stitches, X rays, and a tetanus shot. The Bone and Joint Center of [REDACTED] was contacted and surgery was scheduled. We had a consultation on the 17th and the surgery on August 18, 2015. The surgery required 3 hours at which time tendons were repaired and nerves reattached. We have been informed that she will be in physical therapy for 6 to 9 weeks and probably scared for life. In addition, she will have limited use and sensitivity of at least two fingers. We blame the blender and its total lack of safety interlocks. Her medical bills will soon surpass $25,000, not to mention her pain, suffering and psychological trauma.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations, tendon and nerve damage, requiring surgery and long-term physical therapy, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: 2-3 times each month, the front/left burner will increase its temperature to high on its own and will not turn off by normal means (manual knob).  The only way to turn the burner off is to unplug it or turn off the power at the break. Although there was a massive recall of 200,000 units, this specific model number has not been included even though it is doing the same thing as those that were recalled. On 11/19/15 The consumer contacted the firm "Pyrex" and informed them about the incident. She was told by a Rep (she thinks his name was [REDACTED]) that the combination of the butter and the moisture of the chicken could have caused the incident. Impossible! There was not enough butter to create "grease" and how much moisture can you get from 3 small room temperature chicken legs?  She told the Rep that it was not possible and he said he wanted to read me a paper. He asked the consumer if the dish was cracked or chipped and she told him no - she does not use chipped or cracked dishes to eat on or cook with. He asked if she preheated the oven which she did. The consumer can't remember everything that he read but she did everything that he said she should.  He asked me to send the glass to him so they could check the glass out. The glass was already picked up that morning so the consumer didn't have any to send. After the incident she went to the web site and found several other statements about dishes exploding that sounded like what had happened to me. The consumer also saw an article about the company being sold and the new company started adding more limestone when making the glass and that may be a problem.  The consumer told the Rep this and he said you can't believe everything you read on the internet.  The consumer told him she agrees with that but they sounded too much like what happened to her. As far as the limestone he said that it wasn't true. However, if he was so sure it wasn't true why do they want to test the glass. The consumer was offered a new dish which she did not accept because she does not feel their products are safe. The consumer does not remember where she purchased the dish. She threw the pieces of glass in the trash and they were picked up the next morning.

incident_description:
After closing the door to our Samsung SMH1713 over-range microwave, there was a noticeable buzzing noise coming from the unit.  We purchased this microwave from Best Buy online in August 2013, and I installed it myself, replacing a unit that was at least 10 years old, but probably closer to 15 or 20.  
The buzzing noise was worrisome, and some investigation -- primarily with a [REDACTED] cup filled with cold water -- showed that as soon as the door is closed, the magnetron turns on at full power.  The time cook controls turn on the oven light and turntable, but do not affect the continuous operation of the magnetron.  The power settings do not seem to modulate the duty cycle of the magnetron, either.  
The only way to turn off the microwave is to open the door (this stops the buzzing and heating) or to unplug the unit, of course.  If the door is closed, as soon as the microwave is plugged in, the magnetron turns on.
This seems to be a pretty significant safety issue:  the high-voltage DC modulation circuit to the 1 kW RF generator seems to fail-ON, leaving the (hopefully mechanical and fail-safe) door interlock as the only actual safety circuit.  Though the chamber is metal and the turntable (one hopes) is heat-tempered glass, the turntable drive is plastic and rubber, and possibly flammable.  The oven has had only light household use for 2.5 years.
I have contacted Samsung service, and am scheduled to have a technician come out to investigate the problem on Monday, 2/22.  The estimated charges run $90 for diagnosis and $75/hour for repairs, plus parts costs.  The magnetron specifically is under warranty, but I am not sure if that would apply to the control circuit as well.  The unit cost $240, and $165 minimum for repairs seems hardly worth it, given that the circuit that failed would likely only be replaced, and the underlying safety issue unaddressed.
justification: The microwave's magnetron turns on unexpectedly when the door is closed, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I bought my Hamilton-Beach slow-cooker 12/18/2016 at Wal-Mart in Concord, NC at their Concord Commons store. The CPC bar code number: 40094 33963 The box described it as a 275 watt cooker, type SC26 made in China.

I used it without incident according to the instructions 3 times. The 4th time, the ceramic pot cracked around the entire oval circumference of the shell and the bottom separated from the pot in one piece. I cut my finger slightly pulling the two big sharp ceramic pieces out of the metal shell. More importantly, under other circumstances, I might have cut myself very badly. I might also have burned myself badly. The leaking food juices might or might not have shorted out the electrical heater element in the metal shell (I don't know how well protected they are from liquids).

Sequence of events:
The ceramic pot appeared OK when I went to use it although I cannot rule out the existence of a possible unseen crack. It was clean and at room temperature. I poured into it the contents of a large casserole dish of cold meat, beans and vegetables I'd just taken out of the refrigerator; this just about filled the pot. I then ladled four small, drained, chopped, boiled onions on the top of the these other contents and mixed everything with a metal spatula. The slow cooker was completely full. Several minutes later, I went to plug in the appliance but I noticed brown juice flowing out the bottom. I opened it up and found the problem I described above. I did not plug in the appliance.

I took pictures. I have also saved the pieces for inspection. I'm an engineer with a little knowledge of glass and ceramics. I think this was a brittle fracture. There was a thermal gradient between the large mass of cold food and the small amount of hot onions on top, but I believe mixing the onions ingredients quickly reduced any gradient. The mixing I did was fairly gentle and I did not scrape the pot - I lifted the ingredients up from the bottom several times.

Whatever I did to cause this was well within the operating envelope one would expect for such an appliance -- most people are probably rougher with stuff.

This should be investigated as a hazard to users and a recall considered.
justification: The user suffered a slight injury (cut finger) and there was potential for more severe injury or burns, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the incident happened once out of four uses under specific conditions.

incident_description:
On 1/27/16, our Frigidaire Gallery Electric Range (Model # GLEFZ384HC / Serial # VF83769846) began making a loud noise and then started shooting sparks, flames and smoke from the area below the console panel and above the cook-top. Additional arcing and smoke was noticed in the oven chamber near the broiler element.  

My wife was baking at the time of the incident, but none of the cook-top elements were on or in use. The fires self-extinguished after power to the range was cut (the circuit breaker tripped). 

I am reporting this incident because I believe there is a significant risk to owners of this model range. While this model/serial number was not included in any of the (many) Frigidaire Product Recalls for similar models, I feel the experience we had matches those of other owners covered by the recalls. There seem to be a lot of reports of fires originating at the electronic consoles of Frigidaire ranges.

If there had been anything (grease, pot-holders, etc.) on the cook top during the incident I believe a fire could have spread quickly. 

Further review of the range parts showed significant damage to several electrical components. (Pictures are available for clarification).
Specifically:
*The circuit boards in the console were blackened and burned over approximately 50% of the boards.
*Several of the wires connected to the console were charred.
*The insulation surrounding the broiler element leads were blackened from the fire, as were the wires connected to the broiler element.
*The insulation surrounding the convection fan motor was blackened from the fire.
justification: The incident involved sparks, flames, and smoke from the range, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I am writing this letter to report a dangerous flaw that potentially could injure someone.  We have a Kenmore stove (Model 790.9743,9744 ) that we purchased on November 3, 2009 at a Sears store in Salina, Kansas.  On Sunday (Feb. 7. 2016) afternoon the oven was off and was cooling after my wife baked some rolls.  Suddenly the front glass on the oven door shattered scattering many pieces of glass onto the floor.  Since the glass is tempered safety glass, the bits of glass were mostly small but flew up to 5 feet. If a small child or animal happened to be standing nearby, possible injuries could have occurred.
This is not a rare event as we at first thought until we looked on the internet.  We discovered this event, while not common, does occur quite often.  As far as we could determine we did nothing unusual to the door (reports from others were similar) that could have caused the breakage. While Kenmore is the brand we have, other brands were named by internet reports.
Those of us who reported the shattered glass on Kenmore stove oven doors to Sears brought no offer to repair the stove or pay for a replacement part.  Most of the folks (including me) who called Sears got similar responses such as the warranty has run out and our stoves and parts are made by various manufacturers. 
I am not so concerned about the repair cost even though Sears would be better served standing behind their products when a safety issue occurs.  
Someone could really be injured.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no actual injury, and similar events are reported to occur quite often.

Saw dishwasher was 'paused', pressed 'start'.  Immediate arcing sounds and black, sooty smoke poured out of the top of the control panel into room.  Yanked door open and ran downstairs to hit breaker while yelling at momma to evac kids.

instruction manual, I followed the directions for cleaning the cooktop. Several weeks went by before we were ready
to try the oven. Within 15 minutes of turning on the oven, I became extremely nauseated. I turned off the oven and
ventilated the house. I did not try operating it again until 2/6/2016. This time, the fumes were even stronger and
my eyes began burning. Again, I opened doors and windows and read back through the manual which suggests
that any initial odor will dissipate within 30 minutes of use. The following day, 2/7/2016, I opened every door and
window in the house and turned on fans to blow any fumes out of the house. I turned the oven to 375 degrees and
vacated the house for two hours. Upon returning, I found the fumes to be choking and I experienced a full-blown
asthma attack requiring the use of my inhaler. Today (one day following the last incident), I am experiencing a
burning sensation in my nose, throat and eyes and again I am nauseated. I need to know what type of chemical is
causing this and whether I should seek medical attention. We also want a full refund from Home Depot and want
the electric range removed from our property.
justification: The incident resulted in an asthma attack and ongoing symptoms, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurred multiple times but is unlikely to be a common occurrence for most users (likelihood 2).

A little later in various parts of the kitchen I found the two round covers of the round rivets? or such that attach the handle to the pan itself. incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore electric range (model: 790.97423901; SN: VF00546753) from the Sears at Tuttle Crossing store #01120, 5053 Tuttle Crossing Blvd., Columbus, OH 43016 in February 2010.  On Sunday, January 31, 2016, I was baking cookies in the oven for about an hour at a temperature of 375 degrees.  After baking the cookies, I turned off the oven and left the kitchen while the cookies cooled.  About 10 to 15 minutes after I turned off the oven, the outer glass on the oven door exploded and scattered glass across the entire kitchen floor and even into our dining room.  The stove is not used excessively, maybe 3-4 times per week at normal cooking temperatures of 350 to 450 degrees for short periods of time.  In addition, no damage has ever been done to the stove, e.g., objects hitting the oven door or coming into contact with the glass.  We were very fortunate that no one was in the kitchen or dining room at the time as they could have been injured from the flying glass.  I am concerned that the oven may be a danger to my family and perhaps others who have purchased a Kenmore range.  My concern is whether the glass is defective or if this could be a design flaw causing pressure to build in the oven and cause the glass to shatter.

As a parent of two children, I feel obligated to report this incident to Kenmore, Sears, and the Consumer Product Safety Commission as a safety concern.  In addition, I am asking for reimbursement from Kenmore or Sears in the amount of $71.66 for the replacement door glass that I purchased from AppliancePartsPros.com on January 31, 2016.  If it is determined that this oven is recalled due to poor design, I would like to request a replacement of my range for a new model that does not have a history of this potential safety concern.  I do have pictures of the damage if you wish to review them.   Please contact me with any questions.  I look forward to your response.

cc Kenmore and Sears
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass exploding, causing property damage but no injuries, as no one was present in the area at the time.

It did not break apart, rather it stayed as a single unit but the glass was thoroughly broken into hundreds of interlocking bits between one and two tenths of an inch across.  At first, my wife and I did not understand what had happened and thought the pattern on the lid was due to condensation from the simmering liquid below. Thursday, November 26th, 2015 the caller was cooking her turkey in her electric oven with the temperature set at 325 degrees, however within 15 minutes after the caller put the turkey in the oven the unit reset itself to self cleaning, automatically locked the oven door then the temperature rose to around 500 degrees.

Neither the caller or her husband could open the door or find any way to override the situation until they tripped the breaker of then allowed the oven to cool off.
The callers were still unable to open the oven door once the unit cooled off and was still off power, the door could not be opened until they returned power to the range.
They then disconnect power again because the oven was remaining on and heating.

The caller is reporting this incident as a severe fire hazard due to the extreme temperature that the oven soared to before the breaker was turned off.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer at 1 (800) 253-1301 on November 27th, 2015, she spoke with a female representative who said she would pass the information up but did not take a report.

The caller reported this as a severe fire hazard because the oven reached an extremely high temperature (which would have been fine if she had set it to self clean) AND the door locked itself without any type of manual override.  The grease from the turkey inside the oven could easily have been ignited by the extreme heat. The caller believes that the only reason this did not occur that day was because at that stage of cooking the pan was completely covered with aluminum foil which prevented  the oil from splattering on the hot coils as the temperature rose.

[REDACTED]
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident posed a severe fire hazard due to the oven malfunctioning and reaching extreme temperatures.

incident_description:
Our home's kitchen was equipped by the builder with a Jenn-Air gas grill - cooktop with a downdraft fan ventilation system. Last night I turned on the fan and noticed a faint glow between the fan switch and the escutcheon that covers the fan switch and burner valve controls. As I turned off the fan, I noticed an acrid burn smell, and suspected a fire was burning insulation. 

This morning I turned off the gas and unplugged the unit, removed the control knobs and the escutcheon, and saw that one of the two metal blades conducting electricity through the fan switch was broken off (I will attach photographs). Apparently closing the switch resulted in arcing that burned the switch housing, the wire insulation. 

I am concerned about the following potential hazards:
  - Shock hazard, if the metal surface of the control box or the range were part of an electrical circuit.
  - Electrical fire hazard resulting from arcing
  - Gas fire hazard, if the arcing could damage the gas line or control.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and potential fire hazards, but no actual injury or death occurred.

If we had not been home we could have lost everything!  The wall socket it was plugged into has no damage.  The chord is untouched.  This fire originated from inside of my unused microwave.  I have called the company and have been given a case number.  I have also posted a public service announcement with pictures on my Facebook account.  This microwave was purchased at Meijer around April of 2015.  It is not an old appliance and I would expect better regarding consumer safety from a company with such a big name as SHARP.  Thank you for your time.

Sharp Carousel Microwave
Model: R-309YW
Manufactured Date: July 2014

incident_description:
Tonight, my wife, [REDACTED], was cooking chicken in this pressure cooker. She had stepped away from the kitchen for a few minutes only to come back to find fluid rushing out from the joint of the pot to the lid, shooting downward along side of the pot and fueling a developing fire on the range burner.

I immediately cut power to the range via garage circuit breaker, and sprayed water from the kitchen sink hose onto the flames to put it out.  The house was filled with smoke.  Presumably it was grease from the chicken that was fueling the fire.  

This is not the first time that this pressure cooker has acted strangely, but it is the most concerning.  In the past, [REDACTED] has finished cooking with this pressure cooker, carried it over to the kitchen sink where she would let cool water run over it in order to accelerate the cooling of the cooker so that it can be opened.  Several times when she has done this, suddenly fluid would start to shoot down from the pot-lid joint, and harmlessly into the sink.  

There is a definite design problem with this pressure cooker.  It is very dangerous.  Tonight's incident could have easily caused our house to burn if not caught when it was.

A recall needs to be placed on this product immediately to save others from potential property damage and personal injury.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was quickly contained, resulting in no injuries but significant potential for property damage.

incident_description: Purchased a Samsung 30 inch self-Cleaning Slide-In Electric Convection Range. The control knobs are easily accidentally activated "on" to heat the glass burners. This is a fire hazard and a personal injury hazard to people and pets. After reading other consumers complain of this problem I thought only and idiot would have something like accidentally turning on a stove top happen to them. We bought the stove. Then it happened to us 3 times in two days. Each incident involved the cooktop being covered with protective fabric while working around the oven. Each time the  burners became accidentally activated "on" without the victim's knowledge. The first time a towel was placed over the glass cook top while a handyman was installing an over the range microwave. Although the oven door was locked, a front burner knob was accidentally turned on by the handyman bumping into it and noticed when the towel was scorched and the handyman felt the heat of the scorched towel. Fortunately, he was not burned because the towel protected his hand. My husband and I needed to remove the microwave over the stove (to fix the air vent.) We had covered the glass cook top with a polyester pillow to protect it from possible damage if the microwave were accidentally dropped. We accidentally turned the stove on and didn't realize it until we smelled the pillow smoking. Fortunately, we were right near the burning pillow and removed it from the cook top before it could catch fire. The polyester pillow melted, smoking up the house with fumes and leaving a hard, melted plastic mess on the glass cook top. The stove was accidentally turned on again while re-installing the microwave over the range again.  The problem is that the cook top knobs jet forward on the front of the stove, making them easy to accidentally bump into and also making them attractive and accessible for a small child to play with. A child could easily start a fire or get burned. Adults working near the stove can accidentally activate the burners, starting a fire or getting burned themselves. This product is unsafe because the knobs can be easily accidentally activated "on". Please ask Samsung to recall the product and fix the problem before someone really gets burned or their home burns down.
justification: The incident describes multiple occurrences of accidental activation leading to scorching and melting of materials, but no injuries reported.

There were no other liquids or sauces in the pan, other than a little butter and the natural juices of the chicken. incident_description:
I am writing to you regarding a recent issue I had where a Pyrex dish shattered. The 13"x9" Pyrex dish, approximately 3 years old, was in the oven at 400F and when removed and placed on top of the stove (metal grates, not a ceramic solid surface), it exploded into thousands of pieces. 

I have a degree in Ceramic Engineering with several patents for glass-ceramics used for thermal expansion applications and I can state for a fact that this failure was indicative of a tempered glass failure and not of a high temperature thermally resistant glass failure. It shattered into thousands of pieces which is consistent with tempered safety glass. Safety glass, used for car windows and sliding glass doors, is not meant to be used for high thermal shock applications. This is extremely dangerous and I found no information on the manufacturer's website, World Kitchen, regarding  how to use Pyrex safely or recommended temperatures/conditions for use.

I have used the dish many, many times at 400F without issue. To my knowledge, there were no chips or cracks which I do check for regularly.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering but no injury was reported, and the user has used the dish many times without issue, indicating this is an unlikely but not rare occurrence.

incident_description:
I am writing this letter regarding a recent experience with my KitchenAid Artisan series 5 qt tilt head stand mixer. Our family enjoys our mixer and uses it frequently without any mechanical problems. However, I have a serious safety concern with this particular model. When the head of the mixer is in the up position there is an open area that can easily entrap fingers resulting in injury. This was our recent experience with this particular mixer. There appears to be no safety mechanism or guard to prevent injuries from this area of the mixer.  The top of this mixer is extremely heavy and the weight contributes to injury.

               I was recently using my mixer and just lifted the head to remove the bowl. The head of the mixer is very heavy and easy to engage in the downward position. Since the tilt head does not have an upright locking mechanism my son was easily able to entrap his finger in this open area of the mixer. The entrapment combined with the downward force of the mixer head nearly resulted in a complete amputation of his finger. He required treatment at the local emergency department and received sutures from one side of his finger to the other. I believe that KitchenAid should look for some type of safety mechanism for this device to prevent future injuries of this nature. My daughter was also present during this incident and witnessed the near amputation, severe laceration and large amount of bleeding her brother suffered from the mixer. She really enjoyed helping to make various things using the KitchenAid mixer. However, she no longer wants to come anywhere close to the mixer for fear of the same injury occurring to her.

                I feel that this design can easily result in injuries for people of all ages. I am disappointed that this company did not see this as a design flaw or safety concern. As much as I hate that we experienced this event, I hope that our experience will raise awareness so that KitchenAid can work towards a solution that would prevent this type of injury to future consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration requiring emergency treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests the design flaw makes such injuries likely to occur with frequent use (likelihood 4).

This included the silverware tray, several plastic items in the top rack, and all of the plastic rotating arms.  The latter were in a heap at the bottom as a melted pile of gray goo.  The interior was far too hot to touch.  Leaving the door open to cool didn't work, as the heating element stayed on.  The heating element came on during the night while the dishwasher was closed but turned off.  Had we been away on a trip, we are totally convinced this failure would have caused a fire.

incident_description:

On Friday, January 15th, the service technician opened up the dishwasher to trouble shoot. What he found was catastrophic. This unit had caught on fire, started from the printed circuit board. The entire cavity where the electronic reside burned. We were asleep in the house when this fire occurred. I asked to be contacted by Electrolux management to discuss next steps to make this right. They have absolved themselves of any remuneration to cover out additional out  of pocket costs. The traumatic realization was that our house could have caught on fire, putting us in potential danger while we slept. 

We have asked them to compensate us $499 for us to purchase another dishwasher and  new extended warranty, but we did not ask for compensation for our mileage, cost of our time, inconvenience, and overall psychological trauma.

We declined to have new parts installed in the subject unit, since they were just replaced in August, and we are genuinely worried about another fire.

incident_description:
KitchenAid coffee maker Model # KCM1110B Serial # WF23002531 

Coffee maker failed to shut down after brewing.    There is a switch with a small blue indicator on the front of the unit that is used to wake-up the device, to initiate a normal or a timed brew cycle.  (This indicator is being pointed as it is a visual indicator of the units status).  Normally and in all previous usages the coffee maker would turn off the heating element after brewing and plus approximately 2 hours warming time the blue indicator would then be turned off.  

We had made a pot of coffee, filled our "to-go" cups, turned off the unit and left the house.   When we returned four hours latter and we started to make another pot, I noticed the pot and burner were still very warn to the touch even though the heating indicator was extinguished.  After adding water to the reservoir the brew process started without the unit being turned on.  Not believing what I was seeing I unplugged the unit (app. 2 minutes), when I plugged the back in the brew process restarted once again without the switch being depressed nor the indicator being lit. This morning when I plugged in the unit it started to brew, without being enabled via the switch.  And once again  we returned home we tried for a fourth thing... same thing happened, plug it in and brewing starts. 

The concept of having a 1000watt heat source sitting on my counter top, generating hear for hours on end is worry sum as it could easily start a fire.  

I will admit that the owners manual states "Unplug coffee maker from outlet when not in use and before cleaning. Allow to cool before putting on or taking off parts"  If it should be UNPLUG WHEN NOT IN USE!!! Why then would it come with a clock and a brew timer? 

I am currently testing the unit (fourth test) to see if it continues to misbehave... After this test, the unit did act as it should have, after 2.5hrs the blue light was extinguished and within .5 hrs the heating plate was cool to the touch. 

Bottom line is that we no longer trust it not to burn down our home.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned by not shutting down properly, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a GE cafe series gas stove. I have had this product just under three years. This is a double oven and recently the bottom oven didn't work. I determined that the issue was the igniter, a common issue when gas ovens don't work. I proceeded to remove the bottom tray of the oven to access the igniter. What I found was that underneath the bottom tray and directly over the igniter is a steel deflector shield. This shield had gotten so hot from the igniter that it had melted a hole through it. The melted steel dripped on the igniter and caused it to burn out. I do believe that this is a defect in the stove and a potential fire hazard. Ge representatives state that this is a normal occurrence and they refuse to cover it as a defect in their product.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven igniter causing a steel shield to melt, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death.

incident_description:
Last week (Jan 14th, 11.15 am EST), I spoke to [REDACTED] of the South Dakota GE Customer Service office, in regard to an operational and potential safety problem with our gas range, less than 2 years in service.

The main control knobs, front panel, coordinating the gas flow to all jets have flimsy plastic bushings, and offer only inadequate purchase on the brass drive shafts for each gas control valve.

They are now slipping and turning freely on the shafts, making it impossible for a user to know that the gas is properly shut off after cooking.

According to [REDACTED] of GE, this is not logged in as a known issue, and there are no parts updates or upgrades in the system or planned.

Going forwards, we need to determine a better quality of control knob, as a safe way of operating this stove. 

The range has seen extremely light use, is in as-new condition apart from this physical defect issue, and has been carefully treated by middle-aged owners (ie : operator abuse is not part of the equation here).

I look forward to hearing from you - thank you.

incident_description:
About 3 weeks ago, the consumer stated that she was using the oven for about 1-1.5 hours, when two of the carbon monoxide detectors in her home went off at the same time (CO detectors are located on two separate floors in the house).

The consumer stated that the readings on the detectors were 57-59 ppm. 

The consumer contacted her gas company ([REDACTED]). The consumer had a technician, [REDACTED], come out from [REDACTED] on 12/09/15 for an inspection. The technician turned on the oven on bake and convection features. He tested for CO numerous time. One of the readings from the back vent of the unit came out to 467ppm. The technician took the unit apart and examined the unit. He was unable to figure out what the problem was. 

He asked the consumer to order two different pieces (flame spreader and the oven bottom). He mentioned that the flame spreader was touching the underside of the oven bottom. He was unsure if that was causing the collection of CO or if there was another chemical reaction occurring.

The consumer ordered the two parts through Sears and she's waiting on them to arrive (expected delivery 12/21/15).  The consumer will be installing the parts on their own. They scheduled [REDACTED] technician to come out on 12/22/15 to inspect the unit after installing the new parts.

The consumer will be contacting Electrolux because her unit is having the same issue as the units recalled under #10-048. The consumer's unit serial # falls out of range in the recall.
justification: The incident involved high CO levels detected, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
In December 2015, I Purchased a KRUPS Espresso Coffee Maker Model / Type XP100, REF: XP100050 / 1P0-4513.  I have owned and operated other brands of steam type Espresso Coffee Makers for over 25 years.

In March of 2015, I unpacked the KRUPS and put it into service in my home using it without incident approximately twice weekly. I clean it thoroughly after each and every use.  My preferred brand of coffee is [REDACTED] Espresso Roast ÃÂ ground for me by [REDACTED] specifically for use in a steam Espresso Coffee Maker.

On January 14, 2016, I prepared coffee as I normally do, turned on the KRUPS Espresso Coffee Maker; 2 or 3 minutes later the unit exploded propelling shards of glass, hot coffee, and hot coffee grounds a distance of 15 feet, covering the walls, floor, counters, appliances, and my back. 
Thankfully I had my back to the explosion.  It took nearly 2 hours to clean up the mess and I cut my hand on the broken glass in the process.

On January 15, 2016, I called KRUPS Customer Relations and was told:
1-	There are no safety concerns with this Espresso Coffee Maker.
2-	I probably caused the problem by tamping the coffee too hard or not cleaning the basket thoroughly (untrue and ridiculous).
3-	While there is a safety valve on the water tank, there is no safety valve on the brewing mechanism, that is why it exploded.
4-	KRUPS would not replace the Espresso Coffee Maker under the two year warranty.
5-	KRUPS would send me a shipping label to send the Espresso Coffee Maker to a service center for repair. I would need to pay for packaging of the unit. 

I feel that under the circumstances, I am entitled to either a complete NEW Espresso Coffee Maker or a complete refund of $100. If I had been facing the unit when it exploded, I would have been severely injured. Luckily I sustained only a cut to my right hand and a sizable mess to clean up.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the hand and potential for severe injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
On January 3rd my husband turned on the appliance setting it to broil. Shortly after we heard a loud buzzing sound and looked to see sparks, flame and smoke inside the oven.  My husband went to the breaker box and cut the power to the range from there. Smoke was also pouring from the top of the range around the panel where you set the temperature.  I immediately called hhGregg (the retailer where I purchased the range) and was instructed that the product was under the Samsung 1 year warranty.  I called Samsung who  (after much conversation and multiple calls) dispatched 2 repair technicians from 2 different vendors who both determined that the boil element inside the oven exploded causing damage to the inner frame and interior. 

My concerns are that this range was brand new having been purchased on July 3, 2015. This appliance was used strictly at home for the purpose of cooking for a small family ( 2 adults and 1 child). It had little wear at all. Yet the boil element exploded.  I am worried that had my husband, my 3 year old and/or I had been near or touching the appliance at the moment that there was an electrical explosion we could have been seriously hurt. I also am not convinced this could not have happened if the oven had been off. This exploding element could have easily started a fire in my home or severely burned someone using the oven.  

It took 11 days for Samsung to eventually agree eventually to replace the range but I must say that their slow response and lackadaisical attitude about the entire event has caused me great concern. There was no sense of urgency in investigating the issue or resolving the matter. I would think they'd want to get the range back to their manufacturer immediately to investigate what caused the element to explode. If their reaction is any indication of how they build their appliances, I have grave concerns for other consumers who have a Samsung electric range (or God forbid gas range) in their home.
justification: The incident involved sparks, flame, and smoke from the oven, posing a potential risk of injury or fire, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
First, I'm a family physician and volunteer firefighter trained in responding to carbon monoxide emergencies.  So I want to relay a significant carbon monoxide event that I believe is related to flawed design of a DCS model DCS-RG-486GD stove.

On Wednesday January 6th, I had a dinner party with about a dozen guests.  I was using several large pots to boil lobsters on the stove.  The hood was turned on and is properly vented to the outside.  After about 10-15 minutes, my home carbon monoxide alarms started going off.  As a firefighter and physician, I promptly turned off the stove and opened several doors and moved to clear air.  After several minutes, the alarms went off.  Later that night I experienced symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning, including headache, nausea, severe dizziness, and slurred speech/confusion.  A few of my guests reported milder but similar symptoms.

Several days later, I used a professional "multigas" detector from our fire station to do some testing.  The gas detector was calibrated and can detect CO levels as low as 1-2 ppm.  With the oven and stove burners on full blast with either no pots, or with small pots, there was no detectible carbon monoxide.  However as soon as I placed a large pot on the burner, the carbon monoxide alarm immediately spikes to 100-200 ppm and starts alarming.

The problem is inherent to the stove design.  Because of the tight drip plate and narrow openings in the grate, a large bottom pot prevents air and oxygen from entering the burner.  The result is a mixture that is too "rich" (more fuel than air), which results in incomplete combustion, and significant levels of carbon monoxide.

I have checked the manual.  There are no warnings about using large pots creating risk of carbon monoxide.  This stove is marketed as a "professional" stove and the grates are designed to support large pots.  Unfortunately they don't allow adequate airflow in these circumstances.
justification: The incident resulted in carbon monoxide poisoning symptoms for the host and guests, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the stove design flaw consistently produces dangerous CO levels with large pots.

incident_description:
(11/21/2015) The consumer stated that he smelled smoke when he came home. He heard the refrigerator arcing. The consumer pulled the refrigerator from the wall. When he removed the back of the unit, he saw that the start relay was in flames and smoking. The consumer unplugged the unit. The fire self-extinguished. 

On November 21st the consumer came home to a house smelling of an electrical fire in progress.  

Not seeing open flames in the house or huge amounts of smoke the consumer elected to not call the fire department and investigate the cause on his own. 

During his investigation the consumer found his Kenmore side by side refrigerator (built by Whirlpool) making arcing noises so the consumer pulled it back from the wall so he could remove the back cover and inspect what was going on.
Upon removing the back cover from the unit the consumer quickly noted that the start relay assembly was arcing and producing some smoke and a puff of fire just as seen in the two YouTube videos that follow on subsequent pages.

A quick search of the internet  also resulted in CONFIRMATION that this EXACT SAME REFRIGERATOR design built during the same timeframe as the consumer's under the Maytag name has been recalled by the CSPC for the EXACT SAME failure mode of FIRE HAZARD.

Obviously both Whirlpool and Sears were grossly negligent in not expanding this recall to ALL AFFECTED units built by Whirlpool. Whirlpool would have been aware of this issue being the OEM and OWNER of the Maytag line.
Whirlpool should have notified Sears / Kenmore of this issue.
Furthermore, Sears / Kenmore should have notified all individuals that purchased this product of its inherent fire hazard dangers.

If the consumer would not have come home when he did, this refrigerator could have caught his house on fire. Obviously we would be talking about a massive lawsuit should that have occurred.

My huge issue here is that there was damage to this unit that cannot be repaired by simply replacing the defective start relay. When the relay failed, it also burnt off the hermetic pin terminal of the start winding for the compressor.
Therefore, the consumer cannot just replace the relay to repair the unit as the compressor itself will also need to be replaced.

Whirlpool/ Sears needs to repair and or replace this defective unit at no expense to the consumer as it is clear a design issue (subjected to recall) was at fault that caused this unit to not provide a full service life.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury or death, but potential for significant property damage.
