(11/25/2015) The technician came out and advised the consumer that the problem was in the control panel. He also advised the consumer that sometimes the short-circuit is caused by the stove. The technician told the consumer that the repair would cost $199.

The consumer added her main purpose is safety, but their interest was to repair or replace; after no explanation from repairman who said he was not an engineer and it was above his pay grade. The consumer also added her interest is: Does this product need to be recalled? For dangerous fire hazard? If she was not at home when it [microwave] came on by itself what would happen? 

The consumer noted she could not unplug [microwave] as it was too high, and she almost called the fire department, but got a neighbor who helped her unplug [it].
justification: The microwave malfunctioned repeatedly and posed a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: This product leaks and leaks bad between cups brewing
justification: The product leaks during use, indicating an incident with no reported injury, and the issue seems to occur frequently based on the description.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Freestanding Electric Range, Model #97453, that is 5 years old. As I was preparing Christmas dinner, the front glass shattered randomly while dinner was cooking at 350 degrees. Two of my toes got minor cuts. I am just glad that no small children or pets were around when this happened. This has happened way too many times according to my research, and there should be a recall and a class action lawsuit to replace the glass on these ranges.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts to toes) and the description indicates this is a recurring issue with the product.

incident_description:
Dishwasher circuit board caught on fire, with smoke coming from dishwasher door.

We immediately disconnected the electricity, unscrewed the front door, and took out the scorched, smoldering electronics board.

Had we not caught the situation early due to strong smell of burning plastics, the house would have been in clear danger of catching fire.

Purchased dishwasher in early 2007; manufacture date below is approximate.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but was caught early, preventing injury or further damage.

incident_description:
For the third time the control panel for the oven has worn out. When this happens the oven "OFF" button no longer works. This should be considered at least a fire hazard and since it is recurring about every two years it should be something that is considered faulty.

The control panel is a screen printed circuit that wears out with usage. Seeing that they charge over three hundred dollars for a new control panel I feel it is tantamount to a scam. They know the limitations of it and have done nothing to make the situation better.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the oven's control panel that poses a fire hazard but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I was putting the dish into a drawer. It did not bump or hit anything. It was room temperature.there were no obvious cracks in it. It exploded into hundreds if fragments,some smaller than sand, flying over a radius of over 4 feet. I don't know exactly how old the pan was, but it was not a new pan.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of a dish into fragments, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Hello. My name is [REDACTED].

We purchased the Coffee Ninja Bar http://www.ninjakitchen.com/ninja-coffee-bar-cf080/ and used it for the first time on 12/26/2015.  I reached over the top of the brewer while it was brewing to reach into a cabinet above the coffee maker.  While reaching over the maker, steam started coming out of the top. My hand was in the steam and I received a second degree burn on my left index finger.  

I am an ER doctor, so was able to treat at home without going to the ER, but I am concerned because there is no warning label at the top of the maker to alert someone to the fact that steam would come out of the top. 

pon closer inspection after the injury, I note that there are vents on top of the maker. I believe this should be marked to alert people the risk of steam coming out of these vents. I am fortunate that my burn was not more extensive or deeper than a partial thickness second degree burn.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn, which qualifies as an injury, and the likelihood is considered possible given the lack of warning labels.

incident_description: My dishwasher was running in the wash cycle. I heard a crackling noise and smoke started pouring out the sides of the dishwasher. I tried to shut it off but the controls weren't responding. I called the fire department and they pulled the machine out and disconnected the power wire. The fire dept had to put up a fan at my front door until the air read clear on their meter. I have a bad sore throat today from that plastic burning odor and smoke. I called kitchen aid today and they are sending a tech here in a few days to see what happened.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning odor causing a sore throat, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such electrical malfunctions are possible but not common (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Kenmore Stainless Steel dishwasher. MOD 665.13263k114  SER F41110621

1.6 years after purchasing my dishwasher new from sears(5-31-2014), yesterday it stopped working and we could smell a weird smell.  My husband hit the circuit breaker and took the control panel off.  An electrical fire had obviously occurred and the circuit board was burnt and plastic cover melted.  I contacted sears and they would not help nor even take the above info so they could keep track of this incident with this model number.  I was told this is a rare incident and they had no concern.  I did online research and found this is a common problem!  Any safety devices did not trigger our circuit breaker did not blow nor did it trip anything in the unit itself.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and damage to the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I microwave frequently and for long periods of time. After years of doing this, recently, I had two Pyrex casserole dishes explode on me.
justification: The incident involved exploding Pyrex dishes but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the frequent and long microwave use described.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore elective stove and oven, model number 790.96112409.  The left front burner has always had problems staying on and the handle to the oven door has been replaced twice and just broke off again causing the glass front to almost fall onto the floor.  Now we just lost power completely to the stove and oven causing the breaker to trip.
justification: The stove and oven have multiple recurring issues, including a burner problem, a broken door handle, and a power loss causing a breaker trip, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
MR. COFFEE model VBX23, prong numbers C273(might be G273), ESC
We set up coffee pot in evening, so all we have to do in morning is press ON.  Got up in the morning twice to find a cold pot of coffee.  It had started on its own without being set for "Delay Brew."  Then, happened to be up at midnight and heard the thing start on its own for the third time!  Took it back to store for refund, and reported to Mr.Coffee on line.  No admission it might be a safety problem.
WORSE, found another of same model stashed in the basement, which I forgot about.  We can use that one, it should be OK.  GUESS WHAT??  It did the same thing.  What happens if there is no water in it when it starts?  Could it start a fire?
justification: The coffee pot malfunctioning poses a potential safety risk, but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description: A Samsung over-the-range microwave model #SMH1816B shot violent Blue flames from the back inside with a loud arcing noise..I was able to stop it in time before there was any damage outside the unit
justification: The microwave emitted violent flames and loud arcing noise, indicating a serious incident, but no injury or external damage occurred.

incident_description: bought the Ninja BL660 blender from amazon.  After first use I went to wash it in the sink and the inner blades slid out and cut my hand badly.
justification: The incident resulted in a bad cut to the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description:
Product:   GE MICROWAVE/CONVECTION OVEN 
Model PT970SR2SS
S/N RT612606Q
Approximate date of manufacture:  2010.

Microwave portion of Control panel - led display (which normally shows time of day when microwave is not being used) went blank.  While attempting to restore display by opening and closing microwave door and hitting start, clear, etc buttons on control panel, noticed that the glass tray in the microwave felt warm.  Kept monitoring glass tray... It continued to heat up until after a few minutes, it was too hot to touch.  Finally sent to circuit panel and shut off all power to microwave and to oven.  Then the glass try cooled off.  Talked to GE.  They claimed no knowledge of any similar problems.  Did Internet search and noticed other similar reports of spontaneous operation of microwave, with some reported fires.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing the glass tray to overheat, but no injury or fire occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
Breville Lift and Look Touch Toaster purchased 12/11/2015. First used 12/26/2016.
Design of toaster has buttons for operation on top of toaster towards the front. The buttons are approximately 1mm raised and only take very light pressure to activate which starts the toaster, lowers bread and turns on heaters inside. 
Due to the ease, location, and raised feature of the start button, it is very easy to inadvertently brush up against the button and turn it on. Even a child could do this. If a lightweight toaster cover, or anything else is on toaster at time, It will start a fire.

This is exactly what happened. A toaster cover was placed over toaster and just the weight of the lightweight cover had activated the start button and a fire ensued.

This would not have happened if the buttons were recessed, even by 1mm. There would have had to be direct pressure placed on it to activate the button.

Very dangerous design..
justification: The incident resulted in a fire due to the toaster's design flaw, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: This incident involves a General Electric ceramic glass top stove. The stoves right front burner got stuck and did not shut down when the burner was turned off. There was three burners and the oven used that night. I cooked peas, corn, greens and a salisbury steak dinner. The three burners were all set at 2, enough just to warm the food and the oven was set at 350.  All were turned off once finished, except it seems the right front burner stayed on after it was switch off. It appeared to have stayed on with out my knowledge until it woke me up from chocking on the toxic smoke. I had my grandchildren all day that day and was exhausted once they left and sat day to eat my dinner and never got to because I fell asleep sitting up on the sofa. Had I went to bed the disaster would have been deadly. I woke up choking and none of the 7 smoke detectors in the rental house ever went off. I ran to the kitchen in the dark. The smoke was so thick I could not see to even retrieve or find my cell phone to call 911 and it was after 11 pm. My only alternative was to move the stove to unplug it. There was no other way to get to it to go off. It took me several attempts to get it to even budge, in the process I pulled with all I had (people in desperation can sometimes find more strength then they would normally have) mind you I am handicapped and only have the use of one hand. In those attempts to move the stove with all the force I had I fell into the cabinet and broke my pelvis the first time. The second attempted I made I fell back again and crushed a disk in my back that also crushed a nerve along with it and I am still recovering painfully from that. With two more attempts I was able to move it. I am in and have been in agony ever since that night. I am only 5'2 and weigh only a hundred and fifteen pounds. Upon getting in behind the stove and unplugging it I also burnt my right shoulder by climbing behind the stove and brushing against the melted microwave and my arm was bunt as well. The arm now has a burnt scar that isnÃÂt going away. After getting it off I managed to practically crawl out the back door to the patio where I passed out. I awoke around 7 am and was having difficulty breathing and walking. Once I contacted my landlord and GE, she then contacted her insurance company and they came and got the stove and microwave, but it would take me harassing and demanding answers for them all to initiate a proper professional investigation and inspection of both appliances. This happened July 3rd 2015 and they did not inspect the stove until December 16th. Their inspection claims it was a fire and it was from the right back burner. However it was not, it involved the right front burner. The evidence proves their wrong. First off the burn pattern of the knobs. They claim the knob from the right front burner (that caused the melt down) was off, that is true it was. They claim the back right burner knob was set to medium for which that night it was set at two. But it was off as well to where they claim it wasnÃÂt, however if it had been on medium (it wasn't) but if it had the melting pattern would have been on the opposite side of the knob but it wasnÃÂt... it melted in the off position. And again if it had been on 2 it would not have been hot enough to do the damage it did and the underpinning and back of the microwave under that burner would have been severely damaged, but it was not damaged at all proving it COULD NOT of been the back burner as they claimed. Secondly, the microwave melted on the front right corner directly under the right front burner and the melting part of the microwave melted directly into the pan of peas. It did not melt directly on the cook top or it would caught fire.  Evidence proves and the inspection should have proved the right front and back burner knobs were off. Also had it been a fire as they are claiming the cabinets would have burned. The front right part of the microwave that melted was attached to the cabinets and so snug you couldnÃÂt even slide a piece of paper between the two of them. The photos, the stove knobs melting patterns and the microwave right front melting pattern and my injuries prove their investigation was flawed, wrong and sabotaged. When the stove was first looked at, it was by a company called Kid Gloves, its a restoration company. They could have possibly damaged critical evidence. I threw a fit in late July to have it inspected by a professional with fires and an electrical expert. It took GE and the insurance company 5 more months before they would accomplish that. It seems as well that I cant get a straight answer as to where is the microwave? It is a critical piece of evidence
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including a broken pelvis, crushed disk, and burns, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
"over the stove" microwave fell off the wall, approximately 2years after purchase.
wall mounting bracket was bent.
Luckily, we had just finished cooking lunch at the stove which involved boiling water.

Contacted installer (home depot) who said "installation" warranty was only good for one year.
When we contacted manufacturer, the rep tried to read me the manual and tell me that the mounting bracket, which was provided to mount the oven as an "over the stove" model, was only an accessory and was not covered under the warranty  Representative did not care that mounting bracket had bent and that there was an inherent design defect.

Representative offered to send a new bracket if I sent a copy of receipt.  Copy was sent but bracket never received.  Follow up email never was responded to by company.
justification: The microwave fell but no injury occurred, and the incident was due to a bent mounting bracket.

incident_description:
I removed a tempered glass shelf from my GE refrigerator for a routine cleaning and placed it in the kitchen sink, ready for cleaning. While it was balanced there, and before I had done anything to it (ie. no water or cleaning cloth was applied to it) it spontaneously exploded into many fragments that scattered widely across my kitchen to a radius of some 6 feet, including into my clothing, my hands and my hair. Fortunately I was wearing reading glasses so avoided fragments reaching my eyes. I received a number of small lacerations on my hands which while bleeding, did not require external medical attention. The clean up required disposing of a number of food items that were contaminated by glass, clearing out glass from the garbage disposal, from across the kitchen, across the counters and floor, and from my clothing and my hands. I received several splinters in my hands that I had to remove using tweezers.

The shelf was made of tempered glass and had no visible defect when I removed it for routine cleaning. The fridge is almost 7 years old. 

This is highly dangerous and I was lucky my injuries were not more serious.
justification: The incident resulted in small lacerations and splinters that did not require medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the spontaneous nature of the tempered glass explosion without prior defects.

incident_description: The oven had a power arc while preheating. There was a huge spark that came out of the oven with a buzzing noise and then you could see a fire in the oven coming through a hole in the bottom.
justification: The incident involved a power arc and visible fire in the oven, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: We own a Kenmore Elite oven model # 790.98029802 purchased 2010 that the racks in the bottom oven no longer fit properly.  If we try to cook anything, the racks fall causing the contents to spill in the oven which has caused burns and a mess.  We have found that many other people have the same problem.  Others have reported that it is caused over a period of time because the walls of the oven have expanded from the heat.  Ovens should be built to withstand the heat as the heat of an oven is necessary to cook.  We have been told that the metal used in the walls of the oven was inferior and cannot withstand high temperatures without expanding.  Sears claims this is not a defect and will not do anything to correct the problem.  The fix (putting new walls in the interior of the oven) would cost more than the oven is worth and Sears will not guarantee that it would not happen again.  We believe this is an obvious dangerous defect and the oven needs to be recalled.  If this were a car it would have been recalled long ago.
justification: The incident has caused burns, indicating an injury, and the problem is reported by many others, suggesting it is likely to occur.

incident_description: I have Kenmore slide in range that was purchased just over five years ago.  On Christmas day 2015 while in operation there was a loud "pop", a visual flash arc and the unit shut down, throwing the breakers.  I took the unit apart and found the connector between the main wiring harness and the wiring harness serving the control panel to be melted and burnt.  The surrounding components where blackened and burned.  This is the main connector from the terminal strip serving power to the entire unit.
justification: The incident involved a loud pop, flash arc, and burnt wiring, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Electric Range (Model 790.4678) from SEARS just five years ago, in 2010.  This past weekend, my wife gently opened the door to check on food when - suddenly - the outer glass panel simply shattered into a thousand pieces on the floor.  The shattered glass - with its tiny, sharp edges - was everywhere.  Much of it still is - in nooks and crannies - around the kitchen that escaped the vacuum cleaner and broom.  

The shards of broken glass easily could have seriously injured my wife - or other family members gathered here on Christmas day.  As it was, my wife was wearing socks at the time of the incident and while a few shards of glass were temporarily lodged in her sock and partly embedded in her foot, she was able to remove the glass, apply First Aid ointment and recover.  (My wife is a healthcare provider / X-ray tech and her mother, who was here at the time, is a Registered Nurse. So, in a way, she was "seen" by two healthcare professionals.)  There are four witnesses to this event: my wife (a healthcare provider for the past 25 years); my father-in-law (a trusted funeral director for 50 years); my mother-in-law (a retired nurse) and my nephew (an IT tech for a [REDACTED] company).  

The oven's temperature was a mild 350-degrees at the time and the door wasn't banged or opened in a harsh or violent way.  Indeed, my wife was merely peeking in on the food that was baking.  This oven should be recalled for a serious manufacturing defect.  I mean - who's even heard of this kind of thing happening before?  Instead, I'm getting a $365 repair bill from Sears to install a new door.  

I tried to tell SEARS directly, but as far as I can determine, the SEARS web site doesn't really allow customers to email the company.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injury (glass shards embedded in the foot), but no severe harm. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not commonly reported.

incident_description: The Kenmore Elite Duel Gas Range is dangerous. It has the potential to seriously burn the person using it and starting a fire. The burners are explosive when it ignites. This is because gas escapes at full force for several seconds before it ignites. The flames extend past the controls of the stove. I have had instances where my pans have been engulfed in flames. I feel every time I use the kenmore elite gas range I am putting myself and the people around me in danger.
justification: The description indicates potential for serious burns and fire, suggesting injury is likely, and the issue occurs frequently during use.

incident_description: This blade came with my Cuisinart Prep 7 Food Processor (DLC-2007N), which I bought several years ago. I used it very rarely (maybe 4 times per year) to make dips like hummus and pesto. Recently, while sampling a fresh batch of hummus, I was quite surprised to find a small sharp piece of metal in my mouth -- which clearly broke off from the blade and mixed into the food. I like spicy hummus, but this was not the kind of edge I was going for. I googled the issue, and found several other people reporting the same problem -- the blade breaks at the rivets. I have photos, showing the broken shard, where it came from, and another rivet already showing clear signs of breaking and launching another metal shard into my food. I'd say either avoid this blade, or at least check it after every use -- BEFORE eating the food it created.
justification: The incident involved a small sharp piece of metal breaking off into food, posing a risk of injury but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using the Breville Fast Slow Cookers, Model Number BPR600XL according to instructions.  The timer was not indicating that it was working, yet I released pressure, and thought I released all the pressure before opening the lid.  When I turned the lid, it exploded, the lid, contents went everywhere and caused 2nd degree burns on my body.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree burns, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it involves a specific malfunction under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
This range came as part of a set with an over-the-range microwave.  The safety issue arises with the placement of the burner knobs on the front of the range.  They are positioned such that they are easily turned on when reaching above the range into the microwave, or into the cabinets above the microwave.  Sometime the burner goes on, and sometimes the burner doesn't light and the gas goes on without a flame.  Either case can lead to serious consequences.  
We have had other ranges and over-the-range microwaves and not experienced this problem.  It's the positioning of the knobs and the ease with which the knobs can be turned.
justification: The incident involves a safety issue with burner knobs being easily turned on, which can lead to gas leaks or unintended burner activation, posing a risk of fire or gas exposure.

incident_description: Have had my Keurig mini brewer for about 4 years and many times I use it, I'm being burnt by the hot water pouring out of the bottom. I'm forced to clean spilled water up which pours out all over the place and have just been told today there was a recall!!!
justification: The user reports being burnt by hot water, indicating an injury, and the issue occurs frequently during use.

incident_description: Cuisinart DCC-1200BCH Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker. The product is used to automatically brew one 8-cup pot of coffee. On the incident date, about 15 minutes after brew was complete, the coffeemaker issued loud popping sounds, filled the kitchen with smoke and a strong electrical smell. Because I was still at home this particular day, I was able to pull the plug and air out the room and avert what I believe was the start of an electrical fire. On any other day, I may have left the house with the coffeemaker still on, trusting that the automatic shut-off feature would turn the pot off.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential electrical fire, but no injury or death occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description:
I have a single serve keuriug coffee maker and it was working one day and the next day l
All the water spewed out the side and on to the kitchen counter
 And now will not make coffee. It is almost brand new.
justification: The incident involved water spewing out without injury, fitting severity level 2. Given the description of a new device malfunctioning, occurrence likelihood is possible (3).

incident_description:
I use my Nutribullet every day and discovered the hard way, never never never put hot foods in your container to blend.  I did.  It created so much pressure inside the container that  I was unable to unscrew the blade. So I went to bed and six hours later, I was awakened by a loud pop!  I went downstairs to discover the contents of my smoothie sprayed all over the ceiling, walls, appliances and floor. Apparently the container could no longer hold the pressure I created from grinding hot cooked food. It exploded, which could of caused serious injury. I was lucky, I was in bed.  The manufacturer could remedy this by simply placing a little rubber cork on top of container to pop open automatically or manually when dangerous levels of pressure build up inside. The other complaint I have is that the underside of the blades is next to impossible to clean.

Thank you.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage but no injuries, as the user was not present when it occurred.

incident_description:
The dish was in the oven for approximately 35 - 45 minutes.  The oven was set to 350 degrees.  The consumer went outside to do some yard work and when she returned, she noticed a burning odor.  She checked the oven and found that there was a slit in the glass backing dish and some of the casserole had dripped from it down onto the heating element.  The consumer turned the oven off and attempted to remove the dish.  As soon as she touched the dish with her pot-holder, it began to shatter.  The consumer had other baking dishes in the oven at the time and she said glass shards had flown from the cracked dish into the food of the other dishes that were in the oven at that time.  As soon as she touched it with her pot-holder, the dish began to shatter even more.  There were no injuries.

*  The consumer threw away all of the food in the oven, because of the glass in the other dishes.

11/30/2015.  The consumer called the mfr. to discuss this matter and their rep. referred her to CPSC to file a report.

The consumer said that she believes that this was only her 2nd time using this smaller baking dish.  It came in a set of 2 and the second dish was approx. 9" x 13", but it was not damaged.
 
The consumer said that she saw several other reports of this type of problem online and she questions why this has not been addressed or corrected.
justification: The incident involved a baking dish shattering but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) due to multiple similar reports online.

incident_description: I was going to wipe out the lower oven to use it Thanksgiving morning. As I opened the door, I heard a loud "pop". It was the outer glass popping & breaking. It flew all over the kitchen & into the family room. Shards of glass were every where.
justification: The incident involved glass breaking and scattering, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My husband and I purchased a new Adora GE stainless steel gas range from Home Depot in Saratoga Springs, NY, on 04/09/14.  Sunday night, 12/27/15, my husband placed a pizza into the oven at 400 degrees. About 20 minutes later he heard an exploding sound when he noticed that the 3rd inner-most layer of glass inside the oven door had exploded and shattered leaving millions of particulate, jagged glass all over the inside floor and ceiling of the oven appliance.

 I am very concerned over this, as it could have been extremely dangerous had he opened the door at or just before it exploded and caused him serious possibly even fatal injury. We had to carefully remove the glass and vacuum it up and vacuum the inside of the oven, so that the glass would not fall all over the place and so we could shut the oven door. Now I am worried that there is still tiny particles stuck in the fan that may blow back into our food even after we have had this issue repaired causing more worry and concern.
 I contacted GE consumer relations and spoke to a case manager who offered to waive the trip charge of a local major appliance repair center, A&E. She was very short and curt with me telling me that she would not be able to cover glass and parts until the service person had given her his "findings". I asked her what she would need to know from the technician before GE would take responsibilty for the stove and pay for the glass and labor? How would his findings be any different than what my husband and I had seen? and she could not answer that question, all she kept saying was that "the technician needs to see the stove first so that we know what step we need to take next."
She could not answer the question and kept placing me on hold like she was looking for guidance in answering every question I asked of her. The consumer manager I dealt with was named [REDACTED] and she never once offered any condolences for my troubles or inconvenience or hardship. Though out of warranty of 1 year, this appliance is obviously in need of being recalled due to the fact that the glass cannot withstand normal oven temperatures. It is only just under two years old and I have never ever heard of something like this happening before, until I read several complaints online.  
I feel it is my responsibility to let other people know of this incident, to hopefully prevent any future danger to anyone else, on top of the fact that the oven cost us just under $1000. And if the company is aware of the glass having this tendency, they should be willing to at least extend the warranty on this part of the stove as to not inconvenience people further. Besides the fact that the stove was expensive. They should be willing to pay for an upgrade in glass in the oven, glass that can withstand 400-500 degrees without exploding. Now we are waiting on a January 6th, 2016 appointment that GE is paying for, for a repairman from A&E appliance to assess the situation and reveal to GE what caused the glass to break so they can figure out what to do next. Whether that be, paying for the glass and labor, which they most certainly should do and [REDACTED] could not give me an answer on that question of whether or not this would be covered.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door glass, which could have caused injury but did not, and similar incidents have been reported online, indicating a possible defect.

incident_description:
Last night, at about 8:00 pm, our Kenmore Elite dishwasher exploded into flames and poured thick acrid smoke out of the control panel. Thanks God we were home. We usually turn it on when we leave in the morning or as we go to bed at night. I could not turn the unit off at the Control Panel (due to flames and sparks). I could not imagine what might have happened if we were not here to turn the breaker off on the electrical panel. 
I checked the Kenmore site, and the CPA site, and though our unit was NOT listed as a problem, it exploded into flames just like the MANY other Kenmore dishwasher that ARE listed. This is criminal that they only recall the units AFTER they catch fire. They must be using the same parts in my unit as in the recalled units. We were lucky, and I pray to God that no one else has this problem and loses life or limb. My throat still burns from the smoke.
PLEASE warn other owners immediately! And get this unit recalled!
Many thanks,
[REDACTED]

P.S. While this incident happened on 1-11-2008, I want it on record with as many sites as possible.
I sent this letter to the Consumer Protection Agency the day after the incident. Also to the manufacturer, Sears (where we purchased it), and Consumer Reports.
justification: The dishwasher exploded into flames causing smoke inhalation, which resulted in throat irritation but no serious injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the dishwasher was placed in wash cycle, approximately 30 mins later he smelled a burnt odor.  He opened the dishwasher and noticed that there was water in the unit, he closed the door and tried to continue the cycle but the control panel ceased to operate.  (11/2015) The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that a service technician would be sent out.  (11/2015) The service technician examined the unit and advised that a power cord assembly was burnt.  He was informed that the cord would be sent out to him free of charge from the manufacturer.  He was also advised that it was not part of a recall.

Consumer stated that the dishwasher was purchased about a year ago.

Consumer stated that it has been almost a month since the incident and the manufacturer has not resolved his issue despite emails and phone calls.  He feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that the surface light (on the bottom of the microwave) gets overheated and starts smoking. The consumer stated that the paint on the bottom panel is peeling off. 

The consumer contacted Gold Star Appliance regarding the issue. They informed her to contact GE.
When the consumer contacted GE, they scheduled an appointment with A&E Factory Service (Dallas, TX) for an inspection. 

The consumer had a technician, [REDACTED], come out from A&E Factory Service on 9/11/15. The technician examined the surface light and mentioned that there was no reflector. The technician put a temperature gauge on the inside of the microwave. The inside of the microwave was at 180F within 5 minutes of having the surface light on. The microwave was not running. The technician contacted GE Tech Support. The technician informed GE that he has been servicing microwaves for 39 years and he has never seen a microwave without a reflector. He informed GE of the overheating issue.

GE asked the technician to see if he can order a reflector and install it. The technician stated that he could not find a reflector that was made for the JVM series microwave. The supervisor confirmed with GE Engineers that there were no reflectors made for surface light for the JVM Series.

incident_description:
On December 17, 2015, while washing my 1-cup glass Anchor Hocking measuring cup, it suddenly EXPLODED in my hands for no apparent reason. Shards of glass flew over 8 feet across the room, as well as under the living room sofa, on the kitchen cabinets, kitchen floor, sink and, worst of all, down my garbage disposal! Thank goodness I was wearing a pair of thin latex gloves or my hands would have been severely injured. Even with the gloves on, there were a couple of small abrasions on my hand. Thank goodness, I was wearing my eyeglasses or IÃÂm sure my face would have been injured. The cup had been sitting on the counter for at least half an hour after I used it to pour milk and I did not hit it anywhere on the sink while I was washing it. I was able to get the large shards of glass out of the garbage disposal using kitchen tongs and a flashlight, but the disposal would not work afterwards. Therefore, after a $79 service call to the plumber, who had to totally remove the disposal to clear the glass and reinstall it, it is now working. I still am finding pulverized glass debris in the kitchen and dining areas even after thoroughly cleaning those areas.

From reviewing on-line complaints, this type of occurrence does not seem to be new, and there is a history dating back to 2008 for similar occurrences! It is unconscionable that this problem has not been corrected before someone gets seriously hurt! Needless to say, I will never purchase another Anchor Hocking product and am telling everyone I know not to either.
justification: The incident resulted in small abrasions on the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The online complaints suggest a history of similar occurrences, indicating the likelihood is possible (3).

incident_description: COOKS 780-5008 slow cooker, have had a few years.  Cooked food for a party and was cleaning up the next day.  Washed the bottom and top by hand and laid it out to dry.  About a minute later, the top exploded!  Glass went everywhere.  Nobody was even in the room.

incident_description:
We purchased a Cuisinart Elite Collection 12-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker, Model DCC-3650WS, on April 25, 2015 at the Macy's Department Store located in Palm Desert California.  We registered the product with Cuisinart on April 26, 2015. 

On the morning of December 12, 2015 strange sounds began coming from the coffeemaker followed by smoke which enveloped the coffee pot with smoke also coming from the rear of the unit where the electrical outlet is located.  There was a strong stench that came with the smoke.  When we were able to examine the unit it appeared the top of the coffee filter had burned.

We called the Cuisinart Customer Service Center, 800-726-0190 and informed the customer service representative [REDACTED] what had happened.   After checking the model and serial number the representative told us the warranty had expired on the day we purchased the coffeemaker even though the instruction book said the unit came with a limited three-year warranty.  She offered us a discount coupon.  We told her we would be purchasing a new coffee maker that day so the coupon was of no interest, rather the purpose of our call was to provide an alert.  We are not sure how our alert would or would not be handled within Cuisinart.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from the coffeemaker, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
In the last 10 days my husband has had two glass lids shatter.

The first lid burst and shattered while sitting on the counter next to the stove.  The lid was not on top of a hot surface, pan or pot.

The second lid was placed on top of a pot containing recently roasted beef bones, water and vegetable stock (placed in it and brought to a boil).

This is very disturbing.  I did not think there was an expiration date on glass cookware.
justification: Glass lids shattered twice, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Purchased a Kenmore Gas Range and Over the Range Microwave. Have had it for a year. The microwave was working fine. Put in popcorn to microwave and the inside of the unit where the rack sits caught on fire. Burned my microwave, and cabinets. The microwave was manufactured January of 2014. Model number 790.80323310. Called Sears Customer Assistance Number listed on microwave at 1-800-469-4663 and they have not been any help. And only a few days until Christmas.

Model 790.45492502

No doubt in my mind if we weren't here there would have been a fire.

Here are the facts:
1. It took Viking customer service one month to find a repair person to service the dishwasher.
2. The repair person came out to replace the defective part and discovered that another part ( the electrical board) had been damaged (actually burned) and needed to be replaced.
3. 11/6/2015:  Another call made to Viking: Viking agreed to have another electrical board sent out for placement after a lengthly discussion. 
4 Still waiting for replacement piece.  

This dishwasher was on the verge of overheating and nearly caused a fire in my home.
justification: The dishwasher had an electrical issue that nearly caused a fire, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

When the boiled water was ready, I lifted the pot to pour the water into a tea cup and the entire pot separated into two pieces.  The boiling water spilled onto my leg and foot causing significant first and second degree burns to my foot.  I was driven to the emergency room where I was treated and released and now must follow up with a plastic surgeon.

My husband and I were in the living room, wwhen all of a sudden we heard a glass explosion and we ran to the kitchen to see what fell. Nothing had fallen, but our oven door had exploded and the glass was all over the floor. I'm thankful our kids were in their rooms and the dog was with us. 
I called Sears and they said they would charge me for the door, for the technician to come out and fix it and a service charge, so we are talking a few hundred dollars to fix it. We are not happy that this is a pattern with the Kenmore ovens that start with the model number 790 and we trully think a recall should happen before someone gets hurt.

justification: The incident resulted in injury (glass cuts) and the description mentions this is a common issue with the product, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
(11/14/2015) The consumer noticed that the light was not working. He removed the light cover and saw that there were two holes burnt in the plastic above the lights.

The consumer replaced the bulb and did a video of the inside of the refrigerator with the door closed. He wanted to see why the plastic had burned. When he looked at the video, he discovered that the light inside of the unit did not go out when the door was closed.


The submitter added:

We purchased Frigidaire kitchen products, including a refrigerator on July 27, 2011, in anticipation of our home under construction.  We moved into the home on November 1,
2011.

On Saturday, November 14, 2015, my wife informed me that the lights were not on in the upper area of the refrigerator.  As I was removing the bulbs, we realized that a hole had been burned through the plastic liner above the bulbs. The next day, our son was visiting and placed his recording device into the refrigerator, and closed the door. After viewing the video from inside the storage area, it was obvious that the light stayed on while the door was shut.

I visited the service department [REDACTED] at Karl's on Monday, November 16, and he suggested that the problem was a malfunctioning light switch.

Our concern is of the possible carcinogens that could be present and the possible fire danger created by the heat of the bulbs in burning through the plastic liner.

The hole on the left side, (as you are facing into the refrigerator), is about the size of a silver dollar,and the hole on the right side is about the size of a half dollar.

On November 18, 2015, a service technician from Karl's checked the refrigerator and determined that a shield kit, including a new panel was needed.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved burnt plastic due to a malfunctioning light switch, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Had my gravy on low as I always do, jumped in the shower,  when I came out of the shower I could smell burning. I thought I had a brain fart and hit high on my stove top instead of low.  I tried to lower the temp and nothing happened.  I tried turning the stove top off and nothing happened.  My heating eye element was still on high and would not turn off. The only way I could get it to turn off is by cutting the power off from my circuit box. I have thrown the switch back on several times to see maybe it will reset the computer.  Element still comes on high and blazing and you cannot turn it off.  After doing some research I see that this same product and name was recalled in 2009 with the same issues. Although my model and serial numbers do not match the ones on the recall list.  It is a Kenmore Elite glass top drop range

The top of the range got so hot, everything near my stove was hot to the touch. If I would have been a few minutes longer in the shower, I am afraid my home would have caught on fire.
justification: The stove malfunctioned and could not be turned off, posing a significant fire hazard that could have led to injury or death if not addressed promptly.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the heating element of the oven overheated and was in flames to a point that it broke.  He stated that while the oven was still in the pre-heating mode they heard a noise and noticed the incident.  The control panel was used to power it off.   However, the following day his spouse stated that when she went by the unit it was still warm from not turning off, she turned the heat control to low and the unit cooled down.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this oven could have caused a house fire if no one was present.
justification: The incident involved an overheating oven with flames but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled by turning off the unit.

incident_description:
Entered upstairs kitchen for breakfast and smelled GAS.

Noticed one knob on gas cooktop was slightly ajar (see photos).

Moved knob to full OFF position, opened windows and doors for ventilation, and left house for a couple of hours.
justification: Gas leak was detected but no injury occurred; prompt action mitigated the risk.

incident_description:
Viking gas range purchased from retailer in California, March 2015 then noticed the first time she tried to use the broiler that it didn't work.  This was repaired at manufacturer expense.

On October 6th, 2015 the caller head a pop from her kitchen then saw that the tempered outer glass on the oven door had shattered and dropped to the floor.

She contacted the manufacturer again, she spoke with the technician on October 7th, 2015 and filed a report with him then asked if it was alright to us the oven with only the inner glass remaining and he replied that yes she could.

November 1st, 2015 the caller noticed that the oven was very warm, she opened the doors then saw that the broiler was on although all of the controls were off.

She tried to turn the broiler off but could not until her husband pulled the unit from the wall, disconnected the gas line then turned it back on, however when he turned it back on it created a "poof" and he noticed that there seemed to be some gas leaking.

He disconnected the range.

The service tech came to the home November 3rd, 2015 and advised the caller that the gas valve inside the oven was open.

The tech disabled the oven leaving caller with only access to the burners.

The caller states that she is waiting for the glass for her door and for repairs to the range gas valves for a range that she purchased only 8 months ago.

The manufacturer rep advised the caller that they will be discussing a refund with the decision making persons with their company.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction and gas leakage but no reported injuries, warranting a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the recurring issues with the range.

incident_description: The writer heard a sound coming from refrigerator similar to a crackling sound or popping twice. Upon approach to the appliance, the writer observed a large amount of thick white electrical smoke emitting from the appliance. The writer immediately unplugged the appliance from the electrical outlet. Then called the local fire department. The fire department inspected the appliance and household. The fire department deemed that the source of the fire was from the appliance. That the fire was electrical caused by the appliance.
justification: The incident involved electrical smoke and required fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Purchased a KENMORE Microwave Oven Model 405.7212310 in 2014.
Not 100% on the purchase date, but we have used the microwave for more than a year.
About a week ago, after heating up some food, the microwave turned itself ON after I closed the door. The clock was reading 00:00, but the light went on, carousel turned, fan and (I presume) MW device continued to go. Pushing the STOP button would not make it stop. Pushing the Door Release stopped the oven from operating. This happened once every few days last week, but this morning it happened 3 times.  I called Sears/Kenmore Customer Assistance:  1-800-842-1289  spoke to [REDACTED] about the incident(s). He apologized that the unit was no longer under warranty, and suggested I bring the unit to an appliance repair shop.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on unexpectedly, but no injury or harm was reported.

incident_description: KitchenAid oven, about 7 years old, the glass door exploded about 20 minutes into the self-cleaning cycle.   hot glass filled up the bottom of my oven and poured out the bottom of my oven and onto my kitchen floor.  despite hours of cleaning and vacuuming, the oven still contains pieces and shards of glass in the crevices, as well as powdered glass, throughout the oven cavity.  and the bottom of the oven is completely charred.  Kitchenaid/whirlpool refuses to replace the oven or admit fault.
justification: The oven door exploded during use, causing damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Dear Sir/Ms.
In July of this year I bought a set of dinnerware from a Payless Grocery in Anderson Indiana.
A few days ago I put one of these dishes in my microwave and upon hearing the bell opened the door, reached in and the dish literally exploded. Fortunately I incurred no injury but think of the possibilities.
My granddaughter stays with me often and if indeed she had been injured in a similar event with loss of eye or anything for that matter ..... major suit would have been initiated.
I returned the dishes to the store including the one which exploded. Having no foreseeable need to keep the receipt for dishes I didn't; however, I did take with me the credit card statement showing the purchase,
date, etc.. The manager said no receipt/no refund. I mentioned the safety issue but she paid absolutely no attention to safety .. none.
Since that time I have called a corporate phone number and had them send a receipt to me via e-mail. Upon several conversations with three store managers I have taken care of the refund myself.
Now, I am sending this note to you concerning the all-important subject of a dangerous product. It is evidently
mislabeled, ( says is microwavable safe on dish) defective, and has injurious probability.
In fairness to you I write you first that you may look into this matter thus avoiding further action by me.
Retraction of product from all store shelves requested.
justification: The incident involved a dish exploding in the microwave but no injury occurred, though potential for injury was noted.

incident_description:
This is a 7 cup Cuisinart food processor with a stainless steel blade. It was manufactured in China in 2011 and purchased approximately in 2013. It has been used very little as the blade is still as sharp as when new. We were pureeing a can of diced tomatoes when the blade simply broke. In looking at the unbroken part, I now see that the blade under the rivets that attach it to the round plastic base of the blade assembly is cracked under the two (of a total of 4) remaining rivets. It is clear that the four rivets that affix the blade itself to the round plastic part were pressed on using too much pressure. Cuisinart refused to replace the broken blade as it is no longer under warrantee.

Extremely sharp blade parts in the food one provides to one's family is an obvious safety hazard. This is a manufacturing defect and should be recalled with the blade replaced by a properly riveted blade.
justification: The blade broke during use, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
CBC-6400 PC Cusinart coffee maker. 

The carafe on this model is glass with plastic around the top. The carafe has begun to leak from the bottom of the plastic allowing scalding hot water to drip everywhere and is a serious burn risk.
justification: The leaking of scalding hot water poses a serious burn risk, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:

The parts are mostly stainless steel and silicone which hold up nicely, but the spring is ferrous which rusts and then falls apart leaving pieces much like a steel pin (one such piece was an inch long, others are shorter) in my food!  Somewhat by chance, I found it, avoiding a potentially serious problem. Anyway, I wrote to them and they ignored my letter.  IÃÂll send you the same photos and see if we can avoid future problems with these otherwise good kitchen tongs.  
Feel free to call or write if I can be further help.
justification: The incident involves rusted metal pieces falling into food, which could cause injury if ingested, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: New coffee pot caught on fire during first use.
justification: The coffee pot caught fire, indicating an incident with potential for harm, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
my new gas range has five burners. When the knobs are pushed in you have to turn the knob in order to get gas and ignition. My problem is that by accident a knob was bumped and turned just a bit. this caused the gas to flow but it wasn't turned on far enough to activate the ignition. We found this out the hard way because the kitchen filled with gas. I contacted Frigidaire by email and they told me this was not a design flaw and that I should just be careful. Doesn't seem right to my, or anyone I've talked to.

This actually happened to me twice in the first sew weeks that we owned the stove
justification: The incident involved gas leakage without ignition, posing a hazard but no injury, and it happened twice in a short period, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
(11/02/2015) The consumer stated that she turned the oven on to do some baking. After about 30 minutes she tried to turn the oven off. The off button would not work. The control panel circuit board had melted. The consumer stated that the circuit board had been replaced about three years ago because it had melted.

incident_description: Oven was being used to bake when the oven door (inside) shattered onto food and bottom of oven.  When opening oven, shards of glass fell out onto kitchen floor, causing huge hazard for occupants.  Also, glass continued to shatter after the fact, as the food was pulled from oven and discarded into garbage.  Shards of glass flew across the room as the mess was attempted to be cleaned up with vacuum, leading for further danger.

incident_description:
While handling the Ninja blender in a safe manner, I poured the contents of the blender out after removing the lid. The blade detached and put a deep gash into my finger when I tried stopping it from falling out and breaking the glass. I warned my children not to EVER touch this appliance, it could easily sever a digit or worse. I told my wife about the incident and she didn't heed my warning and cut her finger to the point that she won't let the kids use it and now she is very careful.
Take this product off the shelves before some gets hurt badly.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to two individuals, with deep cuts described, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the repeated occurrence within the same household.

incident_description:
Purchased a WARING Pro convection toaster oven model TCO6000 Serial number 110825 UL Listed 9H90

This is the third toaster oven. The previous two were replaced by Waring and have had the same problem. After use the toaster oven door mechanism becomes jammed it will open a few inches then stick. As you continue to apply force to open the door the toaster oven falls over and can injure the operator if it is positioned on the edge of the counter. There was also a problem with the elements and collars that were located at the ends becoming burnt.

incident_description:
My dishwasher caught fire last night. The model has been recalled but not my serial number. 
Product is a GE
Model is PDW9280N00SS
Serial Number LM818604B
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident but no injury was reported. The model has been recalled, indicating a known issue.

I HAD PULLED THE RACK OUT TO DO THE BASTING BUT IT ROLLED BACK IN PLACE.  IT APPEARS THAT THE RACK SLOPES TO THE REAR OF THE OVEN INSTEAD OF BEING MORE ON THE  LEVEL .

justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from steam and a hot handle, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
All of the plastic tabs broke off of the dishwasher's top rack within a few months of using it (about once a week.)  As the tabs broke off, we replaced it with screws to make it stronger.  I'm sure a replacement rail with the same plastic tabs would only work for another few months. Any recall/redesign will require this part to be made of metal. Having tiny plastic tabs hold up the weight of all the dishes on the top rack is a design flaw.

Each time a tab broke off, the top rack came crashing down while full of glasses.  This is a safety hazard for many reasons; in my case, my hand was jammed onto the silverware below.  Maytag customer service claimed there are no issues with the top rack, despite all the product reviews from people who are having the same problem in the first few months as well. Maytag rep replied that reviews are hearsay and said the design isn't defective because there's no recall....
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hand jammed onto silverware) and the problem is recurring based on user reviews, indicating a design flaw.

incident_description:

Maytag Quiet Series 200
MDB4651AWS
10037666GN

incident_description: This oven is new to me, as it was in a home that I recently purchased. On my second time using the stove I used the warming burner for the first time. It seemed to work fine, but when I turned all the burners off, the warming burner light stayed on. After 5 minutes it was clearly still producing heat. Only flipping off the breaker or unplugging the range/oven caused the warming burner to turn off.
justification: The warming burner staying on poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: On Thanksgiving Day, 11/26/2015, I took a glass Pyrex 9" x 13" baking dish from my cupboard.  I placed 4 yams inside it that had been previously baked and fully cooled.  I put the dish into a preheated 350 degree oven to re-warm.  Shortly thereafter, a loud explosion came form the oven, which we opened to find the dish completely broken into small pieces, many of them sharp-looking shards.  No injuries occurred since the explosion happened while the oven door was closed.  The oven was not damaged.
justification: The incident involved a broken dish but no injuries or damage beyond the dish itself.

incident_description: Brand new dishwasher starts by itself.  When you open the door it continues to run   The only way to turn it off is to turn off the circuit breaker
justification: The dishwasher malfunction poses a potential hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description: I have small Corelle dishes for my children - I was pulling apart 2 small bowls and one shattered into a bazillion pieces. I had cuts on my hands - I didn't see or feel the glass cutting me, because some of the shards are microscopic. I found shards in 2 adjoining rooms as well. I completely understand that glass breaks, but this was like a small bomb went off.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts from glass shards, indicating an injury, and the widespread dispersion of shards suggests a significant breakage event.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the unit was installed in the house when she moved in about 6 years ago. She is not aware if there were any repairs/modifications made to the unit by the previous owner.

The consumer stated that she started the dishwasher cycle. The cycle was almost complete when her husband smelled strong electrical burning odor. The consumer's husband saw black smoke being emitted from the the control panel of the dishwasher. The consumer stated that there are black soot marks on top of the dishwasher.

The consumer stated that the unit did not turn off from the control panel area. They had to cut the circuit to the unit from the circuit breaker in order to turn it off. 

The consumer stated that part of the plastic on the control panel area (outside of the dishwasher door) melted and turned yellow. 

The consumer did not notice any flames. She believes that they turned the dishwasher off in time to avoid further issues. 

The consumer contacted Kenmore on 9/2/15. They informed her that they can come out and replace the motor under the recall. The consumer believes that the control panel is the issue and is what needs to be replaced. The consumer was informed that a technician will have to examine the unit to determine the issue with the control panel. 

A technician from Sears is supposed to come out on the 9/15/15 for an inspection. The cost for motor, labor and service fee will be covered by Kenmore. 

The consumer mentioned that she has to keep the circuit break off to keep the unit off. The consumer turned on the circuit and the unit started running again.

incident_description: (10/28/2015) The consumer stated that she had turned the dishwasher on. After about 30 minutes the consumer saw black smoke coming from the right side near the Kenmore logo. The consumer open the dishwasher which usually turns the unit off, but it did not turn off. Water was shooting out of the bottom of the unit. The consumer had to turn the unit off at the circuit breaker.

incident_description:
On 11/04/15 the consumer wanted to use her oven but noticed that some of the buttons were not working. The consumer states the oven went to rapid reheat and then to the broil setting with the temperature at 500 degrees. The consumer pressed the ÃÂcancelÃÂ button but the button did not work and the oven was still getting hot. She is elderly and cannot pull out the range and go to another part of the home to shut off the circuit breaker. incident_description:
My new COCK POT cookers lid shattered during its fourth use.  While cooking soup and standing right next to it.  Scared me big time with a loud POP ! incident_description:
Jenn-Air Refrigerator

incident_description:

The consumer was suggested to replace the racks and few other things in the unit. They informed her that they will not replace the unit this time since they already replaced it once before. incident_description:
(11/1/2015) The consumer stated that she had used the oven to cook biscuits. The oven had been off for about 15 minutes. While she was in the kitchen doing the dishes, the outer glass of the oven door shattered and popped out on the floor.

incident_description: Bought the Toucan battery operated can opener.  Put the 4 AA batteries in it.  Pushed the button, but nothing happened.  Reversed the batteries around several times, but nothing happened.  I Could feel some warmth on the underside where the batteries were held, and kept trying to see if it would work.  Decided to leave it alone on the counter and probably take it back to the store where we bought it.  Finished eating dinner but could smell something that didn't seem right.  Went to the TouCan can opener and it was very hot.  Lifted the cover and could see the paper on the battery lifting up.  Afraid of an explosion, I took it outside and knocked the batteries loose.
justification: The device malfunctioned and overheated, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred as the issue was addressed in time.

incident_description: Smelled something hot in my kitchen area and found that the lights in the refrigerator would not shut off.  I double checked to make sure the doors were closed completely but the lights were still on.  When I looked in the refrigerator I could see that the light housing cover was melted and the light ballast were discolored.  I removed the melted cover and lights from the fridge.  I later found that this is a known issue with these refrigerator and part of a class action lawsuit in 2012.  I had Sears Repair come to the house and they confirmed this was part of the previously identified problem but they are no longer fixing it as part of the settlement according to his Service Flash on his computer and wanted $500 now to fix it.  I should have been covered by Sears  SF46-515R4 but he says that it shows on his computer but is grayed out so he can not access it.  There is multiple reports of this same problem on the web.  I'm glad I was home at the time and it didn't cause any further damage or spread beyond the refrigerator.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light that caused melting and discoloration, but no injury or further damage occurred.

incident_description: I was about to wash a square glass Pyrex backing dish that was soaking in the sink all day with room temp water. I pored the water out and was holding the dish with my right hand and using a sponge in my left to get the food off the dish. All of a sudden it shattered in my hand. incident_description:
On Nov 20, 2015, I was preparing toast with my Cuisinart "Total Touch" Convection Toaster Oven Broiler, when I heard the oven make an odd electrical sound.  Upon examining it, I noted that the oven appeared to have shorted internally - I could see flames inside, and smoke started billowing out of the top vents.  I immediately unplugged the product, and took it outside - where the smoke continued.  I poured water on the product (not a good move for an electrical fire, I now recognize), and finally noted that all activity with it, had stopped.

There was no previous damage noted to the product, and it had performed quite well for the several years we have owned it.  To see this event take place - risking my home, and the health and safety of my 5-year-old son especially ÃÂ was very troubling.

I called Cuisinart at 800-726-0190, and reported the issue, providing my model and serial number:
 
Model: CTO-140PC
Serial: 30412

The agent [REDACTED] took my name, address, and phone number, and indicated I would be contacted by corporate in two to three days.

However, a week later, I still had yet to hear anything back.

So, I called them again on Nov 27, 2015 at the same number.  The agent this time,[REDACTED] , took my name and phone, again confirmed the model and serial, and asked for details of the situation.  As before, she asked if there was any injury or property damage.  I indicated "no", and indicated that I have photos and video of the results of the incident.

Apparently, NO RECORD of my previous call was available in their system. She asked for my address, and again logged my phone number.  Also asked for a email address - I provided them [REDACTED].

While on the phone, I also reiterated that the Cuisinart rep at Bed Bath and Beyond (on the previous Friday, 11/20) assured me that Cusinart Corporate would take care of the situation - no matter how long ago we purchased the product.

She (as [REDACTED] did before) indicated they would call me back within 2-3 business days.  I indicated my lack of confidence in this process, but she indicated she "guarantees" that someone will call me by Tuesday, Dec 1, 2015.

It is now after close of business on Tuesday.

I am obviously very concerned at the problem encountered with the product - but especially troubled by the lack of engagement of Cusinart.  They appear to have phone representatives who take down information, ask questions of the consumer to flesh out their report, and then completely ignore the resulting information.

I am therefore reaching out to the Consumer Products Safety Commission for assistance.  Not only do I want Cusinart to take this incident seriously, but I need them to answer as to why I've experienced so much frustration in simply trying to report the issue to them.

Please advise.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with no reported injuries or property damage, and the likelihood of such an event is unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: On 11/23/2015 I went to use my Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Range 790.79383400. I pressed the bake button on the panel when all of a sudden the panel start making cracking sounds and all the lights started flicking on and off immediately followed by black smoke and flames shooting out the back vents hitting the microwave above. I grabbed my fire extinguisher and sprayed the back of the stove. I had my wife run to the garage to shut off the breaker for the stove. With the fire out you could still hear the sizzling wires inside and smell electrical burning for hours. I unplugged everything from the range and just let it sit. I called the Sears repair line (1-800-4-MY-HOME and got to talking with a customer service rep who showed no concern for the fact that this range almost burnt my house down. She was more concerned with selling me a broken appliance warranty. I made an appointment to have a service tech come out anyhow. I then emailed Kenmore with exact details of what happened and have not heard a word from them.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
An incident occurred to me that seems ripe for a Rossen Report. I suffered a very scary incident over the weekend with my Frigidaire stove, as set forth in my Facebook post I am copying below. So far, Frigidaire has indicated that they will not be replacing or repairing the product under any circumstances, and that it will be several days before anyone even contacts me. Certainly, we will not be able to have Thanksgiving dinner at this point, and I have suffered a very large second-degree burn on my arm, for which I had to seek medical treatment. The burn occurred because the handle is mounted on the glass front door (not to any metal frame) in this model, meaning that when I opened the door to place food inside, and the glass shattered (without having made contact with anything), the handle detached and caused the door (375 degrees) to snap back and burn my arm. The terrifying part is that I have a 9 month old baby and a 3 year-old son. Had they been anywhere near, the injuries could have been much more serious. I was told by Frigidaire that this is a common occurrence and can happen if there is a hairline crack, even if not visible. This is absolutely an unsafe product, and I just want to ensure that other persons (and potentially children) are not seriously injured. Frigidaire had no trouble taking payment from me for their defective product (only purchased two years ago), but is very slow to address the damage  and injury caused by their negligence.  Please help me get this important safety issue heard and addressed. 

If you own a glass front Fridgidaire oven, be warned. Last night, I simply opened My oven to put dinner in to cook and the entire front shattered, spraying glass shards in every direction as far as 10 feet. The door didn't hit anything and had no visible/known cracks. After shattering, the door snapped closed on my arm, resulting in a second degree burn. I also had several minor cuts. I'm only posting this because I feel so lucky that my babies weren't anywhere near at the time. This is a very serious safety issue. I want others to be aware of it. My initial call to Fridgidaire was met with indifference. The operator offered to assist me in "purchasing a replacement part." Um, no thank you. Instead, I will be filing a complaint with the Consumer Products Safety Commission. Your faulty product could have blinded or maimed me or my children. I will not be paying you to replace your faulty parts.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity level 3). Frigidaire indicated this is a common occurrence, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
My wife and I recently received a battery-operated can opener as a gift. The design is such that it rests on top of the can and at the push of a button rotates around the top of the can.  A blade slices through the edge of the top can seam separating the lid from the can. The opener is stopped at the second touch of the button and there is no automatic mechanism to stop the opener from rotating.
On first use after stopping the opener, I pressed up on the lid with my thumb and received a needle-thin splinter of metal, drawing blood. On closer observation there were numerous, fine metal spines protruding from the cut edge of the can. I suspect they are caused wherever the cutting blade makes an additional pass over where it has previously cut. As there is no automatic stopping mechanism, the opener can make numerous circuits around the can before being manually stopped. These small metal slivers can easily be transferred to food removed from the can!
I spoke with the elderly friend who gave us the opener; she had already identified the dangerous problem with the identical opener she had purchased.
Model: ÃÂTouCan -- WorldÃÂs Easiest Hands-Free Can OpenerÃÂ
Distributed by TeleBrands, Fairfield, NJ 07004
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (a metal splinter drawing blood) and the description suggests this is a common issue with the product.

incident_description:
GE Profile refrigerator purchased December 2010 from P.C. Richard in Yonkers, NY
Model No. PSB42YSXASS, Serial No. DT590119

On November 20, 2015 our nine-month old baby was crawling by the fridge and stuck his right hand fingers into the metal grate at the bottom of the fridge. When he pulled them out it cut the skin off the top of two fingers leaving a crater in one and a gash in the other. We immediately took him to his doctor who responded to the emergency by applying a tight bandage to stop the bleeding.  After two days with that, the bandage was loosened. He is healing.

THE ISSUE: The metal grate is sharp, like a knife.  It should have been sanded down. It is also an appealing feature to a baby because it is shiny, and it is hidden from an adult's view because of it's position on the floor under the fridge.

I think it is very reasonable to believe that other crawling age babies have had the same injury and some may have fared even worse.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a baby, and the description suggests the hazard is likely to affect other crawling babies due to the design of the fridge.

But this unit has been trouble from the start; and we had it repaired several times while it was under the service contract.  Even after demanding that the temp control be replace on our final service call, it never fixed the problem of fluctuating temperatures and overall oven performance.
