incident_description:
The oven was on approx. 350 degrees for a couple hours.  The consumer conducted a few test and he said that the lower oven emits excessive levels of CO after about 3 hours of use.  The consumer noticed the problem when his CO alarm went off, while cooking.  The CO alarm is in his bedroom, which is adjacent to his kitchen.  

6/3/2015.  Their CO alarm went off and displayed a reading of 46 ppm.  The consumer called the local Carmel Fire Department and went outside.  The fire department came out and confirmed that there was a high level of CO in the home.  The firemen notified the consumer's local gas company, Vectren Energy, who also sent a technician out to verify the problem.  The Vectren tech. confirmed the fire department's findings and advised the consumer to contact the manufacturer's local service company.  Both the fire department and the energy department technician confirmed that the range burners were operating correctly and that the problem was limited to the oven.

6/4/2015:  The consumer contacted the mfr. the next day and they sent out a technician a few days later.   The mfr's tech. confirmed that the oven emitted excessive levels of CO.  The tech. ordered replacement parts and came back out a week later to replace the upper and lower igniters in the oven.  The tech. tested the oven after installing the new igniters.  He left the oven on for approx. 5 - 10 minutes, but his detector did not identify excessive CO levels, neither did the consumer's CO tester.  The tech. was very busy and could not spend a lot of time (hours) at the consumer's home.

8/19/2015:  The consumer's CO alarm went off again and displayed approx. 33 ppms for CO levels.  The consumer called the service tech. again and he called Whirlpool, who he said owns Maytag now. The technician agreed to come back out.  The rep. in Whirlpool's Safety Dept. said that the consumer should have this issue looked at again and provided him with a Concession Number:  [REDACTED], so that he would not be charged for the return service visit.

  *  The consumer discontinued use of the oven while waiting for the tech. to come back out.

Approximately a week later, the mfr's tech. came back out and checked the oven again, but he could only test it for 5 - 10 minutes, due to how busy he was.

The consumer decided to conduct his own test with the oven on 350 degrees.  The consumer said that his CO tester does not register ppm in the range of 0 - 30, but does once the levels exceed 30 ppms.  After 2 hours: 58 minutes, he got a reading of 31 ppms.  The levels progressively increased and after 5 hours, the levels reached 38 ppm.  At that point, he turned the oven to the off position, for fear of inhaling too much CO.  During this time the consumer had the CO detector in close proximity of the range.

8/25/2015:  The consumer checked the lower oven again and he called Whirlpool again and told them that the service tech. would have a hard time identifying the problem, because he could not spend the amount of time necessary to get the excessive reading.  The mfr's rep. offered the consumer a discount of the purchase of a new range.  The consumer declined that offer due to concerns of the same thing occurring with another range/oven made by this mfr.

8/29/2015:  The consumer also decided to test the upper oven, because he was only using the lower oven in the previous instances above.  The consumer's tester can measure Max CO levels manually, when it's less than 30 ppms.  The consumer found that when the upper oven is in use, it emitted a Max CO level of 18 ppm.  The consumer discontinued use of the lower oven.  He also sent his test results to their service tech. and to Whirlpool.   The mfr. provided the consumer with a Reference Number:  [REDACTED], that is related to this issue.

9/7/2015:  The consumer received a response back from the service tech., who advised him to discontinue use of the lower oven and indicated that the would contact the mfr. for a further response.  However, the consumer has never received any further responses from the mfr.

The consumer also followed up with the service tech. a few more times, but he did not get any further replies from him.

The consumer is concerned about the excessive levels of CO associated with this oven and the fact that the mfr's  has not been able to correct the problem.

THERE IS ALSO A CONCERN THAT WITHOUT A CO DETECTOR A CONSUMER WOULD HAVE NO KNOWLEDGE THAT A HAZARDOUS OR DEADLY CONSITION EXISTS
justification: The incident involved excessive CO emissions confirmed by multiple tests and authorities, posing a clear risk of injury or death if undetected, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer was cooking with the front left range burner and it switched to a high heat setting during use.  The consumer said that the burner may have been in use for 10 minutes or less on a very low setting, but the contents began to boil.  She could not turn the burner off with the use of the control knob.  She tripped the breaker and left the power off for approx. 30 - 40 minutes.  When she turned the breaker back on, that same burner switched to the high heat setting and could not be turned off.  The consumer had to trip the breaker again in order to turn off the burner.

The consumer said that her problem was similar to the one in Recall CAP# 09-333, but her model number was not included.


NOTE:  Approximately 1 - 2 years ago, the right front range heating element quit working properly.  The center portion of the rings for that burner quit working, but the 2 outer rings continued working.  The consumer assumed that this was due to the age of the range and she discontinued use of that burner.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that could not be turned off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We accidentally came into the kitchen to find that our GE GLD6700N00WW s/n FM930165B dishwasher had visible smoke and soot coming from the latch and front panel vent area while operating a normal cycle.  The main breaker did not trip and there was nothing damaged in the tub.
justification: Visible smoke and soot indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: The oven racks, over time, have begun to fall off their guides.  I tried replacing the racks (thinking they had warped or shortened, for some reason) and the correct oven rack for the model also falls off the guides.  The only possible reason is the oven liner itself has expanded.
justification: The incident involves oven racks falling off their guides, which is a malfunction but has not caused injury or death.

incident_description:
I was making a grilled cheese sandwich using a Tools of the Trade 8 inch frying pan.
I had butter in the pan over a medium heat on a burner of my gas stove.
I had cooked one side and I turned the sandwich over to the other side.  A minute or two after turning it over there suddenly was some smoke and then a loud bang and something went flying by me and hit the floor a number of feet away. I found out that one of the round metal covers on one of the screws attaching the handle to the pan had exploded off the pan.  I'm very lucky that it didn't hit me.

These pans should not be sold and the manufacturer should be notified.

(I'm reporting this late because I sent this same information to Macy's  (where I bought the pan) to a California address (that I thought was their head location), but my letter was returned unopened as a bad address.)
justification: The incident involved a pan handle cover exploding off, but no injury occurred, making it a severity level 2. Such incidents are unlikely (level 2) as they are not commonly reported.

incident_description:
(10/20/2015)The consumer stated that she ran the dishwasher through the entire wash cycle. About a couple of hours after the cycle finished, the consumer touched the door of the dishwasher, which was very hot. When she opened the door, steam came pouring out. The bottom of the silverware tray had melted and all of the silverware was laying in the bottom of the dishwasher. Also the granite counter top above the dishwasher was so hot that a loaf of bread, that was on the counter, had condensation inside of the bag. The wheels on the bottom tray of the dishwasher had also melted. 

The consumer had a hard time turning the unit off. The unit stopped after a while.

(10/25/2015) The consumer opened and closed the door to the unit to show her son what had happened. When she closed the door, the unit came on by itself. The unit would not turn off. The consumer had to disconnect the unit at the outlet.
justification: The incident involved property damage and a malfunctioning dishwasher, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Gas leak.  Knobs turn with ease allowing gas flow with no flame causing risk of carbon monoxide poisoning.  Additionally, flames go out causing gas leakage and risk of carbon monoxide poisoning.
justification: Gas leak and flame failure pose a clear risk of carbon monoxide poisoning, which can lead to injury or death.

incident_description:
09/23/2015 - The consumer was toasting a piece of bread on the skillet. Approximately three minutes after she turned the stove on, she heard a loud bang and also felt pain on her jaw. A part of one of the caps that covers the rivets on the skillet's handle shot off and this is what hit the consumer in her jaw. The consumer indicates that the diameter of the cap is about half inch. The consumer stated she thought she had been shot.

The injury did not bleed a lot as the piece that blew off cut but also cauterized the wound since the skillet was burning. The consumer iced the wound. She indicates that it inflamed to about the size of an egg. The consumer believes she will have a permanent scar on her face because of the accident.

09/24/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained what had happened. The representative she spoke informed the consumer they would file a report and send it to the correct department and that she would receive a call from them.

09/25/2015 - The consumer received a call back from the manufacturer. The representative she spoke to apologized for the inconvenience and asked that she send the skillet back to them, as well as she go online and choose what product she wanted to receive. The consumer told the representative she would not send the skillet back nor get any of their products as she did not feel safe with them.

The consumer has no injuries or previous incidents to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (a cut and potential permanent scar) from a skillet part breaking off, but such occurrences are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that the left and front burner turns on by itself when another, sometimes when a different burner was done so intentionally. The consumer states that the burner will turn sometimes even heat at temperatures it was not set to.

The consumer indicates that several times he was unable to turn off the burner and so he had to switch off the circuit breaker in order for it to turn off.

10/09/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer about the issue for the first time and explained the problems he has been having with the range. The representative he spoke to informed him that his unit is not included in any recalls and that because his unit is no longer under warranty that he would have to pay for any inspection and repair out of pocket.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident involves burners turning on by themselves and difficulty turning them off, posing a safety hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her gas range purchased from retailer in Massachusetts around February 23rd, 2015.
On October 21, 2015 she heard what sounded like a crash or window breaking, she went toward the sound and saw that the outer glass of the oven door had shattered and sent tiny pieces of glass over a two foot area in her kitchen.
The consumer is reporting this incident as a safety hazard due to the potential for eye injury and lacerations.
There were no injuries with this incident.
She contacted the manufacturer October 21st, 2015 and was advised that they would provide 20% off of cost and waive the shipping fee which resulted in a cost of $79.16 for the glass then she must also pay for the repair tech to install the new glass.
She is asking is she can obtain reimbursement for the cost of this repair.

The submitter stated that there were no physical injuries, but physcological [psychology] injuries. The submitter stated she had a fear it will happen again - i.e., how safe is this oven?
justification: The incident involved shattered oven glass but no physical injuries, though psychological fear was reported. The likelihood is considered possible due to the nature of the defect.

incident_description: Frigidaire cook stove Mod. # GLEFZ369FCB,  Front burner is coming on high and staying on even the dial control is turned to the off position. This burner does not regulate heat to the setting on dial.  This range was purchased in 2009, with the first repair also in 2009 for burner problem not regulating heat properly. The burner problem has occured on a few occasions last one being 11/16/15.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a safety hazard but no injury is reported, and the issue has recurred multiple times.

incident_description: I wanted to clean my oven.  So I turned on the self clean feature today 11/17/2015 around 10am.  My husband and I read the directions and took out the racks and pressed to self clean button.  About 30 minutes later we heard a "boom" and what sounded like pebbles dropping.  We looked around and found that glass was spilling out of the oven.  My husband turned The oven off so that it would stop heating.  Thank God we were home to turn off the oven or it would have started a fire.  In addition we were fortunate that none of my children nor animals were around the oven when it exploded and the glass shattered.  We took pictures and when the Oven cooled off enough my husband was able to determine that it was the middle pane of glass that had shattered.  It is continuing to drop glass.  I called Thermador and had to call back 5 times (due to being disconnected and cross connected) to get service.  I finally have an appt on dec 3... After thanksgiving for the service guy.  I bought the Thermador convection oven ME301JS on 7/8/14 and it was delivered and installed 9/10/14. It is still under warranty and I have all receipts.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no injuries or fire occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I was using a Pyrex brand glass baking dish to roast a chicken. The chicken was on a metal roasting rack. The oven was set to 400 degrees Farenheit. I left the room while the chicken was cooking. After about 20 minutes, I heard a loud sound of glass breaking, and opened the oven to find the Pyrex dish had shattered. There were small glass pieces all over the oven.

Per Consumer Reports (http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/magazine-archive/2011/january/home-garden/glass-cookware/glass-cookware/index.htm), apparently this is something that has happened to others. I had no idea this could happen. Fortunately no one was hurt, but it could have caused serious injury.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass dish but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the reference to similar incidents reported by Consumer Reports.

incident_description:
09/15/2015 (Approximate) - The consumer indicates that as soon as he puts water in the unit, it leaks water at the base of the handle approximately where the electricity runs through.

09/22/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the situation he had been having with their unit. The representative he spoke to informed the consumer that although the unit is under warranty, they would have to inspect it to make sure he did not cause intentional damage to it. If they found the consumer to not be at fault, they informed him they would replace the unit.

The consumer searched online and indicates that many people are having the same issue. The consumer has since returned the unit to the manufacturer.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident involves a leaking unit with no reported injuries, and multiple consumers report the same issue, indicating it is likely to occur.

incident_description: We bought a home recently that has a wall oven (dual) by GE. The oven exterior gets extremely hot when the oven is used and the control panel is peeling off. The model number is JTP35S0M1SS. Though GE has recalled some ovens, this model number has not been recalled, though I see a similar problem in my model too.
justification: The oven's exterior getting extremely hot and the control panel peeling off are incidents that could pose a risk, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: blade fell out of blender and almost cut my finger off, had to go to emergency room for 11 stitches
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring emergency room treatment and stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with improper blender use.

incident_description:
LG Microwave oven door exploded and cut my husband.
Husband was heating up a brat/sausage in microwave.  Did not heat all the way first time so put back in.  When he took out the (microwave safe) glass plate, it was a little warm and was holding the plate with his hands and closed the microwave with the back of his hand/arm.  When he closed it, he heard a high pitched squeal, the microwave door blew up and out at him, sending glass into his hand and clear across our kitchen.
Contacted LG..Disgusted with how this is being handled.  The first time I called (weekend), I was told the department I needed to speak with was not open today and could I call back tomorrow (Monday).  Should they not be contacting me back?!?!  Poor customer service.  Upon finally (after calling back and having to go through 5 minutes of questioning again) getting ahold of the "Supervisory Department" I was told that the item has passed the warranty unless I have purchased the extended warranty.  To which I explained I had not but, that still doesn't mean its ok for a microwave door to BLOW UP just because it's more than a year old!  So, I was told I would have to pay out of my pocket for diagnostic testing and IF it could be proved that it was manufacturer defect and I had the purchase receipt then they would see what they could do for me.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (glass cuts) from the microwave door exploding, but such events are unlikely based on typical microwave usage.

incident_description:
Item:  Kitchenaid Wall Oven
Model:  KEMS308SSS00
Serial #: XU4108505

Oven bought and installed in October 2007 from Sears as part of total kitchen appliance upgrade.

On 15 November 2015, while using the oven self-clean utility for only the second time since install, the inner glass panel shattered.  Glass was shot out the bottom of the oven door, reaching as much as 10 feet distance from the oven.  Glass was hot enough to scorch baseboards (flooring is ceramic tile).

The glass panel was never subjected to any abuse and was kept clean usually by wiping with a damp dishcloth while the oven was at room temperature.  Never used chemicals to clean.

No one was near the oven when the glass shattered, else there would have been very painful burn injuries, and cuts from flying glass.

To remove all glass particles, oven will have to be dismounted and disassemble to ensure all glass dust is removed from the convection fan system.

Unsure what KitchenAid will do to remedy.  Hopefully, it's not unreasonable to expect an expensive (~$3200.00) appliance to function as promised?
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering and causing property damage, but no injuries occurred as no one was nearby.

incident_description: Fire crews responded to a residential structure fire at a single family dwelling. the fire originates in the control panel of an under-the-counter dishwasher. The female occupant was transported to a nearby hospital for minor burns and smoke inhalation.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns and smoke inhalation requiring hospital transport, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My dishwasher was 2/3 full of dirty dishes and was NOT running.  I was gone about 2 hours.  Came home to a house filled with acrid vile smell and haze.  Found granite on top of dishwasher very hot to touch.  Opened door and it was hotter than opening an oven.  Hot smoke came out.  We turned off breaker.  Inside had several melted components.  A few items in it were damaged.  Tub is stainless.  I believe it was a huge safety issue and likely could have had a fire it I had been gone longer.  3 hours later when I was going to bed the granite was still hot to touch over the dishwasher.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and caused damage to components and items inside, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I had just used my Ninja BL660 to blend up frozen fruit to make a smoothie.  After I had finished blending the fruits, I took off the lid to pour the smoothie into my glass, but as I poured the drink the metal blades fell out of the blender and lacerated my thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, which is an injury, but such occurrences are unlikely given proper blender use and maintenance.

incident_description:
I had a 9-inch x 13-inch Pyrex baking dish sitting on my stovetop. I accidentally turned on the burner underneath it (I meant to turn on another burner to heat water for tea). Several minutes later, the dish exploded. It sounded like a violent explosion. I did not initially know what had exploded, but I saw glass all over the countertop, stovetop, and floor within a 3-foot radius. Some pieces of glass traveled as far as eight feed from the source. I left the room to put on shoes so that I could clean up the mess. When I returned and was assessing the damage, I noticed that the burner was on, so I turned it off. I rested my hand on a dish towel that was hanging over the oven handle, and I touched a piece of hot glass that was on the towel. I then proceeded to clean up the glass, and later I entered the room barefoot and got a glass splinter in my foot. I suspect I will be finding chunks and shards of glass for some time.

Actual injury: 1st degree burn to palmar surface of hand; glass splinters in hands and feet from cleanup.
Potential injury: Hot glass flew through the air up to eight feet from the source; I'm lucky nobody was standing closer
Actual property damage: hot glass that landed on the floor melted the linoleum flooring and left stains
justification: The incident resulted in a 1st degree burn and glass splinters, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as accidental burner activation and glass explosion can occur but are not everyday events.

incident_description: The water shot out and burnt me. Also, the bottom leaks no matter how much water I put in. I would like a refund or upgrade please.
justification: The description mentions being burnt by the water, indicating an injury, and the leak suggests a recurring issue.

incident_description: After baking at 325 degrees for 35 minutes, smoke started pouring from the oven and visible sparks were observed from the top back of the display area of the stove.  After removing the food from the oven that heavily burned on the top, we discovered that the broiler element had turned on during the baking process and was stuck on.  We are still not certain what caused the sparks.  Had we not been in the room to stop it, a fire certainly would have started.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks from the oven, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Hello, I used my blendtec blender, then was cleaning the counter that it was sitting on. I cleaned with a sponge and went close to the right side and where or is comes up on the sides I felt pain and had a bad strach that was bleeding. Upon investigation I see that there are extremely sharp points on all the plastic corners. I then cut my hand a second time while cleaning. I believe they change the design but should check the points of the base and round them.
justification: The description mentions two instances of cuts causing bleeding, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I was boiling water in a Revere Ware 16 qt stock pot (with 87-a on the bottom).  I grabbed both handles and picked it up to move to pot.  As I did, one handle broke and dumped boiling water onto my ankle and foot.  I went to the St. Elizabeth Hospital-Edgweood KY emergency room for treatment.  The burns on my right foot and right ankle were classified as 2nd degree.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I have two K10 Mini Plus Personal Brewer's which have stopped working and I learned that both of their serial numbers are under recall. 
S/N: 31.2019.0032312 stopped brewing water, leaks hot water from bottom, and will not shut off.
S/N: 31.0004.0259351 stopped brewing water, leaks hot water from bottom, does not turn on.
Both units inoperable.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning equipment under recall, posing a risk of leaks and operational failure but no reported injury.

incident_description: Sears Range Model # 79097473803 Self-Cleaning Oven with optional delay.  Turned on Self-Cleaning function resulting in fire and sparks from back of oven.  Opened up back of oven to find Oven Control Module and harness wiring completely charred.  Should the optional delay function have been activated and no individual is around to smell burning plastic, I am convinced that oven cabinetry and kitchen could have caught fire.  This oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with potential for significant property damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was reheating some zucchini in a ceramic dish (back of dish did not mention anything about use in a microwave), a dish I've used for 5 years in this microwave without incident.  I covered the dish with a paper towel. Shortly after starting the microwave, within a few seconds, I smelled something burning and looked inside to see the paper towel was on fire and getting out of control. I quickly grabbed the dish with towel on fire and threw it in the sink dousing it with water.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly controlled without injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
While using my Cuisinart DLC-2009 s/n 30918  food processor  I heard something didn't sound right.
Upon closer inspection I found a part of the blade in the food, I also see fractures or cracks around the rivets. Broken part was small and very sharp could have been swallowed.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade in the food processor, which could have caused injury but did not, indicating a potential hazard without actual harm.

incident_description:
Discovered this week that our Kenmore Stove/Oven Ceramic top element will not turn off. The only way we could get it to turn off was to unplug from the wall. I am on SSDI and require a special diet so I need to have a stove that actually functions correctly. The only way around this problem is to plug it in and unplug it after each use, requiring moving it in and out of the space and unsure if it is even safe and could potentially cause a fire. Discovered last night when we were going to bed and discovered the stove top element was still red hot in spite of it being turned off hours ago. Help!  Suggestions Please! 

I live in a condominium/townhome and have seven families living in our building so I cannot risk using this appliance. I was told there was no fix for this and to report it to the government.
justification: The stove's inability to turn off poses a fire hazard, especially in a multi-family building, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The dishwasher racks burned (melted, blackened & partially disintegrated) in the front and along the bottom of the tub.  
Because a nearly identical model number was recalled for starting fires, I am concerned that this particular number was simply missed by evaluators and should have been included in that recall.  Mine is Maytag model MDB7600AWB, serial # 22414904EE. The recalled dishwasher was also MDB7; however, my serial number wasn't listed and should have been (in my opinion). http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2007/Maytag-Recalls-Dishwashers-Due-to-Fire-Hazard/
justification: The dishwasher racks burned, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the runner and the screws that hold the shelves onto the freezer wall pop out causing the shelves to fall.

The consumer stated that the two bottom shelves are the ones that she has had problems with falling out.


The consumer contacted Sears about the issue. 

The consumer stated that a technician came out three times. The first two times they were unable to repair the unit. The third time, the technician (around June/July) moved the shelves higher and used a heavier screw. 

The consumer stated that in Oct 2015 the shelves came out again.

The technician informed the consumer that the wall is too thin and is backed by styrofoam that cannot hold the screws.

The consumer stated that her 14 months old granddaughter is currently living with her. She is afraid that the shelves will fall on her and injure her if she opens the door by mistake.

The consumer stated that the unit is not manufactured and designed properly.
justification: The incident involves repeated shelf failures with potential to injure a child, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence and moderate severity due to risk of injury.

incident_description:
On 10/9/15 the consumer walked in the kitchen and noticed the oven was "On". The consumer states the knob was in the "off" position. The consumer notified the security of the apartment building and he notified a maintenance employee who turned the circuit breaker off. 

On 10/12/15 the consumer contacted the firm (800-432-2737) and the rep referred her to the Consumer Relations department. The consumer called the Consumer Relations department (800-386-1215) and informed them of the incident (case # 13724471). The consumer provided the rep (name unknown) with the model and serial number. The consumer was told that [REDACTED] was the case manager assigned to her case and [REDACTED] would call her on 10/14/15. The rep also told the consumer that a technician would repair her range on 10/16/15. [REDACTED] called the consumer on 10/14/15 and informed her that a technician is not available and she would call the consumer on 10/16/15 to arrange a date for the repair.

The consumer believes her range poses a fire hazard. 

The repair guy came on 10/17/20 and when he turned the circuit breaker back on, the oven broiler lit back up and could not be turned off without turning the circuit breaker off.  He then took off a back panel and saw a burnt spot & said the consumer needed a new part.  He unplugged the range & told the consumer to leave it unplugged.  In looking thru the oven mauel, the consumer saw that it was an automatic oven - meaning, it can be set to turn on & off at certain times.  The consumer thinks that part got messed up.  On, 10/26/2015, the part arrived.  The repair guy is scheduled tomorrow.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a frigidaire oven model number DGEF3051KFH I performed a self clean on it. After the self clean the oven quick working. Upon opening the back we noticed that it had burnt up one of the wire attached to the circuit board. We repaired that. Then in a couple weeks we had a fire start in the back of the oven. We were told the circuit board was smoke checked. This occurred because doing the self clean burnt up the sensor and it was allowing the oven to get too hot. We then had to replace the circuit board and the sensor. Not cheap parts. Looking online this looks like a very common problem with frigidaire and has many recalls however not for our model number. I want to make sure this is made aware as well as I'd like to talk to someone and insure that these repairs will fully fix the issue so we have no more fires. Thank you
justification: The incident involved a fire starting in the oven, which poses a risk of injury, and the problem appears to be common based on the description.

incident_description: On November 13th our GE Profile Dishwasher caught fire at 2:00 i the morning, fire department called, responded, no actual flames but smoke throughout house.  The circuit panel had not tripped, so cut power and removed to our garage today.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but there were no injuries or deaths, only smoke damage.

incident_description: slid out and cut hand
justification: The description mentions a cut hand, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I used the blender to make a smoothie. While I was rinsing and cleaning up afterward, the blade fell out as I was pouring the excess water out into the sink. My finger was cut in the process. The blade is very sharp and cut clean & deep requiring a trip to the ER and 5 stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut requiring ER visit and stitches, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Laceration to the finger as a result of the blade
justification: The description mentions a laceration, which is an injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: I have been cut several times by the blades of the Ninja Blender BL660.
justification: The description indicates multiple cuts from the blender blades, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Ninja Professional Blender BL660
I had a deep cut to my finger from the blade of the blender as I was carefully washing it. I had reported this to Ninja and all they said was to be more careful. I requested for a refund and take the item back (although purchased from Amazon) but they said that they cannot do that because it was not purchased from them directly. Amazon too rejected the return since it had passed their return policy. I purchased this blender last September and found after that it was too dangerous that I wanted to return it. Sadly, both manufacturer and seller refused to take the return. THE BLADES ARE INCREDIBLY SHARP AND EVEN THOUGH YOU HANDLE WITH EXTREME CARE, YOU CAN STILL GET LACERATIONS! Please help!
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut to the finger, indicating an injury, and the description suggests that such injuries are likely given the sharpness of the blades.

It healed ok but now I have a nasty scar. incident_description: I received the Ninja Mega Kitchen system blender as a Christmas gift in December 2013. As I unpacked the box and tried to take the 64 oz blender out of the box, I couldn't get it to release from the styrofoam.  I pulled up on the handle not knowing that it was a locking mechanism. As I pulled the blender from the box, the top pulled off and the bottom of the blender fell away while the chopping blade fell out.  The chopping blade lacerated the back of my leg, severing my sural nerve.  My leg was operated on and an attempt to reconnect the sural nerve was attempted.  Unfortunately, I deal with the pain daily from the injury almost two years later.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring surgery and causing ongoing pain, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is low as such injuries from unpacking a blender are rare.

incident_description:
We purchased four sets of the "Highball Glass" by Artland from Wayfair.com.  When we received the glasses (four different colors) we noticed that the "bubbles" in the glass were on the inside of the glass.  The first thought was that this would make them harder to clean, but an even worse concern has arisen.  We noticed a spot in one of our glasses where drink mix deposits simply would not come clean.  At closer inspection, we saw that the glass covering one of the bubbles had broken off leaving an opening into the "bubble."  When we noticed this, our main concern was "What happened to the piece of glass that broke off?"

We have immediately stopped using these glasses as the danger is either:  1:  When stirring in drink mixes, the spoon will break glass from over the bubbles and you will drink the broken glass.  And: 2:  The opening caused when the glass breaks is impossible to get clean and is a breeding ground for disease.

The glass that had this happen is: the Amber colored glass (SKU #: AAN1198) and we also bought these glasses (four each) in:  Light Blue; Light Green; and Plum
justification: The incident involves a potential hazard from broken glass and unsanitary conditions, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The caller received a case of a 10 days old baby that suffered from severe abdominal pain issues from extreme gas. 

The caller stated that the mother used the Baby Breeza Formula Maker to mix formula powder with water. 

The caller reported two issues with the machine.

1) The caller stated that there are areas that have turned black and red (mold and possibly bacteria). The caller stated that this was seen in various parts of the machine. The caller stated that the baby formula gets contaminated causing severe heath hazards to a baby. The caller has not ran any culture tests to check exactly what the growth is.

2) The caller stated that steam condensates and goes into the formula causing the powder to clump. The caller stated that this dilutes the formula since the proper amount of powder is not measured. This caused the baby to not receive proper amount of food supply. The caller stated that the incorrect dosing of the formula to a baby can cause drop in sodium levels (causing possibility of seizure along with other health concerns like low blood sugar, inability to gain weight, etc).

The caller received photos from the mother of the product disassembled. The caller saw patches of red and black colored growth. 

The caller advised the mother to not use this product. 

The caller stated that the mother contacted the company to inform them of this issue. The mother was informed to clean the machine after every 4th bottle. The mother was informed that if she followed the instructions, the issues should not occur. 

The caller stated that the company is asking the users to clean the machine every 4th bottle which can be generally every day or twice a day. The caller stated that since parents are using this product to save time, they may not clean it as often.

The caller looked up product reviews online and noticed other health professionals who commented on similar heath hazards with the product.
justification: The incident involves a baby suffering from severe health issues due to contaminated formula and incorrect dosing, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) given the reported issues and similar online reviews.

incident_description:
This caller purchased her blender system around the end of June/beginning of July 2014 time frame.
She used it with no problems until August 29th, 2014 when she was blending a shake mixture of fruits, vegetables and water when after less than four minutes it suddenly blew up.
The explosion of the blender system left the caller with burns on her forehead, face and neck.
Her forehead and the side of left cheek bubbled up from the heat.
She went to her physician also on August 29th, 2014 who diagnosed her with 3rd degree burns of her face, forehead and neck.
She was referred to a dermatologist and then plastic surgeon.
She was seen by dermatologist around October 13th/14th, 2014 and was advised that the burns were most likely 2nd degree from what she was looking at 6 weeks after the incident.
She was worried about the scarring of the front center of her neck.
The caller's primary doctor advised her that she would need to be seen by a plastic surgeon to treat the scarring on the front of her neck then provided the caller with a referral.
The caller stated that she thanked God that she was wearing her glasses because she is already blind in her right eye and the explosion if she hadn't been wearing her glasses could have worsened damage to her eyes.

She contacted the manufacturer in June/July 2014 but was advised that they would replace their part but that she should only have had the unit running for two minutes but she ran it for almost four minutes.

Incident occurred:  in the kitchen
justification: The caller suffered 3rd degree burns requiring medical treatment, indicating a significant injury. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common with blender use.

incident_description:

stove was being used but was turned off before the problem oven was at 400

incident_description:
(02/2015) The consumer state that her mother smelled gas in the home, The fire department was called but could not locate where the smell was coming from. The consumer stated that her mother was feeling groggy . The consumer stated that her sister took her mother to the hospital just to make sure that she was alright. The consumer refused to pay for service since the incident did not occur at their fault. After speaking with various people the consumer was referred Sedgwick Claims. The consumer spoke to their representative, [REDACTED], and explained the situation. The consumer was provided a claim # and advised to call Sears back with the claim #. The consumer was to contact Sears and inform that this is a diagnostic service call at no charge.

The consumer contacted Sears and a technician, [REDACTED], came on 11/2/15 for an inspection. The technician came with a regular service order and asked the consumer to pay. incident_description: Our Breville Lift and Look Toaster self activate in the cabinet and caught fire.  We kept the unit in our appliance garage in the corner of our kitchen.  Monday morning my wife got out of bed and poured a cup of coffee.  A few minute later the house filled with significant smoke and the smell of wire was strong through the house.  The Battlefield Missouri Fire Department responded to help track down the source but never found anything so they told us to get our furnace checked out.  The fire had apparently went out where ever it was and the smoke in the house started to clear.   We called a local HVAC company who gave our furnace a clean bill of health ($73.00 charge).  About 5 pm my wife called me to tell me the furnace test out fine.  I told her to check every outlet in the house and check every device plugged into to those outlet as whatever had caused the problem may have just burned up.  When she got to the appliance garage the door would not roll up, but as soon as she attempted to roll it up smoke started to pour out and the fire started once again.  She determined the toaster had apparently activated itself.  We had to break into the cabinet as the plastic channel the roll up door used had melted closed.  When we finally go into the cabinet we found a box of coffee creamer had fallen over an was laying on the switch which apparently started the toaster.  The toaster is a total loss and the inside of the cabinet us burned up.  I had an incident once before when I accident touched the toaster getting something out of the appliance garage it activated itself but I was able to catch it.  This is a great toaster but it is no a safe design.   My wife does have photos of the toaster on her phone.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by the toaster self-activating, resulting in property damage but no injuries.

If they are on you can't turn them off and if they are off you can't turn them on. It's been this way since we purchased it. Once the burner was on low and a breeze blew it out and I had to run to the basement to turn the gas valve off to the range. Luckity we were close and smelled the gas.

We put up with it for too long and finally got fed up enough to file the complaint. We've talked to Whirlpool on numerous occasions.

My electric Frigidaire range caught fire Sunday, October 18,  2015. I turned on the oven to preheat it before I cooked and all of a sudden I heard some type of explosion come from downstairs. I got downstairs and saw smoke coming out of the kitchen. I thought my kitchen was on fire. I walked in the kitchen and saw flames coming out of the oven. I turned it off and the flames went out. all of the smoke detectors in the house alarmed.  I then called the fire dept and they disconnected the stove from the wall. The heating element is destroyed the fire caused it.  So, I have been without a stove for a few weeks.
This morning I called the local appliance part store and described the incident. The lady said, " oh, they do that all the time." then she gave me the price of the heating element, which was too expensive and I said thanks.
Model# EFE326FBB, Serial # VF62638121
Part # 316075104
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant damage to the oven, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The appliance store's comment suggests such incidents are common.

incident_description: I bought this range and when the heating element went I called my home warrantee company who called Sears to fix it but the technician couldn't fix because there were holes in the upper left panel of the oven. I thought it was made of metal but no. It looks like it is made of plastic. This oven received just average use, no neglect, or deliberate damage. The panel melted and now I can't have it fixed because it is a non replaceable part and non covered item and on top of that no one will fix the heating element because the panel is unsafe so I am screwed. This kind of shoddy product is uncalled for and we need to stop letting companies get away with this.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven with a melted panel, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
In the early hours of the morning Saturday November 7th 2015 we were woken by a beeping/alarm.  We investigated and there was smoke filled in our kitchen coming from the stove.  There was an error code (maybe F30, can't quite remember) and the two right hand burners showed that they were hot.  There was a smell of burning plastic and smoke so we turned off the breaker to the stove and secured everything until morning.

My husband took off the front control panel in the morning to see what was going on and if it looked like it was going to be repairable and saw that the control board 316441801 was burnt and had damaged the one next to it and melted the plastic on the range control panel.  We were so lucky there was some kind of beeper/alarm that awoke us in the middle of the night and there was not more damage to our house or us.  It appeared that the cost of buying new parts was going to be higher than we wanted to pay.  Today we went out and spent over $1500 on a new stove.  It was only afterwards when friends asked what could have caused it that they suggested checking to see if there was a recall.  We found that our model had indeed been recalled.

It was a Frigidaire Professional model PLES389ECE and serial number NF62218063.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burnt control board, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: This incident pertains to our Kenmore Elite model 790.48173000 double wall ovens, date of manufacture December 2010. During the Flex Clean cycle, the middle sheet of safety glass in the door of the lower oven shattered. I heard it go though I did not realize it was the door glass shattering until the oven had cycled off and fully cooled and I opened the door to wipe down the interior. The affected door's interior and exterior glass is still intact and the middle sheet, though thoroughly shattered, is, for the most part, still in place. The lower oven is very rarely used. In preparation for the upcoming holidays, the upper oven had been Flex Cleaned without incident the day before. The lower oven itself had been cleaned at least once previously without a problem. Given the other reports I've read regarding Kenmore oven glass doors literally exploding, our incident was relatively minor: still very, very unsettling , though.
justification: The incident involved shattered safety glass but no injury, and the oven is very rarely used, indicating a low likelihood of recurrence.

She went to the kitchen but felt heat coming from her dishwasher, the counters and all surrounding area.  She touched the control button that read heated/dry and the dishwasher began shutting down.

After the unit cooled down which took a couple of hours she looked to see if there was any scorching but there was none.

The caller has disposed of the unit and purchased a new dishwasher July 2nd, 2015.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid Dishwasher model number kuds301Xwh1. Last night my son opened the dishwasher and pulled out the fully loaded top rack. It, and all the glassware loaded in it, collapsed out of the dishwasher. Fortunately, my son, who is 17, was strong enough to catch the rack. A wine glass and a bowl shattered.

Upon closer inspection, the roller assembly of the upper rack failed. The plastic axels that the rollers attach to have deteriorated over time. A quick internet search shows that this is a common occurence. And for us, this is the second time these pieces have failed. The first was just a few years ago.

A consumer should not have to worry that the top rack's attachment mechanisms might randomly fail, sending several pounds of glassware onto the consumer and the floor. There is clearly a major design/manufacturing fault in this product that is putting consumers at a major risk simply through use of a product as designed and intended.

We only ever use the "normal" function on the dishwasher, so the plastic, by definition, is subjected to "normal" heat and water conditions. I have most of the failed parts.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher rack failure causing glassware to shatter, but no injuries occurred as the son caught the rack. The failure is described as a common occurrence with this model.

incident_description:
On 10/04/15 I bought a Fridgidaire Pro gas range from Lowe's. It was delivered on the 7th. It's Model FPGH3077RFA, Serial # AF53503772. The price was $2400.

The range has a storage drawer at the bottom. The description clearly stated that it was a storage drawer, and not a warming drawer or broiler. Just as I always had with my previous range, I put oversized  cookie sheets and baking pans and my plastic proofing box (folded) inside the drawer. 

After the first time I used the oven, I noticed a 2x4 x 1" deep hole had been melted into the lid of my proofing box. I was upset, but figured the drawer might be getting overly warm, so I removed the proofing box and left only metal pans in the drawer.

On October 24, my 27-year-old son decided to bake a frozen pizza. He set the oven on preheat, and five minutes later reached into the drawer to get a metal pizza pan. When he grabbed the pan, it was so blisteringly hot that it raised a welt on his right hand, in the web between his thumb and forefinger. I checked, and every pan in the drawer was way too hot to touch.

I contacted Frigidaire, and had an online dialogue with them over several days, but got nowhere. They "investigated" my complaint inhouse, and concluded the problem occurred because I was storing items inside the oven, which the manual prohibits. But I wouldn't do that--this happened in the storage drawer, which the customer service person admitted IS a designated storage drawer! 

I told them the hole melted into the bread proofer was rectangular with rounded corners, and they said that it might correspond to a  vent that cools down the oven. If so, it shouldn't be transferring such extreme heat to the storage drawer. I asked them to send someone out to check the range in person, but so far have got no reply.

At this point, I'm afraid to store anything in the storage drawer. I worry about eventually using the oven's self-clean feature. The storage drawer is neither insulated nor fully enclosed, and when temperatures in the oven reach 600 degrees, I fear it could be a fire hazard. 

I suspect this range might have the subject of Consumer Product Safety scrutiny in the past. When it was delivered, the delivery man handed me a plastic bag containing an "anti-tip" bracket. It requires the purchaser to drill holes through their floor and underlying concrete to secure the range with 2" bolts. It warns that "A child or adult can tip the range and be killed" if this is not done. I have never seen anything like this on a free-standing range.

The burn on my son's hand has now healed. But I'm wary about using this range as intended, and feel it may have the potential to cause much greater harm.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the son's hand, which has since healed, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is assessed as possible (3) given the described conditions and the potential for similar incidents if the issue is not addressed.

Purchased a Oster Food Processor model #FPSTFP5273-DFL from Walmart.com.  I was attempting to shred an 8oz block of mozzarella cheese.  I was pushing the cheese in the chute as directed.  A large piece of cheese went up under the lid, broke off a piece of the plastic lid which shot out at me.  

I contacted the company, they are sending a new one.  I am scared the new one will do the same thing.  I think it is a manufacturers defect.
justification: The incident involved a broken piece of the food processor lid shooting out, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I baked a quiche in a Pyrex pie pan that I've owned for several years. When I removed the pan from the oven and set it on the counter, the pie pan made a loud pop sound and "exploded", sending glass chunks and shards throughout the vicinity of the counter, ruining my quiche and making quite a mess. Fortunately, there were no injuries, but there could have been if the pan exploded while I was carrying it, or if small children or pets were around when the incident happened.

There was no drastic temperature change, nor did I use the pie pan in an unusual manner. I did not notice any cracks or chips in the pie pan when I began baking.
justification: The incident involved an exploding pie pan causing a mess but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such events are not common but can occur with aged cookware.

incident_description: Cuisinart coffee maker model DCC-1200 had been on for about 2 hours keeping warm when I hear a boiling sound coming from the kitchen. I went in to the kitchen to  find the coffee was boiling. The led light was off but the warming plate was very hot. I removed the craft and the warming plate was smoking and had a burning plastic smell. I unplugged the unit and cared it out side while it was still smoking.  I wonder if I was not home to unplug it would it have created a fire?
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that was smoking and emitting a burning smell, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I put water into the coffeemaker reservoir and turned it on to brew. After a couple of minutes, I smelled burning and the coffeemaker had smoke coming from the back of it. After unplugging it, I realized the bottom of the coffee maker had a melted  hole in  it, exposing the electrical parts . The coffee maker at that time had also started a burn hole in my counter top. The coffee maker hot plate detached from the bottom frame of the coffeemaker where you place the pot. The plastic is melted around where the hotplate connects to the bottom frame in addition to the hole on the bottom. I have contacted Mr. Coffee through e-mail. This was brand new purchased  at Walmart.  Please advise on this matter. I can e-mail photos and send product if Mr. Coffee reimburses for shipping. It was only twenty dollars but this could have been a fire situation. Thank-you. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffeemaker causing smoke and melting, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it was a brand new product with a defect.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire Gas Range Model #LGGF3032KMB from Lowe's back in 2009. A few weeks ago I noticed that anything cooked in the oven either cooked too quick or did not cook enough. I started to keep track of the oven temperature when I used the oven and it was always off by anywhere from 20 to 80 degrees. Now the problem has escalated to the oven not turning off when I hit the off button. If I keep pushing the button eventually it will turn off but I am afraid that it may start itself up when I leave the house. Has anyone else with this range encountered this problem?

incident_description: Water came out of the machine and I burn my hand.
justification: The description mentions a burn injury, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Samsung produces various microwave products which contain a resistive/capacitive touch panel for control.

It has been noted by customers and review organizations, that these control panels malfunction causing erratic behavior.

We purchased model ME179KFETSR/AA "OTR" microwave oven in Dec. 2012 from retailer HHgregg, and were smart enough to purchase a 5 year warranty.

Repair for our microwave, for the same exact problem, has occurred three (3) times in the past, and has just recently failed again, prompting yet another service call- for the same exact problem.

To provide a sense of how serious and potentially dangerous this is, we have personally witnessed the following with our microwave:

- During the start of a cooking cycle, we were not being able to stop the process (wasted food and potential fire hazard);

- After preparing food and placing into oven, closing the door, the control panel is non-responsive (no danger, just malfunction)

- Being awoken in the middle of the night to hear the microwave beep, only to find it had prompted (on its own) the start of its cleaning cycle (potential fire hazard).

Samsung and the warranty company have repaired the unit each time, but after 3 years and new models (and the same complaints by owners), it would seem Samsung is either not acknowledging the issue or doesn't care.

Before injury to property or life is threatened, this needs to be reviewed.

As important, the test lab hired to test/certify as to the product's safety needs to reviewed as well.
justification: The malfunction causes erratic behavior and potential fire hazards, but no injuries or deaths have been reported yet.

incident_description: Lid from slow cooker shattered while removing from the cooker.
justification: The lid shattered but there is no mention of injury, so it's an incident without injury.

incident_description: On 10/24/2015 my Kenmore Elite Dishwasher Model 665.16582200 Serial Number FM2002942 Type 577-0 caught on fire at the circuit board.  There was smoke coming from the control panel on the right hand side.  Luckily it happened as I walked into the kitchen and was able to stop the dishwasher immediately by opening the door.   Immediately after doing so the control panel caught fire but did not catch anything else on fire because it was now partially open.  Had I not opened the dishwasher door a bit, the fire would have been able to reach the Formica countertop.   The dishwasher was purchased in 2002.  Luckily there was no damage to anything other than the dishwasher except for the awful smell of plastic and electronics burning.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but there was no injury or death, and the fire was contained without spreading.

incident_description: After flex clean (self clean) the ovens would not heat. They displayed 100 degrees F but they were not hot. I took off the back covers. There is a block of wires on the back right bottom which had burned through wires and wires with melted insulation.
justification: The incident involved damaged wires and melted insulation, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Started the self clean cycle.  2 hours into the cycle, the glass in the oven door exploded, sending small shards of glass throughout the kitchen and inside the oven. Fortunately, no one was standing directly in front of the oven.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, causing damage but no injuries as no one was nearby.

incident_description:
Sitting at home about 10pm 10/19/15, other person in house working at office desk, no one in the kitchen.  The oven had last been used on 10/16/15 at the very earliest.  We hear a pop and shattered glass in the kitchen.  Went to check on the noise and the outer glass of my oven (Frigidaire GLEFZ384GC) had basically exploded into tiny cubes of glass and long slender pieces (3" long) and shot clear across my kitchen, about 12".  Glass was everywhere in the floor and a small frame of glass that was shattered but still together was still in the door.

If I had been cooking it would have been a major problem, or if a child had been in the kitchen, a major problem!

Caller stated that the dishwasher door broke when it was opened to load dishes and almost fell on his wife's leg.  He does not know what cause the dishwasher door to break , he feels it is a safety issue and should be reported.

incident_description: My microwave stopped working.  After I entered the cook time and Start, the light would come on and the timer would count down but the heating did not work.  I called a GE repairman that came out, said the problem was one of three switches inside the microwave and the cost would be appx. $280, which I declined. When I removed the microwave from the cabinetry (newly built and installed in May 2014 as well), there was a large burnt spot on the cabinet. About a year after I bought the appliance it started beeping fluctuating between temps, top oven would never work properly.  Had techs come out to fix it he told be that I shouldn't be using both ovens at the same time, and that these appliances only last 5 years.  He said he fixed the panel but it continued to happen.  A cupel weeks ago I was making chocolate chip cookies in the top oven and bottom, the top oven became extremely hot and burned the cookies within a 1-2min time period.  On 10/19/2015 I was cooking meat loaf in top oven and brownies in lower oven.  My daughter and I were sitting in the kitchen and heard a pop, she was like that was your oven.  I said no its fine, a couple seconds after that the oven started beeping and flashed F 10 error. The top oven somehow went to broil mode and was burning the meat loaf when I went to open it.  I kept bring to turn it off but it kept on hearing to the point where the outside of the oven became extremely hot.  We finally got it to turn off.  If I was not home and decided to use the automatic timer Im pretty sure my house would have burned down.  I have read many complaints on this oven every one of them has the exact same issue.  When will you recall this?  When someone gets hurt or when some ones house burns down?  Sears will not help, they are rude, Im not paying for something that should be recalled! This is my second oven from this company, the first oven was a [REDACTED], now I've learned that it was recalled but after I got rid of it because it was doing the same thing this one is.

incident_description:
Freestanding 30ÃÂ GE Range installed in my kitchen caught fire, without any prior  warning incident, at 3:00 AM February 10, 2015. Subject product is Model Number JGBS23BEA3WH, Serial No. DA 140595P. Purchased New from Home Depot, Newbury Park, CA. I am reporting the  following hazard and   consequent event. This range is in the similar model and  manufacturing category as the recalled Dual Fuel Range, recalled in 2009 after numerous fire  events. 

This Freestanding Range, although apparently not the subject of the recall, nevertheless has a similar wiring harness defect. 

The defective wiring harness is immediately next to the gas inlet pipe and the valve body and Regulator assembly. This harness overheated, the resulting short circuit caused sparking and/or arcing  that eventually pierced an aluminum gas pipe. This circumstance was confirmed by a licensed professional cause and origin investigator engaged by my insurer, State Farm. The investigator is Reliant Investigations of Rancho Cucamonga, California, the principal of the investigating  firm is [REDACTED]. The investigators in this firm are CFI and CFEI  certified. Contact information is as  follows:
  
Address: 	[REDACTED]
		Rancho Cucamonga CA 91730

Phone	[REDACTED]
Email	[REDACTED]	

They conducted the investigation at the request of the State Farm adjusters who, incidentally,   have since declined coverage, another issue which itself is most likely a potential consumer complaint. 

The investigators took custody if the range as evidence, examined the appliance and the fire scene, photo-documented the  investigation, prepared their report which was submitted to State Farm. Due to my insurer's denial, I was able to have custody of the evidence range returned to me. And I have obtained a copy of the full report by Reliant, who indicates there have been at least a half dozen more similar fires involving the same or equivalent model of GE ranges since my loss: a defective wiring harness overheats and causes the range to catch fire.  This model that I own is not the recalled dual fuel model that was the subject of the CPSC fine excised against GE on February 19, 2015. However, Reliant Investigations states the defective wiring harness is either identical or virtually similar, and in their recent experience causes serious fires. 

In my situation, the fire began in the lower left rear area of the range, directly adjacent to the gas inlet piping and valve body, ignition of gas leaking from the damaged pipe was by the short-circuited defective wiring harness, which also caused the initial gas leak. The fire, fueled by a pressurized propane source, created a torch event that set fire to surrounding wood cabinetry and overhead hoods and cabinets. That ensuing gas  torch-fed fire then fully engulfed the residenceÃÂs kitchen,  which fortunately was separated from the  other rooms in the residence by 5/8" fire stop gypsum board  walls and ceilings, and solid core wood doors, which were closed. 

Upon awakening to the smoke and heat alarms, the building was safely exited by my  tenants, two elderly persons, who despite the  building being filled with acrid choking smoke, were able to  escape. I heard cries for  help, as  the subject building is a 3 bedroom, accessory building guest  house, part of my residential property in Malibu, CA. I was able to observe the extent of fire, called 911 and then attempted to knock down or control the fire until the fire department arrived. The kitchen, a 16 foot x 18 foot space with 11 foot ceilings was fully involved, but due to the closed doors and windows was somewhat oxygen starved. Opening the lower half of an exterior double hung window did not, very fortunately, cause a blowback, and I was able to successfully knock down most of the fire before LA County Fire arrived. They suppressed  the  smoldering remaining cabinets and  kitchen foodstuffs, opened the walls and ceilings and removed the charred wood elements and the range and hood. They also shut the gas supply, removed the  flex pipe and removed two fully burned duplex outlets and protected the exposed wiring with wire nuts.

Reliant Investigation's report concludes the GE range is both the cause and origin, and they state they are experiencing numerous similar fires caused by the same or similar GE model, all manufactured in Mexico, which are apparently not the subject of the 30ÃÂ dual fuel range implicated in the February 19 fine against GE, but they appear equally hazardous.

I am now seeking settlement of a  significant 5  figure claim  from GE, but  report this  event to suggest  the CPSC examine all models of the GE 30ÃÂ Free Standing Ranges.

Were it not for the  fact that I was  able to put nothing more than a  garden  hose on the fire,   but to have successfully knocked it down through a pushed-out  window, the local LA County Fire Department Captain observed that such quick action had saved the building from  total   involvement, and he  estimated that    the  fire  was perhaps no more than 30 seconds  from escaping  the kitchen and burning the entire  building to  the ground, especially  considering the time LACFD required to  arrive on scene, and to  lay hose from the  nearest  hydrant. 
In fact the most  significant  aspect of LACFD   emergency response  was to  shut of the  gas at the outside  valve, use  heat imaging to  look for  smoulders and   place an exhaust fan to vacate the smoke.     

I have  a  copy of  Reliant Investigations examination and concluding  report as well as  extensive on-scene photographs which I will make available to the CPSC upon request. 

I have contacted GE and their liability carrier, Electric Insurance,  to initiate a  settlement claim.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant property damage but no injuries or deaths, and similar incidents have been reported with this model.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid electric oven purchased June 2014 from Sears in Illinois.

This caller is reporting that around August 7th, 2015 her electric range overheated after preheating to 350 degrees then baking for an additional five minutes .
The caller became aware that the temperature had escalated past what it had been set at when she heard the glass from the 10" x 10" dish explode.

She said that the oven had become so hot that it was uncomfortable for her to stand in front of it and the round dish that was in the oven with the exploded dish did not exploded but was brown as if it had been sitting in fire, however there were no flames.

After this incident of overheating the oven is now not working at all.

There are no injuries being reported.

This caller is reporting this incident as a severe burn hazard and states that if the dish had not blown up there could have been a major fire and a possible explosion that could have potentially resulted in injury.

The caller contacted the manufacturer August 13th, 2015 and was advised  that the product is not on recall.
justification: The incident involved an overheating oven and exploding dish, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was having an issue with the oven portion of the unit since she purchased it. The oven was heating to high temperatures than selected. The food in the oven would get burnt. The range knobs would get extremely hot to the touch.

The consumer contacted Sears in Aug 2015 regarding the issue. Sears sent out a technician that repaired the unit with Electrolux parts. The technician replaced the temperature sensor and a piece on the electrical board. The repair was covered under warranty. 

The consumer stated that she noticed recently that the knobs to the range still continue to get too hot when the oven is on. The consumer stated that earlier they thought this issue occurred because of the issue with the oven. They thought that fixing the oven would resolve this issue. However, the issue is still not resolved and the range knobs still continue to get too hot to the touch when the oven is on. She stated that she has to use oven mitts to touch the knobs while the oven is on.

The consumer contacted Electrolux regarding the issue. The consumer was informed to contact Sears. The consumer informed Electrolux that this is a design flaw and it should be inspected by them rather than Sears.

The consumer contacted Sears but they cannot understand or explain why this happens. 

The consumer has a 3 year warranty on the unit.
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with the oven and range knobs getting excessively hot, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Caller is irate after her father contacted her to inform her that a product had been recalled.

The caller had purchased an oven in February 2008 and caller had cut herself on it in 2008 while cleaning it and she began smelling a faint burning odor in August 2015 then around September 5th, 2015 the unit stopped working.

Her husband took the oven outside and when he looked at it he observed that the unit had evidently been slowly burning internally over the two months that his wife kept smelling a burning odor.

The caller is reporting this issue as a severe hazard of fire stating that at any time she and her family could be out or could have been sleeping and the  unit could have caught fire.
Caller still has oven in garage.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller has contacted the manufacturer, spoke with a representative but could not quite understand all that the rep was saying but did understand that she was  saying  that they are aware of the hazard but that since there was no recall they are not paying for any repairs.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described internal burning over time.

incident_description:
This is regarding a Kenmore Elite dishwasher installed in my kitchen.   The top rack of the dishwasher is a "easy slide" rack and the top rack will slide forward when open this door of the dishwasher or while the door is open.   The problem is as you try to load the bottom rack of the dishwasher you have to constantly keep pushing the top rack back into the dishwasher.   If you are not watching it as you are swinging down to load a dish in the bottom rack not realizing the top rack just slide out, you can hit the rack with the dish and have had the case where I broke a plate.  There is no resistance to keep the rack from sliding around on it own.  

We had a technician from Sears to come to the house and look at the issue in which he reported there was nothing he could do to fix the issue.  The dishwasher was level.   Sears decided to send me a new dishwasher and the new one is doing the exact same thing.   The technician told me this was the 3rd service call within a week reporting the same issue.  To me there is a serious design flaw with how the top rack is mounted and needs to have something that does not allow the rack to slide so easily.     

I paid a visit to the Sears store where I purchased the dishwasher.   The sales person informed me that he had another customer earlier in the week complaining of the same issue.   Also found out this model of the dishwasher had been removed from the floor.   

I am now going through a second round with Sears for another technical to come to my house and review the situation.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing inconvenience and minor property damage (broken plate), but no injury or death.

incident_description:
On Sunday, October 18, 2015 I turned my Sears Kenmore oven on to preheat at 350. I was standing with my back to the oven when I turned around I saw fire through the glass door. I open the oven door the bottom heating element was in flames and shooting sparks amidst the smoke now coming from the oven. I shut the oven door and turned the oven off, the flames and sparks continued for a few minutes than went out. It had burned the element in half.  Had I not been in the kitchen my home may have burned down? 

This stove is 8 years old, purchased in 2007, I called sears they tried to sell me a new stove saying it would cost almost as much to fix it as it would to buy a new stove.

There is definitely a defect and definitely a safety issue here and Sears ought to step up and fix this defect. This is not a problem from normal wear and tear but one of, in my opinion, a defect in the product.  Model #790.90934601 _ Serial #VF70453176
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no injury or death, but posed a significant safety risk.

incident_description: We have a Sharp Microwave Oven Drawer, Model KB6025MS, manufactured in May 2008.  It has a round insert in the top of the microwave, secured by four plastic clips.  The insert deteriorated over time (unknown to us, as it is difficult to see up inside the drawer), and eventually caught fire.

incident_description: The Magic bullet was used to mash a ripe banana. As the banana was being fed to a year old infant, increasingly noticeable were more black specks than one would consider normal. In an attempt to strain the specks, it was discovered that the specks were pieces of black plastic from underneath the blade of the base attachment (as per photo attached). There was no visible injury, however, it is noted that no distinguishable plastic particles were uncovered in his subsequent bowel movements. It is of great concern to the childÃÂs grandmother that any plastic fragments remaining in the digestive track could possible cause harm over time.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the glass on the microwave door exploded spontaneously. The consumer stated that the microwave was not in use when it happened. The consumer used the microwave approximately 9 hours prior to the incident. 

The consumer stated that the glass shattered all over the floor. The glass is safety glass and so she was not injured. 

The consumer contacted Samsung on 09/17/15. The customer service representative made an appointment for someone to come out on 09/18/15 for an inspection. The consumer received a call from Unique Repairs in the morning of 09/18/15 informing her that they wouldn't be able to come out until 09/21/15. They also asked for credit card information and informed the consumer that it would cost her $107 for inspection. The consumer canceled the appointment.

The consumer contacted Sears and was informed that they can come out for a repair and provide 1 year warranty for $260.

The consumer went ahead and bought a new unit for $255.

This last time it came on by itself and we had to unplug the whole stove in order to get it turned off.
