However this last time my elderly mother is the one who woke up and found it on this could have been a tragedy. I hope that it not what it takes for this company to change their so called policy. I understand there is recalls but if you have fixed the so called recall and it continues the apparently that's not the problem. If you can't fix the problem then replace it with a new item.

incident_description: I have a Hamilton Beach Food Processor that's been in use for around one year, for normal household tasks in accordance with manufacturer instructions. When using it I noticed pieces of black plastic in the food. After disassembling I saw the metal shredding disk had cracked metal all around which were pulling out from the plastic in the center. Reported to company, asked if they had changed the design due to this defect, was informed no they had not, and that the defect I reported "was not a normal occurrence". I wish to have this documented as I received the impression they were not being proactive in investigating a potential danger that likely would affect other consumers purchasing this product. Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a defective product causing foreign material in food, but no injury was reported. The company stated this was not a normal occurrence, indicating it is unlikely to happen frequently.

incident_description:
The dishwasher was running for a little over an hour. When it started the drying cycle, black smoke came out of the top, front vent of the dishwasher. Thankfully, my husband and I were both in the kitchen at the time, and were able to turn it off immediately. Because we were in the kitchen, the only damage was to the dishwasher itself. If we hadnÃÂt been right there, there could have been a fire.
My husband unplugged the dishwasher to make sure it was safe and there was no further danger. It was obvious that the smoke came from within the door itself. He unscrewed the front panel from the door, and observed that the wiring had started to melt.
 
Also of note, there was a recall on the heating element for this product a few years ago. We DID have the dishwasher fixed according to the recall by an authorized professional.
justification: The incident involved black smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Gas oven turned on by itself with knob turned to off and no light indicating heating. Entire oven became extremely hot. Had to unplug electricity and turn off gas to stop oven.

[REDACTED]

incident_description: I bought a Sears Kenmore microwave model # 72185033111 serial # 209TA09445 ...the inside caught on fire and melted
justification: The microwave caught fire and melted, indicating an incident with potential for harm but no reported injury.

incident_description: I gave my daughter her sippy cup to drink from and she started crying saying "wwww yucky!" I took the cup from her and took a drink. What came out of the cup was a putrid taste, and I started gagging and ran to rinse my mouth out. That is when I took the cup apart and to my horror there was a greenish brown mold on the inside. After looking at reviews on amazon, I saw that I was not the only one who had this problem with the sippy cups because the valve is impossible to clean.

incident_description: I have two tommee tippee sippy cups. In the lid, there is a stopper to prevent it from leaking. Tonight, while putting a cup together (i always unassemble the cups when washing and then store separately) i noticed dark inside the stopper. I immediately stopped what i was doing and cut it open. Im sorry but the way these are designed, there is no way to fully dry them out and prevent moisture accumulation to prevent mold! Kids are going to get sick from these and they need to be pulled from the shelves! I have photos but have thrown the cups and stoppers away.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while using his oven toaster the toaster glass door exploded within 2 mins of operation.  He had just placed the contents in the unit and stepped away when he heard the explosion, there were glass pieces shattered everywhere in the room.  He feels that if a child had been close by the incident could have caused serious injuries.

(8/7) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that they acknowledge his issue and that he should contact one of their facility for instruction in operating the unit safely. (8/10) He spoke to a representative and was told to take it to a retailer repair facility for inspection.

Caller feels that this toaster is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved an exploding toaster glass door causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as similar incidents are acknowledged by the manufacturer.

incident_description:
09/14/2015 - The consumer used the microwave and when his food was ready, he opened the microwave door to extract it. When he did so, the unit turned on again and started cooking. The consumer unplugged his unit in order for it to stop.

The consumer states that his has happened an approximate six times.

09/15/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer via e-mail but has yet to receive any word back.

The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident involved the microwave turning on unexpectedly, posing a safety hazard, but no injuries were reported. The issue has occurred approximately six times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I was baking two chicken breasts in my oven at 375 degrees for 40 minutes. I had coated the dish with Pam. 23 minutes into the timed 40 minutes, I heard a loud bang. The baking dish exploded into hundreds of pieces in my oven.
justification: The baking dish exploded but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: My glass  oven door exploded. I went online and discovered that this is an ongoing issue with tempered glass. We had to use the oven and hour prior to the explosion. however, there were people online to whom this had happened and they have not use their oven for over 24 hours.  This is an issue during the manufacturing process where there is a defect in the tempered glass. And this can happen at any time under normal circumstances. I would like to know  what can be done to have my oven glass door replaced/fixed for no cost to me.
justification: The oven door exploded but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue is described as a manufacturing defect that can occur at any time, suggesting a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Electric Range model 790.96113408. It has been installed in my condominium for about 10 years, exclusively for home use, and not too often (about once or twice a week to prepare meals). The product has been well cared for, kept clean, and has not suffered any damages.

The oven handle keeps coming off when I pull on it to open/close the oven. As a result, the heavy glass oven door comes apart and crashes onto the floor. This has been happening for a couple of years, and now more frequently since the handle threads are getting worn out from having the screws reattached so many times.

I am lucky nothing more serious has happened, but this is a safety hazard nonetheless for the following reasons:

1. The glass door falling onto the floor could cause serious injuries (from bruises to lacerations and broken bones) to anyone standing in front of the oven.
2. If the glass door shatters, it could cause serious cuts.
3. More than half of the time I need to open the oven is because there is hot food inside that needs to be taken out. When the handle comes off, there is no way to re-attach it without opening the oven door; and without the handle, it is necessary to pull the door open from the sides, which are extremely hot. The space between the door and the unit is very narrow, so I cannot even use an oven mitt to protect my fingers when opening the door.
4. I've had burns on my arms and fingers from trying to hold the door open after the handle came off. Fortunately, these were minor injuries; I did not see a doctor and don't have records of the burns, aside from a couple of small scars.
5. If the food remains longer in the hot oven because I cannot open the oven door, even after turning off the heat, it could catch on fire. I live in a 43-unit condominium and most of the apartments have the exact same Kenmore range. It's only a matter of time before the lives of all the residents are compromised because of this issue.

From researching on the Sears website, I've come across numerous related complaints, and it is obvious that the screws provided by the manufacturer are too short to hold the handle in place. I've tried to contact Sears and they tried to sell me replacement parts for about $7 each screw for a total of over $40 including shipping, which I think it is an unreasonable cost for two screws that should have come with the product in the first place.
justification: The incident has caused minor burns and poses a risk of more serious injuries from the falling oven door, but no deaths have been reported.

incident_description:
Two left burners on flat top stove turned on without being used on two separate occasions.  Would not turn off or change heat (were glowing red non-stop as if on high).  Knobs were in off position at time of malfunction.  Only remedy was to shut power off at the circuit breaker.  When flipped back on, the digital setting read "ER" as if error, and after 5 minutes, reset to "HE" because the burners were still warm, and eventually shut off.  

I called about the issue seeming to be related to a known recall on this model of stove, but was told it was corrected by the time my unit was manufactured.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could not be turned off normally, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was using the Orka Flavor and Oil Mister.  I have had it for two years.  I refilled it with oil today and then pumped it.  About 30 seconds later, it exploded and the part that holds the oil flew across the house in to the other room (about 15 feet).  Luckily it is not glass so it did not shatter, however, if someone had been hit by it, I think they would definitely have been injured.  Oil sprayed all over the entire kitchen.
justification: The device exploded and caused property damage, but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such incidents are not common but can occur with faulty equipment.

incident_description:
Purchased IKEA "NUTID" 4 burner induction cook top in February 2011 from IKEA store in Emeryville, CA.  Professionally installed in April 2011 and started using it in May 2011 in a remodeled kitchen.  Mid November 2011 after using the unit approx 50 times, I had just finished cooking a dinner for 6 guests and had been using the unit for 90 minutes or so, whereupon I de-powered the unit by turning the normal master power switch off on the burner control panel as I normally would do when I finished cooking.  Twenty minutes into dinner I noticed an acrid burning electric insulation smell from the kitchen and grey smoke coming from the edges of the cook top where it sat upon the granite counter top.  I lifted the cook top and the area below spontaneously burst into open flames.  My dinner guest had the where-with-all to bring me a halon fire extinguisher with which I extinguished the flames and my wife turned off the 220 volt feeder circuit breaker at the electric panel.  Upon examining the area of the fire I noticed the feeder cables and the electronics area of the unit were nearly melted and destroyed by the fire.  There was absolutely no grease or food spillage or any other combustible matter in the area of the fire.  If I had not been at home that evening, I am certain my condominium would have been destroyed by the electrically fed fire which had started.  Whirlpool appliance replaced the unit in February 2012 and the appliance repair technician said that in his opinion the fire had been caused by a fault in the electronic control unit which had improperly commanded full power from a de-powered unit.  The new unit functioned normally until August of 2014 whereupon a fault light caused one of the elements to become permanently inoperative.  Whirlpool then replaced that unit with the third NUTID cook top and that one has been in service for about 14 months now.  I would have reported this earlier but I only found your web site recently. incident_description: I was using a press-down style apple slicer to slice an apple. The slicing blades broke free of the plastic ring. My hand and wrists were hit by the ends of the blades. A 1/4" one way or the other and my hands/wrists could have been cut very badly.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning tool that could have caused injury but did not result in any actual harm.

incident_description: On Sunday 11th October 2015, after cooking sons dinner the glass hob cover exploded in the kitchen. The force was so bad that glass was thrown into the next room. One of the front hobs had been knocked and was on which heated the glass to the point of it exploding. When this happened my husband, 4 year old son and I were fortunately in the room next door and absolutely dread to think what could have happened if we had been in the kitchen. We are aware that the glass cover should not be in place when the hob on but we did not know the hob was switched on. The glass shattered into millions of pieces but they were mostly very sharp. If anyone was in the kitchen when this happened there is no doubt serious injury would have occurred. My first thought when it happened that a brick had been put through our window. I'm sure this will be a popular item and need to warn others of the risk of this happening to them. I'm still in shock and feel so lucky
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the glass hob cover causing significant damage, but no injuries occurred as the family was in another room.

incident_description: Kemore ceramic cooktop stove - Turned oven to bake and programmed to 325 degrees.  I put in what I intended to bake and set the timer.  I shortly began smelling something burning.  When I went to check, I saw smoke coming from opening as if I were broiling something.  I opened the oven door, and even though my food was not even halfway through cooking, it was burned - black and charred, and I noticed that the broiler was on.  After removing the item (amid smoke detectors going off and the house being filled with smoke and a horrible smell), I turned off the stove.  I continued to check, and despite the stove being turned off, the broiler remained on, and the sides of the stove were extremely hot.  We had to switch off the breaker.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove causing smoke and burned food, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore electric stove, Model 79092902010. It's about 5 years old (young).  Last night while baking chicken at 350 f temp, the glass on the oven door spontaneously exploded and shattered all over the kitchen.  Thankfully, no one was near it.  It have not been hit or slammed, ever.  There was a loud, explosive noise as glass spewed all over the place.  My brother, when called, said somehow pressure must have built up inside the door.  I have never heard of this, and strongly feel that there was a defect that finally resulted in this situation.  I have pictures, but was unable to paste them to this box.  I have been calling Kenmore for two days and am getting nowhere.  Because the warranty has run out, no one will help me.  I think when you see the picture, you will see it's not from a hit or slam; the entire glass area blew out all over the place.  No hanging glass or holes or cracks.  This was a very dangerous situation.  I've spoken to all kinds of customer service folks, managers and parts people to no avail.  I cannot use the oven, given its condition.  Also, given my concern with what could have caused this, I don't want this damaged unit in my home.  I will be looking for another stove, and another brand, given the lack of concern that Kenmore has.  However, I feel they should look into this for the safety of others.  I also feel they should compensate me given the danger that this posed, expensive stoves are suppose to last a lot longer than 5 years, and this was not due to anything I did.  Also, dealing with them has been a nightmare.  I have attached the pictures.  I also want to be sure that other Kenmore owners do not have this happen to them.  If we had been near the stove we both would have been covered in glass, (eyes, face, body).  I'm still attempting to vacuum it all, as little specs are all over the place.
justification: The glass on the oven door exploded, posing a potential danger, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
One of the heating elements on our Kenmore Elite Electric Range (model 79097472802) turned on spontaneously and heated to a glowing red, showing a high level of heat.  We tried to turn the element off but the on/off button was not working.  Eventually the only thing that would turn the stove off was unplugging it.  
 
This happened on Sept. 27 2015 while we were roasting food in the oven.  Just before the element kicked on and heated up (within about a minute), we heard an odd grinding-like noise coming from the stove.  

We bought this stove Jan. 6 2010 from Sears.  We've had to have it fixed several times; the problems always seeming to revolve around the electronics.  We have continued to update the warranty, however Sears has sent a contracting company out twice to address this latest incident and still can't fix the stove.  The second technician came today (Oct. 12 2015) to replace the stove circuit board, aka the control board. While here he noticed that several wires that are part of the wiring harness are burnt.  He is going back to his office to see about replacing the wiring harness.  In the mean time I contacted Sears at their product complaint section about this and received complaint case # [REDACTED].

My point is that it may be worth the CPSC's time to investigate a 5-year old stove that turns on spontaneously and gets hot to enough to be an obvious fire hazard, and which won't turn off unless unplugged.  Is there any way that you can help my family with this?  I would appreciate your help.
justification: The incident involves a stove heating spontaneously, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I finished cooking something on the left, front burner of my Kenmore electric smooth-top stove. I wanted to put the pan on simmer, so I pressed the "Simmer Select" button, and instantly there was a pop, and sparks flew from behind the top, left corner of the stove. The stove continued to work, but now there is an electrical burn mark on the wall panel behind the stove.
justification: The incident involved sparks and an electrical burn mark but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. Such electrical faults are uncommon but possible with aging appliances.

incident_description: I purchased a Samsung above the range microwave me16h702ses.  I was was attempting to heat up popcorn.  Within 5 seconds, the light started to flicker, then sparks came out thru the top, then smoke started to come thru the top of the microwave.  I immediately opened the door and unplugged the microwave.  I am now waiting to contact Samsung customer relations department as they are not available at this time.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the microwave, but no injury occurred as the user unplugged it immediately.

incident_description:
Turned on dishwasher detected a strong odor and breaker flipped.  Opened dishwasher to assure there was nothing jamming/blocking the water heads or flow.  Reset breaker and turned dishwasher on again.  This time odor was stronger and smoke was coming out of the door panel.  Breaker tripped again.  

Ordered new dishwasher.  In the mean time since my spouse and I are both engineers, we took the door panel apart and took pictures of the obvious shot/breakdown of the control board.  At the power connection to the board, the board had big hold melted in it.

Obviously this is a common occurrence (http://kitchenaidfire.com), with over 1000 cases documented of the same problem and nearly 100 of the exact same model that I have (KUDP01FL).
justification: The incident involved smoke and a tripped breaker but no injury, and the problem is documented as common with over 1000 cases reported.

incident_description:
I was repairing a neighbors GE ice dispenser with a broken auger drive cup and found ground up plastic particles in the ice dispenser. It appears some units were built with the wrong parts or incorrectly designed augers. These units have the auger length to long and the front end drills into the plastic ice dispenser bucket.
The problem appears to be on both new refrigerators that came with our houses and in replacement buckets from parts supplies.
I don't know if the plastic particles are harmful, as most appear to be a fine powder, that can exit while water or ice is dispensed. The problem was also seen on you tube comments when people were repairing their ice dispensers, as the dis-assembly becomes very difficult as the auger has to be forced out of the plastic it has drilled into.
justification: The incident involves plastic particles in ice dispensers due to design flaws, but there is no evidence of injury or death.

incident_description: Surface comes on by itself. will not shut off when it does and has to have breaker pulled. THis has happened multiple times over the last 5 years.
justification: The surface turning on by itself and requiring a breaker pull is an incident with no injury, and it has happened multiple times over 5 years, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description: The outer glass panal on the oven shattered.  It was an LG gas oven model number LRG3095ST that was purchased new in 2011, and was approximately four years old.  Thankfully no one was near the oven when it happened.  The oven was fully cooled having been used about 2.5 hours prior.  The prior heating use consisted of a temperature of 425 for 30 minutes.  There was no other use in the previous four days.
justification: The glass panel shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I purchased a munchkin brand sippy cup with a soft spout for my baby this summer at Target. [REDACTED] used the cup several times without an issue. Then one evening I noticed he was soaking wet and discovered that the spout of the sippy cup and had come completely off. Fortunately he spit out the tip of the cup and did not choke on it. The piece that came off is small and a true choking hazard. I still have the cup, top and spout at home. I also have a picture I can send in if you like.
justification: The sippy cup spout came off, posing a choking hazard, but the baby did not choke or get injured.

incident_description: I was using the "bacon Wave" microwavable bacon cooker and it caught fire in my microwave. It damaged the microwave and could have burned the kitchen if I was not right there. I have used it before but I never had this problem. I still have the item. it caught fire in three areas on the tray. Very scary.
justification: The incident involved a fire that damaged the microwave but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as the user mentioned it never happened before despite prior use.

incident_description:
(Anyone buying this model and not testing the temperature is at risk!)

I purchased two Kenmore Model 60412 refrigerators from Sears online Store, one for myself and one for my tenet. They delivered and installed them and I set the temperature controls to a little beyond the normal setting for safe measure.

Three weeks later I got food poisoning from a jar of jam, I knew it was from this because my stomach started boiling inside very soon after eating some, and closer observation saw mold. Jam seemed like an unlikely source for food poisoning and as I do not keep food very long this prompted me to investigate.

As I am HVAC-Universal Certified I had all the equipment needed to check the temperatures properly inside the fridge and freezer sections.
I was shocked to find the fridge average temperature was 46 F and the freezer 16 F.
The high temperatures recorded overnight being 48 F and 28 F.
Now I have both refrigerators set at maximum cold position and averages are 40 F and 9 F. The high temperatures recorded overnight being 46 F and 23 F. 

As I was just past the 30 day return when I had figured out about the problems I was forced to opt for having Sears attempt to repair them.
It took three weeks to get them to the house as the parts showed up one day after the first scheduled appointment. The technician said they seemed to have sent the wrong parts for the problem as they sent defrost controls and not thermostats.
He called in and asked about it and they had him install the parts anyway. He also put some silicone on the freezer door of one refrigerator that was also icing up.

As the Sears tech expected it did not address the problem, the refrigerators where still too warm. The silicone that was added to the one door seal shrunk and pulled about 15 inches of the door seal away from the fridge when closed, leaving a gap wide enough for me to slide my fingers through without compressing the seal.

I contacted Sears about this always being very polite, and they tell me itÃÂs improbable that I got two bad refrigerators and kept me on the line for awhile before hanging up on me. I did get another appointment online to fix the door seal the technician destroyed and it will take another two weeks for them to get out and fix the seal problem.

They have no plan to address the temperature problems at this point.
I looked at the service paper from the fridge and noticed that it says the expected freezer temperature at 65 F ambient is between 2 F and 8 F, this seems like an admission in writing that the freezer will not hold 0 F.    

Looking at the 1 & 2 star reviews on the Sears website I see this is not an uncommon problem for this model. 
I have figured out that the problem is with the restart function of the thermostat or control board, the fridge stays off way too long to keep food safe.

Kenmore 18 cu. ft. Top Freezer Refrigerator Model # 60412
http://www.sears.com/kenmore-18-cu-ft-top-freezer-refrigerator-white/p-04660412000P?prdNo=1&blockNo=1&blockType=G1
justification: The incident resulted in food poisoning (injury) due to improper refrigerator temperatures, and similar issues are reported in multiple reviews, indicating a recurring problem.

incident_description: Purchased an electric range, floor model from Sears in Seabrook NH about 5 years ago.  The smooth top range doesn't match the recall model and serial numbers listed here http://www.cpsc.gov/en/recalls/2009/frigidaire-and-kenmore-smoothtop-electric-ranges-recalled-due-to-fire-hazard/ but it is having the same problems.  The burners will turn up to high on their own and recently will not turn off.  We have had to unplug it from the wall.  I called Kenmore and was basically told if the serial number and model numbers don't match I will have to pay for the repair.  My model number is: 790.94332700 and serial number is: VF73553723, which are slightly different than what was listed in this recall.  I have the original receipt as well.
justification: The electric range has malfunctioning burners that turn on and stay on, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The Samsung freestanding range model number FE710DRS has temperature indicator printed on the stove top back panel for each burner such as lo 1,2,3,-9, hi.  these numbers will wipe off of the stainless steel with only soapy water during cleaning which leaves the consumer guessing as to what temperature is set when cooking. further, you are unable to tell if the stove is off or turned on medium as the dial points up and down as to off at the top and medium at the bottom and the hot stove top indicator light stays on until the stove top is cooled off, several minutes (about 15-20 minutes).  When you think its off and you leave a pot/or pan on the burner its still on and results in a grease fire, water boiling over and onto the stovetop and floor.  the potential for burning a person or burning a house full of children down extremely likely.  Especially if cooking late at night.

 This is a safety issue as when you think the stove is on low its actually on high which has resulted in grease fires, burnt food and smoke.  This range was purchased at Lowes in September 2014.

Someone is going to die as a result of this defect and this should be addressed immediately as all the ranges that Samsung produced that are stainless steel seem to have this problem.

Lets just hope a house full of children do not die because mother had to warm a bottle for baby [REDACTED] at 2:00 A.M. and thought she turned off the stove but actually turned it on high and went back to bed
justification: The description indicates a high potential for death due to grease fires and burns, especially with the likelihood of the stove being left on high unintentionally.

incident_description:
The igniter on my GE stove (model number JGS968T0H3WW) has a wiring defect that caused the plastic wire harness and wires to melt.  If the stove hadn't shorted out, I think it would have caused a fire.  GE denies that this is a safety issue.

I did some research and see that many models of GE stoves from this same year (2004) have already been recalled for safety issues related to wiring.  I think the recall should be expanded to include my model.
justification: The incident involved a wiring defect that caused melting but no injury or fire occurred, and similar models have been recalled for safety issues.

incident_description: I started my GE Profile (PDW9880N00SS) dishwasher and then noticed the smell of burning plastic. The heating element will not turn off. I unplugged the dishwasher and called GE support line. There are many other GE dishwashers that have been recalled, but for some reason this model is not on the recall list. GE could not give me a reason why so many others are recalled, but not the PDW9880N00SS.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and a malfunctioning heating element, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated while the oven self cleaning was in process for approximately an hour he smelled a burning odor, he cancelled the operation and when he tried to open the door there was extreme heat dispersing from the oven so he had to restrain from opening the door.  Later, after the oven had cooled down he reached for the door handle and it broke.  Caller stated that he had noticed that the handle had become deformed after using it several months from the heat of the oven.

(8/2015) The manufacturer was contacted and a service technician was sent out for inspection, he was advised that the information she retrieved would be sent out to the company.  He was also advised that if there should be any repairs it would be at his expense since the oven is over a year old. 

Caller feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and a broken door handle, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as similar issues have been reported.

incident_description: Unit started out as leaking hot water when being filled and then progressed to actually appearing to explode on two occasions. I was trying to brew my normal coffee and did everything as normal, I put the K-cup in and then the next thing I knew I heard something spraying and there was hot water and coffee grounds spraying out of the area where the K-cup is inserted. When I opened it up after it cooled off there was coffee grounds all over the kitchen counter, wall and immediate are surrounding the unit.  The K-cup itself had a much larger than normal sized hole and had the appearance that it had blown up during brewing.
justification: The incident involved hot water and coffee grounds spraying, which could cause burns or other injuries, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Elite Electric Range Model 790.9747*, 9748*, that was delivered on 12/9/09. We paid $1559.99.00 for this, with delivery fees, taxes and extended 5 year warranty the total invested was $1765.56.  In April of 2013, in the middle of the night, we woke to the sound of loud explosion. We discovered our kitchen and laundry room covered in pieces of glass due to the outer glass door of the oven exploding.  We had not used the oven in days.  After seeing the force of the blowout, we were very frighten to think of the damaged that could have been done had we been in the kitchen or even worse any of our small grandchildren.  So we were hesitant to just replace the glass. We spoke with Sears, and they told us they had never heard of this happening and assured us it was an extremely rare situation. Only after being assured this would not happen again, we arranged for repair. When the service representative came, I was still troubled about this. I questioned the technician and was told that they had not seen this before and assured me it was extremely unlikely.
Last night, 10/6/15, I cooked dinner (using the same oven)  for my son and his family. While cooking my 2 year old grandson and 10 month old granddaughter were in and out of the kitchen, inches away from the oven. We were taking the food out of  the kitchen and placing it on the table in the dining area, when we heard the explosion; immediately we knew the outer glass of the oven door had exploded again. Thank God that none of us were in the kitchen at that moment. It was tempered glass and did shatter into thousand of small pieces of glass for the most part with some larger pieces that were still bonded together. However, the potential damage it would have caused the small children, who were eye level with the door was unbearable to consider. I used the words "WOULD have caused harm" only after having seen how far the pieces of glass were thrown.
Today, I researched this to see that oven glass doors have been reported exploding since 2007.  I understand it has happened on many different oven brands. There are hundreds of reports of this on Kenmore ovens alone. Surely this could be resolved! And at minimal consumers warned.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door with potential for injury, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught on fire while running. Smoke coming from buttons on the front. We took the front off of the dishwasher and the control panel had burned.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke and damage to the control panel, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: In 2007 I bought 2 Kenmore Electric Ranges & a refrigerator. We put one range & the refrigerator in a house we were selling. We put the Kenmore 790.96010407 in our home. We didn't use it much and of course, after the warranty was up the range would not turn off. It would stay on high and I would have to pull the range out & unplug it. I called the company & said that model was not on the recall. Seems funny that was the same problem that the other ranges were recalled for.  We did not have the money to have a repairman come out & fix it as the repairman was not sure how much it would cost, but the service call was $100.00. The range would most of the time turn off, but it would take spurts and not turn off. On October 22, 2013 my granddaughter was in the kitchen with me. I had turned the range off, but it did not go off. She hit her hand on the range & burned it pretty bad. Now I keep her out of the kitchen completely when she's here. Now the range is not turning off again. I am going to purchase another range, but it will definitely not be a KENMORE!!! Please let me know if you have had any other complains of this nature on his model. Thanks.. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the granddaughter, which classifies it as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) because the range frequently fails to turn off, posing a consistent hazard.

incident_description:
IKEA Godis Glassware

Shatters with slight contact

I had this problem one time before but thought I must have had the dial slightly out of place. I researched online and found a number of other complaints on this issue.  I contacted Sears who admits that while they have an open safety recall for this exact description on other ranges, my model is not on the list so they will not assist. incident_description:
The consumer stated that she used the coffee maker to make some coffee. She set it the coffee maker to 4 hours.

About 5-6 hours later, the consumer went to clean the coffee maker. The light on the coffee maker had turned off so the consumer thought that the unit was off. The consumer went to wipe the hot plate with a damp cloth and burned herself. The consumer burned 3 fingers on her right hand. The consumer has blisters. She applied at home first aid to her fingers.

The consumer thought that the light may have gone out and pressed the on/off button on the coffee maker to turn it off. The consumer came back about 15 minutes later and noticed that the plate was still hot to the touch. 

The consumer stated that the coffee maker never turned off and only the light turned off. She had to unplug the coffee maker to turn it off.

The consumer tried to contact the firm at the number on the pot (800-807-6777) but received a prompt that the number that was not accessible to California.

I am letting the LG Corporation know that my LG microwave Model LMV1813ST (S/N 307TAEJOA668) has a serious quality defect that could lead to a fire. My unit overheated without being operated. incident_description:
Kenmore flat top electric range.  The front left burner activated to full power despite the control knob being left on a lower power setting.  When this was noticed, we immediately turned the control knob into the "off" position but the burner did not respond, and continued to burn at full power.  After frantically turning the knob on and off to try to get the burner off, it finally did go out.  We left the knob in the off position (and turned off all other burners as well), but the front left burner came back on to full power within a matter of seconds.  Again we tried turning the knob on and off several times before the burner would actually turn off.  This sequence happened 4-5 times total before the burner stayed off.
We have unplugged the unit to prevent it from turning on automatically at a random time of day or night.

This product has a related recall for the same issues, but my model number falls outside of the recall list so Sears will not help me.  Obviously the recall was not comprehensive as not all affected units were recalled.
justification: The burner malfunctioned repeatedly but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was mitigated by unplugging the unit.

incident_description:

08/23/2015 - The consumer indicates that he made a pot of coffee. The consumer states that he noticed the coffee boiling and smoke was coming from the unit approximately forty-five minutes after the coffee was made. The consumer unplugged the unit immediately and no fire occurred.

The unit stays on for approximately two hours after brewing and then automatically shuts off.

08/24/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained what happened. The representative he spoke to seemed uninterested in the matter. He was informed that he would have to pay shipping to send the defective unit back for testing as well as shipping for a replacement unit. The consumer spoke to the Supervisor as well and was given the same information.

The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.

incident_description:

The consumer stopped using the oven.

incident_description: We purchased a GE Convection Microwave and product trim kit as the unit is installed in a cabinet (vs. countertop).  When using the convection mode, the exterior of the unit gets extremely hot.   There is a return for the hot air coming out of the unit, but it is expelled approximately an inch from the metal trim kit.  There is no venting for the hot air (there was in the prior model) so the trim kit gets scorching hot.   We contacted GE.  Over a period of a couple months, they have sent two technicians to assess the unit (as well as a new trim kit (the same one we already had), which is not the issue as it still doesn't safely release/vent the hot air)  One of the technicians tested the temperature of the trim kit from the exterior and the temperature of the metal was 160 degrees (the unit had been turned off for a brief time when he took the temp).  We independently purchased a surface thermometer and have taken readings hotter than that.  You are unable to touch the exterior as the surface is so hot it would burn you.  We have asked GE to do a return / credit us and we will purchase a traditional microwave.  They refuse to do so as they insist the unit is working as it is supposed to and is not a safety hazard.
justification: The exterior of the microwave gets hot enough to cause burns, indicating a risk of injury.

incident_description:
I bought this KitchenAid counter top microwave less than 4 years ago. After a little bit over one year, one of the micro switch is burned. I replaced a new one to it. On second year, two more micro switches were burned again.

And then last week, it doesn't heat food any more, I opened box and found one wire (black color) which connects the transformer to the micro switch is burned and broken. I can sent you picture for this.

Even though I reconnected the wire and the microwave works again, I believe there is some short circuit inside somewhere which causes the burning over and over again.

And more important is that this product has a big potential fire hazard and potential human body damage. I strongly ask this product to be recalled and replace it with a new one.
justification: The incident involves repeated electrical failures and potential fire hazards, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:

Since the two self-start incidents, I contacted Whirlpool and was told the company would cover sending a technician to evaluate the oven, but would not cover any repair.
justification: The microwave started by itself, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

The consumer sets the temperature to a certain degree but shortly thereafter, the unit either increases or decreases the original temperature it was set to, usually increasing it. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer approximately four or five months later and explained the issue she was having. The representative she spoke to informed her that they would send a Service Technician over. When the Service Technician inspected the unit, he adjusted the screws in the knob.

The consumer tested the unit for about two weeks but the unit was still not malfunctioning. The consumer contacted the manufacturer and another Service Technician inspected her unit. The Service Technician inspected the unit. The consumer informed the Technician that her grandson touched the gap between the faceplate and the top of the door and burned his fingers. This gap is almost an inch wide. There is also a gap on the sides where heat escapes from. The Service Technician informed the consumer that that was the way the oven was designed and, as far as her grandson, that she should keep him away from the oven. The Service Technician made no repairs. The Service Technician informed the consumer that he should call the manufacturer and complain.

08/04/2015 (Approximate) - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and spoke to [REDACTED]. After she informed what had been happening, [REDACTED] suggested they change the knob and the thermostat on the unit. The parts were ordered and the consumer received the parts. [REDACTED] asked the consumer for pictures, which were e-mailed. [REDACTED] offered a discount on the purchase towards a new unit.

The consumer has been trying to contact the manufacturer in order to have the parts they sent her installed on her unit. She has been unable to contact them.

The consumer states that she has ceased use of the unit as of August. The consumer only has issues with the oven; the burners work properly. 

The consumer believes the product poses a safety hazard to consumers. The consumer has no other injuries to report.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the consumer's grandson, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the ongoing temperature control issues and heat escape from the oven.

incident_description:
1. The product had been used earlier in the evening to heat food.
2. About 1 hour later, as I was sitting at the kitchen table the microwave started on its own. No one near it. I heard it turn on due to a loud buzzing sound and went to investigate.  The LED read-out was blank and the STOP button did not stop the operation.
3.  I opened the door and it stopped running, closed the door and it started up again.
4.  I attempted to program it by entering the timer, but it flasher, "Set the clock" which I attempted, but it would not take the entry.  
5.  I went to the basement and turned off the power (220 V double breaker for the oven and microwave) and waited for about 1 minute.  Thinking the electronics would reset.  Turned the breaker back on and came upstairs.  It was running again with the LED screen blank.  
6.  Opened the door to stop the unit, returned to the basement and turned off the power. 
7.  Called Sears for service. Due Tuesday
8.  Checked the recall list and find that earlier models (older than my unit) had been on recall for this same problem, but not mine.  
My concern is that if I had not been sitting there in the same room, it might have caused a fire, as it is a built-in unit in wood cabinets.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was stopped before causing injury or fire, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions and user presence to mitigate.

incident_description:
This morning, after brewing a pot of coffee as usual in my Black & Decker 12 Cup Smart Brew Coffee Maker Part #: DCM2000b Type 1, the upper plastic handle retainer broke loose from the pot.  I was very fortunate that I keep the coffee maker at the rear of my counter-top so that when the pot fell, it hit the countertop and did not drop the scalding coffee on my leg and /or foot.  It appears that the glue that also hold the handle to the pot also separated and the only thing that saved me was the lower handle screw in a retainer.  Although the pot did not fall to the floor, there was a large counter-top spill and a few splashes of coffee did fall on my foot.

Upon examination, that screw was actually on its last thread and if the counter had not stopped he pot from dropping, would have failed also.  We use this coffee maker twice weekly (on weekends) and this unit had been in service for about 6 months.
justification: A few splashes of coffee fell on the foot, which constitutes a minor injury.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid 36ÃÂ Cooktop Explosion					File # [REDACTED]

On Sept. 16, 2015, I turned on the front left burner of this cooktop under a 5ÃÂ tall pot containing oatmeal and water.   There was a large flame up to the top of the pot and completely around it.  It scared me and I turned off the flame immediately.   Then the entire cooktop exploded shooting glass up in the air and across the room.  The iron grates were blown up against the stone backsplash.  I was completely stunned.  I had minor cuts on my arm and glass fragments in my hair.  I must have turned away from the cooktop just in time to be out of the main thrust of the explosion.  Pieces of glass flew over the kitchen island into the great room beyond for an approximate distance of about 15 feet.  At no time did I notice any smell of gas although I donÃÂt know what propane gas smells like if different from the smell of natural gas.   This is a dangerous appliance that needs to be removed from the marketplace. 

I grabbed my phone, went outside and called Valley Propane who instructed me on how to turn off the main valve on the outside propane tank which I did.  They arrived about a half hour later and disconnected the cooktop and capped off the gas line to the cooktop.   One of their men removed the remaining small glass fragments from my scalp and hair that I was unable to do myself.   I put alcohol on all the cuts and bandages on the 2 cuts that were bleeding.   None required additional medical attention as there was no nearby facility to go to anyway.  They also helped me calm down from the shock. 

I took pictures of the explosion which I previously emailed to you and am enclosing additional copies herein.   It took me a day and a half of my vacation to clean up the mess.  There are now minor dents in the island cabinets facing the cooktop, the tall cabinets on either side and in the prefinished white oak flooring between the cooktop and the kitchen island.  I repaired the dents as best as possible with refinishing gel.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts) and significant property damage, but no severe injuries or death.

incident_description:

incident_description:
The caller stated that the refrigerator has two light bulbs in the top center of the unit. The light bulbs have one switch each (one on left side door and one on the right side door). The consumer stated that both of the light bulbs overheated and melted the ceiling of the refrigerator. There is a hole (about 3 inches) above each of the light bulbs. incident_description:

My wife called GE and a repair person came out on 07/28/15, during this call we were told if the problem was a health and safety issue the microwave would be replaced. The repair person came out on 07/28/15 and stated that GE's computers were down and that someone would contact us in 24 hours. No one contacted us so on 07/30/15 I called and e-mailed GE. incident_description: We've had this Kenmore Stovetop for several years and we have loved it, however when we were cooking a pot of spaghetti sauce on the back left burner and a different pot of sauce on the front right corner, the glass stove top melted to the bottom of the front right pot (bigger burner). Possibly heating element keep heating up or air bubble in glass???  We are very upset over this and were extremely thankful that our children, dogs, etc were not in the house at the time this occurred.  90% of the glass stayed on the stove top, however we cannot figure out why this would occur when no one was in the room for this duration. The model number of this Kenmore Electric Smooth-top Slide-In Range is No.  790.95212201 and serial number  VF30621030.  I am having trouble locating legitimate looking sites for this Electrolux owned product as well; one site said recall, one did not-- please help if you can, would love to get this fixed or at the very least help others not have this issue.

incident_description: While running, a fire started inside the control panel of our Kenmore Elite 665.139 dishwasher generating noxious toxic fumes.  We cut the electrical power at the circuit breaker.  I unscrewed and opened the door where the control electronics are housed to ensure there was no more open flame. I traced back the source of the fire to power connection on the control board (Whirlpool Corp. P/N W10195344).  There was absolutely no moisture inside the dishwasher door.  I concluded that the electrical fire was either caused by a design flaw (insufficient electrical trace clearance, sizing, or isolation from the ground plane) or manufacturing conditions causing a poor solder joint - I could not be certain as that portion of the board was completely obliterated by the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire and toxic fumes but resulted in no injury or death, and such electrical fires in appliances are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
Please see attached sheet as the space on this form was not sufficient for my information. Thank you.
I am using this page because the space on the pdf form was not sufficient for my information.

On 9/15/15 I was preparing to make pasta sauce. I put a little olive oil in my pan on my right hand front
stove burner. This is a split burner that can be used for both large and small pans. My range is a
Frigidaire Gallery Series smooth cooktop. Model # GlEFS77CSA Serial # VF32440851. We purchased this
stove on 6/22/03. We have never had any repairs done on this stove. It has not been moved since we
bought it. I placed my sliced garlic in the oil in my pan and turned the burner onto the low heat setting.
I turned back to my counter and proceeded to chop my onion. Within a minute I could smell burning
garlic and the oil was spitting. I turned back to my stove to see my burner was red hot and indeed my
garlic was burning and the oil was almost gone and spitting. I pulled the pan off of the burner, looked at
the burner knob, noticed that indeed it was on low and then quickly shut it off. It was very disconcerting. 
If I had not been right there, what would have happened? I took a breath and then tried to turn the burner
on low again. When I did, it immediately turned bright red and burning hot with no temperature regulation 
as it should have for a low temperature setting. I turned off the burner and decided to use my other front 
large burner for my sauce, intending to look into this issue later in the day.

When I did look into the issue with my stove, I was surprised to discover that there was a recall of
Frigidaire Gallery smooth cooktops made by your office on Aug. 28th, 2009. It is release # 09-333. I
researched this further to discover that my range serial number was in the recall range, but my model
was not. I decided to call Frigidaire and speak to them about this since it was a known problem with
other ranges in the Gallery series, manufactured and sold during the same time period. I spoke with 6
people during the 2 day time period of 9/15-9/16/15. I was shuttled back and forth from the recall to
the customer service dept. then back to the recall dept. Each time the person saying the other dept.
could help me. Finally on 9/16/15 a woman named [REDACTED] in the customer service dept. tried to really
help me. I explained what happened and how I didn't understand why it was so hard to have my issue
covered under the recall when my incident was what the recall was for, my range is a gallery range,
manufactured and sold during the same time period, probably manufactured alongside the gallery
models that are listed on the recall and most likely has the same parts in question that are faulty and
have caused safety problems in the past. My serial number is in the recall range. She understood what I
was asking and went to her supervisor. After a time she came back and said that both the model and
the serial number have to be what is on the recall for it to be covered. That those are the rules of the
Consumer Protection Agency. I kind of understood that, but thought that since this is a known safety
issue with similar gallery models that they would do the right thing and cover my issue too and offer to
replace whatever part is faulty. She said no that they couldn't do that.

So I said I would call the Consumer Protection Agency and file a claim. Which I did this morning 9/17/15.
I spoke with [REDACTED] who listened to my story and said she would help me file my claim. Unfortunately,
she said she was having trouble with the online form and could I call back or try online. I said I would. I
tried online and I too had difficulty with the online form. After I wrote this information down and hit
next, it said cannot locate this page. Everything I typed was lost. So I downloaded this form to email in
to you. I feel as though since my range was both manufactured and sold during the recall time period,
that it is a gallery model as is listed in the recall, and that the problem that I am having is a known safety
issue that the recall is addressing that my model should be added to that recall # 09-333. I am asking for
this consideration from your office. Thank you for your consideration.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On September 7th, 2015 I purchased a Waring Pro electric deep fryer, model # DF280, through Amazon.  After using the fryer twice over the past few days I decided to clean it yesterday.  Following the manufacturers instructions I took it apart, drained the oil into a used oil container, and placed the lid, oil tank, and large frying basket with attached handle into my dishwasher.  The basket and handle went on the top rack, the other parts went on the bottom rack.  The dishwasher was then run on a regular cycle.  Later that evening, in preparation for making chicken cutlets for dinner, I reassembled the fryer, filled it with oil and set it to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.  When the oil was ready I took the large fryer basket from the top rack of the dishwasher and placed it into the hot oil.  Immediately water started pouring out of the handle (which later examination showed to be two-pieces screwed together and hollow) with much of it going directly into the hot oil.  This caused an oil explosion, splattering me and my kitchen with hot oil.  Fortunately I had the lid handy, and was able to use it as a shield to approach and then cover the spattering oil, then get the unit unplugged.  I received several 1st and 2nd degree burns to my arms and hands when this happened, my counter tops were a mess and dinner was ruined.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st and 2nd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances of water entering hot oil.

incident_description: Brand new electric range/oven used for approximately 12 days was preheated to 350 degrees.  I placed my casserole dish and pizza stone with mini pizzas in oven and began washing dishes.  Approximately 2-5 minutes later, I heard a very loud smashing sound.  When I turned around, I discovered that the interior glass of my oven door had shattered all over the inside of my oven.  The glass seemed to have almost exploded, as it reached my casserole dish on the top shelf and was all over the oven, even far in the back.  Nothing had touched the glass, nor had anyone been in contact with the oven while it was cooking, the glass broke seemingly for no reason.  This was very alarming, as I have young children who could have been seriously injured from the broken glass if I had not been right there to immediately clean it up.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered oven glass) but no injuries occurred, though there was potential for harm to children.

The consumer stated that there is a feature on the unit where the oven can be set up to start at a different/later time. When I leaned in to see what it was I realized there was a fire behind the button panel where the circuit board is, I ran to turn the breaker off, so I could toss water around if need be. After a few grueling minutes of waiting for someone to reply back to me, someone finally did, only to tell me that they couldn't help find out if there is a recall on the device that would have burned my house down! Products break all the time but they don't catch on fire! I have looked online and this has happened to many people! This product needs to be recalled before someone gets hurt because this could have been so much worse if I hadn't notice the tiny flicker of light reflecting on the glass top!

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire Professional Electric Range in March 2014 Brand New. Model # FPEF3081MFA. While using my oven, the front right stove top burner got hot. I initially though it was just residual heat from using my over - I had been roasting tomatoes all morning, as my stove top was not turned on and I was not using it. I finished what I was doing and clean up and turned the oven off and left it to cool and left my house. I came home a few hours later and the burner was red hot and obviously "on" even though the controls said it was off. My first instinct was to try the controls and see if it would turn off - I turned the burner on and was able to set the size to the large burner and saw the whole thing beginning to get hot, then I turned it off, the large burner turned off but the center stayed on and HOT. I unplugged my range and waited several hours for everything to cool. When I plugged it back in the front right burner turned on immediately and began to get HOT. I researched this issue and found that similar products were recalled for this same issue, but upon contacting the manufacturer learned my model number was not included and they were unwilling to budge. This malfunction could have very easily caused injury or a fire and my entire unit cannot even be used until I get it fixed - even then I worry that whatever caused this will happen again with a different burner.

I smelled an electrical fire, opened the panel on the dishwasher, and the main board was on fire.
The capacitors c301 and c302 burned through black. There are also black burn marks on the board around r301 and r302.
If I had not been home to stop it, we could have lost the house, and Oregon would be on fire now. We are on extreme fire alert here, and I live in the forest.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire in the dishwasher, which could have led to severe consequences if not addressed, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
RE:  heating element on my Cuisinart Toaster Oven Model T0B-40.
I was utilizing this product in normal day-to-day use.  I noticed the heating element expanding and forming a balloon on one area of the element.  I was concerned it would explode.  When I researched this online, I found numerous complaints regarding this issue.  I called Cuisinart customer service and they stated they could do nothing as the toaster ovenlwas out of warranty. (This is true.)  I then spoke with a supervisor to voice my concerns over the hazardous nature of this issue.  She explained to me I could write a letter to the corporate office.  I admit I did not do so.  Since I had researched the issue and found many complaints about the heating element, I knew Cuisinart was not interested.  Most of the other consumers did not get results when contacting Cuinsart.

Some examples when googling this issue:
http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-TOB-40-Classic-Toaster-Broiler/product-reviews/B004JMZGM2

http://www.jasonlrobbins.com/2014/04/cuisinart-toaster-ovens-consumer-liability-customer-service-conundrum/

And from your very own website:
http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1374338
justification: The heating element showed signs of potential failure but no actual injury occurred, and similar incidents were reported by other users.

incident_description:
Samsung fridge has design defect in support system for shelves in main fridge area.
This is a french door fridge with shelves on left and right side.  Both outer edge shelf holders have more than adequate fasteners to hold shelves, but design flaw exists in that the center rail only has two screws, one on top and one at the bottom.

Any first year mechanical engineering student (and as I am a registered electrical engineering EIT working in the fire and forensics field) would be able to figure out that this support structure is not enough for the product.  This possesses a major flaw in that the one and only screw at the top penetrates the substructure by only about 1/8".  This creates a safety hazard when heavy items are placed (such as gallons of milk or other liquids) on the shelves, as the upper screw will pull out and allow the items on the shelves to fall out onto the unsuspecting child, without touching those items.  This can be and WILL be very dangerous.  What was Samsung's response to this? to place a screw (for those that complained) that was only another 1/8" longer.  So after another 6 months of use on the product, that screw has started to pull out as well, creating the deadly scenario again.

Even after making Samsung aware that their fix was not sufficient (as the center rail needed at least the same if not more support than the outer rails), they refused to correct the situation.
justification: The design defect poses a safety hazard with potential for injury, especially to children, due to falling heavy items.

incident_description: The center pane of glass in the oven door shattered while the home was unoccupied for a week or so.
justification: The glass shattered but no one was present, so there was no injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Hamilton Beach percolator model 40622 at Bed Bath and Beyond.  We have been using it for about a year.  This morning he set up the coffee to perk.  A short while later the glass bulb at the top exploded and shot coffee and glass all over the kitchen.  Fortunately nobody was hurt but it took almost 2 hours to clean up the mess.  This product is not safe.
justification: The incident involved an exploding coffee pot causing a mess but no injuries, indicating a minor severity with unlikely recurrence based on the description.

incident_description: Philippe Richard 8-Quart Pressure Cooker, Aluminum, manufactured on 1/2014, after only a few uses it exploded, gasket failed. I was burned on my abdomen, going to the docter in the morning. This product has a lot of complaints on several websites.
justification: The pressure cooker exploded, causing burns that required medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This evening I had a large glassware baking pan explode in my kitchen upon removal from the oven. This baking dish exploded in my boyfriend's hands leaving glass chunks, shards, slivers and dust all over my kitchen- stovetop, inside of oven door and oven, countertops and floor. 

The Anchor Hocking website, on the Bakeware Facts page, states:
      ...  these pieces generally lack sharp edges when it does break, resulting in a lower likelihood of severe cuts from the broken glass.

        Likewise, having the bakeware break in a safer manner by breaking into pieces generally lacking sharp edges and shards is a priority.

The bake ware broke into pieces and shards that did contain sharp edges- some pieces were large, long, and sharp. Other pieces were very small and sharp, including a glass dust that I had to wipe and vaccum surfaces several times to remove. I am still  not confident that I can safely walk barefoot in my kitchen or use my countertops for food preparation.

We have owned this bakeware for about three years, and have always followed the safety instructions during use.

My family is on a limited budget- I had to throw away the food we were preparing.  This product caused an inconvenience, as far as dinner was concerned. But far more concerning is the safety issue this product poses. Luckily my boyfriend has quick reflexes and did not sustain any physical injuries.

I have sent an email to consumer@anchorhocking.com with this same description of the incident
justification: The incident involved a glassware explosion causing significant mess and potential hazard, but no injuries were sustained.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore model 790 drop-in electric range. The complete model number is 790.46769901.  This morning at 11:00 am, my wife, daughters and I were in the kitchen. Suddenly the entire outer oven door glass exploded outward without warning. The majority of the broken glass landed within the two foot radius in front of the oven. Some small pieces of glass flew as far as eight feet, and onto the four of us. Nobody was injured, other than a couple of small cuts on my feet.

The rangetop and oven were both last used approximately fourteen hours prior to the incident. The oven is clean and well-maintained, and nobody in the home can recall any sort of impact against the door. 

While researching a replacement part for the range, I found many complaints about exploding outer door glass with the Kenmore model 790 stove.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts, which qualifies as an injury, and there are multiple reports of similar incidents with this model.

incident_description:
We have a set of Anchor Hocking Coffee glasses with handles  that we've used for the past couple of years without incident.   Tonight,  after I poured boiling water into the glass mugs which had tea bags in them, one of the glasses violently exploded.  I was not wearing shoes at the time and our kitchen floor is slate, so I instinctively jumped back more than a yard to avoid injury.  The shards of glass were large and jagged.  They flew several feet across the room.  I stood frozen and called for my husband to help me.  Fortunately I was wearing glasses and was not injured.  

This was a very traumatic experience for me.  What if this had happened to a child or an elderly person?  This glass did not break, IT EXPLODED!
justification: The glass exploded violently, but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for similar incidents with improper glass use.

incident_description: Kenmore Ultra Wash Dishwasher Stock no. 17003   Type 5750-0  Serial no. FR4502704  Model no. 665.1733400 This is the second time we have had an electrical short in the front of this model.  Both times we we're washing dishes and noticed an "electrical" smell.  There was a short in the dishwasher, but it had not gotten to the point that a fire started nor had the breaker tripped.
justification: Electrical short occurred but no fire or injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
We are writing to lodge a complaint about our defective LG refrigerator and express serious concerns about the safety of refrigerators that LG continues to sell.

Refrigerator Information

Refrigerator Model: LFX31925ST/01
Serial Number: 205KRGG24751
Purchase Date: July 31,.2012 (sold by J&R) 
Delivery Date: August 9, 2012 (delivered by HDS)

Refrigerator  Defect

On or about January 22,2015, after owning this refrigerator for only 2.5 years - it suddenly created an extremely strong odor of burning in our kitchen. It smelled like plastic melting. We were extremely concerned about the risk of fire.

We called our local appliance repair provider to investigate. There was a burn mark approximately 3 inches long inside the refrigerator -- see attached pictures. The inside of the refrigerator was also completely permeated by the burn smell.

The appliance repair provider told us this created a serious fire hazard because the foam was melting, and that the defect could have created an electrical fire. He also said that the refrigerator could not be repaired and it would be dangerous to continue to use it. We were concerned about the fire risk, and purchased a new refrigerator.

In researching how to contact LG to request a refund, it came to our attention that this is a known issue. In reading about the Connie McLennan v: LG Electronics USA case, it appears that this is the same or a similar defect. We are troubled that LG would continue to sell refrigerators with this dangerous defect. 

We did contact LG and were routed to a "proof of purchase" upload portal.  We tried to upload documentation into this portal, but the link would not accommodate the number of pictures we had of the issue. As a result, we are sending you this letter to document our experience with the defective product. 

We are requesting compensation from LG.  Please see attached documentation.

Requested Compensation

Refund for my defective refrigerator:                $2,947.41
Refund for my service call:                               $    80.00
Refund for the estimated cost of spoiled food:  $  500.00
                                                                      ---------
                                                                     $3,527.41
 
Thank you for your consideration.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(12/2014) The consumer stated that the microwave came on by itself. The consumer turned it off. About two hours later, the unit came back on again. 

(12/2014) The consumer contacted the firm. A technician came out. A part was replaced behind the number pad.

(07/2015) The consumer stated that they started using the microwave again. She smelled burning wires. The consumer unplugged the unit. The consumer tried to use it one more time after that but the microwave did not work.

(08/2015) The consumer contacted the firm. A technician was sent out. The consumer was advised that all the working parts have to be replaced.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned multiple times, including turning on by itself and emitting a burning smell, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(08/20/20150) The consumer stated that that the oven door was in the down position. He walked around the door to get something off of the counter. He bumped his left leg on the left corner of the door which cause a laceration.

The consumer went to the emergency room at Waccamaw Hospital Center in Murrells Inlet, S.C.

incident_description: Kenmore oven model 9500 2102 set at 350 kicked onto broil and could not be shut off without pulling breaker.  Smoked profusely as there was food in oven which caught fire when oven door was opened.  This is the third time for such an incident, twice having been remedied with replacement of sensor #10181986. incident_description:
This caller is reporting that his wife started the dishwasher purchased in 2004 on the evening of August 9th, 2015 but then twenty to thirty minutes it began smoking at which time she called for her husband.
He came to the kitchen, saw black smoke coming from the right top corner of the unit where he states that the circuit board is location.
He tried to open the front door of the dishwasher but although the door was opening the dishwasher kept running at which time he turned the breaker off to cut power to the unit.
The caller and his wife opened windows and door to rid their home of the smoke/fire odor then moved the dishwasher to their garage.
The caller is reporting this incident as a severe fire hazard due to the overheating being a potential for eventual fire.

There are no injuries being reported.

He contacted the manufacturer a few times today at 1 (800) 479-6351 using option# 6, he did not obtain the name of any of the manufacturer contacts but was provided with case# [REDACTED].

He was offered an after purchase 10% discount on a new dishwasher but due to the hazard with his dishwasher being fire he doesn't believe this to be a fair offer.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher smoking and potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:

There were no injuries.

The consumer contacted the Sears Repair Department and was advised that he would have to pay for the service call and glass for the oven door.
justification: The oven door glass exploded but there were no injuries, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
(08/18/2015) The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in the wash cycle . It was set for 37 minutes. Halfway in the cycle, the consumer noticed water in the floor at the bottom of the unit. The consumer turns the unit off and opened the door. 

The consumer called the place of purchased who sent a technician out. The technician stated that the heating element got so hot that it melted the bottom of the tub.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing water leakage and damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We were using our Samsung electric range to cook pizza on a 425-degree setting. With no warning, there was a "pop" sound and flames appeared coming from behind the range. I used a fire extinguisher to smother the flames, and after it was out I contacted the manufacturer. They scheduled a service call, but the technician said I would have to pay for the parts. He disassembled the range, and it was clear that it was an electrical fire.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with no reported injuries, and such events are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: Lower oven rack fell while baking a turkey breast because the oven cavity has expanded and the cooking rack no longer extends over the cavity lip far enough to consistently secure the rack when any amount of weight is placed on the rack. Upper oven cavity of this range still works as designed.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard (falling oven rack) that could lead to injury if someone is nearby when it occurs, but no injury is mentioned in the description.

incident_description: Purchased GE Monogram Refrigerator model ZIPP360NHASS. The shelves have razor sharp points which have caused cuts to a family member's arm. It is dangerous to simply reach into the refrigerator. We contacted customer service. They promised to send out the safer shelves ASAP (we haven't received them yet). I find it incredible that they actually ship this product with shelves that are so obviously dangerous when they supposedly have safer replacement shelves available.
justification: The description mentions cuts to a family member's arm, indicating an injury, and the dangerous design suggests a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The 2 original manufacturer-supplied light bulbs at the ceiling of the refrigerator have burned holes through the plastic interior.  This is a definite fire danger and a compromise of the cooling system.  I have  unscrewed the bulbs so they will not come on, but the damage to the refrigerator is in need of repair.
