Model: LGHN2844MFO
justification: The incident involves a fire danger and damage to the refrigerator, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Sharp microwave purchased December 2014 from an online location for home products store.
The caller is reporting that from the beginning of December 2014 purchase, his microwave door did not close properly, the manufacturer was contacted then sent repair techs to the home May 2015 and repair was completed.

In July 2015 the caller's wife informed him that the microwave had begun tripping the breakers and having a rubber burning odor.

She contacted the manufacturer who sent another tech to their home around July 26th, 2015.  The tech took pictures and checked connection to be sure it was plugged in properly.

The tech is scheduled to return to the caller' home to take more pictures, check installation and plug in connections.

The caller is reporting these incidents as a fire safety hazard.

The caller is stating that he would like to purchase a new model with manufacturer voucher assistance since this microwave is less than one  year old.

There are no injuries being reported.
justification: The microwave has a history of malfunctions including a burning odor and tripping breakers, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description: My GE Profile dishwasher eas in use last evening and began smoking. I immediately opened the dishwasher door and turned the electrical switch controlling power to this appliance to the off position. After the smoke cleared, I was able to see that the top of the door had melted.
justification: The dishwasher began smoking and the door melted, indicating a significant incident but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Coffee was so hot it burned and blistered lips. Have had keurig for a year and a half. It did not spray out of the machine, was just so hot it scalded lips.
justification: The coffee caused burns and blisters, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: My mini Keurig is spraying hot water/coffee out of the machine.  It burned me the other day.
justification: The incident caused a burn injury, and the description suggests it is a recurring issue with the machine.

incident_description:
Oster Toaster Oven Model # TSSTTVVG01

Toaster Oven had erratic toasting behavior, usually toasted too much in its previous usage.
The last time used the oven was turned the off setting, but continued to heat anyway.  When re-entering the kitchen I witnessed the handle of the oven began to melt away from the door and caught the handle before it was able to reach the countertop, immediately unplugged the unit and removed it from service.
justification: The toaster oven malfunctioned and overheated, but no injury occurred as the issue was caught and addressed in time.

incident_description: I bought a Kenmore electric range (model 790) in August of 2010.   On August 31, 2015, the front oven glass door exploded throwing small glass pieces everywhere. I was just cooking some chicken in the oven at 350 degrees.  I was lucky enough to not have been in front of the oven at the time.  Had I been, I would have had bad injuries.  I was also lucky in that my dog that usually lies in front of the oven when I am in the kitchen was not there either.  Had he been, he would have had major injuries.  I tried talking with someone at the Sears national number listed on the back of the manual for my oven only to get told they did not know how to handle such a thing and that I had to call my local store.  After several tries to get a person on the phone here in Meridian, MS, I could never get anyone.  I ended up having to go to the store in person.  Unfortunately, no one there could help other than to replace the oven door which I would not want to do since this is NOT a normal wear and tear situation that I should be responsible to have to pay for.  I found out online that the oven doors are apparently being made with inferior glass doors now and that hundreds of people are experiencing an exploding glass oven door. I feel, as others do, that this problem is due to a manufacturing defect and should be compensated by Sears.  As I mentioned to you already, such an incident as this could have severely injured me or anyone else that could have been in front of that oven door when it exploded.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing a hazardous situation, but no injuries occurred. The description mentions that similar incidents are happening to hundreds of people, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I purchased my Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator (model number 795.77546600, serial number 608KR00389) about 7 years ago. I had called the Sears  parts service center in the morning to replace the small Allen screws that hold the bottom mounted freezer handle in place. I had removed the handle to clean the surface of the freezer door and the handle itself, and was hoping the new screws would close the small gap between the handle and the door where the two pieces connect, as my daughters shirt had caught on this the week before and ripped. As I went to reattach the handle, it slipped slightly in my hand, and the next thing I knew, there was blood all over my kitchen floor. The ends of this handle where it tapers to meet the door are actually sharper than the knives in my home, and this handle barely touched me but went through my hand like butter. I now have a 2" gash across the base of my thumb where the handle sliced my hand open. I would be happy to send photos of the gash, my daughters ripped shirt, and the ends of this handle that have been doing the damage.
justification: The incident resulted in a 2-inch gash, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) since the sharp handle design poses a recurring risk.

incident_description:
My Kitchenaid oven (Model #KESC300HBL4; Serial #IML0614050) was purchased in 2003 and has worked well during the time we owned it.  Two weeks ago (August 20, 2015) the heating element arced and sparked and broke in two pieces near the back corner.  I found a replacement heating element on Amazon, being sold by Virginia Service Supply Co., of Goochland, VA and received that element and connected it.  All seemed to be working fine until Saturday Sept 4, 2015, when, out of nowhere the interior glass window popped and shattered while my wife was cooking bacon at just 350 degrees.  A glass chunk about 2" long and 1/2" wide along with a lot of fragments broke out and landed in the oven.

It seems an odd coincidence that both issues happened within 2 weeks of each other and I am shocked that the glass broke at just 350 degrees.  Many of the web reports that I have read refer to this issue when they are using the Self Cleaning function.
justification: The incident involved the oven's glass shattering, but no injury was reported, and similar issues are documented in web reports.

incident_description:
I have a 9-cup Cuisinart Food Processor with a steel metal cutting blade. Where the rivets hold the blade to the spindle mechanism there were apparently stress cracks. When using the processor, a sharp piece of metal, about 4mm wide broke off and ending up in the batter of some scones. I bit down on the metal shard, and was able to spit it out before swallowing it.  When I examined the underside of the blade, I see that almost all of the other rivets had similar stress cracks. 

I called Cuisinart and it seemed to know all about this problem. Also, all over the internet, especially on Amazon reviews, there are reports of these stress cracks. I found these after the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in a metal shard being bitten on, which constitutes an injury, and the widespread reports indicate a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: One of the burners remains on high and will not turn off.  Even after resetting the main kitchen breaker, the element still comes back on high.  Major fire and safety hazard.  This has happened on at least 5 occasions.
justification: The burner remaining on high poses a major fire and safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the interior lights in the refrigerator section stay on after the door is closed. The light fixture holds two light bulbs.

The consumer stated that the plastic diffuser on the light fixture melted from the heat of the light bulbs. The consumer stated that the diffuser melted and fell down to the back. The melted diffuser and its heat also melted a plastic tab that holds the diffuser into the light fixture.

The consumer stated that there is burning odor in the refrigerator. The consumer stated that some of the melted plastic from the diffuser is stuck onto the light bulbs.

The consumer stated that the heat from the bulbs spoiled the food in the top shelf of the refrigerator.

The consumer has not contacted a technician or the manf yet. The consumer has removed the light bulbs from the fixture. 

The unit does not appear to be under any recalls.
justification: The incident involves property damage (melted plastic, spoiled food) and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The Maytag dishwasher (mine is MDBH979SAM1) manufactured by Whirlpool has a design flaw.  The same design was used in multiple models from 2010 to 2015.  Generally the only effect is that the dishwasher stops working but sometimes the flexible circuit which connects the external control panel (with the buttons) and the internal control panel (the brains) in the door corrodes in a way that it heats up and in some cases causes fires).  This defect exists in 10's of thousands if not 100's of thousands of units.  Whirlpool is aware (phone 1-866-931-7384) and has redesigned the part but will not acknowledge the flaw (due to the cost exposure).  So many of these parts are defective that the part is on national backorder for many/most models.  The important point is that this not only causes the dishwasher to malfunction but can cause a fire.
justification: The dishwasher's design flaw can cause fires, which is a severe incident, but the description does not mention injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Normal load of dishes.  At approximately the end of wash cycle, black  smoke started coming from steam vent.  The smoke smelled like an electrical fire. I was able to turn off circuit at fuse box before fire burned beyond the interior of the front door of the dishwasher. Before turning off power, I could hear electrical arcing inside the front panel. Had I not been standing next to the dishwasher when this began, I expect that the fire would have continued.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire in the dishwasher, which was contained without injury but had potential for greater damage if not addressed promptly.

incident_description: On June 24th, 2014 I attempted to use the Soda Stream Source Machine for the first time.  It was fresh out of the box and I followed all instructions perfectly.  The machine blew up in my hand and caused a high impact contusion and severe nerve damage that led to dystrophy of my left hand nerves.  I have prepared to file a law suit against the company and would like to offer the opportunity to anyone who is interested to join me in a class action suit.  Please contact [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in severe nerve damage and dystrophy, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Such events are rare, as indicated by the low frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: My husband and I was serving stew into bowls, And while he was holding one that i was putting stew into it exploded.  NO one was hurt but the stew was ruined the glass went everywhere.  I am really surprised no body was hurt.
justification: The bowl exploded causing a mess but no one was hurt, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: While sitting in my living room, I heard the microwave running.  It should not have been used at that point so I checked in the kitchen and found it running with nothing inside.  My children were present and denied touching the microwave.  I assumed it was an accident, stopped the microwave and forgot about it.  Last night around 3 a.m. I awoke to a beeping sound.  I checked the kitchen and once again found the microwave running with nothing inside.  It was very hot and smelled of an electrical fire.  I turned off and unplugged the microwave.
justification: The microwave was running empty and became very hot with a smell of electrical fire, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Twice in 24 hours, my 9 year old (with special needs) and my 5 year old retrieved ice from the ice maker and shards of plastic came out with the ice. My 9 year old son came and brought the larger pieces of plastic to me. The 5 year old emptied her water and ice out...when I asked her why, she told me that there was something floating in her water. I then took pictures of the ice and plastic because I realized that it was pieces of the ice maker itself that was being broken up and dispensing out with the ice.

I called Sears to check for any product recalls to no avail. They told me they would send a technician out on September 28 to check my problem.

I feel this is a huge safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved plastic shards dispensed with ice, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is possible as it happened twice in 24 hours.

incident_description: I was using the ikea coffee maker and was pressing the plunger down when it burst on the bottom of the glass pot right where the metal stand was touching the pot. The glass from the pot hit me and coffee sprayed all over the front of me. I have a blister from the burn on my right hip.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn blister, indicating an injury, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description: Because of loose oven racks in a KitchenAid dual fuel range (model KDRS505XSS01) it was replaced, after quite a bit of effort and cajoling on my part and after paying for a service call and a $250 fee. I recently discovered that Whirlpool corporation which made the KitchenAid range has recalled [REDACTED] ranges for the same problem. It would seem that Whirlpool has been aware of this problem but still has not recalled other KitchenAir ranges. The defect caused the racks to dislodge when pulled out of the oven. Luckily my wife managed to partially catch the turkey as she slid the rack out, avoiding a serious burn and I was happy at the time that we got a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a defect causing oven racks to dislodge, but no injury occurred as the wife managed to partially catch the turkey, avoiding a serious burn.

incident_description: We had an older Model Downdraft model range and it had relatively thick doors that were well insulated.  We recently had to buy a newer model and the door is about 1/2 as thick and not well insulated.  One of the instructions for the new range was to do an initial burn in at 400 degrees for an hour.  The door got very hot and would have burned a child.  (it almost burned me.)  I think it is too bad that a company would sacrifice safety like this when older models did not have the same issue.  The technology exist to better insulate oven doors.  It seems like companies should use it and keep kitchens much safer.
justification: The door got very hot and almost burned the user, indicating a high likelihood of injury, especially to children, with frequent use.

incident_description:
I am writing to let you know about an ongoing problem we have been having with our GE range, model number JBP24WOH2WW, oven element melting and catching fire. This has now happened twice. The first time, August 25, 2011, the element, which was original to the model, caught fire (electrical fire--sparks). We called 9-1-1 and turned off power to the range and the fire put itself out. The coating of the element had melted off in a bent area and that is where the fire originated. The element was replaced and lasted for four years. A few days ago I started smelling a burning smell and then a smell of soy sauce (which I was not using). Yesterday, August 28, 2015, the replacement element started shooting sparks, catching fire. We caught it much sooner this time and shut off the oven.

We have also had to replace all of the surface elements of the range. It seems this model has an ongoing problem with uneven heating leading to electrical fires. We have not heard of any recall, but wonder if others have the same problem and if it will eventually be recalled.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an oven element catching fire twice, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The recurrence suggests a likely ongoing issue.

incident_description:
I have a Black & Decker oven, model #CT0650.  It recently gave me an electric shock by just touching the handle.  I unplugged it immediately   When my husband came home from work, he tested it with a meter and found that the outside of the oven was ÃÂlive.ÃÂ  I contacted Black and Decker and received a phone call from [REDACTED].  He said there was nothing they could do because it was out of warranty but offered me a discount on a new one. I found this response very irresponsible.  This is a dangerous issue.  A discount or replacement was the least of my concerns.

(photos) Here is what we found after taking the side panel off the oven.  My husband, an electrician, believes the terminal block, which has melted, is underrated for this oven.  Without taking it apart further, his theory is, that during the melting process, one or more of the screws may have ÃÂfloatedÃÂ down making contact with the metal frame of the oven.  Even if his theory is incorrect, this should be of concern to someone!  There were no signs that this melting was accurring   No smell or smoke and the oven was operating as it should.  Even though the shock hurt tremendously, my ears popped and I had chest pain for approximately an hour, had I NOT been shocked, this melting could have continued without our knowledge and turned into a fire.  Also, it was fortunate that it was me that got shocked, as my husband has epilepsy and who knows how he could have been affected.  We have used the oven responsibly.  It has never been dropped or abused in any way.  It has never even been moved from itÃÂs present location.  It has always worked well and weÃÂve been pleased with it otherwise.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe electric shock causing chest pain and other symptoms, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the unexpected nature of the malfunction without prior signs.

incident_description:
(07/27/2015) The consumer was blending leaves in the blender. She turned the blender off to taste the mixture. She took a taste with a spoon but got distracted and left the spoon in the blender. The consumer turned the blender back on and immediately the glass blender shattered. 

The consumer went down to get someone to take pictures of the blender and noticed that the spoon was mixed with the mixture and the broken glass.

The consumer thinks that the metal blades came in contact with the spoon.

The consumer stated that there was a tiny sliver of glass in her neck. No medical attention was required.

The consumer stated that there is no safety feature shut off on the unit.

Also, the recipe section on page 22 and page 2 of the brochure given conflicting information about adding ice.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor injury (tiny sliver of glass in neck) but did not require medical attention, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the incident resulted from a common user error (leaving a spoon in the blender) combined with a lack of safety features.

incident_description:
This happening in the early morning. Microwave was beeping. An error code 5E or SE was flashing in the display. I opened the door and the tray was very warm and scorched like it was recently used. I asked my mother if she had used the microwave (she has a profound hearing loss and would not have noticed the beeping noise without her hearing aid and cochlear implant and since this was early morning, she did not have them in) and she replied no. There was no response to the touch pad. I unplugged the unit and plugged it back in and the display returned to normal (normal for when the power has been interrupted), then a few seconds later it started beeping again. I unplugged the unit and left it unplugged. I feel there may be a concern of this condition posing a possible fire hazard.

Samsung SMH9187B
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred; the issue was resolved by unplugging the unit, indicating a possible but not certain fire hazard.

incident_description:
After moving into my new home (previous owner left kitchen appliances, including Samsung refrigerator M# RS2630SH/XAA, SN# 006242BY900765P), my 8 year old son burned his hand on the refrigerator panel. The fridge is a side-by-side model, where the doors come together at a panel that runs up the middle of the fridge. This panel runs intermittently hot, varying from extremely hot, to excessively warm. The left side of the unit also runs warm; however, this does not pose a safety issue as the unit is not designed for hands to enter at that point.

The burn required medical attention that was dealt with at our home as both parents are medical professionals. It was a superficial burn and he did not sustain permanent damage. He was in a great deal of pain however. When I contacted Samsung to report the issue (ticket #4131899819) I was informed that Samsung would not be taking any action as the burn did not require medical intervention and no reimbursement was due to me since there were not medical expenses incurred. I find this very alarming as the refrigerator is clearly malfunctioning and my three children are at risk of injury every time the fridge is opened. I feel Samsung is not performing the required due diligence to determine if there is a malfunction that puts other users at risk.
justification: The incident resulted in a superficial burn requiring home medical attention, indicating an injury but no permanent damage.

incident_description:
We purchased the Kenmore Elite Electric Range from Sears in Nashua, NH.  Shortly after receiving this product, we realized that the top oven was not working properly and called the customer service department.  We were told to move the oven rack to the topmost position (foods cooked in this top oven were burning on the bottom and not cooking on the top).  After many calls back and forth to try and get the issue resolved, we got nowhere and eventually gave up.

Approximately one year ago, we noticed that the bottom racks on the larger, bottom oven seemed "loose".  After moving the racks around in the oven, thinking that perhaps they are designated as uppermost racks, bottom racks, etc., we weren't able to rectify the problem.  Again, a call was made to customer service and we were told that there was nothing they could do because the oven was out of warranty.  Within weeks of the first phone call, the racks would no longer fit in the oven.  The sides of the oven had expanded so much, that when you put a dish on the racks, it would collapse!  There were two incidents where hot liquids from the dish splashed up and burned my forearm and hands.  Phone calls to sears reporting the incidents were met again with no resolve whatsoever and only an offer to send a service technician out to look at the problem - at our expense.  We now have had to wrap aluminum foil around the sides of the racks and squeeze the rack into the side grooves.  This stabilizes the racks, but of course they now cannot be moved to remove food.  Sears has told me that the reason for the oven walls expanding may be due to using the self-clean feature of the appliance (this has been used one time and the problem did not start right after this was done)
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the forearm and hands from hot liquids due to oven rack failure, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I used the self cleaning mode on my Kenmore oven and set the time for 2 hours. This is the minimum amount of time I could choose, the Max was 4 hours.  After about 1hour and 30 minutes, I noticed that the top of my oven door was melting. I pushed the stop button, the "door locked" button blinked and I was able to open the door and stop the clean cycle. The oven got so hot, it melted the plastic on the top of the door which ran down the tin on the inside of the oven and burnt the gasket that seals the oven when it is closed.  I am afraid of what would have happened if I had not noticed it melting.  I called Sears and Kenmore and was transferred numerous times but neither of them were any help.  They want to charge me a service call fee and have a technician come look at it.  I do not feel I should have to pay a fee when their product is defective and unsafe.  I want to te report this so it can be put in to see if it should be recalled.  I checked and it is not recalled yet.  I would hate for someone else to have this happen to them.  I am afraid to use my oven because of the plastic that has melted into the inside.  Also, if we replace the parts and clean the oven again, I am afraid the issue will not be address properly and it will happen again. Maybe next time, the whole thing may catch fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused melting and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The viking dishwasher I purchased caught on fire and burned up my kitchen before the fire department got there. Model VDB325SS
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and caused significant damage to the kitchen, but no injuries or deaths were mentioned.

incident_description:
On 8/28/15, while using the oven on my Samsung FTQ3531WUX/XAA electric range, I heard a loud pop and had flames shooting up about 18" from the back of the stove.  Had I not been within 5' of the range, I have no doubt that my house would have burned.  Later I removed the back panel behind the printed circuit and saw that much of the plastic had started on fire and melted.

There were 6 people in the house at the time, including a 3y/o and 8 mo. child.
justification: Flames and potential fire hazard occurred, but no injuries or deaths were reported despite the presence of multiple people, including children.

incident_description:
There are 4 issues with my Electrolux ICON cooktop E36GC70FSS1

1) Big pots come so close to the knobs in the middle of the cooktop, that you have sometimes no chance but to be too close to the knobs. This is not only a design error, the knobs start melting once a big hot pot or pan like a canning pot gets close to them. 3 of my 5 knobs have burn marks by now (2.5 years), one needs to be replaced as it melted to a point where it was deformed. Suddenly, I saw the knob steam and had I not been right there, it would have probably caught fire. Scary with a gas cooktop!

2) If you clean the knobs while leaving them on the cooktop and you don't watch it carefully, suddenly you might have turned one half on so that gas starts streaming in your kitchen without any warning. There is no light or off-switch ÃÂ dangerous!

3) Sometimes the burners don't start right away when turning them on. So after a few tries, they suddenly turn on with a big flame and poof. I expect this by now, but easy to burn your fingers holding a pot or pan.

4) If you take the knobs off for cleaning, food crumbs might fall in the holes below the knobs and there are little tightening metal parts within the knobs that might fall out by taking the knobs off the top for cleaning. Those are considered part of the knob and it won't work without them. Once one is lost, you need to replace the entire knob for over $30...., never mind the hassle to find the part number of the installed cooktop, which is right under it. No fun if the cooktop is installed in a drawer cabinet.

The worst of all is, that Electrolux ignores these issues. I found other reviews for this product on Amazon and they are stating the same issues.
justification: The incident describes potential hazards like melting knobs and gas leaks, which could lead to injury or fire, but no actual injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
My Cuisinart  12 -cup Grind and Brew  coffee maker is used in my home to make one pot of coffee a day. I got it for Christmas in 2012. Today, on Aug. 29, 2015, the coffee maker overheated and wires started burning. Thankfully we were near the coffee maker and noticed it before something bad happened. 
I left the burner on for several hours, but that was no reason for the coffee maker to become a fire hazard.
justification: The coffee maker overheated and wires started burning, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Dishwasher started on fire during normal operation.  Sparks, flames, smoke from the control panel, behind the controller buttons.  Stopped when hit the on/off button.  Incident date August 30, 2015.  No damage beyond the appliance itself.

Bosh SHU3302UC/U11, FD 8005 170318, purchased from Fred's Appliance, Spokane, WA June 25, 2000.

We never received any notice of the recall.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was stopped without injury or damage beyond the appliance itself.

incident_description:
We own a Kenmore Range, model #790.92803010 purchased 16 months ago from Sears. Yesterday while my wife was baking the outer layer of glass on the oven door exploded. Wife & family thought it was a gun going off. Oven door was closed & for no known reason (no impact or movement at the time & a regular 350 degrees cooking temp) door exploded showering the kitchen & my wife, daughter & children in glass! My wife called me in a panic, she had cuts to her legs from glass around the ankles (lucky it was a cooler day & she was wearing longer pants). She was terrified & upset, we have younger children in the house down to a 2 year old & it is very lucky that he or any of our other children were not in front of the range at the time of the incident!

We are now very concerned regarding the future safety of this product if we have it repaired. After this happened we researched the Kenmore product online & found numerous incidents of the glass exploding, shattering or breaking! What concerns us & shocks us more is that there has never been a safety recall issued on this product & Sears just wants to sell an extended warranty on the product to get more money & are not concerned regarding the safety of this product!

What is our best course of action regarding this issue? Obviously I am concerned for my families safety if I have the product repaired but on the same note cannot afford to run out & spend $1000 on a replacement range! We want a replacement Range from Kenmore that doesn't have this issue!
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts to the legs) and could have been worse, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported similar incidents.

incident_description:
heating up soup in microwave.  Microwave turned off.  Opened door, microwave turned on (lights and turntable rotated) closed door. Opened door again because I am an idiot and same thing happened.  Unplugged microwave for 10 minutes and replugged in - microwave turned on again when door was opened.
Not sure if I was microwaved or not but continuing to eat dessert first just in case.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but there was no injury reported, only a potential hazard.

incident_description: We bought our house in April 2015 with all brand-new appliances, including a Samsung gas range and oven. A little over a week ago, as I was unloading our dishwasher, I moved a tray from the cabinet next to the oven and tapped the right edge of the exposed glass pane that covers the front of the oven. I heard a little click and then the entire piece of glass began cracking and falling apart into many tiny pieces. We had not used the over in over a week, so temperature was not a contributing factor. As the appliance is brand new and still covered under warranty, we expected that Samsung would respond quickly to correct this problem at no cost to us, but they are claiming that it is "physical damage" and therefore not covered. It is extremely frustrating as I have been doing research on this problem (see linked article - http://www.abc2news.com/homepage-showcase/experts-explain-when-why-tempered-glass-can-randomly-explode) and understand that it is a manufacturing defect - therefore definitely would fall under Samsung's responsibility.
justification: The incident involved property damage (glass cracking) but no injury, and the likelihood is unlikely as it's a rare manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
We have a Frigidaire electric smooth top slide-in range that is experiencing the same hazards listed in the recall for the smooth top cooktops.   The surface heating elements turn on unexpectedly by themselves, the elements heat at temperatures other than expected and then donÃÂt turn off as expected.   I feel this model / product is very unsafe as it will turn itself on and off at random times throughout the day.

The number on our range is FGES3065KFB and is not listed on your recall information.
justification: The range turns on and heats unexpectedly, posing a hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
(07/22/2015) The consumer stated that the microwave was not in use.  The outside glass in the door of the microwave shattered. The last time that the consumer used the unit was 7/21.

No injuries.


(07/22/2015) The consumer contacted the manufacturer to advised them of the incident. She was told that the unit was out of warranty. The consumer was also advised that her complaint could not be processed because she did not have all of the necessary information for the unit. She was advised and provide the manufacturer date.
justification: The microwave door shattered but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My kenmore appliance has done this two times now. I turn it on to a specified temperature, but instead it turns on, but only stays at the absolute highest temperature. It then refuses to turn off. Even when I flip the breaker off for hours, it will come back on. It has been both front burners. Last time it happened, someone worked on it and fixed one side. Now the other side has done it. I'm lucky that I pay attention, because if I had walked away it could have started a fire. Both times it was so hot I could barely stand to be even 4 feet from the stove. It is a complete fire hazard. I saw a recall on some sears stoves that did the same thing. Mine was not listed on the recall, so it is obviously affecting way more appliances than they are admitting too. Now I have to have my stove breaker flipped and I cannot use the stove at all until I get it fixed yet again.
justification: The appliance malfunction poses a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Purchased a Whirlpool Gas Range from Lowe's this week. Got it home and paid plumber to hook up. Used it for the first time today. Stove top there is no problem; however I baked some chicken in the oven and the oven glass door got sooooooooooo hot that you could be burned. I was not burned, because I was pre warned via internet. There is no warning of any kind about the hot door. Dangerous. Luckily I have no small children in my home, but a child could be seriously burned by this oven door. There are complaints on the Lowe's web site, but I discovered these after I had purchased the stove. While searching the internet to see if there was a replacement door available, I discovered others have the same issue with this stove.  There needs to be some kind of fix for this problem. I thought Whirlpool was always a good product, but I  am upset about this range. The item number is Model WFG320M0BS, Free Standing Whirlpool Smooth Surface Freestanding 4.8-cu ft Electric Range (Black-on-Stainless) (Common: 30-in; Actual: 29.875-in).  I guess I am stuck with this range, but I would hate to think because I did not report some child is going to be burned. One review stated that her child got second degree burns from this stove. Please do the right thing an investigate this problem. Maybe there is a way to correct this by issuing a better insulated replacement door.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous condition with the oven door getting excessively hot, posing a burn risk, and mentions a child suffering second-degree burns, indicating injury is likely.

incident_description:
On August 9th, I used MaxiMatic EWM-6171 Elite Platinum  3-Tray 2-1/2-Quart Buffet Server 
to warm-up meat in the tray. While I was placing trays to tray holder of the MaxiMatic EWM-6171 Elite Platinum  3-Tray 2-1/2-Quart Buffet Server, I cut my finger due to very sharp edge of tray holder.
The tray holder is about 21 x 13 x 3 inches hollow rectangle shape made out of stainless steel.
The thickness of the stainless steel is very thin, less than 1/64th inch and  it has very dangerous sharp edge along the short side of rectangular tray holder. 

The demo video was taken to demonstrate the sharpness of short side of edge.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger due to a sharp edge, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Our Samsung Convection Microwave oven model# MC17F808KD, has been repaired for the same issue  3 times in 1 year.  The device is selecting options ( i.e. temperature/time ) and turning the light on and off on it's own.  Recently it select a convection oven temperature of 350 degrees and turned the oven on, and we were not in the same room.  It would not stop heating, even after opening the door until it was unplugged.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on and heating without user input, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: August 24,2015, evening time. Not in use. Smell of fire. unplugged dishwasher. Checked electric next day. GFI plug blown out. No power or lights when plugged into good plug.
justification: There was a smell of fire and a blown GFI plug, indicating an electrical incident, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Today about 3:00 PM 8/3/2015.

I was using a Farberware serated kitchen knife to slice off a section of watermellon and without warning the plastic knife handle snapped.

I was extremely fortunate my hands were in the clear when this happened.

Photo link here.

http://i57.tinypic.com/2copg84.jpg!

While the knife set is old, it appears repeated exposure to dishwasher temps and soaps have caused the
handle plastic to deteriorate.

I have not notified the manufacturer as of yet..

I was not able to find a model # or serial #.  Knife was part of a set.  Assume the rest in the set use same handle material.
justification: The knife handle broke but no injury occurred, indicating a minor incident. The likelihood is possible given the age and deterioration of the knife set.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she had been experiencing problems with her gas range.  The range had melted the knobs because of the heating element and also leaked CO into her home. (8/5) She contacted the gas company and they advised her of the levels of CO that the range had caused and her gas was tuned off.  This incident has been ongoing since 2013 with the melted knobs, the retailer was contacted initially and she was told not to use the front burner.



8/5/15 The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that a service technician would be sent out at her expense.  However, caller explained to the company rep that the knobs were melted and the rep. informed her that there was nothing they could do about that issue.  Caller stated that the heating element is too close to the right burner.  She had moved the knobs around which caused all the knobs to melt.



Caller is concerned about the failure of this range and feels that she should be compensated by getting a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a gas range malfunction leading to CO leakage and melted knobs, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I own a Maytag over the range microwave. It was manufactured April 2005. It automatically started while my wife and two adult children were in the kitchen, then smoke began to billow out of the top. It was good that we were there close to unplug it for it may have started a fire in my home.
The model number in MMV1153AAW. I did not call Maytag because I have read complaints online from multiple people who did not receive any good answer from the manufacturer.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and produced smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We ran our dishwasher in the evening as usual. Woke up to a burning smell in the early morning. The heating element had not shut off as it is supposed to when the cycle completes and it had begun melting everything in the dishwasher. Thankfully we were home and were able to cut off the circuit before it caught fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: This incident has happened at least 15 times over the course of the last year.  Two large front burners will increase to high temperature even when set on another temperature.  These same two burners will not turn off when we turn the knob off.  We try turning it off and on back and forth and they will not turn off.  The only remedy is to cut power via the circuit breaker.  Even then sometimes when we turn the circuit breaker back on the elements are still on.  So we have to wait a while sometimes.  This has happened numerous times and we have burned food and nearly ruined some of our pots and pans.  It is a VERY serious fire hazard that jeopardizes my household.  Now I am forced to fix it due to the item being reported on a home inspection and the buyers not wanting to inherit a seriously defective stove.   Kenmore/Sears should recall and fix this item for free as many people have the same issue.
justification: The incident describes a serious fire hazard that has caused property damage and poses a risk of injury, with frequent occurrences (15 times in a year).

incident_description: I was using my 4 year old GE stove and smelled burning plastic smell.  The stove sudden shut off and was smoking coming from the rear of the stove.  I quickly shut off power to it.  After investigating I found that the 220V power cord had burned thru and melted the terminal block on the rear of the stove.  The insulation around this melted wire was dripping down by the gas line coming into the stove (as its a duel fuel stove).  This very likely could have caught fire or caused an gas explosion burning down my home!  There are recalls on similar duel fuel GE stoves to mine for similar safety issues, but my model is not included in those recalls.  Recall # 09-189,  I am a GE engineer and have a huge concern here.  I contacted GE and they just didn't care or seem to want to do anything about it.  Just been giving me the run around.   Due to the serious nature of this issue, I'm afraid to just repair the oven now as I don't know if that same thing would happen again.  Also concerned for others with the same stove.
justification: The incident involved a stove malfunction with potential for fire or explosion, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I had just preheated oven to 400 degrees, put frozen french fries in to bake. they  had only been in for about 8 minutes. I was at the sink in kitchen heard bunch of loud popping looked over at oven and saw sparks coming out from top behind the display clock area then lots of black smoke started pour out of back of oven husband ran over and went to shut off oven and grab fire extinguisher (while smoke alarms were going off) then breaker tripped  and oven shut off. we pulled oven out from wall and luckily breaker tripped and shut the oven off so we did not have to use the fire extinguisher and no one was hurt and house did not burn but the oven is ruined.  samsung has been awful to deal with hard to get a hold of.  been on hold so many times and has taken over 2 weeks just to get someone out here to look at. Samsung said they would only cover the cost of labor on this issue which is clearly a manufacture defect. samsung authorized service person came out and said this would be a $350-400 repair (parts only) samsung said they would cover labor which is around $165 I believe this is a major safety concern if I had been outside during this it could have started a house fire.  please look into this as samsung clearly doesn't care.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the oven, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
The interior lights in our Kenmore Elite refrigerator, Model 795.77544600, are continuously on.  The plastic cover for the two light bulbs has begun to melt, and the fixtures the light bulbs screw into has begun to scorch from the heat.  The food on the top shelf was warm to the touch.  
The plastic cover was removed, and the bulbs were unscrewed to the point where the bulbs went out. 
If the interior lights had remained on there no doubt would have been more damage done to the interior ceiling of the refrigerator, the light fixture housing/wiring, and all the food within the refrigerator.

Online there are many examples of this event occurring, but the Sears helpline person (name not available), at 800-479-6351 option 6, could not cite a recall or other company response to previous situations.
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator and risked food spoilage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: This morning, my Samsung microwave oven (model SMH9187ST) started on it's own three times without anyone's presence in the kitchen. I cannot confirm that it wasn't doing this while we slept. Initially the Stop/Clear button worked to turn it off, but the third time that did not work and the door had to be opened to stop the cooking cycle. It was started in the Popcorn mode each time (a function that we do not use). Shortly after the third ghost start the microwave display showed "-- 5E --" (or SE) and no buttons on the unit would function. Concerned about this continuing without anyone home and/or causing a fire hazard, the unit is now unplugged.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and started on its own, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore oven racks are falling  off the oven when in use, anything heavier than an empty plate will make rack collapse resulting in splattered food and burns.  When looking at the oven racks it may seem that the racks are not wide enough to fit on the shelves but with closer inspection the wall seemed to be bowed out.  There are many postings of this issue online.

This has been the issue since first purchased in 2007-2008.
justification: The incident involves oven racks collapsing, which can cause burns and splattered food, indicating potential for injury but no reported deaths.

incident_description:
Our Sears Kenmore Elite Double Oven gas range (Model# 790.78923002) caught on fire 2 times within the last year. The first was on December 24th, 2014 and the second time occured on August 18, 2015.

On December 24, 2014 I was baking a pumpkin pie in the bottom oven. I turned on the  top oven to preheat and within minutes he smoke detector went off (I was not near the oven at the time). I ran downstairs and I saw OVEN FLAMES coming out of the top vent of the stove. I immediately shut off both ovens. Luckily we caught in nick of time or our house could have burned down.  A Sears technician came and replace a valve and ignitor.

On 8-18-15 we had a SECOND FIRE with the same stove. I was cooking wings in the top oven and smelled burning plastic. When I opened the top oven door a giant flame cam shooting out of the oven. I turned both ovens off ASAP. We are no longer using the oven and will contact Sears for a refund on the stove and prior repair cost.
justification: The incident involved flames and potential for significant damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
LG Refrigerator

    I removed the bottom glass shelve from the refrigerator because we had spilled something on it. I placed it in the kitchen sink and washed both sides with dishwasher soap and a sponge. Then I rinsed it off with warn/hot water. All of a sudden the glass shelve exploded into many tiny pieces. I received superficial cuts to my hand and arm. I immediately called LG to report it and they sent me a replacement glass shelve.  I reviewed the use and care manual and nowhere did it mention not to remove the ice cold shelves from the refrigeration and wash them with hot water. I am reporting this because I would hate to see what might have happened if a young child was standing next to me. I believe the glass shelve they are using is not tempered. Therefore creating a potential hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in superficial cuts to the hand and arm, indicating an injury, and the likelihood is considered possible given the described scenario.

incident_description: The dishwasher was running through a cycle when it started to smoke. Upon opening the dishwasher door, smoke poured out of the machine. The door was then closed and then opened again and that is when fire shot out of the top of the dishwasher door. My mother in law received minor steam burns to her right forearm. The breaker was then tripped and the unit was removed from under the counter. There were moderate burn marks on the bottom of the granite countertop. Had the countertop been built out of lumber, the fire would have been far more severe.
justification: The incident resulted in minor steam burns to the mother-in-law's forearm and could have caused a more severe fire if the countertop was made of lumber.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore Elite Dish-washer. Model Number 665-17464300, S/N FP3801110 that almost caught fire yesterday. The dishwasher was running while I was out, when I cam inside the house it smelled of smoke and white smoke was pouring out of the control panel of the dishwasher. It would not turn off, even by opening it! I had to pull the circuit breaker.  

I am concerned that had I not come home, and smelled smoke I would have lost my home to fire.

I have done some online research and have become aware that this is an ongoing problem (see attached news link).

http://www.kgw.com/story/news/2014/07/24/12324270/
 
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The dishwasher almost caught fire, posing a significant risk of property damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Started oven in my freestanding range to do some baking. There was an area in the lower element that was glowing a bit brighter than the rest of the element during the preheat time. Loaded item to be baked into the oven and continued on with work in the kitchen. After a short time, likely a couple of minutes at best, I looked into the oven as I walked past it to put items away in nearby cupboard. The area that had been glowing brighter had gotten exceptionally hot/bright and was throwing off sparks such as one would see with a fireworks sparkler. Not as many sparks as fireworks, but definitely a fair amount of them. I immediately shut off the oven using the electronic control panel located on the back-splash area of the stove. The excessively hot area did not stop or decrease in its intensity and was moving along the element. Direction of movement was along the element working its way towards where the element entered the oven at the lower left side. Incident started on the right side of the element on the first pass going towards back of the oven. It moved along the element around the shorter center loop and back along the left side of the shorter loop before starting around the back right loop. I attempted to try to cool the hot, exceedingly bright orange/white glowing area with a spray-mist bottle with no effect at all. I then noticed that turning the oven off at the control had not worked as the element was still showing a dull glow all the way from where it enters the oven at the back right entry location all the way to the area undergoing catastrophic failure. In order to end the event I had to trip the breaker in the main breaker panel in the garage.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven element with sparks but no injury or property damage occurred, and such electrical failures are uncommon but not unheard of in appliances.

incident_description:
Toaster oven door falls wide open during operation

I own a Breville BOV800XL toaster oven - convection smart oven 1800 watts. Recently I placed a food item in it, closed the oven door and walked away. Upon returning 20 min later, I found the door wide open and the oven full on!  I closed the door and it immediately fell wide open. The oven is designed with a heavy bar handle, located up high on the door.  The design Places the center of gravity up high on the door, requiring an appropriately designed closure spring to hold the door closed.  

I called Breville to notify them of this design flaw and request a replacement oven.  This is a widely distributed product carried by Bed Bath and Beyond - I wasn't sure of purchase date. As I communicated to Breville, this is a design flaw - a weak spring not capable of holding this heavy door; over time the spring breaks allowing the door to simply fall open.  Breville customer service as much as admitted the spring has since been redesigned. I provided a number from the back of the oven and was told it was manufactured in 2010. Breville is unwilling to replace or repair the oven unless I pay a $120 service charge (the eventually agreed to do it for $90).

Frankly, I don't care about the money.  I will likely ship it back and have it repaired because otherwise I like the item.  But, I do not have young children in our household so this enables me to consider the problem from a different point of view.  What shocked me was Breville's complete lack of acceptance of the fact this design flaw could result in a serious burn injury.  I would think this rises to the level of a recall for a repair.  I have worked as a Product Manager for over ten years; telling consumers to pay to fix a serious safety design flaw seems, well, flawed!

How many thousands of these ovens are in consumers homes, being used daily, with the potential the door will flop open at any moment?  Shouldn't Breville at least issue a safety warning?

I would be happy to send you an iPhone mpg of the door falling open (immediately after it is closed) if this is helpful.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that could lead to serious burn injuries, though no actual injury was reported in this case. The likelihood is 'possible' as the flaw is present in a widely distributed product.

incident_description:
The gas range was installed in mid-January 2015.

This relates to the defective and dangerous gas kitchen ranges by Sears and Electrolux due to self-extinguishing burners. In late June of this year, we discovered that two of the top burners would self-extinguish when the oven door was opened. THIS WAS A VERY DANGEROUS CONDITION BECAUSE THE GAS WOULD CONTINUE TO FLOW FROM THE BURNERS.

We complained to local store and also to the parent company's service department. They sent out technicians on several occasions, but could not fix the problem. THE TECHNICIAN ADMITTED THAT THE STOVE WAS A DANGER TO ME AND MY FAMILY IN ITS DEFECTIVE CONDITION. The technician's manager then decreed that we would have to have the gas company (which happens to be the City of Rockport) come out and check the gas pressure at the stove. I asked the technician why he could not check the gas pressure himself, as that test can be made with a simple and inexpensive tool or meter. He told me that he did not have such a tool, notwithstanding the fact that he had been requesting the tool for a year or so.

The City of Rockport Gas Department was extremely helpful, and had a technician at our house with ten minutes. The City of Rockport technician had a very nice tool that would detect the presence of natural gas, and THE TOOL REVEALED THAT ALL FOUR TOP BURNERS AND THE OVEN BURNER WERE LEAKING GAS ON A CONTINUOUS BASIS. The City of Rockport technician declared on the spot that the stove was dangerous and had to be shut down. That was about a week ago.

The local Sears store now refuses to take back the dangerous stove and reimburse us. The local Sears store told us we would have to call the Parent-Sears service people. The Parent-Sears service people have a system in place for referring us from person to person and then hanging up the phone.

Our stove remains in its defective and highly dangerous condition, and is sitting in the middle of the kitchen, disconnected. We have a beautiful new home, but cannot even cook a meal in it. I wish we had purchased our appliances from [REDACTED] or anyone but Sears.

The submitter added he has learned that the CPSC has ordered the recall of other Sears Kenmore gas ranges made and sold by Electrolux and Sears, due to hazardous, selfÃÂ­ extinguishing burners...This recall was done under CPSC Recall No. 15-143, and it involved Sears Kenmore Elite model no. 790.42603xxx with serial numbers ranging from AF42500601 through AF43000916 and model no.790.42613xxx with serial numbers ranging from AF42500541 through AF43103647.

The submitter also added he BELIEVES THAT THE GAS STOVES RECALLED UNDER  CPSC RECALL NO. 15-143 ARE MECHANICALLY IDENTICAL TO THE GAS STOVE THAT SEARS SOLD TO him...IF TRUE,THEN SEARS AND ELECTROLUX ENGAGED IN UNCONSCIONABLE ACTS BY KNOWINGLY SELLING him a gas range that they knew was extremely hazardous to their health because it had TWO defects: (1.) self-extinguishing burners and (2.) burners that leaked natural gas continuously into their living environment.

The submitter noted he believes that they are extremely lucky that they were not killed by a violent explosion or asphyxiated due to leaking gas. The submitter also noted there was no traumatic injury, but he believes they were poisoned slowly due to the natural gas leakage into their home.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous gas leak and self-extinguishing burners, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high given the defective nature of the stove and the recall.

The consumer was cleaning her kitchen and she had a wet towel wiping down everything. When she opened the oven door slightly so she could wipe down the top of its door and gently closed it again. When the consumer turned her back on the unit, the oven glass door immediately exploded. The consumer received many abrasions to her hands and arms.

The consumer's husband, who was not in the kitchen, heard the loud explosion and his wife's screams and hurried to the kitchen. He immediately switched off the circuit breaker that supplies electricity to the unit.

The consumer wrapped her arms and hands. Because the next morning her arms and hands were throbbing due to the injuries, she went to the Emergency Room. They x-rayed her arms and hands to locate the small glasses that were still in her flesh. They extracted these small glasses and re-x-rayed her arms and hands to make sure there were none left in the consumer. They finished by bandaging her and sending her home.

06/12/2015 - The consumer contacted her Homeowner's Insurance and they sent somebody out immediately to inspect the damage. A claim was submitted. She was told the unit seemed it was combustible.

06/17/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer contacted Jenn Air and explained everything that happened. The representative she spoke to asker her how she felt and informed her that they would send an inspector out on 07/02/2015. After inspection, the inspector told the consumer that although glasses can shatter, it was the first time that he had seen somebody with injuries do to it. He cleaned out as much glass as possible under the oven and threw them away. He filed a report with the manufacturer.

07/15/2015 - The consumer received a call from Whirlpool Corporation. She did not receive any answer as to what could have caused the incident and they offered to completely replace the range or credit her 2,449.00$ towards the purchase of a new range. 

The consumer has not made any decisions regarding the offers she received. She was informed she has thirty days to do so. 

The consumer asked about her medical expenses and she was told that their Law Department would send her a Claims Form so she can fill it out and submit. The Claims Form was e-mailed.

The consumer indicates that she has an appointment with a plastic surgeon on 07/20/2015 to consult on her injuries to see if there could be scarring and what can be done about it.

The consumer indicates that Jenn Air is the only brand that sells downdraft ranges in the world. After what happened, the consumer does not feel safe with any Jenn Air ranges or downdraft ranges. Because of this, restructuring and remodeling will have to be done to her home and kitchen.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The consumer suffered abrasions and required medical attention, indicating injury (severity 3). The inspector noted it was the first time he had seen injuries from such an incident, suggesting it is unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
On Monday, August 10, at 6:57 PM I turned on our Samsung oven. It was the firs time using the oven although we had used the stove for two weeks. After 10 minute the temperature reading still showed 150 F. I thought I could hear a fan or something running. I leaned forward and opened the oven to look inside.

A blue and yellow fireball erupted, engulfing my entire head. I slammed the door shut and fell back, patting my head to make sure that I wasn't on fire. I checked in the mirror: no flames or smoldering but lots of singed hair. I called 911. I turned off the oven. Injuries: eyes felt sunburned the next day. Today my nose has some peeling skin but no blisters and minimal pain.

A few minutes later the paramedics and I took a look at the oven. There were no residual flames, sooty areas, or other signs of problem. The only evidence was my singed hair and a slight burn to my nose. We speculated on the cause and decided to try it again. This time when I turned on the oven the digital reading of temperature rose quickly, which I had expected the first time. When I opened the door the oven was clear and hot. I cooked my meal in the oven that evening with no further troubles.

Possible factors:
* This was the first use of the oven
* Aluminum foil on the bottom of the oven (to catch drippings and make cleaning easier)
* A clean, empty cake pan was inside the oven when I turned it on. I did this by mistake.
* The was an oily smell from the oven. Perhaps the coating was becoming gasified and caught flame when I opened the door and allowed in fresh oxygen
* I installed the range myself. There was no leaking, the stove worked well, and I checked all lines with a soapy spray to check for bubbles. There were no leaks. A friend who installs appliances checked my work. I had not "flushed the line" (his words), so it took a few seconds before the burners on the stove lit. Perhaps there was air in the line to the oven and, without gas, the igniting sparks had ended before gas came through. I don't know what would have ignited the flame, however, unless there were new sparks or some flame inside.
* My friend (who installs kitchen appliances) speculated that I might have bumped a knob on the stove, allowing gas to leak out without catching flame. I do not believe that happened. Neither of the paramedics nor I observed this on Monday when we  inspected the stove.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including singed hair, sunburned eyes, and peeling skin, but no death or severe burns.

incident_description:
On 07/23/2014 I purchased a Breville BOV800XL/A toaster oven based on the high recommendation published in Consumer Reports magazine. Generally, my complaint has to do with it gets VERY HOT on the outside. 

When I first used it the following morning, when I opened the door to remove my toasted English muffins, my finger touched metal door frame and I got a painful burn. I then ran another cycle and my laser thermometer indicated between 110 and 120 degrees. Subsequent test yielded temperatures on the outside door frame of 109 degrees (top) 96 and 99 degrees (sides), and 141 degrees (bottom). The metal frame inside of the door ranged between 140 and 160 degrees. The top of the oven was 162 degrees.

I then ran a ten minute broil cycle at the 500 degree setting and the door frame was about the same as with the toasting and the sides and back were between 90 and 110 degrees. However the tip was 185-290 degrees.

There are warnings in the manual on page 4 and 5 under a column title "important Safeguards" and made reference to exceptions for top storage on page 47. They also made reference in that section to a bamboo cutting board designed to fit on top. Some of the consumer comments on the Amazon.com web site indicated the cutting board was of marginal quality and the feet on the bottom elevated it that made it appear to be a heat shield.
justification: The user experienced a painful burn from touching the hot metal door frame, indicating an injury (severity 3). Given the high external temperatures reported, burns are likely to occur frequently during use (likelihood 4).

Ran dishwasher in early afternoon and had cycle completed indications before opening to get dishes to feed cats.  They were too hot to use so took other dishes from cabinets to feed cats.  We thought it was normal that things are hot just after cycle completing so we just shut the door.  We left for a family evening out about 1730 and returned about 2330.  Opening entry door to house we were met with heavy smell for burnt plastics.  Family members went to find all cats and open windows/doors to ventilate house while I went to check for source of smell in kitchen.  Opening dishwasher door solved that.  I shut the door and opened the breaker for the dishwasher in the outside breaker box.  We spent the next few hours ventilating house before we felt safe to go to bed around 0230.  During that time we called our master maintenance plan to get the process started and get them to our house ASAP - did not come until Monday, 08/10/2015.  The next morning I took pictures (available on request) and afterwards started to remove dishes that could be broken free of the now solidified plastics.

Damage assessment:
 - all dishwasher safe plastics were melted beyond recognition
 - most plastic dishwasher parts were melted beyond recognition - e.g. flatware tray totally gone
 - could not move upper and lower trays - wheel damage and plastic stalactites fusing everything together
 - estimator report on 08/10/2015 provided us a $3500 parts and labor for just what he could see in the dish washing space - i.e. he did not disassemble to look at motor, controls, etc. - they will replace unit
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (melted plastics and dishwasher parts) but no injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
On Sat., Aug. 1, 2015, at approximately 1:30 am, I was in the living room of my coop when i heard what sounded like a hail storm in my adjacent kitchen.  It was a very hot night and I was preparing to go to bed but this sound was alarming and frightening.   
After walking over to my kitchen, I saw that the entire front glass part of the oven (Kenmore Gas Range Model#790 725 0901 0 -  October, 2011) - purchase ) had just shattered completely and the glass was crumbled and splattered onto my kitchen floor. Black and clear glass and jagged edges were everywhere in my kitchen!  I had been home at work for 10 hours that day and the oven was cold and there were  no cracks in the glass door prior to  explosion. 
I note that a very similar complaint about "exploding in glass door"  was filed with CPSC on June 26, 2015 concerning Kenmore Gas Range (model# 790-7754-3800), purchased in September 2010 one year before my purchase. While the range models are different, the materials and manufacturing of the glass doors is most likely the same or very similar.
This was, and is, a very dangerous situation and it is perplexing as to why this happened.  This oven does not have a self-cleaning feature and the oven was cold and had not been used that day or for several weeks before. There were also no cracks in the glass door prior to explosion.  It is a very basic oven that is not even 4 years old!  I am not afraid to even use the stove and burners of this appliance which means i am without a stove and an oven!  I have tried calling several numbers for Sears, to no including their "Customer Care Network" a telephone that rings and goes unanswered.  When a Sears agent answered a call, they only tried to sell me a warranty on this defective and unsafe oven and were very defensive repeatedly saying that nothing could be done because this appliance is out of warranty. This response by a Sears representatives is very unfortunate and disappointing to me and my family who have been customers of Sears for 45+ years.  Perhaps this kind of poor and indifferent customer service has contributed to Sears losing its competitive edge as a national retailer.  The CPSC must look into this complaint and any related ones concerning Kenmore Gas Ranges, regardless of the gas range model number, where  glass doors that spontaneously explode and shatter. These are most unsafe and dangerous products.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous shattering of an oven glass door, but no injuries were reported.

On 06/01/15 (approximately) as the submitter's mother was passing by the range she slipped and caught her fall by putting her left hand on the stove top. The submitter states the glass top shattered and the submitter's mother sustained lacerations on her hand. The submitter's mother did not seek medical attention. 

On 06/02/15 (approximately) the submitter contacted the firm (866-640-7146 ex [REDACTED]) and informed them of the incident. The submitter was told by a firm rep (name unknown) that the glass top would be replaced free of charge. 

On 06/30/15 (approximately) the technician came out and replaced the glass top. While the technician was replacing the glass top the submitter noticed wires near the right front burner were burned. The submitter informed the technician but the wires were not replaced.

incident_description:
On 07/24/15 when the consumer woke up and walked in the kitchen she noticed the front right burner was "on". The consumer noticed the control panel indicated the burner to be "off". The consumer had to shut off the circuit breaker. The consumer states the electric range was last used on 07/22/15. About 5 hours later the consumer turned the circuit breaker back "on" and noticed the front right burner immediately turned "on". 

On 07/24/15 the consumer contacted the firm (800-449-9810) and informed them of the incident. The consumer was transferred to the recall department and the rep (name unknown) told the consumer that her electric range was not recalled. The consumer was told that any repairs would be at her own cost. The consumer states the call was disconnected and she was not able to schedule a repair. 

The consumer plans to buy a new electric range. 

There are no prior incidents. The electric range is used daily.

The consumer believes the electric range poses a fire hazard and should be recalled.
