incident_description: My husband woke up this morning to discover that the middle, inner glass window in our Amana stove's oven had shattered.  The outside glass in intake an the inside glass is intact.  The pane of glass inside those two panes is shattered.  The oven was not used the day before or this morning.
justification: The incident involved a shattered inner glass window in the oven, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
06/15/2013 (Approximately) - Since this time, the control panel to the unit shuts down and goes black, turning off the displays to the range. The consumer has to unplug and re-plug the not for it to start up again.  The consumer called GE & they said she must have gotten the control panel wet.

02/15/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer was cooking some food and left the kitchen. When she came back approximately thirty minutes later, she noticed the control panel had shut itself down but the burner she was using was still emitting flames. The consumer finished cooking her food but tried to turn on the remainder of the burners and was unsuccessful. When the consumer finished cooking, she unplugged and plugged the unit back on and the control panel and everything came back on and functioned properly.  She did not try to put oven on due to concerns w/ range functioning. 

The consumer indicates that if she is cooking on the stove and the control panel shuts off, the burners still work.  Or at least they did prior to 2/15/2015 incident.

04/15/2015 (Approximate) The consumer was pre-heating her oven at 350 degrees (bake) and approximately five minutes later, the consumer noticed that the oven had completely shut itself off because the control panel shut off as well. The consumer proceeded to turn the oven on again and it stayed on for approximately ten minutes before shutting off again. The consumer tried this a couple more times but ended up with the same outcome. The consumer no longer uses her oven.  The consumer is too scared to use oven self-clean feature due to poor product functioning.

The consumer indicates that if she happens to have the oven on and the control panel shuts off, the oven will shut off as well.

06/01/2015 (Approximately) The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained all the issues she has been having with her kitchen range. The representative informed her that they would not be able to send a Service Technician to inspect her unit for over a week. She contacted a local third-party Service Technician to inspect her unit. Who charged to consumer $146.00.  After inspection, he informed the consumer that the problem was most likely that her control panel was defective. It would cost her several hundred dollars to get her unit fixed. Everything else checked out fine. Control panel controls entire product function so the consumer would not say all else is fine.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer does not plan on contacting the manufacturer again.  There is no one to discuss or advise on product.  Only people who send techs out at huge fee.

The consumer lives in a co-op w/ other apartments & is concerned about general property safety.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning control panel that disrupts appliance function but has not caused any injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
While making popcorn with a Cuisinart model CPM-100 Hot Air Popcorn Maker, my daughter attempted to turn it off after completing the process, using the ON/OFF switch. When she did so, the popper continued to run, and we observed the sound and smell of electrical arcing. She had the presence of mind to unplug the unit prior to any of the plastic catching fire.

The device is less than a year old, and has the following on the label: 120V 60Hz 1500W. It also has 20627 as a possible serial number.

This device has never been immerced in water, nor used outside, so the switch has not been exposed to water, the only reason for this type of incident other than the switch being insufficient for the amperage of the device.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing but was promptly addressed without injury or fire, indicating a severity level of 2. Given the device's age and proper usage, such an occurrence is unlikely but possible due to potential switch failure.

incident_description: The outside glass on my oven door on the GE 30 inch stand alone range shattered today. There was no warning. It was not turned on at the time but I had been using it for years.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no injury occurred, and such incidents are unlikely based on the description of long-term use without prior issues.

incident_description:
On December 9, 2014, I turned on my GE Profile Triton XL dishwasher (model number GSD6900J10WW, serial number DL826872B) at about 6:30 pm.  I went upstairs to give my sons (ages 3 and 6) a bath.  After their bath, we were relaxing on the bed upstairs playing on the computer when I heard the smoke detector alarm around 7:20 pm.  My husband was not yet home from work.  I went downstairs to investigate, finding that our kitchen was full of smoke.  I could see that the source was the dishwasher.  I opened the dishwasher door and saw flames 12-18 inches high coming from the lower left rear of the inside of the dishwasher.  I immediately ran upstairs to get my two small boys.  We escaped down the staircase and out the front door while I was dialing 911 from my cell phone.  The fire department arrived in 8 minutes.  They entered the house to discover heavy black smoke from the 9 foot ceiling about halfway down.  They made their way to the kitchen to find flames about 6 feet high engulfing the dishwasher and the kitchen cabinet adjacent to the dishwasher.  The fire department was able to extinguish the flames using a 2-gallon extinguisher, although they did have the fire hose loaded and ready to use, if necessary.  Once the fire was extinguished, they attempted to prop open every window on the first and second floor of our two-story home to let out smoke.  (The fire department had to prop open our windows with boxes and random items because our windows did not open properly ÃÂ a separate problem.)  Black smoke was coming out of every open window.

While the flame damage was mainly in the kitchen, smoke and soot damaged our entire house (both floors).  Structurally the house is sound, but it needs to be gutted.  Nasty black soot is on literally every surface you can imagine.  It worked its way into every crevice of every item.  As a result, we lost all of our personal property in the home.  Several examples of where soot got inside:  underneath the wrapping paper of a wrapped Christmas gift that was under the bed in the master bedroom upstairs, the closed toothbrush sanitizing cabinet of a Sonicare electric toothbrush in the master bathroom upstairs, all electrical outlets, and every place that was not air-tight.  It was a devastating fire.

We estimate our overall damage at more than $500,000.  In addition, we have been damaged by needing to live elsewhere for the past 8 months and counting, dealing with attorneys and insurance companies who do not want to fix the house properly, and wasting many hours painfully inventorying our damaged items one at a timeÃÂnot to mention the stress and uncertainty of having our lives suddenly thrown in turmoil.

A fire investigation, requested by our insurance company, American Strategic Insurance, was conducted on December 19, 2014.  In attendance were several forensic engineers, including those representing our insurance company, Beazer Homes USA (our homebuilder which installed the dishwasher) and GE (the dishwasher manufacturer).  Despite our numerous requests through our attorney, all parties have failed to provide us with any official written results of the fire investigation.  It is strange how this has been kept so secret.  Beazer did write us, however, that the investigation revealed that the source of our fire was an electrical defect within the dishwasher itself, and that it did not have to do with the installation or our use of the dishwasher.  Our attorney has tried to contact GE to open a dialogue with them, but they, through their Electric Insurance company, refuse to talk with us about the incident.  Their behavior is forcing us to file suit against them, subjecting us to a long, costly legal process that will damage us even further.

Unfortunately, we learned after our fire that there was indeed a recall on our model dishwasher several years ago and GE failed to notify us.  GE most definitely knew the model and serial number of our dishwasher.  In early 2008, we noticed that our dishes were not coming clean.  We scheduled a service call with GE AppliancesÃÂ GE Consumer Home Services for February 21, 2008.  A GE employee visited our home on that day to troubleshoot our dishwasher.  He concluded that the dishwasher itself was fine, but we needed to run the hot water at our kitchen sink before turning on the dishwasher.  This would allow the dishwasher to have the hot water it needs to clean the dishes.  We have a receipt from this service call, which clearly shows the model number of our dishwasher.  GE knew the model number and serial number of our dishwasher.  It is frustrating to think that all of our troubles were completely avoidable had GE simply informed us about the recall.  Clearly there is a major problem with GEÃÂs recall notification process.

The responsible parties need to be held accountable.  We view both GE and Beazer as responsible for our fire.  In the automotive world, Takata has had major problems with airbag recalls.  However, Takata does not notify car owners that their specific car has a recall.  Instead, the automobile manufacturer (Ford, BMW, etc.) notifies their affected customers about the recall.  Should it be similar here?  Beazer sold us this dishwasher, and they should have known what they installed.  Are they obligated to notify us?  Of course, GE should have known what was in our house, as well.  We feel that both companies are responsible and need to be held accountable.  Beyond the major damage our property sustained, it would have been so easy for one of us to be injured or killed.  We were lucky.

If you would like any more information, we invite you to call either me or my husband [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a significant fire causing extensive property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Product is a Nostalgia Electrics "Retro Series" electric ice cream maker.  With this product, the lid/motor assembly screws onto the base counter clockwise.  The machine also churns counter clockwise.  While trying to churn my first batch of ice cream I heard the lid separate from the machine and begin to spin on top of the machine.  By the time I ran into the kitchen to turn it off, the machine had spun enough to pull the cord into the bowl assembly and reeled the cord into itself like a fishing reel.  Once it reeled enough cord inside itself, the machine pulled itself a couple feet across my counter and fell into my kitchen sink.  Had my children been doing dishes as the time this electrical appliance walked itself into my kitchen sink, the unthinkable would have happened.  All they had to do was have the lid/motor assembly locked onto the base in the opposite direction of the machine rotation, this would never have happened.  In my opinion, this machine needs to be pulled from shelves before someone gets seriously hurt or electrocuted.  

Part number is ICM150RETRORED
UPC code is 0826677217912
justification: The incident describes a dangerous malfunction that could lead to injury or electrocution, but no actual injury occurred in this case.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:

I would like to report a major safety  event to your agency.  About 9 years ago I purchased a Kenmore Gas Range. The model number is 9078582404 and the serial number is VF52709133. This stove had functioned without problems until Monday, June 1, 2015 when I was awakened early in the morning by a "chirping" noise. Thinking it was my smoke detector, got out of bed to investigate. I found that this noise was not the smoke detector, but my gas range. The stove had turned on by itself, and as I watched it, the oven went on and the temperature of the oven increased automatically. I attempted to lower the oven temperature  with  the controls  and also to turn the oven off.  All controls were nonresponsive as I attempted to solve this situation. I then pulled the plug on the stove. A few minutes later I plugged the stove in again, but it still did not respond to my actions.

I had been away for 10 days, just returning 3 days before this happened and was very thankful that this did not happen while no one was home in my house. I feel it could have resulted in a house fire and damage or loss of my home.

I have never before  experienced such a situation, and am concerned that this product could result in a much greater  disaster. I believe that by reporting  this, I may save others.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas range that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dishwasher started smoking while it was in use.  He stated that approximately 5 mins after the unit was operational, smoke emanated from the sides of the door.  Fortunately he was home to unplug the dishwasher.

Caller feels that he experienced similar problems of  Recall#05-123.  Hazard: An electrical defect within the dishwashers' wash motor wiring poses a risk of the motor overheating and possibly catching fire.

Caller stated that he noticed that there were numerous complaints on the dishwasher. The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that this incident occurred because the dishwasher was old.  He was also advised that a service technician would be sent out at his expense, the technician came out and he was advised that the control board malfunctioned that caused the fire.

Caller feels that this dishwasher should be recalled.

incident_description:
On 07/15/15 the consumer set the dishwasher to a wash cycle. About 15 minutes later the consumer noticed smoke coming from the dishwasher. The consumer states the dishwasher was "off" and when he opened the door he noticed burn damages near the control panel. The consumer opened the control panel and noticed melted wires.

The consumer has not contacted the firm and does not plan to. 

The consumer states there are no prior incidents. The consumer states the dishwasher is used 3 times a week.

The consumer believes the dishwasher poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burn damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the consumer's belief of a fire hazard and regular use of the dishwasher.

incident_description: The control module on my Bosch dishwasher (model SHX46A05UC/40) failed, nearly causing a fire.  It was taking a long time for the dishwasher to complete its cycle and I noticed an odor of something burning.  I researched the long cycle time on the web and found that the control modules on some Bosch dishwashers can overheat, causing the solder points to melt.  I removed the module from my dishwasher and found that the plastic cover had a melted area and the circuit board had a large burned area.  I purchased an OEM replacement module and installed it and the dishwasher seems to be working fine now, however, I am concerned that this may happen again and possibly cause a fire.  I contacted Bosch and they will be sending a technician to look at my dishwasher and determine if it is safe to continue using it.
justification: The control module failure caused a near-fire incident with visible damage but no injury or death.

incident_description: After cooking some garlic bread in the oven of our Kenmore Elite Smooth Top Stove (model 665 95804000 Serial No. RL0520683) my son noticed that the oven heating element was still red even though the stove was turned off.  We tried multiple times to push the "off/cancel" button to no avail.  Eventually, I went to the breaker box and flipped the "range" breakers to the off position.  After 10 minutes I flipped the breakers back on and turned the oven back on.  When the element was glowing red I once again tried to turn it off with the "off/cancel" button to no avail.  After realizing this switch failure could cause a fire, I searched the internet for similar complaints and found plenty.  Several of the chat pages mentioned a "recall" but when I contacted Sears they said there wasn't a "recall" on this particular model.  They offered to send a technician out and that if the trouble was from the computer control board then the total repair would be $335 including labor.  My concern is what will keep the same electrical switch failure from happening again?  My wife and I are talking about getting a new stove as I don't see how we can ever trust this stove again.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven heating element that could potentially cause a fire, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: On July 25 th, 2015 at approximately 5 pm  I was preparing dinner  I set the oven temp and set the timer on my Kenmore stove and went  to the counter to  continue preparing dinner.  I looked up and the entire stove had flames shooting from the back of the stove
justification: Flames shooting from the stove indicate a significant fire hazard, which could lead to injury if not promptly addressed.

incident_description: On Sunday, June 28, 2015, at 6:30 p.m. while cooking with our 2010 Kenmore Microwave/Wall Oven, the microwave oven electrically malfunctioned. It happened when I started the unit to defrost a small amount of pesto in a Pyrex class measuring cup, and the microwave oven compartment immediately began to emit a loud electrical-current arc sound with many bright shooting lights, much as a lightning storm will do in a night sky. I called to my husband to shut down the unit, and by the time he got into the kitchen and the oven was shut down, this electrical arching had continued non-stop for nearly a minute. At approximately  8 p.m., or 1 1/2 hours after this incident, I noticed very bright arching lights in my left eye that continued throughout the night. The next day on Monday, June 29, 2015, I went to see my ophthalmologist, and after performing a thorough exam, she concluded that I had sustained "arc burns" on both eyes that were similar to the burns that arc welders can sustain while arc welding. In addition, during the week immediately after this incident I experienced an alarming increase in my blood pressure. In the week prior to this incident, my blood pressure averaged 127/78. After the incident my blood pressure steadily increased until Friday July 3, 2015 it registered 180/103, and I immediately went to see my doctor.  I was temporarily given HTN medication to lower my blood pressure. I have also had an electrocardiogram to check my heart function, and I was found to be hypertensive. (In the past 12 years, I have not been on any HTN medications; I am a healthy, athletic slender 58 year old woman.) I believe there is a direct correlation between my experience with the microwave electrical current malfunction, the arcing injury to both of my eyes and the hypertension.  Since the incident, we have never restarted this unit, and have since purchased a new Microwave/Wall Oven from a different manufacturer. We are keeping the Kenmore microwave oven in storage, in case it is needed for testing.
justification: The incident caused arc burns to the eyes and hypertension, indicating injury (severity 3). Such electrical malfunctions are rare but possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description: I purchased a brand new Panasonic 2.2cft 1250 watt microwave in may for Mothers Day and after 3 months of service it is arcing while operating between the door and the body of the microwave.  It also smells of burning electrical.  It has not been used very much as we only use it to reheat a meal from time to time.  The inside edge of the door was hot and had burn marks through the paint of the body where it was arcing to the door.  Inside the microwave when it was operating looked like a welding arc.  This is a definite fire hazard and could have been a disaster if I had not been standing there watching the food cook. This microwave has never been operated for more than a few minutes at a time to reheat food or heat water.
justification: The microwave is arcing and shows signs of burning, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: New GE refrigerator sent a shower of sparks from top left upper side of cabinet.  Door shocked hand when ring made contact after 2 months of ownership.  Incident tripped electric breaker. GE contacted and sent a technician, found a bare wire contacting door hinge. Temporary patch put on wiring outdoor GE to order a new door and Hinge within 7 to 10 days.  New parts supposed to be shipped to house.   Parts did not arrive technician called his dispatcher to find out about parts, and are back ordered for unknown amount of time.
justification: The incident involved a shock to the hand and sparks, indicating injury, but the likelihood is low as it was caused by a specific wiring issue.

incident_description:
We had a fire AFTER a recall repair was performed for that same fire hazard.  The Compliance Department recommended I file this report.

After moving into our home in April 2013, our home inspector notified us that our GE Profile Dishwasher was part of a recall (#11022 dated October 26, 2010).  The hazard:  ÃÂWater condensation can drip onto the electronic control board, causing a short circuit and resulting in an overheated connector. This poses a fire hazard to consumers.ÃÂ  I contacted GE and chose the RECALL REPAIR option.  A GE technician came to our home approximately April/May 2013 and performed the recall repair.

On July 21, 2015, my Mom loaded and ran the dishwasher before going to bed 3-4 hours later.  Upon awakening the next morning, she smelled a strange smell and upon entering the kitchen saw the dishwasher had caught on fire (fire damage to the control panel and soot on the cabinetry and dishwasher door panel).  Fortunately, the breaker tripped; however, this failed recall repair put my family at risk of injury and possible death.  

I called the GE hotline to report this fire/failed recall repair.  They sent out a GE technician ([REDACTED]) who immediately upon entering my kitchen, stated, ÃÂthis is the worst fire I have ever seenÃÂ and advised me that my dishwasher was ÃÂnon-repairableÃÂ.  Please note that [REDACTED] did not open my dishwasher door nor did he remove the door panel to investigate the recall part that had been installed in 2013. [REDACTED] stepped outside my home to call into his office and then came back in to advise me that GE would call me the following day with their offer.  

GE contacted me the following day with an offer to replace my GE Profile with another GE Profile of THEIR choosing.  I advised them their offer was unacceptable and that my family does not feel safe with another GE product under these circumstances.  GE replied, this was all they were allowed to offer ÃÂper the lawÃÂ.  We remain dissatisfied with their offer, their lack of concern for our safety, and the harm and possible injury and death that could have occurred as a result of this failed recall repair.  We do not want anyone else who has had this specific recall repair performed to think the risk of fire no longer exists.
justification: The incident involved a fire due to a failed recall repair, posing a risk of injury or death, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: In 2006 Purchased 2 Frigidaire Professional Series Ovens for newly built home.  Model number for Both: PLEB30S9FCA.  The inside oven walls of the oven used the most have expanded to the point that the racks will no longer stay on the tracks.  I am sure if the other oven gets the same use, it will also encounter the same problem.

Handle swung up while in my grip and the spring loaded door slammed against my wife's oustreched arm. Luckily, I grabbed top of door edge with my other hand and opened door away from her arm. Cooktop temperature is not consistent with the temp selection.  The temp selector goes from Low to high - 0-10. There have been occasions when I tried to turn the burner off, but it will not shut off without trying over and over.

One year later it has malfunctioned again.  The fan has stopped working and the seal is getting hotter and hotter each day. We came home and the glass from the outer glass panel was shattered all over the floor. Glass was still "popping" on the floor. Fortunately, because we were not home...there were no injuries.

incident_description:

When she  opened the oven door to check the pizza, a big ball of fire came out of the oven. The fire ignited in the consumer's face. Her lashes, eyelids, arm, face and hair was burned.  Medical attention was required.

It is uncertain at this time, but possible, that the product involved in this fire may be subject to CPSC Recall 09-145. I then used the low broiler setting to brown the top of the fish for about 3-5 minutes. I turned the oven off, took out the fish and had dinner. Breaker needed to be thrown to remove power from the unit.  Until that was thrown, sparks and smoke were observed with the door open or closed.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore smoothtop electric range and have been experiencing problems with the right front burner cooking very hot even when the dial is set to low or medium. Food began to burn and the kitchen filled with smoke from the burning food. Tonight the burner was not shutting off when the dial was in the off position.  For several minutes after it was turned off the burner would light up hot red up and then shut off. This continued for 5-7 minutes until I could assess a temporary solution online. I did notice a small quick spark come from one of the coils.  I had to turn the circuit breaker off for the burner to shut itself off. I have not turned the circuit breaker back on, nor will I until it can be looked at.  this is a safety and serious fire hazard. 

I have been online to check for any recall notices for this unit and while Frigidaire issued a recall notice back in 2009, this unit was not listed in the recall. It seems others are experiencing the same issue with this model. Yes, I will call the 800 number to report this. Without an active recall, I will likely have to fix on my own. Hoping by reporting this, the manufacturer or Safety Commission will take notice.  

Incident Date 7/29/15
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner causing smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the range came with the home they purchased in 2007.
The consumer stated that she used the oven at 380F for 5 minutes to heat up bread. The consumer went to remove bread from the oven and she saw flames in the oven. 
The consumer stated that the bottom heating element in the oven was in flames. The consumer stated that the flames were as high as 2/3 of the oven.
The consumer stated that she shut off the oven but it did not stop the fire. The consumer had to unplug the range to stop the fire. The consumer stated that the bottom of oven burned.
 
There is no recall on this range.
justification: The incident involved flames in the oven requiring unplugging to stop the fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the outer glass on the oven door shattered. 

The consumer stated that the oven had not been used in the past two days. The consumer heard a loud crash in the kitchen.

The consumer had fire department out to inspect the home for any gas leak. They informed her that there were no gas leaks and the explosion did not occur due to gas.  

The consumer's husband fell while trying to get to the kitchen when the explosion happened. He fell and hit his prosthetic knee. The consumer stated that her husband does not appear to be injured but she will monitor him and provide injury information upon receiving the report.  Follow up with orthopaedic surgeon is being pursued.  Dog cut paw

The consumer contacted LG and informed them about the incident. The consumer was informed that they would like to send out a technician in addition to the technician that will be coming under her extended warranty.  

LG sent out a technician, [REDACTED], on 6/30/15. The technician informed the consumer that they may be able to replace the door. The consumer was informed that it may not fall under extended warranty since the outer door shattered. The technician took photos of the unit and informed the consumer that he will turn them into LG. Technician informed the consumer that she will have to pay a service fee. The consumer stated that she should not have to pay the service fee since LG insisted on having the service technician sent out. The consumer did not pay the fee.

The consumer does not feel comfortable with a replacement door and would rather have the unit replaced. 

The consumer also contacted the extended warranty company. The consumer has an extended warranty through Assurant Solutions. They will be sending out a technician, named [REDACTED] FROM [REDACTED] on 7/2/15. 

The consumer is not satisfied with how LG is dealing with this matter. They were unable to find her in the system when she called back on 6/30/15 after the technician left. The consumer had to get a work order # from the technician and provide that to LG for them to look her up in their system. 

Photos - Re: Pictures
Each tile is 12x12.  The glass shot out (it did not fall out).  Glass was spread approx. 8ft by the same wide-even found glass in her foyer.  Channel 2 news 10P-July 8- have expose from 2089.  Something should be done.  Serious injuries will occur-please take steps to prevent this and hold manufacturers accountable.  You may contact the consumer.  The consumer doesn't want this to happen to anyone else, especially a child.  If you need pictures of the consumer's husband's knee and dog, contact her.
justification: The consumer's husband fell and hit his prosthetic knee, and the dog cut its paw, indicating minor injuries.

incident_description: My daughter was pre heating the oven when it made a loud pop. Immediately there was a sparking and flickering at the back of the stove control panel. It then flamed up and scorched the back of the stove and wall. I had her turn off the breaker to the stove on the electrical panel for the house. Terrible smell of burnt plastic that lingered for days. I am so glad that this did not start a house fire. If the oven had been turned on to use, and I or my daughter had stepped out to sit on the patio or work in the yard it could have burned down our house. I have an extended warranty on the oven and called for a repair. The repairman said the wiring was all cracked and the cracked wiring caused an arc which started the electrical fire in the control panel. That was 5 months ago. Now the convection oven fan is making a loud noise when in use and will shut off when the oven temp reaches 300 degrees. So I decided to not use that oven feature and just use the non-convection feature. The convection fans turn on, and they never have before when using the non- convection. I believe the non-convection feature is not working. Hopefully not from cracked wiring again. I am going to for repair on this tomorrow and have the wiring looked at again.  This oven needs to be recalled before someone gets killed from it starting a house fire. I have put things in the oven to cook before on lower temperatures to slow cook and gone outside to work or run a quick errand. This could be catastrophic! Please recall. I have searched the Internet and so many people with this,  and similar Samsung models have had the same problem.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and potential for a house fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: microwave is going on by itself.  this has happened a number of times and we are now keeping it unplugged.  no one has been injured or any damaged caused by it.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no injury or damage, but it has happened multiple times, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught on fire.. walked into house and smoke was billowing everywhere!
justification: Dishwasher fire caused significant smoke but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I purchased this gas range from the Home Depot in March. After using it, I discovered that the heat that emerges from it during cooking with the oven or convection, gets so hot that my microvwave hood fan comes on automatically. The entire door which is a very large surface is not only hot to the touch but scalding hot. The knobs on the stove are also untouchable while the oven is on. The handle to open the door is also hot because the exhaust from the oven apparently is along the entire top of the oven door. There is no safety notice about the entire door and knobs being hot. A small child could not touch any part of the face of the oven without getting seriously burnt. Just this week my mom was cooking and leaned against the oven and burned both her legs. Which is what prompted me to make the call to Whirlpool.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the user's legs, indicating an injury, and the description suggests that burns are likely to occur frequently due to the oven's design.

incident_description:
While placing two pans of enchiladas back into a hot oven, the rack in the oven collapsed, and the pans fell out of the oven.  One of the hot pans fell all the way out to the floor where I was standing.

The middle of the oven has expanded, and no longer is narrow enough to hold a loaded pan.  The oven is less than 3 years old, and is no longer safe to operate with hot, heavy foods or pans.
justification: The incident involved hot pans falling but no injury was reported, and the oven's condition makes recurrence likely.

incident_description: Purchased Copco 14oz stainless steel travel mug from Walmart. First time use with hot coffee the seal between the metal and plastic at the top of the mug leaked. As I tiped the mug to drink, the hot liquid poured out of the seal below the drinking spout onto my chest. I could have been burned if coffee had been hotter.
justification: The incident involved a leak that could have caused burns but did not result in actual injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the description of the product's failure on first use.

incident_description: We purchased a GE Spacemaker Microwave Oven on 02/13/2013 from Amazon.com.  Yesterday while cooking a potato in this unit, the entire inside burst into flames and the flames were about to engulf the framework around the unit.  Luckily my wife saw what was going on and I grabbed a fire extinguisher and put it out.
justification: The microwave burst into flames, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The Kenmore Elite Gas Cooktop is unsafe because when you use the control to lite the right or left front burner, the flame is so large that it reaches out and burns your hand which is on the control.
Also, after cooking with this cooktop, the control knobs are too hot to turn the burner off with a bare hand.
justification: The description indicates that the flame is large enough to burn hands and control knobs become too hot to touch, which suggests a risk of injury.

incident_description: Product: Williams Sonoma Duralex Picardie Glass Tumbler.  Glass had been washed in a top-rack dishwasher cycle and had thoroughly cooled to room temperature.  Daughter reached in to take glass out of the rack. She extended her hand and placed it on the glass but had not applied any pressure and it exploded in her hand. Small cut on hand but nothing serious.  However dishwasher drain is now full of numerous tiny chunks of glass that fell into it and is no longer working properly.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut on the hand, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence is unlikely (2) as glass exploding without pressure is not common.

incident_description:
This is the second  Cusinart TOB-40 toaster oven that the heating elements warped and cracked. The first time the lower rear element warped, cracked and caught fire. Luckily I was nearby and was able to prevent it becoming a serious kitchen fire.  I contacted Cusinart and got it replaced although it was not a consumer friendly process. The replacement is now about 1 1/2 yrs old and we noticed the top rear element is warped to the point of touching the top and is cracked. We are afraid to use any longer for fear of fire. I contacted Cusinart and while they will replace it I have to ship it back to Arizona from Connecticut and pay shipping BOTH ways. They also will not ship the replacement before 7-10 business days after they receive mine. This will leave us without a toaster for possibly 2-3 weeks. I explained we used it often and this would be a hardship. The insisted the process cannot be changed. So much for customer service

I am very disappointed with Cusinart who claim to have premium products. It is not an inexpensive toaster oven. This is the second unit with a similar defect and they do not acknowledge the heating elements have a  problem. I consider this very serious due to the risk of fire.
justification: The incident involves a toaster oven with a recurring defect that poses a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred this time.

incident_description: Meat and vegetables cooking in Rival Slow Cooker on high for 2+ hours when loud snap/pop noise came from kitchen.  Upon inspection found lid of cooker shattered, but still intact.  Unplugged and shut off cooker.  When cooled, removed lid by edges.  Thrown in trash, touched lid handle & lid fell apart.  No injuries.
justification: The incident involved a shattered slow cooker lid but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) since such incidents are not common but possible with faulty equipment.

incident_description: I was cooking chili in my crock pot on low setting.  It had only been on for about 2 1/2 hours when a heard a loud noise in the kitchen.  Upon further inspection I noticed the glass lid of  my crock pot had shattered and glass was in the food
justification: The glass lid shattered, but there was no mention of injury, only an incident with potential for harm.

incident_description:
I purchased the following product from Best Buy.

KitchenAid - 30" Self-Cleaning Freestanding Electric Convection Range - Stainless-Steel
Model: KERS202BSS SKU: 6897326

The range was brand new, never used, but was an "Open Box" product as a scratch and dent floor model.

The product was delivered and setup and turned on for first time use:  Bake 350 degrees.  I was told to leave it on for about 1/2 hour and then turn it off until I wanted to use it.

About an hour after turning it off, I leaned against the top to set the timer and the surface was scalding hot, so hot that I thought that the burner was turned on, but it wasn't.  I attempted to open the oven door and the handle was hotter than the surface.

I called Best Buy, they apologized, found another unit that was brand-new, in the box, never used, and they exchanged it a few days later.

The delivery folks performed the same setup, turned it on at 350 degrees and left.  About a hour later, I decided to bake something.  I leaned on the surface to prepare food and was immediately burned again.  

Perplexed, I checked the manual and didn't see any warnings about not using the surface when the oven was on.  I tried the handle and it was insanely hot also.

I used my cooking thermometer to record the temperatures of both areas and took photographs.

One picture shows the temperature of the handle area (137 degrees) and one the surface area (113 degrees).

I did call Best Buy and instructed them to pickup this new, 2nd unit immediately.
justification: The incident resulted in burns from the hot surface and handle, indicating an injury occurred. The issue happened twice with different units, suggesting a possible design flaw.

incident_description:
(04/2015) The consumer stated that she had the oven in the self-cleaning mode. About three minutes after closing the oven door, there was smoke and the smell of burning plastic coming  from the top of the oven. 

The oven door was locked. The consumer let the self-cleaning mode run it course because she did not know how to turn it off. After the cleaning was finished the oven handle fell off because the grill holding the handle had melted.

The vent on the back of the stove also turned brown.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting parts but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: purchased a Casa Essentials pressure cooker a few years ago at Macy's.  I had used previous cookers and this cooker as well without incident.  I placed ingredients for stew, following instruction to not overfill the cooker, and cooked the stew for 17 minutes after it came up to pressure.  After cooking I waited for about 20-30 minutes and pulled off the regulator to check for any residual pressure.  There was no steam released and no sound of steam.  I then opened the pressure cooker and as I did so, it exploded, and the stew contents hit my chest, neck and face which left me with first and second degree burns.  I sought medical attention immediately.  Apparently the locking mechanism which should have prevented me from opening the cooker while under pressure did not function.  I did not have to use force to open the cooker.  It opened easily.
justification: The incident resulted in first and second degree burns requiring medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the user had used the cooker multiple times without incident before this failure.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his over the microwave oven starts up by itself.  He stated that whenever this happens it turns off itself and display an error code of error-13.  This incident occurred twice.  He has since unplugged the unit to prevent a fire.

The manufacturer was contacted and was informed it was no longer under warranty and would need to be repaired at his expense.

Caller feels that this microwave is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a potential safety hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I have a Norcold model 1200LRIM refrigerator in my motor home. Upon opening the lower right hand door, the plastic door frame holding the hing broke which allowed the door to fall, injuring my right foot.
The hinge on this model is held on by a thin piece of plastic which is insufficient to handle a door this size and weight. 
This model with doors attached with plastic door frame material is a SAFETY HAZZARD..

I made several contacts to Norcold-Therford, the manufacturer's who stated that they had not received any complaints, while many complaints have been filed on-line. Also, their non-caring, impatient response was unacceptible.

In a product with a cost in excess of $3,000, should contain a more stable material to attach the doors vs plastic.

This product is very dangerous and could cause serious injury to adults and children.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the foot due to a faulty refrigerator door mechanism, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to multiple reported complaints and the inherent design flaw.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore stove model 790.97452801.  After using the oven, the button on the control panel to turn off the timer was pressed.  In the wall behind the stove, the reflection of flames was seen and a popping and crackling sound was heard.  Upon opening the back of the stove, it was discovered that the control panel had burned itself up.  The heat was so high during this event that the connectors on the wiring harness welded themselves to the control board.  No response from Sears to my report of this incident.
justification: The incident involved a stove malfunction causing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on the box of the frying pan, in the front, the pan's handle is advertised as "Oven safe up to 450F."

The consumer stated that when he took out the pan out of the box, there was an insert in the pan. The back of the insert stated that "T-Sal cookware items and covers with plastic handles or knobs are oven safe up to 350F."

The consumer contacted the mfr to get clarification on this matter. The representative informed him that the pan is safe to use in the oven up to only 350F. They informed him that the 450F on the front of the box is a typographical error.

The caller stated that if someone does not look at the insert and just go by the front of the box, they might misuse the product at a higher temperature than required for it to be safe to use in the oven.

The consumer added the frying pan did not come in a box, but was hanging from a hook by it's handle and included cardboard packaging which was seen on both the front and back of the frying pan.  The consumer noted he has included several photos of packaging.  The consumer also noted the part of the packaging that was visible to consumers stated that the handle was oven safe to 450 degrees F, but when the packing opened, on the inside it stated that it was oven safe to 350 degrees F.

The consumer also added he has included a revised incident details to reflect the correction and have attached it to the original report.  The consumer also noted he has retained the original packaging in case the actual packaging needs inspecting.
justification: The incident involves misleading packaging that could lead to product misuse, but no actual injury or harm was reported.

incident_description:
Sometime within May/June, 2014 this caller turned the left front burner of his electric range off after cooking, however the burner did not go out until the breaker was tripped.  
This was repaired at caller's expense June 16th, 2014 by a repair shop local to his residence.

The caller states that around May 5th, 2015 the left front burner again would not turn off after use until the breaker was tripped.

There are no injuries being reported 

The caller contacted the manufacturer in June 30th,  2015, he spoke with [REDACTED] and was offered only a discount on the repair part with an expiration of offer within 30 days of that date.
The caller finds this offer unsatisfactory and he is asking for a recall of this model and serial number with repair at manufacturer expense.

He is reporting this incident as a fire and burn hazard.
justification: The incident involves a burner not turning off, posing a potential hazard, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description: Kenmore bottom freezer refrigerator- purchased from Sears 2/23/05. Safety issue is that the crisper drawers for fruit/vegetables have a plastic frame above the drawer which has a slightly beveled edge and is very sharp. Have cut/scraped skin on arm/wrist/hand reaching in to get items out of the drawer on several occasions.
justification: The description mentions cuts and scrapes on the arm, wrist, and hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The issue has occurred on several occasions, indicating a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: Crock Pot 6 quart slow cooker.  When cooking on low, went to check on food, the lid was shattered for no reason.  It wasn't thermal difference or damaged.  Glass was on the counter and in the food.  I looked like an automobile windshield.
justification: The incident involved a shattered lid with glass in the food, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using a Presto hot air popcorn popper. My 5 yr old son was a safe distance away from the machine. As the machine was heating up the kernels, one kernel popped and pushed another extremely hot kernel out of the machine, down to the large bowl and caused it to bounce out unto the table and all the way to where my son was. It went inside his t-shirt resulting in him getting badly burned. As he tried moving the hot kernel it only burned another spot. This machine is dangerous because it has no way of stopping the hot kernels from not only being pushed out by the hot air, but by the corn as it is popping too. When the popcorn starts popping, the impulse is strong enough when combined with the hot air blowing out to push the hot kernels a very good distance. My son was a very good distance away and he still got badly burned. There's also no on/off switch. As you need to turn it off, you need to reach for the power cable and pull it out. In an emergency, it can be easily tipped over causing more burns.
justification: The incident resulted in a child getting badly burned by a hot kernel, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The description indicates that the machine's design makes such occurrences likely when in use.

incident_description: On July 18, 2015 while in self-cleaning mode, the glass in the oven door shattered.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Frigidaire Cooktop Model #FEC32S6ABF Serial # NF91833267 has temperature control issues. It changes to a higher temperature on it's own. Also does not turn off when manually placed in the off switch position. This caused a small fire to ensue on my cooktop; luckily I was able to quickly put the fire out.
justification: The cooktop's malfunction caused a small fire, indicating potential for injury, though none was reported in this instance.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his microwave purchased with home around June 2011.
The caller had no problem with the microwave until a few months after using.

When the microwave is used for five minutes or more then turned off, it will turn itself back on and caller has to turn it off at the breaker.

This incident doesn't occur if the use of the unit is under five minutes.

This caller is reporting this microwave due to chances of potential fire and injury if self restart is not noticed.

There are no injuries being reported.

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The microwave malfunction poses a potential fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
On March 5, 2015 I purchased an electric range.  About a month after the range was installed I ran the easy clean cycle only to find that a full clean cycle would be required.  As the range was new and different from the other brand ranges Ive owned previously, I pulled the users manual out to learn how to go about using the self clean function.  I followed the directions step by step for both easy clean and self clean.  

After about an hour of running the self clean cycle, the lights in my home dimmed and I heard a loud pop noise come from the oven.  As I was not in the kitchen at the time the event occurred, I made my way to the kitchen to find the oven was extremely hot.  The oven became hot enough that it began melting the glue holding the adjacent laminate counter tops together.  As the oven was still running the cycle and in the locked position I pulled the oven away from the wall and let it continue to run the cycle as the directions stated should happen.  When the cycle was complete and the oven had cooled down I opened the oven door to inspect for damage.  Much to my surprise I found the seal around the oven door and door itself had sustained damage.  Pictures below.  The damage to the oven door is permanent and not able to be cleaned. 

Ive spent the last 3 months trying to find a solution to the problem at LG Electronics who is the manufacturer of the product.  LG states they feel the problem was due to user error resulting in "cosmetic" damage only.  LG refused to understand that the clean cycle was run using the exact instructions given in their users manual and the oven still became hot enough to cause burns if touched and almost started a fire.
justification: The incident involved property damage (oven seal and countertop) but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with proper use.

incident_description: Rival toaster that started a home fire.
justification: A toaster starting a home fire is an incident with potential for property damage but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Interior glass shattered during the self clean cycle. Oven was installed in February 2015. This was the first time I used the self clean feature. The retailer I purchased the oven from has a service department and will send a technician to look at the oven on 7/20/15.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no injury was reported, and the issue appears to be isolated to the first use of the self-clean feature.

incident_description: I removed the heating elements and the drip pans to clean up the stove. I lift the top of the cooktop and use a cleaning wipe to clean and I received a strong electrical shock.
justification: The individual received a strong electrical shock, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I had mixed breakfast casserole ingredients in my largest duralex bowl, transferred the mix into a baking dish then washed my bowl.  As I was rinsing the soap out of the bowl it EXPLODED in my hands!  It sounded like a firecracker went off next to me, shooting fine shards of glass clear into the dining room.  It cut my arm, and fine shards of glass were in my fingers, neck, etc.  I cut my feet trying to find a clear course out of the kitchen.  There were thousands of small pieces of glass throughout my kitchen and dining area.  The water was hot, but not that hot and I had not cooked in the bowl nor did it go in the microwave.  I am afraid to use my other bowls made by this company, I would have thought if the bowl was compromised it would have cracked, but not explode!
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts and injuries from exploding glass, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) because such explosive failures of glassware are rare under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
I have had multiple Crate and Barrel glassware items spontaneously crack or break under normal use. 

Today, I had a wine glass spontaneously crack while sipping from it.

Previously, I had a tall drinking glass break in half while washing. The base of the glass fell off. Crate & Barrel replaced the glass and the replacement also cracked and broke.
justification: Glassware breaking under normal use poses a risk of minor injury but no severe harm has been reported in the description.

incident_description: GE microwave oven starts on its own.
justification: The microwave starting on its own is an incident with no injury, and such occurrences are uncommon but documented.

incident_description: Kitchenaid Stovetop Oven model KDRP407HSS4. The oven goes on by itself. The dial is on the "reset" position and the oven's broiler goes on anyway. It is a very dangerous fire hazard. There is no reason for the oven to go on when the dial is in the off position.
justification: The oven turning on by itself poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she experienced similar problems of recall#15-142 with her range.  Hazard: The stainless steel trim below the range control panel can have a sharp edge, posing a laceration hazard to consumers.  She stated that she had receive minor laceration on her left ankle, however, she is not concerned about that, she needs the range to be included in the recall because of the danger it poses.



11/2014 The retailer was contacted and she was advised that the unit was not included in a recall.
justification: The caller received a minor laceration from the sharp edge, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is known but not widespread, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: I purchased this appliance on 03/26/15 in new condition. All inner packaging was in place, books, registration card, etc.  I sent my registration card in to Kitchenaid(Whirlpool) within the week.  The first time I used the self cleaning option was in June.  As we sat at breakfast in the kitchen about 45 minutes into the cleaning we heard a loud bang and looked over and there was shattered glass all over the kitchen. There were kids and pets in the kitchen. My niece ended up with glass in her foot. Luckily no serious injuries. I have owned many ovens and used the self cleaning options many times. I have never seen anything like this happen. Our NEW oven is completely inoperable. I have contacted Kitchenaid and because I don't have a receipt they will not warranty the glass.  They claim they don't do anything with your registration cards. They show it registered to Sears in 2012 and said it may have been a floor model.  I don't see how glass exploding during a normal oven function is a warranty issue. This is definitely a manufacturing issue.  The glass could not handle the heat plain and simple. What kind of glass are they using?  I do know it was a discontinued model and although we received a discount we still spent over $1500. Now they want to sell us a part for $75 + shipping.  I am not convinced this won't happen again.
justification: The incident resulted in glass shattering and a minor injury (glass in the foot), warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the user's extensive experience without prior incidents.

incident_description: Upon putting bacon on the large front burner, there was a burst of fire with a loud bang and the coiled burner popped and cut a whole clean through the pan.  It also put a crater in the coiled burner.
justification: The incident involved a burst of fire and damage to equipment, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was home with my two children when I heard popping noises coming from my stove.  Black smoke was coming out of the top, from behind the stove where the clock was on the control area.  I then saw flame reflecting in my glass tile back splash.  I called the fire department, got my children out and used a fire extinguisher to extinguish the fire and the fire department assisted when it arrived and removed the stove from my home. The stove was a smooth top electric range that spontaneously started on fire. It was a Frigidaire Gallery, Model No. FPEF3081KFC, Serial No. VF02163339.  The internal portion that ignited was behind the clock/electronic controls.  I have photographs, but have been unable to upload them to this complaint.
justification: The incident involved a stove fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported; the fire was extinguished without harm.

incident_description: Dishwasher overheated and went on fire
justification: The dishwasher overheating and catching fire is an incident with potential for injury, but the description does not mention any harm.

incident_description: I was cooking corn on the cob in water on y electric cooktop stove. The water had come to a boil and I added the corn to the pot. after it had been cooking for a few minutes I went to check on it and touched my finger pads to the cooktop surface (not the burned eye). The cooktop had heated up enough to give my 2nd degree burns on 2 figure and started warping the cooktop itself. The pot was slightly larger than the burner itself so I can only imagine the heat was transferred from the pot, but it still seems like the design should have allowed for more space between the top of stove and pot or pan.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as burns can occur when touching hot surfaces, though not every cooking session leads to such injuries.

incident_description: While using the machine to make coffee I was burned when the water started to boil over and escape from the top where the "K" cup is located
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from boiling water, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My ceramic range elements, on the right side, began independently coming on and heating up.  I found out through a forum that this was a recall.  I came here to check and indeed it was.  I went to the site and my model was in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a recalled product malfunctioning without causing injury, fitting the criteria for severity level 2.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bosch double wall oven from Aus-Tex Appliances in February of this year (2015) and installed it in my summer kitchen, which is in a covered patio in South Florida. After using the oven a maximum of three times total, I turned the oven on to preheat it, and after reaching approximately 375 degrees F, the inside glass shattered.

I contacted Bosch, as the oven should have been under warranty, and they sent a technician out. He is refusing to fix the issue, because the oven was installed outdoors, although it is in a covered summer kitchen in an enclosure that meets building codes.

After researching the issue online, it appears that this exact situation is not uncommon, and that there was an issue with improperly tempered glass being used in this type of oven.

Bosch now wants to charge me $180 for labor and $60 for the glass.

According to my sister, who was onsite when the technician arrived, he spent 30 minutes examining the oven and talking with someone on the phone, looking for ways in which the warranty might not be applicable.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass) but no injury or death, and the issue appears to be a known problem with the product.

incident_description: Pyrex 4 qt glass bake ware:  I preheated for just  a few minutes, my pyrex bake ware today.  Immediately upon taking it out and placing it on my stove top (which was hot also - it is electric so was hot from the oven being on), the pyrex glass bake ware exploded sending chards of glass all over the kitchen.
justification: The incident involved glass bakeware exploding, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: I purchased a Danby chest freezer at Costco. We immediately noticed that the freezer top locked after we shut it. Initially we thought it was a safety feature but could not find a release, nor could we find any info on it locking in the manual or on Danby's website. We contacted Danby today-their customer service person told us it was not possible for this to happen and that we should pull harder or put vegetable oil on the gasket to make it easier to open. Or, to return it if we were not happy with it. We do plan to return it, however I have many concerns about the potential safety concerns of this and who knows how many other units. My husband and 20 year old son were not able to force the lid open until several minutes later when it opened without any problem. If a child were to get into it-witnessed or not there would be no way to open the top. As a RN and a mom I am very concerned about the potential for injury with this product and wanted to let someone besides the manufacturer know, Thanks.
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard with the freezer lid locking unexpectedly, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I turned my oven on last night to pre heat, I went in about 10 minutes later. I saw what I thought was the oven light on, I opened it to place dinner in the oven and saw that the light was not on, the coil in the oven was glowing like a hot ember and sparks were shooting from it. I immediately turned off the oven. I noticed that that section of the coil was disintegrating. What would have happened if I left to run my errand and left my teenage children home alone? I have never had nor seen an oven where the coil has broken down..
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven coil with sparks, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Using a Kenmore electric range, the oven was turned off after baking.  Later the oven turned back on and could not be shut off using the controls.  After removing the range from the premises, the back panel was removed and there was evidence of a fire at the back side of the oven light and appears to have spread up above.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven, which is a significant safety hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: We had a freak accident with an Emerson toaster oven (Model TOR59). We own a red Emerson toaster oven. Last week it was sitting on the kitchen counter (wasn't being used, and hadn't been used at all that day) and the glass shattered and fell all over the counter and the kitchen floor. There was nothing around it to suggest what may have caused it. Fortunately nobody was in the kitchen at the time and didn't get hurt. Please see the pictures for more details. this product is definitely not safe for use. I hope you will take some action.
justification: The toaster oven shattered without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description:
On 06/22/15 when the consumer opened the microwave door by pushing the release button, the microwave began running. The consumer noticed the light inside the microwave turned on and the turntable began to spin. Once the consumer closed the door the microwave shut off. The consumer states he did not set the timer on the microwave. 

The consumer tried to repeat the steps and the microwave continued to turn on when the door was opened. The consumer states he never set the timer on the microwave. 

On 06/22/15 the consumer contacted the firm's support department (800-243-0000) and informed them of the incident. The consumer was told by a rep (name unknown) that this was a known issue but there was no recall. The consumer was told that his unit could be repaired at his own cost. 

The unit is used daily. There are no prior incidents.

The consumer believes the door latch is defective and poses a safety hazard.
justification: The microwave operates unexpectedly when the door is opened, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he is not the original owner of the range, having purchased it approximately on 09/15/2014. He estimates the original owners used the unit for ten years.

06/23/2015 - The consumer was using the range's oven and had it set to BAKE at 400 degrees Fahrenheit. Approximately ten minutes later, the consumer noticed that the oven had switched its setting to BROIL after the range had beeped and displayed error code E2F3 (the consumer searched online for what the code meant: overheat/ over-temp). The consumer tried changing the setting back to BAKE and it would not change. The consumer proceeded to turn off the oven and the display turned off. It was not until about five minutes later that he noticed that the oven had never shut off as it was still extremely hot and the upper elements were still bright red. At this point, the consumer tripped the circuit breaker supplying energy to the range.

The consumer's food was burnt.

The consumer states that he did not notice any damage to the range in general or the oven specifically, most likely because he was able to catch the problem in time. The consumer states that he has not tried turning the unit back on. The consumer states that this is the first time he has had any issues with the range or its oven.

06/24/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained what happened with his unit. He was informed that the unit was not under warranty and so any repairs would have to be paid in full by the consumer. The consumer was also informed that his unit is not included in any recall.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that overheated but did not cause injury or damage, only resulting in burnt food.

incident_description: I purchased the Presto PopLite Hot Air Popcorn Popper model 04820.  When making popcorn the machine spit out hot corn kernels, some of which hit my son in the side of his neck as he was standing approximately 3-4 feet from the counter.  This caused two burns on his neck which peeled off the top layer of skin.
justification: The incident caused burns that peeled skin, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Given the product's design, such occurrences are possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Caller stated that her spouse was drinking from the 10 cup water filter jug because he was not able to find a cup.  When he swallowed the water he realized that he had swallowed the plastic cap from the opening of the filter.  She took him to Progress West hospital in St Louis where it was removed surgically, he was treated and sent home.

Caller feels that this product is a safety hazard that could have been fatal and feels that it should be reported for a recall.
justification: The incident resulted in a surgical procedure to remove the plastic cap, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Microwave oven runs when the door is opened.
justification: Microwave running with the door open is an incident with potential for harm, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
The Samsung RF 263 refrigerator that has an unsafe design.  There are many instances on the internet describing the defect and how to temporarily fix it.

 It is supposedly an auto defrost but the design is incorrect and the defroster freezes up, blocking the fan and ultimately turning off the refrigerator.  I just discovered this when I went to get some milk and found the refrigerator at 65 degrees F.

A call to Samsung found they knew how to fix it (manual defrost) but they disowned the problem.

This refrigerator is a crap shoot with salmonella.  I can imagine an older person who is not attentive getting very sick from the food kept in this refrigerator after the defroster turns off the compressor.
justification: The refrigerator's design flaw can lead to food spoilage and potential health risks, but no actual injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
Microwave oven repeatedly turned itself on without any user interaction. This happened about every 3 minutes. The display showed "Express" and the oven appeared to be fully activated (turntable spinning, light on, motor running, etc). I kept turning off the oven using the keypad.

When I opened the door to prevent the problem from occurring, the oven appeared to try starting by itself again. After a few attempts, the oven began to beep and a message showing "keypad needs service" showed on the display
justification: The microwave malfunctioned repeatedly without causing injury, but posed a potential hazard due to unintended activation.

incident_description:
On Sunday, June 28, 2015, I was roasting something in my GE Profile Oven.
As I was standing in the kitchen with my son, we heard a humming sound, then a buzzing sound, then -all of a sudden- sparks and a ball of fire were in the oven cabinet.  I started to run to the stove but then my son told me not to go near it.  My husband heard my screams and he came in and turned off the stove.   It then went completely dead.  I have been extremely distressed about this...the product was only 6 years old, and just off the extended warranty.  I also have been having anxiety attacks thinking about what might have happened if we weren't there at the time this happened.

I called GE, and they sent a service man to look at the unit, and he determined that the convection unit malfunctioned and the fire in the cabinet destroyed the computer.  The estimate to repair was about $700.

When I went back to the store where the product was purchased, and conveyed my disappointment that the stove was only 6 years old, the salesperson replied "well, they only make them to last 7-10 years anyway"......
justification: The incident involved sparks and a fire in the oven cabinet but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the description of a malfunctioning convection unit.

incident_description:
Arching within the microwave when rack is in place.
Whirlpool model WMH32519CTI
Ser # TR47718220
Purchased 2-5-15
Whirlpool advises they will do nothing because the rack was in place.
Our concern is that the user may be out of the kitchen when the arching occurs which may cause a fire and or electrical failure.
Why sell a microwave with a shelf/rack & tell the owner not to use it.
This information was not provided at time of sale nor prior to installation.
justification: The incident involves arcing in the microwave when the rack is in place, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: oven liner expanded causing racks to fall thru
justification: The incident describes racks falling due to an expanded oven liner, which is an operational issue but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
On a Monday morning I was walking out the door to head to work.  I'd forgotten to take my cold medicine, so I went back in for just a second to get it.  While getting a glass of water I heard a buzz/sizzle sound in the kitchen.  I looked around, but didn't know where it was coming from.  About 15 seconds later I heard it again, followed by a slight whiff of electrical burn.  Within about 30 seconds my kitchen was filling up with black smoke coming from under the refrigerator.
I looked behind and saw sparks.  I unplugged the unit and it stopped.  I removed the back panel and saw that the connector to the compressor and the wires into it were charred black.  I don't know if there had been any flames, as it was caught right away.  If I hadn't gone back into the house at that moment and caught it, I'm scared for what might have happened to my sleeping family and pets, and everything I own.  Now I see that there was a recall in 2009 due to this very issue and fire hazard. I register everything, so I'm shocked that I was not notified about this as they have my contact information.
I had to get a new refrigerator, and it was NOT a Maytag !!!
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire hazard that was caught early, preventing injury or death, but caused property damage and required replacement of the refrigerator.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his electric Range purchased sometime in 2011, he believes that the computer is damaged and the range is not heating properly.

The alerts read that the burner is on when it isn't on.
When he is cooking on the range the temperature fluctuates no matter what temperature he sets it to reach and remain.
The oven at times after food is checked mid cooking does not continue cooking it turns itself off.  Related stains marks trapped between the inner and outer section of the glass door

He is reporting the range as having a possible short in the wiring that could potentially lead to a fire hazard.

There are no injuries to be reported

Manufacture was first contacted in 2012 in reference to glass door.  Told at the time that the door was not covered.

He contacted the manufacturer around April 14th and May 5th or 6th, 2015 but was advised that he had owned it for over one year with warranty no longer active.

Addendum
2012  The first reported problem was in regard to the trapped staining in between the door glass: warranty department said that this was not covered and the glass needed to be replaced to correct.

6 /16/15   Awaiting replacement parts!
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range with potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description: My wife was using her Bella rocket extract pro blender to make her morning smoothie when the blade broke and came through the plastic container cutting her arm. Luckily it did not require medical assistance. But this could have caused serious injury had it been to the face or a small child near by. I have contacted the manufacturer several times and even sent reviews from other customers with the exact same issue. They claim they have never heard of this before and have closed the file. I have photos but no able to up load to this website.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut that did not require medical assistance, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to multiple customer reports of the same issue.

incident_description: Kitchen Aid stove has an intermittent probe problem that has caused the temperature to be set to 600 degrees which creates a fire hazard.
justification: The stove's intermittent probe problem creates a fire hazard, which is an incident but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Our refrigerator that we had bought in March of 2013 sparked an electrical fire out of no where July 3, 2015, I heard a frying sound, ran over to the refrigerator and smoke was coming out of the back of it, I threw the main breaker to the house because I am unable to pull the refrigerator out by myself, my oldest son helped me pull it out and unplugged it. My husband got home and removed the back at the bottom and can see the wires at the compressor are burnt and melted. If I had not been home we would have had a large fire. npw I'm without a refrigerator after special ordering this size for almost 1300.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire from the refrigerator, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I was putting a 8x10 pyrex baking dish into a cupboard and was putting a smaller baking dish inside.  Neither of the dishes were hot or cracked.  I put a slight pressure on the large dish with the small dish and the large dish exploded!  Shards, pieces and slivers of glass went into the cupboard, all over the kitchen floor, countertops and me.  Fortunatly I had on glasses and didn't get glass in my eyes.  My lens have three scratched places where the glass etched them.  I've had both pieces for years and have done this exact procedure many times before.  This was a very dangerous experience. 

Virginia
justification: The incident resulted in scratches on the glasses but no direct injury to the eyes, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description:
(03/28/2015) The consumer stated that she was cooking popcorn in the microwave. After about 30 seconds the microwave started sparking inside. The consumer opened the door. There was smoke inside and a hole above the metal rack.
