The consumer called Sears. A technician came out to look at the unit. The consumer was advised that the inside could be repainted. A tiny bottle of paint was sent to the consumer but she did not use it.

(05/12/2015) The consumer stated that the same thing happened a week ago. She stated that she was heating a little piece of meat skin on a paper towel. She laid the food on the rack per the instructions from the technician. She had the microwave set for 25 seconds. Almost immediately the groves that hold the rack caught on fire. When the consumer tried to open the door to the unit, it would not open. The consumer tried three times before the door would open. There was only smoke when she got the door open. 

(05/13/2015) The consumer stated that Sears sent another technician out. She was advised that the piece that burned out could be replaced. The consumer did not want the microwave repaired.

The consumer was offered a replacement.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence suggests a possible likelihood (3) of similar incidents.

incident_description: When I was using kettle, received a steam burn due to kettle not shutting off automatically when full boil point reached and continuing to keep boiling.
justification: The incident resulted in a steam burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Kettles failing to shut off is a known issue, making the occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description: I turned on the self cleaning cycle. After about an hour or so I noticed a burning order was coming from the oven. I turned the cycle off. When the door unlocked, I opened the oven. The plastic around the inside of the door had melted in some areas.
justification: The incident involved damage to the oven but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description:
(05/29/2015) The consumer noticed a piece of plastic in a glass of ice. The consumer looked at the auger and noticed that it was broken.


(06/08/2015) The consumer called the GE Customer Complaint number to advised the company of what happened. The consumer was advised to call CPSC.

According to information plastic particle or pieces swallowed when using ice could caused death or serious bleeding with emergency surgery.  How many needs to die before GE will change this to safe product?
justification: The description mentions a piece of plastic in ice and potential for serious harm, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
(06/05/2015) The consumer stated that he was warming a steak for one minutes. After  about three or four seconds the inside light began blinking off an on. The consumer opened the door and closed it. After he started the unit again, the microwave began making a grinding sound and was  sparking on the inside near the handle. 

The consumer will contact the manufacturer.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned with sparks and grinding sounds, posing a hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: 9x13 Pyrex glass baking dish shattered while I was carrying it from oven to place on counter.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: I purchased 6 espresso pots by the brand of Imusa.  This morning the last incident happened similar to the first two.  I make my coffee in the pot as usual.  All of a sudden the top portion of the pot blew off and their was coffee and coffee grinds all over my kitchen ceiling and walls.  If I had been close to the stove at that point it would have hit me in the face or head.  This is the 3rd time this has happened with the same type and brand of espresso coffee pot.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred. The occurrence is likely as it has happened three times with the same product.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her refrigerator purchased April 8th, 2011 from Lowes.com.
She had no problems with this refrigerator until around the second week in May 2015 when she noticed that the ice maker was not working properly.  
She contacted IV Appliance who sent a repair tech to her home.
She accepted a repair of a new ice bucket as well as other parts and she has been waiting for the parts to be delivered so that repair could be completed.

Around May 11th or 12th, the caller gave her 2 yr old granddaughter a cup of ice to chew on when she noticed the child was sucking on something that she told her to spit out.
The child spit out a clear piece of plastic that was sharp at one end, was approximately one inch large and in the shape of a triangle.

Later that same day the caller's  husband had a drink with ice and also found that a piece of 2" clear plastic, in the shape of a triangle and sharp on one end was in his mouth after a sip of his drink.

She still has the pieces of plastic from both incidents.

She contacted the manufacturer on May 12th, 2015 and their representative named [REDACTED]created case# [REDACTED] and sent a repair tech from A&E Appliances who said that they would replace the icemaker but the caller declined stating that she does not want another plastic auger with the same safety issues.

She contacted the manufacturer again and spoke with [REDACTED] who sent someone to her home May 21st, 2014.

She is reporting these incidents as choking and laceration hazards.

The manufacturer has stated that they will attempt to provide an upgrade and will inform caller when they do find one that they can put in her refrigerator but have not contacted her again.

She is not using the auger.
justification: The incident involves a choking and laceration hazard from plastic pieces in ice, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there is manufacturer's defect with her oven and it presents a burn hazard.

She stated that looking at the oven, it seems like the door does not close properly.  However, even when the door is closed properly, a person can stick their hand into the space between inside of the oven and the oven door.

The consumer contacted the manf in regards to this issue. They sent out a technician on 05/2015. The technician informed the consumer that the unit is working properly. He stated that the door is sealed properly. The technician informed the consumer that the oven is designed to be that way.

The consumer stated that her 15.5 months old daughter tripped near the oven. Her daughter grabbed onto the oven to maintain balance. The daughter's hand went into the oven space and got burned. The consumer took her to a doctor and was notified that her daughter received first degree burns on the hand.
justification: The incident resulted in first-degree burns to a child, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the design flaw allowing hand insertion and the child's injury.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his two door w/bottom freezer refrigerator purchased approximately eight years ago in Texas.
Around May/June 2014 he noticed that the light would sometimes go off when he or his family shut the door but other times the light would remain on.
He also noticed that the area around the light fixture would become extremely hot after very short periods of time and at times would remain on for over an hour.
At the times that it remained on for the longer periods of time he could smell the odor of burning electricity.
There are no injuries being reported.
He is reporting these incidents as a potential fire hazard and is asking for repair at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard with no injuries reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) due to the intermittent nature of the issue and the presence of burning odor.

incident_description:
Kenmore electric range purchased the Summer of 2013.
The caller had no problems with the range until June 14th, 2015 when the outside glass of the tempered glass door exploded and shot glass as far as 20 feet across the kitchen floor.

She notes that she had just used the self cleaning mode and it had completed the day before this incident.

The caller is reporting this incident as a laceration hazard if this glass was to hit a person especially in the eyes.

There are no injuries being reported other than a scrape on the caller's finger obtained while cleaning the glass up.

She contacted the manufacturer the morning of June 15th, 2015 and scheduled a repair tech for June 16th, 2015.

She has asked that manufacturers re-examine standards of the tempered glass that is being manufactured before someone is injured severely.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass door causing a minor scrape, but no serious injuries were reported.

incident_description: This concerns a Black & Decker FusionBlade Blender- PB1002 purchased at Target in December of 2014. I was clearing up the kitchen after dinner. Somehow I depressed the on button of my husband's personal smoothie maker (I think with the handle of a pan that was on the counter. At the same time my left hand passed against the blade of the machine, and it sliced my thumb and the palm of my hand. This is a unique product because the blade can be attached to one of two personal cups, and somehow the design allows for the motor to operate and the blade to spin even when there is no cup in place. The warnings in the instructions account for this, but since it's not my appliance and I don't use it or clean it, I didn't read the manual. This is definitely a candidate for recall based on dangerous design.
justification: The incident resulted in a sliced thumb and palm, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The design flaw makes such injuries possible if the blender is activated without a cup, suggesting a likelihood of 3 (possible).

incident_description: I turned on my Frigidaire gallery oven to preheat. Within a minute there was a loud buzzing noise from it and smoke came out of it. Before I could get to the breaker it popped. I inspected the oven and found that the light circuit had failed and had caused a short to the chassis of the oven. This caused an amount of current large enough to actually catch the insulation on fire. Had anyone been in contact with this oven with this current flowing they easily could have been injured or possibly killed or had there been any flammable foreign matter in the area it could have resulted in a fire. I contacted Frigidaire on multiple occasions with no response.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical fault that could have caused injury or death, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Self-cleaning Oven Range, 
model number: 790.97439802 
Serial number: VF00263283
I was baking bread at 325 degrees and after approximately 15 minutes, there was a fire in the oven. We tried to turn the oven off, but ended up having to shut the breaker off to cut power to the oven. Once we removed the bread, my husband turned the oven back on and the temperature read over 500 degrees. He then took an external thermometer and that read almost 700 degrees! Following instructions from Kenmore website, we again turned the breaker off for 30 minutes to "re-set" the oven. We waited a day and pre-heat ed the oven to 325 degrees...however, the same issue occurred with the oven reaching temperatures above 500 degrees! 
We called CPSC with our problem and they said there was no recall on our model number and they transferred us to Sears to talk with them. After explaining the problem, we were told that there were no service technicians and if we weren't comfortable using the oven we would just have to buy a new one! I asked to speak to a supervisor and was subsequently hung up on. I immediately called CPSC back and told them we were hung up on and they transferred us back to Sears customer service and yet again we were hung up on! I waited a few days and then called Kenmore to report this issue and said that after doing lots of research other Kenmore ovens (different model numbers, but looked the same as ours) had been recalled due to fires & we also found consumer complaints online for the EXACT model and serial numbers that had fires. The Kenmore representative,[REDACTED], said that we would have to pay for a service call and any parts that were replaced. I expressed my discomfort at having the same problem occur even after a technician "fixed" the problem. I stated we don't feel safe having this oven in our home and that the potential for property, and more importantly physical damage to my family is not an "acceptable risk" and requested to talk with a supervisor. [REDACTED] hung up on me! We then called our local store and got a call back yesterday from the store manager, [REDACTED] who was kind and very concerned about nit only the oven issue, but the fact that we weren't being heard and had been hung up on several times. She gave us another customer service phone number and I called today and spoke with [REDACTED]. She was great, but said all she could do was set a service call up. Unfortunately there are no direct service companies in our area in[REDACTED] so she said that they would try to find a company to come out to our home. I said that we really wanted to trade in our store for a different one and she said she understood, but she could not authorize that. The best she could do was give us a 15% discount on the purchase of a new oven. While this is a nice offer, we don't have the money to purchase a new oven, nor do we think we should since the oven is faulty and extremely dangerous! We have a case[REDACTED] I am now waiting for a service company to call us to give us an estimate on the home visit and set up an appointment.
The bottom line is that oven is not safe! Others with the same oven should be made aware of this serious fire hazard and there should be a recall on this model. As a consumer I feel that Sears and Kenmore should take the responsibility of their manufacturer deflect seriously and replace the oven to one that does not put my home and family in jeopardy.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven and dangerously high temperatures, posing a serious risk of injury or property damage, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Gas Cooktop 30" stainless steel cook top.  Four Burners Item # 02232533000.  Installed professionally and inspected by city fed by low pressure Natural Gas.  While cooking with a large pot the control knob became extremely hot causing minor burns.  Knob eventually melted from the heat before I could reduce the temperature.  This happen on the so called "Power Burner" with Medium-High Heat.

I would speculate a large part of this is a design flaw.  Most cooktops and stoves the controls are slightly below the cooking surface and protected by distance and sturdy heat resistant materials.  In the case of the Kenmore cooktop the controls are angled directly up towards the cooking surface and stand less than an inch from the cooking grate. The controls appear to be made of a flimsy light weight plastic.  Because of the nature of a smaller 30" cooktop larger pots will naturally extend ever so slightly over the edge of the grates and exacerbate an already subpar safety situation as the plane of heat is directed right onto the controls of the cooktop.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns due to the control knob becoming extremely hot and melting, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was using a small pot by Cuisinart to heat some water to make tea. After adding some tea leafs, I turned back to do something else in the kitchen until I heard a gun fire like sound. I turned back and saw tea was all over the range and gas was still on with some water and some tea still inside the pot. 

I had no clue what caused it all and decided to drain out the water. I noticed a shining object in the sink and tried to retrieve but it went through the drain. I then noticed that a piece of metal that covers the screws inside the pot was missing, which I believe caused a little explosion. 

I know for fact that had I not turned away after adding tea to hot water, the hot water would have splashed over my face.

Making tea is very routine for me and this has never happened before. I would like to request the contents of this pot are inspected to ensure it's safe to use it to cook hot meals and it can sustain hot temperatures.
justification: The incident involved a small explosion with no injury, but potential for harm if the user had not turned away.

incident_description: Black and decker 4 slice toaster caught fire in my kitchen when not in use. No one was in the home or was injured.
justification: The toaster caught fire but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
My two children (ages 4 and 10) grabbed the tongs for a few moments while I was out of the room. They were brand new - not even out of the packaging yet. When the ten year old tried to take them from the four year old, the tongs slid through my younger child's fingers. His pinkie finger was sliced severely. There seems to be incredibly sharp metal on the inside of the handles.

The finger bled intensely, and required gluing in a ER to repair. We cannot tell if there is nerve damage.
justification: The child suffered a severe finger injury requiring medical treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the incident involving children and sharp objects.

incident_description: Interior light on LG refrigerator, model LFX25960ST, will not turn off, overheats, melts the light fixture and the top of the refrigerator as well as ruins all of the food in the refrigerator.  This first occurred in August 2014 and LG replaced the light fixture indicating that the new fixture contained a sensor which would turn off the light and prevent overheating.  The new fixture has now also remained on, overheated, melted the fixture as well as further damaged the top of the refrigerator.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted fixture, damaged refrigerator, ruined food) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I see a recall has been issued for the "Kenmore Elite Ranges Recalled by Electrolux Due to Laceration Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Sears from May 2014 through April 2015."  However, my gas range also has a laceration hazard and I have felt it while cleaning before. It is located along the horizontal bottom edge of the stainless steel below the range control knobs. I noticed it a long time ago, but had no idea I could submit a safety concern on this website until I saw the recall for the newer model.  The one that I have is the KENMORE GAS RANGE, Model #790.77483801. I do not remember when I bought it, but I do know I bought it from Sears.
justification: The user reports a laceration hazard but no actual injury, fitting severity level 2. The hazard is present and has been noticed before, indicating a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description:
I am the owner of a General Electric side by side refrigerator model PIE23NGTCFSV. This refrigerator comes with an ice dispenser. I gave my 5 year old son - who has autism - a glass of water with ice - dispensed from the refrigerator. After a few minutes I saw him choking. I found in his mouth a piece of plastic (clear color - same as the ice!!! - photo included). This came from the auger (located in the ice drawer) which pushed the ice from the drawer - through the dispenser to the glass. 

Kindly note the following:
It is the 3rd time this part breaks on my refrigerator. The last time (2nd time) was a year and a half ago. At that time I raised my concerns as to the safety of this product, and the GE authorized technician informed me that this happens because the ice drawer over-floats (which is true). He claimed that GE is aware of this and have changed the part that stops the production of ice in the dispenser, so that this does not happen. He advised me to purchase the new part and replace the old one, so that this does not happen again, which I did in order to prevent any future accidents. 

I decided to raise this safety concern with you, as I read in Amazon comments that other people - in the US- had swallowed parts of the auger.
justification: The incident involved a child choking on a piece of plastic from the ice dispenser, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The recurrence of the issue and reports from other users suggest the likelihood is possible (3).

incident_description:
I was using my Kenmore Microwave oven to prepare bacon using a covered dish manufactured specifically for microwave bacon cooking.  The dish contained all grease/spatter so none got on the microwave.
During cooking, the microwave stirrer cover on top of the cavity spontaneously caught fire and partially burned.
I was able to extinguish the fire without harm or further damage.  There was no grease buildup or any other contributing factors on or around the stirrer cover.  The inside of the oven was clean at the time of the fire. 
The cover was the only thing that burned, although the top of the cavity suffered some fire damage.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but was extinguished without harm or injury, and the damage was limited to the stirrer cover and top of the cavity.

incident_description:
I am writing to make you aware of exploding oven glass doors.  I had this to happen to me when I was out shopping on Wednesday, 6/24/15. The oven was not on nor was it plugged into the power source.   Glass was on the floor - spread a couple of feet away from the stove.  I own a Sears Elite Gas Range - model 790-7754-3800, purchased in October 2010.  

I goggled this problem and found there are many such cases documented online.  I HAVE SEEN NO WARNING ABOUT THIS.  There is no warning in the manual  Also it was not only Sears mentioned but [REDACTED].  

Today, Friday, 6/26/15. I called the Sears Headquarters in Hoffman Estates to see what they had to say about this incident.  I spoke with [REDACTED] in Customer Solutions at approximately 4:15 p.m.  After explaining my problem, [REDACTED] put me on hold for about 5 minutes.  He came back to tell me there were neither government nor Sears recalls on this product.  I told [REDACTED] that, from the number of times Sears was mentioned in the incidents cited online, Sears had to know something about their exploding oven glass doors.  Suddenly, I was disconnected from [REDACTED]. 

I called back and was connected to [REDACTED] who, after hearing my story said, if I wanted a complete new door that would eliminate this problem, he would give me the number for the manufacturer who might give me a replacement for free.  I asked what would I do with a new door.  He said Sears could install it, but I would have to pay for their service if I didnÃÂt have their warranty.  I was more than disappointed by Sears since I have been a loyal customer for many years.



While we were not home when the glass exploded from our oven, there are many stories online when people were home and some injured.  Our damage was lessened only because I hang decorative towels on the bar handle of my oven and it diffused the explosive spread from doing damage to other appliances.  



[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven glass door with no injury, and similar cases are documented online indicating it's a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I was baking in my Thermador double oven and during the process I was able to observe a flame inside the lower oven about 4" in height that appeared on the bottom heat element.

I turned off the oven while it was filling quickly with smoke.  I kept the door shut so the flame would eventually die out.  After the oven was vented, you could see that a rupture in the heat element had occurred and various spots on the heat element had corroded (pictures are available).  I called Thermador and they sent out a technician on June 24th to conduct a diagnosis.  The tech looked into the oven and said it was due to wear and tear.

This is the third heat element I have had to replace in these units.  I have been a homeowner for 25 yrs. and this is my third house.  I've never seen this happen in any oven before and feel there must be some sort of manufacturing defect with these heat elements and am concerned that it is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a flame and smoke but no injury or death, and the issue has occurred multiple times, indicating a possible manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
At 4:00 pm I opened the GE Profile PDW9980L00SS dishwasher door and saw that I had 1 minute left of my speed cycle with added heat drying.  I closed the door and 10 minutes later reopened the dishwasher door.  At this time, the dishwasher display said that the cycle was over and the dishes were clean.  I removed some of the standing water left in the cups and kept the door ajar for the dishes to cool down and dry further.
At 7:00 pm, my husband put away the clean dishes / utensils out of the dishwasher and put in dirty ones.  He fully shut the dishwasher door but did not touch any buttons to turn it on.
At 12am, I smelled something burning.  It was the dishwasher (2 floors lower than when I originally smelled it).  When we opened the dishwasher door, nothing but smoke and chemical smells came out.  The windows and doors were opened immediately.  The granite countertop above the dishwasher was hot to touch.  
The heating element never turned off from the "completed" cycle, and when my husband shut the door it just stayed on heated dry.  It was so hot, the plastic utensil holder in the dishwasher melted and my silverware fell out to the bottom of the heating element.  The dishwasher's rotating arm melted until the metal was showing.  I had a heavy duty plate made for microwave cooking, that melted.  
The dishwasher is obviously ruined with nothing but melted plastic at the bottom of it.  Most of the plastic liquefied was part of the actual dishwasher itself.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage (melted dishwasher components) but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
This is another incident with a different consumer with the same stove as another comment - 

Incident Description Sears Kenmore smooth top range model number 79096009601 both front burners will stay on high after range has been turned down or off completely. Burners will turn on spontaneously. These are the same symptoms of Kenmore Elite and Frigidaire smooth top ranges recalled August 28th 2009. 
See below: 

About 200,000 Frigidaire and Kenmore Elite Smoothtop Electric Ranges have been recalled after 126 reports of problems with a defective heating elements, which could turn on spontaneously, fail to turn off or heat to different temperatures than what is selected. 
The U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission announced the electric range recall on August 27, involving of several models of Frigidair, Frigidair Gallery, Frigidair Professional and Kenmore Elite smooth top ovens with rotary knobs and digital displays on the electric range. 

At least four reports involving burns and two reports of property damage have been linked to the defective smooth-top ranges. Consumers have been urged to immediately stop using them until a free repair can be arranged. 

All of the affected rangers were manufactured by Frigidaire, and sold at Sears and other stores throughout the United States between June 2001 and August 2009. 

The recall affects Frigidaire models with serial numbers from VF 122xxxxx through VF831xxxxx and model numbers beginning with FEFBZ90GC, FEFLMC55GC, FEFLZ87GC, GLEF396AB, GLEF396AQ, GLEF396AS, GLEF396CQ, GLEF396CS, GLEFM397DB, GLEFM397DQ, GLEFM397DS, GLEFM97FPB, GLEFM97FPW, GLEFM97GPB, GLEFM97GPW, LEEFM389FE, PLEF398AC, PLEF398CC, PLEF398DC, PLEFM399DC, PLEFMZ99EC, PLEFMZ99GC, PLEFZ398EC, and PLEFZ398GC. The recall also affects Kenmore Elite models with serial numbers from VF122xxxxx through VF334xxxxx and model numbers beginning with 790.99012, 790.99013, 790.99014, and 790.99019. 

NEED I SAY MORE???
justification: The incident involves burners turning on spontaneously, which has led to burns and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3 due to reported injuries.

incident_description: I purchased a Vita-Mix 7500 blender online based on Consumer Reports high rating.  After cleaning it, I tested it out.  Tiny black particles were emitted into my food; about the same amount on each of 5 tests (maybe 30-50 visible particles in 2 cups of water in a white bowl; the water was free of visible particles prior to being blended).  Online research finds many such reports; apparently Vita-Mix has told consumers the particles are Teflon shards coming from an O-ring on the blade assembly.  Not every individual blender is affected, but all models may be involved.  They have not recalled the blenders, stating Teflon is inert and therefore safe for consumption.  A redesigned container and blade apparatus is being worked on and may be ready at the end of 2015.  I notified Consumer Reports for their awareness in rating these blenders, and they suggested I contact CPSC, as well.  Teflon may be inert, but it seems irresponsible to sell a product touted as useful for healthy eating, even as you're aware that parts of the apparatus are being consumed with that healthy food.
justification: The incident involves the emission of Teflon shards into food, which is a health concern but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
05/19/2015 - The consumer's wife turned the oven on to bake potatoes. When oven was turned on, oven buzzed, then flames shot out.  The consumer's wife noticed smoke coming from the unit. When the consumer was closer to the unit, she noticed that flames were being shot up from behind the unit. The consumer's wife had yet placed the potatoes inside the oven to bake.

The consumer's wife was able to contain the fire by moving the range from the oven door in order to disconnect it. When the consumer's wife moved the range, the maple hardwood floor underneath it was scratched; aside from this, the consumer has no other damages to report.

The consumer indicates that after the incident happened, him and wife have tried a couple of times to plug the unit back on to see if it would work or if it would display error codes but it does neither. 

05/19/2015 - The consumer contacted the retailer and explained the situation. The consumer was then referred to the manufacturer. When he explained the situation, he was informed his unit was included in a recall and that he would receive a call back so that they can arrange for an inspection of the unit. 

05/21/2015 - Having not heard from Kenmore, the consumer contacted them again. This time, he was informed that his unit was not under warranty nor included in any recall and thus no assistance would be provided to him. He was referred to the US CPSC so that the agency "can resolve his issue."

The consumer indicates that prior to the incident and for approximately the past three years, the unit would give error codes that would eventually go away when the consumer's wife would turn off and turn the unit back on. The consumer is unaware how frequently these error codes appeared. The consumer never contacted the retailer nor the manufacturer of the unit regarding the error codes as the unit functioned correctly after it was restarted. The consumer is unaware what type of error codes the unit was displaying.

The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the oven, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had few splatter on the inside wall of the oven. The consumer started the self clean feature for 1 hour to clean up the splatter.

The consumer stated that she started working around the house when she notified by her grandson that the knobs on the unit were melting. 

The consumer stated that she went and checked on the unit. She saw that all 5 of the knobs and the perimeter of the oven door was melting. The consumer stated that the plastic on the knobs melted and dripped onto the floor. The perimeter of the door melted into the oven. 

The consumer stated that her hood/microwave unit above the range became discolored. She stated that the fan turned on in the microwave. The consumer stated that it is a safety feature that turns on automatically when the microwave overheats.

The consumer stopped the clean feature. The unit was locked until it cooled down.

The consumer stated that she cleaned off the melted plastic from the floor. The consumer stated that some melted plastic is still on the knobs. 

The consumer stated that this happened about 45 minutes into self cleaning.

The consumer contacted Sears. They informed her that there are no recalls on her unit. They informed her that because she did not have a maintenance agreement on the unit, they could not provide repair.

The consumer stated that there were no injuries. The consumer has not used the unit since then.
justification: The incident involved melting knobs and oven door, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
GE JES1142SPSS 1.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Countertop Microwave

Bought in Jan 2014, built in July 2013.

Unit emitted burning plastic smell during operation; a noise then followed, before my wife was able to turn unit off.  As off key failed to turn off unit, she opened the door to stop operation.  The power plug was removed from the outlet and the unit was immediately removed from the kitchen and placed in storage.
justification: The microwave emitted a burning smell and noise, but no injury occurred as the unit was turned off and unplugged.

incident_description: On 6/11/2015, I preheated my oven to 425 degrees.  When it reached temperature, I placed a Pyrex 9 x 13 glass baking dish with olive oil and fish into the oven to bake.  Halfway through baking the fish, I opened the oven door to turn the fish.  The glass casserole dish exploded sending pieces of glass into the oven.  I was not hurt but I left the oven door open and backed away to let the dish cool before trying to remove it or clean up the glass.  After about fifteen minutes, I used pot holders to move the shattered dish to the stove top to cool further.  The stove top was cool and had not been on.  Five minutes later, it exploded again, sending more glass flying.  I have never had a Pyrex dish do anything like this before.  The oven temperature was not excessively high and there was a slight coating of oil in the pan, so it was not dry.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding twice but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. Such occurrences are rare, hence the low likelihood score.

incident_description:
I purchased a VisionsÃÂ®4-Pc Cookware Set and have been using them for a little over a year. On 5/5/15 When I was using the bigger piece (2-1/2L Round Stewpot), the pot cracked ~2 hours into cooking with low heat on the stove. The pot suddenly split completely in half. It nearly spilled the hot chicken soup on my son and created a big mess in the kitchen. This is not only a product issue but also extremely dangerous as my family could've been hurt. This product has been around for years, and I am appalled to be experiencing something like this.  This pot is meant to be used over a stove and I did not receive a warning not to use it on a stove.

I tried contacting the company on 5/6 and was unsuccessful.
justification: The pot cracked and nearly spilled hot soup on the son, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: On Saturday, June 20, 2015, around 1:30 my GE oven door exploded. My eight year old hit it with a spoon, and glass went flying. Thankfully, he didn't get hurt, and my little boys were nowhere near the kitchen when it happened. I found little shards of oven door glass in my dining room, too.
justification: The oven door exploded but no one was injured, placing it at severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as rare since such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
On 05/31/15 the consumer used the oven mitt to take out a baking sheet (11" x 15") from the oven. The baking sheet was in the oven for about 15 minutes and the oven was set to 375 degrees. The consumer states seconds after grabbing the baking sheet he felt his finger tips burning. The consumer dropped the baking sheet and removed the oven mitt. There are no burn damages on the oven mitt. The consumer has burn marks on his left middle and ring finger. The consumer states his ring finger has more severe burn damages. The consumer's sister is a nurse and treated the consumer's fingers. The consumer did not go to the hospital or visit a physician.

This was the first time the consumer used the oven mitt. 

On 06/01/15 the consumer emailed the firm, by filling out a form on the firm's website (www.bwtc.com) and informed them of the incident. The consumer received a response from [REDACTED], a firm's rep who offered the consumer another oven mitt. The consumer said [REDACTED] wrote in the email that depending on the weight and temperature of the pan it may require the use of 2 oven mitts to protect from any burns. 

The consumer is not accepting another oven mitt from the firm. The consumer believes the oven mitt poses a burn hazard to consumers and should not be sold.
justification: The consumer suffered burn injuries on their fingers, which were treated by a nurse but did not require hospitalization.

incident_description:
The consumer reported several issues with her gas range.

1) The consumer stated that the oven door does not properly shut. The heat escapes from the edges of the door and heats up the exterior of the unit. The consumer stated that it can cause severe burns. The consumer stated that the sticker and lettering around the knobs have burned and melted off. The consumer stated that the unit smokes a lot even if there is nothing placed in the oven. The consumer believes the reason that may happen is because the oven door is not properly sealed.  The consumer stopped using the oven portion of the unit.

The consumer stated that she has called the manf several time (since 2004) in regards to this issue. The consumer stated that they were unable to diagnose the cause of the issue. They informed her that they did not have any other reports on this issue. 

The consumer stated that she has received minor burns on her wrist and hand from the heated exterior of the oven.

2) The consumer stated that the burners will spark to ignite but do not flame. The consumer stated that the burner can try to ignite for up to 10 minutes without having a flame. The gas escapes the whole time. The consumer stated that sometimes when trying to turn on one burner the other burner starts to click to ignite.

When the consumer called the manf in regards to this issue, they asked her to clean the burners with rubbing alcohol. They did not provide any other assistance.

3) The consumer stated that in 2003 she had a repair work done on the unit. The consumer stated that the oven stopped heating. The consumer contacted the retailer about the issue. The range was out of warranty by then. A technician came out from the retailer and replaced the computer panel/board on the range. The consumer paid over $1000 out of pocket for the repair. 

The unit does not appear to be under any recalls.
justification: The consumer reported minor burns from the heated oven exterior and ongoing gas leakage issues, indicating injury and a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Caller stated that all the gas knobs on his range is sensitive, they do not ignite immediately when it is powered on, and if brushed against accidentally the gas escapes.  This incident started since he purchased it.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.  He stated that he noticed that other brands had the same complaints online and they maybe made by the same manufacturer.

Caller feels that these gas ranges with these knobs are extremely dangerous and should be recalled.
justification: The gas knobs are faulty and can lead to gas leaks, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description: I purchased a set of 3 Nuby Wash or Toss cups. Within the first use, my son dropped the cup on the ground a the cup itself cracked and leaked. I used another cup on another day, and when dropped, the area where the spout is on the lid cracked. Further, using the third cup, the cup was dropped and a small piece of plastic from the spout of the cup broke off completely. This plastic piece was small enough for a toddler to put in his mouth and choke on. Thankfully, my child did not swallow the plastic piece, but these products should be recalled before another child gets injured or chokes. Out of 3 cups, all 3 broke within a single use.
justification: All three cups broke upon first use, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
KENMORE ELECTRIC RANGE 665.95804000 serial RK 3613409
baking a roast at 350, niticed extra hot and broiler was on.  Could not turn broiler off, had to turn off circuit breaker.  Tried to restart and same thing happened.
THIS ID DANGEROUS AND A HUGE FIRE RISK, THIS SHOULF BE RECALLED.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range that could not be turned off, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The keurig usually heats up first and then starts dripping. This started dripping slowly at first. Then it got faster. Then the hot water just exploded and landed on my hand. I have second degree burns and blistering. Have reported to company.
justification: The incident resulted in second degree burns and blistering, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
On the evening of June 17th we were using a Zojirushi NS-LAC05XT rice cooker which was placed on a plastic cutting board on top of the grating for our gas ranges (which were off and cold, as was the oven).  The rice cooker exudes considerable steam and this placement allowed us to vent that steam from the house.  The cooking process takes more than 30 minutes and during that time we heard a loud POP.  My wife went inside to see what happened and called me saying "[REDACTED], THERE'S A FIRE!"

I had her give me a fire extinguisher and put out the fire but it was evident the rice cooker had exploded, melted the front of the cutting board into the gas grating and bowl.  Shrapnel from this explosion was in the melted board as the main source of the explosion was the bottom of the rice cooker, half of which was blown out.
justification: The incident involved a fire and explosion of the rice cooker, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Started my GE Front control (in slate color) dishwasher when I left for work. Came home to melted cups in top rack. Called appliance repair man who came and said that we could have had a fire, and that GE should be responsible for this.  Called GE, they say there is no recall on the model.
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused melted cups and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I removed some potatoes from a [slow cooker] and put them in the Rubbermaid clear glass storage container and it exploded within a few seconds.
justification: The incident involved an exploding container but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have the Nutribullet 900 Pro.  I have enjoyed it however this week while making a protein shake  (with mostly liquid and only about three ice cubes)  The blade broke off in my drink.  I did not notice it until after I drank my drink.  Luckily I did not ingest the blade.  It was in the bottom of the cup.
justification: The blade broke off but was not ingested, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while oven was on for approximately 10 mins and the oven outer glass door exploded.  The glass pieces shattered all over the kitchen floor.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.  There were no prior incident or service calls associated to this unit.


Caller feels that this oven door is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to shatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Put 2 cups [REDACTED] frozen organic rice into Pyrex bowl, covered with [REDACTED] wrap, poked air hole in [REDACTED] wrap, set microwave timer to cook 4 min.  In the middle of cooking heard sound like glass dish falling and breaking.  Looked into microwave and saw bowl had split.  It continued to fall apart as I watched, with some big pieces and some small shards.  No injuries, but a big mess.  The bowl was part of a set of three clear glass bowls which are at least 10 years old and have been used many times to microwave.
justification: The bowl broke during microwaving, causing a mess but no injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her daughter in law turned on the preheat (350/375 F) mode in the oven. The consumer stated that she walked into the kitchen about 2 minutes later and heard crackling sound. She saw flames coming from the back of her range. 

The consumer stated that the flames were about 3-4 inches high. The consumer's husband cut the circuit to the range. Her son used a fire extinguisher while waiting on the fire department. 

The consumer stated that the wall is charred from the flames. The microwave above the range has also turned black. 

The fire department came out within 15-20 minutes and moved the range outside for safety precautions. They informed her to not use the microwave until it was inspected.

The consumer contacted the retailer on 05/28/15.

The consumer had a technician from Sears come on 6/4/15. The technician informed the consumer that the range can be repaired for $310. The consumer was not interested in a repair. They offered her a 20% discount towards a new range. The consumer stated that she would like a replacement range but the technician informed her that since she does not have an extended warranty on the unit, Sears would not provide her with a replacement. The technician informed her that she can clean the microwave and continue using it. 

The consumer stated that she slightly burned her right arm while trying to help her husband move the range away from the wall. The consumer stated that Sears was not interested in her injuries.
justification: The incident involved flames and property damage, and the consumer sustained a slight burn injury while moving the range.

incident_description: I was in need of a new can opener as my wife was unable to easily use a manual opener any longer. We checked around and found a good deal at Kroger on a Proctor Silex 75217F. My wife liked the product and we thought all was well. Unfortunately during dinner I got choked. After a period of time I was able to get out of my throat what had become stuck. It in fact was not food but a micro thread size strand of metal. I looked around and found that this can opener is leaving micro, near invisible very sharp metal strands around the lid and they are falling into the can when you open them. This was an incredibly dangerous and scary situation. This did hurt the inside of my throat and I am incredibly fortunate that it did not go any lower and I was able to get it out. I thought maybe it was the can that it opened so I tried other cans and I ended up opening other cans and they ALL did the same thing. I truly believe this should result in an immediate recall of this product.
justification: The incident caused injury to the throat from metal strands, but no death occurred.

incident_description: Pampered Chef made a " slice and serve" cake cutter with a sharp serrated edge all around. I was using it to cut a cake and the handle broke.  That caused the serrated edge to cut my hand quite deeply.  I reported it to them, but they did not seem to think that they needed to recall the product or to report it to your office.  I do not want anyone else to get hurt. They sent a replacement and the handlebars been changed from the one they used before!
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut to the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) as the product has been modified, indicating a known issue.

incident_description: We purchased the product, Elite Platinum 1.7L Glass Cordless Electric Kettle (EKT-200) by Maxi Matic, less than 6 months ago.  It was put to normal use.  Yesterday, we smelt smoke coming out of the product.  Today, we saw that a wire on the bottom of the kettle burned through the plastic and was clearly visible.  It even melted some parts of the base.  We informed the company, asked if there was a recall, and asked for a refund.  They told us there was no recall on the product and denied a refund.  Because it is fire hazard, we are taking the additional step of reporting the product.
justification: The incident involved smoke and visible wire damage, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was broiling some things in the oven when all of a sudden I heard a pop sound in the kitchen and opened the door and saw the inside glass had shattered.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of oven glass, which could potentially cause injury but no injury was reported in the description.

incident_description:
(05/04/2014) The consumer stated that he loaded the dishwasher normally. The lights in the house were going dim. His son told him that the dishwasher was on fire. Small flames were coming from the top panel. Black smoke was pouring from the top of the dishwasher. 

The consumer opened the door of the dishwasher to cut off the power. The consumer also cut off the power at the circuit breaker.


(05/05/2014) The Consumer contacted Maytag. A service technician was dispatched on 05/08. It was determined that the product was not fixable. 

(05/06/2014) The consumer contacted Maytag and was advised that he could pick a new product from their web site at 30% off. The consumer have not responded to the offer.

The consumer accepted their with free installation & haul away offer.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, which is a significant safety hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was making a cup of coffee with my Keurig K10 Mini and hot water began coming out of the bottom during brewing, which I had never seen before (I've seen the water overflow, but it's never been hot water).  So my reaction was to open up the top lid and at that point hot water exploded all over my face and neck scalding me and burning my entire neck and chest.
justification: The incident resulted in scalding burns to the face, neck, and chest, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such occurrences are unlikely (likelihood 2) as the user noted it was the first time experiencing hot water leakage.

incident_description: While using my GE Cafe oven, the glass in the door exploded.  The oven was set at 365 degrees.  The middle of 3 layers of glass shattered, sending pieces of glass onto the floor.  Most of the glass showered down into the drawer beneath the oven.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but no injury was reported, only property damage.

incident_description: The is the second time our outside glass on our GE oven exploded sending pieces of glass that covered our kitchen floor.  We were not using it, had not bumped it or disturbed it in any way.  We heard the explosion and went to see what it was.  Our biggest concern is for our two small pets who eat in the kitchen and could have been killed by the flying glass!  If that happens, we will file a law suit, and it will be class action since so many people have experienced the same phenomena.  Our GE oven Model # P5968T P2CC.  The Serial # FV2 418 480.  We purchased it new on 4/9/11 from Tate Appliances in Oldsmar.  As I mentioned, this has happened once before and we had to pay to have it fixed in the amount of $300+.
justification: The glass explosion caused an incident with no injury, but poses a potential risk to pets and humans.

incident_description: Oour GE Microwave/Convection oven spontaneously started.  We were not using the device at the time although we did happen to be in the kitchen.  The buttons on the device would not allow us to turn off or reset the machine and the door wouldn't open.  We finally had to turn off the electricity in the kitchen and pry the door open with a screwdriver.
justification: The microwave started spontaneously and could not be turned off normally, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was cooking with my crock pot which had been cooking for 6 hours. I went to removed the lid when the food was
completed. The plastic handle separated from the glass attachment. I went to grab the lid before it fell on my foot and I
scalded my hand in doing so. I immediately called Rival Crockpot and informed them what happened. I spoke to a
[REDACTED] the supervisor. She was not sympathetic at all to what happened. She told me she was unable to talk to me about this injury until she had the pot returned to them for evaluation. I immediately sent her pictures via email the
night the injury occurred, of my scalded hand and crock pot I mailed the crockpot back to them and they received it on
3/30/15. I have called 7 times and each time [REDACTED] never returned my calls. I finally received a return call when I left a message that I was calling the Dept. of Consumer Affairs. [REDACTED] made multiple excuses (deaths in her family) for no return calls. She then stated that there was still no resolution to the claim and they would not be taking any
responsibility for this injury. I demanded my crock pot be returned to me and never has been. It is my crock pot and I
would like it back.
justification: The incident resulted in a scalded hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described scenario of a crock pot handle failure.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was heating up dinner in her oven. The consumer heard a buzzing sound followed by a pop/explosion. The consumer looked at the oven and saw that something was on fire. She took out the food. The consumer noticed that the bottom heating element was broken. The consumer stated that the heating element broke in two parts (small and large). The large part was on fire. 

The consumer tried to extinguish the fire with a fire extinguisher but it did not work. 

The consumer contacted a volunteer fireman. He took the unit out and unplugged it. The fire went out soon after the unit was unplugged

The consumer stated that there was no smoke. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer through e-mail on 4/30/15. The consumer did not have a model # and serial # at the time so they were unable to assist her.
The consumer purchased a new range which was delivered on 5/1/15. The delivery person from Home Depot also installed the new range. He took out the old unit and took it with him. He assisted the consumer in finding a model # and serial # on her unit.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer through e-mail with model # and serial # on 5/1/15. The consumer is still waiting to hear back.

The consumer believes that the unit was installed in the home by the builder when the house was built in 2001.

The range did not appear to be included in any recalls.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer states the space between the top door handle of the refrigerator and the freezer door handle is 3/8 of an inch. The consumer has injured his right thumb multiple times when using the refrigerator. The consumer did not seek medical attention. The consumer believes he could injure his thumb severely in the future while using the refrigerator. The consumer believes the refrigerator is not safe and the space between the 2 door handles should be bigger. 

The consumer has not contacted the firm and does not plan to. 

The space between top and bottom handle in consumer's box is about 3/8" so the consumer got his thumb wedged between a few times
justification: The consumer has injured his right thumb multiple times, indicating a recurring injury, though no medical attention was sought.

incident_description: I had purchased a rubber duck-themed "Room & Bath Thermometer" from Dreambaby Products (Tee-Zed Products, LLC; P.O. Box 1662, Jamestown, NC). In its initial use when drawing water in the bath tub for my 6 YO son, I noticed the cover on the underside of the product was easily displaced (coming off with just a slight amount of pressure), exposing a button battery. I tried several times to replace the battery cover in a manner that would make it more secure, but was unsuccessful. The battery cover does not include in its design a screw to hold it in place. Being familiar with the hazards of button battery ingestion among infants and toddlers, and the fact that this product is primarily intended to be used with this age group, I feel as though this product design poses an imminent hazard to consumers. The product packaging indicates that the product has been "Tested to Toy Standard (EN 71)."
justification: The incident involves a design flaw exposing a button battery, posing a hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was preheating the top oven of my dual gas oven - the lower oven was already cooking just fine.  As the upper oven was preheating I smelled and noticed smoke.  When I opened the oven door a huge flame (jumping out from the oven at least 10 to 12 inches and the width of the door) erupted and singed my forehead and eyebrows.  After running cold water on my head and face, I shut the oven off and called the manufacturer to file a complaint.  They indicated all that they could do was send a service technician to check it out.  The technician came and could not find the source of the flame out.  I am afraid to use the oven again and will be getting rid of it as soon as possible.
justification: The incident resulted in a flame that caused injury (singed forehead and eyebrows), warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the technician could not find the source, suggesting it's not a common issue.

incident_description:
GE 36" Gas Cooktop Model CGP650SETSS

Switch/valve for main burner became stick in on position and could not be turned off. Flame went out with resultant gas leak into house. Home had to be evacuated and fire department called to investigate. The fireman was ultimately able to turn off by using a pair of pliers to manipulate the valve stem.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak requiring evacuation and fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Jenn-Air wall oven/microwave combo along with a gas cook top on 10/15/2004 when I remodeled my kitchen.  In June 2005 the oven door feel off while my 13 year old daughter was baking.  Fortunately she was not injured and door was not damaged.  A factory authorized repair service was contacted and the technician replaced the hinges on 7/1/2005.  Approximately 5 years later, the door fell off again.  Again, no one was injured and the door was not damaged. We reseated the door in the hnge pins according to the instructions in the operator's manual and installation manual.  Now, 5 years later, the door fell off again, but this time the glass shattered into a million pieces.
I filed a complaint with Jenn-Air.
They stated that the door is not replaceable, but repairable if the parts are available.  I am doubtful that all of the required parts are available.  Anyway, do I want this door back on my oven??  When researching this problem, I noticed that there have been plenty of reports of the oven door falling off and I am sure Jenn-Air has even more that we don't know about.
This product is a serious safety problem and should have been recalled.  There is a chance of injury due to the weight of the door falling on a leg or foot, serious burns from a hot door, and danger from shattered glass.  Jenn-Air needs to take responsibility for the safety of their customers and rectify the problem by replacing the product with a safe door.
justification: The incident involved the oven door falling off multiple times, with no injuries reported but potential for harm.

incident_description: While doing nothing but standing in my kitchen the front glass on my 4 year old Kenmore oven exploded into a million pieces. Model number 790.92803010. Lucky no one was injured or this would be a different report. Sears says there is nothing they can do besides sell me new glass and have my pay to have it installed.
justification: The oven glass exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury. Such occurrences are unlikely but not unheard of.

incident_description:
I received a new Mr. Coffee 2 Qt. Fresh Tea Maker yesterday, and attempted to use it today. It has an "on" button/switch, and the directions indicate that it should be pressed in order to begin the brew cycle.  However, it began sending hot water out as soon as it was plugged in, all over my hand.  I am not badly burned, but I did receive a mild one despite reacting quickly.  We tried several more times (prepared this time) to plug it in and toggle the switch, but it started immediately each time.  I assume the product I have is defective, but online reviews often mention that it can be difficult to turn on.  Mr. Coffee's website suggests that this is because the button can be stiff at first. I believe I experienced something similar, except that it is always on instead of always off.

The directions included with the product say to plug the power cord into the electrical outlet and push the ON button to begin the brewing cycle.  Upon closer inspection, the unit itself does have a warning embossed onto the top (white on white, very difficult to read) that says to prevent injury do not plug unit in until water is in the reservoir and pitcher is in place.  However, it is difficult to read, and this information is not included with the instructions.
justification: The incident resulted in a mild burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the product's design flaw and unclear warnings.

incident_description: We cooked fish in our glass casserole dish at 500 degrees and when we lifted the dish from the oven, it exploded into hundreds of small pieces. That explosion resulted in burns and cuts.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and cuts, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: On 4/24/15, a consumer started her dishwasher.  About 5 minutes later she saw flames and smoke emitting from below the controls.  She stopped the dishwasher cycle and called the fire department.  When the fire department arrived, the fire was already suppressed.  The fire department collected the control module.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was suppressed without further damage.

incident_description: I purchased a new Kitchen Aid Electric Oven on September 6, 2014.  The oven was manufactured with a blue porcelain paint covering the entire interior.  On May 6, 2015 a large shard of blue porcelain paint was found in food my wife cooked in that oven.  If anyone had consumed that paint shard it would have been a medical emergency and might have been fatal. On inspection I discovered that the interior blue porcelain paint has begun to detach from the oven wall in sharp glassy shards. I have attached some photos of the defective paint sharding.  On May 7, 2015 I called Kitchen Aid / Whirlpool customer service to report the defect and seek remediation. Kitchen Aid customer service told me that the defect was considered cosmetic and was not covered under warranty.  I explained that the defect was a health and safety hazard but they were unmoved.  After a cursory internet search I found that this defect is not uncommon and many other people have received the same response from Kitchen Aid customer service.  Our oven is unsafe to use and is therefore unusable.  I don't believe any remediation can make it safe again.  This defect is an original design and manufacturing defect.  This oven should be recalled and affected consumers should be compensated.  Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a hazardous defect with potential for severe harm, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On 12/01/09 (approximately) the consumer states while the unit was being used the consumer noticed a burn odor. The consumer opened the door to stop the cycle and noticed burn damages on the bottom of the unit near the heating element. The consumer states the control panel stopped working since then and the unit has not been used. The consumer states the control panel never worked properly and had issues with it since the unit was installed. The consumer contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The consumer was told that her unit is not part of a recall and the unit would be repaired at her own expense. 

The consumer called the firm again about a year ago for assistance with a repair but the firm told the consumer that any repair would be at the consumer's expense. The consumer believes her unit should be included in recall # 07-094. The consumer believes the unit poses a fire hazard and the firm should repair the unit free of charge. 

The unit was used 3 times a week. 

The unit's model number is listed in recall # 07-094 but the serial number is not included.
justification: The incident involved a burn odor and damage to the unit, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: 10 year old side by side Whirlpool refrigerator in our garage caught fire and destroyed everything in the garage and caused smoke damage throughout the house.
justification: The refrigerator fire caused significant property damage but no mention of injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
Keurig coffee maker(s) trip GFI detector.

Have tried 3 different GFI units.

Cannon determine if it happens when unit is off BECAUSE the end result is always the same, the coffee maker is found in the OFF state and the GFI has blown.

I see on the web that many others have this problem.

Therefore it strikes me as a safety issue.
justification: The incident involves a safety issue with the coffee maker tripping GFI detectors, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Water continuously leaks out of brewer, always hot, got burned a couple times.
justification: Hot water leakage caused burns, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I was making egg salad for sandwiches in a pyrex container. I was scooping out the last spoonful of salad and the container exploded in my hands. The container was not hot nor cold, it was taken out of the cupboard and was room temperature. I had been mixing the egg salad for about 10 minutes and noticed nothing unusual about the container itself. The glass went everywhere in my kitchen as well as into my hands, arms and feet. I have never had this happen before and was quite amazed that something like this could happen.
justification: The incident resulted in glass shards causing injuries to hands, arms, and feet, but no death was reported. Such occurrences are rare, as the user noted it had never happened before.

incident_description:
I purchased a Wal-Mart  Rival toaster within the last 6 months.  Model # 16041  UL listed #54J9  E81296.  I toasted two english muffins smelled something strange and noticed the unit caught fire.  

The top part of the plastic housing melted-shrunk exposing more of the metal toaster frame.

I cut the plug off and I'm still in possession of the toaster and plug . Luckily the damage was contained to the toaster.
justification: The toaster caught fire and melted, but no injuries were reported and the damage was contained to the toaster.

incident_description:
This caller and his wife were relaxing in their family room when his wife smelled an odd burning odor which they both agreed that the odor was similar to burning insulation.
They went to the kitchen to investigate and saw that that their dishwasher had whitish grey smoke coming from the operation panel in front with most of it coming from the right hand side of the panel.
The caller pushed the stop button on the panel but the unit did not respond to any of the buttons.
His wife opened door but the dishwasher kept running and spraying water out.
They then pulled the power cord from behind the dishwasher which stopped it.
They opened the doors & windows then set up fans to rid their home of the smoke.
The caller and his wife are reporting this incident realizing that this may be an older model, however they expect it to stop working but not catch fire.

There are no injuries to be reported.
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
The caller is requesting assistance from the manufacturer for purchase of a newer, safer dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved smoke and malfunctioning equipment but no injuries were reported, indicating a non-injury incident with possible likelihood given the equipment's age and condition.

incident_description:
05/17/2015 - Fifteen minutes after the consumer had made herself and her husband some coffee, the consumer's husband explains that he smelled smoke coming from the adjacent kitchen. When they went to check what was happening, they noticed the smoke was coming from their coffee maker as the unit was melting.

The consumer indicates that the coffee maker stays on for two hours after the coffee is done in order to keep the remaining coffee warm.

The consumer indicates that this is the first time she has had any issues with this specific coffee maker, which is actually a replacement to another coffee maker of the same model that she owned. This original  coffee maker was replaced by the manufacturer because of the same problem: it had melted. For this same reason, the consumer does not intend to contact the manufacturer as she does not feel safe using their coffee makers.

The consumer checked online and found out that hundreds of reviews had been submitted on [REDACTED] about consumers who had similar issues to hers.

The consumer has no injuries to report nor damages other than the one to her coffee maker. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a melting coffee maker causing smoke, but no injuries or damages beyond the appliance itself.

incident_description:
I purchased my Kenmore free-standing stove in Dec. 2013.  Two days ago, the inner glass on the oven door actually EXPLODED with a huge noise.   I was baking at 350 degrees and did not do anything to bump, hit, or scratch the glass.

It will cost a lot to replace this glass but I believe the glass was defective to have exploded with no provocation.   Sears will not cover replacement as the warranty is one-year only.

This is a dangerous situation and the only way to get attention is when someone gets hurt and sues the maker of these stoves.   Luckily the only thing hurt was the batch of cookies.
justification: The oven glass exploded unexpectedly, but no injuries occurred, only property damage.

incident_description:
(05/07/2015) The consumer stated that she placed the dish, which contained broccoli and olive oil, in a preheated 375 degree oven. About four minutes later, she heard a pop. She went to the oven and saw that the glass dish had shattered. The contents had spilled and cause a fire in the oven. The consumer turned the oven off and got a fire extinguisher to put the fire out.

(05/08/2015) The consumer called the manufacturer's call center who advised her that the information would be referred to the corporate office.
justification: The incident involved a shattered dish and a small oven fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
microwave oven magnetron keeps operating after oven timer stops. Fan and turntable both stop, but magnetron continues to generate heat. Apparent potential for fire from overheated food, or equipment.
Make: Kenmore (Goldstar/LG Electronics)
Model: 721.66339
Serial #: 205TA02900
justification: The magnetron continuing to operate after the timer stops poses a risk of fire, which could lead to injury.

incident_description: We purchased a Kenmore Elite Microwave/oven combination model 790 12/25/14 which was installed 1/12/15. The most recent problem on this unit is with the microwave. My son tried to warm up some food and the microwave (which had been working fine an hour before) began to hum loudly and glow orange inside. Within 2 seconds he hit the stop button and the microwave did turn off. When he opened the unit, smoke was coming out of top and there is a charred mark inside on the top (fire?) We are very worried. We have found numerous complaints the same and similar as ours regarding the Elite series appliances, and are concerned that this is just the beginning of issues with our purchase. Have called Sears for repair service, and they have scheduled a repair for next week.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, emitting smoke and a charred mark, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore 790 Electric Range

Purchased for $1043 in November 2007.   Shortly after original warranty expired one of the cooktop burners went out.   A few months later, while baking in the oven the oven started to heat up exceeding the baking temperature and the panel began to spark and wires to burned.  We quickly unplugged the range.  We called a local licensed repairman who replaced the control panel.  A few months passed and another stovetop burner went out.  Then, in May of 2015, while using the oven it began to heat up past the 425 degrees it was programmed for.   We tried to decrease the heat and the panel would not respond.  We quickly pulled out the range and unplugged.  We believe this is a hazard after looking online to see if it had been recalled and finding a number of situations like ours.   I called Sears to report and they will do nothing about it so I told them I was obligated to report this to Consumer Protection as it is too dangerous to  be in a consumer's home.   I have been forced to purchase an new range for the protection of my home and family.
justification: The incident involved repeated malfunctions and potential fire hazards, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore double convection oven. The model number is 79047772405. I was making pizza.  The timer beeped and I opened the oven door. As I opened the door, the outer glass of the oven door shattered. It shot glass up to 10 feet away.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I bought a Stanley Digital Timer model TM231 (Item #31207) on 12/4/2014. I used it for the first time on 3/15/2015. A small decorative light was plugged in. A short time after the timer turned the light on I smelled smoke and saw the smoke was coming from the timer. I was able to grab the very hot, smoking timer and throw it outside. The plastic was already discoloring and sticky with strong fumes and a lot of smoke. If I had not been in the room when this happened I'm sure a fire would have resulted.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his outer oven glass door shattered while the range was not in use.  Caller stated that this is the 2nd time the incident occurred , the door was replaced in 2013.

(5/2015) The manufacturer was contacted and they advised that the glass would be replaced at his expense.  Caller stated that each time he has had to pay for a replacement that is a faulty which is a safety hazard.  He feels that the manufacturer should be held responsible and recall this unsafe product.
justification: The incident involves a shattered oven door with no reported injuries, but it has occurred twice, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
The broiler element in this oven stopped working about to weeks ago. Today, 6/6/15 my wife put a batch of brownies in the oven to cook. Shortly thereafter she began to smell them and thought that was odd as they were in a short while.
She opened the oven to find the broiler element activated and not the bake element. 
I double checked to make sure she did not activate the self cleaning mode or any other possibility. 
Needless to say as she finishes cooking dinner the oven is in the off position, the self cleaning handle is in the unlocked position and I can find no cause for why this element is powered up. 
I shut the breaker to the range hoping to reset the malfunction with  no success. 
The only way I will be able to power down the oven will be to shut the 40 amp range breaker when she is done cooking. 

My number one concern is if this had activated in the middle of the night? There is explicable reason for the the broil element to be powered up and it's even more troubling the only way I will be able to power it down is with the breaker.
justification: The broiler element malfunctioned without injury, posing a potential fire hazard if left unattended.

incident_description:
The submitter is filing a report on a gas range which he feels poses a fire hazard. The submitter purchased the range and put it in a house that he rents to a family. 

On 03/01/15 (estimated) the submitter's tenant used the right front burner and when the tenant tried to turn the knob to the "off" position the knob would not move. The knob seemed stuck or locked and would not move in any direction. The tenant removed the pot from the burner and called the submitter. The right front burner was on high heat level. The submitter arrived about 20 minutes later. The submitter used the oven door to pull the unit out and away from the cabinet. The submitter moved the unit to the left so he could get to the back of the unit and shut the gas valve off. Once the gas valve was shut off the submitter noticed the burner turned off. 

On 03/02/15 (estimated) the consumer contacted a local technician to examine the unit. The technician told the consumer that the unit needed a new valve. The consumer went to a local appliance store to order the part which cost $85. 

On 03/07/15 (estimated) the consumer receive the replacement part and the consumer installed the part in the range.

On 03/09/15 the submitter contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The firm told the submitter that the unit is out of warranty but he could purchase an extended warranty.
