The submitter was concerned that the valve was damaged on a relatively new unit but the consumer states the firm did not seem concerned with the safety hazard the range may pose. 

The unit is used daily. There are no prior.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas range that could have posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore Oven would heated to hot and heating element would not turn off. The oven would only stop heating once the electrical breaker was switched off.
justification: The oven overheating poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
I have Cuisinart pans with glass tops the tops have metal handles.  The handles get very hot and I have accidentally picked up the handle and been burned.  I try to remember to use the pot holder but sometimes we forget.  If any just walked up to pot and wanted to lift the lid they would be burned I frequently remind people.  I have asked the company to replace and they tell me to use a pot holder or follow the instructions in the booklet it does not help

I have been burned in the past not severely but would have been if I had not thrown the lid down.  I can't recall dated for us as I have had the pans about 5 years.  I did not use them often as I was ill for lot of the time.  I am well now and cooking and experiencing this problem.  .
justification: The description mentions burns from hot handles, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurs frequently, as the user forgets to use pot holders and has been burned multiple times.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the oven came with the house they purchased in Sep 2000. 

The consumer stated that since purchasing the house, the lower oven has been only used once in 2014. The consumer stated that she mainly uses the upper oven for reheating purposes. The upper oven has also not been used much. The consumer has never used the self clean feature on the ovens. 

On 5/10/15, the consumer stated that she was sitting in her living room when she heard a loud explosion. The consumer checked out the kitchen and noticed that the outer glass on the lower oven door had exploded. The consumer stated that the glass fell all over the kitchen floor.

The consumer contacted the firm and reported the incident with them. The consumer was informed that they will send out a technician for inspection and cleaning. After inspection, they will offer her an estimated repair cost or discount towards a new unit.

The consumer stated that she will also contact her homeownerÃÂs insurance company. 

The consumer stated that the door glass exploded spontaneously without any previous use or damage. The consumer believes there is a serious injury hazard.
justification: The incident involved an oven door glass exploding without causing injury, fitting the 'Incident, No Injury' severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) due to the spontaneous nature of the event without prior use or damage.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his standalone microwave in 2011 and had no problems with it until the beginning of May 2015 when it began turning on by itself.
The caller noticed the beginning of May the caller noticed a warning on the microwave that read "Front panel shorted, service may be needed" but the message went away when he pushed 'stop'.
A few days later he was in the kitchen and noticed that the microwave began running.
He states that this could result in a severe fire hazard and he would like a replacement for the unit at manufacturer's expense.

There are no injuries being reported 

The caller contacted the manufacturer May 20th, 2015 and was advised that he could schedule a repair for an estimated $100 charge.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased and registered an LG kitchen suite. Range, microwave, refrigerator and dishwasher. The range started a fire in my kitchen in Sept 07 because the burner remained extremely hot after turning it off. I had a large insurance claim and contacted LG to no avail. Then, in 2011, a fire started INSIDE my refrigerator because of faulty interior lights. LG sent a technician to repair. In April of 2015, I cleaned the oven to prepare my home for renters. It got so hot, it melted the interior edge of the (expensive) cabinet door and drawer! I contacted LG again and received no response. I even sent pictures. This is an extremely faulty line of appliances.  The dishwasher does a ridiculously poor job of cleaning dishes, and if there is steam rising from the stove, the panel on the microwave goes on the fritz and won't work for a few days. 
The range is the biggest worry as it is a fire hazard. The model isModel no. LRE30755ST
Serial no. 606KMQG04004
LG Household Electric Range
I can provide photos of the damage.
justification: The description reports multiple incidents of fires and significant property damage, indicating a high likelihood of injury if the issues persist.

incident_description:
Turned off oven after baking something.  A few minutes later smelled an odor coming from oven, looked to display and it showed oven was off. Opened door and almost was burned as the broiler element had turned on and was extremely hot.  It would not turn off, had to unplug the oven to get it to turn off.

Kenmore Ultra Bake Self Cleaning Super Capacity Oven, Model 665.95004102
justification: The oven malfunctioned and remained hot despite being turned off, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased the oven in question back in 2010 and about 3 years ago the racks in the bottom oven will just fall, they do not fit properly anymore.  I thought maybe I was using the wrong rack for each level, but it doesn't matter.  I also recently had issue with the electronic control board and the temp probe.  They sure don't make them like they used to and charge way to much for products that expire within 5 years, when they used to last over 15-20 years.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning oven racks and electronic components, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I emptied my refrigerator to clean it and noticed the lights had gotten VERY hot.  Hot enough where they melted 2 holes in the liner ceiling of the unit.  It was so hot it opened up the plastic liner and exposed the insulation. The bulbs are charred but still work. The refrigerator works properly.  No, it was not a power surge. My whole house is on a surge protector.  Upon further review the bulbs in the freezer were in the same shape. Black char on them.  I've worked to hard to have my house burn down by a refrigerator and feel this incident is more than justified and this manufacturer and the public need to know what happened and the risks involved. 

I do have pictures to show how bad the burns are.
justification: The incident involved significant heat damage to the refrigerator liner and charred bulbs, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: It was 10pm. My husband goes out to the kitchen for a drink only to find our microwave is on by itself, sparking and flaming. He quickly unplugged it and was able to put out. No one had used it for it to be running. Had he not woke up and went for a drink we would have lost everything. There was NOTHING in the microwave for it to even spark. I had noticed when cleaning it a week ago that the top part was bubbling and some paint was missing. Which worried me to start. We had not been using because of that issue but it was still plugged in. Very strange to say the least!
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and caught fire, but no one was injured and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description: Container was holding a piece of casserole (no liquid covering the bottom) and went directly from the fridge to the microwave. The lid was un-sealed, but left sitting on top as to prevent a mess while microwaving. Container was in the microwave for one minute. Then set again for a minute and a half. With :24 remaining the glass shattered in the microwave. There were no injuries since the glass was contained within the microwave.
justification: The glass shattered in the microwave but no injuries occurred as the glass was contained within the microwave.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting her three door refrigerator that could have burned her home down if her daughter had not come by her home to check it while the caller was on vacation.

When the caller's daughter entered her parent's home on Thursday, April 23rd, 2015 she smelled a burning odor which she followed to the kitchen and narrowed it to the refrigerator.

She opened the refrigerator door and saw that the plastic casing covering the lights had melted and the wires were obviously melting and very hot.

The top inside of the refrigerator had bubbled.

The daughter asked a neighbor to assist her with removing the lights from the sockets then saw that everything was burning.

The daughter and the neighbor disconnected the lights from the refrigerator which is still running and is cooling.

There are no injuries to be reported.

This caller spoke with the manufacturer, she did not obtain the name of the representative but the caller was advised that although there is no recall, there is a flash number for this incident. 
The flash number is not available at the time of this report but the caller may be able to provide it when she returns the report with her signature.

incident_description:
On or about April 22, 2010, I purchased a Kenmore Electric Range Model # 790.9611340F from Sears located at 11033 Carolina Place Pkwy Pineville, North Carolina 28134 with the assistance of [REDACTED], one of the Appliance Select Plus consultants. 

I also purchased a refrigerator, microwave, and dishwasher at that time for delivery to a home she purchased on May 17, 2010.

When I purchased the electric range it was already fully assembled and was delivered to my home and installed by SearsÃÂ appliance installation services. At that time, I also purchased a 3-year protection/maintenance agreement.

On August 12, 2014 at approximately 5:30pm, while preparing a meal for my family, my leg was sliced open by the sharp metal of the oven door when I walked around the door of the open stove. incident_description:
I purchased a Simply Calphalon Easy System Nonstick5 QT Dutch Oven & Cover, a Newell Rubbermaid Company. The UPC is 1831240 or 016853055999. 

I purchased it from the AAFES in Kaiserslautern, Germany on a US military installation. It notes on the box the ease of draining pasta or vegetables with the pour spouts ad straining holes. I made pasta and boiling water spouted out of the pour spouts like a geyser. I contacted the company and notified them that water spouted from their product while I was cooking and that I was luckily unharmed. Their solution was to replace the lid. incident_description: I purchased a Samsung stove model NE58F9710WS on may 1 2015. This is a slide in model stove with the burner knobs at the front. On no fewer than 8 occasions the burners have been turned on inadvertently when the knobs are leaned on. On the first occasion, I was getting ready to walk out the door when I smelled something and came back to find my electric tea kettle melting and black smoke billowing out. Admittedly it is not a great habit but for 4 decades, I have left my electric kettle sitting on the stove to save counter space and have only ruined one kettle when I stupidly turned on the wrong element. This time, I did not turn the stove on at all. When I retraced my steps, I realized the element had turned on when I was reaching over the stove to put something in the cupboard above the stove. I have also leaned on the knob reaching a pot on the back burner. My husband has also leaned on the knobs and between us we can count 8 instances where the burner turned itself on. Fortunately one or the other of us has noticed before anything too serious has occurred. The knobs need to be pushed in before they will turn but they require very little effort to push and only need to be pushed in about 1 millimeter in order to turn the knob. I am just over 5 feet tall and under 100 pounds so no great weight is pushing on he knobs. Because of my height, I often have to reach above or behind the stove ..... to clean the backsplash for example. I have owned other stoves with knobs situated at the front and have never encountered this problem.
justification: The incident describes multiple occurrences of burners being turned on inadvertently, leading to potential hazards, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description:

Advised consumer of recalled 09-333 and the hazard.  Consumer stated that she had not experienced, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected.

Consumer feels that the range should be recalled due the melting of the electrical wiring.

incident_description:
The magnetron occasionally fails to turn off and, after more use, never turning off forcing me to have to unplug it when not using it.  Purchased at Sam's Club in [REDACTED] in early 2013, the microwave worked well for a year.  Then, one day, in early 2014, when I was done cooking my small frozen pizza in the microwave, I heard a fairly faint (about 20 db at 1 meter distance) humming sound coming from it and the food was still cooking despite having pressed the stop button.  By simply unplugging it, waiting a few seconds, and plugging it back in, the magnetron stopped running and the microwave returned to normal.  About 4 to 6 months later, it happened again and the simple power cycle returned it to normal.  It happened once again about 3 months later and the usual fix worked.  Then, on June 2, 2015, the usual fix stopped working.

Knowing that microwave ovens work by emitting electromagnetic radiation at the right wavelength so that water molecules absorb it, heating up and thus heating up the food being cooked (since food has a lot of water in it), it is very unsafe to open the microwave while the magnetron is going since the human body is primarily water.  Thus, the only safe way I can use the microwave, which has a hazard of its own, is to have it unplugged, open the door, insert my food item I want to cook, get the timer going so it rotates, press stop when done, unplug the microwave, then open the door.  Due to the heavy power draw of the magnetron, repeatedly plugging in and unplugging the machine results in sparking inside the plug which can pose a potential fire hazard.
justification: The microwave's magnetron failing to turn off poses a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet. The issue has happened multiple times, indicating a recurring problem.

It went off after playing with the knob for a few seconds.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore bottom freezer refrigerator Model #795.79733.900 Serial No. [REDACTED] in July 2009.  I had been very satisfied with the product until we experienced a problem with the automatic ice maker.  A 1.5ÃÂ piece of clear plastic broke off the circular disk inside the ice bucket. incident_description:
I purchased a new Kenmore kitchen appliance set in 2012 (refrigerator, dishwasher, dual fuel stove, and dishwasher).  The design and handles were matching so it appeared like it was a set.  The duel fuel gas slide in stove, Model 790-41093, has had a couple of problems.  1)  It is exactly like Model [REDACTED] , and has very sharp metal edges.  Although we have not been injured, you have to be very careful cooking and cleaning on the product.  2)  If the burner plates on the 85 BTU main burner are not seated properly, flames can shoot out in one direction in heights of 6"-8" causing a concentrated burst of flames to occur. My family has experience multiple burns and damage to our kitchen due to this.

Secondly, the microhood, Kenmore Elite [REDACTED], handle has cut my family with some pretty lengthy lacerations.  The plastic metal the wraps around the handle separates and causes a sharp edge.  My door assembly was replaced under warrantly once due to this problem but the second replacement door had the same malfunction. It is now wrapped in a commercial tape that is resistant to the heat so we no longer cut ourselves.  Sears did reimburse us for $500 for the microhood however the product was never recalled.  This product is still being sold and I strongly feel LG should replace the defective handle material to one that does not warp or split.  When I phoned LG about the injury, they said the injuries were not severe enough to file a claim.

Your website would not allow me to upload correspondence and photos of the incidents.
justification: The description reports multiple burns and lacerations from the appliances, indicating injuries but no deaths.

incident_description:
My sister's KitchenAid dishwasher, Model KUDE40FXSS5 had the water pump hose blow off.  There is a recall on this model for that problem, but the recall does not include the Serial Number of her machine.  However, her machine had exactly the same problem as the recalled units.  Her machine does not have the improved hose clamp (Part Number W10548435) that is applied on the recall.

http://www.trailappliances.com/files/pdf/bc/recalls/KitchenAid-dishwasher-recall-letter.pdf

Her Serial Number is F21907405.
  
The recall only includes machines with Serial Numbers up to FS213---------.

I contacted KitchenAid Customer Service.  They said that since her machine is not included in the recall, they could offer no assistance.

I believe that the KitchenAid recall should be expanded to include all machines that do not have the improved hose clamp.

If this hose blows off, a huge amount of water is expelled from the machine onto the floor.  Besides the water damage to the floor, this could easily cause a fire if water gets into the electronics, which are located nearby.  My brother received an electrical shock (fortunately not severe) while cleaning up water from the floor.
justification: The incident caused an electrical shock (injury) and poses a risk of water damage and fire, indicating a significant hazard.

The glass fell mostly into the kitchen sink, but some flew 2-3 feet. I had a few minor scratches and found some pieces of glass inside my shirt.  I called to report it to the retailer, Sears, and learned that the part wasn't described as safety glass/tempered glass, but simply as "glass."  When I then examined the other shelves, none of them stated "tempered glass." Shelves on other refrigerators I've owned are labeled as tempered glass. I am concerned that if I replace the shelf under warranty with regular glass it could shatter again and injure myself or others.

incident_description: I purchased an Emerson microwave MW8999SB. The microwave started shooting sparks from a side panel in the microwave. I contacted Emerson and the sent me another microwave of the same Model. I thought maybe the first one was just a faulty one. They told me to cut the cord from the old microwave and throw it away so that noone else could use it because it was dangerous. Now the second microwave of the same Model started shooting sparks out of the side panel again. This time sparks were so strong they lit up the inside of the microwave and burned holes in the top of the microwave. I am afraid this microwave is not only a fire danger but is also releasing to much radiation. After the sparking and the burnt holes in the microwave it still continues to work. I am concerned about consumers continuing to use them until they stop working completely when they are damaged and dangerous. I was using the microwave to heat some soup in a microwavable container. I have kept the microwave clean and used it properly. I made a point of not touch the microwave for fear of shock. I unplugged it quickly. When I opened the door fumes from inside of the burned microwave filled my kitchen. I was inhaling emissions from the microwave and had to be very close to it to unplug it.

Consumer also turned on the exhaust fan for the oven and also one for the kitchen.  At about 5:30 p.m. the fire alarm went off.  Consumer observed flames shooting through the vents of the oven. incident_description:
Gas oven would not turn off. This has happened before where we try to press CANCEL, even pressing START first and then CANCEL, but it would not beep or register at all and if someone else tried it would work. In other words, it worked most of the time, but failed intermittently. This time I put the oven at 425 and it beeped when I went to shut it off, but it *DID NOT go off. We could hear it, and the oven and the control pad were very hot. We kept pushing CANCEL and it would beep but not shut off. Finally, it went off on its own about 15 minutes later as I was frantically calling the gas company. I've Googled this, and it's happened to other people. KitchenAid said they'd charge $100 to just diagnose it. But they changed the design on the later models. Their control panel now has buttons that are rubberized bubbles....and they're still having the problem. Reportedly, if one wire in there fails they all can fail. There has been no recall and they gave me a hard time with insisting on my reading the model number and serial number, which were tiny and very hard to read for someone in a wheel chair. 
The receptionist said she didn't think I read her a valid serial number. (The first numeral, or letter was either a 1 or an l or an I.)
(one, el, or eye)

(05/068/2015) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that the unit was not included in the recall-Rel# 09-333.

incident_description: During the night the glass door on the front of the oven exploded. The glass was all over the floor in the morning.

incident_description: I had not been home for the last 3-4 month (We winter in Florida). Someone looks into the house around 2 times a month. Last visit on April 30. She found everything normal. On May 15 she found the kitchen floor littered with small glass fragments. The outside door of the oven had exploded. Again the oven had not been used for several months. The oven is a GE slide-in range Model # JGSP28DEN 1 WW; SERIAL # LS2 37049Q. Oven is ~4 years old.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded oven door) but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: A piece of plastic broke off from the inside of our icemaker.  It's clear plastic and invisible in the middle of all the ice.  It came out into my glass and ended up in my mouth. If I had swallowed it, it might have killed me.

incident_description:
Frigidaire
model#:  LGUB2642LF2
Serial#:  4A11816144

while at home with my family at approximately 6:00pm on 05/19/2015 my mother in law alerted me that she could smell something burning.
Thinking it was the rice cooker I brushed it off until the smell became stronger and smelled of an electrical burn coming from the refrigerator.
Quickly I opened the fridge and found smoke and fire spewing from the upper icemaker.
Knowing that electrical fires can easily get out of control if handled with water I reached for my fire extinguisher and put the fire out. I immediately got my family out of the house and opened all the windows to air out the heavy burn smell.

at approximately 6:25pm 05/19/2015, I called the phone number listed on my fridge 1-800-944-9044 which prompted me to call a separate number for customer service (706) 860-4110.
I spoke with a customer service representative {REDACTED].
{REDACTED] gathered all my information and verified that she sees my fridge has been registered.
I explained to {REDACTED] what had happened and that I was concerned for my family and the safety of others out there that may have this same fridge.
{REDACTED] replied that because it is outside of warranty their is nothing they can do about it.
{REDACTED] advised that I have a technician look at it and diagnose the problem and then have it repaired. I asked if Frigidaire would cover those expenses and {REDACTED]Kendra replied NO since it is outside of warranty.
{REDACTED]Kendra offered me the option of getting an extended warranty but said it was expensive, running approximately $600 or more for 3 years
I then asked to speak to her supervisor. After holding for 3-5 mins {REDACTED]Kendra came back on the line to tell me her Supervisor says that because the unit is outside of warranty there is nothing they can do for me.
I then asked again to speak with the supervisor. after a brief hold the supervisor {REDACTED] came on the line. I explained my concern and my loss and {REDACTED] says again their is nothing they can do since it is outside of warranty.
{REDACTED] told me I should call the Corporate escalation department but did not have a phone number for me.
I found the number on my own and called only to find out they are already closed for the day.

5/20/2015 at 12:11 pm
I called in to the customer service department again 706-860-4110 and spoke with {REDACTED].
{REDACTED] verified my info and then transferred me to the Frigidaire Corporate Manager {REDACTED].
{REDACTED] heard me out and said that Frigidaire is very concerned in this case but because it is outside of warranty they can do nothing for me.
{REDACTED] then recommended that I contact a local Authorized Service Technician in my area but when she did a search she could not find one and that I should just call ASE or Sears for assistance.

I let {REDACTED] know that my biggest concern is all the people that own a fridge like mines that could potentially burn their home down when they are at work.

{REDACTED] reassured me that there is nothing they can do since the unit is outside of warranty but if I pay for a service technician to come out and diagnose the problem and then pay for the repairs, she could "possibly" get me a discount on the parts.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the refrigerator, which was successfully extinguished without injury, but posed a significant safety risk.

incident_description: I seriously cut myself twice within 15 minutes while using this blender for the first time.  I would not recommend this blender for anyone.  In my opinion it is defectively designed.  The Ninja uses a long attachment with concentric circular blades much unlike the normal blade design typically used in blenders.  The Ninja's "razor blade Christmas tree" design provides no discernible benefit over the normal blade design yet increases the risk of injury exponentially.  I seriously cut the index finger on my right hand while inserting the blade attachment into the pitcher.  Minutes later, the attachment fell out of the pitcher into my left hand while I was pouring the contents of the pitcher onto a plate (the poorly mixed, half-blended contents, I might add).  It caused a deep gash in my palm requiring four stitches to close.  The attachment fell out of the pitcher because it is designed to sit loose on the base of the blender with no secure connection whatsoever.  Not surprisingly, a quick review of Safer Products complaints shows others have been injured in the same manner and even more seriously.  I was lucky to escape with only four stitches.  I immediately returned the blender to the place of purchase for a full refund.  Avoid at all costs.  The Ninja blender is needlessly dangerous, almost as if the manufacturer set out to create a booby trap.  Mission accomplished.
justification: The user suffered two serious cuts requiring stitches, indicating significant injury. The description suggests the design flaw makes such injuries likely for others.

incident_description: I have a Maytag Dishwasher undercounter model MDB7709AWW1 Serial FY3101294 Stainless Steel interior. The panel board indicated it was in a dry heat cycle and stuck on for several hours with a locked door until the electronic pad burn't out.  This was made the same time the other recalled models were made.  I have reported it twice in great detail to MAytag who refuses to investigate it , and wants me to pay for pulling out the part to see if it is the same defective hazardous part used in the other model who are recalled beginning with MDB Models!
justification: The incident involved a hazardous malfunction causing a locked door and burnt electronic pad, posing a risk of injury, though no injury was reported.

incident_description: My LG refrigerator, model # LFC25760SW, when the door are shut the light stays on in the refrigerator. It melted the plastic cover and you could smell the burning plastic. Food was HOT and had to be thrown out. This is extremely dangerous and could have started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard and spoiled food, indicating a risk of injury, though none was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Pyrex Storage Dish( 6 cup 1.5 liter Barcode- 071160032842). On Tuesday May 5th 2015, I took off the packaging of the brand new dish. I started to hand wash the dish in hot water and the piece exploded in my hands. A chard of glass stuck in my right fore arm. I pulled out the piece of glass and cleaned the wound.
justification: The incident resulted in a glass shard causing injury to the forearm, which is classified as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the rarity of such events with Pyrex products.

incident_description: ... extremely dangerous product; we didn't realize, at point-of-purchase, sears' top-of-the-line Kenmore hand mixer, model 100.89109, is prone to a domino affect; a fundamentally defective design, its (1) defective retractable cord prone to suddenly retracting, no rhyme or reason, (2) jerks the hand mixer into its on position, which (3) subsequently entangles your fingers and hand, into the beeters of this hand mixer --
justification: The description details a defective hand mixer design that can cause injury by entangling fingers and hands in the beaters, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence and significant injury risk.

incident_description:
On 04/14/15 the consumer used the right rear burner for about 5 minutes and when she turned the knob to the "off" position the burner failed to shut off. The consumer had to shut off the circuit breaker to turn the unit off. The consumer then turned the circuit breaker back "on" and the consumer states the right rear burner remained off. The consumer then turned the right rear burner "on" and when she pushed the control button to the "off" position the burner failed to shut off. The consumer states she checked the front and rear left burners and those burners also failed to shut off. The consumer also checked the front right burner and the burner shut off when she pushed the button to the "off" position. 

On 04/15/15 the consumer contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The firm's rep (name unknown) told the consumer that the unit was not part of a recall and the consumer would have to pay for any repairs. The consumer states the firm's rep did not take interest in the safety hazard or take a report on the matter. The consumer was referred to CPSC (800-638-2772). 

The consumer is upset that the firm has recalled similar units for the same issues and her unit poses a fire hazard as well but is not included in the recall. 

The unit was repaired once before for a different problem (electrical defect) but the consumer does not remember the details of the repair.
justification: The burner failing to shut off poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting her electric range purchased from retailer January 14th, 2007 and she is reporting that she has been having problems with the unit since approximately two years after purchase.

When the left front large burner is set to low it still escalates to extremely high temperatures.

The burner has since April 25th, 2015 the same left front large burner began turning on by itself on and then begins building to the highest heat.

The caller is reporting this product as a severe fire hazard and asked that her model be recalled for this reason with free repair at manufacturer expense.

There are no injuries being reported
justification: The electric range has a malfunctioning burner that poses a fire hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Gas Range - Model number 79070403010; purchased 8/28/11

Regarding - Glass door explosion

On 5/14/15 my less than 4 year old oven was set to 375 degrees and had been on for 30 minutes. No out of the ordinary usage. An explosion was heard in the kitchen and upon entering the kitch it was found that the middle glass panel had exploded and shattered. The inner and outer panels were intact. The oven was turned off at this point. The door was opened to further inspect and the inner panel shattered further which caused glass to fall out of the door and into the broiler and on the kitchen floor. There were no injuries. 

On 5/15/15 Sears and Kenmore was contacted; no resolution was offered except to have someone come out to look at the oven and repair it, all of which would have to be paid for by me. They were extremely unhelpful and kept giving different phone numbers to call (10 different numbers, one which was for Whirlpool, not even Kenmore!!!). This is extremely disappointing. All they can say is that there are no recalls so there is nothing they can do. Doesn't exploding oven doors seem like it should be a manufacturer issue?!?!
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) since such incidents are not common based on the description.

incident_description:
My husband was cooking a pizza in our Kenmore oven.  He opened the glass oven door by the handle to check on the pizza.  The handle screw came out on one side, causing one end of the handle to come off the door (we had no warning that the handle was loose or faulty).  The outer glass door exploded onto the kitchen floor, across the kitchen, over a kitchen counter and into the breakfast area.  Glass pieces could have embedded into our grandchildren's eyes, had they been there.  

I contacted Sears / Kenmore and Frigidaire, who is listed as the manufacturer on the Model number.  Frigidaire told me to contact Kenmore, stating it was their product.  Sears /Kenmore said they would register my report, forwarded me to a claims department to report the incident, and also stated they could send a Sears repairman at our expense.  

I also spoke about this incident to several people in my community and learned that another person had her Kenmore oven door do the same thing while she was out of her home (the oven was not on).  I am requesting that someone look into "tempered" glass oven door shattering / exploding.
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door with potential for severe injury, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
My GE Cafe Dishwasher twice dangerously overheated:

1. THe first time after a washing cycle - the heater DID NOT TURN OFF AND THE PLASTIC ITEMS INSIDE MELTED BECAUSE SO HOT _ I AM GUESSING OVER 400 Degrees - over 5 hours!!! So Dangerous...

2. I TUrned off and opened the door. Left everything inside to cool off.

3. I closed the door and the dishwasher went automatically into a heat cycle and melted the dishwasher structure (.e.g. the boxes that hold silverware!!!) inside as well as everything AGAIN. 40

NOT ONLY IS THIS A HUGE FIRE HAZARD BUT THE FUMES FROM THE MELTING PLASTIC ARE A HUGE HAZARD
justification: The dishwasher overheating and melting plastic items poses a significant fire hazard and toxic fume risk, which could lead to injury if not addressed.

incident_description:
We purchased a brand-new GE double oven in June 2013. Today the glass on the top oven door shattered. The oven was not in use, and had not been in use for several days. In reading several online sites, this appears to be an extremely common issue, which has been going on for at least ten years.

GE refused to warranty the glass.
justification: The incident involves a shattered oven door with no reported injury, and online reports indicate it is a common issue.

incident_description: On May 15 th, 2015 I was baking chicken in my KitchenAid oven at 350 degrees for 1 hour. This incident happened at the end of the cooking time before the food was taken out of the oven. The oven door has three layers of glass. The middle layer of glass shattered and the pieces dropped to the floor through the vents in the bottom of the door. This shattering of the middle glass caused the outer glass to shattered also but it initially remained intact much like safety glass. The inside glass closest to the food was not compromised. My son was standing next to me in front of the oven. Fortunately no one was hurt. This model is a microwave/oven/warmer combo wall unit.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was hurt, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
This concerns a Hamilton Beach slow cooker, model 33472.

We have owned this for about 5 months, and have used it about 20 times without incident until now.

We made some rice pudding overnight in the slow cooker, cooking on the "low" setting.  In the morning, my daughter opened the lid, placing it vertical on the plastic hinge, and began serving it into bowls.  After about 10 seconds, the lid shattered into 1/8" fragments (approximately), scattering pieces up to several feet away.

The room temp was 67 degrees.

We didn't note any cracks or other imperfections prior to use.   We can't think of an incident where the lid would have been abused.
justification: The lid shattered but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I constantly burn my hand on water that gets shot out o my keurig. I've burned my hand on numerous occasions.
justification: The description mentions repeated burns from hot water, indicating an injury (severity level 3) that occurs frequently (almost certain).

incident_description: I was using the West Bend Air Crazy 4-quart Popcorn Popper as directed. The plastic on the safety shield bubbled and melted, making it no longer fit the machine. This, in combination with alarmingly high air speed, also causes very hot un-popped popcorn kernels to shoot out at the user. This could cause severe burns from either touching the safety shield or being struck with a kernel.
justification: The incident describes a risk of severe burns from hot kernels or melted plastic, indicating potential injury (severity 3). The issue is likely to occur given the described conditions (likelihood 4).

incident_description: We heard a strange buzzing noise in the kitchen. When we found the noise it was the toaster/egg maker. I unplugged it and went to move it but the egg cooking end was too hot to hold onto. It would've been a terrible fire had we not been home and heard it. The smell of burning/hot was awful! The toaster hadn't been used for a couple of days. The egg cooker hadn't been used but a few times ever and hadn't been used in over a year.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard and the appliance was too hot to handle, indicating a risk of injury if touched.

incident_description: We bought a Black and Decker infrawave toaster oven about a year ago from Deals Only. Yesterday it turned on by itself and wouldn't turn off. I had to unplug it to get it off. Sparks flew. I let it set over night and tried using it again. When I plugged it in, it turned on. None of the display buttons seem to work and I cannot turn it off except by unplugging it and seeing sparks fly.
justification: The toaster oven malfunctioned, causing sparks and inability to turn off, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Coffee carafe ("Bonavita BV1800TH 8-Cup Coffee Maker with Thermal Carafe", purchased 12/2013, though only used since February 2015) was being washed in lukewarm water, with soap and brush. Carafe/coffee was cold - had been out all day. While washing, my husband heard a pop, like a gunshot, and the interior carafe glass coating exploded in shards. Some of it came out, most landed at bottom of the carafe. No injury, but great potential for injury - shards could have popped up into my husband's eyes. After googling it, it is a repeated & common issue with others. Apparently, Bonavita does not take care of the issue for consumers, but I think it should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved an exploding carafe with no injury, but potential for harm was high. The issue is described as common and repeated by others.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the inner glass on the top oven door exploded while the unit was in the clean cycle.The consumer stated that the glass exploded about 2.5 hours into the clean cycle (clean cycle is 4 hours long). 

The consumer stated that the glass exploded all over the kitchen floor, counters, bottom oven and the inside of the top oven. The consumer stated that her wood flooring in the kitchen where the hot glass fell has melted. The floor has bubbles on them.

incident_description: I am reporting an incident when my Viking 48" Professional Gas Range & Oven heated up to the point of burning my hand when I touched one of the knobs. Several months ago it would heat up so much that it shut off, and the Viking Tech repaired a seal around one of the oven doors. This time it was a certified Viking tech that responded, as they no longer send out Viking repair techs from my local Viking Range LLC office. He explained that there is a part that was NEVER installed in the unit that provided proper ventilation. In fact there was no fan or ventilation system in place to keep the heat where it was supposed to be. They have and after market part that is the 033879-000 Blower Service Kit that Viking says in an upgrade, and won't cover it. I have already paid for the labor, among other things, and would not pay this bill. The tech and parts rep agree this should be a covered part for the unit. This is a $12,000.00 unit that is 4 1/2 years old. It should not be an upgrade to use it without burning myself by turning a knob on or off. They are aware of this problem, and should be held accountable to repair it.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from touching a hot knob, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue is recurring and known, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: We own a Kenmore Elite smooth top stove. The stove is experiencing all the same problems listed in your most recent product recall notice (burner won't shut off, can't regulate temp. etc.). However upon reading the recall notice provided by a neighbor we're unable to find our serial # [REDACTED] or model # 790-96599601 listed in those recalled. We purchased the stove new in March of 2007.
justification: The stove exhibits dangerous malfunctions (burner won't shut off, temperature regulation issues), but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
My GE stove top gas burner model number C2S980SEM1SS and serial number FR2047039 has defective knobs that turn the gas on and off. The knobs are made of plastic and the interior of each knob is cracked. Further, when you try to turn the stove off the knobs just spin in circles making it impossible to fully turn the gas off. This becomes problematic and extremely dangerous given the stove has a self igniting spark. Once you have noticed your kitchen smells like gas if you turn the defective knob you're either going to turn the gas up higher or ignite your house up in flames. My house almost blew up and my face was hit with a giant flame as I tried frantically to turn the gas to the stove off. 
     I contacted GE and they sent a repair man to my house. He told me that GE has known about this problem going on four years now. They no longer use plastic knobs in the newer models. I believe there should be a mandatory recall for any consumer using the defective plastic knobs on the older models before someone gets seriously injured or dies. 
     After talking to GE my self and voicing my concern over this major safety issue It is my belief they will only do a recall unless forced. I have saved my old knobs if they need to be used as evidence or if you would like to send an independent technician out to verify the defective product in use with my stove. 
     GE is replacing my knobs free of charge. My concern now is for every other consumer out there using the old knobs. Someone should not have to get seriously injured or die in order for GE to do the right thing.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (face hit by flame) and poses a significant risk of more severe outcomes, including death, due to the defective knobs.

incident_description: Microwave filter disintegrating and dropping filings onto stove, and potentially into cooking food.
justification: The incident involves a microwave filter disintegrating, which could contaminate food but does not indicate immediate injury or death.

The consumer contacted another Service Technician and when he inspected the unit, he informed the consumer that her unit was included in a recall. The consumer had to pay out of pocket to fix the unit.   

04/24/2015 - The consumer's daughter informed the consumer that she was using the microwave and it was making more noise than usual.

Her daughter complained that the microwave was making more noise and sparking than usual still and when the unit stopped, the consumer indicates her daughter complained as well that the food did not heat.

05/01/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained everything that has been happening with the unit. The representative informed the consumer that she saw the notes of the previous times the consumer had called. The consumer was informed they would send a Service Technician but that without the serial number, they could not do anything.

The consumer also noted the technician put the part in and two days later the microwave did the same thing again, and it is not working.

The consumer also added she enclosed a copy of receipt of service.

incident_description: My son wanted to reheat dinner in the microwave, pushed the Reheat button and it never stopped cooking; the sensor never kicked in.  The quiche caught fire and cracked the plate .  Son put out the fire with water.

incident_description: My Kenmore oven door exploded before i could turn it on.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the dishwasher is installed in the home she purchased about 3 years ago.

The consumer stated that she ran the cycle for the dishwasher. During the heating cycle, the consumer started smelling smoke. She noticed gray smoke coming out from the bottom of the dishwasher. incident_description: I went to unload the dishwasher and when I opened the door sparks went off.
justification: Sparks occurred but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was using my Frigidaire Professional Series Electric Range FPES3085KFD  Serial no. NF14120972 to cook something using the front left burner.  When I was finished, I turned the burner dial off, but the burner stayed on and turned red hot, then down, then red hot again, cycling on and off.  It would not turn off until I shut the range off at the circuit breaker.  This happened before about a year ago, and we had to have a repairman replace the switches, which are daisy-chained together so that if one goes bad, they all have to be replaced.  Needless to say, it's a fire hazard to have a range whose burners turn themselves on and won't shut off.
justification: The burner cycling on and off without control is a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On Sunday, 10 May 2015, my husband prepared a pork roast in our 1-year-old Hamilton Beach Set 'n' Forget 6-Quart Programmable Slow Cooker.  We were not using the probe, and the lid clamps were locked.  After it had been cooking undisturbed on the kitchen counter for approximately 6 hours, on the "low" setting, I discovered that the lid had completely shattered.  The pieces had not fallen into the pot, but after my husband very carefully removed the lid from the pot by grasping it by the outer rim, the pieces did finally fall away onto the kitchen counter.  Out of caution, we did not eat the roast.  Today, 11 May 2015, I ordered a replacement lid from Hamilton Beach's website.
justification: The incident involved a shattered slow cooker lid but no injuries occurred, and the food was discarded as a precaution.

incident_description: On Easter I was preparing dinner which included baking 8 Cornish Game Hens in my Kenmore Elite Electric Range.  When I was pulling the pan out of the over, the oven shelf collapsed, spilling the liquid in the pan on my hand, the door of the oven and the floor.  I checked to be sure that I had inserted the shelves correctly, which I had.  Since that time, if there is any weight on either of the two shelves, they have collapsed, including today baking brownies.  This range was purchased  4-6-09 and this had not happened previously.  The self-cleaning program has been used on several occasions since purchase, including February, 2015. Numerous comments were found on the internet addressing this issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from spilled hot liquid, and the shelves collapsing under weight is a recurring issue.

incident_description: I was cooking with an Aircore walk-away cookware pot, and the pot exploded. The double layered pot's layers separated and one of the layers struck me in the forehead just above my right eye. I received six stitches at the emergency room and had headaches, ringing in my ear, and other side effects from the concussion for several months after the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion requiring stitches and caused prolonged symptoms, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: I was baking potatoes in the oven in my glass square pyrex dish along with spinach chips on a cookie sheet on the top rack of the oven.  The pyrex dish had only been in the oven for about 15 min. when I heard a loud bang and the oven rack shake. incident_description: Crock pot exterior got so hot that the plastic control knob partially melted.  Unit was set to high for 1 hour, then switched to low for 8 hours.  Would be burned if you touch the side of the unit for more than about 1 second.  Very hot!
justification: The crock pot's exterior became dangerously hot and melted a control knob, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Sears Member was cleaning their range just below the timer, and came across a razor edge and slightly cut themselves on their pinky finger.
justification: The member sustained a minor cut, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Our GE Monogram dishwasher (model ZBD6880N00SS, purchased September 2007) would not stop running after many hours and we had to turn off the circuit breaker in order to stop it.  On opening the door, we noted signs of scorching along the control panel at the top of the door, and an acrid smell that permeated the house for the rest of the day.  The dishes inside were unaffected, so it would not seem to have been a case of the heating element staying on.  There was no water in the tub, but the motor was continuing to run.  There does not seem to be any recall describing this particular problem.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned with scorching and an acrid smell, but no injury or property damage beyond the appliance itself occurred.

incident_description:
11/2010:  The consumer's dishwasher was repaired under recall 11-022.  The consumer did not experience any issues with the dishwasher at that time.  She received a recall notice and arranged for the remedy to be applied to the dishwasher.


4/10/2015:  The consumer turned the dishwasher on and approximately 20 - 30 minutes into the cycle and it started emitting smoke from all across the top of the dishwasher and mainly from the center.  The consumer's husband opened the dishwasher's door in order to stop it from operating.  None of the items inside of the dishwasher were damaged.  The granite counter-top underneath the dishwasher was damaged and there is discoloration to the underside of the counter lid above the dishwasher.  There were no injuries.

4/10/2015:  The consumer called the manufacturer, but they were closed.

4/13/2015:  The consumer called the manufacturer and explained the incident to a rep. [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] made arrangements to send a technician out on 4/15/2015. [REDACTED] told the consumer that this sounded similar to the problem identified in recall 11-022. [REDACTED] said if it was the same problem in the recall, they would cover the cost.  The consumer was given a [REDACTED].

The consumer said that she is now concerned that even if the repair is done again for the recall issue that the dishwasher may still present a fire hazard.

4/17/15:  The consumer noted GE agreed to replace the dishwasher on 4/15/15 and a GE technician came out.  Consumer also noted she was told it was the same problem that they had a recall on in 2010 and it was repaired under this recall.

4/23/15:  The consumer added a new GE dishwasher was delivered and installed.  Model PDT760SIF1II and serial DF822553B.  The consumer noted they [mfr] took the old dishwasher away.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the same issue post-recall suggests a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: I was using my Crock Pot slow cooker to make chili as I have done many times before. It was set to high and left on for about 4 hours. When I went to stir the chili and check on it, I lifted the handle and it came off in my hand. The entire glass lid was shattered and pieces of glass from right around the handle fell into my chili. When I tried to get the lid off of the slow cooker, it completely shattered. This is incredibly dangerous and I am fortunate that it only resulted in a loss of the chili and not more serious cuts from the glass.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with shattered glass, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On 4/26/2015, we were microwaving a potato on automatic/sensing mode.  We had just cooked three potatoes prior to this one which all came out OK.  This time however it cooked for several minutes (I noticed it was taking a while) and then went POP and burst into flames inside the microwave.  The fire was sustained and we quickly grabbed a fire extinguisher, opened the microwave door and and discharged it into the microwave.  The microwave was ruined with fire damage.  The potato was completely burned ash/charcoal 100% of the way though - it was like it had turned the potato into pure ash.  There were no injuries to people other than minor smoke inhalation.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant damage to the microwave and minor smoke inhalation, but no serious injuries.

incident_description: I purchased a coffee/tea cup at Marshalls and intended to use it for the first time earlier this morning. As I was pouring boiling water over the instant coffee I heard a loud cracking sound and the hot liquid spilled all over the table. Luckily no one was sitting at the time by the table and no one was holding the cup. The cup cracked at the whole length of its side and bottom.
justification: The cup cracked and spilled hot liquid, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his spouse turned on Dishwasher and the unit started smoking.  The circuit breaker was used to switch off the power.   He stated that when he returned home he switched the circuit breaker back on and noticed that there was a popping noise and a flame dispersed from the dishwasher.  He switched off the circuit breaker again.  Caller stated that he noticed that after pulling the dishwasher apart the control board was charred.

Caller is concerned that the dishwasher could have caused a house fire if there was no one present.

(4/13) The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that his model was not part of a recall and to contact the agency.
justification: The incident involved a smoking dishwasher with a charred control board, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(12/15/2014)The consumer stated that her daughter was baking pizza rolls on a metal cookie sheet in the oven. The temperature was set at 450. She put the oven mitt on to remove the cookie sheet. When the mitt came in contact with the cookie sheet, the hand part of the mitt ignited into flames. Her daughter flicked her hand to get the mitt off of her hand. When she did this the mitt flipped back and burned her forearm. Her daughter was burned on the palm of her right hand and her forearm.

(04/13/2015 and 04/14/2015) The consumer contacted the manufacturer to advised them of what happened. She was advised that she would receive a call back. There has been no response.

The consumer also contacted Amazon.com after seeing the product on their web site. The consumer stated that Amazon removed the product.
justification: The daughter suffered burns on her hand and forearm, requiring medical care, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:

incident_description:
On 01/03/15 the consumer set the unit to a normal wash cycle. The normal wash cycle takes about an hour. The consumer states just before the unit was about to complete the cycle he noticed flames coming from the top of the unit, near the control panel. The flames last for a few seconds and the unit shut off on its own. The consumer shut the circuit breaker off. He then opened the unit's door and noticed an electrical burn odor. The consumer feels the unit poses a fire hazard and he does not believe he should pay for any repairs because it is a manufacturer defect. 

The unit is used once a day. 

The unit has only been repaired once prior to this incident. Sometime in March 2006 (estimated) the consumer contacted Sears and a technician replaced the unit's water pump. The unit's one year warranty was over and the consumer had to pay $365 for the repairs.

incident_description:
Travel Tumbler purchased sometime around October/November 2014.
The caller's niece normally fills this tumbler with hot water and takes it to her room so that she can prepare a middle of the night bottle for her baby without leaving the room.

April 6th, 2015 the caller's niece boiled her hot water and began pouring it into the tumbler as she did every night but this time after she replaced the top and picked it up the tumbler exploded burning her left hand.

She was holding her 13 month old baby at the time but the baby was not burned.

She has not been seen by a medical professional yet but is planning to go to the emergency room at the coaxing of her aunt/the caller.

The nieces left hand has a blister 1 1/2" long with severe redness all around it.

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to once she obtains their phone number.
justification: The niece suffered a burn injury with a blister and severe redness, requiring potential emergency room care, but no death or injury to the baby occurred.

incident_description: My GE Model #JVM1540DP1WW over the range microwave turned on by itself.  The cook time registered 1 minute and counted down, but I was unable to stop or clear it.  The light turned on and the turntable activated so I can only assume that it was actually heating and running.  I had to unplug the unit to turn it off.  After researching online, I found quite a few posts containing the same complaint from other consumers, some of which resulted in fires inside the microwave.  Luckily, I was in the kitchen when my unit came on so it only ran for a few seconds before I disconnected it.  I have always used GE products for my appliances and have never had issues with their other products, however, I feel that this particular over the range microwave is a hazard and will not be purchasing any more of their microwaves.  I'm only glad that I was at home when this incident occurred.
justification: The microwave turned on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred as it was quickly unplugged.

incident_description: I was given Magic Glove as a gift.  On the manufacturer's box it said "Withstands extreme heat up to 480 degrees F",  "The box Includes: 1pc Magic Glove with Non Slip Silicone Grip", "Made in China", "Tekno Products Inc. Rutherford, NJ 07070".  I used them for the first time yesterday to pull a cookie sheet out of my oven.  The oven was set for 350 degrees.  The plastic "silicone grip" melted to the cookie sheet and started smoking.  I was able to scrape the plastic residue off the cookie sheet with a sharp knife.  I consider them usable with hot items as described on their packaging and are a hazard to consumers.
justification: The glove failed under normal use conditions, causing a hazardous situation but no injury.

incident_description: Started the Whirlpool dishwasher.  After 2-3 min. the control panel started to smoke and filled the kitchen and house with thick acrid smoke.  Flames from the panel were seen.  Tried to stop machine by opening the door.  With door open, the machine continued to run spraying hot water on my wife and all over the kitchen.  Called 911 and fire department.  Opened the circuit breaker to dishwasher to stop the machine from running and smoking.

incident_description: Our crock pot lit (glass) exploded in my wife's face today. She was just taking out some food and put the lid back on and it blew up! We have a 25 year old crockpot that works fine and know how to use them and handle them. This crock pot that exploded was purchased at Walmart in Logan UT on 4/11/2015. incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Dual-Fuel Range (gas stovetop burners/electric range)
Model 790.75503207

Cooked food in oven. Turned oven off and 30 minutes later, noticed smoke coming from just under stovetop.
Isolated problem to the small button on the oven frame that turns the oven light on and off when the door is opened and closed.
That oven light "button" was stuck in a depressed position. When we tried to pry it out into a "non-depressed" position, sparks flew (electrical shock hazard), then the wiring caught on fire. We were abe to blow out the fire and turn off electricity to the stove.
Had we not noticed the smoke, the wiring may have continued to burn and cause a fire with significant more damage.

Spoke with Sears the following day. They did not have a recall notice for this problem. They said they could not fix this safety hazard without charge.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a small fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The Samsung Over the Oven Microwave Model SMH1816S that we purchased in May 2013 recently began arcing and throwing sparks inside the casing (not in the food chamber, in fact we tested it with nothing in the food chamber after the initial incident and the unit continued to generate sparks).  We feel this is an extreme fire danger and have disconnected the unit pending an inspection by Samsung's service representative.

I then googled this GE profile - spacesaver (model # PEM31SM4SS) online and discovered that many GE microwaves had caught fire.  I chose to remove our microwave and purchase a new one because it wasn't worth the risk of the whole house burning down.  This product should definitely be recalled and GE needs to be stopped from making microwaves until they figure out what is wrong.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that the center grill is not in line with the two side grills. The consumer stated that in order to center the pan on the side burners grill, the pan has to be also placed on both the side grills and partly on the center grill. The consumer stated that since the pan is not placed evenly on two surfaces, it easily slides off. The consumer has to be very cautious and careful with pans that she uses on the center grill.

Consumer stated that she experienced similar problems of recall#09-333 with her range.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

incident_description:

After unsuccessful attempts, I pulled the unit away from the wall and unplugged it to turn it off. Frigidaire model number PLEFMZ99GCG, serial number [REDACTED]. Spoke with Frigidaire representative on 4/21/2015, she informed me this unit was built in September 2009 and was not subject to the recall. She informed me Frigidaire has no liability for the unit because it is not part of the recall.

I turned the knob back on and then off again the burner looked like it went off then immediately went to glowing red again with the knob turned off. I tried 4 times to get it to cut off my husband finally had to shut the breaker off to get the stove to turn off.

incident_description:
02/16/2015 - The consumer used her blender before she went to work. The consumer indicates that while the unit was blending her smoothie, she heard an unusual sound coming from it but did not think much of it. Though the consumer usually drinks her smoothie right from the blender glass, she was running late and had to place its contents in a mason jar. When the consumer was in her vehicle, she started consuming her drink via a straw. At one point, she noticed that no juice was coming from the straw even though the container was not empty. Believing that possibly a vegetable had gotten stuck, the consumer proceeded to try to extract it with her hand. When the consumer got her hand out, it was actually one of the six prong blades that had broken off.

02/17/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer via e-mail and explained what had happened with their unit. The consumer received an automated response from the manufacturer indicating that they would contact her within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. 

02/19/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer received a call from Products Specialist [REDACTED]. He informed the consumer that he was very sorry she had to go through what she did and that it was the first times that it had happened. He asked the consumer that she should mail them her unit. The consumer informed him that she wanted to receive something in writing indicating what they would do should she send them the unit. [REDACTED] agreed to her request.

02/25/2015 - The consumer had not received an e-mail or any other notice from the manufacturer. She proceeded to e-mail them once again informing them that she was rather upset she never got any response from them and that she would take the matter to a higher level. 

03/11/2015 - The consumer e-mailed them once again as she had not received any response, She asked to speak to the [REDACTED] of the company as she was surprised by their apathy. 

03/15/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer received a call from what she believes was a [REDACTED] but he was unintelligible. She tried contacting him several times and was not able to. 

03/18/2015 - The consumer e-mailed the manufacturer and informed them of the [REDACTED] incident and how she had been trying to get a hold of him.

The consumer received a very nasty e-mail from "[REDACTED]." He indicated that she must have been dialing the wrong number. "[REDACTED]" also informed the consumer that he wanted to speak to her directly as well as verify the legitimacy of the blender.

After the consumer answered that she had not, [REDACTED] informed her that they had done a "ridiculous test" and that after numerous times of blending some contents with an x number of ice cubes, a blade would break off. The consumer did not understand everything [REDACTED] was saying. He asked her if she could send him pictures as well as a picture of the serial number on the blade. The consumer also learned that [REDACTED] is the [REDACTED] of the company. He offered to give her the same blender model she owns.

When the consumer got home, she took some pictures of what was asked of her and sent them to [REDACTED]. The consumer then later looked up the consumer report on the unit and after having read everything, she was left flabbergasted because what happened on the testing they did was exactly what had happened to her blender.  Same model!  900. ... except the fact that the consumer did not use seven (possibly twelve - she does not remember the exact digit) ice cubes when the incident occurred (the consumer indicates that she always uses three iced cubes).

03/22/2015 (Approximately) - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and spoke to [REDACTED]. She asked the [REDACTED]'s address ([REDACTED]) because she wanted to to send him a personal letter. [REDACTED] informed her that she is not at liberty to give her that information. [REDACTED] said she could provide her [REDACTED] and/ or [REDACTED] contact information, to which the consumer declined. 

03/24/2015 - The consumer was contacted via e-mail by their [REDACTED], [REDACTED]. He informed her that he was aware she wanted to speak to the [REDACTED] and not him nor [REDACTED]. He informed the consumer that her case would not be escalated any further. He expressed his disappointment that the consumer did not do as she promised - send them their unit - though the consumer indicates that she never promised such a thing.

03/25/2015 - Several e-mails were exchanged later on. The consumer thanked [REDACTED] for his time and enlightening her on the consumer report. He wrote her back and she responded that she want all consumers to be reimbursed for their faulty blenders as well as recall her blender model.

The consumer indicates that she uses her unit once a day. 

The consumer has no injuries to report nor other incidents. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a broken blender blade but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the consumer's daily use and the manufacturer's acknowledgment of similar incidents.

justification: The incident involves damage to the microwave but no reported injury or harm to a person.

incident_description: Kenmore range front glass shattered. This is the second time in 4 years that it shattered. The first time it was not in use. Second time I had just turned it on and opened the door.

incident_description:
We purchased from Pier One Imports  a set of dishes Ironstone
They are called Maribeth
On the back of the dishes they state that they are dishwasher safe and that they also are microwavable safe -- may become hot.
We have had three different dishes blow up in our microwave upon use with food on them.
I called the company to report a complaint and the store manager stated that the word microwavable -- may become HOT .... is the same as the dishes saying.... they will blow up if overheated!!!

I called the corporate level and the customer service rep acted as though they have good dishes and after looking further into their system ... she saw that they report yes, they may possibly blow up if overheated in a microwave.
However, there is not a recall to date on this product the exploded while my son was microwaving it that could have caused him bodily harm.
