incident_description:
April 10, 2015

To Whom It May Concern:
In 2014 we purchased an Anchor value pack of 3 glass casseroles from Walmart.  Last night (4/9/15) at approximately 5:30PM, we were cooking Cornish Hens in the 5 quart glass casserole.  Half way through the cooking process, the glass casserole exploded inside the oven, seconds after I had been attending to the hens.  I was cooking the hens according to the directions of a recipe IÃÂve cooked several times before.   We stuffed the hens with rosemary & garlic and cooked them in a 450 degree oven for 25 minutes, then lowered the temperature to 350 degrees and slowly poured 1/3 cup of white wine & 1/3 cup of chicken stock over the hens.  Both of these ingredients were at room temperature and I had opened the oven door to lower the inside temperature before slowly pouring the wine/stock mix over the hens.
All 3 of the glass casseroles as well as the packaging state the casseroles are safe for conventional ovens which is how we were using it.
The clean-up process was horrid, glass and shards were everywhere.  We had to use a shop vacuum to clean out the inside of the oven and the surrounding areas.  We discovered that the oven door was hit so hard by flying glass that the door now has a vapor leak and the door will need to be replaced.  The hardwood floor in front of the oven is a mess.  Thank God I had my reading glasses on or I might have received serious injuries to my face not just cuts to my hand or my foot.  
Needless to say I was a nervous wreck and jumpy the entire night.  Even today, thinking about how I could have been seriously injured or maimed, I remain very upset and concerned for others.
This morning I googled Anchor glass explosions and discovered that this is a long standing problem with these glass casseroles.  Why would you allow these items and packaging to still say safe for conventional ovens with no warnings?   I also question Walmart selling this product.  What about consumer protection?
We have photos of my cuts and the shattered glass casserole.  We kept the glass pieces from the shop vacuum for possible further analysis, we have a video of the inside of the oven after the explosion, we have a picture of the temperature of the stove just after the explosion and we have the remaining 2 casseroles from the value pack.
We will notify Walmart of the explosion and our concerns for consumer protection.
Please contact us if additional information is needed.
{REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in cuts to the hand and foot, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the user mentions this is a long-standing problem but not a common occurrence for most users.

incident_description: We received a 9x13 glass Pyrex bakeware dish as a wedding present 3.5 years ago. It was used lightly/moderately. We used it to bake a meatloaf last evening, at 350. After it finished baking, we placed it on top of the stove and removed the meatloaf. We did not clean the pan as there was severe inclement weather, and we had to take shelter outside our home for most of the evening so the dish sat at room temperature for around 24 hours. Today, I began to boil water on a different burner. The pyrex pan was approximately 5 inches away from the heated burner and the pot sitting on it. I heard the water begin to boil but did not attend to the pot for a few minutes to allow it to reach a full rolling boil. Just before I re-entered the kitchen, There was an extremely loud sound and I heard glass landing. I entered the kitchen and found my water at a rolling boil in its pot and my pyrex dish exploded into small and large shards. These flew over the entire kitchen and down our hallway, the furthest being approximately 15 feet away, most being within 6 feet of the dish's original location. This may seem irrelevant to this report, but is important enough to me to include. At this time of day, my 15 moth old typically is playing with his kitchen toys in the exact area where most of the shrapnel was.This would have resulted in me being in the same area with my second son, who is not due to be born for 3 more months. It was nothing more or less than the grace of God that he took the shortest nap of his life earlier in the day resulting in me putting him down for a second nap at that time and preventing us all from standing right in front of the explosion.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass dish causing property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions.

incident_description:
Some time after using our "Cuisinart TOB-40 Custom Classic Toaster Oven Broiler" for toast at 7:30pm the device activated itself and the heating elements became red hot.  We awoke at 9:30pm that evening to the smell of burning plastic and general "hot" smell.  We found the toaster with hot elements glowing in the dark kitchen, even through all control dials and lights indicated the toaster was off.  The only course of action was to unplug the device after which it cooled normally and displayed no damage.

This is a HUGE concern to me as this presents a sizable fire hazard and it frightens me to think how many times this toaster may have activated while I was not at home.

Reading one star reviews of this product on Amazon.com show many users with similar self-activation complaints, and still others with deformed heating element issues. I obviously have no way of knowing but it seems those issues could be caused by self-activation and over heating cycles while the user is not present.

Please investigate this product to protect consumers who, like me before yesterday, are not suspicious that this appliance could destroy their homes and loved ones.  I will not be leaving this product plugged in any more, and will consider whether to discard it completely.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The toaster oven activated itself, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: left front burner remained hot with indicator for that burner lit. the element on light was off. I had to cycle the switch back and forth to get burner to cool off.
justification: The burner remained hot with a misleading indicator, posing a potential burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
RE: Presto Mod 0484602 Popcorn Popper
In the process of popping a batch of popcorn, this product spews very hot popped and un-popped kernels of popcorn in a radius of about 3 feet, out of it's discharge chute. The floor, countertop, and adjacent sink have approximately 20 of these hot projectiles scattered about them in the process of popping a batch of popcorn. We do not overfill it. Even when a large bowl is held up directly under the discharge, the emitted kernels spread around it. My wife suffered a 2nd degree burn on the top of her exposed foot when a very hot un-popped kernel landed on her. We won't use this product any more, because we believe that it is poorly designed in both safety and efficiency
justification: The incident resulted in a 2nd degree burn, which qualifies as an injury, and the description indicates this is a recurring issue with the product.

incident_description: I was using the crock pot on the low setting when it shattered.
justification: The crock pot shattered but there is no mention of injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: We have owned a built-in Kenmore microwave hood combination for several years. Two weeks ago, while we were in other parts of the house, it started running on it's own on full power and with the vent running on high speed. When we got to the Kitchen and realized what was happening we tried to to turn it off and could not!. We had to pull the plug from the outlet in the upper cabinet. The whole unit was very warm to the touch. I suppose if we had not been home it would likely have caused a fire.
justification: The microwave operated unexpectedly and could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I baught a Baby Bullet in February and yesterday 04/10/15 after only using it a few times I found a piece of plastic from the lid in my babys food. The lid on the baby food maker has 2 tiny pieces of plastic that secure the lid in place while its runing and on mine both pieces of plastic have broken off. We found one piece out of 2 in my babys food, im worried we fed our baby a piece of the plastic lid. Im sure im not the only one this has happend to.
justification: A piece of plastic from the lid was found in the baby's food, indicating a product defect, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she started having a problem with the dishwasher about three months after it was purchased.

The two plastic wheels that hold the top rack keeps breaking. The consumer stated that the top rack falls in your hands whenever the rack is pulled out.

The consumer stated that parts were ordered and replaced twice by her husband.

About two weeks ago, the consumer pulled the rack out. The rack was filled with dishes. Her hands were in between the rungs and the rack fell on her hands.

No medical attention was required.

(03/11/2015) The consumer contacted the company to advised them of the issue. The consumer was advised that a replacement part would be sent to her.
justification: The incident involved a recurring issue with the dishwasher rack breaking, leading to inconvenience and minor incidents, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
Please see the attached letter to which I have never received a response. The stove has been sitting there for more than a year now without the back panel. (See attached photographs). I heard the promotion for the special on CBS news report, "Shattering Glass/' but was out of town and did not have an opportunity to timely view it. I thought it was important to let you know that this is not a new story about "shattering glass" and that Whirlpool has consistently denied over time, that it is even possible for the glass to shatter without any kind of impact to it. I would appreciate any assistance in dealing with Whirlpool.
...
Some years ago, I purchased a Kitchen Aid gas range. Shortly after, while using the back burners on the range, the gals panel shattered. The company took the position that the problem should be resolved by replacing the glass back panel. I was concerned that I or someone else using the stove might get hurt, and asked if there was an alternative to the glass panel. I was told that there was, and that there had never been an issue of glass shattering, unexpectedly, without impact to it, with the range.

Reluctantly, but having no choice, I had another glass panel sent to me in the mail. Later, an authorized repair person was sent to put in the panel. In conversation, with the repairman, he told me that the company was lying because it was his experience, that the glass panels shattered all the time and that it was a design defect to place the panel so close to the back burners. He said that the only way to ensure that the back panel would not shatter was not to use the two back burners or to be certain they were always used on low. As at that point my family often needed all the burners to be used at once, I wrote a letter to your corporate office explaining that I did not purchase a two burner stove and needed the stove to be replaced. I received a letter from your company which emphasized that the glass would not shatter and even if it did, it was tempered glass and therefore would pose no problem. And of course, the letter also stated that no one else in recorded history had a problem with the panel.

In December 2013, while standing over the stove cooking breakfast on the front burners, as I have feared all these years, the glass back panel spontaneously and inexplicably shattered and went flying all over the stove, the kitchen counters, the floor and hit me in my face. I called Whirlpool and spoke to our Customer Care Department. The persons I spoke to kept repeating that Whirlpool would send me a new glass panel. I explained the history of the situation and emphatically refused to have the issue resolved by sending me another glass panel.
...
I have a mark on my face from the bruise where the glass hit me, could not use the stove for days, had to clean up the glass from all over the kitchen and stove and have spent hours on the phone talking to your staff...a staff that is stuck on giving me another panel to redress Whirlpool's malfeasance.
...
justification: The incident resulted in a facial injury from shattered glass, and the description indicates a recurring issue with the stove's design.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dishwasher while in use caught fire.  He stated that his spouse had placed the dishwasher to run and towards the end of the cycle, they smelled a burning odor and discovered that the unit was emitting smoke from the control panel (top of door). The smoke started to engulf the room, he used the circuit breaker to switch off the power to the unit and ventilated the room.  The smoke eventually dissipated.  There were no prior incidents or service calls for the dishwasher.


The manufacturer was not as yet.

Caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and posed a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his dishwasher which he states that the upper rack is pulled out on gliders.

He is reporting that the connector that attaches the upper rack to the gliders is faulty, could easily break instantly causing the rack to drop, presenting consumer with a sudden, heavy weight and potentially lead to users to be injured by either the rack hitting their hand or possibly glasses or dishes breaking, also potentially causing cuts.

A connector repair kit has manufactured and was included in a repair to this callers dishwasher at his expense.  Caller attests that this safety issue is well known to the manufacturer
Adjuster part # W10712394.  This part was re-designed by manufacturer replacing plastic with metal parts because of many failures reported.

The caller was charged for this "adjuster" and is asking that this connect 2 adjusters & gliders become recalled or become an automatic repair from manufacturer at manufacturer expense.

He would also ask to be reimbursed by the manufacturer for this repair due to it's being a safety issue.
justification: The description indicates potential for injury due to the rack dropping or broken dishes causing cuts, and the issue is known to the manufacturer with many failures reported.

incident_description:
(12/1/2014) The consumer stated that an ice cube that came out of the dispenser had a chunk of black plastic inbedded in the cube. 

The consumer called Whirlpool and advised them of what  happened. The consumer was advised that it would cost him a minimum of $89.95 for a home visit. The consumer declined the offer.

(12/1/2014) The consumer emailed [REDACTED]-CEO, with photos of the ice cubes that came out of the dispenser. The consumer received a phone call from [REDACTED],Product Safety. on 12/4.  The consumer was advised that a local service from a department store would reach out to the consumer to replace or repair the product at no cost.

(12/16/2014) A technician from Martin Appliance came out and placed a new ice maker module in the refrigerator. The consumer was advised that the mold heater connection was burned out and  a portion of the ice maker module housing was cracked and missing.

04/05/2015)The consumer stated that a chunk of black plastic came out of the ice maker when ice was dispensed. 

The consumer will contact the manufacturer again.
justification: The incident involved a foreign object in the ice dispenser but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence suggests a possible likelihood (3) of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Cuisinart easy pop cpm900 popcorn maker has defective handles.  the latch mechanism breaks - probably due to heat breaking down the plastic and/or bad design.

This is not obvious and when one attempts to separate the top from the bottom in order to get the popcorn out, it requires excessive force and can cause you to burn yourself from the sudden release.

The bottom plate is burning hot - it's an electric heated element - and the only way to use the product is to separate the bottom plate from the base in order to turn it over.

Unit suddenly came apart due to defect in the clips and I almost dropped burning plate and popcorn on my nephew who is a toddler and was visiting.

This part has failed twice on my unit - the manufacturer refused to extend the warranty and there are numerous reports of this happening to others - including the newer model.  We do not use it often, so it should absolutely not have failed due to age or use.

The manufacturer should be required to warn consumers of this danger, recall all these units (both models) for replacement, redesign the latch to a better material such as high-temp plastic or metal and extend the warranty for this failure.
justification: The incident describes a near-miss with potential for severe burns or injury to a toddler, but no actual injury occurred. The defect is reported to be common, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The same as incident # 20130224-003CA-2147458488    The 'off' position has malfunctioned and after the light goes off, the oven timer continues to run until it reaches the 'on all the time ' position and then the oven TURNS ITSELF ON INDEFINITELY.  This is very dangerous.  Why hasn't something been done about this ??
justification: The oven malfunctioning and turning on indefinitely poses a significant hazard, but the description does not mention any actual injury or death.

incident_description:
02/01/2015 - The consumer was back in his home for a few days from vacation. During this time, he indicates that he never used his unit. Because an incident occurred, the consumer assumes that he must have bumped into the unit's knob and accidentally turned it on. The consumer does not remember ever bumping into the stove but he assumes he must have since nobody else was there. The consumer left his home. 

02/13/2015 - The consumer's daughter went to visit her father's home and upon opening the back door of the house, he indicates that his daughter informed him that the entire house was filled with gas. She proceeded to close the door. The daughter contacted the consumer and the consumer gave her directions to turn off the propane tank on the outside of the house. The daughter turned off the tank and waited thirty minutes before she opened the house doors and windows in order to it let air out. 

When the daughter went into the kitchen, she noticed the left burner knob of the stove was in the LOW position. The consumer informed his daughter that the gas smell must have came from the stove. Approximately an hour later, the consumer gave his daughter instructions to turn the furnace on as the weather was very cold. Because of the incident and the lingering smell of gas, the consumer's daughter and her family did not feel safe staying in the house so they left. 

02/16/2015 - The consumer contacted the retailer, the manufacturer and his gas company in order to inform them of the incident. When he spoke to a manufacturer Customer Representative, his incident was recorded under Reference No.: 771 223 2970. 

The consumer is very concerned because of the possible disaster that could have happened due to the stove's knob accidentally being turned on with the slightest of touch. 

07/15/2014 (Approximately) - The consumer was in his kitchen and all of a sudden he heard a hissing sound. Looking around, he noticed that it was coming from the same left burner knob. When he contacted the retailer, the store owner put him on hold to try a small experiment. When the store owner, [REDACTED], came back to the phone, he informed the consumer that he was appalled at how easy it was to bump into the stove and inadvertently turn the stove on. [REDACTED]offered to send one of his Service Technicians to inspect his unit but the consumer denied the offer. 

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer has no injuries to report.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with no reported injuries, but potential for serious harm.

incident_description:
Caller stated that around 2007 the electrical wire nuts melted while the dishwasher was in use.  He stated that there was smoke emitting from the unit and they powered it off. He stated that had installed the wire nuts himself and thought that he might have possible done something wrong. He stated that he noticed complaints online about this issue and realize that he is not at fault.  He replaced the wire nuts and continued to use the dishwasher.


Caller stated that he noticed a recall online and he contacted the retailer, he was advised to look for the serial number on the base of the machine on the front but it was not.  He was told to contact the manufacturer and he was advised that it was stamped on the door panel or a tag on the side of the door.  He was informed that they could not assist him until he provided the numbers.  He stated that he noticed that there is a location where maybe a tag used to be.



3/2 He was notified by his spouse that while the dishwasher was in use there was smoke emitting from it.  She powered it off and open the door which filled the room.  He stated that when he arrived home he disassembled the door and noticed that the plastic area on the door had melted and fused together.


Caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard.

Dishwasher has now been repaired after many calls and much run-a-round by Bosch "call center".

Caller found their original paperwork - there was no identification on the door.  Kelsy Appliance fixed - They are located on RT. 90 West Rockport, ME
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting components but no reported injuries, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is possible given the recurrence of similar issues.

incident_description:
We purchased a few of these glass tumblers from Walmart, "Mr. Coffee 18-oz Glass Tumbler with Lid" The single ones are sold in stores, Walmart item #552018950.  The 2-packs are sold on Walmart.com, item #552156498.  I have not seen them sold anywhere else.

The first incident was on March 21, 2015.  My husband was holding one and tripped.  It shattered, slicing his hand open in many places.  A trip to the hospital was avoided, but barely.  We figured since he tripped, it made sense, but shouldn't travel mugs be a little sturdier?  Made of tempered or shatterproof glass?  

Well, he gave them a chance, and purchased another one.  The second incident happened April 5, 2015.  His second tumbler was on the table.  My finger tip barely brushed the top, not even enough to knock the cup over, but it shattered!  It is clear that it broke when I touched it, because there were large shards of glass on the table.  If it broke when it hit the floor, there wouldn't be glass on the table.  Thankfully, I froze, and my husband was wearing shoes, so he was able to get mine and we could clean up.

I am terrified that a small child will touch their parent's tumbler and the same thing will happen, maybe even with hot coffee in it!  These mugs are extremely unsafe!  Similar reviews have been posted on Walmart.com.

Please recall these!  Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring near-hospitalization and repeated occurrences suggest a pattern of unsafe product behavior.

incident_description:
The glass front assembly panel on our Frigidaire electric oven exploded. The model number is GLED388ASD. It was purchased from Sears approximately 12 years ago.

The stove has rarely been used; it was in perfect condition. The oven was not on when it exploded. The assembly panel is a double pane of decorative glass that covers the entire oven door. It's installed in front of a second interior glass panel set into a metal frame (that did not break). 

A stainless steel pan from an adjacent counter was accidentally knocked off and must have hit the oven door. The glass front did not simply break but exploded outward with literally hundreds of shards reaching up to as far as 4 to 5 feet from the stove. About a quarter of the panel remained in the setting, albeit broken into minute pieces and crackling.

Obviously, a young child who picked up a pan or other toy and struck that stove front could easily have been blinded or worse. 

I was completely dumbfounded that could have happened ÃÂ no idea. Unfortunately I did not take a photo.

There were no injuries. I was the only adult in the kitchen and was standing at the sink facing away from the stove.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the oven's glass panel causing significant damage but no injuries, as stated in the description.

incident_description: While trying to toast a matzoh, the appliance burst into flames. The flames were almost two feet high. It was terrifying. Thankfully, I was quick thinking and able to put the fire out without injury to myself or my pets. My other family members were not home at the time of this incident
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description: While the oven was preheating, the coil wire inside the oven caught fire and the oven is broken.
justification: The oven caught fire but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description: My wife was warming a dish and the Sears Kenmore Microwave Oven  Model number 721.67909800 shut down. She opened the door on the oven and it started up. I was in the kitchen at the time and I told her to shut the door and unplug it.  This model microwave oven may fail like this and hurt some child.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) based on the mention of potential harm to a child and the model's history.

incident_description: First, the ovens are not accurate in there temps by as much as 75 degrees too cool. Second, one cool day, the controls for the cook top started flashing a code and sounding an alarm. This was when the unit was out of warranty. Over the next two days the unit continued. When the weather warmed up, the unit stopped alarming and went back to operating. Third, and most dangerous is the inside of the lower oven has warped and the grates no longer stay in position. They are too small for the opening. I had a turkey fall down first and now the upper shelves are totally useless as the will not stay up at all.
justification: The warped oven interior and unstable grates pose a risk of injury from falling items, and the issue is likely to recur given the described conditions.

incident_description: My husband was tightening the loose screws on the oven door. The door exploded all over the kitchen floor and into the foyer. Having made contact with Kenmore they are willing to send out a tech for $170+tx with the glass and labor charges of $160 or I can purchase a 1 year warranty for 298 dollars that would cover all expenses. Next call was to try to talk to a supervisor. The person was very pleasant throughout the conversation but would have to send me to customer solutions because this was a recall product. Customer Solutions check all her info and it is not a recall product. After some research on the internet it appears this is not a new problem and the glass that is being used for various products is not safe.  Most of the complaints are for the Kenmore oven glass door and I'm having difficulty understanding since most of the complaint started in 2009 why this product is still being used. There are 299 complaints from 2009 to 2015. What does it take to get a recall on a product.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing damage but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. With 299 complaints over several years, the occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely).

incident_description: Cuisinart DCC-2205 Coffee Maker electrical fire.  This was the replacement coffee maker sent by Cuisinart for a coffee maker that had also had an electrical fire.
justification: The incident describes an electrical fire in a coffee maker, which is a significant safety issue but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: Electric range. one burner does not turn off, just burns hotter.  Must be turned off by disconnecting the range from electrical source.
justification: The burner not turning off poses a risk of overheating or fire, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: Pyrex exploded in my hands when I pulled it out of oven

incident_description: Unsafe Products - We have a Whirlpool Velos Microwave/Convection Oven (several years old).  On or about March 26th, while heating a small cup of water (in a microwave safe container) my wife and I witnessed the Microwave door burst open, shooting all contents across my Kitchen. Had my wife been just 12 inches closer, she would have sustained injury.  The event was powerful enough to fracture the latches that keep the door secure while in use. In addition, the unit shows no signs of life or power at all. When we spoke with a Whirlpool rep (just today) she did not exhibit any signs of concern. The Rep suggested that we call out an authorized repair person and have the item repaired at my expense.  My immediate concerns is that there is no indication that the unit will not again explode but perhaps next time while my kids or others are closer to the unit and become harmed.
justification: The incident involved a microwave door bursting open with enough force to fracture latches, posing a clear risk of injury if someone had been closer, indicating potential for harm.

incident_description:
Our Dishwasher heat cycle turned on by itself, it overheated. We smelled smoke/melted plastic, when I went to open the dishwasher, the handle burned hand and caused blisters. I used a potholder to open the dishwasher, it was full of smoke and all the plastic had melted. Including all plastic parts of the dishwasher and my plastic dishes/utensils etc. 

This was a GE Profile Dishwasher, there have been multiple reports about this Model having this issue but GE has not put it on the recall list. It was very dangerous, especially because I have little kids at home.  Our tile countertops above the dishwasher were to hot to touch.  We turned off the dishwasher and left it open a few inches, it still continued to heat. We finally had to turn off the circuit breaker. 

I called GE, the sent a repair man out to take a look at it, the cost to repair it will be over $800, I am waiting to hear back from GE to see what they will cover.
justification: The incident caused blisters from burns and significant property damage, indicating an injury severity. Multiple reports suggest the issue is not isolated, making occurrence likely.

incident_description:
The condiment bin, on our refrigerator door, broke off and fell on my foot.
The condiment bin had condiments in it, including ketchup, mustard, relish, mayo, etc.
The condiment bin was Not filled to capacity (overloaded)
Some of the condiments jars, in the condiment bin, were made of glass and shattered when they hit the floor.
I was not adding or removing anything from the condiment bin when it broke off.
I was grabbing something out of the main part of the refrigerator when the shelf fell onto my foot.

This is the second condiment bin to break on my refrigerator.
Both times, the bins broke in the same way.
Both condiment bins fell from the refrigerator door, without touching them.
justification: The condiment bin fell on the person's foot, causing injury, and this has happened twice in the same way, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I have the Hy Cite Enterprises Royal Prestige Cookware with the thermal walls that was recalled. I sent my cookware in as prescribed in the recall that was seen for pans collapsing. After getting my pans back from the company my 1.5 qt pan constantly made a whistling noise when I used it. One day as I was cooking some caramel sauce in it, the pan was whistling like it had been doing since the pans had been returned. As my sauce was almost done, all of a sudden it made a great popping sound and the plug in the side blew out and the pan flew off the stove while flinging hot caramel sauce all over the kitchen and myself. Fortunately for me I managed to jump and escape most of the caramel sauce that went all over as it was very hot and could have really caused some severe burns instead of the few tiny blisters that I received from the hot caramel sauce landing on me in spots. The of course I had to deal with cleaning up caramel from one side of the kitchen from the other. I was very unhappy with this and have been concerned about using any of the other cookware since then.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (tiny blisters) from hot caramel sauce, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since this appears to be an isolated incident post-recall.

incident_description:
We have owned this set of glasses for about 6 years, and I do not remember where they were purchased. They are drinking glasses with a heavy bottom, identified by the letters PALAKS in the bottom. I washed the dishes in the dishwasher at 8:00 PM on March 28, 2015. At approximately 8:00 AM on March 29th, I was taking the dishes out of the dishwasher and putting them away. I grasped one of the 12 ounce drinking glasses between my thumb and forefinger to pick it up from the dishwasher, and it exploded in my hand. I was fortunate I was wearing eyeglasses, because several small glass shards hit my face. I was not cut by the flying glass. Now I'm afraid to pick the glasses up by the bottom. 

The dishes in the dishwasher were slightly cooler than the air temperature, because the house thermostat had been set for 68 degrees F. overnight, and the furnace had just heated the air temperature to 70 degrees F.

I have photos that I can provide of the scene of the explosion. The "Add Files" button does not work for me. I originally received a message that I needed a different version of Flash Player. I went to the Adobe web site and downloaded and installed the most recent version, but the "Add Files" button still does not work, even after closing and restarting Internet Explorer and Firefox.
justification: The glass exploded but no injury occurred, only minor impact from glass shards that did not cause cuts.

incident_description:
On Easter Sunday, April 5th I was cooking a casserole in my Kenmore glasstop electric range/oven (Model: 790.928030310, SN: VF02465189) that I bought from Sears at Collin Creek Mall in Plano, TX on Feb 8, 2014. As I put my hand on the handle to open the door to get my casserole out, the outside glass literally exploded. There was a very loud POP then it shot glass all over my legs/feet. The oven had been on 375 degrees for 45 minutes. 

I have had no previous problems until this one. I can only the damage it would've caused to my eyes/face had I been crouched down in front of it, looking through the glass watching my casserole brown, like I usually do.  My kids help me cook all the time too so it scares me to think about what would've happened to them had they been standing in front of it helping me. I wont even use it now because I have NO idea why it happened and I don't trust it any more. Futhermore, there were 3 other adults and 2 children in the house who are witnesses to this event.

Monday morning I called/twittered Sears. Their "computers were down" so they told me someone would call me to schedule an appointment. They didn't. The Twitter response told me to call the "recall hotline". I called customer service back this evening and they told me it was out of warranty (...of course it is) and that I would have to pay $100 for them to come look at it and I would have to pay for the glass to be replaced but they couldn't even give me a cost. (I will NOT pay to have it replaced - warranty or not. I didn't break it.) It is defective and highly dangerous and I want a recall issued on it immediately. Nobody else should have to go through this. I also called the Sears "recall" hotline and they said it wasn't under recall and that I had to work with Kenmore now and they washed their hands completely of the entire situation and said "Sorry we can't help."

I called/twitted Kenmore and am waiting on a response. In the meantime I want to report this product as it is very dangerous and the results could have been disastrous. And the company who sold it to me couldn't care less.
justification: The incident resulted in glass shards hitting the user's legs/feet, which constitutes an injury. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) since the user had no previous problems with the oven and such incidents are not commonly reported.

incident_description: My Bodum b.pour coffee maker is melting the plastic housing when in use. The smell of burning plastic alerted me to this issue. The housing section on this coffee maker is clear plastic, so I can see that the wiring connector on the water heating element is positioned too close to the housing. I think a simple heat shield on the connector will solve this dangerous situation.
justification: The incident involves melting plastic and a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Summary: Electric stove top range fell apart and the 220volt burner landed inside the chassis.
Turned the left burner on and it made a loud popping noise and bright flash - pretty much immediately and the clock started blinking. Waited a few minutes and tried again with the other left burner and it popped too. Now none of the stovetop burners work. 

Kenmore Model 790-90153408  SN: NF41931997
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove top with electrical issues but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
08/20/2014 (Approximate) - The consumer was in her living room and heard a very unfamiliar & loud noise of an appliance turning on coming from her kitchen. When the consumer went to her kitchen, she noticed her microwave oven had turned itself on. The consumer tried shutting off the unit and was unable to. When the consumer touched the outside of the microwave, she noticed that it was very hot to the touch, something that had never happened before. The consumer proceeded to unplug the unit. According to the consumer, all this occurred within fifteen seconds. 

The consumer contacted the Fire Department because she did not feel safe plugging the unit back in. When they arrived and tried to plug in the unit, it would not turn on. The Fire Marshall informed the consumer that the unit was dead and that they wanted to throw it away because of the safety hazard that it posed. The Fire Marshall informed the consumer that it was a good thing that she was in her home because if not, there most likely would have been a tragedy.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained what had happened with their unit. She asked to be called back by an Executive but never was.

When the manufacturer did not call the consumer back, she proceeded to file a report with the Better Business Bureau, who also referred her back to the manufacturer. The consumer also contacted her State Attorney General's Office to let them know of the incident.

01/15/2015 (Approximate) - The consumer contacted the manufacturer. This time, they asked her to send them the unit back so they can analyze and inspect it.

03/24/2015 - The consumer received a letter from the manufacturer informing her that they would send her the microwave back as it was in perfect conditions and that nothing could be found wrong with it when they had eval. it.

The consumer does not want to receive the unit. The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard as the fire department also did.  The consumer does not want another microwave oven, ever.  Esp. the one that was hers and is a fire hazard.  The consumer will ask Emerson Radio Corp. to send it back to her, keep it in box, in case CPSC needs to examine it.  This is what CPSC advised the consumer to do.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave that posed a safety hazard but resulted in no injuries, and similar incidents are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: Woke up Sunday morning to see my oven door was shattered and glass was blown 7 feet from the oven door.  It is only my husband and myself.  There was no damage to the door before we found the glass blown out of the door.  I am very concerned that the glass shattered 7 feet from the oven door, what would have happened if someone was standing next to the door or opening it.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (shattered oven door) but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
the glass top of my GE Profile Gas Range (Model J2S968SOH3SS) exploded. This happened as I was cooking salmon burgers on one of the burners. The incident happened precisely as I was turning off the stove. There was the sound of a small explosion. The glass top of the range shattered and sent shards of glass on the floor along with the pan I was cooking the salmon burgers with. I had been cooking the salmon burger for roughly 10 minutes before the incident happened and the cooking area was being actively vented with my above range vent.
Afterwards I called the local gas company (PG&E). They came out to my house and determined that there were no gas leaks.
justification: The glass top exploded but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Heard pop behind double oven, saw flash. Oven breaker tripped we couldn't get the breaker to return to normal w/out having oven flash or pop. we decided to pull oven out and we saw that there was an issue w/the wiring behind the oven. There was melted plastic, wires had been fused together. There was soot, melted plastic or rubber underneath the wire box mounted to the wall, there was also soot on the back side of the oven where it met the wall/wiring harness.
justification: The incident involved electrical damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Keurig issued recall kits to retrofit brewers so consumer could install to prevent burns. My brewer is now exhibiting the behavior after retrofit.

To add to the "risk of harm": the coffee machine intermittently sprays hot water, steam, and coffee grounds around the appliance. Although I have not been burned, any consumer in the vacinity of the appliance when it malfunctions, is at great risk of steam burns/scalding. Again, this is after the retrofit to the appliance for the very same problem.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning coffee machine that sprays hot water and steam, posing a risk of burns, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I am the owner of a Kenmore Electric Range Model# 79092803011.  Recently, my wife was using the oven to cook dinner.  We began to smell smoke and noticed that the food in the oven was burning.  We made several attempts to shut off the oven but, it wouldn't shut off and continued to get hotter.  The oven temperature exceeded 500 degrees and only shutdown when the circut breaker was cut off.  Thankfully, the house did not catch fire.

I was so distressed by this experince that I searched on-line to see if there were any recalls on this product.  I was shocked to see how many similar complaints have been posted.  Complaintsboard.com has more than I can count, all with very similar circumstances.

My wife received minor burns trying to remove the burnt food from the oven.  Fortunately, we were close by and acted promptly, otherwise I'm sure the situation would have been much worse.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns (injury) and the description mentions numerous similar complaints, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Oven racks collapse, causing hot food/racks/dishes to fall to bottom of oven. Racks no longer fit securely on tracks, and it appears oven liner has bowed.
justification: Hot food and dishes fell, but no injury was reported. The issue with the oven racks and liner suggests a recurring problem.

incident_description: We had turned off the icemaker and had the appliance pulled away from the wall to replace the flooring, paint etc.. several days later, we left for about an hour and came back to a horrific odor and found that the ice maker had burned the entire interior, melting out an entire section of the plastic body that houses the maker. The ice maker was still turned off. The entire freezer and refrigerator is saturated in black soot. some of my groceries were not salvagable, if it was things not in sealed packaging. It was a miracle the entire house did not burn down.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was brewing my coffee as usual in the keurig k10 brewer and when i went to check if it was finished smoke started to come out of the top of the brewer and very, very hot water spewed all over my arms, and a slight burn on my face about an inch from my eye.the water was hot enough as to where i was lucky it didnt cause serious damage to my eye but the burns on my arm and cheek were fairly severe and needed some treatment.
justification: The incident caused severe burns requiring treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with standard coffee brewer use.

incident_description: Pyrex pan shattered in preheated oven 25 minutes after placing in oven.
justification: The Pyrex pan shattered, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore range (model # 790.92203014, serial # VF21448148), and the back right burner will not shut off. We have had to cut the power to the stove/range. The range is no longer under warranty, but it has created a fire hazard in my home, one I don't feel I should have to pay for. I have called Sears at least 10 times and have been given the run-around by completely unhelpful customer service representatives, the last of which finally told me that it wasn't their problem and they aren't legally obligated to fix it.
justification: The burner not shutting off creates a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: As I reported in report number  20150324-1EA09-2147434280 on 3/24/2015, my GE microwave set paper towel / plate on fire when operated with the turn table off as the item being microwaved was too large for it to rotate.  Also, when I placed two small plates in this microwave to warm them & turned the turn table off as they were too large to rotate & removed the plate nearest the "microwave beam" and handed it to my wife, it blistered her hand such that she dropped the plate and had to be treated for the minor burn injury.  I contacted GE & they eventually sent a technician to check my microwave.  He stated that it "worked as designed".  After further follow up with GE, they offered to have a second technician check the microwave.  He called me today & stated that, per GE's instructions, he would charge me for the "service call" if he found that the microwave worked as designed.  After he told me how he was going to test the microwave, which was rudimentary at best, I declined to have him make the service call.  One technician stated that he is seeing more fires in microwaves, now that more recycled material is being used in paper products, the other indicated that the design of the microwave oven is such that fires can occur and that hot spots in dishes routinely occur.  GE states that this microwave works as designed & it causes fires & causes bodily  harm to users, with no warnings included in the associated literature.  As such, this microwave has a MAJOR DESIGN FLAW THAT IS HAZARDOUS TO USERS and should be recalled completely.  This type microwave should not be allowed to be sold in the USA without appropriate design changes to eliminate the current hazard or should at least REQUIRE HAZARD WARNINGS BE PLACED PROMINENTLY ON THE APPLIANCE AND IN THE USER LITERATURE to not use the buttons to turn the turntable off except under very limited operating conditions!!!!!!.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn injury to the user's wife, and the description indicates that such injuries and fires can occur with this microwave design.

incident_description: After using a veggetti vegetable slicer I bit something hard and I spit it out and it was a piece of metal that had broken off of the inside of the device.
justification: A piece of metal broke off the device and was ingested, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(03/15/20150 The consumer stated that his wife woke up and smelled something. She went onto the kitchen and discovered that the oven was on. The temperature was higher than the mode used for self-cleaning. The plastic items that were on the top of the stove had melted. None of the controls were in the "on" position. The cabinets around the stove were too hot to touch.

The consumer disconnected the unit at the circuit breaker. The consumer unplugged the unit and placed it on his covered patio.

The consumer contacted Sears and was advised that they will send an accident report to the corporate. 

The consumer wanted to send the information directly to the corporate office but was not given any contact information.

They consumer was also offered a repair visit at a cost to him. The consumer denied the visit.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plastic items and overheated cabinets) but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her microwave around September 2013 and had no problems with it until March 2015 when her husband opened it to heat his coffee and it began running while the door was open.
When he shut the door it stopped running, he set it at one minute, heated his coffee, retrieved it when the unit signaled completion and stopped but when he opened the door to pick his coffee up the microwave began running again.
The same incident happened again the next morning with the caller.
They tried to see whether it was gong to continue and each time they open the microwave door the microwave begins running.
The caller is reporting this incident as an extreme safety hazard noting the heat and radiation emitted by a microwave and the potential harm it could cause to humans and property.

There are no known injuries to report at this time

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them
justification: The microwave operates unexpectedly when the door is open, posing a safety hazard, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description: We have a Sharp Corporation, Model No. R5H81, Microwave Oven. It always worked safely and satisfactorily. But, since a month, it randomly turns on itself while it is OFF. It does NOT stop when STOP/CLEAR button on Control Panel is pressed.
justification: The microwave turns on randomly but there is no mention of injury or harm, only a malfunction.

incident_description:
On or about July 2013 I purchased some of the same "Glassware" Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, Inc. uses in their restaurants throughout North America to serve Margaritas and other beverages in.  I purchased 3 cases that held 12 glasses each.  The glassware is seriously defective.

The "glassware" was not used until December 2014 so I had no idea prior to this time that the product was seriously defective.  During this time I was putting the glassware away in my cabinet (holding the glass by its base) and the base separated from the drinking portion and smashed on the tile floor in the kitchen.  It literally exploded when it hit the floor and shards of glass flew everywhere throughout the kitchen and family room areas.  It took approximately 2 hours to clean up and luckily none of us were injured from this incident (our dog, 3 cats, and my daughter).  When the glass shattered and flew everywhere, I found pieces in our pets food/water dishes, on the furniture, the countertops, in the throw carpet and pretty much every nook and cranny within the areas previously mentioned.

In early 2015 a second incident occurred and another glass separated, smashed on the file floor and shards flew everywhere once again.

On or about March 17th, 2015 a third incident occurred.  I was holding another glass by the base and this one separated as well.  Fortunately, I caught the main part in my other hand as it was heading for the tile floor.

That day, I immediately called the restaurant manager for the Chandler, AZ location where I had initially purchased them.  A new manager was now overseeing this location.  I explained to him how I had come to purchase this glassware, explained that they were seriously defective, I wanted to return them for a full refund, but more importantly I expressed my concern for the safety of other guests they serve beverages to in their restaurant chains throughout the country -  if it could happen to me 3 times in this short period, it could potentially happen to others.  Thankfully, no one in our family were injured.

Long story short, it was extremely challenging to get these two managers (store and/or Regional) to take me seriously regarding the defective glassware and my safety concerns.  I persisted in calling their Franchise office.  A young lady that I spoke with stated she would immediately pass information on through the chain of command.  This was an extremely important issue for me - several reasons. Thus, I did not want to leave it until I felt satisfied that a higher up would take me seriously and that immediate action would be taken taken by the Corporation.

Finally, I spoke with the [REDACTED] [REDACTED] at the RR corporate office.  I explained my concerns to [REDACTED]; my experiences and concerns for the safety of others who may come in contact with this defective product.  [REDACTED]informed me that the glassware in question was made in China.  I made it very clear to all the parties I spoke with, that I would be reporting this matter to the CPSC to ensure that my concerns did not fall on deaf ears, get pushed to the side, or lost in the shuffle per se.

[REDACTED] was great.  After we spoke he sent me an Email stating:

"...I apologize that the glasses were breaking. I share your concern for safety and will pass on the concerns to our purchasing department and our supplier..."

As at the date of this submission, I have no idea what RR corporate has been done about having this defective glassware removed from their locations, nor do I have any knowledge whether or not RR has made their own complaint submission to the CPSC for their information, investigation and follow-up.
justification: The incident involved defective glassware breaking multiple times, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she noticed that approximately 6 weeks ago she noticed that whenever you leaned against the knobs it would turn the burners on.  She stated that her spouse leaned against the knob and when he had left the kitchen they noticed that the plastic container that was sitting on one of the burners started melting and flames erupted.

3/2015 Caller stated that a service called was placed at the repair facility and a technician was sent out.  She was informed that there had been several complaints on this particular model because the knobs turn on easily.

Caller stated that she contacted the manufacturer about the problems she was having with the range and she was advised that the range was working properly.

Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled before it causes a house fire.

This range continues to be a problem.  Everyone is afraid to get near the range as it turns on the burners and the lights in the oven.  They don't dare put anything on the top.

The caller doesn't feel they need to live like this worrying about a range that turns on when you get next to it.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to the range turning on unintentionally, causing a plastic container to melt and flames to erupt, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Exploding oven glass
Maytag Gemini
Gas Double Oven Range
Model #MGT8655XW00
Serial # D04042021

Outer oven glass of large oven exploded out into the kitchen. Oven was not in use at the time. I contacted Maytag, but they were totally disinterested and didn't even respond to my emails. It's being reported now as I thought at the time it was possibly a unique circumstance. In looking online now I see the incidents have skyrocketed, yet nothing has been done. 

Whether design or quality, a fix should be mandated from all manufacturers and recalls implemented. Had a child (and there are children present) been walking by when this happened, it would have been exactly even with their face. I can't comprehend this being ignored when the problem is so widespread and across all manufacturers.
justification: The oven glass exploded but no injury occurred, though there was potential for harm. Online reports indicate the issue is widespread, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: toaster has 4 slots, each  surrounded with a strip of stainless steel surrounding the opening. While removing finished toast my finger touched the stainless steel which was extremely hot and resulted in a burn of about 1 inch on my finger
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) as touching hot surfaces while using a toaster is a common occurrence.

incident_description:
02/15/2015 (Approximate) - The consumer's wife opened the microwave door and all of a sudden, the turntable started spinning. The consumer's wife and her husband tried closing the microwave door several times and pressing the OFF button however, whenever they opened the microwave door, it would start again. The couple tried unplugging and plugging back the unit but nothing worked: the microwave would turn itself on when it was opened and turn off when its door was closed. 

The consumer's wife stated that if they programmed the unit, it works fine but when the door is opened, it starts again so they do not want to use it because of this same reason. 

The consumer's wife indicates that the only way the microwave will function properly is if it is unplugged, the microwave door is opened, the food container is inserted, the microwave door is shut, the microwave is plugged back in, and then started. You then have to stop the microwave, unplug it, open its door, take your food out, and then plug it back in. The consumer's wife states that although this works, they only tried it a few times but that they are not using the microwave because they do not feel safe using it.

The couple tried this for the first three or four days. The consumer's wife indicates that they use their unit approximately three to four times on a daily basis. 

02/27/2015 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer. After explaining his microwave situation to a representative, the representative informed the consumer that they had not heard of this before. The consumer was informed that they do not service his area but that they could refer them to a couple of service companies so they can inspect his unit. The consumer refused this information. The consumer asked to speak to somebody else about technical issues but he was informed that they do not give any technical information to consumers. 

The consumer contacted a service company, Judd & Black, but was informed that they could not assist him as they do not service microwaves by General Electric. The consumer was informed that the issue he is having with his unit is most likely due to the microwave door. The consumer was advised that it would be better to just buy a new microwave since the cost to fix it would be high.

The consumer went online to see if other people had been having issues with microwaves and found out that they have, though he is not aware if with his same model. The consumer plans on replacing his unit for a newer one.

The consumer has no other incidents or any injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was identified and addressed by the consumer.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his dishwasher while in use for a few seconds started to emit smoke  and when he opened the front panel of the door he noticed that the electrical wiring had melted.  He also noticed that the control panel was charred and the plastic upper part of the door melted.  This is a unit at a rental property.  

He stated that he researched the dishwasher recalls but his unit model was not included.

The manufacturer was not contacted.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and melting wiring, indicating a significant hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
my Samsung microwave oven model#smh1622s / serial#j6k77woc700313w - the problem is when I open the door to place food in the microwave the microwave turns on while the door is still open
I have contacted Samsung about this issue and my safety concern but they only offered me to purchase an extended warrant to address the issue.
justification: The microwave turns on with the door open, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I work for a retirement community that purchased over 100 Frigidaire over the range microwaves  for a several year time period. One of these microwaves recently had a fan motor short out WHILE NOT IN USE and start a fire.  The resident was in sleeping at the time of the fire.  Staff responded to the fire alarm and found flames had already started coming out of the vents in the front of the microwave, so a small aerosol extinguisher was used.  The flames came back as the resident was being evacuated, so a larger 5lbs. dry chemical extinguisher was used to extinguish the flame. Smoke had filled the top 2'-3' of the room.  
As soon as possible the microwave was removed from the room and torn down.  We found the fan motor had shorted out and started the fire (we presume).  The microwave is two years old, so out of its one year warranty period.  When a call was placed to Frigidaire they didn't seem surprised to hear about the fire, but instead offered a parts discount for any parts needed to repair our microwave. Since the microwave is now covered in dry chemical, we declined.
justification: The incident involved a fire that required evacuation and use of fire extinguishers, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My daughter found a piece of metal, measuring about 1/4" in a cake I baked. I had ground almonds in my coffee/nut grinder and found that a piece of the metal blade had broken off into the nuts and were baked in the cake. The product is a Salton Coffee Grinder Model #GC-6. Fortunately she discovered the metal in her mouth and didn't swallow it. I am writing to report this problem so this problem doesn't happen to another person.

I can provide a photo of the broken blade if you provide an email address.
justification: The daughter found the metal piece in her mouth but did not swallow it, indicating no injury occurred.

incident_description:
We received a new Whirlpool range in June/July in 2014 as part of a kitchen rehab in working with a Kitchen and Bath firm.  In October of 2014 the oven unexpectedly got extremely hot (could not touch any part of the oven), and completely burnt a pizza to 100% black, while it was in the oven less than 10 minutes.  The oven stopped working.  Black smoke billowed out of the oven, all smoke alarms went off, and our eyes were burning from what seemed like a chemical and awful smell.  Contacted Whirlpool who seemed very unconcerned that this situation was a potential fire hazard, and contacted their contracting company that handles their repairs.  No use of oven for over 2 weeks while we waited.  Repair service came, couldn't fix it, ordered a new part.  They replaced the part, and the oven seemed to work okay.

Now in March of 2015, just 5 months later it did the exact same thing again.  Cooking a pizza, and within 10 minutes it was burnt 100% black, horrible black smoke billowing out of the over, smoke alarms going off, oven so hot you couldn't touch any part of it, and the oven shut down with a digital message.  Contacted Whirlpool again.  Again, no concern of the potential of a fire hazard.  You would have thought I called because a knob broke.  They contacted their repair service again, they came out, and again could not fix it, and had to order a part.  We are now waiting for the part to come in (and and again no use of an oven for who knows how long, and Whirlpool never said they are sorry for the inconvenienced or any type of atonement.  

I am reporting this, because I am shocked this oven has done this twice, and am very concerned this range will continue to be a safety hazard and could potentially catch on fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing extreme heat and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was making graham cracker crumbs in the cuisinart when it started making a weird noise.  I stopped the machine to discover that the metal cutting blade had sheared where it was riveted to the plastic cylinder.  Two chunks of the blade in had shattered in the crumbs- a large section and a small very sharp triangle of blade.  Yikes!
justification: The incident involved a broken blade in a food processor, which could have caused injury but did not in this case.

incident_description:
Jug found at this link:
http://www.pasabahce.com/urunler/kataloglar/essentials/kosem/43414.aspx

Jug was at room temperature. Tea bags were placed inside and hot water(boiling several minutes ago) was poured inside over teabags. When jug was half full, it began to shatter and spilled the scalding water over the counter onto my upper front thighs. Caused serious burns, including blistering within 5 minutes of contact, despite ice and burn-gel being applied.

incident_description: Frigidaire Smoothtop range model FEFL79GCA serial #vf72419995. The left front burner periodically does not turn off or will heat much hotter than the dial is set. These are the same symptoms for which other models of this stove were recalled and there are multiple reports of the same issue online with other users.

After about 15 seconds a popping sound like popcorn in a microwave started and blue arcing could be seen through out the unit. the main 200 amp breaker tripped after what seemed an eternity

incident_description: Kenmore Dishwasher Model 665.17364301 - I started the dishwasher and during the wash cycle the door began to smoke and smell of an electrical fire.  I tried to stop the dishwasher and was unable to, I opened the door and it continued to run, water spraying out the door. I considered calling the fire department at that point, but when I closed the door again the dishwasher shut off, smoke slowly stopped coming out of the vent on the door.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she started the cycle on the dishwasher. The consumer stated that there was burning smell and black smoke coming from the dishwasher after 20-25 minutes of turning it on. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in the middle of the big wash cycle.

The consumer stated that she cut off the circuit to the dishwasher.

incident_description: A four slice toaster Model # RV949 purchased at Walmart was in our breakroom heating without either one of the bread plungers pushed down.  The heating elements should not have been heating without the plungers being pushed.  The toaster became very hot and we could smell the scent of something burning. incident_description: My  wife was cooking with our 1 yr old Whirlpool induction range when she heard 2 loud "pops" and all the power to the range went out.  According to the appliance repairman the induction module board shorted out and began to burn.  Fortunately the house circuit breaker tripped and averted a potential electrical fire.   This product contains defective electronics which are a fire hazard.
