incident_description: Our 36-inch Wolf oven is exhibiting frequent delayed ignition at turn-on. I'm concerned that this will cause an explosion and/or injury. The unit model # is AS36KI-7, and serial number is 11010571. I've called Wolf but they say this is not covered by any recall. The same model oven is under recall for serial numbers up through 11006106, so I'm wondering if the list of covered serial numbers needs to be expanded.
justification: The oven exhibits delayed ignition, posing a potential risk of explosion or injury, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: I was standing at the kitchen counter making dinner preparations, when the lid on my Original Crock Pot Slow Cooker completely shattered.  I had not touched it or moved it, it simply shattered out of nowhere, leaving shards of glass in my dinner, as well as on the counter and on the floor.
justification: The incident involved a shattered lid causing glass shards in food and surrounding areas, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The heating element at the bottom of the dishwasher got so hot it melted the tub allowing water to leak onto the floor and wires below.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted tub and water leak) but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description: The control panel on my Kenmore range shorted out and started a fire. Burnt the wall behind the range. After several phone calls to Sears, where it was purchased, they refuse to do anything about it. I contacted Kenmore directly through their web site and they have not replied after nearly a week. Model 790-92302012. It is 3 1/2 years old.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Kenmore electric range model 790.9611340A. Left front burner will not turn off. had the trip breaker in order for burner to turn off.
justification: The burner not turning off is a malfunction but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
Purchased possibley late 2011 
GE Glasstop Electric Range noticed around February 17th, 2015 that the right front burner wouldn't turn off but once the caller finally got it to go off she has left it off.

Tuesday February 24th, 2015 the caller was cooking on the left back burner, turned it off then left the kitchen but when she returned fifteen or twenty minutes later she saw that the left back burner had not turned off when she turned the knob to off and the element was bright red.

There were no injuries

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but she does intend to contact them.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but there were no injuries, indicating an incident without harm. The issue occurred multiple times, suggesting a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the burners on the cooktop turn on while the cooktop is in the locked position.

On 2/6/15, the consumer stated that one of the burners (center, front burner) turned on by itself while the cooktop was in the locked position.

On 2/21/15, the consumer stated that three of the burners (three front burners) turned on by themselves at the same time while the cooktop was in the locked position.

During both times, the consumer was in the kitchen and caught the issue right away. The consumer stated that during both of the incidents, she had to cut the circuit breaker to the range to turn off the burners.

The consumer stated that she has not used her cooktop since the second incident.

The consumer contacted the manf on 2/6/15 and she was informed that the unit was out of warranty. They provided her contact information for two technicians in her area that can fix the range. They informed her that it was her responsibility to get the range repaired.

There are no recalls on her range.
justification: The burners turning on by themselves poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred as the consumer caught the issue immediately.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she went to pick up the pot from the counter to clean. The consumer slit her right hand finger on the end of the handle.

The consumer stated that the cut is about 1/2 inch.

The consumer stated that that the handle has an open end with raw piece of metal. The consumer stated that all of the pots/pans in the set have the same handle design and hazard.

The consumer will contact the manf.

The consumer was unable to find any product information on the pots/pans. The consumer does not have the packaging.
justification: The consumer sustained a 1/2 inch cut from a raw piece of metal on the pot handle, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This caller is contacting the hotline on behalf of his parents regarding their Frigidaire/Electrolux microwave purchased April 2010.

Around April/May 2011 the microwave kept running past the time set with fan and light going off but heat continuing.

After the first incident this same incident would repeat occasionally until February 2015 it began running, would run with no fan, no light but heat building until the caller unplugged it.

It remains unplugged, the caller has advised his parents not to use it at all.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller did contact the manufacturer March 11th, 2015 at 10:30AM, spoke with [REDACTED] but caller stated that the representative seemed unconcerned and then became rude.
justification: The microwave was running past the time set with fan and light going off but heat continuing, which is a incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The Keurig punctures huge holes in the top of the coffee and there is tons of coffee grounds in the coffee. When your finished brewing the coffee, not only do you have coffee grounds but the coffee is Luke warm. We have tried cleaning and it spewed water all over the place.
justification: The incident involves equipment malfunction causing mess and inconvenience, but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Brand new range emitted an acrid, plastic burning smell when heated to 450 degrees for one hour. Smoke poured from an otherwise clean, brand new oven to the point that it was choking. At the time the oven was first heated I placed a box fan in one window and opened a window across the room in anticipation of a 'first use' smell. Still, the odor was overwhelming, irritated my eyes, nose and caused a cough. The odor persists today, a day afterword with the fan still airing out the house!

I called the manufacturer who gave the excuse that it was outgassing from the acrylic binder used in the insulation of the unit and who assured me that it would dissipate with time. They recommended I run the self cleaning cycle to speed the process. All this did was increase the odor.

At this point GE has basically absolved itself of any responsibility for the product. It is such a widespread problem that the manual suggests moving birds out of the room! This product is basically unsafe for anyone with even minor respiratory problems.
justification: The incident caused eye and nose irritation and coughing, indicating minor injury, and the manufacturer acknowledges it as a widespread issue.

incident_description:
I just visited the Consumer Product Safety Commission concerning a problem with a GE Profile dishwasher.
The product recall number is 12-244 which list several models of the GE dishwashers with the prefix for the model number and serial numbers. Although our GE Profile model number or serial number is not listed we still had a problem. Our model number is PDWF800R10BB and serial number is DT718621B and was purchased during the time frame listed on the recall. Recently the dishwasher was running and we heard a loud pop. When I checked the circuit breaker was tripped and the plug, where the dish washer was connected was burned and melted. I had the plug replaced and reconnected the dishwasher and it seems to work with the exception of the heating element. We have two of the GE Profile dishwashers purchased approximately the same time period. After reading the report I now have concerns as to the safety of the units. The only reason I came across the recall was because I was checking out replacement heating elements.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing a circuit breaker to trip and a plug to melt, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased a GE Microwave that turns on by itself at random times.  If an item is left in the microwave, that item can be baked any number of times before we become aware. We have heard the microwave go off at various times of the night.  We have found items in the microwave scortched and smoking, setting off the smoke detector nearby.  We have unplugged the unit to stop this action. We plug in only to use, then unplug.
The item is GE Microwave Model:   JVM1540DP1WW
Serial Number: RT 956926B
Manufactured: August, 2010

We believe this to be a dangerous item, as it does not give warning that it will run.
justification: The microwave turns on by itself, causing items to scorch and smoke, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: While cooking food in oven opened door on oven to find lower element arcing. Turned off oven and element continued arcing. Electrical arcing continued until breaker was turned off.  Element seems to be switched on neutral side allowing a ground fault to continue after turning oven off.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing but was resolved without injury, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
(03/21/2015) The consumer was baking a pizza at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes. Thick smoke started coming from the oven control panel followed by visible flames and sparks. The consumer disconnected the unit at the circuit breaker. The fire went out on its own. The consumer pulled the stove out from the wall and removed the back cover panels to make sure there were no more flames. The connection where the external power cord meets the internal wiring was melted


(03/21/2015)The consumer contacted GE via email. He is waiting for a response.

The consumer is aware of a recall-Rel #09-189-for the GE Profile Duel Fuel range, but his model is not included. The consumer thinks that the model numbers should be broadened.
justification: The incident involved visible flames and sparks but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was contained by the consumer.

incident_description:
On 02/28/15 the consumer states his daughter set the unit to a wash cycle. The consumer states his daughter called him worried because there was smoke coming from the unit. The consumer's daughter had burned her finger when she tried opening the unit. The consumer states the unit stopped on its on. The consumer was not home but arrived shortly after he received the phone call from his daughter. When the consumer got home the unit was off but he still unplugged the unit from the wall.

On 03/02/15 the consumer's wife contacted the firm and left a voice mail informing them of the incident. On 03/09/15 (estimated) the consumer's wife received a call back from the firm and was told that the unit was not recalled. The firm arranged for a technician to examine the unit, free of charge. 

On 03/11/15 (estimated) the technician went to the consumers home and examined the unit. The technician told the consumer that the control panel had failed and caught on fire. The technician said the unit was not repairable. The technician told the consumer that the firm would contact them regarding this matter. The consumer spoke with [REDACTED] who offered a discount off of another KitchenAid dishwasher but the consumer does not feel safe using another KitchenAid appliance. The consumer was then offered a $150 credit towards another brand dishwasher.

The consumer spent $1250 (including tax and installation) on the dishwasher and is surprised that the unit failed after 6 years. The consumer believes the unit is a fire hazard and should be recalled. 

There are no prior incidents. The unit is used at least once a day.
justification: The consumer's daughter suffered a burn injury from the incident, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as there are no prior incidents mentioned and the unit was used daily for 6 years without issues.

incident_description:
January -2015:  The consumer baked a pan of cookies in the oven for approximately 20 minutes, on 350 degrees.  The consumer turned the oven off, but it remained on and the temperature continued increase.  The consumer had to trip the breaker in order to turn the oven off.

The consumer read the owner's manual and it recommended to unplug the oven/range from the outlet and indicated that this worked as a reset feature for the unit.  The consumer tripped the breaker multiple times in an attempt to reset the unit.  However, the unit has not reset itself with this last incident.

The consumer has experienced this problem 2 times prior to this current incident.  One incident occurred earlier this year and the other incident occurred approximately a year earlier.

The consumerÃÂs product appears to present a problem similar to the ones in Recall CAP# 09-333.

January-2015, the consumer called the manufacturer and asked for a replacement oven control circuit.  The consumer had done some research on-line and he thought that by replacing that part, the problem would be solved.  However, the manufacturer was going to charge the consumer $220 for the part, so the consumer declined to pay that amount.

The consumer had an aluminum pan in the bottom of the oven, to catch any food or drippings that may have fallen to the bottom.  The pan was charred in spots and several holes were also burned through the bottom of the pan.  This happened with the incident in January 2015.

(3/7/2015)  The consumer cooked a turkey in the oven and turned the oven off and removed the turkey, so that they could carve it.  He placed the pan with the turkey bones and drippings back into the oven, while it was still in the off position.  However, approximately 10 ÃÂ 15 minutes later, he noticed smoke coming from the oven.  The consumer opened the oven door and found that the heating element had remained on and appeared to have increased in temperature.  The drippings in the pan that the turkey was in were caramelized and burned and the pan was scorched.  The consumer had to trip the breaker in order to stop the oven.  Once the oven cooled down, he turned the breaker back on and found that the oven automatically turned on as well.  The consumer tried this several times, but each time, the oven turned on as soon as he turned the breaker on.

A code of F1 showed up on the control panel where the time is normally displayed.

The breaker is currently tripped for the oven and the consumer is afraid that if he turns the breaker on and leaves his home, that the oven might turn on and possibly catch fire.
justification: The oven malfunctioned multiple times, causing overheating and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While dishwasher was running in a normal cycle, smoke (not steam) started coming out of the right side, top of the door.  I opened the dishwasher and it kept running and spraying water.  I closed the dishwasher and pushed the cancel button, but it kept running and smoking and a burning smell was coming out.  I turned off the breaker to the dishwasher and it stopped smoking.  The dishwasher is a Kenmore Elite, model 665.16262400, serial number FR4502221 with a stainless steel tub.  If I hadn't been home or if I had been sleeping, I hate to think what could have happened.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This toaster only has an 8-inch cord. Any way you use it is a danger. Instructions state this is for safety. Directions then state that if a longer cord is needed use an extension cord. The first time I used this toaster I had to turn my dish rack upside down sit the toaster on it which still strained the cord and then moved the top of the toaster only 7 inches from the bottom of my cabinets.
Adding an extension cord will increase fire risk and chance of a child pulling this off the counter. A cord at least 18 inches long would be better.

Toaster is Hamilton Beach
model 226142
Type 95
Wal Mart number 40094 22614
purchased 3-20-15
justification: The toaster's short cord and need for an extension cord increase fire risk and potential for accidents, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
On January 9, 2015, I bought a Samsung Electric Range, Model # NE58F9710WS, Serial # J1927DCFA00500T from Best Buy, Norwalk, CT.  

Unfortunately, this product appears to be very dangerous.    I would give this range an good/excellent rating if I wasn't having such a problem with the stovetop controls. Almost every time I am cooking or using the microwave which is installed above the stove, I accidentally turn on a burner by leaning into one of the knobs on the front of the range. On many occasions, I have turned around to smell or feel the heat of the burner, which I unknowingly turned on. I am 5' 5" tall and when using the microwave above the stove, the same thing happens, I've accidentally pressed into a control know and a stovetop burner is accidentally turned on. Also, when wiping the front panel or cleaning the stove, it is easy to turn on the warming drawer at the bottom of the stove. Again, very dangerous. I have almost caused a fire on 2 occasions with this range.
 
I look forward to your reply and a resolution to my problem.  I have also emailed Samsung about this problem.  Please contact me at the above email address or my cell phone [REDACTED].

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with accidental burner activation, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Recently a piece of Pyrex bakeware completely shattered in my oven when my husband was taking it out after cooking some chicken.  This was very scary.  My husband received minor cuts, and our seven year old daughter was standing close by at the time.  We were unaware that this could happen while simply removing a dish from the oven.  I knew to be careful to prevent thermal shock such as putting a hot dish on a cold countertop.
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts (injury), and while the occurrence is not common, it is possible with certain bakeware under specific conditions.

incident_description:
(04/7/2014) The consumer stated that she noticed that the ice was coming out of the dispenser after she released the lever. The consumer gets small puddles of water in front of the unit because ice cubes fall to the floor.

(10/2014)The consumer stated that she got up in the middle of the night to get water. She went to get water from the dispenser. She almost fell but caught herself.

(12/2014) The consumer's niece was in the kitchen standing near the refrigerator. She turned to come back out the kitchen and slipped and fell on her right knee. There was water from the melted ice cubes on the floor.
No medical attention was required because she was not hurt.
The consumer stated that she got the run-around from the place of purchase.

There is definitely a design flaw which Whirlpool wants to repair instead of a new replacement.  Since contacting you, the problem has worsened, as ice falls out more frequently now.  Please see following reports from others experiencing the identical problem.  The consumer paid for a new appliance.  That's what she wants or her money back.  Also, the consumer has fallen again!!!  This is a serious accident waiting to happen.
justification: The incident involves slips and falls due to ice dispenser issues, but no injuries requiring medical attention have been reported.

incident_description:
Cuisinart Food Processor blade has a manufacturer defect.
While chopping some salmon the stainless steel blade broke and a small piece of the blade ended inside my food.  This is the second blade that broke, same place, next to the screws under it.  Also sign of crack next to another screw.
This blade is dangerous since it keeps breaking, and Cuisinart will not replace it, or recall this product.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade contaminating food, but no injury was reported. The defect is recurring, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught fire wile in use in my home
justification: Dishwasher caught fire, but no injury was reported

incident_description:
A recall on kenmore refrigerator model 795.77312600, serial 705MRWV09753 which Sears never notified us of. The light in the refrigerator compartment did not shut off and this caused it to melted the plastic cover and holder. Sears replaced it with the same part (not a fix to the part) free of charge in 2013. This also happen to a relative with the same refrigerator.
Last week the same part started to burn again but we caught it before it caused any damage. We contacted Sears and were told that the part only had a 90 day warranty and that it is our responsibility to pay for the service call and part.  This part could cause further damage if not caught immediately. If a part is defective shouldn't they have to fix the issue before they replace it? 
If we purchase an after market part instead of a Kenmore part will this cause more problems?
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it could have caused damage to the refrigerator if not caught immediately.

incident_description:
I had a glass lid explode in my microwave.  I was steaming cut vegetables  with a couple tablespoons of water.  Room temperature veggies, water from the faucet and placed in the microwave.  It had been on high for about 2 minutes when I heard an extremely loud bang.

 

Attached are pictures of what the inside of the microwave looked like.
 

This glassware is almost brand new.  Bought after Thanksgiving (could've been after Christmas) at Target as a three pack.  Has been used in the oven not more than 3 times total (over the three dishes), always at less than 400 F.  Used in the microwave at most a couple times a week (again over the three dishes).  They were always washed in the dishwasher.

 

The print on the bottom:

 

Anchor

Ovenware

CASSEROLE

573 in DIA 20 oz.

145 mm DIA 50 mL

OVEN & MICROWAVE SAFE

USA 21 1036

NO STOVETOP OR BROILER USE
justification: The incident involved a glass lid exploding in the microwave, causing no injury but potential for damage, and the product was used as intended.

incident_description:
Caller purchased set of Green Pans a few years ago. The 8" pan was replaced with a [REDACTED] collection pan one or two years ago.

He was heating the smaller 8" pan on the front right burner, he forgot it was on the burner then after about ten minutes he saw something fly across the room.

Once he inspected what went flying across the room he realized that it was one of the 1/2" in diameter covers that were over the screws.

He went into the direction it came from he saw that the pan he had placed on the burner was extremely hot so he used a towel and removed it from range.

There are no injuries to report

The manufacturer was contacted 02/24/2015 and the call left a message but hasn't received a return call
justification: No injuries occurred, but an incident involving a pan part flying off due to overheating was reported.

incident_description:
Roasting a chicken in a 7x11 Pyrex dish -- have had and used for several years. There were no obvious chips, cracks, or scratches to the dish.
Glassware dish was at room temperature. There was some liquid in the bottom of the glassware.  Conventional oven was fully pre-heated to 400 degrees when dish (with chicken) was placed in. I did not re-open the oven door or alter the temperature once it began to roast.
Twenty-six (26) minutes into cooking, there was a loud noise from the oven.  When I opened the oven door, I discovered the dish had exploded into a gazillion shards. All of the juice had naturally fallen on the heating element so much smoke billowed out of the oven. Portions of the glass adhered to the underside of the chicken which had to be peeled off. Pieces varied in size -- some chunks, others longer (~2 inches) thin slivers, and many, many, many miniscule pieces on oven floor and adhered (thanks to chicken juice) to oven door and top. 
Despite being careful, received cuts on my fingers from the sharp-edged slivers.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts on the fingers from sharp glass shards, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the dish was in good condition and properly used, making such explosions rare.

incident_description:
I bought a GE Microwave on November 1st, 2014 from Home Depot. The microwave was installed 2 weeks later. It wasn't used at all until December 25th, 2014. On March 15th, 2015 I received a call from a tenant telling me the microwave caught fire while making oatmeal. I immediately called GE and made an appointment for the repairman to come and look at it. On March 17th, 2015 the GE repairman came out and stated the microwave was repairable and that he would retrieve the part from his truck. When he came back, the microwave was plugged in and turned on. Within 6 seconds the microwave caught fire a 2nd time. The repairman called the GE engineer and provided me with a case manager number. He stated to me, my father and a tenant (who is a residential insurance agent) that the engineer agreed that the microwave is to be replaced.  I stated I would not sign anything as this case should not be closed as the productive is defective. If he relayed that information of the second fire, while he was on my property, there would be no need for this complaint as the microwave would have been removed. That is not this case, so he then left. 

I called the case manager and was told that the technician's notes were that the microwave is perfectly repairable. The technician lied. That microwave is a fire hazard.

On March 18th, 2015 I filed a complaint against GE Appliances with the Better Business Bureau. I received a call from [REDACTED] (GE - Georgia Representative [REDACTED] phone- contacted by the better business bureau to handle my complaint) and he repeated the technician's notes that the microwave is repairable even though it caught fire and that operator error exists. I told him that the technician was unprofessional, laughed at the idea that we think this is a fire hazard and that is incompetent. [REDACTED] and the technician do not understand that 2 fires (not an arc, not a spark,) but a flame with smoke is unsafe. I demand that this microwave be recalled and that I should be entitled to a refund.
justification: The microwave caught fire twice, posing a clear fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Fridgidare ElectricRange ES200/300 bought 2002.
Tonight my wife was cooking and could not turn off the oven.
Neither could I.
We could also not get the door open.
Finally I turned off the circuit breaker.
We still could not get the door open.

We called Fridgiaire. I told them their oven had a life threatening defect.
My wife doesn't know how to turn off the circuit breakers.
Its a good thing I was home as I was afraid the house would burn down.
Their customer service rep said "Its not a defect because she could not find
a product recall on it". I told her the web was full of problems people had
shutting off their ovens. She offered to help me find a service repairman in
my area that I could pay to fix the oven. She didn't seem to care that I was more
worried about the house burning down than fixing the oven.

Since, I've learned this is a common problem with Fridgidaire electric ovens.
Google: "fridgidaire oven won't turn off" and you'll see 5 to 10 hits on the first page
about Fridgidaire ovens not turning off.

This company should not be in business.
Your poorly designed web page seemed not to allow me to "register".
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I own a GE Microwave oven that is in my vacation home.  The model number is JVM1540DN1WW.  The Serial number is FS 901911 B.  The microwave starts a cooking mode for 1 minute by itself.  It just spontaneously starts cooking.  Prior to this incident, we would enter our home and find it beeping incessantly.
justification: The microwave starts a cooking mode for 1 minute by itself, which is a hazard but does not cause injury.

incident_description: I had just finished cooking in my Kenmore Elite oven (model number 790.7755) and about 3 seconds after I closed the oven door, there was a popping sound and the exterior pane of glass shattered. Could have been very hazardous if my three-year-old son had been close.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured, though there was potential for harm.

incident_description: While standing in front of my Sear Kenmore Range Model 790.9744 9745 the front glass door panel exploded all over me and onto the floor into thousands of tiny glass cluster pieces. The oven was not in use, not turned on, not being touched and had no visible signs of stress or damage prior to explosion.
justification: The glass door exploded, posing a risk of injury from flying glass shards, though no injury was reported.

incident_description: The toaster oven door shattered, well exploded really. There was nothing in it and it was not on or hot.
justification: The toaster oven door shattered but no one was injured and it was not in use, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
11/25/2013 (Approximate) - The consumer was done cooking dinner and noticed that after she had turned off the range, the back and left burner was still on approximately fifteen minutes later. Because the knob to the burner was in the OFF position, the consumer believed that the knob was not properly set so she proceeded to remove the knob with some pliers. The consumer confirmed that the setting was correct. After the consumer removed the knob, there was smoke coming out from where it was located. The smoke ceased approximately three to four minutes later. The consumer put the knob back on.

When the consumer went to turn the burner back on the next day, the consumer indicates that the burner never heated. Because her unit was out of warranty, the consumer did not contact the retailer (whom is now out of business) nor manufacturer.

The consumer indicates that she now uses her range on a daily basis, though initally this was not the case. The consumer states that to date, her range has never been serviced by a Technician. She states that her other three burners are working properly but not the left and back burner.

The consumer has no injuries to report. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer plans on contacting the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner with no reported injuries, and the issue appears to be isolated to one burner with no recurrence mentioned.

incident_description:
On 02/21/15 the consumer noticed a burn odor in his home and realized it came from the range. The consumer looked in the oven and noticed the broiler was "On." The consumer tried to turn the broiler off by using the control knobs but the broiler failed to turn off. The consumer shut the circuit breaker off and the broiler turned off. The range was very hot. The consumer does not use the oven often and believes it was last used days before the incident. The stove top is used often and was last used on 02/21/15 about 4 hours before the incident occurred. 

There are no prior incidents. 

The consumer purchased another range on the Sears web site. The new range was delivered on 02/23/15 and the old range was hauled away. 

The consumer has not contacted the firm and does not plan to because he feels the firm would not provide any assistance.
justification: The incident was a fire hazard but no injury was reported, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his LG Electric Range is included in recall #13-031. 

The consumer had a 4 year warranty on the range. The consumer stated that he had the technician come out 4 different times within 3 years under warranty. The consumer contacted the warranty company before the warranty expired to tell them about the lock issue with his oven. They informed him to cut the circuit and restart the oven. The issue did not go away and so when he contacted them again they informed him that his unit was no longer under warranty.

The consumer stated that his oven would lock itself up . The consumer contacted the manf for the issue in 11/2014. The consumer was informed to purchase a new part that cost $100. The consumer purchased the part and replaced it. The consumer stated that the issue was not fixed.
The consumer was never informed about the recall on his range at that moment.

The consumer contacted LG again in 12/2014. They informed him that there is a recall on his range. They arranged to have a technician sent out. The consumer was sent the part for repair under recall. The consumer stated that this was the same part that purchased from LG a month before. The technician came and replaced the part on 12/26/14. The consumer stated that the issues was still not solved.

The consumer contacted LG in 01/2015. LG sent out another technician. The technician came and informed the consumer that the whole wiring harness needs to be replaced. The consumer was informed by LG that they no longer make that part.

The consumer was called by LG and they offered to buy the range back for $249. The consumer was informed that they will come and get the range and once the range reaches warehouse, they will send him a check. They informed him that the range is at the end of its life spell. 

The consumer purchased the range for $1799 + tax. The consumer stated that if the recall offers repair then it should be repaired under the recall, not bought back for such a low price. 

The consumer stated that he also had issues with the burners heating to different levels than selected. The consumer stated that his burners would heat to lower temperature than selected.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance with no reported injuries, and the issue is likely to occur given the repeated problems and recall.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting his smooth-top range with front right burner that just turns on and begins escalating temperature to a glowing red.

Callers moved into home 2009 range was in kitchen but presented no problems at that time.

Around 2012 the callers noticed that the right front burner was becoming difficult to turn off.

In January 2015 the caller and his wife noticed that the same burner was turning on by itself and on March 4th, 2015 the caller's wife was cooking, laid a pan on the right front burner with dough in it because the burner was not in use.

She noticed that the dough was rising when it should not have been rising then noticed that the burner had lit by itself again.

The caller and his wife finally turned the burner off but it took a while to turn it off by spinning the knob until it turned off.

This incident is being reported asking that the public be alerted and the product inspected then recalled due to the potential for fire and destruction of human and property damage.
