Recently on one slow cooker, the handle came off and the lid fell to the floor and shattered (3/6/2015).  On the other slow cooker, the handle came off and the lid fell into the food splashing a little bit of the liquid on my wrist (3/14/2015).  No serious injuries occurred as a result of either incident.  I started searching online for replacement lids and came across a recall of this model for the same issues I encountered.  I seem to have missed the opportunity to receive a replacement but wanted to report the incidents I had.
justification: The incidents involved handle detachment leading to lid falls, with minor splashing but no serious injuries, aligning with severity level 2.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE monogram dishwasher model #ZBD0710N20SS serial number DR741121B on 18 February 2008 from The Home Depot Company.  This Morning (15 March 2015) I awoke to to an extremely hot kitchen dishwasher with a melted interior rack, and an appliance drying/heating cycle that would not turn off.   I have checked the GE recall list, but our specific Model # is not currently on the recall list.

I am sure, given the amount of damage (melting) to the interior of the dishwasher and the untouchable temperature of the glassware and plates inside, that a fire would have started if I had not come downstairs early in the morning.

Clearly a short circuit or other electrical failure has occurred and GE currently will not acknowledge it for this specific model, though they have recalled similar models for similar failure.
justification: The incident caused damage to the dishwasher and could have caused a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
West Bend 82418R Air Crazy Hot Air Popcorn Popper:  I bought this appliance a little over a week ago.  On the third use, it started to screech while my wife was using it and she turned it off.  I turned it on again to see if I could detect the problem, and it started to screech and smoke.  I turned it off and unplugged it.  A few minutes later, it burst into flames.   

I sent emails describing my experience with this product to both Target (where I bought this product) and West Bend (the manufacturer).  Afterwards, I found a number of related complaints in reviews posted on Amazon.com, prompting this email to Consumer Protection.  The experience reported below, by [REDACTED], is similar to my experience, although my popper actually burst into flames.  Had I not been close by, the results could have been disastrous.   

Motor burnt out during third use, March 5, 2015 
By 
[REDACTED]" (Chicago, IL, USA) - See all my reviews
This review is from: West Bend 82418R Air Crazy Hot Air Popcorn Popper (Kitchen) 
We bought this at Target as an impulse buy. It seemed all right at first, lightweight, easy to use, fast. During the third use, it made a horrible screeching noise. I turned it off and on a few times, then I noticed smoke coming out of the top and bottom; the motor was burning out. It's going back to Target.
justification: The incident caused a fire, but no injury was reported, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: I have a Black & Decker Convection Toaster Oven, Model #TO1675B.  I made toast this morning and when I left the room, my smoke detector went off.  Apparently, something is wrong with the electronics in this oven, because there was no way to turn it off.  The heat stayed on and the only way to turn it off was to unplug it.  I never had this problem before.  If I would have left my home, it would have probably caused a house fire, because it was extremely hot.  Hot enough to set off my smoke alarm.  This oven is only one year old.  I believe that Black and Decker needs to recall this item.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toaster oven that could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The product being used was a class Pyrex 10 cup bowl. I had baked mac and cheese in the bowl 2 days prior. After the dish was completely cooled it was stored in the fridge. Once the bowl was emptied it was filled with water to soak. I emptied the water out of the bowl and holding the glass bowl with one hand, I began to clean it with a scotchbrite pad with the other hand. I believe the bowl exploded in my hand at this time. I suffered a significant wound to the palm of my hand, which required 9 stitches and appear to be leaving a nasty scar. I also had several scratches from flying class pieces on my forearms. The doctor that saw me in the urgent care center even questioned how the scratches got on my arms from the bowl in my hand. I am in shock that a bowl can just explode this way.
justification: The incident caused a significant wound requiring stitches, making it a level 3 severity.

incident_description: My "Power Pressure cooker " exploded with fire hot chicken soup in it, covering my entire kitchen, hitting my in the head with a piece of chicken, and burning my arm. My 7 year old child and his friend had just came through the the kitchen not seconds before this happened. The exposition did damage to my walls and cabinets, and had anyone been standing closer to it, it could have killed or seriously injured my family and my son friend.
justification: The incident caused burns and physical injury, and had the potential for death if others were closer, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood is considered possible given the described scenario.

incident_description:
Samsung Microwave (Model SMH1816S) turns on automatically without starting it.  Inside turn table glass gets extremely hot and not safe to touch.  Removed the power/kept microwave door open to avoid automatic turn on which may cause fire hazard. 

Contacted Samsung support and waiting.
justification: The microwave turns on automatically, which can cause fire hazard, making it unsafe to touch. This is a serious incident that can cause injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her range was installed in the home she purchased in Dec 2002.

The consumer stated that she turned on the oven and noticed sparks right away. The consumer stated that there were flames inside of the oven. The consumer stated that the flames were about 1-2 inches high on the bottom element.

The consumer stated that she turned off the oven from the control panel. The consumer stated that it took about 5 minutes after turning it off for the flames to completely go out.

The consumer contacted the manf and they asked her to not use the range. They sent out a technician on 2/23/15. They informed her that they can replace the element. The consumer was informed that they will pay for the part but she would have to pay for the labor ($161.99).
The consumer was informed by the GE representative that this is a common issue.

The unit is not included in any recalls.

The consumer is afraid to use the oven or cook-top even after repair.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks in the oven, but no injury occurred. The manufacturer indicated this is a common issue, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
heating element overheated
We smelled something burning and tracked it to the dishwasher
Opened the dishwasher and saw the element overheating and melting the plastic water dispenser and the bottom of the Appliance
Could not turn it off
Ran to garage and flipped the breaker
Went on manufacturer site and saw they had recalls for fire hazard on GE Profile dishwasher from the same years
Checked our unit and it is not on recall list

We have pictures of the damage but we are unable to use the upload feature of this web site.  Please contact us for copies of the pictures
justification: The incident involved an overheating heating element causing damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
(02/09/2015) The consumer stated that as his wife as cleaning the top of the stove, all of the burners came on by themselves. 

The consumer stated that this happened before but it was only on the two right burners. The consumer stated that a service technician came out that time and replaced a computer card.
justification: The incident involved burners turning on unexpectedly, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported. The issue has occurred before, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
Caller stated he started experiencing problems with his gas range.  The iron grates on the burners started to become unstable (broken) about 3-4 years after purchase.  During this time he would move them around to prevent an accident.

(2009) The retailer was contacted and he was informed of the cost of replacing the burner which was very costly.

Caller feels that these grates for the burners are a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves unstable iron grates, which could lead to accidents, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On 02/23/15 the consumer used the unit to mix the ingredients he had to make muffins. The consumer put the muffin mix on a muffin tray and left it in the oven for about 20 minutes. The consumer removed the muffins from the tray and noticed a silver item on the bottom of one of the muffins. The consumer took the screw out of the muffin but did not know where the screw came from until he was cleaning the unit and noticed a screw missing on the bottom of the mixer blade. 

On 02/24/15 the consumer contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The firm offered to sell the consumer a replacement blade for about $10 plus shipping. The consumer did not want to purchase the replacement blades. 

The consumer uses the unit frequently and has not had any prior incidents.

The consumer has some safety concerns with the unit.
justification: The incident involved a screw in the muffin mix but no injury occurred. The consumer uses the unit frequently without prior incidents, indicating the likelihood is unlikely.

incident_description: My coffee maker was plugged in but not on; I had put water and coffee in it for the morning, but had not programmed it. I heard a funny noise from the kitchen around 10pm and when I investigated, there was pungent-smelling smoke (it smelled like burned plastic) coming out of the bottom of the unit. I unplugged it and dumped out the grounds and water. The unit continued to smell so I took it outside.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. Such electrical malfunctions are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description: On March 10, 2015 my Sears Kenmore Elite Dishwasher caught on Fire. I called 911, the Fire Department came out and said it was the electrical in the panel that caught fire. The dishwasher is fried to beyond repair, it also damaged my countertop and my kitchen cabinet.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Jenn-air JDB-5 (JDB1100AWB) heating element did not shut off after a wash cycle causing plastic items inside the dishwasher to melt.   

FIRE HAZARD!  Had I not been home I may not have noticed this was happening, and my house may have burned down.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard that could have led to death if unnoticed, indicating high severity, but the likelihood is lower as it requires specific conditions.

incident_description: Bosch dishwasher model SHU53A, Serial # FD8403 00811 had an electrical malfunction at the control panel circuit board causing a small fire inside the unit and a smoke condition in the dwelling.
justification: The incident caused a small fire and smoke, but no injury or death, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description:
This consumer purchased his induction cook top December 2013 and had no problems with this unit while he was using lower temperatures, however within the first five minutes that he used the maximum heat option on January 22nd, 2015 the cord became so hot that he could not touch it.

There are no injuries to report 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer/distributor then discovered that the actual manufacturer is in China.  He has been unable to discover the name of the manufacturer in China.

Due to the cord becoming so hot the caller is reporting this product as a fire hazard.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it is a fire hazard, which is a serious incident.

incident_description:
I have an Aroma brand rice cooker model ARC-757SG.
It is about 2-1/2 months old.

On Fri 3/6/15 when using it at usual, instead of shutting off when the rice is done as it is supposed to do, the heat stayed on at full power and the unit starting burning the rice and smoking very profusely. 

If I had not unplugged it, it would have continued heating until the rice caught fire, at which point it could have burned the house down. It would be a huge understatement to say that this is completely unacceptable.

Obviously this unit does NOT have an over-temp or over-heat sensor which would shut if off when the primary heat sensitive shut-off fails, as it clearly did in this case.

I still have this unit with the burned rice in it. I would be very pleased to send it to you for investigation.

This unit should not be allowed to be sold. All such products should have fail-safe circuits that prevent them from overheating to the degree that they could start fires.

This unit's label indicates that it is UL listed. How could such an poorly designed unsafe product have a UL listing? This should not be possible.

I am a very experienced electrical engineer with some experience in electrical safety design requirements.

PLEASE take strong corrective action immediately. This product is very dangerous and could easily kill people and cause large amounts of property damage.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: My Kenmore electric range comes on on it's own and gets extremely hot. If I was not home it would have started a fire. F1 shows on the display and it starts to beep. I unplugged the stove and plugged it back in days later. and after a little bit it starting heating up and F1 was on the display and it started heating up very HOT\ very fast. Kenmore model number 790.95201100  /Serial number VF13304360
justification: The electric range turns on and overheats on its own, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern:

First, I want to say I am woefully disappointed in this product, a Pyrex 9x13" rectangular glass cookware I have owned for the past 5 years. I purchased it in 2010 when I moved into my first apartment in Maryland.

We have used this dish for many years, cooking baked macaroni and cheese with crab dishes amongst others, in various ranges of temperature, from 250 - 425 (Farenheit).

Tonight, I baked some fish, took it from the oven, and placed it onto my oven top (which was warm) and it shattered. SHATTERED. Gratefully, it did not hurt me or my husband. However, dinner was ruined. My house is at a warm 68 degrees and outside is freezing at 30 degrees (Farenheit). The kitchen was about 75 degrees, thanks to the oven.

My husband has experience in testing glass. He stated this cookware was not even tempered as evidenced by the large fragments of 9x2 and 4x4" glass sections. Tempered glass fractures into smaller particles.

Words cannot express my disappointment with this product. I resorted to Google and found COUNTLESS testimonies of similar situations. Dinners ruined. Glass particles in hands and arms. Why haven't these products been recalled or the formula changed? What does it take?

This is gross negligence on the manufacturer and failure by external regulations, hopefully, designated by the Government for consumer safety. 

In conclusion, I am throwing out all Pyrex dishes I owned, replacing them with either metal or ceramic, and ensuring my family and friends know our ordeal and encourage them to throw out their Pyrex implements into the garbage. 

I will never own another piece of Pyrex glassware, so long as these reports continue to exist: http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/magazine-archive/2011/january/home-garden/glass-cookware/glass-cookware/index.htm
justification: The incident involved the shattering of a glass cookware without causing injury, but with potential for harm and property damage.

incident_description:
Kitchen Aid double wall oven - lower oven door glass shattered / exploded.

Oven was preheating and the inner glass exploded, the door was forced open by the explosion spewing hot glass on the floor.

Nobody was in the kitchen at the time but had there been, someone could have been seriously injured.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
My GE Over the Range Microwave Oven (Model No HVM1750SP1SS) caught fire when my wife attempted to warm a cup of water for making tea. We smelled strange "electric"/rubber burning and saw smoke come out from inside. It turns out that the white round disc-like thing caught fire and melted, causing about a nickel-sized hole in the plastic ceiling of the microwave. I am sure, if I was not there and it was some other food requiring longer microwave time, I would have a burned-down house! 

It was very scary. Since the unit cannot be immediately removed--- it is a over-the-range type--- I was panicking as to what to do. I disconnected the power chord--- thankfully, it was accessible--- and put a large bowl of ice inside to cool the ambient temperature down. 
I have never experienced such microwave-fire from any manufacturer before. This is inexcusable. I called the GE Repair number and was routed to the GE Consumer Relations group. They opened a case and promised to send a technician to my home and "go from there". It remains to be seen what they ultimately do. But no one should be allowed to sell products that get bolted down (i.e. not easily removable) and can still cause fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and such events are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description:
(11/27/2014) The consumer stated that she turned on the oven which automatically sets for 350. The pre heat button came on but the oven never got hot. The consumer turned the oven off. About 20 minutes later she turned it back on and the code F10 flashed on the control panel. 

(12/01/2014) The consumer called Lowes and was advised to unplug the stove wait five minutes, then plug the stove back in, set the clock and turn on the oven. The consumer waited five minutes, set the clock. When she did this, the control panel burst into flames.

(12/01/2014) The consumer called Electrolux. The consumer advised the person that she spoke with of the incident. The consumer was advised that nothing could be done because the product was over a year old. The consumer was advised that Electrolux would pay for parts and labor. The consumer would have to pay for a service call. The consumer was also offered an extended warranty. 

The consumer was transferred to the Recall Department to see if her unit was involved. The unit was not included.
justification: The incident involved a control panel bursting into flames, which is a significant hazard, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I was just going to clean a Frigidaire refrigerator glass shelf and it literally exploded in my hands. No bumping, no dropping or scrapping. When I googled the issue it is quite common. This exploded all over me (lucky to not have any in the eyes) my skin is covered and it hit a 20' radius in my house. Buyer beware; it's alarming that they are aware of this issue and have chosen to sweep it under the rug.
justification: The incident resulted in glass shards covering the person's skin, indicating potential minor injuries, and the issue is described as common.

incident_description: While I was working is the kitchen, there was a sudden shattering of glass. It took me a moment to figure out what actually broke, but apparently it was my Anchor Hocking 9 x 13 glass pan. I had it sitting on the shelf and it hasn't been used in over a week.
justification: The glass pan shattered but there was no injury reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I have a kenmore elite refrigerator.  My daughter smelt something burning in the refrigerator. I looked in there and
Saw everything under the light bulbs melted. Also the food that was exposed was singed. My medicine that was supposed to be kept refrigerated and out of light was spoiled. As I was checking the food that was exposed to the lights, my hand touched the light bulb and I got burned pretty bad. It was apparent that the lights would not turn off in the fridge. This is a fire hazard and an obvious defect and needs to be fixed before it does start a fire.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and spoiled medicine, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the ongoing defect and fire hazard.

incident_description: Was using my 4 year old Kenmore oven model 790.92803010 and the outer glass on the door shattered throwing glass at my son and me. Very scary!! Doesn't seem right that the company won't stand behind the product and replace it for free or recall the product.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, throwing glass at the user and their son, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our Whirlpool Gold microwave oven Model GT4185SKS-2 worked well for 10 years without incidents or repairs; however one day after warming up a glass of milk (use completed and clock displayed) we closed the door and it began making a low, constant humming sound. We opened the door, the humming stopped and the interior light came on. Curious, we placed a glass of cold water in the center of the microwave and simply closed the door without touching the keypad. The humming sound immediately started, the interior was dark, no light on, and the turntable did not move. Within 60 seconds we could see our water boiling. We opened the door, the light turned on, the humming stopped. Our water was boiling and steam came pouring out the top of the unit. Then we smelled a bit of smoke, something was burning although we don't know what. We immediately flipped the fuse and began unscrewing its 27" trim kit to remove the microwave from our cabinetry. We believe had we not been home and awake to manage this issue, and the wherewithal to cut the circuit and remove the microwave, it would have burned our house down.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing overheating and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: When using a large pan of stock pot for any prolonged time the heat of the pot melts the cooktop knobs.
justification: The incident describes damage to equipment (cooktop knobs) but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I got up this morning and made a cup of coffee in my coffee machine.

I took the full, hot mug of coffee from the holder and walked toward the opposite counter in my kitchen so I could put the mug beside my sink to drink my coffee and do some dishes, but before I reached the other counter the mug became separated into 2 pieces.  The hot coffee poured down my right arm, stomach, and right thigh, burning me.

The mug was purchased from star bucks and is not to be used in the microwave, which I have not,  as it is a 2 piece mug that is metal and ceramic.  This mug is marked dishwasher safe, made in china and marked with a 2004 stamp on the bottom which is rubberized.

I am extremely concerned as I have a 1 year old son, and am horrified to think what may have happened if this occurred, while he was around me or walking beneath me at the time of this incident.


NOTE:  If the consumer thinks of any other relevant details, they may add them to the report upon receipt of it.
justification: The incident resulted in burns from hot coffee, indicating an injury, but no death or severe harm was reported.

incident_description:
On the evening of 3/6/15 I opened the oven door of our LG electric stove (Model LRE 30453SB/01).  Suddenly there was loud pop and all the glass from the door shattered, spreading in a wide area around the room and on my feet.  The stove was not in use, and hadn't been used for at least 2 days.

The stove was installed in April 2010.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injury was reported, only the spread of glass around the room and on the feet.

incident_description:
(02/13/2015) The consumer stated that he had the skillet set at 350 degrees. He was frying eggplant in vegetable oil for about 30 minutes. When he finish frying the egplant he noticed that the surface underneath the skillet was extremely hot. The skillet was on the counter and the heat from the skillet caused a crack in the counter top. 

The consumer stated that he has used the skillet before.

The consumer thinks that the product should be tested in the CPSC labs because it is unsafe.

(02/13/2015) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. The company offered to replace the product. He was asked to send in the electric cord.
justification: The consumer was frying eggplant in vegetable oil for about 30 minutes. The heat from the skillet caused a crack in the counter top. The consumer was not injured.

incident_description: My husband and I had just made a pot of coffee in our Krups thermal drip coffee maker, model KT720D. My husband decided to open the coffeemaker and add a little cinnamon. When he attempted to lightly stir this, the coffee pot exploded with a huge noise. Glass from the lining blew out all over the kitchen, luckily missing ourselves and our dogs. the bottom of the pot totally cracked. Hot coffee was pouring out from everywhere. This morning I am still finding small pieces of glass, the size of glitter, all over the kitchen. We were so lucky someone did not get hurt. This needs to be corrected or taken off the market. We still have the outer heating part of the coffee maker but not the carafe.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: This incident involves our Cuisinart toaster oven, model number TOB-40 120 VAC 80 Hz 1800 W. On Thursday, February 19, 2015,  while we were toasting bread, one of the bottom heating elements caught fire without any apparent cause. There was nothing touching the element when it ignited. I quickly shut off the toaster and unplugged it, and the flame slowly dissipated. The heating element is now deformed (bubbled). We have not used the toaster since. This is a major product safety hazard because, not only because of the spontaneous fire, but the speed at which it occurred. Had I not been standing right at the toaster, I would not have been able to put it out.  Please look into this product.
justification: The incident involved a fire, but no injury was reported, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: Frigidaire Electric Range Model #LGEF3045KFH serial# VF24351654. The range was purchased from Lowes on 11/20/2012. Within the first 7 months of use the automatic door locking mechanism wouldn't unlock after a self cleaning cycle. We call Frigidaire customer service department and were informed that this happens and all we need to do is turn off the breaker, wait 5 minutes, and then turn it back on. This worked and the door unlocked, but this needs to be done every time you use self clean function. 6 months later after turning off the oven, there was  very loud pop from behind the stove. A flame, smoke and sparks jumped up the back of the stove. Luckily I was standing directly in front of the stove when this happened. I pulled the unit away from the way and grabbed a fire extinguisher. I immediately called Frigidaire customer service again. I was told it was the circuit board shorting out and I could purchase a replacement part. On 9/20/2014 while pre-heating the oven, the front panel display an f10 error with loud beeping. The oven could not be turned off while the f10 error was flashing. none of the buttons were responding, so the unit was turned off at the breaker. Frigidaire customer service was contacted for the 3rd time. This time we were informed that it was thermostat and that it should re-set after a 5-10 waiting period before turning back on. I explained that the oven/stove had become so hot that the countertops and floor surrounding the stove were extremely hot to the touch and one of our teenagers been using the oven at the time, there was a strong possibility a fire would have occurred because they don't know about a breaker box. We were informed that we could buy a replacement part but the reset should work. Finally on 2/28/2015 the f10 error occurred again, this time filling our home with massive amounts of smoke. We need to evacuate the first floor of our home and place fans inside to remove the overwhelming amount of smoke that filled our house.  We will no longer use our stove because of the fire risk. Frigidaire said they can't do anything for us.
justification: The incident involved multiple dangerous occurrences including flames, smoke, and sparks, posing a significant fire risk, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I was using my GE Electric Range, Model JK5000SF1SS, which was installed Nov 2013.  Serial number:  RA603845Q
I was cooking with my oven at 350ÃÂ°F for 20 minutes, and changed to Low Broil.  Within 3 minutes, there was a bright orange flash and flames within the oven.  I immediately turned off the oven, but did not open it.  There was a lot of smoke coming from the oven.   After opening all windows and doors of my house and letting the oven cool, I opened the oven door.  There was white residue inside the oven.  Upon closer inspection, there were tiny pieces of metal within the oven.  The rear right coil was noticeably melted and I have pictures that show the coil had completely disintegrated in one spot.   It seems as if during the low broil setting, the metal had become dangerously hot and exploded, starting a fire inside the oven and showering metal.
Luckily, no one was hurt.  There was a lot of smoke and it made us a little light-headed, but there were no burn injuries, mostly because we did not open the oven until the fire had gone out and the oven had cooled.
justification: There was a fire inside the oven with smoke and metal pieces, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: While running our daily load of dishes, the dishwasher started smoking, setting off the smoke alarm and leaving a horrendous burning smell. Luckily we were home and stopped the load of dishes. My husband opened up the dishwasher body to discover the electronic panel had started melting.
justification: The dishwasher started smoking and the electronic panel melted, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: from 3-3-15 to 3-7-15 the GE Profile Dishwasher had mild odor of  hot rubber about it, though we did not identify what this was until 3-7-15. On 3-7-15 There was a strong odor of melting plastic and smoke came out of top of door. After turning off the machine via the electric switch to the dishwasher and opening the door, the inside door panel was hot to the touch, far warmer than any other part of the machine. The electronics display had been acting oddly for many months. On the short cycle, for example, the time had gone from 32 minutes to 28 minutes to 31 minutes without any adjustments. The long cycle increased in length by 30 minutes, again without any adjustments to the machine,  which was why we were using the short cycle. The dishwasher cleaned fine and had no trouble pumping out water.  We have never used the heated dry cycle on this machine, except once or twice by accident after the power was out and the machine re-set to default to heated dry.  The heated dry cycle was off on 3-7-15 when the dishwasher came close to catching fire. We did not have to use a fire extinguisher or call 911. It took several hours with our whole house fan on to clear the house of the burn-smell.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a strong odor of melting plastic, but no injury or need for emergency services, indicating a non-injury incident. The occurrence likelihood is possible given the described malfunctioning electronics and heating issues.

incident_description: The incident involves an Asko dishwasher Model # D5893 XXL FI US, Serial # 094101874967.  The unit was installed by an Authorized Asko Dealer.  On the evening of February 7, 2015 the unit was off and empty with the door slightly ajar.  We left home for the evening.  While away we were notified by our alarm company that the water alarm was triggered.  When we returned home we discovered the unit on with the control screen frozen, smoke in the room and large amounts of water on the kitchen floor.  The dishwasher had turned on by itself and started to burn.  The only way I could turn the unit of was to pull the power plug.  I contacted Asko to report the issue.  Unfortunately, it took multiple phone calls and almost two weeks to get to the right person who opened a claim.  A representative of Asko called me back to help me file an insurance claim.  This person was rude and suggested that the dishwasher burned because it was installed improperly and/or due to faulty wiring of my home.  I told the Asko representative that the dishwasher was installed by an authorized Asko installer and the wiring in my home which was built in 2008 was properly inspected by the local building department.  In the end, Asko replaced my unit at no charge and took the damaged dishwasher away.  Unfortunately, my home was damaged by water and working with the Asko liability carrier was disappointing so I am left with a damaged kitchen.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: Microwave comes on whenever the door is closed even when not being used.  The oven emits microwaves, but no fans or lights are on and timer is not set.  Has almost caused a fire when food was in microwave after timer went off, but microwave continued to cook.  You can boil water just by putting it in the microwave and closing the door.  The microwave only turns off with the door open.
justification: The microwave malfunction poses a fire hazard and can cause burns, but no injuries or deaths are mentioned.

incident_description:
Handle melts on glass bowl. Causes burns.

Anchor Hocking Clear Glass 2 qt. Batter Bowl Item# 81605L11

Purchased at the local Menards store on March 5, 2015.

The item is marked as microwave safe.

Placed a quart of water into bowl (which looks like a large measuring cup) 
and placed into microwave (residential 1050 watt) to heat the water.

Went to check progress after several minutes.  Side of bowl was barely warm, water was barely warm.  Reached for handle and it was extremely hot.  

Received burns across all fingers including some blistering.

Closer examination of bowl showed that the glass handle had melted and was misshapen.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and blistering, indicating an injury.

incident_description: GE profile dishwasher when done cycle and in drying mode caused the blade on bottom of dishwasher to catch on fire and and burn and melt racks dishes and leave a chemical smell that woke me up at 4 am. No other damage to kitchen area.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to the dishwasher and its contents, but no injuries or further property damage were reported.

incident_description: The door fell off the refrigerator suddenly, just as described in the recall information posted online. We have a baby and it could have killed him.
justification: The door fell off suddenly, posing a potential fatal risk to the baby, though no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Bosch dishwasher started having a burning smell while we were using it.  The smell was from the outside.  After reading several reports of issues in the electrical box I unplugged the unit and took off the electrical box cover.   Right when I touched the hot wire it just fell off.  This wire was completely burnt.  The inside where the wires connect to the metal posts was completely melted.  The neutral wire was also burnt and also fell off.

When I took off the metal posts, the inside of these was also burnt, where the wires continued underneath the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and burnt wires, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his dishwasher in 2003 and had no problems with it until January 14th, 2015.
The caller's dishwasher beeped that the cycle was over, however his house keeper opened the door to allow cooling and put dishes away.
When he opened the door flames came out from both sides and the bottom of the dishwasher.
He immediately grabbed water and threw it on the flames then called 911.
The fire responders checked to be sure all was out and safely extinguished.  Removed the dishwasher.
There is a scorched place inside the cabinet approximately the size of a dinner plate.

There are no injuries being reported.

The caller is reporting this incident with the thought of what could have happened had his house keepers left the house.  Home would probably had a major fire.

The consumer did contact the manufacturer a few day later because he was out of town at the time of the incident.
The manufacturer informed him that his unit was not recalled.
He is asking that his model and serial number be added to those recalled before someone is seriously injured.  There was a big recall in this time period.
justification: The incident involved flames and required fire responders, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the handle on the slow cooker broke off. The consumer stated that this happened to the right side handle (when facing the front of the cooker).

The consumer stated that she was taking the slow cooker out of the cabinet. When she lifted the cooker, she noticed that the handle had broken.

The consumer stated that the cooker was not hit or it did not fall.

The consumer contacted the manf. and they informed her that her slow cooker has not been recalled. They informed her that there were no other complaints about this year/model. They offered to sell another one.
justification: The consumer was not injured, but the handle of the cooker broke off, which is a safety hazard.

incident_description: Prior to leaving home for 4 hours my wife placed our chicken dinner in the oven and set it to bake at 250 degrees.  I confirmed the temperature setting before leaving.  The meal was cooking in a Le Creuset cast iron pot, which has been used in the same manner for several years.  Upon arriving home our daughter noticed heavy smoke in the house, an error code of F3 and flames from the oven, so she shut off the range circuit breaker and called 911.  When the firefighters arrived they removed the flaming pot of chicken and vegetables (which were burned to a charcoal-like consistency), and the range, which had heavy brown smoke/burn marks on the front panel and rear vents.  Our back splash had similar marks, and the bottom edge of the cabinets were scorched on both sides of the range.  We were merely moments away from a fully involved kitchen fire.
justification: The incident involved heavy smoke, flames, and significant damage to the kitchen, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: On 2-26-2015 my wife was drinking from her water bottle and noticed a large, sharp plastic object in the cup with her ice; she showed it to me. This is the third time our ice maker has spit out pieces of plastic. The first time it happened I cut my lip. The ice maker malfunctions breaking off sharp, jagged pieces of plastic into the ice bin. This will be the third incident reported to Samsung, and my third reported to the CPSC. Samsung still wont recognize this as a dangerous product and refuses to replace the whole refrigerator, instead opting to continue to replace the ice making unit. It is an obvious design flaw that is endangering myself and my families lives. Enclosed is a picture of the piece of plastic found in my wife's water bottle. Please send me a hard copy in the mail that you have received this report.
justification: The incident describes a previous injury (cut lip) and a recurring hazard with sharp plastic pieces in ice, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated occurrences and lack of resolution suggest a high likelihood (4) of recurrence.

incident_description: I was on the phone with the Keurig company and the customer service rep has been check different things with a paper clip.  I tell him that water is dripping out from the bottom.  He says well empty the drip tray.  I did and more water was dripping.  I turn the machine to the right and lots of hot water just rolls out onto my fingers rolling on my palm to my wrist.  The rep could of said becareful that hot water may pour out further.
justification: Hot water caused injury to fingers, palm, and wrist, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore range, Model No. 790-9641340E, Serial No. VF84335671, which I purchased on 11/08/08.

Late on Monday, March 2, 2015, about 5 minutes after removing a pan of roasted vegetables from the oven, I was washing dishes in my kitchen.  Suddenly I heard a crackling sound, then a loud crash.  I turned around [in my galley-style kitchen] to find the outer oven glass door had shattered.  I kept hearing a crackling sound for the next 15-25 minutes, and wasnÃÂt sure if it was due to the cooling down of the oven interior [I'd turned it off after removing the roasted vegetables], or the force of gravity on the pieces of glass still stuck to the oven door frame. 

Thankfully, I did not suffer any cuts by the exploding glass even though I was approx. 18" away from the oven when the crash occurred.  And, thankfully I was able to keep my cat away from the kitchen; she would have most definitely suffered cuts to her paws otherwise due to all the glass on the kitchen floor.

In my 35+ years of living alone, cooking and using ovens, NEVER have I had an oven's glass explode.  In the past few days, I have searched this problem online and see where many other consumers have encountered the same problem.  

Why are manufacturers allowed to install sub-standard glass into ovens?  Why does the federal government not require ovens to be manufactured with the same standard of glass that was used 20-30 years ago?  

Since 3/2/15, I've read that using the self-cleaning oven feature can cause exploding glass; I have self-cleaned my oven only once, and most definitely no more than twice, since purchasing it.  I do not slam the oven door when closing it.  I do not hit or bang things against it.  I live alone, so no one else has used my oven.  In other words, I have not been negligent in its use.  If the Feds would require oven manufacturers to use quality glass, THIS WOULD HAVE NEVER HAPPENED TO ME, nor to many other consumers.

Now, I have to incur a costly repair, have been unduly scared as a result of the incident & fearful of using my oven, as well as extremely inconvenienced.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering but no injuries occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as the user reports this has never happened in 35+ years of using ovens.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she placed the oven on self clean and in half hour when she returned to the kitchen, she noticed that the knobs were melting.  She turned it off, opened the door and noticed that the ceramic sides of the door had melted.  (1/2015 )She contacted the company and they advised her that the unit was not part of a recalled.  They offered to send out a service technician at her expense. She declined the offer because they gave her an option to use her own repair person.  

Caller stated that after the unit was turned off she smelled gas and this was second time after turning it off she smelled the odor.  She can no longer turn it on using the control knobs, she has to use a pliers to operate the unit.
 

Caller feels that the oven is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident caused damage to the oven and smelled gas, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she has been experiencing similar problems of Recall#09-333.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

(2013) She stated that there was smoke emitting from the front panel of the oven, while it was at 325 degree temperature.  She contacted the manufacturer and they offered discount in replacing the control panel.  However, this did not resolve the issue, the incident re-occur while she was using oven at convection roast 325 degrees.   (1/7/15) She contacted the manufacturer and while she was placed on hold the call disconnected, however, no one has attempted to contact her.  The oven remains inoperable at this time.

Consumer feels that although her serial number is not part of a recall this unit should be recalled because of the fire hazard it poses.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard with smoke emission but no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the issue suggests a likely occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her dishwasher was placed in use and while it was in the wash cycle it overheated.  She stated that she smell smoke and when she opened it she noticed that her plastic containers had melted.  There were burnt marks on the interior of the unit and the bottom plastic part of the door melted as well.  Caller stated that there was still water in the unit.


Caller stated that since last year the water remains in the dishwasher she has not been able to drain it.  The unit remains inoperable.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description: I own a Frigidaire smooth top electric stove model fefl79dbl. The front left electric coil temperature fluctuates. We will be cooking with that burner set on level 4, for example, a low to mid setting. Walking away from the stove, we will suddenly hear or smell the food in the pan and realize the burner has gone to "high" on its own and will not stop. We cannot simply reduce the switch because it has no effect on the burner. We will turn the switch completely off and sometimes it still will not turn off. After repeated clicking the switch into and out of the on/off position, the burner will finally turn off.
justification: The burner's uncontrolled temperature fluctuation poses a risk of overheating food or causing a fire, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
The tea kettle has a minimum and a maximum fill line.  Regardless of how much water was poured into the kettle, water spewed out it forcefully when it was poured.  The consumer said that she could not figure why the water was dispensed so forcefully.  The user could risk either getting burned or water could spew all over the counter.

The instructions for use suggested that the kettle came with a squeeze and pour handle.

The consumer said that she pours the water out of the tea kettle at night, but it took several months for her to figure out it contained rust.  The consumer is unsure when she discovered the rust, but it may have been mid-year 2014.

Consumer has ingested rust and maybe black coating inside of tea kettle unknowingly

1/7/2015:  The consumer called the manufacturer and explained her problems with the product.  The rep. agreed to send the consumer a replacement with a different design.  The rep. asked the consumer if she could send this one back to them so that they could analyze it and the consumer agreed.

Please see addendum as to what didn't happen!

The consumer said that she has burned her hand while using this kettle.  The consumer used burn cream for her injuries.  The consumer said that she burned her hands multiple times.  The consumer said that the cream made her hand feel better in a day or so, but she had to apply a bandage and it actually took several days for her burn to heal.

[REDACTED]
Addendum to report #20150108-D3755-1461149

Jan 30, 2015 consumer didn't receive new stainless steel tea kettle as promised.  She called and was told the company doesn't have any.  Consumer asked "why didn't anyone from the company call to tell her that".  On 1/7/2015 they promised it 10-14 days .  The Rep stated their "backup".  Consumer at this point requested a cash refund.  The rep agreed but it's going to take 6-8 weeks.  Seeing is believing.  The rep never requested the old tea kettle back to analyze it so nobody else gets burned.  The company original was suppose to send her prepaid postage and instruction.
Thank you
{Redacted]
justification: The consumer reported multiple burns requiring burn cream and bandages, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue with the kettle design and rust ingestion suggests a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: The door to my stove exploded.  The stove was not in use.  Th door glass completely shattered and exploded all over the kitchen and dining room.
justification: The stove door exploded, causing glass to shatter, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:
On 01/14/15 the consumer was using the oven to cook pizza for about 10 minutes. When she opened the door she noticed that the pizza and rack fell down. The consumer states this occurred also on 11/27/14 when she was cooking a turkey. When she opened the door and tried to move the turkey the rack fell. 

The consumer states the first time this occurred was about 2-3 years ago. The rack fell while she was cooking and she contacted Sears. The consumer received replacement racks from Sears but they racks continued to fall when she would put something on top of the rack. The consumer informed Sears the problem was still happening and Sears replaced the liner of the oven. The consumer describes it as the metal insert that is in the oven. The repairs were covered under the extended warranty.  

On 12/15/14 (estimated) the consumer contacted Sears and informed them of the problem but the consumer states she was getting the run around. The consumer requested to have a supervisor call her back but the consumer did not receive a call back. 

On 01/16/15 the consumer contacted Sears and expressed her concerns. The consumer spoke with [REDACTED] who advised her unit is not recalled. [REDACTED] asked the consumer if she would like to arrange a repair at the consumer expense but the consumer declined. The consumer does not feel safe repairing the unit and is not willing to pay for any repairs. [REDACTED] provided the consumer the CPSC recall hotline phone number and advised the consumer to file a report. 

The consumer states when she slightly presses down on the rack it falls.

Please note that dates are approximate & that Sears repair service should have mote details about previous repairs while under warranty.


The consumer tried to take pictures of how racks sit on side supports, but it was not clear enough to add additional detail to this report.  Essentially - rack does not sit properly on side supports & seems worse in the back.  Changing out the racks does not help.
[REDACTED]
justification: The consumer was not injured, but the rack fell down when she was cooking, which is a safety hazard.

incident_description: GE Microwave spontaneously starts running.  Model JES1451DS1BB.  Product is less than 6 months old.
justification: The microwave spontaneously running is an incident with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. Given the product's age, occurrence likelihood is possible.

incident_description:
There is a chemical smell and release of a toxic substance that spread inside both the refrigerator and freezer food storage compartment areas of the unit. 
It became unbearable after inhaling the fumes from the same substance that mysteriously started leaking inside the fridge, for days now.
 It was discovered on 02/08/2015, as a rancid smell coming from inside and outside the fridge. 
The same thing was happening inside the freezer drawer compartment, simultaneously blowing in with the cold air climate system.
The odor became overwhelming after a very short period of time, as I began removing the food from inside. Any packaged products enclosed with cardboard or thin plastic wrap was already penetrated by the same ammonia / fishy smelling aroma coming from inside and has now saturated or permeated the inside walls, drawers, everything and everywhere inside, having some kind of toxic release effect that was constantly moving fumes around. 
Food was now spoiled and couldn't be eaten after opening the package and cooking it, and at that point, I knew this was rather an unusual contamination with a bitter after taste to boot.
After breathing in the unknown substance for some time, while evacuating the food, it wasn't long afterwords before my lungs were feeling heavy and then a burning sensation was felt between my esophagus and lungs. I had chewing gum inside my mouth that began to taste of rancid chemicals and the mere contact of my face with my hands from handling the contaminated product left a taste and smell that could not be easily removed, even if I attempted to use soap. Its a very nasty situation and I now know that my lungs and skin are susceptible to the spread of the unknown toxic chemicals leaking out from somewhere. I cant get near the refrigerator for long and its been unplugged.
Never, have I ever experienced anything like this before with a consumer product, and the reason for giving this detailed report.
justification: The incident involves exposure to toxic fumes leading to physical symptoms like heavy lungs and burning sensations, indicating injury.

incident_description:
(1/26/2015) The consumer had the oven set at 325 to bake bread. She was going to check on the bread. The handle came loose on one side of the door. She open the door to check the bread. She then closed the door. She stepped away from the oven to reset the timer when suddenly the outer glass of the oven door exploded and shattered. Glass sprayed over the entire kitchen. The consumer stated that a shard of glass cut the top of her foot. There was bleeding but no medical attention was required.


(01/26/2015) The consumer called the Customer Service Department at Sears. The consumer was advised to shut the oven off and call the gas company. The consumer was transferred to the Technical Support Department which advised her that he had never heard of the incident before. The consumer was offered a new warranty or have repair service people to come out to do an estimate.

The consumer elected to get the warranty.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut on the foot) but no medical attention was required, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the technical support had never heard of such an incident before.

incident_description:
The consumer noted she was preparing to make a smoothie and plugged the base of the blender in the wall electrical outlet...Immediately the blender turned on...She reached with her left hand to press the silver button to turn it off and an exposed blade lacerated her palm...She then had to reach with her right hand to unplug the machine...She was taken, by her husband, to the North Florida Regional Medical Center Emergency room for wound care and stitches...Upon returning home she looked at the blender and saw that the lid was on the base with the blade exposed. She received stitches and later on had to receive follow up surgery from a specialist on 2/2/15.

Caller feels that this blender is a safety hazard and that it should have been designed not to operate if the product is not closed properly.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The consumer added the product was purchased in Summer 2014 by her mother, and she gave it to her the day she was injured.
justification: The consumer suffered a laceration requiring stitches and follow-up surgery, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that an incident happened with the first toaster oven in 2013.

The consumer stated that piece of toast caught on fire.

The consumer contacted the manf and they asked the consumer to cut off and return the end of the cord. The consumer was provided a replacement toaster.

The consumer stated that he started using the replacement toaster and the same exact incident happened with the replacement toaster in Jan/Feb 2015.

The consumer stated that he put in 4 pieces of bread to toast. The consumer turned the setting knob 2/3 way. The consumer stated that he went into another room and then smelled smoke few minutes later. The consumer went to the toaster and noticed that the toast had caught on fire. The consumer unplugged the toaster, opened the door and tried to suppress the fire. The consumer moved the toaster outside and dumped it in the snow.

The consumer stated that the toast setting knob is supposed to also act as a timer and eventually turn off the toaster after certain time (depending on the setting of toast). The consumer stated that the spring failed in the knob and failed to turn on the timer. The toaster stayed on the same setting until the consumer got to the toaster and unplugged it.

The consumer stated that this is exactly how the toast caught on fire in the first toaster as well.

The consumer contacted the manf in regards to this incident as well. They sent him a pre-paid mailing label and box to return the toaster. The consumer will be provided a refund.
justification: The incident involved toast catching fire twice with no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence of the same issue with a replacement toaster suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The submitter is filing the report on his mother's behalf. 

On 01/07/15 the submitter's mother woke up due to a noise and noticed that the unit was running on its own. Since then when the submitter's mother would use the unit it would run on its own after she closes the door. The submitter and his mother feel the unit poses a fire hazard. 

On 01/27/15 the submitter spoke with the firm (case #[REDACTED]) and informed them of the incident. The firm told the consumer that they would send a technician and the repairs would be free of charge since it was a safety hazard. 

On 02/11/15 the technician examined the unit and told the submitter that the unit needed a replacement part. The technician told the submitter that the issue is a safety hazard but the firm would have to give authorization to provide repairs free of charge. However, the submitter contacted the firm on 02/12/15 and was told that the issue with the unit was not a safety hazard. The submitter spoke with [REDACTED], who informed the consumer that the replacement part would cost $300 and it would be additional for labor costs. The submitter is very upset and feels the firm should repair or replace the unit free of charge because it poses a fire hazard.
justification: The unit running on its own poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred. The issue is a possible safety hazard as indicated by the technician.

incident_description: I was cooking chili in my Cuisinart CSC-650 slow cooker when it stopped working.  The cord failed to retract and I removed the cover on the bottom over the retractable housing.  What I found were corroded wires that were continually overheating until they finally broke off free of their connectors.  On the white retractable cord spool, the power cord had melted, along with the plastic disc which was also burned housing.  The yellow disk, which should be white, suffered long-term heat damage and is where the unit is fed from the retractable cord, it too suffered long-term heat damage and was burned.  The saving grace is when this shorted out, the burned components and live wires were all housed in sheet metal.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning slow cooker with significant electrical damage, but no injury or death occurred as the hazardous components were contained within sheet metal.

incident_description: The crockpot was being used to cook chicken. It was on high and had been cooking for 3 hours when it suddenly exploded.  Glass flew 5 feet from the location of the crockpot and the lid shattered causing most glass to fall into the crockpot.
justification: The crockpot exploded, causing glass to shatter and scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: While making coffee hot water shot out from the top of the maker
justification: Hot water shooting out poses a burn risk, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that whenever she uses the oven it emits CO. 11/2014 The fire department was contacted and they came out and inspected her home and informed her that there was low levels of CO escaping from the oven.  She was advised not to use the oven.  She noticed this incident early November when her CO detectors would go off everytime the oven was used.


11/2014 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that a service technician would be sent out at her expense.  She informed the representative that she should not be held responsible for this fee because there is a safety issue with this unit.


Caller feels that this oven should be recalled.
justification: Low levels of CO were detected, but no injury or death occurred. The incident is documented and the oven was advised not to be used.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting his trio refrigerator purchased in 2007 and that he had no problems with until the week of February 4th, 2015.
The callers wife opened their refrigerator door and saw that the light to their unit was out.
She shut the door then opened it but the lights did not come on then she opened and shut the door and light was on.
Her husband checked the light and surrounding area and the lights were so hot that he could not keep his hand on the bulb.
There is no browning or melting of the plastic portion of the refrigerator but there is browning at the base of the bulb leading the consumer to believe that this problem has just begun.
To avoid any fire hazard he has removed the bulbs.
He states that all else in the refrigerator works as it should.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator light that became excessively hot, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
After finishing cooking for the evening and tidying up the kitchen I heard the igniters on our  31/2  year old KitchenAid Architect Series II , KGSS907SWH02, 30" Slide In Gas Range spontaneously start. The gas knobs were all in the off position. Within about 40 seconds of the igniters continually firing we could not believe it when we heard the igniter in the oven turn on. Not only did it turn on, but it also turned on the gas in the oven and the broiler flame started. We could not believe our eyes. The broiler flame was very strong and had there been anything left in the oven even on the medium rack it would have caught on fire. This was at about 10pm. Scared for the safety of our family we evacuated our two kids and two pets from the house, had the fire extinguisher on hand and ready as we had no idea what this gas range was spontaneously doing. My husband then ran downstairs to cut the electricity from the electric panel. The sparking stopped and the flame disappeared. As we did not know what issues were causing the gas to spontaneously start we were concerned that there could also be a gas leak overnight. With limited options available at that time of night my husband pulled out the stove and manually turned the gas supply valve off behind the stove and we left the breaker turned off at the electric panel. We brought our kids back in the house and set up the carbon monoxide detector closer to the stove...just in case. This was a terrifying issue affecting the safety of our family and our property. I can't even imagine if we were not at home at the time to catch this spontaneous fire in the oven. and the igniters spontaneously sparking on the stove top.  

Upon contacting Whirlpool we were advised that an Authorized Whirlpool Repairman was not available for over 14 days as it was the Christmas break and they did not have anyone available during this time. As this was not acceptable service, given the safety issue, and the absolute inconvenience at a very busy entertaining time of the year, and the fact that we still had to feed our family of five over the holidays I advised them I would contact a local repair person to come. The local appliance repair company arrived Christmas Eve day and spent a good part of the day trying to determine the issue. After completely removing the 'appliance manager' component the issue continued. When we turned the power back on, with all the stove and oven controls off, the igniters would randomly start to spark and within a minute the igniter in the oven would spontaneously start and the gas in the broiler element would ignite. ( The repairman had also reopened the gas valve in the back of the stove.) The repairman was able to pick up a Whirlpool Corporation Factory Certified Electronic Spark Module ( #8273977). Upon replacing this module the problem appeared to be fixed. 

It is now just two months later and last night the igniter on the front left burner randomly turned itself on again and started sparking. The stove and all the burners were turned off. Again, concerned for our safety we immediately went to cut the electrical power to the unit and the igniter stopped. While the gas in the oven did not turn itself on while we observed ( and took video) for about a minute and a half we decided not to wait any longer before cutting the electric power as we started to smell burning electric parts. 

Upon reporting this last night to KitchenAid we have to wait 4 days ( this is the earliest appointment available by their service department) for an authorized repairman to come to the house to see the problem.

This range is a huge safety issue and should be recalled by the company before it results in a personal or property damage as a result of a fire or carbon monoxide poisoning.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous ignition of gas and igniters, posing a significant fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This is concerning a replacement decanter for a MR. COFFEE 10 and 12 cup. for Coffee makers :
EJ,ET,IS,LM AND VM series.
I simply dropped and broke the previous one as my mistake. 
My wife purchased this at Target store in Grapevine Texas. Upon the first use when the decanter was lifted from the maker the black plastic handle separated from the glass bottom. The glass bottom fell and shattered on the counter top and splashed hot coffee on me and sent glass and hot coffee across the counter top and floor. After cleaning up I noticed that the black plastic handle seemed to be intact. The top rim of the glass decanter was intact. These is a silicone type material around the rim that wound have been between the glass and the black handle assembly. This silicone looked to have one clear crack through it and several below the surface.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from hot coffee and shattered glass, but the likelihood of recurrence is low as it was due to a specific product defect.

incident_description:
SEARS ELITE ELECTRIC RANGE MODEL # 790.4661.3502 with electronic controls

one burner heats up to high and cannot be turned off.  this is the same issue as involved with recalls of model #s 790.99012, 790.99013, 790.99014, 790.99019 .  The only way to turn off the burner is to disconnect at the main house panel circuit breaker.
justification: The burner cannot be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I was using my Ninja Professional blender. I mixed the pancake batter and was unable to remove the top. I tried several grippers in order to remove it and it wouldn't bufge. I sat it upright on the counter and turned to do something else. All of a sudden there was a loud bang. The top flew off and went about 12 feet. The top contains the very sharp mixing blades and fortunately it did not fly in my direction or hit someone. The blades and force could have killed a child, pet or severely cut someone. Batter flew everywhere. I know that the lid was on straight. I have used this to mix this batter many times. I feel this is a great safety hazard. I did call the company about this incident but they seem to only be interested in settling a claim for damages. I do not feel that is an issue, but product safety is the issue.
justification: The incident involved a blender top flying off with potential for injury, but no actual harm occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the user had used the blender many times without prior issues.

incident_description:
I cooked a frozen pizza at 400 degrees for thirteen minutes, like I have countless times before.  Once my pizza was done, I took it out of the oven and turned the oven off.  Approximately thirty minutes later, I heard a crash in my kitchen.  Upon investigating, I found the outer glass oven door had exploded, throwing glass approximately ten feet across my kitchen.  The oven was cool to the touch at this time.  There was no damage to my oven previous to this incident.  GE was contacted and set up an appointment for a service representative to come to my house to examine my stove, but on the day of the appointment, the service tech called and refused to come stating this was not a safety hazard and more than likely I had damaged the door to my stove and just hadn't realized it.

incident_description:
I was using my new Kitchen Living Turbo Convection Oven that I bought at Aldi's to cook chicken breasts.  The scant directions in the user guide recommend a 400 degree setting for 40 minutes on the top rack of the cooking bowl.  I set the chicken on the top rack and started the cooking process.  This was only the third time that I used this cooker since buying it in December.  
 I lifted the lid up, by the handle, after 20 minutes of cooking to turn the chicken.  To do this, I had to turn the lid upside down to rest on the counter top.  You can't just set it upright as the cooking element light won't turn off.  
As I lifted the lid by the handle, the handle completely pulled out of the lid!!! I was shocked but managed to catch this heavy glass lid, which weighs almost five pounds, before it could fall and shatter onto my ceramic tile floor.
I was able to complete the cooking of the chicken after carefully setting the lid back in place.

After the lid cooled, I examined it.  This is a very dangerous product that should be recalled from the US market.  The handle on the lid is held in place with two cheap plastic pegs that are under 3/8 of an inch long.. I also found that the metal holding the handle in place had cracked and the handle was no longer secure.  As the lid is used and heats up, the plastic becomes pliable and the pegs are not effective in holding the lid.  The handle is what controls the on and off operation of the cooking device and also the mobility of it.  If this lid had fallen onto the floor, the glass lid would have shattered, the light bulb within the lid would have shattered, and the electrical connection in the lid may have caused a shock or short.  I really would like to see this product removed from our US stores.  Thank you
justification: The incident caused a potential hazard that could have resulted in injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On November 5, 2014 I order a BlueStar Cooktop of Reading , PA (Model# RBCT304BSS-NAT, SN:1409033) for my wife. I received the cooktop on December 16, 2014. The cooktop was installed December 19,2014 by Master plumber [REDACTED]  licence# [REDACTED](Maryland). The purchase price was 1,652 purchased from Plessers of Babylon, NY.  

Upton installation, my wife noticed safety issues with the cooktop. They are as follows: 
1) top two burns work differently than the indicators show. The top burner knob indicates that it should turn on the burner at the top right, but it turns on the top left. The next knob down from the top indicates that it should turn on the top left, but it turns on the top right. 
2) The iron grates are uneven. Creating an unsafe cooking surface (i.e. a pots contents splash about.).
3) The printed knobs indicators are upside down. 
4) The starting point for the knobs is away from the cook (user) making it difficult to know if the burner is on. (My wife has already burned herself twice because of this flaw. She as also left the burners turned on thinking that they were off due to the faulty indicators.  

All of this information has been passed on the retailer and the manufacturer. The retailer response was we're only willing to replace the iron grates. The manufacturer's response was "that's the way it was designed." I feel your agency needs to address these issues because these items are consumer safety issues. Please address these issues before someone gets hurt!

We had loaded it and started it up and headed out to our son's band concert.  When we got home an hour later, we smelled the most horrid electrical burning smell as we entered our house.  We determined it was coming from the dishwasher when we noted black soot on the counter above it.  We turned the circuit breaker off to it and my husband removed the front panel.  The entire control panel is blackened and the wires are clearly melted and soot covers it all.  It horrifies me to think that our house could have burned down and/or my family could have been injured/killed if this had happened when we were sleeping or if we had been away for longer. incident_description:
The range exhaust hood is provided to the consumer with the grounded and ungrounded conductors wired in reverse.

Additionally, the electric grounding conductor is not bonded to the power outlets provided in the hood to power an external fan.

The hood contains four E27 light sockets. Due to the improper wiring the socket itself becomes energized, posing a shock hazard.

Similarly, any fan powered from the power outlets in the hood will not be bonded to the electric grounding conductor. Power will also be supplied via the grounded conductor. This also poses a significant safety hazard.
justification: The improper wiring and lack of grounding pose a significant shock hazard, which could lead to injury or death if someone comes into contact with the energized parts.

[REDACTED] 02/24/15 From Consent form: 

To Whom it May Concern:
This document is to clarify and expand on the "Incident Description" as taken down by the CPSC personnel during our phone conversation. While the oral brief is fundamentally accurate, my hope is that a more complete description will more fully alert others to the problem we experienced.

FACTS
We bought our built in KitchenAide oven (model KEBS107SSS02 in 2009. It was purchased new from a local retailer and was installed by a highly experienced and reputable licensed kitchen remodeler. The unit sits under a cooktop of a different brand, and has a metal frame door holding 4 large panes of glass with air gaps between the layers of glass to allow cooking food to be viewed for insulation.

In 2011, while the oven was being preheated, at least two of the inner panes of glass shattered with an explosive pop, sending shards not only throughout the inside of the oven but also cascading onto the floor through the gap between the door and the oven. While the glass is "safety glass", meaning that there were no large pieces with sharp points immediately on the floor, there were hundreds of pieces up to a quarter inch in diameter as well as a huge amount of finer pieces, some going down to the size of a glass powder. Inside the oven were the rest of the remains the glass panes, including larger but fragile pieces along with smaller and powdery fragments.

KitchenAide replaces the glass after that incident and assured us that we should not be concerned about a recurrence, citing the likelihood of a defect in the original glass as the cause of the failure.

In January of 2015, however, the new oven glass shattered again. Photos are at the end of this document.

KitchenAide is denying any responsibility, since we did not buy their warranty protection plan, and are not considering the possibility of a design flaw in the manufacture of either the metal portion of the oven door (e.g., a slight warp, which could stress the panes) or of the glass itself.

CONCERNS AND CONJECTURE

We consider ourselves lucky that no one in the kitchen was hurt, since even broken safety glass (especially the fine powdery shards) represents a significant hazard.
Obviously, any food exposed to shattered glass would need to be thrown out.

We have never used the "self cleaning" feature of the oven, but given the extreme heat that this produces, we suspect that this would likely increase the stress on the oven.
justification: The incident involved the oven door exploding twice without causing injury, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The recurrence suggests a possible design flaw, making future occurrences possible (likelihood 3).
