I ordered a replacement glass and had it installed 1 week later. In January of 2015 the same door shattered again. Again the oven was not on and had not been in use that day. I notified Sears again and asked if they had any door options because I do not want to replace this glass door again. They did not acknowledge any problem and no solution.
justification: The oven door shattered violently twice, but no injuries were reported. The recurrence suggests a possible but not certain likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that when she turns the oven on bake mode, the heating element lights up red. The oven makes a loud popping noise while pre-heating. The oven door comes open and closes from the pop. 

The consumer stated that this issue occurs at any temperature. The consumer is able to turn the oven off at the control panel. 

The consumer contacted the manf regarding the issue. They provided information for repair, inspection and cost.

The consumer stated that the oven has been a problem from the time that she purchased it.

Please note that this is the second time the ignitor was changed on this oven.
justification: The oven exhibits dangerous behavior (loud popping, door opening) but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
GE Profile Dishwasher came new with newly built home in July 2007 then recalled 2012.

The unit was repaired in 2012 according to the remedy for release# 12-244.

The unit now has the same problem that it was recalled and repaired for with release# 12-244.

January 16th, 2015 the caller and his wife loaded the dishwasher, started it around 10:00 PM and then went to bed around midnight.
They smelled a light odor of burning but describe it as that odor when we turn the furnace on for the first time.
They searched for the source but couldn't find it.

Around 2:30AM January 17th, 2015 the caller's wife woke, went to the kitchen to get something from the cupboard, smelled the faint odor of burning but could not locate the source until she accidently brushed against the counter by the dishwasher and surface burned her abdomen.

She opened the dishwasher to discern the source of the heat but hot air came blasting out of the dishwasher.

The experience is described as if she had stuck her head in a hot oven.

She looked in the dishwasher once the heat passed and saw that all the plastic products in the top rack were melted to the rack.

She does not consider her surface burn as an injury because there are no lasting marks or redness.

 The caller's spoke with GE representative [REDACTED] who holds badge# [REDACTED] January 20th, 2015, she advised caller that they would not repair the unit again at their cost, they will not replace the unit but will provide the caller with $100 gift card toward the purchase of a new unit.

The caller and his wife are asking that the manufacturer replace the dishwasher with a different model and take the safety issue seriously.

He states the the entire development he lives in has the same dishwasher and the potential for harm from fire in his opinion is very great.
justification: The incident resulted in a surface burn, which qualifies as an injury, though minor. The recurrence of the same issue after a previous repair suggests a possible likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire gas stove 2 weeks ago from Home Depot.  The model number is FFGF301LW.  Yesterday, I was cooking in the oven (this was only the third time I had used the oven).  The temp I was cooking at was 350 for 30 minutes.  After the food was done and the oven had been off for about 10 minutes,  the middle piece of glass in the oven door shattered.  I think there are 3 pieces of glass the one that shattered was the one in the middle so the glass is mostly contained withing the door but I have been finding little pieces of glass around the oven.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was utilizing the self cleaning option on my 8 month old GE Monogram wall convection oven for the first time. After 1.5 hours into the cleaning cycle, I heard a loud bang and  popping sound in my kitchen. When I looked in the kitchen, all seemed normal. When the cleaning cycle was completed & the oven unlocked, I opened the oven door to see how clean my oven was. To say I was astonished to see the inner glass shattered within my oven & spilling onto the floor, is an understatement! I had just spent $3400 on this! I am blessed that my dogs & children were not harmed by the glass & that it is covered under warranty. Consumers need to be aware though that this is VERY common! I did months of research prior to my purchase & never saw one mention of this hazard. When I specifically searched "shattered oven door glass GE Monogram self clean", I was disgusted with the amount of complaints. Even more disappointing was how GE will not support their consumers if it is beyond their warranty period.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered oven glass) but no injuries or deaths, and the description notes it is a common issue with this product.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased the range in April 2014 and had it delivered in May 2014. 

The consumer stated that there is no problem with the stove top. 

The consumer stated that there is a plastic-burning, chemical smell when she uses the oven. The consumer stated that sometimes it smells like something is burning.

The consumer believes that the heating element could be burning a wire.

The consumer stated that she initially contacted the retailer within the 90 day warranty period with this issue. They informed her to continue using the product and the smell will go away. The consumer called Lowe's for 3 months letting them know that the smell is not going away. The consumer was informed to contact the warranty center. The consumer contacted them in August 2014. A technician was sent out to inspect the unit. The technician stated that everything seems to be functioning correctly, he was not sure what was causing the smell; he did notice the smell as well. 

The consumer was informed that maybe the plastic from instruction got caught in the oven. The technician instructed the consumer to check the drawer to see if there was anything stuck there. The consumer checked that and noticed that the smell was still present. 

The consumer was informed by Lowe's that she could not return the range since it was past the 90 return period.  The consumer stated that if she would have known earlier, she would have returned the range rather than waiting for the smell to disappear.

The consumer stated that the smell gets into the meal that is being cooked in the oven. The consumer stated that the smell gets into her hair, clothes, house, etc.

The consumer stopped using the range until January. The consumer used it on 1/18/15. The consumer stated that the smell caused her eyes, throat and skin to burn. She had to throw out the meal since the smell got into it.

The consumer stated that when she used the oven on 01/18/15, she saw faint gray/white smoke coming from the back of the unit. The consumer stated that the smoke dissipated quickly so she continued to use the unit.

The consumer stated that the smell is only present when the oven is heated. 

The consumer called Lowe's again on 1/19/15. They informed her to get the R number from the manf and they will take the unit back.

The consumer spoke to customer service with manf on 1/19/14. They refused to give the R number. The consumer was informed that they can send out a technician. The asked to speak to a supervisor and was transferred to [REDACTED](at Electrolux).

 Ms. [REDACTED] informed the consumer that she will not swap the unit just for an issue with smell. The consumer asked for a refund. The consumer was informed that she cannot get a refund. Ms. [REDACTED] asked for proof of purchase because the unit was manufactured in 2012 and it would be unusual for it to be at the store in 2014. The consumer was informed by Lowe's when she purchased the unit that this was a Fall model that they were clearing out in the Spring. The consumer stated that she would not have purchased the unit had she known it was manufactured in 2012.

The consumer stated a technician is supposed to be coming out from the manf on 1/21/15 for inspection.

1/21/2015

[REDACTED] from AAA Appliance came to look at the stove today. He took off the bottom panel of the oven to expose the heating element and what he called the "bake element base" under the heating element. The bottom panel of the oven had a white residue on the underside of it that looks like white mold. The bake element base had some sort of film all over it. Parts of it looked like rust spots and some of it looked like a white powdery film. [REDACTED] from AAA called [REDACTED] from Frigidaire. [REDACTED] said that [REDACTED] advised him that there has been residue on the bake element base in the past. [REDACTED] advised that he did not know what the residue consisted of. He advised me that Frigidaire would send a new bake element base and a new bottom panel to be installed in about a week. [REDACTED] also asked me to run two more self cleanings on the oven -- with the residue in it -- which I will not do as it burns my eyes, nose, skin, and throat.
justification: The consumer experienced burning sensations in eyes, throat, and skin, indicating injury from chemical exposure.

incident_description:
2010:  The consumer baked several cakes in the oven and later that day, it quit working.  The error code of F-15 came up.  The consumer went on-line and found that the unit needed to be reset.  He unplugged it and waited for approximately 15 minutes and plugged it back in.  This allowed the range to reset itself.

On 2 separate occasions, the large, front right burner (if facing the stove) came on by itself.  The consumer could not turn the burner off by the use of the control knob.  The consumer had to trip the breaker in order to turn the burner off.  The 2 incidents happened within a week to 10 days of each other.  This happened in late September/early August of 2012.  About a week after the 2 burner incidents, the clock-board on the range burned out.  This incident burned the back of the range, the wall behind the range and caused discoloration to the range itself.

The range was under warranty and the consumer had a dealer's technician come out and look at it.  The technician checked the clock-board and determined that based on the charring in that area, that the part needed to be replaced.  The tech. called the manufacturer and ordered a new clock-board.  Approximately, 1 week later, the consumer received the replacement part and a dealer's tech. came back out and installed it.

Approximately 3 weeks later, the burners quit working all together. The consumer called the dealer's technician again.  The tech. came out and looked at the range and told the consumer that all of the control boards had to be replaced and it would cost $800.  The consumer declined to repair it and placed the range in his shop.

The consumer called Sear's about this issue, but they were not willing to do anything for the consumer.

The consumer said that the range was not included in Recall 09-333.
justification: The incident involved equipment malfunction and property damage (burned range and wall), but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore model 790.9743802 electric range that I purchased new in 2009.  While using the convection oven, I heard a buzzing/crackling noise and saw smoke coming from behind the control panel.  I immediately shut off the oven and allowed the stove to cool.  I then disconnected the power from the stove and removed the cover from the back of control panel.  Upon inspection, I saw that one of the connectors and wires on the circuit board for the control panel was burned and melted.

There does not appear to be any safety recalls for this particular model appliance, but there are numerous posts on the internet that reference similar problems with Kenmore/Electrolux electric ranges.  I am concerned that this appliance has a design flaw or material defect that poses a serious fire hazard if the problem goes undetected and is not properly repaired.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burned connector, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidaire Smooth Top Slide-in Range, Model# FGES3065KFB, Mfgd Mar 2010 that we purchased from Lowe's in May of 2010.  There was a recall for this same type of range (http://www.recallowl.com/Consumer+Recalls/Household+Products/Frigidaire+and+Electrolux+ICON+Electric+Smoothtop+Cooktops+and+Slide-In+Ranges+Recalled+Due+to+Fire+Hazard). My model number is not included in the recall but the design is almost identical and my range is exhibiting the same behaviors as mentioned in the recall.  I contacted Frigidaire and was politely informed that my range wasn't recalled and that the warranty period had expired so I should contact a qualified service center for repairs.  Sadly, the repair estimate amount to almost half the amount we purchased the range for.  

Indications I've seen over the past six months, elements heating with controls off.  Burner temp was around 160 degrees based on my temp gun.  And each time there was no hot element warning on the display.  The left front also displays intermittent incorrect temps.
justification: The range exhibits unsafe heating behaviors similar to a recalled model, posing a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: ge range top jgp989k2bb control knobs caught on fire shut off gas inside and outside also tripped off breaker smothered fire out aprox 1 min later glass range top explodes sending glass all over kitchen  several cuts on face and arms.
justification: The incident resulted in several cuts on face and arms, indicating injury, but the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: I was baking a take and bake pizza in our oven when the glass window in the door spontaneously exploded.
justification: The incident was an incident with no injury, which is a common occurrence in the industry.

incident_description:
Heated water in Capresso electric tea kettle (Model 260) as usual (glass carafe with plastic handle, separate electric base).  While pouring near-boiling water from the kettle, the top of the handle suddenly separated from the glass carafe and the glass portion of the carafe began to fall.  Caught falling portion of kettle near spout. Bottom portion of handle also separated from carafe.  Burn treated at home.

Contacted manufacturer regarding safety concern and subject of recall; informed that this model was  not subject to recall, was discontinued, and out of warranty. Offered purchase of replacement at discount.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn that required home treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it's a specific model issue not under recall.

incident_description: I was using the K130 Keurig Brewing System, and while in operation it opened and spewed coffee grounds and hot water on my shoulder causing burns. After checking the Internet, this is apparently a common problem. Why is this product on the market?
justification: The incident caused burns, indicating an injury, and the problem is described as common.

incident_description: Hot liquid escapes from machine while brewing.
justification: Hot liquid can cause burns, which is an injury.

incident_description: On 2/6/15 I was sitting in the living room with our GE profile Dishwasher Model PDW8880JSS finishing a load of dishes and it was on the dry cycle. I could see something flashing in the kitchen. I went to check and had 3 to 4" flames shooting from the front panel. I immediately unplugged the unit and doused the flames. I also took photos of the damage.
justification: The incident involved flames shooting from the dishwasher, but no injury or death was reported, and the flames were quickly extinguished.

incident_description:
This report is related to the GE JES1656SRSS microwave from General Electric.

Last week we noticed the circuit where this microwave was connected the fuse was open (standard 20A). I didn't notice anything obvious and I plugged back the microwave and it worked as usual. few days later I heard a very strong humming from the microwave just after it stopped working. I couldn't figure out then why it was doing that noise until I touched one of the sides of the oven and it was extremely hot. I carefully moved the microwave and all the enclosure was too hot to handle (I decided not to open the door anyway) and when I tried to disconnect the microwave from the power outlet I noticed the power cable was also too hot to handle so I used an oven mitten I unplugged it. When I touched the plug I noticed it was too hot to the point it melted the plastic enclosure of the plug, I got a small burn from that but it didn't require further care. If I wouldn't have noticed or disconnected the microwave I'm sure it might have caused a fire.
justification: The incident resulted in a small burn from the hot plug, indicating an injury, and the potential for a fire if not noticed.

incident_description:
In recent weeks have experienced abnormal operation of a GE over-the-range microwave oven, model PEB2060DM2BB, manufactured in April 2011.  First problems were the microwave would not respond to keypad controls to stop the operation.  Only way to stop was by opening the door, but closing the door, the unit would start again.

This evening, with nobody in the kitchen, I heard the microwave come on and it stayed on until I opened the door.  Researching on the internet seems to bring back many occurrences of GE microwaves starting spontaneously.
justification: The microwave operates abnormally and starts spontaneously, posing a potential hazard but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
My lady friend purchased a 10 inch Silk brand ceramic frying pan from T.J. Maxx, for me as a Christmas present.  Upon examining the fry pan, I discovered the rolled over lip at the top edge of the pan was razor sharp.  If you are cleaning the pan with either a sponge or would run your finger around the lower edge of the rolled lip of the pan, it would cut you.  Fortunately I discovered this hazard before being injured.  I did cut a piece of plastic, placed on the surface of a sponge, to demonstrate the hazardous issue to my lady friend.  She returned the pan to store where she purchased it and notified the manager as to the hazard.  

I will attach digital pictures of the pan and product labeling.
justification: The incident was discovered before any injury occurred, but the sharp edge of the pan could have caused injury if not noticed.

incident_description:
December 25, 2014

National Product Testing and Evaluation Center
5 Research Place
Rockville, MD 20850

RE: Kitchen Aid Architect Series II, Model KERS807SSS02, Ser. XW4704146

To whom it may concern:

I am writing you regarding a design flaw in Whirlpool's Kitchen Aid Architect Series II, Model KERS807SSS02, which I've brought to the attention of [REDACTED] several times as well as Consumer Reports, The Better Business Bureau, and Consumer Complaint TV.

First let me say that it should not cost hundreds of dollars each and every time a pot overflows on a range. Kitchen Aid (Whirlpool the parent company) has a serious design flaw in the above-referenced oven model and they should step up to the plate and take responsibility. At the very least, it would demonstrate that they respect their customer base and know the value of customer service.

I purchased a Kitchen Aid (Architect Series II, Model KERS807SSS02, Ser. XW4704146) oven five years ago, which included a 5-year extended warranty. The first time I had to use my extended warranty was the first time a pot over boiled thus causing the liquid in the pot to cover the top of the range.

The controls on this model are located in the front, directly below the stove top. It seems quite obvious to me that the design should have included protection from moisture reaching the controls or a moisture barrier. It is very common for pots to over boil on a range from time to time, but this should not cause the controls to malfunction due to moisture seepage.

Again, it should not cost hundreds of dollars each time a pot overflows on a range.

Had I known that the oven model I purchased had a design flaw that allows moisture to reach the computer controls, I would have purchased the oven with the controls above the cooking surface. Kitchen Aid/Whirlpool has designed an oven which demands customers to carry extended warranties on their appliance. I've conducted some searches on the Internet and this seems to be true for a variety of other customer complaints with their ovens concerning the oven controls (see attachment).

I invested over $2K on this oven because having owned Kitchen Aid appliances in the past, the Kitchen Aid brand had historically proven reliable.

I'm not asking for much, just honest repair to my range OR an even exchange with a 2009 model with the controls in the rear and above the range top away from contact if moisture from an overflowed pot should reach the controls since you did not include a moisture barrier in your design.

I hope your agency can offer assistance unlike the Better Business Bureau and [REDACTED], [REDACTED] of Whirlpool.

Kind regards,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a design flaw causing malfunction without injury, and the likelihood is high given the frequency of similar complaints.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she experienced similar problems of release#09-333.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

She stated that while using the range it displays F1 and when the oven is powered off the heating element stays on and it has to be unplugged to prevent a fire.  this incident has been ongoing for about 2 weeks.

1/12/15 The retailer was contacted and she was given a number for Kenmore which was invalid.

Caller feels that her model should be included in the recall.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating element posing a fire and burn hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
On 01/18/15 the consumer set the unit to a normal wash cycle. Shortly after she noticed black smoke emitting from the unit and opened the unit's door in effort to stop the cycle. Then the consumer shut off the circuit breaker and opened the windows to air out the smoke. The consumer contacted her local fire department. The consumer states the firemen checked the unit to make sure it was not "on" and put a heat sensor on the unit. 

On 01/19/15 the consumer contacted Pepco, her electricity supplier and informed them of the incident. [REDACTED], an adjuster from Pepco insurance came to the consumer's home and took pictures of the unit. [REDACTED] advised the consumer that the smoke would go away once the unit is removed from her home and advised the consumer to contact KitchenAid for assistance with repairs. 

On 01/19/15 the consumer contacted the firm and informed them of the incident. The firm arranged for a technician to examine the unit on 01/27/15. 

On 01/17/15 the consumer noticed a strange odor coming from the unit shortly after she set it for a normal wash cycle. The consumer opened the unit's door and examined the unit. The consumer did not see any damages or smoke so she let the unit complete the cycle. 

The consumer states there are not property damages. The consumer noticed the unit's control panel is burned and she believes the control panel failed and caused the unit to emit black smoke.

The consumer uses the unit daily and sets it to a normal wash cycle.
justification: The incident involved black smoke emission and a burned control panel, but no injuries or property damage were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: This is an issue with the cast iron grates above gas burners on a stove top.  The heat from the burners over a 3 year period has caused the grate to sag, resulting in an unstable platform for cooking utensils.  Extreme care must be used at all times to prevent the utensil from upsetting and spilling its contents onto the cook top or the user.  This is a case of a poorly under-engineered product.
justification: The incident describes a potential for spills due to unstable grates, which could lead to minor accidents but no reported injuries.

incident_description:

Once the burners are on, they stay on and continue to get hotter and hotter.  The only way to get the burners to turn off is to unplug the Stove. incident_description: MICROWAVE BEGINS TO RUN WHEN DOOR IS OPENED.  I HAVE A PACEMAKER AND IT SEEMS UNSAFE.
justification: The microwave running with the door open is an incident with no injury reported, but poses a potential risk, especially to someone with a pacemaker.

incident_description:
My wife and I were baking dinner this past Sunday when we noticed that our food was burned.  We thought maybe the temp was slightly off in our Kenmore oven so I read the manual on how to calibrated and adjusted it down by 35 degrees.  

This past Tuesday my 16 year old daughter was baking cookies and within 10 minutes there was smoke coming out of the oven and they were burnt.  She pulled them out of the oven and it was extremely hot.  The oven started beeping and giving an error code F10 but would not turn off or stop beeping.  My wife rushed home from work and the only way to turn off the oven was for her to trip the circuit breaker.  

I have read numerous complaints online that this is a serious problem with the 790 series ovens from Kenmore.  It is my opinion that this is a serious safety issue and that these ovens should be recalled before something serious happens or worse yet someone gets hurt.

The full model number of our Kenmore oven is 790.92709012
justification: The incident involved smoke and overheating without injury, and online complaints suggest this issue is likely to occur with this oven model.

incident_description:
Text of consumer's complaint received by Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade, and Consumer Protection on October 24, 2014:

Purchased 8-27-12. Magnetron failed and started sparking. Called company 11-9-2012 and they issued case# [REDACTED]. They sent a repair man to replace the magnetron. The microwave is sparking again and starting things on fire again. Company will send the magnetron to a service dealer, but say that I have to pay for all of the service costs. I feel this is a defect issue by the company with similar complaints on the internet. If it isn't part of a safety recall, it should be.

The magnetron should fail by not working instead of starting fires in the microwave. It can start sparking in 2 or 3 seconds with things like onions, potatoes, or oatmeal. I think the company should repair or issue a coupon for another microwave.

The manufacturer returned the purchase price of the product and the consumer's concerns with them have been resolved.
justification: The microwave's magnetron failure caused sparking and fires, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The report indicates the light switch or light circuit in the board failed.  The interior light bulbs located at the top of the refrigeration side of the unit remained on when the refrigerator door was closed.  The heat generated by the continuously lit bulbs led to the melting and charring of the plastic light fixture.  The light socket melted, the wiring harness melted into the socked assembly, light switch, and control panel.  The heat was intense enough to warp the Dairy Compartment clear plastic cover, some of the adjustable door bins, and the interior door liners.  Also, all food containers made from plastic such as salad dressing bottles, mustard, ketchup and mayonnaise, etc. were disfigured.  Of course all the contents from both the refrigerator and freezer had to be disposed.

Before leaving on an extended trip we have been following the instructions ÃÂpreparing for a vacationÃÂ listed on page 19 of the ownerÃÂs manual.  On our departure date the food that would not have lasted more than two weeks was removed from the refrigerator.  The ice bin was emptied and the wire shut off arm was raised to the OFF (O) position.  Note, page 19 does not mention to set the 
Sabbath mode when leaving for a short or long vacation. 

We were out of state from December 21, 2014 to January 2, 2015.  The condition of the refrigerator was discovered at about 9:30 PM on Saturday, January 2nd.  Upon opening the door the Dairy Compartment Cover fell to the floor.  We could immediately see the damage but did not know the source.  As a result, the unit was turned off.   The ownerÃÂs manual was consulted along with a review of the Dacor web site.   The office was closed on the weekend so Monday was the earliest we could obtain names of Dacor authorized repair agents in the Phoenix area.

Why did this happen?  A review of consumer appliance reviews, the Office of Consumer Affairs, and the US consumer Product Safety Commission web sites revealed there are numerous incidents similar to ours in which the interior lights stay on after the doors are closed.  In some cases, individuals were burned when the doors were opened; there was smoke damage, and even a fire.  We were fortunate.  The heat was contained within the refrigerator.  However, the Dacor technicians need to review the incident, find a solution, and notify consumers who have similar refrigerators about the potential danger.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the refrigerator and its contents but no injuries or fatalities were reported, aligning with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
Electrolux Icon Smooth Top Electric Cooking Range.  Tonight 2/5/15 we were cooking on the front left element.  We turned the element off - and the digitial display showed the "HE" symbol indicating it was warm, as normal.  We walked away from the stove top and returned within a few minutes and the digital display was rolling through/showing erradict numbers again and again while the knob was still in the off position.  Then the digital display stuck on "9" and the element began to heat up to full heat or even hotter.  Despite our attempts to turn off the element with the knob, the element remained red hot and the digital display just showed random numbers as we turned it.  We could not get the element to turn off.  After a period of time we eventually had to turn the breaker off for the stove on our main panel.  Once we had the stove off, we turned the breaker back on and the digital display now reads "ER."  

Obviously our concern is that this stove could turn itself back on to full heat while we are away from our home.  This is a clear fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was cooking bean chilli in a CrockPot brand slow cooker on their high setting for 6 Hours. We heard popping sounds coming from the kitchen but didn't see that the glass lid was cracking until I went to lift the lid from the pot. The handle came off in my hand and pieces of glass fell into the food. The latches on the cover were not closed and there was no sudden temperature change. It happen while cooking. The unit was used twice before and was only 2 days old. There was no injuries.
justification: The incident involved a cracked glass lid and handle failure, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the product was new and used correctly.

incident_description:

She turned the food item over to its other side and turned the burner knob to a low heat level. After a few minutes she noticed the food was burning. The consumer states the burner did not get red but got very hot. She left it on for a few seconds and turned the burner knob to the "off" position. The consumer used the stove top everyday. The consumer used the oven once every few weeks.

incident_description:
Whirlpool electric range in home when built in 2010/2011.

The caller had no problems with the range unit until July 2014 when he began noticing that the large heating element located at the right front of the range.
When it is set at low to simmer or cook slowly it will not remain at the set temperature, it keeps rising and remaining as hot as it can become.

incident_description:
We bought a gas range from Sears in October 2013.  Last fall (2014,) we began having problems with the range after I used the self-clean feature.  It was sooting when we turned the oven on, and shorting out when the temperature went over 375.

On the first repair visit, the Sears man cleaned out a ton of soot and told us the propane conversion had not been done properly.  

The propane man said it was all done properly. He cleaned out a ton of soot and said the burner was cracked. 

Sears replaced the burner on January 23.  Almost immediately we began again having the same problems.

On January 31another Sears repairman took the stove apart.  The new burner (one week old) was covered in soot.  He called his "technical people" who told him that with this particular model, (Kenmore 79074339310) there is an on-going, known problem where "the manufacturer's threads on bake and broil gas fitting spuds were not cut deep enough."

The repairman was working with some kind of tool and to "deepen the spuds", when the oven exploded, a fireball shot out and his pants caught on fire.  At that point, despite the fire, the Sears man's "technical people" told him to try "one more fix".  I refused, because I was frightened of another explosion.  I asked him to shut off the gas and unplug the stove.
justification: The incident involved an oven explosion and a repairman's pants catching fire, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I poured boiling water into a clear glass coffee mug that I purchased at Dollar Tree. I began to stir the water with a spoon to mix with the chai tea mix I had placed in the mug ahead of the hot water. As I began to stir, the mug exploded, cracking in half, and the hot water went all over the counter and splashed onto me, soaking my pants and burning my leg in the process. I did not place the mug in the microwave, I boiled the water in a separate container and only poured hot water into the mug, assuming that a coffee mug could handle a hot beverage.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from hot water splashing onto the leg, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
We have a 
Black & Decker Toaster Oven  approximately 5 to 7 years old.  Here are all the numbers on the bottom of the oven:  CAT. No. cto612ob  --  type1 -- miramar -- fl. 33027 --no.1335.1&1335.2.9 --
3099249.  This number is on the end of the cord that goes into outlet -- 747x0.

You turn the oven on, then when it is supposed to stop automatically, it keeps moving to the position of stay on.  which means the oven will then stay on until you shut it off, but if you put it to the off position, it will move again to stay on.  Therefore it will not turn off and it will stay on until it is unplugged.

We have tried numerous times to let it shut off by itself, but it will not.  So therefore  we feel like it would be a fire hazard.
justification: The toaster oven's failure to turn off poses a fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury if left unaddressed.

incident_description: When cooking, I had two Pyrex dishes of mine exploding when taking them from the oven. I wanted to get tips on what I should do about this or possibly a further investigation. I cut my foot on the glass and it was bleeding pretty badly making it difficult for me to walk. I have pictures of all of it.
justification: The incident caused a serious injury, making it a severity level 3.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern,
A Pyrex pan in use to bake a chicken exploded in my oven. It had been in a 375 degree oven for about half an hour and I was adding room temperature broth to the pan. It exploded with such force that glass shards were sent flying three feet across the room. It shocked me not only that it exploded but that the glass was in so many pieces and there were so many bits and shards to contend with after the fact.
Fortunately, I was not injured but the bits of glass were really tough to deal with. It was very difficult to get them up off the floor and out of the oven. In the oven, the liquid in the pan caused the glass to stick to the interior surface and I had to run an auto clean to burn off any residue so I could then be sure I got all the glass. The pieces were so tiny though that I don't know how anyone could really be sure they got it all.
[REDACTED]
justification: The Pyrex pan explosion caused no injury but created a significant cleanup issue, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description:
I own two Panasonic NN-SD967S Microwave ovens for a few years. Recently one of them broken down. When I opened up the oven, I observed that the wires from one connector is burned. It must be due to overheat on the connector. I took out the connector to examine. It is badly burned up. I was surprised, if the wires is not burned to the point that got it disconnected, it can cause fire.

I opened the other microwave oven of the same model, it is obvious that the same connector also got overheated, as the while wires that connected to it has turned black, although it is not disconnected.

The product is listed as consuming 1250W and the label on the unit says the input is 12.7A. However, when I measured both units, they took over 1900W and over 16.7 A.

I have pictures that can be included for investigation.
justification: The incident involves overheating and potential fire hazard in microwave ovens, but no injury or death was reported.

The unit turned off but after 1 minute the unit began to beep very loud. The consumer noticed the control panel displayed an error about the circuit board but she does not remember what exactly was on the control panel. The consumer pressed the clear button to stop the beeping noise. The unit would stop beeping for about 1 minute and then begin beeping. The consumer would press the clear button again and this repeated 3 times. 

The consumer unplugged the unit and waited for one minute. Then the consumer would plug the unit back in and the unit would immediately begin beeping. This repeated for about 3 times. The consumer has unplugged the unit and it has remained unplugged. 

The consumer uses the unit at least once a day.

I have a Hamilton Beach-brand slow cooker, model 33156SZ. I conducted slow-cooking for approximately 2 cups (soaked) of garbanzo beans, at low heat, over a period of six hours. I could not lift the lid by the handle, as the handle came detached from the lid. I had to remove the lid by holding the edges.

Neither myself nor anyone else was injured in this incident. The slow cooker had been on a "low" setting for six hours, and approximately 2 inches of water remained above the beans at the time of my checking the slow cooker. The beans were, however, ruined.

incident_description:
My wife and I moved into our current home in November, 2009.  The Maytag dishwasher in the home was there from the previous owner.  (Model #: MDB4651AWB)

In April, 2010 - we received a letter from Maytag/Whirpool indicating a recall on some dishwashers and stated that ours was of the affected units.  More information on this incident can be found at http://recall.maytag.com  - From the website: "Hazard: An electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element can pose a serious fire hazard."  We called the phone # from the letter and scheduled a date/time for a technician to service our dishwasher for a complimentary repair.

 They sent out a technician on 4/20/2010.  From the technician receipt, it states "Replaced heating element."

This past week, my wife and I noticed that the counter above our dishwasher was extremely hot.  However, we had not run the dishwasher in over 24 hours.  Reaching in the dishwasher to touch some of the dirty plates/glasses that remained in the washer, it was evident that they were scalding hot to the touch.  We called our local Maytag dealer/servicer, Miles Maytag of York, PA.

Miles Maytag sent a technician over on 1/26/2015.  The technician noted that our heating element was not turning off and was extremely hot.  As noted on the "Service performed" receipt -- "120V to heater constantly.  Shut off at breaker: safety issue".  The technician stated that the issue was an extreme safety hazard and we were "very lucky you didn't have a fire."  He reported that the cost to fix the dishwasher (including parts/labor) would be over $300.  Not to mention the fact that we were charged $78.97 for the technician to come out and look at the defective machine.

At this point, we have the circuit breaker turned off for the dedicated circuit that powers the dishwasher as it is an extreme fire/electrical hazard.  I was urged by [REDACTED], the service manager at Miles Maytag to contact Whirpool corporate.  I called Whirlpool corporate and explained my issue.  I explained to a customer service representative that they had services my dishwasher in 2010 to repair a defective heating element.  However, this clearly did not fix the problem and I am lucky that their defective part did not cause a fire in my home.  The customer service representative stated that there was nothing they could do for me as they already issued a repair for the recall and they are only authorized to do that one time. 

I asked to speak to a manager.  A manager from Maytag/Whirlpool explained to me that they are authorized to perform one recall repair, after which time "any further problems are the consumer's responsiblity."  In pleading my case, I asserted that it may be due to negligence/error on the part of the 2010 technician, or simply an issue with defective parts/machinery.  However, their so-called recall "repair" did not truly repair the issue, and a major electrical/fire hazard remained.  Regardless, the manager stated that there was simply nothing she could do, except to extend an offer to purchase a new Maytag dishwasher (an offer which I politely declined).

I feel that Whirlpool should be held responsible for providing a defective product that caused a clear safety hazard.  They claim no liability in this matter.  Thank you for your assistance.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer's range is included in recall #09-333.

The consumer stated that he turned on the front left element on the cooktop and put a pot of soup. The consumer then turned on the broiler. The consumer stated that the control panel on his electric range caught on fire within seconds of starting the broiler. The consumer reported flames as high as 6-8 inches across the back of the range. The consumer was able to pull out the range and unplug it. The consumer stated that he had to use fire extinguisher to extinguish the flames.

The consumer reported melting on the back of the range. 

The consumer stated that his rear-left element had randomly self started two times previously. The consumer would have to cut the circuit breaker to the range to turn off the range.

The consumer stated that he called the manf on 11/22/14. The consumer also e-mailed the manf regarding the incident on 11/24/14. 

The consumer had a technician come out inspect the range. They informed him that timer clock EOC had malfunctioned and started the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire that required extinguishing but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On 11/30/14 the consumer used the unit for about 1 minute and a half to heat up a cup of water. When he took his cup of water out and closed the door he states the unit turned back on. He states the unit was not set for more time and that it ran for about 30 seconds. The consumer states that it has occurred about 6 times in the past week. He states the unit will begin running by itself without anyone touching it. Also when he placed his hand on the door it began running. He states it normally runs for approximately 30 seconds every time. 

On 11/30/14 the consumer called the firm but was not able to speak with anyone. He then called the retailer but they were closed. 

On 12/01/14 the consumer has contacted the retail store and spoke with [REDACTED]. The consumer advised [REDACTED] of the incident and [REDACTED] advised the consumer she would call him back. [REDACTED] informed the consumer that she spoke with the firm and there was no recall on the unit. [REDACTED]advised the consumer that the problem was 2 switches that need to be replaced and the repairs would cost the consumer $164. 

The consumer has not had the unit repaired or had any problems before.

After contacting CPSC the consumer called GE repair and they sent out a repair person.  He determined that it was probably a door switch problem.  He ordered the door switches and a new board.  When it arrived (the parts) another service person came out and determined that only the switches needed replacement.  He also realigned the door and it has worked without mishap since.  [REDACTED]
justification: The unit malfunctioned by turning on by itself multiple times, but no injury or harm was reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his electric oven broil mode comes on without the unit being powered on.  This has been ongoing for the past 3 weeks, he has to power it off from the circuit breaker.

12/5 -12/9 The manufacturer was contacted and he was transferred to a lot of departments but no one was willing to assist him with this issue.  He was also informed that his range was not part of a recall although it displays similar problems of Recall#09-333.Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

Caller is concerned that this oven poses a fire hazard which can cause a house fire and feels that it should be recalled.
justification: The oven's broil mode activating without power poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Glass electric cooktop with burners that come on by themselves. I thought my husband was exaggerating until I read other reviews online with the same reports with some terrible outcomes!
Fridgidaire model number fec30s6asf
justification: The cooktop turning on by itself poses a fire hazard and potential injury risk, as indicated by multiple reports.

incident_description: The microwave caught on fire while not in use.  We were in the room at the time, and saw it within seconds so there was no damage to anything other than the microwave.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was noticed immediately, causing no injury or damage beyond the appliance itself.

incident_description: I was using my Ninja Professional Blender (Model BL660) to blend frozen fruit and milk. This blender was purchased on or around August 2014 from BJ's Wholesale Club and was being used as it has been each day since purchasing. After blending for approximately 10 seconds,  the right side of the blender exploded out, and shot about 8 feet across my kitchen landing next to the table where my 2 children were eating breakfast. There were 2 separate pieces that were approximately 2" and 4", with razor sharp edges. The contents of the blender were sprayed across my kitchen out of this opening. Needless to say, I am EXTREMELY concerned about this product and have contacted Ninja twice regarding this matter. I have not yet heard back from their claims department. I took several pictures of the blender following the incident that can be provided if necessary.
justification: The blender exploded, but no injuries were reported, only property damage and a hazardous situation.

incident_description: The glass in my oven exploded kitchen aid claim no responsibility I feel its a safety issue.  It seems to be a common problem on the repair fourms.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass explosion with no reported injury, and it appears to be a recurring issue based on repair forums.

incident_description: I picked a metal shard out of my mouth that broke off of the Veggetti Spiral Cutter that I used to prepare a salad. There is a metal piece missing from my spiral cutter that should be held in by the plastic portion of the tool. This design flaw could have been extremely dangerous if metal piece was swallowed. I am infuriated of the internal damaged this could have caused!!! I have pictures of my product and the missing piece from it. This is the web site for the company: http://www.buyveggetti.com
justification: The incident involved a metal shard breaking off but no injury occurred, though there was potential for harm.

incident_description:
On 11/13/14 the consumer was using the unit to heat a potatoe. The unit was set for 3 minutes. Before the 3 minutes were up the consumer noticed the inside of the unit was on fire. The consumer put out the fire and took the unit outside. 

The consumer has not had any problems or incidents with the unit. The consumer uses the unit about 5-6 times a day. 

The unit came with the house. The home is 3 years old. The consumer has been in the home for 6 weeks. 

There were no property damages. The inside of the unit is black and mildly burned. The unit will not turn on. 

The consumer plans to contact the firm after filing this report.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or property damage, and the unit is no longer functional.

incident_description:
10/2014 Consumer stated that the gas company had came out and tested for CO and the levels were very high around 560 which is emitting from the gas oven.   The oven emits CO whenever the oven is turned on. 10/2014 She contacted the repair service (A&E appliance) and someone was sent out, she stated that he informed her had he known it was about CO, they would not have came out.  She was told to contact the manufacturer.  She contacted the manufacturer and she was informed by an agent that she would need a CO detector, however, she did not receive any from the company and she has been calling back since but is unable to speak to someone.


The gas oven is in a rental home that she rented to her tenant, the tenant has a small child and she is concerned for their safety.  Consumer is frustrated that she has been complaining about the range and is unable to get a replacement or repair to the issues she is having.  This incident started around early October 2014.  Caller feels that the gas range is unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves high CO levels from a gas oven, posing a serious risk to the tenant and child, though no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Mr. Coffee maker with stainless steel carafe apparently has a manufacturing problem with the brew basket that can result in hot coffee being released at the bottom of the basket when the carafe is removed.  The "button" and spring at the bottom of the basket is poorly made and comes off easily so the stream of coffee continues if the carafe is removed during brewing to pour a cup.  I've tried to find a replacement part and it is not available.  At various sites I've found similar complaints, including the Mr. Coffee replacement parts site.  Apparently these break often and no one seems to be able to find a solution. 

It's a minor thing that it's an expensive coffee maker; the major problems are the real possibility of being burned (to say nothing of the mess created) and the unavailability of a solution.
justification: The incident can result in hot coffee being released, which can cause burns, but there is no injury reported.

incident_description: We have purchased a Sears Kenmore Dishwasher 665-13963KD13.  Repeatedly the top rack which is poorly made has cheap plastic male part on the rack that holds the wheels of the rack on.  There is too much give side to side movement that causes these cheap plastic clips to break and thus the wheel falls off causing the rack to fall off.  The incident that occurred involved my 7 year old who was helping me unload the dishwasher when the top rack fell and caused the glasses to break and get glass inside dishwasher and on floor
justification: The incident caused a minor injury to the 7 year old, but no serious harm was done.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his spouse had placed the dishwasher into cycle and approximately 20 mins later the smoke detector alerted him.  He noticed that smoke had started to engulf the kitchen and flames were erupting from the the control panel of the unit, he contained the fire with the extinguisher.  The circuit breaker was used to switch the power off.  He contacted the fire department after this was done and they came out disconnected the dishwasher and removed it out of the house.

(1/10/15) The manufacturer was contacted and they informed him that they could provide a 10 % discount to another dishwasher.

Consumer feels that this dishwasher could have caused a house fire if no one was present and should be reported.
justification: The incident caused a fire and could have caused a house fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have a 3 year old kenmore elite range,model #790.97503000, while roasting a dinner i heard a load bang and found that the oven racks had fallen spilling the entire contents on the bottom of the oven. The racks no longer stay in place, rendering the oven useless. After researching the oven I found that there are many complaints on line( some involving personell injury and or fire) yet Sears and Kemore refuse to acknowledge that a problem exists.
justification: The incident involved oven racks falling, causing a mess but no injury, and there are reports of similar incidents with potential for injury or fire.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Electric Double oven purchased November 2013. The first time we used the self cleaning cycle the glass in the door shattered after about 45 minutes into a 3 hour cycle. It was the inner glass, but it sprayed glass out the bottom into the room.The oven was not particularly dirty and there was little spilled on the floor of the chamber. The glass in the door only had whatever food vapors had settled on it.

I guess the glass was defective or installed improperly and perhaps stressed from the heat.

I contacted Whirlpool but they did not seem concerned.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) as such defects are not common but have been documented.

incident_description: After I washed the lid of my Rival Crock Pot Stoneware Slow Cooker Model 64451 I placed it on top of a pot to air dry.  Within 5 minutes it completely shattered sending glass everywhere into a bunch of pieces.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of a slow cooker lid, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller's mother was in kitchen preparing her breakfast this morning December 18th, 2014, she placed waffles in her four slice toaster oven purchased just the day before.

The farthest piece of glass was scattered over the entire distance of the caller's mother's kitchen floor.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the inner glass oven door exploded while in a cleaning mode approximately 30 mins later.    She stated that she read online that the manufacturer is not taken any responsibilities for the issues at hand.

Caller feels that the gas oven is a safety hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description: The consumer and her husband were at home one evening. They heard several popping noises from the GE electric oven in the kitchen. Then they heard a loud "boom," and the oven exploded in fire. The house was partially destroyed by fire and has smoke damage throughout.
justification: The oven explosion caused significant property damage but no mention of injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
The outer glass panel on my oven door shattered for no apparent reason.  I was cut on the face and hands. What remains of the oven still presents a danger to me and my kids.  The remedy I seek is a replacement door, installed by a professional.  The oven was not used in any unusual manner; nor was it abused in any fashion.  Please review the events below and the attached photos.
Model# FES 365 ESA
Serial# NF52907731
A copy of this complaint is being forwarded to the CPSC.

Thurs., Jan 15 2015

Went to the stove to open the oven.  As I began to pull the door open, the outer glass panel on the oven door suddenly shattered, covering the floor and my feet with broken glass.  A few pieces remained attached to the upper frame.  One piece dislodged and fell between my glasses and cheek as I was trying to read the serial and model #s on the inside frame of the oven.  (See photos)


I called customer service about 20 min. later.  The first rep advised there was nothing Electrolux/Frigidaire could do because the oven is no longer under warranty.  I requested to escalate call to a supervisor.  Was transferred to [REDACTED].  After review, she advised Electrolux could offer a 30 %  discount on replacement parts and also started a liability claim regarding my cuts caused by the broken glass.  I advised her that due to the severity of this incident that  I expected Electrolux to replace the door free of charge.  Loss of function after the warranty period is expected, exploding glass doors are not.

I requested further escalation, [REDACTED] advised that there was no higher level.  She gave me the mailing address for corporate offices and advised me that the liability claims dept would be in contact & possibly be of more assistance.
Incident # [REDACTED]
Liability claim# [REDACTED]
[REDACTED] contact # [REDACTED]

It took me 3 hrs to clean up the glass.  I found pieces of glass as far as 6 ft from the oven and am still finding stray pieces.  I had several small cuts to my fingers during cleanup.  There is a strip of jagged glass still attached to the frame which will require force to remove.  I have not attempted to pull it off because I do not wish to further injure myself.  However, leaving the strip of glass as it is also presents a hazard.  I have no idea how to proceed with the situation.

 Wed Jan. 21, 2015
Was contacted by [REDACTED] from Electrolux liability claims dept. I told her what happened and that I need a replacement oven door.  She reviewed the file and my account of the incident and advised me that since the warranty was expired that Electrolux could do nothing.  I advised that I would contact the Consumer Protection Agency regarding the matter.

I do not understand why this product has not been placed on recall. I am aware that similar incidents have happened to others with Electrolux/Frigidaire ranges and am prepared to contact the news media in order to warn other consumers about this product
justification: The incident resulted in cuts to the face and hands, indicating an injury, and the remaining glass presents ongoing danger.

incident_description: I brewed a cup of coffee with my Mini Keurig and it spewed coffee all over the counter. It only happened one time and I assumed it was a faulty K-cup.
justification: The incident involved a coffee spill with no injury, and it was a one-time occurrence likely due to a faulty K-cup.

incident_description:
GE Electric Range/Oven Model # JBP26GV2AD  Serial# RM224176G

Heard loud buzzing noise while standing next to oven and turned to see sparks shooting from under bottom edge of oven door and smoke rising from the vent at the right rear burner.  Turned oven off (it was empty and was still pre heating) and bright flickering light and sparking noise was visible through view glass in door.  Opened door to see a constant bright white burn on upper element with sparks continuing to shoot from that same spot on the upper right element.  With door open, sparks shot out of the door towards us and burnt small place on kitchen rug.  Also noticed what appears to be slag that had dripped from element to oven floor.  It very much resembled a tig or mig welder the way the element was burning and arcing.  Element continued to burn white hot and spark continuously even 5 minutes after cutting oven control to off.  I had someone turn off the breaker for the oven at the house electric panel, which caused the bright burn to immediately stop, ceasing all noise and sparking.  Element now appears to be melted across 2.5 inches, and is completely burned through in one spot where there is now just a gap in the element.

I understand that the element is now bad, but what I don't understand is how this electrical arcing can continue after the power control to the oven has been turned off unless there is a defect in the control or the way it's wired.  Obviously during this condition the element is still getting power despite the controls, but up until this point, the oven obviously didn't heat when it was powered off with the front control panel knob.

My concern is that if the element is getting power even when turned off, this condition could happen at any time, including when we are asleep or away from the house, and could ultimately cause the fire to spread beyond the oven and to the house itself causing property damage, injury, or potentially even loss of life.

This is the 2nd time weÃÂve had this happen as we had this happen on the bottom element last year as well.  Again the arcing and burn would not extinguish until we turned off the house breaker, and it immediately ceased upon turn the house breaker off.

I have video and photos of the incident while the fire was in progress and after it was extinguished.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a small burn on a rug, but no injury or death. The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a likely defect.

incident_description:
Saturday, 27 December 2014, my Day Shift Sergeant called me to advise he had to call the fire department out to our police station because of a smoke / odor investigation.  It was discovered that the newly purchased microwave had overheated without anyone using it.

The FD used the thermal on the wiring & our electric dept came out & checked the outlet.  It is working fine & showed no heat signature.  The back of the microwave had brown scorching around the fan vent area & the thermal heat signature showed just above 150 degrees.  Again, it was confirmed no one had been using the microwave for approx. 5 hours.

The microwave was purchased on 10/17/2014.  It is a Hamilton Beach model # P100N30AP-F4 with a serial # of: F40816E00680.  

While in a business setting, it is normally only used 3-5 times daily & not for very long.

Monday, 29 December 2014, @ approx. 08:30 hrs, I contacted Hamilton Beach Customer Service (800-267-6419) to advise them of the problem.  I spoke to operator [REDACTED] who advised he had not received any notification or complaints about this particular model of microwave & to just take it back to the store.
justification: The microwave overheated without use, causing scorching but no injuries or further damage.

incident_description:
The Blendtec Wildside Blender jar exploded while I was operating it in my kitchen on Monday, January 12, 2015.  
I purchased the Blendtec from Costco approximately two years ago. I make a protein shake every morning with the following ingredients:  ice, water, zucchini, spinach, beet, carrot, small baby cucumber, banana, frozen berries, and protein powder.
I generally ÃÂpulseÃÂ the shake a number of times, to cut up the big pieces, and then press the button for ÃÂwhole juiceÃÂ or ÃÂcrush ice/shakes.ÃÂ  I did that on January 12, and, within a few seconds of putting the machine on ÃÂcrush ice/shakes,ÃÂ (my hand was still on the lid), the jar exploded with a ferocity that sounded like a bomb going off.  It just so happened that the side of the jar which exploded was facing the windows in my kitchen and the wall.  My arm was in front of the jar, so it ÃÂbrokeÃÂ the explosion a bit from spreading even further.  My arm was covered with a thick, fuzzy jacket, so the plastic and food hitting me did not cause any harm.  Unfortunately, in addition to the walls, floors and everything in range, my bench seat (with custom made cushions, one chair cushion, and one of my two blinds in the kitchen were covered with the contents of the shake.   

Of great concern, of course, are the safety issues.  As is obvious to me, if the rupture had been on the side where I was standing, the plastic pieces could very well have exploded onto my face.  The plastic pieces, are shaped like shards of glass ÃÂ with sharp points.  With the force of this explosion, and an unlucky spin of the plastic, an eye could have been lost.  This is the gravest apprehension I have with continuing to use the Blendtec.  

I also have great concern that the manufacturer told me they were "sorry," sent me a new Blender Wildside jar and did not explain why the jar exploded.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it could have caused serious injury, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: My Fagor Dishwasher (model LFA-86XL) had a heating element that shorted and caught fire. This has has happened twice. The first time it happened (in the first year of ownership), Fagor's warranty covered a repair. It happened again recently. Both occurrences happened with normal use of the dishwasher.

incident_description:
Baking a cake at 325 degrees.  Placed cake in oven when it came to temperature, not 2 minutes later the oven dinged again.  There was an error message (E3 and F?) and suddenly a pop and fire from the broiler which shouldn't have been on.  I pulled the plug, the smoke alarm was off, there was acrid smoke. incident_description: Pyrex Storage 6-Cup Rectangular Dish broken when we took it out of oven and put on countertop.
justification: The incident was a broken dish, which is not a serious incident, but it was an incident.

incident_description:
purchased GE convection microwave (model JVM1790) in July 2007. I have not had any issues with it until today. After cooking in it tonight, after it was off and I took the food out, closed the door, the microwave starting humming. I opened the door and the humming stopped. I closed the door and it started again. Then with the door closed and humming, there was a small fire/spark starting in the upper right side. This microwave is only 6 years old and it catches on fire when off. We immediately unplugged it and thankfully the small flame went out.  I will now have to pay $90 for GE to come out just to determine what is wrong. This is completely wrong. When their product fails and catches fire, they should be responsible. Fortunately, I was home when this happened so I could unplug it and no further damage was done as far as I know. Of course that may change after this microwave is taken down. 
I am reporting this as this could have had a very serious outcome.

incident_description:
Microwave oven, not in use, self-started on it's own!
In the middle of the night it made keypad beeping sounds and then started up.
It is a Magic Chef Model MCO160UB, Serial Number DJ07X02148, manufactured in October 2007.
The company said it would send a replacement keypad and a repairman to install the keypad.
This is very scary. There could have been a fire if we were not home to turn it off.
There should probably be a recall of these products.
justification: The microwave self-started without use, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased a few months back a set  of Pyrex glass containers. They were only used for food storage until my wife used one to cook a casserole. It was placed in the oven at 350 for around 45' and then removed and placed on top of the stove to cool. From another room, we heard a loud crashing noise and upon entering the kitchen were shocked to see that the bowl had shattered and exploded glass shards  all over the stove and adjacent areas. 
I contacted the manufacturer through their website and filed an online form. I assumed they would want to know about this. I never received a response. I then tried calling their "customer care number" as listed on their website. All I ever get is a recording saying your wait time it 30' and to call back.

justification: The rotisserie exploded, causing glass shards to fly, but no one was injured as the kitchen was empty.

incident_description:
Our Whirlpool refrigerator caught fire in the ice maker.  While we slept at night, something seemed to explode in the freezer.  By the time we got woke up and came in, we assumed it was the ice maker dropping ice, as it is usually loud.  
In the morning, we were overwhelmed with a gas-like smell.  When I found the smell originating from the freezer, I opened it and everything was black.  There was a large hole in the ceiling of the freezer, and melted plastic throughout the upper section of the freezer.  
What really concerns me the most is that the seal was almost completely burned through.  If it had continued through that seal, it would have easily spread to our wood cabinets directly above the fridge, and throughout our home--as we slept.  
Ultimately, we contacted Whirlpool who sent out a repairman.  He determined that the fire started in the ice maker, not the relay switch as we assumed (after reading about all of the recalls from Whirlpool and Maytag previously due to relay switches catching fire).  I can only trust that we were told the truth about what started the fire.  
However, in any case, an ice maker should not be the cause of a fire inside your fridge, especially not a well-respected name brand like Whirlpool who is all too familiar with freezer fires.
We were also told by Whirlpool that the side by side model we have is made to contain the fire inside. In our case, this was true, but this was only by luck I believe.  I will be attaching pictures showing the freezer's seal almost completely burned through.  
 
Thank you for your attention to this matter.
justification: The refrigerator fire caused significant damage but no injuries or deaths, and the fire was contained by design.

incident_description:
Product:
Maytag Dishwasher about 10 years old
Mod: MDBD880AWB
SER 27368521AE

E39927

incident_description:
Caller's daughter purchased a GE range approximately 18 months ago.

They are having problems with the knobs on her gas range which turn on very easily.

The caller is reporting that if a person just rubs past or is reaching over the range the knobs turn at times and begin releasing gas but do not ignite.

He said that this has happened a few times and that just recently the dog walker came into the home and smelled gas then turn it off.

There are no known injuries at this time 

The caller contacted the manufacturer on December 4th, 2014 and he was advised that a service technician would be sent to the home December 9th, 2014.

The caller will update this report with the technician's statements before he returns it.

1.  At 1:30 on Dec 9th G.E. Technician ([REDACTED] stopped by the caller's daughter's residence, the caller explained to him the problem.  He operated several of the knobs on the range.  He said without hesitation that there was nothing he could do about it, that it was a problem with the design of the knobs.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the capresso machine spontaneously turns on by itself.  The caller stated that since purchase she has had 4 replacements and they displayed the same problem.  She has had these replacements within a year.  The machine has to be unplugged to prevent this incident from occurring.  She stated that the heating plate has a failure as well.

(12/2014) She contacted the company and they informed her that they were not aware of these problems.

Caller feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The machine spontaneously turning on poses a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Why on vacation at The Hilton Garden Inn in New Orleans. I started the pot to brewing and walked away about 6 ft. I heard a spewing sound, when I turned around it had spewed hot water out on the floor about 3 ft in distance. I was thankful that I was not in front of it because I had just gotten out of the shower.
justification: Hot water spewed out but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
My three year old Frigidaire Professional electric cook top suddenly turned on with no user input. One of the burners came on spontaneously, even though all knobs were in the Off position. The digital readout for the burner was erratic, and the burner knob would not control the burner; i.e. the burner went to Hi, even when the knob was turned to Lo, and the knob would not turn off the burner.  I had to trip the circuit breaker to turn the cook top off.  The next day, I turned the breaker back on, and after about 2 hours, the same thing happened again. I had to turn the breaker off to turn the burner off.

I reported this to Frigidaire, but the customer service rep had no knowledge of similar occurrences. Since the product is out of warranty and there is no current recall, Frigidaire accepts no responsibility.
justification: The cooktop malfunctioned spontaneously, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Our GE Built-In Oven Model JTP15W0A1WW was in preheat and we experienced a loud pop and a fire.  We immediately turned the unit off with no impact to the fire.  I then used the fire extinguisher with no results of reducing the fire.  After throwing the main breaker the fire finally went out.  GE has been contacted and sent out a rep to make sure the oven would work after the element was replaced.  They have not requested the part and have been less than interested in the fact that the only resolution to stopping the fire was by throwing the main breaker (not by stopping power to the unit).
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported, and the fire was eventually extinguished without further damage.

incident_description:
On or about Jan. 06, 2015, we were cooking on our GE gas range. During the activation of the front burner, we witnessed a popping sound with the stove, causing the power to go out with the stove. We
had to reset the breaker. We tried the stove again, but the burner was not working and a strong smell of gas was being detected. We gave the stove one more try, but now a strong smell of burning rubber was detected. At this point, we called Sears for service. Our product was still under warranty, in fact it was only 6 months old. The technician discovered a burnt wire in one of the burners and later replaced the wire. So far, we continue to use the stove and no further problems have occurred. The model# is
JGV650SEF1SS and the serial# is TA130085P.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove with a burnt wire and gas smell, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I received an email from Amazon  where I purchased the Keurig K10/B31 MINI Plus Brewing System, Black. The machine DID NOT cause any physical harm because when hot water started coming our of the dispenser I was not handling it as such but  there was hot water. This does not happen all the time. I thought that when it happened that it was dirty so I cleaned it but it happen while cleaning it and shortly after it was clean. Actually it seems to be very temperamental. Not having this item before I thought perhaps it was normal or that I was putting more water than its capacity.
justification: The incident involved hot water release without physical harm, indicating an incident with no injury. The issue is intermittent, suggesting a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Oven Model 790.980223800. Serial # NF84507096.
Right front burner was set to low heat setting of 1.5, while cooking soup. Pot boiled over due to sudden temperature increase. The unit was out of control and poses an extreme fire threat due to defective circuit board. The push button controls would not function. Indicator LED readout for this burner read OFF, while the burner "eye" continued a rapid temperature acceleration to levels not designed for routine cooking.

Local appliance repair isolated this incident to a faulty circuit board.
justification: The incident caused a fire threat, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I just had a glass baking dish explode over my entire oven. I had pasta in the dish, which I placed into an oven heating up to 350 degrees. After a few minutes of being in the oven it just exploded. It was my first time using this particular baking dish.
justification: The baking dish exploded but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: I was processing peeled garlic. The food processor began to vibrate and then made a loud noise and stopped. Removed the lid and found the blade had broken (an entire "fin" had broken from the riveted area) and lodged itself deeply into the side of the workbowl, and the food was peppered with broken metal and plastic shards.

incident_description: Electrical fire in dishwasher.  Bosch model SHX53T55UC/01, bought new from Lowe's Home Center (Austin, TX) on 08-13-13 and installed professionally. Big concern is that the kitchen and house could have caught fire (scary scenario, as we have small kids).

incident_description: The Product was throwing out hot liquids from an area that shouldn't be having liquids come out of it. Its very unsafe and are just thankful nobody was injure or hurt in anyway.

incident_description: I put my 15x10 pyrex pan into a 400 degrees oven - it was filled with scalloped potatoes. I had warmed the milk before pouring it over the potatoes. I covered the pan with tin foil, with the intention of taking off the tin foil halfway through to sprinkle cheese on top. After 10-15 minutes in the oven, the pan (really) exploded. I have a picture of the exploded pan

incident_description: while pouring hot tea into a Teavana Kiran double wall insulate tea glass the inner glass imploded. Due to the fact the glass is vacuum sealed the glass filled the chamber and didn't fly out of the glass. the teavana item # is 30516 000 014, Kiran Glass. This item was purchased in July 2014.
