incident_description: I would like to report an incident with my pyrex glass 2-cup measuring cup that was sitting on the counter.  The cup had been used to measure some dry ingredients, but had not been in contact with any liquids for at least the entire day, had not been exposed to any heat, and had not been bumped against any surface.  All of a sudden it just exploded, leaving the base of the cup intact but with multiple hairline cracks and the rest in pieces and shards. Fortunately, I was far enough away and was not cut.  I discovered on youtube a similar incident of a gentleman who had taken a similar pyrex measuring cup out of the cupboard (not bumping it) and it exploded in his hand covering his arm with shards.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass measuring cup but no injuries occurred, and similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Elite dishwasher (Model number 66512776K310) in March of 2014.  Last week, the top rack failed and nearly came crashing down full of dishes.  The failure is due to the small plastic prongs which hold the top rack in place.  These prongs have cracked off in several places.  I tried to order replacement parts from Sears and was told by two different representatives that they no longer make the part.  This seems strange since it is a pretty new machine.  They are going to send a repair technician out to look at the dishwasher in 2 weeks time.  I asked how the technician would fix the machine, since they no longer make the part.  I was told that the technician would be able to fix it.  Hmmm.  Seemed suspicious to me, so I did some research online and found that many, many consumers have had the same exact problem - many have posted pictures showing exactly the same broken plastic prongs.  I believe Sears and/or Whirlpool (the manufacturer) know that they have a defective part, which is why they no longer make this particular part.  If you google the part number ( W10350376 ), you will find a lot of dissatisfied customers.  Many tell stories of how they were charged for service calls and/or parts that are supposed to be under warranty. There is plenty of evidence that the part is defective (becomes brittle and cracks off because it is not capable of withstanding the high temperatures in the machine) and that they are aware of it (they discontinued making and selling this particular part).  It seems obvious to me that Sears/Whirlpool should be forced to recall any dishwasher with this defective part.
justification: The incident involves a defective part causing the dishwasher rack to fail, but no injury or death was reported. The issue is common among many customers, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: The crockpot was turned on low and left to cook overnight, the lid was not locked in place. In the morning when I entered the kitchen the crockpot lid had been shattered and was still on top of the crockpot. Glass shards had fallen down into the food being cooked.
justification: The incident involved a shattered crockpot lid and glass shards in the food, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:

The consumer asked to have a shipping label sent out so she can return the unit for them to inspect. They kept asking her to discard the unit. The consumer is still waiting to receive the shipping label.

The consumer stated that the manf did not seem interested in detecting the issue of the unit since they kept asking her to throw it away. The consumer is worried that if someone does not realize that the unit fails to shut off, it can cause a fire.

After a cool down period of about three hours we turned the electric and gas back on. The electric starter for the griddle came on on its own and so did the gas without us touching the knobs. All knobs were in the off position. We immediately shut the breaker off and the gas valve. GE service has not responded yet.

Dual fuel range burned pancakes during use & the griddle knob when turned to low remained extremely hot. When the units knobs were turned off the burners remained on & caused 4 tiles behind the stove to fall off. The electric & gas was shut down & then turned on when

The Electric griddle burner knob on the dual fuel range was turned low during use but it stayed extremely hot & caused 4 tiles behind the stove to fall off the wall. When power was shut off to the unit & turned on back again the electric & gas burners came on by themselves.

incident_description:
I have a GE stove Model: JGBS60DEFBB, Serial No:VD123164.  The stove was delivered to my home on Dec. 3, 2014.  
The stove has a defect that allows the gas to be turned on without first pushing in the knob.  The knob does not retract due to an interference fit with the bezel.  Twice, within the first three days of delivery, the knob was bumped and the house smelled of gas until we caught that the gas was turned on part way, evidently due to being bumped,  Then I looked into the problem and discovered the interference fit that was causing the problem.
A GE repair person arrived Dec. 15, agreed with me, and ordered a new manifold and a new bezel.
The new manifold and bezel arrived Dec. 19 and they are identical to those on my stove, so the replacement was not completed.  
Stove display units in our local Home Depot have the same problem and the department manager agrees that there is a problem with the design or manufacture of the stove.  The manager called GE and talked to somebody who said that there is no design problem.
Frankly, I believe that this stove has a design error such that the manifold is mounted well below the bezel hole center line.  This can (and in my case does) cause binding of the control knob so that the knob spring cannot eject the knob into the lock position.
Twice, within the 3 days after purchase, we bumped the knob (that was stuck in the ÃÂin positionÃÂ) and later returned to discover serious gas odors in the kitchen.  After finding the problem source, I taped the knob and I have been trying to address the problem through GE and Home Depot, but there is no indication that the problem is being addressed.  Needless to say, we are glad that we discovered this before we had an explosion.  
I have used the channels suggested to me with no satisfaction and I will not stop until I have an acceptable solution.  In other words, I will not accept a stove that has marginal clearance of the rear burner knobs.  The front burners, by the way, are fine because their bezel openings are, for some reason, 10 mm larger than the rear burner openings.  So, even though the center lines are not centered, there is no interference fit.
After repeated calls to GE, all I hear is that GE engineering is working on this.  Meanwhile, I need to keep the burner control knob from accidentally turning on and filling my house with gas.
I want to prevent explosions both in my home and in the homes of others who bought this appliance.
Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The defect allows gas to leak when the knob is bumped, posing a risk of gas exposure, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:

incident_description:
I was pre-heating my oven when I noticed my oven was on fire. The heat element was on fire and disintegrating. There were flames in the oven and I couldn't get them to stop until I went into my basement and powered down all the electricity to my house. 
I called the customer service number and they took a report  and asked me to email pictures of the fire- which I did. They promised a call back within 2 business days. When the call came in the department said that because there wasn't further damage to anything other than my oven they needed to refer me back to customer service. I contacted customer service and the customer service wasn't able to offer assistance. I asked to speak with a supervisor. I spoke with [REDACTED] and she said the stove wasn't under warranty and they couldn't help. I reiterated my concern that Frigidaire is aware that there is an issue with the heating element and it did cause a fire so I wanted it rectified.  She said if I paid for a repairman with my own expense and if they declared that the stove (mind you it is burnt to a crisp) is fixable then they would consider giving me a 20% on replacement parts. I expressed my dissatisfaction and I am pursuing a formal complaint. the stove is unsafe and would have caused a house fire if I was not in the Kitchen when the flames erupted and I took immediate action.

incident_description: I was making coffee, as usual, per the product instructions. The machine started shattering and hot water kind of shot out. I thought that I should clean the machine, so I did. It hasn't happened since, but I didn't know how/where to let someone know, so I just let it go. I didn't know other people had the same issue.

incident_description:
On 12/25/14 the consumer heard a loud explosion in the kitchen. She walked in the kitchen and noticed the glass oven door had shattered. The consumer states the last time she used the unit was on 12/24/14. The consumer used the oven on 12/24/14 for about an hour.

The consumer has not contacted the firm but plans to contact them.  

The consumer states she has not had any prior incidents. 

The are no other damages to the range other than the shattered glass or property damages.

incident_description:
The consumer is filing a report on his refrigerator which he feels is not safe and poses a fire hazard. 

On 11/26/14 the consumer opened the unit and he smelled a plastic burn odor. He noticed that the thermostat was hanging and the brackets that hold the thermostat had melted. The consumer contacted Sears and advised them of the incident. Sears arranged for a technician to examine the unit on 11/28/14. The repairs were done at no charge to the consumer. 

On 11/28/14 (estimated) the technician examined the unit and advised the consumer that the 2 bulbs located on the top inside of the unit failed to turn off causing the brackets to melt. The technician advised the consumer that this problem occurs with 1 in 40 similar units. The technician advised the consumer that a repair kit would be ordered and should arrive within 3 days. The consumer was advised that the unit would be repaired after the parts arrive. 

The technician removed the 2 bulbs in the unit and informed the consumer to keep checking the temperature so it does not go above 37 degrees. The consumer states that when the door is opened often the unit's temperature goes up and he has to manually reset it. The consumer states this occurs at least 3 times a week. 

The consumer has not had prior incidents. 

The consumer states he has contacted Sears 3-4 times in the past month to try and have the unit repaired but he has been getting the run around. The consumer has been told repeatedly that the repair kit has not arrived and someone from the parts department will call him back when the repair kit arrives. 

The consumer is upset that this problem is a common issue and there has not been a recall. The consumer does not feel safe using the unit and would prefer to have it replaced.

incident_description:
On Saturday, January 17, 2015, I was baking cookies in the oven of my Kenmore Range, Model 665.95802, SN # RK 4431605 when the following incident occurred. 
I selected bake and selected my temperature at 375 degrees.  The oven went into a Pre-heat mode and when the signal came on indicating the temperature had been reached and the window display showed ÃÂonÃÂ I put the first batch of cookies which were on a Farberware Cookies Sheet into the oven for 10 minutes.  After 10 minutes the timer signal indicated the time was up and I removed the first batch of cookies from the oven and immediately put in the second batch of cookies which I had waiting on the counter right next to the oven.  While they were baking I put the rest of the cookies batch on the first cooled cookies sheet and turned around to look at the window display to see how many minutes the second batch had left to bake. It was approximately 8:30 P.M. I noticed smoke coming out of the top portion of the range and then the house smoke alarms went off.  I opened up the oven door and saw flames.  I quickly shut the door, pushed the oven ÃÂOFFÃÂ button, grabbed a box of baking soda from the cupboard next to the range and threw baking soda into the oven.  The flames near the front of the oven died out but the ones in the back continued so I took an oven mitt and pulled the oven rack out a little ways and then threw more baking soda into the oven.  All the flames died out but then I noticed the broiler element was on and was beat red and it was not getting any cooler.  It should not have been on at all because ÃÂbakeÃÂ was selected and that broiler element only comes on during the pre-heat mode and goes off once the temperature is reached.  That element was NOT on when I put the second batch of cookies in or I would have noticed it right away.  After I got the fire completely out I think it was then that I noticed in the window display the message ÃÂF ÃÂ 2ÃÂ.  Later when I looked that up in the range book it said you should call for service, a little late I would say.  
Anyway, about that time my husband came in and of course could smell the smoke and I showed him the oven and he could also see that the broiler element was still on and was very red.  So he took some pictures of the inside of the oven and then he went downstairs to the electrical box and turned the breaker for the range off.  The broiler element immediately went off and then he pulled the range away from the wall and unplugged the range from the wall outlet.  
I could not call Sears as by the time everything was taken care of they would have been closed.  I went online to see if this range had ever had a recall and I tried to file a complaint with the government bureau but I typed what happened 3 times and when I got to the part to submit the complaint I got the same message each time that the site wasnÃÂt available.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, and such malfunctions are unlikely but possible.

incident_description:
I have a GE Microwave Oven, Spacemaker, Model CVM2072 SM2SS which started on its own two times last night.  My husband and I woke up to the beeping sound of the microwave and he went in the kitchen to see it was cooking "Pasta".  He turned it off and left the kitchen.  The microwave began beeping again as if someone was pressing the buttons and when he returned to the kitchen it was cooking on the "Coffee" setting.

incident_description: I have a gas range from GE Profile SS Model PGB975SEM1SS Serial MM273741P that has knobs that do not lock.  The slightest brush against them allows them to release gas.  A check of the internet shows that this is a common problem with no solution. There are hundreds of complaints on the Consumer Affairs site. incident_description: My wife was using the Frigidaire smooth top oven model FEFL79DBL and she heard a loud pop, followed by white smoke and burnt smell. incident_description:

Below is a picture of my adult daughters hand.  She was burnt while pouring herself a cup of, just brewed, coffee from the Cuisinart coffee maker Serial # 10310--Model # DCC-1100.  The problem is with the cruet, while pouring, suddenly the arch of  coffee "stream" will surge forward and with out warning the coffee will be flowing onto the counter or in this case onto my daughter's hand as she held the mug she was filling.

She climbed on a stool to unplug the unit; the unit burned her including her cheek, ear & neck.

incident_description: We bought our 80+ year-old mother a Vitamix 5200 blender for Christmas (made by the Vita-Mix Corporation headquartered in Cleveland, OH).  The first time she went to use it, she had the idea to remove the lid (while it was still running) to help stir the mixture of vegetables she was grinding up in the Vitamix, using the plastic pusher device that comes with the machine. You can imagine the scenario from there, but the worst part is that the plastic food pusher shattered when she unintentionally contacted the in-motion chopping blade.  The pieces of the shattered food pusher became high-speed projectiles that went everywhere.  By the grace of God, none of the flying pieces of sharp-edged shattered plastic hit my mom, which was a truly miraculous escape of injury. That the Vitamix machine is able to operate even with the lid removed is a real concern because I know my mom will not be the only person out there to try that stunt, and in all likelihood, others will unfortunately not be as lucky as my mom was in avoiding injury.  In seeing those shattered pieces of hard, sharp-edged plastic, and how far they flew across the room, I can tell you that anyone being hit with any of those pieces would have every potential to sustain serious or even life-threatening injury.  This product is excellent for its intended purpose of grinding food, but the lack of a safety switch to prevent its operation with the lid off is a serious safety omission that needs correcting to prevent severe and life-threatening injury to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with potential for serious injury, but no actual harm occurred. The likelihood is possible as similar unsafe actions by users could reasonably occur.

incident_description:
I cut my finger twice while attempting to clean my new Joseph Joseph Mezzaluna Folding herb chopper with integrated blade guard.  The handles fold over the blade is such a way that they create a pinch point against the blade.  There isn't any locking/safety mechanism thus allowing the handles to swing back and forth. 

This item is very dangerous to use and clean.
justification: The user sustained injuries (cuts) while cleaning the herb chopper, indicating a severity level of 3. The design flaw makes such injuries likely during use or cleaning.

incident_description: A Duralex Paris Clear Dessert Plate Exploded in front of my child while she was eating dinner off of it. We had just starting eating dinner when my child's plate spontaneously exploded sending glass fragments up to six feet away on the kitchen floor. Miraculously, neither of us were injured. My child was understandably upset and crying because she could not eat her dinner. I had purchased the food at a restaurant, so there was not another portion to give to her. The plate was taken directly from the cabinet and food placed on it. The food was not overly hot or cold. Photos are attached.
justification: The plate exploded but no injuries occurred, only distress and inconvenience.

incident_description: Cooking breakfast and the right front burner stayed on high.  Had to trip the breaker for it to shut off!
justification: The incident was a minor incident with no injury, but it could have caused a fire if left unattended.

incident_description: Less than half way through the dish washing cycle, black smoke and an electrical burning smell was coming out of my dishwasher.  Kenmore Ultra Wash Model # 665-16362301 Serial # FR3517014, purchased Sept 2004. Tried to turn it off would not shut off.  Had to unplug the unit.
justification: The incident involved black smoke and an electrical burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Maytag dishwasher element stayed on after cycle completed. Melted plastic dishes. Serial number matches a recall that vendor has for a problem that is almost exactly what happened to me but says its recall isn't exactly the same so it's not covered. Thought someone should know because this issue is going to cause a fire and kill somebody if it's not corrected by the manufacturer. I'm fortunate I caught and can afford to replace it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing property damage (melted dishes) but no injury, and the likelihood is high given the recall and potential for fire.

incident_description: While the coffee maker was turned off (but plugged in) the heating element came on.  The indicator light did NOT come on.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned but no injury or damage occurred, indicating a minor incident.

incident_description:
I had a Hamilton Beach [slow cooker], the "set and forget" 33967. I had it for five years, and hadn't had any problems, until yesterday. It had been set on high, for four hours, to cook a broth.  My husband was home at this time, and with in a 30 minute period, it went from "just fine" to explosion of broth all over the kitchen. 
First of all, the lid was not clamped down, so there was no reason for it to explode due to pressure. Second, I was cooking the broth in four hour increments, because I am cautious. 
According to my husband, it started beeping, didn't stop beeping, and when he came in to see why, it was frothing over with extreme heat. He managed to unplug it without burning himself. 
Now why, when this [slow cooker] started to malfunction, would it lock into an extreme heat, unlike anything we'd ever seen before? Why wouldn't it just shut off? The broth managed to hit items 2 feet away, which is quite unlike anything I've ever heard off. 
We've gotten a new [slow cooker]. I will never buy anything by Hamilton Beach again.
justification: The slow cooker malfunctioned, causing an explosion of hot broth, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Keurig  overheated, burning the countertop surface the brewer sat on
justification: The Keurig overheated and caused damage to the countertop, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Machine made weird noises after brewing about one ounce of coffee, then when I attempted to fix it coffee grinds and water spit out. Would not brew a full cup
justification: The machine malfunctioned, causing coffee grinds and water to spit out, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: I took my Pyrex oblong baking dish (not sure of size, but larger than 9 x 13) out of the cupboard and sprayed it with non stick cooking spray in preparation for baking acorn squash. I prepared the squash, put the baking dish in a preheated 400 degree oven. Within 10 minutes, I heard a loud bang. I opened the oven door and found the dish had exploded all over the oven mostly in small, sharp shards of glass.  There were two large pieces of glass under the squash. I am thankful this happened inside the oven and not on the countertop, but feel this was extremely dangerous.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was dangerous and could have caused injury if the glass had exploded outside of the oven.

incident_description:
On 01/04/14 the consumer was using the unit and set it for about 2 minutes. After the unit finished the 2 minutes the consumer removed the item from the unit and shut the door. The consumer states the unit turned on, the digital panel was blank, however, the light was on and the fan was running. The consumer manually pressed the "off" button but the unit continued running. The consumer opened the unit's door and the unit turned off. The consumer shut the door and the unit remained off. 

The consumer states the incident occurred again on 01/08/14.

On 01/09/14 the consumer walked in the kitchen and noticed the unit was running. She states she was not using it. The last time she used the unit was 2 hours prior. The consumer opened the door and the unit shut off. The consumer closed the door and the unit remained off.

The consumer states she has had a similar incidents in December. 2014. The unit would begin running after she shuts the door. The consumer states after opening the door the unit would turn off. 

The consumer contacted the firm (800-422-1230) on 01/09/14 and informed them of her safety concerns. The firm advised the consumer that the unit was outside of the 12 month warranty and recommended that the consumer purchase another unit. 

The consumer states the unit was already in the home when she moved in on 07/30/13. 

The consumer feels the unit is not safe and does not feel safe using it. The unit does not have any damages and their have been no property damages.
justification: The unit was running without being used, which could lead to overheating or other hazards, but there was no injury or death.

incident_description: Noticed smell of burning plastic when opening Kenmore Elite refrigerator. Also felt that the temperature inside was higher than normal. Saw scorch marks above the inside light bulbs and bubbling and melting of the plastic surfaces around the light bulbs.
justification: The incident involves visible damage and signs of overheating but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Our gas oven emitted carbon monoxide enough to set off our carbon monoxide detector to which I contacted 911.  The fire dept. came and detected that our house had some levels of cm in it and they in turn called The Black Hills Gas Co. to send someone to see where the leak was coming from.  It was determined that the gas oven was the culprit, as when he turned the oven on, the flame was burning orange and emitting a lot of cm.  The serviceman came today thinking he could just replace the oven burner unit, but when he removed the bottom liner of the oven, the flame burned blue and showed no signs of cm.  However, as soon as he replaced the cover (the bottom liner) of the interior of the oven, the flame went back to orange.  He then said he will order a new regulator and thinks this will solve the problem.  We purchased this range new on June 6, 2012 and I think the unit deteriorated over time plus the fact that sometimes I open windows when it gets too warm in the kitchen.  Regardless, I think this needs to be known to others to be on the safe side.  Luckily we had a detector to warn us.  I also would like some feedback on this report especially if others have experienced this.  As mentioned earlier, it is a Kenmore gas range, model 790.7231.
justification: The incident involved a gas oven emitting carbon monoxide, but no injuries were reported, and the issue was detected and addressed promptly.

incident_description:
The consumer moved into his home in 2007 and the unit was already in the home. 

On 12/10/14 the circuit breaker went off and the consumer reset it. The consumer contacted Harvesd Electric (an electric company) to inspect the wiring in his home. The electrician arrived to the consumer home and inspected the wiring. The electrician concluded that the problem was the range. The electrician and the consumer inspected the unit and noticed burned wiring on the back of the unit. The consumer did not see any smoke or fire. The electrician advised the consumer there was a electrical failure with the unit and to stop using the unit. 

On 12/11/14 the consumer called the firm's recall hotline (888) 352-9764 (release # 09-189) and was advised that his unit is not affected by the recall. The consumer plans to contact the firm's customer service number 1 (888) 348-7563. 

The consumer has not had any prior incidents and states the unit has not been repaired. 

The consumer uses the unit daily.
justification: The consumer noticed burned wiring on the unit, but there was no smoke or fire. The consumer was advised to stop using the unit.

incident_description:
GE CafÃÂ© microwave oven model number CVM2072SM3SS mfg date Mar 2011.
Problem is the oven start on its own, posing a safety risk. It also will return an error message reporting there is a "short in the control pad" although the problem could be related to the control board too. The cost of the touchpad is closer to purchasing a new one, cost prohibited. These are considered "durable products" with long life spans. Sure reasonable repairs from wear and tear are expected. This however is outside reasonable, or rather designing and selling a product which has one feature which is over 50% of the products values is NOT reasonable. And if it must be that way then it should be very durable. Especially when it has to do with safety (this product starts up when not home or asleep.) Imagine if the brakes of a $20,000 car cost over $10,000 to repair after 4 years. Could a consumer rely on the repair to be any better. We are taking on the risk of ending up with $20,000 in repairs if there is any risk of the repair repeating again.
justification: The microwave starts on its own, posing a safety risk, but no injury or death is reported. The issue is likely to occur given the description of the problem and its frequency.

incident_description: This range has grates that allow a pan to tip over.  This has happened to me and it caused hot soup to spill onto the stovetop and overflow to run down the front of the oven. This is a real hazard.
justification: This incident has caused hot soup to spill onto the stovetop and overflow to run down the front of the oven, which is a real hazard.

incident_description: The heating element at the back of the stove becomes extremely hot when the oven is on. I was unaware that the element was hot due to heat that escapes from the oven through a hole that was designed in the stove and the heat causes the element to heat up enough to where it can boil water. This occurred without the element being on as I was using the oven.
justification: The heating element becomes extremely hot without being turned on, posing a burn risk if touched, but no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description: Cuisnart coffee maker model DCC750 had an electrical fire this morning! A couple of days ago the water pump started to make a strange noise while brewing coffee? We then ran it through two cleaning cycles with vinegar. Made 5 or 6 pots without any problem until this morning! When it was finishing brewing the electrical fire started!! Luckily we were in kitchen by it! We unplugged and got it outside very quickly!!!
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but no injuries occurred, and the issue was resolved quickly.

incident_description: Cuisenart Griddler Deluxe, Model # GR-150, SERIAL NUMBER 30805, turned on and heated up while I was at work, when I returned from work I noticed it and went to investigate, I checked to make sure the knobs were set to off and they both are, but the unit would not turn off when set to off. I am amazed it did not start a fire and would like anybody who has one of these units to be notified of this incident. I expect it will become a major product recall, I called Cuisenart and they refused to investigate the issue unless I were to pay to ship the product to them.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance that could have caused a fire but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: I have the Keurig single serve coffee maker.  Several weeks ago I put coffee grounds in a refillable single serve container, added the water to the machine and proceeded  as usual.  In the middle of it making coffee the machine made a sound (almost like frying something very hot).  It spitted quite a bit of hot water out of the machine from the area where the hot coffee should come out.  It had blown the coffee grounds and a little water into the cup.    I cleaned up the machine and it has not happened since.
justification: The incident involved hot water spitting out, which could cause injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that his mother owns the range and that they are experiencing the same problem of 09-333.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

Caller stated that the problems has been ongoing intermittently over a month or so.

11/2014 The retailer was contacted and he was referred to the agency to file a report.

Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

The submitter added the stove is very dangerous.
justification: The description indicates a fire and burn hazard, which poses a risk of injury to consumers, and the problem has been ongoing intermittently over a month, suggesting a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
In 2013 the consumer received a notice from the firm notifying him of the recall (release # 11-016). The consumer contacted the firm and shortly after received the repair kit. The consumer installed the repair kit using the instructions provided by the firm. 

A day or 2 before the consumer received the notice the consumer had an incident. The consumer was getting ready to leave his home when he noticed the front right burner was "on" (very red and hot) but the burner knob was on the "off" position. The consumer had to cut the circuit breaker to shut off the unit. 

On 11/25/14 the consumer noticed the right front burner spontaneously was "on" (very red and hot) but the burner knob was on the "off" position. The consumer states that the the LED cover next to the burner knob popped off. The consumer cut the circuit breaker off. 

The consumer states the last time the unit was used was the day before. 

On 11/26/14 the consumer contacted the firm's recall hot line (888-360-8556) and informed the firm of the incident. The firm's representative advised the consumer that the unit was no longer on recall but the call was disconnected while the consumer was on hold. The consumer called back and spoke to a different representative who advised him that since the unit was recalled it will always be on recall. The firm's representative arranged for the consumer to receive the original repair kit, a new control for each burner and new LED light covers for each burner knob. The consumer received the parts the next day. The consumer was contacted by D3S Service who would be installing the parts. 

A technician from D3S Service was sent to the consumer's home on 12/08/14 to conduct the repairs. However, the technician advised the consumer that he was not qualified and did not want to continue with the repairs. The technician advised the consumer that his boss would conduct the repairs and arrange it for another day. 

On 12/11/14 [REDACTED], a technician from D3S Service came to conduct the repairs on the unit. The consumer states while [REDACTED] was repairing the unit he broke the glass top. [REDACTED] advised the consumer that he would arrange for the order of another glass top. 

On 12/12/14 [REDACTED] (832-804-8980) a employee from D3S Service, contacted the consumer and advised him  that the firm would not cover the costs for a new glass top. The consumer contacted the firm's recall hotline and inquired about a new glass top. The firm advised the consumer that the glass top breaking was due to an installation issue and the firm would not cover any costs for replacing the glass top.

The consumer states he has spoke with [REDACTED] from D3S Service and [REDACTED] offered to pay for 50% of the cost if the consumer is willingly to pay the other 50%.

The consumer does not want the unit repaired and would rather have it replaced. He is upset with the manner the firm is handling this situation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner and subsequent repair issues, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
11/27/2014 The consumerÃÂs wife prepared an approximate twenty-pound turkey and placed it in the roaster on the rack. The consumer tried placing the turkey inside the oven and the rack moved approximately three inches towards the consumer. The consumerÃÂs wife screamed thinking the consumer was going to fall but the consumer was able to hug the roaster, thus breaking the fall.

The consumerÃÂs wife proceeded to cook the turkey in their old roaster. The consumer believes the rack should be secure so that it does not move around. The consumer indicates that had the turkey been hot out of the oven, the consumer would have burned himself when falling.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety and burn hazard. 

The consumer has no injuries to report.
justification: The consumer was able to hug the roaster, thus breaking the fall, and no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer is filing a report on her unit which caught fire. 

On 12/17/14 the consumer was using the oven and had it on the broiler setting. She states after 2-3 minutes she saw lights coming from the oven and when she looked in the oven she saw flames. She states she did not have anything inside the oven. She opened the oven door and flames and sparks were coming out. She closed the oven door and pressed the "off" button on the unit to shut off the oven. The consumer threw salt and wet cloths inside the oven to put out the fire. 

The consumer adds sparks have damaged some of the black glass in front.

The consumer states the only damage was to the floor (in front of the oven) from the sparks. 

The consumer has not had prior incidents. 

The consumer uses the unit 3 times a week.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks from the oven, but no injuries were reported, only minor damage to the floor and oven glass.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his microwave purchased 14 months ago caught fire December 21/2014.

The unit had not been used all day and the only portion of it that was turned on was the light that shines down on the caller's stove.

Caller was not in the kitchen but smelled smoke from outside, returned to the kitchen and saw first a blue type smoke going up to the ceiling from the unit and that there had been so much heat at the top of the microwave that charred, blackened pieces of plastic had dropped down onto the glass revolving disc.

He quickly turned everything off.

The consumer added he called the manufacturer (GE) and made a report with them..They sent a technician to his home..Consumer noted he was told the unit was not repairable, and there was no failure analysis done.

There were no injuries

This caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them as quickly as he creates this report
justification: The microwave caught fire but there were no injuries, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer started the coffee maker to brew a cup of coffee and it was on for less than 60 seconds, when how water and coffee grinds flew onto the consumer's right arm, neck and her cheek.  She was standing right beside the coffee maker at that time.  The consumer said that the scalding contents shocked her, but she was able to apply cortisone cream to her burns and she was alright in a couple days.

They discontinued use of the coffee maker and purchased a new one.

The model and serial number appear to be included in CAP# 15-054.  
120 V a/c, 1425 Watts, 60 Hz, UL Listed: 24ZV


*  This coffee maker was used every day, prior to the incident occurring.
justification: The consumer suffered burns from hot water and coffee grinds, requiring cortisone cream, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer has an electric range that is included in recall #13-031. 

However, the consumer has not had any issues with her cooktop burners. The consumer is experiencing this same hazard as the recall with her oven.

The consumer stated that regardless of the setting or temperature the oven is turned on at, the oven reaches over 500F. 

The consumer stated that she had this issue since her 1 year warranty expired. The consumer stated that the issue has gotten progressively worse over time with the issue occurring more frequently.

The consumer stated that she plans on calling the recall hotline and customer service.
justification: The consumer has not experienced any injury or incident, but the oven's malfunction poses a potential hazard.

incident_description:
(12/31/2014) The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in use for about 60 minutes. His wife smelled smoke in the house. She could not determine where the smoke was coming from.The fire department and police were contacted and came to the home The fire department determined that the fire started from dishwasher. Everything inside that was plastic was melted. The bottom mechanism was also melted.

(01/01/2015)The consumer stated that the unit was not in use but came on by itself. The consumer stated that he could feel the heat coming from the unit. He open the dishwasher and discovered that it was on and very hot. 

The consumer will contact the company.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction causing smoke and heat, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We have only had the keurig for less than a month and there have been a few times where if I'm standing by the device while it's brewing, hot liquid has sprayed out of it.
justification: Hot liquid spraying out is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The brewer shoots hot water and coffee out of it. It does not brew coffee without spewing hot coffee and water all over the counter.
justification: The brewer spews hot water and coffee, posing a risk of burns or spills, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: I was making tea on Saturday morning for our Family Christmas. I followed the directions and filled the pot properly but it did overflow and it did get on my hands. I ran my hands under cold water for a good 10 minutes. They were both red but didn't bubble blister so I didn't go to the hospital. I put some burn creme on them and after a few days they stopped hurting.
justification: The incident resulted in red, painful burns that required first aid but no hospital visit, indicating an injury (severity 3). Burns from hot liquids are a common household occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I plugged my Keurig in and turned the power on.  I put in a K-Cup and filled the water tank with 8 oz of water, and pressed Brew. Within a minute, it started to brew and very little water came out with some coffee grounds.  I added another 8 oz of water and pressed brew again.  This time the hot water started squirting out everywhere, loudly...but didn't even fill my 8 oz cup, and coffee grounds all in it. It made a big mess and made me wonder, "where is the water I put in?"  This has happened on more than one occasion.
justification: The incident caused a mess and inconvenience but no injury, and it has happened on more than one occasion.

incident_description: cooking a chicken in a Pyrex baking dish at 450 deg. F the dish shattered. the dish had been in the closed oven for almost 1 hour and there was no one close to the oven when it shattered.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered but no one was near the oven, resulting in an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Back of oven behind circuit board (timer and oven controls) a click and then large spark and fire tripping the house circuit breaker.
justification: The incident involved a spark and fire but no injury was reported, and the circuit breaker tripped to prevent further damage.

incident_description:
The consumer is filing a report on her unit which she feels poses a fire hazard and should be recalled. 

On 12/15/14 the consumer was using the oven to bake cookies. The consumer had set the oven on a bake setting and at a 350 degree temperature. After an hour she states the broiler element spontaneously turned and her cookies were burning even though it still had 6 minutes left. The consumer states that temperature was still at 350 degrees but shortly after she noticed an error code on the control panel that read "PF" which she believes means power failure. The consumer pressed the "off" button but the oven failed to turn off. The consumer cut the circuit breaker to shut off the unit. The consumer has kept the circuit breaker off. 

The consumer contacted a local appliance company so the unit can be repaired. The consumer informed the company of the incident and the company advised the consumer that this problem is a common issue with similar units. The company did not recommend that she repair the unit because it was likely that the incident would occur again. The company suggested that the consumer contact CPSC to report the problem.  

The consumer states the unit was repaired but does not recall the date. The "sure simmered" setting was not working and the consumer states it was repaired through Sears under warranty.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: glass (front panel and seal) on microwave door shattered.  the microwave hadn't been used for many hours.
justification: The microwave glass shattered without use or injury, indicating a no-injury incident.

incident_description: The timer does not turner off the oven. If the cooking and temperature dials are set on the over will not switch off once the timer reaches zero time.  The oven will remain on.  This is the second countertop toaster oven from Kitchen Aid that has had this problem.
justification: The oven not turning off poses a potential fire hazard, but the description does not mention any actual injury or damage.

incident_description:
We bought a GF Profile dishwasher in Oct 2006. This Jan 2015 we ran the dishwasher & when it completed the cycle we emptied & closed the unit. The heating element did not turn off & it began to smoke & melt the inside of the  dishwasher.
Thankfully we were home & caught the problem before it became serious. There were no injuries. The thermometer stuck in the dishwasher road over 160 degrees. this was about 5 minutes after discovering the problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing smoke and melting, but no injuries occurred, and the problem was caught early.

incident_description: I have a Keurig Mini K10 Model: Product # 31.2002.0548686.  It is on the recall list.  I have been having issues with mine.  My Keurig just goes through phases where is won't even brew a cup of coffee.
justification: The Keurig not brewing coffee is an operational issue with no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The high occurrence likelihood (4) is based on the recall and reported frequency of issues.

incident_description: I purchased the K10 Mini Keurig brewer from Target in December 2014. The machine leaks water as well takes too long to heat up. When it does finally heat up and begins to brew, the hot liquid shoots out everywhere. This is a danger to myself and family members. Dangerous and defective product!!!
justification: The machine leaks and sprays hot liquid, posing a burn risk, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Put water in top of the Keurig to make coffee and after I hit the brew button, water started to spill out every where
justification: Water spilling from the Keurig is a common malfunction that does not result in injury.

incident_description: Went to make coffee ..the maker stopped ...i waited about 2 minutes longer ..opened the top to see if the water was out and it shot hot liquid on my pants ..it was a gift so I don't  know where it was purchased. I threw it away in December 2014 for fear of it happening again. If I had know about the recall I would have sent it in for repair..i did call and I never had anyone return my call so I forgot about it eventually until today when I looked it up .I'm angry now that I know it could have been replaced...I've missed it and just threw away several boxes of outdated hot chocolate and apple cider.
justification: Hot liquid caused injury (burn on pants), but no severe harm or death occurred.

incident_description: The water coming out of the machine is too hot! Several times I have almost burned myself picking up the mug not realizing that it would so much hotter then it usually was when I first got it. Due to the temperature of the water I have almost burned myself a couple times and in one circumstance I even dropped the mug on the kitchen floor. The machine always spits out water from the spout also right before the brew finishes and makes mess of things.
justification: The incident describes near burns and a dropped mug, indicating potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description:
I was baking on Saturday night Jan. 10, 2015 baked macaroni and cheese in a covered [REDACTED] dish on temperature 375. When I shut the oven off, within a few seconds, I heard a pop.  I looked at the oven, the entire in-between glass shattered inside the oven door. 
The range/oven is six months old. Each time I put the oven on, I heard a pop/bang. I reported this to Frigidaire in an email as well as reporting that the top door didn't line up with the bottom door. They stated nothing was wrong with the oven. 
I tried to upload the pictures, but the system wouldn't allow the upload of the pictures of the shattered glass door.

http://www.frigidaire.com/
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
Have owned this product for 2 1/2 years. Recently -- but it took a while to notice -- the front lower heating element has become more and more warped, until it is now curved almost halfway to the rear element. Looking online I found numerous reports of the identical problem, eventually leading to the element splitting and potentially catching fire.
Additionally, this toaster oven sits on top of a microwave with a grounded metal exterior. We recently started getting an electric shock if we turn the toaster oven on, and our hand makes contact with both the microwave exterior and the toaster oven button. I just confirmed >40v of live electrical current with a multimeter, enough to cause serious bodily harm.
In short, this product is a widely reported fire hazard and an electrical hazard, yet Cuisinart has continued to manufacture it and charge consumers a shipping fee to replace it under warranty. It should be immediately recalled before it kills someone.
justification: The description reports potential for serious bodily harm from electric shock and a fire hazard, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
Purchased a set of 30 Crisa glass tumblers form Burlington Coat factory within the last 3 months. The glasses are shattering. 2 have come out of the dishwasher with cracks. One shattered in hand while removing it from the dishwasher. The items  were completely cool when being unloaded from the dishwasher. The dishwasher is in working order with no other dishes / glasses having a similar problem.  There was Only a minor injury of a glass cut to the hand .  I did not keep the packaging material  that the glasses came in. I did go to their website and  the tumblers appear to be of the "Boston" style tumbler. 
I did send an email to Crisa today via their website to notify them of the problem. 
Thank you for your time.
Sincerely ,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (glass cut to the hand) and multiple instances of glass shattering, indicating a clear hazard.

incident_description:
Here is a copy of the letter I sent to Glasslock USA:
                                                                
								[REDACTED]
								December 30, 2014
Glasslock USA
5820 Bickett St.
Huntington Park, CA  90255

Dear Gentlepersons:

I received as a Christmas gift last week an 18 piece set of Glasslock storage containers made in Korea and distributed by True Source Products Inc.  We used the large container to store pot roast slices with gravy in the refrigerator (not in the freezer).  Last evening (12/29/14) I removed the container from the refrigerator and placed it on the kitchen counter for a little over 30 minutes and then removed the contents to a pan.  I took the container to the sink and ran some barely tepid water into it.  As I held it, the glass container shattered into dozens of pieces in my hand, cutting my index finger.   If the water had been hot or even somewhat warm, I could conceive of a glass dish possibly cracking.  But the glass container was almost room temperature and the water barely warm.  If the product had been manufactured properly, this should not have happened.  It is obvious to me that this product is defective.   

I have retained the shattered pieces and took photographs of the shattered product and injury.  I canÃÂt imagine that there arenÃÂt other consumers who have had a similar experience with this product.  I think the proper thing for you to do is to issue a recall of the product and review your manufacturing process. 

Thank you for your attention to this matter.  I look forward to hearing what action your company plans to take regarding this product.     


							Sincerely,

							[REDACTED]



cc: U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission

incident_description:
Kenmore Microwave, Model # 73169, 
Item number 790057176091; Date code 08, 2013
The microwave was purchased in November 2013 from Sears. The items was in use from December 2013 to Dec 2014. On 31 Dec 2014, the microwave function that allows for the baking of potatoes was utilized to bake 4 sweet potatoes individually. The potatoes were washed and then wrapped in plastic wrap. Three of the potatoes were baked without incident. The potatoes were placed individually in the microwave, the potato button was pressed and the display showed "SC-4". incident_description:
I purchased a Whirlpool Microwave/Convection oven, Model GH7208XRY-4, approximately two and a half years ago and had it installed in my vacation home where it receives very limited use.  About a year after it was installed the electronic control panel failed and was replaced by a Whirlpool factory technician.  

The unit appeared to be functioning properly until a couple of months ago when I noticed that the unit would occasionally beep and the screen would change as if someone were programming the controls without anyone touching it.  I also noted that on occasion the screen would freeze momentarily when trying to program it but the unit otherwise seemed to work normally.  Last month my wife placed a small dish of food in the oven to reheat it and set the timer for 1 minute then left the kitchen area and forgot to check on it after the 1 minute time was up.  About 20 minutes or more later I smelled a strong odor of smoke emanating from the kitchen and found the microwave still running at full power.  I quickly opened the door of the oven which turned it off but the oven was full of smoke and the food was burned so heavily that it looked like lumps of charcoal.  The microwave safe food cover was burned and melted almost beyond recognition.  I can't help but think that had I not been nearby the unit would have continued to heat until something caught fire and caused extensive damage to my home.

I contacted Whirlpool service and thought the until was still under warranty due to the  service six months earlier but they denied any further responsibility and told me they could only fix it if I paid the full cost of repairs which, most likely, would exceed the purchase price of the unit.   Since they can offer no assurance that another repair will last any longer than the previous one I am forced to replace the unit with a more reliable one. 

I did some research on this problem and it appears strikingly similar to reported problems with Kitchenaid brand microwaves also made by Whirlpool which would just randomly start on their own.  I believe that any kitchen appliance that can start on its own or run longer than the time for which it has been programmed is extraordinarily dangerous and should be recalled immediately.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing smoke and burned food, but no injury or death occurred.

Yesterday, 1/8/15, I was cooking on medium heat, before I knew it, the heat had increased to high heat and would not turn off. I found this suggestion to be unsatisfactory given the safety risk and ended the call.

incident_description:
Sears sold a U.S. Consumer Produce Safety Commission-recalled refrigerator/freezer to the consumer after a recall notice (05-213) had been issued and without alerting the consumer to the recall or the potential hazard the unit presented. The unit model and serial numbers are included in the recall notice.

On December 15, 2014, consumer noticed unusual ÃÂclickingÃÂ and constant compressor sounds coming from the refrigerator/freezer.  Upon investigation, consumer noted that the unit was blowing warm air, there was a puddle of water on the floor under the unit and all of the food (frozen and refrigerated) was ruined.  Consumer researched the Sears website for repair service information and, while researching, discovered that the unit was recalled by the Consumer Protection Agency (CPA) several months BEFORE it was sold to the consumer.  The recall addressed a faulty component that presented a fire hazard. Consumer contacted the Sears retailer and was referred to the Sears Recall Office to address the problem. The Sears Recall Office denied knowledge of the recall and refused to assist consumer. Consumer then called multiple Sears corporate offices to seek assistance and in all cases was referred back to the Recall Office who continued to deny knowledge of the recall. Finally, the consumer reached the Sears Customer Solutions office who: 1) acknowledged the recall, 2) ordered and shipped the required parts to address the problem and 3) promised to look into the Recall OfficeÃÂs failure to acknowledge the recall or assist me. Consumer was instructed to contact Sears repair service, when the parts arrived, to schedule a technician.

Several days later the parts arrived and, later still, a technician arrived to resolve the issue with the unit. Upon opening the parts package, the technician found that Sears had sent a ÃÂlight harnessÃÂ instead of whatever was required to correct the issue addressed in the recall. Consumer showed the CPA recall notice to the technician, explained what had happened with the unit and suggested that the light harness was not the problem that caused the unit to fail or address the fire hazard identified in the CPA recall. The technician was not aware of the recall, but did diagnose the problem causing the unit to stop working and replaced a defective Protected Thermal Controller (PTC) switch. The unit began cooling again ÃÂ but the underlying recall hazard was not addressed.

Consumer contacted the local Sears retail store manager, provided copies of the recall notice, the original sales receipt and a transcript of the events thus far (including the loss of hundreds of dollars in food and having no refrigerator during Christmas week).  Consumer also called the Sears District Manager, but could only leave a voice message requesting assistance.  The District Manager has not responded to the consumerÃÂs request.  The store manager ([REDACTED]) looked into the matter and ultimately told consumer that Sears absolutely denied that the refrigerator/freezer was recalled.

At this point, consumer remained very concerned about the fire hazard and seeks assistance in compelling Sears to address the CPA recall notice.
justification: The incident involved a recalled refrigerator being sold without disclosure, leading to property damage (ruined food) but no injury or death.

I unloaded it and reloaded it and just closed the door.  I did NOT start a new cycle.  About 5 hours later, I opened it to add a few more items before leaving for the night to my families.  When I opened up the door I was met with a huge plume of smoke and the smell of burning plastic.  The head synged my hair. I looked inside after the smoke subsided and found that everything inside including the utensal basket had melted and was lying over the heater element.  All my plastic utensals and plastic handels were also melted.  The sprayer arms had also melted and are lying in the heater element.  Had I not opened it at that time before leaving for the night, I'm convinced my home would have caught fire.  

I called the GE Consumer hotline to complain because I fount other safety recals for almost the exact mode as mine for the same issue.  http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2011/GE-Recalls-Dishwashers-Due-to-Fire-Hazard/

Unfortunately it rang for 10 minutes and nobody picked up nor was there a way to leave a message.  I did leave a email but have not received a response.

I also found the following complaint that indicates my same issue below.
http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1263284

incident_description:
This incident concerns a Frigidaire Electric Range, Model No. PLEF398CCB, Serial No. VF32122045.

My wife was baking rolls when she noticed the top internal bake/broil element was on fire and it was throwing off sparks like a sparkler.  I turned the oven off at the display/controller, but the element continued to burn and throw sparks.  I had to turn the power off at the breaker box on the outside of my home in order to stop the element form burning and sparking.  This is a serious fire/safety hazard, as power/current was still going to the bake/broil element even though it was tuned off at the appliance display/controller.
I see where there was a recall about 2009 for a similar issue of the surface heating elements with this same appliance, but I see no mention of the internal bake/broil elements, but they are obviously related.  I also see that report number 20120124-61138-2147471011 on this CPSC site details the same problem I have, and it appears the person who submitted the report states that Frigidaire says they have not heard of this problem.  It also appears the person who submitted the report found many similar issues online that substantiate his issue as being a problem, and I found the same in my online research.
Why are the internal bake/broil elements not mentioned in the original recall?  It makes sense to me that the same controller/control board that is causing surface elements to turn on to full power and not being able to turn off without cutting power at the breaker box is also very likely responsible for the same issue with the internal bake/broil elements that I am experiencing.
I would like for someone from CPSC to give me a call to discuss.  I also plan to call the manufacturer tomorrow, as today is New YearÃÂs Day.  I would like for someone from Frigidaire with technical knowledge of this issue to call me as well.  In reading the report 20120124-61138-2147471011, it appears a recall was fixed on that personÃÂs oven previously, so that tells me it was not effective in correcting the internal bake/broil elements.  So, what is the fix for my issue?  Did the original recall actually address all element control issues with this appliance?
This is a serious fire and safety hazard because large amounts of current are being allowed to be sent to the heating elements even though the appliance has been turned off.
justification: The incident involved a fire and sparks from the oven element, posing a serious fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an Oster Convection Toaster Oven, Model number TSSTTVCG03 from Costco about a month ago.  I had purchased a similar one for my mother in the past and thought they were the same.  

Last night, we awoke to the smell of burning electrical wire at 4 a.m.  We discovered that the oven was still on from dinner the night before.  Upon inspection, we realized that the bottom dial, which you turn to set the time for your cooking, had a peculiar and very dangerous feature:  If you turn it to the right, you choose the number of minutes it is to run and then it turns off automatically when it hits zero.  This is the customary feature on these ovens with dials. However, on this model, to the left of the Zero, there is a "stay on" feature that allows the oven to keep running.  Problem is, if you need to manually turn the oven off because you overestimated the time, and you accidentally turn it a hair too far to the left, the oven does not turn off.  The ticking sound is so faint or nonexistent that you would never know until you smell burnt wires or your house burns down.  This is VERY DANGEROUS and we are lucky to be alive. This is particularly dangerous for older people;  the reason I bought this for my mother is because she forgets to turn the toaster off.  However, on her model there is a "hard" off -- you can't turn it left past off because there is a stop feature at zero.

I'm not sure why the "stay on" feature is necessary -- this is a toaster oven not a professional oven so the timer  should be required.  In this case, the oven no longer works so "stay on" resulted in it burning up after a few hours anyway. However, if I'm missing something and manufacturers want a "stay on" function,  then it should be accessed in one of two ways: 1) by a clearly marked additional button; or 2) by having to turn the dial all the way around (one full turn) to access it.  The oven should have a hard stop when turned left to zero.

I do want to say that Costco has excellent customer service and will take this back  no problem but I am concerned about other stores that sell this and the possibility of people dying in their homes.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction that could lead to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible due to the design flaw affecting users who might accidentally activate the 'stay on' feature.

incident_description:
On Christmas Day, the outer glass on our Frigidaire oven door exploded just a split second after my daughter had walked past the oven with her eight month old baby in her arms. If the glass had shattered a bit earlier, she and the baby could have been showered with sharp chards of glass and maybe seriously injured. In cleaning up, I found glass chards as far as fifteen feet in front of and to the sides of the oven.

The oven had been used in the morning by my wife to bake a cake. Afterwards, our son-in-law had cooked a standing rib roast in the oven and had removed it about fifteen minutes before the door glass exploded. The oven had been turned off for some time before he removed the roast from the oven. At the time of the explosion, the oven was still warm The event caught all of us by surprise. Fortunately none of the chards got into our food, though we did find some slivers of glass on the kitchen counter opposite the oven where our son-in-law was transferring food from the roasting pan  into serving dishes. 

I had cleaned the oven several days earlier using the normal three hour clean cycle. At the time, I sensed nothing at all of a potential problem with the oven. To our knowledge, the glass door had never been subjected to any physical abuse whatsoever. 

I suspect there is a serious design flaw or quality control flaw in the manufacturing of the oven door glass. I am keeping the pieces of glass, and will make them available to your laboratory for testing and analysis.  I want to let you know that I want to work with you to improve your product safety.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass exploding, but no injuries occurred despite the potential for harm.

incident_description:
Purchased a Frigidaire counter depth refrigerator model number FGHG2366PFO and felt that temperature maintenance of appropriate temperature was inadequate from date of purchase, but failed to measure with independent thermometer.  The unit eventually stopped cooling completely which was confirmed by thermometer.  Following repair, the unit failed to maintain cooling below 40F as confirmed by service personnel and thermometer.  After numerous unsuccessful repair calls, the unit was replaced by Frigidaire with a similar (Professional Series) unit, model number FPHG2399PF1.  Unit also fails to maintain temperature below 40F even following service repair.

Refrigerators that do not maintain proper cooling, and offer no indication other than consumer perception that they are not cooling properly, present a severe health risk by not preventing the decay of food and promoting the growth of food born pathogens.  "Use by", "Keep refrigerated", and shelf life dates are meaningless if refrigeration is not maintained properly.

My wife has severe gastrointestinal issues which have resulted in her hospitalization on multiple occasions.  Even though there is not enough evidence to create a direct link relating these two appliance failures to her condition, consumption of spoiled or improperly refrigerated food is a major concern for her health.

I believe that this series of refrigerator models has either a design flaw, or a systemic manufacturing problem that is not being acknowledged or addressed by the manufacturer.
justification: The refrigerator's failure to maintain proper temperature poses a health risk, especially given the wife's severe gastrointestinal issues, though no direct injury is confirmed.

The knife is in a plastic container which also contains a sheath for the knife.  However, the knife is not in the  sheath because the knife has a picture on it that I presume the manufacturer wants people to see through the plastic container.  If the knife was in the sheath then consumers would not be able to see the picture on the knife.  The plastic container is poorly designed.  While pulling the knife out of the plastic container, the plastic container broke open exposing the blade, just as my son was pulling on it.

The knife is made by FARBERWARE in China.
justification: The injury was severe, involving multiple tendons, an artery, and a nerve, requiring emergency surgery, indicating a high severity level. The likelihood is possible due to the poor design of the packaging.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range started on fire.  In previous weeks, the unit would have a slight plastic/electric burning smell during pre-heat.  During a pre-heat cycle last night, the unit displayed smoke coming out of the rear of the control panel area.  I immediately pulled the oven out and disconnected power to the unit (I was unable to get to the circuit breaker in time).

Upon inspection (after letting the oven cool down) it was found that the wiring harness that exits the control board had melted and caught on fire.  This harness area was the yellow wire which extends to the lower heating element.  Upon me removing the harness from the circuit board, the male end disconnected from the board, as the solder had been removed due to heat.  The circuit board trace had also lifted.

I have found several instances of this same issue on the web - one of which is another complaint on this site for the exact same issue (with pictures).

http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1385947

This is unacceptable.  Sears has been notified and I was told since the unit was ~4 years old and that I didn't buy the 'extended warranty' that there was not much else they can do.  I find it completely unacceptable that this issue occurs, and has been reported several times on the web with ovens which use this board/harness.  I went out and purchased another brand of oven, as even though I could fix this one for $160, I do not trust the design.  The extra money is worth it to protect my family and possessions.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, and similar incidents have been reported multiple times, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
The Sunbeam model 3831 toaster was plugged in but empty and the toaster lever was not pushed down.  Several people were in the kitchen when the toaster suddenly burst into flames.  The house circuit breakers did not activate.  The hot fire continued to burn after the toaster was unplugged and was extinguished by covering it with a wet towel.
The plate on the bottom showed that this was a 750 W toaster made in China. the counter was not damaged but the toaster had a burned hole about 2-3 inches across and 2 inches deep.  The hole was near the bottom of a side;  the edge of the hole was about 2 inches from where the power cord entered the toaster.  The bottom and sides of the hole had burned plastic.  I could not see any wiring in the hole.

This toaster was given to us by a houseguest about 2 years ago.  She now lives in Argentina.  It may have been purchased used.  This toaster has never jammed or had any problem.  We cleaned out the crumbs regularly.  This fire could have burned down our house if we had not been present.
justification: The toaster burst into flames but was extinguished without injury or death, and the counter was not damaged.

On the evening of December 25, 2014 I decided to turn on the self cleaning feature of the lower oven (larger, convection). After about 30 minutes into the self cleaning, we heard a loud POP and noticed that the inner glass of the oven door was completely shattered. I immediately turned off the self cleaning. Five minutes later, part of the shattered glass fell down to the oven floor. The door was still locked.

On December 26 in the morning, I reported the incident to LG and Home Depot since I also bought the extended warranty. Up to now, the case is open but the Customer Service provided by LG has been horrible. I was told to go ahead and clean the interior of the oven, which I am doing, but the million glass pieces are a nightmare. I am also very concerned about the repair, if just changing a part will make the oven safe to use, and if I will be able to use the self cleaning feature in the future.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door glass during self-cleaning, causing inconvenience and potential safety concerns but no reported injuries.

The only way to stop it is to pull the power cord.  I am very thankful to have been home when this happened because it IS getting very hot inside when it comes on and I have no doubt that it would have caused a house fire if I wasn't home to catch it. While searching online for any recall information I found that other consumers have also experienced the exact same problem with some people also reporting kitchen fires caused by this microwave. There are videos on youtube documenting this exact model of GE Microwave turning on by itself also. I believe there should be a recall issued for this unit as it is a danger to households.  I shudder to think that it could have come on at night while we were asleep putting our children and family at risk.  Something needs to be done to make the public aware of this potential danger.

incident_description:
On 05/25/2014 in Merrimack NH, our stove began arcing due to a malfunction of the stove.  Due to the arcing, my kitchen was effectively totaled, damaging the surrounding walls, counter and cabinets, all needing to be replaced.   The Merrimack NH Fire Department put in their Fire Report that he ignition of the fire was caused due to the stove's "Electrical Arcing".   I am just happy that my kids were not touching it at the time.   After the fire I contacted Electrolux, Frigidaire's parent company and the representative could not care less.   The rep mentioned that the their had been a recall for stoves with electrical issues (over 200,000 stoves to be exact) but as my model was not part off it there was nothing they were responsible for and the rep proceeded to try to quickly end the call.   
Further frustrating was on the companies on website it states.. "The following model and serial numbers are included in the recall: Frigidaire (Serial Number Range VF122xxxxx - VF831xxxxx)"
My Stoves Serial number is ... VF72842834.  That is clearly within the effected stoves.  The Electrux / Frigidaire rep said, my stoves model number wasn't one that they were mandated to recall.  So because the government hasn't come down on them to recall all model lines that were affected by the electronic defects yet, they did not want to talk to me.  You would have thought they would at least be concerned about their products being potentially unsafe and causing harm to customers such as my family but no, even though it was within the serial numbers listed and even more important, even though the fire department itself listed the stove's arcing issue as the cause of the fire, Frigidaire did not care.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or deaths, as the kids were not touching the stove at the time.
