incident_description:
Caller stated that the electric range burners spontaneously comes on by itself.  The unit was powered off but hours later the same incident occurred.  This has been ongoing since 2009 until now.  There was a service call in 2009 and she was advised that the unit was recalled and a technician sent out and the range was repaired with a repair kit.

Approximately 2 years later the problem started to re-occur, and the manufacturer was contacted and a technician sent out (3/2011) , the range was repaired again with another kit. 

2/2013 She noticed that the range was displaying the same failure (burners turning on by itself), the most current was 12/2/14 and when this occurs the circuit breaker is used to switch it off. Submitter noted another kit was sent out and was installed by a technician and paid by manufacturer.  

12/2/14  The manufacturer was contacted and was informed that another repair would be done, however, she does not feel that this is resolving her problem and could cause a house fire.

Submitter also noted they have now been without a stove for a week 12/8/14

Submitter noted she purchased product in August 2008 and it was recalled in September 2009.  She feels the product should never have been offered for sale and it is a hazardous product.
justification: The electric range burners turning on by themselves poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported. The issue has recurred multiple times since 2009, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: FRIGIDAIRE LGEF3043KFH stove caught on fire while using the warmer burner and oven.  The fire came from the main clock assay and melted the circuit board and part of the harness unit.  The fire was extinguished by the user and stove had to be disconnected from the wall outlet because the warmer burner would not shut off on its own.  Part of the wall behind the unit was damaged as well.  I called the company and they said the stove was purchased two years ago and does not have the manufacturers warranty at this time.  The appliance maintenance person came in and said the issue was in the faulty circuit board  and there was nothing that we did to precipitate this event.  He will change the circuit board, harness, and the clock assay and apparently this will fix the problem.  I don't know if I trust this company anymore since there have been many issues with fires coming from their circuit boards year after year.  Lowes will not refund the money since the cost of the unit is higher than the price to fix it.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the mention of recurring issues with the same problem.

incident_description: Plugged in appliance and there was a big spark where the cord connects to the rice cooker. Tripped circuit breaker in house. The cord wires are bare and exposed at the appliance.
justification: The incident caused a circuit breaker to trip, but there was no injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the oven had an unfinished edge that could pose as laceration hazard. The consumer stated that when the technician came to install the unit on 10/16/14, he received a cut on his leg. 

The consumer contacted the retailer. They informed the consumer to add tube adhesive to the bottom edge to eliminate the hazard. The consumer did not think that was a good idea for a new product. 

The consumer called the manf and filed a complaint. They sent out a technician from Appliance Doctor Inc. The technician came out on 10/22/14. The technician noted that the KitchenAid Microwave/Oven Combo has sharp edges at door perimeter and along bottom edge of trim sharp enough to cut the skin. The consumer has not heard anything from the manf after the technician came for inspection.

The consumer contacted the retailer again. The consumer returned the unit to the retailer and purchased a new unit by a different company. The consumer was charged 15% restocking fee.

The consumer stated that he saw a different model at a different retailer for a Whirlpool unit and that unit had the same unfinished edge as well. The employee informed the consumer that the oven would not usually be installed as high as it was in the display. The consumer stated that his unit was installed as high as the display. The consumer feels that regardless of how the oven is installed, it should not have a a sharp, unfinished edge.
justification: The technician received a cut on his leg from the sharp edge, indicating an injury. The issue was noted in multiple units, suggesting a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Our Maytag dishwasher model MDB7851AWS has malfunctioned. The dishwasher became incredibly hot even though it was not running and it melted the inside components . It also melted the [REDACTED] . The kitchen smelled like melting plastic. 

The Maytag dishwasher.  I did some research online and found that other consumers with this Steamclean model and a stainless tub also experienced the same overheating element problems. 

M#MDB7851AWS
My serial number on the unit is10406883NE
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused overheating and melting of components, posing a fire hazard and potential injury risk.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite 24" dishwasher, model number 66512773K310, purchased November 2013.  The top rack of the dishwasher is poorly designed and unsafe.  The rack slides are under sized and flimsy and do not support the weight the unit is expected to experience in normal use.  Worse, the wheels that the top rack rolls on are plastic, held in place only with plastic spring clips.  On our unit these clips broke, allowing the top rack to fall out of the washer.  If the top rack were full of drinking glasses when this occurred it could cause a serious injury to anyone nearby from falling and broken glass.  It could seriously injure a child nearby.    

This is a commonly experienced product failure.  Numerous consumers have reported EXACTLY this issue with this model, and if their reports are to be believed, the company is well aware of the issue as it is readily acknowledged and recognized by repair staff.  

See http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/sears_dishwashers.html  

This is a defective and dangerous product that should be recalled and redesigned to be safe for its intended use.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that could lead to injury from falling and broken glass, but no actual injury is reported. The issue is commonly reported, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
(11/07/2014) The consumer stated that his wife was in the kitchen making sandwiches. He reached over the stove to get something and felt the heat. He looked down at the stove and saw that the back left burner was red. The knob indicated that the burner was off.

The consumer stated that the same thing happened on one of the burners in 2013. There was a recall but his unit was not included. Since there was a warranty still on the unit, the consumer had all of the knobs repaired.


(11/10/2014) The consumer contacted the company. He advised them of what happened. The consumer was advised that the unit was no longer under warranty. He was also advised that nothing could be done. The consumer was referred to the recall hotline.
justification: The incident involved a stove burner being hot despite being turned off, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I am a fire investigator. On Wednesday, November 26th shortly before 3pm, fire crews were dispatched to a possible structure fire. Upon their arrival, they found the house smokey. The occupant stated that her oven was on and would not shut off. It appeared that the oven was just getting hotter and hotter. Prior to this event, she stated that the bottom element in the oven had stopped working and she had replaced it. This did not correct the problem. She stated that she was still able to somewhat use the oven (I guess that she used the broiler element). This date, the baking element started working and she was not able to get it to turn off. I checked for previous recalls and was not able to find any. The model number is GLEF369DCD; serial number is VF52041830.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing smoke but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Baking chicken at 350deg.  After about15 min noticed different odor than usual.  After another 5 minutes noticed oven displaying E2 F3 (I think) error meaning oven too hot.  Turned oven off, but it remained on, broiler element only.  Had to turn oven off at circuit breaker.  If I had not been present and had not opened circuit breaker at box, I believe there would likely have been a fire. Chicken was burnt.  

Cannot use cooktop.  If breaker is turned back on, broiler element turns on even though oven is turned off.  One would think that controller failure would shut everything down, rather than allowing element to be powered on and heating when nothing is turned on.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: This is a Jenn-Air dual fuel range. The knobs are placed right above the oven. The knobs are made of 100% plastic and they melt with use of the oven. I have complained to the company many times (under warranty and out of warranty) and they tell me to just buy new knobs. On Thanksgiving day, I went to turn off a burner and the knob had melted. I could not turn off the flame. I quickly grabbed another knob and tried to use it to shut the flame off but it would not work. We then tried a pliers--nothing. The flame was on high and I couldn't shut it off. The fire Dept had to pull out the range and shut the gas off at the valve. There are MANY complaints about this online.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove knob that led to an uncontrolled flame, requiring fire department intervention, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: LG refrigerator (lfc25760sw) light did not turn off when doors were closed.  As a result, the housing around the lights completely melted.  We noticed that the interior of the refrigerator was very hot and it smelled like something was burning.  We have removed the lightbulbs and are currently shopping for a safer refrigerator that won't burn down our house.  Burn marks are visible where the lightbulbs had been screwed in.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted housing and burn marks) but no injury or death.

incident_description: Was filling my sodastream using only plain water and only to the indicated line. Had my 4 yr old daughter help. Unit exploded sending top flying up and bottle flying down onto my finger. It was a loud and scary explosion. My finger nail is bruised and it was painful. I am glad it was not my daughter who got hurt. I am afraid to use the product and am attempting to get my money back form the company.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruised and painful fingernail, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this is an uncommon event, hence likelihood 2.

incident_description:
A surface unit switch (part # 3148954) for a large coil element overheated the element on a slightly less than medium control setting causing the element to become red hot. When the switch was inspected for damage, there was a considerable amount of black soot-like material on and inside the switch as well as on the control panel surface behind the control knob. Although to a slightly lesser degree, inspection of the other large coil element surface unit switch revealed similar black soot-like material on and inside the switch.

Replacement surface unit switch parts (part # 3149400) were ordered and installed for the large coil elements. Damaged parts available for inspection if necessary.

This incident occurred on a Whirlpool Electric Freestanding Range.

The product was being used by my spouse at the time of the incident.

The product was being used at the time of the incident to cook food products on a slightly less than medium setting.

No harm or injury occurred at the time of the incident. Significant harm or risk could have occurred at the time of the incident such as injury, death or property damage, if the range had not been attended at the time of the incident. It is not uncommon for some forms of cooking to be left temporarily unattended, on a low to medium setting, to allow certain food products to simmer or slow cook.

Potential risk - Upon further inspection, one of the small coil element surface unit switches revealed black soot-like material on and inside the switch, although to a lesser degree than the large coil element surface unit switches referenced above.
justification: The incident caused no injury but involved equipment damage and potential risk, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the presence of similar issues in other switches and common unattended use.

incident_description:
Kenmore Dishwasher 665-16032402 was running through a cleaning cycle, and members of the family were commenting that they detected a strange smell.  It seemed like the smell was coming from the dishwasher, but was hard to know for sure.  We paused the cycle to check inside the dishwasher but didn't notice anything that was wrong.  After resuming the cycle, we continued to notice the smell.  I'm not certain how long the dishwasher was running, but seemed longer than normal.  Shortly after, I heard a pop sound and saw black smoke coming from the top right of the dishwasher door.  I ran to the dishwasher to open the door and smoke continued to come out of the door.  I told my son to watch the dishwasher while I ran downstairs to turn off the circuit breaker.  After I turned off the breaker, I heard my son yelling fire from upstairs.  I ran back upstairs, grabbed the fire extinguisher and put out the flames that were burning through the inside of the dishwasher door.  
Once everything was settled down, I removed the control panel from the unit and noticed a high amount of damage around the wires to the control panel and plastic of the dishwasher door.  After inspecting the control board itself, I also noticed what looks like a hot spot on the circuit board.
I have pictures to document the incident.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and catching fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I sent a notification of this problem to the manufacturer: Good Cook Bradshaw International, Inc. 9409 Buffalo Avenue Rancho Cucamonga, CA 91730

 I recently purchased one of your GOOD COOK can openers at our local Safeway. From the stamp on the handle of the device, it appears to be model 144A, and was manufactured during the month of 5/2014. Please be aware this model has a serious defect. Upon opening a couple of cans on 11/30/14, I noticed sharp slivers around the edge of the can itself, but not on the lid. Several of these fragments fell off on the table, while others remained attached to the can surface. The thickness of these fragments was about the same as heavy duty sewing thread. Their length varied from 1 mm to approximately 1 cm. The ends are quite sharp. One sliver stuck me in the finger. If consumed, such metal pieces could be dangerous to the human digestive track. Please address this issue before your customers are injured. Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (finger prick) and potential for more severe harm if metal fragments are ingested, indicating a moderate severity and possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The maytag range model #MGR8800DS, when the oven is on the knobs for the burners become so hot you have to use a pot holder to adjust them.
justification: The knobs becoming hot is an incident that could lead to discomfort or minor burns, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
(10/31/2014) The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in middle of the normal wash cycle. The consumer stated that there was a strange grinding noise coming from the dishwasher. She saw flame shooting out of the right top of the dishwasher. There was also an electrical smell. The consumer disconnected the unit at the circuit breaker.

(11/03/2014) The consumer contacted the company and advised them of the incident. The consumer was advised that she was the first person to call about a fire incident. The consumer was given a service date for someone to come out for an inspection.
justification: The incident involved flames and an electrical smell, but no injury or death was reported, and the consumer was able to safely disconnect the unit.

incident_description: The oven on our electric range wouldn't shut down. When manually turned off, it not turn off and an "F-10" notification flashed in the display window. The oven continued to overheat. Everything in the oven was burned to a crisp. The circuit breaker had to be switched to the off position in order to turn off the stove.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure and property damage (burned food) but no reported injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: I, and many other consumers, have been begging Temptations by Tara to examine their bakeware products for quality issues. These bakeware and dish products are breaking, crackling and having disturbing marks appear. Because these products are engaged in the preparation and cooking of food, the food safe glaze must be in tact. The deteriation of the glaze is a safety concern. Additionally I have read about these products cracking in half in the over, while taking out of the oven (resulting in a 2nd degree grease burn on my forearm), in the sink while washing people, animals and children are getting hurt!
justification: The description reports injuries like 2nd degree burns from product failures, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention of frequent incidents involving people, animals, and children suggests a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
(10/24/2014) The consumer stated that a code of F1 appeared on the control panel. The consumer  pressed clear to reset. The F1 code went away but the consumer was still unable to use the burners or the oven. The oven would lock and go into the self-cleaning mode by itself.

The consumer stated that he is having the same issue with the units that were called in 2012-Rel #13-031. The consumer called the firm in 2012 and was advised that his unit was not included.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning equipment with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of similar issues suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I was making dough in my Kitchen Aid Artisan Stand Mixer with the glass bowl. The glass bowl came loose, shattering while spinning. A large spinning shard cut my hand, severing the nerve and partially lacerating the tendon. Additional pieces of glass were found up to 6 feet away in my kitchen following the incident.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury with nerve and tendon damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the described scenario.

incident_description:
We are having problems with the knobs on our LG stove. They are made of plastic on the insides and continue to break, with the stove not being properly turned off. These knobs need to be recalled.

Last night I walked into my kitchen with strong smells of gas. If I did not come downstairs for a glass of water, who knows what could of happened with the gas on during the night.
justification: The incident describes a gas leak due to faulty stove knobs, which could lead to a potential explosion or asphyxiation, indicating a risk of death.

incident_description: my wife noticed as she passed by the stove in the kitchen in the morning when she woke up that the oven was hot so she opened the door and noticed a flame in the bottom of the unit but it had not been turned on since the night before, she called me and I was shocked so I called ge consumer product safety and reported problem and I was given prompt service and the said bad thermostate I still have bad part and kept it in my basement stored away
justification: The incident involved a flame in the oven without it being turned on, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Burner on range would not turn off. After several attempts to turn it off the burner finally stopped heating. A few seconds later the burner turned on to full power by itself.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Our kitchenaid dishwasher Model KUDL01ILBS5 went on fire on 11/28/14.  There were flames and fumes being emitted out of the front of the machine.  I was not in the house at the time, but my cleaning lady was, and she turned off the machine to stop the fire.  The house was full of fumes of burned electrical wiring.  Luckily, no one got burned.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, emitting flames and fumes, but no one was injured as the fire was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
While fixing Thanksgiving Dinner, I had my oven on 250 degrees and I noticed as I was cooking on the stove top, smoke coming from behind the oven.  I immediately pulled the oven away from the wall and noticed an electrical fire was going on inside where the control panel is.  We immediately put it out with flour and called 911.  The fire department arrived and took a look at the situation and could not established what could have caused the fire but advised us to get an electrician out to make sure that it was due to the circuit breaker or outlets.  Once the electrician came out to examine the situation, he then determined that it was the oven itself which was purchased at home depot I do believe in 2009 or 2010.  So the appliance is not old.  It is a Frigidaire range top.  I filed a report with my insurance and had to purchase another oven.  I could have lost everything and everyone if I was not attending to my meal.  Very dangerous and expensive appliance to replace 
serial# vf0333843
Model# fefl68gmh
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with no injuries or deaths, and the appliance was not old, suggesting such events are unlikely.

incident_description: Approximately a year & half after purchasing the electric glass cooktop range the front right burner started turning on sporadically on high when the rear right burner would be turned on.  The plastic touch pad control panel located at the rear of the stove appeared to have small cracks on both bottom corners caused by the heat of both the oven and stove top that seemed to allow moisture to enter the electronic components causing the dangerous  situation  to occur.  Finally after several weeks the right front burner stopped working all together  at which time I called LG customer service to find out about the recall that I found online regarding  this model and was told that my unit was not covered due to the serial number although my unit was experiencing similar to the recalled units. Now I'm stuck paying for the repairs of my unit despite the fact that LG has not corrected the initial problem on my later model unit. I believe  that part of the problem that they have overlooked in correcting the problem  is that the heat that is dispersed by the ovens exhaust, that is located right underneath the the plastic covered control panel, is causing a short circuit of the electronics which because of the plastic it is not able to withstand the excessive heat and eventually cracks.  LG should be ashamed of the poor engineering and lack of proper stress testing of the materials that has obviously  went by the way side  all in the name of maximizing  corporate profits while sacrificing consumer saftey...This recall should be expanded to cover later models that are still experiencing  these same issues that have not been corrected by the initial recalls corrective components  that supposedly my unit already had during its production since it is a later model.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning cooktop that poses a potential safety hazard but does not report any actual injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I turned on my Kitchen Aid lower oven to clean after Thanksgiving.  When I got home there was glass all over the inside of oven and kitchen floor.  My wood floor was burned with hot glass
justification: The incident involved property damage (broken glass and burned floor) but no reported injury.

incident_description: Went to warm food in the microwave, set time and closed door. pushed start and suddenly the microwave started sparking from the side of the unit behind the control panel.   I quickly opened the door to stop the microwave from running.  The sparks stopped but there was a strong burning smell that came from the microwave.   I had the unit looked at by a repair person and they found that the transformer and capacitor had shorted / burned up. The wires connecting the two also melted.
justification: The microwave sparked and emitted a burning smell, but no injury occurred. The incident was resolved by stopping the microwave and repairing the damaged components.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid dishwasher caught on fire tonight. Smoke was visible, followed by visible flames from the control panel on the top right corner.

This is incredibly dangerous as I usually run my dishwasher at night while I'm asleep. Thankfully, I caught it.

There are reports of this happening to many many others, yet there is no recall or warning to let people know about this very hazardous situation.

Model # KUDIO1ILWH5


Serial # FR402537
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore Gas Range Model # 66575775890 Serial # RJ4935384. While using the oven at 350 degrees, the outer glass on the oven door shattered and blew outwards. While the door had been opened and closed about 20 minutes prior to the incident, no one had touched the appliance for in the interim and no one was in the room when the incident occurred. Fortunately being tempered glass, no one was injured attempting to clean up the area.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Faint burning plastic smell had recently began to occur when the oven was turned on and persisted for a few days. Today, as both oven and range were in use, loud static pops and sparks flew out of the bottom of the oven and from the back, spewing black smoke and ash out of the vents. The electricity was still flowing into the unit, as both the oven and burner were clearly on. Smoke continued to pour out of the back of the unit until the main breaker was turned off. Fire department arrived approximately four minutes after the incident occurred (called 911 immediately and fire station is located within .5 mile of our residence) and reported that the area around the range was 180 degrees F. The sparks caused damage to the laminate flooring (melted through) and the area behind the range was charred.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and property damage but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: the outside oven glass door shattered for no reason. With the oven off, we opened and shut the door ,after we shut the door  within a minute it just shattered.  It a kenmore gas rang  model #790.36739700
justification: The oven glass door shattered unexpectedly, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description:
This caller purchased five four piece stainless steel flatware settings from an online source May 13th, 2013 and left it unopened pending purchase of new dishes also.
Around October 2014 the caller purchased the dishes and placed dishes and flatware in the dishwasher before use.
He and his wife sat down to eat when he picked his butter knife  up he cut his thumb and index finger of his left hand.
The caller's wife is a registered nurse and she cleaned, treated and covered his cuts.
Later that same day he was washing the same flatware just as he always washed other flatware, however the knives of these new settings being reported are so sharp that the palm of his right hand was cut.
His wife again treated this cut.
These knives have been put away where no one can use them.
The butter knives used at the table with meals at times have a dull serrated edging but these are being reported as being as sharp as very sharp steak knives.
The caller is reporting these knives as a severe laceration hazard especially since older children are many times trusted to use this type of knife.

The caller contacted the retailer October 4th, 2014 and was advised to contact the manufacturer.
The caller sent an email to the manufacturer November 17th, 2014 and received a generic response to contact the retailer.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts requiring treatment, indicating an injury severity level. The likelihood is high given the sharpness of the knives and the potential for repeated use.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting her electric four burner range top becomes red hot whenever any of  the burners are in use, this became evident from the beginning of purchase from retailer in NJ around October 2010.

The caller leaned over the range and burned her stomach which she treated herself.

All elements are shut off , they will not turn on until the element consumer wishes to use is jiggled to obtain connection, but then sometimes will fluctuate from the temperature consumer sets when in use.  When element is jiggled, bluish-green sparks occur.

When elements are pulled off to clean underneath the caller has noticed that where the element and the connections meet the prongs at the base (red & white) have crumbled and fallen off and prongs remaining are corroded. 

The elements will shut off.

October 2014 the caller burned her finger but ran cold water over it.

Not injuries are being reported, not medical attention has been required.

Caller has attempted to contact the manufacturer by phone but was pushed back and forth so ultimately sent a letter to them.
justification: The caller experienced burns on her stomach and finger, indicating injury, and the recurring electrical issues suggest a likely chance of future incidents.

incident_description:
I had just finished pre-heating our oven at 350 degrees when I opened the oven door, placed the food inside, and was closing the oven door when the glass front exploded showering my legs and the kitchen floor with broken glass.  The glass exploded before the oven door was closed and while I was still holding the handle.

The internet is littered with people having the same issue ([REDACTED]kenmore oven door exploding).  I have no faith that reporting this to Sears will do any good.  I would think a recall on this product would have already occured.  Disappointing.
justification: The incident resulted in broken glass showering the legs, indicating potential injury, and similar incidents are reported online, suggesting a recurring issue.

incident_description: I was given a gorgeous bathroom set for a house warming gift from KMART to put in my children's bathroom. The soap dispenser (sold as a lotion dispenser Item # 048W004874685001P Model # KWLLB00) had some dusty white particles in it when I got it so I rinsed it good with soap and water and put soap in it. I assumed it came from being put together and thought nothing else of it. On 11/21/2014- upon scrubbing my 4 yr olds hands that were covered in blue marker, I noticed it had an odd Smell. Before I had a chance to investigate the smell he started screaming, his hands started turning bright red and blotchy, and extremely painful. After attending to his hands I dumped the soap out to learn the inside of the bottle had an AWFUL smell and was still covered in white particles. I once again rinsed it and realized it was raw fiberglass and I had been scrubbing it into his hands. Please share as someone with bad allergies could have had a more severe reaction. If I would have used this product as a lotion pump as recommended our situation could have been much worse.
justification: The incident caused injury (red, blotchy, painful hands) but no death, and similar occurrences are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: I opened my fridge this morning to find the inside unbelievably hot with the lights hot.  The lights will not turn off when fridge doors are closed.  Light case is melted as is the top of fridge panel.  Top shelf of food products cooked.  Everything was working just fine yesterday and had we left out of town for thanksgiving i fear my whole house would have started on fire.
justification: The fridge malfunction caused significant damage and could have led to a fire, posing a serious risk of injury or death if unnoticed.

incident_description: The GE Over the Range Microwave oven was being used to heat food on a small paper plate. After a few seconds of heating I began to notice a flame (about 2 inches in height) begin to develop on a small plastic bracket that holds a metal rack in the microwave. After noticing the flame, I immediately opened the door to extinguish the flame. I removed the metal rack from the microwave and tried to start the microwave again. The flame began to develop again on the plastic bracket which was still intact.
justification: The incident caused a flame but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: My refrigerator brand name Frigidair caught fire spontaneously.  My five year old grand daughter was sitting less than 5 feet away when this happened.  I would hate to think we were sleeping or away from home.  We wouldn't have a home.  The house quickly filled with smoke and flames was coming from beneath the unit.  After searching the internet I find this isn't the only incident.  I called frigidair and spoke with a corporate manager named [REDACTED].  She only offered to give a part for repair.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a serious incident that could have caused a fire and put the family in danger.

incident_description: The thermador cook top does not ignite immediately allowing gas to build up resulting in a flas of Fire which resulted in burned hair and superficial burns to my right arm.   Also another burner will not not ignite when it is hot and another burner will occasionally not ignite at all unless it cross ignites from adjacent active burner.
justification: The incident resulted in burned hair and superficial burns, indicating an injury, and the description suggests recurring ignition issues.

incident_description: Dishwasher heating element would not turn off at end of cycle. Pressed the heated dry button to turn off and closed the dishwasher door. A few hours later, I could smell smoke and the much of inside plastic of the disaster has melted.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that caused smoke and melting plastic, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I put a pot roast in the Crock Pot at 12:00pm on Low. All of the ingredients that went into the crock pot were previously cooked on the stove, so nothing was cold going in. It was in the slow cooker for 3 hours when I heard a boom from the other room. I went to see what happened, and the glass lid of the Crock Pot was completely shattered, with many shards of glass in the food. It's impossible to remove the lid without the lid handle just lifting off of the glass shards.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of the glass lid without any reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such failures are not common but possible with glass components.

incident_description: Fire Department reported about kitchen fire caused by gas stove. Consumer stated that her husband had started cleaning cycle on stove about 2 1/2 hours before the fire. She came in to kitchen to find heavy black smoke coming up & around the stove. Cabinets above were charred.
justification: The incident involved a kitchen fire causing charred cabinets but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Home builders installed  a GE Gas Range XL44 in numbers of homes where I live.   

Model # JGBS20WEA3WW
TA112186P

My concern are the lack of safety on the knobs the release the gas. 

Its set up so as you turn the knob to the complete right stopping at the igniter initiator (which clicks, until you turn back a hair) the gas is lite into flame.  

The problem is knob has no resistance so if its just lightly bumped it can release gas as the shift in direction doesn't meet the igniter.  So the gas releases until someone notices a smell.  This has happened several times and worst case has been it was releasing while we were sleeping.  We were not aware until the gas smell had filled the rooms and it woke us. its very scarey to think what could happen. 

The stove in the scheme of things isn't that old and I'm surprised it would be made this way. I was surprise that when I called GE its never been reported to them.  By my neighbor has the same one and she too has has this issue. 

GE offered no solution but to look for some after market safety mechanism ..  Perhaps this is something needing attention.  Im sure this model is still in many homes. 

Hopefully can help.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks that could lead to poisoning or explosion, posing a risk of injury or worse, and it has occurred multiple times.

incident_description: My Kenmore Dishwasher, Model #665.16469300, Serial # FR0204104 caught fire.  About 10 minutes after I started it, I heard a strange noise coming from the kitchen.  When I went to go check, there were flames coming from the right top of the dishwasher and popping sounds like an  electrical fire.  I opened the latch to turn off the power and the flames extinguished.  Not before leaving noxious fumes throughout my house and black soot on the counter top above the dishwasher.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing noxious fumes and soot, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung over the oven Microwave model# SMH9187ST back in December 2010.
The other day, the microwave flashed ÃÂBaked PotatoÃÂ and turned on automatically. I was lucky I was at home. I unplugged the microwave, plugged it back in, and in about 5 min, it happened again.  I checked the Internet, and this ÃÂBaked PotatoÃÂ issue was all over it.  I called Samsung, and they granted me a one-time accommodation to cover the labor and parts. Sounds like this is a very common problem.
I will have the microwave repaired, but my concerns are that it will happen again, and I will not be home, and the microwave will catch on fire. 
I was hoping the CPSC could find out if my concerns are warranted, if this microwave is in fact a fire hazard, and that I should stop using it.
Thank you for all of the good work
[REDACTED]
justification: The microwave turned on automatically without user input, indicating a malfunction, but no injury or damage occurred. The issue is described as very common, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
GE Cafe space-maker microwave oven ( CVM2072)installed 2011 started turning on by itself 11/18/2014.
It has happened 3 more times. Each time it stops when you open the door. 1 time it said pasta. 1 time there was a long list of things . don't know what it said because I just opened the door.
I also own the matching GE Cafe stovetop/oven and dish washer. So far no problems with them
justification: The microwave turns on by itself but stops when the door is opened, indicating a malfunction without injury.

incident_description: My husband  purchased a Frigidaire oven from Lowes in the summer of 2010. He passed in September 2010. I was going thru treatment for breast cancer and rarely used the oven until 2012, As I was cooking a roast I noticed the light flash off and on making noise. The next time I tried to turn the oven on it would say preheat but would not ignite, I tried the broiler and it would turn on after a couple seconds. I feel like this is a safety issue due to the fact that the boiler is working but not the oven and trying to turn on is scary cause of gas issues. My husband would normally handle this, I am sure it is out of warranty but if this is going on with other ovens than it is defected.
justification: The oven malfunction poses a potential safety issue with gas, but no actual injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: This weekend a 13 x 9 inch Pyrex brand baking dish (color dark pink) exploded in our oven. We had  been baking chicken wings at a high temperature--450. There was no warning on the dish. The dish was only a couple of years old. The chicken grease began to burn on the bottom of the oven and the kitchen filled with smoke.
justification: The incident involved an exploding baking dish and smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report on his electric range because he feels it poses both a fire and safety hazard. 

10/23/2014 The consumer indicates that a few minutes after his wife had turned the oven on to preheat, the circuit board situated on the back of the range caught fire and flames shot up as much as one foot high above the range. Immediately before the fire, the consumer states that there was a distinct smell of rubber. The consumer was able to unplug the range and the fire ceased thereafter. He reports that the fire lasted an approximate twenty seconds.

10/24/2014 The consumer contacted the retailer and explained to a representative the situation that had occurred. The consumer was advised the unit is out of warranty, the representative informed the consumer that there was nothing they could do. The consumer was also informed that if he wanted a technician to inspect his unit, he would have to pay for the service out of pocket.

The consumer states that this is the first time him and his wife have had any incidents with their electric range. He indicates that the oven is used approximately two to three times a week while the top burners are used on a daily basis. The electric range has not been used since the fire incident. The unit has not been inspected by a technician.

The consumer has no injuries to report.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, and the occurrence likelihood is considered possible given the described usage pattern.

incident_description:
(10/31/2014) The consumer stated that the left front burner come on and off by itself. The consumer had to turn the stove off at the circuit breaker. This happened again on 11/4. 

The consumer indicated that she is having the same issue as the ranges that were recalled in Release #09-333 but her model is not included.

(11/5/2014) The consumer called the company. A service call was set up for someone to come out and look at the range.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was reported for service.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the over the range microwave oven powers on by itself.  This incident started occurring about 3 days ago.  Whenever it powers on it selects a read out from the panel like "baked potato".  He would turn it off and reset the unit but this incident would re-occur.  He has since unplugged the microwave to prevent any damages.

10/29 The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that there was no recalls for the unit.

Consumer feels that this unit is a potential fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The microwave powers on by itself without causing injury, but the consumer perceives it as a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
My Whirlpool dishwasher - model GU2275XTVQ1 serial FY5002598 developed a hole through the bottom of the plastic tub.  The whole appears to be the result of the plastic melting just under the heating element.  There was no contact between the tub and heating element.  Whirlpool repair technician (sent by the company) listed the incident as "no apparent cause..."

Whirlpool Safety division acknowledged that the report indicates my machine can not be repaired (actually the tech. only said the tub could not be repaired).  Whirlpool initually offered me 20% of another Whirlpool product.  They went to 30% upon my complaint of the offer being far off base considering the danger that the machine caused in my home.  I refused this offer and requested a damage claim sheet, which they emailed to me.

Today I received a call from Whirlpool (another person) offering me $250 for the loss of my 4 year old machine.  I have not accepted this offer at this time.

They also wanted me to return the old machine, which I'm afraid has something to do with concealing the defect.

I am seriously concerned about this problem causing a fire for another family.  Please let me know if I need to provide pictures to help you realize the seriousness of this defect.  The whole narrowly missed dumping gallons of water across the electrical connections.  The water narrowly missed my electrical panel in my basement as well.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher developing a hole due to melting plastic, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Today, 11-24-14 my GE Profile microwave/convection over the stove oven started by itself.  The only way to stop it was by opening the door, as hitting the clear button did not work. This oven was purchased and installed in December, 2012. Apparently there is only a one year warranty and my long hold time with GE today resulted in a disconnect on their part.

I checked for recalls on this oven and there are tons of complaints about this product but no recall. I have called my own repair person to see if he can come out and figure what the problem is. I spent $ 700 on this model and am not interested in GE sending out their own tech. 

As this is a horrible safety issue, we will unplug it until I find out the problem.  Due to the rate of complaints online, I will not be purchasing a GE product again.  I will though, try to get through to GE help center later, after my repair person has returned my call.  I can then report how they handled it and I am not expecting them to do anything about it as it is out of warranty. As this is a fire issue, I would like to know why they would not cover it. Who ever heard of an appliance going on by itself?  Why should I have to worry about that?
justification: The incident involved the oven starting by itself, a clear safety issue, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the number of similar complaints online.

incident_description:
The trays on this unit have no stops to prevent the trays from tilting out and down thus allowing whatever is on the tray (s) from spilling, splashing, or falling onto both the door of the unit as well as onto the consumer.  I feel this is a serious design flaw and poses a potential risk to the user.  I contacted Viking LLC and spoke with their Customer Support to determine if my oven was defective but was assured that this is not a defect and the unit was not designed to have stops to prevent the trays from sliding all the way out and falling down.  I have used this unit several times and even though I have tried to be very careful when sliding the trays out of the oven, it is very difficult to find just the right position to remove the contents from the oven tray and not allow the tray to tilt down.  
This is a fairly expensive product and is probably not widely used in consumer kitchens but I feel that you have a mandate to investigate the safety of this product since it is sold and available for purchase and does pose a safety risk.
This unit  is a Viking VCS021SS and the serial number of my unit is 210w000891.  
I contacted Customer Service  on 11/12/14.
justification: The incident involves a safety risk but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
Regarding Hamilton Beach Convection Toaster Oven, Model # 31333, Serial # A3031CE:

The "Toast/Timer" dial no longer shuts the appliance off.  The dial continues past the "Off" position to the "Stay On" position.  This means that the food in the toaster/oven is cooked longer than it should be, hence a potential fire hazard, and the only way to turn off the appliance is to unplug it which causes a spark from the outlet.

When reported to Hamilton Beach, there was no indication of any concern about the safety aspect of this product.
justification: The malfunctioning dial poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Magic Chef fridge caught fire! I checked out online and seen that other models had recalls but not my model CTB1925GRW Serial 20628916EC had the same issue those recalled had. The switch that starts the compressor went up in smoke.
justification: The fridge caught fire, which is a significant incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: A Cuisinart Single Serve Coffee Maker (model SS-300, Serial# 11128) I purchased about two months ago overheated so much that it melted part of the unit.  Contacted Cuisinart and was advised that the product is discontinued, but that there is no recall on the product.  A quick[REDACTED]search of "SS-300 Melting" uncovered several other reports of this device melting.  The part of the device that melted is a significant distance from the heating element.  If it is overheating enough to melt at that distance, it certainly has the potential to start a fire.
justification: The coffee maker overheated and melted, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: On the morning of November 20, 2014, an unsafe incident occurred while using my Frigidaire glass top cooking surface.    I was cooking on the front right burner on a setting of 3.  I placed a lid from this pan on the left front burner.  This burner was not on and had not been on at any time on this day.  3 minutes later, a loud bang was heard and glass shards and pieces of glass came out from under the lid.   In retrospect, I realize that the hot lid on the cold surface formed condensation which created a seal.  Pressure then increased inside the lid to a point sufficient to cause the explosion.  When I contacted Frigidaire, they said I should have known not to place a lid on the stove surface even though the surface was cold. Nearly every coworker and friend I mentioned this to, stated they routinely set hot lids aside on unused burners to stir or tend to their cooking food.  Obviously, this is a common occurrence.   I read my Use and Care guide cover to cover, and there was no mention of this phenomenon, nor was there a warning against placing a heated lid on a cold surface.  This incident could have caused injury or death.  I feel the Use and Care guide should be updated to warn consumers of this possibility.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of glass shards but no injury was reported, placing it at severity level 2. The common practice described suggests the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description: We purchased a Whirlpool gas range with our new home in 2011, in Dallas, GA. On September 18, 2014 the oven (range) caught fire while in self-cleaning mode. They sent a technician who said that there was a fire in the oven. There was 'no one injured. The house filled with smoke and we are left with black soot everywhere and a non-working range. The manufacturer is refusing to replace the range, offering a 25% discount on a new one. The will not reimburse us for any clean-up of the home.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no injuries, but caused property damage and smoke soot.

incident_description: My wife came home to a house filled with smoke, the fire department was called and when they arrived they found that the relay switch that connects to the compressor was on fire. Upon doing some research I found that Whirlpool had recalled 1.6 million refrigerators that were made under the Maytag name for the same component catching on fire. After numerous phone calls and playing hardball with Whirlpool, they have offered me half the original price of the thirteen year old unit ($750.00) which I assume is "Hush money"? I kept asking the supervisor "why have you not recalled this model when you know there's a problem?" I did not get a response! My concern is that there are other units in other homes with families that don't know that they are at risk. Pretty much sounds like the auto industry cover up to me~
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a faulty relay switch, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We had a fire in our dishwasher on November 12, 2014. called GE  to see if our model unit was covered by the recall of the GE Profile recall. GE said their was a recall on the GE Profile units but not the one we have.  The recall is on the Profile with a different model number. That # is one with a plastic liner. The unit we have has a stainless liner. The model number we have is #PDW8800J03WW. All of the fires start in the front panel no matter the model number. I called GE to see what they will do about the problem and they stated there is not safety issue with the unit. they do not consider a fire a safety issue and therefore will only offer a discount if we would purchase another GE dishwasher. Just to make it clear the GE Profile Dishwasher is unsafe and catches fire. We were very lucky our home was not burned to the ground or worse.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher, which poses a significant safety risk, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite Smooth top range Model #790.94453700  Serial # VF74441886.  We had cooked some biscuits on the convection setting @ 350 degrees for 14 minutes.  We were sitting in the living room after dinner and heard a strange noise coming from the kitchen.  We ran into the kitchen to see flames and smoke pouring out from behind the stove.  I ran to the oven and tried to pull it out and realized I should shut of the breaker first.  After flipping off the breaker, we pulled out the oven to see it was still on fire. We were able to put out the fire with water.  After letting the range cool down, I pulled it out the rest of the way and saw the fire had started at the pigtail mounting block.  It had completely melted down and caught the rest of the wiring in the back of the unit on fire and had burnt a hole in the wall behind the range.  The wall is also covered with dark black soot from the fire.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
I was cooking on my LG glass top range that I have owned for 7 years.  I was unaware of the recall on this range.  The burner was set to 7.5 and I was browning sausages in a pan.  I was standing in front of the stove the entire time and was monitoring the progress of the food.  They had been cooking for about 10 minutes and as I began to rotate the meat in the pan, I felt an increase in heat, heard a loud pop and crashing of shattered glass.  The center of the glass top had exploded and shattered into shards and many pieces.  I sustained a cut on my hand, but was extremely fortunate that glass did not get into my face or eyes.  Fine shards of glass did project onto the surrounding counter top and into prepared food which I had to discard.    

As I said, I am extremely fortunate that glass did not get into my face or eyes.  Or that none of my 7 children were in the kitchen at the time this happened.  I hate to think what could have happened if any of my teenage kids were cooking with me at the time!
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the hand and potential for more severe injuries, classifying it as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the recall context and the described event.

incident_description: My daughter was baking a homemade pizza at 500 degrees earlier this evening.  The inside glass on the oven door of our new (just delivered 11/16/14) LG electric range (Model # LRE3083ST/01; Serial # 408KMWUOB433) exploded.
justification: The oven glass exploded but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she put food in the slow cooker. She left it overnight. The consumer had the unit on high for 3.5 hours and low for 8 hours.  

The consumer stated that about a minute before it was supposed to be done, she grabbed the handle with a towel to check on her soup. The consumer stated that the handle came out of the lid and the rest of the glass crackled. The consumer stated that some glass dropped into the food, some glass is attached to the handle and some glass remains on the lid.

The consumer stated that she has never dropped the lid before.

The consumer contacted the manf. They informed her that they will replace the entire slow cooker. The consumer was asked to ship back the damaged slow cooker. The consumer was informed that she will receive the new slow cooker once that model was in stock.
justification: The consumer was not injured, but the slow cooker was damaged, which is a common occurrence with slow cookers.

incident_description:
I had prepared a pot of pasta and was hand washing this 8 quart Farberware 18/10 Stainless Steel pot when the handle snapped/broke off. Fortunately there were no injuries but I shutter when I think what may have happened if this handle had broken off while filled with hot water and pasta. This is a large pot. I could have been scalded or anyone else that was in the kitchen.  There were other family members (including my 2 year old granddaughter) present in the kitchen at the time of this incident. 

I am now scared to use any of the pots or pans in this cookware set. I have also contacted the company to make them aware of this incident.
justification: The handle broke but no one was injured, though the potential for severe injury was present.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she had used the cleaning feature and when she tried to use the oven for baking after a few mins she heard a loud noise which interrupted her lights and appliances.  She had to use the circuit breaker to switch back on the power.  Caller feels that her model and serial should be added to the recall 09-333.  She does not want her range repaired due to the hazard it poses and would like when she purchase another one to be reimburse in case it becomes a recall.


(7/2014)The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that her model and serial number was not included in the recall.


From consent letter: "I believe the oven worked fine until I first used the cleaning feature when the oven was on a very high temperature for an extended period of time. This feature should be tested before marketing this product as I believe it ruined my oven."
justification: The incident caused a power interruption and potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My LG brand range was involved in a recall (#13-031) in November 2012.  After several phone calls to the listed number service was arranged.  The faulty part was replaced on 12/12/12.
It is now November 2014, only 2 years later and the range is malfunctioning in the exact same way it did 2 years ago.  Several control buttons on the panel, including the 'start' button for the oven are unresponsive.  Fortunately, I never had the problem of not being able to turn the range off, but who knows what will happen next since the range is malfunctioning in the same way it did 2 years ago.
justification: The range is malfunctioning but there is no mention of injury or death, only inconvenience and potential safety concerns.

incident_description:
I was using the stove part of the oven to cook. While waiting for my soup to cook on the stove, I went into the other room. I could hear a beep coming ever so often from the kitchen. I hadn't set the timer, nor was I preheating the oven so I ignored the beep (thinking it was on tv) for the first couple times. After about 10-15 minutes I went into the kitchen to see if I could find the beep. There was a message on the clock part of the stove. It said F-4 or F-3 (I can't remember for sure, but it was something I hadn't seen) I could smell something "hot smelling" so I looked into the oven which is when I noticed the Broiler (top part) of the oven was on. I had not turned any part of the oven on so I was surprised it was and already getting very hot. I tried hitting the "cancel, off" button several times on my oven. I turned the stove off as well and tried hitting the cancel off button again. Nothing would work to turn the oven off, it just kept getting hotter to the point that it was making the counter and wall surrounding the oven very hot to the touch. After many failed attempts to turn the oven off we turned the power off to the oven. We tried about 20 minutes later to return power to the oven and immediately it started getting hot again on its own. 
I believe this is a serious safety issue. Our oven is only 10 years old. We have a  receipt of the date purchased. Had this happened when we were sleeping or not home I fear it would have burnt our house down. The amount of heat being thrown off from the oven for the less than half hour it was on was immense and I believe would have only gotten hotter. We currently have the power off to the oven so to prevent it from happening again and there is no way I will be endangering my family by returning power to it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Frigidaire smooth top range Model # FGEF3042KFC

Our range was not in use at the time this occurred. We had not used the range at all this entire day.

We heard a buzzing noise and went to see what it was. Sparks shot out from the area near the display panel followed by smoking. A few seconds later, flames started coming out from the display/control panel. We had to pull the range out and unplug it to make it stop.

What if we had been asleep?
justification: The incident caused flames and smoke, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Electric Range Slide in model  2002    ......Using the oven....what I was cooking was burning & causing tons of smoke...The broiler was blazing hot even though the broiler was not turned on.  We turned the breaker off because the broiler would not turn off even though the oven was completely turned off...Tried turning the breaker on a few times to see if the unit would re-set & again, without turning anything on, the broiler got blazing hot.  This exact model is not on the Sears recall list but the same year and same starting model #'s are on the recall list...Extremely bad fire hazard.  So thankful I was home when we encountered this problem.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
Early in the morning of October 30th at approximately 1:00 a.m., I was awakened by a loud crash in my home.  I went to investigate and as I walked down the hall to my kitchen I saw glass coming from the kitchen into the hallway and I heard crunching noises that sounded like a person or animal walking around on the glass.  I grabbed my dog and my cell phone and ran into my twin boys' bedroom and dialed 911and told them what was going on.  Shortly thereafter 8-10 San Diego policemen entered our home through my six year old boys' window with their guns drawn and swept the house for a possible intruder.  

What they found was that the outer glass panel on my 5-year-old Maytag oven had exploded and that the noise I heard was from the glass jumping and popping and breaking part which it continued to do for the next hour.  I recorded this on video.  I found that the glass had shot all over our kitchen and even found it as high as the top of the microwave which sits across the kitchen on the counter.  I had not used the Maytag  oven in several days and the oven had not been bumped, touched, etc. before this incident occurred.

After some internet research I learned that this has happened to many other people as well.  I am filing this report because myself or my children could have been seriously hurt by the flying glass if we had been in the kitchen at the time.  I am hoping that the CPSC will force Maytag's parent company, Whirlpool (and any other companies), to issue a recall of all appliances with this dangerous glass 

I filed a report with Maytag and they told me that it was just a "part failure".  I told them it was dangerous to consumers just like faulty brakes on a car and that it should be recalled but they did not care.  They said that the glass was safety glass but I did hurt my foot on a piece and I am sure that if it flew into someone standing nearby, into someone's eye, or fell onto a baby crawling under the oven someone could be seriously hurt or killed.

Please let me know what the CPSC is going to do to stop people from being hurt or killed by this exploding glass problem.  I can be contacted by way of my information below and I also have many pictures and two videos of the result of the glass explosion in my home.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (hurt foot) and had potential for serious harm, but no death occurred. The likelihood is 'possible' as similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description: I have an LG range, model LRE30755ST, serial no starting from 603. The burner fails to turn off
justification: The burner failing to turn off is an incident that could lead to potential hazards, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Basically the range at times will not close and the stove top will remain on at maximum heat. All controls on the LCD panel will be disable. The only way to close the LG range is to unplug its power from the outlet directly. I initially reported the indecent to LG after 53 weeks of usage and they told me that it was out of warranty. They only provide a 1 year warranty I was told. Other issues with this range include the LCD functions do not correspond ( example pressing the 8 on the LCD won't do anything and pressing the 2 will instead output 7 ). Yesterday the LG range decided to go into self clean mode and locked out the entire panel and did not respond. I was forced to pull the power from the wall, then waited an hour or so before plugging it back.

incident_description: [slow cooker] Lid Shattered
justification: The slow cooker lid shattered, but there was no injury.

incident_description: Bosch 500 SHE65T55UC 24" Dishwasher was purchased October 2013 and delivered mid-November 2013. Hardly used because of extremely bad odor from the dishwasher. I mostly would run it to clean it with vinegar and other suggestions by Bosch. Few weeks ago the junction box caught fire. Bosch authorized an appliance repair shop to diagnose and the repair shop took pictures and sent it to Bosch. Now Bosch has authorized repair of the box because they say it caught fire because of a power surge!!! When I search on the internet, I see a number of reported fires in exact part but with different models.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the junction box but no injury or death was reported, and similar issues have been reported with other models, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
On October 25, 2014, we had 10 over for supper.  My wife was cooking a pork roast in the lower oven and had just put the vegetables in the upper oven.  I was in the other room with a couple guests when she rushed in and asked me to take a look at the oven.  I opened the top oven and it exploded.  The only thing I assumed was that somehow gas was getting into the upper oven but it did not ignite until I opened the door.  I got a "sunburn" but nothing more serious.  I called Frigidaire on Monday, October 27th and explained what had happened.  The agent told me that she would call a service company to come to the house to repair.  She came back on the line and told me that someone from AllState Appliance (Rhode Island) would be here the following Thursday.  I told her that this was not satisfactory in as much as we were fearful to use the stove at all.  I then called Allstate and they nicely got someone to come over that afternoon.
The serviceman inspected the stove and told me that he thinks that when my wife "self-cleaned" the upper oven, it not only buckled the display panel but also "burned out a diode" that allowed this explosion to happen. He told me that he would order the parts and that they would be in within 7-10 days.  I asked if it was safe to use the stove and he told me that it was OK to use.  I didn't get a lot of comfort considering what had happened.
On November 3rd, I called Allstate to see if the parts were in.  They were not in.  She told me that the distributor did not have the parts in inventory.  I asked again: "Is the stove safe to use?"  She told me that "It should be safe after the parts are installed."  
On November 11th, I called Fridigaire to see if they could expedite the delivery of the parts.  [REDACTED] told me that they could not send parts to AllState as they had to send them to the distributor.  "OK, so when?"  [REDACTED] told me that it would be at least a week or more.  I asked her if it was safe to use the stove and she told me that it should be OK.  Not a lot of comfort here.
This is a new stove and it appears that Frigidaire doesn't really care about what happened.  I am concerned for our safety and others who have the same stove.
justification: The incident resulted in a 'sunburn' injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such oven explosions are not common but have happened in this case.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire refrigerator, purchased 12/2010 at Lowe's in Lexington, KY.  I was cleaning the shelves and vegetable bins this morning and one of the glass shelves exploded as I washing it.  The shelf had been removed from the refrigerator and I was holding it as I immersed it in about two inches of water in the sink.  The glass exploded and went ALL over the kitchen.  I was the only person in the kitchen when this occurred and was not injured.
justification: The glass shelf exploded but no injury occurred, making it an incident without harm. Such events are unlikely but not unheard of.

incident_description:
I have a Custom ClassicÃÂ Toaster Oven Broiler TOB-40.  Today I noticed that one of the two bottom electric heating element is bent upwards and has a longitudinal split.  There is now a separation between two layers of the element.  

I didn't hear anything.  I didn't see any sparks.  There was no indication that something had happened.  I just happened to notice the problem.  I don't know if the split happened at one time or if it was a gradual failure

incident_description:
Burnt index finger on T-FAL Encore 7.5" pan.
Metal gusset is long enough on the [REDACTED] type handle that a natural grip has index finger on the hot metal.
Even knowing this, I was also burnt on the next use.
Skin red, thick, joint stiff. No blister.

incident_description:
cooking microwave popcorn, I started smelling acrid smell.  I checked microwave, I pushed stop button, opened the door and flames were coming out of the top. I snuffed out fire with kitchen towel.  the top is melted, burned holes are in the interior, top of the microwave.
