incident_description:
Last month, I was eating meatloaf and bit into metal, which I later realized came from the blade of my less than three year old Cuisinart DLC-10S food processor. I will post a picture if that feature is available. It broke at one rivet and is cracked around two others. I'm really lucky I didn't break a tooth, cut my mouth, or swallow a piece of metal! 

When I went to buy a replacement blade, I learned that it is common for these blades to break, and people have reported this to Cuisinart and to you. See http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-FP-100TX-blade/product-reviews/B000TENO5A/ref=cm_cr_dp_qt_hist_one?ie=UTF8&filterBy=addOneStar&showViewpoints=0 and http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-FP-100TX-blade/product-reviews/B000TENO5A/ref=cm_cr_pr_hist_2?ie=UTF8&filterBy=addTwoStar&showViewpoints=0&sortBy=bySubmissionDateDescending
Altogether, 19 of 68 reviewers mention their blade breaking or cracking.

My blade broke from the underside, which is not someplace I ordinarily see. Cuisinart should include a warning to inspect all parts of this blade after use.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is high given the number of similar reports.

incident_description: I was making microwaveable popcorn in my Samsung over-the-range microwave (Model SMH1816S) when the door gasket melted and scorched. The extent of the damage was such that melted material clung to the inside of the microwave when I opened the door at the end of the cooking cycle. At the time, I was using the "popcorn" program button, and the cooking cycle was going normally. (My food did not burn at all.) There had been no other indication of microwave malfunction.
justification: The incident involved damage to the microwave but no injury or harm to the user.

incident_description: My wife was cooking dinner tonight on our 1 1/2 year old Kenmore range (model# 790.92183011) when the outer glass exploded, throwing glass everywhere. The oven temperature was set at 350 & thankfully my daughter had just moved out of the way. This is very disturbing to me being I have read numerous reports tonight describing similar  incidents with this model range. I feel this is a serious safety concern and that it needs immediate attention. Unfortunately, when I called Sears they said it could have been a bad batch/group of glass but they wouldn't cover it under warranty.
justification: The glass exploded, but no one was injured as the daughter had just moved out of the way.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore oven purchased in 2002, model #79075604104.  In the early morning on Saturday, November 8, my husband heard 3 loud noises.  On further investigation, we found that the inside glass on the oven door had cracked in 3 places.  The oven had not been used since Wednesday, and was turned off and cold.  We had not had any trouble with the oven in the past.  A quick internet search uncovered multiple reports of Sears' oven glass doors "spontaneously" breaking, many on newer ovens; however, when I contacted Sears, there were no reports of a recall.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous cracking of oven glass without injury, fitting severity level 2. Similar reports suggest this is a known but not extremely common issue.

incident_description:
(10/06/2014) The consumer stated that she had turned on the oven and set it to 350 degrees. In a matter of seconds she heard a crackling sound. She thought that it was the radio. She heard it again and went toward the stove and saw smoke coming the back of the stove. She immediately turned the oven off. She ran downstairs and flipped the circuit breaker box. She called her husband to tell him about the incident. When he came home, he pulled the stove from the wall and discovered that the attachment that goes into the circuit plate on the stove was burned.  

(10/07/2014) The consumer sent an email to Sears to advised them of the incident. She has not received a response.
The consumer is replacing the stove but will take pictures.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burned attachment but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The dishwasher was being used to wash dishes once a day. Approximately 10 days ago, the dishwasher begin to emit a burning smell, growing in intensity each day. We decided to not let the dishwasher run at night so it could be monitored. On 10/24/14, the dishwasher failed completely and would not start. 

Upon consulting the internet, we found that others had complained of a burning smell and the problem was with the control board. We disassembled the door panel and found that the control board had been completely burned through, and a connector and wiring harness were also burned and melted. 

The control board is mounted in a plastic cradle, and the top of the door  has a large plastic tray. We feel that there was substantial risk of a major fire and that the product should be investigated for recall. In addition, the fumes that were being emitted as the product burned up were potentially toxic and dangerous to humans and pets. 

Kitchenaid had replaced this unit in 2009 since our original dishwasher developed a leaking tub, which was guaranteed forever. That unit was bought from a big box store in 2007.
justification: The dishwasher was completely burned through, and a connector and wiring harness were also burned and melted. There was substantial risk of a major fire.

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report against her unit because she feels it poses a safety and fire hazard.

10/20/2014 The consumerÃÂs top oven burnt her food. Initially, she set the oven to 170 degrees Fahrenheit for ten minutes. For the past three to four days, the consumer reports that no matter what temperature she sets the oven to, within five minutes of turning it on, its temperature will automatically increase to 550 degrees Fahrenheit. The overheating of her oven prompts the fan to turn on automatically. She was able to become aware of the overheating problem with her unit because she hears the fan running. Since she has been there to turn the oven off, she has not burnt her food though she reports that indeed it has started turning black. Upper coils are red hot as if oven was set to broil.

The consumer uses the top portion of her double oven on a daily basis, while the bottom portion approximately ten times a month. 

10/21/2014 The consumer contacted both retailer and manufacturer. Representatives at both firms informed her that since there was no recall including the model and serial belonging to her unit, there was nothing they could do to assist her. 

The consumer reports that other than a burnt area above the top oven where the smoke comes out, her unit looks brand new.
 
The consumer states that the bottom oven has never given her problems. She is very careful handling the bottom oven and so does not have injuries of any type to report.
justification: The oven's malfunction poses a fire hazard and has caused food to burn, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report against her product because she feels it poses both a safety and fire hazard. 

10/11/2014 The consumer woke up in the morning and noticed the front, right burner on her range was turned on and fully engaged. Said burner is the hottest and largest one of her unitÃÂs five burners. The consumer reports that everything surrounding the range was hot, including the cabinets, granite, etc. The consumer slightly burned her fingers trying to shut it off because of the heat radiating from the unit. The consumerÃÂs husband had to switch off the breaker that provides electricity to the range. The consumer does not know the length of time the range was on. She went to sleep the night before with the range off and woke up to it on. 

The consumer reports that the control panel was not working for the remaining four burners. In order to continue using her range until she could repair it or afford a new one, the consumerÃÂs husband had to cut off the wires connecting to the faulty burner. The consumer indicates that this was the only way the burner would maintain itself off and the remaining would turn on when needed. 

The consumer called the retailer and they informed her that her unit was not included in a recall and therefore were unable to provide any assistance free of charge. They indicated that work on her unit would have to be paid for out of pocket by the consumer. 

The light on the microwave situated above the range is no longer working, although the consumer does not know if this is in correlation to the incident. The consumer reports that she uses her range on a daily basis and never had problems with it. She indicates that there are no apparent physical damages to her unit.
justification: The consumer was slightly burned, which is an injury, but there was no death or serious injury.

incident_description: Since purchasing the Samsung Dishwasher we have been displeased with several failing and melting plastic parts inside the washer. We constantly would smell a slight burning odor. We finally gave up on its inability to wash dishes and purchased a replacement. Upon removing the old washer we found that the cabinet it was against had been ruined from water damage and had some light burn marks. There is a plastic reservoir that I assume holds hot water and is not insulated or protected from exposure to the surrounding surfaces. The insulation around this piece was saturated from condensation. We feel fortunate that this unit did not cause a fire as we usually run the dishwasher at night when we are sleeping.
justification: The incident involved property damage (water damage and burn marks) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to recurring issues with the dishwasher.

incident_description: I purchased the Ge Cafe stove/oven on 3/14/12. I did some quick research on-line, and it appears from ConsumerReports.org that microwaves can turn on by themselves, especially KitchenAid and [REDACTED] brands. I will try calling KitchenAid tomorrow to see whether they've had other reports of this happening to the particular model we have and see if they have a specific suggestion as to what part might need fixing or whether to just have a repair person come out.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned without causing injury, but poses a potential fire risk, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the reported frequency of such incidents with this brand.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire Gallery Series Stainless Steel Smooth Top Electric Range and the front burner does not turn off. It will nit go down to low and sometimes comes on all by itself with out the switch being touched. On several occasions now have almost started a fire from things being on the stove and melting because the burner that was supposed to be off was still on high even though the switch is off.
justification: The burner malfunction has caused near-fire incidents due to unintended activation, posing a significant hazard without reported injuries.

incident_description:
This is concerning coffee cups that were purchased at a store "Anthropologie".  The cups are made in China and say they are microwave and dishwasher safe.

The first time we warmed something in them in the microwave, they did fine.  Since then, though, each time we microwaved them, they got so hot it was like a piece of metal out of an oven.  We decided we wouldn't put them in the microwave any more, but my husband wasn't aware of that and used one in the microwave a couple of days ago.  Although he didn't have it heating for long, it was so hot that it burned his fingers.  It looks like the milk he was warming was burned to the inside of the cup in one area.  

Another thing I found odd about these cups is that after they were microwaved a couple of times, some sort of material seems to have beaded up and burned on the edge of the cup.  Sort of like the cup had a coating of some sort over it that was damaged by the extreme heat.

In other words, this cup doesn't behave like a normal cup when microwaved. 

I worry about other people being burned by these cups, especially children, and worry about the material that beaded up on the edge.  If it is some unhealthy material used to coat the cup with.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the user's fingers, indicating an injury, and there is concern about potential harm to others, especially children.

incident_description: Toaster oven door was glass. It shattered as I opened it to take out the contents of the oven (hamburger patties). Glass flew into my eye. Glass flew across the room where my family was sitting. Glass flew all directions, as much as 12 feet away.
justification: Glass shattered and flew into the person's eye, causing injury, and also posed a risk to others in the room.

incident_description:
We purchased a Cuisinart Stainless Steel cooking set from our local JC Penney just over a month ago. After
dinner we set one of the lids in the sink by itself. About an hour later, we heard a loud bang. When we looked in the sink, the glass lid was shattered. We made sure nothing had dropped on it and no water was running. It had broken all by itself leaving glass in our sink and on our counter top. 
I did an online search and found a number of similar complaints. Cuisinart will replace the lid if we pay the shipping. But, who wants a lid that can shatter at any time? I don't want anyone in my household using these glass lids. So, we're left to buy replacement lids at our expense.
justification: The glass lid shattered without causing injury, but poses a potential hazard if used again.

incident_description: I used the apple wedger once and it broke and slit my thumb open.
justification: The incident resulted in a thumb injury, which is classified as a moderate severity level.

incident_description: When trying to turn on burner(s), the electronic (spark) ignition fails, but gas continues to emanate without control until a spark eventually lights flame or gas valve is manually closed.  At one point, the delay allowed a significant amount if gas to build up and spark occurred creating a ball of gas/ fire that covered the entire stove-top.
justification: The incident describes a significant gas buildup leading to a fireball, which poses a clear risk of injury.

incident_description: Kitchen Aid microwave khms155lss turns on by itself.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: The LG electric range malfunctioned and almost started a fire in my daughters house.  She turned the oven on and the thermostat/heating element did not shut off after preheating.  This resulted in the paint burning off the part of the oven where the vent is located.  After contacting LG we found out that there was a recall on this appliance.  They were uncooperative and refused to help.  Apparently the recall was for the top burner issue only. This range was purchased brand new about 7 or 8 years ago therefore the warranty is no longer in effect.  LG only offers a 1 year warranty. All the kitchen appliances that were purchased at that time are LG.  The refrigerator and the dishwasher.  The dishwasher has never been able to do an adequate job.  The refrigerator seems to be the only product which is functioning normally.
justification: The malfunction almost started a fire but no actual fire or injury occurred, and the issue is related to a known recall, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: (10/20/2014) The consumer stated that when she opened the door to put a cup in the microwave, the microwave started by itself. The consumer closed the door, waited a minute, open the door again. The same thing happened. The consumer stated that this has never happened before.
justification: The microwave started by itself without user input, which is an incident but caused no injury.

incident_description: Purchase a Kenmore dishwasher model 665.13032K113 about a year and a half ago. The heating element broke a piece off and burned a hole through the plastic dishwasher causing our floor to flood. The metal was so hot from the broken piece it actually made a hole through the plastic. A little longer and the hot piece of metal would have melted through completely though causing a risk of a fire below on floor or plastic parts below the dishwasher. Warranty did not cover but I think this is a safety issue more than anything and product should be recalled. Also we be contacting consumer rights groups and my personal attorney for immidiate refund as I believe it is not fair to have this for over a year and the amount to fix cost is greater than the purchase amount.
justification: The incident involved property damage (flooding and a hole burned through the dishwasher) but no reported injuries or death.

incident_description: Received new Samsung free standing stove/oven.  Upon hooking up the appliance and turning on the oven to see if it was working there was fire and smoke that erupted from wires in the back.  The burners were working fine as was the oven but something happened and smoke and fire started to erupt from the bottom back wire area.
justification: The incident caused fire and smoke, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using my oven, set at about 400 degrees when the inner glass door exploded. The door blew open with the force of the explosion and glass shot all over the kitchen. This is a new GE stove.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and glass shattering, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Bosch Free Standing Range HGS7282
After purchasing this Bosch Range In 2006, when I was cleaning the oven, heat escaped from It and melted the
knobs on the front of the range. Bosch repaired the item and it has worked fine until recently when the same thing
occurred. This time I got an error 41 message. When I called Bosch they told me to turn off power to the range at
the mains (which I did). It melted the knobs again and discolored the stainless steel outside above the door. the
Bosch repairman came today and said that heat was escaping from the door. They want to repair It, but I have a
concern this could happen again since it has happened twice now. The repairman told us that this was not a
common problem, although I have seen mention of it on the Internet.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: The Buck Company 501 pocket knife has a locking mechanism for the blade.  The locking mechanism on my recently purchased knife is defective.  This caused an injury that required me to go to the emergency room to have the wound taken care of.  This happened on the job and I filed a workman's comp claim and report.
justification: The defective locking mechanism caused an injury requiring emergency care, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the microwave oven is intermittently turning on and off, the control panel fails to power it off when this incident occurs.  The unit has to be unplugged.  He noticed the problem about a week ago.

10/2/14 The manufacturer was contacted and they advised him that they were aware that the microwave is defective and is willing to provide a discount to a new one.  10/9 The service technician came out and inspected the unit, caller was informed that repairs would cost him $450.00.

Caller is concerned that this unit is a fire hazard and that the manufacturer should be held responsible to recall and replace these units.
justification: The microwave's malfunction poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
((10/01/2014) The stated that the problem is with the ice maker tray. The consumer stated that the plastic piece on the end of the auger is breaking off. These pieces are going into his glass when he get ice from the ice maker. The consumer stated that he has gotten pieces of the plastic in his mouth.

(10/13/2014) The consumer called the manufacturer. He advised them of the incident. He was advised that there was not a recall on the unit. The consumer was advised that there was nothing that they could do about the issue.
justification: The consumer has gotten pieces of plastic in his mouth, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer is filing a report on his unit and all units with the same heating element design. He is concerned that KitchenAid and [REDACTED] ovens spontaneously turn on when the heating element breaks. The consumer was advised by a technician that the heating element in the oven is always energized with voltage so if the heating element breaks the unit turns on unexpectedly.

On the evening of 8/01/14 (estimated) the consumer's wife set the upper oven to cleaning mode. He states after 3 hours (a full cleaning mode cycle) the unit is supposed to shut off. However, the next morning the consumer noticed that the unit was "On" even though on the control panel indicated that it was "Off."

The consumer states the unit would not shut off and he had to cut the circuit breaker off. When the consumer turned the circuit breaker back on the unit remained off. 

The consumer states the next time he used the oven, the unit failed to turn off. The consumer states this occurred each time he used the unit. 

A technician has examined the unit on 3 different occasions since the incident occurred. He does not recall the dates. The technician informed the consumer the unit had a broken heating element that caused the unit to spontaneously turn on. The technician informed the consumer that all KitchenAid ovens have the same heating element design that cause the ovens to spontaneously turn on when the heating element breaks. One technician stated that [REDACTED] has the same failure mode. 

The consumer feels the units pose a burn and fire hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that turns on unexpectedly, posing a potential burn and fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Organicgreen Flip Jake Pancake Pan--I just bought this product last month at ROSS Department Stores in Corpus Christi, TX.  I've used the pan less than 5 times and today when I was cooking some bacon in it I lifted it off of the oven burner and the PLASTIC handle broke where it connects and is riveted into the pan base.  It was a clean break and from what I can tell the heat from the pan weakened the plastic handle which caused it to separate from the pan.  I was lucky because none of the grease in the pan burned me, but it did create a mess.  I called the Organicgreen customer support number (800)-280-5424 and talked with [REDACT] to tell him of the defect.  He said that I should return the pan and that they would send me a new one.  I DON'T WANT a new one, there is a defect in the design and a significant safety issue!!  [REDACT] mentioned that he would take it up with his supervisor...whatever?  I took pictures of the pan immediately after the incident and asked [REDACT][REDACTED] if Organicgreen wanted to see the photos of the pan.  No that's not required was the response.  Evidently Organicgreen isn't too concerned about safety related issues with their products??  They need to replace the plastic handle with a metal on like the rest of their pan have.  I'm an aircraft mechanic so I'm not stupid when it comes to engineering.

[REDACT]V/r  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a broken handle with no injury, but potential for harm due to hot grease, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with similar products.

incident_description: The eye on my smooth top range came on by itself on high and would not turn off.  I had to turn off the breaker at the box.  It is a Frigidaire Electric Smooth top slide in range PLES389ECG.  The manufacturers web site said my serial number was not in the recall list.  My serial number is NF64713248.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sharp Microwave Convection Oven R930CS-P Serial No 14984 Mgr April 2010 Purchased new 1012
Professionally installed during kitchen renovation
Platform does not securely sit on metal tri-armed wheel mechanism regardless of imprinted instruction of topside installation caused frequent arcing and burning metal oven sides

Recently the gearbase  holding this metal tri-armed wheel mechanism melted  filling oven with acrid smoke and again causing metal revolving platform to arc when coming in contact with oven walls. I burned my hand trying to remove the affected parts.

Curiously the touch pad does not light (except for time LEDs), which might allow operation empty ....did not happen in my case.  This oven was never used a convection, used sparingly for reheats, and kept meticulously clean.

incident_description:
I got the "Farberware Professional Ice Cream Scoop" on October 16, 2014.  I used it for the first time a few days later.  Had no problem with the first use.  The second use was on November 1, 2014.  After scooping the ice cream from the container, I depressed the lever on the scoop to eject the ice cream.  Two of the plastic gears in the eject mechanism broke/stripped off and fell out of the unit onto the kitchen counter.  

After assessing the situation, I felt it necessary to discard the bowl of ice cream, concerned there may be other fragments of the plastic gears in it.  It was chocolate chip ice cream, so the fragments would likely not have been very noticeable.

My concern is that this same situation could occur with others in the future, leaving plastic fragments in the food, potentially causing tooth damage or even choking.  I used the product as any reasonable person would use an ice cream scoopÃÂto scoop ice cream.

The phone contact number on the product packaging indicated that it was for "Residents of the state of California" only.  I did not bother writing or emailing the Company.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction that could have led to injury but did not result in any actual harm.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her husband turned on the microwave. The consumer stated that big flames and sparks came out from the inner side of the microwave. The consumer stated that the flames were coming from a plate on the inner right side.

The consumer stated that her husband pressed cancel and turned off the microwave.

The consumer has not used the microwave after that.

The consumer contacted the retailer and informed them of the incident. The consumer was told that microwaves only last for 2-3 years. The consumer was not offered any other assistance. 

The consumer purchased another microwave and is waiting on it to be delivered. 

The consumer has not contacted the manf yet but plans to do so.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks from the microwave, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool Range, Model RF364PXPQ1, purchased new in [REDACTED].

I recently discovered that the "HOT SURFACE INDICATOR" light, located in the cooktop surface,was no longer working. I removed the cooktop surface for further inspection, and found that the indicator lamp assembly, bearing part number 8523740 (which, according to two local appliance parts suppliers, has been discontinued by Whirlpool and there is no other replacement available) was partially melted. I unplugged the connector where this lamp plugged in at the back of the stove and checked for voltage. There was no voltage with the burners off. After turning on one of the burners, the circuit became energized at 120 volts. The circuit remained energized until the cooktop surface cooled down and power was shut off to the circuit. The lamp is a small neon indicator bulb which is enclosed in a plastic housing. This style of lamp draws very little current. It looks like the lamp gradually melted due to heat being trapped below the cooktop surface. I am concerned with two potential hazards here. First, there is no longer any warning that the surface is hot, which could lead to a burn if somebody accidentally touched it, or a fire if something accidentally was left on the surface. Second, because the melting distorted the plastic housing, this resulted in a bad internal connection in the lamp housing. As the plastic distorts, the bare contacts of the lamp could potentially contact one another and cause a short circuit when the circuit is energized. It is important to note that this circuit remains energized at 120 volts for several minutes after the surface has been turned off.
justification: The melted indicator lamp poses a burn and fire hazard due to lack of warning and potential short circuit, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
My large burner turned itself from 1.2 to high heat when I was simmering chicken stock. The broth was exploding from the pan and the unit was smoking. I had to move the pot while the boiling broth was splattering everywhere and got minor burns. I had the pull the whole unit out from the wall while flaming hot because I was unable to turn it off.
The faulty part was replaced and a few months later the same thing happened!  I was just holding some stock warm in a pot and it turned itself to high and was splattering everywhere. I had to do the same thing to turn it off. That time I was without a stove for 10 days.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns and repeated dangerous situations, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of the issue suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: On 10/8/2014 my dishwasher caught fire.  Luckily we were home and were volunteer firefighters.  After shutting off the electrical breaker, We disconnected the dishwasher and moved it outside.  We contacted Maytag/Whirlpool who opened a case, and sent a local technician to inspect the unit.  It was deemed unrepairable, and Maytag but has not returned our calls.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but no injuries were reported, and the situation was managed by volunteer firefighters.

incident_description:
I had purchased 50 count, 18 oz, Hefty plastic drinking cups, in green for a party I was having. Myself, my girlfriend, our son, and all our guests were drinking out of these cups. The next day, as I was drinking out of one of the cups, I got something stuck in my throat. I was able to cough it up and it was a long "shred" of plastic. I then looked through the rest of the package of cups and removed several more pieces of plastic from the inside of the cups. I saved the pieces and wrote a letter to the Reynolds company. I plan on sending the letter along with the bag of plastic pieces, but wanted to contact you first. I have brought the unused portion of the cups back to the store and received my money back for them.
When I had purchased them, I had bought a package of black and a package of green, the black ones did not appear to be faulty, only the green. I have purchased these same cups in the past and never had this issue before.
justification: The incident involved a physical injury (plastic stuck in throat) but no lasting harm, and the issue was isolated to one batch of cups.

incident_description: I am contacting you in regards to a product I bought 2 of for my children.  Spill proof, double wall, bpa free, sip chug Cool Gear canister/cup.  Halloween editions: Pumpkin Potion & Witch's Brew.  This is NOT safe for children what so ever!  (*There is also NO age limit for this cup)  My youngest son (age 3) got his thumb stuck inside of the spout.  There is an absolute RIDICULOUS design of a flap (inside the spout-attached to the slide to open/close) -it made it almost impossible to get his finger out.  (When we pulled up on it it clamped his finger even tighter)  My husband and I had to quite literally break the slider off in order to release his finger.  It took us almost 20 minutes of him screaming bloody murder in order to get it off of him.  I am absolutely appalled and angry that this product is available for children when it is a hazard.  He has a huge blister now, swelling and redness.  Thank goodness he can even move his finger after that!  I don't want anyone else getting hurt by this product.  Please put a stop to this!
justification: The child suffered a significant injury (blister, swelling, redness) requiring intervention to free his thumb, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
(10/12/2014) The consumer stated that she was cooking her dinner. Eight minutes before the end of the cooking time, the timer clock changed and indicated F3. The oven started glowing red. Extreme heat was flowing from all areas of the oven. The oven door locked. She looked at the display which indicated cLn-cooL. This indicated that the oven had gone into the cleaning cycle. The consumer tried to hit the off-cancel button to do a safety shut-off. But it would not respond. The consumer stated that the oven was so hot she had to use oven mitts. The power had to be disconnected at the circuit breaker.

(10/12/2014) The consumer contacted Sears. A dispatch was set up for 10/14/2014.

(10/14/2014) The technician came out. His name was [REDACTED]. He pulled the oven out from the wall, and open the back to expose the circuit. He went to the breaker to turn the power back on. Immediately, the oven went to broil. The dispatcher wrote in his notes that the temperature probe open to EOC-EOC shorted out-Broil is on all the time. The consumer was advised that the connector to the circuit board failed. 

(10/14/2014) The consumer's husband called the company and advised them of what happened. He was advised that they would email them a 10% off coupon or have a technician come out to service the oven. He was also advised that they would forward the safety concerns over to the manufacturer which is now LG.

(10/14/2014) The consumer called Sears and spoke to [REDACTED]. The consumer called to advise them of what the technician had found. 

The consumer was also advised that the company had researched and found no recall on the unit. The consumer was advised that the safety information was forwarded to LG. She was also advised that safety warnings would be left up to LG.

The consumer was advised that Sears would only offer them the 10% coupon.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a safety hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
I have a 10 year old Kenmore oven. Model number 790. The bottom ovens glass front exploded at 8:30 am. There was no one in the kitchen at the time. Small pieces of glass were all over the kitchen as far as 15 feet away. The oven door exploded at a time that the oven was not on nor without anything hitting it. The lower oven had not been used in months and has never used the self cleaning option. Only two of us live at the home and there are no small kids running around that could have bumped into the glass over time.
This is a safety concern because of the of thousands of little pieces of glass that traveled at high speed up to 15 feet from the oven. Someone could have been seriously injured if they were in the room at the time.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing potential injury risk, but no one was present at the time.

incident_description: Plastic handles that cover the side metal lifting loops crumbled due to overheating.
justification: The plastic handles crumbled but there is no mention of injury or death, only material damage.

incident_description:
Cuisinart DCC-3000
When the coffee stopped brewing, it started coming out of the coffee maker ,burned me and overflowed all over the counter and floor. This a coffeemaker "on demand". You are supposed to put your cup under the maker, and push the lever down to get your coffee.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) given the described malfunction.

incident_description: I was putting a Duralex glass bowl into my cabinet and it literally exploded - like it was a bomb.  The glass explosion cut my leg.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the leg, which qualifies as an injury. Glass explosions are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his over the counter microwave purchased in September 2005 with no
problems at all until September 24th, 2014, when the front tempered glass shield fell from the
appliance door when the caller shut the door.
The caller said he did not shut the door hard, he shut it just as anyone allows the door to be shut after
removing whatever has been heated.
He is reporting this incident happened as a failure of the supporting frame on the appliance door
cracked and precipitated the fall of the glass panel shield on to the stovetop below. The caller reports
that the color of the plastic at the bottom area of the support failure is significantly different from the
extant frame of the appliance and hypothesizes that a related cause in the incident is the long-term
presence of heat originating at the stovetop. The caller reported that the distance from any source of
heat was over twice the recommended distance recommended by the appliance manufacturer, hence
this catastrophic structural failure of the support frame of the door panel glass shield should not
have occurred.
It is being reported as a safety hazard due to a consumer expectation that an appliance designed to
be installed above a source of heat such as a stove top for any number of years of service cannot be a
source of structural failure when utilized in that capacity because food, oils and liquids may be in the
process of cooking and preparation and be the source of scalding or fire to the user or bystander
when both areas of stovetop and microwave oven are in use simultaneously.

There were no injuries reported.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does plan to contact them.
justification: The incident was a structural failure of the appliance, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Came home and opened fridge to find light very hot and the fixture melting, terrible smell of burning plastic. After finding out online that there was a product recall I called Sears and our fridge is part of the recall (I'd like to add that we were never informed of this recall even though we had registered and even had the extended warranty). After further online research I am wondering if we shouldn't insist on a whole new fridge as it seems many people have had this problem repeat itself. What if we are on vacation and this happens again? Or even just gone for a bit too long? Our home could catch on fire! I am very nervous about this now. Scary!
justification: The incident involved a hazardous situation with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

Looked it up online and discovered that MANY, MANY users have had the element crack, on both the first unit and the warranty replacement. I believe the unit should be recalled.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG range model LRE3083ST in July of 2014.

I called LG, and they stated this was expected behavior.  They would not send a technician to investigate.

incident_description: 1 year old Panasonic Microwave Modle NN-SA6615 caught fire when melting chocolate in a glass bowl.  The fire stopped when the microwave was disconnected and started again with nothing in it when we tried restarting for a few seconds.  No one was injured

incident_description:
Cuisinart Convection Toaster Oven Broiler TOB-60 Series
To run the toaster you have to turn the dial past 20 minutes and then back to where you want it, usually about 3 or 4.  The oven element heats up and the timer ticks, the dial turns to zero.  It stops ticking quietly but never dings, and doesn't turn off.  Has to be manually turned off.

incident_description: This item is a Kenmore Elite Refrigerator Serial #303KR00364 purchased from Sears stores in Fresno Ca. This product is used in my home kitchen. The item does not work properly as the fridge's fan stops working and allows everything to melt causing water to pool in the kitchen. Yesterday I feel because I didn't notice a pool of water on the kitchen floor. Sears has sent their extended warranty team twice already to repair the fridge to no avail a it breaks again after a few weeks of them coming to fix it. I purchased the refrigerator July of 2013 and by August 2014 the problem started, so they say I was 2 weeks out of 1 year warranty  so they can't replace it ( I bought their extended warranty). They have been here twice this year already to fix the fridge, this will be their third time since August 2014 to attempt to fix it. This product is dangerous to me and my family as my husband is 72 years old and his falling can have bad consequences. I fell and now my elbow hurts. Please investigate this product. Please

incident_description:
Ref to Report Nu.: 20141029-2aa0b-1437662
Our house was build around 2005. We just purchased this pre-owned home. We have a GE Microwave and double wall oven (32681230p001 model nu. JTP48S0F3SS Serial nu. GH604308 )NOTE I am reading these numbers off the second oven door. On 10/27/2014, I set the top-oven to self-clean and few minutes later heard a hugs noise and find the inner oven glass-door cracked/shattered in a very tiny pieces. I have never ever seen this before. My small research online shows many others have reported the same issue with their GE appliances. Although, it appears there is no report on this serial nu? Was told by GE Consumer Relation that there is no recall on this oven/issue. I have taken few photos and had a repairman to come and check it on Oct 28th. But I think, this is very dangerous if one would open the door and shattered glass would be everywhere or on them. If a blind person was operating this oven would be hurt badly  by the shattered glasses. So Please do something about this important safety issue. Thanks

incident_description: A month or two ago, I was baking fish in a pyrex baking dish in the oven at 375 degrees.  It was towards the end of the process when the dish suddenly shattered in the oven.  I thought it was very unusual and had no explanation.  Then yesterday, I was looking something up (unrelated) at the library in an older issue of Consumer Reports and discovered that this is becoming a common problem, related to a change in formula that [REDACTED] and Pyrex are now using to make their products in a cheaper way.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering in the oven, but no injury was reported. The occurrence likelihood is high as it is described as a common problem.

incident_description: This morning (10/28/14) at 4:30am after making an espresso, my Nespresso U espresso machine started to emit dense white smoke and the outer plastic case of the machine began to deform. After quickly unplugging the machine and carrying it outside it continued to emit dense choking white smoke that was apparently the plastic melting.
justification: The incident caused damage to the machine but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: The big glass door on my Kenmore double oven stove basically exploded.  The stove and ovens were not in use at the time.  It was a Saturday and the last time the oven had been used was on Tuesday of that week.  Glass  particles went as far as 10 feet.
justification: The glass door exploded, causing glass particles to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Maytag refrigerator that can be very dangerous. The handle on the freezer door comes all the way to the bottom of the door sticking out several inches. When leaning into the refrigerator to grab something you have to duck down not to hit the corner of the freezer door. Many times I have hit my head and just thought that was stupid then one day I hit it hard enough to knock me out and down to the floor. I have looked at many of their designs online, they have more than Maytag and I see most of the Top Freezer refrigerators have the freezer door handle too low and is a danger to hitting a person's head. They NEED to make there handles flush or almost flush with the bottom of the freezer door.
Please, someone look at these it's just a problem on their refrigerators with the Freezer on top. The freezer handles stick out several inches making it possible to hit your head. I like my refrigerator I just shouldn't have to duck down to not get hurt by the handle. This is the current models that are selling today, many others will have this same problem.
justification: The description reports a head injury severe enough to cause unconsciousness, indicating injury severity (level 3), and mentions frequent head impacts, suggesting a likely recurrence (level 4).

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she is experiencing problems with oven racks.  Whenever she is baking in the oven the racks tend to collapse which is very dangerous and can cause burn hazard to the user.  She stated that she had noticed numerous complaints online and does not why there has not been a recall as yet.

This incident has been ongoing for a year.  She has not received any service calls since.  She has contacted the retailer 10/2013 and at least 4 times after about this issue but each time they were charging her to send a technician out but she did not feel that she should be charged for a manufacturer's defect.
justification: The incident involves a hazardous situation with oven racks collapsing, posing a burn hazard, but no actual injury has been reported.

incident_description:
(10/19/2014) The consumer stated that he had something in the microwave. The timer went off. He opened the microwave and it was still going. He hit the off button a couple of times but the unit would not turn off. The consumer disconnected the unit at the circuit breaker. The unit went off. The consumer tuned the breaker back on. The microwave came on by itself.


(10/19/2014) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. He was advised to take the unit to their repair office. He was also advised that he would be charged for the repair. 


(10/20/2014) The consumer called the Corporate office and was advised of the same thing.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue was addressed by contacting the manufacturer.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore gas range model number 79077483804.
Today I was starting to use this gas oven.  The oven was cold and looked perfectly fine, I set the oven temperature to a low temperature of 220 degrees Fahrenheit then immediately opened the oven door, the oven was not warm yet as I had just started it.  As I pulled the door open in the normal way the outer door glass shattered into pieces.  I did not touch the glass at all, I simply pulled the handle to open the door and the glass shattered.  Again, nothing touched or struck the glass.  The two layers of inner oven glass is intact, only the outer glass panel broke.  Again, the oven had just been turned on to a low temperature setting and was not at all warm yet. 
There were glass pieces as far as five feet from the oven, there were no injuries.
This gas range has been in service since July of 2009 and until now (10/23/14) has worked perfectly.
I have a photograph of the incident.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of the oven door glass without any injuries, fitting the criteria for severity level 2.

incident_description:
Regarding:  Kenmore Refrigerator Model 795.77314600, Serial 608MRRH09486, Manufactured Date 2006.08.

On October 21, 2014 I opened by Kenmore Side by Side Bottom Refrigerator to find a fire hazard.  I opened the door and hazy smoke and an acrid smell confronted me.  I then notice that the digital display and lamp (bulb) unit on top were melting off the top off the refrigerator.  I immediately unplugged the refrigerator to be sure that the unit would not start a fire.  I called Sears and after first telling me to remove the bulb and that they would send a replacement if I requested it. I was unsatisfied with this answer and spoke to another individual in the Customer Solutions area.  She informed me that a service call would not be available until November 13 (the earliest).  I waited on hold (at least 20 minutes) as she made the appointment to this other department located in North Carolina while she is located in Texas.  I called again the next day and got the same responses, however, it was revealed that the refrigerator was on a "Newsflash" but not a recall.  I got a [REDACTED], and was told that she send several message to put my repair date sooner.  She stated that someone would be available on October 27 between 1-5pm to look at the refrigerator.  

Today, October 27, I called to confirm the appointment, and to my surprise there is none scheduled.  At this point, I disappointed with the treatment of the employees of Sears as well as the lack of dignity and respect they show me as a consumer.  More than that, I believe this product should be recalled for the fire hazard that it is.  If I had not opened the refrigerator at that time, my family and I would have gone to bed without realizing there was a problem and potentially suffered physical, emotional and personal property damage.  It seems that Sears will not accept the responsibility for the defective product and the potential damage that it may cause and will not replace the refrigerator. 

I am hoping this issue can help myself and others to get a replacement for the defective appliance.  We should not bear the cost of faulty workmanship and inferior materials. At this point, I have no refrigerator and I am waiting for the supervisor ([REDACTED]) of the Customer Solutions area to call me back.   She has the luxury of a 24 hour window, while I have a cooler filled with food and 3 more weeks to wait for a repairman.  

My family has purchased several appliances through Sears, but in the future, we will seek out a company that is dignified where their consumer is concerned.  Any assistance with regard to this problem would be greatly appreciated.  Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with melting components, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description:
When the door of our Kenmore Elite wall oven was opened, the oven rack fell off the side support, slopping a pot of 350 degree food in the oven. Only luck and fast responses prevented major burns to the person checking on the food.

We are now able to use the oven only with the rack in the lowest position, with light dishes.

The oven is a model 790.47882602, serial number NF81113819.

I have contacted two different Sears customer service phone numbers, each time being told that if I am not the original purchaser of the oven, nothing can be done, and that I would have to pay for a service call to be provided with a repair estimate. When I explained that it is a safety issue they didn't respond any differently.

There are multiple descriptions of this oven failing the same way, in all ages of the oven, so I believe Sears is probably aware of the problem.
justification: The incident involved a safety hazard with potential for burns, but no actual injury occurred due to quick response.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that earlier in the day she had used the self-clean feature. Afterward. the oven came on by itself. She stated that she had to unplug the range to get the oven off.

justification: The incident involved a flame and malfunctioning oven, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Dishwasher started smelling like burning electronics and plastic while it was washing dishes.  

I removed the door panel to investigate. The burning smell was coming from the control board. It appears to be a relay that was overheating and smoking. It also melted the power connector to the control board. It is very likely this would have resulted in a fire had I not been nearby.

GE Profile Dishwasher
Model number PDW8700J10CC
Serial Number HH829513B
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoking components, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The oven turned on by itself and was on for several hour
damaged the laminate on counter top
It turned on by itself again while my wife was in the kitchen
justification: The oven turning on by itself caused property damage but no injury, and the recurrence suggests a possible likelihood.

incident_description: I was driving when I had lifted contigo auto seal pinnacle travel mug containing hot tea and taken to my mouth to take sip. There is a button on the side which I pressed as instructed to get the tea out. Suddenly while vehicle in motion hot tea sprayed out on to my face burning the upper portion of my face. Later in the day I was diagnosed for 2nd degree burns.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents can happen but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
(10/03/2014) The consumer stated that she noticed a smell of gas. She looked at the stove and noticed that the fuse was blown. Her husband checked the circuit breaker and turned it back on. When he turned the breaker on something sparked from the stove and a lot of black smoke came for the back of the stove. The consumer took a fire extinguisher and squirted it on the back of the stove. incident_description:
Bosch dishwasher model number SHU53A06UC /14,  serial number FD830300121

At approximately 23:00 last night, the dishwasher was operating in wash cycle, when the front control panel burst into flames.  Luckily I smelled smoke immediately, and put the fire out with an extinguisher.  The plastic laminate countertop above was heat damaged (blistered) and the house filled with smoke.  

Upon googling "dishwasher on fire", I discovered there was a 2009 voluntary recall of this product, citing specifically the danger of fire from a defect in the control panel.

Although I registered my product when I purchased it in 2003, I HAVE NEVER RECEIVED ANY WRITTEN, E-MAIL, PHONE OR FAX NOTIFICATION OF A PRODUCT RECALL.  I was completely unaware of the recall until last night.  I have no recollection of any public notice in Canada (newspaper, billboard, radio ad, TV ad) of this recall, nor has any of my friends and neighbours I've spoken to.

My children, ages 9 and 6, were asleep at the time.  It is a miracle no one was hurt, and damage to the house was not worse.

I ask you, what assurance do we have as consumers of REASONABLE NOTICE of a product recall, when the defect is LIFE THREATENING.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing property damage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I was using the toaster oven to reheat pizza.  I set the timer dial to 10 minutes and after that time heard the bell go off signaling it was done.  I was working on something else in the kitchen so I didn't get the pizza out right away.  A few minutes later I smelled something burning & went to the toaster oven...The timer dial had gone past the 'off' point and continued all the way to the 'Stay On' position.  Moving the dial back to the 'off' didn't turn the device off, the timer again travelled to the 'Stay On' position.  Not having any other means to turn the device off, I unplugged it.  

This is a faulty design that could have caused a fire.  This spring-loaded timer dial works by turning it clockwise from 'Off' to set a specific time and turning it counter-clockwise from 'Off' to have the oven be constantly on.  Unfortunately, a faulty 'stop' at the Off position causes the unit to go to the 'stay on'  position indefinitely.  The failsafe 'stop' position on an oven like this should be OFF, not ON!
justification: The incident involved a faulty toaster oven design that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

I was baking french fries in our GE Spectra Oven (electric) and went to the living room for a minute. One of my kids noticed what appeared to be flames and sparks through the glass oven window. I ran back to the kitchen where smoke was pouring out of the oven and I turned it off and backed up. The flames and sparks stopped almost a minute after I turned it off, however smoke continued to fill the kitchen. We opened the windows and ventilated the house.
After everything appeared calm in the oven and the smoke had cleared, I opened the oven to see what had happened.  The top heating element (broil element?) was broken into pieces laying around the oven and on the fries I was cooking.
Clearly this is a severe issue considering the flames, sparks, and smoke that filled my house and after visiting numerous other consumer websites, this is an issue that has been experience by hundreds of other consumers.
WHEN IS THE RECALL?
I am about to pay out of pocket to replace the oven because who knows when the bottom element will have the same issue? Or, if I replace the top element, when will it catch on fire again? And the next time, will I or someone else notice before the whole house is filled with smoke or food in the oven catches on fire and the fire potentially escapes the oven catching my house on fire, in either case threatening the lives of my family? Plus the smoke damages the house and reduces it's resale value unless I pay to repair the damages.
THIS IS A SIGNIFICANT, PERSISTENT ISSUE, MORE THAN WORTHY OF A RECALL -- GE SHOULD EITHER PAY TO REPLACE THE HEATING ELEMENTS WITH SAFER COMPONENTS OR PAY FOR NEW OVENS.
Apparently, they are aware of this issue and have done nothing at this time.

My light bulb housing is melted and warped like the other units that I have read about.  My understanding from reading is that this issue is caused by a bad controller board causing lights (there are two bulbs in this unit) to stay on and melt the light housing components.
justification: The incident involves a safety-related issue with the light housing melting, which could lead to food spoilage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
On November 29, 2010, my husband and I purchased a built-in double oven from Lowe's of Abilene, TX, Store# 138.
The salesperson was [REDACTED]. This was a combination regular oven, plus a smaller convection/microwave. The oven was installed in our kitchen on February 22, 2011, by Lowe's installer [REDACTED] The double oven is a GE Profile Model number PT916S R1SS, and the microwave/convection oven is Model number PEB 1590 SM 2SS.

I am very concerned that the installation was not done correctly, or that the product is defective, because whenever I use the upper convection oven, the wood cabinetry above the oven become so hot that I'm fearful they will combust and catch fire. The items in the cabinet above the oven also become very hot to the touch ... too hot to pick up. I have even tried opening the cabinet doors in hopes of some of the heat escaping, but the cabinet shelf above and the items inside still become extremely hot to the point I'm fearful of a fire (not to mention the that the wood cabinets would begin to warp due to extreme heat).

I am very disappointed that Lowe's has not corrected this problem. Our original salesman, [REDACTED], did come out with another staff person some months after we stated our concerns. But during his investigation, he turned the oven on for only a short period of time, which did not provide an adequate test of the extreme heat conditions I have continued to experience above the microwave convection oven. I had not used the oven much, but as I began to use it more, I have become more and more concerned. I spoke to the manager [REDACTED] about this last month, and he said there was nothing
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to excessive heat, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that it was reported to him that the dishwasher caught fire.  He was not present at the time so did not have much detail of what led up to the incident.  He feels that the heating coil overheated which caused the electrical components to melt.  The Manchester Fire Dept Manchester, NH filed a report in regards to the incident.  Time approx 7pm. The dishwasher model was not visible due to burnt marks.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that the dishwasher poses a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries were reported. The incident was documented by the fire department, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
Glass door on Kenmore range exploded.  Hot, shattered glass all over the floor, in a house full of children and pets.

Kenmore will not replace because it is out of warranty (3 years old).  However, they tried very hard to sell me 1-year service protection plan for $239.99.

The Customer Service representative asked if the oven got too hot.  This is an oven, folks, the darned things get hot - biscuits hot!  What kind of question is that? 

I will be filing complaints every place possible.
justification: The incident involved a glass door explosion with no reported injuries, but potential danger to children and pets.

incident_description:
Was using the range to bake a fish for about 30 minutes and then I switched  Bake to Broil.  After more or less 5 minutes of broiling, when I tried to Cancel broiling, the Feature Guide is so hot and soft and I am not able to Cancel or turn off the unit. The lower part of the  outer metal part below   the Feature Guide is starting to get brownish discoloration or starting to smell burnt. The only way the unit can be turn off is for us to pull forward the range unit to access the gas line shut off valve and to disconnect the gas and electric.  When the unit cooled off the the FEATURE GUIDE key pad is wrinkled.  The fish being broiled is not burnt.

The unit in being reported for posing a fire hazard and safety concern is a whirpool Stainless Steel Gas Range  # 705975  which was bought on line on Costco.com on June 20, 2014  ordered # [REDACTED] and was returned to Costco outlet here in Stockton on October 5, 2014. I was informed Costco will return appliance to the manufacturer when I requested for them to make a consumer report.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance that posed a fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
Our KitchenAid refrigerator caught fire on 10/10/2014.  We were fortunate to be home and able to take action pulling the refrigerator out and unplugging.  Fire still continued with lots of black smoke filling the room and home.  I removed the lower back cardboard panel and put the fire out. Flame was still 3 plus inches with power removed.  The starter solenoid on the compressor shorted and melted also melting the metal prong on the compressor and electrical wires connected to the relay.  

Today a technician came out and verified the refrigerator damage and stated the relay is not wired to ground so power continues without tripping the circuit beaker resulting in fire.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a serious fire that could have caused significant damage if not stopped.

incident_description:
As I was making a smoothie a couple of days ago (Oct. 8th), a piece of the blade broke off the NutriBullet without my knowledge. I poured my smoothie into a glass and proceeded to drink it. A piece of the blade was in my mouth and thinking it was a piece of strawberry I chewed it. If I swallowed it I would have choked. I want to know why a blade would break off during making a smoothie. I have only had it for 5 months. What action do they plan to take and how are they going to prevent this from happening to someone else. What if this happened to an elderly person or a young child? I was promised a newer, hopefully better, version. However, they had FedEx come to pick up the damaged harmful NutriBullet and have not given me a full refund or the newer NutriBullet. I have fibrous dysplasia (benign tumor) in my mouth (jaw area), if this had cut that area or I had swallowed it (the blade is smooth, but sharp) I would have been seriously injured or it could have been fatal. I have pictures that I would like to send to your attention. Nutribullet was sent the pictures and is aware of the problem, however they are doing nothing to address it. Order placed: May 11, 2014 Received Tues. May 20, 2014 TOTAL $117.77 SHIP TO [REDACTED] ORDER # [REDACTED] I am now requesting a full refund and the replacement as promised. I would like the public to know the dangers of the Nutribullet that I received, so that no one is injured, especially the elderly and children. 

P.S. I have pictures that I would like to share with you of the blade.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade that could have caused serious injury or death, but the user only experienced a near-miss with potential harm.

incident_description:
Consumer reported that she have always been pleased with the cookware and dishware that was purchased from Pyrex, and have always recommended their products. However, recently she had a Pyrex glass cookware explode when pulling it out of the oven. Not only did it ruin her dinner, but it also ruined her oven. When the glassware shattered, it fell on the oven door, shattering the glass on the inner door. Luckily her one yr old was not present in the kitchen at that time, because it sent 400 degree temperature glass pieces everywhere, and was thankful she was not harmed either.
 
She is extremely displeased and disappointed in the product in which she purchased. She would be more than happy to send pictures of this matter, and would appreciate any assistance the agency may offer in this issue. She attempted to contact Pyrex concerning this issue, and they informed her that after she sent in the glass remains that their "examiners" indicated there was a "scratch on the inside sidewall surface which was the origin of breakage. And, and that the dish broke as a result of being chilled while it was hot." She found it interesting that they concurred that a non-visible "scratch" was the cause of the glass explosion in my kitchen.  Thus, ruining my oven, and unnecessarily placing my toddler and myself in danger. They magically discovered a scratch after it exploded into tiny shards, when she didn't see it prior to putting anything in the dish, because if she had, she would not have used the dish. Also they falsely accused her of chilling the dish while hot. It was never chilled, nor did she state anything of such. The dish broke in the oven, and that is how it broke the oven door, unless their examiners think an oven is a refrigerator.

It sounds to her, they might want to invest into better "examiners" and into a better product, because if a non-visible scratch was the cause of this incident as they stated, doesn't sound like a very durable product. She is fully aware of Pyrex capabilities (glass grenade) and limitations (everything food related), and feels that the agency should be aware as well.  She will keep in mind if she ever want to have exploding glass in my kitchen, and a broken oven again to be sure to use Pyrex, and will recommend to others of such. Also, she feels that they should make sure to add to the safety and usage, that once the product is removed from bubble wrap, the object is a consumer hazard.
justification: The incident involved exploding glass cookware causing property damage but no injuries, as the consumer and toddler were unharmed.

incident_description:
Caller purchased an electric range July 2014 and she cannot use the oven without the broiler turning on also.

The caller has used the oven only a few time but the broiler has turned on each time and burned her food.
She is reporting to alert the public of any safety issues regarding this issue.

There are no injuries

The caller has contacted the manufacturer and she said that they told her to contact CPSC

The consumer added: Self-cleaning oven turned it on to clean the oven...The door won't open until the oven is clean and the stove door won't open until the oven has cooled off....Also, there is smoke coming out of oven to the top left side of the stove...Thank you
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven causing burned food and smoke, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was getting milk out of the refrigerator in the morning. The consumer smelled plastic burning before she opened the fridge. The consumer opened the fridge and the smell got stronger. 

The consumer stated that all of the food on the top shelf (where the lighting compartment is) had melted.

The consumer stated that that the two bulb sockets that hold the bulbs have turned brown. 

The consumer stated that there is no plastic melting in the bulb compartment, as of now. 

The consumer's unit is not included in any relevant recalls.

This was a very scary event!  When the consumer opened the door to the fridge, the heat was intense.  Outside door very warm.  Consumer had raw chicken on top shelf that was partially cooked from the heat.  Consumer was leaving for vacation the next day.  Consumer's house would have burned down without a doubt had she not been home.  Had consumer been at work her dog would have died in a fire.  Not to mention all food had to be disposed off do to heat.  This was at least $300.00 worth of food.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Our dishwasher burst into flames and smoke. I unplugged it under the sink. It filled the house with foul smelling smoke. we opened the doors and set up fans.
I could see the top control panel was burnt, meted and warped with smoke damage coming out of both right and left ends and the latch. I removed the inner metal panel of the door and we could see all the wires black and a widespread burned and melted area with a hole melted completely through the circuit board and connections all fried. also a burn hole back into the dishwasher.
I used a plastic garbage sack slid over the dishwasher door and secured with tape around the bottom to contain the foul smell of the burnt parts so we could sleep later on after running the fans for 3 1/2 hours.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a serious incident that could have caused injury if the fire had spread.

incident_description:
Product: Whirpool Side by Side Refigerator
Model No. GD5SHAXKQ00
Manufactured November 2011

My refrigerator stopped cooling so I moved the refrigerator away from wall and saw black burn marks on the wall behind the refrigerator. I removed the back cover of the refrigerator and saw there had been a fire in the refigerator. 

I called Whirlpool and they sent out a technician to repair the refrigerator with no cost to me. About a year later, the week of September 22nd 2014, the same thing happened again. I called Whirlpool, and this time, they won't pay to repair the refrigerator. They also said they didn't have a record of my previous incident.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a serious incident that could have caused a fire, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: I was cooking broth in my crockpot. I turned the temperature from high to low and seconds later the glass lid shattered into hundreds of pieces. I had only used it 5 times and there had been no visible damage.
justification: The glass lid shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The top oven glass door of our Double Wall oven (KitchenAid KEBS208SSS) exploded like a bomb spitting out hot glass through the vents as far as 20 feet across the kitchen, during the self clean cycle. There were thousands of tiny pieces of tempered glass shatters left within the oven itself and across our kitchen. Luckily, no one was in the kitchen at the time and even more fortunate, we were home and able to shut the power off at the main circuit to turn the oven off. What if we had not been home? Would our house have burned down? I would never consider leaving the house with the oven on self clean but others might. 
After many phone calls to the head office in Tennessee, and a lot of back and forth, our oven was finally replaced in July 2014.
justification: The incident caused significant damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is low as it's a rare event based on the description.

incident_description: my Jenn Air stove / cooktop range  model JDR8895 serial number 10763539GA caught on fire from the control panel.  flames came out the back of the control panel while I was cooking on the stove top and using the top oven.
justification: The incident involved flames from the control panel, indicating a significant hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Refrigerator light remains on when doors are closed resulting in overheating of the light assembly sufficient to melt the plastic cover and frame, scorch the light sockets and melt the refrigerator's plastic ceiling above the light fixture recess.
justification: The incident causes damage to the refrigerator but does not cause injury or death, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: While running dishwasher, it stopped in the cycle, and the appliance smelled like something was hot so, I unplugged it (It is a portable unit) and called the repair company I use. He came out and found that the connector that connnect the power cable to the dishwasher wiring harness had gotten hot and burned the wires. He fixed that with wire nuts and it works now.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Gallery series range/oven Part Number GLES389ESC. Normal use. The first problem occurred after a normal cleaning of the oven and control surfaces. Two burners turned on by themselves and error codes were evident.

Reset the unit a few times using the circuit breaker. All seems well. Then the right front burner turned on high while off. The left rear burner was randomly unable to work and then was on high suddenly.

The Left Rear control board fried completely (electrically burned traces in the board). I removed it and verified the part number from the manufacturer and replaced it. Then reset the system using the breaker circuit. Everything worked fine for a while.

Then the Right rear burner was unable to work on high, instead only able to cook at 9.5 or less. Later I reset the breaker again and the burner seemed to work properly again.

Then the Right front burner began to turn on high all by itself, we were able to reduce the heat setting of the burner and reset it by cycling the breaker. Then randomly the burner would turn on and not be able to turn off again. And again. Then just as suddenly the burner would turn on HIgh againÃÂand randomly allow itself to be turned down or off. The Right Rear Burner and the right front now randomly are unable to adjust below 2.8 or above 7 and then they work again.

I beleive that this is the same board system used in many other recalls however I could not find a recall notice for this unit, nor did the manufacturer discuss that there is a recall when I called them for help.

If this is a recalled unit then I need to know exaclty how to resolve this problem and how to report the manufacturer for not informing me of recall when I called them.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning burners and electrical issues, posing a potential fire hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Frigidaire glass top stove turns broiler on along with oven and it overheats which causes a fire safety issue.
justification: The incident describes a fire safety issue due to overheating, which poses a risk but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: Frozen sausage was sitting on counter in anchor glass dish for 4 hours. Was placed in oven. The temperature was 350. Sausage was in oven for 30 minutes. We were in other room when we heard the glass shatter in the oven.
justification: Glass shattered in the oven, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her husband received an inch long cut on his thumb from the slicer as he took it out of the box. The consumer's husband applied at home first aid. The slicer was only wrapped in a clear, plastic bag.

The consumer contacted the manf on 9/30/14 regarding the incident. The consumer stated that the representative listened and took down the model # and purchase store information. The consumer was not asked for her name or any other contact information. The consumer was not provided further information. The rep stated that he would talk to his boss. They did not ask to have the product shipped back for inspection. 

The consumer stated that when she spoke to the manf, they informed her that the product should have been in a neutral position, so it should not have been able to cause any injury. However, the consumer stated that when her husband took it out of the box, the blade was raised.

The consumer stated that there are no warnings on the outside of the packaging asking to take proper care when opening the package. The consumer stated that the labeling is on the insert, located on the inside of the packaging.  

The consumer also contacted the retailer, but they did not know what to do about such an incident.
justification: The incident resulted in an inch-long cut requiring first aid, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as improper packaging and lack of warnings could lead to similar incidents.

incident_description:
On 9/24/14 the consumer heard a fan like noise and noticed the unit was on. The unit was running like it was set to heat a item inside. She tried to shut off the unit but it would not shut off. The consumer opened the unit's door and states the fan continued to run. The consumer states when she closed the door the unit immediately turned back on. The consumer states she could not get to the unit's cord outlet to unpug the unit so turned off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer states a friend assisted her to unplug the unit so she could turn the circuit breaker back on.

The consumer did not see any smoke and states there were no property damages.

The consumer states she has not had any prior incidents. 

The consumer is disabled and only could provide the model and serial number at this time. 

The consumer states the appliances came with the home. 

The consumer feels the unit poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning unit but no injury or property damage occurred, and the consumer took corrective action by turning off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: Oven glass shattered on GE oven/range Model #-JBP24W0K3WW, Serial #-SL251374Q
