justification: The oven glass shattered, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
My Magic Chef microwave oven (model # MCO160UQ) came on all by itself, and could not be shut off by pressing Cancel/Off. I was in another room when I heard the microwave oven running. I immediately pressed Cancel/Off to no effect. I opened the door to stop it. I closed it, and a few minutes later, it happened again. I opened the door again to stop it unplugged it allow it to reset controls plugged it back in and in a few moments it beeped and began running again. The interior of the oven was very hot I have no idea how long it was running when I noticed it.
This is a dangerous fire hazard.
Item performed well for about 5 years but needs to be recalled as a fire hazard
justification: The microwave turning on by itself and not shutting off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: used my slow cooker on 10/4/14 half way thru I looked in on it and a bad smell coming from it. With further inspection noticed one of the cookers 3 leg stands completely melted down to my countertop. Now off balance the cooker is resting on the melted legs along resting on the electrical cord which had been melted to expose the wires!. I have Notified the company CE NORTH AMERICA LLC MIAMI FL sent them photos, was told by the rep he contact his boss and tech people about this issue. They refuse to send me another or even talk compensation due to the fact I have no proof of purchase which was purchased a year ago. Whether it's under war or not this stupid thing nearly cost me my home! I have told them how unhappy I am with their lack of concern of what may have taken place.
justification: The incident involved a slow cooker malfunction causing damage to the countertop and exposing wires, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(09/28/2014) The consumer stated that the oven was pre-heating to 350 degrees. After about five minutes she heard a loud sound that sounded like an electrical short-circuit. Black smoke was coming from the control panel. She also saw flames coming from the control panel. The consumer put the fire out with a fire extinguisher,pulled the stove from the wall and unplugged it.

(09/29/201040 The consumer contacted Sears. She advised them of the incident. The call was disconnected while they were checking for a recall.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the oven's control panel, but the consumer successfully extinguished the fire without injury.

incident_description:
Caller reported that his electric range had electrical failures such as arching and short circuiting inside the burner/coil temperature controls - one of back wattage.  He has not visibly seen any melted wires, but know that there has been an orange from inside temperature controls with a small amount of smoke from the range.  There is an intermittent popping noise when the range is powered on.  This incident has been ongoing for about 3 weeks.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet. Submitter wanted to check with US CPSC, first.

Caller feels that this range is a safety hazard, a potential fire hazard, and should be reported. 

Caller was made aware of Alert#04-576, is model or serial number was not part of the recall.
justification: The incident involves electrical failures and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Electric range from TV and Appliance store in Oregon October 1st, 2005.

Caller had not used the self cleaning feature and decided to finally to use it in May 2014 and did so with no problems.

June 2014 the caller turned the oven on to preheat 450 degrees, the oven was on for approximately five minutes and the caller noticed an odor like that of a chemical smell.
She looked into the oven, noticed a flashing light then opened the oven, she saw that it was caused by the broiler element that was arching with a circular spiral of arching moving around the broiling element.
Caller turned the stove off.

The caller is not using the oven anymore after this last incident.
She uses the cooktop only.

No injuries have been reported other than a minor burn to her right index finger when sparks hit it.

No treatment has been necessary.

She contacted the manufacturer September 2nd, 2014 and was advised by female representative after creating report with her  to contact CPSC to create an incident report.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn (injury), but no further harm or treatment was required, indicating a low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I own Frigidaire smooth-surface cooktop FPCC3685KS. For the third time since owning this unit, liquid spilled on the control knobs caused the underlying control board to go defective.

Two days ago when this happened I had paper towels sitting on a burner that was turned off. I had a pot of water boil over, spilling liquid onto the control knobs. When this happened, all of the burners turned on to high heat, catching fire to the paper towels. The burners couldn't be turned off with the control knobs as they were already in the "off" position. The only way to disable the unit was to turn off the breaker switch on my home electrical panel.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a defective control board, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Concerns: KitchenAid unsafe food processor
MOD: KFP715WH2
SER: WH04878819
I own a KitchenAid food processor which I was satisfied with until last week when my top finger and part of my nail was chopped. While top part was removed the on button was accidentally pushed and the unit started, my finger was too close to the blade of the slicing disc & cut my left index.
You would think that quality product such as KitchenAid would have a reliable security on their unit to prevent these types of injuries while the top part is removed. Unfortunately, it turns out that I was wrong thinking that, luckily the injury is not as serious as it could have been.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the finger, which is classified as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) because the injury happened due to an accidental activation of the food processor while the top part was removed, a scenario that could reasonably happen again under similar circumstances.

incident_description: Bosch dishwasher caught on fire.  Melted the front and completely destroyed the circuits on the inside and bottom of the dishwasher.  Filled my home with smoke.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and caused significant property damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
(08/31/2014) The consumer stated that he was preparing to use the deep fryer . He picked up the basket and the handle to the basket fell into two pieces. There was hot oil in the fryer but no one was injured.

The consumer stated that he rarely uses the deep fryer.

(09/5/2014) The consumer sent an email to the manufacturer. He received a response on 9/6 apologizing for the inconvenience.
justification: The handle broke but no one was injured, and the consumer rarely uses the deep fryer.

incident_description: I was home with three young children when I noticed an awful electrical burning smell but I couldn't figure out where it was coming from. Soon my whole downstairs was filled with haze- there was smoke in my house! I immediately checked the walls and felt light switches to check for hotness to determine if there was an internal electrical fire. Soon I discovered the top of my counter was extremely hot, and when I opened up the cabinet under the sink, I got blasted with a heat wave. It wasn't until I touched the dishwasher and burned myself (it was scalding hot), that I realized it was the dishwasher. It was so hot that if my one year old twins had touched the dishwasher, their little hands would have blistered. I had to open the dishwasher with oven mitts, and everything inside was melted, even the silverware rack and dishwasher parts, such as the spinner on the bottom. I cannot even get the bottom rack out, as everything is fused together in one big melted mess. I turned off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher so that the electrical current would be cut, becausee apparently there was an electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element that was causing this!
justification: The incident caused property damage and could have caused injury, but no one was hurt.

incident_description:
Caller stated that while sitting in her living room she heard a loud noise and in her investigations discovered that the over the range microwave oven glass door had shattered without being in use.  There were glass pieces all over the floor and on the stove as well.  There were no prior incidents or service calls with this unit.  The unit was only in service for 10 months.

(9/2014) The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that this was not a known case.  A service rep was sent out 9/13/14 and she  received a replacement door.

She stated that her spouse advised her that he had seen numerous complaints online for this incident.  She feels that this unit poses a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident was a minor incident with no injury, but it poses a safety hazard that should be reported.

incident_description: The panel where the knobs are on my gas range get extremely hot when I use my oven or Broiler for any extended period. Thus the knobs also get too hot to touch at times. I had two technicians in who stated that I should use the fan and that should help-it has not. They also felt that with time the temperature would lessen. They may be but the knobs still get very hot. My range is still under warranty.
justification: The knobs get extremely hot during use, posing a burn risk, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: Kitchen stove glass panel of door shattering during routine oven usage. Frigidaire gas stove, model FFGF3019LWE, ser # VF20943314, purchased new 4 Feb 2013 from Home Depot, Melbourne, FL. On 7 Oct 2014, a glass panel of the door, "sandwiched" on the inside of the door (a third glass panel) shattered loudly during routine baking with no person present nor top burner in use at the same time.No injuries.Oven in use approx 30 mins, temp approx 425 F.Have contacted Frigidaire online to report/request assistance with customer repair/replacement due to warranty expiration. Received replacement glass panel details, ordering info from Frigidaire.com. Have photos but cannot upload to this screen, therefore will "attach" via email separately and reference this report.
justification: The incident involved a glass panel shattering with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but have been reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there are two hazards with his refrigerator. The first hazard is with the ice box in the freezer and the second is with vegetable bin.

Ice Box: 
The consumer stated that he had the same incident occur twice with the ice box.

The consumer stated that about 2-3 months, 2 pieces of plastic came off of the ice tray into his glass when he was getting ice from the machine. The consumer stated that he saw the pieces and didn't drink from the glass. The consumer stated that the ice pieces were about an inch long each.

The consumer stated that he contacted the manf. They sent out a technician from Capital City Appliance to repair the issue. The consumer sated that the technician replaced the whole ice making unit including the ice tray.

The consumer stated that on 7/5/14, he was getting some ice water. The consumer took a drink of the ice water, and a piece of the plastic cut the left inside of his mouth. The consumer stated that the piece is about 1/4 inch. 

The consumer went to the retailer and informed them about the issue. He was informed to contact the manf. The consumer stated that he looked at the other units in the store and saw that the manf no longer makes model with similar ice box.

The consumer contacted the manf and left them a message. The consumer was called back and left messages three times by the manf asking him information about doctor and hospital. The consumer spoke to the manf and informed them that he did not go to a doctor or hospital. The consumer stated that the rep he spoke to seemed to not care about the incident once he informed her that he did not seek any medical help. The consumer asked to have the whole refrigerator replaced with a model that has a different ice box design.

The manf sent a technician on 7/16/14 from Computek Warranty. The technician informed the consumer to not use the energy saver button. He stated that this has happened quite often with this model. The technician replaced the ice box and put in a new gasket.

The consumer has the piece of plastic that injured him. The consumer stated that he has been running around in circles with the manf. The consumer has not been able to speak to anyone higher up. The consumer stated that this is a design flaw with the unit that will keep re-occurring even if the ice box is replaced.


Vegetable Bin:
The consumer stated that the lower right side bin does not cool the vegetables enough. The consumer stated that they have discarded some things due to spoilage.

The technician from Computek Warranty looked at this issue and informed the consumer that the manf left a piece of foam (used in packaging) inside the vent. The technician removed the piece. 

The consumer stated that the bin still does not cool as much.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor injury (cut inside the mouth) from plastic pieces in the ice, and the issue has occurred multiple times with the same model.

incident_description:
The consumer states that on 7/26/14 he woke up around 6am and saw that the unitÃÂs left front burner was on high heat level but the switch was off. He states the control keyboard was on child lock setting. The consumer tried to turn the unit off using the electronic control keyboard. The unit does not have knobs or a switch; it is controlled by the electronic keyboard.  The consumer turned off the circuit breaker and waited a few minutes. When he turned the circuit breaker back on the left burner would automatically turn on. The consumer states he turned the circuit breaker off and back on about 6 times during the next few days and the left burner automatically turned on each time.

The consumer states he has not used the unit again. 

The consumer used the stove the day before (7/25/14) and he states it was working fine.

The consumer states the unit received repairs in 2010 and 2011. The unitÃÂs right front burner and control keyboard were replaced both times because the unit had the same problem of spontaneously turning on but would not shut off unless the circuit breaker was turned off.  The consumer states the technician who conducted the repair in 2011 advised him that he should not have this problem again. Both repairs were covered by the consumers extended warranty. 

The consumer contacted the firm on 7/28/14 (case# [REDACTED]) the firm advised him the unit was not on recall and he would have to pay for any repairs. The consumer did not want to repair the unit because he has had the same problem and the unit repaired on 2 occasions. The consumer wanted a different unit and was offered a 10% discount on a new unit. 


The consumer feels that the unit poses a fire hazard and should be recalled with the other ranges in recall # 09-333.

The consumer is a retired fire dept for 30 years and feels this unit poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove that poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
I ran my GE dishwasher on the evening of 10/5 around 7-8pm.
This morning on 10/6 my husband indicated the dishwasher was still hot and he asked when i ran it. I told him last night between 7-8 pm and it was now 6:45 am and the dishwasher was so hot he couldn't touch any of the items. The dishwasher was extremely hot and smelled like something was burning. We had to turn off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher as we were afraid of fire. I checked General Electric's recall list and this machine is not listed on it, however it is presenting as the same issue:

Model no#GSD6900J10BB
Seriel no# RL843324B
justification: The dishwasher was extremely hot and smelled like something was burning, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My wife was removing the safety cap on the Kuhn Rikon  Corn Zipper and it sliced two of her finger tips. She had to go to Urgent Care and the wound has been extremely painful and will take weeks to heal. The gadget does not have a safety warning and more importantly, it has no way of gripping the safety cap so that your fingers are protected. Seems like a safety cap should enhance safety of the use of the product, not increase its danger.
justification: The incident caused injury to the wife, requiring urgent care, and will take weeks to heal.

incident_description: My daughter went to grab a drinking glass from the cabinet and it exploded in her hand when she touched it. She did not drop it; she merely touched it. Tiny shards of glass exploded throughout the cabinet, on the countertop, and on the floor. The glassware is marked Duralex made in France. She experienced some small cuts on her hand.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts on the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Glass exploding upon touch is uncommon but not unheard of, making the occurrence likelihood 2 (unlikely).

incident_description:
Caller stated that the outer glass of the oven door exploded while not in use.  She was standing in front of the unit when the incident occurred, the glass pieces shattered to about 3 feet to another room.  No one was injured.


(9/9/14) The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that her range was out of warranty and it would be at her expense to replace the glass door.


Caller feels that the range is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The oven door glass exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The Kenmore Elite bottom freezer refrigerator was plugged in as normal.  When I opened the door, it was blazing hot inside.  The cover to the light bulbs was melted, and there was a burning smell.  My husband removed the cover and the light bulbs were so hot he had to use a towel to remove them.  The light bulb sockets were charred and discolored.  The food on the top shelf was hot and ruined.  I know that the doors to the refrigerator had not been left open because during the night I had gotten a drink of water from the water dispenser and it had worked, which would not have been the case if the door had been left ajar.

This was so dangerous!  I am surprised the unit didn't catch fire!!!!   We called Sears and it will be two weeks before they send out a technician.  I told them that it was a safety issue and not a warranty issue.  They will still not verify that the service call will be free of charge, even though I gave them a service flash number 46-515R4 which I found online where multiple other consumers have had the same safety issue.
justification: The incident involved significant damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I used the reynolds slow cook liner in my [slow cooker] to make pulled pork (I've used this liners many times before without incident). After cooking the pork, vegetables, etc. I proceeded to take the liner our of the [slow cooker], with just the liquid and vegetables in it, the liner brought, hot liquid splashed onto my clothes and face, burning a few spots next to my eye, as well as all over my counter/floor. Hurt like hell. It could have been much worse, I was lucky, but that product is dangerous. If there had been a child next to me......
justification: Hot liquid splashed onto the face and clothes, causing burns, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The unit has two channels on either side of the heating element.  Condensation from the brewing process collects on the lid of the unit and drains into the channels.  There is no outlet for this water and it flows onto the electric heating element.  I am fearful this accumulation of water contacting the heating element could cause serious problems.
justification: Water contacting the heating element could cause electrical hazards, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
LG french door refrigerator
Model #LFX25978ST /00.
Serial #302MRQK12732
Manufactured 2013

- Glass shelf (from over the three bins) shattered all over kitchen floor, tables, even inside utensil drawer and several small pieces of glass were embedded in my wife's left side (neck, arm and hand,)

In a separate previous incident:

- Door shelf brackets broke off causing bottles to fall and break on the floor.
justification: The incident caused injury to the wife, but no death or serious injury, so the severity level is 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 because the incident has occurred before.

incident_description:
For the past week, I've noticed a burning smell coming from the refrigerator. It wasn't until the light fixture melted away from the top of the refrigerator that I realized the amount of heat it was generating. I have had to throw away the warm food. The soda bottles screw off caps actually weree too hot to screw off without using a towel.  I'm hoping my disabled daughter with a jeopardized immune system (as well as the rest of the family) does not become ill because of eating food that was warmer than it should have been in the refrigerator.  I'm also concerned about fire.  Sears is charging me $99 just to send someone out to  in 5 days. Researching online has shown that this problem is inherent in Kenmore refrigerators. 

My refrigerator is a Kenmore Elite Trio, model number 79577543600, serial # 607KR00767
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator causing heat and potential food spoilage, but no injury or death has occurred yet. The likelihood is high given the described symptoms and online research indicating this is a common problem with the model.

incident_description:
LG Electric Range - LSC5683WW

Oven doesn't stop heating when it reaches temperature. Oven got up to oven 500 deg F and was still heating.

Assumed thermostat had gone. Now discover there is a recall for cook top. (Bought from Home Depot but no notice from Home Depot received.)
justification: The oven overheating is a malfunction but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
LG Electric Oven/Burner
Model: LRE30453ST /01
Serial: 003MMCB01027

The front right burner set itself very high even though it was set to very low and the display showed low (level 02). It could not be turned off in anyway. Charred the food. Found dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a burner malfunction that charred food but did not cause injury, indicating a minor operational issue.

incident_description:
Good morning,

Last night I baked two chicken breasts in a 9 x 13 Pyrex glass pan at 350 degrees.  I had added a half a can of chicken broth and covered it with aluminum foil for 30 minutes.  After 30 minutes I opened the oven and removed the aluminum foil  when the dish absolutely shattered.  Liquid and glass flew five feet down across my kitchen.  I was not injured thank goodness.

I have attached pictures of this incident and will never purchase a glass baking dish again.  If you have any questions, please contact me.  Thank you.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass pan but no injuries were reported, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description: The person draining the oil from the vat (to filter it) forgot to turn the fryer off first. The safety switch mentioned in the manual (which is supposed to disable the burners if the drain valve is opened) did not function, and the oil overheated and caught fire once the temperature sensor was uncovered. A cover was then placed over the vat, which extinguished the fire. No damage or injury occurred.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no damage or injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The safety switch failure suggests this could happen again if not addressed, making occurrence likelihood 4 (likely).

incident_description:
(09/17/2014) The consumer stated that she was preheating the oven to 350. After a few minutes, the consumer notice flames in the back of the range near the electrical panel. The consumer pulled the range away from the wall and unplugged the unit. She placed the unit outside.

(09/18/2014) The consumer contacted the manufacturer and advised them of the incident. The consumer was advised that the range was not under warranty. The consumer was advised that they would have to pay for repair or replacement.


The consumer is concerned that her house could have caught on fire if she had not been at home.  

There is fire damage to wall behind oven.  All electrical wiring in range is unsafe.  Breaker flipped in basement on electrical panel.
justification: The incident involved flames and fire damage but no injuries or deaths, and the likelihood is unlikely as the consumer was able to intervene.

incident_description: With the oven on, the appliance top (not the burners, just the top area) gets hot enough to burn your hand. Anything sitting on a top burner, with the burners off also gets hot enough to burn your hand to the touch. My mother burnt her hand on just the top of the stove when the oven was on. No medical attention was given.
justification: The incident caused injury to the person, but no medical attention was given, so the severity level is 3.

incident_description: Front burners (right and left) spontaneously increase to highest setting, even if lowest setting is selected. This has begun happening more and more frequently with time, and there is no way to shut off the right front burner except to manually cut power to the stove at the circuit breaker.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard that could lead to injury, but there is no injury reported yet.

incident_description:
(11/2013) The consumer stated that he was using one of the forks when one of the tongs broke off in his mouth.  The consumer used another fork to pick up some salad and it shattered into the salad, with the broken pieces being clear they are hard to see.

The consumer was not injured.

The package is misleading and false by stating the forks are made of heavy duty plastic.
The information on the package listed the forks as heavy duty plastic.  

The consumer stated that the product is unsafe.  These easily breakable forks are a serious choking hazard.
justification: The consumer was not injured, but the incident involved broken fork pieces that could pose a choking hazard.

incident_description: I was using my Kenmore 790.9742 electric oven last night at 350 degrees F, when the front glass of the oven exploded. I had opened the oven and took out my pan, closed the oven door, and was stirring my dinner when the glass shattered. It was purchased in 2010 from Sears so it was only 4 years old. The glass covered the entire kitchen floors and no pieces were left unbroken. No one was hurt because I cleaned the glass up as fast as possible but some of the broken glass is stuck in the track where the glass had been so I could not get everything cleaned up. I have contacted Kenmore and explained this problem as well.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing significant damage but no injuries.

incident_description: Upon opening oven door to remove something from oven and leaving door in open position I moved to right to place pan on counter when my leg brushed against the sharp exposed steel edge of door cutting a 3" x 1/4" deep gash on shin. In seconds shoe was full of blood and pooling on the floor, blood was coming out so fast that in hindsight, being by myself, it was not a good idea to try to handle incident myself and not call an ambulance.  I came real close to passing out.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep gash with significant blood loss, indicating a serious injury.

incident_description:
A dinner plate of food was placed into the microwave to reheat for 2 minutes 30 seconds.  The microwave came on and a burning smell was noticed but the food was fine.  The plug was pulled and the microwave was turned so we could see the back where the burning and the smoke was coming from. The safety fuse panel had melted down.  Instead of the fuse tripping, the wires leading into it melted causing smoking and burning.  The microwave was unplugged before it could catch fire. The microwave was well ventilated and the fans were not blocked.  

We contacted Hamilton Beach about the incident and they stated there was nothing to be done as the warranty had run out.  Did not seem concerned that a major safety feature had failed on the microwave.
justification: The incident involved a microwave malfunction causing smoke and burning, but no injury or fire occurred due to prompt action.

incident_description:
On 08/01/14 (estimated) the consumer was using the unit for approximately an hour. He states he was using all 4 burners. The consumer states the front left burner was set on a high heat level and he used the knob to lower the burner to a medium heat level but the burner remained really hot and red. He unplugged the unit and the waited 2 minutes for the burner to cool off. The consumer plugged the unit's cord into the wall outlet and states all 4 burners were off. 

The consumer turned the front left burner on to a medium heat level but he states the burner got really hot and red as it does when it is on a high heat level. When he turned the front left burners knob switch to off the front left burner did not shut off. He repeated the process 3 times and the same thing happened each time. 
 
The consumer uses the unit except for the front left burner. He states the other 3 burners do not have this problem

The consumer purchased a new infinite switch for the unit on 09/02/14 and he installed it on 09/03/12. The consumer purchased the infinite switch (part# 316436000) online from [REDACTED]
On 9/3/14 after the consumer installed the infinite switch he turned the front left burner on to a medium heat level but he states the burner got really hot and red as it does when it is on a high heat level. When he turned the front left burners knob switch to off the front left burner did not shut off. He unplugged the unit and plugged it back in. The consumer discontinued using the front left burner. 

The consumer feels the unit poses a fire hazard. 

The consumer also noted he contacted mfr and was informed there is no recall on this product.
justification: The consumer states the front left burner was not shutting off, which poses a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(09/06/2014) The consumer stated that the top broiler, the oven light, the convection fan came on by itself. The computer LED readout indicated the number 8. The consumer shut the gas off to the appliance. After the range cooled down, the consumer open the oven door to see why everything came on by itself. 

The consumer stated that nothing was in use on the range when this happened. 

(09/06/2014) The consumer contacted the company. The consumer explained the incident. He was advised that they might be willing to help him out with the cost of a new circuit board. The consumer was also advised that he would have pay for service visit. 

The consumer stated that he checked the internet and found similar complaints with the same model.

The consumer thinks that this product should be recalled. He does not want it repaired.

The consumer stated that his biggest scare is that this could have happened when no one was at home.

The consumer also noted the top broiler, the oven light and the convection fan were on the gas range...The computer LED readout indicated the number 8...The incident occurred either before or during a short duration thunder storm...The LED control panel would not respond to repeated attempts to shut the range down...The gas was shut off to the range and the oven receptacle, stopping the convection fan, oven light and LED display.

The consumer indicated nothing else in the house was effected by the weather which included (Ex: refrigerator, security system, microwave, washing machine, clocks, coffee pot, TV)...The range was not in use when the incident occurred..The delayed oven programming has never been utilized on the range...The range top had not been used in a week and the oven had not been used in months.

The consumer stated in contacting the mfr the recorded menu on the toll free number (1-800-944-9044) in the range manual, steers the consumer to a toll number (706-860-4110) to make an incident report...Numerous complaints were found on the internet concerning this model range, including control panel fire, one range having replaced circuit board multiple times. 

The consumer also indicated Frigidaire did not advertise or disclose to consumers that this range could turn itself on unwantedly...The broiler gas valve opened without programming, human input or knowledge...A legitimate fear of this occurring during a two week vacation absence or that the broiler gas could be released without being ignited is an unacceptable risk that he is unwilling to take with this appliance.
justification: The incident was a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore refrigerator caught on fire. Model# 106.59069990 and SER# sk0636230. This is a side by side refrigerator/freezer with ice maker and water dispenser on the freezer side. After plugging the fridge in I heard some noise in the fridge, and assuming it was nothing, walked away. The smoke alarms went off after 5-10 minutes and I rushed to turn off the appliance immediately.When I opened the fridge part smoke was billowing out of the air vent, but no damage in this compartment. I opened the freezer compartment and saw that the door lining was melted away and the insulation was exposed. The top left part of the ice maker was melted into the side of the freezer compartment and there was black soot on the surrounding surfaces.

I was very alarmed that this could happen and the next day I contacted Sears to see what could be  one about this issue. To make a long story short, they were very unhelpful. After spending 2 hours being transferred to different departments I still didn't have any answers.

I found out that the manufacturer of this particular Kenmore refrigerator is Whirlpool, so I called Whirlpool. They said that there was nothing they could do and I would need to go through Sears for this issue. I understand that this is probably how their agreement works, but I had to try anyway.

I must say that prior to contacting Sears I had read many reviews of defective Kenmore products and many people were complaining that there was very little interest by Sears to help resolve the issues. I am also very disappointed with the the horrible customer service I received from them. I expect more from a corporation when a hazardous appliance causes a safety issue. Luckily I had turned off the power before any serious damage was done. This product could very well have caused injury and death, had the problem not been caught in time.

The best advice I got from one of the Sears reps. was to go to a store, where they can't transfer you around and must deal with the issue at hand. I will be going to complain in person today, and hope there will be a better response to my issue.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, causing damage to the appliance but no injuries or deaths, as the issue was caught in time.

incident_description: I was baking squash in the oven at 350 degrees, and my daughter leaned on the oven door for a minute, and both layers of the glass shattered.  Thankfully, it did not explode out onto her legs!  I don't know if her leaning on it for that short minute was the reason it exploded, but I don't really suspect it was, especially after researching this on the internet.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
On Sunday evening, Sept. 28, 2014, I turned my Bosch convection oven on to preheat.  Shortly, I heard a loud pop only to find the interior glass had shattered into little pieces.  We moved into this home only this past August and it was only the second time I used this oven.  It was like new because the prior owners worked in Washington, DC and were here only on weekends and either ate out or barbequed.  I called Bosch and reported the incident.  They agreed to send out a technician to diagnose the problem (?shattered interior  glass) and he would tell me what needs to be replaced and that cost would be on me.  Surely, this is a defective piece of safety glass, and I feel the cost should be borne by Bosch.
The model  number is HBL5450UC/08.  The Serial number is 920800174.
justification: The incident involved shattered oven glass but no injury or harm occurred, and such failures are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: We purchased a Samsung slide in range several months ago. model#NE58F9500SS On several occasions we have turned the burners on by simply brushing up against them. The knobs are in such a position that makes it far to easy for this to happen. They also turn too easily. We have  always noticed and were able to turn them off before anyone got burned. However yesterday we had someone working on our backsplash  and had placed a towel on the stove top to protect it. He had placed his drill case on top of the towel. As he was working the burner turned on and by the time he noticed what was happening, the drill case had melted through and when he lifted it up the towel  burst into flames. He got out the fire but had he not acted quickly it could have been much worse. I feel the design of the control panel is poor and this product is unsafe.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by the stove's design flaw, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: I bought the "Pyrex Portable 4-Piece Set, includes 1 ea 3-qt Easy Grab Oblong, RedCover, Large Unipack, Black Carrier" through Amazon approximately 2 years ago and used the dish less than 10 times.  Last night, after pulling the dish out of the oven --I'd made fries using russet potatoes -- the dish shattered as my husband placed it on the countertop.  It was literally still in his hand when it shattered, and the hot shards of pyrex flew all over the kitchen and lodged into his legs and foot.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from hot shards of Pyrex, but no death was reported. Such incidents are uncommon but not unheard of with glass cookware.

incident_description:
GoldCoast 3 bowl set. Red with a shinny "chromelike" finish. I left one of these bowls on my back porch with some recently picked produce in the bowl. In short order the leaves of lettuce were smoking. The bowl focused the light to such a point in started to burn the lettuce.
I later went to check the other two bowls one of which was sitting on my table with a small paper bag in it. My son picked it up and noticed a burn hole right threw the paper bag.

These bowls are dangerous. I can only imagine how many fires might or have been started by these bowls. 


I'd hate to know someone died or went to jail because of these bowls.
justification: The incident describes property damage (burned lettuce and a paper bag) but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) given the potential for repeated incidents with these bowls.

incident_description:
Capital Range GCR304N - gas range

The oven turns itself on when the control dial is firmly set to the off position.  This creates a risk of fire as the oven may turn itself on and burn at a high temperature when no one is present.  
I contacted the manufacturer to report the condition.  After speaking to two employees who appeared indifferent, I was able to reach a member of the management team who agreed to send a contract repair technician to inspect the range.  The manufacturer also shipped me a replacement thermostat under the assumption that the thermostat installed in the range was defective.  The repair technician inspected the range and observed it turn itself on when the control dial was in the off position.  He then inspected the replacement thermostat and was able to reproduce the condition.  According to the technician, the tolerance between on and off is very small and the thermostat can connect to be in the on position while the control dial is set to off.  He demonstrated the replacement thermostatÃÂs failure several times.  The technician advised, and I agreed, that it would not be appropriate to replace the thermostat in the range with a clearly defective replacement part.

I would like the root cause of the dangerous condition to be identified and appropriate repair or replacement to be made by the manufacturer.
justification: The oven turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I had  damages caused by a stove explosion in my home.  The explosion caused injury to my foot (3rd degree burn requiring a visit to the hospital),my kitchen (including a newly laid kitchen floor) and destroyed the stove.  Fire fighters informed that the explosion appears to have been related to an electrical problem inside the stove because it takes 2500 degrees to melt stainless steel of which it melted from bottom of my cooking pot, there were pieces of stainless steel flying all over the kitchen area of which many of them landed on my floor. I reported this incident directly to whirlpool for further investigation the very next day. 
Someone needs to take charge and investigate this matter to prevent from happening to anyone. Its unsafe and could cause someone's home to burn down or even worst cause death.I was left without a stove, are having to eat outside of home and spending more than I would have to for not being able to cook at home since 9/18/14 
I would like a resolution from whirpool  for the repair of the damages and replace the stove. 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a 3rd degree burn requiring hospitalization, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific electrical problem described.

incident_description:
Product: Halloween Theme Oven Mitt from Dollar Tree

I attempted to use stated oven mitt to move an item from my oven to my stovetop for cooling. Upon touching the pan the outer orange layer of this mitt instantly stuck/bonded to my dish. The inner white supposedly cotton portion just completely melted/shriveled like plastic (did not act like cotton material) leaving my thumb fully exposed to the hot dish.
justification: The incident resulted in the user's thumb being exposed to a hot dish due to the oven mitt's failure, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: As I open my refrigerator to gather my produce for the meal of the day. I notice a burning smell coming from the inside of my fridge. After inspecting my fridge I came to the conclusion  that the smell was coming from the ceiling where the light bulb sits. The bulb was now melted inside the plastic of the refrigerator. Which makes it impossible to take out the bulb. Trying to figure out what could have actually caused this to happened I when online to do some research and notice this is not an isolated incident. I believe that this product is a fire hazard and the manufacture should issue a recall immediately.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
1 bought a range from Sears. It blew up and caught fire during use (cooking a pizza). I had my 2 year old granddaughter
home at the time and this could have burnt down my house and Injured or killed my family. I contacted Sears and the
Frigidare company. I sent pictures of the burnt and faulty wiring. Frididare told me that the range was out of warranty and
that it was registered under another name. I stated that I purchased It new from Sears. When I contacted Sears about the
range being preowned, faulty wiring and caught fire. They denied it and stated that all they could do was to have the range
looked at by their serviceman which would be at my expense.
justification: The range caught fire during use, posing a risk of injury or death, but no actual injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The pins which hold the wheels onto the top rack of my dishwasher break every 9-12 months. I discover this when the top rack unexpectedly falls when the rack is pulled out to load or unload dishes. Fortunately I have caught the rack before it crashed into the bottom rack where it could break glasses and ceramic dishes. I'm glad it has not occurred when my elderly mother pulled the rack out, as the rack and dishes were rather heavy when falling unexpectedly, and could easily have pulled her off balance and caused a fall. I have owned the dishwasher for 2 years and am on the 3rd adjuster replacement. I note many others complaining of the same thing on line. Mine is a Kenmore dishwasher (Model 665.13292K112), but it appears[REDACTED]is the manufacturer. Kenmore has reimbursed me for the first two adjusters, but it appears they continue to use this same dangerous rack wheel/adjuster design in the models presently on display.  This part should be made sturdier before an injury occurs.
justification: The incident causes no injury, but it is a serious inconvenience and could potentially cause injury if the rack falls unexpectedly.

incident_description: The handle on the oven door had come loose on one side. While trying to tighten the screw that had come loose, I opened the door (impossible to tighten the screw without opening the door) and the glass on the front of the door shattered and much of it flew across the floor of the kitchen, up to 15 feet away from the oven. This was a Kenmore oven purchased from Sears, model number 790.36909902.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injury was reported, making it a severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as oven door issues are not uncommon but not frequent.

incident_description:
Samsung Refrigerator French Door Model: RF 261 BEA ESR / AA

The tempered glass shelf shattered during the night.  On opening the door in the morning, shards of glass were all over the inside of the fridge -- all over food containers, in the door, all over the other shelves. There were no hot or heavy items on the shelf.   

There was no warning or explanation for the glass shelf shattering. 

While no one was injured,  had this happened while someone had the door open, the injuries could have been severe.  

We have children at eye level with the glass shelves.  They could have been cut or even blinded.  

Samsung denies this has ever happened before.  However[ REDACTED] research would indicate otherwise.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass shelf with no injuries, but potential for severe harm if someone was nearby.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the smoke alarm went off in the middle of the night. The kitchen and dining room were filled with smoke. The top element in the oven and the inside of the oven was glowing cherry red. The wood cabinets surrounding the oven were hot and the wood was making crackling sound. The consumer stated that the pans in the cabinet above the oven were so hot that he couldn't touch them. 

The consumer could not turn off the oven. The consumer had to cut the circuit breaker off. The consumer stated that the oven came on by itself in the middle of the night.

The consumer's model is included in recall #08-110. The consumer had the unit repaired under recall. 

The consumer scheduled the repair through manf's recall hotline when the recall was announced. The consumer stated that the technician replaced the latch in the microwave. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manf regarding the incident on 09/05/14. They provided him a case #. The consumer was informed that he would receive a replacement unit but before that a technician would have to come out and verify the safety hazard. The technician appointment was scheduled for 09/09/14. The technician did not show up on the scheduled day, so the consumer called manf's customer relation line. The consumer was informed that the technician ordered parts for his unit and rescheduled the visit. The consumer was never informed about the rescheduling of the visit or part order for his unit. The manf was supposed to get a call for a follow up from the case manager on 9/10/14 but still has not received a call.

The consumer stated that the manf is not trying to follow up with the incident he reported with them. 

The consumer stated that he pulled out the unit just enough to look behind it. The consumer did not notice any damage behind the unit.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused smoke and heat damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Our Maytag stove oven has the same problem that is listed in this web site. The problem is the ove does not ignite and causes an explosion. It is strong enough to push open the oven door and if you sre standing next to the stove possibly cause severe burns. The maytag company has not list our model as a recall yet. here is the Model #MGR5775QDQ, SERIAL # 15048021EE
justification: The description indicates the oven can cause an explosion strong enough to push open the door and potentially cause severe burns, which constitutes an injury risk.

incident_description: Kenmore Smooth top Range model 790.96010407 s/n VF80564814 .. the left front burner sometimes will not turn off and then when you get it turned off after playing with the knob for a while it will turn itself on at times in the middle of the night and then sometimes when you turn the oven on both front burners come on  this very DANGEROUS .. no injuries and or fires yet ...  possible just a matter of time the Range is only 5 years old and should not be having this kind of problem
justification: The burner malfunction is described as very dangerous with potential for injury or fire, but no incidents have occurred yet.

incident_description: I purchased a KitchenAid food processor, Model KFP1330, on February 1, 2014.  The unit did not grate mozzarella cheese - it would clump.  On July 25, I followed suggestions to freeze the cheese first for a short time to firm it up so that it would grate.  It did grate the first portion of the cheese but when it came to the end of the piece, it balled up and the cover of the processor flew up into the air.  This means that it disengaged from a locked position.  I gave it another try, and the same thing happened.  Shaken because of a near miss to my head, I phoned the customer service number and explained my problem.  The supervisor was quick to decide to send me a replacement bowl and top.  I have not received these and have been without the processor for eight weeks.
justification: The incident involved the food processor cover disengaging and flying, causing a near miss to the head, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Puchased an LG electric range from Home Depot in 2007 bought the 3 yr warranty, had numerous problems with preheat and timing and intermittent working and not working functions, such as bread proofing and the warming tray.....after many visits from repair and two replacement computer panels, I learned to kind of work around these problems and just to forego some features altogether.... until today.  Luckily it is a Sunday and I am home.  one of the features I still was able to use was the delay then cook, then hold, feature....so I am home working outside in the yard and have the front left burner on 1 to slowly cook some homemade spagetti sauce.  when I did re enter the house it was filled with smoke and the burner was on high.  I turned it off.....so I thought.  nothing I did could turn it off,  my husband and I pulled the oven away from the wall and unplugged it...we let it sit for 10 min or so and re plugged it ...same thing, the burner immediatly went to high....we called LG and got a lukewarm response with a " try calling back Tuesday" ......In my opinion, had the home burned to the ground LG would have a lawyer sitting on their front porch Monday morning.....I want them to completely go thru and replace computers or whatever....even perhaps a new oven with all the "bugs" worked out.....
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range causing smoke and inability to turn off, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the recurring issues with the appliance.

incident_description:
On Saturday September 28, 2014 at approximately 8 AM, I opened the door to my GE Monogram Refrigerator (purchased in November 2013). As I opened the door I heard a loud explosion! I looked around my apartment to determine the source of the sound - only to realize that it was coming from my refrigerator: The top glass shelf exploded - sending millions of particles of shattered glass all over me, my refrigerator and my apartment!
As I checked my body for shards of glass - I found them on my chest, feet and hands (pain and blood indicated location - too tiny to actually see the small slivers)
The blast sent glass through my kitchen, dining and living room area - all the way to my hallway
Glass shards landed everywhere: in my food, in the refrigerator bins, on the shelves, on the floor and carpets; not one inch of the refrigerator was clean - all covered with specks of glass!
I immediately called General Electric to get technical help for this disaster - only to learn that there is NO Emergency Hotline, NO Customer Service, NO one to contact for this EMERGENCY - because - for GE it is a weekend - and the c-suite executives do not work on weekends!
The only working number for GE was to buy parts or to schedule a service call (later in the week) as NO ONE could / would even admit that an exploding glass shelf qualified as an EMERGENCY...if one shelf explodes - who is to say the others will not explode???? I am fearful that the entire refrigerator will explode.
I now fearfully open the refrigerator door - protecting myself by standing behind the door as I open it!
I have asked on Facebook and Twitter for someone from GE to call me - to get this LEMON of a product out of my apartment - immediately!
This DISASTER follows on the heels of a disaster this summer with the ice draw...when it stopped making ice! When the repair person arrived - he said that I had to shut down the refrigerator for 48 hours and allow it to defrost. This did not appear to be an appropriate response and merely an answer to get me out-of-his way. (I have been without ice all summer)

ÃÂ·         Fortunately - I did NOT follow his advice for I have read online that other consumers (who did follow the instructions) had to have the technician take the entire freezer apart to fix the problem

(The GE repairman that was sent out was so incompetent that finally we called 1-800-Appliance and they figured it out in 10 minutes. It is a design flaw in the refrigerator. When we turned it off, all the built up ice in and around the ice maker would thaw and drain into the different components. When we turned it back on, it would freeze and clog everything up. The 1-800-Appliance repairman had to take apart the whole freezer to clean out the ice. The whole experience was so frustrating and GE's customer service is horribly inept)
justification: The incident caused injury to the user, but no death or serious injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that all five metal knobs on the gas range become extremely hot. The consumer stated that the knobs become extremely hot when the oven is on. 

The consumer touched a knob when the oven was on, and he was burnt on his right thumb. The consumer put water on it to avoid blistering. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manf around 9/1/14. They sent out silicone sleeves to slide over shaft of the of the knobs. The consumer stated that the silicone sleeves did not make much difference; it would still burn the user. 

The consumer called the retailer on 9/11/14 . Since the consumer was under retailer's warranty, they sent out a technician from Boston Joe's Appliance Repair (Manchester, CT) on 9/15/14. The technician ordered plastic knobs to see if they would help eliminate the issue. The consumer is waiting on the knobs to arrive and be installed. 

There are no recalls on this unit. 

The consumer is not sure if the plastic knobs would make much difference.
justification: The consumer was burnt on his right thumb, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue persists despite initial fixes, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I was cooking lemon chicken at 350 degrees in a 13 x 9 Pyrex dish.  The timer had went off and my daughter in law turned to assist me.  She had opened the oven and I just leaned over and grabbed the dish, and IT EXPLODED!!!!
What a mess.  The glass shreds shot into my leg and foot along with the hot liquid from the dish splashing and burning the two of us.  The larger pieces flew with such force that they cracked the glass window in my oven!
All I could think of was Thank God we turned our faces away and that the children were not right there.  They would of been eye level.  
Everyone at the table jumped up and we all tried to clean up this terrible mess.  Now not only was our dinner ruined for the night, and  I was out the money for the food that was just ruined, but my oven was broken.  
Please inform people of this warning. I have used this dish before and never had a problem.
It is a little scary when you have to be afraid of  something like a pyrex dish.
I also need to know how I should proceed as I feel someone should make good on the damage.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries from glass shards and hot liquid burns, and significant property damage, but no deaths.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting her smooth top electric range, purchased around April 2014 and from the very first day she very lightly brushed against the knobs on the front of the range and  the burners came on. Consumer noted range was not returned.  This continued until problem fixed during the end of August by customer. 

There were no injuries, cover on the stove top was burned.

The caller contacted the manufacturer around the beginning of July 2014.

Consumer also noted photos show burners protrude past oven door handle. She stated screen is usually blank. She also stated nudging panel turned on a heating unit that destroyed a stove cover and could have set fire to the house had she not detected it by chance.

Consumer indicated her husband has corrected the problem by installing a steel bar and attaching it to the range in front of the burner knobs (see photo). They can no long come on by accident.

Consumer suggested burners should be recessed or oven door handle protrude 3" to avoid having your body touch the stove. She also noted touching the panel screen lightly should not turn on a burner especially if you can't see the symbols. Consumer stated maybe a buzzer to alert you that a burner came on or make burners harder to turn.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but there was a risk of fire and damage to the stove top, which is a serious incident.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Dishwasher started smoking/fire from the circuit board while trying to run the dishwasher and would not stop until circuit breaker was switched off.
Someone who would not know to turn the circuit breaker off on the main electrical box could allow the scenario to become safety critical to a point of burning the home down.

Model Number 665.16052400 
Serial Number FR4403761
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher smoking/fire, which could escalate to a safety-critical situation if not addressed, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Flat Top Stove.
   The left front burner is turning on randomly by itself. The burner has had several problems with shutting off when you move the knob to the off position. The burner has recently began to turn on to high and you must unplug the entire unit to get the burner off.
justification: The stove is turning on by itself, which could lead to fire or injury, making it a serious incident.

incident_description:
Cuisinart FP-14DC Elite Collection 14-Cup Food Processor, Die Cast

This food processor is equipped with a [REDACTED]safety feature that's supposed to prevent the unit from running when the lid properly locked into place. However, on several occasions, once turning On the unit, it will not turn off. Removing the lid or pressing the Off button does not turn the unit off. The only way to turn it off is to unplug the unit from the wall. This means that the exposed sharp blade continues to run inside the food processor even when the [REDACTED]safety lid is removed, and this is extremely unsafe.

Upon reading reviews on several websites such as[REDACTED], it appears that this is a common issue that's been reported by several consumers. I'm surprised that a safety recall does not already exist for this model food processor.
justification: The food processor fails to turn off, exposing users to a running sharp blade, which is a significant safety hazard. Reports indicate this is a common issue among consumers.

incident_description: I was boiling water on our new stove and I began to smell something burning. When I went to look where the smell was coming from I noticed that the plastic between the stovetop and the control panel was literally bubbling and melting causing smoke and a terrible odor. As this was right next to the control knobs I could have easily burned myself and had I not turned it off immediately I'm afraid of what could have happened had it continued to burn/melt. When we contacted Frigidaire they told us this was a cosmetic issue and they couldn't do anything. This stove is incredibly dangerous and a potential fire hazard and I'm appalled that they didn't seem to think it was a concern.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and smoke, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Came home from work & saw that the outer over door glass had shattered. The glass was all over the floor.
justification: The shattered glass indicates an incident occurred, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Stove oven element does not turn off after off button is pressed. The light goes out indicating the stove is off but I felt it the next morning and the oven was still on even though there were no indicator lights indicating that it was on. This seems to be the same problem listed under a recall issued by the CPSC for Kenmore stoves sold between  June 2001 through August 2009, which this is. The model number on my stove is 79096212404 and the serial number is VF52044202. The recall was originally issued August 27, 2009 by the CPSC and can be found at:

http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2009/Frigidaire-and-Kenmore-Smoothtop-Electric-Ranges-Recalled-Due-to-Fire-Hazard/
justification: The stove's failure to turn off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: On or about the evening of September 19, 2014, my mother was in the kitchen and informed me that the microwave start on its own. I looked at the display and saw that it was blank. That is, the time was not displaying as it normally does. A few minutes later, while my mother, my uncle, and I were in the kitchen, the microwave turns on again. This time, the three of us saw the microwave turn on by itself. We quickly unplugged it for fear of a safety hazard. I noticed that there are two other reports of this nature in the past couple months. This needs to be investigated.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential safety hazard but no injury occurred, and there are similar past reports indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
I have an LG gas range Model LRGLRG30915W which I purchased on 3-8-11. On Friday, 8-29-14, I was preheating the oven on 350 degrees. I was standing next to the oven and getting a pan out of the bottom cabinet. All of a sudden I hear a crackling noise. I look up and see the oven glass still mostly still in the door completely shattered. Then as I stood there, all the glass fell out of the oven. I was barefoot. I went to get my shoes, but because glass scattered all over the floor I ended up with a cut on the bottom of my right foot and a piece of glass in my left foot.

My left foot also had glass in it. On 3/7/14 I went to emergency to have it removed. I am diabetic - this could have been dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts and glass embedded in feet) requiring emergency care, especially concerning due to the individual's diabetes.

incident_description:
I bought a Vilking VGSO 100 SS oven on Ebay in Nov 2013.  I was not able to install it until my apartment alterations were finished in April 2014.  At which point it was installed.  When turned on the oven spews gas.  Even after it is hot,  it still spews gas.  It is REALLY DANGEROUS.  It makes my eyes water and I fear it will cause an explosion.

On May 2, 2014, I called Viking Range Corp., the manufacturer of the oven, and gave them the serial number.  Viking told me it was refurbished "B" stock.  It had previously been serviced three times for the temperature gauge in Sept 2011, ignition replacements in Nov 2011 and Bake ignition switch in Feb 2012 and finally the unit was replaced and refurbished and resold.  I told Viking about the gas leak and asked whether they would fix the oven.  They told me it was no longer covered by a warranty and therefor not their problem.  Since May 2, 2014, I have had the oven serviced three times for an ignition and miscellaneous oven parts at a cost of $1300.  The oven still does not work and continues to spew gas.  I have a wife and two children in the apartment and fear for their safety whenever I turn it on.  The oven is defective and dangerous.
justification: The oven spews gas, which is a serious safety hazard, but there is no injury or death reported.

incident_description: Turned on ignitor position on gas cook top.  Control knob began electrical arching uncontrollably underneath knob inside cooktop, with large visible flashes, until controller burst into flames
justification: The incident involved a gas cooktop ignitor malfunction leading to flames, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using the skillet to make tortillas on medium heat. After five minutes of making tortillas, one of the rivet caps began smoking, so I turned the heat off. Shortly thereafter I heard a loud pop (similar to an exploding firework) and the rivet cap launched across my kitchen. I examined the rivet cap a few minutes later and found black residue around the edge where it would connect to the rivet.
justification: The incident involved a rivet cap smoking and launching across the kitchen, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On Wednesday, September 3, 2014 after pouring the final cup of coffee from the carafe of a Mr. Coffee coffee maker, I attempted to turn off the unit by pushing the off switch.  Upon applying pressure to the rocker switch pad a sharp cracking sound occured and an arc of electrical flame shot from the switch burning and blackening my index finger.  I disconnected the power cord from the electrical outlet and observed that there was a small burn point on the switch pad which was frozen in the off position.  This unit was a Jarden Corporation, Mr. Coffee model DW 12 and had a date code which was G073 with a supplier code of DG.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the index finger, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I have contacted Kenmore about a legal claim.  We purchased a Kenmore Elite 790 range ($1700) less than 3 years ago, during self cleaning it fryed out the computer boards within the oven and power surged to our Air Conditioner and blew out the capacitor in our AC unit.  We have 4 children and have spent hundreds of dollars feeding them without a stove for several days.  We have been sleeping in a 90 degree house for several days.  There are several cases of this issue that have not been dealt with by Kenmore.  We had this confirmed by an appliance repair expert who repairs these all day.  He stated that the range gets to over 600 degrees during self-clean and continually fries out the computer boards, that it's a known issue."  Then why isn't the CPSC doing anything about these manufacturers allowing the production of defective products?  The pop sounded like a gun shot, it scared me and my children.  There is no accountability from these companies.

Someone needs to call me to mitigate this issue.  I found several cases of this stoves issues online and will be reporting this to the CPSC as well.  I have contacted my homeowners insurance at Allstate and this will be a covered claim and they will subrogate against Kenmore, but I want a case opened and Kenmore to be held accountable.  A $1700 range should last more than 2.5 years.  It's unprofessional & dangerous.
justification: The incident caused a power surge and damaged the oven and AC unit, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have owned the stove for 15 months and 10 months into owning it the stovetop broke while i was cooking on it. NOTHING dropped, crack from front to back and spider cracks to the sides. Frigidaire said it was not covered under warranty because it was not manufacturer defect but i did not do anything. Long story short we had it replaced  on our expense and not even 5 months later it has done it yet again! Before the incident i noticed the range staying a hot red color on low but didnt pay any attention to that FRIGIDAIRE is yet again claiming it is not their problem and our warranty is up so they wouldnt be able to do anything. If this problem has happened more than one the same exact break they are responsible this could cause some serious damage to my home and my family,being such a dangerous device they need to stand by their products like they say they do. I did not plan on replacing my appliances in a year they were supposed to last for 10 plus years what a horrible company/brand never again will i buy or recommend a Frigidaire/electrolux product again they LIE AND STEAL FROM CONSUMERS!
justification: The incident describes a recurring stovetop malfunction without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence suggests a likely occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
Sunbeam Electric kettle model number SEK17 has a faulty switch. This shows up in a couple of ways.

1/ When the kettle reaches a full boil, I can hear the auto-off mechanism click 'off', but the electrical switch inside stays on and the kettle continues to boil in the off position.

2/ With the switch in the off position and the kettle 'off' I was filling the kettle with water and the internal switch went on, providing power to the kettle element, even though the external switch was still in the off position.

I believe that if left unattended, the kettle would fail to switch off, then boil dry and possibly melt down and cause a fire.

FYI - I have been using other brands and types of electric kettles for 45 years and I am very familiar with their normal operation.
justification: The faulty switch could lead to the kettle boiling dry and potentially causing a fire, posing a significant safety hazard.

incident_description:
We were using the microwave to defrost beef (50% power for 2 minutes).  After the two minutes, the timer ended, but the microwave continued to run full power for some time (about 10+ minutes) until the beef caught fire.  At that point, we noticed the problem,unplugged the microwave, and put out the fire.  Now, any time the microwave is plugged in and the door is closed, it will run at full power, regardless of any times or settings.  We have since replaced the microwave for safety.
Magic Chef Microwave
Model HMD1110B
We reported this problem to Magic Chef.
justification: The microwave malfunction caused a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Our whirlpool oven safety glass shattered while no one was near it and it was not in use and has not been used in a couple days.
justification: The safety glass shattered without causing injury or being in use, indicating an incident with no harm but potential safety concern.

incident_description:
My boyfriend was removing a Home Essentials Glacier 17 oz cooler drinking glass from the top rack of the dishwasher and it suddenly exploded in his hand, sending thousands of broken glass pieces all over the kitchen and into his hand.  If his face had been near it or had there been anyone standing by, this could have flown into his eyes or other people/animals.

I purchased these from TJ Maxx in San Carlos, CA - bought 2 boxes of 10 in each box - Home Essentials Glacier 17 oz cooler drinking glass.
justification: The incident caused injury to the boyfriend, but there was no death or serious injury.

incident_description: I was baking scalloped potatoes in a large glass Pyrex glass at 450 degrees when we heard a loud noise.  The glass dish had exploded in the oven.
justification: The glass dish exploded, but there is no mention of injury or death, only a loud noise.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she used the cooker three times successfully, following the instruction. The fourth time she went to use it, the cooker seal failed.

The consumer was reaching up to the cabinet to the left the range. The cooker was on the right back burner.
The consumer stated that the steam was coming out from the failed seal. The consumer felt the cooker explode
The consumer was injured from the steam. The consumer was burned under her right breast (1st and 2nd degree burns). The consumer has two marks on her breast from something hitting her. The consumer also received steam burn on her face. The consumer was wearing eye glasses and they were severely damaged. The consumer believes that if she wasn't wearing glasses, she could have lost her eyes. 
The consumer's brother took the consumer to the bathroom and put cold water on her. The consumer was treated by family who is a CNA. The consumer called her doctor and spoke over the phone. The consumer was provided prescription medication for her burns.

The consumer spoke to the manf. They informed her that she might not have used the cooker properly. They asked for the consumer to return the cooker. The consumer does not want to send back the cooker because she would like to have it tested for product safety. 
The consumer also contacted the retailer and filed a complained with them. Their insurance company has opened a claim. The consumer stated that the retailer will mostly pass the claim to the manf. The consumer stated that the manf is trying to blame her for misusing the product. The consumer asked the manf to send that statement to her in writing.
The consumer was informed by the manf that there have been no complaints on this product.
justification: The consumer suffered 1st and 2nd degree burns from steam and impact, requiring medical treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the manufacturer claims no prior complaints, suggesting such incidents are not common.

incident_description: LG MICROWAVE CAUGHHT ON FIRE SECOND MICROWAVE ON THE VERGE OF STARTING ON FIRE. FIRST FIRE WAS MY DAUGHTERS [REDACTED]. MY MICROWAVE IS IDENTICAL MODEL, S/N DATE OF MANUFACTURE. STARTING TO BURN IN THE TOP PORTION
justification: The microwave caught fire, but there is no mention of injury or death, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite Microwave/Wall Oven Combination. The wall oven has expanded to the point that the racks will not stay in place and fall to the bottom of the oven if anything heavier than a cookie sheet is placed on the racks and the racks or container are moved.  On several occasions, the rack has fallen with a hot casserole on it resulting in my arms bring burned by scalding liquid. I've also fallen onto the hot, open oven door when trying to remove a hot casserole because the casserole falls while I'm holding it.  

This is a well documented problem.  Please refer to report number 20140619-25516-2147443555.   The defective, expanded wall cavity creates a dangerous situation and Sears, or the manufacturer Frigidaire, should be required to fix this defect.
justification: The incident describes burns from scalding liquid and falls onto a hot oven door, indicating injuries have occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the plastic under the black rubber is falling apart. The consumer stated that he noticed pieces of plastic falling into his salad.

The consumer stated that he moved the black rubber and saw that the plastic underneath it is damaged.

The consumer contacted the manf through e-mail in August. The consumer was informed that he would receive 20% off of a new one. They informed him that he would need a receipt in order to receive a replacement. The consumer was given the product as a gift and does not have a receipt.

The consumer stated that he sent the photos of the defective product to the manf as well. 

The consumer believes that this is a safety hazard as pieces of plastic can be consumed without being aware that the product is breaking apart. 

Consumer stated he emailed mfr several times over the past few months and also spoke to them over the 
phone but they were not interested in replacing the product or looking into possible defects.
justification: The consumer reported plastic pieces falling into food, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG French Door SS refrigerator from Home Depot on or around 2006/2007.  Though the appliance is out of warranty, I believe what has occurred is a fire hazard for this model and possibly others.  The model number is LFC25760ST.

Over an unknown period of time, apparently both light bulb fixtures in the lighting casing and controls the temperature settings, have apparently burned up, and today the whole unit literally fell from its attachment to the top of the inside of the appliance. There was a burning smell which was the plastic casing for the screws holding the unit up. The heat from the bulb fixtures had heated this plastic to the point where they both melted and the whole unit dropped down hanging only by the wire connector which allows the temperature portion to regulate.  

I have no doubt this could have caused a fire if not for the plastic casings melting resulting in the unit dropping down today.
