justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to melted plastic and burning smell, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description:
GE over the counter microwave with a metal shelf caught fire and started arcing on September 8 of this year.  I noticed it after a few seconds and turned it off.  Plastic tab in wall is all blackened, there is a black streak from the fire on the wall of the mike and little black specks all over inside.


I am scared to use it and feel it must be replaced.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was turned off quickly, causing no injury, only damage to the appliance and minor wall markings.

incident_description: I received a Frigidaire FPEC3085ks model cooktop. Serial number NF10818969 direct from Frigidaire and installed by their service tech as a recall replacement for model PLEC30s9ec serial number nf93104560.  The original issue with the PLEC30s89ec was the red indicator lights would overheat and break from the red lenses cap. Tech came out twice on previous model to replace the PS1151075 part and now on new unit both red indicator lights are broken part 318337201. This is clearly a manufacturing design issue and they need to get the design right. It is a hazard as when the light breaks away it allows moisture to enter the control area and becomes a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a manufacturing defect causing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: In the middle of the night while the whole house was sleeping the microwave beeped and the it started running all by itself. I turned it off and it was very hot to the touch. We unplugged the microwave immediately.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was turned off without injury, making it an incident with no harm.

incident_description: Middle rack in open slides off the side of the range spilling contents. Rack is not bent, fits into bottom ok. Middle of oven seems to have expand and wont hold rack.
justification: The incident involves a rack falling off the range, but no injury was reported, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: Loud noise, sparking and fire in control box and power supply .   Fire extinguished
justification: The incident involved a fire in a control box and power supply, which was extinguished without reported injuries, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
I was Browning ground beef in a Wolfgang Puck Stainless Steel Skillet on Low-Med Heat. I heard a "pop"  and saw that the lid cracked over the ground beef causing glass to fall into the ground beef.  I took pictures of the lid and have them if needed.

This is very concerning as I paid a premium price for the whole set of Wolfgang Puck Stainless Steel cookware as well as for the Ground Beef.

Please let me know if you would like the pictures.
justification: The incident involved a cracked lid and glass falling into food, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This coffee maker is equipped with a wand/spout for steaming milk.  After several uses, it actually separated from the unit allowing hot steam - and the hot milk created - to spray all over hands, clothing and the surrounding area.  Since so much hot steam is shooting from the exposed connection, it's very hard to hit the stop button since you're most concerned about getting your hands anywhere near the shooting steam.  I sent the product in for repairs and made specific note of this problem.  I did some reviews online to see that this flaw was not uncommon and reported on Amazon among other sites.  The coffee maker was returned quickly and everything seemed to be working fine. The repaired unit included a brand new nozzle that I assumed was reengineered to fix the earlier separation problem.  After several uses, it separated once again shooting hot steam on my hand and hot milk all over the counter and my clothing. 
I contacted the company and complained about the problem and repeated burn danger.  The service team was very responsive again but simply sent my another new nozzle. 
After being burned several times, I refuse to try this new nozzle for an extended period and believe that the company needs to issue newly designed nozzles to eliminate this hazard.
justification: The incident describes repeated burns from hot steam and milk, indicating injury (severity 3). The problem is reported as not uncommon and has recurred after repairs, suggesting a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
when I was heating up baby food. I
set it for 10 seconds, walked away to put my baby in his
chair, walked back and the micro was still going, which I
thought was too long. I opened the door and watched a second
to see if the food was overheated and bubbling, which it
looked fine. I took it out and put the spoon in to stir it
and it exploded on me, the floor, the cabinets the ceiling,
everything! I had burns to my face and wrist to which I
still have the scar on my wrist. I didnt do anything at that
time because I gave it the benefit of the doubt that MAYBE I
had put an extra 0 or somehow hit the wrong button. BUT more
and more afterwards I noticed it would keep going and time
would not go down. It also turns on by itself sometimes when
you just close the door. This means the whole baby food
episode was not my fault. And thank GOD I didnt have the
baby in my arms at the time.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the face and wrist, indicating injury (severity 3), but the microwave malfunction described seems uncommon, suggesting a lower likelihood (2).

incident_description: I bought my GE 1.4 cu ft 1100 watt microwave oven model # WES1450DN1BB 2 years ago. I got up one morning last week and heard a beeping sound and found my microwave had come on. It was very hot inside and warm on the outside. I had to open the door for it to stop...wouldn't respond to buttons. I unplugged and left it off for several hours and plugged it back in...set the clock and several minutes later it started on its own. It is a fire hazard.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself and overheating poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I reheated a slice of pizza in my microwave using the 30 sec. button.  Soon after it started the microwave began making a humming sound.  At the end of 30 seconds, the timer stopped, the turntable stopped and the light went off but the humming continued and I could hear the pizza continue to sizzle.  Next smoke started coming out of the vents and the microwave itself was getting hot.  Finally, my neighbor came over and unplugged the microwave.  The food inside was seriously burnt.  It is out on the deck cooling off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave causing smoke and burnt food, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
We were cooking stuffed peppers in the oven on the eveing of September 11, 2014.  We got a pyrex casserole dish (which was at room temperature) and placed the two stuffed peppers in the dish and put some water at the bottom of the dish per the[REDACTED]recipe instructions.  We then placed the pyrex casserole dish in the oven.  Once the food was done cooking, my husband went to get the dish out of the oven.  When he picked it up and was pulling it out, it shattered in his hand.  Fortunately he pulled his hand away in time and did not sustain any injuries.  

I am a Federal Employee with NASA and my husband is a pediatrician in San Jose.  There was nothing I saw that indicated that these Pyrex dishes should not be placed in the oven.  I hope your agency really looks into this so that no one gets seriously hurt.  It is just a matter of time before someone gets hurt unless their product is improved or safety precautions are updated on their product.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered but no injuries occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description: The Kenmoore Elite Dishwasher filled the house with smoke, charred the counter top, from the result of an apparent electrical fire in the electrical panel.
justification: The incident caused property damage (smoke and charred countertop) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: GE Over the Range Microwave oven, Model: JVM7195DFBB turned on by itself.  Stove was not used at all the entire day.  Microwave had been used sporadically throughout the day, but not for at least 3 hours before the incident.  About 20:00, Family was watching TV and microwave started by itself.  Turntable was not spinning.  Light was on.  Cancel button did nothing.  Opening door caused it to shut off.  Closed door and it immediately started again.  No message in display area except clock time.  Unplugged unit, plugged back in and immediately started again.  Left unplugged and will call manufacturer.  Unit was only purchased and installed in May (4 months ago).
justification: The microwave turned on by itself without causing injury, but posed a potential hazard that required unplugging the unit.

incident_description:
Our GE spacemaker turned on by itself while no one was in the kitchen.  It was making a grinding noise which alerted us.  It smelled horrible like plastic burning or an electrical fire.  The lights were off, the numbers on the panel gone but the inside turn table was spinning.  Oven continued to spin when opening to stop it.  The only way the appliance stopped was to go above cabinet and unplug.  Device was hot to touch as well as surrounding cabinets.  Fire department was contacted to inspect wall for fire, they plugged it in briefly and it immediately began to smell and make same noise but no lights then sparked.  They unplugged again and circuit breaker was shut off.  Microwave was removed from the house once it cooled down.  Thankfully someone was home or our house would have burned down.

GE Spacemaker JVM1630WB
Serial #LA9694245
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave that posed a fire hazard but resulted in no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The plastic spacer between the door handle and the door to the microwave fractured resulting in a jagged edge.  Using the microwave can result in a minor laceration to the users hand.

Since this is an above range microwave, the angle at which the user reaches up to the door handle causes the jagged edge to catch on the side of the users hand on the pinky finger near the first knuckle, resulting in a minor laceration.
justification: The plastic spacer between the door handle and the door to the microwave fractured resulting in a minor laceration to the users hand.

incident_description:
frigidaire freestanding electric range control panel failure turns oven on randomly. error code f-11.  This is a fire hazard.  We were home at the time of the failure and disabled the product by turning off the circuit breaker, so there were no injuries and no loss of property except the appliance itself.  This is the second time since the product was purchased in Nov. 2011 that this appliance has had a major fire hazard problem.  The first failure was a failed oven temperature probe in Dec 2013. Error code f-10  The oven temperature would go very high or fluxuate randomly despite the set temperature.  Power to appliance was turned off to prevent further hazard at this time too.  The control unit was replaced at this time as a fix.  This part has failed again.  This range has been used for normal household use only.  It has not been abused or even used excessively.

This is unacceptable and Frigidaire will take no responsibility for unacceptable performance or saftey hazard of their products.  They will not admit to any product recalls on this model or any updates or fixes for defective parts.  How likely is it that my unit fails two times in a year unless there is a product defect?  Do the math.
justification: The incident describes a control panel failure that poses a fire hazard, but no injuries or property damage occurred due to prompt action. This is the second occurrence of a major fire hazard issue with the appliance.

incident_description:
Cuisinart DC-2200 coffee maker caught on fire.  Serial 60309C. After brewing on normal start setting about 30 minutes. Had poured coffee from the carafe and was drinking. Tasted fine. Noticed the on light indicator was not lit and checked. There was not enough time elapsed for the auto-off feature to turn it off. When I approached I could see coffee in the carafe was almost boiling and the maker seemed to be turned off. I reached to unplug and noted smoke pouring from the opening where the cord goes into the back of the coffee maker. Bottom of the coffee maker was burning. Rancid burning plastic electrical smell. I was fortunate to be in the kitchen when this happened. The amount of burning in such a short time would have caused a house fire had I been upstairs on a work morning. This happened on Sunday so I was downstairs in the kitchen. Scary to think it could have burned me, my husband, my pets, my house and property. 

Upon researching for possible reasons I found this has been a common occurrence with a variety of models and sizes of Cuisinart coffee makers. It appears that Cuisinart should recall coffee makers.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire, posing a significant risk of injury or property damage, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My daughter was in the living room adjacent to the kitchen after I had gone to bed.  She heard a beep in the kitchen and investigated.  She found the microwave running in the dark kitchen with nobody else around.  When she tried to stop it, the keypad controls were unresponsive.  A code of -SE- was displayed.  She unplugged the microwave and reported it to me the next morning.  This is the second issue with this microwave, the first was about a year ago when one of the sensors mounted to the bottom plate behind the control panel burned up.  This was discovered after the microwave stopped functioning.  That part was replaced and there were no more incidents until now.  We have not plugged the unit back in.  Two failures on a 4 year old appliance is too many, especially considering if my daughter hadn't decided to play some video games that night, we could have had a fire.  It will be replaced by, hopefully, something without these problems.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave with potential fire risk, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
My Samsung Microwave Oven is approximately 3 years and 7 months old.  It has worked well for all this time.  However I returned from a 2 day trip and was sitting in the family room and suddenly the microwave came on  with the window stating POPCORN.  I never use that function but it was running full blast empty which causes it to heat up very quickly without something to absorb the rays to heat.  that cabinet got very hot fast.  I pushed the stop/clear button and it went to time. I decided to reset it like the instructions stated by unplugging it for 10-12 seconds and then plug into power.  It came on ready to set the clock again which I did.  however in less than 2 minutes it came on again to POPCORN and the inside plate was turning it had full power.  If this had occurred while I was gone it could have resulted in a serious kitchen fire..I have heard of the before but never thought a good product like Samsung would do that.  The vendor  RC WILLEY was notified of the incident.  I had a 5 year warranty on it.  They called back and stated that ti would cost more to fix it than to get a new one and told me to come in and pick out any brand I wanted and they would uninstall the defective one and install a new one.\
Product Information:  Samsung MicroWave Oven
l.8 cubic feet 1100 Watt 10 ower LV 
Serial #:  J46W7MOZ800678R
I reported this to the Samsung 800 number and they said to contact the vendor since I had a warranty.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred. Such incidents are unlikely but possible with electronic devices.

incident_description: Oven racks do not fit properly anymore due to oven walls warping. Burns can occur when  Racks drop causing hot  food to splash and spill.
justification: The incident can cause burns, which is an injury, but not death.

incident_description:
On 6/21/2004, I purchased an Electrolux side-by-side refrigerator: Model #E23CS75DSS1, Serial # LA41109108.  Since purchase, I have consistently changed the water filter cartridge every 6 months with no problems.

On 7/22/2014, I purchased a replacement filter from East Coast Appliance where we originally purchased the refrigerator.  On 7/29/2014, I installed it in accordance with manufacturers instruction manual.  As soon as I started the 3 minute flush and check for leakage, the filter exploded from the refrigerator's filter housing  with such force it landed 11 feet from the refrigerator in the great room. Given the mass of the filter and it's acceleration, it could have seriously injured someone.  I re-installed the old filter with no problems noted.

Thinking it was a defective filter, I returned it to East Coast Appliance and they gave me a replacement.  The results were the same.

At this time, I thought there may be a design issue with the new filter.  I did a web search and found others with the same issues.

I called Electrolux customer service.  The representative understood the filter was redesigned but because of issues with older refrigerators, the filter was re-redesigned.  He shipped me one (Part #EWF2CBPA).

I installed it, the results were the same.

I called Electrolux customer service.  The representative understood the filter was redesigned but was not re-redesigned.  She needed the Serial Number which I did not have handy.

I called Electrolux customer service with serial number.  The representative understood the filter was redesigned.  Admitting no issues or responsibility, she said she would ship me a filter base (Part #240396002) as a matter of "goodwill".  She did not believe they needed to send a technician to the house it that replacement "only required three screws" (which turned out to be absolutely incorrect).

Today, 6 Sep 2014 I successfully changed the filter base and filter.

I believe Electrolux knows there is a safety issue with older refrigerators.  Their redesigned filter made my refrigerator obsolete and dangerous.  Because of the above very dangerous issue, I believe the older units should be recalled.  Electrolux customer service should warn customers.  The filter base should be changed out at Electrolux expense. 

Thank you in advance for your consideration,
[REDACTED]
justification: The filter exploded with force but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Our coffee pot just posed a significant fire risk. The product details are listed below, and I see on Amazon that many other users are reporting the same thing in the product review section. Scary. 

What happened: We brewed a pot of coffee on a Saturday morning, drank most of it, and let it sit. The auto-shut-off worked at the 2 hour mark, then soon after that, I heard what sounded like another pot of coffee brewing, but LOUDLY.  The coffee pot light was still off at this point. Then there was smoke, and a strong smell of burning something -- wires? -- that was definitely not coffee. We ran the coffee maker out to the deck and hosed it down, which produced a ton of smoke and much more smell. Truly scary, as this clearly would have led to a fire if left unattended. We now unplug all of our appliances after use because we are so nervous! At least I know it may be a faulty product. I only hope it is recalled before someone loses their home. It's an incredibly popular item, and consumers need to be protected!

Purchased February 2011
"Cuisinart DCC-1200BCH Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker, Black Chrome"
Kitchen
$65.19
Purchased from Amazon.com, LLC
justification: The incident involved a significant fire risk with smoke and burning smell, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: In 2010 I purchased a GE gas Cafe range $2500.  A few months later it has a gas leak. The control valve was replaced. Service man left, used the range, another gad leak right away. Seems the bad part was replaced with another bad part.  Weeks pass each time service is needed, part has to be ordered then another service date scheduled to put the part in.  We had the same part replaced three times. In August of 2014 another gas leak in the range. This time we did not want this range any longer.  GE agreed to replace it but we had to pay $1,000 for the new one.  We agreed only because we felt better to pay the money than die from gas poisoning.  We has the range installed by a gas certified tech.  The first time I used the oven you could smell the gas pouring out of the oven again.  My service tech advised me that he has seen this problem with many models of GE gas ranges. Waiting for repairs again.
justification: The incident involves repeated gas leaks with no reported injuries, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence based on the service tech's experience with similar models.

incident_description: At approximately 11:30pm on September 9, 2014, a loud pop and explosion was heard in the kitchen.  It was discovered that the front glass in our oven had exploded, Kenmore model No. 790.97453804, serial No. VF00853619.  Large pieces hung to door and small shards were all over the kitchen floor.  The oven was NOT on at the time.   Earlier in the evening at approximately 6:30, oven was on at 350 for approximately 30 minutes, and was turned off.   The product was purchased March 12, 2010.  Very concerned that even if this is repaired it could happen again at any time with no warning.  I have children who could have been injured and I am scared to use this oven.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing potential injury risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
We own a Kenmore stove that is exhibiting the same problems as the stoves that were recalled in 2009. However, our model and serial number are not in the range of recalled stoves. 

The two large burners will sometimes go into high mode even when the selector switch is on low. They also fail to shut off when the switch is turned off. The high mode seems to be hotter than even the highest setting. 
The front left burner has powered on even with the switch in the off position.

Model # 790.96009600
Serial # VF64037928

We have contacted Kenmore previously and they said that they could not help due to the stove not being in the recall range. I believe this to be a fire hazard and Kenmore refuses to acknowledge the problem.
justification: The stove's malfunctioning burners pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: I set my range to preheat. About 2-4 minutes into the preheat I heard a loud pop or crack coming from the location of the range. When I went to investigate I seen an orange glow coming from behind the stove and the control panel lights flickered for a few seconds. I then realized the stove was on fire internally. I pulled the stove out quickly and pulled the electrical cord out from the wall. I seen flames inside an attempted to put them out. They finally went out (Thankfully) so the entire damage was contained behind the control panel and internally behind all metal pieces. There was no indication of any issues or problems prior to this incident and this stove had been used every day since purchase without incident. Nothing was on or inside the stove at the time of incident.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was contained without injury or death, and the stove had been used daily without prior issues.

incident_description: Purchased a Fridgidaire Gallery Electric Cooktop in August of 2000. Within the first year, I noticed the outer ring on one of the large elements did not function properly, but we still had the other so we did not report it. Over the next few years, we began having problems with both of the larger cooking elements. We had to jiggle the knob to get the one remaining large element to work (the other had stopped working completely). I did not contact the manufacturer or retailer as I believed it was out of warranty. After both of the larger elements stopped working, the surface light that indicates the stove top is on remained on even though none of the four elements were warm to the touch. Until last night (September 8, 2014) our two larger elements had been dormant for several years. We had gotten so used to them not working, we foolishly placed things on top of the surface. Last night my wife smelled something burning. I got up to investigate and discovered that the back left burner (that had not worked for over 3 years and was in the "off" position with the knob removed, had suddenly turned on and melted/burned a loaf of bread. The resulting minor fire tripped the circuit and left us both shaken thinking about the "what-ifs." I've read about the recall on Fridgidaire cooktops manufactured a year later than our model, but the descriptions of the problems with those models are very similar to what we experienced.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cooktop that caused a minor fire but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recurring issues and similar reports in other models.

incident_description:
I was at home last night watching TV and the microwave turned itself on.  It ran for 1 minute then turned itself off.  Several minutes later it turned itself back on for a minute.  The control panel was frozen and I couldn't turn the oven off.  This continued to happen until I climbed up to the upper cabinet and unplugged the unit.  The oven was very hot.  I can't imagine what would have happened if I wasn't at home or was sleeping.  This was very alarming.  I had just gotten back from a 2 week out of town trip. If this had happened while I was away there could have been a fire.  

I'm older and don't have anyone else using the microwave so it is gently used and is less than 5 years old.  

JVM1740SM1SS
SS 901084B
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and could have caused a fire if unattended, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
to whom it may concern:

glass door of our ge oven shattered into many pieces- no cause identified & the oven was not being used at the time. 



   
The oven is a GE Model # JBP81B0K2BB
Serial # GL268431Q
justification: The glass door shattered, but no one was injured and the oven was not in use at the time.

incident_description:
On three separate occasions this kettle has burned me. Once, I accidentally let the edge of my knuckles hit the metal on the kettle when pouring, and this caused me to spill the boiling water over my countertop, but thankfully not on me. It caused burning to my knuckles, even though they were only in contact for a few seconds.

On a separate occasion, I was closing the top lid to refill the water and it was incredibly hot, burning my fingers when I was closing it.

Finally, just today, I was reaching for something else and accidentally had my arm touch the side of the kettle, burning me. This similar incident also happened to another member of my household. 

This kettle heats up the outer metal portion too much and has the potential to easily burn skin, sometimes severely. Additionally, such high temperatures persist long after the kettle is turned off. This issue has also been addressed in multiple reviews at Amazon.
justification: The description reports multiple instances of burns from the kettle, indicating injury (severity level 3). The repeated incidents and mention of similar issues in reviews suggest a high likelihood of recurrence (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
The consumer noticed on 8/1/14 that the power cord had exposed copper wire. Consumer believes this poses a safety hazard. The copper poked through the insulation, where it meets the female connector. 

The consumer states 2 months after he purchased the unit the light on the side near the base of the unit would go off and when you would push the unit back to the wall the light would turn back on. The consumer states that by pushing the unit back it would cause the power cord to press in toward the coffee pot, turning the light on. 

The consumer called the firm and they advised him that the firm ÃÂpulled their GE Walmart line from WalmartÃÂ. The consumer suggested sending the unit to them.  They didnÃÂt want to look at the item. The firm advised him that if the unit was older than a year it is out of warranty and they couldnÃÂt do anything about it.
justification: Exposed copper wire poses a safety hazard, but no injury or incident was reported. The issue is possible but not certain to occur frequently.

incident_description: First incident involved the plug to the oven and occurred while the oven was in use at 350 degrees in March 2013.  The plug "box" that came from the oven melted than began to burn the wall behind the oven.  Luckily our breaker tripped and I was able to put the fire out with a small extinguisher.  Needless to say, we ate out that night because our entire home smelled like an electrical fire.  My husband replaced the plug box the next day.  Second incident is still ongoing.  The front large burner does not respond to any temperature control that you select.  When I would turn the burner on "2" for example, the burner would come on high heat and not turn off until I turned the knob to "off".  Same goes for every other setting available for that burner.  The burner will get so hot that it turns white and will remain hot for a good 5 minutes after shut off.  The small burner directly behind it has begun doing the same thing since July 2014.  I burnt many meals before I caught on that it wasn't the cook, but the stove top.  Scared to use it and has since tripped my entire house breaker twice in the past month.  Burn marks are still on the wall behind the oven from first incident if pictures are requested.
justification: The incidents involved electrical fires and malfunctioning burners causing potential fire hazards, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We started a load of dishes and the door of the dishwasher started to emit smoke.  Flames were also visible.  I opened the door of the dishwasher and the sprayer did not stop so I ran and threw the breaker which stopped things.  I contacted Whirlpool and they sent an appliance guy to inspect it.  They are in the process of replacing it with a Maytag comparable model for free.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames from a dishwasher, but no injuries were reported and the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
Kitchen Aid electric oven, model #KERS306BSS purchased three weeks ago. Second degree burn on two different occasions, both from the top of the oven door touching (very briefly) my shin and once on my upper arm. The oven vents it's heat at the top of the oven door at the door handle.
The handle stays cool, but the part of the door that tucks under the cook top has NOTHING to protect a consumer from a serious burn. Bare stainless steel with all the oven heat that's been venting onto it for as long as you've been cooking. I was wearing jeans w/holes in the knees and went to get my food out of the oven I naturally bent a bit at the knees and barely touched the door and bam, it gave me a second degree burn on my knee cap! While reaching into the oven while door open half way I touched my tricep area to the door and received another burn.
During baking process the oven being set for 325 and convection, right before my eyes the oven went into what I can only assume was clean mode and my independent thermometer was pegged at 600 degrees and the oven showed no signs of slowing down and I could not turn it off.
The still glowing and operating oven said to unplug the oven. Nobody can shimmy a smoking hot and still running oven out from between it place with the cabinets!
I ran to the garage and flipped the breaker. Geek squad replaced main computer/control board. Once the oven did this while food was in it but I could turn the oven off and I thought it was ME that had pressed something while setting the timer. It took only a couple minutes to turn bread dough to smoking black heap.
Neither incident showed any kind of display saying it was NOT on bake. To it's credit the oven did have a kill switch in place disabling consumer from turning it on again until it was repaired.
I have been cooking for decades so another burn mark is no big deal and the oven is a real performer in keeping a perfect baking temperature (I am a baker) so I'm just extra careful, but can you imagine what would happen if while taking something from the oven a child were to walk by and touch brand new baby skin to the door? My god!
Holidays are coming and families always gather in the kitchen. Including the babies.
justification: The incident describes second-degree burns from brief contact with the oven door, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to repeated burns and the oven's design flaw.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his spouse was lifting the glass cover of the bin from the refrigerator when it shattered into several pieces. She received minor lacerations to both her hands, she did not need medical attention.  8/20 and 8/21 He contacted the manufacturer and he was informed that they would contact the company that manufactured the glass in Asia.



Consumer feels that this glass is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident resulted in minor lacerations to the hands, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the description of the glass shattering.

incident_description:
I opened the package of IKEA cups and proceeded to wash the cups.  As I reached down into one of the cups with sponge in hand, I felt something going into my finger under my fingernail.  When I looked into the cup, I noticed at the bottom, on the side, a defect, which was similar to a ÃÂbird swing defectÃÂ according to this site (http://www.ams.usda.gov/AMSv1.0/getfile?dDocName=STELDEV3003498).  

It seems that in a regular bird swing defect, the top end is connected, but in my cup, the top, sharp end was pointing straight up.  It became lodged under my fingernail and I had to have it removed by a surgeon (while my finger was anesthetized, my fingernail was lifted to remove the spike).  

It is conceivable that, had I not discovered the defect through the handwashing, the glass cup could have been put to use, and if something was placed inside the cup (e.g., ice, spoon, etc.), the glass defect could have dislodged from the cup, and someone could have drunk from the cup and swallowed the spike.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring surgical intervention, and there is a possibility of further harm if the defect had gone unnoticed.

incident_description: GE microwave, model no. JVM1750SM1SS and serial no. VS 902764 B, started on its own and would not turn off. The only way it could be turned off is by pulling the plug.
justification: The microwave started on its own, which could lead to a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My GE dishwasher blew up and started a fire it was supposed to be fixed but we were never notified by GE they had it in their Web but who looks at companies we for recall   I asked the. To evaluate the incident and they promised someone but they did not show up. My husband was home and was able to out out the fire we were very lucky but now I am extremely stress and upset about the way they are treating me. incident_description: While cleaning the Ninja Blender I poured the warm water soap solution out (as indicated by the directions) at which point the blades fell out of the blender hitting my right hand creating deep lacerations across my middle and ring fingers. This immediately caused loss of control and sensation in my ring finger. I was taken to the emergency department for medical treatment, I have since been under the care of a hand surgeon who was able to surgically reattach my tendons, though I may have some permanent nerve damage. This product has caused me a great deal of unnecessary pain and suffering. The Ninja blender product design is flawed and needs to be removed from the market to prevent any future injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in deep lacerations, loss of sensation, and required surgical intervention with potential permanent nerve damage, indicating a severe injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Electrolux electric slide-in range; model number EW30IS65JSA, serial number NF10928958 stove on  April 12, 2011.  This appliance broke for the second time in three years due to a spillover and a poor stove design.  Recently on several occasions my daughter and I got shocked when touching the stove and the overhead microwave.  On August 22, 2014 I had a home inspector visit my house and I explained that my daughter and I have gotten shocked.  He inspected the microwave to see if it was grounded and it was.  On August 24, 2014 I was putting a plate of food in the microwave to reheat and my arm was touching the microwave while my right hip was leaning against the Electrolux stove.   I received a big shock that went through my left arm and caused me to drop my cell phone
 
Because of this, I contacted a licensed electrical contractor/electrical inspector and he examined the microwave and the stove on August 30, 2014.  He determined that the microwave was indeed grounded.  However, upon testing/inspecting the stove he found that between the exterior of the stove and the microwave exterior there was 125 volts AC present.  Upon further investigation he said that the stove case was energized with this referenced voltage.  He considered this an electrocution hazard and he turned off the circuit breaker which turns off the power to the stove. This action eliminated the voltage on the exterior of the stove.  The electrician recommended that I contact Electrolux immediately and have a representative come out to examine and correct this dangerous situation. Please contact me to set up an appointment.  Thank you.  
 
This is the contact information of the electrician:

[REDACTED] 
 
 
 
Sincerely,
 
 
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes multiple instances of electric shocks, including one severe enough to cause injury by dropping a cell phone, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description: Range model#790 90929403 serial # vf54639649 On several occasions I was cooking and I saw sparks and smoke while cooking . I got electric chock  on my hand running up my arm while holding the handle from the frying pan. My son was frying some eggs and it also happen to him. I decided to lift the cover and to my surprised the whole wire that is connected to the burner had completely burn. I call sears to report the incident but they said they could not help.
justification: Electric shock and visible damage to the appliance indicate a clear injury risk, with multiple occurrences reported.

incident_description: Counter top microwave made by Whirlpool adds its own time to settings. Last night the unit came close to causing a full on fire. Whirlpool model WMC20005YD-0. I have looked this up on the internet and there are other people with the same experience.
justification: The microwave nearly caused a fire, indicating potential for injury, and similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore Elite Microwave Oven 2-11-12.  My wife was using it to heat some food and it shut off.  She went to retrieve the food and when she opened the door the microwave came back on.  She immediately shut the door and the unit shut off.  She opened the door again and it came back on.  We tried this a couple of more times and it continued to respond in the same manner.  I unplugged the unit and let it sit for approximately 10 minutes thinking something inside might need to reboot.  I plugged the unit back in and when I opened the door it started running again.  I contacted Sears and they were no help.
Hopefully this isn't happening to other consumers.  If they do not understand the dangers of the microwave process they could be in a very hazardous environment.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on when the door was opened, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
(06/2014) The consumer stated that he was using the back right burner. The front right burner came on by itself. Then the consumer heard a loud popping sound and saw a flash of light underneath the same burner. This tripped the circuit breaker. The consumer reset the breaker. A light that indicates that the element is hot stayed on for weeks.

Afterwards, the consumer stated that each time another burner was turned on, the front right burner would come on. The consumer unplugged the stove and discontinue use until it was serviced on July 8, 2014.

(08/09/2014) The same incident happened again. 

(06/2014) The consumer contacted Kenmore and advised them of the problem. He was advised that the his unit was not recalled nor was it under warranty. The consumer was advised that he would have to pay for service.  

(08/15/2014) The consumer contacted the company. The consumer was advised that the model was not recalled.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner causing a loud popping sound and flash of light, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using my apple corer/slicer to cut through Granny Smith apples in preparation for baking. I was using the usual firm pressure necessary to move the slicer through an apple, but on this occasion the blades separated from the frame and remained wedged high in the apple. The outside of the slicer, which I was still holding onto, passed rapidly by the now-free blades, slicing deeply into the pads of both my thumbs.
justification: The incident resulted in deep cuts to both thumbs, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
GE dishwasher Model number PDW8200J10WW , SN ML906260B
This dishwasher has been working for 5 years. Now, it is turning itself on and the heater is melting all the plastic in it - by itself!.  
Two days ago, in the morning the countertop was hot and then I noticed the dishwasher was EXTREMELY hot. I could not touch the contents without burning my hands.  Plastic parts were melted and pooled in the bottom.  Yesterday, we came back home in the evening and it did it again during the day!  Luckily, this time we caught it sooner because it wasn't quite as hot.  
The door was closed, but it was not turned on.  It doesn't even get that hot when it is running.  

I discovered the recall notice and apparently this model is not one of those covered. It should be.  This is dangerous!
justification: The dishwasher is malfunctioning and overheating, causing burns and melting plastic, but no severe injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description: the pressure cooker exploded on the stove while I was cooking bean soup; spewing hot bean soup in a 4 ft radius around the pressure cooker
justification: The pressure cooker exploded, but there was no injury, only a 4 ft radius of hot soup was spewed.

incident_description:
Severe laceration down the length of my fifth finger into extensor tendon that required surgery. Laceration occurred while using the Spiral Vegetable Slicer made by Paderno/World Cuisine which has NO GUARD WHATSOEVER to protect user from multiple exposed blades. User manual does  not provide adequate warning other than advising that the blades are sharp.
Vegetables like zucchini are fixed in a horizontal orientation onto the machine with plastic spikes that rotate the vegetable as the consumer rotates one end with a hand crank. The opposite end of the vegetable fits up against a series of triangular blades protruding toward the oncoming vegetable and another blade that works like a mandolin slicer. The device turns a zucchini into spaghetti as a hand crank is turned at one end pushing the zucchini into the array of blades. 
When I began turning the crank the zucchini slipped out of position and I reached to steady the zucchini and the device at the end close to the blades and probably miscalculated; the dorsal side of my fifth finger was sliced open on the triangular blades below the profile of the zucchini. 
My doctor advised me the machine is VERY dangerous!!!!! So many people are buying this same device and I am worried someone will loose a finger. These blades could easily be protected by a simple guard without interfering with the function of the device.
justification: The incident caused a severe laceration that required surgery, indicating a serious injury.

incident_description: Dishwasher heating element failed.  Continued to heat without having the the dishwasher on.  Returned home on Saturday evening and smelled something like "electric burning". Walked over to dishwasher and smell got stronger so I opened the dishwasher, smoke came out, and burnt my right hand on counter top.  A few of my dishes and a cutting board were melted and ruined. Immediately turned breaker to unit off.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific failure mode described.

incident_description: The outer glass of the gas oven door shattered by itself with a loud noise while baking a pork roast in the oven. Broken glass scattered all over the kitchen. Luckily no one was in the kitchen at that time. No one was injured. The gas oven model number is RGB746HED3WH by GE/Hotpoint.
justification: The glass shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was cooking on my smooth top range when I began hearing sizzling coming from the back of the range. Next sparks started coming up with small flames and then loud sizzles and pops and then thick black smoke was billowing out the back. At this time the breaker was tripped and the fire was out. No serious damage was done to my house. Fortunately we had a backsplash behind the stove so the wall was protected. The thick black smoke came off of the wall for the most part. We have not used the appliance since the incident occurred.
justification: The incident involved sparks, flames, and smoke but no injury or serious damage occurred, and the breaker tripped to stop the fire.

incident_description: I have a LG electric range Serial # LRE30453. serial #907mmqh00004. The front right burner does not shut off. It just happened today. I had to shut off the circuit breaker to get it to shut down. This is an extreme fire danger.  I know that there was a recall on this model for this same thing but my stove was made in July of 2009 verses June 2009.
justification: The burner not shutting off poses an extreme fire danger, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
While using the Progressive International Corp "Dice and Pop Cuber" (GPC-2750, UPC 0-78915-04170-8) per the provided instructions, and while pushing down on the handles, a blade dislodged and swung over the handle and nearly cut  my finger.  Upon inspection I noticed that another blade was missing and was discovered embedded in the cut potatoes being prepared for frying.  The blades can easily bend allowing them to lose their anchor to the base and handle assembly.  

As a result this product should be considered both a laceration and choking hazard.
justification: The incident describes a near-miss injury with a blade dislodging and nearly cutting a finger, indicating a high potential for injury. The discovery of another blade in the food also suggests a significant choking hazard.

incident_description: While holding the handle of my Capresso electric kettle, model 259-3, to pour water in my teapot after it reached its boiling point, it came unglued from the kettle itself.  I was lucky enough that I did not incur any injury, but it was a close call!
justification: The incident was a close call, but no injury was incurred, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not a rare occurrence but not very frequent either.

incident_description: The shut-off feature on my Capresso PerfectTea 48 ounce Glass Kettle has stopped working creating a fire hazard.
justification: The malfunctioning shut-off feature poses a fire hazard, which is an incident with potential for property damage but no immediate injury reported.

incident_description: My family had turned our Amana Big Oven (ACF422GAC model number) off and gone outside to eat the pizza we just cooked.  When we came back in the house about an hour later and the oven was so hot that the plastic items sitting on the cook top were melted and a glass jar on the cook top had cracked.  The oven was so hot that you could feel the heat from 5 feet away in the middle of the kitchen.  The oven was turned off and yet it was reading F2 error code on the display.  F2 means the oven is over 100 degrees above the maximum allowable temperature.  After we turned off the breaker, we looked up repair options for error code F2.  It said to replace the oven temperature sensor.  We did this but the oven is still broken and extremely dangerous.  If we turn the breaker back on, the oven immediately goes back to over 100 degrees above the allowable temperature.  If we had left our home after cooking the pizza in it, I think it would have burned down our home.  I have called Amana to discuss this with them but only get the run around.  I am extremely disappointed that this could happen to an appliance.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This was a Verismo coffee brewer by starbucks. August 13, 2014
Tried brewing coffee and  water didn't start coming right out as usual then boom, sprayed with scalding  water and hit by 2 pieces of the unit that blew apart from the front of the  brewer. Frightened tried to jump back away from debris and get the hot wet shirt off of my stomach started to fall. Reached for counter for support but couldn't stop my fall.  Bounced against cabinet doors, edge of counter and fell on floor. 
3 people at starbucks told me they knew of issues but didn't know why it was happening. Maybe brewer or pods
Called starbucks. And they Insisted I go to the ER
I have gone to the ER twice and my own doctor with The Veterans Clinic and my Mental Health provider with the Veterans Administration.
justification: The incident caused injury and required medical attention, but no death was reported.

incident_description: Came home from the store to find my refrigerator extremely hot on the inside along with a burning plastic smell.  When I opened the doors i found just that.  I then got my cell phone and recorded the inside of the refrigerator with the doors shut.  I discovered the interior light were remaining on when the door were completely closed.  I then got on some hand protection and tried to remove the bulbs.  This took several minutes since they were roasting hot.  After i removed the bulbs I let the refrigerator sit for 1hour.  As i opened the door all of the plastic that was hot fell from the top of the refrigerator. I was finally able to remove all the parts to take pictures.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and extremely hot components, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Used self clean feature and my cabinets caught on fire. Luckily I was home and put most of the flames out with a fire extinguisher. Still had to call the fire department to finish putting fire out.
justification: The incident involved a fire that required intervention from the fire department, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Product info:
Oster
Toaster Oven
Model: TSSTTVSM9L
Sold at: Bed Bath and Beyond

Luckily, it only caught my fingers.

incident_description:

light no longer comes ON until after the over is hot?
the fans inside that circulate heat are now making loud strange noises.

incident_description:
I purchased this Emerson Microwave from Walmart about 3 years ago. The microwave itself works- heats etc. However, the microwave door is melting from using the microwave as instructed. I have contacted Emerson and basically was told to throw away the microwave and discontinue using it. As i explained to the representative that this was not an issue of the microwave not working which would be the warranty which is expired but a safety issue. I tried requesting a manager and was sent to voice mail and my phone calls have not been returned. As a consumer, I feel that Emerson should had been more concerned with this safety issue and made a report as well as trying to address this issue. 

model #MWG9115SL
serial # 004049636MM
manufactured April, 2010
justification: The microwave door melting is a safety issue but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The wires under my dishwasher heated to an extreme  temperature and melted interior elements of my dishwasher.  Had the circuit not tripped in my home, there could have been much more extensive damage and fire.  The damage appears to be consistent with other recalls by Bosch- when I contacted Bosch and described the problem, they indicated that my dishwasher was not part of their recall.
justification: The incident caused damage to the dishwasher and could have caused a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The Frigidaire gas range was new/never used when I moved into the house in July 2012. On August 31, 2014, we cooked a pizza and turned off the oven. A short time later, the center panel of glass inside the oven door completely shattered. The outer and inner panes of glass were not impacted, however; so I do not understand how only the inner glass panel was affected. When I opened the oven door to verify that the inside pane remained intact, glass shards started falling out of the bottom of the door. Keeping the door closed helps; but tiny shards are still managing to fall out of the bottom of the door -- and I have stepped on a few of them in the last two days, even though I keep washing and re-washing the floor.
justification: The incident involved glass shards causing minor injuries when stepped on, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the event and its consequences.

incident_description:
While baking some cookies at 350 degrees, the glass on the oven door suddenly exploded and widely scattered in front of the stove.  After I stopped shaking, I called the department store for repair. While cleaning up the mess, the service man said he had ÃÂseen this happen beforeÃÂ in other homes.   Fortunately, the range was still under warranty so it was only necessary for us to pay the service charge for his visit and no more than that. 

My stove is no longer under warranty. It is now not yet 4 year fours old.  Recently while I was using the top of the stove to pan fry, the glass on the door suddenly exploded again! The oven was not even on!

incident_description:
My daughter ([REDACTED]) bought me a Hamilton Beach toaster oven for Christmas, 2013. I read the directions and used it as a toaster for morning toast, (1 piece) following directions. On about July 22nd, I awoke and fed the cats, made coffee & put a piece of [REDACTED] bread into the toaster oven, plugged it in and turned it on, as usual. incident_description:
I purchased the currently very popular Veggetti (as seen on TV).  After extracting it from packaging, I was looking it over before washing and using it when I discovered that the two metal 'handles' down the sides have edges that  have been just slightly turned inward, but those inward edges are still very easily accessed by fingers and are EXTREMELY sharp.  Very much like 4 sharply honed knives.

The packaging does warn of the sharpness of the cutting blades within the product, but something should be done about the "ergonomic comfort grip" as described by the packaging.  I'm afraid to have this in my home and I don't even have children around to be concerned about.  I can't imagine how dangerous this would be in the hands of a child.  I'm sure I'm not the only person to have discovered this and I'm just as sure there are people who must have sliced open fingers in the discovery.  Fortunately, I made the discovery before doing any damage to myself.
justification: The product has extremely sharp edges that could easily cause injury, but the user discovered the issue before any harm occurred.

Thanks,

incident_description: I was using a Pyrex baking dish in the oven. It is the second time I used this dish. The dish was at room temperature and the food was also at room temperature when placed in the dish.  The food consisted of cooked ground beef, corn tortilla strips, tomatoes, and cheese.  The oven was completely preheated to 350.  The dish was to be heated for only 10 minutes. Some time between 8 and 9 minutes, the dish shattered in the oven.  No one was injured.  The oven temperature was then tested to make sure the oven was not producing more heat than the dial said, the oven was functioning properly.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered in the oven, but no one was injured.

incident_description: I am writing to report what I consider to be a serious safety issue with Pyrex glass.  Last night, I had a Pyrex 8-cup measuring cup disintegrate into tiny shreds in the dishwasher.  This cup had never been used in the oven or stove, it had only been used to measure or hand-mix at room temperature.  It was last used on 8/18 to mix a pre-packaged salad kit.  It was stored in the refrigerator with the leftovers.  On 8/19 it was rinsed in room temperature water and placed in the top rack of the dishwasher, where it sat for the next 2 days along with other regular glass items, including fine glass wine glasses.  On 8/21, the dishwasher was run in the normal wash cycle, with both "sani-heat" and "heated-dry" options turned off, therefore, the glass was not exposed to extreme heat or thermal shock.  Later that night I opened the dishwasher, only to find hundreds of tiny pieces of glass scattered all over.  The pump section of the dishwasher had to be taken apart to clean and remove the glass shreds.  The drain pump impeller was found to be broken with a piece of glass jammed into it.  Even after carefully cleaning everything with a vacuum cleaner, I'm still finding tiny shreds of glass all over the dishwasher.  Frankly, I'm now afraid of using this machine to wash my dishes, knowing small pieces of glass, nearly pulverized, are likely to be circulating with the wash water.  No matter what the manufacturer might say, this is not normal.  I'm not a glass expert, but as a Mechanical Engineer I have studied materials and their behaviors.  Over the years I've seen glass break under various circumstances, but never something like this.  It is important to note that other fine glass items were sitting right next to this measuring cup and did not break or suffer any damage.  Something is very wrong with this glass.  I'll be happy to send the broken glass for your review and analysis.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex measuring cup disintegrating in the dishwasher, causing damage to the appliance but no injuries.

incident_description: I was having problems with my front left burner maintaining the right temperature. I called Kenmore and Sears and none of them wanted to do anything about it.  They weren't even interested in making note of the problem for further reference.

incident_description:
I have a Maytag Gemini range with two ovens and 4 burners model MGR6772BDS SERIAL NUMBER 11347286CC.
Yesterday, August 22 2014, the oven started clicking, the sound that the piezoelectric burner igniters make. No one was in the room and the oven had not been used in about 4 hours. As I a approached the kitchen, I saw orange flames coming up around the burner control knobs, followed by dense black smoke and the odor of burning plastic. I unplugged the over from the wall outlet.
Today, after having no success on the Maytag website trying to get someone to inspect and repair the oven, I searched for recalls for this model and saw the CPSC website listing for this model and serial number and the reports of unsafe upper oven and flames. I called the 800 number and got the recall part of Maytag. I had a difficult time with them since they were not aware of all the recalls after being purchased by Whirlpool, but eventually I got someone who said they would send my information to an independent service company. 
I think this oven is a serious safety hazard. Even if repaired I would not trust it again, and I'm a bit concerned about the fumes that were released in the house while I went in to unplug the unit.
My telephone number is [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death, and the recall history suggests this issue is likely to occur.

incident_description:

While researching this issue, I came across several recalls for this brand of units. I also came across a ton of this brand that have the same issues that are NOT on the recall list. They should be. Someone could be seriously injured or their house could be burned down!

incident_description: During the night on 8/19/14, our Frigidaire microwave oven turned itself on and ran for hours, getting very hot in the process. The  1.1 cu ft 1100-Watt Countertop FRIGIDAIRE FFCM1134LS Microwave was taken out of the box in April of this year, and was only used three times. When contacted, Frigidaire said they were made with defective control panels, but would not refund or replace the microwave. This happened two weeks before we planned to leave for a week away from home. It could have easily started a fire in that time.
justification: The microwave turned itself on and got very hot, which could have easily started a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My Cuisinart Compact Single Serve Coffee Maker Model SS-300 normally, after brewing a cup of coffee, automatically turns off. Two weeks ago, I made a cup of coffee and was about to leave the house when I smelled something burning. I returned to the kitchen to find the Cuisinart coffee maker smoking and when I lifted the brewer head and looked inside, it was glowing bright red. I immediately unplugged it and took it outside. If I had not returned to the kitchen and unplugged the machine, I fear that my home could have been damaged or destroyed by a disastrous fire.

I have pictures of the melted inside parts of the machine below the filter compartment and the melted filter holder that sits on top of it that I can provide.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and overheating coffee maker, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Our 2004 Thermador PD486GEBS1/01 Dual Fuel range burst into flames when it was not in use. Thankfully, it was in the middle of the day and our cleaning lady was in the living room. If she had not been there to extinguish, our house would likely have burnt down. When Thermador was contacted about the problem, they sent inspectors out to our house where it was mentioned that a faulty circuit board had cause the accident. Thermador management told us it was a "safely contained" defect and offered us a 10% discount on a newly purchased range. My family could have been killed if the range had exploded at night when we were asleep. I will never buy from Thermador again and believe their products are poorly designed and dangerous to use.
justification: The range burst into flames but was extinguished without injury, though the potential for severe harm was high.

incident_description:
The caller is filing the report on behalf of his mother in law. 

 The oven had not been used for 3-4 days prior to 7/10/14. On 7/10/14 at approximately 4:30 am the consumer was awaken by a loud noise in the kitchen. She went to the kitchen and noticed that the outside glass door of the oven had shattered. She saw glass pieces everywhere around the unit and approx. 15ft in distance from the unit. The oven was off and no sign of heat emitting from the unit. 

The consumer contacted the firm and filed a report with [REDACTED], a rep from GE. An appointment was scheduled for 7/15/14 for a technician tobe sent to her home and look at the unit at no expense to the consumer. 

On 7/15/14 a technician went to her home and inspected the unit. The technician stated that the unit was repairable but needed a part number for the outside oven glass. The consumer contacted the GE rep. at 1-800-386-1215 [REDACTED] but was not provided with a part number for the outside oven glass. Since the part number was not obtained the technician could not conduct any repairs. The technician could not give any explanation for the shattered glass. 

On 7/24/14 the consumer called [REDACTED] (GE rep.) but was not able to speak with her. The consumer spoke with another rep from GE and they advised her that the incident was still under investigation and she would be contacted on 7/25/14. 

The consumerÃÂs case number with the firm is [REDACTED].

Caller stated there have been no prior incidents.
justification: The incident was a minor incident with no injury, but it was a incident.

incident_description: Maytag electric range was turning on by itself, we awoke to a smoke filled house. We had to unplug  the range,we threw the breaker. I contacted Maytag, they made an appointment with Howie Voigt to look at the range. No service fee. A tech came to the house, knew right away what had to be replaced. He informed me that there would be NO charge at all. He returned several days later with the part installed it and left. A week and a half later I received a bill for $185.92. I contacted Howie Voigt and complained and was told the tech must have misunderstood the paper work when he told me there would be no charge. I was informed during this call the only thing covered by Maytag was the cost of labor. When I said again I was told there was not going to be any charge the person at Voigt' said I had to take up the issue with Maytag. I called Maytag and was told the problem was with Howie Voigt and it was Howie Voihts mistake. I am unsure if I knew what the cost was going to be if l would have had  the repair done or purchase a new range, but since I was told there would not be a charge the repair was made and now I have a bill for close to $200.00.

incident_description:
I have a Mr Coffee VBX23 model coffee maker.  I've had it for about 2 years.  While using it today, the unit start producing smoke.  

It had completed the brewing cycle about 5 to 10 minutes before the incident and the hot plate was on to keep the coffee warm.  I noticed that it was producing quiet popping-like sounds, and shortly later, I smelled the smoke.  Smoke was quickly coming out of the rear of the unit, where the electrical cord goes into it.  I quickly unplugged the unit, brought it outside, and hosed it down to prevent a fire.  I double checked and there were no items resting or close to the coffee making that would have been the source of the smoke.
justification: The coffee maker produced smoke but was promptly unplugged and hosed down, preventing injury or fire.

incident_description:
I bought a home in 2005 with a brand new 36" Wolf LP Range.  Model R366-Lp
When I use the oven the room fills with gas smell, and once at it's temp., if it needs to re-ignite the is a VERY large explosion, and even though the door is very heavy, it blows the door open 4 to 6 inches.

I have paid for new igniter, and gas valve, I am into this $450.00 in repairs.  Even my repairman is at a loss.  There seems to be nothing more that can be done.

I have also checked with my propane provider and they affirm that the tank is full and properly pressurized.  Also when the oven is on, sometimes the burners have difficulty lighting, or the all 6 spark as though they are trying to ignite.
justification: The incident involves explosions and gas leaks, posing a significant risk of injury, and the issue occurs frequently during oven use.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her gas range when she purchased her home around May or June 2005 but did not receive it until 2006 when she moved into the home.
She had problems with the oven from the very first used the heat escalated to temperatures much higher than what she had set them at.
She bakes her cookies at 350 degrees but with this range, each time that she bakes the oven temperatures escalate from the set temperature upward to 400 and 500 degrees and her cookies become burned.
She is reporting theses incidents as severe fire hazards.
She is asking that GE help her and replace her range at manufacturer expense or at least repair it with a lasting repair at manufacturer expense.

There have been no injuries

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven causing burned cookies, but no injuries or fire incidents have occurred.

incident_description: My wife was using the popcorn setting to pop popcorn when she noticed fire coming from the magnoter (spelling) unit at the top of the microwave. The plastic covering melted and burned a hole in the popcorn bag. We pulled the plug and put out the fire. But the microwave is ruined.
justification: The incident caused damage to the microwave but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: We started hearing noises in the blender but did not know what it was. We noticed a metal taste in our smoothies and then the whole blade unit came apart in pieces.  My husband almost got cut collecting the pieces not knowing there was two loose blades.
justification: The incident involved a blender malfunction with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was rinsing out my Bonavita Glass Carafe with warm water when it suddenly exploded with  glass shards.  The carafe was last used at 10 am that morning and it was being washed out after the dinner dishes at 7:15 PM. 

No brush or other item came into contact with the inside of the carafe.  Luckily, my face was turned away when the explosion occurred.  The carafe was the last item in the sink and it was sitting by itself with only the water inside the carafe, the sink did not contain water.
justification: The carafe exploded but no injury occurred as the person's face was turned away.

incident_description: Cooking pot was being used on the stove to cook a meal when smoke started coming from either the inside of the pot or the base of the pot.  When the pot was lifted off the stove, the base came apart falling to the floor and releasing an unknown melted metal substance on the floor.  The floor was damaged in multiple spots.
justification: The incident involved property damage (floor) but no reported injury.

incident_description: While taking a baked Item out of a toaster oven, the mitt sparked and caused my daughter to pull her arm out of the toaster oven and burn her arm on the top of the oven. The mitt also melted and caused a burn on her arm and got all over the counter and smelled up the whole house. It never caught fire, mind you, It just sparked and she got scared. The rubber material melted onto a small part of her hand and burned her and she received a burn from removing her hand quickly as to avoid potential fire. The oven was set at 250 F and the mitt Is supposed to be heat resistant up to 47SF.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the daughter's arm and hand, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Several months ago I noticed that the racks in my Kenmore Elite slide-in oven were suddenly too short. I have to adjust them very precariously to get them to stay up. They have fallen on multiple occasions, sometimes spilling food. I checked on line, and within minutes found several sites with the same complaints for this brand of oven, some resulting in burns. Many had already contacted Sears and Frigidaire (manufacturer), only to get a run-around. I, likewise, emailed Sears Member Services and was told to contact a repairman, who could come at a cost of $75, to diagnose the problem. I had read that someone else had done this and was told the walls were made of poor, non-heat-resistant metal, and that it would cost $400 to repair.
The model no. is 79046704600, serial no.
 NF63729330. It was purchased at the local Sears at the Redcliff Mall in St. George, UT. I don't remember what year--more than 5. When we make a major purchase like this, however, we would expect it to last for many years.
This is clearly a manufacturing defect. This wide-spread problem is a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involves racks falling and spilling food, with reports of burns from others, indicating a safety hazard.

incident_description:
We have a Sears Kenmore Microwave / Wall Oven Combination Model 790.4784 (Oven Model 79047849408/
SNNF83109375). The front tempered glass (Part#318261361) on the door of the oven exploded when my daughter was opening the door. She and my wife who standing next to her; were very lucky not to be injured by the flying glass.

We were going to insert a pan into the oven with food to bake, when my daughter was opening the oven door and glass exploded.
justification: The incident involved an oven door glass explosion with no injuries reported, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description: (08/11/2014) The consumer stated that the microwave came on by itself. The consumer was not able to turn it off. The unit was turned off at the breaker.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was safely turned off at the breaker, causing no injury.

incident_description:
My husband and I were upstairs in bed, and it was 11:45 p.m. We heard a loud breaking and crashing sound, followed by crackling and breaking. 

We thought someone was intruding in the house. We went downstairs and the oven door of our GE electric range, model #JB640DR5BB had spontaneously broken and pieces were as far as into the next rooms.

The product was not in use. The stove top had been used the day prior, and the oven had been used two days prior.  No injuries were sustained since we were upstairs and have no pets or children.

GE is very helpful with customer service and will be out on 08/22/2014 to repair the problem.
justification: The incident was a spontaneous breaking of the oven door, no injuries were sustained.

incident_description:
We have a Frigidaire wall oven, Model No. FGEW2745KWA, Serial No. NF00738201.  It was purchased in 2010 from Sears and made in Canada.  Yesterday, as my wife was baking, the exterior glass of the oven door shattered into the kitchen.  This is a flat piece of tempered glass which forms the outside of the oven door.  There were no injuries.

The temperature of the oven was set to 350ÃÂ° F.  The food inside was not burned which indicates that the set baking temperature was not exceeded.  There were no external blows to the glass, either shortly before the failure, or ever, that we can remember.

Fridigaire told me that there was no record of a recall of the unit associated with this issue.  In researching the problem on the internet I found a number of references to the issue with different ovens or ranges.  Some of the failures happened when the occupants were away from home.  A remark was made that the Consumer Product Safety Commission was investigating.  Hopefully this report will help your investigation.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but there were no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not widespread.

incident_description: We purchased a Figidaire model FDB520RHS2A on 11/26/2010, delivered on December 12th 2010. From the beginning this Figidaire Dishwasher has been a Faulty and Dangerous appliance. Within the first 11 months we had to report 3 service complaints in which two included a failed washer motor impeller component that when it fails, the Dishwasher becomes "stuck" in the washing cycle WITHOUT WATER BEING PRESENT and becomes OVER HEATED. You can smell something over-heating or burning inside the Dishwasher. Figidaire sent warranty repair techs to fix the unit, but AGAIN this last week (8/18/2014) the Motor component had failed AGAIN (that is THREE in less than 4 years) and the Dishwasher began a run-away over-heating because it was again stuck in the wash cycle with no water present in the machine. Had we not noticed the burning smell, this would have surely caused a FIRE!!  This model and similar ones, should be RECALLED by the Product Safety Administration! I have called Figidaire Corporate in Augusta GA and was essentially told "too bad, you should have bought an extended warranty" by a Customer Service Manager!!! I have read hundreds of Similar complaints on the Consumer Affairs website for many Figidaire models. Why is the Product Safety Administration doing nothing about this??
justification: The dishwasher's repeated overheating and potential to cause a fire poses a significant risk of injury, and the issue has recurred multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Our microwave oven started on fire the evening of July 30, 2014.  The microwave had been on about 1 to 2 minutes when we saw a flicker in the upper part of the microwave.  We turned off the microwave immediately.  There was a flame in the ceiling of the microwave, which burned a hole.  

The microwave was a GE Spacemaker over the range oven.  Model JVM 1540 DM5 WW and was slightly over a year old as it was installed on July 13, 2013.  

GE sent a technician to diagnose the problem.  The technician said the stirrer blade above the ceiling of the microwave must have come loose and started arcing, causing the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but was promptly turned off with no reported injuries, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it was caused by a specific mechanical failure (stirrer blade coming loose).

incident_description:
In December 2011, I purchased a Cuisinart Toaster Oven, model # TOB-40, through Amazon.  In July of 2014 I noticed the lower heating element had warped upwards and the insulation had split about 1 1/4 inches, exposing the element.  In seeking product info on Amazon, I noticed about 25 user complaints documenting the same problem that I experienced.  Some of the users noted they had received an electrical shock or had seen sparking, in addition to the obvious fire hazard.  Personally, I experienced sparking.  Here is a link to that web page:
