I inquired whether they had modified or corrected this model to address the defect and they had not.  I declined their offer to replace the unit with the same model #TOB-40.
justification: The incident involved sparking and a fire hazard, but no injury was reported. Multiple user complaints indicate a recurring issue.

incident_description: Yesterday I bought two coffee mugs that say 222 Fifth PTS International on the bottom.  They say dishwasher and microwave safe.  The first time I used them to make tea the complete bottom came out of both mugs, spilling boiling water all over!  I would be happy to provide photos of the mugs.
justification: The incident involved boiling water spilling due to defective mugs, which could cause injury.

incident_description: In April of this year I purchased a new blender through Amazon.com.  The actual seller is STL Pro, Inc.  The blender cost $124.99+shipping.  Yesterday, 8/18/14, as I was using it to blend some almond milk, oats and blueberries, it began to burn.  I pulled the plug, but I have severely damaged lungs from my military service and was driven out of the house by the smoke.  I went to Amazon.com and looked at the user comments for this particular blender.  There are 85 comments of which 3 mention that the unit started to burn when they used it.  I contacted Amazon who referred me to STL Pro.  STL Pro wrote that because the 30 day return policy had expired I had no recourse.  I assume they will continue to sell this product which is clearly defective and dangerous.
justification: The incident caused severe lung irritation due to smoke inhalation, indicating an injury, and similar incidents have been reported by other users.

incident_description: I opened the door on my Sears Kenmore Elite refrigerator ( model number795.77573600) and found the lights had been burning when the door was closed. This caused the light cover to melt and fall off. I was lucky it had only been a few hours and I was able to unscrew the bulbs and stop the plastic from melting and save the food. This is a fire hazard. If I had been out of town it could have set my home on fire. I have called Sears and they were no help. This needs to be under a recall. Please warn others of the fire risk before someone is killed because of this product.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury or death, but potential for significant damage if unattended.

incident_description: On August 18 2014 at approx 945 pm a strong burning electrical smell and smoke was coming from the fridge. upon further investigation sparks were coming from the rear. It was discovered that the the compressor relay was burnt up. If noone had been home the house would have caught on fire.
justification: The incident caused smoke and sparks, but no injury was reported. The severity level is 2 because it was an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the oven rack is faulty, it collapses while using it.  This poses a burn hazard to the user as well as other household occupants who maybe standing nearby, or can cause a house fire.  This has been on going for approximately 2 months.  



7/25 The retailer was contacted and a service technician was sent out 7/30/14, she was advised that the cavity of the oven wall has expanded which causes the racks to fall.  He stated that repairing this would not guarantee that the incident would not occur again.  He also advised her that this is due the material that made the interior of the oven.



Caller feels that the oven is a safety hazard and should be reported
justification: The incident involves a faulty oven rack that poses a burn hazard, but there is no injury reported.

incident_description:
I have a Sears Kenmore Elite Electric Range Model 790.9801 that I purchased in 2009. Since that time the lower oven racks have been getting looser and looser and now are at the point that whenever anything is placed on the racks and they are moved slightly the rack falls. On Aug 3, 2014 I was cooking a roast in the oven and went to take the the roast out when the rack fell causing burns on my hand.
I have discussed this problem with Sears, 8 different people and the manufacture, Frigidire, with no help except to have a Sears Repair person come to my home on Aug 14th, charge me $79 to tell me the oven cavity is warped therefor making the racks fall and that a replacement oven cavity would cost me $437.76.
I have found on the internet and CPSC website that other people have experienced this same problem with this model range.
justification: The incident resulted in burns, indicating an injury (severity 3), and similar issues have been reported by others, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: My LG Oven/Range Model# LRE30451SW Oven will not turn off. I have to turn off the circuit breaker to turn the oven off. This model is already on a recall list for the top burners not turning off which is also happening with my oven. LG will fix this problem but not the oven because it is not on a recall list. Both problems are in the control panel and are heat related and should both be on a recall list before someones house burns down if that hasn't already happened.
justification: The oven's inability to turn off poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
My LG Refrigerator - model # LFX25960ST overheated when the interior light stayed on continuously.
All food in the refrigerator was spoiled and the interior temperature was well above room temperature, measured with a passive infrared thermometer at 120 degrees farenheit.

The plastic around the light assembly inside the refrigerator is melted beyond repair and the sockets containing two bulbs are discolored from overheating.  I removed the light assembly and tested the sockets which feed electricity to the bulbs.  Both sockets are 'hot' electrically speaking even when the door switch is pushed in.  I cannot reconnect the light assembly safely.

I researched the problem online and found that many other consumers reported the same issue.

What can be done to force LG company to repair this issue or require a recall on this obvious safety issue ??
justification: The incident caused property damage and food spoilage but no injury or death, and similar issues have been reported by other consumers.

incident_description:
Frigidaire oven model FEF352AUE serial VG32202168, approximately ten years old.  Preheating oven for the evening meal, when observed only about one inch of oven lower element was glowing and sparking.  Glowing section started about three inches from the oven wall.  The glowing section started slowing moving along the element with the appearance of a metal fire.  A box and one half of baking soda covering the entire element failed to put out the fire (progress 3" to 6.5").  Quantity two, 25 ABC fire extinguishers burying the element in two to three inches of material failed to put out the fire (progress 6.5" to 11").  Slowly pouring water on the element dimmed the glow and caused some sparks (progress 11" to 18"), but the fire immediately resumed when water flow stopped.  Placing a water soaked rag on the glowing section and adding water finally cooled and extinguished the fire.  Oven removed from the residence by the first responders.

Same oven had been used earlier in the afternoon at low temperature for bread rising and at 325 degrees for baking bread with no issues identified.
justification: The incident involved a significant fire in the oven that required multiple attempts to extinguish, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Microwave turntable would stop, slow down, restart then unit would power up, then down, arc and spark.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned with arcing and sparking, posing a potential hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that about 2 years ago, he put the oven on self-clean mode. The consumer stated that when the clean mode was complete, the door was locked and would not open. The consumer waited until the next day but the door still did not unlock.

The consumer contacted the retailer and they sent out a technician. The technician was able to use a coat hanger to unlock the latch and open the door. The technician informed the consumer that he had seen this issue with other similar models.

Consumer paid $180 for the technician to come out. The consumer stopped using self-clean mode after that.

The consumer stated that after 8-9 minutes, he heard a beeping sound. The consumer looked at the display and noticed that the oven went into cleaning mode from bake mode. 

The consumer tried to turn off the oven and open the door but the door was locked. The consumer pulled the door with force and opened the door. The consumer stated that the pizza caught on fire and filled the kitchen with smoke. The consumer took the pizza out with tongs and put it in the sink. 

There are no recalls on this unit.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused a fire but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The glass on the door of the upper wall oven exploded.
justification: The glass exploding is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
LG Bottom Freezer Refrigerator Model # LFC25760TT

Interior ceiling lights fail to turn off, which led to melting and browning of the light bulb sockets,a burning smell, a warm refrigerator, and blistering of the ceiling above the bulbs.   The digital control unit is now held up with duct tape as the brackets melted.  We removed the bulbs, leaving our refrigerator in the dark.  This is the third, and most serious incident over the past year.
justification: The incident caused property damage and a burning smell but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I bought a new Whirlpool built-in electric microwave oven combination wall oven two weeks ago. The model  is WOC54EC7AB01 and the serial# is D43020052.  When I turned the lower oven on 450 to cook a potato, the whole unit became very hot.  The bottom of the microwave was hot to touch without being used.  The metal strip on the side of the oven where it is screwed into the wooden frame was so hot that it would burn your hand.  Even the buttons on the controls at the top of the unit were hot.
When I called Whirlpool, they said they could send a repair person out or I could call the people who sold it to me.  They didn't seem to be concerned that it could have burned down my house.  I certainly wasn't going to allow a repair on a two week old unit.  I went back to the store and they are replacing the unit.  I have been told Whirlpool makes a very good product but I'm not sure.  I will give the new unit a try but if it gets hot outside of the oven, I'll just get my  money back.  I thought some one should know about this problem.  If there have been others reported, then it's a bigger problem than just one oven not built correctly.
justification: The incident was a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We had our Thermador Double Oven Model MED272JS  installed April 2014. August 15,2014 we turned on the self cleaning mode for the upper oven for the first time and about 20 minutes into the 1-1/2 cycle heard a loud pop and noticed the interior glass shattered.
justification: The incident involved a loud pop and shattered glass during oven self-cleaning, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Emerson Microwave MWG9115SL suffix G. Microwave turned itself on and ran unexpectedly. Here's what happened. First I microwaved a cup of water for 1 minute. The beep sounded to indicate the cycle was complete and I opened the door, took out the cup, and closed the door. About 5 seconds later I hear the microwave running again. The motor was running, the light was on, and the table was turning. The display showed "0:00" the entire time this happened. I summoned my husband. He first yanked open the door which stopped it from running, and then he unplugged it. We have not plugged it back in since, and intend to discard the microwave.

Other details - We've owned the microwave about 2 years old and it is cleaned regularly. It was used 3 or 4 times a day on average to microwave food and drinks, and the heating element feature was used once every couple of months.

The bottom of the inner chamber is rusted where the enamel has been worn away from the turntable. In the past we also have periodic arcing incidents and occasions where the microwave shuts down mid-cycle and cannot be used again for 15 minutes (apparently after cooling down). Serial # 204023436MM April 2012
justification: The microwave turned on unexpectedly without user input, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I have an Electrolux Icon gas range and I have now had multiple incidents of hot boiling pots tipping forward toward my body and nearly dumping over onto the floor while standing in front of the stove. The issue lies in the construction of the metal grates on the stovetop/range. There are gaps on the front of the grates where the design of the metal grates is not contiguously rectilinear, which provides dead air space below the pot, which in turn creates a propensity for a pot to tip forward and onto the user. This creates an extremely dangerous situation for the user of the range.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with boiling pots tipping toward the user, posing a high risk of injury, and it has occurred multiple times.

incident_description:
(07/2014) The consumer stated that she placed a pan of chicken on the middle rack.  Immediately,  the rack fell down to the bottom. This happens each time something that weighs at least two pounds is placed on the rack. It only happens with the middle rack.

The consumer stated that she saw on the internet where this has happened to others.


(07/30/2014) The consumer called Sears Customer Service 1-8002954809. She spoke with [REDACTED] and explained the issue. The consumer was offered a 15% discount on another range since her unit was out of warranty. The consumer refused the offer. The consumer was also given a case #[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a rack falling when weight is applied, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Capresso Electric Water Kettle 259.03

The water kettle was brought to a boil and the water was poured out but the automatic off switch did not engage and the heating element was left on. No injury occurred but could have under different circumstances.
justification: The incident involved a failure of the automatic off switch, but no injury occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer had a measuring cup filled with water that she placed in the microwave and set it for 2 and a half minutes. After about 1 and a half minute, she took the cup out of the microwave. She then shut the microwave door and pressed the stop/off button. 

A few seconds later she heard a pop noise come from the microwave. When she turned around she saw flames coming from the microwave. She states the flames were coming from the top of the microwave on the inside. She opened the door and put out the fire with a towel. She states the plastic had melted from the top of the microwave and created a hole. 

The consumer states she did not use the microwave for anything prior to using it to heat up water.

The consumer has not had any prior incidents.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as the consumer had no prior incidents and the event was isolated.

incident_description:
(07/6/2014) The consumer stated that she was using the blender. The consumer forgot to unplug the unit and was rinsing it. The consumer touch the power button and the blade severed the index finger on her left hand.

The consumer went to the MD Now Clinic in [REDACTED] She was seem by Dr. [REDACTED]. She was given seven stitches in her finger.

(07/15/2014) The consumer contacted the company. She spoke with [REDACTED] She advised him of the incident. She was advised that that the incident would be escalated to the Claims Department.

(07/24/2014) The consumer received a letter from the company dated 7/16. The consumer was advised that the incident was her fault and that there was nothing that the company could do.


The consumer thinks the power button does not have enough safety measures.

The consumer would like for the product to be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring medical attention (seven stitches), but no death occurred.

incident_description: This is our second GE microwave within one and a half years that has had a defect in the same spot.  The first microwave caught fire at the top where the fan rotates.  The GE Service Rep told us that the fan was not rotating, was beyond repair, and replaced the microwave with the same model.  Today, August 14, 2014, the microwave caught on fire in the same place, but this time the flames were much bigger and engulfed the inside.  We were able to extinguish the flames, and the top fan area is completely black and charred.   The model number of these two microwaves is JVM1540DM5BB.  The serial number of our current microwave is 200288.  I will be notifying GE of this problem on August 15th.  Thank you for your time.
justification: The microwave caught fire twice, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Oven glass shattered. Was not in use and no one was home.
justification: Oven glass shattered but no one was present, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: Carbon Monoxide alarm went off on 7/20/14 as a result of the range giving off carbon monoxide.  We immediately called the fire department, opened all doors and windows, and removed ourselves from the home.  American Range was purchased from Appliance World.  Appliance World were contacted but they said they couldn't do anything.  Appliance World told us to contact American Range's Eastern marketing.  They too were contacted and told us that they couldn't do anything and to contact headquarters.  [REDACTED] was the person spoken to at American Range.  She did not do anything about the carbon monoxide problem but sent a technician for another problem (the oven door was not on appropriately).  Technician came on 7/25/14 and did mention that there is a manufacturer defect that is causing the massive amounts of carbon monoxide.
justification: The carbon monoxide alarm triggered a response, but no injury or death was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the confirmed manufacturer defect and repeated incidents.

incident_description:
Aug 12 evening. Cooking dinner. Turned off stovetop, but later smelled something burning. Saw unit was still on and would not turnoff. Had to flip circuit breaker.

Aug 13 morning. Flipped circuit breaker. Unit came on spontaneously and would not turn off.
Flipped circuit breaker to turn off.

Aug 13 lunch.
Flipped circuit breaker.
Unit did NOT come on. It did turn on when the button was pressed and turned off. Seems normal for the time being.
justification: The incident was a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a fridgidaire refrigerator in Nov. 2012.  Had a repair person come out several months later because my food in the freezer was all going bad and I had ice build up inside.  The repair person came out and said the gasket needs to stretch out and it takes time.  It has now been a year and a half, in the beginning it was not so bad, even got better for a while.  Now all my frozen food is going bad and my ice sticks together because things are melting.  Fridgidaire will not send me a replacement part for free without me paying for there service providers time.  I feel that they need to send the replacement part free of charge since the gasket has been bad since I bought the unit.  I am not even asking that they come out and replace it for free. I am only asking for the part to be shipped to my house.  I should have the right to hire my own repair person to install it.  Especially since there repair company gave me a bologna excuse.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator causing food spoilage but no injury or death.

incident_description: Two week old GE gas range.  Preheated oven to 400 degrees to bake a pie.  Heard a loud noise and the sound of glass breaking.  Quickly turned oven off.  When all the noise and sound of breaking glass stopped, I opened the oven door to find that the inside glass on the door had exploded in hundreds of little pieces all inside the oven.  It is GE model #JGB695SEFSS.  Not something you expect to happen in a brand new appliance.
justification: The incident involved property damage (broken glass) but no injury or death.

incident_description: My over the range GE microwave oven began starting on its own and would not shut off until I shut off the breaker switch. It was very frightening and it appears this would cause a fire. I tried using the microwave again but after an hour or so it started on its own again.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning and starting on its own poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was making scrambled eggs in a Cusinart 8" teflon fry pan when the fry pan exploded sending a metal cap across the kitchen and throwing pieces of scrambled eggs all over the kitchen.  The handle of the frypan is held on with two rivets and a metal cap covers the rivets.  The cap some how must have gotten moisture underneath it and it got super heated and blow the cap off just missing my face.  I suffered no  injury, but it could have been a disaster, such as the loss of an eye or even worse.
justification: The incident involved an exploding fry pan with no injury, but potential for severe harm, indicating a moderate likelihood given the described mechanism.

incident_description:
smelled burning and heard noises, my coffee pot smoked, fire glow from under heating plate coffee was boiling.
We had it for awhile and never used it, kept it as a spare, very disappointed, It could of caught myhouse on fire
justification: The coffee pot smoked and showed signs of potential fire, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The product is Kirkland Signature brand Himalayan Pink Salt from Costco in a disposable, adjustable grinder (368.5g container). It was purchased in June or July 2014.  Soon after we started using it, cracks began to form in the plastic ring (the part you turn to grind and dispense the salt).  It still worked so we continued using it.  At some point a plastic disc also fell out of the top, but it still worked so we kept using it.
On the evening of 12 August 2014, I was dispensing salt when one of the cracked edges cut my left hand at the base of my index finger.
These are large containers that last for months when used by a typical family.  In the past, we have purchased the sea salt and black pepper grinders from Costco in the same containers, and used them completely up without ever seeing any cracks.  This Himalayan pink salt container developed cracks immediately.  We also just bought another black pepper grinder from Costco in late July and it already is starting to develop small cracks as well.  It makes me wonder if they recently changed the design (thickness or material) of the top of these grinders.  We will be returning both of these to Costco for a refund.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut injury from a cracked plastic grinder, and similar cracks have been observed in other recently purchased grinders, indicating a possible design issue.

incident_description: Fire and smoke out of top of stove and exploding noise
justification: Fire and smoke indicate a clear incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
approximately 20 min. after starting Whirlpool dishwasher the control panel started to burn, smoke and sickening odor. I found it burning probably within a few minutes, the working smoke detectors had not yet gone off.
There was no damage or burning inside the dishwasher itself, just the control panel.
Because it was the control panel it would not turn off, door had to be left open until electricity could be turned off and wiring to dishwasher cut-it was a built-in hardwired dishwasher.
No injuries, just nausea from the odor, house aired out.

Whirlpool model GU1200
Ser # M1624020

approx 12 years old.
justification: The incident involved a burning control panel with smoke and odor, but no injuries or damage beyond the appliance itself.

incident_description:
My Mr. Coffee coffee maker overheated to a degree that could have caused burns or a fire. I purchased the coffee maker only a few months ago. I was brewing coffee as normal, and the unit became so hot by the buttons and clock that I would have burned myself touching it if I hadn't put on oven mitts. It also didn't turn off correctly after the normal two hour cut-off. If I had not been home to unplug it, I believe it would have started a fire. I am very careful to follow the instructions carefully, and I don't overfill the water tank or coffee filter. 
The model number is BVMC-SJX33GT. The time code is G070. The purchase location code is DG. 
I purchased the model about April 12th or so at Wal-Mart. 

Please look into this lot of coffee makers so that other people don't suffer burns or fires. 
Sincerely, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The coffee maker overheated to a dangerous level, posing a burn and fire risk, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
The product is a double over from Whirlpool, model #1BD650PXS00, s/n D22949575, sold through IKEA.

After a year's use, the product overheated during a self-clean cycle and set off the smoke detector just past midnight and would not shut off. Two service calls have not repaired the product, as both motherboards and transformers melted. The service rep informed us that IKEA is aware of the problem and continues to sell the product.
justification: The product overheated and caused a smoke detector to go off, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
On my 04/04/2013 I purchased a Frigedaire Refrigerator Model #FFHS2611LB7, Serial #4A30811744 from Lowe's. Yesterday 08/10/204, that refrigerator without any warning caught fire. Fortunately being Sunday both my son and my husband were home. While eating breakfast I heard an odd crackling noise, fearing I had left a pan on the stove I went in to the kitchen. Immediately the kitchen was filling with smoke and there was a strong odor. I yelled which brought my son and husband into the room where they immediately identified the source of the smoke as being from the back of the refrigerator. As they moved it out from the wall I saw the flames and became very concerned as they then worked to unplug it. 
I contacted the Extended Protection Plan number and provided the necessary information, I was given a date of August 13, 2014 for a repair persons visit. This morning I received a call telling me my appointment had not been scheduled and I needed to call Frigedaire for any service or warranty requests. Upon calling Frigedaire I was told they would not grant any warranty or service requests because I had purchased my extended protection plan from an outside source. Now I am on the phone with the original number I called once again trying to request service. I am grateful that my mom who is 91 and bedridden was not the only other occupant home with me yesterday morning.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, posing a significant risk of injury or death, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Kenmore model 790.47859401 oven. The outer glass has exploded three times in past three month. The most recent occurrence was 8 August 2014.  First occurrence happened on 17 June 2014 as oven door was being opened to remove food which was being cooked.  Second occurrence was 25 July 2014 as oven door was being opened. Third occurrence was 8 August 2014 as door with replacement glass was being reinstalled.  Unacceptable!
justification: The outer glass exploding is an incident that has occurred multiple times, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite 400 watt 5 quart Red Stand Mixer
Product faultiness description
Serial #100.8920890A / 120Va.c 60Hz
Made in China
8/9/14

To Whom it May Concern;

I was given a Kenmore Elite 400, 5 quart Red Stand Mixer as a gift from my then boyfriend in the Christmas of 2010. I haven't used it since 2012, the last time I video taped it spinning out of control. 

This mixer will suddenly speed up in the middle of mixing something on slow speed. I would be mixing say, some cake batter on #2, it immediately would speed up to #9 in half a second. Very quickly! It would fling batter or flour everywhere. My son would be baking with me and he got really got scared of it. I would stop it immediately of course. It scared me too! The mixer is pretty heavy duty and something really serious couldÃÂve happened, fingers hurt, parts couldÃÂve come undone, who knows. No injuries have occured. I tried to use a few times after but it would speed up even more frequently. This mixer is really dangerous and unpredictable. I do not recommend buying this product and I hope there is a recall on it.

Thank you, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The mixer's unpredictable speeding up caused fear and potential danger, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: The dishwasher was running and I noticed an unusual smell in the kitchen, I turned around and saw smoke pouring out of the dishwasher.  I quickly determined the dishwasher was on fire, turned the dishwasher off, got the fire extinguisher and my husband then went to the basement to turn the circuit breaker off.  The fire extinguished itself.  We pulled the front panel off of the dishwasher to find the inside charred and that the circuit board had caught fire (I have photos).  We are grateful that we were home and that there were no injuries and no further damage to property, this could have had a very different ending.   I noticed that there was a recall for GE Dishwashers manufactured during the same time frame as ours and for the same problem, but I did not see our model # on the list.  The dishwasher is a GE Profile, model #GLD6860N00SS, s/n ZL764463B.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher fire with no injuries or further property damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) due to the recall notice for similar models.

incident_description:
My few months old programmable coffee maker somehow became defective and defaulted to the ON position with the heating element being on. Tried to turn it off, but stayed in the ON position. Tried to unplug and plug it back to see if it cleared, yet still stayed in ON position.

This seems to be a serious safety issue, as the defect caused the coffee maker to default to the ON position. Luckily we were home and noticed this, but I can only imagine the results if we were out for a prolonged period and the coffee maker sat on counter top getting hotter and hotter.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned but no injury occurred, though there is a potential for fire or injury if left unattended.

incident_description:
I purchased a PROSMART slicer at a Von's market on 7/28/14 after seeing a demonstration of the product. The person demonstrating it said that it was approved by the "culinary institute for the blind" for safety!

I own another mandolin/slicer from a different manufacturer and have never had a problem, but when I brought this home and tried it out, I then rinsed it off and sliced my finger, at which point I realized it has NO SAFETY setting, meaning the blade is always exposed on all settings and cannot be put in a neutral position. I found this very disturbing and it is clearly a lack of a safe setting i for this  very sharp blade.  I was not certain how a company could produce a product that was so blatantly dangerous even when not in use.

I tried looking up the manufacturer and the information contains only an address, no phone number or email! (there is an email for returning "broken"or defective equipment at: www.twintowerstrading.com
this is a dangerous product!
justification: The severity of this incident is 3, which means an injury occurred, the occurrence_likelihood is 4 because of the lack of safety settings.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Dishwasher Model # 665.17034400. Yesterday, 8/6/2014, it caught fire. Apparently, there was some sort of overload in the controller. My wife smelled something burning before seeing any smoke. When she could not identify the source, she and my daughter got out of our house and called the fire department. By the time they arrived, smoke was coming out of the upper right portion of the dishwasher door, leaving a sooty residue. (I have pictures if it would help.) No one hurt, no serious damage, save the dishwasher itself.

The dishwasher came with the house, which we purchased in 2006. I could not determine a manufacture date. It gets heavy use, and I had replaced the main motor myself about 2 years ago. 

I am concerned that the controller could overheat so badly without tripping the circuit breaker or some other safety mechanism. I wanted to report the incident in case there have been other problems. 

I am also reporting the incident to Kenmore.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but no one was injured, and the damage was limited to the appliance itself.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore electric range, model # 790.96113409, serial # VF64615102. The front left burner was being used at a medium heat setting, but the burner went to high. The element was constantly on, and even when we turned it off, it remained on! I had to turn off the circuit breaker to turn it off. All other burners work properly, so we just don't use that burner any more. Today, I saw that there was a recall in 2009 on other Kenmore/Frigidaire ovens, but our unit is not part of the recall. Since our oven is having the same problem, I think our unit should be included also.

This same oven also had a code F10 (run away temp) last week. We were baking food at 350, but the broiler (top) element came on at some point and the unit shut down and the F10 error code appeared. This oven is a dangerous fire hazard!
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: KitchenAid Dishwasher control panel caught on FIRE. Model KUDI01ILBL2. Serial # FP3514559
justification: The dishwasher control panel caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
We bought KITCHEN AID mircrowavehood combination Model # KHMC1857BSS  SR# TR33216844 ON9/24/2013 from LOWE'S stores Location ID# 1743 under Invoice # [REDACTED].
We also bought Kitchen AID GAS COOK TOP Model# KFGS306VSS03 SR# D30901049 from the same store under the same invoice particulars.

KA OTR MICRO KHMC1857BSS:
Microwavehood combination equipment door handle and front control panel gets extreme hot after usage of 30 to 35 min with  convection or microwave function  that door cannot be opened with bare hands.
Microwave feature of the equipment cannot be used immediately after completion of baking or roasting. If someone tries to use microwave inadvertently immediately after the completion of bake or roast cycle that overheat results into injury.
Microwave fan creates noise level from 110 to 90 dB up to 20 to 30 minutes immediately after the completion of any automated baking cycle.
As per the manual and specs provided by the manufacturer one can use Aluminum foil to bake the food.  However it starts sparking while using the aluminum foil. It is very scary to use the equipment as oven. It comes with the baking rack as a part of original equipment but cannot use in the baking cycle.
 

KA KFGS306VSS03:
Gas cook top control Knobs gets so hot after 30 to 60 minutes of cooking that knobs cannot be shut off with bare hands. 

One of our family members got burn injury on RTE hand while operating Microwave hood combination equipment.

We have senior citizen (Age80+) and a child (Age9 Months+) and other members of family with age group of 20 to 55 years.
Our major concern is with the injury due to excessive heating and Nosie level which may impair hearing over a period of time.
justification: A family member suffered a burn injury from the microwave, and there is a clear risk of further injuries due to excessive heating and noise levels.

incident_description: Almost three years ago my friend bought me a crock pot from Walmart on Black Friday. Ive used it about 10 times since ive had it and almost always cook food at a low setting. Well I haven't used it in about 2 or 3 months. I live in Phoenix and usually made soup in it,  and since the last time its been washed, sitting on my counter near the sink (for a lack of space) with the lid sitting on top, upright with the cord laying inside. This evening for no apparent reason it suddenly cracked into a thousand pieces but stayed put together.  Luckily there was no food in it and no one was near by. After looking online and asking a few friends I guess this does occasionally happen.  Ive never, in my 28 years of living, seen or heard any of my mother's crock pots do this. Im assuming it's the brand.
justification: The crock pot cracked but no one was nearby and there was no food in it, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: Burned my hand on underneath of oven door when I opened the sliding drawer underneath and stuck my hand inside to get a pan. Extremely hot to touch on outside of oven door when oven is in use. This is only just on the bottom of the oven door accessed by opening the drawer underneath.
justification: The incident describes a burn injury from touching the hot oven door, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting her dishwasher purchased August 16, 2008 from an appliance company in Florida.
The caller had no problems with this dishwasher until June 28th, 2014 when he was preparing for bed while the dishwasher was running.
He and his wife smelled smoke, returned to the kitchen, and realized that the dishwasher was extremely hot and had heated everything around it.
The counter tops and cabinets were too hot to be able to touch.
The caller opened the door to stop the dishwasher then immediately noticed a strong smell of melted plastic.
After a few moments he could see that the rack that normally holds the flat-ware was melted, coffee cups had melted to a much smaller size and his flat-ware was lying on the bottom of the unit due to falling through the plastic unit when it melted.

There are no injuries to be reported

This unit is not on recall

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them

Close Window
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (melted dishwasher components and surrounding areas) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE above the range microwave for my son at Best Buy in September of 2013 and gave it to him for Christmas.  A couple weeks ago the top portion (fan area) caught on fire.  

Best Buy sent it in for repair and it was returned "Operator Error".  They would not repair or replace.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a fire hazard, which is a serious incident.

incident_description: I have a General Electric Microwave oven.   Model: JVM1540SP1SS, Serial No:DT920450B.  When it is plug in, it will automatically turn on and "heat" for at least one minute.  There is no one near the oven and it will start by itself.  I have contacted the manufacturer and they are trying to tell me based on visual inspection only that the problem is in the keypad.  Although that may be correct, I don't know what it randomly started to occur after four years of service.
justification: The microwave turns on by itself, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Bought a Cuisinart pod type coffee maker a few weeks ago.  One morning, July 21, 2014, I had used it, making three cups of coffee.  Then it shut off automatically, as it was supposed to.  About an hour later I happened to be in the kitchen, heard a noise and looked over to see the unit steaming and smoking.  The heating element at the top, under the water reservoir was bright orange and red.

I removed the unit outdoors, so keep the smoke alarm from activating.  I phoned the company, which said they would send me a replacement unit, but that they would not pay for return shipping of the defective unit.  I will not return the unit at my cost, since I did not manufacture and sell a defective product.

I seems very irresponsible that the company would not want the unit back to examine, and perhaps help avoid fires at future customers' residences.

The model # is SS-300.  Serial #31200 (or 31206 - difficult to read on the unit).
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing it to steam and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have never been treated as poorly by a company in my life. We purchased a stove on 7/2 and as soon as we got it home it had a hot surface light on when the cooktop was not being used. I called immediately to tell them of the problem and was told we would have to bring the oven back to them to be fixed. I requested a refund because we had just purchased it and it was not in working order and they refused. I was told as long as the cooktop worked the light would eventually burn out (It did not) or I could bring it back to be fixed but a refund was not an option. 3 weeks later after only using the stove a couple of times because we were on vacation we were baking dinner and the stove would not shut off. It kept getting hotter and hotter to the point it was about to catch on fire, my husband had to pull out a VERY hot stove to unplug it. We sent an email with not response on 7/26, on 7/28 we called and again said at this point we felt this was not a safe item and wanted a refund. We were told [REDACTED] would have to call us only he could authorize. He never called so I called again and he refused. He said to bring it in for repair. He became so rude he hung up on me once, I called back and he kept talking over me and would not even let me speak. He raised his voice and was the most rude business person I have ever dealt with. When I informed him I would file a complaint with the BBB and Attorney General as well as use social media to let everyone know how I was treated he responded he didn't care that there was nothing I could do. He charged us $275 for a used stove and I found one NEW for $299. My husband took the stove back on 7/28 at 10:45am and we have pictures of them unloading the oven. I again asked for a refund and was told no he would not that he didnt care I felt unsafe and it was only a couple weeks old. I received a call a couple hours later that said the stove is now working fine and they wont refund me the money. We are now without the stove and without our refund. They literally have now stolen our money. We are very scared at the quality of this oven because of the fact it was about to catch on fire and there are other consumer reviews of the same thing happening.

To Whom It May Concern,

In reviewing your online information undar "What is a Report?"  I consent to your agency publiciling this report in your data base and you are encouraged to provide my name and this report to the manufacturer of the  Frigidaire Freezer. I have photos of the freezer area which I am writing about, photos of my finger in its current state, and medical reports from a hand surgeon and orthopedic surgeon, who performed my hand surgery.

I currently have a product I feel is unsafe and in fact dangerous to any and all who own this  product. The Product is a Frigidaire Upright Freezer, Model#FKFH21F7HWB, and the Serial# is WB11141913. The incident took place almost two years ago and is summarized below.

Upon returning from our Italian vacation on 8/29/12 we discovered we had lost power during a storm Including the GFI outlet controlling our upright freezer. All the food was spoiled. The next day, 8/30 I began the process of cleaning the freezer. I reviewed the Frigidaire User & Care Manual prior to beginning, put on a pair of rubber gloves and proceeded to clean the freezer. Once done, for whatever reason I removed the gloves and, using paper towels did one last "dry down" of the inside, and that's when I cut my finger on an "L" shaped plastic lip that sets on the bottom shelf of the freezer immediately in front of the drain plug. I cut the right index finger and in reading the doctor's description of the initial exam, obtained "a transverse laceration right around the level of the DIP joint crease of his right index finger". In effect I severed the nerve and the tendon in my right index finger, which required surgery. I have since showed this lip on this freezer to the 
manager at [REDACTED] and the Appliance Department Manager at [REDACTED] in Myrtle Beach and they, upon touching the lip felt the sharp edge.

My feeling this freezer is improperly designed, and in reviewing the Use and Care Manual nowhere does it show this "L" shaped bracket or discuss the danger associated with cleaning the freezer. I feel fortunate I've only lost partial use of my right index finger. Should I have had to reach into the back of this freezer for any reason I would have had to reach across the "L" shaped lip with my wrist I believe I could have severed blood vessels and my accident could have been significantly  
worse.

BELOW IS A COPY OF A LETTER SENT TO DUNKIN DONUTS 1/8/14:

Dunkin' Donuts
Consumer Care
130 Royall Street
Canton, MA 02021

RE:	Dunkaccino Machine Accident
Store:  WilcoHess, #4001
	3663 Roy Messer Hwy, 37890
Date:	12/31/13 


Dear Sir/ Madam:

I am writing regarding your Dunkaccino machine at the WilcoHess location.  
We visited this store (#4001) on 12/31/13 @ 3:15PM.  This is a self-service Dunkin Donuts location.  
My son attempted to get a Dunkaccino.  The instructions on the machine stated that you should push the button to release the liquid but stop when the cup was half way full.  He went just past that halfway point when filling his cup before he released the fill button.  When the cup began to overflow onto the counter, he panicked, grabbing the cup from the machine and scalding his hand.  The salesperson quickly came out to check on us & cleaned up the spill.  My son immediately ran his hand under cold water, took Tylenol for the pain & inflammation, & was given an ice pack by the store manager for the drive home.  His entire hand up to mid forearm was pink & edematous.  Fortunately, he did not blister.  He had discomfort for the remainder of the day & a few days later had peeling of the skin as if he had a sunburn.

I felt it necessary to contact you to ensure this does not happen to anyone else.  The store employee stated that this has happened before, indicating that this is not an isolated incident.  

Safer practices should be put into place.  It would make sense if the machine had a button the customer could press based on the cup size.  The cup would be placed onto the machine, a button pressed for size, and no further interactions would be required by the consumer until the machine is finished.  No gray areas for someone to have to look into the cup for a halfway point or misjudge the level to stop the machine before it overflows.  
 
There also seems to be no safety switch to prevent a young child from quickly pressing the button without even having the intent of getting a beverage.

I urge you to look into this hazardous issue.  I would appreciate a response with a plan on what will be done to keep this from reoccurring.  I look forward to hearing from you.
justification: The incident resulted in a scalding injury with discomfort and peeling skin, but no blisters or long-term harm.

On July 30, 2014 the left front burner would not turn off and I was forced to turn off the breaker.  This appears to be a fire hazard and I would like to report this in the event there are others who are experiencing the same thing.   Had I not been vigilant about staying in the kitchen while cooking anything, there would definately been a fire.
justification: The incident involved multiple malfunctions without injury, but with potential for fire hazard, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I thought it was odd when I walked out this morning in the pitch black.  It appeared that the center strip between the fridge french door was softly glowing.  I pushed on both of the doors and they were indeed closed.  Also, it has a door open alarm that beeps after 30 seconds but that never went off.
I opened the fridge and noticed a hot plastic smell and the top inside of the fridge was hot.  The housing around the fridge light was half-melted and distorted.
I unplugged the fridge.  The housing was too hot to touch so I left the doors open to evacuate the heat.
The freezer was still cold and the bottom of the fridge was still cool, just the top was hot.
I suspected the light was the problem since it was all that appeared damaged, so I removed the warped plastic lens and housing and unplugged the light wires.  The area above the light had blistered, despite having a metal heat reflector between it and the light.  The light bulbs appear to still have filament but I can't remember if they lit when I opened the fridge.  I think they did.  Anyway, the bulb receptacles are burnt looking at the top sides of each.
I have not touched the bulbs in case they need to be investigated.
Thinking I have removed the problem, I plugged the fridge back in to try and salvage our food.  It is cooling back down and seems normal, just now there is not a light and we don't fully trust that the wire that feeds the light is safe.  We threw away some groceries that got very warm on the top shelf.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning fridge light causing heat damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Dear sears,
I purchased this Kenmore Elite Electric Range model #79097473804 Sn VF94442709 From Sears in 2009. Since then it has been a constant failure one after another.
The glass door has exploded 4 times sending glass on our legs and feet.
The control panel has been replaced at least 3 times as well as over heated relays.

However on 18 July we had a new serious failure. We nearly had a fire. The house filled with smoke. The range was beeping with a flashing FLO ERR on display. It was impossible to shut the top coils OFF and the Oven could not be turned OFF. All were ON

It was too hot to get close to the stove for more than a second. I had to run and open the main breaker.
I reset the breaker and the range now works.
Service came the next day and ordered a new computer and control pannel at over $800 then add on a couple hundred in labor. I was told to open the breaker when I leave to prevent an un commanded ON in the range!

The problem is a design flaw! The computer is sitting on top of the stove with NO AIR flow and no fan the cool the CPU. An over heated CPU will hang. That is what we saw. with FLO ERR flashing. That means that all outputs are stuck ON holding the relays ON.

This is an unsafe product and Sears refuses to exchange it.
How did UL pass this as a safe range?

I wait for your reply and any assistance you can offer

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a near-fire situation and repeated failures causing injury from glass explosions, but no death occurred.

This caused the hot water to instantly boil and spray to the side. This would have resulted to serious injury had I not moved quickly.
justification: The pressure cooker depressurized and sprayed hot water, but no injury occurred due to quick reaction.

incident_description: My kenmore electric range has a mind of its own.  Model number 790.96011406.  It won't shut off on the smooth top,  most of the time the breaker has to be shut off. It gets stuck on high and will not change temperatures.  This happens on multiple burners.  I have been burnt several times by the uncontrollable temperature.  This is starting to happen more frequently.

incident_description:
Kitchen Aid Undercounter Dishwasher Started on Fire
Model KUDP01FLBL0
Serial FM4201561

Started dishwasher yesterday  morning, July 21th 2014....thankfully I was home.  
I was sitting in my home office about 15 feet from kitchen.  
Thought what I heard was the faint sound of a coffee grinder being used in the kitchen.  
Went to see what the noise was and saw smoke coming from around the top of the dishwasher door.  
Proceeded to open the dishwasher door, kitchen filled with smoke. 
After the smoke cleared I looked at the bottom inside of the dishwasher thinking a piece of plastic may have fallen on the element.  
That was not the case.  Door was extremely hot and could see the smoke coming out from INSIDE the door.  
Shut off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher then proceeded to removed the screws on the panel of the inside of door to see if in fact the cause of the smoke was in the door.  
Upon removing panel could plainly see the circuit panel caught fire and was burning at the time I first saw the smoke.  
We purchased this home 1.5 years ago, home was built in 2002, with this dishwasher and we also have a Kitchen Aid flat-top Oven/Range which we have also had nothing but what appears to be electrical issues.  
I will never buy another Kitchen Aid appliance....EVER.  
I am taking photos of everything and keeping the dishwasher for documentation purposes as well.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but there was no injury or death reported.

I was bleeding all over and screamed for my sisters help. As she ran to assist me, she accidentally kicked the blade that was lying next to me, as she did not see it. This resulted in half her toe being cut off, and part of the bone. We spent most of the day in the ER. I got away with just stitches and a tetanus shot... My sister was referred to a plastic surgeon to get a skin graft on her toe. Maybe this company should consider putting a button release for the blade, considering it is sharp enough to cut bone.

I had cooked the chicken and onions until tender.  I expelled the pressure in the cooker.  After it was safe to open the cooker, I added a few additional ingredients which didn't take as much time to cook as the chicken.  I replaced the lid on the cooker and started the pressure cooker again.  It began to increase in pressure but didn't sound exactly as it had before.  It was not to have built pressure if everything was not operating correctly.  I leaned over the cooker to see if there was a problem and it exploded in my face.  I had to go to the emergency room with  2nd degree burns on my scalp, face, shoulder and back.  I was hospitalized and have had some other complications after the injuries.  I am still in the process of healing.

incident_description:
The consumer reported that she and her family were experiencing what they thought were allergy symptoms due to mold. 

A specialist tested their house and detected high levels of formaldehyde. The high levels were traced to their gas oven. 

Formaldehyde levels were tested twice in June 2014. The first reading was in the range of 0.24-0.35ppm, depending on the location in the home. They conducted the second test right after cooking breakfast, 4 days later from the initial test, and level was 7.7ppm.

The consumer stated that she let the house ventilate. The consumer tested the home after ventilating it and found formaldehyde level at 0.3ppm. The consumer turned on the oven and and tested the level again to see if the oven was causing the issue. The consumer stated that the formaldehyde level was high again after turning on the oven.

The consumer stated that the manufacturer was uncooperative and informed her that they havenÃÂt received enough similar complaints to warrant a recall. The consumer was not provided any other assistance.

The consumer stated that she doesn't use the oven anymore. The consumer continues to use the stove-top. The issue does not exist with the stove-top.

The consumer stated that she and her daughters have experienced various respiratory conditions but as of yet they have not been proven to be linked to high levels of formaldehyde.
justification: The consumer and her family experienced respiratory conditions likely linked to formaldehyde exposure, but no direct medical proof was provided.

incident_description:
Samsung vent hood microwave starts by itself multiple times with the display showing 'Baked Potato'.

Keypad will not respond to turn off unit while this happens.

The unit will stop only if door is opened.

If left unattended the microwave will run continuously and can overheat causing a kitchen fire.

incident_description:
I had roasted vegetables in a full-length glass Pyrex dish (purchased less than a year ago) at 400 degrees for 45 minutes. I pulled the dish out and set it on the range to cool. The recipe I was using called for pouring marinade over the vegetables after taking them out of the oven, so I did that. As the liquid hit the dish, the dish exploded loudly, propelling glass and hot oil at me and within a 7 foot radius. 

I understand now that one is not supposed to pour liquid into a hot Pyrex dish. However, common kitchen mistakes like that should not result in such a violent explosion of the product. It was quite scary and unsafe.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion of a Pyrex dish, but the description does not mention any injury, only that it was scary and unsafe.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool gas range purchased 13-Oct-2012. When you stand too close to it, the gas will come on. Often times, you don't realize it until you smell the gas throughout the house. This happens frequently. There doesn't appear to be any type of safety device to prevent this. My dad is almost 84 years old and lives with us now. Though he is very aware of things, has no sense of smell. I'm so afraid the house is going explode one day due to this problem. It doesn't seem to matter who is at the stove;  my husband, dad, son, or myself, the gas arbitrarily comes on if slightly touched. I called Sears and Whirlpool about this today, but they just want to send a repairman at the cost of $75-$125 for a service call. I know I will likely have to do this, but it is apparent to me that there is no way we are the only ones experiencing this problem. Whirlpool basically just insinuated that it must not have been too much of a problem since I waited almost two years to report it. I told [REDACTED] at Whirlpool I had my other range almost 30 years without it ever coming like this. I also told her that she should be looking at it like I do...only two years and already fed up with the range. It's a death trap.

In the Incident Date box below, I will put the latest date of occurrence, but it happens very frequently.
justification: The gas range frequently releases gas when slightly touched, posing a significant risk of explosion, especially given the resident's lack of smell. No injuries or deaths have occurred yet, but the potential for severe harm is high.

incident_description: A 2 cup size Anchor Hocking glass measuring cup exploded in my kitchen cabinet. I was in the kitchen at the time and heard a pop and shattered glass falling. Small pieces of glass were all over the cabinet. This product had not been used for several weeks.

The consumer's wife called him to see what happened. The consumer stated they were unable to turn off the range and had to cut the circuit breaker.

The consumer stated that they have not turned on the range after that. 

The consumer contacted the manf. He was unable to speak to anyone there.

The consumer's model is not included in recall.

incident_description:
GE profile Spectra electric range - baking brownies at 350 degrees in the oven when a very bright glow like a welders torch developed on the lower  burner element of the oven and began to flame and crackle like a sparkler. Fortunately my daughter and her friends were in the kitchen and noticed the bright glow and alerted us. Turning off the oven alone did not stop the problem - had to pull the oven out and unplug it. The lower burner element had broken or burned through. Fortunately someone was  present in the immediate area and noticed it quickly. This type of failure could have caused a very serious fire if we had set a timer and been in another room. 
In checking to see if the lower element was easily removed for replacement we took off the back panel on the range and found singed and burned insulation and singed browned wire coverings as well. 
Needless to say we opted to discard the Range and purchased a new one, NOT GE this time . 
GE needs to put a stop fail of some sort on this part to prevent catastrophic failure. If the element is going to fail it should stop working, lose power , not burn up! 
This happened suddenly, with NO warning and with no prior issue or concern with the unit at all. 
Hate to think what it could have resulted in under other circumstances such as roast in the oven which you wouldn't stand nearby and watch for 4 hours. If we had not been in close proximity we could have returned to find the range up in flames and the kitchen too.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical failure that could have led to a serious fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
On 7/21/2014 at approximately 7:15pm , while sitting in the living room my husband and I heard what sounded like glass break coming from the kitchen. We immediately went to the kitchen and saw that the glass on the inside of the door of the top oven on our GE built-in double oven had shattered into pieces.  Because the top oven is a convection oven I hardly ever use it. It has been months since last used. I only use it on special occasions (Thanksgiving, Christmas, etc.). The bottom oven is my everyday oven of choice. I had used the bottom oven this morning at 10am  for about 40 min. at 300 degrees. The oven was off since 11am. 

The oven is approximately 2 years old and was installed brand new. I find this an unacceptable for an oven that is new and hardly been used. We have taken pictures if needed.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering in an oven with no reported injuries, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description:
GE Profile Refrigerator icemaker caught on fire. I smelled smoke and plastic burning and started looking for the cause. Saw smoke coming out of refrigerator. Opened freezer to see fire in ice maker. Flames were about 6 inches high. Could not get to plug to unplug electric to refrigerator. My son unplugged the ice maker inside the freezer and put out fire. 

this appliance is at our week-end home. If we had not happened to be here at the time and in the kitchen and not sleeping, then our home would probably have burned down, and worse, we could have died in the fire. The refrigerator is GE Model PTS225HS. Other numbers on the label are   PC40196 20013421P038 (GE #'s)
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity level.

incident_description: I hade a Cuisinart M#DCC-1100 S#00907 Coffee maker catch on fire. I had just put my coffee on and  the brew process had finished . I was standing about 10ft away from the coffee maker when I heard a boiling sound , I looked at the coffee pot and the coffee was boiling on the hot plate of the maker. I did not think too much about this then I saw the hot plate turn cherry red then start to smoke. Be for I could reach the maker he lower part burst into flames setting the coffee lower plastic on fire. I first cut the off switch and that did not help the hot plate was getting bright red now. I then unplugged the coffee maker but the fire still was burning and the upper part was melting. I had to use a CO2 fire extinguisher to put out the plastic and dish towel and curtains. If I had been in a different room in the house or outside this could have been a kitchen fire.  It looks as if the hot plate went into thermal overheat for some reason. I also could see no breaker or secondary protection for the hot plate portion of this coffee maker in the burnt coffee maker.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire, causing damage to surrounding items, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I just typed a description into this box and hit the NEXT button at the bottom and was unsure whether it was submitted to you, so I will try again. The glass front of the oven exploded all over the floor with some of the glass landing on top of the counter top, as well as all over me.  I was not directly in front of the range and fortunately only received a small cut on my foot.  The issue I have is that about half of the glass broke into pebbles like it should, but the other half shattered into tiny slivers and shards.  Luckily I was able to reach a towel and clear a path to get out of the glass on the floor.  It has been very difficult to clean up and could have been a very dangerous situation.  I took photos and contacted Sears asking that they replace the glass at no cost.  So far they have denied my request, even though they have stated that they are very committed to safety in their products.  This is very much a safety issue and could cause serious injury.

incident_description: Emerson microwave is making a lound noise and throwing sparks inside and wont shut off until i open door. This is not the original microwave i purchased the first one was melting around the inside of the door and burned my hand i contacted emerson and they repalced with this diffrent model  Now this model is having dangerous issues with spaking and not turning off could cause injury or fire.

incident_description:
Sitting in another part of house when smoke alarm sounded.  Saw smoke in kitchen area and found the kitchen filled with smoke.  Wife headed toward range where smoke seemed to be originating.  Just before she got there a glass casserole sitting on the stove top exploded.  Found front right burner on Frigidaire electric range on even though knob showed it to be off.  Ran knob through various positions and seemed to control heat level but would not turn burner off.  Turned off power to range at breaker panel to make safe.  No injuries and only damage was loss of casserole dish and glass everywhere but hate to think what might have happened if my wife had been closer when the casserole exploded or we had not been home.

Range is Frigidaire smooth top slide in model FGES3065KWA, serial # NF94824078.  Checked your recall pages and found a previous model Frigidaire range had been recalled for the same exact problem.  Called the Frigidaire recall phone #.  They simply said my model # was not included and they could not help.  Said they would document call and offered to connect me with customer service.  Customer service also said I was not in the recall and since my warranty had expired, there was nothing they could do.  Asked her to elevate to supervisor and only change was the offer to call a repairman for me but it would be at my expense.  Told her not to bother.  I would never feel safe turning that range on again repaired or not.
justification: No injuries occurred, but there was an incident involving smoke and an exploding casserole dish due to a malfunctioning stove.

incident_description:
Pushed the button that turns the toaster oven on and heard a loud noise and flames shot out the back. 
I could smell a terrible burning smell afterward. I told my son and unplugged it. I didn't get a chance to tell my husband he plugged it in and tried to use it and the same thing happened. The toaster oven is on counter away from anything else and has space around it. We have had it for four years and it has always been in the same place. This could really have started a fire. Luckily it is on tile and just has tile behind it and nothing flammable near by.

incident_description:
Purchased KitchenAid, convection, vented hood microwave near beginning of 2013.  We were in the process of using the timer which had about 15 minutes left on a 1 hour setting.  We were not touching the microwave when the fans began to blow fiercely.  Opening the door had no impact on the unit and it was getting dangerously hot and quickly.  We killed the power supply by disengaging the breaker within a minute of when the unit started itself.  

Once the unit cooled, we were able to unplug the cord from the wall socket and inspect the unit.  The convection oven must have been running un-commanded.  The glass turntable has black markings in it and the plastic at the base is now warped.  I believe the space inside the microwave is damaged as well, but this is just speculation at this point.

I am confident that if we had not been at home and readily in the area to stop the power feed to the unit then there would have been a fire or an explosion from the microwave starting on its own.

incident_description:
Re-sending, as it appears the first attempt didn't go through...

Farberware Soft Grip Ceramic Peeler
http://www.walmart.com/ip/Farberware-Soft-Grip-Ceramic-Peeler/17813013

The ceramic blade on this peeler is held in place by a very flimsy plastic cradle, with an equally flimsy plastic locking tab, inadequately glued together to hold the blade in place. 

In normal use, the pressure on the peeler is enough to flex the cradle, break the glue bond, and pop out the locking tab and ceramic blade out. For us, this happened after a few uses. Another reviewer on Walmart.com said it happened on the first use.

A small, razor sharp ceramic blade is hazardous to pick up, esp. for kids or the elderly. God forbid that it gets into someones food. As it is white ceramic, it looks like plastic, so nobody would expect it to be sharp.

While we were unharmed, this is an accident waiting to happen.

incident_description:
About two months ago, we received a gift of a Oster Clairborne 12" Aluminum [Glass] Covered Saute Pan Charcoal Grey With Helper Handle -- we believe it was manufactured by the Gibson Company, part of the Jardin Company.
My 84 year old wife had used it perhaps two or three times until July 2, 2014 ...
She was alone at home [I was shopping], in our kitchen,  preparing a meal in the Pan which was on our range top ...
While holding the Pan's handle in her hand and looking through the [glass] Cover, there was suddenly was a sound of an "EXPLOSION" and the Cover's glass "SHATTERED" into hundreds of shrapnel-like glass shards ...
Many tiny shards punctured her arms and legs, but luckily not her face -- and the Cover's small plastic handle, blew upwards and landed in my wife's hair ...
She was "frozen" in place, afraid to move in  stocking feet through hundreds of pieces of glass shards on the floor ...
Fortunitely, no one else was in the kitchen with her so there was no more severe hurt and the TRAUMA of the EXPLOSION could have resulted in a heart attack or stroke but gratefully didn't ...
She worked laboriously and carefully to clean up the glass all over the kitchen counter tops, the range and floor ... My daughter came, gave 1st aid to remove  tiny shards from my wifes body; there were no cuts still bleeding ...       She went to her doctor  by week-end to check her blood pressure; she remains afraid to be cooking in the kitchen ...
justification: The incident resulted in injuries from glass shards puncturing the victim's arms and legs, but no death or life-threatening conditions occurred.

incident_description:

Around Memorial Day this caller was baking on low baking temperature 295 degrees for about one hour when it beeped one time then flashed error code L2F3.
The caller tried to open the oven and could not open the door, he looked in and saw that the broiler element was red hot.
The caller's food was still in the oven however badly burned.
                                                                                                                                                The consumer tried to turn the oven off but since it is hardwired into the wall he could not turn it off until he turned the breaker off.
He still could not open the oven door until he waited an hour for it to cool off, flipped the breaker back on and then he could open the door.
Once he flipped the breaker back on, the broiler element again came on and began getting hot.

He turned the breaker off and called the manufacturer who sent a repair tech out the next day.
The repair tech turned the breaker on, witnessed that the broiler element automatically turns on and begins heating to extremely hot and can only be turned off by turning the breaker back off.

The repair tech informed the caller that the control board or the thermostat has failed and that the manufacturer no longer creates the control board.

He recommended replacing the oven but at consumer expense.
Consumer has stated that he can understand the oven going but  not with the safety hazard as this one has and has requested that manufacturer replace this unit at manufacturer expense.

There are no injuries to report

incident_description:
My complaint is in reference to the All Clad slow cooker, model SERIE SC01, which has a ceramic insert.  Twice the insert has mysteriously cracked out of the blue after cooking for several hours.  It was not due to cold or heated ingredients being added, nor from careless mishandling or accidentally knocking against other hard surfaces as I am very cautious about this.  During the first incident, I happened to notice a small crack near the handle (which did not leak liquid) but I believed could eventually expand and lead to a safety issue.  I ordered a new (and expensive) replacement crock through All Clad ÃÂ alarmed, but not throwing in the towel just yet.  After using the replacement crock for one and a half years, it mysteriously cracked while cooking on low after two hours.  Fortunately I was home when it happened.  I heard a loud pop in the kitchen and knew right away what it was.  By the time I made it into the kitchen, I saw liquid pouring out onto the counter.  There was a sizable crack down the side and across the bottom of the crock.  Within seconds the hot liquid contents were spilling out of the crock into the bottom of the metal cooker, through a spill hole onto the counter top and streaming down onto the floor.  The mess, albeit a real pain to clean up and a ruination of my anticipated dinner, was the least of my concerns.  What if I had not been home to see this problem and the contents continued to cook without liquid?  Would this start a fire?  Could the liquid spill onto an electrical cord nearby and cause an electrical fire?  Would the crock break apart in my hands spilling its hot contents all over me as I tried to dump them into another container -creating a burn incident?  I plan to keep the crock as evidence.
I went out onto the Internet to try to contact this company and decided that given the numerous other consumers who were having the exact same problem with their crock insert, it was time to get the federal government involved.  Based on the number of complaints, it appears that if you own this slow cooker and you actually use it, you will eventually have this cracking issue.  Not sure if other owners had their crockÃÂs liquid contents spill out like I did - but there is no doubt it is a safety issue.  I believe All Clad has a serious safety concern with this product and they need to step up and either correct the problem, or take the product off the market.  Can you help to hold them accountable?
I plan to contact All Clad and demand that they provide me with a reliable replacement crock that is not ceramic.   I just hope you will follow through with this case and will put an end to All CladÃÂs unscrupulous business practice of selling a defective product, then profiting off of the replacement parts ÃÂ while our safety remains at risk.
justification: The incident involves a cracked ceramic insert leading to potential safety hazards like burns or fire, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Yesterday evening, June 28, 2014, I placed a hot 9 x 13 inch Pyrex baking dish on an unlit gas burner ring on my stove to cool. I was standing a few feet to the right at my sink when I heard a strange noise. I turned toward the stove in time to hear a bang and see the dish explode into thousands of pieces of all shapes and sizes, including some icicle-like pieces several inches long with sharp points. I was hit by several small pieces and suffered minor puncture wounds on my left hand and arm and my left foot.

There were bits of glass all over the stove, in my dog's food and water dishes, the floor, etc. I cut my finger trying to clean up the glass on the stove. Today I'm still finding bits of glass.

I bought this baking dish at the grocery store 2-3 years ago and use it about once a month. I have other Pyrex dishes that belonged to my mother and grandmother (going back at least into the 1960s) that I use even more frequently, and have never had a problem.

I understand that the formula for the glass used in Pyrex has been changed, and learned from online research last night that exploding Pyrex is not unusual. How can a product with this much potential for injury remain on the market?
justification: The incident resulted in minor puncture wounds and cuts, indicating injury (severity 3). Online research suggests exploding Pyrex is not unusual, making occurrence likelihood possible (3).

justification: The incident caused no injury or damage, but it has occurred twice, indicating a possible design flaw. The likelihood is rated as likely (4) due to the recurrence and potential risk to a small child.

incident_description:

I did get cut with a piece of the glass but this could have been my worse since my granddaughter was just behind me when I was mixing.  If she would have been in open next to counter she could have been hit in the face with the glass.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from glass shards, and while severe outcomes were possible (e.g., harm to the granddaughter), they did not occur.

incident_description:
Oven door handle falls of causing outer portion of door to crash to the floor. Potential to cause broken glass cuts and burns from hot door. This is the second time this has happened to me.

This occurs because Sears' has made the screws too short so they eventually strip the holes in  the plastic bare.
