incident_description: Refrigerator section alarmed high temprature, when checked the temprature was 60 degrees. Unplugged and called authorized repairman. Repairman came and found that the light bulb remained on in the refrigerator when the door was closed, the lightbulb had burned a hole through the plastic inside cover and insulation was exposed. Repairman stated that had I not been home at the time and unplugged the refrigerator it could have caught fire.  The incident was reported to Fridgidaire by both the repairman and I. They told the repairman that it was a problem with the "mother board".  Fridgidaire made no attempt to rectify the situation. Upon researching online it appears others have had issues with this same problem. I have children in the house, thank goodness this did not catch fire during the night! The refrigerator was purchased at Lowe's on 9/10/2011. Model # LGHN2844MFO, Serial # 4A12413780. It is a Fridgidaire Gallery refrigerator, freezer is on the bottom and has french doors on top. Purchase price was $ 1816.89
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was cooking in the pan. The consumer put little bit of oil in the pan. The consumer cooked a batch of chicken fingers. The consumer went to cook another batch of chicken fingers and the pan exploded and popped up from the stove.

The consumer stated that her stove was on for about 10-15 minutes.

The consumer was taken to Albert Einstein Medical Center (Germantown Pike, PA). The consumer was treated for burn injuries. 

The consumer's daughter put out the fire on the range that occurred from the oil spilling on the range. 

The consumer has an attorney for this case. 
The consumer has not directly contacted the manf.

incident_description: On June 5th I put some chicken into the microwave for 1.5 minutes. The microwave burned up shooting acrid smoke out the bottom vent. The fire stopped when the kitchen ground fault circuit popped. My lungs were still sore the following day from the smoke. The fire was not in the food area, it was inside the generator area at the back of the oven. I e-mailed Hamilton Beach to inform them, but they have not responded.
justification: The incident caused smoke inhalation leading to sore lungs (injury), but the fire was contained and stopped by the circuit. Such incidents are unlikely but not rare.

incident_description: I have a Kitchenaid diswasher - model:  kudio1IL.  I started it last night to wash the dishes and about 10-15 minutes later started smelling an odd odor coming from the kitchen.  I walked out into the kitchen and my dishwasher was smoking from the upper right hand corner.  Very bad smell. incident_description: We were heating some frozen pizza in the oven. We pre-heated the oven to 425 F in accordance with the instructions. It had just beeped to indicate the oven had reached the correct temperature. I took the oven door handle in my left hand and opened it as I stood to the right of the oven door, and the glass suddenly shattered and fell out onto the floor. This was only the outer glass. The oven side glass remains intact.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the deep fryer bottom near the heating element got extremely hot, he smelled an odor of burning plastic.  He noticed that the multi purpose deep fryer had started melting at a temperature of 350.   It was in use for approximately 20 mins when the incident occurred.  He unplugged and disconnected the unit.

Caller feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her daughter had finished using the blender and while she was pouring out the contents a blade fell out and caused her to received laceration on her left hand.  She was given first aid from consumer who is a medical professional (nurse).  There were no prior incidents.  She had used it several times before this incident occurred.

The manufacturer was contacted 6/12/14 through email but she did not receive a response as yet.

Consumer feels that the blender is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the blender had been used several times before the incident.

incident_description:
Product:  Frigidaire Gallery Professional Series Gas Oven Window
Model No: FGF379WECS
Serial No: VF93818107

     At approximately 3:00 am I was awoken to a loud bang.  It sounded as though it came from the kitchen.  I was concerned someone tried to break into my home or an animal had entered into my house through the doggy door.  I quietly crept into the kitchen and continued to hear a clattering noise (as though rice was being poured over a metal surface).  When I turned the light on I realized there was glass all over my kitchen floor and on some counter tops.  I then realized the glass covering of the oven door had shattered.  Glass was scattered immediately in front of and within a 10 ft. radius of the oven door.  Glass had accumulated in the warm and serve drawer underneath the oven door. There were also glass fragments on the opposing counter top (approximately 10 ft. away).  The oven and stove top were not on at the time of the incident.  The stove top had been used the night before around 5:00 pm.  The oven had not been used and the door had not been opened in over a week.
     I thoroughly swept and vacuumed the glass up, however I am still picking up pieces of glass 3 weeks later.  Very minor injuries have occurred as a result of the broken pieces of glass.  I had a couple small scratches on my hands while cleaning up the glass.  Since the incident my husband, my dogs and I have all stepped on pieces of glass and have needed to remove tiny pieces from our feet.
     I am reporting this incident because we have been inconvenienced by having to continually clean up pieces of glass and treat minor injuries.  Additionally, I have researched the costs to repair the window and they are ranging in prices, but all over $150.  I have seen other reports of this odd incident occurring.  All of the reports have been similar to mine ÃÂ there seemed to be an explosion of glass while the oven was not in use.  I wanted to see if there have been recalls or if the Frigidaire would compensate me to have the oven repaired.
justification: Minor injuries occurred from glass fragments, including scratches and stepping on glass pieces.

incident_description: Respondent reported that they responded to an emergency fire call, they discovered that a microwave was burning substantially while not in use.  He unplugged the unit to contain the fire.  The caller was informed by the owner that she was not using the microwave, however, it erupted in flames.  There were no other damages except for the microwave.
justification: The incident was a fire that was contained by the respondent, with no injuries or deaths reported.

incident_description: I was sitting in my living room on the evening of 6/17/14 when I heard a very loud sound, sort of like a window shattering. Upon going into the kitchen to inspect for damage, I found a pool of liquid on the counter where my Pampered Chef Ice Cream Scoop had been sitting. The scoop itself was down in my sink, along with the little plastic end cap. There was liquid on the floor and sprayed across the wall opposite of the counter, about 6' away from where the scoop had been. I noticed a quarter-sized metal disk laying on the floor up against baseboard. When I looked up the wall a little farther, I noticed that the wall had also been sprayed with the liquid from inside the scoop, and there was a chunk of wood missing from the oak trim around the door frame in that area, where the metal disk had made contact with the trim.
justification: The incident involved property damage (broken scoop, liquid spray, and damaged trim) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
During the night, our oven/range started humming loudly and then cracked, popped, and started spewing smoke from the wiring shield and the back of the display box. The breaker was tripped and the unit shut off. There is a large burn in the wall behind the unit that was hot to the touch immediately following the incident. Had the breaker not shut off or the unit been pulled away from the wall, it could have started a fire. 
The heating elements for the range also have a history of varying temperature uncontrollably, often exceeding set temperatures and heating to high even at low settings.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred, and the issue has a history of recurring.

incident_description:
(05/20/20140 The consumer stated that she turned the cook top off after cooking dinner. There was an HE code on the control panel. The consumer stated that she didn't think anything of the code. She walked away. When she came back to clean the counters, she smelled a plastic burning smell. She realized that the element was still on. She turned the cook top it off at the breaker. When her husband home, he checked the element and discovered that it was doing the same thing.

incident_description:

incident_description: After using convection oven for cooking dinner, while the oven cooled the door glass exploded. There are 3 panes of glass in the door and the 2 inner panes exploded.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass exploding, but there was no mention of injury, so severity is 2. Such incidents are uncommon but not unheard of, hence likelihood is 2.

incident_description: I have a frigidaire glass top stove and the right front burner will not regulate temperate. Once it is turned on it will keep getting hotter and hotter even if it is set to simmer. You can feel the heat from the burner a couple feet away. incident_description: My GE Monogram dishwasher was in the middle of a wash cycle when there was a smell of burning electrical wiring and then the unit stopped working.  I immediately contacted a GE repairman who discovered faulty electrical wiring where the AC power comes into the dishwasher.  He replaced the short-circuited wiring and the unit is now functional.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was trying to use his oven to bake. He pressed the button to start the oven, but it would not respond. He had to apply a considerable amount of pressure in order for the button to react. He stated that this happen after the first time that he used the "self cleaning" option. He believes that after the oven was submitted to the "self-cleaning" the control panel was affected by the heat and this is causing the oven control buttons to not work properly.

I am frightened every time I use this $995 stove that seems to have had problems even after people have them repaired with a new electronic panel board. I won't really feel safe unless LG gives me a cash refund so I can purchase a new range. that has much better performance record. No more LG products for me.

incident_description:

The unit displayed an error of F10, overheated, sparked and a flame erupted just for a few seconds from the rear of the oven, while it was on at 350 degrees.  The oven was on for approximately 30 mins before the incident occurred.  She switched off the oven by using the circuit breaker.

This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

incident_description: I was using the blade device on my hand blender to finely chop tuna.  When I went to clear the tuna from the blade, I apparently inadvertently pressed the on switch which requires only the lightest of pressure.  I nearly chopped off my left middle finger. The "warning" on the device is barely legible (same silver color as the device) and the on switch is WAY DANGEROUS!  Far too sensitive....is triggered by the lightest of pressure. The stove is model #P2S975SEP1SS. 
The microwave handle conducts heat. If we are cooking either water for pasta, which we do several times a week, or I am making soup, we use the right front burner. This makes the microwave door handle, which is directly above the burner, dangerously hot. When we open the microwave we get our hand burned, if we forget to use a potholder. incident_description: I have owned a GE side by side refrigerator for just over a year.  I have a freezer door that distributes water & ice. I dispensed ice into a glass and found that there was a small piece of clear plastic (which mixes in with the ice and looks like it) in the glass. I removed the ice tray and dumped the ice finding a larger piece of clear plastic mixed in. Upon examination of the unit I found that the fins that move the ice forward toward the distribution point are made of clear plastic and one of them had broken off shattered and mixed in with the ice. It is hard to see these pieces as they look like the ice. I find this to very dangerous as children or someone else using this ice dispenser would  most likely not notice the sharp plastic in their glass and possibly ingest it. I have called GE for service, but I feel that this condition needs attention
justification: The presence of sharp plastic pieces in ice poses a risk of ingestion and potential injury, though no actual injury is reported yet.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool Range Model GS773LXSS0 Serial Number RT1812687. I called Whirlpool because of an obvious and dangerous defect in their range.  If you accidentally brush against the knobs and don't know you even hit the knob, the burners will turn on without igniting and gas will pour into the room. I recently walked into my house and the entire house was full of gas and the fireplace was on. It took over 30 minutes to clear the house of the gas. We were lucky that the entire house didn't explode and go up in flames. We have had two other instances in the past month in which this has happened and we have had to open our windows and doors to clear the house. Something needs to be done immediately to correct this action of Whirlpool's faulty oven.
I have notified the Whirlpool company and they do not care that their oven could cause costumers to die.When I was talking to the Whirlpool representative they told me it was something that could not be corrected. So I told them. " You mean to tell me that you know you have a defective appliance that could kill someone and you are doing nothing to fix this problem?" and [REDACTED] the Whirlpool representative replied" This is the way it was designed and there is nothing we can do about it." 
So I guess Whirlpool is telling me that I can go buy another range because there is nothing that they will do about it and that they do not consider it a defect even though according to their own representative the company is aware that this range is extremely dangerous.
I wonder how many people have died due to this issue. I thought that the US government required all appliances to be built to certain safety specifications. I thought on ovens it was required that you have to PUSH in and turn for the burners to light. With my oven you don't push in but it lights if you brush against it and you don't even know that gas is spewing into the house. How many consumers have gone to bed not realizing that gas was coming out of their range and have died due to CO2 poisoning?
Something needs to be done immediately to protect the health and safety of Whirlpool customers.
Sincerely
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a dangerous defect leading to gas leaks, which could result in death, but no actual injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description: I was not in the kitchen when the incident occurred, but I did hear the  sound.  Gas range, Kenmore, 2011 purchase.  I was in the garage dealing with AAA for a stalled car when I heard a loud sound--couldn't even tell what it was.  When I went inside, I found that the entire glass portion of the oven door was in thousands of pieces--nothing bigger than an inch, most the size of a grain of rice or a small corn kernal.  Also lots (lots!) of glass dust, plus shards. The latter 2 had worked down into the tiny cracks between the hardwood floor boards.  There was also glass in the bottom of the oven and in the warmer drawer at the bottom.  The oven had not been used for at least 48 hours, possibly more.  I had bumped my knee into it earlier in the day, but it was just that--a bump.  I called Sears, ordered a new door and scheduled an appointment to have it installed.  Then, when I thought about it, I decided the glass should not have shattered like that. I'm pretty sure it was tempered.  And the internet is full of stories back for several years.  Many Kenmore.  Many people said they reported it to Sears but were told they didn't have any complaints and didn't know anything about it.  So I decided to continue with my complaint here.  I will next go to Consumer Reports, then on to Bottom Line, [REDACTED], whoever will listen.  Somebody could get hurt.  Nobody did in this case, although my puppy thought the glass was crushed ice and did try to snag a few pieces. I did save all the pieces.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of an oven door with no reported injuries, but potential for harm exists.

incident_description:
On the evening of 6/14/14, my husband set our barely 6 month old Samsung electric range to self clean at the minimum allowable amount time permitted, of 3 hours. It was during this time that the fumes were so extreme to cause burning eyes and headaches even after having the doors and windows open and fans on full blast. It wasn't until 4/17/14 when we went to use the range again for this first time since cleaning, that we noticed both cabinets and drawers on either side of the oven were damaged. The white laminate had peeled and melted away from the wood and in one place started to turn brown and looked as if it was getting ready to burn and start a fire. 

After calling Samsung on 6/17/14 @ 7:31 pm and telling them what had happened for 41 minutes, I was instructed to unplug the unit. 

On 6/18/14, I was sent an email from Samsung requesting a professional estimate from a licensed contractor for the damage as well pictures of the damage. I was able to provide pictures via email reply and was waiting for a licensed cabinet repair person to call me back. After no call backs, I realized, no one repairs cabinets, they replace them... 

On 6/20/14, Samsung had sent a technician out to the house by the name of [REDACTED], from Complete Appliance Service, Inc in Cleveland, OH.  Upon his arrival, [REDACTED] stated that he was instructed to only take pictures and send them in to Samsung. He even called his office in my presence to verify his instructions. During his picture taking, [REDACTED] said that just by looking at it you couldn't see anything that would suggest a bad seal and that he would have to take the entire range apart to see if maybe he could tell what happened. Then he left... Later that evening, the Home Depot technician that I contacted, came over to provide an estimate on the cabinets. Because the cabinets are 13 years old, the style of doors is no longer available and therefore, all the doors and cabinets need to be replaced. However, this does not take into account that the existing cabinets, which are also white, may not match exactly the new doors and drawers. Another dilemma...

So.... after being told to unplug the range and repeated attempts calling Samsung to get this faulty range removed from my house and a refund issued, nothing else has happened. Executive Customer Relations stating that they can't remove the unit until a technician has serviced the unit. Hello??? What am I supposed to do in the interim? Use the range they told me to unplug for fear of burning down my house and everyone in it, continue to eat out or cook in the microwave (yuck)? Circles of nonsense, that's all Samsung has been able to effectively provide me with in this situation...

6/24/14 3:37 pm, received a call from Samsung's insurance carrier regarding the Home Depot estimate I submitted stating that until they have been provided a reason from a service technician regarding the problem with the range, they cannot move forward with my claim (more circles).

6/24/14 4:02 pm. received a voicemail from Complete Appliance Service, Inc., [REDACTED] quoted after submitting the photos, Samsung finally got back to them stating that within the User Manual it sates "Caution, caution, this range has been designed to comply for maximum allowable wood cabinet temperature rating of 194 degrees Fahrenheit etc... I have searched the user manual 3 times and found no such verbiage even resembling this. I could not even locate a temperature reference anywhere let alone cabinets. To sum up the voicemail, [REDACTED] said it is between Samsung and us at this point.

So now, I have a faulty range that could overheat and/or cause serious injury at the next use and Samsung stated to unplug and provided no follow up. I will start calling again tomorrow...
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted cabinets) and potential safety hazards, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: This coffeemaker is a hazard.  The warming plate stays hot whether or not you use the carafe side.  This is a problem when the right side single-cup brewer doesn't work.  It sounds like it's heating up but the water stays in the unit.  When I try to empty the unit, sometimes the water comes out and sometimes it doesn't.  Today, suddenly, the water came out 5 or 10 minutes after I removed a mug.  While trying to stop the flood, I inadvertently burned my skin with the hot water and the plate, which was still hot after the single cup brewed.  I had to take the carafe off the unit in order to drain the water that never came out of the single serve side.  Fortunately, I was near a sink and applied cold water and ice immediately so I will be fine.   It is a defective and dangerous product and I am requesting a full refund from Hamilton Beach.  I purchased this at Sam's Club in Fridley, MN in November, 2013 so it has been less than a year.  I paid $79.99 plus tax.  I could probably get a receipt from Sam's, and it will like be on my credit card, but I think Hamilton Beach should refund the money regardless of whether I can find the receipt from last November.  I have emailed Hamilton Beach with this exact complaint and I told them I would be filing a complaint with the Consumer Product Safety Commission.  I hope you will investigate this problem and remove this product from the market.  While it is a novel idea, the product is too dangerous to be sold.

I pulled the melting cover off the refrigerator as the plastic was soft enough to stretch and come free.  I then unscrewed the light bulbs to keep them from melting more of the refrigerator.

incident_description:
I just purchased a new Kenmore Microwave Oven Model No. 405.73099310 Serial No. 14044006458 from the Visalia California Sears on 06/19/2014 and discovered the microwave will start on its own and will not turn off unless you unplug the device. 

When I first installed the microwave in my kitchen, I plugged the microwave into the power outlet on the wall and began cleaning up the packaging. Within a few minutes, the microwave started on its own (turned on) and would not turn off. I had to unplug he power cord from the wall to turn it off. 

After plugging the microwave oven back into the power outlet, the over started and would not allow me to press the stop button to stop the power. I again had to unplug the device. When trying it  again and the microwave would start when I open then close the door. I have video fro my phone showing what I am explaining.

No damage or injury to my person or home, but extremely fear this will cause a fire if turned on and left unattended. I am planning to return this defective microwave back to Sears as soon as possible unless otherwise directed.

In addition, I have phone video of how microwave acted and photos of identifying information if needed.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but caused no injury or damage, though there is a potential risk of fire if left unattended.

incident_description:
Dishwasher ignited itself on fire.
No injuries sustained.
Only damage was to the dishwasher itself, as I was present to control the fire.

Dishwasher is 12 years of age; Never had a problem with it.  Normal use, turned it on, and while I was present in the kitchen, after less than 10 minutes of operation the control board behind the display panel started popping, sputtering, sparking, smoking and instantly ignited.

Billowing black/grey smoke and bright white/orange flames from the operators panel, I opened the dishwasher door and the flames started to subside, with the smoke still pouring out - smelling of burning plastics, insulation, and circuitry.  While the door was open, the circuitry for the control being shorted, the dishwasher spewed hot soapy water everywhere.

I slammed the door shut and flames started right back up again.  I reached for the dry-chem fire extinguisher and the phone to call 911, but thought to unlatch the dishwasher door again. The flames subsided, and I terminated my 911 call attempt.  I pulled out the dishwasher from under the counter to disconnect the power, and found it was hard-wired into the wall.  I proceeded downstairs to turn off the associated breaker.

Through good fortune I was present at the time.  Many are the times when I set the dishwasher to it's task and head out the door to work.  My wife, kitchen, home, my business at home, and my best canine friend are all very lucky that it didn't happen while we were away.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the dishwasher ignited and caused significant damage, indicating an incident with no harm to people.

incident_description:
I turned on the top oven broiler to the temperature of 400. I rarely use this as a broiler. I was letting it warm up when I heard a popping sound. I looked at the oven and saw a fire and sparks. I turn the oven off. When it cooled down I saw that the broiler coil had broken into  pieces. The oven was empty at the time.

I went on the web and googled maytag Gemini oven fire and saw that others had similar experiences. Someone has even posted a video of this experience. It seems dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a fire and sparks in the oven with no injury, and similar occurrences have been reported by others, indicating it is likely to happen again.

incident_description:
We have an 8 year old combination oven and microwave, KitchenAid Superba model #KEMC308KSS04, Serial #XT2211387.  We are moving and my wife decided to clean the oven for the people buying our old house. This was the first time the oven was cleaned utilizing the built-in high temperature cleaner. During the process the window of the microwave situated above the oven blew out scattering flying glass throughout the kitchen. Fortunately, nobody was injured.

My wife contacted the company and was told that they have no recall for this product. Because of the explosive nature of the defect we believe that this product is dangerous and should be thoroughly investigated by the Consumer Product Safety Commission.
justification: The incident involved flying glass but no injuries, and the product defect appears to be rare based on the lack of recalls.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she has been having ongoing problems with her gas range for about 2-3 months.  The gas knobs turns on easily without any one's knowledge especially when you brush against it.  This causes gas to escape into the room and there is an overwhelming smell of gas after which it is then turned off.  Most recent incident was on 6//6/14. incident_description:
(05/04/2014) The consumer stated that he was using the knife blade to puncture a piece of plastic. The multi tool has a locking mechanism but it failed as he was using the tip of the knife to puncture a hole in the plastic. The blade closed on the back of his right thumb and severed the tendons.

The consumer went to the emergency room at St. John's Hospital and Medical Center 22101 Morass Rd. Detroit MI 48236. He was seen by one of the attending nurses. His thumb was stitched back together. The consumer had to go to see a hand surgeon to get the tendons re attached.

The consumer sent the tool back to the manufacturer with a letter stating what happened. he also sent a picture of his hand.

The consumer left two or three messages but got no response from [REDACTED].

The consumer was advised that they had received his letter and the tool.

The burner will not turn off until the range is unplugged.  After contacting them they noted there was a recall for that problem however my products serial number did not fall into the recall range so there was nothing they could do for me. incident_description: I have a Bosch Range #HGS255UC/01.  This was an expensive range$1800. It has had several problems since we purchased it. The latest problem is a real safety problem. The door doesnot close properly. My knobs on the front are damaged from the heat escaping. The front of the stove gets extremely hot and my cupboard beside the stove gets hot as well. I leave my cupboard door open when I use the oven so it will not burn. The replacement part as very expensive. Bosch has acknowledge a design problem with this door and has made the repair very costly for the consumer. A product recall should have been done on this part at the cost to Bosch.

incident_description: My stove is a Frigidaire Electric Range Model #model # glefs79dcl .  We first noticed the right side burners would not regulate heat - they ran full blast regardless of what temperature we wanted.  Now the left side burners are doing the same thing.  It usually happens when the burner is turned to a hot setting first and then turned down.  When you try to turn the temperature down, it will not respond.  On the right side burners, they sometimes continue to run full blast for a few seconds even after you have turned the burners to off.  The left side still turns off when you turn the burner to the off position.  I worry that one day I will not be able to get the stove to turn off at all.  We have inquired with Frigidaire about recalls before but they tell us that our model has no recalls even though other models by the company have recalls for this very same problem.
justification: The stove's burners malfunction by not regulating heat and sometimes not turning off immediately, posing a risk of overheating but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: my fridgidaire dishwasher model fdbb945dc0 sparked by the control panel and started smoking. the kitchen was filled with smoke. I called the company and they said because it was purchased in 2005 they would not fix what was wrong. luckily I was home when this happened and turned off the circuit breaker. this product is a fire hazard, I wasn't even using it when this happened.

incident_description:

The defect effects the oven primarily where the middle racks slide in, and in my own case, only the lowest rung will hold a rack, and only about 50% of the time. Due to the low nature of this, I have nearly fallen into my oven 3 times, and have burned my hand once. When attempting to roast a turkey in the oven, the rack fell out several times, causing a grease fire hazard.

This is a very dangerous situation, and the oven walls should be recalled and replaced by Sears.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the side by side refrigerator defrosting heater by the water tank in the unit caught fire and melted the tray which dispersed black soot everywhere inside the refrigerator.  If the circuit breaker had not tripped it could have burnt her house down.  (4/14/14) She contacted the manufacturer and she was informed that someone would be sent out 4/24/14, she was also offered a 30% discount to a new refrigerator, caller declined.  She received two reports on the refrigerator from the manufacturer and a local repair person.

 There had been no prior incidents or service calls with this product.

 Caller stated that this refrigerator is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries or deaths, and the likelihood is unlikely as there were no prior incidents with this product.

incident_description:
GE microwave model # PVM1790SR1SS
This is an overhead unit installed above the stove. The microwave is used about 10 to 20 times a day. Over the last couple of months we noticed that the microwave would turn on intermittently for a few seconds then shut off. We thought nothing of it. Today after returning home from grocery shopping we noticed smoke in the kitchen area. The microwave was running and was extremely hot. We pulled the power cord to the microwave  to shut it off and sprayed water on it to cool it down. I have no doubt in my mind that if I would have returned home any later that the microwave would've caught fire and caused serious damage. I checked online to see if there are any recalls and there are none for this microwave at this time. While looking online I noticed that other consumers have faced similar problems, some homes have even caught fire. There is a video on YouTube titled: GE profile Pvm1790sr1ss starts on its own! This video shows exactly what mine did before it started to smoke. This seems to be a serious safety issue not too sure why nothing has been done about it?
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing smoke and extreme heat, posing a fire hazard that could lead to injury or property damage, with similar incidents reported by other users.

incident_description:

The caller began having to check the dishwasher when he knew the cycle should be completed so that he could be sure it was off.
He contacted the manufacturer in March 2013 and then in following months but couldn't get them to send a repair tech.
Around February he spoke with someone because he began to smell a burning odor.
At this time the manufacturer sent a tech who said nothing was wrong with the dishwasher.
Aggressive Appliance sent a tech out who diagnosed motor problems.

He finally spoke with someone with the manufacturer around February 2014 who sent a repair tech out from Topline Appliance.
April 21st, 2014 this most recent tech pulled the dishwasher from the wall and both he and the caller witnessed excessive burning around the power supply in the back and going into the unit.
He has been in touch since then with the manufacturer a couple of times today, April 21st, 2014 with the manufacturer asking for additional pictures.           

There are no injuries being reported
The caller is in touch with the manufacturer
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning dishwasher with no reported injuries, fitting the criteria for severity level 2.

incident_description:

We reported this to the warranty company and have called each time to find out if this product has been on recall.  Each time we have been told that this product is not on the recall list and there is nothing they can do about it.  We have 5 children in the home and we are lucky that each time except the most recent incident an adult has noticed the burner on and we ensured the children were no where near the kitchen.  

However this is very dangerous as our last incident occurred whilst we were away for the night.  It was lucky that my wife entered the home and straight into the kitchen to check and released that it was hot.  Had something been on the top or fallen on top somehow we would have not had a home to come back to.  

No one is willing to take responsibility for this malfunction and I'm sorry but I am not prepared to loose my home or have any member of my family hurt due to a faulty item.
justification: The stove burner turning on automatically poses a significant risk of injury or fire, especially with children in the home, and has occurred multiple times.

incident_description:

April 29th, 2014 this caller woke, went to her kitchen and was met with a lot of gray smoke.
She could see that the smoke was coming from the dishwasher so she opened the units door, took out the melted dishes.
Her husband turned the breaker off.

There have been no injuries to be reported

The manufacturer  scheduled a repair technician to install a new broiler handle free of charge because the range was still under warranty. About one week after, the repair technician installed a replacement broiler handle. The consumer never used the broiler again.

The consumer thinks this product poses a fire, burn and injury hazard.

No relevant CPSC recalls were found.

incident_description:

I have had the oven for approximately nine years and have never had any problems with it.

It is model JE1290ML01, manufactured in 2006.
justification: The incident caused a fire but no injury, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: My Kenmore electric range caught  on fire. I turned it on and smelt smoke. I went to the stove and it smoked and caught fire to my stove and back wall. It was the control unit that turns on the stove. The model number is #79092209014. Serial# vf11427491
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death was reported, and such electrical malfunctions are uncommon but not rare.

incident_description:
I have a Black & Decker blender that is approximately 6 to 7 years old. Has been used less than 50 times in its life. I used the blender the morning of 6/13/14 to blend a protein shake. After finished I washed the glass container and put it back on the blender base. I forgot to unplug the unit after I was done. I worked a 48 hour shift at the fire station and returned home on the morning of 6/15/14. No one was in the house during this 48 hour period of time. When returned home I noticed pieces of plastic on the counter. I began to look and noticed that the blender had come on and run until the plastic gears and base on the glass jar had come apart. Not sure if the motor burned up or not but the counter was covered with a black soot. I have no idea how long it ran before this happened but I am for sure it is a fire hazard.

Black & Decker CAT. NO. BL1900
Type 1 550W 120V-60Hz
justification: The blender malfunctioned and caused damage but no injury or death occurred.

It does not take 8 hours to bake chicken breasts at 350 degrees. I have followed your instructions to the "T" trying to get this [REDACTED] range to work.  I am forced to throw away my food because of the errors with this range.  I am not the only resident of this malfunction.

incident_description: Two-slide Dualit electric toaster purchased new on Oct. 15, 2013. It has received light use in a one-person household. justification: The toaster's timer malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was baking in his range's oven for 45 minutes at 350 degrees. He tried to turn off the oven by pressing the "off" option on the control panel keypad. The consumer pressed the button multiple times, but the control panel did not respond and the oven would not turn off. Immediately, the consumer decided to disconnect the range's power by turning off the circuit breaker. The consumer was not injured and no property damage was associated with this incident. He discontinued the use of this product.

The manufacturer offered to cover the costs of labor and diagnostics but not the replacement parts which would cost around $300.00. The customer service representative informed the consumer that they would have to replace the control pannel and an electronic latch. The consumer declined the offer.

The consumer believes this product poses a fire hazard.

No CPSC recalls involving this specific product could be found at this moment.

The consumer stated that the heat from the oven causes the exterior to heat up.

justification: The straw broke off in the child's mouth, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: Hamilton Beach reversible griddle G43.  Bacon grease does not drain into the grease trap very well.  Instead it collects on the griddle then seeps down between the two reversible griddle plates and has the potential to come in contact with the electric heating elements.  Creating a fire hazard.  I have had several occasions where smoke has come from under the griddle plates but no fire.
