incident_description: TRU 18 quart Capacity Roaster Oven, sold by KOHLS.  Used only 2 times.  At Thanksgiving last year the rubber legs came off when cooking and scorched a cork pad that I had under it on my counter.  The legs only have little nipples on it and then go into a holes on the bottom of the roaster.  They do not screw in or anything.   Pushed back into the holes on the bottom of the unit securely on the left side. They were on it when I started using it.  On May 10th, 2014 I made a potatoes dish.  Between the pans (because it had sour cream and milk product, and cheese) I placed 1 cup of water.  I have been raised with roasters and my recipe states to add up to 2 cups water when cooking in a roaster with any of the above products to keep it from burning.   When my son in law went to move it, he lifted it up , and his wife told him wait a minute. So  he went to sit it  back down on solid surface.  The 2 legs came off on the right side,  and he did not see that.  When he set it down on the counter the weight of the 15lbs in the roaster shifted because the it did not sit level now,  and he was severely burned by the steam from the roaster when he went to sit it down on the solid surface.  He suffered 2nd. degree burns.  Luckily he was a ems for 6 years, severed as a medic oversees 3 x, and is a police officer now.  However, he did have to seek medical care, was treated for 2nd degree burns, and had to see a burn specialist.  He missed weeks of work.  I decided to do an experiment with just water in the roaster at 325 degrees.  When the roaster is sitting on a flat surface and the unity has been on say for any length of time the it gets warm, it you slightly pick it up, the legs come off as the metal on the bottom of the unit is hot and  must expand so the little legs come off.  This is very dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring medical treatment and missed work, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests the legs frequently detach when the roaster is moved, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: GE Microwave Profile Series "Over Cooktop" Model PVM1870SM3SS.  While I was defrosting food for dinner in the microwave, the Grille Assembly fell off the top of the microwave oven and shattered on the cook top below.  Fortunately there was nothing on the cook top at the time.  The Grille Assembly weighs 2-3 lbs, and had there been a frying pan or pot of boiling water on the cooktop, I would have suffered severe burns.  As it was, pieces of hard, sharp plastic flew all over the kitchen, starting at about my waist (~36" above the floor) and could have caused damage to small children's eyes.
justification: The incident involved a falling Grille Assembly that could have caused severe burns or eye injuries, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description: I have a LG Electric Glass Top Stove  LRE30451.   This burners on this stove will sometimes NOT turn off. Or other times heat to a higher temp when the temp is not raised.   I called LG and they promptly sent a tech out to fix this.   The next day.. the SAME problem. Called LG back, they send a tech back out for a second fix. This fix lasted a while. We rarely use this stove as we usually eat out and use our toaster oven. Last night again, I could not get the stovetop to cool down., it would keep turning on and heating back up like the last time we had the problem.  I went to wipe down the surface where we were not cooking and two of the other burners were warm and glowing.  This threw me off because I did not expect them to be warm and there was no indication on the stove they were warm. We had not even used them and they were glowing. Had they been any warmer I would have burned myself.  I called LG back and they said they will come "fix" this again.  I told them that this was a faulty dangerous product and I did not want it in my home.  It is sitting in my house unplugged.  They said they would only fix it. They are fixing this product with the same faulty parts that are causing the problems.  Very very very dangerous.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a burn risk, but no injury has occurred yet. The issue is recurring despite multiple repair attempts, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: Dishwasher was running on normal cycle . I was upstairs when I noticed a strong smell coming from downstairs. I went down stairs and saw smoke  / haze in the kitchen. I saw it was coming from the dishwasher control panel when suddenly flames burst out of the top of the panel. I shut the power off and the smoke and flames stopped. Later that night my husband removed the face of the control panel to find the wiring burnt and melted.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My less-than-three-year-old high-end KitchenAid dishwasher was running on a 1hour wash/heat dry cycle when it made several loud pops that sounded like explosions, followed by a crackling/fizzling sound.  My daughter and husband were nearby and raced to the dishwasher.  My husband immediately cut off power to the appliance using the power switch on the wall.  Then, he opened the dishwasher door and the kitchen and 1st floor rooms filled with smoke.  Thank goodness my husband was home, as my daughter would not have known to cut the power.  The damage could have been much worse.

On June 10, when the certified KitchenAid service technician examined the inside of the dishwasher door, he found charred parts and smoke damage. The parts that must be replaced include: control panel, control board, inline fuse, and complete wiring harness - only some of these parts are covered by warranty.  He said that he had never seen anything like this.  Of course, if my husband had not switched off the power immediately, this could have caused a fire and the technician would not have been the one to examine the remains of the dishwasher.

I contacted KitchenAid by tweet yesterday.  They called me and have offered to pay for repair of my dishwasher. However, I am concerned that, if the fire was due to a manufacturing defect, the repaired dishwasher might catch fire again.
justification: The incident involved loud pops, smoke, and charred parts but no injury or death occurred, and the technician mentioned he had never seen anything like this, indicating rarity.

incident_description: A screw fell into my food from the top of a Viking oven (Model LVESO130SS).   No injuries incurred since I immediately noticed the screw on the pan.  Upon inspection, I noticed several uncovered screws in the top of this oven that have the potential of falling into utensils and food unnoticed.
justification: A screw fell into the food but was noticed before consumption, indicating an incident with no injury. Uncovered screws increase the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The glass door in my GE oven (model jtp55s p1ss) shattered after it was used for about 30 minutes.   The unit is 2 years old.
justification: The glass door shattered during use, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I started a roast in my Crock Pot brand crock pot around 9:30. At 1:30 I heard a loud pop and found the lid had shattered, glass flew up and all over the counter and into the food and even shot small pieces on my arm resulting in a few small cuts.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts from shattered glass, indicating an injury (severity 3), but such occurrences are unlikely (likelihood 2) based on typical crock pot usage.

incident_description: While I was cutting cheese with the knife, it snapped at the point where the blade and the handle meet. This caused the blade to be forcefully ejected from the counter and cutting board, in this case harmlessly onto the floor. Upon inspection of the knife I discovered that its connection to the handle is about 1 cm by 1 mm thick. It would appear that this knife does not have enough strength to withstand cutting a block of cheddar cheese, which was my intention when I purchased it a week prior.
justification: The knife broke but no injury occurred, indicating a minor incident.

incident_description: I was cooking dinner tonight in my 3 year old oven.  When the timer went off, I opened the door to remove my food and the glass on the front shattered all over my legs and the floor.  Fortunately I was uninjured except for a few small slivers of glass that I had to pull out of the bottom of my feet, but what if my children had been in the kitchen with me?  I called the Sears repair line to inquire about the frequency of this accident, and to my dismay, it happens all the time!  How long is this going to be allowed to continue without a recall on the product before an oven explodes all over and infant?
justification: The incident caused no injury but involved significant risk, especially considering the potential for harm to children. The high frequency of similar incidents reported by Sears indicates a likely recurrence.

incident_description: The front right burner of my Kenmore smooth top range was turned on to high and when I turned it off, the burner didn't go off.  I turned it on and off again and still it stayed on high.  After several minutes, it turned off on its on.  I just bought the house in Sept. of 2013 so I don't have much of a history on the stove.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but turned off on its own without causing injury or damage, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire Gas Range/Oven (Model#FGGF3032MB-Serial # VF31367295) in May 2013 from a local appliance outlet (PC Richards). It was delivered to my home on May 11, 2013 and installed by the local appliance outlet. It worked until Sunday June 1, 2014, when while using the broiler, the electric key pad and range control melted. There were no items on the stove top. I was only using the broil setting when this occurred. The product has a twelve month warranty which expired on approximately May 11, 2014. I called  Frigidaire and they also said the warranty expired but after listening to my complaint that the electric key pad and range control melted, the tech told me they would authorize the parts to repair it for free but I would have to pay for the service ($152.37) from an authorized repair company that have listed. Finally, today the oven was repaired, for now, but my worry is that this problem may happen again. The vent for the oven is located under the control panel. I have noticed that the vent area gets very hot when using the broil cycle. I believe this is a dangerous problem and a possible product defect. Is there any information on this problem happening with this oven for other owners? I also believe that I should be reimbursed for the service fee and Frigidaire should re-think the placement of the oven vent. I will be more wary of using this product.
justification: The incident involved the melting of the electric key pad and range control, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Left front burner on Kenmore Glass Top Stove heating to extreme high temperature, and not turning off when rotary knob is in off position.   Model  number  790 96029404  is not listed in recall, but exhibiting all the incidents of present Kenmore recalled glass top stoves!  I've burned food, and this is a fire hazard to my home!
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a fire hazard and has already caused burned food, indicating a clear incident with potential for injury or property damage.

incident_description:
An Emeril T-fal pressure cooker was being used to cook soup.  After a loud bang it spewed the contents of the spot out and up.  Soup was on the ceiling which is 15 feet + high.
The person making the soup narrowly escaped injury.  He received hot soup on his face and hands but removed it immediately.  He does not appear to be injured.
It appears that the pressure release valve waited far too long to function and relieve the growing pressure inside the cooker.
justification: The incident involved a pressure cooker malfunction causing hot soup to spew, but the person narrowly escaped injury with no apparent harm.

incident_description: I was putting dishes away and took my Pyrex 2 cup measuring cup out of the cabinet to place into another  larger measuring cup and it exploded.  It was handled very gently and did not simply crack or break normally.  It unnaturally exploded all over the kitchen.  Shards of glass and pieces of glass that looked like crystallized balls flew up into my face.  Thankfully, the pieces did not go into my eyes.
justification: The incident involved an exploding measuring cup with glass shards flying into the face, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My Kenmore 790 series outer glass exploded sending pieces of glass at least 15 feet across the kitchen.  This happened as my wife was opening the door to remove cookies she was baking.  Sears is fortunate she was standing off center of the glass and only sustained minor cuts on her arm or they would be talking to my lawyr.  In researching this topic I see Kenmore has a history of glass shattering events.  It seem something needs to be done because this could result in significant injures.  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts on the arm, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The mention of a history of similar events suggests the likelihood is higher than rare.

incident_description: Soda stream Penguin.  Makes carbonated water.  The glass bottle inside the Soda Stream Penguin model exploded during use.  Water and glass shards were ejected from the containment vessel under high pressure.  Now the vessel is jammed shut, trapping the remaining water and the bulk of the broken glass inside.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and ejection of glass shards, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Toxic smell when first using the oven, had to not cook the thanksgiving turkey in our new oven due to the smell.  The whole extended family agreed to the need to turn off the oven due to the terrible chemical smell (eyes/throat burning).  I had tried several times thereafter, same thing.  So four years later our family still doesn't use the oven (and uses a $100 toaster oven instead if the $2000 frigidaire gallery oven).  There are many reports of this on the Internet.  I never tried to return the product, but feel it should be investigated.  It was bought early 2010.
justification: The incident caused discomfort (eyes/throat burning) but no reported injuries, and the issue persists over time with multiple reports online.

incident_description: This product was purchased at Starbucks in Nov 2013.  On Tuesday, [REDACT], I was using it in the morning to make my coffee at my desk (home office).  I had just filled the press with boiling water when i moved to pour into my coffee cup, across my desk.  It was full.  As i began to pour, the plastic bottom fell off and the glass sleeve (like a beaker) slid out.  The glass beaker fell to my desk, hit the corner and tumbled into my office chair.  My chair is all leather (looks more like a piece of living room furniture) and the contents of the beaker immediately poured into the seat, the one i was sitting on.  I jumped up as quickly as possible, but i was burned badly on my backside.  I jumped into a cold shower (my skin was actually "steaming") to cool down and sat on ice packs for a couple hours before going to the doctor.  The diagnosis was first and second degree burns to my backside (butt and lower back).  I received a prescription for burn cream and pain medication to ease the discomfort.  It not quite a week, but the burn area remains extremely uncomfortable.
justification: The incident resulted in first and second degree burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such product failures leading to injury are not common.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using her pan for about 5 minutes in medium flame frying onions in oil when she noticed a 4 inch gap between the two layers of the pan. Immediately, she notice steam coming from the inside of the gap, the inside bottom part of the pan started to raise or "bubble up". Instantaneously, the contents of the pan where ejected from the pan and scattered around the kitchen. The consumer felt afraid, turned her back to the pan and called for her husband. Her husband removed the pan from the stove and placed it on the floor outside the back entrance of the kitchen. The consumer stated that oil splattered over her back but she was not injured. She discontinued the use of this product.

The consumer plans to contact the manufacturer in the near future.

The consumer believes this product poses an injury hazard, and she is concerned for the safety of the public.

Release #03-069 may be relevant to this report because includes products of similar description exhibiting a similar defect.
justification: The incident involved a pan malfunction causing oil splatter, but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3, as similar defects have been reported, suggesting possible recurrence.

incident_description: Frigidaire Gas oven/stove turned on by itself.   The oven became EXTREMELY hot and since I was not home, ran for an unknown amount of time (up to 3 hours).  House was hot when I returned home, as was the counter and floor around the appliance.  This is a Serious fire hazard!
justification: The incident caused a serious fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased the Farberware Family Size Griddle Model Number G767 yesterday at my local Walmart. The box has a picture of the griddle being placed in  the lower rack of a dishwasher and states it is dishwasher safe. As this is electric, I had my doubts and read the brochure thoroughly. It states not to submerge the griddle in liquid and says the warming tray and drip tray are dishwasher safe. This is very deceiving to the consumer who is. Easily led to believe the griddle is somewhat like the George Foreman and dishwasher safe given the photo on the box and accompanying statement to that effect. If placed in the dishwasher or submerged in water and then plugged in, this could be dangerous
justification: The description highlights a misleading product label that could lead to dangerous misuse, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
A couple of days ago while using the oven on our Kenmore stove, we noticed it was smoking a lot.  We opened the door and it seemed like the temperature was much higher than normal (it was set to 400 degrees) yet the lower element was glowing orange.  We turned off the oven via the control panel, and the display responded as if the oven had been turned off (the temperature display disappeared) but the element kept glowing orange.  Also there's usually a "click" when the oven cycles on or off and we did not hear that when we shut off the oven.

After a couple of minutes, the element was still bright orange and it was obvious that the oven had not actually shut off.  I went downstairs and shut off the circuit breaker for the stove and only then did the element start to cool.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but was safely turned off via the circuit breaker, resulting in no injury or damage.

incident_description: While cooking this evening the LEFT FRONT Burner on my LR30755ST was set to Low after boiling and wold not turn off or lower the heat.  Unplugged the range for safety.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue was mitigated by unplugging the range.

incident_description:
We were baking in the oven of our Kenmore Electric Range when the oven suddenly got extremely hot and would not shut off. Apparently the broiler element came on all by itself and was not controlled by the temperature control. We disconnected the power to the range in order to get it to shut off. Later we tried to reconnect the power, but the broiler element would come on full force while the unit was turned totally off. This is obviously a great fire hazard, and it renders the range completely unusable.
The model is 790.95200102 and serial number is VF20713502.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven that poses a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On Saturday, May 31, I was using my GE Profile dishwasher with the heated cycle.  I was outside working in the yard when I returned to the house, there was a strong odor of something very hot/melting.  We searched the house and came to determine that the dishwasher was so hot that it melted several plastic items on the top rack of the dishwasher.  These items had been washed and dried previously with no problems.  My husband immediately unplugged the dishwasher.  A large plastic bowl melted and is stuck to the top shelf.  A plastic cup is completely melted into the wash spinners, inside the stainless steel tub and the heating element.  On Monday, I looked at the General Electric appliance web site and noted that there was a recall for plastic tub GE profile dishwashers because the heating element overheated and caused damage.  Those dishwashers were made in the same time frame as my dishwasher - 2007.  There was no recall on stainless steel tub GE profile dishwashers which I own.  Therefore I was not notified of any recall.  However, it seems that my heating element overheated as well.  GE has been contacted.  The cabinet and sink near the dishwasher were both very hot when touched as a result of the overheating the dishwasher.
justification: The dishwasher overheated, causing damage to plastic items and making nearby surfaces hot, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The product is Chef'n Pull'n Slice mandoline.  While using the julienne attachment one of the blades fell out of the attachment.  I noticed it when I took the mandoline apart for cleaning.  I started to turn the salad I was making and after a while I found the blade still in tact, so it had not been splintered.  This product is made of plastic, as an added comment, it is made in China and if any product that can go bad, it comes from China.  I  purchased it from Williams-Sonoma about a year ago.  It is made by Chef'n Corporation in Seattle, WA.  Their phone # is 866-642-4336.
I feel that this product should be recalled and redesigned before being allowed to be sold.

If you need the product and pieces, I have them.
justification: The blade fell out but was found intact with no injury reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: While cooking a pork roast in oven, more less around 2 hours into the cooking i decided to flip roast over so it could cook more evenly. As i closed the oven door front window of range exploded outwards sending tempered glass around 10-12 feet in front of oven, fortunately i was standing to a side of it and was home alone.
justification: The oven door exploded, but no one was injured as the person was standing to the side and was alone.

incident_description:
I was sitting in my living room around 9:45 PM watching television when I heard a loud explosion type sound. I ran into the kitchen and the glass on my oven door had imploded and glass was all over the kitchen. The oven was not on and none of the burners were on. I had not used the oven since around 11:00 AM that day. If I had been in the kitchen when this happened I would have been cut by the glass. The range is a Kenmore elite.  I don't understand what caused this, but it is a safety concern. Thank you.

[REDACTED]
justification: The oven glass imploded without injury, but posed a potential injury risk if someone had been nearby.

incident_description:
On October, 2010 you issued a recall notification for a Electrolux Icon Smoothtop cooktop Model Numbers E30EC65ESS and Serial Number Range: NF501XXXXX through NF045XXXXX.  I own a unit with that number and serial number NF61619275.   My unit shows the same issues mentioned in your recall notification: water can enter the control panel and a fire hazard exits.
Two days ago, I turned on one of the coils and seconds later another coil turned itself on without me touching the knob.  I tried turning it off and turned off the one I had turned on while the one which turned itself on kept on and to the maximum heat capacity.  I had to turn off the main circuit breaker to turn the coil off.  An hour later, I turn back on the circuit breaker and the coil turned itself on, a foul smell came out of the unit and an electrical explosion occurred with sparks flying.  I had to turn off the circuit breaker again and unplugged the unit.
Fortunately, I was away from the unit at the circuit breaker panel and received no harm.  The only thing below the unit is a microwave unit which didn't ignite.  I this would have happened with no one home a fire could have had started.
I formally request that the recall be expanded to include latter serial numbers since apparently this problem has not been corrected by the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and electrical explosion, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is high as the issue is known and similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description: I purhased a Model# NE58F9500SS 5.8 cu ft. slide in electric range made by Samsung from The Home Depot in January 2014.  It has a glass top.  On several occasions either my husband or I have accidentally turned on a burner when leaning against the oven. Luckily, we have not had anything on top of the burner when it was started.  However, I am fearful that this could happen and result in a fire.  This oven was a replacement for another glass top oven which we had for almost 20 years.  It is normal for us to set the mail and/or other items on the stove top when it is not in use.  I am reporting this today because my husband accidentally turned on a burner again.
justification: The incident involves accidental burner activation with no injury or damage reported, but poses a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the range came with the house that he purchased in 2005. The consumer believes the unit to be manufactured in 2003/2004.
 
The consumer stated that the front-left burner goes beyond the set heat level. The consumer stated that the burner heats to different temperature than selected. The right burners seem to be operating normally. The consumer stated that the rear-left burner could be overheating but he's not sure.

The consumer spoke to the manf. The manf informed him that he can contact their repairman to schedule an appointment for repair. The consumer did not feel the need to pay the cost for repair on a 9-10 year old unit.
The consumer's model # is not included in recall #09-333 but is having similar hazard.


To whom it may concern:

This letter is an addendum to a report that I sent to the CPSC on September 23, 2013.
For your convenience, I send herewith a copy of that report.
On May 20, 2014, without warning, the burner switch (right rear) on my Frigidaire
smoothtop range malfunctioned in the same fashion as the lower left burner switch that I
reported in September 2013. The Frigidaire burner switch's part number is 316021500.
The Commission has received similar reports from other consumers who own or have
owned Frigidaire smoothtop ranges.
The right rear burner switch, somewhat like the lower left burner switch, went well beyond
the set heat level. I was cooking something on medium heat and monitoring cooking
temperature with a remote thermometer. In no time at all, the right rear burner spontaneously
went from medium to high heat. I turned off my range and shut off its circuit
breaker. Although I have other ways to cook, my range's burner switches are an understandable
cause for concern. Are these burner switches on all Frigidaire smoothtop
ranges? Should these burner switches be recalled and replaced free of charge with a
safer burner switch (possibly part number 316463000) instead of the ranges on which
they were originally installed? When these burner switches malfunction, why don't they
shut off instead of overheat?
If you or Frigidaire should need more information, please let me know. Thank you very
much for your help.
Very sincerely yours,
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that overheats beyond the set level, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: While my family and I were sleeping we awoke to the fire alarms in my home ringing.  As we went down stairs and approached the kitchen we saw smoke billowing out of our Kenmore range (model: 95822002, serial Number RL2013064).  Upon further investigation we saw that the broiler turned on all by itself during the night. We attempted to turn off the range using the off button on the range with no result.   We ran to the circuit breakers in our home and threw the switch for the stove/oven which finally turned off the range.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that produced smoke but resulted in no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had cold vegetables inside of the fruit bowl , covered with cling wrap and placed the fruit bowl in the refrigerator. After 12 hours, the consumer noticed that the fruit bowl had broken in three horizontal pieces. She removed the fruit bowl from the refrigerator, discarded the food and stored the broken fruit bowl.

The consumer plans to contact the manufacturer in the near future. She stated that in previous occasions her husband has tried to contact the manufacturer and has not been successful.

The consumer thinks this product poses an injury hazard.
justification: The incident involved a broken fruit bowl but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as rare (1) since no injury occurred and the issue seems isolated.

incident_description:
This caller purchased her electric smooth top range 2000/2001 and had no problems with it until 
The beginning of February 2014 it began continuously heating to higher temperatures than set at, callers could not turn off.
The caller and her husband unplugged the range and tripped breaker off.
The caller's husband flipped the breaker back on after approximately one hour but the range continued heating and being unable to be turned off.
He contacted the manufacturer the same day, tech came out February 12th, 2014 then returned on February 27th, 2014 and "repaired" the unit.

May 8th, 2014 the caller took her daughter to school, returned 15 minutes later and when she opened her door she felt heat, heard beeping, walked into the kitchen and saw that the range was flashing "F1".
The entire range was really hot.
She noticed that the oven was on but no one had used the oven this morning or the night before.
She pushed "off" and the signal went to clock, the beeping stopped and all seemed alright.
Within just a few moments while she stood there all beeping, error codes etc. began again.
She could touch the handle but could not touch the range anywhere because of the heat.
The oven element was blazing red.
The caller turned the breaker off and has left it off.

She contacted the manufacturer today (May 8th, 2014), she was advised that they will send a tech to 'assess the situation'.
The caller is afraid to trust this because they did just "repair" the range.
She is reporting as a fire safety hazard and is asking that this range become recalled with assistance to purchase a new range at manufacturer expense or if she has already replaced it due to fear of fire hazard she is asking to be reimbursed at manufacturer expense.

There are no injuries being reported
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning range posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:

This is to inform about a fire that occurred Saturday May 17 2014, in our 2008 Frigidaire refrigerator. As we sat drinking
coffee in the morning, a popping, cracking sound emanated from the bottom of the appliance. This was followed by
intense smoke which filled the house. We quickly unplugged it and, opened windows venting the house. Had we not been
there,( we just got back from a all day trip) our house may have burned and our dog would surly have died! The pic is
where the problem was and you can see scorching on the wiring harness. The following are the empirical info.

Model # FRS6R5ESBE
SERIAL # 4A71605272
LOT # 00016572
justification: The incident involved a fire in a refrigerator that produced intense smoke but no injuries or deaths, and the situation was controlled without further damage.

incident_description: kirkland 6 qt. deep saute pan with glass lid.  washed the glass lid in the dishwasher  on regular cycle no sani wash or extra heat.  air dry. i went to remove something next to it and it exploded!! BOOM! glass went everywhere with in a good 5 feet! i had it in the dish washer, on the counter, the floor,  on the open dishwasher door. my legs and feet where covered in tiny shards that i could hardly see.  when i went to dust them off it cut me ans i started to bleed.  quite a mess!  my husband is a window glass contractor and was shocked! it happened over memorial weekend so i will call costco on Tuesday.  i dont expect a problem but would have like to avoided this all together as it could have hurt some one. my dog was close by and he would have gotten glass in his eyes! im  still finding pieces!
justification: The incident resulted in minor injury (cuts from glass shards) but no severe harm or death, and similar incidents are unlikely to occur frequently.

incident_description: Toasted waffle in toaster oven; left the kitchen for a few minutes and when went back into kitchen the toaster oven was smoking and was on fire.
justification: The toaster oven caught fire, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Courant 1.7 Liter Stainless Steel Cordless Electric Kettle. I've used electric kettles in the past and noticed this one behaves differently with the auto shutoff feature. There are two flaws with the design: 

1. when the kettle it removed from the base while it is still heating it does not trip the auto shutoff. If you then empty the kettle and put it back on the base it is still turned on. 

2. The boil dry auto shutoff does not seem to work correctly. It turns the unit off with a click but the switch seems to be in the middle (ie not completely off) and seems to cycle between off and back on again. The result is the kettle gets hot, though not hot enough to cause a fire.
justification: The kettle's auto shutoff flaws could lead to overheating but no injury is reported, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
May 19th, 2014 the caller's dishwasher had been running for about thirty minutes when they heard a loud pop, flames began shooting out the top of the door along with black smoke pouring out of the vents in the door.

He could smell electrical burning.

The caller opened the door, observed that there was no fire inside the dishwasher but was still in the door.

He ran to grab the fire extinguisher, came back then noted that the fire appeared to be subsiding on it's own.

There are no injuries being reported 

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer and does not intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Range.  One oven rack began falling a few years ago and now all the racks fall even with very little weight on them.  I assumed this was from the racks wearing out and I did a web search looking for replacement racks.  I came across this from the Sears web-site.
https://www.sears.com/community/questions/the-oven-racks-in-kenmore-elite-model-79031043302-fall-down-and-have-caused-burns/#comment-42634

Clearly this is an oven design flaw that Sears is aware of.  Despite this potentially dangerous flaw they now only have not recalled these ovens, but the take no responsibility for helping consumers remedy this issue. 
I guess they are satisfied waiting for someone to sustain burns and contacting their lawyer.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw causing oven racks to fall, which could lead to burns, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I turned on the oven of my range by setting a temperature of 350 degrees. After a couple of minutes, the control module of the range started to pop and the orange LED display started cycling wildly, creating a flashing effect. Black smoke pored out of the back of the stove behind the module. Flames appeared briefly--a few inches above the top of the back of the stove. The flames lasted for a few seconds and then extinguished themselves. There was a strong, acrid smell from the smoke.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she has been experiencing problems with her electric range since purchase.  The left rear burner stays on and will not power off.  Approximately 6 years she had call the fire department because of the failure of the burner.  It took about 45 mins to finally power it off. The oven at times stays on, heats to higher temperature and emits smoke whenever it is being used and this has been  on going since purchase. She stated that lately there is a liquid that is leaking from the rear right top of the oven to bottom surface of the unit which appears black. 
(2009) She contacted the manufacturer right after purchase and notified them of the problem but she did not receive any assistance. At times when she had called they advised her that there would be a charge for someone to come out and look at the unit.
Caller feels that she is experiencing similar problems of Release#09-333.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

Caller feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

Delivered 04-15-2008 10:30 AM
justification: The electric range poses a fire and burn hazard, with ongoing issues since purchase, including a past fire department call, but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his electric range in 2000 and has never had to have repair for it.

May 17th, 2014 the caller had preheated his oven at 350 degrees, according to directions he cooked his preprepared food item for one hour, then took it out to remove cover and placed it back in the oven planning for another twenty minutes.
He stepped outside for just a moment but when he stepped back into the kitchen he noted that there was black smoke coming out of the bottom of the oven door.
The caller took the food out of the oven and saw that the food in just those few moments had become charred and blackened.
He attempted to turn the range off using the buttons but was unsuccessful.
He turned the range off via the breaker.

There are no injuries being reported

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involved smoke and charred food but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common with properly maintained appliances.

incident_description: My Mr Coffee (Sunbeam URTX 85 V098SX) coffee maker started by itself when I was using a coffee grinder that was plugged into the same outlet.  After the coffee was done brewing, the coffee make did not shut off.  I smelled smoke (electrical fire smell).  Smoke was coming from the lower back side of the coffee maker.  I unplugged and threw it outside.  If I wasn't there, I am concerned that this could have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kohl's drinking glass shattered with liquid inside, while attempting to drink. Cuts sustained. Despite extensive communication with Kohl's and more glasses shattering, they refuse to remove them from store shelves or issue a recalL Upon more digging, I found customer online reviews of broken glasses posted months before my purchase. It's nine months later and they are still for sale online and stocked in my local store. All comments I attempt to attach to my review on the Kohl's website to warn other consumers are repeatedly blocked and returned via email from their customer service. As of today 5/07/2014, no corrective action has been taken by Kohl's.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts, indicating an injury, and there are multiple reports of similar incidents with no corrective action taken.

incident_description:
Slipped and fell on large area of water from fridge.  Jammed wrist.  fridge has consistently leaked for over a year.  whirlpool issued a part to correct the issue.  however, the consumer must pay for the part of pay $100+ for installation.  communicated w/ whirlpool today re: this issue and was told to pay for the part myself.  this is a common problem
whirlpool gold # GB9FHDXWB02
some other citations of this issue:

incident_description: Kitchen Aid 2 Cup Measuring Cup exploded on 20 degree F drop in Temperature (70 degree F => 50 degree F) Moving from Kitchen to Garage.
justification: The measuring cup exploded due to a temperature drop, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Dishwasher Model number 665.16264401.  I started the dishwasher and about 35 minutes into the cycle I smelt something burning.  I went into kitchen and white smoke was coming from the control panel of the dishwasher.  I opened the door which normally stops it and it kept washing and spraying water.  I closed the door and black smoke started to come out, I then ran to the breaker to turn it off.  I turned the breaker back on and it started up again.  I had to unhook the electricity to the dishwasher.  The front panel was very hot and front was starting to melt.  Glad I was home or the house would of been on fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore electric range model # 790.9611340A. Left front burner of stove would not turn off after using to cook. Burner also would become hotter than the setting it was placed on (i.e. set on med but was extremely hot. This has happened a couple of times (eventually it would turn off) the stove had to be unplugged this time because it would not turn off.
justification: The burner malfunctioned and became excessively hot, requiring unplugging, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:

can possible cause someone to get burned. Also hot liquids could spill.
The consumer stated that the cook top was replaced, but the issue is still the same.

(05/02/2014) The cook top was replaced. The symptoms were the same as the original cook top.
Whirlpool set up a service call with Appliance Hospital to come out and inspect the stove on 5/7/2014. 

(05/05/2014) The consumer contacted Home Depot. She spoke with [REDACTED]. A copy of the Reliable Appliance repair statement was faxed to her. 
The consumer received a call from [REDACTED] advising her to come in for a refund to pick out a new stove top.

incident_description:
Microwave oven caught fire.  Being used for only 10 seconds and a pop was heard, I turned back and saw the fire thru the window.  Immediately shut off, some smoke was still coming out so immediately unplugged.  The model # MH1150XMS-3.  The fire appears to have come out of the opening where the plastic hook is for holding the rack.  It does not appear to have come from food or dish, etc.   thankfully, I was still in kitchen when this happened, I had only made it 3 steps away when I heard the pop and turned back and saw the fire.  Called whirlpool and after a long wait and aggravating conversation with a "safety supervisor" as she described herself, stated they would send a repair man out but I would be responsible for cost of parts to repair......  I simply want someone to know that this product is dangerous.  

If any questions, I can be reached at [REDACTED] or [REDACTED]

Thank you.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was quickly controlled without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description:
(04/2013) The consumer stated that she sets the burners on medium to high. The burners get hotter and hotter on it own. The consumer stated that she has to keep turning the burners down.This happens all of the time with all of the burners.


To whom it may concern,
Gentlemen, the consumerÃÂs name is [REDACTED] and she is writing concerning a General Electric range stove purchased in July of 2009.The stove has not worked right from the time it was purchased and had gotten so bad she recently had to call a repairman to come out and check things out. [REDACTED]

incident_description: GE Microwave, Model:JVM1540DP1WW, manufactured: August 2010.   Began turning itself on by itself, could press stop button, but would not make it stop and had to open the door.   Upon closing the door, the keypad then worked, but it would turn itself on again after a few seconds without being touched.  Had to unplug it to make it stop.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
HOTPOINT (General Electric) 24" Compact Gas Range
Model No.  RGA724PKWH;    Serial No.  FS101454A
Date of Mfg.  Unknown (2009 est.)  
Purchased and Installed.  July 2009

Gas leak in oven pilot circuit.  Joint between pilot gas feeder line and pilot assembly leaks.
  Design and/or Manufacturing issue will not allow full tightening between the feeder line and the pilot assembly resulting in a continuous gas leak.
  This condition creates a potential explosion hazard and health risk.
  Manufacturer's part number for pilot assembly is WB19K10023

Note.  Problem believed to exist from inception but just noticed.  Range only used during summer months at remote California Wilderness location.
justification: Gas leak poses a potential explosion hazard and health risk, but no incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
In a 3 day span, our GE Microwave Oven, model #JVM1540SN1SS, purchased in 2009, turned on by itself without any touch.  We tried unplugging and plugging back in the microwave and it worked fine for around 45 minutes.  At that time, it set itself and turned on for 1 minute cooking on high.  We were in the other room and heard it come on.  We hit cancel on the keypad, left it was nothing showing on the keypad and it turned itself back on within 15 minutes, again for 1 minute.    AFter that we unplugged the microwave and left it unplugged unless cooking with it.  

Contacted GE who stated it sounded like a faulty keypad and wants to charge me $300.00 to fix.  I have video of it starting on its own 3 times in 15 seconds after I have manually turned it off using the keypad.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was taking the bottom glass shelf out of the refrigerator to wipe it off, when it literally exploded in my hands...glass shards everywhere. I live in Hawaii so you go barefoot in the house. My foot is cut, my fingers are cut, and can feel shards of glass in my fingers. Sears needs to do something about this since I just read many other complaints on this very same issue.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts and embedded glass shards, indicating an injury without death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that this was the first time he was using the casserole dish.

The consumer stated that the glass lid on the casserole dish exploded.

The consumer stated that his wife put the dish in the microwave for about 2 minutes or so, to heat up food.

The consumer stated that the glass lid exploded before the microwave time stopped. The consumer stated that the lid exploded into various size pieces (between 0.5 inch to microscopic)

The consumer stated that his wife cut her left hand finger. The consumer stated that the cut was about 1/4-1/2 inch. 

The consumer contacted the the corporate office for the retailer. The consumer was informed that they can provide him $25 credit. The consumer did not take the offer and felt that the retailer did not take into consideration the safety hazard. 

The consumer stated that he is not going to continue using his microwave. The consumer stated that there could be small glass pieces that.
justification: The consumer's wife suffered a cut on her finger from the exploding glass lid, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
(04/26/2014) The consumer stated that she heard a crackling noise but could not locate it. She smelled something burning. Her husband went down to check the circuit breaker and discovered that the breaker was off. He flipped the breaker. Smoke started coming out of the handle of the dishwasher and the vent of the dishwasher. The dishwasher was not is use. The consumer unplugged and disconnected the dishwasher. Also,the circuit board was was melted. 

(04/28/2014) The consumer called the manufacturer to tell them about the fire but wanted to get information on the parts. The consumer was not given any information. 

The manufacturer offerd to send someone out to look at the product.

The consumer's dishwasher is still not working even though Whirlpool has sent a repairman 3 times.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a melted circuit board but no injuries or deaths, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description: We have a Whirlpool Gas Range Model# WFG710HOAS, Serial # R21611731. I heated it to 450ÃÂº and while I was baking, I was also cooking on top of the stove and needed to get a lid out of the storage drawer. I actually dropped the lid as it was as hot as the oven and that should not be. I am just  thankful I didn't ask my granddaughter to get the lid for me. When you look In the drawer you can see  the flame from the oven and it needs to have something between the oven and the drawer to prevent this happening. What If a paper towel or pot holder had been in that drawer,we could be dead from a fire. We contacted Whirlpool with no results. Just their standard answer. Have you ever checked the temp.in the storage drawer of an oven? If it was the a broiler I would understand, but this is simply a storage drawer.Something has to be done about this, it is dangerous and a fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with potential for injury or fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I had set my Whirlpool Gas Range Oven (model# WFG114SWB0) to 350 degrees. While preparing food, the door glass exploded all of sudden, spilling hot glass on my feet and floor. There was no food in the oven, and no apparent reason for the glass exploding.
justification: The incident resulted in injury due to hot glass spilling on feet, but such occurrences are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: Our refrigerator caught on fire last night. After finally figuring out what was burning in our kitchen we saw a fire under the refrigerator.  We quickly unplugged it and removed the back grill, cleaned the area out and discovered the fire came from the capacitor. After researching the products online we discovered similar issues with other refrigerators, however, ours was not on your recall list. I think it  should be and will you assist me with this issue?
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he retrieve the precision induction cooktop  from the mailing package, he placed it on a countertop next to his stove. Immediately, when he plugged the power supply to the wall socket he noticed sparks emanating from the wall socket. The sparks stopped almost immediately and he proceeded to use the product. He did not noticed any sparks during or after use.

At a later date he placed his precision induction cooktop on a counter top next to his refrigerator. Immediately, when he plugged the power supply to the wall socket he noticed sparks emanating from the wall socket. The sparks stopped almost immediately and he proceeded to use the product. He did not noticed any sparks during or after use.

4/28/14- The consumer contacted the manufacturer. The consumer made the company aware of the incidents. The customer service representative informed the consumer that they would send a replacement and a mailing package in order for him to return the defective item.

5/5/2014- The consumer contacted the manufacturer. He inquired about the status of the replacement cooktop. The customer service representative inform the consumer that no replacement will be mailed and that the sparking is part of the normal function of the product.

The consumer contacted the CPSC because he thinks this product poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved sparks but no injury or fire, and the product was used without further issues.

incident_description: Purchased Calphalon Coffee Maker Model HE121CMG at Bed Bath and Beyond October 2013 and on May 19, 2014 I heard an odd rattling noise coming from kitchen.  I noticed that the glass coffee pot was shaking and the coffee in the pot was boiling.  Within seconds smoke starting coming from the coffee maker and it smelled of burning rubber.  I quickly unplugged the coffee maker from the electrical outlet.  Smoke continued to emit from the maker and it was so hot that I needed a pot holder to lift it.  The coffee maker appeared to have caught fire inside.  If I had not been in the next room I suspect that it would have burned my counter and possibly started an electrical fire in my home.  I attempted to return it to Bed Bath and Beyond with an explanation as to why.  They stated to me that the product had been discontinued, but not recalled.  This seemed very suspicious to me so I called CPSC and they told me of other similar reports.  I hope this my report is helpful and that Calphalon recalls this coffee maker as it is a serious danger to any consumer that buys it!!!
justification: The coffee maker emitted smoke and nearly caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
During the last 4 or 5 loads in the dishwasher we thought we could smell something burning like an electrical fire.  At first we thought it was something in the washer itself but could not pinpoint anything. When the dishwasher stopped working completely (May 12, 2014) we found that the power connection from the household wiring had melted at the connector block on the dishwasher. The block itself was melted as well and thankfully one wire broke or melted to the point it was no longer making a connection, which is probably what saved a fire. That wire had also melted into the romex towards the interior of the wall. At no time did a circuit breaker trip. We contacted Bosch and Loews, where we purchased the unit from in August of 2008. Loews contractor installed the unit on August 13, 2008.

Bosch sent out a technician and stated he believed the screw connecting the wire to the block was stripped or loose and that's what caused the high resistance and subsequent damage. Bosch then called to advise that this was an installer problem not a defect with the machine. We have not heard from Loews since the store contact with the installation manager about 2 weeks ago.
justification: The incident involved a potential electrical fire hazard but resulted in no injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description: Last night I was awoke to a buzzing sound, thinking it was one of my child's toys, I wandered around the house until I entered the kitchen.  The buzzing was coming from my toaster, at the time I walked into the kitchen, the smoke detector goes off.  Smoke was rolling out of the toaster, I tried to make sure it was not pushed down in use, and it wasn't, the buzzing and smoke continued.  I unplugged it from the wall and the buzzing stopped.  The toaster was NOT in use.  It had not been used since three days prior to last night.  The toaster is a Back To Basics TEM 500 brand toaster with poached egg attachment.  I have contacted the company Westbend this morning as well.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toaster causing smoke and a buzzing sound, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was standing in the dining room visiting with my family when suddenly my oven door exploded. There were tiny pieces of glass everywhere that continued to pop after the initial shatter. Some of the shards were as fine as powder. We had not used the oven in over 24 hours. We were no where near the oven when this occurs nor had we dropped anything on it, hit it, or slammed it. We are very gentle with our appliances and are baffled as to why this happened out of no where.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a sudden and unexpected event that could have caused injury if someone was near the oven.

incident_description: Was warming up some food in the microwave, then there was a loud explosion noise that came from the microwave followed by sparks and flame coming from the top vent of the microwave. I took the microwave down from above the stove and there was Charing on the cabinet from the flames. I called Samsung they sent out a repair man to look at the microwave. The high voltage capacitor blew up. Samsung is not taking this issue serious, as this could have burn down our house. They said it's out of warranty, and could be repaired, and they want me to pay for it. I am more concern if this is a bigger problem that is effecting more microwaves that are being used by other consumers,were this defect could kill someone or burn their house down...after taking the cover off my self I notice that the small explosion cracked the plastic support holding the mounting screw and also the transformer connections were also burnt.
justification: The incident involved a microwave explosion and flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The likelihood is unlikely as such severe malfunctions are not common.

incident_description: On or about April 13, 2014, our Krups Stainless Steel Karafe coffee maker began to refuse to shut off the heating element necessitating that we unplug it to keep the hazard of fire from becoming a reality.  The Model number is MTE12110000; type 229; SN F2294G56/860-01094.
justification: The coffee maker's failure to shut off poses a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I was running my dishwasher when it just quit and smoke started coming out of the vent and I smelled a hot burning wire smell. I went to open the latch and hot smoke burned my hand.
justification: Hot smoke burned the person's hand, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: This product is the Electrolux stove model ew30ef65gsh. I had the stove temp set to 250 on oven bake. Intermittantly the entire circuit display would flash showing an error code f20 in the clock area. When I would open the oven door the flashing would stop and when I closed it again all the icons on the display would light up. I turned off the oven and waited a few minutes and turned it back on. The same events repeated itself 3 times within an hour. I looked on line for the error code and it said to unplug the stove and wait 5 minutes and re-plug it in. When I pulled out the stove the junction box where the stove was plugged in was partially melted and the plug burning hot.  About 2 years ago I had a similar incident with the same stove but a different error code and Electrolux replaced the circuit boards in the oven.  I believe this could have caused a fire had I not pulled out the stove and continued to try and use it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove with a melted junction box and hot plug, posing a significant fire hazard and potential for injury.

incident_description: Rear large burner  on our electric smooth top range  model # fec30s6abf serial #nf71121540 will not turn off. It will go to lowest setting sometimes but is usually on the highest setting. It also just turns on by itself. It has come on and I smelled something getting very hot and found the burner on high heat and a pan getting extremely hot. I've had to resort to turning it off at the circuit breaker due to the fact that it turns on by itself randomly.
justification: The burner turning on by itself and reaching high heat poses a significant risk of injury or fire, though no injury is reported yet.

incident_description: Frigidaire cooktop  model number FPEC3085KSA was purchased June 2011. Smoldered and smoked until turned off at breaker in December 2012. Frigidaire denied there was a problem but after multiple complaints agreed to completely repair unit at no cost. Today, 5/26/14, it almost caught fire again, smoking until it was turned off at breaker. In both instances the unit failed to turn off, or turned itself back on, after the knob was turned to off.
justification: The incident caused smoke and smoke, but no injury, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 because the incident occurred twice in 3 years.

While using Cuisinart Electric cordless kettle I found that an insulated (fiber wrapped) wire in the base started to melt through the plastic base.

Model # KUA-17
sn 61215C
justification: The incident involved a melting wire but no injury was reported, indicating a non-injury incident with possible likelihood given the described malfunction.

incident_description: Bought a GE profile gas range,( model PGS968SEPSS) had it less than a month when it caught on fire. The first time we turned on broiler flames were noted in the oven and then thick black smoke came pouring out quickly filling up my kitchen and adjacent room. The fire dept was called and they felt it may have been a failure in the fan motor , they advised me not to use the stove and turned off the gas to it. When checked the next day by serviceman he felt there was some plastic that burned. Not sure what the cause but frightening experience.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no reported injuries, and such failures are uncommon based on the description.

incident_description: On March 29th, 2014, I was baking fish in a Pyrex dish in the oven, like I have always done.  I opened the oven door and added water and the dish exploded into a thousand pieces, hitting me in the face & eyes with glass & hot water. I went to Wiregrass Medical center in Geneva, Al, where I live, and saw dr. [REDACTED] who was the Emergency room doctor.  My eyes were dilated & washed out & I was dismissed.  I was told to see my ophthalmologist who is [REDACTED] at eye center South, Dothan, Al.  I saw Dr. [REDACTED] on March 31st and he removed a piece of glass from my right eye and said that I had a cut in my left eye on the eyeball.  He prescribed an antibiotic cream that I used for several days to heal my left eye. I was in pain during this time. I have used Pyrex products for over fifty years but will never use them again.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring medical attention, including glass removal from the eye and a cut on the eyeball, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the user's long history of using Pyrex without prior incidents.

incident_description:
Product: Viking electric 27" double wall oven.
Install: professionally installed by a local appliance store where it was purchased. A certified Viking dealer.
Age of unit: 6-7 months. Originally installed November of 2013 around thanksgiving.
Home: Built in 1993. No changes in electrical wiring, updates, etc.
Weather: perfect, 80 degrees, clear sky.
Day and time: Wednesday May 14th, 2014 at 5p.m.
Prior issues with the unit: bad convection fan and bad main control panel upon within 1-2 days after initial installation.
Details: around 5p.m. both the upper and lower oven were turned on. They were both set to bake. The upper was set to 350 degrees and the lower to 400 degrees. After coming up to temperature for 10 minutes there was a loud sound consistent with a blown bulb but much much louder. This was followed immediately by the unmistakable smell of an electrical fire. Flames could be seen within the unit where the cooling vents are located between the upper and lower oven. Fire department called. Fire put out and the unit unplugged. Local appliance store contacted. Viking contacted. Awaiting response. Unit still in place. Any additional damage to the cabinet unknown at this time.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with visible flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was baking and the stove beeped like it was completed. I went to take out cabbage and it was burnt on top and had only been in the oven for 5 minutes. I turned the stove off and took out the cabbage and threw it away I came  back to check on the stove  and it was still glowing from the broilers even after it was turned off. I flipped the breaker and waited till it had cooled down and then flipped the breaker back on. After a few minutes went back into kitchen to check stove and the broiler was glowing again even though it was showing off as before. turned breaker back off and unplugged
justification: The stove was glowing even after it was turned off, which could have caused a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Black and Decker Toaster Oven has faulty timer switch. Stopped working. Opened it up and found switch overheated and melted near where the wires are attached. Could easily have broken free and became and electrocution hazard by touching nearby metal body of toaster. Unacceptable.
justification: The faulty timer switch could have caused an electrocution hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The knobs of my gas range have broken. I have switched them around to be able to use the most used burners but they all have broken now.  Now I have to turn the burners off without the knobs. When I was using the stovetop the other night, I thought I had turned off a burner but it remained on, at a very low setting. Had I not turned off the room  lights  immediately after, I would not have noticed it on and would have left the burner on indefinitely. LG will replace defective knobs for other models but refuses to replace for my model, LRG39355st.  They gave me a parts distributor that quoted $63 per knob (with 5 knobs, that would be over $300, might as well buy a new range that works). I cannot afford either at this point so I will have to do without a stovetop for now.

incident_description:
I purchased a Breville Compact Smart Oven model BOV650XL approximately 2 years ago at a local Bed Bath and Beyond.    
Recently the upper heating elements stopped working.  I searched the internet and found reading Amazon reviews other owners reported their ovens also had heating element issues.  Some people fixed the problem by ordering new elements and replacing them.  Being a handy person I ordered new top elements.  When they arrived I took my oven apart.  I found a spade (for the top element) that should be soldered into the PCB was completely loose and it fell out.  The area around the circuit board was burnt from excess heat. I documented it with photos which I have included.  This is a manufacturing defect and quite possibly could have caused a fire in my home.    
I contacted Breville customer service USA in Torrance CA.  I was admonished for opening up the oven and told the unit is out of warranty.  They offered to give me 40% off the purchase of a new unit.  I told them I wasn't interested in buying another Breville appliance.
justification: The incident involved a manufacturing defect that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Product: Kenmore French Door Bottom Freezer Refrigerator
Model: 253.70319
The fan that moves cold air from the freezer to the refrigerator (possibly the evaporator fan?) stops working for several weeks at a time.  Consequently, the temperature in the refrigerator stays around 45-48F, well above the safe zone for cold food storage.  From reading online reviews, this is a widespread problem with this fridge (and with similar models 70312 and 70313), caused by a poorly designed evaporator housing that is prone to accumulating frost that causes the fan to bind up and stop working.
It's commonly reported as a failure of the ice maker, because the airflow passes through the ice maker and then into the fridge, and when the fan fails, the ice maker doesn't get cold enough.  But the major safety issue is that when the fan fails, the fridge doesn't stay cold enough either.
justification: The incident involves a refrigerator not maintaining safe temperatures, posing a risk to food safety but no direct injury or death.

incident_description:
I will detail three major issues with the Maytag Microwave/Hood model MMV5208WS1 that are design flaws. 

1. The unit was designed with a plastic panel beneath the door. This panel has melted once already while the unit was under warranty and has started to deform again. The unit is professionally installed and a Maytag warranty repairman confirmed it was installed in accordance with the provided installation guidelines and specifications. The inclusion of plastic as the surface most directly in proximity to the stovetop below the hood is the problem. The design of a critical safety part like a sealing door for a microwave oven is a big responsibility.

2. More recently, the unit initiated its automatic vent fan and shot the upper vent panel off at a high velocity. This metal and plastic object struck my girlfriend in the forehead and caused bodily injury. Upon inspection of this part, it was apparent that another design flaw contributed to the failure of the vent panel. This large and weighty piece of hardware was affixed via plastic tabs and two small screws. The tabs holding the screws appear to have sheared off due to the stress caused by the moving air passing through the part.

3. Once the upper vent panel of the unit became detached from the unit itself, I am able to see other deteriorating and failing screw connections, which appear to conceal dangerous electronics contained within the unit. Note that the warning labels on the unit are in Spanish only, a clear violation of the ANSI Z535.4 standard. I fear that the other failing screw connections within this unit may cause a catastrophic failure involving the exposure of internal parts.
justification: The incident resulted in bodily injury when the vent panel struck the user's girlfriend, and there are multiple design flaws indicating potential for further incidents.

incident_description:
On March 31, 2014 the outer glass from the upper oven door on our Jenn Air Model JJW9630 double oven exploded with such a force that glass shards were found on top of counter tops over 8-feet away. Glass everywhere! The noise was very loud, like a car wreck. Fortunately my wife and I were out of the room at the time so no one was injured, but if anyone happened to be in the kitchen when it exploded, they would have been hit with a rain of glass shards, causing lacerations from head to toe. Although the oven is 15 years old, it was used very sparsely during the first 11 years as we lived full ÃÂtime in another state. I contacted Whirlpool (Jenn-Air) and spoke to their Safety Department about the explosion. They just shrugged it off and said that this sometimes happens with tempered glass. SOMETIMES HAPPENS...I can understand broken or cracked glass, but not an explosion. I donÃÂt buy that! 
I wonder how often has it happened? How many people have been hurt? Have there been any fatalities? I mean, this is a serious situation that needs to be addressed. I don't care how old an appliance is, it shouldn't explode...never! Cracked or broken glass I understand, but EXPLOSION goes a whole different route.

Now here's the kicker...I have the original manual, and nowhere in it does it talk about the dangers of tempered glass or explosions. There is no mention whatsoever in the 2-page "Important Safety Instructions" section. In fact, the only safety-related reference to the oven door is a single sentence at the bottom of page 20, in the "Maintenance" section where it states, "Scratching, hitting, jarring or stressing the glass may weaken its structure causing an increased risk of breakage at a later date." Nothing is again mentioned about the danger of explosions. I think this is clearly a situation that needs to be addressed.
After talking with Jenn-AirÃÂs Safety Department, they offered me a 15% discount on the purchase of a new ovenÃÂwhoopee! I can get a better deal at any appliance sale. And they told me to make sure to unplug my oven in case there is a problem, so we canÃÂt even use the ÃÂgoodÃÂ lower oven for cooking. They did send an independent service company to check it out but he just looked at it and wrote on his report that the "outer glass on upper door blew out". What they didn't do was to ask for the photos, which I told them I had, and take back the oven for inspection and testing to see if there were any defects.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the oven door glass causing significant damage but no injuries, as the occupants were not in the room at the time.

Shortly after moving into a rental townhome in November, 2007, I surprisingly discovered the range burners on the right hand side of an approximately two year old stove automatically switched to high heat while cooking. I stopped using those burners; left side burners worked sufficiently.

Yesterday after heating dinner for fifteen minutes at 400 degrees (timed to add additional food), I opened the oven door to discover a very bright white light burning on the bottom coil. I turned the oven off, but the light continued to crawl along the coil getting brighter as it moved. I called the non-emergency fire department number and was told to call 911 and get out of the house. Before evacuating, I opened the door to extremely hot air and a larger, brighter light.

A few minutes later, when a fire fighter opened the oven door, the bright white light was gone but the short remaining undamaged coil was bright red. The fire department scanner showed a very high heat in the oven and wall behind and commented on the white residue under the coil. They unplugged the stove and declared the stove unusable. 

Today I did a search on "oven heating coil fires" and was shocked to find numerous complaints dating back from 2007 to present all related to Kenmore stoves, describing my experience and some much more damaging to property. One post from an engineer stated the foreign produced Kenmore stoves do not have a circuit protection built in. 

Why should my landlord have to purchase a new stove due to an obvious defect and more importantly, why has the CPSC not required a recall on this dangerous product?
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction of an oven, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I turned the self cleaning oven feature on for the first time on the top oven and let it cycle. After a couple of hours, it had finished it's cleaning cycle I checked the control panel and all seemed well and went to bed.
When I got up in the morning, I walked by the stove and discovered that the control panel plastic face had melted, and found that the control panel buttons were un-responsive. I killed the power to reset the stove, and found that the control panel was flashing an error code indicating that the keypad was shorted. 
Guess I was lucky the stove hadn't caught fire in the night while I was sleeping.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted control panel) but no injury or death, and the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the description.

incident_description: Bought a new Maytag double oven to replace my 7 year old one. Went to perform the self clean for the first time on the top oven and after about 40 minutes I could smell an odor and investigated. I found the cabinet drawers next to the oven starting to melt/burn and stopped the cycle right away. I don't know what would have happened if I let it continue and I will not use that feature now. Even when I use the oven for cooking it seems to be really hot around the edges. I contacted Maytag and they sent a tech to check the oven. The tech said everything was operating properly and I should pull the oven out to self clean in the future, because they are making them to be hotter than ever for cleaning. NOTE- I never had a problem with my [REDACTED] oven when I did a self clean. It was mentioned that my laminate cabinets were to blame, because they are not UL rated. I contacted the cabinet maker and the cabinets comply with the ANSI/KCMA A161.1-2000. They also said that the appliance manufacturers are making the self clean ovens too hot. I feel this is a real concern for those that have this type of oven because who knows what would have happened if I was not right there. The Maytag safety supervisor ([REDACTED]) contacted us only to tell us that "we should have asked Lowes if the oven is ok to use with laminate cabinets before we bought it"!  I looked in the manual and there is nothing about laminate cabinets in it and when I mentioned that to the safety supervisor ([REDACTED]) she said "We will have to add that to future manuals".  Also, it is well within the clearance margins set by the installation manual.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melting/burning cabinets) but no injury or death, and the likelihood is considered possible given the described conditions and manufacturer's response.
