incident_description: Turned on dishwasher about 7:30 for a normal wash cycle with no heated dry. About an hour later, smelled something burning. Traced it back to the dishwasher - cut power and opened noticing the heating element was on (despite no heated dry) and very hot. The heat element was popping/sizzling. If we had not been home to notice the smell this could have resulted in a home fire. My dishwasher model type was recalled by not my specific dishwasher (serial number not one of the ones recalled). Given the similar sounding nature of our incident with the recall, it makes me suspicious that it's the same problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the issue was caught in time and similar incidents are not common.

incident_description:
GE Microwave Oven Model JVM1540DP1WW, Mfg JAN 2010 was found in alarm mode by son who unplugged it.
Later investigation revealed that the unit would turn on by itself starting a 1 minute Express Cook cycle which the CLEAR/OFF button could not stop. The magnetron was functioning and did heat the cup of water placed in the oven for safety reasons.
My concern is that this could have happened with no one present (or sleeping) and could have started a fire.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
I purchased a Cuisinart Toaster/Broiler Oven. Model TOB-40, Serial Number 30802.  It was purchased online from Amazon.com though it was provided to them directly from Cuisinart.  Purchased 12/7/2013, arrived 12/9/2013.  Worked as described until 5/9/2014.  While cooking a pizza, both within the pizza maker company recommendations and within the usage recommendations provided by Cuisinart, the the glass on the front "door" of the oven shattered when I opened it.  The entire door failed - handle came off, and the left side of the door came off too!  Glass shattered to a distance of greater than one meter from the toaster oven.  I have a few pictures, taken with my mobile phone, showing the damage. 

I was using the oven in bake mode at 400 degrees.  Well within the recommended design use.

After a call to Cuisinart's Customer Service, they are replacing the oven.  However, I am concerned this may be a design problem.  I have owned two other toaster oven/broilers, and neither had this type of failure.  Both just finally stopped working.  

I just recommended by great aunt, who is in her mid-80s, to purchase one and she did.  I am worried that this could happen to her.  If it did, she could be injured as she would have a hard time cleaning up all the of tiny pieces of glass.  I've had to clean my kitchen with a damp cloth - including the floor on my hands and knees - to make sure every small piece of glass is thrown away.  I  have had to throw away all of the cat food on the floor, and also throw out all of the water for my cat.  She may not be able to get down to do that, instead having to wait for her homemaker to help do that days later.

I just want to make sure this isn't a problem with the oven itself and not an isolated incident.

Thank you.
justification: The glass shattered and the door failed, but no injury was reported. The concern is for potential injury, especially to an elderly person.

incident_description:
FIRE HAZARD!  On May 8, 2014 at approximately 11:55 pm, my wife asked me to come check on a strong burning smell emanating from our LG LFX25960SW Refrigerator.  I opened the French doors and was met with a strong smell of something "burning".  I noted that the cheddar cheese on the top shelf was liquefied.  The plastic container under it was very hot to touch and was softened.  I then noted that the inside lights enclosure was starting to melt and the lights would not go out when you held both door switches closed by hand.  The light housing was falling off of the fixture and the screws pulled through the plastic housing when I tried to remove it according to the LG instructions in the LG Guide.  The lights were too hot to handle.  They were extremely hot.  We unscrewed the bulbs with the help of oven mitts.  The electrical sockets had begun to discolor from the excessive heat.  

Given the condition of the plastic materials that were beginning to melt in this refrigerator, there is no doubt in my mind that if we did not happen to catch this problem and defect tonight, the heat from the lights would have ignited the plastic in the refrigerator and create a fire that may have burned my house down, killed my pets, and possibly my family.  

I called the phone number of LG (1-800-243-0000) and asked to talk to the technicians, but they were not available.  I was asked to call back tomorrow.
justification: The incident describes a severe fire hazard with potential for death, as the refrigerator's components were melting and could have ignited, posing a lethal risk to the family and pets.

Twice the flame goes out by itself. Then the room smells like gas. 
The consumer contacted h.h. gregg several times and advised them of the problem. No response from the store.

(01/27/2014) The technician came out to install the new regulator. The problem still persists.

Injury to my  two toes on the right foot from the hot coffee and the FULL pot hitting the toe's has left a bruise/blood clot (since I am sensitive to bruising and bleeding due to medication). incident_description:
Called to [REDACTED] for a stove that won't shut off, something glowing inside. Nothing showing upon arrival but smoke detector sounding. Residents were inside the building. Owner directed us to stove. Stove very hot to touch, appeared to be on high with all knobs and control panel off.

The consumer saw smoke coming out from the bottom-front of the unit.

The consumer was informed by 2 people that she would have to pay for shipping and by another rep that the shipping would be covered.

incident_description:
The consumer was cooking asparagus and a potato dish in a metal bowl. The consumer put the bowls in the oven. The oven was set at 350 degrees and was on for about 10 to 15 minutes when the consumer saw flames inside the oven and noticed smoke coming out. 

The two dishes were on fire. 

The consumer noticed that the top broiler coil in the oven was on. The consumer cut the power to the oven with the circuit breaker. The oven had a lot of smoke soot. The consumer cleaned the oven thinking that she had turned the broiler on by accident.

The next day, the consumer was cooking an apple dish in a metal bowl when it also caught fire. The broiler had turn on by itself again. The consumer turned off the circuit breaker again.

There was no damage to anything else and no injuries reported. 

The fire department was not called.

The consumer called the manufacturer and they said there was no recall. Consumer asked for help with the repair bill but representative said they could not do it. The technician came and said he has had other consumers with same problem with this product before.
justification: The incident involved fires in the oven with no injuries or damage beyond the oven itself, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the issue suggests a higher likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I was cooking on the largest burner of the largest element on the cooktop and after turning the burner off it actually stayed on and appeared to be glowing red on High. I turned the circuit breaker off for a few minutes and upon turning the power back on the element once again glowed red. After repeating this several times with the same outcome, I left the breaker off and went to bed. The next morning I turned the power back on and once again it glowed red but this time I tried turning that burner on and lowering the temperature and it did respond then I turned the burner off and it went off and stayed off. The most disappointing thing about this is that LG sent someone out two weeks ago to change the circuit boards to fix this issue (it had happened on several occasions before) and it is still happening.

Once I got it off I went to living room and when I came back the burner was back on!  My house could have burned down, my son could have been burned! incident_description:
On April 24th, 2014 the caller and his wife were baking bread.
The oven had just completed the preheat stage, the caller placed bread in the oven to bake.
Approximately four minutes later the caller smelled smoke, both he and his wife were still in the kitchen so knew very quickly that it was coming from the electric range.
He check the oven but found that the broiler had also come on and was causing burning and smoking.
He hit the cancel button, unplugged the range and pulled it away from the wall.
   
There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer Monday, April 28th, 2014 but stated that they gave no assistance.    

The caller adds on the consent form: I might add that I plugged in the range after  approx 1/2 hour and started the preheat cycle to check the bake cycle. The broiler came on and did not go off causing the oven to get very hot. It stopped an after the preheat cycle ended.
Four days later we checked it again and the oven worked correctly and we were able to complete a loaf of bread without incident. However we could not trust this to be reliable for unsupervised baking. We have replaced the range.
justification: The incident involved smoke and malfunctioning equipment but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
This complaint and warning is for the side-by-side Sub-Zero Refrigerator Model 690/S, Serial # P1872009 and is in regards to the stainless steel molding trim panel around the ice and water dispenser. This stainless steel molding trim panel is affixed the the refrigerator door with some sort of 2-side adhesive which has lost part of its adhesion properties allowing the molding trim panel to come lose to be permanently displaced from the refrigerator door's surface and raised about 1 inch.

Since this trim panel is immediately below the door handle, there is a permanent dangerous interaction with anyone accessing the refrigerator door with fingers and hands reaching right by the the stainless steel trim panel. The danger resides with this now-raised trim panel which has a true razor-sharp edge all around, having already severely injured an adult's finger with a very deep cut. The potential for a child's hand or fingers is to virtually sever or cut-off an entire finger.

This very deep cut occurred on Jan-4-2014 and the picture we have is from 4 days later clearly showing the injury on my left hand, ring finger. The injury is still not completely healed to this day.

On Jan-07-2014, I called Sub-Zero customer care line 800-222-7820, 2:05 PM, who promptly transferred me to the company's legal counsel voicemail box, where I left a detailed message reported the occurred incident. I never received a call back or follow-up from Sub-Zero regarding the injury or more concerning, on their solution to fix or replace the trim panel in question.
justification: The incident describes a severe injury to an adult's finger from a razor-sharp edge, with potential for even worse injuries to children, indicating a high severity level.

The consumer stated that she saw 6-8in flames and a lot of smoke. The consumer stated that there was a lot of black soot on the first floor of her home. The consumer stated that there is a burnt plastic smell left in the home. 

The consumer stated that there was no other property damage. No injuries.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manf on 4/16/14. A repairman from the local shop ([REDACTED])  is supposed to come out in a week to examine the unit. incident_description: I purchased a new General Electric Gas Range (GE-JGB630DEFWW) on January 25, 2014. Installation was not completed until March 25, 2014. My concern is that the knobs on this range turn too easily, and when I reach over the range on the left or right cabinets to retrieve items, the knobs turn on. incident_description: I have a Kenmore refrigerator Model # 795.78409.800 . The refrigerator was purchased brand new from Sears a few years ago. After one week of owning this refrigerator my mother went to get ice from the dispenser. She dispensed the ice and filled her cup with water. After taking a drink she noticed a silver screw in her cup. It was determined by me the screw came from the inner ice bucket/dispenser. We contacted sears who sent out a service man as the Refrigerator was brand new and under warranty. The service man came out when my elderly parents were home, said the ice maker is working fine, and he didn't know what they wanted him to do. Upset with the service visit, I ordered a new ice bucket/dispensers through sears parts online and replaced it myself. The new ice bucket/ dispenser has lasted a few years, but on this evening after drinking from the container I heard something rattling. Looking further I observed a silver screw in the bottom of the container. this screw is identical to the other screws in the ice bucket/ dispenser and has white plastic still wrapped in the threads. There is an observable hole were the screw should be located on the ice bucket/ dispenser. I believe this designed is flawed and puts the consumer at risk of injury. I believe the mechanical ice dispenser when activated puts increased pressure on the walls of the ice bucket causing the screw to pop. Gravity allows the screw to fall through with the ice and into a cup. I often eat the ice and it is by luck I did not ingest or sustained injury due to the screw falling into my cup.
justification: The incident involves a screw falling into a cup, which could potentially cause injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:

Prior to that, I had bought the same microwave without keeping the receipt and encountered the same issue after having the microwave for fewer than 4 months.  I thought it was surely just the one microwave that was defective, so I accepted their store policy of exchanging the broken one for one of the same model.

At night, I was awoken by a fan noise and went out of my room to see what it was.  The microwave had turned on by itself, and had set the timer to a very long time.  This is alarming because it has happened with two microwaves of the same model and seems to happen spontaneously.  The first time I noticed it, over 8 months ago, I was coming home from work and as soon as I walked in the door I found that the microwave was on!  This is obviously a fire hazard. With nothing inside the microwave, the magnetron on the first microwave I bought had burned itself out.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: A Pyrex baking dish shattered in my hand.  It was a newer model (one with openings in the handles and it comes with a plastic lid), approximately 13 X 9 inch clear glass type.  I believe it was a Pyrex Portable Easy Grab. The details leading up to the incident are as follows:  About four days earlier, I baked a casserole in this dish.  After the meal, I refrigerated the left overs in the casserole dish (which was by now room temperature), covering it with the red plastic lid it came with.  Two or three days later when the casserole was all eaten, I soaked the dish in water in the sink overnight.  The next morning I hand washed the Pyrex baking dish in warm soapy water, rinsed it in warm water and began to dry it.  I had the fingers of one hand through the opening of one of the glass handles letting the dish hang down and I was drying it with a towel in my other hand.   The dish did not knock against anything.  With no warning the baking dish shattered into hundreds of small pieces with such a force that it sent the glass all over the kitchen where I was standing, into the adjacent dining room and through the open basement door, down the steps and into the basement itself.   There was nothing left at all in my hand of the glass dish I had been holding a second before, not even the handle.  The knuckles of the fingers that were holding it all had cuts and there was a cut over my eye.  I had used this dish only about four times prior to this last event.  It was in good condition before I used it this last time.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts to the knuckles and a cut over the eye, which qualifies as an injury.

The oven went to LOCK cycle and then started (what appeared to be) the self cleaning cycle operation. Thick Black smoke started to pour out of the front control panel and flames could be seen inside the oven. incident_description: On 10/2008 I purchased an LG LRE30453ST/01 ceramic glass top electric range from Home Depot. On 7/2009 my husband instructed my oldest son to turn on the stove in preparation of us being 5 minutes away. He placed a pot on the stove on the largest eye and set the stove for 3.5 with a little grease inside the pan. My son said that as soon as he did what was instructed and sat down on the couch when he noticed immediate smoke coming from the pot. He looked inside the pan and noticed a ring of fire inside the pan that began to escalate fairly quickly and evacuated himself and my youngest daughter out of the home for their protection. Within five minutes of giving him these instructions we received a call back from him stating that the kitchen was on fire. Fire department came but the fire self extinguished itself before they were able to take action. The fire caused 8k worth of damage with us paying a 1K deductible. It damaged the cabinets above the stove, the microwave above the stone, and the stove itself which sustained the most damage. The pot was actually not destroyed, but the stove was. The insurance company had no clue how this escalated so quickly so therefore the pot had masked the true natural cause of the fire which was the stove itself. The stove was replaced with the exact same model stove in 2009 and in 4/2014 while I was cooking on the largest eye once again with a cast iron skillet, the bottom of the dry skillet began to smoke from underneath  with a temperature set at 3.5. I noticed the extreme heat coming from the largest eye and attempted to turn it off with no response from the stove to reduce the heat even though the stove read H5 which means a warm status. The heat was so extreme that the other eyes started to read as H5 and they weren't even on. The extreme heat from the largest eye also prompted the microwave vent to come on by itself. My kids and myself started to get nervous and tried to power down the stove by turning off the circuit braker with no response so we had to unplug the stove from the wall. We waited about 5 minutes and attempted to replug the stove and the largest eye came on immediately flashing red several times sending out extreme heat so we decided to keep it unplugged. I called LG the next day to find out that a recall was issued in 2012 for my model number. I was completely taken back. The recall stated "The burners on the electric ranges can fail to turn off after being switched off or the temperature setting can increase unexpectedly during use, posing burn and fire hazards to consumers". What else do you need? I asked why I was not notified and they said it was on TV and because I did not register the product I didn't get notified by mail. I'm a working professional mom of three, really! I can't believe they said that. They offered to repair the stove I currently have in my home and offered apologies for the fire in 2009. Is there no recourse or responsibility of the manufacture for damages that occurred to homeowners before the recall. How can this be right. LG is claiming statue of limitations is 3 years but what about the fact that a recall was not issued until 2012. How was my insurance suppose to know that their product was defective when their was no recall in place. How is the consumer suppose to be protected in a case like this. I'm not asking for the 8k that my insurance paid out but at least take responsibility for the deductible I had to pay for your fire hazardous product I placed in my home that nearly killed my kids. How can the statue of limitations be set for 3 years when the defect is not found until the recall is issued? PS: I should be able to seek reimbursement of my deductible (money loss) under the NC Gen Stat. 1-50(6) which is 6 years from the date of incident.
justification: The incident caused 8k worth of damage but no injury, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidaire Range Model Number = FEF352AUC Serial Number = VF21105537.

On April 20, 2014, after cooking the range recorded an error and the broil element was on high and would not turn off. I attempted to turn the oven off 2 more times and the broil element continued on high. The range did report an error code of F1, but that was the main indication of a problem (besides the heat continuing to come from the oven). I contacted the manufacturer. Frigidaire referred me for repair. Here is a copy of the email I sent and response.

My email to Frigidaire after initial consultation:
"Thank you for the reply. 

I am much more concerned about the safety aspect of this oven. I see that there are no recalls, but this could have been a very dangerous situation. Do you want some representative to at least pick up the oven for testing? There seems to be some design flaw. I would expect a better situation would have been to fail "off" instead of on broil high. 

A google search also yielded this: 
Oven would not shut off after using. - AppliancePartsPros.com 


Oven would not shut off after using. - AppliancePartsPro... 
View on www.applianceparts... Preview by Yahoo 

Hence I am not the only person to find this situation. I realize this is a discontinued product, but the design flaw could have continued in later models. 

Please let me know how you would like to proceed. "

And Frigidaire's response:

"Dear [REDACTED],
Thank you for contacting Frigidaire.
I completely understand your frustration regarding the problem you're having with your range. You will need to schedule an appointment for service to determine what part is required for your repair. Based upon the model and serial number, the service company will provide you with the amount of the service call charges. I hope that you will accept our apologies for the difficulty you experienced.
Thank you again for contacting Frigidaire.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
Correspondence Specialist
"

I believe this to be a serious safety issue. This could have easily caused a fire. It is my belief that a range should be designed to fail in the OFF position, not ON. I am also concerned that this design flaw might be in current models of Frigidaire range products
justification: The incident involved a range failing to turn off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

Yesterday our toaster stopped working and instead of buying a new one, we decided to get this toaster oven out of storage. incident_description:
Installed July 2004 - Thermadore Electric Self Cleaning Convection Oven SC301ZS overheated during a clean cycle that made the oven door way too hot to touch!  I first noticed the problem because of a char odor; and when I approached the oven ...the heat coming off the oven door was hotter than my woodburning stove!  The wood cabinet was hot to touch!  I did not dare to touch the oven door.  A child could have been seriously burned!!  My wife was able to touch the electronic panel and turn off the oven.   It took several hours for the oven to cool down.  The next day we checked to see if the oven would work.  Because of he excessive heat, I put an electronic 'K' thermocouple into the oven to monitor temperature just in case.  We set the temp for 300F.  At first it appeared Ok; however, within a few minutes the temp was at 300F and then quickly rose to 325, 350, 375, 400, 425,450F.  We lowered the set point to 275F but the temp continued to rise.  We lower the set point to 250 and the oven temp started to drop.  Once it dropped near 250 it stated up again to above 350F.  We lowered the setting to 180 and the oven temp began to drop.   Because we could monitor the temp at the center of the oven cavity (and baking bread), we set the temp to 250F and when it reached 350F, we lowered the setting to 225...and the temp would drop.  When it dropped to 250F, we raised the temp setting a bit higher and the oven would get hotter ...when it was above 350F, we again moved the setting lower.  It took over 2.5 hours to bake the cake.

Aside - About 6 months earlier, the display panel became dimmer ...difficult to read temperature.  I can not read it ...color blind for some shades of Red!  But I don't bake!
justification: The incident caused excessive heat, but no injury was reported.

We were fortunate to still be home and were able to unplug the machine and remove it from the home before it caught fire or damaged the home.
justification: The coffee maker started smoking and had a red-hot heating element while off, posing a fire risk, but no injury or damage occurred as it was promptly unplugged.

incident_description:
used the bodum coffee maker: 11001, date code 5012.
makes good coffee, but not safe: the brew basket has no retention feature to keep in position, when I pull the coffee pot out, the basket came out with it and spilled the coffee ground and hot coffee on my hand. I recommend a full recall on this item, or at least adding positive retention, not come out easily
with the coffee pot. Pictures available upon request.

incident_description: I have been smelling a burning plastic/wiring smell from my Kemore oven. I do not have anything on the services that heat and the smell is not from inside the oven but with it shut. I know this smell and it seems to be the internals of the oven. I am now afraid to use the oven for worry of a fire. After a lot of research I have concluded that this is a common occurrence with these ovens. The fumes from the oven caused nausea and headache for almost my whole family. We had to air the house out and now cannot use the oven.

incident_description:

No medical attention was received. incident_description:
(06/12/2012) The consumer stated that she was boiling water. She smelled something burning. She turned off the rice cooker. She checked the rice cooker. Two hours later she turned the rice cooker upside down and looked at the label. She lifted the label and saw the bottom of the pot was melted.
The label was not melted.

The unit was in use for approximately 5-10 mins, he powered off the unit and left the room but he noticed the incident the following day.  He is not sure of the time it occurred.

He attempted to contact the manufacturer but the number proved futile.  The retailer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this toaster oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The toaster oven overheated, causing damage to nearby items but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

Called vendor the next day. Service came out and confirmed with the beeping gas sensor that both of my high BTU burners were leaking. According to repairman its a know issue. As this is a life and death issue I want a recall so know one ends up dead. 

PRODUCT: KITCHENAID 30 INCH SS RANGE KGSS907XSP GAS
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with no reported injuries, but it posed a potential risk to life, and the repairman indicated it's a known issue.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that this was bought by son-in-law.

On 03/09/14, the consumer's wife was cleaning the pan. The consumer's wife was injured while picking up the pan inset.
The consumer's wife was taken to the hospital for injuries to her left hand pinky finger. At the hospital's ER, the consumer's wife's finger was treated for laceration to the artery. The consumer's wife is on medication for blood thinner. Her finger was stitched up which caused it swell and turn purple. The consumer's wife was opened up again and further examined to find a slit artery. Her artery was stitched up to stop initial bleeding.

On 03/11/14, the consumer's wife went to the specialist for a surgery. Her finger's artery, nerves and 2 tendons were reconnected. 

The consumer stated that the pan insert in the electric roast is very sharp and has a straight edge. The consumer stated that it should be rolled or have a smooth edge.
The consumer stated that they have two of these and they both have sharp, straight edges. 
The consumer stated that he called company's # on the manual (1-866-369-4170 ). The consumer stated that the number is for a sweepstakes offer.

incident_description:

incident_description: We own a Kenmore Elite Ultra Wash dishwasher, Model #665 17482300, Serial #FR3403252, purchased 12/27/2004.  On Monday, 4/21/2014 we turned it on to do dishes.  Shortly thereafter the dishwasher door caught fire.  The control panel was burning.  House filled with terrible smelling smoke.  We opened the door and pulled the plug on the dishwasher.  It was definitely the control panel on door that burned. Thank heavens we were home at the time.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, filling the house with smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I had per-heated my oven to 300 degrees to put in taco shells.  I went to put the tacos in and saw my Pyrex casserole dish in the oven.  I pulled it out, and set it on a cookie sheet that was on the stove at room temperature.  I turned back around to grab the shells to put them in and heard a loud noise and saw glass flying everywhere, including into my arm.  The Pyrex dish exploded into thousands of pieces and shrapnel.  I have glass EVERYWHERE!  

The dish was not at a very hot temperature, nor exposed to an unusual circumstance.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from glass shrapnel, but the circumstances were unusual and not typical for Pyrex dishes.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a smoothtop range with model number that ended in one F but the retailer delivered one with a model number that ended in two F's.
Around June 15th, 2012 the caller's husband's shirt tail caught on the knob to the front left burner where a pizza box was sitting.
The family noticed this had happened when the pizza box caught fire.   
The caller noted in the chaos that the middle section that is between the front left and back left burners had been turned on.
July 4th, 2012 this same incident happened with the caller's husband who thought the knob may have caught on his pants pocket, turned the right front burner on and caught a dishtowel that was lying on that burner on fire.
September 2012/Labor Day weekend, the caller was at the range, her bathrobe sleeve she believes is what caught the knob, turned the front left burner on and caught pot holder that was lying on the burner.

The range was not in use from September 6th, 2012 through November 9th, 2012 due to caller and family being out of town.

November 12th, 2012 the caller reached over the range to place something in the microwave over this range, her belt buckle turned the right rear burner on and when she back up to wait for the microwave she noticed that the burner was beginning to glow.  Nothing was near the burner at that time.  

Also on Nov 25th, 2012, knob knocked on accidentally (unnoticed) and scorched skillet sitting on eye. 

January 29th, 2013 this incident happened again when the husband reached to place something in the microwave and again somehow one of the range burners was turned on again.
Caller believes that it should be necessary to push in then turn these burners before they can light.

There are no injuries to report 
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them
justification: Multiple incidents of burners being accidentally turned on, leading to fires, but no injuries reported.

incident_description:
On September 6, 2010, we bought a Bosch gas 5 burner cooktop, model, NGM5654SS, for $813.06, at ABT Electronics at 1200 North Milwaukee Avenue, Glenview, Illinois 60025 (see attached). Gradually, we began having difficulty to turning the gas on or off. On a couple of occasions only the smell of gas alerted us that despite the knob pointing to the off mark, in fact had not completely shut the gas off. We then realized that ALL of the knobs were cracked (see attached pictures), we went to ABT Electronics and express our safety concerns about the low quality and fragility of cooktop knobs we had bought from this store. They did not show any concern about selling a product with that high risk safety issue; the only response was to sell us the replacements for $18.00, dollars plus tax a piece, totaling over $115.00.
Failing to get our safety concerns through with ABT Electronics, we went directly to Bosch and Siemens Corporation, 1901 Main Street, Suite-600, Irvine, CA 92614, (949)440-7100. We contacted this company by telephone and spoke to Ms. [REDACTED] Customer Service, explaining in detail the potential for gas leaks, fire, explosion and Carbon Monoxide poisoning resulting from the defective cooktop knobs. She did not express any interest or concern and like ABT Electronics, only offer to sell to us the same frail, Inadequate and unsafe cooktop knobs, but with 10% discount. I strongly made clear to her that my fear was the unsafe design and poor quality of the material of the knobs, not a handout. Furthermore, I sent to Ms. [REDACTED] on January 27, 2014, all the pictures from the 5 knobs and her only email response was, "Thank you so much for sending me the information. I will attach it to your file.'' To this date I have not heard anything from Bosch and Siemens Corporation. 
We have tried to find on the market better designed replacements for the knobs, but none of them fit this particular cooktop model, which has rendered the expensive cooktop useless for us. We then contacted the City of Des Plaines Fire Consumer Protection Section and I was directed by Fire Chief, [REDACTED] on February 4, 2014, to contact you.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with the cooktop knobs, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
We have a dual fuel range made by Electrolux.  Model EW30DS65GS8. A few nights ago after cleaning the stovetop we retired for the evening and went to bed.  About 1 AM my wife awoke to a very strong smell of propane in the home. She woke me and we opened windows and started to investigate. We found the knob controlling one of the burners to be slightly open and allowing gas to flow into the home.  The electronic igniter did not activate. After closing the valve and airing the house everything was fine.
I phoned Electrolux only to be told that was the way the stove was designed.  Had we not awoken we may have been killed in a violent explosion.
It seems to me that once the gas starts to flow, the igniter should initiate and the burner should light.  That way we would know the valve is turned on.
The current system allows gas to flow into the home without ignition if the valve is turned slightly, say by cleaning with a sponge or a cloth.
We are concerned this may be a deadly flaw that the manufacturer is ignoring.
justification: Gas leakage without ignition poses a significant risk of explosion, which could lead to death, but no actual injury occurred in this instance.

He also noticed that a considerable amount of plastic shavings appeared in his glass when the ice melted.

incident_description: As I was cooking a rib roast in the oven at 450 degrees, the oven began beeping and flashing a F10 code.  I immediately shut the oven off.  It was VERY hot and smoke-filled.  When it had cooled off, I turned it back on to 325 degrees.  Shortly, it repeated the alarm, code, and smoke.  The oven glowed red through the window - the broiler element was lit, even though I had not turned on this function.   The oven had NEVER glowed red before during broiling.  I again turned it off, however I left my meat inside as we discussed what to do.  In a few minutes, the meat began to sizzle.  When I went over to the stove, the broiler element had turned itself back on even though the oven was turned off.    We unplugged it.
justification: The oven malfunctioned, emitting smoke and activating the broiler element unexpectedly, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(1/2013) The consumer stated that he came home and could hear a hum coming from the microwave. The cabinet above the microwave was hot to the touch. The consumer unplugged the microwave. The consumer checked on line and saw that there may have been a problem with the control board.  The consumer followed the recommendations to fix the problem. The consumer replaced the magnetron.
 
(03/22/2014) the consumer stated that he used the microwave. He walked out of the room. He came back into the room about twenty minutes later and heard the humming coming from the microwave. He unplugged the microwave and plugged it back it. The humming continued.
 
The consumer stated that he unplugged the microwave. He put some water in a cup and placed it in the microwave.  Then he plugged the microwave back in. The consumer waited for about ten seconds, unplugged the microwave. He checked the water and the water was hot. The consumer stated that he did not push any buttons to cause the water to heat up in the microwave.
 
The consumer stated that this is a dangerous situation because it could cause a fire. 

After reporting the issue with the microwave to the CSPC and continuing to have the reported problem, Iremoved the PCB board.Upon examination,I was able to see some darkening on the PCB board in the areas labeled D106- 0109. I ordered and received a new PCB board  (part# RAS-SM7MGV-07), which Iinstalled.This has corrected the issue that I was previously having with the microwave and has not re-occurred since.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave that could potentially cause a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The issue was resolved after replacing the PCB board.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he feels that he is experiencing similar problems of Release #12-244, he has noticed a few items that had been discolored or melted (not sure when).  The heated feature was never used on the unit before but he feels the heat system has a failure and might be staying on.  Hazard: An electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element can pose a fire hazard.  The most recent incident occurred 3/11/14.

He researched the unit online and found out that there was recall but his serial number did not match.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.  

Caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

Following the call with CPSC where this report's data was submitted I called the manufacturer, GE. I finally got through to a live representative and explained what I had seen happening with our dishwasher in terms of the heatnig coil being very hot when no heated drying was called for and damage to items in the dishwasher. The representative said that the recal issue was related to a different issue of a serious part failure outside the tub.

I told the agent that in the over three years since the diswasher was installed we did not use heated dry and had never had a single incident of items in the lower rack meltiong and deforming. I also had never seen, at the end of a cycle, water dripping from dishes and "sizzling" when he drops the landed on the heating unit. While I wated he did some research. He came back on the line and told me that what I had seen happening might happen and was not part of the recall. No further assistance was offered.

She immediately turned the vacuum cleaner off then went to inspect, however the minute she got to her kitchen door she saw glass on her kitchen floor.
The glass had gone as far as three and one half feet out from the oven with the majority of the pieces staying inside the oven.

The caller is reporting this incident as a severe hazard.

Not only is this an unexpected incident but could be extremely dangerous should anyone child, elderly person, invalid, user or company standing nearby.
She states that the oven glass door actually imploded unlocking the door and causing glass to also explode outside of the oven.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer via email Saturday, April 5th, 2014

incident_description:
I purchased new appliances from Whirlpool "White Ice". In my opinion there is a major design flaw in the stove/oven.

First incedent was when we were broiling something in the oven and my wife touched the top of the stove (control panel) with one hand and set the timer with the other and burn her hand. I went to grab a pizza pan from the drawer below the oven and burnt my hand. Called Whirlpool service and they sent a tech out. He said the stove will get hot and that I wasn't supposed to store pans in the pullout drawer. I told him I have had a dozen stoves and never burnt my hand on a tray from the pullout drawer and asked him to leave.

The second incedent was broiling again. I had a 4 quart pot on top of the stove with the microwave cover resting on top. The pot is 4-5" high. After cooking I grabbed the microwave cover and had noticed that it had melted on top of the stove... no burners were ever on. I placed a cooking thermometer in where the plasic melted and it went above 200 degrees. I called Whirlpool Corporate this time, sent them pictures, etc. 3 or 4 days later i received a phone call referring me to pages 12-14 where engineering says the stove top may get warm. I just want someone with authority to tell me I am wrong and its normal for an oven to melt plastic 5 inches above the oven.
Please, this flaw will burn down a house!
justification: The incident resulted in burns (injury) and the description indicates repeated occurrences of excessive heat causing harm and property damage.

incident_description:
We had a fire in the oven in the Thermador Pro Gas range we use in our kitchen on 2/28/14. The fire started roughly 15 minutes after the over was turned on. This could have led to a whole house fire and we were fortunate that my wife was in the kitchen at the time. She started screaming and I rushed to the kitchen to see smoke and small flames coming from the oven/range. We were lucky that the fire did not spread.

The technician from the local applicance repair company who inspected the appliance pointed out that the wire harness and controls for the push button models were closely packed in the range and if the button was not fully pressed in, it could cause arcing and lead to a fire. Appartently this has happened with other Thermador push button range models.

We contacted the Thermador Customer Service immediately after the incident and are still trying to resolve this with them. Their File # is [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, but potential for significant harm if not promptly addressed.

incident_description:
Yesterday, on beautiful Easter Sunday, 4/20/14, I had a dozen family members gathered at my home for dinner and conversation. I had spent the day before preparing delectable food entrees including a labor intensive vegetable lasagna for the family vegetarians. I used the covered Pyrex 3 quart glass bakeware lasagna dish (9" by 13") for this and cooked it on Saturday, 4/19/14. The following day I first brought the dish up to room temperature and then placed it in a 275 degree oven for about a half hour, then increased to 300 degrees for about 10 minutes before we heard the shattering noise coming from the oven! Much to my horror, as I opened the oven door I saw the glass pan had shattered into hundreds of very small and large pieces. ......needless to say the lasagna was glass ridden and inedible. I then spent the afternoon cleaning out the oven and am still finding slivers between the oven doors.

I am throughly disgusted with this product, especially in light of its' claim to go from ""refrigerator to oven." The material is obviously of inferior quality as the oven temperature was not even considered to be high heat!!

How do I go about getting compensated for this?
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass bakeware) and food contamination, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On Saturday, April 19, 2014,  my dishwasher started to smoke and caught fire.  I started the dishwasher just minutes (10 minutes at most) before this occurred.  The smoke appeared first; it was black.  Immediately after the smoke was noticed, flames were seen shooting out from above and below the control panel.  The door was immediately opened.  This stopped the burning/fire.  The breaker switch was manually turned off as well.  Quick thinking prevented my house from catching fire.  Luckily, we were home and awake.  I usually run the dishwasher when we go to bed or as we are leaving for the day.  The result could have been deadly and would have absolutely been more destructive than a defunct dishwasher.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was quickly controlled, resulting in no injury or death.
