Glass shards and hot potatoes and sauce were strewn about the oven. We opened the door after hearing the explosion and looking through the oven window. My wife's hand was burned when she tried to slide out the oven rack and I cut myself on the glass trying to move the mess of the hot stove element.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and cuts, indicating injury (severity 3), but such events are unlikely (likelihood 2) given proper use of oven-safe cookware.

incident_description: I was using a Pyrex baking dish that I had used recently.  It was purchased for our wedding last summer, so it was fairly new and I hadn't used this one particularly much.  I had put two pork chops, with a liquid glaze in the dish and preheated the oven to 360 degrees.  After about half an hour, we heard a loud noise and when I opened the oven, the glass had shattered, leaving pork chops and sauce all over the interior of the oven.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering in the oven, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: Microwave oven turns on by its self
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, and such malfunctions are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: On 4/20/14, my electric range turned on a burner on it's own.  The knob was in the off position.  The indicator panel read 8.5.  I was unable to turn the burner off.  After messing with it, it would say Lo, but it would not shut off.  I had to unplug it.  My safety concern is obvious - it started to burn and smoke as a tray was set on it (as the cook top was not being used).  What concerns me even more, is that I reported a Frigidaire range in 2009 through this agency.  An agent came out, a report was filed, the ranges were recalled and the company replaced my range with this one.  Clearly the problem has not been solved.  The current range is not listed under any recall, and it is a serious safety concern.
justification: The incident caused a fire and smoke, but no injury was reported, so the severity level is 2.  The occurrence likelihood is 4 because the problem was reported before and it is likely to happen again.

incident_description: On the morning of April 18, 2014, I was awakened by a burning odor. I woke my wife, and we began looking for the source. The odor was stronger as we went downstairs, and overwhelming in the kitchen. The burning smell was strongest near the fridge, so I pulled it out and unplugged it. I removed  the cardboard cover at the lower back, and after inspection with a flashlight found a square white connection on the compressor still smoldering. The fumes were enough to nauseate my wife.
justification: The incident involved a smoldering fridge connection causing nausea, which qualifies as an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Two identical incidents occurred with an LG Microwave Oven, Model number LMV1680ST, Product Code MV1648ADL.CSBELGA, manufactured December 2010, serial number  012TAHQ06065. 

The first incident occurred in early October of 2012, eleven months after the purchase, installation, and daily use of the unit. This first incident with the unit is being reported now for the first time. Without any human intervention whatsoever and without the unit having been programmed or otherwise touched in any way, the microwave turned itself on, could not be turned off, and emitted black smoke. Every attempt to turn the unit off failed, so ultimately to avert a fire the unit was unplugged from the outlet. Since the unit was under warranty, LG sent a service technician on October 11, 2012. The repair technician found a burnt printed circuit board, a melted control, and a melted top. He therefore replaced the control assembly and the top grille. When questioned, the technician replied that he had never seen or heard of any such incident, and assured us that since he had just installed a new control assembly that it could never happen again. I took pictures of the burnt control circuit board because of my concern about the incident.

Despite the assurances received that this type of incident could never happen again, on April 10, 2014 the exact same incident occurred. The microwave had not been used or even touched for over 12 hours, and yet it turned itself on, it could not be turned off, and emanated black smoke. In order to turn the unit off, the plug was again detached from the wall. I am reporting both incidents simultaneously as I am now very convinced that LG has either a latent defect or a design flaw which seriously impacts safety. Fortunately, in both instances detailed above, someone was home to intervene and avert a fire. If someone had not been home I can only surmise that a major fire would have occurred.   

LGs focus after the both incidents is on the repair of the unit. I firmly believe this to be a serious safety issue and that LG and/or the appropriate government agency must undertake a full review of the product's design before a catastrophic event can occur.
justification: The incidents involved the microwave turning on by itself and emitting smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The likelihood is unlikely as it happened twice over several years.

incident_description:
I purchased a Black & Decker convection/toaster oven last summer. I have only used it about 4 or 5 times. Last night, the glass door oven exploded for no apparent reason.

I was baking lobster cakes at 400 degrees. I pre-heated the oven for about 10 minutes and then baked the food for about 10 minutes when I heard a big crashing noise. When I went into the kitchen, I found a zillion little pieces of the glass door all over my kitchen counter and floor. The small piece of "door" left is filled with cracked glass, too, and I am afraid even to pick up the toaster oven and throw it out.

The model number is T01675B
justification: The glass door exploded, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: We purchased the Dinera plate set from IKEA in December, 2013. These plates are listed as microwave safe. My husband heating food in the microwave on the plate when suddenly he heard a loud explosion in the microwave. He immediately stopped the microwave, and when he opened it up, the plate had cracked completely down the middle. This is an obvious safety hazard!
justification: The plate cracked in the microwave, but no injury was reported, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description:
I prepared lamb in my oven using a pyrex glass dish.    As a I added more liquid to the pan, the pan violently exploded in the oven sending  a stream of shards of glass out of the oven door.  It is complete coincidence that I did not sustain severe injury including possible disastrous eye injuries.

I have used pyrex dishes all my life and adding liquids is a common and acceptable use of the product.   However when I researched this incident, I found that my pan that was bought a couple of years ago at Walmart was NOT made like the original  PYREX pan but simple just carried the label PYREX.   The original PYREX was made of borosilicate and this new on is made of soda-lime glass, a much inferior products as far as thermal expansion is concerned.

What is going on here is simply that a company uses a brand name that had a great reputation cheapened it down and making it unsafe for many uses that the old pan was just fine.    

This is very much similar if a company would buy the rights for [REDACTED] that has been proven to be safe for generations, and then secretly uses inferior ingredients making it unsafe for many uses.  The consumer would assume that this product has the same safety record as the original but it does not.   A hideous form of Bait and Switch and it is harming a lot of people.

I urge you, please stop the sale of this product in the current form before more people are getting injured.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion of a glass dish causing potential for severe injury, though none occurred in this case.

incident_description: My 16 month-old Cuisinart coffee maker experienced an electrical fire at the end of a normal brewing  cycle.  We were able to unplug the device without injury.  I have contacted Cuisinart to obtain a replacement since the device had a 3 year warranty.  The coffeemaker had light usage, rarely more than two 4-cup pots per day.  It is concerning that serious injury/property damage could have occurred  on such a new device that did not experience high usage.  It seems like that should be investigated.
justification: The incident was a fire, but no injury was reported, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: On December 27, 2012, I was at home, opening and setting up the Wusthof 14 piece Gourmet series knife block I had bought.  I placed all of the knives in the butcher block and carried the entire thing over to the kitchen counter, placing the steak knives blade side up to keep them sharp.  I removed the old knife block set from the countertop and went to place the new set in its place.  I pushed front of the block set with her left hand and went to put my right hand on bottom of the butcher block to pick it up and move it further back on the countertop.  As I placed my right hand on the bottom of the block, my hand encountered the exposed tips of the steak knives protruding from the bottom of the block, and as I pulled my hand back from the pain, I realized that I was cut.  I reported to the emergency room, and on January 7, 2013, I had surgery to repair my tendon and nerve.  On May 24, 2013, I had a second surgery, a PIP (proximal interphalangeal) joint capsulotomy, and tenolysis to improve her feeling in her finger and her range of motion, which had been reduced by around 20 degrees. I also underwent a carpal tunnel release surgery, and at the same time.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injury requiring multiple surgeries, including tendon and nerve repair, and reduced range of motion, which qualifies as a severity level 3.

incident_description:
We own a 36 inch Wolf Range that we purchased in 2004.  When we turn on the oven, there is a delay of about a minute.  Then the gas turns on for 10 seconds, filling the oven with gas.  During this period, the kitchen gets a strong odor of natural gas.  Finally, after 10 seconds of gas filling the oven, the ignitor lights the gas.  Since the oven is filled with gas, there is a small explosion.  If I open the oven to check to see if the oven is lit yet, the flame jumps out at me.

I brought this matter to the attention of Wolf/Sub-zero in 2009, and they refused to fix it under warranty.  I created a video in 2010 of the entire lighting cycle and posted it on You Tube:  http://youtu.be/O-XdmGMutdw .  After posting this, others have told me they have the same problem, so I don't think my experience is isolated.

The symptoms we experience closely match those experienced with recalls of the same oven on October 18, 2001, and the recall of 48 inch ranges in 2008.  

In the October 18, 2001 recall, the serial numbers included in the recall were 60-10000000 through 60-1099999 and 11000957 through 11006106.  Our serial number is 11115391 so we were not included, although the symptoms were the same.

I believe that Wolf sold us a range that should have been fixed during the recall in 2001, but wasn't.  It's a dangerous issue, and I don't think we should fear our oven every time we light the oven.
justification: The incident involves a small explosion and flame exposure when the oven is used, posing a clear risk of injury, and the issue is reported by multiple users, indicating it is likely to occur.

incident_description:
The oven had a loud bang and a fire while baking a pie. The fire went out quick as the door was closed. We noticed after cool down that a 2 inch by 1/8 inch burn through the metal surround around the fan. This is a convection oven named the Profile by General Electric.  Our email to GE has not been answered. We seek no refund as the range/oven is 10 years old. We do not believe an oven should cause a fire or burn through metal.
We believe this product is unsafe.
justification: The incident involved a fire and minor damage to the oven, but no injuries or further harm occurred.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire Smooth top range Model # FES365ECD  bought in 2006. After hearing about the recall for burners not turning off or heating hotter than what was set, I realized others had the same problem I had.  I looked up my model and noticed that it is not part of the recall. The first few years that I had the range, it worked great and I love the smooth top.   I have had numerous (approximately 10+) times over the past few (2-3) years where the  the left rear burner (others have not been a problem) would not turn off.  Rather than turning off it would heat to high.  Fortunately, I was close by and was able to wiggle the knob and get it to turn off.  I use the burner on a regular basis and it is intermittent.  The range still is in excellent condition barring the left rear burner issue.
justification: The burner intermittently fails to turn off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury has occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: Ran microwave for 1 minute with nothing in it and a burning smell was noticed within that period.  When the door was opened smoke poured out and it was obvious that the inside wall of the microwave had caught on fire.  Two photos are being provided.
justification: The microwave caught fire, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that when she closes the refrigerator door, the light does not shut off. The consumer stated that the heat has caused melting of the plastic light cover.

The consumer stated that all other containers in the refrigerator are hot to the touch. The consumer stated that the light bulb was hard to remove from the socket. The consumer did remove the light bulb.

The consumer stated that she has noticed this happen multiple times (at least 3 times).

The consumer stated that she knows that the refrigerator is not being left open because there is a feature in the refrigerator that causes a beep sound if the door is left open.

The consumer stated that the light bulbs are the original bulbs that came with the refrigerator.

The consumer stated that the issue initially started about 6 months ago. The consumer stated that she contacted the manf at that time. The consumer was informed by the manf to either buy an extended warranty or pay for the cost of the repair and inspection. 

The consumer stated that she did not feel like the manf cared about the issue so she did not call them when it happen again this time. 

There are no recalls on this refrigerator.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator light causing heat and melting, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: We ran a load of dishes and the heating element was still on 12 hours later. The interior of the dishwasher was extremely hot with plastic items having started to melt.
justification: The dishwasher overheating caused damage to plastic items but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an LG cooktop. The plastic knobs failed within one year so I called LG for replacement as this is a serious safety issue. After several calls with LG support, it was determined LG would not replace the knobs. 
I purchased new knobs for ~$25 each, totaling $125. FOR A NEW COOKTOP!
As a precaution I started turning off the gas under the cabinet. 
The knobs have failed again making the cooktop more unsafe.
justification: The incident involves repeated failure of cooktop knobs, posing a safety risk but no reported injury.

incident_description:
West Bend Stir Crazy popcorn Popper.
After 15 months of occasional use it started to smoke and sparks came from the base.  I let the unit cool and tried it again, it immediately started to spark and make a popping noise.
justification: The popcorn popper sparked and smoked, indicating a malfunction, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Model 790.9611 range a few years ago.  The range worked fine until recently when the front left burner would not turn off.  The range had to be unplugged for it to cool down.  It has happened several times the past month.  I see where there is a recall for the model 790 range for this burner issue, but not for the model 790.9611 model.
THIS IS A HUGE FIRE HAZARD!
justification: The burner not turning off is a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: Purchased an LG gas range oven model #LRG 30355 ST  and have had problems with the burner control knobs cracking and breaking from normal use. Knobs are made from cheap plastic. They are loose and spin freely. Difficult to tell if gas is turned off. Very dangerous condition. I have read numerous complaints about this  problem on many different sites.
justification: The incident involves a dangerous condition with gas range knobs that could lead to gas leaks, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The pressure indicator blew out of the pressure cooker lid. I contacted the customer service number repeatedly but was referred to their website or to leave a message for return call. I left a message expressing safety concerns and inadequate reassembly instructions fro the valve assembly in the Operating instructions.

The model was marketed by Farberware under the Nutrimaster brand. Farberware referred me to Fagor.

The bottom of the pot is labeled as follows:
NUTRIMASTER
FARBERWARE
C8S06 60T 5 7 L
justification: The pressure indicator blew out, indicating a safety issue, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought a set of Anchor Hocking drinking glasses from Walmart several months ago. Recently, while putting hot water into the glasses, the glasses cracked and the bottom part came off. It happened to 2 of the 16 glasses. I was lucky that I was not holding the glasses when that happened. Imagine what injuries it would cause if the glasses broke and hot water spilled on the body! I stopped using the glasses and contacted Anchor Hocking but didn't get any response yet. Those glasses should be recalled!
justification: The glasses cracked but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is possible as it happened to 2 out of 16 glasses.

incident_description: We have a Caloric Gas Oven and we have had it since we have lived here which is 2 years.  I know it is an older model, and I know it had to of been here for a few years before we moved in.  In the middle of the night last night (4/8/2014), the glass door on the oven spontaneously exploded into a million pieces all over our kitchen.  My husband woke up at 6:30 AM for work and walked out to the kitchen to make coffee only to find a shattered glass oven door in a million tiny pieces all over the floor.  This is very alarming to us seeing as we have a one year old child.  Luckily it happened in the middle of the night and not when he was around.
justification: The oven door shattered but no one was injured, and the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the age of the oven.

incident_description: Was going to melt cheese on top of onion soup in ramakines and placed them inside p 13x9 pan till dinner time set the pan on top of stove and prepared stuffed lobster tails along side and BOOM THE PAN EXPLODED . I have pictures and it was all over stove in lobster and in soup. This is not my only insisdent. About a year ago I was reheating some chicken wings fro fridge to microwave and BOOM IT EXPLODED in the microwave .
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a serious incident that caused damage to the stove and food.

incident_description: A piece of the metal blade DLC-861TX in a Cuisinart food processor broke off and was found in a smoothie that was prepared in the food processor.  The piece came off at one of the rivet points and cracks in the metal blade can be seen at two other rivet attachment points.
justification: A piece of the blade broke off into food, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased the dishwasher in Oct 2012. The consumer stated it was installed around Dec 2012. 

The consumer stated that his wife put in a load of dishes. The consumer stated that the dishwasher started smoking after about 10 minutes. The consumer stated that they smelled burning (electrical burning).

The consumer shut off the power. The consumer tried to use the dishwasher again and the same thing happened. 

The consumer stated that he hit the cancel button to drain out the water. 

The consumer stated that it tripped the GFI circuit breaker within 1 minute. 

The consumer pulled out the unit to inspect. The consumer stated that there was melting on the unit around the wiring. 

There are recalls on this unit.
justification: The incident involved smoking and melting but no reported injuries, indicating a non-injury incident with likely occurrence based on the described events and recalls.

incident_description:
The consumer was cooking a vegetable dish in a glass bowl. He set the oven to pre-heat at 350 degree. 

The consumer placed the dish inside the oven. The oven was on for about 30 minutes.

Oven was smoking prior prior to black smoke. (overheating) The consumer smelled burning wires or plastic. Then the consumer saw black smoke coming from the back of the range. 

The rangeÃÂs digital displayed was showing F10 for ÃÂrun away temperatureÃÂ but the range did not turn itself off as it should. Keypad was also locked! Unresponsive.

The consumer unplugged the unit from the wall and the smoke stopped. He did not see any flames. 

The consumer opened the back of the range and saw that one of the resistors was burned. There were burn marks above the resistor.

The consumer did not call the fire department.

No injuries or other damages were reported.

No recalls on the range. 
The consumer contacted the retailer. The representative informed the consumer that the range was out of warranty and did not offer any further assistance. The rep informed the consumer that they could send a technician for repair the range at the his expense.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoke but no injuries or damages were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: After cooking some food this morning our microwave would keep running after closing the door. We couldn't get it to stop unless we open the door or unplug it. Now, when we plug it in it starts on its own and keeps running. The turntable doesn't turn but it keep cooking. The walls inside get hot. The only way to turn it off is to unplug it. We called GE service and they are coming out this week. It's a good thing we noticed it running or it would have just kept cooking.
justification: The microwave keeps running after closing the door, which could lead to overheating or fire, but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
Today our oven overheated and burned what was baking.  In about 10 minutes it burned items that should have taken close to 30 minutes to bake at that temperature, so it was considerably over the heat selected and indicated on the digital face.  Upon smelling the burning we turned off the oven, at which point sparks flew from the control panel.  This thing is a fire hazard.

Kenmore Electric Range, model 790.97432801
justification: The oven overheated and caused sparks, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The knobs on the stove do not lock and easily get moved into the gas on position by nudging or when cleaning. We have had them go accidentally many times and didn't know it until someone smelled gas.
justification: The incident involves gas being accidentally turned on, posing a risk but no reported injury, and it has occurred many times.

incident_description:
In April, 2001, we purchased an Amana model ACF3375A gas range for $705 from Metro Builders Supply in Springfield.  We now face the prospect of buying a replacement because of a faulty door hinge (part number 31946302), for which there are no available replacement parts.

Because of the faulty hinge, the oven door will not close tightly and heat escapes from above the door, creating both a fire and injury risk.  The burner control knobs above the oven door get too hot to touch.

I have had a repairman here who says the parts are not available.  Extensive searching online has confirmed that.  Obviously there was a design fault so severe that all the available replacement parts have been utilized.
justification: The faulty hinge creates a fire and injury risk, with burner control knobs too hot to touch, indicating potential for burns.

incident_description:
The consumer has a microwave/oven combination unit where the mirowave is located above the oven. 
The consumer stated that she turned on the oven on self clean mode. The consumer stated that the oven was set to self clean for  approximtely 2 hours.
The consumer stated that the microwave glass exploded.  The consumer stated that the shattered glass went all over the kitchen.
The consumer contacted the manf on 3/24/14 and they informed her that they would repair the unit for her. The manf would pay for the expense. 
The unit is not under warranty. 
The consumer has previously used the self clean feature in the oven.
There are no recalls on the unit.
justification: The microwave glass exploded, causing shattered glass to spread, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
3/18/14 Caller stated that he turned on the control panel for the electric oven and burner and flames erupted from the back of the control panel about few mins later after turning it on scorching the back wall where the unit is located.  The flames were about 6 inches high he immediately used the fire extinguisher to contain the fire. There were no prior services or incidents with the unit.  The electric range remains inoperable at this time.

3/27/14 The manufacturer was contacted and he was referred to the recall hotline, the recall hotline referred him to the agency.
Caller is concerned that this range is fire hazard and should be recalled.
The product is not part of a recall.
justification: The incident involved flames and required a fire extinguisher, but there were no injuries or deaths reported.

incident_description: Slicing cheese, handle broke on the knife I was using. This has happened before with a different knife from the same set.. Sent knife back, company replaced the knife.
justification: The handle broke during use, but no injury was reported. This has happened before with a similar knife, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
The Ewave over the stove microwave oven caught fire while not in use.  

The oven began cracking and popping as it caught fire.  There was nothing in the oven at the time it caught fire.  The fire melted the oven, burnt the three cabinets that surround the oven and caused smoke damage throughout the house.

A fire investigator hired by the insurance company showed us where the fire started, behind the touch pad.
justification: The fire caused smoke damage and burnt the cabinets, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Glass suddenly and unexpectedly broke in my hand while I was holding it.  Shortly after filling the glass with ice and soda, the bottom of the glass detached and fell to the floor.  My reflex reaction to the falling piece of glass was to try and catch it.  In doing so, the glass sliced a large chunk of skin off my fingertip.  The wound is sizeable, bled profusely, and will most likely leave a pretty noticeable scar since I was unable to recover the severed piece of flesh.  Went to my family doctor the following day and was told that wound could not be stitched due to the amount that was missing.
justification: The incident caused a sizeable wound that bled profusely and will most likely leave a noticeable scar, indicating a level of injury.

incident_description: Son cooking fish sticks in toaster oven.  Heard a pop.  There were flames between the outside of the oven and the inner box of the panel (looking at oven it was the back, top where the wire feeds into the top of the cooking part of the oven).  Was able to unplug and move outside prior to any property damage.
justification: The incident caused flames but was resolved without injury or property damage, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
Several types of Black and Decker broiler ovens have had the same problem.  I have had one fire because of it.  They keep replacing with better stovetop oven broilers but they all have the same problem.  Someone is going to get very hurt.

The on off switch can turn on but when you counterclockwise turn it off it goes further than off into another area where is is on but looks like it is turned off. ALL of their products have had the same problem and they never apparently attempt to fix them.
justification: The incident caused a fire, but no injury was reported, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description:
03/10/14- The consumer stated that she sensed a light burning plastic odor coming from her refrigerator. She opened the refrigerator and remove milk from the top shelf. When the consumer ingested the milk she sensed that the it was too warm compared to the temperature setting of the refrigerator. Her husband touched the light bulb casing inside of the unit and noticed that it was hot to the touch. The consumer turned off the internal light bulb switches inside of the refrigerator and the light bulbs would not turn off. She decided to remove the two light bulbs. Once the light bulbs were outside of the refrigerator, she noticed brown stains around the socket of the light bulbs.
3/31/14- The consumer contacted the manufacturer. She was advised that since the refrigerator was out of warranty coverage there would be a $89.00 fee plus cost of repairs for a technician to inspect and repair the refrigerator. The consumer declined the offer.
The consumer thinks this product poses a fire or burn hazard .
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Caller and her husband were given a toaster oven for Christmas and had no problems with it until March 19th, 2014 when the glass from the door exploded sending glass everywhere.
The toaster oven hadn't been used for about one month.
The caller placed a chicken patty in the toaster oven, turned it on, walked to another area of the kitchen and within two minutes at the most the glass in the door to the toaster oven exploded sending glass from directly in front of the unit to as far away as three feet from the unit.

There were no injuries to report
She contacted the manufacturer March 19th, 2014 and was advised that they had no reports of this type of incident happening. 
The caller did not capture the name of the rep she spoke with, the rep took a report but did not provide a report number to the caller.
justification: The incident was an incident with no injury, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 1 because the incident was rare.

incident_description:
Home was buit in 2008 and electric range was in home when caller moved into home.
He had small issues with the range prior to September 2013 but nothing he felt was a safety hazard.
The caller states that his appliance model and serial numbers are very near the one's recalled.
He states that after use his front two burners many times remain on after he turns them off then 10% of the time the burners don't turn off when the knob is turned to off.
90% of the time his burners work but that the 10% that they do not then he has to turn them on and off a few times before they will remain off.
There have been no injuries to report
The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range with no reported injuries, and the issue occurs 10% of the time, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: OVEN OVER HEATS AND CAN BURN/CATCH FIRE CONTENTS IN OVEN.  THE OVEN DOES NOT MAINTAIN THE HEAT OF WHICH IT IS SET AT.  IF SET AT 350 SOMETIMES IT GOES TO ONLY 250 OR SO AND OTHERS OVER 500 !!!  YOU NEVER KNOW IF IT WILL JUMP HIGH OR NOT....EVEN IF I CHECK IT WHILE BAKING IT MAY AT THAT TIME READ AN OKAY TEMPERATURE BUT WITHIN MINUTES IT CAN JUMP OVER 500 DEGREES AND POTENTIAL CAUSE A FIRE.  VERY UNSAFE !
justification: The oven overheating can cause a fire, which can lead to injury or death, making the severity level 3.

incident_description:
Range control knobs on the front of the range can be easily operated by a young child resulting in potential gas release, fire if something is on top of the range, or burns to the child

The knob requires that you push them in approximately 1/8 inch before they will turn.  My 18 month old who is barely 30 inches tall can reach up and operate the knobs.  While we watch him closely and have child-proofed our cabinets and doors, he has turned the knobs on the range to the point where gas was flowing yet the igniter was not yet engaged, resulting in gas leaking into the room.  On other occasions he has turned the burners on, off, or changed the settings of an operating burner.

I informed LG technical support about this hazard and asked if some sort of cover was available to prevent a child from operating the knobs from below.  I was told that there was no cover available and that the push-turn lock function was enough to prevent a child from operating them, even though I explained how my child had already done so.  I have had to fashion my own cover that extends from beneath the knobs and allows access only from above.
justification: The incident describes potential for burns or gas-related injuries, and the child has already operated the knobs multiple times, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
A baby/toddler dropped a new sippy cup, about 1/2 full of water, from table height onto a tile kitchen floor. The lower section of the cup shattered, leaving several sharp edges on the remains of the cup, and three completely broken off, sharp edged, pieces.  The broken pieces would easily be swallowable.

It seems like a baby's sippy cup simply being dropped to the floor should not create dangerous sharp fractured pieces.

The cup is labeled
Sippy Cup
200 09 1639  ID054422
Dist by Target Corpl, Mpls., MN 55403
Made in China
@2014 Target Brands, Inc
bar code is:  92000 91639
justification: The incident resulted in sharp broken pieces that could be swallowable, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
GE Model JKP905P4SS, Serial FA607089Q installed on June 7, 2013, in our residence, as part of kitchen remodel. Unit was purchased on March 12, 2013 from local Home Depot Store. Unit tag indicates it was manufactured March 2013.

On April 3, 2013 at 7:45AM bacon was cooked in the unit. Bacon was taken out of unit and unit door was closed and fan stayed on. At approx 8AM, noticed the display was dark, the fan was off and left the kitchen. Returned to the kitchen at approx 9:30AM and the microwave's display indicated the clock needed to be reset which was done. Opened the microwave door and the inside was very hot, closed the door and noticed the fan was running. Oven mittens were required to remove the glass turntable and left the door open thinking it would help the microwave cool down. At 11:45AM closed the microwave door and the fan started. Crackling and popping started and smoke started to come out of the top vents above the microwave. The door was opened and the crackling and popping stopped. The main electrical breaker for the microwave oven cooking center was turned off. The smoke stopped, but the possibility of a fire within the built-in cabinet existed and GE was called at approx 12 noon to determine the proper course of action. It was not possible to speak with a person so a message was left and the call was returned by [REDACTED] at approx 4:10PM but did not speak with her until Friday and gave her the details provided above.

GE sent a service technician on April 7, 2014, who removed the microwave's control panel and energized the unit. After several minutes, the technician reported the noise heard was the magnetron energizing and not the fan running, as we thought, because a relay on the microwave's control board was stuck in the on position. The technician disconnected wires from the microwave's circuit board and said the breaker could be re-energized and the oven portion of the unit was safe to use until he returned to replace the microwave's control board and the magnetron later in the week. 

While the unit's control panel was open we noticed both circuit control boards for the unit had dates of November 9, 2007 while the unit's manufacture date was March 2013.

We are very concerned about the exposure to a fire risk, in an inaccessible cabinet, that the unit presented to our home and ourselves.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire risk but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore smooth top stove/oven combination. It was manufactured in 2003.  

This afternoon my wife made two loafs of homemade bread in the oven. She set the oven at 350 for 29 minutes. We went outside to work in the yard. 20 minutes later the smoke alarms in the house started to sound. We entered the house to find it full of smoke. My wife pushed the cancel button to turn off the oven.  She took the two loafs of charcoal outside.  

I started opening windows and getting fans out to get the smoke out.  My wife told me the broiler was on and would not shut off.  We pressed the cancel button on the display which indicated everything was off but the broiler burners were still on.  The broiler must have started on its own.  To shut it off I had to trip the breaker.  I allowed the oven to cool before turning the breaker back on. Upon turning the breaker on the broiler started again (display didn't indicate anything was on).

I am thankful we didn't set the timer on the oven to start while we were gone or we could have had a fire. 

After calling three numbers and getting a run around I finally was able to talk with someone that basically said they could send out a repair man for a minimum charge of $75.00.  I wasn't satisfied with this so I requested to speak with the manager.  The manager was very professional but all he could offer me was 10% off of a service call.  I no longer feel comfortable using this oven even if it does get "repaired".  

We left our windows open for a couple hours (about 62 degrees out). Everything still smells like smoke. 

I am not happy about this!  Shouldn't a company stand by there product. This is a major hazard!  These units should be recalled!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that produced excessive smoke but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I had just finished baking macaroni and cheese at three hundred fifty (350) degrees for twenty minutes. I removed
the dish from the oven, set it on the counter, and closed the oven door. The outer glass in the closed oven door
shattered and spewed across the floor with a loud explosion. I wish to note that this is a replacement door. A similar
incident occurred on the morning of October 24, 2013. I filed a report, including pictures, with the CPSC after that
incident. This door, the subject of THIS incident report, is the replacement door that I paid to have Installed after the
October incident. Please note that this door exploded five (5) months after the previous incident. The October 2013
incident occurred in the morning before the oven was turned on. It was cold. All uses of this stove have been well
within what is conventional usage. We have used it only for baking and broiling. After the October incident, I went
to the Sears web site to look to see if others had reported similar experiences. I noticed that there were quite a few
questions about replacing the oven door on the model of the stove that is the subject of this report. There were also
reported incidents of the glass spontaneously exploding on their web site. I suggested to Sears and to the CPSC (on
both of your web sites) that this was likely a product defect. I also warned that the potential exists for an individual,
or child to experience serious injury if their faces are in the vicinity of this door when it 'destructs'. I still believe that
to be the case and seriously ask that a recall be Issued immediately.! have pictures of the results of the incident that
is the subject of this report.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
I purchased a new Samsung side by side Refrigerator model RSG257AARS/XAA from sears on Saturday May 11th, 2013. After six months of use, we noticed a strong odor coming from the back of the refrigerator. Around the same time we noticed the smell our family including my daughter recently came down with upper respiratory infection. After further inspection and removing of the back panel I noticed standing water from the defrost cycle. The water was covered in mold and the compressor fan was blowing the mold into the air we breath. 
We called Samsung to complain, the sent out a technician who poured bleach into the bottom of the refrigerator. This was temporary fix and now the moldy water is back.
I believe refrigerators without a removable drip pan are a hazard to the consumers health. All refrigerators should come with a removable defrost pan.
justification: The incident caused an upper respiratory infection due to mold exposure, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is recurring but not universal, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she made her pot of coffee. The consumer stated that the coffee maker was on warm mode for about 20-30 minutes. The consumer stated that she heard noise coming from the coffee maker like it was trying to brew again.

The consumer stated that the coffee maker was really hot and the coffee in the pot was bubbling. The consumer stated that she smelled strong odor like plastic/electrical burning. The consumer stated that there was smoke coming from the top and base of the coffee maker.

The consumer unplugged the unit and put it in the sink. The consumer stated that she let the coffee maker cool in the sink.

The consumer contacted the manf. The manf informed her that they had no other reports or problems know to them for that model. They informed her that they would send out a replacement coffee maker if the consumer can cut the cord and send it in to them. 

The consumer informed the manf rep that she did not want the same model as a replacement. The consumer was told by the manf rep that they had fixed the problem and that this coffee maker would be fine. 

The consumer stated that if the rep informed her that there was no problem with the coffee maker, how can they tell her that they fixed the problem.

The consumer stated that she had filled out a registration card for the coffee maker. The consumer asked the manf rep for the purchase date of her coffee maker. The rep informed the consumer that she cannot give that information out but her 3 year warranty had expired.

There are no recalls on this coffee maker.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker with smoke and burning odor, but no injury or death occurred. The manufacturer's lack of prior reports suggests this is an unlikely occurrence.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire range's control panel burst into flames.  I pushed the button for broil and the control panel made a popping sound and flames approximately 9 inches tall came from the back of the control panel and up the wall.  They burned for several seconds and then went out.
This is a Frigidaire electric range model number GLEFM397DQA.  Serial number VF45109660. It is 9 and a half years old.  I called Frigidaire and after being on hold for a long time the woman told me that if it was still under warranty or an extended warranty that I had purchased they would see about getting it repaired and that there was no recall on it.  I politely asked if Frigidaire cared that their product could have burnt my house down and didn't they feel that an actual fire was a circumstance that would justify service outside of the warranty period and they hung up on me.  
I feel people need to know that this range could burn their house down with no warning and that Frigidaire doesn't care.
justification: The incident involved flames from the control panel but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a GE range in January 2013 (model PS905TP).  From the day it was installed I have complained the dual burner does not work properly.  When the small burner is turned on the entire burner comes on making it extremely unsafe.  After burning my arm I had to quit using the small burner all  together. I paid a lot for this range, and it is disappointing I cannot use all the burners because I am concerned about getting burned.  A non GE repairman said he had never seen a dual burner without a divider.  This is not our first range with a dual burner,  but this is the first time we have had a problem with a dual burner.
justification: The incident involves a serious injury, which is a 3 on the severity level, and the occurrence likelihood is 4 because the problem is almost certain to occur.

The consumer stated that she had the oven on self-clean mode. The consumer stated that this was the first time she used the self clean mode.

The consumer stated that she smelled plastic burning while the oven was in clean mode. The consumer stated that after the clean mode was over, she noticed that the oven door melted around the top edge.

The consumer stated that there was no smoke or sparks. 

On 8/12/13, the consumer contacted the manf after seeing recall #01-236.  The consumer contacted Maytag regarding the recall. They informed her that they didn't have a recall on it. The consumer was provided information for AE Factory Service to schedule a repair.

The consumer was informed by AE Factory Service that they would send out repairman to inspect. The repairman informed the consumer that she would have to pay for the repair. 

The consumer called again regarding the recall. The consumer stated that her unit is recalled so she should not have to pay for repair work. The rep informed her that they would send out another repairman. The second repairman informed her the same thing as the first one.

The second repairman informed her that the unit is not worth fixing because it was going to be too expensive. He also informed the consumer that this occurred due to an operator error. He stated that the door did not latch properly while the unit was in self-clean mode. The consumer does not understand how that is possible since the door locks while in self-clean mode. 

The consumer has discarded the unit and replaced it. 

The consumer stated that when she called Amana #, they kept telling her there was no recall. The consumer stated that they were not willing to acknowledge the recall.

The consumer's model and serial #s are included in recall #01-236.


The consumer contacted: 
866-640-7146 X [REDACTED] (Amana)
1-800-771-3029 (AE Factory Service - Repair)

incident_description: I own a Bonavita 1800 Glass Carafe Coffee Maker.  I have had 2 separate incidents as of today where, after brewing, I have tried to insert the carafe cap onto the carafe.  (The design of this coffee maker is such that the brewing basket sits directly on the carafe and is removed after brewing is complete.)  On the 1st incident, I was attempting to put the cap on the carafe and it pushed all the way through into the brewed coffee.  I did not experience an injury but had to retrieve the cap out of the hot coffee.  On today's incident, I was attempting to put the cap in place and it again pushed through into the coffee.  This time my hand went in with the cap and submerged up to my wrist (I had brewed a full 8 cup carafe).  Coffee splashed over my clothes, the counter and the floor.  My hand suffered burns equivalent to a sunburn, especially at my wrist.  I took photos of my hand, my clothes and the cap inside the carafe.  Thankfully, the carafe did not break as I could have also have broken glass and possible cuts.
justification: The incident caused burns to the hand, which is a injury, but not a death or serious injury.

incident_description:

The consumer tried to turn the fryer around to see the back of the appliance when she got burnt on her second and third finger of her right hand by melted plastic that was dripping from the back of the deep fryer. The consumer disconnected the appliance and proceeded to apply cold water to her burnt fingers. She discontinued the use of the deep fryer. The consumer had blisters on her fingers for three days after the incident.
 
2/19/14- The consumer contacted the retailer/manufacturer. The retailer/manufacturer customer service agent indicated to the consumer that her claim would be evaluated by a specialist, but since she bought the product almost one year ago there was nothing they could do for her.
 
The consumer thinks her deep fryer poses a fire hazard to the consumers and should be reported.
 
This product is not affected by a recall.
justification: The consumer suffered burns with blisters, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident involved a specific malfunction, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
Just yesterday we were preheating our Kenmore Elite 790 and the control panel caught fire and spread to the wall. Thankfully I was in the kitchen and was able to grab a fire extinguisher in time. I have made numerous phone calls but because the unit is out of warranty I have been unable to get anywhere with Sears and Kenmore. They seam indifferent to the apparent risks that this unit poses.

I have read descriptions of situations similar to mine at the link below:

https://www.sears.com/community/questions/kenmore-electric-range-model-790-control-panel-burned-out-in-less-than-5-years/

I have found out that Frigidaire actually manufactured the KE790 that I have, and interestingly enough the serial
number matches that of a Frigidaire recall for fire hazard. I wonder whether or not this unit was intended to be
included in the 2009 Kenmore recall and if so, consumers should be instructed to cross reference both the Frigidaire recall list and the Kenmore recall list. Considering the fire danger this unit poses and the fact that it may have been intended to be part of the earlier recall, I believe that this unit should be recalled.
justification: The incident caused a fire but no injury, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: While cooking on electric range, LED panel caught fire.

incident_description: Our microwave caught on fire. I was cooking oatmeal in a bowl, it was only set for 2 1/2 minutes. I heard a crackling noise and looked and saw flames shooting down into the microwave. They kept getting larger and larger. I grabbed the fire extinguisher and evacuated my grandchildren, and turned off the power at the breaker box. I did not open the microwave, not wanting to add oxygen to the flames. The gire eventually went out. After an hour or so, I opened the door and saw that the top of the microwave had melted down toward the center. There was a chemical type smell. I emailed GE. I looked for recall information. Our exact GE Profile microwave was not in a recall, but one similar was. We had a fire with our GE dishwasher less than 3 months ago and did not realize it was in a recall. We have already replaced it.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was extinguished without injury, though it caused significant damage and a chemical smell.

incident_description:
Kenmore range model # 790.95662102

We had an issue with our Kenmore range which, if we had not been paying attention, would have absolutely resulted in a fire.

My wife was cooking a cake in the range, on bake @ 350 degrees.   After 15 minutes notice smoke in the kitchen and when we opened the door noticed that the top of the cake was burnt to a crisp and that the temp of the oven was well above where it should have been.  What we also noticed is that the broil element was on, apparently full strength.  Thinking this was human error, we attempted to shut off the oven and restart with a new batch.  At that time we were unable to turn the oven off and after a few minutes, recognizing that this was a dangerous situation, switched off the main breaker to the stove.   30 minutes later when things had cooled down, we turned the oven onto bake, 350 degrees and after about 1 minute noticed that the broiler element came on, full power, and was unable to turn it off using the switches on the stove.  Killed the breaker again and unplugged the stove permanently.  After further inspection we noticed that the paint around the vent on the stove had gotten so hot that it had bubbled.

To sum it up:

1.)	Stove will go from low bake to full broil without the user knowing creating a dangerous situation which could result in a fire
2.)	Stove will not shut off once it is in this state

Thanks
justification: The incident could have resulted in a fire, but no injury was reported.

After disconnecting the dishwasher from electricity I disassembled the front door of the dishwasher where the smell was the strongest and found that the main electrical board was charred and melted through.

THE INSTALLER TOLD MY HUSBAND TO SET THE OVEN AT 350 ABOUT 20 MINUTES TO ALLOW THE "NEW SMELL" TO BURN OFF BEFORE PUTTING ANY FOOD IN THERE.  HE WAITED FOR 30 MINUTES. THEN HE INCREASED THE TEMP TO 375 AND PUT A FROZEN DINNER IN THE OVEN.  ABOUT 25 MINUTES LATER WE HEARD A LOUD "POP".  HE RAN INTO THE KITCHEN AND SAW THAT THE GLASS ON THE INSIDE OF THE OVEN DOOR HAD EXPLODED ALL OVER THE OVEN AND THE DINNER!  WHEN WE SLOWLY OPENED THE DOOR, "NUGGETS" OF GLASS FELL EVERYWHERE AND EVEN INTO THE GAP BETWEEN THE DOOR AND THE RANGE.

incident_description:
I am writing to bring to your attention a situation in which the bottom melted and fell out of a Beka brand water kettle.  The melted metal parts in turn burned my kitchen floor and counter top and my hand.  I believe this product to be extremely dangerous and that it should not be allowed to be sold in the United States.

I have written the company asking them to contact me to make arrangements to pay for the cost of repairs to my house and to my hand, but they have not replied.

Specifically, the product is a  Beka Cookware Claudine Water Kettle - 4.25 Quart that I purchased through Amazon.  

I have also written to Amazon.  Their automated systems seem willing to allow me to return the kettle, but they have not responded to my request for assistance in repairing damages.

Several photos are attached.  There are other photos including one of my burned hand.

Please let me know whether there are similar reports on file with your office and what I need to do to establish an official record and investigation.

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

The consumer turned his oven on bake setting at 350 degrees for about 5 minutes when he noticed that a considerable amount of sparks and smoke was emitting from the control panel and the back of the range. Last week I decided to use the self cleaning feature for the first time since the repair.  Since then the oven thermostat sometimes works and at other times, the oven temperature heats up well above the selected temperature.  Hotter than I would ever set it and the door is unlocked.

incident_description:
Product: KitchenAid wall oven, model # KEMS308SSS05, serial # D13598342, in-service date 6/21/12 (currently beyond the manufacturer's 12-month limited warranty)

Incident: Saturday, March 22, 2014 @ 12:17 PM (MST)

Location: Residence @ [REDACTED] in Mancos, Colorado

My KitchenAid wall oven was approximately 2 hours into its "self-cleaning" cycle when the door's INNER glass exploded violently akin to a shotgun blast, spewing both beads and dagger-like chards of glass into my kitchen from beneath its closed and locked door. (and despite its OUTER door glass remaining intact!) One would logically assume that the door's perimeter gasket would contain what's inside the oven! 

A violent glass explosion that's contained is one issue, but the abrupt ejection of broken glass past a closed and locked oven door into the kitchen space is clearly a major safety concern in my opinion. I was seated approximately 15 feet from the appliance when the glass exploded, but was fortunately uninjured. The subject appliance was registered with KitchenAid when purchased and I have never received any recall notices or bulletins from them. 

Why would an oven door glass suddenly "explode" for no apparent reason? Has there ever been similar incidents reported to your agency with KitchenAid wall ovens?

I have thorough photo documentation and video footage, both immediately following the event and when the self-cleaning cycle had ended and allowing me to open the oven door for a look. I have also preserved the oven door's glass beads and chards as forensic evidence.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a violent explosion of glass that could have caused injury.

incident_description: electric range surface unit goes to high heat setting (unit glows cherry red), regardless of setting of control.  this has happened the last two ranges we have owned and is currently happening to the range we own now.  the problem is intermittent at first, but gradually becomes constant.  This has happened on two different brands.  if the surface unit control is going to fail, for safety it should go to an off state NOT full HIGH.  this has happened a total of six times, all four controls on a Frigidaire and currently on two units of a Tappan.  please note that this has the potential of causing fires attributed to "food left unattended".  while this is technically correct, the fire would occur in a much shorter time frame than if the control was working properly.  It would also be much harder for firemen to find at the scene due to knobs melting and general destruction that occurs during a fire.  to state,  surface unit is turned on to medium heat (I seldom use high setting), either immediately or after a period of time (usually seconds to minutes) the surface unit goes to high heat.  this has to be a control issue because if there was a short to ground the surface unit would not go to high heat.  a ground would cause the unit to heat at about medium heat (120 volts) and high heat requires the voltage controlled by the unit control (220 volts0
justification: The incident describes a recurring malfunction that poses a significant fire hazard, which could lead to injury or property damage, and has happened multiple times across different brands.

incident_description:
RE:  Yoshi blade
I am writing to point out how dangerous this product is and to suggest that the product be removed from availability in the United States.  The first time we used the Yoshi knife the tip of the knife broke off.  Fortunately, we saw this happen and we were able to dispose of the meat is was used to cut.  We put it away and decided to use it only on softer items in the future.  It was used only a couple of times in over a few years for cutting bread.  Last December we decided to use this knife to slice new potatoes.  A chunk of the blade broke off but it was not immediately noticed.  We had to toss 2 pounds of potatoes rather than take a chance on someone ingesting the blade.

In trying to locate information on this company today so that I could send a complaint I came across a huge number of comsumer complaints about the blade breaking or chunks breaking off.  This indicates a very dangerous situation.

I would like to suggest this item be investigated and indeed that it should be barred from sale to consumers in the United States due to its dangerous composition.

Thank you.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous product with multiple reports of blade breakage, but no actual injuries were reported in this case.

I read that it is safety glass, but it projected hard enough that I felt those glass pieces hit my arm as it exploded. It is 3 days later and I am still sweeping up glass. The model of the oven that shattered is 790.47769405. Consumers need to be made aware of the possibility of that glass front exploding. If my 6 year old niece, or any small child or pet had been standing near that oven when the glass exploded, they would have gotten glass in their face. That is very dangerous.

incident_description: The flame control knobs on my LG gas range repeatedly fail, often resulting in gas leaking even when knobs are in the off position. LG replacement parts for the same model also fail within days of normal use. There is an internal plastic component in the knobs which fractures (possibly due to heat) and this prevents the knob from engaging the flame control mechanisms. This has resulted in delayed ignition, flares, and most commonly, gas leakage. There are numerous complaints online regarding the same issue and the same model #. LG sends replacements knobs which also fail.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage and potential flares, which could lead to injury or fire, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire smooth stove top burners start in the "high" setting, regardless of temperature on dial. When a low to
medium temperature is selected on the dial and the burner ignites at the high setting, the dial cannot reduce or
turn off the burner and the electrical breaker switch must be disengaged. One burner (left front) starts randomly (in high setting) without ever being turned on. When the stove is not in use, the breaker switch must be disengaged.
This pattern of unsafe behavior started within the first year after purchase. The heat generated is enough that an
aluminum pan has deformed by melting and a glass pan has exploded. Nothing can be left on the smooth top
surface unless the breaker is off.
When I began contacting Electrolux/Frigidaire in 2008, I was told that they had this same model which was having
similar issues, but ours wasn't produced at the same manufacturing facility so it didn't qualify. I have received minor burns and cuts, through gaining experience of how to use a stove with a mind of it's own. I just cannot believe that this company can deny that an operating issue isn't included in a recall, while the behavior is identical.
justification: The incident involves burns and cuts from a malfunctioning stove, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue is persistent and has caused multiple incidents, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
This product is extremely dangerous. We purchased this product at Fry's Food Store as part of a Fry's promotional piece which was announced over the loud speaker. The person arrived to give everyone free gifts and then proceeded with a presentation--- he used the slicer with his hands.  We asked the Chef if this slicer was safe for children--he responded that it was very safe.  I purchased the slicer for my 14 year old daughter.  Upon arriving home, I attempted to use it on a tomato to demonstrate to her how to use it and---- within seconds---I suffered a severe laceration to my right thumb. The injury resulted in 5 stitches and doctor ordered absolutely no use of the hand for three (3) days. 

I have googled this product and noticed there are several similar incidents on the internet--also with photos. The ER mentioned that they had also stitched-up other victims who tried this slicer.

The consumer stated that his wife was using the dishwasher and she stated to smell a burning plastic odor. The consumer stated that she opened the dishwasher and it turned off the cycle. The consumer stated that his wife called for him, he came in closed the door of the dishwasher and noticed that the smoke was being emitted from the right side of the door. The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they removed the dishwasher from his home. The consumer stated that he purchased a new dishwasher.

He stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they did not provide any assistance.

incident_description: The consumer was cooking when she noticed something burning after about 15 minutes.  She noticed a bit of smoke was coming from the back of the stove. GE gas range

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire stove that was purchased in March of 2010.  This morning I turned the oven on the preheat and turned away to wash some dishes.  I heard the sound of glass shattering and turned to see the outer glass in my stove door had completely shattered. My husband is bedridden with cancer and we live off social security so we can't repair it ourselves and can't afford to have it repaired.  We are basically screwed because no one will take responsibility for this issue.

 A couple of hours later on, he was loading the dishwasher again. The consumer stated that the inside of the dishwasher was extremely hot again.  He opened the door again. The consumer stated that it seem as if the heating element would go off if the door remained open.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his microwave in April 2006 and has had no problems with it until February 26th, 2014 when he opened the door and it automatically turned itself on while the door was open.
He had not touched the controls nor had he placed his food in the unit.
He is reporting this microwave due the belief that if it is running with the door open there could be radiation escaping.

There have been no injuries to report
Caller contacted the manufacturer February 26th, 2014 and was advised that they would send a tech to his home at his expense.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on with the door open, posing a potential radiation risk, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I started my dishwasher. After approximately 10 minutes, the dishwasher began to emit an electrical arcing noise and smoke appeared at the top of the door. I opened the door and saw arc flash and flame coming from the top of the door, right hand side. I had to disconnect power fro the appliance to disable it.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing, smoke, and flame, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I cooked something at 325 for 20 minutes... then took it out of the oven and turned the oven off. About 10 minutes later, I heard a huge explosion from the kitchen and saw the the door glass had shattered. I took a picture.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My glass top Kenmore oven, Model #95022101, has gone haywire and is a serious fire hazard.  I came home from a meeting today to discover the kitchen filled with smoke as if the self-cleaning feature had been turned on, but it had not.  In fact, the power was off.  The oven door was not locked.  I finally had to pull it out from the wall and unplug the whole unit.

After it cooled down I tried plugging it back in, and even tho I kept punching the off button, the heating elements inside turned on.

This apparently has happened to a number of people with the Kenmore glass top models labeled "Ultra Bake Self-cleaning Super Capacity" and I think this entire line should be recalled.  I shudder to think what may have happened had I not come home in time.   My kitchen counters on both sides were blazing hot.

I will not be purchasing any more Kenmore appliances because I am concerned for my family's safety.  I have 5 children, and I cannot have my oven turning on spontaneously like that.
justification: The incident describes a serious fire hazard with potential for injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I have a Kitchen Aid Dishwasher that the circuit board shorted out while the unit was running and could easily have caught fire. I am a retired fire fighter and identified the smell of plastic / electrical burning and finally pinpointed it to the area of the running dishwasher. I noticed smoke coming out of the side of the dishwasher door and shut off the unit. I opened the dishwasher compartment and could feel the heat on the inside of the Stainless Steel door. I have since Purchased a replacement circuit board and changed it out which also required me to repair the melted wire plug. I am currently using the repaired dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard but was detected and mitigated without injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Elite 7800 double oven in 2009.  The control panel goes out when you boil liquid on the back two burners.  The control panel overheats and turns off.  When the control panel goes out the ovens quit working you could be in the middle of cooking and it will go off.  You have to wait until it cools off to get the control panel to work again.  Sometimes the control panel turns on the oven after it over heats.  You just never know.  I looked up this problem on line and it seems that sears has corrected this design flaw.  That's what there repair men call it.  But they do not want to give the poor people that bought the older version in 2008 or 2009.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning control panel that disrupts oven operation but does not cause injury or death.

incident_description:
Using Sango Brand Microwave safe, dinner ware plate. Plate was put in microwave at level 10 setting for 90 seconds, with a piece of beef. (Approximately 9 ounces). On touching the plate, received  severe blistering burns to middle, index finger and thumb.


Sango  Newport Cream 3022 Microwave, Oven safe Dishwashersafe (China)
justification: The incident resulted in severe blistering burns, indicating injury (severity 3). Microwave-safe plates causing burns is a known but not extremely common issue (likelihood 3).

incident_description: I have a Kenmore glasstop range/oven.  Model number 790.9642240c.  I was trying to preheat it when I got a message and beep on the display.  The message was F10.  I turned the oven off, but it turned on again spontaneously.  No matter what I did, it kept turning on and continued to get hotter and hotter.  I finally pulled the stove away from the wall and unplugged it.  I called Sears. They took my information, told me that there was no recall when I asked them, and said that they could send someone out to repair the appliance.  I declined because I have already gone around and around with Sears about a dishwasher that continues to have the same electrical problem over and over again.  I am not paying a few hundred dollars to fix something that will not stay fixed.  I am totally disgusted with Sears.  I have also read other posts on this site from people who have had similar problems.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and turned on spontaneously, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Refrigerator light did not shut off creating such heat that it melted the cover of the light. There was a smell of burning plastic.  It was so hot that all food in upper shelves was hot.  We had to unplug refrigerator to let the light bulbs cool enough to remove them.  There is still a smell of melted plastic in the refrigerator.  All perishable food had to be discarded.  Fortunately we were at home at the time or this would have caused a fire.
justification: The incident caused property damage and food loss but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for fire if unattended.

incident_description:
I currently have a Maytag dishwasher that is leaking water on it's power lines.  This could potentially be a fire hazard.  

Please see "Maytag Recalls Dishwashers Due to Fire Hazard" Release #07-094.  My dishwasher has the same model number in the above article but I was told because the serial numbers did not match I was not eligible to have this fixed.  I find this ridiculous when as I said the model numbers match and I am experiencing water coming in to contact with the power lines.

I would like the rebate available and not to have this product fixed due to the fact I am concerned with it's safety.

My model is MDB7600AWW, serial number 14177130ax.
justification: The dishwasher is leaking water onto power lines, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore Elite Range that the racks fall off all the time.  It initially was occasional and we just dealt with it, but now they have fallen several times causing steaming food to spill everywhere.
justification: The racks falling off is a recurring incident causing spills but no reported injuries.

incident_description: On 3-10-14, we started the dishwasher.  Kitchenaid KUDP01ILBL5 SER # FR2501653.  After several minutes, while still in the kitchen, I heard a crackling/buzzing sound.  Looked at dishwasher, and white smoke was pouring out of the washer from the washer door.  Had to manually turn breaker off to stop washer, for as the smoke bellowed, the washer continued to run.  House is now filled with foul electrical fire smell.  Checked the Internet, and find out that hundreds if not thousands of these have caught fire in circuit board area (which is definitely where it was coming from).  Please do a recall as soon as possible, as this surely would have burned the house down if we had not been standing right nearby at the time!  The time to deal with this has come - people are going to be hurt or killed by these fires if something is not done. There is no excuse for this to be happening, even if the washer is almost 10 years old.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This Spacemaker GE Model HVM1540DN1BB spontaneously started when no one was in the kitchen.The licensed GE repair person reseated the touchpad ribbon after determining it was not worth replacing  keypad and it worked for a few weeks, then turned itself on again-this time late at night when no one was in the kitchen. It stopped when the door was left open and then when unplugged. We now keep it unplugged unless needed for use.This is a safety hazard because the cooking chamber was very hot and could have melted or caught fire if we hadn't noticed it. After finding over 100 incidents of this type regarding the GE and [REDACTED] products on line,it is surprising this appliance has not been recalled.
I will not be replacing this microwave with a GE.
justification: The microwave spontaneously turned on, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We had a grease fire in our range due to grease catching fire that drips under the griddle feature. We did not know the grease was there. After the fire we discovered that the griddle design allows grease to drip underneath the griddle.  The manual states you are not supposed to take the griddle apart to clean it. We always cleaned the surface of the griddle but didn't know there was a thick accumulation of grease underneath.  Now we can't use it as it was designed for fear of it happening again.
justification: The incident involved a grease fire but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw and lack of awareness about grease accumulation.

incident_description: Was baking tuna casserole in Anchor Ovenwise Casserole 2qt with lid at 425degrees (oven was preheated) when 5 minutes into baking the lid explode. Larger glass pieces went into the casserole, medium size and tiny pieces of glass went all over oven. I have used this casserole dish many times and did not notice any cracks in the lid.
justification: The incident involved an exploding lid causing glass fragments to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Electric Wall Oven model GLEB27S9DB serial number NF44713663 Even Cook Convection Oven with black smooth face and touch pad control panel.  Purchased November 28, 2004.  I set the oven to convection bake 425 degrees, and in just a few minutes it started making a crackling noise. I turned around and saw sparks in the oven compartment. The control panel started flashing and the "locked" symbol illuminated and smoke started to come out of the vents. The was a strong electrical fire smell.  the oven door was locked and the control panel would not respond, so I turned off the circuit breaker.  The door remained locked.  Removed the control panel and the ribbon relay was scorched.  We have damage to the cabinet above the control panel.  Fear we would have had far more extensive damage had I not been within arms reach of the oven when the issue occurred.

I have pictures of the damage and burned control panel should you wishful to see.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and a locked oven door, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Purchased OXO steel Mandoline at Bed Bath and Beyond.  I read the safety information.  Used the safety guard.  Product slipped and sliced a piece of thumb and needed 4 stitches.  I still do not have some feeling in hand.  Spoke with company and they claim they cannot find an issue with product.  However, I was using it to slice salami.  Cut both ends off to make even edges.  I feel this product should either warn against use with cold cuts and or advise the use of special glove, which I found out later was available for minimal cost.  This product is not safe and I do not want others to suffer the the same fate.  I spoke with company and they will not reimburse for lost wages, suffering and pain, etc.  They wanted to give a little compensation to appease me.  But I feel they need to advise others of the dangers and proper safety equipment available as well as compensate properly.

Please advise.
