My wife had a load of dishes in our GE Adora Stainless steel dishwasher. Model GHDF360R10SS SER
SS718973B. I could smell something hot or burning in the kitchen. It was coming from the area near the
dishwasher. It had a hot rubber or plastic smell. The dishwasher was in the middle of a rinse and hold cycle.
I stopped the cycle and opened the door and could feel very hot air filled with some smoke coming from the
dishwasher.The dishes were so hot that you could not touch them without being burned. Too hot to unload
the dishes. I let them cool down and after inspecting the bottom of the dishwasher i could see that the lower
arm spray assembly had one side of it melted off. The tip was melted into two pieces only being held by the
metal.
plate on the underside. I have ordered a part to replace the part that is ruined. Part PS2339990 at the cost
of $69.62. l feel uneasy about running this dishwasher due to the extreme heat that was coming from the
unit. If this would have happened when we were both out of the house at work, it may have turned into a
serious incident. We will be washing dishes by hand until we resolve this issue. 
I have checked online and found a recall from GE on Adora dishwashers due to fire. The model number on
our unit did not match the recalled product numbers, but I do not know if there is a expanded recall for this

No personal injury has occurred due to this incident.

1/20/14 Caller stated that he noticed his original microwave oven had a hole in the fan cover.  He contacted the manufacturer and he was informed that they are aware of the problem but does not replace the unit until there is a fire.  He contacted the retailer and he received a replacement 1/26/2014 and installed 2/1/2014.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite smoothtop (e.g., glass top) electric range, model number 790 46999 1000, serial number NF 12608551 manufactured in June, 2001 in Canada and sold to me by my local Sears store here in Jacksonville,
Florida in 2001. It is a slideÃÂin style rather than a freestanding style. It should have been among the 200,000 Frigidaire & Kenmore smoothtop electric ranges recalled on August 27, 2009 & April 5, 2011 by Sears after
investigations by the Consumer Product Safety Commission but it was not included in either. The same range was also recalled by Sears Canada on August 26, 2009.

Like the freestanding models that were recalled mine heats to different temperatures than selected, posing a fire and burn hazard to consumers. Specifically, it has only two possible temperature settings: high and off.
When you turn on the range top, no matter what temperature you select, from Lo, 1 through 9, or High, the range top element heats immediately to the highest setting and remains there regardless of adjustment until it is turned off. This does not happen as a single or occasional incident. It happens every time the top of the range is in use. (The oven works fine. Just the range top is malfunctioning and getting worse as time goes by. High is getting hotter.

I have talked to Sears about it many times, including in person in the store where I purchased it. Sears has been totally unresponsive. This slide-in range is identical to the freestanding models that were recalled with the same
combination rotary dial controls for the cook top and digital controls for the oven. On my range, because it is a slide-in model, the controls are on the front rather than the back, but they are identical to those pictured in the
documentation for the recalled ranges. I am a lifetime customer of Sears, having always bought all of my high end kitchen and laundry appliances from them. This will no longer be the case. This is a very dangerous product and I do not appreciate SearsÃÂ lack of corrective action on selling this defective ÃÂtop of the lineÃÂ product and not taking action to correct the defect.
justification: The range consistently overheats, posing a fire and burn hazard, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he purchased the house in Dec 2009. The unit came installed in the home.

The consumer stated that he had the unit repaired because there was a recall on his unit.

The consumer was sent a kit from GE. The consumer stated that the kit had missing parts so they had to wait for all of the parts (12/28/2010).

incident_description:

I was unable to turn it off or turn any of the other burners on or off.  I turned it off at the circuit breaker, then turned it back on, hoping it would work correctly.  It didn't.  It began "popping" and a noxious burning odor was noticed.  Also, the other burner again turned itself on.  I again turned it off at the breaker box and called for a service technician, who arrived several days later.  He removed the cooktop and inspected it.  All five of the circuit boards were burned and the connecting wires were partially melted, fused or blackened. He said the top would have to be totally rebuilt.

The service company and Frigidaire have declared this cooktop a total loss with parts and labor in excess of $1,100.  I have been talking to Frigidaire to try to get a replacement cooktop from them, but so far they haven't budged, saying the cooktop was "out of warranty".  This is a 3-year-old item used in home cooking.  There is no doubt this electrical/circuit board failure would have caused a major fire in my home had I not been there to stop the current in the 40-amp wire.

incident_description:
Samsung Convention Oven FTQ353IWUX manufactured in May 2009.
For several months, the bake feature of the oven has not been working properly - the oven is unable to reach and hold temperature.  Some online posts had commented about wires burning off, so before I spent money on parts, I decided to unplug the oven and remove the back cover to see if I noticed anything amiss.  Sure enough, one wire (the red wire) to the bottom heating element was burned off at the connector to the heating element.  The tip of the wire and the insulation for about 2" was black and the wire was dangling in free space.  Obviously, this is why the bottom heater element is not getting hot.  Upon checking the other wire (yellow wire), it too shows signs of heat exposure (insulation slightly melted and rigid).  Similarly, the wires (red and brown) to the top heating element show the same signs - partially melted insulation, wires very stiff near the connectors to the heating element.  I am very concerned that this is a serious fire and/or electrical shock hazard.  I could easily put new connectors on and replace the wires, but this should not have happened in the first place and I am concerned that it could happen again.  If I were to replace the wires, I would use a higher temperature insulated wire (the wires that burned off appear to be standard low temperature plastic insulation), but I am think that for my and my family's safety, I am simply going to buy a new oven (of a different brand).  Surely I am not the only one to experience this problem, and you can find online postings, with photos, of the same problem.  This oven needs to be recalled.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven with burned wires, posing a potential fire or electrical shock hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

Just google "Samsung microwave turns on by itself" and you will see.

incident_description: My front door to my Whirlpool oven started to shatter, from what I could gather for no apparent reason. I use the oven almost on a daily basis, sometimes for hours at a time. I have had this oven for about seven years. On the day of the incident, I had used my oven to cook sweet potatoes at 425 during the middle of the day and during the evening I had cooked dinner which I was cooking several different things in a two to three hour period.

The defects tend to occur when the gas range is being turned on; therefore, it makes turns on the gas but stops short of lighting it on fire. This is a major safety hazard as it allows gas to leak.

General Electric dishwasher overheated, melted plastic ware into molten platic puddles,
coninued to overheat with door closed until mains power was shut off to dishwasher.
Dishwasher was [REDACTED], 4 years old. GE has had many such problems with

incident_description: My coffee pot was on when I noticed a strong smell coming from my kitchen.  It smelled like burning plastic and was very strong.  I finally realized it was my coffee maker and by that time the outlet had turned the coffee pot off.  Upon inspection of the coffee pot, I noticed that on the bottom of the hotplate was where the burning had been.  It was discolored and the smell was very strong.  I called Cuisinart and reported the problem and they informed me they would send me a new one after I gave them the model number of the coffee maker.  I am concerned, however, that they would send me one with the same problem that could cause a fire in my home.  I have 3 children and am concerned with their lack of concern with this problem.  Tonight I was doing research and found that many people have had the same problem.  Why is Cuisinart still allowed to sell such a dangerous product?!
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and discoloration but no actual fire or injury, indicating a minor incident. The likelihood is possible given the reported frequency of similar issues.

incident_description: [REDACTED], my spouse, was slicing an apple to add to our salads for lunch. We had purchased the product: Gourmet Club Apple Wedger from Walmart less than 2 months ago and have only used it 5-6 times. While [REDACTED]] was pressing down on the apple slicer as directed, the blades separated from the plastic holder and got stuck in the apple, slicing into his hand. If he did not respond as quickly and had pressed down even a fraction of a second longer, he would have needed stitches instead of just disinfectant and bandages! Trying to locate and get a hold of the company Best Brands Consumer Products, INC. is difficult, and I have in the process found many more stories similar to what happened in our home. This product is dangerous and should be recalled!
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring disinfectant and bandages, and there are reports of similar incidents, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Duralex Picardie 16 7/8 oz drinking glass exploded inside dishwasher while I was trying to unload. Didn't think anything of it at the time. Just thought somehow the heat of the dishwasher did something that led to the explosion.

A month or two later, another drinking glass exploded in my hand while I was clearing away dishes from our dining room table. Chards of glass went on me, on the table and other dishes/bowls, on the floor, flew out of the room into my adjoining living room. I got small cuts while trying to clean off the glass. No heat/temperature change was present this time.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts from flying glass shards, indicating an injury occurred.

The consumer believes that a person would need three hands to remove waffles safety from the maker. The consumer claims that she received minor burns as a result of this issue.

incident_description: I bought an Intermatic T-104-20 Mechanical DPST timer rated for my water heater. I bought this product new from Amazon.com LL C I installed this on the water heater for the owners suite in a utility room on the north side of the house. 5-1/2 months later the timer was noisy you could hear it inside the house in a room adjacent to the utility room. Then the hot water on that end of the house started to run out quickly. So I grabbed the key and my tools and unlocked the closet and opened the gray box it was in (NEMA 1 enclosure) there was black burned reside on the inside of the box and some on the wood siding behind the box. The plastic shield covering the terminal screws had a 1 inch burn hole in it. The screw terminal pressure plate was sparking again the line wires which was no longer attached, The insulation had melted back to the fitting where it entered the box and all the insulation of the timer motor leads was burned off including the plastic buss bar that all terminals were in. I removed all of it and the wood behind the box had the black residue on it. I got my meter out and checked the breaker to make sure there was no substantial loss across it. I used the Ohm meter and checked the thermostats and heating elements. I noticed that one set of contacts in the timer had fused together. So I got a steel box and connectors and straight wired the heater to the circuit. I was happy that it did not ignite the wood behind it because it would have gone straight to the attic and burned this place down. 24 hours later the water heater is working fine without the timer and the water was good and hot for the morning shower.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the timer and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My then 9 month old daughter was with my husband and I when we were putting groceries away and my daughter was holding herself up on the side of the freezer watching us put things away. When my husband reached over to get some more things to put away the door started to close and my daughters thumb was stuck in one of the sharp wholes they have on the side of the freezer. When we finally got her thumb out it was bleeding horribly. We immediately called 911 and they came and took her in a ambulance to the hospital. When they got to our house they couldn't believe all the blood was just from her little thumb. They took some xrays at the hospital and luckily there was no broken bones just a severe cut to her thumb. We thought it was going to heal just fine and that would be just a horrible experience but come to find out it was starting to grow very weirdly and we took her to a specialist and found out that she had damage to her matrix which is her nail bed and wouldn't grow correctly anymore. Luckily after a year of a really weird nail it has gotten to a point that it doesn't look as bad as it started out but the specialist said this is the best is would look and will have to have to have her nail look this way for the rest of her life. Samsung doesn't want to change the make of the fridge and thinks it was a freak accident although we found on this site there is another family that had 14 month old that did in deed get his finger amputated from the same design fridge made by Samsung. I dont know how many times they want this to happen before they change the way this fridge works! The freezer automatically closes which makes it that much worse and dangerous!

Here you can find the other report.
http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1286955
justification: The incident resulted in a severe cut and permanent damage to the child's nail bed, classifying it as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the presence of another similar reported incident involving the same fridge design.

incident_description: We bought a new gas stove with oven  It's an Amana model AGR4433XDW2. The burner grates are very slippery and the corners are rounded. On several occasions while cooking have had pans slide off the grates. I have contacted Amana directly and their response was to hold onto the handle the of the pan or pot.This I have documented this action.  Apparently they don't cook. While cooking I often use several pots and pans. No one has been injured at this point. But it's only matter of time. I feel that they should provide grates with square corners that they currently provide with other models. They seem to have no concern  which I find unacceptable. If I or a member of my family gets injured I will pursue the issue through legal channels.
justification: Pans sliding off the grates is a documented issue, but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description: I have a Maytag gas range Model MGR8674AS that has knobs on the  front of the unit above the oven door.  The slightest pressure on them causes the gas to start flowing.  I have had several situations where someone leaned on it to reach something nearby and turned the gas on slightly.   The auto ignition clicker sound did not turn on to alert you that the gas is flowing.  Shortly thereafter, I have had natural gas filling the air in my kitchen and then throughout my home.  If this were to happen prior to someone leaving the home, it could be disastrous upon their return when they unlock the door to get inside.   This is not an isolated incident.  It  has happened to my family on more than one occasion.  Incredibly dangerous for adults as well as children.  All it takes is to brush up against the knob for it to turn on.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation where gas leaks occur due to accidental activation, posing a significant risk of explosion or poisoning, which could lead to death.

incident_description: I had just finished cooking bagels in the oven at 425 degrees and removed the food from the oven. I closed the oven door hit the off button and within seconds after shutting off the oven the inside tempered glass shattered. The door was closed when the oven was turned off, the inside tempered glass shattered without warning and nothing was done but turning off the appliance. No one was injured at the time of the incident but the glass should not have shattered under normal cooking temperatures. This is a brand new appliance which we only had for two days and this was only the  second time the oven had been used since installation.
justification: The incident involved unexpected glass shattering in a new oven, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: Two weeks ago we awoke to a strange smell in the house, and discovered the heating element in our GE Adora dishwasher model GHDA670N00BB had come on during the night and stayed on all night long.  We had to turn off the circuit breaker to get it to stop.  Last night, as soon as we started the dishwasher and it began to fill with water, gray smoke started pouring from the door vent along with a strong smell of burning plastic.  We immediately shut off the breaker and have not used it since.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning smell but no reported injuries, indicating a non-injury incident with a low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: We were using the self-cleaning function on our Electrolux Icon double wall ovens. About one half-hour into a three-hour cleaning cycle, we heard a loud POP and saw that the interior glass on the oven had shattered.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering during a cleaning cycle, but there was no mention of injury, indicating a non-injury incident. The likelihood is unlikely as such events are not common but do occur.

incident_description: I had a brand new wall oven installed today.  The Owner's Manual suggested that removal of the new-oven odor could be expedited by running a 3 hour self-cleaning cycle.  During the self cleaning cycle, the middle layer of glass shattered.  Very hot glass dropped onto the floor.  Before the middle glass shattered, the exterior glass had not been too hot to touch.  After the middle glass shattered, the exterior glass was too hot to touch and could have easily burned my children or pets.  Because the control panel does not allow a self-cleaning cycle to be turned off, I had to stop the cycle by turning off the breaker.  If I had not noticed the broken glass and turned off the breaker, there could have been a burn injury.
justification: The incident involved very hot glass that could have easily burned children or pets, indicating potential for injury, though none occurred this time. The likelihood is unlikely as it requires specific conditions (self-cleaning cycle) and was noticed before injury occurred.

incident_description:
My electric oven was on for approximately 20 minutes at 425 degrees. I turned it off. Five or ten minutes later, it began beeping and flashing the F1 code. The element on the bottom of the oven was on and was not cycling off -- iEthe "Clear" button, the oven turned off, and about 2 minutes later turned on again with the same result. 
This continued until we flipped the circuit breaker.

incident_description:
Hello, I would like to share with you my terrifying experience with a new Pyrex dish that exploded on my last night.  I have photos enclosed as well, fortunately the only injury was a  small cut to the bag of my right hand. 
 
I recently purchased a brand new 3qt Easy Grab Pyrex baking dish at Fred Meyers in Eagle River, AK.  This was to replace an older 9ÃÂx13ÃÂ Pyrex dish purchased probably 10-12 years earlier, that I had left at a friends house.

Late afternoon yesterday, around 4:30 pm, I pre-heated my [REDACTED] Gas oven to 375 deg. F.  I coated the pyrex dish with a pressurized spray can of coconut oil, then coated the bottom of the pan with 1/2 enchilada sauce. After various other tasks going on (typical mom multi-tasking) I finally filled the pan, covered with foil and placed it in the lower 1/3 of my oven. This was around 5:40 pm. I baked for 20 minutes, then removed the foil and baked another 2 minutes.  I removed the pan and placed the pan on my cast iron stove top, which was warm due to almost an hour of preheating the oven, and something I have done dozens of times with my other Pyrex dishes (I have a lot of photos of my food).  I removed one enchilada to serve to my son, then I moved 2 feet to the left of the range to clean dishes, when 5 minutes later there was a loud explosion and I felt something hit the back of my right hand. I was shocked and scared when I turned around and saw the glass shards strewn about my kitchen!  Thank goodness my son and 2 dogs were not within 6 feet of this incident, or more serious injuries would have occurred besides the small cut to the back of my right hand. 

I cleaned up the rest of the glass shards, but was very disturbed that this would occur. I am a very experienced home cook, and have been using Pyrex safely, or so I thought for over 38 years. and have never encountered this problem before. Needless to say, I will be throwing all of my Pyrex into the trash tomorrow, new or old, I wonÃÂt expose myself or my family to that risk again.  I have seen a friend place a hot Pyrex dish into a cold sink of water and seen the glass shatter, but not explode in this violent matter. I certainly have never, nor would have treated my glass dishes this way so I was surprised and very angry to have had this happen.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut to the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3), but such explosive failures of Pyrex dishes are uncommon (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
The inner oven glass window of the Whirlpool 30" free-standing oven range ( Model# : WFC150MLAW ) shattered during normal use.  Owner was cooking dinner at about 6pm on Thursday, Feb. 13th, and preheated the oven to 425 degrees.  While he was preparing the food to put in the oven, he heard a loud bang and crash. He turned from the counter and could see that the interior tempered glass had shattered.  He opened the oven to assess the danger, saw several bits and pieces in the oven and closed it again. When he opened the oven, many  pieces fell to floor, which he cleaned up after allowing them to cool. 
The Owner was extremely lucky that there was not injury to anyone.  The exploding of the inner glass of the overn is a customer safety issue.
The oven range was purchased from Lowes and was only 1 month old. It is under warranty. However despite multiple calles to Lowes they repeated told me that Whirlpool consider this a cosmetic issue and the owner would need to replace the oven glass or door at their expense. It is extremely concerning that both Lowes and Whirlpool do not consider this a customer safety issue and consides this to be a cosmetic issue.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of oven glass during normal use, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: KitchenAid undercounter dishwasher during normal operation. Spouse started dishwasher and went to bed. I returned home about 1 hour later to find kitchen full of smoke. Traced smoke to dishwasher. Dishwasher was stopped due to malfunction and fire. Removed control panel cover which revealed a blackened and melted green circuit board and melted circuit board cover and melted secondary cover. Dishwasher installed in wood cabinet  with wood framing and facia above fire source ( control panel / circuit board). Disconnected power cord. Online research revealed many consumer reports of dishwasher fires which in some cases ignited surrounding cabinets. Testimony and comments from consumers of KitchenAid and Maytag dishwasher owners who were unable to get help from the manufacturer. Reports of these dishwashers being repaired and catching fire again.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher fire that caused significant damage but no reported injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple consumer reports of similar incidents and recurring fires after repairs.

incident_description: While using a cooking pan in the kitchen I was injured when a rivet used to secure the handle to to pan base exploded. The rivet turned into a high speed projectile that impacted and embedded into my left wrist. During its path it severed a tendon and cause severe nerve damage. I quickly went to the hospital where I required micro surgery to both remove and to attempt to repair the damage it caused.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury requiring micro surgery, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rare (1) as such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
The consumer reported that she was cooking in the range oven in baking setting at 350 degrees for 5 minutes when black smoke started coming out of the upper back panel and she noticed an odor similar to burning plastic. Immediately after turning off the circuit breaker for the range she noticed that the smoke and odor stopped. 

2/03/14- The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that since the range was under the warranty period they would send a repair technician to inspect the oven free of charge.

2/04/14- A repair technician from a repair firm representing the manufacturer, dismantled the back of the control panel of the range and informed the consumer that the panel was burnt. This technician also stated that he would contact the manufacturer to order a replacement control panel.

2/04/14- The consumer filed a safety complaint with the manufacturer because she thinks this product poses a fire hazard. The consumer also contacted the repair company and asked if the replacement panel would be the exact same as the one burnt. The repair company informed her that no upgrades or modifications have been made to the control panels and that the replacement would be the same type of panel as the burnt one.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning odor but no injury or death, and the issue was promptly addressed by the manufacturer.

incident_description:
This is the third time I've input this information. NEXT resulted in page not found. 
Sears Kenmore elite free standing range/oven model # 790.99014102 Serial VF31512947.

I (homeowner) was using front right burner to reheat simmer a taco / beef mixture. I went to the restroom. Upon return burner had gone to high heat and a boilover with smoldering had occurred. This triggered the smoke alarm. Turning the control to OFF was not effective. Burner was stuck on full power high heat. I cut the power and cleaned up after the burner had cooled. I restored power and that burner came on, and was on high (even though the control was set to OFF). The burner did not cycle (as an uncovered burner should) but stayed on high continuously. Device is now disconnected. This could have resulted in a house fire.

We have 3 small kids at home ranging from 2-7 and even though no one got hurt there could of been a different outcome.  There was no cracks in glass and no one was near the stove for them to of hit it with anything.

incident_description:

01/26/2014- The consumer stated that she was baking a cake at 300 degrees for about 10 minutes in the oven. Immediately after, she smelled an odor similar to burnt plastic. The consumer states that she pressed the stop button on the control panel to turn off the oven and noticed a spark and immediately after the control panel caught on fire. The consumer went to look for her fire extinguisher.  She was away for 1 minute and when she came back in the kitchen the fire was extinguished. The consumer unplugged the unit from the wall outlet.

01/27/14- The consumer contacted the retailer. The retailerÃÂs representative, named [REDACTED], advised the consumer to have the range inspected for a minimum of $79.00 plus the cost of repairs.  The consumer did not agree to this at the time she was speaking with [REDACTED].

1/27/14- The consumer stated that she intends to contact the manufacturer. The consumer thinks this product poses a safety hazard.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she heard a loud popping noise and noticed that the flames were erupting below the cook top (burners) which is in between the location of the oven.  The range was off at the time this incident occurred.  Her spouse immediately used the circuit breaker to switch off the power to the range and the flames dissipated.  There was prior service call approximately 2 years ago for the lower oven spontaneously turning on by itself.  A new control panel was installed at the time, which resolved the problem.

2/11/14 The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that a service technician will be sent out 2/12/14 for inspection.
Caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
On Feb. 12, 2014, a service technician sent by JennAir (Whirlpool) inspected the range.  He was unable to examine the space directly beneath the cooktop where the fire occured, due to the fact that the screws attaching the burners to the cooktop (especially those on the most heavily-used elements) were corroded so badly that they would have been drilled out.  He then did a visual inspection from the rear of the range.  He had us restore power to the range to see what would happen.  As soon as power was restored, the sparking and arcing occurred again.  After immediately shutting off the power again , the technician stated that "the burner switch shorted out, causin arcing and smoke."  We believe we were lucky to be present when the incident first happened, and we were able to shut off power immediately.  Had we been absent or asleep (this happened when the stove was not on, not being used), we may have been injured or sustained property damage.
justification: The incident involved flames and arcing from the range, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
while kneading dough using my KitchenAid Stand Mixer -- the speed control suddenly went to 'full speed' WITHOUT TOUCHING OR MOVING THE CONTROL.  
  The Control has settings as follows:  Stir, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. -- 10 being full speed.  I was using the mixer on "2" (which is recommended for kneading dough)   When it went to full speed, the mixer started to flail about on the countertop and threw flour everywhere.   I was able to quickly grab the mixer by the top of the motor  and then shut the control off.  I am, however, a man in his 50s -- over 6 feet tall and over 200 pounds.  Had this been my mother or my sister-in-law, or someone else of shorter and lighter stature -- or a senior citizen or young person,  I shudder to think what may have happened as the mixer is quite heavy -- and further, the whirling dough hook could also cause injury.   Interestingly -- each time I tried to turn the control back on, (to "2" - it would immediately go to 'full speed" -- then, after cleaning up the mess (about 45 minutes later)  the control seemed to work fine.....I am afraid to allow anyone to use the product because I worry that it will once again go to full speed without provocation.

KitchenAid did not seem to be concerned about this - and they offered me 20% off on the purchase of another KitchenAid product --   The mixer was purchased in February of 2013 and has been used less than a dozen times.
justification: The incident involved the mixer malfunctioning and flailing, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the sporadic nature of the malfunction.

justification: The refrigerator started smoking and burning, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore select clean self-cleaning electric range model 665.95802 that was purchased in July of 2000.  This evening I was using the oven to make dinner, set at 375, for a little over an hour when the buzzer beeped and displayed the error code E2 F3.  When I opened the oven door I was suprised to see the broiler element aglow.  Thinking that I had accidentally turned it on, I immediately punched the CANCEL button and left the door ajar.  After 10 minutes it was obvious that the element continued to heat and I resorted to unplugging the oven.  After it had cooled down, I plugged it back in and the broiler element began to heat up.  Doing quick research on this issue I found many threads with other people having the exact same problem.  At this point in time I am unable to use the stove top because the broiler element heats up when the range is plugged in.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While using the microwave oven to heat water, the microwave oven electronics/wiring began emitting smoke and a harsh burning smell.

The microwave heating was stopped, but the smoke and smell, which seemed to be that of burning electronics or rubber, continued for more than five minutes afterwards -- at which point we contacted the local fire department.

The smoke and smell did not come from the cavity of the microwave where food is inserted, but instead appeared to come from the internal wiring or electronics, likely via the back vent before exiting through the front grills.

The fire department then arrived, and moved the microwave oven outside of the house, advising us to ventilate the area and avoid further breathing in of the fumes that had permeated the area.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning smell from the microwave's internal wiring, posing a potential health risk from fumes, but no immediate injury was reported.

incident_description:

I unplugged it and ran it under the faucet of the kitchen sink. I'm left with a hole in the front, through which you can see an electric wire and an electric component ÃÂ I think a rheostat ÃÂ which I suspect overheated to the point that it set the plastic on fire. I don't know if the flame would have grown high enough to set my cabinet on fire, but since the body of the entire toaster is mostly plastic, I suspect it would have. 

Would a recall make any sense? It does seem a basic design flaw to put any kind of electrical component right behind a plastic plate, so that when it does eventually fail, it sets it on fire.

incident_description:
Dear [REDACTED]

Enclosed is the Hamilton Beach Stainless Steele 12-Cup Percolator that I reported to you on November
27th as causing a sever burn across my abdomen to which I emailed pictures to you.

The burn occurred on the evening of November 26th when I accidently spilled coffee while sitting down
on the couch. I was clothed in pajamas and a cotton robe tied in thE front. When the liquid spilled out
of the cup onto my robe, I immediately felt it come through to my skin and jumped up and tore my robe
loose and pulled my pajama pants away while screaming in pain. My husband was sitting in the recliner
next to the couch and jumped up to assist me and noticed the immediate blistering.

On November 27th, I visited my doctor's office and Dr. [REDACTED] classified the burn as a 2"d degree with the
blisters and recommended to keep aloe lotion on the burn and [REDACTED] as needed and take [REDACTED] for
pain.

Prior to sending you the percolator, I experimented following the owner's manual and comparing to my
Hamilton Beach coffee maker. Using a meat thermometer, I determined that the percolator reaches
195 degrees after percolating at the point the light indicator changes from blue to green signaling ready
to pour contents. Then, I waited 2 hours and retested the coffee temperature and it was still 185
degrees. My Hamilton Beach coffee maker averages 165 degrees from the time it stops processing
throughout the time the warmer is on.

This test concluded that there is a significant difference in temperature between my Hamilton Beach
coffee maker and the enclosed Hamilton Beach percolator. I truly had no idea the temperature
difference since there are no warnings or information regarding the scalding heat level and serious burn
risk.

Based on consumer market research, the average age of purchasers of this percolator are between 54-
65 years old. As we age, our skin thins and burns become more severe and healing takes longer so I take
this very personal and am concerned that there simply is not enough warnings on this percolator. The
only warning in the manual and on the pot is to not immerse in water because of the electrical base.

A disturbing statement contained in the manual and as part of the specifications is, "coffee stays hot
with a gentle keep-warm heater." In the instructions, it also indicate the liquid stays "warm" without
warning of just how hot the liquid is kept at on the warmer. I can assure you that there is nothing
"gentle" about the keep-warm heater and the liquid is not kept warm, but just below boiling
temperature. The only mention of scalding is if the cap is removed during the percolation cycle, not
from the liquid after the light turns green.

There is a negative impact to my life since this incident occurred. I am not able to wear normal clothes
because of the location and size of the burn across my stomach. Instead, I am wearing elastic band
workout pants with the elastic pulled down below the burn. While I am able to work remotely at home,
I have had to cancel several face-to-face meetings and decline certain holiday functions. Today, I will
email you an updated photograph of the burn so you can see that even after 8 days, there is little to no
improvement.
 
I am forwarding a copy of this letter to an attorney friend as I believe this is a serious matter that
requires escalation.

Thank you for your kindness and immediate response to my report of this incident on November 2th.

Sincerely
[REDACTED]

Dear [REDACTED]
I received your reply letter and must admit that I am disappointed in the lack of data to support your
short statement concluding that the percolator was not defective. I took the time and effort to conduct
a series of tests between the Hamilton Beach percolator and our Hamilton Beach coffee maker to
determine the temperature differences and would have appreciated at least the same level of data to
support the ruling of "not defective" based on your internal testing.
I am not looking to fight or sue Hamilton Beach. What I am expecting is reimbursement for the
purchase, doctor's appointment and the few medical supplies to soothe the burn and pain along with a
promise that Hamilton Beach will apply more warnings to this percolator raising awareness of potential
scalding.
I can assure you that as a home-based worker for 13 years that consumes either hot tea or coffee all
day, I have spilled my share of liquid on myself. However, I have never experienced a burn such as the
one I did with the coffee from this percolator. It has been over 5 weeks since the accident occurred and
the burn is still very red and continuing to heal. Enclosed are a set of the time-lapsed photos taken
immediately after the burn on 11/25 through 12/31 evidencing that I am still healing. It just amazes me
that I sustained a burn such as this through my robe and pajama top. I cannot imagine how severe it
would have been if I had not had my robe on at the time of the spill.
I remain very concerned that Hamilton Beach refuses to acknowledge that they have insufficient
warnings on this percolator and in my opinion has the following false statement in the instruction guide,
"How To Heat Water I Step 8: Ready Light will glow when water is hot, and percolator will automatically
go into a keep-warm mode." The liquid remains extremely hot, not warm.
Based on my tests and comparisons, the water heats to scalding and the warmer maintains a very hot
heat level. Therefore, by stating gentle keep-warm heater misrepresents the hot temperature that is
continuously maintained by the warmer. The only reference to scalding is if the cap is removed during
the percolation cycle.
Since Hamilton Beach insists there is nothing wrong with this product and refuses to acknowledge the
potential for scalding if spilled, I am reporting this to the North Carolina Consumer Protection Bureau
and the United States Consumer Product Commission in hopes they will encourage Hamilton Beach to
improve their warning and avoid others from experiencing such a painful ugly burn.
I am enclosing receipts for the expenses I've incurred due to this accident I sustained by purchasing this
percolator and am requesting full reimbursement at your earliest convenience.

Sincerely
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as burns from hot liquids are not uncommon but depend on usage and handling.

Caller was in the living room and heard a pop sound, she went into the kitchen to ask what the sound was and was advised by her daughter that the baking dish had exploded, the entire bottom portion is in one piece but all four sides exploded.

Almost all of the exploded glass remained on the 40 x 60 table.

The dish belongs to the caller who has had it and baked in it for about ten years until this incident.

incident_description:
GE Profile Gas Cooktop model JGP970 had its gas valve knobs removed for cleaning.  The stove was not used for over 12 hours prior to this cleaning.  An aerosol cleaner was sprayed on the cooktop by a cleaning service person and allowed to sit for a minute or so.  It was "Easy-Off Oven Cleaner Heavy Duty".  The cleaning solution went up in flames with a large flame burst.  Fortunately, the person was not directly next to the cooktop when this occurred or they would have been badly burned.  

The fire was started because of the harness switch part # WB18T1036.  It has an electric switch that sits on top of each gas knob and enables the sparking feature that ignites the burners when the knob is turned on.  The cleaner seeped into the switch given it's not water tight and ignited the cleaner.  

I contacted GE consumer relations and opened case # 13124419.  They initially were very concerned and then backed down and agreed only to pay for a service visit and split the cost of labor and parts to repair.  Though this helped financially, I don't believe they responded accordingly. The service person stated he sees this occur at least twice a year and didn't think it was a safety issue.  I later responded to GE with pictures of the burned part exposing the design flaw of their components and they stated they have done all they need to do.  I explained to them that people clean their oven tops and knobs by design can come off to help with that process.  I agree spraying oven cleaner on the top was not the best choice for a cleaner, but starting a fire is an unexpected result which GE should have accounted for in their design.  Especially since the knobs are on the top flat surface of the cooktop.  I simply wanted them to acknowledge the saftey issue, refund the cost of the entire service and ask for me to ship them the bad part for further investigation.  That did not occur which is why I submitted this complaint.

Model# JBP970SEK2SS
Serial# DL7080280
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, and the service person mentioned seeing this issue at least twice a year.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:

Re: Viking Professional Oven-30 Inch
      Model Number VES050SS

In April, 2007, my wife and I had our kitchen remodeled. It was a complete tear out and replacement - oak plank floors, 
custome cabinets, granite countertops, etc.

As part of the remodel, we installed Viking Professional appliances, including a refrigerator, oven and microwave. We chose Viking because of our impression of the quality of thier products. For the quality we were willing to pay a premium price ($2,849 for the oven). We have now encountered a serious and dangerous defect in the oven.

There is a broiler element on the top of the oven. It has a glass cover. We just discovered the glass had cracked and glass shards had fallen on the floor of the oven. The shards could easily have fallen on food being cooked. Had we not discovered this when we did, further cracking could have occurred and additional glass shards could be dropped onto food and be ingested when eaten. 

Like most users, to accommodate easy loading and unloading of the oven at waist level, the oven is placed low on the wall. It is therefore difficult to see the top of the oven unless you get on your hands and knees. The cracking glass would be easy to overlook.

The oven has since been repaired by replacement of the broiler element at a cost of $791. Viking refused to pay for any of the replacements costs or the labor to remove the old element and replace it with the new. Viking seems totally unconcerned with the possibility of injury to those using their ovens.

Viking seems indifferent with this issue. In our view, the glass should never crack must less shatter into the over or the food. We believe it poses a serious health hazard.
justification: Glass shards falling into food could cause injury if ingested, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
GE Gas Range Model # JGB810DET2CC and Serial # MZ214221P
During the last week of June 2013 I woke up to a clicking sound.  The sound was the clicking before the gas comes on the surface burner.  I walked to the kitchen and the center burner was on and the center knob was turned enough to start the burner.  I had to turn the knob off.  A&E Factory service was called since the stove was under warranty.  Two technicians came to the house on July 5, 2013 and checked the surface burners and said the stove canÃÂt turn itself on.  Their note was ÃÂTested system.  No problems found.  Working to OEM specÃÂ.
One month later on August 6, 2013 I woke up to the smell of natural gas.  The whole house was filled with the odor of the gas and the center knob was on enough to turn the burner on but no flames.  I had to turn the knob off.  I had to open all doors and windows to air out the house.  I left the doors open and asked me mom to stop by later and close everything.  She called Cascade Natural Gas since I had a gas leak.  This was documented.  The gas odor could be smelled outside by the Cascade Gas representative sent to investigate the leak.  I called GE Consumer representative and received case # [REDACTED].  GE representative [REDACTED] made an appointment with A&E Service Factory.
On August 8, 2013 the A&E technician came to investigate the situation.  The technician decided to order the center surface burner valve.  Aug 19, 2013 was the appointment to replace the valve.  The center surface burner valve was replaced. 
December 16, 2013 I came home at 4:30 pm and the small precision simmer burner was on.  Again there was a clicking sound with the burner on.  The knob was turned enough to start the burner.   I had several cookie sheets on this part of the stove.  The bottom cookie sheet had about 2-3 inch diameter discoloration from the heat.  The burner acted like the first burner so I thought I had a month before the burner would turn on and only natural gas would be released.
December 17, 2013 I called GE customer service and received case # [REDACTED], from case manager [REDACTED].  An appointment with A&E service was made for 12/24/2013.  Around 3:15 pm on December 17, 2013 my parents called me at work from my house and stated the small precision burner knob was on enough to allow the natural gas to leak.  Luckily they caught it in time before the house was filled with gas.  I have 2 pets that stay in the house while I am at work.  I asked them to check on the house not knowing the burner would act this way so soon.  I expected in a month this would happen since it appears to have a similar valve failure.
December 17, 2013 I called my case manager [REDACTED] to ask to expedite my case because of the gas leak.  He could not change the appointment date.  I used the stove while I was home but had to turn off the gas every time I left the house.
December 24, 2013 an A&E technician came to the house and stated he was going to replace 4 surface burner valves since I had a problem with the precision simmer burner.  GE was going to pay for all of the valves to be replaced.  The next appointment to replace the valves was on January 7, 2014.
On January 7, 2014: an A&E technician came and replaced four surface burner valves. 
I did not trust the gas range so when I left the house nothing was on the range and a window next to the range was open to allow air circulation.  I was afraid a valve would fail and I wanted to make sure the window was open for my pets.  When I was home I did not have the window open.  After I finished cooking I thought I could smell gas but wasnÃÂt sure where it came from.  
January 18, 2014 my mom was at my house and I asked her if she could smell gas around the burners.  She suggested I call Cascade Natural Gas to check out the range. 
January 19, 2014 I called Cascade Natural Gas and told them I had a gas leak around the range.  The person on the phone told me to turn off the stove.  A Cascade Natural Gas representative came to the house and I told him about the issue.  He asked me to turn the gas on.  He used a gas detector device around the burners.  As the natural gas was filling the lines he was moving the detector over the burners.  The precession burner, which had the initial problem, and the front left burner were indicating leaks with a loud beeping sound.  He repeated this pattern for several minutes and the beeping sound increased and he told me I have two leaks.  He red tagged my range and told me not to use it.  I needed to contact the service people.   
January 20, 2014 I called GE and customer service was on a holiday.  I called NilsenÃÂs appliance store and informed them of the surface burner valves leaking.  [REDACTED] told me to call GE customer service line.
January 21, 2014 I called GE customer service and stated the new problem of two valves leaking natural gas when the knobs are off.  I wanted a refund because I have an unsafe range in my house.  I emphasized this is a safety and life issue.  I also told the person Cascade Natural Gas technician had tagged my range to where I canÃÂt use it because of the two leaks.  I referenced my case # [REDACTED] and the person told me that my case manager [REDACTED] wanted to discuss the issue with me and he will call me on January 24, 2014.
January 23, 2014 I called GE customer service and spoke with [REDACTED] and referenced my case # [REDACTED].  I wanted a refund and the stove removed.  I told her all about the issues with the surface burner valves failing and the gas leaks.  She told me it is GEÃÂs policy to only replace or repair but not to give a refund.  I had to call NilsenÃÂs, the store where I purchased the range from.  She did set up an appointment to have a technician come out and verify the leaks since Cascade Natural Gas technician did not work for GE.  The A&E technician will come out and check for the leaks.  Then they are supposed to talk with a GE engineer to see how to resolve this problem.  The appointment is set for January 28, 2014 in the afternoon.  
This is unsatisfactory.  This is a health and safety condition that should be urgently fixed before there is an accident that results in a death or fire.  This could be the reason that on the GE website, this model is no long being manufactured.

incident_description:
I have a Cuisinart 12 cup food processor and I am disappointed in one aspect of its function that I believe is a grave safety concern.  This model has push button on and off.  There is no way to tell that this machine is on or off because it has flat "buttons".  

I plugged in my Food Processor, then attached the large work bowl with the work bowl cover attached (because of how I store the work bowl and cover and blades to keep them with the food processor away from my children, I had the large chopping blade and the Shredding disk inside the work bowl). 

My machine was plugged in and as soon as I connected the work bowl to the machine, the chopping blade and shredding disk went spinning and swirling about inside the work bowl.  I immediately unplugged my machine.  My work bowl is scratched.  My work bowl cover has the plastic rim shredded.  I have a damaged chopping blade and damaged shredding blade.

I find this to be a huge safety issue as there is no way to tell that this machine is actually clicked into the "ON" position prior to plugging it in or connecting the work bowl.  God forbid if this had continued and shattered my bowl sending metal blades through my kitchen.

There is no way to actually tell on this machine that the ON button is actually deployed.  I find this feature to be a pure disregard for safety.  There is no switch.  I thought, given the structure of these buttons, that when unplugged, the "ON" switch would reset to the off position (or at least, this is what it would appear to do) so I thought the machine would not defaulty be "ON" given the fact that there is no way to tell (ie:  a switch or other way to look at the machine to realize it's turned on).
justification: The incident involved unexpected operation of the food processor causing damage to the equipment but no injury to the user.

incident_description: Anchor Hocking baking dish exploded in my mother's oven on Sunday, Jan. 12, 2014.  My mother was fixing meatloaf, potatoes, and carrots in a baking dish recently purchased at Wal Mart in Sidney, Ohio.  My mother and I have used this bake ware for decades never having a problem with how we used it.  We did not know of the changes to the newer product that altered how to use it.  We have always been able to put it in the oven and turn it on or program for starting to cook later, with every expectation that nothing would go wrong, it never had before.  The baking dish was put in the over then was lit to start heating, minutes later it exploded in the oven.  The food inside was still cold, the meat raw not even beginning to get warm.  The sound and the was horrendous!  After this incident I researched the problem to see what possibly could have caused it.  Then I discovered the advice to always put in preheated oven, not a former requirement of the old products.  This means this is no longer a safe product to use in programmable ovens where it starts cooking when no one is home.  It is difficult for the elderly who have used a product the same way for decades to realize the product has changed, that they are put at risk if their habits are no longer applicable to the new lines of products.

incident_description:
LOWER HEATING ELEMENT OVERHEATED. OVEN WENT FROM 190 DEGREES TO A VERY HIGH TEMPERATURE AND WOULD NOT SHUT OFF USING KEYPAD. HAD TO FLIP THE CIRCUIT BREAKER IN MY FUSE BOX. NO ERROR CODE PRESENT ON OVEN CONTROL PANEL. ONLY NOTICED THIS POTENTIAL FIRE HAZARD WHEN I SMELLED SOMETHING BURNING, THEN OPENED OVEN DOOR. CHICKEN WAS BOILING IN [REDACTED] DISH, HOUSE FULL OF SMOKE.

THIS ISSUE AND LACK OF ERROR CODE ARE A CONCERN. NO IDEA IF IT WAS CAUSED BY FAULTY ELEMENT, HEAT SENSOR, OR MORE EXPENSIVE FAILURE OF CONTROL BOARD. NO WAY TO TELL UNLESS I REPLACE THE ELEMENT AND TURN OVEN ON TO HEAT. I AM NOT A REPAIRMAN WITH AN OHM SENSOR TO CHECK THE OTHER PARTS. ONLINE RESEARCH SHOWS THAT REPAIRMAN VISIT IS AT LEAST $75 FOR A VISIT NOT INCLUDING COST OF FAULTY PARTS.

PURCHASED LOWER ELEMENT FOR $35, AND NO GUARANTEE THIS IS GOING TO FIX THE ISSUE. UPON FURTHER INTERNET RESEARCH I AM ALMOST CERTAIN IT IS EITHER THE HEAT SENSOR MALFUNCTIONING (APPROX $25) OR THE CONTROL BOARD (APPROX.$250). PRICE OF NEW STANDARD ELECTRIC RANGE (WITH COILS) IS APPROX $350-$450. 

I DO NOT HAVE RECEIPT FOR THIS OVEN, AS IT CAME WITH HOUSE I PURCHASED IN 2008. OVEN WAS NEARLY NEW AT THE TIME. PREVIOUS ELDERLY OCCUPANTS RARELY COOKED.

I FEEL THIS IS A DANGEROUS ISSUE AND SHOULD BE FURTHER INVESTIGATED IN THIS PARTICULAR BRAND OF OVEN. PRIOR RECALLS TO OTHER MODELS DUE TO FAULTY CONTROL BOARD, BUT MY PARTICULAR MODEL NOT INCLUDED. (FEF365BWA)

HAD I BEEN WORKING OUTSIDE IN THE YARD OR OTHERWISE INDISPOSED, I AM CERTAIN THE OVEN WOULD HAVE CAUGHT FIRE. I SHOULDN'T BE FEARFUL OF WALKING OUTSIDE FOR A FEW MINUTES OR TAKING A SHOWER WHILE I AM SLOW ROASTING FOOD AT A LOW TEMPERATURE.

Note:
Was slow-roasting chicken in oven @ 190 degrees. Chicken was in covered [REDACTED] dish. No drips, leaks, or grease on bottom of oven or element were present to cause burning or potential fire hazard. Oven was thoroughly clean prior to overheating incident. I also Do Not use the self-cleaning feature of this oven, or any chemical cleaners.
justification: The incident involved an overheating oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

My husband put some dishes in the dishwasher and closed the door.  the power button was in the on position, but he did not start the dishwasher.  He only closed the door.  Shortly thereafter, he noticed a large amount of smoke coming out of the top of the door.  He turned off the circuit breaker and then poured water into the door in an effort to stop the fire.  Fortunately, he was able to put out the fire very quickly. The smell was horrible, but luckily since were at home, the fire did not spread throughout our house.


I reported this to Asko on December 9th in hope that any design flaw could be corrected and that any necessary recall completed, so that this does not happen to anyone else.  I also requested compensation.  Asko's response about the safety was as follows: "Our dishwashers D3251 have been thoroughly tested at the UL Labs and they are not on a recall list."  However, I believe there is an obvious problem, if it caught on fire.  Regarding compensation, they indicated that they would supply parts and I would be responsible for the labor to repair the dishwasher.  However, this dishwasher was damaged beyond repair because of the amount of water that we had to pour into the door to stop the fire and smoke.  Our primary concern at the time of the fire was to put it out rather than put our family and home at risk.  Additionally, repairing a dishwasher that has caught on fire does not seem safe.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was quickly extinguished without injury or death, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
My wife and I purchased a high-end Electrolux ICON 48" Dual Fuel Range in May 2010 Model# E48DF76EPS Serial
Number CF8000187. We have had a gas leak in the main manifold that was finally resolved last month by replacing the main manifold assembly part# 5304453241.
Earlier multiple service trips by qualified Sears Home Services miss-diagnosed the problem as "several leaky gas valves" and that the entire manifold rail assembly would need to be replaced since if more than one valve is leaky, you end up paying for the whole rail anyway.

I am very disappointed that the FINAL ROOT CAUSE that was identified in a subsequent service trip by a DIFFERENT Sear Home Service Team identified a FAULTV WELD on the end of the manifold. The manifold is a fabricated iron pipe with welded end caps that are intended to be gas/air-tight. This manufacturing defect should NEVER have passed quality control. All of the gas valves were good, and did not leak. The welded end cap on the end of the manifold rail was the cause of the problem. It appears that after the welding of the cap, the person doing the fabrication ground the excess weld of, but ground too much and opened up a LEAK! I have the original part for inspection, and I expect that Electrolux will act responsibly and provide me with a full refund on the cost of the manifold rail assembly, since there was a factory manufacturing defect on the rail that should NEVER have shipped from the factory.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a manufacturing defect, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We bought our Kenmore oven model 790.97453804 in January of 2010, within the first year our oven door exploded shooting glass all over our kitchen and into the adjacent room.  We raised a stink with Sears and tried to get a replacement oven, even the local manager fought for us but sears corp would do nothing but repair it.  We were assured it wouldn't happen again.  Then the next year our stove started smoking (coming from the top of the oven where the controls are).  We immediately killed the power and found out from the tech (the same one who repaired the glass) that it was only the circuit board, nothing to worry about.  He was very nice but joked about how these units were junk and that we should not let our warranty expire as we would probably need something repaired yearly.  We did let our warranty expire because we thought to ourselves if it breaks again we are getting rid of it!  In our 3rd year of ownership the over door exploded again (this is the 2nd explosion).  I called Sears and explained how once again, they were lucky we weren't calling from a hospital and that they need to get this oven out of here.  I even told them every incident that I would buy a different one from them if they would return this one, even if it cost more money I would spend the difference just to have something safe.  I have small animals, young children..  We have a 5 yr old girl (now 5).  She loves to help bake and could you imagine if she were looking through the glass at the time of explosion?  I can only imagine Sears would take us seriously if that would've happened..  But why not take us seriously before an injury?   When I spoke to sears the 3rd instance and pleaded for some kind of return even if not 100% they said nothing they could do, they said they were very sorry and had little children too and can only imagine what that would be like.  Then for our troubles they offered us a 10% discount if we bought a new unit.  We declined.

The reason for my post / report is because I firmly believe these units have an issue with the door.  I also believe that Sears is ignoring this when they only choose to replace the glass and not the entire door.  All these people I read on the internet are having their oven doors explode.  If something isn't done someone will get hurt, if they haven't already.  Plus you have all these people who are out money on these stoves they bought.  I don't recall exactly what I paid for mine, I want to say 1,200 to 1,500 maybe.  I also want to mention the old stove I replaced when I bought this was from 1991 (one of the first glass tops ever), still worked perfectly, we only replaced this for the stainless look when we redid our kitchen.  I learned since then that Kenmore was made by a different company in 1991, that is why it was built better.

I just ordered another stove as I don't feel safe using this one anymore.  I do not know what to do with this stove.  If I sell it used will I be putting someone else's child at risk?  I can't live with that.  I called my attorney and am waiting to hear what they say.  Otherwise I assume we will have to scrap it and just learn that Sears doesn't deserve our business, ever.  

Does anyone here know of other options to try and recoup some of our loss?
justification: The oven door exploded twice, posing a significant risk of injury, especially to children, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description: We purchased and installed a Napolean vent free gas stove, Model GVFS20N.  Upon first use, 10/29/2013, discovered that the amount of time between opening of the gas valve and ignition of the burner significantly exceeded manufacturers specification.  We recorded 32 data points over a period of 24 days.  The ignition time averaged 53.25 seconds, with a low point of 2 seconds, and a high point of 180 seconds.  The manufacturers specification states "a 5 to 10 second total light up period is satisfactory."  When the gas valve opens, and the unit fails to ignite within the specified time, the room becomes flooded with natural gas, creating a hazardous condition.  The performance of the stove was verified by a licensed contractor who inspected adjustments and settings, and had a lengthy direct communication with the manufacturers technical support people explaining the issue.  The problem was not resolved at that time.  We registered a warranty claim with the manufacturer and are currently awaiting a disposition.

incident_description: I am the owner of (2) GE dishwashers, model ZBD0710K15SS purchased new by me in approximately 2006, serial numbers ZL770078B and ZL770135B.  Both of these dishwashers as of late have been running a motor or timer indefinitely after a cycle is complete ÃÂ this is a relatively new and atypical behavior.  At approximately 4am the morning of 01/09/2014 we were awoken to a strong burning smell, smoke,  and a fire alarm.  Machine #078B had been loaded with a few dishes the night before and had NOT been run, but the door completely closed.  #078B had apparently, without cycling through a wash cycle, turned the heating/drying element on and sat in that state for many hours, completely melting most if not all plastic dishes/cups inside, the silverware basket, and melted away the plastic coating of the upper and lower pull-out racks leaving only the wire frame and melted wheels.  At of today, 01/10/2014, #078B is still installed but functionally destroyed as a result.  It appears to me, left unchecked, this machine would have eventually started a fire.  Considering #135B is exhibiting the same symptoms of an ever-running motor or timer, I plan to uninstall both units and replace them with different units.  I have pictures of the damage.  I am reporting this event as both units seem destined for the same ultimate fate and desire to possibly prevent a much more serious outcome to people who may still have these machines in service.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that caused significant damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as the issue is recurring in a second unit.
