Consumer stated that while using the oven at 350 degrees, the broiler mode spontaneously came on but itself approximately 10 mins later.  She smelled a burnt odor, there was nothing placed in the oven at the time, the heating element was red hot.  The control panel displayed that the broiler was off, she was unable to power it off and had to use the circuit breaker.

12/30/13  The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that the unit was not included in a recall so they were unable to assist her.

She is concerned that this oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.

The oven model and serial number is not affected by a recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
kenmore wall oven 790.4878 roughly 3 to 4 years old.
Cooked a rack of ribs in the oven for 3 hours at 325' . When I slid the dish forward the rack fell out of the side tipping the hot food onto the oven floor and hot juices out onto my feet. I was not injured but it was a near miss.
justification: The incident involved hot food and juices spilling but no injury occurred, indicating a near miss with potential for harm.

incident_description:
The consumer says the knobs have melted three times, the control panel has been replaced twice and has melted a third time.  She says the metal bar underneath the panel is also melted.  She has called everytime it has happened she had to call the manufacturer who replaced it under warranty.  

They no longer want to repair it under warranty.  She was sent to a different department. The company told her that no one else has ever had this problem and that they will keep replacing the parts.
justification: The incident involves repeated melting of knobs and control panel, indicating a recurring issue, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was cooking and there was fire in the grill (top portion). The consumer stated that after the fire, she heard a loud pop. 

The consumer stated that the range was on for about 20 minutes before the incident occurred. 

The consumer stated that she tried to turn off the range. The consumer stated that after the incident, the range no longer works. The consumer stated that the unit is unplugged.

The consumer stated that she burned some parts of her hair and her right arm. The consumer applied ointment to the burned area. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manf regarding the incident. The consumer stated that the manf sent a technician. The technician informed the consumer that he is not an electrician and that she would need to call an electrician regarding this matter. The consumer stated that she has tried to contact the technician after the inspection and he does not call back. The technician informed the consumer that this is a not a safety issue. 

The consumer contacted the manf again and they informed her that they do not provide electricians to come and inspect. 

The consumer stated that the range was installed in her home when she purchased it in 2004/2005.
justification: The consumer suffered burns to her hair and arm, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
GE built-in dishwasher - purchased in March, 2005 and installed at that time.  Model No. PDW8700J03BB, Serial number FH754849B.

Unit proceeded to burn wiring harness and other electronics on 1-3-14.  Also melted water blade in the bottom of the unit to the heating element.  Contacted repair person and unit is completely unable to be repaired due to unavailability of a wiring harness through any parts depot.

Caused smoke to be emitted into the kitchen.  All wiring was completely melted.
justification: The incident caused smoke and damage to the dishwasher but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: LG French Door Refrigerator LFX25960ST interior lights will not turn off.  Like all the other reports here, I opened the door to find the lens cover melted and hanging down and the bulbs extremely hot.  I have contacted LG, but honestly this company needs to be forced to recall and repair these units at their cost.  Lights in the refrigerator compartment will not turn off when switches are pressed in,
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing melted lens covers and hot bulbs, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I smelled a funny smell in my clean refridgerator. I then saw some white smoke at the top of my refridgerator and realized the light bulb had melted the plastic in the roof of the inside of the refridgerator. I have a Frigidaire refridgerator and have found this is a common problem with these. I'm lucky my refridgerator didn't catch fire. I have since removed the light bulb and currently use my refridgerator with no light bulb.
justification: The incident involved a melted light bulb and potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says she had just turned th oven on and blew the door open.  they shut it down.  She contacted the manufacturer who sent out a technician.  He replaced the igniter.  He let it stay on for a while.  The consumer opened the door when a powerful gust of fire shot out at her.  It hit the side of her face.  

The technician took the plate off the bottom and the same thing happened to him.  The technician said they had to shut that unit down.  The consumer believes that there may not be a part available.

This product is under recall (Release # 01-108) and was sold to her in 2003, after the recall was issued.
justification: The incident caused injury to both the consumer and the technician due to a powerful gust of fire, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the product was sold after recall and the issue recurred.

incident_description:
Whirlpool dishwasher model#  with serial# purchased during the Spring of 2008 and had no problems with it until Friday, November 22nd, 2013.

Caller had just started the dishwasher then he and his wife were standing by the unit talking for no more than one minute when they heard an odd noise and flames shot up from the control panel.

The flames were approximately six inches high.

The caller ran to the breakers, switched the one to the dishwasher off then came back and unplugged the unit under the sink.

The dishwasher remains without power.

There are no injuries being reported 

Caller tried to contact the manufacturer, was on hold for a long time so hung up and contacted the retailer who took a report from the caller via email.

He may attempt to contact the manufacturer again.
justification: The incident involved flames from the dishwasher's control panel but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is unlikely as such events are not common but have been reported before.

incident_description:
(12/01/2013) The consumer stated that they smelled something  burning in the kitchen  so they shut off the power to the dishwasher. The consumer called, [REDACTED]a friend.

!2/17/2013) [REDACTED]took the dishwasher apart and discovered that the circuit board had caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved a circuit board catching fire, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
The oven was installed in the home that the consumer purchased. 

The consumer stated that she was in her room. The consumer's daughter left brownies in the oven. The oven was turned off.

The consumer stated that when her daughter went to take the brownies out, she heard cracking sound. The consumer stated that the outer glass of the oven shattered.

The consumer stated that this happened 15 minutes after turning off the oven. 

The consumer's daughter was using the oven on 325F. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the retailer. They informed her that there was no warranty on the product and that it was not registered by the previous owner. The consumer was informed that the tech would charge her $80 for inspection. The consumer was informed that the repair cost would be determined after inspection.

There are no recalls on this unit.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no injuries were reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The dishwasher had been in use for approx. 60 - 90 minutes and it was on the drying cycle. when the consumer's husband noticed a burning odor in their home.  The consumer also noticed the odor and saw that the kitchen began to fill with smoke.  The smoke appeared to be emitting from the bottom of the dishwasher, but it was difficult to see, due to the amount of smoke in the kitchen..


Both consumer's saw sparks emitting from the bottom of the dishwasher and when they opened the dishwasher door they saw flames in the bottom of the dishwasher.  The husband unplugged the dishwasher from the wall outlet and ran to get the fire extinguisher.  The husband sprayed the extinguisher on the flames and he was able to put them out.  The inside of the dishwasher is grey, but it was discolored from the fire.  
 

The consumer said that it appeared that the fire started underneath the dishwasher and burned up through the bottom of it, before the husband put it out.  The consumer said that the heating coil remained intact.  There were some plastic items in the top rack of the dishwasher, but they also were not affected by the fire.  The floor of the dishwasher tub melted and had actually been in flames.


(12/26/13)  The consumer called the manufacturer and reported the incident to them.  She spoke with [REDACTED] and the consumer was given a Complaint # [REDACTED]. 


The consumer noted that she uses the dishwasher daily most of the time.  The dishwasher has never been serviced for any prior reasons.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher causing smoke and flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The insullation around the heating coil of new my Black and Decker electric griddle (model #GD2011B) exploded the first time I plugged it in.  Small particles of very hot insullation material were strewn all over my counter causing burns which are too deep to be removed.
justification: The incident caused burns that are too deep to be removed, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Turned on the dishwasher and about 10-15 minutes later, just as we were dozing off, we heard an awful noise and realized it was our dishwasher. By the time we got up and flipped on the lights, our kitchen was filling with smoke. Smoke was boiling out of the control panel/door, but yet it it never lost power shutting itself off. [REDACTED] was finally able to get it to stop but it continued to burn from the inside of the control panel/door. It filled our house with smoke and a terrible burned chemical smell.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and a chemical smell, posing a significant fire hazard and potential health risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I put a cup of water in a microwave (Built-in, Maytag) and heated it up for about 2min at night on Jan. 4, 2014 as usual. (I do not use microwave frequently. I use it 3-4 times a week)
Then, I was sitting in a sofa in living room and drinking a cup of water heated in microwave but about 10 min later, I heard something weird and thought that sound came from a refrigerator.
However, the sound was too weird so I went to the kitchen to see what's going on, then found there was fire caught on the top of microwave in the electrical parts.
It was such a emergency and I called 911. Before the fire department arrived, I barely put out a fire with my neighbor's help but my kitchen already had significant damage.
If I had fallen asleep, it could have exploded due to the gas stove below the microwave and burned down whole building. Moreover, it could have cost many lives.
Fire department looked into the microwave and told me the fire was caused by electrical short circuit from microwave.
The fire occurred from a defective microwave and I am very sorry about this incident.
Therefore, I report this issue and request investigation of my microwave and Maytag product
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant kitchen damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Bacon Wave Microwave Bacon Tray partially melted when I cooked bacon in the microwave, following package directions.  The tray has vertical ribs to hold the bacon strips.  Plastic skewers are pierced through the slices to hold them in place.  One of the ribs melted and was deformed.  Another rib melted and had a piece of bacon embedded in the melted plastic.  Also there was a chip of plastic embedded in at least one of the pieces of bacon.  There may have been more that we inadvertently ate!! Unfortunately we did not notice the melting until we were cleaning the device, after we had eaten the bacon.  Since we have no way to know if we ate any plastic, we don't know if we were victims or not.  Therefore we are not reporting any victims.
justification: The incident involved plastic melting into food, but no injuries were reported, aligning with severity level 2.

incident_description:
(06/23/2013) The consumer stated that her mother was cleaning off the stovetop. She walked away and heard a big explosion. The consumer stated that the glass in the oven door shattered. The consumer stated that the oven had been turned off for about two hours. 



(08/15/2013) The consumer stated that she called the company today. The consumer was advised that there was a recall. She was then transferred to the recall department and was advised that there was no recall. The consumer was transferred back to the customer care department. She spoke with [REDACTED] who explained to her again that there was no recall. The consumer was given an offer to repair the oven door at 50 % off of a part.
justification: The incident involved a stovetop explosion and shattered oven glass, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Caller was awakened in the middle of the night December 23/24, 2013 to the smell of burning and when he checked for the source he found that his GE Dishwasher was smoking profusely.

The plastic components of the dishwasher  ie: plastic cutting board, cutlery baskets etc. were all melted.

The [REDACTED] Top of the unit was so hot that it could not be touched.

He opened the door and immediately his smoke alarms began sounding.

There was too much smoke to tell where the beginning was.

He never saw flames.

There were no injuries

He has sent the manufacturer an email regarding this incident.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking and had melted components, but there were no injuries or flames observed.

incident_description:
We were broiling some fish for dinner with two guests  in the toaster oven when we started to smell a strange electrical burning smell.  We turned off the broiler and removed the fish, and sat down to eat dinner.  However, the smell lingered and when my husband and I went into the kitchen to check the toaster oven, we saw that the heating elements were still red, even though the oven had been turned off.  (Normally, the elements stop glowing red almost immediately after turning off the oven.) We tried turning it on and off again, but the elements simply remained on.  The only way to turn off the elements was to unplug the toaster, which is of course what we did.  The next morning, to see if anything had changed, I plugged the oven back in and immediately the elements started glowing red without my having turned the oven on.  My husband then took the oven apart to see if he could identify the problem, but after reading information about the oven online, we found out that you cannot replace the circuit board, which we assume had shorted out.  The oven is, I believe, between five and six years old, but this model is still for sale.

This is an extremely hazardous situation -- what if we had left the house thinking the oven was actually off? The potential for burns is also significant --fortunately I was wearing an oven mitt when I took the fish out of the oven.  There is clearly something wrong with the wiring in the oven and just brief internet research indicates that other people have had this problem with this model.  Krups should recall this model.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toaster oven that remained on despite being turned off, posing a burn hazard and potential fire risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: The glass shattered but there were no injuries.
justification: Glass shattered but no injuries occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: We purchased a Kenmore Side by Side Refrigerator in October 2006 from Sears and today, January 3, 2014  we were luckily home when we heard an electrical buzz and pop coming from the kitchen. When we entered the kitchen a large plume of smoke was coming from the back of our refrigerator. We quickly pulled the fridge forward and noticed flames coming from the slats in the bottom left corner and we quickly unplugged the fridge. Additionally, a dark, syrup like liquid had pooled in the corner where the fridge was and was continuing to drip from the spot where the flames erupted. When we called Sears customer service they were completely unconcerned and offered to have a technician come out 2 weeks from today at our expense. Even after I explained the severity of the safety hazard this product posed to me and my family they continued to read from a "script" indicating that they could only offer an appointment 2 weeks from today but offered a service contract for $200 plus dollars. We are thankful that we were home when this happened as our entire home could have gone up in flames had we not been here to unplug the fridge. When I explained to customer service that upon my research I noticed other situations such as this with these same refrigerators they denied ever having that problem despite a news report and video explaining a relay switch malfunctioning in Kenmore, [REDACTED], and [REDACTED] refrigerators.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the refrigerator, posing a significant safety hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher control made a poof sound and then began smoking and then  arcing sounds and more smoke while running. Neither the Cancel button nor opening the door would stop the motor. Only unplugging stopped the machine.   Kenmore Elite (Whirpool) Model 665.16059400, Serial no. FS0906331
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned with smoke and arcing sounds, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The handle on the lid broke off while I was checking the soup in the crockpot; the lid dropped into the soup splattering hot liquid.  The crockpot had been on the low setting for approximately 6 hours.
justification: The incident involved a broken handle and splattering hot liquid, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore glasstop electric range was heating to (high/boil) when only set at a low temperature setting.  Burner was then failing to turn off when swithing the burner to the off position.  The only way to turn off the burner was to turn off the breaker in the breake box (eliminating power to the unit).  This happened with the original burner, and on at least replacement parts.  It is occuring again and this time happening wth two different burners.  It is creating a fire risk that the burner is not turning off when it should.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range that poses a fire risk but does not mention any injury or death.

incident_description: Yesterday our microwave oven started by itself and ran for about 5 seconds before shutting off.  It started by itself about 30 minutes later and ran for almost 1 minute; we had to open the door to turn it off.  We contacted the manufacturer who told us to unplug it for 30 minutes to reset it.  We have kept it unplugged unless we are in the kitchen as we are concerned about the fire hazard.
justification: The microwave started by itself but no injury occurred; the issue is concerning but not yet causing harm.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite refrigerator, french door model purchased in 2006. The Interior lights stay on when doors are closed. Caused the light cover to melt, become disfigured and fall off.  The heat from the light bulbs spoiled the food. The light bulb sockets are slightly charred.  
It is a fire hazard. I have removed the light bulbs to prevent a fire.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted light cover, spoiled food) and poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We have a General Electric Stove Model #JBS17GR2AD. Approximately 3:30 a.m. on December 25, 2013, I was awakened by a smell burning my nose. I got up and walked into my kitchen to smoke. I pinpointed the smell to my oven. I opened up my oven door to discover that the lower burner was on. A couple of seconds later the pan of oil, that I normally just stick inside, burst into flames. I got the pan out of the oven, the handle broke and the grease and fire fell to the floor and spread the fire further. The pan landed flat on my vinyl flooring with the oil still burning inside causing the floor to melt causing excessive smoke and smell. After calling 911, we were able to put out the fire. No dials were turned on to the oven. The oven came on by it's self and was extremely hot well above the broil point as it melted the pan handle causing it to break off. We was able to turn off the electric and allowed it to cool down. We then turned it back on and the stove continued to heat up again. It will not shut off. We unplugged the stove.  A couple days later, we plugged the oven back up and it continued to do the same thing.  We were very lucky, the only injuries I received was a burn to my hand and foot.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the hand and foot, indicating an injury, and the stove malfunctioned repeatedly, suggesting a possible recurrence.

incident_description: general electric/walmart 12 cup coffee maker model 169209  trips GFI during brewing and in keep warm mode
justification: The coffee maker tripping GFI indicates an electrical issue, which is an incident but no injury is reported.

incident_description: New year's eve, with friends kids in the house, the broiler element heated out of control until the oven was scorched and some parts warped.
justification: The incident involved property damage (scorched and warped oven parts) but no reported injuries, making it a severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but can occur with faulty equipment.

incident_description:
On new years day we were making stuffed pork chops. Luckily we had just returned from Church as we noticed the stovetop burner top on the flat surface was heating up with it turned off.  No one had touched it. We tried to turn it on and off but it wouldn't shut off. The burner got blazing hot we had to go shut off the whole electrical breaker off to be safe. If we had not been home or if this would of happened during the night I am sure we would of lost our home if not our lives.  Very scary.  We took pictures to show the burner was in the off position and continued to heat up.  This time of year is scary as could of had goodies sitting around ontop of the stove. 
 It is so unbelievable dangerous I refuse to use it again.  what if you fix part of the burners and the other ones have the same defect.  We could die next time or lose our home. So not worth it.  We bought the oven/stove at either Lowes only a couple of years old. Modle number is LEEFM389FEB it is a Fridigaire Elements they were expensive we have already replaced the fridigiare elements dishwasher due to malfunction after only 1 year of use, and now the stove.  The fridigiare elements fridge has also had issues the ice dislodges into the back by the motor or won't cool. These appliances are [REDACTED] very disappointed in the quality.  We lost freezer food twice. Do NOT buy you will regret it.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction of the stove that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have an LG gas range Model #LRG30357ST.  The control knobs are made of plastic and the sleeve to turn the gas on and off is made of plastic.  Due to the heat of the oven and range, the plastic sleeves crack.  THis cracking causes the knob to spin around the control stem.  Once this happens you can not tell by the setting of the control knob whether the gas is on or off.  Over thanksgiving we did a lot of cooking and thought the gas was off only to wake up to the smell of gas due to the inability to control the stem.  THe house had to be cleared and the range disconnected.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to faulty control knobs, posing a safety hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
GE Profile front load dishwasher
Model number: PDW9200N20WW
Serial number: AR861366B

Returned home on Dec. 31, 2013 at about 2:45 p.m. after an absence of 24 hours, smelled very strong noxious odor. Dishwasher door was very hot. Opened door & discovered that the heating element had superheated & melted the plastic rotor in the bottom & a few plastic dishes in the dishwasher, plus the pastic utensil tray. I turned the outside circuit breaker for the dishwasher off. 

The dishwasher is destroyed & will need to be replaced.

I had turned the dishwasher off before we left. The green "Start" light was off. The heating element malfunctioned & turned itself on.

No other damage outside the dishwasher.
justification: The incident caused property damage (destroyed dishwasher) but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I had a Crock-pot SCCPQP600-B slow cooker that after the first use melted the plastic in the base (smelled up my kitchen) and stopped working.  Reviews on amazon.com reported the same, but I figured it was user error or something.  I sent it back to the company (Jarden) and they graciously sent me a free nearly identical replacement (I got a SCCPQP600-S instead).  Yesterday was the first time I used the replacement and it too melted the base and smelled up my kitchen AGAIN.  Only difference is this one still works.  See the reviews on Amazon for the -B model if you want additional evidence that this should probably be recalled.  http://www.amazon.com/Crock-Pot-SCCPQP600-B-6-Quart-Smart-Pot-Squond/product-reviews/B003HFC9SG/ref=dp_top_cm_cr_acr_txt?showViewpoints=1

I've been using crock pots for years, I am a very technical/mechanically inclined person, so this is NOT user error.  This product is absolutely defective and unsafe.

I'm already in contact with Jarden about this defective product and they're offering me a refund after I mail this one back to them.  If you all need proof I have taken pictures of what happened (unfortunately only of the second one), but I can give as much detail as you all need...
justification: The incident describes a defective product causing melting and odor, but no injury or death, with multiple reports indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
We have a Kitchen Aid dishwasher that caught on fire last night.  My wife and I started a load of dishes, and shortly after smelled electrical burning and saw smoke coming out of the control panel area.  Luckily we were sitting near by to see this.  We quickly ran to the dish washer to open the door and shut it off.  The dishwasher kept running with the door open.  We then tried to hit the cancel button, and the appliance still wouldn't shut off.  I had to run down into the basement to shut power off to the dishwasher at the electrical box.  Our kitchen was filled with smoke, and our whole house smells like an electrical fire.

*Also we would like to know if these washers are able to be safely fixed.  We are sure of the extent of damage yet, as the repair man has not come yet.  But have the replacement circuit boards been safely redesigned?  We are concerned of still having a fire hazard in our house if we make repairs, as we've heard these dishwashers can catch on fire even when they are off.  Any information or suggestions you could give us would be very much appreciated.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, filling the kitchen with smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On more than one occasion, my glass cook top (Kenmore) has failed to shut off when the burner knob was turned to the off position. It has also produced constant "high heat" regardless of what heat setting the knob is turned to. This has caused damage to cookware and a minor burn to my hand when I grabbed a handle that should not have been hot to the touch, as the stove was on low. I found a recall that described these problems, but my stove's serial number was not listed.
justification: The incident caused a minor burn and damage to cookware, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue has occurred multiple times, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: Frigidaire Wall Oven Model GLEB30S9DBA. My wife was using this oven to cook dinner, and she heard beeping and smelled burning electrical. All the LEDs were illuminated, and she couldn't open the oven because the oven lock had engaged. I came and inspected, and suspected an electrical fire. I ran downstairs to throw the circuit breaker, which then stopped the smoke and beeping. After removing the control panel, I noticed the back of the control board was burned. I inspected our other oven (we have 2 wall mounted ovens, both the same model), and it had minor burns on the back of it was well, but was working fine. This is clearly a manufacturing failure, and not an isolated incident. The home and ovens are only 8 years old.
justification: The incident involved a burning electrical smell and a burned control board, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury occurred. The presence of similar issues in another oven suggests a recurring manufacturing defect.

incident_description: My fridge developed an bad bitter smell and items were no longer cold, especially on the top shelf. I found that the interior light was not shutting off even when door closed and the bulbs had melted some of the plastic surround and spoiled some of the food. Internet search show this is not an uncommon failure of this fridge.  Even pressing the buttons on the doors that shut off the light manually has no effect.
justification: The incident caused spoiled food and minor property damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The issue is described as not uncommon, indicating a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
Our Jenn-Air dual fuel range started on fire tonight. 

After about three years of use, I came downstairs to the kitchen because our dog was barking to find the range was billowing black smoke. I turned off the circuit and unplugged the range.

The ignition switches on the stove top were clicking and popping. This must have started the fire.

I looked up the description of Jenn-Air dual fuel range and fire on the Internet and it has happened to a number of other people. 

This range is not safe. If we were not home I am not sure how far the fire would have gone.

Please look into this product and force a recall. I would not trust this range at all.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, but potential for significant harm if occupants were not present.

incident_description: My GE refrigerator/freezer caught on fire.  Model TBX21N1PRAA.  It appeared the fire started on the inside of the freezer by the automatic factory installed ice maker.  Yesterday I smelled something like and electrical fire and today the unit is totally smutted up and the food is a total waste.  Plastic inside the freezer is now warped and deformed.  The whole unit smells terrible.  I am fortunate that this electrical fire did not burn down the house.  I am very concerned and worried.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, causing property damage and food waste, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I woke to the smell of gas about one half hour after my husband left for work. I immediately went down stairs to the kitchen to find the gas burner on the stove on high without a flame.  My husband was in cabinets and must of bumped the front knob, turning the gas on.  I immediately turned the gas off, opened all the windows and door in the house.

Fortunate for us, I had the day off from work. Typically I leave for work before my husband (6a) and we do not return until 8p on most days.  This could have been catastrophic as you can well imagine.  Our children are all in college and not home but we do have multiple pets that would have perished with the house and it's content.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with no injury or death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was caused by an accidental bump of the stove knob.

incident_description:
I have a GE side-by-side refrigerator model ZFSB23DRGSS. Water was pooling up in the bottom of the refrigerator side. The refrigerator was running at 40F and the freezer at 0 F.

The evaporator fan motor assembly contains foam insulation, as does the beverage center duct. Both pieces of insulation were impregnated with ice and appeared to be frozen solid. Even after sitting out at room temperature, the foam wouldn't dry out.

Additionally, the foam surrounding the evaporator fan was covered in black mold/mildew. All of these parts have been replaced, but the problem of condensation on the parting wall and high refrigerator temps persists. Although I've cleaned the refrigerator from the mold/mildew, I'm afraid it will return and pose health risks.

A similar issue was reported by another consumer as incident # 20120618-0EC21-2147466518.
justification: The incident involves mold/mildew and persistent condensation, posing potential health risks, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: The glass in the oven door spontaneously shattered. The oven was not in use at the time, nor had it been used in the past 24 hours. The gas was not on. It was not hot. There was nothing in it or near it. The door was upright and in its typical fixed resting position. It simply shattered for unknown reasons. Oven model is Whirlpool Super Capacity 465 Self-cleaning Oven. It is old but in good shape.
justification: The oven door glass shattered spontaneously, but no one was injured or at risk since the oven was not in use and no one was nearby.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on March 20, 2012 his dishwasher caught on fire while it was running the cleaning cycle for approximately 10 minutes. The upper part of the door (control panel) was emitting flames. He tried to turn the dishwasher off through the control panel and it did not work. He turned it off from the circuit breaker and by the time (unknown) he got back to the kitchen the flames had stopped. 

The consumer stated that the control board and the circuit were chard, melted and burnt. The dishwasher is no longer usable and the consumer does not plan to try to use it. He stated that this was the first time that he experienced any problems with the dishwasher.

There was no damage to the consumerÃÂs home. He did not have to contact the fire department.  There were no injuries.

The consumer feels that this is a fire hazard because it could of cause a house fire and possible deaths. He feel that this should be investigated.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was contained without injury or property damage, and the consumer reported no prior issues, indicating this is an isolated incident.

incident_description: Crock pot overheated and the cord melted off, also causing my kitchen counter top to crack.  This was verified by factory rep that it was a heat crack.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted cord and cracked countertop) but no injury or death.

incident_description: I had used the oven for approximately 1 hour at 400 degrees making two batches of nachos. There was a 15-20 minute time between the two batches. There was no spill, drip or any mess what-so-ever on the element from the nachos. When the second batch was done, I turned off the oven. A little while later, I see smoke coming from the back of the stove which happens when I use the broiler. I open the oven and the element is bright red and the oven is very hot. I check to see if I had turned the oven off and yes I had. I push off/cancel again and the oven beeps several times with f1 flashing on the panel. I quickly get out the manual and read about the f1 indicator. It suggests I push cancel and reprogram oven. If that doesn't work, I should record fault number and contact Sears for service. First of all, while I am waiting on the phone for Sears service, my oven is getting about as hot as it can without catching fire. Then,LOC starts flashing on the display panel. I close the oven door and it locks which is probably a good thing. Less chance of fire. Still no Sears on the line so I hang up. It finally dawns on me to trip the circuit. The scary part of this is that there was no indication that the oven was malfunctioning until I saw the smoke and pushed off again. If I had just stayed in the other room eating nachos with everyone else who knows what could have happened. We have tried turning on the circuit again and the oven just heats up, very hot, all the while indicating nothing. Very dangerous! I have seen on YouTube that many people have experienced the same thing. This product should definitely be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred, and similar issues are reported by others.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting Electric Range purchased in June 26th, 2008 and had no problems with her range until April 7th, 2013.

Model#  with Serial# VF81953653.

April 7th, caller had placed a dish of food in the oven set 350 degrees and had been turned on for approximately five minutes when she happened to look over at her range and the coil was on fire, flames were in the center, were possibly an inch high and were slowly burning while slowly moving from the center to include the sides. 

Range is beside the sink so it was simple to throw water on it

She contacted the manufacturer April 8th, 2013, at 8:15AM, spoke with [REDACTED], created reference# [REDACTED] and was advised that they could only schedule repair at her expense due to the warranty having expired.

There have been no injuries
 If consumer has range repaired or replaced she would like to be reimbursed.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the electric range but no injuries were reported, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description: I bought the Bela Juicer for Christmas. Juiced the first glass with no issues. During juicing of the second glass, which included cranberries, lemon, orange (peeled), and a small knob of ginger, a large chunk of the plastic cover broke away and was shot towards the ceiling. It came from the top clear cover and was located on the opposite side of the dial. The piece of plastic was about 1 inch wide and 1 1/2 inches long, it hit the ceiling and then fell back down. This also caused pulp and residue to fly all over the walls and cabinets. If I had been standing on the opposite side, it could of flown and hit me in the face or a small child who is watching the juicer work. There was alot of velocity and force to break the plastic and send it flying to my 9 foot ceilings.
justification: A large piece of plastic broke off with significant force, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Was cooking soup, went to turn off the burner, and the left right burner was stuck on!! Had to turn off my breaker, tried to turn it back on hoping it was off, and the burner was still on high, and will NOT turn off!
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The right front burner on the smooth top cooking surface came back on by itself after being shut off. We turned off the breaker switch, but if you turn the breaker on, the burner will come on by itself. If we had left home without noticing the burner had come on, I fear a fire would have started, or the very least using up a lot of power.
justification: The burner reactivating by itself poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: We have a LG Range Model #LRG3095ST with the manufacture date of March 2013. On November 20,2013 my wife was preheating the oven, when all of a sudden she heard a loud pop. She went into the kitchen and saw the interior glass of the oven had shattered and the oven was only at 340 degrees.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering during preheating, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
In regards to my 2009 Kenmore wall oven (model number:  79047789406).

Was cooking in my oven at 400 degrees when out of nowhere the outer glass of the oven door exploded all over my kitchen, throwing glass all the way to the other end of my dining room and also going under the door into my office and utility rooms.  I had two small children, under the age of two, who were sat in the dining room, about 15 feet away, playing on the floor and while fortunately they were not injured, the were sprayed with glass and terrified after the incident.  The glass was over 20 feet away from where the oven is.  I have not used the self cleaning function of this oven, I have not closed the oven door on the wire rack, and certainly have never hit the glass door with anything.  This product is entirely unsafe and a recall should be issued to prevent injuries or children being sprayed with glass.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, spraying glass over a wide area, including near two small children who were unharmed but terrified. This indicates a high potential for injury.

incident_description: I own a GE Profile Dishwasher model PDW9880N00SS, serial number AM762945B. On Friday, December 27, we loaded and started the dishwasher about 3 p.m. At about 6 p.m. my daughter opened the dishwasher to take out silverware to use for dinner with guests. The steam that rushed out was scalding hot and caused her cheeks to immediately turn red. She used a towel to remove the silverware and closed the door. At approximately 7:30 p.m. while serving appetizers to guests we noticed a burning smell coming from the kitchen. We finally located to smell and found the plastic containers on in the dishwasher melted and dripped onto the element, washing arm, and the bottom rack. The temperature within the dishwasher was in excess of 350 degrees. We attempted to over-ride the cycle by pressing the cancel button on the top panel to no avail. The dishwasher would not turn off. We immediately unplugged the power cord and left the door open to cool the remaining dishes that were on the racks. The counter above the dishwasher was scalding and it took nearly an hour for the dishes to cool to a point that they could be removed. I am very concerned that this could have started a fire if it would have been running overnight.
justification: The incident caused injury (red cheeks from scalding steam) and had potential for more severe harm (melted plastic, high temperature, risk of fire).

incident_description:
On Saturday December 28th, our GE Profile dishwasher melted and nearly burned. 
The serial number is LL766905B.  More details below.
I turned on the dishwasher mid-afternoon using the same method of stacking the dishes, same type of detergent, and same cleaning settings we have used for the past six years. In the early evening I noticed that the machine was still washing, but did not recognize that the device was broken. It did strike me as odd though. 
I returned to the kitchen in the late evening (11pm) and immediately noticed the very strong smell and higher temperature in the room. There was significant smoke coming from the device, and the granite counter top above the dishwasher was too hot to touch. Had I not returned to the kitchen I have little doubt that there would have been a fire. The internal plastic parts of the dishwasher melted, our dishes now have cracks, the cutlery is also covered in blackened plastic.

Please contact me to discuss the event and next steps. I may be reached by cell phone at [REDACTED] or by email [REDACTED] I have taken photos of the damaged dishwasher.

Below is a copy of the output from the GE web site that lists recalled devices.  Our dishwasher is not included in the list of recalled units that exhibit the same problem,but it does match the first two letters of the serial number of recalled devices on your website. 
http://www.geappliances.com/products/recall/dishwasher_2012/outcome1.htm?MODELNUMBER=PDW9280L00SS&SERIALNUMBER=LL766905B

Your dishwasher is NOT included in the recall.
Model number: PDW9280L00SS
Serial number: LL766905B

Based on the model and serial numbers you submitted, your dishwasher is not included in this recall.
justification: The dishwasher melted and nearly caused a fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dishwasher was placed in wash cycle, after it completed the cycle the heating element stayed on.  She was alerted by her spouse who informed her that he smelled a burning odor (like burnt plastic).  She discovered that the odor was emitting from the dishwasher because it never powered off.  The plastic racks had melted inside.  She was unable to use the control panel to power it off, the circuit breaker was used to switch it off

The dishwasher was left opened but she inadvertently bumped into it and close the door and it spontaneously turned on.  The unit is being kept off using the circuit breaker.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.

The product is not part of a recall.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, causing a burning odor and melted racks, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood of recurrence is high given the spontaneous reactivation and inability to power off normally.

incident_description:
(10/2013) The consumer stated that she was cooking chicken breast. The slow cooker was set on low. The consumer stated that she went near the  area and could feel excessive heat coming from the product. She picked up the slow cooker and saw that her counter was burned. The consumer unplugged the unit.

The consumer was advised to send in estimates for repair or replacements of the damages. She was also  asked to send the slow cooker back to them as well as pictures. The consumer stated that she did not hear from the manufacturer again. 

12/02/2013) The consumer called the manufacturer. She was told  that they could not get the cooker to re-create the incident. She was advised that the product works properly. The consumer asked the manufacturer to send the cooker back to her.

The consumer was given case #05784168.
justification: The incident involved excessive heat and counter damage but no injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as similar incidents are not uncommon with faulty appliances.

incident_description: We have a Whirlpool Gold Electric Range  (GFE461LVS) we purchased on 8-12-09.  On June 16th, 2013 and December 14, 2013 the oven malfunctioned.  In particular, the oven while in use jumped from bake 375 degrees to broil at 550+.  On both occasions the contents that were cooking caught fire, and the oven would not turn off.  Smoke was billowing out of the oven, our smoke alarms went off and we had to throw water into the oven to stop the fire.  Since the oven would not turn off, we had to flip the circuit breaker to stop the oven from maintaining the broil temperature.  Both times that this has happened, we were cooking different items.  The second incident required us to use a fire extinguisher and to contemplate calling the fire department.  I have researched this issue online and there are others with the same issue with the Whirlpool Gold ranges.  The oven both times, was just a few minutes from catching the house on fire.  This is an extreme incident that cannot be ignored.  We will be having to replace this range since we do not trust the oven not to catch fire again.  We will not be getting it serviced since when I did my research those who are having the same issue, no servicing helps and they have to buy a new range.
justification: The oven malfunctioned twice, causing fires that required intervention to prevent house fires, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Control Panel on Kenmore Dishwasher exploded and burned during use. Sounded like a muffled boom and there was a flash. There was melted plastic and metal. The damage was extensive to the control board, housing panel and wiring harness. Cost to repair was more than 75% cost of a new comparable dishwasher
justification: The incident involved an explosion and fire causing extensive damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: The oven was on bake and preheated on the lowest temperature that it has. All the sudden the room got very bright, and the oven was on fire. The fire was contained to the interior of the oven. After putting out the fire, the broiler seemed to be the cause of the fire, though the oven was not on the broil setting. The boiler element continued to have a small fire until the unit was unplugged. Once the unit was unplugged, the small fire eventually stopped.
justification: The fire was contained to the oven interior and no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such incidents are not common but possible with faulty equipment.

incident_description: coffee maker turned on by itself then started smoking,strong burning smell and smoke were coming out of base of unit. Had to put coffee maker in water to stop smoke from coming out. Potential house fire danger if i was not allerted to smoke by smoke detector

incident_description:
While cooking bread in the oven with tthe temp. of 350 degrees,  My oven door exploded.  I heard a loud pop and glass shot out and shattered everywhere.  I looked on the computer and noticed that this was a common problem with the Sears ranges.  I called the local Sears and the manager told me I needed to call the Customer Solutions.  I called them and they told me that there was no recall on the product so they could do nothing for me.  I purchased the range September of 2010.  The warranty just ran out about 3 weeks ago. I did not purchase a warranty because I believed in their product.  I  purchased this range to replace one that I had for 13 years. and we were changing the kitchen to stainless appliances.My old Kenmore range worked perfect when I sold it last year.  Sears said it was not their problem.  I am thankful that my children were not in the kitchen when this happened.  Sears needs to recall this oven.  
On their website (Sears) under the same range (model #)someone posted the same problem (exploding glass) on June 26, 2011. 
 This is a problem that needs to be addressed and I should NOT have to pay to fix the door.  This is a hazard and should be recalled.  This range is defected.  I am concerned that when the glass is replaced this will happen again.   Customer Relations told me that they could do nothing about the problem even if it happened again and YES he thought it needed to be recalled too.

incident_description:

incident_description: I have had my dishwasher for a number of years. Recently the control panel would only work intermittently. It stopped working all together after filling the dishwasher with water the last time. I took the door apart to inspect the control panel and the wires. I found that the wires had melted into the sound deadening material on the door due to extreme heat. I researched this issue online and found that this model dishwasher was the subject of a recall due to fires caused by the overheating. Unfortunately the recall apparently only covers plastic front models where mine has a stainless steel front.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with melted wires, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: A 6-cup Pyrex glass dish had just come out of the oven (350 degrees) with a small ham portion. It was sitting and cooling, my wife walked out of the kitchen and a minute later, walked back in and the glassware had shattered.

incident_description: Hi..was baking a roast pork in a shallow baking dish, made by Corning, which we've had for a few years.It was on the middle rack in the oven, set at 425 degrees according to the directions on the meat packaging, for the proper length of time, after only(40)minutes  we heard a funny sound come from the kitchen, as we were in the next room. incident_description: While using my stainless steel kenmore gas range Model #790.71513400, Serial# VF44156721 my left shin was lacerated by the corner of the open oven door where two sta inless steel metal edges came together to make the corner of the oven door. When the toaster in on the counter top and your standing in front of it, you cant see the heating element because its view is blocked by the top of the oven.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore oven, model #790.72903013.  Today I used the self cleaning feature.  I followed the instruction carefully for the self cleaning feature.  All was well, until just after the cleaning cycle stopped, my daughter said something made a big "pop" sound in the oven.  When I investigated, I noticed the glass on the oven door was shattered.  It appears to be a 3 pane door.  The outer most, and inner most glass are somewhat intact, the the inside glass is shattered.  I was cleaning the outside of the oven after this happened and noticed tiny shards of glass on the floor in front of the oven, and in the corner of the handle to the warming drawer.  I am about to contact Sears and see what they can/will do for me.

incident_description: Our Kitchenaide electric range-oven started by itself in the middle of the night reaching a temperature of 450 degrees.  We heard beeping in the middle of the night, but never suspected the range.  Had there been anything flammable in the oven, there certainly would have been a fire.  We have repeatedly reset/unplugged the range, but within 5 minutes, the oven again starts by itself, sometime setting itself to 500 degrees.  Kitchenaide was called and has refused to recall or notify owners of this issue.
justification: The incident involved an oven starting by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
I have GE Profile PDW8680N00SS dishwasher. I started a cycle at 10:00PM last night before going to the bed. When I woke up at around 5:30AM, I smelled a horrible smell of burnt plastic. I figured out that its coming from the dishwasher. As I opened the door to the dishwasher smoke came bellowing out of it. This was not just any smoke, it felt really toxic, made our eye tear up and you could see smoke through out the house. Keep in mind the washer had been turned on more than 7 hours earlier.. what if we didn't wake up? The granite counter was so hot that you can get burnt just by touching it. The heater inside still kept pushing heat even when the door was open. I had to disconnect the power to dishwasher for it to stop pumping heat.

All the plastic-ware inside were melted. Any part of the dishwasher that was plastic had melted too (spray arm at the bottom, the rack where we keep spoons and forks and even the front control melted and was bent inwards)

This is a real fire hazard and it was a scary situation to see all the smoke come out. My model was the GE Profile with the stainless steel interior, GE has already recalled another model from the same batch that has a plastic interior. So they told me its not part of a recall even though the problem that triggered recall on plastic model is exactly the same. This is not an isolated case - other people have reported same melting (fire hazard) on this stainless-steel model. Its high time that GE recall this model before somebody gets seriously injured.
justification: The incident involved a significant fire hazard with toxic smoke and potential for injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: We bought a Kitchenaid Artisan gas stove and when using it the knobs get so hot that they have burned my fingers. We have small grandchildren and are very concerned that they will get burned by these knobs. we have only had the stove for a week and while it works well, I don't like getting my fingers burned each time I use the oven and the stove top
justification: The knobs get hot enough to burn fingers, which constitutes an injury, and the presence of small grandchildren increases the likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The oven was preheated to 350 degrees and the pan was being used to bake chicken breast.  After 30 minutes in the oven, I opened the oven to turn the chicken and the pan exploded inside the oven with the door opened.  No one was hurt, but varing sizes of  glass pieces were inside and outside of the oven.
justification: The pan exploded causing glass pieces to scatter, but no one was hurt.

incident_description: I'm reporting a serious safety issue with a Maytag ice dispenser in refrigerator model number MFI2568AEB Serial number 12569744LR. A few months ago one of us almost swallowed and choked on a white piece of plastic that came out of the automatic ice dispenser. When I looked in the ice dispenser I did not see any plastic but only the metal auger. Today my wife said that my daughter got another piece of hard plastic in her drink this morning 12/19/2013. When I saw the plastic it looked just like the one that I found before. incident_description:
In July, 2012 my husband and I purchased a Whirlpool 30" Electric Glass Cook Top Range with Steam Clean. We purchased it new and received a one year warranty.

Within two months of purchase, the plastic gliders for the storage drawer cracked and broke--thereby rendering the drawer useless as far as ease of access was concerned.

In December of 2012, I noticed a drip on the glass window.  I figured I would clean it when I cleaned the oven.  Low and behold, it would not clean.  It took me a few months (2-3) to realize the seal on the glass window of the oven had a leak.  The drip was on the inside.  This is a serious problem.

In September of 2013 (when the range was out of warranty) I had a problem with the glass cooktop.  I had a saucepan of rice simmering on the back right burner.  I was sitting in the living room.  I was hearing a very light crackling sound and presumed it was the wind and trees outside.

We had dinner.  The next day, I attempted to clean the stove top.  There was a spot on the burner where I placed the rice which I could not remove.  Over a period of a week or two, I would give it a little cooktop cleanser and rub--to no avail.  

Imagine my surprise when I discovered under a strong light the spot was not a spot.  Rather it was an area where small bits of glass popped off all over the top of the range--and possibly in our food.  You can see the spot and feel the gouge in the surface of the glass.

I was absolutely appalled.  I have been cooking for over 40 years.  I've used gas and electric without any problem.  I previously had a glass gas cooktop in my former home.  Glass has never been a problem until Whirlpool.  

These specks of flying glass could blind someone.  They are dangerous and justify a recall.

I clearly remember the problem several years ago with the exploding glass [REDACTED] Cook Ware.  

This problem was not of my doing.  Neither was the seal break in the window.  I do not abuse my appliances.  I take very good care of them and only replace them when necessary--never just because some new innovation has arrived on the market.

When I was seven years old, a boy on the playground was throwing rocks at me.  One hit me square in the right eye and bloodied it.  My mother had me at the doctor first thing the next morning.  The doctor told my mother I would have to be hospitalized for at least a week.  

For seven days I laid flat on my back in St. Margaret's Hospital, Minneapolis MN.  The doctor ordered both of my eyes to be completely covered to prevent straining my left eye.  He informed my parents directly the injury had a little better than 50% chance of blinding me for life.  

For seven days I laid in darkness and was spoon fed.  I recovered.  However, the doctor warned my parents any more injury to this eye would result in the loss of sight--permanently.  

I am sure you see my concern.  I would fear a young child being blinded by popping and flying glass.

Whirlpool is unconcerned.  Both contacts with them only resulted in the solution of calling for repair service.

A glass cook top should not snap, crackle and pop all over my kitchen after 15 months of use.  

Whirlpool is very ambivalent about this problem.  To replace the cook top would cost me approximately $300.  I'd bet money, marbles or chalk the same problem would recur.

Whirlpool needs to Man/Woman Up on this one.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning cooktop with potential for injury from flying glass, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Both ovens were in use.  The lower oven was set to 375 degrees.  The consumer said that she heard the oven's fan come on and thought it sounded unusual.  The upper oven was also set to 375 degrees and it had been on for 5 - 10 minutes.  The consumer noticed a strange odor after the food was placed in the upper oven.  It resembled a burning electrical odor.

The consumer opened the top oven to see if some food had fallen.  A gas ball shot from the oven and nearly hit the consumer. She immediately slammed the oven door.  The husband heard a popping sound, but neither he or the consumer knew where the noise came from.  Within a minute, smoke began emitting from the vents in the front of the oven.  The consumer immediately turned both ovens off, but they could also see flames behind the stove.  They used a fire extinguisher to put out the flames.  The fire was contained in the back panel of the oven and there was no damage to the house.

The fire department was contacted and they responded within 5 ÃÂ 10 minutes.  The firemen inspected the home to ensure that there was no fire still left in the home and there was not.  The fireman said that a pocket of fuel had built up in the oven and that is what shot out at the consumer.  The fireman confirmed that there was a defect in the oven and they advised the consumer to contact someone about the stove.  The electrical panel in the rear of the stove is what ignited.

The consumer also noted that the oven's controls remained lit even after she turned it off.  It wasn't until she unplugged it that the lights were off.

The consumer also called her propane company and the person she spoke with reiterated what the fire department had said.

The consumer said that her son sustain a few blisters while removing the hot stove from the house, but no medical treatment was needed.
justification: The incident involved a fire and minor injuries (blisters) to the consumer's son, but no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:
As I was leaving our home for work I noticed a burning plastic smell. I ran to the kitchen to discover the largest front left stove eye was bright red and very hot. No one had used the stove. The stove was off earlier when I fed the cat. A plastic pan handle was over the eye and smoking. There was grease in the pan. The knob was in the OFF position. When I returned home, I turned the stove back on and I was able to capture HD video the stove eye turning red and the control display malfunctioning. I can send it to you for your reference if you would like.

incident_description:
I wanted to register with you that within the past 3 months I've have 2 CrockPot brand crock pot lids shatter into small shards of glass.
Neither was being used in any way against their instructions. The first was cooking a pork tenderloin (on low). I complained to the company - they sent me a new one. Within 3 uses the lid of the new one shattered on Thanksgiving Day. The CrockPot contained mulled cider.
I will be calling the company again on Monday to complain, but I will not use their product again. It is very dangerous, aside from the fact that I lost some expensive food to the debacle. I have no faith that it will not happen again.

incident_description: This is regarding an LG microwave oven, model LCS1410SW, which I purchased on 11/29/2011. A problem recently developed where burning and sparking occurred on the front edge of the oven frame (where it meets the bottom of the door). The inside of the door has special insulating material but the bezel of the oven that the door presses against only has a painted surface. Due to what I believe is a manufacturing./design defect, small amounts of paint have come off in one or two spots, thereby exposing bare metal to the microwave energy and causing burning and sparking. I covered up the spots with cloth tape to stop the sparking but I feel that this is potentially a safety hazard that LG should correct.  I contacted LG via e-mail but since the oven is past the 6 month warranty they will not fix this defect at no charge.  The oven is working fine otherwise. A service call expense would exceed the value of the oven and were it involving some other part of the oven I'd understand LGs position.  However, I feel that in this case there is the potential for leakage of microwave energy or at least the possibility of a fire if additional paint comes off.

So the company knows that they are selling a defective and dangerous product but is taking no steps to recall it. This is unacceptable. 

Please investigate this product quickly before someone gets killed in a house fire!

incident_description: The upper oven would not turn off.  After using my GE Built-in Electric Convection Oven last weekend when I went to turn it off a small section of the bottom element in the upper oven continued to heat.  I watched it for a couple of hours thinking it would eventually cool, but the oven continued to stay hot and in fact the element started to burn through along its length.  After investigating this problem on the internet we discovered that this was a common problem and had resulted in house fires when the element burned all the way around and then continued to heat which caused the back of the oven to catch fire.  Upon finishing the repair to our oven, we were told that this is a known problem caused by a design flaw at GE.  Evidently for a period of 5 to 7 years GE eliminated one of the relay switches in the ovens to try and save money; however, when they started to get complaints about the problem caused by this measure, they went back to the original design.  We have never received any notification from GE about the potential hazards caused by this design change and in fact had to pay to have the problem corrected.  In fact, they problem still exists because the only repair was to replace the element that had failed.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven element that could lead to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My mother has a Whirlpool Natural Gas Cook Stove.  It is model WFG51050AW, serial number R33570420.  This burner knobs on the front of the stove use a very weak spring mechanism to keep the burner knob from accidentally being turned and thus igniting the burner.   On three occassions my mother has reached up over or beside the stove to put something in a cabinet and the unit was lit when she has brushed the knobs.  Due to the type of clothing she was wearing she did not catch her clothing on fire.  This is a safety hazard!    

Most people expect that this will only happen when a "larger" person hits the knob.  My mother is 5-6 and weighs about 120 lbs.   I was able to walk up to the stove and catch the knob with my belt buckle and cause it to turn.  It did not turn to the ignition point, but natural gas flowing.  

The repair man came out and stated that there is nothing he can do about this.  This is the way the stove was engineered.  

Older model stoves required a more substantial forward motion to allow the knob to be turned.  

With this model it would be easy for a child to light the stove and catch combustibles on/near the stove on fire.  It would be just as easy for an adult to brush up against the stove and cause it to ignite.  

I am reporting this for my mother as I am the [REDACTED] for the Volunteer Fire Department that serves that area. Any contact with the victim will need to be scheduled through me.  Thanks,  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard where the stove knobs can be easily turned, potentially causing gas flow or ignition, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

I set the timer for the pizza to 15 mins. At 8 mins. I heard a noise similar to silverware hitting the floor. I did not notice anything on the floor upon investigation. A minute later, I heard a loud cracking noise and noted the oven glass door on the inside of the oven had cracked visibly. I opened the door and a large glass shard fell into the space between the inner and outer glass doors. I turned the oven off and transferred the pizza to the lower oven (it's a double oven). incident_description:
Item:  NuWave Induction Cooktop - a nationally TV advertised device found also on e-bay and e-mail outlets..

Has worked well - does not maintain the temp on the setting but does hold a temperature.  The device, when working safely, is a valuable addition to kitchen work. 

However the device rapidly becomes dangerous. The danger occurred recently (item is less than a year old). The various buttons on the device that select temperatures and on/off/program functions is made of a flexible plastic placed that covers an  opening in the frame of the control panel on the front of the device. The plastic covers a hole through which a small extension plastic piece permits movement (pressing) of the covering plastic to transfer the pressing movement to a  micro switch on the printed circuit board enclosed within the control panel). The opening faces upward toward the cooking surface and is directly exposed to any liquid spill or boil over.  Fluid that enters the hole drains directly onto the electrical power supply and control of the machine.  The hole is approximately 1 1/2 Cm in diameter.  It slants from  the spill over surface and directs liquid into the control compartment. 

The plastic cover becomes brittle with age and cracks. In this case the age is less than one year.  When cracked, the crack increases in size and shape in a day or two and opens completely to the size of the frame's hole that it has previously covered.  1 - 1 1/2 cm diameter.

I have reported this defect to the Nu Wave information service that I have addresses for  I have had no response from that organization.  I have reported it to some consumer safety organizations.  No response has returned.  I am uncertain that I have found a correct address for reporting. 

This information should be available to purchasers so that the hole can be covered.  I have no information how the company can or will repair the defect.

[REDACTED]

A boil over or a spill causes shortages and becomes electrically charged moisture on the surface. 

To prevent being shocked painfully, It become necessary to cover the hole with a sturdy adhesive tape.  When this loss of cover to the electrical circuits occurs the machine is no longer safe at all for children older people who cannot move rapidly or quickly pickup a heavy object.
justification: The device poses a risk of electric shock due to design flaws, which can lead to injury, especially for vulnerable users like children and the elderly.

serial number :NF84621015 started fire when it was not being used.
In proximity of the range there were two candles, not lit, which melted from the excessive heat and large fire started. Fortunately I was in the kitchen and extinguished  fire with a minute or so. In case I would be absent the fire would ignite kitchen cabinets above and whole house would burn. In case if this would happen in the night, me and my wife could die due to the fumes inhalation.
I am an electrical engineer myself, and I own company which makes electronics for medical research.
I am aware of possible design errors which led to manufacture this defective product. I have no schematic of this product, but I suspect that Electrolux is using solid state switches to control voltage to the burners. It is my 40 years experience I know that such devices have inherited failure rate. It my be small but possible. Such solid state device when in failure mode can be either shorted circuited or open. Open will deny voltage to the burners, but shortage will provide unregulated power to the burners and can be source of fire. In addition this units do not have central common, mechanical power on/off swish which could make possible to turn rapidly  the range off when solid state switches fail. 
Recomandation by manufacturer that the circuit braker in the power panel in the basement is not convincing. Power off switch should be next to the range. In conclusion, replacing "defective" controls on the cook top is not a good and sufficient solution. This range should be replaced with reliable design.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have led to fatalities if not for immediate intervention, indicating high severity. The likelihood is deemed unlikely (2) as the user's expertise suggests a rare but possible design flaw.

incident_description:
Our 6 yr old (purchased on 11/25/06 but not delivered until 04/18/07) Kenmore Elite Double Oven caught on fire from the outside, underneath the oven inside the cabinet, on Thanksgiving Day!

On November 28, 2013, we hosted 18 family members at our home for Thanksgiving dinner.  I cooked the turkey in the bottom oven for 5 hrs at 325*, then turned the oven down to 200* so we could keep casseroles warm and I turned the top oven on 350*.  About 30 minutes after the oven was at 200*, the vents on both ovens started to blow out a little bit of smoke.  I opened up both ovens and there was no smoke, but I was razzed by my family because there were a few crumbs of a frozen pizza on the bottom of the top oven and they thought that it must be burning, because I didn't remove those crumbs prior to turning on the top oven.  About 10 minutes passed and the smoke was a little more prominent, so I turned off both ovens and my husband went downstairs and flipped the circuit breaker to the oven, off. 

We sat down to eat our Thanksgiving dinner when I looked into the kitchen from the dining room and I saw that the room as very smoky.  I jumped up and a ton of smoke was coming out of both oven vents.  I once again opened both oven doors and there wasn't any smoke inside the ovens. Our daughter felt the cabinet on the side of the oven as well as the living room wall on the back side of the oven and she told us that the wall and cabinet were both warm. I felt them both just to confirm this and I then called 911 and requested the Fire Department. My husband ran and got a screw driver and proceeded to remove the screws of the oven from the cabinet walls and in the process, he cut his hand and scratched the cabinet walls on the outside in a few places.  Once the screws and the hard plastic strip were removed, my husband and my cousin grabbed pot holders so they could slide out the oven from the cabinet. We placed two of my kitchen floor mats on the floor so they could place the oven on them, so it would not burn the hardwood floors. 

Now, the smoke was billowing out of the cabinet and we could see a burned square on the 3/4" piece of plywood that the oven was sitting on was black, smoldering and it had about a 6" hole that burned straight through it, into the drawer below the oven. To drawer contained a glass baking dish, roasting pan and a ton of plastic/felt backed tailgating tablecloths, that were now smoldering.  My husband pried up the burning 3/4" piece of plywood and ran it downstairs along with the burning table cloths and soaked them with the hose. We then removed all of our food from the kitchen and placed it on the kitchen and dining room tables. By this time, the 3 fire trucks and ambulance arrived and the firemen entered our home. The firemen and Fire Chief tilted the oven and took out (unplugged) the heating element from the bottom oven and the stainless steel plate was also burnt looking, as well as the piece of white insulation between this plate and the ceramic element. We were then told that the Fire Marshall will be in touch with us to come over and determine the probable cause of the fire.

The firemen all left and my 18 family members had to then put on their coats because we had to open all doors and windows to allow the smoke to escape, and it was very cold outside. All of our Thanksgiving dinner food was cold by then so it was not a very pleasant Thanksgiving to remember, especially since this was the first time we hosted Thanksgiving at our home for my family.

Even two days later, when we hosted an already scheduled Carolina/Clemson Party at our home for 62 people, the smoke smell was still in the house. A lot of our guests decided to stay outside and watch the game on the outdoor TVs that we also had set up. Once again, our guests had to improvise, due to the smoke smell.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage and a minor injury (husband cut his hand), but no deaths.
