The circuit breaker remains off, and will remain so until we either repair or replace it. The front left was the burner I was using tonight. My stove is a Frigidaire model number FEFB66ECE. The serial number is VF6490873. I am concerned that while you seem to know about other models with the same issue, you do not seem to be aware of this one. This is a dangerous and scary problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: This morning we came out to a horrible burning stench of  our Cuisinart DCC1200 coffemaker burning. My husband says the warming plate was glowing orange/red and smoke was coming out drenching the room with the smell of burning plastic. Thankfully he was there or it could have easily burned down our kitchen. We have owned this approx 1 1/2 yrs. Due to the many numerous complaints i have seen since this happened, this product very definately should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a burning coffeemaker with smoke and a strong burning smell, but no injury or death occurred. The mention of numerous complaints suggests this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description: My microwave goes on byitself several times during the night and sometimes during the day
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no injury, and it occurs frequently both at night and during the day.

incident_description:
The Consumer reported that his electric range/oven was placed on 375 degrees and he placed some cookies in it.  Approximately 10 mins later he noticed that they were turning brown really quickly, he looked inside and noticed that the broiler came on spontaneously by itself.  The top heating element were extremely red and the control panel displayed an error code.  He was unable to power off the oven he had to switch it off from the circuit breaker.

The incident caused the contents to charred.  (10/7/13) He contacted the retailer and he was informed that the model was not part of a recall.  He was advised that a service technician could be sent out at his expense. He feels that he experienced similar problem of Release#09-333 Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

He is concerned that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
The range is not involved in a recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused charring of food but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar issues have been reported but are not widespread.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had used the oven approximately 1 hour before the incident at a 200 degree temperature. She stated that she heard a loud noise, turned around and the glass oven door had exploded. The consumer stated that the oven door had an inner and outer glass on the door and the outer glass shattered. She stated that the glass door exploded outwards. The consumer stated that the glass reached approximately 4-5 feet away. 

No one was injured and there were no damages to her home structure. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that her model was not included on the recall. 

The consumer stated that she believes that this product should be investigated due to the laceration hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The oven door exploded but no one was injured and there was no structural damage, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the manufacturer confirmed the model was not part of a recall, suggesting such incidents are not common.

incident_description: On 11/24/2013 at approximately 5:40pm, the glass door on my Kenmore (790-70403012 series) stove/oven range suddenly shattered and popped. I was holding my 3 month old infant in my arms while standing in the kitchen doorway when I heard the shattering followed by what sounded like a gun shot. It was the inner glass layer between the two outer glass layers that shattered and glass shards fell from the bottom of the door onto the floor. I was preheating the oven at 350 degrees. The unit was purchased on 01/09/2013... not quite a year of use.
justification: The glass door shattered, but no injuries were reported despite the presence of an infant.

incident_description:
While blending ingredients for pumpkin pie the blade apparently broke and came off. I had no idea since you set it upright when not in use or it makes a huge mess. While my pie was baking I went to wash the bowl I had mixed everything in and there was half of the blade stuck on the bottom of the bowl. I just threw out the half baked pie because I cannot find the other half of the blade and I have no idea how many other pieces are in the pie. 
This item has never been in the dishwasher, and isn't even used to make smoothies (crushing ice) etc. I use it more like a mixer, always with soft ingredients.
justification: The incident involved a broken blade but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as the blender was used with soft ingredients and not subjected to harsh conditions.

incident_description: GE Profile Range caused an electrical fire.  The fire occurred behind the control console.  Prior to the fire, the console had displayed the error code "F1".  The fire occurred while the oven was operating.  The wall behind the oven was blackened from the fire.  The fire was extinguished when the breaker was manually turned off from the house's electrical panel.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
We originally purchased a Samsung Induction Range model FTQ307NWGX on 11/8/2009 from BestBuy in
Massachusetts. That particular stove and two others were replaced under warranty or extended warranty for a
variety of reasons (first unit: electrical malfunction; second unit: door could not be closed with oven racks in
place; third unit: large burner would turn itself off spontaneously during cooking). The fourth replacement
FTQ307NWGX was installed in our kitchen on 4/2/2012. It was operating normally until 10/10/2013.
On 1 0/10/2013 I was cooking an omelet. I had used the largest ring to soften onions and peppers in a nonstick
pan on a medium heat (5) for approximately 8 minutes, then turned the induction stove top off, removed the
pan and turned away from the stove to prepare the eggs, when the stovetop exploded with a deadening sound
just a foot from my ear. The stovetop over a different burner zone (ie not the one I had been using to cook) had
literally exploded, with the glass shattering and spraying glass shards flung all over.
Obviously the stove top had a catastrophic failure. As the stove was not on at the time and had last been used
a few minutes earlier, it appears to be something internal that caused the cooktop to shatter. There was no
foreign object that fell on to the stove nor did the glass surface have any scratches or wear or damage.
I have photos of the stove taken immediately after the incident that I can submit if desired. We have not used
the stove since. The area that did explode had not been used for at least 24 hours before the incident.
I have reported the incident to the manufacturer (Samsung). Samsung sent its repair subcontractor to evaluate
the damage. They agreed that this was not due to any misuse of the stove. They have offered to "repair" the
unit. Needless to say I have no desire to have a repaired or replaced Samsung induction stove in my house
after this incident, given the seriously injury that such an explosion could inflict.
Samsung is not pursuing this explosion to understand the cause of the catastophic failure and I do not think
that most consumers are aware that there is any risk of explosion when using the induction range as it was
designed to be used. We were not. Any assistance you could provide in ensuring that the company takes this
seriously and that a recall , if appropriate, is instituted, as well as consumers made aware of the risk would be
greatly appreciated.
justification: The incident involved a catastrophic failure of the stove, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased the house in March 2008. The builder put in the appliances.

The consumer stated that there was smoke coming out from the top part of the unit (maybe door, but did not open to check). The consumer stated that there was burning smell associated with the smoke.  The consumer stated that the door was hot to the touch. Smoke filled the whole house.  Strong burned wire smell.

The unit is now in the garage because of strong burned wire smell.

The consumer stated that the unit was running on normal cycle. 

The rep from GE ([REDACTED]) informed the consumer that his model is not included in recall. The consumer stated that the rep did not seem to care much about the incident. Wanted to charge $90 for service call.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
As stated in the report I submitted the house filled with smoke as result of the Dishwasher malfunction. This was a strong smell of burnt wiring. The close proximity to wood cabinets leads me to believe if the dishwasher has not been attended to the cabinets may have ignited. In addition my wife has asthma and caused her to have an attack. She also could not stay in the house that night.
justification: The incident caused a strong burning smell and smoke, leading to an asthma attack for the consumer's wife, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Appliance name and model number: Jenn-Air Double Oven Freestanding Range, model no: JDR8895AAS. The oven randomly turns on to broil settings and 170 degrees Fahrenheit. At this point, the control panel does not always respond to button presses to shut the oven off. Even if the oven responds to button presses and successfully shut the oven off, the oven turns on again after a few seconds. The only safe way to counteract the issue is to shut the power off to the oven at the main breaker panel. 

The danger with this issue is that this could happen while there is no one at home, or during the night when there is no one there to shut the oven off. As it is a heat source it could pose a fire hazard under certain circumstances.
justification: The oven turning on randomly poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned, hence severity level 2. The issue is described as happening randomly and could occur when no one is home, making it likely (4).

incident_description: Kenmore undercounter dishwasher caught on fire Friday, November 22nd, 2013.  Fire started in control panel where circuit board and relays are located.  Fire was contained within control panel: no other personal property was damaged and no persons were injured in this incident.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was contained within the control panel, causing no injuries or additional property damage.

incident_description: My stove top will not turn off. I tried un plugging it but as soon as it's plugged in, it turns immediately back on. Sears said they couldn't do anything and to call kenmore. Kenmore said they would send a repair person out in 3 days but it would be at my expense and to unplug it after every use until then.
justification: The stove top malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Kenmore range Model 79092702013, s/n VF22177166 was being used for oven, at 375 F, and back right burner on medium.  Oven door was about a third open when it was pushed closed.  When the door closed, it jarred the oven slightly.  At the time, the house lights flickered, and the power on stove went out.  The breaker had tripped.  When it was reset, it immediately tripped again.  After waiting for 5 minutes, and making sure that the burner was turned off, the breaker was tried again, and immediately tripped once again.
 Stove was pulled out, and unplugged.  The access panel in the back was removed, to find that the black power connection had come out of it's plastic holder, and 'welded' itself to the metal access panel cover on the frame. In essence, it had made the shell of the oven attached directly to the hot wire!!!
In addition, the red wire connection had melted into the plastic holder -  not sure if it was touching the metal chassis at this point or not.
justification: The incident involved a serious electrical fault that could have caused injury or fire, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description:
I am writing because I do not know who else to contact or what else to do about a problem with my gas range.  I purchased it from Sears in 2009 and had it professionally installed by our propane company.  The range itself has worked fine since then, however, after the first time I cleaned the self cleaning oven, the racks no longer fit into the oven (too narrow). When anything is placed on the racks, they fall down to the bottom of the oven floor. I really dont think that the racks "shrunk" at all, but what  I do believe is that the oven was so hot during cleaning that the walls have bowed out making the racks appear too small  for the rails they are supposed to sit on. Since then I have been "balancing" the racks with tin foil wrapped around the edges.  This is clearly not acceptable and very clearly dangerous. Many times, the rack AND pot of food has collapsed to the bottom of the oven. Both myself and my husband have been burned by hot food.
I went into the store (Enfield) where I purchased the range and they told me to call customer service. First they said they would send someone out (at my expense).  Then they said they did not have any other complaints (which is untrue,just by checking the internet) and lastly they refused to do anything and I can not reach anyone higher up at Sears to discuss this problem with them.They are saying I should have purchased the extra "insurance" for the appliance.
I am sure they will not do anything else for me and that it why I am contacting you. If nothing else it should be reported that this range/oven is hazardous to a consumer.
Very Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in burns to both the individual and their husband, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: The two (2) light bulbs in the refrigerator section stayed on with the door closed.  The bulbs generated enough heat to blacken the bulb sockets and melt the entire light and temperature console until it finally fell from the ceiling of the refrigerator.  The smell of burning plastic was evident.
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator's lighting and console but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: My wife was using her model 665.95002102 electric range this afternoon to bake a cake.  We heard a beep and she went to the oven to take a look.  An error code was on, so she opened the oven door.  The cake was on fire and smoke bellowed out of the oven.  The broiler element was on and red hot.  Turning the oven off did not turn it off, so we quickly turned off the breakers.  If we had not been close by, this accident would have resulted in a serious fire in our kitchen!  While searching online, I see that this may be a common problem that many others have experienced.  Is this a malfunction that may have been or should be considered a safety recall?  VERY DANGEROUS!
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven, which could have led to a serious kitchen fire if not promptly addressed, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description:
On November 12 the glass outer door on my daughter's Kenmore microwave/oven combination exploded.  The glass was in shards, and flew across the room and to the top of the refrigerator.

Kenmore model:  790.48842900

justification: The glass door exploded, causing shards to fly across the room, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a gas range around a year and a half ago (estimated to be maybe April 2012) and didn't notice any major problems in the beginning but she wasn't baking regularly).
In May of 2012 she was baking vegetables and other foods and at first noticed that the handle on the microwave above the range was very hot and then noticed that the handles of pans on top of the stove were also very hot.

She was advised that no one could contact the manufacturer and that they didn't have the phone number.

She is planning to contact the manufacturer.

There have been no injuries

incident_description:
On May 18, 2012 we purchased a Maytag Frost Free Refrigerator with a bottom Freezer, Model #MBF2258XEW1, Serial # K21704209. The freezers of frost free refrigerators remain frost free by defrosting regularly and the water drains from the freezer to a drain pan under the unit and subsequently evaporates. Unfortunately, my refrigerator and all the other similar units built by Whirlpool for all the brands It owns came with an improperly designed drain; It falls to do the job.
The end of the drain is too narrow for all the melted water to drain Into the drain pan during the defrost cycle. The water that remains refreezes until the next defrost cycle when it melts and refreezes. This cycle continues until the drain is frozen solid and any ice that melts refreezes and stays on the bottom of the freezer. Eventually the ice expands along the bottom of the freezer and pushes against the inside front of the freezer drawer preventing it from closing all the way. At this time the water had no place to go except out onto our ceramic tiled kitchen floor creating a slip and fall hazard for unsuspecting consumers such as us. Fortunately my 76 year old husband was able to right himself before he fell and was seriously injured.
The water started leaking when the unit was about 14+ months old. We never saw the Ice on the bottom because the food In the freezer drawer blocked the view. When my husband contacted Maytag he was told to call for a service call because the unit was more than a year old. We called the vendor we purchased the unit from; he sent a certified Whirlpool repairman who told us what was wrong and that a newly designed replacement part called a P Trap or Tube-Drain, part # W10619951, has just become available and he has four on back order. He advised us to call Maytag to see if they will send us the part and install it without charge.
We contacted Maytag and they agreed to send us the part at no charge but refused to pay for the service call and Installation of the newly designed replacement part. We received the part and it has been installed by a certified Whirlpool repairman for a charge of $149.95; an unwelcome challenge for senior citizens. He also informed us that he is being kept busy correcting this problem in brands of similar units built by Whirlpool.
Why is it when an automotive company makes a mistake the car is recalled and the manufacturer pays for the part/parts to correct the problem and the labor costs while an appliance company gives you the part if you are lucky enough to have someone tell you what to ask for and you have to pay to have it installed? Why aren't Whirlpool and Its brands more forthcoming when they screw up and willing to pay for their mistakes instead of hitting the consumer with the cost of correcting their mistakes? How do I get my $149.95 back from the manufacturer?
Thank you for your time and consideration in this matter.
justification: The incident involved a slip and fall hazard due to water leakage, but no actual injury occurred. The issue is described as common among similar units, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased whirlpool 6.2ct electric range (Model WFE540H0AS) on 3/16/2013 from Lowes, Fremont, CA.  I tried to bake my cake on 11/19/2013, and pre-heat it to 400F degree.  When the temperature achieved to 400 degree, I put my cake in not even 5 minutes and go to dining room to pick up something.  When I turn around, I saw the oven window is so bright and I open the door right away, it has fire from the left side bottom.  I turn off the power right away but still has big fire.  So I use the fire extinguisher to get the fire off.  

I went to Lowes to complain it, this product still under the manufacture warranty and I also purchased two years extended warranty from the store.  Lowes sent the 3rd party technician come over to check, they open the bottom element and insist I drop something to caught on fire. He tried 350F degree is working and tell me oven is ok. But the fact is, there's nothing drop, no oil, water or and any ingredients, only fire extinguisher powder all over the bottom.  Technician put back the cover, I asked him, how do I clean up the bottom extinguisher mess, he said you don't need to, just clean the top and won't try 400F degree for me since the top didn't clean up.  I asked him, I am so fear to use it now, you asked me to clean it up and try again.  If he insisted the bottom has something caught the fire, then now has extinguisher powder there, too. I only use my oven to bake cakes, cookies, and muffins, and that day the cake even not still raise yet.  How could it caught on fire? Is this product defective? And have a big safety issue since nothing actually drop in the bottom.

I also called Whirlpool, they said most likely is short circuit, they only provide the repair, unless it can't be repaired, then they will replace it.  Manufacture also told me that my temperature is too high.  I don't think so.  I have no problem to use any oven with 425-450F degree in the pass.  If this is high, why the stove has function to that high degree?  I am so upset with both of service.  For my concern, nothing dropped to bottom and caught on fire.  They all refused to replace the new one and asked me to continued use it.  I really don't feel confident to use this one and don't know who can help me to let the manufacture replace it. I think this is defective product and have a big safety issue.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recurring nature of appliance malfunctions.

incident_description:
Microwave turned itself on by itself.
Microwave is less than 1 month old.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore model 790 electric range that I purchased in 10/2010. I set the oven to convection preheat to 355 degrees. At about 325 degrees the front glass on the door spontaneously exploded, shattering glass across the entire kitchen floor. Fortunately, no one was near the range when the incident occurred. I called Sears and they gave me a 4-hour appointment window (3-7pm). The technician never called or showed up. It wasn't until I called Sears again that I was told he ordered the glass and I was given an appointment for the glass to be installed. I have complained about the technician's behavior as well as the fact that it seems there is a flaw in the design of the large glass viewing area which makes it susceptible to breaking. I am dissatisfied with the quality of this product as well as the way Sears is handling the fix. Unfortunately, there is no recall of this product at this time.

incident_description: The top oven burner turned on when using the oven normally but it appeared to begin having temperature control problems.   Oven was turned off using the control panel but the top oven burner continued to produce heat and appeared to work with no temperature limits.  A small fire was created in a pan in the oven due to the constantly heating top burner.  The circuit breaker had to be turned off to shut down the oven.  No error codes were observed from the oven control panel.
justification: A small fire occurred due to uncontrolled heating, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was preheating my Jenn-Air oven. When I opened it to place a cookie tray inside the glass in the middle (there are three panes) shattered into tiny fragments. The fragments fortunately remained inside the remaining two panes.
justification: The glass shattered but no injury occurred, and such incidents are unlikely to happen frequently.

incident_description:
MY family ana I recently moved into a home that was equipped with a Frigidaire smoothe top electric range,
model # FEFL79DSK, serial # VF64043654, white in color. On the evening of November 19th, I was using
the left front burner on heat setting 4 (low), when I noticed that the burner suddenly became very hot. I
removed my pan and turned the knob to "off," but the burner continued to get hotter rather than cool down,
and the range top was glowing red/orange, and beginning to discolor and smoke. I realize that smooth top
range surfaces remain hot after the burner is turned off, but on this occasion, the burner was very obviously
in an active heating mode. To be clear, I was only using the left front burner at the time; the other burners
and oven were off. Ultimately, I had to run to the basement and tum the stove's power off at the breaker. We
very nearly had a kitchen fire.
Once the stove had sufficiently cooled, I turned the power back on at the breaker, and the left front burner
immediately heated up again with the burner knob still toggled to "off." I immediately turned the power back
off at the breaker and left it off. Upon further research through the CPSC website, I found that several
Frigidaire smooth top electric ranges were recalled for this very problem, but my particular stove is not
among those recalled. Please consider calling for an expansion of this recall, as this is a very dangerous
situation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that nearly caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I used the microwave to heat a cup of coffee on 11/21/13 and was sitting about 5 feet away for several minutes before the oven suddenly switched on without anyone near it and nothing inside. I quickly moved to look at the display which indicated it was counting down from 4 min--was showing 3:58" . I hit Stop and opened the door and unplugged the unit. I called the store that I bought it from today and also contacted Frigidaire and reported the incident. I do not want another of these since it is the 2nd of this exact model that I have had since May. This one was a replacement for the original that stopped beeping last July. if there is even a remote chance that any of these could operate when the owner is not home--this Frigidaire counter-top microwave model should be recalled. It is model FFCM1134LS and serial number KG31653362 and was delivered 8/8/13.
justification: The microwave turned on unexpectedly without causing injury, but it's the second occurrence with the same model, indicating a possible defect.

incident_description: PREHEATED OVEN TO COOK DINNER.  NOTICED A SPARK IN OVEN AND HEARD A CRACKLING SOUND.  HUSBAND OPENED THE DOOR AND AND HEATING ELEMENT SHOT OUT FLAMES AND SMOKE INTO KITCHEN.  I RAN FOR FIRE EXTINQUISHER. THE ELEMENT SHATTERED AND FLAMES FIZZLED OUT.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Fire erupted as I was cooking.  I turned on only one burner, but two burners were ignited unbeknownst to me.

incident_description: The toaster oven was on "Toast" for a few minutes with bagels in it when the glass door exploded outward in tiny pieces, including the frame and handle.  The hot glass flew into every corner, hitting but not cutting my husband.  We bought the Euro-Pro T0156 toaster oven from Walmart several years ago and use it several times per week on average.  It has never been dropped and did not have any damage that we could see.  It was not dirty or over heated.  It was approximately 6AM on Sunday, November 17, 2013 and the temperature in the room was about 75 degrees.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Range, model #665.95002102. I was baking a frozen pizza at 375 degrees for 20 minutes to return to find it burned. I turned the oven off, but didnÃÂt think to check it until going back 15-20 minutes later. The heat coming from the oven was so intense it could be felt three feet away from oven. I then noticed that although the oven was off, the BROILER was on instead of the baking coil and I could not get it to turn off.  The oven did not turn off when the off button was pushed! We had to turn off breaker to get oven to turn off. It was too hot to move to unplug. MAJOR safety hazard! When my research found that this has happened to other people with Kenmore ranges, instead of having it repaired, we bought a new range that is NOT a Kenmore. VERY disappointedÃÂ.

incident_description:
My 4 month old Mr. Coffee CG-13 NP coffee maker caught fire last week.  It had been operating fine up until that point.

I was able to take a video of it as it continued to bellow black smoke out of the back, even after it was unplugged.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire and produced black smoke, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
My refrigerator caught fire on 11/4/13 at 3:00AM. My daughter awakened to get a drink of soda. She closed the
refrigerator door and then heard a pop and sizzle sound. She then noticed smoke and the flame coming from the
rear of the refrigerator. She immediately unplugged the power cord from the outlet and the flame and smoke
stopped. She then woke me and upon examination I found the start relay that mounts to the compressor was
melted along with the wire connections. This could easily have caused my house to catch since the refrigerator sits
next to a wall. I was fortunate that my daughter was present when the incident occurred.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The incident was contained quickly by unplugging the appliance.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidaire smooth top oven 10 years ago - model #FEF366BCA  serial #VF21223317

Twice in the last 2 years, I have turned the oven on and it would not shut off.  I had to turn it off at the breaker.  Not only would it not turn off, but the temperature could not be controlled.  The element became so hot that it caught on fire.  When I replaced the element, it did not have a problem cutting off.  

While it began working again properly, I am afraid of the oven.  I do not feel that it is safe.  It should not have uncontrollable temperature or cutoff features and catch on fire when the element needs replacing.  It is a hazard.
justification: The oven caught fire due to uncontrollable temperature and failure to shut off, posing a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
Caller purchased an apple corer Thursday, October 10th, 2013 then used it for the first time the following morning.

As he centered on the apple and pushed down, the corer stopped cutting the apple about half inch into it then folded over with the metal portion of the corer cutting the caller's right thumb between the first and second joint.

Caller treated the cut himself 

He contacted the manufacturer October 11th, 2013, was offered $20 which he refused then contacted CPSC Hotline.

He is reporting because he said that someone else could become much more badly injured with this tool.
justification: The caller suffered a cut injury requiring self-treatment, and the incident suggests potential for similar injuries to others.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her 9 months old grandson burnt 3 of his fingers on his left hand on the oven drawer door.  The oven was just turned off after using being used at 450 degrees, he was crawling around and used the oven drawer to hold onto to pull himself up.  He was taken to emergency room at Lutheran Pediatrics where he was treated for 2nd degree burns.

She had never noticed that the drawer gets that hot.  The oven drawer was never used while using the oven.
10/18/13 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that a technician would be sent out.  A technician came out and advised that there was nothing to correct it, it was designed that way.

She feels that this oven is a safety hazard and should be reported.
The product is not part of a recall.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
She would like a removable label to be affixed on the bottom drawer that indicates it becomes hot enough to burn when the oven is on and written in the owner's manual under "Safety."
justification: The incident resulted in a 2nd degree burn injury to a child, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the design flaw and lack of warning labels.

incident_description:
THIS IS THE 5TH TIME THAT I'M TRYING TO SEND THIS REPORT -- YOUR WEBSITE LOCKS UP AND KICKS US OUT EACH TIME WE TRY TO UPLOAD THE PHOTO ---  SO LET'S START AGAIN !!!

Good Afternoon.  My name is [REDACTED] of [REDACTED] / [REDACTED].

I purchased a brand-new gas range from the Home Depot on November 11, 2013 by ordering it ONLINE.

The gas range is an Amana 4.4 cubic foot range in white, and was on sale for $298.  I paid $340 in total for taxes, delivery, installation and haul-away of the old range.

Amana's Tel:  800-843-0304  /  Model:  AGR 3311 WDW  /  Serial"  VE34006515

The first red flag area was when the delivery guys "bolted" the gas range to my kitchen wall with metal brackets. They said ... "This model has a danger of tipping forward."  This was not disclosed on the Home Depot site but is only the minor issue.

The main issue are the GRATES.  Grates are the large "black iron" things that you set your pots and pans on with the fire buring beneath.

Grates need to be manufactured WITH ROUGH TRACTION ... in such a way that the pots and pans DO NOT SLIDE OFF the stove-top.

This model, however, does NOT provide SAFE TRACTION.  Hysterically, the grates are COATED WITH PORCELAIN ... which makes the grates SO SLIPPERY ... that an pot with boiling liquid can SLIDE OFF the stove with just the SLIGHTED nudge.

Try to picture a porcelain vase ... it's smooth, shiny and slippery. Well, that's what they've coated the grates with !!!

Last Friday  I was boiling water to make mashed potatoes. I poured the potato flakes into the pot with one hand and stirred the boiling water with the other. I've done this many times before with my old [REDACTED] range, which had ROUGH iron grates.

While stirring, the pot DID NOT STAY on the grate. THE POT SLID OFF twice and some of the hot liquid spilled on the floor and on my leg.  

What if a pot slides off and there's a toddler standing beneath. (They're always hoverung around the mother when she's cooking in the kitchen -- right?)

I called Amana and asked for replacement grates WITHOUT the porcelain coating and they said they have none.  

They also did not care that their pots slip and slide around - not even when I presented them with the "toddler scenario." 

Really?

Then I told them that --- to make the grates safer for me to use -- I would have my handyman FILE OFF the porcelain coating with a steel file -- to which the customer service rep said, "Oh no, don't do that; you'll ruin the coating!"

Apparently their coating is more important that consumer safety.

Then I wrote a review with the online Home Depot review page. The review came back this morning as "Rejected."  Home Depot is also not interested in the danger of this product.

This brings us back to the minor issue that the gas range has a propensity to tip forward. I've never heard of any range doing that.

If you would like me to send you a video of this problem, let me know.

Thanks for your time.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a hot liquid spill causing injury to the leg, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I forgot to mention just what I meant by the knobs to turn on the burners "work too easily."  If I am reaching over the range, such as cleaning the backstop, stirring on the back burner, or cleaning the cupboard door overhead, just the motion of my tummy against the burners will turn them on.  As I said...to easily turned!

Can you match this comment with my original note to you?
justification: The incident describes burners turning on too easily, which could lead to accidental activation but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: On 11/16/13 I was mixing up a batch of cookies while my Kenmore Elite electric range was preheating. I went to open the door to put in the pan of cookies and I only opened the door about 3-4 inches when all of a sudden it just shattered all over me and my kitchen. I have never used the self cleaning mode and have cared for this oven by following all rules in the manual. For no reason at all this door glass shattered everywhere!
justification: The oven door shattered unexpectedly, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
The knobs on our Kenmore gas stove do not have enough tension.  They at times turn on if you lean against the knobs.  When I reach into the cabinet above my stove, many times it turns the gas on.  
We have been eating and in a few minutes will smell gas and sure enough the knob is turned slightly and gas is escaping.  Last night, my husband was serving dessert to a guest.  He went into the kitchen, removed the dish from the refrigerator, placed it on the countertop and laid the lid on top of the stove (no burners were on).  He served the dessert in our family room and in a couple of minutes we smelled something burning.  He went into the kitchen and the lid was melting and on fire.  

These knobs need to have a tighter tension or some built-in mechanism to lock them.  It is especially dangerous if you have small children.  It is a hazard, and incidents have occurred quite a number of times.
justification: The incident describes gas leaks and a fire caused by the stove knobs, indicating a clear hazard with potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description:
I recently moved into a house with a Frigidaire Gallery LGGF305MKFH installed in the kitchen.  During my first use of the warming drawer I experienced burns on my fingers (according to my doctor somewhere between first and second degree).   

I was using the back left burner on the stove.  I turned the burner off and moved the pot off the burner.  I then turned the knob to turn on the warming drawer.  It is at this point that I burnt my fingers.  It seems that having the back left burner on had heated the metal knob to a temperature where first/second degree burns are possible.  

I consider this to be a serious and dangerous design flaw in your product.  This puts anyone in my house using my the appliance at risk and would make me liable should injury occur.
justification: The incident resulted in first to second degree burns, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the design flaw could affect users under similar conditions.

incident_description: I purchased a set of Paula Deen cookware at Walmart and the very first time i used one of them it exploded and the second one also exploded and ruined my flat top glass stove exploded the glass.... The company is trying to insist that this is my fault how is a unsafe product my fault?
justification: The cookware exploded and damaged the stove, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she baked for about 30 minutes on 350F. The consumer turned off the oven and walked away. 

The consumer came back in the kitchen 3 hours later and noticed the heat coming from the oven. When the consumer opened the door, the oven was still hot enough to burn someone. The consumer pressed the off button again even though the oven was off.

The consumer cut the circuit breaker off. 
The consumer has not used the unit after the incident.
The consumer spoke to the manf and they informed her that her unit was not included in the recall. 
The consumer spoke to a repair shop. They informed her that they would oder and replace the "clock" for $275.
justification: The oven remained hot after being turned off, posing a burn risk, but no injury occurred. The issue was identified and addressed without further incident.

incident_description:
Oven racks do not fit the oven causing them to fall with very little weight/pressure. 

I have had several incidents where the racks have dropped while holding hot casseroles, turkeys, & pot roasts. They fall to the bottom of the oven and cause hot grease/liquids to spatter. 

When researching this dangerous defect, I found this video (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePS3CysxQ7M) with MANY comments reporting the same problem.
justification: The incident involves hot grease/liquids spattering, which can cause burns, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reported incidents and a video with many comments confirming the issue.

incident_description: Our Kitchenaid dishwasher control board caught fire! I see that there is a class action lawsuit for some models but it doesn't appear that anything has been done about this ongoing issue with Kitchenaid dishwashers. Our dishwasher was purchased in 2006, model: KUDK03CTSS 1, Serial number: FU4001106. We came home one day to a VERY potent melted electronic/plastics smell and discovered that the dishwasher was no longer working. When we had a repair person out, we found that the circuit/control board had caught on fire and was charred/melted through. The wires connected to this were also melted/charred. This is very scary as it could have easily spread and burned our house down. We are scared to have this repaired now as this appears to be an ongoing issue. Kitchenaid needs to recall these affected dishwashers before someone is killed by this defect!
justification: The dishwasher control board caught fire, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: After using the oven for a few hours, the oven beeped and displayed an E2 F3 error. The broiler immediately came on and would not turn off using "cancel" or "off". Turned off the power at the breaker. After about two hours turned on the breaker. The broiler immediately came on again, so turned off the breaker again. This same thing happened about a year after we originally purchased the oven. We had to replace the control board at that time.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a potential hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
We have owned our Bosch dishwasher for approximately 7 years. 

One night we started a load of dishes. We noticed a few hours later that the dishwasher seemed stuck on "1 minute" and would not complete its cycle. The dishes did not seem to be washed, and the interior was cool -- not normal for a Bosch! We found out from a repair person that the heater relay on the control board of our dishwasher failed. He said that Bosch has the name and reputation as the best, but that they use inferior small parts that fail so that they get some more money from you for those expensive small parts. If you build a dishwasher to last, how will you make any more money off the consumer? Repair estimate: $265. Dishwasher cost: $550. 

After looking online, we saw that there was a recall of dishwashers made during the time ours was. Ours is a SHU33A02Uc/40, though apparently our model's serial number does not fall into the recall category. I believe it should. What happened to us should not have happened. We are completely disgusted that Bosch would make a product that would fail so soon. My parents had their [REDACTED] dishwasher for 25 years! C'mon!

We ask that the CPSC and Bosch evaluate expanding the recall to include models like ours. We believe that the heating circuit failed like the others in the recall. We just feel lucky that ours didn't start on fire.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction without any injury or death, but with potential safety concerns.

incident_description: I own a Michael Graves signature tea pot sold by J. C. Penny. I recently placed it approx half full on my stove. I waited for the whistle to blow and then opened the spout to pour water. I didn't realise the spout had been heated to a dangerous level. When the boiled water poured over the super heated spout, the water blew out of the spout like a geyser. No one was in the range of the flying water, but they would have been seriously burned if someone had been facing me and the pot.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with potential for serious burns, but no one was actually injured.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting his electric double wall oven - upper oven has broiler element w/bake and convection fan feature.
His wife was baking dinner, stepped away, which is when the broiler feature kicked in and burned the dinner.

He contacted repair then was informed that the control board needed to be replaced.
He is asking that these units be inspected for this particular safety hazard.
He states that this could result in fire damage to property and life if the users were not close enough to catch the issue.

This unit/model#/serial#  is recalled with release# 10-118 for the reason being that when on self cleaning mode the heat could catch surrounding cabinets on fire due to a gap in the insulation where overheating can occur.

There have been no injuries

Caller will be contacting the firm's recall hotline after this report is complete.
justification: The incident involved a burned dinner and potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated whenever she uses the electric range and attempts to power it off the unit stays on, after several attempts and the control panel does not respond, the circuit breaker is used to switch it off.  This incident started occurring 3 days ago.  The circuit breaker was switched on and the range powered on, so it remains switched off from the breaker.

Caller seems to be experiencing similar problem of release 09-333.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can:  (2) fail to turn off after being switched off;

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The model is not part of the recall.
justification: The electric range fails to turn off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the burners turn up to the highest heat level on her electric range. The consumer stated that sometimes the burners do not turn off when the knobs are turned to off position. The consumer has to unplug the unit. 

The consumer stated that this happens to at least 3 of the burners. The consumer stated that the burners turn bright red.

The consumer spoke to the manf who informed her that there was no recall on her unit. The consumer was informed that she would have to pay for the repair.

This model is not included in recall #09-333.

The consumer stated that the problems started occurring about a year after purchase.
justification: The burners malfunctioning and not turning off poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his gas range spontaneously turned on by itself and heated to high temperature.   On his return home he discovered that his kitchen was filled with smoke.  He could not power it off by the control panel, it had to switched of by disconnecting it and using the circuit breaker.  He contacted the fire department and they contained the smoke.  A fire report was filed. He has not used the range since the incident occurred.  Property damages were estimated at $12000.00

7/28/13  The manufacturer was contacted and a service rep was sent out for repairs.  However, they are willing to replace the unit but they are unwilling to reimburse him for property damages.
Consumer feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and required fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Side of Teapot handle was burning hot to the touch.  Dropped it like a hot flame, water spurted out on my arm & chest.  Passed out and my arm went down on the flame.  Sustained 3rd & 4th degree burns.  Amputation of fingers, bones etc.  used my lat muscle to make an arm.  Over 20 surgeries,  over 12 weeks in hospital ,  still have ongoing procedures.  That's the crux of it in a very shortened form
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including 3rd & 4th degree burns, multiple surgeries, and amputations, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: The toaster doesn't turn off causing bread to burn and fill house with smoke the oven also does not turn off when the door is opened
justification: The toaster and oven not turning off caused burnt bread and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Whirlpool dishwasher caught on fire
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description: I bought the apple corer/slicer this week at Walmart. I used it a couple of times without incident. Around the third time using it, I placed the corer on top of my apple and proceeded to push it down to slice it. Not even half way down the apple the metal center of the slicer bent and came apart from the plastic handles. The plastic handles slammed to the counter and the metal (still in the apple) sliced into the fleshy part of my thumbs on both hands.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to both thumbs due to the metal part of the slicer bending and slicing into the user's hands.

incident_description:
My coffee pot made a full pot of coffee and then when I went back for a second cup about an hour later, the GFI had tripped.  I unplugged the cord from the wall, unplugged the cord from the pot check out the cord.  It looked fine.  Plugged the cord back into the coffee pot, reset the GFI and plugged it into the outlet.  The coffee pot did not turn on.  So I pushed on the cord to make sure it was all the way into the pot.  There was a big flash and I was shocked.  Then the cord burned for a good 4-5 seconds before the GFI tripped again.  The flame was about 3 inches tall and it scorched the place mat that it was sitting on.  

My in-laws have the same coffee pot and it also shocked them a few weeks ago.  It did not start on fire though,
justification: The incident involved an electric shock and a small fire, indicating an injury and potential for harm, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as similar incidents have been reported with the same coffee pot model.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his electric range was moved because his was renovating his floor. The consumer stated that after the floor was put in, he tried to put the range back into its place. He stated that he plugged the range and turned the circuit breaker on. The consumer stated that when he went to turn on the circuit breaker the range instantaneously made loud noises, emitted sparks, smoke and a burning odor. 

The consumer stated that the circuit breaker tripped and he decided to leave the electricity off. He decided to open the back of the range and found that the left hand lug had melted and blew off. He stated that this particular lug was supposed to be attached to range, but after the incident it was hanging from the wires. 

He stated that there was charred marks on the center and right lug. The consumer stated that there were no damages to his home structure.  
The consumer stated that no one was injured. 
The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they will be sending a technician to service 
the range on 02/28/2013. The consumer stated that stated that he was unsure if he would have to pay for the service. 
The consumer stated that he believes this product should be investigated do to the fire hazard that it poses to the consumer.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and a burning odor, but no injuries or structural damage occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the microwave would come on by itself. The original unit purchased in 2005 was replaced by the retailer since it was under warranty at the moment. Another unit was installed in 2007 by the retailer.

The consumer stated that the new replacement is having the same problem since installation. The consumer stated that the incident has become more frequent over time. The consumer stated that the control panel does not work when the unit goes on by itself. The consumer stated that the door needs to be opened to shut the unit off.

The consumer had a technician from the manf come over for inspection in mid Oct 2013. The technician stated that the parts are no longer being made for that unit and that the unit should be replaced. The technician informed the consumer's wife they the manf will provide $400 towards a new purchase. The consumer stated that he purchased the unit for around $1800.

The consumer contacted the manf on 11/8/13 asking for a status on his product. They informed him that the unit is out of warranty and they would not be able to replace it. The consumer wanted to know if the product is dangerous and if it can cause a fire. The consumer stated that the manf did not inform him that.

The manf informed him to immediately disconnect the power if the unit is turning on by itself. 

The consumer would like a letter stating that the product is safe for his home. The consumer stated that if they are not able to do that, then they should be offering replacement.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard, but no injury or fire has been reported, and the issue is described as frequent.

incident_description:
I was chopping carrots and sweet potatoes in the food processor.  It quit working.  I took off the lid, cleared food from beneath the blade.  As I was reseating the blade, the machine came on badly injuring my hand.

My safety concern is for others like myself who believe a food processor will not operate when disassembled.  I have never operated a food processor (this one included) that would come on with the lid off.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected behavior of the food processor.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that after using the glass cookware at 350 degrees, she removed the contents into another dish at that time the cookware exploded, shattering glass pieces everwhere.  She had used this glass container many times but have never experienced anything like this before.  She believed she purchased it about a year ago.  No injury was sustained from this incident,

The manufacturer was not contacted because she did not know how to contact them.

She is concerned that this product is a safety hazard and should be reported.

The product is not involved in a recall.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of glass cookware but no injury was sustained, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as the consumer had used the product many times without prior issues.

incident_description:
We have a Ronco Standard Rotisserie Electric Roaster.  It is about 15 year old.  I had loaded my chicken in the oven as directed.  It was plugged in but not on.  There was a piece of chicken skin hanging down and touching the pan that touches the grate so I went to grab it to cut it off.  It was then that a received a strong shock that I felt go from my left hand through my chest and out my right hand that was holding a knife.
I had no injury, but we through the thing away.
justification: The incident involved a strong electric shock but resulted in no injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the age of the appliance and the described scenario.

incident_description:
The consumer says the stove top gets extremely hot to the touch. This has happened since he purchased the unit.  The consumer says that a technician for the retailer/manufacturer came to his home and said their is nothing they can do and it is of poor design.  The consumer says that his friend burned his hand from simply placing it on the cook top.    

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
Consumer had a burn causing redness and pain.  No blister.
justification: The consumer reported a burn causing redness and pain, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that when she opened the refrigerator she noticed that the light bulb had stayed on which melted the plastic housing and the plastic above the light were scorched.  It seems as if this incident occurred during the night.  The contents of the refrigerator had become warm from the refrigerator bulb overheating.

10/3/13  The retailer was contacted and she was informed that a service technician would be sent out on 10/17 for assessment.

The consumer feels that this refrigerator is unsafe and should be reported.

The product is not involved in a recall.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plastic and scorching) but no reported injuries, making severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but have occurred before.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he has been experiencing similar problems of Release # 09-333 with his electric range for the past 6 months. The front left burner comes on by itself and he is unable to power it off from the control panel. The circuit breaker has to be used to switch the power off.

Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

(10/31/13) The manufacturer was contacted and he was not able to speak with someone he was placed on hold then the call got disconnected.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range that poses a fire and burn hazard, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Shortly after starting our Kenmore dishwasher on 11/5/2013, black smoke erupted from the front door panel.  The dishwasher continued to run even after opening the door and pushing the control panel buttons to stop the unit; the unit stopped once I tripped the electrical breaker on the outside, house breaker-panel.  The local fire department removed the unit to check the cabinet area, but the only visible damage was the dishwasher panel door.

Dishwasher unit data: Kenmore ID Model # 665.16024400; Serial # FR3601006; Mfg Date stamped on rear of casing 08/30/04 at 03:06 am.  Maintenance to the liquid rinse agent dispenser is the only service call on the unit and it was performed by a Sears service technician.
justification: Black smoke and failure to stop indicate a significant incident, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The dishwasher is located in the place the consumer is renting. The consumer is not aware of when the dishwasher was purchased. 

The consumer stated that she turned on the dishwasher. The consumer heard a pop and saw a spark fly out. The consumer saw a lot of smoke coming out of the dishwasher. The consumer opened the door to make sure she didn't place anything wrong in the dishwasher. The consumer saw fire on the bottom of the dishwasher.

The consumer contained the fire by shutting the breaker and closing the door. The consumer contacted the fire department. The fire department came out, checked the dishwasher and informed the consumer to file an incident report.

The consumer stated this happened after 30 seconds of turning on the dishwasher.

The consumer stated that there is no other property damage. 

The consumer's model is not included in recall #12-244.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher but was contained without injury or property damage.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her electric range September 10, 2011 and had no problems with it other than the oven not holding a consistent heat range until the last week in September.
The last week in September the caller finished cooking then pushed button to turn the front left burner off but it would not turn off.
She tried repeatedly until finally after five or six tries, the burner finally turned off.
She did not contact the manufacturer with this incident because she believed it to be isolated.
She had no further problems with this range until sometime around October 12th - 14 when she was cooking on the back right burner.
The results being the same as the previous incident with the front left burner.
Home Depot extended protection plan.

She contacted the manufacturer and they sent the technician again on October 29th, 2013 and ordered part.

The repair tech returned to callers home November 6th, 2013 and placed new relay board. saw that lights lit up, said that heat had begun then left.

The tech had been gone approximately 20 minutes when the caller turned her burners on then began preparations for dinner but when she placed pots on the burner there was no indication that they were on.
She placed her hands above the burner then on the burner but there was no heat coming from them.
She then tried to turn the oven on but that would not heat up either.

She contacted the repair tech and was advised that he could not return to her home unless he had a ticket from his company instructing him to come back out.  (A & E Factory Services in Sharon Hill, PA).  repair returned next day Nov 7,2013. Determined new board shorted out and ordered a new board.

Caller is reporting this incident as potential safety fire hazard due to the lack of dependability of the electric range functions.
She is asking for complete repair at manufacturer expense even if covered under warranty.

There are no injuries to be reported
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range with no reported injuries, but poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: Failure of DeLonghi Toaster Oven.  Type: AS 670.  Serial # 90707. Heating element on bottom began sparking and smoking.  Turned oven off.  Discarded it.  Oven was over 15 years old.  Might very well have been a major fire resulting from this if we had not been right there when it happened.
justification: The toaster oven sparked and smoked, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred as it was turned off in time.

incident_description: I bought a marquis waterford martini pitcher w/glass stirrer.  The stirrer scratches glass off the pitcher and I'm worried that it has made the item unsafe to use and also severely mars the finish.  I've tried to contact the manufacturer but they have essentially ignored me.
justification: The incident involves product damage and potential safety concerns, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: While cooking garlic toast for about 5-10 minutes on my Sears/Kenmore Range Model #: 46762 the door handle fell off on the left hand side. It has done this before and I tightened it with no problems. This time when I tried to open the oven door on the right side the entire glass front just exploded. I called Sears, then Kenmore and they will do nothing because the warranty expired. I bought it Jan. 2011.
justification: The incident involved the oven door handle falling off and the glass front exploding, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: I have a CrockPot brand slow cooker classic oval 4-7 qt cooker, model #SCV700-B.  The slow cooker was 1/2 full of beef vegetable stew, set on low for about 8 hours, on the kitchen counter.  We heard a loud pop and I discovered the oval glass lid had shattered into a million pieces for no reason.  The slow cooker is less than one year old and has only been used a few times.  It didn't have any cracks, chips or other defects that I could visually identify. Nothing was touching it or around it.  It just shattered on it's own.  I feel this is a safety issue or poor lid design that should be corrected.  The large oval lid seemed thin and flimsy. Older models of slow cookers had thicker more robust lids.
justification: The glass lid shattered unexpectedly, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Oven control caught fire-burned circuit board and wiring harness
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven control, causing damage to the circuit board and wiring harness, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Electrical wiring problem causing the light in the refrigerator to remain on when double doors are closed. This has occurred twice causing the plastic lamp case to melt. New part has been ordered and will call an electrician to see if the problem can be located.
justification: The incident involves a wiring problem causing the light to stay on and melt the plastic case, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
On 1/12/13 my wife put some cookies to bake.  I came inside and noticed smoke coming from the oven and open the oven door to find that the cookies were about to flash into a fire.  I quickly took the cookies out with the kitchen smoke detectors now going off and noticed the oven was on the broil function and I could not change function.  So I unplugged the oven and noticed that the entire frame was very hot.  The next day I plugged back in and verified all functions were off.  A few minutes later the broil function then automatically came on and the only way to turn off was to again unplug oven.  I then went online and noticed literally hundreds of complaints a the following link:  http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/kenmore-oven-c14186.html

However, a majority of them are for Kenmore Model 790 and mine is a 665.  Then I went to this website and noticed that from 4/01/11 there were 19 similar incidents (broiler malfunction) which caused some to catch fire and caused at least 1 reported injury.  I then removed the oven from the house understanding that if Sears deems these safety incidents as serious then a recall would be issued in due time.  So I decided to store the oven in my garage in case it could be used for the purpose of investigation.  Since that Jan-2013 there have been 3 additional reports on Model 665 with mine being the 4th.  How long until Sears takes action?
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that nearly caused a fire, with no reported injury but clear potential for harm. Similar incidents have been reported, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: When any of the surface burners is burning at the low flame setting and you open the oven door, the flame goes off but the gas continues flowing. If this goes unnoticed for a period of time the resulting accumulated gas can ignite and cause a fire or explosion.
justification: The incident can lead to a fire or explosion, which has the potential to cause death, and the scenario is possible if the condition goes unnoticed.

incident_description: I preheated the oven on my free standing electric range to 400 degrees and the inner glass panel shattered. The range is only 7 months old.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass panel) but no injury was reported.

incident_description: MICROWAVE COMES ON BY ITSELF. IT HAS MELTED DOWN ITEMS IN IT. IT IS A FIRE HAZARD! I LEFT THE DOOR OPEN HOPING THIS WILL NOT LET IT POWER ON AS IT IS AT OUR CAMPING LOT AND WE ARE NOT THERE OFTEN. THE WHOLE INSIDE IS BROWN FROM IT TURNING ON AND DOING WHATEVER WHILE WE ARE NOT THERE. MAKE MAGIC CHEF MODEL MCD990ARB 900 WATT. THIS HAS HAPPENED SEVERAL TIMES BUT THE LATEST TIME IS BELOW.
