incident_description: I started my dishwasher and went outside , I came back in and my house was filled with smoke and the smell of burning electrical wiring. I discovered the smell and smoke was coming from the control panel of the dishwasher. I turned of the circuit breaker.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning smell from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I'd purchased the Teavana Glass tumbler Tamira Travel BLU 14 oz.30920 400 014 10005649. On a normal day tea was prepared with it, as it set to cool I went to take the top off and it shattered cutting my left foot and causing deep lacerations.
justification: The incident resulted in deep lacerations to the foot, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I thought I had sold my juicer about ten years ago, but it had been in storage and I was elated when I discovered it.  I had a bumper crop of apples this year and I thought I'd make some apple juice.  The basket strainer broke just like you've mentioned and the plastic cover exploded all over my Mom's kitchen and left a huge sticky apple juice mess with literally 100's of small plastic pieces.  My Mom was truly frightened and said we should be thankful that no one was hurt.  I was telling a co-worker and she insisted that I contact the company.  I said I purchased the product years ago, and she said that a reputable company would want to know about how their product was performing.  A web search brought me to this site and your site says that you are still interested in knowing about problems with this product....so I'm doing my civic duty!

This happened at my Mom's residence, which is the address below.

My contact information is:

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a broken juicer causing a mess and frightening the user, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Microwave being used in residential kitchen to heat and reheat foods according to instructions from manufacturer.  Oven began smoking and within a minute filled kitchen with smoke that smelled strongly of electrical insulation.  Circuit breaker tripped.

Unit is a Kenmore model 401.85053010 Microwave Hood Combination
justification: The microwave smoking and tripping the circuit breaker indicates an incident with potential for harm, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Kenmore Elite 790.46702603 electric range would not turn off.  I pressed the off button, and everything turned off except the oven.  The temperature became very hot and could not be turned off.  Luckily I noticed quickly before my oven caught on fire.  I turned the breaker off and the heat subsided.  I have been looking online to see if others have had this problem.  It turns out many people have had this problem and many ovens have been recalled with similar numbers to my model.  However, my model is not part of the recall despite having the same issues.  Now I am afraid to use the oven, and I have the breaker turned off.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred due to quick action.

incident_description: I have had multiple problems with this range and runaway burners.  Turning off the knobs at times does not turn off the burner and I have had to unplug the range from the wall before the unit catches fire.  I have replaced the knobs and the control board and it works for a while.  the light in the oven does not go off, there are serious electrical problems with this product
justification: The description indicates a recurring issue with runaway burners and electrical problems, posing a fire hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description: Fire incident involving a newer GE stove
justification: The description mentions a fire incident but does not indicate any injuries or deaths, so the severity is limited to property damage.

incident_description: We have an LG French door refrigerator model number LFC25760ST.  When I went into the kitchen, I could smell burning plastic.  I opened the refrigerator to find the control panel had virtually melted off of the ceiling of the fridge.  It was so hot inside the refrigerator that the butter had liquified and melted out of the butter compartment.  There were clear scorching marks at the ceiling.  I am afraid that if I did not wake up when I did, the fridge would have caught fire.  I called LG at 800-243-0000 and notified them of the fire hazard and asked them to escalate within their reporting structure. I'm very concerned for anyone who has this fridge in their house. It is a clear danger.
justification: The incident involved a melted control panel and scorching marks, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was making dinner. I had the oven preheated to 350 degrees. I set my dish in the oven when it reached 350 degrees. Within 5 minutes I heard an explosion and saw glass all over the floor. My 2 year old son and husband were  in the kitchen and I was standing right next to the oven. I was barefoot at the time and my husband had to pick me up and carry me from the room to prevent me from stepping on the hot glass. 

My concern with this situation is as follows:
1. My son was in the kitchen and his height is eye level with the top of the oven door. 
2. I was standing very close to the door when it exploded and could have had hot glass landing on my bare skin.
3. I have had the product for less than 2 years and use the oven about once a week. I feel that the damage was due to a manufacture defect, rather than by any misuse. Yet GE fails to see that this is a safety and quality issue.
justification: The incident involved an oven explosion with hot glass, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I was cooking a pork tenderloin in the crock pot,it had been on for about three hours on low and we were in the living room when we heard a noise from the kitchen,went to investigate and found that the glass lid of the crock pot had shattered, of course the meat was ruined as glass was in the crock pot.
I will be reporting this to the company also.
justification: The glass lid shattered, causing the meat to be ruined, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(10/18/2013) The consumer stated that she was cooking her soup in the sauce pan.  She smelled an awful smell. She thought that it was the handle of the sauce pan burning. The consumer stated that when her soup was finished, she poured out the soup. She put water in the pan and placed it in the sink. The consumer stated that she drained water out of the pan and saw residue in the bottom of the pot. She got a paper towel to clean it and noticed that the interior coating of the saucepan was cracking and peeling. 

The consumer thinks that some of the residue was in the soup that she had eaten.
justification: The incident involved a saucepan coating peeling into food, but there was no reported injury or illness.

incident_description:
Kitchen collection is selling a set of mesh colander which deteriorate, causing minute bits of metal enter strained foods. Please see email for products details.  Used strainers one or two times to sieve baking  ingredients when my daughter-in-law and I noticed the damaged mesh.

Order number [REDACTED]
SKU 01040563
Style 02755
Kitchen Collection set of 2 mesh colanders at 9.99 Plus shipping
I purchased these colanders for the express purpose of sifting baking ingredients. They are not suited for this
or any other food related purpose. I see that this item is still listed for sale on the website.
http://www.kitchencollection.com/Temp_Products.cfm?sku=01040563&RankThis=Y&Searched=colander&

Please note that this merchandise is defective, should be withdrawn from offering for sale, and should no longer be sold. Not only did the wires begin to disintegrate after only one or two uses, but the fine mesh
wires break into small, almost undetectable metal pieces which are easily combined with the food being
used. Advertised stainless steel 18/10 never rust is discolored and flimsy, mesh does not even fit the outer
band correctly.

Not only are these items poorly made, but in comparison with similar dollar store strainers, which I have
owned and used without incident for 15 or more years, would be overpriced if not defective.
justification: The incident involves a defective product that could potentially cause harm by introducing metal bits into food, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he noticed that handle of his build-in oven thatÃÂs bolted onto the glass door felt loose and he decided to try to tighten it. The consumer stated that he opened the door to the oven and simply touched the screws of the handle and the glass door immediately exploded. 

The consumer stated that there was glass all over his kitchen and reached as far as 10 feet away. 

The consumer stated that the outer glass of the door exploded outwards. 

The consumer stated that he was not injured since the door was facing the floor. He stated that there were no damages for his home structure. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they informed him that his oven no longer was under warranty. The representative informed him that they could only provide a rebate for the glass door since it was out of warranty. 

The consumer stated that he believes that this product should be investigated due to the laceration hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a glass door explosion causing widespread glass dispersion but no injuries or structural damage.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her dishwasher sometime in the Spring of 2007 and had no problems with it until around the week of October 14th, 2013 when she loaded it and started it.
When it became quiet she thought that all the cycles had completed and went to bed.

The caller's husband woke up around 2:00AM, went downstairs and smelled something burning, he followed the odor to the dishwasher, opened the door to the unit, felt that it was very hot inside.
He saw that the heating element had become so hot that it melted the callers [REDACTED] knives and the plastic mixing portion of her food processor and a plastic cup.

The caller is reporting due to the extreme heat indicating that if her husband had not woken up this could have resulted in a house fire with property and human damage.

There are no injuries being reported

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the dishwasher malfunction caused significant property damage and posed a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the coffee maker was filled up with smoke. The consumer stated that the plastic underneath the coffeemaker was damaged. 

The consumer stated that this incident occurred within 5 minutes of turning on the product. 

The consumer spoke with the manf regarding this incident and they were willing to replace the coffeemaker for her. The consumer was asked to cut the cord and send it to the manf. The manf sent the consumer a brand new coffee maker. 

The consumer discarded the damaged coffee maker after sending the cord to the manf.

This model is not included in recall.
justification: The incident involved smoke and damage to the coffee maker but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that was using the oven of her smooth top electric range for approximately 30 minutes before the display of her control board was showing an error message. The consumer stated that she was using the oven at a 350 degrees temperature. The consumer stated that she tried to push the ÃÂoff buttonÃÂ to turn the oven off and when she did the display of the control panel returned the ÃÂclockÃÂ display.

 She stated that since she pushed the ÃÂoff buttonÃÂ she thought the broiler of the oven had turn off, but instead it continued to increase. The consumer stated that she thought by turning off the circuit breaker all night it would reset the range. incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had used the range in the morning. The consumer walked out of the house to close the garage door. When the consumer came back in the house, there was white smoke coming out of the front right burner. The consumer stated there was plastic/wire burning smell as well. The consumer unplugged the unit.
The consumer and her husband took the range out and put it in the yard. The consumer stated that the range continued to smoke for about 6 hours after moving it out. 
The consumerÃÂs husband cut into the brackets to lift out the top range cover. The consumer stated that the white insulation underneath the cover (in the location of front right burner) was charred. The consumer did not see any burnt wires.
The consumer stated that she contacted the manf several times, but they told her that her warranty had expired. The manf informed the consumer that they could not do anything in this matter. They informed her that there was no recall on the unit. 
The consumer stated that this product could have caused a fire if this she was not home at the time of the incident.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as the consumer was present to address the issue.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she has experienced similar problems of Release # 09-333 three times within this year with her electric range.  She is not sure of the dates.
Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.

10/3/13  The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that her model was not affected by the recall.  She was advised that a service technician would be sent out 10/4 to assess and repair the problem at her expense.  

The caller is concerned that this range should be included in the recall.

The range model number is not involved in the recall.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range posing fire and burn hazards, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says the cooker does not show what the closed position is.  He has two other brand pressure cookers which clearly indicate both locked and unlocked positions.  This cooker only shows arrows to indicate closed and open but does not state clearly which is which.  

He noticed steam leaking so he closed the lid.  It immediately stopped leaking.  Ten minutes later, the cooker exploded.  The food contents splattered all over the garage where he was cooking.  The lid had fell ten feet away.  

The consumer says he feels lucky to not have been around at the time of the explosion.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who did not show an interest in looking into this matter.
justification: The cooker exploded, causing significant damage and potential for serious injury or death, though no one was present at the time.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the refrigerator freezer drawers fails to open or close.  At times the drawers are frozen and then melts water to the floor.  She feels it might be a potential fire hazard since the refrigerator has to keep running to keep the temperature.  She has had several service call since purchase (problems started 2/28/11) and no one seems to be able to resolve the issue.  She stated that she had fell while trying to open the unit because it was frozen closed.

The most recent contact for the manufacturer was 10/3/13 for a back ordered part which she was informed was discontinued.


The product is not involved in a recall.
justification: The caller fell while trying to open the frozen unit, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I put two pieces of bread in the toaster.  It was set on medium.  I went into another room and the den, kitchen and living room were filled with smoke.  Three inch flames were shooting up from the toaster. It scorched the bottom of my kitchen cabinets.  If I had not taken it outside and hosed it down, the house would've caught on fire.   I had just used the toaster 5 hours earlier and it was fine.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with potential for significant damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: GE Advantium Oven spontaneously caught fire when not in use.  We work from home, smelled smoke and traced it to our GE Advantium Oven.  The oven was too hot to touch, including parts that do not heat while in use (though it was not in use).  We unplugged the oven and it cooled down and the smoke smell went away.
justification: The oven caught fire spontaneously, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire Professional gas range blew out the glass door this morning without the oven being on.
I was sitting at my computer and heard a loud pop/explosion and saw my glass door in a million pieces on the kitchen floor.  My husband contacted Frigidaire and they said they had never had this complaint before.  Lies.  I looked on the internet and their are several complaints related to the same type of incident as the one i described.  This is dangerous. My oven is eleven years old, and thankfully, no one was hurt, but this shouldn't happen to anyone else.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of the oven door, but thankfully no one was injured.

incident_description: On November 6th, 2013 my Kenmore Elite oven's outer glass suddenly shattered.  The oven was used about 2 1/2 hours previously at 350 degrees and was slightly warm when the event took place.  The door nor oven was bumped nothing was dropped onto the door, it was not slammed.  Nobody was in the kitchen when this happened, we just suddenly heard a loud crashing sound like a cabinet full of glasses fell and broke.
justification: The oven's glass shattered without any injury, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description: The Cusinart coffee maker with hot water dispenser started melting and smoking after I made coffee this morning.  The maker was smoking and smelling.  It smelled like burned plastic.  I had to unplug to stop the smoking.  I am glad I was home or the would have been a fire.  I have had this maker for a little over a month.  There are many reports of this on consumer reports website with this coffee maker.
justification: The coffee maker melted and smoked, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Reports indicate this is a common issue with this model.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the front right burner on his electric smooth top cook top turns on by itself. The consumer stated that he was cooking on the right front burner and he noticed that his food was starting to burn. He stated that the burner had increase the temperature on its own and he decided switch his food to another burner. The consumer stated that when he tried to turn the knob to turn off the burner it would not go off. The consumer stated that he decided to turn off the circuit breaker in fear of a fire. 

The consumer stated that this was not the first incident of the range turning on by on its own. He stated that he believes this range poses a fire and burn hazard. 

No one was injured. 

The consumer stated that his range pose the same hazard listed on release #11-016. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that they could only provide a discount on the parts that need to be replaced.  The consumer stated that he hasnÃÂt made a decision on whether he will take the offer provided by the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cooktop that could pose a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she went into her kitchen around 4:00am found that refrigerator was emitting black smoke from the hinges of the doors. The consumer stated that she opened both doors and found that there were flames on the right side of the refrigerator. The consumer stated that she immediately close the door and tried to unplug it from the electrical outlet. She stated that she was unable to unplug it and decided to call the City of Atlanta Fire Department. 

The consumer stated that the fire department unplugged the refrigerator and checked the walls to make sure it was not an electrical fire within the walls. The consumer stated that the fire department found that the fire was completely contained inside the refrigerator. 

The consumer stated that there were burn marks and melted plastic inside the refrigerator.

The consumer stated that there were no damages to her home structure and no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that her model was not included on the recall. The consumer stated that the representative referred the consumer to CPSC.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator fire with flames and smoke, but no injuries or structural damage occurred.

incident_description:
Caller's refrigerator being reported was in home when he moved into it in 2012.
There were no problems with the refrigerator noticed until sometime around September 16th, 2013 when the right side of the door fell off.
These refrigerators have been reported for this same incident.   
Caller is reporting this incident to alert the public because this has happened with other refrigerators.

He would ask for a free repair of his unit and that this model and serial number be recalled for the safety of all households.
justification: The refrigerator door fell off, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(09/15/2013) The consumer stated that the family  went out at about 10am. When they returned around 1230pm, the range had turned on by itself. The consumer stated that the range was in the baking mode at 350 degrees. The consumer stated that the kitchen was very hot. The consumer stated that he turned the range off from the control panel. 

The consumer stated that night around 10:30p, he checked to make sure that the range was off. The consumer stated that around 4:am he woke up because he smelled something coming from the kitchen as if someone was cooking. He went down to the kitchen and saw that the oven was on again in the baking mode at 350 degrees. The consume stated that he turned the oven off at the control panel. He also disconnected the range from the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that there have been different error codes since he purchased the range. The consumer stated that he called the manufacturer about the codes. The consumer was advised to turn off the range at the circuit breaker for half an hour and then restart the range. The consumer was advised that the codes would go away. 

(09/16/2013) The consumer stated that he contacted that manufacturer. He spoke to [REDACTED] who created a file #969259. A technician was schedule to come out on 9/23.
The technician came out but did not do anything. The consumer stated that the technician did not turn on the range. The consumer stated that the technician noted what had happened and advised the consumer that he would send the information to the manufacturer.
justification: The range turning on by itself poses a fire hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the dishwasher was placed into wash cycle (not sure of the amount of time) but he noticed black smoke emitting from the right side of the door, the door was opened, flames and a yellow glow could be seen inside.  The unit was powered off and the flames subsided when the door opened. He used the circuit breaker to switch off the power to prevent further damages. 

The incident caused the electrical components to be charred.  The unit remains inoperable.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet. 

He is concerned that the dishwasher poses a fire hazard and should be recalled.

The product is not involved in a recall.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled by turning off the power.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting her dishwasher that was in her home when she moved into it in February 2012 caught fire on October 3rd, 2013.
Caller was in her kitchen with the dishwasher that had been running approximately 40 minutes on normal cycle, energy saver dry modes.
She said that one second all was fine then the next there was very heavy black smoke coming from the door of the dishwasher.   
The caller ran to get her husband who turned off the circuit breaker, unplugged the dishwasher and opened the door to the dishwasher.
They opened doors and windows to air the house out.

Caller contacted the manufacturer Friday, October 4th, 2013 to file report with them.
The Manufacturer referred her to their safety department and advised that they would send someone out to check and repair it.
Tech came to caller's house Monday, October 7th, 2013, inspected the dishwasher, said that circuit board had caught fire and that it had nothing to do with her but that these incidents happen.

There are no injuries being reported
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries were reported, and the incident was contained without further damage.

incident_description: I have used this Deni single hot plate about five previous times in the last month to heat a pressure cooker.  This time, as all previous times, I turned the temperature control to MAX and once the pressure cooker reached operating pressure, I turned the knob to about one-third of the way from MIN to MAX.  A few minutes later I noticed significant amounts of steam venting from the pressure cooker.  On closer inspection, I discovered that the collar holding the temperature control knob to the metal rod of the temperature controller had melted.  Because of that melting, when I turned the knob nothing happened to effect the temperature set point, and so the temperature was still set to MAX.  I was able to turn the unit off and unplug it.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure (melted collar) but no injury occurred, and the user was able to safely turn off the unit.

incident_description: I was told my recall was on back order since April when I first reported this, it is September, no refund no replacement, I have a coffee maker under my counter for no reason! I took the coffee pot from the holder under the cabinet the handle broke in my hand, coffee burned me and the handle cut me, I sent it back just like I was told, blood and all on it. I have already filled this out twice. Please let me know if it is really necessary to do it a third time!
justification: The incident resulted in burns and cuts from a broken coffee pot handle, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that in the middle of the night they woke up from beeping sound. The consumer stated that it happened for 15 minutes before they got up to check. The consumer's wife happened to walk past the kitchen and heard the microwave start.

The consumer's wife tried to turn off the unit and it did not turn off. The consumer stated that the control panel stopped working. 

The consumer stated that this happens frequently since the first incident.

The consumer stated that the microwave has sparks inside of it when it turns on. The consumer also stated that the microwave heats up as well. 

The consumer stated that the manf informed him to call a repairman. The repairman informed the consumer that he would not be able to repair the unit. The repairman stated that once the unit runs empty, it does damage to the unit that is not repairable. The repairman informed the consumer this on 9/18/13. 

The consumer also contacted the retailer. The retailer informed the consumer that they have received numerous similar complaints about this model. 

There are no recalls on this product.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning with sparks and overheating poses a risk of injury, though no injury is reported yet. The issue happens frequently and is widespread, as indicated by similar complaints.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using her smooth top electric range and burner were heating to a different temperature than selected. The consumer stated that she was using the back left burner, when she turned tried to decrease the heat the burner was actually increasing and burning the food. The consumer stated that she decided to turn off the burner and approximately 3 seconds later the burner turned on by itself. The consumer stated that she decided to turn off the circuit breaker and hasnÃÂt used the range since. The consumer stated that it was the first time that she had experienced the incident.

No one was injured. No damages to her home structure. 

The consumer stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report. She stated that she contacted the retailer and they informed her that her model was not included on the recall. 

She stated that she started to search online and found that her range pose the same hazards listed on release# 09-333. 

The consumer stated that she believes that this product should be investigated due to the fire and burn hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with potential hazards, but no injuries or damages occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wife was running the ÃÂquick cycleÃÂ and approximately 5 minutes later she saw smoke being emitted from the control panel. The consumer stated that he opened the door to the dishwasher and there was no activity in the machine. He stated that he decided to turn off the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that it took approximately 1 day for the smoke to dissipate. 

He stated that the fire stayed contained in the control panel. The consumer stated that that the control panel had melted and when the control panel was removed there were burn marks inside.  

The consumer stated that no one was injured and there were no damages to his home structure. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that his dishwasher was out of warranty. The consumer stated that the manufacturer did not provide any assistance. 

The consumer stated that he believes this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The incident involved smoke and fire in the dishwasher's control panel, but no injuries or structural damage occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there was a loud pop in the dishwasher while it was running after 10-15 mins of use. The consumer opened up the door, but the wash did not stop.

The consumer closed the door and pressed the cancel button. The control panel did not work. The consumer saw increase in smoke from the control panel. Consumer went and cut the circuit breaker off.

The consumer turned on the circuit breaker after some time and the unit turned on and started smoking immediately. The consumer stated that she has the circuit breaker off for now. 

The consumer stated there was gray smoke, and plastic fume. The consumer believes that the fumes might be giving her headaches. 

The consumer will contact the manf regarding the incident and the recall. 

The consumer stated that there are no other property damages besides the dishwasher.

The consumer's unit is included in recall #05-123.
justification: The consumer experienced headaches from the smoke and fumes, indicating a health impact, and the incident involved significant malfunction and smoke emission from the dishwasher.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using the right front burner of her smooth top electric range and the burner would not turn off. The consumer stated that she was using the burner and she turned it off by pushing the off button, but approximately 30-45 minutes later she noticed that the burner had never turned off. The consumer stated that the control panel showed that it was off, but the burner was still hot and red. 

The consumer stated that she pressed the off button several times and it would not turn the burner off. She stated that she had to turn off the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that after having the circuit breaker off for approximately an hour she turned it back on and the burner immediately came back on by itself.  

No one was injured. 

The consumer stated that the manufacturer informed her that her model was not included on the recall.

The consumer stated that her range was posing the same hazards listed on release # 09-333.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Two and a half years ago, our Kenmore oven (model 66595024101; serial RP2714284) was in use as I was baking some brownie.  Once they were done, I turned the oven off as usual and went about my business.  Later, I came back to the kitchen and the oven was on, element glowing orange.  I thought I just forgot to turn it off, so hit the cancel button again.  Nothing happened.  I ended up having to flip the circuit.  A Sears tech came out and found the problem on the circuit board of the oven.  It was fixed and had been working fine until yesterday.  I checked my baking banana bread and decided it needed a couple of more minutes.  When I opened the door a couple of minutes later, smoke came pouring out as the tops were black...this time the upper element was orange and the oven wouldn't turn off.  Again, I had to got to the circuit to cut the power, so it would turn off.  I feel this is extremely hazardous and needs to be investigated!!!
justification: The oven malfunctioned twice, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
LG Refrigerator Model LFD25860TT- Last night I awoke to a terrible burning smell. I went to the kitchen and determined the smell was coming from our LG french door refrigerator. The interior light had stayed on the had melted and fused to the interior ceiling. The interior was so hot all the butter had melted and I had the throw away, half of the contents.

I purchased this item new at R.C. Willey and registered it with LG. When I checked on-line about this issue, I determined there had been a class action settlement, but NO RECALL.  Doesn't the manufacturer have the responsibility to inform the consumer of a potential issue? If not, why?  I was unaware of this issue and had never been informed there was a issue with this model. I traveled for work, and I frequently take trips and am away from home for extended periods of time. My home could have burned down! Now I am afraid to leave home because of the refrigerator--that's NUTS! 

As it is now, the interior is ruined! Why no product recall? I contacted LG and they will be sending a technician to see the damage. So, am I left with a refrigerator that will always smell of burned plastic? I purchased this item in good faith. Something should be done to protect consumers.
justification: The incident involved property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the reported class action settlement and similar incidents.

incident_description: Pot of soup was on the Kenmore range.  It started boiling so I turned down the heat to low, then pushed the simmer button.  After that there was a HUGE bang and flash, and the entire stove went dead.  It blew the circuit breaker for the stove.  After doing some research online, I found out that this is a common problem for Kenmore ranges.  In looking at the back of the stove, the simmer select on the control board looks fried, as evidenced by the soot behind and over the front of the control board.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang and flash, causing the stove to stop working, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We own a Frigidaire Professional Series Range Model PLEF398CCD.  After using the range, I turned the front burner to low to keep the pan warm.  A short time later I heard a popping noise coming from the range.  I observed the contents in the pan boiling.  I removed the pan from the burner and discovered the heating element was bright red as if it were on high.  I turned the burner off and it continued to burn bright red.  I pulled out the range and disconnected the power.  When I attempted to plug the unit in, the burner turned on even though the all controls were in the off position.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The interior part of the door (plastic) on one side is melting to the metal area of the microwave when using the popcorn setting. When cooking is completed and you push the button to open the door , nothing happens, so you have to grab the top and bottom of the door and pull it open. There is now an area 1"x1/4" on the door that is melted away and a burn mark on the metal about the same size. This happens every time the popcorn setting is used.
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing damage to the microwave door, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he placed a 2 minute food package inside the microwave, but by mistake it was set for 6 minutes. The consumer stated that the microwave started to emit a metallic burning odor which was all over his home. The consumer stated that he removed the microwave from the home he opened the windows to ventilate the house. 

The consumer stated that he placed a ventilation machine from 09/20/2013 until 09/23/2013. The consumer stated that the odor completely dissipated. The consumer stated that there were no visible damages to his home structure. 

The consumer stated that he contacted his insurance company and they did not find any damages. 

The consumer stated that he suffered an allergic reaction (reduced body temperature, body aches and nausea), diarrhea and inability to sleep. The consumer stated that he has sought medical attention. 

The consumer stated that he has an appointment 09/24/2013, when his physician found damage to his larynx and prescribed appropriate medicine.

The consumer stated that he had to leave his home to a hotel. He stated that approximately 3 days later his symptoms lessen. 

The consumer stated that he will be contacting the manufacturer and will be filing a report.
justification: The consumer suffered an allergic reaction and damage to his larynx, requiring medical attention, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: My Pyrex 2-cup glass measuring cup I've had for 2 years EXPLODED all over me as I put it in the cupboard.  I haven't used it incorrectly.  Yesterday, I used it to pour cool water into a cool pot.  Then I left it in the drying rack on my counter to dry.  Today, as I was putting it into the cupboard, it exploded in my hand for no apparent reason.  There was no dramatic temperature change involved.  I've heard that many other people have had similar experiences, but I never believed it until it happened to me.  World Kitchen's website says that this does not happen and claims their glassware is well-made and safe.  I can't believe they can get away with saying that.  Their glassware DEFINITELY can shatter explosively and unexpectedly, even when properly used.  That's dangerous.  I'm upset about the company's dishonesty in denying it.
justification: The glass measuring cup exploded, but there was no mention of injury, only the potential danger and the company's dishonesty.

incident_description: ON OCT. 6 2013, I PUT A BEEF ROAST IN A COVERED ROASTING PAN AND COOKED IT FOR 4 HOURS AT 325 DEGREES (OVEN DOOR CLOSED ENTIRE TIME). I OPENED THE DOOR, TOOK OUT THE ROAST AND PLACED IT ON TOP OF THE STOVE, AND AS I WENT TO CLOSE THE OVEN DOOR, THE FRONT BLACK GLASS PANEL EXPLODED AND SHATTERED ALL OVER MY KITCHEN FORTUNATELY I RECEIVED JUST A SMALL CUT, AND WAS ABLE TO GET MY DOG OUT BEFORE SHE GOT HURT BY ALL THE SHATTERED GLASS.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut, indicating an injury (severity 3), but such events are unlikely (likelihood 2) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
(10/10/13) The consumer stated that his wife turned the oven on 350. He stated that his wife put pork chops in the baking dish and placed the dish in the oven. The consumer state that his wife prepared something else to put in the oven. When his wife opened the door to put the next item in, she noticed that the oven was cold. His wife took the baking dish that contained the pork chops out of the oven and placed the dish on a burner on top of the stove. 

The consumer stated that the burner was warm.  After about a couple of minutes, the baking dish that was on top of the stove exploded. The consumer stated that glass from the dish hit his wife on her left arm and caused a big gash that left skin hanging from her arm.

The consumer stated that his wife went to Essentia Health-St MaryÃÂs Hospital in Superior. She was attended to by [REDACTED], RN/CNP. The diagnosis was an arm laceration. The nurse cleaned and stitched up the gash in his wifeÃÂs arm. The consumer stated that she had to get five stitches in her arm
justification: The incident resulted in an arm laceration requiring medical attention with stitches, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such incidents are unlikely (likelihood 2) as they require specific conditions like a cold oven and warm burner leading to glass explosion.

incident_description: Was baking tilapia in Pyrex 13 x 9 glass pan at 375 degrees for 15-18 minutes.  Took the pan out of the oven with a potholder and in the air the pan exploded.  I received a 1 inch laceration on my foot along with some scrapes which required an emergency room visit for suturing.  There was no obvious extreme temperature change unless the air counts.  The product was purchased at Kohls about 6 months ago.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration and scrapes requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
My wife was removing a 6" round Pyrex bowl from the dishwasher after it had been washed. The bowl lightly knocked against another dish, and simply exploded. Glass flew all around the kitchen. Luckily she was not hurt. But these bowls are clearly a significant safety hazard.

The bowl has an embossed "Pyrex" brand mark on the bottom.
The bowl was purchased about two years ago (2011)
justification: The bowl exploded but no one was hurt, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is possible given the unexpected nature of the explosion.

incident_description:
In 2011 I was investigation new silverware and after deciding that Cambridge Silversmith Fiesta Masquerade was my
choice I researched consumer complaints about the product. I discovered on your web site and elsewhere reference to
a similar made in China product where the color chips peeled off the handles. As the defective product had been
recalled and the new product was made in the USA I decided to go ahead with the purchase.
I purchase 8 place settings in 2011, and additional 4 place settings and serving set in 2012, and a salad set in 2013.
In mid 2013 I noticed that a colored chip had fallen off of a teaspoon. Over the next few months the same thing
happened to 5 more for a total of 6 of my 12 teaspoons. I looked at the warranty return address that came with the
product and fortunately then went to the web site and found a different address which I confirmed as correct via email
communication with the company. The defective product was shipped on 10/8/2013 and received by the company on
10/10/2013. Up until today, 11/1/2013, I heard nothing from them.
Yesterday, I noticed that chips had come off 2 soup spoons and a dinner fork. Today I called the company and was asked
what product line I was calling about after which I was connected with a woman responsible for returns of Fiesta
product. She asked my name and then for about 2 minutes I heard here rustling in the background through the phone
which sounded like papers and packages being moved. When she came back on the line she told me that she had
located my package and that a replacement would be processed in 7 to 10 days. I asked why I had not heard anything
since they received my return 3 weeks ago and the only answer that I got was that she had 36 boxes to sort through. I
began to wonder if each and every one of those boxes contained Fiesta silverware with missing color chips.
The last straw occurred as I was preparing dinner tonight. I reached to pick up a lid to cover a pot of food and noticed an
orange color chip from my Fiesta silverware stuck to the rim. Had I not noticed it, that orange chip would have become
part of my pot filled with similar colored seafood and sauce. It seems obvious to me that this company is still shipping
defective and potentially hazardous product and that they are well aware of it.
justification: The incident involves defective silverware with color chips peeling off, posing a potential hazard if ingested, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite 30" wall oven model# 790.48083000 front glass exploded/shattered for no apparent reason.

During normal use, after removing a hot dish from the oven and gently closing the door the front glass of the door shattered violently with a lout "pop" sending hundreds of small sharp and hot pieces of glass all over the person holding the door and the kitchen floor. 

The potential for injury was very high. Fortunately long clothes prevented the flying glass from causing serious injury.

The oven has only been in use for 3 months at the time of the incident.

To add insult to injury -- upon contacting Kenmore/Sears they have agreed to replace the glass under warranty but surprisingly have refused to treat this as an emergency repair leaving us in a hazardous situation with sharp glass pebbles continuously falling from the wreckage of the oven to the kitchen floor where my children could step on them and injure their feet while they ship a replacement part using standard 3-day delivery from Georgia. 

With much faster shipping options available, the decision to put my family members in further risk of injury is a poor and negligent decision. There is no reasonable justification to delaying the resolution of a safety concern putting a customer in immediate risk of physical injury.

I can provide pictures of the aftermath of the incident if needed.
justification: The incident involved a violent shattering of oven glass with high potential for injury, though no serious injuries occurred due to protective clothing.

incident_description:
Into a pre-heated 425' oven I placed a 12"x9" Pyrex brand glass baking dish (one of the "portables" line, but it's no longer sold - got it about 8 years ago?).

In the pan were 2 pumpkin halves (small) and about a cup of water.

About 40 minutes later I removed the pan, using potholders, and placed it gently on the stovetop (metal burner grill), which was at room temperature (80'?).  I noticed the water had boiled away.

AND I realize that the instructions say "place it on a dry hot pad" (NOW I realize this...).

Anyway, I placed it down and almost instantly it shattered into thousands of pieces, scattering in the stove, under it, on the counter and on the floor near my dog, 5 feet away.  Luckily no one was harmed, but it was only chance.

This, while "contrary to their safety warning" is NORMAL KITCHEN USE as most consumers remove items from the oven and place on the immediately above stovetop.....a product shouldn't be sold that can't withstand such a COMMON use!  It's like having car instructions that advise against idling longer than 30 seconds.  Sure, you COULD read and follow that very specific instruction, but no one is going to remember to do that!

I strongly urge that Pyrex and other glass bakeware sold in the US be subject to higher scrutiny and be tested against NORMAL CONSUMER USE before allowing it to be sold.
justification: The incident involved a glass baking dish shattering but no one was harmed, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) as the description suggests this is a common consumer behavior.

incident_description: The floor of my wall mount GE Spacemaker 1800 becomes burning hot to the touch despite the microwave not being used for a couple of hours.  I am worried it is a fire hazard and have unplugged it.
justification: The microwave's floor becoming hot without use indicates a potential electrical issue, posing a fire hazard but no immediate injury or death.

incident_description:
On November 1, 2013, 

I was using the Kenmore Electric Range to bake some fries, like I usually do. Only this time, the oven over heated out of no where and had a F 10 code on the display screen. I cleared/cancelled it out and opened the oven.

The broiler was on? I did not press Broil, I pressed baked!! So for hours the top element stayed lit and hot. I called Sears, but no one would come until Tuesday. So I called around to other local repairs. I even called the Realtor since I am renting this unit and she has not returned my message.

So, I went to the circuit breaker to turn it off. Waited 30+ seconds, then switched it back on. (I thought would reset the range, I was wrong). The broiler [top element] began to heat again. This time, went back to the circuit breaker to turn it off completely. Now I am waiting for somebody to call me back.
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction without any injury, but required intervention to prevent potential harm.

incident_description:
My wife and I woke up in the middle of night to hear a beeping noise and a burnt smell.  I went downstairs to the kitchen and found the broiler was on, the oven fan was blowing, the unit was beeping and the display was flashing F2.  We had not used the broiler for months prior to this.  I pressed the off button and the display turned off for about 5 seconds and then turned back on.  I then tried twice more and the broiler kept turning back on.  I then went and turned off the breaker to the wall oven.  At this point the smoke from the unit had triggered the fire alarms.  

A few weeks later we turned the breaker back on and the broiler automatically cut on without us having pressed any button to turn it on.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning broiler that caused smoke and triggered fire alarms, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We have the Kenmore burner for about 5 years now.  Both the front burners continue to stay on, even when the burners are turned off at the knob.  We had to cut the electricity at the breaker.  This is an obvious fire hazard.  

I see several people have complained about the same issue.  I called Sears and they came saying I had to pay $200+ for a technician to come and take a look at it.  Isn't it obvious by now what the problem is?  Why should I have to pay to get an answer from the technician.....just tell me whether I should get a new electric range instead of running around the bush.
justification: The burner staying on poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught fire from control panel
justification: The dishwasher catching fire is an incident with potential for harm, but the description does not mention any injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Oven handle comes off; screwed it back on and it comes off intermittently.
justification: The oven handle coming off is an incident but there is no mention of injury, so severity is 2. The issue occurs intermittently, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description: Cooking potatoes at 350 degrees.  Heard a popping sound from oven.  The glass door shattered into thousands of pieces.
justification: The oven door shattered but there is no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Have a GE over the range microwave oven.  the unit is 5 years old.  In September, it started turning itself on for 6 minutes without being touched, REPEATEDLY.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential hazard.

incident_description: The plug and cord on our toaster oven become extremely hot during use.  This did not happen when we first had the toaster oven, but now happens each time we use it.  It is sometimes too hot to touch and we have to use a hot mitt to unplug the toaster oven.  My husband and I have both burned our fingers when unplugging the toaster oven after using it.  Due to concerns about risk of fire, we unplug the toaster oven any time we are not using it.  I contacted the manufacturer and was advised to stop using the product, however because it was more than 3 years old they would not offer to repair or replace it.
justification: The incident involves burns from touching the hot plug and cord, which occurs each time the toaster oven is used, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I cooked dinner on 11/3/13 at about 3pm.  At 7 pm I turned the oven back on to 400 to cook the bread.  I put the bread directly on the racks as instructed. I took the bread out and some stuck on the rack.  I turned the oven off and left the door open to cool the oven and to remind me to clean the rack.  After dinner I scraped the rack with a fork and then wiped it off.  

This morning I went to work.  The oven and stove remained unused.  

I arrived home from work at 2pm and I saw that the glass was all over the floor in the kitchen and some in the living room.
justification: The incident involved broken glass but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. Such occurrences are uncommon but possible with oven use.

incident_description: I was slicing apples with the Gourmet Club Apple Wedger from Walmart in Corona and barely started slicing the first apple and the product broke in my hand and sliced my finger bad. It took over a half an hour to control the bleeding. After researching more information about this product, come to find out many other people have experienced the same incident with this product. This product is going to chop someone's finger off by using it what it's designed for. It needs to be pulled off the shelves immediately and the public needs to be warned not to use it before someone has a life-altering accident (amputation of a finger).
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (sliced finger with prolonged bleeding) and there are reports of similar incidents, indicating a pattern.

incident_description:
Our JDR8895aas Jenn Air gas range began popping under the 3rd control knob and looking like it might catch fire.  It has a spark ignition system, and it usually sparks at the burner, but it was sparking under the 3rd control knob.  It did this while NO ONE was touching or near the oven.  This could cause electrical shock or fire as the knobs are plastic and the housing for the switches are plastic.
We now keep a fire extinguisher near until this gets fixed.
I have read on line that this is not an isolated incident.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard and electrical shock risk, but no actual injury or fire occurred. The likelihood is high as similar incidents have been reported online.

incident_description: My Cuisinart Grind and Brew coffee maker, model # DGB-700BC Serial number 00621C, burned up and nearly caused a fire.  The unit was OFF.  I was sitting in the kitchen and heard a boiling sound.  i looked up and saw and smelled toxic smoke coming from the bottom of the unit.  it was getting worse.  i unplugged the unit and it finally stopped smoking after a few minutes.  had i not been there, it would have caught my kitchen on fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that produced toxic smoke but was unplugged before causing a fire, resulting in no injury or death.

incident_description:
On August 4th, 2013, I took a weekÃÂs vacation to visit my Mother.  That morning I heated up some water using her two-quart Courtly Check Enamel Tea Kettle, product # 08 89257.  

While using the teapot, I thought it strange that it was taking so long to heat up, as I didnÃÂt hear any whistling or boiling noises. After a few more minutes I figured the water had to be ready and I took the teapot off the stove to pour into my coffee cup.  At first, no water came out. I assumed this was due to the steep angle of the pourer, so I attempted to pour at a slighter greater angle. Suddenly, the super-heated teapot saucer lid popped off and landed on my finger, causing immediate blistering with 2nd degree burns.  In addition, scalding water poured out of the teapot and caused first degree burns on a good portion of my hand (see attached picture of my hand 10-days after the injury).

This experience, along with being extremely painful, ruined my vacation as I wasnÃÂt able to go swimming, with my family.  I had to watch from shore as my niece and nephew splashed away in the water.  

Having safely used teapots for over 35 years, it is very clear that the MacKenzie Childs Courtly Check teapot is a dangerous and unsafe product for the following reasons:

ÃÂ	No whistle feature: One doesnÃÂt know when the water has boiled and is ready to use.
ÃÂ	Unsafe Loose saucer lid:  The lid on the teapot comes off easily, unexpectedly and at the worst possible times. This was confirmed by my sister who had a similar experience, thankfully she wasnÃÂt burned as the top landed on the counter.  

Upon doing some research, I discovered that MacKenzie Childs has known or should have known about this product defect as early as June of 2009 (See links to Amazon review below) yet has done nothing to my knowledge to correct these defects. 
http://www.amazon.com/gp/cdp/member-reviews/A20WX5NVTUHWC7/ref=cm_cr_pr_auth_rev?ie=UTF8&sort_by=MostRecentReview

A simple product modification of installing a small latch on the inside of the ornamental top saucer to keep the lid on couldÃÂve avoided this painful injury.  
In the interests of consumer safety, I hope Mackenzie Childs will discontinue selling the Courtly Check and other teapots with these design flaws until a latch or other safety features are installed along with a whistle mechanism.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns and scalding, which are injuries, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is possible (3) as similar incidents have been reported but are not widespread.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was using the oven of her electric range on pre-heat at 350 degrees. The consumer stated that approximately 15 minutes later she increased the temperature to 365 degrees and the oven caught on fire. The consumer stated that she saw a flame being emitted on the left side of the heating element at the bottom of the oven. The consumer stated that she turned off the oven and the oven continued to emit white smoke. She stated that she opened the oven door and noticed that the heating element had broken in half. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that the oven was no longer usable. 

The consumer stated that she contacted that manufacturer and they referred her to CPSC. 

The consumer stated that she believes this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The oven caught fire but no one was injured, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description:
Right Side: The consumer stated that the inner right burner quit working. The consumer stated that the light would go on but it would not heat up. The consumer stated that the inner ring does not heat up but the 2 outer rings heat up (on the right side).

Left Side: The consumer stated that if she turns on the left back burner with the bridge, the front burner lights up and gets hot. Otherwise, the front left burner turned on alone will either 1) turn on 2) fail to turn on at all or 3) heat up a lot even on low setting

The consumer stated that she spoke to the manf regarding the problem. The manf rep confirmed that her model was included in a recall but the technician would make the final call on the problem and if it's included in the recall.  Manf sent out a technician. The tech came in today (9/10/13) and informed the consumer that her model is not included in the recall.

The consumer stated that she started noticing problems with her range when her five year warranty expired. 

Model not included in recall #09-333 but the consumer is having similar hazards.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning burners with potential hazards, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that his oven glass door exploded while it was off.  He discovered this when returned home.  The outer glass door had shattered and there were glass pieces on the floor and some fell into the  oven drawer.

(9/13/13) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that there was no recall and the unit was out of warranty.
The caller feels that this unit should be recalled because of the safety hazard it poses.
The product model number is not involved in a recall.
justification: The oven glass door exploded, causing damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
09/25/2013) The consumer stated that the dishwasher was on the heavy cycle. Within minutes heavy black smoke came from the top of the dishwasher. The consumer stated that he unplugged the dishwasher. He stated that he waited a minute or two. The consumer stated that opened the dishwasher and discovered that the inside of the circuit board was burnt and black. 

The consumer stated that the only damage was the circuit board.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burnt circuit board but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. Such electrical faults are possible but not extremely common.

incident_description:
Kenmore electric range model# 79097423901 serial #VF00475456
Front door glass shattered into thousands of pieces. 
Wife was cooking a pizza, at about 350 degrees, using convection heating.
Created hazardous condition to clean up kitchen floor about a 10x6 foot area
There were no previous signs the anything was wrong.
No injuries no one was in kitchen at the time
I talked to Local Sears salesman who claimed to never had heard of such a problem.
Internet is full of the same kind of stories. there should be a recall!
Ordered new glass from Sears cost: $55.74 + $4.03 tax +$29.95 shipping Total $89.72
justification: The incident involved the shattering of the oven door glass, creating a hazardous condition but no injuries, and similar incidents are reported online.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased an electric range with a ceramic top on 08/13/2013. She stated that approximately 2 days after she purchased it she decided to turn on the oven to try it out and the entire outer area (not only the burners) of the ceramic top became extremely hot. The consumer stated that she turned off the oven and let the range cool down. The consumer stated that she turned on the burners to try it out and again the entire outer area of the ceramic top became extremely hot to the touch. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they directed her to the ownerÃÂs manual where it notifies consumers that this was normal for a ceramic top range. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the retailer and they informed her that all of the ranges that they sale become hot. 

The consumer believes that this product poses a burn hazard to consumers and children. The consumer believes that this product should be investigated because the outer [area] shouldnÃÂt become extremely hot to the point where bystanders who are unaware could easily touch it.

 The retailer (A&A) appliances ordered an identical range which he plugged in before delivery to the consumer.  It had same problem - extremely hot where it shouldn't be.  He (A&A owner) claimed every range in his store is that way.  Told consumer this is new normal.
justification: The incident describes a product issue that could lead to burns, but no actual injury was reported. The likelihood is high as the issue was replicated and confirmed by the retailer.

incident_description:
ISSUE:  A slight tap or bump to the stove knobs can turn them enough to allow gas to flow without being aware it has happened. The knob turns slightly but not enough for the igniter switch to come on and light the gas.  No clicking sound is heard.  
Whirlpool  30 in. Freestanding Gas Range w/ AccuBakeÃÂ®  Model # WFG510S0AW1  
Purchased 10/1/2013 at Home Depot 
Noticed several incidences of the knobs turning a bit and gas leaking - usually while cooking.
10/18/13 came home to house full of leaked gas - called Whirlpool (WP)- closed for weekend.
10/21/13 Called WP to report concerns about knobs and leaking gas
10/24/13  WP sent out Appliance Express who did an inspection in response to concerns of gas leakage caused by the knobs moving just enough to turn on the gas but not enough to engage the ignition spark when brushed up against unknowingly. The technician sent WP a report saying this is just the design and the stove is not leaking gas. Told I would hear back from WP in a few days.
I have not heard back yet. I notice today (10/29/13) the technician's report sent to WP gives an incorrect serial number - off by one number.  I will contact and correct.
It is difficult to visually see or notice when the knob has turned unless you are standing over it and  looking directly at it.  This has happened numerous times even with an awareness this occurs and being extremely careful and mindful around the stove.
I have "caught" the knobs turned and the gas leaking  several times and came home 10/18/13 after being out for several hours to find the house full of enough of gas to smell it outside.  I promptly called WP about it this issue but it was Friday after hours and I had to wait until Monday to contact them.  I also called Home Depot but the manager was off.  I have played phone tag with Home Depot since then and only spoke with [REDACTED] today 10/29/13 who said he will make a call and get back with me.
My daughter was cooking last night and accidentally  turned the knobs on four times with her (not big) belly just standing there. So easy.   When she came in to clean up after dinner 30 minutes later, she discovered one of the knobs was on even after she had checked to make sure they were all off before leaving the kitchen. Somebody probably unknowingly bumped it - again... it is so easy to do.  
Last night before I went to bed, I went into the kitchen to get a drink of water and the gas was on.  Once again, the knob was turned ever so slightly and I wouldn't have noticed but I smelled gas. I don't know how the knob was turned on but I know it doesn't take much - just a little bump when you didn't know you did.  Everyone else was asleep. We are all very conscientious and careful and yet this still happens.  
My old stove required you use effort to push in the knob before you could turn  it.  The design on this stove takes just a flick of effort to  do the same thing.  This is very scary to me.  My best friend and her two brothers died due to a gas leak and were gone overnight. Huge loss.
I have made calls to both Whirlpool and Home Depot about this issue and am waiting for  a  response.  I know this is a highly rated stove (It is just what I was looking for) and I feel devastated to have experienced this issue.
Due to the dangers of leaking gas, I feel it is important to report what I feel is a design defect that could cost lives if not addressed promptly.  Sorry Whirlpool this is otherwise a wonderful stove.
justification: The incident involves repeated gas leaks due to easily turned knobs, posing a significant risk of fire or explosion, though no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: The light in our refrigerator (Frigidaire) went out.  Went I went to investigate and remove the bulb, there is a burned hole where the light bulb rests! After reading MANY online complaints for the same problem AND no resolution by Frigidaire, we decided to contact you.  We either want this fixed (so we can have light) or a new refrigerator.

incident_description:
This is in regard to a General Electric Spacemaker Microwave Oven Model JVM1540-DN1WW purchased and installed three years and nine months ago from Lowe's Home Improvement Center In Turlock, California.

On Oct. 20 afternoon my wife and I were seated at our kitchen table when the above-named appliance spontaneously started running. Neither of us had used the microwave that day and were surprised by the activation. I got up to inspect the unit to see what was going on and it was running and the display listed a cycle we never use. I selected the "clear/off" button and the machine ceased operation.

Still surprised and bewildered by this, I was looking at but not touching the control panel when it spontaneously activated again. I felt the unit and the microwave generator was definitely operating because the glass was getting hot. Again I hit "clear/off" and the machine again ceased operation. Each time within a minute or two it would spontaneously start up again.

Thinking this might be a "computer" type glitch in the unit's memory board, I unplugged the unit and let it sit for several minutes, perhaps 20 to 30 minutes, to see if it would reset itself. Then I re-plugged the unit and within a short time it again spontaneously started up. Fearing a fire hazard, I then unplugged it.

The next day, I called GE's product support hotline, but they offered little information except they tried to schedule a repair visit. They also tried to indicate the problem was either, not a problem at all ("maybe you had something hot on the cook top so the unit's fan was automatically engaged, which is normal") or that we had done something purposeful to cause the problem.

Apparently what GE did not count on is the fact that I'm a retired journalist and my wife is a retired reference librarian. We had already done our due-dilligent research and had learned that several brands of microwave of experienced similar spontaneous activations, GE units being one of the main brands at issue.

I could not find our particular model among those known to malfunction but it certainly has done so repeatedly. I feel very fortunately that this spontaneous activation didn't happen when we were away, or in the middle of the night. Outcomes under those circumstances might have been dire.

My wife and I have already ordered a new (not GE) unit and it will be installed and the defective one hauled away this week. However, I feel strongly that is brand and model should be added to your list of those that have activated spontaneously.
justification: The microwave spontaneously activated multiple times without user input, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury occurred.

Had I not noticed this, it could have fallen off my stove and burned me.  My main concern is the possibility of this happening when a child is in the kitchen.  I do not believe they are safe to use because of this.

One other thing about these pots and pans is that the handles are held on with a peg and button-type top.  Food collects in there and is difficult to wash out.  If someone were not careful washing them, I wondered if tainted food left in there could contaminate new food being prepared.  

I tried to return the product, but the store would not take them back.  So, now I am stuck with this purchase.  

I will also be writing to T-Fal about this problem, but doubt that anything can be done, because it wasn't until after I purchased the product that I discovered it was made in China.  From my research, I thought it was made in France.  

Thank you for your consideration of this unsafe product, especially where children are concerned.

I had my kitchen remodeled in September 2011. The appliances were supplied by the contactor. The freezer of the new Electrolux refrigerator didnÃÂt work right from day on and after several attempts to repair it was replaced by the above brand new model in December 2011.
This unit worked well until 10/5/2013 when while filling a glass with ice the entire system shut down. No ice-no lights-no sounds-nothing! A rectangular piece of [REDACTED] had dropped into my glass so I reached up into the ice chute to see if anything was stuck. All I got was a major shock and jolt. I unplugged the refrigerator at that time and removed the ice tray. I found two wires hanging down from the top that had arced to the metal ice auger and shorted the entire system out. This was what was responsible for the shock I got. In the tray were the temperature sensor/thermometer and a rubber hose.

The restraining piece of [REDACTED] was dislodged allowing the sensor and attached wire to hang down into the ice tray.

incident_description:
The caller stated that whenever the gas stove is pushed into place, it causes the screws that are located at the rear of the unit to puncture the gas line.  This causes gas to leak in the house.  The odor of gas permeated her home.  This incident started occurring about 1 month ago.  The stove was disconnected and the technician was contacted to come out to find the leak.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The caller feels that this gas range is a safety hazard and should be reported.

The product is not involved in a recall.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
The design of the stove is such that a small gas supply line, called the T-valve tube, is directly in line
with a sheet metal mounting screw on the stove. The sheet metal screw that protrudes out the back of
the stove is very pointy and separated by less a ~ in from the T-valve tube. When the stoves slides back
in place the pressures on the soft aluminum line and the screw will puncture the supply line. It was
difficult to trouble shoot as when there is pressure on the line the screw that created the hole is
embedded into the line and the leak is slow and difficult to diagnose. When the stove is pulled out it
releases the pressure of the supply line against the screw and the leak becomes greater. I cut the end of
the protruding sheet metal screw off so that it is flat now and and thus should never happen again. A
small design change suggestion would be to use flat headed machine screws vs. sheet metal screws to
avoid this issue.
justification: Gas leak poses a significant safety hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

I am 8 months pregnant. I had made a brown buttered acorn squash using a Pyrex casserole dish. I had the oven set on 400. After 15-20 minutes I took out the casserole dish and set it on the counter where it immediately exploded throwing shards of glass all over my kitchen. Fortunately, being 5 inches away when I had set it down I was uninjured. 

I had looked it up and reportedly, over a thousand people had reported the same thing on consumeraffairs.com. One person even mentioning losing the tip of their thumb. What if a child had been in the room?

Link: http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/pyrex.html

 
This isn't uncommon since 1998 when Pyrex turned to soda-lime-silica glass. I am shocked that this has not been taken off the market since it has happened to myself three times (I cook quite often), my mother once, my boyfriend once, and my cousin once. 

This is even on the news. http://www.consumerreports.org/cro/magazine-archive/2011/january/home-garden/glass-cookware/shattering-bakeware-affects-coworkers/index.htm

I have been contacted by Pyrex but I do not want a replacement of a defective product that may injure a member of my family. I want the product off the market and for people to be aware of the danger.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported. However, the frequency of similar incidents and potential for injury is high.

smelled electrical fire... found dishwasher had stopped running... 20 amp house breaker tripped.
opened front panel on dishwasher door and noted processor board near upper right corner burned up.  board had a ribbon cable on it.. I did not note the board serial number (dishwasher has since been disposed of) but from manual believe it was the electronic control that burned. also noted small melt spot on the face of the front door. 
Sears Kenmore Elite Dishwasher
Installed late 2004 
model 665.17469300
serial # FR2811898

incident_description: Baking food in the oven and flames came out between the rangetop and the control panel. Turned off oven and turned the breaker off.
justification: Flames emerged from the oven, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred as the situation was controlled.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric range 790.96429407

The first time it happened I went to open the stove door, the handle fell off, and the glass shattered, when I called Kenmore they responded that there has been no recall on my range, and this was the first that they've heard of the problem, but their are plenty of similar incedents all over the internet. It appears that the just used screws that are to short to full engage the door. This happened again today as it has many times since the first time. The oven was set at 425 degrees. I burned my hand during the accident. One day somebody is going to get seriously hurt, and then maybe somebody will care enough to fix the issue.


Sincerely
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
Kenmore elite side by side refrigerator model # 106.54786803
purchased 3 years ago, just realized light bulb has melted housing and parts, scorched bulb housings, bulbs are cracked, interior of refrigerator has cracked above light housing, causing screws to fall out.
justification: The incident involves property damage (melted and scorched bulb housings, cracked interior) but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:

I purchased two sets of Royal Prestige cookware 1/21/2007.  I bought the DELUXE COMBINATION which included the SIGNATURE & HOME MAKER sets.  I updated my contact information with the request of a new gasket for one of the lids a couple of years ago.

I called the company and stated my concern using  the cookware based upon the notification but it is my only set of cookware, at that time.  I asked for a refund.  The recall center suggested I return part of the two sets, keep a few pans behind to cook with while they ÃÂfixÃÂ the returned pans with a gasket on the side wall of the pots.  The return was seamless through the local UPS store with the first set being sent 3/19/13.  Once the first set came back, I re-used the boxes and placed the remaining pots in them, again to the same UPS store. As it turned out, I had been without my total cookware sets for at least 6 months.
