They do not have an equivalent product, therefore, I requested a refund due to it being defective and not usable without potential danger to me, the consumer.  I went and purchased a usable set of pots and pans after this 9/19/13 conversation as I no longer wanted to use the ÃÂfixedÃÂ set which they stated needed to be returned.  I am unhappy they warehoused my 2nd set of returned product with my intention of it being fixed and they did not bother to contact me their change in policy.  I had to call to find out about the missing set

incident_description: I noticed some strange noises coming from the microwave while using the crisping pan and quickly shut off my microwave.  Upon removing the crisping pan I noticed the pan had bubbling from the coating on the underside of the pan.  My microwave had never worked since.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage (bubbling coating) but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as microwave malfunctions can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
I had a small Hamilton Beach food processor model 72610, type FC05, series A1940BB. On August 28, 2013 I went to use it. The bowl and blade were already on it but the lid was not. When I plugged it in it immediately came on even though I did not turn it on and had not yet put the lid on.  If my fingers were further in the bowl I would have lost my fingers. The only way to shut it off was to unplug it. I called Hamilton Beach to tell them what happened. They said to mail it to them which I did. After over a month of not hearing back from them I called them back. They said they would replace it if I paid for shipping. I told them I didn't want a new one I was more concerned about all the ones that were out there still and worried that someone would get seriously hurt. They said they no longer make them but they would send me a replacement if I paid postage. I told them again I was not interested in a replacement what I thought was necessary was a recall. They said once again they no longer make them and I told them once again what about all the others still out there. After many back and forths like that I finally said I was contacting you. Both safety features, only on with lid on and button held down, both failed. I could have or someone could loose their fingers and they don't care. I really think it needs to be recalled. I no longer have it because I had to send it back to them but I did take a video before I mailed it in case you are interested in seeing it. 
Thank you for your time.
justification: The incident involved a food processor turning on unexpectedly, posing a risk of serious injury, though no actual injury occurred in this case.

incident_description:
All heating elements go on Hi setting except for Warming Zone which only goes on Low. Cannot adjust any of the heating elements.
Never received any recall notification from LG.
justification: The incident describes a malfunction in heating elements without any mention of injury or harm, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: I have a Hamilton Beach Slow Cooker, model #33162H.  It is about 2 years old.  I used it on the 'warm' setting for about 8 hours one day.  The next day, I cleaned it, in warm soapy water, and rinsed it with warm water.  I then had the glass lid in my hand, and was drying it with a cloth towel.  It spontaneously shattered into thousands of small pieces, in my hands, and onto the kitchen floor.  Luckily, I had on pants, socks and slippers.  I had small cuts on my hands and one on my ankle.  It could have been a lot worse, had I been barefoot and in shorts.  Also luckily, there was no one else in the kitchen at the time.
justification: The incident caused small cuts on the hands and one on the ankle, which is a level 3 severity.

incident_description: One of the burners on my LG stove gets extremely hot and will not shut off even when unplugged.  The burner gets very hot despite the setting we put on the stove (Hi or low). The room gets really hot from the burner's high heat prompting the automatic fan from other appliances to turn on.
justification: The burner's inability to shut off poses a fire hazard and could lead to injury, though no injury is reported yet.

incident_description:
We have had this dishwasher for about 8-9 years. Using it regularly, earlier in the day I noticed a burning smell but didn't see any smoke, and I didn't think more anything of it. In the evening, we started another load of dishes. Within a few minutes, I noticed the same burning smell and saw smoke coming from the handle area of the dishwasher. I immediately called 911 for the fire department and took my family outside the house. The fire department identified the problem as a burned out control panel. They were able to turn off the power to the dishwasher, although the control panel connected to the power apparently shorted out while they did this.  They then safely disconnected the dishwasher. 
After we were safe again, I researched this on the Bosch website and saw that this dishwasher was in a recall in 2009 for risk of fire. This is very upsetting because I had never received notification of this recall and had no idea we were at risk. I called Bosch customer service and was told they will contact me during business hours for further discussion.  (Oddly enough, our model and serial number showed up online as being affected and said do not use, and call Bosch. When I called, she put in our information and said it was not showing up as affected. She still put it through to have them contact us.)
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire department managed the situation safely.

incident_description: I HAVE GE GAS RANGE MODEL PGB918SEM4SS. THE BURNER KNOBS TURN ON VERY EASILY AND SEVERAL TIMES I HAVE NOTICED GAS IN THE ROOM AS A RESULT OF INADVERTANT BRUSHING UP AGAINST THE KNOB. AFTER AN INTERNET SEARCH I FIND THAT THIS PROBLEM HAS BEEN WIDELY REPORTED. I LOOKED IN AN APPLIANCE STORE THIS WEEK, AND THE CURRENT GE GAS RANGES HAVE SAFETY KNOBS WHICH MUST BE PUSHED IN BEFORE TURNING.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage due to easily turned knobs, posing a hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I brewed coffee this morning in my Cuisinart Coffee Maker and went upstairs to shower.  I came down to plug my cell in and my kitchen was filled with smoke that was coming out from under the unit.  The unit sounded as if it were trying to brew again, popping noises and steam sounds, even though it already had brewed an hour earlier and the carafe still had several inches of coffee in it.  I unplugged the unit, removed the carafe and ran with it to my garage.  The underside has a metal plate and it was incredibly hot to the touch (I burned my hand when my thumb accidently hit the underside running with it to the garage.  Despite being unplugged, the unit continued to smoke for about 5 minutes.  I honestly believe that it could have started a fire had it not been on a granite counter and had I not come down to find the smoking unit.  The unit did sustain high use - every day for about 3 years, but I've never had a small kitchen appliance behave that way.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and had potential to cause a fire, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the appliance's age and high usage.

incident_description:
I am reporting the second failure of the handle on a Krups XP1505 Expresso carafe.  The glass unit consists of a glass carafe, a metal band, a screw and a plastic handle/lid assembly.  The handle/lid attaches to the metal band by means of the screw.  The band goes around the glass and the screw tightens it until it is secure.  The glass, the band and the screw seem reasonably robust.
The screw passes through a thin and weak part of the handle/lid assembly to attach to the metal band.  After less than two months of use the plastic around the screw has separated from the rest of the plastic of the handle/lid assembly.  The weight and heat of hot (steam produced espresso) in the carafe make the most dangerous time for this item the most likely time for it to fail.
The user could be easily scalded.  Worse, as most coffee is made at "adult height" little people below that adult in the kitchen are exposed from head to toe.  The falling carafe and the broken glass after it lands also present a danger.
I have had this failure occur two separate times.  The first time I did not know the age of the unit.  The second time I know the replacement unit was in service less than two months.  Two month or two years, the failure is unacceptable.
Krups is aware of this problem and will not remedy it.  There was a previous complaint (not by me see, 20121029-0D5C0-2147462420; 20120308-8079A-2147469460; ) of this precise problem.  However when I reported this to Krups they (representative [REDACTED]) denied it had ever been reported to them before and that, although in no way defective, the carafe was not warranted to be either fit for the intended purpose or merchantable.  (To be fair, Krups maintains that using the carafe with Krups machine X instead of Krups machine Y makes my complaint void.  They dod not explain how espresso made from machine X differed in its impact on XP1505's durability from espresso made by machine Y.)
The Krups response to the first complaint is virtually the same as their response to the second complaint and both are belied by their response to my complaint.
justification: The description indicates potential for scalding and injury from hot espresso and broken glass, with repeated failures reported, making injury likely.

incident_description: Purchased a set of All-Clad Copper Core cookware (pots and frying pans).  Several of the pots edges were not ground to a smooth finish and I and my son have cut our selves numerous times while cleaning them.  I am not sure if we just got a bad batch but have put up with them for a few years now.  Never thought about reporting them until the recent recall of surge protectors that are over 10 years old.  Don't know if the manufacture fixed the issue or not, but the same cookware set is still sold today.  http://www.williams-sonoma.com/products/all-clad-copper-core-10-piece-cookware-set and it's not a cheap item.  Mine was bought through the Army and AirForce Exchange Service.
justification: The description reports multiple injuries (cuts) from sharp edges on cookware, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue persists over years, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely) for recurrence.

incident_description:
On the way to the game tonight, my wife and I toasted some pizza.  This time was different though, we shut it off after toasting and it gives a beep signal to know it's off.  But then as the cab arrived, I smell a little smoke.  It was coming from our Krups toaster oven!  I looked on the front and there were no lights and it appeared to be off.  But looking inside the oven, it was blazing hot with the filaments that bright fiery orange.  We had to unplug the Krups toaster to turn it off, pushing the buttons had no effect.

As we jumped into the cab, all I could think about was what would have happened to our helpless cat and dog had our house caught on fire.  Not to mention the other tenants in the house.  Very disconcerting to say the least.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning toaster oven that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I had purchased the Teavana glass double walled tumbler between Dec. 26-29, 2012 at Mall of America in Bloomington, MN. The tumbler had a silver screw cap, basket stopper and the Teavana logo and vertical circles (with chinese characters in them) on the side. 

On the 4th or 5th time using the tumbler I had filled it with a tea bag and water (near boiling from a hot water faucet - 190-210 degrees). As I returned to my desk I had sat down and carefully put the tumbler floating keyboard tray. Upon setting the filled tumbler down it immediately shattered and spilled the near boiling water onto myself and desk.

I threw the box away in August. The box was fabric lined on the inside and had a side where it opened and folded over and overlapped partially on another side. I don't have the receipt either but I paid cash (around $40-60 total purchase), purchased 2 10oz tea tins (purple and pink) and bought several ounces of Precious White Peach & Pineapple Kona Pop tea.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from near-boiling water, but the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: Electric Cuisinart DCC 1200 Coffee maker serial number 917 made coffee. After coffee was made the maker started smoking and was hot to touch. It melted a a mat underneath and didn't stop smoking until was unplugged.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing smoke and heat damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: A Cuisinart DCC-1200 Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker that I owned and purchased in August of 2010 caught on fire today while using it in the normal fashion.
justification: The coffeemaker caught fire but there is no mention of injury or death, indicating a severity level of 2.

incident_description:
On August 9,2013 my stove, purchased with the home in July 2007 caught fire causing damage to the appliance and my home.  While cooking my family heard a loud noise coming from the stove, and then saw flames and sparks cascade from the back of the appliance between it and the wall, followed by thick black smoke.  I ushered my wife, ten week old daughter, and dog out of the house and returned to fight the fire.  I was able to turn the appliance off and the home escaped with only cosmetic damage.  Since that time, I have been working with Electrolux in an effort to find a resolution to the issue.  I have filed a claim with them, [REDACTED], and have patiently gone through their process.  Electrolux sent a representative out to my home to get a statement and take pictures of the appliance.  When he opened the appliance to take pictures he commented on how 'fried' it was.  
Instead of attempting to deal with the issue of a possible defective appliance; they have decided to delay and discourage me at every point of my claim.  Now they, nor their adjuster (Crawford Company, the employer of the individual sent to my home) refuse to respond to my inquiries.  I have called and emailed multiple times and have not had a response in 8 business days.  I understand that the onus of proof is on me; however, there has been no effort by Electrolux to aid in the determination of a defective product.  The fact remains the only thing that was on fire was the appliance, no wiring or other electrical was damaged.  As I have gone through this process their solutions included:  Purchasing parts from them (if available) at a discount rate and having the appliance repaired on my own.  This is foolish since the fire was caused by a faulty part  
To have a repair individual come out and repair the appliance, on my own and then allow them to determine if further testing is necessary.  A repair individual cannot determine causality and will not come unless he is going to 'repair' the appliance, and the damage is so extensive it should not be repaired.
Obtain proof of causality through a forensics firm at my cost (typically more than $2500) to determine if their appliance is at fault.  The sheer cost alone is beyond what most consumers would spend, and they no that. 
Electrolux has not sent any communication since 9/24/13, and has refused to comment on my inquiries.  
Although the phsyical damage was not extensive it could have been.  I was in the right place to avert what could have been a devastating situation causing massive property damage and the potential loss of life.
justification: The incident involved a stove fire causing cosmetic damage but no injuries or deaths, and the likelihood is considered possible given the description of the event.

incident_description: 4 times from unknowingly brushing up against stove, knobs were turned and gas emitted for hours
justification: Gas was emitted for hours due to accidental contact with stove knobs, posing a hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: I have a frigidaire smooth top range/oven Model LGEF3033KBF Serial Number VF21956476. A few days ago we smelled plastic burning somewhere in the house and I couldn't find the source.  Yesterday my stove gave me a F10 error code and today I began trouble shooting it.  I found the EOC or (clock timer) melted and black soot all over the circuit board.  It had gotten so hot it melted the connectors onto the board. To the best of my knowledge we were not using the stove or range top at the time I smelled the burning plastic. This is very worrisome and thought I would report it.  The stove is just a little over a year old.  I have the part that failed saved in case it needs to be evaluated.
justification: The incident involved a melted component and soot, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the stove is just over a year old and such failures are not common.

incident_description:
We have a GE gas range (model #JGBP33CEL2CC, serial #SL241160P).  Several times, the oven has started to heat up spontaneously.  The display does not show that the oven is heating, and the oven seems to get very, very hot.  The only way to stop it that we have found is to unplug the unit.  My husband researched the problem and discovered at an online forum that this is a known problem with other GE ranges from a few years ago.  The online search revealed that it is probably a problem with the electronic controls.  

There does not seem to be a recall listed on the GE website.  This seems to be a potential fire hazard, if it had happened when we were not home or at night.
justification: The oven heating spontaneously poses a fire hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet. The issue is likely to recur based on the description and online reports.

incident_description: GE Profile Microwave/Convection oven automatically turns on convection mode when the door is closed. Oven becomes extremely hot and can not be turned off. Unit has to be unplugged to turn off. As soon as unit is plugged in it turns on and overheats.
justification: The oven's malfunction poses a risk of overheating, but no injury or death is mentioned in the description.

incident_description: I purchased my Frigidaire Gallery Series, Model# FGEF3055KF, for $796.98 on 12/12/2010 from AppliancesConnection.com. Upon installation, the range seemed to operate normally. I had noticed shortly afterwards that my utility bill increased quite a bit but I had no reason at that time to consider the range as the cause. In April of 2012, I had noticed that one burner on my stove (front left, quick boil) was not heating correctly whereas it would turn on & off at odd rates and it was not cooking as it had before. A few days later, I attempted to use the "keep warm" burner. When I turned the knob to the "off" position, the burner indicator light did not go out. I tried a few more times, but the light stayed on. I waited a few minutes & did confirm that the burner was actually still in operation and would not shut off until it was unplugged. I did call for service under the extended warranty plan I had purchased. In the meantime, I was able to use the range (with caution) as this was our only method for being able to prepare food. Before service, I also found that when using the oven, it would also remain on despite the control panel showing it was off. I confirmed this by measuring the temperature in the oven 4 hours after I had supposedly shut it off. The temperature was still at 348 degrees. Once I opened the door, the oven did shut off, but only if the door was opened & then closed after the control panel was "shut off". Realizing that the range was remaining on, I investigated the impact on my utility usage by checking my meter speed when the range was unplugged versus running versus "false off". The meter was notably faster durinng the "false off" test stage. The repairman did come & said that he didn't see a problem with the cooktop burners but replaced a switch (?) anyway. He also didn't find a problem with the oven whereas I don't believe any repairs were made there. The issues seemed to be resolved immediately after the repair but I did note that after using the oven, it still seemed to remain abnormally hot for an extended period of time. Until now, I remedied this the same way I had done prior to the 'repair', by opening the door for a short time after turning the oven off. After cooking breakfast this morning whereas I used the front left/quick boil burner, the right front burner and the keep warm burner, I had turned all the knobs to the "off" position as usual. The front left/quick boil burner was turned to the "off" position about 10 minutes prior to the other 2. I removed the pots from the unit and my husband & I proceeded to eat breakfast. Approximately 35 minutes after eating, I attempted to clean the surface of the stove top. When I wiped the front left burner, I sustained a first-degree burn on my right palm, index finger & middle finger as the burner was still extremely hot. After applying ice, I examined the stove and confirmed that all knobs were "off" and that the "hot surface" light was out. However, the front left burner, though not glowing red, was still (at least 50 minutes after being turned "off") hot enough to cause blisters on my hand. After inspecting, I had turned each knob to listen for any noises, etc. but noticed nothing that seemed abnormal. At this point, though, the keep warm burner experienced the same problem as before where as it would not shut off regardless of what was done. The unit is now unplugged and I'll be contacting Frigidaire for service under the extended warranty again. After  some internet research, I am extremely concerned since there had been a previous recall by Frigidaire for several model versions previous to mine and similar models in 2009 due to the same problems I have experienced and which has now caused a minor injury. I also uncovered hundreds of recent (since the previous recall) complaints & consumer accounts of the same or similar issues with this company's ranges including the model I own.
justification: The incident resulted in a first-degree burn, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar issues with the same model.

incident_description: Stove  top elements turn on spontaneously, fail to turn off or heat to different temperatures than what is selected .  Once the stove top was turned completely off, it spontaneously turned the burners  off an on.  resulted in potential fire.  Frigidaire  Serial # VF83880992  MODEL# FEFBZ90GCD
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a fire hazard, which is a significant incident but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: During some point during a six month deployment to Afghanistan the ice maker in my GE TFX26KRDAWW refrigerator caught on fire.  The inside of the freezer is covered in black soot and the electro-mechanical portion of the ice maker is burnt.  Additionally some of the plastic in the area is melted.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the ice maker causing damage to the refrigerator, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
GE Dishwasher Model ZBD0700K10II 
After starting wash cycle, machine caught on fire. Smoke and fire were observed coming from top of machine. Opened door and fire was coming from door panel. Turned circuit breaker off. Open panel and discovered computer as the source of the fire. Melted main wiring harness, display and harness, and control panel wiring harness.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher with no reported injuries, hence severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) based on the description of a specific model issue.

incident_description: The microwave turns on by itself when unattended.  The only way to stop it is to open the door, and then when you close the door it often starts again.   Otherwise it will run by itself for long periods of time.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: I have a GE Spectra range that is about 11 years old.  The heating element on the oven started flaming and sparking.  We turned off the oven, but it did not stop right away.  I had to close the oven door and it eventually went out.
justification: The incident involved flaming and sparking from the oven's heating element, but no injury was reported, and the situation was controlled by turning off the oven and closing the door.

incident_description: Microwave caught fire while in use, melting shelf hooks, scorching interior and causing control touch pad to shatter. This is the second time since purchase and installation that I have had issues with this microwave. It is an over-the-oven model, three years old, clearly poorly designed.
justification: Microwave caught fire causing damage but no injury reported, and this is the second occurrence with the same model.

incident_description: The outer glass of my oven door shattered spontaneously on 10/13/13, while the oven was cold. The appliance had not been used in some weeks. I was not aware of any shocks or damage to the glass. No injuries--the tempered glass failed as intended and formed non-sharp pebbles.
justification: The oven glass shattered but caused no injuries, as the tempered glass failed safely.

incident_description: GE Microwave turned itself on at 1am.  I had walked by it 10 minutes earlier and it seemed fine.  Time was showing.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no injury, but it could indicate a potential safety issue.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Elite Ultra Wash dishwasher Model No. 665.16052400

Built in 9 year old dishwasher circuit board overheated and started fire on circuit board in control panel - burned through plastic box in which circuit board is located and then into plastic control panel - burned through control panel leaving soot on panel and smoke in air.  Noticed when smelled smoke while in another room.

No recall noted on Sears web site.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an overheated circuit board, which resulted in damage to the dishwasher and smoke in the air, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was warming [REDACTED]'s yellow corn tortilla chips in my toaster oven.  I bake them for 10 minutes at 225 degrees Fahrenheit.  I have done this dozens of times before.  On 9/28/2013 the chips ignited.  I suspect that the cause was that the appliance did not maintain the proper temperature, as 225 degrees is not enough to ignite tortilla chips.
justification: The incident involved chips igniting but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as it happened once despite dozens of previous safe uses.

incident_description:
I was baking a casserole dish on September 20 , 2013 around 10:28pm my oven glass front shattered.  I was washing dishes during the explosion, therefore my backside was facing the occurrence.  I have no idea what may have triggered the sudden breach.  The oven was per-set as usual 350 degrees.  It had warmed to the 350 degrees and I had about 30 minutes remaining on my dish. The food was prepared in a [REDACTED] bakeware. The lid was mounted properly.  There were no other items in the oven.

However, I am still struggling with clearing the glass from the oven.  There are a few particles that are not bulging from the frame.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no injury was reported, only inconvenience in cleaning up the glass particles.

incident_description: Purchased a Kenmore Trio French Door refrigerator and the light stayed on all nite in fact melting, Now the refrigerator wont retain the same temperature causing sickness in my home due to under cooled tempertures
justification: The refrigerator malfunction led to under-cooled temperatures, causing sickness in the home, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: The Kitchen Aid Dishwasher purchased in 2010 caught fire burning the control panel.  The unit continued to run after the cycles were over and we have had to turn the breaker off leading to the unit or it will just continue to run and burn.  After looking into this product is seems there has been a class action lawsuit filed against the company because of the thousands of complaints and their refusal to recall the product.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but there was no mention of injury or death, indicating an incident without injury. The mention of thousands of complaints suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a Bosch gas cook top model #NGM5664UC on March 5th, 2013.  I noticed that while using the cook top with a normal sized pot (1 or 2 quart) on the cook top, the area around the knobs and the knobs them selves seems to get quite hot.  I called Bosch to report this matter, which they sent out an appliance technician who measured the temperature of the area around the knobs.  The technician reported that this area was registering at 172 degrees fahrenheit.  The technician told me that 150 degrees is the top end of the acceptable range, I found the 172 degrees very alarming.  I followed up with Bosch to find out the next steps as the temperature is clearly over the threashold and can cause 3rd degree burns to myself or my family within seconds by touching an area that is ment to be touched (I can only imagine what would happen if a child touched this area).  During my follow-up with Bosch, they told me they were going to talk to an engineer to find out the cause of this.  As that was approximately 3 weeks ago, I followed up with Bosch to find out the status of my issue.  They told me that they had closed my issue.  They told me that they now have to send out another technican (I am not sure what another technician is going to do) on October 11th, 2013.  I am extremely concerned for the safety of myself and my family.  Please let me know how I should handle this matter and let me know if you need anything from me.  Thank you for your time.
justification: The cook top's knobs reach 172°F, exceeding the safe threshold and posing a burn risk, especially to children, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: This report relates to a Electrolux smooth top oven. Always worked perfectly until a few weeks ago. Went to oven, and burnt my fingers on top metal part of oven. The cook top was also very, very hot. The front metal attached to the top was very, very hot. Repair man came and tried to diagnose. He called the Frigidaire/Electrolux company and they said there is no regulation or solution for how hot the outside of an oven can become. Something is obviously very wrong with an answer like that.  I have children, so this is especially scary for me. No one at Electrolux will help. This is a scary fire/burn hazard with no resolution. Spent $2,300 and very unhappy.
justification: The user reported burning their fingers on the hot oven, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is described as ongoing and unresolved, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: A DELAYED IGNITION WHEN USING THE OVEN CAUSING GAS SMELL AND A SMALL EXPLOSION WHEN IGNITED, THIS RECENT INCIDENT CAUSED A SMALL FIRE BUT WENT OUT WHEN OVEN WAS TURNED OFF
justification: The incident involved a small fire and explosion, but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Dear CPSC Representatives,

I am writing to report a shattering incident with a Pyrex glass baking dish on Sept. 24/2013. The empty dish was at room temperature, just taken out of a kitchen cupboard, and set on an Epicurean brand cutting board on a laminate kitchen counter.  At the time of the shattering, it was located on the counter beside (not on) a 350 degree oven where food was cooking.

Right before the shattering, there was a cracking sound and then the dish shattered with explosive force onto the counter and kitchen floor.  I was a few feet away from the dish when it happened -- I was hit by a few stray pieces of glass, and my vinyl floor was damaged.

I do not think that any baking/cooking glassware with shattering properties like this should be allowed in North American kitchens.  It was a mistake to manufacture it and all glassware items of this formulation should be recalled.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a glass dish shattering, causing minor injury from stray glass pieces and floor damage, but no severe harm or death.

incident_description:
Sliced a finger on each hand grasping the baking tray in order to clean it under the faucet. Underside of top lip of tray is razor sharp

PS  I noticed too late there were typos in my email address  Correct address is [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on each hand, which is an injury.

incident_description:
The product is a residential wine cellar.  It was being used to store wine in my home.  The product received it's power through a surge protector.  I smelled smoke from within my home and located the source to be the wine cellar.  The unit was immediately unplugged.  Upon inspection I had noticed that electronic components near the AC input were scorched and plastic near the source was beginning to melt.

I feel this product produces a fire risk.

I have had 3 of these units and all 3 have failed in the same manner at different times.  The first ran for 10 months then this failure occurred.  The company replaced that and I had acquired a second at the same time for occasional use.  The next one ran for approximately 2 years and then had the same failure.  I then ran the third for a few weeks (it had run from time to time before) and the same failure occurred.  I have contacted the company again, first by e-mail (with no response) then by phone.  No reason was given for the failure and nothing was done to address my concern for the potential issue.

The first failure did not raise a large concern with me about the safety, it was the identical failure with the following two units that alerted me.
justification: The incident involved smoke and scorched components, indicating a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred. The repeated failures across multiple units suggest a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
We have a Sears Kenmore electric range/oven, purchased about 2 years ago.  On Thursday night, 9/19/2013, when my wife turned the oven on by pressing the Bake button, the electronic circuitry in the top of the stove (what I call the tombstone on the back where the controls are) caught fire.  Small flames came out the vents in back, and the smoke poured out from the control panel.  I turned off the power at the breaker, and the fire went out.  We did not use a fire extinguisher and the fire department was not called.  The stove is under an extended warranty, and we are expecting the sears repairman today, hopefully, they've been no-shows twice.

Model No:  790.92209012

Serial No:  VF05040864
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven's control panel but was quickly controlled without injury or need for emergency services.

incident_description:
I was washing dishes on Friday when the range made quick popping noises (it was not being used).
On Saturday, I turned on the stove and it made popping noises and burst into flames.

I went online to see if anyone had similar experiences.
There were many complaints of fires even when owners were not in the room.
justification: The stove burst into flames, indicating an incident, but no injury or death was reported. Online complaints suggest similar incidents are likely.

incident_description: On 3-15-13 I purchased a Magic Chef Countertop 0.9 cu. ft. Microwave Oven from Home Depot online.  Model No. MCD991R. Tonight less than three minutes into warming my dinner a horrendously loud clattering/clanking noise came from the microwave and a spark from the outlet it was plugged into.  I unplugged it.  It scared the daylights out of me.  I have owned two previous microwaves - both inexpensive.  The first lasted 10 years and was working when I passed it along.  The second I had for 10 years also and I took it to the office where I work and it is still working there.  I never had anything like this happen before.  This microwave is only 6 1/2 months old. I have already written Home Depot and Magic Chef.  If I had not been standing right there and quickly pulled the plug, I don't know what would have happened.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and a spark, causing fear but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I received a 13x9 glass Pyrex baking dish.  I used it once before without incident.  Today I baked a cake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes.  I took the cake out of the oven & placed it on the top of the stove to cool.  About 30 minutes later I heard exploding glass.  When I got to the kitchen, the Pyrex dish had exploded, sending shards of glass out over the kitchen & stove top & into the food. The glass shards ranged from larger pieces under the food, medium pieces over the floor & counter tops, to tiny pieces as well.
A very dangerous situation.
When investigating this further online it was disturbing to read so many articles that indicate this product is safe, & the exploding glass was most likely due to consumer error.  This was definitely not the case.  Pans are kept in a cupboard.  There was no "thermal shock".  Oven was 350 for 40 minutes. Cooling was done on top of the oven.  
I own Pyrex that was used continually by my mother & grandmother without incident for decades.
I am grateful I was not in the kitchen when it happened.  I am also grateful I was not holding a hot casserole.
And especially that children were not in the area.
Reports seems to indicate there are so few reports filed, it must not really be an issue.  Thereby, my reporting my incident.
I do not believe this is an isolated, rare occurrence.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of glass, but no injuries were reported, placing it at severity level 2. The description suggests this is not an isolated event, indicating a higher likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I brewed a cup of coffee using a k-cup and it brewed normally.  I turned the coffee maker off and within 5 minutes I heard it start up again like it was heating up.  There was no water in the reservoir and I was confused because I had turned it off.  I opened the k-cup lever and the heating mechanism was glowing red inside and smoke began pouring out.  It smelled like hot plastic.  I unplugged it and poured water into the reservoir to extinguish the heating element.  I reported this to Cuisinart over the phone and they said they had not heard any other similar complaints.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that produced smoke but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My issue is with a cook-top/oven from Frigidaire. The item is known as model FPGF3081 KFN serial VF30570429.The
knobs of the cook-top are defective. When one grazes the knobs, they randomly slightly turn on thus causing a gas
leak. It only takes a slight graze pass the knob to open it. Additionally, as you may reach forward to use a above mounted microwave, a slight rubbing on the knobs causes them to open. In any case, one does not know the knob is beginning to emit gas. the open knob is only slightly open but enough to cause gas to leak. we have had the above experiences 4 times since 4/4/2013. we have experienced our kitchen filling with gas on all occasions. It can potentially be an explosive situation. It will only take a spark or lighting a match to explode the kitchen or the whole house. The knobs need to be hard to push in before the gas valve is turned to left. They are not. Frigidaire has been contacted twice. they refuse to investigate with their technician or outside repair person. They only claim that they made for shorter people.

Again, I mustrepeat that a slight rubbing on any of the gas knobs causes them to slightly open and emit gas. this occurs even before it reaches the electronic ignition location.

I ask that frigidaire be called to task on this unsafe and very dangerous design.
justification: The defective knobs cause gas leaks, creating a high risk of explosion, which could lead to death. The issue has occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: This refrigerator was used in our garage. We bought it new as a discontinued model from Lowes in 2007 or 2008. The breaker was blown in the garage which knocked out the lights. About a minute later, and because I was standing next to the refrigerator, I could smell something electrical burning.  I looked toward the fridge and saw an orange glow behind it that quickly turned to flames coming from the bottom in the back. The fire extinguisher was not handy so we dragged it out of the garage, then put the fire out.  The whole process lasted about 4 minutes. We then checked Maytag for recalls, did not find our model listed. We called Maytag, explained to them what happened, and they sent out a repairman. He condemned it and it will not be fixed. He also said it was the worst he has seen.  There was no damage to the house other than burn marks on the garage floor. We had very fortunate timing as we had not been in the garage for several hours or we would have had a very different ending.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no injuries or damage to the house, only burn marks on the garage floor.

incident_description:
Our Frigidaire Slide In Range (Model: FPCS3085LFA; Serial: NF01628476) was not in use and began beeping and displaying an error code (EO 37) across the displays. This has happened before and we have contacted Frigidaire but been told unless the code is actively displayed when a service tech comes to the home it cannot be evaluated. In the past the code and beeping have stopped after a few minutes or we have had to turn off power to the range and they have not resumed when power is turned back on.

During the most recent incident and after the code and beeping continued for 10 minutes or so we turned power off to the stove. After turning the power back on the error code and beeping continued.

Next, the left rear burner spontaneously turned on to high / bright red and failed to turn off, which is our chief complaint. The control was in the off position. A package of mushrooms had been placed on the cook top and began smoldering and power had to be shut off to the stove to turn off the burner. 

In recent weeks, the front left burner has also been heating to a high temperature when a low temperature is selected. 

This range has a hybrid induction / electric cook top. The left burners are electric. After researching this incident we discovered Frigidaire has had two previous recalls (our model is not included) and the hazards are identical to what we experienced with our range.
justification: The incident involved a burner turning on spontaneously, causing smoldering, which could lead to injury if not addressed promptly. The recurrence of similar issues and past recalls suggest a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Dishwasher stopped working and the smell of burning plastic was all over the house.  The wires in the junction box under the dishwasher are all charred.  The circuit breaker on the main panel tripped as a result.  From the photos you can see the damage.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction with charred wires and a tripped circuit breaker, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We came home and found that the outer glass door on our Maytag Gas Precision Touch Control 500 range (Model MGR5765QDQ) was shattered in a million pieces.
justification: The glass door shattered but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: The front burner on the Electrolux electric range (model # EI30EF55GSD) turned on by itself when no one was at home and could not be turned off (the entire unit had to be powered down to avoid the danger of fire in the house). Contacted Electrolux customer service, who refused to register this incident and suggested that they are not responsible, since the unit was out of warranty period (purchased in January 2010).
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While pureeing tomatoes and water, the base of the blender was blowing out smoke, and stopped after it started smoking. I thankfully was beside it. Unplugged it, the cord and plug were extremely hot to the touch and I burned myself unplugging it. 
I did not require medical treatment, iced it at home.

Called The company that manufactures this blender and they don't care.

For a blender that could have caught my house on fire they want me to pay $30 to ship it back to them. 
If I was 5ft from that blender, only God would know what would have happened.
justification: The incident involved a blender malfunction causing smoke and a burn injury, though no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the lower oven element failed (overheated) and caused it to warp coming in contact with the bottom of the oven.  He discovered this when the oven was not heating when it was powered on, he removed the covering and noticed this failure.  

8/9/13  The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that a service rep could be sent out at a cost to him, he declined due the fact that he did not feel that he should have pay for the manufacturer's product failure.  He replaced the element himself and the oven now works.
The unit is not included in a recall.
The caller feels that the oven is a potential fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a failed oven element causing warping but no injury or fire occurred, and the issue was resolved by the caller.

incident_description:
09/18/2013) The consumer stated that she called Sears and was advised By [REDACTED] that there was no recall on her range. The consumer stated that she was also advised to call CPSC. 

(09/18/2013) The consumer stated that the oven had been on for about twenty-five minutes. The consumer stated that she had baked brownies. The consumer stated that she took the brownies out of the oven and set them on top of the stove to cool. 

The consumer stated that she turned the oven off and went to the den. The consumer stated that about five minutes later she detected an electrical smell. She went to the kitchen to make sure that the oven was off. The consumer stated that the indicator showed that the oven was off.  The consumer stated that she opened the oven door and saw that the broiler was on. 

The consumer stated that she had to cut the breaker off to disconnect the stove.

The consumer stated that about thirty minutes later, the stove was still too hot to touch.
justification: The incident involved an electrical malfunction with no reported injury, but required intervention to disconnect the stove.

incident_description: I placed the Bella slow cooker on a cutting board then placed a thermometer between the board and the bottom of the slow cooker. Within a half an hour it had reached 120 degrees and was still climbing.
justification: The slow cooker reached a high temperature on a cutting board, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: I have a GE Profile dishwasher (model PDW9900N00BB) that was purchased in 2007 for $1,199.00.  On 9/14/13, I noticed that it was spontaneously heating when the door was closed, even though a cycle was not running. I knew that this was a systemic problem with GE dishwashers, because the GE dishwasher I had prior to this one was recalled for the same thing. I checked the GE website but did not find a recall on this unit; however, I did find a large number of reports on the internet filed by others who have the same problem. I called GE to report it and the case manager to whom I spoke, [REDACTED], told me that she would send a repair person to look at it, and that the trip fee would be waived and the parts and labor to fix it discounted to 50%.  (Obviously they know they have a problem if they are willing to discount their services this much!) The tech came and found that the bottom sprayer arm had been melted on the underside because of the spontaneous heating and said that the control unit needed to be replaced. However, I elected not to have him fix it and instead get a different brand of dishwasher since I have ZERO faith in GE. There are recalls on GE dishwashers that have this problem going back many years-it is obviously a well-known problem that they have been unable or unwilling to fix. (There are in fact numerous documented cases of home fires attributed to these dishwashers.) I am not willing to repair the one I have, or go spend a large amount of money on a new GE unit, and risk coming home to a pile of smoldering ash where my house used to be.  I told [REDACTED] that I had elected to buy a new dishwasher of a different brand and asked if any portion of our purchase price could be refunded; she flatly refused since I told her I did not intend to buy another GE dishwasher. She stressed that the unit was not under recall (even though it obviously should be) so there was nothing she could do.
justification: The dishwasher exhibited spontaneous heating, a known issue with potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On Friday, 09/20/2013 at approximately 6:30 pm, my wife was using our General Electric electric oven to cook. Our 13 month old son [REDACTED] placed his right hand in the approximate 3/4" gap in-between the bottom of the oven door and the top edge of the lower storage drawer and began to shriek in pain. My wife immediately picked him up and observed redness to his right index finger and middle finger. This area of the bottom of the oven door was extremely hot and caused severe 2nd degree burns to the tip of several of my sons fingers and blistering to the top part of his index and middles fingers. We immediately put his hand under cool water and called a family doctor friend who advised us how to treat his injuries. My wife and I later felt this same area of the stove after it cooled some and we found the middle part of the door to still be very hot even though it had been off for some time now. The left and right sides of the same bottom area of the oven door were much cooler. It appears that a 6" area of the interior lower area of the oven door is built without the same oven door gasket (WB04T10001) that surrounds the rest of the door. This in combination with a center trim bracket (WB07T10462) with screw (WH02X0930) acting as a conduit for the heat to escape led to my child's injuries. If the oven door gasket completely surrounded the interior oven door, heat would not be able to escape and my son's injury would not have occurred. A range should not be sold to consumers if a child can be burned without the door or lower drawer even open. I can see an accidental burning if the oven door is open or if a child is able to touch a hot stove top surface, but not a closed oven. Shouldn't parents expect their children to be safe around a stove when the doors are closed?
justification: The child suffered severe 2nd degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the design flaw that allows heat to escape from a closed oven, posing a risk to children.

incident_description: This was the fifth time the item has been used. Thermostat failed while using the panini function. Unit was preheated following the included instructions. A timer was set and the sandwich placed on the grill. Within 60 seconds the sandwich was burning. When the grill was opened to remove the food the clips holding the top plate failed causing the now very hot grill plate to fall. The clips failed at too low a temperature which made using the controls to shut off the device dangerous and moving the device in order to unplug it difficult.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure and a burning sandwich, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Using large Pyrex baking dish with a roasting chicken at 425 degrees along side another brand glass dish when the Pyrex shattered--and spilled oil and fat, etc., and caused a fire. Flames in over and coming out of door. Used fire extinguisher and also called Cranston, I Fire Dept, which responded.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported, and the fire was contained with a fire extinguisher and fire department response.

incident_description: (09/07/2013) The consumer stated that his wife smelled smoke. Smoke was coming out of the dishwasher. She opened the door and flames came out from the circuit  board. The dishwasher was in the middle of a cycle. The consumer stated that it did not trip the circuit breaker. He had to go to the circuit breaker and kill the power.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames from the dishwasher, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My Kenmore Elite Trio refrigerator light bulb popped inside the refrigerator and the housing melted - potential fire hazard
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to a melted light bulb housing, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Thursday, September 19th, 2013, I returned home at 12:30 PM after having left home around 8:15 AM to find the front, left burner of our Electrolux range red and blazing hot. A number of the objects on the countertops next to the stove were very hot to the touch as well. The control panel indicated that the burner was off, and the "hot surface" light was illuminated. I pressed the off button several times to try to get the burner to turn off but it remained red and hot. My husband was able to pull the stove away from the wall (it is a slide-in style of range) and unplug it, and eventually the burner cooled down. 

The last time I used this burner was yesterday, September 18th, from about 5 PM- 5:30 PM. It was off when I left the house this morning. 

It is frightening to imagine what would have ensued if something had been left on the range top, or if a breeze from the open window had blown papers from the countertop on to the burner, or if we had been out of town for a few days. 

I have since Googled this problem and think that the fuse in the burner shorted out. A repair person is coming out in a few days to address the problem. I cannot believe that there is not an auto-shut-off safety feature that automatically engages when a fuse blows. This range is relatively new, and this type of feature seems like a basic one!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that remained hot despite being turned off, posing a fire hazard but resulting in no injury or death.

incident_description:
Purchased NuWave "Mini" oven along with regular NuWave oven from Hearthware.  The regular oven appears to be an excellent product.  The "mini" is hazardous as the power head and clear dome that should lift as one will separate with the dome falling whenever the oven is warm.  This happens every time.  The problem does not occur when the unit is cold.  I received (minor) burns several times due to attempts to catch the falling dome.  The oven itself works well.

An email asking for a solution went unanswered by the customer service department.  In a phone call to the company today I was told this was a known issue with no resolution other than to let the oven cool (with the food still inside) or try and pick up the dome and power head with kitchen mitts.  According to the CSR this defect has been reported many times by customers.  

The oven is still offered for sale by the company.  I am concerned other consumers might receive more significant physical burns if unaware of this defect - especially the elderly.
justification: The incident describes minor burns from a known defect that occurs every time the oven is used, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence and potential for injury.

incident_description: The appliance's timer was turned clockwise to start the heating cycle in the usual manner.  The dial slowly turned counter-clockwise as the timer counted down the minutes until the dial reached the OFF position also in the usual manner.  When the dial reached the OFF position, instead of the appliance shutting off with a bell sound to indicate the end of the heating cycle, the appliance continued to heat and the dial proceeded past the OFF position to the STAY ON position with the timer continuing to operate.  The appliance continued to heat until the unit was unplugged
justification: The appliance malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
Our GE Profile Spacemaker XL1800 is 6 years old. Twice now the 'over the stove" light, contained in bottom of the microwave, has exploded, as soon as we turned on the light in the morning. Luckily the plastic cover beneath the 2 (very expensive to replace)bulbs has stayed intact or there would definitely have been injuries from flying glass particles. It happened again today, nearly scaring me to death, and waking my husband in another room. White smoke comes from the light socket after the bulb explodes. why would this happen to a cool light that has been off for over 10 hrs, in an Air conditioned kitchen? 
As with every single GE appliance that our builder insisted we buy when purchasing our new house, this has been nothing but trouble. continuous burned out bulbs, fan vent that wont close, on and on. they are all terrible appliances and ii will boycott them and their products for ever.
justification: The incident involved exploding bulbs with potential for injury, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description: Spectra model electric range stove, approximately 12 yrs old.  Oven would not shut off, despite being turned "off", and indicator light showing it was "off".  coil in oven stayed red for over 4 hours, until power disconnected.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: bought a krups electric tea kettle. it heat water to boiling and then leaks water.
justification: The kettle leaks water after boiling, which is an incident but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: A glass Duralex bowl exploded in my face after removing it from the microwave for two and a half minutes.  I am absolutely shocked that I was not injured.  I microwaved food from dinner the night before for two and a half minutes, took it out, set the bowl down on my kitchen island, sat down, bent in towards the bowl to take a hot bite of food when the bowl EXPLODED!!  It sounded like a fire cracker my face.  It was loud.  Literally thousands of pieces of glass covered by kitchen and family room.  Hundreds of pieces were the size of a grain of salt.  It took me well over an hour to clean the grout, floors, bar stools, etc.  Please investigate this further.  I filed a complaint with the company.  When I Googled "exploding Duralex bowl" I was upset to see that this has happened to many people before me.  Someone could get very seriously injured.  I beg you to look into this matter.  Thank you.
justification: The incident involved an exploding bowl but no injury occurred, and similar incidents have been reported by others, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description: Message = Tried to use: Farberware Waffle Maker Model# 103739. The latch just under the handle locks every time the lid is down (vs. just for storage like some other manufacturer models). You must reach through the handle and depress the latch to open the lid in order to remove the waffle. The problem is, there is so much heat/steam and you really need both hands to open the lid, as the waffle offers resistance. I burned myself each time I tried to remove the two waffles I baked; even while trying to use a hot pad - which was difficult in the tight handle area. I am returning this to Wal Mart and telling them of my issue. The printed Customer Assistance phone number printed on the "Farberware" manual is actually a Wal Mart phone number, which I called. I told them of the issue so, hopefully they will tell Farberware and someone will investigate.
justification: The user reports being burned each time they tried to remove waffles, indicating an injury occurred, and the design flaw suggests this is likely to happen frequently with continued use.

incident_description:
On the 11th of September, 2013, I purchased an Amana Gas Range from Upton Appliances in Bullhead City, Arizona. This item was delivered and set-up to my home on the 12th of September. 
After insuring that the stove worked properly the installer left and I was happy with the situation. That is, I was happy until I used the stove top for the first time. It was then that I noticed that the surface area of the stove top got very hot. I don't mean just warm as you would expect but extremely hot. Hot enough to possibly cause a burn. I am not referring to the actual burners nor to area immediately around the burners, but the entire surface area of the range. If there were small children in my house I would not feel safe using this stove.

I have spent the last two and a half hours on the phone trying to get help with this problem What I am told is that this is normal operation and there is nothing to worry about. To me when a product, during "normal" operation gets hot enough to burn skin something is wrong.

For your information I called the following numbers and spoke with the agents listed:

Upton Appliances [REDACTED] ([REDACTED] the repair tech) 

Amana customer service [REDACTED] ([REDACTED])

Whirlpool customer service [REDACTED] ([REDACTED] - note that this person did try to get a tech to come to my house)

Whirlpool customer service [REDACTED] (one unknown agent and [REDACTED] -- got put on hold and ignored -- no one came back on line).

Product model number AGR5844VDW a gas range/stove.  Serial number R21636298
justification: The stove's surface gets extremely hot during normal operation, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Caller reported that her ceramic stove top exploded while it was on for approximately 5 mins on medium heat.  The unit made a sound like a gun shot, it cracked and a piece of ceramic fell out in regular shape.  She was able to power off the range and it finally cooled down.  There were no prior services or incidents with this unit.

The manufacturer will be contacted later.

She feels that this ceramic top range is a safety hazard and should be reported.

The product is not included in a recall.
justification: The stove top exploded but there was no injury reported, only property damage and a safety concern.

incident_description: We placed a room temperature 9x13 glass baking pan on top of another glass baking dish which was also room temp.   In a few minutes we heard a loud bang and found thousands of pieces of  glass all over the kitchen and 8 feet down the hall.  The pan had exploded.  Thankfully, my husband who was sitting at the kitchen table was unharmed and my 2 year old daughter who was walking down the hall was unharmed. We thank God for His protection!!!  There was not any large pieces of glass remaining from the pan only small pieces that were everywhere. We were shocked!!!
justification: The incident involved a glass pan exploding, causing significant mess but no injuries, as stated in the description.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his smoothtop four burner electric range July 2nd, 2007 and had no problems with it until the beginning of July 2013 when his wife had finished preparing dinner and so it is estimated she may have been cooking sometime around a half hour to an hour.
She turned everything off, however the front right large burner would not turn off.
Caller came to his wife at the range and began trying to turn the burner off using the knob and finally got it to stay off.
He threw the circuit breaker and left it off for four hours for safety.
When he turned the circuit breaker back on four hours later the front large burner instantly began building heat to the highest temperature.

Around August 15th, 2013 the same incident happened but with the left rear large burner would not turn off after cooking and again the callers had to continuously turn the knob on and off until it would finally turn off.

Sometime around Thursday, September 5th, 2013 the front right burner again would only heat to high and would not turn off.
The callers continuously turned the knob on and off but the burner would not turn off until they threw the breaker again.

The callers leave the breaker off unless cooking now because they are afraid to leave it on without supervision.

There  have been no injuries 

Caller contacted the manufacturer September 9th, 2013, was informed that there are no recalls on this particular range.
He spoke with [REDACTED].

Callers are asking that this range be added to the recalled and that repair at manager expense or replacement of product be included in remedy.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that could not be turned off, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Last night I just got done pulling a turkey tenderloin out of my ELECTRIC FRIGIDAIRE GALLERY SERIES OVEN (Serial #: VF51645500, Model #: GLEFM397DQB) purchased in and around 2004 or 2005 when without any warning or prior malfunction whatsoever, I hear loud electrical buzzing and popping as the control panel on the back of the stove top begins to arc and flames climb up the wall from the back of the panel with billowing acrid, black smoke. Thankfully, the circuit breaker popped and miraculously the flames did not catch anything that could cause my entire wall, kitchen and house to go up in flames. Once things were under control and I gathered my composure, I of course googled this brand and found hundreds of complaints regarding similar issues for this model. While I realize that this piece of [REDACTED] (and those made by most manufacturers) are designed these days to break down in 8 to 10 years to force you into expensive repairs or an entirely new unit, I am positively OUTRAGED that something as dangerous as an electrical fire is how it went out. While I can only attest to my own first hand experience, I am extremely disturbed that I read complaints where these units have turned themselves on by themselves and will not go off unless they are shut down at the electrical panel. Why hasn't this garbage been RECALLED before someone is severely burned and there is major property loss or even loss of life? Though my knees have still not stopped shaking, I thank God I was home when this happened and that tragedy was averted. I have a husband, two young kids, and three dogs that could be homeless right now. What if it happened while we are at work or asleep? Like I stated earlier, there were no prior malfunctions or issues until last night - with Frigidaire.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with potential for severe harm, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was frying using my Cuisinart 8" skillet, when there was a loud bang, like the sound of a 22 cal. rifle.  I heard something metal ricochet around the kitchen.  I saw that the rivets holding the handle to the pan actually have a thin metal cover.  One of these exploded, and flew around the room.  If you own this pan return it to the manufacturer, and report them to the appropriate Federal agency.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang and metal pieces flying, but no injury was reported, making it an incident without injury (severity 2). Such failures are uncommon but not unheard of (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
We purchased a Viking D3 Freestanding 30" Gas Self-Clean Sealed Burner Range from Grand Appliance in Madison, Wisconsin on March 16, 2013.  The installation date was April 12, 2013.  The item number is RDSCG2305BSS, the model number is RDSCG2305BSS and the serial number is 030713C10083927.

On several occasions the knobs to the gas range and oven have been accidentally bumped into the 'on' position.  Many times this was not noticed until the entire kitchen was filled with gas.  The ownerÃÂs manual describes the knobs as being "child proof."  They are not even "bump proof."  Because this is a safety issue, we contacted Viking about the issue.  They sent a repair technician, who was unable to remedy the situation.

This is an expensive range which poses a serious danger to our family.  We feel this issue is a flaw in the design and construction of this Viking range model, and are continue to seek a solution to the problem.
justification: The incident describes a gas leak due to accidental knob activation, posing a serious danger but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Whirlpool Refrigerator's motor caught on fire. Smoke filled the kitchen.
justification: The refrigerator motor caught fire and filled the kitchen with smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a set of plates from Target and inside the box taped to the plates was a box cutter. I was not injured but could have seriously been had I stuck my hand inside the box.
justification: The incident involved a potential hazard (box cutter taped inside the box) but no actual injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such packaging errors are not common but do occur occasionally.

incident_description: Upper oven center glass shattered while we were baking
justification: The oven glass shattered during use, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The Mr Coffee brand steam espresso maker exploded on my countertop 3 minutes after it finished brewing the first time it was used.  Broken glass and hot coffee landed all over the counter, floor, and my feet.
justification: The incident involved broken glass and hot coffee landing on the person's feet, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: We purchased a Cuisinart 12 Cup Coffee Maker (Model # DCC-1200) November 20, 2010. It worked flawlessly until this morning, September 15, 2013. We brewed a pot of coffee as we have nearly every day. Two cups were poured, with two cups remaining in the carafe on warm. Approximately 20 minutes later we heard a crackling, bubbling sound coming from the coffee maker. Upon investigation, we noticed the coffee was actually boiling  in the carafe, the warming plate was red and smoke was coming from the underside of the unit. I immediately unplugged the unit and took it outside. Fortunately no one was injured nor was there any damage to the countertop. This was a very alarming incident, and we are fortunate we were able o detect the issue before it became worse. Upon reading reviews from other consumers of this same product, it is apparent this was not an isolated incident. We will not purchase another similar unit, and will be contacted Cuisinart.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that could have led to injury or damage, but no actual harm occurred. Reports indicate this is not an isolated issue, suggesting a possible recurring defect.

incident_description:
I purchased a gas range from Lowe's Model No. FGGF304DLW3. It has two quick boil burners, one on the right front, one on the left rear.  I boiled a tall pot of spaghetti water on the left rear burner and the instrument panel buckled, as if it was melting.  I reported this to Lowe's and said I was afraid it would catch fire if I continued to use it.  They sent a repair guy who said he would replace the panel but that it was not safe to use the back burner for a tall pot.

Lowe's does not have an equivalent stove (features and price) and now they are offering only one option:  upgrade to another stove and pay an additional $700.  I asked them to accept the original stove as a return and refund my money, but they refused.

I have a photo I can send if you would like.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas range that could potentially catch fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While using the Kenmore ultra wash dishwasher, smoke began pouring out of the top control panel. Immediately opened the dishwasher to stop the unit but it kept running, throwing water every where. Unplugging the unit from under the cabinet was quickest/surest way to stop the unit. It appears that the circuit board overheated and was burning.
justification: Smoke and water leakage occurred, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Last night our entire kitchen filled up with smoke and smelled like burning plastic.  We could not figure out where it was coming from.  After unplugging each appliance and then plugging them back in 1 at a time, we determined it was the refrigerator.  After taking off the back panel and plugging it back it, we could see fire and smoke coming from the bottom left corner, where the compressor was located.  We were lucky we were home and NOT sleeping.  I can't even imagine how this would have ended otherwise.  I am writing you so that other families do not have to go through this, or something even worse!  This product is a danger.  I have read the article that Whirlpool thinks the fire would stay contained within the refrigerator and not pose danger to human life. They are WRONG! I have not doubt that had we been sleeping or not at home, the drywall behind the refrigerator would have eventually caught on fire.  Not to mention the amount of smoke that was coming from the back of the refrigerator was dangerous itself.  I have asthma and the amount of smoke in our kitchen which was starting to travel to the rest of our house, was enough to pose danger.  Shame on Whirlpool for not having a recall on these refrigerators and only the MAYTAG brand!  And knowingly allow customers to go through this!
justification: The incident involved fire and smoke, posing a danger to human life, especially due to the asthma condition mentioned, which could lead to injury from smoke inhalation.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite electric range. I went to turn off the burner after using it and it would not turn off. I had to flip the breaker to turn it off. After letting it cool down for an hour. I flipped the breaker back on and the burner automaticlly turned back on to high. I believe that if the relay board fails, it should fail in the off position not the on position.
justification: The burner failing to turn off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she placed her glass dish (6ÃÂ round) in the oven for approximately 15 minutes at a 450 degree temperature. She stated that when she removed the dish from inside the oven the dish exploded on her hands. 

The consumer stated that she was not injured and there were no damages to her home structure. 

The consumer stated that she immediately picked up the glass and discarded it. 

The consumer stated that she will be calling the manufacturer (Pyrex) to file a report. 

The consumer stated that she believed that this product should be investigated due to the laceration hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The consumer reported no injury or structural damage, but the dish exploded, indicating an incident occurred.

incident_description: Today I was cooking game hens in the oven.  I had placed them in a glass pyrex pan.  They were baking for about 45 minutes, when I opened the oven to add some basting sauce (consisting of white wine, olive oil, and garlic).  I was putting in a small amount (no more than 1/4 cup) of this liquid that was at room temperature directly on the game hens.  I slid out the oven door with the bakepan on it before adding the liquid.  The glass bakeware exploded violently, as soon as I started basting my hens.  I mean violently.  Glass shards flew several yards -- all around the kitchen.  Luckily no one was hurt.  (In fact, it is a miracle.)
justification: The glass bakeware exploded violently, but no one was hurt, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
I had an 8 cup Pyrex measuring cup explode in my dishwasher. I think my explosion experience is different from most of the others I have read. I had a 2 quart measuring cup explode in the dishwasher a few days ago. The cup had completely cooled, I was reaching to pull it out of the dishwasher and had just touched the side of it when it shattered into pieces sending shards all around the kitchen, fortunately I only suffered two minor cuts to my fingers, more fortunately I was the only one in my kitchen at the time. This pyrex was at room temperature when it exploded!

Unfortunately I did think to take pictures or save the glass. I can assure you it was Pyrex, I had used it to make pancake batter, there was no stovetop heat, used my normal dishwashing cycle, etc.

I have reported the incident to World Kitchen. I am not hopeful of a serious response from World Kitchen, most of the responses I have read blame the consumer, and use the "small percentage" of explosions as proof of the overall safety. I intend to ask them point blank, what level of consumer injury is considered too much?
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (two cuts to the fingers) but no serious harm, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such incidents, while not common, have been reported multiple times.

incident_description:
A staff member was on refrigerator cleaning duty today.  She pulled the bottom glass shelf out to clean dry milk that was not scrubbing off by just using a sponge and cleaning product.  She scrubbed both sides.  She rinsed one side, and when she turned the shelf to rinse the other side, the glass shelf shattered into many pieces.  The glass did not hit, or knock against anything.  Glass fell on the staff member's arms, hands, chest, hair and feet.  She suffered minor cuts on her right hand and right third toe.

Staff member went to the bathroom to wash off the glass on her arms and hands, and put antibiotic ointment and bandaids on wounds.
justification: The staff member suffered minor cuts on her hand and toe, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the range was purchased in 2007 and immediately after installation, it displayed error codes.  She says the front control panel was replaced in February 2007.  The tech mentioned the back panel should also be replaced yet it was not done.  Three to four months later, the error codes started to re-appear.
