The consumer says that the oven turned on by itself and smoke started to emit from the unit.  The oven nor the stove had been in use at the time the oven turned on spontaneously.  She contacted the retailer who told her the unit is no longer under warranty and offered no further assistance.  caller is experiencing the same hazard listed in recall (Release # 09-333).  The consumer's model is not listed in the recall.
justification: The incident involved the oven turning on by itself and emitting smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Elite, smooth cooktop oven.  One of the burners turns on HIGH automatically without touching to turn on the burner.  We also can't seem to turn it off when it automatically turns on.  This is a big safety hazard and we have to leave the circuit breaker off to ensure it does not turn on when nobody is at home.  

We notice that there were recalls of other Frigidare/Kenmore stoves/ovens in 2009, but it appears to be the same issue.  I have also seen numerous consumers reporting similar issues with the smooth top Kenmore cooktops.

Has there been any other reports on Kenmore Elite model #790.46719600 ?  

Thanks in advance.
justification: The burner turning on automatically poses a safety hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says that her unit is failing to turn off after being switched off also the heat automatically heating to the highest temperature and getting stuck there.  She is having the problem.  

They eventually have to twist and turn the knob to get it to shut off.  The problem is with the two front burners.   The consumer says that she contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not on recall.

The consumer is experiencing the same problems as listed in Release #09-333.  Her serial number is not included in the recall.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning unit that poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
August 18th, 2013 caller and his wife were planning to bake peach muffins and were pre heating their oven.
His wife was still in the kitchen when the oven began smoking and sparking.
She saw four to six inch flames that were coming from the rear of the range where the plug ins are attached to the range.
She went immediately to the breaker room and flipped the breakers off.
Callers have not tried to flip the breakers back on and have no desire to take that chance with the range.
Oven was in home when they purchased it in 2005.

There have been no injuries.
Caller contacted the manufacturer August 19th, 2013 and was advised to contact CPSC.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparking from the oven, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: When using my new Kenmore range, model #79072903010 for the first time a very strong smell of natural gas overwhelmed me.  Once we turned on the convection oven, the smell went away.  I did some research on some blogs to find that many other customers have had this same problem with this same range, yet no recall has happened.  This is a serous danger to consumers.  Now I am wondering if this is why this range was marked down 50% in the store and is now discontinued.  I noticed there is a recall for a higher end Kenmore range with the same type of problem.
justification: The incident describes a strong smell of natural gas, which poses a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The issue is reported by multiple customers, indicating it is likely to occur.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the stove was not in use as they had been away for a week on vacation.  They came back home to find the outer oven glass door totally exploded into small tiny shards.  She says the outer glass was completely shattered out onto the tile floor.

She says it does not appear the glass just fell out but had exploded.  She was not home at the time of the incident.  She says the inner glass is still in tact.  She contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not on recall.  They did not provide any assistance.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded oven glass) but no injury or death occurred as the consumer was not present.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his electric range hadnÃÂt been used for approximately 24-28 hours and the range turned on by itself. The consumer stated that his wife smelled a burning odor and when she went to the kitchen she found that the front right burner was on at a high temperature. The consumer stated that his wife tried to manually turn off the range by pushing the off button. He stated that the burner turned off and in less than 2 seconds it came back on. 

The consumer stated that his wife turned off the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that he turned on the circuit breaker again the burner came back on again. The consumer stated that the range was no longer usable and that he turned the circuit breaker off in fear of a fire.

The consumer stated that he believed that his range was posing the same hazard listed on release # 09-333. 

The consumer stated that believed that this product should be investigated due to the fire and burn hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range that posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the oven safety valve had a failure which caused gas to escape.  He had entered his kitchen to an overwhelming gas odor.  He had to power the unit off from the circuit breaker, the room was ventilated to prevent a possible combustion.

(8/19/13) The manufacturer was contacted and they confirmed that the safety valve failed to work correctly and would replace it at a cost to the consumer.  It was then bargained to a fraction of the cost.

The product model and serial is not included in a recall.

The caller is concerned that this oven which he only had for 5 years has a safety hazard which should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a failed safety valve, but no injury or combustion occurred, and the situation was mitigated.

incident_description:
GE Gas Range purchased around December 22nd, 2011 .
Sometime around the end of July 2013 the callers' wife had been baking for approximately 20 to 30 minutes when she heard a loud bang.
She went toward the sound from the kitchen and saw that glass was on her kitchen floor, on the pots and pans in the drawer below.
The middle glass of the three glass window in the oven door had shattered although neither the inside glass or the outside glass shattered or broke.

She immediately turned the range off and called her husband to ask if he would remove the spare-ribs from the oven and dispose of them because although there was no glass inside the oven she wasn't positive that none came inside.

There have been no injuries

Caller and his wife contacted the manufacturer around August 1st, 2013, filed a report with [REDACTED] and received case# [REDACTED].
[REDACTED] advised that the manufacturer would send the callers' a check for over $100 until the caller informed her that they had already paid for repair in the amount of $247.00.
Once she knew that the caller had already paid for repair she sent them a check for $60.

Caller believes that the manufacturer should at the very least reimburse them half the cost of repair.                                                                               

Caller is reporting this product as unsafe and believes that either of the other glasses in the oven door could have also exploded and someone could have been seriously injured.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door glass but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
05/05/2013) The consumer stated that when she boils water, she has to switch burners to keep the stove from getting too hot. The consumer stated that when she uses any of the burners, the surface of the top of stove between the burners gets too hot. This also happens around the edges of the stove. The consumer stated that it does not matter which temperature she is using. 

The consumer stated she had someone from her homeowners insurance to come out. She stated that he gauged the heat at 207 degrees.  She stated that he also told her that there is a design flaw in the stove. She stated that he raised the top and told her that there was no insulation between the stove and the top to keep the heat from going to the surface of the stove. 

The consumer stated that she uses the stove every day.
  
The consumer stated that this is a dangerous stove. She is afraid that it will catch on fire. 
 
(08/27/2013) The consumer stated that she called the manufacturer to see if the stove had been recalled. She was advised that there were no complaints or recalls on this stove. The consumer was advised that nothing could be done unless the stove was recalled.
justification: The stove's excessive heat poses a burn risk and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her microwave/convection oven would stay on after she hit the ÃÂoffÃÂ button. The consumer stated that she had to leave the door opened to make sure it would not turn back on. She stated that she also turned off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacture and they sent a technician 02/25/2010 and they replaced the heating element. She stated that she had to pay to 275.94 for the labor. 
The consumer stated that the incident happened 3 times and the heating element had to be replaced the heating element again on 11/13/2010. The consumer stated that on May 28, 2011 another technician was sent out to her home, but when he serviced it everything was working properly.

She stated that she was having the same problem with microwave now and it was turning on by itself. She stated that the microwave was becoming really hot to the touch and she feared that it could catch on fire. 

No one was injured. 

The consumer stated that she believes that this product should be included on the recall #08-110, since its posing the same hazards.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned multiple times, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer reported fire hazard with her electric range. She stated that one of the burners turns on automatically and fails to turn off.

The consumer stated that she dropped some water on the rear right burner and noticed it steam. ThatÃÂs when she realized the burner had been on. The consumer stated that when she turns on any one of the 4 burners on the range, the rear right burner turns on automatically. The consumer stated that it does not turn off until the unit is unplugged. The consumer stated that she has to pull the stove out to unplug the unit each time.

incident_description:
Black and Decker toaster oven  TR04080BS
placed two pieces of rye bread in toater, turned dial to "toast" and the timer to correct spot.  i do like my toast well-done, but not on fire.  both pieces of bread caught fire - first smelled smoke, then saw smoke (I had my back to toaster as I made scrambled eggs on stove), opened door - flames shot out.  was able to move toast to sink and douse with water; a few pieces dropped off and i threw a little water on them and got the fire out (probably not the smartest thing, but it worked).  cabinets not scorched, but aluminum pan that was sitting on top of toaster oven (the oven's baking pan) was scorched.  a bit of a mark on the counter top.  later read online that this is not unusual for B&D toaster ovens...
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, and the fire was quickly contained without significant damage.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire Gallery Dishwasher (model number GLDB954BS1 Serial Number TH31555737)  threw a spark from the vent holes and then released a steady stream of black smoke from the handle area.  The house filled with electrical smoke smell.

I called the company and they said that because it was 10 years old they wouldn't look into it.  I talked to 4 levels of management.  Finally the 4th level management agreed to send someone out too look at the damage.  The repair man said there was no water damage or leaking.  The P-5 connection burnt from relay causing extensive smoke and "bad board and membrane".  Quotes are from repair man's notes.  The malfunctioning board burned a hole in the membrane and left visible black smoke damage.

I am thankful we were home to turn off the breaker to cut the power to the unit.  This malfunctioned in a way that was a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and extensive smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I'm writing to you today to inform you of the explosion I had in my house due to your Mr Coffee Espresso Maker Model # BVMC-ECM260.

I purchased this machine at Walmart about 1 week ago because it was a name I thought I could trust in an appliance and the fact that it was black and stainless steel and matched my kitchen.

On 9/8/13 I took it out of the box for the first time and set it up. I read the instructions and did everything it said to do. I set up the machine and walked to the other side of my kitchen to finish cleaning. The machine starts to pour coffee and I walk back over to the machine. All of a sudden it explodes in my face! Glass hot coffee hot coffee grounds are now everywhere all over me and my kitchen. 

The glass didn't just break the actual filter holder flew off just missing my face and the glass shattered and flew everywhere. I had coffee and glass in my hair and all over my kitchen. From the ceiling to the other side of the kitchen.

My 1 year old daughter was right behind me and thank god she was not touched by anything. I took the full hit. 

I was not harmed enough to seek medical attention but this could have been much worse. I have used a different brand machine for years and have never had this issue. I know I put the filter holder on correctly as I have used many espresso machines. 

After the hour and a half it took to clean my kitchen and myself I sat down to look up why it could happen (which I am still finding coffee and glass everywhere). What do I see but more and more stories of the same thing happening with Mr. Coffee machines. 

Each time all I see is the same response to every complaint please contact us. I want this product recalled. No one should have this happen to them! Some one can get seriously injured and your company having known of the issue for such a long period of time (I see complaints as far back as 2011) could be facing a ton in damages.
justification: The incident resulted in no medical attention required but involved hot coffee and glass exploding, posing significant risk, especially with a child nearby.

incident_description:
Kenmore Wall Oven Model 790.40459802. Last night the oven window exploded, throwing shards of glass as much as 20 feet. It happened just after the handle came off on one side, and then my wife opened the oven a little.  Fortunately the glass flew downward and she was able to jump out of the way. But if she had been in a little different position she would be in the hospital now.  Also fortunate that our curious 4 year old grandson was not watching the oven as he often does. After this happened the floor was filled with glass and there was no more in the oven window.

We had been doing nothing unusual, just using the oven to heat some food.  The window has never been struck with anything.

We called Sears and got nowhere.  We bought the oven in October 2011 and it is out of warranty. But this is obviously a product safety issue.  The ovens should be recalled.

A quick search on the Internet came up with 177 similar complaints about they oven.  

How can Sears be so blasÃÂ©?

Please recall this item before people get seriously injured.
justification: The oven window exploded, causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries occurred. However, the incident could have resulted in serious injury, and there are multiple similar complaints.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that woke up in the morning and she smelled plastic burning. She stated that when she went into the kitchen she noticed the light that states hot surface was on and her pocket book had melted. The consumer stated that she had left pocket book on top of the range and the left rear burner on by itself melting the pocket book. The consumer stated that range was extremely hot to the touch. 

The consumer stated that she pulled the pocket off the burner and since the knob was already on the off position she had to shut off the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that every time the circuit breaker was turned on the burner comes on by itself. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they did not provide any assistance. 

The consumer stated that she believed that her range was posing the same hazard stated on 
Release # 09-333. She stated that she believes that this model should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses.

incident_description: My wife was in the living room when she smelled something burning in the kitchen.  Nothing was cooking and no appliances had been turned on but when she walked into the kitchen the LG Microwave was on fire.  It had started up by itself and caught fire.  She called a neighbor to help with the fire but it went out after a few minutes.  The entire interior of the unit is destroyed.  An LG technician is coming tomorrow to "determine the cause".  The unit is less than one year old and is under warranty.
justification: The microwave caught fire without any user interaction, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wife placed his oven to pre-heat at a temperature of 375 degrees. The consumer stated that his wife heard a strange noise and saw fire being emitted from the convection fan on the back of the wall oven. The consumer stated that he turned off the oven by pushing the ÃÂon/offÃÂ button. He stated that as soon as he turned off the oven the flames went away. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured and there were no damages to the home structure. 

The consumer stated that he could not see any visible damages to the wall oven. 

The consumer stated that he had previously had a problem with the oven, because the glass door had shattered. The consumer stated that the manufacturer replaced the glass door back in 2006. 

The wall oven model was not previously included on any recalls.

The consumer stated that he will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report.
justification: The incident involved flames from the oven but no injuries or structural damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting a 30", four burner gas range purchased in 1997 that on August 10th, 2013, approximately 7:30AM the smoke detectors began sounding in callers' mothers' home where his daughter and grandchildren also live upstairs.
Caller's mother, daughter and his grandchildren evacuated the home and called the fire department.

The fire department was at the home within five minutes, they secured the oven by unplugging it and turning the gas off at the main gas line in the basement.

The caller decided to put the gas range to the test so he plugged the range back into the circuit, went downstairs, turned the gas back on and before he arrived back in the kitchen the oven had turned itself back on and was already very hot with all knobs set at off.

There were no injuries 

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them

incident_description:

Three different times, these knobs where turned without my knowledge and created a fire!  I have contacted Whirlpool, along with the service department and they have insisted there stoves are designed correctly and within industry standards.  Even while on the phone with them, they asked me to turn each know without pushing in on them and behold, one of the knobs turned.  I have told them if they could just put a stiffer spring in the knob, they wouldn't have such a hazard.  Two of the fires were small, but one could have brought down my entire house.  The gas was on for probably two hours without me knowing it and then whoosh, just a click of the knob and I had a very scary situation on my hands.  

I am not a regular internet user, and would welcome a phone call from you.  The State of Minnesota Fire Marshall said I would probably hear back from one of you two investigators.  

Thank you very much for looking into this.  

[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I purchased a kitchen a mandolin slicer yesterday at Costco in Dedham Massachusetts. Last night was the first time I used it.

I believe this to be a terrible product which comes with very poor & vague instructions and safety warnings.

First of all, the first time I tried to slice a tomato, the plastic blade cover broke off. The part that is supposed to hold the tomato was virtually impossible to use. The fresh and firm tomato came out like tomato sauce rather than sliced perfectly as per the instructions in the skimpy 4 page manual as well as verbiage on the box.

The second time I tried to use the product, after attempting to re-install the "Blade safety" cover I tried slicing an onion. Again the plastic safety blade shield broke off and the food holder slider did not hold the onion in place.

The third time I attempted to use it to slice a cucumber, the blade safety cover was broken and the food holder slide was not able to hold the cucumber in place even thought I first cut it in half to provide a more flat surface.

As the product was not working as advertised I attempted to slice the cucumber without the food holder or the blade safety cover. After several slices my pointer finger got sliced off about 3/4 of an inch and was bleeding profusely. 
 
After my family assisted with first aid, I went to the Newton Wellesley Hospital the next morning at which time they termed the would as an avulsion and there was no way to stitch the wound.

As a result of the lack of working safety devices and inadequate instructions, I now will have a permanent disfigurement on my right pointer finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a permanent disfigurement due to a finger injury caused by a faulty product, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: I bought a 4 litter tea kettle from Golden Star Imports Inc., which had a thick base (kettle's base, a thick layer of a metal, and another sheet of metal on top of that). Last night after half an hour when I understood that the kettle has ran out of water, I wanted to put it on the counter, the outer sheet of metal fell on the counter while the thick layer of metal, which was lead, was completely melted and dripping on the counter. Thanks God it didn't drip on my foot because it would have melted my foot all the way to the bone. Is it safe to make the base of a kettle which will obviously be in direct contact with hot stove elements with Lead which its melting point is about 621? I know that the kettle had no water for about half an hour, but this should not happen to a kettle or they should have a warning that says if you leave it on stove without water for half an hour the bottom part of the kettle can melt and create very dangerous situation.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with a melting kettle base, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Purchased Hamilton Beach Coffemaker  Model 43253R [REDACTED] on August 9, 2013.     On the morning of August 21, 2013  went to get pot to make coffee and the pot was hot. touched the warmer plate and it was hot.   The coffeemaker WAS turn OFF.  So I thought!!!  For some unknown reason coffeemaker doesn't work with on/off button.  Not known to me coffeemaker was on all night.  The ONLY way to turn this coffeemaker off is to keep it unplugged.

incident_description: While at home my wife and I could smell something burning. We traced it to the kitchen. We opened  the refrigerator door and smoke came out. We unpluged the refrigerator right away. We traced the trouble to the light assembly, it was so hot we could not touch it. lt had started to melt the plastic above the light assembly and the light lens a little bit. We diconnected the light assembly and removed it. We tried to contact Sears. At first they said they would send someone out to check it, but never did. After awhile we just gave up trying to contact them. This incident occurred around July 2012.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting plastic but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents are unlikely to happen frequently.

incident_description:
The consumerÃÂs husband took out his food from the toaster oven. The consumerÃÂs husband left the door open to let the oven cool. The consumer stated that within 1-2 minutes, the door exploded and the glass shattered everywhere

incident_description:
Text of consumer's letter dated 8/12/2013 to CPSC:

Please check up on the GE refrigerator, model # looks like NO. This was a new appliance installed here by the management when I moved into this apartment in 2007.

This refrigerator has heavy doors that automatically close when I am trying to put something away or take something out. I is  very have to do this and try to keep the door open at the same time. I have been hit on the head several times, especially by the freezer door. Last week I was hit on the side of my head by the refrigerator door. I still have a bruise that is sore and swollen. It could be worse, like a concussion.

Is there any reason for this silly idea that the doors have to close automatically?
justification: The consumer reports being hit on the head multiple times, with a recent incident causing a sore and swollen bruise, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his dishwasher was replaced in 2007 due to a recall.  His spouse had placed the dishwasher in use about 1 a.m and then retired to bed.  She awoke around 7 a.m and noticed a burnt odor she then realized that the odor was coming from the dishwasher which appeared to be still on.  He was alerted by his spouse, he immediately switched off power by using the circuit breaker.

The dishwasher was opened but it was extremely hot , there were some utensils that had melted and got stuck to the basket.  There was also melted plastic at the bottom of the dishwasher.  He feels that the dishwasher overheated causing this incident.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.  The model number of this dishwasher is not included in a recall.

Contacted GE 7/31/13  -Spoke to customer svc and consumer relations. Given case #[REDACTED]. Technician was sent to evaluate damage. (Control assembly, filter or bottom screen & cutlery. basket). Repair estimate for parts, labor, & tax=$362.09. Consumer explained that he did not want what was obviously a faulty & dangerous control assemble which caused the damage and presented a fire hazard to be replaced with the same dangerous part.  Consumer believes that this should be added to the recall #12244.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher overheating, causing damage and a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer sated that the microwave turns itself on. When the microwave turns on, the control panel becomes unresponsive. The only way to stop the microwave is to open the door and pull the plug out. 

This has happened about 3 times.

Last night (07/19/13) when this happened, the consumer stated that he left the microwave unplugged for about 15 minutes.  When he plugged the microwave back in, the microwave immediately started again.

When the consumer contacted the manufacturer to report this problem, the manufacturer informed him to contact retailerÃÂs GE department. The retailer took a report and informed the consumer that the microwave is not recalled. 

The consumer stated that there are no patterns and the microwave starts spontaneously. 

The consumer has left the microwave unplugged.
justification: The microwave turning on spontaneously is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that after placing dishwasher in use the cycle was finished before she retired to bed. She discovered the next morning that the unit and countertop was extremely hot to the touch.  It seems as if the heating element was still on.  The circuit breaker was used to switch power off from the unit.  She feels that she is experiencing similar problems of Release #12-244. Hazard: An electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element can pose a fire hazard.

8/5/13 The firm was contacted and reported the incident.  She is concerned about the fire hazard and is not willing to have them repaired it.

The product model number was not part of a recall.
justification: The dishwasher's heating element remained on, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Combo microwave and Oven
GE Mod J-TP90D P4WW Ser.# GA619775Q
The unit is three months old and functioned fine until August 9, 2013.
We cooked a meal in the Microwave and shut it off upon completion. About an hour later I noticed a buzzing but
could not identify the source. If I opened the door it would stop and restart when the door was closed. After a few minutes of this I noticed an odd odor and opened the door. The rotating plate at the bottom was very very hot which indicated that the microwave gun was activated and was the source of the buzzing. The smell got a lot worse and good deal of heat was coming out of the upper vents. It was obvious that wiring was burning! About then the unit shut off I presume via thermal switch. I immediately went to my panel box and switched the breaker off.
Slowly the heat and odor dissipated.
As this is in a wood cabinet the concern immediately became that this could be a source of a fire. The breaker
remains off.
I called the dealer and service after sale is not in their vocabulary .. Given that this was a new unit with a serious
problem one would think that their reputation demands immediate or at least next day service. Instead I was given two time blocks on Tuesday .. three & one-half days later.
Have you had reports of this nature for this product???
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave with burning wiring and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We bought the LG Refrigerator in September of 2010 and since about 4 months of Sears installing it had nothing but problems.
The Ice and Water from the dispensers started to smell of mildew and mold and the taste of the Ice and Water completely changed.
We complained to LG and they kept telling us that the water filter is bad and we need to change it.
We bought a NEW LG water filter and installed it but No change.
We again called LG to complain and they told us to change the filter again.
We have so far changed 4 filters at $50 each.
Finally,LG Service comes to our home and charges us $75 for the visit plus Tax. The Tech has put in the report to LG and we are waiting for a decision.
All this has been going on since about 3 years!
justification: The incident involves persistent issues with a refrigerator causing mold and mildew smells, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Whirlpool dishwasher

model DU1345XTVQ1

serial number F00507437

Whirlpool logo can seperate and become toddler child choke hazard.

Product is defective and should fall under a safety recall.

Whilpool said they have no reports of this product being a problem

I guess we just have to wait for a few deaths.
justification: The description indicates a potential choking hazard for toddlers, but no actual incidents or injuries have been reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Microwave Oven over my stove malfunctioned. I was using the exhaust fan in the microwave, but not cooking in the microwave itself. I was standing in front of my stove, cooking on the stovetop with the microwave eye level in front of me, when I smelled burning rubber/plastic. Looking for the source, I opened the microwave, burning my hand on the glass turntable plate, which had become unexpectedly and dangerously hot, melting the plastic turntable and roller wheels, and causing the glass turntable plate to bubble up. After I turned down the fan and let it cool, the glass turntable plate broke in half along the bubble that had formed from melting glass. If I had not been standing right there, the microwave malfunction would most likely have set my cabinet on fire.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and potential fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described malfunction.

incident_description:
LG Electric Range was being used in "proof" mode (Target temp 95F) and the oven temperature increased rapidly (<30 min) to well over 650F (measured with IR thermometer) starting a small fire.

The manufacture date of the range is 2006.
The Model number is: LRE20755ST
The Serial number is: 609KMVP00783

Please note this is a separate issue to the existing recall concerning cooktop burners loss of thermal control. The issue in this case is a runaway oven.
justification: The incident involved a small fire due to a runaway oven, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
We have Magic Chef 30ÃÂ Gas Range (Model:  CGR3740ADL;  SN:  15895315WM).  This unit started mal-functioning by beeping and at times LCD clock would fade.  After cycling the power, it would work then stop again.  The clock would beep again at times and instead of clock, it would show dots or lines.  Since we didnÃÂt do much baking, we opted to call a repairman after our vacation.  A few weeks later, a day before our vacation, it turned on the oven by itself.  My mother was home alone reading a religious book, she smelled something burning and by the time she looked around, she saw thick smoke coming from the kitchen area.  She almost had a panic attack and called 911 to have them put out the fire.  Now only god knows what would have happed if this was to occur while we were on vacation. Upon googling this problem online, I found that I am not the only victim.  I am saving this unit for your product safety team to study this unit so that it does not happen to anyone ever again.
I have also sent an email to Whirlpool asking them to study this unit and for compensation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas range that caused a fire, leading to a panic attack but no physical injury.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that he has had no problems with his smoothtop electric range purchased August 2nd, 2007 until the past six to ten months.

Sometime within this time range the front right burner first began staying on when the knob was turned to off and during this time and during cooking time the temperature would fluctuate up and down by itself.

Several months after the first burner began being unable to be turned off or controlled the back right burner began performing in the same manner. 

About one month before this report the back left burner began working only on high, it fluctuates on higher temperatures, doesn't go to lower temperatures.

The back right burner and the left back burner can sometimes be turned off using the knob.

There are no injuries being reported 

Caller contacted the manufacturer in late 2012, then again August 14th, 2013 and was advised that his specific electric range is not recalled but he can pay for repair.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning burners with no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue has persisted over several months, making occurrence likelihood likely (4).

incident_description:
His wife was cooking at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.  She turned off the oven when done baking.   While eating dinner they noticed a bad burning odor.  

The oven was off but the broiler was on and extremely hot.  He had to unplug it from the bottom.  He plugged it back in and the broiler went on.  He tried to research and certain models were recalled but his was not.  If they would have stepped out of the home 


The consumer contacted the manufacturer/retailer who offered a $75 credit for inspection.  The consumer has to pay for the repairs.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven broiler that posed a fire risk but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: Hamilton Beach microwave  model HB-P100N30AL-S3 is dangerous.  It comes on by itself.  This product will definitely cause harm if not removed from the market.  A recall should be placed on this product.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, but the claim suggests it is likely to cause harm if not addressed.

incident_description:
The caller stated that her dishwasher had a hole melted in dishwasher that was leaking for months, that no repair person could discover.  It damaged her kitchen floor, basement ceiling, cabinets and walls.  The hole is located just below the heating element. (8/2012) A service call was done.

2/2013  She had turned the dishwasher on and approximately 30 mins later, while she was in the basement she noticed that there was water pouring in through the ceiling.  She noticed spots of water in smaller areas before but they disappeared.  She realized that the water spots had now developed mold.

2/2013 She contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that they felt that she had loaded the dishwasher incorrectly which could have a caused a metal utensil to melt through.

She contacted her insurance company but her claim was denied stating that the areas were covered by mold.

The caller is concerned that the dishwasher is a safety hazard and have caused property damage in the estimate amount of $12000.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
July 17th, 2013 this caller smelled a burning odor coming from his kitchen.
He went to the kitchen, thought it was the coffeepot so picked it up and took it outside with his wife.
The couple decided that the coffee pot had not been burning but the wife remembered that she had started the dishwasher before she came outside which prompted both the caller and his wife to return to the kitchen.

They had the carpets cleaned this same day so all fans were running which makes it impossible for the caller to distinguish whether there was smoke.
They went immediately to the dishwasher, saw that it was not running, opened the door and were met with a terrible odor but could not visually identify any problem.
He compares the burning odor to that of burning hot wire.
He took the front panel off of the dishwasher to access the control panel and observed where smoke had come out from around the panel, circuit board connectors were melted, the circuit board was charred and melted as well as the underneath of the circuit board being charred and melted.
The underside of his countertop is burned from the heat.
Caller said that it appears that the thermal switch did not work at all because the breaker didn't trip off, the burning continued when it should have been blocked.

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.,
There are no injuries to be reported.

Caller is asking that his model become inspected and repaired at manufacture expense and if he has had to have the unit repaired then he would like to be reimbursed whatever the cost was with this cost being placed at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and damage to the dishwasher and countertop, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: [REDACTED] a female is claiming to being shocked by the LG refrigerator she purchased several years ago. The bulb has been recalled for burning the inside of the refrigerator. She is concerned because she fears this will lead to a fire in her home.
justification: The female claims to have been shocked by the refrigerator, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the recall and her concern about a potential fire.

incident_description: Entered kitchen one morning to find broken glass from the outer oven window all over the floor. I had been out of time for a few days. So, no cooking took place during that time.
justification: Broken glass was found, but no injury occurred as no one was present during the incident.

incident_description:
This incident occurred while I was toasting a bagel in a "Euro-Pro Toaster Over" Model TO1612. This toaster over was bought at the Sears Grand store at the Pittsburgh Mills on May 11, 2011.

I noticed some light blue-white smoke coming out from behind the upper (temperature control) knob. Seeing this I quickly remove the plug and the smoke stopped. Thinking the something may have gotten into the area behind the knobs, I removed the outer metal cover from the toaster over to see if the area needed to be cleaned. However, the area behind the control knobs was clean.

Next I decided to find out what would happen if I turned the toaster over back on. I took it outside to the concrete patio and plugged it in again without changing any settings of the three control knobs. Within a minute or so the backside on the middle control (function: keep warm; broil; bake; toast; grill) burst into flames. I removed the plug and the flames went out.

From what I have observed, this toaster over could have caused a fire if I had not been near-by when the first smoke appeared. I do have a smoke detector in the area so I think I would have eventually been alerted to the problem, but, significant damage may have occurred to my kitchen first.

I have taken some pictures of the toaster over and I will hold onto the over and the pictures just in case you would want me to send them to you for further investigation.

Thank you for your attention,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames from a toaster oven, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the potential for fire if not monitored.

incident_description:
We had exploding glass in the thermal carafe.  I read many good reviews of the Bonavita coffeemaker with the stainless steel thermal carafe and ordered it. We used it almost three weeks. While washing it exactly as described by the manufacturer - just swishing it out with lukewarm water, the thermal glass exploded in my partner's hands and face.  Glass went everywhere. 
I had read isolated incidents of this on the Internet but once it happened I found more than one Web site that has several instances of this. Not sure if you have other incidents reported.
justification: The thermal glass exploded in the partner's hands and face, causing injury from the glass shards.

incident_description: Kitchen/hall area was filled with smoke and electrical burning smell was throughout the area.  Fire department was called and could not find the cause. The next day, when freezer was opened on refrigerator, all items inside were unfrozen. We looked at the compressor on refrigerator, the small white box (relay) on the side of the compressor was burnt. The refrigerator is a Kenmore, model 106.51224100.  The compressor is Embraco EGY 80 HLP.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell without causing injury, and the cause was identified as a burnt relay on the refrigerator.

Kenmore Elite dishwasher model 865.14762300 control panel began smoking and shooting out sparks during a wash cycle.

Purchased September 2004 from Sears
justification: The dishwasher control panel smoking and sparking is a hazardous incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My Kitchenaid (whirlpool) Microwave oven started on it's own.
It flashed " F2 "  and "Pan"
It would not stop unless we opened the door
I unplugged it and plugged it back in and it did it again!

Model KHMS155LBL-3 Serial TRT-06-10479
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by starting on its own, indicating a technical issue, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
We Purchased a Kenmore Elite Refrigerator Model # 795.77546600 around 2008.
It was made for Sears by LG.

We have had many service calls on this refrigerator. The latest one was because the ice maker stopped working. When the Sears tech arrived we asked him why the light diffuser was melting. He took it apart and found that the bulbs didn't turn off when we closed the doors. The inside roof of the refrigerator was melted thru to the insulation. He looked it up and found a ÃÂflashÃÂ or a recall on this. He said that it was so badly damaged that it was beyond repair. He showed us the holes where a sensor should have been installed to correct this problem. He said it could have caused a fire and disconnected the whole light assembly. That model has a history of melting and catching fire.

Two days later Sears called and said that they would allow $500 towards a new refrigerator. She also said we should go to LG if we were no satisfied with that offer. We were not pleased with that call.

We contacted LG and they said that they make that model for Sears and that from that point on it is all up to Sears to take care of it.

Our contention is that Sears should have contacted us about the recall in a timely manner so we could have had it fixed on one of the many service calls. If we were notified we would still have our working refrigerator and not this broken unrepairable one. We contend that Sears is at fault and liable for this situation and should replace this appliance with a comparable one.

It would be financially devastating for us to spend that kind of money to replace something that thru no fault of ours was damaged by Sears carelessness.

Please feel free to contact us if you need any additional information, pictures or the Sears tech's no
justification: The refrigerator was damaged beyond repair, but there was no injury or death.

incident_description: I was heating a stick of butter in this mug in a microwave oven. I had put it in for 40 seconds. When I opened the door and grabbed the handle on the side of the mug I received a burn on my index finger, as the handle was too hot to touch.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the index finger, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My wife bought the:

Deni 16310 Stainless-Steel 1500-Watt Tabletop Single Burner 

 off of Amazon.com
