incident_description:
Caller is reporting electric oven/range that overheated.

Recalled models stop at endings GCA and the serial# VF832 endings so it is not recalled.

July 22nd, 2013 caller and her husband had finished cooking dinner turned the knob to off for the rear left burner but it did not go off.

This happened a few times.

The back right burner knob was set on high but it was actually at only 2 or 3.

When caller's could not turn the range off after repeated attempts they turned the breaker off.

August 1st, 2013th callers were using oven but not the burners when the left rear burner turned itself on, couldn't be turned off without flipping the breaker.

Callers contacted the manufacture red 07/23/2013 but were informed that no help for them was available.

There have been no injuries
justification: The incident involves an electric oven/range malfunctioning repeatedly but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On August 21, I set our GE Profile Dishwasher to Wash at 2:00am.  The dishwasher did not shut off and ran for 13 hours.  It melted all plastic items in the dishwasher.  In addition the silverware is now melted into the silverware cart.
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: I set my oven to bake/350 and in a few minutes, heard it beep to indicate it had reached temperature.  A few minutes after that, I heard it beep 3 times in a row, which I had never heard before, and "E2F3" was displayed on the screen.  I also could smell a weird metallic smell. I looked the code up on the internet and found that others that had seen the code found out that their broilers were on for no reason.  I went back to check my oven, sure enough, the broiler was on and I had not turned it on.  I hit "off" on the control panel but the broiler would not turn off.  I had to flip the breaker to get it to turn off.  I kept it off until a repairman came out a few days later.  When I flipped the breaker, the broiler came on again even though no buttons had been pushed on the control panel.  The only way to get it to turn off was to unplug it.  The repairman found that the range only has 1 relay (he says most have 2) and that it was stuck.  I would need to replace the control board to fix the situation, which, I opted not to do as I'm sure a new one is just as unsafe.  I also called Sears at 1-800-549-4505 to file a report as they have asked in their responses to similar reports on this website. If I had not looked on the internet to learn that my broiler might be on, I would never have checked it as the display indicated all items were "off"!!!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven broiler that could have led to injury, but no actual harm occurred. The likelihood is possible as similar reports exist, but it's not a frequent occurrence.

incident_description: I currently own a GE flat top range. Model # JEP67B0H1WH It's around 8 1/2yo with less then moderate useage. The burner switch wouldn't shut off. My husband took the back cover off to look at the control panel to find that the switch almost caught on fire. We have also reported the problem to GE. They are sending a tech.
justification: The burner switch almost caught on fire, indicating a significant incident but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite range with a glass cooktop.  The center element on the 3 element burner comes on by itself.  There is no pattern to the event hence it is upredicable.  Locking out the cooktop does not prevent it from happening.
justification: The cooktop turning on by itself poses a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I installed a new Sears Kenmore "top-freezer" refrigerator on August 7,2013. I was
happy with the functionality and quality of the  unit, but yesterday, my wife and I independently 
discovered an unexpected risk. When stooping to place or remove items form the refrigerator, the 
freezer handle, which is hard plastic with sharp edges, protruding three inches, is often struck by 
the back of your head as you stand up. This is enough to draw blood! This risk is not obvious 
because the two handles meet smoothly and stylishly when both are closed.  I think the  risk is enough  to warrant a
recall or handle redesign and replacement.  Pictures are attached.
justification: The incident describes an injury (drawing blood) caused by the refrigerator's handle, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high as it was discovered independently by two people during normal use.

incident_description: The glass door in my Kenmore Toaster oven, model 100.8000990A exploded. I had used it about an hour before this happened and it was cool. I was in the next room and heard a crash and found the glass shattered all over the countertop. Looking on line I have discovered that this is not uncommon and many people have reported it, but there does not seem to have been a recall.
justification: The glass door exploded, but no one was injured, so the severity level is 2. The incident is not uncommon, so the occurrence likelihood is 4.

incident_description:
When toasting an [REDACTED] brand waffle in a Hamilton Beach toaster my wife and I began to smell something that we
did not initially attribute to the toaster. When the smoke alarm went off, however, we determined that it was the
waffle. The "wire bread guides" in the toaster open wider than the sheet metal toast slots above. When the waffle was "toasted," the bread guides attempted to lift it, but the waffle caught the edge of the upper sheet metal toast slot, preventing the waffle from lifting and preventing the toaster from shutting off. Had we not been attentive to the situation we could have had a fire caused by a burning waffle or anything in the area heated by the toaster and waffle. This is an unacceptably hazardous design. No injuries or property loss were sustained.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous situation that could have led to a fire, but no injuries or property loss occurred.

incident_description:
Bosch Dishwasher caught fire, electrical panel short circuited.   Model no: SHU33A02UC/17  
I turned on the dishwasher left the house to do some yard work, heard the fire alarm go off in the house. went into the house which was filled with smoke, called 911, grabbed the fire extinguisher and put it out myself before it burned down the house.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke but no injuries, and the fire was extinguished before significant damage occurred.

incident_description:
This is a Fridgidaire electric range that we bought on 12/9/10. The product is FFEF3020LW and the serial number VF01364172. 

Last Friday, the oven would not heat up. Yesterday, 8/18/13, my husband turned on the oven again. It started heating, so he turned it off. Suddenly flames came out of the back of the appliance. Note the the appliance was turned off at this time, though was plugged in. Fortunately he was there, saw the flames, and was able to unplug the appliance. When the flames were extinguished, he took off the back of the range, and saw that the control unit is now burnt out.

Thank goodness we were in the house and could see this. If this had happened at night, or when we were out of the house, it could have been a disaster.

Today I called and reported it to Fridgidaire/Electrolux. Their recommendation was that we call out, and pay for, an authorized service technician to look at the range.
justification: Flames emerged from the oven, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred as the situation was promptly addressed.

incident_description: My Frigidaire Microwave came on by itself.  Luckily my we were home and were able to unplug the unit.  If we had not been home I imagine it would have eventually caught fire.  I searched your site and found other incidents of this same thing happening.  It's Frigidaire model #FGMV173KWA   I contacted Frigidaire and they will not help with repairs or replacing the unit.  They told me the parts alone would cost me approx $150.00  If this is happening to other people it's only a matter of time before someone suffers serious property damage or worse personal injury from this.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred in this instance. The occurrence likelihood is high as similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description: KitchenAid Microwave oven KHMS155LSS-4 will not turn off. Displays error message "INCH". I then disconnected power. I tried to reconnect, but microwave turned on by itself and showed same error message. I disconnected again, now awaiting repair man. Searching the web for suggestions to avoid expensive repair call.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue was managed by disconnecting power.

incident_description:
On 8/15/2013 my wife turned our electric range to cook and heard a sparking sound and smelt smoke, she looked behind the range and saw sparks and flames coming from the range where the power cable came out of it. The range was unplugged and pulled out from the wall. Later when it quit smoking and had cooled down the back of the range was removed to see what was wrong. We found that fire had started in the side of the connector block, (where the power cable connects to the stove) and it had melted one side of the connector block and burnt the wire on it and the wire on the power cable. If my wife had not noticed it as soon as she did I have no doubt that we would have had a major kitchen fire, and since we live about 6 miles from a fire station, the whole house could have burnt down.
The electric range is LG model, LRE30757SW/OO, SER# 803KMSA00134. This model electric range was place on recall last year, 2013 and we were never notified of the recall although the LG Corp had all our information. When i tried to notify the LG corp. of the fire problem and the fact it was on an already recalled range, the only thing they were concerned about was just how i found out about the recall, not the fact that we had a fire. THe only thing i could get out of LG Corp. was that they would send someone to fix what the range was recalled for, they were not interested in the repair of the fire damage and would not look at it when they came. What i am wondering is how can you repair recall problems when there is not way to power the range to do electrical work? This range is a fire hazard and a danger to the user and something should be done to protect the public from it.
justification: The incident involved sparks and flames from the range, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a set of T-fal pans with glass lids for a vacation home approximately six months ago. I might have used the pan in question a total of three times, so they were relatively new. The glass covers were stored in a bottom cabinet. Stacked to the left of the lids, there was a round cake pan, a loaf pan, and on top of the pile a plastic bowl. Somehow, the plastic bowl--and only the plastic bowl--toppled over and fell onto one of the lids (from a height of less then 12 inches) shattering it into a million pieces. Needless-to-say, I was stunned that a plastic bowl falling over from less then a foot could do such damage. 

I cannot help but believe that the lid was defective, and now I'm leery of using the rest of the set. If I had actually dropped the lid on the floor or on my foot, for instance, I would have been cut to shreds as there were so many shards of glass in my cabinet that it took me 1 1/2 hours to clean everything up. 

I wrote to T-fal to let them know what happened, but they insisted it was my fault. The bowl, by the way, only weighs 6.24 ounces. I told them that I wasn't looking for a free replacement of the cover, I just wanted to know if I could have that one repaired, or where I could purchase a new one. I was told there was nothing they could do since it was my fault, and that they didn't sell replacement covers. 

I feel that the covers of the T-fal pans are a huge safety concern. They obviously are not using break-resistant glass, which they should be considering that the pans are used on a daily basis to prepare food.
justification: The incident involved a glass lid shattering without causing injury, but raised safety concerns about the product's durability.

incident_description:
My Kenmore oven, model # 66595014102 and serial #RN0232931, was in use yesterday afternoon to bake bread.  Without any warning, the broiler turned on and caught the bread on fire.  I shut the oven off, only to discover a few minutes later that the oven was continuing to get hotter.  The broiler continued to heat up and glow red hot.  I turned off the breaker.  A few minutes later, I truned the breaker back on, and the broiler turned on again!!  In order to turn the broiler off, I had to unplug the appliance.
My 13 yr old son is home alone through the week when I am at work and makes himself pizza & nuggets in the oven.  I can't imagine what might have happened if this incident had occurred when he was home alone!!!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to injury or fire, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I used the boiler for ten minutes, and pressed "OFF" to turn it off when I was done cooking. However, the heating element could not be turned off and continued to heat. I had not realized that for while until the element became unusually hot. Even the stove top was dangerously hot. We had to unplug the range to stop that. Since then, every time I plug in the unit, the element heats up and there is no way to turn it off. This range is a very dangerous fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning boiler that poses a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Oven would not turn off.  I turned the service breaker off at the power supply panel in my basement.  Waited 10 to 15 minutes and turned it back on.  Oven stayed off for about an hour.  It turned back on by itself.  It did this twice and I decided to keep the main breaker off.  I searched the web to see if this was a common problem and found that Electrolux/Frigidaire had a product recal. 
I called and talked to Electrolux customer service and they informed me that this oven is outside the recall. Since this is a safety issue and not an operation issue I was a little disappointed that they would not correct the manufacturing safety defect with the oven.  I did get in contact with a supervisor and did get a discount on repair parts for it.  I ordered the oven control board and had them add a thermostat since it was not much more.  I talked to [REDACTED] in customer service and [REDACTED] was the supervisor I spoke to.  I can only hope that Electrolux has upgraded the control card so that the oven starting by itself will not be possible to happen again and correct this safety defect in their product. 
I understand that parts fail and appliances require repairs.  But parts should not fail and create such a safety concern when they do.  This is a major engineering fault with their product.
Frigidaire Professional Series Oven/Range
Model PLES389DCE
Ser NF51906507
justification: The oven turning on by itself poses a safety risk, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: On July 25, 2013, our Bosch Dishwasher model SHE43F16Uc/60, Serial # 900500974 caught fire where the wiring harness attaches to the terminal junction block. The fire burned the terminal junction block, wiring harness and extended to the electric supply wiring through our floor. We were very fortunate that we were home and awake when this occured as the burning wire smell alerted us to the fire. Upon investigation by an electrician and a factory service technician, both concurred that the fire originated where the wiring harness attaches to the terminal block due to a loose connection that caused the wires to arc. The factory repair technician indicated that he has seen this failure in other Bosch dishwashers.While Bosch contends that the fire was a result of an installation issue, the dishwasher was installed in July, 2011 without any incident until July 25, 2013.  Also be advised that the terminal block-wire harness connection was factory installed and not to be adjusted by the installer. In fact the installation guidelines make no reference at all to the terminal block-wiring harness connection. The instructions are limited to the instalation of the ground, neutral and hot wire to the terminal screws.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, and the technician noted similar failures in other units, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: My husband had made about 8 cups of coffee and the maker still had about another cup left in it.   The coffee maker had already automatically shut off.   We heard popping noises and went to see why the maker was doing this.  It was smoking from the bottom and when we pulled out the carafe, the burner was turning red.  We unplugged the unit and took it outside.  The counter was hot where the unit had been sitting.   We were lucky that we had been sitting there when the unit started burning otherwise there is no doubt there would have been a house fire.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing smoke and a hot burner, but no injury or fire occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: After 7 years of light use, this stove decided to have an electrical fire behind the back panel.  The wires going into the unit on the power cord melted causing the electricity to spark up under our control panel and burnt other parts.  Would cost a minimum of $465 to fix and perhaps about $800.  What a piece of junk. Sears nor Kenmore would stand behind their product.  They just kept repeating how I didn't buy a warranty.  What a joke!  No oven should catch on fire from faulty wiring, extended warranty or not. Sears has lost my business for life.  This is a safety hazard that should be recalled.  Sears doesn't want to take accountability for their products even when completely defective and dangerous.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and damage to the stove, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore electric oven surface cooking unit suddenly went from low to maximum heat, and would not turn off. Had to go to circuit breaker to turn the unit off, otherwise it could have caused a fire. The affected area was the inner circle of a 3 circle cooking area.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction that could have caused a fire but was mitigated without injury, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite smooth-top electric stove, slide-in with front control panel. 

Model number: 790-46803-991 

Serial number: NF9441xxxx, purchased on 5/1/2000.

Stove burners come on sporadically, after having been turned off.  This identically matches the symptoms that prompted the recall of Kenmore Elite stoves listed at: http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2009/Frigidaire-and-Kenmore-Smoothtop-Electric-Ranges-Recalled-Due-to-Fire-Hazard, originally issued 8/27/2009

The model number of the stove is not included in the range of recalled model numbers, however the symptoms match the recall report precisely:

"Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers."

Online research shows this issue is not restricted to the range of model numbers shown on the recall page, but indicate that the recall should be much broader in scope.
justification: The stove burners turning on sporadically poses a fire and burn hazard, matching symptoms of a recalled model, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
I was taking a dish out of my kenmore stove which I purchased at Sears in Waterbury CT.  When I reached into the oven to get the dish, I banged my leg against the oven door.  It caused me to have a laceration which required 7stitches to close it.  The oven door is surrounded by a very sharp metal edge as is also the bottom drawer of the stove.  I contacted Sears by e-mail because when I called, the person on the phone said this had to be addressed by e-mail.  The person I chatted with said I could not replace the stove but they would repair it, and tried to sell me a package deal for over 200 dollars.  I told him the product was defective and Sears had an obligation to repair or replace this dangerous stove with sharp metal edges.  He then offered to help me for 70 something dollars.  I said I wanted Sears to pay for all repairs since they sod me a defective product.
He said sears would not do this and asked if there was anything else they could do for me!
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring 7 stitches, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The sharp metal edges on the oven door and drawer make similar injuries likely if not addressed (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description: We have purchased the Viking Cooktop, 36inch, NGAS 6B, Model VGSU1646BBK, Serial# 041513C10089665 in May 2013.  The control panel and knobs heat up to the point where one cannot touch the knobs without getting fingers burned while cooking.    We have complained to the Viking, the manufacturer, numerous times but there has not been any resolution.
justification: The incident describes a situation where the control panel and knobs heat up to the point of causing burns, which constitutes an injury, and the issue has been reported multiple times without resolution, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
The product being reported is a GE side by side refrigerator model pcf23ngtd s/n RL428726. Installed 9/2006.
I'm issuing the report because this is the second time this appliance has experienced an electrical fire and I am concerned for my safety.  Furthermore, I have found no on-line recall data for this model and feel there should be.  Fortunately I heard and smelled the start of the fire and was able to prevent any causalties or additional property loss.

I was sitting in my living room at approximately midnight, and heard the sound of loud electrical shorting coming from the general direction of the kitchen. I turned the TV down but the sound stopped.  I went into the kitchen but could not trace the source. There was a distinct smell of burning electrical. The refrigerator was still working. I went through the whole house feeling outlets, circuit panels, and appliances, etc, but could not locate the source.

Reluctant to go to bed, I waited almost another 2 hrs when I heard the sound again.  This time I ran into the kitchen and saw what can only be described as a lightening storm and smoke pouring from under the appliance.  I immediated pulled the unit out from the wall and unplugged it.  The sparking and smoke immediately stopped. I then pulled the rear cover off the unit to confirm there was no fire still smoldering.  There was not.  I am going to be contacting GE on the next buisness day, but this is not about repair/replacement so much as I believe these manufacturers sould be accountable to build appliances which do not go up in flames to which their response is we will repair that after the fact....if your still alive.

Approximately 1 yr ago the main control board also went up in a much smaller electrical short that also resulted in burning to the system board.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with no injuries or deaths, but significant potential for harm.

incident_description: I had made coffee and came into the kitchen. I noticed the power light on the unit was not on even though I had not turned it off, so I pressed the power switch to see if it would turn on again. Nothing happened. I turned to get my coffee cup then noticed and a visible flash from the controls area, like an electrical short. Then I started smelling something burning. The warmer plate started smoking and turning red. I unplugged the unit.
justification: The incident involved an electrical short and smoking, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her microwave caught fire while it was on.  She was using it a few days ago and she noticed that it sparked, she contacted the firm and they told her it was no longer under warranty.  She was also informed to make sure that the unit was cleaned because grease could make it spark.  She cleaned it thoroughly inside and outside and placed a microwaveable bowl inside, within a few seconds she saw a flash of flame.  She immediately unplugged it.  This was the second incident.

7/30/13 She contacted the manufacturer again and was told the same thing that they could not assist her the unit was not under warranty.

The incident left a black soot on the interior wall of the microwave.  She feels that this microwave is a fire hazard and should be reported.

The product is not involved in a recall.
justification: The microwave caught fire, but there was no injury, so the severity level is 2. The incident happened twice, so the occurrence likelihood is 3.

incident_description:
The consumer says that when turning the knob off the toaster oven does not turn off.  Usually a bell rigs when hitting the off spot.  However if you turn the knob too far past the off position, it will stay on.  

The consumer says he does not notice that the unit is on by the time he is ready to clean it or cook something else.  Yesterday he burned his hand.  It has happened to his other family members as well, including his children.

The consumer says their is also no indication of when the unit is on, such as an indication light.  He has had these issue with the toaster oven since he purchased it.
justification: The incident involves burns to the consumer and family members, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue has occurred multiple times with family members, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that they were cooking when they heard a loud bang, like an explosion, coming from the range. The consumer stated that they ran to the kitchen and saw smoke coming out from the back of the range. The consumer stated that they also smelled electric burning.

The consumer stated that he immediately turned off the range and pulled the plug out. The consumer stated that they moved the range outside of their home to prevent fire.

The consumer is not using the range at the moment. 

The consumer stated that he took the back cover off of the range to examine it. The consumer stated that there are wirings that are badly charred in the ÃÂelectronic oven controlÃÂ (in the back of the oven). Consumer stated that the electronic oven control has part #: ES565

The consumer stated that he believes this model is a fire hazard. This model is not included in recall.
justification: The incident involved a loud bang and smoke from the range, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
ÃÂPresto PopLite Hot Air Corn Popper model# 04820
Purchased in April of this year - the transparent plastic top and measuring device/butter melter melted. Nothing was in the butter melter. It was about the 2-3 batch of popcorn in a row (making a larger quantity for a recipe) but still did not expect it to get hot enough to melt the plastic.
justification: The plastic parts melted during use, indicating a product failure, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I dropped my knife on the floor and a circular chip came out of the middle of the blade.
justification: Dropping a knife caused damage to the blade but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Electric Stove from Sears in August of 2007.  On July 30, 2013, at approximately 11:15 p.m., I heard a noise in the kitchen, when I went to check what happened I discovered that the glass on the oven door had shattered and there was glass all over my kitchen floor.  I had not used the stove at all on the 30th, nor was I even in the kitchen when this happened.  After speaking with Sears, I felt that they thought I had somehow caused this glass to shatter.
justification: The glass shattered without any injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: GE Microwave turns on by itself. Will stop when door is opened but has been found to be running a couple of different times with no input from users and no food in oven. Have been standing in kitchen doing dishes when it just turns on by itself. I can still use it but I must unplug it after every use as I can't always be there to shut it off it if starts on its own.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she preheated her oven to 375 degrees for about 30 minutes.  She placed the meat in the pan and marinated for 30 minutes and placed in the oven.  After 40 minutes she removed the pan from the oven.  

The dish exploded while in her hand as she was walking towards the counter.  She was not injured.  She said that the unit shattered in many pieces and exploded and there is nothing left of it.
justification: The dish exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: On July 28, 2013 I purchased an 18 piece set of Pyrex from my local Costco (703653 item #).  During week, I cooked some cabbage and put remaining leftovers in the square Pyrex piece. On Friday, August  2, I was cooking a dinner of surf and turf for my husband, mother and myself. I decided to have the cabbage leftovers as a vegetable to go with our dinner. As I wasn't sure if the Pyrex could go into the microwave for reheating, I goggled the question on my [REDACTED]. Basically it read that Pyrex could be used for heating in the microwave. However as I read other sources, the subject of Pyrex shattering also came up. I decided I didn't want to take a chance so I took out half of the cabbage and microwaved it in another bowl. The Pyrex and the extra cabbage was left sitting on the countertop, untouched. As we had just sat down to dinner, there was a loud bang of glass shattering behind me. We turned around and the Pyrex container had literally exploded/shattered sending glass everywhere. This piece of Pyrex  had not been heated at all, as a matter of fact it was still cold from the refrigerator. The only heat in the room was a little humidity from boiling corn on the cob approximately  12 feet away. We had cooked both the filet and lobster on our outdoor grill. As dinner was late in the evening, I waited to call the manager at Costco until Saturday morning. I gave him the item #703653 and told him what had happened so he could take the product off the shelves. I returned the Pyrex with some other items on Monday morning and again mentioned to refer the returned pyrex to the manager, as a safety precaution. Please see enclosed picture that I will be sending to you. Note: I tried attaching photo that I had taken, if you don't receive photos with this report, please contact me and I will send you the 3 photos that were taken of incident.
justification: The Pyrex container shattered without causing injury, but it posed a potential hazard due to glass shards.

incident_description: My son was drinking out of  the spill proof cup and put it down. He then fell forward onto it and bruised /punctured right underneath his eye.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruise/puncture under the eye, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that knobs on the oven are over sized. The consumer stated that even bumping up against the knobs turn the burners on. The consumer stated that sometimes the gas ignites and other times it only leaks. The consumer stated that this problem started soon after purchase.

Last night (8/5/13), the consumer stated that her whole house was filled with gas. She was woken up by her dog. The consumer stated that she opened all of the windows and turned on the ceiling fans to let the gas escape.

Consumer put older knobs from her previous range on to the new range about a week after the purchase. The older knobs are smaller. The consumer stated that the incidents still occur but less frequently with the smaller knobs.

The consumer contacted the manf today (8/6/13) and they informed her that this was a known problem. The consumer was informed to go purchase safety knob protectors. The consumer stated that the manf should provide the safety knobs if this is a known problem. 

The consumer stated that she still uses the range but is extra cautious. 

There are no recalls on this model.
justification: The incident involves gas leaks and potential ignition, posing a serious hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Our dishwasher (KitchenAid Model KUDP01ILWH2, Serial # FP3909822) was in use during the early afternoon of 12 July 2013. I was at a business meeting and my teenage son was home. Partway through the cycle, my son heard noises while he was in the Family Room, which is adjacent to the Kitchen. As he began to look for the source of the sounds, he noticed smoke accumulating in the Kitchen and Family Room area. Upon further investigation, he noticed smoke coming from the dishwasher. He called me on the phone at my meeting and advised the dishwasher was smoking. No flames were observed, but he did hear noises. 

As he opened the door to stop the cycle, the machine continued to operate; the cycle did not stop as was expected. I instructed him turn off the dishwasher at the local disconnect switch by the kitchen sink. When he did so, the dishwasher did stop operating. My son opened the house to air out the plastic smell (and also removed our pets, including his leopard gecko, which is very sensitive to smoke). 

Discoloration and distortion of the plastic housing on the door of the dishwasher can be clearly seen in the vicinity of the control panel. The dishwasher door has discoloration above and below the control panel (see photos provided), and there is a "bubble" in the door plastic that has formed below the controls. The "bubble" is approximately the size of a U.S. nickel (5-cent piece). 

The unit remains powered off and is no longer used. The unit's door has *not* been opened to view the actual control panel, but the access panel to water and electrical supplies has been removed (below the door) in preparation of either repair or removal.
justification: The incident involved smoke and discoloration but no injuries or flames, and the situation was controlled without further escalation.

incident_description:
The consumer says her daughter was finished cooking and turned the burner off.  They sat down to eat when the smoke alarms went off and flames shot out of the front burner.  The consumer says that the overhead exhaust fan was completely destroyed. 

The consumer says that her daughter had only been cooking 20-30 minutes in the oven.  She says they never had an issue with the range prior to this incident.  

The consumer says that she contacted the manufacturer and filed a claim.  She was told the unit was made by Frigidaire.  She contacted them and was referred back to the branded company(Kenmore) to speak with their Liabilities and Claims Dept.  She filed a claim with them. 

She experienced the same problems as listed in the recall (Release # 09-333).  Her model number is not included in the recall.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not rare but not frequent either.

incident_description:
I have a Black and Decker Infrawave toaster oven.

I received a call from my fire alarm company. I come home and the firefighters was at my house and they tell me that the small oven in my kitchen was on and red and then, they put it outside in the backyard.

The oven was on, very hot. The power button and lights was off and when I unplugged it, the heating element went off. When I plugged it back in the heating element fires up. A lot of smoke in the house and almost burned my house.
justification: The oven malfunctioned, causing smoke and nearly burning the house, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Glass oven door on my 5-6 yr old Kenmore oven suddenly shattered for no apparent reason. Was baking a the time but only at 350 degrees. A friend directed me to a news report on-line that said this has happened with some frequency with Kenmore ovens.

Thanks.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the mention of similar frequent incidents with Kenmore ovens.

incident_description:
The consumer stated this gas range is designated to be a house fire in waiting and should be taken off the market.
Opposite to every range, gas/electric, the controls work in reverse.
Full ccw, the normal off position, is not off, it's the simmer position.
Full cw, the normal on position is not on, it's the off position.
Even under constant vigil, simmer has been on parts of the day, overnight, and for 2 weeks vacation.
Incidents include: pot fires, flaming aluminum frying pan that melted bottom of pan, and regular smoke alerts.
justification: The description reports incidents like pot fires and smoke alerts, indicating actual incidents but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Product: Sears Kenmore Dishwasher
Model:  665.16469300
Serial #: FR1005983

On 8/12/2013 our dishwasher had smoke and fire coming out of the front control panel.  After opening the dishwasher door, the unit continued to run, smoke, and throw fire out the front panel.  We immediately shut the circuit breaker off to the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved smoke and fire but no reported injury, and such events are uncommon but documented.

incident_description: The glass on my Kenmore Oven door shattered for the 2nd time - SECOND TIME......I finished getting ready for work and came downstairs. When I entered the kitchen, i saw the front glass of my oven door was shattered and glass was all over the floor. The oven had  not been used in over 48 hours.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, causing a mess but no reported injury.

incident_description: Brand new 2013 GE Adora Gas Range. Knobs are easily turned on. If you barely bump them they spin and allow gas to flow. Contacted GE Customer Support and they said nothing they could or would do.  We now have a $1000.00 range sitting in our kitchen with the knobs off for safety.
justification: The incident involves a gas range with easily turned knobs, posing a risk of gas leakage, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: I  was using the munchkin chop and steam baby food preparation unit. It has metal cross cut blades to first chop vegetables and fruit before they are steamed. I used it today to chop sweet potatoe and after I had finished I found many pieces of white plastic in the chopped sweet potatoe. The plastic had been shaved from the piece that pushes the food through the blades. on closer inspection of the food, approximately 10-15 plastic shards of about 1/8 & 1/4 inch long pieces were mixed with the food. I have used this product once before and fed the batch to my baby over the last week, I'm obviously worried that he has previously ingested these plastic fragments, before I realized the product was faulty/dangerous. I have images of all of the equipment and the plastic shards if you want me to provide them. I will also keep the pieces of plastic for when I contact the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involves plastic shards in food, which could potentially harm the baby, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My Frigidaire microwave model number FFCM0934LW bought in 2010 caught on fire inside today (August 12, 2013) when my friend was microwaving 2 sausages on a paper towel and we had to junk the microwave because it is too dangerous.
justification: The microwave caught fire but no injury was reported, only property damage.

incident_description:
Order# [REDACTED] from Amazon.com--a Primula glass teapot, 40 oz., advertised as microwave safe.  Notification below just sent to Amazon.

Dear Amazon,
I'm not asking for replacement or return, but want Amazon to know of a safety issue with the product-- a glass teapot made and sold under Primula brand. Though listed as dishwasher and microwave safe, the entire handle simply separated from the pot as I was pouring microwave-heated tea on Sunday, leaving a hole in the side of the glass pot as it fell to the table. 
   I had only a couple of small burns from sloshes hot tea and two tiny finger cuts (like paper cuts, so not serious) from the ragged edge  where I picked it up after it fell--very lucky. The main part of the pot did not break-- It appeared the handle bond just failed with no warning-- apparently from cumulative microwave use..?
   I will be happy to send a photograph to you or the maker, but definitely recommend you remove the "microwave safe" from the product listing and warn the maker. I will do a review (my first) to share the warning, but worry about others who already have purchased. In was fortunate to be at the table when pouring, but others could have the thing smash down and drench them in scalding tea.
Thanks,
[REDACTED]
Main email address: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns and small cuts, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of cumulative microwave use leading to handle failure.

incident_description: I came home from work last Wednesday to find the oven light on and the oven warm.  I live alone and no one else was in the house.  Since I leave the house early in the morning, I certainly would have noticed the illumination from the oven light.  This is a very scary thing and I have flipped the breaker off for the oven and after reading some of the other complaints, am fearful of having the oven fixed.
justification: The incident involved an unexpected oven activation with no injury or damage reported, but it caused fear and required action to mitigate risk.

incident_description:
Occassionally the front left burn will not shut off when the indicator on the display shows off.
There is also a "clicking" noise in the display portion of the stove when all burners are off.  
I am fearful of having the stove catch on fire!
justification: The burner not shutting off poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: We have a 2006 Bosch dishwasher (model # SHX43C05UC). The control panel went out on it recently and it would no longer start. We tinkered with the machine and got it to work again temporarily. When it stopped working again we found the user manual and took the face off to see if we could figure out what part needed to be fixed/replaced. Upon opening the machine a metal box in the bottom right corner was visibly singed. We took the box off and it revealed electrical wiring. The wires were also singed. Upon moving the wires (only slightly) the wires sparked and caught fire. Thankfully we keep a fire extinguisher in the kitchen and were able to extinguish the fire (creating quite a mess). We have turned the breaker that runs to the dishwasher off until we can get it removed or replaced, but this is a terrifying incident. Our regular habit was to run the dishwasher at night immediately before bed. We have a five month old baby. incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Dishwasher, Model 655.17032400, Serial Number: FR3601375, on October 17, 2004 at a Sears store in San Rafael, CA. Original receipt receipt shows I paid $461.

On August 7, 2013, without warning, the dishwasher's control panel caught fire while in use.  The circuit breaker didn't trip. I extinguished the fire by smothering it.  Acrid, white smoke continued to pour out of the dishwasher through the vent holes for 15 minutes, despite the control panel unit being fried to a crisp.  Although I was home when the control panel burst into flames, I was actually on my way out the door when I heard strange noises emitting from the kitchen: clanking, knocking and hissing.  I was alone in the home so I went to investigate the noises.  This is when I discovered the dishwasher on fire.

Later, I phoned Sears' 800 number to inquire about any recalls for this model. Two reps denied any recalls for my dishwasher, however, they happily offered to sell me a replacement control panel for $124.  I declined, stating I thought a pro-rated amount would better indicate a show of good faith on their part, but they declined, saying essentially that they were not responsible for the (sealed) control panel catching fire, especially since, as they claimed, there were no reported issues for this problem.

I have since come to find that in fact, Kenmore, Kitchen Aid, and Whirlpool, all under the same umbrella, have documented histories of their respective control panels catching fire (see kitchenaidfire.com).
justification: The dishwasher's control panel caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I have owned a Pyrex 2-cup glass measuring cup (contemporary- uses modern logo) for more than three years.  I use it to brew tea in place of a teapot.  This morning I filled it with boiling water as usual to brew tea, poured out the tea three minutes later, and left it sitting on its usual place on the counter while I made breakfast.  About an hour after preparing the tea, when the Pyrex was cooled to room temperature, I heard a sound like the crack an ice cube makes when it's dropped in water, followed by the sound of shattering glass.  I turned around to find the Pyrex cup had simply exploded.  Three quarters of it was sitting on the counter, shot through with cracks, and the rest of it including the large solid glass handle were strewn around the kitchen.  I was alone at the kitchen at the time and can confirm nobody bumped it and nothing fell into it.  The remains of the Pyrex continued to crack into smaller and smaller pieces as I watched.  I draped a plastic bag over it in case it exploded again and waited for several minutes before sweeping it up.  It was not near a heat source and all the fragments were room temperature.

I have used Pyrex products for more than ten years to brew tea and have never had a spontaneous explosion like this.  I feel very lucky I was not facing or using the Pyrex when this happened.  I expect Pyrex products to be durable and not to explode for no apparent reason.
justification: The Pyrex cup exploded without causing injury, and the user has never experienced this issue before in ten years of use.

Regarding:  Electrolux Smoothtop Cooktop Model: FPEC3685KSA

After cooking pasta for my family a few nights ago using 2 of the 5 burners for about 20 minutes, I was about to walk outside to join them when I noticed a slight burning smell.  The burners were all in their off position and the indicator lights all indicated that the burners were turned off.  I moved one of the pans to find that one of the small inner burners was on at full blast.  I tried to turn it off by turning all of the knobs, but nothing was working so I opened the cabinet under the cooktop hoping to unplug the unit.  At that point, a plume of smoke came out from under the cooktop and a strong stream of smoke was emerging from under the unit.  Unable to unplug the unit that is hardwired to the wall, I ran outside to flip the breakers.

Last night, I opened up the unit to see that that some of the plastic/wiring was badly burned with scorch marks all over one of the circuit boards.

I feel very fortunate that no one got hurt and that my home is still standing.  Given the nature of the problem I could easily have left the house without realizing that the stove was still on.  Also given that the unit is hardwired to the wall, if my wife or babysitter had been the ones this had happened to they would not have known how to flip off the circuit breaker and the kitchen would almost certainly have caught fire. 

I hope this note has been helpful.   I would be happy to send photos of the burnt circuit board if that would be helpful. 

Thank you, 
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I was baking bread and muffins in a JennAir dual fuel double oven range model jdr8895aas. I happened to have  both ovens going at the same time with very moist doughs in each so the steam that vents  from just below the control panel on the top of the range was more pronounced than usual. I heard an arcing sound like you hear when someone is welding, and I noticed this light coming from the digital control panel. The sound lasted about 2 seconds when  flames started coming from the  back of the digital control panel. I ran to the garage and flipped off the breaker. I went back inside the kitchen and opened the patio door to let the smoke out. It smelled of burning plastic. When everything had cooled down I removed the back panel on the stove and saw the electrical connectors at the control board were blackened and fused along with the wires leading from the ovens and that the baffle that supposedly separates the oven vent from the control panel has two gaps one at either end. This allows steam and heat from the oven to enter the area of the control panel. So in effect they let heated steam run across live electrical circuits.I believe it was the steam from the use of both ovens at the same time that caused the arcing to start.
It's like venting a clothes drier  through a desktop computer. Sooner or later something bad is going to happen and in my case it was nearly a very very bad thing. If I had not been standing right in front of the stove the kitchen could have started on fire and I could have  lost my house . Instead I only lost a 2000 dollar stove. These thing should be recalled and redesigned so that  they are not vented across the control board.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to steam exposure to electrical components, but no injury or death occurred, only property damage.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Elite Dishwasher was  running and flames and smoke started to come out on the upper right hand side of the door below the control panel. My wife opened the door and the flames and smoke stopped within a few seconds. We closed it again to shut it off but within seconds,you could see a bright red glow behind the white plastic front door cover over the control panel on upper right hand side. Opening the door caused the glow to stop within a few seconds.
Called Sears and reported this and someone is to contact us.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Sunday I made marshmallow [REDACTED] treats at 9am in the microwave; pressed the warm treats with my bare hands into the 9X13 Pyrex baking dish.  The dish with treats went to a noon picnic, came home around 5pm and was placed on a granite counter top where it sat, untouched until about 8pm.  At that time, with no one in the kitchen, there was a loud bang and crash.  We came in to find the 9X13 baking dish in pieces all over the counter, sink and floor.  There were big and small pieces, long sharp shards and a lot of small pieces and slivers everywhere.  I had heard of the exploding Pyrex phenomena but didn't really believe it.  I am a believer now!
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding Pyrex dish) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that when she woke up in the morning, she noticed that the oven door glass (the middle one) had shattered all over the kitchen floor. The oven was turned off overnight, and the consumer and her husband had last used the oven 3 weeks prior to the incident. The consumer stated that the outside and the inside glass to the oven door are fine, just few scratches on its inner sides from the middle glass shattering.
The consumer stated that there are still some shards of glass stuck in between the outer and inner glasses. Also, she stated that the clips holding the middle glass are visible and there is a lot of space between the outer and inner glasses.

The consumer has not used the oven since the incident occurred. 

The consumer stated that the retailer's technician came out to see the oven. The consumer was informed by the retailer that she would have to pay for the inspection fee of $185 if the glasses are still intact since the consumer does not have a warranty on the product. If the glasses are not intact, the retailer would not charge her an inspection fee.  After inspection, the technician told the consumer that she would have to pay the bill since the outer and inner glasses were still intact. The technician also told the consumer that they conducted middle glass replacements all the time, and it is not a safety hazard to use the oven without the middle glass. The technician also informed her that if she wants to use the oven she may do so since the outer and inner glasses were still intact.

The consumer also stated that there are visible wires underneath her oven. The consumer was told by the retailer's technician that the visible wires are normal. The consumer does not trust the words of the technician. 

The consumer also contacted the fire marshal of her city and he informed her to not use the product even though the technician informed her that she could. The fire marshal told the consumer that there could be explosion or fire if she used the product. The consumer stated that the fire marshal is supposed to come out and look at her oven. 

The product is not included in any recalls.
justification: The incident involved shattered oven glass but no injuries occurred, and the fire marshal's warning suggests potential but unconfirmed safety hazards.

incident_description: Samsung Over The Range Microwave SMH9187ST.  Three years old. Error Message -SE- on keypad.  Incessant beeping once error occurs.  Will reset after removing plug and plugging back in.  Error comes back within a few hours rendering microwave unusable. Once error message -SE- starts microwave can turn itself back on and cook without notice.  My oven went on all by itself without my touching it and apparently was on for about four hours without my knowing it.  Oven was hot to touch on exterior, interior was untouchable, as hot as a gas oven, interior shelving burned my hand.  Very dangerous and very scary. At first Samsung says they don't have any issues reported with this model and that it is out of warranty and a repairman will come at owner's expense. I pushed for a different result and spoke to Executive Customer Relations, where the response changed. Samsung is indeed aware of problem (and so is the web), but will replace keypad only.  This model should be pulled from the marketplace. Owners should be given a replacement or refund, not just a keypad replacement.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, turning on by itself and causing burns, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I was cooking a pork tenderloin in my 11x7 glass Pyrex dish, which I have done many times in the past.  After the dish had been in the oven cooking for about 35 minutes, I went to take it out of the oven to check on the pork.  Midway between grabbing it in the oven with a potholder and placing it on top of the oven, I heard a popping noise and the glass completely shattered in my gloved hand.  The pork fell to the floor and glass pieces and shards went all over my kitchen (floor, counters, stove top, table, etc..).  My 14 month old son was standing in the kitchen with me and, although he was a safe distance from the oven, he was amidst all of the glass.  Luckily and thankfully he was not hurt.  He is traumatized though as he points to his feet and the oven a lot since it happened.  Pyrex is a popular household name and I would not expect this to happen.
justification: The glass shattered causing a mess and potential hazard, but no injuries occurred despite the presence of a child.

incident_description:
She noticed the range turn on by itself today.  She says that they were set all the way up too high.  She said it was constantly changing numbers on the digital display and she could not turn it off.  She had to shut off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: My electric oven (Frigidaire model # FEF376ASE Serial #VF21210278) turns on and starts heating.  The only way to stop the oven from continuing to heat up is to turn the electrical breaker off.  As soon as the breaker in turned back on, the heating elements in the oven come on.  Luckily, I was home & awake when the serious fault occurred.  This is a major fire hazard that can cause both property damage and loss of life.  I have submitted this information to Frigidaire today but have not heard from them yet.  From the responses on the internet, it sounds like they are aware of this issue but because such ovens are out of warranty they are not concerned.

incident_description:
Make:  GE
Model: JGB281SER5SS
Serial: AA237586P
We have purchased a new range to replace one that broke down, that has been in the exact same spot in our kitchen for almost 7 years.
Within days we kept noticing gas smells, and we figured out they were coming from the new range due to the following cause.
ALL 4 of the knobs on this range are easily turntable, meaning there is almost no resistance when trying to turn the knob (where as normally a knob needs to be pushed in, and the turned) and being that it was so easily turntable, a simple walk to a cabinet or counter-top near the range - would turn the knob (or some time more then 1 - or more knobs) ON where as GAS was coming out of the burners un-be-known to the person walking by!! Typically the knobs would only move a bit (say approximately to the 10 o'clock position) causing just gas to come out, but short of engaging the automatic flame starter spark - therefore the action was silent, and went unnoticed for long periods of time, until the GAS smell became apparent, and in most cases, the occupants had no sense of smell of GAS, since the gas gradually entered the atmosphere, and only when someone came in from the OUTSIDE, did they announce the strong smell of GAS in the house.
THIS IS VERY DANGEROUS SITUATION, ESPECIALLY WITH CHILDREN IN OUR HOME!!
We have attempted several times to resolve this with GE (consumer relations) and they have dispatched numerous technicians to our house - and each technician - although some acknowledged our safety issue,  failed to resolve it, as their only ability was to repair an issue with the "functionality" of the range, and being that they perceived the range to function properly (cook / bake food etc) - they told us that this was out of a serviceman's capability, and left without resolving our huge SAFETY concern!! 
We have made many calls and voicemails to GE consumer relations personnel,  and pleaded for them to replace the unit due to SAFETY concerns - but all they can offer was for us to PURCHASE a new one!!
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to faulty knobs, posing a significant safety risk, especially with children present, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: I have a ge microwave hood, model jvm1730dm1bb.  We were reheating a burrito, using the 30 second button.  My husband left the room to put something away.  When he returned, the microwave was on fire.  The inside is burned, and melted.  Before I purchase another microhood, I wanted to find out if this microwave is under recall.

incident_description: I went to wash the "The Pampered Chef Ice Cream Scoop" when all I heard was a very loud bang.  The scoop had exploded. My right ear started feeling like everything was muffled, like someone was holding a thick towel against my head.  My head started hurting and still does today and I felt sick to my stomach. incident_description:
I purchased the Ninja Mega Kitchen System 1500 8 Cup Blender in June of 2013.  Recently I decided to use the food processor for the first time so I removed it from the box.  After removing the plastic wrapping and the sticker from around the food processor I pressed the lid release button that holds the lid to the food processor on.   The lid wouldn't open up easily so I tried to use both thumbs to apply more force to the release button.  As I did that, the lid came off, the food processor fell on it's side on my kitchen counter, and the food processor blade came rolling out of the food processor, right on top of my left foot.  I immediately fell to the floor,with intense pain (as I could no longer stand up)  and my kitchen floor became covered in blood.  

The blades in the food processor were not packed in securely like the blade in the blender was.  It literally was just sitting in the food processor unsecured. The blades in the food processer were not secured properly and I was completely unaware that the blades were exposed in that manner.

I was rushed to the emergency room and received treatment which included wound irrigation, Tetanus shot, antibiotics shots, multiple anesthesia shots directly around the wound area.  The end result was 6 hours of emergency room and hospital time, 16 stitches in my left foot, a completely severed tendon to my left toe that had to be reattached, and loss of feeling in the foot and several toes.  I am on crutches for the next 4 to 6 weeks, then in a cast/walking boot, and after that headed for rehabilitation to insure that I'm able to walk correctly after all of this heals according to my Dr.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury including a severed tendon, stitches, and loss of feeling, requiring extensive medical treatment and rehabilitation.

incident_description:
In October 2007, we ordered a Kitchen Aid Single Stove Model #KEBS107SSS, Serial from Sears.  In June 2008, the appliance was installed in our new home.  We paid extra for the 3 year warranty, even though we felt it should not be necessary for a major appliance.  

On November 15, 2012, we called Sears to repair the oven.  The oven would not heat up after it was cleaned using the self-clean function.  The repair man replaced the thermostat and recommended to never use the self-clean function as the oven will not work again.  I did not listen to his advice; because I purchased the oven with self-clean to use it, not to clean the oven manually.  Also, I understand there was a recall on a similar Kitchen Aid oven with the same thermostat problem!

On July 16, 2013, the oven would not heat up again after the self-clean function was used. We contacted the Sears repair office and the next available appointment was 7 days out.  The repair office stated an oven with similar features, but not the same oven was recalled for the same, identical problem.

We wrote to Sears Holding Corporation and directly to Kitchen Aid.  At this point, we aren't sure what else we can do.  We are afraid to use the self-clean again.  And why should we have to clean the oven manually when we paid top dollars for this appliance.  Do all in-wall ovens have the same problem?  Please advise where we can go to get this oven replaced. from our Sears customers.  We apologize for the inconvenience you have

[REDACTED]
Sears Holdings Corporation

incident_description:
**POTENTIAL CAUSE OF FIRE**
Kenmore Elite Microwave Oven:  model 721.66463500

This microwave started running without any operator input, without anyone even in the room with it.

It activated and started running on its own.

Thankfully I was home, walked in the kitchen, heard it running, and was able to stop it.  It was so hot I could not pick it up to remove it.  If I had not stopped it, it could have burned my house down, being surrounded by wooden cabinetry.

The control panel was replaced approximately 2011 by Sears after failing to function.  The unit was first purchased in Dec 2006.  The brand is Kenmore "Elite".  Obviously it is not "Elite" in any respect.

The control panel input has obviously shorted out again but this time activating spontaneously. 

Touch sensitive electronic control panels do not mix well with heat and humidity.  That is a well established fact.  A return to old type control knobs and push buttons would make for safer and longer lasting appliances.

Putting sensitive push button control panels on items with high heat and humidity is moronic, and in this case, imperiled life and property.  

I've heard that doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result is the definition of stupidity.  That's what I think these touch sensitive controls are on appliance with high heat and humidity are...stupidity.

incident_description:
In November 2012 we purchased a General Electric "Adora" Gas Range, installed by Home Depot.
Model Number: JGB605SET2SS
Serial Number: VZ200406P
Made in: Mexico

This range has an Oven, and also five (5) gas burners for cooking.  There are five (5) burner controls on the front of the range.  Each of them, if turned on, actuates the electronic starter to ignite the gas flame.  However, if the controls are turned (CCW) too quickly, the ignition does NOT occur but the gas is actuated to the burner. Each of these conrtols must be pushed, before turning them in the CCW direction to use the gas burners.

Our issue is with the two controls which activate the two REAR burners.  These seem to require nearly NO pressure to indent, rotate and engage the burners.  On Friday, 7/19/2013, I entered the kitchen and smelled gas.  The stove had the control for the RIGHT REAR burner rotated about 45 degrees CCW and gas was flowing, but there was NO flame!

Investigation revealed that another household member had used the Microwave (mounted as a Range Hood above the stove) and apparently had leaned against the front of the stove, inadvertently activating the right rear burner so quickly as to not have the electrical spark ignition!  In my opinion, this gas release could have resulted in a major household explosion if any detonation sparks had occurred after a longer time (if undiscovered).  

As a short-term solution, I have fabricated plastic 'inserts' to fit beneath the two Rear Burner controls which prevent them from being 'pushed' until the inserts are removed.

In my opinion, the manufacturer should change the design of these "push-to-activate" controls such that a much stronger spring requires considerably greater pressure to activate the gas burners!
justification: Gas release without ignition poses a risk of explosion, but no actual injury or explosion occurred.

incident_description:
My wife owns a Cuisinart Food Processor about six months old. ÃÂ I was helping my wife in the kitchen. ÃÂ I removed the basin from the motor base to pour out the semi-liquid contents into a storage container. ÃÂ As I poured about half the contents in the bowl the razor sharp blade fell out bounced off the counter and landed on the top of my right foot. ÃÂ I am aware that the blade just sits by gravity onto the motor shaft. ÃÂ However, when the basin is full you can't see the blade. ÃÂ I was so surprise and disgusted with myself to see the blade literally shoot out and bounce off the counter.

It was late at night. ÃÂ The cut was very deep in the top of my foot on the highest point in line with my big toe. ÃÂ A compression bandage stopped the bleeding after losing 750cc of blood. ÃÂ I went to my doctor who butterflied and redressed my wound. ÃÂ It has been two months and my big toe is no longer controlled by the flexor tendon. ÃÂ It appears my Flexor hallucis longus tendon was either severed or damaged so badly I can't lift my toe. The flexor tendon does not pull up making a ridge like it does on my uninjured left foot.

I believe that having a razor sharp blade held in place only by gravity, in a container designed to be tipped over to transfer processed food, is dangerous. The blade should be mechanically held in place to resist falling out. ÃÂ It makes no sense that you need to blindly reach through the processed food, that obscures the razor sharp blade only held in place by gravity, before you pour out the contents safely. ÃÂ 

My foot will likely never be the same. ÃÂ I have intermittent sharp pain across the deep scar in my right foot. ÃÂ I would not consider surgery to repair the injury. ÃÂ Surgery could make it worse. ÃÂ The biggest bummer is the effect my injury has on my passion for rock climbing. The big toe strength is essential for free climbing. I am optimistic over time it will get better some or I'll learn to compensate for the reduced big toe strength. ÃÂ 

Please fix this problem with your food processor. ÃÂ Good Design does not cost much. ÃÂ Engineers, like myself, and manufacturers, like Cusiniart, have a duty to protect the public. ÃÂ As a licensed California Structural Engineer I take that responsibility very seriously.ÃÂ 

[REDACTED]ÃÂ
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut and tendon damage, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the blade falling out is a known risk but not frequent.

incident_description:
I had a glass casserole dish explode on Monday night, May 27.  The dish was given to me probably more than 10 years ago and was part of a set.  The dish which exploded was approximately a 2 quart, rectangular dish, with sides about 2 inches high.  It exploded inside the oven and no one was harmed.  The events related to this are below:
Earlier in the evening I removed a stick of frozen butter and put it in the dish on the counter.  It probably stayed there 30-60 minutes.
I pulled another item out of the oven (thinking it was done) and placed the dish with the butter in the oven (to melt the butter).  The oven was probably set at 350-360 degrees.
After a few minutes, I realized that the other item was not done, so I removed the dish with the butter and set it on the (glass) stovetop (which was warm to the touch, but one could leave his hand on it and not be uncomfortable).
After maybe 10 minutes, I removed the other item from the oven and returned the dish with the butter back in the oven to finish melting the butter.
When I came back a few minutes later and checked the dish in the oven with the butter, it had exploded with glass pieces (and butter) all over the oven.  I turned off the oven, left it closed, and allowed it to cool before attempting to remove the glass pieces and clean.
After it had cooled, I collected the glass pieces and cleaned the oven.  I have the glass pieces and paper towels used to clean the oven in a heavy trash bag.  The oven has been fully cleaned and vacuumed to remove any remaining small pieces of glass.
justification: The glass dish exploded but no one was harmed, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
Re:      Whirlpool Stove installed WITHOUT Anti-tip bracket

Dear Sir/Madam:

My wife and I purchased three Whirlpool appliances, including a Whirlpool stove from the Lowe's 
store in Ft. Walton Beach, Florida in April 2013. These appliances were purchased  to  replace   
older   appliances   in  a  beachfront   condominium   we  recently purchased.   All items  were 
delivered for installation  on Wednesday,  April 24, 2013 at Condominium in Fort Walton Beach.

THE NEW STOVE WAS INSTALLED BY LOWE'S  EMPLOYEES WITHOUT THE REQUIRED ANTI-TIP BRACKET.  
When they arrived and removed the old stove, a horizontal anti-tip bracket was already in place, bolted to 
the floor.  The new Whirlpool stove  came  equipped   with  an  L-shaped  bracket  and  several  
warnings,  which  taken individually or in total, warned that the stove should never be installed 
without the antiÃÂ­ tip bracket.  Notwithstanding  these warnings and the actual  bracket being 
shipped with the stove, these employees  proceeded to simply slide the stove into the opening 
without installing the new anti-tip  bracket.   After their installation,  I could easily pull the 
stove over.  When I told them that I wanted the anti-tip bracket installed, they told me that they 
had neither the training  nor the tools to do it.   I was shocked  because  I am sure both Lowe's 
and Whirlpool know the dangers of installing stoves without the anti-tip bracket. This is a crucial 
safety device.   Hundreds of children and elderly have suffered serious to fatal bums and crush  
injuries when stoves have been accidentally  tipped over.  This has been a well-known hazard in 
the industry for many years.

After the employees  left, I had another individual  actually install the bracket.   I
also called the Fort Walton store and spoke to an employee whose name was given to
me by the deliverymen.    When  I told him what had happened,  he stated  that he was
"surprised" and that his men did have the training and know-how to install the bracket.  I am  very 
skeptical   of  his   response,  especially   since  I  was  told  by  the deliverymen 
that I was only the second person in the last year to ask for the bracket's installation.   To 
compound  this irresponsible  behavior, I was asked  to sign a delivery form essentially stating 
that either the bracket had been installed or that I did not want it installed.  While I refused to 
check either of the boxes, I am convinced that many other families have been put at risk when 
stoves are installed without these anti-tip brackets.

Both  Lowe's   and  Whirlpool  have  superior  knowledge  of  the  need  for  these brackets and  
the dangerous  consequences  if they are  not  installed.  Both  companies should immediately  
institute  practices to insure that anti-tip  brackets  are installed each time a new stove is 
delivered.

I expect this letter to be placed in the proper file or files which may be subject to formal 
discovery in any existing or future lawsuits involving this safety issue.
justification: The stove was installed without the required anti-tip bracket, posing a potential hazard, but no actual injury occurred.
