incident_description:
The consumer says that she was cooking on the left front burner. When she went to turn it off it would not shut off.  She took off the knob and tried to turn the handle with a set of pliers but it still would not shut off.  She had to unplug the unit to get it to shut off. 

The consumer says her next step is to contact the manufacturer. The unit is experiencing the same problem as listed in Release # 09-333 and has the same brand.  Her model number is not included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that could not be turned off, but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says the oven switches from bake to broil by itself.  He says the top burner in the oven sometimes wont shut off.  The consumer says there was a pie on fire on one occasion.  He says that he has to shut off the circuit breaker in order to get it to shut off.  

The consumer says that a technician came out in 2011 who just tapped on the box in the back of the unit and got it to start working.  The tech told the consumer that it could work fine for years or it could break down tomorrow.  It worked well for about another year before this issue started happening again.
justification: The oven malfunction caused a fire (incident) but no injury was reported, and the issue has recurred over time.

incident_description:
Sometime around June 7th, 2013 caller's had cooked supper using their oven, callers wife turned the oven off then sat down to eat dinner.

They began cleaning up after dinner when the range began beeping and displaying an "F1" error code.
They went to the electric range and found that the oven was on.
The callers tried to turn it off then tried again but it still would not go off.
The caller finally disconnected the breaker.
They scheduled service for June 28th, 2013.
The repair tech advised them that it would $188 plus labor with total cost being around $300.

The repair tech performed a temporary repair with used parts that were in his truck.
Caller said it stopped working once since the temporary repair but he beat on it and it began working again.
He has not contacted the manufacturer and he does not intend to contact the manufacturer because he said that he did that once and "nothing was ever done".

Caller is asking that this model be added to the recalled with a free repair at manufacturer expense.
There are no injuries being reported
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction with no reported injuries, but required a repair and caused inconvenience.

incident_description:
On Friday, July 5th, I was making bacon in my GE HOTPOINT Stove.  I purchased this stove in November 2009 through Home Depot.  Model Number RGB530DEPWW  serial no.  TT139220R
 
About 10 minutes after I started the oven the glass door exploded spraying my whole kitchen counter tops, table top, floor and into the dining room and hallway with glass.  My legs took a goodly amount of glass but gratefully there was only one deeper cut from the glass.  Also gratefully nothing required stitches but took a bit of time to stop the bleeding as I am on blood thinners.  The fact that I am also a diabetic was worry some due to the high incidence of infections.  My doctor instructed me to clean the wounds and keep an eye on them.  
 
After doing so I contacted GE at 800-432-2737 which was found on the back of the book that came with the stove.  They told me that they would send a service technician out on Monday it being the holiday week and all and that if the service technician found this to be a safety issue it would be covered by GE.  They assigned me a case number of [REDACTED].
 
I found that statement rather uncalled for and amusing at the same time since I was almost killed by an oven door.

On Monday, the very unpleasant service man walked in the door, looked at the mounds of glass on the floor and said, ÃÂhmpf...ÃÂ,  then proceeded to sit down and write a ticket. He handed me a long white piece of paper that looked like a receipt from the grocery store and told me that it will be $540 to fix the stove. I remarked that the stove only cost $337.98 at the time of purchase. 

Since the customer service representative was clear to tell me this professional would be able to tell me what happened and make a determination, I inquired as to what caused the stove door to blow up, He remarked, "I don't know, never saw that but I have seen the inside of the door blow up". When I inquired as to why GE was not covering the issue he remarked that it was not a safety issue. Now, call me crazy but when a glass door explodes and shoots shards of glass all over three rooms of the house and into my legs I think that is a safety issue? 

The paper he gave me by the way only listed the parts to fix it which came to $209.50 and $11.40, so when I called GE to state my case after his visit, they told me that whatever the man says goes and they assume like I did that the labor was the difference between $540 and the estimate for the parts. NO ONE could give me a definitive response on the labor fees. I found this about as interesting as an exploding oven not a safety issue.

The customer rep did tell me that they would discount the repairs by half which would still be about the same price as the cost of the stove in the beginning and frankly... I do not think this is my responsibility.

I am sorry I purchased this stove to begin with.  When in use whether it be the oven or the range top the whole stove becomes very hot as I can attest due to multiple burns learning the hard way.   Gratefully I have no children with me on a regular basis because the stove is not safe in that regard as well.

My last conversation with the GE representative left me very frustrated and provoked me to contact facebook users to see if they have experienced this issue and further to look on the net for similar circumstances.  I have found multiple incidents of this particular stove's door blowing up on the net.  How can the service professional tell me he never heard of it?  I am hoping that someone other than a customer service rep gets an email that I today sent to eresponses@ge.com in their hands and has the courtesy to address this issue with me.  

I really thought GE had more credibility and better products.

The more I think about this I do not even want them to fix the stove but in fact think since this is what appears to be a more common than not occurrence with this stove they should replace it with one that is not a danger to use.  Several of the incidents I viewed on line were in exactly the same time frame as this stove.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut and multiple minor injuries from glass shards, though no stitches were required. The occurrence likelihood is high as similar incidents with this stove model have been reported online.

incident_description:
I have a 
MDB8959AWS6 Maytag Dishwasher 
S/N F14004717

The unit failed, upon performance diagnosis to determine part failure the thermal fuse was blown.

While identifying the fuse, I noticed burn damage (brown insulation) on the wire harness, most likely not the wiring insulation, but the rubber sound proofing adjacent to the wiring.
The power plug on the wire harness connecting to the control board was melted.
There was heat damage (brown discoloration) around the power blade terminals of the plug on the control circuit board.
There was electrical burning odors in and around the dishwasher when it failed mid cycle.
The unit has a dedicated circuit breaker that was not blown.
The unit was set to normal wash, no heat dry, and sanitize mode.

Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved significant electrical damage and burning odors but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
the front right burner on the range doesn't turn off when the dial is turned off. HUGE FIRE/INJURY HAZARD! 

the heat level goes to full heat when you turn it off and continues burning, sometimes staying on for long periods of time and not turning off unless the appliance is turned off at the breaker.
justification: The burner not turning off poses a significant fire and injury hazard, as it can remain on at full heat for extended periods.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she stepped out for a moment after just finishing cleaning the stove.  She came back inside and saw a huge mountain of glass on her floor.  She says the outer glass on her oven door completely shattered.  She says the glass pieces were small like crushed ice.  

She contacted the manufacturer who offered no assistance.  They said it was out of warranty and the glass that she has is no longer available because they don't make her model anymore.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We started noticing hundreds of little opaque *lines* in the bottom edge of the housing (the part that actually sits on your cutting board) and were like, "What's that?" After investigating, in slow motion, we realized what was up.

The outsides of the waffled blades are so close to the edges of the clear plastic housing that they inadvertently collide, thus shaving off little bits of the plastic housing and intermixing them in whatever food we're chopping.
justification: Plastic shavings intermixing with food poses a risk of injury if ingested, though no immediate harm is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE JGB281DERBB gas range in October of 2012. From the very first day, the flame on the back right burner completely cuts out, leaving no flame and a house full of gas.  There have been several occasions when I inadvertently had my house fill with gas because the back right burner loses its flame at the lowest setting.

I had to wait for the City of Alexandria to inspect the installation of this range to insure that it was not a faulty installation that caused this problem.  The City inspector came in April and determined that the installation was fine. The inspector also observed the problem with the back right burner losing its flame at the lowest setting and noted this on his report.

A General Electric repairman came to observe the problem, and he did observe that the back right burner did indeed lose its flame at the lowest setting.  The repairman ordered a new regulator and installed it on July 8. 2013. This did not solve the problem.  He claimed that there is a problem with the gas pressure in the house.  I don't fully buy that theory and think that this product is dangerous.
justification: The incident involves a gas range repeatedly filling the house with gas, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
My Electrolux-made, Figidaire-branded refrigerator, model GLHS36EESB0. It caught fire in my home on 7/7/2013. Fortunately, the damage was limited to just the refrigerator and it could have been much, much worse. I called Electrolux (parent company for Frigidaire) on 7/9/2013. Electrolux will not compensate my family for the food lost due to the fire (not that I really expected them to; the unit is seven years old after all). However, they didn't even want my pictures. 

[REDACTED]
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, causing damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: We noticed smoke coming out of our GE Dishwasher model# GLD6800N00BB.  There was also a strong odor that something was burning.  We immediately opened the dishwasher; the smoke stopped. We opened the front panel and found the control panel and connectors charred and smoldering.  There was also rust along the inside top of the panel. Hard water stains were visible at the bottom of the inside of the front panel. Both indicating that moisture had been getting inside for quite some time.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning odor from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred. The presence of rust and hard water stains suggests this is a likely recurring issue.

incident_description:
I am the [REDACTED], the incident occurred at my own residence. my wife observed our Frigidaire Electric Range oven left burner turn itself on after hearing some clicking noises. She then turned the breaker off when it was not in use in order to ensure that it would not turn on again we both researched that there was a recall for the SAME issue but our model # did not fit the category I notified Sears and Frigidaire and of course they claim that it is not covered under the recall. 

Our Frigidaire Electric Smoothtop range is Model # FESL79SCB Serial# VF64685048
justification: The burner turning on unexpectedly poses a potential hazard, but no injury or damage was reported. The issue is possible but not frequent, as indicated by the recall history.

incident_description: Turned stove off with knob. Burner was off but came back on it's own. This is an on going issue with multiple stoves. As a result there has been 1 serious fire and other smoke damages. Numerous reports of red light indicator remaining on and the burner becoming hot on it's own. Numerous reports about blue sparks from burners. Numerous reports of smell of burning wires. Face of stove by knobs very hot to the touch. Stove is listed on recall list. Model # is RB526H
justification: The incident involves a stove malfunction that has caused a serious fire and smoke damage, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description: I purchased a Baby Beaba cooker to make fresh food for my baby. I have owned it only 2 months and the bottom plastic (around the blade) is cracking. This poses a big safety concern as pieces of this plastic once broken off will end up in my baby's food and pose a choking hazard, and potential for internal injury if ingested. I have a friend who purchased the same cooker with me and her product is already chipping, she noticed missing plastic pieces and immediately notified me. Upon inspection of my own unit I noticed dozens of cracks in the bottom of my unit, thankfully no (visibly) missing pieces. My friend had to throw away all her baby food and is unsure how long her unit has been flaking plastic into her baby's meals!
justification: The incident involves cracking plastic that could pose a choking hazard or internal injury if ingested, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: When cooking with oil my pan made a load popping noise and upon later inspection it was made apparent that the sidewalls of the pan had been pushed outward all around the pan. Over the next hour or so as the pan cooled sections of the bowed out pan started popping back into their original placement. Had I been using more oil, it would have spilled out causing damage to me or my property.
justification: The incident involved a pan deformation with potential for harm, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Toaster Oven would not turn off and toast almost caught on fire.  This was a brand new BD Toaster Oven with three knobs.  There is nothing on the toaster oven which indicates that the oven is set to off.

I called BD Customer support and they explained that the bottom knob should be turned parallel with the countertop.  Going all the way over leaves the unit permanently in an on position.  There is a O which is supposed to indicate Off but the word Off does not appear on the Toaster Oven.  This is a terrible design flaw.  Even the DIrections for Use are not clear on this.
justification: The toaster oven almost caught on fire due to a design flaw, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Walking into my kitchen on the morning of 17 June, 2013, I noticed the center heating element of the multiple size elements on my Kenmore Elite Electric Smooth-top Range was on.  Upon getting closer, I noticed the range was off, and the element was giving off an extreme amount of heat.  Turning the other elements on, then off did not resolve the problem.  I immediately turned the range breaker off to disconnect the power to the range.  After 30 minutes, I turned the range breaker back on to see if this corrected the problem.  However, the center heating element spontaneously turned itself back on.  After this point, I turned the breaker back off, and called a repair man. The repair technician stated the problem could not be fixed due the electronic controls of the range.  Therefore, a new range had to be purchased.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning heating element without resulting in injury or death, and such electrical issues are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: I had my [slow cooker] at a picnic. It was just the [slow cooker] and lid, not the entire unit (so obviously it was not plugged in). It had been sitting on a table for several hours. The [slow cooker] was completely cool at this point. I was standing about 8 feet away talking with a group of people when we heard an explosion. We all looked at each other and walked over to the table (no one was around the table at the time of the explosion thank God). Here the lid to the [slow cooker] had exploded all over the place. It was in and on other food and all over the table. We had to pitch some food and take the table cloth completely off because there was no way to clean up all the glass as it had flown everywhere. It was very scary to think my kids or other kids or even adults could have been in the path of the flying glass!
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the slow cooker lid causing property damage but no injuries, as no one was near the table at the time.

incident_description: I was away for 2 weeks. When I returned I was reading and heard the microwave 'bing' than start running ALL ON ITS OWN. I immediately went to the microwave and it said 'baked potato.' I turned it off, unplugged it and waited about an hour. I plugged it back in and within a minute it did the same thing-bing, read baked potato and began to run.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but caused no injury, and such incidents are unlikely to occur frequently.

incident_description: My Frigidaire range turns on spontaneously, sometimes heats to the max even when the dial is set on sim or low. Sometimes it also stays on when turned off.  This is only one burner, the left front one.
justification: The range turns on and heats spontaneously, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I had been using the Tea Tumbler for about 2 weeks while, at work, I boiled water and poured it into the glass in order to brew some tea. I turned in my computer chair and went to set the glass upon my desk when it barely bumped the bottom corner of the glass causing burning water to spill on my pants and hand, and glass flying everywhere. Luckily no real damage was done to myself or other sitting around me.
justification: Burning water spilled on the person's hand and pants, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: The glass oven door exploded. Caloric Heritage Series 4 burner gas range. Over 15yrs old. It had been on about 30 minutes before to heat some pastries and had been turned off about 30 minutes. No one was in the kitchen when it exploded, it wasn't hit.
justification: The oven door exploded but no one was present, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
I am once again writing to inform the public of yet another fire we experienced while making toast on 6/11/13, with
our free replacement Black & Decker Countertop Oven. Needless to say, after three different model replacement
ovens from Black & Decker (Model #TR0480BS on 7/5/10 and Model# TR0480BS on 2/23/11, referred to in Report
No. 2011 0323-6D9C3-1172288 filed with the U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission and recent Model#
TR04075B with a QC Pass 2 sticker on it), I am totally convinced- Black and Decker/ aka Applica- is making junk. At
one time, I had confidence in buying the Black and Decker brand, but no more. The fact that we live in a throw
away society and the fact that the government does not recall these products is appalling to me. To make matters
worse, the internet is full of reviews concerning fires with these products and they continue to remain on the shelf.
After filing and researching my two previous complaints, which requested an investigation into this matter, I was
told that only the most serious complaints are investigated. Therefore, the products remain on the shelf. The
remedy to the problem was two-fold. I could either file another complaint and/or stop buying the product.
Needless to say, I filed another complaint, bought the #1 rated toaster oven, and will never buy an appliance from
Black and Decker again.
justification: The incident describes a fire while making toast, but no injury or death is mentioned, indicating a severity level of 2. The repeated occurrences and online reviews suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Electronic board on Whirlpool dishwasher caught fire shortly after beginning wash cycle
justification: The fire was a minor incident with no injury, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: I preheated my new oven to 450 degrees, the put in a pan of food to bake. I closed the door and left the room, about 3-4 minutes later I heard a loud crash and ran back into the kitchen to find that my inner oven door had exploded into a million pieces.
justification: The oven door exploded, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This is not to report an acute safety hazard risk, such as causing an immediate injury.
It's rather a longer term health hazard, up to including consumer poisoning from aluminum.
I'm owner of a bread machine (Manufacturer: Zojirushi Model: BB-PAC20 Home Bakery Virtuoso)
After 15 months of use; I noticed that one of the paddles (or "kneading blade" - in Zojirushi terms) stopped rotating while kneading. I removed the paddle and noticed that it's notch completely worn out. So the rotation of shaft was not transferring to paddle any longer. The other paddle was also just about to loose the connection as well. I'll try to attach a picture to my report (if your system allows it - otherwise please email me so I can send it to you). If you look at my picture; you'll see that 15 months old paddle next to a brand new one. You'll see the notch on the new paddle. Thickness of it is about 1/8". That tiny notch is the only contact point where the strong torque of powerful 100W motor is transferred to paddle. While the rotating shaft is made out of machined stainless steel, paddles feels like cast from some aluminum compound (it's very light and soft). So within time and under heavy pounding of rotating shaft; that paddle notch wears out by means of aluminum shavings.
Consumer eats those metal shavings in their bread.
Two important points with that design:
1) While rotating shaft is made of machined stainless steel, paddles are not. 
2) Rotating shafts are about 1" long. Why Zojirushi keep that paddle notch at only 1/8" thickness and not the full length of that shaft? Then the pounding impact would have much larger surface to transfer - hence much less (even totally eliminated) abrasion on the paddle.
Combined end result is; aluminum shavings in your bread.
I contacted online customer support of Zojirushi USA and asked if they are considering redesigning of those paddles. I have their email reply, stating that they don't consider such a change.
That's an unacceptable health hazard (aluminum dust in bread) forced upon public due to poor mechanical design.
justification: The incident describes a long-term health hazard from aluminum shavings in bread, which could lead to consumer poisoning, but no immediate injury is reported.

incident_description: Loaded dishwasher and started machine.  While cleaning up other items I walked back into the kitchen and white smoke was pouring out of the top of the machine (where the latch and controls are located).  I went to open the door and flames came out of the top right side about 6-9 inches tall. I immediately closed it and smoke kept pouring out but the flames died down.  Kitchen smells like an electrical fire.  Thankfully I was around.  We usually turn the dishwasher on as we go bed.  Never again.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Saturday, July 6, 2013 at 8:00 pm the top element in our Kenmore Model #66595781000 electric range come on by itself.  The only way to turn it off was by turning off the circuit breaker.  It is now 1:00 pm on Sunday, July 7, 2013 and we turned the circuit breaker back on.  The broiler is still on!!!

This is a huge safety hazard.  We now have to keep the circuit breaker flipped off all the time.  I called Sears and they claim that this is not a common problem.  However, the internet is full of complaints and incidents related to the exact same problem with the exact same range.  

To have them come out here will be $239.  The part itself, if we were to install it, is $200.  Sears should rectify this obviously known issue for free, or provide a credit towards a new SAFE range.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range that poses a safety hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Refrigerator burning hot.  metal strip between the door seals is burning to the touch.  the compressor in the back is also.  it's definitely hot enough to start a fire.
justification: The refrigerator is dangerously hot and could start a fire, but no injury or fire has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Glass door on upper wall oven of Kenmore unit shattered upon opening the door scattering shards of sharp pieces everywhere including on me.
Called Sears and they said they've heard about such things happening but there is no recall on record.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass door causing scattered shards, but no injury was mentioned. Sears acknowledged similar incidents, indicating it's not a rare occurrence.

incident_description:
Frigidaire solid surface stove top
Model: FEC30S6ABF
Serial: NF74417616

Large, front right burner turns on by itself and (or when turned on) immediately goes to high regardless of setting chosen.  Once burner is on, it cannot be turn it off from the stove - requires the circuit breaker to be turned off for at least 30 min to allow the burner switch to cool off and reset.  

Burner gets extremely hot and has created a fire hazard.  (Assume it is short circuiting the internal switch.)
justification: The burner turns on by itself, gets extremely hot, and creates a fire hazard, posing a significant risk of injury.

incident_description: My wife purchased a Kuerig B70 Platinum coffe maker last year. It stopped brewing last week - no water going to the KCup dispenser. Looked online and there are numerous articles on this brand and type of coffee maker and this specific defect. I removed the outer cover and noted that mine also had water leaking from the solenoid valve onto the electronics.  I contacted Kuerig customer service and they stated that they had not heard of this issue before.   Hard to believe based on the numerous articles, blogs, and home fixit sites describing this very same defect.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning coffee maker with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The widespread reports of the same defect suggest a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
We purchased an over the counter built in GE Microwave oven and had trouble several times with the touch key pad located on the right side of the installed unit.  The touch key pad was replaced last year shortly after we purchased the unit and today the Key pad was no longer properly functioning as it read "Keypad error, service may be needed."  I was looking at the warranty book when to my amazement, the microwave went on all by itself!  I quickly opened the door and it shut off and when i closed it there was a 1:00 on the display so i cleared it on the touch pad and left it alone and 2 minutes later it went on again all by itself.  I realize that if there is nothing in the microwave that a fire can easily start and after this happened a 3rd time, again with nothing touched on the keypad AFTER it was cleared.  
I called GE and they were not willing to replace the unit free of charge even though this module was replaced just last year for a similar problem.  They said i would have to pay for the service and the part which is totally unacceptable to me.
The Model # is JVM1540DPWW and the Serial No: GV304588
Please let me know what can be done here as GE's response was not acceptable in light of the danger this type of problem poses.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
My Cuisinart coffeemaker nearly caught fire this morning. If I hadn't been home, it would have likely caused a serious fire in my home. 
I was walking past and it started crackling and smoking, huge billowing smoke. I immediately unplugged it and took it out to my lawn. It took a good 1/2 hour to cool down completely. The heating element was glowing and it was extremely hot.

I also burned my hands when I picked it up to move it outdoors. 

It is the Cuisinart 12 cup 1200 model, Brewmaster. 

I have heard this has happened to many people, after reading online. 

Why hasn't this been recalled? Is Cuisinart waiting until someone's house actually catches on fire?? 

I have owned this for less than 1year. 

Please help do something about this dangerous product!
justification: The incident involved a near-fire and a burn injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention of similar incidents online suggests the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description: Refrigerator light is overheating my interior side of the refrigerator. The lights stay on and the refrigerator warms up. This is causing alarm and food spoilage. I had to disconnect the lighting to save from damage. This is a serious problem and very unsafe.
justification: The overheating refrigerator light caused food spoilage and required disconnection, indicating a significant safety hazard but no direct injury.

incident_description: On Tuesday evening July 25th, 2013 I was cooking with a new Anchor Hocking glass casserole dish and had it in the oven for 25 minutes at a temperature of 350 degrees Fahrenheit. The dish belonged to my sister-in-law who got it as a wedding gift in January. It was during the time that I was checking to see that the chicken had cooked all the way through that the glass dish suddenly exploded with a loud "pop" and sent bits and large shards of glass all over the kitchen. One of these shards, approximately 8" in length flew off of the table and imbedded itself in the top of my left foot. After removing the shard an approximate "dime-sized" hole was left in my foot and I had no use of two of my toes. The wound was treated with thorough cleaning, compression, and medical glue. The incident has left me on crutches for a, nurse practitioner recommended, week.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring medical treatment, but no death occurred. Glass cookware explosions are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
While baking a pizza in the oven at 425 degrees  for approximately 20 minutes she attempted to open the oven door when the handle to the oven detached from causing the oven door to slam close.

 She was able to get the oven open by using a oven mitt to grab at the screw that was left exposed since the handle fell off.  She received a minor burn to her right hand when the oven closed, when trying to get the pizza out while keeping the door open.

The firm was contacted on 7/21/2011 and she was advised that there were no recalls involving her model number and serial. She was advised to schedule a repair.  She indicated that she would hire another company not associated with the firm to make the repairs. She ended up ordering a new handle and replacing it herself- new hande looks the same.

The consumer  indicated that she had experienced other failures with the handle  about  the handle was loose on the left side and her husband attempted to tighten it each time. There were other occasions when the handle fell off on one side and  her husband was able to make the repairs to put it back on the range.  

No repairs have been made as of yet. However, she indicates that she has teenagers that use the oven quite frequently and what if they were to experience the same failure. She also indicated that they could be severely burnt.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The handle has failed multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Consumer states that porcelain pieces 1 or 2 inches long have been flying off his electric range from every direction whether caller is cooking on it or not.

He states that the porcelain is sharp and he is afraid that if the porcelain hits him, his wife or his dog in the eye it could blind them.

Range is not found as being recalled.

There is no wind near the range to enable the porcelain pieces to fly, no fan or window nearby and no specific time of day that the incident happens.

These incidents began about three weeks around May 27th, 2013.

Purchased in Greensburg, PA approximately five years ago.

Caller is asking for either repair or replacement at manufacturer expense.
justification: Consumer states that porcelain pieces are flying off the range, posing a risk of injury to the caller, his wife, or his dog.

incident_description:
The consumer says the unit had shorted out and smoking almost immediately after turning it on.  Had he left the house it could have caused a serious fire.  He says smoke was coming out of the control panel. 

He contacted Sears/Kenmore who said his model is not on recall.  The consumer says they offered him a $75 gift card.  He says all the wiring is burned out and had to disconnect the circuit breaker to get the unit to shut off.  

The consumer says he and his wife were getting ready to step out and leave the unit running.  Had he done so he said it could have caused serious damage.
justification: The unit shorted out and smoked, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I returned home from a business trip to find my Kenmore oven was on and extremely hot.  The knobs were in the off position.  The indicator light was off.  The oven had turned itself on!  Luckily, there was no damage....just emotionally upset of what could have happened.  The oven/stove unit was purchased in 2000 when we moved into our home.  Model #911.95582990 and Seriel # 9T187804Q.  I have done some research and see that there were other model #'s recalled because the Stove top turned itself on...thus causing some serious damage/death. incident_description:

They (consumer & her husband)  knew right away that something was wrong with the freezer.  They opened the refrigerator and the light was "off".  They asked their son about this.  The son said that about 6 months ago, he reached in the back of the refrigerator and felt heat coming from the light fixture.  The son removed the light bulb with a light cloth.  This was the original light bulb that came with the refrigerator.  The son also discovered a 2" - 3" deep burn in the top of the refrigerator, where the light housing is located.

(6/24/13)  The consumer called the mfr. at [REDACTED] number, but she was referred to a number:  [REDACTED].  She stayed on the line for approximately 15 minutes, but was unable to speak with a representative.

incident_description:
Blue star is the brand of oven

Purchased on Sep 5th 2012 but was not installed until late Jan 2013 due to delays in kitchen remodel

incident_description:
Caller retired for the night around 9:00AM June 4th, 2013 with no odors or problems in his home.

He woke around 2AM or 3AM the night of June 5th, 2013, noted an acrid odor but didn't find reason for it then returned to bed.
He had problems sleeping because the odor just didn't seem natural but he could find no place of origination.
He arose again around 5:30, went to the refrigerator, opened the freezer and noted that the ice was melted.
He unplugged the refrigerator then moved the food and drinks to a spare refrigerator and freezer.

He checked the refrigerator he noted that the compressors starting device was charred and fused to the compressor.
He touched the starting device then began taking it off, however when he tried to remove it the starting device just crumbled.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturers and is not positive he will contact them.
There were no injuries
justification: The incident involved a charred and fused refrigerator component with no injuries reported.

incident_description:
Electric Smoothtop Range being reported was in home when callers purchased it in January 2010 and the house was approximately three years old at the time.

Around June 2010 caller began noticing while cleaning that the right, rear burner would be warm when it hadn't been used that day.
This incident kept repeating which made the caller realize that the burner was turning on by itself.
She called repair who informed her that it was being caused by a small electronic part which he replaced and that specific burner has not had any occurrences since that time.

June 24th, 2013 mid cooking classes being conducted by caller with her 22yr  old Autistic son, when she walked away just a moment her son began calling her.
She walked back and the front left burner was flaming red, she checked the dial and verified that it was still only set at 4 but the heat coming from the burner was extremely intense and the burner was vibrant red.
She and her son verified that no food or liquid had dropped on the burner and that it was clean.
Caller moved the pan from the burner, turned the dial to off but the burner would not turn off. 
The caller turned the knob a second time in the opposite direction, heard a pop coming from the knob then the burner began cooling off.

June 25th, 2013 her son was cooking, caller was outside when she heard a scream.
She and her husband both ran for the kitchen where they were met by their son who explained to them that the burner wouldn't go off again.
She went to the range where her son had moved the pan from the left burner over to the right burner.
She checked again to be sure that it was the burner, that it hadn't been turned up.  The dial was on 4 again but the burner was red hot.
Again the caller turned the knob, burner wouldn't go off then again she turned the dial/knob a second time in the opposite direction, heard a pop coming from the knob then the burner began cooling off.

June 27th, 2013 caller, her son, his helper were all present he set the dial to 4.5, put his meat in the pan, browned it, drained it and was beginning to put the seasoning into the meat when she heard high, rapid sizzling as if the meat was cooking too quickly.
She checked the burner, dial was at 4.5 but the same burner was at extremely high temperatures.
They moved the pan off the burner.
Caller began the same ritual;turned the knob, burner wouldn't go off then again she turned the dial/knob a second time in the opposite direction, heard a pop coming from the knob then the burner began cooling off again.
Caller and her husband performed a test with the two front burners and couldn't repeat the incidents.

This morning July 1st, 2013 callers realized they may either not be testing long enough or not have a pan on the burners while testing.
They and their son were cooking breakfast this morning, had been cooking for approximately fifteen minutes when they noticed that the left front burner was flaming red, no liquid or food was on it and the dial was still set at 4.5.

Callers have not contacted the manufacturer and do not intend to contact them because caller said they already know that the manufacturer will do nothing for them.

No injuries are being reported
justification: The burner malfunctioned multiple times, posing a potential hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Upon returning from a short walk I smelled an electrical fire in my home.  I quickly identified the sources, my Kenmore dishwasher (made by Whirlpool), model 665.16572201, serial FP0802734.  

After turning off the power and water, I unscrewed the mount and pulled it from the cabinet, and identified the source as the control board in the door, which was burn, melting the surrounding casing, and hot enough to cause minor damage both the cabinet and the counter, and the heat discolored the metal tub of the appliance.  The thermal overload switch was charred but failed to trip (which is a second failure, and odd for a part known to trip without cause).  With a melted board, the display was still operational.  The motor was running during the dry cycle, and thus very, very hot - a second potential source of fire. 

No personal injury was incurred, only property damage, which was limited by early detection and quick action.  

Repair costs for destroyed parts is about $225 plus labor.

justification: The incident involves gas leakage due to accidental activation, posing a fire hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
WE have recently experienced a kitchen fire (May 2013), with appliance and smoke damage that has cost our insurance company over $17,000.  It has also cost me the $500 deductible part of the policy which I would like to recover.
We believe the fire was the result of a defect in the electric range we purchased from Sears in 2007.  The problem we believe is the rotary knob control switch for the left front burner.  The burner does not go off when the switch is turned to the off position.  This happened twice, the first time within 2 years of when we bought it and the second time causing the recent fire.
The range in question is a Kenmore smooth top model #790.96122409, serial #VF71312207.
I cannot find a recall notice or class action suit for this model number and am curious as to any information you may be able to provide me regarding this particular appliance.

[REDACTED]
justification: The fire caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2.

incident_description:
The consumer says that her two sliced toaster had cardboard inside the toaster.  Their was no metal.  She is concerned that this would pose a fire hazard.

She looked on the bottom of the box and called the manufacturer.  She was asked if it was functioning, the consumer said yes.  

She was then told that it is not broken.  The consumer says she also burned her finger in one incident.
justification: The consumer burned her finger, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the toaster was functioning and no further incidents were reported.

incident_description: I turned the broiler on to cook dinner. An hour after turning off the broiler i realized it was still on even though it was turned off on the digital pad.  After several attempts to turn off the broiler, the flames went out but the gas continued to feed the broiler.  The gas began to fill up inside of the house. The fire department was then called to turn off the gas line feeding the oven
justification: The incident involved a gas leak and required fire department intervention, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The microwave randomly turned on.  We thought it was the fan, but, the glass turn table in the microwave was hot.  We were nowhere near the microwave.  We thought it was a fluke, however, it happened, again a few hours later.  I unplugged the microwave and plugged it back in.  The next day it happened again - twice.  We have unplugged the microwave and plan to buy a new one.  This is very dangerous.  It should not randomly turn on.
justification: The microwave turning on randomly poses a potential hazard but no injury occurred, hence severity level 2. The repeated incidents suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
After purchasing a new Frigidaire/Electrolux dishwasher, I had to install a water hose coupler to
the underneath to complete a water hookup to our existing water line,while doing this,I lacerated the top part of my 
hand 2 places,I bled profusely, and my wife had to obtain a cloth and ice to help stop the bleeding 
and take the swelling down,this was caused from a extremely sharp edges,that the manufacturer 
failed to deburr the sharp edges of this machine, especially the entire bottom of the frame work of 
the machine, it is my experience from machining parts,all parts should be deburred before leaving 
the factory.
We reported the incident to Electrolux, but they denied the claim.Claim Number [REDACTED].

I have pictures available of my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations and profuse bleeding, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I went to my freezer to take out food and found that the freezer was extremely hot to touch and it was making a
very loud clanking noise. I opened the door and found all my food had been defrosted and ruined and 
had to throw away a  few hundred dollars of food. I think if I had not gone to the room with the freezer that it would have caused a fire in my home. The consumer safety report said to unplug and discontinue use.
I can't seem to get any help with this matter even though I had to now buy a repair plan. The 
repair man came, plugged in the freezer and it appears to be working  ok for now so he did not 
repair anything. It is not a matter of "if' but  "when" something bad happens, yet without it 
plugged in and running the man cannot diagnose a problem until he sees it or hears it, until it 
acts up again, (that is what he said), therefore I still have no freezer or remedy. What ever 
happened to the days when the place where you purchased something took it back and gave you a 
working model? The USA has become a pathetic  example for doing business.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning freezer causing food spoilage and potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We have an LG LRE30453ST electric range.  During the cleaning process the top of the stove gets EXTREMLY hot...without any warning. I reached over to turn on the oven light and the black stove top burned my forearm.  We thought at first we put the cleaning on 3 hours and that possibly this was the reason.  The second time we cleaned we put it on 2 hours and went to bed.  
Yesterday I again put it on for 2 hours early in the morning.  I began to do things around the house.  My 93 year old father lives with us.  He got up early went into the kitchen and he must have felt unsteady grabbed onto the stove and burned his fingers.  It was just a brief grab because he felt it was hot - screamed and I came running to the kitchen.  I got him settled and called our doctor.  Thankfully it was not as bad as it could have been.  In the meantime I checked the cleaning and left it to continue its cycle.  I want to also add that there was a plastic bag that had bananas in it - this was sitting rather close to the top of the stove - it was melted.  That is how hot the top of the stove gets.  I put chairs around the range and waited for the cycle to end.  

I am reporting this because it is a potential fire hazard as well as a something that should be told to people with children in the house.  

I would be happy to have someone come out and witness this.  I have called LG - which I have had repairmen out for other issues 3 times...There is no recall for this and there should be
justification: The incident resulted in burns to both the reporter and their father, indicating an injury severity. The likelihood is high given the repeated occurrences and potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: On June 23 at approximately 2:30 P.M. while the oven was in use in convection mode, the exterior door shattered scattering shards within 15 feet of the oven. The shards consisted of sharp pointed fragments of glass and some composite. Had an adult or child been present, serious injury could have resulted. No one was injured although if any person had been near the oven, an injury could have resulted. The oven had been properly used. The door had not been damaged. The oven door had not sustained an impact in the 14 months since it was installed.
justification: The oven door shattered, posing a potential injury risk, but no one was actually injured.

incident_description:
A Cuisinart DCC 3650 Coffee Maker caught on fire while brewing coffee.  After a minor overflow, the cause of which we do not know, smoke with a strong stench of electrical burning poured out of the top and power cord hole, filling the kitchen.  (The GFI for the outlet did not trip.)

This coffee maker had been in service for less than a year, with no prior problems.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire and produced smoke, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
I own a 2 year old Samsung over the range microwave oven, model smh9187w.  I heard an unfamiliar beeping coming from my kitchen.  Upon investigation,I observed the led screen on the microwave displaying E/13. I've never seen this before.  I went to the microwave and felt substantial heat as my hand and face neared the unit.  I touched buttons on the control pad and none were responsive.  I opened the door and it was like opening the gas oven.  I then took the temperature of the glass turntable inside the microwave with a infrared laser temperature gun that I use in the kitchen for cooking.  The glass was 385 degrees farenheit.  I unplugged the microwave for about an hour and plugged it back in.  It rebooted normally, but about 15 minutes later it started on its own again.  The led screen displayed "baked potato".  I will not plug it in unattended and every time since, it continues to start on its own.

            I believe this issue could be potentially very dangerous possibly resulting in serious personal injury and/ or substantial property damage

                                                                                      Respectfully
                                                                                      [REDACTED]
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, generating extreme heat and starting on its own, posing a risk of injury or fire, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a pot and pan set at the military exchange on Fort Hood Texas. The set is from the "Martha Stewart Collection" and is labeled "Exclusively for Macy's." The 3 quart sauce pan while being used on an electric burner stove, over medium high heat to boil water suddenly cracked along the rim of the saucepan before the water even began to boil. The pot was over half full of tap water. After removing the pan from the stove a second crack appeared. Both cracks are along the rolled rim and extend downward for approximately one half of an inch. This pan, as well as others from this set are no longer being used out of concern of failure causing leaking of contents or creation of a further sharp edge that can be hazardous during use or cleaning. The pan in question was not dropped or otherwise damaged in any way.

 I contacted the place of purchase for return and was instructed to contact the manufacture which has proved unsuccessful.

Poor customer service is bad enough however, I am more worried of a potential hazard to others using this same pot and pan. I have taken several macro photos of the cracks and have retained the pot. If this is a systemic issue I feel others should be warned of this defect.
justification: The incident involved a pot cracking during use, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer reported that he is experiencing problem with the ice maker in the refrigerator. He noticed plastic shards in his water 3 different times. The consumer said that the plastic agar in the ice box that helps move the ice forward has shattered 3 times already. He said that these incidents occurred in May 2011, July 2012 and June 2013. 

Consumer mentioned that GE has replaced the ice box unit (this time and the previous 2 times) but GE informed the consumer that they will not replace it again if it happens in the future and he should just purchase a new refrigerator.
justification: The incident involves plastic shards in water but no reported injury, and it has occurred multiple times over several years.

incident_description:
Defect in the top rack of a 13-month-old Kitchen Aid dishwasher (model KUDE20IXBL8). 

When I pulled the top rack out to unload it, the left side collapsed without any warning, spilling dishes and glasses down onto the crockery in the bottom rack and out onto the floor. 

When I looked for the cause, it was obvious that one of the two flimsy plastic ÃÂspringÃÂ pegs that retain each wheel of the upper rack on its axle had broken.  This allowed the wheel to pull off the axle and thereby allow the entire left side of the top rack to collapse.  It seems to me the axles on the rack adjuster (Part number W10350376) are very poorly designed and is not made as solidily as the wheels on the lower rack. This is despite the fact that both upper and lower racks are of the same dimensions and, so to me as an average consumer, both should be able to support a full load of dishes.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher rack collapse causing dishes to spill, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was scooping ice cream that was fairly soft when the spoon snapped right where the metal and the handle join.  This resulted with my fingernail being bent back where it's not supposed to bend!  It bled and there is also a small pool of blood under the nail.  My business is handmade jewelry and now I can't even put pressure on that fingertip without pain, so making jewelry has come to a screeching halt right in the middle of a project costing me time and money.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful injury (bent and bleeding fingernail) that impacts the ability to work, but it is not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a Black and Decker toaster oven (Model #TRO480BS) from a local store. The Timer/Toast control knob does not stop the heating element upon completion of the toasting cycle. The end result was the toast oven catching on fire. I sustained burns to my hands while moving the burning toaster outside.

I have tested the Timer/Toast control knob and it does not properly cut power as designed.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the hands, indicating injury (severity 3), and the defect in the toaster's control knob suggests a possible recurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Used the microwave for 2 minutes followed by a wait of about 5 minutes then another 2 minutes use. About an hour later the microwave started beeping occasionally. A message about overheating and maintenance required was being displayed. Unit was hot to the touch and the door window is distorted. The door would not open. Unplugged unit and allowed it to cool. Was able to pry the door open as it was fuzed to the bottom of the interior wall which melted. Both inside and outside window parts are distorted.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and overheated, causing damage to the unit but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I own a 2007 Kenmore Elite Trio refrigerator; bought in 2007. model #is...77544.    On May 30th 2013 my husband
opened the door and felt alot of heat.  The light sockets were burnt and blackened, the plastic light cover was melted and the bulbs were so hot  he had to use a towel to get them out and a burning smell. The light does not go off when door is shot.

Consumer talked to asst manager [REDACTED] at Sears in the Schuylkill Mall in Frackville, on June 3rd...He was excellent and immediately sent all the info to the Chicago office...[REDACTED] from Sears Executive office in Texas called on the 4th and sent the technician that day...There was no charge...

Replace parts were an N ciruit box...also a thermal switch...and lower watt bulbs and replacement cover...The tech. was excellent...

Sears is fixing the problem only after it occurs...so they are fully aware of the situation.  Consumer's concern is for the families that don't know this might happen...

Thank you.  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved burnt and melted components but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description:
The consumer says that he cooked that morning on the stove top with the sauce pan for about 20 minutes.  He left it on the stove, which was off.  
Three to four hours later he was in the bedroom and heard a cracking noise.  He says the lid was shattered into small tiny pieces.  
He says that he contacted the manufacturer who offered a new lid.  He is concerned with the lid exploding.  They said that
justification: The incident involved a shattered lid but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My electric glass top stove had an incident where the left rear burner came on by itself even with the control knob in the off position. I had to turn the breaker switch off to cut power to the stove. Other similair models were involved in a recall for this same symptom. I call the customer hotline and was told that my model number was not included in the recall. Fortunatly we were home and nothing caught fire but had we not been home and something left on the burner we would have probably come back to a house burnt to the ground along with our family dog.
justification: The burner turned on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred this time.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore smooth top cook stove. Which has begun having the same issues as in current recall Release # 09-333. The burner elements will get stuck on while cycling to maintain set temperature control. Burning extremely hot and will not turn off; even when you remove the pan or turn the control knob to the off position. It happened once or twice with one burner over the past year, I didn't think much about it. But, over the last few days it has happened every time I have used either one of my front two burners. Things will burn in the matter of seconds; even while keep a close eye on it. This very dangerous situation is what prompted me to check recalls in the first place. However my model number is not included in the list. Model # 790.96009601 serial # VF73870449. I called the sears recall line anyway; thinking they would help, but my range is out of warranty. I did not buy it at Sears, it came as part of the appliance package when I bought my new house in 10/2009. I really do not believe that warranty should be the issue; but the hazard that this product poses. I feel that this recall should be expanded to cover more model numbers.
justification: The burner elements getting stuck on and burning extremely hot poses a significant risk of injury, and the issue has been occurring frequently with recent use.

incident_description:
My wife set our dishwasher, turned it on and left for work.  I came home from work about an hour later to find the kitchen full of nauseating, noxious fumes.  I localized the source as the dishwasher and discovered it to be completely dead and still full of water and dirty dishes. I turned off the circuit breaker and opened all the windows and doors to try and clean out the stench.  I then called the Kitchen Aid Extended Service Plan representative and explained what I had found.  They scheduled a service tech to come to the house the next day.  

The service technician determined that the circuit board and associated components had burnt up and since the warranty company could not be reached Saturday, he would have someone come back the Following Monday...today.  That technician made the same determination and stated that the unit could not be repaired but that it needed replaced and that the warranty company would call to arrange the replacement.  The warranty company would not replace the unit and stated that it was at their discretion to offer a check for a depreciated amount and that I should go to Best buy and use that toward the purchase of a new unit. 

I mentioned the information about all the other examples of this type of situation happening to others and they disavowed any knowledge...even though they are a "partner" of Whirlpool and Sear Holding.

I cannot tell you all that was damaged but can assure you that the circuit board and wiring were overheated and burnt as I could see the charred circuit board, melted wires and melted plastic.  

Manufacturer - Kitchen Aid (Whirlpool)
Model - KUDP01FLBT5
Serial No. - FR2301071
justification: The incident involved noxious fumes and electrical damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I just finished baking brownies at 350 degrees on my new GE electric range.  When I opened the door to retrieve them the exterior top of the door touched my leg and it burned my thigh.  I then touched the closed door and realized it was pretty hot for my adult hands and if I was a little kid it would probably burn me.  I was curious to see how hot it actually was so I rested a meat thermometer on the metal it reached 160 degrees just resting on the door.  I took a picture of this with my cell phone to document. 

I am concerned about other people that may have small children with this same stove and worried kids may get burned.  This is the over safe teacher in me :).  I imagine it would get even hotter on the exterior if it was cooking at a higher temperature or especially if it was in cleaning mode. 

Please let me know if anyone has reported this or if you can look into it. 

Thank you, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and the likelihood is possible as the hot oven door could affect others, especially children.

incident_description: My General Electric Monogram dishwasher caught fire and burned last night during normal usage.  The machine is not located in the main building of our home and so the problem went undetected all night.  When we opened the door this morning, the machine was still running and hot and the there was no way to turn it off except through the circuit breaker.  The dishes and plates were scorched and blackened.  The heating element was shattered and burned up.  All of the plastic parts inside the dishwasher were melted and stringy.  General Electric said this model is not on the recall list though they have tens of thousands of recalled dishwashers all with same reported problem.  They told me I should report the problem to CPSC.  It is urgent that these machines be recalled before people are hurt or killed in a house fire caused by these malfunctioning machines.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and caused significant damage, but no injury or death was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but not all machines are affected.

incident_description: I turned coffee maker on and when almost finished I smelled something burning and heard cracking noise, the hot plate was extremley red  so I pulled the plug
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and a red-hot plate, but no injury was reported, indicating a minor equipment malfunction.

incident_description: When I first got my parang machete I was putting it in the sheath but I put it in wrong and it cut through the sheath and cut on my left hand my middle and ring finger the ring finge it went to the bone all I did was treat it myself by wrapping it. It took severial weeks for it to heal
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury to the fingers, requiring weeks to heal, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible as improper handling of sharp tools can lead to such injuries.

incident_description: Refrigerator inside lights didn't turn off when door was closed. Lights got so hot they melted the plastic housing around the lights. I had to unscrew the light housing so I could disconnect the wiring.  Luckily we were home at the time and could smell the plastic melting. I am convinced that this could have easily started a fire if we were not home at the time. I contacted the manufacturer via internet chat on their website. They told me it was covered under a special service bulletin. They scheduled a repair company to come out and repair the problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction that could have led to a fire but was caught in time, resulting in no injury or death.

incident_description: The Mr. Coffee 5-cup coffeemaker model number JWX9 turned on automatically throughout the night and the burner under the detainer was hot to the touch. This model is equipped with an auto start timer, but I never use this feature because of the random hours which I drink coffee. Besides receiving a burn to my finger no other injuries were sustained. I will use the coffee maker again only after I buy a GFCI power strip for the kitchen counter.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the user's intent to continue using the coffee maker with additional safety measures.

incident_description: After working correctly for first few months of ownership, The timer began having issues with shutting off. The timer would not shut off and the oven kept heating. Even after it was unplugged the timer continued to run. When it was plugged back in the area around the controls began smoking (electrical component burnt smell) and got very hot. Un-plugged and tried exercising the timer knob, tried plugging it back in and it again began to smoke. Un-plugged it and permanently put it out of service.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven timer leading to overheating and smoking, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Noticed smoke smell coming from dishwasher while it was running.  Stopped dishwasher and took off bottom panel.  Melted wires and components, and evidence of a near fire visible.
justification: Melted wires and evidence of a near fire indicate a significant incident, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Emerson MW9339SB began sparking, flashing and making loud noises even when nothing was in it.  We have only had the unit about 5 months.  Today I decided to take a look and when looking at the wave guide cover plate I noticed a dark spot on it, I removed the plate and there is arc damage between the cavity metal of the wave guide and the cover.  I believe if this was on any longer than a few second it would have caused the wave guide cover to ignite.  I see alot of problems reported with these units but ZERO recalls.
justification: The microwave exhibited dangerous behavior (sparking, flashing, loud noises) and had visible arc damage, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My microwave turned on by itself. It would not turn off when I hit off on the keypad nor when I opened the door. It had to be unplugged to turn it off.  If I had gone to bed or was not home I am afraid that there could have been a fire. After plugging the unit in again the next day, the same thing occurred later that day.  Then my keypad became entirely unresponsive.  I have a GE Spacemaker Microwave Oven model number JVM1540 which I purchased from Sears barely two years ago.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself could have caused a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Crock pot brand crock pot. purchased approx 1 year ago but I no longer have the receipt. I was cooking frozen butter beans, with plenty of water, had them on low for about 4 hours. I heard a loud crash, went in the kitchen, and the glass lid to the crock pot had shattered into a million pieces. still somewhat holding together in a lid shape until you touch the plastic handle. 

I did nothing to the crock pot before it broke. i had not touched it in a couple hours. it was not bothered in anyway, just sitting on my counter cooking on LOW. I have used this crock pot plenty of times before this incident.
justification: The glass lid shattered unexpectedly, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Trudeau brand fondue pot at the thrift store. It was still wrapped up in plastic, no box, and had never been used. We used the pot for the 1st time and when my husband went to lift it up the handle broke, causing hot oil to spill on him and my 13 year old child. Luckily, the burns were not severe enough to seek medical attention. I do have the box for the item and no product #, only instruction/recipe pamplet with Trudeau on it. It is not the same pot that you have on your recall list.
justification: Hot oil spilled causing burns, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
The consumer says that when the unit is pre heating she notices an acrid smell.  When she opened the oven door it would burn her eyes.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who would send out a technician.  

The technician said that this is normal and not harmful.  Her contractor however said that it is not normal and needs to be inspected right away.  The contractor scheduled another technician who determined that when the unit is set to preheat, it leaks carbon monoxide.  Atmos energy is the provider for natural gas which heats the range; it was their technician who utilized the meter to detected carbon monoxide.  Report from Atmos Energy is enclosed.

Over the years she has experienced numbness on her lips and ringing in her ears, and headaches.

Her next step is to contact the manufacturer.  

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER: 
From the time of installation of our Whirlpool gas range (SUper Capacity 465, Model SF395LEEZ0) purchased by my mother [REDACTED] in 1997, for my husband and me when she came to live with us, we complained to Sears technicians of an acrid odor emanating from the oven during the preheat phase (approx. 10 minutes) that stung our eyes and burned our noses each time the oven was turned on.  A Master Service Protectin Agreement was purchased at the same time the appliance was purchased and has been renewed without lapse of coverage since original purchase.  Subsequent visits by Sears tecnhnicians always resulted in the same determination: there was nothing abnormal in the operation of the range.  All three of us were in excellent health in 1997.  However, over the 16-year period since the installtion of the range, both my mother and my husband developed congestive heart failure. I developed arrhythmia as confirmed by a cardiologist's heart monitor. I have also developed an auto-immune disease and intermittent numbness of my lips.  Over that same period of 16 years, a series of three pet cockatiels were found dead in the bottom of their cage.  They were not suffereing from any prior illness.  Both my mother and my husband are now deceased.

While it may not be possible to prove conclusively that there is any direct connection between the above stated ill effects sustained over the period of time since the purchase of the gas range, there remains the question of what adverse health effects may have been attributed to short, ten minute bursts of carbon monoxide gas being release into our  home almost daily (and frequently,  more than once daily).  Certainly, it appears that Sears technicians were negligent in not having adequate equipment to test for gas leaks as did Atmos Energy.  

The odor that the gas company incorporates into naturally odorless gas is doubtlessly a life-saving safety measure but is rendered ineffective for the welfare of their customers or if they lack necessary equipment to check for life threatening emissions.
justification: The incident resulted in death (congestive heart failure, arrhythmia, and auto-immune disease) and was caused by prolonged exposure to carbon monoxide leaks, which were almost certain to occur during daily use.

incident_description:
January 12th, 2013, caller opened package received and cut his thumb while pulling his Gerber Machete out of the packaging used when packing it to send to him.  

He has had surgery, cannot bend his thumb and can only move it up and down. Two arteries where cut during this accident, both tendons were cut and all the nerves were cut.  He has been advised that the nerves may grow back within the next two years.

The caller traveled to the Denton Regional hospital by driving himself after wrapping his thumb very tightly.
He then spent two months in D&D Rehabitional Center in Denton, TX.  He was released after four hours of surgery with pain medicine and antibiotic.

He has not contacted the manufacturer yet but does intend to contact them.
justification: The caller suffered a severe injury to his thumb requiring surgery and rehabilitation, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had an electric range and the left front burner continues to turn on by itself. The consumer stated that she verified that the knob was on the ÃÂoffÃÂ position and she noticed that the burner was hot and the red light was on signaling that it was on. The consumer stated that no one was using the range before the incident happened.

The consumer stated that she turned off the circuit breaker and it turned off. The consumer stated it took approximately 2 minutes for the burner to cool down. The consumer stated that it happened 6-7 times already.
The consumer stated that no one was injured. 
She stated that she verified online to see if there was a recall and found that there was one yet her model was not included. The consumer stated that her range was posing the same hazard listed on release # 09-333.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they confirmed that her model was not included on the recall. 
The consumer stated that she believe that this product should be included on the recall and should be investigated do to the fire hazard that it poses to consumers.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury was reported. The issue has occurred 6-7 times, indicating it is likely to happen again.

incident_description:
(07/10/2012) The consumer stated that the microwave statrted coming on by itself. The consumer stated that the turntable on the inside would be going around. The microwave would be hot on the inside. The consumer contacted the manufacturer. A repair technician was sent out three different times. Twice when repair came out, they did nothing. The third time when repair came out, the technician could not do anything because the wrong part ,which is a panel assembly,was been mailed to the consumer from Whirlpool. The consumer does not have the dates nor who she spoke with. The repair technician advised the consumer that even if the part was correct, he felt that it would not have solved her problem. The consumer was advised that even though she unplugged the microwave, there was enough electricity store to cause the microwave to come on by itself. She was advised to unplug it and leave the door open. The consumer is afraid that the microwave will catch on fire.


(06/2012) The consumer contacted Whirlpool because the part was not right. The consumer stated that she left messages and no ever called her back.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a potential hazard, but no injury or fire occurred, and the issue was addressed with repair attempts.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she was experiencing similar problems with her smoothtop electric range as other consumers with the same model number that she had noticed reported.  Although the range cook top was off it became exceedingly hot, she had placed the oven at 385 degrees and it appears as if the temperature had increased and there was smoke emitting from vent of the oven.  The unit was unplugged to prevent a fire.  She has since replaced the range.

Although caller had experience problems of Release # 09-333, her model and serial was not part of the recall.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.  The caller does not believe this incident should have occurred  because the range is only 2 years old.  She feels that this range should be investigated for a recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that emitted smoke but was unplugged before any injury or fire occurred, indicating no injury or death.

incident_description:
