THERE IS A SERIOUS DESIGN FLAW IN THIS $2,700 PRODUCT.  (I am an engineer, so I know what I'm talking about.)

On the touch-screen control panel, if you press the two "buttons" in the upper-left corner, it will turn off the fridge, with no warning.  The company calls this "demo mode", for use on the showroom floor.

Since there's no warning when it happens, and since this is very easy to do (for example, if you rest your hand there while opening the French doors), there is significant risk of complete loss of all perishable food -- which is exactly what just discovered had happened to us at noon on May 22, 2011, when we discovered that the unit had been off for 24 hours.

The user's manual DOES NOT MENTION THIS AT ALL -- not even in the "Troubleshooting" section under "what to do if it is not functioning".   It does not warn you not to do this.  It does not even mention "demo mode" anywhere in the user's manual.

Furthermore, the people at Samsung tech support misinform customers when we complain, saying that using the child lock will prevent this from happening.  Leaving aside the fact that the salesperson in the store never mentioned that, nor did the person who installed it in our house, nor does the user's manual -- IT IS UNTRUE.  I can easily demonstrate that employing the child lock on this model DOES NOT defeat the "demo mode".

This product is a health hazard.  Many people, given the high cost of losing all food in your fridge and the current tough economic times, will be tempted to simply turn it back on and count on their noses to tell them what food has spoiled.  This will inevitably lead to cases of food poisoning, since not all spoiled food smells bad, and food poisoning can cause severe health problems, including death, in people with compromised immune systems.

AND, Samsung refuses to compensate consumers for food which is lost in this manner.  They take no responsibility at all for the situation, even though it is their poor design that is ultimately responsible.

Have you ever rebooted a PC?  Control-Alt-Delete?  There's a reason why that key sequence was chosen, many years ago -- it's impossible to do accidentally.  In fact, it takes two hands.

In contrast, Samsung has designed the control panel to make it easy for the person setting out a display unit to put it into demo mode (only very few units ever go on the showroom floor -- most are delivered to the consumer's home in the original factory container).

Instead, what they SHOULD have done is to make it very, very difficult to do this -- for example, (a) hold these two (non-adjacent) keys for 3 seconds with the door open, then (b) hold these other two (also non-adjacent) keys for 3 seconds with the door closed.  Or something like that -- you get the idea.  It should be something that NEVER could happen accidentally.

So, now we're out over $200, and Samsung refuses to do anything about it.

And, I've had diarrhea for two days, because we ate food from the fridge on the evening of the 21st and the morning of the 22nd, before we discovered that it was no longer refrigerating the food.  We didn't discover it until we left for the gym at noon on the 22nd and went to put ice in the water bottles.  Only water came out of the ice maker.

==> They should not be allowed to foist this ill-designed product on the unsuspecting consumer.  They should be forced to redesign it, and to recall all of the units with this design.  And maybe even to pay damages for those of us who have lost food.

Thanks very much -- I can be reached at [REDACTED] if you want more information.
justification: The incident resulted in financial loss and food spoilage, with the consumer experiencing diarrhea, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Dishwasher (model # 665.16039401, serial # FR5201579) caught on fire while running normal dish washing cycle.  Fire originated in control panel; pressing cancel button would not stop unit from running; after opening door the unit continued to run spraying water on the ground; the entire time plastic on front of door behind controls was bubbling and blowing smoke.  House was quickly filled with smoke from burnt plastic and components.  After running to circuit breaker panel and turning off power, smoke and symptoms of fire subsided.  Unit was purchased new from Sears retail store in Northeast Mall, North Richland Hills Texas, in 2005.  Research on CPSC website and other online sources revealed numerous incidents of same symptoms for this model dishwasher; Sears refused to initiate recall of product despite numerous reports of fires.

Numerous reports of same type of fire for this model dishwasher are listed on-line.  My numerous calls to Sears were a waste of time--passed from department to department with no assistance.

Sears always cut-and-pastes the same statement in response to complaints--("Sears Holdings takes product safety issues very seriously. We investigate each CPSC database incident report. We encourage our customers to provide additional information about incidents to our Customer Care Network, by calling 800-549-4505")--I am refuting their claim--if Sears took it seriously they would either recall the product or at least warn consumers about the hazard.  
When we called them about it they did nothing.

If they owned up to the problem I would not be writing this.  This product could burn down someone's house--I was just lucky enough to be home and shut off power to the unit.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported. Online reports indicate this is a recurring issue with this model.

incident_description:
In March 1999, two Asko dishwashers were installed in our home #1585.  Serial #985200407288, kitchen and one in our bar, #985200407299.  Both had a recall, Kitchen Dishwasher recall kit was installed when I had the dishwasher repaired in February , 10, 2003.  I paid the bill.  Bar dishwasher had recall kit replaced October 16, 2007.  On January 11, 2013 the kitchen dishwasher caught fire, smoke pouring out.  Smoke filled the kitchen, family room and bar.  We unplugged that dishwasher.  Since the dishwasher was 13 years old, we replaced it at our cost, but we were urged to notify ASKO due to the fire, and we had an email dated August 2, 2003 from ASKO certifying the dishwasher was safe to use.  I contacted ASKO.  First response was we did not have the recall kits installed.  I sent copies of the bill, pictures of the burnt dishwasher and email showing recall kit had been done, and email said it was safe to use.  Basically ASKO said it was not the company's responsibility.  I asked to have the dishwasher replaced in the bar, because it has the recall kit installed, and I am fearful it will catch on fire.  They refused to give us any  discount, money or help.  They tried to blame us for not having a recall kit installed, but I had proof we did follow the guidelines for the recall.  And even with the recall kit installed we still had a fire.  Fortunately we were at home and could unplug the dishwasher, and prevent the fire from spreading.  
Anyone who has this dishwasher, even with a recall kit installed is still at risk for having a fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is considered possible given the recall history and the fact that a fire occurred despite the recall kit being installed.

incident_description:
GE Self Cleaning Oven Model JGB908

The oven igniter has not been functioning properly for the past several weeks.  This has been progressively getting worse and now happening each time the oven is in use.  When the oven is turned on, it does not light right away.  The start is delayed until there is a gas build-up.  Then there is a loud boom when it finally ignites.  The oven door pops open partially from the pressure of this mini-explosion, endangering anyone in front of the oven.  Had my little daughter been standing there when this happened it would have knocked right into her head and who knows what could have happened.  This is a dangerous situation that can cause larger explosions with higher gas build-up until ignition. The GE technician that came down in response to my service request stated that this is a common part to go bad and can be repaired by switching it out at the customer's expense or with a discount that GE may offer.  The problem is that GE should recall this defective part on all similar ovens and not endanger their customers by allowing a part that often goes bad to remain in their homes, when there is a strong likelihood that it will eventually cause explosions if not diagnosed and repaired shortly after it begins to go bad.  GE needs to use more reliable components in an oven and not endanger their customers with risk of explosions in their kitchens by using parts that deteriorate on their own after only a few years without any misuse on the part of the consumer.  GE refuses to record this as a potentially dangerous and hazardous situation and just considers it a common technical issue for their business records.
justification: The incident involves a delayed ignition causing a mini-explosion that could potentially injure someone, as evidenced by the oven door popping open and the risk to a child's head.

incident_description:
Kitchen Aid Model  KGCC506 RWW04 is a fire hazard.

I spoke with Kitchen Aid's Safety department to report that flames shot up out of a knob hole because water went into the hole and activated the electric starter without the knob being turned on.  Their response was:

- no recall or fix will occur other than to repair my cooktop
- no changes will be made to the design of the cook top
- users must change their behaviors in order to prevent the problem

I am quite concerned that this hazard exists in my home and many other homes around the country.  It is very unrealistic to expect that a pot will not boil over or that people will not drip water on the cooktop to clean it.

The safety supervisor even reported she had seen the problem in her home 3 years ago and suggested a fix to the design team yet she was told it could not be done and did not feel comfortable escalating the problem further.  She even had to pay for the repair herself!  It is very disconcerting to hear that Whirlpool/KitchenAid has such a poor work environment that the safety supervisor has to be concerned about her job just for reporting and attempting to resolve a legitimate safety issue.  

Murphy's Law dictates that this problem will continue to occur.  You cannot depend on users' behaviors to change.  Pots boil over, beverages spill, people use water to clean stoves, water leaks occur in homes, kids play around with squirt guns, etc., etc.  Whirpool is guilty of knowingly allowing a serious hazard to exist in consumers homes.

There is a very simple fix that would resolve probably 90% of the incidents.  Flexible water catchers can be slid over the knob stems into the holes.  Our previous KitchenAid cooktop did not have this problem; certainly it can be solved.

I also would like to know that new models are not designed/manufactured with the same hazard.

I hope you decide to take this matter seriously and will immediately take steps to begin solving this problem.
justification: The incident describes flames shooting out of a knob hole, posing a fire hazard, which could lead to injuries. The likelihood is high due to common user behaviors like spills and cleaning.

incident_description: I set my oven (Whirlpool Model RF385PXE) to cook at 350F as usual, placed a casserole dish with chicken in the oven, and set the timer for one hour. A short time later I heard a click sound in the kitchen so I went to investigate. The oven had the letters "CLN" and "locked" which is the self clean cycle. I hit cancel and the message changed to "COOL". However, there was a red glow coming from the oven which was the "broil element" and it was red hot. I waited a couple minutes thinking the element would cool off, but it was still red hot. I had to turn the oven off with the circuit breaker. I then let the oven cool for a while. Our oven has an electric lock so I had to turn the circuit breaker back on to allow the oven to unlock. Thinking that maybe I had inadvertently hit "auto clean", I thought I would try turning the oven back on. Again, I set my oven to cook at 350F. A short time later I heard a click and once again the oven had the letters "CLN" and the "broil element" was red hot. I again cancelled the oven, but the "broil element" stayed red hot. So I turned off the oven with the circuit breaker again. After the oven had cooled down, I turned the circuit breaker back on. Without touching anything on the oven, the "broil element" came back on red hot again! So it appears as though there is something faulty with the top "broil element". According to the manual, the broil temp is automatically set at 500F! It is scary to think that this oven would go into broil mode or self clean mode with food locked inside and no way to cancel it short of turning off power to the oven!
justification: The oven malfunctioned repeatedly, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

I was using the brand new Breville BJE510XL Juice Fountain Multi-speed juicer. This was the first time that I had used it.  I read all the directions, unpacked, cleaned and assembled it before the first run. There were no left over packing parts. Everything was seated correctly and the safety arm was in place.
 
I was juicing ginger root which has about the same consistency as carrots so the machine was set on 5. Initially, I was not at all impressed with how much juice was coming from the juicer. I was using it 4-5 minutes when my wife said she smelled electrical burning. She was about 10 feet away in back of the juicer. At that time, the warning E did not appear on the LED screen. I stopped the juicer, refitted the parts. I did not smell any electrical burning smell anywhere around the juicer. I believed she smelled the ginger.  I started it up again, and within half to one minute, my wife said the juicer sounded as if it were straining. As I was looking down to the LED screen again to check, the plastic filter bowl exploded with an extremely loud noise, showering me on the chest and abdomen and about a third of the kitchen with plastic shards, wire mesh shards and ginger pulp. It was fortunate that the juicer was on a low counter so my eyes were not level with the filter bowl.
 
I sorted through the debris and collected as many pieces as I could find as well as spent 45 minutes cleaning walls, cabinets, and large appliances that were in the direct line of the explosion. I searched carefully through the pulp container and all of the dispersed pulp looking for any possible foreign body that might have been in the ginger but found no hard or metal objects other than the remnants of the micro mesh filter basket.
 
To say the least, under the wrong circumstances, the explosion could have blinded me or caused facial damage, not to mention that the sound scared the hell out of both of us. I have reported this to the Consumer Product Safety even though you said that this was a rare event, as I feel that your product could inflict serious injury on another customer.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage and potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred.

The consumer stated that he googled refrigerator leaks on the internet and found out that this is a common problem.

The consumer's wife stated that she wants to see Whirlpool take some action to remedy the product.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring surgery and rehabilitation, and the description indicates that refrigerator leaks are a common problem.

incident_description:
During the period of May 8th to May 11th my microwave, MAGIC CHEF Model MCD1311ST experienced multiple electric surges causing my circuit breaker to trip.  Not knowing if it was my outlet or the microwave, I moved the microwave to another outlet. Within two days the microwave had another power surge and a slight electric burning smell came from the unit.  The unit would no longer power on.

Looking for a replacement unit, I went to Amazon.com.  I was amazed to read reviews on my microwave. 50% of those reviews reported similar problems within 2 years of purchase
justification: The incident involved electrical surges and a burning smell without injury, and similar issues were reported in 50% of reviews, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased these Pyrex dishes in the fall of 2012.  They have been used just a few times, no more than 10. This particular dish was used and placed in dishwasher over a week ago, and was placed in my cabinet, with 2 other glass casseroles on top, as usual.  

I was taking a shower and my son was in the other room watching tv, when we both heard a loud sound. He said it sounded like something fell or broke, but we didn't see anything until later that day when I was fixing dinner, I noticed tiny pieces of glass on the counter. When I opened the cabinet, there were literally thousands of pieces of glass everywhere .    There was no one near the cabinet, and the dish hadn't been used in over a week

I have pictures of dish if you need to see them
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered without any contact or recent use, causing glass pieces to scatter, but no one was injured.

incident_description: Dish in question was around four years old. It looked new with no chips or crazing and was well maintained. I prepared a box of scalloped potatoes mixing two cups of hot water with potatoes, sauce mix and .5 cup of evaporated milk. I added an additional cup of chedder cheese to the dish. I put the dish in a large toaster oven which had been preheated to 425. The oven was on convection mode. After around five minutes the pan simply broke into many many pieces spreading a cheeezy milky mixture through out the oven.
justification: The dish broke, causing a mess but no reported injury, indicating an incident without harm. Such breakage is unlikely given the dish's maintained condition.

incident_description:
Hamilton Beach 6 Slice Capacity Toaster Oven. Model 31507R, Series A1901DV

Timer failed, such that timer continues past the "Off" position and continues until it stops at the "Stay On" position.  Oven then continues to operate indefinitely.  On testing for the problem, the timer consistently failed to stop at "Off", failed to sound the bell, and continued to "Stay On".  This failure is not obvious to the operator until the contents of the oven begin to burn.  This is a serious fire hazard as well as a burn hazard for anyone who, unaware the oven is still operating, touches the outside of the appliance.  Once the failure occurs, the oven cannot be turned off, except by unplugging the power cord.
justification: The timer failure poses a serious fire and burn hazard, but no actual injury or death is reported in the description.

incident_description: I set the oven to the self cleaning cycle.  After the self cleaning cycle had ended and the door unlocked, I opened the oven to check and see if the oven was clean.  When I opened the oven the inside layer of glass (the glass between the inside glass and outside glass - there are three layers of glass) shattered and glass fell out every where.  This was only the second time I had ever run the cleaning cycle on the oven since we purchased and closed on the house on 3/1/13.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was an incident that caused damage to the oven, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: We had a Pampered Chef 4 cup glass batter bowl explode while sitting in a pantry cupboard.  There was nothing in the bowl or on it and no lid sealing it.  The bowl exploded blowing glass up into the shelf above and to the shelves below.  (I have photos)  It hadn't been used in over 36 hours and then only for room temperature diced produce.  If it had been out on the counter, someone could have been seriously injured.
justification: The bowl exploded causing property damage but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury. Such spontaneous breakage is rare.

incident_description:
(04/28/2013) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. She was advised that it was not involved in the recall. She was advised that they would not pay for the repair. The consumer stated that she is having the same problem as the recall-Rel#09-333.

(04/26/2013) The consumer  stated that she went to cook dinner. The stove would turn on and off on its on or would not come on at all. She checked the internet and discovered that there were problems with the stove. She disconnected the stove at the circuit breaker. She stated that she did not have any problems before. The consumer stated that the problem is with all of the burners.

The consumer stated thath she thinks that Kenmore should repair her stove.
justification: The stove malfunctioned but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller moved into her new home in 2008 and in the home was a new smooth top electrical range that gave the caller no problems until around April 20th, 2013.

Caller had the front left burner and the front right burners turned on and set to 5 or 6, however the left front burner felt noticeably cooler than the right front.
She attempted to adjust the temperature but could not turn the left burner off, on and could not adjust the temperature.
The right burner responded to the knob that turns it off with no problems.
However the left burner would not turn off until caller tried three or four a tempts 

When the burner did turn off, it sparked from behind the unit.  This has now happened on 2 occasions.

Caller has contacted the manufacturer and they are not concerned

There have been no injuries
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that sparked but caused no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The issue has occurred twice, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: [Electrical] fire in our dishwasher - Kenmore model 66517472300.  Seriel Number FR2602312.  Fortunately it was caught very early and caused no apparent damage to anything else in the house.  Fire department arrived and shut the electrical circuit and checked the device.  They suggested we check to see if the unit had been recalled.  It does NOT appear that this particular model has been recalled.  however, I noticed that similar GE/Kenmore dishwashers (1997 to 2001) WERE RECALLED for risk of electrical fire.  our unit is from 2004.  So, I thought it would be best to report it, in  case others with this model had the same problem.
justification: The electrical fire caused no apparent damage or injury, and was caught early, indicating a low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
On May 14, 2013 at my residence of [REDACTED]. A 2.5 year old Kenmore Electric Smooth Top electric Range. 790. 9210 Black.  While in the kitchen, the oven turned on to preheat, the top control panel arched continuously as flames erupted from top leading edge of the right side of the control panel face and out from the back of the range.   It was not until the breaker in the basement was turned off that the arching stopped and shortly thereafter the fire burned itself out. 

The fire department was called and confirmed that the fire was out.  The fire department took the range out of the house.  A fire marshal inspection took place the next day. 
In calling Sears, I was advised there was no warranty or coverage for this loss.  Sears made no mention of a recall.  It was by CPSC web search that we learned of the recall.  I called Sears back, brought this recall to their attention and their response was much different.  The end results of the call to Sears remains unknown to us.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the fire department confirmed the fire was out without further issues.

incident_description:
Dishwasher caught fire ;
Caller purchased her dishwasher in May 2001 and had no problems with it until April 30th, 2013 around 8 o'clock when she started the dishwasher then went upstairs to take her shower.

Approximately twenty minutes after starting the dishwasher and during her shower she began smelling a burning odor, she grabbed her robe and returned downstairs to find that her dishwasher had been on fire and that her entire downstairs level of her home was filled with black smoke.

There were holes burned through the area where the controls had been and the front of the dishwasher was blackened.

She contacted the manufacturer May 1st, 2013 and a tech was sent to her home, said that her dishwasher was not fixable and then took the front portion off to show her that her wires were burned.

The Bureau of Consumer Protection referred caller to CPSC

She believes that the breaker may have tripped which removed power from the dishwasher and so extinguished the fire.

She also stated that if this had not happened she believes that her home could very well have burned down and if she had not smelled the burning and had not known to get out of the shower it could have been tragic.

There were no injuries
justification: The dishwasher caught fire causing significant damage but no injuries, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but do occur.

incident_description: OVEN FROM MAGIC CHEF GAS RANGE TURNED ITSELF ON AND FIRE STARTED WITHIN OVEN COMPARTMENT.
justification: The incident involved a fire starting in the oven compartment, which is a significant safety hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a GE stove, model number JBP15DM1WW, serial number FZ243414P. I purchased this via website because I was looking for various features, such as front mounted knobs. A few days after it was installed I noticed that the oven had been turned on. Apparently this occurred when I brushed up against it with my backside. Two days later the oven was turned on again, this time by my dog's wagging tail. The burner knobs need to be pushed in and then turned, which is not the case with the oven knob. I've since removed the oven knob to prevent my house from burning down. Even with the knob removed, the stem can easily be turned by hand.
I contacted Lowe's, where I purchased the stove and they sent out a repair person He stated that this is the way it was made. I then contacted the GE Customer Advocate. She stated that there are models that are made this way.
I canÃÂt believe that anyone would intentionally design a heat generating appliance with such an unsafe, hazardous feature. There are many people who store food in their ovens, bread, chips, etc. With an oven that can be turned on without human effort or knowledge is a fire and/or lawsuit waiting to happen. I can just imagine someone's grandchild turning on the oven, even using just the stem. Then fire erupts in the middle of the night and there are fatalities, with GE being responsible due to an unsafe product.
In addition, why isn't there an indicator light which goes off when the oven has reached its set temperature?
justification: The incident describes an unsafe design that can lead to unintentional oven activation, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
April 15, 2013
US Consumer Product Safety Commission
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814
Regarding: Important danger in the following product
We purchased a new Frigidaire Gas Range from Sears in Coeur d'Alene, 10 in October, 2012 for our new home.
The range is a Gallery Model# FGGF3031KBJ/VF20747412.
Our Microwave is set above the range where the cabinet provides the space, as most are.
When you put something in the microwave or take something out it is natural to lean against the front of the range to
reach it. The pressure from leaning on the nobs ignites a burner and has caused many close calls from catching our
clothes on fire.
Also there has been three times that the burners did not ignite but the gas has escaped into the rooms.
The last incident was yesterday. I was sick in bed with a bad cold and my husband came home and I got up to greet him.
He said, "What is that smell?" and I said "I don't smell anything!" A burner was just slightly turned and it had probably
been like that since I warmed my coffee in the microwave that morning. We rushed to open everything up and it took
hours to get the gas out. I had been in the back bedroom most of the day.
I am asking you what would be the right action for us to take so we don't burn our new house down. We can't always
remember to check the burners and sometimes other people in the family use the stove.
As I said, it turns a burner on with just the slightest pressure on the nobs when you are reaching up and if you turn your
body to set something down after using the microwave.
We were very lucky that were not burned badly or were not asphyxiated from the gas fumes.
Please inform us what we should do in this case.
We like the range except for this problem.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
cc: US Consumer Product Safety Commission
Association of Home Appliance Manufacturers
justification: The incident describes close calls with potential for injury or asphyxiation due to gas leaks and accidental burner ignition, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Fire in GE stove/oven
                                                                                       Design Defect

Our 4 month old GE stove/oven has had 2 fires in the last 3 weeks which I believe is due to a
design defect. Mice from the neighboring field had stockpiled food/nesting material in the
bottom of the oven below a steel plate, making this fuel unnoticeable when loading the oven.
An examination of the range shows that there is no screening whatsoever to prevent mice
entry; in fact, the back and bottom of the range is wide open giving unfettered access to the
burner area.
GE has done nothing except tell us they are unilaterally voiding our warranty due to an
undisclosed policy. I don't expect GE to catch our mice, but I do expect that they would be
cognizant of mice in kitchens and design their products to prevent mouse-caused fires. A little
screen in the manufacturing process would solve the problem.
GE model : JG8282DETWW
justification: The incident involved fires caused by a design defect allowing mice access, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says that he washed his dishes.  When the cycle was done he closed the door and shut the machine off.  He left at 6:30pm and came back around 10:30pm to the presence of fog and the smell of burning plastic. 

The dishwasher and granite counter top were extremely hot.  His wife opened the dishwasher and it was extremely melted.  The fire dept was called and they said they believe the heating rod never turned off and the extensive heat relief valve did not work.  The valve is supposed to turning the power off when it is too hot and it did not.  

The consumer received a letter from the manufacturer in October 2012 about possibly on a recall.  The consumer contacted the firm by phone and read the model and serial number and was told by the mfr that the unit was not covered under the recall and was safe.

The fire department mentioned that his house could have been completely torched if they had not come home for another thirty minutes.   

He has contacted the firm via email a day after the incident and a follow up phone call and has not received a response.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and a near-miss for a house fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We recently had Wausau paper towel dispensers installed in our childcare center through a paper supply company.  Three of our adult staff have already gotten lacerations to their fingers including myself when pushing on the dispenser bar.  There is a rotating cylinder inside the machine that rotates that the blade is attached onto.   Most times you can push the bar and nothing will happen but paper dispensing.  Sometimes, however, if the blade is positioned on the bottom, your finger will be sliced.  I took a picture of my painful, bleeding finger if you would like me to send it to you.  Most people will be embarrassed if this happens to them and not report it.  We know how to work a paper towel dispenser being in the daycare environment for many years.
justification: The incident describes lacerations to staff fingers, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as multiple staff have been injured and the issue is recurrent.

incident_description:
Consumer place the oven on self clean for about 3-4 hours. Consumer heard a sound and was unsure of what the sound was. She looked in the kitchen and didn't notice anything because the oven was locked and still being cleaned. Once the cleaning function was complete the oven unlocked and she noticed the glass cracked in the window. Consumer thought the door began to condensate. 

She states a glass panel in between the door broke. Pieces have shattered because consumer's left middle finger was cut. Though consumer is unsure of how it happend.

The consumer spoke with the retailers department 12/31/12 (rep's name unknown). 
The information was documented and a report was filed. An appointment has to be made by the consumer to have a repairman service the range. The consumer was told there were 3 layered glass panes in the door. The middle layer of glass has cracked completely. 

The middle left finger was ran under water and pressure and band-aid was applied. 

There were no damages to report.
justification: The consumer sustained a cut on their finger from shattered glass, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
(03/14/2013) The consumer stated that she had the oven on and also one of the burners was on. There was a code of F10 came on the control panel. The stove started beeping and she was not able to turn the oven off or stop the beeping. The consumer had to pull the stove out and unplug it to get the beeping to stop. The temperature was super hot. The food inside the oven was blackened. Also the pan was burned. The consumer stated that she had a company called Mr. Appliance at 508-917-5055, to come out to do the repair. They told her that the control unit needed to be replaced. It had burned itself out. The consumer did have the control unit replaced. The consumer also stated that her neighbor has the same stove and is having the same issue.  

The consumer stated that she is having the same problem as the stoves in the recall Rel #09-333.
(04/16/2013) The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer to check on the recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove causing overheating and property damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My wife received a burn while attempting to remove the lid. The burn was a result of touching the side of the cooker.

The Sunbeam d.b.a. Jardens Consumer Solutions would place a visible warning on the outside of the box warning consumers of the potential of receiving a burn while using this device.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) based on the frequency mentioned.

incident_description:
(04/6/2013) The consumer stated her husband was going to open the refrigerator door. He is right handed. The door opens from left to right. When he opened the door, the plastic handle broke. He lost his balance. He fell to the right on his right arm. He hit his head on the floor and also broke his arm. Her husband called her to tell her that he fell. He could not get up from the floor because his arm was broken. She came home and with the help of her brother, got him up off the floor. She told him that he need to go to the hospital because his head was bleeding.  She stated that his arm was very red. They went to Claramaass Medical Center in Belleville, NJ. He was was seen by [REDACTED]. The doctor did some blood work. He stitched up the gash in his head. The doctor also did a cat scan. He xrayed his arm and found that the arm was broke. His arm was put in a fiberglass cast. He was referred to an orthopedic doctor. Her husband was seen by the orthiopedic doctor on 4/8-[REDACTED] in Montclair, NJ. He advised him to keep the fiberglass cast on. He advised him that he did not need on operation to reset the break. Her husband mentioned to [REDACTED] that he experienced blurry vision. The doctor advised him to see an optomologist. He put a hard cast on the arm on 4/12.

The consumer stated that her husband saw an optomologist on 4/15. His name is [REDACTED] in North Arlinton, NJ. [REDACTED] was concerned with the blurry and double vision. He suggested that theysee their primary care physician and get another cat scan. They went to see [REDACTED] in Nutley. The doctor suggested an MRI of the brain and the orbits. Nothing significant was found.

Her husband is still experiencing a problem with double vision. [REDACTED] suggested that he see a neurologist. The consumer stated that they have an appointment for 5/15.

The consumer stated she first call the place of purchased. They advised her to call the service people. The service company wanted $110 for the service call, &26 for the handle and $75 labor to install the handle. The consumer called the manufacturer to tell them about the problem. She was told that they would send her a handle for $26. Her warranty and extended warranty had expired. She was told that her husband could put the handle back on. She advised him that her husband broke her arm. She stated that she was told that she could put it on.  

The consumer stated that her husband has gone through a lot because of a cheaply made product. She stated that the handle is made of plastic.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken arm, head injury requiring stitches, and ongoing vision problems, which classify it as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) because such severe outcomes from a refrigerator handle breaking are not common.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his smooth top electric range was not working properly. He stated that the left rear burner continues to turn on by itself and it would not turn off. The consumer stated that he turned the knob to turn it off it would not go off. He stated that he had to turn off the circuit breaker to turn off the range. 

The consumer stated that he had not use the range since the incident and he kept the circuit breaker off in fear it would turn on again. The consumer stated that it was the first time he experienced this problem.

No one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he noticed online that there was a recall (# 09-333) for the same hazard, yet his range was not included in the recall. He stated that he believed that this recall should be expanded. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that his range was not included on the recall and that there was nothing they could do. He stated that informed him that he was going to have to get his range repair on with an independent technician.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that posed a potential hazard but resulted in no injury, aligning with severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the consumer's report of a first-time issue and the existence of a related recall.

incident_description: I ran the dishwasher through a regular cycle.  There seemed to be more steam than usual toward the end of the cycle and I could smell a plastic burning odor.  WHen I opened the door after the cycle ended, it was so extraordinarily hot that I left the door open and went to another room while the dishwasher cooled down.  It took a long time to cool down and when I could finally access it, the soap holder latch had completely melted as had parts of the dishwasher lower rack.  The dishes were not clean and were spotted with a brown scum in some places.  The dishwasher is unusable.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher and potential safety hazards (burning odor, extreme heat), but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I turned my oven on to 350 degrees to preheat oven. In less than 5 minutes, lower left coil in oven turned white, flaming and continued to burn towards back of oven along coil! Turned oven off, grabbed fire extinguisher and ran to turn off breaker. When breaker was turned off, fire slowed down and stopped. Smoke came out of vents on top of range. Smoke continued for a period of time.

Coil completely broke off about two inches from where coil first started on fire. Oven was completely clean when preheating. No burnt food, etc in oven!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but was quickly controlled without injury, indicating a moderate severity and unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
On 14 May 2013 my wife made her daily pot of coffee using her Krups KM405 coffee maker (KM405550/5CA). It was a birthday gift for her purchased in Sept 2012. She made coffee about 11 AM. At about 12:30 PM she left house to go shopping. The coffee maker has auto shut off after 1 hour (Programmable 1, 2, or 3 hours). The carafe had about 1/3 pot of coffee left in it.
I was working in yard and came back in house about 1:15 PM. Nothing appeared out of ordinary. I left house to go to store about 1:30PM. Upon returning I was in house and nothing appeared out of ordinary. I went out and was working in front of garage. At about 2:15 PM I heard a strange sound and went to investigate. As I walked on porch I realized it was our house alarm, fire alarm going off. As I entered kitchen flames were coming out of coffee maker and going up front of cabinets and to ceiling. I grabbed the kitchen fire extinguisher and put out fire. Heavy black smoke was throughout downstairs.
The damage was: 1) large burned spot on cabinet top, 2) soot over cabinet fronts and bottom, 3) soot on ceiling and 4) large hunks of melted plastic all over the counter tops. l started to clean up mess. I was able to get most of soot from cabinets and walls as well as the small splatters of melted plastic from walls and cabinets. The ceiling (white) is too covered so I will have to paint it. The burned spot on counter top will require new counter tops.
I touched coffee maker after fire was out to take it out of house and burned tips of two fingers.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage and minor burns to fingers, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I was baking in the oven and went to open the door. I heard a pop and the glass door shattered.
justification: The glass door shattered, but there was no mention of injury, so the severity is 2.

incident_description:
When pulling oven rack outward with a full-size baked lasagna, the oven walls bowed outward causing the rack to fall from one side, dumping the dish and contents into the oven. This is the second time this has happened and upon closer inspection, I noticed the oven wall are constructed of rather thin, flexible metal.  Apparently any dish with much weight causes the oven walls to bow out wider than the racks. We are fortunate no one was severely burned by this incident. I am 57 and have owned/used many ovens in my lifetime, some more than 20 years old, and have never experienced such an occurrence. Upon researching this, it appears to be a common problem with certain Kenmore ovens. I do not understand why there has been no recall or Sears doesn't at least stand by their product reputation by fixing or replacing such an obvious design flaw.  Every incident I have read about online, Sears expects the consumer to pay for "repairs." There is at least one other report on this site of the same issue and in what appears to be an auto generated message from Sears, they state they take these reports seriously and provide an 800 number to call. I called the number and an automated message gave me 7 options to choose from. None related to customer service or concerns unless you were calling about an existing repair call. No option existed to speak with a customer "care" representative.

Oh, and another hazard with the same oven, as I was wiping down the oven door one day, my finger slid along an edge of the door frame and an un-smoothed edge sliced through my finger like a razor blade!

The Kenmore Elite Double oven stove manufacture date is 2009, and the model is 790.98023800
justification: The incident caused injury (sliced finger) and potential for severe burns, with a recurring design flaw.

incident_description:
The metal molding around the exterior surface of the range gets extremely hot when the oven is in use.  The consumer noticed this problem from the earlier times he used it, but didn't think much of it.  The oven was used at 350 when he noticed the problem, but the consumer became extremely concerned when he used the oven at 450 degrees, because it became hotter at higher temperatures

(5/2 or 5/3)  The consumer contacted the retailer and they arranged for a service technician to come out and look at the range/oven.  

(5/4/13)  A technician from Countrywide Appliance came out and looked at the range/oven.  The tech. had asked the consumer to set the oven to 475 degrees prior to his arrival and the consumer did as requested.  When the tech. measured the outside molding with an infrared gun, it registered in the range 160 - 166 degrees across various parts of the oven door.  The tech. said that it was within specification, because it allowed for 180 degrees.

(5/7/13)  The consumer called the mfr. about his concern, but their rep. indicated that they were within specifications.  The rep. told the consumer that they would pass this information on to another department.

The consumer also responded to the mfr's survey and he stated that he felt this presented a potential for a burn.
justification: The metal molding gets extremely hot, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
My wife cut her thumb and required 4 stitches.  This occurred while washing and drying the dual purpose cutting blade for the first time.  The problem is that the cutting blade is a disk and has cutting blades, for different purposes, on the top and the bottom.  Of course the bottom ones are out of sight.  After the incident I also washed and dried the disk and found that it was necessary to concentrate so as to not cut your fingers where you naturally hold it on the bottom.

I plan to return the appliance to the store.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut requiring stitches, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) due to the design flaw in the cutting blade.

incident_description: I was preheating the oven, when an explosion occurred causing fire in the oven.  I immediately shut the oven off.  When my son looked at it, he found that not only had the element blown out on the oven but it had burned a hole about 2 inches in diameter in the bottom of the oven.  It should be noted that the oven on this stove had not been used very much.
justification: The incident involved an oven explosion causing fire and damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(04/24/2013) The consumer stated that the igniter switches are not clearly marked with off and on. There is no warning light that indicates that the burner is on. The consumer stated that he believes it should be retrofitted with a red LED or some device to indicate that the burner is on. The consumer sttaed that this is an unsafe product.

The consumer stated that he will include a picture.
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard but no actual injury or incident occurred.

incident_description:
2 year old Corelle Livingware (pattern Serenity) dinner plate tipped off our standard height kitchen counter onto the wood floor and shattered into tiny shards with a very loud cracking sound. It was not knocked with any force, just not quite placed all the way on the counter. The hundreds of razor sharp pieces extended at least 10' from the point of impact, unlike other dishware which might break into several pieces close to where it hits the floor. The plate was dry with a small amount of food residue on it; plate, counter, and kitchen were all a normal room temperature. The plate had not been heated in the microwave prior to being used for the meal.
Based on the manufacturer's exclusion of "accidental breakage" from the warranty (which appears to cover almost nothing that realistically might happen to a dish in use in a household) and many other consumer reports of manufacturer inaction in response to similar incidents, I did not report this to the manufacturer; however, I took pictures to document the breakage.
justification: The plate shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The high occurrence likelihood is based on similar consumer reports and the described breakage scenario.

incident_description:
The handle caught fire, although, the package indicates that it has a "heat resistant handle." There were significant
flames and the proof is that there is soot all over my apartment. I will need to clean the walls, perhaps repaint, and
empty the cabinets. We put the fire out with salt and then a wet cloth. I'm just grateful I got to it on time before it
spread.
justification: The handle caught fire causing significant flames and soot, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was contained.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Range (model #790.78733406). The door handle broke unexpectedly pulled apart as I was opening the oven door. Close inspection revealed the handle screw thread stripped and popped open. During this event, the thin stainless steel cover cut my finger. No medical intervention required, but concerned about the quality and safety potential.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut finger) but did not require medical intervention, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the handle failure.

incident_description:
The gas ignited when the door was opened.  This happened in the lower oven twice between April 2012 and May 2013.  Each time the oven was set to preheat and the indicator showed the temperature rising.  A gas smell kept getting stronger.  When I opened the door, there was immediate combustion of the gas.  

The first time it singed my hair, eyebrows and melted my eyelashes.  Although my face felt hot, it was not burned.  I called the manufacturer who directed me to have it looked at by an appliance repair person.  He came by but could not replicate the problem (it was under warranty). The repairman advised me to use the unit cautiously, standing to the side when opening the door in case of a reoccurrence. 

Today, May 13, 2013, the smell of gas was getting stronger while the digital display showed the lower oven pre-heating.  I cautiously opened the door, standing to the side after the first incident.  The gas ignited and singed the hair on my right arm.  I called the manufacturer again who directed me to call an appliance repair person.  I called Apple Appliance Service again and left a message, waiting to schedule an appointment.
justification: The incident caused singed hair and eyebrows, indicating minor injury, and occurred twice under similar conditions.

incident_description:
10/21/12 	a) Purchased from Home Depot, a Gas Range Oven (with 5 year Protection Plan).     Model# MGR7662WW .
05/05/13	a)  Used Self Cleaning Oven for first time.
		b)  1/2 later, the inside glass shattered all throughout the oven.  For several hours as stove cooled down, I could hear glass falling inside the range.
		c)  Contacted Home Depot Warranty Number [REDACTED] and reported the incident to a rep named [REDACTED].  She mentioned that she had heard of it happening before.
		d)  Agent said someone would be out on Tuesday (05/07/13) to repair the range.
		e)  I told the agent that I wanted to request a replacement range because I would not be comfortable with the possibility of remaining glass left in the oven, falling into my food.
		f)  Agent told me that I would have to escalate that to the tech upon arrival.
		g)  Incident #[REDACTED] issued to me.

05/07/13	a) Contacted by tech [REDACTED], from A&E Factory Service.
		b)  Tech says he could not expedite my request for a replacement range.  Said he didn't have the authority to do so.
		c)  Since glass had to be replaced anyway, tech orders and replaces glass and uses a vacuum to try and suck out the shattered glass.
		d)  I called the Home Depot warranty number again and spoke with a rep named [REDACTED].  Told her that the rep couldn't escalate.  She told me that I would have to escalate to Home Depot.
		d)  I contacted the local Home Depot Service manager where I purchased the range.   I told her my concerns about the broken glass and not feeling comfortable cooking and eating from a range that had shattered glass all inside the range.  I also shared with her that the tech could not determine what caused it to happen.  And, I also told her of my request for a replacement range and the finger pointing between the Warranty dept and tech).   I was told by the Service Manager that she understood my concerns and apologized for what I'd experienced, but Home Depot could not replace the range and gave me the number to Maytag [REDACTED].  The Home Depot manager said only Maytag would have the decision to replace the range.

05/09/13	a)  After a day and a half of trying to properly contact and communicate with Maytag, I finally reached one of their agents, [REDACTED], who was rather rude, abrupt and abrasive in her tone of voice to me.  As I tried to explain my situation, she would cut me off and tell me that if my range was fixed there was nothing else Maytag could do.  I finally had to request her to change her tone of voice and to stop being abrasive in her voice to me.  Her tone of voice and behavior kind of subsided afterwards. She told me there was no escalation.  She had already done so.
		c)  I ended the call by politely telling her that I would do my own escalation.

incident_description:
The consumer placed a bowl of instant grits in the microwave oven and turned it on.  The bowl was ceramic.  Within 2 seconds of starting the microwave, smoke began billowing from the bottom of microwave (and in front of the door) and he noticed an electrical burning odor.   The consumer turned the microwave off, by using the control feature and then he unplugged it from the wall outlet.

The items that were placed inside the microwave were not damaged and the food did not even get warm

The consumer has never had any problems in the past with this microwave. 

(5/2/2013)  The consumer called the manufacturer and he was transferred to a rep. (name unknown).  The rep. took some information from the consumer and told him that someone would give him a call back within 24 hours.  The consumer was advised to discontinue use of the microwave oven and he does not plan to use any more.

The manufacnturer's rep.. gave the consumer a reference # [REDACTED].

UPDATE:
I received a phone call from a Panasonic representative and all she said was that the microwave needed maintenance.  No offer made by Panasonic to fix it.

incident_description: 1 hour ago I started our Whirlpool Model MH1160XS Microwave Hood combination (manufacture date 2007) and after about 3 minutes smoke and a terrible odor began billowing from the upper right corner of the unit.  I immediately opened the door to stop the cycle.  Smoke continued to pour from the unit for several minutes.  There was not a fire, but I happened to be in close proximity to the unit when the smell and smoke started.  This is an over the stove unit which is mounted under a short kitchen cabinet.  If I had not been close by, there would have been a potential fire situation.  This is extremely dangerous!!!  We have smoke detectors, but I caught the problem before it went off.
justification: Smoke and odor emitted from the microwave, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: My kitchenaid microwave turns on by itself and powers on very high heat to the point where the entire inside and OUTSIDE are extremely hot to the touch and no matter what we do it won't turn off unless we unplug the entire unit. If we were not home or asleep when it happened our entire home would have been on fire. I see on line that there have been numerous complaints about this same issue with this same model number....why is a recall not happening? Kitchenaid wants to replace the control panel but unlike some others my control panel did not state  "PAN" or anything at all and I don't feel safe with this unit..a recall needs to be issued this is a very SERIOUS matter which can cause much destruction! We are not talking about a broken handle we are talking about a fire occurring!
justification: The microwave turning on by itself and overheating poses a significant fire hazard, which could lead to severe destruction if unattended.

incident_description: My Kenmore oven glass door shattered about 30 minutes after I had cooked something. No one was near the door or had bumped into it. I read online about similar incidents; one news agency stated that the CPSC wanted to hear about these incidents.
justification: The oven door shattered but no one was injured, and similar incidents have been reported, indicating a known issue.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore elite stand alone oven with gas burners.  When we bake or clean the oven, a noxious smoke comes out regardless of how clean the oven is.  Upon investigation, the insulation under the bottom of the oven is disintegrating and burning up.  It has crumbled into "charcoal" pellets.

When I called Sears (where we purchased), it indicated that my oven was not part of any recall and I would have to pay to have a service repairman look at it.
justification: The incident involves noxious smoke from disintegrating insulation, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Kenmore Over the Range Microwave Oven P/N 721800114401 S/N 506TA0231.  Glass in door spontaneously shattered when not in use.
justification: The glass in the microwave door shattered spontaneously, which could potentially cause injury if someone was nearby, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Re:  Cuisinart Coffee Plus DCC-1200 defective.

About 2 months ago, while we were away our cleaning lady told us that when she came to clean, our coffee maker was left on and very hot with no coffee in the carafe.  The pot had been turned off before we left.  She unplugged it and removed the carafe.

Today May, 11, I heard a hissing, snapping & crackling sound, like liquid hitting the burner.  Also an acrid smell.  I went to the kitchen and found the coffee maker  OFF but smoking.  When I removed the carafe from the burner, the burner was RED HOT.   In fact it looked ready to burst into flame.   I immediately unplugged the coffee maker and moved everything outside.

Had our cleaning lady not come by to clean and discovered this the first time, and had we been gone on our planned  vacation (we are leaving on the 12th), our house would have burned down and yet there has been NO recall on this defective product.  This is unacceptable.
justification: The incident involved a defective coffee maker that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it happened twice under specific conditions.

incident_description: The right front burner on my Kenmore Elite will not shut off. This happened a few years ago and we repaired the range. There was a recall at the time. Now it's happened again. I noticed what I was cooking was burning even though I did not have the burner turned up very high. I lifted the pan off the burner and saw it was red hot. I turned the burner off and it stayed red hot. I had to shut off the breaker for the appliance to get it to shut off.
justification: The burner not shutting off poses a fire hazard but no injury was reported in this incident.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite dishwasher control board experienced failure that appears to include a minor fire as described by other owners of Whirlpppol, [REDACTED], REDACTED], and Sears Kenmore dishwashers.  Dishwasher was started and wife went to run errands.  It failed to complete the cycle and left water in the base of the unit.  The unit would not start but lights would come on for diagnostic mode.  Upon inspection it was discovered the control unit had a burnt area at prong P8, which separated the male prong from the board, leaving it embedded in the female plug (which was also melted).  Additional burn marks and indicator on the inside of the control unit cover.
justification: The incident involved a control board failure with minor fire evidence but no reported injuries, indicating a non-injury incident with possible recurrence based on similar reports.

incident_description: The glass on a Kenmore wall oven shattered when it was preheating. Fortunately neither of the young children were in the kitchen or the situation would be much worse.
justification: The glass shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: 2005 GE Dishwasher pdw9280j0ss Serial tg815865B.  The unit had a saftey recall due to control unit fires.  Mine had the recall performed but still caught on fire on 5/6/13.  GE has confirmed the fire and is replacing it.  They are not however helping me with the replacement of another unit in my house.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire despite the recall, indicating a significant safety issue, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was making dinner and after cooking my fish I put the oven in "keep warm" mode.  I went upstairs to put my son to sleep.  Approximately 15 minutes later I smelled smoke.  I came downstairs to discover that the broiler had spontaneously turned on and the oven was at its maximum temperature and the food was burning.  I turned off the oven which resolved the problem.  This problem, where the oven spontaneously turns on the broiler has recurred multiple times.  The oven was serviced on 11/1/10, 9/22/11, 12/15/11, 1/10/12, 2/23/12, and 1/18/13 for this same problem.  In early January 2013 the oven did this in the middle of the night on a Friday night while in "Sabbath Mode"  Had the smell of smoke not woken up our dog we would not have known that the oven was overheating.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred. The problem has recurred multiple times despite servicing, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

35 3/4 (W) x 34 1/4 (D) x 69 3/4 (H)

incident_description:
Kenmore Digital 4-slice Toaster Oven Model No. 100.80009
I owned this appliance for about three years, using it only 3-4 timer per week, still in like new condition. The glass door at the front of the toaster oven suddenly without warning, "exploded" with a loud crash, sending many small glass particles as far as three feet on the kitchen counter and all over the floor. Even the handle "flew" two feet away from the appliance. Luckily nobody was near the toaster oven at the time. When the glass shattered, the appliance was plugged in, but not in use. 
Even though my appliance was beyond the two year warranty, I tried contacting Sears (online, per telephone, at the store), but only got "the runaround". I feel that this is a safety issue, which has nothing to do with normal usage. My previous toaster oven lasted close to 20 years, until the heating elements finally gave out. I certainly would never expect the glass door to shatter.
This toaster oven is still being sold online and in stores as item no. 0081937000, model 19370.
Upon reading online reviews posted by other consumers, I learned that this is not an isolated occurrance. Several people posted that their glass doors exploded/shattered as well. Some owned their appliance only a few months when it happened. 
I believe that this is a dangerous product and should be taken off the market and recalled.
I would appreciate any feedback.
Thank you,   [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a toaster oven's glass door shattering, but no injuries occurred. Similar incidents reported by other users indicate a possible defect, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: I have a Samsung model SMH9207ST over range microwave oven which has begun turning on on it's own. Unplugging is the only way to stop it.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential hazard.

incident_description: My kitchen aid oven was on self clean mode. While I was in the bathroom I heard an explosion and something falling all over kitchen. I came out to my 2 yr old screaming and 9 month old crawling through shards of glass. I called whirlpool and the safety team wasn't sure if I should turn oven off or leave it on. They told me they can't have someone out until tomorrow afternoon and that I should buy a shop vac and clean it up. I told them I can't even close the door to the oven. They told me they have no control over their contractors and maybe someone will [be] out tomorrow to order parts!! They also told me that there may have been a tiny fracture in the glass that was not visible to the naked eye that caused this!!! Where is the warning???? My kids could have been blinded by flying shards of glass that flew from my kitchen and through my dining room.
justification: The incident involved an oven explosion with flying glass shards, but no injuries were reported despite the potential danger to the children.

incident_description: While cooking scalloped potatoes in my gas oven, the Anchor Hocking clear glass 8x8 2qt cooking dish shattered into more than 50 pieces and causing the door to my oven to slightly jar open, make a very loud sound, and scattering the contents of the pan all over the oven.  The oven was preheated to 425F, the dish was in the oven approximately 12 minutes into a 25 minute cooking time.  I have owned the cookware piece approximately 3 years and have used it for this exact purpose more than 20 times without incident prior to the sudden shattering.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish shattering but no injuries were reported, only property damage and a loud noise.

incident_description:
The caller stated that his electric range left front burner will not power off after it is being switched off.  He has been experiencing these problems- Section 3 for about a month and Section 2 on 4/29/13 only.  Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.  He has unplugged the unit to prevent a house fire.


4/29/13 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that his model was not part of the recall.  There were no prior services. A month ago he had problems with the range heating to different temperatures but the problem was resolved by switching off.

The caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while his spouse was using the oven at 400 degrees for baking, the temperature started to increase approximately 30 minutes later.  The heating elements were extremely hot, which appeared red.  She was unable to power it off, the circuit breaker was used the switch it off.  After a few mins the circuit breaker was switched on and the oven powered back on.  He unplugged the baking part of the oven. There were no prior services.  

The elements were red to yellow and no change in degrees. The only code showing was (DR).

Approximately 2 years ago there was a similar incident, however, when the circuit breaker was switched back on, the range did not power on.


4/28/13 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that a part would be sent out a cost of $200.  However, he does not know if the part that will be sent out would resolved the issue.  He feels that the range after 11 yrs should be able to function properly without a fire hazard.


Note:  Caller will add more info when report is received.

incident_description:

Range was turned off and had not been used since the night before.
Caller's husband was leaning against the range when the oven exploded on Sunday evening April 28th, 2013, however no one was injured although glass was thrown up to nine feet across the room.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

Burned my fingers because when stove is in use, especially when using the front burners, the knobs that control the flame for cooking get so hot that they are untouchable.  Fortunately the burns on my fingers weren't as bad as it could have been had I not realized and actually used the knob.

The knobs stay hot for a quite awhile once it has been turned off (which in all honesty is quite a feat to do because it is so hot).

incident_description: Our Frigidaire microwave oven (model MWV150KWA) sometimes starts on its own, It has done this more than once.

incident_description:
I wanted to alert you to a possible FIRE HAZARD in an electric oven/stove that I own (Maytag Gemini series), and whose model number is MER6872BAS. Recently, the rocker-type switch on the right side of the control panel that allows the user to switch between a large and a small stove burner (manufacturer's Part #74006467) became "frozen"/inoperable. Around that time it was noticed that an electrical burning smell was experienced but the source was never pinpointed. Upon further investigation, it was found that the switch apparently became very overheated and actually melted the interior components of the switch as well as the exterior housing. 
Is there any kind of a recall that has been issued for this part or this model oven/stove in general? Please advise. Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard due to an overheated and melted switch, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Crockpot purchased in the fall of 2012.

They put it away and didn't use it for a while and when they took it out around December 2012 they discovered that  it had mold all over the inside so they cleaned it thoroughly, used it then cleaned it thoroughly again before putting it away.

.

incident_description: On my Kenmore range, model 790.71313709 (2 years old), the digital panel which turns on and off the oven has broken off twice and fallen down into an area where it cannot be controlled / turned off. This could result in someone trying to disconnect the gas while the oven is operating, obviously a very dangerous situation. Sears is not fixing it, saying it is out of warranty.
justification: The broken digital panel could lead to a dangerous situation, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: daughter woke me up to dishwasher being on fire, smoke in house. was stuck in drying mode and wouldn't respond to cancel cycle. had to pull circuit breaker.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and caused smoke, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
(03/31/2013) The consumer stated that she had baked a cake. She took the cake out and shut the oven off. After about ten minutes she smelled something burning. She looked at the stove and saw flames coming out the vent on the back of the stove. She reached to unplug the stove and burned her right arm. The cabinets to the left of the stove was scorched. When she unplugged the stove the flames went away. 

The consumer stated that she did not require medical attention on her arms. She stated that she does have scabs on the burn.

The consumer stated that she had planned to leave the house that day. She stated that if she had, her house would have burned down.



(04/01/2013) The consumer contacted the manufacturer. The consumer told them what happened. The consumer was told that a service representative would come out. The representative come out the same day. They found that the control panel on the back of the stove had burned out.  The repairman told her that he had never seen a control panel that was burned like the one on her stove.

The consumer stated that Whirlpool replaced the stove. She also stated that she had to pay $140 because it was over two years old.
justification: The consumer sustained burns on her arm but did not require medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident involved a rare stove malfunction, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description: We own a Bosch Dishwasher.  On March 10, 2013, the dishwasher was running at night.  We had just gone to bed.  Luckily, smoke alarms warned us of fire.  We woke to find the house filling with smoke.  We found flames shooting from the control panel of our dishwasher.  We called the fire department, but in the meantime were able to beat down the flames before they spread.  They did, however begin to burn the adjacent wooden cabinets.  The fire department arrived and removed the still-smouldering dishwasher door.  We had extensive smoke damage through-out the entire house and beyond-repair damage to our kitchen counter and cabinet.  We subsequently contacted our insurance company and Bosch.  Bosch sent a representative out within two days and confirmed, in a written response, it was a recalled unit and responsible for the fire.  I was assured by phone that I would be receiving forms by email.  Since then Bosch has refused any customer service or contact whatsoever.  If we had not been alerted by our smoke alarms the damage would have been catastrophic, not to mention the fact that being asleep, we would have been lucky to have escaped uninjured.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant property damage and potential for injury, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description: Hi. I have a Kenmore electric range#790.96102800. a few months back the wiring caught on fire on the back of stove and we were told that the harness was bad and needed to be replaced. we did that. It seems that when this refrigerator was assembled, the door handle on the fresh food side was not properly tightened, resulting in it coming off the door and causing injury to my head (cut, contusion, and concussion), on March 30, 2013.

I requested service to my refrigerator and the technician [REDACTED] came out on April 5, 2013. He immediately suggested that there was nothing wrong with the handle, and stated that he had the same refrigerator. He then said that I was using the handle incorrectly to open the door and it had been pulled up on resulting in dislodging. Is there an instruction manual on how one should open this refrigerator door? I donÃÂt think so. He finally suggested that if the design is faulty, I would need to take that up with the manufacturer. 

I think the handle was inching up upon each use, until it eventually came off the door. I removed the handle for the technician, with very little effort, and he proceeded to make adjustments to tighten it. I am not certain what he did, but the handle did feel much more secure. I opened the oven door to check the roasting pan and baste the meat. As I was closing the door I heard a loud pop and hiss and a fireball appeared on the bottom element. It began to flame and throw sparks and follow the element. I closed the door and turned the oven off, but it continued. I then used the circuit breaker to sop the current, and it eventually went out. I researched this on the Internet and have found many references to this happening to others, but all said that GE did not admit to a problem. I'm afraid to have this fixed and use the oven again since this is definitely a known issue. I'm certainly happy this happened when I was there and shudder to think what would have happened if it happened an hour earlier.
justification: The incident involved a fireball and sparks in the oven, but no injury or death occurred. The issue is a known problem with the oven model, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer placed a cup in the microwave for 45 seconds. While using the microwave it became stuck on 11 seconds.The display told the consumer to close door but it was already closed. The lights were on and the microwave continued to run. After sometime had passed the microwave finally powered off. 

2/21/13 There was an incident with his wife were she put the time on for 49 sec. the microwave started by itself. The display told her to push start while it was already running. She opened the door to the microwave to stop it but it continued to run. She pressed the stop button multiple times and the unit finally stopped.  

He read the Consumer Reports magazine talking about microwaves powering on by themselves and starting fires. He now keeps the microwave unplugged not in use. Consumer wants to report his microwave safety concern. 

Today, the consumer spoke with the Manager with the appliance sept. She referred him to service dept. ([REDACTED])who transferred him to CPSC.

UPDATE:
All in 2013:
