incident_description:
In February 2008 we purchased a GE Cafe Series Dual Fuel Convection Range and with the exception of one item, we have been very pleased with the product. The exception is the tit and feel of the adjustment knobs on the front of the range. The knobs do not feel solid; they wiggle and wobble as they are being adjusted, primarily due to the long plastic shaft that weakly connects the knob to the valve shaft.
I showed the situation to a GE repair technician making a repair call for our refrigerator and he showed me that a cracked plastic shaft (see photo 1) caused the problem. Every burner knob had the same defect. The lower oven knob was OK, probably due to the shorter plastic shaft and/or stronger material used for that knob. Due to the high cost of replacement knobs (the service technician thought replacement knobs would have the same design), I decided to just Jive with the wobbly knobs.
However, I recently returned to a smoke-filled home caused by a burner being left on under a pot of food. My wife had turned the burner knob to the off position before leaving home but the knob had slipped on the valve shaft and the burner remained on. In the daylight, the flame was not visible under the large pot
Upon inspection of the knob, I found that the cracked plastic shaft had allowed the metal insert to fall out, thus making the knob Jess connected to the valve shaft (see photo 2). I verified that the burner could remain on with active flame even with the knob in the off position. It made my wife feel better that she hadn't forgotten to tum off the burner, but it pointed out to me a issue with this knob design that should be brought to your attention.
In the interim, I have decided to repair the plastic shaft with epoxy. If replacement knobs are available of a higher quality, I would strongly consider purchasing them. At minimum, I would appreciate receiving one or two of the metal inserts that have been lost so I can more effectively repair the knobs.
justification: The incident involved a burner being left on due to a defective knob, resulting in a smoke-filled home but no injury or death.

incident_description:
On April 6, 2013, at approximately 12:45, consumer began preheating her oven to a temperature setting of 350 degrees F (not in Convection Mode). It was the first time it had been used on this day, and it had been operating normally since it was delivered in 2005.
At approximately 13:00, she noted that the unit had not yet ÃÂbeepedÃÂ (an indication that it had reached the setting temperature). She opened the oven and observed, on a hanging thermometer, that it had reached 350 degrees, so she placed her a caramel-pecan bars (in an aluminum flat pan), on the center rack.  After closing the over door, she selected the ÃÂTimer Set / OffÃÂ button on the control module, entered ÃÂ20:00ÃÂ [minutes] from the module keypad, and then pushed the ÃÂStartÃÂ button on this same module. Upon pushing the ÃÂStartÃÂ start button, the module began sparking from the vent area behind the module, followed by visible flames, also from the vent area behind the module. The flames lasted for approximately 10-15 seconds.
She wasnÃÂt quite sure what to do at first, but then pushed the ÃÂStop / ClearÃÂ button on this module, at about the same time the flames were going out.  With flames and smoke no longer visible, she contacted her husband, on his cell phone at 13:14 to report what had just happened. I directed her to pull the stove away from the wall, and unplug the large plug (220 VAC plug / outlet) at the base of the appliance. She was able to do this. There was no need to notify the Fire Department, as the fire had extinguished itself.4 Upon returning home that evening, I noted soot on the wall behind the appliance, in the area of the control module. On the morning April 7, 2013, I began photographing the fire damage with my cell phone.  During the course of my examination, I took numerous photographs; these photographs are available upon request.
I pulled the appliance away from the wall and examined the 220 VAC plug and outlet. I noted no signs of arcing and no abnormal discoloration.  I noted that the 40A Circuit Breaker for this appliance, located in a 100A Service Panel, in the NE corner of the basement, had ÃÂTrippedÃÂ, de-energizing the appliance circuit.
I noted that damage appeared to be most visible in the area of the control module, located on the back, upright portion of the appliance, between the individual stove top controls. This damage corresponded to the soot stains visible on the painted drywall behind the appliance.   I then removed the back protective panel, in proximity to the control module. I noted soot on both the inside and outside of the panel, in proximity to the right (as you are facing the  appliance) portion of the control module. I noted that damage appeared to be primarily contained the internal portion of the module / back side of the circuit board, which was enclosed in a black plastic frame. The wiring harness to / from this module appeared intact, was soot stained in proximity to the right module area, but otherwise undamaged by heat. I noted no melting of insulation or arching of the wiring harness and its components outside of the control module frame enclosure.
I noted ÃÂspatterÃÂ debris in the sooted areas of the white enamel appliance frame, adjacent to the aforementioned damaged area.   Based on my examination of this damage, and all the information available to me at this time, I  recommend that an engineering evaluation of this control module be done, so as to determine  both the probable failure mode and its likelihood to reoccur in other, similar appliances. It is also my opinion that had readily ignitable materials and / or an excessive grease  accumulation  been present at the time of this faulting, the heat energy generated by this faulting control  module would have been sufficient to extend this fire beyond the appliance. 
The appliance Repair is scheduled to replace this control module. The damaged control module will be simply unplugged from the wiring harness by the technician and retained by us for further engineering evaluation.
Regarding the use of this appliance, it should be noted this it had been used more often than most similar unitsÃÂfor daily meal preparation, but also especially for baking items for friends, coworkers, and charitable events. [REDACTED] will typically turn the oven on, and then do all her baking for the day, at the same time. [REDACTED] keeps the appliance exceptionally clean and free of food / grease accumulations.
On April 9, 2013, the control module was replaced with a new module. Upon turning the appliance on, it indicated a ÃÂCook Top FailureÃÂ. An  additional module will need to be ordered and replaced at a future date.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven control module, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was contained without external intervention.

incident_description:
On 23 Mar 2013, my wife and I purchased a Kenmore dual oven electric range from Sears. On 31 Mar 2013, my wife had something baking in the top oven (we used all week with no issues), but thought she would make a cake, so she placed the lower oven on 350 degrees and after about 20 mins the oven glass exploded and shattered into a million little squares. This happened after one week of our purchase of the range. The outer shell glass did not break, just the inner glass and then another inside glass appeared to be okay, but I am certain that it is damaged to some degree. We immediately called Sears and reported the incident and they scheduled a technician to come out to make the repair. On 2 Apr 13, a service technician came out, but had to order the two necessary pieces of glass requiring installation. On 11 Apr 13, two pieces of glass arrived and after inspection seemed in order, but it was covered in plastic, which was not removed. On 13 Apr 13, a service technician showed up and began repairing the door, but my wife notice two pin holes in both pieces of glass about 4 inches apart (perfectly 4 inches on both), so the technician thought it to not be a good idea to replace it and just simply order the entire door to be installed. 

I feel this is a recall in progress and feel that one of two things havhened here: 1) the manufacturer has went to a lower grade glass to save money or 2) a machine is making the holes in the glass before it becomes more solid and is causing them to be defective. Both technicians informed us that if there are any imperfections in the glass it will more than likely shatter, it's just a matter of when. I have never heard of oven glass shattering, but after this incident went on line and was amazed that this is common, but businesses don't appear alarmed. If my wife had opened the door as it exploded it would have been horrific or if a child was standing in front of the door when it exploded...God forbid.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering, which could have caused injury but did not in this case. The likelihood is considered possible as similar incidents are reported online.

incident_description: I purchased the smooth top Kenmore Electric Range in 2007.  We have not had any problems with the stove until the week of April 15, 2013.  On Tuesday my husband was cooking vegetables in a pot on top of the stove.  He pushed the simmer button and we heard this extremely loud noise.  I was quite a distance away in another room and heard the sound like someone dropping an iron skillet on the floor or some other type of sound similar to iron plates colliding together.  The sound was very loud.  I came into the kitchen to find out what happened and my husband then informed me that when he pressed the simmer button, that's when the stove made the loud sound.   After that happened, the stove will not turn off.  Even though the stove or oven is not hot, the "element on" light remains on 24-hours a day and the stove makes sounds as if it is on.  We have unplugged the stove but have not been able to get the light to go out.  The sound was very disturbing and we don't know what caused it or what type of damage was done.  When I read Kenmore had recalled some stoves in the past and I read what happened to those stoves, I felt like that was very similar to what happened to my stove.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and malfunctioning stove, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Last week I was visiting my newly married daughter in her new home.  We got out some of her new Pyrex bake ware to make brownies.  We chose the 9 x 13 glass pan.  We followed all package directions and put the brownies in the oven at 325 degrees and set the timer.  Before the timer went off, I checked the brownies and they looked finished so I took them out of the oven and set the pan on top of the stove.  After several moments, I got a butter knife out to loosen the brownies from the edges of the pan.  I touched the first edge gently several times and all of a sudden the pan exploded with glass flying everywhere.  It hit me in the chest and face and flew all over the kitchen.  If a child had been standing next to me at the stove, there would have been severe injuries.  

Needless to say, I was shocked at what happened and my daughter came running when she heard the huge popping noise.  We cleaned up the glass and were wondering what could have possibly caused this to happen.  After cleaning up, I looked online and found many people reporting problems with Pyrex that broke in this manner.  I posted a picture of the broken glass and brownies on my FB account and the next day one of my friends sent a message that the same thing happened to her that day!

People need to know about this hazard waiting to explode in their kitchens!!  I took several photos and saved some of the glass. 

There needs to be major warnings going out about Pyrex glass bake ware.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (glass hitting the chest and face) and potential for severe injuries if a child had been present, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Incident Description: On January 7, 2013, I purchased a brand new Kitchen Aid Empire Red 14 cup
coffee pot (Model #KCM1402ERO) (Serial #WE23207957) from Target. The very first time I used the
new coffee pot, it malfunctioned. This coffee pot has a spring loaded basket where you place the coffee
grounds. I was standing at the kitchen counter making toast, which was right next to the coffee pot,
when all of a sudden, the basket door of the coffee pot flew open. It was filled with hot water and hot
coffee grounds, which splashed onto my left wrist/hand area and down the left front of my shirt,
burning me with scalding hot liquid and hot coffee grounds from the basket. Hot coffee grounds and
hot coffee splashed on me and all over the kitchen counter and down the fronts of the cabinets. I
immediately put ice on my burns, (my left wrist/hand area and a quarter size area on my stomach).
After cleaning up a huge mess in the kitchen due to this incident, I made a second pot of coffee,
thinking that maybe I didn't close the basket door properly the first time. Not more than 2 to 3 minutes
into the 2"d attempt to brew a pot of coffee, the exact same malfunction happened again. Once again, I
had a big mess to clean up. I called Kitchen Aid and reported the incident. They gave me a report #
(SR# [REDACTED]) I talked to "[REDACTED]". She told me that they did not have any other complaints
or reports on that model coffee pot, therefore she suggested that I return to them that coffee pot and
they would send me a new one. I was reluctant at frrst, but she assured me that I was the only one that
had a problem, thus far.
They frrst had to send me a FedX shipping label so that I could return the non-working coffee pot to
them, and once I did that, they sent me a new one. This was a 6 week timeframe.
I received the new coffee pot, exact same model (KCM 1402ERO) and the new Serial # is
WE24141881. The very frrst pot of coffee that was made with the new pot, the exact same
malfunction happened. Five minutes into the brewing time, the basket door flew open with hot coffee
grounds and hot coffee splashing everywhere. On March 27, 2013 I contacted Kitchen Aid once again
and this time I requested a refund. Kitchen Aid wanted to send me a THIRD coffee pot. I refused. I
talked to "[REDACTED]" and he told me that I had to give them my original receipt from Target in order to get a
full refund. I did not have the receipt to give them so after a lengthy argument, Kitchen Aid agreed to a
full refund. Once again, I will receive a F edX shipping label to return the coffee pot to Kitchen Aid
and once they receive it, they will process my refund. I strongly suggested to Kitchen Aid that they
recall this coffee pot before it harms another consumer. They continue to suggest that they have not
had any other complaints on this Model. I do not believe that and I am convinced that there is a design
flaw with the basket door. I had 2 brand new models and they both malfunctioned. Once the basket
fills with hot water, the weight of the coffee grounds and hot water causes the basket door to slip below
the latching mechanism thus releasing the basket door allowing it to open, filled with hot liquid and hot
coffee grounds that splash out during the force of the door being released. The spring on this basket
door is a heavy duty spring. I was a Target yesterday and this Kitchen Aid Model Coffee Pot remains
on their shelves. I have included copies of my correspondence from Kitchen Aid and also pictures of
the coffee pot. I sincerely hope that the Consumer Product Safety Commission takes whatever action
necessary to force Kitchen Aid to recall this dangerous product. Please note ... the scald burns that I
received from this incident was bad enough that the area on my left wrist/hand peeled, and I still have a
quarter size scar on my stomach. I medicated myself and did not seek outside medical treatment. I was
lucky that the burns where not more serious. I told the personnel that I spoke with at Kitchen Aid that
the next consumer that gets burned by this design flawed coffee pot might not be so accommodating.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and a scar, indicating an injury, and the malfunction occurred repeatedly with the same model, suggesting a likely design flaw.

After a couple of weeks, I thought this new blender was ok but one day, after blending another drink, pouring it into a glass and drinking a few sips, I noticed the gasket was wrapped around the blades again and torn apart. After fitting the gasket pieces back together again, I was missing one tiny piece so I know I drank the piece of rubber!!! 
3... To see if it would happen again, I put in the new gasket and every day blended just plain water (without drinking it)...and about a week later, it happened again. THE GASKET WAS WRAPPED AROUND THE BLENDER AND TORN INTO PIECES!   
I honestly feel this could present a MAJOR CHOKING HEALTH HAZARD...IF NOT DEATH...if you were not aware this could happen and just mixed the drink and drank it right away.
This product should definitely be taken off the market.  It's a great idea but also a great health hazard!

incident_description:
This concerns a GE Profile Dishwasher (Model: PDW8600N00WW; Serial No: RM793860B).
The dishwasher was run Sun, 4/14/13 in the evening around 8:00 PM.  My wife ran it and I did not know when it had been started.  The next morning around 7:00 AM, I opened the dishwasher to retrieve a few dishes to use as part of preparing a quick breakfast for my son.  I noticed that the dishes were very hot and there was no residual moisture on the tops of the glasses and cups.  I also removed the silverware tray from the bottom.  The silverware was extremely hot to the touch, and was hotter than I could pick up and hold onto without immediately letting go to keep from burning my hand.  I had to dump it out onto the counter to cool so I could get what I needed.  At this point, I thought my wife had started the dishwasher early in the morning and that it was just finishing up.  I could not, however, explain why there was a total lack of moisture/steam as normally would be the case when opening it right after completing the cleaning cycle and the dishes are still hot.  I shut the door to the dishwasher and left to take a shower and finish getting ready.  When we came downstairs to leave, I could smell burned or melted plastic and immediately went over to the dishwasher.   I opened it up and it was still very hot, but this time there was a red substance over several of the dishes in the lower shelf and there were fibrous strings connected between the shelves.  I knew something had melted, but didnÃÂt have time to investigate, so I left the dishwasher door open and switched off the electrical power to the unit.  When I returned home in the evening, I carefully looked into the dishwasher to determine if I could identify the root cause of the problem.  The red substance coating many of the dishes was from a [REDACTED] thermoplastic lid that was in the top shelf and had completely liquefied to the point where there was no trace of it remaining in its original form.  Other plastic items in the dishwasher on both the top and bottom shelves had either deformed, partially melted or completely melted and there was a large pool of re-solidified plastic on the bottom of the dishwasher that had been transferred to there as a liquid.  The water dispensing sprayer at the bottom of the dishwasher separated and popped open because of the excessive heat.  It was only after talking with my wife later on 4/15/13 that I became aware that the overheating was occurring about 11 hours after the dishwasher had been initially started on the night of 4/14/13.  We have never set or used the ÃÂdelay startÃÂ features and my wife is confident that it started immediately after she had activated it.   Tonight (4/16/13), I looked for a possible GE dishwasher recall, found the most current one, typed in the unitÃÂs model and serial numbers and was surprised that is was not included in the recall.  Our model starts with ÃÂPDW8ÃÂ which is not included in the recall, but models starting with ÃÂPDW7ÃÂ are included.  I am entering in this report out of an ethical concern that the current recall of 1.3 million dishwashers might not have captured all of those that contain the faulty wiring issue.  What happened in my dishwasher should have never happened in a normally functioning appliance. Please feel welcome to contact me if I can be of any further assistance.
justification: The incident involved excessive heat and melting plastic but no reported injuries, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it appears to be a rare malfunction.

incident_description:
In August of 2007 I moved into a newly constructed home and purchased a 
Kenmore appliance package through my builder which included a smooth top
range, fridge, and dishwasher. Over the past five years we have had 
nothing but problems with your appliances; from a broken ice maker 
(after 2 months of use), to a dishwasher that will only run on one 
cycle. These issues are great annoyances, but not nearly as concerning 
and shocking as our most recent problem with our smooth top range; model
number 790-9600-9601.

The issue began with the front left burner. I noticed that when 
attempting to cook on a low to medium setting, the burner would only 
cook on high heat, so naturally I avoided cooking on that burner. 
Shortly after realizing I had a faulty range, I realized just how 
dangerous my Kenmore range was. The back left burner began turning on 
spontaneously and would glow red hot until we unplugged the range or 
tripped the breaker in the basement. I feel fortunate that I was home to
realize this problem and that it did not take my house burning down to 
find out.

Upon realizing the severity of our service needs, I immediately began 
researching to see if others had experienced something similar with 
their Kenmore range. I found an overwhelming amount of complaints and 
posts along with four Kenmore ranges that had been recalled for 
identical problems. My next step was to contact Kenmore to find out if 
my range had been recalled. I assumed that it must be; as my complaints 
were identical to those which had been recalled. After three unanswered 
e-mails, four redirected phones calls and frequent requests made via 
social media and Sears Service Center, I finally got a live person on 
the line who told me my model number had not been recalled, and that I 
would have to pay for a service person to come to my house if I wanted 
anything done.

I find this to be ridiculous. I have reported a range that could 
potentially burn my house down due to mechanical failures identical to 
those that have been recalled. So why hasn?t my range been recalled? Why
is it that Kenmore is not willing to do anything to rectify this 
situation? And why, to top it all off, is Kenmore?s customer service so 
terrible?
I will not stop until this situation gets taken care of. It is 
unacceptable to wait until someone gets hurt or a house burns down to 
recall this range, and it is unacceptable to ignore service requests 
from concerned customers.
justification: The incident involves a faulty range that could potentially burn a house down, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

The consumer says the burners on the range all work fine.  she has never had any previous issue with the range.  The consumer says the glass traveled about 8 feet.
justification: The glass panel blew out but no one was injured, and the incident is rare based on the description of no previous issues.

incident_description: my refridgerator suddenly started pouring water out of dispenser and would not stop.  I unplugged it but not before it fried it causing whole house to smell burnt. lucky I was awake and able to unplug it when it started otherwise could have started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My stove is a JennAir JDR8895AAW, a gas cooktop/dual electric oven.  There is a washer on the cooktop that allows water to drip onto the self-igniter switch for the right rear burner control.

This morning, a small fire started at that switch.  Fortunately, my home circuit breaker shut off the power, and the fire quickly stopped.

Investigating underneath the cooktop, I see that a wire from the ignition harness had somehow broken loose, and had made contact with the cooktop, sparking the fire.

The fire itself was in the plastic that surrounds the gas control knob, scorching and possibly melting part of the control assembly.

I have turned off the gas, and unplugged the appliance.  However, anyone that allows any water onto the cooktop, whether from overflowing cooking or from cleaning the stovetop, will have this same problem.
justification: A small fire occurred but was quickly contained without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Stove starts on its own at night.  The stove when found heated up flashed the F1 code and would not shut off.  Had to run to the 220 breaker to shut it off.  NOT SAFE AT ALL!  turned the breaker back on and the bottom element in the stove started running by itself so the whole system must be screwed up.  Already aware that there was a recall but not on this ??? Please this is a total recall issue!
justification: The stove malfunctioned and turned on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Elite dishwasher Model 665.16464300, Heard a loud pop and the saw smoke and flames coming out of the front door of the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Heating element in dishwasher burnt the plastic inlet cover. Potential fire hazard.
justification: The heating element caused damage to the plastic cover, indicating an incident with no injury but a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: Microwave caught fire while it was being used to cook bagged frozen vegetables 30 seconds into the cooking cycle.
justification: The microwave caught fire, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: My husband removed a Pyrex pan from the oven  and it "exploded" in his hand! It sent shattered glass everywhere! It left several burn marks on my kitchen floor, which I now have to replace.
justification: The Pyrex pan exploded, causing shattered glass and burn marks on the floor, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Glass liner of thermal coffee carafe shattered while washing under warm tap water.
justification: The glass liner shattered, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Oven was being used for baking when oven began producing excessive smoke and the smell of electrical burning. The wife noticed a flame burning inside the cooktop cavity between the top of the oven and the bottom of the cooktop while peering through the vent located at the top front of the range.
 
There was the sound of an electrical short, the power was shutoff and the flame went out.

Upon removal of the back panel of the range it was noticed that the blower motor (Part No. 108 on Kenmore Elite Smoothtop part list for model 790.46729700), located at the top right rear of the range, under the cooktop had caught fire and burned.
justification: The incident involved a fire and electrical short, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was going to bake some sweet potatoes, was pre-heating the oven when I heard a crackling sizzling sound, an orange looking electric flame shot through the back of the stove to the top of the digital display, I then heard a pop sound and the display turned off and black smoke came bellowing out from the back.
justification: The incident involved an electrical malfunction with visible flames and smoke, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Electrical fire of Whirlpool range model RF364PXPQ1. The cause was the power cord to stove terminal block. An aluminum strap is used to connect the power cord to stove wiring. This strap overheats and causes the plastic block to melt and the wiring catches fire. Research has found that when copper wire is connected to alumimum excess heat is generated at the connection point. This connection is used in almost all electric ranges. Have experienced similiar copper/aluminum overheating in a home in the mid 1970's where aluminum wiring was used.
justification: The incident describes an electrical fire caused by overheating at a copper-aluminum connection, a known issue, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
A refrigerator, made by Frigidaire,  caught on fire when the main light bulb used to provide light burned the roof plastic and scorched a hole that went past the plastic.

The fire caused by this incident could have been far worse if no one was in the house to attend to the burning smell that consumed the entire apartment.

Thankfully, this was noticed early and was prevented in becoming something bigger.

This refrigerator was bought in Lowes, and turned out to be the worst decision made. The manufacturer and store was called to report this issue and they all denied responsibility because the warranty expired and they were no longer responsible.

The incident is a defect in the model, which left the light bulb extremely close to the plastic surface, which caused the light bulb's heat to melt the plastic.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a refrigerator defect, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The caller stated that placed chicken in the glass bowl into refrigerator overnight.  When she retrieve it and placed it in on the counter approximately 3 mins later it exploded, shattering into several small and medium size shards of glass pieces.  The glass pieces projected as far as 7-8 feet away from the counter.  There were no injury sustained by this incident.

The manufacturer was not contacted.

The caller feels that this glass bowl is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a glass bowl exploding, but no injuries were sustained.

incident_description: Outer glass of our gas range exploded. Was not being used. Came home to glass every where.
justification: The gas range glass exploded but no one was present or injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer says that both front burners automatically go on the highest temperature just by turning it on.  the consumer says that they will then not shut off.  The only way to turn them off is by shutting off the circuit breaker.  
The consumer says that he then has to wait about five minutes before turning it on again in order to avoid the same thing happening.  
The consumer contacted the manufacturer who stated the model number is not on recall.  It started with the right front burner that was only doing this.  Now both front burners are having this problem.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance that could potentially cause a fire or burns, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the interior oven rack fall to the bottom of the oven.  The wall of the ovens are bowed out and is a manufacturer's defect.  On a couple of occasions she has had a roast fall to the bottom of the oven and causing grease to spill inside the unit posing a serious situation. 

She contacted a Sears technician who referred her to the retailer and said it is a manufacturer's defect.  The manufacturer refers her back to the retailer. The retailer has a specific department called the Blue Ribbon Group which she keeps getting sent back to.  The tech said it would cost $900 to have it fixed.

She says she has noticed the same thing happening to other consumers online.  The consumers who report it online all keep saying that the retailer tells them that no one else has ever had this problem which is the the same thing that she was told. Blue ribbon group offered no help.
justification: The incident involves a product defect causing inconvenience and potential safety hazards, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Consumer was at his rental home address and his wife pre-heated the oven on 350 degrees. His wife began to hear a crackling type noise and then a big boom type sound. She went into the kitchen where she saw that the outer glass of the oven door had shattered. She then powered the range off and the couple cleaned up the shattered glass.  

The range has not been in used since the incident. 

Consumer spoke with sears today and was told that the range was not listed under recall. The consumer was then referred to CPSC. 

There are no damages or injuries to report.
justification: The oven door glass shattered but there were no injuries or damages reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: GE Electric double wall oven:  Glass door shattered during self clean cycle
justification: The glass door shattered during the self-clean cycle, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Approximatelly 1 1/2 years ago I purchased and had installed an Electrolux microwave model number E30MH65GPS.  Over this period of time we have used it numerous times and the unit has performed nicely. Last night we were using the convection function with the rack installed to bake two casseroles that weighed maybe 4 lbs each. This is the first time that I noticed that the rack supplied is a total piece of JUNK!!The rack bowed so bad we were afraid that it would pop out of the support clips in the side of the oven. This has got to be the cheapest, thinnest excuse for a rack that I have ever seen. The next time we have a need to use the rack we will have to reconsider even using the oven. The rack needs to be redesigned using a heavier gauge wire so that it doesn't bow like the one that was supplied with the oven we purchased. Using such thin wire in an oven rack is an accident just waiting to happen.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning rack that bowed significantly but did not cause injury or damage, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
(03/20/2013) The consumer stated that her daughter loaded the dishwasher and put it on the normal cycle. Everyone went upstairs to bed. He son came down about twenty minutes later and discovered flames coming from the side and bottom of the dishwasher. He pulled the handle up to stop the wash cycle. He sprayed water on the dishwasher from the kitchen faucet.  The consumer stated that her husband pulled the dishwasher out from under the counter and took it outside. The entire house was filled with smoke. The fire department was not called. The only damage seem be under the counter where the dishwasher was located. The consumer stated that her husband is going to look at the wiring under the counter to see if there is any damage. 



The consumer stated that she will call Whirlpool.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries or deaths, and the fire was contained without requiring emergency services.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the toaster oven is poorly designed which causes the contents to burn at times if the user is not being carefully.  At times if the user turns it pass the off button it does not turn off.   He has had the unit for over a year.  He stated that the product was never tested UL and was tested by Intertek.  

The manufacturer was not contacted.

He is concerned that this toaster oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.


Note:  Caller will add more info when report is received.
justification: The toaster oven's design flaw poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer says she set the oven to 375 degrees to pre heat.  She then noticed that flames were coming out of the unit after a few minutes.  She unplugged it immediately.   She called the Fire Dept.  She says the coil is completely melted and torn apart.  Only melted on right side front.

She contacted the manufacturer who took a report and sent out a technician.  The technician mentioned that he sees this all the time.  The consumer says she was offered to repair the unit for $260.  She refused the offer and purchased a new one.  

Her case # with the manufacturer [REDACTED]
justification: Flames and damage occurred, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he heard when the dishwasher turn on by itself. He stated that approximately 1 minute after it turned on he started to smell a burning plastic odor. He stated that he opened the door to the dishwasher and the cycle stopped. He stated that he smelled inside the dishwasher to see where the odor was coming from and found that it was from the door. 

He stated that the burning odor was coming from the control panel. He stated that there were no visible damages. 

The consumer stated that he turned on the breaker to reset the dishwasher, but when he turned the breaker by on the dishwasher turn back on again. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that his model was not included on the recall. 

The consumer stated that this product should be investigated do to the fire hazard of the product.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher emitting a burning odor, but no injuries or visible damages were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer turned on the dishwasher on normal load. After a couple of minutes of the cycle starting she began to hear a sizzling noise. She then notice black smoke coming from the top of the dishwasher. The dishwasher stopped running and the consumer opened the machine. She stated there was about an inch and a half of water remaining in the dishwasher. 

The consumer has not tried the dishwasher and does not believe it is safe. 

The consumer has not yet contacted the manufacturer but does intend on doing so. When she contacted CPSC to file a report it was discovered that her dishwasher was listed under recall# 09-100. 

The dishwasher was purchased as a gift so the retailer is unknown.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a malfunctioning dishwasher, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: While pre-heating our Tri-Ply Clad 20cm frying pan, we heard a loud sharp "bang" and discovered that the rivet on the handle had exploded off the inner portion of the pan. The rivet was lying in the pan as it must have hit the side of the pan and then landed in the pan. Had the rivet cleared the top of the pan when it exploded off the handle, it could have caused serious injury to myself or wife, as it was very hot and made of metal. The underside of the pan shows Member's Mark, Made in China, the NSF logo in a circle, and number 80116/190. We feel this product should be immediately be pulled off the shelf and a worldwide notice be posted to prevent serious injury to anyone. If you require any further information, please contact us. Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a rivet exploding off the pan handle but no injury occurred, though there was potential for serious harm.

incident_description:
My Sears Kenmore Range 790.9641340C had an electrical fire.  Feed from circuit in back of oven was faulty.  Eletrical fire occured in back of stove.  I smelled arcing and I pulled stove back from wall.  The wall showed scorching and fire was coming from back of stove.  Popped off tin covering back panel and one of feeds into stove from wall was on fire where it joined stove.  I have photos of damage and a party of 20 witnesses who can confirm.

Product was purchased at Sears, installed by Sears.

STOVE IS DANGEROUS AND SEARS OVERSEAS CALL CENTER TOLD ME I SHOULD GO IN TO STORE TO ASK IF IT WAS STILL IN STOCK.
justification: The electrical fire caused scorching and was witnessed by 20 people, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher was running, began smoking.  Son smelled burnt plastic. Source was identified as dishwasher due to smoke coming from front panel. Husband opened dishwasher door to stop machine from running.  Machine continued running even with door open.  Water everywhere!  Husband shut off circuit breaker to dishwasher---it stopped and stopped burning.  We removed dishwasher. If we were not home, this could have ended with much more of a problem than a burning smell and water all over floor.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing smoke and water damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
This is a smoothtop electric range by Kenmore. 

Left front burner on stove is not able to be controlled by the knob. Once it is turned on, it just gets hotter and hotter. Adjusting the knob does nothing.  You can turn off the burner but the burner will still keep getting hotter and hotter. You actually have to go and turn off the circuit breaker, and then wait for the element to cool off before restoring power to the range.  If you simply flipped the breaker off and on, while the element was still hot, it would continue to heat up once power was restored.

I had two incidents of this back in October 2012, and just stopped using that burner. I told my husband about it, but he forgot. Recently he tried to cook something on that burner, experienced the same problem. He did not think to turn it off at the circuit breaker. The stovetop just kept getting hotter and hotter, and then there was a blue spark at the back of the stove (behind where the knobs are) and the power to the burner went off and the burner finally cooled down.  He now knows not to use that burner.

No one was injured in these incidents, but I think we were just lucky. An issue like this could easily give someone a severe burn or set a house fire.

I see there is a recall on similar (more expensive) models of this type of range for the EXACT same issue, however my model/serial number is not listed in the recall, so I have to pay for a technician to come and repair the problem.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the malfunctioning burner poses a clear hazard, with potential for burns or fire if not addressed.

incident_description: My Maytag stovetop range's glass door shattered for no apparent reason.
justification: The glass door shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: At the end of the washing cycle, the heating coil of the dishwasher remains on until the door of the unit is opened.  Depending on how long the problem remains undetected, the unit becomes so hot that plastic items inside the basin melt, and the counter top becomes hot to the touch.  This problem poses a significant fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a significant fire hazard due to overheating, which can cause property damage but no direct injury or death.

incident_description:
Consumer and his wife were in their bedroom asleep. His wife heard the motor go on in the kitchen. The discovered that the microwave powered itself on. There was nothing shown on the display of the microwave's control panel. It was full of smoke that was seeping from the closed door.  She climbed on a ladder and unplugged the unit. 

The unit is still unplugged and will not be used again. 

There are no damages to report. 

The control panel in the unit has been replaced by the retailer on- 12/03/04

The consumer has not yet contacted the manufacturer but does intend on doing so.

The consumer does not intend on contacting the retailer.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, producing smoke, but no injuries or damages occurred.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while using the oven for approximately 5 mins it burst into flames.  The door was open and a large flame erupted and then sparks projected to the floor.   The sparks and flames disipated within 30 seconds. The heating element melted and there was a burnt hole at the bottom of the oven.   The oven has not been powered back on.

Approximately 2 years ago the rear burner came on by itself and again 6 months later.  The control knob was switched on and off intermittently until it powered off.   The caller feels that she experienced problems of Release # 09-333.

The seller was contacted and they advised her that there were recalls on certain models and to call the manufacturer.  The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents have happened before, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
The caller stated that his spouse was using the oven on low temperature, the broiler came on by itself and stayed on.  He was not sure of the time factor that the incident occurred, but she reported to him that the contents she was baking was charred until they ignited flames.   She was unable to turn it off, the circuit breaker was used to switch the power off.  There were no prior incident or services with this unit.

2/25/13 The manufacturer was contracted and he was informed that someone would call him back.
The caller is concerned that he is experiencing similar problems of Release 09-333 and feels that this incident should be investigated to be included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused a fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Please be advised that I represent a housing cooperative as their legal counsel. In 2011 my client entered into an appliance replacement program for 292 ranges, refrigerators, and dishwashers from Lowe's. The ranges in question are Whirlpool WFG361LV & WFG374LVS.

After the appliances were installed, we found that the operation of the knobs on the gas ranges were defective. Our members have experienced the knobs being too easily engaged by lightly being brushed against, releasing gas while not igniting the flame. We contacted Whirlpool, who sent engineers out to test the ranges. They maintain that the ranges are safe and in compliance with safety regulations.

Since then, we have received multiple complaints from our members who say that the ranges are still turning on when they brush up against them (for example, when they are reaching for a microwave or a cupboard above the range). If one doesn't notice that the knob is slightly turned, gas will seep out. We have had multiple complaints that members have awoke in the morning to the smell of gas, or have returned home from work to the smell of gas in their house. The only way to fix the problem is to remove the knobs from the ranges and place them on the counter. This creates a dangerous situation, and is only a matter of time before there is an explosion or a fire due to the seeping gas and the defective ranges.
justification: The incident involves defective gas ranges that release gas when brushed against, posing a significant risk of fire or explosion, though no injuries or deaths have been reported yet.

incident_description:
Consumer was wiping the off the counter and noticed spots on the edge of the ceramic countertop.  Damp paper towels would not remove the spots.  Turned to re-wet the paper towels and saw from the corner of  her eye, flames coming out of the knob!  All of the burners were flaming. She ran downstairs and tripped the circuit breaker to shut off power supply to the range. When she returned upstairs there were no more flames, just black smoke. 

The consumer then called the Fire Department and was directed to 911 and within a couple of minutes they were there. The Fire Department made sure the circuit breaker was powered off and began to unplug the cords to the range. The Fire Department then removed the range because it was too hot to keep in the house. 
 
The consumer's son now has the range in his shed. So some information may not be available. Son took cooktop apart. It was completely burnt inside!  He trashed it in dumpster

She got a ruler and measured were the flames were and she stated they were about 8-9 inches tall. 

There are no damages to report.
justification: No injuries or damages reported, but the incident involved flames and required Fire Department intervention.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Elite stove interior oven rack falls off wall of hot oven when returning rack with hot casserole back into oven. A video shows the wall of the oven bow as the rack is returned to the oven and both the rack and casserole fall to the floor of the oven.
justification: The incident involves a rack and casserole falling inside the oven, which is a clear incident but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: LG LDF8072 dishwasher emits toxic organic volatile compounds as a result of asphalt-like material heating up and gassing off during the wash cycle. LG uses this material to dampen the noise. This material covers most of the drum from the outside. Based on reviews online, LG used this material on older models and a complaint on Consumer Reports web site dates back more than 2 years. Symptoms: noxiousness, headache, vertigo. Long term harm: neurological damage, carcinogenesis, teratogenesis. http://www.amazon.com/gp/cdp/member-reviews/A8YPGUJ6B5D7F/ref=cm_cr_pr_auth_rev?ie=UTF8&sort_by=MostRecentReview
justification: The incident involves exposure to toxic compounds causing symptoms like headaches and vertigo, with potential long-term harm, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue has been reported in multiple reviews over years, suggesting it is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
My GE dual-fuel stove caught on fire during the end of using the self-cleaning phase. It should be noted that my stove was not very dirty and was very well maintained. I smelled a strong smell of an electrical fire and realized that smoke was pouring out of the top area of the range where the controls are. After just a few minutes, fire began bursting out of the same area, licking around the top and side of the stove, singeing the wall behind the stove. After calling the fire department, we eventually doused the fire with water, vacated the house and waited for the fire department. The fire department did determine that the fire was out and arranged fans to help remove the smoke and odor from house.

That day I called GE customer service to make a complaint and was told by the assistant that they were not aware of such problems with these stoves. She made a very minor offer to provide a $100 voucher towards a new stove, opened a report and I told her that I would research and follow-up. After researching I have learned that this stove is indeed the subject of a recall for exactly the type of fire that occurred. After calling the recall hotline, this was confirmed as the same model/style stove. A technician is now coming to my house to check the stove; however I am deeply disturbed at the handling of my original call by GE and their failure to disclose the recall to me. 

I have pictures of the stove, damaged wall and model number but could not upload during this initial report. I can make them available as needed.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, and the stove model is known to have recall issues, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Occupant was using gas cooktop (1 burner). When she went to turn on a second burner, there was an "explosion" which resulted in shards of the glass cooktop shattering and being thrown about the kitchen. The knobs for the cooktop were also blown off the unit. 

No injuries or fire extension.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and damage to the cooktop, but no injuries or fire extension occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kitchen Aid oven/cooktop #KGRS202BSS0 two weeks ago.  Every day, since I have had it installed, I have found that the cooktop knobs automatically turn on when I lean over to turn on the oven or even when someone just passes by.  As this stove has two very large flames in the front this is very dangerous.  Yesterday, even though I am aware of this problem and am extra careful, I reached over to adjust the oven temperature and almost burnt my chest. Several times in the last two weeks, people coming into my home commented that they smelled gas.  When I checked my cooktop, I found the knobs slightly on.  As I am the mother and grandmother of young children, I remove all the knobs when they are home, but this item is dangerous for children and adults alike.  I contacted Kitchen Aid, who told me that this is not the first time they have gotten this complaint, but this stove features a "soft touch" turn on.  I asked about the safety and was told that yes, you have to be very careful, but there is nothing they could do about  it.
This cooktop is a safety hazard, a fire hazard and a burn hazard.  I believe it should be recalled and I should have a replacement.
I would be more than glad if someone from the CPSC would come down to my home to see this product
justification: The incident describes a near burn injury and repeated gas leaks, indicating a clear safety hazard with frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
Bought a home with built-in KitchenAid double oven - Model # KEBS208SSS04.
The first time we attempted to use the self clean feature, the inner glass of the oven door shattered into small chards.  Glass was all over oven and some external in area.  Stopped the clean cycle.  When door was opened after cool-down glass went everywhere.

Had door repaired professionally and we attemped to use the self clean feature again, and similar results.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2.

incident_description: Maytag mzd2766ges started a fire in the kitchen.
justification: The incident involved a fire, which is a significant event but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description: Our Kenmore Coldspot Refrigerator model number 106.52284201 manufacture date 2002 caught on fire today.  Luckily I had just come home and was next to the kitchen when it happened because it could have burned the house down.  I have looked this up on the internet and found that this has happened to a good number of people.  These should be re-called.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred. The incident is described as happening to a good number of people, indicating it is likely.

incident_description: We had preheated our oven to 400 degrees (did NOT use the broiler).  After setting in the taco shells filled with our beef, green chili and bean mixture, we covered them with cheese and set them in the oven for 10 minutes.  After the meal had been in the oven for 7 minutes, we heard a loud sound come from the oven.  It sounded like a cookie sheet that warps in the oven.  We opened the oven to see a completely shattered Pyrex casserole dish (and a ruined meal).  We turned off the oven.
justification: The incident involved a shattered Pyrex dish but no injuries occurred, only property damage and a ruined meal.

incident_description:
Sunbeam microwave oven SGB8901.  The unit is about one year old.  I was heating some food on a china plate covered with "microwave safe" wax paper when the paper caught fire.  I (stupidly) retried this the next day and the same thing happened.  This time I noticed a change in the sound just before the fire, as if the power level had suddenly jumped.  I contacted Sunbeam today, but haven't yet heard back.

UPDATE: I'm not interested in reporting the wax paper (the second item) - I've used that
numerous times without incident. As far as "risk of harm," the contents of the
microwave caught on fire, which might have caused damage to the unit as well as a
structure fire. When removing the flaming material from the microwave I burned my
hand (slightly) and some pieces of burning material fell onto the floor, which again
could have started a fire.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight burn injury and potential for a structure fire, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of the issue suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
I just spoke with your staff who asked me to submit the following by email which documents recent problems with a microwave and subsequent discussions with General Electric.    
 
Thank you for your review.
 
[REDACTED] 
 
PRODUCT-PURCHASE BACKGROUND:
Purchased GE electric range August 2, 2013, from Specialties Appliances & Plumbing Fixtures, 2800 West Eleven Mile Road, Berkley, MI 48072 (Phone: 248-548-5656).  Invoice #[REDACTED]; ModelPVM1790SRSS (PVM1790S, 1.7 CF SS Profile 1000 Watt Convection OTR Microwave installed September 9, 2012.
 
INCIDENT: 1-22-2013 
Experienced minor head injury at home in kitchen while cleaning around microwave.
 
I contacted GE Consumer Relations (800-386-1215) on 1-22-2013., Talked with [REDACTED], case manager.  Informed her that I had hit/scraped my head on lower exterior metal edges of microwave while cleaning under the cabinets. I 
requested that she document my concerns regarding exceptionally sharp and pointed edges on the right and left lower front corners of the microwave.  I stated that this was a problem to me and likely a problem other consumers might experience if they had the same product. I also asked if there was an after market fix or remedies for this problem.  
 
[REDACTED] took product info, assigned case #[REDACTED] for reference and told me she would follow up with me in a few days.
 
GE 1-29-2013 RESPONSE:
I called [REDACTED] on 1-29-2013. incident_description:
I had quite a scare this morning.

I put a piece of bread in my KitchenAid Countertop oven, set the position switch to ÃÂtoastÃÂ, and set the timer for 6 minutes.  When the timer is up, the machine ÃÂdingsÃÂ and turns itself off.  There is nothing abnormal here.

This time, the appliance did not ÃÂdingÃÂ, and did not turn off.  And I forgot about the toast.  After maybe 15 minutes, I smelled something burning, and found heavy smoke pouring out of the countertop oven.  I noticed the timer was still set at 6 minutes, and the oven was still on and really hot.

I turned the appliance off, and left the door closed.  I did not want to introduce oxygen to the mix.  But the smoke was extensive and continued to pour out, and I knew I had to get the toast out or my house would smell for months.  I opened the window, grabbed a hot pad, opened the oven door, grabbed the toast, and flung the really burnt toast out the window.  There were no flames, but I suspect ignition could not have been more than moments away.

After the oven cooled, I cleaned it up, and examined the timer switch.  The timer is a mechanical spring-wound clock-like device that ticks as it counts down.  It operates without electricity.   When the timer times out, it opens a set of electrical contacts to shut off the power to the heating elements.   

I rest the timer numerous times.  Ninety percent of the time, the timer would ÃÂtickÃÂ and  run down normally, but twice, when setting the timer at 6 minutes, the timer would not start ticking.  It would just stay at 6 minutes, with both top and bottom elements on.  The oven would have stayed on indefinitely.  I have not found a one-line diagram or traced the internal circuitry, but I expect the thermostat is only in the circuit when the oven is used for baking, not when used for toasting.  For toasting, all elements are on full power continuously.  

I reviewed the ownersÃÂ manual, and found it suggests for times less than 5 minutes, moving the timer switch to greater than 10 minutes, and then turning it back to the time desired.  But my problem was at 6 minutes.

The oven is Model KCO1005ER.  The serial number (WGT2610420) dates the appliance to 2006.  No recalls were found.

I see this as a definite fire hazard.  I welcome your comments, questions, or suggestions.

This lasted less than a year again until 3-2013, only this time it blew the breaker (it never had done that before) . Upon removing the back cover I was horrified to find the oven plug that plugs into the control unit MELTED! I only can say I'm glad it didn't start a FIRE. I'm writing this complaint to worn people of a possible FIRE hazard. I'm junking this range
justification: The incident involved a melted oven plug which could have caused a fire, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: The glass in the door of my Kenmore oven exploded this morning. No one was using the oven and no one was in the room when it happened. My husband and I heard it and went in to investigate.
justification: The oven glass exploded but no one was injured or present in the room at the time.

incident_description:
While my wife and I were in bed we heard a loud "bang" noise from the other side of the house. I went to investigated this immediately (occurred around midnight) I discovered localized smoke. I recognized it as electrical fire smoke. My wife and I cleared the rest house and found the smoke originated from the kitchen only. After examining various appliances, outlets, etc, we noticed the stoves front panel was not displaying the time. We pulled the stove out from the wall and saw burn marks on the wall and the back of the stove black from a spontaneous electrical fire/short. The back of the oven was very hot with some smoke still emanating from the device. We disconnected the stove from power. Device is a Kenmore Elite Range model #790.99022800

this just happened and I am filing this report while the situation is fresh in my mind. Due to the numerous accounts of this similar thing happening with Whirlpool/Kenmore stoves/ranges I thought it best not to wait to file a report.
justification: The incident caused localized smoke and burn marks, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,
Tonight I was putting leftovers into one of the rubbermaid glass containers with easy find lids.  I was dipping the food (corn beef, cabbage, potatoes) using a slotted spoon from a [slow cooker] into the glass container; it was warm food but not excessively hot.  The glass container exploded in my hands and all over the kitchen into hundreds of shards of glass.  I am very fortunate to only have a few minor cuts on my foot, arm, and hand.  I have a two year-old daughter and am terrified at the thought that she could have easily been close to where the explosion occurred.  I think this is a very dangerous product, and should not be marketed that it is okay to microwave or in any way hold a warm liquid.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts on foot, arm, and hand) and could have been more severe if a child was nearby.

incident_description: Fire started in 8-year-old Sears Kenmore dishwasher. Consumer believed dishwasher was under recall, but Sears told her it was not. She continued to use the unit until the incident occurred. The deputy fire marshal examined the unit, and reported that it is under recall.
justification: A fire started in the dishwasher, indicating an incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer states that her range get so hot that it burned the rack on the inside. The consumer bakes on 170 degrees because the oven get so hot. The consumer is now limited in what she can bake in the oven. Or she would have to bake in time intervals because of the excess heat. She also is fearful of leaving the kitchen while the oven is on. The oven also gets so hot that it has started to burn the coating off of the stove. 

02/10- The consumer's spoke with the retailer indirectly and  can't recall what transpired. 

04/11- the consumer paid the retailer check out the range and they replaced the control panel on the range. 

9/17/12- Consumer's son spoke with [REDACTED]about the range

The consumer also stated she wrote a letter to CPSC about her range.
justification: The oven's excessive heat caused damage to the rack and stove coating, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: (03/04/2013) The consumer stated that he noticed that the inside left of the oven was hot. One night he was taking a pan out of the oven. He stated that the pan was hot. The oven was not on nor had it been used that day. He checked it another time, and it was hot again. He started checking periodically. One morning he checked it and noticed that the igniter was glowing. The consumer open the oven and discovered that it was hot. From then on he would unplug the stove after each use.
justification: The oven was hot when not in use, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller's dad purchased an 8qt pressure cooker and presented it to her July/August 2012 and although she has only used it a couple of times she has had no problems with it until March 1st, 2013 when she was cooking beans in it with plenty of water and her child was sitting about 2 feet away playing with magnets on the fridge.

After cooking approximately 30 minutes with the units temperature set to medium, the caller heard a sound like pressure and spewing liquid and she turned around to see steam and water spewing and billowing all over the kitchen.  Initial sound was a loud pressurized release.  

The steam filled the room during the 5 to 10 second spewing the water out of the pressure cooker. steam was very thick fog. Almost looked like smoke, but wasn't.

Once it stopped spewing the water out, she then grabbed a kitchen towel to reach over and turn the pressure cooker off.

After it cooled a bit she began trying to open the cooker, she had a lot of trouble opening but after 20 or 30 seconds she got it opened and found that there was almost no liquid left in the cooker. It was pressure sealed shut even though all steam had left.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

There were no injuries.
justification: The incident involved a pressure cooker malfunction causing steam and water spewing, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Kenmore oven, Model # 79046783900     Racks are not supported by oven liner and fall to bottom of oven.
justification: The incident involves oven racks falling, which could cause inconvenience or minor damage but no injury.

incident_description:
This complaint is about the "Perfect Tortilla Pan Set" --THE COATING OF THE PANS CAME OFF ONTO THE TORTILLAS IN MANY PLACES. 

We bought the "Perfect Tortilla Pan Set" last week. We used it for the first time on Monday (3/18). We did was the pans in warm soapy water before using and followed all directions, baking at the recommended temperature. We ate the tortilla for dinner. My husband ate about one-and-a-half tortillas. I wasn't hungry so ate little. My husband said he felt unwell last night after dinner. I questioned him, and he said that midway through dinner, he started to feel feverish and to have pangs of nausea. It wasn't until Tuesday at lunch that I saw the many metal-colored marks on the leftover tortillas, and I also saw that the coating of the pans had flaked off in many places. On Tuesday evening after work, before I told him about this, my husband complained of continued waves of nausea.

Obviously these pans are defective. We are also worried that they are dangerous! We hope we didn't ingest something dangerous to our health! We want to have the metalic residue on the tortillas tested to know what it is, and if it is dangerous--can you help us with this? We also want to warn others about this defective product!
justification: The incident involved ingestion of metal flakes causing nausea, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description:
Caller is contacting CPSC to alert the public to a safety hazard not covered with release# 05-258.
His blade housing was replaced several years ago.

Around March 2nd, 2013 callers daughter was using the product, had toasted a piece of bread, cut into quarters and put into the chopper to create bread crumbs to place on a recipe she was preparing when the top of the blade assembly flew off around the locking mechanism, hit the plastic bowl with the unit still spinning causing plastic pieces to fly out.  There are four pieces of plastic that are approximately 1 1/2 inch by 1 1/2 inch, with other sizes near that measurement but progressively smaller.

He is reporting because the original release does not imply pieces flying off the product which could cause laceration, eye damage etc.

There were no injuries

He contacted the hotline for the original recall hotline and spoke with [REDACTED] who advised him that she would be happy to receive pictures that she would share with her supervisors, however they had blade assemblies, no bowls but she would conduct a search for him.

He is reporting because of the safety issues and laceration or eye damage hazard.
justification: The incident involved a safety hazard with no injuries reported, and the likelihood of occurrence is possible given the described malfunction.

incident_description: Purchased a new Pyrex baking dish last night and when I pulled it from the oven from it's first use it literally exploded shards of glass and boiling liquid up to 10 ft around my kitchen. Dinner ruined, leg burned and thank God my kids had gone to wash their hands because this would have been at eye level. What product EXPLODES??
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and potential for more severe harm, but such explosions are uncommon with proper product use.

incident_description: My GE kitchen gas cook stove oven did not shut off when I turned the oven control knob off this morning. In addition it had heated up to an unsafe temp. Smoke was beginning to appear from the back. The oven control was set at 325degrees when was heating up some food then shut it off. Several minutes later I checked  it again to make sure I had turned it off before I left for work. The control knob was off but I noticed a yellow glow at the bottom of the oven. I opened the broiler and the gas flame was still on at full. The turned the control knob on and off several times but the gas flame did not go off. I pulled the extremity hot stove away from the wall to unplug it. The entire stove was too hot to touch without protection. I unplugged the stove which stopped the gas flame.  I'm sure the stove would have continued to heat up and would have set the wood cabinets and wall on fire destroying my house.
justification: The incident involved a gas stove failing to shut off, leading to unsafe temperatures and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We have two your glass tea tumblers. At 4 am this morning, an empty tumbler was sitting in my 15 year old son's room and it completely exploded. Glass was spewed all over his room. Had his bookcase not blocked the flying glass pieces, they would have flown into his bed. We have taken video and retained the few large pieces. There was no tea or liquid in the tumbler. Before we report this to the Consumer Protection agency, please advise what you would like us to do.

There appears to be a major design flaw with this tumbler. The only thing we can figure out is that we had a rain storm come through our area at that time which would have resulted in a drop in the barometric pressure. This tumbler made a very loud bang/explosion when it broke apart. Not good. Flying glass is dangerous and can cause serious damage.

The above incident description was sent to the company, Teavana and after waiting a week for a response, we decided it was best to notify the CPSC.

We also forwarded images of the damage caused and a video which can be forwarded to you.
justification: The tumbler exploded, causing flying glass, but no injury occurred as the bookcase blocked the glass from hitting the son.

Microwave purchased January 2011 in Michigan.
Around the beginning of December 2012 she heard a boom sound, couldn't find source  but that evening she was going to heat something in the microwave but when she opened the door, glass began coming out.
She looked for a bullet hole because she couldnt' find any reason the glass would be broken.
Sears repairman couldn't tell her what happened to it because he had never seen anything like what could have caused all the glass to break.

She has replaced the microwave.
She has not contacted manufacturer and does not intend to contact them.
There have been no injuries

Sometime around February 12th, 2013 callers began noticing odd incidents happening with their electric range that was purchased around March 15th, 2008.

If consumers set the burner to simmer it escalates to maximum heat setting then other times they can set to simmer and it just turns off.

These incidents are so far isolated to the two front burners.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer yet but does intend to contact him.

There have been no injuries.

incident_description:
BENZENE and benzene derivatives were being emitted from my GE Electric Profile Range, Model No. PB900DPBB, Serial No. DV243799.  A Senior Quality Control Engineer from OEM Solutions, Owens Corning and a Senior Advanced Development Engineer from GE in Louisville, KY both told me that benzene should not have been in my GE Profile Range.  Also, toxic fumes that came from the range caused my husband & I to experience burning of our eyes and nose and coughing spells.  The toxic odor was on our kitchen cabinets, walls, counters and curtains and had to be washed down to remove the toxic smell.  The Owens Corning MSDS sheet lists formaldehyde and acetaldehyde in their insulation and it says these 2 chemicals can cause eye, nose and throat irritation when the oven is in the self-clean cycle.  However, given the strong, toxic odors and fumes coming from the oven, these chemicals may have been at abnormally high levels.  

I purchased my GE Profile Range from P.C. Richard & Son on February 18, 2011 and it was delivered to my home on April 9, 2011.  The Owners Manual that came with the stove instructs you to turn on the self-clean oven cycle for 3 hours and it will give off a burning or oily odor in a new oven that will disappear in time.  Also says a strong odor from the insulation around the inside of the oven is normal for the first few times the oven is used and to keep birds in another room when stove is in self-clean to prevent illness or death.  

After only 1 minute on the self-clean cycle, a noxious, toxic smell along with greyish white fumes were coming from the back and front of the stove.  I immediately turned off the self-clean cycle and called the GE hotline.  After 2 calls and almost 2 weeks later a GE technician came out to check the stove (people at the hotline kept telling me to put the stove on self-clean for 3 hours even though I told them the smell was unbearable).  On April 21, 2011 the GE technician came out and when he turned the self-clean cycle on, that same toxic odor along with the greyish white fumes came out of the back and front of the stove.  He immediately turned the stove off and said he never smelled anything so bad in his 20+ years of servicing stoves.  

The range was removed from my home on April 22, 2011 and taken to the P.C. Richard & Son Warehouse in Carteret, NJ.  On June 16, 2011 a certified fire inspector hired by GE came to that warehouse and took a SUMA Canister air quality test on my stove.  My husband and I were present during the air testing and ensuing examination of the insulation, which was removed from the stove that day. The GE Profile Range is now at GE Appliances in Louisville, KY, supposedly undergoing further inspection.  The range has been there since September 2012 and I still have not gotten a definitive answer as to why BENZENE was in my stove or why these toxic fumes were being emitted. 

Under separate cover, I am emailing CPSC (1) detailed information from the people I spoke with in the past 22 months concerning this toxic odor, (2) a copy of the air quality test results done at EMSL Analytical, Inc., (3) photographs of the insulation and stove, and (4) other pertinent information.
justification: The incident caused burning eyes, nose, and coughing spells, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence is unlikely (2) as it appears to be an isolated case with abnormal chemical levels.

incident_description:
February 22, 2013
U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission
4330 East West Highway,
Bethesda, MD 20814-4408
Dear Sir:
While reading the latest issue of "Consumer Reports" (March, 2013), I came upon the article called "Microwave Mystery." If I didn't know better, I would swear that the article was written about my situation. Let me explain. In the fall of 2007, I purchased a KitchenAid Microwave Hood Combination. (Model KHMS 155L), and had it installed, professionally, over my range top. For about 2 1/2 years, it worked perfectly. In July of 2010, I began having problems with the touchpad. It would not work correctly. I called the 800 number, indicated in the manual, and was informed that a local service representative would be scheduled to fix it. Since it was still under warranty, the part would be replaced for free but I would have to pay the service charge. Long story short, I had to cancel several appointments because the touchpad started to work again. Then, on August 3rd, at 2:30A.M., I heard a strange noise coming from the kitchen. I am a senior citizen and a light sleeper (comes with age). So, I
went downstairs to investigate and found the microwave running, on high, by itself. Thankfully, no damage was done. I called the 800 number the next day, and was connected to a woman who handled "property damage claims." I informed her that, fortunately, I turned the unit off almost immediately. She apologized and asked if there was any damage, and I told her no. Then, she reiterated that the touch pad would be replaced for free and, this time, there would be no service charge. I queried if the company had had similar problems with this unit and she said yes. The control pad was replaced and it as worked fine ever since. I am still a little concerned, however, because there was never a recall and This article was the first time that I had read about it. What if it happens again and I don't wake up in time? It is a scary thought!
Very truly yours,
[REDACTED] 
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
P.S. 1 contacted Consumer Reports about the problem and they suggested I contact you people.
If you would like any additional information, my phone number is [REDACTED] and my email address is
[REDACTED]
