incident_description:
We are writing to you regarding the Viking 30" Gas Range that we purchased last year. As a result of numerous problems with the range, it is clear to us that this range is defective. We are requesting a refund or store credit.
The range was purchased from Warehouse Discount Center in Torrance, CA on 3/10/12. We paid $3,413.62 (including tax). Our sales associate promised delivery quickly, but there were many delays and we did not receive the range until late March. Already frustrated with the late delivery, the range was poorly delivered on the back of a small pick-up truck by one older man. He had no one else to assist him to bring in the range into our house. We were surprised to see the lack of care and caution used in delivering a high-end and very heavy kitchen appliance. 
Right away, we had issues with our range. Our first service call happened in early April, 2012. The oven was not heating up properly. Whatever we were baking or roasting was not cooking properly. The oven would start to heat up, but then the finished product was still raw and uncooked. The thermostat was adjusted and it appeared to be working well again, but as we discovered later, it was never repaired properly that time.
The second service call was much more serious. In late April the oven started going on by itself! One day, we finished dinner, cleaned up and were in the living room when we heard the clicking sound of the oven being ignited. No one was in the kitchen and no one turned it on. The oven dial was off, but the oven was clearly heating up, quickly and quite hot. We could not turn it off by turning the dial, so we were forced to unplug it from the back. At that point the oven was extremely hot and it was a dangerous act to try to move a heavy and hot range to unplug it. We called Warehouse Discount Center right away, to ask for help and express our concerns.
We spoke to the manager at that point, but he said that all he could do was order service for us. When the serviceman came out, no problems were discovered. We were outraged when we plugged our range back in to make dinner and the turning on of the oven by itself happened once again. Luckily, we were home and we heard
the clicking sound once again. When I opened the oven door to check the temperature, large blue flames shot out of the oven towards us. It was very scary! My husband was not home, so my 14 year old son and I had to move the extremely hot oven out from the wall once again to unplug the range. It was again a dangerous
thing to do. Once again, I called Warehouse Discount Appliance and Viking for repair on this issue and a new Thermostat Kit and DSI Module were replaced on the Viking range. Although this issue occurred twice and has been repaired, we are still fearful that it may reoccur. This could be extremely unsafe if it happens when no one
is home, or even worse if one of our older children are home alone. We are confident this is something your company would not want to be responsible for. The third service call was requested in July of 2012 for the range not cooking properly again. This time, the repairman said it was due to lack of preheating and
called it an "education" service call. We feel strongly, especially with my husband being a private chef, that we know how to operate our range and it wasn't a preheating issue, but the uneven and incorrect cooking arising again. Our fourth service call in January of 2013 was requested because the range was not cooking properly just as we foresaw. We had preheated the oven, set a chicken in to roast, came back after an hour of roasting and the chicken was still raw in a luke warm oven. We could reach in and place our hands on the metal grates inside the oven and not burn ourselves. Although the dial read 350 degrees, it probably was only about 100 degrees. We were so infuriated by having our range out of service once again. Dinner could not be finished and take-out had to be ordered again. Once again, I called Warehouse Discount Appliance and spoke to a salesman at the store. He knew, by voice, who we were and remembered all of our numerous problems with our Viking range. We told him of our current problem and he said again that he was sorry, but that service would have to be called out on the issue. He continued to tell me that he uses our story, of our Viking range going on by itself,
to encourage his customers NOT to buy Viking ranges. Instead, he guides his customers to other ranges with better reviews. It is insulting to know that the store we assuredly purchased a very expensive range from, is now using our story to sway their customers to purchase other "better" ranges, while we still have our defective range sitting in our kitchen. I followed up with a phone call to the store manager, to express our concerns over our range and our disgust that our personal story is being used to sway consumers away from Viking ranges. We asked for our range to be returned and to receive store credit to purchase another range. He had to check with upper management and he would get back to me in a few days since it was the start of the holiday weekend. When he did, he said no, he was sorry but we could not return it for store credit. We want a reliable appliance in our home, especially since we paid a large amount of money thinking we were getting one of the best professional grade appliances. 

In February 2013, the entire electrical panel of the wall where the Viking range is plugged into shorted out and the electrical plugs had to be replaced. This electrical problem did not occur anywhere in the house, only to the wall where the range is plugged into. Again, this range remains defective in more and more ways. Being so outraged over the numerous problems on a major appliance that costs over $3000.00, we called the Southern California Viking Distributer and spoke with you. As you know, we expressed our concerns that this product is a "lemon" and needs to be replaced. You stated that if we wanted the range returned, we would have to contact the national Viking product center in Mississippi. We called that location and spoke on January 15, 2013. She listened thoughtfully to our concerns and expressed sympathy to our issues, but she did say that a return would have to be authorized by you. We found this confusing because you had stated that you could not authorize a return, but that only the Mississippi office could. After receiving these conflicted messages, our frustrations with our Viking range grew.
We are now formally asking for our defective range to be returned to Warehouse Discount Appliance and we request store credit or refund in the amount of $3,413.62. We ask this of both Viking and Warehouse Discount Appliance. We look forward to a response from both parties in order to receive the fair resolution we are seeking. If we do not receive a response from you by March 15, 2013, indicating your agreement to make us whole, our only available course of action will be legal action.
Thank you for listening to our requests and concerns.
justification: The incident involved a defective range causing potential safety hazards, including the oven turning on by itself and emitting flames, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Message = We purchased dishes from Macys that are labeld "The Cellar manufactured exclusively for Macy's". Pattern Code is CLRCLR42.  These were sold as individual peices, not a set. These are marked Microwave Safe. However when placed in the microwave for minute settings they become burn hazards. The other items such as plates, bowls in the Cellar collection have similar temperature readings. These are extremely unsafe. They have caused burns to our hands. incident_description:
Frigidaire Smoothtop Electric Range
MODEL# PLEF398DCC
SERIAL # VF44455219

Last night while prepping my dinner, the knob control panels turned on and began to flash and make loud beeping sounds. (My stove was not turned on yet...it turned on all by itself)  Then all the stove top ranges turned on too. Within 15 seconds an electrical fire broke out from behind the unit. Then the main motherboard turned on, flashed and made noises too, which then caught fire as well.

LUCKILY I was home as I was able to pull the stove away from the wall to stop the fire from igniting the rest of my kitchen, and ran to shut off the main power to the unit from my electric panel.

When I called Frigidaire, they told me the control knobs were recalled and would send me out the replacement parts, but they said they would not replace the main (expensive) control panel (motherboard).

My complaint is that if one recalled electrical part is bad and catches fire and then causes another main part which is right next to it to catch fire, then all the electrical parts in the top part of the unit should be part of the recall as well.  Had I not been home, this recalled part of the appliance could have set fire to not only the motherboard, but to my entire house! Therefore, I think to protect myself and future consumers, Frigidaire should expand this recall to include replacing the main control panel as well. Had the recalled parts not went on fire (and just burnt out) then my motherboard would still be intact and not need to be replaced.

Thank you 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but no injury or death occurred, and the user was able to prevent further damage.

missed it by a few numbers. This recall was in 2009. Wondering if ours would fit in now. Don't see any online. I
called Colson who repaired it the first time and they said it would cost $125. thought that was too much so called
Denvers Best Appliance Repair and they said they'd come out and look at it and if we got it repaired they would

incident_description:
This is a refrigerator with 2 doors side by side on the top and one large drawer below for the freezer.  Since it was new, the refrigerator doors must be closed forcefully or thy do not close completely. We had to clear out the fridge several times before we learned to slam the doors. Sometimes, the doors do not close and we don't realize it until we go to the fridge again.. We do not get rid of food every time this happens; it would cost a lot of money. 
I called Whirlpool when this first happened and they said there was nothing they could do. I called again today, 2 and 1-1/2  years later and was told the same thing. 
It seems to me that this is a potentially dangerous  design flaw that could cause food poisoning.

The model number of this refrigerator is GX5FHTXVB93 and it was purchased at Sears on September 15, 2010.
justification: The refrigerator's design flaw may lead to food spoilage, posing a risk of food poisoning, but no actual incidents of injury or death are reported.

incident_description:
First our ice maker stopped working last summer. Next we heard a grinding sound when the door was closed, which stopped when the door was opened. This noise lasted for a couple of days and then went away, and we did not notice any obvious cooling issues at that time. The noise occurred 2-3 months ago. My children began to get sick with gastrointestinal symptoms on February 21st. It was intermittent and there was no obvious pattern or source. The only one who was spared was my 3 month-old who was not eating anything from the refrigerator. All along the thermostat in the fridge was indicating a correct temperature. Then, on the morning of 3/6 we woke up to all of the milk in our refrigerator completely curdled. A thermometer placed in the fridge read 60 degrees (the digital thermostat still said 36). We called a local repair company who came that day. While at our home the technician found that the back of the fridge (inside, behind the back panel) had iced up accounting for the ice maker not working (the line froze up and no longer delivered water to the ice maker), the grinding noise (the fan was hitting ice forming around it until it became encased in ice and stopped) and the cooling problem. He said he read about the issue and how to fix it in a bulletin from Samsung. He had to order us a seal and a clip (and a new fan since being stuck caused it to burn out). The clip holds the drain line at a distance from the cooling system that prevents it from freezing--the original clip installed by Samsung is not long enough to prevent freezing. We had to thaw the refrigerator overnight and we are still waiting for the repair since the parts had to be ordered. I contacted Samsung on 3/8 (i have a transcript). There was supposed to be a claim filed to help us replace our lost food, which was substantial. I have not heard back about that yet. I am hoping they will also pay for the repair, since any decent company would have initiated a recall for something like this. 

When we can't trust a refrigerator to cool properly it becomes a food safety issue, and I feel that by their inaction Samsung put my family at risk. I also worry for pregnant women and immune compromised individuals who may experience severe health problems from eating food that has not been chilled properly.
justification: The incident resulted in gastrointestinal illness among family members due to spoiled food, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is possible (likelihood 3) given the described malfunction and its impact.

incident_description:
Consumer went to pre-heat the oven by pressing bake. The temperature did not change on the oven. The consumer opened the oven door and smelled a strong gas smelled. The oven was then turned off and the oven door was left opened. To air out his home he also opened the windows inside to rid the gas vapors. 

Once the vapors cleared, the consumer attempted to pre-heat the oven again. He left the oven door opened and heard clicks coming from the unit. The gas vapors began to emit and the oven still did not heat.

The consumer states the broiler and the stove works fine. The only problem is with the baking function of the range. 

1/30/13- The manufacturer sent a repairman ([REDACTED]) to fix the range. The spark wasn't sparking at the ignitor because the wire was not insulated. 
2/4/13- [REDACTED] from the manufacturer was contacted. She told the consumer that there were no previous problems with the range. He stated he preferred to have a new range instead of having the new range repaired. She stated his warranty only covered repairs, not replacements. 

Another repairman ([REDACTED]) was sent out to fix the same issue with the range. The ignitor was adjusted to be closer to the gas line to help it slight be the spark.

2/2/13- The retailer was contacted and referred the consumer to the manufacturer. 

The consumer believes that this a defect in the range. The spark needed does not ignite so gas will emit though the oven which is not heating.
justification: The incident involved gas emission and potential ignition failure, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was addressed by repair, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:

incident_description:
We purchased a Kenmore ceramic cooktop range with electronic control panel, model 790.99122405  serial number VF53448033, in Oct of 2005. Evident very quickly, the front rim of the cooktop would get very hot from the oven heat. It gets hot enough that it could burn a child. Several attempts have been made by Sears service to correct this problem to no avail.
Secondly, the first time we used the oven self-cleaning cycle, the porcelain on the bottom of the oven interior cracked spider web like, and it has begun to rust. 
Finally, about a month ago, after using the left rear burner, when it was turned off the burner kept cycling on and off at max heat. Cycling the on/off switch had no effect. Had to turn the circuit breaker off to the range. When the breaker was turned back on the condition was still there. After turning the breaker off again, I raised the cooktop and disconnected the wire to the burner. We cook a lot so this is a real inconvenience. I feel that this could happen with any of the other burners at any time and this could be a real fire hazard. After reading the problems associated with models 99012/13/14 and 19 that had a recall, I feel that this and associated models should be in the same category.
justification: The cooktop can burn a child and the burner cycling issue poses a fire hazard, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
On March 10, Sunday night at 11:00 while our dishwasher was running, smoke began pouring out of our Bosch dishwasher. Then flames leaped out of the door at the top and bottom and front (plastic area) of the door. I grabbed a fire extinguisher and fired several bursts of the chemicals at the fire. Then the fire leaped out of the door again and I fired several more bursts. Finally the flames died. My wife had called 911 while I was fighting the fire. When the firemen arrived, they removed the dishwasher and put it in our driveway. Melting plastic from the front door had fallen on the linoleum floor of the kitchen and burned it. The house was full of smoke and the chemicals from the extinguisher were everywhere. We spent the night at our daughter's house. 
After notifying our insurance company, we spent the next five days dealing with giant fans, and cleaners and shampooers of rugs who spent long days in our house, putting everything else on hold. 
Besides the damage to the house and the disruption of our lives, I suspect that our health might have been compromised by our breathing toxic fumes from the burning plastic while fighting the fire. 

I searched the internet for more examples of burning Bosch dishwashers and discovered more than 80 complaints about them. Some people even lost their homes to the fire because they weren't home while the dishwasher was running and it ignited. Bosch has been unresponsive from the majority of complaints. I also read that there might have been a recall, but most people weren't aware of it. One complainant said that Bosch told him that Bosch had hired a company to handle the recall, but that Bosch wasn't responsible if the company didn't do a good job. (We learned that our dishwasher was among those that were recalled, but we were never notified. Our dishwasher was 9 years old.}
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage and potential health risks from toxic fumes, but no direct injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a new Hamilton Beach Coffee Maker Model 43254R, Series A4011DT from Sams Club in Dale City, Virginia a few months ago.

I made coffee in the morning.  I always make enough for two days of coffee and just microwave the remaining or make iced coffee with it later.  I left in the morning for the day.  I came home late at night and it was only because my child wanted a dinner at 9:30 p.m. that I was even in the kitchen.  After making dinner I kept hearing the pop of a heating element.  I searched everywhere - no heating element indicator lights on anywhere in kitchen.  I gave up, shut off all lights and started to go upstairs for the night, heard the heating element sound again.  So I started touching things - and this coffee maker, all lights off, was on and HOT!  It had evaporated my half pot of coffee during the day and all that was left was a welded black hardened mess at bottom.

I have unplugged it, but this is new, and shouldn't be happening.  The auto-off feature has ALWAYS worked.  I almost never turn it off manually.  There is no auto-off override.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned by not turning off automatically, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED] and I purchased a Sears Kenmore Elite Electric Range in April of 2007.  The Model number is 79046703605, and the serial number NF71612736.  On Wednesday,  February 13, 2013 I called 911 in reference to white smoke coming out from the range as well as the smell of an electrical type fire.  Neither the oven nor the cook top was on, or in use at the time.  I heard a noise from the kitchen area, smelled the odor, then smoke.  The Daytona Beach Fire Department responded and advised it was my oven.  After, the fire department cleared the scene, I called Sears Home Repair at 1-800-4 my home.  Sears advised they would not be able to send a repair contractor out until Saturday, February 16, 2013.  I asked if they could get someone to respond sooner as I would be out of town that weekend at a pre scheduled conference.  Sears replied that was the earliest they could send someone.  I replied, that was unacceptable and I would be forced to contact another repair company.  I contacted Superior Services appliance repair in Daytona Beach Florida.  They sent a repairman out that afternoon on February 13th.  The repairman removed the back panel where he found the parts that caught on fire.  The parts were  1 fan motor part number 5304467898, relay board part number 316418101, board part number 316460900.  Had I not been home at the time I could have possibly lost my pets and my home due to the this appliances internal fire.  Further, I had to wait two weeks for the parts which were coming direct from the manufacturer.  The total cost I paid for repair was 345.55.  When I called Sears they claimed there was no manufacturer defect on the product.  An appliance should not catch fire especially when not in use. This is a serious safety concern/defect with this appliance.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common for appliances not in use.

The oven control panel was not illuminated but the heating element inside was extremely hot.   She stated that the oven was never used before retiring to bed.  The oven was unplugged to prevent further damages.  Her spouse replugged the oven the next day and waited a few mins and noticed that the oven became extremely hot like it was on self cleaning, he immediately unplugged it again. incident_description:
The consumer stated that the oven self cleaning mode malfunctions which causes the oven to be extremely hot externally.  He has taken the oven apart being a professional and discovered that the firm had not built the internal connections properly, which would allow the oven to stay cool external while it is operating in that mode.  He has to stop the self cleaning functions while it is operating to prevent a fire.  He has had to stop using this mode.  This incident has been occurring since installation.

The consumer has contacted the firm on several occasions over the years about the problem and they have not assist him.

The self-cleaning feature worked only one (1) time.  The next time consumer's wife tried to use it they heard a loud constant noise.  The consumer stopped the self-cleaning feature.  A repairman was called and he put on a new fan assy (for cooling the exterior of the oven?)  He did not stay to put the oven thru the self-cleaning feature.  It made the same noise again and was stopped.  (Self-clean disengaged)  The consumer pulled oven out and discovered that as oven heated during self-clean the fan expanded and moved down the shaft striking the screen in rear.  Cheap fan should not be a press fit on shaft.  If you do not turn self-clean off fan would engage screen, stop, and oven would overheat.  

Descriptioin of fire danger!  (Drawing) point to back of oven, point to  wire screen, point to plastic fan and bushing.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven with a high risk of overheating and potential fire, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

Consumer would also like to note that when relating this incident on her homeowners association page, she was informedthat another homeowner also encountered a similar problem. Their element in the oven blew out and they had to call fire dept.
justification: The consumer stated that no one was injured, but the incident caused a fire hazard and the wires underneath were burnt.

incident_description:
We own a GE Dishwasher, model PDW8700N00BB, serial # SM886165B.  It was purchased in 2007 along with an extended warranty that expired in Nov. 2012. The inside cavity is stainless steal.  Last week my wife put in a load of dishes and went upstairs.  I came home to find a pervasive smell of burning plastic.  When I opened the dishwasher some smoke escaped.  I found that inside parts had melted and that part of the washer arm had broken off and was burning against the heating element.

The next day I called GE and their "Consumer Advocate" went into defensive mode.  She tried to insist that the burning plastic was not toxic, etc.  She scheduled one of GE's techs to look at it and he affirmed that a mechanism in the door failed and caused the heater to remain on and go into overdrive, thereby boiling the water and melting down the inside parts.  He said he had seen this a few times before.  He called it 'very dangerous', etc.  He supposedly reported it to GE's division that handles technical failures. 

When the Consumer Advocate called back the next day she affirmed the above.  Her offer of a remedy was that I should pay GE over $700 for a new dishwasher.  When I stated that my family was at risk due to their machine's catastrophic failure and that it might be related to the issues causing other models to be recalled she essentially said 'take it or leave it.'  

After a limited amount of surfing I found other examples of similar events with this model.  I am requesting an investigation.  In addition, I believe that despite the dishwasher's extended warranty ending a few months ago, GE should replace it in light of what appears to be a serious defect.

Thank you!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction causing melting and smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The technician noted similar prior occurrences, indicating a possible but not frequent issue.

justification: The oven's ignition issue and loud 'WOOSH' sound indicate a potential hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting his microwave/convection model# not available at this time with serial# not available at this time purchased in CO estimated around June 15,2005.

Caller and family use the microwave portion of this unit only and they use it regularly.

Caller didn't have any safety issue with this product until the week of January 14th, 2013 when he was baking potatoes (no wrapping on them at all), when it caught fire with flames coming down from the top of the microwave downward into the microwave after running for only 4 or 5 minutes into the 22 minute cycle.

Caller's son alerted him to the microwave being on fire.

Caller immediately turned the microwave off leaving the door shut so that it would run out of oxygen.

Caller contacted service tech thinking the fire may have been a result of some sort of build up, however the service tech stated that the magnetron was "going out". 

He assured family that he had repaired this problem.

When caller came home he turned the microwave on, no cooking, just checking it out and it caught fire again the in the same manner as the first time.

The service tech and the caller came to the agreement that there may be an issue with the microwave being manufactured in a manner that does not allow cleaning of the working areas at the top inside of the unit.

Service Tech also advised him that he should on occasion boil water in the microwave and let the steam clean the microwave.

He followed the service tech's advice and has had no problems since he began "steaming".

Caller contacted the manufacturer, spoke with  [REDACTED] who advised the caller that the problem was the magnetron but offered no remedy.

There are no injuries reported with this incident

Caller is asking that his microwave be inspected by CPSC, add a warning to the instructions advising consumers that the microwave can catch fire  if this "steaming" is not practiced to keep those components in the top of the microwave 

It was the use of the convection feature that started the two fires.  The consumers rarely use that feature.
justification: The microwave caught fire twice but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was using his dishwasher on the normal wash cycle for approximately 5 minutes and it started to emit smoke. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was emitting smoke from the top of the door where the control panel was located. 

The consumer stated that the dishwasher blew the circuit breaker. He stated that he waited 1 hour before opening the door of the dishwasher. 

The consumer stated that there were no visible damages to the dishwasher. 

He stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he will be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and blew a circuit breaker, but there were no injuries or visible damages.

incident_description:
I have a stainless steel crock pot brand smart pot. I bumped the pot with my hand while using it and now have a 2nd degree burn on my hand which is about 1 inch long by 1/2 inch wide. This burn became infected and I have had to be on antibiotics. Additionally, when it does finally heal, I will have a good size scar on my hand.

My concern is that I had no idea that the outside of the crock pot was so hot during use. There are no safety warnings on the pot itself. If I received this type of burn, I can only imagine what would happen if a child touched the pot while in use.

No counter top cooking device should become so hot on the exterior that it can cause this type of injury or certainly should have a large warning on the outside about the potential danger if touched during use.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn that became infected and will leave a scar, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) since the description suggests the pot's exterior heat is a consistent hazard during use.

incident_description:
The consumer says that on February 10th she put the oven thru the self cleaning cycle.  she then used the oven on February 13th.  She smelled something strange as she was cooking dinner that evening.  She went to bed when the carbon monoxide detector went off.  

She called 911, when they told her to open a door and go outside.  The fire dept and medics arrived.  The Fire dept determined the level of carbon monoxide to be extremely high to the point that there house could have caught fire or they could have died.  She called the propane gas company the next morning who determined the issue was with the oven and they red tagged the unit.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said she did not have the extended warranty or recall.  They offered to send out a technician for a fee.  she called again and they offered a service smart agreement.  She emailed them three times and did not get responses to those emails.
justification: The incident involved extremely high levels of carbon monoxide, posing a risk of death, which was only averted by the carbon monoxide detector and emergency response.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while she was using the oven to bake at 350 degrees, it switched at some point to broil mode.  She noticed that because the contents she removed were very dark and then she realized the oven was on broil.  It then automatically turn itself off.

1/21/13 The second incident occurred when she attempted to bake some cookies, however, a few mins later she smelled the contents burning and noticed that the oven was on broil mode.  She was unable to power it off from the control panel, the circuit breaker had to be used to switch it off.

1/24/13  The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that the range was not recalled and she should report it to the agency.

The caller feels that this electric range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved the oven malfunctioning and burning food, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his dishwasher in 2005, had no problems with it until February 14th, 2013 after he had
started the dishwasher then went to bed. He got up the next morning, smelled smoke, opened the
dishwasher and saw burn marks inside the door and on the edge of the stone countertop above the
dishwasher. He turned the circuit off. The fire had occurred sometime throughout the night, and had
extinguished itself.

This recall could not be accessed at the CPSC web site but can be accessed at the GE web site.

No injuries have been reported. Caller contacted manufacturer who is fulfilling the remedy: A
technician will inspect the unit, and if the unit is not repairable, manufacturer will replace it at no
charge; but if it is repairable, they will repair it or provide a rebate toward the purchase of a new
dishwasher of the same brand. The caller stated that a few hundred dollars toward a dishwasher is
insignificant, and he would rather the manufacturer replace the dishwasher. (Note: since this report was
initially filed, manufacturer has deemed the unit not to be repairable, and has replaced the unit.)

Caller contacted manufacturer who is fulfilling the remedy, however caller states that the remedy is not actually sufficient because a few hundred dollars toward a dishwasher is nothing and he would rather the manufacturer replace his dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved a fire with burn marks but no injuries were reported, and the fire extinguished itself.

incident_description:
The microwave basically turns itself on, it self starts when it senses heat from the stovetop.  The consumer says that she gets messages on the microwave that tell her to set the time, or have random codes on the digital display.  

 She says that the random messages would come one when she was using her stove top.  The consumer feels that the heat from the stove top would make the microwave think that it is getting ready to cook. 

She immediately unplugged it or hit the off button.  This would make the messages go away.  After this happened several times, she stopped using it altogether.  When the microwave sends messages,s he hits the off button.  Them she decided to unplug it permanently. She is afraid to use it or even keep it plugged into the socket.

She contacted the manufacturer who told her the unit is not on recall and there is nothing they can do.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury occurred; the issue was resolved by unplugging the device.

incident_description:
On February 9th, 2013 the caller entered her kitchen then noticed that the front left burner of her electric range was on and burning red hot although she had not yet used the range.

In addition to the left front burner of her range turning on spontaneously the other three burners do not heat accordingly.  If turning burner to high it will go to medium, if turning to low the burner will go to another setting, none will stay where set.
Range had been working fine before this incident.

Caller unplugged range.
She said that the switch was repaired by a repair tech but it still does not work properly.
so she unplugged it and is afraid to use it or have it plugged in while she is not home or not in the kitchen.

There have been no incidents.   
Caller contacted manufactuer around February 12th, 2013, was advised that the range was not under warranty.
justification: The burner malfunctioned spontaneously, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: Kohl's food network 16" electric fry pan  style 18012 -- on off switch and temp setting is not readable when plugged into fry pan--you either have to look at an angle  or unplug from fry pan to set temp.  Doing this creates possible burns to your hands etc.---temperature on/off switch design flaw
justification: The design flaw in the fry pan's switch creates a potential for burns, indicating an incident with no injury reported yet.

incident_description: Employee was in the process of pouring hot coffee from a coffee pot into her cup. The glass decanter separated from the plastic lid/handle component. The decanter fell to the floor breaking and splashing hot coffee on the employee. This pot and two others were purchased last week from a local office supply company. These pots were new and an accident such as this would suggest a possible defect with the pots that can cause additional accidents and injuries.
justification: The employee was injured by hot coffee due to a defective coffee pot, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident suggests a possible defect in multiple pots, making recurrence likely.

incident_description:
(01/12/2013) The consumer stated that the microwave was making a loud noise while in use. She noticed that the turnable was stopping and starting instead of turning continuously. The consumer was cooking food, (she did not remember what she was cooking or how long it was cooking), which became super hot posing a burn hazard. It also caused the plastic container to melt. The microwave had been used before this incident.

The consumer thinks that there might be an electrical problem with the motor. She stated that one day when she was out, there was a power outage in her apartment. She checked with the other tenants and they did not have an outage in their apartment. 

The consumer stated that her mother has the same model. She stated that her mother is experiencing the same problems. 

(01/16/2013) The consumer called sears.com and spoke to [REDACTED]. She told her that problem. The consumer stated that they did not seem to be concerned. She was advised that UPS will pick up the product. She advised [REDACTED] that her brother had taken the microwave from her place so that he could return it to Sears.

The consumer stated that she went to her local Sears store and spoke with the manager, Mr. [REDACTED]. She told him about the problem and also gave him a letter. She told him that the microwave should be recalled. he advised her to call the Service Center and have someone to came out to look at it. She told him she longer had the product.
justification: The incident involved a burn hazard and melted plastic, indicating potential for injury, and the problem was reported by multiple users, suggesting a possible issue with the model.

incident_description:
Consumer pre-heated the oven to about 425 degree. The consumer noticed that the range started making a sizzling noise. Immediately the control panel burst into a fire, the flames were about 3 inches tall.  The consumer pulled out the stove from in between the cabinets and unplugged the unit. He also patted out the flames until they were gone. He stated that the fire only came from the inside the control panel.

The consumer burned his right hand removing the range which was hot from the fire, but did not sustain any damage to his skin or hand beyond soot and heat. The consumer ran his hand under cold water to aid the discomfort. Consumer also hit his head on the fan over the range while he pulling it to unplug the electric cord. 

There are no damages to report. 

Consumer still has the range and it has not been used since the incident. 

The consumer has contacted Kenmore around 2/18/13 because he saw on the news that ranges have caught on fire. The consumer was told his model was not listed on a recall.
justification: The consumer sustained minor injuries (burned hand and hit his head) but no serious harm or property damage occurred, indicating a moderate severity level. The incident is unlikely to recur given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: The oven would not turn off.  Flashing a F! code, went to max temperature.  I had to unplug the oven to get it to turn off.  it would not reset, once I plugged it it it turned on by itself and the oven again went to max temperature.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I've had consistently hazardous experiences with a certain brand and model of can opener, such that I think it probably shouldn't be on the market.

Following original purchase, I've returned and tried two more of the same model (three total), and found that each time the can opener not only doesn't perform its specified function, but it creates metal shrapnel that inevitably contaminates the contents of the can.
justification: The can opener creates metal shrapnel that contaminates food, posing a hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The consumer says the paint started chipping and arching.  she also says the microwave started running by itself.  She had to unplug it to make it stop.  The more she used it, the louder it became.  

She tried restarting it a few times but it would not work.  She said the control panel went blank.  Sometimes the unit would reset itself.  

Her brother bought her the exact same model and it would run by itself and also continue to run even with the microwave door was still open.   

She contacted the manufacturer who offered to send out a technician for a fee
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning appliances with no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence across multiple units suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
My husband and I were standing in our kitchen when suddenly the entire front glass door of our Whirlpool AcuBake Electric range completely SHATTERED and rained onto our kitchen floor.  My husband and I were shocked as neither one of us had touched the stove.  The stove had not been used in at least 2 days.

I contacted Whirlpool regarding this occurrence and was told that this repair would only be covered under the manufacturer if the stove had been purchased within the past 12 months.  We purchased our home over a year ago and the stove was already installed in the home.  

I certainly believe this repair should be covered by the manufacturer considering the oven was not in use or touched and obviously this is a defect in the product and this occurrence could have caused severe injury.  I have three young children and I am grateful that they were not in the room when this occurred.  I large piece of the glass door landed on my foot but luckily there were no serious injuries from this incident.
justification: A large piece of glass landed on the person's foot, indicating an injury, but the incident was not life-threatening. The spontaneous shattering of a glass door is unlikely but not impossible.

incident_description:
01/23/2013) The consumer stated that around 1230pm CT, his wife was sitting in the family room. She heard a loud explosion. She walked into the kitchen and saw glass on the floor. The oven door on the gas range had exploded. The consumer stated that the oven had not been in use for 3 or 4 days before the incident happened. The consumer stated that he called the appliance store. They gave him the number to call Frigidaire.

(01/23/2013) The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer around 1pm. He spoke with [REDACTED]. He was transferred to the extended warranty department. He spoke with [REDACTED] . He was advised that she would find a repair company. He was given an authorization number to call A & M in Romeoville, Il at 815-577-3710. He left a message at 1:30p. He has not heard from A & M. 

  
The consumer stated that his wife went on line and saw a video showing different manufacturers having the same problem with their product.

The consumer also stated that they are senior citizens who take extremely care of everything.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
On Monday March 4, 2013 at about 9:15PM I wiped my  gas kitchen stove off with a kitchen dishcloth, I remember in the back of my mind that when I wiped the stove it seem to hang just bit on one of the knobs.......(not knowing that it turned the gas on and passed the automatic ignition button) I left the kitchen and laid down.    About 11:15PM  I walked back into kitchen and realized that the gas was leaking from back burner without any flame. At that time It had been expelling gas for over 2 hours. I immediatley turned the burner to the off position.   The gas smell was very strong and I immediatley open a couple of windows and went out the front door, called Center Point Entergy and reported the gas problem.  About 30 minutes later the gas company arrived and noted that when they got out of the truck that he could smell gas immediately in the yard, he checked the gas meter and inside house to make sure the leak was not elsewhere (which it was not). The kitchen area is located in the central part of my 3,000 sg ft house, therefore I believe the gas spread thruout the kitchen area and great room and maybe that is why I did not smell it until I walked into the kichten again. CenterPoint Entergy recommended not to stay in the house that night.

This was a very dangerours event and how it turned the gas on without the igination switch lighting the stove.  

Stove type:  dual fuel range slide in model - Frididaire 
model number PLD28504RDC1      Serial number TH51160877
justification: The incident involved a gas leak with no injury or death, but posed a significant danger.

incident_description:
Consumer recently read the March 2013 Consumer Report magazine. Inside on page 34 there is an article about Microwave Ovens powering on by themselves. 

The consumer states that his microwave powers on by itself; especially when there is a power interruption. He has experienced this problem over dozen of times over the microwaves life span. 

A new microwave was purchased 12/12 to replace the microwave that powers on by itself. The consumer still does have the older microwave. 

The microwave has not caused any damages; the consumer would like to have the incident documented. Since this was noted in the consumer reports magazine.

Today the consumer contacted ([REDACTED]) the manufacturer @ 800-211-7262 and filed a report# [REDACTED].
justification: The microwave powers on by itself but has not caused any damages or injuries, fitting the criteria for an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
In Oct. 2004 we bought a Thermador Sm272 Wall Oven / Microwave combination. Since then it's been in the repair shop 3 times. Twice for a wiring fire that started in the door lock motor wiring. Once for a Magnetron replacement for the microwave. My wife resorted to blowing the flames out by mouth because the fires were inside the cabinet.

Had no one been around, I might have lost my home!!
I'd be interested in joining any class-action lawsuits involving this oven.
I will NEVER buy another Thermador product because of this.
justification: The incident involved wiring fires and a magnetron replacement, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I was preheating the oven to 350 degress when I heard an explosion. The outer glass door on oven shattered and many pieces of glass flew across kitchen and into family room. Model JKP90D
justification: The incident involved an explosion and shattered glass, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Dear US CPSC,

I'd like to report a problem with a Black and Decker toaster/convection oven that I believe is a hazard.  This is in reference to Model #CT04400B Type 1.  This toaster oven has a unique issue with its on/off button.  If you turn the dial ever so slightly past the off setting, the toaster oven remains on, and I believe that this is a significant fire hazard.  We found that frequently, the toaster oven would remain on for very long periods of time and get very, very hot.  It was very easy to mistaken leave the oven in the on setting, when you meant to tum it off.  I have enclosed a couple of pictures of what I mean.

I wanted to let your organization know about this dangerous appliance.
justification: The toaster oven's malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Food Network Slow Cooker
Sensio Inc. 
Model: YDE-1006
ITEM: 18014

I've had the slow cooker for approx. 2 yrs.  

I noticed that the slow cooker had not heated the food after 4+ hours.  I checked on it several times throughout the day & the display was working normally.  My husband, who has some experience with electrical work, took the slow cooker apart & discovered that in two places the insulation appeared to be burned through & the wires were charred. The wire insulation is brittle & falling to pieces along the length of the wire. What was left of the wire was black & very brittle.  We are very glad we found this b/c it stopped working as opposed to someone being shocked b/c of the short. We are keeping the slow cooker for a while and would be happy to send pictures.

I bought it new & since I've had it I don't believe it has had any abnormal use (used dry, on too long, etc.).
justification: The slow cooker malfunctioned with burned insulation and charred wires, but no injury or shock occurred.

incident_description: Had set oven to self clean cycle. Approximately 30 minutes later heard a very loud pop. Checked to see what noise was to find inside glass window of oven had shattered. I have children and pets that potentially could have been hurt.  Fortunately outer glass held.  Repairman coming tomorrow to replace (i assume) the window.

She discovered that the oven spontaneously turned on broil which caused the contents to burn.  She was unable to power it off, it was extremely hot, the heating coil was red.  The circuit breaker was used to switch it off.

The caller is concerned about the way this oven malfunctioned as a fire hazard.

incident_description: On 3/4/2013 I had a repair technician out to replace the keypad on my KitchenAid dishwasher because some of the lights (heavy wash, sani-rinse, high temp scrub) were stuck on and my dishwasher would not always start.  On 3/5/2013 I started my dishwasher.  About 10 minutes later, I noticed a strong burning plastic smell.  When I went into my kitchen it was filled with smoke.  I opened the dishwasher and there was a lot of smoke coming out of the top of the dishwasher door.  I have turned off the circut breaker to the unit.  If we had not been home at the time, my house could have burnt down.

I no longer feel comfortable with this appliance in my home but feel Sears should be held accountable.  This could have resulted in great property damage and possibly even death.  I look forward to a reply to give me direction in getting my concerns addressed.  Thank you in advance for your attention in this matter.....[REDACTED]

incident_description:
In reference to Kenmore Elite under the counter dishwasher, model # 66515932000.  I turned my dishwasher on today and after it running for a little bit I smelled a burning odor and I looked over at the dishwasher and I saw smoke coming from the button panel on the front of the door. Thank you, 
[REDACTED]

Respondent was baking @ 325 for less than 30 minutes. The respondent noticed through the oven window that the broiler coil was lit. incident_description:

However, about 30 mins later she heard a popping noise followed by a crackling sound, she noticed that there were flames erupting from the rear of the oven.  She was unable to power it off from the control panel, the display board was flashing, the circuit breaker was used to switch off the unit.

burners worked when used once that day and then stopped working completely the next day. On

couple of seconds throughout the heating time. My oven did not do this before the refurbished or new
control board was installed!
justification: The incident involved flames and scorching but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I own a Bosch dishwasher, model SHE44C05UC/22, serial number FD8605 01545

The heater relay on the control board of my dishwasher failed, melting the relay pin.

On the morning of March 3, 2013, my wife started a load of dishes. We noticed a few hours later that the dishwasher seemed stuck on "1 minute" and would not complete its cycle. Some Internet sleuthing told us the dishwasher's control board was to blame. I took out the control board and was stunned to see a burned PCB board where the heater relay had shorted out, burning itself partially off the board. The pin of the relay was melted through.

I easily replaced the relay but as I thought about it I became very concerned that a fire could have occurred. The heat was enough to melt the solder on the board, so it was hot enough to start a fire.

I am aware of the 2009 voluntary recall on Bosch dishwashers. Though my model's serial number does not fall into the recall category. I believe it should. What happened to me was absolutely unsafe and has rattled my confidence in an otherwise fine product.

I ask that the CPSC and Bosch evaluate expanding the recall to include models like mine. Dishwashers should not be so vulnerable to catching fire.
justification: The incident involved a failed heater relay that could have potentially caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We turned on our Whirlpool Dishwasher Model GU2500XTP81.  Shortly into the cycle, an acrid smell came from the dishwasher and smoke came out the front. We turned off the dishwasher and the circuit breaker.  We opened the control panel this morning and found the plastic had melted where the wires enter the controls and also the black plastic housing had melted.  This is a very dangerous situation - the dishwasher did not shut itself off as Whirlpool reported it would.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting plastic, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I have a kitchen aid built in microwave oven which was installed in 2002. During use, the top side of the microwave sparked on caught on fire.  The T.V. dinner in the microwave was not the culprit.  There was no metal in the microwave.  It was the microwave itself that ignited.  The flames melted the top of microwave.

incident_description:
Oster Countertop Oven Model TSSTTV0000. Yesterday it burned the food in the oven. The temperature set was 400 deg F. We let the oven cook and set the temperature at 400 deg F. We put an oven thermometer inside. The measured temperature passed 400 deg F, and then 450 deg F, and was still rising so we turned the oven off.

incident_description:

I have had several incidents of " smoke and burned bread " during last few weeks which each time I've though was due to my error on setting the timer.

The consumer explained that the toaster works with a spring timer, which you have to turn until 20 minutes and then you have to bring it down to a lower time.

incident_description:
The consumer says when cooking over the stove he began to smell the strong presence of gas.  This happened very seldom at first.  He would get light headaches as a result.  He contacted the manufacturer who took him to the safety dept who sent out a representative. 

The tech ordered a gasket for all four burners but it was not available.  After a few weeks they came to the conclusion that the part is not being made anymore and said he had to purchase a new unit.  He did not realize right away were the presence of gas was coming from.

UPDATE:
I built my home in 1996 and had a Maytag Gas Range installed by a licensed Plummer.
The unit was purchased from Montgomery Ward's store in Beaumont, TX. Some time
after purchasing the unit I began to smell a faint scent of raw natural gas when cooking
on top of the stove. Initially it was difficult to detect where the gas scent was coming
from, as the odor would always be mixed with the food odors .I have experienced
headaches that I now attribute to the fumes from the stove.
This brand and model were selected because of Maytag' s advertisement. It was portrayed
as a range with very low repair maintenance. The safety feature included having sealed
burners on the range. These features were important to me.
About six years ago I called the Maytag Company to complain about the smell of gas
while using the burners. Customer Service was not helpful. They brushed me aside
saying they were sorry and that the range was out of warranty.
Again, in early December of 2012, I called the Maytag Company only to be informed that
it is now The Maytag Whirlpool Company. I explained my problem, giving the model
and serial numbers to Customer Service. I was referred to the safety department. I again
explained my smelling of raw gas when the burners were on and the problem was getting
worse. On December 27,2012 The Maytag Whirlpool Company sent a factory service
technician to access the problem. The technician confirmed that this model uses sealed
burners to keep spills contained and to keep raw gas from escaping. This is done with
gaskets for each burner. The gaskets would get hot, wet, and cool down repeatedly which
made them prone to cracking and or deteriorating. An attempt was made by the
technician to order all new gaskets at no cost to me for the burners, only to be informed
that they were no longer available. Maytag Whirlpool came to the conclusion that the
parts were not being made anymore and that I had to purchase a new unit. I was offered
only 15% off on a new unit. I feel this is not adequate compensation for the ongoing
problems that I have experienced.
Enclosed are copies of a receipt and a card from the Technician.
Thank you for any consideration given this matter, as I have been a loyal user of your
products .(Washer/Dryer and Dishwasher which were also purchased when the home was
built)
justification: The consumer experienced headaches due to gas fumes, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The issue persisted over time, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
Caller purchased her single oven, 27" wall oven May 2011, Model#,and hasn't had any problems with it until today.

Friday, February 15th, 2013 around 11:00AM caller turned on her self cleaning function on her less than two year old Kitchenaid electric wall oven and sat down to read.

After approximately one and a half hours she heard what sounded like a huge bang with what sounded like glass hitting something.

She went immediately toward the sound to discover what it was causing the sound.
She saw that the inside glass of the oven door had exploded.

The outside glass in door did not explode however when the inside glass door exploded it sprayed out three to four feet into the kitchen area and continued to shoot glass out of the bottom as the glass cooled off.

She is asking for inspection and recall of this wall oven and for assistance to obtain repair at manufacturer expense or replacement of the range.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but her husband contacted the store where range was purchased and they are contacting the manufacturer. 

UPDATE:
Husband later called mfr who agreed to replace glass panels on oven door at mfr's expense because they had information  that the glass panels had problems.
justification: The incident involved an oven door glass exploding, causing glass to spray into the kitchen, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Our 8.5 year old dishwasher (Kenmore Elite Model 665.17464300) suddenly started making an unusual ticking noise while it was running, and in the 10 seconds it took to go to the kitchen to look at it, smoke and flames started coming out of the control panel at the top right side of the door.  We splashed some water on it to douse the flames, then got the door open in order to turn it off, then we turned the circuit off to totally cut power to it.  The noxious fumes of melting plastics and electronics filled the house for several days.  After it cooled down, we opened the control panel off the door, and took some photos.  There was a lot of blackened parts, and a wire harness completely burned through.  Luckily we were close by, so the countertop didn't catch fire.  (We would often set the timer to run while we're not home.)

We had no previous problems with the dishwasher, and no indication of anything wrong before this.  I did make a report to Sears, but they said this particular model is not recalled.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries, and the model is not recalled, indicating such events are unlikely.

incident_description: Was cooking chicken in oven, timer went off, turned chicken over and reset timer.  Several minutes later I heard a "beep" from the oven and checked it since was too soon for timer to go off.  Opened oven door and saw top element (broiler) was on and very red...chicken was burning. incident_description: My husband and I purchased the Maytag Performa Electric Range with the Glass Cooktop and Self-Clean Oven for our new home which we moved into on Oct. 1, 2008. I hadn't used my oven very much so it wasn't very dirty but decided to try the self-cleaning oven anyhow around the middle of Dec., 2012. I read and followed the directions, but when I tried to move the locking lever to the right, it only went a little past halfway. So I called the number for the Maytag Stove, spoke to a woman there and was told that was correct and to verify that it was locked, I would see the word "lock" lit up by the clock. So I proceeded to turn it on. The next day I wiped out the small amount of residue and put the racks back in. Several days later when I opened my cabinet door next to the top side of the oven door, I noticed that the finish had been melted off my cabinet door. I checked the cabinet door on the other side of the oven door and found the same problem. I was shocked and upset, especially since my house is only 4 years old. I had the same kind of Maytag Range at my former house, the lock lever went all the way to the right and it did a beautiful cleaning job without any damage. I have since mentioned it to a couple of my neighbors and now they are afraid to "clean" their ovens and have noticed also that their oven door does not close tightly. I called the Maytag Stove number to let them know and they blamed it on the installer. When I called the company the stove was purchased from, they gave me the phone number for a service repair who charges for a house call plus so much for every 15 minutes additional. I feel something is wrong with the construction or insulation so therefore Maytag should be responsible for their stove and replacements of my cabinet doors.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted cabinet doors) but no injuries or deaths.
