incident_description: Since October, 2012, we have had problems with our LG Free Standing Electric Range; Model # LRE30955ST; purchased here in California; our problem is that the electric range top burners go on and off automatically, at all hours of the day and night; we have discovered that LG has recalled this particular range as of November 8, 2012; Recall Number: 13-03.  We reported the problem to LG and have had technicians to our residence to repair the problem on four separate occasions     [December 7, 11, and 27, 2012 and February 4, 2013].  Though electrical panels were replaced on the two first visits, the problem has NOT resolved.  We were told that the range would be replaced; and now LG is refusing to replace the range; they have stalled us since October 2012, and we have NOT had a working range since that time.  It is an extremely dangerous situation, since the range will turn on automatically with NO effort or direction of the user.  We have made every good faith effort to get the range repaired, but it is NOT repairable.  We now want the range replaced with one that is NOT a danger to our family and household.
justification: The electric range turns on automatically without user input, creating a dangerous situation, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
My Keurig B70 brewer stopped pumping water for the brew cycle.  I called Keurig customer support and the representative walked me through several trouble shooting tasks.  The unit still failed to function and the representative said that it was not repairable.  She offered me a replacement brewer at a reduced cost as the warranty had expired on mine a few months earlier.  I accepted the offer and was instructed to return only the K-cup holder and then dispose of the old brewer.

Prior to disposing of the old brewer I took it apart out of curiosity.  I found what appeared to be two electrically actuated water valves at the top of the brewer.  Both valves had stains and corrosion consistent with long-term water leakage at the lower seals.  The valves had been leaking directly above a transformer which was also water stained.

Below the transformer was a pump which was stained and corroded, and appeared to be the component that had failed.

I own two brewers identical to the one that failed, and I am concerned that there may be a safety issue if they also contain leaky valves.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure with no injury, but there is potential for safety issues due to water leakage near electrical components.

incident_description: GE OTR Microwave self started and could not be turned off with the keypad.  Magnetron was running as well as the vent motor.  Opening the door of the microwave would not turn off the magnetron or the vent motor.  Finally removing the power cord from the outlet stopped the unit.  By that time the interior of the microwave was very hot.  Thank God we were home and still awake and noticed the microwave had self started in time to take action.  The glass turntable was too hot to touch.  After everything cooled down, I plugged the power cord back into the outlet and the microwave immediately restarted.  After leaving the power cord unplugged for 24hrs the power cord was again plugged in and the unit now functions normally, but I will not leave it plugged in.  The GE technician came and determined that the control panel had an internal short and offered to replace it.  Estimated charge $265.52.  I ask him to determine if the new control panel was the same design as the old one or if it had been redesigned to fail safe when shorting out.  He told me the control panel had not been redesigned so I am not willing to spend money on a design that is still defective and could result in a fire.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was stopped before causing injury, though it posed a significant risk of fire or burns.

incident_description: This evening (2-23-2013) I turned on my GE oven (purchased in 2008) to bake some cookies and noticed a strange burning smell in my kitchen. The smell definitely smelled like an electrical device was burning. As I inspected my oven I noticed a bunch of smoke coming from up over the back of the oven. I turned the oven off and opened a window. After the oven cooled I pulled it away from the wall, unplugged it and took one of the back panels off to see what was burning. The white fluffy insulation around the wires had melted and discolored in some spots, the main electrical cord that plugs into the outlet was scorched where it connects to the back of the oven and had a melted hole in it, and a section of wires leading into the center back of the oven were discolored and scorched. Also, where the main grey power cord connects the metal bolts and plastic housing have discolored, melted and cracked. Can be seen in photos attached.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and visible damage to the oven's electrical components, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says he had the dishwasher on timed delay.  it was set to start at 9:30pm.  His wife said that the unit started steaming before it started.  The consumer says several dishes had melted, the plastic clips melted as well.  He says that the bottom wash arm is melted and stuck to the heating element.  

He also has cracked glassware in the dishwasher.  The consumer says he never had any issues with the unit prior to this incident.  He had to shut off the circuit breaker in order to get the unit to stop running.  

The consumer says that the dishwasher was extremely hot to the touch and they were moments away from having a serious fire.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher and dishes, but no injuries or fire occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says she woke up at 2:30 in the morning to something burning.  They traced it to the dishwasher.  

She opened the unit and saw the plastic melting and dripping to the bottom of the dishwasher.  The unit was not on at the time so they unplugged it.  She says that it needs to be recalled.  

The consumer says they had no prior issues with the unit.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher melting plastic but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: plugged in [slow cooker] on low for few hours- turned it on high for few hours.......took it to school and plugged in surge protector on WARM- cooker started on FIRE after a few minutes on warm
justification: The slow cooker caught fire, which is an incident with potential for harm but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire stove model fefl67dca
Stove left front burner started staying on and won't shut off.
Will also go on by itself then not shut off.
Only way to turn off is unplug it or turn off the breaker.
Reported to Frigidaire but they said it is not on recall so out of luck.
justification: The stove burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported, and the issue can be mitigated by unplugging or turning off the breaker.

incident_description:
Kenmore Microwave
Model #721.89941490
Serial #50300265

Microwave stopped working for a couple of days, or so I thought.  Could not get it to turn on or do anything.  Got up in morning on or about February 18, 2013.  Microwave was running having turned itself on sometime during the night.  I touched it to open the door and it was very, very hot.  Have wood cabinets all around it as it is over the stove model.  Very, very scary.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on unexpectedly and overheating, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
We have Kenmore electric range stove, model 790-909 3260, serial # VS65132549, where left front burner is not working properly. The burner has a problem where putting the knob to ÃÂ2? makes the stove blazing hot , as it is past MAX.  In other words, the burner will go to maximum no matter what setting is on!  This caused a ÃÂhugeÃÂ fire in the kitchen that ended up burning my wife to 3rd degree burns.  At the time of the incident, my wife was cooking a dish (fried chicken) with a vegetable oil on that burner.  
Thanks,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in third-degree burns, indicating severe injury, and the likelihood is deemed unlikely based on the specific malfunction described.

incident_description: My husband was using the range to cook dinner. He had the oven set at 550F degree to roast vegetables. He opened the oven door to check on the food and then the glass on the oven door shattered into thousands of pieces.  He didn't bump the door or do anything to prompt the door to shatter.  The oven was purchased in 2010, so it's less than 3 years old.  Shattered glass was all over the kitchen.  No one was injured. I contacted Sears, but they are unwilling to do anything about this.
justification: The oven door shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm. The occurrence is unlikely as the oven was less than 3 years old and no prior issues were mentioned.

incident_description:
I have a kenmore 30 in electric freestanding range with radiant elements. Model # 92029101, serial # RL 3910421. purchased in 2001. I have not found a recall, but noticed there was a recall on similar unit with same problem I had.
 My range oven would noit turn off after used for 10 minutes. I kept getting hotter and appeared to be off. The oven element did not turn off until we unplugged it. When we plugged back in, the oven burner immediately turned back on although, the digital screen appeared off.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, only an incident requiring unplugging the appliance.

incident_description: I was cleaning my Bodum Brazil French press when it shattered in my hand leaving a cut that required a trip to the emergency room and 6 stitches. I check it regularly for cracks, but there's was no signs when this occurred. The same thing has happened to 3 of my friends.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring emergency care, and the same issue has occurred with multiple others, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: At about 3 AM I woke up to a huge crashing noise and went into the kitchen and the glass door to my oven was all over the floor. It wasn't in use, it wasn't in a cleaning cycle. I probably haven't used the oven in almost a month. I have no clue to why this happened but I'm happy I wasn't standing there when it did or I'd be considering a law suit.
justification: The incident involved property damage (broken oven door) but no injury, and such occurrences are unlikely.

incident_description: I used the self-cleaning cycle on our KitchenAid double wall oven for the first time this afternoon. The oven is less than a year old.  An hour into the cleaning cycle, the inner glass door exploded with such force that shattered glass blew through the seams of the locked oven door. There is glass all over my kitchen, and the oven itself is filled with broken glass. If someone in my family had been standing closer to the oven at the time, there is no doubt that serious injury would have resulted.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was using my Kitchen Aid oven this evening to cook dinner and the glass door shattered during normal use (not on the cleaning cycle or other high temperature).  The glass exploded sending hot shards all over the kitchen, thankfully no one was nearby.
justification: The oven door shattered during normal use, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
I own a Sharp microwave oven model R530EW-T which I purchased August 29, 2009 from H H Gregg, 5545 Executive Blvd, Huber Heights, OH.  
The microwave has begun to start on its own. 
There was no time showing on the timer.
When I open the door, it stops.  
When I close the door, it begins running again.
justification: The microwave starting on its own poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: Toaster did not 'pop-up', starting a fire on the burnt toast.
justification: The toaster malfunction caused a fire, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Consumer was half way completed with a regular cycle in the dishwasher. The load was on for about 50 minutes when she began to smell a burning odor. The consumer noticed that the smell was coming from the dishwasher.  He immediately shut off the circuit breaker and unplugged the dishwasher. He had to wait for the dishwasher to drain out by itself because if was in the middle of a cycle. 

Once the dishwasher was drained the consumer conducted an inspection and discovered the wires  that connects along the protective cap had been melted. The dishwasher no longer works and there were no damages to the home. 

Consumer has spoken with the manufacturer. but because the item is not under the recall nothing further can be done.  He has yet to speak to the retailer.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing a burning odor and melted wires, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
I have a GE Profile range with convection heating and self-cleaning functions. Last night I started the cleaning cycle--there was a loud popping noise followed by bright sparks. Smoke came out the vent. 

I promptly turned it off. When I tried opening the door  there were flames in the oven. 

The fire department responded, the fire was contained in the oven and eventully burned out.
justification: The incident involved flames and required fire department response, but there was no injury or death, and the fire was contained.

incident_description: Fire started in back of my frigidaire refridgerator
justification: A fire starting in a refrigerator is an incident with no reported injury, and such occurrences are relatively uncommon.

incident_description:
(12/01/2012) The consumer stated that the front left burner stopped working. 

The consumer stated that the oven element was repaired in November because it would not get hot.
(01/16/2013) The consumer stated that she look in the computer today to find out  how to open the top of the stove. She discovered that the wires to the left front burner was burned.

The consumer stated that she checked for a recall but her model and serial number was not involved in a recall.
 She then alled CPSC to place a report.
justification: The incident involved a burner malfunction and burned wires, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says she was making coffee.  She had two cups out of it.  She stepped outside to take the trash out.  She came back inside, went into the kitchen and immediately smelled wire burning.  She looked over and saw sparks flying out of the base of the machine.  She says their was also a lot of smoke.  The consumer unplugged the unit, picked it up, walked out the back door and set it on her patio.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said they have never heard of this and never had a complaint.  They told her the unit is not on recall.  They said the best they can do is replace the exact same unit.  This is after going onto CPSC's web site and her reading off several complaints to them.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the coffee machine but no injury or death occurred. The manufacturer's lack of prior complaints suggests this is an unlikely occurrence.

incident_description:
On Saturday morning, February 9, 2013, during operation of the dishwasher, the pump motor made a "kick" sound at which time thick black smoke was witnessed coming from the dishwasher.   I was able to take immediate action, which included turning off the main power wall switch, opening all doors in the house, and utilizing a box to clear out the smoke. The dishwasher was in the early phase of a wash cycle, with the initial water still in tub, and the wash pump running. The settings were "normal wash" and "sani-rinse".

Further investigation of the control panel revealed charred and melted components at the control panel assembly circuit board module (whirlpool p/n 8534963).  The two large connectors (CON1 and CON2) were fused to the circuit board. Evaluation of the "hot spotsÃÂ indicate most of the damage on the component side of the circuit board is near contact P6 (heater), and near contact P10 (vent/small load AC) on the trace side of the board.
justification: The incident involved smoke and damage to the dishwasher but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she placed a sweet potato to bake on a paper plate in the microwave.  It was set to bake for 2 mins, however, she was alerted by the smoke detector later and discovered that there were flames and smoke erupting from the microwave.  The microwave powered off itself and now remains inoperable. She had used the paper plates before and they are microwave safe.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The consumer is concerned that the microwave is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the microwave, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Dishwasher purched August 2001 with no problems until February 13th, 2013 when it caught fire.

Caller's wife started dishwasher and went to other room then approximately ten minutes later caller's husband heard a popping, sizzling sound.

He got up, walked to kitchen and saw flames coming from handle portion of dishwasher, he grabbed his fire extinguisher and sprayed to extinguish and walked to the sink but then saw that the handle was on fire again with flames shooting down then around to the top of the dishwasher enflaming the entire top.  He used the fire extinguisher to put the fire out.

Caller has ordered a new dishwasher but due to the fire hazard, he is asking reimbursement at manufacturer expense.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the fire was successfully extinguished.

incident_description:
The consumer says she turned the dishwasher on.  Twenty minutes into the cycle she smelled smoke.  Her daughter started screaming.  Half of the house was filled with white smoke and acrid electrical burning smell.  

She smelled the presence of burning plastic.  She went to the dishwasher and saw the control panel was not lit, she did not open it.  

She says the unit burned itself out.  She opened the unit and saw it had 3" of water in the bottom.  She contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not on recall and their is nothing that they can do.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no reported injuries or deaths, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but do happen occasionally.

incident_description:
Consumer woke to the smell of smoke, consumer discovered it was the dishwasher emitting smoke. The dishwasher was programmed to begin regular cycle after the consumer went to bed. The consumer attempted to shut the dishwasher by opening the door but had to unplug the dishwasher. 

The consumer removed the panel and saw it was charred and completely burned. The dishwasher has not been plugged or used since. 

There were no other damages beyond the control panel.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and charring of the dishwasher panel, but no injuries or further damages occurred.

incident_description:
7/31/12/ - Initial Purchase of Hamilton Beach Ensemble 12-cup coffee maker (product ID 43254R) - online. Programmed/used once monthly for early meetings.

12/3/12 - had noticed slight burning smell in break room week before and realized this day that hot plate had come on without ever turning on the machine. Carafe extremely hot, and machine would not turn off without unplugging. Spoke with HB - replacement to be sent under warranty for cost of shipping.

12/20/12 - received replacement. Within 1 month, noticed auto shut-off feature not working - light shuts off, but hot plate remains on and won't shut off without unplugging. After this, kept unplugged, though we bought this product for the timer feature and it would need it to be plugged in to use this. Did not bother returning, as same problem as last time and didn't want to pay shipping yet again.

2/19/13 - Opened cover to place filter. Took out filter basket to clean (did not touch the front of the machine) and the machine immediately got very hot and began steaming (must have had water remaining in the system). Coffee maker was not turned on. I hurried to fill the water and place filter and coffee while steam coming out. Made entire pot of coffee without ever turning on the machine. Emailed HB again, with product info (43254R, A4221D). 

Seems to be a hazard to have a coffee maker that comes on and gets very hot when not in use. Now, looking at reviews online, I'm not the only one this has happened to.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned multiple times, posing a burn hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that he has been experiencing problems with the microwave for approximately 3 days.  The unit intermittently comes on by itself and sets to a min then goes back off.  The microwave has been unplugged to prevent this incident from re-occurring.  This problems had occurred at least 6 times in the past days.  

The caller has attempted to contact the manufacturer but the line was busy, he will try again.  He is concerned that this microwave is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a potential hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet. The issue has happened multiple times, indicating it is likely to recur.

incident_description:
GE Spacemaker II: Model #JEM25WY 001; Serial # HT 902307 B.
The unit will frequently beep and turn on by itself. To prevent the unit from inadvertently turning on, the door has been left open. Numerous codes will be displayed during the aforementioned. On occasion the unit will lock the keypad. After an undetermined period of time, the unit will resume a series of beeps and one may manually depress the 'clear' button to return to the 'time' indication. Unless the unit starts the unwanted beeping, or the keypad is locked, the unit can be used. The unit is presently unplugged and in storage.
justification: The unit exhibits malfunctioning behavior but no injury or harm is reported, fitting severity level 2. The issue occurs frequently, as indicated by the high occurrence likelihood.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while his dishwasher in use about 10 mins into the washing cycle, he smelled smoke.  He discovered that there were flames and smoke emitting from the side of the door.  He opened the door but the dishwasher continued to operate, he noticed that there were flames in the vent of the door.  He had to use the circuit breaker to switch off power from the unit. 

The caller used a wet dish rag to to contain the flames.  There were no prior incident or services with this dishwasher.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The compressor Relay on my Whirlpool Side by Side refrigerator caught on fire. Luckily my husband was home and we were able to unplug the appliance and no one was hurt.
justification: The compressor relay caught fire, but no one was injured and the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
(02/10/2013) The consumer stated that the dishwasher had been running for about a half hour. He noticed something burning. He stopped the dishwasher and opened it. Then he closed it back. When he pushed the start button ,flames and smoke came for the control panel area. The consumer opened the dishwasher and pulled the plug. The dishwasher was damaged at the control panel. The kitchen area was filled with smoke. He did not have to call the fire department.


The consumer stated that he went on line to Kitchenaide fires.com and saw reviews about fires with the product.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, causing damage but no injuries or need for emergency services.

incident_description:
(09/17/2012) The consumer stated that she was standing in the kitchen in front of the refrigerator. She heard a noise. She looked over to the range and saw that the glass on the door and broken and was fallen to the floor. The stove had not been on. The consumer stated that the oven had been used before. 


(10/18/2012) The consumer contacted Whirlpool by letter. She stated that she explained the situation to them. She was told that their only obligation was to replace the glass, which they did.
justification: The glass on the oven door broke without causing injury, and the issue was resolved by replacing the glass.

incident_description: We had used the waffle maker many times--maybe had made about 20 waffles. This time, we heard a pop, and a chocolate chip shot out of the middle of the waffle. A few seconds later, the iron split in 2, with the waffle flying out completely, and the hot iron landing on the counter. Bits of hard plastic flew around the kitchen. Nobody was hurt, thankfully, but I think it was just due to our location when the appliance popped.
justification: The waffle maker malfunctioned, causing hot iron and plastic to scatter, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while using the dishwasher for approximately 20 mins, he smelled smoke.  He discovered that smoke was emitting from the top of the dishwasher and he was unable to power it off.  The circuit breaker was used to switch off the unit.  The drying racks and the blade at the bottom of the dishwasher melted.

The consumer stated that he feels that he experiencing similar problems of Release #12-244.  Hazard: An electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element can pose a fire hazard.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.
justification: Smoke emission and melting parts indicate a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer made dinner and used the dish to bake a potato casserole. The dish was placed on the back burner of the range. The consumer's (21 year old) niece went to warm up a baby bottle using the stove and accidentally turned on the burner where the baking dish was. She immediately turned off the burner and tried to move the dish off the range. However the glass dish exploded as she sat the dish down. 

The consumer and her family cleaned up the glass shards throughout the kitchen. 
There were no damages but the consumer did cut her thumb on her left hand cleaning up the glass. The consumer ran her thumb under cold water, and ointment then bandaged it up.  


The consumer emailed the manufacturer last night but she has not spoken with anyone as of yet.
justification: The consumer sustained a minor injury (cut thumb) while cleaning up glass shards from the exploded dish, which fits severity level 3.

incident_description:
THE STOP TOUCH BUTTON ON THE PANEL OF THIS KITCHEN AID 30' GAS RANGE MODEL KGRA806PSS01 HAS STOPPED WORKING. ONCE THE OVEN IS TURNED ON IT WILL RAMAIN ON SINCE THE STOP BUTTON WILL NOT WORK... UNLESS I  SHUT THE MAINS (KITCHEN) OFF.
I THINK THIS IS A SAFETY HAZARD AS THE OVEN WILL NOT TURN OFF BECUASE OF THE FAULTY MEMBRANE SWITCH THE KITCHEN AID HAS USED IN THEIR PRODUCT.
I DID A RESEARCH ON THIS AND FOUND OUT THIS IS A WIDELY KNOWN PROBLEM WITH THE KITCHEN AID GAS RANGE THAT HAS TOUCH CONTROL PANEL AND YET THERE HAS'NT BEEN ANY RECALLS FROM THE COMPANY.
I AM NOT USING MY OVEN ANYMORE.
justification: The faulty stop button poses a safety hazard as the oven cannot be turned off normally, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
(12/29/2012) The consumer stated that she was asleep. She woke up to go to the bathroom. She realized that there was a horrible smell in the house. She came downstairs to investigate. There was smoke in the house. She heard a sound coming from the refrigerator but didn't think anything about it. She also checked in the basement. She came back upstairs and heard the sound coming from the refrigerator.  It was a zzzzt sound.  She went to the basement and shut off electrical service to the refrigerator at the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that the refrigerator was removed to the garage. The consumer stated that the smell is still in the house. 

(12/31/2012) The consumer called Whirlpool. A service technician was scheduled to come out on 1/4. The company was called A & E. The technician found that the relay was bad and that caused the relay wiring and the compressor to melt. The technician advised the manufacturer of the problem. The consumer was offered $250 if she gave them the refrigerator. She was also offered 50% off of the purchase of a new refrigerator. The consumer declined to purchase a new Whirlpool refrigerator.

The consumer stated that she did a search on the web site and found several articles that mirrored the same incident that she experienced
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator causing smoke and a bad smell, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: while I was cooking on stove top with heat on low burner went onto high and I could not lower or turn off burner, needed to turn off breaker, I never received any recall info from LG after calling them they told me that a recall was issued for range has not been fixed yet should be on 2/26/13
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue is linked to a known recall, suggesting a higher likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My Kenmore Flat top stove was recalled model # 790.99019100. Repair was completed. Now oven stays on after all controls shut off. Repair service diagnosed as another control unit in stove. Now have to turn off circuit breaker after every use for fear of fire. Repair service quoted $400 to repair. Have not repaired.
justification: The stove's control unit malfunction poses a fire risk, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
On 24 Feb 13, I turned my oven on 400 degrees to preheat for a pizza.  Five minutes later, I heard loud noises coming from the oven.  When I walked to the kitchen, I saw spaks and flames in the oven and turned it off.  When I opened the oven, I found that the heating element had broke in half and melted metal (white) was located under the element.  Model 79096014404, S/N: vf54628138.

This appears to be a common issue, reference http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/kenmore-oven-c14186.html?page=10. I would hate to see someone lose their life, home, or pets due to a known issue that nobody will do anything about.  There is no doubt in my mind if I would have walked away for ten minutes this would have resulted in my home going up in flames.
justification: The incident involved sparks and flames in the oven, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high given the reference to it being a common issue.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his electric smooth top range continuously turns on by itself. The consumer stated that although the knob was on the off position, the heating element of his oven comes on by itself. He stated that he has to turn the knob once and bring it back to the off position and it would turn off the heating element. The consumer stated that he had not experienced any problems with the burners and that only the oven turns on by itself. 

The consumer stated that he believes that this poses a fire hazard because at any time it could turn on by itself and cause a fire in his home. 

The consumer stated that no one has been injured and there were no damages to his home. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that it was not included on a recall. The consumer stated that every time he contacts the manufacturer they disconnect the call. 

The consumer stated that he believes this product should be investigated do to the fire and burn hazard that it poses to the consumers.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that could pose a fire hazard, but no injuries or damages have occurred yet.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the microwave came on by itself and would not stop she had to unplug it.   The microwave has been unplugged since the incident. There have been no prior services or incident with this unit.

(1/21/13)The retailer was contacted and she was advised that someone would be sent out to look at the unit 1/22/13.  A service rep came out and informed her that there was nothing wrong with the microwave.  She contacted them again and was told that someone would be sent out 1/6/13. After reading March Consumer reports 2013...

The caller feels that this microwave is unsafe should be reported.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, and the issue was addressed by unplugging the unit.

incident_description:
We had a spontaneas fire in our electronic oven contro l(EOC) at 4:0 pm on 1-8-13.My wife put some food into the oven using the touchpad button 'Warm & Hold", then pressed the "Start" touchpad  button as she has done over the 8 yrs  2 mos we owned the range (It was bought new).About 20 mins later we heard a loud pop and crackling  noises emanating from the kitchen. We both entered the kitchen from the living room to find 4ÃÂ-5" flames and black soot coming from the back of the stove panel. I pulled the range away from the kitchen wall as my wife pulled the electric cord from its receptacle simultaneously. Upon inspecting the back of the range it appears the malfunction started the fire in the vicinity of the "Start" button.
No injuries were incurred or damage to the kitchen wall except for black soot which cleaned up. I believe this can be attributed to our quick response upon hearing the strange noises in the kitchen. I shudder to think if we were in another part of the house out of hearing range. The 40 amp dedicated range circuit trip switch on the main circuit panel did not trip off. This raises the the question in my mind is there no device, fuse or otherwise to prevent this kind of occurrence to appliances with touchpads especially high voltage/amp devices like cooking ranges?

PRODUCT: Kenmore electric kitchen range (30") stand alone Model No 790.9661
justification: The incident involved a fire with no injuries or significant damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting safety issue with microwave   After use caller cannot turn microwave off because it continues running until caller unplugs it.

She purchased the unit sometime around 2008 or 2009 and had no problems until these incidents began around June or July 2011.

Microwave continues running even when the door is open.

Caller is reporting as a severe safety hazard and for her it also poses a fall hazard because she can only reach the plug while standing on a chair.

Her husband cannot unplug for her because he is disabled.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

No injuries have been reported
justification: The microwave malfunction poses a safety hazard and fall risk, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description:
Caller and his wife purchased a microwave in May 2010 and had no problems with it until around January 17th, 2013 when he got up one around 10:00 in the evening, walked into the kitchen and the microwave was running.
His wife was still in bed and he was the first in the kitchen.
He tried to turn the microwave off and he could not until he opened the door then unplugged it.
Microwave display was scrolling the message, "Short in keypad may need service".

This happened again when he plugged it back in to check whether initial incident was a fluke

There have been no injuries.

Caller contacted the manufacturer around January 20th, 2013, was placed on hold then came back to offer 50% of repair costs after the caller paid $90 for her to send tech out then the 50% of the repair.
He and his wife went shopping and purchased a replacement microwave from a different manufacturer.

He is asking for reimbursement of his monies spent for the new microwave he had to purchase due to faulty microwave being reported having such an issue of fire danger and it being less than three years old.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but there were no injuries, only an incident requiring replacement.

incident_description:
Caller states that her dishwasher was new in her home when she purchased it in 2006, that it has only been used eight times in the twelve plus years she has lived there because it smoked from the very first time she used it in 2006.

She contacted the manufacturer  in March 2006, service tech came out and replaced the timer.

She noticed slight smoke just afterward but continued using it thinking it was alright but the smoke became increasingly thicker.

She contacted the manufacturer the second time August 26th, 2006 and they again sent a tech to her home then replaced the timer.

She tried one or two times again to use the dishwasher, called the manufacturer again but was informed that she would be charged.

She stopped using the dishwasher then and never contacted them again until August 2012 when her model came up on a recall.

She contacted the manufacturer who advised her that her model beginning is shown on the release but not her serial number

then advised her to contact the CPSC Hotline.

There have been no injuries
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Recently had new construction at a shore residence with new kitchen appliances purchased from Gerhards in Philadelphia.

On Saturday, February 23, we tried to use the Frigidaire range for the FIRST time.
Following the instructions from the associated manual for the range.....I preheated the oven to 400 degrees and opened window to allow any smoke from the new appliance to escape.

As the oven was warming - never reached 400 degrees - we heard a lot "POP" and saw that the glass in the oven door shattered - blown out!  The shattered glass was  in the door, and in the oven, and some glass pellets fell out the door.

Luckily nobody in my family was injured.  But now I have a brand new appliance that I am fearful of using. Good god.  This is definitely a manufacturing defect and needs to be recalled!

incident_description:
Frigidaire Range control panel caught FIRE after turning oven on

Frigidaire model number PLEFM399DCB
Serial number VF50550396

At approximately 11:30am on Saturday 2/23/2013, when turning the oven on, the control panel started making loud popping noises with sparks, then the control panel caught on FIRE. Smoke was coming out the back vents, and we could see flames thru the control panel window. The flames continued and would not go out. I had to pull the unit away from the wall and use a fire extinguisher aimed into the back vents behind the control panel. This finally extinguished the fire. There was minor damage on the wall (just soot), but the fire extinguisher contents when everywhere in the kitchen, ruining an expensive coffee maker.

A service person from the local appliance store came over after I had discussions with Frigidaire. They found that a ribbon cable on the electronic range control (ERC) unit to the front panel overlay had ignited, caught fire, and melted. The part number for the ERC is 316418704, and the overlay part number is 316419700, according to the service technician.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

The only way to get it turned off was to flip the circuit breaker on the electrical panel downstairs.  I took the unit apart tonight and found the circuit board beneath the touch pad control to be badly burnt .  Several of the electrical connector plugs to this board were also melted.  - repeatedly lock and unlock the touchpad
 - display messages requesting various cooking requirements such as cooking time, power level, recipe number, number of items, weight of items, etc.  

At one point the microwave restarted and heated the food and cooking dish enough to catch the food on fire and melt the dish.  For safety reasons we keep the circuit breaker off when the oven is not in use and under constant supervision.  The microwave is a fire hazard.

The microwave is the top part a two-oven combination oven.  The bottom oven is a conventional oven that operates normally when the circuit breaker is reset.

The oven combination was purchased from Sears.  The Sears repair service made 8 to 10 visits from June, 2012 to January 2013 and changed every part that controls the cooking, but none of the changes repaired the problem.  Then the Jenn-Air repair service made several visits but could not fix the problem.  

Now a safety representative from Whirlpool Corporation is telling us that the microwave is designed to work the way that it does.

The problems with the microwave oven have been occurring from April 2012 to the present.  Repairs on the oven have been ongoing since June 2012.

Once power was removed from the range, I opened the door to reduce the temperature in the oven and found the inside of the empty oven to be smoking heavily and well beyond the stated limit 550 *F. Purchase a Kitchen Aid gas cooktop, model number KFGS366VSS02.  It was a brand new cooktop from a box that had appeared to have not been opened previously.  It is still under warranty.  it was installed by a licensed contractor and was in use for about 2 months prior to the incident.  The gas source is natural gas provided by a public utility.

I put a pot of water on the back right burner.  I turned the burner on and within seconds, a loud pop followed by flames shooting up from the two left burners occurred.  The pressure wave was enough force to lift the left burner grill up about 12 inches, lift all the burner covers from every burner, move the center and right burner grills back one inch towards the back wall, and blow every stove knob off.  I was standing facing the stove within 12 inches of the detonation and flash fire.  I had to replace a knob to turn off the burner under the boiling water pot.  I then went into the cabinet under the cooktop and turned off the gas shutoff valve.  There was no odor of leaking gas prior to the incident.  The items in the cabinet below the cooktop, where the cooktop pressure regulator is located, were in disturbed and the cabinet doors did not move.  I have pictures of how the cooktop looked immediately after the event.

The contractor who installed the cooktop came immediately afterwards to ensure the cooktop was in a safe disposition.  The contractor found that the pressure regulator gasket, that is part of the cooktop, was leaking.  Note that this pressure regulator is outside the stainless steel box the cooktop burners sit in.  There is a seal where the pressure regulator outlet piping enters the stainless steel box that should prevent gas from entering the stainless steel box where the burner orifices are contained.  This was still intact.

I contacted Kitchen Aid who then sent out a repair person.  The repair person confirmed the seal in the pressure regulator was leaking.  When the cooktop cover was removed, the person found two screws that are suppose to secure the left front burner orifice in the bottom of the stainless steel box and the screws were stripped.  The repair person felt that the leak appeared to originate from within the stainless steel box.  Since the repair person felt there was no way to leak check everything that is contained within the stainless steel box and guarantee the safety of the cooktop, Kitchen Aid was contacted to authorize a replacement in kind.  Kitchen Aid approved the replacement.  I am awaiting the replacement installation within the next 2 weeks.

I am concerned the incident will occur again with the brand new cooktop.  When I do a web search, I found several similar incidents involving Kitchen Aid cooktops.  I am very fortunate that I am not dead or severely hurt from the explosion and flash fire incident.  Please investigate this.

Microwave turns itself on

incident_description:
On Sunday, February 10, 2013 at about 10:00a.m., I took hold of my oven door handle to open it when the entire exterior front of the door exploded out at and on me and the shards/pieces flew across the kitchen. The oven was NOT turned on and NEITHER was the stove top, it had not been on since the previous evening. I was wearing jeans so other than my knees stinging from the impact, I did not suffer any injuries. I was very startled and it took my husband and I repeated sweepings, vacuumings and washings to get all the tiny shards of glass off the floor. Although I was lucky not to be injured, the potential for serious injury was enormous. If I had been bending down to look through the glass, the explosion would have caught me in the face and throat. Worse, yet, if one of my 4 small grandchildren had been in the kitchen, the explosion could have very well been deadly to them. Since it was Sunday, the Maytag Customer Service Department was not open so I found a site online where I completed two different reports to Maytag. The next day, February 11th., a Maytag representative called me regarding my reports and I went through the details with her. The representative expressed her sympathy for my experience but said there was nothing else that Maytag could offer me regarding the matter. I asked to speak to someone of a higher authority so she said that she would transfer me to a supervisor. After several minutes of being put on hold and the representative coming back online to tell me repeatedly that she was having difficulty transferring me to a supervisor, she offered to transfer me to their Safety Division and I asked that she do so. Well, that was an exercise in futility and sarcasm. I again went through every detail of the exploding oven door event. The safety rep reminded me that my range was over 7 years old and no longer had a warranty. What the rep offered me was a part replacement, however, I would have to pay for their designated, authorized repair man's trip fee, first for his initial visit to assess the damage, and for his second visit to replace the part as well as the cost of labor. When I told him that his offer was not acceptable, the rep repeatedly told me, "Hey, I thought I was being helpful!" I then asked him if he would listen to what I had to say, and I said that my main concern was that the exploding oven door was a major safety concern and had the potential of seriously injuring or killing someone. He interrupted me and said, "But No One did get hurt!" I further said that I wanted to know why this had happened, what would cause an oven door to explode, especially when the stove and oven were cooled and had not been used for a day (not that it should have ever happened even if they were on,) the rep did not even respond to this question. I also told him that we no longer felt it was safe to use the range and we expected Maytag to reimburse us for the purchase of a new range. I told him that this was an issue of quality and safety, not an issue of the stove's age; this should never have happened no matter how old the stove, and 7 years is certainly not "old." I also told the rep that I was not asking be to reimbursed for any medical expenses, nor was I asking for punitive damages, I wanted only to be reimbursed for the cost of new range. I asked if there was someone else I could appeal my request to and he said "No." The rep then told me he would offer me this "one time only, good for only 30 days, 20% coupon" to use towards the purchase of another one of their ranges. I told him this was not acceptable and he again reminded me of how helpful he thought he was being to me. I concluded the telephone call.   
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an exploding oven door causing no injuries but had potential for serious harm, and such events are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description:
I had cooked dinner and was about ready to sit down and eat when I heard a loud pop as my oven door glass shattered into a million pieces. My child was about two feet away from the stove when it shattered and luckily didn't get hurt. The stove was off and was cooling off for at least 5 minutes before it shattered. They have been terrible to work with.
justification: The oven glass shattered unexpectedly but no one was injured, though the child was nearby. The incident suggests a manufacturing fault, but such failures are rare.

incident_description: I was using the blender for the first time. I put it together as shown in the quick start guide. After blending my smoothie I tried to pour some of it through the small flip top lid but it was too thick so I had to remove it. the blade tower seemed to snap into place when I placed it in the unit and I thought it secured. As I poured some of the smoothie into a cup to check the consistency the blade tower came out slicing my thumb. When I contacted the company I was told that I should reach into the blender and whatever is in the blender to remove the blade tower before pouring anything. This makes no sense since the blades are covered by in this case a thick, viscous and opaque material ie... fruit smoothie. I could not see the location of the blades in the unit nor would I stick my hands in and grab them if I could. This product is inherently unsafe and the company should know that.
justification: The incident resulted in a thumb injury due to the blade tower coming out unexpectedly, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the described design flaw and user instructions that increase the risk.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidare (Electrolux) Professional series electric range, Model/PLEF398CCB, SN/VF32450983 that I purchased new on 7/26/2003 from Appliance Direct, Melbourne, Florida installed in my kitchen. At the time of purchase I filled out & mailed the product registration form which was supposed to enable me to receive recall information on the product in the unlikely event it was necessary.

On Saturday, Feb 16, 2013, my wife turned on the right front heating element of the glass cooktop to make lunch. We noticed the food was very rapidly cooking, when we moved the pan off the element we noted that the inner heating element (inside section of the expandable element) was operating on full 100% of the time and would not shut down. The control on the stove was in the "off" position for the burner and the display indicated "HE" for a hot element. Moving the knob to various positions had no effect, nor did returning the element control to the "off" position subsequent to this. We turned off the stove at the house circuit breaker panel to avoid a fire. Restoring the power to the stove 2 hours later after cooldown repeated the same results. This appears to be a hard failure. We again pulled power on the stove. 

Internet research reveals a voluntary recall on stoves with my model and serial number range for this exact issue. I will be notifying Frigidare/Electrolux this morning of the issue with the range to obtain my repair. I am MOST CONCERNED that I was NOT NOTIFIED OF THE RECALL BY ELECTROLUX prior to an incident occurring that could have resulted in a kitchen fire, especially since I completed and filled out the product registration card upon taking possession of the unit and installing it in 2003. This was an expensive range and I would expect better attention to notification of their customers of a potentially fatal flaw in this type of product then what was provided by the company.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning heating element that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
On two different occasions, our electric range/stove could have caused a serious incident or fire in our home.  A few years ago, our cook top, the back left burner came on and raised and lowered the heat all on its own with out being turned on.  This high and low of the heat continued to occur a couple times and the range beeped with error codes.  We turned the breaker off to the stove and did not leave on while we were not home.  That situation did not occur again.  We had the repair service come out and do a repair/replacement of a part (i believe) then some time after that we received possible recall letter for the range and I was told our model was not included in the recall.

Now, November 2012, comes the second incident.  While cooking a chicken in the oven on convection mode, after some time had passed, there was a loud bang/pop and flash of light from the kitchen the range was beeping and flashing error codes (I do not recall which codes).  While removing the chicken and my husband trying to pull out the range from the wall we began to smell the odor of melting/electrical smell, basically, the start of an electrical fire, so we turned off the breaker and unplugged the range.  Once my husband could pull out the range and get behind it, it was too hot to touch the back panel.  We have not used the range since and will not, we have figured it is no longer a working range, especially given the lingering smell of burnt electrical that lasted the rest of the evening.
justification: The incidents involved potential fire hazards but no actual injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is moderate given the recurrence.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that she has to open the door to stop the process, The microwave has to be turned off at the breaker. When she flip the breaker back on, the electric will return to the unit. After about a couple of hours the unit will turn on again by itself. 

The consumer stated that this is the second unit that was installed. The same problem was happening with the other unit. The first unit was the same make and model. 

The consumer stated that it was reported to the main tenace department. She requested a difference make and model. She is still waiting for a repone.

incident_description:
Jan.23,2013 1:30pm Ran my Bosch dishwasher, heard a "POP!" sound, ran into the kitchen to see black smoke and flames coming from the front panel of my dishwasher. Also some ash from the flames dropped to the floor and a small fire was on the floor. I grabbed a dishtowel and whacked
the flames out, and continued to do the same on the floor. Flames went out, but the smell was horrific. I was never notified about any recall, and glad I was home when this happened. I am grateful I did not put it on at bedtime, and go to bed!? (Like I usually do) I will never purchase this maker again, and never will I leave any appliances on at nighttime and leave. . . grateful we are all safe and ALIVE to report this. Very angry. . .Why wasn't I notified? My relatives who also have the same brand were never notified either.

She pre-heated the oven to 400 degrees. She placed mushrooms on the sheet and placed the  baking sheets in the oven. The timer was for 10 minutes. He husband came upstairs and told her that something was smoking. She went down stairs and saw smoke in the entire house. The smoke was coming from the oven. She opened the oven and took the pans out. When she took the first pan out, it hit her arm and burnt her left arm. Her husband opened the door to the house and threw the pans outside. There was a toxic smell that bothered her eyes. The consumer stated that she had to open all the windows and door to get the smell out. 

The consumer iced her arm, but it did not require any medical attention.

There was smoking and an electrical smell. The stove continued to smoke for about a minute and a half. The consumer turned on the stove and the oven about thirty minutes later. And nothing happened. Later that evening, her husband turned on the stove  The oven worked and the left side burners work.The burners on the right side did not work. The consumer stated that the she can hear and smell the gas on the right side.

incident_description: On Feb 10 2013, our 3 week old Kenmore model  790.92402 sn VF24234846 range turned the broiler on after a momentary power interruption while we were asleep. We smelled smoke and a heard a beeping and rushed to see what was wrong. The oven door was closed but the broiler had come on and was red hot.The display showed "F13". We pushed the STOP button but nothing happened. We read the instructions book and pushed every button several times to no avail. Finally we shut off the circuit breaker for 5 minutes as directed in the book and reset  it. We reset the clock but the broiler and bake function did not work and showed a "dr" code. The cook top burners did work.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased the Oster 3 cup chopper August 2011;  used it 2-3 times.  I could not line up the index marks;  additional force would have cracked the plastic bowl and/or lid.  Still, the unit ran.

Away from home for most of the next year, I didn't try again until fall 2012.  I re-read the manual. but still could not align the marks.  When I removed the cover for a closer look and accidentally touched a start button,  I was shocked to see the blade start!  Like any food processor, it should NOT run without the cover.  The Oster chopper not only runs without the safety index marks aligned,  it also runs with the cover completely removed!

I wasn't injured, but this product is an accident waiting to happen.  Possibly it's unique to a particular batch from 2011.  Although several consumers reported the same hazard to CPSC,  I found no indication  that any action was taken.  

The product is still readily available, therefore anyone experiencing the same issue is urged to file a report with CPSC.
justification: The incident describes a product safety issue with no injury reported, but potential for harm exists. The likelihood is possible as similar issues were reported by other consumers.

She heard a popping noise and in her investigations she discovered that the middle glass door had shattered. 1/5/12 The retailer was contacted and she was informed that she should contact the manufacturer, however, the number she was given was the agency.

incident_description:
(12/30/2012) The glass door on the oven exploded and blew gas everywhere. The stove was used previously but was shut off around 6p. The incident happened around 11p. The consumer went in the kitchen to check for a dish in the oven. As he pulled on the handle the glass exploded. The glass went everywhere. The entire kitchen floor was covered with black glass. About 11 or 12 shards of glass stuck in his legs below his knees and in his hands. The consumer managed to get all of the bleeding stopped after about 45 minutes to an hour. There was no damage in the kitchen.
He did not require medical attention.

(12/31/2012) The consumer contacted Kenmore. He was told that it would cost him $279 for a repair.
justification: The consumer sustained injuries from glass shards but did not require medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances of the oven glass exploding.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the refrigerator lower bottom drawer (freezer) was opened and closed by her 5 year old child.  During the process of closing the freezer drawer her 14 month old son finger got caught in it and the incident amputated his right index finger tip.  The child was taken to the Yale New Haven hospital in Connecticut where he was admitted for surgery overnight, he was released the following day for follow up.


The refrigerator has a design flaw, there is a support glide (metal charred edge) like a cutter to assist with the mechanism of opening and closing of the drawer.  She stated that the freezer does not operate properly because the seal is not holding the door so this causes the problem to re-occur quite easily.

11/27/11 The manufacturer was contacted and she was referred to their compensation department.

The caller is concerned that this refrigerator has caused serious injury to her child and the manufacturer has not comply.  She feels that this unsafe refrigerator should be taken off the market.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury (amputation of a finger tip) requiring surgery, which falls under severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the reported design flaw and the ease with which the problem re-occurs.

incident_description:
I've been a long-time consumer of Sango dishware products for over 10 years now and have cabinets full of Sango products, but after my experience last night I will not only be empting my cabinets of all Sango products but will also be contacting authorities to see how our products can be recalled - specifically Sango Nova Brown products.
 
This product line is notorious for defects - sometimes arriving in shipping with chips and cracks, and cracking easily in dishwashers.  What I did not know until last night was that the product is a true hazard and should be recalled immediately.  I was using a large Sango Brown mug, which I rarely use - to make a large mug of Jasmine tea.  I boiled water in my tea pot, an when I put the water into the mug it was fine at first.  I had a tea infuser in the cup as well.  About 10 seconds after I picked up the mug and was stirring the tea, the cup audibly split on the side and developed a crack through which hot water spurted out and onto my t-shirt.  I developed serious, painful burns with significant blistering and on my stomach, and am hoping and praying that I don't have scarring as a result.
 
This product line should be recalled immediately as it is a hazard and there is some obvious defect in the manufacturing or design of the product.  The mug that I have that cracked did not completely break apart, but has a very large, visible crack about 1.5 inches to the right of the handle that goes from the top edge of the mug to the bottom of the mug.  If these mugs are not designed for hot water, then there should be a warning on them stating such.
 
I hope you will take this seriously - this is a serious problem that should not happen with any consumer products.
justification: The incident resulted in serious burns with blistering, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The description mentions the product line is notorious for defects, suggesting occurrence is likely (4).

incident_description: While using our oven it overheated and caught fire.  The fire was in the top back of stove in the Electronic control area.  Luckily my wife was in the kitchen and contained it or it would have burnt the house down.  We have had this stove for only 2 to 3 years i think and it has not been mistreated.  I think that this range presents a danger to anyone who owns one.

incident_description:
Frigidaire electric range Model PLEFM399DC had 'stove dead' problems and door-hinge problems early on but which seemed to subside over the last few years; I would, however, find Left Front Burner ON HIGHEST -- very scarey to wake up and find burner ON HIGHEST or come home from being out and find burner ON HIGHEST; also temperature would sometimes increase while cooking to higher temp causing boiling/burning.  I was never contacted by Frigidaire of a problem (have copies of my warrenty registration I sent in) nor was I contacted by appliance store where I purchased range model so I was not aware of a problem -- thought I was losing my mind until range turned itself ON HIGHEST one Sunday and husband/I were not able to turn it off until we shut the breaker.  I then had it repaired and it took weeks (Oct/Nov. 2012) for different parts and ~$450 out of my pocket, I looked up my model number on web and saw there was a problem.  Feb. 2013 while cooking on burner (low for stew) and oven (350 heating pizza), I heard a loud POP and saw dark black smoke coming from behind stove and traveling up wall and smelled a bad electrical smell; I ran to shut the breaker but whatever happened had shut the breaker.  I was petrified of the range.
Both Frigidaire/Appliance Store not compassionate -- said range was 7 yrs. old -- denied fire hazard -- tried to reason with them for ~$450 towards another range.
I have since bought another range -- not Frigidaire; too afraid to deal with the Frigidaire PLEFM399DC -- bad experience was not a squeek but a fire hazard and both were quick to tell me I was being treated wonderfully; neither bothered to tell me of a Recall issue.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We bought a brand new Samsung refrigerator RSG257AARS/XAA in August 2011 as part of a total kitchen remodel.  On 12/16/12 we came home after being out for several hours to a flooded kitchen.  Water was actively pouring from the front door ice dispenser chute, as if a faucet was on.  We immediately turned off the power to the fridge and this stopped the water from pouring out, we also then turned off the water supply.  When we opened the freezer door a wave of water escaped.  Ultimately the water that pouted out in those few hours did incredible damage to our home.  Our insurance spent $12,000  to replace the kitchen floor, the floor in adjacent rooms, the ceiling and 2 walls in the finished basement below the kitchen. This is not including the initial tear out of wet materials and mold abatement work that had to be done.  It is now February and we are still working on the repair work.
There were no signs of anything wrong with the ice maker or water dispenser previous to this.  The unit was no longer under warranty.  A refrigerator repairman sited the ice maker and/or water valve to be the faulty parts, and Allstate took the parts to attempt to recover funds from Samsung to cover the repair costs that they paid to us.  We thought about trying to make a claim on Samsung but didn't know how to approach this.  We had to pay the $1000 deductible as well as pay for the refrigerator repair (replacement of those parts) although now I am terrified to even have this fridge in my home in fear that something like this could happen again.
I read on the Sears website that another customer with this refrigerator had a similar experience.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I was sipping the last bit of water out of my Cool Gear Insulated cup with straw while I was driving when I detected something hard and sharp in my mouth.  I stopped the piece of sharp hard plastic from being swallowed by pushing it against my teeth with my tongue while pulling my car to the side of the road.  I took the piece out of my mouth and found it was a piece of the bottom of the hard plastic straw that is part of the cup.  Over time, the plastic had cracked and broken off unbeknownst to me.  I followed all instructions on not washing the cup/straw in the dishwasher etc or exposing it to extreme hot or cold temps.  I did not wash the cup EVERY time I used it, but would open the top and fill with more water so I was unaware of the breakage at the bottom of the straw.  The cup is less than one year old.  We bought it at a Walmart in Somerset PA last spring (spring of '12) while camping nearby.  If I had swallowed the piece of plastic, it may have gone through my body, but considering the piece was triangular in shape and sharp at each point, passing the piece of plastic would have been highly unlikely and internal bodily damage would have resulted.
justification: The incident involved a sharp plastic piece from a straw that could have caused injury if swallowed, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
On October the 18th 2012 his wife was making a pot roast when a hold was melted through the bottom of the cooker and burned a hole in the countertop.  The cooker never shut off.  It was on roughly 4 hours prior to the incident.   

Had his wife not discovered this it could have caused a serious fire.  he contacted the retailer who said that they were not very concerned.  

He said they were more concerned about getting the product back into their hands.  He contacted the manufacturer's representative and they did not seem very concerned.  

Approximate cost of damage $6,600.00
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is possible given the description of the cooker malfunction.

incident_description: Kenmore Model 71 8965380 (Over Oven) Serial #: 90200945 microwave randomly starts and runs for various times. Often times 'delay' is displayed on the screen as the unit is running. The unit was manufactured in February 1989. It has started doing this about a month ago. It sometimes displays different power settings.
justification: The microwave operates randomly without user input, posing a potential hazard but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: The dishwasher was in use.  We heard a strange grinding sound from the kitchen, but then it stopped, so we didn't go in to check.  Within a minute or two I smelled an electrical-type burning smell.  When I entered the kitchen I noticed the dishwasher had stopped and there was a black char residue on the upper right-hand corner of the unit.  I opened the door and there was no evidence of any further burning inside.  My husband immediately cut off power to the unit.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with visible damage but no injury or further escalation, indicating a minor equipment issue.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Elite Dishwasher Model 665.17463300 - shortly after starting the dishwasher the control panel began emitting smoke and strong fumes, then caught fire. There were no problems, symptoms, or modifications prior to this incident. We manually tripped the circuit breaker to interrupt power and the fire went out on its own. After allowing the panel to cool, we disassembled the panel cover and found that the control circuit board at top right of the door had overheated and melted part of the plastic housing that it was mounted in. The circuit board was blackened and charred but still intact. The label on the plastic housing reads as follows:

Whirlpool P/N 85344963 Rev A

GWDC - 02 DC 4178

3496300070610

FSP

Jabil Circuit

Made in China


In addition there is a barcode that is visible on the circuit board itself and reads as follows:

RH00HW7B

We were fortunate in that we were just about to go upstairs and go to bed, but were still in the kitchen when the incident occurred. Our two young children were already asleep. Needless to say we are very concerned about this incident and will never leave a dishwasher completely unattended going forward. We will be contacting Sears and Whirlpool about this.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and catching fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the issue was isolated and no prior symptoms were reported.
