incident_description:
Consumer was cooking for about 20 mins and the stove was turned off. The consumer noticed the heat coming from the kitchen and saw the right front burner was still lit. Consumer went to lower the temperature and notice the range was off. She attempted to power the stove off, by adjusting some of the control knobs, but it still remained hot. The consumer then unplugged the range but the burner was still too hot. So the consumer had to trip circuit breaker to the range to turn off the range. 

The next day the consumer plugged range back into the outlet and the burner immediately powered on. The consumer unplugged the range and it has been unplugged and untouched since.

Consumer has contacted retailer and was told that they knew the range had problems but because the model not listed in a recall, she would be financially responsible.

(date unknown) Consumer has spoken with manufacturerÃÂs rep. [REDACTED] and was told the same the thing. 

There were no injuries or property damages to report.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove with no injuries or property damage, and similar issues are known to occur with this model.

incident_description:
My wife and myself have accidentally leaned against our new Whirlpool range and the burner quickly ignited to a high flame within several inches of us.  And on Mon, 2/11/13 we had a technician from Abt Appliance in Glenview, IL where we bought this range install a new Microwave Oven above this range.  This technician said he had more that 15 years of experience installing microwave ovens, etc and he too leaned against this range thus setting off one of the front gas burners at high flame.  He too was within inches of getting burned.  

I maintain that this is a poor and dangerous design and at least should have some kind of a "grill" or "guard" preventing these knobs from being accidentally pressed.
justification: The incident describes accidental activation of high flames with no reported injuries, but clear potential for harm.

incident_description:
The Park Forest Fire Department responded to an activated smoke detector that was called in by a neighbor of the townhouse in question. There was no answer at the door with light smoke visible through the door. Entry to the unoccupied unit was then forced. Once inside, the fire officer found  burned chicken inside a gas oven. The burner knobs were all in the off position but the oven burners were lit. The fire department shut off the gas at the incoming line and the stove was relocated to the exterior of the building

The resident came home while the fire department was still on the scene and told the fire officer that, after heating some chicken, he turned off the burners to run an errand. He said that he left the chicken in the oven to stay warm while he was absent. 

There is a potentially dangerous problem with the gas valve to this stove which is less than 1 year old.

Stove Manufacturer: GE  Americana Gas Range
                Model #  AGBS300EP2WW
                Serial #   F2110799P
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas stove that caused light smoke but no injuries or deaths, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the identified dangerous problem with the gas valve.

incident_description: MY Bosch dishwasher caught on fire last night from the control panel.  It was extinguished without much damage to the house. We are lucky we were home or the house would have been a loss.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was extinguished without injury or significant damage, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I got a Sodastream home soda maker for Christmas from my parents. I was using the home soda maker on Monday the 28th of Jan. and I used it with only water and did the 3 buzzs it makes for avg. fizz like the manule says to do. and when i went to take the bottle off that was sent with the home soda maker the top of the machine blew up and the bottle blew down and there was a great force inbetween the machine and the bottle like a bomb. and the sound was like a bomb too. my right hand was holding on to the bottle twisting it off the machine like the manule tells you too do. when the Sodastream blew up. I went to the ER quickly after the explosion. the doc. told me i was burned and had contusion of the hand. I was in a lot of pain still and could not straiten out my right index finger so Friday i went to my regular doctor and she said i was greatly brusied inside of my right hand and burned. i am glad i was not a child it would have killed a child if it had hit them in the face.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and contusions to the hand, requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with proper use.

incident_description: I purchased a gravy boat from Walmart back around Thanksgiving 2012. When I got it home, I hand washed it and allowed it to dry before storing it. We then used it for gravy with our Thanksgiving lunch. When we were done, I put it in the dishwasher to wash with the rest of the dishes. When the dishes were dry, we stored it in a cabinet on top of a stack of saucers. At Christmas, I got it out again to use for gravy, but the bottom of the boat that has not been fired when made had black mold all around it, and the top of the saucer was also covers in black mold in the shape of the boat. We do not have any type of mold issues in our house. I think it is a result of the porcelain not being fired properly. I did not return the product to Walmart because I did not have the receipt.
justification: The incident involved mold growth due to improper firing of the gravy boat, but no injury or health impact was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer started to cook a roast in the slow cooker on the low setting and placed the lid on. Within 5 minutes the glass lid shattered and the handle on the lid flew off. The lid still remained on the cooker, but it was shattered. There is a 3 inch wide hole where the handle once was secured to the lid.  Some of the pieces of glass near the handle also separated from the rest of the glass.

After cleaning the kitchen twice to remove the fragments of glass; the consumer's daughter [redacted] , sustained minor cuts to both hands by untraceable pieces of glass. The cuts on her right wrist and left thumb were rinsed off and bandaged; no medical attention was needed. 
Consumer has only used the slow cooker about 4 times, since receiving it as a gift before the holidays. There were no known cracks or blemishes on the slow cooker. 

On the same day the consumer spoke with mfr ([redacted] operator#[REDACTED]) who stated she could send a replacement lid and it would be referred to the Claims Mgr [redacted].  The consumer did not indicate whether or not he would accept the replacement lid.  He was more interested in speaking with [redacted].  The consumer was told that [redacted] would call him back at a later time.
justification: The consumer's daughter sustained minor cuts that required rinsing and bandaging, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident involved a product failure but is unlikely to recur frequently (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
The caller stated that while using the chopper parts of the blade came through the plastic bowl.  The blade detached itself and was lodged inside the container.  The chopper was only in use for 20 mins while he chopping some olive leaves.  There were no prior incidents.  He stated that he found Release #05-258 on the internet.

The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that the blade would be replaced but the caller stated that it would not solve the problem because the blade had damaged the bowl lid as well.
justification: The blade detached and damaged the bowl lid, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The dishwasher turned itself on over the night and heated uncontrollably, destroying plastic utensils, plates, and inner workings inside the dishwasher.
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I am refiling this report due to the fact that it mysteriously disappeared. 
It was originally filed on 12-13-11

These ice cream scoops ÃÂALLÃÂ need to be recalled.

On Tues, December 13 at 11:25 a.m. my Pampered Chef ice scream scoop exploded in my hand.
I had received a notice of recall and was told not to use this scoop because the end cap was coming loose and the liquid inside was leaking out.  So, I  placed it up on my kitchens plant window to wait for my replacement because, I didnÃÂt want my daughter using it. Today while cleaning my kitchen, I saw it there, and I reached over to grab it to throw it away when it exploded in my hand. The force shot the scoop into my kitchen wall leaving a hole. It felt and sounded like a shot gun going off in my hand and my hand was the barrel of the shot gun.  I honestly didn't think my hand was still there, but it was.... I  really just had a lot of extreme pain and stinging. It sounded like a bomb went off in my house. My ears were ringing for a good 2 hours after the Pampered Chef ice cream scoop exploded.  I was lucky my hand and wall and ears took the most of the force of the explosion. I immediately put ice on my hand. 

 I contacted Pampered Chef immediately and advised them that this product should not even be on the market. The next person may not be as lucky. This could have killed me if it were pointed towards my head. This product will kill a small child,  if all of them are not removed from the houses across America..
Please! Please! Please! Make sure these ice cream scoops are taken off the market. 

Since this happened to me,  I have done research and this has happened to numerous other consumers. This is not just an accident anymore, people need to be aware of how dangerous this product is before somebody dies. Pampered Chef told me that they were not responsible for any injuries because they just sold the product. They then referred me to the manufacturer Zeroll Co.  
I believe that Pampered Chef should be held liable for selling a product in which they knew was dangerous. These types of ice cream scoops have been exploding since 2002, this is the first report I could find. Pampered Chef in my opinion is liable for punitive damages to all that have suffered from their lack of regard to public safety. They knew exactly why they were recalling his product. It was not because the cap was leaking, it was because they were exploding!

Since my report was filed on 12-13-11 there have been at least 5 more people injured.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (pain, stinging, and ringing ears) and potential for more severe harm, with multiple similar incidents reported.

incident_description: My Kenmore microwave starts running on its own.  Sometimes when you shut the door and do not start it  and on occasion if you are not even near it.     This has happened on various dates.  Yhe most recent on Feb. 10, 2013
justification: The microwave runs on its own without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm but potential safety concern.

incident_description:
I purchased a Hamilton Beach microwave, model # P100N30ALS3B (manufacture date March 2012) around summer/autumn of 2012 (I'm not sure exactly what month).  Around 3-4 months ago, while sitting in my living room, I heard the microwave start.  No one else was home - my son was at school and my husband was at work, so I knew no one had been in the kitchen to start the microwave.

I went to investigate, and found the microwave was running.  I opened the microwave door, and as expected, the microwave shut off.  However, when I closed the door, it immediately started up again without me pressing any buttons.  I opened the door again, and once more the microwave shut off.  Yet again, I closed the door, and again it turned back on of its own accord.  I had to unplug the microwave to get it to stop turning itself on.  After plugging the microwave in again, all seemed normal.

This happened again a few days later, and has happened around 12-15 times in total since it first began.  The last time it happened was approximately a week ago, but I have no doubt it wasn't the last time it will happen.  We now have to leave the microwave unplugged at night, and while no one is at home, simply as a precaution because we don't know when the microwave will randomly turn itself on again.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: My GE Profile Microwave starts running on it's own after I finish cooking in it and close the door.
justification: The microwave running on its own is an incident with no injury, and such malfunctions are possible but not frequent.

incident_description: I had used my Progressive Microwave Tea Kettle for years without a problem, but the top caught on fire tonight.  Electrical arcing was visible at the site of the burn.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and a fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I saw a report about the microwaves. I have a Whirpool microwave(over the stove microwave) It turns itself on sometimes. I didn't think much of it at first so I just left it alone. But I never unplugged it. But now since I know what could happen it's unplugged.. It comes on often at least every other day.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported, and it has been unplugged to prevent further incidents.

incident_description:
(10/28/2012) The consumer stated that she was making vegetable soup. She had chopped potatoes, onions, celery and carrots. She was chopping potatoes and onions when she noticed that one of the blades was missing. She looked through the pan of soup to see if she could find the blade. She drained the soup and found the stainless steel blade in the pan. The consumer stated  that she uses the chopper maybe once a month.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the dishwasher in use for approximately 15-20 mins. He heard a loud noise and then his spouse alerted him that the unit had caught fire.  He noticed that the door was flaming red where the control panel is located and there was smoke emitting from the door as well.  The room was engulfed in smoke , he had to use circuit breaker to switch the dishwasher off.

(11/20/12) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that a service rep would be sent out.

The caller stated that he is concerned that this dishwasher could have caused a house fire, if no one had been home.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The incident was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
The reporter stated that the consumers were not using the electric range and the heating element came on its own and would not turn off. The consumer stated that because the heating elements were coming on by themselves they replaced the burner switches.  The first set of replacement switches did not fix the problem so they replaced the switches again and this corrected the problem.  All work was performed by a reputable appliance repair company. 

The reporter stated that on 10/25/2012 they were cooking a pizza in the oven and the heating element broke and flames were inside the oven. The reporter stated that when the consumers saw the flames inside the oven they immediately unplug the electrical supply and used an extinguisher to put out the flames. 

The reporter stated that no one was injured. 

The reporter stated that she researched online and found that her range was posing the same hazard stated on release #09-333. 

The reporter stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.
justification: The incident involved flames inside the oven but no injuries were reported, and the issue was resolved by replacing the burner switches.

incident_description:
(12/19/2012) The consumer stated that she ran the dishwasher on 12/18.  The consumer stated that the dishwasher was not hot earlier in the morning because she opened the door around 7:30 am. The consumer stated that she reclosed the door. The consumer stated that about two hours later when her husband opened the door to remove the utensils, they were burning hot.  The consumer stated that her husband burned two fingers on his right hands. The consumer stated that it did not require medical attention. The consumer stated that she checked on line and saw that the dishwasher was on recall. She stated that her model number was included but her serial number was not.

UPDATE: After taking the dishes uot of the dishwasher, many cups were melted, bowls cracked. We still have them for record if needed.
justification: The husband burned two fingers, which qualifies as an injury, but it did not require medical attention.

incident_description:
Recently ordered Cuisinart model DCC-2800 coffeemaker, serial #20112.
Product appears to have been assembled incorrectly at factory.
Appears to be a DCC-2800 body with a DCC-2900 control panel installed.
Cannot set auto off time for the warming plate.
Warming plate heats up when brew setting is selected.
Don't know if there is an electrical hazard or not.
justification: The product was assembled incorrectly, causing functional issues, but there is no indication of injury or immediate hazard.

incident_description: Range door will not properly close due to door hinge failure, requiring excess temperature to cook and excessively heating the room. Extended product use at abnormally high temperature increases parts failure and risk of burn or fire.
justification: The door hinge failure leads to excessive heating, increasing the risk of burns or fire, which could cause injury.

incident_description:
Caller loaded dishwasher on Christmas Afternoon, started it and was standing in the kitchen talking with her family when they heard an explosion inside the dishwasher.

Flames that measured approximately two feet high began coming out of the control panel then extinguished but were followed by slight black smoke.
The unit continued to run as if it were washing the dishes.

Caller's husband turned off the dishwasher, flipped the breaker  and water supply off to the unit.

After about twenty minutes the callers husband reconnected everything, started the dishwasher but although it was running it still smelled like burned wiring.
They disconnected power, water then unplugged the dishwasher and have ordered a new replacement dishwasher which they would ask for reimbursement or partial reimbursement of from the manufacturer at manufacturer expense.

Callers have not contacted the manufacturer but do intend to contact them.
No injuries are being reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher but no injuries were reported, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
Caller is contacting the CPSC Hotline on behalf of her daughter who was cooking November 21st, 2012 (the day before Thanksgiving) with the oven set at 350 degrees.
Caller's daughter had baked bread at 350 degrees so oven was preheated, she took the bread out and placed one slice of microwave bacon on a piece of foil in a pan in the oven for a few seconds, however when she shut the oven door she noticed that the mode went from bake to broil and door to oven locked.

She tried pushing cancel, tried to open the door multiple times but could see that the control panel was displaying "ERR" for error.
Within a couple of minutes of trying to open the oven door or turn the oven off a fire flashed in the oven with flames engulfing the entire oven forming a ball shaped fire.
She dialed 911 and seven fire engines responded but during the short period of time that the fire began and the fire department arrived the fire had extinguished itself.
Fire responders had to allow the oven to cool down, they brought in a huge commercial fan and some sort of tubing as precautionary measure check for fire in the walls, due to the high level of heat caused by the oven fire.

Neighbors contacted the manufacturer but state that the rep was no assistance at all.

The oven remains inside caller's daughter's home with power not attached.

She tried to use the oven November 27th, 2012 in the evening, heated to 400 degrees with mode set to bake, she placed her food on the sheet plate, shut the door and turned around to prepare other food.
She turned around and saw that the oven was again glowing very brightly, the broil and the bake modes were on but the door had not locked yet.
She ran outside to turn breaker to oven back off and it remains off to this date.

Caller is asking on behalf of her daughter that this model be recalled with replacement offered at manufacturer's expense.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injuries or deaths were reported, only property damage and a safety hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer says that he was at work at the time of the incident.  He said the unit started smoking and popping.  His wife told him that she did not see any flames. There is some scorching inside the dishwasher.  No other damage was done to his home.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him the unit is out of warranty and that he is out of luck.  

The consumer says CPSC should review the web site kitchenaidfire.com.  He says there are many people sitting on a ticking time bomb if they have this product.  

He threw the dishwasher out.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and popping dishwasher with no injuries or flames, and the unit was discarded without further damage.

incident_description:
I purchased a Whirlpool gas range Model #: WFG510S0AS from Lowe's in September 2012. ÃÂ (AccuBakeÃÂ® temperature management system - a built-in sensor monitors oven temperature and controls the cooking elements ÃÂ Custom broil allows you to set your preferred broiling temperature in 5-degree increments)  I noticed that when using the oven it would click off and on often making a loud puff sound. I assumed this was the way this oven operated.  Today I had set the oven to preheat to 350 degrees and walked out of my kitchen into another room. About ten minutes later I could smell a gas odor in my home. I went and checked the stove only to discover that the electronic ignition had not started the oven.  

My concern is that this is very dangerous because if a stove or oven are suppose to have these safety features on them when you purchase them. A consumer do not purchase these items with the expectation of them breaking down in the matter of a few months and little use of the stove/oven. This is very dangerous for people with small children, the elderly, physically challenged individuals, and smokers. The gas fumes escapes very quickly.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to a malfunctioning oven, which poses a significant risk of injury or death from gas inhalation or explosion.

incident_description: On 2/10/13 We used the microwave several times and each time it sparked. We notices later the bottom of the door and frame of the microwave has burn like damage on it.
justification: The microwave sparked and showed burn damage, indicating an incident but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
In using the birch wood Coffee stir sticks I discovered that the sticks are breaking apart in the hot beverage. In drinking my last bit of coffee in my cup I managed to get an inch long shard lodged in my throat. I was able to get the stick out but had I not it would have been a hospital trip for me. My throat is still sore from the stick. 
The product is Burch Wood Coffee Stir Sticks  from STR Supplies Inc.  [REDACTED] 

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injury (shard lodged in throat causing soreness) but no death, and the likelihood is possible given the product's failure in hot beverages.

incident_description:
The consumer used the front right burner for approximately an hour  at 2:00 and powered the burner in the off position.  Around 6:30 pm the oven glass door exploded causing the glass to shatter and pop off from the range. The outer glass was what had exploded.

The pieces in glass range in size from small to large. The consumer estimates using the oven last 10/17/2012  for approximately 15 minutes at 300 degrees.

The range was installed in the home in April of 2006 so the consumer does not know where it was purchased from.

justification: The incident involved the oven glass door exploding, but no injuries were reported, making the severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but have been documented.

incident_description:
LG  MICROWAVE OVEN
MOD. # LCRT1510SV
SER.# 109TAKK42-109
12/5/2011-THE UNIT WAS DEAD & CALLED LG SERVICE.
12/7/2011-REPAIRED & FOUND TO HAVE A BURNED OUT CONTROL PANEL. 
12/12/2011 PICKED UP THE UNIT FROM LOCAL SHOP
8/14/2012- Unit went dead again. I talked w/LG service and the local store that I went to last time said that they now chanrge $75.00 to determine the problem if the unit is an LG. I stated that it was under warranty and they said that is the way it now is with LG Products. I ended up going to Sunnyvale (which is approx/ 30 miles one way) to have it repaired.  The problem turned out to be a burned magnetron.

11/15/2012- Knowing full well that this is beyond the original warranty period, and I don't have an extended warranty, I called LG.  They said to mail a copy of the original sales receipt so they they could see if it will be approved for repair. I did this 2 times and waited to hear from them.

11/27/12- I called and was told to call back tomorrow and talk w. the original person handling the case.

11/29/12-  I got tired of waiting so I called again and was told again that I will hear from someone within 24 hours.

12/4/12- At 2:45 I received a call and they said that they would not repair the unit.  THE UNIT WAS GIVING TROUBLE ABOUT 1 WEEK BEFORE WARRANTY RAN OUT.  The reason I hadn't called before the unit was out of warranty was because I was in the hospital getting my gall bladder removed with some complications. I was home for a few days recovering and my wife had her appendix explode which caused complications in itself, so I was not in a position to deal with the microwave problem. I explained this to their service people.

The problems that I was having with the microwave:
1. Timer stops but the unit keeps running
2. Timer blinks off and on occasionally as it feels like it
3. Timer repeatedly stopped at 22 seconds but the unit kept running
4. Comes on approx. 3-5 seconds after the timer is set and the start button pushed
5. The unit starts and stops by itself without anything touching any of the buttons or being near the machine.

Because of this problem being a perceived fire hazard. or possibly an explosive hazard, we had elected to unplug the unit after each use, which is quite inconvenient.  Also, we have since the beginning of ownership, plugged this unit into an industrial surge and spike protection unit, as we have done with all of our previous units as well, to protect them.  

I will include the paperwork from each repair so that it can be verified if necessary. 

I will never buy or own another LG product as long as I live, and I will pass this info to anyone who will listen, the internet and to the ends of the earth.

Now I understand why the local merchant wanted a $75 up front deposit, because from his demeanor things seemed as if he was having trouble getting his money from LG, but that is just my opinion.  When I called the last time he said at that time it was even more to obtain servce on an LG product, but I didn't ask how much would be required.

I have never been treated so poorly by any company in my lifetime.  People don't usually treat their customers in this fashion, or at least they never used to. It is a shame that a company the size of LG has to be so petty and produce such a dangerous and shotty product.

I don't feel sorry for them because as I learned when I was young "you treat people as you want to be treated."
justification: The microwave exhibited dangerous malfunctions but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: GE Adora over-the-range microwave self starts when the door is closed following use.  Problem is intermittent but increasing in frequency. Microwave was manufactured in Jan 2011 (according to label on the inside) and purchased in March 2011.
justification: The microwave self-starting poses a risk of incident without injury, and the problem is intermittent but increasing in frequency.

incident_description:
While the oven was in use (350 - 450 degrees F), the left rear burner spontaneously turned on and would not turn off until the oven had cooled.  The food (roast chicken and vegetables) in the oven at the time the burner turned on was creating steam which was venting from just beneath the control knob for the left-rear burner.  The area around the knob was noticeably moist from steam; I presume that condensation from the steam was possibly causing a contact closure in the electronic circuitry in the main power board or at the control knob.

I tried rotating the dial to other settings and back to "off", but could not get it to register (on the electronic read-out) that it was off (which was expected to be "HE" for "hot element").  Repeated turning of the dial eventually reduced its maximum temperature, but would not turn it completely off.  It was possible to reduce the heat indication to as low as 1.2, but placing the control knob in the "off" position would set the digital temperature control reading to "HI" and the burner would be heated to full temperature.  The control was adjusted so the indicator displayed its lowest achieved indication (1.2) until it was possible to get the burner off.  After the oven was turned off and cooled for about 30 minutes, it was possible to turn the burner to the "off" position and have the heating element cool down (with the expected digital indication of "HE").  I then was able to move the range and unplug it.  Plugging it in the following day (today), it worked normally, but the range cannot be trusted to not spontaneously turn on again.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven burner that posed a potential hazard but did not result in injury or death. The issue was resolved without harm, though the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the description.

incident_description:
In July, 2010 my Whirlpool Gold microwave/convection oven self started. We were sitting only a few feet away
when it started smoking. It cost us over $500.00 to repair it. We contacted Whirlpool, but they would not accept
responsibility. Now I am hearing on the TV news that Kitchenaid (which are manufactured by Whirlpool) are selfstarting and causing fires.
justification: The microwave self-started and caused smoke, but no injury or death was reported. Similar incidents with Kitchenaid appliances suggest a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My Pampered Chef ice cream scoop was sitting in my dish drainer after being hand washed two days previously and literally exploded.  I was standing using the other side of my double sink when I heard an extremely loud noise and felt a very sharp pain in my left breast.  I lost my hearing for a short period of time because of how loud it was and actually thought I had been shot through my kitchen window.  I held my left breast because of the severe pain and kept looking for blood on my hand and sweater that I was wearing but never found any.  After further investigation, my 6 year old grandson found a small metal disk on the floor around where I had been standing.  This is when I discovered that the Pampered Chef ice cream scoop had exploded.  It had not been in any water and nobody had been using it - I had used it 2 days prior to it exploding at my husband's birthday party and it had been hand washed as the directions had clearing stated.  I had not put it away in the drawer yet and it was just sitting in the dish drainer.  Since then I have had to have a mammogram, two Dr.'s visits and possible ultrasound and more Dr.'s visits because of the damage it caused to my breast (it broke my skin and severe bruising and hematomas through my bra and the sweather I was wearing).  When I contacted Pampered Chef they knew exactly when I had purchased the ice cream scoop (August 2010), who had held the party and who the consultant was and informed me that this is when defective scoops were sold.  WOW!  I couldn't even remember exactly when I had purchased it!  And they didn't even send out notices to let people know this could happen!  When my car has a recall they send out notices to get it fixed but they couldn't send a letter to inform me of a possible explosion and bodily harm of this ice cream scoop!  My Dr. told me if this would have hit my grandson in the face (he stands about the right height that it would have hit him in the face had he been standing at my kitchen sink) it very well could have killed him with the damage that it did to my breast.  I had to wait 5 weeks to be able to get a mammogram because my breast was damaged so badly that I could not stand to have it done until then.  I'm sure I will heal and be fine but this is ridiculous that they were so negligent in informing consumers of this hazardous product!  Shame on you Pampered Chef!  I hope nobody else gets injured from this defective product and that Pampered Chef stand up and sends out notices to those who bought this product in July, August, and September of 2010!!!!
justification: The incident caused severe pain, hearing loss, and required medical attention, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer tested an electrical hand mixer on 12/13/12.  She stated that the mixer sparked when she plugged it in the wall outlet.  The consumer was not mixing any hand ingredients at that time.  

The consumer tripped the GIV outlet and reset the circuit breaker.  She stated that she then tried the mixer again and it sparked.  She reinserted the mixing blades believing that it would help, but the breaker tripped again.  The consumer discontinued use of the mixer at that point.

The consumer plans to contact the retailer (Target) at a later time.

No injuries or property damage.
justification: The incident involved a sparking mixer but resulted in no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
The caller stated that he passed by the range and his body brushed against the front burner which caused it to slightly turn on without his knowledge.  After a few seconds he started smelling gas and realized that the range was on.  

The caller is concerned that this gas range can ignite causing an explosion while the gas is released in the air.

The manufacturer was contacted but he was unable to speak to a live person.

UPDATE: Gas is coming out of the burner at this point. If you do not get to the igniter and lite the burner you will have natural gas. Gas going into your kitchen until it ignites?
justification: Gas leakage poses a significant risk of explosion or fire, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual harm has occurred yet.

incident_description:
On Saturday, December 8th, 2012 the caller was using her stick blender when she began to smell a burning odor and saw a small amount of smoke, she stopped the unit and turned it off.

After the unit cooled off, she removed the attachment and saw that the coupling that connects the attachment and the motor had melted and stripped itself of all threading.

Blender is no longer usable without being a fire hazard and this is why she is reporting.

She contacted the manufacturer Tuesday, December 11, 2012 and was advised by a representative and a supervisor who advised that there is nothing that can be done because it isn't on warranty and they have no known issues with it.

She did not obtain names.



There have been no injuries
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning blender causing smoke and melting, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(11/07/2012) The consumer stated that she had used the bake ware to cook a casserole. The oven was set for 375 degrees. The consumer stated that the casserole was in the oven for about 30 minutes. She removed it from the oven and placed the dish on a wooden trivet. The dish had been sitting on the counter for about twenty to twenty-five minutes when it exploded  and scattered glass throughout the kitchen. 

The consumer stated that she uses the dish at least once or twice a month. 

The consumer stated that she read reviews where the same set had exploded.


The consumer did not know the name of the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I purchased a 5 cup coffee maker, made  by General Electric, at Walmart about 2 years ago. In less than a year the cover for the pot broke off.  I called GE and then returned the coffee maker to Walmart, where it was replaced. That was in February, 2012. On Feb. 5, 2013 I made a pot of coffee, and when I went to pick up the pot, the one piece handle and lid broke off, leaving several small pieces of plastic and the screw which tore loose from the metal band around the pot. The pot fell forward, and I was scalded from my ribs down to about the middle of my leg.  I was wearing only underwear because I had planned to drink the coffee while I got dressed. I immediately got in a cool shower (painful burn) and when I could stand to touch the area  used [REDACTED] cream.
I am writing because two of these pots broke in a very similar way. With the first one, the lid broke off when the plastic didn't hold. With the second one, the entire plastic mechanism broke as soon as I lifted the pot of scalding coffee. I think these pots should be tested for inferior quality plastic, which can result in serious damage.
When I called GE at [REDACTED] and told the robot the model number printed on the front of the booklet, it insisted there is no such number, but obviously there is. The model # is 898677.Below that is UPC605388986771.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful burn injury requiring immediate treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of similar failures suggests the occurrence likelihood is likely (4).

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Refrigirator Model 795.77563600
The refrigirator *suddently* generarting excessive heat from the light bulb... it melt the housing and burn when
touch, please see attached pictures of the defected product. when called for services, they refused to accept this is
product defect and and for servcies fee and charge for labor to repair it.
If i did not stop to using this frig, it may most likely burn and could cause fire hazzard, while checking on [REDACTED], it
seems many people have similar problem, and i hope you can issue a recall for

UPDATE: The service company did repair this free of charge, but this is still a defective product.

incident_description:
Caller purchased smooth top electric range in late 2002 and had no problems with it until around Thanksgiving 2007 when she was cooking and the range went automatically from bake to cleaning.
She tried to turn the range off or have it revert to the bake mode again but she had to trip the breaker to turn it off.
She tripped the breaker back on to finish cooking but had to wait a few days before she could get back to normal function for the range because previous tries had still placed it back into the cleaning mode.
Each time it switched modes while she was cooking it would flash an F1 display and she could not clear the display so she had to trip the breaker.
After a few days the range seemed to perform normally for intervals of one to three months during episodes.
The digital board was replaced in December 1st, 2011 with the belief that this would correct the problems with the random switch of power and mode.

November 16th, 2012 caller was cooking with oven set at 350 degrees when the oven automatically went from bake mode to broil mode.
Caller again tried to turn the range off but had to trip the breaker to disconnect power before the range would turn off.
She again tried to turn the power back on by tripping the breaker again, left it off for a week, tried using it again by broiling bread and it worked fine for approximately ten minutes then she couldn't go to the bake mode or turn the range off.
She disconnected the breaker again then purchased another range from a different manufacturer.

She is asking to be reimbursed at manufacturer expense for $649.00 price of new range.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
There were no injuries reported
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range requiring repeated breaker trips, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: LG Refrigerator Model LFC21760ST. Noticed an electrical smell in the refrigerator and touched the plastic digital control unit that contains the lights. did some troubleshooting and found out the lights do not turn off when the doors are shut.  My husband looked a little closer and saw that the plastic is melting.  I went on to the LG sight and all they say about lights not turning off when the doors are closed is to call for a service repair. My husband unplugged the refrigerator in fears of a possible fire.  I see that others have had the same problem with this. Why isn't LG and the government safety doing anything to notify and fix this problem. Are they waiting for the appliance to catch on fire and someone is injured or dies?
justification: The incident involves melting plastic and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Elite gas range purchased in 2009 has control knobs positioned so close to oven ventilation on front, that when oven is used for less than one half hour, they got too hot to touch.  This Thanksgiving we had an incident in which a grandchild burned himself ( no treatment necessary) after touching a knob.  His father tried to touch the knob, and it was too hot to touch.  When the oven is on for an extended cooking period, the stove knobs can only be touched by using oven gloves/pads.

Two service technicians checked the stove, and both agreed, and documented that there appears to be a design flaw.  The stove was working properly.  New knobs were ordered, but same results.

Sears has authorized replacement of range with a dollar amount allowance.
justification: A grandchild burned himself but no treatment was necessary, indicating an injury without severe consequences.

incident_description: Glass front on a 2 year old Kenmore wall oven exploded leaving glass all over the kitchen. The oven had not been used in 2 days.
justification: The oven glass exploded but there was no mention of injury, making it an incident without injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it's not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
i started dishwasher at 5:30 pm. it is a 90 min. cycle so should have been finished around 8 pm. i did not check on it before going to bed as i have never had a problem with it and just completely forgot i had turned it on. the next morning i noticed that my countertop was very warm as if the dishwasher was in the drying stage. i opened the door and sure enough the heating element was still going from the night before. the dishes were bone dry and i almost burned my hand getting the silverware out. there is no way to turn of the heat element that i know of at this point so i unplugged the appliance and waited a few hours for everything to cool off. when i plugged it back in, to see if i could just bypass the heated dry and still use the wash cycle, the heat element was already hot enough to burn me and i hadn't touched a thing on the controls. i again unplugged it and am not able to use it. i was lucky i did not have a fire overnight with the heat on for that amount of time and all the plastic cups and plates that were in the load. 
the dishwasher was a Maytag Quiet Series 400 bought in 2007
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that could have caused a fire but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:

The property where this unit is installed is occupied by tenants.  They called about the problem.  They literally came home and microwave was running.  It also happened several evenings while the family was home watching TV and no one was near the microwave!

I've read about the class action lawsuit for certain GE microwave models via a March 2013 article in Consumer Reports magazine.

I've since replaced the dysfunctional unit with a [REDACTED].  Do I have any recourse with GE?

incident_description: I have a GE microwave oven model JES1451DS1BB.  The microwave self started one time and since that time it has been virtually unusable.  Now it won't turn off.  The only way to turn it off is to either unplug the microwave or open the microwave door.  As soon as it is plugged back in, it starts running and it displays 88:88 on the time LED.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a potential hazard but no injury has been reported, and the issue can be mitigated by unplugging or opening the door.

incident_description:
Turned Frigidaire Electric Range on to "Broil" and instrument panel popped and caught on fire
Burned out in about a minute but blackened backsplash.  Panel was shot so I had to purchase a new stove.
justification: The incident involved a fire that caused property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
We had a Sharp microwave that self started.  We notified Sharp twice and NEVER got a response from them!!

Based on my first-hand experience Sharp's assertion that " it is not possible for the cooking operation to begin unless the door is closed, time is entered on the control panel and the START button is pushed" is demonstrably false. At this very late date the suggestion that "the customer have the unit evaluated by a Sharp authorized servicer" is laughable.

After the initial non-responsiveness of Sharp I vowed that I would never have another Sharp product in my house. Based on the 2/19/2013 response I can see I made the right decision.
justification: The microwave self-started without user input, but there is no mention of injury or damage, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I was baking with my glass Anchor Hocking brand dish. I was baking potatoes in the dish at 350, took them out after they were done and set the dish on top of the stove as it was warmed from the oven temperature. It wasn't like it was a cool surface, the oven had been on for over an hour and the stove top and trivet had heated up. I have always done this. Thank goodness I took a couple of steps back to pick something up because there was the loudest noise as my dish exploded into shards of flying glass. It flew across the counter tops both ways and onto the floor. I am so lucky I had walked about five feet away or I could have had glass embedded in my face and upper body. I did have some smaller slivers cut me as I was cleaning surfaces, don't know yet if I was able to get them all off of the floor as its [REDACTED] and will be tricky. This is so scary, as my kids often help get dinner started while I am on my way home from work. Now I am afraid to use glass baking products not only for myself but for my children.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries from glass shards, and the potential for severe injury was high given the flying glass.

incident_description:
I have used Black & Decker toaster ovens for years.  Sometime in late summer I noticed a toaster oven with a timer which I thought would be a helpful feature so I purchased one- I believe the model number TO1412B.  I gave the old toaster oven to a family that had lost everything in a fire.  The first few times I used the toaster oven I had no problems but then I was summoned to the kitchen by the smoke alarm.  On arrival I noted smoke and flames coming from the toaster oven.  When I grabbed the handle to pull it away from the wall to unplug it (as the instructions state) I sustained 1st degree burns on the back of my fingers.  When the fire was extinguished the inside the toaster oven was covered in a layer of black soot.  The charred remains of the bread I had attempted to toast sat on the rack.  Although I was fairly sure I had set the timer I couldnÃÂt be certain.  I cleaned the toaster as well as I could and tried to use it while I stood by and observed, it worked as intended.  Thinking that I had been mistaken about setting the timer I didnÃÂt return it at that point.  I used it a few times after that but was always hovering nearby observing because I didnÃÂt trust it and then it happened again i.e. the timer reached time zero and failed to turn the toaster off- I returned the toaster oven to Walmart and was given a replacement which has worked OK for the last 3 months. 
Since I ÃÂve had toaster ovens in the past I note that the temperature selection knob is not as tapered at the selection end as it was on previous models.  This makes it a bit difficult to see the temperature it points to at a quick glance. I have since painted a dot on the temperature selection end.  Nor do I like the fact the the heating element seems to come on at full power to get the unit up to the set temperature as this results in burning any items that are on the rack when the machine is turned on.
justification: The incident resulted in 1st degree burns (injury) and a fire, but no death. The issue occurred multiple times, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in use for approximately 10 mins and he noticed that there was flames and black smoke emitting from the front of the unit.  The flames were 2-3 inches high.  He opened the dishwasher to stop the cycle but water erupted from the dishwater.  He used the circuit breaker to switch electricity off from the unit, but when he switch it back on, the unit would start.

1/8/13 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that his model number was not a part of the recall.

The consumer is concerned that if he had not been home his house would have caught fire and his model should be included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the consumer was able to mitigate the situation.

incident_description:
The consumer says he was heating a teapot of water.  The large right rear burner blew into flames.  he says it looked like a blow torch.  He says it actually looked like someone took a welding iron to it or tack weld the bottom of the teapot.  

Luckily he was able to reach from the side to turn the burner off.  If no one had been in the room at the time it would have definitely set the house on fire.  

He contacted the retailer/manufacturer who did not seem to know who he should talk to.  

UPDATE: Consumer says the oven now does not work at all.  They bought a new range.  This appliance i sboth dangerous and defective.
justification: The incident involved flames and potential for fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Fire in oven control panel.  Oven purchased new Jan. 28, 2007 from Sears retail store located in Killeen Mall, Killeen, Texas  02487.  No past problems with oven.  On  Saturday, Feb. 2, 2013 at approximately 6 p.m.  prepared to broil steaks for supper.  Turned oven on to broil and there was a loud popping noise, crackling sound and flames erupting from the top of the control panel.  The electric breaker immediatly switched off.  There was smoke and a phenolic-like odor (burning plastic ?) but no more flames.  It appears only the control panel was involved. There were no flames or smoke from the oven itself.  This is a Sears 30" Kenmore Elite single built-in electric oven model 790.49073400 serial # NF43716600 (info from the sales receipt and sticker tag inside the oven) This oven is built-in to surrounding wooden kitchen cabinetry and could very well have caused major damage to my residence.  Thanks to the breaker switching off immediately, there appears to be only very minor smoke damage to the wooden cabinet trim above the control panel.
I believe this oven is a definite safety and fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the control panel but no injuries or significant damage, thanks to the breaker switching off immediately.

incident_description:
Recently I noticed water dripping into the basement from under the dishwasher. I pulled the dishwasher out and removed the panel from underneath and noticed a serious design flaw in the unit which has created a fire and water damage hazard. The Kenmore quiet guard standard Dishwashers heating element is installed using no washers and only a soft metal flexible twist-on retainer to hold the element in place. As a result the hot water enters the washer and as it reaches the heating element the water leaks (significantly) past the heating element and directly into a high voltage electrical connector that powers the high amperage heating element. The water leaks onto the floor and out of sight of the consumer (under the cabinets) until it has ruined the sub flooring. 

This is a serious fire hazard as water and electricity are not a safe combination. During the observed wash cycle no internal fuses (if present) blew nor did a circuit breaker pop. If the water leak is significant enough and water extends out into the living space there is a high probability of electrocution to the consumer should they come in contact with the water which is in direct contact with 120 volt power source and the high amp heating element. 

Kenmore Dishwasher Model number 587.15188401
justification: The incident describes a serious design flaw that poses both fire and electrocution hazards, with potential for injury or death if not addressed.

incident_description:
Samsung over-the-range microwave Model SMH9187ST purchased 12/24/2010. Over the last year I had several instances each month when the oven emitted loud noises while food was heating - like a popping sound but no sparks, almost like someone was applying brakes to the turntable (a loud bumping and popping sound). The table was turning, so the roller ring and turntable were functioning properly and I did inspect them. Nor was it the sound food sometimes makes when it gets too hot, as the sound would start as soon as the oven was turned on and food would not heat properly. I had several visitors also express their concern about the sounds. In all instances food was being reheated in microwaveable plates covered with waxed paper in a clean oven. I woke up at 2:30 am this morning to the sound of the microwave beeping as if food was finished being cooked. The oven was empty, door closed and turntable was not turning, but the light was on and the oven kept beeping. I tried pressing the stop/clear pad but the beeping did not stop. When I pressed the start pad, the display panel listed letters and numbers that I had never seen before. I kept trying the stop button but the beeping would not stop and the light remained lit. Not knowing if there were microwaves present even though the turntable was not turning, I did not open the door. The beeping continued until I was able to get a ladder and unplugged the microwave from the outlet above the cabinet. I had NOT used the microwave at all the previous day. It started by itself. 
While there was no fire or injuries, I consider myself lucky and will NOT use this oven again.
justification: The microwave exhibited unusual behavior and loud noises but caused no injury or fire, fitting a severity level 2. The issue occurred multiple times over a year, indicating a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
(11/11/2012) The consumer stated that she heard clicking in the kitchen. The stove had tried to turn itself on. There were sparks coming from the all of the burners and the grill. The consumer stated that they tried to turn it off but nothing happened. The consumer stated that the stove had to be disconnected  from the outlet. The consumer stated that prior to the incident, they discovered that the two of the knobs on the left side were faulty. She stated that the knobs would just spin around which made  it difficult to turn the burners on or off. The consumer had those replaced. Later on, the other two had to be replaced. 


(11/11/2012) The consumer stated that she contacted LG.  The manufacturer checked to see if there had been a recall but found none. The manufacturer offered to send a technician out. The technician can out on 11/14/2012. The technician plugged the stove back in but the incident did not happen. He replaced an element in the stove that was causing the popping. The technician stated the the element had nothing to do with the sparking on the top of the stove.
justification: The incident involved sparks and malfunctioning knobs but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description:
I have a Keurig Elite Coffee Maker that is about 4 years old.  It has started coming on by itself.  I press the power button to off but if I leave it plugged in it will come on, heat the water and dispense the hot water continually until the water storage bin is empty, then it will continue to try to pump.  

The first time it started on it's own I was within hearing distance and hear the sound of the water running out.  I have been unplugging it since but the other day I forgot and the above episode happened where it kept pumping out hot water till the bin was empty.  However, you could hear the pump trying to pump more water.  Since the unit has a program that is supposed to stop pumping when the water is low and engage a warning light to tell me that it needs more water, that function must not be functioning either.

It works if I make a cup and unplug it when I'm done but if this is happening to others....as it is because there are movies of it happening on You tube....if this had happened when I wasn't home I fear it would have caught fire as the water bin must have been hot because it is not a little warped.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioning and dispensing hot water continuously poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he turned on the oven on at 300 degrees for approximately 30 minutes. The consumer stated that he noticed that what he had in the oven was burning. The consumer stated that he decided to open the door to the oven and an excessive amount of hot air came out from the oven.  

The consumer stated that he tried to turn off the oven by pushing the off button and he had to press it several times before it turned it off.  The consumer stated that the thermometer inside the oven, hanging from one of the racks, was to its highest temperature. 

No one was injured.  

April 23, 2011 A technician serviced the range and replaced a heat sensor for $152.00. 
The consumer stated that on 01/2012 he experienced the same incident and a technician was contacted and he replaced the control board for $325.00.

incident_description:
We have used pyrex baking dishes for years and never had a problem.  A few days ago, my husband used one of our favorite pyrex dishes to bake something.  It was in the oven for about 20 minutes and he opened the door to squeeze some lemon juice on the crab cakes.  He closed the door and within seconds we heard a horrible crashing sound.  I was in another room of the house and I heard it and thought something was falling out of our cupboards.  I ran into the kitchen and he realized that the entire pyrex baking dish had exploded.  He was just lucky that he had closed the oven door when he did and that the glass in the door didn't shatter too.  It took him forever to clean all of the glass out of the oven after it cooled off and we are very upset.

We have many pyrex products and we are now throwing all of them out!  My husband doesn't even want to donate them to Goodwill because they are too dangerous.  

I am now in the process of ordering new, safe products on-line to replace all of our pyrex and it will be expensive.  I'm replacing a large covered casserole, 3 rectangular bakers, one square baker, 2 pie plates, 2 loaf pans, 2 oval bakers, measuring pitcher and too many different sizes of bowls to count.  We are not happy about any of this and feel pyrex should be taken off the market because it is so unsafe.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but no one was injured, and the incident caused property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description: I was cooking with a 9in glass pyrex baking dish in a 400 degree oven. The dish was in the oven for approximately 15 minutes. I removed the dish and placed it on the stove top, which was cool to touch and had not been used all day. Within 1 minute of setting the dish down it exploded. Shards of glass were shot across my kitchen in a 15ft radius.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass dish causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
My two-year-old Rapidia pressure cooker exploded (seal broken). 

There are two reasons why I want to report this incident. First, I believe that the cooker wasn't designed properly. Its safety valve should have prevented the incident to happen by releasing the steam pressure, or a stronger seal needs to be used.

Second, I believe there is a design flaw in the location of the safety valve which is bundled together with the normal steam outlet. This design can prevent people from telling if the steam is from the normal outlet or the safety release valve. Because of the design flaw, it's very hard for most users to tell the difference between steams released from the safety valve and from the normal valve. As a result, it'd be impossible for most users to tell when the safety valve is open and when to remove the heat from the cooker. If the steam is out from the safety valve, users would be able to identify the problem in time and remove the heat to avoid the explosion.
justification: The pressure cooker exploded due to a design flaw, but the description does not mention any injury or death, only the incident itself.

incident_description:

Serial number 610KR00127  Made in 2006

She called me and we found the 2 light bulbs (60 W each) had been on for very long time in the frig even the doors were closed completely.  I tried to push the 2 door switches to see if the light would go off but the lights were still on.  So I pulled the power plug immediately and removed the 2 bulbs.  Our inspection showed the transparent plastic cover for the bulbs was melt at one side.  The corner of the cover stuck to the internal wall very tightly, the while body of the cover hanging in the air. I had to break the cover from the wall. The 2 bulb seats were baked to brown. incident_description:
Kitchen Aid refrigerator compressor relay failed and started wiring & connectors to smoke & burn.  
Model KSRU25FK8T01      SN SL1730558      Manuf 04/01
Have had refrigerator  in continual use since originally purchased from Sears in 2001. 

Discovered late at night when the faint smell of burnt wiring reached the bedroom.  Strongest smell was in kitchen.  Pulled refrig away from wall and noted faint smoke coming from rear grill.   Looked through the cardboard grill and noted electrical arcing on compressor relay.   Small flame noted in addition to arcing.  Unplugged refrig and then blew out small flame.  Removed grille and noted significant damage to the relay and connected wiring from overheating.   Took several pictures of damaged area.  Moved food into coolers and a 2nd refrigerator we have in garage.  

Next day surfed internet and found several others have had the exact same problem.   Purchased replacement parts from McCombs Supply Co (Lancaster, PA) and made repair per the provided instructions and guidance from various appliance repair websites.

Extremely disappointed with Whirlpool that they have not addressed this design fault and other consumer product safety orgs have not forced a manufacturer's recall/repair.  Also I don't understand why Whirlpool did not notify owners of this failure mode.  Their lack of response to this design fault and their use of a cardboard grill within inches of this area is inexcusable.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and a small flame, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was resolved without harm.

incident_description: My GE Profile Microwave/Convection Oven (Model number PVM1790SR1SS Manufactured March 2011) self started when no one was home and could not be turned off. Our oven is clean and has no grease or anything that would have gotten into the vents to the heating element that caught fire.  I usually just bake breads and things that never spill.  There is no reason for a heating element in my oven to catch fire.  Especially when the element is under the floor of the oven and does not come into contact with food drips like the older ovens used to.

incident_description:
I purchased a one-cup Anchor Hocking measuring cup and used it for the first time on January 22, 2013. Because the cup is marked safe for microwave use, I believed it was resistant to heat, i.e., safe to rest a spoon used to stir oatmeal inside the cup. The cup exploded. It didnÃÂt crack. It didnÃÂt break. It literally exploded sending glass flying 4-5 feet in all directions. There was not one recognizable piece of the measuring cup remaining. The largest piece of glass was an inch. In addition to chunks of glass scattered all over my kitchen, there were very fine slivers, shards, and glass dust all over the floor and countertop. 

Thankfully, I was about 3 feet away and my back was turned when the explosion occurred (although some of the glass hit the back of my head), otherwise, IÃÂm sure a visit to the emergency room would have been required, as the glass would have been embedded in my face and eyes.

I am not interested in getting my money back or in another Anchor Hocking measuring cup; I donÃÂt intend to use their products any longer. However, I do think their glass products have the potential to cause serious bodily harm. There should be a label warning consumers that, even though their glass products are supposedly safe for microwave use, they can explode when exposed to temperature fluctuations.
justification: The measuring cup exploded, causing glass to scatter and hit the user, though no serious injury occurred this time.

incident_description: At 9 pm, December 31, 2012, my wife turned on the whirlpool gold dishwasher and then went to go take a shower.   As I watched tv in the adjoining family room I smelled burning plastic, turned and saw much smoke billowing in the kitchen.   I ran to the unit to turn it off, but the control panel was not working. incident_description:
I purchased a Kitchen Aid double oven less than 9 months ago and I just used the self clean option for the first time. I called KitchenAid just to have them walk me through it for the first time.  It was simple.  The self clean feature was supposed to run for 2 1/2 hours and after only 45 minutes I heard a loud explosion!  Thankfully my kids were not in the kitchen but when I went running to see what happened I was shocked and terrified to see that the glass door had exploded and shards of glass were flying through my kitchen and with such force that they flew into other rooms in the house as well.  I was naturally flipping out and trying to figure out how to stop this but couldn't get near the oven for fear of being hit and cut by flying glass! My husband ran upstairs to the computer to see if there was information on that model to try and trip the fuse when he uncovered that there were multiple people who experienced this same dangerous expoding glass issue!  I can't understand how KitchenAid/Whirpool could allow the oven to continue to be sold and not recalled when this is a recurring problem.  Can you imagine if my daughter who always sits at the kitchen island to do her homework was sitting there when this happened?!!!
It never dawned on me that KitchenAid would not stand by their product and quickly come and get this unsafe oven out of my house.  I truly thought they were going to feel awful and apologize and make good on their product.  Instead, the safety department was almost bored with my phone call and just said, "Ok ma'am your glass broke so we will send you a new piece of glass!  Can you imagine?!!!! I said absolutley not, how am I supposed to know that this oven is safe when it just exploded in my kitchen!  I'm terrified!  She said well ma'am we can send a technician out to deteremine if it is safe.  The next day they sent a serviceman, (not a KitchenAid serviceman) out who came with a [vacuum cleaner] to clean up my kitchen!  When I told him that I thought he was supposed to run some diagnostics and determine the damage this may have caused to my oven he told me that's what they tell everyone this happens to!  He said my only orders are to come here, clean it up and order you a new piece of glass!  I am furious and so scared this will happen to another family who won't be as lucky as I was that no one was in the vicintiy of the kitchen when this explosion occurred!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of the oven door, but no injuries were reported. The occurrence likelihood is high due to multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Subject:    Unusual behavior of a Sharp microwave

Appliance:   Sharp 1200 watt Model R-510-ER microwave

Manufactured:   June, 2001

Purchased:   Last half of 2001

Use:   Household consisting of 2 retired adults in their late 60s

Issues that have started occurring in the last 6 months

1	After entering or even in the process of entering a run time the microwave will start before the Start button is pressed
2	The microwave has started on its own upon the closing of the door before any time entry is made or the Start button is pressed
3	Food has been placed inside, the door shut, a time entered and Start pressed.  The timer failed to start and ran past the entered time.  We had to press Stop/Cancel to stop it
4	At least once on a spontaneous start-up, we had to unplug it to get it to stop.  The controls had no effect
5	Food placed in, door closed, time entered, Start pressed.  The unit failed to start.  Cancel pressed, process repeated and the unit started

I realize this is an 11 year old appliance and it has probably given us service beyond expectations, but it has not had a lot of use (primarily reheating foods with little actual cooking) and has been kept in a like new condition as far as cleaning inside and outside.  The problems are very random time wise and probably are occurring only 5 or 6 times per month.  We have not experienced any of the spontaneous startup problems as described in the March, 2013, issue of Consumers Reports but are following their suggestion of reporting the problems to the manufacturer, CPSC, and Consumers Reports.  A response to this report would be appreciated.
justification: The microwave exhibits erratic behavior but no injuries or damage have been reported, only operational incidents.

incident_description:
Jenn-Air Model:  JMC9158BAS
Serial Number:  12421375NR

The microwave was being used to defrost frozen soup.  After microwave timer went off, the microwave continued to buzz.  After investigating, I discover that, even thought the control panel said that the microwave was OFF the magnetron was still ON! The magnetron would turn OFF when the door was opened, but, would turn back on when the door was closed again (The control panel relay is connected to one side of the magnetron and the door safely switch is connected to the other).  This same problem happened before while the microwave was still in warranty and was fixed by Jenn-Air by replacing the control panel.  The inside of the microwave got hot and there was the odor of hot electronics (because the microwave was OFF the ventilation fan was not running, however, the magnetron was operating).
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Re: Kenmore Ultrabake Smoothtop Electric Range
Model No.: 92002102
Serial No.: RN0226865

I am writing to request repair or replacement action on the above range. It was purchased new on
2/2/2003. This first unit delivered 2/6/2003 was refused because of visible damage. The second
unit was accepted on 2/11/2003. The first service call was the following week, 2/22/2003. The
first service person could not repair the range so a second person showed up on 3/6/2003 and
replaced the control board for the oven control. The range worked fine for several years.

After several years the top burners started heating in an uncontrolled way; sometimes seemingly
turning themselves off and sometimes heating at the highest level even when set on low. The most
recent problem occurred on 11/4/2012. While baking a chicken at 350 degrees F and with about
20 minutes more to cook the food began to burn and the juices in the pan popping and sizzling. We
opened the oven door and found the broiler on full blast even though it was not programmed to be
on. We removed the chicken and cancelled the cook cycle. The oven element went off and the
broiler element stayed on.

I have 35 years of experience in safety electronics so knew my next step would be to try and reset
the control unit. I turned off the power at the circuit breaker, waited two minutes and then
repowered the unit. The broiler came back on but would not shut off at the control panel. I tried
resetting the unit one more time by shutting off the power at the circuit breaker for five minutes
with the same results; the broiler would not shut off with the control panel. I turned the power off
for the night for safety and again retried it the next morning with the same result; the broiler would
not shut off with the control panel. In order to at least be able cook some food I have removed the
broiler element and the control panel seems to be operating the baking element satisfactorily.
However, this is not a solution.

After checking the Internet IÃÂve found many postings of people with the identical problems IÃÂve
detailed (a very recent posting is on Saferproducts.gov) but no recall has been made for this model
or serial number. Thankfully we were inside when this unit malfunctioned or it could have burned
down the house! If we were sleeping and the unit turned itself on (which some of the Internet
postings have detailed) we could be dead! Is Kenmore waiting for people to die before they
remedy this defective and dangerous unit?

I will forward this letter to as many consumer protection groups as I can for their review and,
hopefully, positive action. In the meantime I will keep my copy and records off-site, not at home in
case the stove burns the house down!

incident_description:
I would like to file a request to investigate a particular product. I believe that the Fisher & Paykel DCS cooking downdraft DD-36SS has a safety flaw that may cause severe burns.  The unit has a push-button switch on the top that actuates the unit and it rises out of the countertop. Because it is directly behind the stove, it is very easy to have a pot handle, perhaps with boiling water, extended over the rising downdraft such that the water will be spilled or the pot overturned. Because the switch is unguarded, it is very easy to inadvertently actuate it simply be setting something down near the edge of the stove. The switch should have a guard so that it cannot be actuated accidentally.

While we have not had a safety incident yet with this product, we have had at least two occurrences of accidental actuation of the switch, causing the cooktop to rise from the countertop and overturning pots on the stove or other cookware.  Thankfully, nothing was hot at the time.

incident_description:
Blue sparks from behind back panel of Kenmore Electric range. On one occasion the front right burner powered onto "High" when the dial was turned to a lower setting. On a later occasion, the front right burner turned to "High" and stayed that way despite the setting on the knob. The only solution was to power off the range, and remove the switch from behind the backpanel.

Upon further investigation of the failed switch (one of these http://www.amazon.com/Kenmore-Range-Infinite-Switch-316436001/dp/B001DPT2QY), it appears that there is a little pressure sensitive conductive pad that carries current to the element (over 2000 watts). In my case the metal contacts shorted out and caused the conductive pad to fuse the two contacts together permanently. The result was that the front right element was permanently powered on at the highest setting,

This is an extreme fire hazard and these products should be recalled for repair immediately.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range that poses an extreme fire hazard, but no actual injury or death is reported.
