incident_description:
There was a kitchen fire on July 5, 2009 involving a Frigidaire Electric Smoothtop Slide-In Cooktop, Model No. PLES 399 ECC, Serial No. NF 61524055.  The morning of the incident I had washed some  dishes and and other items.  The dishes were placed in a dish tray to dry, and I placed a large vase and frying pan on the cooktop to dry.  At the time the stove was OFF and the cooking surface was cold to the touch.  I had placed a dish towel on the cooktop to catch any water dripping from the vase and frying pan.  The vase was located at the front left side of the cooktop and the frying pan was on the back left location.  After washing the dishes, I left the apartment to go shopping.  When we returned from our errands, we found the Fire Department cleaning up after the fire.  At that time, I was interviewed by the Fire Investigator and shared with him what had happened before we left the apartment.

In the fire report it indicated that the cooktop control knob for the Left Front burner was in the ON position when the apartment security personnel responded to the fire alarm in our apartment.  I told the Fire Investigator that when I placed the items on the stovetop all controls were in the OFF position.  I did not know for sure why the control knob for the Left Front burner was in the ON position, unless I may have accidentally bumped it while retrieving something from the upper cabinet.  This was the only explanation I guessed at that time after the fire.

Damage to our unit were the charred stove top and cabinets, and water damages from the fire sprinkler system that was activated.  Damage to other units, adjacent to and below our unit also occurred due to the fire sprinkler activation.

On October 27, 2010, all apartment owners and residents in our complex received a Recall Notice from the apartment management office.  In the notice it said that the model cooktop in all apartments had a defect that had caused 70 incidents involving this Frigidaire cooktop. The hazard detailed in the recall notice said:  "Liquids pooling under the control knob can cause the surface heating element to turn on unexpectedly, heat to temperatures other than expected and then not turn off, posing a risk of fire and burn hazards to consumers."

The recall notice also informed us that there was a Seal Kit that would be installed to protect against this hazard.  And it included a number to call to arrange for the kit to be installed.

While I still cannot be 100% certain how the control knob was turned to the ON position, I now suspect that water dripping from the large vase I had placed on the cooktop, may have gotten behind the control knob to initiate the hazard as detailed in the recall notice.
justification: The incident involved a kitchen fire causing property damage but no reported injuries, and the recall notice indicates a possible but not certain defect-related cause.

incident_description:
The consumer says she turned the oven on to pre heat at 425.  she said the unit started making a "popping" noise, and flames shot out of the back. 

The consumer says they pulled the stove out and unplugged it.  they have not used it since.  Her back wall was blackened.  The consumer says that there are numerous reports of the same thing happening with this unit.    

The consumer contacted the retailer who said the unit is not on recall.
justification: Flames and blackened wall indicate a significant incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My husband put chicken and a little water in a 9x13 pyrex baking dish and put it in the oven preheated to 350 degrees.  After about 5-10 minutes, the dish exploded.  He was near the table and said it sounded like a shotgun being fired.  He turned toward the stove and saw smoke billowing out of the oven.  When he went and opened the oven door, the chicken was laying all over the racks and glass was all over the bottom of the oven.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish, which could have caused injury, but the description does not mention any injuries.

incident_description:
While cooking Thanksgiving dinner at our cabin, I pulled the turkey part way out of the oven to check the temperature.  The entire turkey pan started sliding out of the oven and almost landed on the floor. 
The problem is that when you pull out the oven rack part way, it is on an angle and the pan tries to slide forward, causing burns, etc.
When cooking on a cookie sheet, the same thing happens.  While cooking chicken nuggets I pulled the oven rack part way out to check for doneness and the whole pan slid forward and dumped the hot food all over the oven door.
The oven rack is on an angle unless it is pulled out all the way.
This is unsafe!
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with potential for burns or injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says that yesterday morning he was finishing preparing Thanksgiving dinner.  His wife set the unit to self cleaning mode.  

He noticed a strange odor and then saw smoke.  Flames shot up from behind the range.  He tried to contain the fire by smothering it with a blanket but the flames got larger.  They contacted the Fire Dept who put the fire out.  The stove is totally destroyed.  

The Fire dept determined that the consumer had not done anything wrong and that it is a faulty product.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who apologized and filed a report.  They told him the unit is not on recall.  They are going to send inspectors to determine if the unit needs replacement. 

The consumer says that his kitchen cabinets are scorched and sook all over his kitchen.  

The consumers wife said the unit started smoking about an hour after it was set to the self cleaning mode.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the faulty product causing the fire.

incident_description: Coffee mug is stamped dishwasher/microwave safe. I was reheating coffee in the mug inside the microwave and the entire cup including the handle gets very hot even after a few seconds. I had to use a pot holder to remove it from the microwave. It is coated in a shiny/metallic brown paint which I believe conducts the heat.
justification: The mug became excessively hot, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
GE profile dishwasher, purchased in 2005, model PDW9280J00SS; SN: GH861770B .  We started the dishwasher cycle, and somewhere during the cycle we smelled an acrid odor and smoke was coming out from the control panel of the dishwasher (we think it was starting the dry cycle).  We checked to make sure it wasn't something fallen down onto the heating element, and started it up again (the start light was flashing which was not normal).  Within a minute of starting back up again the smoke was viewed clearly coming from the control panel area.

We stopped the dishwasher cycle and disconnected the power to the unit.  We later found that the unit was under a recall for the very problem we experienced.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an acrid odor but no injury or death, and the unit was under recall for this known issue, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
We purchased a brand new, GE Microwave (Model #PEM31DM3BB) that was professionally installed in our new home last year.  The microwave caught fire while microwaving a glass bottle containing baby milk for 1 minute.  Fortunately, my wife was present to see the microwave catch fire and quickly extinguished the flame, however the inside of the microwave melted from the flames.

We have reported this to GE and they sent a technician to investigate.  His initial assessment was that this was caused by food in the microwave getting caught behind the plastic walls of the microwave and catching fire.  This seems unlikely since the microwave is cleaned regularly and the only food that could have been caught in the plastic walls would be very small.

In any event, this might be broader issue affecting these devices.  It sounded and smelt more like an electrical short than burning food.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was quickly extinguished with no injuries, indicating an incident with no harm to people.

incident_description: My GE Profile Gas Stove - 30 inch, Model # JG8905SEF3SS, Serial # VG289831P has a faulty electronic panel that overrides other commands and turns on the self clean mode when I use the back left burner of the stovetop.  Last night, while I was warming an item in the oven at 350' and heating a small saucepan of liquid on the top left rear burner the self clean mode came on an was difficult to disengage. This seems to be a serious fire hazard.  If I had stepped out of the kitchen, we could well have had a catastrophe!
justification: The incident involves a faulty electronic panel activating self-clean mode unexpectedly, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire dishwasher, that is less than 3.5 years old, started smoking.
Model FGHD2433KF0

I noticed that the heater element is RUSTED THROUGH to the electrical elements!

How can a manufacturer make a heater element out of a metal that is going to rust and deteriorate to the point of starting a fire?

I am thankful that I came back downstairs after going to bed, and smelled the smoke, before it became a major fire.
justification: The dishwasher started smoking due to a rusted heater element, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: circuit board caught fire in back of stove and smoked up kitchen
justification: The circuit board caught fire and produced smoke, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Your Message: We bought a new Electrolux stove. When we use the oven it produces a noxious gas that makes us sick and makes the house smell like we had a fire. I think this is a serious problem with these stoves. The problem seems to be getting worse. The model number is ew30if60isb serial number vf21567356. The service man says that we just need to cook out something in the insulation,but we can't stay in the house when the oven is on.
justification: The noxious gas from the oven is causing sickness, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The problem is persistent and worsening, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
Cuisinart Classic Toaster Oven Broiler (TOB-30 Series)
Purchased: 03/08/2007
NOTE: out of warranty

We never leave it plugged in when not in use.
We only use it to toast and bake.  
On average, we use it five (5) times per week.
Over the last week we've found that when we pull the plug out of the wall, the cord & plug are hot.
Today, my wife needed to use a pot holder to pull the plug, because it was so hot after toasting one item.
We always pull it using the plug and not by pulling the cord. 

We will not be using it anymore (and will be buying a new toaster oven), but will keep it for a while, in case you wish to examine it.

I am reporting this, in case you have had other reports that might lead to bigger safety concerns that might require a recall or safety notice.
justification: The incident involves a hot plug and cord, posing a potential burn risk, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I purchased a toaster oven broiler. I set the temperature on 350 degrees. I noticed smell as if it was really hot so I turned it down to 250 degrees. I was warming biscuits. I was sliding the oven further back on the table. I placed one hand on the back and the other on the top of the oven. My fingers were burned. The feel and appearance of my fingers changed. My fingers had a smooth look where they touched the oven. This was not just a warm oven but hot enough to cause serious burns. I contacted the company who told me there was nothing they could do about it. Also said toaster ovens get very hot be cause they are not insulated. They said that this information came with the product. I asked if it was written on the box. She said if not then it is in the manual (THE MANUAL THAT I CAN"T SEE UNTIL AFTER I PURCHASE PRODUCT). The info was not on the box but in the manual, pg 5 2nd paragraph. If this info is put on the box, many would not buy it. I contacted CUISINART January 3, 2013.
justification: The incident resulted in serious burns, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as burns can occur when handling hot appliances without proper warning.

incident_description: I bought an Anchor Hocking 7-Piece Bakeware Set from Walmart a while back. Last night, I baked a deep dish pizza in the large glass oven dish. When I took it out of the oven and placed it on a wooden cutting board, the glass exploded, sending scalding hot shards of glass in all directions. This is a very dangerous product in my opinion
justification: The glass exploding and sending hot shards in all directions indicates a significant incident, but the description does not mention any injury.

incident_description: My wife was washing a glass lid for a pan when it exploded in her hands sending sharp glass shards all over and cut her hands. The lid was not hot and the water was at most luke warm as she was waiting for the water to get hot to wash it. The brand is "Wearever".
justification: The incident resulted in cuts to the hands, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Glass lids exploding under normal washing conditions is rare (likelihood 2).

incident_description: I had a CorningWare SimplyLite 2.5qt dish explode into 1000s of pieces and shards in my oven.  I placed 1/2 Costco chicken enchilada casserole in a preheated 350 degree oven.  Within 5 minutes I heard the explosion.  There were so many pieces and shards of glass that when I opened the door many pieces slipped through vents of the lower oven door and ended up there.  I FOLLOWED THE SAME PROCEDURE THE EVENING BEFORE USING THE SAME CASSEROLE AND SAME DISH WITHOUT INCIDENT.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish causing significant damage but no reported injury, and the likelihood is low as it occurred unexpectedly despite prior safe use.

incident_description:
I purchased from Target, online, a Bella Housewares 12-cup coffee maker. The box it came in said "2-hour shutoff" and "auto shutoff." The instruction manual under the heading "brewing coffee instructions" (page 6) said "Note: The coffee maker will turn OFF automatically after 2 hours."

The first two times I used the coffee maker, I was surprised to find many hours later that the coffee maker's blue light was still on and the pot was still hot. It clearly was not turning off automatically. When I called customer service for Bella, I was told that the coffee maker does NOT, in fact, turn off automatically and that the packaging and instructions were erroneous.

Imagine how many owners of this machine are risking burns and possible fires expecting that the machine will turn off automatically when it does not! This Chinese-made product, with its FALSE claims, should be immediately recalled. It takes little investigation and a simple call to Bella to confirm.

This is the link to Target's web site for this product:
 http://www.target.com/p/bella-dots-12-cup-coffee-maker-lime-green/-/A-14114705?ref=tgt_adv_XSG10001&AFID=Google_PLA_df&LNM=|14114705&CPNG=Unassigned&kpid=14114705&LID=PA&ci_src=17588969&ci_sku=14114705
justification: The coffee maker's failure to auto-shutoff as advertised poses a risk of burns and potential fires, though no actual incidents are reported.

incident_description:
I bought my wife a set of Saber Knives  from COSTCO.COM the Christmas before last. 10 months later, while using the 6" utility knife, it BROKE IN HALF. Wow! I called SABER and the CEO explained "they had a problem with that particular knife". He assured me that the rest of the knife set was safe and sent me a new, serrated 6" utility.

One month later the 7" Santoku BROKE IN HALF while I was using it and this time I WAS CUT. Angry, I called SABER again for an explanation. He assured me he had never had anyone with two broken knives. Gave me a story about how much he trusts these knives, that his family uses them and so on. He then sent me a new set of his best knives. My folks also purchased a  set for a gift.
This afternoon, my wife was cutting some smoked salmon fillets with one of the 4.5" steak knives and guess what? Yes, ANOTHER BROKEN KNIFE! A "German Steel" (made in China) knife simply broke in half.

I hope I don't need to explain how dangerous this can be. In MY OPINION, the steel used in these knives is FLAWED. When have you ever seen a steel knife BREAK INTO TWO PIECES? I DO NOT BELIEVE these knives can be trusted. We always hand washed and dried these knives and never abused them. A good knife should last many, many years and NEVER break in half.

With the previous set on COSTCO.COM there were dozens of reviews, although about half of them mentioned broken knives. I have submitted no less than 4 reviews to COSTCO.COM and all have been rejected for one reason or another of which my contact there cannot explain. It is ridiculous that I have to try to walk on eggshells to get my review posted on COSTCO.COM and still it does not appear. If they only allow POSITIVE reviews then the public is being DECEIVED as to the performance and more importantly the SAFETY of these products.

All the SABER knife sets on COSTCO.COM contain knives that are known to break via my experience and other users who have also posted on COSTCO.COM therefore the public has a RIGHT TO KNOW about the DEFECTIVE STEEL used in the construction of ALL SABER KNIFE SETS sold by COSTCO.

[REDACTED]

COSTCO: [REDACTED], Quality Assurance Officer [REDACTED]
COSTCO: [REDACTED] , Web Site Supervisor [REDACTED]
SABER KNIVES: [REDACTED], CEO  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a knife breaking and causing a cut, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). Given multiple reports of similar incidents and the CEO's acknowledgment of a problem, the likelihood is high (4).

incident_description:
(11/22/2012) The consumer stated that they were removing a turkey from the oven. The oven rack was on the bottom and it became dislodged. This happens where ever the rack is positioned. The consumer stated that it is unsafe.

No damage was caused. There was a big spill in the oven.

The cooktop lock out button does not work properly. Other functions are triggered when the panel top is wiped. This happens consistently. Also, the meat thermometer activates when not plugged in.
justification: The incident involved an oven rack dislodging and a malfunctioning cooktop, but no injuries or damage occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore Trio Refridgerator purchased from Sears in 2006 model number 77552600. The overhead light in the fridge did not turn off when the doors were closed. Which caused the fridge to overheat, melting the light cover and blackening the wires and light bulb casings. I am positive had I not discovered this in a timely fashion it would have resulted in a fire. Every item on my top shelf of the fridge had melted and the entire fridge was like a blast furnace when I opened the door. The wiring and bulbs had started to turn black and were well on their way to causing a fire. No one will take responsibility for the fridge. I purchased the fridge from Sears and the fridge is marked a Kenmore but Sears says the fridge was manufactured by LG and so they refer to LG for any type of property damage. LG states they will only give you 250.00 towards food even with reciepts showing a larger food loss. In addition parts to repair the fridge (though who would ever want to repair it, or trust it again) are on backorder for 4 months. I also had a 5 year extended warranty from Sears on the fridge that had just expired. Sears and LG are just playing hot potato with a fridge that should be recalled before it causes a loss of life or greater property damage.
justification: The incident caused property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My wife was melting butter in a small Duralex glass bowl.  She put the bowl in the microwave for 30 seconds.  When she opened the microwave, she reached up to grab the bowl and it exploded into a thousand tiny pieces.  She has a few cuts on her face from this because the microwave was above our range and it exploded at eye level.  It could have been much worse so we are thankful it did not hit her eyes.

We have used these bowls for several years and not had any issues.  In researching this on the Internet, it appears that many people have had this happen and the bowls spontaneously explode.  I saw several comments from people where the bowls exploded just sitting in their cabinets.

How in the world these products can still be sold is beyond me.  This is an extreme danger to anyone using them.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts on the face) but no death, and similar incidents are reported by multiple users indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
At Christmas I received the OrGreenic ceramic Green Non-stick fry pan from my Grandmother. The next morning I decided to use the pan to cook breakfast. As my grandmother and I are standing in front of the stove cooking breakfast, I notice a glow under the pan. At first I thought it was just something on the burner, but after it got worse I removed the pan and noticed the bottom was on FIRE. It burned the bottom of the pan and it melted my grandmother's heating coil on her stove top.
So I immediately stopped using the pan.
I called the company to speak to someone about the situation and all I was told was that if I would pay to have the pan shipped back to them and include a check for $7.99 they would send me a new pan. I told them I don't want a new pan and they should be responsible for replacing my grandmother's heating coil. I was told they are not responsible for damages!!!!!!!!!!! I then asked to speak to a manager/ supervisor and was repeatedly told they would tell me the same thing.
After about the 4th time of asking for a manager the operator put me on hold for about 2 minutes and came back on the line and said the managers were all in a meeting. He again told me they would tell you the same thing, NOT responsible for damages!!! At that point I hung up!!
justification: The incident involved a pan catching fire and damaging the stove, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
During a wash cycle the dishwasher caught on fire.  This was 01-09-2013 at approximately 8:00 CST.

We were informed of the fire by a cat (oddly) who started acting odd.

Upon entering the kitchen we found the kitchen full of smoke and smelled of burning plastic.  Black smoke was coming from the door of the dishwasher at the top mostly from the right side.  Flames also could be seen to the right of middle.

When opened the water was shooting upward with force.

The circuit breaker was pulled and the water turned off.  When the flames died I removed the front to make sure the fire totally extinguished and not smoldering.

Sears was contacted via phone and online "chat".  They finally took my statement as a "feedback" on 01-10-2013 3:00 CST but the feedback did not include any method to contact me, to know how bad the fire was, to know what parts were involved, or even the model.  So ... I assumed they really do not care.

If we were not home I have NO DOUBT the house would have caught on fire!  Period!
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant risk to the house, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Refrigerator was source of strong electrical burning smell but seemed to be otherwise functional.   Source of smell was small fire around the power connector for main compressor.  If I had not been home at the time to detect the burning smell, it would likely have caught the house on fire.
justification: The incident involved a small fire but no injury or death, and the likelihood is possible given the potential for fire if undetected.

incident_description: The oven on my LG range, model # LRE30755ST/02 heated to a temperature much higher then it was set for.  This occurred several times, burning the item in the oven and creating smoke that filled the kitchen/house when the door was opened. I had the unit serviced twice for this problem, the first time having the thermostat probed in the oven replaced, which did not resolve the issue. The second time the "mother board" was replaced which seemed to fix the problem at least somewhat.  At this time the oven does work but when the set temperature is checked against a separate temperature gauge that the repair used the temperature is consistenly 10 to 15 degrees different.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: LG Range makes crackling noise in control panel when oven is not on. Sometimes when oven is on, it wouldn't heat to the tempature set to. On Jan. 5th, I set oven to 400 and it went WAY beyond that getting EXTREMLY hot.
justification: The oven's malfunction poses a potential hazard (overheating), but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The Cooktop On and Hot Surface On indicators on our GGE388LXS02 stove are severely inadequate to convey the dangers associated with the cooktops hot surface.  

I burned the fingertips of my left hand today because the Cooktop On and Hot Surface indicators did not call the condition of the cooktop to my attention.  When I was retrieving the coffee pot that sits next to the stove, I placed my hand on the cooktop which immediately burned my hand.  The cooktop was used in the morning, and it was apparently left on the low setting.  I had been on for approximately five hours.  My husband and I had traversed by the stove throughout this time and neither one of us noticed it was on.  

These indicators on our previous whirlpool range were significantly larger and brighter than the indicators on this GGE388LXS02 stove.  I believe the indicators on our current stove should be just as bright.  After this incident, I thoroughly inspected the indicators and found that both indicators tend to wash out when viewed at an angle which contributed to us not noticing the cooktop was left on.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury due to inadequate indicators on the stove, and the likelihood is high given the design flaw and frequent use of the appliance.

incident_description:
I took the door apart on this Maytag DW when it suddenly stopped working last Sunday. No lights; completely unresponsive. When I detected current at the junction box behind the base panel, but none at the door switch, I followed the black & while wires down the door. At the point where the wires exit the door and go under the tub, four of them are worn through, exposing bare wire. It also appears some of the plastic insulation around them is charred. At least one wire is severed. 

Although this DW is not part of a recall (based upon the last 2 of the SN) this seems like a product design issue. 
     Model #: MDB9150AWW
     SN: 2793279CR

Use is 1 time per week at a church. Info below is for the church.
justification: Exposed and severed wires with charred insulation indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: The KitchenAid wall oven was set to self-clean cycle.  30 minutes after cycle started the inner tempered glass door "blew up."  Glass was scattered in the interior of the oven and on the kitchen floor, damaging the floor.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering, causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: The Viking 48" models were recalled due to an issue with the door falling off, as published in 09-242.  I have experienced the same issue with my 42" model refrigerator, model DFSB423, purchased and installed in May of 2006.  The unit was installed by Viking-certified technician [REDACTED], ID Number [REDACTED], of Coast Installation.  In the years after installation, the refrigerator-side door almost fell off its hinges while still under the original 3-year warranty, again similar to the issues in 09-242.  Once the hinge was replaced by a Viking-certified technician, the door has not been able to maintain a proper seal, and sits at a noticeable angle relative to the refrigerator.  Even though the 42" models have never been part of the recall, I believe that there are 42" models with the same issues as certain 48" and 36" models, and should also be subject to recall.
justification: The incident involves a door falling off, which is a safety hazard but does not cause injury.

incident_description:
One of the handles on my crock pot cracked and broke off.  I looked on line to see if there was a replacement or recall and there was.  My model was not included in the recall even though it has the same handles as Model 5025 which was recalled.  The other handle has now cracked and is ready to fall off.  
It is the Rival Crock Pot Soneware Slow Cooker Model 3355.  I cannot find a date code on the plug prong.  I did find the following information.  LT-3017 / E124791 / LIAN DUNG C
These slow cookers are dangerous and should be added to the recall.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard with a crock pot that could lead to injury if the handles fail during use, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: We own a Kenmore Elite range Model # 79099123400.   On or about January 3, 2013 my wafe was baking something when the range begin to smoke and then had an arc of fire shoot out the back. The smoke charred the wall and caused the circuit breaker to jump.  The range continued to smoke and we unplugged it from the outlet.  The damage done to the range was in the neighborhood of $1,000 causing any repairs to not make financial sense.  The range was purchased from Sears in the fall of 2006.  I understand a recall was issued for the turn knob style of this range.  Ours was not a turn knob style but a display push pad model.  Should that model be included within the recall?
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Incident happened on a Kenmore Elite Free Standing Range, Model# 790.97103010, Serial # VF04146460.  Less than 10 minutes after starting the oven and the front element, we hear a popping sound and see black smoke coming from the top back panel, the panel then catches fire.  I rush downstairs to turn off the dedicated circuit breaker that controls the stove.  Even after a fire this circuit breaker was not tripped, which is troubling.  We pulled the stove out from under the cabinets, unplugged the unit and let the fire burn out.  Our house is filled with a terrible smell that in nauseating from the fire and black smoke.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no reported injuries or deaths, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the specific nature of the event.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the dishwasher was left to run the cycle, however, when they returned home later, (not sure of time) there was smoke emitting from the unit.  The room was engulfed in smoke he was unable to use the control panel to power it off , the circuit breaker was used to switch off power from the dishwasher.

The smoke appeared to be projecting from the side of the dishwasher door. There was no visible damages to the unit.  The caller stated that there might be smoke damages to the dining room.

(11/11/12) The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that the unit was not recalled and should file a report with the agency.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and potential smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
As the Hotpoint Dishwasher was running, our home was filled with a burning plastic odor.  The Burning plastic odor was coming from the dishwasher.  The wires melted at the Power Supply & Junction Box.
Model # HDA3220Z02BB  Serial # AV82601ZY
justification: The incident involved a burning plastic odor and melted wires, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Text of Consumer's Letter:

October 26th 2012

General Electric Company
3135 Easton Turnpike
Fairfield, CT 06828

Re: My Defective Dishwasher

To Whom It May Concern,

I have a GE dishwasher model # GSD3230Z04WW, Serial # HV853063B, that has been repaired over five times for a sparking and burning smell. I did look at your product recall notice and saw almost the same model number. When I called your helpdesk they told me that the unit was not recalled, and they were not going to offer any replacement. The problem with the recalled units was the fact that the liquid from the soap dispenser leaked on the lower wires causing the unit to either catch on fire, do dead, or spark. My unit was sparking, has soap liquid on the wires, and then became dead before repairs were competed. For whatever reason, this unit should have been on your recall list. It is a fire hazard and I do not want it after five repairs.

This letter is a documented warning that should this unit cause any injury or death to any person(s) and / or fire damage to my premises, I will file legal action against the General Electric Company.

Sincerely yours,
[REDACTED]

cc: US Consumer Product Safety Commission
justification: The dishwasher exhibited sparking and a burning smell, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On the morning of Jan 20, 2013 we woke up and found the dishwasher was incredibly - dangerously - hot! I thought that opening the door would stop the heat, but it didn't work. By the time we realized the heater was still on, all of the plastic dishes in the unit were melted and ruined. My wife discovered that turning the unit off, turning it on and then turning off the "Heated Dry" control disabled the heating element and thereby stopped the overheating.

I started shopping for a new dishwasher and stumbled across CPSC recall notice #12-244 dated Aug. 9, 2012 on the Consumer Reports website. At first, I thought that my unit was covered under this recall, but it is not. The model number is on the list, but the serial number is not.

It may to be that the malfunction we experienced is different than the above referenced recall. Our malfunction appears to be due to a controller malfunction, and not "an electrical failure in the dishwasher's heating element" as described in CPSC Release #12-244. In our case, the dishwasher works without overheating if the "Heated Dry" option is turned off at the control panel.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted dishes) but no injuries, and the issue was resolved by adjusting settings, indicating it's unlikely to recur frequently.

incident_description:
We own an Frigidaire Gallery 30 inch. FGEF304DKFB model  - just a little over 1 year after owning this unit - the racks in the bottom oven no longer hold up when putting anything on them due to the cavity of the oven being defective / expanding.  This problem has led to multiple spills and presents a significant risk of burning of hands when trying to retrieve items that have spilled. Spilled food also results in smoke and fire inside the oven.

Frigidaire recommended we speak to a service provider for repair.  The service provider they recommended indicated that this problem could not be fixed and have had prior instances of this issue.

We feel this product is unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves burns from spilled food and potential fire hazards, indicating injury risk, and the problem is recurring based on service provider feedback.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidaire Gallery Range that has burners that will not shut off.  The 1st incident happened about a year and 1/2 ago, the front left burner would not shut off -- stayed on full blast.  had to unplug the range.  Warranty was over and had a repair technician come to fix.  The part and labor was cost prohibitive to repair, opted to disconnect and never use that burner, allowing us to continue using the rest of the range.  Last Saturday, a 2nd burner malfunctioned and will not shut off, the burner is on full blast when the range is plugged in.  Had to unplug and the range is inoperable.  

With a 2nd burner acting up on the same range, it made me wonder how many more of these are out there that are likely in the same condition.  This range is a fire hazard and safety hazard to say the least.  I felt I should bring this to your attention.  It is upsetting when you spend a lot of money for an appliance and it malfunctions.  However, a severe safety defect like my range has is not right.  This thing could have burned a house down had we not been home to deal with it right away.  

Appreciate your advice regarding any rights I may have.  I feel the manufacturer should be responsible for repairing this unit before someone gets hurt.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning range that poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Magic Bullet blender from Costco about a month ago. Over the weekend I made a smoothie containing ice and frozen fruits, plus water. I served myself and a friend. My friend pulled out from his mouth an extremely sharp shard of plastic that he almost swallowed, about 3/4 of an inch in length, and maybe a 1/4 inch maximum width. Had he swallowed it, it could have definitely caused perforation or tearing along the digestive tract. 

The piece fits into one of the four longitudinal, internal plastic ridges on the inside of the blender. I'm guessing the ridges are meant to provide structural support; however, they should probably be on the outside of the blender since they (apparently) shear off with the slightest of provocation.

He spit it out and I taped it to the registration card, which I planned to take back to Costco...but then thought I should report it to CPSC first.
justification: The incident involved a near-swallow of a sharp plastic shard that could have caused serious injury, but no actual injury occurred.

My husband then inspected the Baby Bullet, and confirmed that the gasket had indeed broken into pieces and was mixed in with my baby's food. The consumer stated that she used her electric range and when she turned the burners on the complete top becomes extremely hot. The consumer stated that she would turn one burner on and the complete top would become hot. She stated that she would have to turn the burner off and wait the range top to cool off. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they replaced the range for her on Sept 6, 2012 with another range of the same model. The consumer stated immediately after using the range she started to experience the same problem.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they sent a technician on Sept 20, 2012 and he informed her that the range could not be fixed. The consumer stated that the manufacturer informed her that they could not provide any remedy since itÃÂs out of the returned policy time frame.

incident_description:
My wife was using the range on the lowest setting late in the evening and left the kitchen for a few minutes.  When she returned the range was on high heat and contents of the pan was on fire.  She was not able turn the range off, and it remained on high heat until the power to the range was disconnected.   When the power was reconnected in the morning the range appeared to operate normally, but the cooktop was permanently discolored. 

Safety concern:  The range setting can spontaneously change, potentially causing a fire and burns.  This incident occurred at about 1:00 AM and I was sleeping.  We consider ourselves lucky to have caught the fire while it was small, and confined to the contents of the pan.  However, we are reluctant to use the range because the controls are not reliable and potentially dangerous. 

Range: Kenmore Elite 790.99124405
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, and the range's malfunction poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: I purchased a Maytag Electric Wall Oven Model# MEW5627DDW, Serial #11719305GE from Lowe's in Toledo, Ohio on August 25th, 2005. On September 15th, 2010 the oven was on and the oven spontaneously switched to broil, burning and igniting the food in the oven. I contacted Maytag and was told the control panel had failed. They admitted no liability, but discounted the part and I had a new panel installed. Yesterday (1/13/2013), the same failure occurred. I will re-contact Maytag. I believe this problem represents a serious fire hazard, as a spontaneous change from  "bake" to "broil" can obviously cause food to burn and ignite. If this has happened twice to me, I suspect it has happened to others. I would like your help in investigating this issue, and get the Company to respond appropriately. Many Thanks!
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard due to the oven spontaneously switching to broil, which could lead to injury if not addressed.

incident_description: I had a fire in my whirlpool refrigerator model number ED5PHEXNL00. According to the repair man who came to my house it is the compressor start device. I have pictures if you need them. The fire department was called when my wife came home from town and said it smelled like plastic burning. The fire department used a thermal image camera to find the location. They determined it to be coming from the refrigerator and shut it down. Once I got home I removed the back off the refrigerator and found the part had burned and fused itself to the compressor. This happened on 1-3-13. A technician is in the process of ordering parts. I am currently using my brothers refrigerator. Not sure if this is a recall item or not. I am also not sure if you need to know. Thankfully my wife came home when she did, who knows how bad it could have got.
justification: The incident involved a fire in a refrigerator, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Product: Krups F654 Waffle Maker purchased at Costco 75 Freshwater Blvd, Enfield, CT 06082 on 12/26 2012.

Grip handle became extremely hot and caused burns to fingers when opened. Smoke was visible from vertical slit opening when handle clips closed.

incident_description:
We purchased a new freestanding gas range, maker GE, Model JGB250DET2BB from Sears in November  of 2012.  The problem is the gas knobs turns on so easily, that it will come on with very little pressure and leak gas into the kitchen.  Someone brushing past the knob can flip it on, leaning over the stove to reach the oven controls will flip it on. There is the danger of setting yourself on fire or an explosion in the kitchen if you are cooking.  I was cooking on the left front burner and inadvertently turned on the right front burner. Luckily I smelled the gas before it set me on fire! 

After inspecting the stove, it appears the spring tension for the knobs is too light, thereby allowing you to just flip the knob on with your finger tip, or brush it with your coat or other body parts, and not even realize it has occurred. 
There is a video on you tube demonstrating exactly what occurs. 
We need this stove either replaced or repaired before we have a sever injury, fire or explosion. 
Thank you for your time. 
[redacted]
justification: The gas knobs can be easily turned on, posing a risk of gas leaks and potential fire or explosion, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Microwave failed to shut off after timer ran out. Loud buzzing continued and food continued to cook and began to burn. Luckily I was near the kitchen at the time and noticed it.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was noticed before any injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: As I was removing a Pyrex 13x9 glass pan from the serving table, I experienced a laceration on my left thumb and palm when the glassware broke in my hand. The glassware broke into two main sections with shards piercing my hand, requiring emergency care. This injury required three stitches to my thumb and one stitch to my palm, as well as antibiotics and a tetanus shot. Now, two months after this incident, the wounds have healed, but I cannot fully bend my thumb and it continues to be highly sensitive and I am seeking further medical attention.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring stitches and ongoing medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We've had this slow cooker for multiple years and have had good luck with it. But, over the past year we had the grey plastic handle, on the clear glass lid, crumble and fall apart while washing the lid. We did a temp repair job, since we needed to use the slow cooker, by placing a small bolt through the lid and putting two nuts on to have something to grab with a hot mitt. We just used the cooker again and I noticed the side handle is cracking and ready to fall off. All these plastic parts should be able to stand the heat temps that emit through the sides of a slow cooker. It has been a good cooker up until now with these problems, hate to have to buy a new one just because plastic parts are failing. There was a recall noted on another filed complaint on this site. I believe the recall was in 2005 which made it too old to affect that consumer and myself but thought I'd post my experience in hopes of warning other users of this model slow cooker. Thanks
justification: The incident involves plastic parts failing but no injury or harm reported, only inconvenience and potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
My wife and I own a Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Range, Model #790.7938...  We purchased it as a wedding gift for each other on May 6,  2005.  On Christmas morning (12/25/12) we were cooking muffins in the oven and heard popping and cracking from the kitchen.  My wife and I ran to the kitchen and found black smoke and flames coming out from the back of the clock and electronics.  I quickly turned off the oven and the flames stopped.  I then turned off the circuit breaker too.  We then pulled the oven away from the wall and turned off the gas.  Now the oven is locked like it is self cleaning mode and we cannot open the oven door to get the muffin pans out.   I am a electrical engineer who designs circuit boards that operate high voltage and high current energy.  This type of design failure is unacceptable and consumers should be warned of the inherent danger in these products.  

As it was Christmas morning when this failed my wife and I gave thanks that we were home when it did so no one was injured and nothing other than the range was broken.  Many time since we have reflected that one of the features we use routinely is the delayed start function, imagine if this failure mode happened one of the days we used this feature.  We could have come home to our house on fire!
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries, and the potential for a house fire if unattended increases the likelihood.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Oven 790.77513800 front glass shattered while not in use.  Told by Sears representative the glass is suppose to shatter in small pieces without shards. In my case there were shards. 
See many internet threads where same incident has occurred and Sears says no "manufacturing" recalls have been issued.

incident_description:
Purchased a Kenmore Elite Gas Range Model 77523 in October 2008 (stainless steel)
On January 15, 2012 the glass on the oven shattered in a million little pieces for no reason at all
called Sears and they stated they have never heard of a problem with the stove
I am grateful none of my children or pets were in the kitchen

justification: The glass shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Kenmore built in dishwasher's control unit on upper part of door caught fire.  We were in the kitchen and were alerted by sizzling sounds.  When we opened the dishwasher door, smoke and flames shot out and water sprayed over the kitchen since the cycle failed to stop.  We were able to shut the unit down using the wall switch.   The fire then extinguished itself.  There was no  damage other than to the machine itself, however had we not been in the room we most likely would have had a kitchen fire.  This machine is 8.5 years old, so failure is not a big surprise.  Nevertheless, the possibility of failure by burning up represents an unsafe design feature.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury or damage beyond the machine itself, and the age of the machine suggests possible but not certain future occurrences.

incident_description:
I STRONGLY SUGGEST THAT THIS PRODUCT BE REMOVED FROM THE SHELVES ASAP.

My wife was using the hand cranked Snoopy Sno-cone Machine to make grandkids sno-cones. She had made the first sno-cone with 3 ice cubes and gently scooped the shaved ice out with the plastic spoon that comes with the machine. She then made my 2nd grandchild one and was watching them eat the sno-cones when she noticed a gold piece of metal inside the sno-cone that my 1st grandchild was eating. It was cylinder-shaped. It seems to be about 1/4 inch high and "ragged looking" around the rim as if it had been torn apart. She then noticed that it was one of the two rivets that are inside of the metal ice compartment. The jagged metal edges on the torn-off rivet would make it very dangerous if swallowed!

 I STRONGLY SUGGEST THAT THIS PRODUCT BE REMOVED FROM THE SHELVES ASAP.

incident_description:
On Christmas Eve 2012ÃÂ..Our Kenmore Trio Refrigerator started a near fire in our home!  The lights inside the fridge got so hot they started to smoke and melt all the plastic surrounding the unit....even with the doors closed. incident_description:
I was doing my holiday baking on Friday, December 21 and the large oven had been at 350 degrees for about two hours.  I was in another room when I heard beeps coming from the range and went to investigate.  I noticed the oven had dropped to 290 degrees and was in the pre-heat mode trying to get back to the correct temperature.  I continued my baking and this dropping of temperature continued until I finished about 2 hours later.
I called Sears and reported this problem and tried to see if this oven was on a recall list, since this is the second time we have had a similar incident.  I was told by Sears there is no recall and that I needed to talk with [REDACTED], who they said manufactured the unit.  I called the number Sears provided, and [REDACTED] said I needed to go through Sears.  All Sears could suggest was sending a technician out to look at the unit, but since the extended warranty had expired, it would cost between $79 to $239 dollars.  I decided not to incur any additional cost at the time, so did not schedule any service appointment.
Since this range has been questionable, we connected it to a power strip after the first incident in 2011 and turn it off whenever we are going to be gone for any extended period of time.  Saturday, December 22 we left in the early morning to visit family and friends and returned about 5:30 p.m.  Later that evening we turned the range back on and heated something on the stove top about 9:00 p.m.
We were in bed asleep at 10:00 p.m. when we were awaken by the kitchen smoke alarm.  The large oven had turned itself on, possibly set to the self cleaning mode, and it was bright orange.  we immediately switched off the power, but it seemed like it was still heating, so we turned off the gas to the unit.  I had cookie trays and a skillet in the oven, which were darkened and must have started to smoke which caused the alarm to sound. We have not turned on the gas or the electricity to the unit since.
I called Sears on Wednesday, December 26, and talked with the Customer Solutions Department, and the most they could offer me was a 10%, up to $100, rebate on a new unit.  They did fill out a Product Safety Form, which they indicated was an internal report that would be sent to the Recall Department.
We had a similar issue with this range in 2011 when the smaller oven was turning on by itself.  A technician came out and within minutes of me explaining the problem knew exactly what the issue was and told me I had to replace the oven control board. The technician was very familiar with the problem and had seen it other times.  In May, 2011 we had the control board replaced.
At that time I had also made a report to the Consumer Product Safety Commission - Report Number [REDACTED], and [REDACTED] had come to our home to investigate the issue.
Presently, the range is still in the kitchen, without electricity or gas.  I have researched the internet and have seen where others have experienced the same issue.  To date, I have not had any further communication with Sears.
justification: The incident involved the oven turning on by itself and causing smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The problem has recurred multiple times, indicating a possible issue.

incident_description: I turned on my oven and set tempurature to 275 degrees. after it beeped to indicate ready, i put in a rack of ribs. After about 10 minutes I began to smell smoke. I went to the kitchen and found smoke pouring from the oven vent, and the broiler,which I had not turned on, was on high! I pushed the off button repeatedly but the range would not turn off. I had to go to the breaker panel and pull the breakers to shut the range down. This thing could have set my house on fire and i'm really concerned that this product could kill someone.

incident_description: Cooking on the LG double oven gas range produced burning odors which I could not at first figure out where it was coming from.  After a few weeks I noticed that the handles on my pots and pans were browning.  One day as I was boiling some water using the superBoiler burner, the handle twisted from being weakened from the heat coming from the burner.  The flames shoot exceptionally high on this range in order to reach/heat the pan.  The grid is higher than a lot of other manufacturers.  The high level of the grid means the fire has a longer reach to get to the pan, so the space in between leaves more opportunity for anything like pot holders, scarfs, long sleeves, pan handles, etc. to receive direct heat, intense heat or flame contact.  And I have experienced all of this.  This is not a safe product for children or adults to be around.  I am especially concerned about my pan handles that seem to have melted away - making them extremely weak and risky to handle or even to continue using.  The fumes from the melting handles eventually give you some warning that something is amiss with this range, but you may not make the connection right away because in my case this was a new stove so I thought it was burning off its newness as I was told by the installer that it would take awhile for that particular smell to go away.  Handling pans with weakened handles makes it dangerous to cook on because the handle may tilt or worst, give way all together and spill hot food or liquid on-not just the cook, but anyone else nearby.  Luckily I only received burns on my fingers and wrist trying to safely get the pans from the stove to the table when I experienced a sudden wobbling in the handle.  I now have to replace all of my pans to be sure the handles don't just give out while cooking or trying to move them from one spot to another.   Please recall this product or let others know about this unsafe feature.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to fingers and wrists due to weakened pan handles, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests frequent exposure to high heat and flame contact, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
Here's an email I sent to the manufacture and never heard back.
[REDACTED],

Yesterday I came home and noticed that my Belique Pot Lid was cracked in tons of pieces! Crazy. The even crazier part about this is nothing fell on it, no wind blew it over or anything. After some research I discovered,

Spontaneous glass fractures are due to the presence of nickel sulphide inclusions. The inclusions in a typical glass batch are rare. Nickel sulphide has a delayed phase transformation. Nickel sulphide has a high temperature and a low temperature form. In ordinary glass, nickel sulphide inclusions do not cause problems because the transformation occurs as the glass is cooled slowly during manufacture. However, the transformation is sluggish and when glass is rapidly cooled in the manufacturing process, the nickel sulphide remains trapped in its high temperature form until some years later when its transformation spontaneously breaks the glass.

I have enclosed photos. What you see inside the pot is glass and crumbs from cleaning up the broken glass everywhere.

Can you send me a new one?

Thank you,
[REDACTED],

SpontaneousÃÂjpg
justification: The incident involves a cracked pot lid with no reported injury, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) based on the description of spontaneous glass fractures being uncommon.

incident_description:
Product:  Anchor Hocking 4-quart glass mixing bowl purchased within the past five years

I was baking pumpkin bread. After mixing the ingredients for one loaf, I decided to bake an additional loaf and placed the glass mixing bowl in the sink to wash it before mixing the ingredients for the second loaf. The white porcelain sink in which I placed the bowl was protected by a [REDACTED] sink mat. I ran hot water into the bowl. As the water was running into the bowl, I turned away from the sink to put a utensil in a nearby drawer. When my back was turned, the bowl broke, exploding into 50 or more shards of varying sizes, a few of which were expelled out of the sink onto the floor.

I was not injured in any way.

There were no unusual temperature variations that could have caused this breakage, i.e., the room temperature was approximately 72; the bowl had been at room temperature for some time; my water heater is set at the "A" setting; the water I ran into the bowl was not at the maximum temperature possible on the kitchen faucet (not as hot as it might have been).

Additionally, I have not dropped or cracked the bowl or banged utensils against it. I have used the bowl only as a mixing bowl, i.e., I have never put it in the oven or microwave or on the stove top.

I have no logical explanation for why the bowl broke.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely, [REDACTED]

P.S.  Unfortunately, your photo-upload function is not working; hence, I will submit this report without photos.
justification: The bowl broke, but no one was injured, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 1 because the bowl broke without any unusual temperature variations or other logical explanation.

The bottom of the cup has a sticker which says "Lifetime Brands, Garden City NY, Made in China."  The rim around the bottom has the Cuisinart name, and "Patent Pending."

One mug did fine, but the lid to the other mug suddenly, with considerable force blew off the mug dumping the contents in our kitchen, and to a minor extent on my hands.  We assumed I must not have had the lid screwed on correctly, so my wife made a second cup of coffee, filled the mug, carefully screwed on the lid, then pushed the button which seals the cup, turned it upside down and the lid blew off again.  We can and will return these to the store where we purchased them, but our concern is what if this happened when someone was trying to drink from it?  Clearly very serious burns would result.  Worse yet, if it occurred while someone was driving their car, which is it's purpose, the results could, and probably would be devastating.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Elite 30" Double Oven Freestanding Smooth Cooktop Range 11/16/08, Model # 665.98019801, Serial # 11311098PA.  This model number was provided to me through a Sears "chat" about parts - the number on the part is 2298019.

Wednesday evening, 12/26/12, I heard a random beeping.  Upon investigating to find the source of the beeping, it was discovered that the broiler on the bottom oven was on Hi.  After turning it off, I thought perhaps I bumped the button to turn it on while wiping down the stove, even though that didn't seem likely since it had never happened before.

The next morning (Thursday, 12/27/12), when I came downstairs, I immediately noticed a "hot" smell like something was burning.  The air was very acrid and my eyes were burning.  I once again discovered the broiler unit was on Hi, and blazing away!  I pushed the button to turn it off and opened windows and doors trying to get things cooled down.  Everything around the stove was so hot, I was worried something might catch fire.  

Baffled and scared, I went to the computer in the next room and started searching the internet for broilers coming on spontaneously and was horrified to find that there had been a recall for the smooth cooktop burners coming on by themselves, but not for the broilers doing it, EVEN THOUGH THERE WERE MANY, MANY REPORTS OF THIS HAPPENING!

While I was at the computer, I heard the broiler click and turn back on again, so I went back in the kitchen and turned it off.  This continued happening at shorter and shorter intervals until I had no choice but to turn off the breaker in order to keep the broiler from turning on.

I did some more research and concluded this may have happened because a Broiler Relay switch was stuck and needed replaced.  So I called Sears to ask about repair and to find out if they had any other reports of this happening with this particular model.  Their lack of customer service was appalling; the information I finally received was that it was not part of a recall and I would have to pay for the repair.  I was concerned that since this did not seem to be an isolated incident but Sears was not recognizing that there was a problem, the repair would have been to replace the failed part with the same thing, possibly with a much more catastrophic outcome.

I telephoned the local Sears Hardware Store where I purchased the range, but could not even get through to someone in the Appliance Department.

Next, I checked the website for Sears parts to find out how much the part cost and if it had been replaced by a new part.  When I could not locate my model, I used their "chat" function to get some help.  Their response was to try to sell me a broiler element using a model number that was "close".  After much insisting, I was finally given a model number that allowed me to search for schematics / diagrams for my actual range and found the part runs close to $300!  It did not indicate that this part was anything different than what was already in the unit, so I chose to not go this route.

This is not a cheap range.  As a matter of fact, it was my dream range and I bought it the same place I have purchased almost every other appliance my whole life - Sears.  While it is hard to accept that the Sears I knew and loved is gone, it is even harder to believe that they know about and refuse to be responsible for an issue with their product that could have cost me my home, my family, and my life.

Others need to know about this problem and that it could happen.  I am purchasing a new range - not from Sears - as I do not feel this range is safe or replacing the part will make it so.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning broiler that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

THE SUPERINTENDENT IN MY APARTMENT BUILDING DISCONNECTED THE GAS SUPPLY. HOWEVER, THE IGNITER CONTINUED TO BURN. HE HAD TO DISCONNECT THE POWER LINE IN ORDER FOR THE IGNITER TO TURN OFF. Two service calls were made--Whirlpool and Home Depot insist a fifth service call must be made in order to repair and reassess the problem.

12/2/12: WHILE BAKING, THE OVEN FLAME WENT UP AND DOWN UNCONTROLLABLY FOR A PERIOD OF ABOUT 30 MINUTES UNTIL I TURNED THE OVEN OFF. This was clearly NOT a matter of the thermostat raising and lowering the flame in order to maintain a normal baking temperature. (No service call was made.)

January 2012: Within a week of purchasing the oven, WHEN I TURNED THE OVEN ON TO BAKE, THERE WAS A POPPING NOISE AND THEN A FIERY GLOW AGAINST THE KITCHEN WALL BEHIND THE OVEN, ON THE RIGHT SIDE, NEAR THE BASEBOARD. Two service calls were made and the problem did not seem to recur.

The consumer has been in the engineering profession for about 23 years.  

UPDATE:
"I am an electrical engineer and former engineering executive. I am very familiar with product safety testing
and fault analysis. In my professional opinion, the fault clearly occurred in the power distribution connector
section of the control circuit board. I fire was hot enough to breach the flame retardant plastic enclosure below
the printed circuit board. If I were not present at home at the time, it is likely that the fire would have rapidly
spread. "

incident_description: The incident involves Cuisinart CSB-76 Smartstick Hand Blender. Severe finger laceration requiring approximately 9 stitches occurred after the device failed to turn off while being disassembled. It is possible for the main power switch to be in the "on" position, allowing the blade to continue turning while a second "detach" button is pressed. The detach button is not properly designed, because when pressed, that button should de-energize the appliance before it can be disassembled. I note there have been at least 3 other similar incidents located on the CPSC website, but could find no corrective measures or recalls to date.  I recommend that the company be required to recall these devices and install a properly engineered safety interlock device that makes it impossible to energize the blender while it is being disassembled. This would make it impossible for injuries such as this to occur in the future. The instruction manual's advice to unplug the device is important, but fails to meet widely accepted safety engineering standards. Please advice on CPSC's action in this matter. Thank you. Sincerely, [REDACTED]
justification: Severe finger laceration requiring stitches indicates an injury (severity 3). Multiple similar incidents suggest the occurrence likelihood is likely (4).

incident_description: I really don't know how to describe this other then the pan shattered on the counter top. The larger parts were about 2 1/2 to 3 inches apart from each other some smaller parts were found 7-10 feet away. We did not take any pictures we just cleaned up the area and went about our life. I am reporting this due to the news feed on the "Kitchen calamity: Reports of shattering cookware on the rise" found on the web. Just wanted to throw our information out there on this. justification: The slow cooker's exterior reached a high temperature, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Both left burners blow out when oven door opened and then closed.  if not noticed, the house fills up with gas.  House full of gas has happened twice.  Burners blowing out has happened on numerous occasions.
justification: The incident involves gas filling the house, which poses a significant risk of explosion or asphyxiation, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: The knobs for the top burners for a newly purchased Fridaire gas stove require no more than 1-2 mm of depression before they easily turn, releasing gas into the kitchen.  We have had the stove for only a week and already the kitchen has filled with gas three times.  The slightest bump or brush rotates the knobs turning on the gas with no discernable noise or effort.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage, which poses a significant risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: The right back burner knob is in the off position, yet the burner is still on. Also, the temperature of this burner doesn't match the back left burn when on the same setting.
justification: The burner being on when the knob is off poses a potential hazard, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Kenmore Electric Range Model Number:665-95802000 has a problem with the broiler element relays sticking on and not turning off until the power to the range is terminated with the circuit breaker.  Pressing off/cancel button on controls does not fix problem.  You can sometimes bump the panel where the relays are located and get them to release and switch off.  This has happened on at least one other occasion for a total of two incidents with this range.  There are many reports of similar problems with various Kenmore ranges like this.  I couldn't find a recall on this model but I wanted to add it to a list in case enough units had problems to investigate.  A burner until that won't turn off is a fire hazard that can lead to loss of or property.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard due to a malfunctioning broiler element, which could lead to property damage but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: I was running my Dishwasher, when my kitchen filled up with smoke, and then the Dishwasher stopped working.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned and produced smoke, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Sparks, glow, popping, crackling, and smoke came from behind the electronics panel.  This lasted for7-10 seconds and the breaker tripped.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: I have had numerous times when the front right burner will turn itself on a very high setting, while cooking.  I couldn't manually turn the temperature down, unless I shut the burner off.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says when she came home to a smoke filled house.  She says the motor were burned and melted.  The consumer says it was on when she left her home but off at the time she arrived back.  

She says it was on approximately 30 minutes.  She says that the control panel was also blackened as well as the door to open the unit.  She says she does not think that the cycle was not finished because there was a pool of water at the bottom.  

She has yet to contact the manufacturer.  The dishwasher falls just outside of the recall for Release # 05-123.
justification: The incident involved a smoke-filled house and a damaged dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Cuisinart DCC-690 series Grind & Brew 10-Cup Automatic Coffee Maker; unit malfunctioned (grinder spontaneously turned on), and then caught fire.  Large amounts of smoke emanated from base, under burner.  I unplugged it and removed it from the house.  Once unplugged, the smoke eventually stopped.

Over the two or three weeks prior to this incident, the unit would often turn on or off by itself.  Sometimes, the grinder would spontaneously start up.  More recently, the grinder would spontaneously start and not stop after the normal amount of time, running indefinitely.
justification: The unit malfunctioned and caught fire, but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The prior spontaneous behavior suggests a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: We have owned the Cuisinart Griddler for a few years. The cooking plates are removable for cleaning, and can be reversed. The clips that hold the plates on seem to have lost their integrity, the upper plate fell off several times when the top was lifted during its last use, causing a serious burn hazard had I been flipping the food that was on the cooking surface.
justification: The incident caused a serious burn hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: It was 2 am when I heard a loud quick boom.  When i walked into the kitchen I noticed that the glass from my gas oven had exploded outwards.  It was not on and had not been used in over 3 days.  It was spontaneous and quite scary.  Thank god no one was near the oven at the time.  I had just bought the general electric (GE) gas range oven 3 years ago!! BAd product! They came over and fixed it for half off entire parts and labor.
justification: No one was near the oven when the glass exploded, so there was no injury, but it was a significant incident.

incident_description: During filling of coffee maker water came pouring out the bottom, steam and could smell something burning. Unit was unplugged and allowed to cool at which time I removed the top cover to see if it was something I could repair. After discovering what parts were needed I found online that there was (or is) an open recall on my coffee maker for the exact problem I am having pertaining to the pour in bowl melting. The release number is 05-189. I have tried to contact the company by phone and e-mail with no answer or response.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the known recall and multiple reports of the same issue.

incident_description: I placed a glass pyrex container labeled microwave safe in the microwave for 7seconds to heat pancakes. After roughly 5 seconds, the dish exploded.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no mention of injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Kenmore Dishwasher Model #587.15173400 started smoking from the control panel/handle while NOT in operation.  After loading some dirty dishes, the door was closed and minutes later, smoke started billowing out of the handle while all the lights on the control panel blinked.  The front of the control panel was very hot and the unit smelled of burnt plastic/electric fire.  Sears' Customer Service transferred my call around a bit, and ultimately, because there was no recall for this item, stated that my only avenue for resolution was to pay for one of their technicians to come look at the unit.  

I'd rather just buy another dishwasher from anywhere other than Sears.  Had we not seen/smelled the smoke immediately and cut off the power to the unit, there's no telling what damage could have been done.  Sears didn't seem to think this was outside of the norm, and in fact, I've found multiple incidences of this same occurrence on various forums and websites.  Truly unfortunate that a company wouldn't offer a better resolution considering what kind of damage could have been done due to their faulty product.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents have been reported multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Kenmore smooth top range: Oven set to 400 degrees, unit got so hot it gave error code E2 F3 but did not shut off, just kept getting hotter.  Top oven burner on and red hot.  Top of range extremely hot, strong burning smell (worse than when using self clean feature).  Unit would not shut off with controls, had to shut off power to range at circuit panel.    Same problem got more expensive units recalled while reports online show these also have the issue.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that became extremely hot and emitted a strong burning smell, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Maytag Gemini range upper oven door exploded while not in use.  The oven had not been used in at least 24 hours.  Pieces of glass filled the upper and lower ovens,
justification: The oven door exploded, causing damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I was cooking with a fairly new Pyrex casserole dish.  I had just put it in the oven and heard a strange sound.  When I looked in the oven, the dish had exploded after being at 350 degrees for only 6 minutes.  My dish had exploded into glass shards on the left side.  I had just purchased it 1 month ago and had used it only 5-6 times.  I am very concerned now about Pyrex dish safety.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but there was no mention of injury, only concern about safety.

incident_description: I was cooking Chicken Corn Soup in a large 6 quart saucepan by Cuisinart, and turned it down to simmer.  The lid had been on the pot halfway when it was cooking but when I turned it down to simmer I put the lid on completely, and about two minutes later, the glass lid exploded.
justification: The glass lid exploded, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: Baking Roasted Vegetables in a Pyrex Pan and took it out of the oven and landed it on the granite countertop in a normal fashion, and it exploded, sending glass shards everywhere just as my guests were arriving.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex pan causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description: I was using a ISI Twist and Sparkle.  The bottle was not at the expiration date nor was it damaged.  The bottle exploded, the charger shot through a glass light fixture at which point glass and plastic flew at me, embedding shards in my skin.  I had to pull the shard out and had a large bruise.  The light was broken.
justification: The incident resulted in injury with shards embedded in the skin and a large bruise, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I was microwaving some left over cold meat gravy...after a few minutes, it exploded inside the microwave.
justification: The incident involved an explosion inside the microwave but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Upon using the newly purchased snoopy sno-cone machine two brass colored rivets fell off the ice shaver and into the edible snow cone.  It wasn't until my daughter started consuming the sno-cone both rivets were found.  Thankfully they were not ingested.
justification: Rivets fell into the snow cone but were not ingested, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Soup was being heated up on our Kenmore electrical  stove in a [REDACTED] pot.  Only the front left burner was in use.  It was on high and the pot was on the stove for about 1 minute when there was a loud boom and large flames. We doused the fire quickly.  We turned the knob to the off position but the red surface light still indicated it was on so we then turned off the power to that electrical outlet.  The pot ended up with a hole on the bottom where it appears the burner cut through. The burner itself was destroyed, it looks like it just burst/popped.  We purchased the burner from Home Depot about 2 years ago.   The food was not burned or scorched just splattered on the wall.   No other area of the pot was burned except for that section with the hole.  Then we noticed on the right side of the stove near the rear burner, there was a black burn line.
