That is  where the electrical wires run.  We cannot lift up the stove top, it is burned shut on the rear right side.  The burn line is not on the stove top itself but rather down the right side.  It is about 1-2 inches in length.
justification: The incident involved a fire and equipment damage but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Our Maytag wide-by-side refrigerator Model# MZD2766G was purchased in 2002. Last week we woke up from the smell of smoke, I went downstairs and saw that our kitchen and family room were filling with thick smoke that smelled like an electrical fire. Called 911, firemen came and after several minutes realized that the smoke was coming from the refrigerator. It was something behind the refrigerator back panel that was smoldering.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We used our dishwasher this am and when we returned home at 1:30pm, I opened the dishwasher to get a bowl and it was burning HOT. I didn't think anything of it, just thought the dishwasher must have just finished drying. We began to smell a burning smell in the house. Later at 7:30 pm I opened to get more dishes out and it smelt of burning/melting plastic and the dishes were still burning HOT.  The heating element will not shut off. I then opened and shut dishwasher, hit cancel to see if it would turn off and that didn't work. My husband then went and turned the circuit breaker on and off and half an hour later it still was on and burning HOT. He then went and shut the circuit breaker all together.  We researched recalls and Maytag does have recalls for this problem and it says with serial numbers ending in JL which ours is but when I go to submit recall it tells me that it doesn't qualify for recall.
justification: The dishwasher's heating element malfunctioned, posing a burn risk, but no injury occurred. The issue is known and has recalls, indicating it's a possible but not certain occurrence.

incident_description: Our GE Profile Gas Cook-top (Model: JGP975BEK2BB, Serial No:TV702803Q) had the child safety switch break in May 2012.  It required a new switch harness (the computer brain of the unit which controls the electric start & safety switch).  In November 2012, the new switch harness failed again.  This time it started trying to light all the burners at 3 am.  Luckily my husband was awake with our baby & heard the unit trying to light itself.  He could not stop it, so he had to unplug the unit from the electrical socket.  Although the gas was not on, the main burner sparks on the outside of the housing each time any of the burners attempt to light.  Had anything flammable been left on the stove, we could have had a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cook-top that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I have an LG electric range and from what I have read on the consumer reports it looks like the model LRE30453ST is on the recall list, However when I called LG the representative states that the serial number (105 MMBE10501) does not include this model.
I have had problems with the range for several months, with either not turning on or off when buttons pressed. I had several times that the burners did not switch off after the button pressed. Several of the burners stopped working all together, and this afternoon again it did not want to switch off and I had to pull the circuit breaker of the house because I could not get the temperature to go down or switch off. After that I was able to use two burners again, however now none of the burners work.
justification: The range malfunction poses a safety hazard (burners not turning off), but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
(12/1/2012) The consumer stated that she told her son to turn on the stove to heat up some chicken. He pushed the indicator up which automatically goes to 350  degrees. The stove immediately  made an explosion noise and sparks came from the electronic clock where you increase the temperature. After the explosion the clock fell into the top part of the stove. The consumer stated that she tried to turn the stove on and nothing works.


(12/1/2012) The consumer stated that she called Sears to get the stove replaced. A repair person was scheduled to come out on 12/4 but did not show up.  The consumer stated that she call Sears again 12/4/2012. She was given the CPSC number to call.

Injury - just received a quick sohck.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and sparks from the stove, resulting in a quick shock, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had his electric range oven on at a temperature of 350 degrees for approximately 1 hour. The consumer stated that he noticed smoke and sparks were being emitted from the back of the range. The consumer stated that ashes were going through the vent of oven, because the temperature became so hot that it burnt the food inside. 

The consumer stated that he immediately turned off the circuit breaker off. He stated that he opened the windows and doors to air out the smoke. The consumer stated that it took approximately 40-45 minutes for the smoke to dissipate. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured.  

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed the consumer that they would send a technician to service the range on 12/5/2012. The consumer stated that they informed him that he would have to pay for the repairs. 

The consumer stated that this product should be investigated do to the safety hazard that it poses to the consumer.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks but no injuries, and the consumer took immediate action to mitigate the situation.

incident_description:
Woke up this morning and the kitchen smelt bad, I noticed black residue on top left of Kenmore elite dishwasher
665.16052400, dishwasher appear to be burned out.

Did some research and this is apparently common, but very troubling, a dishwasher is not supposed to burn, this was the control panel burning not say a rag that we put inside , nothing inside was burned.  We routinely run the machine at night while we sleep as it is the best time, and many times when we leave home, the house could have burned down 

Very troubling there is no recall, Sears says they will send a technician at my expense who will tell me the panel needs replacing, this is not about the machine, if the panel had just stopped working after 5 years (the machine is 7 years old) then I guess that was its life, but it should not catch fire.
justification: The dishwasher's control panel burned out, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description: Oneida 12" skillet with glass top with vent hole in top.  The glass top cracked into a million pieces while saute-ing.  The glass didn't shoot out but was more like a windshield that stays together.  When I tried to remove the lid, the knob on the top came free and then the pieces fell into the skillet.
justification: The glass top cracked but did not cause injury, and the incident was contained without further harm.

incident_description: "Sodastream Soda Machine exploded while adding the carbonation.   The back and front of the machine blew off across the kitchen and water everywhere.   The bottom of the bottle blew completely off.  VERY DANGEROUS.   My Adult son could have been serious hurt and if it were my youngest it could have impaled his eyes.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing significant damage and potential for serious injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Glass Pyrex baking dish exploded when I took it out of the oven. Shards of glass flew everywhere, and there were hundreds of pieces.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish with glass shards flying, but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
GE MONOGRAM DISHWASHER STARTED SMELLING,SMOKING LIKE ELECTRICAL FIRE AND IT WAS. DC ELECTRICAL CURRENT TO DISHWASHER.  CLEARED SMOKE FROM HOUSE WITH VENT FAN 
CALLED GE AND THEY ARE SENDING REPAIR TECHNICIAN TO FIX PROBLEM.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Preheated oven to 350 degrees, placed a room temperature 9 x 13 Pyrex glass baking dish with handle cutouts filled with room temperature ingredients into my oven.  After a few minutes I heard a noise and discovered the dish had exploded in my oven.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no mention of injury, making it a non-injury incident. Such occurrences are unlikely but possible with improper use of glass bakeware.

incident_description: put the lid in the sink, on a towel because it's glass,  there was a loud pop the lid exploded, the knob at the top flew accross the room, this has happened two times.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass lid with no reported injury, and it has happened twice, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
After allowing a large batch of rice pudding to cool for 15 minutes on the stove, I poured it into the 9" x 13" Pyrex baking dish, which was on my countertop and was at room termperature.  The pudding was still very warm at that point, but had cooled considerably from the time I stopped cooking it.  Everything seemed fine at first.  Then just after I had walked away from the counter area where the pan was, I first heard a slow cracking sound, followed by an explosion of the glass which sent the glass forcefully flying not only throughout the kitchen, but also into the adjoining dining room, hallway, and family room.  Had I still been standing in front of the counter, I would have been seriously injured, but what was even more chilling was to think if a child had been standing near the counter, the child would have been blinded or even killed by the explosive force of the glass. 

I have used Pyrex baking dishes for more than 45 years, and had never had a problem with them until this incident, even when pouring boiling water into a Pyrex measuring cup or bowl.  It is my understanding that the Pyrex ingredients were changed after the license was sold by Corning Glass, and that the new "formula" was supposed to improve the product.  However, I suspect that the reason the ingredients were changed  was for lowering productions costs and increasing profits.  I do not believe this new Pyrex has been adequately tested before putting it on the market.  I purchased the baking dish the same day as the incident from the Wegman's supermarket in Niagara Falls, New York.  If you require an exact date, I may be able to have the supermarket verify the date of my purchase.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of glass that could have caused serious injury or death, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I placed hot rice into a glass baking dish, put a serving spoon into it, and placed the glass top on the dish to keep the rice warm while the family had salad.  The dish was placed on a counter top behind the table. The lid of the dish exploded sending glass pieces into the backs of the people on that side of the table and showering over their heads and between them onto the table top.  Only the top broke.  The bottom of the bowl was fine.  Most of the glass was found in little bead like forms, but numerous tiny shards were found in the table cloth, rug, and clothing of the people sitting close to the dish.  Had I placed the dish on the table, the explosive action would have been toward the faces of the family and could have been disastrous.  I never thought this would happen!
Feels really unsafe to me.  We were lucky.
justification: Glass shards caused injuries to people, but no deaths occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it requires specific conditions like placing hot rice in a glass dish with a lid.

incident_description: I was baking a potato dish in the oven at 350 degrees.  When it was done I brought it out to cool and I placed it on a trivet.  About 15 minutes later we all heard a loud crash.  The dish had completely shattered.  Thankfully no other food/people were around so the only damage was to the potato dish.  This was the first time using this baking pan.
justification: The incident involved a shattered baking dish but no injuries or damage beyond the dish itself, and it was the first time using the pan.

incident_description: I was using a purex glass 9 x 13 baking dish and I was baking chicken breasts and rice. I went to pull out the dinner and the glass pan broke in several big chunks and glass shards went to the bottom of the oven. I heard this pop sound as I bent down to lift the dish out of the oven and looked down to see that the pan had exploded. I wasn't hurt, but it scared me. It was not an old pan, but a newer one.
justification: The glass pan broke, causing a scare but no injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
I was frying eggs on the dual element burner of my stove, and suddenly I heard a loud pop, and saw sparks flying.  I turned it off.   The glass didn't appear cracked.  I used the burner later and noticed the inner part of the element was dead (not glowing red as usual)

UPDATE: I just opened up the smooth top surface of the range, and saw a wire that had shorted to the metal frame, scorching and melting away the metal where it contacted the frame.  The wire insulation was melted , and the metal wire inside was melted.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a short circuit, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: About 6 months ago our Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator 795.77253601 interior light bulbs remained on all day with the doors securely closed. Light fixture melted and interior roof bubbled, contents inside warm. I removed fixtured, ordered replacement light fixture and light door switches, replaced all. It worked fine for about 3 months then it occured again but we caught it before the complete melt down. Now just removed the bulbs. I changed the light switches again but that did not correct the issue.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted light fixture, bubbled interior) but no injury or death. The issue recurred after initial repair, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
On Dec. 30,2012 my kenmore stove began making loud cracking and popping sounds after I had turned on the warm and hold element.  The stove then caught fire.  The back was burnt.  The mother boards destroyed extensive electrical damage to the stove.  Sears insists on repairing where I want a new one.  They will repair with rebuilt boards as they do not have new parts.  Presently the CPSC has a number of these stoves on recall ours is not inculded but should be expanded to include this model as well.  Our model number is 790.96613402 purchased in 2004.
I have read many stories with similiar results from this Sears model.  I would like to see the recall expanded to protect others and myself.  I am thankful that my husband and I sat in the kitchen to have coffee while we kept breakfast warm waiting for our two duaghters to get up. Had it been a weekday or my older daughter making herself breakfast perhaps this letter would have a tragic ending instead of a concerned ending that requires the CPSC to further expand this recall to ensure the safety of all consumers who who have bought these stoves, one tragic result is one too many.
justification: The stove caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries, and similar incidents have been reported with this model.

incident_description:
I have an old microwave - I just went to kitchen and it had turned itself on - very hot and smoking, I don't know how long it was running for - could have been hours

Samsung
model# MW650WA
serial# 7MBT805614F

now unplugged and reported to samsung
justification: The microwave turned itself on and was smoking, indicating a malfunction, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I turned on my GE Range to cook a ham. after couple of minutes I saw sparks and a flame in the oven. The lower heating element looked like an arc welder, it was on fire and sparking. The time display was flashing like crazy. I turned the oven off but the fire did not go out.
I pulled the lower drawer out so I could reach the electrical plug and I unplugged it. The fire eventually went out. I went to a appliance parts store and bought a replacement lower heating element for $35. I installed it. I plugged the oven in and it was flashing code "F3". The oven would not heat up. I did research on-line and was directed to check the resistance of the temperature probe, I did this and the ohms were 1,083. This indicated the probe was "good". The next possible correction was to replace the control board. Since the part cost was approximately $250 I made the decision to buy a new range and have the GE hauled away. We are a family of 5 and are fortunate that we were in the kitchen and acted quickly. Our house could have burnt down.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven, which was quickly controlled without injury, but posed a significant risk to property.

incident_description:
GE Profile Dishwasher Model: PDW9980N00SS Serial: AM859855B

The unit was in the middle of a wash cycle and caught fire. The fire was in the control module and wiring harness located in the door. It appears that some steam or moisture had made its way into the door and into the control module or wire ends/plug causing a short. The unit was damaged beyond repair.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but there was no mention of injury or death, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but do occur.

incident_description: Didhwasher caught on fire and was destroyed.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and was destroyed, indicating property damage but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have a newer whirlpool slide in gas stove, approximately 3 years, its model GW397LXUB05. I want to alert you to what appears to be a manufacture defect in the assembly and routing of the gas tubing line that runs up the right side of the stove to the 4 burner connection point. I smelled gas in my home around the stove on 10-13-12, a very minor smell of gas but I isolated it to the stove on the right side. After doing the soap suds procedure on the common valve connection points in the stove with no evidence of leakage I then proceeded to trace the path of the gas tubing line mentioned above. What I found is that the oven door spring that mounts on the right side of the stove was causing the problem. When the door is opened and closed it rubs up and down the inner side of approximately one inch of the gas tubing. It had scratched a one inch slice in the tube over the past few years and finally put a small puncture in it. My entire house could have blown up if the stove were in use and the oven door spring continued to dig deeper into this gas tube. I would like this issue identified by whirlpool as a problem and have this stove recalled / serviced. I have pictures of the side of the stove with the spring and gas tubing proximity identified, since the tubing has the gouge on the inner side it doesnÃÂt show. I used a small dental mirror to view that from the front of the tubing. In the pictures you will see that the spring hook is not touching the gas line, this is because the side panel is off to take the pictures. When the side panel is reinstalled it pushes the gas line tubing directly against the spring mech. I did not receive a return call or email reply from Whirlpool corporate, they would not speak to me. I did however reach the service department that did come out and replace the tubing gas line.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to a manufacturing defect, but no injury or explosion occurred.

incident_description: Maytag refrigerator (S.N. 10978988ZQ) caught fire in our kitchen 19:30 on 12/3/2012 for no apparent reason (Model Number MSD2456GEQ)
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, which is a significant incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: The handle broke on my coffee pot and hot coffee spilled on my hand.
justification: Hot coffee spilled on the hand indicates an injury, and broken handles on coffee pots are a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
I've owned the frigidaire gas oven/stove for 2 1/2 years.
The model is LGGF3032KWF serial # VF01457214. The oven was leaking carbon monoxide. The firemen shut off the gas to the oven until it is serviced and fixed. There were no injuries since we reacted to the carbon monoxide alarm quickly. I have contacted frigidaire at this point. I am waiting to see if there are other complaints and also to see how they respond. Other people may not be so lucky.
justification: The incident involved a gas oven leaking carbon monoxide, but no injuries occurred due to quick response to the alarm.

incident_description:
Product complaint:
Frigidaire Dishwasher-M#PLD4375RFC2--S# TH82184501

DEFECTIVE CONTOL PANEL DESIGN-water leaks in and shorts out the control panel

  -Frigidaire has replaced the control panel on our unit, once during warrantee period

Called Frigidaire 12/2010 for repair- Frigidaire Complaint #[REDACTED]- company offered to replace part-but we must pay for the service person to perform the repair. 

All price quotes for repair work were more than $150 for all Frigidaire certified repair technicians in our area. We did not have the money to pay for the repair person, so the unit has sat unused since 2010.

12/22/12- Frigidaire Complaint # [REDACTED]-Called Frigidaire to see if there has been a product recall-(internet has many complaints for same product and reason). Company will not repair or replace part.

I would like to have the unit either replaced or obtain a full refund to purchase a different unit
justification: The incident involves a defective control panel causing water leaks and shorting, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Information below was transferred from the Consumer's email to CPSC.


I purchased a Frigidaire Cooktop model number PLEC36S9EC in August 2007. In November 2007, while the unit was under warranty, I had an electrician replace the right-front burner control because that burner was turning on by itself while the control was in the OFF position. 

In October 2010, the product was recalled under CAP# 11-016 because it was a fire hazard. In April 2011, the recall was updated. I have since obtained the free repair kit and had it professionally installed.

Last weekend, my wife and I returned home to find one of the burners ON and glowing bright red with the control knob in the off position. 

We could not turn the unit off except by turning off the circuit breaker to the kitchen. Had anything combustible been near the stove our house would likely have burned down. As of now, we have to leave that circuit breaker OFF to prevent a fire in our house.

We have had the unit professionally repaired twice -- the second time using your repair kit.

I no longer trust this product in my home, because I believe that it continues to present a problem similar to the one described in the recall..
justification: The incident involved a burner turning on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Bunn Automatic Coffee Maker leaks water just like the last one I sent back that was recalled a couple years ago.  I pour in 10 cups of water to make the coffee but only 8 cups go into the pot the other two cups end up all over the counter.  The waters is leaking from where the power cords comes out of the machine at the bottom and also from the side near the back.  The model number is GRX-B with a date code of 034810 CR.  The water started out leaking only a little then as time went on got worse.  It is at the point that water may be possibling get into the electric parts at he bottom.
justification: The coffee maker leaks water, posing a potential electrical hazard but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
A 2 cup Pyrex measuring cup exploded in the cupboard all by itself.  It wasn't being used, it just shattered while sitting in the cupboard.
This happened about a year ago and I had forgotten about it until I saw the article online about other people having this shattering problem with other Pyrex items.
I didn't say anything to Pyrex about it at the time but I want someone to know it's not just happening to people who aren't following directions for safe handling of Pyrex.
justification: The Pyrex measuring cup shattered while unused, causing no injury, and the incident was reported as rare based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: I had used this dish for a baked cranberry dish for Thanksgiving with no problem after purchasing a set of two (the 9"x13" and a smaller dish with covers) at Walmart. I prepared baby-back-ribs with an oriental sauce, baked at 350 degrees covered with foil for about an hour or so and then for about half an hour uncovered.  I removed the pan from the oven and placed it on knitted hot pads (my grandmother had made these for me years ago and they were room temp and dry!) on my room temperature glass top stove.  I had turned my back to the stove and pan to continue preparation of our meal ...my 11 year old granddaughter had just stepped away from the stove! ... a loud BANG made me jump and turn to see what on earth happened ... I expected to see my granddaughter hurt!  The Pyrex dish had EXPLODED!!! In fact, the explosion was so extreme that the ribs had been blown UP and landed back on the stovetop, but sauce and shards of glass where blown all over my kitchen ... stove, cupboards, floor, the facing cupboard and counter about 8 feet away, and I even found glass slivers about 15 feet away in the dining area!!! I had some small marks on the backs of my bare legs where I had been hit by flying glass, but thank God, my granddaughter was not hurt. I returned the lid and the smaller dish and lid to Walmart ... the lady referred me to a manager because I had only the LID of the exploded dish to return ... when I quite loudly started explaining how the larger dish exploded but I would gladly retrieve the shards I had cleaned up and put into the trash with other customers becoming involved ... the manager advised I must fetch another set from their shelves, and when I did, she refunded my purchase.  When I posted this shocking experience on Face Book, two nieces reported that Pyrex dishes had exploded on THEM previously!!!
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (small marks on legs from flying glass) and could have been much worse, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents were reported by others.

incident_description:
I was making a pumpkin pie. All of my ingredients were room temperature as they had been sitting out on the counter for over an hour prior to using them. The ingredients were 1 can of pumpkin pie mix, 1 can of condensed milk, 2 eggs, pre-made pie crust (not in a tin). I pre-heated the oven to 400 degrees and built my pumpkin pie in a 9.5" glass Pyrex pie plate. Once the oven was pre-heated, i placed the pie in the oven to bake. It was to bake at 400 degrees for 15 minutes, then the temperature was to be reduced to 350 degrees. As soon as I shut the oven door, I heard a strange sound. Opened the oven up and the pie plate had shattered in the oven. This pie plate was brand new. I had bought it several months before but had never used it.

I called Pyrex and they tried telling me I did something wrong, however, I had followed their instructions perfectly. They shipped me 2 pie plates as replacements. After reading the article on NBC news, I am hesitant to use them. I also felt the need to report the issue I had as well.
justification: The incident involved a pie plate shattering in the oven, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: i was in the kitchen and my baking dish anchor hockey was on the counter. I had use that item 2 days prior and had washed and clean this pan. out of the blue this dish exploded even though it had not came out of the oven. it was really starnge the only thing i could figure is cool air somehow made this dish do this. just 4 weeks ago it happen again except i had removed the dish from the oven and set over the back burner where the heat from the oven keeps your food warm i finally removed it from the stove to the counter and set it in another pan to protect my counter that cool pan it set there 2 mins and exploded also cutting me in 3 places glass went 10 feet across my kitchen and burn my kithen floor, i think im done using glass baking dishes....[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injuries from glass shards and burns, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of similar incidents suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: I was pouring boiled water for use in new born granddaughters bottles when the pyrex cup/pitcher exploded.  This happened on Saturday, December 15 in my kitchen.  Luckily, I was alone, because in addition to the cup exploding, the hot water poured out and burned my foot and belly.  I don't know what changed with the pyrex products but I will not purchase another one.  I have two baking dishes and a 16 oz measuring cup since 1971and there is not so much as a chip in them.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the foot and belly, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the event and the user's long history with Pyrex products without prior incidents.

incident_description: I made meatloaf, put it in a pyrex glass dish.  this was a brand new pan, never used before. i bought it brand new.  the meatloaf had been in the oven for about 40minutes when i heard something "explode" in the oven... it was the pan, it had shattered all over the inside of my oven, literally exploded in the oven.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering in the oven, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I am reporting this for my 87 year old father who is a disabled (wheelchair bound) WWII Vet. He had a Whirlpool range in his house, which he had for years. One evening recently he was using one of the burners on the top of the stove on a medium temperature. As he was approaching the range, in his wheelchair, to check on the food he was cooking.The glass front on the oven door exploded. Glass was strewn everywhere! Thank God he was not hurt. Since the oven door was close to his eye level in his wheelchair, we are thankful that he was not blinded!!! He was shaken up. He called the Fire Dept. since he was home alone. They made sure he was okay and cleaned up the glass for him.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, but no injuries occurred, and the likelihood of such an event is unlikely.

incident_description: I placed my Frididaire oven on self cleaning and about 2 hours into the cleaning cycle the outter glass of the oven door exploded into pieces.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased 2 sets of Mainstays brand drinking glasses. While washing one of the glasses, I sustained a deep cut extending from below my knuckle to my thumb. The glass is brand new and was not in any way broken. Once I got my injury taken care of, I inspected the glass carefully and noticed that the rim of the glass was jagged and poorly made. I was extremely upset that an unbroken, new product could cause this much damage and pain. I am taking the glassware back to Walmart where I purchased it and hope they do something about it.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut, indicating an injury (severity 3). Poorly made glass rims are unlikely to cause injuries frequently (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
IÃÂve had two separate incidents where the Pyrex glass cookware I was cooking with exploded.

The first time I was baking a graham cracker crust. I took the Pyrex out of the oven and placed on a burner that was off.  I stepped over to my refrigerator to grab something and the Pyrex dish exploded.  Had I been standing in front of the dish I probably could have been injured.  Luckily the refrigerator door shielded me from the flying glass shards. 

The second time this happened I was broiling a steak, I opened the oven door to take the internal temperature of the steak and again the Pyrex dish exploded inside the oven.  Luckily the pieces it broke into were large and did not go very far. 

Since these two incidents I have not purchased any new Pyrex cookware.  I know go to thrift store and look for the vintage/original Pyrex, which I know is safe and will not explode when used.
justification: The incidents caused no injury, but the glass shards could have caused injury if someone was standing near the dish.

incident_description:
I took the glass baking dish out of the oven heard a loud pop ab
Nd the glass went everywhere.
justification: The glass baking dish shattered, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I thought I was the only person that had experienced the exploding cookware phenomenon until I read an article online. I too had experienced this. I cooked a pan of lasagna in the oven and when it was finished, I pulled it out and placed it on the stove to cool and set for a while. I went to the living room to watch some tv and it sounded like rain was hitting the kitchen window. When I got up to see what the ruckus was, I was in awe to see the lasagna slowly oozing out of the Pyrex cooking dish. It had splintered into a thousand long slender pieces. I was just lucky to not have had the hot dish in my hands or worse, set it on a table with hungry guests. The only loss was a healthy portion of good ingredients and about two hours of preparation and clean-up. Again, I was grateful that no one was injured.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding cookware) but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the description of a known phenomenon.

incident_description: Baked two pies at one time just before Thanksgiving 2012.  One was an older pyrex dish and the other was a newly purchased pyrex dish. The oven was at 350 degrees. Both pans were placed on top of the oven to cool. The top of the oven was not particularly hot or I would have placed on the counter.  Within two minutes, the new pyrex dish exploded all over the kitchen into about 50 pieces. Shards of glass were everywhere on the floor. The older pyrex dish was fine.  The new dish never made it past its first baking experience. There was nothing to return to the store to get our money back. The top of the oven was cool enough to place our hands on it with no problem so I don't think it was due to sitting on top of the stove.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
My wife had used the oven earlier today to bake some cakes, after a while she walked into the kitchen and she noticed the oven was on. (She had turned it off earlier) She observed that there were none of the stove lights on indicating that the stove was on. She saw that the broiler, that she had not used baking a cake, was on. She tried to turn off the broiler controls even though they were indicating that they were off. She called me into the kitchen and I observed that the broiler was on with no electronic lights indicating that it was turned on. I tried using the controls, but they just lit up as normal and turned off as normal, but the broiler stayed on. Thank goodness we were home. Un attended I can see a very dangerous if not fatal flaw with this unit. The only way I could turn off the oven was by turning off the breaker switch at the electrical panel. 
  I pulled the unit away from the wall to look behind it, but did not notice anything that may have been shorted out. I tried turning back on the oven after it had cooled down, but the broiler came on and would not shut off until I tripped the electrical breaker in the main electrical panel.
  I found the oven's model number and started a search on your site for a possible recall. The oven's information is as follows: 
  Sears Kenmore range, Model # - 790.95214200
I found where you had another kenmore model number listed - 790.99012 - 790.99013 and it stated that depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.
  I contacted the sears hotline but was told that no recall had been issued for my model. I explained to them everything that had happened (as I have reported to you in this letter) but they were not interested in with my concerns. I informed them that I was going to report this problem to CPSC but all the lady said was ok thank you, goodbye.
  I am a retired Fire fighter and something like this really disturbs me. We could have placed leftovers in the oven overnight and the result could have been a tragic fire possibly resulting in a fatality. 
  As of this statement to you my kenmore Range is unplugged!!! Please look into this as there may be others out there with the same problem that may occur or has already occurred and no one knows what started the fire!!
  Thank you for your attention in this matter. Please feel free to contact me anytime about this either through email of call my cell phone at [REDACTED]  Thank you,
 [REDACTED]
justification: The oven malfunctioned by staying on without indication, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I put together a breakfast casserole that sits in the refridgerator until morning and then you pop it in the oven for 45 min to bake. The dish was cold but not frozen. When I put it in the oven at 350 degrees I expected to have a nice breakfast soon. Within 10 min. the whole dish exploded into a million pieces. I have cooked with this same pyrex dish for about 2 years. It is very handy to store leftovers because it has a plastic lid that fits on top. The lid is not meant to be used in the oven, only the microwave. But I don't use the dish in the microwave because I prefer the taste from the oven. I never use the plastic lid except for storage in the fridge.
justification: The incident involved a dish exploding in the oven, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer says she started smelling a plastic burning scent.  Her and her husband walked in the kitchen and noticed that smoke was coming out of the dishwasher.  She says that the control board caught on fire.  

She didn't see any flames but says if they had not been home there house would have burned down.  the consumer says the unit was on no longer than 15 minutes before the incident occurred.    

The consumer has yet to contact the manufacturer but it is her next step.  Her model is listed in Release # 05-123, the serial number however is not part of the recall.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Heating element in dishwasher stays on when machine is not running. Burning smell and cabinet of dishwasher heats up including plates and other contents. Checked with Maytag but model is not included in safety recall.
justification: The heating element staying on poses a burn risk and potential fire hazard, indicating injury severity. The issue is not part of a recall, suggesting a possible but not certain occurrence.

incident_description: I was using the oven portion of a Kenmore electric range. I had been preparing to cook dinner for that evening for my daughter and husband. The oven was preheated and I had just put the chicken into the oven. After the appropriate amount of time for the chicken to cook I called my daughter into the kitchen and began to take the food out of the oven. As soon as I placed my hand upon the over door glass exploded outward from the glass covering of the oven door. The glass went several feet away from the door spraying near my daughter and the family dog. The glass continued to break out slowly over several minutes and on occasion fell out in large chunks. Thankfully no one was injured but this incident could have caused injury to myself, my daughter, or the family pet. There was no warning that came with the product that this type of accident could occur. I was following appropriate usage guidelines and the product should not behave this way when used as intended. I would hope that in the future no one would be subject to exploding glass oven doors whilst cooking dinner for their family.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, posing a risk of injury, but no one was harmed in this incident.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Smooth Top Electric Range Oven (Model: 66592002102 Serial: RP0327286) purchased in 2003; on Christmas Day 12/25/2012 after dinner was prepared I turned the oven off and enjoyed dinner with my family and friends.  It started getting really hot in the house and we figured it was just from all of the cooking and family filling our home.  We opened two windows in our kitchen and went back to having fun.  It continued to get even hotter in the downstairs of our home.  I then looked over our kitchen island at the stove to see that it was glowing orange.  I looked at the digital display on the oven and it was turned off.  I walked over and pushed the off button numerous times to no avail.  I quickly went to my garage and shut the breaker off.  The disaster was averted for now.  The next day I turned the oven breaker back on to see what would happen.  The oven screen turned on with a (PF) code which is normal anytime you have a Power Failure.  I cleared that code by pushing the OFF/Cancel button on the control panel.  The oven was never turned on however, the element began to glow bright orange.  I left the breaker on for just a few minutes and in that short time the oven temperature was extremely hot.  

I contacted Sears about this issue and they said that even though it was a similar problem to another recall that because my Model/Serial number was not included then I would just have to pay for a repair.  

They further told me to contact Kenmore directly because they would have to deal with the safety issue.  After speaking to [REDACTED]  (Employee #[REDACTED]) I was told to contact Sears because they would have to deal with the safety issue.  

What they want to do to resolve the issue is to come put a new part in the oven.  The same part that faulted out this time in a manner that causes a huge safety issue.  I am not comfortable having a new part put in this oven if I have not been reassured that it has been redesigned so that this type of fault could not happen again.  I have a family of six and do not feel safe going to sleep at night with an oven that could turn itself to high heat at any point.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the recurring nature of the issue.

incident_description: Preheated oven to 350 degrees to bake a pizza. Oven was empty and clean. Suddenly heating element popped, crackled, and had a bright white ball of flame around it. Turned off oven immediately, pulled circuit breakers, cut oxygen to oven, but fire continued. Heating element burned through. Used chemical fire extinguisher to put out fire, but fire still continued along the heating element. Fire subsided, then reignited, then subsided for good. Fire destroyed heating element. 8 inches or more of the heating element fell off.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the detailed description of the fire's persistence and damage.

incident_description:
My Kenmore electric range Model # 790.96112408 has several times had the left front burner overheat and then fail to turn off with the control knob. The only way to turn it off was to unplug the stove. The surrounding counter top was very hot to the touch.
I have read reports of others who have had this problem who also had the burner turn on by itself. I am very concerned about the fire hazard this presents. It seems the only way to safely use this range is to not use the left front burner and to turn off the breaker when the stove is not in use.
justification: The burner overheating and failing to turn off presents a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My mother has a Kenmore oven, purchased from Sears in 2009; model number 790.47859400.  Last night, as the oven was on warm, the glass in the door exploded and shattered all over the kitchen.  After researching online, it seems to be a recurring problem with glass doors.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, causing damage but no reported injury.

incident_description: In October 2012, we had company visiting from Texas.  It was the last night of their visit so we prepared a special meal.  I prepared Apple Crisp in a 9 X 13 Pyrex dish.  I preheated my oven to 350 degrees and then placed it in the oven when it reached the temperature.  We were eating outside while the Apple Crisp was baking.  After cooking for approximately 20 minutes I heard the explosion.  The others at the table thought it was some kind of noise from the neighborhood so I didn't go into check inside the house. A few minutes later when I went in to take the Apple Crisp out of the oven, I found the shattered glass and apple crisp in my oven.  I took a picture of the disaster in my oven.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish exploding in the oven, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: A hot pan was placed on the Pyrex cutting board and it shattered into hundreds of small pieces. We have had this board for about 5 years and many times placed hot objects on it. The manufacturer stated that the cutting board was safe for objects coming from an oven.
justification: The incident involved a shattered cutting board but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as it has happened before but not frequently.

incident_description: I had baked chicken spaghetti in a glass Pyrex casserole dish. My daughter, her significant other and my 2 year old grandson were over to eat dinner. I removed the dish from the oven, placed it on 2 pot holders that were positioned side by side due to the length of the dish, this was also to protect my countertops, and suddenly it exploded. Food everywhere, glass all over he kitchen and my grandson had no shoes on at the time. Fortunately, we were able to get him away before he stepped in the glass. I was standing right next to it when it exploded and I am so thankful I did not get a piece of glass in my eye, etc. I fear baking with a glass dish to this day regardless of the instructions. The instructions did not help me nor did they work.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding, causing a mess but no injuries, as everyone was safely moved away from the glass.

incident_description: Cooked a dish one evening in a pyrex glassware 8" X 8" dish (I believe) in the oven, removed from over and placed cooked food on a plate to serve, let the glassware cool on the stove while eating (roughly 30- 45 minutes) before placing in an empty sink, about 15-20 minutes later there was a loud shattering sound
justification: The glassware shattered but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
I was roasting vegetables in a 9x13 glass pyrex dish in a 400 degree oven. When I removed it, I placed it on a clean/dry stove top and it exploded.
Glass shards flew several feet and cut my arm.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (cut arm) from flying glass shards, but such events are uncommon with proper handling of Pyrex dishes.

incident_description: Dec. 2010 ,  In pyrex 8x12x2 glass baking pan , @ 350 degrees for 1 hour in oven .  Mexican enchellades done cooking ,  removed from oven and set on glass stove top to cool AND BOOM .  The pyrex exploded , pieces everywhere ,  even bouncing off of front living room window 28 feet from stove . No one injured thank God ,  we began picking up the pieces to discover burn marks on countertops ( formica ) . I haven't reported this till now ,  somehow believing it was my fault . Now I see I am not the only one to see this happen to .
justification: The Pyrex exploded causing damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are uncommon but documented, hence likelihood 2.

incident_description: I was using a 9x13 pyrex dish purchased at the local Target. I was baking a chicken dish with liquid sauce. I took the dish out and put it on a granite counter. In approximately one minute the dish exploded into many tiny pieces. Thank goodness I had stepped away to get a spoon. It took my husband and me over an hour to clean up all the little pieces of glass.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but no one was injured as the person had stepped away, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Making hot rolls, my  "new" blue Pyrex cake pan was sitting on top of the stove, with 2 other cake pans that I use to make rolls in, as the oven heated under them. The bread dough was ready to make the rolls and the new pan exploded, like a bomb!  I had just turned my back on the stove, or my face would have been over the pan.
justification: The pan exploded violently, posing a significant risk of injury, but no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description: On thanksgiving of 2012 my mother in law was heating up our stuffing and when she pulled out our glass casserole dish she sat it on the counter in the kitchen and two seconds later it completely exploded. Shooting glass all over stove and kitchen floor. She then accidently stepped on a big piece of glass and it cut her foot open. We then had to take her to the emergency room to get a couple stitches in toe. We had never heard of glass casserole dishes exploding.
justification: The incident resulted in a foot injury requiring emergency room treatment, placing it at severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the unusual nature of glass casserole dishes exploding.

incident_description: Saturday December 15th I was having a christmas party.  I heated some ham in a pyrex dish and I was transferring the ham into another dish and the pyrex just shattered in my hands.  I was wearing heating mittens so no one was hurt but the glass shards were all over the food.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered, but no one was injured due to the use of heating mittens.

incident_description:
I placed breaded pork chops in an Anchor Hocking 2 quart glass baking dish.(Purchased as a 2 Piece Value Pack of 2qt  & 3qt clear glass bake ware.) I placed the baking dish in my cold oven, and started the oven to preheat at 350 degrees. The oven reached 350 and was baking for about 10 minutes when I heard a loud popping noise. I put my oven light on and thought my 3year old oven glass door exploded. I then realized it was the baking dish with my pork chops in shattered glass laying on the oven floor. There were,  what seemed like thousands of pieces of glass, all over the oven. I'm thankful the pork chops weren't baking too long, because if there was any grease splattered it may have caused a fire.

I have been baking with the same [REDACTED] oven ware  for over 40 years and have never experienced anything like this before.  My Anchor Hocking Ware is less than 5 years old and used maybe 4 times.
justification: The incident involved a shattered baking dish but no injuries or fire occurred, making it a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description: I was cooking roasted potatoes in my glass casserole dish by Pyrex, I cooked the potatoes for 45 mins at 350 degrees. After I took it out of the oven I laid it on a pot holder to cool, I turn around to wash dishes and then I hear a loud bang.  I look and the glass had exploded and shattered everywhere. My dog was right beside me and we were both lucky to not have been injured. I have only had these dishes (I have another one that i purchased with it) for about a year and i really love them but now I am scared to use it in case me or my puppy do get injured this time.
justification: The glass dish exploded but no injuries occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the incident.

incident_description:
We have A Kenmore Electric Range model # 665.92014102 there is a major safety problem with this product that causes a fire. 
For the second time in about 4 years this range has went into broil mode by itself and cannot be turned off, it gets so hot that what ever is in the oven will catch on fire and fill the house with smoke, if you donÃÂt turn off the breaker in time the house could go up in flames,	
The first time this happen I told Sears about the incident and it was treated as it was no big deal, I had the repair man come out to look at it, he said it was the control board and it would need to be replaced, that it is a common problem with this range, I had the repairs made at a cost of more then $200 to me. Now it has happened again, and after looking on the web I see that this is a common problem for lots of people with these Ranges, this is very dangerous something needs to be done. When a product fails it should not turn on, it should just not work.
justification: The incident describes a recurring fire hazard with the electric range, posing a significant risk of property damage and potential injury, though no injuries or deaths are mentioned.

incident_description:
My Panasonic microwave, model NN T945SF, stopped working and gave an error message.  I restarted the clock and restarted the microwave 3 additional times.  Next I smelled smoke, the circuit interrupter turned off the electricity at the plug and one of the prongs on the plug had blackened.  
The manufacture date is 12-05 for the unit.   It is a large, 1250 watt unit.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common with proper use and maintenance.

incident_description: I just purchased Slushy Magic from my local Walmart and when I took the contents out of the box the special ice cubes inside the box have something black inside them. The substance in them appears to be mold. The product says only water and salt is in the special cubes. Do I return these to the store or do I need to give these to someone to further investigate?
justification: The product contains mold, which is an incident but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: 8 or 9 inch square Pyrex baking dish removed from oven and set on a cooling rack exploded with 2 eye witnesses to the event.  It sounded like a shotgun blast throughout the building and glass was located as far as 8 ft away embedded in paper towels and all over floor and counter.  3 weeks later, an employee picked up the big Pyrex batter bowl by the handle from the dish drainer.  It had been sitting there overnight without incident.  Immediately, the thing exploded in her hands.  She had shareds of slivered glass everywhere...in her eyelashes, down her blouse, etc.  Both of these incidents occurred in my kitchen and very close together in time frame.  No one has to tell me not to buy more Pyrex.  All of it has been removed from my house.
justification: The incident describes injuries from glass shards, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents happened twice in a short timeframe.

incident_description: I have used Pyrex for years. I purchased a new set last year. While cooking some chicken in one of the new set, I warmed up the oven, I had the chicken all seasoned and in the pan with the vegetables. Waited for oven to warm up as always, put the chicken in, 25 minutes later, I heard this explosion in my oven. I went and looked and the pyrex pan had shattered into a million pieces. I am still finding pieces of broken glass in the oven. I have been using pyrex for years and this has never happened to me before.
justification: The Pyrex pan shattered but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
Yesterday at 4:15, I started to get things ready for my dinner which consisted of baked trout, pasta and green beans. I put the fish in my Pyrex clear glass baking dish and placed it on the left front of my stove top. I put water in a pot and placed in on the back left burner and I put green beans in a pot on a front right burner.   At 5 pm, I turned my oven on to preheat. At the same time, I turned on two stove top burners ÃÂ one to boil water and one to cook the green beans. I then left the room and sat down in a room nearby and visited with two of my sons.  I heard a little crackle about two minutes later but figured it was just some water that was on the outside of one of the pots. Luckily, I delayed in going to explore. One minute later, there was a loud noise. When I went into the kitchen, I realized my mistake. I had turned on the wrong burner. I turned on the burner under the fish and not the one under the water. My mistake, yes, but I never imagined that it could have potentially been a life changing mistake.

 

The Pyrex baking dish did not just crack or shatter into small pieces; it EXPLODED! There were small pieces, medium sized pieces (3 inches by half an inch) and a few larger pieces within a 4 foot radius of the baking dish. Glass was everywhere. It was a pain to clean up and dinner, of course, was ruined. I could have been extremely mad about the situation but I wasnÃÂt. I was just so thankful that my children or I had not walked into that room at the wrong moment. If someone had been in the kitchen, they would have been hit by flying glass. They could have incurred minor injuries or suffered extremely severe injuries. I get sick thinking about how our lives could have changed instantaneously.

 

I realize that the directions on the Pyrex dish state not to use it on a stove top. However, I donÃÂt think I am the only one who will ever accidentally make this mistake. To me, this product has a safety issue. This morning I was surprised to learn on the internet that many people have reported similar issues. Pyrex is aware of these reports, but it keeps denying that it is a problem. I believe this product should be recalled.

 


Barbara Erbe
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I recently saw an article about reports of shattering cookware and I decided  that I should report the incident that occurred in my home about 3 months ago.  My daughter-in-law baked a chicken a large pyrex baking dish (like she had many times before).  She did not put water in the bottom of the dish because she didn't know she was supposed to.  When the chicken was done I took the dish out of the oven and placed it on a non-working electric burner on the stove (again I didn't know I shouldn't do this -- we were given the dishes from a friend who no longer used them).  I removed the chicken from the dish (thank goodness) and we were eating dinner when about 20-30 minutes later the dish exploded all over the kitchen.  It shattered into hundreds of tiny pieces.  Fortunately no one was hurt and since we were mostly done with dinner no food got glass in it. The noise was like a gunshot going off and it scared the dickens out of all of us.  My son cleaned up the glass as best he could but we were finding glass for weeks afterwards in all kinds of strange placed in the kitchen -- even 10 feet away.  

The reason I am reporting this now is that I'm relatively certain that the majority of the shatterings go unreported so your statistics are not at all accurate.

Thank you,
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: A pyrex baking dish exploded when I took it out of the oven. I had been baking enchiladas for dinner. It exploded throwing tiny shards of glass all over the kitchen, narrowly missing my 10 month old grandson, me, my wife, my son and 2 another guests. Some of the glass actually melted on a rug and in the oven causing it to become non functional. We had to buy a new one. There were no injuries other than a slight scratch.
justification: The incident caused a slight scratch (injury) and significant property damage, but no serious injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: My Ancor Hocking 13x 9 " glass baking pan exploded in the dishwasher during the cleaning cycle. It damaged the dishwasher and pieces of glass lodged themselves in the motor of the dishwasher. Needless to say I had to replace my dishwasher as it no longer worked.
justification: The incident caused property damage (dishwasher) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I was baking trout in a Pyrex clear baking dish.  The fish was done and I opened the oven, pulled out the oven rack, and as I did so the baking dish exploded with a loud pop.  Glass shards went all over the oven, the floor, and flew farther out into my kitchen.  The glass pieces ranged from very small to larger, long shards, and were all extremely hot and dangerous.  I was so lucky I wasn't injured.

The Pyrex dish was purchased in the last ten years.
justification: The baking dish exploded, causing glass shards to scatter, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I placed my stuffed chicken breasts into the Pyrex baking dish. Place them into my pre-heated oven(350degrees). After only 5 min. or less there was a huge explosion-like shattering noise followed by a cascading of broken shards falling through the racks in my oven. It sounded a bit like rain.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering in the oven, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I baked granola bars in a Anchor Hocking 8x8 baking pan for 20 minutes at 350.  I preheated the oven and used a timer to stay at 20 minutes.  When I removed the pan from the oven I placed it on a heat pot holder.  About ten minutes later the pan exploded shattering glass over a ten foot area.  I was not in the kitchen when it exploded so no one was injured but would have been if close to the pan when it exploded.

Including picture!!!
justification: The pan exploded causing damage but no injuries occurred as no one was nearby.

incident_description: My Pyrex 9x13 baking dish shattered in my oven while I was cooking a casserole.   The Pyrex dish was not cold, as I pulled it right out of my cabinet and put the tuna noodle casserole ingredients in it.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: Recently I read an article about glass Pyrex dishes shattering.  I then remembered that this happened to me too earlier this year.  However, it wasn't soon after being removed from the oven.  I had taken a dish to a food day at work, and on the way home, the pan was sitting in the passenger seat and I kept hearing this sound like glass breaking.  I kept checking my windshield for rock chips and the longer I drove, the more cracking sounds I heard.  I was really concerned something was wrong with my vehicle but then when looking out the side window for evidence, I happened to look down and saw the handle of my pyrex dish shattering.  The bottom cracked in mulitple places, and by the time I got home, not even 20 minutes later, the dish was crumbled to the point I needed a vaccum to remove all the small pieces.  I've never seen anything like it, it just dissinegrated!  I kept thinking, what if this would have happened while at work and someone ingested a piece of glass, or my family, or while I was carrying it.  It literraly just started popping, cracking and fell into pieces.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering without causing injury, and such occurrences are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: I put salmon into my pyrex pie dish (as I had done many times before), put it in the preheated oven per instructions on the salmon packaging. I realized that my house was filling with smoke and quickly looked in the oven. The pyrex pie plate had split right down the middle and all of the juices (grease) from the salmon had dripped in my oven, causing the smoke.  I had never had a pyrex container do anything like this before. It created a mess and the possibility for a fire in my oven.
justification: The incident caused a mess and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I recently bought a new set of Pyrex bakeware from Costco.  A nice 9x13 and 8x8 piece, each with a cover and carrying case.  I've had old pyrex pieces for years but was attracted to the accessories for ease of transporting dishes.  I used the 9x13 to bake scalloped corn for Thanksgiving.  Given the introduction of a lid and the carrying case, I read and followed the directions carefully.  I took the casserole out of the 325 degree oven and immediately (directions stated to do so within 2 min.) put the cover on and put it in the insulated carrying case.  The casserole then was put in the trunk of my car, on a 50 degree day, sat there for the 90 min. drive to my brothers.  I took it out of the car, carried it into the house.  My sister in law took it out of the insulated carrier, and set it on the table.  About 5 min. later, I heard a strange noise.  Just as I looked to see where the noise came from, the casserole EXPLODED in front of my eyes.  It shattered thousands of pieces of glass all over the table and floor.  Not only was the food made inedible, my niece and my sister in law were cut by the glass.  I brought the remaining pieces back to Costco and got a refund.  I went out and bought a [REDACTED] pan to replace it because I am spooked by the experience and not feeling safe to buy another new pyrex product.  That is unfortunate for me as I loved the accessories.  I know Pyrex type glass casseroles have limitations and need to be properly cared for, but for 35 years, I have had, and still have, old pyrex casseroles with which I've never had a problem.  There must be something new in your product and, quite frankly, I am now scared to buy anything new that is Pyrex.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts) to the niece and sister-in-law, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific conditions described (following directions carefully and using the product as intended).

incident_description: I was baking a casserole type dinner at 350 degrees and when it was done, I went to remove the pan from the oven and it shattered everywhere. I have several scratches and cuts on my hand, wrist, and arm from the glass and was lucky that it did not cut me worse! I have used my pans before and not had any trouble.
justification: The incident resulted in several scratches and cuts, indicating an injury (severity 3). The user mentioned no prior issues with the pans, suggesting this is an unlikely occurrence (likelihood 2).

incident_description: I was baking a small roast in an Anchor Hocking Meatloaf pan and during cooking (in gas oven) I heard a loud boom , opened the oven door and saw my pan had exploded.  Glass was everywhere in my oven.
justification: The incident involved a pan exploding, causing glass to scatter, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:
We purchased a Whirlpool model WFG371LVB 30" free-standing gas range in early 2011.  Almost every time we would reach over the range to get something from an upper cabinet we would lightly bump the control knob on the front of the unit.  This would either allow gas to escape without igniting or would ignite the burner as we were reaching over the unit.  Several times it came close to starting clothing on fire.

Because this involved a safety issue we contacted Sears where we purchased the range.  The technician  determined it was design flaw and nothing could be done.  He suggested putting child protectors over the control knobs.  We attempted to do this but the control knobs are too large for the available child protectors.

Because this inadvertent gas escape/burner lighting was continuing and we believe it to be a safety issue, we offered a report to the CPSC in October 2011.  (See report No. 20111005-13818-2147474642.)  In talking with the CPSC the only suggestion given was to contact the manufacturer again.  The manufacturer has no suggestions or remedies for the problem.

The problem continues to this day and it is only a matter of time before something more serious happens (gas explosion, clothing fire, etc.).  In looking over the CPSC reports I found that others have submitted similar reports for the same problem.  (See report Nos. 20110905-C74BA-2147475640, 20120412-E138C-2147468480, 20120502-78F2F-2147467940.)

Because this is a serious safety issue we believe that Whirlpool should immediately recall the range or offer a repair kit to correct the problem at no cost to the consumer.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing gas leaks or unintended burner ignition, posing a risk of fire or explosion, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: I started my dishwasher on a quick wash cycle around 11PM on Friday, December 21. Normally I would go to bed but happened to stay up for a few minutes and it was fortunate that I did. Within a few minutes I heard a strange noise, clicking sound coming from the dishwasher, when I looked at it a flash and spark came out around the power button and smoke started coming out of the front control panel. I tried to turn off but an orange flame appeared. I yelled for my son to turn off the breaker which he did.  The smoke was an acrid, electrical and plastic burning smell.  It was so strong we had to open the window and doors for a half hour to get it out of the house.  The smell still lingered in the kitchen for a few days.  Since the dishwasher was 10 years old I did not call for repair, it was also the weekend before Christmas and I needed to have a dishwasher for Christmas day. I quickly bought another and had it installed Christmas Eve. My son took the control panel apart and it had clearly burned and melted inside.  I decided to check the internet to see if this had happened before and was astounded to see many reports at kitchenaidfire.com that described exactly what happened to my dishwasher.  This could have caused serious damage or injury if I had been in bed or not in the house when this occurred. We have disposed of the dishwasher but do have the burned control panel.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction causing sparks, smoke, and a small flame, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: On 11/21/2012, Wed prior to Thanksgiving I was heating bread in my Oster Convection Oven, it is a combination convection bake, reg. bake, toaster, broiler, warmer oven. Temp range 200-450. It has a glass door with timer and clock. I had the temp set on 300 degrees. I had just looked in the glass door to check bread, turned my back and there was a terribly loud explosion in the kitchen, at first I was so scared could not wonder what  exploded turning around the glass door had exploded and like a jet perpulsion blew off the oven. There was charred glass everywhere. I was the only one in the kitchen (I am a senior citizen) and was so glad the grandchildren were not in the kitchen or anyone was at that moment. I still cannot believe how this door blew off and the door just shattered in so many pieces and was in the living room and dining area, we have open concept kitchen. I immediately contacted Oster, and explained what happened. Naturally, they were apologetic, waiting for a label to ship back so they can investigate what caused this. By turning my back I was not hurt. Cut fingers picking up glass but it could have been so much worse if my family was present. Oster has sent me a new updated model so I am using it. I truly do like the product but I am honest I use it with apprehension.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing injury (cut fingers) but no severe harm or death.

incident_description: I preheated the stove and then started cooking potatoes.  All of a sudden I heard a crackling popping sounds and looked over the sparks were flying from behind the stove along with black smoke.  My husband was able to quickly shut the breaker off, thank goodness.  We pulled the stove out and the big cord looked fine accept one little wire looked melted.  He took the big metal back off and we found that all of the wires and the main terminal was complete melted, so wires were touching each other.  The exact model number is 790.96214408.  It looks like there are been several problems with this.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the stove, but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The mention of several problems with this model suggests a higher likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Our Kenmore Dishwasher suddenly started smoking, sparking and smelled of burnt plastic.  We shut it off and hit the electrical breaker as well as unplugged it.  This is the second dishwasher from Sears that has started on fire.  The first one was a [REDACTED] purchased before 2004.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking, sparking and smelled of burnt plastic, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Oven door glass shattered all over kitchen for no reason. Cannot use the oven safely after glass broke due to unbalanced door. Several burns due to door closing on our arms. Repairs are expensive, and not covered under warranty, even though this was a relatively new appliance.  Finally decided to repair it to keep from getting burned, agan, but after researching, found that there is a possibility it will just happen again.
justification: The incident resulted in several burns, indicating injury, and there is a possibility of recurrence based on research.

incident_description: A 11 cup pyrex  brand cooking dish shattered after one use. On Dec 24, I cooked mac & cheese in a  350 preheated  conventional oven. On the evening of Dec 26, I took the container from the refrigerator and placed it on the kitchen counter. About 5 to 10 minutes later I heard a cracking sound, and found the container in pieces. I think  blue plastic  cover and mac and cheese  stuck to the sides kept the pieces from shooting out.  I used other pyrex  pieces on Dec 24, a 3 and 6 cup,no problems yet.  I'm going to sit the 3 cup out today inside a bag to see if it shatters.  Now I am afraid of this cookware.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered but no injuries occurred, and the incident was contained by the plastic cover and food residue.

incident_description:
Received a Presto "Cool Touch" electric griddle as a gift. While using it for the first time I sustained
 burns to my finger tips on both hands. Seems the "Cool Touch" handles are only about an inch
wide and when I reached under it to move it my fingers easily contacted the heating element.
I cannot believe the handles are so narrow and there is no barrier to keep one from touching the heating element. Worst design on a piece of kitchen equipment I have ever seen.
justification: The user sustained burns to both hands due to poor design of the griddle's handles, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the design flaw makes accidental contact with the heating element easy.

incident_description: My wife was pre-heating the oven to 425 degrees for a pizza. The oven chimed when complete, she opened the oven door and a large flame and explosion engulfed my wife. Her hair started on fire in three places and her face, chest, ears, nose got burned. She lost her eye brows, nostril hairs, eye lashes, and quite a lot of hair. She was admitted to the emergency room at the hospital, treated and released. She suffered first degree burns.
justification: The incident resulted in first-degree burns requiring hospital treatment, indicating injury (severity 3). Oven explosions are uncommon but possible (likelihood 2).

incident_description: My GE Profile microwave turns on by itself and cannot be turned off unless unplugged. The model number is PVM1870SM3SS. It was manufactured on 3/2011 and purchased on 6/11/2011.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says she was cooking a roast for three hours at 325 degrees.  She then made biscuits and set the temperature at 375.  

After about 6 minutes the unit was smoking and she saw an F1 code on the digital display.  She could not turn the oven off by the controls so she had to turn off the circuit breaker.

She contacted the manufacturer who told her there was nothing that they can do.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an error code, but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was resolved by turning off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: Burner on my stove stayed on after I turned it off and a pot melted on the cooktop, when the pot was removed it tore chunks of the cooktop off.  On another occasion the burner would not turn off and the stove had to be unplogged.  I contacted Frigidaire/Electrolux, was told it was under recall, then transfered, completed a report, and was told it wasn't, that the electrical panel was broken and needed to be replaced, that this was not uncommon and to be expected on any stove.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted pot and damaged cooktop) but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Dishwasher control panel started arcing and smoking during rinse cycle.  I could hear it arcing from the next room.  Smoke was streaming out of the top of the door where the control panel is located.  I opened the unit and the door seemed to be hotter than during a normal cycle.  Smoke continued to stream out accompanied by a smell of burning plastic.  I turned off the power switch and circuit breaker.  The unit continued to smoke.  I tried to pour water in the small openings hoping to stop the internal burning, but the smoke continued.  As fast as I could, I disassembled the door and looked for the source of the smoke inside.  I found wires next to the control panel were embedded in the melted black, tar-like insulation on the back of the stainless door (tub side).  The smoke had stopped.
