I unclipped the control panel after removing the wire connectors and immersed it in cool water to ensure the fire was out before opening it.  When the control panel was disassembled, I found the source of the arcing was at the base of the circuit board adjacent to the connector with two largest wires.  The fire appeared to spread from there to the rest of the circuit board and burned a 2.5-inch-diameter hole in the white plastic housing (the side against the inside of the stainless door -- tub side).

No one was hurt.  We had the fire department on call until I was sure the burning was contained and stopped.  The kitchen counter did not start on fire.
justification: The incident involved significant electrical arcing and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was contained without spreading.

incident_description: I was using the fryer as intended to cook french fries. The fry basket handle is attached in such a poor way that if you tilt the basket (Such as to dump the food out) the handle detaches from the basket causing the hot basket and oil to fall. I did receive a mild burn from trying to catch the basket.
justification: The incident resulted in a mild burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The description suggests the handle detachment is a recurring issue, making occurrence likely.

incident_description:
i was useing my knife(a racheal ray gusto grip  #fur812) when the blade snapped off the
handle hitting me in the head. i have tried calling furi but they insist that these are not their knifes.
last week i called and at that time was told that they could send me a new knife.
but that they dont make them anymore
i didnt want to have  a new knife but to report a serious problem with one of their products.
i dont know who to call to make a report so could use some direction. thanks
justification: The blade snapped and hit the user in the head, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was using a Cuisinart Smart Stick immersion blender.  After use I rinsed it offer using my index finger to clear some sauce from the blade area.  As I moved it toward the water I inadvertently pressed the power toggle switch and activated the blender.  In less than a second it sliced through my finger three or four times snapping the upper bone in my index finger in half.  I immediately knew the injury was significant as the end if my finger was flopping around.  As my wife and two boys watched in horror as I wrapped my finger in 5 or 6 paper towels and raced to the hospital.

My injuries required a skilled hand surgeon over an hour and 20 sutures to reconstruct the end of my finger.  The end of my finger was severely lacerated.  My fingernail had to be removed.  My nailbed was ut multiple times.I may require further hand surgery depending on how I heal.

When I told the ER nurse how it happened she said "we're seeing a lot of those".  This is an unsafe category of products whose on/off switches must be safer for the consumer.

I've used immersion blenders for years without any prior incidents.  But this one time I let my guard down and this machine mangled my index finger in my dominant hand.

It's products like these that can define the good work you do for us as consumers.  I think it might behoove you to consider implementing stronger safety measures for this type of product.  Mine was bad but it could have been even worse.  I
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations, bone fracture, and required surgical intervention, indicating a significant injury. The ER nurse's comment suggests this is a known issue, making occurrence 'possible'.

incident_description: The dishwasher was running through a normal cycle.  It suddenly started making a popping noise and black smoke started rolling out.  We opened the door to stop it, thinking something might have fallen on the heating element.  The noise and smoke immediately stopped.  We saw nothing on the heating element, so we closed it to start again.  It started up again and the noise, smoke, and this time flames immediately started.  We opened it to stop again, and the noise, smoke and flames stopped.  After closing it a third time, and opening, the flames continued and we could see flames and sparks coming from the top right of the door at the control panel.  We were able to put the flames out, and turned off the circuit breaker.  Thankfully we were standing nearby when the sparking and fire began so we caught it very quickly before the fire got out of control.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks but was quickly controlled without injury.

incident_description:
(09/30/2012) The consumer stated that she was in the kitchen. She left the kitchen. When she came back in the top left burner had turned itself on. It was glowing red. The consumer stated that as she watched it, the glow started to spread under the glass. Then there was a horrible smell as if something was burning. She stated that she could not turn it off. She had to turn it off from the circuit breaker. Fire has spread under the dial.

(10/01/2012) The consumer stated that she called Whirlpool. They sent out Platinum Service Company on 10/08. The technician checked the unit. He found the switch burnt. The technician replaced the switch but the stove still did not work. The technician advised the consumer that she needed an electrician. The electrician checked the wiring and told her that nothing was wrong with the wiring or the breaker.

The consumer stated that she was billed.

(11/27/2012) The consumer called the company. She was told that they would sell her a new cooktop at a discount. Whirlpool said it would reimburse electrician bill.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that posed a fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: We have a VIBB536RSS Viking refrigerator purchased in 2011.Last evening my husband went to open the refrigerator door and it seared of the hinge and pinned him between the door and our kitchen island. This is a dangerous and critical issue. I had just had surgery and could barely help him to push the door back on the frame. We have no access to food or supplies, compounded by unavailability of help on Christmas. This is a profoundly scary and unsafe problem that apparently Viking is aware of and does not inform consumers.
justification: The refrigerator door seared off the hinge and pinned the husband, indicating physical injury and a dangerous situation.

incident_description:
I purchased a Oster Blender/Food Processor Model #BLSTCC and I found that it was unsafe due to the fact that there seemed to be no safety mechanism when the blades were turning, when being used in either mode. I have used other Food Processors and they have all had safety devices that would not let the sharp blades turn if the lid us unlocked.
I called Oster told them about this situation and they sent me another product of theirs which was basically the same thing, this one's Model #6878. When it arrived I was shocked to see it had the same issues. No safety mechanism! I have used it but was always very careful when doing so. I feel it is fairly safe when being used as a blender, but definitely not as a food processor! 
I am asking you to please explore these products for safety before someone gets injured. God forbid a child or teenager or young adult tries to use this and really gets hurt. 
If you find them unsafe please take them off the market for consumer's safety sake.
Thank you!
justification: The incident describes a safety concern with no reported injuries, but potential for harm exists due to lack of safety mechanisms.

incident_description: Smelled burning odor coming from the kitchen.  Saw smoke coming out of vent near handle on dishwasher.  Tripped circuit breaker and removed the fornt panel from the dishwasher.  found burned control board which had started melting the plastic cover.  It was fortunate we were home and detected the problem imediately or the dishwasher may have caught fire.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We purchased the refrigerator in January 2011 for our family of 5 to enjoy.  In May 2011, we noticed pieces of clear plastic in our crushed ice.  The icemaker auto dispenser quit working.  Deduced that the plastic on the auger that moves the ice to the crusher had broken.  Contacted Sears, and they replaced the entire bin & auger for free.  By February 2012, it broke AGAIN.  More plastic in the ice.  Now was out of warranty.  Now we have to order another new one, at a cost (through partsdirect.com) of $70.  We can order the upgraded auger that the manufacturer now provides, but it will cost over $156.  From what the tech at partsdirect can tell, they now make it out of metal.  Shouldn't GE be providing the replacement part for free, as a recall?  After all, in reading the incident reports on other GE fridge models, this is a very common problem.  Clearly, it was a manufacturing flaw.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator part causing plastic contamination in ice, but no injury or death occurred. The problem is described as very common, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I filled my 8"x8" Anchor Hocking glass bake ware with a noodle pudding and placed it into a pre-heated 350 degree oven and baked it for 1 hour. During that time, the oven door was not opened nor was the light turned on. When the timer went off, I went to the oven. But before I could open the door, I heard a loud cracking noise and what sounded like rain in the oven. When I opened the door, I found the bake ware had exploded and was broken all over the oven. Some large pieces were left on the wire rack, but about half of it was on the bottom of the oven. It was only the 4th time I had used this dish. No injuries occurred because of this incident.
justification: The bake ware exploded but no injuries occurred, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that after using the blender to blend her child's food (4 month old), she noticed that there were pieces of plastic shredded in the food while feeding her.  She is not sure if the child swallowed any particles when she fed her 2 spoonfuls.
The consumer discovered that the blade had shredded the gasket which is the plastic ring around the blade.

10/22/12) The manufacturer was contacted and a message was left for them to return her call.
 The consumer is concerned that this incident could have caused a choking hazard for her child.
justification: The incident involved plastic particles in food, but there was no confirmation of ingestion or injury.

incident_description: The electronic board on my Kitchen dishwasher caught fire and burned.  It emitted smoke and fumes throughtout my house and I had to dispose of it.  Fortunately I was home and avoided further damage.
justification: The dishwasher's electronic board caught fire, emitting smoke and fumes, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
About 10PM last night, I heard a noise coming from the kitchen. When I inspected the room, I found my Mr Coffee maker (model DRTX85) running at full output with no water and considerable overheating coming from the machine. The unit exhibited no operating lights, it had not been set to automatically come on at any time and hadn't been used since early that morning. 

I feel that if we hadn't been home or if I hadn't heard the noise, the unit would have been a fire hazard.
justification: The coffee maker overheated without water, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: coffee maker off but plugged in, last used 14 hours previous. Maker heard to start sizzling and popping and then fire noted coming out the bottom. Quickly unplugged and fire extinguished on it's own.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly controlled without injury or death.

incident_description:
One and one half years ago, I purchased from Sears, a Kenmore Elite Slide In Electric Range when my daughter got married at home.  Since the beginning, the oven racks have collapsed, unpredictably, with or without weight, with any movement.  

Today, on Christmas Day,  2012, the rack fell holding a roast.  One month ago, on Thanksgiving Day, the rack fell holding a turkey.  On Thanksgiving, the rack also fell holding something as light weight as a pie.         

I am now looking forward to the birth of my first grandchild and am concerned about the safety of the oven for family events.  

This defect in the product design should be corrected by the manufacturer immediately.  

The product should be recalled since there are many reported incidents online about this particular product, including third degree burns.  Online accounts indicate that Sears is not forthcoming in addressing this serious and extremely dangerous issue with its product.
justification: The incident describes repeated oven rack collapses, including with food, but no injuries are mentioned in the description.

incident_description:
I was running my Kenmore elite Model: 665-15953000
when black smoke started pouring out of the control panel.  I opened the door it didnt' stop so I threw the breaker.  I looked up on line and similar models had been recalled for this problem but apparently not this one even though there had been a number of similar complants.  Had this happened when I was asleep or gone it could have been very bad.
justification: The incident involved black smoke from the control panel, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Similar complaints suggest this is a recurring issue.

incident_description: We purchased a Fridgedaire electric range model number FPEF3081KF seriel number VF11236101 on July 4, 2011. Tonight, the control panel caught on fire! Thankfully, my husband was in the kitchen at the time or else it could have been tragic since we have a home with four young children. There was no food on the stove, nor was anything burning in the oven. The oven was on at the time, but there was no fire in the oven - it was strickly confined to the control panel. This range is out of warranty since it is over a year old; however, my husband says he would not want it back in the house anyway due to the obvious threat to our home and children. I looked online and saw that many other models were part of a recall, but this was not one of the listed models. I believe that this product is dangerous and needs to be looked at closely.
justification: The control panel caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injuries or deaths occurred due to immediate intervention.

The LCD display first indicated an ÃÂE1ÃÂ error and then went blank.  Soon we could see a stream of smoke emitting from the top of the refrigerator/freezer. incident_description:
I purchased the Black and Decker BFE53 Chest freezer on 05/11/2011. Approximately one week ago, it just shut down while plugged in. The outside became very warm. If I weren't home I don't know what would have happened.
I called Haier at their toll free number and spoke to rep. After hanging out on the phone for a while, I am told that my freezer does not fall under the recall because of the date I purchased it. I purchased it 05/11/11 and the recall evidently falls between Jan 2010 and Sept 2010. My model number and beginning serial number do match the recall requirements. What a vast improvement they have made on their freezers. Their date needs to be extended.
No injuries to report, and the product was being use for general freezing purposes. Not overloaded or in a tight space.
justification: The freezer shut down and became very warm, posing a potential hazard, but no injuries were reported.

justification: The incident involved a dish shattering but no mention of injury, so severity is 2.

Maytag 6.2 cu. ft. Electric Range MER8674AS

justification: The incident describes a gas leak scenario which could lead to a hazardous situation, but no injury or death is mentioned.

justification: Smoke filled the room, posing a risk to people and animals, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The timer would not shut off and the oven kept heating. Even after it was unplugged the timer ran for several more minutes. When it was plugged back in the area around the controls began smoking and got very hot.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that smoked and got very hot, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Toaster oven timer ticks down to "off" setting but then jumps to "always on " setting. Could cause a fire by overheating.
justification: The toaster oven malfunction could lead to a fire, which is an incident with potential for property damage but no immediate injury mentioned.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore dishwashwasher started smoking through the control panel.  We disconnected the power by tripping the breaker before any serious damage could be done.  I opened the control panel and observed what appeared to be burn marks around several of the connectors.
The model number appears to be 665.17514 and the serial number is FP103038.
justification: The dishwasher started smoking and had burn marks, but no injury or serious damage occurred as power was disconnected promptly.

incident_description:
My wife was baking cookies in our seven year old Kenmore electric range and the oven temperature controller failed  with the heat output locked at 100%. The controller indicated a failure but the heat remained on and the temperature increased uncontrolled. The oven gave a strong vinegar smell and the only way to stop the oven was to shut off the main power breaker. I put in a thermometer to see how hot the stove got but the temperature was higher than the sensor could read (higher than 600 degrees F)

I reset the breaker and the oven stayed off but if I turned on the oven the temperature once again ran away until I shut the breaker off. If this failure occurred when no one was home I am sure 

I checked the cpsc website and did not see a  recall for the model range I have.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire or injury if not manually intervened, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite refrigerator, Model # 79577553600, Serial # 702KR00082. Refrigerator on top has 2 side by side doors, freezer at bottom. The light on top is getting extremely heated up and give a very bad smell. This happened on Dec 13th 2012. The light casing was melting off and could be a potential fire hazard. The entire first level was boiling hot and all of the food was extremely hot to touch. The diary products in the first level was also melting. The smell was heavy and it smelt very burnt.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard and property damage (melted light casing and spoiled food), but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that she pre-heated the oven at 350 and approximately 5 mins later she placed the contents in the oven.  About 2 mins later the smoke detectors started going off and she noticed smoke emitting from the oven, the contents were on flames, they were removed and discarded. The unit could not be powered off, she waited and kept pressing the control panel, it eventually powered off.  They ventilated the house to disperse the smoke.

The caller noticed that although the oven was set for baking, it automatically sets itself on broil mode.  This was the first incident.  She had seen the oven flashing the time in the past but she had assumed that there was power loss sometime during the day.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The caller is concerned that this oven is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with flames and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
LG Dishwasher
Model: LDS5811ST
Electrical short
Two years ago, our dishwasher ceased functioning, indicating that it had a failed pump motor.
I replaced the motor, only to discover that I still had the error code.
After researching the problem on the internet, I was directed to check the wiring inside the front door panel.   To my shock I discovered several wires that had seperated, exposing the insulation, and one wire had seperated entirely.  This was caused by inadequte wire lengths, and lack of proper wire guides.  The wires had become embeded in the some sort of soft black insulation, and had no give to them at all.   To repair the problem, I soldered in wire extensions, and the dishwasher went back to working properly.
A few months later the problem resurfaced, and this time you received a mild shock if you came in contact with the metal face of the dishwasher.  Again, more wires had seperated and were contacting each other, and the metal face of the dishwasher.   Again I repaired the affected wires.
The next time this problem occurred, we noticed a burning smell.   Again, more wires had seperated (not any of the wires that had been previously repaired), and this time a short ensued.
I again repaired the wires, along with any that looked like they were coming apart or had inadequate slack in them.
Today we again have the same problem.
This unit is a hazard.  From researching on the internet, LG seems to have little interest in fixing design  flaws in their product..
justification: The incident involved a mild shock and recurring electrical shorts, indicating potential for injury, and the problem has repeatedly resurfaced, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: LG electric range model LRE30453ST.  I bought the stove a little over a year ago.  Two of the control panel switches started to work intermittently.  Sometimes I could not turn the burners on and sometimes I could not turn them off.  I would have to pull out the range and unplug the stove to get the burners off.  After reading other reviews, I learned that is not an unusual problem and other people had resorted to going to the fuse box and flipping the switch there.  I had the control panel replaced and so far no problems.
justification: The incident involved intermittent control panel switches, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: GE Profile dishwasher had a fire in the door within 5 minutes of turning it on.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher door, which is a significant safety hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The heating element in the bottom of the oven exploded causing a four (4) inch piece of the element to disintegrate.  During the incident, the element made a very loud electocution type noise until it completely burned.
justification: The heating element exploded, but there was no injury or death, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: A normal load cycle had completed on my Frigidaire dishwasher.  Approximately 15 minutes after the cycle had completed (not timed, but within reason of that time estimate), we heard a light buzzing from the control panel area, followed by smoke from an obvious electrical burn (indicated by smell and smoke color).  I quickly opened the door latch to break the circuit.  I then flipped the circuit breaker off to prevent further instance until I had a chance to open the panel.  Upon opening the panel to look at the circuit board, I found that a short had occurred; circuits had apparently arced and began burning the board and surrounding plastic.  I am just thankful that I had been standing next to the dishwasher when the arc first occurred, or the fire may have become much more expansive (possibly engulfing our kitchen?).
justification: The incident involved an electrical short and smoke but no injury or death, and such electrical faults in appliances are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: After cooking one evening, discovered that the front right "expandable element" burner would not shut off. I tripped the circuit breaker for the range and re-engaged, hoping to "reset" the range. Burner came back on, and was unresponsive to control.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The issue is unlikely to recur frequently based on the provided statistics.

Frigidaire smooth top range
I know there was a recall on these ranges a few years back and when I called 877-435-3287 ant talked to [REDACTED] I was told there were model numbers before and after mine that were in the recall but mine was not yet I'm  hving the same issue - the warmer burner does not shut off when I turn the knob.  I find it a little disturbing that my model is not included.
GLEF2384GCA
VF72522832
justification: The burner not shutting off is a safety issue but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: After brewing a pot of coffee, the Cuisinart Brew Central Coffeemaker DCC-1200 started to snap, pop and smoke. We unplugged the unit and took it outside where it continued to smoke and melt from the inside. Our house had a lot of plastic smoke smell in it. The counter underneath the machine was black and was starting to burn. We are no longer using the unit.  It was smoking from underneath the plate and out of the top.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting but no injury or death, and such events are uncommon for this type of appliance.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart brand toaster oven that was previously replaced by the company due to sparks near the switches. The unit has a toast feature with a "darkness" setting. When the food being toasted reaches the desired result, the unit is supposed to turn off. This feature has maflunctioned and does not turn off. This is a safety & fire hazard as the food being toasted could burn and start burning if someone assumes it would turn off by itself.
justification: The toaster oven's malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: Cuisinart drip coffee maker model DCC-1200 electrical components at the bottom of the appliance started smoking and caught on fire.  Was able to unplug the unit, stick it in the sink, and douse it with water to put out the small fire.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire but was quickly extinguished without injury.

incident_description:
Electrical burning smell throughout house.  Discovered it was coming from refrigerator and that refrigerator was no longer cooling.  Unplugged refrigerator and called for service.  Service technician discovered that compressor start relay had caught fire and self-extinguished.

This start relay is the same relay as that for the Maytag Whirlpool refrigerator relay fire recall but Whirlpool has refused to include Kenmore in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was addressed by unplugging the refrigerator and calling for service.

incident_description:
Our ~9 year old Kenmore dishwasher - model  587.15072201. was off the other night. We were in the kitchen and I closed the DW door. Black smoke started pouring out of the control panel and did not stop when I opened the door. We turned off the circuit breaker and called Sears repair. They quoted a price for the repair and said NOTHING about known problems with this model. We set up a repair appointment.  Because it was such an alarming problem, we then looked on the Web and found numerous reports to the Consumer Products Safety Commission and others about the same problems with this model. 

I called Sears again and told them that I knew of others with the same problem with this model. They refused to replace the DW and again told us we'd have to pay to have it fixed and that there was no recall on the model - they would not even discount a repair! Our house could have burned down.
justification: The incident involved black smoke pouring out of the dishwasher, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Oven remained on after it was turned off.  We woke up arounf 1 am with smell of smoke in the house.  I ran downstairs and the range was smoking and was displaying FIRE.  I pulled it out and unplugged it and burnt my hand while pulling it out.  At this time, it does it all the time now.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and a potential fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The description states this happens 'all the time now', making the occurrence likelihood almost certain.

incident_description: I have a two year old Kenmore Elite oven/range in which the oven racks fall, causing hot foods and liquids to fall and splash.  It appears that the oven walls/liner have bowed, causing the racks to have insufficient support.  Two members of our household have been burned by this oven to date as a result of the racks falling. I contacted Sears/Kenmore to report the problem on 12/11/2012.  I was told that the product was out of it's one year warranty and, therefore, not covered.  After seeing numerous reports from other consumers on the same and similar models with the same dangerous problem, I continued to pursue the Customer Solutions department as this appears to be a manufacturers defect. A Sears tech was sent to my home to inspect the unit and determined that in fact the unit is defective, that the liner suffered from "thermal expansion", and deemed the unit, in writing, "Unsafe to use".  Sears/Kenmore Customer Relations first told me that the unit would be replaced and referenced a five year warranty that included "thermal shock", but later retracted and advised that the actual manufacturer (LG) only covers the glass cooktop for thermal shock. Kenmore/Sears has previously acknowledged reports of this identical problem on this very website, yet the company offers no safe resolution or repair, and I am financially unable to replace the unit with a safe one.
justification: Two household members have been burned due to the oven racks falling, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue is recurring and acknowledged by the manufacturer, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: My Kitchenaid dishwasher caught fire.  The model number is KUDSO1FLSS3 and was purchased in 2004 from Sears.  The circuit board shorted which started the fire.  We had to cut power to the unit to prevent further burning.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire due to a short circuit, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
KitchenAid free standing oven will not turn off.  

Model number KERA807PSSOO

I am reporting this because it appears to be a well known problem (known by both the manufacturer and repair companies) that occurs with nearly EVERY unit.  If you own this unit, it is only a matter of time before the off button stops working.  I think the inability to turn your oven "off" is hazardous.  The manufacturer should redesign the switch membrane so this does not happen.
justification: The inability to turn off the oven is hazardous but no injury or incident is reported.

incident_description: Burned hand on multiple occaisons while using product.
justification: The description indicates an injury (burned hand) occurring multiple times, suggesting both injury severity and high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Ken more elite trio refrigerator has a potential fire hazard. The product has been in use for 5-6 years. Today I found that the interior light switch had malfunctioned and the light has been burning inside for some time, not sure how long. The whole interior compartment was hot, and the light fitting has melted off its casing. The next potential stage is a short, once it melts the wire and the unit will catch fire.
justification: The refrigerator shows signs of a potential fire hazard with a malfunctioning light switch and melted casing, but no actual fire or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Light bulb in the refrigerator stays on and heats up the entire first level unit.
It was even melting the light bulb cover. Very hot to touch a extremely smells as if there was something burning within.
justification: The incident involves a burning smell and extreme heat, posing a risk of injury from burns or fire.

incident_description: Left front burner on Kenmore glass top stove would not turn off.
justification: The burner not turning off is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential hazard if left unaddressed.

incident_description: The first time it happened was when I was baking a casserole. I pulled out the rack to see if it was done. As I pulled out the rack it collapsed on one side tiping the casserole so that it spilled into the oven and onto the oven door. No one was burned but it is dangerous. It has done  this numerous times. It is also getting worse. We don't pull out the racks anymore. The range is about 3 years old and no longer under warranty. You can see that the oven liner is warped. If you hold a straight edge on the left side you can see that it is bowed out.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the oven rack collapsing, causing spills but no injuries, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence with current severity.

incident_description: I turned on my Kenmore Electric range, the oven would not heat up then I saw a blue arc coming from the back of the controller.  I immediately turned off the stove, pulled it from the wall and ran out and tripped the breaker.  After watching it with fire extinguisher nearby for a few minutes I pulled off the back panel to find the controller had started to catch on fire due to an electrical fire.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire but was promptly controlled without injury.

incident_description:
I turn on my range to Broil to heat up before I put in my food.   There is a vent that leads from the oven to the range top just under the electronic control panel.   That part of the range gets very, very hot.   The control panel which operates the range also gets very hot.  This is my second range and they both do the same thing.  I called the service dept on the first range and the tech took the temperature coming out of the vent and it was approx 186 deg F.   This is before the oven even got started.   I had asked for a replacement range and Samsung replaced the first range with an identical range the second time.   I used the new range again and the same thing happens.   There is a book that comes with the range and in that booklet it says that the vent can become warm.   That's WARM   not HOT.   I have burnt my hand and since this is the second time this has happened I think that there is something the matter with the design of the range.   Please keep in mind that this happens when I either bake or broil with this range.   I am afraid that after a while that the electronics will eventurally fry and the range will nolonger be any good.   But,safety is the first thing that needs to be taken care of   The model number again is
FX510BGS
justification: The user reports burning their hand due to the range's vent becoming excessively hot, indicating an injury has occurred.

incident_description: Strong smell of burning plastic and electrical started coming from dishwasher along with some smoke.  Disconnected power and called fire dept.  Fire contained within dishwasher, but upon removal of the door shell wiring and electronic module (plastic) were completely burned through and melted.  No one was injured, but there is smoke damage.
justification: Incident involved smoke and fire damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but possible.

I have contacted Emerson and they could careless i will never buy there prouducts again.
justification: The incident involved a significant fire hazard with sparks and burns inside the microwave, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: when the oven is on and food is cooking steam comes up under the knobs and an alarm sounds and the burner blinks on and off.
justification: The incident involves steam and an alarm, which could cause confusion or minor disruption but no injury.

incident_description: I purchased model # DLC-8S serial #90409 Cuisinart Pro Custom food processor in September 2009.  While using the plastic work bowl, pieces have continually fallen off into the food I am preparing.  The first time it happened soon after purchase, the plastic was found in our meal.  Subsequent times I have been able to catch the broken pieces and disposed of the food.  This work bowl is clearly defective.  The cracking includes both small internal fissures around tension points (crazing) and actual broken/cracked pieces.  The final piece that engages the lock to operate the appliance has broken and the appliance is rendered inoperable.
justification: Plastic pieces falling into food pose a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I bought  a 1.8 quart stainless steel whistling tea kettle manufactured by Le Creuset in September. On first using it I was alarmed to find a serious and dangerous design flaw. After the water has boiled, and when you try to pour water into a cup or bowl, the water fizzes and bubbles out of the spout in an arc of boiling water that goes all over kitchen surfaces. It is highly dangerous because any hand close to the kettle risks severe scalding. In my view this product should be recalled immediately.
   I thought I might have been sold a single defective kettle, but looking at recent reviews on Amazon shows that other people are suffering the same problem, and danger. I refer you to the Amazon reviews dated october 16 by [REDACTED] and september 13 by [REDACTED].
  I emailed le Crueset's customer service department pointing out the risks of this product and calling on them to withdraw it. I received in return a message that did not address this issue but offered me a credit note if I returned the product and they found my complaint valid.
   I have not taken this up because it misses the point. A child could be scarred for life by this product. It is should be withdrawn from sale immediately.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous design flaw that risks severe scalding, with evidence of multiple similar complaints, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description: We had stored some roasted vegetables in a Glasslock kitchen glass tupperware.  While chewing a bite of the vegetables I cut my tongue badly and after spitting out what was in my mouth found a 1 inch very sharp glass shard.  After examining the edge of the tupperware, we found a large linear chip where the glass shard had broken off.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut tongue from a glass shard, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I was using the Baby Bullet, baby food maker to puree some food for my 6 month old daughter.  I had only used it a few times.  This was the third time.  I had followed all of the manufacturers guidelines on how to use and clean the device (hand wash, and top rack dishwasher safe). 

I was feeding my daughter her food and she was struggling with something in her mouth so I reached in and pulled out a piece of plastic/silicone.  This was from the units blade component. There is a plastic/silicone gasket around the blade.  It had popped off and had been cut into pieces.  I am very upset about the whole thing.  I was about half way done feeding her when I noticed something was wrong,  so it is is possible she might have eaten a piece earlier.

I tried to call the company but they are closed until tomorrow.

After some investigation on the Internet I have discovered that many other people have had similar stories about this unit malfunctioning and causing a choking hazard.

Please feel free to contact me about this report or my incident.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard from a broken part, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On November 22, 2012, my husband purchased the 23-piece Paula Deen cookware ensemble for me from Wal-Mart in Central, South Carolina, while we were visiting family. When we returned home on November 24, I opened, inspected, and washed the entire set. 

I have used various pieces of the cookware set over the last three weeks, with no issues until this evening. Around 6 pm, I cooked dinner in the 3 quart saucepan, using the lid to cover the dish in the pan. Once we had finished eating dinner, I promptly hand washed the lid and pan, and placed them securely on the drying rack in my kitchen. About an hour and a half later (around 7:30 pm), while in another room, we heard a pop and what sounded like pieces of something scattering across the floor of the kitchen. Upon entering the kitchen, we found the pan lid, in the same position on the drying rack I had earlier placed it in, shattered, and glass from the lid across our kitchen counters and floor. 

I am concerned that the lids, being apparently unable to withstand the rigors of being utilized in their intended manner, then hand washed and allowed to air dry, could be a safety hazard, as they shatter without warning, being dropped, or otherwise abused.
justification: The incident involved a shattered pan lid without injury, indicating a safety hazard but no harm occurred.

incident_description:
The light bulbs  did not power off with the doors to the refrigerator closed.  The consumer noticed that the light bulb covers were melted on both sides. The light bulbs caused the light fixture to melt and the refrigerator filled with a burning plastic odor. The consumer also noticed that the light housing has shiften down as well.  Food on the top shelf near the light were warm and melted.  

There are two light bulbs located one on each side of the refrigerator. The consumer removed both bulbs from the refrigerator.  She is currently still using the refrigerator.

The firm has not been contacted but the consumer states that she will contact them.
justification: The incident involved melted light bulb covers and a burning odor, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Run away heating element.

While baking with the in the wall electric oven, the oven overheated after 30 minutes of use, When the door was opened after 30 minutes of baking everything appeared OK. Fifteen minutes later we smelled smoke and the dish had burned. The oven was overheated and could not be turned off. Couldn't turn of the extremely hot oven off using the oven controls. The controls were inoperative. Circuit breaker was thrown to stop the oven. There should at least be a power cut off switch that would turn off the power to the unit. This was never a problem with mechanical controls.
justification: The incident involved an overheating oven that caused smoke and burned food, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
electric range purchased in January, 2009, then in 2010 he purchased a refrigerator & when the installer brought the refrigerator he asked if the caller had obtained the remedy for the recall of his range.
When he checked he found that although his model matched the recalled appliances his serial number did not.  The manufacturer at that time still repaired his unit but has informed him that they will not repair it at their cost at this time.                                                    

The range now heating on the right to temperatures exceeding set temperature.
example if set at simmer (2.5) it still heats continually.

Range is easily turned off.

Caller would like his range investigated, recalled and repaired at manufacturer expense.
If Range has been repaired by consumer by this time he would ask  to be reimbursed at manufacturer expense.
justification: The range is overheating but can be easily turned off, indicating a potential hazard without reported injury.

incident_description:
My wife was simmering sausage in a 2 quart pot (half filled) on the back right burner. She turned away and went to the sink which is about 3.5 feet. She was at the sink for about 1.5 seconds and the cooktop shattered (blew-up). The glass was tempered and about 99% stayed intact. Pieces of the remaining 1% of the glass was found up to 22 feet away from the cooktop. My wife got hit with some of the glass (some pieces were found in her hair), but she was not injured and no medical attention was needed. My daughter was in the family room, the most distant area where glass was found, she was not hit with any flying glass. I received a cut on the bottom of my foot from a piece of glass ( during the clean up stage). My wife removed it and no other medical attention was needed. I called Bosch on 12/03/12 (Monday) to report the incident. If my wife happened to be in front of the cooktop she very well would have incurred some serious injuries or possibly been fatally injured.
The Bosch cooktop was purchased in 10/23/99 and was installed sometime in December 1999 during the the final phase of construction. I have had many issues with this product and have work orders from 2004,2005,2006,2009,2011. The last three occasions were installation of an enhancement kit: NHT72# AUC Field Kit, 820119. The kit calls for the following parts to be changed: Valve Bypass Screws (L.P.), Burner Orifices (L.P.), Gas Tubing (Valve to Burner), Burner Mounting Brackets, Burner Gaskets, Spark Igniter, GasRegulator (4" to 5"), Rating Label, Burners will be changed and rotated. The last kit was installed on Dec. 2009. 
Bosch Model NHT726A, Serial # 78111244

incident_description: While baking cookies I opened my Kenmore oven to place a pan of cookies in the oven when the inner glass exploded.  The stove was one week away from being a year old.

incident_description:
(11/02/2101) The consumer stated that she turned the oven on 450 degrees and it started to pop immediately. Flames started to shoot from the back of the display panel. The consumer state that she pushed the off panel button and pulled the stove out in the middle of the floor. The flames extinguished on its own after about 45 seconds. incident_description: My Kenmore Elite Dishwasher 8 yrs old caught fire.  First we heard a pop, then a few electrical arcing sounds.  Smoke was coming out and my wife saw a flame starting as I was headed to turn off the breaker.  The unit was just starting a cycle.  Glad we were home and nearby when it started.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the description of electrical arcing and flames.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite Dishwasher Model # 665.1643300.  Smelled smoke about 10 minutes after starting it.  Luckily I was home.  I went in the kitchen a saw smoke going up from the circut board and flames shooting out from under the board and up toward the countertop.  I unlatched it.  It was still smoking, snapping, and shooting out flames.  I turned the electrical switch off under the sink and it stopped.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite french door refrigerator with freezer drawer, model 795.7757360, Serial No. 605KR02646. I noticed a burning plastic/melting smell inside the refrigerator compartment. The clear plastic cover on the refrigerator light had melted, deformed and fallen away. The two light sockets were discolored brownish. It was clear the interior lights in the fridge had been staying on while the door was closed. Light could be seen around the door seals when the doors were closed. Activating the door switches manually indeed did not turn off the lights. Unplugging and replugging the fridge did not resolve the issue. 

Safety hazard 1: Fire hazard. It is clear the fixture is not safely designed for standard appliance bulbs. Under normal operation, this is not an issue, as the lights are lit for only a minute or two at a time, and then the refrigerator itself cools everything down. However, with the light stuck on, the fixture began to melt even inside a closed, operating refrigerator, and could have started a fire or ignited paper wrappings or other materials stored on the top shelf.

Safety hazard 2: Food safety hazard. The incandescent appliance bulbs were constantly generating heat inside the refrigerated storage compartment, raising the storage temperature of products near the light. The neck of a beer bottle near the lights was warm to the touch. creating potential food safety issues.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard and a food safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Was cooking dinner using two burners and pre-heating the oven when the back of the range started to pop and crackle and flash. Smoke and flames came out of the back of the range where the control board is mounted. 

Kenmore smooth top oven
model #790.96614401

incident_description:
GE Dishwasher (Model # GSD4200J00WW) . I started dishwasher as I normally do. Left house for extended period of time (24 Plus Hrs) and returned to find the timer/selection rotary switch had not moved from the plate warmer setting. Also the motor was running and the heating element was still on.
Also noticed that the detergent cup had not opened and the dishes were dirty, as if no water had been introduced. I had several plastic lids in the top rack that had melted down onto the bottom rack.
Smell of burnt plastic throughout the house as well. I had to unlatch the door to stop the machine. The switch wouldn't budge. I also shut it off at the house electrical panel as well to be sure it was off.
Seems very dangerous to not have some type of thermal shutdown in case of an event like this.
I contacted GE and there only offer was to "discount" another dishwasher. Well....their idea of a discount was about  $100 more that I could buy one and have it delivered and installed. rather ridiculous I think. Even though the unit was out of warranty, there was an obvious malfunction that could have been catastrophic. I will go out of my way to avoid any GE appliances in the future since I felt their lack of concern and less than fair offer doesn't deserve my patronage.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing property damage (melted plastic) and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Our Kitchenaid dishwasher is 8 years old. It caught on fire December 9th. and the dishwasher would not turn off. My husband turned off the power at the breaker switch. We usually run the dishwasher at night when everyone has gone to bed. This night we started it early so when the fire started my family was able to respond immediately. The fire dept responded but the fire was out by the time they arrived
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was extinguished without injury or death, and the family was able to respond immediately.

incident_description: The pilot on my Gas Range Amana Standard Cleaning Gas Range (Model # AGR3311WDW1; Serial # VEO3301791) comes on on its own.  I only turn the gas on when I need to use it to cook or bake something.  I am not sure when this began, my best guess would be in August.  I didnt know what to do as this appliance came with the home when I bought it and I have only been in the home since 10/2010.  At first I thought it was an oversight but than began paying closer attention to it and realized it was coming on (the pilot would ignite) but it would not fire up as the thermostat was not turned up and then would go out within a minute or two.  Since I am on a tight budget and in all honesty did not know where to turn until I saw the report on the Electric Range that had a mind of its own and that you were able to assist those consumers.  I thought that perhaps I could get some assistance resolving this issue as well.
justification: The pilot light igniting on its own poses a potential safety hazard but has not resulted in injury or death.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the gas range right burner displays an ignition failure.  It would not ignite and when it did it would make a noise similar to a minor explosion.  There would also be an odor of gas while attempting to use the burner.  The grids on the burners are too smooth which causes containers (pots and pans) to slide off posing a burn hazard.

The manufacturer was contacted and a service rep was sent out on 10/24 but the problem was not resolved.  She was informed that someone would get back in touch with her but no one did.

The caller is concerned that this range is a safety hazard and should be reported.

incident_description:
Maytag Gas Range MOD: MGR7662WB 1   SER: R00514282.  A safety concern I have noticed with this range is the physical location of the control knows are above the oven door.  If the oven is used for approx 2+ hours, the knobs soften and it is not possible to turn off stove top burners.  If the knobs are removed, it is often difficult to turn the stove top burners off using pliers.  It appears as if the brass valves swell due to heat and cannot be turned off.  A few times, I have been forced to pull the stove away from the wall, while the oven and burners were lit, to turn off the natural gas supply causing the burners to extinguisher. This, of course allows the necessary cooling so he gas valves can be closed.

I have called Maytag a few times on this, beginning 11/2/2012, again on 11/20/2012, both times being promised a call back form someone in the "safety" department.  A final attempt on 12/10/2012 was met with resistance from Maytag simply stating "we have no complaints of that problem".  I am unable to get any results from Maytag.
justification: The incident describes a safety concern with the gas range that could lead to inability to turn off burners, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Inner oven door spontaneously shattered while oven was at 350 degrees F
justification: The incident involved spontaneous shattering of the oven door without reported injury, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
Front Oven Door Shattered

On November 26 at approximately 8:30 pm I got up from watching TV in my back bedroom and proceeded to walk to the kitchen to get a drink of water.  The kitchen light was off and it was dark.
I stepped into the kitchen where I remembering slipping and started to fall to the floor.  That was one of the last things I remembered.
I later found out that I slipped on broken glass, that was in a million pieces on my kitchen floor, from my G.E. oven that had shattered without my knowledge.  
A friend was going to stop by that evening which she did and was banging on my door as I didn't answer.  She later told me she was calling my name, continued banging, was getting worried and was going to now call my home on her cell phone.  What I was later told I eventually opened the door looking dazed and confused.  The front door once opened and you enter you can see the kitchen.  She screamed and said "oh my God, what happened."  I looked and she said I responded "I don't know."  She told me she then asked me if I was hurt.  She again told me I replied "I hurt my elbow."  She looked at it and saw that I had glass in my elbow and removed it and she told me she put something on the elbow to clean it out.  
Not knowing until the next morning when I woke up that I had blood on my pillow.  I sat up in bed and my head touched my head board.  I felt a lot of pain.  I touched the back of my head which had glass in it.  I called a friend to immediately come to my house to take a look.  Once here she looked at my head and pulled glass out and again put some cleaning liquid on my head.  I had glass in my bed from the fall.  We now realize that I was unconscious from slipping on the broken glass.
I went to the emergency room, had CT Scan, X-rays to find I suffered a concussion, injured both elbows and my neck.

This is the second time glass has shattered in my oven.  The first time that I used it the inside glass shattered.  Now the outside shattered and I hadn't used my oven in a few days.

It's been brought to my attention, that this has happened to many consumers.  G.E. blames the consumers for a problem that is theirs.

This could have been a lot more serious situation, I could have fell face first into the glass, or my dog or a friend could have been seriously injured or even death.

I'm continuing with my treatment for my injury's and I hope that you will be able to get G.E.'s attention this time around.
My G.E. case # [REDACTED]  Their phone# 800 386-1215
My friend took pictures of the oven, the shattered glass and my injury's.  I couldn't up load them but I do have them.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including a concussion, injured elbows, and neck, and required emergency room treatment.

incident_description:
I have a freestanding gas range from Frigidaire that was purchased about June, 2010. The model # is FGGF3041KFF; the serial # is VF01456583.

Per a service visit and customer service from Frigidaire, the range has no safety mechanism to either reignite or cut off gas, should a flame go out on the rangetop.

When the flame gets too low, it goes out. And it does not reignite.
justification: The gas range lacks a safety mechanism to reignite or cut off gas if the flame goes out, posing a potential hazard, but no incident or injury has been reported.

incident_description: I moved into the Berkshire Apartment at Hoffman Estates on Nov 25 and one week later when my Wife was cooking on the cooking range the Flames just broke open like a burst and burnt my wife's hair and parts of her face. This was a Kenmore appliance and probably 20 years old
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the wife's hair and face, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Tonight I cooked cabbage, carrots, and potatoes in a pot on the stove. I took the top off the pot and let the food cool for about 20 minutes before placing it in my 9x13 Pyrex dish for storage. It was cool enough to touch, but still warm.The dish was on the room temperature countertop. I had put about 3 scoops of food, drained of liquid, into the dish when it exploded EVERYWHERE. I got a small cut on my arm and another on my cheek from a shard of glass. Thank god my pets weren't in the room. The glass went everywhere within a 6 foot radius. There were large pieces and VERY tiny pieces. I just received this dish as a shower present. There were NO cracks, dings, or any other problems. The food was warm, but not hot. This was the first time I used this dish. I got a whole set of Pyrex for my shower that I'm now afraid to use. From what I am reading on other sites, this is a pretty common occurrence with newer Pyrex (manufactured in the last 12 years or so). It appears that the company is blaming every incident on consumer misuse when this is simply not the case. Pyrex is extremely expensive and I now have an entire set that I'm afraid to use. The worst part? When I received this set I gave my old bakeware to Goodwill. So now I have nothing to cook in. Even if the company is willing to send me a new dish, I will not accept it. This bakeware is dangerous. It should be recalled and a full refund should be offered for this entire bakeware set. Would you trust it with your pets or children around? I certainly don't.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts on arm and cheek) from glass shards, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) based on the description of similar incidents being common with newer Pyrex products.

incident_description:
Pyrex glass lid shattered in oven -
On Nov 12, 2012 I purchased 3 Pyrex glass lids from Corningware, Corelle & more at 114 Pine st Corning NY.  I still have the receipt.  Tonight, 12/7/2012, I put a baked ziti leftover from the refrigerator into a Corning 1.5 qt casserole and placed one of the glass lids on top of the casserole.  I turned on the oven, placed the covered casserole inside and closed the door.  The oven had preheated to 190 degrees, when we heard a "pop" sound.  We looked in the oven and saw that the Pyrex lid had shattered and was all over the bottom of the oven and inside the casserole dish.  I have pictures.  The imprint on the 2 remaining glass lids are "23 PYREX A7C A" & "27 PYREX A7C A".  We have used the one labeled  "27 PYREX A7C A".  at least once without incident.  I do not know what the imprint on the shattered glass was.  I am reporting this for you to take action.  Thank you.
justification: The Pyrex glass lid shattered in the oven, but there was no mention of injury, making it an incident without injury. The occurrence likelihood is possible as similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description:
We bought a house exactly a year ago. The oven had a strange smell when turned on like plastic burning but nothing that we could see. Thanksgiving last month the oven had a runaway temperature issue that popped up. We followed the instructions from the manual to unplug and replug in the oven. It appeared to be ok and started functioning again. Then a couple days ago it stopped working.  We opened up the backpanel to see what part might be having a problem and discovered that the plastic had melted. [REDACTED]
This explains why it smelled of burning plastic. This oven is only 1 year old and it's a good thing that it stopped working as this could have burned down the house. I look online and I see a number of people who have had similar unresolved issues. This is dangerous and shouldn't be allowed to continue.
justification: The oven malfunctioned with a burning plastic smell and a runaway temperature issue, posing a fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

I thought maybe I did something wrong, so I made another one and it worked fine.  This was in July of this year.  Then on 12/1/12 I went to make a pumpkin pie and it burnt it.  Again my oven thermometer registered 550 degrees.  So I let it cool and the next day I made another one, same thing.  So I gave up, called my repair man.  When he came he turned it on and it did it again.  He said it would cost me $300+ to fix it.  I had to have 3 boards replaced in it 14 months before that because the burners wouldn't turn on anymore.  That was expensive as well.  I am truly disappointed in my LG oven.  I spent alot of money buying LG appliances for our new home and certainly didn't expect to be paying repairmen this soon!

incident_description: I have a GE brand Food Processor bought at Walmart a year ago or so.  It is 14 cups and model number 169203.  I have been having trouble with the plastic parts of the processor chipping off and getting into the food product, putting my family at risk for ingesting plastic shards. I had this happen right when I got the unit and then was careful to watch for additional chips and not use that food.  Yesterday the plastic post that the chopper blade seats down on failed and put lots of little plastic shavings and powder into the food.  This is a repeating problem so yesterday I searched the internet for the modle and found that it had been recalled for a different propblem, but I thought you should be aware of the food contamination issue as well.  I wonder how many times I missed very small plastic chips getting into food?
justification: The incident involves plastic parts chipping into food, posing a risk of ingestion but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her daughter was using the oven on the baking feature and approximately 15 minutes she noticed smoke coming out from behind the range. The consumer stated that her daughter pulled the range out and she noticed flames behind the control board (located above the burners). The consumer stated that she immediately unplugged the range and the flames went out. 

The consumer stated that her daughter opened the window and placed a fan in front of the range towards the window. The consumer stated that it took approximately 20 minutes for the smoke to dissipate. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the fire department and they measure the heat being release by range. The consumer stated that the fire department informed her that the fire had completely gone out. The consumer added that the fire was limited and contained inside range. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they offered 50% a new product. The consumer stated that she declined, because she believed it should be completely replaced. She stated that the manufacturer informed her that her range was out of warranty. The consumer stated that the manufacturer offered $100 gift card and the consumer also declined. 

The consumer stated that the manufacturer sent a technician to her home 10/19/2012 and they informed her that she would need to pay $237 for parts and labor. 

UPDATE:
After numerous contacts to 1-800-4-my-home, Customer Services at Sears and Sedgwick Insurance between 9/24 and 10/23, I Have opened up a claim/report with CPSC.  Sears is not going to give me a stove that does not set itself on fire, and they told me that they do not recall appliances, that the CPSC does. They will replace it if it is on recall, which it currently is not.  I asked if they cared that a 15 1/2 month old stove burst into flames. They said they understand my frustration and appreciate me shopping at Sears. I have enclosed 8 photos of an appliance in excellent maintenance whose wires behind the control panel ignited upon using the oven.  I have also enclosed a 5-page report from the fire department.  The stove will be stored in my garage for anyone who cares to look at it.  Please do what you can to get this stove off the market, or at least hold someone accountable for its replacement.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries, and the fire was contained and extinguished without spreading.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she had just finished cooking, using the cook top and the oven.  Fifteen minutes later the unit caught on fire.  It was not turned on at the time.  She says for the past several weeks the large burner would turn on without being turned on and would heat to different temperatures than selected. 

The flames shot out of the back of the unit, from the control board.  The consumer says that she contacted the Sears and they informed her the unit is not on recall.  She then contacted the manufacturer who told her they would not handle it. 

The consumer says that the flame disintegrated itself.  She pulled the stove away from the wall.  She says the control board was melted and burned.  It smelled of an electrical fire.  No other damage was done to her home.  Her husband shut off the circuit breaker.  

This unit is experiencing the same thing as listed in recall # 09-333.  Her serial number falls outside of the range of the recall but her model number matches.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a malfunctioning stove, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I am a Baking&Pastry student at Savannah Technical College, and also recently received my Culinary Art Degree.  I was preparing dinner for my family when I tried to turn on the oven light,  it would not work so I thought something was wrong so i backed away and looked in and out of know where the oven glass shattered into a million pieces.  This is very unfortunate with christmas being right around the corner, and my mothers family coming to visit which we hopefully get a see once every two years.  We were told the earliest someone could come out would be December 24th which is Christmas Eve.  My mother spoke with numerous people first she spoke to a represetative from sears that had never heard of this incident before, and that the manger would give her a call tomorrow.  At this point she was frantic and distraught at the thought of me getting injured.  While she was on the phone I researched mulitple cases of this happening that even made the news. Next she spoke to a kenmore warrenty department representative that had never heard of this even and apologized for it happening.  Next she spoke to a representative to set up an apointment unfortunately we were told they could not get to us until December 24th, but they would try there best to get this resolved sooner.  Even though our warrenty is not out until March my mother fears there could another accident in the future, and someone in my family could easily get hurt.  We believe the public should be well aware of this happening and be warned.  We appreciate your assitance in this matter.

We immediately unplugged the appliance and extinguished the fire.    Fortunately, we were home at the time and the fire was limited to the refrigerator unit. incident_description:
Kitchen Aid Dual Fuel Double Oven Range - Model #KDRS505XSS01

Cooking 2 sweet potato casseroles in [REDACTED] 9"x9" glass casseroles in lower of 2 ovens.  Lower oven has 2 shelves - 1 "normal" the other is a roll-out rack.  The 2 casseroles were on the roll-out rack.  When attempting to gently pull the roll-out shelf out to remove the casseroles, they slid towards the back of the rack and ultimately slid off the back of the rack and landed in the bottom of the oven.  My pull on the rack was very gentle - as verified by the person in the kitchen with me - and should not have caused the casseroles to move with such force.  The glass casseroles may have contributed to the movement but the roll-out rack has nothing on the back of the rack to prevent this from happening.  Clips to hold the entire assembly in place might also help stabilize the roll-out rack.  Sustained minor burns on my hand.

incident_description: Maytag gas range model# MGR8880AB. The oven had several problems but most importantly, when the oven is set to 400F or more, it cannot stop preheating. The needle of a separate oven thermometer strained past 550F (the thermometer's upper limit) and the oven was still preheating. We don't know how high the temperature really got and we shut off the oven when we realized what was happening so luckily, nothing bad happened. We've called Maytag's customer service hotline and Maytag sent a repair company which has unsuccessfully tried 4 times in the past month to fix this problem. We were told by the repair company that it's a control module problem. They've tried replacing the module twice with new parts ordered from Maytag. The first time they tried replacing it, the repair guy told us that the new part was defective so he had to order another new part. The second time he replaced it, the oven still gave us the same problems. We've spoken to Maytag's reps several times but they've refused to replace our product or even refund us and are insisting that we have the repair company send someone out as many times as necessary to fix the oven. We're very worried because it's a gas range with a defective control panel that can't seem to be repaired or even diagnosed by experienced repairmen.
justification: The oven's failure to stop preheating poses a significant safety risk, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Wife cooked 2 pizza bread slices at 350 deg. An hour later she noticed the oven seemed very hot. 
I placed cooking thermometer in oven: 347 deg. 
Checked further discovered that all indicators were in their normally off setting. 
Pressing Stop/Cancel had no effect. 
Unplugged oven and inserted power tester inline with power cord. 
Replugged and found oven drawing 551 watts. 
Tried controls again - set oven to broil, timer to 0:30 (seconds), start - did not count down, Stop/Cancel did turn element off. 
Power reduced to ~4 watts. 

Left thermometer in oven with alarm set to 122 deg. 
Checked several times during the night. 
21 Nov 2012 11:00 oven turned on without being touched and thermometer sounded alarm, Power = 530 watts.
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunctioning and turning on by itself, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: I was shopping for a Juicer in Best Buy Store On February 2, 2012.  At approximately 920p.m.  I was injured while inspecting  a Cuisinart Juicer on display in Best Buy Store in Laurel, MD.  As I was examining the product, I reached for the handle when the metal strip on the handle closed and trapped the fleshy part of my palm between the thumb and index finger.  The metal part slammed on the hand.  There is no release button.  I had to call out for help as I could not remove my flesh from the product.  My had was securely and firmly trapped in the handle.  I called out for help.  A Best Buy Sales Associate ([REDACTED]) was nearby.  He came over to assist.  He could not get the handle unlocked.  He attempt to slide my flesh out but it was to painful.  The slight manipulation of the Juicer caused excruciating pain.  He finally took a pocket knife out of his pocket to and used it it lift the metal bar to release my hand.  Upon release I suffered a small laceration on the inside of my hand that was trapped under the metal strip and the handle.  My palm blanched white due to lack of blood circulation for approximately 4 minutes.  The palm of my hand was swollen.  My hand was  severely pale at the site that was trapped.  The palm of my hand was  moderately swollen, red and painful for one week after the injury.  This is a dangerous Juicer.  The two part handle has no warnings on it.  This incident happened in the Best Buy Store.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, swelling, and prolonged pain, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such specific injuries from juicer handles are not common.

incident_description:
As my wife was preparing grilled cheese sandwiches in our Cuisinart frypan on med high heat, one of the rivets shot off of the pan with a loud report like a gun, becoming a very hot projectile of metal. After richocheting off the range hood landed on the counter on a plastic bag where it became lodged. After coming my wife down and taking a few pictures, I contacted the customer service department of Cuisinart where the young lady told me to send the pan to them and they would determine whether the pan was defective and they would replace it with they're lifetime warranty. When I told her that my wife and I were concerned that it could happen with any of the rest of the set she remarked that since there was no injury that was all she could do. I told her to have her superiors call me and assure me this could not happen with the rest of the cookware set. I have heard no response from them.
 I searched the Internet to see if this was a fluke and found other instances of Cuisinart cookware rivets exploding off as they were being used. I believe the company is aware of this and should stop producing dangerous products that could potentially hurt someone or worse. The other defective products had different model numbers which make me think this is widespread throughout their product lines.
 Their failure to reply or communicate shows a lack of concern or responsibility.
justification: The incident involved a hot metal projectile but no injury, and similar incidents have been reported online, indicating a possible but not certain risk.

incident_description:
Product: Kenmore Electric Oven/Range
Model: 790.95301100
Serial: VF13410726
Problem: Oven would not shut off

I turned the oven on to preheat and cook a meal as usual and after the meal was finished I turned the oven off to go eat. About 30 minutes later I noticed a strong burning smell then my oven started to beep. I Went in to the kitchen and noticed my oven was smoking and beeping and displaying a error code on the display of "F1" I opened the oven and noticed the bottom coils were bright red/orange, apparently the oven did not turn off. So I attempt to turn the oven on, then back off and nothing seemed to work. My last option was to run downstairs to switch off the breaker and completely shut down the power to my appliances.

A few hours later after the oven finally cooled down I flipped the breaker switch back on hoping to reset the unit. However as soon as I switched the breaker on, the oven immediately started to heat up again. So, I now have the breaker off and defective Kenmore oven that I can't use. Thankfully I was home when this occurred or it could have very easily burned my entire house down.

I did some research on several website and noticed that there were recalls on many Kenmore ovens a few years back with the exact same problem however my serial number was not one of them.

The temperature goes much higher than it is supposed to.  If you walk away from the stove for a moment your food will be burned.  We have burned many meals on this stove.  

You can turn the stove off and the burner will stay on and get hotter and hotter for hours until you go behind it and unplug it.  Sometimes you will cook on one burner and the other one starts going.  It gets so hot that you cannot hold your hand within a foot of it.

I said, how can that be, when it's doing exactly the same thing as the recalled stove.  No offer of help was given.

My wife called again today, and was told they would charge us $75 just to come look at it.  

If there were children in our house, someone would've been badly injured by now.  This stove is dangerous.

The other recall is listed here: http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml09/09333.html   It is clearly the exact same problem.  I am unsure why Kenmore refuses to help us.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidare Range(Model # FGGF3032KB   Serial # VF13055862) in November, 2011, and since that time gas flowing from the burners without igniting has filled our kitchen on 3 occasions.  We were lucky we did not have an explosion or become asphyxiated. So if the knob gets bumped to the left less than ÃÂ¼ to ÃÂ½ inch off center, the gas will flow and you need to turn the knob about a ÃÂ¼ turn to the left to start the clicking noise for the burner to ignite. 
We are adults, have no children in the home, and have had gas ranges for over 30 years.  We have had none like this range that has knobs so easily depressed by bumping against them to cause gas to flow without the operator being aware of it. 
We contacted Frigidare customer service on 3 occasions, once by email and twice by phone, to see if the range has any recalls or a ÃÂfixÃÂ for this problem.  They maintain that it is user error and the range is constructed within company standards. If we had small children in our home they could easily turn the knob so the gas flows out, as the knob is so easily depressed. The history of my last 2 contacts with them are as follows:

Most recently I emailed Frigidare Customer Service and corresponded with [REDACTED].  These are copies of the email content:

Check to see if they lock out when you turn them off. If they don't then you need to call our customer service department at 800-944-9044 and let them assist you in setting up a service call to have the range checked.
