The drawer is not referred to and there are NO warnings about opening while the oven is on. This is an accident waiting to happen, and they have no intention of recognizing that.
justification: The incident resulted in a 3rd degree burn, indicating a severe injury, and the issue is likely to recur due to the design flaw and lack of warnings.

incident_description:
Frigidaire ES510 electric range - ceramic cooktop with bake -n - warm double oven.

Burners turn on by themselves.  The burner turns red-hot and I am unable to turn off the burner- I have to unplug the range for the cooktop to turn off
justification: The burner turning on by itself and becoming red-hot poses a burn hazard, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
Caller purchased glass loaf pan which is approximately 9" x 3" .

She was baking bread on September 24th, 2012, had set oven on 330 degrees, was using an old loaf pan.  The old pan was [REDACTED].  The new one was made by Anchor Hocking.  Bread had been baking for approximately one half hour when the caller heard what sounded as if something had exploded.

She returned to the kitchen, turned the oven light on and then looked inside the oven seeing that the new loaf pan had exploded, sending glass chards all over the oven as well as onto the bread in the old pan that did not explode.

Caller slowly opened the oven door, couldn't think of what to do and actually is not remembering what she did. She removed the glass pan by sliding what she could onto a cookie sheet, hoping to save the other bread.  Not possible.  The other loaf was coveered with glass slivers.

She called the manufacturer September 25th, 2012 and was first asked if anyone had been injured and then advised by them to send the glass chards to them.
Caller was instructed to check oven by setting the oven on higher temperatures to see whether her oven was functional and operating normally.
Caller's oven was fine.
She will be checking it's function while on self cleaning and then after returning to normal function this weekend. Self-clean is ok.
The consumer was instructed to ship the glass chards to manufacturer for testing, which she did. 
 
There were no injuries
justification: The incident involved a glass loaf pan exploding in the oven, but there were no injuries reported.

incident_description: A small Pyrex baking pan fell out of an open cupboard and onto the countertop.  The pan broke into thousands of tiny shards that resulted in cuts on my hands.  The advertising for Pyrex pans says that when the glass breaks it is suppsed to break into large pieces that don't have sharp edges - not shards.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts on the hands, which qualifies as an injury, and the occurrence is possible given the unexpected breakage of the pan.

incident_description: Shortly after starting the dishwasher the control panel starting smoking and had flames coming out. I attempted to shut the power off at the control panel as I called 911. It would not shut off so I had to flip the circuit breaker off. The flames and smoke started to decrease so I asked the dispatcher if the fire department still needed to respond. I was told that yes they did. They have all the info on make, model and what damage was done I their report.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the situation was controlled by turning off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: I had a Pampered Check ice cream scoop that exploded on my wife. In reviewing the recall sheet, the information states the scoop was sold between July 2010 - September 2010. Our scoop is much older than 2010, but had the exact same issue with the end cap blowing off the scoop and striking my wife in the face. I have contact Pampered Chef who has requested the scoop. Before sending, I want to check with the CPSC as to whether your office would like the scoop, as opposed to the manufacturer/distributor.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (striking the wife in the face), but similar incidents are unlikely given the specific and dated nature of the product.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he put the dishwasher on the ÃÂauto-cleanÃÂ cycle which usually last 2 hours. The consumer stated that approximately an hour later the consumer hear a loud explosion. 

The consumer stated that the first loud noise put a hole of approximately 1/4 ÃÂon the right top side of the door. The consumer stated that smoke was being emitted from the front top area of the dishwasher. The consumer stated that he also smelled a plastic burning odor. 

The consumer stated that he immediately open the door to stop cycle and then turned off the circuit break. The consumer stated that he opened the windows and doors to ventilate the kitchen. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that they could send a service technician to look at the product. The consumer stated that he would be contacting the manufacturer to schedule an appointment. The consumer stated that he was unsure if he would have to pay for the service.
justification: The incident involved a loud explosion and smoke emission, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a 7 qt. KitchenAid Pro Stand mixer. Upon unpacking it, I found that it had a substantial amount of metal shavings located in the front accessory drive port. Some of the metal shavings could be easily cleaned, but some cannot. There are metal shavings behind the permanently attached trim ring for the front port. The consumer can't clean this area but the metal shavings could easily migrate and fall into the unit's mixing bowl with use. The accessory drive port is located directly over the mixing bowl.
justification: The presence of metal shavings poses a potential hazard if they migrate into food, but no injury or harm has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had the oven on the ÃÂbaking featureÃÂ for 400 degrees. The consumer stated that it was on for approximately 20 minutes before it switched to broil on its own. The consumer stated that his wife heard a noise and she checked the oven and it had switched to broil. 

The consumer stated that it did not say ÃÂbroilÃÂ on the control panel. The consumer stated that he was unaware of the temperature. 

The consumer stated that he turned off the oven, turned it on to bake and it immediately changed to broil. The consumer stated that he turn off the circuit breaker and the oven started to work properly again. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they sent a technician on 10/01/2012. The consumer stated that the technician informed him that the control board was bad and needed to be replaced. The consumer stated that they informed him that he would have to pay 360 dollars to have it repair. The consumer stated that he did not make a decision on whether he would repair it. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he believes his oven was experiencing the same hazard stated on release # 09-333. 

The consumer stated that he will be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.
justification: The consumer stated that no one was injured, but the oven switched to broil on its own, which is a hazard.

incident_description: Operated oven earlier in the day.  5 hours after use the outer glass pane in the oven door suddenly exploded outward by itself putting safety glass shards across the kitchen.  There was no contact with anything prior to the incident. This appliance in 1 yr 7 months old.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, causing safety glass shards to spread, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore electric range  
model number 790.9742  p/n 316902001(0904)

Exploding glass is definately a safety concern. The outside portion of the glass door spontaneously exploded while not even being used. No one was even in the kitchen when this occurred. There are many, many complaints about this issue online and yet no recalls that I am aware of. Thank goodness my 3 year old was in another room. Something needs to be done about this sub-par manufacturer and  the less-than-helpful store  (Sears) that continues to carry these faulty products.

I am repulsed by this whole experience and it's extremely dis-heartening that in an awful economy we spend hard-earned money on a product that shouldn't even be allowed to be sold.
justification: The glass door exploded spontaneously, posing a significant safety hazard, but no injuries were reported in this instance.

incident_description:
Our LG Range model number LRE30453, Serial number starting 910 (which was not included in the recall on November 8, 2012) is also having the same issues mentioned in the November 8, 2012 recall.  

Our range turns on randomly.  The temperature rises.  My mother-in-law has actually burned her hand while cleaning the stove because even though everything indicates the stove is off, it still randomly heats up or turns on.  

The most recent incident happened last night.  We have unplugged the stove and will call LG tomorrow to see if they will fix the problem.  This range was bought at Best Buy on or about October 2009.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the mother-in-law, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue occurs randomly and has happened multiple times, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he noticed that the heating element of the range continued to turn on by itself. The consumer stated that the knobs continued to turn on and off by themselves. 

The consumer stated that she disconnected the range and turned off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that her range poses the same hazards stated on the release 11-016. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that her model number was not included on the recall. The consumer stated that the representative offered him to send out a technician but he would need to pay for the diagnostics. The consumer stated that the representative informed her that she would not need to pay for the parts. 

The consumer stated that she believes this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses to the consumer.
justification: The range's heating element turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. The issue is likely to occur given the consumer's description and the reference to a known hazard.

incident_description:
Incident involves a Frigidaire Electrolux professional series smooth top range.
Model # PLEF398CCB
Serial # VF32209768
While using range top front right burner on low, burner switched to high on it's own accord and now will not turn off. Electrical panel breaker must be turned off to get burner to turn off.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On November 14, 2012, my DCC-1200 Brew Central 12-Cup Coffee Maker finished brewing 8 cups of coffee, out of which 2 cups were poured. The coffeemaker was purchased in 9/2010. About 45 minutes later, I noticed a loud popping, hissing and cracking noise coming from the machine while I was in another part of the house. I found the coffee maker to be off (operating light was not lit), and the coffee inside the carafe was on a hard boil. The coffee maker had what seemed like a combination of smoke and steam (smelled like burnt coffee and burning plastic) coming from underneath the carafe and underneath the unit altogether. I immediately unplugged it and took it outside to avoid chance of fire and setting off the building fire alarms. It continued to smoke outside for approximately 10 minutes. I also noticed what appeared like some of the plastic had melted onto the glass carafe. 

I contacted Cuisinart on 11/15/12, who offered to replace it for me at no charge on the condition that I cut off the cord from my defective machine and mail it in at my expense. The customer service rep said she had never heard of this happening before and did not know of any recall/ safety concerns associated with this product.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The customer service rep had not heard of this issue before, indicating it is unlikely to happen frequently.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the grates keep cracking and posing a burn threat.  she says this has happened three times and each time has gotten it replaced.  A technician with the retailer says that it is a serious safety issue.  The technician came out yesterday. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said that they don't  carry that product anymore and told her to deal with it.  

She has to use a wheelchair to get around in her home.  The technician said that they are aware of the problem.  She says that the average life of these grates are two years, then needing replacement.  

The last time the grates were replaced in October of 2009.
justification: The grates cracking pose a burn threat, but no injury has been reported yet. The issue has occurred multiple times and is acknowledged as a serious safety issue.

incident_description:
(9/8/2012) The consumer stated that her dishwasher was running on the normal cycle for approximately 15 to 20 minutes. The consumer noticed that the upper right corner of the door begun to emit smoke. The consumer immediately opened the door and checked to see if anything was touching the heating element, which there was not. The consumer shut the door back and let the cycle continue. Approximately 10 minutes later flames started to shoot out from the upper right corner of the door. The consumer immediately tripped the circuit breaker for the dishwasher and the fire died out.  Damage was limited to the dishwasher.
CONSUMER ADDED:  Faulty control board on dishwasher caused wire harness to catch on fire.  $699.00 estimate to repair per sears technician on 9/10/12

 

-The consumer stated that this was the 1st incident since purchasing the unit in 2004.

 

(9/8/2012) The consumer stated that she contacted the retailer, but she got the appointment line.

The consumer will attempt to contact the mfr. at a later time.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The occurrence is unlikely as it was the first incident since 2004.

incident_description: My dishwasher severely overheated, causing damage to the dishwasher and several items inside.
justification: The dishwasher overheated causing damage to the appliance and contents, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
GE Glass Top Gas Range is not recalled, however the caller reports that it should be recalled.  The range was purchased 2002 but noticed rusting within weeks of receiving product she noticed that there was rust in the burners, door frame etc.  She stated she  tried to scrub it out but could not get it out, she now must use rubber gloves to clean the suface because in the past she received slivers and splinters of paint into her finger tips which took days to get out her fingertips.    

She contacted the manufacturer who sent her parts and cover up but then again the rust began coming through, she contacted the manufacturer again, asking for a representative in her area but there was none.  As she has had splinters, and cut her fingers, she asks that this range be recalled and either repaired or replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: The caller reports receiving slivers and splinters of paint into her fingertips, which caused injury, and she has cut her fingers while cleaning the range.

incident_description: The outer glass of the oven door shattered spontaneously.  No one was near it, thankfully.  It was not on.  We have not turned the oven on for several days.  It was not cracked and we haven't damaged it.  After we cleaned up the shattered glass, we could see rust along the ridge, right where the glass sat in the door.
justification: The oven door glass shattered spontaneously with no one nearby, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Re: GE electric cooktop: Model Number "J P651 0C1AD" (no quotes), S/N ML737797.

Hi U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission,

We have a GE electrical electric cooktop (aka cook top, or cook-top). It has four electric coil elements on a small island in the middle of the kitchen). On Thursday evening 11/8/2012 the coil exploded on fire. The fireball was about one feet with sparks flying out in all directions. I was outside and heard the loud noise it made. My wife was scared to death and shaking when I rushed inside. She was near to the range while incident happened. She had just walked two steps away towards the sink, and thankfully was not scalded by the blast of boiling water and steam that was ejected. The explosion left a black sooty film and spots in a 3' diameter area, all the way to the refrigerator. Thankfully there was only water, and not cooking oil in that pot.The fireball burned a hole in the bottom of the cooking pan too. Also thankfully, the circuit breaker tripped automatically. 

After cooling down, I removed the damaged coil. I also removed the control panel (with the four turn knobs on top) to inspect for further damage. In addition to the blown out area on the heating element/coil, the two wires that run from the control panel knob/switch to the coil had burnt areas on them (one place I could see copper wire poking out).

After cleaning up the mess, I started the circuit breaker again. I saw the burner light does not off even though all the burner switches are off. 
After the incident, I did little on-line research. I was able to find a CPSC report at
http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1201875
That report describes almost exactly what happened to us. Because of the similarity, I did use some of their text as a framework to compose our report here.

I also found CPSC Recall Alert #04-576 at :
http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml04/04576.html?omni_key=Ranges_and_Wall_Ovens_Recall
Our model number JP6510C1AD and S/N ML737797 are not listed in the recall notice.

My wife [REDACTED] called GE Consumer Relations at 1-800-386-1215 and spoke to [REDACTED] at Ext: [REDACTED]. She arranged for a service technician to visit us yesterday on 11/15/2012 (ie. GE Consumer Relations Case# [REDACTED]) . The technician looked at the coil, wires and damaged pot. He told us that it is normal for burners to fail in this way. Honestly, I've known of coils/elements/burners failing over the years, but they normally just stop working, not explode without any warning whatsoever (and damage the control switches in the stove too). He mentioned something about repairs and I told him he was only here to inspect per GE's request, and not repair (at our cost for parts and labor). When I prompted him about the burner light that does not off even though all the burner switches are off, he mentioned something about a short in one of the switches.

Today we received an email from [REDACTED] at GE. She wanted to know how the how the technician's visit went. We have not responded to her yet, pending filing this report with you first.

I have attached photos of the damaged burner, cooking pan and burnt wires. Some were taken on 11/8 and some I took today with my other camera to get (hopefully) better pictures. You ask for a purchase date. We don't know for sure, it came with the house when we bought it back in 2000.

We would greatly appreciate it if you could take necessary action. We have not had use of the cooktop since 11/8/2012. There are three remaining coils/elements on this unit. Based on what happened last Thursday to my wife. I don't think the cooktop is safe for her or anyone else in the house to use. Next time someone might get seriously hurt. Next time it might blow up cooking oil and burn down our house. Next time it might happen at some other unsuspecting residence with a child standing next to it. There is no notice of imminent failure whatsoever.

Please help us. We look forward to your reply or phone call.

Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fireball and sparks causing significant damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
On October 2nd, 2012 the caller was cooking tomatoes for canning on the front right burner of her electric range when she noticed that they were burning.

Since she never cooks on high she kept turning it down but the temperature kept going higher.

She turned the tomatoes down to 4 and walked away for possibly 5 to 7 minutes when she smelled something and returned to the stove and the tomatoes were burning although they had been in plenty of water at a low temperature.
The large pan holds several gallons of liquids (possibly 10).

She threw away all of the tomato solution, cleaned the aluminum canning pan and turned the stove off.
The stove kept coming back on although the element read "off" but he burner was bright red and very hot.
She kept trying until the third try the burner finally remained off for this time.

She contacted the manufacturer 10/10/2012 and was advised to file a report. 
While filing her report with the manufacturer she noticed the phone number for CPSC and decided to call this agency also.

October 9th, 2012 she was cooking donuts in oil on the same front right burner with the same results, she kept turning the burner down but it kep going higher and hotter.
Again it took several tries to turn the burner off but it finally turned off and remained off.

Caller is asking that this range be investigated and recalled.
She is having her range repaired today 10/10/2012 if under $500 or she is purchasing another if over $500 and would ask that she be reimbursed for whichever avenue taken.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that caused food to burn, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The issue occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: about 2 months ago the smooth top units stopped turning off. Then they are spotty as far as turning on and off. Now the oven itself will not turn off and we have to flip the breaker to shut down the oven anytime we use it.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning equipment that requires manual intervention to shut down, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: While baking bars at 350 degrees F, the broiler element continued to heat while the bars burned.  The oven would not shut off or reset.  The only way to rectify was to unplug the oven.  After leaving unplugged for 30 minutes and replugging, the broiler element started up full bore again.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be shut off, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says the electrical assembly, gasket and lining are blackened and melted.  He says 
He contacted a technician who came out today and told him there was a malfunction in the electrical switch which left the lights on inside the refrigerator even when the door closed.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer today who told him that this should not have happened but there was nothing that they can do.  

He said there was a problem 6 months ago with the power supply board which was replaced also by an authorized service dealer.  

He says he had to turn off the power through a switch in the refrigerator.  He said had he not done that it would have started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was previously addressed, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: I have a Maytag Percision Touch Control 700 Electronic Smoothtop Range that I purchased in 2005.  The glass on the front of the door fell out as I opened the oven.  It is held in place mostly by a spongy, double stick tape that failed on the range side.  I put it back in, tightened all the screws, and it fell out again.  I doesn't stay in without the tape.  I see this as a design flaw, using tape that fails under high temperature in a stove!  I wasn't injured, and the glass didn't break, but I can see where people could be injured.  The glass probably wouldn't break, since it's tempered and it only falls a little way. (and the fall is broken by your feet!)
justification: The glass fell out but no injury occurred, though there is potential for injury.

incident_description:
The unsafe product is a GE electric range, model # J BS07 M1WW serial # HV124830P

I was braising a pork roast on low on one of the larger burners.  I set the temperature dial at "2" (dial options are Lo, 1-9, Hi) to maintain a slow simmer.  Two hours later, the pot suddenly started to boil over and the entire burner was glowing red-hot.  The dial was still set to "2."  

Later the same day, I turned the burner back on to see if the same problem occurred.  It did, but not immediately.  The burner seems to work normally for awhile and then turns itself on fully without human intervention.

I believe that this malfunction is "unsafe" and a fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning electric range that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: On 11-17-12, I began self cleaning a new Bosch 27" built in oven.  Within 15 minutes of the self cleaning process a loud pop was heard.  I immediately turned off the self cleaning option and noticed the glass had exploded.  I waited till the self clean light went off and then opened the oven door to find  glass had shattered all into the oven.  I called the Bosch warranty hot line and am being told that this has never happened before but can not be fixed until November 27th. This is leaving me without cooking for nearly 2 weeks.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded oven glass) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Bosch Dishwasher model SHX33A02UC/14 with the serial number starting with FD has the heater relay overheating and burning through the solder connection.  The dishwasher then will not heat the water leaving powdered detergent grit on the dishes.  The dishwasher will also run for hours as it's trying to heat the water.

When looking at the control panel insides you can see the relay has overheated and burned through.  While no fire started I would assume the potential is there.

Bosch had a recall for a similar issue with other dishwashers, I believe the recall was not as wide spread as it should have been.

Thanks for your attention.
justification: The incident involves equipment failure (overheating relay) without injury or fire, but with potential for further issues.

incident_description:
I purchases a Gourmets onemug coffee maker at Discount Drug mart.  It is item #W14A4980.  Model # WM-6101.  SVC Code 3174. It is distributed by Atico International USA, Inc.  In Ft. Lauderdale Florida.

The coffee maker works as promised, however, there are two items that need to be addressed.  It has a small reusable filter basket and the directions say to use 4 tablespoons of coffee.  That fills the basket to the top and it did overflow on me.  (I tested it as it seemed as though that was way to much, it was.)  The second and more serious , after the coffee is done brewing, I let it set for about a minute or so then open the lid to empty the grounds so they do not drip onto the base after I remove the cup.  As soon as you open the lid, some of the remaining moisture drops back into the reservoir and there is a blast of steam that comes out of the lid.  If I were a shorter person, that steam would have hit me in the face.
justification: The incident describes a potential for injury due to steam exposure, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
The Amana 5 cu.ft Self Cleaning Gas Range, model AGR5844VDW2 is unsafe, in that the knobs on the front of the stove do not lock in the off position and easily flip to the gas-on position before finding the "light" position, causing gas to emit into the room without lighting.  In other words, this has happened to me twice when just brushing by with a towel or bag of lettuce, without my knowledge until the gas smell filled the house.  

The first time was when I wiped down the surface of the range.  I had a cold and was home alone for several hours before my husband came home and noticed the "funny smell", which due to my cold I could not smell.  We evacuated and aired out the house.

The second time was when I carried items from the refrigerator and it was probably the bag of lettuce that brushed against the knobs.  There is no noise when it happens, as it doesn't turn all the way to the "light" function wherein the clicking sound happens until the unit fires up.  Again my husband happened to be in the kitchen, and after the first incident watches the knobs more closely and noticed that it happened again.  We caught it before we had to evacuate, or worse before we lit something else in the vicinity.

The range was purchased at The Home Depot in The Dalles, Oregon, on May 14, 2011.
justification: The incident involves gas emission without ignition, posing a risk but no actual injury occurred. The issue has happened twice under specific conditions, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description: Glass front on oven door of Maytag Electric Smooth Top Range shatters and breaks without warning in middle of night.  I own a Maytag Electric Smooth Top Range purchased in December 2009 from Nebraska Furniture Mart in Omaha, Nebraska.  In the early morning hours of November 14, 2012, my wife went downstairs to our kitchen and to her shock found the outside glass window on the door of the Maytag oven had shattered and was strewn on the floor in front of the oven.  The oven had been used at about 6:30 pm the night before and the incident occurred between 12:15 am and 3:30 am.  I do not know how often this occurs but this is a major safety hazard.  Can't imagine if a small child would have been standing by this and it happened.  Very dangerous.  My wife is extremely shaken by this event and even hesitant about using the oven even after it will be fixed.  Thanks for your efforts to address this incident.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering without injury, but poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
The caller stated that he experienced an electrical fire in the dishwasher control panel.  The dishwasher was on (not sure of the amount of time) when he opened the door the cycle was incomplete.   The caller stated that there was no signs of smoke.  The dishwasher became inoperable.  

10/3/12 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that the dishwasher was repaired from a recall 5 years ago and that should have taken care of the failure.  A service rep was sent out 10/4 and he was advised that the control panel was burnt.

The caller feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: Electrical fire in the dishwasher control panel with no signs of smoke or injury, but the appliance became inoperable.

incident_description:
We own a Viking 30" black cook top. The largest and most powerful burner is located in the front, near the on/off knobs. When a large (12 ") frying pan is used on the front burner, the associated knob becomes so burning hot that the inside expands, does grip the metal core and the burner cannot be turned off. It is necessary to lift off the knob with a pot holder and turn off the gas flame with a plier. While this should have been reported earlier, my busy schedule prompted me to simply deal with a ridiculous situation in the above manner.
Recently, a guest in my home tried to help me as I heated up an appetizer and burned his fingers on the knob.

We have reported this to Viking Co. They sent out a technician who was horrified to see that the finish on the stove near the front burner had melted. He took pictures and wrote a report. Viking took months to research this issue and just told us based on their research they will not replace the range top. No explanation was forthcoming.
justification: The incident resulted in a guest burning their fingers, which qualifies as an injury. The issue is persistent and has been observed multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I heard a funny noise coming from the coffee maker and when I bent down to see where the noise was coming from, the hot water shot out and burned my forehead and area around my eyes. I was injured but not enough to seek medical attention. I assumed that the problem was with the [REDACTED]. I returned the box of [REDACTED] to Walmart and purchased a different flavor. A few days later, My wife had the same experience with the burns to the face. We unplugged the coffee maker and stored it in the basement. We disposed of the [REDACTED] we had on hand and returned to the old way of making coffee.
justification: The incident caused burns to the face, but not enough to seek medical attention, which is a level 3 severity.

incident_description: The handle on the Carafe for our Black and Decker model: SDC740B broke loose and the carafe landed on our counter top and broke, spilling hot coffee on my wife from the waist down.  The glass shattered all over the floor.
justification: Hot coffee spilled on the wife causing injury, and the glass shattered, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description:
Over was set a 350 deg on 8 minutes time to bake cookies.After approximately 5 minutes we smelled smoke coming from the oven a found the product blackened and smoking profusely.
Shut the oven off,but the broiler coil continued to glow,even though it was not set for broil,bake only.
Reporting this because of the potential for a fire if not more closely monitored.Never had a problem with the oven before now.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore 790.9611340A Serial # VF72841673
Smooth Top Stove - Left front burner switches to high by itself and will not shut off with control knob.  Only way to shut off is to unplug or turn off breaker.  Very dangerous.  Other 790 models are on a recall list for the same dangerous condition, but I was told by Sears that my model is not.  ??
justification: The stove's burner switches to high by itself and cannot be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I was sitting about 10' away from the dishwasher when I heard a loud sizzling noise that sounded like a short.  I had no idea what it was but when I looked into the kitchen I saw smoke billowing out from the upper right side of the dishwasher door.  The smell was acrid. I opened the door to see if something fell on the element.  Nothing had fallen the smoke was coming from the control panel on the dishwasher door.  I ran and turned off the power at the breaker. I investigated it more by removing the door and the control panel cover to discover the inside of the control panel completely
burnt!  If I had not been right there at the time I'm sure the kitchen would have been in flames.  The smell was horrible and it still lingers.  Thank God I was nearby and was able to take quick action.  Needless to say the dishwasher was removed and I still have the charred remains.

I have since seen and read many reports of the same thing happening to others.  I wonder why nothing is being done to stop this.  Why no recalls?  Why no notification?  Why are stores still permitted to sell faulty equipment that can cost people their lives?
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical fault in a dishwasher that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to quick action.

incident_description:
Please look into recalling LG model LRG3095SB Gas range. The burner valve is too sensitive, when brushed up against turns slightly and opens up the gas valve and leaks gas. I have multiple times reached up to my over the stove microwave and brushed up against the valve and turned on the gas.  It is turned so slightly that you don't even notice that it is even on.  On Sunday night 11/11/2012 my house filled up with gas and upon waking up I smelt gas and noticed that the stove was on. I opened all the windows and called LG the next day.  LG stated unless there is a recall on this gas range it is no longer their responsibility, even if this malfunction cause carbon monoxide related death.  

At a separate occasion they had replace all my stove knobs because they cracked at the stem of the knob so you couldn't see if the stove was on and they replaced them even though my warranty had expired.  I assumed that they did this because of a safety issue but upon talking to them on the above issue they said that it was only a curiosity.  I have seen many complaints about this on-line and LG would not replace the knobs because the warranty expired.
justification: The incident describes a gas leak due to a sensitive burner valve, which poses a significant safety risk but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Several times while using my LG electric range model #LDE3017 ST, the burner has increased settings unexpectedly and burned food. If I don't watch while I cook it could cause a fire.
justification: The burner increasing settings unexpectedly can lead to burned food and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Hotpoint electric oven is shocking me terribly. Occurs when wiping surface down with damp cloth,or touching silver electric eye trim and touching oven handle with dry skin and more severe if hands are wet.

Number on oven door #317B6641P001

Rear knob panel controls (black turning knobs white enamel oven
justification: The description indicates the oven is causing electric shocks, which can result in injury, especially when hands are wet, making it likely to occur frequently.

incident_description:
GE Dishwasher that was a part of the August recall. We had it repaired for the recall on August 22, and today it caught on fire, filled my house with black toxic smoke. Thank God we were at home with the dogs instead of at work. We disconnected the power and have called GE who is going to send their investigative crew out as soon as possible.

So I think people need to know that their repair doesn't work. People could be living with a fire hazard and think all is well if they had the recall fix applied.

Scary to think that the house and the dogs would have been lost had we not been at home to react so quickly.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death occurred as the occupants were present to disconnect the power.

incident_description:
This letter is regarding fire hazard in  refrigerator model Frigidaire FRS23H5ASB8.
 This morning my family woke up to house filled with smoke and smell of burning. We could not locate source of the smoke immediately and we called fire department. Fireman showed up quickly and after searching the house for while identified source of smoke coming from the back of refrigerator. Luckily they were able to disconnect the fridge and stop the fire before spreading and causing damaged to cabinets and the rest of the house. They told us we were lucky this did not happened earlier at night and that we were home and were able to call them quickly. I'm concern that this unit is not safe to use and could be a hazard to my family or others.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard that was contained without injury or death, but posed a significant risk to property and safety.

incident_description: Figidaire electric range model #FEF365ASE Smoothtop Electric Range experienced uncontrolled overheating condition while unit was turned off. Had to use circuit breaker to shut it down. Repeated several times. I see numerous complaints and two recalls but they do not include my model number for some reason.
justification: The incident describes an uncontrolled overheating condition with no mention of injury or death, but it required intervention to shut down the unit.

incident_description: I have an Electrolux Gas range which has a front burner that has a hesitation to light and when it does light it lights extra powerful due to the delay and extra gas release.  We had a tech look at it and he said that it is a performance issue that he sees consistently with the unit.  Sadly, my shirt caught fire a few weeks ago due to the problem and I now avoid usage which is not right if there is a safety issue with product.  The front burner has a extra large performance burner that is causing issues but Electrolux doesn't want to fix the problem I guess. Maybe you can made sure this doesn't cause injury to another person, Electrolux is difficult to work with as a consumer.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (shirt caught fire) and the issue is described as a consistent performance problem, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: my dishwasher is a maytag model MDB4100AWW SERIAL # 27763943ZS IT GETS STUCK I AM GUESSING ITS THE SENSOR BUT IT WILL RUN ALL NIGHT AND MY DISHWASHER IS SUPER HOT CAN BE A FIRE HAZZARD
justification: The dishwasher gets stuck and runs all night, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I started my Whirlpool Quiet Partner II dishwasher on the normal cycle wash at approximately 3 pm on 11/10. I stayed in the kitchen to straighten up and glanced over at the dishwasher to see what I thought was steam coming out of the left hand side vent, about ten minutes later. It looked strange so I went over and put my hand out to find it was not warm like steam. At that moment more smoke quickly  starts pouring out the right side and smells terrible. I open the dishwasher slightly as to not get burnt if there was flames. After a few moments the smoke subsided, strong smell of burning wires and plastic. Water never filled the basin, but the dish soap had been expelled into the bottom. I did not sense heat on the interior. I am glad I was standing right there, had I not been there I strongly feel like it would have flamed and caused major damage. I found that this is happening all across the US and no recall issued yet for many models.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a strong smell of burning, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: GE Profile dishwaser control panel caught fire.
justification: The control panel caught fire, which is an incident but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The front glass on my GE electric range oven shattered.  The oven hadn't been used for 2 days.  At 2:30 in the morning I heard an explosion and jumped out of bed completely terrified!  The glass was shattered into tiny pieces all across the kitchen floor.  The glass was making popping and cracking noises and actually moving on the floor.  I have a video of this.  Has there been a recall that I was unaware of?
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven glass causing a loud noise and scattered debris, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Bosch Dishwasher Model SHE44C05UC purchased 8/30/05 caught fire in the control panel.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, indicating an incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: LG Over-The-Stove Stainless Steel Microwave Model# LMVM2075 ST/01 purchased 9/19/07 sparked, flamed, smoked, and melted the plastic interior on 10/20/12. There was no metal objects within the microwave, only popcorn in paper bag. All contents were removed and briefly turned on again, with same results. Unit is a fire hazard.
justification: The microwave sparked, flamed, and smoked, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I own a LG Electric Range, model number LRE30757ST, mfg in 2009.  I bought it from Best Buy.  One 11-6-12, I set it to self clean.  I noticed a smell that was worse than I have ever smelled when using the clean feature, it smelled like burning rubber, and quickly the house became immersed in the smell, even though we opened all the windows.  It also burned my throat after awhile.  I stayed outside, and soon began to smell the fumes coming out of the house, even though I was sitting quite a ways from my sliding door that was open.  The clean feature had been running for about an hour when I became concerned and went in to check the range.  The top of the range was so hot you couldn't touch it, as well as the stainless steel along the top of the range.  The oven door was just as hot.  I felt the sides of the range, as it sits between two cabinets made of wood.  It smelled hot and I became concerned that it may be burning rubber around the glass top.  I noticed the gasket on the oven door looks burned, and is no longer plyable, it looks stiff from being burned.   I turned it off and haven't used it since.  I have used the clean feature before, and it has never gotten that hot.  It would have caused serious burns if someone touched it without knowing, it seems to me there is no need to lock the oven in clean feature, if the rest of the range is as hot on the outside, as it is on the inside.  Today, 11-8-12, I noticed a recall on this range, (Release # 13-031 dated 11-8-12) so I am submitting this report to inform you, as the recall was because of the burners.  I believe there is something wrong with the oven part of the range, and that I may have had a fire if I had not turned it off.  I will be calling the firm's recall hotline to tell them of this experience and see if they will come and look at it.  I also have a warranty through Best Buy, so I will be contacting them also. LG has informed me it is not covered on a warranty, and will not fix it as it is not a part of the current recall.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and excessive heat, causing throat irritation but no serious injury. The likelihood is rated as likely due to the described conditions and the recall notice.

incident_description: My  Sears dishwasher has caught one fire twice.  Sears refused to replace it and will not even talk to me.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire twice, indicating a recurring incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I started the dishwasher as normal on a regular cycle in the evening.  About 15-20 minutes into the cycle I heard an unusual noise coming from the dishwasher.  I came into the kitchen and could smell melted plastic and could see smoke (not steam) coming out of my dishwasher.  I then opened up the door and when I did a snapping sound occurred and a horrible odor came out with more smoke.  This happened again when I opened the door again to show my husband.  I then removed all the dishes, unplugged the appliance, and left the door shut.  I had a repair person come to check on it who said there was a fire in the front panel and the entire dishwasher would need to be rewired, which is illegal for them to do.  She called to the service department to check on a recall, and they told her they had a number of written complaints about the dishwasher but did not see a recall.  I then called Sears and after approximately 6 phone calls I was told there was no recall and was informed that all service calls related to any faulty appliance is directly reported from the service company to the Federal Agency in charge of recalls.  I then contacted the service company and they told me that Sears had misinformed me: I would have to report the incident myself.  My concern is that someone could have a fire, lose their home, or worse yet, their lives, because there is a fault in this dishwasher.  If I had gone to bed, been out of the house, or even been in a different part of the house and not heard the noise, who knows what could have happened.
justification: The incident caused smoke and a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that approximately 3 weeks ago, the light bulbs in the refrigerator overheated and melted the plastic brackets for the control panel.  This incident blackened the light sockets.  The bulbs was removed to prevent a fire.  No switch to turn off the lights that stayed on.  Faulty circuitry.

9/2012 The service department was contacted and she was advised that there was a safety alert on the refrigerator, however, when she contacted the retailer they told her there was no recall on her model.  She could purchase a service agreement for $300.00.  They then offered her $500 towards a purchase of a new one which would only be $200.00 because she had purchased the agreement.  After 3 weeks she was told no parts to repair.

The caller feels that this refrigerator is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting of components, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On July 14th, 2012 Caller's daughter was visiting and was preparing to baking a meat loaf when the broiler came on automatically. 
Estimated time meat loaf was in oven is about 30 minutes during which time the daughter had left the kitchen and then walked back in to find heavy smoke.

PF code appeared in control panel.

She went to get her mother who shut off all buttons however, the broiler wouldn't turn off. 
They then shut the breaker off. 

She contacted a service company that she had used for repairs previously and who explained that it isn't worth repairing and that this code could affect two parts.

Caller states that she is lucky it didn't burn her house down. 

Caller has not contacted manufacturer but does intend to contact retailer.

Caller would not purchase another of this manufacturer's product again.

She would like to ask the company whether they quality test their products.
justification: The incident involved heavy smoke and a malfunctioning broiler, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as similar malfunctions have been reported.

incident_description:
The dishwasher was running through its normal wash cycle when we heard a loud popping noise.  We were startled to find that the dishwasher door had blown open - while the dishwasher was still running!  

The cause of the failure was a blown heating element.  To get the dishwasher to stop, we had to close the door and then open it again.  The dishes were covered in a fine grit .  The heating element wire was exposed.  The circuit break did not blow.

We are so glad that this happened when we were at home!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with no reported injuries, but potential for harm due to exposed wiring.

incident_description: My dishwasher had been running for about 20 minutes when I heard a pop and noticed flames shooting out of the upper right hand corner, followed by black smoke.  y husband quickly turned off the breaker and the fire stopped.  I am very grateful I was in the room when this happened as we often run the dishwasher while we are asleep and I hate to think what might have happened.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injury or death occurred due to quick action.

incident_description: After turning off the oven last night, the oven started beeping with an error code. When I checked the oven, it was still on, even though it had been turned off. I selected oven on again and then off, and the same thing happened. It would not turn off.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
(9/26/2012) The consumer stated that he was using his toaster oven on the bake setting for 5 minutes. He stepped away and later heard a loud noise. When coming back into the kitchen he saw that the glass door to the oven shattered.

There were no injuries associated with the incident.

(9/26/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and they advised him to bring the unit to the repair location, but they will not cover the expense.
justification: The glass door shattered but there were no injuries, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Gold Cooktop Model is GJC3634.  Care guide book is for all models.

The largest burner or main burner will not turn off completely.  It turns itself back on. If it is turned to use, it cuts self off and heats really high.  This is the same problem as the LG Recall I read about today.  I keep the electric breaker off until I want to use the other 3 burners.

Purchased at Lowes in May of 2002.  This problem began the last week of October of 2012.  I have contacted Lowes online and reported problem today but do not expect to hear from anyone until next week.

Only option given upon calling Whirlpool 1-800-253-130l is to schedule a repair or order parts.  But office is closed for weekend to talk to anyone.
justification: The cooktop burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Earlier in the year, one of my cooktop elements quit working, and the hot warning indicator light did not work on turning off any of the other elements.  I took it apart to replace the element and found that the element was not the problem - the wires connecting the electrical equipment were too short, the assembly worker had to bend the terminals so that they were almost touching to assemble the parts.  The wires were so tightly held together at another location that the constant pressure and heat caused the insulation to melt and an electrical arc resulted.  I have a ppt file with pictures showing this condition
justification: The incident involved an electrical arc due to melted insulation, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Le Creuset Classic Whistling tea kettle on 11/06/11.  When heating water on the stove, at times, just prior to the water coming to a full boil, there is a kind of explosion heard inside the kettle.  If the whistle is not covering the spout, nearly boiling water has shot out almost 3 feet from the spout.  If the spout was not pointed away from me, I would have been burned on the face & neck.  This has happened more than once.  This happens with the water below the level of the spout, and has happened when the burner on the stove was on "medium".
justification: The incident describes a near-miss with potential for severe burns, indicating injury risk (severity 3), and the issue has occurred multiple times (likelihood 4).

incident_description: A Pyrex 2 Qt (024   24)  baking dish was used to bake fish at 350 degrees temp.  As the finished dish was being carried to the dining room table, it shattered into a large number of pieces covering a large portion of the dinner table with large and small shards.  Fortunately , the only injury was a small cut to his hand and some burned fingers.  It was not set on anything and was not in contact with anything cool or cold.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut and burned fingers, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described circumstances of the baking dish shattering.

incident_description:
I have an Emerson microwave model: MW9339SB that was just at the end of the one-year warranty when this incident occurred. A few weeks ago I put baking chocolate in a microwave-safe dish to melt. The microwave immediately began sparking and making loud noises. I immediately turned it off. The chocolate smelled burnt and was not melted. Since then, other foods usually do not cause that same problem, although one time the microwave did spark with a different food item in it. 

I tried two other times to melt chocolate, and every time the same sparking, burning occurred. When contacted, the company said to send a number of parts back and they would send me a new one. However, after reading a stream of similar complaints on the internet, I do not want an Emerson microwave.

Why isn't there a recall as this is certainly a safety issue?

Is there any recourse for the consumer? Apparently they have known about this problem for a long time yet they continue to sell this item.

Any assistance would be appreciated.
justification: The microwave sparked and made loud noises, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My emerson microwave model number MWG9115SL Suffix D is having electrical problems creating what looks like a "lightening storm" inside. After this malfunction kept occurring, I looked online and found that many other people were having this same problem. Emerson should recall this product and replace it.
justification: The microwave exhibits electrical problems ('lightning storm' inside), posing a hazard but no reported injury. The issue is common among users, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Elite French Door Refrigerator. Late in the evening on 10/28/2012. My husband noticed a smell of plastic burning. Upon investigation he detected it was coming from the refrigerator. When he opened the door he noticed the lights were on and the fixture was so hot, it melted the sockets and the plastic cover. It was hot enough inside it heated the food located on the top shelf of the fridge. Had he not noticed before we retired for the evening, this could have resulted in a fire. Luckily there was no fire. He unplugged the appliance. The food on the top shelf was ruined. We tried to save as much as we could move to a smaller refrigerator/freezer, but could not save everything.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual fire or injury, but significant property damage (ruined food and melted components).

incident_description: The consumer says over the last year the dishwasher has been repaired 5 times.  Her husband opened up the dishwasher and found that the control panel was melted, along with other wiring.  She smelled a bad odor coming from it.
justification: The dishwasher has a melted control panel and wiring, indicating a significant incident but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The light mechanism in our LG French door refrigerator (model number LFC25760ST) malfunctioned.  The lights (2 60 watt bulbs) remained on over night even though the refrigerator doors were closed.  The bulbs have a metal reflector above them that heated to the point that it melted the plastic housing, melted a tub of butter on the top shelf and toasted 3 full loaves of bread.  The only way to get the lights to turn off was to remove them, however they were way too hot.  Removing the screws that held the housing in place revealed that the plastic inside was soft to the touch.  We unplugged the lights entirely to break the circuit and prevent further damage and/or potential risk of fire.

We did report the issue to the manufacturer who informed us they were aware of issues like this with our model and several others.  A technician is scheduled to come out. Not sure why if this is such a known issue and so many models are affected, why there hasn't been a recall issued.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted housing, food items) but no injury or death, and the manufacturer is aware of similar issues, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description: Above range micro wave oven comes on in "popcorn" mode randomly without any prior inputs on the keypad.
justification: The microwave turning on randomly is an incident without injury, but it poses a potential hazard if unattended.

incident_description:
Deep fryer control box had wires get too hot and burned through the plastic handle.  Wires exposed and caused burn.  could be bare wires inside and might cause electrical shock.  Others have had the same problem as noted in customer reviews of the item.
Walmart GE mdl 18021915.
justification: The incident caused a burn due to exposed wires, indicating an injury, and customer reviews suggest it's a recurring issue.

incident_description: After the third time of using this coffee pot after about 15 minutes of being on the coffee pot began to smoke and continued to smoke more up to the point of it being unplugged. I believe it would have caught on fire if it had not been unplugged.
justification: The coffee pot smoked heavily and could have caught fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(09/04/2012) The consumer stated that she was roasting a rump roast in her oven. The temperature was set for 300 degrees. The oven had been on for about five minutes. After about  thirty minutes the consumer stated that she open the oven door to place her meat thermometer in the roast. She took the thermometer out and shut the door. She went out of her house to take something out to her recycle bin. She was closing the front door and heard a boom. She went to her kitchen and turned on the oven light. When she turned on the light she discovered that the roast was sitting on the rack and the pyrex dish had exploded. 

The consumer stated that she hit the button and turned the oven off.

The oven was not damaged.

The consumer stated that she was not injured.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex dish but no injuries or oven damage, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents are not uncommon with glass cookware under certain conditions.

incident_description: Started the dishwasher on normal cycle.  After about  at some point during the cycle, my 11 year old son noticed the dishwasher smoking.  We could smell a plastic or electrical fire smell filling the kitchen.  I opened the door to stop the cycle, bu it would not stop. I flipped the dedicated circuit breaker and the smoke and washing cycle stopped.  Turning the breaker back on started the cycle and the burning smell again, so I left the breaker off.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was resolved by turning off the circuit breaker.

incident_description:
Message = Approximately seven years ago I purchased a Sears Kenmore elctric Cooktop, Model 790.4272, P/N 318293825. Four months ago my wife said to me that the "Cooktop was turning on by itself?" At first I assume that she had been cooking, took the pot off the stove and just forgot to turn off the burner...I went over to the stove and all knobs were in the OFF position I then went into the basement to the electric control panel and turned off the breaker to the cooktop and the burners went off...I waited a few minutes and turned the stove back on, and they stayed off. I assume that it was just quirk and went about my business, a few hours later I was watching the Jay Leno show and I smelled something burning...I went into the kitchen and ALL FOUR BURNERS WERE ON...Full high...The knobs were in the off position, I turned the knobs thinking that maybe they were jammed on the wrong way, the burners just kept of burning full power...I went into the basement and this time turned the burners off, went up stairs and checked to make sure the burners were off, and they were. The next morning I went back to the basement and turned on the breaker and immediately the stove was back on, again NO ONE turned the stove on...It just lite up by itself...

My concern is that had the stove not started when i was awake, it could have easily started the wooden cabinets on fire and eventually burned my home down...I called Sears and they said "The unit is out of warranty!" I said I am not interested in the warranty, I have already replaced the cooktop with another brand, I am concerned that there are other units of this type in service that could lead to house fires, injuries and even death to people who are not aware of the potential for injury this cooktop has...I still have the old unit, again my reasson for contact the Gov't is that I find it difficult to believe that my cooktop is the ONLY ONE in America that has this apparent defective control issue....
justification: The cooktop turning on by itself poses a significant fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury if not addressed, though no actual injury or death occurred in this instance.

incident_description: Error lights came on.  Oven broiler element red hot when oven was on "bake".    We turned off oven (nothing else was on).  We were in the kitchen for 15 minutes more and there was no further indication of a problem.  About an hour later, our smoke detectors went off.  We saw/smelled no smoke but when we checked the kitchen, stove was too hot to touch. Stove lights indicating hot burners were on, but  stove and oven were off according to the control panel.  We immediately flipped off circuit breaker.  When stove cooled down, we looked closer.  The oven had ash inside as though it had gone through cleaning cycle.  The oven/broiler element(s) must have come on by themselves.  Had we been away, we could have had a fire.  Very scary!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Frigidaire Gallery Series Smoothtop Electric Range will not turn off after being switched off.  The burner will switch to high heat setting on its own without being selected.  This is an ongoing occurrence.  I am not able to use the right front burner at all because last time it would not cut off after it switched over to a high heat setting and my husband had to pull the stove out from the wall while the burner was still on and unplug it in order to turn the stove off.  This could have potentially burned him as well as catch something on fire if I had not caught it in time.  The left burner is also switching over to a high heat setting on its own when I am cooking on medium heat.  Very disappointed in the Frigidaire company right now.  I called to get help from the customer service line and explained that I saw there was a recall on several of their ranges but because mine was not included in their recall, they would not help me even though my range has the exact issues that are described in their recall on the other ranges.  I will never purchase a Frigidaire again.  PERIOD....  I guess I have to wait until someone gets burned or my home burns down before something is done.....  Don't purchase Frigidaire anything.....
justification: The burner switching to high heat on its own poses a significant risk of injury or fire, as evidenced by the need to unplug the stove to turn it off and the potential for burns.

incident_description: Woke up to a kitchen full of smoke.  Called the fire department not knowing where the smoke was coming from. The fire department thought that it was from our Central heat since we had just turned it on for the first time.   After they left I went into the refrigerator and noticed that it was not working.  We went and checked the breaker box and noticed that it was tripped. Re-set it and the refrigerator started smoking again could smell wire burning.  We disconnected it and called a repair man to come and check it out.  He came and stated that it was the relay and that it had actually burned the compressor He cleaned all the terminals with a [REDACTED] tool due to residue from relay catching on fire melting unto compressor terminals and  compressor.  He told us to let it run for 24 hours but was not sure if it was ok.  I now am worried that this may happen again and do not feel safe leaving my home.  I do not trust this product at all.  Whirlpool refrigerator Model #ED2VHGXMB10.  Mfg Date 01/2004. I noticed that the Maytag Refregerators were recalled for this exact problem but not the Whirlpool.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue was repaired but concerns about recurrence remain.

incident_description:
GE Profile Dishwasher heating element continued heating for 8 hours after wash cycle had finished.  Counter top reached approximately 100 degrees.  Inside the dishwasher, one plastic water glass melted, ceramic bowls and metal utensils burned fingers when touched.   
Controls Selected: Cookware, Added Heat, Heated Dry
Model: PDW8680N20SS
Serial: HR755014B
Purchase Date: May 25th, 2008
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted glass, burned utensils) and minor injuries (burned fingers), but no severe harm or death.

incident_description:
Preheated oven to 375 F.  Sprayed Anchor Hocking large rectangular (28cm x 38cm) 5L baking dish with cooking spray.  Added chicken breasts with olive oil and spices to bake.  Left the closed oven for another room.  Heard a loud explosion less than 10 minutes later.  Opened oven to find a shattered dish with shards of broken glass and an oily mess.

Baking dish had no cracks or chips before this incident.  I had used this dish for identical cooking 5-10 times in the past.
justification: The incident involved a shattered baking dish but no reported injury, and similar incidents are rare based on past usage.

incident_description:
I purchased my Baby Bullet in December 2011 and was using it as instructed when the inner plastic sealant ring came off and was blended into the food I was making for my 7 month old daughter. Not only did the ring get chopped up and mixed with the food but it is also clear in color and hard to see. I have read many reviews of this product and this exact issue happening with other people on sites for Target, Babies R Us, Amazon and more. While Baby Bullet is now making this item so that the sealant ring is permanent within the mixer, many people still own the earlier version of this product where it is not permanent. incident_description: My wife opened our LG Model 25760 TT refrigerator door to find the interior incredibly hot, she called me and I observed the entire machine was extremely warm and the interior lights were too hot to touch.  The entire light assembly had turned into a burn hazard and could have caught fire if we had not have noticed there was a problem.  I realized that the lights had come on all by themselves and stayed on.  I turned the electricity off and called the manufacturer.  They admitted this was a known issue with this model and gave me the number of a service center who, they said, would come out and repair it at no charge to me.  I called the service center - Whidbey Appliance 360-240-9050, they responded that is was "not worth their while to come out".  I offered to pay them whatever their hourly rate was on a portal to portal basis to come out and repair this refrigerator, they would not come out.  I removed the light bulbs from the refrigerator and restarted it as suggested by the manufacturer.  It ran for about ten minutes and then produced a fault code ER FF (freezer fan).  I called the manufacturer again and they suggested I turn it off for four hours because maybe this fan had iced up.  I complied and it created the same error.  The manufacturer said they would contact the repair center themselves and get back to me.  I have never heard another word, that was four days ago.   I used to repair appliances and took a look at the unit myself.  In doing internet research I discovered LG has been sued for defects in this refrigerator that have caused fires and melted light assemblies.  There are clearly design defects and an even worse service structure in place.  There are thousands of consumers blogging online about their problems with this refrigerator.  Shouldn't your department be forcing a recall or refund for these consumers?  I have taken a look at my fan problem too.  This fan is a little DC motor that is under engineered for the job it is supposed to do and destined to fail.  We are lucky to have not had a fire, now four days with no refrigeration, no resolution in sight and have thrown away about $500 of spoiled food, LG has failed to meet every expectation of safety, service responsibility or product performance with this product.  I have also called LG corporate at 256-772-8860 and left a message for [REDACTED} who is an executive assistant there.  My hope being that someone at a higher level in the company cared enough to arrive at a solution.  I have never even received a call back.   This refrigerator is a serious safety hazard in anyone's home.   By the way, the time to go from functioning to almost on fire was less than two hours, our food was so hot inside the mayonnaise jar exploded.  This refrigerator has two incandescent 60 watt light bulbs right next to one another, that creates lots of heat in a very small space.  If a consumer is lucky enough to have LG repair the unit the repair involves installing a lighting harness with a thermistor that turns the lights off when they get too hot, replacing the motherboard with one with a bigger relay because the original is undersized for the job and sticks on.  I would think they need to replace the lights with LED lighting that creates virtually no heat and upsize the fan motor too because it is doomed to fail - there is clearly some seriously deficient engineering in this refigerator that demands a global recall.
justification: The incident describes a refrigerator with a known defect that poses a burn hazard and fire risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a GE Cafe dishwasher 4/8/11. I did not have any issues with this dishwasher until 1 1/2 yr later. On october 24, 2012 I ran a load of dish, just as I always do, around 5 pm. The settings on the dishwasher are never changed. Each load of dishes is ran on the same setting and always has been that way. The next morning, I got up to get my daughter a sippy cup out of the dishwasher and I touched the dishwasher and immediately pulled my hand back because it was so hot it almost burnt my hand. The outside of the stainless steel as well as the top of the granite were so hot you could not touch it. On the inside, the plastic cups in the dishwasher were melted. Now, I am not certain whether or not the dishwashers heating elemtent never turned off or whether it turned itself back on at some point in the night. Eitherway, it had become so hot it melted the cups inside. Luckily, we caught this issue before it spread smoke throughout the whole house. I contacted GE and they informed me that there was no recall on the dishwasher. I proceeded to do some research online and I found that both the GE cafe and the GE profile have had several reports of this same issue happening. Some families were unfortunate in the fact that their homes filled with smoke to the point they had to call companies to come out and treat to get the smoke smell out of their home. They received the same respones from GE as I did when I contacted them. They told me that they would fill out the paperwork and send it to their engineers but that they couldnt tell me what would happen with the information other than it would be reviewed and would not keep me updated on what they found out because they claim it to be proprietary information. Additionally, they told me that to their knowledge this dishwasher does not get hot enough to ignite a fire. I find it amazing that a company waits until a fire ignites to issue a recall on a product or a part for their product. They also told me that if I wanted to claim an injury or replacement of my dishes I could file an insurance claim. I am not interested. I'm more interested in the company fixing this problem so it doesn't happen to other families. If my children had touched the front of the dishwasher before I knew what was going on it could have burnt their hands. I have 4 small children in my home. Furthermore, if my home had filled with smoke while we were sleeping because of this malfunction my children could have had smoke inhalation issues. Im not only concerned about my family but other families as well. 
Luckily, we purchased the extended service plan through Lowe's when we bought the dishwasher.The company came out and looked at the dishwasher and they had to replace the computer board, they did that this morning. I am now currently running my first load of dishes since its been replaced. 
The dishwasher is a GE Cafe model # CDW 9380N20SS serial # AR878151B

Given the lack of response that I received from GE, I filed a complaint with the Better Business Bureau. I again received a lack of response from a GE representative. I contacted my local news who told me to report this incident to this website.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing excessive heat and melted items, but no injuries or deaths were reported.
