incident_description:
On November 1, 2012, I was injured by Rubbermaid glass with easy find lids food storage containers.  The numbers on the container were: 
5.5 cups	7N64
1.3L 		16

I heated up some leftovers (rice & beans) in one of the glass containers in the microwave for 2 min.  (I took the glass container directly from the fridge to the microwave).  I left the container in the microwave for a couple minutes to cool off and then removed the container from the microwave.  When I removed the container there was no damage.  

I sat down to work at the computer while eating at the same time, unfortunately not looking at the food on my spoon.  Towards the end of my meal, I took a bite and then had a severe stabbing pain in the back of my throat.  I thought some type of chicken bone or something like that got stuck at the back of my throat (although there was no chicken in the dish).  It turns out it was 1.5-2" long shard of glass, which I had to dislodge from my throat with my tongue and fingers.  Heavy bleeding immediately occurred.  

I immediately called the doctor wondering if I should go to the ER, but since it seemed that the glass was out they asked me to come to their office immediately.  With my mouth bleeding, choking on blood and no one around to help me, I had to grab my 2 year old daughter and drive myself to the doctor.  After the doctor looked at my throat, it appeared there was no more glass in my throat although it was likely that I had swallowed some glass as well.  I have cuts in my throat as well as on my tongue that are very painful and has caused swelling.  It's painful for me to swallow, talk, eat and drink.

After I got home, I took pictures of the glass container and I also took a photo of the shard that got lodged in my throat. We had these containers for about 10 months, taking extremely good care of them.  When loading the dishwasher, we are ALWAY sure that the containers are not touching anything else to prevent chips or damage.  So somehow after taking the container out of the microwave and starting to eat, the container chipped off a huge chard of glass into my food.  The container was NOT bumped or dropped or damaged in any way. It seems that in the process of microwaving the container, which is labeled microwave safe, that the glass was not durable enough to withstand the heat.   I have the container if you need me to ship it to you.

The scary part is this was the SECOND time a chip like this has occurred.  A few months ago, I was heating leftovers from the fridge.  After removing the container from the microwave, a small chip of glass broke off into my food.  The container was NOT bumped, dropped or damaged.  Luckily I noticed it right away and tossed the container, thinking it was just a defect to this container.  So this is TWO containers that had the same problem.

Not only was this an extremely scary situation for me, but it scares me to think that this situation could have been much worse if the glass got stuck further down in my throat where I couldn't pull it out.  It scares me to think that this could have happened to my 2 year old and it scares me to think that this could happen to anyone else!!  This is a serious health hazard, which my doctor said I need to notify the Consumer Product Safety Commission.

incident_description:
My family & I were on our way out to take our children to soccer last Wednesday October 24th 2012 when my son smelled smoke. I immediately went to my oven to make sure that I had turned everything off and determined that it was safe but still smelled the smoke. When we finally saw the smoke coming from underneath the fridge we all panicked and pulled the fridge out to which the sparks and smoke got stronger. My husband immediately unplugged the fridge and we unscrewed the back of the fridge to see the melted parts with smoke all around. Needless to say we couldn't leave the house  as we were afraid of the damage that would have happened if it was 5 minutes later when the house would have been empty. It was 7pm at night so we didn't what to do but borrow neighbors freezers and put our daughters insulin and all of our food outside on the back porch for the night. The next day my husband went to go get the part to try to fix it himself (missing work) and the parts store told him to speak with a repair place because he believed it was a fire recall item. When the repair man came 2 days later it was discovered that the fire had casted the condenser to break down as well and that we needed to coact May tag direct to see what they were going to do. I have been in "phone" contact off & on for the last week with week with May tag and the only thing they will offer is 25% off one of their products to purchase a new fridge or fix the condenser. The fridge smells now and I don't feel safe with this fridge knowing that the fire caused the condenser to break down too, we are also wondering what other problems will arise from this fire in the future and are not willing to take that chance. 
We have been not sleeping for the last 9 days moving food around, our children have to go outdoors to get their milk and my daughters insulin. We've lost  food and time trying to figure out what we should do. We are very disappointed with Maytag's offer because when I asked why we weren't contacted about this recall she explained it was all of the television and that our fidge wasn't registered, however if we had seen it we would have fixed the issue at that time so that we could have avoided all this stress.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks from a fridge, causing panic and inconvenience, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I bought a $80 [REDACTED] 12 cup programmable coffee maker from Target and followed the instructions for cleaning prior to use.  I even brewed 2 cycles to ensure the item was clean.  However, when I started drinking the coffee, there was a distinct bad taste.  I'm not sure exactly how much I ingested as I wasn't really paying attention at first, but as I focused on the problen I noticed that there was both a strong smell and taste of melted plastic.  I then smelled the hot unit and could smell it more strongly when I lifted the basket compartment lid.  That afternoon I had diarrhea (very unusual for me) and a nasty aftertaste in my mouth. Even today, (Saturday) I still have that plastic taste in my mouth, although my stomach did start feeling a little better yesterday afternoon. My concern is that the plastics being manufactured for these units may contain toxins that I somehow ingested and that could make other people more sick than what I have experienced.  This is the first time I've bought a kitchen appliance that produced a melted plastic smell/taste associated with use.  I have notified both [REDACTED] and Black and Decker about the problem in the hopes that they will research the problem and rectify it, and have posted my concerns [REDACTED].  However, I thought I should notify someone in authority/government, just in case this is far worse than what I've experienced.  I don't know if this is considered a poison but it sure made me sick.

incident_description:
We have a Frigidaire Range we purchased approx. 4 years ago.  The Range was turned off and we had a heavy glass 8 cup measuring cup with tea sitting on the range.  The range had not been used that evening.  My husband and I were sitting on the outside porch when we heard a loud crashing sound.  Our 11 year old son had just walked in and we thought he broke a dish.  When we went in to investigate, we learned the glass measuring cup had exploded just seconds after our son passed by it.  The glass blew all over the kitchen, dining room, and family room.

We checked the stove and found that it was on high.  I was confused as to why it was on and when I looked at the dial it was in the off position.  The digital display changed settings by itself going from high to low and back.  We could not find the circuit breaker to shut it down and had to call the fire department.  They responded and ended up pulling the range out and unplugging it.

We contacted Frigidaire and Electrolux.  After approx. 2 hours it was determined there was a recall for that model for turning on unexpectedly.   They did not volunteer that information, we specifically had to ask them if there was a recall and they advised "yes".  We then had to ask them what the recall was for and they said they would check.  That was when we found out why it was recalled.  They advised they would get back with us after they determined if the range qualified for the recall.

This occurred approx. 2 - 3 months ago and we still have not heard from them and we are still without an operating range/stove.  To me this is unacceptable.  I would like to know if there is something you/I could do to speed this process up short of calling an attorney.  I would appreciate any help you can provide.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]

The butter in the upper compartment on the right side door was melted.  I pressed the 2 pins/buttons on the fridge that would turn off the lights when the doors were closed.  The digital temperature screen went dark but the lights stayed on.  We purchased the fridge in 2007.  Had I not opened it - we may have had a fire.  No, I'm sure we would have.  It's an LG French Door Lower Freezer Drawer Model #LFC25760ST.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to a malfunctioning light fixture, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Electric Range, and we had a fire in the oven top electrical unit. We turned it on and moments later we heard a pop sound  and flames were coming out of the top . We turned the oven off, and flames continued to come out of the top. The only way to stop the fire was to shut it off from the fuse box. VERY SCARY--Thank god my husband and I were standing there, I ran to get my children and he ran to pull the fuse. This could have been tragic!

I looked for recalls and found the same type of problems with other Kenmore ranges that have been recalled. I checked the Model # 790.92203011 on my range, and it did not match the numbers on the recall. It is the identical problem that the recalled  have. This is really a SAFETY HAZARD!!!

My Kenmore range was purchased new August 2010. I called Sears today and told me that since the warranty ran out after 1 year, today is October 2012 I will need to purchase a new range. Are you SERIOUS? This is clearly a manufacturing defect. Aren't ranges suppose to last more than 2 years? Kenmore and Sears knows this is a defect with their ranges and they continue to sell them and then hold the consumer responsible? This does not give me any confidence or trust in buying from Kenmore any longer. They should stand by their products not cause FIRES in innocent families homes. 

TERRIBLE BUSINESS KENMORE AND SEARS.
justification: The incident involved a fire with no reported injuries, and similar issues have been reported with other Kenmore ranges, indicating a possible defect.

incident_description: I was baking brussel sprouts in my oven and all of a sudden a pop and hissing sound sound came from the stove and the top where the push button controls for the oven are located burst into flames, and black smoke.  My husband shut off the circuit breaker to the stove.  The smell was awful, what an electrical fire would smell like.  I researched the internet and see similar incidents posted for ranges that look exactly like mine.  I have never received a recall for this range.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death, and similar incidents have been reported online, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: I used my Mastrad TopChips Maker a few times and really loved it, but then all of a sudden my husband saw a spark and I turned around to see a fire filling my microwave.  Also, after using the chip maker a few times in a row my microwave plate started making noises and it turns out that it was very hot.  I feel that this product is unsafe if not watched continuously while in use, and also may cause damage to a microwave.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave and potential damage, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the processor stays on even when the lid is off.  He says that the switch mechanism gets stuck.  When this occurs, the unit can be turned on posing a laceration hazard.  

He is concerned that a child may get his hand inside the processor while it is on.  The consumer says that just a simple shove can turn it on making it very dangerous.
justification: The processor can turn on unexpectedly, posing a laceration hazard, especially to children, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: Our Sears Kenmore Gas Range Model No. 790.78852602 has a handle that repeatedly comes loose from the screws it's held on with and causing the handle to come off when opening the hot oven or closing it after putting items in/out of the oven. The handle comes off of the hot door separating and causing you to burn yourself from the door closing on your arms. This has happended on multiple occasions and takes two people to handle the door when it happens.
justification: The incident involves a loose oven handle causing burns, indicating injury (severity 3), and it has happened multiple times, suggesting a high likelihood (4).

incident_description:
General Electric 12-cup coffee maker:  Model # 169209.

This is very similar to the recall that GE put out in 2010.  This model also has a tendency to overheat, and the heating element will burn a hole in the water recepticle and the water will leak through the bottom of the base and onto your counter top.  Can also cause an electrical shock from the water leakage.
justification: The description indicates potential for overheating, water leakage, and electrical shock, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
Amana electric range model aer3311waw0.  When the oven switch was turned on the switch started making a buzzing noise and black smoke appeared from behind the switch.  I removed the switch and it was charred and melted on the bottom.

My concern is if the oven was in use and unattended a fire could have destroyed my house and/or caused possible injuries to persons and pets.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning switch with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We are writing this on behalf of our son.  This matter concerns a TEM 500 Back to Basics toaster (originally purchased by my wife and myself years ago but since passed on to our son in very good condition).  Our son has reported to us that this toaster had come within seconds of self igniting into what could have become a serious apartment fire here in Seattle.  Here is a quick summary of the situation:  On 5/22/2012 our son was awakened from his sleep at exactly 2:24 am by a loud electrical buzzing noise coming from the plugged in TEM 500 toaster.  Yes, the toaster was plugged into the wall socket but it was definitely in the "off" position.  The toaster had apparently reached a very dangerous hot temperature and was emitting noxious fumes.  In short, the toaster was aggressively burning itself from the inside out.  Our son told us he was severely shaken up mentally and unable to concentrate properly at work the next day from lack of sleep and emotional exhaustion.  Our son still is in possession of the toaster.  Like the prior complainant (here at safeproducts.gov) we had contacted the company who wants us to mail back the toaster which we are still mulling over.  In reply to our complaint the company rep has told us that the toaster instructions call for the user to unplug the toaster after every use to prevent such incidents.  We ask you...is this ever a cop out or what?  Seriously now, how many people would go ahead and buy a toaster or any kitchen appliance for that matter having known in advance that unless the appliance was unplugged after each and every use a fire might result! We think this is a very convenient way for this company to cover their you know what.  And, indeed, it was not terribly difficult to find out about other very similar self igniting scenarios with the TEM 500 with a simple [REDACTED]  search.  As a concerned family we are not exaggerating when we say this could have been a disaster if the toaster self ignited while our son was away at work during the day. At the very least we felt this merits reporting to the federal government for a possible recall on the TEM 500.
justification: The toaster nearly caused a fire but no injury occurred, though the son was emotionally shaken. Similar incidents suggest a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
Magic Chef Slow Cooker Model # MC SC600 E70052 at a luncheon at work. Turned the cooker on high for about an hour, then turned it on low. People were getting food from the cooker all morning. Suddenly the sound of an explosion, and glass flying all over the room. Luckily a person just turned his back to the cooker. No one was injured.

I called Magic Chef, but said they never heard of such a thing, and the retailer is responsible. We are not after anything, except an answer to how this could happen. Our fear having one explode and someone getting seriously injured. By the way, Magic Chef said I should call Wal Mart. I did and got the same response. Never heard of such a thing!
justification: The slow cooker exploded, causing glass to fly, but no one was injured.

incident_description: My mom had bought me brand new coffee maker (Black and Decker Model # CMD3500MBT) I had used it once, on Sat. Aug 28th to make coffee. I did not use it again after that time, but kept it plugged in due to the clock feature. On Tuesday, August 31, 2010, it shorted out catching my kitchen on fire and killing our pet dog, Wilbert. An electrical engineer stated that it was a short in the machine that caused the fire and definitely not a problem with the electrical wiring because of the burn pattern. Although it didn't burn through the roof and burn my house down, it was still a total loss and we lost everything. Thankfully I was at work and my children were at school when it occured.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a pet dog and a total loss of property due to a fire caused by a short in the coffee maker.

incident_description:
Product: Frigidaire 30" Gas/Convection Range #FGGF3054MBC
Purchased: September 7, 2012 from Allan & Peterson local retailer
Installed in home Oct 11, 2012. 2 weeks old at time of incident
After using the Broil feature (550 degrees) to cook fish on rack #5 for about 10 minutes and warm bread on rack # 2 for the last 5 minutes of cooking, I turned off the oven and set all my items on top of the cook top grates while I dished up plates. The fish was on a foil lined cookie sheet and the bread was in a glass bake dish that I covered with a towel to keep warm. I heard a beeping and looked to see why that happened when I had already turned off the oven and noticed the towel covering my bread was on fire. The over range outside vent was on, the flames were lapping up on the electric control panel of the oven and had turned on the "pizza" setting so the oven actually turned on. I was able to put out the fire without injuries. The dish with bread covered in the towel was sitting at the back of the stove top, where the heat exhaust exits the oven. This area remained extremely hot and unable to be touched, including directly below the electric control panel. The lower half of the electric panel is now burned, plastic has bubbled and is disfigured but still controls the oven. A few hours after this incident, the electric panel began to display error messages and I had to unplug the stove.
This oven is only two weeks old, I have three children in the house under age 5 and I am extremely concerned about this safety feature. There is a small warning in the instruction manual regarding the safety risk of burns or ignition but I believe the company needs to sell safer products, not expect the consumer to "watch out" for heat escaping from the oven causing a kitchen fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described safety issue with heat exhaust.

incident_description:
(09/24/2012) The consumer stated that the left burner was on a temperature of eight. He was cooking with a round pan with a glass cover. The stove had been on for about five minutes when he heard a pop sound. He stated that he looked at the stove and saw a hairline crack from the back to the middle of the burner on the left side. He immediately turned off the stove. 


The consumer stated that recently the temperature on the right side of the stove has been uneven.

(09/24/2102)The consumer stated that he called the manufacturer and was told that the stove was not under recall. He was told that the glass top was available at a cost to him.
justification: The incident involved a hairline crack in the stove's glass top with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents are not uncommon but not frequent.

incident_description: GE Spacemaker Microwave has started to randomly turn on/off.  Microwave, Model JVM3670SK06, turned itself on without hitting any controls, did not count down time, and continued to operate.  Had to open door to shut off microwave - closing door RESUMED microwave operation.  If unattended and it happens to turn on by itself again, this will lead to a melt down or fire.  Use must be immediately discontinued.  The Magnetron on the unit has already been replaced within the warranty.  This brand of microwave is completely unsafe and a fire hazard.   Previous models have had this same problem and it appears GE has still not fixed this safety issue after almost 12 years of problems with these models.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, which could lead to death if unattended, and the issue has persisted across multiple models over 12 years.

incident_description: We purchased an LG Refrigerator Model #LFC22760 and Serial #612MRYA16 in 2007. Last night the refrigerator light didn't shut off and melted the light unit and destroyed the control panel. Our repair person (Same Day Service, Inc.) said that this is known and common problem with this refrigerator but that LG had not issued a recall. I spoke with LG and they confirmed that they do not have a recall in place. This problem could have started a fire in my house and if this is a known problem, LG has the responsibility to fix it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction that could have caused a fire but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: kenmore electric range top element went out of tempature control heating up with no upper temp limit and also not responding to any shut off switch.  This almost burned up the unit and could have resulted in a house fire and who knows what else.  The unit could have sustained damage after viewing wiring and carbon marks but I believe it's able to be fixed.  Reading on line it looks like a known problem with a faulty bake/boiller relay.  It this a recognized issue? and has a safe improved part exist? thanks
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range top element with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On my Viking built-in bottom mount freezer/refrigerator (manufactured January 2007) - the screw attaching the pivot plate of the top hinge on the door sheared causing the door to detach from the hinge pivot plate and fall off.  It also damaged the other supporting hinges/brackets on the top and bottom of the refrigerator door.  I'm thankful that this did not occur while a child was opening the door.

Viking currently has a recall in place for the exact same issue on built-in refrigerator/freezers manufactured prior to April 10, 2006.  When I called them to report the problem, they took my statement and would only say that my refrigerator is not part of the recall as it was manufactured after in January 2007, after the manufacture date of April 10, 200 for the recall.  The hinge shearing issue clearly has not been resolved by Viking in their products.  The door is very heavy and I'm concerned that if this issue is not proactively addressed by the manufacturer, it could create a dangerous situation for consumers - particularly for children and smaller adults.

My Viking refrigerator information:
model #:DDBB363LSS
Serial #: 010507R00000543
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator door detaching due to a sheared screw, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Firgidare Gallery series stove/oven Mod # GLEFS76ASA. The oven turns on all by itself and shows no indicator lights. I've shut off the circuit breaker and turned the stove back on after a half an hour. The oven started to heat again showing ni indicator lights.
justification: The oven turning on by itself poses a potential hazard, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Heard fizzling noise and then room filled with smoke.  After fire department removed back panel the compressor was glowing red, insulation was damaged and electrical connector was melted.
justification: The incident involved significant equipment damage and smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: i had a partial amputation of my middle finger on my left hand caused by my hand hitting an extremely sharp edge on my GE wall oven.  i went to the er and the er doctor sent me to a plastic surgeon.  he put in over 20 stitches. he repaired the skin and the cut tendon.
justification: The incident involved a partial amputation and required medical attention, including stitches and tendon repair, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: My LG refrigerator, model# LFC25760ST, has had a problem as of late where the lamps in the fridge would stop turning on. I noticed that the temp in the fridge was hot and the bulb area was very hot to the touch. There is a smell of something burning, plastic? I am concerned that there may be a thermal issue with my refrigerator. I have looked for a possible recall on the manufacturers website but have not found one. This issue has been off and on for a couple of months now. The issue also occur once or twice during the first few months of ownership but disappeared.
justification: The refrigerator shows signs of overheating and a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, which could lead to injury.

incident_description: Oven made pop noise, and outer glass layer of glass exploded out to 3 feet around the kitchen
justification: The oven's glass exploded but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
(09/14/2012) The consumer stated that she had hand-washed the glass lid and layed it in the sink to dry. The consumer stated that nothing else was in the sink except a plastic cup, bowl and a spoon. The next morning while she was in her kitchen making coffee, she heard a loud explosion that sounded like a gun shot. When she turned toward the sink, she discovered that the lid had exploded. She also stated that a couple minutes earlier and it would have exploded in her face. The consumer stated that she is now afraid to use the other lids. 

The consumer stated that she uses the product often. 

The consumer stated that it left small nicks in her porcelain sink. 

The consumer stated that the lid is glass with a silicone handle. It is part of an 8 pc set gray in color.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass lid causing damage to the sink but no injury to the consumer, fitting severity level 2. The consumer uses the product often, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
(09/24/2012) The consumer stated that she placed the glass baking dish on the stove top. She then proceeded to preheat her oven and set it on the baking setting. Approximately 5 to 10 minutes of the dish being on the stove top, the consumer hear a loud pop. When she turned around, she saw that the baking dish had completely shattered and spread across the entire kitchen. 

The consumer did not receive any injuries.

Note: The consumer also stated that in the inside of the pan there is a warning that advises consumers not to place the baking dish on the stove top.
justification: The baking dish shattered but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the explicit warning against the action taken.

incident_description:
Using the 7 qt Martha Stewart Enamel Cast Iron Collection cookware on my stove top to brown meat. stove top on medium, with olive oil in cookware.  Heard a Pop sound and then discovered that the enamel had blown off the bottom exposing the cast iron. Pieces of the enamel were floating in the olive oil.
I was not standing next to the pot when it cracked off and was flung against the pot. Some particles flew onto the countertop.

This was the older model purchased at Macy's between 2009/2010
justification: The incident involved damage to the cookware but no injury occurred, as the user was not near the pot when the enamel cracked.

incident_description:
I placed a frozen cinnamon raisin English muffin on a small, clear glass plate and put both in the microwave.  I shut the door and programmed 3 minutes on power level 6 and pressed START.  I walked into another room approx. 20 feet away.  After one minute, my smoke alarm sounded and I turned towards the kitchen to see white smoke filling the ceiling down to about 18".  I ran to the microwave and saw flashing lights inside and the smoke pushing out of the unit.  I pressed STOP and evacuated my pets.  I opened the house windows and doors and put on my exhaust fan for my stove.  Then I opened the microwave and found the plate broken into 3 major pieces and some shards.  The English muffin was smoking as well as the plate; however only the very edges of the muffin (approx. 1/2 cm) was singed.  There were large brown dots on the plate and on the microwave tray about two inches in diameter.  
With oven mitts on, I took the microwave tray outside to cool down.  For the next 10 minutes, the smoke billowed from several windows of my house.  There was a yellow film on the interior of the unit and all around the door.  For several days, now the unit and my house has smelled of smoke. 

I phoned Panasonic, and spoke with [REDACTED] who gave me a case # [REDACTED]  She told me someone else would call me back.  An hour later, [REDACTED] from Panasonic called, clarified some details, and said he's going to label it as a food fire.  
I told him that on power level 6 for less than 2 minutes for a frozen bread product with raisins should not have had this kind of incident.  He said he was not going to do anything else about it.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common with standard microwave use.

incident_description: The Frigidaire 30inch wall electric/convection wall oven was baking a roast when it made a buzzing sound.  Flames shot out the top of the oven immediately.  The oven was quickly turned off and the breaker was turned off.  The oven locked and will not open.  Roast beef is still inside while we decide our course of action.  The oven was purchased in May,2008.  It almost burned down our log home.
justification: Flames shot out of the oven, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
All Clad Slow Cooker unit, Model SERIE SC0.
First unit I purchased did not work at all. All Clad sent a replacment which after 3 uses began to smoke and issue a burning smell. They replaced that unit also. Third unit after 4 uses also burst in smoke and burning fumes. I reported this to them and the re seller, Williams-Sonoma. Thankfully my wife an I were home on both occasion to immediately shut the unit down and put it outdoors. 
If like most you use a slow cooker and leave to go out/work, etc. Our house could have burned down!
Looking on-line it seems this issue and a fault with the ceramic insert is not new. I think this unit needs to recalled and consumers refunded before someone is seriouly hurt!
justification: The incident involved multiple units smoking and emitting burning fumes, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: GAS RANGE TURNED ITSELF ON WHEN NO ONE WAS HOME RESULTING IN AN OVEN FIRE EXTENDING TO COUNTERTOP AND CABINETS.
justification: The incident involved a gas range turning on by itself, causing a fire that extended to countertops and cabinets, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Heating element does not shut off on Maytag Dishwasher.  Model # MDB7600AWQ SN 25377656ET.
Must turn off circuit breaker.
There is a 1.7 million Maytag Dishwasher recall for this issue, but my SN does not fall into the range.
justification: The heating element not shutting off poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: Coffee maker (Cuisinart DCC-1200), in "off" position, started boiling coffee (c. 1 cup remaining in carafe) on its own. When examined more closely, noticed smoke coming out of rear at cord. Unplugged unit and took outside. Turned over to see smoke pouring out of bottom metal plate. Potential house fire averted.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned and produced smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We own a Cuisinart 6.5 quart programmable slow cooker, and we have been very pleased with its performance. However, last week, the handle came off when I was lifting the lid, leaving a jagged stem. I was surprised to see that the handle is not much more than a few pieces of plastic covered with foil.  Luckily, the glass lid did not break.


We are a household of two, and have not given this appliance any hard use whatsoever.  In my opinion this is a design flaw, and a potentially dangerous one at that.
justification: The handle broke but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of a design flaw.

incident_description: My Cuisinart coffeemaker was set up to come on automatically in the morning.  It made coffee as usual and I came out from the bedroom and the kitchen was smokey and smelled like burning plastic.  The coffeepot was burning.  It was less than 3 years old and had always worked fine.  There were no flames, probably because I quickly unplugged it and put it in the sink.  But there was smoke and burning plastic smell.  I had to air out the house.  It was on a granite counter top, so there was no damage to the counter.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no flames or injuries, and the appliance was quickly unplugged to prevent further damage.

incident_description:
We own an LG-Range (Model: LRE30757ST/SN:904MMYF00314).  My wife has used the "Self Clean feature only twice. During the 3rd use, the area became extremely hot, cabinets were hot to the touch and the microwave hood's safety fan turned on, automatically.
Within the last 45 minutes of the self-clean cycle, the range turned off/no power.  The door was stuck in the locked position.    
I decided to investigate, myself.  In short, the thermal fuse had tripped.  Although, I was more concerned of the safety concerns that were found:
1) The granite back splash had a burn/flame stain
2) The range's rear/metal panel had 'burn' stains on its exterior and interior
3) The internal/metal panels had burn/flame stains by the heating element motors and light bulb.
4) Wires and a plastic connector were melted and showed evidence that a fire had ignited. Had the thermal fuse not have tripped, my kitchen/home would have been in flames.
Regardless of the thermal fuse, the range should never have caught fire or exhibited such burn markings.
I've made attempts at coordinate resolution with LG but they have not responded.  I created a report and submitted the purchase receipt, details and images to LG.

Chronological order of events:
October 10, 2012: Incident Occurrence
October 11, 2012: Spoke with an LG CSR who instructed I coordinate a service call.
October 12, 2012: Performed a Live Chat and instructed to fax receipt (transcripts in the 	Appendix).
October 16, 2012: Performed a chat for follow-up (transcripts in the Appendix).  IÃÂm told nothing can be done until management reviews the details.  I am concerned management does not understand the severity of the new findings.  I have faxed this document, using the same number provided for the receipt.  

After replacing the thermal fuse, my wife has been using the stove top and a toaster oven to feed a family of 5.  My family can no longer continue with limited range use.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with burn marks and melted components, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product is an LG Gas Oven, model LDG3016ST/00.  This model contains a dual-oven configuration, with two separate compartments and doors with a larger bottom compartment.  Both doors contain a metal frame and a glass viewing window.

During the incident, I preheated the bottom compartment and placed a dutch oven inside.  When I went to remove it, the dutch oven lid touched the top compartment glass, which immediately exploded and sent shattered glass all over the kitchen floor and into the oven below.  The bottom portion of the oven's top compartment exterior glass is not protected by any covering and the incident is easily repeatable and could be very dangerous.

Because this is a newer model, the glass replacement was covered by a warranty.  I contacted the company directly and they mentioned that they do not view this as a safety issue.  The remedy--placing a metal or other covering under the door glass so it is not exposed--is simple and inexpensive.  The repairman also acknowledged the design flaw with this oven, which apparently is LG's first attempt at this design.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass that could cause injury, and the design flaw makes it easily repeatable.

incident_description: Fire department responded to a building fire.  The smoke detector was sounding & the unit was starting to fill with smoke. Neighbor stated that occupants were not home at the time. Upon entry, a small fire was discovered & contained in oven in kitchen.  They opened the oven, extinguished the small fire & unit was shut off from homeÃÂs circuit breaker panel. The estimated property loss on this incident was $100.  The estimated content loss was $400.
justification: The incident involved a small fire with no injuries, but caused property damage, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The likelihood is possible given the commonality of kitchen fires.

incident_description:
Following is CC of correspondance with manufacturer;

Good morning;

 

My wife and I received a Bella Kitchen 1.2 liter fryer from our daughter and her family as a Christmas gift last year. The unit is your model number XJ-6K116G. 

 

It has had light use  and has been cleaned in accordance with the instruction manual and towel dried after each use. It has not been immersed in water. Up until last night it has operated to designed intent. 

 

Please refer to the attached photos. There is one each of the front, the base, and of the interior of the appliance.

 

Last evening I experienced an unacceptable failure. I plugged the fryer into the outlet and set the thermostat to high in preparation for use. The indicator light came on and I went about preparing the rest of the meal. When the preheat cycle was complete and the light went out, I placed the chicken in the fryer basket, lowered the basket into the hot oil and installed the lip on the fryer. I set the timer  for four minutes and went on preparing the meal. When the timer went off I turned around and was greeted with the sight of 350* oil pooled on the countertop beneath the fryer, across the countertop and down the face of the cabinetry, which was on the countertop adjacent to our Jenn Air gas cook top. 

 

I immediately pulled the plug out of the receptacle in order to shut off the power to the unit and grabbed the fire extinguisher. This morning, after the mess was cleaned up, I washed the fryer and examined it carefully. The aluminum interior housing, which serves as the oil vessel, has numerous small holes in it, which allowed the oil to leak out of the fryer. See attached photos. The largest areas of aluminum decomposition are noted by the red arrows. 

 

This failure poses an unacceptable safety hazard due to the potential for accidental contact with superheated cooking oil flowing over the countertop, not to mention damage to cabinetry and the potential for fire when the oil comes in contact with the adjacent gas cook top.

 

Your prompt reply to this matter is requested.

 
[REDACTED] 

CC; US Consumer Product Safety Commission
justification: The incident involved a hazardous failure of a kitchen appliance leading to a potential fire risk and property damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was talking with my daughter while I was getting ready to make coffee. all of a sudden the coffee pot started popping, I turned around to see the white incasement of the maker glowing orange and my lights above my head stated flickering. I reached behind the maker and unplugged it. The smell of burnt plastic is something I don't care to smell again. The coffee pot is a Bunn coffee maker. I had just put coffee in the basket and walked away to fill the decanter, The switch was still off, I didn't even turn it on yet! Bunn model #GR10-W  Code Date 284004 Updated Code 3806. I sent an e-mail to Bunn that night Satday 10/13/12 They replied 2 days later. They want me to send them the maker and they will see what they can do. I ready do not want another Bonn coffee maker in my house after this happened. I am more worried about the people that do have them.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing a potential fire hazard, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common but possible with faulty appliances.

incident_description: The GE double-burner electric hotplate we bought from Wal-Mart had a problem with the control knob for the large burner such that it was operating at the highest heat level even though the control knob could be and was rotated to the "Off" position. The excessive heat buildup from this situation melted the plastic feet under the unit, causing the hotter end of it to settle down onto our countertop. This reduced the circulation of cooling air around the unit, making things even worse. The end result was that our butcher-block type wood countertop was scorched brown and the glue joints in it were damaged from the heat. At some point my wife discovered the situation and unplugged the unit, but it is very concerning to me that this could have happened when we were away from the house or while we were sleeping. This was an internal problem with the control device, not just a loose knob.
justification: The incident caused property damage (scorched countertop and damaged glue joints) but no injury or death.

incident_description: Control panel on my Kenmore 665.1435.3301 started smoking shorttly after starting.  Had to manually shut off the breaker.  Burned up the control panel and connectors.  Luckily we were at home and able to stop from burning down the entire home.  Understand this has happened numerous times on Kitchen Aid, Kenmore & Whirlpool dishwashers.  I will also contact Whirlpool but my understanding is I will be forced in to joining a class action suit for any resolution of this defect.
justification: The control panel smoking and burning up indicates a significant incident with potential for fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(09/25/2012) The consumer stated that the oven to her gas range comes on by itself. This has happened about four times. 

The consumer stated that she did not call her gas company. 


(09/25/2012) The consumer stated that she called her local Sears store parts department. They  offered to come out and replace the thermostat. The consumer declined the offer.
justification: The oven turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential safety hazard.

incident_description:
I bought a Kenmore Electric Range (model: 790.92803011) at Sears on Dec 2010. On Oct 12, 2012, the front outer glass oven door suddenly pop and the glass broken into small pieces without touching it.

The oven was used at about 7:00am on Oct 12 to pre-heat the muffin BAKE at 270deg.  Turn off the oven at about 7:10am. Oven was not in use anymore. Without touching the oven door, at about 8:15am, the front outer glass door oven of the Kenmore Electric Range suddenly exploded and the glass door broken into small pieces.  Luckily, no one got hurt as my kids just left for school and my wife was stand about few feet away when the outer glass oven door suddenly pop broken.

I contact Sears (1-800-469-4663) on the same day, Oct 12, to report about the incident, but Sears have no interest discussing about the product defect, except asking me if I like to schedule for the repair. Sear representative suggest that I should contact Kenmore to report about this Electric Range glass door broken problem.  I follow-up Kenmore with an email describe about the glass door broken but Kenmore have not respond yet.

I plan to contact Sear to get the outer glass oven door replace but afraid the technician will use the same outer glass model, in which I strongly feel unsafe. I believe this Kenmore Electric Range outer glass door product is defect and it should be on a recall list as it is very dangerous to explode like that.  I check Sears website at www.searspartsdirect.com and I think the part number for the Electric Range outer glass door oven is 316452717 (Glass, oven door, black, w/foil). Right now, I will postpone the replacement outer glass oven door until I gather more fact about this Kenmore Electric Range outer glass door product.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but the glass door exploded without touching it, which is a serious safety concern.

incident_description:
At approximately 11:00 am I loaded dishes into my dishwasher and began the normal cycle on my 2005 Kenmore Elite.  Model number 665.17462300, Serial number FR3116690.  About 15 minutes into the cycle, I was on the computer in the dining room when I started to smell a foul odor and started to hear a sizzling noise.  I looked into the kitchen to see black smoke billowing out of the front of the dishwasher and just then, flames shooting out of the right hand side where the dishwasher vents.  I ran into the kitchen and decided to try and stop the cycle by opening the dishwasher. I could accomplish this as the flames were on the right and I popped the handle from the left.  The flames went out and the smoke continued for about 30 seconds or so.

I immediately started searching on the internet for what to do and who to contact.  It looks as if I am certainly not alone in what happened to me.  Sears did recall this model of dishwasher however, only the plastic tub kind and not the metal ones.  The metal ones would "cost" too much money to replace I read.  I am shocked and saddened by this lack of responsibility on Sears part.  I am just glad I was at home so that my home did not burn down and no one in my family was injured.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from a dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore ELite Range Model # C970-445341

Front right burner won't shut off.  Same symptoms as popular 2009 recall for Kenmore and Frigidaire stoves, but my model # doesn't appear to be included. I had to shut off the breaker. Very dangerous! Can't imagine what could have happened if we hadn't noticed.
justification: The burner not shutting off is a dangerous incident, but no injury or death occurred as the breaker was shut off in time.

incident_description: Broiler in stove turns on by itself and will not shut off . Had to pull breaker at panel to shut it off. This is the second time this has happened. The control panel shows off but stove is on high.  Would cause a fire if we had not been home.
justification: The broiler turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred. This has happened twice, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore electric smooth (glass) top range Model 790. (Model 790.96021405) Approximately one year ago, the left front large burner began operating on high no matter what temperature setting was used. Additionally, the burner would fail to turn off when the dial was turned to off. This was repaired by the replacement of the dial mechanism. Now, the right front large burner is doing the same thing. The Kenmore Elite range Model 790 has been recalled along with other Frigidaire ranges in the same style, however these do not appear to have been recalled despite reports of the same issue. Note release 09-333 which details the same issues that the additional Kenmore ranges exhibit.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a potential safety hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The light in the temperature control unit located on the roof/top of the cooler unit did not go off. The resulting heat from the bulbs melted the plastic tabs that holds the screw that holds the unit to the top.  It is now hanging down, numerous tabs for the entire temperature control unit has been deformed by the heat, the roof of the cooler unit itself has bubbles and the beginnings of melted drippings.  The control unit is now being held up by duct tape.
I see this as an absolute fire hazard.  
There needs to be a national recall on this model and others with the same problem.  I have noticed several postings of the same problem but with different model numbers about lights not going off in Kenmore Bottom Freezer Refrigerators.
justification: The incident describes significant damage and a fire hazard but no injury or death, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reports of similar issues.

incident_description: My microwave GE model WES1450DN1BB started coming on by itself. It has flashed "reset clock" and "Service needed". But before this it started coming on by itself, although it could be stopped by opening the door. It happened when we were away for the weekend and thanks to my son for being smart enough to unplug it and not try to use it. In reading other complants on the internet I realize that my house and my children could have went up in flames while I was out of town. It also seems as though GE has never been repsonsive to this problem.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was unplugged before causing harm, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Melting of white plastic and soap dispenser inside the dishwasher.
justification: Melting plastic and soap dispenser indicates damage to property but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: After turning on the oven, the heating element sparked, flamed and caught on fire. I immediately turned the oven off and in about10-15 seconds the fire went out.  After it cooled, I noticed the heating element split in two and there was white residue on the oven.  Also the heating element looked like it had bubbled up or blistered from the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly controlled without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the heating element's failure.

incident_description: Came home from work, house smelled like something was burning.  Checked dishwasher and noted that all plastic placed inside had melted and pooled in the bottom of the unit.  Everything.  GE Profile Model # PDW9980N00SS S# RM816690B.  This unit was a replacement for an earlier GE Profile unit -- replaced on warranty from GE.    Each time the door is closed, the heating element goes on and begins to overheat the unit.  I have had to flip a breaker to turn off.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plastic in dishwasher) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
On a number of occasions the valves on our stove GE model JGB400 have been found ajar.  On one recent occasion my wife returned home and the smell of gas was so potent that she called the fire department.  It appears that the valve can be easily actuated by brushing against it.  There is a slight catch in the valve but it is insufficient to prevent unintentional opening of the valve.  We notified the company about this some time ago but the repair person took no action.  They were willing to replace the valves but the service tech seemed to think that the new valves would be the same.
After this I thought we would just be super careful not to brush against them but the valves are just to easily opened.

Model JGB400SEP355 Serial # AV223602P
justification: The incident involves a gas leak due to easily opened valves, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Priced at 33 cents, a fly swatter may seem like a bargain. But when it can
easily shatter into micro-pieces on the first swat, it's probably overpriced
even at 33 cents -- and perhaps unnecessarily dangerous.
Dolgencorp, based in Tennessee, is distributing 3-packs of brightly colored
plastic fly swatters made in China. I bought two packages -- 6 swatters -- for
$2 total at a Dollar General store in Springfield, Vermont.
I quickly discovered that the plastic swatters can shatter explosively
whenever the user slaps (or attempts to slap) a fly on a hard surface like a
windowsill, a counter or a hard chair. I've even had them shatter when
slapped vigorously against a screen -- and most people swing hard and fast
when attempting to nail a fly.
The pieces that go rocketing off into the air upon impact can be as big as a
half dollar or as small as tiny seeds -- in some cases tiny enough even to
lodge in the latticework of a screen.
I enclose the shattered ends of a couple of swatters, along with some pieces
large and small, and a 'joke" photo I sent my brother to illustrate how the
instruments shatter.
After a couple weeks ' use, only one of the six swatters I purchased is still
totally intact -- and that one mostly because it hasn't gotten much use.
I don't suggest that the fly swatters are as dangerous as faulty brakes on a car.
but an adult -- or a young child nearby -- could easily get hit in the eye with a
shard of plastic, since their pieces can fly quite a distance. Perhaps the
manufacturer should include a pair of safety goggles with each 3-pack of
swatters -- and raise the package price to $2.
justification: The fly swatters shatter easily, posing a risk of injury from flying plastic shards, though no actual injuries are reported in the description.

incident_description:
Stored food in Snapware Glasslock containers purchased from Costco. Transferred food (cooked beans) to a bowl, reheated in microwave, and began eating when I discovered a 2 cm glass shard in my mouth. 

Read similar reports (from Amazon.com reviews) of glass shards being shed from these Snapware Glasslock containers. Luckily, I didn't suffer any ill effects. I plan on returning the set (18 pieces - 9 lids, 9 glass containers) to Costco and at the very least making them aware of the dangers of this product.
justification: The incident involved discovering a glass shard in food, but no injury occurred. Similar reports suggest this is a recurring issue with the product.

incident_description: This is a large cast iron dutch oven.  I noticed that it had large pieces of enamel missing on the sides of the pot and two small through and through cracks on the rim and down the side of the pan.  I found pieces of enamel on the floor.  I thought maybe the pot had fallen to the ground and broken.  I later saw that this was a defect in the product and a safety hazard.  I did not notice this during cooking and my husband cleaned up and would not have mentioned the broken enamel.  I was very disappointed, but assumed someone had dropped the pot.
justification: The incident describes a product defect with potential safety hazards but no reported injury.

incident_description: I preheated my oven to 350 degrees. Then I put an 8-inch square Pyrex dish (purchased in December, less than a year ago) of enchiladas into the oven. I just made the enchiladas with room temperature ingredients, they weren't coming from the freezer. Within ten minutes we heard a loud bang and then sizzling. I opened the oven to find the bottom of the oven covered in many shards of glass (and lots of enchilada sauce). The shards were from the top inch of the rim of the dish, the bottom remained in its same shape, but with a large crack down the middle. I left the oven to cool before cleaning, and the dish continued to crack and break as the oven cooled.
justification: The incident involved a broken dish but no injury, and such occurrences are unlikely with proper use of Pyrex dishes.

incident_description:
On October 2, 2012, I had baked chicken at 350 degrees in a Pyrex dish, then put it under the broiler for just a minute or two.   When I removed the dish from the oven to check the status of the chicken, the dish literally exploded while still in my potholdered hand, sending thousands of jagged shards and micro-particles of glass all over my kitchen, along with micro-particles of chicken, too.

I was extremely fortunate that I wasn't injured by the glass or the heat of the projectile particles. After cleaning up the disaster, I began looking online and read many accounts of pyrex shattering in ovens and microwave ovens too, and of people being seriously injured by the explosions. I now realize the pyrex website says that such glassware should not be used under a broiler, but I, like many consumers, had not read this, and since the product is marketed as bakeware it is understandable such confusion exists.

This is clearly an ongoing problem and, in my opinion, needs to be treated as a product recall with broad media coverage to be sure no further injuries are sustained.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of glassware causing a mess but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple accounts of similar incidents.

incident_description: I was using the Baby Bullet blender to make my daughter some food and the seal was chopped up by the blade. While I was feeding her I noticed some chunks of something and then realized it was small pieces of plastic chopped up in her food. The plastic is clear and very difficult to see. I am very lucky that she did not eat any of these pieces or choke on them. I had checked the product before using it but the seal must have come loose while I was preparing her food. I like this product but I would not want a child to die because this happened to them.
justification: The incident involved plastic pieces in food but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is moderate given the product's design flaw.

incident_description: A large size Pyrex measuring cup exploded in our kitchen cabinet causing shards of every size of pyrex all over the cabinet and everything in it.
justification: The incident involved an exploding Pyrex measuring cup causing damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description: My husband was using the stove (cooktop) portion of our oven.  The oven was not on and had not been turned on in at least 4 days.  The outer front glass of the door spontaneously exploded and shattered thousands of pieces of glass throughout my kitchen, into cabinets, under the stove, under my dishwasher and cabinets with tremendous force.  There has never been any crack, bump or any kind of "trauma" to the oven door.  Fortunately, no one was injured.  The inner glass remained intact.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous glass shattering with no prior damage or injury, classifying it as an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I purchased an Oster toaster oven Model # 6081-000 about 10 months ago.  The first time we used it I was nearly burned badly when the back of my finger came in contact with the outside of the door.  I called the company and complained.  They said that their product fell within safety regulations.  I've never owned a toaster oven that burned me by touching the OUTSIDE of it.  My 2 children and I have sustained several burns over these past few months and I just feel that there is something very wrong with an oven that burns people when the outside of it is touched.  It just doesn't seem safe to me.
justification: The description reports several burns sustained by the user and their children, indicating an injury severity level.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she turned the unit on before going to bed.  She woke up the next day, and immediately felt the heat coming off of the dishwasher.  It stayed on heated dry all night.   It was not smoking.  

She opened it and it would not go off.  She says all the plastic was melted and ceramic dishes were cracked.  The consumer says she had to shut off the circuit breaker to get it to turn off.  She has not used it since.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plastic and cracked dishes) but no injury or death, and similar incidents are uncommon.

incident_description:
Product is a GE Profile Dishwasher Model# is PDW8800J03CC and Serial # is VG834000B.  The unit was bought in late 2004 and installed early 2005.  

The dishwasher had been started and my family was about to leave the house when my son interrupted the wash cycle by opening the door.  When he opened the door, a large cloud of foul smelling smoke filled the kitchen.  When the door was closed, the wash cycle restarted and more smoke came from the hole in the door where the latch is.  A black sooty residue was around the opening.  I disassembled the door to see if the problem was easily correctable, but there was significant fire damage to the electrical components and ribbon connections.  To prevent any further electrical danger, I uninstalled the dishwasher and removed it from the house.  I took pictures of the damaged components and reported the problem to GE the night of Oct. 16 (I have not gotten a response yet).

Please let me know if you would like the pictures or any other information.  Thank you.

[REDACTED]
justification: The dishwasher was damaged, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
(09/21/2012) The consumer stated that the oven came on without being turned on. The broiler coils at the top were red hot. The stove was not on. The consumer had to flip the breaker in the garage to turn it off. The consumer stated that she took the broiler pan from the bottom to unplug the stove. 

The consumer stated that there is a light on the stove that indicates that the stovetop is hot. Now the light stays on even when the stovetop is cool. This has been happening for about a 1 1/2 yrs.

The consumer stated that she will get in contact with the manufacturer.
justification: The oven turned on unexpectedly and the broiler coils were red hot, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: The outer oven window on my 2010 Kenmore free standing oven/ range combo Model# 7902803010 exploded and shattered onto the kitchen floor shortly after removing the food from the oven. The oven had been turned off and was cooling down when this occurred.
justification: The oven window exploded but no injury was reported, only property damage.

incident_description:
(09/16/2012)The consumer stated that the oven heated up beyond the 350 degrees that she had set. The oven had been pre-heating for 10 or fifteen minutes. The consumer attempted to shut off the oven by pressing the off bottom. It would not shut off so the consumer stated that she had to shut the oven off at the the breaker. If she turns the breaker back on, the oven will come back on. 

The consumer stated that the oven was not damaged.
The consumer stated that her house could have burned down. She also stated that this had never happened before. 
The consumer stated that she did not call the manufacturer but she intends to do so.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage occurred, and the consumer was able to shut it off at the breaker.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while she was using the oven at 285 degrees for 3 hours, she heard a beeping noise and noticed that control panel displayed "PF" and "ER".  She canceled the display and open the oven, the heating coil was bright red and there was smoke emitting from the unit. The incident caused the entire kitchen to be extremely hot.  

The consumer stated that she attempted to power off the oven but it stayed on, the circuit breaker was used to switch off the power from the oven.  After it cooled down, the circuit breaker was switched on and the oven came back on.  The circuit breaker has been used to disconnect power from the oven for the time being.  This was the first incident.  


The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The consumer is concerned that if no one was present at the time there would have been a house fire.  She feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and overheating but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for recurrence without intervention.

incident_description: I bought a saucepan from Home Goods Austell, Ga, this year I can't state the exact time. I have used the saucepan a few time, not a whole lot because I'm single and when I come home from work I don't always cook. The information on the bottom of the pan states The Palm Restaurant, stainless steel, made in china.  I put water in the pan and put it on the stove to boil the water and I noticed that it was steaming enough to catch my attention.  I lifted the saucepan and hot water burned my hand.  When I checked to see where it came from, the saucepan had split in 3 different locations and the hot water was coming out through the splits down on the stove also.  I emptied the water out and checked the pan and the splits were so obvious that I could look through them and see light shinning through.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury due to a defective saucepan, which is a clear injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the defect but not common occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while using the dishwasher (9/20/12), he smelled an odor of rubber burning.  The dishwasher was halfway through the cycle.   He noticed smoke emitting from the door of the unit, the door was opened and the circuit breaker was used to switch off the power from the dishwasher.

The service rep was contacted on 9/21/12 and he was informed that the control panel controller card and harness had been destroyed.  He was also advised that the dishwasher was not worth repairing.

The controller card was made in China, by Computime LTD, model number 6630.

He stated that he attempted to contact the manufacturer, GE, but was not able to as yet.
justification: The incident involved smoke and damage to the dishwasher but no injury or death, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with electrical appliances.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wife placed a bake potato inside the microwave on the ÃÂbake potatoÃÂ setting. The consumer stated that the sensor that stops the microwave malfunctioned and it did not stop the microwave. The consumer stated that when his wife went back to kitchen it was filled with smoke and the microwave was still on. His wife immediately turned off the microwave from the power off button on the control panel. The consumer stated that the inside protective shield of the glass completely melted and the smoke damage around the other inside walls of the microwave. 

The consumer stated that there was a lot of smoke in the house and the alarm went off. They were able to cancel the signal that alerts the fire department on their alarm systems. The consumer stated that the microwave was professionally installed. The consumer stated that there were no damages to his home structure and that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that they would only be able to pay for the parts, but he would have to cover the service.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave causing smoke and damage, but no injuries or structural damage occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Frigidaire Slide-In range from Lowe's in Jan. of 2007.  Model number FES 355 EBB. The serial number is NF64721744. I know my appliance is out of warranty, however it doesn't resolve the fact that the oven control wiring harness caught on fire while pre-heating the oven. Thankfully we were here to take care of the problem before it set the house on fire. I contacted Frigidaire through their website. A [REDACTED], Correspondence Specialist, e-mailed me back and stated that the product was out of warranty, there were no recalls, they were under no obligation to remedy, and I could have it repaired at my expense. This is more than a light going out. This is a very serious issue with their products. After researching other forums, and yours included, this appears to be an ongoing problem with this company. Please get these products off the market and force Frigidaire to make refunds for selling products this dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a wiring harness catching fire, which is a serious issue, but no injury or death occurred, and the problem was contained before causing further damage.

incident_description: I turned my oven on and when it got hot I noticed a light in the oven and went to check to see what it was and the element was on fire luckily I was not in another room. I was unable to put the fire out at first but something said turn it off and I did and I threw a large wet dish towel on the flames to put it out. There was nothing that spilled on the element the fire was a little red with blue glow and looked as if the fire was spreading along the element itself.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injury occurred, and the fire was successfully extinguished.

incident_description:
The wiring in the control panel within the front panel of my dishwasher caught on fire. The stainless steel panel became too hot to touch and extensive white smoke, smelling of burning plastic, filled the kitchen.

I was able to turn off the dishwasher and open the door to allow it to cool and vent. I then removed the front panel to discover extensive burnt wires and plastic in the control panel.
justification: The incident caused a fire and smoke, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Control Board developed a short.  It causes the dishwasher to continue to run for hours and hours.  It is the same issue with earlier modes that were recalled, but this is the next series and has not been recalled even though it is exactly the same problem.
justification: The dishwasher running continuously is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she made coffee and approximately 30 minutes later she heard a loud noise coming from the coffee maker. The consumer stated that she smelled a burning odor and saw smoke coming bottom of the coffee maker. 

The consumer stated that she unplugged the coffee maker. The consumer stated that it was extremely hot. The consumer stated that it was emitting smoke for approximately 5 minutes. 

The consumer stated that she would not use the coffee maker because she was afraid. 

The consumer stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.

The consumer believes this product should be investigated do to the fire and burning hazard that it poses to the consumer.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise, burning odor, and smoke, but no injury was reported, and the consumer unplugged the device safely.

incident_description: Kenmore dishwasher control panel started on fire during wash cycle.  I contacted sears with the issue and was told that there was no recall of this model and that nothing would be done for me.  One interesting thing is that a technician had been sent to my home to replace the motor on the unit about a month or two prior to the incident.  To supposedly prevent a potential fire.  I had never been contacted about this recall prior to my investigation related to a problem we had were the heating element burned a hole through the plastic tub of the dishwasher.  The tub was not replaced but there was a recall on the pump motor system.  I had patched the hole with epoxy type material i obtained from a local appliance repair company.  I retained the burned control panel and disposed of the remainder of the dishwasher and replaced with a new unit with no compensation from manufacturer.  These units in my opinion should be recalled as there seems to be many of them with the same control panel fire issue.
justification: The dishwasher control panel caught fire, but there was no mention of injury or death, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she wanted to report the unsafe condition of this product. The consumer
stated that about a year ago (09/29/2011) she was washing the coffee cups when the handle broke off and cut her ring finger. She stated that she did not seek medical attention.  

She also stated that about two weeks ago she was warming food in the microwave on one of the plates when the plate snapped in half. She stated that it had been warming for about two minutes. 

She stated that a couple of the smaller plates broke in the dishwasher. 

UPDATE: These dishes have been chipping and breaking for no reason.  
1. A step was not taken for example:  
2. They are [REDACTED] material. Not only are they not microwaveable as they say, they are not dishwasher safe, they are not handwashing safe.  I still have the 2 sets of dishes except ones that broke in half in the microwave and dishwasher.  I also do not have the cup that handle broke off and cut my hand (finger).
justification: The consumer reported multiple incidents of product failure, including an injury from a broken cup handle, indicating a pattern of unsafe conditions.

incident_description: Our stove that we bought comes on and goes off by itself... Most of the problem is it won't go off.  This has caused us to have minor burns.... We thought we were not doing something right till I read about it... We should have called Frigidaire long ago. Today they said it was not a recall and my problem to get it fixed...
justification: The stove malfunction has caused minor burns, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer says there is a high whistling noise with the front burner and the oven.  A technician replaced the pressure regulator.  He says that when the oven is on there is an odor and burning sensation.  It is not a natural gas odor, more of a burning gas.  The consumer feels the stove is completely dangerous.  

The consumer says when the oven comes on, he has a high whistling noise.  When the flame is turned off the noise goes away.  This is in conjunction with the top burner and the oven.  The first issue was with the right top burner.  Then it started in the oven.  

He contacted the manufacturer, they sent a repairman who replaced the regulator and said that is all he can do.  He says it has been a year since this incident began.  The consumer would like the stove replaced.
justification: The incident involves a dangerous condition with potential for injury due to burning sensation and odor, but no actual injury has been reported.

incident_description: Was cooking a bag of popcorn when smelled something burning and smoke coming from microwave. Thought it was the popcorn that caught fire but found instead that the plastic clips that hold the metal rack caught fire. The rack was not in the microwave when the clips caught fire. The popcorn was under cooked and the timer was set by the microwave for popcorn which was three minutes. Stopped the microwave and have not used microwave again. Looked online for problems with this unit and found there was a recall for units built with a different serial number but then found other complaints with the exact same problem that happened to me, but they were told that they did not fall under the recall. Don't care if it is under recall or not just warn others that this unit can catch fire and not to use them. Thank You for trying to protect the public from defective products. This unit can cause major damage.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury or death, but potential for major damage.

incident_description:
I had just walked down the hall when I heard popping noises. So by time I entered the kitchen, I figured it was the coffee pot making the noises. As I got closer, I was confused because there were no lights on and the timer window was blank but it was still plugged in.  It was still on before this had happened.  I pulled the carafe out and noticed the bottom was glowing red.  Then, it started to smoke.  I quickly pulled the plug and took it out back on the patio where it continued to smoke for another 10 minutes.  
Cuisinart DCC1200 
SN: 91120 h
justification: The coffee pot malfunctioned and started smoking, but no injury or damage occurred as the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
Jan 2011, we purchased a Cuisinart DCC-1200 12 cup coffee maker, serial # 00804H from Amazon.com.   It worked well until this week, when during making coffee it began to pop, smoke, hiss, and sounded/smelled like an electrical fire.  Smoke was coming from out of the unit long after we unplugged it.  

While researching this on line, it appears to be a common problem with this unit.  Cuisinart is sending a replacement and asked only for the cord back, so obviously they know where the problem originates. Thanks

I went to the kitchen to investigate and found smoke coming out of the burner vent, looked through the glass of the oven door and saw that about four inches of the bottom heating element had melted starting at the point where it attaches to the oven wall.
