While it was on fire it was making a loud crackling noise almost like the sound of popcorn popping..
justification: The microwave caught fire but was quickly noticed and no injury occurred, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The outter cover of the oven door fell off while I was openning the oven door. The outter cover fell on the tops of both of my feet bruising them. This outter covering weighs between 5 and 10 lb.

I have had this range for about 8 years, and this will be the fourth time the oven door will be repaired.

incident_description: I heard a popping sound coming from my 4-month-old GE refrigerator.  Upon investigating further, I opened the freezer door and sparks were shooting out the bottom vent in the freezer compartment with minor smoke.  After unplugging the appliance, I began to smell wires burning.  The back of the freezer area on the refrigerator was hot to touch as was the sheetrock behind where the refrigerator was sitting.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and burning wires, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I had the back two stove top burners on my Kenmore gas range (model 790.71383709) operating on low for most of two separate days while simmering chili. An hour or so after turning the burners off my carbon monoxide detector went off and showed a reading of 58 PPM.

The fire department arrived and checked my furnace, hot water heater, and gas dryer finding no evidence of carbon monoxide. The gas range was the only gas appliance that had been running that day, so they felt that was the source. The concentration of CO2 was immediately in the vicinity of the range.

At the suggestion of the fire department, all of the windows and doors in the house were opened for several hours to air the house out.
justification: The incident involved a carbon monoxide leak detected at a low level (58 PPM) with no reported injuries, and the situation was mitigated by airing out the house.

incident_description: Used the Pyrex pie dish in an oven to cook a deep dish pizza. It shattered spontaneously upon removing it from the oven and placing it on the stovetop to cool.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I purchased Hampton Forge Epicure 17-piece cutlery set during the summer.  In the last three months, three of the steak knives have broken.  In one case, I was slicing some cheddar cheese, and the knife broke, and the blade tip punctured the skin on my left hand.  Luckily, no significant injury, but if I had been working on a food item harder than cheese (!), there would have been more force involved.

The issue is that the tang of the knife blade extends only a very short distance into the handle -- a design issue that is not apparent until one of the knives breaks, at which point you can see the very short length of the tang.  The hard plastic is not of sufficient strength to handle the stress of transferring the force from the handle to the tang of the blade.

I still have two of the broken knives -- I threw the first one away, not realizing this would be a common occurrence.  I can send a picture if that would be helpful.

By the way, if one does a [REDACTED] search on "hampton forge epicure knife broke" you will see that this is a _very_ common occurrence.  I am glad that Hampton Forge appears very willing to provide a replacement set if contacted, but that does not solve the safety issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (punctured skin) and the description indicates this is a common issue with the product.

incident_description:
Coffee pot handle broke.

incident_description: I was washing the Pampered Chef ice cream scoop when it exploded in the kitchen sink.  The noise was deafening.  The plastic cap as well as the metal cap that was under the plastic cap at the end of the handle flew off with tremendous force.  The caps hit the inside front wall of the kitchen sink and then flew back toward the kitchen window.  They hit the windowsill and dented the wooden sill.  The caps then flew forward again and knocked over a large styrofoam cup filled with ice and coke.  They knocked over the cup and then landed on the kitchen counter.  My ears rang for several hours after the incident because the explosion was so loud.  If I had been holding the scoop when it exploded, I could have been seriously injured.  If the caps had flown toward me or someone else, they could have caused great injury.  I am amazed that an innocent looking ice cream scoop could cause such an explosion -- the noise was much louder than a gun being fired.  I have found out that the scoops were recalled in December 2011; however, I never heard anything about the recall.  I firmly believe that there should be a mass effort by the media to inform the public of this problem.  The Pampered Chef website has some information about the recall and they state that the plastic cap can pop off.  That is such a gross understatement.  The ice cream scoop is a potential lethal weapon and anyone who has one should be notified immediately.
justification: The incident caused no injury but involved a loud explosion and property damage, indicating a significant incident without harm to individuals.

incident_description:
While roasting vegetables in a Pyrex 9x11 glass baking dish, it exploded while in the oven. Following the directions that came with the set of glass baking dishes, I preheated the oven first. About 2 minutes before the end of the 40 minute roasting time, the dish exploded with a very loud bang. Fortunately, the failure came while the dish was confined in the oven. I can't imagine the damage or injury that might have occurred had that happened on taking it out of the oven or while cooling on a hot pad.

I took digital photos of the broken dish in the oven as evidence of the incident.
justification: The incident involved an exploding baking dish but no injuries occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was confined in the oven.

incident_description:
I have a Frididaire Electric cooktop.  Last night I smelled smoke.  A dish on left on the stove was burning.  One of the burners was spontaneously on be itself.  The only way to turn it off was to trip the circuit breaker for the appliance.
I check at Frigidaire.  There is a product recall on some of their cooktops with the exact same problem as mine, but mine is not part of the recall.

This could have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved a burning dish and a malfunctioning burner, posing a fire risk, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that she loud noise and saw smoke coming from the top of the oven door. The consumer stated that she saw flames that were contained within the inside of the oven. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured.

The consumer stated that she also contacted the retailer and they stated that they would repair it, but she would have to pay for the parts.

incident_description: Mr Coffee coffeemaker model #  BVMC-EJX33 (purchased 8 months ago) suddenly began to smoke and burn after brewing coffee morning of 10-12-12.   Heavy smoke and burning smell from unit began approx 2 minutes after brew cycle completed.

incident_description:

incident_description: We have a Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker that is 18 months old.  After brewing a pot of coffee, smoke started coming out from under the warming plate that the carafe sits on.  No fire was noticed, only smoke.

incident_description: After toasting a slice of bread, the toaster oven (Black & Decker Countertop Oven Model TRO480BS) switched off and the bell rang.  Approximately ten seconds later, the oven exploded with a loud bang, the handle blew off and the glass door shattered and glass flew across the room (approximately 4 feet away.)  Had I been standing in front of the toaster oven, I would have been badly injured.  No fire or smoke was noticed.  The oven was purchased at Macy's on April 4, 2012 and this incident occurred Wed Sep 12, 2012.  I called the Customer Care Line (1-800-231-9786) on the product information sheet and reported the incident on Fri Sep 14, 2012.  The company sent me a new toaster oven (same model), which I have not opened or used.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite smooth top electric range. Model # 92002102  Serial # RP1833073
It was in my home when I purchased the house 2 years ago.
About two weeks ago, the right front burner would not turn to a low temperature. Even at the "low" setting, it was red hot (as if it was on the high setting). This happened only once and since I could not recreate the problem, I did not call for service.

Today I was baking. I smelled something burning and opened the oven to find that both the oven AND the broiler element were on. I know I did not turn on the broiler.  I turned off the oven. About 10 minutes later I again smelled something very hot (fortunately I was still in the kitchen).  I went to the range and could feel heat. I opened the oven door and the broiler element was ON.  ALL the settings were off and there was no way to turn off the broiler. I turned off the circuit breaker as that is the only to turn off the oven. 

If I had not been in the kitchen when this event occurred, it would have burned the house down - absolutely NO doubt about that. I checked for recalls of this model range and although there are several reports of this evetn occurring to consumers, no recall has been issued by the manufacturer.  Even if the control board is replaced, the new part will be designed exactly like the old part since no recall has been issued to cause the part to be re-designed.   There is no doubt what so ever that this is a dangerous product and should be recalled.  Do a web search on this model number and you will see the reports.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore electric slide in range, glass top, Model # 790.96112409. For a few weeks the left front burner would only work on high and would not turn off immediately when knob turned to off position. It would take several times of  turning the knob on and back off before burner would turn off. Today, I have noticed several times the same burner would turn on and off spontaneously while the stove was not in use. Ultimately, we have turned the breaker off to the stove for fear of fire.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I was getting the kids ready for bed and I smelled burning plastic.  I followed the smell to the kitchen and realized it was coming from my dishwasher.  I opened it thinking a piece of tupperware or something had fallen on the heating coil.  Instead I found the one part of the heating coil bright red and flaming.  It had started to melt the rolling dish tray and utensil basket.

I called Sears today to report the problem and was sent to the "Recall Department". They refused to give me any information and just told me to schedule a "service call".  

That's when I hung up and came to this website.
justification: The incident involved a flaming heating coil in the dishwasher, which could have led to injury but did not.

incident_description: The exterior glass oven door of our Kenmore 790.92903010 electric range exploded sending glass shards that covered the entire kitchen.  We had only had the oven less than 2 years and had no unusual useage.

incident_description: I heard a pop from my oven and didnt think anything of it.  Like an hour later I wanted to bake some cookies so I preheated the oven to 350.  I waited for over 20 mins and it was only on 310. I opened the oven and it felt a lot cooler than 310 and it didnt bake my cookies.  It then got a lot hotter.  I turned my oven off and noticed that the heating element in around the fan was bright orange...even when my oven was off!!!  I had to turn off the actual power for the oven from the power box.  I tried to turn it on again later and it still lit up orange, heating away, by itself!!  I dont want to think about what could have happened at night or if no one was home!  Its dangerous!!!  a firehazard!!  I cant even use my range because the oven still lights up. I have to shut off all power for the stove!! incident_description: I have a Kenmore smooth top range that I purchased in 2008 that turns itself on. The burners will come on themselves without reason. This is a very serious issue and I would love some sort of remedy.

incident_description:
My husband was brewing coffee in our Cuisinart DCC-1200 Brew Central Coffee Maker.  He has just finished brewing and poured his first cup of coffee.  He then walked into the dining area to have his cup of coffee, when he heard hissing and popping, returned to the kitchen, and the coffee maker had smoke coming out of it.  The display went out when this happened and he immediately pulled the plug on the unit.  

I researched the history online of any potential problems with this unit, and found numerous complaints, but no recalls by the manufacturer.  

I wanted to report this so that any future consumers can be aware of this fire hazard and hopefully have Cuisinart issue a recall of the product.

I will be contacting Cuisinart today to file a complaint and discuss the warranty.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite Range Model number 7909664**** that has almost burned my house down twice now.  This unit does not seem to be in past recalls, but I have seen MANY of the same issues by other consumers reported online.  First there have been problems with the element not turning off after it has been turned off.  This is the same problem I have seen wide spread on models that are very similar to my model.  Sometimes, we have to touch the off sensor several times to get the element, or part of the element, to turn off.  Because of this, my son caught a pot holder on fire when he left it on the stove top not realizing that the element had not turned off.  Luckily, no one was injured.  The main issue we have had is the oven unit that heats up extremely fast and past the set temperature.  The unit will start beeping and flashing a "run away temperature" code but continues to heat up, and the controls are useless.  The oven went from off to over 600 degrees in less than five minutes and the food inside the oven was smoking with small flames.  It would not turn off with the controls and I had to run downstairs to kill the power via the breaker.  My husband burned himself opening the EXTREMELY hot oven to (1) get out the smoking, burning food and (2) try to cool the inside temperature down.  We only know it was 600 degrees and climbing because we have a thermometer in the oven so we always know the correct oven temperature.  I truly believe that this range and other similar models are a safety hazard.  The estimated date below is for the oven incident and not the stove top problem.  That has been going on for a good while, we have just never looked into.  We did not know there was a recall because of the same issue with similar models, nor did we think about reporting it.  I wish now we would have and think Sear's should have to refund everyone's money on the ranges with these problems.
justification: The incident involved a burn injury from handling an extremely hot oven, and similar issues are reported widely by other consumers, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Kitchenaid double oven inner glass exploded when we ran the self-clean cycle. Company inspector came to the house and said it was a defect and replaced oven. After several months we ran self-clean on the new oven, and it also exploded hot glass all over our kitchen floor.

incident_description:
The Emerson 900W Microwave Oven MW8999RD/MW8999SB has a poorly designed unbalanced rotating tray.  The tray tends to slip if anything more than a cup of coffee is heated on it.  When trying to remove the heated item, the slipping of the tray caused minor burns only because I stepped away from it and did not get the full impact of the spilled liquid. It could be very dangerous for elderly or disabled people or children, even if they are being careful.
