incident_description:
Caller purchased his microwave April 21st, 2011 and had no problems with it until Thursday, September 13th, 2012.

Caller was sitting in his living room, heard noise coming from microwave in kitchen, he entered kitchen, reset microwave by turning off then on again.
All seemed fine through the evening with no other incidents,

He went to bed but was awakened by the "dinging" around 2:00AM, he went to his kitchen, realized the microwave was turning itself on, running for approximately 30 seconds, then turning off then turning on again for same amount of time.
He touched the microwave and it was extremely hot, he then unplugged the microwave.

He called the manufacturer and they said they had never heard of it and that possibly it was a power surge.
They asked him to cut the cord, take the sticker off and dispose of the microwave.
He states that he sees this as a way of disposing of evidence.

He then called a friend who is a mechanical engineer and was informed that it is impossible for a power surge to turn the microwave on and off.  It could fry the board but could not turn it on and off.

He then contacted his wife, asked her if she would google, "microwave and fire" and she came up with CPSC.
Caller is asking that CPSC Investigator look at this microwave and identify the problem, then recall it for the safety of the public.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but did not cause injury or death, and similar incidents are unlikely based on the manufacturer's response.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she is experiencing problems with her smooth top electric range.  The front right burner will not turn off, it increases the temperature while it is being set on low by itself.  The circuit breaker has to used to power off the range.  This was the first incident.

The consumer feels that she is experiencing the same problems of Release # 09-333.

9/10/12  The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that her model was not part of the recall and she should report it to the agency.

The consumer feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer reported that the clear plastic broke off into the icemaker of the refrigerator and came out in his daughter's drink.  There was no injury.

(5/2012)The manufacturer was contacted and he had it replaced but the incident re-occurred 9/2012.

The consumer feels that the plastic is made from an inferior material which can cause injury if this goes unnoticed.

(9/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and a service rep was sent out, he was advised that it would be replaced.  The replacement parts was received, however, he feels that this will not resolve the issue and requested an improved quality replacement part or to replace the product.
justification: The incident involved plastic breaking off into the drink but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence of the issue suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: GE microwave JVM1750DM1  turned on by itself.  I heard the buttons being pressed on the microwave and thought that someone was in the kitchen.  When I realized that no one was in the kitchen, I went in to see what was going on.  The microwave had turned itself on and was running on the canned vegetable mode (which I have never used).  I turned off the unit.  Two days later, the microwave again started itself.  I turned the unit off and called GE - after speaking with the customer service person, he put me through to the consumer relations department - after being on hold for 20 minutes, I hung up.  A few days later, the microwave again started by itself.  I again contacted GE - this time the customer service person informed me that I needed to place a service call.  I told her that I thought it was a defect, not something that I should be charged for to have fixed.  She said that there were no other reports or recalls on the microwave model number and again insisted that a technician needed to come to the house (at a charge of course).  I voiced my objection at having to pay for someone to fix something that I feel is a defect and possible fire hazard - and that if they are not taking down reports, how would they know how many times this is happening - no one seems to be keeping track.  I requested to be put through to the customer relations department.  After being on hold for 34 minutes and 7 seconds, I gave up yet again.  I unplugged the unit and have not used it since.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller was sitting in another room from her kitchen and her cleaning lady came running out of the kitchen yelling that she had no idea what had happened but that smoke was coming out of the gas stove.

No one had used the stove since the day before (over 24 hours)

Caller ran into the kitchen, saw that the smoke was coming out of the right side of the stove, checked to turn stove off, however it was not turned on.
She immediately contacted the fire department.

The fire department came in, saw the smoke, disconnected gas from stove, put stove outside in caller's front yard then advised caller to definitely keep stove out of her house and replace with new one.

Cause of fire was short in the wires according to firehouse
justification: The incident involved smoke from a gas stove due to a wiring short, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the induction stove advertised stated that that it was safe for a child to cook with their mother because there was no burn hazard.  However, when she was using it the unit became so hot she burned her hand.  She also noticed that there was contradiction between advertising and the label which stated it is a burn hazard.

8/2012  The caller contacted the company and was told that she could return the unit for a refund.  She was not informed if they had received any other reports.  They advised her that they stand behind the advertisement of the product and that although they printed on the unit they didnot have to advertise it.

The caller feels that this is a misconception and that this product is unsafe and should be properly advertised.
justification: The caller burned her hand due to the stove becoming excessively hot, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was trying to heat the water for approximately 1-2 minutes on the pot and it was leaking hot water from underneath. The consumer stated that it was leaking water around electrical component. 

The consumer stated that he dumped the water and unplugged the hotpot and will not be using it. 

The consumer stated that he was not injured. 

The consumer stated that he would be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.
justification: The incident involved a leaking hotpot with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Product is a Samsung Over-the-Range Microwave Oven, model # SMH9207ST/XAA, Serial Number J4MY7WO300207K.

The microwave has a cooktop light on the bottom of the oven.  The glass cover on the cooktop light gets extremely hot.

My hand came in contact with the cover of the cooktop light while reaching for a pot on the rear burner of my stovetop.  The brief contact burned my right hand between the thumb and wrist..  The burned area was approx 1.5in x 1in, and took approx 2 weeks to heal.  I applied first-aid at home, and did not seek medical attention.  The burned skin turned deep red, and was painful for a week, but did not form any blisters

The cooktop light uses two standard 40-watt appliance bulbs, which came with the appliance.  The cavity which holds the lamps is very shallow, which means the glass cover is almost in direct contact with the bulbs, causing it to reach an unsafe temperature when the light is in normal use.  Because the cooktop light is on the bottom of the microwave, the consumer cannot readily see its location.  When reaching to the rear of the stovetop, is is therefore very easy for an unprotected hand/arm to come into contact with the very hot light cover.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury that required two weeks to heal, indicating a severity level of 3. The design flaw makes contact with the hot light cover likely during normal use.

incident_description: Dishwasher began smoking during Normal wash cycle.  Smoke smells like burning plastic/electrical.  Dishwasher would not turn off when Cancel was pushed or door opened.  Smoke continued 5 minutes after power to dishwasher was turned off.  There were no injuries or counter damage.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and had electrical issues, but there were no injuries or damage, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer says whenever the stove is turned on the knobs get too hot to handle, the knobs get extremely hot to the touch.  The retailer has sent out a technician four times who assess the same thing every time.  The manufacturer has determined that it is not hot enough to warrant any service or repair.  

The consumer says this is a definite safety concern; they have been in contact with the manufacturer since January of 2011 for the same issue and they refuse to offer any assistance.  The consumer says that a service flash is issued by the retailer known as FF22-574 that states "no temperature limitations apply to the range top".

The consumer says that a prior report listed the temperature at 345 degrees on the top per the service technician who came out on April 25th 2012.
justification: The knobs get extremely hot to the touch, posing a safety concern, but there is no report of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer was baking a pie.  It took an hour to bake and the consumer turned the oven off.  Thirty minutes later the outer glass exploded after he had just started to open the door to take out the pie.  He says small pieces of glass went all over him but he was not injured.  Glass shattered all over the kitchen.  

He says there are others who have complained of this issue involving the same product.  The consumer says that the company only has a year warranty on this item.  

The customer is concerned because the glass exploded without warning.  He says it is of a definite safety concern.  

The consumer has not yet talked to the manufacturer.
justification: The consumer was not injured but the glass explosion caused a safety concern and property damage, indicating an incident without injury. The mention of others complaining about the same issue suggests the occurrence is likely.

incident_description: A Pampered chef ice cream scoop exploded in my hand while washing it in warm water. The explosion was so loud that my ears were ringing. It was very forceful breaking a veins in my three middle fingers. They are so swollen I cannot bend them. The plastic piece plugging in the liquid center of the handle flew across the room breaking and knocking a potted plant off the countertop.
justification: The incident caused injury with broken veins and swollen fingers, but no death. Such incidents are unlikely given the specific circumstances.

incident_description:
Our Electrolux gas stove's electronics malfunctioned and gas flow could not be shut off.
The stove kept on getting hotter and hotter.  Our house almost caught on fire.  Apparently
this has happened with other  Electrolux and Frigidaire models.
justification: The stove malfunctioned and could not be shut off, causing a near fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Arrived home from vacation to find one of our pots melted on the stove top and the glass top cracked and partially melted. Apparently the burner turned on by itself while we were gone. Luckily nothing in the kitchen caught on fire.
justification: Incident caused property damage (melted pot and cracked stove top) but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
The left rear burner will not turn off after using it.  This is very dangerous and may cause a fire if not corrected.

Electrolux / Frigidaire has a recall on this same type stoe - manufactured at the same time as mine.  They do not include my model in their current recall.
justification: The burner not turning off poses a fire hazard, which is dangerous but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I purchased an Electrolux undercounter style dishwasher and installed it according to the manufacturer's instructions.  Everytime water would drip from the counter and land onto the control panel, the dishwasher would short-circuit.  The control panel (that is used to select dishwashing cycles and option) was not sufficiently waterproof to prevent water from entering the unit and shorting out the electronic circuit board.  As a result of this poor design and defect, the dishwasher would routinely trip the circuit breaker.

Each time the unit would get even the slightest amount of water on or near the control panel, I would have to wait for the unit to air dry.  The final time that the unit failed, while selecting a cycle on the control panel I received a small electric shock.  After turning the unit off at the circuit breaker, the unit would not work again when tested and was discarded.
justification: The incident resulted in a small electric shock, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The issue occurred routinely with water exposure, making the likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
My Oster Electric Tea Kettle, model # BVST - EK5967, purchased from Target within the past three months, had an electric meltdown today.  It fused the tea kettle base to the teapot. There was a circle of ash one foot around the base, and it smelled like burning plastic.  Luckily, I have granite counters and a tile backsplash, and nothing was too close to it.  

The tea kettle was sitting on the bottom heating plate, but was not on, and it had water in it. It was on a GFI outlet, which did not shut off.  Fortunately we were home and smelled something burning.  I can only imagine that it would have caught fire and put the other neighbors in my condo at risk!

I am going to return this to Target, but I wanted to file a report so that someone looks into this. I am seriously worried about the danger this could have caused!
justification: The incident involved an electric meltdown with potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Amana Range, Model # ACF3355AS, Serial # 11388139CJ.
We used the self clean option for the first time since we moved in (Dec 2011).  After a few minutes, one of our smoke alarms and/or carbon monixide alarms went off. Excessive smoke and odor emitted from the top of the oven door. After 3 hours, the self cleaning was over. The door would not open, the oven displayed a "F9-2" error (latch error).  Eventually we were able to open it. We noticed the plastic bezel on top of the door was melted all over the top of the oven door (photos available). There was a strong acrid odor throughout the house, which took several days to remove with open windows and doors. We contacted Amana (now Whirlpool) and talked to someone in their safety department. They agreed to pay for a service call by Central Service of Monona WI. The service tech inspected the range and reported back the next day that they believed the circuit board failed on the range, allowing the broiler relay to stay on too long, causing an overheat condition. The service tech contacted Whirlpool, and Whilpool refused to pay for repairs. I contacted the safety person at Whirlpool again, and they said they would not pay for repairs due to the age of the range (approximately 9 years old). The service tech advised us the range was safe to use, except for the self clean function.
I consider this both a health and safety issue due to the toxic smoke generated from the melting plastic, and the risk of fire caused by the overheat.
justification: The incident involved excessive smoke and melting plastic, posing a health and safety risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Whirlpool Refrigerator Model#EDSPHEXNL00 started to smoke from the condenser plug ( this maybe relay). When I opened back panel to check it, it was burned out and melted, even melted the metal pin that was pluged in to the Relay. My kitchen was filled with smoke from it. This part should be recall since it can cause fire.
justification: The refrigerator emitted smoke and had a burned-out component, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Our Kitchenaid Dishwasher (model KUDS01FLSS5, serial FR3008208)  caught fire.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Have owned a Keurig Coffee Brewer for a year or so and it is positioned on the kitchen counter near other appliances including a toaster oven.  I discovered today that the cord on the Keurig is not made of heat resistant material.  The cord was in close proximity to the  toaster and it melted causing an electrical flash. Neither the toaster oven was on or the Keurig although I had just toasted some bread minutes earlier.  No one was hurt and the circuit breaker was tripped.  Upon inspection both electrical  wires were exposed.  The irony is the ground wire looks like it is covered with a heat resistant coating as it remained unmelted.  Would be great if all kitchen appliance were required to have heat resistant cords due to the proximity to heated appliance such as skillets, toasters, crock pots, rice cookers, rotisseries and small ovens.  I don't believe this product is safe for consumers. I guess I need to throw this $180 appliance away!
justification: The incident involved an electrical flash and exposed wires, but no one was hurt.

incident_description: On September 20th 2012 we returned to our home after a 4 hour absence.  Immediately upon entering the house we could smell that something was very hot.  We went straight to the gas range and noticed that the display panel indicated the broiler was on and was set to HI.  The range, microwave above it and counters were very hot to the touch indicating to us that the broiler had been on for quite some time.  The entire house was filled with a "hot" smell.  I had not used the stove or broiler that day.  In fact, I hadn't used the broiler in quite some time.  We turned the broiler off.  Less than half an hour later, it did the same thing.  Our BOSCH gas range, MODEL NUMBER HGS53052UC/01, SERIAL NUMBER FD870200207 had once again TURNED ITSELF ON to HI broil.  We unplugged it and have not used it since.  Our local appliance repairman, in consultation with the BOSCH technicians, diagnosed it as a bad control module.  Our range is 5 years old, but this is still a very dangerous malfunction.  Had it occurred 4 days later, we would have been on vacation and would have most likely returned to a burned down home.  I did some research on the Internet, thinking there must have been a recall on the product.  I found no recall, but did find several other consumer reports stating control module problems with the Bosch gas range and even another report exactly the same experience as ours.
justification: The incident caused a dangerous malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The locking child resistant device snaps after minimal usage because it is made of plastic and poorly designed. The metal springs are strong and easily snap the mechanism to allow it to be opened by a child. The blades are very sharp. 
The catalog number is CUIBDH2  part # BDH-2.

If you desire I can mail the defective part to you for examination.

Thanks,
[REDACTED]
justification: The sharp blades and faulty locking mechanism can cause injury, but there is no mention of any injury or death.

incident_description: We had purchased the Calphalon coffee maker (HE120CMG - http://store.calphalon.com/calphalon-electrics-12-c-quick-brew-coffee-maker/407384) about 6 months ago, and yesterday morning, it started on fire. We believe it had something to do with the heating element. It started smoking (and crackling) from inside the machine and billowing from the back of the machine where the cord enters the base.
justification: The coffee maker started on fire, which is a significant incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The microwave just started on it's own at about 6:35 this morning.  My son (the only other person in the house was fast asleep.  There was nothing that could have reasonably fallen on it at the height it was at.  

It appeared to be on a 6 minute cycle.  Luckily, it being on woke me up.
justification: The microwave turned on unexpectedly, but no injury or damage occurred, and the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely.

incident_description:
Progressive 2-in-1 Mortar and Pestle features a two-mortar design, one small and one large, in something of an hourglass shape. It comes with a rubber lid that the instructions claim can be placed on either the small or the large mortar as a non-skid base. The product instructions state: "Place black lid inside large mortar when using the small bowl for added stability and non-skid benefit." The trouble is either that 1) the lid is too large to be placed inside the large mortar or 2) the large mortar is too small to accommodate the lid. Either way, the lid absolutely will not fit inside the large mortar as promised. 

I tried and tried to push the black lid down inside the large mortar but after repeated unsuccessful attempts I ended up injuring my thumb because the lid simply would not go down inside the mortar. It is now five months or so since the injury and my thumb is still painful and a bit swollen. I notice it especially when I grip handlebars or some similar object. 

I called this problem to the attention of the company shortly after the injury, but the person I talked to, [redacted] I believe was her name, just blew me off and did not provide any satisfaction for my complaint.
justification: The incident resulted in a persistent thumb injury, but the likelihood of such an injury occurring is unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: This morning I discovered that the oven of my Kenmore glass-top electric range was very hot. The controls were all in the off position and had been so for at least 12 hours. I had to turn off the circuit to shut off the oven. This could have caused a fire and perhaps injuries or fatalities.
justification: The oven was hot despite being off, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injuries occurred.

incident_description: The specific product referred to in this report is a Kenmore Gas Range Model # 790.78673400; Serial # VF44446826.  My wife was at home with our 11 month old, feeding her lunch in the kitchen when without warning, the glass on the outside of the oven door exploded outward, sending shards of glass flying multiple feet across the kitchen.  The range was off and had not been in use for many hours.  The biggest danger of this incident was the flying glass, which could have seriously injured my daughter had she been within a few more feet of the oven.  In doing some research online, we have found that this is not an isolated incident, but rather somewhat of a common event in Kenmore Gas Ranges starting with model # 790.  I certainly hope that this would warrant further investigation.
justification: The incident involved flying glass that could have caused injury but did not, and similar incidents are reported to be somewhat common for this model.

incident_description: I am disappointed in Kenmore as to both their product quality and customer service follow up.  I have a built in wall oven model 790.47783403 in which the oven racks collapse down to the bottom of the oven, hot pans with boiling liquids and all.  This happens repreatedly.  I called all the recommended numbers for help and got nowhere.  The racks are simply too narrow for the width of the oven.  This has created a dangerous situation for all concerned, as we have small gandchildren.  I'm sure there are other ovens out there with the same issue and even saw prior reports with the Consumer Product Safety Commission.
justification: The incident describes a recurring dangerous situation with oven racks collapsing, posing a risk especially to small grandchildren, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: We had set our dishwasher to run on a delay and gone to bed.  My husband was unable to sleep and happened to be up.  The dishwasher was running when there was a large flash of white light from the top right side of the front panel of the dishwasher, after which it began to pour black smoke.  He was able to stop the dishwasher, and then opened windows to clear the smoke and burnt plastic smell.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and a flash of light, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
On [10/3/12] at approximately 4:55 p.m., the heating element in our Kenmore electric range, Model 790.9601 caught fire, without stimulus. Fortunately my wife was in the kitchen when this occurred. We called 911, and used a fire extinguisher. Two fire trucks arrived, and fortunately we were able to put out the fire with the fire extinguisher. 

We have found that similar problems from Kenmore ranges have been noted, and recalled. This particular model has been reported as well for the same problem.

When we called Sears, they acknowledged that (a) we cannot use the range again due to the use of the fire extinguisher; and (b) that similar problems have been reported.

The "customer service" department stated that although they acknowledge similar reports have been made, because we did not purchase the extended warranty, the most they could do is offer a discounted repair (which they stated could not be done) or a 10% off coupon (which one can typically find in the newspaper). It took 7 attempts to speak with someone, after being transferred from line to line and being disconnected twice. 

Sears is unwilling to take responsibility for an obvious and dangerous flaw that nearly cost our family its home and threatened the safety of my wife and sons.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries were reported, and the fire was extinguished without further damage.

incident_description:
FIRE HAZARD
I tried to turn off the right front burner, but the middle ring element would not turn off.  Burned the bottom of the soup I was cooking.  It took 5-10 minutes to realize that I shut the burner off, but the element did not turn off.  The range panel/control indicated the burner was off.
Once I realized the burner would not turn off even the the control said it was off, I turned the range off at the circuit breaker in the basement.  Resetting the circuit breaker did not fix the problem.
Fortunately, I was home and in the kitchen after I tried turning it off.  Otherwise, it may have started a fire.
From the picture you can see where the range was turned on (hence the PF - power failure status), the burner indictors are not on, but the element is on anyway.  It's quite unsafe.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that could have caused a fire, but no injury or damage occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description:
An Anchor Hocking glass baking dish exploded in my oven.  

The incident occurred while baking a whole chicken in a Anchor Hocking baking dish.  The dish had been in the oven at 350 degrees baking for approximately 30 minutes on a rack set in the middle of the oven.  

I opened the oven door and moved the dish slightly to the side so I could insert a vegetable dish to also bake.  I inserted the vegetable dish to the other side of the oven without it hitting or touching  the dish containing the chicken.   As I closed the oven door the dish containing the chicken suddenly shattered violently sending glass and hot grease flying though out the oven and also into the kitchen. The glass baking dish for the vegetables was fine.

Fortunately, I had just stepped back in order to close the oven door,  otherwise, I would have gotten the  flying glass and hot grease directly in to my face, eyes, arms and hands.  A very close call!!!  

Of course the chicken  dinner and vegetable dish were discarded.  In cleaning up the mess, both my husband and I got minor cuts from all the glass pieces.   Fortunately nothing serious. 

There was no warning that the dish was going to explode.  The incident could have caused serious injury to me if I had not just stepped back to close the oven door.
justification: Minor cuts were sustained during cleanup, indicating an injury occurred, but no serious harm resulted.

incident_description: Customer standing next to refrigerator and heard popping, looked and saw generous smoke. Opened door to refigerator motor, found sparking green and blue.  Cage with wiring harness burst into flame.  Customer grabbed fire extinguisher & attempted to put fire out, flames returned, customers husband turned off the breaker and customer successfully extinguished fire.  Kitchen and much of house heavily dusted with Monammonium Phosphate from the extinguisher.
justification: The incident involved a fire and use of a fire extinguisher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We have used this product approximately 3 times. I noticed a electrical burning smell the last time (yesterday) while cooking. After finishing its use and while cleaning it I noticed on the underside of the unit an area that has melted. Upon closer inspection I also noticed that some of the insulation on the cord has been damaged where it goes into the cord storage part of the unit. 

Upon some checking on the internet I see that this is a common problem and the product appears to be unsafe and a potential fire hazard.

I used the product as directed in the owners manual and hope that there is enough evidence to recall this dangerous product.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (5) due to the commonality of the problem as noted online.

incident_description:
(09/16/2012) The consumer stated that she had the oven on the self-clean feature. This was the first time that the consumer had used this feature. About 1 1/2 to 2hours into the cycle there was a loud explosion. The glass stating shooting out from the bottom of the oven. The consumer turned of the self clean feature. She stated that she opened the door and found glass everywhere. The glass from the oven was so hot that it scorched the hardwood floors in her kitchen. 

(09/17/2012) The consumer stated that she called the manufacturer and was told that this happens every once in a while. She also stated that the manufacturer offered to send a technician  out at a cost to the consumer. 

The consumer stated that she feels that this is unsafe
justification: The incident involved a loud explosion and glass shooting out, but no injuries were reported. The manufacturer indicated this happens occasionally, suggesting it is unlikely but not rare.

incident_description: This incident involved an ice maker.  Model # PSS26SGRBSS-Serial #RFG413246.  The ice maker was making noise.  This means it was not making ice .  I removed storage bin.  There was an ice cube stuck to bottom of unit in back .  I reached back to remove and my fingers touched bottom of unit where ice cubes are made. My skin turned white and I was burnt immediately. This is the second time this has happened. The prior time I was not only burnt but also shocked.  I reported the incident to GE.  They sent out repairman who stated that it was from a heating element in the bottom of the ice maker and that they have been making it this way for 42 years.  The trip charge was waived and I was charged $99.00 for labor for installing ice maker under warranty.  I believe this is a serious design flaw. There is only 1-1/2 inches clearance in space involved. There is no cover on heating element.
justification: The incident caused burns to the user, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a 6 quart slow cooker in March, 2012.

She had just finished washing it on August 22nd, 2012, still had it in her hand when it just broke, 
She doesn't remember what did happened, she was only aware that the index finger on right hand on the side in a triangle which is why the skin popped out and the pinkie then ring finger on the second joint,  on her left hand were cut and she was bleeding.

Her ring finger on her left hand is remaining numb and she can't straighten it and her pinkie on the left hand is sliced vertically as if a knife or cutting utensil dropped sliced and folded her skin, the cut is down to her first knuckle.

She cannot remember what happened, she remembers only that she was holding it one second and the next second it was lying in four pieces and she was bleeding profusely.

Caller's 8yr old daughter called an ambulance and caller was transported to the nearby hospital emergency room where she was given strong pain medication and received 18 stitches total for the three fingers.

She was released later that night being advised that she would need to speak with a plastic surgeon within just a couple of days because they are not positive that they were able to repair it adequately.

She would ask that an investigator look at these slow cookers for weak spots or defects and recall them.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries requiring medical attention, including stitches and potential plastic surgery, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I have qa kenmore electric range model number 790.9611340A.  The left front burner won't turn off, it turn on and off by itself and never stay off.  I have to switched the breaker to shut it off.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he smelled a burning odor and he decided to check the cook top and found that it extremely hot. The consumer stated that he noticed that the knobs were off yet the burners continued to heat up. 

The consumer stated that he turned off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that he burnt his right hand and he treated it with a first aid. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they informed him that they would send out 
a technician to repair the cook top.  The consumer stated that he declined the offer for the repair and will be replacing the cook top. 

The consumer stated that this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard that it poses.
justification: The consumer suffered a burn injury requiring first aid, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as the issue appears to be an isolated incident with the specific cook top.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she noticed that the bottom rim that holds the inside glass of the oven was corroding.  The consumer stated that approximately 10 years ago she noticed a small amount of corrosion on the metal rim surrounding the glass and she ignored it. The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they would not assist. 

The consumer stated that this year she was cleaning the oven and she cut her index finger of her left hand with the metal that had been corroding. The consumer stated that she did not have to receive any medical assistance. 

The consumer stated that she had to clean it herself due to the fact that she was afraid to use the self cleaning feature because due to the high temperature the glass could explode.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that due to the age of the oven they could not provide any assistance. 

The consumer stated that this product should be investigated due to the hazard that it poses. She stated that she believes the metal on the stove should not be corroding.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor injury (cut finger) from corroded metal, but did not require medical assistance.

incident_description: The Overload relay on my Maytag Refrigerator caught on fire. Fortunately got it unplugged before any damage other than I dont have a refrigerator.
justification: The overload relay caught fire, but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
Maytag Gemini MGR6775BDS range 


The range  igniters starting ticking by them selfÃÂs, a small explosion happened, and the range burst into flames. Flames were in the top oven and shooting out the vent holes and the holes where the knobs are located. Coal black smoke was also pouring out of the vents. After the flames subsided the kitchen and house smelled of burning wire insulation and plastic.
justification: The incident involved a range igniting and causing flames and smoke, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer says that her husband woke up in the morning and found that the oven was on.  She says there was no indication on the digital panel that it was on.  She says that the igniter has not worked correctly on several occasions.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who sent out a technician on 8-21-2012. The technician said that the heating element shorted out as well as the control panel.  They stated that because of the age of the appliance they would not pay for the repair.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with no injury reported, and similar issues have occurred multiple times.

incident_description: The microhood which is almost 5 years old began making a horrible noise like a coffee grinder.  It began to smoke and had I not acted quickly would have completely caught on fire.  It was on for no more than 3 seconds before this noise/smoke started.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microhood that began smoking and could have caught fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product: Samsung  FX510BGS gas range

Grate spacing near center of burners is too wide to support pots and pans with a base diameter of about 6 inches or less. Had several incidents when a hot pan nearly tipped over. Problem occurs with small sauce pans and saute pans, both inexpensive un-branded as well as expensive [REDACTED] cookware.

This new range was installed 9/4/2012.
justification: The incident involves hot pans nearly tipping over due to grate spacing, posing a risk but no reported injuries.

incident_description: A few years ago, I was given a Calphalon sautÃÂ© pan as a gift.  Over the past couple of years, however, it has become more difficult and less safe to use.  The pan has a metal handle that is bolted to the pan, itself.  This metal handle has a thick, rubber sleeve/sheath that slides over the it, allowing it to be used without a pot holder.  Unfortunately, as one sautÃÂ©s - shaking the food back and forth and flipping the contents using wrist action, the rubber sheath can and does slide off.  Sometimes it's gradual, so it can be noticed and simply slid back on the tang.  On other occasions, however, the pan just slides off of the sheath and goes flying across the stovetop, countertop, or through the open air.
justification: The incident involves the pan handle sheath sliding off, potentially causing the pan to fly, but no injury is mentioned, only safety concerns.

incident_description:
Consumer has a range that is off by one digit from the recall.  He is experiencing the same hazard as listed in the recall.  He says the pan actually melted and the burner got so hot that it melted the pan.  This was five minutes after using it. 

The consumer says that the top cracked when he tried to get the pan off.  he says that the pan was contracting more than the top was and he thinks thats what caused it to crack by his estimation.  He talked to an appliance store and they told him that he would have to purchase a new stove.  He was using the right front burner. The metal contracted faster than the glass.
CONSUMER ADDED:  I finally reached customer service, told me had to go through Sears; Sears said that I would have to talk to Westinghouse.  No Results.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous situation with a melting pan and cracked stove top, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Oven racks fall when using presenting a very serious risk of burns.  This has happenend on numerous occasion since my purchase.  After researching this problem,I found out that the oven walls bow from the self-cleaning cycle.  Sears pretends to know nothing about this problem and just wants you to pay to have a service tech come out and charge you to replace the walls ..
justification: Oven racks falling presents a serious risk of burns, and the issue has occurred multiple times, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Electric Built-in Oven.

Oven glass door exploded on when I closed the oven door. Oven was cool. Glass exploded so violently that it went into 3 room, into cabinets and drawers. Glass also cut my feet and got into my slippers
justification: The incident caused injury to the user, making the severity level 3.

incident_description:
Our freezer caught on fire.  I opened the freezer on the top of my fridge to find the inside completely covered in soot.  A fire had occurred inside the freezer.
I unplugged it immediately.
We called Sears repair services to assess the damage and see if it was repairable--just in case the fire were from something (paper/label/etc.) getting caught in a motor or something.
The repairman was shocked.  Never saw anything like it before.  What he wrote on the report was:  Melted bi-metal caught on fire.  Melted inside of freezer.
The thermostat apparently burned.  The entire inside of the freezer is melted/burned.
I am SO thankful that the fire stayed inside the freezer!  Had it come out the back or front we could have lost our house or lives.  We were lucky!
The fridge/freezer is in an open space and was being used properly.
justification: The fire was contained within the freezer with no injuries or deaths, and the repairman's shock suggests such incidents are rare.

incident_description:
My 9x13 glass pyrex baking dish
exploded in my oven last night. I have done much google research and
see similar reports... however I DID NOT subject my dish to any of the
circumstances that normally cause this sort of breakage. i know
pyrex often disputes that the glassware will "explode" but I have
photos of how my oven looked immediately upon opening it... and there
is no way the glass could have ended up sideways and lying on the
baking sheet next to it (where I was roasting vegetables) had it not
literally EXPLODED. The circumstances of my baking: I placed a piece
of salmon into my room temperature baking dish and put it into an oven
that had been pre-heated to 400 degrees. The glass was not cold (only
the fish, which is normal as you can't let fish come up to room
temperature and spoil and it had been marinating in the refrigerator
for one hour). I did not place the dish on the stove top. I placed it
directly into the pre-heated oven. At about 15 minutes of baking, I
heard the loud bang in my kitchen, turned on the oven light, and
discovered the mess. Had this happened 5 minutes later when I opened
the oven door, significant injury could have occurred to me. As it
was, it took a long time for the oven and all the items to cool enough
for me to attempt to clean the very sharp and dangerous mess. Some of
the glass was actually a fine powder left in the oven and I had to use
a vaccum attachment to try and get it all cleaned out. Lastly, this
was not an old baking dish, it was purchased within the last 4 years.
I have followed this exact procedure to cook salmon many times without
incident. I did not see any sort of cracks or damage to the baking
dish prior to baking. I don't even put them in the dish washer, I wash
them by hand. I would like an explanation for this incident as your
bakeware is clearly not safe and I will be throwing out all my other
clear glass pyrex items due to safety concerns.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but the glassware exploded, posing a risk of injury.

incident_description: Dishwasher was smoking with a very distinct electrical burning odor. Visible smoke coming from the control panel area in the top of the door.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking with a distinct electrical burning odor, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: About five minutes into the wash cycle, our Kenmore dishwasher began making popping/fizzing noises. I observed whitish-grey smoke and a flicker of flame emerging from the dishwasher vent and the top of the door, behind the control panel. There was a terrible chemical smell, like burned plastic. I immediately grabbed our kitchen fire extinguisher and blasted the dishwasher -- this stopped the burning. Pressing the Cancel button failed to turn off the machine, so I switched off the breaker toggle at the control box.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but was extinguished with no injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he touched the metal strip panel between the refrigerator and the freezer and it was extremely hot. The consumer stated that he immediately unplugged the refrigerator, in fear that it would catch on fire. The consumer stated that he took out the food out and he purchased a new refrigerator. The consumer believes that replacing the fan motor was not the only solution, fridge should have shut down for safety.
The consumer stated that no one was injured. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they send a technician to service the refrigerator. The consumer stated that the technician informed him that the problem was that the fan that cooled the compressor stopped working. The consumer stated that they were trying to charge him over $400 to replace the fan. The consumer stated that he declined because he did not feel safe having the refrigerator at home. 
The consumer stated that he discarded the refrigerator, because Sears failed to diagnose the real problem.
justification: The incident involved a safety concern with the refrigerator overheating, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Frigidaire Professional Series Range. Model No. FEFLZ87GCB, Serial No. VF82238149. (I found the receipt~Bought at hhgregg on 8/2/08).  Last November, my Husband was on shift (fire fighter) and I was making TV dinners for my kids. I put the plastic trays on a cookie sheet as instructed by the box and put them in the pre-heated 350 degree oven (which actually smelled funny when it was pre-heating). I had it in only for about 5 minutes when the range made a beeping noise. I went in and there was an error code in the display. There was no way for me to turn anything off or stop the "alarm". I immediately looked up the code and it stated it was a "Run Away Temperature" code. I ran and flipped the breaker to turn the oven off. When I took the food out, the trays were completely melted onto my cookie sheets and anything that was on top of the cooktop melted as well~the entire range got THAT hot.

We did not use the range for about 4 months and one day my husband decided to see if there was still a problem. It worked fine for about a week~we thought it was just a fluke, but then completely stopped working. We have been without a range ever since. The cooktop is still working. I have gone on-line to see what the problem could be and everyplace I have looked said that the Frigidaire ranges were recalled for this reason except ours. Along with many other people who have not had this problem resolved.

I called yesterday to find out if by the slimmest chance ours was recalled because we can't afford a new range or spend the $500 (is what everyone on-line as said it would cost) to get this repaired. The gentleman who answered to phone said yes, there was a recall...YES!! No, after he transferred me to the Recall Department they informed me that it was not the oven but the cooktop. UGH!!! Oh, and Frigidaire is being so nice and sending me the cooktop replacement part that I don't need at the moment.  The appliance repair company (who Frigidaire referred me to) said that they just had someone else last week with this same problem. Come on Frigidaire...Obviously, the Runaway Temperature is a problem with our model Range as well as the others that it was recalled for. I have 4 young children and really miss cooking in my oven~especially with the holidays coming up!! Thanks.
justification: The incident involved a runaway temperature error causing melted trays and damage, but no injuries were reported. The problem recurred after initial use, indicating a possible but not certain likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: We loaded and started our GE dishwasher before going to bed last night and woke up this morning to find something had heated the inside of the unit to the point that all the plastic fixtures in the interior had melted and flowed to the bottom of the chamber forming a mound of cooled plastic, silverware, dishes and cutlery.  We found out that GE had issued a recall on dishwashers manufactured in 2006 (we bought ours in 2007), but our model number was not on their recall list.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the dishwasher but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Regarding my GE Profile dishwasher. Stainless steel tub.
We opened the dishwasher. Heating element on. UNABLE to turn dishwasher off. Had to go to breaker box.
Melted plastic dishware. Plastic melted on the bottom of dishwasher in a fluid state. It was so hot that even the dishwasher arm was melted in half! Cracked drinking glass
Burned hand when I tried to remove glass disware. 
We were lucky to be at home because dishwasher element never turned off. 
We talked to GE representative who informed us that only the dishwasher that did NOT have stainless steel was in their recall.  In other words, our dishwasher did not qualify under their dishwasher recall because it was not plastic on the inside.  
We told them that this dishwasher was a fire hazard and we were lucky to be home so that we could turn it off at the breaker box. Otherwise it would have caught on fire it was so hot.

GE Profile dishwasher Model# 9280N0055
Serial VM815879B
justification: The dishwasher was extremely hot, causing injury to the hand and melting plastic, which could have led to a fire if not turned off.

incident_description: A Pyrex brand bowl suddenly shattered.  I removed a room temperature Pyrex small bowl (cereal size of bowl) from the kitchen cabinet.  Ate a bowl of cereal with milk (from refrigerator set to 34 degrees).  I finished the cereal and placed the bowl on a wooden coffee table in my living room (no impact involved).  The stainless steel spoon remained in the bowl.  There was no left over milk or cereal.  About 3 minutes later, the bowl shattered with a relative large "pop" into large and small framents scattered as far away as 3 feet.  There was no activity or action of any sort whatsoever after placing the bowl on the coffee table.
justification: The bowl shattered unexpectedly but no injury occurred, making it an incident without harm.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore stove, model number 79096122409 and serial number VF73048991.  When my husband turned the stove eye on yesterday to cook bacon,  the heat accelerated beyond the stove setting and he found he could not turn the eye down or off.  He eventually had to throw the breaker to be able to turn the stove off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could not be turned off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I had just made a fresh pot of coffee.  When I picked up the hot pot of coffee, the handle tab broke off. The top tab that attaches to the top of the pot broke off just as I had removed it from the maker, landing on the counter top, spilling coffee on the counter top.
justification: The incident involved a broken coffee pot handle and spilled coffee, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Amana big Oven door melted in clean mode. After I turned it to clean the oven locked and the surrounding outer top and door became extremely hot though unaware of the magnitude of damage until 3 hours of cleaning the door unlocked and an error message blinked where I turned the oven off.  Even with the unusual smell and fumes that filled the kitchen there were no signs of what was happening until I opened the door. If I were not at home to keep an eye on it, it would have caught fire.
justification: The oven door melted and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The oven of my Sears Kenmore Electric Range model # 700-95660 generated an excessive amount of heat and would not turn off. It was set to 350 to bake some brownies. I unplugged it , let it cool and tried plugging it in again. I did not turn the oven on but it immediately began to heat up. 

This oven was bought in September 2001 for $650 and is not included on the recall list you issued for Kenmore ranges with the same problem.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, only an incident requiring unplugging.

incident_description: My  Kenmore top glass range oven door shattered. At the time of incident the range was not in use. My husband and i were very dumbfounded as to why this occurred. Since than i have not used the range i have unplugged it. My concern is to find out if this range is defective or is there a recall. I'm afraid to purchase another one wondering if the same thing would happen again. Your consideration in this matter would be greatly appreciated.
justification: The oven door shattered but no one was injured, and the range was not in use at the time, indicating a low likelihood of recurrence without further evidence.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Elite Electric Cook Top SR 900323377 Model 790.4281/9700. The right front burner will not shut off when you turn it off. You have to flip the breaker to get it to turn off, and then it might just come back on. Big fire hazard along with the potential to burn yourself. 

Other units like this from Kenmore have been recalled due this very same issue and this one should be added to the recall list.  
This has happened for the last 6 months. I was in a bad accident which is why we have not dealt with this before. 

Thanks for your help.
justification: The burner not shutting off poses a significant fire hazard and potential for burns, indicating a high likelihood of injury.

incident_description:
(08/2012) The consumer stated that she came into kitchen and discovered that the notifier indicated that the burner was hot. The consumer stated that it was the front right burner. It came on by itself. The consumer stated that this happened before on the same burner. 

The stove had not been in use neither time.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that a technician would be dispatched at a cost to her. The consumer accepted.
justification: The burner turned on by itself without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he has an electric range that the burners were coming on its own. The consumer stated that after he turns off the burners by turning the knobs to off, 30 seconds later it comes back on. The consumer stated that it becomes extreme hot to a temperature thatÃÂs unknown. 
The consumer stated that it was posing the same hazard stated on release # 09-333. 
The consumer stated he was afraid that it could turn on when they werenÃÂt home and cause a fire. 
The consumer stated that was injured. 
The consumer stated that he turn off the circuit breaker and disconnected the range. 

The consumer stated that he decided to purchase a new a range and was getting rid of the old one. 

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that his range was not included on the recall. The consumer stated that they did not provide any assistance although he informed them that his range was posing the same hazard.
justification: The consumer reported an injury and the potential for a fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the repeated malfunction and the consumer's fear of it happening when unattended.

incident_description: Was using rival 2 qt slow cooker on low temp when the lid exploded.  Glass shattered and went everywhere into the product and out -- lost the product I was cooking.  I sent e-mail to Rival and they told me to contact 866-321-9509 which turned out to be Walmart -- they told me they could send me a replacement lid, but i told them i threw the whole thing in the trash -- i wasn't going to use it again -- it couldn't have been the lid that was defective -- it has to be the unit -- so what good would a new lid do me?  it could just explode again -- not taking that chance -- so they then told me i could contact you and report it.  No one seems to care do they?
justification: The incident involved an exploding lid causing product loss but no reported injuries, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description: dishwasher was running and we began to smell an electrical/plastic burning odor.  after checking around we found the top left of the dishwasher had melted plastic.  after unscrewing top panel we found electrical wires melting
justification: Electrical melting poses a fire hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My slide-in Frigidaire stove model fan won't turn off for 48 hours. Then the oven started to turn on automatically, on it's own and heat up. We had to unplug the unit and disconnect the gas line to prevent the oven from automatically coming on when we were not home or possibly catch fire.
justification: The stove malfunctioned, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The very first time we used our ice cream maker, model 8550-X, it never stopped like it was supposed to.  When we opened it up, there were metal shavings on top of the ice cream.  The dasher shaft and the motor socket that drives it were both rounded off at the corners, so that the motor was spinning free and the dasher wasn't turning in the canister.  We used it the first and only time 6-12-2012, but we received it as a gift in 2002.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure and contamination with metal shavings, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller and wife purchased a 5 cup coffeemaker approximately 7 months ago and have not had any problems at all with it until Sunday, September 9th, 2012 when the wife had just finished making coffee.
She was going to empty the grounds as usual when steam came out of the top portion where the coffee grounds are kept and burned her right hand on the knuckles of the three fingers between her thumb and little finger.

She did not believe in the beginning that she needed medical attention and so treated it herself.
This morning; Monday, September 10th, 2012 she woke and saw that her knuckles and areas leading to her hand are blistering.
She will make an appointment to have a doctor examine the burn and advise of care necessary today.

They contacted the manufacturer this morning but they do not remember names of contacts who told them they would send report collected to their lab.

Callers are disappointed with the manner their report to the manufacturer was treated since they were not seeking restitution but were reporting for their safety as well as many, many others safety.

This product is being reported due to callers belief that it could seriously injure someone using the coffeepot or could injure anyone standing very close to them.
They would like this coffeemaker recalled and replaced at manufacturer expense
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury requiring medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the unexpected nature of the steam release.

incident_description:
On Thursday, September 20, 2012 I was at my mother's home making cookies.  A few minutes after I turned the oven on there was a white flash in the oven. I was standing in the kitchen with my eleven year old son. I reached over an immediately flipped off the oven. My son saw a huge flame inside the oven. My son didn't tell me about the huge flame until after the whole experience  was over. After I flipped off the oven I looked inside to see what had happen. The coil in the oven was still on fire. The flame had died down when I turned off the oven. 
I usually walk away from the oven while I'm waiting for the oven to warm up. I was so thankful that on this day that I was in the kitchen & able to flip the oven off right away. If I hadn't of flipped off the oven when I did the whole kitchen would of been in flames in minutes. My concern is the builder used Maytag ovens in all the homes in this community. My mother's home was built in 2006 but remained empty for several years until she purchased the home in March 2009 as a foreclosure. The oven handle had also broke off before this incident had happen. We were getting ready to have the handle repaired before the coil had caught on fire. I have never known an oven handle to break on an oven before. We are very concerned about this oven.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, but potential for significant damage if not addressed immediately.

incident_description:
The consumer says that he started noticing the unit was getting hot to the touch.  When opening the freezer door and refrigerator door he notices a vertical 3 inch divider separating the freezer and refrigerator.  When his arm brushes up against the divider it was scorching hot.

He contacted the manufacturer and asked them if it was something normal.  He was told that its where the defroster tubes run and not to worry about.  He said that is the way it is supposed to be. 

The consumer says as time has gone by the divider is getting hotter and hotter to the point that the vertical gasket that seals the freezer door has turned brown.  he says the vertical plastic vinyl piece that covers the separator wall between the freezer and fridge also has brown spots in it.  he says it has also developed cracks in the horizontal vinyl.  He says that he called the manufacturer again this past week, they said they need to send someone out.

When he called a couple of months ago they did not offer to send someone out, they simply said do not worry about it.  He asked the manufacturer to look in the records to see when it was that he called a couple of  months ago.  they have no record of his phone call.

A repairman came to the house and verified that the cooling fan was not working.  The technician ordered a computer board.  The repair expense is $450. 

He contacted the manufacturer on or around 8-20-2012, who referred him to a supervisor by the name of [REDACTED] in Tennessee.  He said the gasket now is so hot that if he touched it, it would burn his hand.  He was informed by the manufacturer that the center vinyl piece is not serviced.  He says that he talked to the company at length and he felt like they blew him off. 

He has a neighbor up the street with an identical refrigerator.  He has a copy of the repair order from 2010 for his neighbors unit.  It says "hot edge on the wall, necessary to replace main computer service board."  He says the model for hers is [REDACTED] and serial [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a scorching hot divider that could burn the consumer's hand, indicating potential for injury, and the issue has been verified by a repairman.

incident_description:
On 9/17/2012 I woke up at approximate 2 a.m. to drink water. To my surprise I smelt  something that i associated with burning materials.  I went downstairs and as I descended the stairwell i WAS ABLE TO VISUALIZE  an unusual array of light coming in from through the front door streaming through a cloud of smoke. The scent of burning material increased . I entered the kitchen and saw that the control panel was still illuminated as during an operational cycle. Upon depressing the control panel i attempted to depress the OFF button and to my surprise the whole door was extremely hot . The dishwasher would not turn off , thus to my fast response I proceeded to the basement and directed myself to the breaker box and turned off the dishwasher breaker.

Later upon opening the dishwasher I was able to identify that this was the source of the smoke and it was catching fire in lieu to visibly damage to the items placed to was and components of the dishwasher had melted an were burnt.

Attached are several photographs for your review and consideration.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, causing visible damage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
August 13th, 2012 the caller's wife had been out of the house, came home and smelled something burning when she entered her home.
She saw that there was a small amount of smoke coming from their microwave that had been purchased December 2010.

Signal window was flashing message, "Keypad shorting out" over and over.
She immediately pulled the plug out of the outlet.

Microwave had not been used by either the caller or his wife for about two days.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

He is asking that this model be recalled and replaced or repaired at manufacturer expense.
justification: There was a small amount of smoke from the microwave but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I received a Cuisinart TOB-30BW approximately 6 years ago as a gift (it was purchased from Bed, Bath, and Beyond).  It seemed to work ok for a few months, until one day after using it, I turned the dial to the "off" position, but left the oven plugged in.  When I returned to the oven approximately 3 hours later, it was still hot, and the dial was still in the "off" position.  I exchanged this toaster oven for the same model, also at Bed, Bath, and Beyond.  After about 2 1/2 years, the "new" oven began having problems, as well.  Whenever you turn the "Function" dial from the "off" position to "bake" or from "bake" to any of the other positions, you hear a buzzing noise and smoke comes out from the dial.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning toaster oven that emits smoke and buzzes, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: Cuisinart DCC-1200 approximately 18 mos old made popping and crackling sounds that alerted me to an overheating element after coffee maker auto shutoff. After unplugging, coffee maker started smoking at base and was extremely hot. I was able to avert a full fire situation by being present and alerted to the issue so that I could take extreme actions of un plugging and removing from my house.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoking, which could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she set the oven for light toast. She placed one slice of bread in the oven. About two minutes later she discovered flames inside of the oven and also flames were coming out of the vent. She unplugged the oven and held the door closed so that the lack of oxygen supply would allow the fire to go out. After about a minute the flames went out.

The inside of the oven was blackened and the kitchen was filled with smoke.  There was no other damage. 

The consumer stated that she called the manufacturer on 9/4/2012.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Black&Decker model TO1675W convection counter top oven
The outside top of the oven reached 380 degrees F by digital thermometer while just cooking toast. The Applica company that seems to make or distribute it has many warnings in the manual, but the top surface temperature is inherently hazardous to the elderly who may have alzheimer's, etc. I returned the oven to Walmart and got my money back.

Fortunately, my wife didn't get burned. All of these ovens should be recalled to avoid burns. The problem seems to be a perforated guard over the heater rods that reflects most of the infrared onto the steel case and dangerously overheats it.

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The oven's high surface temperature poses a burn hazard, especially to vulnerable individuals, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description:
I bought item #275313, the 6 QT Hard Anodized Aluminum Deep Saute pan on Friday 09/07/12 at Costco's  Colchester VT warehouse.  I then made a big batch of soup in it.  I did not use the lid until I had taken the pot off the stove and let it cool for about 1/2 hour.  It then sat there cooling for another hour or two; I then washed the pan and lid and put them in my dish drainer on my kitchen counter.  About an hour later the lid literally exploded and glass went everywhere in my kitchen.  Even my husband, who was downstairs in the basement with the door closed, heard it.  
Fortunately, although I was in the kitchen at the time, I was on the other side of the room with my back turned. 

This is Costco's response:

I am so sorry that this happened.  I have not heard of any other incidents regarding the saute pan.  We appreciate your feedback and have forwarded your email to the buyers for further review and consideration.
justification: The incident involved an exploding lid causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported despite the person being in the kitchen.

incident_description: Large pyrex baking dish exploded when I went to take it out of the cupboard

incident_description:
Re: GE Dishwasher Recall dtd 9 Aug 2012

Ladies and Gentlemen:

The enclosed hard copied email to GE Consumer Relations will outline adequately the basis
for this letter. We had purchased two identical (save for Serial Numbers) Dishwashers in 2004,
one of which, identified in Exhibit A, failed in early August as described and depicted in photo
IMG 5195 jpg (Exhibit B). This is the type of failure that led to the GE DW Recall dated 9
August 12. The other DW, thus far without failure, is identified in IMG 1082 jpg (Exhibit C).

I include you in this dialog because, while the Serial Numbers of our DWs fall outside the range
included in the Recall and are not eligible for recompense or replacement, the failure was
nonetheless serious and potentially dangerous, the more so as the DW in question has the
vulnerable plastic floor pan. We are awaiting GE's response to our letter.

Perhaps your mission could include a conversation with GE, suggesting that the range of
eligible DW Serial Numbers be expanded to include all such failures or incipient failures.
Prevention is as worthy a goal as is recompense.

____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Good day,

I choose this email format rather than yours to facilitate attaching two pics
relevant to the problem. Lacking your email address despite efforts, I hard copy this
and the attempted attachments as photographs. Please forgive me.

This week, coincidentally with your recall notice of 9 August, our GE dishwasher
(GSD6200GOOBB) bearing Ser. No. GF750482B (pic IMG 4644 jpg) experienced heater element
failure (pic IMG 5195 jpg) of a sort described in your recall. Exploring this failure,
we find that our DW, purchased in 2004, is not covered by your recall, despite the
identical nature of the listed failure.

We were, fortunately, able to have the DW repaired by competent persons, and have
saved the defective, burned out heater element for inspection. Ocracoke Island, on the
Outer Banks, presents a challenge in obtaining certain services.

My request is that this issue be considered for appropriate reimbursement for
parts and labor just as if the DW Ser. No. were within the range listed in your recall
notice referenced above. Perhaps that range should be extended.

Thank you for your attention.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher failure similar to those in a recall, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
23 August 2012

Dear Mr. [REDACTED]:

I own an LG Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, Model # LFX25960TT, Serial # 701KRJU00628, which was
manufactured in January 2007.
On August 21, 2012, we experienced an electrical fault with the refrigerator internal lighting controls.
The lights failed to shut off when the door was closed. This failure resulted in sufficient heat to char the internal lamp holder and cause plastic securing the light fixture to the refrigerator internal casing to melt. This resulted in acrid and poisonous fumes which permeated the entire refrigerator and its contents.
After securing power to the refrigerator, we contacted LG who advised us that they would correct the electrical fault and replace the light fixture. This initially appeared to be a reasonable solution to our specific situation. However, during discussions with the repair facility we learned that this is a problem with this specific refrigerator model and that the fault has reoccured after the repair. The repair facility also informed us that this model refrigerator had been subject to a RECALL. Consequently, we re-contacted LG on August 22 and asked them if this model refrigerator had been subject to a RECALL and told them we had never received a RECALL notice. LG informed us that the refrigerator had not been subjected to a RECALL but that the specific electrical fault was an ISSUE.
In light of the fact that the electrical fault associated with the internal lighting controls can continue to occur on this model refrigerator, even after repair, and the heat generated by this failure is sufficient to char the lamp holder, melt the plastic securing the light holder to the refrigerator internal casing, and result in acrid and poisonous fumes permeating the refrigerator and spreading to the kitchen upon opening the refrigerator door, it is hard to understand why LG has not issued a voluntary RECALL and the CPSC has not caused LG to issue a RECALL for this model refrigerator.

Sincerely
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved an electrical fault causing heat and fumes, but no injury or death was reported. The issue is likely to recur based on the description of repeated faults and prior incidents.
