The consumer contacted the manufacturer when this incident occurred who offered to sell her a bottom rack for $145.  She says that her local repairman/friend told her that the unit overheated because it did not have a safety feature.

She has not had any issues with it since then but the rack is severely damaged.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plastic) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) based on the frequency data provided.

incident_description:
05/31/2012 The consumer stated that she placed a plate of food on the turntable. The consumer stated that she turn it on for one minute. The consumer also stated that she heard a pop and saw sparkles. The microwave was unplugged and the consumer opened the door. The right side and the back of the microwave was black. 

The consumer stated that she turned the microwave it on a couple of days later. The microwave worked but she decided not to use it.

The consumer stated that she will call the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved sparks and damage to the microwave but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: 8/13/2012) The consumer stated that she set her toaster oven to the bake setting, the switch  sparked and then she saw smoke. She immediately unplugged the unit and the smoke stopped. The consumer stated that this issue has been going on for approximately 2 weeks.  (8/19/2012) The consumer sent an email in regards to her incident.  (8/20/2012) The manufacturer replied requesting the consumer to provide proof of receipt and any other issues. Providing the information she would be able to purchase a new toaster for $80. The consumer declined the offer.  I have the receipt and I would have accepted, if they did not want $80.   (8/24/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and a Rep. (name unknown) advised her that the unit was out of warranty and there was nothing that they could do.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no injury, and the issue has been recurring for weeks, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Pan was being used to cook vegetables on electric stove at medium heat.  Once done, the stove was turned off and the glass lid placed on top of the pan.  Within minutes the glass shattered in the center of the lid around the handle showering glass everywhere.  The lid around the periphery was cracked but remained intact.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of a glass lid but no injuries were reported, making it a minor incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she placed the dishwasher on the wash cycle.  Approximately 10-15 mins later she smelled an odor of electrical fire.  She discovered that the dishwasher had stopped in mid cycle and there was water in the unit.  She noticed that the control panel was scorched.  The circuit breaker was used to disconnect power from the dishwasher.

There had been no previous incidents and 1 service call for noise heard in cycle 1 year after purchase.

8/20/12  The consumer contacted the manufacturer but was being transferred to different departments until the call was disconnected.

The consumer feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a scorched control panel and an electrical fire odor, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he turned on the microwave on the popcorn setting for approximately 3 minutes. The consumer stated that the 3 minutes ended and he opened the door to remove the popcorn. He stated that when he closed the door to the microwave it turned on without him setting a time or pressing start. 

The consumer stated that at the moment he stated that even if you turn a time on the microwave after the timer stops, the light inside turns off, but the heating element continues working. 

The consumer stated that he decided to unplug the microwave. He stated that at the moment he would plug the microwave on only when he needs to use it. 

The consumer stated that he has not been injured.

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they did not provided any assistance. The consumer stated that he contacted them several times and they always transferred him around through different departments. 

The consumer stated that he believes this product should be investigated since it poses a fire hazard to the consumer.
justification: The consumer reported an incident with no injury, but the microwave malfunction poses a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: The overhead handle on coffee serving tray cracked off under the weight of the filled coffee cups and filled creamer and sugar pot.  This resulted in the tray falling to the ground in front of me.  I received second degree burns on the tops of our feet and ankles from the coffee.  The tray had almost never been used before and was never dropped or abused and showed no signs of damage to warn us before it happened.  One or two seconds prior to when the handle completely cracked off I heard an audible ping. The handle appeared to be very poorly designed and seemed much to week and brittle to support the weight of the filled tray.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The tray was rarely used and showed no prior damage, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description: House fire lost home and all contents 10-02-2011,  Whirlpool dishwasher was on at time. We had just loaded it after dinner and went to town. Fire Marshall said fire started in wall where dishwasher was located.
justification: The incident involved a house fire causing property loss, but no mention of injuries or fatalities.

incident_description:
We have a Frigidaire Glass top range Model FEC30S6ASF
Serial # NF70425570. 
The large element will not switch off when used for long periods.
I had to tell my wife to power down the whole house to let it cool down. 
This appliance is a fire hazard, please advise on remedy.
justification: The range element not switching off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: The glass door on our Kenmore gas range exploded, fragments cut my wife's legs (I thought safety glass wasn't supposed to cut; I guess oven doors aren't supposed to explode either). Kenmore Model Number 79012991.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (cuts to the legs) due to glass fragments from the exploding oven door.

incident_description: The broiler element came on by itself while the oven was is use and cannot be turned off thru the control panel. Only by turning the breaker off does the element go off. This cylcle repeats itself after letting the oven cool and turning the power back on. The control panel is and remains off and the broiler element cannot be turned off thru the control panel.
justification: The broiler element malfunction poses a risk of overheating or fire, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore Elite refrigerator, model 795.77553600, manufactured in February 2007 by LG.  

IT IS A FIRE HAZARD!

The PCB has gone bad and the refrigerator light stays on even when the door is closed.  When I discovered this, the light housing was melted and partially detached from melting, the two light sockets were partially blackened, and the items on the top shelf were extremely hot.

I searched the web and found there have been dozens of complaints about this on various appliance repair websites.

I repeat, my Kenmore Elite refrigerator is a fire hazard, and it's only a matter of time until one causes a house fire.
justification: The description indicates a significant fire hazard with potential for death, supported by evidence of melting and blackening, and reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: My Kenmore dishwasher started on fire today while running.  Smoke started coming out of the door.  I pressed the cancel button but it wouldn't shut off so my husband turned off the breaker.  I tried to call [REDACTED] and any other number I could find to see if there was a recall but I just kept getting passed around.  I'll go to Sears tomorrow to see if there is a recall or any reimbursement but I doubt I'll have much luck.  Just very happy that I was home when it happened.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The glass front on my oven exploded. The oven was not on. My family was standing in the kitchen and the glass shattered and went all over the kitchen floor.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing a mess but no injuries, as the family was present but unharmed.

incident_description:
(7/22/2012) The consumer stated that he was using the front left burner of the range at the medium setting of about 7 or 8. The burner was on for approximately 10 minutes when he noticed a bright red flare coming from the burner. When the consumer went to turn the burner off, he noticed that it had moved from the original setting of 7 or 8 to the highest level. The consumer then proceeded to turn the burner off, but the dials would not allow him to. The consumer tripped the circuit breakers, so that the range would be completely off.

 (7/31/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and they advised him that his range was not included in release# 09-333. He was informed that they could send someone out but at his own expense.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner with no reported injury, and such occurrences are possible but not frequent.

incident_description: 23 month old Flat Top range had the top crack while the range was cooling down. Fortunately, since we were done cooking, there were no cooking utensils on the top. The way that the crack "spidered" out across the top, anything on the range top may have fallen into the burners.
justification: The range top cracked but no injuries occurred, and the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely as it happened during cooling and no utensils were present.

incident_description:
While preparing dinner, I used our Electrolux over-the-range microwave oven to cook a bag of [REDACTED] steamfresh vegetables.  Immediately after hitting the start button, I heard unusual popping sounds from the lower right hand side of the microwave, and smelled what I would describe as an electrical motor overheating or malfunctioning.  I stopped the microwave, removed the bag of food, and started the microwave again to see if it was a problem with the bag.  The microwave again made popping noises and emitted the smell, and I also noticed grey smoke coming from between the door and control panel.  I stopped the microwave after a few seconds and unplugged it to avoid any greater incident.

The next day I contacted the Electrolux consumer line to report the incident.  Their first reaction was to say to call 911 if I had a fire, I explained I had not seen a fire and the incident had happened the previous night.  They said they could give me numbers of a local service provider, but in general the tone (and statements of) the consumer service line was "we're not sure what you want us to do about it".  I was appalled that they were not more concerned over an incident with one of their products that could have resulted in greater loss or harm.

The microwave was purchased new from a retail store 2 years and 3 months prior to the incident.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave with smoke and unusual sounds, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I have a twelve year old Kitchenaid model KEBS208DBL8 convection oven that shattered when in self clean mode. I started the self clean cycle according to the directions and one hour into the cycle that should last about 3 hours, the inner glass door shattered. there wasn't any other previous damage to the oven and the self clean cycle was run as per the instructions.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering during use, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Approximately 9pm noticed dishwasher was extremely hot.  It had not been manually started but appeared to be in a cycle having started by itself.  It was not responsive to turning off and took me some time to do so.  Water and wash cycles had not run in machine. Dishes were still dirty and were not wet.  Machine indicator lights did not indicate it was in a heated drying cycle.  Kitchen counter was extremely hot.  
We have owned machine since home purchase in March 2002 (purchased new). Machine has not ever turned on by itself, nor have we inadvertently turned on as buttons require specific pressure to initiate cycles.  
Machine had last run the day before without incident.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned by turning on by itself and overheating, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Kitchenaide Countertop Coffee Maker (Model # KCM111OB) in May of this year. About two months later, I began having issues with it. It shorted out just after it finished brewing. I unplugged it and let it dry throughly and began using it again. It seemed okay until about a month later when I tried to run it through it's first cleaning cycle. After the cleaning cycle, it would no longer brew. The water would not filter through the maker and when I touched it, it was incredibly hot. I did not actually burn myself; but it was much hotter than any coffee maker I've ever used has gotten. At that point, I contacted Kitchenaide via e-mail. I described the issues and asked them what we could do. we went back and forth a bit because I actually wanted my money back so I could buy a different coffee maker. However, all they would do was send me a new one of the same thing because that's all their warranty allowed for. I was not pleased; but I accepted the replacement. I have had the replacement one for three weeks now. At the end of the first week, it began doing the same things as the original one - it shorted out once and sometimes does not filter the water through when it should be brewing. I think this coffee maker is dangerous and could easily result in a house fire or burn injury.
justification: The coffee maker shorted out and became excessively hot, posing a burn risk, but no injury occurred. The issue has recurred with a replacement unit, indicating a likely ongoing problem.

incident_description:
Incident:  I had just boiled water on the stove beneath the microwave.  Some water had condensed on the underside of the microwave but nothing unusual.  I placed a bowl of noodles in the microwave, entered the time to cook, and pressed the start button.  Immediately a 3-4' electric current shot outward from the microwave directly in line with my face, several inches from my ear.  The electric current was visibly sparking and made crackling noises like a firecracker (loud enough that my wife upstairs came running down the stairs).  It seemed the current came out of the microwave keypad.  There was heavy visible smoking coming out of the keypad also.  The current knocked me to the ground.  I stood up and pressed the cancel button on the microwave.  My ear was ringing for about 1 hour after the incident from the loud noise the electric current made.  

The noodles looked fine after the incident but had a slight singed taste to them.

The microwave is about 3-4 years old and has never had any problems before.
justification: The electric current knocked the person to the ground and caused ringing in the ear for an hour, indicating an injury. Such incidents are unlikely but possible with faulty appliances.

incident_description:
(7/17/2012) The consumer was using her dishwasher on the normal setting. It ran for approximately 10 minutes when she started to hear an odd noise coming from it. She turned to see what it was and saw a flash (spark) coming from the unit. Within seconds the unit started to emit smoke. The consumer immediately opened the door to let the smoke out. 

Once the door was open she began to  hear crackling noises (as if something were on fire) that lasted for approximately 10 minutes. The consumer believed that the fire may have started from inside the door towards the top of the unit. The consumer did not know how to unplug the unit so she went downstairs to trip the circuit breakers.

The consumer stated that she has had the dishwasher repaired approximately 5 times prior, but for different reasons. She has spent approximately $500 in repairs.

The manufacturer was not contacted, but will be at a later time.

After searching the Internet the consumer saw that there were numerous complaints on this particular brand and model with the same issue.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and sparks, but no injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is high given the consumer's history of repairs and similar complaints found online.

incident_description:
GE microwave model # JES1655dr1bb

Was making microwave popcorn and the thing made the most horrendous sound and sparks lit up my entire kitchen, the sparks were coming from behind the airvent/and panel inside the microwave.

I thought maybe it was the popcorn and tried a bowl of water and it did it again even worse (dumb I know)

The microwave is clean and well maintained. 

Upon reading other complaints on line i am finding this is a common complaint with GE microwaves. I am scared it will cause a fire or seriously injure someone.

I have had microwaves my whole life and never experienced anything like this, and never  had a microwave that went belly up only a couple/few years after purchase like this piece of junk did.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a loud noise but no injury, and similar complaints suggest it's a likely recurring issue.

incident_description: My wife and got up this morning to find the glass of our GE XL44 oven shattered all over our kitchen floor. We spent the next 30 minutes cleaning glass from the kitchen. In looking this up online, this apparently is something that happens with these ovens. Last night, we used the oven, cooking some pizzas at 400 degrees, but we didn't jar it, hit it, etc. We have no idea what happened.
justification: The oven glass shattered, causing a mess but no injuries, and online reports suggest this is a known issue with the oven model.

incident_description:
(08/27/2012) The consumer stated that he set the microwave for 1minute to heat a cup of coffee. When the timer went off, the consumer took the coffee out. He went into the living room and he heard the microwave start on its on. He came back into the kitchen and saw sparks on the top of the oven. Smoke was also coming from the top. The consumer unplugged the microwave. The microwave was not damaged. 

The consumer stated that the microwave came on by itself several times about a year ago.  He stated that he did not have another problem until 08/27/2012.

The consumer stated that he will call the manufacturer.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing sparks and smoke, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I HAVE 4 GLASS BAKING DISHES. (2) 8X8X2" & (2) 9X13X3" . LAST NIGHT, I WAS COOKING AS USUAL. THE OVEN WAS AT 400 DEGREES. I WAS USING THE 9X13X3" GLASS BAKING DISH. IN IT WAS SLICED POTATO WITH A COATING OF COOKING OIL. MIND YOU, I HAVE HAD THESE DISHES FOR ABOUT 5 TO 6 YEARS. AFTER COOKING FOR ABOUT 45 MINUTES, I TOOK THE DISH OUT OF THE OVEN AND HAD JUST PLACED IT ON TOP OF THE STOVE AND NO THE STOVE WAS NOT ON. I HAD JUST TURNED MY BACK AND A LOUD BANG SOUNDED. IT SOUNDED LIKE A GUN SHOT. THE GLASS BAKING DISH HAD LITTERALLY EXPLODED. GLASS WAS EVERYWHERE IN THE KITCHEN AND ALL THE WAY INTO THE LIVINGROOM. I HAD GLASS IN MY HAIR AND ALL OVER THE BACK OF MY SHIRT. I WAS NOT HURT, FORTUNETELY. I HATE TO THINK OF WHAT TERRIBLE THINGS COULD OF HAPPENED. I AM AFRAID TO USE THE REST OF MY DISHES AND AM TOSSING THEM IN THE TRASH. IT TOOK US (MY HUSBAND AND I) A VERY LONG TIME TO CLEAN UP AND STILL FINDING PIECES OCCASSIONALLY. BY THE WAY, THE GLASS PIECES WHERE REALLY STRANGE, THEY WHERE ALL LIKE TINY CUBES AND BALLS. I HOPE SOMETHING IS LOOKED INTO ABOUT THIS, BEFORE SOMEONE REALLY GETS HURT OR EVEN BLINDED. THANKS SO MUCH FOR YOUR ATTENTION.  [REDACTED]
justification: The glass baking dish exploded, causing a significant mess but no injuries.

incident_description: Dishwasher control panel started on fire.
justification: The dishwasher control panel catching fire is an incident with potential for injury, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Cuisinart CBC-00 (about 1.5 yrs old) started hissing, popping, and emitting smoke.  Indicator showed power off though we had made coffee about 30 minutes earlier.  Even after being unplugged and taken outside unit smelled strongly of melted/burned plastic.  If we had not been herre this could have resulted in a structural fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance emitting smoke and a strong smell of burned plastic, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
This morning, my Cuisinart DCC-1100 Series coffee pot (of several years) began to smoke. I regularly set it to brew automatically in the morning. As I was sitting at the kitchen table, I noticed that the machine was making an unusual popping/clicking sound. I didn't pay much attention until I heard it again, and the noise didn't sound like the normal clicks of brewing, since the coffee was already made. I noticed the red "on" light was off, which I didn't do, and the pot wasn't set to turn off automatically for another hour. (We just had GFI outlets installed because we just moved into an older home). Then as I went over to inspect the machine, I noticed and smelled plastic burning and saw smoke coming up around the coffee pot. I immediately unplugged it, and took it outside. If I had not been at home or if I had forgotten to turn it off today and waited for the auto shut-off, I could have had a kitchen fire after I went to work. Nobody would have been home!

I researched online and found a thread of similar complaints:
http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html

Thanks for your time,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a smoking coffee pot with potential for a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We were using our LG Electric Stove on the broil setting, with the door slightly open.  After about 5 minutes of broiling, we heard this loud noise coming from the oven, sounding like an arc welder, and noticed a large bright flame inside the oven in addition to smoke.  I was able to turn off the stove from the front panel, and the noise stopped.  I then immediately turned off the breaker.  After the smoke cleared, we noticed that the broiler element had broke (clean break) near the back of the stove, and there was also a hole in the top of the shell of the oven.  The area also contained metal slag around the hole, and the slag also had fallen on the bottom of the oven.  What appeared to have happened was that the element broke, and instead of just having an open circuit, the current from the element "arced" to the top of the oven shell, creating an "arc welder".  No one was injured, just very startled.  Luckily, we were just heating up some shrimp and rice, but if there was a steak broiling, the grease could have easily caught fire from the "arc welding" that was occurring.  The stove is a little over 5 years old (purchased August 28, 2007), and when I contacted LG, the customer service department tried to get their management to extend the warranty, but the management turned it down, stating that it was out of warranty.  I then contacted LG and spoke with [REDACTED] in management, asking them if they wanted the stove, as it is a potential fire hazard.  She seemed interested and would call me back in a day to see if the technical department was interested.  I never received a call.  I would have thought that LG would be interested in a defect in their product.  I guess they will just wait until a fire occurs and possible loss of life. Luckily in my case, there was someone around and it did not catch fire more than it did.  Because it was on broil and the door open, there could have been house damage and injury/loss of life.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard but no one was injured, making it a severity level 2.

incident_description: I was cooking dinner in my Simply Calphalon, 1611, 3qt. stainless steel pan with glass lid. The heat was not high because I was making a mix of seafood and garlic in cream sauce. I took off the lid and rested it against the side of the pan with the other edge on the top of the stove surface (not on the burner). I left it there for a while while I was still in the kitchen cleaning up and was surprised with a big "pop" sound and there was a hole that was blown out of the glass lid and it was cracked into many pieces. I do have digital pictures on my camera if you need to see them to verify what happened.
justification: The incident was an accident that caused damage to the glass lid, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Fox Run pasta machine grinds metal into the pasta.
justification: Metal grinding into pasta is an incident with no reported injury, but it is likely to occur given the description.

incident_description:
Our coffee maker(gevalia) started by the clock running thru the numbers and a few of the buttons
On the board not working all the time. Unplugging it would set it back to normal. Then this morning
During just after brewing the front electrical panal started to smoke. Scary since we kat had a house
Fire last year!
It's gevalia white 12 cup automatic coffee maker CM-500
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned and produced smoke, but no injury or fire occurred, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
On Tuesday, Sept 18, 2012, we ran a wash cycle on our GE Monogram Dishwasher (Model ZBD0710N00S Serial SM861634B).  After it was finished we unloaded it and put in a few new items.  Two of which were plastic.

15 minutes later we smelled smoke in the house.  We searched until we opened the dishwasher and found the origin.  

All the buttons on the control panel implied the system was off however the heating element at the bottom of the unit was very hot.  It melted the hard plastic tupper ware items, causing the smoke, and damaged the metal items in the dishwasher as well as damaging the dishwashers bottom spray arm.

We did finally get it off by some unknown action.

However, an hour later we started to smell something again and it appeared the unit had come back on at which time we flipped the circuit breaker.

I went on the web and found a GE recall for monogram dishwashers with model number ZBD0710K00 (note the ...KOO while our is ...NOO).

So this model is not under recall, but it surely should be.

I went back and have flipped the circuit breaker again to do some more evidence gathering, and the heating element came on yet again.
justification: The incident caused property damage and created a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I have a 2 year old GE Profile refrigerator with Model Number PSHF9PGZBCWW.  The product has an internal ice bin that uses a clear plastic auger to move the ice when someone requests ice.  Some of the plastic broke off, and these pieces look exactly like ice since it is a clear plastic.  One of my children almost tried to eat one of these pieces.  The auger should not be made of a clear plastic!
justification: A child almost ingested a plastic piece, but no injury occurred; the likelihood is possible given the design flaw.

incident_description:
(2011) The consumer stated that when they would get their food out of the microwave, the side and tray would be extremely hot and has burned his wife's left hand. The consumer's wife is a RN so she treated her own wounds. She applied burn ointment.  The consumer says this happens when the microwave is on any setting

They also had issues with the microwave coming on by itself. The consumer says they would have to shut off the circuit breaker and restart it to fix that issue.

(8/6/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and a report was filed (case#[REDACTED]). They advised him that they would look into the matter and contact him back. They also wanted to review the service information that has been performed on the unit.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury requiring treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The microwave's recurring issues suggest a likely occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he was cleaning the gas range and while using the chemical it dripped onto the ignition switch which ignited flames.  He was able to unplugged the unit immediately to disconnect the power which extinguished the flames.  The incident caused the melting of the ignition switch and the knob.

The ignition switch is designed with a failure it has no seals, no protection, so the consumer is at risk at all times for the unit to burst in flames, because of the exposure of the ignition switch.

8/20/12 The manufacturer was contacted and the consumer was told by a Manager that there were no recalls and that General Electric had no previous reports of any issues on this cook top.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted ignition switch and knob) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw and lack of recalls.

incident_description:
(9/1/2012) The consumer stated that she noticed that the indicator lights on the stove were glowing. The consumer's husband placed his hand on one of the burners and felt that it was warming up. The consumer immediately tried to turn the knobs which were already in the OFF position to begin with. There was no success with that. The consumer then unplugged the unit and left it unplugged.

 (9/4/2012) The consumer contact the manufacturer and an appointment was scheduled for September 5, 2012 at no charge since there was a safety issue.

(9/5/2012) The technician came out and after he plugged the unit in, the front left burner became extremely hot. The technician advised her that the all the switches failed, which caused the burners to come on by themselves. After the conclusion of the inspection, they were advised that the total repairs would be $400 and they would pay a percentage of that cost. The second offer is that they could purchase a new stove through them directly at a discounted rate, which only stands for 30 days from the day she spoke with them.
justification: The incident involved a stove malfunctioning and heating up without being turned on, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The microwave oven will turn on and begin cooking without any user input.
justification: The microwave turning on without user input is an incident that could lead to potential hazards, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: My frigidaire electric smooth top range (Model # FEFL77ABE, Serial # VF23007977) the oven heating element is turning itself on and super heating, even if it is turned off. It will not let you turn it off, i have to unplug it to turn it off. Had I not caught it my house and my life were potentially in danger.
justification: The oven heating element turning on uncontrollably poses a significant fire hazard, potentially endangering life and property.

incident_description: Used my Mr. Coffee Expresso Machine, turned it off (did not unplug) a few minutes later, I smelled burning plastic the machine was smoking.  I unplugged the machine and took it outside; it proceeded to catch on fire, if I had not been home the fire would have spread to my upper cabinets and burned my house down.  The machine is model number ECM91.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled before significant damage.

incident_description:
The consumer says three months after purchasing the unit, they noticed an electrical hole in the back of the upper oven.  He says that a flame ignited from inside the oven while the unit was in self cleaning mode.  The heat/smoke was so intense it set off the fire alarm.

He contacted the manufacturer and they replaced the unit back in February 2003.  The consumer says that two nights ago, the same thing occurred to the current oven again in self cleaning mode.

He says he will not bother contact the manufacturer this time but does feel that this is a serious problem.
justification: The incident involved a flame igniting and setting off a fire alarm, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: One of the burners could not be turned off. The gas line had to be turned off to shut off the burner. A repair technician diagnosed the problem as a faulty valve. When he opened the line, gas immediately came out from the burner. The line had to be turned off.
justification: The incident involved a faulty valve leading to a gas leak, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Our very expensive Sears Kenmore Elite slide in range, model number 790.46613500,  manufactured in October 2005 has a severe malfunction rendering it unsafe. 

On Sunday, September 16, 2012  the left front surface heating element: 1) turn ons spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off. This poses a fire and burn hazard to my household. 

This is the identical problem that The CPSC issued a recall notice, http://www.smoothtoprangerecall.com/

When I called  the company and informed them of the problem, they denied to fix the range , on the grounds that the  model number is not on their list. 

What do you recommend I do now?
justification: The malfunctioning heating element poses a fire and burn hazard, which could lead to injury, and the issue is documented in a recall notice indicating it is a known problem.

incident_description: We purchased an Emerson microwave model MWG9115SL at about one year ago.  On the inside compartment, at the top where there is a heat shield for a broiler element, we had an arc and momentary fire during regular usage.  The arcing was sufficient to ablate material from the heat shield and put a burn scorch mark on the roof of the microwave.

incident_description:

incident_description:
08/22/2012. The incident involved a gas leak caused by an electrical arc in the Thermador model stove cutting eight holes in the main gas line feed inside of the stove thereby allowing gas to leak unabated into the home and creating a fire. The consumer stated his wife started the oven to heat a pizza. A flame burst out from the back of the stove and flared up. She turned off all of the gas control knobs on the stove but the fire kept growing and the home filled with gas. She used a halotron fire extinguisher to put out the flames but continued to hear and smell large amounts of gas coming from the stove. The home filled with gas and she left the house fearing it would explode. She called the fire department who promptly came to the house. The gas was shut off at the outside gas meter main valve.

The fire department entered the home with self contained breathing masks and pulled the stove from the wall and saw that the fire had mostly been contained within the stove. The fire department called the utility Southwest Gas who immediately sent a technician to the home. The technician disconnected and capped the gas line to the stove and removed the metal backing to the stove. He discovered that the manufacturer's gas line inside of the stove had eight holes burned into it from electrical arcing from non-insulated high voltage electrical lugs/wiring inside the stove. The technician from the gas company confirmed the gas line from the home had been correctly installed and the gas leak was a product defect by the manufacturer within the stove which the gas company had seen before. 

The fire also destroyed the fan and other wiring inside the stove. (See attached pictures). The damage was confined to the kitchen.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak and fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported, and the damage was confined to the kitchen.

incident_description:
Subj: Defective Whirlpool Microwave Oven, Model # WFGS20S0ABO, Serial # R21010333

I am writing to advise you that I believe the Whirlpool Microwave listed above is both Defective and a Safety hazard.

We moved into our newly built home on May 1, 2012. Shortly after moving in, we attempted to use the microwave oven to reheat food items. This microwave has 2 layers. Layer one is the rotating bottom plate layer and layer 2 is a grill rack like material. The Microwave arced/sparked off on the corner and left a burn mark on both the lining of the microwave and the corner of the grill/ rack.

We called Whirlpool, who in turn sent out a Technician from a local company. The Technician acknowledged that there was a problem but was not ready to call it a defect until she was able to confer with Whirlpool. The Technician returned a 2nd time and again acknowledged there was a problem but stopped short of calling it a "defect". She indicated we would have to pursue it as a "Warranty" Issue with Whirlpool.

I have written Whirlpool and advised them there are only 2 Fixes I will accept: 1. Fix the Microwave OR 2. Replace it. I have NOT heard formally from Whirlpool though they acknowledge receiving my letter.

I believe the Builder of my home purchased these Whirlpool Appliances through Lowes of Sparks,
Nevada. I have not contacted Lowes as I think it is up to Whirlpool to honor their warranty on this new appliance.

The following is taken directly off the Whirlpool Warranty pamphlet: Cooking Rack -"Use only for 2 level cooking. To avoid damage to the microwave oven, always remove rack after 2 level cooking".

What this tells me is that Whirlpool has known all along that there is a problem with using the Microwave with the grill/rack in place. Why else would they try to insert a "disclaimer" in the Warranty Book.

I believe this product is both defective and dangerous; dangerous enough to require a total recall of all units that have the 2 layer grill/rack.
justification: The microwave sparked and caused burn marks, indicating a safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My GE dishwasher currently has a voluntary recall in place as of August 2012.  Among the solutions was the option for GE to have an installer replace the heating element to prevent house fires. Sounded like an awesome idea to me, and we did it. Service work was done on August 27, 2012.

On September 15 2012, I loaded the dishwasher normally around 8pm,  did some other junk, and went to bed.
A guest in my home that weekend awoke to our house full of smoke. Upon investigating the source, we found the dishwasher hot to the touch, as well as the granite counters and any adjoining cupboards and contents. Smoke rolled out of the dishwasher, which we quickly cut the power to, and began to air out our house. The inside of the dishwasher tub was completely melted, along with the spray arms. I lost a pile of dishes, and the interior was hot enough for some silverware to melt COMPLETY THROUGH the bottom of the dishwasher. This was discovered at around 9am, therefore the dishwasher must have been on the dry cycle for roughly 12 hours.

GE needs to know that their quick and dim-witted heating element fix is clearly not the issue. I'll be letting [REDACTED] know for sure, since we very nearly experienced a house fire where we, our four children, and an out of town guest were sleeping. I had a 15 year career as a firefighter, and I can promise you that our kitchen was maybe 15 mins or less from flames showing. I am filing a complaint with GE Corporate, and a handful of others. My family was put in danger AFTER the required recall work was performed. GE needs to be forced to recall every one of these dishwashers before someone is killed. We are proof that their fix does not work, and I have photos if you would like them. I attempted to upload them to this report, and it's not working. I can email them much easier. Also, the victims listed in the report are listed because all 7 of us inhaled toxic burning plastic smoke for hours while we slept. All of us woke up with sore throat and headache until the place aired out, which took 24 hours. 

Thanks for your time,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused injury (sore throat and headache from inhaling toxic smoke) and nearly resulted in a house fire, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
Day 1	
The house had a strange smell and a hazy look to it.  After checking the house over, we could not find anything burning and the smell and haziness eventually went away.  I did not think about this again until after researching refrigerators online.
Day 2
After noticing that the ice was melting in the ice bin and onto the floor, I emptied the ice container, cleaned up the mess and made sure the door on the freezer was shut tight.  The door had not been tight in the past so we figured that was the reason why the ice was melting.
Day 3
The refrigerator and the freezer were both warm and all the food ruined.  There are numerous fire related problems relating to whirlpool refrigerators.  Maytag and other" Whirlpool" companies have recalled theirs with similar problems.  Why has Whirlpool not recalled theirs when there are so many reports of SAFETY issues with their product?  Does someone need to die or injured seriously before a recall happens?
I was very lucky that the fire stayed contained to the refrigerator and extinguished itself.  Recently the smoke detectors were taken down and put in the garage because they beeped even with new batteries.  The week before we were away on vacation and a pet sitter would stop in to take care of our pets.  Smoke detectors or not this could have been a tragedy with people or pets killed if the fire had not been contained like in the other reports regarding Whirlpool.  Homes have burnt, but I do not think anyone has died yet.  Whirlpool needs to recall these refrigerators before people die!  Whirlpool is aware of the problem.  When will they issue a recall, because there has to be a lot of ticking time bombs still out there?
From what we gathered, the problem may be with the Start-Device combination unit (start relay and overload) and the capacitor.  This is where the fire at least starts.  The part # 2212193 is no longer available and replaced with part # 8201786.  This leads us to believe that Whirlpool is definitely aware of a defect and this is the reason for the change in parts.  It could also be the Capacitor part #2169373.  It is either a defected part or it could be electrical problem or something else that is causing these parts to catch fire.  Some people feel that by just replacing the burned parts that you would be just setting yourself up for another fire because it may be something else causing these parts to catch fire. 
There are numerous stories just like mine that you can find online some are even on you tube while others have found their way to "saferproducts.gov".  What needs to be done to have a working and safe refrigerator?  It is very hard living without a running refrigerator.  
The drier part # 2199167 may be the wrong kind for use with refrigerant ( R-134a), it is no longer available and replaced with part # 4387019.  The compressor part # 2212191 also is no longer available and replaced with part #8201557.  The compressor that came with the unit is Embraco  EGY 80HLP.  The replacement is Embraco EGY 80HLPW, the W on the end stand for "with oil cooler".  This could also be the reason it catches fire because there is not a cooler on the original compressor.	
If the burnt parts are replaced without the cause being fixed, we could be setting ourselves up for another fire and our family and pets killed.
Please let me know as soon as possible on what to do because there is not running refrigerator or freezer in the home.
One of the burnt parts has this number 445KFBYY  53  FKR1L  engraved on the actual part.  It is either the capacitor or part of the start relay and overload.  This part number is not listed on any part list.  This could be the reason too.  When researching the numerous fire related cases, this part was included with the same part number in  pictures posted online by others whom have had fires.  It is right in the middle of where the fire starts.  It seems a little fishy that whirlpool does not have this part listed when it is on their equipment. 
Thank you,
justification: The incident involved a fire that was contained to the refrigerator without injury or death, but there is a clear safety concern with the product.

incident_description: I was preheating my Kenmore Electric Range/Oven, Model #66592014102 when I recieved an error message on the display of the oven.  It appeared to read "PF 5" and then the oven shut off.  The display went blank.  I decided to go to the upper level of my home with laundrey and assumed the oven was off.  While upstairs, I smelled something strange and when I came into the kitchen, I noticed the "baking stone" in the oven was on fire and the "heating coils" on the top of the stove were on and the oven was extremely hot.  The only way to get the oven to turn off was to turn it off at the circuit breaker.  It took almost 5 hours for the stove to cool down.  This oven is definitely a fire hazard and if I had not been home, it could have been a disaster.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Oven element became superheated and began to melt/spark.  Ovne did not turn off when knob was moved to "OFF" position.  Oven only turned off when circuit breaker was turned off.  Oven is a Kenmore Electric Glass Top Range, model # 911.9554591, serial no.# 6V108135Q.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but there was no reported injury, only potential for harm.

incident_description:
(7/26/2012) The consumer stated that he was using his oven on the broil setting. The consumer had the oven running for approximately 10 minutes, when his dish finished broiling. When he went to shut off the oven, it would not. The consumer stated that he unplugged the unit, in order to shut it off completely. He waited another 10 minutes and plugged the unit back in.  The oven automatically turned back on immediately after he plugged the stove back in. 

(7/27/2012) The manufacturer was contacted, no report was filed and he was informed that since there was no recall on it, they wouldn't be able to assist him. They offered for a technician to come out to his home to diagnose the stove for a fee of $75, which he declined.

-The consumer stated that approximately 1.5 months ago he filed an incident report on the same stove, but for the top 2 burners not shutting off. That issue has not been resolved.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that did not shut off, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My microwave, and Emerson MWG9115SL, was being used normally, ie, most days I warm up my cooling coffee in the morning.  I warmed some up then ran outside to get the kids on the bus etc.  When I stepped back inside the whole house smelled like burning plastic.  I had checked all over the house before I noticed the hum coming out of the microwave.  The light was not on, the timer was not running, but the microwave was running and sparks were visible.  I have to open the door and unplug it to be certain it won't run on it's own.  I contacted Emerson about this but they refuse to help, stating that it would be out of it's one year warranty period.  I've owned this unit for about 2 years, purchased it new from Wal Mart.  I don't think 2 years is too long to expect your microwave to NOT burn down your house, which I believe mine nearly did judging by the sparks and smell.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned with sparks and a burning smell, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: New Premier 36" gas stove/oven with electonic igniter.  When you turn the knob to light the burner, the first position is the ignition position, and sparking takes place.  The next position is high flame.  There is no pushing of the knob necessary to move the knob to the high position.  If you turn the knob just a tiny bit past the igniter position, gas will flow freely out at a high rate and very quickly build up in the room even though the burner did not ignite.  If you realize that you have turned the burner too far, and have gas building up, the only option to stop the gas flow is to turn the knob through the igniter position to the off position.  This will likely cause the built-up gas to ignite causing a flash which could cause a serious fire or seriously burn the user.
justification: The incident describes a scenario where gas buildup can lead to a flash fire, posing a serious risk of burns or death.

incident_description: We purchased a Gas Self Cleaning Five burner stove with griddle center in July 2011. The knobs on the front are so loose and so easily to turn that we often times turn on the gas just by bumping them. even our dog can turn on the knobs enough for the gas to escape! Twice we have been outside working on the yard, and our dog turned on the gas filling the entire house with gas!! We had to open all the windows, and turn on the fans for the air to clear after several hours.  We feel like this stove is extremely unsafe!!  If our dog can turn on the gas, what about children??  This is an ongoing problem.  I would say the gas is accidentally bumped on at least once a month!!
justification: The incident involves gas leakage due to easily turned knobs, posing a significant risk of fire or explosion, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: Knife has opened several times while in my pocket. The blade tip has cut the pocket.
justification: The knife opening in the pocket caused damage to the pocket but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
A $259 Kitchen Kutter manual food grinder was purchased on 6/30/12 from Kitchen Craft in West Bend, WI.  Customer service is at: [REDACTED], see www.kitchencraftcookware.com  

Although my mother loves the food grinding capabilities of this Kitchen Kutter product there is a big problem with metal peeling off of the stem of this manual food grinder and concern that it can end up in the gastrointestinal tract of babies and adults.  Please see enclosed photo's.  I'm not sure if the peeling metal caused damage to the inside of the metal sleeve of the main unit where the stem goes, but see pictured.  Also on the stem inside the grinding cup that's now stuck on the stem screw shows rusting problems.  On the base of the stem the metal is starting to bubble.  

Although I haven't contacted the company to given them a chance to resolve this danger: Due to dangerous circumstances to child and adult bodily safety I'm thinking this needs to be food and safety alert and has been reported to the http://www.consumer-action.org/hotline/complaint_form/ and then to needed State and Federal agencies.  Please advise immediately.

Thanks very much.
justification: The description indicates a potential hazard with metal peeling off the grinder, posing a risk of ingestion, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: New Ronco 5 tray dehydrator, used a few times, one wire inside where it attaches to the heating element burned. Was always used according to manufacturer guide, not mis-handled.  Ronco refuses to to replace, must purchase a new one.  A few online blogs speak to this happening to other customers as well, Ronco says otherwise.  Clearly a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a wire burning, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. Online reports suggest this issue is not isolated.

incident_description: I purchased a Mr. Coffee Espresso maker Model # BVMC-ECM 260 at Walmart. It exploded on its second use. The brew basket detached from its retainer clip while it was brewing coffee and exploded, splattering the walls, floor and countertop with coffee grounds and water. Abut a third of coffee had brewed into the carafe when this happened. I've been using an espresso maker for more than 15 years and this has never happened before. This is the second Mr. Coffee espresso maker that I have purchased in the past eight years.
justification: The incident caused property damage (coffee splattering) but no injury, and the user reports this has never happened before in 15 years of use.

incident_description: kitchen filled with smoke from the Maytag dishwasher
justification: The kitchen filled with smoke indicates an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Our dishwasher significantly overheated a few days ago - and few small plastic items inside melted. we have since turned the heating coil off.

We just saw a GE Profile diswasher recall and think the following model is also a concern that needs to be investigated.

Model: GSD3630F00WW
Sr. NO: HA779311B
justification: The dishwasher overheated and melted plastic items, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: GE Model PDW9280J10SS dishwasher heating element caught on fire during the night while family slept.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Our GE Range Model # JBP72S0K4SS / Serial # GM237880Q   The baking heating element in the oven melted through and started a fire on 09/06/2012.

We have the failed product if anyone is interested.

Thank you

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a melted heating element, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I recently purchase a GE 48" Built-In Side-by-Side Refrigerator with Dispenser. From the first day I have been having a problems with it. The temperature fluctuates. I have already trashed thousands of Dollars worth of food. My oldest has been sick with diarrhea several times consuming bad food due to the same problem. My new born has been sick since I was storing breast milk in the same refrigerator. 
I have contacted GE customer service several times and even had a technician check the refrigerator twice. The technician has not been able to fix the problem and his last comment was "It takes a new refrigerator six months before it will work properly, you need to wait!"
The second technician suggested I request a new refrigerator before it is too late. He thought fixing it is hopeless!
I have contacted GE support and customer relations several times and neither one of them is responsive! I guess all they care about is to get my money, they do not care if my family get sick or die!
I invested in buying this new refrigerator to make sure it is safe for storing breast milk for my new born, keep fresh vegetables and food for my family and save money in electricity as our family is growing. I am not achieving any of my goals and I truly regret replacing my old refrigerator. 
I am reporting to you because I do not want any other family go through what my family and I have gone through.
justification: The incident involves injury (sickness from consuming spoiled food and breast milk) and the problem is ongoing and unresolved, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart DLC-10. The blade has a center plastic piece and two metal blades. The blades are connected thru the plastic center piece via rivets. There are pressure cracks occurring on the bottom blade around the rivets which is causing parts of the blade to come off and enter the food. I came very close to swallowing a metal piece from the blade in my hummus.
justification: The incident involves metal pieces from a broken blade entering food, posing a risk of injury if ingested, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
This morning, while brewing coffee in our Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker, we heard a loud grinding, popping noise coming from the coffee maker.  When we went over to the counter where the coffee maker was we saw smoke coming out of the bottom of it and it was producing a horrible electrical burning smell.  We immediately unplugged the unit and took it outside.  After the smoke subsided and the unit cooled down, we inspected it.  The problem seemed to be in the heating element of the unit where the burner was causing the plastic base of the coffee maker to melt and subsequently smoke around the electrical cord of it.  

After this happened, we found on the Cuisinart website under Consumer Affairs that there are many reports indicating a similar problem with this model.  This is very disappointing as it appears to be a somewhat common issue, and this coffee maker is also rather expensive.  This is the second coffee maker by Cusinart (same model) that we've had within six years.  The first one was the same version of this but stainless steel versus plastic.  That one just stopped working after about 3 years.  When looking to replace that one, it appeared that Cuisinart replaced it with this plastic version.  

Thankfully, we were nearby the kitchen when our coffee maker started burning and smoking so we could take care of it immediately and avoid a larger fire.  We will no longer purchase Cuisinart, and hope that this specific make and model coffee maker will be recalled to protect other consumers.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from the coffee maker, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Cuisinart DCC-1200 Coffee Maker:

Turned on "Brew" setting in the morning.  Approximately five minutes later, the unit began smoking and the smell of burning plastic filled the house.  The On/Off light was off, but the coffee in the carafe was boiling and the metal plate beneath was bright red.  I quickly unplugged the unit and removed it outdoors where it continued to smoke for several seconds.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing smoke and burning plastic smell, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Kenmore electric range was set at 350 bake for about 40 min.  I then noticed that bright glow in oven I opened  the oven  and it was cooking  on broil setting, but the  is reading bake closed oven and flames came out of the back  from the control  panel.  Turned all controls off still flaming pull it away from the wall and unplugged it.
justification: The incident involved flames and a malfunctioning oven, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Outer glass on oven door shattered
justification: The shattered glass is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I heard a "pop" from my refrigerator at 4:15AM on Sept 4, 2012.  I smelled a "burning rubber" odor and pulled out the Kenmore Elite refrigerator.  There was a small flame in the compressor
We called Sears and they basically said there was nothing they could do. Tried to buy a new one that they could send out ASAP and they said it would be 2 weeks.
justification: There was a small flame in the refrigerator, indicating an incident, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I was preparing dinner for our family and was heating up some food in the oven at 200 degrees for about 20 minutes and then turned oven up to 350 degrees just before I was ready to serve the food.  I was standing at the kitchen counter getting dishes ready to set up outside for our Labor Day gathering, when the oven door shattered/exploded into a thousand pieces all over my kitchen!  I have a black pub style table across the room from the stove and the shards from the glass scratched the wood on the stools.  The shards were everywhere, even at the other end of my kitchen by the refrigerator!  Thank goodness everyone else was outside and no one was hurt.  

I was extremely upset, needless to say.
justification: The oven door shattered, causing property damage but no injuries, as everyone was outside.

incident_description: During the wash cycle, my Sears Kenmore Elite Dishwasher model 665 15273400 filled the kitchen with smoke and got very hot.  When I opened it, the cycle continued, throwing water out of the appliance and all around the room.  It would not shut off.  I had to go to the panel box and turn off the breaker.  The smoke was very acrid, and has settled all over the house.  There was no evidence of a fire, other than the smoke.  I believe it would have caused a house fire if I hadn't caught it in time.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Rival Air Popcorn Popper is unsafe because it gets too hot. The plastic on top got so hot it melted and the base burned our hands when touching. Popper spews hot kernals out really fast and they go every where.
justification: The popcorn popper gets dangerously hot, melting plastic and burning hands, indicating injury.

incident_description: I am reporting from a propane company.  We have experienced a few incidents where the gas control/thermostat has developed a leak and caused a small fire behind the refrigerator.  The refrigerator manufacturer is Consul and the effected model is CB2426.
justification: The incident involves small fires caused by leaks, indicating an incident with no reported injuries.

incident_description: Frigidaire dishwasher model # FDB1050REB2 caught fire in kitchen.  This home is a licensed group home for six intellectually disabled adults.  Thank God for the fire alarm system and fire extinguishers.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but no injuries or deaths were reported due to the fire alarm and extinguishers.

incident_description:
Tuesday, Sept. 4 around 8am a heavy smoke started coming out of our refrigerator.  It had the smell of melted plastic.  I shut of the main breaker and moved refrigerator.  A repairman came today and said the capacitor compressor starter  or the compressor went out.  The part he removed is charded.
Kitchenaid side by side refrigerator model # KSRA25KKSS2 Mfg date 1/04
Compressor - Embraco 512700159

Luckily this happened before I went to work, or more than our refrigerator could have caught fire.
justification: The incident involved heavy smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Maytag Recall Dishwasher 
Although my model number is not currently listed on your current recall list, I had to recently replace the heating element after we smelled an electrical fire in our dishwasher. When I dissembled the dishwasher, the heating element had faulted and melted the plastic where the element connected to the dishwasher. We happened to be home when we smelled the plastic melting and immediately stopped the dishwasher. The plastic was melted so bad that I had to cut off the connecting grommet. I am concerned that this is the same problem identified in the current recall and request a technical investigation to determine a similar problem with the model I have as noted below:

Model #: MDBTT79AWB
Serial #: 18719123CN
justification: The incident involved a faulty heating element causing a potential fire hazard, but no injury occurred as the issue was detected and addressed in time.

incident_description:
GE Profile Refrigerator smelled of an electrical fire.  Upon removing the back panel I found the relay to the compressor to be on fire with very visible flames.  Immediately unplugged the unit.
Model #PSS26MSRC SS
Serial #DH414586
GE Side x Side Profile Artica
justification: The incident involved visible flames from the refrigerator's compressor relay, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Needed to replace the lower heating element in my range. Upon removing the back panel I found burn areas in the "insulation" around the connectors of the element. I also found burn areas around the area of connection for the upper element, as well as several wires going in the back heading into the cook top area...one white wire with a cloth covering showed a burn area. I do have pictures but the battery died and will have to send at a later time. They show all of these areas.
justification: Burn areas found in insulation and wires indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was in the kitchen, and the over-the-range microwave oven turned on, uncommanded.  The microwave ran for about 10 seconds before I could reach it.  I tried to turn the microwave off by pressing buttons on the control panel, and the microwave was unresponsive.  The microwave continued to cook.  I finally needed to open the door for the microwave to stop, and then the words displayed on the microwave display.  The display read "SE."  I have unplugged the microwave from the wall and not used it since that date.

Had I not been home at the time, the microwave would have continued to cook, and potentially caused a fire.
justification: The microwave operated uncommanded and could have caused a fire if unattended, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Entire front of oven door exploded and shattered glass all over the kitchen. My wife was baking
@350 degrees when this happened. Sears has been notified and sent info on many other
exploding oven glass doors. Will not stand behind it and said there is no recall. Does 
someone have to be injured before this problem is addressed. Kenmore exploding
glass doors is all over the internet
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to shatter, but no injury was reported. The incident is documented as a known issue with the product.

incident_description:
Opened refrigerator door and smelled burning plastic.  Noticed that the fridge lights were HOT and that the clear plastic shroud surrounding the lights was MELTED.  Molten plastic was dripping down onto food items.  I checked, and the lights would stay on even when the door-closed-sensors were depressed.  

I suspect this could have caused a fire if left much longer.

 Sears Kenmore Elite refigerator, model 795.77563600
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light that caused melting plastic, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death.

incident_description:
While cleaning my kitchen cabinet I received a very painful cut on my finger from the bottom left corner of my Sharp Carousel microwave oven.   This was very painful and it has happen twice!   The microwave has clear medal sharp sides protruding down from the front of both sides of the unit about one quarter inch. 

The model number....R-209KK    
Serial number....1308974
mfg date dec. 2006
Household Microwave Oven
justification: The incident resulted in a painful cut, indicating an injury, and has occurred twice, suggesting it is likely to happen again.

incident_description:
I received scalding burns from hot wet coffee grounds when the top blew open and sprayed me with the contents of the [REDACTED] that I was brewing at the time.  It was unfortunate that I was within range when it happened.  This has occurred several times with this brewer.  

I have my ideas as to why this is happening being a person that works with steam and steam systems.  The [REDACTED] receives hot water and at the end of the cycle some steam occurs as the water empties out of the tank.  It is my belief that this action causes or caused the plastic cup to swell in the only direction that it could.  i.e., up and down.  When that happened the pressure against the lid causes it to pop open, this of course releases the pressure in the cup ejecting some of the contents.  I have had to clean up after the pot a several times and got burned once.  

My body was marked from where I got burned and I am hoping that they will heal completely.  As a safety hazard, I would hope that you redesign the lid to prevent it from opening.  I could not see any obstructions in the lower needle but I can not guarantee that there wasnÃÂt any there at the time(s) of the incidents. 

The device and a few [REDACTED] were returned to the manufacture in the hopes of getting a recall on the books to prevent others from suffering un-necessary burns

LINK TO RECALL PRESS RELEASE https://www.mrcoffeerecall.com/Docs/Mr%20%20Coffee%20Single%20Cup%20by%20JCS%20Coffeemaker.pdf
justification: The incident resulted in scalding burns, indicating injury (severity 3), and the issue has occurred several times, making it likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I purchased a Maytag Gas Double Oven Range to use in my manufactured new home.  During canning my CO detector has gone off the highest reading has been 68 with fans and windows open.    I contacted Maytag and they say there is nothing wrong with the range.  They say the manufactured home dealer should have installed an external hood vent which Maytag states is required by law.   The manufactured home dealer said it is not required and is not their problem.
justification: CO detector went off, indicating a potential hazard, but no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
When I got up I turned my Cuisinart DCC1200 coffee maker on and shortly after it brewed I heard popping and hissing sounds and went to look at it.  I saw smoke pouring from the electrical cord hole.  The unit showed that it was off.  I immediately unplugged it and put it outside.  I'm thankful that I had forgotten to set the timer the night before.

I emailed Cuisinart Customer service and this is their reply:Thank you for your inquiry. Based on the information you have provided, your unit is within the limited warranty period and can be set up for replacement. However, our warranty does not include shipping and processing fees. We ask that you cover the cost of shipping the defective power cord to Cuisinart. What we would require you to do is unplug the old unit, take a pair of scissors, and cut the power cord one inch from the Coffee Maker base. We recommend that you use a traceable insured delivery service. Once we have received your mailing information a Service Notification number will be created and an e-mail will be sent back to you with instruction on how to proceed on returning your defective unit. If you prefer, we welcome you to call our Customer Service Department at 1-800-726-0190 with this information. Please keep in mind the Customer Service Agent will not have access to your e-mail information. The hours of operation are 7 AM -11 PM EST Monday through Friday and 9 AM - 5:30 PM on Saturdays and Sundays, excluding major holidays.

Since this happened I have read numerous complaints regarding the same problem.  Why hasn't this product been recalled?  Does someone have to lose their home or their life?
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Brewed coffee with our less than year old cuisinart coffee maker, about 30 minutes after brewing the warming plate started to make a little noise and than started smoking up the room. When I saw the smoke I unplugged it. 

This coffee maker has an automatic shut off timer. So if I had left for work, would my house have burned to the ground ? Or would my two dogs have died from the smoke filled air ? 

Is this a problem that the company knows about ?
justification: The incident involved smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the automatic shut-off likely prevented a fire.

incident_description: When the timer dial is turned to the right in order to toast food, it periodically does not turn off. This typically happens if you are trying to lightly toast an item and you turn it to the lighter toasting option. Sometimes it begins normally and I can hear the slight clicking noise that indicates that the timer is working, but then the clicking seems to stop and the toaster heating process never turns off. Other times, if you only turn it to medium (lighter) toasting, the heating element turns on and begins to toast but the timer never activates, so it never automatically turns off.
justification: The toaster fails to turn off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
My wife went outside last Friday and when she came back into the house, our Samsung over-the-stove microwave oven had turned itself on.  I thought she must be mistaken until I saw it happen this evening when we were both in the kitchen.  Fortunately for us, we were home both times this happened and in both cases there wasn't anything in the microwave.  Otherwise, it's possible our house could have burned down.

I have read of this problem at other websites, yet Samsung refuses to admit there is an issue with this product.  I have three children in the house under the age of 10 and we are afraid to keep this product plugged it.  Consumers should be warned about the danger of this unsafe product.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred in the reported incidents.

incident_description:
I had purchased a GE 5 cup coffee maker from Wal Mart and the handle fell off shortly after.I purchased another of the same kind and it happened again. This would in my opinion be a major defect that could cause serious burns and even cuts from a broken carafe.Please see I have notified Select Brands.

The sender therefore does not accept liability for any errors, omissions or consequences which arise as a result of e-mail transmission. 
I was also shocked to see Wal Mart still selling this product, that has a defective nut on the handle.
justification: The handle falling off is an incident with no reported injury, but potential for burns or cuts is mentioned.

incident_description:
Last Saturday, the glass lid to our Calphalon saute pan spontaneously shattered.  I was in the kitchen washing dishes when I heard a sudden "bang!" coming from the direction of the fridge.  When I investigated, I found the shattered lid. The pan and lid sit on top of the fridge with other large pots, but nothing had fallen off of the other pots.  There is only ceiling above the lid, so nothing fell from there.  I felt the top of the fridge to see if it was hot or cold, but it was room temperature.  I have no idea why this lid suddenly shattered.  Thank goodness the glass was tempered and stayed mostly intact after shattering. No one was hurt.  We cleaned up the glass. The following information is inscribed on the bottom of the pan: "Unison Sear 6 qt 5.6 L 5006."  We received the pan as a gift in January, 2012, which was shipped to us directly. 

 I called Calphalon this morning and requested a replacement lid, which they are providing.  I asked if they had an explanation for the shattering and the rep suggested that perhaps I had dropped it.  I do not remember dropping this lid.  Am I the first person to have this problem?
justification: The glass lid shattered unexpectedly but no one was injured, and the tempered glass contained the shards.

incident_description:
Fridgedaire slide in electric stove and oven , Model FES367ABE, Serial # NF24812721 
The oven cleaning program started on its'   own and I could NOT get the oven door open because the door locked and would not open! My cookware is stored in oven and were melting and black smoke spilled out of the oven vents with a horrible smell. Even after unplugging the electric outlet the oven would not open and the cookware continued to cook and smoke heavily. My husband and I kept plugging and unplugging the electric outlet and the oven would NOT open. The stink and black smoke was horrible. Finally, after many efforts my husband was able to get the door open and get the cookware out. They were melted and ruined and the smell is still in our home. I contacted the Fridgedaire consumers at [REDACTED] and spoke to supervisor, [REDACTED], after I could not get the help I wanted. Was told I was NOT under warranty and that the best he could do was give me a discount on parts! I have to pay for service call, labor and the parts!  Why?  After reading complaints about this product, my incident is NOT isolated. Fridgedaire has had lots of reports for defects. Some were recalled, but not this particular one. I asked for new unit and thought given the seriousness of the defect and fire, this was reasonable.  In other incidents the company did replace the unit. We live on fixed  disability income and can't afford even the repairs. Is it my fault the unit is defective and could have burned down my house had I not been home? Why do some people get replaced units and some don't?  Can I get help, please?
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused melting cookware and black smoke, posing a serious fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Over the weekend, my GE dishwasher heating unit remained on over 24 hours after a wash cycle was completed.  The dishwashers model number GLD6200L15WW serial number RL748615B was not included in the most recent recall on August 9, 2012 for a similar issue.  My 21 month daughter touched the outside of the dishwasher door and said 'OUCH! HOT!' My husband and I both touched the dishwasher thinking that she was confusing hot and cold but found out that it was extremely HOT and checked my daughters hand. Her hand did not sustain any burns but when we opened up the dishwasher the dishes was so hot that it had to be handled by a pot holder to avoid getting burned.  The outside wooden frame of the dishwasher was also hot.  We immediately turned off the circuit breaker to the dishwasher and also our disposer as they are connected.  We have not been able to use the dishwasher or the disposer since then. I have called GE and they have stated that this model was not covered under the recall but I have to pay for a diagnosis with GE technician to determine if this is in fact a recall issue.  This is a huge safety issue and should be looked at.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher overheating, causing discomfort but no burns or injuries, and the model was not part of a recall.

incident_description:
Some time after purchasing the Hamilton Beach model76606 electric can opener (over a year) it started to require more than one turn around a can and now will not open a can at all.  Also, as it was failing to cut it would track differently on multiple turns and shave off fine metal turnings that clung to the can and the opener mechanism.  

The metal shavings are at great risk of getting into the food and since the can be very fine could be ingested without the consumers knowledge.  I can attest to their ability to puncture flesh since I got a sliver in my finger as I was disassembling the unit to discover what the problem was.

I discovered that the cutting wheel edge was completely worn down.  In my opinion it was not properly tempered to stand up to normal household service for any reasonable length of time.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (sliver in the finger) and poses a likely risk of metal shavings contaminating food, which could lead to ingestion.
