incident_description: My Kenmore cooktop model #790.9611340A front left burner will not turn off. It automatically turns to high when on and yesterday we could not turn it off at all. Had to trip breaker and finally it turned off on its own. It also will turn on by itself when knob is turned to off.
justification: The cooktop malfunction poses a fire hazard and potential injury risk, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
GE dishwasher overheating resulting in melting of plastic and detroying dishwasher.  Incident is siimlar to GE recalls in which water leaking into circuit board leading to short circuit and overheating of dishwasher.

Repeated attempts to contact GE service center have resulted in denial of issue (e.g., 30-60 minute waits on line, will not service because model label melted off during incedent).

Note:  Attempts to upload pictures resulted in lock up and loss of all data in file!
justification: The incident describes property damage (melted dishwasher) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to similarity to known GE recalls and repeated service issues.

incident_description:
BUNN ST Velocity coffee maker

Wires feeding the heater shorted out melting the insulation and plastic housing. It generated a strong burning smell that prompted me to switch it off. it was about to catch on fire. Lucky I was in the house.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard but was prevented without injury.

incident_description:
Purchased a solofill automatic K-Cup (coffee pod) dispenser from Bed, Bath and Beyond. UPC Code: 852932003129

Mounted the unit on the wall using the manufacturer instructions, about 45 minutes after mounting, the 18x18 glass front of it flew off of the unit and broke on kitchen floor, cutting both my and my 6 year old daughters legs.

The glass flew off with significant force because the auto dispenser is spring loaded.

Apparently the assembly process uses double stick tape to secure the glass to the base of the unit and the tape process is either flawed or is simply not sufficient to retain the items it's deigned to hold.

Stitches were required to repair my cut, were not required for my daughter.

After cleanup, it is very apparent the tape used to place the glass onto the base is inadequate.

We are extremely lucky that the glass did not hit either of our faces or eyes.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring stitches for one person and minor cuts for another, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the apparent design flaw with the tape.

incident_description: I have a Mr. Coffee Single Cup Brewer and while making my 2nd cup of coffee it burst open hitting my neck and leg and nearly missing my 2 year old daughter.  I have pictures of blistering on my right leg and the right side of my neck.  The cup popped out and splattered within a 5 foot radius.
justification: The incident caused blistering injuries to the leg and neck, and narrowly missed a child, indicating a moderate severity. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
Within the first year of owning the Sharp Carrousel Microwave the small panel inside the oven would catch fire when cooking popcorn or an item with little liquid.
This is a very dangerous problem. I believe the product should be recalled. I have read that this has happened to other people that have the same microwave.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard inside the microwave, which is dangerous but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: This is the second time this has happened and I want some answers! I have a Frigidare Glasstop range that came with the purchase of a new home in 2009. In October 2011 several of cooktops came on by themselves and could not be shut off via the knobs. After trying for several minutes in vain I had to unplug the entire range to get it to stop. After calling several different numbers for the manufacturer I finally get a response and a technician was sent to repair the stove. Well now in September 2012 it has happened again. I was boiling water on the back cooktop and the front one came on at full blast and would not shut off. So once again I had to unplug this unit before it shut off. I will call again for it to be repaired but I will not feel safe until this unit is replaced.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning cooktop that turns on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: At 2 am this morning I heard an electrical arcing sound coming from the kitchen. As I enter the kitchen I could smell electrical burning and see visible flame coming from the back of my refrigerator. I disconnected the power and pulled the fridge away from the wall. The starter relay for the compressor was all burnt up as well as some of the foam insulation in the compressor housing.
justification: The incident involved visible flame and electrical burning, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
SERIAL # SP1054263  MFG DATE MAR 2003. MODEL #ED5GTFXKQ02 SIDE BY SIDE WHIRLPOOL REFRIGERATOR.  Upon walking into my kitchen today (Sept 2, 2012)  I smelled an electrical fire and called for my husband to help me locate the fire.  We found the fire in the back of our refrigerator and quickly unplugged the unit.  My husband was able to pull the relay switch (437NEBYY  -77 FPB3L) from the unit and it was scorched and melted.  We tried to call Whirlpool consumer line and got a recording that they were not open.  I left a message online on their chat  online option and didn't get a response.

Of course I searched the internet to see about locating a replacement part and found an abundance of complaints concerning this issue with this switch.  It is unbelievable this company has not either issued a recall of the switch and replace them with a new switch that is not defective or recall the refrigerators themselves.  So far they have been fortunate in that the owners have been home when this occurs.  It is just fortunate for us that it happened on a Sunday and not Monday-Saturday.  As both of us are at work everyday except Sunday.

On a side note (frustration only!) it is a holiday weekend and we can't get anyone to help us until Tuesday....at which time all of our refrigerated food will be ruined and need to be replaced.  But at least our house didn't burn down and the weather is nice enough that we can open our windows and air this stench out of our home.

I have always been a very loyal customer of Whirlpool.  I own a [REDACTED] along with the refrigerator (All Whirlpool brand) and this is the first issue I have had with any of their products.  Very disappointing in seeing the response this issue has had and how they have handled it.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire in the refrigerator with no reported injuries, but potential for significant property damage.

incident_description: Whirlpool side by side refrigerator, model no ED5FHEXLQ01 caught on fire.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, which is an incident but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description:
My wife brunt her finger on teh exterior of our new oven door.  The exterior temperature is extrememly hot and dangerous, especially becasue we have 3 young children.  

WE called Whirlpool and htey sent out a tech who agreed it was unreasonally hot.  When he called Whirlpool the company techs stated it is operating within specifications.  This is unreasonable and if true, many people will get 1st and 2nd degree burns  on their hands and children are at risk of burning their faces and other parts of their bodies.


Model Number: WFG231LVS0
Serial Number: VE22602007
Purchase Date: 08/17/2012

After pushing back on Whirlpool they have agreed to buy back the oven, but I am more concerned that they are claiming it is operating as designed.  It is dangerous.
justification: The incident describes a burn injury from the oven door, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the oven's design and presence of young children.

incident_description:
Dish washer smelled burned. Contacted Maytag, discovered unit was under a recall. Maytag never contacted me about recall despite registration at phurchae. Maytag agreed to send repair parts. I waited several weeks. No parts arrived. Contacted Maytag again, they again offered to send parts, claiming a computer glitch. Weeks later no parts have arrived.

I cannot plug in washer for fear of fire, but cannot obtain recalled parts as a remedy from Maytag.
justification: The dishwasher poses a potential fire hazard but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The caller stated that his spouse turned on the right front burner and black smoke and flames started emitting from the control.  The range was powered off and then disconnected from the gas.  There were no prior incidents or services for this unit.

8/10/12  The manufacturer was contacted and a service rep was sent out on 8/13.  He was advised by the rep that the repairs would cost him approximately $650.  The diagnostic was a gas leak under the control.

The caller is concerned that this gas range has a failure and should be addressed by the firm.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from a gas range, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: In 2007, we purchased a GE Dishwasher with our [REDACTED] home.  The model no. is GSD3300N00BB and the serial no. is HM828832B.  After using the dishwasher, on at least one occassion there was smoke that could be seen coming out of the top of the dishwasher.  When we opened the dishwasher, the heating element was burning and there did not seem to be water running to cool it off.  After that point, we decided to never run the dishwasher when we were not home since it seemed like a potential fire hazard.  The dishwasher has done this on at least 4-5 occasions.  It generally seems to happen on the pot and pan cycle so we try not to use that cycle.  We are currently searching for a replacement dishwasher since we have a young child and the potential for fire is not worth the risk to our son.  I just wanted to make sure that I reported the problem we were having in case others were experiencing similar problems.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning heating element, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Repeated failure of plastic clips holding control panel on GE JVM2070 microwave oven exposing electronics.

Repair required approximately four times in less than seven years.

GE acknowledged other cases reported to it that when the unit is installed properly over a standard range as it was designed to be and as in the instructions, the microwave oven has been subject to this failure, it has happened more often when the range is gas rather than electric and it has stopped making the microwave unit..
justification: The incident involves repeated failure of plastic clips exposing electronics, but no injury or death is mentioned. The issue is acknowledged by GE and occurs more often with gas ranges.

incident_description: We have a GE Profile Refrigerator.  The ICE MAKER BUCKET, part number WR29X10097, has plastic pieces that break off, and will dispense the plastic in your drink.  These small pieces of plastic can be lodged in your throat, or swallowed.  I am not certain how long its been doing this!  Two large pieces were dispensed and I was not sure where they came from.  Later, I noticed small pieces mixed in with the ice.  After a close inspection, I discovered the plastic near where the ice drops into your glass was breaking off.  I took pictures of the two large pieces and the location on the ice bucket where they were breaking off and sent them to GE.  They have not responded.  It has been a couple of weeks.
justification: Plastic pieces breaking off and potentially being ingested poses a risk of injury, though no injury is reported yet.

incident_description:
Keurig Coffee Brewer model # 65, 0100, 1753164
We smelled something burning and it turned out that the brewer was smoking and smelled like it was burning although there were no flames, the back of the unit was very hot; I immediately unplugged the unit from the wall outlet and called Keurig customer service.  I am waiting for a callback from them.
justification: The brewer was smoking and very hot, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no flames or injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Cuisinart Brew Central Coffeemaker, DCC-1200 Series. A few days ago after brewing a pot, I noticed (thankfully) that the coffee in the carafe was boiling vigorously. The unit was obviously overheating. I unplugged the unit.

This seems to be a serious fire hazard.
justification: The coffeemaker was overheating, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Cuisinart CUI DCC-1200BCH (or near equivilant)
2 year old Coffee maker caught fire after brewing and in the "warming pot" cycle.
Melt down, burned plastic, smoke, but no flame
justification: The coffee maker caught fire, causing meltdown and smoke, but no flame or injury occurred.

incident_description:
We have had Cuisinart automatic coffee maker for about 1 year.  When brewing a new pot of coffee I set it to "Auto On" and it will start at the set time and turn off at the set time.  When it has already
turned off and I want some of the remaining coffee, I turn it to "Brew", the heating plate comes on and reheats the coffee.

Yesterday morning when I got up the machine had already cut off at the set time, I wanted to reheat the coffee, so I turned it to "Brew" and pushed on.  I went to the bathroom and returned in about 30 seconds and the kitchen was full of smoke, coming from the coffee maker.  I unplugged
the machine and took it outside, where it continued to smoke for several minutes.  The Teflon coating on the heat plate was burned and peeling, the plastic of the machine, near the heating
plate was starting to melt.  Had I not returned to the kitchen as quickly as I did, this could have set
my house on fire.  The serial # 90603.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I own an LG Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, model LFD22860. Yesterday evening it caught on fire. We were alerted by the smells of foods cooking in the kitchen as well as burning smells. The plastic lightbulb housing/cover was destroyed... melted through and hanging down, melting and cooking the foods on the top shelf of my fridge. After some investigating I found the lights are not shutting off when the doors are completely closed as they are supposed to. I've had to remove the lights entirely. I will be contacting LG next.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, causing damage to the appliance and food, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The light in my LG Refrigerator stayed on while the doors were closed. This caused the lighting unit to melt.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light causing damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Anchor blue glass cake pan exploded. I have glass all over my kitchen and in my legs and feet. I took it out of a 350 degree oven and I saved the glass in case the company wants the information. I'm concerned that this could have been my children and could happen to someone else.
justification: The incident resulted in glass shards causing injuries to legs and feet, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: acprcall of sdc700 series coffee pots. our handle broke off, luckily with only 1/2 pot of hot coffee. I inspected the unit and believed this would not be an isolated breakage, then I found the recall online. I am following the instructions properly. it has been over a month and have not recd the replacement part. very upset about this. I would rather go buy another company product than have an unusable promise that simply puts me out. THIS COMPANY IS LUCKY NO ONE IN MY HOME - INCLUDING CHILDREN - GOT HURT WITH A KNOWN DANGEROUS PRODUCT.  my complaint is - repair promise not fulfilled.
justification: The handle broke off a coffee pot, but no one was injured. The recall indicates this is a known issue, making future occurrences likely.

incident_description:
The Kenmore Elite Oven 790.36703502 walls warp outwards over time - meaning the the middle shelf will slip off (the top and bottom shelves are fine, only the two middle shelf positions are affected). The net result is that any items placed on the middle shelves will fall spilling hot contents.

From a safety perspective it renders the oven useless.
justification: The oven's warping causes items to fall, posing a risk of spills but no direct injury mentioned.

incident_description: Kenmore Electric Range purchased 12/26/11 from Sears Windward Mall, Kaneohe, Hawaii. Inner glass door shattered while Pre-heating to 375 degrees.  Shards of glass are falling into oven and storage drawer below..
justification: The incident involved the shattering of the inner glass door, which poses a risk of injury but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore 795-77302600 light would not turn off melted the inside of the refridgerator the bulbs are extremly hot.
The bulbs did not go off when the door was shut started melting the upper part of the refridgerator and almost started a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light that caused melting and nearly started a fire, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while was using the oven at 375 for baking, approximately 20 mins later the broiler came on spontaneously by itself and started to burn the contents.  She was unable to use the control panel to power it off.  The circuit breaker was used to switch off power to the unit.

The circuit breaker was turned on again and the oven came on again with broil mode.

The retailer was contacted for service on 8/22/12.

8/23/12  The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that her model was not included in Release # 09-333.

The consumer feels that her electric range/oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
Coffee maker stopped working, upon removal of top cover I found evidence of a small fire having occurred at the top of the electrical terminal. Further disassembly revealed a burst heating element with ceramic falling out of the inner tube. 
This coffee maker  was provided to us by Bunn during the recall of the GR10-B models.
The date code on this unit is 120206.
justification: The coffee maker had a small fire and a burst heating element, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says she has had to turn it off, because the heating coil stays very hot.  She says that she has had to unplug it.  The heating coil looks defferent now than when it was originally purchased.  She says her kitchen countertop also gets hot to the touch when the dishwasher is on.      

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said that her model is not part of the recall.  She says that they are unwilling to help her.  

An appliance tech told her that the problem is with the heating coil.
justification: The heating coil staying very hot and affecting the countertop indicates a potential hazard, but there is no report of injury or death.

incident_description: I have been waiting an unreasonable amount of time to receive a replacement carafe under the recall of the Black and Decker (Applica Consumer Products) Spacemaker coffee pot recall.  This recall was posted by the CPSC on June 1, 2012 (Release #12-191).  My coffeemaker was model SDC750C, was included in the recall, and I executed the on-line recall form with Applica on June 7, 2012.  I still have not received a replacement carafe from them, nor has there been any correspondence from them on a status update (how much longer to receive, etc.).
justification: The incident involves a delay in receiving a recalled product, which is an operational issue but has not caused injury or death.

incident_description:
7/28/2012) The consumer stated that she was using her dishwasher on the light wash cycle. Approximately 30 minutes into the cycle the consumer heard an unusual noise coming from the unit. When she entered the kitchen she saw smoke coming from underneath the handle and from the side of the unit. The consumer tried to push the cancel button, but it did not function at the time. The dishwasher door was then opened, and fire sparks were shooting out of the dishwasher. She immediately shut the door and went to trip the breakers.

 
(7/30/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and they advised her that they would replace the control panel, but they did not have any available tech in her area at the time and to call the next business day.

 
(7/31/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and an appointment for scheduled for a technician from A&E to come out to her home.

 
(8/3/2012) The technician called her and advised her that he was coming out to repair her dishwasher, but it would be at her expense and not the manufacturer's. The consumer advised the tech to not come out to her home because she was not paying for the repairs.
 

(8/3/2012) The consumer contacted the manufacturer again and they advised her that her model was included in release#05-123, but her serial number did not match and they were not liable for the repairs.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks from the dishwasher, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On July 3rd 2012, I was making a cup of tea on stove top, when suddenly a million pieces of shattered glass pieces fell on the floor and my foot. I was shocked and did not know what happened. Later it dawned on me that the gas oven door had just exploded and shattered into pieces. Mind you the oven was not even turned on. After I stopped the bleeding on my foot; I went about cleaning up all the debris that had spread all over the kitchen. I was so shaken up and horrified that the door glass would fall off just like that when I was not even opening the oven door or even using the oven. What if the oven was on; would it have resulted in a catastrophe with temp at 400F?
I immediately called up Sears and told them about the incident. They said the warranty was up as I had purchased the range in Sept 2008. I explained to them I can understand if the oven stopped working or something else had happened, they could invoke the warranty clause. In this case it seemed like an inherent defect and a safety issue in the model. She tried connecting to a supervisor but once I got transferred the automated response said office was closed. I did take some pictures that I am attaching. As I knew July 4th was a national holiday, I refrained from calling Sears the next day still picking up glass pieces all around the kitchen.
On July 5th I again called Sears and the representative heard my incident and transferred me to some one else. I again repeated the story and explained there was an inherent defect in the glass. I told them I googled on internet if this had ever happened to anyone and voila there were at least 10 similar cases where the glass shattered when oven was not on. They told me I need to pay up if I want to get this fixed/or I should call frigidiare the manufacturer.
I was shocked with disbelief.  [REDACTED]I called again Sears but now the calls are getting me no where. There is no concern at the other end to understand the safety hazard the appliance poses.
All I am looking for them to acknowledge the product is defective and there should be recall of the glass door and them to replace my door at no cost to me. Hence, I am filing a complaint.
I cannot believe that a company of reputation like Sears would handle my situation in such a nonchalant manner.
justification: The incident involved an injury (bleeding foot) due to shattered oven glass, but no death or severe harm occurred.

incident_description: My husband was cooking dinner - a FABulous shrimp dish - when the glass pot lid EXPLODED! There were glass shards everywhere.  We are fortunate that he was not injured.  I would have thought that "tempered glass", from which this item is supposedly made, would have broken into rounded pieces.  As it was, these pea-sized pieces of glass were sharp and jagged.  The lid handle dropped into the food and the glass cover scattered all over the stove top, cabinets, and floor.  I will try to enclose a photo of the lid.  This cookware, the Emeril line by All Clad, is made in China. Since there seems to be a breakage issue with [REDACTED] glass containers made in China now also, it may be that they are using something other than silica or are somehow cutting manufacturing corners with other inferior or inappropriate materials or processes.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass pot lid causing a mess but no injuries, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is possible (3) given the description of the event and the mention of potential manufacturing issues.

incident_description: Microwave turned on and heated oven on its own. Unplugged, waited 30 minutes, plugged back in. Restarted again on its own. Concern over what if we had not been home.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on and heating on its own, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I have owned an Architect Series II KitchenAid gas oven/range for two years.  During the last year, I've noticed that the knobs on the range front attach to the range with plastic sleeves that started cracking to the point that they wouldn't turn the metal piece that turns on the gas.  I stopped using several of them, and before I  knew it I was down to one that worked.  This morning I tried to turn on a flame and the last one broke before the flame caught.  Gas started filling the room but I kept working at it until I finally got the flame to catch.  Then I decided I needed to turn it off, but I couldn't.  By the time I finally got the flame off, I was shaking because I could still smell gas so I called the gas company to come and be sure that the gas was really off.  He confirmed that it was ok, but now I won't be able to use the range again until I get new knobs.  My fear is that they will be just as cheaply made and it will begin all over again.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak due to broken knobs, posing a serious hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: smelled elecrical burning, looked around kitchen, then pulled out frig and took off back plate. When the compressor came on, an electrical fire would start and then fizzle out. Observed this happening several times. Unplugged frig.
justification: An electrical fire was observed but was contained and no injury occurred, fitting the criteria for an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I have a GE combo wall oven and microwave ( # JTP860F6ww) in which the door latch on the microwave doesn't work properly.  It doesn't  release the door for opening  the unit over the last few days. Normally opening the door will stop the microwave but since it has quit releasing reliability-- the unit will continue to run unless the touch panel is utilized to stop it.  The the door can we wiggled to get it released.  This requirement led to a potntial disaster when some food was smoking and the usual procedure was to hit the door release -- which I did to no avail.  After a moment of panic and as the food smoked more I finally remembered to use the touch pad.  I am positive that I averted a fire by less than a few seconds.

I see that earlier GE combo units were recalled for problems with the microwave door latch and it doesn't look like they totally fixed the problem.  I am a mechanical engineer and I find it incredible that this failure mode is allowed. If the parts for the door latch( required to make sure the unit does not run with the door open) are made so cheaply that they are the first part to fail then the cutoff should have still worked even if the door didn't open-- since I am sure that many if not most consumers use the door opening to regularly stop the microwave.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning microwave door latch that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher was running for about 20 to 30 minutes when it began spewing smoke from the door. We opened the door and the dishwasher continued o run, ignoring all button presses. We ran to the box and turned off the breaker. The entire floor was filled with a powerful white haze of melted plastic and electrical wire. There was a low sheen from the melting plastic buttons, indicating that there was a fire in the door. Afraid of possible electricity still present we placed a wet towell over the odor, opened the odors and windows and went outside. After 15 minutes, we checked and eventually removed the interior door panel, and exposed the control board. It was charred with burnt wires. There was burned plastic and the control pod was partially melted. The entire door was severely damaged. I later noticed lung irritation and believe I received several lungfuls of smoke from burning plastic
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and exposure to toxic smoke, resulting in lung irritation, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught on fire.
justification: The dishwasher catching fire is an incident with no reported injury, and such events are unlikely but possible.

incident_description: On August 26 we started our Kenmore dishwasher, purchased 12/2004, and left for about 1 1/2 hours.  When we got home there was smoke pouring from the right front side of the door and the house smelled like an electrical and plastic fire.  We opened the door and turned off the machine.  We called a technician who looked at it and said the circuit board was all burned up.  He has not gotten back to us about the specific cost to fix it, but thought it would be about $200.  We started looking online and saw that this was a major defect in Kenmore dishwashers and that Sears is not doing anything to address it.  When I contacted them they said they would give me a $65 discount towards a technician's service call or a $50 gift certificate.  This does not seem sufficient since it could have potentially caused much more damage.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred. The description suggests this is a known issue, making recurrence likely.

incident_description: The bottom, glass shelf to our Kenmore (model 106.64252401, Serial # ES2720356) exploded into thousands of pieces as it was being dried.  My wife had removed it from the refrigerator, washed and rinsed it in warm (not hot) water and was drying it when it burst apart yesterday.  The sink was filled with shards of glass, the counters and floor had glass pieces all over them; some pieces were 20 feet away having traveled over wall-to-wall carpet for the last 10 of those feet.  Fortunately, my wife had only a small cut on her hand and her glasses protected her eyes.  I can send pictures if you are interested.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut on the wife's hand, which qualifies as an injury, and the glass shelf exploding suggests a possible but not frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
dishwasher get overheated, bent the close cabinets. cycles do not stop, but go on over and over.
happens constanlty.
justification: The dishwasher overheating and damaging cabinets is an incident with no reported injury, but it occurs constantly.

incident_description: The dishwasher heating coil stayed on overnight and was extremely hot in the morning. Opening the door did not shut it off immediately. Closing and opening the door a second time got it to shut off. I looked up the model and serial number on the Maytag recall site and it said we were not part of the recall even though it acted exactly as described.
justification: The dishwasher heating coil malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue was resolved by user intervention.

incident_description: On 8/17/12, around 3:00pm, our Kenmore 790.36932901 oven was being used normally. It was set at 350 degrees for about 45 minutes. During this cooking time, when opening the handle on the door, the left side of the handle became detached. It looked as if it had come unscrewed. The oven was turned off after cooking. The next day, around 12:00pm, my husband, in an attempt to reattach the handle, was slowly opening the door, taking care not to pull on or put pressure on the glass. The outside oven door shattered, sending safety glass up onto the counter tops as far as 6 feet away. The oven was not in use at this time.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered oven door) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a "made for Walmart" coffeemaker, model 898682, serial #ES19586, Date Code 1144, inspector sticker QC(A)   at a local Walmart (store #1982) on 07/14/.  The following day I cleaned the machine and made coffee. I used the machine once a day, every day until 08/9/12.  Approximately 30 minutes after the completion of the brewing cycle, I heard 3 very loud snapping, sparking sounds, followed by a very distinct smell of burning vinyl plastic. Looking into the kitchen I saw a large plume of gray-white smoke emitting from the coffee maker. I immediately unplugged the machine and grabbed my fire extinguisher. I opened the top covers of the machine and gave it a good blast with the extinguisher, and experienced a pretty good-sized cloud of noxious fumes from the machine which even with the oven-hood fan on high and two floor fans caused me a miserable headache, nausea and stinging eyes.   I let the machine cool and removed the machine to another area. My apartment still smells of burnt-plastic that [REDACTED] has difficulty covering.  Needless to say, the machine is no longer operational.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffeemaker that emitted smoke and noxious fumes, causing headache, nausea, and stinging eyes, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My LG French door refrigerator 2 days ago had both lights not go on when I opened the door.  In addition, the external ambient temperature indicator tonight reflected a temperature of 97 degrees, although the room temperature was 75 degrees.  When I attempted to try and remove the plastic cover over the lights, it was so hot I couldn't touch it, even though the lights were off.  A little later I opened the doors again, and the lights came on. When I attempted to turn them off by pressing in both buttons, nothing happened.  A little later, the lights were off again, but still quite warm, although the door  had been closed.  The ambient temperature went down to 93 degrees where it remained.  The top of the refrigerator is quite warm as well.

I went online to see if I could find any information, and discovered a whole slew of comments and complaints about this same issue, stretching back several years. In some cases, the plastic light cover had melted sending noxious fumes out.  Repeated comments indicated LG was not responsive nor cooperative to consumer complaints.  One of the comments mentioned a class action.  When I searched that online, I found that indeed there was a settlement of the class action case involvinng the same issue this past March, 2012.

I have not been notified of the class action, nor of the potential problem, and LG has still not ordered a recall for this problem.  I registered my product, and I know LG is aware that I have the refrigerator as they send me a check each year because they misrepresented the energy costs indicated on it when I bought it.  

I find it appalling that something as serious as a potential fire hazard has not resulted in a recall, even after a class action settlement for this very same issue.  This is callous disregard for consumer safety.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator with potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death reported.

incident_description:
Sent to Breville ("ask us" "feedback" section) via e-mail Saturday 18 Aug 2012:

Just a note to say that my oven caught fire this morning. Shortly after turning it on to make toast, I heard a noise and saw a flame within the right side housing (the flame was visible through the vent).  The flame died out after about five seconds.
I unplugged the machine and moved it to a safe area. Smelled the typical acrid odor related to an electrical component burning. 
Thought you should know in case you have had other reports of same.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
Additional info for CPSC:   I guess the noise I heard could be described as a "poof."  I was only a couple of feet away and the noise immediately drew my attention to the oven. The flame was 1-2 inches tall at max. When I saw the flame, I opened the oven door to see if the flame was in the food chamber; it was not. By the time I closed the door and checked the vent again, the flame was dying out.

The only thing different about our use of the oven over the past weeks was to gently move it the day before the fire--but only far enough to clean beneath it and return it to its normal spot.
justification: The oven caught fire but the flame died out quickly and no injury occurred.

incident_description: At the rear of the stove, (top left backside, behind where the controls are located) the stove started sparking, and caught fire (no damage to surrounding area). The smell of electrical burn was strong.  The stove top is now non-operational due to the control unit not working. The unit has been unplugged and is no longer in use.
justification: The stove sparked and caught fire, but there was no damage to the surrounding area or injuries, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: The front right hand burner of our Frigidaire cooktop model FEC30S6ABF turned itself on after the knob was turned to the off position.  The unit had to be turned off at the breaker to get it to turn off.  I contacted Frigidaire and they informed me that my model was not included in the recall of 200,000 of their units in 2009 and unless I had an extended warranty they would not do anything.
justification: The incident caused a safety hazard but did not result in any injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not a rare occurrence but not frequent either.

incident_description: Frigidare slide in range, model FGES 3065 KWD, Ser. No NF1063 7665, manufactured in Canada has changed cooking temperature on front right burner twice without human intervention, causing the contents to burn.
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing property damage (burned contents) but no reported injury, warranting severity level 2. The recurrence suggests a possible likelihood.

incident_description:
The consumer says on 9-12-2007 the heating element did not want to turn off.  he says it is happening the left front burner.   

He called the retailer who sent out a technician who replaced the knob.  The same thing happened a few months later to the same knob.  The consumer says the heating elements stay on high even when set at low temperature.  He says also that the glass now is cracked. 

The product is having the same hazard as listed in Release # 09-333.  His model is not part of the recall. 

He never contacted the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating element and cracked glass, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Toaster failed and combusted inside.  Printed circuit actually combusted at take-off for quartz heating elements.  Reached temperatures high enough to melt lead.  Circuit board was actually burned and powdered.  Very dangerous considering that there are flamable bread crumbs inside.  Fortunately it was unplugged before any fire was started.  I am not alone. Please see:  http://www.fixya.com/support/t8782546-krups_sensotoast_deluxe_just_stopped
justification: The toaster combusted internally but was unplugged before any fire started, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Last night around 8pm, I started the Maytag dishwasher.  I get up this morning around 8am and went to get a cup of coffee and I noticed the dishwasher was warm. The two lights indicating that it was done were lit.   I'm thinking this isn't normal it should be done and cold by now.  I opened it up and a wall of HOT air hits me in the face, and the smell of plastic was overwhelming.  It melted my coffee cup on the top shelf, it ruined baby bottles on the top shelf too. We thru the breaker right away, and disconnected from electric.  Opened windows to get the smell out.  I have a baby in the house not even 2 weeks old.  I looked on the Maytag site to see if there were a recall for this.  There were for plastic tubs not mine a metal tub.  I called Maytag to find out what to do.  This was no avail.  They wanted to send someone out to check it out.  They want me to connect to power again.  NO WAY!!!  It dang near burnt my house down!!! I told them they can check it out on the patio cause that's where it's gonna be. We are going over to Homedepot and get another dishwasher and it isn't gonna be a Maytag.  This dishwasher is only 3 years old.  I've had it serviced like 5 times for different things.  It's a piece of [REDACTED].
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused significant property damage and posed a serious fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The oven glass door shattered for no apparent reason. The unit had been set at 400 degrees and was operating for about 30 minutes. The outside glass was fine. The model was Kitchen Aid KGRS206SS, purchased 5/16/12.
justification: The oven glass door shattered, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
We came home to find our Kitchenaid Microwave, Model KHMS155LSS-3, beeping and flashing an error code.  After several attempts to get it to stop (pressing the cancel button, various other buttons), it finally did.  Later, while we were out, the microwave went on by itself.  We found it running, flashing a message that said INCH and then various numbers (5, 7, 9).  We stopped it and cut the circuit to it.  The microwave was very hot.

Called Kitchenaid customer service, they are sending a repair person at no cost.  They seem to be aware of the problem, but it shouldn't be up to consumers to bring it to their attention in individual cases.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but did not cause injury, and the manufacturer is aware of the issue, indicating it's a known problem.

incident_description:
I recently badly injured my left lower leg when I accidentally hit the sharp edge of a lowered dishwasher door. My doctors told me that this was a common accident. i am now undergoing plastic surgery to repair my wound. On looking up the leg injury statistics: on "HOSPITAL-DATA.COM", I find that for the years 1997-2010, there were 16,164 dishwasher lower leg injuries.

I would suggest that these huge number of leg injuries caused by accidentally striking lowered kitchen dishwasher doors be reviewed by the Consumer Products Safety Commission in view of remediating this hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring plastic surgery, and statistics show it is a common occurrence.

incident_description: I have had my Chefmate BL-10 blender from Target for 2 years. Today the connection from the blade to the motor split apart and sent shards of plastic across my kitchen, as the recall stated could happen with this blender. I hadn't heard about the recall until this happened. Would you please distribute this recall again, so people don't get hurt? Fortunately the plastic shards didn't hit us, but they certainly could have.
justification: The incident involved the blender malfunctioning and sending shards of plastic across the kitchen, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
My wife woke up last week to a smell of burning plastic and noticed that our dishwasher had overheated and melted from the inside out.  She also burned herself on our granite counter top because of the excessive heat from the GE Dishwasher.

We contacted GE who sent out a technician who described to us that several other dishwashers (not our model) had been recalled for similar reasons.  The heated dry mechanism just continues to run long after it should causing excessive heat.  

Per the serviceman who came out 8/15/12 he stated "the relay stuck on the control board which made the heating element stay on."  He said it was similar to the recall but those were with plastic tubs (ours is stainless steel).  

Per the recall notes, "An electrical failure in the dishwasherÃÂs heating element can pose a fire hazard".

His notes and the recall notes are very similar and because of this I explained to GE that this model should also be recalled before something catastrophic happens to another household.  They explained that they could discount the dishwasher for me if I decide on a replacement but they would not replace it.  They also stated that they would not look into recalling this model because they had not been mandated by the CPSC.  

Due to this reason, I thought it was necessary to contact the CPSC directly and file a formal complaint.  I also spoke to [REDACTED], Compliance Officer with the CPSC, at [REDACTED] who also said to get  a formal complaint down so that a representative from CPSC can come by and pick up our dishwasher. This will allow the engineers to examine the appliance to determine if a recall is warranted.  [REDACTED] mentioned the next steps will be for a technician to call me to schedule a time to pick up the dishwasher.

I need assistance as soon as possible.  the Model number is CDW9380N00SS and this is NOT an isolated incident as I found something similar on your website.  See link to your website below.  Thanks in advance for your time. My number is [REDACTED].

http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1252265

Kind Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and potential fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as similar incidents have been reported but not widespread.

incident_description: GE dishwasher model # GDWF160R30SS tripped circuit breaker on friday 8/17. thought it was just an overloaded circuit. reset breaker and unplugged all other appliances ran dishwasher again and this time while i was in the kitchen i saw a puff of smoke and a spark come from the front of the dishwasher. this unit was bought in may 2011 no problem til now in light of the previous year models having a recall this looks like it could be more of the same. i have since unplugged this unit
justification: The incident involved a puff of smoke and a spark, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The self clean within an hour's time the outside of the oven reached 170 degrees. GE told repairman that the maximum exterior temperature should not exceed 116 degrees. 8/15/12; Repairman replaced the Fan Motor and nothing changed. It is a faulty oven. We purchased 6/23/12 and installed the oven 6/26/12 upon delivery as per instructions and we set upper oven to self clean as instructed [to burn off any chemicals/odors from manufacturer]. At one hour into the cycle I approached the unit to find the exterior extremely hot so I turned it off. It is a fire hazard. The exterior was far too hot to be safe. We then spent much time and effort trying to speak to an actual person to explain our safety concerns with this brand new oven. These attempts to actually speak to a person were to no avail. Finally, through the warranty repair automated phone system, Advanced Appliance Repair contacted me. We scheduled a "repair" time which was ridiculous because a brand new never used oven should not need repairs. The two repairmen set the oven to self clean and at the 45 minute mark they agreed that the outside of the oven reached an unsafe temperature. They then tested the cooling fan to make sure it was receiving sufficient power. It was. They were of the opinion that it's likely a design flaw.
justification: The oven's exterior reached unsafe temperatures, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I used to the oven to bake homemade pizzas.  The temp was set at 425 degrees.  Upon being on for 30 minutes the entire outside of the oven including the top, sides and front were too hot to touch.  The only place it was safe to touch was the handle to open the oven.  The oven being on heats up the entire level of the home and food takes 2x's longer to cook. The 'oven cycle' light is on all the time.

I have tried baking items at lower temps (350 degrees) and the same thing happens.  The entire outside of the oven gets dangerously hot to the touch.  I have had to refrain from using it when young children are in the house due to fear of one of them accidentally touching the outside and sustaining an injury.
justification: The oven gets dangerously hot to the touch, posing a burn risk, especially to children, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I brewed a pot of coffee like normal yesterday morning.  About an hour after the pot finished brewing, I heard a splattering noise in the kitchen. It sounded like eggs frying in a hot pan of butter.  I found that the sound was coming from my coffee maker.   The coffee was boiling!  Smoke was billowing out from the burner.  The smell was awful.  The on/off light was not on.  I switched the lever back and forth and the light wouldn't come on.  It looked off, but the boiling continued until I unplugged the coffee maker.  We will not use it again.  I hope you will recall the coffee maker before someones house burns down.  I am so thankful I was home when the incident happened.  This coffee maker has an auto shut off feature, but it failed and can't be trusted in the future.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing boiling and smoke, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker overheated and started smoking. Had brewed a pot of coffee and the carafe w/ coffee in it was on the warmer. Heard sizzling noises from the coffee maker, saw smoke/steam/fumes coming from the warmer plate area and smelled smoke or burning electrical component. Clock had shut-off. Unplugged unit immediately. Unit was 2 years + 2 months old. No prior problems. Researched unit on Amazon and discovered similar reports from other consumers. Then searched Cuisinart DCC-1200 fire hazard and found many other instances. Cuisinart claims their built-in safety feature automatically shuts-down the unit in case of overheating.
justification: The coffee maker overheated and produced smoke, but no injury occurred. Similar incidents reported by other consumers indicate this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description: We own a Cuisinart Burr Grind & Brew model DGB-700BC coffee maker. My husband is awake for work day around 4:30 a.m. and I normally sleep until approximately around the time my husband leaves, or shortly thereafter. The program was set to start the brew process at 4:30 a.m., as is customary in our home. My husband awakened me in a bit of a panic to say that he, needed my assistance to determine the root cause of the smell of electrical smoke in our kitchen. We quickly determined that it was the coffee pot, and observed a thin trial of white smoke arising from the lower back portion of the unit. The unit was immediately unplugged, never again to be plugged in; at least not in our home. I was unnerved to imagine how the story would be told if the unit over-heated after my husband left if I were not yet awake! After locating online similar stories from various other consumers, I called Cuisinart. The agent never requested the age of the unit nor purchase date, but I assume this is because we are on file with their company - the unit in question was the replacement of a warranted unit that failed less than two years before. I was advised that I'd receive the shipment in 7-10 business days. Outrageous!! Surely Cuisinart, if any company, can understand the plight of a rural-living, work-from-home, happily-caffeine-addicted customer who would have to travel approximately 10 miles one way for a commercially made cup of Joe! What's more, I would hope that my circumstances are not so usual and customary that they would have great difficulty meeting the demand of expediting a shipment to customers who experienced their unit over-heating. After failed efforts with the CSR, her supervisor promised 5-7 business days. It took a voice mail to the director of customer service (which was rapidly returned), and a call to a very competent professional in risk management who was able and willing to do the needful before I was assured that I should expect the package about 1 business day later. I was advised that Cuisinart coffee makers are equipped with 3 (I assume that 2 are for fault tolerance) thermal fuses that prevent the unit from actually catching fire, and to Cuisinart's credit, I do not find any reports of consumers observing flames after such an incident. However, it's worth noting that the unit does overheat enough to generate smoke. Also, sparing the minor details of difficulties such as receptionists who want to route you back to customer service or keep you on indefinite hold, or CSRs who direct the customer to corporate, but cannot provide the contact telephone number this experience was akin to a tooth extraction minus even local anesthesia. Compare this to my original warranty replacement was very easy and uneventful, and I'm left baffled for an explanation.
justification: The incident involved electrical smoke but no injury or fire, and similar incidents have been reported by other consumers.

incident_description: Making coffee with the Black and Decker Space Saver Coffee Pot ( SDC  740B )  Once the coffee was ready and I picked up the carafe to pour some coffee, the handle broke away from the glass carafe causing the hot coffee to pour all over the top of my counter and down between the stove and counter as well.  Fortunately,  I was not burned, but that is only  because I acted quickly and put the carafe down on the surface as fast as possible.  We were lucky we did not get injured, however, we had an all day cleaning event as we needed to remove the electric stove and cabinet from the wall for cleaning as hot coffee poured everywhere.
justification: The incident involved a broken carafe handle causing a spill, but no injuries occurred as the person acted quickly.

incident_description:
(7/6/2012) The consumer stated that the night before she set the oven to self-clean. When she went to open the door after it cooled down. She took a paper towel and cleaned up the residue from inside the oven. Without notice the glass door to the oven exploded and flew into her kitchen and living room. The consumer received a minor abrasion on one of her fingers.

-The consumer stated that she has been searching the Internet and came across many complaints with the brand and the same model.

(7/8/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and she spoke with the [REDACTED] (last name unknown) at [REDACTED]. Her case number is: [REDACTED]. She informed her that they would offer half towards everything including, labor, etc. They also scheduled for a technician to come out on 7/9/2012. [REDACTED] advised the consumer to call her as soon as the technician arrives.

(7/9/2012) The technician came out and inspected the oven. The tech noted that the glass may have been weakened, cracked or from using the cleaner. They both tried calling [REDACTED] as instructed per her request, but they got no answer. The technician placed an order for a replacement glass door.

Note: The consumer feels that the oven is a safety hazard and the design should be changed. She feels that if she had the oven door upward she would have gotten glass in her face. The consumer also wants the manufacturer to take full responsibility for the costs and not just offer half.

I was wiping ashes from the oven floor. P cleaning 
11:15 AM  Oven door (glass) exploded in kitchen blowing glass particles into living room.  Big explosion blew over and around me.  Kitchen floor covered with glass.

12:15P  Called [REDACTED] Sears.  They gave me a number to call for repair.  (1-800-469-4663)  They wanted me to pay for call, labor, and parts.

Cleaned up mess!

Called CEO/President (@ 1-847-286-8371) of Sears.  Got a recording.  They asked me to leave a message which I did and they would call me back within the hr.  Waited for about 1-1/2 for call that didnÃÂt happen.  Called again with no results or returned calls.  Son-in-law came and took pictures.
 
6:45P  No return call at all.

July 29th 2012
RE:  Oven door exploding

CPO called back and stated that they pay for half of the oven repair which came to 184.50 of $368.00.  I could see no other way for repair and so I accepted.  Personally I felt that Sears should have paid 100%.

Repair was made and I am holding my breath hoping this will not happen again.

Thank you.
[REDACTED]
justification: The consumer received a minor abrasion from the exploding oven door, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident appears to be part of a pattern with the same model, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: The electronic control panel started on fire and may have caused a house fire if I was not in the kitchen at the time. The oven was on , but all of the burners were off.  There were sparks, smoke and flames coming from the rear of the control assembly panel. I have already reported this to Sears and they claimed that there is no history of this problem with this model.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and flames but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was contained without causing a house fire.

incident_description: Own a kenmore 790.9611340A glass stove top and oven which is in a condo I own and the tenants report the same issue that has been reported regarding other kenmore and [REDACTED] models.  the heating element will not shut off even though the knob is in the off position.
justification: The heating element not shutting off poses a risk of overheating or fire, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I am shocked at GE reportting only 15 fires. I had major smoke with this appliance on May 6, 2012 and i lucky wife and i with a guest came home.  Wrote to them. got a response to write to erxxxxxx@GE.com.  never heard from again.  Used same [REDACTED] to intall last 3. 
 I have had GE for 40 years. never never  again. Took two weeks to get smell out of house

To offera $200 rebate is a insult. they are so wrong.  Obviously  I bought a new dishwasher that week for $1800-not a GE. i want cash trebate, not product
justification: The incident involved major smoke but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high given the user's personal experience and dissatisfaction.

incident_description:
At 2:00 am I was awakened by the smoke alarm in my hallway.  I smelled acrid smoke.  I searched for the source and found charcoal gray smoke coming from the top of my dishwasher, literally rolling out into the kitchen, dining room and living room. I hesitated opening the door to the dishwasher, fearing a flash fire, but I had to determine where the smoke was originating from.

The electronic panel on the inside of the door had been burning due to a short circuit.  It burned all of the computer elements, wiring, and the back plastic panel.  Opening the door shut off the electricity to the control panel.  The underside of my kitchen cabinet was on fire and I used a fire extinguisher from under my kitchen sink to put out the fire.

I have filed a complaint with Electrolux, the maker of my Frigidaire  dishwasher, which was purchased in 2003.  An inspector came and took pictures of the damage, but I have heard nothing in three months from Electrolux.  Under implied warranty, I believe the company is responsible for the cost of replacing the dishwasher ($426), and needs to replace my kitchen counter as well
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a short circuit in the dishwasher, which was extinguished without injury or death.

incident_description:
BonJour 2-Quart Stainless Steel Tea Kettle with Copper Bottom was left on the stove too long.  Link to the model on Amazon.  Our purchase was from a local kitchen supply store.

http://www.amazon.com/BonJour-2-Quart-Stainless-Kettle-Copper/dp/B002LGFF6U/ref=cm_rdp_product_img
This model kettle does not have any whistle and the water boiled all out.  The bottom overheated and the inside layer (lead? Tin?) portion of the bottom, between the copper cladding and the steel body and inside bottom had melted.  The copper cladding failed when the over heated kettle was moved and spilled out liguid metal onto the stovetop and splashed onto the floor near the stove.  The person who moved the overheated kettle also got some second degree burns on the bottom of a couple of toes as they moved away and stepped on a metal splashing on the floor.  

The stove and the burner had quenched metal on various portions, but did not appear to suffer any real damage.  The linoleum floor has some scorched marks where the metal splashed.  

The concern here is the low temp metals used as a heat sink in the base of the kettle that liquified with just stove top temperatures.  Combined with the rupture of the copper cladding, this created a very hazardous situation.   There was no indication of this other lower melting point metals beyond the steel and copper components on the literature we had for this item.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific conditions required for the kettle to overheat and fail in this manner.

incident_description: Kitchenaid dishwasher slightly more than 1 year old began emitting burning smell as it was running. Smell was worse when we stopped it and opened door.
justification: The dishwasher emitted a burning smell, indicating a potential malfunction, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that on 07/16/2012 he heard a loud sound. The consumer stated that he was sitting approximately 12ÃÂ away from where the microwave was located. He stated that he looked back and noticed that the towel that was on top of the microwave was burning. The consumer stated that the fire seemed to have started from the back of the microwave. The consumer stated that he had not used it that day and it was not in use when he heard the loud sound. 

The consumer stated that he can estimate the flame on the towel went up approximately 4ÃÂ high. He stated that he noticed discoloration on the back of the microwave, burnt marks on the back tile wall of the kitchen and the burnt towel. 

The consumer stated that he grabbed the towel and he placed it in the sink to put the flames out. The consumer stated that he unplugged the microwave. 

The consumer stated that he was not injured. 

The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they requested for him to mail the microwave back to the firm. He stated that the representative informed him that once he mailed it to the firm; they would evaluate and get back to him. 

The consumer stated that he decided to take the product back to the retailer and they exchanged the microwave for him. 

The consumer stated that this product should be investigated for the fire hazard that it poses to the consumer.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described event but no indication of frequency.

incident_description:
While roasting some potatoes, the left back burner on my Frigidaire free standing electric range turned itself on high. After I noticed this, I tried to turn the burner off, but the burner would come back on at full heat. The digital display began to display numbers that did not match the knob settings (for instance when I turned the knob to off, the display read high, and when I turned the knob to High, it read 1.2).  The tap would flicker "HE" like it was going to turn off, but would immediately turn back on within a minute. The only way we could get the tap off was to disengage the wiring that goes to this particular burner. I researched the issue and discovered that there was a recall on this model of stove, but that the recall did not extend to my serial number. The recall ended with serial numbers VF831XXXXX, and my serial was VF91058106. My stove exhibited the same problems as the recalled stoves (original recall October 2010), so I called Frigidaire to see if there was anything they could do. I was told that since my serial number was not included in the recall, there was nothing they could do, even though the technician acknowledged my stove had the same issue as the recall. 
Frigidaire Glass Top Free Standing Electric Range (self-cleaning oven)
Model: FEFLZ87GC D
Serial: VF91058106
This could have started a fire or injured my small children (ages 2 and 4). I now have a stove with only 3 burners working (since we disconnected the control in the back panel), but I am afraid to use this stove. According to the recall, the oven is not properly vented, and moisture can enter the control panel for the back burners causing them to spontaneously heat and turn on. I believe this is what happened because steam was exiting from the back of the stove causing condensation in the left burner control knob and display. The design of the oven itself is flawed. Frigidaire refuses to fix the problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could have caused injury or fire, but no actual harm occurred. The issue is likely to recur given the acknowledged design flaw and similar past recalls.

incident_description:
We have an 8 year old, side-by-side refrigerator (Model#ED5PHEXMB00). It started making a crackling/popping noise and then white/gray smoke began to come out from behind and underneath the refrigerator. We pulled it away from the wall and unplugged it. 

We contacted Whirlpool the same day and they were very helpful. The service technicians came out the next morning and determined that the relay to the compressor burned out and melted parts into the compressor. The technician indicated that it probably would not have caught on fire since it is designed to burn out, melt, and simply stop working, but he said there is really no guarantee of that. Whirlpool covered all costs for the service call and repairs, which totaled almost $700.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was promptly addressed.

incident_description: microwave stopped heating.  I have an extended warranty and called for service.  At first they thought it was the magnatron tube that was bad but when they took it off the wall and looked inside they realized there were burn marks where the unit was arcing on the inside and scorching the inside of unit.  This is the 2nd unit I have had that GE will have to replace for the same problem.  The first model # was jjvm1850dm2bb.   I bought new appliances which were delivered 11/30/07 but weren't installed until 2/08 because my kitchen renovation hadn't been completed.  The microwave worked but had this loud motor sound on and off.  It completely failed on the beginning of June 2009 and service came out on 6/12/09 and looked at it and said "internal damage, not repairable, no visible outside damage".  GE agreed to a replacement (same make and model) and it was delivered to my home and installed on 6/30/09.  GE offered me a manufacturers warranty extension on the new unit from the period of 7/1/2009 thru 1/01/2011.  On August 16, 2012 the micro stopped heating, I called for service and on 8/17/12 Ayres appl., came out and said they would order a magnatron tube they were sure that was the reason it wasn't heating.  Part came in and on 8/21/12 they removed micro from wall and took off cover and noticed burn marks inside back of micro and told me microwave is not repairable.  They have called the extended warranty company to see how to handle this.  I am scared to death of this microwave.  I have read volumes of reports of GE microwaves catching fire when in use and when no one is using them.  Please do something about this.
justification: The microwave exhibited internal damage and burn marks, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a fire which was caused by one of the recalled GE dishwashers.  The fire occurred on 03/16/2011, at my parent's home (address below).

	Just after completion of the dry cycle, my 86 year old mother opened the dishwasher door to remove the dishes and flames shot out of the interior of the dishwasher. My mother described the fire as being similar to what she (and I) had experienced in the past when the heating element in the oven burned through and set the oven on fire. 

	The fire rapidly spread to the adjacent cabinets and caused significant damage before my 90 year old father was able to halt its spread with a fire extinguisher. Firefighters, whose station is about 2 minutes from their home, arrived shortly thereafter, put the fire out, and cleared out the smoke. 

	Fortunately, no one was physically injured. The only reason that my motherÃÂs face and arms were not burned is that she was standing to the side of the dishwasher, rather than in front of it, as most people would have been. She had a shoulder problem which made it easier for her to open the dishwasher door from the side. Both of my parents are in ill health and have heart conditions. Imagine what could have happened if the fire had occurred after they went to bed, or if the fire department had not been close by.  

	Although there were no physical injuries, the psychological injury was significant because of my motherÃÂs unique circumstances. My mother is a survivor of the largest and final battle of WWII in Europe, the Battle of Berlin, which ended with HitlerÃÂs suicide and German surrender. Over the course of 16 days, much of the city of over 4 million people was leveled by bombs and fire. Approximately 20,000 civilians and 180,000 troops were killed in that single battle, and more than 1 million left homeless. Needless to say, she is terrified of fire. Two days after the fire she had a stroke. She believes that stress related to the fire caused her stroke. She had horrible nightmares and flashbacks to the battle for months. 

	The fire was investigated by [REDACTED], [REDACTED], Department of Fire and Emergency Services, Town of Hamden, CT. His phone # is [REDACTED].

	The damage was covered by my parentsÃÂ insurance company, The Hartford. The claim number is [REDACTED]. The insurance company paid out about $13,000 in damages. A detailed list of the damages is attached to this report.
justification: The incident caused significant psychological injury and stress leading to a stroke, though no physical injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a 2005 Kenmore Elite slide in range.  I opened the oven door to take a loaf of garlic bread out and the oven racks collapsed to the bottom of the oven.  This is extremely hazerdous - and has high potential for serious burns.

I contacted Sears but could not reach Kenmore directly.   When I pursued the issue with Sears Customer Care they did offer to cover the cost of a service visit to diagnose the problem and connected me with the CPSC.  The issue is that the oven liner has warped from heat.  This is not an isolated incident and identical situations have been reported to the CPSC and on mysears.com.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with high potential for serious burns, and similar incidents have been reported, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
This is in regard to a "BODUM" vacuum maker, the model being a "SANTOS" model. 
This model is currently marketed under the "PEBO" designation.
It is a glass model of the metal type of vacuum makers popular during the 30's, 40's
and 50's designed for range top use.
The top or funnel, as is the lower unit, is made of high temperature glass.The lower unit 
holds the finished coffee after brewing. The lower unit has a narrow collar in which
the upper unit fits. The lower unit has a black plastic handle aroung its filler neck.
The owners manual does not have any prohibitions against heating the unit in a 
microwave oven. It is because of this, I decided to heat clean water in the lower
unit for the purpose of cleaning the unit.
I filled the lower unit, or carafe, to a water level of 10mm below the filler neck top.
I placed the unit in the microwave oven, set the timer for four (4) minutes and 
observed the water being heated , the purpose being to prevent the water from
boilling over the filler neck.
As I was watching the unit, I heard a muffled "pop". I immediately shut of the
oven. I thought the glass might have cracked. Using oven mitts, I carefully removed
the carafe. There did not to be any indication of the glass being damaged!
Removing the carafe, I did notice a stream of hardened plastic coming from a
small hole, approx. 5mm, dia. in the handles plastic collar , located along the
horizontal line of the handle collar.
The hole did not appear to go all the way thru the collar.
There two things that could caused this to happen.
1. The collar had an implanted RFID chip. (not likely though)
2. A small piece of  a metal substance contaminated the plastic "shot" during molding.
I am concerned about the integrity of the handle as hot liquids are involved.
If it will be of assistance to you, I can remit images of the unit.
justification: The incident involved a small plastic handle damage with no injury or glass breakage, but potential risk for hot liquid handling.

The consumer says that his model is doing the same thing as listed in the recall 09-333 but is not included.  He contacted the manufacturer on 7/6/12 who is unwilling to assist him due to the unit being four years old. 
 
The consumer says that the burner stays lit even when trying to turn it off.  His wife says that the burner will go down and get bright again.  He says if he spins the knob around and get it to turn off.  The consumer says this is happening to the left and right front burners only.
justification: The burner staying lit poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage is reported.

incident_description:
Thursday, July 12th, 2012 caller's two yr old electric smooth range top exploded in an audible fireworks type of explosion.

No fire or sparks but the "boom" sound it made reminded caller of fireworks.

She had food on the right front set to low temperature, had her one year old grandson in her arms while she was stirring the pot but had placed him in his highchair.

The only burner lit was this right front burner, however the left front burner blew up with the extremely loud noise.

Glass flew everywhere, going approximately two feet out from the stove, in front of the stove.

All glass pieces were very, very small with the exception of those still on the range and those were a bit larger.

Caller and husband contacted the manufacturer July 13th, 2012 via email and received response with list of options for calls but seemed totally detached from the situation.

Caller's will be attaching pictures to their copy of the report.

Food was ruined, caller is asking that her range be inspected and replaced at manufacturer expense with different model but at same value of $1400 paid for this one.
.
justification: No injuries reported, but the explosion caused property damage and posed a potential hazard.

incident_description:
The caller stated that she had to replace her electric smooth top range glass 3 times because it cracked.  The crack is large and she unable to use the range when this occurs.  She stated that she researched the unit online and found out that there was a recall for other models in release# 09-333.  She feels that she is experiencing similar problems with the unit, such as "heat to different temperatures than selected". 

6/14/12 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised to contact appliance repair to resolve the issue.  She stated that this incident had been occurring for the past 3 months.

The caller feels that the range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves repeated cracking of the range glass and operational issues, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: While our dishwasher (Whirlpool Model GU1200XTLQ1, serial number FP0713650) was running it started emitting strong electrical smell, and some black smoke from the control panel at the top of door.  We turned off the circuit breaker. I removed the control panel cover to find the circuit board, components, and connectors were burned, and in several places, melted.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and showing signs of electrical damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Oven Door really hot. Very unsafe to touch unlike other model's out there.
Other GE oven doors are not as hot as this unit.  If children are around can burn hands on the oven door.  I personally  burned my hand just bumping the door while opening it.
Unit is a GE JBS55D M4BB
