incident_description:
The consumer stated that during the night the dishwashers heating element turn on by itself and her husband smelled a plastic burning odor. The consumer stated that he went into the kitchen and when he touched the counter top above the dishwasher it was extremely hot. 

The consumer stated that her husband shut off the circuit breaker, opened the dishwasher door, and removed the dishwasher from underneath the counter top. 
She stated that the dishwasher racks on the inside of the dishwasher had melted. The consumer stated that also some of the dishes inside were damaged. 

The consumer stated that there were no damages to her home structure.

The consumer stated that no one was injured.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they sent out a technician to service the dishwasher. The technician went to her home 7/18/2012 and he informed the consumer that the control panel had a shortage causing it to turn on by itself.  The consumer stated that they did not offer any other remedy for the situation. 

The consumer stated that the technician informed her that the dishwasher could no longer be repaired. 
The consumer believes that the manufacturer has not informed their consumers properly that this problem with their dishwashers exists. The consumer stated that she believes that this product should be investigated for the fire hazard that it poses to the consumer.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted racks, damaged dishes) but no injuries or structural damage, warranting a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was caused by a control panel short, a known but not widespread defect.

incident_description: twice now the heat dry cycle of our dishwasher has stuck on and created a very hot counter top to the point that you couldn't touch the granite surface. Appears to me to be a fire danger.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the dishwasher's heat dry cycle causing extremely hot surfaces, posing a potential fire hazard but no injury or death.

incident_description: I ran my GE dishwasher (model number PDW9980N00SS )in the morning and about 4:30pm I started to smell plastic burning. Upon opening the dishwasher with my infant son in my arms,a cloud  of smoke poured out and irritated my eyes. I closed the dishwasher and turned off the power source.  The fire department looked at it and told me plastic had melted onto the heating element.  After they left my husband took a closer look at it and discovered the wheels, and basket had started to melt.  We called GE and they sent a technician out the next day. The technician said the control panel malfunction and the heating element never turned off. He then proceeded to tell me it was no longer under warranty and not part of the recall. I paid $329.93 to have it repaired.  I contacted GE again to inquire more about the recall and after getting the runaround from two representives, getting disconnected, and being on hold for a total of three hours, I final spoke with a supervisor and she refunded me my money. She said that my dishwasher model is under a program that they are looking into but is not part of the recall.  She also stated that even thought the heating element didn't turn off it eventually would have and wouldn't  of caught on fire.  I feel that the product is unsafe and she looked into further.
justification: The incident involved smoke and eye irritation but no serious injury, and the fire department confirmed no fire occurred.

incident_description: GE Monogram Dishwasher from about 2007 or 2008.  Two problems:  1) when door is opened, it begins to fill up with water; this has gotten progressively worse over time, and 2) recently, the heating element did not shut off after the dishwasher cycle should have ended.  There is apparently a recall of GE Dishwashers that matches the time I bought mine, but my model is not covered; however, the reason for the recall and my problem with the heating element seem similar.
justification: The dishwasher has malfunctions (water filling when door opens and heating element not shutting off) but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says the oven does not sense the internal temperature.  She says the unit continues to heat until it catches the food on fire.  The consumer says the heat sensor has already been replaced twice.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer last week who only offered to replace the heat sensor again.  She says she does not feel comfortable with just another replacement of the same part since this has already occurred now 3 times.

Addendem:  Since the consumer originally spoke with our office, a GE repairman discovered a crimped and frayed temperature probe in the oven, which he replaced.  However the oven would then not heat.  So they want to replace another part.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven that could potentially cause a fire, but there is no mention of actual injury or death.

incident_description: The dishwasher was in use when , it tripped the fuse in the fuse box, I had to go out and put on the fuse box, when I put the dish washer on again, it tripped the fuse and have therefore not been able to use the dish washer again. After research, I called the manufacturer in early June and they offered to send out a service call for a $100.00 to see what is going on,  then fixing it would cost extra, after the service call if I did not want to fix it for the additional cost( labor and parts) then I would get a $100.00 for
justification: The incident involves a dishwasher tripping the fuse, causing inconvenience but no injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer says she has been smelling a burning smell for about a week.  Friday, she was outside on the porch.  She came in when again she smelled the burning smell.  She turned her oven to pre heat.  She instantly heard a noise.  She says it caught on fire inside the oven.  The consumer shut off the circuit breaker.   She says that the stove, door and grates are all burned.

The repairman from GE came out today and saw the wiring harness burned, and the insulation behind it.  They want to repair the unit.  She is scared to use it.  The consumer says that if she were not home it would have caught her house on fire.  

She says her throat is still sore from inhaling all the smoke.  The consumer does not want the stove anymore.  The technician also said the unit is not repairable but the manufacturer is stating that only a repair needs to be done.
justification: The consumer suffered a sore throat from smoke inhalation (injury), and the incident could have led to a house fire if not addressed.

incident_description:
I received the new T disc holder because my coffee machine was affected by the recall of the disc holder. The new holder does absolutely nothing to fix the described problem. My coffee maker spilled ground coffee and hot water before and does so after I installed the new part. 
I feel like this fix is just a pacifier for consumers but not a fix to a bad product. I still believe that the machine is dangerous and that I could get burned from it. I always stay 2 feet away from it when I am making coffee. 
I called Bosch and informed them about the problem but they don't seem to care and don't want to take care of my issue. 
It is unfortunate that I have to go this route but a dangerous product needs to come off the market. 
I wish I could just return the machine and buy a different coffee maker.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning product causing spills but no reported injury, with the user expressing concern about potential burns.

incident_description: Coffee maker overheated. Liquid in pot began boiling, smoke emitted from back of machine. Odor indicating electrical fire or smoldering was detected. Power switch apparently inoperative. Power indicator light not functioning.
justification: The coffee maker overheated and emitted smoke, indicating a potential electrical issue, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My wife made a small pot of coffee successfully but before removing pot to fill cup was confronted with tremendous odor as though something was burning and/or melting. Didn't recognize source immediately but became bad enough to alarm children upstairs. Upon realizing coffee making was to blame, unplugged unit and burned hand trying to move off counter. Pot holder needed to remove unit outdoors. Very surprised counter top didn't melt. Warming plate beneath carafe was clearly so hot as to  melt unit's internals. Second unit to suffer similar fate. Good unit but not worth potential grievous injury.
Unit involved is Cuisinart programmable drip coffee maker perhaps 3 years old.  Whether it be 3 months or 5 years, I don't believe there ought be a time limit attached to consumer safety.
justification: The incident resulted in a burned hand and potential for grievous injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the description of a second unit failing similarly.

incident_description: This morning I was brewing coffee in our Cuisinart DCC1200.  It started gurgling, the warmer plate got extremely hot, the power light went off, there was a strong electrical smell.  I've now read that this is not an isolated experience with this product.  It obviously could have burned our house down.

incident_description:
I have the Cuisinart DCC 1200 in Black & Chrome, purchased at Macy's in 2010.  I programmed the coffee maker to go off at 6:30 a.m.  I was in the kitchen making breakfast at 7:20 when I started to smell something weird & then heard some popping & crackling noises.  Upon looking around, I noticed the smoke coming from the coffee maker!  I unplugged it quickly and took it into the garage before it woke up my 4 children from the smoke alarm and burned my hand in the process.

My concern is that if I hadn't been awake yet, the potential for a fire could have caused more serious damage, including being life threatening.

Upon googling this, I found numerous complaints about this particular model from Cuisinart and it's disheartening to know that this is something that's a known problem yet still being sold.  I have left a message at Cuisinart and have no idea what their recourse is but I'm concerned about purchasing another one of their products.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burned hand) and potential for more severe outcomes, justifying a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple complaints about the same model.

incident_description: On a number of occasions, the refrigerator light stays on when the doors are closed causing the light housing to overheat and burn/melt.
justification: The refrigerator light staying on causes overheating and melting, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
My family was in the living room watching TV when we heard a loud pop and then glass shattering and crashing to the floor.  I went into the kitchen to find that the outer glass on my oven door had shattered into a million pieces.  It had been two hours since I had used the stove top while cooking dinner and OVER A MONTH since I had used the oven.  It is hot here in the summer and we cook on the grill rather than turn the oven on.  The cracking and falling glass continued for a few minutes.  Some of the glass flew about 4 feet, colliding with the cabinets on the other side of the kitchen.  Luckily no one was in there.  We were shocked that this could happen.  

When I called Sears the next morning, I spoke with two different operators, neither of whom seemed to be surprised that this had happened.  They offered a brief apology and then proceeded to set up the repair service.  They did ask if the oven was hot and I explained that it had not been used in over a month, but also that my husband had checked the inside and it was at room temperature.  I have a protection agreement on my range because it is an induction cooktop and that is new technology.  Sears ordered new glass for the door and set up an appointment for a technician to come in a week to install it at no cost to us.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 2 as it is not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
(7/15/2012) The consumer stated, while in the kitchen he heard something fell. When he turned around to look he noticed that the door handle to the oven had fallen off. He walked over and inspected the handle. The glass door then shattered unexpectedly. The consumer's wife received minor injury to the bottom of her foot when she accidently stepped on a piece of the broken glass. The wound was minor and treated at home.

 

(7/16/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and they informed him that the warranty expired in 2011. They were not going to assist him unless he paid for a technician to come out and inspect the unit. The consumer declined the offer.

 

(7/16/2012) The retailer was later contacted and they were only offering to sell him an extended warranty. He was transferred to the safety department and the Rep. (name unknown) disconnected the call.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury to the consumer's wife, treated at home, which fits severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with faulty appliances.

incident_description: As I went to open our Black and Decker chest freezer, I noticed that everything was thawed out. So I went and checked the setting turned it all the way up to 7 the highest it can go and it never turned on. This freezer is not even two years old yet and has only been moved from store to our home. We went and checked by the grate on the side you could smell the smoke and it was very hot. I have never had this happen to us before but with a family of 6 this was very economical for our family and now we dont know what to do since the freezer was filled with meat and other food. I unplugged the freezer and we have not tried to plug itback in since the smoke and the heat came from the side of it.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidaire professional stove about a year
and a half. Since then, the stove top has been switching on extemporaneously and
when I try to cut it off, it doesn't cut off, resulting in me unplugging the stove. I am
very frightened about the problem because this occured once when I was sleep and
coincidently, I could hear the tick of it's start-up and was able to cut it off before
anyone was harmed.

After this incident, I researched and realized that others were having the same
problem and that the product was recalled. I immediately called the Recall Hotline
and they sent a replacement part quickly. The part was operable until about 1 week
ago (roughly 1 month after the recall item was repaired). I was resting again and
heard the same start-up tick. I called the Recall Hotline again and the product was
replaced yet another time. While speaking with the service technician, he advised
me that there is an accessory piece that surrounds the stovetop to reduct the
amount of moisture to the motherboard. He recommended this to me and said it
may resolve the issue, however, I was responsible for the payment. I called the
Recall Hotline and spoke with [REDACTED], who advised me that I will have to purchase
the accessory part because it was not covered. She was very argumentative and
indicated that Frigidaire was indeed not responsible for the part.

I know the Electrolux Group prides itself on having innovative and quality products in
order to maintain its sustainability goals globally. I am emailing because I purchased
the stovetop brand new not purchasing any accessory parts, however, for the
product to be opearble it seems to be required. If this is the case, then the part
should not be an accessory, but a requirement and why do I now have to pay the
accessory part so that I don't have a potential fire. I am an insurance underwriter
and I am well aware of liability and potential hazards that could evolve and my
concern is why is your company not proactive in making sure the parts are operable
with no additional hazards. As a pregnant woman, I am very concerned about this
item because I am not always going to be around when the stove spontaneously
cuts on. My husband is in the military and is out a lot to sea, so I am not able to
manage the spontaneous cut-ons of the stove and take care of a newborn baby--
worse case scenario is if a fire starts when I am not at home. I would just like to
have an operable stove without paying out of pocket any more money that I have
already paid for this stove--upwards of $160--and if it requires contacting the
needed sources to looking into this, then I will do everything possible to maintain a
safe environment in the home. I would like to resolve this matter as soon as
possible, so if you have any options for this matter, please contact me.

Thank you for your time.
justification: The stove's spontaneous activation poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: On August 17, 2012 the Woodbridge Fire Department was dispatch to to below address for a reported stove fire. The occupant of said apartment stated she was cooking frozen pizza when she discovered smoke and a smell of something burning coming from the unit. Upon investigation the fire department found the insulation of the oven was burning. The oven was a Avanti serial number A5685120017119000071 electric model with no other identifiers on the unit. I turned everything off and  noticed the heating element had broke off in two places.  I am glad I noticed this or it could have caused a major house fire. incident_description:
The consumer stated that she came in her home and noticed a burning odor in her home. She stated that she looked around to see what was burning and found that the smell was stronger around her freezer box.  The consumer stated that she turned off the the whole icebox (it is a side by side).

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer for assistance and they referred her to a technician. She stated the technician and he came to her home on 07/09/2012. The technician informed the consumer that the manufacturer informed him that the insulation that was installed inside the freezer box melts when it gets to a certain temperature.  The technician confirmed that the insulation had melted and that the burning odor was being emitted by the insulation. 

She stated that the technician informed her to keep the freezer on because he needed it for it to be on for him to replace a part. 

The consumer stated that she was concern because she was unaware of what chemicals were being emitted by the insulation. The consumer was concern because she was not aware whether the chemicals could be toxic to her and her children.

My Frigidaire cooktop Model FEC30S6ABF (Serial #: NF81309940) has a manufacturer date of March 2008 on the bottom.  One of the burners does not turn off.  I can't get anyone from the company to call me back to handle this.

But upon closer inspection realized the coffeemaker was actually smoking and emitting the smell of melting plastic. I unplugged the machine immediately.

Dear Sirs,
I have a KitcheAid Diishwasher purchased approx. July 2004. Over this past weekend, there was significant amounts of smoke pouring out of the consol, during the drying cycle.
Fortunately, I was home, as I was just about to leave when my 6 year old son saw te smoke.
immediately I shut oof teh dishwasher with the wall switch.

KitchenAid Dishwasher

incident_description:
We started our dishwasher this morning, like we would any other time.  I decided to work from home today and thankfully I did.  As I passed near the kitchen, I noticed an odd smell, which burned my eyes.  I noticed the odor was coming from our dishwasher.  I went to open the dishwasher and immediately noticed that the area near the dishwasher was extremely warm and the door itself was hot to the touch.  Once open, the fumes of burning plastic screamed out of the dishwasher along with a wall of heat.  I ran to shut the break off at the panel and turned the wall switch off as well.  

All my plastic cups had melted as well as some parts on the dishwasher.  This is extremely upsetting as a neighbor in our development had recently offered the residents a GE Dishwasher recall website for Dishwasher heating element failures which resulted in some fires.

http://www.geappliances.com/products/recall/dishwasher_2012/

incident_description:
I have a broiler/convection/toaster oven from Cuisinart that sits on a counter top. The style number is TOB-195. It is an expensive all stainless steel unit. It is seemingly a nice oven, but there is a defect in the design that can prove to be EXTREMELY dangerous, especially to CHILDREN. The elements of the oven are at the top of the unit and very close to the exterior steel casing. There does not seem to be any insulation between the steel and the elements, and if there is - it does not work as it is insufficient. As a result the outside of the unit gets extremely hot when in use to the point that it cannot even be touched without actually causing a burn to the skin. It can actually cause second and third order burns to the epidermal and dermal layers of the skin. That is how hot it gets. Other toaster broilers I have had and still have may get warm but not so hot you cannot even touch the unit. The Cuisinart is of poor design and poses a very serious risk to children in the home, and adults who may inadvertently touch the outside while in use, which is an easy thing to do. It also poses a fire risk, and will melt any plastics that you may place on top while in use. My wife and I have both burned our hands on the unit. We stopped using it, as we did not want our small and teenage children to burn themselves.
    I contacted the company and they gave me a pat, flip corporate answer which of course absolved themselves of any responsibility in the matter, even though I know they receive the same complaint all of the time. I personally know several people that have the same complaint, including my sister who was also duped into believing the most expensive toaster oven on the market, would actually be a good product. Supposedly Cuisinart knows how to make small appliances, but apparently not. What I do not understand, is why they are still allowed to make and sell this product, and what's even more - is why they would willingly still make and sell this product after knowing about this problem and receiving complaints.
    It is a poorly designed product, it is a dangerous product, it is a very expensive product. It is a product we and others cannot use, because of concern for our safety. It is a product that will eventually harm children, if it has not done so yet - however, I think a child somewhere has already been burned by this product. 
    I contacted the company and they gave me a pat, flip corporate answer that admitted the problem, but takes no responsibility and blows me off:

"    Thank you for your inquiry. With this toaster oven you have, the heating coils are right at the very top of the toaster oven. The heat from those coils will make the outside extremely hot, due to the stainless being a conductor. There is no manufacturers defect with the unit as it is operating as it is intended. It is strongly recommended not to place anything on the unit due to the high heat. If you have any further questions please reply, with history, to this email. We invite you to call our Customer Service Department at 1-800-726-0190 , if you prefer. Please keep in mind the Customer Service Agent will not have access to your e-mail information. The hours of operation are 7 AM -11 PM EST Monday through Friday and 9 AM - 5:30 PM on Saturdays and Sundays, excluding major holidays."
    Really? They know it gets extremely hot, they intended for it to get extremely hot, and apparently it is operating as it should - which means it is OK to burn people. And the only thing they could say is not to place anything on top. What if my 11 year old decides to touch it for whatever reason? Am I supposed to constantly police my toaster oven? I should not have to have a special protocol in use just to use a countertop appliance. How ridiculous!
    So basically, they admit and know the unit gets extremely hot and can even explain why, and they admit this is exactly how they intended for it to be - to get so hot that it can actually burn people, and yet all they can do is tell me not to place objects on top, as if I am an idiot and cannot figure that out. That isn't the point. The point is that I should not have to worry about the obvious unsafe functioning of a product like that, especially when the company is aware of the problem. And especially in a product that cost $175.00 - which is three times the price of their competitors that do not seem to have the problem of burning people.
justification: The oven's exterior gets extremely hot, causing burns (second and third degree) to users, including children, and the company acknowledges the issue.

This microwave has set in one location away from the stove and sink since it's purchase; we are the original purchasers.

Today, 15 August 2012, at about 8:30 AM,  my wife heard a noises in the kitchen: First: sounded like glass breaking, then a large bang.  She walked into the kitchen, and found the oven door was slightly ajar, and the control panel was leaning out at the top of the unit.  She could see into the inside, where it was sparking and arcing.   She unplugged the unit and closed the oven door.

She called our mid-20's son from the downstairs, and by the time they got back to the kitchen moments later, it was burning.  
Quick work by a fire extinguisher brought the flames under control, whereupon they then moved it to the floor, and sprayed it again with the extinguisher.  They were able to move the oven out to the middle of the driveway.  

In the process of dealing with the burning microwave, and subsequently putting out the fire, they both inhaled a fair amount of smoke and extinguisher material.

Had they been moments later, or if no one had been at home, we would have lost our home and contents due to fire.

The oven was not currently in use, it has been used about 3 hours prior for about 2 minutes.

The dishwasher was still running with the dial stuck between START and SHORT WASH and had just kept getting hotter and hotter. The formica countertop above it was so hot I couldn't lay my hand on it. I flipped the lever and opened the door and a thick cloud of hot steam just exploded out and nearly knocked me over.  All the detergent had scorched onto the dishes since it never got to the first rinse.  The dishes were blistering hot, it took a long time for them to cool down. I had to scrub them by hand twice to get the slick coating and smell off them.  I couldn't afford a new dishwasher at the time so I just washed dishes by hand for a couple of months.  Then decided to try a different cycle and test it - put it on Pots&Pans and it ran without the dial hanging up.  I'm still using it on P&P with no problem but I don't dare leave it unattended.  If I hadn't left the bedroom door open that night to where I was able to smell the scorched wood odor and wake up when I did and get it shut off, the kitchen would surely have caught on fire.  Being in the center of the house it would have all gone up in flames before the volunteer fire department could have gathered up all its men in the middle of the night and made it over here.  They need to add Nautilus to their list!
justification: The incident involved a near-miss fire hazard with significant property damage risk but no actual injury or death.

incident_description:
On Monday, August 6, at approximately 10pm.  I had put the dishes in the GE Profile Quiet Power II dishwasher, turned it on, and gone to bed.  My roommate was up studying for an exam, and came to get me when he heard strange noises coming from the dishwasher.  I ran downstairs, could smell electrical fire smoke, and quickly opened the dishwasher.  When I did, flames starting coming out of the bottom of the door shooting inside the dishwasher.  I quickly closed the door, sent my roommate for the fire extinguisher (kitchen ABC powder type), opened the door and put out the fire, having to put the hose at bottom of door and aim within.  The plastic of the door had already begun to melt from the fire.  We turned off the electrical switch to the unit.

Had we both gone to bed, the result could have been a disaster, as the flames were quile large and intense.  I also checked to make sure that nothing had disloged or blocked the mechanical action of the dishwasher.  Nothing had.  It appeared to be electrical in nature judging by the electrical fire smell and source of the flames.  There was no fire damage in the tub itself to indicate that it came from the heating coil at bottom.

While this dishwasher was new when I bought the house in Oct. 2001, it has never had any problems or been repaired.  It worked well until the date of the fire.  I am having the unit hauled away today by Sears, who is installing a new KitchenAid.  This is my second GE appliance to have electrical issues, so I'm giving up on GE.

Approximately 30 minutes after brewing a pot of coffee, I walked into my kitchen to find smoke billowing from the unit and the acrid smell of burning plastic.  I unplugged the unit and moved it outside where it continued to burn for several minutes.

I was lucky to have caught this. Had I used the timer to automatically brew my coffee while my family and I slept, this could easily have led to a fire resulting in injury or death.  At the least, had I left the house with the unit on, there would have been a catastrophic fire.

This is entirely unacceptable and, from what I've found online, all too common.  There is absolutely no reason to engineer a product in this way in this day and age.  The engineering and parts cost to make sure this can never happen again is trivial.

incident_description:
On July 12, I used the Calphalon Mandoline Precision Slicer for the first time.  It amputated the fingertip of my middle finger on my right hand, and I had to be rushed to the emergency room, where they stitched it back on.  As a result of my injury, I may have permanent loss of sensation in my fingertip.

This particular mandoline slicer lacks proper warning labels and specific instructions.  The only label on the device when a customer opens it is deceiving.  The label that tells the user how to disable the safety guard on the blade -- a setting not recommended by the for most users.  First-time users are left with the impression that they must disable that safety feature to be able to use the device.  There is no warning label that the blade is *extremely* sharp, or that the user should never use the item without the safety gripper / hand guard.

The design of the flexible food gripper is also unsafe.  The material used is flexible and does not afford users the stability needed to slice food safely.  In the instructions, Calphalon indicates that items larger than the gripper can be sliced by removing the cap of the gripping mechanism, which undermines its integrity, renders it unstable and forces the food object to bind against the blade.  As a result, it does not work properly, leading users to try to use the device without the safety gripper, significantly increasing the risk of injury.  **This is the only mandoline slicer on the market with this design.  ALL other mandoline slicers have a firm, solid plastic handle for users to hold onto, and most have a mechanical plunger that moves the food closer to the blade.  This design forces the user to manually compress the food item with their hand, moving hands and fingers closer to the blade.  The flexible nature of the food gripper makes it unstable, and the gripper does not fit securely on the cutting plane.**

Many customer online reviews indicate that they cut themselves using the device and that the blade did not cut properly -- that it shredded their food and their fingers.

A [REDACTED].com video promoting the item also shows an advertising representative holding the safety gripper improperly.
justification: The incident resulted in a fingertip amputation with potential permanent loss of sensation, and the design flaws and lack of warnings make such injuries likely for users.

incident_description: We have had several safety concerns with our Electrolux stove. I have asked Electrolux to state in their documentation that I am concerned about fires, etc. Every time I ask the next rep to tell them what I have reported they have left out this information and continue to downplay any safety issues or document them. The problems range from simple items like burned out LEDs to what I consider more serious like the appliance turning on, including burners, by themselves. The appliance has had seven attempts to be repaired and continues to give us electrical problems. During the last incident in July I was cleaning using self-cleaning and it appears to have burned out many boards ( i have only used this twice and the first time was okay). The repairman stated this is common for electrolux and showed me the charred wires and boards where it looked like fire had started. I am also going to report this to our local news and to the attorney general.  I find this a very unsafe appliance and I would not donate it due to fearing it could injure someone.  Electrolux has yet to confirm that is or is not a safety concern to them.  The appliance remains unusable at this time (has been down for several weeks.  Even if they gets parts to get it running again I still feel our safety is at risk due to burned cables and all of the electrical problems we continue to experience.

incident_description:
Recently I purchased a Pyrex 8 cup 
measuring cup for my soup business. I've used Pyrex products for years 
with no problems and always thought they were safe for use in the oven 
and for hot liquids. My understanding has been that Pyrex can withstand 
heat unless subjected to great changes in temperature (i.e. cold to hot 
or visa versa). Yesterday while ladling hot liquid (less than boiling) 
into the measuring cup for the fourth time, the measuring cup exploded 
and shattered glass all over me, another worker and about $500 in 
prepared food. Fortunately my hand only sustained minimal damage and no 
one else was hurt. I shudder to think how close the exploding glass was 
to our eyes. I had glass in my hair, but no lacerations. I am very 
unhappy about my loss of profits for this week and having to recreate 
50 quarts (12.5 gallons) of soup from scratch. I looked on the pyrex 
website to see if I might have misjudged the heat resistance of the 
product, but have found nothing that specifically addresses this issue. 
I would like to feel comfortable using Pyrex products and recommending 
them to my friends and family, but quite honestly I am now fearful that 
they may not be as useful and safe as I once thought.
justification: The incident resulted in minimal injury to one worker and no injuries to others, placing it at severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as similar incidents are documented but not frequent.

incident_description: My husband and I received a Baby Bullet food processor as a baby shower gift.  We read the manual thoroughly and cared for the product and prepared all of the food according to the instruction in the manual.  We have used it a total of 6 times.  The 6th time of use, we pureed sweet potatoes for our son.  While feeding him lunch the next day he began to choke.  I was able to dislodge what he was choking on and pull it out of his mouth.  I, at first, thought it was a sliver of potato, but upon closer inspection realized it was a one inch piece of rubber.  That rubber was a piece of the rubber gasket on the Baby Bullet that had been chopped up and made its way into my son's food.  Who knows how much he actually ingested.  My husband, [REDACTED], called the Baby Bullet company to file a complaint about the product and we were informed that a "couple of months ago" the company had changed the care instructions in the manual because the heat from dishwashers was causing the rubber gaskets to fail and they have also changed the structure of the product and instead of using a removable rubber gasket, they are now permanently seated.  We did register our product when we received it, yet we were not notified of these changes.  The company told us that there was such a small percentage of occurrences that they did not send out notifications.  Had they sent us a notification, the incident of my son choking could have been avoided.  How is it determined what is an acceptable percentage to not have to notify consumers or initiate a recall?  I feel like any percentage of failure that could be hazardous to a human life is too high of a percentage.  Baby Bullet has requested that we pack our Bullet up and leave it on the porch so that they can send FedEx for it and we have complied with their request.  I did take pictures of the product showing the broken gasket and the piece that my son choked on.  I want other parents to know that this product can be dangerous.  Not only should parents be informed, they should also be sending out these replacement parts.  I do not want any other parent to have to go through this.  Next time it could result in something much worse, like the death of an innocent child.
justification: The child choked on a piece of rubber but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the product's known issue but not all units are affected.

incident_description: About 20-30 minutes after running my Kenmore dishwasher -- model no. 665.1703#### -- my daughter informed me that there was a smell coming from the kitchen.  I went to the kitchen, the dishwasher was running, and faints wafts of white smoke were coming from the control panel.  The smell was definitely an electrical fire type smell.  I pressed the Cancel button on the control panel and the dishwasher continued to run, even past the 2 minute Cancel (Drain) cycle.  I then opened the dishwasher door and the dishwasher continued to "run" -- the arms were not turning, no water was running, but the sound of the motor was evident.  I then turned off the circuit breaker and that finally killed the dishwasher.  When I turned the circuit breaker back on, the dishwasher started "running" again.  I turned the circuit breaker off and left it off.  The smoke eventually stopped and the very warm right side of the control panel eventually cooled.

Viking electric built in oven was set on self-clean.  Within an hour on starting the clean cycle, smoke started pouring out of the oven.  My smoke alarm was connected to the fire department, so they responded within minutes.  The house filled with dense smoke.  The oven was so hot that firefighters had to wait a long time in order to remove the oven and check the wall behind it and the wood cabinets for hot spots.  They oven had overheated and set the cabinet next to the oven on fire.
   When the Viking Rep removed the side panel, the fans and wiring were melted inside the oven. He condemned and oven and said it was "fried". The fire department said another ten minutes and my house would have burned.  They said it was good that I was home and had a direct line from the smoke detector to the fire department.  Also my breaker box was labelled, so they could turn off the breaker to the oven.  All those things helped prevent total destruction of my home.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and risk of fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that he is experiencing similar problems of Release #11-016.The electric range right front burner heat to temperatures other than expected and then not turn off.  Whenever this incident occurs he has to switch it off from the circuit breaker.  This has been ongoing for the past 3 months when he moved into the house.  On 7/13/12 the manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that this model was not part of the recall and he could file a report with the agency.  The caller feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.  NOTE:  Caller purchased home with range already installed.

CONSUMER ADDED:  It is important to note that when the right front burner of this electric range stovetop malfunctions that it always causes the aforementioned burner to become stuck on full/high heat The control knob for that burner no longer controls the heat setting. The burner is stuck on high. Even with the control knob turned off the right front burner remains on high. The only way to turn off the burner is to terminate the electrical feed to the stovetop by running outside and switching the circuit breaker off. Even then, it takes considerable time for the burner to cool down. 

As stated in the Incident Details section of this report, this problem is similar to the one listed in Release #11-016; however there is one exception. That report states that the electric range only malfunctions if liquid is spilled and seeps under the control knob. This is certainly true; every time liquid seeps under the control knob for the right front burner, it becomes stuck on high. However, additionally, the right-front burner of my electric range has experienced the same malfunction even when no liquid has been spilled and the surface is dry. Thus, liquid spills are not the only cause of the malfunction.
justification: The electric range malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death has been reported. The issue occurs frequently, as it has been ongoing for 3 months and requires intervention to prevent potential fire.

incident_description: Toaster Oven glass door exploded spraying glass all over the food and kitchen.
justification: The toaster oven door exploding is an incident with potential for injury, but the description does not mention any actual harm, just property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer was using his dishwasher on the normal wash cycle for approximately 5 minutes. His wife saw smoke and flames coming from the top of the unit. They immediately opened the door and saw flames. The consumer went to shut off the circuit breaker. A little later, the dishwasher was examined and the fire appears to have started in the area near the control panel.
 
The consumer has not had any prior incidents with the dishwasher.
 
The manufacturer was not contacted nor the retailer, There is no phone number for the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
(7/8/2012) The consumer's dishwasher was on the wash cycle for approximately 20 minutes. While in the kitchen he and his wife started to smell a plastic burning odor. They both walked through the kitchen, trying to locate which appliance it may have been coming from. It was indeed the dishwasher. The consumer immediately opened the door and saw smoke coming from the control panel. He ran upstairs to shut off the circuit breakers, not knowing whether a fire may occur.  

(7/10/2012) The manufacturer was contacted and the consumer spoke with a rep. (name unknown) from the service center. The rep. informed him that there were not aware of any issues with the brand or that particular model. The consumer then asked to speak with a supervisor. The supervisor (name unknown) came on the line, while explaining the incident the supervisor advised him that he would want to contact their safety department, since the unit was emitting smoke. The consumer was transferred to the safety department. While on the line with the safety department, they took his report and set up an appointment for a technician to come out to his home and inspect the unit. The appointment was set for Friday, July 12, 2012.  

-While surfing the Internet, the consumer came across many complaints on this brand and model. He also saw that once the consumer had the unit repaired the failure re-occurred.  The consumer feels that the product is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission from the dishwasher, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kitchenaid dishwasher MODEL # KUDP 02CRBS2 Main Control Board and Wire Harness caught fire. Fire contained in door of dishwasher and extinguished itself. Resulted in main motor failure. Unsafe situation.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was contained and extinguished itself, resulting in no injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
On July 24th @ midnight, everyone was asleep and I heard this horrific CRASH sounding like a ton of marbles hitting the floor.  I went out into the kitchen where I heard it come from - and on the floor was the front of my General Electric Oven Door on the floor in pieces.

It is only a year old and the warranty ran out two days ago.

Nothing touched it and it was the same temperature it always is in my home.  The oven nor range was on.  Nothing touched it.  

I took me two and half hours to clean it all up.  

I was lucky that no one was near the oven when it happened.
justification: The oven door shattered unexpectedly but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: I purchased a GE Hotpoint gas range, product #RGB530DEPWW, 01/12/2011.  This month my tenants have noticed that the kitchen was warm at random times throughout the day & night.  After further investigation, we have found that the oven is turning on and off on its own, creating a possible fire hazard.  One appliance repairman has stated that it is a thermostat issue but was not sure.
justification: The oven turning on and off on its own poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Problem:  Sanyo Microwave model EM-S6588S (serial number 1111USM07029A) runs with the door open.

Today I was going to use the microwave in our break room when I found it was unplugged.  Not finding any note I plugged it in, and it came on with 0000 displayed (which I assumed was due to no clock being set).  I put some food in for about 30 seconds and when I took it out (hot), the microwave was still on with the door open - I had already put my hand in to get the food before I noticed the turn table spinning and the fan on.  I was later told by a co-worker that the unit had done the same thing earlier (ran with the door open after the time was supposed to be done) and that was why it was unplugged.  I have since notified the facilities dept here and posted a note, so hopefully this unit will be replaced. 

I also found a review on Amazon with a similar complaint about this unit - scroll down to the review of this microwave - Sanyo EM-S6588S 1-Cubic-Foot Microwave Oven, Stainless Steel.

http://www.amazon.com/gp/cdp/member-reviews/A1PSVZBM894R5H/ref=cm_cr_pr_auth_rev?ie=UTF8&sort_by=MostRecentReview

This microwave is dangerous and should be recalled.
justification: The microwave operates with the door open, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description:
The Samsung microwave had an "SE" error warning. We cleared the error and then proceeded to cook some food. The food was removed.  About two minutes later the microwave started itself cooking on the "baked potato" mode.

On the internet, we have seen this isn't unique.  One person indicated it started a fire in his kitchen, causing extensive damage.
We have since unplugged it and am afraid that it could start up at any time.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and started cooking on its own, which is an incident but no injury occurred. The likelihood is high given reports of similar issues and potential fire risk.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the toaster stays on even after the timer goes out.  It stayed on and almost started a fire.  

He contacted the manufacturer the same day.  They told him they would send him a new unit which they did within a week.  

They said they would also give instructions on how to send back the plug to the old unit.  They still have not done so and are now telling him that he has to pay for postage to send back the plug.  He is not going to do that.  
\
The consumer feels that the manufacturer is not that interested in receiving the defective toaster oven in attempt to avoid a possible recall.
justification: The toaster malfunctioned and almost started a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was reported and addressed with a replacement, though the return process is unresolved.

incident_description:
Frigidaire FEFL63FSB range (2009)
Oven element when turned on for preheat, turned white caught fire and shattered.
The right front stove top element heats at extreme temperatures regardless of setting. 
left front stove top will turn itself off & or you will need to manipulate the dial repeatedly to get it to turn on.
2 days after warranty ended the light bulb on the oven appeared to have burned out. When replaced 
never worked again.
When I called the company they advised not on recall list that warranty was over and that the element in oven had burned out. That it was similar to a person having a stroke. Sorry lost them here. Had no idea what the reference was intended to imply.  Actually found it offensive. 
Sounds like similar problems as the recalled ranges had?
justification: The incident involved a fire and malfunctioning elements, posing a risk but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had the oven pre-heated at 350 and then she increased the temperature to 425 degrees.  However, approximately 5-10 mins later she noticed flames emitting from the heating element.  She immediately powered off the oven and the flames went out.  This incident caused the melting of the heating element.

She stated that this was the first incident and if she was not present this could have caused a house fire.  The oven remains inoperable.  

7/12/12 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that a service rep would be sent out at her cost.

The consumer feels that this electric range/oven is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved flames and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible since it happened once but could recur.

incident_description:
(7/1/2012) The consumer stated that ice cube maker started giving crushed ice instead of cubes. His wife had pulled out the dispenser and immediately yelled out. When she viewed her right hand, there was a blister on it. She did not receive any medical treatment. A mark still remains on her right hand, which resulted from the blister.  It is believed that the wife may have come in contact with the electric motor portion of the ice maker.
 
(7/3/2012) The consumer contacted the retailer and their rep. (name unknown) indicated that a manager was not able to speak with him at that time and it was recommended that the consumer contact the manufacturer himself. The manager from the retailer contacted the consumer 2 days later and he referred him to (800) 944-9044 or (706) 860-4110. After calling those numbers, he spoke with a rep (name unknown), who took a complaint from him. The rep. later advised the consumer that she was transferring him over to their Litigation Dept.  The consumer left a voice message on the automated system for that dept..
 
(1 week later) He received a letter from the manufacturer on what he had reported.

Nothing else transpired.
justification: The incident resulted in a blister on the wife's hand, which is an injury, but no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the electric range /oven was in use at a temperature of 350 degrees.  Approximately 5 mins later he noticed that the oven was extremely hot, he opened the door and the interior glass was crack and the contents were burnt.  The sealing of the oven door was charred.  The glass door was warped and interior of oven was charred as well.

The caller immediately turned off the oven.  There was one instance where he had a grease fire while the unit was on oven clean.  There was no prior incident of this nature.


The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.


The caller stated that he noticed that there was a recall but not for his model.


The caller is concerned that this range/oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the oven but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I found white, very sharp, glass like shards in an iced drink. If chewed on or swallowed, this will cause  harm. I noticed the particles before swallowing and no harm was done, however several pieces are missing and they might have been consumed already. The source of the debris is the ice maker of the Jenn-Air side by side fridge JCD2389GES.

It seems to me that this is a general design problem and the ice maker should be recalled.

The problem is that the very strong, geared motor couples to the ice maker via a plastic drive ring. The plastic is very hard and glass like. If it disintegrates, the debris will go into the ice tray.
justification: The incident was discovered before any injury occurred, but the sharp shards could cause harm if consumed.

incident_description:
My dishwasher gets so hot it melted the controls in the door as well as the sides so that they expanded and the unit lost its seal.  estimated repairs are $250 but the repair person says it will just fail again and again. 

GE Dishwasher 

Model GLD4500N10BB
Serial  HS741250B
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused property damage but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The repair person's statement suggests the issue is likely to recur.

incident_description:
GE OTR/Built-in microwave Model JVM1850DM2BB Serial No. VM900163B
Exterior glass on door of microwave is either faulty or designed poorly - glass inside door has exposed edge and open.  I tapped edge of glass when door was open with ceramic bowl and heard loud crack.  I was sprayed with glass bits, pieces hit my eyeglasses, chest, went down my shirt and flew across my kitchen floor.  I have approx.5 oz.of glass bits that were sprayed out from the glass door.  For 15 mins. approx.after incident the glass continued to pop, crack and fragment across face of glass spraying glass powder down onto top of my stove/range.  To protect myself and my home, I wrapped the front of the glass and edge with duct tape.  
This cannot be a safe design and/or this glass was faulty.  As I shopped for a replacement microwave I noticed that many of the leading brands on the market (all of them displayed at local Sears) do not have a protective bracket  around the edge of the glass that fits in the front door.  That means that the glass is exposed near the handle - a high traffic 'area'.  I do not believe that these product lines as designed are safe.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering and spraying bits, causing minor injuries (glass bits hitting chest and eyeglasses) but no serious harm.

incident_description: Dishwasher fire
justification: A dishwasher fire is an incident with potential for property damage but no mention of injury or death.

Black & Decker Toaster Oven Model TO14915

incident_description: My toaster oven switches itself on. The only way to keep the toaster oven from heating is to keep it unplugged. The toaster oven has 3 dials, one of which controls power state. From the "off" setting, you can turn the dial to the "on" setting on the right if you want the oven to stay on, or you can turn the dial to a "Dark...Medium...Light" "toast" setting on the left. The "toast" setting is controlled by a mechanical count-down timer that rotates the dial back to the "off" position. Now instead of stopping at "off", the dial continues to rotate to "on", where it stops. The same thing happens if you manually set the dial to "off".
justification: The toaster oven switches itself on unexpectedly, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: After heating pizza in our oven, closing the door and walking away the exterior glass window on the oven shattered and landed as far as 2 feet from the stove. The door was not slammed and the shattering did not happen instantly - I had time to close the door, turn away from the oven and set down the pizza tray before I heard the loud sound of the glass exploding. I contacted Sears and the person I spoke with explained that the item was no longer covered under warranty. She did not express that this was a common occurrence as I later found out when researching replacement parts online. I am concerned that this has happened many times and a recall has not been issued.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the user's research indicating this is a common issue.

incident_description:
On Aug. 8, 2012 at around early evening, my client; [REDACTED] came home from being out and about. When she opened her freezer she found it had caught on fire.
[REDACTED] call me, [REDACTED] with Bishop and Son Appliance Repair, llc, and requested service. I arrived and opened the freezer door to find a fire had taken place. The fire went out due to lack of oxygen, but not before causing some excessive damage,
I carefully removed all burned out parts, taking pictures along the way.
This is my second report. I suppose the last report has been lost in cyberspace.
The refrigerator is Kenmore brand, model # 10653544300.
justification: The incident involved a freezer fire causing excessive damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The caller stated that while the dishwasher was in use for approximately 10 mins.  There was a flash of light and then there was smoke emitting from the front of the unit.  The control panel was irresponsive and the circuit breaker was used to switch the unit off.  There was black soot on the front of the dishwasher.  The unit is now inoperable.


7/4/12 The retailer/manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that a service rep would be sent out at an expense to her.

The caller feels that the dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved smoke and soot from the dishwasher but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was contained by turning off the circuit breaker.

incident_description:
I first noticed something was wrong with the stove back when I blogged about the broiler failing a few weeks ago. When it failed I had to come up with an alternative way to finish dinner. I didnÃÂt think much of it and just assumed that IÃÂd no longer be able to use that function on the oven. Not perfect, but I knew the oven was a few years old and I figured it was slowly dying.

Then this week my sonÃÂs girlfriend made dinner for them and within about 10 minutes I started smelling a strong hot, metallic smell. Just as I was about to ask my son if he smelled it (we were all upstairs and the kitchen is on the main floor), every smoke detector in the house started going off. I live with a fireman so we have LOTS of detectors and they were going off even though it was hot and we had every window and door in the house open.

The chicken was black and the heat was so high it stained the opening around the door of the oven. My son opened the oven, laughed at his girlfriend for burning dinner, and then turned off the stove. He saw the broiler element was on and assumed sheÃÂd hit broil instead of bake and chocked it up to her using a stove sheÃÂs not familiar with.

I had him switch the oven off again and then wait 3 minutes. The element remained on. I sent him to shut off the breaker and finally the element went off.

I started shopping for a new stove assuming this one was just broken when the hubby came upon note after note of other people with this same Kenmore stove having similar incidents. It wasnÃÂt long before I found a recall for Kenmore stoves from 2001 to 2009 (ours is a 2003 ÃÂ I know that thanks to a review I wrote about the stove when we received it on Epinions.com). Looking into if further, things could have been worse. HereÃÂs what happened to someone who has the same model as mine:

On Monday 1/16/12, i was making dinner, baked potatoes in aluminum foil, and my oven turned onto self cleaning mode after cooking for 30 minutes. It locked down, and caught on fire. We called 911 because our house was filled with smoke, and fire in the oven. The Fire Department instructed us to contact Sears, to report it, and I did. They also instructed me to report this to you as well.  - source http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1225253 
And itÃÂs not an isolated incident. Here are other online notes about similar safety hazards:

help! kenmore range /oven model 665. 92014102 oven wont turn off. have to trip breaker to get oven to stop heating. Source: http://applianceguru.com/forum1/8581.html 
Kenmore range 92014102 ÃÂ Page 23 - Kenmore stove, ÃÂbroiler came on while in the baking mode and will not go off until range is unpluggedÃÂÃÂ Source: http://www.fixya.com/tags/kenmore_range_92014102/page-23  
Why is the oven not turning off on my Kenmore range? I have a Kenmore electric range model number 665.92014102 that the oven will not turn off & has an E2 F3 error code...  Source: http://www.managemylife.com/mmh/questions/153928-why-is-the-oven-not-turning-off-on-my-kenmore-range-1
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could have led to a fire but was controlled without injury, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The recall and multiple reports suggest this issue is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I bought a plate from Ikea and it suddenly exploded and shattered into hundreds of pieces in my kitchen cabinet
justification: The plate shattered but there is no mention of injury, making it an incident without injury. Such occurrences are rare.

incident_description: The microwave turns on and off on its own.  The problem is well know on the web with the microwave(refering to a poorly made door swith).  The problem started about 13 months after we purchased it, and for many people on the web 12-18 months.
justification: The microwave turning on and off on its own is an incident with no reported injury, and the problem is known to occur frequently within 12-18 months of purchase.

incident_description:
I placed a microwaveble heating pad in the microwave.  I pushed the #2 on the pad and it is supposed to heat for 2 minutes.  Upon returning I found smoke in the kitchen and the microwave was still cooking 10 minutes later.  The inside of the microwave had caught fire.  I opened the door and took the product outside in flames.  I cleaned out the microwave. 

The second incident happened about 1 and 1/2 months later.  I was heating food and was standing there watching it as it heated for 2-3 mins.  When the counter counted down to zero it went from 1sec-74 minutes.  Luckily I was there and was able to stop it before it could have caught on fire again.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injury or death occurred, and the issue recurred once with potential for fire.

incident_description:
Holder did not hold the potato I was slicing because it has no spikes, merely small plastic pyramid shapes.  My hand slipped when the potato slipped and I cut off my fingertip.  Amazon reviews report a high rate of injuries with this product.  There are also many comments about the inadequacy of the holder. Some even say they know the product is dangerous, but they use it carefully.   A few even say they use it without the hoder, that they know it is dangerous, but continue because it cuts well and they are being careful.  Acidents can happen.

I hope that you check Amazon reviews and other sources as many never file a report and it is free information.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut off fingertip, which is an injury.

incident_description: My refrigerator stopped working and the motor became very hot.
justification: The refrigerator malfunctioned without causing injury, but the hot motor could pose a risk if not addressed.

incident_description: We purchased a Frigidaire "Professional Series" glass top stove within the last three years. Today, 08/04/2012, my husband came home and found the house filled with smoke. My husband called the Fire Department and soon after they arrived, they traced the cause of the smoke to the stove. They pulled the stove away from the wall and determined a "short" must have occurred in the rear lower panel of the stove. The steel on the back panel was melted and had turned white from the heat. The heat set the kitchen wall on fire. Fortunately, the breaker had tripped before my husband came home and found the smoke. The wall was still smoldering red embers when the stove was pulled away from the wall. The entire stove was hot to the touch, including the control panel and the entire glass top surface. The stove had not been used by myself or my husband since Thursday, 8/2/2012 and all the controls were in the 'Off" position.  If my husband had not come home when he did, this "defect" would have burned down our entire house. When I researched the stove on-line, I discovered several recalls related to the stove. We were not notified of these recalls. We have made a claim with our insurance. This is outrageous. This should NOT happen!.
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On 07/26/2012 at approximately 12:15PM my youngest daughter age 12 set our stove to "Preheat". There was an explosion that then occurred within a minute or two. I was at work when I received a frantic call from my eldest daughter and called a friend two houses down to go to my home. He determined that there was a late ignition of gas and that an explosion occurred. He shut off the gas to the stove.
The explosion blew 4 LB grates off of the stove - one about two feet into the air where it knocked the overhead exhaust. The oven door was blown open and the unit moved several inches away from the wall by the force of the explosion. Cabinet doors in the kitchen were blown open. There were no injuries and no other apparent property damage, however had my daughter been standing next to the stove - I have no doubt she would have been injured. I also believe that had the oven door been locked (clean mode) that the explosion might have been catastrophic.

[REDACTED] a manager at Frigidaire offered nothing more than sending out a technician (at my expense) to determine the cause of the problem. I told him, I am NOT looking for a free repair or a free replacement. That Frigidaire needs to be serious and investigate this incident. I can't be the only owner of a nine yr old stove that has issues. He indicated that there is nothing his company will do.
justification: The incident involved an explosion with significant force, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the oven was pre-heated at 425 degrees.  Approximately 2-3 mins after placing the contents into the oven, she heard an explosion and noticed that the inner oven glass door had exploded.  The glass pieces were scattered onto the broiler section and the kitchen floor.  She is concerned that if she had been closer to the oven, she would have been injured.

7/9/12 The manufacturer was contacted and they informed her to contact the retailer for repairs.

7/10/12 The retailer was contacted and she was informed that a service technician would be sent out for repairs.  The service technician came out and advised that the oven glass would be replaced.

The caller feels that this oven is a safety hazard and should be replaced.
justification: The oven glass exploded, causing a potential hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This incident occurred with my Frigidaire Professional Series Glass top stove.  Model # PLES389ECG.
This stove is 4 years old.
My husband and I came home from work on a Friday to find the outer most glass of the oven door shattered all over our kitchen floor. There was no one in the house that day, and nothing could have fallen into the glass.  The oven part of the stove had not been in use for several days and the stove top had not been used that day.
Upon some research I found that this is not an isolated incident with this particular brand of stove.
I called Frigidaire about replacing the glass, they will replace it but I have to pay for it.
I thing that something of this sort, that has occurred several times to other people should be a recalled defect.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass) but no injury or death, and similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid model #KESC300HWH4 electric range. I put piece of fish in oven to broil. Timer was set for 5 minutes. About 30 seconds after timer sounded, I went to kitchen to turn fish over, but before I got there I head a loud noise. When I opened the oven further, I saw that the inside glass of the door had exploded into the oven. I shut the door all the way & turned the oven off, but did not go near for a while until oven cooled, afraid that the outside glass might also break.

I called Kitchenaid on Tuesday AM (I was not available on Monday) & spoke to someone in consumer dept. & she took safety info from me. Then I was transferred to another person who said that although the oven is 12 years old, they would pay for part only to repair this oven, but I had to pay for all labor & I would have to pay for someone to look at it for an estimate as to the cost of labor.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass exploding, but no injuries were reported, making it an incident without injury. Such occurrences are uncommon but not unheard of in older appliances.

incident_description: I woke up and opened my bedroom door on Friday, July 27th to the smell of smoke and my living room and kitchen very hazy with smoke.  Went quickly to look around and couldn't find anything.  I woke my husband up and he searched in and outside the house and in attic.  The smell and smoke got very bad and we were fixing to call 911 when we noticed smoke rolling out from under our refrigerator.  My husband quickly pulled the refrigerator out away from the wall and unplugged it.  When we got it outside, my husband found that a little white box and all of the wires connected to the side of the compressor had burned. incident_description:
We own a  General Electric Profile microwave/convection oven that we purchased new about two years ago.  One afternoon when we were steaming broccoli in a glass bowl with a lid on it, fire started shooting out of the small panel on the right side (looking in) of the microwave.  Luckily, my wife saw the flames and shut the microwave down.  The fire went out, but the microwave would work no longer.  It just sent sparks flying when tested a few minutes later.  
I reported this safety problem to GE but I am not satisfied with their response.  I am concerned that if my wife had not seen the flames that the microwave could have caused a fire in our kitchen.
The appliance technician that I arranged to fix the microwave found the problem to be a faulty magnetron, but rather than the usual crack in the magnetron, it showed black marks.  It also burned the wave guide plate covering the magnetron.  The plate also had to be replaced.
I learned from watching the repair that GE used an LG magnetron in this microwave, not something I would have expected.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is considered possible given the specific fault in the magnetron.

incident_description:

When he removed the left back panel he discovered that there was a connection that was "fried" and causing the burner not to work.

He then inspected the connection to the right back burner which was working but he noted that the wiring to this burner was in the process of becoming "fried".

Caller states that he believes that these ranges are being manufactured without the ability to hold the voltage.

the gauge of the wire and the quality of the connecter cannot carry the load of the range.

He is reporting as a safety issue due to a potential fire hazard or shock hazard.

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

He would ask that his range be upgraded to a more secure range with better quality of wire and connector.

At the very least he would ask for reimbursement amount of present repair and an upgrade of wire and connector to more durable and dependable grade.

He states that with this range and the quality of wire and connector he believes that he would be continuously making these repairs as well as trying to head off safety issues.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Over the Range Microwave Model #721.80409400  Serial #409KM01048 Manuf. date Sep 2004, but bought end of 2004.  Was cooking broccolli in the microwave for 5 minutes  and had about 1 minute left.  Look at the microwave and flames were shooting out from the vent above the door.  I quickly opened up the microwave door to stop the microwave, but nothing happened.  It kept on running making a zapping noise.  I quickly unplugged and that stopped the microwave, but the flames were still shooting out.  We quickly got the fire extinguisher and put out the flames, but the cabinets around the microwave were extremely hot to the touch.  All my alarms were going off and the fire dept. showed up.  We quickly unhooked the microwave from the installed bracket and brought it outside.  The fire dept inspected the cabinet and walls and noticed the black marks and said any longer it would have caught onto the cabinets and walls.  Thank goodness I was right there.  Microwaves are supposed to be safe to use for kids and elderly which I have both in my house.  My house would have burned down if any of them would have used it.  They would have not been able to respond like we did.  My kids could have put something in the microwave and went upstair and left it and the house could have caught on fire.  We called the recall center and found that there was a recall on 92,000 kenmore microwaves from 2000-2003, but not my model #.  I called Sears directly and all they had to say was that it was not under warranty any longer like I was reporting that the microwave just stopped working, not "CAUGHT ON FIRE and almost burned down my house and who knows what else that could have happened".  We talked to 3 people who were supposed to be higher in charge than the last and nobody could do anything.  I even asked if there was something I could fill out to report this because maybe there should be recall on this microwave just like the 92,000  others.  Nope, there was nothing like that available.  My question is how many people just said "OK, thanks" and hung up.  The last person we talked to said they would have someone higher up call within 2 hours, but of course that phone call never came in.  They did finally give us a case # [REDACTED] after being on the phone for over an hour, but what that was for I'm not sure of.  It just distubs me that nothing was even asked about how bad the fire was or if anyone got hurt.  It was like it's common for a mircrowave to catch on fire.  I thank God this didn't turn out worse than it was, but I'm astonished how this is being handled.
justification: The incident involved flames shooting out from the microwave, requiring a fire extinguisher and fire department response, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Whirlpool 9.6 cu. ft. Top Freezer Refrigerator w/ Contour Doors
Sears Item# 04609059000 | Model# ET0MSRXTB
Delivered less than one month ago
Cute stylish fridge, good size for a small cabin or apartment
Well, my BRAND NEW WHIRLPOOL FRIDGE FROM SEARS that was delivered on July 2 gave me a fright last night.
I opened the freezer (!!) to prepare a meal to see FIRE (!!) behind the vents. I thought maybe it is reflecting the color of the wood of the paneling behind the unit.
No.
It is not.
The vents of the freezer don't have an opening in the back. It's completely enclosed inside the unit. That's where the flames were.
I look more closely.
It's like a flaming toaster oven or fireplace on the other side of the freezer vents.
I put my hand inside the freezer, on the bottom near the vents on the inside of the back of the freezer box (inside of the freezer) and it's HOT HOT HOT
there was FIRE BACK THERE. In the freezer!!!
Searched the internet and apparently there was a recall for some faulty wiring of 1 million + refrigerators in 2009.
For some wiring that causes the compressor to overheat and causes the fridge to burst into flames.
And houses to go on fire.
Figure they have a similar problem and have not fixed it
I unplugged my fridge completely.
I called Sears.
They are replacing the fridge with a brand new fridge and they say they will bring it Friday morning.
The freezer is not blackened inside, but some wires were definitely flaming inside the unit I definitely am glad to have a new fridge coming. I am very lucky to have seen the flames inside the freezer and to have been here when it happened.
You don't expect that and I am wondering if people have the freezer packed with food, this could be happening to them and they would not notice it since the vents would be covered, behind the food items. I recently got my fridge, and did not have too much in the freezer yet.
I hope this complaint is investigated and if there is a similar design flaw to the last recall that they recall these refrigerators. There could have been a house fire and fatalities here. This is a wood structure.
Please follow up. This was a brand new item. Thank goodness for the local Sears' fantastic customer service, they stepped up to the plate and were very supportive about fixing the problem and exchanging the unit with a new one right away and taking this one to service and track down the problem. They said better safe than sorry.
The manufacturer and the Consumer Safety Board need to investigate these reports. Very dangerous flaw and it seems that there are other complaints and the manufacturer needs to get more proactive with this. Not Sears' fault, but Whirlpool's.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the freezer, posing a significant risk of injury or death, but no actual injury or death occurred.
