I turned it off and opened it up to let it cool off----it was extremely HOT!  It seems at though it came on by itself.  Also seems as thought it should have some sort of safety feature to prevent it from overheating because this could have easily started a fire.  It will no longer work and shows a 5E error code.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and overheated, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Samsung Refrigerator RS2630SH in approx 2006.
We have had nothing but trouble with it. It is heating up to the point that
it will burn when you touch it. This is the second time we have to fix this problem.
I think these refrigerators should be recalled.
justification: The refrigerator heats up to a dangerous level, posing a burn risk, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her manual sea salt grinder is potential safety hazard as the grinder fell apart and shards of glass found their way in her and her daughterÃÂs food, which they consumed. The consumer and her daughter had to be seen at the emergency room. The consumer stated that the grinder has a clear top. The consumer was grinding the sea salt grinder and fell apart and the salt fell in to the pasta she was cooking.

 The consumer was unaware that glass had mistakenly fallen into her pasta since she could not see the clear glass shards. The consumer noticed a foreign object in her and saw that the glass was in her throat. The consumer was coughing glass and had uncomfortable cough. The consumer's daughter was coughing constantly the following day all throughout. The consumer went to the hospital on Monday September 19 2011. 

The consumer stayed at the hospital for nearly 12 hours. The consumer's daughter does not show any physical signs of injury but has been coughing consistently. The consumer did sustain cuts in her mouth. The consumer was prescribed Maalox mixed with medicine. The consumer went to [redacted]. The consumer was advised to schedule a follow up with a herself and daughter. The hospital took x-rays on both her daughter and her neck, mouth and throat. 

The consumer has yet to call the retailer or the firm. The consumer did go to retailer on September 18, 2011. The consumer was told by the store manager that they are willing to offer a replacement or a refund. The consumer found that there numerous of these products on the shelf. The consumer stated that the product came with no instruction.
justification: The consumer sustained cuts in her mouth and both had to be seen at the emergency room, indicating injury.

incident_description: Not sure how long we have had the snapware glasslock, but we finally decided they were just too dangerous to keep in the house.  We would notice shards of glass in the containers so we threw any away that had parts from them.  Then we washed the remaining ones.  Just this week my husband bit into some food and had a long shard of glass in it.  I had done the same previously.  We just decided they had to go.  Something is not right when the glass keep breaking off and ending up in the food.
justification: The description mentions finding glass shards in food and instances of biting into glass, indicating potential injury.

incident_description: oven quit working took apart found circut board almost caught on fire and another connector showed signs of heat at the time this happend my 9 and 10 year old were home with the babysitter it was hot enough to discolor the circut board
justification: The oven's circuit board showed signs of overheating and nearly caught fire, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: microwave burned a hole through a [REDACTED] dish.  When removed from the microwave the dish exploded.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burned dish and explosion) but no mention of injury.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to file a formal complaint against Liebherr, manufacturer of the refrigerator that my family currently uses. We bought the brand new fridge (Model: CS1650) as part of the purchase of our new apartment in September of 2008. The fridge is priced at about $5,000 on the market, a very costly fridge by our standard.

The fridge started to have performance issues since Q4 of 2010, less than 2 years since our original purchase. It would suddenly stop working for about 10~20 seconds and then restart to work again, making some beeping sound at the same time. The screen indicating the temperature would start blinking as the temperature started to rise. However, the issue was intermittent at that time and it was gone after we reset the power. It worked as normal until a few months ago, when it would stop working overnight for no reason. The most annoying issue is that you canÃÂt predict when it would happen. We couldnÃÂt even remove items to other storage (e.g. neighborÃÂs fridge) in time. We have a two-year-old daughter who needs to be fed milk three times a day. We even had one incidence where the temperature raised undetectably and she had spoiled milk and food poison subsequently. We called Liebherr for the issue and they insisted itÃÂs out of warranty even we explained that the same issue happened back in 2010. To avoid the spoiled milk incidence, we had to pay the service company to diagnose the fridge on site. But the earliest we could have an appointment with the repair person was 3 days later. However, by the day of the appointment, the issue disappeared so the repair person couldnÃÂt diagnose. The nature of the issue makes the case so difficult since it may not replicate itself when the repair person comes to inspect it. Of course, the same issue started again a few weeks later, which has been extremely frustrating. Finally, a couple months later since we spoke to Liebherr, the fridge was identified (still not 100% sure) by Liebherr customer service as having circuit board issue and requires a ~$700 repair.

We have been extremely disappointed with the fridge and LiebherrÃÂs services. Many of other unit owners in our condo also had problems with their fridges (same brand and model). It seems to us to be excessive and unacceptable for a $5,000 brand new fridge to have so many problems within 2~3 years. Since the warranty only covers us for two years, the repair cost (parts and labor) have become very expensive. For some of my neighbors, the repair costs have exceeded $1000 which is probably sufficient to purchase a brand new fridge. For our case, the issue clearly happened within the warranty period but the nature of the issue makes it impossible for us to get it fixed within the warranty period. We feel that these defects seem to fall outside of the normal range and indicate the manufacturerÃÂs irresponsibility to consumers. We believe that proper investigation is warranted and the voices of LiebherrÃÂs customers should be heard.

Thank you very much for your kind attention. We sincerely appreciate your supporting the New York consumers.

Sincerely yours,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator leading to spoiled milk and food poisoning, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The issue is recurring and affects multiple units, making occurrence likelihood high (4).

incident_description:
I had a Pyrex small baking dish explode spontaneously in my kitchen. It was sitting on my counter undisturbed. It had been used the day before to bake a casserole, but it was cleaned and had sat overnight on a drying rack. This particular dish is just over a year old and has been used maybe a total of 20 times.

I was in a different room when I heard shattering glass. I found the dish on our countertop in two large and fifty small pieces. It seemed to explode out and against our kitchen backsplash. Hopefully this is a freak occurrence, but it is still unnerving as most of the rest of our baking and storage is done with Pyrex.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish exploding without causing injury, fitting the criteria for severity level 2.

incident_description:
My wife walked past the kitchen at approximately 11:30 PM and heard an unusually loud and different sound coming from the microwave oven.  The touch screen was not lit and heat was radiating from the oven.  The view window was protruding. Immediately threw the electrical breaker to turn the power off to the oven.  Note that an electrical storm had passed thru the area about 30 minutes prior but no lightening strikes were noted in our immediate area.  
This oven was built into a cabinet.  The trim kit was immediately removed and we attempted to remove the oven from the cabinet.  All surfaces were hot, but the top and bottom surfaces were so hot that we could not touch them without gloves.  After the unit was removed, I noted the electrical wire leading from the wall outlet to the oven was not hot.
About noon that day, I attempted to use the oven and it would not respond to my input. I interrupted the power to the oven by recycling the electrical breaker.  The oven then responded normally.
Unit maintenance history:  The touch screen had been replaced twice over the ten years we used the oven.  The screen failed again about 3 month ago.  This makes 4 total screen failures.  We continued to use the oven after the last screen failure, punching in numbers by memory.  The light inside the oven failed about 2 month ago. 
Note that this incident took place just prior to my wife and I going to bed for the night. If it had occurred 1or 2 hours later, I am confident that we would have had a kitchen/house fire while we were asleep.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: As I was mixing cheesecake batter, I heard a knocking noise as is the paddle attachment was hitting the side of the bowl. After stopping the machine and looking closer, I realized that a screw had fallen out and into the batter.
justification: A screw fell into the batter, which is an incident but caused no injury.

incident_description:
Frigidaire electric smooth top range, front left burner does not shut off all the time even when knob is rotated to the off position. Sometimes turns its self back on after a brief time.  Burner will not heat consistently, sometimes goes to hi heat on it's own. 

Went to frigidaire.com to get information on my malfunctioning smooth top electric range and noticed a recall due to fire hazard.  Contacted Frigidaire's recall center and gave them my model and serial number and was told that model number was not under the recall notice.  I explained that our electric range was doing the exact same thing as the recall and that the serial number was within the range noted on the recall.  We were directed to customer care and was told the only thing Frigidaire would do is refer us to a service provider in our area.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My maytag disherwasher caught on fire at the point where the wiring connected to the dishwasher. It was in use when I noticed a burning odor. The fire was contained within the machine. The machine also had a leak prior to the fire occurring. My model number is MDB5130AWW and my serial number is 10345994ZF
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but was contained within the machine, and there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Dishwasher burner never shuts off!
justification: The dishwasher burner not shutting off is an incident that could lead to overheating or fire, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: I purchased the unit on 2/3/11. Roughly July 10, I got an error that said that the keypad had shorted, and that the unit may require service. I unplugged the unit for at least an hour, and then it was fine. About 3 days ago, the unit turned on by itself. The keypad was not responsive, and I had to open the door or unplug the unit to get it to turn off. I unplugged the unit for a while, and then plugged it back in, and everything seemed to be fine. Early this morning, I woke to the microwave beeping. I got up, and it had the "surged" error on the display again. I unplugged the unit, plugged it back in, and it started microwaving again without any input from me. I unplugged the unit and went back to bed. When I got up this morning, I inspected the inside of the microwave and saw that the door and part of the inside plastic was burned. I am afraid that my house would have caught on fire if I had not woken up and unplugged the unit. I contacted the manufacturer, and they refused to do anything because it has been over a year since I purchased the microwave.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing burns to the unit but no injury to the user, and the issue recurred multiple times.

incident_description:
This happened on a glass top stove.  Stove burner was set to a low temperature but was blazing hot.  We could not get the burner to lower without turning it off.  The next day, the burner was used on high, but it would not turn off at all.  It continued to blaze for approximately 20 minutes while I tried switching it on and off, lowering the temperature, etc.  Eventually it did turn off.

I looked on-line and found that Sears had a recall on our Serial Number.  Another worrisome safety concern I found described was that the burner could also spontaneously turn on.

When I called for the "free" repair, they said that my Model number was not in the recall even though my Serial number is, and I am definitely having the same problem as many others.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove burner that could not be turned off, posing a safety risk, but no injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the recall and similar reported issues by others.

incident_description:
I bought a Rival microwave oven at Walmart in Lawton OK.  model EM720CWA-PMB.

Out of the box when first plugged in the unit turns on and will not shut off.  None of the buttons turns the microwave off.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned out of the box but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
At the end of March 2012, we purchased GE Coffee Maker model # 898682 at a Walmart store. On July 11, 2012 we set a pot of coffee to brew as a part of our normal routine. Within minutes of completing the brew cycle, we began hearing a faint crackling sound and could smell burning plastic. We quickly approached the kitchen where we could see heavy smoke coming from the rear of the unit, we promptly unplugged the unit. Once the smoke began to disipate, you could smell the burning plastic smell the heaviest underneath the water storage tank at the rear of the coffee maker. We've not plugged this unit in since. 

Our local Walmart store refused to accept a return/ exchange on this unit as we do not have our receipt from 4 months ago.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the described malfunction.

incident_description:
I have a GE coffee pot from Wal-mart  and I looked up and they had a recall in may 2010 made from china they start fire or melted down . I just bought one a few months ago and it just melted down.
I was home and got it stop. I have a different number but it looks the same.
so I don't think they really fix the problem. i will not buy any more drip coffee pots.

justification: The coffee pot melted down but was stopped without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: We are on vacation in  a rental home  equipped with the black GE Walmart coffee maker.  I prepared 1/2 pot of coffee per usual procedure.  Upon pouring the first cup, the handle separated from the carafe.  It shattered on the floor between my feet.  Fortunately, I was wearing shoes; otherwise, I would have like been burned and cut by breaking glass.
justification: The incident involved the carafe breaking but no injury occurred due to wearing shoes, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description: I was baking with Frigidaire smooth top stove Model # FFEF3050LS, I went and turned my timer and oven off there was a pop, then the stove started smoking and there was a small flame, but it did not kick the breaker.  My husband kicked the breaker and unplugged the stove.  He then took the back off the stove and found that the Spitfire Controls had caught fire.
justification: The incident involved a small flame and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Refrigerator start relay shorted out while refrigerator was running normally. The plastic relay burnt and could have potentially started a larger fire.
justification: The refrigerator relay shorted and burned, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher loaded and ran in evening.  Later that evening putrid odor of undetermined origin was noted in home.  Search throughout house to find the cause, but not located.  Next morning, dishwasher found to be extremely hot on outer surface (door) and countertop.  The heated dry light was on, along with the start button, which would not reset or turn off.  The Unit had to be disconnected by turning the electrical breaker off.  All contents were either melted or had a strange brown film, along with broken tines and melted silverware rack in the dishwasher.  Even the water dispenser in the bottom of the dishwasher was melted / broken.  A GE service representative was called and his report stated "Unit left heat on for too long and caused excessive damage to product.  Due to excessive damage unit non-repairable."  He shared with me he had never seen this much damage done to a dishwasher.  Spoke to GE Consumer advocates x2 and their solution is to provide me a discounted price on a new appliance and the email address for formal complaints.  When I inquired about if there had been resolution to the cause of this problem because I wanted to make a formal complaint, I was told there is not a safety issue with the heating unit.  I then spoke to a GE resource in Recall and she shared with me that it is a known issue of overheating and destroying contents, but it has not caused a fire.  Igniting a fire = justification for a recall - can we not be proactive.  This department is working with me and ensured that in newer models this potential hazard does not exist, but other consumers who have purchased in this model (PDW9280N20SS) should be aware of the potential fire hazard - everything was very hot.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On 3/14/2012 the consumer put her oven on self clean. (approximately 450 to 500 degrees.)

Once the oven locked automatically the entire glass front of the oven door fell onto the floor. 

When she purchased the stove there was double edge adhesive tape at the bottom of the glass front, sellers instructed the owner that it would dissolve as they continued to use the stove.

There were no injuries associated with the incident.

The manufacturer was contacted 4/10/2012 appointment was set for a technician to come out. 

Technician arrived a few days later and after replacing the glass front with exactly the same glass with the same double adhesive tape,  he advised her that everything was operating accordingly.


Unsatisfied with the repair and advice from the technician on 4/12/2012, caller contacted the manufacturer again on 5/7/2012. Another technician was sent out 5/14/2012.

The technician that came out on 5/14/2012 took her statement, said he would submit to his superiors but they have yet to discuss a replacement glass or unit.

The consumer believes the product is unsafe due to poor design and the adhesive used.

The consumer was also concerned that due to the front of the stove being all glass that this incident could potentially have injured someone in her home if they were close enough.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass falling but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recurring issue with the adhesive tape.

incident_description: The standard blade for a 14 cup Cuisinart Food Processor (blade # DLC-001TX) has a critical failure that could be extremely dangerous.  My blade just lost a small piece around the mounting rivets and was cracked through at all the rivets.  Luckily I found the small piece of steel before it got into any food.  While ordering a replacement blade on Amazon.com, I was horrified to read that this is not a new occurance.  Many people have had the blades crack, some people have eaten the metal parts, and in some cases, the blades fly apart during use, exiting the machine.  I suggest you look at the customer comments at this link.  http://www.amazon.com/Cuisinart-DLC-001TX-stainless-steel-blade/dp/B000TEPM6O/ref=sr_1_5?ie=UTF8&qid=1343747489&sr=8-5&keywords=cuisinart+blade    someone has even posted a picture of a completely broken blade.  According to the online discussion, Cuisinart has not responded to complaints about this product flaw.  I personally did not try to contact them.
justification: The incident describes a blade failure with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred in this case. Multiple reports indicate this is a recurring issue.

incident_description:
The glass cover of the wok exploded sending glass all over the stove, counters and floor.  Cooking had been completed over 1 1/2 hours ago and the wok and cover were completely cool.  The handle on the lid had fallen into the wok and left a ring of shattered glass around the rim.

It is fortunate that no one was in the kitchen when it exploded, as it might have caused serious injury to the eyes, face and body.  The sound of the explosion could be heard outside of the house.
justification: The glass cover exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: my frigidaire dishwasher, model # PLDB998CC0 started to smoke than small flames came out the front panel, after i unpluged the dishwasher i removed the front panel an saw that the main circuit board had shorted out, causing the smoke and fire in the front, i have tried to get a replacement board but was informed by frigidaire the part is no longer made and frigidaire has no recall on the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved smoke and small flames from the dishwasher, but no injury or death was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but have been reported.

incident_description:
Maytag Gemini gas range (approximately 3 years old) turns its ovens on by itself, usually in the middle of the night.  This took us a while to figure out as it is located in our second home which is only used 9 weeks a year (summer).   For a while, we just thought we needed to cut power and reboot, but that doesn't solve the problem. As we reviewed our winter gas bills, the gas expense was hundreds of dollars higher the winter of 2010-11 (we threw the breaker panel this past winter).  To our horror we realized the oven was on most if not the entire winter at 350 degrees.  
Now Sears is going to install a new circuit board, (for $500) but are we to trust the new one anymore that the original one that was just about brand new?  The stove/oven has probably been used a total of 100 times over the past three years.  This is extremely dangerous and could easily start a fire.  I'm surprised we didn't lose our entire house the winter of 2010.
justification: The incident involves a gas range turning on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Unit experienced electrical problem upon the completion of a pre-heat cycle. A large "pop" was heard from behind the unit with the unit immediately appearing to lose power. A small amount of smoke was observed coming from underneath the control area. The smoke smelled of burning wire and quickly dissipated. The electrical service panel for the home was quickly inspected with the breaker for the electric range observed in the "tripped" position. The applicance was allowed to cool before being moved to inspect the rear of the unit. There was no obvious external damage visible. The cover of the terminal block area was removed with severe electrical and heat damage being observed at the "red" terminal connection. The "red" wire of the cord has completely burned through at the terminal connection with heat damage impacting the terminal block and discoloring the main "red" oven wire. All terminal nuts at the terminal block were loose with cord terminals allowed to move freely creating a fire and electrical hazard. The unit was installed by an unknown party prior to my purchase of the home. Lock nuts and/or lock washers were not used to secure the terminal ends to the terminal block and were not recommended or required within the manufacturer's installation instructions, but clearly in this instance would appear to have reduced the risk of fire and electrical hazards. This unit has been in service for residential use since January 2011.
justification: The incident involved electrical damage and smoke but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the observed hazards and improper installation.

incident_description:
My Maytag dishwasher's (model # MDBTT53AWW1) control panel shorted out after only 23 months of light use because the manufacturer failed to install a rubber gromett around the inlet holed in the power box.  This resulted when the wire insulation was cut due to the sharp metal in the junction box. This could have resulted in fire or an electrical shock.  Thankfully the control panel blew before that happened but Maytag will not stand behind their product since we did not buy an extend year warranty. They do not show that they have issued a recall for this type of problem with other dishwashers. There only recourse is for me to schedule a service call which is out of my pocket and the cost of the service call is more than I can buy the replacement control panel. 

I am glad this did not turn into a fire or an injury but it easily could have and wanted to voice my concern.  I imagine I am not the only one with this issue and if not, I would like my complaint to be added to any others if it prompts a product recall.  I have one year to return the control panel I am purchasing.  I will be checking for product recalls on your web site.  Thank you for providing consumers a voice since Maytag was not interested in hearing from me.
justification: The incident involved a control panel shorting out without resulting in injury or fire, but with potential for more severe outcomes.

incident_description:
Cusinart 12 cup programmable coffeemaker   Model DCC 1100  s/n 91020   Purchased 31 DEC 2009


Heating Plate turned red-hot and began vaporizing black non-stick coating. 


For your product engineers:
From: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermal_cutoff
"Thermal fuses are usually found in heat-producing electrical appliances such as coffeemakers and hair dryers. They function as safety devices to disconnect the current to the heating element in case of a malfunction (such as a defective thermostat) that would otherwise allow the temperature to rise to dangerous levels, possibly starting a fire."
justification: The coffeemaker's heating plate malfunctioned, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I own a Black and Decker Spacemaker White coffeemaker, Model #SDC740, on several occasions for no reason I will make the coffee and walk off, or set it to come on automatic in the morning and come back to the coffee grounds and hot water coming from the basket area and not going in to the pot but flowing all over the counter top.  This has happened approximately 12-13 times over the last year that we have owned the coffee maker.  We assumed we had done something wrong.  Both my husband and I have made the coffee and had this happen.  It makes a gigantic mess and coffee grounds go all down behind the counters and our white refrigerator.  The most recent time the coffee grounds went into the surge protector that we have all of our spacemaker appliances plugged in to.  So as a result of this coffee maker overflowing from the filter basket it has burnt out our toaster oven, coffee pot and grinder.  All 3 appliances do not work now and I spent over $250 on these Spacemaker appliances.  Again, I assumed that I had done something wrong, although for the life of me, neither myself nor my husband could figure out what that might be.  We always fixed the coffee to come on the evening before or that morning, always in the same manner and some mornings we would wake up to a lovely surprise of hot water and coffee grounds all over the granite countertops, tile floors and down the white refrigerator, not to mention inside tiny holes in the white coffee maker that it took forever to clean up, requiring a [REDACTED] and about 50 towels that than had to be washed.  The thing that caught my attention the last time it happened is it smelt like the house was on fire.  The coffee grounds had dripped into the surge protector (which is now black in the areas the appliances were plugged in), I assume than burning out all of the appliances connected into the surge protector (the spacemaker toaster oven and coffee bean grinder).  So, I went on the internet to search for new appliances, not at all thrilled that all of our appliances were ruined and found that Black and Decker had a recall in 2009 for a different model coffee maker with a very similar problem.  I would like for B&D to look into if it is possible that my model coffeemaker (SDC 740) could have the same problem with the basket shifting as the Consumer Release #09-252.  If so, I would appreciate it if Black and Decker would replace my  Spacemaker Coffee maker, Toaster Oven and Coffee Grinder with a different model that actually works, as it seems that all of the time and energy I have wasted cleaning up these huge messes in the mornings when I am in the biggest hurry is due to a faulty appliance and not human error!  Furthermore, had we not had our appliances plugged into a surge protector, our house would have caught on fire while we were sleeping and possibly burned the house down.  I would highly recommend that Black and Decker recall this product for this reason, all it would take is one other SDC 740 to have the same problem and be plugged into an outlet near the coffeemaker and someone could very easily die in a house fire while they sleep awaiting there fresh coffee to be made upon them waking up.  Again, if it happened to a product that they made in 2009 and it happened to me, it is highly likely that this product may be faulty and need to be recalled. My name is [REDACTED] and I can be reached at [REDACTED], my address is [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involves property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I have a kenmore elite dual fuel range model # 7907938. It is about 5 years old. Tonight while making dinner I preheated the oven and moments later I heard an electric crackling sound and smoke and flames were coming up from behind the top of the oven. My fiancÃÂ© had to grab the fire extinguisher and put the flames out before the cabinets and wall caught on fire. After the flames were put out the control board was completely blacked out and the oven no longer worked. Luckily we were in the kitchen when this occurred or we may have lost our home. After researching online about this issue, I have seen numbers complaints of the same exact incident with this model range. I have yet to see any recall of this product. How many complaints have to be reported in order for this to be recognized as a manufacture defect. If this issue is not addressed someone may loose their home or worse, a loved one.  
Please contact me with a response to this report.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injury or death occurred. Online complaints suggest this is a recurring issue with the model.

incident_description: Our Kenmore dishwasher caught fire in the control panel area of the door.  We had started it on our way out to the store, and our daughter was left by herself in her room.  When we returned, there was an awful smell in the kitchen.  The dishwasher had caught fire.  Fortunately, it had self-extinguished, and did not spread.  I have turned off the power at the breaker.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but self-extinguished without spreading or causing injury.

incident_description:
Kenmore Refrigerator model 106.53559202:

While in the kitchen, I heard crackling and popping sounds coming from underneath the refrigerator.  I soon noticed a bad smell and started seeing smoke come from behind the fridge.  I immediately turned the unit off; thankfully I happened to be standing right there when it happened.  To further troubleshoot, I took the bottom panel off the back so I could see if it was possible to determine what was wrong (thinking potentially the evaporator fan motor).  I turned the refrigerator on one more time and the fan worked, but within about 3 seconds there was the orange glow of fire from under the compressor.  Fire was extinguished with a fire extinguisher without further incident (except for a lot more smoke!).  I have a new fridge ordered.
justification: The incident involved visible fire and smoke, but no injury or death occurred as it was promptly extinguished.

incident_description: My kenmore oven glass door just exploded into a million pieces. It was not even on on. I have not used it in days and it just broke all up. There was no crack in it at all. I just cant believe it. I have never heard of this.
justification: The oven door exploded but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: On Wednesday, July 18th, I was baking pork chops in a Anchor Hocking Glass Baking Dish. I had lined the dish with aluminum foil for easier clean up. My husand removed the dish from the oven and placed in on the cooktop, which was not turned on, to put a meat thermometer in to check the temp. As he stood there waiting for the temp to read, we heard a pop and the glass dish exploded everywhere. It went all over the counter top and all the way across the kitchen floor. It is amazing he was not cut. I have a picture of the broken dish.
justification: The glass dish exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I work at a non-profit organization and we had a Black and Decker Toast-R-Oven. It caught on fire twice. Both times, someone put a piece of bread in to be toasted and walked to another area of the kitchen; they returned to find flames coming out of the toaster. After the first incident, we purchased a fire extinguisher to sit beside the toaster. After the second incident, we decided to throw away the toaster as it was burned on the front and clearly poses a fire hazard. I've found other complaints online about this product.
justification: The toaster caught fire twice, but no injuries were reported. The issue was addressed by removing the hazard.

incident_description:
I set the oven to 350 degrees to bake chicken.  Five minutes after placing the chicken in the preheated oven, there was a snapping sound from the oven.  I saw flashes and heard pops coming from the electronic instrument panel.  I attempted to push the stop button repeatedly, but it did not turn off the unit.  After approx. 5 seconds the instrument panel popped loudly and caught fire.  Luckily, we were able to put the fire out with a dry chemical fire extinguisher before there was any significant damage to the kitchen.  The oven instrument panel is destroyed and the unit is completely unusable.  

Kenmore Elite
Model 790.99123402
Serial VF44831499
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant damage to the oven, but no injuries or significant damage to the kitchen were reported.

incident_description:
Our refrigerator GE model GSS25QSTSS purchased in 3/2007 caught on fire today and left black soot covering the entire inside of both refrigerator and freezer compartments. Our condo tenant smelled something burning and traced it to the fridge. She saw the soot after unplugging the unit and opening the doors.  Upon researching the topic I come to find out there is a pending class action lawsuit on this topic.  

Luckily our tenant was at the condo when this happened and unplugged the unit.  I have taken pictures and written and email to GE. There are complaints like this all over the internet and even a you tube video of one fire. Something wrong is going on here with that many identical complaints, and very dangerous at that.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire but was unplugged in time, resulting in no injury or death, though the incident caused damage. The mention of numerous similar complaints suggests this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I own a Emerson microwave oven model # MWG9115SL that I purchased at wal-mart about a year and a half ago. We were using it one day and it started to spark really bad. We looked at it and finally figured out that some of the paint had peeled off of a screw in the top of the microwave that was holding a part on.
justification: The microwave sparked due to paint peeling off a screw, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using my Cuisinart Mini Prep Plus to chop toasted sliced bread (not rock hard dried bread, but lightly oven toasted bread), and while the machine was on, one of the blades broke off and broke through the bowl. It got wedged there, with about an inch of blade sticking out. As the bowl regularly dislodges itself, I typically keep my hands on the bowl, and had I been doing it at that time I would have sustained a serious injury to my hand or wrist. Upon further inspection of the blade, I found that it had rusted off. I never machine wash the parts of my food processor, and take good care of it.
justification: The blade broke and could have caused injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Sharp Microwave oven, Model # R520ks, Manufactured in April 2007
The glass door of our microwave shattered and exploded around our kitchen. The microwave was NOT in use at the time and at least 4 hours had passed since it had last been used. No one was near the microwave when it occurred so there was no external cause to explain the shattering of the glass door.
justification: The microwave door shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the refrigerator was not operating properly.  There is a cardboard plate that covers the lower part of the refrigerator where the compressor and fan is located which had caused the insulation to deteriorate. 

The consumer started experiencing problems with the unit not keeping a cold temperature around the first week of March.  There was also a clicking noise.  She discovered that the insulation had turned into dust particles which was on the fan and could have caused a fire.

3/2012 The consumer contacted the manufacturer through email but had not receive any response as yet.

The consumer feels that this refrigerator is a safety hazard due to the faulty design and should be recalled.

UPDATE:
The insulation that covers the back cardboard panel of the refrigerator turns/disintegrates into fine powder.  This powdery dust covers  the compressor fan motor as well as the evaporator pan, in which was full of this material.  The combination of dust and water along with the clogged compressor fan poses a serious risk of fire, injury and possible death, as the insulation dust prevents the compressor fan from operating properly.  There are several wires that became covered with (insulation) dust and water because the fan was running sporadically.  This product is dangerous.  I have enclosed a speciman/sample in order to illustrate the decomposition of the insulation material.  The sample is from the left side.  The right side of the panel was too fine to bag.
justification: The faulty design of the refrigerator poses a serious risk of fire, injury and possible death, as the insulation dust prevents the compressor fan from operating properly.

incident_description: The says the relay switch tries to kick the compressor on but it wont.  The consumer says all her food is spoiled and had to throw it all away.  The consumer says her unit is totally warm and wont cool anything.  The consumer says she is having the same issue as in Release # 09-145 but her last two characters of the serial number do not match.  The consumer says when she first purchased it she had to replace the refrigerator twice. Consumer Added:  Replaced because it was not cooling.

incident_description:
Accidental turning on burners of gas stove. The product is Whirlpool Gas Stove Model # GFG461LVS2,  SERIAL # R12820116. This product was installed by the builder of our new home as a standard option. Since February of this year there has been approximately 6 occurrences of accidentally turning on burner by brushing up against the burner control knob. This occurred without our awareness until we smelled gas fumes. Apparently just brushing up against knobs while working in kitchen, using microwave above stove, or using controls on back of stove pushed knobs in and rotated enough to open valve without igniting. These controls push in very easily and turn without resistant. Two women in our 60's occupy this home. We are of sound mind, aware of our surroundings and are not obese with big abdomens( I weigh 130 pounds and am 65 inches tall). I feel that just doing our routine cooking activities should not pose a potential hazard or even death! There is no way to lock these controls. I feel this is a very unsafe stove if there were children or elders in the home because it is a hazard to even us active, alert and careful adults.

I talked with Whirlpool and they said there is no problem with this product and advised to not lean against the knobs! 

I would like to get this info out hoping that it may prevent injury or even death to others. I plan on getting rid of this stove and will not purchase another Whirlpool appliance. I can afford to purchase another stove unlike a lot of other individuals. My conscious will not allow me to sale this stove. I will have someone cart it off to the dump.
justification: The incident describes multiple occurrences of gas leaks without ignition, posing a hazard but no injury or death.

Maytag Refigerator/freezer compressor controller failure.  Refigerator no longer cools or freezes contents.

The repairs cost $195.00 plus approx. $200.00 in food spoilage.

incident_description:
GE Profile Dishwasher - White
Model - PDW9800J00WW
Serial - MG767547B

After setting the dishwasher to wash the dishes and with approximately 10 minutes left to the cycle, my husband began smelling an intense burning plastic smell. When he opened the dishwasher to check, smoke was coming out of the door. He turned off the breaker and after opening the door to check for fire or melting, we found the large black junction box at the top right of the dishwasher door was melted and burned along with the wires that are attached to it. The box was extremely hot and we removed the box to avoid a fire. If we had not been home or had set it before bed, we would not have caught the burning and most likely would have had some type of house fire.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and smoke, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We purchase a GE Profile bottom freezer Refrigerator in 2007. The unit was completely replaced by GE after three service calls for the unit not being able to maintain temperature. The unit was replaced with same model in 2008 PFS22SISBSS with a new unit.  To this day, the unit barely keeps it correct temperature, and now we realize that we had been making excuses for the unit due to our teenagers using the product and possibly leaving the doors open.  Well, the fact of the matter is that we conducted an experiment while on vacation, and returned home after two weeks, to our unit being at 61 degrees, both freezer and fridge, and the unit was sealed for two weeks!
We are constantly throwing away spoiled items and have moved all frozen food to a freezer in our unattached garage (that [REDACTED] Refrigerator is over 10 years old!)
We purchased top- of- the-line appliances for our new home in 2007, sparing no expense and all appliances, dishwasher, refrigerator and stove/range have had a minimum of two service calls a piece!
We will never purchase from GE again, but do we have any further recourse??
If you [REDACTED] the Model number of the refrigerator, we are not alone in this identical and repetitive issue!
Thank you for any and all assistance in this matter.
[REDACTED]

incident_description:
Using a relatively new Crock Pot brand Crock-pot.  They product was purchased 6 mos ago.  I had the item on with a dinner inside and heard a pop.   After looking at the crockpot the entire lid was shattered and I had glass all over my food and the floor. I have small children and dogs, so the idea that they could have stepped on the glass before I had seen it scares me.  
I contacted the company who basically told me that I need to reread my manual, to learn how to use the product correctly.  They said they had never heard of this issue before, and never have cracked lids.  
I asked for my money back, as I have no confidence in their product.  I had previously had another brand before for over 10 years and had never had a problem.  They Crock Pot company refuses to give me my money back, stating the cracked lid was my fault.  They did send me an email after our phone conversation with a tracking number for a new lid.  
I am very fearful to ever use this produce again.
justification: The incident involved a shattered lid causing potential hazard, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the company claims this is a rare issue.

incident_description:
I purchased a Panasonic microwave oven in November of 2011. I recently noticed that the oven was becoming
increasingly hot when heating things in the oven. I noticed a charred area on the interior of the oven near the
magnetron. The plastic had partially melted and was blackened. The area was approximately 1 inch by by an inch
and a half. It appears to be located adjacent to the magnetron which is located on the right side of the oven behind
the control panel. There was also paint peeling on the left side of the oven on the upper left edge of the door and
the door opening. The item model number is NN-SN671 S. It was manufactured in September of 2011 in China. My
concern is that the area where the charred surface appears might begin burning and start a fire if the plastic reaches
its ignition point. I do not know whether this is an isolated incidence or whether similar units made in China will
experience similar episodes. I believe that this matter needs to be investigated in order to prevent a more severe
event such a fire to occur. Thank you for your consideration
justification: The incident involves a charred and melted area inside the microwave, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: My Frigidaire cooktop which I bought new in March of 2008 started getting stuck on high heat no matter which setting it was on. I would be able to just turn it off. Then it started sticking on high and I was not able to get it to shut off at all unless I turned the breaker off. I looked online to see if there were similar problems to mine. I found there was a recall on certain models for this very problem so I called Frigidaire but was told my cooktop was not among the ones under recall even though mine is doing the very thing the others were being recalled for. Evidently this is a recurring problem but they are not willing to stand behind their product. I am very disappointed in them and will not buy another Frigidaire product. I believe this to be a very serious problem on a cooktop that is not that old!
justification: The cooktop malfunctioned by staying on high heat, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I read with interest the Consumer Reports article on exploding 
Pyrex.  After decades of problem free Pyrex use, I had two incidents 
and my mother had one incident, for a total of three incidents within 
about two years.  In each case, the Pyrex was knocked while inside of 
a cabinet and the pieces went everywhere.  The good news is that no 
one was hurt because the explosions were contained by the 
cabinets.  The bad news is that it's still very dangerous because 
every food container in that cabinet had the potential to harbor a 
dangerous and invisible glass shard that could end up in a future 
meal.  Still, I'd rather dig glass shards out of cabinets than dig 
them out of people.

Incidentally, I have a Pyrex measuring cup that has completely lost 
its measurement markers.  They faded until they disappeared.  That 
tells me that the formula has changed not only for the glass, but 
also for the paint (or glaze).
justification: The description mentions three incidents with no injuries, but highlights potential danger from glass shards in food containers.

incident_description: I used my Pyrex glass 913 baking dish to bake brownies.  I removed it from the oven and placed it onto a wire rack to cool.  I then went to watch a movie in the next room.  About 20 minutes later, I heard ice exploding in my kitchen.  I discovered that it was the glass baking dish exploding not ice.  It was all over my kitchen in small gem-like pieces, small and large shards, and glass dust.  It also was embedded in the brownies which we threw away.  Thankfully, my son, who was sitting in the kitchen, was not hurt by the exploding glass.  This dish was purchased at a grocery store and came with a red plastic lid.  I believe it is called the "Easy-grab" pyrex brand.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a serious incident that could have caused injury.

incident_description:
We have a Black and Decker two slice, bagel toaster. Recently I heard a noise coming from the toaster after my toast was done. I tried jiggling the main button. Hit the stop button and the bagel button. Nothing stopped the buzzing noise. Eventually I unplugged the toaster to get it to stop. incident_description: We woke up to the smell of smoke.  We discovered smoke coming from the freezer part of our frigerator.  We called [REDACTED], who we have a service guard with, and the repair man noted that the heating element in the freezer (used to defrost the appliance) was in contact with plastic.  He noted that the paint had been burned and the plastic was melted causing the smoke.  Whirlpool said they were unable to do anything because I had not called them first.  The appliance was purchased Summer of 2010 from Lowes.

incident_description:
Normal use heating water with microwave only. Bright Electrical arcing was seen coming from the oven electronic control cabinet, NOT the cooking area.

A fire started in the interior of the oven electronic area. After burning for awhile, main power to the unit was cut off at the dedicated circuit breaker for the oven and the fire then went out.

Following disassembly and troubleshooting of the oven it was determined that massive electrical arcing emanating from the magnetron had electrically burned and welded closed the door safety switch and the control cabinet thermal cutoff switch.

The result was a runaway failure condition which destroyed system safeguards, allowed the unit to operate WHILE THE DOOR WAS OPEN and allowed an overheat fire condition to persist while NOT shutting down power automatically.

Thousands of internet messages are indicating trouble with arcing and thermal cutoff switches in the Advantium series of microwave ovens.

Model number SCA2001KSS a 220 volt unit manufactured in 2008
justification: The incident involved a fire due to electrical arcing and system safeguard failures, posing a significant risk of injury or property damage.

incident_description: We have a kenmore refrigerator, model number 795.77319600. The lights will staay on whenever they please. We have to unplug the refrigerator to reset the lights. The top light cover has completely melted off the screws, big chunks of the center plastic is now missing, and it hangs now from just the wires. incident_description: We purchased a new home from a builder in May 2011 and opted for the appliance package.  The package included Kenmore products to include a dishwasher, glass/smooth top stove and built-in microwave.  Whenever we would wash dishes in the dishwasher it seemed like it took forever, but we never really gave it a second thought.  On July 8, 2012, upon returning home my daughter washed two loads of dishes.  At some point during that time, I walked into an area adjacent to the breakfast bar and found that my carpet was soaked to the point that water squished out and over my foot.  This area is on the other side of where the dishwasher is installed under the breakfast bar.  At first I thought maybe my dog had soiled the carpet, but I realized that there was too much water in the area for this be the case.  I immediately opened the cabinet doors and looked under the sink to see if there was a leak but the area under the sink was dry.  I then removed the screws from the kick plate of the dishwasher and there was a pool of water standing in the area under the dishwasher.  When my builder installed the hardwoods in the kitchen, he left the area under the dishwasher clear and it actually created an area the width and length of the dishwasher where there is no flooring and you can see the concrete slab foundation under the house.  Well, this area was flooded like a small swimming pool.  I guess with washing several loads the water had filled the area and the overflow traveled under my breakfast bar and onto the carpet area on the other side.  I called the plumber to report the leak thinking that this was a plumbing issue.  When the plumber arrived the next morning and looked under the dishwasher, the water was gone.  I guess it had soaked into the foundation.  He told me after looking at the dishwasher that the dishwasher was the culprit.  He was right.  When the technician arrived and inspected the dishwasher he stated that the element was bent and that the element had actually burnt a hole in the vinyl tub (as strong and thick as it is).  When I explained that in the past the dishwasher ran a long time, he stated that it was because the hole was allowing water to escape and it took longer to fill up.  He stated that this was a defect in the dishwasher and that it could quite possible a fire hazard.  Upon looking at several websites and the government website it seems that Sears has had problems in the past with their dishwashers and I even spoke to someone who told me to they had a Kenmore dishwasher and the same thing happened to them with the element.  Then I met a person in a [REDACTED] who said they would never buy Sears or any product they sell because their dishwasher actually caught on fire and that my incident may have possibly escalated into a situation that cause a fire or electrocution if during the time I stepped into the water I picked up an electrical apparatus.  I have contacted both Sears, their claims department and my builder.  No one wants to replace the liner or the dishwasher, although with the dishwasher burning out (so to say) only after one year of use and just as the warranty ended, do I really want to buy another Sears product and subject myself to the same thing next year - quite possibly.  As the technician stated, although the flooding didn't occur until 2 months after the 1 year warranty ended, the burning happened over time and there was no way I or my 16 year old daughter could have bent the element, especially since we don't wash cast iron or other pots and pans in the thing.  My safety concern is that this could cause have caused a fire or electrocution - as someone pointed out.
justification: The incident involved property damage (flooding) and a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
When I turned the heat from Hi to 8 on the left front burner of my cook top, I saw sparks behind the control panel directly behind the knob. I tried to look behind the panel (without pulling the stove away from the wall), but I didn't see fire or smoke. I made note of where the fire extinguisher was and kept an eye on the range, checking it throughout the evening. Nothing else seemed to happen.

I called Sears tonight about it; the gentleman suggested I go to www.searshomeservices.com/chat to talk with a technician. I did that, but the person with whom I chatted seemed not to be a technician but a saleswoman. For $256.79 I could have someone come look at the range as many times as I wanted for a year, and if they couldn't fix it, they'd give me a coupon for $500 toward a new range. 

We purchased the range in April 2010. I feel this is a manufacturer's safety issue, even though it is out of warranty.

I am worried about using the cook top, especially after hearing that others have had problems with the wiring and burners.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a burning odor but no actual fire or injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recurring nature of similar issues reported by others.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was not experiencing any problems with the dishwasher prior to these two incidents.

On 4/8/12 the consumer started the wash cycle and it was running fine. She was in the kitchen ten minutes later (ten minutes into the dishwailling cycle) and smelled smoke. It was immediately discovered that it was coming from the dishwasher. When the door of the dishwasher was opened, smoke poured into the kitchen. The consumerÃÂs husband
immediately shut down the power to the kitchen island at the point of the main circuit breaker in the basement.

4/9/12 the manufacturer was contacted and the consumer was advised that a service rep would be sent out, without a charge, to the consumer.

On 4/12/12 a service rep visited and dismantled the door panel to reveal an electronic control board that was melted and burned. The service rep said he was authorized to replace the burned out control board in the door without charging the consumer any of the costs. Prior to this service call, the consumer had researched and learned of numerous
problems with the electrical control units (including a class action lawsuit for the exact electrical board of the same model KitchenAid dishwasher) and therefore insisted that the same control panel unit would not be acceptable. The service rep provided the different part nmaber, with different number of digits (compared to the part number of the first control panel), and stated that he was certain that the part was from a different manufacturer. The control panel was replaced with the new part.

6/28/12 (ten weeks later) the dishwasher was run in the morning, unloaded and sitting empty (and ofT) for hours. In the middle of the day, the consumer again smelled smoke, and through searching the house, again discovered that the dishwasher was emitting smoke. Again, the circuit breaker was shut down at the main control panel and again the manufacturer was contacted. This time, the consumer stated that she would not allow for any parts to be swapped out. The manufacturer stated they would agree to pro-rate the cost of the seven year old dishwasher and provide the consumer that money in the form of credit toward another Kitchen Aid dishwasher. The consumer declined th.e offer. The company arranged for a service rep to visit the home and look at the dishwasher.

On 7/6/1.2 a different service rep (from a different company) came to the house and dismantled the door and discovered that the new electrical control panel had two areas of melted wires and the heat/fire had burned the insulation casing across from the wire bundles. The service rep explained that "this is how theyÃÂre made" and that itÃÂs "because of all the heat" normally generated during the wash cycle. The consumer questioned the logic of a design that would cause the wires to burn during the normal functioning. The service rep then suggested instead that it "was an act of God" and. recommended that he be allowed to simply replace the electrical control board (this time there was a charge for
that service). The consumer declined to allow the service rep to do anything and he left.  

Several calls have been made to the KitchenAid company, by the consumer and her husband. No response has been received.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and potential fire hazard from the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

Cuisinart continues to sell these, they should include a warning that the unit never be left unattended due to

The consumer stated that the technician came over to service the range, but no repairs were done because they wanted to charge. The consumer stated that the technician stated that the problem was with the control panel. 

The consumer stated that she believes this product should be investigated because of the fire hazard that it poses.
justification: The incident caused smoke damage but no injuries or need for emergency services, fitting severity level 2. The recurring malfunction suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Heard two or three loud pops shortly after the dishwasher started, saw black smoke coming from the vent holes. I cut off power at the circuit breaker but there still seemed to be a glow behind the control panel so I called 911. The firefighters said the control panel had shorted out.

KitchenAid Undercounter Dishwasher, Model KUDROITJWH, serial FL1012252, purchased 4/14/2003.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My kitchen aid microwave model KHMS155LSS-4 started operating in the middle of the night on its own with the word "Pan" displayed on the keypad. When I cancelled the operation, the microwave stopped and had a F-2 Code displaying. The microwave restarted after some time and ran for a couple of minutes before I woke up again and stopped the microwave. I have since unplugged the microwave so it will not continue starting and stopping on its own.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by operating on its own, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
My daughter cut her head on her sippy cup. It is a bunny sippy cup that we bought from Target. She cut her head between her eyes at the top of her nose. This caused crying and bleeding. We did not take her to the hospital at first because we got the bleeding to stop and it was around 9pm at night. After speaking with her pediatrician we were advised to take her to the hospital for stitches. 

I looked up the cup online to report that it is hazardous and found that it had been recalled in April of this year. I had no idea that it had been recalled or I would have not let my child use it.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut that caused bleeding and required medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The tools of the trade basic cookware set that is sold by [REDACTED] gave me a 2nd degree burn. I have been out of work for a week and I do not know when I will be able to return back to work. The handle from the pot broke off of the pot that I was boiling water in as I was taking the pot from the stove to the counter. The hot scolding water spilled on to my leg and as a result I have a 2nd degree burn. It is very painful and I can only walk for a short period of time, before I begin suffer severe pain. Other have stated that they also had problems with the handle breaking off since 2010 until now. I do not want anyone else to suffer what I am currently going through.
justification: The incident resulted in a 2nd degree burn and inability to work, indicating an injury. Reports of similar handle breakages since 2010 suggest the issue is likely to occur.

incident_description:
-Yes - I put the dish on oven- was using two dishes and have little counter room.  The consumer says she placed baking dish on burner.  It had not been used yet.  She accidentally turned on the burner.  After a couple of seconds she heard a loud pop sound.  

She thought she turned back burner on to boil water for pudding recipe

She says the glass dish exploded.  The consumer says had she not moved to make a phone call the dish would have exploded on her face.  

The consumer says there are burn marks on her kitchen floor tile.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding but no injury occurred, only burn marks on the floor.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchase a glass dish set of 4 pieces. The consumer stated that her partner went to remove the dish out of the oven and the glass dish exploded. The consumer stated that the glass dish was inside the oven for approximately 10 minutes at a 350 degrees temperature. 

The consumer stated that as he was removing the dish it exploded splattering glass all over her kitchen. She stated that her partner covered his face, fell back knocking her to the wall and landing on the floor. The consumer stated that her partner hurt his back, and suffered cuts on his right arm. 

The consumer stated that her partner did not receive any medical attention. The consumer stated that she hit her side when she was pushed to the wall. 

The consumer stated that the glass splatter approximately 5ÃÂ away from the oven. She stated that there is glass all over her floor and the pieces of glass were stuck inside the linoleum flooring. The consumer stated that there were also burnt marks on the linoleum. 

The consumer will be contacting the manufacturer to file a complaint.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts and back pain) but no medical attention was required, placing it at severity level 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described circumstances.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the electric range was used.  After using it, his spouse attempted to power it off the front right burner but she could not do so.  The circuit breaker was used to switch the unit off.  The consumer stated that they are experiencing similar problems of Release # 09-333.  There were no prior problems or services for this range.

7/13/12 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that their model was not part of the recall.  He was informed also that a service technician would be sent out at a charge to the consumer.

The consumer feels that this range is fire hazard and should be included in the recall.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range that could not be turned off normally, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Baking in kenmore range, model 665.92002102, baking at 350 degrees for 34 min. per recipe instructions. Something failed in the circuitry or electronics of the range and the broiler came on at some point which was unknown to us. We noticed smoke coming from range and took out baked dish and tried to shut oven off by cancel off switch on range panel. Broiler/oven would not shut off, just kept getting hotter.Had to pull range out from counter and pull electrical plug to turn off broiler/oven.This is a significant fire hazard. If we had not been home and had set to "timed bake", could have caused fire and burned house down!!! We did [REDACTED] search and found there have been numerous complaints listed online regarding this problem with this model kenmore range and similar model numbers in this classification of kenmore electric ranges. See for yourself, [REDACTED] search this model kenmore range.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that posed a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer said that the handles on her stainless steel pans have come loose, while she was using them.  The handles have completely separated from 2 or 3 of the pans and a total of 5 pans have or had loose handles.  

The consumer stated that her pans appear to be similar to the ones in CAP# 03-069, but she only recently found out about recall by using the Internet.  Although her frying pans have not exploded, the consumer is now more concerned that they may present an explosion hazard and/or a handle separation hazard.  Some of the pans have fallen down on her stove due to handle separation or loosening, but she has not sustained any injuries.

The consumer said that she paid $500.00 dollars for this set of cookware and it was even was sold with an additional pan that matches the set.

(6/2012)  The consumer saw that the recalling firm is out of business (based on CPSC CAP# 03-069) but she went back to the retailer to see if they would be willing to assist her.  The consumer said that the retailers' representatives  were rude to her and made fun of the fact that the cookware was old.  The consumer said that the  rep. were not willing to assist her with her safety concerns.

The consumer noted that this cookware came with a lifetime warranty.  She understands that the firm is out of busies, but based on the potential safety hazards with her pans, the retailer should be willing to replace them wish a  a comparable set of cookware.
justification: Handles have separated or loosened, causing pans to fall, but no injuries have occurred. The issue is likely to recur given the product's defect and lack of manufacturer support.

incident_description:
In the early morning hours of June 21, 2012, the inside of our Kenmore refrigerator model number 106.50522101 and serial number SM1231180 spontaneously caught fire.  Fortunately the home was spared any obvious damage, as the fire was contained within the freezer compartment of the unit.  My wife and I woke to a plastic burning smell and soon discovered that it had been the inside of the freezer portion of the refrigerator.  All our food was obviously ruined, and we were concerned for the health of ourselves and our infant due to the toxic fumes released from the burning plastic.  We immediately opened all windows and and turned on all fans in an effort to get the burnt plastic fumes out of the home.  I have attempted to work through the "customer solutions" department already, however due to my inability to produce the receipt for this refrigerator (purchased in or around 2002 and transferred to us when we purchased the home 4 years ago), they claim to be unable to assist with this matter.

This is a major safety hazard and could easily have resulted in loss of our home or even the loss of life.  Whether the unit is still under warranty or not, this is obviously not an acceptable risk and certainly raises fears about the other appliances in our home that are made by the Sears company as well.  The unit was apparently manufactured by Whirlpool, however they have been unresponsive to contact as well.
justification: The incident involved a fire contained within the refrigerator, causing property damage and health concerns but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The plastic handle on the glass lid of my Rival Crock-Pot (model 38501) broke while lifting the lid off of the crock-pot during cooking.  This caused the glass lid to be dropped back onto the stone base of the crock-pot.  In order to open the lid a utensil was needed to pry the lid off of the crock-pot which exposed the consumer to the steam inside the crock-pot.  The breaking handle appears to present a risk of cuts by broken glass and burns.

There are multiple reports of these handles breaking on the internet across multiple models of Rival Crock-Pots.  This web site is a good example of other consumer's experiences http://www.fixya.com/support/t264593-need_plastic_handle_rival_crockpot_lid
justification: The incident involves a broken handle leading to potential cuts and burns, but no actual injury was reported. Multiple reports indicate this is a common issue.

incident_description:
In April 2011, my dishwasher stopped working.  There had been a "hot" smell in the kitchen that I hadn't associated to the dishwasher until we looked at the control board and wiring.  There was a brown spot on the control board indicative of overheating; some of the wires had bare spots on them and a plastic guard / plate was melted to the shape of the wires.

I contacted KitchenAid and said that I was concerned that this was a safety issue; it seems to me that an electrical overload that doesn't throw a fuse or have some other safeguard but instead allows overheating and melting of wires / plastic is a concern.  They sent a repair person out to evaluate but did not cover the cost of any repairs as it was out of warranty and not a safety or fire hazard.  I told them I could fix the appliance, but the root cause would not have been addressed.

They told me in an e-mail that "we cannot explain what factors have contributed to your concern since no recalls or known issues are present with this model" and "because there was no fire or smoke, this is not considered a safety issue at this time".  

Now - a year later - the board has again failed.  Again, they will not acknowledge any quality issues or safety concerns with this product.  

There have been several reports on your site and others for KitchenAid dishwashers, some with actual fires reported so I guess we were lucky; but perhaps the models use a similar design and share components.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting of wires and plastic, but no injury or fire occurred, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the issue and similar reports suggest a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Kenmore countertop microwave oven starts when the door is opened, even when the unit is off but plugged in.  To use the unit safely, you now have to unplug it before opening the door, and plug it in only after the door is closed.  This is the second identical unit of this model we've had, the first one was returned under warranty but had the same problem after only a few months of use.  The current unit began to experience this problem after 3.5 yrs of ownership.
justification: The microwave starts unexpectedly when the door is opened, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
This morning I was making pancakes on my Whirlpool Super Capacity 465 Range.
While using the front left burner set at # 5 (medium) within 20 seconds it began to glow red got so hot the pan itself was smoking.
I immediately turned off the burner.
I decided to test to make sure it wasnt a fluke so I let the burner cool completely down and turned it back on to 5.  the same thing happened.
To further verify that there is something wrong, I turned it off, cooled down and turned on ALL burners to #5 (which is medium heat) and ALL burners began to glow red AND smoke.
I turned everything off, unplugged the stove, waited 2 hours, plugged the range back in and repeated my experiment.  Sure enough, it happend again.

I feel that this poses an EXTREME fires danger AND extreme risk for accidental but severe burn injuries.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that poses a fire hazard and risk of burns, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Frigidaire gas range oven not working smell gas. Called a technician to repair oven was told that oven gas valve not working.
justification: The incident involves a gas leak, which is a serious hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While the dishwasher was not in use  when he the consumer noticed a electric burning odor. The consumer did not see any smoke coming from the appliance. When he got closer to the dishwasher that was when he noticed that the odor was at  its strongest. 

The circuit breaker was powered in the off position.  The consumer indicated that he had not used the appliance in over a month when the failure occurred. He opened the door to the dishwasher and did not see any damages inside.

On 2/26/2012 the consumer hired a private electrician to take a look at the appliance. The electrician advised the consumer to leave the circuit breaker off and not use the dishwasher because it posed as a fire hazard. 

The firm was contacted on 2/27/2012 and the consumer was advised that he would be required to pay to  have a service technician come out. The consumer declined and stated that he will not make any repairs to the appliance but instead will replace it.

The circuit breaker is still powered in the off position and he has not attempted to use the appliance since the failure occurred.
justification: The incident involved an electric burning odor but no visible damage or injury, and the dishwasher was not in use at the time.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the food chopper operates without the lid when it is turned on.  She accidentally hit the button while the unit was open and it started to operate (blades moving) which could have caused injury to her hands. 
The consumer had other food choppers before which would not operate without the lid on.  Without a safety mechanism in place that this unit cannot operate with open lid consumers are at the risk of being injured.
 She had returned the first one to the firm thinking it was defective which was replaced by the second one which has the same mechanism in place.  She feels that this food chopper is a safety hazard
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard where the food chopper operates without the lid, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I was making my daily amount of coffee (6 cups as measured on the carafe) in the coffee maker as usual when, just as it appeared to have finished the brew cycle, I heard popping noises from across the room and began to smell a putrid smoke.  It sounded different from the noise moisture makes when it gets under the carafe, so I thought something might be wrong immediately.  When I got over to the coffee maker, I thought initially that the gfi circuit had blown because the clock and "ON" indicator light were both off, but as I pulled the plug, a visible spark occurred.  When I pulled the carafe out, I noticed that a portion of the circumference of the warming plate was glowing orange and smoking heavily.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker with visible sparks and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.
