incident_description: Client was using a Sunbeam 6 Quart Aluminum Pressure Cooker when the handle broke. The pressure cooker fell to the floor and exploded, a piece of which severed her leg. A man used a belt as a tourniquet to stop the bleeding until the paramedics arrived. Client was also covered in the boiling liquid.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injury (severed leg) and potential life-threatening situation, warranting a severity level of 4. The occurrence likelihood is low (2) as such catastrophic failures are rare.

incident_description: My kitchenaid microwave hood combination turned on spontaneously. I could not turn it off with the controls. It was displaying the word PAN. If I opened the door it would stop but beep annoyingly. If I closed the door it would start again. I found many, many reports of this on comsumer affairs.com. the model number is khms155lss. The only way I could turn it off was through the circuit breaker, as I could not pull out the u it to u plug. if I had not been home when this happened it may have well caused a fire.
justification: The microwave turned on spontaneously and could not be turned off normally, posing a potential fire hazard if unattended, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased our new home in August 2007. As part of our negotiation, the builder provided us with a Kenmore Elite Trio refrigerator, model 795.77573600, Serial No, 707KR00060. 

We have recently discovered the bulbs not coming on when doors are open. We removed the bulbs and after testing them, we noticed they were fine and noticed the bulb housing getting very hot. We are extremely concern about melting/potential fire problem. 

Please tell us what to do before our house gets burned down.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to overheating bulb housing, but no actual injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The cosumer says the control panel caught on fire.  The unit was on for about an hour and thirty minutes before the incident.  The control panel and the door were both scorched and blackened.  

He has yet to contact the manufacturer.
justification: The control panel caught fire, causing damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she walked into the kitchen and could smell something burning.  The dishwasher was just ending its cycle.  A few days later she tried to turn it on and could once again smell an electrical burning smell. 

She is afraid to try to turn it back on cause of a possible fire hazard.  

She contacted the manufacturer on March 29th and was told not run the unit in its current state.  They told her that the unit is not on recall and there was nothing that could be done.  They are no longer taking her calls.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard with no injury reported, and the likelihood is high given the recurring burning smell and manufacturer's warning.

incident_description: The front left burner of the Kenmore smooth top electric range will often not stay on the level set by the knob. The temperature will increase to high or what seems hotter than high. This poses a fire hazard and is dangerous for the user. I called sears to see if the product was on the recall list as other very similar models have been recalled, and was told curtly that my product was not on the recall list. When I said I would like to report an issue about the burner and see about repairs the customer service rep began their closing script and disconnected the call, so I was unable to get further information or report the malfunction as an issue.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard and is dangerous, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her oven was placed on 325 degrees.  In approximately 5 mins the oven became extremely hot she felt that it would start house fire.  The control panel was used to power off the unit but that did not work.  Her spouse reached underneath the oven and disconnected the electrical power.

The consumer stated that there was smoke emitting from the vent of the oven, which dispelled into the kitchen.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The consumer feels that this electric range/oven is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says she was baking cookies at 350 degrees.  Suddenly on its own, the broiler came on.  She is concerned because had she not been in the area, the situation could have been worse.  

The consumer says this happened without warning.  She says on the display panel it showed that it was baking although it was not.  The consumer says this happens within a few minutes of the oven being on at 350 degrees.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer today 6-13-12, who said they would arrange an appointment for a fee.  The issue is similar to what is listed in Release # 09-333.  her model is not included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved the broiler activating unexpectedly, but no injury occurred. The issue is known and similar to a previous release, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
On 6/10/2012, the consumerÃÂs oven was placed on the setting of 7 and used for a couple minutes. The consumer later turned the setting down, but the temperature would not decrease. He started to hear loud sounds inside of the oven and when he opened it, he saw sparks inside.  The consumer quickly closed the oven door and turned the stove off.
 
The stove was serviced under CAP# 09-333 in 2009 and the relay board corrected or replaced.
 
The consumer contacted the manufacturer 6/11/2012 and they advised him that the warranty for the recall work under release# 09-333 was for 30 days.  The mfr. was not willing to do anything further.
 
The consumer feels that the product is a potential fire hazard. He also feels that the recalled part should be covered for a free repair no matter how many times the parts fail.  The consumer is concerned that the stove may present a fire hazard and/or electrical safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved sparks and loud sounds in the oven, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite model # 795.77566300 SN# 802KR03493. The interior lights stayed on when we were away from home. When we returned I smelled hot plastic. When I looked at the light cover it was melted. After one week the lights come on only intermittently. I am afraid they will stay on again and maybe cause a complete meltdown and fire. This refridgerator is a $2000 +/- unit and should not have these issues. It is supposed to be top-of -the-line, not to mention the obvious safety issue.
justification: The incident involves a melted light cover and intermittent operation, indicating a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death.

incident_description:
Kenmore Dishwasher obtained as replacement one that failed in 2002 (he can't remember month)

This replacement dishwasher caught fire.

Caller's wife started dishwasher in evening Sunday, June 3rd, 2012, walked out of the kitchen for approximately 20 to 30 minutes to watch television.

Caller's wife's sense of smell has diminished so she didn't smell any odor, however, when she returned to the kitchen there was smoke billowing out of the vent on top of the dishwasher.

She opened the door and immediately a flame shot out of door by the seam of the control panel on right.

At that time caller came in and cut the power to the dishwasher by tripping the breaker.

Manufacturer was contacted immediately after this incident, service tech was schedule for June 7th, 2012 and has been to the house.

The service tech advised caller that manufacturer would replace the part responsible for fire.

Dishwasher is under extended warranty.

Caller does not feel safe with repair of this part and is requesting CPSC assistance with obtaining a replacement dishwasher of a different brand or at the very least a different model at manufacturer expense.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On 4/02/2012 The consumer was using the left front burner at a temperature of 3.5 (out of a level of ten) degrees. She was only using one burner at the moment of the incident and the oven was not in use. The consumer stated that prior to the incident the right front burner was not working properly.  

The consumer was using the range for approximately 12 minutes before the oven glass door completely exploded. The glass shattered out across hitting the consumerÃÂs legs, and scattering about 10-15 feet away from the oven.  

The consumer immediately turned off the burner and she did not see any other signs of damages to the range.  The interior glass door was still intact.  

The consumer used the product after the incident. She has only used the burners, not the oven. 
The consumer was not injured and there were no damages to her home. 

04/02/2012 The consumer contacted the retailer and they stated they would send a technician. The technician was supposed to come service the product 04/04/2012. The technician never showed and he only called to state that he would order a part to service the range. He stated he would be coming to fix the range on 4/11/2012.
justification: The oven glass door exploded, but the consumer was not injured and there were no damages to her home.

incident_description: Electric burner remained on after switched of. I had to un-plug the range to turn the burner off. Later I plugged the range back in to check & the burner immediately turned on.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
On Saturday, July 7, 2012 while warming up lunch for my husband, myself and my husband's daughter and her husband and two small children, my step-daughter and I were in the kitchen working while lunch was warming up. The oven was set at 350 degrees. There was a LOUD pop! Very scary! I carefully opened the oven door and was shocked to see the glass on the door had shattered.  We were very fortunate that the glass shattered inside and did not explode into the kitchen were we were working.
I have put a call and sent an email to Sears [REDACTED] the representative who help with the quote on our new appliances for our new home that was just built and we moved in about 2 months ago.  Sears is sending our a technician to only look at the oven before deciding what they will do. It is taking Sears 10 days to come look at the damaged oven. There is nothing to assure us that this will not happen again and at this point we do not want another Sears Kenmore electric oven/convenction oven in our home. The product is Model No. 790.92903
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express her concerns about her electric range as the oven's broiler element will turn on sporadically and warm to almost excessive temperatures. The consumer stated that this has happened 5 times within the last month. The consumer ordinarily has to try to power off the broiler at the digital panel repeatedly until the model shuts off. However, last night the consumer experienced the problem and the range would not respond to commands at the digital interface.

 The range was set to bake at 350 degrees, for 5-10 minutes before the broiler element turned on. The consumer's husband had to power off the range at the circuit breaker and has not powered the range back on. The consumer went online and found an abundance of reports similar to her incidents. The consumer has not called the fire department or her home insurance company. The consumer started that range appears to be fine.

 The consumer has not sustained any property damage. The consumer has not been harmed or injured by the product.  The consumer called the retailer today and was informed that her product was not on recall and offered no further. The consumer has yet to call the firm.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range with no reported injuries or property damage, but it poses a potential hazard.

incident_description:
On 6/24/2012 the consumer had her dishwasher on the anti bacterial setting and was running for approximately 15 minutes. While in another room she heard a loud pop, which caused her dogs to start barking. She immediately went into the kitchen, where she saw flames coming from the control panel. The consumer used a fire extinguisher to put out the flames. She never unplugged the unit because she didn't know how. There were no surrounding damages in the kitchen, but the entire dishwasher was destroyed.

The consumer stated that this was the 1st issue that she had with the dishwasher.

The manufacturer was contacted 6/25/2012 and the consumer was transferred through different departments. She finally got in contact with someone whom let her explain the situation, but didn't ask any questions nor did they giver her a  report number of any kind.

The consumer then contacted a local repair place (RC Appliances) and they came out to her home on 6/26/2012. After the technician inspected the unit he determined that the control panel was the cause and the entire unit needed to be replaced.  

The consumer has a home warranty whom she would later contact in regards to getting a replacement since the manufacturer has not offered any assistance.
justification: The incident involved flames and property damage but no injuries, and it was the first issue with the dishwasher, indicating it's unlikely to recur frequently.

incident_description: Kenmore dishwasher just started smoking almost caught fire. Dishwasher was not running when it started smoking and had to go cut main power off the get it to stop
justification: The dishwasher started smoking and almost caught fire, indicating a significant incident but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I took a Pyrex 2 cup bowl from the refrigerator that had a little over a cup of leftover rice in it. I added a pat of butter and put it in the microwave. About 40 seconds into it the bowl shattered into pieces some large some shards. The bowl was less than 1 month old purchased as a 4 piece set.
The bowl was uncovered and the microwave small.

When i went to the Pyrex site it spends a lot of time trying to debunk the "myth" of exploding dishes. All i can say is that i was surprised and saddened. I left them an email and never heard from them. These things present some form of danger. It would be nice if that was acknowledged by them.
justification: The bowl shattered but there was no mention of injury, only surprise and sadness.

incident_description:
I purchased a Good Cook kitchen strainer from Kroger grocery store in Nashville, Tennessee. On July 6th cut my hand on a Good Cook kitchen strainer purchased at KrogerÃÂs. My finger is still red, bleeding, and irritated. I was injured when i washed the strainer by one of two metal bars on the bottom of the metal mesh strainer that were razor sharp. The cut is fairly deep. ÃÂ I reported the incident to the store as well to the corporate offices of Kroger. I have yet to have anyone follow up on the matter as far as contact goes. Any contact that has been made has been made by me. I also made contact with the company who manufactures the Good Cook kitchen strainer. Thus far I have only been contacted in order to provide my phone number and address. I have pictures of my injury. I have sent pictures of my injury to KrogerÃÂs. The cut seems to be closing but still has puss.
A label should warn of the sharp edges on the product if the product is to remain on the shelf. I would like to know that someone other than a customer service representative or a secretary has been made aware of my injury and the productÃÂs defect.
justification: The incident caused a deep cut that is still bleeding, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
OXO Product #1064468 - Splatter Screen

I was using this product while frying bacon.  The collapsible handle (for easy storage) does not lock into position when using while cooking.  When I picked up the splatter screen while cooking (very hot), the screen part collapsed backwards onto my arm, burning it in 3 places.  My burns (first degree) are now peeling causing scabbing (may result in scarring).  I did not seek medical attention (but used over the counter ointments to treat my burns).  The handle should lock into position while using so that the screen part does not move (the handle and screen act as one unit).
justification: The incident resulted in first-degree burns that required treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Euro Pro T0161 Toaster Oven

The timer will not shut off.  It runs past zero until it gets to the Manual "on" setting and
then automatically turns the Toaster Oven on.  The consumer has turned the oven "off"  
but as a result of this timer defect, the toaster oven comes on and stays on.

This is a very serious fire hazard.  The toaster oven gets hot on the outside when it is on and
anything left in contact with the oven has the potential to catch on fire.

This item needs to be recalled.  I have spoken with the company and they seem unconcerned!!
justification: The toaster oven's defect poses a serious fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The caller stated that after using the blender for approximately 10 mins, it erupted into flames. It was not running when it erupted into flames.  He immediately unplugged it and placed it in the sink with water to extinguish the flames. While blending the contents he did not detect any unusual odor to indicate any fire.  There were no prior incidents.


6/2012 The caller stated that he attempted to contact the manufacturer but he was unable to reach a working phone number. 


The caller feels that this blender is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The blender erupted into flames but no injuries were reported, and the incident was isolated with no prior occurrences.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was placing a towel on the upper handle of the range. She stated that they are 5 oval holes above the handles that measured approximately 3/8ÃÂ by 5ÃÂ. The consumer stated that when she placed the towel on the handle her left hand little finger was caught on one of the holes. The consumer stated that the hole had very sharp edges. 

The consumer stated that she received a 1/8ÃÂ laceration on her left hand little finger. The consumer stated that she added pressure to stop the bleeding. She stated that it took approximately 2 hours for the bleeding to stop. The consumer then proceeded to add antibiotic ointment and a band aid to treat the laceration. The consumer stated that she did not have to go to emergency room. 

5/30/2012 The consumer stated that the manufacturer stated that they would send a technician to repair the machine. The consumer stated that the technician went to her home on 5/31/2012 and stated that he order a part to repair the part. The technician stated that he would be replacing the part on 6/11/2012.

The consumer stated that this product should be investigated do to the laceration hazard that it poses to the consumers.
justification: The consumer sustained a 1/8” laceration requiring first aid, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident is possible (likelihood 3) given the sharp edges on the product.

incident_description: We purchased a home two years ago and a Bosch stainless steel dishwasher was already installed. We believe this product was purchased about 5 years ago. Over the weekend the dishwasher lost all power while running a cycle. I discovered one of the main power wires and nut melted completely. Upon doing research I found the Jan 15, 2009 recall notice on it. My dishwasher is SHU43C05UC/14, which is one of the recalled models. I've called the hotline to see if I still have any options and have yet to speak with anyone there.
justification: The dishwasher lost power due to a melted wire, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Burner started smoking - unit displayed -- in LCD panel and started making crackling noises

Manufacturer:  Cuisinart
Model:  DCC-790 (Costco)
Serial Number 90824C
justification: The burner started smoking and made crackling noises, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: When we came back home, we noticed our Kitchenaid Microwave model KHMS155LSS-3 was beeping and was very hot.  We turned it off and several minutes later, we observed it coming back on by itself for 3 minutes.  We promptly turned it off and unplugged it before it had a chance to do something serious.  This microwave is not that old and has not been used often.  We investigated and found that this defect is quite common and it is more than shocking that neither Kitchenaid/Whirlpool or the government has issued a recall on this product.  It is EXTREMELY dangerous and is only a matter of time before it kills someone.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but was turned off before causing harm, indicating an incident with no injury. The defect is described as common, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The caller stated that she noticed that when she pulled away her electric range from the wall she noticed that her cabinet had a burnt mark.  This was an indication that the range had been overheating to cause damages to her cabinet.   The right front burner was blackened with burnt marks at the connection point.

The electric range had service done within 2 months of purchase, because she had smelled something burning.  She stated that she had 3 incidents that indicates that the range is a fire hazard.

6/18/12 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that she should not use the range and that the range was out of warranty.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burnt cabinet and range) but no injury or death, and the repeated incidents suggest a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Our diswasher caught fire near the control panel while it was running.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
On 6/13/2012 the consumer was moving his microwave around to clean around the surface, he pushed up against the door which then turned the microwave on.

 The manufacturer was contacted the same day who advised him that there were no other reports or recalls on the unit.

The consumer feels the unit is a safety issue because he has young children and if they were to push on the door it would automatically start. He says that the microwave is to only start when having settings in place and then pushing the start button.
justification: The incident involved the microwave turning on unexpectedly, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible given the consumer's concern about children potentially activating it.

incident_description: cut hand while washing 11-inch diameter scanpan ceramic skillet, top outside edge not champhered, while making circular motion around the rim of the skillet with a soapy sponge, received a cut at the base of thumb
justification: The description indicates a cut injury to the hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the sharp edge and common activity.

incident_description: Relay for defrost stayed on too long which caused the liner in the freezer compartment to melt and burn.  Defrost board has been replaced 3 times within the last 8 years.  Maytag insists this unit is not subject to a voluntary recall that is posted on the CPSC web site.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted and burned liner) but no injury or death, and the defrost board has been replaced multiple times, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: My Kitchenaid Model KUDD03DTSSO motor and circuit board shorted out.  The repairman said the  The wires were black and the wire nut was also burnt.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and burnt wires, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The exterior glass window on our oven suddenly shattered.  The stove was not being used and no one had used the oven for the previous 2 weeks.
justification: The glass window shattered, but no one was injured as the oven was not in use and no one was nearby.

incident_description: On 6/26 approx 1:00pm my wife was outside and could smell burning plastic.  She ran inside the house and found the dishwaser (GE Quiet Power 1 Model # GHDA455L00CS) was billowing smoke out of the front panel. She opened the door to the dishwasher and cut power to the front panel.  This, luckily stopped the process.  She then called me at work to let me know about it and I asked her if anything was on the heating element.  She inspected it and found nothing.  I did a search on the model number and came a cross the GE Dishwaser Recall and checked to see if this model was involved.  It was not.  I contacted GE customer service and they put me in touch with GE Consumer Relations who opened up a claim number.  A repair man came to the house the next day and looked it over.  It was deemed unrepairable due to the lack of availability of the wiring harness.  The connector had melted and the main board (WD21X10247) was burned through.  I feel a fire was averted by the luck of my wife's presence and quick thinking.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but was averted without injury, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it required specific conditions and was not part of a known recall.

incident_description: I was baking a cake at 375 degrees and about 15-20 minutes into baking, the whole dish exploded in the oven.  The "4 simple rules" were followed so I thought it might have been an isolated incident.  After taking a look at other reports, this is NOT so unusual, and quite dangerous.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish in the oven, which is dangerous but no injury was reported. Other reports indicate this is not unusual, suggesting a likely occurrence.

incident_description: My son (approximately 14 months old) was using the Nuby Easy Grip Supersipper cup to drink his milk.  I was in the kitchen with him, but working on dinner prep.  I looked down to find him chewing on something.  When I checked to see what was in his mouth I found about half of the straw had broken off of the cup and he was chewing on it, posing a choking hazard.  I always check the cups for wear and tear before giving them to him and had found none.  These cups were less than 2 months old so they should not have been worn out.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely given the cups were new and regularly inspected.

incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED] and my Brew Central model # DCC_1200c started to smoke from the warming plate.

I was on my way to work at 5:00am in the morning, thank goodness I noticed it smoking before I left and unplugged it and took it outside as my wife was still sleeping and has MS.

She could have had serious problems if this started on fire with only her at home with her mobility issues.
justification: The device started smoking but was unplugged before any injury or fire occurred, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer says the range turns on by itself at 350 degrees.  She says it stays on or sometimes it goes off on its own.  There is also an F11 code that comes on and shut off.  she has heard beeping.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer who sent out a technician on  1-13-12 who told her the issue was a faulty relay. 

She was told by the technician to unplug the unit when she steps out of the house which prompted her to contact us.
justification: The range turning on by itself poses a potential hazard, but there is no report of injury or death, hence severity level 2. The issue is recurring, making the occurrence likelihood likely (4).

incident_description:
I began to smell a hot plastic/electronic burn odor in my house.  As I began to investigate, I discovered that my microwave was "humming."  Investigating further, the top and the sides were too hot to touch with bare hands.  When I opened the door, the humming stopped. I did a 30 second cycle with a cup of water, and the microwave functioned normally - but the humming continued after the beeper stopped at the end of the cycle.

Investigating further, I placed another cup of water inside the microwave and shut the door - but didn't operate any type of cycle.  Within three minutes, the water was boiling even though the microwave was "off."  I have never seen a microwave fail in the "on" position before, and felt it was worth reporting.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but no injury or damage occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Caller purchased Coffeemaker on May 12th, 2012.  The night of Wednesday, June 6th, 2012 Caller programmed her coffee pot to prepare coffee at 6:20AM - 6:30AM Thursday, June 7th, 2012.

The morning of June 7th, 2012 around 8:30 caller was sitting in her living room drinking a cup of coffee when she heard a clicking noise and thought that it was the coffeemaker turning off at the two hour interval.

Approximately 15 minutes after hearing the clicking sound she smelled an electrical/plastic burning odor, she got up and went into the kitchen, saw a minimal amount of smoke coming from the coffeemaker.

She states that the odor was strong but the smoke was light enough that she could not discern which part of the coffeemaker it was coming from.

She grabbed a pot holder, unplugged the coffeemaker and took it out to the patio.

She doesn't know whether the plug was hot or not but didn't want to take the chance of being burned.

She attempted to contact retailer on recall line but it was busy.

She went online and saw other GE coffeemakers recalled but not her model.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

Caller is reporting this coffeemaker as a fire hazard believing that if she had not been awake this incident could have resulted in a fire with extensive damage.

There were no injuries
justification: The incident involved a coffeemaker emitting smoke and a burning odor, but no injuries or fire occurred, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: Kenmore Range 790.9656 Simmer Select Button switch and/or circuit board short. Loud pop, bright flash of light.
justification: The incident involved a loud pop and bright flash of light, indicating an electrical short, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer says he left a plastic [REDACTED] bowl on top of the stove overnight.  Nothing was on at the time.  He woke up to all 4 burners being on at different temperatures.

The locked cooktop touch keypad was on and all of the other keypad switched were flashing on and off. 

He says that the bowl caught on fire.  This is the first time he has had any problems with it.  

He contacted the manufacturer who told him they would investigate it.  

Other phone# for manufacture- 1800-469-4663.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as it's the first reported issue with the appliance.

incident_description: frigidaire FEC30S6ABF cooktop  did not turn off and was burning hot , i could only turn it off from the circuit breaker. when reset breaker it did the same thing.  another day my wife is in the kitchen and the cooktop turned on by itself ... this is a huge fire hazard
justification: The cooktop malfunctioning and turning on by itself poses a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his toaster oven as the model had smoke pouring out of circuit board. The consumer was in his kitchen and saw the model smoking, he went over to product and placed it outside. The consumer was not harmed or injured and his home was not damaged. The consumer stated that the product is unusable. 

The consumer has not called his home insurance company or the fire department. The consumer has not called the firm or the retailer. The product was off before the incident and had not been used for quite some time. The consumer has worked in electronics for years and believes the issue is that similar products, including his, don't have a mechanical off switch while it is not in use.
justification: The incident involved smoke from the toaster oven but no harm or injury occurred, and there was no damage to the home.

incident_description:
I Purchased a Krups KM8105 coffee maker.  The unit has a detachable water resevoir,  the resevoir began to leak shortly after purchase.  I'm an Army Helicopter pilot and have a fair understanding of engineering and although I thought the design was poor I elected to not use the detach feature of the resevoir and just fill it in situ.  Now less than a year later the unit is leaking profusely and I can see the water entering into the interior of the unit as well as covering the counter whenever it is filled with water.  I belive this presents a significant risk of electrical shock and possibly fire.

 I have contacted Krups North America and spoken to a a customer service rep who told me Mr. [REDACTED] would contact me today.  He did and was rude and condescending, and explained that without a receipt he couldn't help and ended our conversation by hanging up.  I don't believe that Krups North America understands the hazard this product represents nor do I belive that they have any regard for the safety of their customers.
justification: The leaking coffee maker presents a risk of electrical shock and fire, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Kitchenaid KBRS22KG refrigerator began making a very loud noise.  Over the course of a month the noise increased.  Cleaning under and behind the refrigerator did not help.  Finally it began to not keep the temperature properly and I pulled it out again to clean.  When i did I discovered a charred, melted area by the compressor start relay area.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator with no reported injury, but potential fire hazard due to charred and melted components.

incident_description: Cuisinart DCB-700BC Grind & Brew coffee maker.  We purchased this coffee maker approximately 6 months ago.  This morning 7/8/2012 my husband and I were drinking a cup of freshly brewed coffee in our family room when we smelled a hot electrical smell.  We traced the smell back to our Cuisinart DCB-700BC Grind & Brew coffee maker located on our kitchen counter that was smoking and extremely hot.  We immediately unplugged the coffee maker and cleared the smoke smell from the house.  I looked the problem up on the internet and was very surprised to see all of the complaints about the Cuisinart coffee makers over heating, smoking and catching on fire.  I am very upset that these coffee makers are still on the market. have not been recalled and that Cuisinart has no concern for consumer safety.  I can only imagine what may have happened if we were drinking our coffee on the patio this morning and not caught the problem before the pot went up in flames. Consumers have the right to know that Cuisinart is potentially putting them and their families in harms way.
justification: The coffee maker overheated and smoked, but no injury or fire occurred. Similar incidents are reported frequently, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I was making guacamole and I noticed that a piece of avocado was stuck under blender blade. Blender was off but plugged in. I used my left index finger to dislodge avocado. As I rotated blade the motor engaged and started. One of the blender blades became embedded in my finger and I could not remove my finger as I realized the blade was probably stuck in the bone.
I rinsed off my finger and placed a towel around. My husband rushed me to the ER. The ER doctor had no idea how to remove the blender. My husband went home to retrieve a tin snips and special wide edge pliers. The Dr. and my husband and the male nurse took turns cutting the housing down in sections and removing it like peeling a banana. Then the dr. held onto one blade with a pliers as he rotated the embedded blade to remove it from my finger. Xray was taken and I had a stabilized fracture as a wedge of bone had been cut out from my finger and two tiny bone fragments were visible on the xray. I had to get a tetanus shot. I received several IVs of antibiotics while in ER. I also received two stitches and an RX for 10 days of antibiotics. This happened June 30th, 2012, approximately 4 pm. My biggest concern now is for infection in the bone/stitches area. I am taking the antibiotics and keeping injury as clean as possible. Stitches are to be removed in 7-10 days from injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a stabilized fracture, bone fragments, and required medical intervention, classifying it as an injury.

incident_description: My black and decker conventional oven was in bake mode set at 400 degrees and was in use for about 5-10 minutes when the glass door exploded shooting glass and the handle across the kitchen.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, which is an equipment failure, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Programmable coffeemaker supposed to automatically turn off after 2 hours, did not turn off at least twice.
justification: The coffeemaker failing to turn off is an incident but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
Caller's wife was baking biscuits Sunday morning, May27th, 2012 when she smelled an odor that she identified as an odd smell.
She went into the bedroom and made that comment to her husband and then returned to the kitchen where she found the stove on fire.

Fire was coming out of the upper back portion of the stove which is a gas top/electric oven range.
Caller immediately used the kitchen fire extinguisher to put the fire out which included flames 5 to 6 inches high.

He called retailer May 27th, 2012 but since it was Memorial Day Weekend it took a couple of days for a service tech to be sent.
The service tech said that the range would require an entirely new wiring harness and that there was nothing he could do for them other than offer a $100 discount if they ordered new stove immediately while he was there.

Callers initially ordered but then canceled.

Callers purchased new range of a different model from a different manufacturer. 

Caller took the range apart and discovered that there is a terminal block, the internal components hook to this terminal block.  Caller discovered that where the the internal components were supposed to be attached, it caused arching which caused it to catch fire.

They still have the wiring harness from the original range that caught fire and would request that the manufacturer reimburse them or provide voucher toward new range.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly extinguished without injury, and the issue was identified as a specific wiring problem in the stove.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite Slide in Range, model 790.41073101, and after using the self clean cycle, the oven walls bowed out just enough so that the racks no longer fit and they fall down if a weight is put on them, especially a heavy weight such as a Thanksgiving turkey.  This is a very dangerous situation and these and other affected models should be recalled.   I noticed another report that was similar on this site--see also 20110603-BF642-2147478569.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with the oven racks failing under heavy weight, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
On June 11th, 2012 the consumer stated that he had the dishwasher running for approximately 20 minutes. 
He smelled smoke from another room. 

After inspecting the home and checking the kitchen they saw that the plastic had melted outside the washer onto the front control panel. 

The consumer immediately unplugged the unit.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer June 12th, 2012 and they advised him that his model number was part of release#05-123, but the serial number did not match. 
They advised him that he would have to pay for someone to come out and inspect the unit.

The consumer believes that the product is a safety hazard because it may have potentially started a fire.
justification: The incident involved melted plastic and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Sunday, May 27th, 2012 the caller's wife was turning electric range oven on to preheat when the center console burst into flames.
She immediately reached for the fire extinguisher but in those few moments the fire extinguished itself so she opened windows to clear the smoke from her kitchen.

Breaker did click off when this incident occurred.

Flames are estimated to have been approximately five to seven inches high using the wall above the range as a measurement with the scorching on the wall being five to six inches above the range height.

She called her husband who advised her to unplug the range.
It has been pulled from the wall, unplugged and is inoperable.

Caller contacted the manufacturer May 30th, 2012 and was advised that his range is not on recall, not covered by warranty and that they could repair it at his expense.

Caller does not agree that this repair should be at his expense due to the range being only seven years old and fire not being an acceptable issue.
He would like repair successfully completed at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the fire extinguished itself quickly.

incident_description: My husband was using our soda stream machine to make carbonated water.  He put fresh water in the bottle and hooked up the machine.  After 3 button pushes the bottle exploded sending parts of the bottle into the machine which then sent parts of the machine and bottle flying into our kitchen.
justification: The incident involved an exploding bottle and flying debris, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My daughter was using the Hot Air Popcorn machine in her kitchen.  She used it a number of times and complained about how hot the outside of the machine would get.  The last time she used it, it started to smoke and caught fire.  she unplugged it immediately.  Nostalgia Electrics is the maker and it was purchased at J C Penney store.  She also complained that the machine would not pop about 1/4 of the corn.

I purchased the same machine for myself as well as the one my daughter had the problem with.  I have noticed that mine also gets very hot and you have to use a pot holder to empty out the last of the popcorn from the machine.  This is a safety hazard, espeically with a product designed for families.
justification: The machine caught fire, but no injury was reported, making the severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 since the machine gets very hot and can cause fire.

incident_description: My mother has the bistro wolfgang puck pressure cooker elite 7 quart model # bpcrm040, last night around 5pm the pressure cooker exploded when she went to open it, even after all the pressure was suppose to be out of it  luckily she covered her face with her left arm but her left arm , neck and chest all the way down past her breasts were all badly burned!. My father had to take her to the emergency room she was in so much pain!She has burns all over and huge blisters, she is still in a lot of pain! Please anyone please use caution around this product or for that matter do not use it at all! Thank god my 1 year old son wasnt in the kitchen with her when this happened!
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns requiring emergency room treatment, indicating significant injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the specific context of a pressure cooker malfunction.

incident_description: I was using a Cuisinart immersion blender and something got stuck in the blade. Unfortunately, I did not unplug it but it was off. I stuck my finger in to dislodge the item, and picked the appliance up. It has a touch/pressure on/off switch on the handle and accidentally turned it on. I dropped it and it turned off, but my finger was severely lacerated. Because I was in the middle of a colonoscopy preparation, I was unable to go to the ER. After the procedure, I sought medical attention. Apparently  no bone, nerve or tendon damage, but a long healing process and possible surgery at a later date.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations requiring medical attention and potential future surgery, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described scenario of accidental activation and improper handling.

incident_description: I purchased a new condo in March 2011 and the kitchen has a built in KitchenAid microwave hood combination Model KHMS155lSS-4.  Today while sitting in my living room I heard something beep on several occasions so finally I decided to investigate only to find out that my microwave oven had turned itself on.  The error code is either -F2- or PAN and the only way to keep it from coming on is to keep the door open or unplug it.  I unplugged it earlier hoping that it would reset itself, but when I plugged it back in it started again by itself.  This is very disturbing as there's nothing in the microwave and I'm afraid it may cause a fire.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description: After using my gas Kitchenaid gas range the "off" button failed to operate making it impossible to turn the oven off without using the circuit breaker. This is not the first time it has happened. In August of 2008 we had it serviced and they replaced the switch membrane which corrected the problem. Until today, July 3, 2012. Granted it has been 4 years since we had the problem fixed the first time, it's the same problem and Kitchenaid seems to be well aware of the issue but only "warranties" that part for 90 days even though it is a safety issue. In searching online I have found many people experiencing the same problem. It seems that even though they are aware that this is a safety issue that many people are experiencing they are not correcting the problem and forcing people like me to have it serviced and have the part replaced, while in the meantime we are not using the oven and keeping it turned off at the circuit breaker. I hope it doesn't take someone getting hurt before they take responsibility for this issue. The model # KGRA806PSS02, Serial # XT1208237.
justification: The incident involves a recurring safety issue with the oven's off button failing, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Last Saturday, 6/30/12, my husband (and LTC in the US Army) was severly burned while lifting a Rival Crock Pot.  The handle broke from the side and the scolding juice poured over his left hand as he guided it back onto the counter.  Had he not gotten it back to the counter it would've hit the ground and burnt more of his body and probably any other people in the kitchen.  He has now suffered for 4 days from 2 degree burns.

I have tried to upload many pics, but was told that my file is not supported.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) since such handle failures are not common.

incident_description:
We have a Maytag dishwasher.  We have had it for about 5 years.  Last night the heating element did not shut off that dries the dishes.  This morning we discovered it.  It was so hot the paint burned of off plates.  

Also a very heat durable plastic piece from our expresso maker warped.  It would take a lot of heat for that to happen.

Even when we had the unit turned off the heating element kept heating.  I had to turn off all power to the unit from the circuit breaker.
justification: The heating element malfunction caused property damage (burned paint, warped plastic) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
LG 3 door refrigerator light cause melting of plastic and might cause fire.  I have model number lfc25760sw serial number 703kruc01238 manufacture date of 2007 that the light failed to turn off in the refrigerator top section.  It was only discovered when the door was opened and a strong smell of plastic burning or melting.  From further investigation it was noticed the light housing had drooped and was hot to the touch.  The unit has 2x 60 watt incandescent light bulbs.  I worked the door switches that would turn off the digital temp display and lights.  The display would turn off every time where the lights would turn off only few of the times.

  I contacted LG WHO STATED THEY WERE AWARE OF THE PROBLEM and would send a service tech to the house to repair the issue for free.

  I am pleased LG is taking care of the issue, my only concern that I was not made aware of the issue until I had the problem.  My concern is that consumers should be made aware of the issue before a fire occurs.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and potential fire risk, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as LG acknowledged the issue, indicating it's a known problem.

incident_description: The Kenmore oven/electric smooth top range was first not heating to correct temperature (the stove top kept getting hotter) and the second problem on the front left burner would not turn off.  It was red hot and it kept getting hotter, and would not turn off.  I had to throw the breaker switch off and then back on.  I retried this the next day and the same thing happened.  This almost caused a fire and my family's safety was endangered.  We are a small family and only use the that burner about 7 times a week.  I bought the product in 7/2007.  The Kenmore product number is:  790.9612340 and the SN# is VF73038028.
justification: The malfunctioning burner posed a fire hazard and endangered safety, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Elite 790.4670* Slide in Range.  The oven walls have warped on this oven and the oven racks no longer will hold food items.  It is a very dangerous situation as hot pots, pans, and food have fallen during cooking.  I also came very close to a very severe burn when the oven rack collapsed while removing a hot pan full of food. My wife has suffered burns from similar incidents in the past.   I have checked my racks and the racks are all perfect with no bends or problems whatsoever.  The problem is that the oven walls have warped to a point that the racks no longer can hold in place.  I called Sears and they contend they have "never heard of such a problem" before...which is hard to believe as I have seen numerous complaints about this product online that have been reported to sears.  In addition, Sears has refused to accept any responsibility for this defective product and insists that any repairs will be fully at my expense.  I am totally disgusted with Sears and this obviously defective product which was touted as a "top of the line" product at the time of my purchase.  This is a very dangerous and personally hazardous product.  I wish someone could come to my aid to help fix this very expensive and defective product.
justification: The incident describes burns suffered by the user and their wife due to the oven rack collapsing, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as similar incidents have occurred multiple times.

incident_description: Our Kenmore smooth top electric ranges burners will not turn off when turned off and when using them on a selected temperature they go to high on their own. There is a recall for the same issues that I have for a Kenmore Electric Range but not the one I have. My model # is 790.9601 1 1406 and the serial # is VF64158171. We had purchased extended warranty on it and had a repair man from Sears , which is where we purchased , come out. It was only one burner that was doing it at that time. He said he repaired it. We also had them come out again before the extended warranty expired for a check over of the stove to be sure all was ok. After that and the warranty was out ,  the second large burner started doing the same thing as the first. We've had the stove now since 08/04/2007 and it continues to do the same thing.
justification: The incident involves burners not turning off and overheating, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the burners are not shutting off unless unplugging the entire unit.  He says its happening to the front right burner.  He says the Front Left burner goes up to high while in a low setting.  He has to wait a while before plugging it back on.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer this morning 6-18-2012 who said the unit is not under recall.

He is experiencing the same issues as in Release # 09-333.  His model is not listed in the recall.
justification: The incident involves malfunctioning burners but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
this stove was purchased in Aug. 2007. although  I turned  the knob to the off  position off  on stove  for the front burner., IT DID NOT GO OFF BUT PROCEEDED TO GET RED HOT! the only thing that helped was to flip the breaker switch. This particular  front burner (not the dual burner) has not worked since that day. Sears would not fix, the manufacturer warranty had expired. 

this happened about 2 years after purchase. this second incidence with the inner glass of  door oven shattering happened about 5 days ago. 
My husband had the oven on  375 ( preheating) all at once there wall a loud pop from the stove area. the inner glass had shattered in many, many pea sized pieces.. the glass did not go into the oven nor out the front of oven  but the many pieces fell out thur the bottom of the oven door into warmer tray.
justification: The incidents described involve equipment malfunction (burner not turning off and oven glass shattering) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: About 20 minutes after my coffee finished brewing today, I heard a crackle and popping sound. When I got to the kitchen, the coffee was sizzling, the plate was hot, and smoke was pouring out of the base of the coffee maker. The heat from the base was starting to melt the countertop, so I quickly moved the hot maker to the sink by holding the top. It may have automatically shutoff, but it was hot enough briefly to start a fire. I'm so glad I was nearby!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing smoke and heat damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This coffee maker has been unsafe from day 1.  When you insert the pot underneath the basket, it pushes a lever and allows coffee to drip into the pot.  That lever did not work properly, and most of the time, if you were not standing there to watch it, it would dump about 8 cups of water and coffee grounds all over the counter.  When I complained (after taking out the lever so I could at least make coffee) the company sent a new basket with a new lever (I threw the old one away, as it wasn't correct), and that has been working well.

This model drips more water on the counter than any other pot I have ever used.  Water drips from above the water container when you remove or replace the container.  Water drips from above the grounds basket when you remove or replace it.  Not a small amount either, much more than you would think possible.

Then, the coffee pot handle had come loose.  So recently, the company sends me an e-mail explaining the recall, because the pot is unsafe.  Unfortunately, the only way to get a new pot, is to mail the old one in first, wait approximately 2 - 3 weeks, hope the new pot comes in, hope the new pot works.  The company has not been able to offer me a suggestion as to how I am supposed to make coffee during this 2 to 3 week period, nor do I see why, after paying a premium price for this contraption, I should have to worry about that.  Why not send me the replacement pot, and I will put the old one back in the  same box, and return it to you? 

If I had the opportunity to get one of these again, I would definitely not.  I am even thinking of acquiring all future coffee makers from another company.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning coffee maker causing spills and inconvenience, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
My toaster oven caught on fire today.  I bought it a year or so ago.  It was a Black and Decker Series TRO390.  About a week ago it burned the toast.  Today it burned the toast then started to burn-flames.  I turned off the timer (don't think it was working properly, but I don't stand there looking at the toaster).  I pulled the plug.  Still flaming.  I grabbed a box of baking soda and threw chunks of it on the flames, putting them out.  I threw the toaster out.

I'm fed up with products of inferior quality made in China.  I have 2 ceiling fans where after about 6 weeks I have to replace the light boxes.
justification: The toaster oven caught fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased a cookware 10 piece set. The consumer stated that he was using the 3 quart sauce pan with the pots and lid and was boiling water. The consumer stated that it had been on for approximately 1.7 minutes. 

The consumer that the copper and steel seam detached from each other causing the hot water to splash all over his kitchen. The consumer stated that the water reach approximately 4ÃÂ away from the range. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer stated that there were no damages to his home. 

The consumer stated that the manufacturer informed him that they had experienced some consumers contacting them with the same incident. The manufacturer offered to exchange the product.
justification: The incident caused hot water to splash but no injuries or damages were reported, and the manufacturer has received similar complaints.

incident_description: A "Munchkin Brand" sippy cup, the "Mighty Grip 8 oz. Trainer" had the plastic/silicone spout on the lid rip while my 13 month old son was drinking from it. When the top ripped it allowed too much water to flow through at one time causing my son to choke on the water. His lips and tongue began to turn blue and he was given the infant heimlich maneuver to clear his lungs of the water. We called 911, but he was breathing and crying by this point. The 911 operator  said that if he was crying he was getting enough air but we should still have him looked at by a doctor. He also sounded wheezy so we were concerned about that as well. We noticed that a piece of the cup's inner spout was missing. We brought him to the Holland Hospital ER and he was given a chest x-ray. Although nothing showed on the x-ray the doctor suggest transferring him to Helen DeVos Children's Hospital in Grand Rapids, MI. He was brought into the OR and given a bronchoscope where the surgeon found the small piece of the spout stuck in the main air way to my son's left lung.  We have medial documents and the surgeon also gave us the piece that was stuck in his lung.
justification: The incident caused injury requiring medical intervention, including a bronchoscope to remove a foreign object from the airway.

incident_description: Maytag Dishwasher model #MDB6000AWW purchased in May 1999 began smoking and it appeared as if the motor was burning. I originally had the other recall completed and this is completely different.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking and the motor appeared to be burning, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We purchased a new set of the Anolon Advanced Bronze cookware from Macy's in February.  It has had very light use.  We were simmering rice in the 3 quart sauce pan on the lowest heat setting on a gas range when suddenly the glass lid exploded with a loud pop.  It appears to be safety glass and most of it fell into the food, but a good amount was strewn around the rangetop, counters, and floor.  I reported the incident to Anolon custumer service and they are sending me another lid.  The model number stamped on the bottom of the pan is either 0011T or QQ11T.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but the glass lid exploded, which is a serious incident.

incident_description: Turned on dishwasher and it seemed to go through the cycle. Kids were  home and a strong plastic burning smell came from dishwasher. The dishwasher stopped working. Checked the breaker and it did not trip. Opened the control panel and there was fire damage. A large capacitor fell out with burn damage. The circuit board and the ribbon cable were black and melted.
justification: The incident involved fire damage and a malfunctioning dishwasher, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his 8 cup coffee maker as the consumer was brewing his cup of coffee, and the product's coffee pot became very hot. The consumer estimates that the coffee maker was brewing for 3-5 minutes prior to the incident. The consumer would estimate that the hot plate under the coffee maker, exceeded the desired temperature. The consumer could see flames from the plastic base surrounding the hot plate.

The flames were nearly 2 inches high. The consumer unplugged the product and the flames continued to burn. The consumer took the product outside with an oven mitt and put dirt and water to douse the flames. The consumer stated that his tile counter top cracked and was discolored by the intense heat of the product. The consumer would describe the product as unusable. The consumer cannot recall the retailer as the product was given as a gift. 

The consumer has yet to call the firm. The consumer did not notify the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. The product is currently in the consumer's garage.
justification: The incident involved flames and property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I Heated a pot of water, and turned the burner off, but the burner would not turn off. After turning it off and on several times, and lighting other burners, it finally went off. The gas guy came out, and when he turned the burner on low, the flame had re-adjusted to a high flame. He re-adjusted the flame height, turned the burner off, and back on. When he turned it back on, the flame height was again high on low, and then the burner would not shut off. We then began to smell heavy gas fumes, and he had to run out to the tank to shut the main tank off. He deemed the stove hazardous, and disconnected the gas line from it. He surmised that he thought the valve may be coming apart, which could cause an explosion. The stove was only 5 months old.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning gas stove that could have led to an explosion, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: About 3 months ago after cooking in our range, we noticed that the broiler element was still on after we had shut the oven off. We could not get the broiler to shut off by manually pressing any of the buttons on the oven.  All controls were set to off. Finally had to unplug the oven to get to turn off.  We plugged it back in & all appeared to be ok at this point.  Same thing happened  about 5 days ago, the only difference being I had to keep it unplugged for a couple of hours before the element stayed off before plugging it back in. Today my daughter was baking a cake, when the broiler came on during the baking process & burnt the cake.  This filled the oven & house with smoke causing our alarms to go off.  I unplugged the oven to let it cool.  Have tried to plug it back in several times within the last few hours & each time the broiler automatically turns back on. There is no other way to shut this off other than unplugging the unit. I feel that this is very unsafe & have had to keep the unit unplugged at all times fearing that it would automatically turn on & start a fire. I have searched online only to find that there are others out there that have had a very similar experience with this model.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven broiler that poses a fire hazard but has not yet caused injury or death, though the risk is significant.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he had his previous Coffeemaker replaced by the Release #06-220.  However, while he was away his coffeemaker was left plugged in, but not powered on.  He came home and noticed that there was an overwhelming odor of wire burning.  He discovered the GFCI was unreceptive, so he tried to use another one and the same incident occurred.  The unit had tripped the circuit breaker.

The coffeemaker although replaced present the same risk as it was previously recalled for.  There had been no previous incident.

5/29/12 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that there was no recall for his coffeemaker.

The caller feels that this coffeemaker is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and tripped circuit breakers, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This can opener leaves thin strings of metal if it is run around some cans more than once.
Strings of metal can fall into food.
justification: The incident involves metal strings falling into food, which is a hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description: I have a kenmore stove. The front left burner will not respond to temperature control. It stays on high which I consider it to be a fire hazard. I have recently read numerous complaints about  Kenmore models of doing this and there has yet to be a recall to include all these models. Not only is this a fire hazard but a safety issue with the consumer as well.
justification: The burner staying on high poses a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Range purchased in 2004 caught fire.  We were baking for no more than 10 minutes when range made a loud popping noise; smoke and a flame appeared at back of oven.  Fire department was called.  Firemen believed that the cause was a faulty circuit board.  No damage to our house.  Sears offered no help whatsoever other than a 10% off coupon for a future purchase.

Model #: 790.79913302
Serial #: VF43520433
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: kenmore elite trio bottom freezer, lights stayed on and melted the plastic light cover, and heated up contents directly below lights, unsafe to use lights
justification: The incident involved melted plastic and heated contents but no reported injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) based on the description of the issue occurring.

incident_description:
The consumer says she went in the kitchen early this morning and saw the front left burner was on.  She says it stayed on for twenty minutes while the knob was in the off position.  This has already happened several times already.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer today, who told her the product is not under warranty and offered no assistance.  


She says it is not normal for a stove to be doing this.  She is very upset that the manufacturer did not provide further assistance.
justification: The burner being on while the knob is off is a malfunction but no injury or damage is reported, making it a severity level 2. The issue has occurred several times, indicating a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: Popper caught the popcorn on fire, about 2-3 minutes after being turned on.
justification: The popcorn catching fire is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Fridigaire electric range with a smooth top.
turned on the front left heating element and the top cracked in a few seconds, sending a couiple of small pirces of glass into the air.  the top was not hit or damaged in any way - just cracked shortly after turning on the heating element.
justification: The incident involved the cracking of a glass top on an electric range, with small pieces of glass sent into the air, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: we bought a Frigidaire gas range 2 years ago April. the gas stove was not in use. we heard a loud noise the glass door had exploded with tint pieces of glass every where I would hate to think what would of happened if someone was in the room. we have a small grand child living with us. I reported it with no satisfactory results . they claimed they had no complaints of this happening to anyone else but I  doubt it. We have gone without the use of an oven for 1week.  I also wonder about using safety glass.
justification: The glass door exploded, causing potential harm, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is considered possible due to the lack of similar complaints but the potential for harm exists.

incident_description: On July 1st 2012, at 1230 our Whirlpool dishwasher M/N: DU1050XTPS3, S/N: FS0301360, started to emit a burning plastic smell. The dishwasher tripped the designated circuit breaker. After disconnecting the dishwasher I started to trouble shoot the smell. I disassembled the front cover and discovered the circuit board to be burnt and melted. The circuit board P/N is Whirlpool P/N 8564544 REV REL, The circuit board was assembled in Mexico and is called a "Jabil Circuit". The S/N appears to be 6454400283302.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and a tripped circuit breaker, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid Microwave KHMS155L-4  manufactured Feb. 2006

Started on its own.
Had to unplug it.  I am afraid to use it now and see it is a common problem.

Why has there not been a recall?
justification: The microwave started on its own, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Microwave trips circuits every time it runs
justification: The microwave tripping circuits is an incident with no injury, but it disrupts normal operations.

incident_description:
We purchased this GE Profilre Range in 2009


In May 2012 my wife noticed the oven door was open about  5 inches while she was cooking and the knobs (all 5) were melting. The knobs are made of plastic.
 Our main concern is this may have caused a fire. I voiced this to GE
justification: The incident involved melting knobs and an open oven door, posing a fire risk but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was in my kitchen standing at my sink, when suddenly I heard what sounded like a gunshot. I felt a spray all over the back of my legs and then saw black glass shards all over my counter top & sprayed all over the floor. The tempered glass on the front of my oven door had exploded. I had not that day nor the previous 3 days used my oven.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, causing glass shards to spray, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
6/26/2012 microwave came on by itself.  I heard it running and opened the door pressed clear and shut the door.  A few hours later it did it again.  Opened the door pressed clear closed the door without latching it.  Several hours later I heard the microwave running.  The door was not latched.  Opened the door all the way and it still ran.  I had to turn off the breaker to stop the microwave.  The inside of the microwave was so hot it took several minutes to be able to touch the turntable.

Manufacter:  GE
Model:           WES1450DNDN1BB
Serial #:          DT919804B
Manufacter date Feb 2010

I used the contact email at the GE web site  this morning to inform them of this incident.  Just wanted them to be on notice.  

As I know that this could have caused a fire I will make myself available for a statement if any serious incidents involving this microwave arises.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Bosch Dishwasher Model Number SHU4326hc/U12, Batch number FD8106190132 caught fire. I was unaware fo the recall, never received notice from Bosch of recall. .. Luckily, I was in adjacent room and heard the spark and housemate in same room saw the fire as it started. I was able to put it out, but that is a VERY dangerous situation! What if no one had been nearby?
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries occurred. The incident was dangerous but was quickly contained.

incident_description:
Set of 4 silverware (4 forks, 4 spoons, 4 salad forks, 4 butter knives) purchased from the Disney Store - come in different colors.

On the bottom of each piece of silverware, there is a silver cap that comes off easily and is small enough to become a choking hazard.

I looked everyone in the internet for anyone who may have reported this product, but haven't seen anything. The Disney Store will not return the items.
justification: The silverware has small parts that can detach and pose a choking hazard, but no incidents or injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: My mother had a Pyrex baking dish explode several months ago, which exploded into thousands of shards.  Fortunately, she had just turned her back on it after taking it out of the oven, so her eyes were safe.  She says she was not baking anything unusual, and did not set the dish on a cold surface.  The shards were everywhere, even in the adjacent dining room, and left burn/melt marks on her floor.  I see from internet searches that some authoritative sources consider exploding Pyrex a myth, but I saw the aftermath of this dangerous incident.  My mother's email address is [REDACTED]
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but no injuries occurred, as the person had turned away in time.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to illustrate some of her concerns about her under the counter dishwasher as she discovered that the lower spray arm of the dishwasher is melting. The mechanism consists of a combination of metal and plastic. The metal appears to have gotten so hot during a cycle and caused the plastic to melt. The consumer is not sure when this began to happen. 

The consumer has pre-existing allergies and has noticed an increase in her symptoms in the last month as she has been feeling sick and dizzy as of last month. The consumer has stated for the last month that she has noticed the dishwasherÃÂs control panel has been displaying an error code of CL towards the end of the washing cycle indicating the closing lock mechanism is not functioning. 

CONSUMER ADDED:  In the fall the consumer began to have ocular migraine and saw an eye doctor about the problem, also saw Family Doctor.  Returned to Family Doctor and he believed the melting of the plastic in the dishwasher caused the ocular migraines.

The consumer called the firm today and they were not willing to help her because the warranty expired on the unit. The consumer is not sure of the retailer as the dishwasher was in the home when she first moved in to the home. The consumer has not called the fire department or her home insurance company about the concern about the dishwasher.
justification: The consumer experienced health issues (ocular migraines, dizziness) linked to the melting plastic in the dishwasher, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Without cause, our Whirlpool Gold Microwave, Model GT4175SPS, began to burn.  Smoke was released via the stainless surround.  An incredible electrical melting smell continues to be present.  Had there been no one home, the home could have been destroyed by fire.  Fortunately, our son smelled the problem, ran downstairs, and was able to stop the electricity to the unit.  We are currently looking to replace the microwave.
justification: The microwave caught fire and released smoke, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his gas range as the dials on the range that point outward are very sensitive. The consumer stated that the dials at burner top of the gas range are easily manipulated by the slightest contact. The dials point outward and can be turned on by a slight touch and brushing against the dials. The consumer stated that the gas escapes and is released into the air but does not ignite to indicate to the consumer that the gas is on. 

The consumer woke up in the middle of the night and found that range was on and gas filled his home. The consumer stated that this happened again today by merely walking past the range too closely. The consumer was not harmed by the product as the consumer could smell the gas discharge. The consumer has removed the knobs from the range. The consumer stated that the product does not appear damaged. The consumer has not called the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer has not contacted the firm or the retailer.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage without ignition, posing a hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high as the issue has happened multiple times with slight contact.

incident_description:
We have a Bosch dishwasher model SHU43C it's a few years old.

We were out doing some work in the yard while washing dishes. My wife went into the house and smelled something burning like plastic. We couldn't locate the source at the time.

A few days later the dish washer wouldn't work, no power to the machine.
I touched the block with my meter leads and the power arched and sparked 
I checked the TERMINAL CONNECTING BLOCK is was melted I secured power to the unit.
.
I contacted Bosch to find out about any recalls on this product. They had recalls but not on that
model or problem.

I  ordered a new part, still waiting on the part.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with a melted terminal block, causing sparks but no injury.

incident_description:
I have purchased Kenmore Gas five burner cooking range little over a year ago (06/18/11) from Sears. The Product Number is 79070602013. Last night (06/27/12) I smell natural gas leak at my house.
