I called [REDACTED] to check any gas leakages. They found out that the gas is leaking from the cooking range regulator. They shut the gas off and asked me to call the Kenmore personal for repair.

This is a serious safety issue with the product. Luckily I called the [REDACTED] on time otherwise my wife and kids have to suffer from the gas odor.
justification: Gas leak was detected and addressed without injury, but poses a serious safety risk if not caught.

incident_description:
My Microwave (owned by my Landlord) has been going on by itself for at least a year if left plugged in.  It will beep twice, then run for a while, then stop.  When it stops, you must press stop before starting again, unlike a normal run, but I haven't noticed any particular mode display.  I'm not exactly sure how long it will run, but the times I recall seeing when I go over to shut it off quickly have been 3:05, 9:??, 5:??. It tends to run about twice a night, two or three nights in a row, first set for 3:05 and then again for longer if left plugged in.  When it runs for 9+ minutes, which seems to be the max, it can be quite warm, but I haven't seen signs of arcing (yet). 

Samsung Model MT1066SB, s/n 00197DAW901484A, Manufacture date Sept 2003.

I see on the internet there is a recall for similar units in [REDACTED] (I think 2 recalls, one for this problem, with the touchpad to be replaced, and another for another problem related to installation bolts). There is also a class action lawsuit [REDACTED], for [REDACTED] models manufactured by Samsung. I also see you have previous similar complaints on file for other Samsung models.

I called Samsung June 18, 2012, and was initially old there was no recall for this model. When I asked to report this model for consideration of recall, they took some information and said someone would call, but they have not called back so far.
justification: The microwave operates unexpectedly but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Last night while the knob was in the off position, the front left burner turned red hot.  It would lower in temperature but remain on and kept going back to bright red.  This kept occurring so the consumer shut off the circuit breaker.  

She says the temperature would fluctuate on its own.  She contacted the manufacturer who informed her the unit is not under recall and provided no assistance.  The serial number is within range of the recall  for release # 09-333.  The model number falls outside of the range.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue was mitigated by shutting off the circuit breaker.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he contacted the manufacturer and they informed him that the metal knobs are design for the metal knobs to heat up to 150 degrees. 04/13/2012 The consumer stated that he contacted the retailer and they sent out a technician service the range and informed him that the knobs were reaching temperatures of 160-167 degrees. 4/20/2012 Also the consumer contacted the manufacturer and they offered to replace the metal knobs with plastic or rubber knobs. The consumer stated that he refused the replacement because he felt they would be unsafe. 

The consumer stated that on the 4/20/2012 he spoke with the firm again and they stated that they would send out a repair technician to from private company Jersey coast Appliances, and they serviced it on 4/23/2012. The consumer stated that the technician stated that the temperature was so high he was unable to service the range. The consumer stated that the technician went back to service the range on 4/25/2012 and he measured the temperature which were 175 degrees at the top of the knob and the bottom of the knob was 200 degrees (measured from 6 ÃÂ away from the knobs). 

The consumer stated that there were no visible damages to the range. The consumer stated that he was not injured and there were no damages to his home. 
The consumer stated that the technician went back to his home 05/02/2012 and he was going to replaced the inside frame (the shield heat protectevr/chol) of the range door. The consumer stated that the technician was unable to change the inside frame because they provided him with the wrong part. 

The consumer stated that he is concern because he believed that it was a fire hazard.
justification: The consumer reported no injuries or damages, but the knobs reached unsafe temperatures, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description: I have owned the TFAL Avante 6 Elite toaster oven for one year.  This evening the glass spontaneously shattered.  I have had no issue with the device.  I noticed several reviews when I was on amazon regarding the same incident.  The glassis tempered and should not do this.
justification: The glass shattered, but no injury was reported, making it a level 2 incident.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught on fire
justification: The dishwasher catching fire is an incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: Cooking on range last night, two loud pops, sparks and smoke came from beneath the top. Continued to sizzle and burn until I pulled the range out and unplugged it.
justification: The incident caused sparks and smoke, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
June 2nd, 2012 the consumer set her dishwasher to run overnight.

Approximately 2a.m on June 3rd, 2012 the consumer and her family awoke to a house full of smoke. 

The fire department was called because they couldn't tell where the smoke was coming from.

After clearing the home the fire department advised her that the heating unit in the dishwasher never shut off and melted everything inside.

On June 4th, 2012 the manufacturer was contacted and they advised her to contact their extended warranty division. 

The warranty division was contacted the same day and inspection was scheduled for June 7th, 2012. 

The consumer believes this product to be a fire hazard because the unit should have shut off automatically once the cycle was complete.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and required fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
GE Microwave oven
Model: jes1451dn1bb

Unit turns on and starts running automatically, at random times.  For safety reasons, we are forced to leave the unit unplugged when not in use.  At times, it takes multiple attempts to to get the unit to start again after being plugged back in.
justification: The microwave turns on randomly, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
12 cup Coffeemaker is less than a year old.

Caller prepared a pot of coffee this morning June 8th, 2012 and while it was brewing, her daughter, who is visiting. asked  her whether she had burned something.  She answered that she had not.

She fixed a cup of coffee then took it into the living room.

Approximately ten minutes after caller walked out of the kitchen, her husband went into the coffee to pour himself a cup.

When he entered the kitchen he saw smoke pouring out of the bottom portion of the coffeemaker with the coffee in the pot boiling as if it had been sitting over a fire.

He was going to turn the coffeemaker off and though it may have already turned itself off but pulled the plug out very quickly to assure that there was no power going to the unit.

Then left the coffee maker sitting on the countertop while he and caller opened all the windows.

She contacted the manufacturer June 8th, 2012 and was advised that they would replace the coffeemaker with the same model but she is afraid to accept the same model for fear of fire.

Caller would like to have this coffeemaker recalled and would like a replacement of a different unit/model or a voucher assist for purchasing a better/safer coffeemaker.
justification: The coffeemaker emitted smoke and boiled excessively, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore tall tub dishwasher in 2006. It recently developed a leak. I looked closely at the tub and observed water dripping from underneath. I looked inside the tub and there is (what I thought was food stains) a burnt spot directly under the heating element on the left side of the unit. This burn has created a noticeable crack in the tub and that is where it is leaking from. incident_description: This is a Deni Model 9700 Pressure Cooker. After about 6 months of use the plastic pressure release mount disintegrated. Holding the knob in place is a thin plastic mount that heats up and cools down with each use making it brittle. When this plastic breaks the pressure cooker is useless and may blow the knob off. I would send the unit in for repair if I thought that would take care of the problem. Because of the design I feel this will continue to happen. The photo is the mount for the pressure release knob. In the lower part of the photo you see a metal cup the site on the metal lid. Inside that medal cup is where the plastic mount goes that holds the whole assembly together. This plastic mount is about 2cm thick and will not stand up to constant heating and cooling. You can see that it wasn't just a random piece of plastic braking the whole assembly disintegrated. All of the little pieces of plastic should be one piece. What would have happened if that failed under pressure? Deni concern for their customers safety should include this piece. It may be that this product should be recalled for safety reasons.
justification: The pressure cooker's plastic mount failure could lead to injury if it fails under pressure, and the design flaw suggests this is likely to happen with regular use.

technicians who came out subsequently to repair the oven and the refrigerator that our unit was
not subject to recall.  The igniter was replaced in early December, 2011.

We had complaints made to Electrolux of strong gas smell when the oven was on (no problems with the top burners).  They sent technicians out several times, but found no problem with the oven.  They did not bring any emission testing equipment, just verified that the oven burners were ignited.

Our carbon monoxide detectors went off beginning on June 13, 2012 Electrolux again sent a technician
on June 19, 2012 who reported my complaints to Electrolux but stated that he found that the oven
burners were igniting.  Electrolux authorized a second opinion on 6/22/12, but the servicer was not available for a week.  On that date, June 22, 2012 I called our local gas utility, [REDACTED] , who immediately dispatched an emergency technician to my apartment, who turned the range on, stated that the gas connection to the range was not defective, his gas level testing equipment revealed that the range released dangerously high levels of carbon monoxide and he shut off the gas service to my apartment and issued a warning card that is affixed to the range.  The utility will not turn on the gas unless I replace the range and that range is tested by [REDACTED] .

UPDATE FROM SUBMITTER: The consumer's husband was hospitalized due to alleged injuries
incurred from exposure to carbon monoxide from faulty Electrolux range. The reporting consumer has been receiving outpatient medical treatment.

The noise sounded like electrical wiring arching and was followed by an massive amount of smoke coming from the top right corner of the dishwasher door (near the LED Display). I ran over to the dishwasher and pushed the power button on the dishwasher however, the dishwasher continued to arch and smoke and the LED display would not go off. incident_description:
I set my dishwasher to run as usual in the late evening. I went downstairs to watch tv. About 15 minutes later I asked my husband if he could smell electrical burning. He did, so we both went running upstairs to thinking it was a new box fan we had just purchased. What we found was smoke pouring out of the dishwasher from behind the upper right hand corner where the start and stop buttons are located.  I tried pushing the stop button only to find it unresponsive. I noticed that it felt hot and then saw there was a quarter sized bubble protruding from the front panel immediately under the stop button, it was extremely hot and soft to the touch.  At this point  we try opening the dishwasher to get it to stop and it stays powered on, spraying wont stop, smoke still streaming out. I grab our fire extinguisher hand it to my husband to stand by while I run to the breaker panel to try and cut power. I try the first three breakers labeled kitchen, no luck. I run back up to check to see if it worked, then run back down to look at breakers, I notice there is a single breaker with a different Label for dishwasher, off.  That works to power it off and smoke slows down. We decide to turn it back on to see if we can get it to drain, we get it to drain. My husband opens the door to check and see if the draining is complete. That is when the fire flash of flame comes out of the right side, then about 2 seconds later a larger flash of flame, soccer ball size, happens. That is when I fly back downstairs and hit the breaker again. This slows smoke and stops fire. The kitchen reeks of electrical fire two days later as I write this.  The dishwasher needs to be replaced and smells awful still.  It is a kitchen aid, model KUDP01DLBL5 serial number FR2701257 Also says type 577-0. It was purchased before we bought this house. I have paperwork showing that the warranty ran out August 2005.

I hope this is enough information to be helpful. We are very thankful that we were awake when this happened instead of it being in the middle of the night when I usually run it.  We were lucky, but I don't want something to happen to someone else.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

The bottom of the bottle blew off, the plastic and brass valving broke into pieces and blew out about the kitchen, and it blew parts, plastic pieces, and water all over me and my entire kitchen.  I have ringing in my ears from the explosion.  I notified sodastream by telephone.

A 52 YOM reports soda maker machine exploded during use causing him to experience ringing in his ears.  The bottom of the bottle blew off, the plastic & brass valving broke into pieces & blew out & it blew parts, plastic pieces, and water all over him & his entire kitchen.
justification: The incident caused ringing in the ears, which is an injury, and significant property damage, warranting a severity level of 3. Such explosions are rare but documented, indicating an occurrence likelihood of 2.

incident_description:
I own a  Frigidaire electric stove, serial #VF61859231

The stove top burners go on by themselves at any point in time.  There is no way to shut it off. 
Last night June 20, 2012 I heard a beeping noise in the kitchen at about 2:00AM.  The burners were on at "Hi" according to the digital screen, yet the manual control knob was in the off position.
I could not shut off the stove top burners and they were red hot.  I had to shut off the breaker in order to turn off the burners.  I am very concerned about  the potential for a fire.

Prior to this the stove top burners could go on if the oven was heating or if you placed a hot item on the stove top. Frigidaire has sent several service repair men and each time they assured that the problem was fixed. 

This is the first time the stove top has gone on by itself in the middle of the night and it seems that the problem is getting worse and more dangerous.  The stove could go on by itself when no one is home and continue to heat until something catches fire.  Or someone who does not know of this problem could leave something on the stove top and it will catch fire.  This last happened to me, when I placed a carry out roasted chicken in a plastic on the stove top to cool off.   This was how I discovered the problem.  Fortunately I was home, I smelled the smoke and was able to stop the fire before it caused damage.  I have pictures to prove my case.
justification: The stove top burners go on by themselves, posing a risk of fire, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: I purchased a GE coffee maker from walmart about three months ago.  This morning I woke up to my smoke detectors going off and my coffee maker fully engulfed in flames.  come to look up on line and this coffee maker was recalled in 2010 for the exact problem.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his under the counter dishwasher as the model began to smoke from the control panel. The consumer stated that the model began to smoke 10 minutes into the cycle. The consumer shut off the dishwasher at the circuit breaker to prevent further damage. 

The consumer stated that the damage was isolated to the dishwasher and the consumer was not injured. The consumer has not called the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer has not called the retailer as of yet. The consumer called the firm today  and was informed that they would send a technician to his home to inspect the model free of charge.
justification: The dishwasher began to smoke, indicating an incident, but no injury occurred and the damage was isolated to the appliance.

incident_description:
Lower oven was set to self-clean. About 30 minutes after starting, the inner-most glass door shattered.
This was the first time I had used the self-clean feature of the lower oven.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering during self-cleaning, but no injury was reported, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence for first-time use.

incident_description:
I purchased a Maytag QuietSeries 200 dishwasher Model #MDBH945AWW3, Serial #NY3514751 in 2009.  This appliance has performed well up until about 6 months ago when I began experiencing electrical problems with the unit.  Problems include the electronic control panel lights not working and the control panel not responding when making selections.  Now the unit does not function at all.

I have taken this dishwasher apart to examine the wires inside the front door leading from the main electronic control board to the exterior control panel and have also had an electrician examine the wiring of the unit (see attached pictures).  Upon conclusion of this inspection I have found that the main wiring harness from the control panel to the electronic control board is severed and burned in an area of the wiring that is not covered by a plastic layer of protection or coating.  I believe that this electrical wire has been damaged by moisture buildup during the normal operation of this dishwasher.  

I hope to find a positive resolution to my problem and I have contacted Maytag/Whirlpool customer support.  The support service has directed me to a service number to pay to have my dishwasher repaired.  I believe that this is a quality control inspection issue or design flaw of the appliance, and it is clearly a problem that should not occur with a dishwasher that is only 3 years old.
justification: The incident involves electrical failure and damage to the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I had a very serious incident with my GE Elite Dishwasher

On 16 June 2012 I found my dishwasher had completed its cycle, however the heating element remained on.  I discovered this while on my way to bed for the night noticing a burning smell.  When I opened the dishwasher there was a blast of hot air.  I tried to reset the dishwasher, however the heating element would not turn off.  I finally resorted to taking out the circuit breaker to get the dishwasher to turn off.  When I investigated the dishwasher I found multiple pieces of melted plastic ware, multiple broken glasses and the  dishwasher tub itself was scorched and melted.  Had I not noticed this before I went to bed for the night I am fearful that my house would have caught fire with me and my family asleep.  

I investigated the recall notices for GE Elite dishwashers and have noticed that there are other models with the exact same issue, however my model was not listed as a recall item.  

This is an extremely serious defect in this appliance that could easily cause great harm or death
justification: The incident caused property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My gas range is 4 years old.  I broiled pork chops for 20 minutes, turned off the oven and proceeded to feed my family. About 30 minutes later my entire family was sitting at the dinner table and I heard a pop. I looked into the kitchen to find the outer glass door to my oven shattered and in a thousand pieces on my kitchen floor.  Nobody was in the kitchen at the time and the oven had been turned off for the last 30 minutes.  Luckily, my three children were sitting at the dinner table and nobody was injured.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: Toaster was plugged in. Smelled like it was burning. Not able to push or pull the lever or cancel the toasting smell. Handle broke off in the process. Blackened inside. Afraid it might have caught fire. Unplugged it.
justification: The toaster malfunctioned and showed signs of potential fire hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
The Insinkerator model Pro 17 garbage disposal will not turn off.  I contacted the company and it is past the 7 year warranty since it was installed in 2004. We have had issues turning it off for several months but always managed to get it to stop prior to last week.

My plumber has informed me that he installed many of this model when they were new and has subsequently replaced as many as 2-3/month over the past several years.  This model is distinctive because it turns on/off via the top piece that closes the unit instead at a wall switch.

The manufacturer said the model was discontinued but would not say there were problems with the design.

This seems like a huge safety issue and I'm wondering why there was never a recall.
justification: The garbage disposal not turning off poses a potential safety hazard, but no injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express her concerns about her electric, double-wall oven as the racks that support  cook pans on the lower oven are too small and easily fall to the  base of the oven. The consumer stated that this poses a burn hazard to consumerÃÂs while cooking. The consumer stated that she has not been injured by the product. 

The consumer mentioned that there has not been any damage to the oven. The consumer called the retailer today and was referred to the firm. The consumer called the firm today and was informed that there were no recalls for her and referred her to the CPSC. The consumer stated that the racks are so small that they are not supported by the inner housing of the lower oven.
justification: The consumer reported a potential burn hazard but confirmed no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Five Burner (if counting Warmer) Electric Range, smooth top.


All was turned off on range when the left front burner (if facing range) made cracking/pop sound and cracked the portion of the glass top that was around that burner. 
There are more than a few cracks but they are contained in the burner area.

The right front burner element size can be adjusted to inner, middle or all but skips over middle.

This same burner when turned on and used for cooking,  shoots tiny little sparks under the glasstop.


Caller contacted manufacturer today, April 24th, 2012 and was advised to create a report with CPSC.

Caller would request that her range be repaired at manufacturer expense or if she has repaired the range she requests to be reimbursed all charges at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved a cracked glass top and sparking burner, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught fire while running.  The door could be opened, but the dishwasher could not be shut off.  The only way to stop the burning was to turn off the circuit breaker.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident that could lead to injury if not promptly addressed, though no injury was reported in this case.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while he attempting to pour the hot water from the kettle, the handle separated itself from the kettle which caused the kettle to fall to the floor.  The hot contents was spilled which could have serious burns if he did not act quickly.  There was no injury.

The consumer stated that the screws are inadequate to hold the plastic together, this is an inadequate design.  The kettle also has a thermostat which automatically shuts off once the water is boiled.

The manufacturer was not contacted.

The consumer feels that this kettle handle is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved the kettle handle separating and spilling hot water, but no injury occurred. The design flaw suggests this could happen again, making it possible.

incident_description:
An Anchor Hocking glass baking dish exploded after normal use.
An 8x13 glass baking dish that I'd used for approximately 8 years exploded in my kitchen. 
I took the dish from a room temperature cabinet, added room temperature ingredients, baked for 25 minutes at 350 degrees. I removed the dish from the oven and set on a metal trivet and took two servings. 
About 10 minutes later, the dish exploded into many small pieces and several larger pieces. The pieces went flying through my kitchen - had a person been in the kitchen at the time, they would have sustained serious injury.
justification: The glass baking dish exploded, causing potential for serious injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I had used the toaster to make toast.  After removing the toast, the toaster was in the off mode.  Several minutes later a member of my family screamed that the toaster was on fire...flames were shooting several inches out of the toaster.  After unplugging it, it continued to shoot flames and we threw it outside into the snow .  Fortunately, someone was in the kitchen to see the toaster on fire, as there was no toast cooking in it and it appeared to be off.
justification: The toaster caught fire but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The glass door of my frigidaire glass top stove spontaneously exploded and glass flew everywhere.  The stove was not on and was not in use.  Nothing was touching the stove.
Model #FES3655ESC
Serial #NF64111374
justification: The incident involved a spontaneous explosion causing property damage but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
A Frigidaire FGES3065KW range with smooth cook top was installed in our kitchen January 2011. It has had normal domestic use since that time.  I have used the cleaning feature on it 2 or 3 times, the last several months ago. Today, June 19, 2012 I heated the oven to 350F to bake something.  I noticed earlier in the day the left side of the handle was loose, and even fell down on the left, appearing as if there were some problem with the screw holding it onto the oven door and through the layers into the inside of the door.  I just reset it onto the screw and thought I would fix it later in the day after baking. 

I prepared the item to bake (a pan of brownies) and set it down and opened the door to put them in. I also noticed a mild but odd smell, perhaps a bit chemical ? but nothing I could place.   Without warning, the outside glass door e x p l o d e d all over the kitchen, onto the counter top to the left and across the kitchen floor, about 10 to 12 feet away from the door.  It appeared to explode in the direction of where the handle had come loose earlier as there were no shards of glass to the right of the oven.  I spent hours cleaning up the glass, which thankfully was safety glass, so I had not been diced to bits after being hit by it. 

We have called the place we purchased it at, Standard TV and Appliance in Beaverton, Oregon and will have it fixed.  It is just beyond warranty so it is our expense.  I am leery after reading about others' experiences with this event and don't know what to do to prevent this in the future, as there was nothing unusual in my use of it.  Should I not use the cleaning feature provided? We have done nothing to the door to cause the handle to loosen.  I did read online about one man, a mechanical engineer who felt that the Frigidaire factory was using power screwdrivers while constructing their products that stripped the threads on the screws in their ovens. I am 5 feet tall and not a particularly "rough" person, just doing a normal amount of cooking and cleaning of the oven. I use the convection feature rarely, but wonder now if I should never use it?   I am the only cook in my house.  I never set anything on the oven door when it is open and am careful to keep the door closed (as I was instructed) after the oven is turned off and the fan is still on, in order to keep the electronics cool in the panel. 

The next oven I purchase will NOT have a glass door after this experience, but I am stuck with this one for a while, wondering when and if the next door will go as this was an expensive oven (to us) and is already installed.
justification: The incident involved the oven door exploding, but no injuries were reported, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
30" Jenn Air Gas Center Down Draft cook top "Grates"  the paint disintergrated in the center of the grate leaving raw cast iron exposed the the gas flame causing High amounts of Carbon Monoxide in my home.  Readings by Centerpoint Entex Gas company, Sears repair and American Home Shield repairmen as follows
CO 94
CO 69
I HAVE TWO PHOTOGRAPHS OF THE INSTRUMENTS reading.  I sent a registered letter to Whirlpool and they tell me they are not responsible because the unit is too old.  This is the second set of grates since I purchased in 1996.

Model No CVG4280W
Serial  SN123074QN
Faulty Grate Item Number 12001428

My kitchen is open and large, a small kitchen or home, someone could die.  I paid a lot of money to have my air condition/heater/vents cleaned only to find the cause was my cooktop.  I had Black Sticky Suet everywhere in my home.  I still need the carpets cleaned and more.  But the most important issue is Whirlpool must issue a recall so that no one dies.  One repairman told me " You don't know half the story!"  Grandma just laid down last night and died!"
justification: The incident involves high levels of carbon monoxide, a lethal gas, with potential for death as indicated by the repairman's anecdote.

incident_description: We started our Kitchenaid KUDP01ILWH dishwasher serial number FR2702023 (purchased in 11/20/2004).  A few minutes later we smelled a strong odor of plastic burning.  My wife opened the door to see if something had fallen into the heating element. When she opened the door the diswasher was still filled with water and black smoke was coming out from behind the control panel. I pulled the plug on the dishwasher and the smoking stopped.  The right side of the control panel was hot to the touch.  Had we started the dishwasher a few minutes later and then went to church like we normally do, we could have had a house fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was a singular event with no prior occurrences mentioned.

incident_description:
Amana Range Self clean oven Model ACS3350AS
Just purchased home and was preheating oven to cook pizza. Noticed oven door would not shut tight. Noticed burning on outside of oven, control overlay panel and knobs. Oven became extremely hot on the outside during cooking. Burnt myself touching above oven door. Pizza would not cook according to directions because oven is releasing heat and frying control panel. Did research online and noticed MANY complaints regarding this range. The hinges are faulty which is frying the control panel and the unit becomes extremely hot. There is a class action lawsuit in Florida regarding this unit. This is a known problem out there but Amana refuses to acknowledge it. I am afraid to use my oven. They refuse to fix the problem.
justification: The user reported being burnt by touching the oven, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description mentions many complaints and a class action lawsuit, suggesting the issue is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: When using the ice dispenser on our LG Refrigerator Model lfx28977, a flame came out of it and the inside filled with smoke. This refrigerator has been in use for less than 3 years. The smoke had a strong chemical smell to it. Now if we try to use the dispenser we get the chemical-smelling black smoke.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I bought an Ultrex pressure cooker about 8 years ago and it worked fine until today..  It exploded and flew into the air.  Luckily for me, I was about 10 feet away when it happened.  The entire side connector blew off and steam shot out and the cooker flew up and landed on the floor of my kitchen, with pieces flying everywhere..I had just been standing in front of it and went to set a timer and it happened.  I almost got killed.  I went on line and found that there was a recall on this particular product in 2006, but I was never informed.  I called Home Shopping Network, where I bought the product and they said they will look into it for me.  But, I felt I should notify you also.  They also said that shortly after the recall was issued that Ultrex went out of business.
justification: The pressure cooker exploded, causing significant damage and potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred as the user was not directly in front of it when it happened.

incident_description:
Caller purchased set of two glass baking dishes April 8th, 2012, one 13" x 9" and the other in package is square two quart size.

Caller preheated her oven to 375 degrees, placed chicken in 13" x 9" glass baking dish set timer two hours and went into living room.

She had only been in living room for approximately ten minutes when she heard a loud bang sound.
She thought at first that one of her large pictures had fallen off the wall.

She went to the oven and saw that the dish she had placed chicken in had exploded with all pieces of glass still contained in oven and broiler.
She opened the oven door and glass fell through the open crack to her floor.

She turned her oven off, allowed dish to cool and then cleaned oven of glass pieces.
Caller estimates cleaning time for oven at approximately an hour and a half.
She has saved pieces of baking dish.

She has not contacted the manufacturer yet but does plan to contact them and called CPSC after reading online that this incident had happened to others.

She would like to be reimbursed for the baking dish and for the chicken that was ruined during this incident.
justification: The glass baking dish exploded, but no injuries were reported, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had the dishwasher on for approximately an hour, which he believed was over the normal cycle time. The consumer had the dishwasher on the ÃÂwash cycle.ÃÂ He stated that started smelling a burning odor and opened door to the dishwasher and it continue running the cycle although the door was opened. The consumer stated that usually when the door is opened the cycle stopped. 

The consumer stated that he closed the door and pushed the manual button stated to ÃÂcancel/ drainÃÂ and this option allowed the dishwasher to drain. The consumer stated that after it drained he noticed that the dishwasher was stuck on the ÃÂdrain cycleÃÂ although all the water was out.  The consumer opened the door to see if it would stop the cycle and it did not stop. 

The consumer stated that in order to turn the dishwasher off he had to turn off the circuit breaker. 

The consumer stated that he believes that the problems seem to be that the circuit board of the dishwasher was starting to have electrical problem. 

The consumer stated that there were no injuries and there were no damages to his home structure. 

The consumer stated that he visited a website where he signed a petition against the manufacturer. The consumer stated that he did not contact the consumer by phone because he believed that no remedy would be provided since the product was out of warranty. 

The consumer believes that this product should be investigated do to the fire hazard that it poses.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with no injuries or structural damage, but poses a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: Turned on Kitchenaid Dishwasher model number KUDP01ILBL3 Sunday afternoon. After about five minutes, a terrible burning smell filled the kitchen  - smelled like electrical wires burning. Turned it off, allowed it to drain (by pushing cancel button), A little later we tried again and had same result. Appears to be a fire hazard. Checked online and found a class action lawsuit -- several people have already experienced fires with the KUDPO series of Kitchenaid Dishwashers. People need to know about this because it has the potential to cause a fire in the home. Will call company tomorrow, but apparently they will not help and have not recalled the faulty dishwashers yet -- at least according to reports on the internet and the class action lawsuit filed last November.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard with no actual fire or injury reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reports and a class action lawsuit indicating a known issue.

incident_description:
Refrigerator  -GE  Monogrm
Model # ZFSB23DRGSS
Serial# TL443287


I placed my GE Monogram refrigerator in service in December of 2006.
In 2011  noticed brown rusty buildup and liquid settling on the bottom
of  my unit. After removing shelf  I farther noticed small compartment
on the back inside wall form which the rusty fluid is coming out.
I the same area I also noticed presence of  mold.
Using the screwdriver I removed small grilled cover. Under the removed
cover I uncovered heavily corroded metal plate. Condensation water on
the top of extensively corroded meal/zinc plate caused it to produce brown
liquid and spill all over the inside the refrigerator and on near by food. 
I have pictures that I would like to share with you.
Since this crates serious health hazard I asked GE to either replace faulty part or
the unit itself. My request was denied.

On November 12, 2011 at 1 PM GE technician arrived at my home to asses  
the situation. Based on a several pictures I showed,  he identified faulty part but
was not sure who is going to pay for labor and parts and left without repairing anything. 

Several days later I contacted GE customer service and I was informed that 

"In checking the service record, it states that the technician replaced a defrost
 drain pan on 11/12/11 at no charge."
In fact nothing got replaced at all. ÃÂ The technician did not even get close to the refrigerator.
he didn't even  look at the refrigerator.
All he did is to look at the pictures I showed him..
Why records state that the technician replaced a defrost drain pan on 11/12/11 at no charge
remains mystery.
The presence of corrosion and mold inside my refrigerator crates health hazard and this is 
primary reason I report it to Consumer Product Safety Commission.

Please, help.

Regards

[redacted]
justification: The incident involves a health hazard due to mold and corrosion in the refrigerator, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was experiencing problems with the electric range front left burner.  These incidents has been ongoing for approximately 6 months.  Originally, she was unable to turn burner on.  Once it came on, she was unable to power off without using the breaker box.  When breaker was turned on again, the burner spontaneously came on by itself.

2/23/12 The consumer called for service and the service agent turned on the burner but was unable to turn it off, she had to switch it off from the circuit breaker.

2/23/12 The consumer contacted the manufacturer and she was advised to contact the agency to find out if the range had been recalled, but it was not part of the recall.

The consumer feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a safety hazard but no injury has been reported. The issue is ongoing and likely to recur based on the description.

incident_description:
LG Refrigerator purchased from Sears as a Kenmore appliance [3 door type].  When I happened to open the door of the fridge. I smelled smoke or something burning and noticed the light unit with control temperature panel had began to melt light bulb cover.  It was extremely hot, so tried to loosen, unscrew the bulbs; the unit pulled away from its housing on the inside roof of the refrigerator.  Now have no lights, but at least its not burning up.  Tried to work with Sears Repair--no help.  Independent dealer in our small town is trying to figure out what to do to try and fix, but will more than likely get this refrig. [AKA oven] hauled away to be replaced with a new NON LG product.  Not worth the worry of when it will happen again.
Reading all the same type of complaints certainly indicates a recall should be made; looking at new refrigs notice the design has changed somewhat [flush surface, no control board, and small LED lights completely covered], but still would NOT trust LG based on their history record of not seeming to do things for other clients registering the same problem many many times over.  Seems like a typical wolf dressed in sheep's clothing--or playing 3 blind mice--hear, see and do nothing about a problem being expressed time and time again.  Customer service is thing of the past.

Hope some sort of resolution will be made before further damages occur to others and possibly at a horrendous cost!
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and melting components but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Elite Model 665.16262400 caught on fire and was emitting thick smoke out of right side of the front panel.  The unit did not shutdown when door was opened or cancel was pressed.  The fire was extinguished by removing power.
justification: The appliance caught fire and emitted smoke, indicating a significant incident, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Frigidaire glass cooktop's right front burner will not turn off. When on, the temperature rises to a dangerously high level. When frying, the temperature rose so rapidly, that the grease splattered everywhere and the pan was damaged.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with potential for injury due to uncontrolled high temperature and grease splattering, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
Maytag dishwasher Serial # 10908481UF recall repair completed January 2008.

June 2012 during rinse cycle the circuit board got very hot, melted front panel and made lots of black smoke. It quit smoking when circuit breaker was turned off. Digital display was off and unit had stopped running.

Thankful that I was at home before situation became more serious.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing smoke and damage, but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was a specific recall-related issue.

incident_description:
We have a GE quiet power 3 model GLD6860N00SS, serial: DM833411B 

while my wife was washing a normal load of dishes she started to notice a smell like something was on fire. When she walked back in to the kitchen she noticed that our dishwasher was on fire, luckily only internally and it did not affect any kitchen surfaces.

The motherboard control unit is completel charred, and of course, the unit is now inoperable, and likely beyond repair. My biggest concern now, as luckily no one was hurt, is that this model appears to have been manufactured between the 2003-2006 recall, and is not included on the list, despite the fact it appears to suffer from the same defect as units recalled.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire internally but did not cause injury or spread to kitchen surfaces, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Cuisinart DCC-2205 coffee maker started smoking from electrical cord penetration on rear of machine.  This began shortly after the completion of the brewing cycle.  Luckily, I smelled the burning electrical components in time to unplug the machine and prevent a fire.  Unit was purchased new from Kohls in March of 2012.
justification: The coffee maker started smoking but was unplugged in time to prevent injury or fire, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
About 1.5 hours after finishing brewing coffee, my Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker began popping noises and smoking from the bottom of the maker.  It turned off (all lights and clock) went off.  Hot plate start sizzling.  I was afraid it was going to catch fire.  I unplugged the maker and placed it outside on the pavement for safety reasons.  

I had purchased this coffee maker originally on December 26, 2010 at Bed, Bath and Beyond (Foxoboro, MA).  It was used almost daily until this incident.  I had a previous model from 2002 that lasted 8 years, so was hoping for the same from this maker.  

I have read other review of this happening to others on-line.  The coffee maker is a fire hazard and should be recalled.  Please help us consumers!
justification: The coffee maker exhibited dangerous behavior (smoking, popping noises) but no injury or fire occurred, and the issue is reported by others online.

incident_description:
Friends gave me a

Toastmaster 4-slice Toaster Oven/Broiler Model TOV320

for my Jersey shore summer condo.  There have been several fires in it, on several occasions the timer has not advanced and the appliance not shut off causing the toast to burn, and it has also overheated on many occasions.  (have pictures on cell phone -- unfortunately don't know how to download to this form)  

Having had the problem several times I forbid my grands from using it.  When I recently saw the complaints I realized it was past time for me to report this unsafe product.  

Went to the manufacturers website and inasmuch as I did not bring the appliance home and it was required that I put in numbers from the cord it would not accept my complaint.  Called the number on the booklet and that was futile.  Went to consumer reports, underwriter laboratories, and finally found numerous complaints on SelectSmart.com. Could not believe all the complaints and they are still sold in stores -- [REDACTED] etc.

I then called the number for Consumer Products Safety and was directed to this site.  
I have been online for hours with this complaint.

Incidents ranged from July 2011 to June 2012.
justification: The toaster oven has caused several fires and overheated multiple times, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I bought a new Black & Decker toaster oven Model TRO480BS and loved it for 11 days. On day 12, while toasting within normal operation, the timer "dings" and the glass door explodes sending hot glass over the kitchen counter and floor. Glass was found inside, underneath and 4 to 5 feet in front of the unit. Fortunately, no one was in the room.
justification: The toaster oven's glass door exploded during normal operation, but no one was injured as the room was unoccupied.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire refrigerator started on fire on Sunday 6/10/12...from the inside...

Model number FRS6L9EFSS3
Serial 4A63409032
Manufactured 8/06

I'm not a fire expert, but it certainly looks to me like the electronic thermostat adjustments shorted out -- repeatedly, creating a burning, boiling blob of plastic refrigerator lava.

I can't get anywhere with the company, and they aren't taking me seriously -- I realize this isn't life-and-death at this point, but as you can see from the photos, I was a rubber seal away from my house burning down. I returned from a trip to the east coast on Sunday night to an extremely upset pregnant wife, a fridge on my front patio full of boiled food, and a house full of black burnt plastic smoke.

My wife called me Sunday morning to tell me the refrigerator quit. I told her that I'd take care of it when I got home, and she headed to work. I called my dad to see if he knew the measurements, so I could shop online for a replacement while at the airport. Fortunately for our home, dog, and cat, my father and brother-in-law stopped by the house and smelled the burnt plastic. Some quick thinking, the removal my house's front door, and some muscles saved the day!

Since that time however, I've been getting the runaround from Frigidaire. They say they require a report from the fire department or a Frigidaire authorized service rep to confirm the fire...
Scottsdale Fire was helpful to a point, but since no other damage was done to the house, the refrigerator was moved outside, and no emergency call was placed -- they won't write a report. 
Frigidaire service hasn't returned my calls. The local numbers have all told me that they don't service appliances over a year old, or that I have to pay $79 for a service call -- requiring a day off from work to wait for a two-hour window because they need me physically present to look at the burned refrigerator in the front yard. They aren't coming to address the safety concerns, nor to fix it, just confirming a fire. But again, the runaround...

I have my communications all documented, as well as photos of everything right down to a bottle of 2011 [REDACTED] that I was planning to opening in celebration of my son's birth this coming October.

The fridge is still on my front walkway -- until the homeowners association sees it or Frigidaire takes action.
justification: The refrigerator fire caused significant property risk and distress but no injuries or deaths were reported.

On 2/28/2012 the consumer was notified (they did not call us, WE HAD TO CALL THEM) (Confirmation #[REDACTED]) that the microwave had not been installed properly and, therefore, the consumer would be responsible for the costs of repair.

On 3/18/2012 Consumer noticed arcing on the inside left rear of the appliance while again popping popcorn. The consumer noticed that the popcorn which had been placed on the glass rotating tray lifted the metal grate sitting above the popcorn as the popcorn popped. As it kept raising, the metal grate touched the inside rear of the microwave causing lit to arc. The consumer pressed the control button immediately causing the microwave to stop, but noticed another burn mark on the plastic surface inside.

The consumer noticed that the rotating glass tray which has been placed on the inside left rear lifted the metal grate as the popcorn popped. The rotating tray touched the side of the microwave which caused it to arc. He pressed the cancel button immediately and noticed a burn mark.

incident_description:
We blended cooked food and water in the "baby bullet" food processor. While feeding our 13-month old son, we noticed he was having difficulty chewing. He finally let us look into his mouth and we noticed a piece of rubber that was approximately an inch long. (It was the gasket to the food processor that sits at the base below the threading where the cup screws into the blade.) We matched that piece with the remaining gasket that had broken and found that there is still a one-inch piece missing. The remaining gasket was still firmly seated in the bottom of the base. We believe the missing piece was swallowed by our child. Fortunately, he did not choke on it necessitating an ambulance to help in a lethal situation. Our pediatrician indicated that since this material is plastic, it will not appear on an x-ray. We can only watch our son and wait to see if he has any side effects or if the piece will pass through his intestines. 

Before using the processor, I had removed the gasket to clean it since food was trapped underneath it. Replacement gaskets were included with the box. Again to reiiterate, I firmly inserted the gasket back into the bottom after washing it. 

The "baby bullet user manual and cookbook" indicates to inspect the gasket before using. It does not instruct on whether or not the gasket needs to be replaced at set intervals nor does it give instructions on how to replace it. This would be helpful information since food does get trapped below it regularly causing bacteria to build if not removed and washed.

This product needs to be taken out of distribution immediately. This information needs to be reported to the news agencies.

Please respond to us as soon as possible.

Thanks
justification: The child swallowed a piece of rubber, which poses a risk of injury if it causes internal damage or obstruction, though no immediate choking or lethal situation occurred.

incident_description:
Please help us.   Every resident of our five-story, 137-unit  condo, which is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is designated as an official City of Seattle Landmark,  is in clear and present danger  due to defective KithchenAid microwaves. The parent company, Whirlpool Corp., is headquartered in Benton Harbor, Michigan.
            At about 11:45 p.m. on May 22, 2012, my husband and I were asleep in bed in our third story loft when we were jolted awake by a booming sound that felt as though a jetliner was revving its engines for takeoff.  As we tumbled over each other as we jumped out of bed, we saw flashes of red and yellow dancing underneath the doorsill of our closed bedroom door.  Just as I put my hand on the door to open it,  the acrid smell of something on fire hit me like a club.
            Opening the door, we saw red and yellow arcs jumping wildly inside the microwave.  While this was going on, the booming sound continued, along with a pervasive scorched smell spreading over the condo.  Within seconds, my husband grabbed the fire extinguisher in our kitchen as I called 911 to summon the fire department.  My husband managed to turn the microwave off in the midst of this terrifying incident. Suddenly, the large red and yellow arcs (what we presume were electrical arcs) halted, along with that terrible booming sound.  The glass turntable was scorched, along with the plastic tripod doohickey it sits on.
            The firefighters arrived shortly after my call, and although all but the smell had died before their arrival, they checked to make sure there was nothing smoldering inside the wall, etc.  Moreover, one of the firefighters checked the main circuit breaker of our unit.  There were no signs of any fuses anywhere being tripped and there were no blackened areas around any outlets nor did our condo lose power at any time during or after this incident.
           This is an EXTREMELY important part:  Please bear in mind that the microwave - which had not even been in use in a couple of days - TURNED ITSELF ON IN THE MIDDLE OF THE NIGHT.  Not only were we in a lot of danger, so was everyone else in the building.  What if we had not been there to react so quickly?  There is no doubt in our minds that the microwave would have exploded in flames.  The firefighters indicated they suspected a possible defective microwave.  They told us not to attempt to turn it back on and it is currently unplugged.
         Since we reported this very dangerous incident to other residents and our board of directors, other  scary situations involving KitchenAid microwaves are pouring into our board.    Those reports always involve the microwaves turning themselves on at will and in many of the cases, the residents were UNABLE to get their microwaves to turn off without unplugging them.  This is extremely unsafe. One resident, for example, wrote our board that he was so concerned with the microwave situation that he termed it a matter of  "life and death. "
            Despite repeated requests by our board and complaints from residents,  Whirlpool has adamantly refused to send out technicians to inspect the microwaves in all units.  There are additional reports of very dangerous incidents on consumer blogs ( such as www.fixya.com) concerning the same model number, KHMS155SS-3.   Moreover, when my husband initially contacted the KitchenAid hotline and told a staffer about firefighters being summoned, etc., she said that KitchenAid believes the fire dangers are caused by faulty circuit boards built into that model of microwaves.  She expressed zero surprise about what happened to our micro.
            We are horrified that the company did not and has not informed residents in our building about the dangers they apparently are aware have been taking place. Although, after hearing about the fire department being summoned in out case, they agreed to repair our microwave.
              Despite calls to the company's headquarters, Whirlpool told us and others in a defiinite decision that they would only check out safety issues with microwaves ONLY after something happens or a problem is encountered with each individual microwave.  In my opinion, that is a short- sighted, dangerous decision.  It's akin to knowing that an airplane fleet has been experiencing safety issues and the acting only if a plane gets in an emergency situation with passengers on board. These incidents with the microwaves can and have happened with zero warning from the microwaves.
              We want a recall issued, especially since the company refuses to provide safety checks by their technicians at no cost to consumers and the fact that they have not notified consumers about defective microwaves that could harm or kill their customers,
               Thank you for reading this.  Please help us.  Our board can be reached at [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a microwave turning on by itself, creating a fire hazard, and multiple similar reports suggest a pattern of dangerous behavior that could lead to injury.

incident_description: My wife and I got a gift certificate for Macy's as a wedding gift. Sometime late 2010 or early 2011 we use the certificate to purchase a set of Belgique cookware. When we purchased the set we had a bit of money left over and got the 2 pack set of Hard Anodized with Silicone Handles 10" & 12" skillets. The stock number on both pans is #30209. For the first year or so they were fine and worked very well but over time the silicone and the metal in the handle has evidently separated allowing water into the handle when the skillet is washed. It does not matter whether it is in the dishwasher or in the sink, it allows water in. When the skillet is placed on the stove the water trapped in the handle turns to steam. The handle becomes scalding hot and will burn you. My wife filled in the online complaint form on the Belgique website around 6 months ago and got no response from them. I got a pretty bad burn (no blistering but redness and tenderness) early last week and decided to call Macy's about the problem last Thursday because I could no longer find the Belgique website online. I asked the customer service representative for the contact information for Belgique and rather than supplying the information that I asked for, she began to ask questions. I was fine with this. She informed me that she would check with the buyer to see if there were problems with the cookware and call me back that afternoon with instructions on what to do to get replacement cookware. This is Wednesday of the following week and I have heard nothing from the lady in customer service so I called again and asked to speak with her. I was put through to another agent and was told she was on the phone but would call me back shortly. No word of course and it has been over an hour.

incident_description:
We bought our home new 5 years ago and the electric range/oven (Kenmore model# 790.9611340a) came with it.  It has worked okay in that time but for recently the left front burner will not turn off.  The first few times it happened jiggling would turn it off...sometimes a spark or click would come from the back so we just avoided using that burner.  
Last night I turned the oven on, used it, did dishes and sat on the couch.  It's then I heard the clicking noise the range sometimes makes when it is on and looked to see the left front burner had turned itself on!  WE DIDN'T EVEN USE THAT BURNER.  No amount of turning or jiggling would turn it off.  I finally unplugged the whole thing and called Sears.  The call center drone tried to sell me a maintenance plan and in no way was interested in the fact this could have been a huge problem.  My wife often sets her purse/groceries on the stove when she comes home and we have a six and three year old who often set things on there as well.
I'm glad I caught this when I did.  
Several Internet searches found that there are other models with this exact problem being recalled but my particular model is not one of them...yet.
I work in the homeowners insurance industry and can tell you if this had caused a loss of some sort we would surrogate this company to the hilt.  I also know it takes several losses and some math for the corporation to decide it's more cost effective to recall a model than to fight lawsuits/insurance co's.  It's too bad someone is going to have to loose their property, become hurt, or die before Sears does the right thing.  But that's business...I'm getting rid of mine and going to a local appliance business.
I hope this complaint adds to the list to get something done.

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer on 05/14/2012 and explained that the dishwasher was not working and the manufacturer informed her that they could not assist her because it was out of warranty. 

The consumer stated that her husband decided (05/15/2012) to open the control panel to see what happened, before they contact another repair technician. The consumer stated that her husband saw that the ÃÂblue plugÃÂ inside was melted and burnt on the left side. The consumer stated that there were no other visible damages to the dishwasher. 

The consumer stated that she turned the dishwasher off from the circuit breaker. She contacted the repair technician and she is awaiting his response.  The consumer stated that she will not be using the dishwasher until the repair technician looks at it and she is considering not using it again. 

The consumer stated that she was not injured and there were no damages to her home. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that they would not repair the dishwasher, because they had already repaired it before. 

The consumer stated that she believes this product should be investigated, because it poses a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with a melted plug, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he had placed the oven on bake 350 degree.  However, it automatically switched over to broil at 500 degrees, he was not able to power it off from the control panel, he had to switch it off from the circuit breaker.  He stated that whenever the circuit breaker was turned back on the broiler came on.  He had to unplugged the unit.

There were no prior problems with this range.  

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

The consumer is concerned that this electric range/oven is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off normally, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern. I am an owner and board member of a 137 unit condominium building in Seattle WA. 
Recently we have had about 8-10 know issues with our KitchenAid over the range microwaves that were installed in the building during construction.
The construction was started in 2005 and the last condos were finished by the end or 2007, approximately. All 137 units have the same microwave installed. 
The issues are (1) self-starting with no turn off possible at the key pad. (2) Self-starting with sparking (fire department was called in this case) (3) self-starting and unit becoming extremely hot to the touch. In each case the only way to turn off the unit was to un-plug or switch off the breaker at the panel.
KitchenAid model #ÃÂs involved are: KHMS155LSS-3 and KHMS155LSS-4. Manufactured between 2005-2006 I think. 
Is the CPSC or Saferproducts.gov aware of these issues with these KitchenAid models? Is there an official recall that you know about? How do citizens start or petition a recall of these units?
My interaction with KitchenAid to date is that they will fix, for free, only if you have experienced a problem. If you have not had a problem they will send out a technician but the owner will incur the service charge if no problems are found. 
Our HOA is deeply concerned that the microwaves that have not had any problems to date are basically sitting time bombs in our condos and have the potential of causing serious consequences including death if KitchenAid does not fix or recall all microwaves with these model numbers.
As a homeowner I have not experienced any of these problems with my microwave. But since I have been made aware, my microwave stays unplugged when not in use.
As a board we have sent out numerous awareness emails and letters stating the hazards and if individual owners are concerned to un-plug there microwave and to contact KitchenAid.
KitchenAid is unwilling to mitigate this issue as a group problem. Is there anything more, as an association, we can do to get help in fixing this extreme and potential deadly issue? Your insight and help would be greatly appreciated.
justification: The incident involves microwaves self-starting and sparking, with potential for fire, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description:
frigidaire cooktop will not turn off and not heating at set temperature.
Model FEC30S6ABF 
Today I was boiling water on high and turned it to simmer. A few minutes later the pot was boiling over. The eye was glowing on a low setting so I tried to turn it off it took 3 attempts before it turned off. A month ago this happened on that day I had to turn the eye off using a circuit breaker. That time when set to  off it would glow then go dark and glow again repeatedly. The breaker stopped the cycle.
justification: The cooktop malfunctioned but did not cause injury or death, only inconvenience and potential safety hazard.

incident_description: The consumer purchased a microwave and five months later it caught on fire while in use.  She contacted an electrician who checked out the outlet and there were no problems there.  She put a bowl in the microwave, after less than a minute the microwave started flaming from the inside.  She called the manufacturer and received a replacement microwave.  The same thing occurred to her replacement five months later.  She contacted the manufacturer again and is awaiting a response.
justification: The microwave caught fire twice, but there were no reports of injury or death.

incident_description: I bough Stove (Kenmore electric power range) from Sears 5 years ago. Now, everytime, I turn the switch off, but the burner still on. I have to unplug the power to make the burner off
justification: The stove burner remains on despite being turned off, posing a fire hazard but no injury has been reported.

incident_description:
I purchased this Whirlpool microwave oven on 3/7/10.  On 5/24/12 I cooked a bag of microwavable vegetables in the microwave like I have many times before.  The microwve burst into a fire and blew a hole  on the left side of the microwave. Dangerous  fumes came from the microwave and caused me severe headaches.  I immediately contacted Whirlpool at [REDACTED] and they sent a repair man out that said that it was a manufacturer defect.  The repair Man was named [REDACTED].  Repair man also took a photo.  They refused to replace the microwave and offered $63.00 and wanted to haul the microwave away.  They never showed up .  They still have this microwave oven for sale at Lowes with different serial numbers.  I am 83 years old and am warning others to beware of this microwae and that Whirlpool has pool customer service.  This product is defective, dangerous.  The defective one is sitting in my Garage
ModelPF4M Serial WMH2175XVB-1 TRY 4347609.
justification: The microwave fire caused severe headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). The defect was confirmed by a repairman, but such incidents are unlikely (likelihood 2) based on the description of a single occurrence.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool Oven.  It is model # RS610PXGW8 Serial # XP3103528.  The oven does not turn off.  The bottom heating element comes on and never turns off during any cycle of the oven.  I had to turn the breakers off to the oven in order to turn it off.  When I turn the breakers back on the oven turns on by itself and does not turn off even though no buttons were pushed.

I spoke to my next door neighbor who had the esame model and they had the exact same thing happen to them and it nearly burned their house down.  The wall behind their oven was charred.  Our homes were built at the same time and are only 6 years old.
justification: The oven's failure to turn off poses a fire hazard, as evidenced by a neighbor's similar experience resulting in charred walls, though no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express her concerns about her under the counter dishwasher as the consumer had a home fire occur last night. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in the cycle for nearly 10 minutes before the unit began to smoke. The consumer could smell electrical burning and her home filled with smoke. The consumer suspects the motor under the dishwasher was the cause. 
The consumer opened the door of the dishwasher and it continued to operate. The dishwasher did not trip the circuit breaker. The consumer called the fire department and they arrive 90 seconds later. The fire department tripped the circuit breaker and removed the dishwasher from under the counter after capping the wires. 
The fire department also vented out her home with a fan and used a small fire extinguisher on the motor of the dishwasher. The damage was isolated to the dishwasher and the consumer was not injured. The consumer called the firm and the firm did not offer any assistance since her product was not on warranty. The consumer stated that her retailer  is out of business.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher smoking and causing a home fire, but no injuries were reported. The damage was isolated to the dishwasher.

incident_description:
On Thursday January 26, 2012, my Cuisinart FlavorBrew 12-cup Coffeemaker, model DCC-750BK caught on fire. I started the brew cycle and stepped into another room. During the brewing process, the coffee pot began began making a loud buzzing sound and I could smell burning/melting plastic. When I re-entered the kitchen, smoke was pouring out of the brew plate area at the bottom of the device. The brew plate was glowing bright red and small flames/sparks were coming out from beneath the front area of the brew plate. It was very frightening! If I hadn't been in the house at the time, there would have been a fire and smoke damage.

I'm concerned that is coffeemaker is a potential fire hazard. I'm reporting this incident because I'm concerned that my experience may not be an isolated occurrence.  And I want the Consumer Products Safety Commission and other consumers to be aware of the potential fire hazard. 

My Cuisinart FlavorBrew 12-cup Coffeemaker was purchased January 28, [2011].  It was in use for only one year.  It has a 3-year limited warranty.
justification: The coffeemaker caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express some of the concerns she had about her 14 cup coffee maker as the product began to smoke during use. The consumer stated that after 5 minutes of usage, the unit began to make loud popping noises and smoked from nearly all of the unit's components. The consumer then unplugged the unit from the outlet and took it outside. 

The consumer was not injured and did not suffer any property damage to her home. The consumer stated that she has not called her home insurance company or the fire department. The consumer considers the product to be unusable. The consumer called the manufacturer yesterday about her concerns and they informed the consumer they were not willing to assist her.
justification: The coffee maker smoked and made loud noises, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: The consumer was cooking a roast.  It had been on 6 hours when he heard a loud 'popping" noise and the lid shattered.  He saw many online reports of the same thing ocurring.  The screw that holds the glass lid to the plastic top is too tight.  The manufacturer offered to provide a new lid free of charge.  The consumer says the unit has only been used three times since they have had it.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and shattered lid, but no injury was reported. The manufacturer's response and online reports suggest this is a known issue.

incident_description:
On 5/8/2012 the consumer was heating up some food in his toaster oven for approximately 10 minutes. While sitting at a table he heard a loud noise. When he turned around he saw that the entire glass to the oven had shattered and spread approximately 4' feet across the room.

There were no injuries associated with the incident.

The manufacturer was not been contacted yet.

The consumer feels that the product is safety hazard because the glass could have potentially been life threatening if it had hit someone and injured himself or a family member.
justification: The glass shattered but no injuries occurred, making it a severity level 2 incident. The likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such incidents are not common but have been reported.

incident_description: This morning, when I went into my kitchen I noticed that the glass oven door of my gas range had shattered.  There were shards and pieces of glass and broken plastic all around my kitchen floor in the area of the gas range.  The oven had not been used in over a week.  I am unsure what happened, as it clearly occurred overnight, when no one was in the kitchen.  Thankfully so, as it could have been much worse had the oven been in use or others in the vicinity of the appliance.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) since such events are uncommon and no prior usage or human interaction was involved.

incident_description:
KitchenAid Microwave/Hood caught fire.  
Model: KHMS155LSS-4
Serial: TR T 19 24182
Manufactured May 2006

I was using only the timer and the fan at the time.  The microwave itself was not on at the time.
There were flames inside the right back corner of the unit.  Fortunately, I was home at the time. Smelled the smoke and was able to extinguish the fire.

This is the SECOND time the unit caught fire.  The last time the unit was off and somehow turned itself on.

I researched this issue on the internet and saw that it is a common problem.

I am surprised that these units have not been recalled.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was extinguished without injury, and this is a recurring issue indicating a common problem.

KitchenAid refrigerator compressor switch overheated, emitted smoke, and nearly caught on fire.

incident_description: I own a microwave combo from Emerson MWG9111SL.. It was manufactured in April 2007.. It overheats and then shuts off for twenty minutes at a time or more.. there is NO electricity running on the unit when it does this.. justification: The trash compactors started smoking, indicating a potential safety issue, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The product (Safety First Clear View Stove Knob Covers 48409) is designed to cover the knobs on your stove to prevent toddlers and young children from turning on the stove and starting a fire. Our son is 15 months old, and he has figured out that if he tugs on the cover hard enough he can open it, or pull it off entirely.  He likes to then turn the knobs on the stove, which in our case is gas, so it presents more safety concerns than just the possibility of starting a fire. The unsafe knobs have actually created more interest from him, rather than deterring him.
justification: The child can remove the covers and turn the gas knobs, posing a fire or gas leak hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I purchased 7 Nuby Easy Grip Sippy Cups at Walmart about 3 weeks ago. So far 3 have broken, and the cracks go from the bottom of the cup to the top.
They are packaged stating that they are for 6 months and up, So I would think they would be able to withstand being dropped and thrown, be it while standing or from the high chair. My son is 19 months old. The first one broke because it slipped out of his hand in the kitchen right after I handed it to him (full of milk). It cracked and spilled all over the floor. The second one was dropped from his high chair and again cracked and spilled. The last one dropped in the sink while cleaning it and it cracked and cut me.
These are plastic cups that are marketed to babies, I don't see how they are breaking so easy, and injuring people.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut injury from a broken cup, and the description indicates multiple instances of breakage.

incident_description: My Cuisinart DCC 1200 started smoking and produced an acrid smell. I  unplugged unit and let it cool. Seems like the unit could start a fire, I am wary of replacing it without a fix from the manufacturer.

incident_description: I purchased a Waring Pro electric waffle iron Model WMK300 about 5 years ago. I have used it many times. Today, my daughter and I were making waffles, the first waffle mix was placed in the waffle maker and turned. When the ready light signaled for a cooked waffle, my daughter turned the handle and the rear of the waffle iron collapsed, failed and fell, being held by only the electric wires causing a short, several sparks until I quickly unplugged the unit. It appears as though the plastic just failed.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure causing sparks but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: I came into the kitchen to see smoke rolling out of my dishwasher.  I turned it off as quickly as I could.
