This is a manufacturing defect which Sears says is not covered by warranty and they will not repair it.

We cut the breaker but every time we turn the breaker back on the broiler comes on. I don't have my model number handy but it is a smooth top, ultra bake, self-cleaning, super capacity. If we did not catch this it would have created a fire. Please issue a recall!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning broiler that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I turned on my oven to pre-heat it and in few minutes I heard a strange sound and looked inside my oven.  There was a fire in my oven.  The heating element burnt through.  What if I hadn't been close by and heard and/or saw this?  The company has sent me to a local repair unit and has taken no responsibility for the fire hazard.

He found that the fire started in the assy harness connector.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have caused serious harm, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Shaft inside microwave oven that is used to rotate the food melted in two.  No fire but there seems to be a fire potential.  Manufacturer has been contacted but does not appear to have any sense of urgency in this matter.
justification: The incident involves a melted shaft with no fire or injury, but there is potential for fire, indicating a moderate likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she started her dishwasher at 8.30am on the ÃÂnormal/heated dryÃÂ cycle. The consumer stated that the dishwasher normal cycle runs for approximately an hour and a half. She stated that approximately at 4pm the consumer returned to remove the dishes and she noticed that her counter top above the dishwasher was extremely hot. When she opened the dishwasher to remove the dishes she burnt the pointer finger on her right hand. The consumer stated that she had plastic dishes and a cutting board that melted due to the extreme heat.

She stated that later that evening nothing was inside the dishwasher, but smoke was being emitted from the dishwasher (not specific of the location). The consumer also stated that the counter top above the dishwasher had become extremely hot again. 

The consumer stated that she opened the door to insure that it was off. The consumer stated that she did not see any visible damages on the dishwasher. She stated that she did not see any visible damages on her counter top, but she is having someone come to service it. 

The consumer stated that she spoke to the manufacturer and they assisted her by scheduling a service appointment for a technician to come out on 05/18/2012 for the price of $89.00. Also the representative informed her that they would provide her with a $100 voucher for the purchase of a new GE dishwasher. The consumer was unsure if she would be buying a new dishwasher. 

The consumer feels that this product should be investigated due to the fire hazard it poses.
justification: The consumer suffered a burn injury and there was property damage (melted dishes), but the incident appears isolated with no widespread pattern indicated.

incident_description: I have been using my Cuisinart DCC-1200 Series Brew Central coffeemaker for approximately 2 months.  Up until today I used the gold tone filter that came with the coffeemaker.  Today I used one of the paper filters that came with the coffeemaker.  When I was cleaning out the machine tonight, I found that the paper filter had scorch marks on it, that were not on it when I put it in the machine this morning. i was concerned this could have lead to a fire.  I searched this site and found more reports of fires starting with this model.
justification: The scorch marks on the filter indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was standing in my kitchen when I heard a kind of popping noise and began to smell smoke like an electrical fire.  I called my husband and we began to unplug and check outlets and appliances in the kitchen.  We finally noticed smoke coming from the dishwasher.  I had washed a load of dishes about an hour earlier, but it was not on at the time.  Each time we closed the door, the smoke smell got stronger and more smoke continued to come out of the vent.  My husband turned off the breaker for the dishwasher and then took the control panel off.  One of the wires had caught fire and was burning the plastic around it.  I did a search and found that there is a recall on some Kenmore dishwashers for this problem; however, my model number is not included.  I called Sears and they are sending out a technician to look at it tomorrow afternoon.
justification: Electrical fire incident with no injury, but potential for harm if not addressed.

incident_description: When I went to unload my dishwasher which had just finished a normal wash cycle I noticed rinse water still in the pan and that power was completely off. After checking the breakers (which had not tripped) I unplugged the unit and notice the Ching Cheng power cord was burnt on the end. This was not due to the receptacle and is some type of failure with the unit. I am concerned this could have started a fire due to defective materials and/or workmanship.
justification: The incident involved a burnt power cord which could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: Crofton Classic  milkshake maker. Item # 6136-12 Followed manufacturers instructions. . According to owners manual the spindle is permanently mounted. At some point durring usage the spindle fell off.  More of a concern was that the kitchen GFCI tripped when I used the product. The GFCI tripped twice, only when product was in use. I have discontinued use.
justification: The spindle fell off and the GFCI tripped, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: After starting the dishwasher, the smell of an electrical fire and apropriately colored smoke coming from the vents in the door.  The dishwasher was unable to "cancel" the cylce and power at the breaker box to interupt.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire smell and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I had set my oven to a temp of 350 and placed a meatloaf in the oven to bake. About 20 minutes in I started to smell smoke and heard the food sizzling. When I opened the oven door I was assaulted with smoke and could feel the broiler element heating, even though it was set to bake not broil. Both elements were heating. I immediately shut the oven off for a couple minutes (although it didn't shut the element off) then turned it back on. The oven beeped 3 times then read an error message on the screen. I was forced to physically shut the breaker off to the range to get the elements to shut off. From what I have researched on the Internet, there have been several of this model that present this same safety concern.

incident_description: Had turned the oven about 5 minutes previously  to preheat to 375*.  At the stove cooking when I heard electrical humming, then saw black smoke, followed by flames from the rear of the control console.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the oven, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have a kenmore dishwasher model # 665.16939. On June 3rd 2012, we smelled something burning with the dishwasher. The controller board was charred as well as the ribon connecting to the contoller board, the plastic connectors were also burnt and charred. If I had not been home, the dishwasher would of created a fire.
justification: The dishwasher was charred and could have created a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We own a Kenmore model 665.92012 smoothtop electric range/oven unit. On Friday, June 1, 2012, we used the oven to bake bread.  The oven heated to a temperature well above the temperature to which it was set, causing the bread to burn, the oven to fill with smoke, and smoke to begin to fill the kitchen.  Turning off the oven did not turn off the heating element.  Removing the bread ended the immediate smoke problem, but the oven would not turn off until unplugged from the wall.  Upon plugging in again, the heating elements turned on again despite the control showing no oven setting.  After a second unplug (where the oven remained unplugged for approximately 2 hours), plugging the oven back in again resulted in the heating element turning on.  There is no way to disable the heating elements via the controls; only unplugging the oven accomplishes this.

This problem was preceded by a more minor problem; if the problems are related it is possible that the minor problem may be a warning sign for the more major (safety) problem. For the last several weeks, the (electronic) controls for the oven were functioning abnormally.  To adjust oven temperature on this model when it is working, you must press the temperature up/down buttons repeatedly from the default ("bake") setting of 350 degrees.  In recent weeks, these button presses did not register properly and sometimes were ignored.  Other times, a single button press led to repeated changes in temperature setting.  We suspect this is the result of a defective computer control.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that overheated and produced smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The plastic gasket in the bottom of my Baby Bullet detached and got chopped up and pureed in the baby food.  I ended up feeding the baby 4 jars of it before I noticed a big plastic piece in it and went to investigate.  Sure enough the plastic gasket was all caught up around the blade and pieces were missing which were chopped up in the food I fed him.  I've been using the product for about 2 months with no issues.  I read all instructions before use and have been following all of the correct cleaning guidelines.  I did not notice that the gasket was loose before using it.  When I looked online it seems hundreds of people have had this happen to them as well.  This is a HUGE safety issue and I'm really upset that my baby has been eating plastic pieces.  I'm just lucky he didn't choke on anything and hopefully this plastic will all pass through with no issues.
justification: The baby ingested plastic pieces, which constitutes an injury, and the issue is reported by hundreds of users, indicating it is likely to occur.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidaire stove Model FEC30S6AS. The front burner turns on by itself, and then will not turn off; it has to be turned off at the breaker. In addition, the stove burner when turned on will heat up to high heat instantly. It is a fire hazard.

I have contacted a Frigidaire servicer, but Frigidaire has sent the wrong part to them four times. I have called Frigidaire, but they refuse to be of assistance to me. They are, however, willing to sell me a new stove; they are not willing to replace or repair my stove. I have been working with them now for over eight months and no resolve has been found.

Similar models with similar problems have been recalled. I'm guessing because this is an entry level appliance Fridigaire is not willing to recall it. However, it is faulty, presents a hazard, and should be recalled.
justification: The stove's malfunction presents a clear fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I was in the kitchen while my dishwasher was running. I heard a loud zapping noise, and smoke started to come out of my dishwasher. I opened it up to discover smoke coming from the dishwasher door. I immediately got our fire extinguisher. Then, I closed the door and turned the dishwasher back on for a second. The zapping noise continued and more smoke came out. I immediately turned off the dishwasher. The smoke dissipated slowly.

My husband disconnected the dishwasher from the electrical circuit and opened up the dishwasher front panel. The circuit board at the top of the door was burned. 

I am so thankful I was standing right there when it happened. My dad's house burned down as a result of the Maytag rinse-aid defect. I cannot believe that the same thing almost happened to me.

The make/model is:
Frigidaire Electrolux PLDB999C0. Purchased May 2002.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burned circuit board but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: SKYBAR WINE OPENER: the encase needle part broke off from the stainless steel shaft, leaving a sharp edge. The could cut someone who was pumping it. Too expensive to break this way.
justification: The sharp edge of the broken needle could cut someone, but there is no injury reported.

incident_description: I woke up at 1:45 a.m. and smelled something burning hot I walked downstairs to kitchen and noticed all the green lights were on, on the dishwasher, which was strange, because I turned it on before bed at 9p.m.  It should have been off by now. I came closer and noticed it was very very hot. I opened it up and some of my dishes were broken and extremely hot.  I tried to get lights to turn off and they will not. I wanted to cool it down, I took the racks with dishes out and still it was very hot. I then tried to pull it out and unplug it.  When I opened the dishwasher door and took out the rack, I burned my fingers cause the dishes were so hot.  This dishwasher had a recall on it before, and now here we go with another issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burned fingers) and the dishwasher had a previous recall, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
Product - KitchenAid double built-in electric wall oven. Model KEBS207SS; Serial # D14428728.
Purchased from Charlotte Appliance, Lake Ave. Rochester, NY. Installed 11/11/2011.
The first time we tried to use the self-cleaning feature was on Mother's Day 2012 (05/13/2012). We followed the instructions to the letter including removing loose burned food particles on the bottom of the oven. Being only 6 months old, the oven was only lightly soiled. 
We set the upper oven on a light cleaning cycle. Soon after it began it's cool-down cycle, but while still in locked mode, the inner glass exploded with a loud bang, sending a shower of hot glass onto the kitchen floor through a gap in the bottom of the door. 

We attempted to clean up the mess, but as we tried to remove the glass trapped in the space between the upper and lower doors, more glass kept pushing out from the gap in the upper door. Some of this found it's way into the door of the bottom oven between it's inner/outer glass panels. When the oven cooled down, we had to seal the off the space between the two doors with duct tape to prevent more glass from spilling onto the floor and into lower oven. 

The next day, May 14th, I phoned Charlotte Appliance who referred me to their local authorized warranty service provider, County Wide Appliance. County Wide ordered the part and it has been on backorder since that time. 

At this point we've been without the use of either oven for three weeks, and still lack a confirmed date for repair.  County Wide did call Whirlpool (KitchenAid parent company) on Friday, 06/01/2012, and was told they would try to expedite a part from the manufacturing floor. 
Having lived with several self-cleaning ovens since the late 1960's when the technology was new, I was appalled that this type of dangerous failure would occur on a presumably high-end appliance.  After a short web search I learned that other people have had a similar experience with the very same model oven, and in New York State there is even a class action lawsuit against Whirlpool/Kitchenaid.

I wrote to Consumer Report about this and they recommended I write to you as well. 

Thank you for your consideration of this serious situation.

Regards,

[redacted]
justification: The incident involved an oven glass explosion causing a mess and potential hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My electric kitchen aid oven, model KESI901PBS02, serial XT2701858 WOULD NOT TURN OFF!! After making a pizza, the "off" button would not turn off the oven, we had to turn off the circuit to the oven, and we have not used the oven since then, as it's a fire hazard.  Upon calling whirlpool, they want me to  pay for the part to repair my oven, when I think a safety recall needs to be issued.
justification: The oven failed to turn off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
KitchenAid Microwave/Hood combination  model # KHMS155LSS-3, serial # TRS4039513 purchased installed October 2005 when the building (new structure) was built.  

I noticed that several times, the microwave seemed to have gone on by itself, because I noticed several time that it said: "END" on the display panel. On two occasions I noticed it go on and it usually lasted anywhere from 30 secs to a minute and sometimes longer.  When I noticed this, I immediately unplugged it.  I called the building manager who told me that over 20 units have reported the same problem.  When the first two or three were reported to KitchenAid they sent a replacement control panel which seems to go awry after a while and charged the owners some $300.  When it got more prevalent, the building manager called KitchenAid and spoke to a supervisor who agreed to refund the money and from then on, they have been replacing the control panel for free.  

I think this could be a real fire hazard especially for unit owners who go on vacation and do not unplug the units.  It certainly had a lot to do with an increase of my electrical bill last month. KitchenAid has not offered any explanation for this problem.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths have been reported. The issue is widespread among units, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased two tempered class counter tops from DBROTH through Amazon.  I received the product, and was very happy.  However, yesterday morning one of the counter tops completely shattered sending glass throughout my kitchen.  I was very fortunate that myself, or my family were not in the room at the time.  The counter top just shattered, for no reason or cause.

My concern is that someone could be seriously injured by this product.  This product is very unsafe and dangerous.

Thank you for your time and attention in this matter.
justification: The counter top shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it was an isolated event with no clear cause.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the dishwasher was in the wash cycle.  He says during that time the control board caught on fire.  There was a lot of smoke and damage to the unit.  He says that the control panel and the panel cover were burned. 

 The wire harness was also blackened and burned.  The consumer says the unit was on for about 30 minutes prior to the incident occurring.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him that the unit is not part of the recall.  The model and serial number are both a match to being part of Release # 05-123.
justification: The dishwasher's control board caught fire, causing smoke and damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed the base of the tub inside  of the dishwasher has  a dime size hole in it. The consumer also noticed that there are scorch marks around the hole.

The consumer noticed the hole  n 4/16/2012 but states that she noticed some scorch markings in the area for almost a year.

The firm was contacted on 4/16/2012 and the consumer was advised to have a service technician  come out . The consumer has not scheduled a service call and is unsure at this point how she will handle the matter. 

The consumer has discontinued the use of the dishwasher in fear that it poses as a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to scorch marks and a hole in the dishwasher, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says their are sharp, large and small plastic pieces coming out of the ice maker.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they told her it is out of warranty.  They would only offer a service call.  She says that she looked in her glass and saw a tiny piece of plastic.  Her husband had a large plastic piece in her glass.
justification: The incident involves plastic pieces in the ice maker, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: My Kenmore model # 911.95582990 oven caught on fire.  I had turned the oven on and about 5 minutes later, I heard a loud pop and then a flash of light went through the kitchen.  I looked in the oven and it was on fire.  I hesitated to use a fire extinguisher because I could see that it was an electrical fire.  I called the fire department.  They turned off all power to the oven.  Eventually, the fire went out.  The lower heating element split in half.  I have been on the phone for the last two days and have been repeatedly told that this model is not under any recall; however, I have done some internet research and see that I am not alone.  This same incident has happened many times in the past.  I would love to know how many ovens in my model # have caught on fire. And exactly how many incidents does it take in order for a recall to happen?   Lucky for me, no person or property was injured.  We're just without any home-cooked meals for awhile.
justification: The fire caused no injury, but it was a serious incident that required fire department intervention.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Electric Range freestanding model 665.92029101
The broiler element will not turn off.  NONE of the controls on the stove will turn it off!
Even after I unplug it or turn the breaker off, when it is plugged back in the broiler element 
is still on.
If we were not watching it close, IT COULD HAVE BURNED THE HOUSE DOWN!!!
It will just get hotter and hotter and hotter like a kiln element.
There need to be a recall before someone gets hurt.
justification: The broiler element malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller purchased refrigerator in 2008, had no problems with it until around March 27, 2012 when it dispelled a screw when callers wife was putting ice in glass.
Refrigerator has double doors, freezer on bottom and ice maker in door.

Caller contacted the firm's recall hotline, obtained repair part and attached.

He at first thought this to be an isolated occurrence.

Now the incident is happening again and he would like it reported for fear that someone may not notice this problem and choke on the screw.

 
He would like his refrigerator repaired to avoid this happening again but moreover would like the public to be aware of the potential issue.
justification: The incident involves a screw being dispelled by the refrigerator, posing a potential choking hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: On 5/22/12, my less than 2 year old Sharp microwave caught fire while heating my children's lunch. The microwave made a terribly loud buzzing sound and it looked like lightning bolts coming out of the side panel where the heating element is. I noticed a flame coming through this panel and smoke so I stopped it and unplugged it. The smoke filled the kitchen. There is burn damage on this panel as well as the metal unit itself. I immediately phoned Sharp and received a case number  of [REDACTED]. They told me my case needed to be reviewed as my microwave is out of warranty. Meanwhile, it is less than 2 years old and almost caught my house on fire.
justification: The microwave caught fire and caused smoke damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have a Frgidaire ghlass top cookstove model number FEF368CC. While cooking a pizza in the oven at 400 degrees I turned on the left front dual burner to warm up a pot of food when I heard the glass pop really loud. The glass cracked from the center of the stove around the left front burner all the way to the other side of the stove. I have had problems with a black liquid oozing out from under the stove every time I use it. The burnes seem to get extremely hot and stay hot enough to burn you up to 30 minutes after they are turned off. I accidently burt the side of my hand from this.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from the stove's excessive heat, and the recurring issues with the stove suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Purchased Model SBD0700N00II, GE MONOGRAM DISHWASHSER, IN JAN 2008 FROM HH GREGG.  IT GOT STUCK ON HEAT CYCLE .  ULTIMATELY HAD TO CUT THE POWER SOURCE.  MELTED PORTIONS OF THE INTERIOR OF THE DISHWASHER AND SOME OF ITS CONTENTS.  MODEL NO IS NOT SHOWN AS A RECALL BUT IS CLOSE.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, causing damage to the appliance and its contents, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The drive cup for our built in ice maker in our GE Profile refrigerator (model PSS26MSWC) has broken apart several times causing plastic pieces to be mixed in with the ice.  On several occasions the plastic has ended up in our drinks and in turn in our mouth.  The cup has been replaced several times and continues to break after normal use.  It is made of a white plastic so it is undetectable once mixed in with the ice.  I am very concerned that someone will eventually swallow one of these sometimes sharp pieces of plastic.  A quick search of the internet will reveal this to be a common problem.  GE should recall this part and design something that will stand up to the cold temps of a freezer.  To truly be safe we will need to stop using the ice dispenser.
justification: Plastic pieces from the broken ice maker cup have been ingested, posing a risk of injury due to sharp edges, though no injuries are reported yet.

incident_description: My Cuisinart 12-cup Programmable Coffee Maker - Model #DCC-1100BK, is overheating and has slightly melted my countertop.  The machine appears to intermittently have an electrical short (problems turning on or brewing) and only intermittently becomes too hot to the touch.  I contacted Cuisinart about this maker.  The has me ship the product to them.  After their research, I received a letter stating they did not find any problems with the maker after 3 brew cycles, and they shipped it back to me stating it was safe.  I continued to complain to them that it was not working properly.  They sent a new maker, same model.  I have looked at the reviews on Bed, Bath, & Beyond's website regarding this product.  It appears there are several other customers who have had a similar complaint, but also state fire and smoke.  I wanted to file this report to let you know there is a product that could potentially catch a house on fire and harm families.
justification: The coffee maker is overheating and has caused minor property damage (melted countertop), but no injuries or deaths are reported. Multiple similar complaints suggest a recurring issue.

incident_description:
12 cup drip coffee maker Cuisinart DCC-1200 had just finished brewing a pot. The "ready" signal sounded. I poured one cup. Then I heard a loud gurgling sound not unlike the tail end of a brew cycle but it kept on going. I went into the kitchen to investigate and the base of the unit was emitting, not steam, but the acrid smoke of electrical parts on fire. A cursory search of the Internet reveals this was hardly unique.

If I had not been physically present to hear the problem, my house could well be gone. I unplugged just in time yet the warmer plate stayed very hot to the touch for over 5 minutes.

I've read the manufacturer's rebuttal to one similar report in which they say units returned for electrical fire have shown no problems whatsoever. I know what I heard, saw and smelled, and that kind of corporate response must not be allowed to stand. There needs to be an immediate recall.
justification: The incident involved a coffee maker emitting smoke and posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description:
Heating elements switched to highest heat automatically; Food caught fire

Cause: spring driven timer recoils past the off position when time runs out and moves to the broil position which allowed both top and bottom heating elements to burn indefinitely at highest setting. 

Oven in service for one month.
justification: Food caught fire due to a malfunction, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: After frying bacon my husband unpluged the skillet and removed the detachable cord, he then picked up the skillet full of hot grease to pour it out so he could wash it and the handle broke off in his hand and he dropped the skillet causing the legs to break and the skillet to bend and breaking the other handle. I purchased Four of these skillets at the after Thanksgiving (BLACK FRIDAY) sale at two different Dollar Generals Garners Ferry Road Hopkins S. C. and Eastover S.C. I gave one to each of my three daughters for Christmas and kept one for myself. My daughters have experienced the bottoms rusting out and one of them caught fire and she hadn't even put anything in it yet all she did was plug it up and turn it on it started sparking and the cord caught fire. Her husband threw it away. I reported this incident to someone in the Corporate offices at Dollar General but haven't heard anything in response to my complaint. The brand is Continental Electric Platinum Series 12 inch Electric Skillet with cool touch handles, made exclusivly for Dollar General Corporation. They originally sold for $30.00 but were $15.00 each during this sale. I want a refund for all four skillets.
justification: The incident involved a skillet handle breaking, causing potential injury from hot grease, and another skillet catching fire, posing a clear safety hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express her concerns about that her medium 13X9 sized, clear, glass baking pan as it ÃÂexplodedÃÂ as the consumer was attempting to dry the dish by hand. The consumer stated that she was cooking with the dish the day prior before she attempted to wash and dry it. The day prior, the consumer placed the dish in her oven for 20 minutes, while the oven was set to 350 degrees. 

The consumer stated that she could not hear sign of cracking prior to the incident. The damaged cookware left shards of the glass in the consumerÃÂs sink. 
Luckily, no one was injured .The consumer has yet to call the retailer or the firm. The consumer kept the parts of the pan in case he needs further analysis. 

The consumer and her husband found multiple reports on similar incidents happening. The consumer sustained no further property damage. The consumer felt it was imperative to report this issue to the CPSC. The consumer stated that the dish came in a package of one dish. The product has no signs of damage prior to the incident.
justification: The glass baking pan exploded but no one was injured, and there are multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: I purchased Wolfgang Puck cookware from home shopping network approximately 4 years ago.  They worked fine until recently.  4 of the pots and pans have come apart while cooking within the last 2 months.  The bottom comes off, and you are left with the bottom of the pan on your stove, with liquid aluminum in it which is needless to say, very hot.  I called home shopping network, who gave me Wolfgang Puck company's phone number.  I spoke with the company representative who stated "this happens, you should only cook on low heat".  This was the Bistro set I purchased which have a separate bottom attached that has an aluminum disc in it.  To this date I have had no resolution with the Wolfgang Puck company or HSN regarding the safety issue this poses.
justification: The incident involves pots and pans coming apart while cooking, posing a burn risk, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description: have a frigidaire gas range with double ovens that has been worked on over 3 times and still blows convection oven door open while preheating. i have burnt my eyebrows and lashes by opening door while in use and a fire ball coming out of oven. have contacted frigidaire and was only told to get serviced again and they tried to sell me an extended service plan. oven is 11 months old and first service call was within 2 months.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burnt eyebrows and lashes) and the problem persists despite multiple service attempts, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Frigidaire refrigerator model#FRS6R4EW7 the compressor starter switch part#241524605 shorted out and caught on fire. There were no exposed wires. The switch shorted out internally and melted from the inside out catching the foam insulation under the compressor on fire. My wife heard the spark and smelled the burning plastic. I returned home and removed the back cover and the compressor came on and within seconds the sparks ignited and I saw flames. I immediately unplugged the unit and pulled the part. On the under side of the starter there is a large portion of melted plastic gone. Had my wife not been home there is no doubt in my mind my house would have burned down and I would have lost everything I own.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a shorted compressor starter switch, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
April 8th, 2012 caller's husband placed the oven at self cleaning around 3:15pm.
Caller had taken their two children across the street to an Easter Egg Hunt.

When caller returned around 4:00 she and the girls remained outside for a short while until their relatives began arriving with their children.
 
In all the commotion and in a very few moments the callers 14 month old daughter began screaming.
The caller's mother in law, brother & sister in law ran to the baby, saw that appeared that her hand was literally stuck to the oven of the stove. 

When they arrived at the stove, they grabbed her, picked her up, tried to put water over her hand and then aloe thinking it wasn't as serious as it appeared to be.

Within ten minutes the baby's hand was covered with blisters.

Callers decided to take her to the Urgent Care Unit but they were turned away and referred to the hospital emergency room due to the severity of the burn.

The emergency room diagnosed the baby with first and second degree burns, submerged her hands into ice water for approximately thirty minutes.

Then put burn cream named in notes on her hand and wrapped her hand in gauze instructing that the wrap be changed a couple of times a day and followup with pediatrician in two days.
Caller in the beginning was having to change the gauze about ten times a day due to the baby tearing them apart but now it has settled a bit.

Caller contacted for repair and tech came out Thursday, April12th, 2012 stated that self cleaning mode became excessively hot and to watch it because the manufacturer could turn it around on them.  She asked him to leave and rescheduled for another tech.

April 16th, 2012 the second tech  arrived, after asking the caller to turn the self cleaning mode on so that it would be running the same three hours it ran when the baby was burned.
He tested the oven outer layer during the self cleaning mode with a thermometer at the area where the baby had placed her hand and said that the temperature was at 198 degrees.

The baby has been in extreme pain, the blisters began breaking open within a few days.
At the follow up with the doctor on April 17th, 2012 the doctor cut the blisters off.

Caller is reporting this oven as a severe safety hazard due to the extent her daughter was burned.

She believes that this product or at least the door needs to be recalled.
justification: The baby suffered first and second degree burns, requiring medical treatment and follow-up care, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I turned the oven on to preheat and before it preheated the glass on the oven door blowed into a million pieces. I was getting something out of the cabinet beside of the oven and glass shattered all over my face and in my hair.
justification: Glass shattered on the person's face and hair, indicating physical injury.

incident_description: Glass shattered (for the SECOND TIME!) all over my boyfriend's feet and legs, all over the  kitchen. All he did was open the door normally to get dinner out of it and the glass exploded into a million tiny little pieces everywhere. This happened once before about two years ago not long after I bought it, same scenario, only it was covered under it's 1 year warranty. Now it's not. I have read hundreds of consumer reports all over the internet of people complaining of KENMORE RANGES AND TOASTER OVENS FRONT DOOR GLASS BREAKING/EXPLODING. ( http://www.selectsmart.com/DISCUSS/read.php?34,601635,page=1) If you copy and paste this link, it will take you to SIX PAGES of people complaining of the SAME EXACT INCIDENCE.
justification: Glass shattered and caused potential injury risk, but no actual injury reported in this instance. The incident has occurred multiple times based on consumer reports.

incident_description:
Caller purchased electric stovetop in 2005 and has had various issues with the codes over the years.
Callers did not consider them a safety issue and would reset the cooktop and continue on.
They had purchased a microwave & a dishwasher at the same time and had technicians come out who were unable to repair the products and in one instance the tech wanted to paint the inside of the microwave to keep the glass tray from coming off and he lost all trust in their techs.

He noticed on April 27th, 2012 while cooking dinner with family in kitchen that the left front burner had come on by itself with temperature going immediatley to high with the burner became quite hot, could not be turned off or turned down.
He disconnected the circuit breaker and has been unable to use.

Caller spoke with [REDACTED] at the manufacturers regarding electric stovetop May 1.2012.
There have been no injuries.

Caller is reporting as a severe burn or fire hazard.
Caller would like repair at manufacturer expense.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injuries occurred, and the issue was mitigated by disconnecting the circuit breaker.

incident_description:
The consumer has a double wall oven and placed the bottom oven on the self cleaning option. Approximately an hour and half into the cycle the consumer noticed a popping sound.

The consumer then noticed that the inside layer of glass (oven door glass has two layers) had  exploded into tiny pieces onto the kitchen.

The firm was contacted immediately after the incident occurred. The consumer has a technician scheduled to come out to the home on 4/5/2012.

The consumer states that the same incident occurred in 11/2011 with the top oven. The consumer had the oven glass replaced in 11/2011.

The consumer noticed a blog site where other concerns had experienced the same incident with similar model  numbers.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded oven glass) but no injury, and similar incidents have occurred before with the same model.

incident_description: Several years ago I purchased a Belgique silicone frypan with stainless handle with a rubber grip.  I have used this for years as my favorite pan.  Nothing sticks and the heat is very even.  All of a sudden last week, I almost got a severe burn on my hand as I gripped the handle.  This had never happened before so I was not prepared for such a hot handle.  It even gets too hot now through a hotpad.  How can that happen so suddenly when I've used it for years without a problem?  I still use the pan, but have to keep a heavy hot pad over the handle at all times so I don't forget that it gets so hot  IT WILL BURN YOUR HAND IF YOU DON'T LET GO!  Is there some way to get a replacement as I'm afraid someone will really get hurt.
justification: The incident caused a severe burn risk, but no actual injury was reported, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
The consumer baked a cake in the glassware in the oven at 350 degrees for 45 minutes. The range that was used was electric glass top range.  The consumer removed the glass dish on a wooden board  and within 15 minutes heard a loud explosion.
The glass dish exploded into large and small shards and fell into the floor.  Some of the cake had fallen out onto the floor as well.  
The consumer noticed that some of glass baking dish was still intact. Parts of some of the cake was still sitting in the glass tha  did not break. 
The consumer placed the glass baking dish, pieces of the cake and the broken pieces into a box and returned it to the retailer. She received a full refund and voiced her concerns with the retailer.

The consumer contacted the firm around 12/27/2011 and was offered a $50.00 rebate in which she has excepted.

The consumer has discontinued using the brand of glass baking wear in fear that it could cause an injury to herself.

The consumer also states that prior to her using the baking dish she read a article in Consumer Reports (Jan 2011 issue).  The report mentioned to place the hot dish on a wooden surface and not a lass or cool surface.


Purchase made a couple days before 12/25/2011.
justification: The glass dish exploded but no injury was reported, only property damage and consumer concern.

incident_description: I have two Munchkin Insulated Stainless Steel sippy cups (they are less than one month old).  As I was washing one of them (always hand washed, never dishwasher), the stainless steel liner came loose and then was able to be pulled out of the plastic outer shell.  Inside the plastic outer shell, in the bottom of the cup, was a loose screw.  This could have been a choking hazard if my 14 month old had been using the cup when it came apart.
justification: The incident involved a loose screw in a sippy cup, posing a potential choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I have the Jura Capresso model Impressa S7 espresso maker.  This model has a water reservoir which always contains water.  It is able to froth milk for cappucino, makes espresso, and supplies hot water for tea.  The hot water either comes out of a coffee spigot, a steam spigot, or a hot water spigot.  I was making espresso a few days ago, the unit first froths milk from a steam nozzle.  The steam did not shut off when it normally would.  It did shut off about 20 seconds after it normally would.  The coffee came out of the correct spigot after that.  The unit did something like this once before, at the time I called Capresso and I was told to wiggle a flap and clean it.  I was also told to change the fineness of the coffee grind setting.  I did this this time again and thought the problem was solved.  The next morning my wife was making espresso, the machine redirected all of the water through the frothing nozzle, no coffee came out.  The frothing nozzle alternated between boiled water and steam through the entire cycle.  I called Capresso and spoke to [redacted], I asked him if there was a recall on this unit. He said there isn't.  I explained what was happening. He told me I could send the unit in for repair.  I told him I had this unit reconditioned one year ago and don't want to do this on a yearly basis.  He told me to cycle the knobs on the unit from coffee to hot  water to steam and see if that will free a stuck valve.  In the process of doing this, the container I was using, filled up.  The unit stopped pouring water, I emptied the container and the steam nozzle started spraying steam suddenly.  I ran to put the container under the nozzle and scalded my finger.  There is no blister just a painful red spot, nothing to worry about but enough to think what if a family member was standing by the machine when it would start spraying steam.
justification: The incident resulted in a scalded finger with a painful red spot, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description: Our new Le Creuset stoneware casserole dish got a small crack in the side when I ran lukewarm water over it after taking it out of the oven (with the intent to let the remaining food in the dish soak). We let it on the counter overnight, and when I picked it up this evening to move it out of my way, the stoneware shattered into two large pieces. In the process, my finger was severely lacerated and required 5 stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration requiring medical attention (5 stitches), which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer and his wife stated that his electric stove has a simmer select switch that had being working properly. On March 24, 2012 his wife turn on the stove and turned on the simmer switch for approximately a minute and instantly heard a popping noise and the back of her stove emitted a bright light and sparks. The consumer smelled a wire burning odor and they immediately turn the knobs to turn off the stove.  In fear that it would catch on fire they unplugged the stove. 

When he looked behind the stove they saw demarcation marks on the wall. He opened the back of the stove and at a first look he did not notice any damages, until he looked at the control panel that links to the simmer switch. The plastic connection on the control panel that has four wire connection had heat damage and discoloration. Next to the plastic connection is the screw that connects that control panel to the stove, this had visible heat damage consisting with an electrical arc. In general you can see the heat discoloration on the control panel. 

03/25/2012- The consumers contact the retailer and they informed them that this product does not have a recall. incident_description:
The consumer says the oven was on for about 10 minutes.  Suddenly he heard and arching noise and the oven control panel caught fire.  Flames were shooting from the back of the range and against the wall. Smoke and flames were visible above the top of the stove.

incident_description: I have a KitchenAide dishwasher Model #KUDS03STSS#. It is 2 years old. After reading and hearing all the stories about dishwasher fires in Whirlpool made units, I called a local repair service and had them come out to checkout my dishwasher. The repairman had not heard anything nor seen any fires with Whirlpool made dishwashers nor had any other retailers and repairmen that I had talked to. He took off the front cover and was inspecting the machine. He said he had to go back to the office for something. He put the cover back on and told me to turn off the circuit breaker and not use the machine until he came back the next day. The next day he returned. He took the door cover off and showed me where he had found the wiring in the control box had started to melt and had stuck the plastic wall. He said he had spent time researching the problem and had found that many of these machines had gone on fire in the control box. He strongly recommended that we leave the power off and not use this machine. He also said he would not recommend replacing the control box because the problem has not been resolved and we would be in the same situation of a possible fire. Now I have a very expensive dishwasher that cannot be used. I consider myself lucky in that I caught the problem before it went on fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual fire or injury, and the repairman indicated that similar issues have occurred in other machines, suggesting a possible but not certain risk.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool Gold Gas oven/cooktop, model # GW395LEPSO1, that I put on self-cleaning mode. After an hour of being in this mode, the oven shut off, and the LED panel on the front went dark. The oven would not un-lock, even after 5 days. After replacing the thermostat in the past, this still happens from time to time. I am very concerned about potential fire hazards due to the product malfunction.

incident_description:

The sound was coffee boiling in the carafe sitting on the warming plate of the Cuisinart DCC-1200 (made in China). I felt that not much research could be obtained from the cord so I returned it to the KohlÃÂs store in Kokomo, Indiana. incident_description: I have a Whirlpool stove, Mod #RF364PXKV, Serial # RM0511345. Today the stove was very hot and I thought someone left it on. I pressed the off button. I went back to the stove a couple of hours later and it was burning hot.....even though it was off! I could not get the oven to shut down even though it appears off. My husband had to uplug it. No matter how  many times I press the off button, the oven will not stop heating up. I have 4 children and now have no safe stove to cook meals in. Really upset and scared.

incident_description:
Recently, I awoke to the smell of natural gas. Natural gas was coming from an unlit burner on my kitchen stove. I determined that one of the burner control knobs was just barely off the OFF position (about 1/8th turn toward LITE position) and unlit gas was pouring out of the burner.  Later testing determined that it took ADDITIONAL knob movement to reach the LITE position and ignitor initiation.  My wife and I took over three hours to safely ventilate the house, even though the oven had been releasing gas for little more than one hour. 

I contacted the manufacturer and their representative asserted that the stove was functioning as designed.  It is SUPPOSED to release gas even though the LITE position (and ignitor function) has not been reached by the control knob. When I explained that I thought this seemed unsafe and certainly was not the same operation as my previous gas stove, which did not release gas until the ignitor was functioning, she again told me that was the way it was designed to function.

I had apparently contacted the control knob with my clothing while leaning across the stove to wipe the rear control/indicator panel. Again, the control knob was less than 1/8 turn from the off position - midway between OFF and LITE - and this allowed gas to flow freely from the unlit burner.

Am I crazy, or shoudn't a stove's burner release gas only AFTER the LITE position is achieved and the ignitor begins to function?
justification: The incident was a gas leak, which could have led to an explosion or fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:

The burner switch shorted out spontaneously with a loud explosion followed by a white hot shower of sparks that shot up at least 12 inches above the cooktop.  Fortunately, there was nothing flammable in the vicinity.  Had there been a newspaper or dish towel near the cooktop, our new house would be cinders

The glassware was at room temperature when I placed it in the oven with three stuffed peppers for baking. I had coated the bottom of the glass with non-stick spray before placing the peppers on it. I was approaching the oven to take my dinner out when I heard a what sounded like a gunshot then the sound of shattered glass falling. I feel this should not happen especially since I was properly handling the glassware.

incident_description:
Kenmore 30" Free Standing Self-Clean Glass Top - Radiant Unit (Model #911-95459 590) has a bottom heating element in the oven that turns on even though the oven control knob is in the "OFF" position.  I have been awakened from sleep two separate nights, weeks apart, because I could smell "heat" and discovered that my oven was burning red hot even though the oven knob was in the "OFF" position.  We resolved the problem each time by turning the breaker off.  When we flipped the breaker back on, the oven would remain off as it should.

The last time we used the self-cleaning feature on the oven, about 4 months ago, the oven seemed to get hotter than it had the previous year when we used the self-cleaning feature.  This time, it also seemed to emit a strange chemical, or plastic burning smell.  And it seemed the oven stayed on way too long, over 4 hours, until I manually turned the cleaning feature off.  We have not used this feature again because of the horrible smell and the long cleaning duration and intense heat the oven put out.

This week we are dealing with the oven coming on and heating up beyond the temperature set and then not turning off when we turn the oven control knob to "OFF".  Again we have to remedy it by turning the breaker to the stove off.  However, when we turn the breaker back on, the oven's bottom heating element begins burning red hot, though the controls are "OFF" and no lights come on the stove top indicating that the oven is  ON.  This is a serious safety issue and we cannot leave the breaker to the stove in the ON position like normal.  As it is, the breaker to the stove is left off until we have to use the stovetop.  We use the stovetop to cook (meanwhile, the oven heating element comes on and burns hot the entire time though the oven knob is in the OFF position and no lights have come on to indicate the oven is even on) and as soon as we finish using the stovetop to cook, we flip the breaker to OFF again.  This is not normal operation for a stove and a serious safety issue.
justification: The oven heating element turns on unexpectedly, posing a fire hazard and emitting strange smells, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: I purchased an Emerson microwave model MWG9115SL Suffix D from walmart. I was heating a couple hot dogs in the microwave for the kids.  While fixing the buns I looked up and noticed molten metal falling on the paper plate they were cooking on. I immediately unplugged the unit and put the fire out that was burning the plate. I am glad I noticed the arching and was able to stop the self destruction of the microwave before it caught my house on fire or killed someone. I have kept this microwave unplugged and discontinued use. When making the decision on the purchase of this microwave we chose Emerson for the quality and features, it also happened to be the most expensive unit walmart had at the time(you get what you pay for). If the microwave is left unattended and goes unnoticed IT IS A FIRE HAZARD!!!

incident_description:
We are a 1st Class RV Resort with over 413 sites.  We recently replaced five trailers, that we rent out to guests.  They are Breckenridge Lifeline furnished trailers.  They came equipped with GE Self Cleaning Gas Ranges, Model JGBS180DET1BB, Propane.  The ranges have electronic ignitions.  Twice last week the burner control knobs were inadvertently, and unknowingly bumped, which caused the propane to leak and fill the trailer with propane gas.  Our staff was alerted when the Propane alarm in the trailer went off.  To their surprise, they found the trailer completely filled with propane.  The trailer could have exploded at any minute, causing human loss of life and property, not only to the trailer itself, but to nearby RV's and trailers as well.  The potential liability here is goes way beyond five ranges in what could be a disastrous domino effect throughout the park.  

Our propane distributor advised us that unless you turn the burner control knobs all the way up, until you hear a clicking sound, then back to the desired flame level, the units will leak into the trailer.  He also stated that there is a law suit in Wisconsin whereby a family was killed when their trailer exploded due to this exact condition.  I am unable to verify this.  Breckenridge trailers has referred me to GE, maker of the range.  GE does not have a warning or recall on this product at present.  The product literature does not advise the consumer to turn the control knobs all the way up, nor are their any stickers, labels on the ranges alluding to this problem.  

Any input or assistance you can provide on this matter will be greatly appreciated.  At present, our business is looking at having to replace all five of the ranges at our own expense, but one that will ensure the lives and property of our guests.
justification: The incident involved propane leaks that could have led to explosions, but no actual injuries or deaths occurred. The likelihood is high given the repeated incidents and potential for catastrophic outcomes.

incident_description:
On our Frigidaire range, you can have the burner knobs set to a position where gas will be coming out, but the ignitors will not be sparking.  After speaking with Frigidaire customer support, this is normal and how they make gas stoves.  This can also happen by accident.  My wife was reaching for something in the cabinet above the range, and she accidently pushed in the knob and turned it to that position.  She did that without knowing what happened.  There is nothing mechanically wrong with the stove or the ignitors, this, apparently is how Frigidaire makes gas stoves.  
     The first time this happened, we noticed a strange smell in our house.  It did not smell like the normal gas smell.  At the time, we had a cat and I thought that is was a urine smell from her.  After several hours of smelling and sniffing, I finally found the stove was leaking gas.
     This is extremely dangerous and I cannot believe that they are even allowed to make stuff like this.

Frigidaire gas range model number: FGGF3054KFK
                               serial number: VF10517997
justification: The incident involved gas leakage without ignition, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as it can happen accidentally.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that while the dishwasher was placed in wash cycle, approximately 10 mins later, she smelled an odor of electrical fire and noticed that there was smoke emitting from the top of the unit.  She attempted to power it off but it would not turn off, the circuit breaker was used to switch off the unit.

This incident burnt the circuit board and she had it replaced not being aware that there were problems with these dishwashers.

2/20/12 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that they were not aware that there were any problems with their dishwashers.

The consumer is concerned that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical fire odor but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was resolved by replacing the circuit board.

incident_description:
Front portion of the grill work on the top of my microwave oven fell without warning on my daughter's head. She was cooking at the time on the range below. The microvave is a GE Spacemaker (PVM1870SMSS). The entire top front portion of the microwave fell. The oven had been installed less than two yeras ago by the store where it was purchased.
The serial number of the oven is HT921289B.
justification: The grill fell on the daughter's head, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer brewed coffee at  6:50 am and left the home. She returned home approximately 8:15 and noticed a very strong electrical odor. She noticed the little coffee that was left  in the carafe boiling as the coffee maker made a hissing sound.  

The consumer states that the appliance stays on for two hours to keep the coffee warm and should shut off automatically. The consumer states that it does not appear that the appliance shut off and it began to overheat.

The consumer reached to unplug the machine from the rear and smoke began to bellow form the appliance. The consumer placed the carafe in the sink and placed the appliance outside on her patio so it could cool down. 

The retailer/firm was contacted on 4/19/2012 and the consumer was advised that there was no recall involving her model number. The consumer was advised that she could return it and receive a full refund.


The consumer has discontinued the use of the appliance  states that she will return it.  The consumer states that if she did not arrive home when she did there could have possibly been a fire in her home.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high given the appliance's failure to shut off automatically.

incident_description: A pork loin was placed in an Anchor ovenware clear glass 9x13 baking dish.  After 50 minutes in a 425 degree oven, it was finished cooking.  The meat thermometer read 160 degrees.  It was removed from the oven, placed on the stovetop and about 30 seconds later, it exploded into hundreds of pieces.   A piece has been saved, if it is needed for testing.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding dish) but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The consumer set the dishwasher on heavy/heavy duty scrub and within 2 minutes when she heard a loud clicking nose. She also noticed black smoke coming from out of the appliance door. 

She immediately pressed the stop button but the appliance continued to smoke. The home filled with a electric burning odor. The circuit breaker was pulled and the appliance stopped smoking. 
The appliance door was opened and there was still water inside of the machine. The smoke was coming from the control panel. 
The consumerÃÂs husband removed the control panel and noticed the wires on the circuit board has melted. 
On 2/27/2012 the firm was contacted a incident report was filed. The consumer was advised that the report would be forwarded to the safety division and she would receive a call within 48 hours. 

The appliance was replaced and the consumer placed the dishwasher that experienced the failure inside of the garage.
The consumer indicated that she was glad that she was home when the failure occurred. She stated that the incident could have been a potential fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was re-heating chicken on a paper plate. I turned around to do dishes and turned back and it looked like there was fire in my oven! I opened the door and it kept running, so I closed it and pushed the cancel button and it turned off. The 2 lights in the ceiling of the unit, possibly halogen (?) were bright orange and they were smoking. I thought my house would catch on fire! I got a stool and unplugged the unit in the cupboard above it and called the store where I purchased it. They set appt to come out to see it. I called Whirlpool and they said "tough...it is not under warranty". they can not help. The repairman is coming later today. LATER:: The repairman is here. He said the lights that were glowing and burned out should never have come on while reheating, which is what I was doing. we called whirlpool product safety and she talked to repairman and gave him a code to allow him to take it to his shop and see what caused it and to repair it if it can be. but she said I will have to pay for parts if he can repair it, and if he cant repair it, she will prorate a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and smoke, but no injury occurred, and the situation was controlled without further damage.

incident_description:
Have a GE over the stove microwave.  On 5/21/12 I put a cup of tea water in the microwave, turned it on, and went into my office in the next room.  The house started to fill with smoke and the smoke detectors went off.  When I went back in the kitchen the room was filled with smoke.  I was able to get to the unit and turn it off.

Charlestown Fire Company responded via 911.  They looked at the walls with the thermal imaging camera and found nothing there.  According to the firefighters the camera showed that all the heat was contained within the microwave.  While the firefighters were there we put another cup of water in the microwave and turned it on.  The room quickly filled with smoke.  

My contractor and electrician came yesterday and looked at all the wiring.  They assured me there was nothing wrong with the wiring.  This is clearly an issue with the microwave.

I searched the internet and found out I am not alone.  Others have had similar problems.  

I am a paramedic and member of the fire company.  For this reason I knew what to do and was able to minimize the damage.  It appears others may not have been so lucky.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Similar issues reported by others indicate a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Hello ÃÂ this is to report that our Bosch Dishwasher Model No. SHV46C03UC/14,  serial number FD8303 00943 has twice been repaired under our American Home Shield Warranty program due to loss of power from melting wires and wire nuts, and now for a third time, the unit has again shorted out with evidence of melted wires and a non-functioning main control board otherwise known as control module.  A burning smell is evident each time this has occurred. I contacted Bosch and learned while this unit was manufactured in the same time period as a long list of other Bosch dishwasher models under recall for fire hazards, our particular model is excluded from the recall even though it was manufactured at the same North Carolina plant in the same years as the units placed on recall (1999 -2005).  I explained to a Bosch supervisor the history of the unit, its date of manufacture in 2003, and the likelihood that it should also have been recalled for a potential fire hazard condition.  While this unit was installed new in 2004, the home was not lived in full-time until we purchased the home in 2008. The Bosch supervisor refused to assist us with the repair, saying it was out of warranty and that it was not recalled. I asked that my call and concern for the safety of our home and family be considered by Bosch, they provided an address to send a concern to their legal department.
justification: The incident involves repeated electrical malfunctions with evidence of melted wires and a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: Cuisenart CBC 00 coffee maker started making strange popping noises after brewing pot of coffee.  When I checked it the heating element was smoking, producing an acrid smell and the electrical controls were all off.  Luckily I was still home so I was able to unplug the unit and take it outside.  If it had been left unattended I'm quite sure the unit would have caught fire.
justification: The coffee maker exhibited dangerous behavior (smoking, potential fire risk) but was safely unplugged with no injury or damage.

incident_description:
Cuisinart DCC-1100 coffee maker burn-up.  
After brewing several cups of coffee, and then letting it strand for an hour or so, unit started to make a gurgling sound like it was trying to brew more.  Then noticed the smell of burnt plastic and finally noticed smoke coming out of the back.  Also noted that clock and LED lights were no longer working.  Unplugged unit before any further damage resulted.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burnt plastic but no injury or death, and such malfunctions are uncommon but not rare.

incident_description:
I bought a new 2-4 cup Farberware Percolator from Bed Bath and Beyond in Garden City, Long Island on Merchants Boulevard.(UPC code 3205102243). Other Numbers on the box PK 4000SS, A/W #1498-00, Date code 1117 08
1 000 W 120V 60HZ

Before using, I washed it as per instructions in the manual.  While washing the lid, I sliced my finger.  The bottom of the lid is so thin and knifelike that it sliced into my finger easily and caused a significant cut.  I brought the product back to the store and told them what happened and advised them of the danger present.  I believe this product should not be sold as it presents a danger every time the lid is handled.  The edge of the lid can easily cut through flesh.

I tried several times to contact the company.  The number for Farberware which you can get on line - 800-809-7166- refers you to another number 800-233-9054.  I tried this number several times.  One time, it put me on hold for an inordinate amount of time and I had to hang up.  The second time, it put me on hold and then a mesage in French came on which I did not understand and I did not continue to hold.  As yet, I have not notifed the company of their problem with the lid.

I feel this product is not safe to the consumer and should be addressed.  Although the cut on my finger healed, I could have been worse and lids present a danger.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant cut to the finger, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the lid's design poses a consistent cutting hazard during handling.

incident_description: I preheated my oven to 450 degrees to bake a pie crust. The oven was done preheating and as I was standing in the kitchen the glass just exploded. I did NOT hit the oven at all. My husband took pictures of the incident and went up to Sears and they said we must have hit it with something or banged the door which did not happen. The oven is only 3 years old.
justification: The oven glass exploded without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm. Such spontaneous breakage is unlikely but documented.

incident_description: TODAY WAS THE MOST TERRIFYING DAY OF MY LIFE. I WAS VACUUMING MY MASTER BEDROOM, WHEN I HEARD A LOUD SHRIEKING NOISE. I SHUT OFF THE VACUUM AND REALIZED THE SMOKE DETECTOR WAS GOING OFF. I RAN OUT OF MY BEDROOM AND, AS I CAME LEVEL WITH THE KITCHEN/HALL PASS THROUGH BAR, I SAW THAT MY KITCHEN WAS ON FIRE. I GRABBED MY FIRE EXTINGUISHER AND DOUSED THE FLAMES WHICH, THANKS BE TO GOD, QUICKLY PUT THE FIRE OUT. THE CULPRIT..... A G.E. OVER THE STOVE MICROWAVE OVEN. IT WAS NOT IN USE AND HAD NOT BEEN USED FOR AT LEAST 24 HOURS!! I COULD HAVE DIED, AS I WOULD USUALLY HAVE BEEN SLEEPING, I AM A NIGHT NURSE, THANKS BE TO GOD THAT I STAYED UP A LITTLE LONGER THAN USUAL. I HAVE LOOKED ON LINE AND SEE THAT THIS IS GETTING TO BE COMMON, SOMEONE IS GOING TO BE KILLED, YOU HAVE TO DO SOMETHING. NOW I AM LEFT FIGHTING WITH MY APARTMENT OWNERS ABOUT WHOSE INSURANCE SHOULD COVER THE EXTENSIVE DAMAGES, NOT TO MENTION THE FACT THAT I AM AFRAID TO SLEEP, I HAVE TO KEEP CHECKING THE KITCHEN, MY DAUGHTER LIVES IN THE APARTMENT ABOVE ME, SHE COULD HAVE DIED. THIS WAS 2 IN THE AFTERNOON, FEW PEOPLE ARE HOME AROUND HERE AT THAT TIME. I GUESS THE ONLY LUCKY PART IS THAT I WAS AWAKE AND KNEW HOW TO USE A FIRE EXTINGUISHER.
justification: The incident involved a kitchen fire that could have resulted in injury or death, but was quickly extinguished. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the microwave was not in use and such incidents, while concerning, are not frequent.

incident_description: My two-year-old lit our gas kitchen stove. I was only 2 feet away making lunch when he pushed the knob in and turned it. I don't know how long the gas was on until he turned it far enough for the pilot light to click and light it. There were paper food boxes near by that could have easily caught. It's so stupid that they still make stoves with knobs on the front where kids can turn them instead of having knobs by the back splash, seems like such a no-brainer. I think the "push then turn" feature is supposed to be a safety feature, but was easily defeated the first time I've ever seen him touch it. It is a GE brand, but I don't know much about it because we are renting this home and have no paperwork on it. I do know it's newer because this home was just built in 2011.
justification: The incident involved a child turning on the gas stove, which could have led to a fire but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
Undercounter dishwasher manufactured by Kenmore. Purchase about 8 years ago.
Model Number 587.15072201.
Serial number is TH33342044. 

Incident Date - 05/20/20112.
After finished cleaning the kitchen counter and the dishwasher front panel.
Control panel lights were flashing. Burning smell and smoke coming out from the exhaust.
Shut off breaker in power panel.
Proceed to open the cover, discovered one of the power terminals (the red one) connected to the control board was burnt with black smoke emitted from the area.

Took photos of the burnt control board and cover.

incident_description: I own a Sears Kenmore Elite three door refrigerator model number 795.775446500.  On two occasions I smelled plastic burning and discovered that the light fixture inside had over heated and melted. Upon further checking I determined that the door switches are failing to shut the light fixture off when the doors are closed.  The first time this happened I simply ordered the part, replaced the light fixture, and everything functioned properly.  This time I caught the problem before any damage occurred.  My safety concern is this product has a faulty design or part. Had I not detected the malfunction in its early state this overheating of the plastic light fixture by the failure of the bulbs to shut off when the doors are closed could have resulted in a residential fire, personal injury, and or death. I have researched this issue and have determined that this is problematic of this model and needs to be addressed in a recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning light fixture that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or damage occurred this time.

incident_description: In November 2004 I purchased a Kenmore Elite UltraWash Dishwasher from a Sears store in Mountain View, CA, model number 66516282400, serial number FR4301293.  On March 21, 2012, our housecleaners called to report smelling something burning.  After some minutes, they were able to determine that the foul-smelling fumes were coming from the Dishwasher.  They turned off the Dishwasher.  Upon returning home that evening, I turned on the Dishwasher to assess what was wrong.  The Dishwasher made an abnormal sound.  Dark grey, foul-smelling smoke then began to emanate from behind the right upper corner of the Dishwasher, just below the control panel.  I tried to turn off the Dishwasher by pressing the ÃÂCancelÃÂ button, but the Dishwasher continued to operate, and smoke continued to pour out of the Dishwasher, spilling into the kitchen.  I saw flames coming from inside the Dishwasher below the control panel in the area where the smoke was coming out.  I pressed other buttons on the Dishwasher in an unsuccessful attempt to turn it off.  I tried shutting and opening the door of the Dishwasher.  Rather than shut down, water started spraying out of the Dishwasher.  I closed the Dishwasher and prepared to extinguish the fire which I thought would spread outside of the Dishwasher.  Smoke was quickly pouring into the kitchen by this point.  My wife and I thought we and our children might be hurt. I ran into the garage and flipped the circuit breaker.  Doing so cut power to the Dishwasher, and the Dishwasher shut down.  Eventually visible smoke stopped coming out of the Dishwasher, and the fire appeared to die down.  The acrid, burning smell in the house was intense and remained so for over a week.  The previously white exterior of the upper right corner of the Dishwasher had been turned dark grey from smoke in an area closest to the fire.  The next day, I discovered a website called ÃÂkitchenaidfire.comÃÂ which detailed accounts of hundreds of incidents involving similar types of Whirlpool and Sears dishwashers combusting very similar to my incident.  Despite these incidents, no recall notice appears to have been issued.  I have contacted Sears and Whirlpool, and I worry that many hundreds of thousands of others will experience similar problems with more drastic consequences.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and flames, posing a significant risk of injury, but no actual injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On 5/6/2012 the consumer had used her stove approximately around 6p.m. that evening. After settling down that night she and her husband heard a loud explosion downstairs. When they went to inspect they saw that the glass door to the stove had shattered.  

The manufacturer was contacted 5/7/2012 and they advised her that her model was on a recall. After being transferred a few times they informed her that her model was not recalled and they would send out a technician to inspect the stove and its door.

There were no injuries from the incident.

The technician came out 5/8/2012 and informed her that they would offer a $60 gift card towards a new door or she could just replace the stove entirely at her expense.

The consumer feels that the product is a safety hazard because it exploded without any warning and may have caused bodily harm to any of her family members.
justification: The incident involved a stove door shattering without causing injuries, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but have been reported.

incident_description:

The smoke continued for 5 minutes after it was unplugged and taken outside.  It was used as directed on the box.  After the corn finished popping, the popper was turned off at the switch.  My daughter walked to the other side of the kitchen with the popcorn, and she turned around and the smoke was pouring out of the top and the bottom.  

It didn't come with any instructions or information inside the box.  The outside of the box has very limited instructions and no warnings regarding potential problems, etc.  Also, my 12 year-old daughter was the one using the popper.  It needs warnings regarding the use by children.  (Although, I would think that a 12 year old is competent in using a hot air popcorn popper.)
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing smoke but no injury, and the likelihood is possible given the lack of warnings and instructions.

incident_description:
Frigidaire electric smooth cooktop 
Model# FEC32S6A series
Serial# NF71723712

Most of this Frigidaire cooktop are using the same technology regardless of models, & there's a lot of people having the same or similar problem.   Thanks for looking into it.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning cooktop that could lead to a fire if not addressed, but no injury or death has occurred yet. The likelihood is high as similar issues are reported by many users.
