incident_description:
On Saturday, the day before Mother's Day, I was making a cup of coffee on my Mr. Coffee Keurig coffee maker.  I stood in front of the coffee maker, waiting for it and when it was almost done,  I started to turn for the milk.  I heard a loud pop and the hot wet coffee grounds shot out and burned my right check, neck and shoulder.

I quickly reached for a dishtowel and started rinsing off the coffee grounds in the sink.  That wasn't enough so I ran and jumped in the shower.

When I came back to investigate, I saw that the part of the coffee maker that holds the little coffee cup had fallen open and the cup's foil top had a large hole in it.  There was wet coffee grounds all over the counter and floor.

My husband came to see why I was yelling and wanted to take me to emergency.  I was busy with mother's day preparations and I didn't want to waste hours in Emergency, waiting to be seen.  On Sunday, when my family saw my burns, they were upset that I hadn't seeked professional help right away, so early Monday I did see a doctor.

I have blisters on my face and neck.  Some as large as a quarter.  My doctor says I will have scars.
justification: The incident resulted in burns with blisters and potential scarring, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence is unlikely (2) as such malfunctions are not common with coffee makers.

incident_description: I have purchased 4 Rubbermaid glass bowls with Easy Find lids recently, mostly due to their advertising with coupons in the Sunday paper. I froze some stuffed peppers in two of the smaller bowls, then I ran the bowls through the dishwasher after moving the food to plastic bags for longer storage in the freezer. I do not use the heated dry cycle in my dishwasher; instead, I air dry the dishes for a few hours before putting them away. These four bowls were stored in our kitchen cupboard nested inside one another and on top of their lids, with the two larger bowls sitting inside the smaller, shallower bowls. My husband and I were awakened a few days later, at approximately 3:30am on May 4, 2012, by the extremely loud sound of something that sounded like a rocket shooting through our apartment.  Our two cats jumped up and cowered in fright under the bed. After checking doors, windows, etc., we were completely perplexed as to what the noise could have been.....until later in the day when my husband discovered the completely shattered smaller bowl spread all over the inside of the cabinet he'd opened to get to our vitamins.  Given the loud noise the bowl made when it disintegrated and how far the small pieces of glass were in proximity to where the bowl originally was, we believe the bowl basically blew up. It scares us to death to think of what might have happened if this had happened when we were handling the bowl, and we firmly believe these bowls pose a real safety risk for anyone using them. Since we did nothing to mishandle the bowls in question, we feel they should be taken off the market immediately.
justification: The bowl shattered without causing injury, but the potential for harm is significant if handled at the time of breakage.

incident_description: Our stove - a Frigidaire smoothtop electric range - model #FEFLZ87GCA - spontaneously turned on (small back burner) and did not turn off when the control knob was in the "off" position. We learned about a recall through the CPSC about a year ago and went to the Frigidaire website to let them know that we owned this defective model. Frigidaire did not respond. I clicked a link to report this problem to Frigidaire today, after the incident, but got an error message telling me that it was not functioning. A phone call to Frigidaire's number from the CPSC website found their office closed for the day.
justification: The stove turned on spontaneously but no injury or death occurred, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmor Elite Glass Top Electric Range. I was cooking pastries for dessert after supper on Monday evening, 5/7, and smoke started coming out of the oven. I quickly removed the the pastries from the oven and ran them outside, they were on fire but only slightly. I shut the oven off and closed the door. The house was filled with smoke and the smoke alarms were going off. I opened all the windows in the house to start to air out the house. The air began to clear and the smoke alarms shut off after about 4-5 minutes. I thought that I had maybe over cooked the pastries or that I had put them in for too long. I check the package and re-read the directions and everything had been done correctly. About 15-20 minutes after this happened, smoke started coming out of the oven again. I opened the door to see what was going on, there was a fire inside the oven. It was mostly just smoldering. I noticed that the top element inside the oven was glowing bright red, but the oven was off. I hurried downstairs and shut the power off to the range. I got the fire out and got the smoke vented out of the house. When I had everything cleaned up, I tried turning the power back on to the range. As soon as I did, the top element in the oven turned on again and was bright red in a matter of seconds. I shut the power off right away again and have not turned it on since. I've called Sears, Kenmore, Electrolux, and I've been given a bunch of phone numbers to call. I was told by one of the numbers I called that it was under recall and to call Sears at [REDACTED], but when I call that number they tell me that it is not under recall.  Please help, this thing could have burned my house down. Since it's not under a recall they will fix the range by replacing the parts that are broken with the same type of parts the range was built with and I'd be at risk of this happening again. I'm not sure what to do next, it's going to be tough not having a range for a few days but I'm holding off on fixing it until your organization has a chance to review this occurrance.

Thanks,
[REDACTED]
Range Model # 790.95663201
Range Serial # VF24406910
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with smoke and potential for property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Bosch Dishwasher that was installed by our home-builder in late 2001 continued running non-stop during the night in late January 2012 and eventually overflowed which resulted in a flood in our kitchen - ruining our floors and some sheetrock wall meterial. Recovery firm brought in to limit mold and other damage. All home repairs have been completed as of April 2012. Repairman was brought in to diagnose the reason dishwasher malfunctioned and he recognized it as being part of the recall issued in 2009. Apparently, the circuit board did catch on fire but fortunately in our case the forever-running water must have drowned the fire. Instead of fire damage we had water damage. We were never notified of the recall and so therefore were not aware that repairs were needed.
justification: The incident caused property damage (flooding and material damage) but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it was due to a specific recall-related malfunction.

incident_description:
Caller purchased single cup coffeemaker around mid 2008, had no problems with it until lately when she placed the t-disc into the coffee and after a couple of seconds it spewed  out and sprayed caller causing a burning sensation but not burning the skin.
Caller would like her coffemaker added to the recall.
Her date is FD6118 which is not included at this time.
Her model number is unknown.
She would ask that her plastic disc, or T Disc, that holds the coffee or tea also be replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved a minor burning sensation without skin damage, indicating no actual injury, and the frequency suggests it's a possible occurrence.

incident_description: Unit became hot on outside and burned my finger
justification: The unit became hot and caused a burn injury to the finger, indicating a clear injury.

incident_description: Kenmore Glass Stove Top Exploded
justification: The description mentions an explosion but does not indicate any injuries or deaths, so severity is 2. Stove top explosions are uncommon but not extremely rare.

incident_description: Gas burner failed to ignite and gas continued to flow.  Person couldn't hear or smell the gas.  Product has electronic ignition but no thermocouple to prevent gas flow without ignition.
justification: Gas flow without ignition poses a risk of gas accumulation, which could lead to an explosion or fire, but no injury or death was reported in this incident.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Dishwasher started smoking during the first 5-6 minutes of running. White then brownish smoke. Thankfully I was in the room and noticed the smoke.

MODEL GU2500XTPT6
Serial # FS4204214
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke but no injury occurred, and the issue was noticed promptly.

incident_description: The consumer says that she sat the  product on a lit burner on the stove while the burner was on.  This was after the dish was in the oven.  The consumer says the baking dish was on the burner for less than a minute before it exploded. The consumer feels partially responsible for taking the dish out of the oven and placing it on a lit burner.
justification: The incident involved an exploding baking dish but no reported injury, placing it at severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it requires specific misuse of the product.

incident_description:
I have an Emerson MWG9115SL  Microwave oven that I was given as a gift from WalMart. It was purchased around Nov. 2010 I believe. I began using last May (2011). The microwave sparks from the top right corner inside and makes a humming noise about half the time I use it. I am scared to use it for more than 20 seconds at a time. It also blew my electric outlet and I had to go to circuit breaker to reset. This is a fire waiting to happen.

Since I don't have a receipt and it was purchased several months before I received it, I was not able to return to Walmart. I believe it is now out of warranty.
justification: The microwave sparks and causes electrical issues, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: I have a 2001 kenmore Self Cleaning Electric range I cooked a dinner in the oven and shut oven off then smelt burning opened oven and the top broiler was glowing red hot would not shut off had to unplug tried plugging it back in and it came right back on. this is a very unsafe could star fire
justification: The oven malfunctioned and could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I plugged in my deep fryer and about a couple of minutes after I did, smoke started coming out of the electical unit that goes in the oil. I smelled plastic burning.
justification: Smoke and burning smell indicate an electrical malfunction, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: November 24, 2011, and may 8, 2012:  my mother-in-law and I were both home preparing Thanksgiving dinner when I turned around and noticed the stove was on.  I asked her why she had turned the stove on and she said she had not touched it.  When I looked closely all the dials were tuned to the off position but the digital indicator was on high.  We could not turn the stivetop off and we had to turn off the circuit breaker and then restart it about 30 minutes later.  This incident happened again after this date and I photographed the stove. MIT shows the time and the dials set to off.  Again today I was putting my children to bed when I heard a beeping sound from the kitchen.  There was smoke coming off of the stovetop and the front and back range were on.  Three separate times this product has proved defective and unsafe.  It could burn my house down.
justification: The incident involved a defective stove turning on by itself, creating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to illustrate some of his concerns about his electric wall oven as the inner coils of the oven melted and nearly started a fire in his home. The consumer was cooking in the oven for 10 nearly minutes, before the consumer was in his living room with and noticed the oven flaring up. The consumer powered off the unit at the breaker before any further damage. The consumer was surprised to find that the ovenÃÂs coils had melted.

 The consumer stated that his oven is a single door wall oven. The consumer is not sure of the retailer as the oven was already in his home when he purchased the property. The consumer stated that no one was injured during the incident. The consumer has not called the fire department or his home insurance company about the incident. The consumer has not called the firm.
justification: The incident involved melted coils and a near-fire, but no injuries or further damage occurred, and the consumer acted promptly to prevent escalation.

incident_description: Target Bunny cup - I checked the straw in the cup before I ever gave it to my child and it tore and the top inch of the straw. If I'd given this to my child she could have choked on it. I immediately removed the rest of the straw and put the cup aside thinking I might be able to use a disposable straw instead. However I've now read that the cup has been recalled because the bunny ear could poke my child's eye. Disappointing product.
justification: The incident involved a potential hazard (torn straw and bunny ear) but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the product recall.

incident_description: This unit turns itself on and starts heating when no one is in the room.  It has done this multiple times in the past 24 hours.  I tried unplugging it and after plugging it back in, it did the same thing.
justification: The unit turning on and heating without presence is an incident with no injury, but it has occurred multiple times recently.

incident_description: About 15 or 20 minutes into cycle, the dishwasher made a loud sound and then black smoke started pouring out from the top of the door.  My husband tried to turn it off but it wouldn't so he had to cot the power.
justification: The incident involved black smoke and a loud sound, but no injuries were reported, and the situation was resolved by cutting the power.

incident_description: Middle panel of upper oven door glass of our Kenmore double oven (purchased in 2011) shattered a couple of weeks ago for no apparent reason (other than the oven was on). A couple of days after it was replaced, the same thing happened to the middle panel of glass on the lower door. This will now need replacement, but obviously we are concerned about a safety issue, especially if this happens again to one of the inside or outside glass panels.
justification: The incident involves glass shattering without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence suggests a possible likelihood of 4.

incident_description: The light did not turn off in my Kenmore elite fridge when the door was shut.  There was a strong smell and the bulbs were very hot and the cover was melting.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning fridge light causing overheating and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The bottom heating element in the oven went from 350 degrees to high heat on its own. We tried to cut the oven off with controls but the element would not cut off, the controls said it was off but the element was still glowing bright red and still on high. The only way to cut off was at the breaker switch.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, only a failure to respond to controls.

incident_description:
On 1/28/2012 I was using the stove and it would not turn off when I turned the dial off.  I didn't think it was right... but didn't pay too much attention to it. 

On 1/29/2012 I came out of the shower and smelled burning.  I rushed into the kitchen and found that the stove top had turned on by itself.  The dial was switched to OFF...  Had I not been at home, my house would have burned down.  I called Sears and told me that there was no recall for this model.  MODEL: 790 96122409  SERIAL:  VF715 20321

Now I don't know what to do... I had to unplug it for safety issues and I called Sears for repair but they told me that it was not not on the recall list.  Can you make any suggestions?  Or do I have to go out and buy a new stove?
justification: The stove malfunctioned and turned on by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Stove was being used in bake mode around 375 degrees.
The stove started flashing L10 error for "Runaway temperature"  and smoke started coming out from the stove.  The stove went to broil on it's own, and after turning it to off, it started working again on it's own in broil mode in about 5-10 minutes after it was turned off.  The stove had to be shut off from the breaker panel at this point.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove with smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Preheated oven to 400.  Oven beeped 5 min. later indicating reached temp.  Put in food.  Opened door after one minute when I smelled a mechanical burning odor.  Saw broiler coil bright, red.  Looked at oven displays which read 400 Bake ON.  "On" is only active when you haven't reached the temp.  I reduced temp to 300.  Still on, with broiler coils BRIGHT RED.  Turned off.  Broiler coils would not turn off.  Unplugged.  Took a while (5-10 minutes) for coils to not be bright red.  still something showing bright red inbetween door and stove top area (inside part when looking at oven face-on).  Melting smell.  Moved stove to outdoors (25 degree weather).  Cooled down after 30 minutes.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Plastic dishwasher tub developed a crack immediately under the heating element (hotspot?).  Resulting water damage estimated at $13000.

Sears repair technician told us he had seen the problem before and repair was covered by recall.  Unable to find our particular machine in a recall list and Whirlpool told us it was not recalled. It probably should be because the damage appears to have been caused by a hot spot in the heating element.  I believe Whirlpool had a major recall for overheating heater elements in a product near our model and serial number.
justification: The incident caused water damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as the issue was seen before but not widespread.

incident_description:
I have a a Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator Model # 795.77542600 which is sold under the Sears Kenmore Elite Brand, but is made by LG.
On January 27th, 2012 I opened my refrigerator and saw that the light lens and housing inside the refrigerator were melted and deformed and that the light bulbs were really hot. The food on the upper shelf nearest the lights were also hot. I removed the lens, housing, and light assembly and then disconnected it. 
   I then wrote down my model number and searched the internet to see if this has happened to any other people. I went to the www.mysears.com website and found a posting titled "Light Burned Plastic Housing" in the owner forums. As I read further this same incident has happened to many other owners of this model refrigerator.
I think that this is an unsafe refrigerator that can cause a FIRE, and that it should be recalled by Sears and LG. If this is an Elite model, I wonder how the regular models are.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous condition with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My wife pushed the button for "simmer select" on our Kenmore 30 inch electric range (model 96212) which was purchased new at Sears in May of 2005 for $579.99 plus tax.  This option has been used a few times before, I am guessing maybe 10 times or so.  When she pushed it, it sounded like a shotgun went off with a little smoke, and it kicked off the circuit breaker in the basement. I was concerned about fire, but upon a really quick inspection, all was well.  After settling my wife down, I took the back panel off the stove, and noted the circuit board for the simmer select (sears part number 316429301) had burns on it, along with burn marks on the paint behind it.  I called Sears, and they wanted to sell me one, and were unable to send me one quickly, so I bought one from our local appliance store for $30.20 plus tax and replaced it.  I then decided to look it up on the internet if others had this problem, and came upon the Appliance Repair Forum, where it sounds like multiple people have had this problem.  Sears had nowhere to really report this problem.
justification: The incident caused a loud noise, smoke, and tripped a circuit breaker, but no injuries or fire occurred.

incident_description: i have a ge profile dishwasher. never had a problem for over four years. all of a sudden the heating cycle did not turn off. the counter top was so hot you couldnt touch. the [REDACTED] that was in the dishwasher all melted. the only way it turned off is by shutting the circuit breaker. this is very dangerous. if i would have not been home for the night.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction causing extreme heat and property damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On May 6, 2012 I purchased the Ninja Professional Blender (BL 500) @ WAlMart on Tangerine Road in Tucson, AZ.

When attempting to clean it before use as directed my finger accidently came into contact  with the blender blade and was sliced. My husband had the same thing happen when he came to my  rescue. The blade is razor sharp and trying to assemble the machine or disassemble there is no possible way to prevent contact.  It is not weighted well and flops in your hands. If left out to dry it is more dangerous than a knife because it is exposed on all sides. 

This blade could cut an artery, or slice off a finger with minimal contact.

The good news - when we plugged it in it would not work anyway. Quality may be another issue.

I am a Registered Nurse (40 years) and this product could cause serious injuries needlessly. I have used multiple types of blenders over the years (name brands) and have never encountered anything so dangerous.

Product should be pulled off the shelves immediately.
justification: The description reports injuries from contact with the blender blade, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw making contact almost unavoidable during assembly or cleaning.

incident_description:
When we first got this stove there was a problem with temperature regulation for the large back burner.  To lower the temperature of the burner you had to turn the burner off and then back on to the new temperature.  Since I almost never use this burner we just dealt with it when needed.

A few days ago the front large burner started doing the same thing.  That lasted 24 hours.  Then the burner would turn on but would automatically go to full heat.  

Customer service could not provide any assistance.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove burner with no reported injury or death, but it poses a potential hazard if not addressed.

incident_description: First the refrigerator in the elements series with model # LEEB30T9FEA (this is the doubled oven #) started leaking in the fridge area where the water gets filtered. I would put in a new filter, it would stop leaking and then 2 days later start leaking so much so that it ruined my wood floor. Can you help me?
justification: The incident involves a leaking refrigerator causing property damage (ruined wood floor) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Started wash cycle on our Kitchen Aid dishwasher and the control panel started sizzling and caught fire.  Had to turn off the circuit breaker to kill power to the unit.
Kitchen Aid model: KUDP01ILBL3
Serial Number: FP5002964

incident_description: control panel fire on Kitchenaid dishwasher

2007 Consumer contacted manufacturer and they advised her to contact a retailer that sold the unit and they would pay a portion of the cost if the rep made any repairs.

I had to self fill with water and soak water out by hand thats why I quiet using it several years ago.

incident_description:
This microwave is turning on by itself for no apparent reason.  Searched for a recall and only found that it is happening over & over to people.  Here is the link to these incidents:
http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/magic_chef.html
I don't know how much this is happening with mine...thought the first time was a fluke...just caught it happening again today.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, and it is described as happening repeatedly to multiple people.

incident_description: Bad seal in dishwasher pump caused a slow leak in and under the kitchen. About $15,000 to $25,000 worth of damage.StateFarm won't pay. Says it was a slow leak and thats not covered.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: We purchased an Emerson 0.9 Cubic Foot microwave for Wal-Mart April of 2011 with an extended warranty. Since we have had the microwave, it has had intermittent spark sounds from inside. I called the warranty department and they would not warranty it because we had lost the receipt. 4 days ago, while trying to use the microwave, it started to spark white and smoke. We then unplugged it from the wall and stuck it in the garage. Now, we have no microwave, and this model has reports of causing fire hazards, yet not one will help.
justification: The microwave exhibited dangerous behavior (sparking and smoking) but no injury or death was reported, and the issue is described as a known hazard.

incident_description: The GE 12-cup coffee maker, model number 898682, is defective. I bought the coffee make on April 10, 2012 at Wal-Mart. The coffee had an odd plastic taste to it, and per instructions for GE/Wal-Mart customer service, I ran vinegar and water through the coffee maker. It worked fine. This morning, the coffee maker started to smoke after making a pot of coffee. It smelled like burning plastic. I unplugged it. I tried it again a few hours later, and now it doesn't work at all. I suspect there is a faulty thermostat. I called GE/Wal-Mart customer service and told them about it, because it could be an inherent defect. I know Wal-Mart will take care of it. But I won't be getting another GE coffee maker. I returned the coffee maker to Wal-Mart for a full credit and bought another brand.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned by smoking and emitting a burning plastic smell, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to illustrate his concerns about his under the counter dishwasher as the dishwasher began to smoke while the consumer was having dinner with his family. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in a cycle for nearly 10 minutes before it began to smoke. The consumer put out the smoking by shutting off power the dishwasher then shutting off the circuit breaker. 
The consumer stated that the unit appears to have sustained damage at the control board. The consumer  stated that the damage was isolated to the dishwasher and did not damage the structure of  his home. The consumer was not  injured and did not call the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer not yet called the retailer or the firm. The consumer has done some research and found numerous reports of such incidents online with similar products.
justification: The dishwasher smoked but was quickly controlled without injury or structural damage, fitting a severity level 2. Online reports suggest such incidents are not rare, indicating a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
in reference to this recall:
http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml12/12162.html

My daughter used this cup, she was about 11 months old. and it poked her in the eye so severely we had to go to the ER immediately. Luckily no optical bones were broke-just severe bruising and swelling that subsided within hours.

I did call Target the following day and reported this incident. All they did was sent me a gift card with didn't cover the ER visit and then they played it up like they were very upset. They told me they were going to have someone personally come to my house and pick up the product and i was no to return it to the store. never happened.

this cup was cute but awful-no age recommendation, hard thick plastic. AWFUL!
justification: The incident resulted in severe bruising and swelling requiring an ER visit, indicating an injury but no permanent damage or death.

incident_description: We started our Kenmore Elite Dishwasher in the Smart Wash Mode, approximately five (5) minutes after entering the active wash cycle I smelled burning electrical and smoke and walked back into the kitchen to find smoke pouring out of the right front section of the control panel. I shut the  machine off and secured power at the breaker. After the unit had cooled I removed the front panel section and found the source of the smoke was a small electrical fire on the control board. Upon further inspection I found burn damage at the following board components: Relay K2, Resuistor R9, Pin P8 on Connector #2. There is also evidence of heat damage at pin P6 on Connector #1, Capacitor C22 and a relay pack that I am assuming is K3 but there is too much soot damage to read the board. Un attended this fire, being in an under counter appliance could have easilt resulted in a house fire.
justification: The incident involved a small electrical fire and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such incidents are not common but possible with electrical faults.

incident_description: we have a 2.5 year old kenmore dishwasher. (model 13843K) at the age of 2 the internal racks started melting leaving exposed rusty end pieces.  We called kenmore and were told this happens often and that the racks usually last for 2 years. They sent replacement racks that are not the same as the original and do not clean as many dishes at the same time.  We were never aware that their racks had a 2 year shelf life and now dont use the unit as we are afraid of rust pieces coming off the racks and getting onto our silverware
justification: The incident involves melting and rusty dishwasher racks, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has occurred. The issue is described as common by the manufacturer.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to illustrate that her side by side refrigerator is a potential fire hazard as the light bulb on the inside of the refrigerator will stay on when the door is closed. The consumer stated that the light bulb has melted and warped the housing of the light bulb. The consumer stated that the bulb has not yet burned out. The bulb did blacken from the intense heat and is still intact. The light bulb in fixture was an unknown amount of watts.

 The consumer noticed this 3 months ago and removed the light bulb from the refrigerator. The consumer was not injured by the product and the consumer did not sustain extensive property damage. The consumer did not call the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer has not yet called the firm. The consumer has not had the product serviced prior.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no injury or extensive property damage, and the consumer took action to remove the bulb.

incident_description: After leaving home for about half a day we came home to discover a burning smell coming out of the fridge.  after opening the upper portion of the fridge was melting and very hot.  all the food was hot and spoiled.  I was afraid of it bursting into flames when I opened the doors.
justification: The fridge showed signs of overheating and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
On 12/29/2011 at 1 am there was a notice of a burning odor in the home which was coming from the sides and the control panel of the dishwasher. She attempted to press the cancel button and open the door but it continued to run. 

The circuit breaker was pulled to  cease power to the dishwasher. There were smoke damages in the cabinets. The dishwasher was set at 9 pm on 12/28/2011 for a four hour delay in which it started at 1 am on 12/29/2011. The setting  it was placed on was not provided along with the timing for the cycle.

  The firm was contacted on 12/30/2011 and a service technician is scheduled to come out on  1/10/2012 to only make repairs  to the motor assembly. She advised the representative (name unknown) that she believed that the hazard was within the control panelÃÂs  circuit board.

The representative advised the consumer that once the technician comes out to make the necessary repairs to the motor assembly and he is able to locate a failure with the control panel then they would make a decision at that time on how to handle it.
justification: There was a burning odor and smoke damage, but no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
(1) Smelled burning odor in my "warm" refrigerator. 
(2) As it turns out the lights were not turning off when the refrigerator door closed. 
(3) Because the lights were not turning off, they were heating, melting, and burning the plastic cover for the lights in the refrigerator. 
(4) This may be a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and melting plastic due to lights not turning off, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Problem involves a Sears Kenmore Elite TRIO Refrigerator Freezer purchased new 7/2006.  Opened refrigerator door and smelled melting plastic and noticed food and containers on top shelf near interior light were bulging due to heat.  Interior light enclosure was deformed due to melting.  Appears to be problem that interior light was not turning off causing excessive heat build up and melting of plastic cover.  Top interior of refrigerator above light bulb reflector/shield coating was blistered, light sockets are brown due to excessive heat and clear plastic insert was fused into opaque plastic interior light dome housing.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and heat build-up in the refrigerator, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the microwave was in use for approximately 2 mins it stopped running, she discovered that the trimming around the door and the stickers inside the microwave was scorched and melted leaving a hole in the door trimmings.  The contents that she had placed in the microwave was still frozen.

11/18/11 Consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and was advised that there was no recall and that she would have pay to have someone diagnose it, she declined and then was offered a partial rebate towards purchase of another microwave.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be reported
justification: The microwave malfunctioned, causing scorching and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Purchased a toaster at Dollar General store in Mount Jackson, VA. Toaster is a Continental Electric (made in China), model CE232411 DG. When in use the sides got extremely hot. The temperature setting knob goes from 1 to 7. When set on 4 the sides of the toaster were very hot. Tried again with the setting on 2 and still too hot. This is a safety hazard and can result in a fire or severe burn to child or adult users.
justification: The toaster's sides getting extremely hot poses a safety hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he had turned on the microwave without anything inside for approximately 4 mins at full power, however, he noticed that there was smoke emitting from it and discovered that the door seal and the plastic inside melted.

Consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer is concerned that this microwave is a fire hazard and/or should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting parts but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as misuse of microwaves is common.

incident_description:
The microwave has a feature sensor cooking  that she placed on bake potatoes and start and it should shut off when the time is completed. The machine did not stop running and smoke began pouring from the inside of the machine. Smell from smoke lasted over 2 weeks.  Clothes and furniture full of smell.

She attempted to power the appliance in the off position with the switch and when that did not work she opened the door and the unit stopped operating . 

She had to open two doors in the home and run a few fans to get rid of the smoke and used fans throughout.  She indicated that she has used the sensor cooking button several occasions before and nothing happened in the past.

She contacted the firm  on 10/17/2011 and  spoke with a representative who indicated that she would pass the information on t o someone with the company and have someone get back with her. 

She received a follow up call on 10/26/2011 while filing a report with CPSC. She indicated that she would give them a call back. She has used the appliance but not on the sensory cooking setting and it works but it still has the burning odor in it. 

When the appliance is not in use she unplugs it from the wall outlet and when it is in use she plugs it in to use it.
justification: The incident involved smoke and odor but no injury or death, and the microwave malfunctioned but was eventually stopped without harm.

incident_description: The consumer says she finished cooking and went to clean the microwave and noticed the side panel had melted from the bottom up.  She had not used the microwave that day as she was cooking with the oven.   The consumer contacted the manufacturer who offered $85 for a replacement shield.  She feels that the control panel needs replacement.  The manufacturer told her that because she has tiles in her kitchen it generated the heat with melted the panel which she cannot believe.  She says this model was made to be vented which she does not know if it is a reason for unit melting on the inside.  The consumer would just like the panel be replaced.
justification: The incident involves a melted microwave panel with no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: The stove range that we have does not have a safety switch to turn it on.  On several occasions people visiting us or our kids have turned on the range without our noticing it.
justification: The stove being turned on unintentionally is an incident with no injury reported, and it happens frequently based on the description.

incident_description: I have a KitchenAid (manufactured by Whirlpool) dishwasher (model #kuds01flbt1) that quit working. Upon some investigation I determined the problem was likely the control board. After removing the front panel to access the control board I found the board had shorted and burnt, and also melted some of the wire on the wiring harness. There was no fire beyond that, but can easily see how this short could have caused a major fire. I did some research on-line and found there are already quite a few instances of fires from this dishwasher, and a television report from January 2012 said the CPSC was investigating. So, basically this report confirms I have a similar experience to many others.
justification: The incident involved a shorted control board and melted wiring, posing a fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred. Online reports indicate this is a recurring issue, suggesting a higher likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
Empty microwave oven self-started while unattended. Feared empty unit might explode or cause fire. Unable to shut off with keypad.  Keypad not responding.  Opened door to shut off.  Unplugged unit to try to reset. Plugged unit back in. Unable to reset.  Keyboard not responding.  Unit self-started unattened again.  Keypad unresponsive. Opened door to shut off.  Unplugged unit. 

Called manufacturer at [REDACTED]  to report incident:  Magic Chef Model # MCO160UW Serial #DJ07Z03206 Production date: Dec 2007
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but did not cause injury or damage, only fear of potential fire or explosion.

incident_description: The consumer says she had her dishwasher on when she heard a strange sound.  She saw smoke coming out of the control panel.  She says it could have been a matter of minutes before it caught fire.  Her husband shut off the circuit breaker.  She says the unit was on for about an hour.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who will send out a technician next week.  She feels the unit should be recalled.
justification: Smoke was observed, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On December 17th 2011 a 65 ft motor yacht (Fridaspirit) caught fire at Grove Harbour Marina in Coconut Grove, FL.  The boat burned and sank. 5 other yachts were damaged or destroyed during this incident.  It also caused damage to the Marina itself.  The unit was factory installed equipment purchased with the yacht.  The attorney has put the manufacturer on notice of the investigation and they have sent in house engineers.  

The determination was made this morning that this product is involved in the recall for Release # 09-145.  The attorney has preserved the remains of the refrigerator and internal component parts.  The attorney would like an investigator from CPSC to examine the evidence.  Investigation into the cause of the fire continues.  The attorney says there were 4 persons on board the yacht at the time of the fire, and were treated for smoke inhalation.  One of the occupants had severe second degree burns to the upper body.  

The captain sustained a foot injury.  According to the occupants of the yacht, they were sleeping on the lower deck when the husband of the family woke up early that morning.  He went up to the main deck when he saw smoke coming from the vessel's galley, on the port side.  He went back downstairs, and woke up his family.  By the time they went up to the main deck there was so much smoke that they could not see.  The family was able to get off the boat.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including severe second-degree burns and smoke inhalation, but no deaths were reported.

incident_description:
While the microwave was not in use it  began to operate without being switched in the on position with the  fan inside of the appliance and the vent opening and closing. He opened the door and it still opened and closed.  The appliance was unplugged from the wall outlet.

He has the mother board replaced in 2009, 2010, and 2011 for the same failure.  The consumer indicated that in order for him to use the appliance he had to plug it in to the wall outlet and then unplug it. He contacted the firm on 1/5/2012 and the consumer was advised that they were not going to replace the mother board anymore.

He has not made any final decisions on what his next step will be as far as replacing the appliance.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned without causing injury, and the issue has recurred multiple times, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the dishwasher was in use for approximately 5 mins,  a weird noise and smoke was emitting from the door (control panel area) he immediately disconnect the electrical connection to prevent further damage.  This was the first time this incident had occured.  There was no visible damages.

1/4/12 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and he was advised that his model was not part of a recall and that there was nothing they could do since the dishwasher was out of warranty.

Consumer is concerned that his dishwasher might be a fire hazard and feels that this should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a weird noise but no injury or damage occurred, and it was the first occurrence.

incident_description: Magic Chef model MC0160UW over-the-stove microwave oven is turning itself on and starting what appears to be the "popcorn" cooking cycle.  The keypad was not responsive when I tried to stop it and it could only be stopped by opening the door.  It has now done this several times. I tried disconnecting the power completely for several hours in case there's any form of reset but it still intermittently power itself on in the same manner once reconnected to power.
justification: The microwave turns on unexpectedly, posing a hazard, but no injury or death has been reported. The issue occurs intermittently but frequently after reconnecting power.

incident_description:
I would like to bring this critical matter to the attention of Whirlpool and KitchenAid.  I trust you will be able to properly direct my concerns with the quality and safety of Microwave Hood Combination product, KHMS147HSS.

I am the first original owner of the KHMS147HSS with the serial number XCJ4511772.  The unit was purchased on 11/30/1999 for $663.00, and installed in my home as part of its new construction on 3/11/2000.  

From practically ÃÂday-one,ÃÂ I have had problems with the unit.  It was a part of the fire-safety recall of January, 2001.  Claim #1190520 was opened with Whirlpool on 11/7/2001.  The in-home repair technician,[REDACTED], struggled to implement the recall enhancement on 1/2/2002.  

Being that I was an un-married bachelor, the microwave merely functioned as a device to reheat leftovers and heat water for my morning oatmeal.  Due to the safety recall, I never had confidence in the unit.  But with a purchase price of $663.00, I naturally continued to use the unit.  That is, until this past Saturday.

When the unitÃÂs interior oven light was not functioning, I located my original ownerÃÂs manual for the steps to replace the burnt-out light bulb on 11/12/2011.  Following the instructions, I disconnected the power cord and proceeded to ÃÂremove the burnt-out bulb by squeezing the wire clip together, pulling to the right and lifting upÃÂ as described in the ownerÃÂs manual, page 23, step 5.

At this point, I observed sparks and the odor of burnt electrical components.  I was perplexed on how this could happen with no power applied to the unit.  After changing the light bulb and reconnecting the power cord to the unit, the microwave would no longer function.  It was dead, yet the electrical outlet was verified to be a live circuit by means of a voltage tester.  Upon further examination, I was shocked to see the poor design of the ÃÂwire clipÃÂ being a metal conductor in extremely close proximity to that of the light bulb socket holder and its non-insulated wire connections.  I have included these pieces for your Whirlpool techniciansÃÂ examination.  I conclude this design to be yet another major safety hazard of this Microwave Hood Combination product!!!

The now defective KHMS147HSS with serial number XCJ4511772 is in the recycle center of Naperville, IL, (180 Fort Hill Drive, Naperville, IL 60540), 11/15/2011.
justification: The incident caused a safety hazard but no injury or death, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not rare but not certain to happen.

incident_description: About 1/2 hour after brewing a pot of coffee, the coffee maker suddenly started loudly hissing, gurgling, and popping...similar to the normal sounds at the end of the brew cycle, but louder.  At the same time, smoke began appearing, accompanied by a strong acrid odor like that of an electrical fire.  The machine's on-light was off, though it had not been turned off.  We unplugged the unit, removed the filled carafe, and allowed the machine to cool down, with no further incident.
justification: The coffee maker exhibited dangerous behavior with smoke and an electrical odor, but no injury occurred as it was promptly unplugged.

incident_description:
Cuisinart coffee programmable coffee maker model DCC1200 purchased new in Nov. 2010 through Amazon.com.  On 5/4/12 after a two-hour brew and keep warm sequence, I was in another room and heard a loud sizzling and crackling sound coming from our kitchen.  The unit was apparently off, but bluish smoke was pouring from the unit and the remaining coffee in the carafe  (about two 5 oz. cups) was quite hot.  I quickly unplugged the unit before things got worse.  Thankfully, my kitchen counter top was not damaged and I was home to intervene.  It supposedly has a three year warranty, but other owners have lamented the hassle of repackaging the defective product for return and paying for round trip shipping costs totaling nearly $30.00 (for returned and replacement units).  

I will not have another Cuisinart coffee maker in my home- it's not worth risking a fire and endangering my family.  Multiple Cuisinart coffee maker failures across different models identical to my scenario have been reported through the CPSC saferproducts.gov web site.  Cuisinart should be compelled to recall and stop selling these defective units and back their product with full refunds regardless if under warranty; no questions, no hassles.  It is only a matter of time before Cuisinart is going to face property damage or loss of life claims from knowingly continuing to sell a dangerous product.
justification: The incident caused smoke and a hot carafe, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
In the summer of 2010 I purchased a Samsung convection range, model FTQ387LWGX.  In August  (or may be Sept ) of 2011 while cooking on the stove I noticed an electrical burning odor and smoke coming from the back of the range and then one of the burners stopped working. I cantacted Samsung and a technician came and found that the wires to the control knob had burned through. He replaced them. Yesterday 12/27., The same thing happened with the same knob and burner. I am VERY concerned that this issue will cause a fire or electrcal shock and am concerned that others with this same range may experience the same problem.  Below is the email I sent to SAMSUNG a few minutes ago.

on 9/19/10 I purchased the above range serial # 18897DDSA00403N with a twelve month warranty plus the addition3 or 4 months. Last summer (August, I believe) I experienced an electrical burning odor and smoke emanating from the back of the range and then the front right burner would not work. . After finally figuring out how to contact Samsung, a technician came and said the issue was  behind the back control panel, that wires had burned through to the knob. The actual burner was ok, it was the wiring to the control knob. It took him about 5 minutes to repair and worked fine until yesterday when apparently the SAME THING HAPPENED. Smoke and burning electrical odor from the back and the SAME burner is now out. I am EXTREMELY concerned, not about the inconvenience, but the saftey of the appliance. I have a 15 yr old as well as a handicapped 18 yr old  home alone in the afternoons  and have now told them  "DO NOT USE THIS STOVE", only I will use it . I am concerned about the potential for a house fire or electrical shock.  I believe there is a design flaw or inferior component at work here. Never have I owned a range that required service twice in its lifetime let alone twice in less than 18 months,and for  FOR THE SAME ISSUE. I believe that you should, at your expense, come and do a complete check of this stove and reassure me that it is, in fact, safe to use. I am keeping a record of this correspondence as proof that you have been notified of this problem, should there be any disaster with this stove. I am also forwarding this to the Consumer Products Saftey" commission as I am concerned for anyone else who may have purchased this item. Please respond ASAP.
justification: The incident involves smoke and burning odor from the stove, posing a risk of fire or electrical shock, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
LG Range Model#LRG3095ST/00..Serial Number 110MMTS0F089
Product Code FG4331ES.FSTELGA

I purchased this gas range brand new from HH Gregg retail store, Towson, Md 21204.
This stove has a flaw in it's design, this is the second time this stove has out of the blue
started trying to ignite itself and the only way to stop it is to unplug it from the wall.
Both time I have been home, and been able to unplug it before a problem arose, what happens when someone isn't home.

LG comes out and claims that it is repaired, but yet it continues to happen causing a danger to family and home.
justification: The stove's repeated malfunction poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet due to timely intervention.

incident_description:
When cleaning off my two-weeks-old mixer at my kitchen sink, I received a shock as I went to turn off the (grounded metal) faucet.  I had been running the mixer in a mixing bowl full of soapy water to help clean off the "beaters."  The mixer was not at all submerged, but my hands may have been a little wet.  I was plugged into a GFCI receptacle.  It was a low-current shock, and I did not experience any burning or muscle contraction (the GFCI also did not trip, though it has been tested to be functioning).

This is a consumer product and I was using it at home, but professionally I work as an Occupational Safety and Health Professional for an electrical contractor.  My opinion is that the device is leaking current, and we just never realized it until the conditions were just right (my hands were wet and I touched a grounded source--the faucet handle).
justification: The incident involved a low-current shock with no burning or muscle contraction, indicating no injury but an incident occurred.

incident_description: I bought a emerson microwave model mw8991sb in january 2011.  In february 2012 an aluminized piece of a cardboard started sparking and caught fire. I returned it to where I bought it for a replacement.  Now last night the the open button has jammed .
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave causing sparks and a jammed button, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: i have had this unit around a year and a half or so.and i do not want to hear that i dint clean it or clean it wrong like so many others have been told we have taken care of unit .when u turn the unit on it starts to spark orange sparks.almost looks like a fire on the inside also there is rust starting on the inside of the door when u open it.we have cleaned this unit with soap and water.but im sure it will be something we have done .i chose this one cause i liked the looks and options it had.but now i and so mad i will never but this name brand again.we have owned many microwaves and they have last a lot longer and we have had no problems even close to this.and please do not send email back that we are the cause of this you have a ton of people who are complaining about the same thing or close to it happening.sounds to me maybe you should evaluate this situation if you want to keep customers .i would greatly appreciate some type of response since we did pay a good amount for this and now have no use of unit anymore ...
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning microwave with sparks and rust, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: the handle has a safety switch which when enabled allows the safe operation of the oven.  this is poorly designed and malfunctioned to cause the constant operation  of the oven even when the handle is lifted .  the oven has to be unplugged in order to stop the oven.
justification: The malfunctioning safety switch poses a risk of continuous oven operation, which could lead to overheating or fire, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: The consumer says that she placed a pot roast and liquid inside the slow cooker.  Put it on high for one hour.  She came back to check on it after the hour was over when she noticed the base was very hot.  She looked underneath the cooker, the plastic bottom bubbled out and one of the legs started to cave in.  The consumer unplugged the unit and removed the contents.
justification: The incident involved damage to the slow cooker but no injury occurred, and such malfunctions are possible with electrical appliances.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express her concerns about her juicer as the a piece of the product very nearly struck her in the eye and the product began to smoke. The consumer was in the process of juicing carrots and apples in the upper portion of the juicer. While the consumer was holding down the juicer, one of the two plastic flaps on the top panel of the juice broke and the debris went up in the direction of the consumer. The plastic flap struck the consumer in the face, startling but not injuring her. 

The product continued to juice on its own for nearly another 20-30 seconds, the product began to smoke. The consumer unplugged the juicer from the outlet. By design, the 2 plastic flaps are on opposite sides of the juicer.  The consumer did not call the retailer as she is not sure of who they are. The consumer also did not find it necessary to call the fire department or her home insurance company. 

The consumer called the firm 2 days ago about the incident and was told they could not help her as the product is out of warranty. The consumer stated that there was no damage to the structure of her home.
justification: The plastic flap struck the consumer in the face but did not cause injury, and the product smoking indicates a potential hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer says the unit spontaneously start spraying hot water all over the place.  The consumer says this does not occur while its in use.  This only happens when the product is not in use.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told her it is out of warranty so there is nothing they can do.   She says it splashed her in the past and almost on her 10 year old daughter this afternoon according to her husband.   This has happened about 5 times since February 2012.UPDATE: 
4/6/12- Keurig rep agreed to replace the product at reduced price (about 35% off retail price ($119 to $79)
justification: The incident involves hot water spraying, which has splashed the consumer in the past and nearly affected a child, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her dishwasher had a burning odor and the control panel would no longer work. She was not in the house, but left the dishwasher on the ÃÂdelay startÃÂ option. Her husband was awakened by the burning odor; when he walked in the kitchen the dishwasher was already off and would no longer work.  He was unable to be precise on whether there were flames, sparks or smoke. 

The consumerÃÂs husband opened the back of the control panel to look inside and examine the damages. He found that the inside had cables burnt and the plastic areas had melted.  There were no damages to her home and she did not have to contact the fire department. 

The consumer believes that this a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and damage to the dishwasher, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
This afternoon my Maytag Model MMV 1153 AAB (GE) Over-The-Stove type Microwave stuck on after normal use without warning but only the Power Transformer was buzzing until it burned through my empty microwave dish, blackening it and broke the glass turn table from overheating. I would never had noticed it until I smelled an electrical smoldering smell as I was using just the exhaust fan of the unit so it drowned out the buzzing until I turned the fan off. I had to open and close door several times and kept pushing the off switch until it stopped buzzing. I then unplugged power cord and I am still watching it to make sure I don't have a fire tonight. About three years ago, I found Glass Turn Table broken & replaced it at hefty cost but I did not know how the break occurred but I now believe this may have stuck on once before and now I have 2 broken glass turn tables in 3 years. I do not find any Maytag Recalls for this model and I wonder why! Please help me to get this taken care of somehow. I live in [REDACTED] area.

[REDACTED]

UPDATE: 
On February 28, 2012 A&E Factory Service came to my home and only spent about 10-15 minutes looking at my Maytag Microwave and mostly writing notes to his computer.
In this time, the Technician did not even remove a cover to the main components and
condemned the Circuit Board and Broken Microwave Turntable Glass Dish.
He said that Maytag would pay the labor but I would have to pay $221.32 for the parts required to fix the Microwave.
I do not trust this Microwave, as I believe that a dangerous fire could result even if they
fixed the current problem
I wanted them to replace the complete unit or at least cover all the charges including the
parts but the Technician said that they wouldn't.
Today, March 29, 2012, I called the Whirlpool Company Customer Service, the
manufacturer ofthis Maytag Microwave and spoke with [REDACTED] at 12 Noon CST.
[REDACTED] consulted with her supervisor who told me they would not pay for any parts for my microwave so I am filing this report without any satisfaction from the Manufacturers.
I hope that CPSC can do something to help me with this problem and others who might also be experiencing this dangerous problem
justification: The incident involved a microwave malfunction causing damage but no injury or death, and the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the history.

incident_description:
The consumer sÃÂ mother in law accidently bumped into the range on one occasion and within a matter of minutes the fire alarm went off. The consumer went into the kitchen noticed that the oven was powered in the broil position. 

The consumer powered the oven in the off position and was able to carefully notice that the knob went just a little past the off position and he noticed how it would get easily positioned on the broil position.

On or around August 22,2011 a service technician came out to the home to do what is known as a ÃÂsafety checkÃÂ. The technician advised the consumer that the range needed a thermostat to prevent the failure from occurring.

The consumer indicated that he would order the part and that he would make the repairs himself because the firm wanted to charge him for the parts & labor. 

The range is located in the consumerÃÂs in laws home and he isnÃÂt aware if it is being used or if it is in the unplug position from the wall outlet. He indicated that prior to the technician coming out to the home the range was unplugged from the wall out.

UPDATE:
Dear Sirs, The incident report as stated herein does not adequately exemplify either the extreme dangerousness of the problem, nor the fact that it was caused by a faulty design, and cheaply manufactured plastic part which the company, sent someone out to confirm that this part was the problem, but than refused to fix this dangerous design problem. I own multiple rental properties with approximately 21 natura1 gas appliances and I have never had any failure that caused such a dangerous situation, and this from an appliance that is only a couple ofyears old, newer than all of mine. A tiny piece of plastic that performed as a stop and allowed the oven temp broiler nod to turn only one direction, broke off thus making it actually tricky to turn the stove off, and making it easy to inadvertently pop it on to broil without even knowing that it was turned on. This happened on multiple occasions. I strongly urge the consumer product safety commission to recall this product and all other models made with the same design, IT IS NOT SAFE!
justification: The incident involved a faulty oven design that could inadvertently turn on, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she walked into her apartment and they noticed a smoke odor. She was unsure of where the smell was being emitted from. The next morning the consumer went to use the dishwasher and it would not turn on. The consumer was not aware of any outer damages to the dishwasher.

The consumer did not experience any damages to her home structure and no one was injured. The consumer was informed of the recall release# 12-147 and believes her dishwasher is experiencing the same signs. 

02/07/2012 The consumer contacted a repair company authorized by the manufacture and they sent a technician to service the dishwasher.  The technician stated that the dishwasher had an electrical problem. He stated that the ÃÂcontrol panelÃÂ burnt up.  The technician informed her that she would need to replace the control panel (part# 021151-000). The technician informed her that she would receive an estimated pricing for the repairs. 

2/13/2012 The consumer received the estimate of $419.00 dollars (out of pocket) for the labor of the repairs. The consumer has not made a decision whether she will declined or accept the repairs. 

The consumer believes that this is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a smoke odor and a burnt control panel, but no injuries or structural damages occurred.

incident_description:
During the wash cycle, the dishwasher became so hot the countertop above was too hot to touch and we smelled smoke.  After tripping the breaker to be certain it stopped heating, I waited for it to cool down.  When I opened the door, the sprayer arm and part of the door assembly and styrofoam was melted, as well as several plastic items and the handles of two knives.  When I called the service number, I was told the machine was out of warranty (by only a few months) and the only thing they offered was a slight reduction in the price of new dishwasher.  After MUCH arguing with successive levels of personnel at Frigidaire, they agreed to pay for the parts to repair it and we agreed to pay for the labor.  

I WAS NOT SATISFIED AND WILL NEVER BUY ANOTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT.  

The machine was repaired after about two weeks (initially the wrong parts were sent for the repair) and we have used it (only when we are at home and awake, as I DO NOT feel safe otherwise) until we can afford to replace it.  I believe the Frigidaire company should have replaced the machine and paid for the damaged utensils.
justification: The incident involved significant damage and safety concerns but no reported injuries, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: smoke came out of the unit when we were heating a cup of coffee.  Lots of smoke, seem to come from the motor
justification: Smoke emission indicates an incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My Frigidaire dishwasher model: FDB1050REC2 had been leaking slightly so I checked underneath and the plug where the heating element was attached to the dishwasher had overheated, causing the seal to burn away and allowing water to leak through the seal.  This water leaked onto the wired terminal and caused a short as well as some substantial corrosion.  This is a clear safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a safety hazard with overheating and water leakage, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our GE Cafe over-the-range microwave, spontaneously turned itself on.  We were fortunate that we were home and that we heard it promptly. It was very early in the morning and actually woke me up. The oven was making an alarm sound as if it was at the end of a program but it never turned off.  There were many reports on the internet related to serious fires from this same type of incident and I do not feel as though we can leave it plugged in when not in the immediate area.
justification: The microwave turned itself on without any injury, but there was a risk of fire, which is a serious incident.

incident_description: I have a GE Microwave Serial # LS90398713 Model # JVM154DN1BB , This microwave comes on all by itself and will not go off until you unplug it. I believe this may be a fire hazard. I have contacted GE which they deny this is a problem I have read numerous complaints on consumer complaints.com  about the same product so therefore, this is not an isolated case.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported. Multiple complaints indicate this is not an isolated issue.

incident_description: The consumer says she was heating up water for tea, she set it for a minute then white smoke started coming out of it.  She says the water was not warm enough so she set it for another minute and more smoke came out of it.  The consumer opened the door and all the lights inside the unit went off.  She tried to contact the manufacturer but could not get to speak with anyone.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical failure but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
when plugged in the microwave starts on its own & after about 1 minute 
it says key pad short with an alarm beap.
 Since then I have unplugged it & verified with others & they have the same problem.
justification: The microwave starts on its own and displays an error, posing a potential hazard, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: I bought a Pyrex baking dish set with 3 quart and 2 quart (new style with the handles formed in the glass) on 9-02-11. I baked a cake in the 3 quart for Thanksgiving and never used either dish since. On 4-20-12 we heard a load bang like someone had shot the house with something. We checked the house and found nothing. The next day we opened the pantry and discovered that the 3 quart baking dish had exploded. It had been sitting in the bottom of the pantry with the 2 quart sitting inside of it. There was no change in temperature or anything we can think of that could of caused it. It did not just break - it exploded into tiny pieces that were everywhere. Nobody was hurt.
justification: The baking dish exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
In (approximately) August, 2011, I purchased a Tassimo Home Brewer.  There was a recall due to the discs exploding in the machine.  I received the new part in early March, 2012 and used it according to the directions provided.

The discs continue to explode.  When this happens, HOT WATER and GRINDS SPEW from the machine.  I have taken pictures on various occasions to document this dangerous condition.

On April 27, 2012, I sent an e-mail to Tassimo Customer Service with the photos and on April 28th, I received a response that someone will be in touch with me within 24 hours.  Nobody contacted me so on May 3, 2012, I called Tassimo.

incident_description:
In 2006, I bought a Anchor Hocking 13ÃÂ x 9ÃÂ glass baking dish so that I could bake  cakes for a bake sale.  I bought the dish in Vero Beach, Florida.  I used the 13ÃÂ x 9ÃÂ approximately two to three times per year since its purchase.
I play shuffleboard at the [REDACTED] community where I own a condominium.  At the end of winter season, the folks who play shuffleboard have a party.  On March 20, 2010, I was baking pineapple upside down cake for the shuffleboard event.  I have been making pineapple upside down cakes for approximately 30 years.  I had baked one pineapple upside down cake in the oven at 350 degrees for 35 minutes using the glass baking dish described above.

Before using the dish it had been sitting in the storage drawer under the oven.  It had not been exposed to cold or to any cold or damp surfaces.  When the cake was done, I removed the baking dish from the oven and placed it on a metal cooling rack on the counter  to cool.  The counter was dry.  After about 20 minutes, the cake had cooled and I flipped the cake and placed it on a tinfoil lined cardboard box bottom.

I then placed the baking dish back on the counter for approximately 15 or more minutes.  I then washed the baking dish with water and dried it thoroughly.  I washed the dish with [REDACTED] or a similar liquid dish soap as I always had washed the dishes.  I placed the dish on the stove between the burners and not on the burners as I was about to prepare a second cake.  None of the burners were on and they had not been on since 4 hours earlier when I turned one on to heat some water.

I placed melted butter in the baking dish momentarily after placing the dish on top of the stove, not the burners.  I then turned to mix cake batter in my kitchenÃÂs sink.  The sink is perpendicular to the oven so my right side and back were facing the oven.  The dish was on the stove top between the burners for less than ten minutes when I heard a loud boom.

I felt a sharp pain in my left Achilles Tendon and blood was pouring from it.  I looked over at the glass dish and it had exploded violently and pieces of glass were everywhere.  Later I found shards of glass more than 12 feet away from the stove.  I later found out my Achilles Tendon had been completely severed.

At no time during my ownership of this baking dish have I used any abrasive chemical to clean it or used sharp objects on it.  I have never seen any nicks, scratches, chips, cracks or other imperfections in the glass dish.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (severed Achilles Tendon) caused by the violent explosion of a glass baking dish.

incident_description:
Visible electrical arcing from under our Maytag ÃÂOver the Range" Microwave Oven followed by the house
fifteen amp circuit breaker shutting off power, was found to be caused by the 'Cooktop/Nlght Light' bulb socket coming loose from its mounting bracket and shorting against the frame of the microwave. In order to resecure the socket to the bracket, the aluminum bracket flange had to be bent downward where it is discovered that there is only one tab on the bracket to hold the socket in place whereas there are two mounting holes on the socket; in other words, the socket is secured to its bracket by a single 1/8 " piece of bent-aluminum tab. It was noted the first time the bulb was replaced some six months ago that the socket was loose and apparently the opening and closing the microwave door shook the socket loose with the resulting arcing. After reinstalling the bulb socket with the single tab on its aluminum bracket, the bracket bulb-socket assembly was then bent back upward to its original position. Because of the low clearance between the bottom of the microwave and the oven below, access to the 'Cooktop/Nightlight' bulb compartment is very constrained, which means that the probability that the socket will come loose from this bracket during a bulb change is very high ... -with the arcing we experienced or worse, an electrical shock for the person trying to change the bulb if the socket comes loose ..
Picture 1 shows the socket bracket (bent down) with the wires of the loose socket laid across the bracket 'yoke' .
Picture 2 shows the socket left 'ear' which is not secured when the socket is mounted in the bracket.
Picture 3 shows the cramped access to the light compartment and resulting shock hazard from a loose socket.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and a potential shock hazard, indicating a risk of injury, and the constrained access increases the likelihood of recurrence.
