incident_description:
Product: Sanyo SK-CV8S, Convection Toaster Oven

I am writing because this unit has a fundamental design flaw that should disqualify it from the market: the oven rack has no fasteners to prevent it from falling out when trying to remove items from the oven. That means when you go to pull a 400 degree baking dish out of the unit, you need to put your hand entirely inside the unit in order to extricate the dish. If you do what a normal user would want to do and slide out the rack a few inches so you don't have to put your hand within inches of the top heating rods, the entire rack tips forward and dumps your 400 degree food directly onto you!

I have had this incident happen to me several times to date, with items as relatively innocuous as toast (today) to items that present a real danger such as casserole (last month). I truly fear that if a consumer is not aware of this design flaw and goes to remove a hot dish from this convection oven with a child at his/her foot, there is a very real possibility of permanent burn injuries to that child.

After the rack fell completely out of the oven toward me the first time, I tried to be careful by not pulling the oven rack out too far. This, of course, brought my hand in contact with the top heating rods, scarring my left hand. The design flaw makes this product a "lose-lose" for users. If you want to pull your items out of the rack, you end up with your 400 degree food on your legs and feet. If you try to avoid the rack falling out, you end up burning your hands inside the unit.

I am taking the time to report this product because I truly believe you will see reports of burn injuries as a result of this product, with the unrestrained rack being responsible for most of these injuries.
justification: The incident describes repeated burn injuries from hot food or contact with heating rods, indicating a significant risk of harm.

incident_description: DETAILS ---- I recently put a pot of water on my glass GE stove top and went into the other room. About 2 minutes later I heard this deafening boom. I returned to the kitchen and the entire stovetop had exploded and sent shards of glass, some of them 8 to 10 inches long, across the kitchen. If I had been in the kitchen at the time, it would have seriously maimed me at the least or could have killed me outright. After 4 months of trying to get GE to replace and install another stove top, they have decided to charge me for a new stove top and installation because it is out of warranty. I asked them if the original warranty covered explosions which they admitted it did not so I asked them if explosions werenÃÂt covered in the warranty what did it matter if it was under warranty or not? I asked them if they designed their stove tops to explode. They said they didnÃÂt so I told them if you donÃÂt design them to explode, then the stove tops which do explode must be defective. They then said that they couldnÃÂt be sure that I hadnÃÂt done something to cause it to explode so I told them they couldnÃÂt prove that I had so it was a moot point. The tech they sent out told me he had seen other instances of this problem and that it was possible to cause microfractures in the stovetop by scratching it or dropping something like a frying pan or can of food on it which would eventually cause it to blow up. So, is a consumer supposed to inspect the stovetop with a magnifying glass before each use? What if there are microfractures and he misses them? Is it then the users fault if he is killed or injured when it explodes? If GE knows that it has a problem where the stovetops can injure someone, shouldnÃÂt they do a recall before that happens? This is a multi-million dollar corporation and it would probably cost them less than $100 to do the right thing but instead they price a new stove top at over $500 plus close to $200 dollars for installation. At this point, I think III just become someone elseÃÂs customer and take them to small claims court. It will cost them more to send someone to court than it would for them to just do the right thing and replace the stovetop and have their tech install it. I hope that no one is ever hurt by their product in the future but, if they ever are, I hope they (or their survivors) wind up owning GE. My next stove top will definitely not be glass.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of a glass stovetop, but no injury occurred as the person was not in the kitchen at the time.

incident_description:
Model# FRS6HR5HB1 - Frigidaire Refrigerator (side by side)
Purchased ~July/Aug 2007.

This unit caught fire 4/28/2012.  I noticed a burning smell in my kitchen and eventually tracked it to the vent at the base of the refrigerator.  I proceeded to slide the refrigerator from the wall and observed a flickering light emanating from the rear bottom of the unit which I quickly realized was a fire.
The fire went out on its own.  I unplugged the unit and noticed that the device which connects directly to the compressor had been burned and the resulting smell was pretty bad.

I punched the model number of the unit in to Sears Parts Direct to identify the burned components.  Sears Link:  http://www.searspartsdirect.com/partsdirect/part-model/Frigidaire-Parts/Refrigerator-Parts/Model-FRS6HR5HB1/1428/0165000/R0702017/00006?blt=06&prst=0&shdMod=FRS6HR5HB1

The parts are a part of the "System" assembly and those which caught fire appear to be:
30: Starter, PART NUMBER: 241707701
55: Capacitor, PART NUMBER: 218909913, Substitution: 5304464438
32: Clamp, PART NUMBER: 241650901

A google search revealed that this type of malfunction, a "compressor relay fire", is not uncommon with refrigerators, though I found no existing fire reports for this model online.  I visited the Frigidaire's website and found no recalls for this product.

I have a licensed technician coming to investigate the issue, but I am greatly concerned about the overall safety of this product and its performance even if the faulty parts are replaced.  Had I not been present during the malfunction, a very damaging fire would likely have resulted.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, but there was no injury or death, and the fire extinguished on its own.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting five burner gas range that he and his family have noticed a safety problem with regarding the knobs that turn the burners on.

He states that when reaching to the microwave that is over the burners the knobs are very easily turned by the clothing around their stomach area.

One time the burners were lit and on for 15 minutes before being noticed.
The knobs turn enough to start the gas but not enough to ignite the burner with 95% of the time the middle burner being the one that is turned.
The left back burner is also one that occasionally becomes turned on by the clothing catching on it.
He states that the knobs turn so easily that you don't realize that it is being turned. About  1/8 inch or less press defeats lock on valve.

Many times since the person at the microwave doesn't notice that the knob on the gas range has turned, the kitchen becomes filled with gas before they smell it.

As soon as the knob is touched/turned whether accidently or on purpose the first setting is at high.

He is reporting as a safety issue due to the ease that this knob is turned and the danger of asphyxiation or explosion if gas is not detected quickly enough.

Caller would ask that the manufacturer either redesign the knob so that it cannot so easily become turned possibly by changing the knob so that it has to be pushed in before it comes on both for this particular reported issue as well as he has noted that a baby could also turn the knobs on very easily.

Caller would also ask to be kept in the loop with any correspondence or change. 

Part of knob catches clothes or body.  Rounder knob or more positive lock on valve needed.  Previous range knobs were rounded and never caught clothes or got turned on.
justification: The incident involves a safety hazard with gas leakage, posing risks of asphyxiation or explosion, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: The consumer says when someone leans on the stove, the burners will ignite.  Also, the burners turn on by themselves.  She says the other day, her son leaned up against the stove and the front and the back burner both lit up and almost caught her son's shirt on fire.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said that they do not have a safety division.  They have offered no assistance.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation where burners ignite unexpectedly, nearly causing a fire. No injury occurred, but the risk is significant.

incident_description:
A number of weeks ago I brewed a pot of coffee in my Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffeemaker. After starting the process I left the kitchen and went to another room. A short while later I heard a popping and crackling sound from the kitchen area. I went to investigate and I saw smoke coming from the coffeemaker and I smelled burning plastic. I unplugged the coffeemaker.
I called the Cuisinart customer service number and was told that the computers were down and that I could not be helped. I called the next day and was told that the computer was only processing new sales orders, not service orders. I waited several days and called again. This time I was told that the coffeemaker would be replaced. I was given a service order number and instructed to cut the electrical cord from the appliance and mail it in upon receipt of my replacement.
Weeks went by and I received no replacement unit. I called the Cuisinart customer service number and inquired about my replacement, which they explained had not yet been shipped. It's now a week later and I still don't have my replacement.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning plastic from the coffeemaker but no injury occurred, and similar incidents are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description: My Kenmore dishwasher was in operation, when it began making a clicking and buzzing sound. Soon after black smoke started pouring out of the control pannel. I quickly flipped the main switch to the dishwasher off. The smoke smelled terrible like electric fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an electrical smell but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On Saturday April 28, I baked some chicken in my oven.  I turned the oven off  but left the pan of chicken in the oven. I went outside and came back into the house about 30 min. later only to find my the oven broiler operating on an extremely high temperature and burning  the chicken and the foil and scorching the glass baking dish. When I opened the oven all of the smoke detectors went off in the lower level of the house   The oven display did not indicate that the oven was on and the only way to turn the oven off was to unplug it.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burned chicken and scorched dish) and activated smoke detectors, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On April 28th, I put my Kenmore gas stove/oven into clean mode.  I placed the fan above the stove on high and went to the other room.  I returned approximately 35-40 minutes later and noticed a burning odor.  I went to touch the control panel and before I could I noticed the area was incredibly hot.  I grabbed a damp cloth and tried to turn it off, but the panel even with the cloth was too hot.  Through the plastic piece one could see the metal fingers of the control board discoloring the plastic.  Since no manual controls were available and the control panel was too hot, went to the basement and turned the kitchen breaker off.  Upon cooling, i turned it back on and the panel was beeping with an F11 code.  The control panel and oven are unusable.  Given the seriousness of the panel damage, I deem this to be a serious safety hazard and it should be investigated.

I contacted Sears today and after numerous (unhelpful operators) I was informed it was manufactured by Frigidaire.  Given the lack of helpfulness to even listen to my safety concern, I find no alternative, but to let the CPSC do it.  

Note:  this appliance was with the house when we moved in, but after much research I was able to determine its origin from the 2008-9 timeframe.

Model 790.78782402
Serial VF51017885
justification: The incident involved a serious safety hazard with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore range/stove model number 79094339700. Left the burner comes on and stays on high no matter how it is set and will not turn off. Exact same problem noted in recall of Kenmore Elite series, but this model is not part of the recall. Extreme fire hazard. This seems to be a problem with many Kenmore and Frigidaire brand ranges recommend avoiding all until Kenmore stands up and does the right thing and issues recall for all defective units. Do a [REDACTED] search about this issue before you buy any Kenmore range or stove.
justification: The description indicates a malfunction that poses an extreme fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
The oven/range was not in use when the consumer heard a loud explosion. The consumer  noticed the outer glass from the oven door had exploded and shattered all over the kitchen floor.

The glass shards ranged in sizes from a quarter inch and a inch long. There was also  insulation that came out of the are that the glass exploded from. 

The consumer states that she has not used the oven/range in about a week. She also states that she was not near the kitchen when the incident occurred.

The consumer contacted the retailer/firm on 4/16/2012 & 4/17/2012 where she was advised to pay for a technician to come out.  The consumer was also advised that there was not recall involving her model number.  

The consumer declined in scheduling a technician to come out to the home. She states that she does not feel like she should be required to pay out of pocket.

The consumer saw a new segment where the manufacturer had received several reports of the same incident occurring to other consumers but they are not willing to offer any assistance.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the oven door glass causing damage but no injuries, and similar incidents have been reported by other consumers.

incident_description: Near the beginning of the wash cycle, our Kenmore dishwasher made a "pop" sound and smoke starting coming from the door.  None of the buttons worked and opening the door did not stop the cycle.  Flames appeared before cutting power at the circuit breaker stop the dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Closed door and the exterior glass door shattered.
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered glass door) but no reported injuries.

incident_description: On 04/26/2012 the outside glass on my Kenmore Range Oven door just exploded. Tiny pieces of glass were shot everywhere. Thankfully no one was near the oven and it had NOT been used that day. First, I spoke with [REDACTED] from the Repairs Dept. who told me this can happen but "unfortunately there is no recall" because "some people" didn't have the problem. He said because the oven is a few months over warranty the only thing I can do is buy another warranty agreement for $240 to get it fixed. I then googled "Kenmore oven door shattered" and was shocked at the pages of posts  that come up with complaints of people who had the same problem Some had pictures of the damage which looked exactly like ours . There was even a news station in Rhode Island that broadcasted a story titled "Kenmore keeps News 4 viewers in the dark on exploding oven doors". I printed out these articles and brought the stack into my local Sears, where I purchased the oven, to show the manager. I tried to explain to him this needs to be replaced and fixed because I can't take the chance of this happening again, this time injuring my three year old daughter who likes watching her cookies bake. The manager, [REDACTED], told me he had no power to do anything and just put me on the phone with [REDACTED], an employee with the National Customer Relations Dept. She listened to my concerns then just kept reading the warranty agreement over and over. [REDACTED] said she would fill out a product safety form and told me there is no one else I can call. This is a serious defect that can disfigure or seriously injure someone if not fixed and Sears just won't address it.
justification: The incident caused a shattered glass door, but thankfully no one was near the oven, so there was no injury.

incident_description: My husband took our 9x13 pyrex baking dish from the oven and placed it on top of the stove, to add [REDACTED] sauce, when it violently exploded into millions of shards. Luckily he was not seriously injured but, it did however damage my stove and made one heck of a mess which took 3 hours to clean.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion causing property damage and a significant mess, but no serious injury was reported.

incident_description:
I would like to report that a glass Pyrex dish in which I was baking fish at 350 degrees suddenly exploded in the oven for no reason after 15 minutes into the bake cycle.  The dish was not subjected to temperature changes, staying at a constant 350, nor was it damaged/cracked in any way. Had I opened the oven to check the bake progress at the time this dish exploded, I may have been pulling shards of glass out of my face.

The sides of the baking dish completely separated from the bottom and small shards of glass were sent airborne across the entire oven.  I have photos of the resulting dish if required.  

As per the Consumer Reports investigation and recommendation, I am writing to you to report this incident.  As I empty my kitchen cabinets of any semblance of glass dishware made by Pyrex, I urge you to pull this dangerous product from the market.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding in the oven, which could have caused injury but did not in this case.

incident_description: The consumer says her husband turned on the oven to pre-heat.  He heard a noise and saw a bright fire behind the digital display.  He pushed the stop button and flames shot out of the back of the range.  She says that her circuit breaker box in her house blew up.  She contacted the manufacturer who is unwilling to provide any assistance in the matter.  They told her to call the retailer.  The retailer is telling her to call the manufacturer.  She says the unit was on just a few minutes before the incident occurred.  the unit is similar to the recall listed in Release # 09-333.  Her serial number falls outside of the range of the recall.
justification: The incident involved flames and a blown circuit breaker, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Elite dishwasher (model 665.17059400) - control panel apparently overheated and filled kitchen area with smoke and an electrical smell during a normal cycle.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an electrical smell but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but have been documented.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express her concerns about her under the counter dishwasher as the product began to smoke and nearly caused a fire in the consumerÃÂs home. The consumer stated that the product was on a normal cycle for nearly 45 minutes before smoke filled her kitchen. The consumer stated that the damage did not spread to her home but the unitÃÂs control board is burned and  the internal wires have melted. 

The consumer stopped the unit from smoking further as she turned off the unit at the circuit breaker and the smoking subsided. The consumer did not call her local fire department or her home insurance company. The consumer has not called the firm or the retailer.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and the damage was contained to the dishwasher.

incident_description: The consumer says the left front burner, will make an eletrical zapping noise.  The left front burner turns bright red to its highest and hottest power no matter what number the dial is turned to.  The dial is on low of #2 the burner will act as if the dial has been turned to high or #8.  It is a fire hazard and a major safety hazard to myself and young children.  Sometimes it will act as if it is working right on a number setting and in the middle of cooking the burner will suddently turn "red hot" as if it has been turned to  high.  Also the metal body on the top of the range around and between the burners will contract and expand as the range top gets hot.  The metal is very thin and not durable to hold its shape while cooking many things at once.  She sees the electrical light on the back of her stove reflecting on the ceramic.  The burner has had this problem for a couple of years.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told her the unit was not on recall.  She says the electrical buzzing noise occurs everytime the unit is turned on and off.  She also says the oven door handle has fallen off several times.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard and safety risk, especially with young children, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Purchased LG refrigerator model LFC25760SB in July 2006.  Didn't have any problems until a few months ago when the lights went out in the refrigerator.  At first we thought it was the bulb(s), but we tested them and they were fine.  As our warranty expired we decided to live without the lights since my husband figured it was a circuit problem and sometimes the lights would come on when we opened the door(s) and calling for and paying for a service call especially if it seemed to work at that particular time would be  a warrentless expense of a lot of money since we are seniors and live on a fixed income.  Now, after a couple of months the lights returned on and everything seemed fine.  Once in awhile they would go out when the door(s) opened.  Then today April 26, 2012, when we returned home from food shopping, I opened the doors to put the food away and the first thing was a strong electrical burning odor.  The inside of the refrigerator was warm, the lights were on and smoke was coming from the area around them.  My husband pushed in on the switch that depresses when the doors are closed and that did not shut the lights off.  My husband then proceeded to take down the plastic that was covering the light area, burned his hand, and then we got a pot holder and unscrewed the light bulbs.  If we had been gone another hour or so who knows what would have happened.  I am sure all my food would have had to be thrown out not to mention the melting of the top of the refrigerator or even worse an electrical fire that could have burned down my home!
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard and burned the husband's hand, indicating a level of injury.

incident_description:
My Emerson microwave oven - burned up. It filled the house with smoke and was very hot to the touch. 
There were no burn marks on the exterior. 
The microwave was not turned on at the time, only plugged in.
justification: The microwave burned up and filled the house with smoke, but there were no injuries or burn marks.

incident_description:
Caller purchased Electric Range at price of $1,300.00 on May 5th, 2010.

Caller, his wife and his two daughters were in the kitchen January 10, 2011 when with no warning, the glass exploded from the oven door.

He contacted the manufacturer who sent glass to his home on January 13th, 2011.
February 3rd, 2011, Retail Tech came, replaced glass in door then tried to sell extended warranty to caller.

March 5th, 2012 caller's wife was in the kitchen cooking dinner with oven oven set at 350 degrees when the glass again exploded out of oven door.

Consumer contacted retailer March 5th and 6th, 2012 who offered him a discount on replacement of glass at the rate of $100.00 off price of service call set for March 8th, 2012.

Caller does not believe that he should have to pay for this repair since this range is less than two years old.

Caller respectfully requests that due to age, circumstance and safety hazards that the manufacturer repair glass completely at their own expense instead of repeatedly trying to sell caller extended warranty which would still put expense with caller when he fully believes that there is an obvious defect.
justification: The glass exploding from the oven door is an incident that occurred twice without causing injury, but it poses a safety hazard.

incident_description:
Turned on the left front burner of range and it stays on (high). Had to turn off circuit breaker to range in order for burner to stay off. Don't know if this link to managemylife.com will help you. There were several others having the same problem.

http://www.managemylife.com/mmh/questions/253707-electric-slide-range-79046713605-burner-turn-unplug-wrong
justification: The burner staying on high poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. The issue appears to be a recurring problem based on similar reports.

incident_description:
I have a Viking Dishwasher Model # VDB 325SS that is only 2 years old and has major problems. First, it continued running all night long several times. Secondly, it wouldn't start three times because there was water in the pan. For 2 of those times, I had to let it sit for over a week until the water evaporated. The other time I called a repairman and encountered a $325 bill. He said that I had put too much soap in. However, I consulted the directions and discovered I had followed their guidelines. 

The same model of dishwashers that were made a year later have been recalled for a fire hazard. 
While this dishwasher was not subject to the recall, it is still faulty and probably dangerous. The condo developer where I live purchased the same dishwashers and multiple people have experienced the same problems. Some have had their units catch on fire, too.

This model has additional problems beyond the fire hazard that has been the subject of recall and it should be looked into further.
justification: The dishwasher has caused operational issues and potential fire hazards, but no injuries or deaths are reported in the description.

incident_description: We have a GE Monogram dishwasher.  Last night while falling asleep my husband smelled something burning.  We went all over the house and realized it was coming from the kitchen as there was smoke.  We then heard a weird noise and I realized it was from the dishwasher that I had turned on before we went up to bed.  When I opened the dishwasher, tons of smoke came out and there were a lot of sparks and it looked like there was a fire.  My husband called the fire department.  When they came they took the front panel off the door, and saw that the control panel had burned up.  They said if we had not stopped it in time, the cabinet and then kitchen would have caught on fire.  The stench in our house last night and still this morning (as I am writing this) is terrible.  It smells like plastic burning.  I have opened up windows to try and air out the house and any smoke that may be left.  I called GE appliance repair and then are sending a repairman out tomorrow, April 27, to take a look at it.  They also sent me to a Consumer Relations person who has opened up a case.  My husband just saw on your site that there have been incidents of a fire with the model of our dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and sparks, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
We were sleeping.  The cooktop had a cookie sheet with a silicon baking pad on it and about a half dozen cookies.  The right back burner turned on automatically, scorching the pan and pad and burning the cookies.  The house filled with dense smoke and now the smoke odor is in everything.  Frigidaire is sending us paperwork to file a smoke damage claim.  They will not fix the range because it is out of warranty (unless I pay for an extended warranty).

This is a very dangerous range.  We are turning off the electrical circuit until we can get it replaced or repaired.
justification: The incident caused property damage (smoke damage) and posed a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Electric coffee maker failure with overheating and smoking. Heard a "sizzle and popping" sound from the kitchen and found the coffee maker emitting white acrid smelling smoke from the burner plate and rear power cord port.   The clock was blank and the LED light was out. The pot had been on after making the morning coffee and was on the warm cycle.  I recorded a short video and unplugged the appliance.  Inaction would likely have resulted in a meltdown or fire.
justification: The coffee maker overheated and emitted smoke, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED] and I'm reporting this on behalf of my mother in law (her address is listed in this report), [REDACTED]. According to [REDACTED] the following is a summary of what happened at her home on April 4, 2012:

About 2:45pm, my daughter [REDACTED] and I were home. She was sitting at the kitchen table and I was in the family room. All of a sudden all three of the smoke detectors in our home went off. As I jumped up to see what was making the detectors go off, my daughter turned to the kitchen and at the same time, we both saw flames coming out of the back of the Brew Station. My daughter instinctively yelled fire and I ran to the kitchen to help put the flames out. I unplugged it quickly (it was plugged in but was not in use/not turned on at the time) we struggled to get the flames out because they were coming out of the back of the unit, near the top rather than the bottom where the cord is at. We managed to get the Brew Station into the sink so we could douse more water on it to extinguish the flames entirely. It took a minute to get the flames out but we did. We took the Brew Station out to the garage in an attempt to remove the smoke and charred smell. The smell lingered in the house for some time afterward. As can be seen by the pictures of the unit, the fire clearly came from within the unit and near the top of the backside of the unit. Had we not been home, our kitchen and house would have clearly caught on fire. The unit is clearly ruined and has extensive damage - far more than ever imagined. I certainly hope this has not ever happened to anyone else and am now very concerned that the product was not safe to begin with. To think of what may have happened had we not been home to extinguish the fire so quickly, clearly we would have had far worse fire/smoke damage. I am very disappointed with this product. Coffee makers are likely one kitchen product which is used most frequently in a home.
justification: The incident involved a fire from a coffee maker, which was extinguished without injury, but could have caused significant damage if not addressed.

incident_description:
On February 17, 2012, my wife was baking a cake in a Whirlpool 24" Built-in Oven, Model Number: RBS245PDB10, Serial Number: XK5101063, Purchased at Sears in Auburn, Massachusetts on January 23, 2001. About 30 minutes into the cooking cycle, my wife, who was in the kitchen, heard the oven click and lock the door into the auto clean cycle, without my wife touching anything. The temperature in the oven kept rising and the cake caught fire. The fire department pulled the oven fuse and forced the oven door open to remove the smoking cake pan. There was no physical damage to my home other than the odor of smoke for a few days.
I removed and discarded the old oven and replaced it with a new [REDACTED] builtin unit.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injuries or physical damage to the home, only smoke odor.

incident_description: On April 24, 2012, we turned our dishwasher on using the light wash cycle.  It began the cycle and then stopped.  Our circuit breaker had flipped off.  We reset the circuit breaker and then pushed light wash on the dishwasher again.  This time it went on and then we saw black smoke coming out of the top of the washer.  The dishwasher was purchased in 2002 and is a Maytag model MDB7100AWBand serial number 27211605AA.
justification: The incident involved smoke from the dishwasher but no injury or death occurred, and such electrical faults are uncommon.

incident_description: I bought a Kenmore electric glass top stove 790.95379802, purchased in 8/2010. The oven was hot yesterday morning after I used it the night before. The controls were off.  I had a repairman inspect today and he said it was working fine. He did smell a burnt odor at the control panel. he said maybe a relay was working erratically in the control panel/clock. Now I am afraid to use the stove.
justification: The stove exhibited abnormal behavior but no injury occurred, and a repairman found no immediate danger, though a burnt odor was noted.

incident_description: power cord is stripping and fraying due to cord rewind mechanism causing shock hazard
justification: The fraying power cord poses a shock hazard, which could lead to an incident but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: On Electrical Range, Frigidaire Range/Oven (Model FEFL79DCD, Serial Number VF51445616), the right back range heating unit does not stay off.  I can turn it on, and then turn it off.  After a hour or so, the electrical heater begins to heat up.  The burner heat "on" light is off, but the burner is hot.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating unit that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had just removed the Pyrex pan from the oven when it exploded.  She had baked in it for 20 minutes at 350 degrees in a preheated oven.  When placed on the counter top, it exploded into several pieces.  

The consumer received injury which was inflected by a piece of chard glass that projected through her leather shoe into her 4th left toe.  She went to the Mount Graham Emergency center where she received 7 stitches.  She was treated and sent home for followup.

The consumer is concerned that this dish is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The consumer suffered an injury requiring medical attention (stitches), but no death occurred. The incident appears uncommon based on the description.

incident_description:
On March 22, 2012, I used a potholder, purchased at Publix in Boca Raton some years ago, to remove a hot broiler pan from the oven, set the pan on top of the stove and put the potholder on the counter top. I turned to the sink opposite for a moment and turned back to find the potholder in flames. I smothered the fire and found a burn on the white formica counter top.

incident_description:
My husband and I purchased $5000.00 worth of Kitchen Aid appliances from Carl's Appliance in Grand Blanc, Michigan, in January, 2009. One of these appliances was a range, model #KERS807SSS02, serial #XW4604115.
Since I like to use the self cleaning feature as seldom as possible, I am careful to wipe up spills and keep the oven as clean as possible. As a result, I used the self cleaning feature for the first time in September, 2011, and the oven was still only lightly soiled. I selected the three hour cleaning cycle. An hour and a half into the cleaning process, the control panel went out, and the oven door would not open even after cool down.
My husband called Kitchen Aid and was told to call a repair service. The repairman said that the problem was due to a defective sensor, and an open TCO. After the repairman was here, my husband went online to a KitchenAid trouble shooting site and found dozens of complaints regarding exactly the same issue. We also found that a class action suit has been filed against KitchenAid in California regarding this problem. It is obvious that Whirlpool Corporation has an issue with KitchenAid ranges which is not being addressed. The range was repaired today for $305.52. Based on the fact that there have been so many other KitchenAid owners who have experienced exactly the same problem, we believe that Whirlpool should cover the entire cost of this repair., irregardless of the fact that the range is out of warranty. We have been loyal Whirlpool customers for over forty years, and would like to continue believing that the Whirlpool name is one we can trust.
Further, if this situation is not resolved to our satisfaction, we will be filing a complaint with the State of Michigan Attorney General's office, Consumer Protection Division.
A week after the range was repaired; I tried the self clean feature to ensure that it was working. Again, the oven shut down and the door locked half way through the cleaning cycle. The repairman returned and got the oven working, and 1 decided not to try the self clean feature again. 
February 14, water boiled over onto the glass cook top and shorted out parts of the control panel. The oven would not heat, although the panel lit up appropriately, and the oven light would not turn off. I have been told by an electrician that the short could have caused a fire, or resulted in a severe shock. I do not know whether this incident was due to the repairman disturbing the seal when he had the front panel off several times to repair the range, or if was the result of poor design on Whirpool's part. Liquids should never be able to leak into the wiring of a properly sealed cook top as this creates a dangerous situation.
The repairman came on February 16, and we were told that this repair would cost $770.00. So far, we have put $259.00 into a range that was only two and a half years old when the repairs began. If we decide to have the range repaired, we will have spent $1029.00 in repairs on a three year old range which we paid $1459.00 for! Further, I will be afraid to use the self clean feature, or have a boil over on the cook top for fear of another repair bill. 
I am deeply disappointed with Whirlpool, a company I have respected for years. I believe that this range should be replaced free of charge due to the number and cost of the failures of this product to perform as expected. Since I consider this latest incident a safety issue, 1 am also sending a copy of this letter to the State's Attorney General's office, Consumer Protection Division. Please feel free to contact us with any questions at [REDACTED], or cell phone # [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involves repeated appliance malfunctions and potential safety hazards (short circuit, fire risk), but no actual injury or death occurred.

I immediately unplugged the dishwasher.  Although it didn't smell like it, I thought that possibly some dry powder soap had spilled on to the heating element.  I cleaned everything and when I tried again, the same problem occurred. My roommate also examined the inside of the dishwasher and everything seemed fine.  We used the dishwasher several times without incident and I thought that the problem was fixed.  Last night I used the dishwasher as normal and the smoke came back AGAIN.  Again, I promptly unplugged the unit, opened all of my windows, and turned on all of my fans to rid my house of that awful burning smell.  I am afraid to use the dishwasher again.
justification: The incident involves smoke and a burning smell from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the pyrex dish was removed from the oven at 350 degree temperature, it was placed on the countertop which was neither hot or cold, it immediately exploded shattering glass peices all over the countertop and the floor, which contaminated other foods that were close by which had to be discarded.  The shards were also on the floor and some of his relatives got stuck in their feet.  No medical attention was needed.

Consumer stated that the glass dish shattered about 7 ft across the floor, so that there were peices in numerous places.

11/2011 Consumer spouse contacted the retailer and reported the incident.

Consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer is concerned that this glass dish is a safety hazad and should be taken off the market.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering and causing minor injuries (feet stuck with shards), though no medical attention was needed, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described scenario and consumer concern.

incident_description: My 4 cup Mr. Coffee coffeemaker spontaneously turned itself on in the kitchen with no one anywhere near it. It hadn't been used in over 3 weeks and there had not been anyone in the room for over 3 hours. It was making a snapping sound and when I unplugged it from the wall, the entire unit was extremely hot. I live alone, so there was no one who could have accidently bumped it or hit the on button.
justification: The coffeemaker turned on spontaneously and overheated, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Plastic handle broke away from glass lid while crock pot was in use. Lid fell into stoneware crock, causing hot food to splatter on walls, floor, and onto my skin and clothes. I was burned by the metal edge of the lid as it fell, and also burned by the hot food.
justification: The incident resulted in burns from both the metal edge and hot food, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Self Cleaning Smooth Top Oven Model Number 79092411102, Serial Number VF23527102.  I was baking cupcakes and the element on the bottom got way too hot, burned the cupcakes and when I tried to shut it off - It shut off then 10 minutes later the oven was beeping and an error message of F1 appeared on the screen. The element on the bottom was on when I had already turned it off.  The element was SUPER HOT!  I turned the oven off again, I went to pick my daughter up from school and when I came home the oven was searing hot but no beeping and no indication that the oven was on and NO ERROR MESSAGE!  I pulled the oven from the wall and unplugged it thinking that I just had to reset something and it would be ok.  (The oven was so hot that when I pulled it from the wall I burned my arm on the metal of the oven. I waited four hours and plugged it back in - it was fine for about 10 minutes then it heated (within 30-40 seconds the oven was so hot I could not put my hand in the oven) I again, unplugged the oven I waited 26 hours and plugged it back in.  AGAIN it heated up.  I am afraid for my family and pets.  This a very serious problem.  What if someone had this plugged in and went to sleep, would they wake up?
justification: The oven malfunction caused a burn injury and poses a continuous fire hazard, indicating a high severity and likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: During the self-cleaning cycle of my Kenmore Elite wall oven (model 790.48023801) the oven door glass window shattered.  No one was near the oven at the time.
justification: The oven door glass shattered during a self-cleaning cycle, but no one was near the oven, so there was no injury.

incident_description: We cooked dinner using our Kenmore electric range which is less than a month old. The oven was off and cooling, and we were in the dining room eating dinner. We heard a noise from the kitchen, so we went to see what it was. The inside glass pane of the oven door had splintered into hundreds of cracks and the middle part exploded out. This stove was less than a month old and has been used a couple of times.
justification: The oven glass shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury. Such failures in new appliances are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description:
Panasonic Model NN-SD698S / SD688S

This microwave is 2 years old.
The microwave was not used on Friday April 13th 2012.  At approximately 10PM on the 13th a slight smell of hot or burning electronics was noticed in the kitchen.  A quiick investigation did not find any abnormalities, the microwave was not specifically inspected but the trash can next to the microwave was closely investigated.  The smell was not noticed on Saturday April 14th.  However, at approximately 5PM on the 14th the microwave was used warm some plates (set on intensity of 10 for about 2 minutes). The microwave became very very hot and shut down.  The external case was too hot to touch, particularly on the right side and top.  After cooling down the unit still works intermittently.
justification: The microwave overheated and became too hot to touch, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
We purchased an LG LFC25760SB french door refrigerator in May of 2007.  This past Friday (April 13, 2012) my wife opened the door and noticed the cream cheese container in the top door was very warm.  She also noticed a burning smell.  Upon further inspection, we noticed that the entire housing for the light which is mounted to the ceiling had started melting, particularly through the front screw holes and was hanging from the ceiling.  The unit has an alarm which beeps (annoyingly) to alert you if the door is opened, but this alert was not sounding so I know the door was closed, but apparently (after doing some research) the light remains on, causing heat build-up to occur.

We had been planning to leave on vacation that day and she just happened to go into the refrigerator to make a quick bite to eat before we left.  I can only imagine what would have happened had we left without checking it and left the refrigerator in this state.

We unplugged it and ordered a new (Non-LG) refrigerator which will be delivered tomorrow.  After doing some research, it appears that there is actually a class-action lawsuit for the same exact model as mine except the last two designators are SW, not SB.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator malfunction causing a burning smell and melting parts, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a GE Spacemaker XL1800. It turns on every time the door is opened.  This is extremely unsafe.  I can't believe there isn't any redundancy to prevent this from happening.  I called GE thinking this was so unsafe they would simply replace it. They told me it would cost $80 to have someone look at it and if the quote was too expensive they would give me a $100 rebate towards a new one.  When I told them I'm not financially able to do this right now they told me to call back when I had money.  Pretty ironic the phone number is 1-800-GE CARES.
justification: The microwave turning on when the door is opened is a safety hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Just sitting here visiting with a neighbor and all of a sudden this buzzing sound started ... went to the kitchen to find the toaster buzzing! The egg maker was HOT ... I unplugged it and did an internet search to find similar results .... ! YIKES ... I would hate to think if we weren't hope. This happened at about 7:30 on April 15, 2012.


http://www.fixya.com/support/t2516135-paula_deen_toaster_egg_poacher_caught

incident_description: Frigidaire cook top burner does not always turn off when knob is turned to off position, and also does not maintain temperature selected. Burner will go to high on its own.
justification: The cook top burner malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: My Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker started to make a crackling sound about 10 minutes after I brewed a small pot.  The coffee was boiling and there was a strong electrical burning smell.  The maker was extremely hot.  I unplugged it immediately.  I hate to think what could have occured if I wasn't in the kitchen when this started.
justification: The coffee maker exhibited dangerous electrical behavior but was unplugged before injury occurred, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
our cusinart coffeemaker DCC-1200 started making popping noises this morning. When I went to investigate, the coffee maker was much hotter than normal and I then smelled smoke coming from the bottom. I unplugged the unit immediately and took it outside, where it continued to smoke for many minutes longer.

Thank goodness I was home and awake as I'm afraid it could have caused a house fire. It was scary and the smell (acrid, plastic, awful) was bad.

incident_description: We have a Bosch above stove microwave oven in our kitchen.  When we use the microwave oven after boiling water on the stove, there is a very loud popping noise and a very visible blue flash of light inside the unit.  This problem continues to get worse.
justification: The incident involves a loud popping noise and visible blue flash, indicating a malfunction, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I have a Tassimo Bosch coffee maker TAS4511 UC/01  FD 8809   Serial # 1017286
The top disc exploded and sprayed hot water and hot steam on my wife hitting her on her fingers and hands.  
About two months ago I contacted the company and was told they would send me a new part but
I never received it.  Now I saw there is a recall on the product.  I called again and they are sending out a new part.
justification: The incident caused injury (hot water and steam burns on fingers and hands), and while the recall suggests a known issue, the likelihood of recurrence is reduced by the company's response to replace the part.

incident_description: My mixer suddenly starting turning on when you plug it in even though the on/off switch is in the off position. Fortunately My hands were clear of the beaters so I didn't get hurt but it is obviously unsafe. I have tried several times to wiggle the switch and such to make sure that it was fully in the off position but it continues to mix even though it is firmly in the off position. The only way to turn it off is to unplug it.
justification: The mixer turns on unexpectedly but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The issue persists despite attempts to correct it, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
The electronic control panel on my Sears Kenmore (made by whirlpool) dishwasher caught on fire. We had ran our dishwasher in the middle of the night while we were sleeping.  The next morning, we had smelled a strong plastic burining smell in our house. At the time, we couldn't determine where the smell was comming from.  But it was obvious and smelled the strongest comming from our kitchen/family room area.  Later that day, when we went to use the diswaher again, it would not turn on.  We called Sears to schedule a service call.  When the service technician arrived a few days later.  He immdeiatley took the control panel apart.  The technician advised we had a fire inside the comparment that houses the control panel.  He showed the compartment to me and the area had black soot stains and had melted palstic.  He advised I would need a new control pannel, wiring harness and various misc parts and provided a $700 repair estimate.

Sears Kenmore
Model = 66515934000
Serial = FL5005632
Purchased = 2002 (appliance is 10yrs old)
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher's control panel but resulted in no injuries, and such events are unlikely given the appliance's age and condition.

incident_description: On April 11, 2012 the door handle broke free from one side of the heated oven.  the 2 screws are all that hold the outer decorative glass panel in place at the top.  As the hot door was attempted to be opened the decorative glass broke, shattering into a pile of tempered glass pieces.  The model number is 790.48839900 purchased in 2010.
justification: The incident involved a broken oven door handle and shattered glass, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:

Unit starts on its own !   No telling for how long.  Have been present twice when this has occurred.  To make it STOP I have to literally UNPLUG it from the wall.  Glad I was home to do so!!  finding recalls for units made the same year 2001 but this one is NOT listed on whirlpool site.
justification: The microwave starts on its own, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description: We bought this range and the slightest brush against the cooktop knobs turns them on so that the gas releases.  We have had it happen several times but were here and noticed right away.  Yesterday, my Husband came home and the whole house was filled with gas!  We called Whirlpool and they sent someone out but they couldn't do anything since techncally it is not broken but       "functioning properly".  They did agree it is a design flaw and suggested that we get safety locks.  Not really what I had in mind when I bought a streamlined stove.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her coffee & espresso maker hasnÃÂt been working properly since she purchased it.  The consumer turned on the coffee maker and she managed to make the coffee with no interruptions. Then the consumer tried to steam milk and it would not steam the milk. She turned off the coffee maker and waited for 10 minutes until it was cool enough to remove the coffee holder.  Pressure had build up behind the coffee holder causing it to emit a loud noise and it exploded causing coffee to spill everywhere. 

The consumer tried to use the machine again following the instructions on the manual and with the help of a mechanic. She waited for 20 minutes this time giving it a longer period of time to cool down. When she tried to remove the coffee holder the same incident happened. 

The consumer contacted the manufacture and they stated that the product was not working properly because she was using filter water. The representative informed her that she needs to use bottle water instead of filter water. She informed the Consumer that the minerals in the water are needed for the machine to work properly. 

While on the phone with the representative from the manufacture she tried to use the machine again with bottle water.  When she plugged the machine it turned on by itself, the representative indicated that it should not turn on when she by itself.  The representative informed the consumer that she would provide her with a $10 discount to purchase a new coffee maker and the consumer declined the offer. 

After 10 minutes of hanging up the call with the representative the consumer decided that she would no longer used the machine and proceeded to clean it realizing it was still extremely hot. The consumer burnt the palm of her left hand.  She treated the burn by placing ice on it.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the consumer's hand, which requires treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue recurred multiple times under similar conditions.

incident_description: At 3:00 a.m. on Easter morning, I awoke to the smoke alarm going off.  The house was filled with smoke, so I followed it into the kitchen and saw flames through the crack on the door of my dishwasher.  I unplugged it and opened the door.  Flames shot up to and beyond the top rack.  Almost all of the door on the inside was melted and my dishes were ruined.  I immediately extinguished the flames and opened the house to get rid of the horrible smoke.  Water was all over my floor.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I was pre-heating my oven to bake a frozen pizza. At about 400 degrees, I became aware of a loud crackling sound coming from the oven and opened the oven door to find an open flame and the element sparking and melting. It looked like an arc welder inside the oven. I turned it off and closed the oven door. The element continued to spark and burn, so I cut the circuit, dragged out the unit and unplugged it. 

There is a large hole in the element, where it melted through. I hate to think what would have happened if the pizza had been in the oven.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous electrical malfunction in the oven, but no injury occurred as the situation was promptly controlled.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his microwave turned self on and caught fire in the middle of the night (sometime between 11:00PM March 8th, 2012 and 3:30AM March 9th, 2012 causing cabinets to burn, etc.

Caller awoke to the smell of smoke and of burnt bread.  (He normally stores his bread in the microwave and there was a loaf in the microwave at that time.
He and his wife had been sleeping for approximately five hours.
His 22yr old son was also home, but sleeps downstairs, his parents woke him.
The house was full of smoke, no flames were coming from the microwave and caller could not distinguish where the smoke was coming out from the microwave.
One cabinet door damaged, microwave destroyed and callers may have suffered possible lung injury.

They opened all windows and doors to let smoke out, then unplugged the microwave and took it to the garage where it sits waiting for manufacturer to come look at it Tuesday, March13th, 2012.

Caller would like to have the microwave replaced by the manufacturer, his cabinet repaired and would like a satisfactory explanation
justification: The incident caused possible lung injury due to smoke inhalation, and the microwave fire resulted in property damage.

incident_description: Frigidair smooth top range turned itself on multiple times and could not be turned off. The problem seems to occur when steam from cooking or baking penetrates the control panel. The model has been recalled although I recieved no information from the manufacturer. I registered on their website for the recall but had no response for a month untill I called the recall hotline.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning appliance that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire kitchen range: Model Number LGEF3043KFC; Serial Number VF0456082; was used in the self cleaning mode for the first after owing it for almost one year.

The range got so hot and seamed not to seal properly. The heat escaping from the top edge of the door melted the adjacent cabinet door fronts and an adjacent cabinet door. We smelled something like plastic burning and saw vapor coming from the cabinets. The range was shut off and the cabinets opened to avoid a fire.

Frigidaire refuses to acknowledge this happened and wants the defected part back. Lowe's, where the range was purchased was informed and replaced the range with an new one of a different make.

They saw the letters I relieved from Frigidaire and are asking for a 'RO'.

All I want is for them to pay for the cost I incurred. They refuse to pay for the 'alleged incident.'

I now feel this range is defective and they do not want to acknowledge it.
justification: The incident involved heat damage to cabinets and a burning smell, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My wife turned the oven on to heat it up for cooking and after a few minutes we heard a loud pop and smoke came from the under side of the control panel and it smelled like electrical fire.  It tripped the breaker when this happened.  We were in the kitchen when it happened.  We called a repair service who came and checked the unit and determined that the circuit board has shorted out and informed us of recalls on this product.  After calling the recall number they informed me that this was not covered by the recall but they would send the "kit" to fix the problem that is covered under the recall but were not liable for the problem we are having with their product.
justification: The incident involved an electrical malfunction and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Caller was sitting in another room from her kitchen March 13, 2012 around 1:45PM Central Time when she heard a loud noise, she got up thinking that a dish or something had fallen in the kitchen or a window had been broken.

She went to the kitchen and found that the glass in her oven door had broken/exploded with glass being immediately in front of the range and also three feet away.

She had not used her oven at all today, she had used the two front burners earlier in the day.

She began cleaning the glass up so that her cats didn't get into it.

She would like to alert the public, she states that her range was purchased in 1995 and that she would expect many issues to arrive but not glass explosion. She believes she is fortunate not to have been in the kitchen at that time.Consumer Added:  I contacted Amana.  All they were interested in if I had insurance on the stove and said there was no recall on this product and if I wanted someone to come out to investigate it would cost me money for them to look at it. I said NO Thank You!
justification: The oven glass exploded without causing injury, but the incident could have been severe if someone was nearby.

incident_description:
Caller purchased wall oven in March 2009, she was using self cleaning option for the first time March 18, 2012.

Oven had been on for approximately one and one half hours when the inner glass exploded sending glass pieces four to five feet away from the oven with much of it remaining in oven.

There were no injuries.

Caller contacted manufacturer 03/18/2012, who inquired whether the product was on warranty, however warranty had expired.

Caller would sincerely request that CPSC investigate this product and that repair be completed at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass explosion with no injuries, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence based on the description.

incident_description: 3 apple corer slicers I've owned (2 same, 1 different) have broken causing substantially serious cuts to hands. The units break apart in center causing hands to come down quickly while sharp metal breaks through the fruit to the outside edges slicing hands on the downward cutting force.
justification: The description reports serious cuts to hands from broken apple corer slicers, indicating injury.

incident_description: On 09Apr2012, we were using our Yonanas machine for the second time.  We made the mixture per the instructions listed in the manual which came with the machine.  After the frozen banana mixture was made, we noticed white slivers in the bowl with the mixture.  I disassembled the machine to see what had happened and found that the bottom of the cone is heating up and melting the bottom edge of the cone.  As the cone rotates, plastic slivers are mixing with the frozen banana treat.  This could be a hazard due to swallowing slivers of plastic.  I have contacted the company to report the problem and asked for further guidance

incident_description:
1) Purchased Nonself-cleaning gas range
2) Cooked pizza at 425 degrees
3) Front panel and front sides reached 110 degrees
4) Could not touch these spots without pain

While Whirlpool offered nothing, Colders let us upgrade to self-cleaning range. This range has the "proper" seal around the oven door.

My complaint is resolved!

I am requesting that you check into all nonself-cleaning ranges manufactured by Whirlpool. My range came with a thin rubber seal around oven door. Heat was allowed to escape making this range a dangerous product around children!

incident_description:
When the dishwasher is used, it occasionally trips the circuit breaker.  This has happened 3 times so far.

Approximately 3 weeks ago, the consumer attempted to use the dishwasher, but it would not come on.  The consumer looked at the circuit breaker and noticed that one of the breakers had tripped.  The consumer turned the breaker back on and the dishwasher started immediately.  Another time, the machine stopped after 10 mins of a cycle.  The dishwasher only worked after the breaker was turned back.

The consumer has contacted the mfr. several times about this matter.  A service tech. was supposed to come out to her home on 3/16/12, but the tech. did not show up.  The appointment was scheduled between 1:00am - 5:00pm.  The consumer called the mfr. around 3:30pm to see if she was still on schedule and the rep. (name unknown) said that she was.  However, the tech. called the consumer at 3:45pm and told her that they could not make it and asked to reschedule.  The appointment was rescheduled for 3/19/12.  

(3/19/12)  The technician came out and inspected the dishwasher.  The tech. told the consumer that he had to replace the wire harness and he ordered the part.  The consumer is being charged $97.57 for the part, but the firm is covering the labor and the cost of the service call.

On 3/29/12, the technician cancelled the appt to fix the dishwasher and did not show up (the second) time.

The dishwasher is used once a week.


The consumer had the person who installed the dishwasher take a look at it.  He also has done other work around the consumer's home.  The installer examined the machine and showed the consumer that there was some black discoloration near the control panel of the machine.  It could actually be seen from the outside of the machine.

The consumer said that she believes that this is a potential safety hazard.
justification: The dishwasher trips the circuit breaker occasionally, indicating an electrical issue, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: handles broke off rival crock-pot model 3850. Spilled contents! Very dangerous!

incident_description: The consumer says he purchased the food processor for his wife.  She was making pizza dough.  After the pizza was baked he bit into it and bit on a chard of plastic the size of a penny.  He contacted the manufacturer for a replacement lid.  he was told by the manufacturer that the lid was discontinued.  Several days later a crown in his tooth came loose and eventually came out.  He went to the dentist who told him the tooth was cracked and needed to be pulled.  The consumer says a replacement tooth is over $4000.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer in October.  The manufacturer asked for pictures and copies of his dental bill which he sent them.  They asked for him to ship the product to them which the customer refused.  The consumer is in pain with a big hole in his tooth, as he does not have $4000.
justification: The consumer suffered a cracked tooth and had to have it pulled, which is a serious injury.

incident_description:
While warming up a plastic bowl filled with oatmeal for a minute the consumer noticed a burning odor. The consumer noticed that the plastic bowl inside of the microwave caught fire.

The consumer opened the microwave (which canceled the setting it was placed on) and removed the rotating tray the plastic bowl was sitting on. The consumer placed the rotating tray and bowl  in the sink and ran water on them.

The fire was extinguished by the water and the home was filled with the burning odor and smoke. While removing the rotating tray it brushed up against the consumerÃÂs right arm and caused minor burning.

The consumer contacted the firm on 3/5/2012 to advise them of the incident that she experienced. The representative that she spoke with (name not provided) advised her that someone from the safety department would be giving her call by 3/7/2012.

[REDACTED)] came out to the home on 3/6/2012 and cleaned the home to get rid of the smoke. The consumerÃÂs clothing were removed and taken to a drycleaners. 

The consumer went to see her Primary care Physician (name not provided) on 3/8/2012 after receiving the minor burn to her right arm.

The consumer then followed up with the firm on 3/8/2012 in reference to the bill from [REDACTED]. The consumer was advised that they (the firm) did not believe the appliance was at fault and would not pay.

Insurance covered the charges for my maintenance department, [REDACTED] Community Service and the consumer removed the microwave from above the range. She states that she has not used it since the incident occurred. The microwave is located on the floor of the consumerÃÂs kitchen.

The consumer placed the microwave above the range shortly after purchasing it in 2010.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn to the consumer's arm, which constitutes an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with proper microwave use.

incident_description: Screws from the housing of the mixer fell out and went into cake batter.  The cup cakes that were made ended up with 2 screws in them.  My sister bit into one of them and the remaining cupcakes were discarded
justification: The incident resulted in injury when the sister bit into a cupcake containing a screw, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) because such incidents are not common but can happen with equipment failure.

incident_description:
My dishwasher that is a GE Nautilus has been running on the heating cycle and not turning off.  It has happened a few times in the past, and I assumed my family didn't set the dishwasher correctly.  (although it had happened to me)  The dishwasher now has taken to skipping or going through the washing cycle then getting stuck on the heating cycle.  I put on my dishwasher the other day and I was working in the yard.  When I came into the kitchen two hours later it felt warm and the dishwasher was still on the heating cycle.  The counter top above the dishwasher was so hot I couldn't touch it.  I know there was a recall on two other GE dishwashers and I was wondering if there is an issue with mine.  The following are the MOD#  and ML#.  I would like an answer, the dishwasher was bought in Home Depot in Aug./Sept. 2006.

incident_description:
On 12 -30-2008 when using oven to my GE Proflile Gas Slide in Range allowing oven to preheat at 350 degrees about 20 minutes the bottom of oven door blew out with flames coming out, I open the oven's main door and flames were shooting out, I shut the door and switched the oven to off position but the flames were still coming out when opening the door. I then went to main gas shut it off there. I called the retailer Home Depot in Cadillac, MI. told them what happen they advised me to contact Ford Electronic and Appliance from Lake City, MI. that they were certified to work on GE Appliance, also that there were no GE company with technician in our area. Ford Electronic came to my home on 1~5-2009 to replaced a valve and ignitor.
On 8-04-2010 while baking a casserole on 350 degrees I opened the oven door and flames came out cinching my bangs ( hair on my fore head) my husband was in living room and heard the poof sound of extra gas that came out of oven, then came out to see what was going on. We turned off the oven. Called Ford Electronic from Lake City, MI. ,they came to our home 8-19-2010. Replace safety valve the same kind as before. On 12-25-2011 I put oven on at 350 degrees noticed there was no heat at all the oven would not work. The top of the gas range did work. Called Ford Electronic from Lake City, MI. they came to our home 12-27-2011 replaced ignitor the same kind as before. But the technician said there was an upgrade ignitor and hope that will work, the technician said that something was going on for them to upgrade there part. I contacted GE Corp. I was giving a number to call to their GE consumer Relations 1-800-386-1215 talked to 2 different people there on tel . She said the only thing they would do was offered to let me buy another stove at a percent off. I would pay about $963.18 for the stove and they would take my stove out and they would keep it. I ask to talk to a manger. I then was given to manager, we talk about everything, the parts replace new upgrade on parts. I could not afford new stove. incident_description: It was Monday March 26th late afternoon.  I turned my Frigidaire gas range on to cook brownies.  The oven was on approximately for an hour.  As the brownies cooked I worked in the kitchen.  Just after taking the brownies out, what I thought was the smoke detector started to sound.  After a few minutes I realized it was the carbon monoxide detector.  Eventually I decided I had no choice but to call the Lynn, MA fire department.  They told me to exit the house and wait on the porch for them.  When they arrived I walked back in the house with them and explained what had happened.  They immediately went to my furnace and cleared that.  They then took their CO detector to my oven and said get out.  They pushed me and my dog to fresh-air opened all my windows and doors and red tagged my oven.  My oven was tagged at 56ppm's.  This reading was approximately 40 minutes after the oven had been turned off.  I was light headed an experiencing headaches but waited until about 18 hours after the incident to go to the doctor.  The CO in my blood was higher than it should have been.  I spent a week trying to reach a repair person.   The stove is under warranty and I can only use their techs. None would call me back.  On Tuesday April 3rd Frigidaire sent a repair person to my home.  He said their was nothing wrong with the oven.  He did not check for CO.  I made him come back the next day and he refused to sign off on the red tag put their by the fire department.  Per order of the fire department he had to disconnect the stove.  I also contacted the gas company and they tested and found high levels of CO coming from the stove.  Frigidaire says my only option is to have one of their so called qualified techs to come to my home and talk to tech support and fix the problem, then if they can't fix it they will replace it.  He said he can't just replace on a phone call    I do not want this Doctor Kevorkian oven in my home.  It has been deemed condemned by the Fire Department and is marked dangerous equipment, do not operate.  This is a safety hazard and thank God I have carbon monoxide detectors, but what about the young pregnant mom cooking Thanksgiving dinner for six to eight hours.  Please help.  This is a Frigidaire oven model # FFGF3053LSE Serial # VFO4680542.  Please contact [REDACTED] at [REDACTED] if you have any further questions.  Thank You
justification: The incident resulted in injury (light-headedness, headaches, and elevated CO levels in blood) but no death. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but can happen with faulty equipment.
