incident_description:
On a Friday night, January 27, 2012,  prior to going to sleep, my wife smelled a very foul odor similar to burning plastic and other toxic chemicals coming from downstairs.  In the process of trying to figure out what was burning and where the odor was coming from, she forgot to open up all the doors and windows in the house and nearly collapsed.  Had I not arrived there just on time to do so, she would have collapsed and possibly died,  and this communication with anyone would have been completely different.    I was then able to quickly isolate the source of the problem -  it was coming from behind our Kenmore refrigerator purchased in 2001 - and quickly disconnected the refrigerator.   

Initially, I almost dismissed the problem as being a fluke, a technical malfunction due to the age of the refrigerator.  However, after going online to figure out the extent of the problem, I realized, to my surprise, that my wife and I were not alone and that this life-and-death issue is a problem that Whirlpool and Sears have been aware of for quite some time,  and that the age of the refrigerator had nothing to do with this malfunction since many such complaints had been lodged before from individuals who only had their refrigerator ranging anywhere from a couple of years or more.    Some even had their houses burned down as a result of that. 

Needless to say,  had we fallen asleep prior to detecting this burning odor, we would have died in our sleep without ever knowing we were living with a ticking time bomb waiting to explode.  There is absolutely no reason for Whirlpool not to alert the public about this problem since they come from all walks of life.  The catastrophic effect this could have on the elderly and,  particularly, young families with infants, babies, and young children who are most susceptible to being victimized by such callous criminal negligence on the part of Whilrpool is immeasurable. 

Here is a link to just one of the sites that I visited which exactly replicate the experience I have had: 


http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/kenmore-refrigerator-hoffman-estates-illinois-c48843.html

My first instinct was to contact an attorney who specializes in class-action lawsuits in order to bring some attention to this issue since this is much more than just a "customer service," limited warranty,  or "technical support" issue.  This is a LIFE AND DEATH ISSUE which must be addressed immediately so that more families do not fall victim to this cover-up.  It's no longer just about us.  We have children and grandchildren that we are also concerned about and so is the case with thousands, if not millions, of other families.  At the very least,  customers should be notified that such life and death issue exists instead of trying to bury it or sweep it under the rug.   

With respect to our own situation, and as corroborated by hundreds of complaints on the internet, the Sears service technician determined the following:


1.    The spontaneous combustion was due to a "burnt compressor start relay" - Part Number 8201786.      This defective part is obviously used in several refrigerator models manufactured by Whirlpool and is certainly not confined to a specific model or year.    

 WHY this is happening is critical for everyone to know.    Otherwise, asking to have the problem repaired will only postpone the inevitable and we may not turn out to be so lucky to be alive, or with a house intact, the next time around.  As well, fixing and selling the refrigerator to someone else would be criminal on our part since we are already aware of this life-threatening issue.  We do have a conscience and a sense of social responsibility, and so should Whirlpool.
   
How long is it going to take to fully resolve this matter once and for all?

After reviewing the hundreds of comments made online on these various sites, and seeing the run-around and frustration that these individuals had experienced, my first inclination was to contact the relevant media, consumer agencies, governmental and legal entities in order to bring some attention and light to this issue.   Something needs to be done about this.
justification: The incident involved a life-threatening situation that could have resulted in death, and similar incidents have been reported by others, indicating a possible risk.

incident_description: On 11 Apr 12 at approx. 1200p.m. Noticed an unusual bad odor coming from refrigerator. Upon further investigation, found lights in kenmore elite model# 795-77553600 stay on when doors are closed and switches engaged creating a possible fire hazard.  Light fixture housing and lens melted as did some food packaging  causing some spoilage of food products. Also found light sockets brown and charred.  Had to use towel to remove lights. Had we been asleep or if no one had been home (i.e. work, vacation) to rectify this problem in a timely manner, I believe the results would have been catastrophic.

Jan 25, 2012 He had a technician changed the fuse on the control panel which corrected the problem. He used the dishwasher for the next four days without any interruptions. The consumer stated that the dishwasher stopped working by itself; he did not have to turn it off. He stated that it took approximately 20 minutes for the smoke to disappear from his kitchen, but the burning smell linger in his home for almost a week. 

He did not see any fire and did not have to contact the fire department. The circuit board on the dishwasher had burnt itself out. There was no damage to his home and no one was injured. He contacted the manufacture who did not offer any assistance.

incident_description:
Kenmore Gas Range model # 79078632601 serial # VF420889 purchased Dec 24 2007
Gas leak noted on April 5 2012.   This condition rapidly (overnight) built up a heavy smelly gas odor in the kitchen, that was spotted. Luckily no explosion and it was shut down safely but it could have been a major explosion.  Gas company came and red tagged the appliance, after verifying there was no gas leak in the gas line elsewhere.  Sears service technician came and tested the appliance and claimed no problem on April 9. Gas company called back to reconnect, and they tested the appliance at my request on April 10, and pinpointed the existence of a noticeable gas leak and pointed to the broiler oven gas valve bypassing gas and leaking in the order of 0.3 cf.  Sears technician called back and tested nothing this time, they took the gas company at it word, and provided an estimate for replacing the gas valve, estimate of $464.92 (!!!), so we will purchase a replacement of this range, from Sears. 
I am concerned, given incompetence of Sears service and the possible liability of the company, that this condition will not be flagged and reported to Consumer Safety Agency, and that evidence may disappear when they take the faulty appliance away.  This is a major hazard that could have cause injury and property damage if not (by luck).  Range is just over 4 year old and use of it has been very light...looks almost brand new.
justification: A gas leak was detected and could have led to an explosion, but no injury or damage occurred. The incident was resolved safely, though the potential for harm was significant.

incident_description: I own a GE  Model # JGB281SER3SS gas stove.  Around September 2011 I noticed that a couple of times the gas was turned on at the burner with no flame and I had not been cooking, I thought it was just a fluke but in February 2012 the whole downstairs of the house smelled like gas. This has happened so often that I am afraid to use this stove.  I find this very dangerous, what if someone would bump into the stove right before bed? It could build up enough gas to either asphyxiate us or cause an explosion. I have also experience a strong gas smell every time I turn a burner on or use the oven. I find this highly unacceptable and I want this fixed before it does cause a deadly accident.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidaire Gallery electric range model #LGEF3043KFA on July 12, 2009.  
On April 10, 2012 I was using the convection oven at 350 deg. F to bake a cake.  Approx. 20 minutes into the baking time, my smoke detectors went off.  I ran to the kitchen where I found that the top broiler element was on and had burned the top of the cake.  I removed the burned cakes from the oven. I had not previously  turned on the broiler feature.  I then cancelled the quick bake function, but the unit would not turn off.  I looked in the oven and the broiler element appeared to be brighter and there was extreme heat coming from the oven. 

I heard a popping noise and then noticed that fire was coming from within the control panel.  

I pulled the stove away from the wall, turned off the breakers, and called 911 for assistance.

I have called Frigidaire to register this incident as the fire men suggested.  The customer service representative at Frigidaire said that since the unit is not on their recall list, is not within warranty, and is not a liability issue (since the fire did not damage my home) that I would need to contact their authorized servicer to determine what was the cause of the fire.  Once the servicer provided me with a report, I would then need to fax that report to Frigidaire and they would determine if they would assist me in repairing the unit.

I find it appalling that this company has had these issues in the past and continue to "pass the buck" when electronic failures in their units can claim lives and property.

incident_description:
The handle for the oven door came off several times. The screws that hold the handle fast to the oven door serve another purpose--to hold the two parts of the oven door together. When the handle came off, the front part of the door fell to the ground (with the windowglass resting on it); the inner part of the door was fast against the oven opening.  The large, heavy piece of glass was not fastened inside the door, it just floats inside the front and inner part of the oven door; I did not break, even though it is not fastened in any way. When I tried to put the two parts of the door together, I noticed that the screws seem short, only about less than 1/4" to go into the plastic handle to fasten the handle onto the front of the oven door. The glass inside the door makes the door heavy, so when the handle is engaged to pull open the door, it seems there is a lot of stress on the screws that hold the oven door together, and also hold the handle onto the door.  I believe this is dangerous; thankfully, the glass hasn't broken in the numerous times the door has slammed to the ground, but if it were to happen, it might be disastrous--hot door, hot glass, etc. It is also difficult to get the oven door open when the front part of the door is on the floor; there is are springs between the doors and when the door slams it is because the door is heavy and the springs are tight; it is difficult to get the doors to go together because you have to squeeze really tight, and there is not enough of a screw to put securely to accomplish the dual purose. I believe this design is problematic because the likelihood of the handle coming off the front of the door is random; I never know when it will happen and I am always cautious about checking to see the screws are intact.  
The Sears serviceman told me the only thing he could do to correct the situation was to put two of the same screws into the door/handle, but I didn't think that would help because the screws are too short to hold securely the amount of weight/force of repeated pulls on the handle/holding together the two parts of the door.
I have called Sears numerous times about this and have been told they haven't had any other calls on this matter, but on Friday, I spoke to someone who said he would send an email to their safety department; he directed me to the Call Center in Tucson, AZ and the woman I spoke to said she's had many calls about the handle coming off because of the short screws.
justification: The incident involves a hazardous oven door design with potential for injury due to falling glass, though no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
On 3/6/2012 the consumer placed the oven in the on position on 150 degrees   for an hour and a half and when she noticed that the heating element was red hot. The consumer states that it appears as if the temperature changed without her changing it.

 The consumer attempted  to power the oven in the off position she noticed that it would not power off. The heating element continued to glow a bright red. 

She went to the garage power the circuit breaker in the off position. When she powered the circuit breaker back into the on position the oven stayed off.

On 3/13/2012 the exact same failure occurred causing the consumer to once again shut off the circuit breaker.

She contacted the retailer on 3/13/2012 and was advised that they would send out a service technician but she would have to pay for the labor and any parts that were required. 

The consumer states that she was also advised that there was no recall involving her model number. 

The consumer will contacted the retailer/firm again to schedule a service call. The circuit breaker is currently in the off position and the range has not been used since the second failure occurred.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her electric freestanding stove may be a safety hazard as the inner glass window of her oven has cracked twice under pressure of the broiler. The first incident (date unknown) the consumer had the broiler set for under 5 minutes. The consumer suspects that the heating element may be the cause of these issues but is not sure.

 The consumer was using the oven for under 5 minutes on the first occasion and the oven door cracked and the glass cracked and glass remained intact. On the second occasion on January 17, 2012, the consumer was using the range for under 5 minutes and the inner glass door cracked and shattered onto the inside of the oven.

 Both times the consumer called the firm and was told both times that they cannot assist her because she does not have a warranty. The consumer has not been injured by the product. The consumer stated that her home was not damaged by the product. The consumer called the firm immediately after the first incident, and the first time it was fixed by the firm at no charge.

 The consumer called the firm immediately after the second incident. She was informed that she cannot be assisted by the firm because she doesnÃÂt have a warranty. The surface is a smooth surface. The consumer was only using the oven both times and not the range. The consumer had not called the retailer on any occasion. The consumer stated that the range currently doesnÃÂt show any scorch burns. The outside glass of the oven is presently intact.
justification: The incident involved a cracked oven glass but no injury or damage occurred, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence suggests a possible likelihood (3) of this issue happening again.

incident_description: My maytag dishwasher Quiet Series 300, MDB6601AWW although not part of the recall-the heating element has been staying on and will also stay on when the door is open.  I believe this can be a potential fire hazard.  The element gets very hot and will only shut off if the door is opened.  Sometimes it will stay hot even when the door is opened.
justification: The heating element staying on poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: toaster did not shut off and started fire
justification: The toaster malfunction caused a fire, which is an incident but no injury was mentioned.

incident_description: We have an LG LRE30755ST that we purchased in May of 2007. It was manufactured in April of 2007. On April 6, 2012, while cooking dinner in the oven, a loud humming noise started and we noticed there was a fire inside the oven. I immediately grabbed the kids and ran, and my husband shut the oven down & grabbed the extinguisher. After it cooled down, it appears some sort of wiring between the warming drawer & the bottom of the oven caused the fire and it burned a hole through the bottom of the oven. I contacted LG about this, even though it was out of the 1 yr warranty, and the only thing they had to offer was to send out a technician to perform a diagnostic test for $89. ÃÂ I told her there was nothing to diagnose, there is a HOLE burned in the bottom of my oven, it needs to be replaced. The agent simply said "I'm sorry for any inconvenience this may have caused you.". We are furious as this is a very dangerous product, and have seen several other reports of the exact same circumstances, yet the product has not been recalled, simply/conveniently "discontinued". If we had been in another room, this could have been a major fire and done damage to our home. ÃÂ LG needs to be held accountable for their poor products.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven, which is dangerous but did not result in injury or death. Similar incidents have been reported, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer has a safety concern with the switches (knobs used to control the burners) for the burners. He states that where the knobs are placed they could easily be switched on  accidently.

The consumer states that any slight to bump or brush up against the knob could cause it to release gas.

The firm was contacted the week of 3/12/2012 and a technician came out to the home 3/16/2012 . The consumer states that the technician used tie straps and glue to prevent any accidentally turning of the knobs. 

The consumer states that the fix that he received was a temporary solution and solve the problem.

The consumer states that  firm agreed that they are aware of the failure with the range  and has discontinued making that part of the range. 

He was advised to place child locks on it and or remove the knobs to prevent any future hazard.

The consumer still currently uses the range but is very careful.
justification: The incident involves a safety concern with burner switches that could accidentally release gas, but no injury or death has occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) due to the consumer's continued use of the range with caution and temporary fixes in place.

incident_description: Something unusual happened when trying to preheat our GE JB720CN1WW, electric oven on Saturday  4/7/12.  The oven started smoking, it tripped the circuit in our house, and after cleaning it up, it appears that the top broiler coil in the oven, touched the thin metal wire that holds the glass light bulb cover on, in the top back, left side in the oven.  There appears to be some melted silver on the glass cover, and a few inches of the broiler is now missing, and is on the bottom of the oven floor in small pieces..  We bought this oven new in June 2009 @ Sears.  Today I went to a few appliance stores, & looked inside new GE ovens, & the broiler location is now farther away from the light bulb cover.  I have photos of the inside of my oven, that I can share with you. I have not seen that there have been any recalls on this, but have seen on your website that others have had a similar problem.
justification: The incident involved smoking and electrical tripping but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on similar reported problems.

incident_description: The plastic under the latch that secures the door for running has begun to burn from the inside. It is turning brown, and while the unit is running, the smell of burning plastic is present near the latch.
justification: The burning plastic and smell indicate an incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
When turning on one of the hot plates another turns on by itself and stays on.
We have to turn off  the circuit breaker for the range every time we need to use it.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning hot plate that turns on by itself, requiring manual intervention to prevent potential hazards, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Cuisinart Smart Stick handheld blender (or immersion blender) from a reputable retailer.
Upon using the blender for the first time (when I say first time I mean this particular blender--I have used these before), I read the instructions first.  I made a milkshake in the plastic cup provided. I then unplugged the blender and disassembled it as the instructions read.  I brought the bottom part to the sink to clean it. I was using my left hand to remove some of the excess shake before rinsing and the blade snapped.  I at first thought my thumb was caught between the blades but then looked in horror and saw the blade was imbedded in my thumb.  I became hysterical as the blender was stuck to my finger.  I called my boyfriend and he calmed me down and talked me through getting the blender blade out of my thumb (I used my right hand and cut my right index finger deeply while doing so).  I was bleeding a lot, and wrapped both my thumb and index finger in a white towel.  My boyfriend was an hour away so he called my sister who woke her 1-year-old and came to get me.  She lives 15 minutes away.  She brought me to the emergency room.  This was approximately 8:15 pm.  I was hysterical because I had no idea how bad my thumb was.  They saw me right away at the hospital and said I would need stitches and everything else should be fine.  I ended up with 8 stitches to my left thumb and my right index finger was cut deeply but able to be bandaged vs. stitched.  I was sent home with care instructions which I have been following (redressing the wound daily, applying Bacitracyn).  I was told the stitches can come out 10 days later (Tuesday April 10th).  It is Tuesday April 10th today and I don't think they are ready to come out--but I will check with a doctor.  I contacted Cuisinart on Monday April 2nd and they said their Claims Dept. would be in touch within a couple of days.  It is now over a week later and I've heard NOTHING.  I am really angry that their defective product injured me, resulting in a hospital bill, an upcoming doctor's bill to remove stitches and left me unable to work--I have a home-based skincare studio (go to [REDACTED] for confirmation of this) and had to turn away clients which has been incredibly upsetting.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring medical attention (stitches and bandaging), but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe injuries from blender use are not common.

incident_description: Bosch Dishwasher Model SHU66C05UC/14. Will not power on. It seems that the circuit board is fried. The back of the panel has black smoke/residue.
justification: The dishwasher's circuit board is fried with visible damage, indicating an incident but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to illustrate his concerns about his under the counter dishwasher. The consumer stated that the control board in the dishwasher has burned twice. The consumer found that his model is similar to other models by the same firm that have been recalled. The consumer did not call the fire department after both occasions or his home insurance company. The consumer has not been harmed or injured by the product. 

The consumer has not experienced extensive property damage because of the product. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in a long cycle both times and the consumer found that the board was burned in two different places in the respective incidents. The consumer called the firm earlier this week. 

The firm was not interested in filing a report, told the consumer that the product was not on recall and referred them to the CPSC. The consumer has not notified the retailer on. The consumer had the first incident occur in 2007 and occurring again last Sunday.
justification: The incident involved a burned control board but no injury or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the issue suggests a possible likelihood (3) given the two incidents over a long period.

incident_description: I purchased two different Farberware 12 cup coffee and tea makers. The carafe on both leaked as I poured hot coffee, spilling hot coffee down the front of the carafe, once on my shoes, the second coffee maker I poured over the sink to see if it would do the same. It leaks around the black hard plastic seal on the front of the carafe carafe. I purchased the first coffee maker at a Wal-Mart in St. Roberts, MO, and the exchange was done at a Wal-Mart in Columbia, MO.
justification: The incident describes a product defect causing spills but no reported injuries, fitting severity level 2. The issue occurred with both purchased items, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was baking contents in the pyrex dish for approximately 1 hour at 350 degrees she decreased the temperature to 325, however 10 mins later she heard a loud noise and discovered that the dish had exploded in the oven, shattering peices all over the inside of the oven.   She managed to save a peice of the dish for evidence.

8/17/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised to save evidence for someone to analyse it and that they would send her a replacement within 14 days.  They never wanted it back for analysis.  

Consumer feels that this product is unsafe and should be reported. Consumer received a slight cut while cleaning up the mess.
justification: Consumer received a slight cut while cleaning up the mess, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description: I needed an extra dish for the biscuits I was cooking. I used the 9 x 9 Anchor Glass baking dish. I did not use any oils of any kinds for non-sticking, the food did not require it. Placed in a pre-heated oven of 350 F for 16 minutes. I removed the dish, set it on the stovetop (which had not been used yet) and about 45 seconds after I set the dish down it exploded into a million pieces, all over the stovetop, countertops, on my kitchen floor, shards of glass were covering my clothing as well as my kitchen floor, I come to find that there were more pieces in my living room which is a good 15-20 feet from my stove, and there were also shards and chunks of glass in the front room (another 15-20 feet from my stove) and in the hallway 9 feet away.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding, causing widespread glass shards but no reported injuries, making it an incident with no injury (severity 2). Such events are uncommon but not unheard of (likelihood 2).

incident_description: The issue is safety with the Frigidaire Gallery Gas Stove. You can accidently bump the control knobs. The gas will start flowing slowly and you cannot tell until you start smelling gas, without trying to flame. I called Frigidaire company just to warn them, this could result  in a dangerous situation , the customer service rep said there was nothing they could do. There should be some kind of safety device that will stop the gas flow if it does not heat.
justification: The incident describes a potential gas leak scenario which could lead to a dangerous situation, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Maytag electric double oven range Model MER6755AAB in October 2005.
Yesterday we used the bottom oven: baking meat in a deep pan.

The oven was on for over an hour and working fine, then the bottom coil of the bottom oven actually started flaming by itself, and the flame curled around on the coil, and then went out.

There was no grease or food on the coil to burn.
Nothing was dripping on to the coil.
There was no food or grease on the bottom of the oven to catch fire.
Had there been a shallow pan or anything near the coil, there would have been a big fire.

The fire went out by itself;  we shut off the oven.

We restarted the oven, and the bottom coil would not heat up.
There is rough corrosion on the coil where it was burning.
The burnt area is not near the electrical connection.

I have ordered a replacement part, which has not yet arrived.
We're certainly not using the oven until the part has been replaced.
justification: The incident involved a flaming oven coil that self-extinguished without causing injury or property damage, indicating a minor incident with no lasting harm.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range controls failed to work resulting in runaway oven heating. We put a turkey into the oven to cook at 325 degrees. Everything was fine for a few hours. Then we noticed the coils weren't going on and off and the oven temp had climbed rapidly to over 500 degrees. We couldn't turn it down. We couldn't turn it off. It didn't turn itself off as it is designed to do. So we shut off the power at the circuit breaker panel. If we hadn't noticed, it would have set the house on fire. If we'd been asleep, we might have died.

We inspected the stove after it cooled. There were no physical defects seen by the resident mechanical engineer. Given that none of the control buttons worked at all, the problem seemed to be in the circuitry. We replaced the stove and have kept the electronics, but not the carcass of the malfunctioning stove.
justification: The incident resulted in a runaway oven heating, which could have caused a fire or death, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
Oven Rack Collapsed.

Baking a pot roast in a enameled cast iron dutch oven, the oven rack collapsed from the left side of the oven onto the lower rack.   This caused the dutch oven to slam into the left wall of the oven and spill it contents all over the left side and bottom of the oven.  What a mess. 

Safety concern was the potential fire hazard and amount of smoke generated.
justification: The incident involved an oven rack collapse causing a mess and potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
this Kenmore Self cleaning electric range automatically turned on in clean mode while we were not in the house. Each of us thought we had turned the oven cleaning mode on but no lights indicated that. It looked as if the over was off, but it was so hot in the room.
No lights or indication showed on the panels, but our kitchen was very hot, the microwave fan above the range kicked on. My plates in my cabinets above the range were warm to touch.
My husband turned it off at the breaker box since the entire oven was very hot. The next day, he turned it on again so we could use the burners, and I turned them off after using. Again, the oven kicked on in clean mode while we were home. My husband again turned it off at the breaker box, and we went and bought a new range.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and turned on in clean mode without indication, creating a potential fire hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: My Kenmore kitchen stove has a burner that will not turn off by the switch.  When you turn the dial to off, the burner stays lit and produces heat.  I have model # 79096122408.  I see that higher models from the same time period has been recalled for the same issue, but this model has not.  This is a burn and fire hazard.
justification: The stove burner not turning off poses a burn and fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
The  consumer placed the dishwasher on the normal wash setting (cycle is approximately 45 minutes long)  within five minutes she heard popping. 

She noticed smoke and sparks  coming from the bottom of the appliance on the right side. 

She pressed the cancel button and unplugged the appliance from the outlet. When the appliance was unplugged the smoke stop pouring from the appliance and sparks stopped.

The retailer was contacted on 3/21/2012 and the consumer was advised that there was no recall involving her model number.  She has not used the appliance since the incident occurred and it is still currently unplugged from the outlet.

The consumer saw a news segment that spoke about fires caused by several brand dishwashers. The consumer stated that she was glad that she was home when the incident occurred. She also states that she could have been the next victim to a dishwasher fire.

The consumer has not made decisions on contacting the firm and or having a technician come out to the home to take a look at it.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
(3/14/2012)  The consumer said that the microwave oven shocked her on 1 occasion.  The microwave was in the "off" position at the time.  The consumer was opening the microwave oven door, when the incident occurred.  There was no injury.

The next day, the consumer walked into the kitchen and saw that the light underneath the microwave oven was on.  She turned it off.  A couple minutes later, the consumer saw that the light had come back on by itself.  She turned it off again, but later found that it came back on.  She noted that it kept turning on by itself more frequently as time passed.   Finally, the consumer unplugged the microwave oven from the wall outlet.

(3/16/12)  The consumer called the mfr. and explained the problem to a rep.  The rep. advised the consumer to unplug the microwave oven from the wall outlet and leave it unplugged.  The rep. started to arrange for a service technician to come out, but he checked their system and saw that the consumer's warranty had expired 11 days earlier.  Therefore, the rep. did not arrange for a tech. to come out.

The consumer did some checking around on her own and a local repair person told her that it would cost $200 - $250 the microwave oven.  The local technician told the consumer that he had repair 2 of 3 of these microwaves with a similar problem in the past month.  The tech. said that the panel on the front had a short in it and he might have to replace some wires or the entire panel.

The consumer opted to purchase a new microwave oven by a different mfr.
justification: The microwave oven shocked the consumer, but there was no injury, so the severity level is 2. The microwave oven kept turning on by itself, which is a common occurrence, so the occurrence likelihood is 4.

incident_description: Although this microwave worked wonderfully, and was very easy to clean, it started to turn on by itself. It was as if someone had pushed the number one for a 1-minute express cook. Then when I would try and turn it off, the key-pad would flash a message that said there was something wrong with it and that it may to be serviced. I was looking up research on the model and maybe some troubleshooting advice and I saw that a lawsuit was in action from a law firm in Washington. I also found reports (in Florida I think) that say some of the microwaves actually started house fires. I believe they were the same model. The lawyers asked for us to send it on on their expense so that their professionals may take a look at it in regards to the lawsuit. We only had a one year warranty on it when we bought it and didn't get an extended warranty on it so GE would not cover even manufacturing defects so we have to pay for a brand new microwave out of our own pockets. The microwave is only 2 years old.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by turning on by itself and displaying error messages, but no injury or fire occurred. Reports of house fires with the same model suggest a possible risk.

incident_description: The consumer says there was a fire behind the digital display.  Her husband said there was an electrical burning smell.  The consumer says there was an F10 error code on the digital display.  She tried to turn off the oven, but it would not.  Her husband had to shut off the circuit breaker.  The consumer says the food had only been cooking for an hour prior to the incident.  Oven was set at 300 degrees at the time.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not on recall and there is nothing they can do.  She said she stepped out for a moment and luckily her husband was at home to witness the incident otherwise their house could have caught on fire.
justification: There was an incident involving a fire and electrical issues, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled by shutting off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: Coffeemaker began to make a crackling noise, emit acrid smoke and become very hot on the bottom portion. We unplugged it and carried it outside (using oven mitts). It had been purchased new only 16 months ago.
justification: The coffeemaker malfunctioned but was safely handled without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: The consumer says that the rack has two adjustable areas.  when a pan is on the rack, the rack slips out on one side.  she says the rack can get tilted which can cause a burn hazard.  She says there is no catch on it, so when the door is open the rack can slip out and fall on the floor or on her foot because there is no stop on it.  She says it has a label that said "caution hot surface".  She says it gets hotter than any other oven she has ever had which concerns her of how much insulation it has.  The consumer says the unit takes twice as long to cook anything whether broiling or baking.  The consumer sent the company an email this morning.  She has gotten a confirmation back that they have gotten her email and will respond to her.
justification: The rack slipping out and tilting poses a burn hazard, and the lack of a stop increases the risk of injury from falling objects or burns.

incident_description:
Family and I were staying in a condominium at the Hyatt Escala Lodge in Park City, Utah for a ski vacation.  I got the 12" Cuinisart skillet out to fry some hambergers.  Two days earlier I had commented to my wife that I would not buy that type of cookware because one of the four small aluminum covers on the rivits that held the handle and additional stablizing grip on the opposite side was missing.  I did not think twice why one would be missing but, in hindsight I now know.

I started the [REDACTED] range and then place the burgers in the pan.  I turned around to do something at the sink and suddenly (3-4 minutes)it sounded like a gunshot or M80 firecracker exploded.  I heard something hit the ceiling then the wall then the glass window and bounce around on the floor.  I turned to the stove but nothing looked out of order.  I checked the oven where I had turned on the broiler to toast the buns but nothing was out of order there.  I did remove the burgers from the heat and went into the dining room to see if I could find what I heard bounce around on the floor.  I then found the small rivit cover which is just shy of 1/2" in diameter (see attachet picture) on the floor.

I picked up the piece and could not believe it.  I realized what had happened and thought how lucky I was to not have been hit buy this projectile.  This piece shot out of the skillet like a gun.  I thought it was maybe because I had first had the gas on high which heated the outside of the skillet and may have caused the aluminum pieces to expand quicker than the rest of the skillet.  I turned the heat down and placed the skillet back on the flame.  

Approximately two minutes later a second rivit cover did exactly the same thing.  At this time the burgers were finished so I removed them and turned off the heat.  I later washed the skillet and took it to the management of the lodge to explain what had happened and suggested they remove all of this cookware from their condos due to liability issues.  

I later decided to do a bit of sleuthing on the internet and sure enough, I ran across two incidents where the exact same thing happened.  One  interesting fact from the other two occurances I found on line was that one happened on a [REDACTED] range as well.

Considering how one hovers over things cooking on the stove this is extremely dangerous to have a hot metal projectile coming from a frying pan.  It could easily cause extreme damage to one's eye or worse.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous projectile from a skillet but no injury occurred, and similar incidents have been reported online.

incident_description: On Saturday, March 31st 2012, my Kitchenaid Superba Model KEMC308KSS0 oven door exterior glass shattered into hundreds of pieces.  No one was in the kitchen at the time and the oven had not been used all day.  Both my partner and I were startled by the loud crack/pop the door made as it shattered and ran to investigate where we found glass all over the floor in front of the oven.  So much for Superba.  This seems less than superb and I'd call it inferior.  I've had several ovens with glass doors over the years but never had one explode, especially when it wasn't even being used.
justification: The oven door shattered without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm, and such events are unlikely based on the user's experience.

incident_description: Jenn Aire dishwasher overheating even when not on a cycle.  Closing the door causes the dishwasher to heat up.  Running a cycle caused the dishes to be too hot to touch for almost an hour.  Many dishes were ruined due to the extreme heat.
justification: The dishwasher overheated, causing damage to dishes but no injury to people.

incident_description:
Caller's double oven was purchased 12/29/2008, installed in her home January 2009.

January 16th, 2012 around 1:00PM caller was pre heating her electric upper oven  (she has double oven) to approximately 400 degrees, taking pizza out of plastic wrap while she waited.

She looked up at the oven, saw that it was at 397 degrees, had just put her hand on the oven handle to begin opening the door when she actually heard explosion, she jerked her hand away from handle while turning her head out of instinct.
In between the two ovens there is a vent where some glass came flying out onto the pizza.

She was very shaken, she had no idea what had just happened.

Her husband came into the kitchen, turned the oven off immediately, opened the upper oven and glass came flying out with enough force that it went out of the kitchen and into eating area which is approximately ten to twelve feet away from the ovens.

He had instinctively turned his head also so was not injured either.

Caller pulled out her user's manual for the double oven, noted the manufacturer's phone number and called around 1:30PM, same day, January 16th, 2012.

She spoke with manufacturer rep named [REDACTED] who in the very beginning asked her if she was alright, said she would be right back with her but then returned to the line and told the caller that she must have done something wrong such as taking racks out or hitting the rack.
It has been two and half months, she cannot use her top oven, she is afraid to use her bottom oven.
She has been told about six times that the part had been shipped or is on the way but it never arrives.  She believes that there may be another issue with this part.

She spoke with one rep at extended warranty who said they would issue her 75% of cost of new double oven but she would have to pay removal, installation, etc. which would run her alone as much as approximately $1600.

Caller could not find the date of manufacture.

She would like the public to know to be aware and be cautious.

She believes whole heartedly that there is an extreme safety issue with this oven and would like to have a replacement of same value, better & safer quality at manufacturer expense including removal, installation.
justification: The incident involved an oven explosion with flying glass, but no injuries were reported, indicating a non-injury incident with rare likelihood based on the description.

incident_description: The consumer says he turned on the range.  One minute later the glass top shattered.  He never had any issues with the range prior to this incident.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who offered a $130 service fee.  The consumer says the glass is in one piece but there is a spider web crack on it.  The consumer says the radiant cartridge may have been the cause for the heat tempered glass to shatter.  He says they were not very concerned and he is very disappointed that the manufacturer did not provide him with further assistance.
justification: The incident involved the glass top shattering without injury, and prior issues were not reported, indicating it's an isolated event.

incident_description: purchased 4-13-2009 at home depot, Elk River,MN, Found that the vent was located in the rear of the built in dishwasher. Since dishwasher is enclosed and covered with insulating material, the steam and moisture generated from the dishwasher has no where to go, except to saturate the insulation, the cabinets on both sides as well as the sheetrock wall behind it. Thus the dishes never dry and the walls and cabinets are damp and wet causing mold and mildew to grow in the wood cabinets as well as the drywall. We have called and have had service calls placed 6 times and were told that it was not repairable and that it was a design defect by the manufacturer, therefore not covered by the manufacture warranty or the extended warranty we purchased. The dishwasher does not preform as stated in the consumer information, has caused damage to the interior of our home and is a serious health hazard.
justification: The incident describes property damage and a health hazard due to mold and mildew, but no direct injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Dishwasher was operating when the control panel began a buzzing/clicking noise and black smoke poured from the opening for the catch.
Opened the dishwasher to stop the cycle, then opened the circuit breaker.
Disassembly of the control panel revealed burned components inside.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with smoke and burned components, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The coffee maker, which was programmed the night before, began to make coffee.  My husband heard a funny noise and went to the kitchen to check it out.  He found the coffee maker with smoke pouring out of it.  The coffee itself was boiling.  There was a strong odor of electrical components melting.  My husband unplugged the coffee maker and put it in the sink so it didn't damage the countertop.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing smoke and a strong odor, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I own one of the Bosch Tassimo coffee makers affected by the following recall:  "Tassimo Single-Cup Coffee Makers Recalled by BSH Home Appliances Due to Burn Hazard".

I contacted Bosch and did receive a part, per the recall "solution".  I installed the part according to the directions and have been using the machine ever since.  This morning, the machine exploded while brewing an espresso using a new disc I had just ordered from Tassimo.  Thankfully, I was in another room.  I was unhurt but am concerned that I may have been burned if I was close to the machine.  I did take photos, but they are a little blurry.

I thought you needed to know that their so called fix is not fixing the problem.  I feel there is still a risk of burns.  Another gentlemen had posted a similar account on YouTube.
justification: The machine exploded but no one was injured, though there was a potential for burns if someone was nearby. Another similar incident was reported, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
Caller was taking Pyrex pie dish out of cupboard on May 15, 2011 around 8:30PM when it fell 18 inches out of cupboard, hit the linoleum floor and exploded.
Caller states that he wants to report as a serious danger because the explosion resulted in pieces landed 20 feet away to other side of room stopped only by the wall.
It took him two hours to vacuum all pieces up.

incident_description:
This morning, 4/4/12, I placed an english muffin in the Black and Decker toaster oven (model T01485B) I have in my kitchen. I set the temperature to the "toast" setting, the function to the "toast" setting, and the timer to 20 (recommended in the user manual). 

The toaster had been in use for approximately 2-3 minutes when I heard a loud "pop". I turned around in the kitchen and there was glass all over the counter and kitchen floor. The front glass door of the oven had shattered and thrown glass across the kitchen. I immediately unplugged the toaster and waited for the glass to cool. While I was waiting the glass continued to make crackling/popping sounds.
justification: The incident involved a toaster oven's glass door shattering, causing no injury but creating a hazardous situation with glass debris.

incident_description:
The dish ware set Italian Villa by Home Trends is used by my family as an everyday dish ware set. My mother and I purchased this 8 piece set from Walmart and I was looking for a set that was microwave safe. The stamp on the bottom of the dishes state that it is dishwasher and microwave safe. The dishes have safely been used in the dishwasher but the microwave use of these dishes have been of an increasing concern and now just plain and clear that it is unsafe for usage. Microwaving a bowl of instant oatmeal has always left the bowl so hot that pot holders and kitchen towels had to be used to transfer the cooked oatmeal into another bowl to be eaten. Heating up an already made cup of tea has burned my 14 year old daughter's hand and two weeks ago I burned my finger with 3 linear burns and blisters as I attempted to retrieve the cup of tea from the microwave after heating it up for 1 minute. I attempted finding Home Trends online and found the website www.hometrends-dinnerware.NET in which I sent 3 emails detailing the burn injury I sustained from the unsafe dish ware set that I have in my possession.

Today, stupid me, I should have learned my lesson, but I again put a cup of tea into the microwave to reheat it for 1 minute and was again burned on my hand. I am now taking these cups out of my cupboards so noone will be injured by these cups again. I contacted Walmart and spoke to the manager and then was referred to Gibson in California and will now forward pictures and a detailed email of my experience. I think the composition of these dishes are not made safe for the microwave use and should be investigated. This is not an isolated incident from what I have read.
justification: The incident describes multiple instances of burns and blisters from using the dishware in the microwave, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
We purchase a Kitchenaid KEBS208SS double oven for $2,720 on September 5, 2011. We can provide receipt if required.

Today, March 31 2012, we used the self cleaning feature for the first time. After about 2 hours, the inside glass of the glass door shattered and glass flew everywhere in thousands of small pieces. My wife, who was home at that time said it sounded like an explosion.  She even got a small cut cleaning up all the glass on our kitchen floor

I can provide pictures if required.

This oven has a serious safety issue and needs to be recalled. 

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused a minor injury (small cut) and significant property damage, indicating a moderate severity level. The likelihood is deemed unlikely as it's the first reported issue in six months of use.

incident_description: The consumer says that she has used the self cleaning feature twice.  She says it gets so hot that it blows out the control panel.  She contacted the manufacturer who said they don't know anything about it.  A technician she contacted on her own told her not to use the cleaning feature.  Another technician was sent by the manufacturer about four years ago who replaced the control board.

incident_description:
The consumer says she has had problem since she has had it. The consumer says she can smell gas coming from the unit even when it is not turned on. She can hear a clicking sound when trying to turn on the heating element but it will not turn on. The consumer says the unit is sometimes extremely hot. She is afraid of a possible fire hazard. She contacted the manufacturer, who only offered a repair for a fee.  The consumer says a technician came to inspect the unit about a year ago who said nothing was wrong with it.

UPDATE:
I had a [REDACTED] gas range that would not work properly, because it seemed to be too hot. When I cooked meat or cookies they were not cooked evenly I don't know how old the range was, but I didn't move to present address until 10/2004 and it came with the house. I went to Home Depot & purchased one. It has digital buttons. At first, I thought it was just me, but even my daughter tried using it. Press bake, the temp would automatically go to 350 degrees, then you had to press temp gauge button what temp you wanted .. . then it would show 100 degrees again, showing you the temp rising to where you wanted as it heated up. You would get either . 1) nothing at 100 ..... 2) 100 with smell of gas with a clicking sound .. no heat because oven did not go on 3) sometimes if you are "lucky", the oven would eventually heat up to the temp you wanted (took a several minutes) then a bell would go off to let you know the oven was "ready". incident_description: Outside glass of my Kenmore oven door shattered. I was at work when it happened, luckily nobody was home or the kids or myself would have been hurt had we been in the kitchen. It was fine when I left in the morning. It looked to have just exploded, glass was everywhere. Most of it piled underneath the oven on the floor but there were shards of glass all across the kitchen, some I found approx. 7 feet away under my kitchen table. I had not used my oven for over a week and was turned off at time. The oven came with the house when I bought it 2 years ago and I can't find any paperwork on it. I am assuming it is no longer under warranty. I also can't find the model #.

incident_description:
Model: PVM1870SM3SS
Over-the-range GE Profile Microwave with recirculating, hidden vent fan. 

My PVM1870SM3SS over the range Microwave (installed new May 2010) broke in a rather shocking and dangerous way while I was cooking -- the hidden vent assembly broke off during normal use. The recirculating vent design is a thick, heavy, hidden door held up by two thin plastic mounts. Normally it sits flush with the front of the microwave above the main door but when the microwave oven is turned on, a motor causes it to tilt forward so air van recirculate upwards and out of the top of the microwave in front of the cabinet. This door assembly is several inches thick and weighs several pounds and when the two, paper thin plastic mounts failed it dropped onto the range below while I was cooking. Thankfully I was just cooking eggs -- not boiling water -- or I would have been severely burned.  

I have no kids. I am not home very much. I don't cook much, I usually eat out. The unit was virtually new and yet it still failed dramatically and dangerously. Oh, 1 year warranty, so it's my problem.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous failure of the microwave vent assembly, but no injury occurred as the user was not severely burned.

incident_description: fire in unit

incident_description: Simply cooking popcorn in the Microwave, it began crackling and popping, then fire was seen on the inside of the unit at the wave directer area and with some smoke.  I turned off the unit and found that the wave director cardboard installed on the inside of the unit had been charred and burned all the way through.  The Microwave is part of the Electrolux built in elecric oven.  According to a service tech, the unit is not safe.  To repair the whole unit has to be taken out of the cabinet, and the Microwave would have to be rebuilt.  There is no specification for or way to replace just the microwave.  There is no warranty and the whole unit has to be replaced.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the microwave with no reported injuries, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is unlikely as such events are not common with proper microwave use.

incident_description: I was attempting to bake banana bread in my Pyrex Easy Grab Glass Loaf dish.   The pan was in my cupboard and was room temperature when I put into the oven. The bread batter was not really cold or hot, nor was the dish, so there was not any extreme temperature change.   The bread was baking for approximately 15 minutes, when I heard a loud noise.  When I looked inside the entire baking dish exploded inside the oven into a tiny pieces and shards.  The banana bread was still runny and only a little ways cooked at that point.     Fortunately the oven door was shut as I cannot imagine what could have happened if it was not closed.  Scary to think about.  When trying to clean the oven up, every larger piece of broken dish had splintered all throughout it and would just crumble when picked up.
justification: The baking dish exploded, but no injury occurred as the oven door was closed.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Elite Electric Range, Model 79099123408, caught fire while cooking a ham in the oven. The ham had been cooking for nearly 2 hours (1 hour left) at 350F when the range started making a crackling sound. The panel lights turned off (with the exception of the clock) and the two left burners turned on by themselves. At the same time, smoke could be seen coming from the back of the range. A quick inspection revealed the power board was on fire. The range was pulled away from the wall and unplugged resulting in the fire losing intensity. I was able to blow on the fire between the back vent slots in the back panel and it extinguished the fire. The range was quickly removed from the house to ensure no damage would occur to the kitchen/house. Damage to the range includes the power board 10%-20% significant burning and the associated electrical wiring 

Other information:
Bought the range new from Sears on September 14, 2005
Sears service replaced all of the electronic control boards, including the damaged power board in June 2008
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly controlled without injury or death, fitting severity level 2. Given the age of the appliance and previous repairs, such failures are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description:
Woke up this morning and thought I smelled a slight burning plastic smell.  Made coffee and, upon retrieving cream from refrigerator, noticed that the cream was warm and the refrigerator did not seem to be cooling.  Further investigation revealed that the interior lights were HOT and would not turn off.  I contacted the Sears Service Dept and (after giving them an explicit description of the problem) was told that they could not be here for a repair/service call until Tuesday (4 days away!).  

A friend came over to look at my refrigerator and discovered that the cover over the interior lights was fused (from the heat) to the housing unit and had to be pried down to allow access to the screws holding it in place (we could NOT remove the bulbs as they were stuck in the sockets).  Once removed, the plug was disconnected and then it was observed that the interior of the unit casing had started bubbling/melting.  A couple of more hours and my refrigerator would have been in flames.  

Thank God this happened today and I was home.  Otherwise, I would have come home to a house in flames or burned to the ground!

I subsequently contacted Sears - again! - and was placed on hold for over an hour without anyone coming on the line at any time to give me the status of my call.  I finally hung up.

How many of these instances have occurred?  How many more have to occur before something is done?

I have been an avid Sears/Kenmore customer - have owned nothing BUT Kenmore my entire adult life - but this experience (between the lack of customer service and the lack of a recall of the item - or notification) has me rethinking my allegiance to this company and their products.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator malfunction that nearly caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: For the past few months our Kenmore Electric glass top range (Model# 790.94349700) has refused to turn off one of the burners even though the dial temperature control is set to the "off" position. On 3/29/2012, we used the range for dinner around 7:00PM (EST). This afternoon we noticed the range felt hot and the left front burner indicator was still lit! Once again, the dial control for the temperature was set to the "OFF" position and the "burner" light to the bottom right of the range was not lit. The stove just doesn't want to shut off it's burners. This is a huge fire hazard and and seems like it should be covered under warranty services but unfortunately the range is 3 yrs out of warranty.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that poses a fire hazard but no actual injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that on June 1, 2011 her microwave oven caught on by itself. The consumer stated that she was in her bedroom until she smelled a burning odor with a "sickly sweet smell" and came to find the microwave was on by itself. The consumer stated that her microwave was very hot to the touch to the point where she could not touch it at all. The consumer had her cake in the microwave at the time and the microwave had the light on as well as the fan blowing. The product is an over the range microwave. The product has a plastic door with a glass inset.

consumer turned off the main switch to power off the product as well as everything in her house including clocks, lights and lamps. The consumer called her neighbor, from Southern State Electric to make sure she didn't have a wall fire and the fix the microwave if possible. The consumer and attempted to turn on the breaker and the product. However, the microwave would not turn on; concluded that the product was burned out and will not power on. Luckily, the product did not catch fire. 

The microwave is charred on the inside but no physical damage on the outside that the consumer can see. There is no visible damage to the structure of her home. The consumer was initially going to call the fire department but decided not to. The consumer noticed other reports on the internet of this product catching fire. The consumer has not noticed any formal recall of this product. The consumer stated that the product is less than 3 years old and is upset because she could have had her house burn down or worse since it was only her and her dog in the home at the time of the incident.

 The consumer called GE to inform them about the incident and the number of similar incidents with this model as can be found on the internet- and- to ask hwy there had been no recall of this product.  Consumer had owned this microwave since Au 6 2007.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and became dangerously hot, but no fire or injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Maytag Dishwasher repaired per recall about a yr & a half ago.  08/02/2010 per release# 10-255. 

Saturday, March 10, 2012.. this overflow machine  (used only with extra company when main dishwasher is full) began.

Since repair per recall on release# 

Dishwasher was not being used, was just sitting in the kitchen island and began smoking, spewing out gray smoke, odor of burning electrical wires or components.

Caller unplugged dishwasher.

Called manufacturer Monday, March 12th, 2012, advised caller that repair per recall had already been completed but that it began smoking while not in use. The caller told the manufacturer that the dishwasher began to smoke while not in use. The manufacturer said the machine was out of warranty and they had no more responsibility. This dishwasher has only been used and estimated ten times.

Caller would like to have machine repaired or replaced without cost. If the machine is repaired, caller wants to know why this happened to be assured that it will not happen again and burn his house down.

Caller would like to have this dishwasher repaired at manufacturer expense and placed on recall again.

incident_description:
I have had an ongoing battle/struggle with the Whirlpool Corp concerning a refrigerator which we purchased in February 2010. It is a poorly designed unit which causes considerable problems and has caused injury to myself on more than one occasion. None of the injuries were serious, but could have been. They have caused bruises and skin breaks on more than one occasion.

We have not heard from you nor Whirlpool concerning our problems with our Whirlpool
Refrigerator -- Model ED2HAXVQ, SN HR00453231 that we purchased at your store about two years ago. It has been a problem ever since we have had it and continues to be a problem even today. It is of such poor design that it should be recalled and replacement given.

When I attempt to remove the ice dispenser to defrost it and clean the ice clumps it is a very difficult chore with ice flying all over the kitchen. incident_description:
While consumer was sitting in his living room Saturday, March3rd, 2012 he began hearing popping sounds.
He got up, followed sounds, couldn't follow to any source and so sat back down but then began smelling a metallic odor, he went to kitchen to check electrical appliances or devices.

He noted smoke swirling through microwave door, opened it and smoke filled the room.

He unplugged microwave, opened windows and doors.

He had not in the beginning thought the odor to be coming from the microwave because he had not used it for over 12 hours and then only to heat a cup of coffee.

He contacted the number given for the manufacturer but was told only that the warranty was over.

He does not believe that fire should be an issue that would not still be covered and would like his microwave replaced or at the very least successfully repaired.
justification: The incident involved smoke from a malfunctioning microwave but no injury or death occurred, and such electrical malfunctions are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description:
3/2012 The consumer stated that the dishwasher stopped working and the control panel would not illuminate.  She found out that the reason could be that the "Thermal Fuse" needed to be replaced. Her husband ordered a new one and replaced it on 3/7/2012.  After they replaced it they turned on the dishwasher and it worked for the first load. 

3/15/12 The consumer placed the dishwasher in wash cycle approximately 3-5 minutes later, she heard a popping sound. When she came back into the kitchen she saw that there was smoke coming out of top of the control panel of the dishwasher. She opened the door, but was afraid to turn it off from the control panel. She had to switch it off from the circuit breaker. 

There were no damages to her home. Her husband took it apart and saw that the electronic components from the control panel had melted.

3/15/12 The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that they would refund her for the Thermal Fuse. They stated that the dishwasher was out of warranty and that the unit was not recalled.

The consumer feels that this dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melted components but no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recurring issue with the dishwasher.

incident_description:
Investigated a kitchen fire in a sprinkler apartment. The sprinkler system extinguished fire early on and its obvious
the fire started at the toaster. The plastic bottom melted out onto the counter top. We found burnt French bread in
the toaster. We also found the handle in the down position.

We got an exemplar and tried to start a fire with French bread. No luck despite repeataed cycles of toasting. All of
the heat is vented up and out of the toast slots. Recorded only ambient temperatures on the plastic bottom.

Next we introduced a fire at the printed circuit board where the power cord attached. Produced almost identical
fire damage to the kitchen. We think this started inside the control area and probably was NOT due to operator
misuse or error. Furthermore, we learned that the post-fire position of the toaster handle is a function of fire
damage, not the pre-fire position of the toaster handle. We are Certified Fire Investigators, not electrical engineers.
Consequently we're submitting this to CPSC for review.
justification: The incident involved a kitchen fire that was quickly extinguished by the sprinkler system, with no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: At approximately 2pm on the day of the incident, the upper oven (Kitchenaid double wall oven Model KEBS207SSS02, purchased in 2008) was turned on and preheating to 425ÃÂ°F.  The oven remained on while preheating for about 10 minutes, but was then turned off manually and not used again until 5:30 pm.  At this time the upper oven was heated to 375ÃÂ°F to reheat restaurant pizza on a cookie sheet.  During this time the oven functioned normally and the food and cookie sheet were removed from the oven.  Around 5:45 pm, the oven temperature was adjusted to 475ÃÂ°F and preheated normally.  The oven was empty at this time.  At 6:15 pm a frozen pizza was placed on a cookie sheet in the oven on the middle rack.  The oven continued to bake for 15 minutes.  At 6:32 pm, three adults were in the kitchen.  I turned on the oven light, pushing the button labeled "Oven Light."  As I stepped to the left side of the oven, I heard a loud pop and saw fissures form on the inner glass panel of the upper oven.  The glass immediately shattered and exploded out the bottom of the oven door.  I was not injured, but hot glass exploded onto the floor, on my pants and shoes.  Just prior to the explosion I had been near the oven door, looking directly into the oven from the outside.  The glass could have cut my face, sending shards into my eyes.  Glass shards ranging from 0.25 in to 1 in in length were found in areas at least 3 feet away from the oven.  Immediately the oven was turned off, but the oven light remained on.  Glass was coving the inside of the oven.  Broken glass was found in between the outer-most glass panel and the second pane.  A red rubber seal from the inside of the door was also loose and could be seen hanging from the inside oven door panel.  Glass was found in the seal around the oven doors, in the door hinges, and in the tracks of the bottom rack.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of glass from the oven, but no injuries were reported despite the potential for harm.

incident_description:
My GE Microwave Advantium 120 oven was installed in january 2011. The other day the microwave just suddenly stopped working. This is a built in oven and is out of warranty. I removed the oven and opened the cover to troubleshoot the problem. I found one of the primary wires to the high voltage transformer for the magnetron was disconnected. On closer inspection I found that the lug on the transformer that the wire was connected to (spade type connector) had melted through completely. The wire's insulation was scorched and melted. I am relieved that the connector melted before catching fire. I believe this was caused by a serious defect in assembly or design and is a potential fire hazard. I have reported this to the manufacturer, General Electric and I am awaiting their response. 
Regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The microwave malfunctioned with a melted wire and scorched insulation, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says the label on the oven, and the specification in the operating instructions booklet show power consumption 12.7 amps.  The booklet shows 1460 watts.  The consumer measured it using two different instruments with the same results of 16.4 amps on full power.  The consumer measured 1950 watts on another instrument and on the utility's meter.  What he measured would require a 20 amp circuit as is stated in the manufacturer's booklet.  


The consumer says the unit does not come with a 20 amp plug which means a consumer could plug it into a 15 amp outlet, overloading the outlet and possibly tripping the breaker.  The booklet is the only place where it advises to use a 20 amp circuit.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him he is not measuring it right.  The consumer disagrees.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who asked him to ship it back.  The consumer had a different microwave with same brand and same model number and the same hazard.  
The Consumer Added:  The reader of my complaint should be made aware that, as permitted by the National Electric Code (NEC), residential kitchens rarely have 20 amp outlets on the 20 amp "s mall appliance circuits" that are required along the kitchen counters. The st andard outlets are 15 amp "duplex receptacles" with a 20 amp feed-through rating. This means these outlets are permitted to be on 20 amp circuits but that appliances plugged into them must be limited to 15 or 12 amps, depending on the length of time the appliance can be set t o operate. The only appliances in our kitchen that exceed 12 amps is our 4-s10t toaster; it draws 15 amps, but is designed not to operate continuously for more than a few minutes.
Thi s microwave oven seems capable of running for an hour or more and thus may be l i mited t o 12 amps by the NEC or UL. The Panasonic Canada web site lists similar mi crowaves, but they all have lower output wattage ratings. I suspect the Canadian Standards Associat ion (CSA) or UL Canada required this reduction t o lower the amp draw to 12 amps. I have a l ot more faith in Canada than in the US when it comes electrical equipment. When I replaced all the outlets and switches in my home about 25 years ago I made sure they all had CSA approvals on them.
One reason I decided to check the amperage of my Panasonic microwave oven it because it is not approved by CSA or Canadian UL.
justification: The incident involves a potential electrical overload hazard due to incorrect labeling, but no actual injury or damage has been reported.

The sound was tremendous and the glass shard were sent flying in all directions. Luckily the majority was aimed away from me and therefore I only received minor cuts. 

I placed the dish on my stove top but DID NOT turn on the stovetop. I was simply preheating the oven to 425 to cook with the dish and placed the dish above the stove while it waited to come to temperature. Within a few minutes the dish exploded. The glass was very hot and I can only conclude that the heat from the oven below eventually blew up the dish. 

However, the temperature change was not sudden, the oven had been preheating for at least 6-7 minutes before the explosion occurred. Secondly, I can only assume that the stovetop itself did not even reach the 425 temperature the inside of the oven was set for. In fact I could still touch the top of the stove with my hand for short periods of time without any burns. I would imagine it was no hotter than 350 on the stovetop, and yet the glass still exploded. 

This situation is very dangerous as I did not violate any warnings at a basic level. It was on a stove top that was heating up from second degree heat, but from my view, it was simply waiting on a cool stove while the oven preheated. This situation could be very common for cooking. 

I understand consumer reports has already done investigations and confirmed that imperfections in the glass and the type of glass used (in contrast to previous glass types) has led to a far more susceptible dish to explosion. 

Before any more citizens blind or kill themselves, I suggest a serious inquiry is made and action is taken to return to the old types of glass or increase quality in manufacturing so that glass defects cannot donÃÂt let this happen.

incident_description:
Below is a copy of letter faxed to Thermador on 3/14/2012:
We purchased the unit in July, 2001 at RenovatorÃÂs Supply along with other appliances that were to be installed in our 2nd home at [REDACTED] which was being renovated at the time.
In December of 2001, the kitchen renovations were completed to the point where appliances, cabinets, etc. were to be installed, ready for use.
From January, 2002 until October of 2009, this residence was used as a vacation/get away home mainly on weekends throughout the year and summer vacations.
Since November of 2009, this residence has been our permanent home, living here full time, year round. 
My wife and I both recall at least one service call sometime between 2002 and 2008 (or there about) to have the oven unit serviced due to a non-functioning micro-wave. It is our recollection that this problem occurred after we had performed a self-clean operation. I have searched my records, but at this time, have not been able to find any documentation.

A month later (see attached service call receipt), we had a similar problem, a non-functioning microwave. This service call resulted in a different diagnosis but the suggested repairs were not done, since microwave operated properly and there appeared to be no issues.
Early in February of 2012, we performed another self-clean operation and shortly thereafter, we again had problems with the micro-wave. This time the microwave would work sometimes after several attempts or after using the oven in COOK-SMART mode for a few minutes than trying it in microwave mode. Immediately after our conversation, I called Jersey Coast Appliance and set up an appointment with them for 3/14/12.

This afternoon, the service man came and as it turns out, he was the same service man who was here in 2010. His initial comment was,ÃÂ microwave not working again after the self-clean, huh, heard that beforeÃÂ. He tried to bypass the fuse to see if he could determine if anything else could be wrong, but that test did not work. At this point, we are hoping that THERMADOR will review our situation and resolve this problem to everyoneÃÂs satisfaction.
Today, I checked the CPSC web site and found that this unit has been recalled. Our serial number is listed as one of the models, our serial number 20070043, Model #CM301US. Thermador is telling us that it is not under recall. I need soemone to assist us with this problem.
