incident_description:
There was a grease fire on the griddle assembly.  The fire was extinguished using a fire extinguisher.  

The griddle design allows the grease to roll back under the griddle surface and drip on the heating elements.  Subsequently, we have raised the back of the griddle up by resting it on the back of the griddle "hole," and this helps, but grease still drips down the edges of the grease tray and puddles under it, then drips down the front face of the oven (inside the door) all the way to the floor.

A service technician has been out and determined that the unit is properly installed.

A Bertazzoni representative suggested raising screws in the back of the griddle burner assembly, but this would lead to further issues, such as batter flowing down the griddle since it is not flat.

The griddle needs a method to force the grease to drip into the grease tray and keep it from rolling back.  Additionally, the grease tray needs to be wider than the griddle so that it doesn't drip on the sides of the tray and down its sides.
justification: A grease fire occurred but was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no harm. The ongoing issue with grease dripping suggests a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Noticed one day that the green power light on panel of dishwasher was off. Did troubleshooting listed in users manual but could not get any power. Checked household circuit breaker for the dishwasher, and it was not tripped. Called appliance repairman who discovered that the entire circuit board in the control panel of the dishwasher was burnt out. Heat has been sufficient to penetrate the holder for the circuit board and blister the covering of the front control panel. Amazingly, no fire was started.
justification: The incident involved a burnt-out circuit board and heat damage but no fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: After cooking on Electric range, left rear burner remained on even after turning off.  Would not stop until I turned off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: I have a 5-6yr old Kenmore Elite free standing electric range (model #790.99123403).  Last evening the oven was turned on and set to 375 degrees.  After approximately 15 minutes of opperation, there were loud crackling and popping noises emitted from the range, black smoke began rising from behind the top user interface area, then flames shot 12-18", reaching my vent hood.  Knowing immediately it was an electrical fire, I ran to my breaker box and cut the power.  I then used a kitchen fire extinguisher and directed it's contents down behind the range.  My house was full of thick, black smoke.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with flames and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The oven was set to preheat at 425 to bake fish. After the beep, we put the food in the oven. After 10 minutes we checked on the food and everything was burnt. The oven had heated to a very high temperature and we were unable to shut it off. Only after switching the fuse in the basement, did the heating elements on the bottom start to cool down. As soon as the fuse is switched back on, the oven starts to heat up without being turned on. We had to unplug it and aren't able to use the oven or stovetop.
This is a fire hazard and could have started the house on fire. Luckily we didn't leave the food unattended.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and posed a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

If this continued a while longer a fire was a definite possibilty. The bulbs were too hot to touch and all the food on the top shelf was hot.this started on 03-19-2012 .

incident_description: Had used a relatively new (1 or 2 years old) pyrex measuring cup to make cream cheese frosting.  Bowl was clean, dry, stored in cabinet at time of use.  Made frosting with room temp. ingredients, washed bowl with warm water, set out to dry on a counter top away from any heat source.  Went to put away in cabinet an hour later and the whole bowl exploded in my face.  Lacerations on my hands and arms, thank goodness nothing in my eyes.  Thousands of sharp shards, slivers and chunks of glass everywhere.  Very very frightening.  I am throwing away the rest of my pyrex for fear this will happen to one of my children.

incident_description: Maytag dishwasher model MDB9150AWW, Serial number 24156777YZ was running when started to arc internally, and then smelled burning material.  I turned off the circuit breaker, opened the door, and found several bare wires which had shorted against metal and burned off the insulation.  A fire could have occurred if I had not been home at the time.  Definitely a fire hazard and a safety concern.

incident_description: Our Kenmore smooth top range model number 79096009601 has had problems for a while.  The burners will often not turn off after we have turned the knobs off. incident_description:
We have a Kenmore smoothtop electric range and have been experiencing problems with the burners not shutting off, coming on without being turned on, and changes to the temperature of the cooking element without changing the dial.  This evening we used the left front burner and 10 minutes after it was turned off the burner lit up to high and then shut off several times.  Immediately after that, the unit began making an arcing noise and suddenly sparks began shooting out of the top left control dial while the unit was turned off.  Thankfully we were home at the time and I have turned the circuit breaker off for the unit.   Had we not been home there could have easily been a fire.

I have been online to check for any recall notices for our unit and while Frigidaire issued a recall notice back in 2009, our unit was not listed in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range with potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Wednesday, 3/7/2012 our KitchenAid dishwasher model KUDM01TJBL0 spewed smoke and shot flames out of the upper-right corner of the door.

We had started a load of dishes washing and within 5 minutes the unit started making very loud, crackling and popping noises, and started sending out thick, black smoke.  I wasn't sure what to do, but I thought that opening the dishwasher door might cut the power to whatever was burning.  I pulled open the door just as flames started to shoot out of the upper-right corner of the door.  The flames only lasted a few seconds after that.

The circuit breaker the dishwasher was on did not trip the whole time; I turned off the circuit breaker myself shortly after the flames extinguished.  We ran fans to clear the house of the smoke and the house smelled like burnt plastic for a couple of days.  Other than the dishwasher itself, there was no other damage.

I took the dishwasher door apart and took pictures of the area that caught fire.  It was the controller circuit board that burnt, along with a few connectors, a low-voltage ribbon cable that disintegrated, and a shell holding the controller board that had a hole melted through it.

I've searched online, and I've found other pictures of KitchenAid dishwashers that caught fire, and the damage to the circuit boards is very similar, so this seems to be a common failure mode.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injuries or deaths, and similar failures have been reported online, indicating a possible common issue.

incident_description: Recall of dishwasher was not reported to consumer. Dishwasher caught fire during operation.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Opened LG refrigerator this morning to find butter melted and light fixture had fallen down, lights on although refrigerator door was closed. Lights had partially melted the top of a yogurt container.  Inside plastic on the top of the unit was hot to the touch and burning plastic odor permeated all.  Smoke damage inside. Went to the basement and tripped the breaker to shut off electricity to unit.

LG instructed me to remove the light bulbs and they would arrange repair, covering parts and labor.  They had my contact information in their database but never contacted me to notify me that there is a problem with this unit, which is troubling.  It seems likely from the amount of commentary on the internet about this problem that the problem is well known to them.  The unit is a LG LFC25760SW with serial number beginning with 704.  Purchased in 2007.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted items, smoke damage) but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The widespread commentary online suggests this is a known issue, making occurrence likely.

incident_description:
I recently put a pot of water on my glass GE stove top and went into the living room. About 2 minutes later I heard this deafening boom. I returned to the kitchen and the entire stovetop had exploded and sent shards of glass, some of them 8 to 10 inches long, across the kitchen. If I had been in the kitchen at the time, it would have seriously maimed me at the least or could have killed me outright. After 4 months of trying to get GE to replace and install another stove top, they have decided to charge me for a new stove top and installation because "It is out of warranty". I asked them if the original warranty covered explosions and they admitted it did not so I asked them if explosions weren't covered in the warranty what did it matter if it was under warranty or not? I asked them if they designed their stove tops to explode. They said they didn't so I told them if you don't design them to explode, then the stove tops which do explode must be defective. They then said that they couldn't be sure that I hadn't done something to cause it to explode so I told them they couldn't prove that I had so it was a moot point. One tech told me that if something like a frying pan or a food can were dropped on it, that could cause microfissures which later could cause it to explode.  Do they expect people to inspect the stovetop with a magnifying glass everytime before they use it?  What if they miss a microfissure when the inspect it?  Is it then the consumer's fault if it kills them?  If GE techs are aware that this could happen, shouldnÃÂt GE warn consumers or initiate a recall of the stovetops?  Is it possible that they feel that it would be less expensive to pay damages for injuries than to do a recall?

Searches online have shown other glass stovetops from other manufacturers have also exploded. I hope that no one is ever hurt by their product in the future but, if they ever are, I hope they (or their survivors) wind up owning GE. 

This is a multi-million dollar corporation and it would probably cost them less than $100 to do the right thing but instead they price a new stove top at over $500 plus close to$200 dollars for installation.  My next stove top will definitely not be glass.  I hope you can bring this to your viewers' attention before someone IS hut or killed.

justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion with potential for severe injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Hot plate area of coffee maker started smoking while keeping coffee hot.  Brew completed. Smell of burning rubber.  Quickly unplugged and moved outdoors.
justification: The coffee maker started smoking and emitted a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury occurred as it was quickly unplugged and moved outdoors.

incident_description: About 2 weeks ago we had some friends over the dishwasher was running I stepped into the kitchen to get some things and saw a small haze  thru the air it smelled like something was burning.  I called my husband and a friend came in they smelled it to we checked all over the house and the smell was coming from the dishwasher area.  We turned the dishwasher off thinking the unit was done as it had not been drying the dishes completely it was in the house when we bought the home.  I did not use it again until trying to yesterday.  I tried to restart it to drain the water in the base but it would not turn on.  So I drove to town and purchased a new dishwasher.  Upon removing the bosch dishwasher the electric lines going in are burnt about 3 to 4 inches up.  My husband went downstairs and did find the breaker was popped.  Thank god, we were out of town for a weekend and if that breaker had not popped we could have lost our home and pets.  Today I looked online for recall or issues and found some dishwashers had been recalled for the same problem.  My model number is not on the list.

I purchased 16 piece set of Anchor Hocking Rio style glassware about 3 months ago. I had a tumbler break while in the dishwasher. It had a right triangle shape break off the top of the glass, about 1.5 inches by 2 inches.
The dishwasher was ran on a normal cycle with energy saving (low heat) dry cycle.
It was on the top shelf, and did not have any other items close that could have banged into it.
Used Finish brand dishwasher tablets,  I do not use abrasive items to scrub the glasses.
justification: The glass broke in the dishwasher but no injury was reported, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
Christmas Eve, 2011. Glass dish 9x12 pyrex brand exploded in front of us at the dinner table.
Cooked lasagna, let it cool on side of oven then transferred to table. Within minutes, popping sound, then hundreds of glass pieces on table, on floor, tiny pieces, big pieces. Total mess. No one touched dinner, some thought they could eat from the middle. but when we picked it up, the glass went up from the bottom of the dish into the meal .
Feel very strongly a consumer report should be put out about this product.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: We have a Maytag ceramic top range. On Friday (3/9) night, my wife was baking chicken when all of a sudden there was a loud crackling noise coming from the oven. There were flames and sparks flying. We shut the oven off and called the fire department. They came and said the heating element was the cause. The range is not new but 2-3 years ago, Maytag ha da recall due to heating element issues. We filled out the necessary paperwork and the service company came and replaced the heating element. Should the element have failed in this manner which could be a real safety hazard? Thank you.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks but no injury or death occurred, and the fire department confirmed the cause was a faulty heating element.

incident_description: My wife and I were in the Kitchen when we heard the range making a buzzing noise. My wife was cooking dinner and had the oven set on convection. We both looked at the range when we heard the buzzing sound, that when we saw an orange yellow light illuminating behind the oven which lasted 3-5 seconds, the display went out and black smoke followed. It would be understandable if had buzzed and then stopped working, however I am very disturbed that this product cased a fire to start.
justification: The incident involved a buzzing noise, an orange-yellow light, and black smoke from the oven, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Our dishwasher is about four years old and has had no previous issues.  One evening it began to produce a strange smell during a normal wash cycle. The fumes grew stronger and more noxious the next time we ran it, so we turned off and opened the dishwasher before it finished the wash cycle. We could see no heavy scale buildup on the heating element nor obstructions in the drain.  We then disconnected the power supply and removed the front base plate.  On the underside of the dishwasher, we saw that one of the wires attached to the heating element was completely exposed.  About an inch of insulation and the connector had melted away - the melting plastic was emitting the fumes every time the heating element turned on.  There also appeared to be some corrosion on the brass connector to which the wire is soldered.  We have not used the dishwasher since then because of concerns of a risk of overheating and fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with exposed wires and melting insulation, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I wish to report a safety concern regarding a Kenmore Dishwasher that I purchased from Sears at the Arnot Mall, Horseheads, New York. 
On March 14 2012 my wife loaded the dishwasher and started a normal wash cycle.  Within six or seven minutes heavy dark smoke began to pour out of the upper control panel of the machine.  I immediately opened the dishwasher door in order to stop the wash cycle but the machine continued to run throwing hot water out into the kitchen and the smoke also continued to come from the upper control panel.  In order to stop the machine I went to the main house electrical box and turned off the circuit breaker which stopped the machine although smoke continued to come out of the panel.   I then took my tools and removed the control panel to insure the fire was extinguished.  The fire appears to have started in the wiring ribbon (tail) that connects to the electrical circuit board.  I have taken some photos of the damaged components for reference.  
Machine History:
Kenmore Dishwasher
Model:  665.17483300
S/N:  FP4402110
Stock: 17483
Type: 55770
Purchased: Sears, Arnot Mall, 3/13/2004

Although damage to my home was limited to heavy smoke odor and slight discoloration to the underside of the kitchen counter top I am most concerned about what might have occurred had I not been standing next to the machine when this occurred.  I believe this situation needs to be fully investigated by the manufacturer (Whirlpool) and Sears.  It appears that the door latch assembly may have worn through the wire ribbon after years of use.  This is an out of warranty situation and replacement of the damaged parts needed to repair the machine far exceed the cost of a new machine.  
I contacted Sears Customer Support to report a "potential product safety issue" but after being passed off to five different people in multiple departments it became obvious that no one cared nor had any idea  on how to handle my concern, therefore I am turning you your organization.
The following sears part numbers identify each part of the machine that were damaged due to the fire.  Board=8538871, Control Panel=8558062,  Handle=8269632,  Latch bolt=8193882,   Electric Control=8564543,  Actuator=8524471,  Wire tail assembly=8539449,  Thermal Fuse=8193762
justification: The incident involved heavy smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
On 2/12/2012 I bought a Black & Decker countertop oven at Sear's.  The model  number is TRO480BS.  I used it for the second time (3/13/2012) today to toast a bagel. All three knobs were on the correct settings for toasting.  The timer has a picture of a bagel which must be a couple of minutes.  The timer went off and I took the bagel out.  As I walked away the glass door exploded sending hundreds of tiny pieces of glass all over my kitchen.  I luckily,  recently bought metal shelving unit and had placed  the oven lower than counter height and away from the high traffic area in my kitchen.  If I would have had this on the regular height kitchen counter the glass would have exploded onto my face arms and chest.  When I realized what had just happened I stepped on some pieces of glass and sustained several minor cuts on the bottom of my feet not realizing I was barefoot.
     I found the receipt and booklet and called Black & Decker immediately.  They were apologetic and said they would send a new oven out to me or a refund.  I took the replacement oven but am curious about incidents you may have received on this model oven.  They would forward my incident to engineering.  What I would like to know if this is an isolated incident or if there are other reports of this problem.
     Most ovens and toasters are kept at very little distance from one's face and body on a regular height kitchen counter.  An incident like mine would have sent me to the hospital with cuts on my arms and face.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts on feet) and could have been more severe if the oven was at counter height, but the likelihood of such an event is low based on the description.

The water did not hit me in the face, but it cold have if it were pointed at me.  As it was, it just sprayed boiling water droplets on my hand.  I would consider it a design defect to have the hot water exit point on a location (the lid) that can lift to point it at you.

incident_description:
I loaded the KitchenAid dishwasher at 7:45, pressed "normal" and "energy saver dry" and start.  I left to take my son to preschool.  At 8:15, I returned home to a house filled with the smell of melted plastic.  The dishwasher light had switched to "energy saver dry" only but water was still cycling.  I attempted to turn off the dishwasher by pressing "cancel" but nothing happened.  I opened the door hoping to turn off the machine.  Water spewed everywhere and the dishwasher kept running.  I ran to the control panel and switched off the fuse.  I could not see any damage to the washer.  I allowed the dishwasher to sit about an hour and turned the fuse back on.  Then, I pressed "normal" and "start".  Immediately the light switched back to "energy saver dry" only.  Again, the only way I could stop the machine was to flip the fuse in the control panel.  A neighbor disconnected the electric from the dishwasher at the dishwasher.  After the dishwasher cooled down, I removed the panel and found the circuit board black with smoke and wires were beginning to melt.

I immediately called KitchenAid Customer Service.  The representative said KitchenAid had not received a complaint like this with this model dishwasher.  She offered to schedule a service tech visit at my expense.  I requested to be transfered to her manager.  [REDACTED],  wrote up the incident, Ref #[REDACTED].

incident_description:
We are writing to alert GE to a serious fire safety hazard with one of your older electric
ranges. In 1998 we bought a GE Profile self-cleaning electric range MODEL NO.
JBP79W Y3WW (serial No. GT51923G) from an authorized dealer who installed it.
The range served us well until last Sunday evening, February 5, 20012 when we turned
it on to "Broil High" to toast a bun in the oven. Within a minute, the inside of the oven
was sparking and flashing like a welding torch. The oven door was closed and we shut
off the electric panel breaker to to stove which stopped the electrical arcing that was
going on inside the oven.
After the smoke cleared and the oven cooled down we saw that the upper electric
element had burned through leaving about a two inch gap in the element - enclosed are
some pictures we took of the burned out coil. We understand that there have been no
recalls on this stove.
Our concern is that if this had happened with a steak or chops in the oven there would
have been a serious fire. We rarely use the broiler and then usually to brown garlic
bread, rolls or casseroles.
We replaced the old range with a new GE electric Model [REDACTED] and hope that
when it dies it goes out with a whimper not a flashlbang the way this one did.
We are genuinely concerned that this may prove harmful to other owners of this GE
Range.

On my "GE" brand electric blender model # 169202, the drive gear of the blade assembly had cracked during operation and a small quantity of smoke came from the blender as the motor continued to drive the plastic gear on the square nut of the blade shaft. When the blender body was removed from the motor base small plastic fragments were visible as well as a smear of melted plastic across the square nut. This occurred while making a smoothie with frozen fruit, which must have jammed the blades. The blender was returned to Wal-Mart and was replaced under the two year warranty. It would be difficult to be injured in such an incident, and even running unattended the blender has a 3 minute automatic shut off which, I think, would prevent any fire concern from the melting plastic. I thought I would notify you of this incident in case there are other reports of problems with this product.
justification: The incident involved a cracked drive gear and smoke emission, but no injury or fire occurred due to the automatic shut-off feature.

incident_description:
I purchased a plastic coffee tumbler from Starbucks a few months ago. It was a Christmas theme mug with the message Let's Merry. I drank some coffee from it this morning but decided to reheat the coffee so I took it to the microwave, put it inside the microwave and set it for 1 minute. I walked around the room and noticed flames inside the microwave and a horrible burning smell. I stopped the microwave and took out the mug. It turns out that metallic in the lettering of the coffee tumbled caught fire. 

I then poured out the coffee to see if it said "DO NOT MICROWAVE". No where did I see that. I finally noticed that it was etched into the lid but the way I read it, it means not to microwave the lid, nothing about the tumbler. So I called Starbucks, they said that a paper insert inside the mug says not to microwave it. They also said that plastic mugs should not be microwaved since they can melt or disform. I told her that I wasn't worried about the melting, you guys added metal to a plastic container that the average person would never notice. She never took my personal info, just said that she would tell corporate.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injury was reported, making it a minor incident with low likelihood due to specific conditions (metal in lettering).

incident_description:
I purchased a Maytag Gas Range Oven(Gemini) in early 2007, Model MGR6775BDS, Serial 11722825JX.

On March 11, 2012, I had a 8 oz cup of water next to my gas range. I accidently knock the cup spilling some water onto my counter top and the top of the gas range. Some water spilled into the control knobs of the gas jets. At the moment of the spill I grabbed a paper towel to pick up the spill and  the electric ignitor activated without the knob turning. The electric ignitor was active for approximately 3-4 seconds, while I attempted to turn the knob to shut of the ignitor, without success because the knob was already in the off position. It was at this time a flame burst out of the knob while arm was above it, causing damage to the sleeve of my bathrobe. I was able to contain the flame and shut of the main breaker to my electrical panel, avoiding a potential tragedy to my family and myself.
justification: The incident resulted in damage to clothing and a flame burst, indicating potential for injury, though none was reported.

Normally these glasses are quite durable and can take a fall to the floor or in a sink without damage. Upon inspecting some of the other glasses, I found one with a small shard missing from its bottom. As a result I have boxed all of these up and put into storage for the time being.

incident_description:
Purchased a Maytag Gas Range (Model MGR7775WB) in July, 2011.  I had several incidents of leaning against the knobs on the front of the range and having them turn on just enough to allow the gas to come through.  Once I was leaning over the stove to clean it and the knob turned on and the gas burner ignited right under me. Luckily I was not burned.  In the fall I contacted the Maytag customer service and explained my problem and my concerns through their on-line system.  I few days later I received a voice mail from someone at Maytag regarding my complaint. Over the next several weeks I called the number I was given and left messages that I was returning this message.  No one ever called me back.  The problem has continued, although I have tried to be more careful when working around my stove.  I have had gas ranges all my life, and have never had this problem.  All of the ranges I had in the past required me to firmly push in on the knob and then overcome a slight friction or bump in order to turn on the gas.  On this stove, there does not seem to be this "friction" factor, so casually leaning against the knobs allows them to turn just enough to allow the gas to come through.

Yesterday I was in my kitchen, not doing anything at my range, and left the room for about 45 minutes.  When I returned, I noticed a strong odor of gas and looked at the range, and sure enough one of the knobs was slightly turned on.  It must have happened as I brushed by the stove, as I did not use it for anything, nor did I work at or near it.  I quickly left the room, opened a window on the back porch and went to a distant part of the house to allow the gas to dissipate.

I sent another communication to the Maytag corporation about this continuing problem.  someone did call me back immediately.  Her reply to my complaint was that she would "make a note of this design issue." and to urge "caution" when around my range.  My concern was that this situation is extremely dangerous.  Had i left my house for the entire day, my house would have been full of gas by the time I got home and could easily have exploded when I returned and opened the door.  (Some years ago I had a house a couple of doors down from a house where this exact scenario happened. It literally exploded off its foundations when accumulated gas from a leak ignited.)  I also pointed out that I or someone else could be severely burned if a burner ignited again while someone was leaning over the stove.  This also represents a danger to homes where there are small children, as a small child could with NO EFFORT whatsoever turn on the gas burners of this stove.  She seemed completely uninterested in this issue of the potential dangers here.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage and potential ignition, which could lead to severe injury or death, but no actual harm has occurred yet.

1.

incident_description:
We had been at home and having our usual morning coffee on the weekend.  Me and my wife each had a cup and the warming plate was still on, keeping the remaining pot of coffee warm.  A little later in the morning I heard a very loud hissing noise coming from the kitchen.  When I went to investigate, I found the noise was coming from the coffee maker.  It appeared that the coffee was starting to boil and there was foul smoke coming out of the machine.  I quickly unplugged it and took the whole unit outside and set it in my lawn.

There was plenty of coffee in the carafe and the warming plate should not get as hot as it did - to the point where something in the device started melting.  We worry what could have happened if I was not as close by as I was and it actually caught fire or the carafe exploded from the extreme heat.  We would often use the programmable feature of the coffee maker- so it is extra scary to think of what could have happened if we were asleep at the time.  This is actually a replacement unit sent to me by Cuisinart after the one we had bought in the store just stopped working.

I checked Amazon product reviews for this particular model and it looks like it is not just me- others have reported similar experiences.

It is the Cuisinart Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffee Maker, Model DCC-1200
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that could have led to a fire or explosion, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Here is a copy of a letter that I wrote to Kenmore on 2/22/12. I received no response from them:

I purchased a Kenmore Model 790.95200102 Electric Range (Serial number: VF20905230) on 3/12/2002. I would like to report a serious safety issue. In recent weeks, the range has been having intermittent problems where the oven would not heat properly. When set to a certain temperature (e.g., 350 degrees) the preheat light would come on, but it would never heat up to the proper temperature. Eventually after turning it off and on a few times we were usually able to get it to work after much frustration. This has been occurring with increasing regularity.

Then, Monday night a much more serious problem occurred. My wife was baking a batch of granola in the oven at 200 degrees and everything was working fine, when all of a sudden the house was filled with smoke and the smoke alarms started going off. When we came running into the kitchen we found that the oven had mysteriously turned on the broil element and had set the granola on fire. I had to use a fire extinguisher to put out the flames and kill the circuit breaker to turn off the range. The digital display was showing an error code (I believe it was P1 or F1).

After doing some online research, it appears that the clock/timer control board is the likely culprit. I have ordered repair parts to install from www.SearsPartsDirect.com at a total cost of more than $210 (which is outrageous), but the expected delivery of the parts is not for almost a week.

My wife asked if she could at least use the stovetop while we were waiting for the parts. I decided to see if that would work so I turned the circuit breaker back on and tried the stovetop, which appeared to be operating normally. About an hour later while we were in other parts of the house the smoke alarm started going off again. The oven had decided to turn itself back on to broil mode without anyone even touching the oven controls, and had reignited the remnants of the granola that we had not cleaned out since we were waiting for the oven to cool. Once again the house was filled with smoke causing even more smoke damage.

THIS IS A SERIOUS SAFETY ISSUE! If we had not been at home, our house could have burned down. I believe that you should consider issuing a recall of this range to fix this problem. It is not acceptable that the range should ever turn itself on without user actions. The control circuitry should be designed such that if it ever fails it will never fail in a way that turns the unit on!


POSTSCRIPT: We replaced the clock/timer control board and the oven is now working properly, so that was apparently the culprit
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused a fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.
