The consumer pulled the circuit breaker  that controlled the power to the dishwasher. The retailer was contacted on 2/14/2012 and she was advised that her model was not affected by a recall.  

The consumer was advised by the representative that she spoke with (name not provided) that she would forward the information to CPSC.

The consumer indicated  that her concerns are if she was not home there could have possibly been a  fire in her dishwasher causing her to lose her home, or asleep at night, and loss of a family member.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames but no injury or death occurred, and the fire extinguished on its own.

incident_description: Black smoke came out of the dishwasher during the drying cycle. The upper right hand area of the door is sooty and blackened.
justification: Black smoke and soot indicate a fire-related incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: KitchenAid Dishwasher model KUDS0/DJBT0 ser num FK3501337 control panel caught fire, filled house with plastic smelling dense smoke and waking us from sleep. Unit would not turn off, switched circuit breaker off. Electronic control panel destroyed.
justification: The dishwasher's control panel caught fire and filled the house with smoke, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
This is a second identical incident with this product. The first, 09/08/2011, I accepted as just an unusual accident. However, on 02/23/2012, the exact same separation of the handle from the carafe occurred.
The handle separates from the carafe during ordinary use. I'm careful with my possessions. My appliances generally last for years but this one created identical problems in less than one year.

I just realized that had either of the carafes contained hot espresso at the time the carafes fell from the handles that hot liquid and glass could have injured anyone ( or pet ) in the area. I. Guess I was lucky that they were empty each time.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. If I'm being an alarmist I'm sorry for taking your time with a trivial matter.
justification: The handle separation occurred twice during ordinary use, but no injuries were reported as the carafes were empty. The potential for injury exists if hot liquid is present.

incident_description: The consumer says when walking by the knobs and brushing against them, they quickly turn to the on position.  The consumer says that gas has filled the apartment of one of his tenants because of this issue.  It has also happened in his own home for the same reason.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who sent him to consumer relations Dept and was on hold for 30 minutes but no one ever answered.  Their have been three occurrences of strong smelling gas scent.
justification: The incident involves gas filling the apartment due to knobs turning on easily, posing a risk but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
A home owner started the self-cleaning function of his built-in oven.  About 30 minutes later the oven began smoking and the smoke alarm sounded.  He called 9-1-1 and fire department personnel responded.  The oven was pulled from its shelf in the wall.  The shelf that held the oven had started burning.   The fire damage was concentrated on the supporting shelf, which was holding the oven in place. A review of the installation instruction manual found that no space was called for between the oven and the wooden particle board shelf. 

It was apparent that the heat of the oven transferred into the particle board shelf through radiant and conductive heat. A small hole was burned through the particle board and fire began to extend up into the back portion of the wooden cabinet. Fire was extinguished at that point and was confined to the immediate area of fire origination
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to the oven shelf and cabinet, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer placed a microwavable meal on the metal rack inside the microwave on four minutes. With one minute remaining, one of the plastic clips used to hold the microwave caught fire. 

 When the door was opened to the microwave and the fire extinguished itself. The inside of the microwave has scorch marks there.

The firm was contacted and  consumer was advised that a appliance could be repaired for $200.00. The consumer declined in the repairs.

The consumer indicated that her concerns are that the failure could occur again with the other three clips. She discarded the metal rack and has decided to replace the microwave.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury, and the consumer has taken steps to mitigate future risks by discarding the metal rack.

incident_description:
At 6 pm, we began a three-hour self cleaning cycle on our Frigidaire oven/cooktop (model PLEFMZ99ECA, serial VF53147024). Even for a self-cleaning cycle, it produced a lot of smoke.

At 9 pm, the display showed the cycle ending. However, no reduction in smoke followed, and a large amount of heat was still generated.

At 11 pm, we began looking for the breaker, which we located and threw at 12 pm. Shortly afterward, we discovered the range had been recalled. At this point we opened the door after checking to make sure that the oven itself was not the primary heat source.

At 2 pm, the stove was still too hot to touch and emitting smoke. In order to rule out the possibility of an electrical fire, we had to call the fire department. They moved the oven outside and tested for carbon monoxide.

We were glad to see our model had been recalled. We hope that you take any similar concerns seriously; obviously any wiring issues in a self-cleaning oven are extremely hazardous!
justification: The incident involved excessive smoke and heat from a recalled oven, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Danger! Danger! Danger! We have a Cuisinart mini Prep and the blade broke as well, smashed hole in the container and flew across the room. Thank goodness our 5 and a half year old granddaughter wasn't with Grandma when this happened. This is a serious problem and this is the only forum where the problem is listed. e-mail me for pictures. [REDACTED] I have not posted this anywhere else, I am not disingenuous and I am very concerned about the safety of the users of this product. Yes! Cuisinart just suggests that you buy a new blade and bowl. This is a product safety issue. This product is a potential killer!!!!!!!!!  [REDACTED]
justification: The blade broke and flew across the room, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Bosch SHU 9952 UC12 dishwasher caught fire about a year ago;  it was approximately eight years old.  Active flames were shooting from the terminal box, smoke was coming from the top of the door around the control buttons,  and the area of the door around the control module was extremely hot.  The fire damaged plastic near the terminal box and part of the wooden kitchen cabinet.  

I paid about $250 for the first repair visit during which the repairmen ONLY cleaned the ends of the wires and put on new wire nuts.  They refused to dismantle the door to check the reason for the door cover being hot and smoke coming from top of door.  Although the unit was properly wired to 12/2 wire and they did not ask for it to be changed, they insisted the wiring was faulty (I know, that's contradictory and confusing).  

The first use after their visit, the unit smoked again around the control buttons.  I called Bosch and they said it must be a faulty control module, which they would pay to replace.  The repairmen returned with the new module, installed it and promptly billed me for another visit (about $150 this time).  After a number of phone calls that charge was cancelled.

The unit has performed well ever since.  With the same wiring.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injuries were reported, and the issue was resolved after repairs.

incident_description: Our Kenmore Ultra-bake Stove model 9200-4102 Serial number #RP0315209 has a reoccurring problem which is very dangerous. On at least two separate occasion over the past few years has turned itself on a cleaning mode which causes the stove to heat up over 500 degrees and stay on. It does this randomly by itself and can't be turned off without someone pulling the breaker. It has only been luck that someone has found it before the stove has overheated itself and possibly lead to fire. We have continued to keep up a full warranty on the stove and the Sears contractors that come out say that it is a common problem. In each case, they have replaced some part on the stove as covered by our purchased warranty. The most recent incident was today. We feel that Kenmore is not addressing the overall problem; that they have a very dangerous, potentially deadly design flaw in this stove. Our suggestion would be that at the very least they place an override switch on the outside of the stove which disables the power to the stove so that a person may turn it off and know that it will remain off.
justification: The stove's random activation of cleaning mode poses a significant fire hazard, though no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: The left front burner turned on by itself in the highest temperature (Hi) it doesn't turn off, have to turn the breaker off from the house main panel.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his under the counter dishwasher is a potential safety hazard. The consumer stated that the dishwasher caught fire under the mechanical board. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was in a normal cycle for about 10-20 minutes before the product caught fire.

 The consumer opened the door of the dishwasher and the fire burned itself out. The consumer described the unit as unusable and there are burn marks to the stainless steel outer panel. The consumer found that his control panel has burned. The consumer could smell the electrical burning and also could hear a popping noise coming from the dishwasher. 

The consumer stated that his  model was cited in recall release 05-123 and poses the same hazard. The consumer stated that there no was no extensive property damage. The consumer was not injured by the product. The consumer did not call the fire department or his home insurance company. 

The consumer unplugged the unit from the wall outlet. The consumer called the firm today and their response was that his product was not on recall. The firm offered to fix the product at the consumerÃÂs expense. The consumer decided not to schedule a repair. The consumer called the retailer today and was referred to the firm.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire but self-extinguished, causing no injuries or extensive property damage, though the unit was rendered unusable.

incident_description:
I purchased a Whirlpool gas range on January 25, 2012.  After using the appliance for exactly one month, I called the appliance dealer (on February 25, 2012) to report extreme heat coming out of the oven vent while baking (at 350 degrees F) and that the face of the stove where the knobs are located also heats to a dangerously high temperature - easily causing a burn within seconds of touching the surface - 120 degrees F.  While simultaneously using one front burner to heat a kettle of water to boiling, which takes approximately 7 minutes, that temperature increases to 138 degrees F.

The appliance dealer sent a service technician to my home on March 5, 2012.  He reported that the oven flue was venting properly and the internal temperature of the oven was heating as expected.  He verbally stated that the front panel where the knobs are located was very hot and encouraged me to contact Whirlpool.

I called Whirlpool on March 5, 2012 to report the problem.  They sent a service technician to my home on March 6, 2012 who confirmed that the flue was attached properly.  Again, he agreed that the surface of the front panel was very hot.

I called Whirlpool again on March 6, 2012 to report that I believed the range was unsafe to use.  I told them that I wanted to return the product and receive a refund for my purchase.  Whirlpool responded by stating that they would only address warranty issues (i.e., parts that needed to be fixed) and required a service technician to declare the product to be unsafe.  They would not accept a return or refund my money.

Another service technician is scheduled to come to my house to look at the appliance on March 12, 2012, but I do not anticipate any changes to the "diagnosis" of the appliance.

This product is unsafe, as a non-cooking surface becomes dangerously hot during typical use.
justification: The incident describes a dangerously hot surface that can cause burns within seconds, indicating a clear injury risk during typical use.

incident_description:
Microwave oven turned itself on, typically after longer cooking jobs (3 minutes or more). The unit entered one of the pre-programmed cooking cycles. It did not occur after the unit had a chance to cool down fully. Problems were avoided by leaving the door open slightly which engaged a safety switch and kept it from powering up. 

Manufacturer (Jenn-Air) was contacted and replaced the controller in NOV 2010. Issues started again and the controller was replaced again at no cost to me in FEB 2012.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself is an incident with no reported injury, and it occurs under specific conditions (after longer cooking jobs).

incident_description: Maytag plus refirerator cautgh on fire.lost food and damage to floor and cabinet and wall
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: The consumer says the dishwasher control panel caught on fire and burned.  She says the unit was on for about an hour prior to the incident.  The consumer says the unit has burn spots on it.  She contacted a repairman who got the control panel replaced.  The consumer says that she has seen numerous reports of the same thing happening to other consumers.  She did not see any smoke just smelled a terrible burning wire odor.  She contacted the manufacturer who said they never heard of such a thing.
justification: The incident involved a fire and burn damage but no injury or death, and similar incidents have been reported by other consumers, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: Dishwasher was on for dish washing and it did not stop after dry cycle. When somebody returned home, there was burning smell and when dishwasher door was opened it was full of smoke and everything was melted inside. The manual power off button did not work and had to switch off circuit breaker. If we would not have visited house in the afternoon, it could have put house on fire. Also, it could have posed serious risk during night time with kids in the house and other household members.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that could have caused a fire, posing serious risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My GE diswasher, Model PDW9980N00SS, S/N AM771925B, almost started a fire.  The drier's heating element either overheated or never turned off and melted the platice components in the dishwasher.  The plastic lower spray arm and the silverware bin melted.  It was discovered because a burning smell was coming into the kitchen.  The dishwasher had been turned out about 4-5 hours earlier.  Pictures are avaiable of the meltdown.
justification: The dishwasher's heating element malfunction caused melting of plastic components and a burning smell, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: My Frigidaire Stove Model PLEF398DCC, SN VF50641733 caught on fire in our kitchen, it was actually burning.  I was in the kitchen with my wife and she touched the Broil pad, she can't remember if she touched the start pad or not but there was a loud arching noise behind the control panel and flames shooting from the back of the stove.  The circuit breaker didn't trip, it just kept arching and burning.  I pulled the stove out and unplugged it to stop the arching.  The stove continued to burn for 10 or 15 seconds and the wall behind the stove was blackened.  If I hadn't been home the house would almost certainly have caught on fire.  Frigidaire supervisor [REDACTED] from Augusta Georgia didn't even care enough to send someone to look at what caused this fire because the stove is 7 years old and is out of warranty.  My wife and I, of course, did not want the stove fixed because we could never trust this stove again.  We thought Frigidaire should look at the stove to see what caused the fire before it burns down some ones home or worse.  They had the nerve to tell me they would send a technician if I would pay for the call!  I can not believe they didn't want to diagnose what caused this fire.  I visited their web site and told them I had contacted you and the NYS Department of State Consumer Assistance Unit.  After they read this they did send me an email and repeat the offer to come and look at the stove at my expense.  I have reported this problem to you and NYS, my conscience is clear. I don't know how the people at Frigidaire can sleep at night!
justification: The stove caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Yesterday evening, it preheated the over to 450. While pre-heating, I prepared the dish with milk, water, cheese and potatoes and spices, nothing was frozen, everything was room temperature. It was then placed in the preheated oven for 16 minutes, top covered with foil. I removed the dish once, placed it on the stove to remove the foil. The stove top had not be in use all day.
Place it back in the over for another 10 minutes. 1 minute before removing it from the over, it exploded sending broken glass pieces all over in the oven.
 
Upon further research, it seems this has occurred to others as well. The dish is old, possible 7 yr - is that considered old? I am rattled enough to not use Pyrex in the oven anymore, I don't think i'll be using it in the microwave either.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of a glass dish in the oven, but no injury was reported. The occurrence likelihood is 'possible' as similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool Over The Range Microwave Hood Combination 2003 with serial number starting with TR. It started by itself twice and we couldn't stop it by pushing cancel button on the control panel. We had to unplug it for it to stop running. It may pose a risk of fire.
justification: The microwave starting by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore stove model number 790.9601 that just exploded and caught fire.  The bottom heating element exploded.  My wife was alone and our house could have burned to the ground. I have owned many stoves throughout my life and not once has this happened.  It was purchased in 2005.  I called Sears and they are happy to send someone to my house for a minimum fee of $129, not including parts.  No helpful advice for recalls or anything offered.  They weren't willing to tell me how much the part was or alternative places to get a part, as I was maybe willing to fix it myself.   They had not heard of this problem before, yet I can do a simple search on google and find thousands upon thousands of reports on this very matter.  I was hoping you all could provide some advice or feedback. I can't figure out why there isn't a recall or something being done about this problem.  My wife could have died tonight while I was at work.  Luckily she was close enough to the kitchen to hear it explode and shut the breaker off.
justification: The stove exploded and caught fire, posing a significant risk of injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore Wall Oven model nimber 79047789405 outer door glass blew out all over the kitchen while baking.
justification: The oven door glass blowing out is an incident that could cause injury, but the description does not mention any injury occurring.

incident_description:
I was cooking with gas on the stove top.
The stem that controls the flame came loose and the flame went out of control. The front left burner had fallen apart leaking gas in the area under the dip pan surface. As the gas leaked fires burned from all of the burners, the sides front, and back of the range. I went out side and turned the gas off to the house.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak and uncontrolled fires, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Bosch dishwasher 
SHX47A05UC /14
FD830900738

Small electrical fire while dishwasher was running.  Produced a lot of smoke, but self-extinguished once power was removed.  Bosch website indicates that this dishwasher is not subject to the recent recall.
justification: The incident involved a small electrical fire that self-extinguished without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the dishwasher is not subject to recall and such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
On March 4, 2012 I was running our Kenmore Ultra Wash dishwasher, model # 665.16369301, serial number FR3515690.  It started making a strange noise so I went to the kitchen to investigate and there was a flame coming out of the top of the dishwasher so I opened the door to make it stop running.  When I opened it, it didnÃÂt stop running!!  I then turned off the switch to cut the electricity to the machine.  I am so glad I was home because I believe it could have caused a larger fire if I didnÃÂt cut off the electricity to the machine.

I also noticed an electrical burning smell and this stench lingered for over an hour.

I purchsed the machine in September 2004
justification: The incident involved a flame and electrical burning smell, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled by turning off the electricity.

incident_description: On 03/04/2012 cooking dinner with kenmore range 790.95354803, the broiler came on and started to burn the food. The fire alarm came on, I tried to turn of the unit and could not. the unit was flashing code "F10". I had to unplug unit to get it to stop working. This is worry sum because 1:it came on by itself and 2:it didn't shut itself off automatically and wouldn't let me shut it down unless i unplugged it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that caused a fire alarm but no injury, indicating a minor operational issue.

incident_description: My dishwasher was running on a normal wash when it started making grinding noises and smoke was coming out of the front of the control panel. The room was filled with toxic smoke fumes. The dishwasher would not stop flashing and smoking until the breaker was shut off.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: door on LG dishwasher falls down rapidly door initially had a counterweight or buffer to prevent this but now has become inoperable, if the door is closed lightly and not latched it will fall this happened to my wife and she received a large bruise on her leg.  A Child could have been seriously injured as this door weighs over 25lbs.
justification: The incident resulted in a large bruise on the wife's leg, indicating an injury, and the potential for serious injury to a child is noted.

incident_description:
I was preheating the oven at 350 degrees when I saw flames through the window.  Opened the oven door and found the lower heating coil on fire at the front middle section and winding its way along the left side to the back of the heating element.  It looked like a fuse was burning.

I shut off the oven, but the fire was still moving along the coil, then I shut off the main circuit breaker to the stove.  Fire finally stopped, but a portion of the coil broke off.  The bottom
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but was controlled without injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: We have a Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee-maker that briefly after brewing the coffee started to produce a lot of smoke.  There was a growing smell of plastic burning and fortunately my 5-yr old daughter caught it before we left the house.  I immediately unplugged it from the outlet.  I'm happy my house did not burn down, and sad to know that this happened to so many other people as I can see reported here without any serious action being taken against removing this product from the market.  Unfortunately, it will take somebody's house to burn down first it seems.
justification: The coffee-maker produced smoke and a burning smell, but no injury or property damage occurred. The incident is likely, as similar reports exist without serious action being taken.

incident_description: We purchased a Black & Decker TO1216B Toaster/Convection oven on 1/28/12.  When using it on 2/26/12, the glass door shattered and "exploded" out the front of the oven sending glass pieces as far as 8-10 ft across the kitchen and breaking the door of the oven.  We feel that this is a serious safety issue.  We contacted Black & Decker with this information but they do not seem concerned about this and want to replace this with another oven model that we have read on-line reviews of the exact same thing happening. It seems they are not taking this issue seriously and I fear that someone will get injured if this issue is not addressed.
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering and sending glass pieces across the kitchen, but no injury was reported. Online reviews suggest this issue is likely to occur with the same model.

incident_description:
My issue is with a General Electric Profile electric convection oven, purchased in late 2008.

When cooking something that gives off steam in the oven, the oven and stove control panel stops responding to keypresses. The oven and stove tops continue to heat away at their previous settings, but the oven can't be controlled by its control panel. It requires a shutoff at the circuit breaker panel to shut off the stove.

I'm only describing the last time it happened. I've had the control panel circuit board replaced and will have it replaced again, but it has happened four times in the past five years: every time, there is something releasing steam in the oven.

Clearly I have to control the oven from the power source and abandon monitoring the cooking.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven control panel that requires power shutoff, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
On March 3, 2012 my Whirlpool electric range GR478LXPQ0, RSO813194, purchased in 2005 malfunctioned during oven usage.  I couldn't cancel or adjust the temperature or time setting.  This went on for several minutes while both my husband and I pushed every button on the control panel.  Eventually it came back on and we were able to cancel it and turn it off.  This is the 4th or 5th time this has happened.  The first few times it happened, the oven was set over 450 and we couldn't cancel it at all.  We had to turn off the circuit breaker and eventually it cools down and works again.  My daughter has Whirlpool built-ins and this happens to her, too.  We thought the oven went into clean mode and locked itself so we never set it above 450 again, but last night the temp was at 350.  I have never used the clean feature for fear of fire because of this.  When it first happened, I called Whirlpool and they said they had never heard of this happening before.  When an unsolicited offer to insure the stove arrived in the mail, I took advantage of it.  A service call was placed for March 6.

I'll never buy a Whirlpool product again.
justification: The incident describes a malfunction without injury, but it has happened multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: I was using my blender as I usually do to blend bananas and after starting up the blender I was started to hear very loud popping sounds and immediately stopped the blender. I discovered that the stainless steel blade had broke off and was being blended inside the pitcher cracking the jar. There were no inuries, just very frightening and lucky it didn't pierce the container entirely.
justification: The incident involved a broken blender blade and a cracked pitcher, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: We have a Maytag dishwasher.  For several months, the dishwasher and dishes had a funny smell after running through the cleaning cycle.  One morning, after breakfast, I ran the dishwasher and went on an errand, returning home approximately 1 hour 15 minutes later.  The kitchen smelled of burnt plastic and there was black smoke coming from the top of the dishwasher door.  There was sticky, black soot on the top edge of the door and on the inside of the door.  I had recently heard a news report about a dishwasher recall so checked online to see if our unit was included in it.  It was not - the recall was for units with a plastic tub, ours is stainless steel.  I called the dealer where the unit was purchased and a repairman was assigned to help us.  When he took the panel off the door, the coating on the wires was melted and there was exposed  wiring.  He said it could easily have started a fire.  He said that many dishwashers were having trouble with the liquid rinse aid getting into the wiring, and this was possibly the result of that action.  The cost to repair the unit was $246.00.  We wonder why the stainless steel tub units were not included in the recall -- it is a serious safety matter and should be investigated.  Also, an issue of the liquid rinse aid leaving its housing and corroding the wiring should also be scrutinized.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with visible smoke and melted wiring, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: For the third time now since having my electric range, all of a sudden while cooking food in the oven, the temperature skyrockets out of controL, burning the food. The food would have caught fire if I was not in the kitchen when it happened. Then, once the burnt food has been removed from the oven, I cannot get the oven to shut off. The heating element continues to burn bright orange and produce major amounts of heat until we shut off the breaker to the oven. In the past, we have been able to turn the breaker back on and the oven has reset itself and has seemingly returned to normal. However, on this most recent occasion, once we turned the breaker back on, the heating element turned back on without us turning the oven on. When we came back into the house about 30 minutes later, we could smell something burning, which was the oven. We had no idea it would turn back on by itself.
justification: The incident involves uncontrolled overheating and potential fire risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I had the oven set to bake. I noticed the oven seemed to be glowing so when I opened it the broiler was on. The panel display was showing bake. When I turned off the oven it popped and sparked behind the range.  The main control circuit board on the back was partially melted and burnt.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with sparks and a burnt circuit board, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I was cooking meat in the oven according to package directions (375 degrees for 60-70 minutes) and using a timer.  Before the timer went off, I opened the oven because it was smoky.  The food had burned and the oven was full of smoke.  I immediately removed the food and turned off the oven.  The oven display then registered F3 E3 or E3 F3.  About 10 minutes later, I returned to the kitchen and the oven still seemed very hot and smoky.  I opened the oven and the broiler was on, even though the oven was turned off.  I now believe that the oven switched into self-cleaning mode during cooking.  I kept trying to turn the oven off by hitting the power button, but it remained on.  The entire house filled with smoke.  I turned off the power at the home's circuit breaker and we pulled the oven out away from the cabinets.  The wood of the cabinets on either side of the oven was very hot.  We had to open our attic and several windows to minimize the smoke in the house, which my sleeping children were breathing.  This morning, the sides of the oven were still warm.

I am certain that if I had not cut off the power when I did, this oven would have started a fire.
justification: The incident involved significant smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We have received this range brand new with the house we purchased, the product is not heavily used, several times a month at the most.

On Friday,  02-Mar-2012 the oven was put on 400 degrees to preheat and bake some dinner. However, the heating element became red-hot and white and blue and sizzling, you can hear noise like fire crackers. Turning the oven off would not stop the process. We called 911 and the fire department came to unplug the oven and to find out the lower heating element had snapped or burned through - see the attached picture.

After the incident I recall an experience from several months ago where the stove would just become red-hot, no matter where you selected it to be between 1 - 10.

This leads me to think that this is an extremely dangerous product with major engineering flow which can cause fire, death and loss of property.

Please take this into consideration as there may be other people who own the product and be unware of what might be coming. The serial number was not found on this site. The label reads the following:
Sears Roebuck 911.93712020 / 2L220520Q
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that became dangerously overheated, requiring fire department intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: the product is a Kenmore Range. The left front burner will at times go out of control. no matter what the setting is, it will go to high and unable to shut burner off with control. the breaker has to be used to shut off. this is the second time it has done this. the model is 790.9611340A
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Control Board on Kenmore Dishwasher Model 66516032402, Serial No. FS3604991 overheated while it was in operation. Heavy black smoke came out of the top right front of the unit. Shut off the power to unit before any damage could be done.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoke but was controlled without injury or further damage.

incident_description:
General Electric model no. JGBP28MEM7BS Electric Ignition Model
Knob pose a danger to children and adults.
The knob can easily move from the OFF position and gas starts to be released into the area.

My mother (a senior with diminishing senses) was putting away the food on the stove. She must've accidentally leaned on it or moved or brushed against the knob.   She goes off to watch her soap and about 20 minutes later or so I go into the kitchen and since I have an over sensitive sense of smell I immediately smelled the gas and when I looked at the stove I noticed one of the knobs was just slightly out of the OFF position. I immediately turned it all the way to off, turned on the vent, of which I see in the apartments it goes no where except back in. Managed to turn on the stove to let the fire burn whatever was around. 
I know, after thinking about it now it could've blown up on my if there had been enough gas in the air, but I panicked. I went towards the windows near my mom and the smell of gas was there too, but my mom did not even notice.

I shudder to think what would've happened to her and she had gone to sleep with that gas going.

With the knobs in the front any small child can touch and move those knobs.
I would like to request a recall of these stoves too as they pose a danger to all homes and families.
It was manufactured in MEXICO in 2003 from what I could find.

Thank you for your help.
PS - This is not my home but my mom's apartment.
justification: The incident involved gas leakage due to accidental knob movement, posing a serious risk of explosion or poisoning, though no injury occurred this time.

incident_description:
Cleaned glass shelf in Fridigaire, model FRT21IL4FW4.
Glass shattered and hand cut.
Suggest label indicating:  Clean on flat surface only.  Glass can shatter if not on flat surface.
[REDACTED].
justification: The incident resulted in a hand cut, which qualifies as an injury, and the suggestion to add a warning label indicates this could happen again without intervention.

incident_description: Two burners spontaneously started on electric range top. They could not be turned off without unplugging the stove. The burners were very hot; hotter than one would use to cook.
justification: The burners malfunctioned and became dangerously hot, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Cuisinart DCC1200 Coffee Maker Serial # 00914
The unit started smoking very bad and the coffee was starting to boil.
This unit is a fire hazard. I am glad that I was home to hear and smell it.
I pulled out the plug immediately.
I did research online at Amazon and this is a common complaint from the customer reviews on this product. It should be recalled and the problem should be corrected.
The unit is 14 months old it is covered under a 3 year warranty but the company requires you to pay for shipping  and a $10 payment to cover S&H to return. Customers should not have to pay for a common hazardous product only to be replaced by another defective product.
justification: The coffee maker started smoking and boiling, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Online reviews indicate this is a common issue, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Toaster oven with rear "pizza bump out"  overheats at exterior back and melted two appliance cords.
justification: The toaster oven overheated and melted appliance cords, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: While washing a brand new, just out of the box, Anchor Hocking 16oz drinking glass, a chunk broke off, making a rather large cut/laceration on my index finger. I was hand washing all the glasses because there were no instructions given in the box. I had washed all the 11.5oz glasses and was the seventh 16oz glass when it broke. There was no damage to the glass before hand, as I inspected all of them before putting them into the sink prior to washing.
justification: The glass broke, causing a large cut on the index finger, resulting in an injury.

incident_description:
During normal operation, our Kenmore Elite dishwasher caught fire.  My two children, wife and I were asleep at the time.  Smoke filled the house.  We inhaled the smoke as we woke, called 911 and evacuated the house.  The fire department arrived and located the problem:  electrical components within the dishwasher door.  The top of the door of the dishwasher was charred, melted plastic.  I have photos.  The underside of my countertop is also charred.  I am thankful that our smoke alarms functioned properly and woke us before the fire further threatened my family.

I emailed Kenmore to report the problem and received no response.  I called and got nowhere.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke inhalation, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My Amana Instabroil gas range model ARGS7650S, serial number 0011249107 purchased in Jan 0f 2001 started on fire last night. (3/1/2012). The electronic display module made a crackling sound while the oven was on, and shortly afterwards started billowing acrid plastic smelling smoke. We immediately turned off the oven, but the smoke did not subside, and was getting worse. We scrambled to pull out the oven from the wall and unplug it. Once unplugged, the smoke subsided.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Maytag Portable Dishwasher, Model Number: MDC4650AWW, Started cleaning cycle as usual, about 90 minutes later I smelled something burning.  Walked into my kitchen and the floor was covered in 1/2" of hot water.  Water dripped through floor into basement, ruining ceiling.  Unplugged dishwasher and turned off water supply.  Opened door to dishwasher and steam/smoke escaped.  Smell of burning rubber was really intense.  No water remained inside.
justification: The incident involved property damage (water and smoke) but no reported injuries, making severity level 2. Such failures are uncommon but not unheard of in appliances, hence likelihood 2.

incident_description: We own a Magic Chef OTR Microwave.  While cleaning the inside we noticed what we thought was burned food on the track of the turntable.  Upon closer inspection it was determined that it was a scorched from what appears to be the light that illuminates the stove top.  It appears to have scorched the plastic turntable track from the underside.  We did contact Magic Chef, spoke to a representative-[REDACTED]-who said-Sorry, its out of warranty .. get it fixed and hung up.  We feel that if we had left this light on as a night light as we do when the grandchildren are around, that there was a good possibility of a fire starting.  I believe that someone should look into this problem.
justification: The incident involved scorching of the turntable track but no actual fire or injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood of recurrence is possible given the design flaw.

incident_description: I had the product just about 2 weeks.  Plugged it in and it burned up.  No flames but fried the electronics.
justification: The product burned up but there were no injuries or flames, only fried electronics.

incident_description: February 26th, 2012 I came home to find my Kenmore Oven broiler had turned on by itself. I was unable to turn it off using the cancel button.  I had to unplug the oven to get it to turn off. Smoke Detectors were going off, house was full of smoke and smelled of fumes.  My 17 year old was asleep downstairs.  Thank goodness I arrived home when I did.  I started researching online if anyone else has had this happen.  I am shocked that others had complained since 2009 up until just days ago.  Yet Sears will do nothing to compensate or recall product.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused smoke and fumes, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The stainless steel knobs that control the burner are located  on the right side of the range and the consumer feels that if they are accidently bumped they could possibly turned on the valve for the gas to be released.  There is also a delayed with the ignition as well which comes on well after gas is released.  The consumer has not contacted the firm with his concerns but plans to do so. Consumer Added:  This happens all the time.  Accidental gas release before ignition knobs turn on while cleaning stove, etc. and can fill kitchen with gas if not noticed.

No further information was provided.
justification: The incident describes a potential gas release hazard with no reported injuries or deaths, but with a high likelihood of occurrence as stated by the consumer.

incident_description:
Have been using a 12inch "Belgique Hard Anodized" Non-Stick Frying Pan with Silicone handles for several years now. This is a "Tools of the Trade" product from Macy's.

Last night, cooking over less than medium heat the handle got as hot as the pan. I let the pan cool down and then reheated. Sure enough, it did it again and I lightly burned my thumb! Only the outermost tip of the handle remained relatively cool.

Whatever was in the handle acting as an insulator has apparently deteriorated and/or melted. The pan is NOT discolored and there is no indication of abnormal wear.
Please note: I have never used highest heat with this pan, maybe 80% of burner strength at most.

I will now get rid of the 10inch pan also -no problems yet, but I can't trust it.
justification: The incident resulted in a light burn injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue recurred under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
GE Profile Microwave Oven Wall Hung Unit Model PVM1870SM1SS Serial Number MR 902716 B  
Manufactured July 2008
While using the microwave, the unit shut down and a message appeared stating " Check Food - Unit Stopped Cooking" or similar words.  I removed the food and then noticed smoke coming from the vent and the panel. The unit crackled and caught on fire inside the control panel area.  I had to use a fire extinguisher to put it out.  I am lucky I had an extinguisher.  This could have burned my house down.
justification: The microwave caught fire, but no injury or death occurred; the incident was controlled with a fire extinguisher.

incident_description:
Tried to melt coconut oil in small bowl, after less than 10 seconds it started making loud sounds & sparks. Thought maybe the bowl was made out of something unsafe (it appears to be clear glass or [REDACTED] or very hard plastic of some sort).  Tried melting coconut oil again a few days later, in what was more clearly a bowl made of safe glass. Sparks & scary noises again.  Thought that maybe coconut oil is somehow not microwave safe.  As far as I know, roommates continued using microwave without incident over the past few days.

Tried to nuke some Chinese leftovers in a porcelain bowl. Microwave caught on fire. Not the food or the dish, but a part of the inside wall of the microwave where there are little vent holes caught on fire. This was, again, after only a few short seconds of nuking. Had I not been nearby to blow it out immediately, I'm not sure how quickly it would have turned into a house fire.
justification: The microwave caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Coffee maker began to boil the remaining half pot.  Luckily, I heard it from the next room and went into the kitchen.  The coffee was boiling and the base of the coffee maker was smoking profusely. I removed the carafe and unplugged the machine.  There is a strong smell of burnt plastic throughout the house.
I feel fortunate that this happened while I was home.  The results could have been much more serious.
justification: The incident involved a smoking coffee maker but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the circumstances described.

incident_description:
I have had 2 Black & Decker toaster ovens, of different models, cause a fire in the unit in the past 6 to 8 months. In each case I put a piece of bread in to toast, and the bread caught fire. The first time I was in the room and turned to see flames 3 or 4 inches high rising from the toast, blackening the outside of the oven door and creating smoke throughout the house. I was using the controls appropriately for toast and had the timer turned to a short time period.

The second time, yesterday, I was in another room, smelled burned toast and found the toaster with black smoke marks at the door, the toast charred with an ember still orange until I put is in the sink and ran water on it. I was using the toaster the correct way, with a short time set for toast.

Yesterday I was toasting a slice of Portuguese sweet bread with raisins. That may have been the sam bread I used when the first toaster oven fire occurred, but I don't remember for sure.
justification: The incident involved fires in toaster ovens causing property damage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
An apartment tenant was baking in her kitchen over. After opening the oven door she pulled out bottom rack prior to removing a cookie sheet. While doing this she was wearing a oven mitt made of cotton. This mitt extended two to three inches beyond her finger tips and must have inadvertently contacted the bottom electric heating element inside oven. The bottom element was within 5-inches of the rackÃÂs front edge.

This contact went un-noticed and tenant re-hung her oven mitt in the pantry closet. Approximately 10-minutes later she was alerted by a smoke alarm sounding and discovered a fire inside the pantry closet.

The subsequent origin and cause investigation determined the first item ignited was the cotton oven mitt. No ignition sources were found inside the pantry closet. Based upon the tenantÃÂs statement, reenactment and physical evidence remaining this investigator concluded the following:

- The oven mitt came into contact with the hot element inside the electric oven.

- This contact resulted in the ignition of the cotton mitt, just a smoldering ember that went unnoticed by the tenant.

- The smoldering oven mitt was hung in the pantry closet where it fully ignited and ignited other items inside the closet.

- The oven mitt was purchased around Christmas 2011 at an Anthropologie Store. (www.anthropologie.com) and based upon the tenantÃÂs description was style #21235684.

- The kitchen range was a [REDACTED] electric range, Model # [REDACTED] and s/n [REDACTED].

It is the opinion of this investigator that two design deficiencies interacting resulted in this ignition.

1. The material selection of the oven mitt had no fire resistive qualities and should not have been in use near ignition sources or hot surfaces.

2. The design of the ovenÃÂs bottom electric heating element extended forward too close to the front edge of the bottom oven rack and did not have adequate clearance for a hand to grasp the bottom rack to pull it forward.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an oven mitt igniting, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
baking dish exploded when oven door was opened.

I am writing to report a incident that occurred tonight in our home that involved a Pyrex baking dish that my wife was using to prepare baked squash.

The baking dish which we have had and used for many years without incident exploded when my wife opened the oven door to remove the squash after about 40 minutes of baking at 375 degrees F.

The oven had been pre-heated prior to placing the baking dish in.

I have worked for over 35 years in a clinical chemistry lab, and have used Pyrex glassware for many of those years and have not seen anything like this.  About 1/3 of the dish exploded when the oven door was opened. Luckily this happened before my wife was able to grab the dish to remove it, or it could have injured her.

I subscribe to Consumer Reports and remembered an article that I had read in the January 2011 issue regarding bakeware that shatters, in which consumers were urged to contact the CPSC if this problem was experienced.

This communication is being sent to document this occurrence.
justification: The baking dish exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I removed a Pyrex round glass dish from the fridge and put it in the microwave to warm leftovers.  The timer was set at 1:30.  After about a minute, the dish exploded in the microwave, breaking into lots of little and big pieces.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding in the microwave, causing damage but no reported injury.

incident_description: Loaded and started my dishwasher. while watching tv in a separate room i smelled smoke. when i ran to the kitchen i found my Kitchen aid dishwasher smoking. When i opened the door to shut it off it continued to run and smoke. My wife quickly shut off the main breaker to the house. This could of been catastrophic had we not been home.
justification: The dishwasher smoking and continuing to run posed a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The empty dishwasher shortly after it was started expelled black smoked and smelled like burning plastic. We tried running it again and got the same unacceptable result.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no reported injury, indicating an equipment malfunction without immediate harm.

incident_description:
I have purchased a LG gas range model LRG30855ST
there has been smell of "gas" 
I have noted that the knobs on the appliance are cracked, thus ineffective in completely turning off the gas to the cook top. Researching online apparently this is a common complaint among consumers. The type of plastic used, and the construction of the knob predispose it to failure. If the gas is not completely turned off it poses a fire and explosion hazard. I have resorted to using pliers to close off the gas.
justification: The cracked knobs lead to a gas leak, posing a fire and explosion hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: I used my Cruisinart tabletop mixer to make pizza dough. When I finished, I left the unit plugged in but turned off.I was doing other things in the kitchen. After 10 minutes I smelt something strange and started checking to find the smell. I looked at the mixer and smoke was coming out the top and flowing from underneath the unit. I immediately unplugged the mixer and took it outside. Thank goodness I was home and noticed this. It could have caused a fire and burnt the house down. Very scary. The unit was only 3 years old. I have never had any appliance do this before.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or damage occurred, fitting severity level 2. Such electrical malfunctions are uncommon but not unheard of, warranting an occurrence likelihood of 2.

incident_description:
On a Sunday evening I turned on my Kenmore freestanding electric range from Sears that was set to 350 degrees. Approximately 10 minutes into the preheat mode, suddenly "for no reason" the front glass shattered into a thousand pieces all over my kitchen floor. It sounded like a gun shot, if I wasn't standing near the oven I would never believe this happened. Luckily my young son was not standing near the unit as he would have been covered in glass.  

I purchased this unit two years ago (Feb. 2010) and have no complaints.  I contact Sears and they offered no solution except for me to purchase an extended warranty for $260 to cover the damage. 

I later researched this type of incident and notice that I wasn't alone, many consumers have experience the same thing with similar Kenmore electric ranges. I am only hoping for these type issues to be researched further and a solution to be implemented for this defect.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous shattering of glass that could have caused injury, but no one was harmed. Research indicates this is a recurring issue with similar appliances.

incident_description: Smelled burning plastic inside refrigerator. Noticed that light bulbs were burning plastic light fixture. Tested door switches, but lights would not turn off. While attempting to remove both extremely hot bulbs, one of the bulbs exploded . After removing bulbs, removed metal plate holding light sockets and plastic was melted. Cannot believe there has not been a recall for faulty switches. Definite fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved burning plastic and an exploding bulb, indicating a fire hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description: Black and Decker model DLX1050B Coffee Maker starts brewing as soon as the unit is plugged in.  The heating element continues to stay on well after all the water is boiled away.  If left plugged in I am afraid that it would eventually melt and/or catch on fire.  The power usage would be horrible even if it did not fail.
justification: The coffee maker's malfunction could lead to burns or fire, posing injury risk, and the issue is likely to occur if left unattended.

incident_description:
The consumer said that he has the exact same problem that has been identified in recall CAP# 10-255.  The heating element is broken.  The case around the element is cracked.  An electrical failure in the dishwasherÃÂs heating element can pose a serious fire hazard.

The dishwasher would cause the circuit breaker to trip.  The discontinued use of the dishwasher.  He had a service technician come out to look at it and the tech. said that the dishwasher was under recall.  

The consumer saw the recall approximately 5 weeks ago.  The consumer contacted the firm, but he was told that his product was not included in the recall. 

The consumer is upset, because he has the exact same problem identified in the recall and he has the beginning letters and numbers mentioned in the CPSC press release.

The CPSC entered the consumer model and serial number in the firm's website and it indicated that his unit was not included.  The consumer believes that the recall should be expanded based the problems that others may have.
justification: The incident involves a broken heating element posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. The likelihood is high as the issue is part of a known recall and has been reported by the consumer.

incident_description:
CONCERNING A MODEL OF MR COFFEE THAT I HAVE HAD 2 OF, BOTH OF WHICH STARTED STEAMING, POPPING & HAVING THE SMELL OF MELTING OR BURNING PLASTIC, WITH STEAM INSIDE THE CLOCK SWITCHING MECHANISEM WITH THE PLASTIC FRONT GETTING VERY HOT.

MODEL BVMC-SJX33GT, QUALITY CONTROL STICKER: QC PASS B7

incident_description:
In January 1996 we purchased a Dynasty gas range, model #DGR-36-6 from The Super Store,
11 Blair Park, Williston, VT 05495 for $3800 + tax.  The range was crated and not installed
in our new home under construction until mid 1997 when our kitchen was completed.  Our
problems with this range began soon after.  The burner tube keeps burning up and
disintegrating at the ignition area.  We have to get a new part just about every year.  My
wife has already been burned when opening the oven to check on the food.  A flame shot out
and burned her arm.  This has happened several times.  We advised Jade Products Inc and 
spoke with [REDACTED](her email is [REDACTED]).  She sends us a new part
which usually has to be replaced the following year.  She advised us that the part was  
being made with a better material. Well, that did not make any difference.  We sent her a 
photo via email of the damaged burner part which she was to send to their engineering 
director to look at.  We have received no response. We are now in the process of 
purchasing another range.  We have contacted [REDACTED] at Jade Products via email and 
requested some kind of settlement or adjustment since we cannot possibly sell this dangerous Dynasty range.   We have replaced this part at least 8 times over the past years.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burned arm) and has happened several times, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: I have a  Cuisinart DCC1200 Brew Central 12-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker.  Two days ago the pot began to make a popping and sizzling sound.  An acrid smoke began to rise from the unit.  I unplugged the unit and took it outside.  I contacted Cuisinart by telephone and they offered a free in warannty replacement.  My concern is what could have happened  if I had not been home to unplug and reomve the device from the house.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffeemaker producing smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as the issue was promptly addressed.

incident_description: My husband and I were making a cup of coffee just like we do every morning when our coffee maker made a funny noise and when the light quit blinking and it should have been ready to open I opened it up and the minute I opened it exploded hot coffee grounds and it came at me and hit me in the left side of my upper chest area and it felt like a brick hit me, and I was wearing a heavy sweatshirt but the heat burned throught to my skin and left a pink burn spot on my chest area, had I not been wearing the sweatshirt I think I would have been burned really bad, coffee granules went everywhere, they were sprayed all over me luckily they didnt hit my face and I thank God my son wasnt standing there with me at the time.. I was in shock from what had happened, it had scared me so bad because it had felt like I had been hit with a brick or rock in the chest! Whoever would have thought coffee grounds could feel like that! So I went in on my computer and went to custemer service for Tassimo and told them what had happened, and I never heard back from them I waited for a couple of weeks and still nothing, and then I receive an email from direct delivery that my order was on back order and they wouldn't be shipping it for awhile, so I just let it go and thought maybe it wouldnt be to long but I never heard a thing from them, so one day while shopping at bed bath and beyond I decided to just go ahead and pickup a few packages of our t disks to get by untill our order came and that is when I found out about the recall, but I still needed to talk to someone because our coffee maker not only exploded that morning but now it was leaking water around the seal because evidently it got so hot that it melted the plastic seal inside the lid and now we have a leaky seal, and I needed to know if we could get that replaced or what, so I went home and tried calling the company and I never did get a call back. They have never sent me any kind of a recall notice and we bought our machine from their website, and we have been getting home delivery's for several years now.  They are not returning my calls or answering my email I sent to customer service. I have yet to hear anything back at all!
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from the exploding coffee maker, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of a malfunctioning appliance but no indication of frequent similar incidents.

incident_description:
My dishwasher's control panel caught fire.  An awful electrical smell permeated my kitchen and living room.  Luckily, I was home so only dishwasher was damaged.  When I opened the door, the dishwasher would not stop.  As a result, I had an electrical fire issue AND I was standing in water now.  I was able to kill power through circuit breaker.

I paid $1000 for this Kenmore Elite dishwasher and have only used it for 7 years.  My model number is 66516272400.  It was purchased at Sears (Store #1623) on 2/2/05 and delivered on 2/8/05.  

When I asked Sears Customer Solutions if they knew about any problems with this dishwasher, their response was "We checked the CPSC records and found nothing."  I've researched this problem and found www.kitchenaidfire.com website.  I cannot believe so many people have had this problem and CPSC and Consumer Reports have not done anything to warn customers or to force a recall to date.

My hope is that giving you this information will help your investigation into this matter.  Sears only offered two remedies:  1) buy a broken appliance service contract for $200 and if the tech could not fix it, Sears would offer a $500 voucher toward purchase of new dishwasher or 2) join class-action lawsuit (filed in CA in Nov. 2011--see www.kitchenaidfire.com for details).

Unacceptable!  My dishwasher should have lasted another 5 years at least!  And it probably would have if it had not been for the defective circuit board meltdown!  The dishwasher looks new inside and out except for damaged part.  Online chats indicated that the problem will probably occur again if the circuit board was replaced because the seals to keep moisture out was defective?  Other sites say the load is too great for the circuit board?

I hope you get to the bottom of this issue and make the appropriate manufacturer accountable for this defect.  Ideally, that would mean a recall to protect current and future customer from this safety hazard.

Thanks!  Please update me on your findings ASAP.
justification: The dishwasher's control panel caught fire, but no injuries were reported, only property damage.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite refrigerator, I think LG is the manufacturer.  The model number 795.77543600.  The unit is 4 years old and the light kit is overheating.  I've read multiple postings about this issue and it appears to be relatively well known problem.  The light kit is extremely hot to the touch and I've been advised to remove the light bulbs until the technician comes to replace the unit in 19 days.  Sears has scheduled a replacement, but i've read that a repaired unit is prone to overheat to the point that the plastic casing melts.  Very surprised these units haven't been scheduled for recall.  It's one thing to have the water dispenser break or the ice cube maker to stop making cubes, I get that stuff happens.  But to have a fire hazard in the middle of my kitchen is unacceptable.  I'm not alone, you can google this issue and find others, something needs to be done about it.
justification: The light kit overheating poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Last night I was running my dishwasher and heard weird hissing sounds and a smelled something burning.  I looked over at my dishwasher and flames were coming out around the control panel.  I was so happy I was awake and the towel right next to it didn't catch fire as well.  It stopped when I got it turned off.
justification: Flames from the dishwasher indicate a fire incident, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Wolfgang Puck Rotisserie Oven  Model BDCORPS10

This oven has gone from working fine to the light bulb inside the oven stuck on even after power is shut off.  Now the oven will power itself off/on during a timed cooking cycle, had to unplug oven for fear of it starting a fire.
justification: The oven malfunctioning and powering on/off unpredictably poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
KitchenAid built-in dishwasher was running for about 5-10 minutes, when popping was heard. Went over to washer. Observed black smoke and acrid smell coming from upper part of dishwasher.
Opened dishwasher door which was very hot. Disconnected power at breaker ( not tripped).
Unscrewed door. Found control board and connectors burned.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with smoke and burning components, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My father (93 years old) was heating dinner in his GE over-the-range microwave Saturday night when he smelled smoke.  He opened the door of his microwave and smoke poured out.  He saw it coming from the mesh-like area on the interior wall of the microwave behind the control panel, and saw a yellow, flickering light through the mesh-like area, which he interpreted as a fire behind the control panel.  He called the front desk of his condo building for assistance.  The maintenance man asked him not to open the front door of his apartment to air out the smoke as he was concerned it might set off the building's smoke alarms.  By this time, the fire had died out and the worker unplugged the microwave.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a small fire in the microwave, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Coffe spill out of the tassimo coffee machine
justification: Coffee spill is an incident with no injury, and spills are common with coffee machines.

incident_description: My Tassimo coffee maker started to spit out coffee grinds and hot water everywhere. Had to abruptly turn it off and it has never worked the same since.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, spitting hot water and grinds, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have had two incidents with my Tassimo coffee maker spewing hot water and coffee grounds all over when using an Espresso disc.  Thankfully I wasn't burned - but the potential was definitely there for injury.  The first time was when I was camping - I assumed that there was a power surge, or something similar, as we were using a generator for power.  However, the next time I used my Tassimo at home, the same thing happened.  

I have not had any more problems since then.
justification: The incident involved hot water and coffee grounds spewing out, but no injury occurred. It happened twice under different conditions, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
On Sunday evening (February 5, 2012), my wife suddenly heard a whirring noise coming from the kitchen.  Upon investigation, she found that our electric can opener has started running by itself, rather erratically.  As she approached it, she noticed a burning smell and saw smoke coming from the top of the appliance.  She immediately unplugged the can opener and it stopped.

She called me to take a look.  There was an electrical burned smell at the top of the can opener, where the switch mechanisms are located.  We had used the can opener earlier in the evening and I suspect that the cutout contact had not fully opened when it last stopped, subsequently allowing arcing to occur across the contact and resulting in the can opener running by itself.

Neither the Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI), nor the electical panel circuit breaker which serves that particular kitchen circuit tripped.  Apparently the arcing fault current was not sufficient to trip the breaker and the fault was not of the type that would trip the GFCI.  (I used the test button on the GFCI receptacle afterward to test the receptacle and it tripped properly.)

There was no damage to our kitchen as a result of this incident, thanks to the fact that my wife reacted so quickly.  Had she not done so, or if we had not been home at the time, the incident might have escalated into a serious fire, as the can opener was located on the countertop, right beneath overhead wooden cabinets.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with potential fire risk, but no actual injury or damage occurred due to quick action.

My wife and I then purchased the Maytag (Whirlpool) 24" gas wall oven Model: CWG3100AAB25; Serial: DY1703470 from our local Lowes store # 0473 in Vienna, WV.  This oven was installed on February 20, 2012 (superb installation).  Upon first use, my wife burned her hand on the external flu vent.  This vent sticks out 1 to 1.5 inches from the face of the oven, is constructed of black painted metal, and is located between the control panel and the oven handle.  The flu vent is connected directly to the oven's internal chimney allowing for heat conduction from the inside of the oven directly to the external flu vent ribs.  (i.e. if the interior of the oven is 450 degrees, the external flu vent is 450 degrees)  My wife burned her hand by accidentally brushing the vent on her first use of the oven.

incident_description:
We had just started our KitchenAid dishwasher for the evening before we went to bed when I went into the kitchen and could smell  electrical wire burning.  The smell filled the kitchen.  We immediately stopped the dishwasher.  It wasn't running correctly it was stuck in the beginning part of the cycle.  We stopped it and then waited and then tried to start it again but the smoke and smell continued so we stopped it.  My husband opened the control panel up and we could see the wires were starting to melt against the plastic back of the control panel.  We put the smoke detector on top of the counter above the dishwasher before we went to bed.

In the morning I looked up the paper to find out how old our dishwasher was. It had been working fine and this incident surprised us.   It was purchased in 2003 from Sears.  We have had it for 9 years so we were debating repairing it or buying a new one.   Our last dishwasher was a KitchenAid and we had it for over 12 years with no problems.  

That day after work when I was telling a friend about this she said I should [REDACTED] KitchenAid to see how long they should last.  That is when I came across the kitchenaidfires.com website.  I was shocked as many of the entries were exactly what happened to us or could have happened if I had not went back into the kitchen before we went to bed.  We went out and  bought a new dishwasher NOT a KitchenAid.  I had read even replacing the panel people have had it happen again.  We were not taking any chances with our family and home.

I tried to call KitchenAid but have been unable to get through to the correct department.  I only spoke with the parts person who wasn't too helpful in transferring my call to the correct department.  I am going to keep trying.  

These should be recalled before someone loses their life.
justification: The incident involved electrical wire burning and melting, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

Back 3 years ago, we had a Maytag repairman come out and switch out the electrical switch, that powers on the gas oven, he replaced the convection fan as well.  3 years later, the unit caught on fire.  Looking at the internet, I spotted the there had been a voluntary recall on this product 2 years before I had ever bought the oven, and Maytag/Whirlpool failed to keep from selling the faulty oven. Shame on you Whirlpool!

incident_description: The product is a Whirlpool side by side refrigerator model # GD5SHAXKQ08 serial # SL4449254 manufacture date 11/2001.  January 2012 I was in my kitchen and heard a click or crackle type noise---very brief, maybe 2 seconds, but unusual (and on hearing it, I realized that it had made the noise the previous evening but I had not been sure where it came from)---and went to investigate. As I was standing next to the refrigerator and gazing into the adjoining room, it seemed as if there was smoke in the air. My daughter was with me and I asked her if it seemed smoky and she said she smelled "something burning". At that moment, smoke started pouring out of the back of the refrigerator, almost instantly filling the whole downstairs with smoke, so I pulled the refrigerator out from the wall and unplugged it, which caused the smoke to stop. It was lucky I was home and that I was actually in the kitchen. I was extremely angry to then search online and find out that many others have experienced similar instances with their refrigerators---and some had progressed to fires--- and that there was a recall of the Maytag refrigerators, (made by Whirlpool) but not the ones with the Whirlpool labels for smoke, fire, scorching, etc. due to a defective compressor relay. While I was not going to pay to have a repair person come and determine what the problem was with my refrigerator, I watched youtube videos that could have been taken of my own experience and I could also echo the descriptions given of what happened. It is unacceptable to me that these refrigerators have not all been recalled---who ever worries about a fire hazard with a refrigerator??!!; I was lucky enough to be right there.

incident_description:
In mid-2008, we purchased a completely remodeled house with what were represented as new Viking kitchen appliances.  In fact, the range still had tape on the shelves and the broiling pan was still wrapped in plastic.  As this is a second home and I rarely cook, the range doesn't get a lot of use.

In mid-December, I turned on the oven to 325 degrees to heat up some leftovers.  Less than ten minutes later, the oven exploded in flames.  We dialed 911 and the fire department arrived in less than two minutes.  (The advantage of living in a small town.)  They put out the fire and, fortunately, our damage was limited to the oven itself.

Our insurance company sent out a fire inspector to examine the range and he determined that either the function knob or the temperature knob had short-circuited which created a sizable hole in the manifold that delivers the gas to the burners.  He also noted the serial number of the range and recommended that I contact Viking, which I did.

Viking advised me that this range had been manufactured in October 2001 and was slightly more than ten years old.  They acknowledged that it had never been registered and they had no idea where it had been prior to being installed in our home.  Their position was that "after ten years, parts fail" and took no responsibility whatsoever.  

It's my belief that this wasn't just a failed part, this was a serious design flaw.  When the fire inspector removed the front panel, there was a mass of electrical wiring, all abutting the gas manifold.  A failure of any of those control knobs would damage the manifold and create a gas fire.  

The fire inspector told us that we were not only lucky to still be alive, he was surprised that our house was still standing.  We can thank the Carmel Fire Department for that, but Viking should be taken to task for designing, building and selling a product that's clearly so dangerous ... no matter how old it is.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous fire but resulted in no injuries, only property damage. Such events are unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
Regarding the Cuisinart DTC-975 12 Cup Programmable Thermal Coffeemaker:
I have used this coffeemaker for about a year without any problems.  This morning I made coffee as usual.  A beeper will sound when the unit is finished and the coffee is ready.

The beeper sounded and I waited about another 30 minutes before going into the kitchen to pour myself a cup of coffee.  Upon entering the kitchen, I discovered coffee all over the counter top and on the floor.  The pot appeared to be properly seated in the coffeemaker.  When I took it out, hot coffee began pouring out of the filter basket onto the bottom of the coffeemaker.  It just missed my hand.  I grabbed another nearby pot to catch.  Upon opening the filter basket compartment, it was still full of liquid.

The thermal pot was only about 1/4 full, so this was not a case of it being overfilled.  It had stopped filling at that point for some inexplicable reason which resulted in the remainder of the coffee either running out onto the counter and floor or staying inside the filter compartment until the pot was removed.

No injuries were sustained but a major mess in the kitchen resulted.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffeemaker causing a mess but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the description of the malfunction.
