2/13/2012 7:15 pm The cuisinart electric pressure cooker CPC-600 series came open as it was pressurizing. I had set the pressure cooker to cook on high pressure for 15 minutes.  It takes some time for the unit to build pressure and I had stepped away for a few minutes.  When I returned to check on the unit the red flashing indicator had not stopped flashing (to indicate that it had reached pressure and the timer had not yet started counting down).  There was steam and slight whistling sound coming from the red float valve that also indicates when the unit has reached full pressure.  Concerned about the steam and whistling from the float valve I was about to shut the unit down when the lid popped off.  The stew I was preparing erupted in approximately a 3ft radius scalding my left hand and burning my stomach covering the counters and the floor surrounding the cooking area of the unit. 

This was only the 3rd use of this pressure cooker.  I have cleaned the unit according to manufacturers instructions from the 2 previous uses. In the troubleshooting section of the instruction booklet it says that the reason air escapes from the float valve could be that food was stuck in the sealing ring. The other reason is that the sealing ring on the float wore out.  With this only being the 3rd use of the pressure cooker, I wouldn't think that the sealing ring would be worn out unless it was faulty to begin with.  I know I have taken care in cleaning the unit as I have been the only one who has operated and cleaned the machine.
justification: The incident resulted in scalding and burns, indicating injury (severity 3), but the issue appears to be a rare manufacturing defect given the cooker was only used 3 times (likelihood 2).

I did get a tiny cut on my knee while I was kneeling on the kitchen floor to clean up. Most of the pieces were on the drain board under the drying rack. 
I reported this incident to Housewares Int'l and they eventually offered the following explanation:
"I understand, but so far all we have received is that it has never happened before and should not have happened now. They do not have a reason and no way of duplicating the situation to try to make it happen again.  The only thing they can come up with is that there was an occlusion in the glass that was not visible to the naked eye, temperature changes are the only thing that could have made this happen. There is not enough air pressure in you kitchen to make something shatter. If we had a better explanation we would give it to you. We are sorry you had the fright that you did."
The cover has been discarded but I have been using the ceramic casserole regularly. I recently noticed that this has developed numerous cracks in the interior. I originally thought these were superficial but I now see that one crack goes vertically completely through the side. I have stopped using this casserole. I'm pretty sure I have used this casserole at oven temperatures above 400 degrees. In an other email H.I. customer service stated that the casserole shouldn't be used in an oven over 400 degrees. incident_description:
After regular dishwasher use, a cycle ran over night, the dishwasher door leaks water onto the floor upon opening.  
Sears Home Repair has been to our house 8 times to repair the product issue but to no avail.
Sears says that this may be a known issue from the manufacturer, Electrolux. There is no current fix, we are told, but to continue calling Sears and have Sears call Electrolux about the problem.
The technician from Sears Home Repair tells me that the steam in the dishwasher is captured in a vent in the door. The steam is then cooled down with the ambient air, forming water. The water is then to drip down the vent tube and empty into the dishwasher tub. But the water does not make it to the tub, instead spilling onto our floor.
We were told by the manufacturer that we should wait a day or two to let the water evaporate in the tube, but what is the point of having a dishwasher wash my dishes if I can't use them for two days?
So I humored Electrolux and waited a full 24 hours before opening the door.
And the I got the same result. Water from the tube spilled out of the door and on my floor.
The vent tube has been replaced. An "absorbing sponge" at the bottom of the vent tube has also been replaced. A tech from Sears made a home made flap consisting of rubber and duct tape and said it would be a good temporary fix.
None of these fixes, temporary or permanent, have fixed the problem.
Sears has been here 8 times!
This is unacceptable and am calling Sears tomorrow to request they take the dishwasher back.
justification: The dishwasher leaks water onto the floor, causing inconvenience and property damage, but no injuries or deaths are reported.

incident_description:
My Pyrex dish exploded in the oven.  I have had this casserole dish for 10 years and have used it many times.  I was making bar cookies.  I melted butter in another container in the microwave.  I poured it in the pyrex casserole dish.  I sprinkled graham cracker crumbs on top of the butter.  Then I layered chocolate chips, coconut and pecans over that.  I poured sweetened condensed milk over that.  Everything in the dish was room temperatore except the butter.  The butter had cooled about 5 minutes before I put it in the oven. The oven was pre-heated to 325 degrees when I put the dish in the oven.  It was there about 10 minutes and it broke in hundreds of pieces.  I turned off the oven and waited for it to cool.  I cut my finger getting the glass and goo out of the oven.  It wasn't serious enough to require stitches. I have 3 more Pyrex casserole dishes that I am afraid to use. 

Pyrex has a disclaimer on the internet that it's products are safe and it is only a rumor that the dishes break.  This is what they tell you to do:
1.Always place hot bakeware on a dry, cloth potholder or towel. 
?Never place hot bakeware on top of the stove, on a metal trivet, on a damp towel, in the sink or directly on a counter.
2.Never put bakeware directly on a heat source such as on a stove top, on a grill, under a broiler or in a toaster oven. 
3.Always allow the oven to fully preheat before placing bakeware in the oven. 
4.Always cover the bottom of the dish with liquid before cooking meat or vegetables.

I am very concerned that people will continue to use this product.  It is not safe.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut finger) that did not require stitches, and the occurrence likelihood is considered possible given the detailed description of the event and the user's concern about the product's safety.

incident_description: I was thrilled to get a new set of Pyrex bakeware for Christmas 2011. This morning, February 5, 2012, I used a piece of it for the first time. I prepared a sopapilla cheesecake and placed it in the oven to bake @ 350 degrees. It had only been in the oven for approximately 10 minutes when I heard a horrible explosion. My husband jumped out of his chair and said "What was that?!!" I told him that it was apparently the Pyrex that had shattered in the oven. I opened the oven door to see broken glass and my dessert dripping everywhere. The glass continued to pop and crack for at least 15 minutes after I  left the oven door slightly ajar. I will not use my new Pyrex ware again. I have old Pyrex that I have used for over 30 years with no problem. I will definitely tell everyone that I know NOT to buy any of the new products. I can not imagine what the outcome would be if the oven door had been open when the explosion happened. This is one of the most dangerous products I have ever encountered in my 30 plus years of cooking.
justification: The Pyrex bakeware shattered in the oven, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I have a Sears Kenmore kitchen range, model 790-95414103. It is about 7 years old.  Last night, I had a roast in the oven and the range started beeping.  It was not the timer, so I checked the oven.  The element in the bottom was bright red, my roast was burning, and when I tried to shut off the oven, it would not shut off.  I have no idea how hot it was, but when I pulled out the roasting pan and put it on a cutting board, it left black burn marks.  The message "F1" was flashing in the window. There was no reference to this error message in the User Guide, so I checked on line and found, to my amazement, that this is a known problem which has been going on since at least 2009.  This is an extremely dangerous situation and Sears customers should be notified that this may happen to them.  I'm glad I was nearby; I was minutes away from a fire.   When I called Customer Care today, I was told that this happens often, but would not be covered because the stove was not under warranty.  Having random parts break over time is one thing and you accept that when you buy an appliance; having the manufacturer know that their ranges have a defective part and gamble that it will not cause a fire and loss of property and life is another matter.  How do they justify their behavior?

He unplugged it immediately and discontinued the use of it. He indicated that he just used the appliance the day before and it operated normal.

The firm was not contacted but he stated that he would.
justification: The incident involved a water leak but no injury occurred, and the user took immediate action to unplug the appliance.

incident_description: Our seven year old Kenmore Elite dishwasher, model 665.16263400, caught fire last week. We were home, and awake, when it happened. It is our habit to turn the dishwasher on when we go to bed but fortunately we did not on this night. The fire started after the second wash cycle had started. First heard a light pop, thought it was ice cubes dropping in the refrigerator, and then a minute later a louder one that sent us both running for the kitchen. Smoke was coming out the top and my husband saw flames near the bottom. We pulled the door open and that turned the machine off. We then turned the power off at the main source. The fire was in the control panel at top right front of door but a slight char mark was also found on the floor under the machine when it was pulled out.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Microwave oven is unsafe as it draws far more amps and watts than its label states.

It draws 16.4 amps and uses 1950 watts on high.  The label states it uses only 12.7 amps and 1460 watts.

The Operating Instructions booklet states, "The oven must be plugged into at least a 20 AMP, 120 VOLT, 60 Hz GROUNDED OUTLET."  Yet it has only a 15 amp plug.  Nothing on the oven itself says it requires a 20 amp outlet; the amp rating and the plug are clear indications a 15 amp outlet is OK.

When I called Panasonic they transferred me a and "engineer" who told me the high amp and wattage draw is OK and that I could take it to one of their warranty shops to be checked if I wanted to.
justification: The microwave's excessive power draw poses a potential safety hazard, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Caller purchased stainless steel 2qt teakettle November 13, 2011 but didn't begin using it until the end of December 2011.
He states that when he began using it when he would grab the handle of the teakettle after it whistled to swing around and pour water into his cup the water would slosh around in the teakettle and explode all over the floor and everyplace around.

He has done this many times with the same result each time and has been burned.

He has not contacted the manufacturer because they are in China, but he has contacted Calphon customer relations.  Without proper response to these concerns, he is filing this complaint.

He states that this teakettle presents a scalding hazard.
justification: The caller has been burned multiple times due to the teakettle's design flaw, indicating a clear injury risk (severity 3) and a likely recurrence (likelihood 4) based on repeated incidents.

incident_description:
My husband started the diahwasher and then went to pick up our daughter from an appointment,when he got back our dishwasher was on fire. If he would of gotten home 10 minutes later we would of lost our kitchen or worse the house!
When we called LG and told them what happened they could of cared less! They told us it wasn't there problem anynore. The part that started the fire had been replaced four times in four years,
 it was obviously a problem. We think they should of recalled the dishwasher instead of trying to just keep fixing an existing problem. We will never buy nor recomend LG products to anyone we know
there customer service is pretty much non existant once you've bought something from them.
Very disheartened
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant risk to the kitchen and house, but no injury or death occurred.

The second and third time we caught the microwave before it ran too long. The only way to stop the microwave from running is to trip the breaker on my circuit panel. incident_description:
Smelled a burning electrical smell coming out of our dishwasher.  After killing the power to it I inspected the control board and wiring harness.  Connector CON1 and it's mating plastic four wire connector had one of the wires insulation and the plastic connected completely melted through. This would be the tan wire.  The other end of the tan wire at the microswitch has signs of overheating as well.  Also noticed two of the electrolytic 470uf 10v capacitors are bulging quite noticably which is not normal.  

This dishwasher is a Sears/Kenmore 
Model 665.17462300
Ser. # 1811409

Purchased new from Sears in 2004.

Had I not noticed this I suspect it could have led to a fire.  

[redacted]
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to melted wiring and bulging capacitors, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore Oven door shattered.  Last night as we were preparing dinner, my husband checked the food, and as he closed the door, the glass panel exploded into a million pieces.  Shards of glass flew up to ten feet across the kitchen, one of which struck my mother in the face (about an inch from her eye!). Fortunately, no one was injured, although we we all badly shaken.  It's a blessing that our children were not in the kitchen at the time, and that our friends toddler had just left.
   The oven was on at 300 degrees at the time.  We treat our appliances gently, and do not drop things or slam the doors.
The range is a dual fuel Kenmore Elite Model C970 441883.  Serial number is 1939090.  It was delivered in Sept 2010 but was not installed until January 2010.  However, since it is past the one year warrany period, we have been advised that the repair will not be covered under warrany.  I do not feel that this is a warranty issue.  This is a SAFETY issue.  It doesn't matter how old a stove is - the door should not spontaneously explode into a million pieces!  It is lucky that one of the shards of class did not lodge in my mothers eye or injure one of my children.  I think this problem needs to be addressed soon to spare other families the horror of a potential tragedy.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door with flying glass shards, but no injuries were reported despite the close call.

Had to trip the circuit breaker to turn stove broiler off.  When circuit breaker was turned back on, the broiler element also came on, even thought the controls indicated it was not on.

incident_description:
The gas powered oven has two heater elements, Broil and Bake.
When firing-up either of the heaters, gas is first emitted from the selected element depending on the function selected (Broil or Bake). A spark is then emitted the starters of both elements.
In my case the Bake function spark starter did not start but the Broil did emit a spark. Gas was however emitted from the Bake heater element.
The result is the emission of gas from the Bake element without ignition.
Trouble shooting led to a bad earth connection thus not allowing the spark circuit to be completed.

The heater element and the spark igniter are contained on a single unit mounted to the frame of the oven cavity by two self tapping screws.
The rear screw has a collar which holds the heater element through a hole to the oven wall. The collar allows the heater element to move forward/aft about 1/8". This is probably to allow for any expansion of the heater element.
The forward screw fastens the heater element to the oven wall through a forward/aft slot.

The problem occurred because the forward screw, which provides the earth circuit to the igniter had stripped its thread in the metal hole of the oven wall. Not only was the oven frame attachment hole enlarged because the screw had been over tightened but corrosion had developed between the oven frame and the heater element.
This single screw is responsible for providing the earth circuit for the spark igniter.

It would be my opinion that the spark igniter earth circuit be provided by at least two screws, thus increasing the chance of a bad earth by 100%. Also the screw used should be of a non-self tapping type to ensure a good electrical connection is made.
The manufacturer cannot control the precision of the self taped mounting hole size nore can the manufacturer ensure that the screw is not over tightened.
justification: The incident involved gas emission without ignition, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We just purchased the oven for a kitchen remodel.  We only had it for 2 weeks.  We turned on the "self-cleaning" feature and, 30 minutes into the cycle, one of the panes of door glass shattered and poured out of the oven door seam.

The glass was so hot, it burned through the finish on our hardwood floors and caused them to begin to smoulder and smoke.  The floors had recently been refinished.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned floors) but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
Dear Sir:
I would like to bring your attention of an unsafe glass cook top manufactured by Whirlpool, model No. GLT3014GQO, I am writing to make you aware that this product is having a probable cause for human safety compromise. 
Over the Christmas Holidays while cooking, the glass cook top shattered to pieces with glass flying all over and even pieces hitting the ceiling. It was very scary and unsafe. There are 95 homes in [REDACTED] community, South Orange County, California and I know there was a similar mishap in one of the homes. I contacted the Customer Service Department of Whirlpool. They wanted the model No. of the cook top. To my surprise the model no. was hidden under the cook top and I was unable to find it. It was not even listed in the Owner's!User manual. Then an authorized technician from Whirlpool was scheduled to come to my house and assess the damages. He came, looked at the cook top, and started saying "very expensive, very expensive," He then pulled out the entire oven underneath to find the model number. He quoted $880,00 to replace a similar cook top. When I declined to use his services due to the high cost of the replacement, he refused to give me the pertinent details of the cook top, Next day, Whirlpool was contacted again and after one hour, customer service finally read the log of the technician and gave the model no. The actual price of the cook top was only $373.10 .. is this a good faith estimate from an authorized Whirlpool technician? To add furthermore, the customer service at Whirlpool stated that their authorized technician can jack up the prices as they wish. Four days has gone by unable to cook for myself and eating out has only
added to the frustration through this entire ordeal. I am a senior citizen running around looking for a cook top at the local appliance stores to find the right product. Whirlpool could just have been more considerate during these holidays to assist me to find a cook top which is compatible.
Please consider the safety measures to be taken regarding the Whirlpool glass cook tops so incidents like this one are prevented in the future,
justification: The incident involved a glass cook top shattering, posing a safety hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
When attempting to power the oven in the off position by the switch she noticed that the range would not power off.  She pressed the off button numerous times for the oven to power off. The oven was set on 425 degrees on bake for approximately an hour prior to the incident occurring.

On 1/25/2012 after baking in the oven at 350 degrees for an hour when she attempted to power the oven in the off position by the switch it would not. The circuit breaker had to be pulled.

She contacted the firm on 1/30/2012 where she was advised to leave the circuit breaker pulled and a service technician is scheduled to come out to the home to diagnose the failure on  Thursday 2/2/2012.

The consumer was also advised by the representative from the firm (name not provided) that the diagnosing of the failure is free of charge but any repairs she would be required to pay out of pocket. 

While doing some research on the internet she came across a forum/blog that indicated that if  the faulty switch (switch that controls the power to the oven) is replaced in the appliance the could occur again.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven switch with no reported injuries, and similar issues have been noted in online forums, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
Gas Range purchased September 2011

Wife was turning oven on to preheat December 31st, 2011, she heard tick, tick, tick sounds usually associated with the lighting, the oven never ignited but gas never stopped flowing either.

Wife opened oven door to see if it was lit because she didn't hear it light and got a face full of gas, she instinctively closed the door back & called her husband who advised her to never close the door when this happened and pressed shut off.

Caller and wife opened the windows and turned on the high speed blower and it still took at least five minutes to clear all the gas out.

This incident happened around January 7, 2012 and then again on January 21, 2012.
They have now stopped using the range.

Caller said that old stoves had a safety built in so that if burner/oven didn't light the gas flow would have been stopped, however when he asked what the safety is on his presently owned range is he was told that there is none.

He is reporting this range as a severe hazard stating that if his wife had turned the range on to preheat and then walked downstairs she never would have known that the gas was steadily coming out while the ignition had not ignited.

He called the manufacturer January 23, 2012, spoke with [redacted] in General Services Department who created file#[REDACTED] then transferred caller to [redacted] in the Safety Department.

Caller is reporting this range as a severe safety hazard and would very much like to exchange the range for one with same manufacturer but that has a Safety Glow Coil that would manage the flow of the gas.
He said that this range presents a catastrophic problem that he believes could result in much more than property damage.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it was a severe hazard that could have led to death or serious injury.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to report that his gas range is a potential safety hazard. The consumer stated he was cooking pizza in the oven at 425 degrees for 15 minutes, when he noticed that the outside of the oven was so hot he could not touch it. The consumer shut off the range normally without incident. 

The consumer stated that the range is not damaged and did not cause property damage. The consumer has not been injured seriously by the product and his right hand was burned with no markings. The consumer did not see a physician for his burns. The consumer has not called the fire department about his product. 

The consumer stated that the oven is in perfect condition.  The consumer had a technician inspect the range was informed that the temperature on the outside of the range is 110 degrees. The firm told the consumer this was normal and recommended he purchase a hot pad for the range to put on his hands before touching the oven. 

The consumer called the retailer and informed the consumer they will not help him because the firm is claiming that there is nothing wrong with the oven.
justification: The consumer experienced a minor burn with no markings and did not seek medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was deemed normal by the technician but still caused discomfort.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her dishwasher was filled with smoke. The consumer stated that the dishwasher was running for 10 minutes. The consumer shut off the dishwasher by turning off the circuit breaker. The consumer found that the control panel melted. The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer opted to not call the fire department. The consumer noticed that her dishwasher was making an odd noise. 

The consumer opened the dishwasher and found that smoke was filled in her kitchen. The consumer called the retailer but could not reach anyone. The consumer hast not yet called the firm. The consumer has not experienced any property damage and has not called her home insurance company. The consumer has noticed numerous reports online of this happening and will have a technician come to her home to repair the dishwasher.

UPDATE: We contacted Kitchenaid (Whirlpool) about the burned up control panel.  They took a complete report and after consulting with their safety dept, sent up the replacement control panel (at their expense) and reimbursed us for the repair service.  They were very cooperative and seemed very interested in sustaining good customer service and maintaining a safe and quality product.  We were very pleased with their response.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a melted control panel but no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the consumer noticing numerous online reports of similar incidents.

incident_description:
Product: Krups coffeemaker (Ref: KM505550/5CA-4609).  Owned about 3 years.
During routine cleaning of appliance with a mild vinegar solution (9 cups water with 1 cup vinegar) the unit began to emit noxious odors.  Water from the reservoir that usually flows up into the filter cone then down into the carafe was not moving through its predetermined path but remained bubbling in the internal plumbing.  Upon that observation the unit was disconnected.  Further inspection showed the plastic body surrounding the heating plate was melted and had distorted.  An opaque sticky, gelatinous substance of unknown composition oozed around the top of the reservoir area.
justification: The incident involved equipment damage and noxious odors but no injury or death, making severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such malfunctions are not common with routine cleaning.

incident_description:
I was pre heating the oven, heard a big pop and several more pops, than flames were in the oven, we turned off the over still was on fire so turned off the main power, the bottom burning element broke at that point on the right side. I had to order a new part and enstalled it two days later, the oven was put in my house in 1999.
Model nbr is JBP24B Y2WH.
We received the first stove in the development was just woundering if any more of the stoves in the area will have the same problem?
justification: The incident involved flames in the oven but no injury or death, and the issue was resolved by replacing a part. The likelihood is possible given the age of the oven and the specific part failure.

incident_description:
Emerson Microwave model# MW9325SL, suffix C, Manufacture date August 2009.  S/N 908049829MM.
I purchased this microwave about one to 1 1/2 yrs ago at Walmart.  Every now and then it would male loud popping noises and lightning-like sparks would flash.  Other times, after the unit ran it's cycle, it would still be 'humming' loud  like the motor was still running, so I would unplug it for a while then plug it back in.  Now, it'll run it's cycle and stop but start again when we open the door.  I'm concerned We've been exposed to high amounts of radiation.  We have to unplug the unit before opening the door.

It recently started smoking around the steam control knob, after a couple of weeks of emiting a burning smell.

I removed the top and the smoke is coming from a plastic cover on a spade connector  connecting onto the heating element
justification: The incident involves smoke and a burning smell from the espresso machine, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We have a pair of fairly new (six months) Bosch model SHE5AL02UC dishwashers. 

If you open the door while the washer is running, about one out of ten times you will be hit in the face (specifically in the eyes) with scalding hot, caustic soapy water. This happens when you open the door just as the upper spray arm is squirting water in the direction of the door. 

Then is no lockout device to prevent the door from being opened while the washer is running.
justification: The incident involves scalding hot, caustic soapy water hitting the face and eyes, which can cause injury, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) as it occurs about one out of ten times the door is opened during operation.

incident_description:
Bosch Dishwasher model SHE55M12UC.  The terminal block left hand side connection to the black conductor melted, the wire insulation melted as well causing the 20 amp breaker to trip.  The electrical supply wire to the dishwasher has been confirmed to be properly sized #12 AWG by a licensed Electrician.  There are several of these compliants and Bosch's answer is that the supply line is improperly sized to cover up a design issue.  Bosch did issue a recall on certain models up to 2005 however my model/serial number was not cover in the recall and our dishwasher was purchased in 2010 so the problem still exists.

This could have easily have started a house fire and very well may have if the smell of melting burning plastic was left uninvestigated.  I also spoke to an appliance repair person who said that his was a common problem with Bosch Dishwasher.  I can not understand why there is no recall on this product at this time.  

Do Not Risk Your Families Safety, Don't Buy a Bosch !!!!!
justification: The incident involved a melted terminal block and wire insulation, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
After placing the room temperature blueberries and dough inside the glass baking dish and placing the electric range (oven) at 400 degrees baking for 20 minutes the sides of the dish blew into a million of pieces inside the oven.

She did not open the door to the oven and instead saw the incident through the glass. She has not contacted the firm or the retailer but  indicated that she would contact the firm. 

She indicated that she is very thankful that she did not remove the dish from the oven because she could have been seriously injured by the exploding glass.
justification: The glass dish exploded but no one was injured as the oven door remained closed, preventing potential harm.

incident_description: I have a Kitchenaid built in double wall oven Model KEBS277SSS. On 02/05/2012 we ran the self clean cycle on the upper oven and when that cycle finished,we did the same on the lower oven. About half way through the 2.5 hour cycle,   the lower oven literally expolded. Apparently the inner tempered glass on the door exploded sending glass particlesflying across the kitchen even though the door  remained in the self clean locked position and the outer glass panels remained in place. Fortunately, there was no one in the kitchen at the time so there were no injuries. I made inquiries to Kitchenaid/Whirlpool as to the possible cause and/or preventitive steps but did not receive a cogent answer.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass particles to scatter, but no one was injured as the kitchen was unoccupied.

The dishwasher was purchased from Pawlak Appliance Inc. and was installed on 6/01/02.  Pawlaks has since gone out of business.  We don't expect an appliance to last forever but we also don't expect it to catch fire.

justification: Contained fire with no injuries or deaths, and no one was present during the incident.

justification: The incident involved smoke and a charred circuit board but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While dishwasher was running there was a loud pop, the dishwasher never stoped running, but the heating ellement on the bottom of the machine had poped open and wires were hanging out, there was only damange to the machine it self, no one was injured.
justification: The incident involved damage to the dishwasher but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is moderate (3) as such malfunctions are possible but not frequent.

incident_description:

She noticed that the dishwasher was inoperable and that it had tripped the circuit breaker.  The electrical component had melted inside the dishwasher.

1/2012 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and a service rep was sent out 1/12/12 for service, the control board was replaced.

Consumer is concerned that the dishwasher is displaying similar problems of the other dishwasher and feels that this is a fire hazard and something should be done.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she had placed the dishwasher on wash cycle before she went to bed, however when she awke the next morning the unit had tripped the circuit breaker, there was smoke emitting from it.  The dishwasher was unplugged and removed. This unit had a service call of replacing the control board in 2009.

12/17/2011 Consumer contacted the manufacture a service rep was sent out who advised that it would be best to purchase another unit because the control panel was irrepairable and it would costly to replace it.

Consumer stated that she discarded the unit and purchased another brand.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and a tripped circuit breaker, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Dishwasher recall seen on news by caller's acquaintance who then told caller who is creating this report
Caller's approximately nine year old dishwasher was not found on recall.

Caller and granddaughter were sitting and talking when they smelled smoke but couldn't find the source with the beginning of their search but after searching for a while they realized that the dishwasher door was blackened as if from burning, the dishwasher had completed all cycles earlier and was thought to be turned off. 

Caller turned off dishwasher and haven't been using it.

Consumer contacted CPSC January 20, 2012 to create report in order to alert public and in hopes of having the dishwasher repaired at manufacturer expense..

CONSUMER ADDED:  Dishwasher stopped itself due to burned out wiring and is inoperable, dishes were clean but not dry when discovered.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a blackened dishwasher door, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore electric coil stove which is not a flat top.  Model #790.9421340G purchased in Nov. 2009.  The electric coils will burn on high even when the dial is set on low.  The elements need to be turned off to stop the burner from continueing on high.  The elements can be set on 5 and the next next minute the coil is red hot and out of control.  This happens everytime we use the stove and believe it is the same problem that the flat top stoves have.  It is very dangerous and extremely difficult to cook on this stove top.  I was told by sears to unplug it if I didn't feel safe, but that was all they could do without a service call.  I believe this is a safety recall issue and feel they are not acknowledging the problem with these coils and rotary switches.  I feel this model and other non flat top models with the digital display and rotary dials should be considered for addition to the recall list.  This is especially true if they are experiencing the same issues.  It cannot be ignored.  There are too many incident dates to include in the form below.  They simply won't fit.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a significant burn risk due to uncontrolled heating, but no injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Elite Oven/Range combo, Model # 790.99119301, Serial # VF40300220. While the range was
off, the right front range came on HIGH by itself. We were not able to turn it off. We had to turn off the fuse at the
fuse box. This incident occurred during the evening hours. The Unit is approximately 5 years old. The appliance
repair center said that it maybe the control panel and would be cheaper to replace than fix. Our concern is that if
we were on vacation, our house may have caught on fire. We left for vacation the following week and just return,
the reason for the reporting delay.
justification: The range turned on by itself and could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Reference:  Kenmore Electric Cook top Model  790 4273403, serial number MF80316697, purchased from Sears 02086, 1404 Old Aberdeen Road, Leigh Mall, Columbus, MS 39705-2129, on 29 JAN 08. 
Please replace or repair this unit.
 On or about 11 JUL 11, while cooking I experienced loud BANG and noticed a crack in the glass top.  Shortly afterwards, I visited the Sears store where I purchased the cook top.  They told me it was safe to use and would not be replaced.  Since then many other cracks have occurred and it is dangerous to use.  The stove needs to be replaced.  I am afraid to use it. incident_description:
Consumer stated that his Electric Range front right burner spontaneously turned on by itself which caught a kitchen mit on fire , they were able to smother the fire immediately.  They were unable to power off the range at the control panel and had to unplug it to prevent further damages.

Consumer stated that for the past week the burners would not turn off completely, he had to keep turning for a couple of mins then it would turn off but now the range automatically comes on by itself.

12/7/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that his model was not part of the recall and that he should report it to the agency.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, but potential for significant damage.

incident_description:
Turned on oven on our 2005 Kenmore electric range model 790.96619401 and a few minutes later we heard an arcing sound coming from the range and a electrical burnt smell.

We turned off the oven and then pulled the range away from the wall and unplugged the range.
We took off the upper back cover and we could smell that the timer panel (316418702) was where the smell was coming from.

We are afraid to order a replacement part for about $207 since we don't know if this replacement timer will be made of better components than the original one.
justification: The incident involved an electrical issue with the oven, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I turned on my Kenmore dishwasher, model #665.17362301, purchased in July 2004, and shortly afterward I noticed it was making an unfamiliar sound.  I was still in the kitchen.  I turned to look at it and noticed a thin plume of black smoke coming from the right hand side of the control panel, near the top.  I called my husband's attention to it.  Another plume of black smoke came out of a second area.  I was about to open the door to stop the machine when a sudden flash of fire came from the front panel, then a loud "pop", and much more smoke.  Now I was afraid to touch the machine but I went ahead and opened it, expecting that would turn it off.  However, the machine did not turn off as it normally would and water sprayed in all directions around the kitchen.  I quickly shut the dishwasher door most of the way, while my husband went to the circuit breaker panel, which fortunately is in the kitchen.  He flipped the switch for the dishwasher and cut the power.

Certain serial numbers of this dishwasher were recalled in 2005, but when I called about mine, I was told that my dishwasher's serial number was not part of the recall, and that my machine was fine to use.

I am horrified by this incident because many, many, many times we have started the dishwasher at the end of the night and gone directly to bed.  And many times we have started the dishwasher and then left the house.  This could have caused serious injury or property damage.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher emitting smoke and a flash of fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Elite Dishwasher, Model Number 665.17464300 Serial Number FR1707552 caught fire in the middle of a wash cycle.  Smoke and sparks began to drift out of the control panel.  Fortunately, we were home and able to stop operation of the dishwasher, which resolved the problem without causing property damage to our home.  When we attempted to drain the dishwasher via the "cancel / drain" function of the dishwasher, the sparks and smoke resumed, so we stopped.

I contacted Sears, and they were unwilling to send a repair person to assess the situation without charging us a repair fee since this dishwasher is not currently covered by recalls covering dishwashers apparently also reported catching fire.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and emitted sparks and smoke, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore model 721.63252301. S/N 507TA06456.  We have owned this microwave for a few years and are the original owner.  My wife placed a microwave safe bowl into the oven with broccoli in it with approximately 1 cup of water.  The timer was set for several minutes and the start button pressed.  Several minutes into cooking the broccoli smoke started come out from the sides of the microwave oven.  The smoke had a very offensive smell and smelled like electrical wires or components burning.  The cord is in perfect condition and was plugged into a GFCI outlet.  This outlet at no time triggered.  The smoke was building so we stopped the microwave oven and removed the broccoli.  The broccoli and water was complete cold so it was clear zero cooking of the item was occurring.  We placed the microwave outside since we were concerned that it was going to cause a fire.  I emailed SEARS customer support and let them know of the issue and they simply responded and said my microwave was out of warranty.  I let SEARS know that I planned on plugging the microwave in again while it was outside to test what would have happened had we been upstairs in the house.  I let them know I was disappointed they were not further investigating the issue.  I have now received another email from Sears saying a store manager will call me.   I placed the microwave on a table outside, put a plastic cup in it with 1/2 cup of water and put 15 minutes or so on the timer.  I pressed start and waited while filming.  After 5 minutes you could smell the odor again.  Very difficult to see any smoke.   Within 15 minutes there was a heavy constant stream of thick white smoke coming out of the sides of the microwave oven.  I actually put the camera down for a few minutes and in that time it when from barely smoking to a ton of steady smoke.   Again, very strong and offensive odor.  I would say it smells like an electrical or plastic component melting or burning inside the unit.   I would say the smoke would fill a standard kitchen in 5 minutes easily once it reaches the heavy stage.  I had the microwave on an extension cord several feet from the house.  I unplugged it from the house once the really heavy smoke started.  I opened the microwave oven door and checked the water in the cup.  It was cold and receiving zero heating.  The smoke took a while to stop flowing from the unit.   I still have the microwave and the video that I took on our small Panasonic camera and it clearly shows the problem.   I could post it on youtube and send a private link if interested?
justification: The incident involved significant smoke and a burning smell from the microwave, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
When any of the burner are in use at any setting for any amount of time  they do not power in the off position when switched off and the range has to be unplugged from the wall outlet.

The firm was not contacted and she has replaced the appliance and placed in a  storage unit.  

She indicated that she would contact the firm and see if any repairs could be made. 

No further information was provided.
justification: The burner not powering off poses a potential hazard, but no injury or incident was reported.

incident_description: I used the oven to bake a dish about 4:00PM at about 5:00 Pm  I turned the oven off making sure the red light was off to indicate the oven was off. I left the kitchen until about 2 AM when I went back to make sure everything was locked and lights off to call it a night expecting total darkness but instead I could see the electric broiler element in my oven was on even though the control panel lights that let you know the oven was on were not on but yet the oven was still on.  When I went to check on why the oven was still on I could feel the heat from the stove and even the knobs were hot.  I still turned the knob as if I wanted to turn the stove on and the lights went on and when I turned the knob to off the lights went out but the oven still stayed on.  I opened the door to the oven while standing back to let the build up of heat out and as soon as I opened the door the inside pane of glass cracked.  Since I could not shut the oven off or move it to unplug it I immediately went to the main breaker box and flipped the 50 amp breaker to the oven off and waited until the oven was cool enough to pull the bottom warming tray out to unplug the stove from the wall as a double precaution.  The next day I plugged everything in again and the same thing happened so I disconnected the oven again because it wonÃÂt shut off even though the lights tell you it is off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I smelled something like crayons burning and checked the house, I could not find the source.  I knew I would be up another hour ( packing for our trip the next day) and decided to see if the smell got worse or if I noticed something.  An hour later i checked the Kitchen and it was foggy/smokey and I saw a stream of steam/smoke coming from the dishwasher.  When I opened the dishwasher it was very apparent that the heating coil at the bottom turned on automatically ( the dishwasher was closed but not on) and melted anything plastic.  My [REDACTED] cutting board is warped, a handle of a [REDACTED] knife melted, [REDACTED] melted to liquid ( this was the crayon smell), etc...The Granite counter top was very hot to the touch as were the side cabinets.  It would not turn off so I went and turned off the main circuit breaker to the dishwasher.  
This is a GE product 
Model # PDW8200NBB, Serial # TM889360B
GE came out to inspect it and started removing all the melted parts from the inside of the washer and was going to attempt to fix it!!!  I had to remind them that had this happened less then 12 hours later we would not have been home and the kitchen ( and house, I will assume) would have burnt down!
They are giving me the run around saying it was originally purchased in 2007 ( which it was not I have proof) and they are looking into it.  I think this is a HUGE issue that they are taking lightly.
justification: The incident involved property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: dishwasher caught fire and caught the house on fire
justification: The dishwasher fire caused significant property damage (house caught fire), but no injury or death was mentioned.

incident_description: General Electric refrigerator model TFX25CR caught fire.  The fire was in the ice dispenser located in the freezer.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
While watching TV, I noticed a flckering light coming from our microwave oven.  It was empty and not operating.  I went to the kitchen, opened the microwave and saw a flame, approximately 6 inches in length coming from the magnetron area of the microwave.  I doused the flame and called my wife to observe.  When I opened the microwave door again, and left it open, no flames occured. I then put a ceramic coffee cup, half full of water, in the oven and put the power on for 30 seconds.  Immediately, the magnetron area turned a bright glowing red.  I stopped the experiment and left the microwave door open the rest of the night.  
The next morning I called the maker, Frigidaire (Electolux Home Products) and reported the incident.  They let me know that the two-year old microwave was out of warranty.  I then reported it as a sfaety hazard, and was issued a case file number:[REDACTED].  There seemed to be no concern on the part of the customer service representative. She did provide me the p/n for the magnetron, if I wanted to have it repaired.  Of course, I did not want the hazard in our house any longer.
Since we had the house built only 2 1/2 years earlier,  I contacted the builder who came to investigate, pulled the microwave out of it's position on top of the oven( it was a microwave/oven combination) and later sent an e-mail to Frigidaire concerning the incident.  I have since replaced the faulty and hazardous microwave with another brand, and had my builder install it, after  I checking wiring etc. I have kept the hazardous microwave on the garage floor, awaiting dispostion.
justification: The incident involved a flame in the microwave, which was extinguished without injury, but posed a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
Consumer stated her gas range grates are coated with some kind of hard surfacing, something like (porcelain), whenever she is using the burners (front right and left rear) the coating breaks off and discharges on the floor and on her body.  This incident has caused burnt marks to her linoleum flooring, and she had received mild burns to her chest.  No medical attention was needed.  

7/2011 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and left a message, however no one had returned her phone call, she will send them an email as well.

1/11/12 Consumer contacted the retailer and was advised that the problem she is experiencing is a cosmetic flaw.
Consumer feels that this gas range is a fire hazard and should be reported.

Handle is made of very light metal and not very strong at all

Not found on recall

Consumer has not contacted the manufacturer, will contact them

incident_description: While in my kitchen I noticed the smell of burning and investigated to find out where it was coming from. From the onset of fumes within one minute there was a distinctive sparking/cracking sound coming from my Whirlpool side by side refrigerator freezer.  I pulled the unit out and unplugged it from the electrical receptacle. I'm a handyman by trade and removed the cardboard rear cover to investigate. The compressor start device had completely burned and melted.  I was grateful I'd been home and in the kitchen standing next to it when it happened, to unplug it from the wall.  I replaced the start capacitor and the start device for my Whirlpool model ED5NHEXMQ1Q, purchased in March 2004.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and sparking from a refrigerator, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Ran dishwasher overnight.  Did not open it  the next morning as we went to work.  When returning home there was a melting plastic smell in the house.  Attempted the open the dishwasher as the smell was coming from there.  Had to really tug to get it open.  Discovered the heating element had stayed on and had melted the rinser spinner attached to the motor, a cutting board and the bottom of the silver ware tray.  2 hours after the unit was opened the granite counter top was still warm.  Since there was already a recall on this model I called the recall line to see if ours was added to this recall.  Maytag directed us to have a repairman that they gave us the option of using to come out to see if there was a defect in our model.  

Appliance Hospital came out and went through our unit.  He said he could not find anything wrong with our unit and said it was user error.  His thought, and he could not provide proof of this, was that something held the spinning arm down and the metal on the bottom of the spinner made contact with the element which kept the unit on.  

First, when pulling the lower rack out we would have felt this.  Second, our dishes would not have been clean if the spray was concentrated in only one area.  Third, there would have been a mark on the spinner from whatever had pressed it down.  Fourth, when I looked at other models as well as ours, there is not that much play in the spinner for it to come in contact with the element.  Fifth, the motor would have burned up if held for 18 hours.  Why was there not a safety shut off/timer for the heating element?

I do not feel that the cause of the heating element staying on for 15 hours was caused by the spinner being held in place.  I also believe that the problem with our unit was not determined and because of this could be a danger to others that own the same unit.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted dishwasher parts) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not widespread.

Luckily my wife was in the kitchen at the time and called for me.   I opened the door to stop the washer and turned off the circuit breaker.   The flame had started to scorch the cabinet next to it.   Had we not been home, this could have easily caused a major fire.
justification: The incident involved a flame and scorching, but no injury or death occurred due to immediate action.

incident_description:
Consumer Product Safety Commission 

Report on [REDACTED]ÃÂs stove, filed 2.4.12

Re: Southbend ÃÂUltimate RangeÃÂ 4601DD-2GR (serial no. 11G295080), purchased by the [REDACTED] ([REDACTED]) in July 2011

It is virtually impossible to determine whether all six pilot lights under the heavy griddle have been lit by the electronic igniters. There are not sufficient sighting ports on the front panel of the range for determining whether the pilot lights have been lit. Two of the three ports that are included in the front panel have stainless-steel plates behind them blocking the sight line. These plates were obviously installed to block any unusually large flame spread from moving through the port and toward the operatorÃÂs face.

ThereÃÂs something of a Catch-22 in this range design. The designers included ports in the front panel so the operator could verify that the pilot lights are lit. But then this presented a problem with any dangerous flame spread or surge. Plates were then addedÃÂjust as they were decades ago for water heatersÃÂto stop any large (and dangerous) flame surge from reaching the operator. The addition of anti-flame-surge plates, which are difficult to remove, makes it impossible for the operator to see all the pilot lights. In the case of the water heater, at least up till recently, the operator could remove and reinstall the anti-flame-surge plate. 

Further, the electronic igniters on this model are reliably temperamental. Sometimes they light the pilot gas, and sometimes they donÃÂt. WeÃÂve had service technicians, from TWC in Atlanta, out twice to work on the igniters of this stove, which is under warranty by Southbend until July 2012. Two days after a visit from a technician we found that some of the igniters were not working. 

The TWC technicians have confirmed five concerns which I initially raised with Southbend upon my early, thorough examination of the stove:

1.   The igniters are inconsistent in operation. Pushing the igniter button on the stove front doesnÃÂt ensure that the pilot lights under the griddle are fired. The probability of their being fired is not very high, because the igniter electrodes are sensitive to exact alignment with the flow of gas from the pilot light hole in the pilot manifold. Heating and cooling cycles surely affect this alignment in negative way. 

2.   Notwithstanding what the instruction manual says about lifting the griddle to verify that the pilot lights are lit, the grill is too heavy and too unwieldy to lift. It weighs over 60 pounds and there are no hand-holes in it. It is not possible for one person to lift it to verify that the pilot lights, underneath, are lit. It would take two people to lift the griddle, and even this would be dangerous.

3.   When all six pilots are litÃÂafter two people have removed the griddle, confirmed that the pilots are lit, and then replaced the griddleÃÂthe sighting ports in the front panel allow a clear visual check of only two of the pilots. One other pilot can barely be seen. The other three cannot be seen at all.

4.   Two of the pilot light tubes can easily be reached with a long match in the event the igniters are known to be in total failure. One pilot can be reached with much difficulty. Three pilots cannot be reached at all. They are blocked by the anti-flame-surge plates.

5.   Unlit pilot lights under the griddleÃÂwhen the main gas valve on the stove is open, allowing gas flow to all pilot light tubesÃÂallow for a dangerous condition: the buildup of raw gas.                      


On behalf of the [REDACTED], IÃÂve talked with Southbend Customer Service and with Southbend Technical Support. From these two departments I have received nothing helpful on the five concerns. There is uncertainty at Southbend on why there are not clear sight lines to all six pilots under the griddle. I have written to the president of Southbend about this matter. The company has not provided a satisfactory answer to my questions. The VP of Engineering told me last September that we could remove the plates blocking the sight lines. A design engineer with the company had said, weeks earlier, that we must not remove these plates. The Atlanta company that sold us the stove, Atlanta Fixtures, has not been helpful.
justification: The design flaws and unreliable igniters create a high risk of gas buildup, which could lead to injury from potential explosions or fires.

incident_description: While boiling water, I heard an electrical "arcing" sound from an adjacent room to the kitchen. When I went to investigate, I could smell something electrical burning, then a second flare up took place, behind the stove, in the upper control area. I quickly pulled the stove out away from the wall and unplugged it to prevent any significant damage. Discoloration of the wall was fortunately the extent of the damage.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and burning smell, but no injury or significant damage occurred.

incident_description:
A short time into the wash cycle of  my kenmore elite tall boy dishwasher it made a popping, gurgling noise which was followed by a terrible smell.  Smoke began to fill up the kitchen. The dishwasher has standing water inside it and is non functional.  It appears to have no functioning electronics. 

  Something inside the door had caught on fire. The smell is still terrible 8 hours after the fire has gone out.  This happened this morning.  I told my brother who had heard of the class action lawsuit so I did some research on the Internet, and it appears we have also been a victim of this faulty product.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher, causing smoke and a terrible smell, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I opened the door of my Kenmore electric range model 790.96213408 and the right side of the handle broke away from the door. I screwed it back together but the next day the handle completely came off when I opened the door. This caused the stainless steel outer part of the door and the glass insert to fall forward while the main part of the door slammed shut.

The top part of the oven door is held together by the two screws that go into the plastic door handle. The screws seem to be way too short; they only go into the handle about a quarter of an inch. The plastic thread ridges inside the handle are worn and don't seem capable of holding a heavy door together. 

Someone could easily be burned if the handle falls off while they are taking something out of the oven and the door slams shut.
justification: The incident describes a potential burn hazard due to the oven door handle failing, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Yesterday evening, the right rear burner on my Kenmore Elite Smooth top range did not get hot after I turned it on to high.   I waited a few minutes, still didn't even get warm.  I thumped the burner thinking something was loose - immediately, all the coils on this burner (visible under the ceramic top) became red hot poker red and hotter than these burners have ever been. with about 1/2 inch of the beginning of the coil becoming even redder, and seemed to flare up and flicker a little.  Made a filament type noise while it was flickering, like when you shake a lightbulb.  This alarmed me.  I've never seen a smooth top do this.    Turned it off and didn't use it.  The other burners seemed to be working as usual.     This morning I re-tried the right rear one - same thing - became immediately very hot with the same flickering up and filament sound.   Oddly enough, this very same burner, which is my favorite and the one I've used mostly, did not seem to be getting as hot as it should for a few months now and the burner did not seem all that responsive to knob temp. changes.   I attributed that to the fact that it is the most used burner, so I didn't complain.  But this business of now overheating and flickering is scary and probably dangerous.    I called several numbers this morning to report this to Sears/Kenmore, including the one in the pat response from Sears on this website - all were totally useless, unless I wanted to pay over $100.00 for a service call.    All numbers, including the local Sears store where I purchased this stove in July, of 2009, were unsympathetic, and seemed more interested in chastising me for not purchasing the "extended warranty".    I have been Sears'/Kenmore's biggest fan for years, and spent a lot of money on a lot of appliances, tv's, etc. with our local Sears, but no more.   The way they are acting about these stove burner problems is inexcusable.   Our stove costs over $1,200.00  and I shouldn't have one burner out of service, and a possible fire hazard to worry about.  I asked for a free diagnostic repair visit, and was refused.     Nothing is going to be done about these matters until the responsible parties are sued.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
This is a safety conccern.
I purchased a Presto Poplite hot-air popcorn popper.
The device is 120 volts and 1440 watts, which, I beleive, translates into almost 12 amps.
The device has neither an on/off switch nor, as far as I can tell, a heat high limit safety.
You plug it in to start the heat and air flow and pull the plug to stop it.  When the plug is pulled, it creates a sizeable spark.
I see this device as both a heat/fire hazard and, moreso, an electical shock hazard.
I can't think of any other household device that lacks an on/off switch.
justification: The device poses a potential fire and electrical shock hazard due to lack of safety features, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I bought this microwave in the box,on clearance, right after Christmas. Purchase date was 1-4-2012. The microwave worked fine until 1-31-2012. On that date, I noticed that after I turned it off and closed the door, the microwave fan continued to run, the light stayed on, and the plate inside still turned around. I called LG customer service, and the man there told me to unplug it. Unplugging it did work, but I keep having the same problem. I had never experienced this much heat from a self cleaning oven in any other range I have ever owned. I tried to turn the stove off but it would not turn off. My brother was at my home visiting and we finally decided that perhaps it was supposed to get that hot. The next day when I tried to use my stove, the controls did not work properly. Half of the burners would only turn on on high temperatures. The oven temperature could not be set either. A repair man from the company Mr. Applicance came to my home on Feb 2, 2012 to give me an estimate on the problems with the range. I have been informed by that company that the heat from the self cleaning cycle was so intense that it warped all four of the ranges electronic control boards. The range's one year warranty expired 7-21-2011. I did not purchase an extended warranty. The purchase price for the range after a military discount for me was $899. The repairs have been estimated at $1018.

Because of the intense heat from the self cleaning cycle and the fact that I could not turn the stove off when I realized it was so hot (the control boards must have already started to warp before this attempt); I feel that this product is a fire hazard and should be investigated.

This range was manufactured May, 2010. I ordered it from Home Depot on 7-7-10 and it was delivered on 7-21-10. It is LG Model # LRE30453S. S/N 005MMXN01826.
justification: The incident involved excessive heat and malfunctioning controls, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: About 10-15 minutes after starting a load of dishes, I heard a noise in the kitchen, glanced quickly in there but didn't see anything amiss. Within about 2 minutes I could smell burning plastic from the family room where we were watching TV. By then we could see smoke seeping out from the control panel on the dishwasher. I grabbed the handle to pull it open but the plastic was too hot to touch...and I could still hear arcing sounds inside. I ran to our electrical box and shut off that circuit to stop the damage. But, by then the entire control board, connectors and wiring harness were burned beyond repair. It took more than a week to get the smell out of the houseÃÂand a lot of cleaning. The fire started behind the main fuse on the circuit board, shorting and burning every electrical component insideÃÂbefore burning the main fuse itself. Our house breaker never trippedÃÂas has been the case with almost all Kitchenaid dishwasher fires we have heard of. Phil's Appliance Repair came the next day (www.phils.com) and told us the control board, thermal fuse and wiring harness were beyond repair, and probably the pump as well, and that the wiring harness is no longer available through Kitchenaid/Whirlpool parts supply system. We paid $61.50 to get this news. But, had we left the house after turning on the dishwasher, which we often do, we may not even have a house to come home to.

incident_description:
After about three years of owning a Kenmore Gas Range Model 790, the right side of the main door handle popped off as I was opening the oven. The door slammed shut and, because the left side of the handle hadn't fallen off, it torqued the left side handle as I still had the right side in my hand while the door was slamming shut.  I found that simply screwing the bolt back in was relatively easy, and didn't think about it for a while. Then it happened again, and again, and again.  The frequency became too high (3 times in one day) in November, and I'm just now getting to writing a report after seeing online many people experience the same problem.  The only way our handle holds now is if the spacers are removed between the interior and exterior panels of the door.

I just got off the phone with Sears, and the only person available on the phone is a dispatcher, not a tech, and he told me that there was nothing that they could do to help without having a tech come out, which we would be charged for.

incident_description: I used my Calphalon 4 qt slow cooker to make soup last night.  The soup cooked on high for 4 hours then warmed for an hour.  When we got ready to eat, I unplugged the [slow cooker].  After eating, I set a timer for 1 hour to let the soup cool before putting it away.  After that time, I put the soup away, rinsed the [slow cooker] and put it in the dishwasher, and then washed the lid by hand in warm water.  It didn't even feel warm to the touch.  I put it on my dish drying cloth on my counter to dry.  About 2a.m. I heard a pop.  I didn't realize until this morning what happened.  My [slow cooker] lid had just exploded -- not imploded, but exploded and put glass everywhere on my counter, window sill, sink, etc.  I called Calphalon and they are sending me a new lid, but I am wary and not sure how the lid could have just exploded especially after than many hours -- what if I or one of my kids would have been standing there? It could have been a serious danger.  I also just did some research online and I am not the first one this has happened to.

incident_description:
The consumer report about a major safety defect in a self-cleaning gas range.
On four separate occasions, consumerÃÂs house has filled with gas because the far right knob that is used to ignite the front right gas burner on the range was engaged without her knowledge.
On the first occasion, her family returned from a weeklong vacation to a house filled with gas. After investigating the matter, it was discovered that the right gas burner knob was engaged without the house sitter's knowledge. A similar situation happened again.  
The latest situation, the consumer was asleep & smelt gas. When she went downstairs to the kitchen and saw that the right burner knob was slightly engaged.  She ventilated the house for 30 minutes to ensure all gas had dissipated.
Upon investigation into the incidents, consumer discovered two things. One, the convection/microwave oven is above the stove and sometimes when food is put into the microwave oven, the person leans on the burner knob on the stove and it becomes is depressed and slightly turned, enough that gas is released from the burner. However, when this happens, the person has no knowledge of it. There is no clicking sound from the igniter.
Two, if you touch the knob with your body as you move around the kitchen, which occurred in the 2010 incident, the knob can become slightly depressed and turned, and gas can be expelled from the burner. Again, without a clicking sound from the igniter.
The consumer is concerned that it has a major defect that could cause her family, her dogs, and her to die.
justification: The incident involves a major safety defect leading to gas leaks, which poses a significant risk of death, and has occurred multiple times under different circumstances.

incident_description:
Item:  Maytag Range, model MER5721BAQ serial number 12690522ZU
Oven overheats with severe fire potential.  The relay that controls the AC power to the oven heating element short circuited permanently in the "ON" position providing power to the heating element that could not be turned off using the controls on the range.  The contacts in the oven relay welded together in the ON position.  The only way to stop the oven from getting hotter and hotter is to unplug the range or turn off the AC circuit breaker.  Fortunately I was home at the time and discovered the overheating oven.  Had I not been home, had not noticed the oven overheating, or if I had used the timer to activate the oven the results could have been disasterous.  

Being an engineer by trade I examined the condition and discovered that a NAIS/Panasonic/Aeromat relay model JW2H-T-F-DC24V-Y8-H had malfunctioned, the contacts welded together permanently in the ON position, supplied uncontrolled power to the oven heating element.  The relay is located in the oven clock electronics assembly.  The relay directly controls the application of 240 VAC to the oven heating element.

Further examination of the oven electrical schematic reveals there is no overtemp fuse or other device to prevent thermal runaway once the relay fails.

This is a serious fire safety hazard deserving of expedited handling.
justification: The incident describes a severe fire hazard with potential for death if unnoticed, and the occurrence is possible given the lack of safety mechanisms.

incident_description:
My wife purchased a Jenn Air duel fuel, double oven range.  
The top burners are gas and are controlled by knobs on the right side of the stove top.
These knobs will activate an electric igniter that sparks beside each burn with just the start of turning the knob.  
The igniter sparks when the knob passes the same spot, BOTH starting and OFF.  
We have had instances where the gas either never ignited or the flame blew out.  In these instances, the gas continued to come out of the burner building up fumes.  Unfortunately you cannot turn off the gas with the knob WITHOUT GOING PAST THE IGNITER CAUSING IT TO SPARK when trying to shut off the gas.  We have had a few 'flame outs', but only because we are watching for this issue has nothing more serious occurred.  I have reported the problem to Jenn Air without any response from them.
justification: The incident involves gas buildup due to flame-outs and igniter sparking, posing a risk, but no injury or death has occurred as reported.
