justification: The dishwasher was hot to the touch and the plastic cups were melted, but there was no injury or death.

incident_description: The coffee maker finished making the pot of coffee, and then about a minute or two later I noticed there was a lot of steam coming out of the coffee maker. As I got closer to it I realized that it wasn't steam, it was smoke. The smoke increased and increased as we quickly opened doors and windows and turned on fans to try to clear the air. We unplugged the thing and ran it out to the backyard. We ended up watching it continue to billow black smoke, while we stood there with the hose at the ready. It finally stopped smoking and we left it out there. Not about to bring it back into the house or garage.
justification: The incident involved a coffee maker emitting smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: We noticed a plastic burning smell and tracked the smell down to our kitchen.  When we entered the kitchen we noticed smoke poring out of the Coffee pot.  We unplugged it and put it in the sink were it smolder for a while.  Before we unplugged it we noticed the clocked had died on the machine, the coffee was near boiling, and the smoke was coming out of the back of the machine around the electric cord.  We had brewed a pot of coffee in it about 20 minutes before this incident took place.  The Left rotary knob on the machine was in the Brew Position, the middle rotary knob was in the up position between ON and OFF (it is a momentary switch that self centers to that position), and the right rotary knob was in the M (for Medium heat) position.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a malfunctioning coffee pot, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I have a Bosch dishwasher SHU3307UC/U12, FB8111200089.  Last night while running a load of dishes, the control panel began popping, sparking and smoldering.  We were home at the time of the incident, and immediately stopped the cycle, which discontinued the sparking.  We closed the door and started the cycle again and the same set of incidents occurred.  We discontinued use of the appliance.  Today, we opened the panel and the control module had melted.  I did a search online and found that the model is under voluntary recall.  I am attempting to contact Bosch to have a service tech come out to replace the control board. Thank God we were home and able to stop the cycle, or I'm sure we would be dealing with a major loss.
justification: The incident involved sparking and smoldering but no injury or death occurred, and the issue is under recall, indicating it's a known but not rare problem.

incident_description:
Pyrex brand bowl was on shelf 1 foot above kitchen counter when it fell onto counter.  The bowl broke into hundreds of pieces.  The major issue was not the fact that it broke, but rather the explosive nature of the shards and the fact that they were very dangerous.

Specifically, Pyrex is supposed to be (1) break-resistant and (2) safe if it breaks.  This product was neither.  Most concerning, for someone with two little kids in the house (ages 3 months and 2.5 years), is that when the product broke it did so in an extremely dangerous manner not befitting a kitchen product.
justification: The bowl broke explosively into dangerous shards, posing a significant injury risk, especially to children, though no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description:
When powering the front left and right burner is switched on and at any setting within a few seconds the burners would heat up to higher temperatures without being selected. The circuit breaker has to be pulled or the range has to be unplugged from the wall outlet to power the appliance in the off position.

The firm was contacted in December of 2007 and a service technician was scheduled to come out to the home but he never showed. WHile using the pot ont he front left burner for about 5minutes on a low setting when the temperature changed and caused the pot to burn.

The failure has continued to occur intermittently and the firm was contacted on 12/19/2011 and the consumer was advised that her model number was not included in the recall (see Release #09-333)  and that she would be required to pay for a service technician to come out to the home.

The consumer has not made any repairs to the appliance  and fears that  it could possibly pose as a fire hazard. She indicated that she has smaller children in the home that are able to reach the front burners of the range. 

She currently still uses the range with caution.
justification: The incident caused a pot to burn due to uncontrolled heating, indicating a potential injury risk, especially with children present.

incident_description:
Oven never turned off once it reached the set 350 degrees. It continued to increase in temperature.  That is why my brownies, which normally take approximately 30 mins to bake, were burnt severely and smoking heavily in 15 min. 

Apparently the gas shattered when I removed it from the oven because of the temperature change.  WHich means the oven reached temperatures in excess of 500 degrees.  The glass shattering was a very scary experience.  The glass was so hot that it burned the floor and started items smoking in a drawer where the glass landed.  I could barely get the glass out of the drawer in time before it started on fire.  Then the oven would not turn off.  I tried to turn it off , it would not do anything.  The then F1 code started flashing. I tried to turn it off for it to reset like the instructions stated but to no avail.  The coils inside were still glowing red.  The only way to turn the oven off was to unplug it. I plugged the oven back in later to see if it reset per manual.  The coils immediately began to turn red even though the oven was not turned on.  Upon further investigation, I learned that this was a huge problem with this model.  It has led to many fires and the compnay does not stand behind their product.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused burnt food, shattered glass, and nearly started a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her saucepan is unsafe. The saucepan is part of a set of Duncan Hines stainless steel cookware purchased in the 1990's.  The consumer had boiled potatoes in the saucepan on her stove, removed the pot from the stove and placed it on the counter.  When she again used the handle of the pot to turn the pot without lifting it, the handle came off in her hand.  The screw holding the handle had completely rusted through.  She inspected her other Duncan Hines cookware and found all of the screws to be rusty.

The consumer contacted the manufacturer via email on November 2nd. The firm responded on November 3rd and asked that the consumer send the unit to the firm so that it could be inspected.  They indicated that they would repair or replace units according to the warranty and that she should include a check or money order to cover shipping and handling.

The consumer responded to the firm on November 4th since she felt that the firm did not address her safety concern.  In their subsequent response, they described the problem as being that the handles became brittle with age, misunderstanding her concern. After she wrote again, the firm responded back to her on November 6th stating that in order to further investigate the matter, they would need to see the item in question, including the handle, screw, washer, and protector.

The consumer has not contacted the retailer and the consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. The consumer stated this incident caused no property damage. The consumer's husband fixed the saucepan on his own and has not sent the saucepan back to the firm. The consumer found similar complaints online.
justification: The handle came off but no injury or property damage occurred, fitting the criteria for an incident without injury.

incident_description:
While baking a cake in the oven at 350 degrees for 40 minutes she heard an explosion in the oven. She powered the oven in the off position and  looked through the glass of the oven and noticed that the glass baking dish had exploded.

The ingredients that were placed inside of the baking dish were mostly at room temperature and it was her first time using this dish.

On 12/26/2011 While cleaning up the glass pieces she noticed that the inner piece of glass shattered into a million little pieces while the sides shattered into large pieces. 

She discarded of the baking dish and does not plan on contacting the firm.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of a glass baking dish but no injuries were reported, making it an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it was the first time using the dish and no prior issues were mentioned.

incident_description: Whirlpool Dishwasher Model #GU2500XTPS3 just caught on fire.  Filled the house with smoke. Dishwasher was midway through the wash cycle made a loud buzzing noise followed by black smoke pouring out of the top of the dishwasher where the electronic controls are.  Had to unplug the unit to get it to stop running.  Good thing we were home when it happened could have burned the house down.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and filled the house with smoke, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Dishwasher was set for delayed start in night.  Was awoken to the smell of burning electrical.  Found dishwasher running but without any of the panel indicator lights illuminated.  Opened dishwasher door to investigate but the machine continued to run.  Finally terminated operation by switching off breaker.  Strong buned electrical odor from machine.  Next morning investigated and found control panel inside door charred and nearly burned through in several locations.  Wiring harness also burned through in two locations and several plastic parts melted.  If I had not awoken or if we had not been home this could have caused a house fire.
justification: The incident involved significant electrical damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My kitchenaid dishwasher model KUDS01DJSPO serial number FK3901087 purchased 2001 started sparking with flames shooting out of the top of the unit near the control panel.  It happened in the middle of a cycle.  I extinguished the flames and shutoff the circuit breaker and called 911.  The fire department responded and checked and made sure there were no hotspots in back of the unit or in the surrounding wooden cabinets.  We later disconnected the unit, removed it and stored it in the garage with no intention of using it again.
justification: The incident involved flames and required fire department response, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
My Sears Kenmore dishwasher control board melted.

Sears Kenmore model 655.16362300 serial number FP4506316. The part that caught fire has a sticker stating Whirlpool P/N 8539379 REL

Incident:
We came home to find our kitchen filled with smoke. We found the dishwasher was the cause and that the control board within the door behind the control panel buttons had burnt. 

The plastic casing around the control board had started to burn and melt as well. There is a hole burnt through it.

Our primary concern is the fire hazard and smoke damage. We were lucky the fire didn't continue to burn and catch into our kitchen cupboards. The fumes from the burning circuit board and plastic casing seem toxic. This happened yesterday and the smell in our house is still bothering us. 

I have taken several pictures of the control board. It would appear that either poorly soldered connections on the circuit board or an under sized conductor caused the circuit board to overheat and burn.

This does not appear to be an isolated incident.

I found another report on saferproducts.gov involving the same part that is in my product that had the same failure. Look up report number 20110625-B6466-2147477854

I found many other reports here http://www.kitchenaidfire.com/
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and toxic fumes, posing a risk of injury, and similar incidents have been reported, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
In the evening of November 12 we noticed that back left burner was cycling on full power for 1-3 seconds, off for 1-2 minutes and on full power again. All of the control knobs on the range were in the off position at the time and the range was not used for at least 3 hours. The back left burner was not used for at least a week before we noticed that it was powering on by itself. We tried to switch the back left burner off using the knob, but it did not work. We pulled the range from the wall and unplugged it. When we plugged it in the back left burner started cycling on full power for 1-3 seconds, off for 1-2 minutes and on again. We unplugged the range and plugged it in again and at this time the back left burner stopped cycling. 

At the time we did not know about the recall due to fire hazard of 4 other models that similar to our range started with 790 number. We thought if we would not use the back left burner it would not be cycling in the future. We were wrong. We never used the back left burner since we noticed its malfunctioning, but between November 12 2011 and January 24 2012 we observed the cycling of the back left burner on at least ten different days. Several times we were able to switch the cycling off by using the knob, other times we simply let it cycling and in an hour or so it would stop cycling by itself. We do not know what forces the back left burner to start cycling because it does it on its own schedule and we do not know when it will start cycling again. On January 23 2012 I lightly touched the glass over the back left burner to check if it was warm and has been cycling recently. The surface was cold but when I  touched the glass the back left burner immediately started cycling. On January 24 2012 when I gently moved the range from the wall to unplug it the back left burner started cycling again, although all of the control knobs on the range were in the off position and the range was not used for at least 24 hours. The range is currently unplugged and I hesitate to use it.

Sears was contacted twice and in both cases they told me that we have to pay full price for the repairs. The second time they actually offered 50% discount on the repairman visit ($65 instead of $129) but we still would have to pay for the cost of all parts needed for the repair.

I did the research online and found out that 4 different models that started with 790 number were recalled due to the fire hazard (790.99012, 790.99013, 790.99014, 790.99019), but Sears America informed me that our model that also starts with 790 is not a fire hazard (or at least is not on the recall list). In April of 2011 Sears Canada announced that it will perform a free diagnostic inspection of its customersÃÂ smooth-top or coil element electric range by one of Sears CanadaÃÂs trained technicians for any customer that contacts Sears experiencing similar issues to those indicated in the August 2009 and October 2010 safety notices but whose range model and serial number are not included in these previous recalls, to verify whether the range is functioning properly. Obviously Sears America is convinced that it has not to do this for ranges that were made on the same factories, at the same days with the same parts that Sears Canada considers are in need of free diagnostic inspection.

We are not interested in paying for the repairs since all of the burners in our range probably have the same defective parts that regulate switching on and off and without a diagnostic inspection we canÃÂt be sure that the other three burners will not start similar cycling in the nearest future.  We are planning to replace the range within the next 1-2 weeks.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that cycles on and off unpredictably, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage has occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he is having similar problems with his electric range as Release # 09-333.
He discovered that the right front dual element had came on spontaneously by itself and he was unable to power it off using the control panel, he immediately unplugged it to prevent a house fire.  He was not sure how long it was on for but the element was extremely hot. This was the first incident.

1/9/12  Consumer contacted the retailer and was advised that his model number was not part of the recall and he should contact the agency.

Consumer is concerned that this range is a fire hazard and should be included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as it was the first incident and the consumer took immediate action.

incident_description:
While baking cookies in the oven at 350 degrees for 12 minutes per cookie sheet, the glass door shattered. This is the third instance when the glass door has either shattered or exploded with the consumer standing nearby. The door had shattered before in 11/2009 and 11/2010, and the door was replaced by Sears.  Consumer was told by Sears that they would replace the glass door, not able to replace wall oven. During each of these incidents the oven door handle was loose. This time one side of handle swung loose as the consumer was about to open the oven. Consumer turned off oven, proceeded to open oven when the glass door shattered.

This most recent time, Consumer declined to have repair to the oven glass door as feels it's unsafe. Sears informed consumer that only repair to the glass door of the wall oven was all they could do and could not give the consumer a new door for this unit.
justification: The glass door shattered multiple times with the consumer nearby, but no injury was reported. The repeated incidents and the consumer's proximity suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
While pressing the bake button to power the oven in the on position a plastic piece that snapped into the control panel popped out exposing wires and started to spark. She attempted to power the oven and the cook top in the on position but there is no power to the appliance. 

The oven was pulled out from the wall and then unplugged from the outlet. The firm was contacted on or around on 12/14/2011 and the consumer was advised that there was no longer a warranty on the appliance and if any repairs were going to be made she will have to pay out of pocket. 

No repairs have been made currently to this date and the appliance is still  unplugged from the wall outlet. She indicated that there were no injuries but could have possibly been a  fire. 

The range was purchased by the builder of the home so she does not have that information. She has been in the home for approxiamelty three years.
justification: The incident involved a sparking oven with no injuries reported, but a potential fire hazard was identified.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his electric range with a smooth top surface is a potential fire hazard. . The consumer had his oven to preheat at 350 degrees. The consumer stated within a few seconds there was flames in his oven. The consumer shut off the oven and the flames subsided. The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer stated that there was no property damage. 

The consumer explained that the product is not usable unless repaired. The consumer suspects the heating element is the cause and is broken in two pieces. The consumer has not had any  problems with the range in the past. The consumer did not contact the fire department or his home insurance company. 

The consumer stated that his model is very similar to the models recalled in release 09-333. The consumer has yet to contact the retailer. The consumer called the firm today and advised him that they can  refer him to a service technician who can fix the range at his expense.
justification: The incident involved flames in the oven but no injuries or property damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the consumer's suspicion of a broken heating element and similarity to recalled models.

incident_description:
On 12/31/2011 while heating up some soup on a 1 minute &  30 seconds  when smoke came pouring from the top of the microwave and all power was lost to the appliance and the consumer also powered the circuit breaker in the off position.


The retailer was on contacted the same date and was advised that they would send out a technician to make the repairs. He contacted the firm and was advised to contact a third party service technician  but the company was located in another state. 

Three weeks after the purchase of the microwave in 10/2010 the same incident occurred with the microwave and the retailer replaced it. In 10/2011 the incident occurred again and the part that was the failure was replaced (part is unknown).

There have currently been no repairs to the appliance and the consumer has also reported the retailer to the BBB because of their failure to offer assistance. The circuit breaker is currently powered in the off position.
justification: The incident involved smoke and power loss but no injury, and it has occurred multiple times with the same appliance.

incident_description:
When attempting to power the oven on  in bake it started to pop and there were sparks comming fromt he control panel. The heating element int he oven does not work. There is still power to the cook top but the control panel to the oven does not work.

The firm was contacted on 1/2/2012 and the consumer advised the consumer that there was not a recall on the oven and his model number was affected by the recall for the cook top (see Release #09-333).

The consumer then contacted the retailer that the range was purchased from  and was advised that they could make the repairs. No final decisions have been made if he is considering making any repairs to the unit as far as the recall is concerned or the oven. 

The range is currently in unplugged from the wall putlet and has not been used since the failure occurred.
justification: The incident involved sparks and malfunctioning control panel, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his coffee pot was making a popping noise while operating it. The consumer was operating the coffeemaker for a couple hours before it began to smoke. He did not see a fire but it did smoke and he did have cause for concern if in the event he was not home to turn off the coffee pot. The consumer stated that the coffee pot does not appear damaged and has not damaged his home. 

The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident and was not injured. The consumer called the firm today on and was informed his product was not on recall. The consumer saw numerous reports online of consumerÃÂs having the same concerns. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The consumer stated that the panel coffee is  not digital.
justification: The coffee pot smoked but did not cause injury or damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar concerns.

incident_description:
Friday morning, December 23,2011, my wife got up at 6:00 am and went downstairs and started a pot of coffee, while I slept in for 15 more minutes.The coffee . had just finished brewing, as I prepared to take out the garbage and get the mornlng paper. I was exiting the kitchen door to go outside, when I smelled an electrical burning odor. I went to investigate, first checking the coffeemaker, then the basement and the rooms on the first floor.This took about 30 to 40 seconds. Finding nothing, I returned to the kitchen and I noticed thick blackish/grey smoke rolling out of the coffeemaker, near the warming plate or the underside of the unit. I unplugged the cord, noting that it was cool to touch. I took the unit outside and put it on the porch. On December 26,2011 I calleed the cousinart toll free number and talked to REDACTED, to
report the incident. I was able to get the serial number and the model number that was molded onto the plastic bottom of the unit so she could record that information I explained to her what had happened and that the unit was about 10 months old. She said that based on the serial number, that was correct. She then offered to send me a replacement unit. I informed her that I had already purchased a different model of a cousinart coffeemaker, because I liked their product. I was not after a replacement unit. All I wanted to do was make cousinart aware of the problem, and if I hadn't gotten up when I did, my house may have burned down. She offered me a replacement unit at least two more times, as I was trying to express my concern with the potential problem with the unit for others using the same unit. Feeling frustrated, I asked to speak to her supervisor. she put me on hold and after four or five minutes, a woman named REDACTED talked with me. I explained the situation to her and she also offered to send a replacement unit, rather than express concern over the incident itself.I explained that I had already replaced the unit, and that I only wanted someone at cousinart to be aware of the problem so they could take action as needed. I then asked to speak with her supervisor. She told me she had no supervisor. I asked to speak to a technition or an engineer, and she told me there was none available. I told her I needed to talk to someone in authority . She put me on hold for awhile, and when she came back on line, she gave me the name and number for REDACTED at REDACTED, who she identified as their REDACTED. I told her thanks, hung up, and called the number. The number rang 30-40 times with no response.  I hung up.
justification: The incident involved a coffeemaker emitting smoke, which could have led to a fire but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description:
On Friday, January 13th, 2:00 AM I was trying to warm 1/2 cup of water in the microwave. The microwave is over the gas cooktop. The cup fell from my hand and 1/2 cup water and the cup fell on the knobs of the gas cook top.

As soon as the water fell on the gas cook top, all the ignitors starting clicking at once. I tried to wipe the water on the knobs but flame developed near one of the gas knob.

Normally such spill would start continuous clicking of the igniter.  This time also all ignitors sarted diong clicking.  But, this time it resulted in a flame at one of the knob.  I extinguished the flame and wiped the spilled water.  The clicking of the ignitors stopped.  Next morning, the ignitor did not function to start the gas cook top.  I called GE for repairs and got appointment for the next Wednesday.  However, I cancelled the GE repair appointment as I am not sure this is a safe design by GE.  Now, I start the gas cook top using match stick.

Please investigate and let me know your findings.  Have you received similar complaints about GE gas cook top from others also?  Do you have authority to force GE to investigate this particular incident and improve the safety of the gas cook top.  I am concerned that the automatic ignitor may result in fire similar to one described above and cause major damage including death.
justification: The incident resulted in a flame but was quickly extinguished without injury, and the issue was reported for investigation.

incident_description: Last night, I turned my Kenmore stove on.  About ten minutes later, loud bang, then the heating element caught on fire.  The fire department came immediately and turned off the circuit breaker.  Searching on the web, I see this has happened to hundreds of people with their Kenmore stoves.  Something needs to be done about this. Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death, and similar incidents have been reported by hundreds of users, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
On the 12/27/2011 the consumer 47 year old  set up the soda machine placed a heavy plastic bottle screwed into the machine and press the button 3 times to start the soda process.  The consumer noticed that nothing happened then the consumer pressed the button another four times still the machine is not working.  

The consumer unscrewed the bottle slowly to figure out what might had happened, and while the consumer was unscrewed it; the plastic bottle exploded and the plastic shatter 20 ft  away all over the kitchen  and the consumer got four deep  laceration on her stomach two cuts on her right hand and her right palm is still swollen and blue.   The consumerÃÂs son took her to the close hospital.  ER bandaged her gave some pain killer and sent her home.

The consumer feels that the soda machine could pose a laceration hazard.
justification: The consumer suffered multiple deep lacerations and required hospital treatment, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the described incident.

incident_description: IsaBlender became engaged by plugging in to electricity.  Unit should only become engaged when cup is engaged and twisted to turn on unit.  I contacted Isagenix and was told it was not under warranty.  My concern is I cut my finger (mild) when I plugged in the unit due to spinning base.  I was not happy with the lack of concern from the Isagenix customer service agent.  This is potentially a very hazardous problem.
justification: The incident resulted in a mild injury (cut finger) due to the blender spinning unexpectedly, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the potential hazard described.

incident_description:
On January 24, 2012 at approximately 1:12am, the KitchenAid Dishwasher completed a cleaning cycle and had just completed filling the dishwasher for another wash or rinse cycle. Initially it appeared as normal steam that emanates from the unit as it dries dishes.  The control panel displayed no indicators normally illuminated.  Without any additional indication, the smoke thickened and filled the kitchen and soon thereafter the entire house filled with smoke.  TR was awakened at 1:18am by LS.  TR manually tripped the circuit breaker at the house's electrical panel, and the smoke slowly halted its escape from the dishwasher.  

The unit was opened on January 25 to determine the source of the smoke before attempting to restart operations.  The control board appears to have burned through its connectors, so no restart was attempted.  The unit is presumed to be non-functional.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission without injury, and the dishwasher was rendered non-functional.

incident_description: I started my dishwasher to run for the evening, when I selected the wash cycle, flames shot out of the top of the dishwasher from behind the control panel.  I immediately went to turn off the electrical breaker and the flames went out, and there was smoke.  We waited a few minutes to make sure the fire was completely out and then un-plugged the dishwasher.  We are very lucky that we were home at the time of the fire, and there wasn't much damage to our home.  I happened to be in the same room and was able to react quickly.  Normally I turn on my dishwasher when I leave for work in the mornings, had I done this that day, our home might have burned to the ground. We live in a rural area, so it takes the volunteer fire department a long time to respond.
justification: Flames and smoke occurred, but no injury or death was reported, and damage was minimal due to quick action.

incident_description:
In the early am of 12/3/2011 he woke up thick  gray smoke was coming from the back of the of the refrigerator  and he immediately unplugged it from the wall outlet and removed the back cover.

The relay that was connected to the compressor  was completely melted open causing the wirers to be exposed. He removed all of the food products from the refrigerator and placed them in another unit in the home. He did some research online and noticed that there was a recall (see Release #09-145 where the hazard was with an electrical failure in the relay, the component that turns on the refrigeratorÃÂs compressor, can cause overheating and pose a serious fire hazard. 

 He contacted the firm on 12/3/2011 and they were not open so he did a follow up on 12/5/2011.The representative that he spoke with  (name was not provided) advised him that his unit was not affected by the recall (see Release #09-145) but they allowed him to purchase an extended warranty and a schedule a service technician on 12/7/2011.

The consumer indicated that he is glad that he was home when the failure occurred cause it could have possibly been a fire with the unit.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard due to a melted relay in the refrigerator, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Our Kenmore microwave continues to run when the door is open.  This caused me to burn my hand when reaching in to retrieve a hot dish.  It continues to function in all settings except when the door is open it runs until you close it and set it for what you want to cook..... I believe the fact that the turn table and unit runs when the door is open is a definite safety hazard.  Because the oven is 15 months old Sear's refused to even look at it.  They  tell us that it would cost more to repair than replace.  However I  am concerned that someone else may get more seriously burned from this type of malfunction.
justification: The microwave running with the door open caused a burn injury, and the issue is likely to recur given the malfunction persists.

incident_description: I have had a Kenmore Electric range # 790.94339700 since 10/03/2007. several times I burnt food while cooking because the left front burner stayed at Hi temp after I had turned it down.  I was always able to turn it on and back off to get it to turn off.  Today, 1/25/2012, I was cooking and turned off the burner.  Thank goodness I had not left the kitchen as the meal burnt, I tried to turn it off, and after several attempts, I had to pull the stove out from the wall and unplug the range.  This is extremely dangerous.  I noticed that you have a recall on similar ranges, but not this serial number.  Please add it to the recall.
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with the stove burner not turning off, leading to burnt food but no injury or death.

incident_description: On Tuesday, January 24, 2012 I went to my kitchen to get a cup of water before going to sleep and I noticed my wife standing in front of the Frigidaire Electric Range Model FEF356GBA. I walked towards her and she asked me if I could hear "that" noise. I approached and started listening and it was like an electric noise, like some kind of short circuit noise. While we were looking smoke start to emanate from the back of the range! I immediately pull the range out from the counter and unplug it. I go get my tools and remove the range's back panel to see if I could see what the problem was. I noticed that the connection to the oven's light bulb had burn marks on it! So I decided to remove the electric cables connected to the light bulb and applied black electric tape to the metallic connectors to isolate them. Whew! If my wife hadn't noticed that sound, that was for sure a FIRE in the middle of a WINTER night! Not fun at all. I called Frigidaire just before posting this and they simply opened an account for me and treated it as what it seemed like business as usual. Their representative simply told me that there were no recalls on that range and I told her that in such a case they should immediately start considering doing one because when a fire can result from a problem with an appliance that is no joke and people's lives are in danger.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard from an electric range, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her over the range microwave is a hazard as the consumer witnessed the glass door explode from her microwave oven. The consumer stated that the oven was off at the time of the incident. The consumer was cooking on her electric range top and was baking a turkey in the oven when the glass from the microwave shattered. The consumer feels that the collective heat from the range and oven caused the microwave door to shatter.  The consumer  The consumer called the retailer on Monday December 19, 2011.  

The consumer was told by the retailer that the microwave was out of stock and could not help her. The consumer called the firm on the same day and they only offered her places to purchase a new glass for the microwave and persons to install it. The consumer stated that the microwave does not have any melting or burning. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident or her home insurance. The consumer stated that her house was not damaged and no one was injured. The consumer has not experienced problems with the microwave prior.
justification: The microwave door shattered but no one was injured and there was no property damage, indicating a minor incident.

incident_description:
I bought the West Bend AIR CRAZY Hot Air Popcorn Popper and turned it on for the first time for about 5 seconds when it started smoking so I turned it off and reread the instructions, which say that the first time you turn it on, "...A small amount of smoke and/or odor may occur..." I decided to try turning it on again and maybe the smoke would go away but this time it started smoking
heavily so I unplugged it and ran to put it outside where I then noticed it was on fire, so I filled a pan with water and poured it on the popper to put out the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Our oven that we purchased in April 2003 when turned on will not shut off. One night after cooking dinner we found the oven off but heating to over 500 degrees. We called frigidaire and they told me that they have not have had any problems like this. After further research I found multiple other complaints with the same oven. This problem has happened multiple times since and am very concerned for the well being of my family. The model # is PLEF398CCB and serial #  is vf31337398. Please help
justification: The oven malfunction poses a safety hazard but no injury has been reported yet; the issue has occurred multiple times, indicating it is likely to happen again.

incident_description: The consumer purchased a new microwave oven just over 3 years ago.  It has been subject to normal household use since that time. The door hinges have come off the frame and now do not hold the door closed properly.  The consumer paid to have an authorized service man come and repair this.  He informed that the problem could not be fixed because the hinges were welded to the frame and the weld failed. There may be a safety issue with this problem.  The ownerÃÂs manual has all kinds of warnings about not running the unit with the door open.  The door does shut with this problem and the unit will operate.  But it is not as tight as before.  The greater risk is that the door will fall off altogether when the door is opened.  The unit is installed over the range.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning microwave door that could pose a safety risk if the door falls off, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The consumer says the unit was on for about and hour when the unit started spitting and sparking.  She says smoke went over the place.  She immediately unplugged it and it turned off.  the consumer contacted the manufacturer who have never heard anything about it but will send them a new one.  She says their are many complaints about this item online.  She is wondering if the manufacturer is sending her parts or an entire new unit.
justification: The unit sparked and produced smoke, but no injury was reported. The incident was resolved by unplugging the unit.

incident_description:
The consumer said that her dishwasherÃÂs heating element turned on spontaneously without being switched on.  The consumer said that she set her dishes to the normal cycle without the heating dry element selected, because she did not want to ruin or melt her plastic dishes.  

Consumer called and explained incident to mfrÃÂs rep. (name unknown) who said that the product was no longer under warranty.  The rep. said that they could send out a technician but consumer would have pay for it.

Consumer feels that the heating element spontaneously switched on without being turned on and that this can pose a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating element that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: I have a kenmore smooth top stove. The stove will not cut off at time I have to unplug it then plug it back up sometimes that work and other times it doesn't. The next thing I will do is keep turning the on and off knob until  the light go off.
justification: The stove malfunction poses a potential hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I had just returned home from my sisters house, with a square, glass, Anchor Hocking baking dish in my car that she had just returned to me.  When I parked my car in my garage, I reached over to the passenger seat to pick up the glass dish and as I picked it up, it literally exploded in my hand.  All I did was pick it up!  Glass shot all through my car.  I had picked up the dish with my right hand but have small cuts and scratches on my left hand from glass shooting all through my car.  I had glass in my hair, stuck to my clothes, down the front of my shirt, in my shoes, it was everywhere.  I had my 3 year old niece in the back seat.  We are both very lucky that none of it got into our eyes and that none of the larger very sharp, pointy pieces hit us.  I have vacuumed my car out several times but am still finding small shards of glass.   After researching this issue online, I see that I am definitely not the first person this has happened to and am wondering why there is no recall on this product.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts and scratches, indicating an injury (severity 3), but the likelihood is unlikely (2) as it's a rare occurrence despite multiple reports.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the oven was in use for approximately 20 mins, she noticed smoke emitting from the door of the oven, the unit was powered off, the content she was baking was removed from the oven, but there were flames erupting inside, a fire extinquisher was used to contain the flames.  The fire dept was called in and the oven was removed and placed outside.  Fire started from underneath the oven.

Consumer stated that where the oven was located had burnt marks and there was soot on other areas of the kitchen and adjoining areas.

1/3/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that they could not evaluate the oven because it was not hooked up.  She was informed that the oven might have been made in 1993.

Consumer feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The oven's age suggests this is an unlikely but possible occurrence.

incident_description: On January 13, 2012, the Whirlpool Dishwasher (Model GU2400XTPS1; Serial # FR4515019) was running.  A large pop and flash was seen coming from the kitchen and when investigated, dark black smoke was pouring out of the control panel.  Power was cut to the unit and the fire stopped.  After the unit cooled, the unit was removed.  The control panel caught fire.  I contacted Whirlpool and reported the incident.  They sent an independent technician to review the unit.  He determined that the control panel had caught fire and the initiation point was the P7 connector.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher's control panel, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
My wife reached inside the oven to clean some grease before she turn on the oven her hand 
touched the heating element that when she got the burn,that when she noticed the oven knob turned off and the light come on and off and some time the light stay on without the knob turned on.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from touching a heating element, and the oven's malfunction suggests a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wall oven/microwave combo was smoking profusely after being off for 4 hours. The consumer stated that his home was not damaged and he was not injured. The consumer stated that he had to power off the circuit breaker to make the smoking stop. The consumer was advised by service that the magnetron started without the fan, without being turned on. 

The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident. The consumer stated that the microwave does appear damaged. The consumer called the retailer on December 27th 2011. and was referred to the firm. The firm stated that they will repair the product for the consumer at no expense.  The repairman ordered parts on December 29th. Consumer added: As of 1/12/2012 unit still has NOT been fixed.
justification: The consumer was not injured, but the microwave was damaged, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description:
January 14,2005 while using the bigger of the two ovens and opened the oven door where the gas ball came out and scorched the consumerÃÂs husband. A technician came out to the  home to make the necessary repairs

The technician indicated that the range experienced a delayed ignition causing the fire ball. Her  husband eyebrows were scorched off and it appeared as if he had third degree burns to his face. He did not seek any medical attention

On 11/15/2011 while preheating the oven at 350 degrees within 5 minutes the house filled with gas. The consumer opened the oven door and a fire ball came out at the husband once again. The firm was contacted (exact date was not provided) and she advised the representative that she spoke with (name not provided) that she no longer want the range and that she would like to have someone come pick it up. 

She was offered to have the unit repaired but she declined. She has not used the oven but has used the cook top since the failure occurred. She is currently awaiting to hear a final decision from the firm.

incident_description:

If it is plugged in it turns on without the power being on.

incident_description:

12/29/11 Consumer contacted the retailer and was advised that a service rep would be sent out.

Consumer feels that this range is a safety hazard especially for children and should be reported.
justification: The range overheats, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
While the dishwasher was in use smoke and sparks started comming out of the control panel. I tried to open the dishwasher and a spark burnt through my shirt sleave and a spark burnt the floor.I turned off the circuit breaker and remover the dishwasher front panel and found an electronic control module was burned up.
If I was not present or sleeping while this happened it would have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke, causing a minor burn injury and potential fire risk, but no severe injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Kenmore smooth cooktop/range burner started changing temperatures on it's own during use. After noticing the problem we discontinued use and used the other burners. On 1/22/2012 the burner in question activated itself to the highest setting without warning, there was a plastic tray on top of the burner that was heated to the point of disfigurement. Upon entering my kitchen, I noticed the "hot" burner warning light was on and tried to rectify the problem. I had to remove the cover of the stove top and physically remove the burner control and seal off the wires. I researched the problem on the internet and came across the "voluntary" recall, in which I realized the problems explained matched mine to the letter but  that the serial numbers included in the recall stopped VERY short of my numbers, by about four hundred thousand. After entering my serial number I was told that my "product is not included in the recall and no further action is required". They could not be further from the truth, this is a very serious problem that could have resulted in the ignition of a fire that could have caused serious bodily harm or death to my family. I feel that they are trying to sweep this problem under the rug and fear there may be others who may not be as lucky as I was in discovering the issue before it was too late.
justification: The burner malfunctioned and heated a plastic tray to disfigurement, posing a fire hazard that could have caused injury. The issue was discovered before serious harm occurred, but the potential for injury was significant.

incident_description: oven would not turn off and heated to an extremely high temperature.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but there is no mention of injury or death, only a potential hazard.

incident_description:
On 12/25/2011, the consumer recently purchased a can opener (Battery operated). The consumer stated that first time use can bound up half way around the can, there is a reverse button on the can but it failed to work, he finally had to cut the can to release it from the can opener then had to pry the remaining piece from the can opener and cutting the palm of his right hand. Remedy at home.

On 12/26/2011, the consumer wife tried to use it the day after and it did the same thing, the consumer had to repeat the release of the can but this time the consumer used a OvGlove to protect his hand, there was still a piece of metal left in the can.

The consumer had not contacted the mfr because he could not found any contact information for this firm.
justification: The consumer suffered a cut to the palm of their right hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The issue occurred twice in two days, indicating a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: Glass food storage container, sitting on a desk and at room temperature, spontaneously exploded sending hundreds of pieces of glass all over the room.  The container was partially filled with food and placed in the refrigerator the night before, it was removed from the fridge and sat on a desk at room temperature for approximately 4 hours before the food was consumed.  Between 5-20 minutes after the food was consumed, the container spontaneously exploded.  It had not been heated up, it was not touched, it had not been dropped - it was just sitting on the desk.
justification: The incident involved a glass container exploding, which could cause injury from flying glass shards, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have a Frigidaire Gallery electric range, model no. GLES388CSA. It was made in June 2003 but wasn't put into service until the end of 2004. I have read about the recall on other models (after this happened). This isn't on the list. I had noticed recently that the right front burner wasn't getting as hot as it was earlier. I don't use the burners that often. Now I have noticed the left front burner isn't getting as hot. I can no longer boil water on either burner. I put spaghetti sauce on the right rear burner. I set the temp at medium. The temperature went all the way to high. I set it at low and it remained on high. I think maybe they should have recalled other models. After reading the horror stories about Frigidaire ranges, I am afraid to use it.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while using the toaster oven to toast bread on medium level for approximately 3 mins, when she returned she noticed smoke emitting from the unit, the toaster had caught the slices of bread on fire.  Her spouse immediately disconnect and remove it outside.

incident_description:
Ge Profile Dishwasher PDW8980N20SS

End of cycle  - dishwasher had shut off and I unloaded clean dishes, reloaded with dirty dinner dishes. Three hours later, I smelled burning food. Dishwasher was super hot to the touch. Opened door, heating element was on. Too hot to touch dishes. Turned breaker off and then on to reset power to dishwasher. Left door open to cool unit down. We were lucky we were still awake!

incident_description:
I purchased a Bosch SHE55M1UC dishwasher at Sears, for which I paid Sears $150 for  a professional installation, which was done on 12/24/2011.

The technician stated that the power cord supplied by Sears for Bosch dishwashers was unsafe, and needed to be replaced by a 14 gauge cord at an additional cost of $45 to me.

He provided a copy of an Email to Sears service providers that discussed the problem, although not the extra $45 charge.  I photocopied and then scanned the letter, which I can provide.

The Sears contact for the safety issue, whose Email was blacked-out but legible in the Email that I copied, appears to be:
[REDACTED]

I contacted Sears installation staff at 1 888 463 7924 and eventually  spoke to a supervisor "(REDACTED]" who did not seem to know anything about the issue, but confirmed that she worked with [REDACTED], and asked for a scan of the above document, which I sent her at c5556ec@searshc.com.

I asked for Sears to confirm in writing that the replacement 14 gauge power cord is safe, and to refund the above charge, and have not yet received a reply.

On 12/26 the service technicians returned to fix an unrelated dishwasher leak involving the same unit, and they mentioned that they had installed four Bosch dishwashers with  replacement power cords that morning.

I asked the lead technician if they had gone back to replace the power cords that they installed before the safety issue was identified, and he said that Sears had not issued a recall and that they had not replaced any cords.

I'm concerned that Sears has potentially installed thousands of Bosch  dishwashers with incorrect or faulty power cords, that may have the potential to cause a fire, but may not be taking steps to correct the problems with previously installed dishwashers.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to faulty power cords, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description: Heating element on dishwasher did not shut off.  Excessive heat caused plastic wear to melt inside of dishwasher.  This has happened 2 times to date
justification: Excessive heat caused damage to the dishwasher but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using a brand new Rubbermaid glass storage bowl to reheat some pea soup that I had made the day before.  It had been refrigerated, not frozen.  I had loosened the lid so it was sitting on top of the bowl, but it was not sealed.  I started heating the soup in two minute increments, stirring and tasting it each time to determine when it was warm enough to eat.  The last time, I heated it for one minute more.  After the microwave beeped, but before I could open the door, the glass bowl exploded.  It literally disintegrated into thousands of tiny shards of glass, and the soup was all over the inside of the microwave.  I was upset because of the loss of the soup and the mess I had to clean up, not to mention the cost of the bowl.  Although I was not injured, I shudder to think what might have happened if the bowl had exploded in my hands, especially the potential burn I might have suffered.  I contacted Customer Support and Rubbermaid but have received no reply.  I have heard of this sort of thing happening and wonder why this product is still on the market.
justification: The incident involved a glass bowl exploding in the microwave, causing a mess but no injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such incidents are known but not common.

incident_description: I received a set of Pyrex Easy Grab Glass bakeware for Christmas. I have some other nice cookware and did not want to ruin it so I made sure to read all of the safety information before using it so I was aware not to do anything that would result in a change rapid change of temperature. I prepared 2 pieces of fully defrosted chicken and preheated my oven to 375F. I gave the oven more than enough time to heat up (it also "beeped" to tell me it was heated after the usual 6 minutes it takes) before I placed my chicken (with a small amount of broth in the bottom as directed by the website) in the oven to cook. After the half hour that the recipe suggested I opened the oven door and using a meat thermometer determined that my chicken needed more time. I closed the oven door and set my timer for another 10 min. About 3 minutes later I heard a loud popping noise and discovered that my glass baking dish had exploded in my oven! Luckily I was not injured but my meal was ruined and there was a very large mess to clean up. The pan exploded into lots of very tiny pieces. I no longer feel safe using my glassware in the oven because of this.
justification: The glass baking dish exploded, causing a mess but no injuries.

incident_description: My brand new Pyrex 9 x 13 glass baking dish exploded in my oven yesterday.   I was baking a potato casserole at 350 for 40 minutes.   Within 10 minutes of it being done, I heard sounds coming from the oven and opened it to see thousands of shards of glass everywhere.    If I had had it in my hands, it would have been disasterous.

incident_description: My GE Profile dishwasher caught fire. The components in the door caused the problem. Luckily I was home when it started smelling & smoking so the only thing damaged was the dishwasher. We didn't have it covered under warranty (it was over 4 years old) & we were told it would be expensive to fix so we just replaced it. I am concerned now though because what we purchased was a [REDACTED] model. From a recent news report I saw, they may have the same problem.

incident_description:
My wife was busy in the kitchen and smelt something burning. She established that the burning smell was coming from the dishwasher so she opened it. She then closed it and tried to restart it. At that point sparks flew from the control panel, so she called me to take a look. I tried restarting it again and  black smoke poured from the control panel.
I removed the screws holding the control panel and noticed that the connectors had melted and the panel had large black mark on it. At that point I searched the internet and found a website, http://www.kitchenaidfire.com/, that listed multiple incidents. I also found report 20111024-62CB9-2147474001 that references this exact model.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from the dishwasher, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: About 11-12 years ago, my dishwasher burst into flames.  I was in the room when it happened.  The dishwasher was running, and there was a quick flash of light. Flames then started shooting out of the vent in the door right above the selector knob.  I quickly unlocked the door, shutting off the dishwasher, and threw a dish towel over the fire putting it out.  There did not appear to be any external damage, so I called a repairman.  He opened things up and the circuit board was scorched and burnt, but all of the surrounding plastic wasn't even melted.  He told me that it was a bad circuit board, this kind of thing was isolated, and if he replaced the circuit board it would not be likely to occur again.  I never run the dishwasher when we're not at home, but it hasn't given any problems since.  I am only reporting this now after recently seeing a CBS news report of the same problem happening today.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, but there was no injury or death, and the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore Oven/Range, purchased from Sears, and have experienced several (at least a dozen) instances of the front left large burner not shutting off after the control switch has been turned to "OFF."  Usually, I have been able to turn the switch back to "ON" and then "OFF" again and the burner shuts off.  However, today, the burner would not shut off regardless of how I turned the switches.  After approximately 20 minutes, the burner finally shut itself off and the stove top has now cooled completely.  I called Sears to inquire as to whether or not my range was included in the recall from 2009, was told that it is not and would have to pay for a service technician to come out, even though I am experiencing the exact same problems that the 2009 recall indicated.  

The Model # is:  790.9612340A
Serial #:  VF72531130

My concern is that this poses a very serious fire risk.  From a cursory search online, I have found several instances of other consumers complaining of the same problem on their ranges with the same model number as mine.
justification: The burner not shutting off poses a fire risk, but no actual fire or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Two days ago, the outer glass door of my oven on my Kenmore Electric Range , and the model number is 790096412400, exploded. The oven was not turned on at the time. Shards of the glass shot across my kitchen. Luckily, the person in the kitchen has only a cut on his hand. The kids and the dog were in the other room. The oven was purchased less then two years ago, in March of 2010. 
Since the incident I have received the run around from Sears and Kenmore.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore Elite dishwasher caught fire on 12/11/2009.  My husband had stopped home in the afternoon and turned it on and left to return to work.  My 14 year old daughter came off the school bus and entered the home to find it filled with gray smoke and horrific odor.  She went next door and got the neighbor who shut off the circuit breaker and opened all the doors and windows.  My husband and I both left work and as we entered the garage you could smell the smoke. This odor lasted for several days.  We had Veitch appliance repair come to our home and they determined that it had caught fire and burned beyond repair.  

We called the Sears store where it was purchased without a response of any concern.  We then went in to the store and asked for the manager.  The most they could do was check if there were any recalls and simply told us no recalls and out of warranty.  I expressed that I was concerned for the safety of others and that this needed to be reported, they would not take any action.  I called Sears again on 11/25/2010 and was transferred to Customer Solutions [REDACTED] and was told I would receive a callback by the end of the business day.  Still waiting.  Called Whirlpool who refused to take a report or talk with me further stating that Sears does not allow them to speak to consumers of Kenmore products made for them by Whirlpool (Sears confirmed ours was made by Whirlpool for Kenmore).  I tried to get a number for the president of Whirlpool and was refused.  Again I voiced my concern that this could happen to others and the outcome could be much worse and wanted to be sure this was taken seriously...they didn't care or even apologize or ask if we were ok.

I saw on the news this past weekend that this has happened all over the country hundreds of times and went online to see what I can do.  I call Sears as it showed in replies on this website.  They only saw where they transferred my call to Customer Solutions on 11/25/2010.  They assured me no recall and offered a $100 credit toward a new purchased and a $65 credit toward a service call.  I told Sears they were more than welcome to send out a repair technician if it would be covered but I am not willing to pay them additional money when I already paid $100 to find out it was not repairable.  They said the report would go to corporate but they keep the information internally and do not report to Consumer Protection.  I find it appalling that Sears takes such a serious situation so lightly.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing significant smoke damage and safety concerns, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Our ~5 year old Kenmore oven model 790 front door glass shattered overnight with no previous damage or warning.  We woke up to see the entire front door shattered with a few pieces of glass on the floor, but mostly intact, indicating it shattered with no impact, but somehow pressure difference or perhaps the metal frame flexing with temperature changes over time weakened it with stress building.

This was a safety concern because if we had children they could have easily gone and found the glass shattered and gotten injured.  

Our dogs were who alerted us as they went and were sniffing the glass shards on the floor.  Thankfully they were not hurt, but this is unacceptable since this is a product defect.
justification: The incident caused a safety concern with no injury, but could have caused injury if children were present.

incident_description: My wife was baking with our Sears Kenmore Electric Range Model #665.95002102 Ser# RM4541940 when it started to heat out of control. Both elements were glowing red hot. My wife was in the immediate area and was able to pull the range out and unplug it. It is certain that further damage would have resulted if my wife had not been able to unplug it when she did. It is not likely that we will repair this unit due to the number of concerns with Kenmore Electric Ranges of this type.

incident_description: This is the fourth time this happened in last four months.  Left front burner heats up high (higher than setting) and element doesn't turn off when knob turned to off position.  This last time my husband was able to get element to turn off after turning knob on and off five or six times.  The previous time this happened to me, 3rd time,  I spent about five minutes trying to turn knob from on to off positions and vice versa.  I even took plastic knob off and tried turning metal post with pliers to no avail.  I finally had to go out to electrical box and turn off electricity to range outlet so no electricity was getting to range/stove.  I had the electricity turned off for four hours because I had to leave house and didn't know whether it would turn on by itself (that hasn't happened yet).  I will be calling Sears now because my hasband saw other ranges (not our model) from Sears having same problems.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that doesn't turn off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore Dishwasher
Model 665.13899K800
Ser. No. FY2612280

On numerous occasions, the heating element used for drying the dishes has turned on spontaneously even though the dishwasher had not been running. The dishwasher would heat up uncontrollably causing the surrounding counter top and cabinets to become very hot. It took my wife about a year to convince me something was wrong because I was convinced she simply wasn't operating the controls properly. After months of observation, we have discovered that whenever the power to the house is interrupted, then restored, this will happen. 

Our city (Plano, TX) has a building code that requires an on/off switch be located on the back splash just above the dishwasher as a safety precaution so that the dishwasher can be turned off quickly at that point instead to having to flip a circuit breaker or unplug the unit. Whenever this switch is accidentally bumped, thus turning the circuit off and on again, the dishwasher's heating element will activate and burn uncontrolled even though the dishwasher has not been activated at its control panel as one might do when starting a load of dishes.

This is a serious fire hazard. We have been fortunate enough to have been at home when this has happened and to have been able to head off any possible fires. I have been reluctant to spend money to have it repaired since I believe the circuit board would simply be replaced with one of the same flawed design. I have recently filed a report with "kitchenaidfire.com" and have joined their class action lawsuit. I have not yet contacted the BBB or written to Sears executives about this problem.
justification: The heating element activates uncontrollably, posing a serious fire hazard, which could lead to injury if not promptly addressed.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore flat top range model #790-96119409.  The large front left burner comes on by itself.  The "element on" indicator does not come on to show that the burner is on but the red light under the dial comes on to indicate that the burner is hot, and it is hot.  When I have tried using that burner, the temperature does not stay consistent with the temperature that is set on the dial.  It either burns at it's highest or at it's very lowest setting. I am unable to use this burner because if I turn it on, there is a chance I won't get it to turn off at all.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the Electric range left front burner automatically came on by itself and could not be turned off, it had to be switched off from the circuit breaker. The circuit breaker was switched back on and the burner powered back on.  

12/26/11 The manufacturer was contacted and a service rep was sent out on 12/27, the faulty burner was replaced.

Consumer is concerned that the other burners might be faulty and there might be a safety hazard.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but was fixed without injury, though the consumer has concerns about potential future hazards.

incident_description:
Mastrad A64601 Top Chips Maker and Slicer Set
We received the microwave chip maker as a holiday gift. New YearÃÂs Eve we tried twice to make sweet potato chips unsuccessfully - the first time 3 minutes cook time recommended by the manufacturer and they were undercooked around the edges. The second try for four minutes and the center was overcooked. Third try with the microwave set at 3:30, I started the microwave and stepped out to the patio to check on my barbecue. Less than two minutes later I returned to find a smoke filled kitchen and a fire in the microwave (with 46 seconds cook time still remaining). Opening the microwave door I found chip maker surface on fire (as in flames) necessitating carrying the burning chip tray across the kitchen and dropping into the kitchen sink using water to extinguish it. There was a 3 x 3 hole burned in it. Thankfully we were able to get the smoke out of the house using a large fan and the microwave was not damaged by the fire. 
 I submitted the incident through the Mastrad customer service website and received no response. This product should be recalled as unsafe for use in American households.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injuries or deaths occurred, only property damage.

incident_description:
