GE Profile PDW7980N15SS
SM827183B
justification: The incident caused injury (burned hand) and property damage (melted cutting boards and spoon), but no death or severe harm occurred.

incident_description: Coffee Makker started smoking real bad and was smoldering - looked and smelt like it was going to catch fire. my wife unplugged the unit and we carried it outside - too us a day to get rid of the smoke in our house.
justification: The coffee maker was smoking and smoldering, but no fire or injury occurred; the incident was contained without harm.

incident_description: The consumer says the porcelain was flaking and rusting in the bottom of the oven.  The retailer referred him to the service dept.  His question was that due to the flaking of the porcelain was it safe to use?  He was told not to use the self clean feature.  The manufacturer also told him that it would be safe to use. A technician was sent out via the manufacturer who said that the bottom of the cabinet has collapsed and its making contact with the heating element.  The manufacturer told him the unit is not repairable.
justification: The incident involved flaking and rusting porcelain with a collapsed cabinet, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible as such defects can occur but are not frequent.

incident_description:
I have a Kitchen Aid dishwasher that I think is 5 years old.  I started a  load yesterday 10 min after it started it started putting out a lot of black smoke and smelling like burning plastic.  I turned the main power off and the smoke stopped.  After it cooled off I took the key pad off to get the stink outside it showed a lot of damage.  I believe if I would not have been home it would have been a big fire.  Looks to me like the plug in connections got loose and heated up.  It is model number 8524569.  This is an unsafe product that will burn someone's house down.

Thank you
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved significant smoke and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
KitchenAid Dishwasher KUDIO1LBS3 control panel (right hand side of panel)) caught fire.
Heavy dark smoke was coming from panel. When I opened the dishwasher door, machine continued to run and flames shot out where the control and inner door met. Machine finally shut down and flames extinquished themselves.
justification: The incident involved a fire and flames, but there was no mention of injury or death, so severity is 2. Dishwasher fires are uncommon, making the likelihood unlikely (2).

incident_description:
WeÃÂve had this stove since 2001 and ignored the faulty oven ignition because after opening the door and letting it ÃÂair outÃÂ so to speak, we wait and later try to light it and it would light. The faulty lighting issue has been happening on and off, starting within the first year of ownership. 
Now that we have our 81 year old mother living with us, we are concerned that she might try to use the oven when we are not home and it might not light, hence causing a potentially serious safety issue.  Now that this web site is available to protect the consumer, we have a way to get our concerns heard and maybe Whirlpool will provide a fix for this defect at no charge to the consumer.
justification: The faulty oven ignition poses a potential safety risk, especially for an elderly person, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The control circuit board in the door of my GE dishwasher caught fire while running.  My model is not listed on any of the previous recalls.  

Model: GLD6760N00SS
Serial Number: AM942608B
justification: The control circuit board caught fire, which is a significant incident but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore glass cook top electric range model 790.96011407 s/n VF7173147, the left front element on two occasions would not turn off or down. I understand that there is a recall on other models, mine is not on the list.
After much research, it appears that the manufacturer has selected a vendor for the element controls that is making a inferior product, and this problem is not isolated to just a few models, but the entire line of glass cook top ranges.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning cooktop element that fails to turn off or down, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: While cooking dinner at my daughter's home, I held a Pyrex 16 oz measuring cup in one hand and filled it with steaming water from a tea kettle. When the cup was nearly full, it shattered in my hand shooting hot water and glass over the counter, food in preparation, and me!
justification: The incident involved hot water and glass shattering, which likely caused injury due to the hot water and glass shards.

incident_description: This is a very toxic product. As instructions said, I plugged it in with 2 cups water, and noticed a strange smell coming from it.  I decided to do this a second time to see if the smell went away..it was stronger and the smell made me dizzy and my lungs are also affected just by the small sniff I took to check it.  20 minutes later I had a headache also and am still dizzy. I am not only concerned for myself, I am concerned for others who may not realize how toxic the substances in this product are. This is extremely dangerous and consumers need to be warned. I bought it at Walmart and have contacted them also.
justification: The user experienced dizziness, lung irritation, and a headache from exposure to the toxic product, indicating injury.

incident_description:
A Bed Bath and Beyond "Bake N Serve",  casserole serving set equipped with a frame with candle holders, set my tablecloth on fire. Within 15 minutes of lighting the candles under the dish, a guest noticed the bottom of the dish was covered in soot and the tablecloth was begining to blacken.  Apparently, since the candles are exposed in  tiny candle holders (a dangerous idea to begin with, I can see that now) they quickly become hot liquid wax under the dish and begin to flare. We were able to douse the fire before the entire tablecloth went up in flames. I returned the item to the local BB&B and explained the incident and my concern about the product being hazardous. They seemed only interested in giving me a refund. This product's performance  may have resulted in a house fire or worse. 

Bed, Bath and Beyond sells several versions of this item, all under their Brand name. The name and UPC for the item I purchased is "Bake N Serve Twin Set" UPC44444468458.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as the incident was likely to occur given the design of the product.

incident_description: I am writing about a Chefmate microwave that seems to have a keypad that shorts out over time. While running the microwave will stop running for a second and then start to run again. The keypad will freeze up and will become unresponsive. Sometimes when you open the microwave the turntable will start turning on its own. I am concerned because others seem to be having the same problem with this model also.
justification: The microwave's malfunctioning keypad and turntable behavior indicate an incident with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The issue is described as recurring and affecting multiple units, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: The glass fronts on our ovens exploded into a million pieces across the room and could very well have blinded someone if they were looking into the oven to check on food (at the very least).
justification: The glass fronts exploded, but no one was injured, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description:
Kenmore refrigerator Model#52602100 Serial# SL1842286 caught fire at the compressor relay overload.  I was lucky to be in the kitchen during the accident, and unplugged the unit.  House was still smoked up pretty bad.  Unit Compressor is EGY 90HLP. Relay is 2212194, or also has numbers 4sp1001.

Called Whirlpool and tried to at least get some kind of reinbursement on the replacement part 8201786, but was turned down.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, causing significant smoke damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I bought a gift set of two specialty travel mugs/flask for tea, four teas and four tins from Teavana (a specialty tea store). It is from the collection INTOTEAS. I followed instructions to make tea such water temperature and steps to follow to use the mug. I added tea leaves to the wire mesh and poured boiling hot water over it and closed the mug by screwing it tight. Then I lifted the mug and tried to remove the upper portion to be able to drink from it and instead of that part opening the entire upper part popped out and boiling hot water poured down my wrist and abdomen resulting in second degree scalding burns.
Product link on Teavana website: http://www.teavana.com/tea-products/tea-gifts/p/intoteas-gift-collection
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it requires specific conditions to fail.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart DC-755 Flavorbrew Thermal 10-cup coffeemaker.  During the brew cycle, it started making a buzzing noise.  After a few minutes, white smoke starting coming out of the base at the back of the coffee maker.  It smelled strongly of burning electronics and so I unplugged it and put it outside until it stopped smoking.  The coffee maker is about 1.8 years old.  I reported the problem to Cuisinart customer service and they were not at all concerned about a potential fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
while doing dishes we noticed a "hot" electrical smell in kitchen. i am a disabled firefighter and investigator so i am quite familiar with this. i narrowed the smell down to the dishwasher. i cut power to the unit immediately. let it cool, pulled it out from under countertop. after a few minutes i restarted the dishwasher to see if this had "reset' or resolved the issue. now about one minute into the cycle, i saw smoke starting to emit from the control panel located at the top right on the front of the dishwasher! 
I immediately killed power again and we have left the machine off now since that event. i called the HOme depot where we purchased the machine a couple years ago, and they siad that they will not service the unit it is out of their warranty. 
I then called the manufacuterer to inform them of this life safety issue. they siad that this appliance is out of their one year warranty and they will not repair or replace this unit!
I was astounded that this machine may be the cause of a fatal fire someday somewhere and they do not care to research this product to see if there is something that they can do!
justification: The incident caused smoke and could have led to a fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: RE: KitchenAid Dishwasher, model#KUDS01DLWH3, serial#FR20003819. Started a "cycle" late in the evening before going to bed. I noticed an odd "hissing" noise emitting from the dishwasher. Suddenly, large amount of smoke were emitted from the top right area of the door/control board area. I immediatley opened the door to stop the cycle. Smoke had filled the kitchen area. Ran to the electrical breaker and cut power. We had family in town for holidays. The smoke and commotion awoke most of our guests. Repairman is due today (1-6-12). Our immediate concerns are, what is to keep this from happening again, once repaired? Is it his an engineering design flaw? We phoned KitchenAid Customer support. They're response was,"we are unaware of any recalls or actions at this time." So, in the meantime, how many more households will trust this appliance, as we did, and go to sleep at night? Or perhaps run some errands after starting their dishwashers? It is very clear to me that this product is unsafe! We were appalled at the lack of concern for the consumers safety. If I had not been standing within close proximity of this event, what could have happened? How do we sleep at night knowing that we have an appliance in our home that could potentially harm us? Most importantly, how do we "get the word out" so that other families are made aware of this hidden hazard? At this time, KitchenAid is not offering any explanations, reccomendations, ( other than for us to call a repairman ), or recall of any kind. Have the "best interests" of the consumer been served? Must we rely on the evening news to give us peace of mind? Our understanding of this ongoing issue, is that it has been happening for some time now, and STILL, no word "at this time," from KitchenAid. Well, it is a sad day indeed, when consumers have a threat like this "dishwasher fire" event, and all you will hear is, "At this time, there is no recall."  Obviously, they can sleep at night. I suspect it is because they do not have this appliance in their homes!
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it appears to be an isolated event with no widespread reports.

incident_description: In September of 2011, I began to smell a burning plastic smell coming from my dishwasher while it was running.  Each time I opened it, the smell went away and I saw nothing on the bottom burning or melting.  December 2, 2011 while a load of dishes were washing, the diswasher shut off and I couldn't get it to turn back on.  It had been reset once before by a technician so I figured it needed to be reset again. As soon as my husband took the inside panel off, he saw that the wires that connect to the circut board were charred and burnt through.  He was very surprised they didn't catch on fire.  I have seen that other Maytag dishwashers have had similar issues and have been recalled.  I feel this model needs to be added as well.  I called and talked to Maytag about the issue and they said there is nothing they can do because we did not by the extended warranty.  The dishwasher was purchased March 2010, so we haven't even had it for 2 years!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with burnt wires but no fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kitchen Aid Superba convection single wall oven November 2010.  On January 12, 2012 I set the self-clean cycle for the first time since purchasing the oven according to the instructions in the manual.  The door automatically locks when the cycle is set and after 20 minutes into the cycle there was a loud explosion, sounded like a bomb went off.  I was washing dishes  across from where my oven is located with my 17mth old daughter beside me.  I turn around to see what happened, only to see shards of glass shooting out of the vents of the oven.  I immediately took my daughter out of harms way and quickly returned to turn the oven off.   There was glass everywhere in the kitchen and scattered all across the family room and the basement stairs.   I was afraid to open the oven door, because soon as the door opened the glass was overwhelmingly going to pour out, and I was afraid that there would be a short circuit or even fire.  I called the fire department and they came out and cut the power to the oven and cleared any risk of fire.  They stated they had not seen anything like this before and recommended I contact the manufacturer.  Broken glass inside the oven had embedded into the walls of the oven from the force of the explosion.  I called kitchen aid the next day, Friday January 13, 2012.  After speaking to the representative I was placed on hold, she returned to tell me that all Kitchen Aid/Whirlpool, could do as a courtesy is to repair my oven free parts and labor.  My one year warranty just expired  two months prior and I explained that this oven was defective and that was my first time using self-clean cycle.  she remained firm, so I asked to speak to a supervisor.  The supervisor apologized that the incident occurred and went on to say that it is the wrong doing of myself and not the oven that the glass shattered.  She said "If there is a scratch on the glass it would shatter due to the high temp. of the cycle".  I told her that there were no scratches on the glass door and she went on to say that "it could have been a hairline fracture that  would not have been visible to the naked eye".  THIS IS NOT A WARNING IN THE MANUAL!  If Kitchen Aid is aware of a risk or that additional precautionary measure be taken, then they certainly donÃÂt disclose that to their consumers.   I explained to her that the oven is obviously defective and that should not have happened and I wanted a refund for my $2000.00 oven.  She said that Kitchen Aid/whirlpool would not exchange or refund the oven, all they could do is repair it.  I am afraid to use this oven again, even after repairs.  I have now found numerous complaints regarding the Kitchen Aid Superba oven glass shattering and exploding while on self-clean cycle.  I do not understand why this product has not been recalled, is Kitchen Aid/Whirlpool waiting for a catastrophic event before they take action?!    For the amount of money spent on this oven I am outraged at the company for their defective product and POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE.  There is currently a class action lawsuit file in the state of New York regarding self-cleaning oven defects, so I cannot understand or accept Kitchen Aid not taking the necessary precautions and issuing a recall on defective ovens.  Maybe Kitchen Aid is waiting to take action when an explosion like this happens to someone standing right by one of their ovens when it explodes.
 
Something has to be done to protect the public from serious damage caused by one of Kitchen AidÃÂs ovens.  I have three young children, I can only say I am thankful nobody was physically injured in my home when the incident occurred, my toddler would not stop crying after this happened and to this day I am still in shock, and i will never use self clean cycle again.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of glass from the oven, but no injuries were reported despite the high risk to the individuals present.

incident_description:
While using my 2 year old Kenmore oven/range, there was a huge spark from the back of the oven which was later identified as total "frying" of the control panel.  In trying to fix the problem, Sears,
who sold me the oven, can not stock the part to fix the control panel and the overlay wiring.  They will not do anything about this problem, except to tell me to wait until March when the production of the control panel will be available.  However, the spark that started this incident was large enough for me to see over the back of the range.  Thankfully, there was not a fire.
justification: The incident involved a significant spark from the oven, but no injury or fire occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the described frequency of such incidents.

incident_description:
On Monday 1/16/12, i was making dinner, baked potatoes in aluminum foil, and  my oven turned onto self cleaning mode after cooking for 30 minutes. It locked down, and caught on fire. We called 911 because our house was filled with smoke, and fire in the oven. The Fire Department instructed us to contact Sears, to report it, and I did. They also instructed me to report this to you as well.                 

Sears Smooth Top Electric Stove 2001 year, model # 665-92014102
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven and smoke filling the house, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

We unplugged it. On the weekend, we unscrewed the panel access to find the control panel completely burned. It burned so hot that it melted the plastic. incident_description:
Saturday night my husband was heating eggrolls in the oven and when he went to put on the timer, the whole pane of glass in the oven exploded out except for an inch around the edges. No piece was bigger than a tiny shard. It exploded so far as to find pieces of glass in 2 other rooms. He did not slam the door or hit it at all. In fact, later I found a website, http://www.selectsmart.com/DISCUSS/read.php?34,601635,page=1

that surprised me by having 6 pages of exploding sears glass on ovens that were just sitting and hadn't been used in days. In almost all the cases, they said Sears told them it never happened before.  I called corporate to have them call quality control and warn them, but they insisted I wanted something more.

Please look into this. If I had a small child in the room, it would have been much worse.
justification: The incident involved an oven glass pane exploding, causing glass shards to spread across multiple rooms, but no injuries were reported. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) based on the description of similar incidents found online.

justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but no injury or death occurred as the electric supply was turned off in time.

incident_description:
For the second time since purchasing the dishwasher in August 2010, the detergent dispenser stopped opening/working in late November 2011.  Previously, in December 2010, a service technician had come out to fix the dispenser for the same reason and found that the wire connection to the dispenser had melted and that the source of the problem was that the control board had overheated due to a wiring issue.  As the dishwasher was still under warranty, he replaced the control board and dispenser with no indication that this could become a repeated issue.  

Dishwasher seemed to work fine for next 10 months.  Then dispenser stopped working again.  Service technician came out today, found the same issue - melted dispenser connection.  He replaced the dispenser and ran the "evaluation" cycle.  When he opened the dishwasher, the smell of burning plastic permeated my house.  He took off the front panel again and upon closer examination, found a blackened & scorched portion of the control board. I still have the damaged - melted and burned - parts.  Offered to replace control board & dispenser yet again, this time at full cost, since warranty now expired on this defective product.  I declined since I am not going to pay to "repair" an obvious fire hazard.

I consider myself very lucky that neither of these led to an actual fire, especially if this second time had gone unnoticed since the burning was immediate this time.  My house still reeks of burned plastic.  And I am out over $500 for a product that worked for about 4 months.
justification: The incident involved a recurring electrical issue in the dishwasher that caused melting and burning, posing a fire hazard but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: We went to bed the night of 12/14/2011 around 11:30 pm, everything was fine.  Around 3 AM that night I woke up and smelled smoke.  I searched the entire house for smoke and found none, however, the smoke smell was very strong in and around our kitchen.  I woke my husband up to have him help me figure out what was going on.  He immediately knew/said that it smelled like an electrical fire. It seemed as though the smell was coming from our refrigerator, so we pulled it away from the wall to investigate further.  After removing the panel/door at the lower bottom, we saw something was burning.  There was a plastic box that held wires to the main motor/compressor unit.  That box was completely charred and melted.  There were also exposed wires and when my husband tried to touch the charred piece, it sparked.  FYI- at this point the fridge was still plugged in and the fridge/freezer were both in working order.  We immediately unplugged it.  There were no injuries and thankfully we were home that night.  Had it happened the following night (when we were out of town) we may not have been so lucky.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire risk with no injuries, but potential for severe damage if unnoticed.

incident_description: Frigidaire Electrolux Free standing range made and electric spark from the control panel and the oven controls went haywire. The oven heat control went up and down by itself and all the buttons including the clock and light controls turned on the oven. This model has been fixed twice by the manufacturer for the controls on the cook top not turning the heating element off. This model has been nothing but problem after problem. Serial No3 VF42434279 Model PLEF398CCD
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven with electrical issues but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
I purchased the Frigidaire Range Mode1 LEEFM389FE, SIN VF8012431R, from the Lowe's Store in Monroe, MI on 2/22/2008 (see attached receipt). The Range functioned with no remarkable incidents until the evening of 11/27/2011. At which time, the Range phantomlike, inexplicably and without warning, had all burners on the top of the Range heated to the highest heat they were capable ofa nd it was as if all burners were on the highest setting possible without human intervention. Just before this happened, I had pulled a tenderloin roast from the oven and it had been placed on the Range Top to tent with aluminum foil covering the roast. When the incident happened, there was no one in the kitchen and we were first made aware of the Range malfunction by the smell of smoke and charred meat. When I arrived, saw the smoke and the Range lit up, I swiped the pan with the roast on to my wooden butcher block next to the Range causing a moderate and very painful bum to my wrist and palm heel of my nand which I continue to treat at home. We attempted to eat the tenderloin roast and although parts of the loin were edible it was way overcooked and quite a bit was burnt beyond being edible and was disposed and a very expensive Sunday dinner for seven people was destroyed.

On the morning of 11/28, through internet research, I determined that the exact model Range was involved in a voluntary Safety Recall. I am highly upset that such a dangerous condition that burned my hand destroyed my dinner and almost burned my family out of the house was only a voluntary recall, leaving me with no notice whatsoever. I intend to petition the UCC to take a better look at this Safety Recall and the dangers involved particularly as these
Ranges are aging and present a greater danger. Obviously, THESE RANGES SHOULD HAVE BEEN RECALLED, BUT PROFIT IS
MORE IMPORTANT THAN SAFElY OR CUSTOMER SERVICE. When I attempted to get the Range repaired, the nightmare
began. The Range, which was cheaply manufactured, had a paper tag with the serial number that had been wiped off and was not legible. Guess what..............you can't get a repair on the stove without the serial number. The Customer Service Department was completely stymied with how to help and a huge snafu, catch 22 got started that is enough to drive anyone crazy and the more you insist to be helped, the more frustrated and rude the Customer Service Representative becomes.

After several hours of being bounced from one person to the next and apparently no one having the authority to offer a remedy, I decided to call you regarding liability. You were able to help generate a serial number and I was able to get the repairs scheduled. But, it was not until 12/5 that the repair technician came to perform the repair. During the repair, the technician determined that the knobs were fused to the stove and had to broken off. He spent many minutes on the line with Customer Service but no one would authorize the knobs to be replaced although, everyone agrees, that they were broken off because of the Range malfunction. The technician could not fix the knobs because Electrolux, Inc would not authorize the charge and my Range remains in a state of disrepair and is an eyesore in my kitchen.
I seek to be made whole for my damages!

Please find attachments to show the purchase of the Range, photos of my injuries which do not seem to depict the severity of the burns accurately and I am still suffering from them. Also, please find the restaurant receipts for meals that were purchased because we could not cook. Please note that we ate a lot of cold cuts and we are only requesting reimbursement for a few meals.

My itemized damages are set forth below:
Tenderloin Roast for 7 people; $ 60.00
Restaurant Meals; $ 86.51
Range Knobs, per Tech; $ 90.00
Burns, pain and suffering; $500.00
Total $736.51
Complaint# [REDACTED]
Policy# [REDACTED]
Model: LEEFM389FE
Serial Number: VF8012431R
Brand Frigidaire
justification: The incident caused a painful burn injury and property damage, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it was linked to a specific recall issue.

incident_description: After making a pot of coffee in the morning, coffee pot had stopped brewing and was in it's typical keep warm setting that is on an automatic timer (about 4 c. left in the pot). Heard popping noises from the room that overlooks the kitchen and smelled a really awful burning smell. Looked to the kitchen and saw it smoking, ran in, and my husband unplugged the pot. It kept smoking and pouring out a really foul, toxic smelling smoke like electrical or plastic fire so I used oven mits to move the unit without the carafe to the backyard where it continued to smoke until it cooled off. Smoke seemed to be coming out of the place where the power cord attaches to the machine in the back.
justification: The incident involved a smoking coffee pot but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the situation was controlled without further escalation.

incident_description: We had just turned on the Cuisinart DCC-2400 coffee maker to brew coffee. It is approximately 2.5 years old. After several minutes, we noticed a burning electronics smell, and observed smoke coming out of the bottom of the coffee maker and a very strong smell. This could have caused a fire had we not been present and thrown the unit outside!!
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Breville Ikon 1.7 electric tea kettle that no longer shuts off after the water boils.  It just keeps boiling.  I feel very lucky that I discovered this before it completely ran dry and started a fire.  

I contacted Breville warranty support and they said they will not send me a replacement kettle because it was manufactured more than 1 year ago.

I can't believe an $80 tea kettle only has a 1 year warranty and that Breville refuses to stand behind their products when a serious safety issue is at stake.  Breville advertises this kettle as shutting off automatically when the water boils.  If it doesn't do that, and people expect it to, serious problems could result.
justification: The kettle's failure to shut off poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred in this case.

incident_description: We had put bread in our toaster to toast, only to come back a few minutes later out of a room upstairs,  to a house filled with black smoke! The toaster did not pop up like it was suppose to and the cancel button didn't even work to stop it when i went running down to see what was going on.  I had to unplug the toaster and force the knob up to stop it from toasting.  The bread was burnt to a charred black little piece of a fire waiting to happen!! I have 2 children under the age of 3 and a puppy and we were all exposed to the terrible strong black smoke.  We live in MN and it is the middle of winter, so it's not like we can just run out of the house or open all the doors and windows and let the house air out for days. It was a very dangerous and scary situation for my family, and left our house smelling of smoke soot for weeks on end.  I contacted Hamilton Beach immediately from the information I had on the bottom of the toaster and they said they would replace it once they received our old one.  It took them 5 weeks to get a new one mailed out to us.  This is a daily appliance we use in our household.  So, today, we finally received the new one via UPS.  We opened it and plugged it in to test it out...the very first time we pushed the handles down in the toasting position, the right one blew out w/a loud sound and sparks.  We tried it a second time, and it did this very same thing again...we immediately unplugged it and will not be using this brand new toaster we were just sent as a replacement. Another very scary incident w/the very same brand of toaster.  We are very very disgusted with hamilton beach and their toaster appliance...not to mention the unfriendly customer service when speaking to them!!!!!!!!!!!
justification: The incident involved exposure to smoke and a malfunctioning appliance, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: While cooking a bowl of soup, microwave hummed loudly, then emitted flames and thick smoke from underneath. This was not the food burning, but something electrical in the unit underside which caught fire. This microwave was well maintained, and used for residential not commercial use.
justification: The microwave emitted flames and smoke due to an electrical issue, posing a fire hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Whirlpool Quiet Partner II Dishwasher Model DUI055XTVQO Serial #FY3459459 had an electtircal short ocurred in the terminal box where the power cord connects to the dishwasher wiring.  The wire connectors melted and the house filled with a burning smell.
justification: The incident involved an electrical short and melting wire connectors, causing a burning smell but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool smooth top stove that's about 5-7 years old, purchased new. Over the last couple years it has developed a problem where the burners, if turned on to a setting, do not regulate the temperature, instead they stay on at full power. This happens intermittently and unexpectedly. For example, place a pot on the burner at medium heat, it heats up, and begins regulating, then for no reason fails to regulate, instead continuing to heat at full power. we ruined several expensive pots and burned a number of meals. Obviously, if a cooking pot or pan was left unattended for any extended period of time, it has the potential to cause a fire or severe burns. 

The Model # is RF368LXMQ ; the Serial number is: RP3311802
justification: The stove's failure to regulate temperature has caused property damage (ruined pots) and could lead to burns or fire if left unattended, but no injuries are reported.

incident_description: I was preparing a honey mustard pork tenderloin in an anchor hocking square glass baking dish. It was the first time I had used it. It was clean and dry. I was cooking the dish in a preheated 375 degree oven. after the dish had been in the oven for approximately 20 minutes, I heard a very loud noise. When I looked into the oven, the dish had exploded and various sizes of glass were all over the oven. Needless to say, I am concerned about using the other larger dish that I own. It was a set that came with plastic lids and a carrying case for the 9 x 13 dish. I have other glass cookware and have used them successfully, but this is the first of this kind that I have used. After spending hours cleaning my oven, I think I will stick with the others. I am just thankful that none of my family had opened the oven door to check on dinner at that time!
justification: The glass dish exploded but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: a childs disney cup exploded where the water globe was after removing it from the microwave. the rest of the cup was in original condition after the damage. the fluid gave my 5 yr old daughter burns on her tummy including blistering. i have had this cup for over a yr, and have microwaved it often. there are very tiny, written in clear, pictures on the bottom of the cup...not sure what they mean.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and blistering to a child, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of frequent microwave use without prior incidents.

incident_description:
While boiling 8 ounces of water in the stainless steel tea kettle on a gas range  until it whisteled.  She noticed that the plastic handle that  also attaches to the spout had melted and liquefied at the spout. 

She returned the tea kettle to the retailer and informed them of the concerns that she had with the product. 

No further information was provided.
justification: The incident involved a melted plastic handle but no injury or harm occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the product defect but no widespread reports.

incident_description:
Each time I've tried to make toast with my new Black & Decker toaster oven  (received for an Xmas present 12/25/2011) the toast burned, but the toast actually caught fire three of those times.  The last time I tried,  (01/15/2012), I had to use a fire extinguisher to prevent my security alarm smoke detector from automatically calling the local fire department.  The toaster oven burned up and the bottom tray had started to melt.  Luckily there was no damage to my counter top.

I must admit I was chagrinned when I  unpacked the product and saw the instructions printed on the front glass:  "In the event of food flare, keep door closed and unplug power cord."

The first time the toast caught fire I had left the kitchen area briefly to check on my 22-month-oldgrandaughte who was visiting with me.  I had to call the alarm company to cancel the smoke alarm and open al the windows (it was<50 degrees Fahrenheit outside.)

After this first incident I never left the oven unattended, but I couldn't make toast.  I had had a
B & D toaster over for more than 18 years and never had a problem.  It finally wore out so I asked for a new one for Christmas.  The new model has been redesigned to make it a counter top oven.  The knobs have no directional indicators, so you can't readily see if they've been tampered with since the last time you set up the toaster oven to "just toast."  

I called the B & D help number and am still waiting to hear back from them.  I really feel this appliance needs to be recalled for poor product design.  I am in the process of giving B & D actual and constructive notice about this situation so they cannot deny the fact that they have been alerted!

How did this product get past the usual safety inspectors?
justification: The toaster oven caused multiple fires, requiring a fire extinguisher and smoke alarm intervention, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Frigidaire oven range model # FEFL77ABE
and Serial # VF21830395. It was purchased and installed in my home in the summer of 2002. On January 11, 2012 I was baking a pie in the oven. The oven was on 380 degrees. It was in the oven for about 35 minutes. When I opened the oven to check it a blast of heat hit me and I knew something was wrong. The pie was blackened on the top. I immedieatly removed the pie. I had to use tongs to set my trutemp oven temperature device in the oven. It maxed out at 600 degrees!! I f I had not been upstairs keeping an eye on my pie my whole house would've burned down! This model is a fire hazard! When I called the company they refused to help me in any way and they refused to recall it! When I called the recall department they also refused any assistance and they  refused to recall the oven! This model could cause serious property damage and or serious injury.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that reached dangerously high temperatures, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Cuisinart coffee maker started fire (contained to appliance).
justification: The fire was contained to the appliance, indicating no injury or death, but it was still an incident.

incident_description:
Our dishwasher was serviced last year for the recall for this model.  Last weekend, it erupted with thick, acrid smoke pouring from the door during a wash cycle. A technician opened it to find the so-called "remedy" in place (a temperature sensor), which obviously did not work as designed. The control board was badly burned, as was the wiring harness.

Fortunately I was at home and was able to get to the breaker box to cut the power. My concern is for all the other dishwashers that have been "repaired." In my opinion, this remedy is neither sufficient nor reliable.
justification: The dishwasher emitted thick smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was contained by cutting the power.

incident_description: I was cooking sauage balls in the oven and about 10 min into the cooking time the oven glass burst shattering to the floor.

incident_description:
I have a Bosch dishwasher model SHE56C06UC/22. This week while running the dishwasher I noticed a strong smell of burning wire insulation. The repairman yesterday informed me that there had been a recall of the Bosch dishwashers for that very problem. On checking he found that my dishwasher was not covered as per the serial number, FD8605 00080. Checking the CPSC website I confirmed that the information the repair technician received was correct. 

Obviously the recall did not include all the dishwashers that had the problem. We purchased this dishwasher in November of 2006 according to the appliance store we got the unit from.
justification: The incident involves a strong smell of burning wire insulation, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Fire Hazard on Kitchen Aid Side by Side Refrigerator
Model #KSRK22ILSS13
Serial #SR1040013
Manufacture Date:  03-04

1/15/2012 @ 0200hrs:
Wife woke me up stating that there was a foul smell coming from the living/dining room and kitchen area.  Knew this was electrical smoke and turned off the power from the circuit breaker not know where the possible burning was coming from.  Checked outlets by touch and went up into the attic to check if there was any visible signs and smell of electrical smoke - none.  Wife mentioned that the smell was stronger near the refrigerator and dishwasher.  Pulled the refrigerator from the wall and pinpointed the smell coming from the bottom of the refrigerator.  Original thought was that the motor might be overheating.  Went through the owners manual and read that the condensation coils may need to be cleaned to keep the refrigerator from over running.  Went to bed happy to know where the problem was coming from, and that an emergency phone call was not needed.

1/16/2012 @ 0900hrs:
Opened the bottom rear and started to delicately vacuum the dust.  Opened the front base grill to expose more of the coils and cleaned the built up dust.  Thought I was good to go.  Plugged the refrigerator back in and noticed a very erie orange glow to the left of the black roundish tank (the compressor?), quickly followed with fire - all happening within seconds from plugging the refrigerator back in.  Quickly unplugged and blew out the flame, knew that this was not right, and researched on the internet to find out that there were many issues similar to this with the Kitchen Aid brand.

I am baffled why the Kitchen Aid brand/model numbers is not part of the expanded recall in 2009.
Found out that the problem is the start relay which I removed and plan on replacing to see if this will fix the problem.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries or deaths, but it required immediate action to prevent potential harm.

incident_description:
Our very first attempt to use the range and oven resulted in a tremendous flood of natural gas into the apartment.  The entire main floor fills with natural gas when we attempted to bake.  And scones which ordinarily take 12 minutes to bake,  took 43 minutes in this oven.  

We asked the apartment complex to investigate and the worker admitted, after considerable discussion, that the oven was not heating correctly and made an adjustment to the temperature control.  The worker told us we didn't understand how gas ranges/ovens operate and that we needed to allow it to "cycle five times while preheating."  I opened the kitchen drawer to pull out the operator's manuel, which the worker took from me and tucked in his pocket, saying we were not allowed to have the manuel.  

However, after one month later, I was constantly experiencing headaches whenever we baked.  I was coughing whenever on the main and lower floors.  My teen was experiencing constant coughing which sounded more like croup, and asthma attacks at night, although she had never experienced asthma or croup ever before.  

I sleep on the main floor and have been waking with swollen eyes and a puffy face, not feeling well.  Finally, when trying to cook cookies, my teen and my older daughter demanded we call NW Natural Gas because the smell of gas in the room was overwhelming.  I looked up the Kenmore 30-inch free-standing range and over on this website.  I found the report about a similar kenmore range with similar parts and similar problems, recall # 10-048.  So I called the gas company who sent a technician.  He confirmed the oven was not operating properly and that the amount of gas coming out of the appliance was outrageous.  He shut it off and wrote a ticket declaring it be repaired or replaced.
justification: The incident caused health issues (headaches, coughing, asthma attacks) due to gas exposure, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description:
Prepared a roast of beef, placed in glass baking ware  and put it in the oven. 
When I opened the oven door to check on the roast, about half hour later, I found the glass pan had shattered and broken pieces of glass were all over the oven floor and racks!!!
justification: The glass pan shattered, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: Stainless steel disc covering the aluminum disc fused to the bottom of a nonstick stainless steel Ultrex frying pan I bought on the shopping channel fell off while I was cooking with the pan. It states 18/10 stainless steel, Inova, Inc., Davenport, IA, Made in Korea

incident_description: KENMORE RANGE MODEL 790.96009600 - For the third time (new unit) Sears has replaced the upper unit for turn off/on - they will STAY ON - OVER HEAT and the only OFF is throw the circuit breaker - they say it happens all the time - Yesterday the baking rod internal melted due to trying to clean the unit (Oven Locks to Clean) - It was not on 5 minutes and the rod smoked and melted.  Sears did not see this as a FIRE SAFETY issue either - cause I turned off the CIRCUIT BREAKER before a fire broke out.  They REFUSED to replace the unit under warranty, but again ordered the repair parts for all 4 upper cooking surfaces and a new rod for the oven.

incident_description: Sears Trio Refridgerator model 795.77729700, serial # 709KR00070 - lights are staying on inside causing housing to get very very hot, burned hand when touching housing, food inside getting warm, chemical/electrical smell inside, after searching online and contacting Sears, it  appears there is already an issue with these refidgerators but apparently mine isn't in the range...I can't use lights inside my $2500.00 fridge, I would like Sears to correct this issue as this seems like a manufacturing defect across the board - I don't need a fire inside my house that I just remodeled and don't want my family placed at harm especially if Sears continued to sell these refridgerators after they knew about these problems

incident_description:

He would like dishwasher recalled and would like repair at manufacturer expense and if repaired before then he would like to be reimbursed.at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved sparks and flames from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Last week, I bought a Black & Decker Convection Toaster Oven, Model No. CT04500S, Type 2. 
Our first use of the product was to toast some breads and that worked ok. Next time, we tried to broil some food. But after a few minutes, with a loud bang, the front glass panel  exploded and showered the kitchen floor with hundreds of small glass shards for upto about 10/12 ft. It was sheer luck that there was no serious injury to anyone because we were about 15/20 ft away from the counter on which the toaster rested. incident_description:

In June I purchased your Toast-R Oven (TRO 490B Type 1) at Wal-Mart.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her niece's daughter got her finger caught in a 2 piece metal baking dish. The child had her finger caught in a hole of the top cover. The consumer stated that the surface is very smooth but the interior is rough. The child got her index finger on her right hand caught. The finger became bruised and the knuckle was bleeding. 

The finger was bleeding but also caught in the hole of the baking dish. The consumer needed to use Vaseline to get the finger out. The consumer called the ambulance and they arrived 10 minutes later. The consumer was able to take the finger out of the before the ambulance arrived. 

The ambulance applied bandages and the child's parents took her to the hospital in the ambulance, where they took x-rays and found no damage the finger. The child given a splint to her single finger for 48 hours. The child's mother has not called the insurance company. The consumer stated that the product was not damaged prior to the incident. The consumer has not called the firm or the retailer. 

The child stayed at the hospital for nearly 2 hours. The hospital is 15 minutes from the place of the incident. The consumer is not sure if there was a follow up exam scheduled but was informed to place ice on the finger daily for two days. The hospital is Richmond University Hospital in Staten Island, NY.  

The Consumer Added:  We have been in contact with Telebrands after we initially contacted CPSC to report our grand niece's incident with Telebrands Bake Pops Product. It is Telebrands belief that we were negligent and should have been able to prevent the incident from occurring. They pointed out that the instructions state that during use ofthis product child
supervision should be employed. Yes, we do Wlderstand that when baking it is important to keep children at a safe distance from any heat. But the product was not being used for its intended purpose at the time ofthe incident, and the oven was not yet turned on. I had just taken the product out ofthe box and placed it on the kitchen table. As I began to read
the instructions my grandniece picked up the Bake Pops pan from the table and that is when the incident occurred. There is no mention or warning ofthe product of itself posing any imminent danger other then when being used for its intended purpose. It is my belief that anyone (child or adult) can injure themselves on the sharp inner portion of the holes. You must be mindful ofthe sharpness of the inner holes while using or cleaning the product, if you aren't there is a chance that you may cause injury to your finger(s).
justification: The child suffered a bruised and bleeding finger requiring hospital treatment, but no permanent damage was found, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Burners wont turn off on Kenmore 79096002601. The burners will switch on to high even when the knob is set to medium and then the burner will not shut off.
I called their help line at 1-800-549-4505. All they could off was to send a technician out for a minimum fee of $150. They have recalled other ranges having this problem but have done nothing in regards to a recall for this model.  This is a fire hazard and could cause serious damage or injury. I can't believe they have not recalled this and are not standing behind this product. I will never purchase a kenmore appliance ever again.
justification: The burners not turning off poses a fire hazard, which could lead to serious damage or injury, though no actual incident or injury is reported yet.

incident_description:
We have a Sears Kenmore Smoothtop Electric Range, purchased in 2007.  When we turn the left front burner on (which is the "simmer select" feature), it makes a click noise.  My husband pulled the stove out, removed the back panel, and looked behind the control knob.  He observed visible electrical arc-ing while the burner was operating.  He also observed excessive carbon build-up behind the knob, indicating a long-term issue and potential for fire due to exposed electrical arcs.  Each time the burner pulses "on" and draws current, another arc happens.

This is not a burner that we use regularly.  The issue was detected due to the audible arc-ing sound that my husband (who works in the electronics industry) noted.  I would not have known this to be an electrical problem and would have probably used the burner, possibly leading to fire.

He heard this noise about three months ago and instructed me not to use the burner.  He just today had time to pull out the stove and noticed the carbon build-up.
justification: The incident involves visible electrical arcing and excessive carbon build-up, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:

The firm was contacted on 12/19/2011 and the consumer was advised that there was not a recall involving his model/serial number. The consumer will contact the firm again  to schedule a service technician to come out to make repairs. 

The consumer was able to gain power to the range bust fears that it poses as a fire/electrical hazard so he unplugged the cord from the wall outlet. 

No further information was provided.

incident_description: I have a frigidaire stove Model PLES389ECI.  It is a glasstop, slide in stove.  On multiple occasions, the stovetop will just turn on buy itself or will change temps without anyone around.  I have been fortunate that no one has been injured and we have been home when this happened.

incident_description:

Smoke continued to pour out, I went to tell my husband that the dw was on fire, he came in and opened the dw access panel in the side wall and inspected for fire.  Did not find any active fire, however, the smoke and smell of buring plastics had filled the house, We opened windows and exhaust hoods to clear out smoke and smell.  [REDACTED] removed the controll board out of dishwasher to discover that it had been the source of the fire.  He removed it from the house and placed it in the garage. incident_description:
Left front burner on smooth top electric range (Kenmore Model 790.9601) turns on spontaneously.   We were alerted to this condition by a dish towel that was lying on the burner began to burn. 

FORTUNATELY, no one was hurt. 

Further investigation, WITH ALL BURNER KNOBS FULLY TURNED OFF, we were able to re-create the situation by placing a teakettle on top of the burner for a few moments. After  removing it the burner glowed.
 
We contacted Sears and they said that a product safety form was filled out. They graciously agreed to pay for a diagnostic test. We will be responsible for further labor and replacements of parts. 

This is absolutely some kind of design flaw.
justification: The incident involved a burner turning on spontaneously, leading to a fire hazard, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sears (Kenmore) glass-top stove/oven model # 790.96113409 for my home
approximately 6 years ago.  (not sure of exact date).  Last evening (1-7-12) my wife was
going to bake cookies and turned on the oven to pre-heat to 325.  She then said: "there's
something wrong, I think I saw an error code of F10".  We both tried to restart the oven again
and noted that the broiler element was actually turning on instead of the bake element
(bottom element in oven).  I found literature on the stove and noted that an F10 code could
be the range probe (heat/temp sensor) or the EOC (electronic oven control board).  OK, I 
understand that parts may fail in appliances.  The alarming part is that once I plugged the unit
back in, the broiler unit came on "by itself".  I can see where a house fire could occur.  If
myself or my wife had not been standing in front of the stove observing this, we could have
come home to a house on fire.  What if my children had discovered this and not known how
to handle this and had gotten injured (burned)?  I then did some research on line on how to
fix this and have noted NUMEROUS reports of others describing the same problem.  I think
it would be prudent to ask the manufacturers to seek some resolution to this particular problem.
I also learned that Kenmore may not be the maker of the oven parts as [REDACTED] and others may
actually produce the parts and others may place their name on the end products such as Kenmore.
I'm requesting some guidance on what steps to take to move this issue along before a serious
incident results in loss of life or someone's home or both.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning oven that could potentially cause a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I bought a new Kenmore electric range, model 790.9280, in December, from the Sears in the Holyoke Mall, Holyoke, MA.  It was delivered and installed by the Sears delivery crew on 12/12/11.  Within a day or two following delivery, I read the "Getting started..." paper ("Read 1st") and noticed the section as follows:
"Q.  When I used my oven for the first time there was an odor and some smoking?
A.  It's possible to experience some odors and/or a small amount of smoke from your new range.  The odor will diminish after first using your oven.  Before cooking in your oven for the first time, we recommend that you turn the oven ON to 400o F for 30 minutes minimum.  This will allow for an initial burn-in period.  You may also ventilate the kitchen by opening a window."

Thinking this sounded like a good idea, I followed this direction, heating the stove to 400o for approximately 45 minutes, turning on the kitchen exhaust and hood fans, and (even though it was December) opening the kitchen and bathroom windows.  The stove produced a noxious odor and I observed some smoke coming from the oven's vent above the rear left corner of the cooktop.  The smell was bad, but not intolerable.

Thinking that this was adequate, based on the information quoted above, a few days later I baked an acorn squash in the oven, at 425o for approximately 50 minutes (I had preheated the oven, too).  During baking I noticed a light noxious odor, the same as noted during the initial use, but told myself that this was just "burn in" as above, and that it probably wouldn't ruin the food.  The squash cooked beautifully, but, alas, was inedible: I took one bite, and tasted a horrible metallic/lighter fluid tang, which hit me like a punch to the stomach.  I didn't even compost the rest of the squash, it went right into the trash.

A few days later I baked a small frozen pizza in the oven, approximately 11 minutes at 400o, preheating again, and found to my dismay that its flavor, too, was spoiled by the taste of burnt metal and solvents.  I resolved not to bake anything else in the oven until this noxious problem was resolved.

The holidays came and went, but on the evening of Monday, January 2, I thought that I would deal with the oven.  After putting my 1-year old daughter to sleep (I wouldn't want her exposed to nasty fumes), I started this project at about 9 pm.  Expecting an odor (but not expecting what subsequently happened), I opened the kitchen and adjacent bathroom windows, turned on the hood and kitchen exhaust fans, and duct-taped sheets over the doorway to the living room.  I cleaned the cooktop, removed the wire racks, and wiped down the inside of the oven, which appeared to be absolutely clean.  I then turned on the the Flex Clean (self-cleaning) feature, set for 2 hours.   After Flex Clean was running for approximately 30 minutes, the smell in the kitchen was so foul that I was forced to turn it off.  Smoke was pouring from the oven exhaust vent, though I saw no smoke in the oven cavity itself (though the interior light wasn't on, so maybe I missed it).  The smell was so horrible that it gave my wife a headache almost instantly.  My eyes stung and my throat was sore.  By 11 pm, while I was trying to figure out how to protect my house and family from the noxious fumes, I had a stomachache, and when I finally went to bed at approximately 11:30, I left the windows open and fans running, despite it being a cold winter night.  The odor had stuck to my clothes so I dropped them in the kitchen, but I still smelled it getting into bed: it was in my hair and on my skin.

On Tuesday, January 3 I awoke at 6:30 (before my daughter) to try to clean the house.  To my utter dismay, the noxious smell had not decreased at all overnight.  In fact, it had seeped through the barrier I had taped up, and was causing my living area to be uninhabitable.  Once my wife and daughter had gotten out of bed, my wife did the best she could to keep my daughter from heading to the living room and kitchen.  Meanwhile, I scrambled around the house with my HEPA vacuum, hoping that that would reduce the odor.  The kitchen was practically impossible to enter, the smell was so bad.  I threw the coats, towels, etc. that had been exposed to the fumes in the clotheswasher, and called the fire department.  Shortly thereafter, three firemen came to my door with a high-powered fan that they use to clear smoke out of burning houses.  They opened a window in every room of the house, and operated the fan for approximately 20 minutes, blowing air out the kitchen window.  (This, despite it being about 10o F outside.)  After the firemen had gone, my wife thought the smell had decreased, but I wasn't sure, and within about 20 minutes of their leaving, my sense was that the odor was as bad as it had ever been.

I went to work late on Tuesday, thanks to trying to protect my family from the odors caused by a should-be normal function of this Kenmore range.  On leaving, I left the fans running and the windows open.  My wife and daughter evacuated the house.  On returning home at approximately 8 pm (we ate out, since our kitchen is unusable with the odor), I found that the odor had not abated.  To the present (Saturday January 7) the smell has still not abated, and our pattern has remained similar.  We are avoiding the kitchen to the extent possible, only entering it to use the sink or access the refrigerator in the evenings and mornings, generally leaving the house during the day.

I have spoken many times with Sears' customer service about this problem.  Eventually they were able to provide a replacement stove.  As fine as it is to get a replacement stove, there remain significant problems.  My kitchen is unusable (perhaps if I had self-contained breathing apparatus, I could in fact use my kitchen as normal, but I don't).  

I believe my daughter's health to be in jeopardy simply by breathing the air in my house, based on the ill effects my wife and I are experiencing after being exposed to these odors for a several minutes.  I am now thinking that I will need to have professional cleaning done to resolve the noxious odor.  One of the frustrations I have encountered is that I cannot discover what the chemicals involved in the odor are, and what the health risks associated with those chemicals are.  To have a noxious chemical smell persist in one's home for several days, a smell that makes healthy adults feel ill after several minutes of exposure, but not to know anything else about it, is very anxiety-provoking, especially when a baby also lives in the home.

It has now been more than five continuous days of having windows open and fans running in my kitchen and adjacent bathroom, 24 hours a day.  This has been the coldest period we've had since last winter; overnight lows on a couple of the nights have been in the single digits.  The noxious odor in my kitchen is scarcely reduced from when I shut the Flex Clean cycle off, and my family and I cannot use the kitchen.  We have had to eat take-out or eat out--not our habit at all--each day.  Sears' customer service by phone has not been particularly helpful (I've had to explain that it is an electric stove and that there is no gas leak, etc., a couple of times, for example). I believe that we are avoiding the worst exposure, and are therefore protecting our health, but the first night of this incident my wife and I suffered ill effects from exposure to these fumes.

Based on the number of comments on mysears.com, Consumer Reports, and other appliance-related websites, the problem with noxious odors being emitted by new stoves is a known issue.  Even with a low-probability occurrence, it is unconscionable for manufacturers of such appliances to not "burn in" stoves in their own factories or other controlled environment.  My kitchen should not be the place where coatings, solvents, adhesives, or other chemicals are vaporized after manufacturing.

I have several questions:
-- what should I do now?
-- what chemicals comprise the odor?
-- do those chemicals pose a health risk in this situation (especially to a baby)?
-- how do I get rid of the odor?
-- what steps will Sears take to ensure that additional range buyers are not subjected to this experience?

I have sent a similar report to Sears via its website, but felt that the situation is serious enough to warrant formal reporting with the CPSC.
justification: The incident caused physical symptoms (headache, sore throat, stomachache) and made the home uninhabitable, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue appears to be a known but not common problem with new stoves (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
My husband and I awoke to smoke in our kitchen on Monday, Dec. 26th, 2011.  Upon inspection of our Kenmore Elite refrigerator, model #795 77543600, the following was discovered.  When the refrigerator was opened the lights on the interior roof of the refrigerator had been on, even with the doors closed, to the point that a plastic butter lid was melted/burnt and all items on the top shelf were hot to the touch.  The cover was warped and melted with blackened smoke stains.  There were visible smoke stains on the metal above the exterior openings where smoke had escaped from the interior of the refrigerator.  The bulbs were so hot that when I tried to unscrew one, it exploded, leaving the metal end of the light bulb in the socket. The light sockets are blackened/stained from the heat and fire.The refrigerator had been properly closed, the lights remain on even after the doors are closed.  We tested this by placing our camcorder in the refrigerator briefly while closing the doors.  When played back the lights remained on, through several different trials.  Both switches at the top of the doors could also be pushed in, which is what happens when the doors are shut, and the lights still remain on.  There was enough smoke damage that we are having to repaint our ceilings in our kitchen and dining area.  Our refrigerator had to be emptied out and cleaned 5 times to remove the smoke damage and smell, which is still evident. We have documented ALL findings through notes, photos, and video.  I got on the internet that night and googled for information on our model number and was appalled at the number of people who have had experiences like ours.  There are even several class action law suits.  Several sites and web pages have been designed for this complaint alone.  

It is harrowing to think that this problem has been reported for over 6 years and the refrigerators have not been recalled or consumers notified that there is a fire hazard associated with the product merchandise due to faulty workmanship.  In our case there was a fire contained within the refrigerator, but the smoke damage extended to the exterior areas as well.  

I sent a letter at 3:27 a.m. on 12/26/2011 to Sears Social Media Customer Service 2 addressing the matter.  [REDACTED], Senior Case Manager responded at 7:31 a.m. on 12/26/2011, stating that a case manager has been assigned to address your concerns.  We will contact you within 24 business hours.  
Received an e-mail @ 11:35 from [REDACTED], Social Media Case Manager with Sears Holding Corporation who issued a case number.  [REDACTED] has been very friendly and helpful.  She set up an appt. with [REDACTED] at A&E to come and repair/service the refrigerator on 12/28/2011.  I informed her that I knew of a class action law suit that was settled in Nov. 2011 where anyone who had paid for damage repairs for this problem would be reimbursed 200% of the costs and the warranties were extended for the problem.  She said this would be at no cost to us.  When A&E arrived,[redacted]informed me that there would be a service charge and I called [REDACTED] back who made arrangements with A&E to cover the costs of the service charge and parts.  The following parts were ordered: Case # [REDACTED]   Lamp Cover #46 795 3550JJ1070B     PCB ASSY, MAI (Panel Board) #46 795 6871JB1423N     Lamp Service Kit #46 795 ABY72971502, (This part has been on back order since Dec. 1, 2011 according to [REDACTED] @Sears recall department 1-888-567-3438 with no information on expected arrival). Total cost of the parts $183.29 with the labor costs totaling $197.29.  Until all the parts are in, the refrigerator cannot be repaired, and the known fire hazard is left in the homes of consumers, with NO guarantee that it will not catch on fire again.  The refrigerator has no lighting and an open live receptacle that will shock/electrocute you if you so much as touch the metal edge of it.  The sockets are damaged from heat and visible smoke/heat scorching.  The consumer is left with a damaged faulty fire hazard refrigerator and a well rehearsed,  "I'm sorry for any inconvenience this has caused you."  It is not just an inconvenience, it is mental anguish when you try to sleep, consuming thoughts that your refrigerator will ignite while you are out of the home or sleeping, disruption of activities, and the fear of touching the metal socket and getting shocked.  Anger at Sears for selling a product with known defects, and at LG for their lack of responsibility in recalling the faulty manufacturing of a product that caused fire damage in our home.  Sears Case Manager has offered a discount on a new refrigerator of 20%-25%, which is unacceptable.   Even though they say they understand, they could not possibly know the mental and emotional distress this has caused in our home and how it continues to disrupt our lives everyday. We have two grand children that I care for who cannot stay overnight with us since this has happened due to the fire hazard that this product presents in our home. We have been told to wait just a few more days for a recommendation or solution to this liability from our Social Media Case Manager.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with smoke damage and potential for injury from electrical shock, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
Product was a Kitchen Aid Wall Mounted Convection Oven Model No. KEBS107SSS04 (the "Unit").  The Unit is new and was professionally installed into a new construction home by the builder (William Lyon Homes).  The Unit is approximately 2 to 3 months old.  Approximately 1.5 hours into the the first time use of the Unit's "self-cleaning cycle", the interior glass plate on the oven door spontaneously shattered and forcibly expelled hot shattered glass shards from the Unit all over the kitchen.  

The "sefl-cleanning cycle" was performed accordng to manufacturers instructions.  A recent internet search revealed multiple consumer complaints regarding the same shattering of glass during "sefl-cleaning cycles" of new Kitchen Aid convection ovens.

The oven is unsafe and dangerous for a home with infant children.  The shattered glass could have caused severe bodily injury to our 9 month old baby had the child been in the kitchen at the time of the Unit's failure.  This Unit is devective and highly dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous failure (glass shattering) but no actual injury occurred, and similar incidents have been reported by other consumers.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that he was sleeping and his wife woke him up at 6AM frantically that the dishwasher was on emitting a burning odor. The consumer stated that his wife tried to open the handle of the dishwasher and could not because the handle is so hot. 

The consumer unplugged the circuit breaker and allowed the dishwasher to cool down. The consumer found that the inner contents of the dishwasher melted. The consumer stated that no one was injured and the damage did not spread to the home. 

The consumer found that his dishwasher is similar to those cited in release 11-022 but is not one of the models listed. The consumer has not called the fire department about the incident. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer.

UPDATE: Consumer tried calling GE 3 times, and was on hold for over an hour each time. He could not talk to anyone to see if they would help on a 3-year old dishwasher. He has since purchased an alternate brand.

incident_description:
Fire occurred on electronic control board in Kenmore Dishwasher (manufactured by Whirlpool), model number: 665.16493300.

During the first wash cycle, the dishwasher began to emit heavy smoke and fumes. Power was removed by selecting the circuit breaker at the main electric panel to off, and the smoke eventually stopped.

I accessed the electronic control panel and discovered significant burning and melting on and around the panel. The touch pad circuit board was completely covered with black soot.

As I was researching the cause and a possible solution, I ran across a post from July 2010 with pictures of a meltdown on this same control board. Both this and my control board melted down at the same place, and neither tripped the thermal fuse. 

Looking at the schematics of the dishwasher, it appears that the component associated with the connection point pertains to the door switch.

This is very dangerous. There is no protection to remove power when this occurs.
justification: The incident involved significant burning and melting but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents have been reported before, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:

As she shut the oven door the panel flashed "Door Lock Error".

Caller had contacted the manufacturer for her range on December 1st, 2011 to report that her oven was heating by itself.  She was told that there was nothing they would do for her oven but that there was a recall on her range but that it was for the burners and they would repair those.
Frigidaire Electric Range Model  with Serial# Previously recalled and repaired for burners release# 11-016 December 9th, 2011

The consumer stated that her electric wall oven is a potential safety hazard as the control element will not shut off when the consumer turns off the dial. The consumer stated that the unit caught fire last year. The oven was on for a few seconds before it caught fire and was set to bake at 275 degrees. The consumer stopped the fire by shutting off the circuit breaker. The consumer called the fire department and they arrived after the consumer was able douse the flames.

incident_description: Bosch Dishwasher number Bosch shu43c05uc/17 Batch #fd840201365 caught on fire after being loaded and turned on.  Fire extinguisher had to be used to put out the kitchen fire.  Fortunately, we were still awake and able to put out the fire.  Normally, we would turn on the dishwasher just before we went to bed.  If we had followed our normal procedure, the house would have burned down, and we would have perished.  We immediately contacted the manufacturer's representative, who gave us an "authorization number' [REDACTED] and a number for a local repair facility.  We contacted the repair facility the following day.  They advised the "authorization number" allowed them to order a part to replace a defective part, but did not authorize them to make any repairs or to come look at the appliance.  We contacted the manufacturer's representative again, and they advised that the "authorization number" gave the local repair shop the necessary information to make a house-call to determine if the machine could be repaired or not.  The manufacturer's representative would not tell us what would be the resolution if the machine could not be repaired.  It was obvious to us that the machine could not be repaired, due to the fire damage.  The electrical smoke and offensive odor were permeating our house.  We told the repair shop that we needed to get the damaged appliance out of our home, and they said that they would need to have the appliance in place in order to do their assessment of whether it could be repaired or not, but they would not be able to make a house call until a week later.  So far we have had no satisfactory response from the manufacture's representative nor their local repair shop.  We have a nasty burned out appliance in our home, presenting a continued danger from fire and smoke with no offer of amelioration from the manufacturer.  This was a high-end appliance from a supposedly high-end manufacturer.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The incident was mitigated by immediate action, though the risk of severe consequences was high.
