incident_description:
RE: circuit board fire-Kenmore Ultra Wash dishwasher (Whirlpool)
      dop: 5/18/2004
     model #: 665.16369301
     ser #:  FR2110795

On the morning of Tuesday, December 13, 2011, I started my Kenmore dishwasher.  I happened to be in kitchen when the dishwasher entered the main wash mode (I knew this after having inspected it for plastic on the heating element, the detergent door was open but there was still some soap in it).  I heard an odd "click" and "buzz-like" grind noise which repeated 2-3 times and then smelled burning plastic.  Initially, I was not too concerned with the noise, as I am usually not present while the machine is running, and thought it was just the motor.  I immediately opened the dishwasher to see if something plastic had come in contact with the heating element, but all was clear.  I closed the door and the cycle tried to start again, but I heard the same noises once or twice and the burning smell became overwhelming almost immediately and smoke appeared from the right side (not the vent side) of the control panel.  Again, I immediately opened the door to stop the machine and contemplated running for the fire extinguisher, but never saw any flames.  I then unplugged the unit and went to the computer to search "smoke from control panel of Kenmore dishwasher".  My search led me to many other accounts of the same thing happening to others with the same types of dishwashers. (main sources: Kitchenaidfire.com, saferproducts.gov (reports))
After reading the other accounts I then disassembled the control panel, and after my husband removed the circuit board, the damage was clear.  The board and components have burn marks and the housing is charred and melted.  It appears to have originated from one of the main wiring harness connections that is melted. (see attached photos)
This was an extremely scary finding, because normally I run the dishwasher before going to bed and on this occasion I had planned to leave to run errands.  I am extremely thankful that I was home and caught the malfunction so quickly.  Others reported flames shooting out, kitchen fires and smoke damage as a result.  There was such a potential for greater loss in this instance.
I attempted to contact the Whirlpool company via their website and contact phone numbers, but was ultimately sent in circles.  After speaking with 4 different people, 6 different phone numbers, and three transfers, I tried one last number and found myself talking with the first person again (who was a representative of Sears recall dept.).  I was never able to speak to anyone directly related to Whirlpool Co. and the agents who were able to look up my unit all said there had been no recalls or reports on it and there was nothing they could do because it was past the warranty period.  I was asked if I wanted to schedule a service call (at my own expense).
I purchased my dishwasher on 5/18/04.  I believe a good quality dishwasher/appliance ought to have a longer life than just 7.5 years.  According to other accounts/pending lawsuits, the Whirlpool company allegedly knew of the defect causing these circuit boards to overheat and possibly burst into flames since 2008.  While my product is past the warranty period, I would expect a reputable and safety conscious company to look out for their consumers by, at the very least, reporting the issue, even if unable to offer compensation.  If the allegations of the Whirlpool company's knowledge are true, I am deeply disappointed and will not feel safe in purchasing their products in the future.
justification: The incident involved a circuit board fire with smoke but no flames or injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple similar reports and evidence of a known defect.

I pressed the OFF button on the control panel but the broiling element continued to glow.  The ultimate solution was to trip the circuit breaker.  After 10-minutes I turned the circuit breaker on and the broiler element immediately turned on full blast.

After some research, it was determined this is a comon fault with the control board.  This uncontrolled operation of the broiling element may result in personal injury or death and property damage.

On 1-2-2012 shortly after starting the dishwasher a large plume of smoke came out from the right side door panel vent.  I opened the door but the dishwasher continued to run.  I then unplugged the unit turning it off.  The smoke went away also but filled then entire kitchen with the acrid smell for hours.   

I removed the door cover and looked inside of the control panel.  The circuit boards were blackened and the dishwasher obviously not able to be used again.  

Heard about other problems with Whirlpool dishwasher fires so I thought you should know.
justification: The incident involved a large plume of smoke and significant damage to the dishwasher, indicating a serious safety hazard, though no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer is not sure where the unit was purchased from it was in the home prior to him moving in.

Shortly after starting the dishwasher on the normal/energy setting  the control board begin to smoke she powered the dishwasher in the off position and left the door open. 

Later in the evening he closed the door and the dishwasher began to operate and smoke began to power out of the control panel began. SO the consumer powered the circuit breaker in the off position. 

The firm was contacted on 12/7/2011 and the consumer was advised that there was no recall on the unit and a report was filed ( Reference number [REDACTED]). The consumer has not made any final decisions on whether or not if he will replace and or repair the unit.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking, but no injury was reported, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 because the dishwasher was smoking and the smoke was powering out of the control panel.

incident_description: I didn't realize that I have an oven that had a safety recall back in 2004. Last night, I decided to use the self-clean feature. The oven and control panel both shut off during the cycle. The oven is now cooled but the door is locked and the control panel is still off. After researching the issue, I discovered that this is a well-known issue with these ovens and that some have had the glass explode during the self-clean cycle. I also learned that they may have faulty wiring, posing a fire hazard.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury occurred, and the issue is a known problem with potential fire hazard.

incident_description: Yesterday afternoon it was Christmas Eve and I'd just finished baking a fruit tart (on rack in oven at 325* for 40 minutes).  I placed the 9" Anchor Hocking glass pie dish pie dish onto a cooling rack on the table to cool.  About 15 minutes later as I stepped into another room, my husband who was sitting at the table where the tart was cooling, heard a loud pop sound and saw something fly past him.  When he looked on the floor he found a small piece of what looked like glass but couldn't figure out where it came from.  We checked all around but could find nothing that would've produced the shard of glass.  A short while later I went to move the tart and the whole dish collapsed in my hands (had potholders on!).  Turns out it was the glass pie dish that had shattered but we didn't realized it until I went to pick it up.  I then found many more slivers all around the table, chairs, and floor for which I pulled out the vacuum to be sure I got all the glass pieces.  I also had to clean all items around the counters and table because of the high potential of slivers having flown in/on anything.  Nice Christmas Eve present!  But also my beautiful Christmas dinner dessert was completely ruined and went directly into the garbage after all my hard work making it - I also threw out the other (unused) twin glass pie dish because I could now never trust them again.  They were so pretty with a nice blue tint and fluted edges - but good only to look at apparently.  I don't know where I bought them but will NEVER buy Anchor Hocking product again!
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass pie dish but no injuries were reported, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
Bialetti Muka Expresso coffee maker has exploded twice sending hot coffee up to the ceiling and all over the kitchen counters. First incident occurred 2 years ago and the company sent us a replacement valve assembly to prevent a recurrence. This new valve was a different design and worked successfully until December 6th when the second valve exploded. Parts of the plastic/metal assembly  travelled upward with enough force to damage the stove exhaust hood and break a glass cover on one of the hood's lights. Hot coffee sprayed an area in an area about 24 inches in diameter on the ceiling above, and required repainting. More importantly, this coffee eruption was within 18 inches of a house guest waiting for the first cup of the day! Major burns would have occurred had he been closer to the stovetop.

The company response was to provide 2 replacement valves and an "IÃÂm Sorry"

One question, unanswered by the company, was whether our altitude of nearly 9,000 ft would impact the release pressure of the valve assembly A possible cause?

I would like to see an independent evaluation of this product before some one is badly burned. THANKS
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a significant burn risk, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
We had an electrical fire today in our dishwasher - thank the Lord we were home and awake when it happened.

We have a Kenmore Elite Model 665-16482300; Serial #FR3406704  It was installed 9/8/2004.

The fire was in the top right of the door.  The controls did not respond when I tried to turn it off so I turned off the electrical circuit breaker.  It gave off a terrible smell and a lot of smoke.

I found several incidences of similar fires of other Kenmore Elite owners on the internet.  I also found a recall on a similar diswasher that one poster believes is the same dishwasher just with a plastic tub http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml05/05123.html
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with smoke but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The consumer  stated that free standing electric range a is a potential fire hazard as oven exceeds the desired temperatures it is set to and would not turn off when the consumer tried to shut it off. The range has a smooth top surface. The consumer was baking at 350 degrees for 15 minutes until the oven became very hot. The consumer had to shut off the oven at the circuit breaker. The consumer stated that her product has not caught fire but did begin to smoke. The consumer stated that the product has not shown any signs of damage. 

The consumer feels that the digital panel malfunction may be the cause as she did research and found that the electrical components of the oven can melt and fuse together. The consumer stated that her home has not been damaged by the product and her home has not been injured by the product. 

The consumer has not called the fire department after the incidents took place. The consumer called a private service to repair the unit 3 weeks ago and was informed that the part to fix the range was discontinued. 

The consumer had the product in her home when the house was purchased. The consumer has yet to call the retailer or the firm. The consumer did mention that her range is similar to those cited in recall 09-333 and poses the same safety hazard. The consumer has not had any issues with the stove top except the power is not as hot as the desired temperature. On one occasion the right front burner did become very hot much like the oven.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that became excessively hot and smoked, but no fire or injury occurred, aligning with severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the described malfunction and similar past recalls.

incident_description:
While using the front right burner and the simmer burner for approximately an half an hour when the carbon monoxide detectors (two to be exact) went off. She does not recall what the readings were on them. The fire department was contacted immediately. 

[REDACTED] Fire Department in [REDACTED] came out to the home and did a reading on the home and advised the consumer to power the oven on and the range  at the same time. All the windows and doors were open to the home and the carbon monoxide levels went back to 0 The reading he got was 15 ppm.

The Fire Department advised the consumer to contact the firm and or a repairman prior to using again and disconnected everything from the range. 

She contacted the firm on 12/8/2011 and she was advised to purchase an extended warranty. She has not made any final decisions on the.
justification: Carbon monoxide detectors went off, but no injury or death occurred. The situation was resolved with the fire department's intervention.

incident_description: My Kenmore Electric oven's electronic control panel sparked, flashed and caught on fire while the oven was preheating. Flames came out the top and singed the cabinet above. The circuit breaker was turned off and the flames went out. The ECP is completely charred as well as the connecting wires, and the oven will need to be replaced.
justification: The oven caught fire, causing property damage but no injuries, and the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore Gas Range Slide-In Oven. It was purchased from Sears 2 1/2 years ago. The oven has always made a large boom sound when it is warming up. Yesterday while it was warming up and things were cooking on the stovetop my mother smelled gas. She opened the oven door to see what the problem was and there was a loud boom. She was burned on her face and neck and her hair, eyebrows and eyelashes were burned off as well. It appears that the oven never ignited and that when she opened the door the gas that was building up came out and racted with the fire on the stovetop. It is a very scary and upsetting incident that we hope doesn't happen to anyone else/
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the face, neck, and hair, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the oven's history of making loud booms and the specific conditions leading to the incident.

incident_description:
Broiler element turned itself on and could not be turned off by using the controls.
We had to turn power off in the electric breaker panel to shut stove down.
justification: The broiler element malfunctioned but was resolved without injury by cutting power, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: Our Kenmore Elite dishwasher, Model number 665.16052400, Serial Number FS1107983, began billowing smoke from the front control panel about 2/3 through a wash cycle. Fortunately, I was at home, noticed the smoke almost immediately and was able to stop it by opening the door and disrupting the cycle. This unit was purchased almost 7 years ago and until this point, had not given any indication of electrical problems. We took apart the front panel and found the circuit card burnt through and the wiring harness melted.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke but was promptly stopped without injury, indicating an incident with no harm to individuals.

incident_description: Upon turning on the oven to "bake" setting, the control panel displayed nonsense. An arcing noise was heard. Sparks shot out the back of the range and sent black smoke into the air.  The range was unplugged and no longer works.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. Such electrical malfunctions are possible but not extremely common.

incident_description: On, December 30, 2011, our Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator, model 795.77546600(purchased 11/25/06 at Sears) overheated the interior light and melted the cover and started to melt the ceiling of the refrigerator.  It got extremely hot and we had to remove to light.  If this had happened overnight, I'm sure there would have been a fire.  Luckily, we noticed it during the day and disabled the light to prevent a fire.  We checked the buttons on the doors that turn off the lights when the doors are closed, and the lights would not turn off.  This is very disturbing and scary.  I hate to think that our home could have burned down due to this malfunction. After researching this problem online, I have found many other people who had the same problem.  I've contacted Sears, and they are sending a replacement light and a repairman to fix the light, but I don't know what will happen regarding the melting of the ceiling due to this being manufactured by LG.  This product needs to be recalled due to the danger of a fire.  Apparently there is a class action lawsuit against LG/Kenmore that claimed these refrigerators contain a defect that caused the interior light to remain on when the refrigerator doors are closed.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting of the refrigerator components, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description: I was using a folding pocket knife purchased at Harbor Freight a few weeks ago to open a box (it was the first time I used this particular knife). I extended the blade completely and when I went to open the box using my right hand, the blade collapsed on top of my right index finger. I immediately applied ice and pressure and was driven to the hospital by my neighbor.  My doctor examined the wound and informed me I had cut off a portion of my finger and that I most likely sustained nerve damage. Since this injury was a slice, there was nothing to suture. A pressure bandage was applied and pain medication prescribed.  When I returned home, I examined the knife and noticed the mechanism that is supposed to lock the blade in place did not (and would not) lock which is why the blade collapsed onto my finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury involving nerve damage and partial amputation of a finger, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the defective nature of the knife's locking mechanism.

incident_description:
The left front burner on my stove does not shut off at times.   It also changes temperature while turned on.   For example, last night I had a pot on simmer and I did not touch anything after 15 minutes of cooking it turned to high without me changing the knob.   I then had to rotate the control several times to get it to turn off. 

The stove has occassionally had problems with that burner turning off.  Last night was the first time it changed temperature by itself.

I am the original owner of the stove, I purchased it in 2007.    

The stove is a Frigidaire  model FEFB79GBA.   The Serial number is VF73542192.

I contacted the manufacturer because there is a recall on similar stoves, but mine is not included in the recall.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Frigidaire Electric range with turn knob burners and digital oven controls.   I now have had two Frigidaire electric ranges with turn knob smooth top controls and digital oven controls.  Both units, right at the three year age have had the electronic control boards go out.  Both caused risk of electrical fire and scorched the back of the appliance.   Frigidaire is aware that they have issues with the board.  It is the same model of board in both ranges.  On the first unit, the control module was so back ordered from repeated issue that they could not replace the piece for over 90 days.  Instead the replace it with another unit that had the same faulty control board.    Frigidaire has issued a recall on this unit but NOT for the faulty control board, only for an issue they claim is unrelated that allows the burners to turn on by themselves.    Clearly Frigidaire/Electrolux is selling a faulty product that is a danger to consumers.  Frigidaire has been given the opportunity to make it right but has been allowed to continue to endanger customers and sell faulty product.
justification: The incident describes a risk of electrical fire and scorching, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
We currently have a Frigidaire Gallery Refrigerator(model FGUS2632LE0).    We have had 2 door bins break off the door after closing the door with a drawer still open.  The pressure was minimal for everyday use.  The last time (Dec. 20, 2011) 2 glass jars hit the floor broke resulting glass shards and liquid  all over the floor. Luckily everyone had shoes on.  Otherwise it would have been easy to step on the glass.

These bins should be more durable, in order to prevent injuries.

This issue is probably not limited to this refrigerator   model.  I have scene the same problems at work, where the dorr shelves or bins easily break
justification: The incident resulted in broken glass and potential injury, but no actual injuries occurred due to precautions (shoes).

incident_description: On Dec. 31, 2011 I had the oven set at 400 degrees to bake a pie.  I placed the pie on a cookie sheet  and placed it in the oven.  I set the timer for 50 minutes.  After 26 minutes of baking time I checked the pie crust to make sure it was not browning too quickly.   It was fine.  Within 5 minutes after checking the pie smoke began pouring out of my oven and the entire top of the pie was black.  I kept hitting the cancel button and the oven would not turn off.  The smoke detectors were going off in the house.  When I opened the oven door flames shot up from the pie.  I poured salt over the pie.  My husband turned off the breaker from the range.  That was the only way we could get the oven turned off.  The next day we turned the breaker for the range back on and the top element of the oven immediately came back on and would not turn off, again.  We turned the breaker back off and it remains off.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames but no injury or death, and similar incidents are uncommon based on the provided frequency.

incident_description: I have a new Electrolux Dual Fuel Range Model EW30DS65GS8. We noticed a strong gas smell and found that the knob to turn on the gas burner was slightly turned on and the igniter did not start the burner flame. Hence the gas continued to flow into the room.  Had we not noticed the smell or had left the room and a spark was set, we believe the house would have exploded. I phoned Electrolux but they did not offer any solution other than to be careful. We believe that there should have been a fault sensor that if the gas was flowing and a flame had not ignited, the stove should automatically shut off the flow of gas.
justification: Gas leak occurred without ignition, posing a potential explosion risk, but no actual injury or damage resulted.

incident_description: After running clean cycle of my cuisinart DCC-1100 coffeemaker, the unit immediately began to overheat.  Although it was turned off (it does so automatically after the cleaning cycle), there was an overwhelming smell of burning plastic and electrical wiring and smoke began to pour out of the top of the unit.  Fortunately, I was standing next to it and was able to unplug it before the heat could intensify further and engulf the unit in flames.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: A screw fell out of the mixer while making a cake and it wasn't discovered until after the cake was baked and sliced.
justification: A screw fell into the cake but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My 22 months old child's upper incisor pull out during a fall while drinking and holding the cup on the  on a padded hardwood floor. The thin edge of straw open/close mechanism on the lid caught inbetween the gap of upper front incisors and the force from the fall levered out the entire incisor. This product should be recall.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (tooth pulled out), but such occurrences are unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: Igniter started operating with controls in "Off" position and did not turn off when control knobs were moved from "Lite" to "Off".  Within a minute, a fire had started from under one of the control knobs.
justification: The incident involved a fire starting due to equipment malfunction, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: GE Profile Dishwasher Model # PDW9280JOOSS; Serial # AH718142B    The dishwasher was turned on as usual.  After 20 minutes of runtime I smelled an odor in the kitchen and determined it was coming from the dishwasher.  It was a burning smell.  I opened the dishwasher and noticed that no water had entered it however it was producing prolific steam.  I tried pressing the "start" button to turn it off and it would only blink on and off.  I could not turn the unit off and no other buttons on the control panel responded.  I had to turn it off from the breaker.  I found this site as I was researching and also found that it was recalled over a year ago.  We were never notified.  I am thankful that I was home and awake when this problem occurred, as it seems a fire was imminent.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned with a burning smell and potential fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Report revised to correct model and serial number
GE Profile Self Cleaning Convection Electric Range JS968
My wife received a serious burn after being touched by the heating element in the oven/broiler part of our electric range. When I looked at the range, the heating element is within about 1 inch of the front edge of the oven and projects downward about 1 inch from the top of the oven. In this location it is very easy to contact accidentally. The manual has 4 pages of safety information and never once mentions this hazard. The oven compartment should be fitted with a guard to prevent such contact, and existing ranges should be retrofitted with this.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious burn, indicating an injury, and the design flaw makes accidental contact likely.

incident_description: GE 4.5 oval slow cooker model #106661 (Walmart - series A4210AS).  I have had this slow cooker for several years (probably 9 or 10) and had no problems.  Used it tonight and when I was cleaning the outside I noticed that the right handle had several cracks in it.  Went online to see if I could purchase a replacement handle and found a recall notice on the cooker dated January 13, 2005, specifically related to this problem.  No injuries (thankfully) from this, but figured I'd go ahead and report it as requested on the recall notice.  It's been a good crockpot.  Sorry I didn't see the notice in time to get a replacement :-).
justification: The incident involves a cracked handle with no injuries reported, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) based on the recall notice and the high frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: On christmas morning and off duty at home, I was running a pot of coffee and hot water for tea in the morning in my Cooks (Brand) Dual Coffee Pot Maker. I heard a loud popping noise coming from the coffee maker. I went to investigate the noise and discovered a strong smell of of electrical wires burning. I then observed smoke coming from a small vent hole in the rear of the coffee maker. Coffee maker was immediately unplugged from the wall outlet.
justification: The incident involved a coffee maker emitting smoke and a burning smell, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Bought a new crock pot for Christmas present. Used it on New Years day for a roast. Went to church and return to the home with a burnt plastic smell. Check the Crock Pot and didn't notice anything burning. Ate the meal and upon cleaning the Crock Pot notice melted plastic under the control panel. Looks like the heating element under the Crock Pot was melting the plastic. It's a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or fire, warranting a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was detected before any actual fire occurred.

incident_description:
During self cleaning cycle, the door glass shattered.  The hot glass was expelled from the bottom of the door and onto the floor.  The floor was burning due to the hot glass.

Kitchenaid acknowleges this problem but will replace glass with same type replacement glass.  The problem still exists.  This problem is chronicled many times on the internet.

Oven Model # KEBS208SSS02, ser# XW3702298, purchased 03/05/2009
justification: The hot glass was expelled from the bottom of the door and onto the floor, causing the floor to burn.  This problem is chronicled many times on the internet.

incident_description:
I ran 2 hours of a cleaning cycle on my Amana, 30 inch width, Gas Range.  The model name on the stove was The Big One, referring to the oven size.  
 
The front edge (the top and just inside) of my oven door melted, and the knobs on the front of the stove were discolored and the plastic part of the knob formed a drip.  The door and top of the stove were extremely hot.  Since I had run the vent fan above the stove during the cleaning process, fumes were not a problem.

The damage was visibly obvious so I did not touch the overheated surfaces avoiding burns.
justification: The incident caused damage to the stove but no injuries were reported as the user avoided touching the overheated surfaces.

incident_description:
We had started the dishwasher as normal. It was the middle of the day. It had been running for about 10 minutes when we noticed black smoke coming out of the right door vent. It smelled like plastic burning. We opened it up and it stopped smoking. We closed it again and we could hear it arcing (shorting out) inside the upper right door. Smoke again started pouring out of the right door vent.  We opened it again and cancelled the wash. We took out the screws holding the door panel together and the circuit board in the upper right door had black soot covering the middle where it attaches to the wires leading down into the door. 

If we had not been home to stop it, it could have started the kitchen cabinets on fire. It still smells like burnt plastic in the kitchen and it's been 10 hours later.  After searching online I found several other people who had a smilar problem with their dishwasher, which prompted us to file this report.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking and could have started a fire, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
While cooking a oven roaster chicken , the inner glass on the lower oven exploded shattering inward into the oven.

Whirlpool 30-Inch Smooth Surface Double Oven Electric Range (Color: Stainless Steel)
Item #: 210007 |  Model #: GGE390LXS purchased through Lowes about a month ago.
justification: The glass shattered but no injury was reported, making it an incident without harm. Such occurrences are unlikely but not rare for new appliances.

incident_description:
Caller & wife were awakened around 4:00AM by the smoke alarm on Sunday, October 16, 2011.
They went to the kitchen, opened a window, turned the ceiling fan on to clear thick smoke that had accumulated in house, then began searching for fire, saw flames coming from rear of refrigerator.
Orange/red flames were no more than a couple of inches high above the compressor.

Smoke was thick enough so that you could see it but not so thick that you couldn't see through it, caller attributes this to the smoke alarm being in the kitchen and so sounding quickly.

Caller's refrigerator is recalled on release# 09-145, he has already contacted manufacturer via the recall hotline and scheduled repair for October 20, 2011, however when he contacted[REDACTED]-Maytag this morning 10/17/2011, informed them that the refrigerator was non functional due to it's catching fire, he didn't get the name of the person he spoke with but states that he was told that they would come out this afternoon 10/17/2011.

Caller would like this refrigerator repaired or replaced at manufacturer expense.

As of this report date repair was only partially accomplished.  Replaced wires were only "wire-nut" connected - there is to be the correct "wire-harness" replacing temporary wiring in very near future, according to [REDACTED]- Maytag technician.

The reported product was purchased on about 1/15/11 from the original purchaser.

The retailer state is Maryland.
justification: The incident involved a small fire with no reported injuries, but it required immediate action to prevent harm.

incident_description:
While baking potato pancakes at about 400 degrees in my Whirlpool electric wall oven, Model RBS245PDB14 (now 8 years old), the oven had been opened once after about 8 minutes to turn the contents over, and then approximately 5-8 minutes later the kitchen filled with smoke as the oven apparently got very hot and caused the food to catch on fire.  The oven locked on its own and we were unable to open it and also could not turn the oven off.  The house filled with smoke while the contents continued to burn.  We had to cut off power to the oven with the circuit breaker in order to stop the oven from heating, and opened all windows and doors to the house.  About ten minutes later when we turned the circuit breaker back on, the oven still was locked and we couldn't open it, the off button still would not respond, and the coils were red again.  The self cleaning cycle was NOT on.  We had to turn the circuit breaker off again in order to get the power off.  We called Whirlpool and they said we should wait a few hours for the oven to cool, then turn the circuit breaker on again and see if we could then open the oven and turn it off.  About three hours later, we turned the circuit breaker on again, were able to open the oven door and remove the charred food, tried to turn the oven power off, but we couldn't and the oven started to heat again (the coils got red hot).  We had to flip the circuit breaker again to keep the power off.  Whirlpool sent a technician on 12/28/11 who tested the oven and advised that the control was bad and since it would cost several hundred dollars to replace, it was more practical to get a new oven.
This is the SECOND such incident with this oven.  About three years ago, my high school son was baking cookies in the oven, and the exact thing happened - the oven locked, the house filled with smoke from burning cookies, and my son was unable to turn the oven off or open the oven door to remove the burning cookies.  Again, we had to open all windows and doors to get the smoke out and wait a few hours until we could open the oven.  At that time, the oven did not turn itself back on as it did this time.  When I called Whirlpool at that time, they advised that my son must have accidentally turned on the cleaning cycle, though he was certain he did not.  I always thought that perhaps he did accidentally turn on the cleaning cycle, but I now know that he did not and the problem was with the oven.
Although we will be replacing our oven, this is obviously potentially very dangerous and we want to make sure it does not happen to other consumers.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing smoke and fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The dishwasher door would not seal all of the time correctly and would cause a flood on the kitchen floor. Would not happen all of the time so you never knew when to expect the leak.

Then the heating element coil inside the plastic tub popped. The element appears to have broken or melted apart while in the heating mode.
justification: The dishwasher's malfunction causes flooding and a heating element failure, posing a risk of property damage but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Caller's dishwsher caught fire on November 23rd, 2011.

Caller started dishwasher, states that it had been running "for a while" (she didn't notice exact length of time) when she heard a noise that she identifies as a "funny crackling noise). 

She got up, looked around the corner and saw smoke and flames a couple of inches high shooting out of top right side of dishwasher.

She opened the door to the dishwasher, the flames disapated, she opened the windows to clear the smoke and her husband shut the breaker off.

Caller contacted manufacturer November 28th, she does not remember who she spoke with but did discontue the call when she believed there was no concern.  The manufacturer contact did offer to send repairman at manufacturer expense to identify repair necessary at consumer expense.  Consumer declined.

Consumer purchased a new dishwasher, allowed this dishwasher to be taken away however; she saved the circuits in case someone wants to investigate

Caller would like to alert the public, have this dishwasher placed on recall and would like to be reimbursed or at least partially reimbursed for purchasing a new dishwasher.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was quickly contained without further incident.

incident_description:
Purchased a Baby Brezza BPA Free One Step Baby Food Maker by Baby Brezza at Babies-R-Us. Their product information is:

Just load your food and water into the machine, set your steam time, and in minutes the Baby Brezza One Step Baby Food Maker will automatically steam and puree your food into a delicious meal for baby.
