The Major Safety Issue is the Unit will Blend without the Bowl Lid in place allow access to the turning blades. There is a safety tab on the Bowl Lid that is supposed to disengage the Blend function when not in place.
justification: The unit can blend without the bowl lid, exposing turning blades, which poses a safety hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description: GE Upright Freezer Model FUF 21SVDRWW . Freezer stopped working. Electronics repairman discovered a short or fire damage in the electronic temperature controller in the front of the freezer in the door. After trying to contact GE for find a replacement part, they would not give any information as to what part might be required. They required a GE repairman to investigate the problem. They would not give any part information without this. [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involves a freezer malfunction with potential fire damage, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Crock-Pot Designer Series Smart-Pot at Kohl's less than a year ago. Whenever I
used it I smelled a burning plastic odor. I went to use the Crock-Pot today, December 29, 2011
and noticed something black fall off of the bottom when I picked the Crock-Pot up to place it
onto the counter. I turned the Crock-Pot over and a large portion of the black, bottom plastic
shell was melted off (exposing the inside parts of the appliance). I contacted the phone number
on the side of the Crock-Pot and they are sending me a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance with no reported injury, but potential for harm due to melting plastic.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Electric Range, and we had a fire in the oven top element. Even when we turned the oven off, it continued to burn. I looked for recalls with this type of problem and found the same type of problems with units that have been recalled. I checked the Model # on my electric range, and it did not match the numbers on the recall. It is the exact same problem that the recalled untis have. This is really not safe. My Model Number is 91199004992 and is a Kenmore Elite the same name as the ones that have been recalled.
The upper element started to burn just like if you were welding. We had the oven door a little open because we were broiling some steak. We did not know what to do, we shut the broiler off and it did not stop. I ran down stairs to get to the fuses, and pulled the fuse out. while I was doing that my wife and son were upstairs and the burning started shooting out of the door opening, they ran out of the kitchen, and when I heard them yelling and running, I ran upstairs. Very scarry. It did stop and we unpluged the range.
justification: The incident caused a fire but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 as the problem is similar to recalled units.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore dishwasher (model #665.17032401) made a loud electrical 'pop' during its normal wash cycle.  We were in the next room and discovered smoke pouring out of the steam ports, with an acrid plastic burning smell.  We immediately opened the washer door, and shut off the breaker.  After emptying the washer, I found the culprit.  It seems to be an encapsulated board behind the control panel - and it had melted the plastic (about 1.25 inch diameter) from the inside.

I found that the CPSC website lists a recall notice for this model, but the serial numbers do not match the website description.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the recall notice and the observed damage.

incident_description:
I have a Maytag YMER8875WS range that I purchased in June 2011. When I put my turkey in the oven on Christmas day, the rack fell down. The sides of the oven have expanded to the racks are no longer wide enough to fit securely. I suffered a burn on the inside of my left forearm and on the back of my right hand. The Maytag tech checked the range and agreed that the oven liner has bowed outwards. A new range has been ordered for me.

I the meantime, I have researched this online and discovered it is an extremely common problem, especially with Kenmore ranges. There is a huge potential risk of serious injury to people using these defective ranges, yet the manufacturer doesn't seem to acknowledge the problem.
justification: The incident resulted in burns (injury), and the problem is described as extremely common, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The consumer says her husband was using self cleaning feature and after 10 minutes she heard an explosion.  She says that her husband was using the "use and care manual".  She says the inside glass panel had shattered.  The consumer contacted the retailer who told her they are no longer under warranty.  She says that is the first time they used the self cleaning feature.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and shattered glass, but no injury was reported, placing it at severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as this is the first time the self-cleaning feature was used and such incidents are not common.

incident_description:
Shortly after arriving home she noticed that there was a electrical burning smell in the home and when she detected the odor coming from the refrigerator that was when she noticed smoke coming from the rear of it. She then contacted the police station who dispatched the  local fire department .

Bowling Green Fire Department in Bowling Green MO  came out to the home and  advised the consumer that the failure was with the relay in the refrigerator and she was advised not to use it. The unit was unplugged to prevent any further use.

While doing some research online the consumer came across a recall  (see Release #09-322) where the hazard was a electrical failure in the relay, the component that turns on the refrigeratorÃÂs compressor, can cause overheating and pose a serious fire hazard.

She noticed that her model number and serial number was affected and contacted the firm on 12/5/2011 and the representative (name was not provided ) advised that her unit was not affected by the recall and they could send out a service technician but she would be required to pay for it.

The consumer declined in the matter and since then replaced the refrigerator. She contacted the CPSC on 12/5/2011 and the representative that she spoke with contacted the fire and was advised that the consumer model number was not affected by the recall because it had a new relay compressor in it.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard from a refrigerator, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue was identified and addressed before any serious harm.

incident_description:
on december 17th my amana refridgerator model #ATB2135HRQ serial #10442346AT, caught fire on the relay starter which melted the prongs on the compressor unit. I feel extremely lucky that my house did not catch on fire. I lost all the food I had in the freezer and fridge because I was not at home when this happened.
I learned this from my repairman at "Ortegas" who came out on the 19th of december.
He told me to call Baillios where I purchased the fridge less than 5 years ago for a replacement fridge.
Baillios told me to call Maytag/whirlpool who now owns amana that they would not replace it.
Maytag/whirlpool put me in touch with the safety recall team there.
I called the safety recall team and was told a repairman for maytag would have to come asses the damage before anyone could do anything.
Mountain Valley Appliance sent a repairman out to see about repairing the fridge.
They told me they would call to see how to handle this situation and was told only repairs would be made to fridge no replacements.
So I called to speak w/ someone and that person [REDACTED], hung up on me there because I wanted to speak to a supervisor.
[REDACTED] at the safety recall team called me back and I put in a complaint w/ her.
the recall team sent a compressor out to the repair man at mountain valley the next day.
they came out and replaced the relay switch and the compressor which did not work.
The next day they said the compressor was damaged in shipment.
The safety recall team called and told me it was too late to do anything till after christmas.
At this point I wrote to :[REDACTED] to complain about not having a fridge for my daughters' birthday party, my holiday parties, and christmas and was told simply "sorry" we can not do anything for you except fix the fridge after christmas.
With further complaining I was offered a walmart gift card of 135.00 to buy a small fridge.
I have not yet received the gift card.
The team sent out another compressor that I have not yet received.
I have lost all the food in my fridge, lost wages from staying home to repair fridge, etc.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, posing a significant risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While the consumerÃÂs two year old toddler was using the plastic spoon to eat yogurt with when he pulled the spoon from his mouth she noticed that the tip of it was gone. 

She assumed the two year old ingested it and will take him to seek medical attention.  She has discontinued the use of the plastic ware and will contact the retailer/firm.

While reading over the label on the product she indiated that she did not see a warning label no intended for use by smaller children.

The doctor is having her monitor [REDACTED] and notify doctor of any unusual symptoms over the next few days.

No further information was provided.
justification: The toddler ingested a piece of the plastic spoon, requiring medical monitoring, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Xmas eve i started my sunbeam bread maker the same as i have done many many times over the past year or two, as i was preparing to leave the house after 25 minutes i noticed a faint smell of plastic heating up and thought to check on bread maker to find that what i assume was the thermostat had broken and the heating coil was red hot and glowing and my dough was cooking on the bottom, I immediately pulled the power cord and started to throw the machine away but as i have no doubt in my mind that this machine would have eventually melted and started a fire in the house had i left the house without checking on the machine - i decided to keep the machine and eventually contact you as i have been unsuccessful in contacting sunbeam
justification: The incident caused no injury, but had the potential to cause a fire, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: Smelled burning plastic and found the dishwasher spewing smoke from control panel
justification: The incident involved smoke from the dishwasher, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My son smelled burning plastic in refrigerator. Researched model online. Saw that there were incidents where interior light would not go off causing melting and a potential fire hazard. Called Sears. They wanted to charge me for service call because it's out of warranty, even though I told them it was a safety hazard. The repair rep asked ME if there was a recall on the refrigerator. I told them that THEY should know that, not me. They then transferred me to recall department. Evidently, there is a known safety issue with the interior lights on this model. They are sending me a replacement light kit. I then asked what I could do to prevent a fire! I was told to remove the light bulbs. My son got burnt trying to remove the bulbs because they were so hot and he was wearing gloves to protect his hands. Also most of the plastic inside the light housing was melted!!! Finally got it apart and removed the bulbs. Then I saw that the plastic refrigerator lining at the top of the refrigerator is bubbled and melted!!!! I'm lucky there was no fire!!! Waiting to see if Sears repairs or replaces my unit to my satisfaction. I will not accept them just changing out the light unit when the interior lining is now damaged.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burn) and significant property damage (melted plastic), indicating a high likelihood of recurrence given the known safety issue.

incident_description: Started baking cookies on bake setting @ 350 degrees.  After 8 minutes the the cookies were blackened and a few were on fire.  The broiler was on at a high setting.  I turned off the oven and pulled out the burnt cookies. Problem is the broiler did not turn off.  I finally had to trip the breaker outside to terminate the broiler element.  I waited for 30 minutes and set the breaker, only to find the broiler now comes on by itself, at the highest temperature.  After some internet searching, I find this is a very common problem with the mother board controls.  Having even found a vendor on ebay "rebuilding" the boards.   I would hate to see what could happen with a disabled or elderly consumer in this situation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven broiler that could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer is not the original owner of the range and did not move into the home where is located until August 22/2011. She indicated that she is not sure exactly where it was purchased and or how long it has been in the home. 

The consumer had two inspection done on the home the second report from  a inspector from [redacted] whom came out to the home on Saturday September 17,2011. 

The inspector noticed that there were high levels Carbon Monoxide being produced from the gas oven. The report indicated that at start up the oven released Carbon Monoxide at over 100 PPM  and continued to produce CO at 27 PPM within 1 minute. 

The inspector recommended to not use the oven until the firm was contacted. The consumer indicated that she has not used the oven and the firm was contacted on 9/19/2011 and a service technician has been scheduled to come out to inspect the oven on 9/23/2011.

The consumer stated that she does not feel safe with having the range in her home knowing that it is producing high levels of Carbon Monoxide releasing from it.
justification: The incident involves a hazardous situation with high levels of Carbon Monoxide, but no injury or death has occurred as the oven was not used and the issue was promptly reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while using the oven for approximately 1-2 hours, he noticed that there was smoke emitting from the cabinets and there was an a burnt odor, the oven was immediately turned off and the smoke dissipated.  

The following day when the pulled out the microwave/oven (unit) and discovered that the unit had badly burnt holes in his cabinet where it was located.

Consumer feels that he and his family is fortunate that it was not a house fire.

12/5/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that someone would contact him.

Consumer feels that this oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled. Consumer says it was the oven, not the microwave, that caused the fire.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burnt holes in the cabinet) but no injuries or fatalities, and the likelihood is possible given the description.

incident_description:
Product:  Electrolux Dual Fuel Range  EW30DF65GS

The oven had been on for about 1 1/2 hours at 400 degrees.  All of a sudden, I heard a loud noise and the middle layer of glass in the oven door had shattered.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The day before Thanksgiving my stove started to have a burning electrical smell coming out of the door. When I opened the oven door, I saw that the switch that is supposed to depress and turn the light off and on automatically when you open the door was glowing. I touched it with a wooden spoon and particles of glowing plastic came off on to my rug. I quickly pulled the stove away from the wall and unplugged it. I contacted Frigidaire and was told that my stove was no longer under warranty, so there was nothing they could do except to recommend an approved repairman. Had I not been home, who knows what could have happened, but I believe there would have been a fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it was a specific malfunction in an older stove.

incident_description:
Today (Dec 29, 2011) I bought a slow cooker from AAFES , Camp Zama, Japan. I brought it home, unpacked it and washed it (crock and lid) by hand in my sink with warm soapy water.
 Immediately after rinsing the lid, as I was  reaching over to set the lid  aside to drain, it exploded in my hand. Shards of glass went all over my sink. I received 1 minor cut on my hand. The shards were very sharp and could have caused significant injury had they gone into my eyes. 

This is a 3 quart slow cooker with the label " Simply Perfect "  ("for the home")

The company:     CE North America, LLC
 Customer service
6950 N.W. 77th Court
Miami, FL. 33166
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut on the hand) and had potential for more severe injuries (eye damage).

incident_description:
While baking a cake in the oven at 350 degrees with the timer set for 40 minutes. Twenty minutes into the bake mode she noticed that the cake had caught fire and the setting on the control panel went blank.

She removed the dish from the oven and put the fire out with water. When she attempted to power the oven in the off position it would not power off so she shut off the circuit breaker.

Allowing the range to cool down for a few minutes the circuit breaker was switched on and the oven powered back in the on position on broiler without being switched on. The range was then unplugged from the wall outlet.

The firm was contacted on 12/22/2011 and the consumer was advised that there was no recall involving her model number. She plugged the range back into the wall  outlet and the oven powered on in broiler mode again.

She has unplugged the range once again and it is still currently unplugged. She indicated that she fears that the range is a potential fire hazard and she intends on replacing it.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, and the oven malfunctioned repeatedly, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: While baking at 180 degrees F, the broiler turned on starting the food on fire. I could not turn off the oven and had to shut it off using the circut breaker. My kitchen, living room, and dining room now all smell strongly of smoke from the burning food.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke damage but no reported injuries or death.

incident_description:
I have 2 Frigidaire electric stove FEF326ABD. On several occasions I have tried to use the oven cleaner setting on both of them. Every time, the glass on the oven doors have shatters. So this is a feature that I can't use at all, in fear that I will again for like the 5th time, replace the glass.
Then there is the issue of the over and/or the broiler either not shutter off or turning on unless it is unplugged. This to me is the bigger issue. Both ovens are now at least 5 years old. This issue is something that comes and goes with both stoves and when I least expect it. I woke up the other day and the broiler was on. I didn't turn it on but it was on. Luckily, I was getting up but also there was nothing in it, no fire had started and it wasn't as hot. It may have just came on less then 20 minutes before I woke up.  I have tried to contact the stores about the issues and they tell me to contact the manufacturers. The manufacturers either take months to get back to me or tell me there is nothing they can do. I've tried looking to see if there was a recall on parts or the ovens as a whole and there is nothing.
justification: The incident involves repeated oven malfunctions (glass shattering, broiler turning on unexpectedly) with no reported injuries, but potential for harm exists.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore brushed stainless steel Elite glass top stove.  I have cut my arm and my finger on the inside of the door edge. The last incident was a cut on my finger that should have had stitches it was that deep.  
 The whole inside oven door edge on top and on the sides has an edge that is razor sharp. There is no smooth "lip" to protect anything that comes in contact with it.   This is definitely a manufacturer defect that the company will not back up after numerous attempts in contacting them.  
Model # 790.9611
justification: The incident caused a deep cut that should have had stitches, indicating a serious injury.

incident_description:
Our Cuisinart DC 1200 smoked, crackled and shot sparks out of the base while in the OFF position.  We have been making coffee in this machine for almost 1 year and have never had any issues.  If we would have been asleep or not at home, this product would have fully caught on fire and potentially burned our home down.  The toxic smoke trigged an asthma attack that required several treatments on my part to control .  

I called Cusinart and was told they they have not had any complaints regarding this machine.  I will be returning to Bed Bath and Beyond for a full refund and would suggest that someone/anyone look into a serious recall of this product.  Further research yields a large collection of consumers who have experienced  the same or similar issue a Cuisinart product- not just limited to the model I purchased.
justification: The incident caused an asthma attack requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests similar issues have been reported by other consumers, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: The Cuisinart DCC-1100 coffee maker which we bought last year, had a meltdown this morning.  Smell of an electric fire, smoked, popped, hissed and had we not unplugged it, it would have caused a fire.  I went on Amazon.com, searched for the product and found that there had been over 7 pages of reviews in which the coffee maker had done the same thing as mine.  Had we been out of town or away, I have no doubt that it would have caused major damage to my home.  This model is still offered for sale on amazon.com.
justification: The incident involved a coffee maker malfunctioning with potential to cause a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred. The high number of similar reviews suggests this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
The victim had finished using the hand held mixer and pushed the combioned eject and power button button to eject the blades.  Instead of ejuecting the blades, she turned the mixer on, fracturing the middle finger of her left hand and lacerating other fingers.  

The injuries resulted a visit on an urgent care facility which referred her to an emergency room.  Further bleeding required another ER visit the next day.  

Her description of the incident is attached along with the product information.
 
The victim has the product.
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured finger and lacerations requiring multiple medical visits, indicating an injury severity. The likelihood is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description: I was cooking Christmas dinner last night. I had a sweet potato casserole in the oven in a 9x13 glass Pyrex dish. I pulled the dish from the oven and placed it on the counter top to cool, and as soon as I sat it down, the dish exploded. Glass and hot food flew everywhere. Pieces landed on me, my sister in law, and her infant daughter that was walking through the kitchen. The glass and food landed in several of our other dishes, and pieces of glass stuck in the wall and in the tile on the floor. We had to trash most of our dinner, and spent about an hour making sure everything was cleaned up. This is an extremely unsafe product that needs to have something done. The flying glass could have badly injured my niece. I will never buy another piece of Pyrex glassware as long as I cook.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to multiple people, including an infant, but no deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have an LG electric Stove Model NumberLRE30451ST, Serial Number 609KMTL00025. It is a flat stove. one day my wife was cooking dinner and after she was done shut down the burners cleaned up and left to run errands. I came home several hours later and found the right front 14" burner glowing red hot. I immediately went to shut that burner control off but found that it wasnt even turned on according to the control panel. I pulled the stove out and unplugged the unit. Everything turned off. Upon letting the unit cool down I went to plug it back in and immiediately the 14" burner was glowing red hot. I unplugged the unit again. and contacted LG via. No response from them regarding the coorispondance.  I later unplugged (disconnected) that burner and plugged the stove back in. several months passed and now the other burners have intermitant controls and in most cases will not turn on. I am suspect of the burner control board at this time. Had we been gone on an extended vacation or left something on the stove the night of the incident a fire would have ensued, resulting thousands of dollars to the kitchen and house.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove burner that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: in the summer of 2010 I had my Maytag dishwasher repaired for the recall on it.  Then I had a recurrance yesterday.  The heating element does not turn off at the end of cycle and turns on any time the dishwasher is closed.  major fire hazard.  maytag said they already fixed the recall once and I would have to pay to fix again.  I dont think it was fixed properly, but they said I have to pay if i want it fixed.
justification: The heating element malfunction poses a major fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Brand new Whirlpool Quiet Partner 1
Model Number: DU1015XTXQ3

Incident:
Machine ran normal cycle with heated dry / high temp.
Burning smell and smoke emitted from Machine and then machine powered off.
Machine no longer turns on. 
This incident occurred during the very FIRST use of the machine.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and smoke, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I own a KitchenAid Signature series dishwashwer, Model kudhc03dtss10, with internal steam vent covers.  These covers are a plastic material that has a history of degrading and failing.  When they fail, a seal between the washer tub and the vent tube fails resulting in water leaving the washer tub.  This water passes through electrical components and on to the floor, resulting in damage.

This plastic component has failed repeatidly over the past year.  To date I have replaced the part 6 or 7 times.  The washwer is only two years old.  While the manufacturer serviced the unit while under warrenty, nothing was done to address this material system failure.

No matter how many times I replace this part, it will fail and I run the risk of electrocution each time a failure occurs.
justification: The repeated failure of the plastic component poses a risk of electrocution, which could result in injury or death, and the part has failed multiple times in a short period.

incident_description: We recently purchased an Anchor two-quart glass casserole dish with cover.  During its first use (cooking a bison and vegetable casserole) the cover exploded into hundreds of shards of glass in the oven.  The temperature was set at 350 degrees, and it is a conventional convection oven (wall mounted double ovens).  I photographed the oven full of glass and the dish.  We saved the pieces of glass.  I have concern that the gaskets around the door could have been damaged by the flying glass.
justification: The glass cover exploded, causing potential damage to the oven but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
I am reporting a case of shattering pyrex. This was a newer pyrex casserole dish, 9 x 13. I was baking chicken in a 400 degree oven. The pan came out of the cabinet and was at room temperature. The chicken had been out of the refrigerator for about 10 minutes before going in the oven. After just a few minutes in the oven (probably less than 10), the dish shattered into a million pieces.

I have consulted the pyrex website, and discovered there that you are apparently supposed to have the bottom of the casserole covered with some kind of liquid. Perhaps that would have made a difference; however, I have used my older pyrex (from the 1970s) to bake chicken in this way with no problems for decades. I am deeply concerned that people using the newer pyrex expect it to behave the same way as the older pyrex and they are setting themselves up for serious injuries.

The breakage happened on Dec. 17, 2011. The dish was about 2 years old, clear glass pyrex 9 x 13, no chips.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering in the oven, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is possible as it's a known issue with newer Pyrex under certain conditions.

incident_description: I have a brand new toaster oven.  I just plugged it in for the first time and got a huge electrical shock up my arm after touching the power button.  Note there is no 'ground' (3d) prong on the plug.
justification: The description mentions a 'huge electrical shock up my arm', indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: While lifting the stainless steel coffe pot with the attached black plastic handle, the handle separated from the pot.  This caused the hot coffee to spill.
justification: The incident involved a handle failure leading to spilled hot coffee, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: This evening while running the dishwasher, we were watching tv in the other room and heard  something obviously electrical arcing. Very loud, so I ran into the kitchen and found flames shooting out from under the dishwasher. I opened the dishwasher and the loud arcing sound stopped but the dishwasher (underside), was still on fire. I grabbed our fire extinguisher and put the fire out. I dissasembled the access plate on the front of the dishwasher and found the motor and all wiring had melted and burned in that area. If we had not been home, I can assure you we would have lost our home. The only thing I can think of we just recently had warranty work done on the dishwasher from Sears extended warranty service.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths, and the fire was successfully extinguished.

incident_description: Ran dishwasher in morning.  After cycle completed removed dishes, and refilled dishwasher over course of the day.  Closed door partially but never completely.  During dinner closed dishwasher completely.  After dinner refilled and closed door.  4-6 hours later noticed smell like dishwasher was cooking what we had for dinner.  Found granite countertop and dishwasher door very hot.  Inside melted most plastic pieces.  Discovered that this has happened to many GE Dishwashers and many have been recalled, but this product has not yet been recalled.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted plastic, hot surfaces) but no injury, and similar issues are known to occur with this dishwasher model.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern, 

Today 12/24/2011, my wife had left a pork roasting in the oven, I went to open the door to check out a smell and when I opened the door a fireball rushed out from the door, I fell down checking my face for burns as your GE oven shot out a fireball directly at my face. I am livid. The oven smells like burned plastic and we are not cooking on this thing due to the fear my brand new house my burn down. I want answers, one of my children could have opened that door. My eye brow got burned.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the eyebrow, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: coffe pot leaks water and shorted curcits cusasing smoke and blows efi. set programable coffee pot on the 26 dec to have coffee in the morning. woke to hear sizzleing  and popping and a acrid smell. when i discovered  that coffee pot was  shorting out and then fulted the EFI curcit..  water all over the kitchen from the coffee pot leaking it seems
justification: The incident involved a coffee pot leaking and causing electrical issues, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The glass door on the toaster oven completely shattered on its own. It was last used in the morning to toast some bagels. In the late afternoon, we heard it shatter from another room. We found chunks of glass in the oven, on the counter and on the floor. The door handle, that was attached to the top of the glass was laying on the counter.
justification: The glass door shattered on its own, causing no injury but creating a hazard with glass fragments.

incident_description:
While cooking a lasagna (approx. 20 min in to cooking time), the handle to my Kenmore Oven door fell off on one side. The oven door was too hot to touch, so I did not attempt to fix it at that time. About 10 minutes later, the entire handle fell off the door, followed by the stainless casing and the glass window. The door was hanging down and eventually bent back and hit the floor.  I had to have my husband get two sets of pliers to open the remainder of the oven door so that we could get the lasagna out and turn the oven off.  
 
It appears that the metal screws that attach the door to the handle melted the threads of the plastic door handle, hence the falling oven door.  Thank goodness we weren't in a cleaning cycle or that I didn't have my two year old in the kitchen with me.  

Truly scary and  the most frustrating thing is that Sears customer service repeatedly passed me on to a repair scheduler.  I think this is a truly dangerous situation that could have resulted in severe burns or injury.
justification: The incident involved a falling oven door but no injuries occurred, though the potential for severe burns or injury was noted.

incident_description: Front left burner locks on high will not shut off. This requires me to throttle temperature knob back and forth eventually it turns off. This is especially dangerous because you could rotate knob to off position and walk away and this burner is locked on its highest temperature.
justification: The burner locking on high poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
The front outside panel of my oven door honey-combed and shattered and fell on my wood floor
and into the oven drawer.
justification: The oven door panel shattered but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: Kenmore oven overheated and did not shut off had to turn off the breaker to shut the oven off. It got so hot that it broke my baking dish.
justification: The oven overheated and damaged a baking dish, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description: Our Bosch dishwasher caught fire while running. the control panel melted and burned, and filled the house with smoke and soot. three smoke detectors in the house went off, and I discovered the fire in time to extinguish the flames. The kitchen floor is ruined (burning plastic dripped on it) and the entire house and furniture has to be cleaned and deodorized.
justification: The dishwasher fire caused property damage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: On 12/24/2011, the oven door fell off and the glass front shattered. It is a Jenn-Air micro/oven combo, model JMW8530DAW, purchased 11/2003.  I have had four earlier service calls for defective hinges, as the door will not stay closed tightly.  One door hinge came loose in 4/2011, but I caught the door before it could twist the other hinge and or cause the other hinge to let go.  The oven door hinges have been an unacknowledged problem by Jenn-Air, now Maytag, or Whirlpool?  as evidenced by numerous blogs.  It has been a problem since the beginning and caused me to purchase extended warranties as I had a bad feeling about this unit.  I feel that the money spent on the ext. warranties is far less than I would have paid for the numerous (other) service calls needed.  But the reason for this report is the safety issue with the shattered glass.  Luckily, no one was hurt.    Jenn-Air (or current owner) should be held responsible to see that proper hinges and stronger, longer, receptacles are installed in these wall ovens.
justification: The oven door shattered but no one was injured, and the issue has occurred multiple times before.

incident_description: All the heating elements on my Whirlpool freestanding electric range (Model #: WFE361LVS) stopped functioning. The contols, clock and lights appeared to function normally. I unplugged the range and removed the terminal block cover to look for a loose connection between the power supply cord (Utilitech 50Amp, 4-wire range cord) and the terminal block. The ring connector on line 2 (red) was severly corroded and broken. The wire insulation and corresponding attachment point on the terminal block appeared charred and melted/deformed. Evidence of corrosion and melted insulation was visible on the line 1 (black) ring connector. The stove was in service of a single family household for 1 year and 4 months. Products purchased at local Lowe's. Power supply cord installed by Lowe's appliance delivery personnel.
justification: The incident involved severe corrosion and damage to electrical components, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her electric powered microwave made noise then smoked profusely and emitted a very foul odor. The magnetron of the product blew and was $175 to replace. The product is a self standing microwave. The product was on for about 45 seconds before it began to smoke. The consumer unplugged the microwave from the outlet and allowed it to burn itself out. The consumer cannot recall when she called the firm initially but has a repair date of 10/27/2007. 

The firm has sent her various parts for the product since the initial incident with the microwave; none of which are the part needed to repair the microwave. The consumer was subsequently sent a capacitator and credit towards her credit card for being sent incorrect parts. The consumer received the product as a gift. The consumer stated that her initial capacitator went up in smoke. The damage of the microwave did not spread to her home. The consumer no longer has the product and took the microwave to the habitat for humanity.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and emitted smoke, but no injury or property damage beyond the appliance itself occurred.

incident_description:
10/18/2011 Caller started dishwasher, left kitchen to go into family room and watch television.
Approximately five minutes after leaving kitchen she heard odd sound coming from kitchen, returned, saw smoke coming from control panel, smelled burning and was rushing toward dishwasher to turn it off when a six inch burst of flames shot out from the control panel which as she pulled the dishwasher door down went back in.

She pulled the plug to the dishwasher out of the outlet.

She and huband opened all the windows, doors to rid their house of the burning smell.
Caller's model is on one of the releases but not the serial number and so is not recalled, however she is asking that her model and serial number be placed on recall for fear of fire hazard.

She would ask that the public be made aware and that her dishwasher be replaced at manufacturer expense because she is also afraid of a potential continued fire risk.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with flames and smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The oven was baking at 350 degrees. We noticed that the food item seemed to be burning. We turned the oven "off", but the heating element did NOT turn off (still glowing bright orange for a couple of minutes after the oven was "off"). We removed the burned food item from the oven, and placed it on the top burner area to cool. A few seconds later, the glass baking dish shattered (exploded) - clearly it was extremely hot. 
The oven heating element was clearly still ON.
I went to the circuit breaker box in the garage and turned off the electric circuit to the range, which of course allowed the oven to turn off and start to cool down.
I took a picture of the exploded dish if it is of interest to you.

This is clearly a safety problem, because the inability of the oven to control its temperature could cause a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have caused a fire, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his freezer on bottom of refrigerator has an internal lights at the top of the refrigerator that will stay on when the refrigerator is closed. The light bulb wattage is unknown. The consumer stated that she would open his refrigerator find that his refrigerator has a burning smell and also find the light bulbs are very hot. The consumer felt that this issue could develop into a fire hazard. 

The consumer stated that this caused the light fixture to melt and there is now a brown burn make surrounding the light bulb housing. The consumer has yet to contact the firm or the retailer. The consumer found that there is no light switch to turn off the lights. The consumer has not called the fire department after the incident or called her insurance company about her concerns. The consumer did not sustain any property damage. The consume stated that there is no exterior damage to the refrigerator. The consumer was not injured by the product. The consumer stated that similar models like his were included in a class action lawsuit.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard with no injury or property damage reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the evidence of melting and burn marks, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
We have a one to two year old  Cuisinart, Brew Central, 12 cup coffee maker.  Serial number 00720h.  We made coffee as usual this morning, poured 2 cups and left the room.  When we returned to the kitchen about an hour later the coffee maker was making odd sputtering sounds.  [REDACTED] picked up the pot and we saw smoke coming out from under the heating element.  We immediately unplugged it and brought it outside.  The movement increased the amount of smoke emitting from the machine.  We wound up dousing it with a hose.  Yes, some steam occurred due to the water hitting the hot elements, but there was quite a bit of grey smoke too.  It was quite a surprise.  

We are convinced that had we not returned to the room when we did that this machine would have started a fire!  It sits under wooden upper cabinets in the kitchen!   

Should I deliver this machine somewhere for further investigation?
justification: The incident involved smoke emission and potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it was an isolated event with no prior reports mentioned.

incident_description: I set the Anchor Hocking 2L glass baking dish on my kitchen counter.  Both the counter and the baking dish were at room temperature.  I microwaved a bag of "steam-fresh" vegetables in their plastic ventilated bag, as directed, and then let that bag stay in the microwave for about 45 seconds after the microwaving process had been completed.  I took the bag of vegetables out of the microwave and set them down inside the Anchor Hocking glass baking dish, and walked a few steps away to the kitchen sink.  Seconds later, there was an explosion that was as loud as if a loud firecracker had exploded.  My husband was in the other room and jumped up and ran into the kitchen.  I was still standing speechless looking at what had just happened.  The glass baking dish had just exploded all over my kitchen--the counters, floor, food that was being prepared, dog's dishes, the living room carpet, and all over the stovetop.  There were large shards and tiny slivers.  When I stopped shaking, I realized how very fortunate I had been in not being hit and possibly badly injured by the flying glass.  We cleaned it up--a process that took well over an hour.  I painstakingly washed the floor and counters and threw out the entire turkey dinner I had been preparing.  I am just lucky I did not lose my eyesight, or suffer other major injuries.  I have saved the exploded glass in a plastic bag and intend to contact Anchor Hocking, in addition to filing this report.  I also let CVS on Del Webb Blvd. here in Las Vegas know about the incident, although I doubt they will pull the product from their shelves.
justification: The incident involved a glass baking dish exploding, but no injuries occurred, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description:
Dear CPSC:
On 10/5/11, I mixed a little cool milk and an egg in a room temperature, 2 cup, Pyrex measuring
cup that I purchased about 2 years ago. After emptying the cup, I placed it upside-down in a
cool, half-full dishwasher (which would not be run until it was full). Twenty minutes later, while
checking the cornbread in the oven across the room I heard a violent explosion of glass behind
me. I looked around, expecting to see the window there smashed, but all was in order. Upon
opening the dishwasher I discovered every part of it was filled with countless, 1/2 inch fragments
of glass. The only part of the measusring cup that was still recognizable was a small piece of the
handle. Although I removed all the glass accessible, even vacuuming out every bit I couldn't see
or pick up by hand, some of the pieces of glass had been flung through the grid at the bottom of
the dishwasher and damaged its mechanism (costing $280 in repairs). Considering that had this
spontaneous explosion taken place 20 minutes earlier while I was using the cup, I was lucky - I
might have been hit in the face by the full force of the explosion, and probably in the eyes. I took
photos of the inside of the dishwasher, but did not keep the fragments, not wanting to have such
sharp bits around.
A few days later I reported the incident to the manufacturer, World Kitchen, on their email site.
Enclosed find copies of their reply and my answers to their questions. Although I was
disappointed that they were not interested in restoring my out-of-pocket loss, I am even more
disturbed by the dismissive attitude they showed, considering the dangerous product they are
responsible for. I send this report to your office so that if there are any other such incidents
reported to you this company may be called to account for their callous indifference.
I have been keeping house for 56 years, and using Pyrex products for longer than that; never
have I even broken one of them; nor have I ever heard of one exploding from friend or
accaquaintence. One must suspect a recent flaw in the modem manufacturing process of Pyrex
brand kitchen ware. I hope they will soon be called to account.
Enclosed find three photos of the inside of the dishwasher, taken minutes after the explosion.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.  Consumer Added: Apparently I was not clear about the explosion of my Pyrex measuring cup.  The cup was merely resting in the cool dishwasher; I did not turn on the dishwasher between the time I placed the cup there and its exploding.  It could easily have been sitting on the counter for the 20 minutes.  The dishwasher had no effect on the cup, but was damaged by the explosion.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex measuring cup exploding without causing injury, but resulting in property damage, indicating a rare occurrence with no harm to individuals.

incident_description: Was LUCKILY home sick from work yesterday....awakened by the dogs....house was filled with a hazy smoke and horrible smell. Sent the dogs into yard and tried to find the source...eventually zeroed in on our Whirlpool side-by-side fridge....horrible smell and could hear a crackling sound. Immediately turned off main breaker, pulled fridge from wall, opened windows and doors. After enough smoke had cleared, with the help of google, i removed the panel off back of fridge to discover that what I now know was the compressor start relay was melted and had obviously been on fire. While I feel EXTREMELY lucky that I just happened to be home at the time, it is terrifying to find that this has been a common problem with this brand. Could you let me know of any recourse I may have with Whirlpool? Only a minute percentage of ppl will contact you, but google the term "Whirlpool refrigerator fire"
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injury or death, but significant potential for harm.

incident_description:
This is a "duty to defend". I have purchased a tea kettle from what I thought was a
reputable catalog company called: Ginny's in Madison, WI. The first time I used the tea
kettle on my flattop stove, the water burned out of it and when I went to remove the
kettle, the handled had melted offl After grabbing hot pads to remove, the tea kettle had
partially melted onto my stove damaging it. I am furnishing you pictures to prove what
had happened. I could have been burned with the handles & lid melting!! Their
company says the bottom of kettle was not damaged but I have pictures to prove
different.
It would cost me $500 to replace my stove top! I am on a fixed income and this company
should be held liable for their product. I appreciate due process on this issue.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning product causing property damage but no reported injuries, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but do occur with faulty products.

incident_description: Pre-heated oven to 400 to make a pizza.  Once pre-heated placed my pizza in oven, about 10 mins later I heard a beep and went back into the kitchen to investigate.  Stove was showing error code E2 F3.  Pizza was burnt.  Attempted to turn off oven and it would not shut off,  even when all dials and window indicated product was off.  Top burner (broiler) was red hot.  Had to unplug oven to get it off.  Even when plugging  oven back in the broiler turned on my itself.  Mod # 665.9580400
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing a burnt pizza and required unplugging to turn off, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: twice in the last two days our Kenmore electric range model 790.95662102 has gone onto maximum heat when set at 250 and 350 deg. respectively.  Then tonight it would not turn off at all without using the circuit breaker.  I see many models are included in a recall for doing the exact thing ours is doing, however our model does not appear to be on the list..
justification: The electric range malfunctioning and reaching maximum heat unexpectedly poses a potential safety hazard, though no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The consumer is unsure of where and when the range was purchased it was in the home prior to her moving in, in 2006.

 While baking in the oven at 425 degrees for 6 minutes when she smelled smoke and went into the kitchen to find that the pizza that she placed in the oven was burnt to a crisp.

She made several attempts to power the oven in the off position but it would not power off . She then powered the circuit breaker in the off position and waited briefly before powering it back on. WHen the oven would heat up to an unexpected temperature the kitchen would get extremly hot.

 She then noticed that the oven was switched to off position but started to heat up. She powered the circuit breaker in the off position and left it in that position over night. 

When she would need to use the range (cook top or oven) she would power the circuit breaker in the on position and when not in use she would power the circuit breaker in the off position .

The firm was contacted on 9/21/2011 where she was advised that she could have a technician come out to the home to take a look at the range.  The consumer has decided to discard of the range and it has been replaced.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused smoke and overheating, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Food processor began chopping when the safety lid was completely removed.  cut off fingers.

Walmart is now denying any liability as the seller and telling us to contact manufacturer in China.
justification: The incident resulted in the loss of fingers, which is a severe injury.

incident_description:
In October I bought a GE Profile gas range model # PGB 918 DEMWW. The knobs on the front are so easy to push in and turn that just walking past and brushing them will turn them on and gas will leak.  I have done this several times just by brushing past them or by bumping them while trying to get items out of the microwave or cupboards overhead.  Our plumber was here two days ago working on the sink and bumped them and did not realize it until my son came into the room and smelled gas.

This is a huge safety issue to me.  When I contacted GE for advice they said the only thing I could do was to take the knobs off.  This is not an acceptable long term solution to what I consider to be a design problem. No one has been hurt yet, but we may be if we are not careful.

Thanks for your help.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage due to easily activated knobs, posing a safety risk, but no injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description: Made 4 cups of coffee; left one cup in the pot to stay warm on the hot plate.  While drinking the coffee, heard loud crackling noises and upon looking at the coffee maker saw grey smoke pouring from the bottom of the machine.  Terrible electrical burning smell.  Unplugged it and placed it outside where it continued to smoke for a few minutes.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from the coffee maker, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While using the right front and left burner for an half hour on a medium low setting  when there was popping sound and smoke began to pour from the back of the control panel along with flames. 

The lights in the home began to flicker so he went to pull the range from the wall and unplugged it and then powered the circuit breaker in the off position.  Once the appliance was unplugged from the wall outlet. 

The firm was contacted on 12/8/2011 and the consumer was advised that his model number was affected by the recall (See Release#09-333) and they would send out the replace parts for the recall. 

The consumer  informed the representative that he spoke with (name not provided) that there was a fire in the rear of the range and would they be responsible to make repairs to that as well.

The consumer was advised that when the technician comes out to make the repairs for the recall that if they are able to diagnose the problem with the range it would not be covered under the recall and he would be responsible to pay for the parts and labor. 


The consumer was informed by the representative to wait for the parts to arrive and then call back to schedule for a technician to come out. He will leave the range unplugged. 

There are minor smoke damages to the wall the range was on du to the smoke comming from the back of the range.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke damage but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the issue was linked to a known recall.

incident_description: I woke up from falling asleep on the couch and smelled something burning (around 1:00am) . I went into the kitchen and the smell got stronger. I looked at the diswasher and saw an orange glow coming out of the bottom of the door of the dishwasher. I went over to the dishwasher and the lights were going off (dishwasher shutting off and on also) and on. I cancelled the washing process and let the water run out. I opened the dishwasher and smelled a strong burning odor. I went down and throw the breaker off. I stayed up till about 1:30am to make sure there was no fire. I went to bed untill about 2:30am to check to see if there was any fire or heat and found nothing at this time.  This is a Whirlpool gold dishwasher model GU1100XTLQ1 serial number FP3714818. This was on Friday December 2nd around 1:00am. At this time I am afraid to use this appliance.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with visible signs of malfunction but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says the upper left burner sometimes does not turn off when being turned off.  The consumer says he can get the burner to turn off by hitting the knob on and off a few times.  The consumer says this poses a real fire hazard.  The consumer says he contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not on recall.  The consumer has brand and hazard for product listed under Release # 09-333, but his model number is not on the recall list.
justification: The consumer says the burner sometimes does not turn off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: I was washing a newly purchased Hamilton Beach slow cooker before using.  When I washed the lid I slid my hand over the inside of the lid to rinse it off and received a very deep cut approximately2 1/2 inches long to my left hand.  The screw holding the knob on the lid was extremely sharp on the inside of the lid and caused the cut.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such injuries from sharp screws are not common but possible.

incident_description:
Lights in the refrigerator melted housing.
Latest fault lights stay on and heat interior.  They do not shut off with door switchs closed.
Had to remove bulbs so unit would cool.
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator but no injury or death occurred. The issue is possible to recur if the fault lights are not fixed.

incident_description:
Woke up to a hot refrigerator with melted housing unit for dome lights. Our food was hot and the whole inside smelled of burned plastic. We tested to make sure the doors had closed, and they had. The lights would not turn off, and the plastic was melting off the screws. So I had my husband unscrew the bulbs with an oven mitt, as they were on fire HOT. We had to pull off the melted plastic cover. I am still scared because those lighting units are still active.HELP!! 
Of course our warranty was up last year, so I knew that I could only lodge a complaint and hope that someone could help us get these dangerous units out of homes. After I contacted Sears, We were told it was Faulty wiring by the help line of Sears. Then they proceeded to disconnect us when we asked to make a recall complaint. Then after a third call, I was given the "Corporate Office's Number". WRONG, I was given KMart's number. The lady there, proceeded to inform me that she was being so helpful but that I had to call [REDACTED]. When that number didn't even work, I contacted the CPSC. Thank Goodness. I just want this dangerous thing out of my house, and a safe Fridge in it's place. How hard is that? This thing needs to be recalled. Thank Goodness we were home. I cannot imagine what we would've come home to, if we went on Vacation. I WAS a fan of Sears and Kenmore until this incident. I hope my Faith in them and their quality of care will be restored with this report. I just wish they would've helped when I gave them more than enough chances.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator with melted parts and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While baking a  dish in the oven at 325 degrees  within a minute of use the food caught fire and the oven would not power in the off position when it was being switched.  The dish was removed from the oven and the fire was put out and the fire department  was contacted. The home filled with an electrical burning odor and smoke .

The Webster Fire Department in Webster Massachusetts came out to the home  and pulled the range from the wall an unplugged it from the wall unit. They were also able to measure the degrees from the back of the range with a  special thermometer and the reading was at 700 degrees. 

The Fire Department stayed at the home until the temperature went down and returned to normal. The consumer was advised not to use the range until they could contact the firm for further assistance. 

On the same date of the incident when the fire department left the consumer plugged the range back into the wall outlet and without being switched on the oven powered on. He then unplugged the range and left it in that manner.

The firm was also contacted on the same date of the incident and they offered to send out a service technician to take  a look  at the unit but the consumer declined because he  is concerned with the appliance posing as a fire hazard . He has decided that he will replace the range. They couldn't come to 12/8/11.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke, but no injuries were reported, and the situation was controlled without further damage.

incident_description: My daughter suffered an injury from a Maytag french door refrigerator. As she was opening the bottom drawer out, the handle came off and cut her left arm. I contacted Maytag and they sent out a technician to my home. The technician wants to put the broken handle back on even though I have expressed my concern of this incident repeating itself and the handle comming off again due to stripped holes on the bottom door. He didn't care and is going to simply put the broken handle back on. They have completely disregarded the fact that this part inflicted injury to my child and simply have expressed that they just don't care. Now my daughters arm is cut and my fridge is broken. Maytag should be ashamed of themselves.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the child's arm, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood of recurrence is high (4) due to the stripped holes and the technician's disregard for the issue.

incident_description: Fire on relay switch at bottom of whirlpool refrigerator
justification: A fire on a relay switch is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Heard a "pop" sound from our dishwasher.  Thereafter noticed a burning smell and saw smoke emitting from the control panel.  Could not turn off the dishwasher via the control panel or by opening the dishwasher door.  Had to flip the circuit breaker to get the machine to stop.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such electrical faults are not common but do happen occasionally.

incident_description: The rivot came out of pancake dispenser and could have fallen into the batter causing a choking hazard.  The small metal piece fell into her garbage disposal.   She says its a tiny piece at the top of the dispenser and is not supposed to come out.  The consumer took it back to the retailer.
justification: The rivet came out but did not cause injury, and the consumer returned the product, indicating no harm occurred.

incident_description:
On Friday night, I was in my living room when I heard a loud sound of breaking glass in the kitchen. Vlhen I went to investigate, I found a few small pieces of glass just inside a cupboard
door. I store Pyrex baking dishes on the shelf in this cabinet: an llx7 nested inside a 9x13 with an 8x8 sitting gently atop both of them. (They have been stored in this way for decades with no problem.)
Now the 11x7 baking dish had shattered spontaneously and small pieces of glass were scattered throughout the cabinet, although most of the llx7 pan was still resting inside the 9x13 with numerous "fault lines" throughout, as well as several missing chunks of glass. The 8x8 pan On top had not shifted and was stili in its usual slightJy angied position atop the other two.
None of these three baking dishes had been used in more than a week. The cabinet is next to the oven, but it hadn't been turned on for three days. The temperature in the kitchen at the time was 72 degrees.
I remembered reading an article about problems with heated Pyrex, and when I googled "exploding Pyrex" it referenced the story in the January 2011 Consumer Reports. All of the examples cited in that article --and all of the countless complaints on Google --referred to breakage occuning when the pans are heated. Are there other instances of spontaneous breakage of unheated pans? This was very scary. I am considering replacing all ofthe Pyrex in the house. But I'm wondering if pieces marked "Pyrex by Corning" (which I know are 30 to 45 years old) are still considered to be safe to use.
justification: No injury occurred, but the spontaneous shattering of the Pyrex dish constitutes an incident.

incident_description:
Consumer wanted to report that her medium sized Pyrex glass baking pan exploded in her oven. She stated that she had the dish in the oven to heat up spinach and water at 350 degrees for about 15 minutes. The consumer did point out that the oven was on for a total of 30 minutes in a pre-heat cycle. The consumer was in kitchen and opened the oven door. The Pyrex dish exploded and glass forcefully came out of the oven and some shards embedded themselves into her vinyl floor tile. Luckily no one was injured. 

The consumer was off to the side of the oven door when she opened the oven door and was out of harmÃÂs way. The consumer did not call her insurance company about her flooring. The consumer has a typical oven with a boiler pan underneath. The consumer could hear the shards falling into her broiler. The consumer has not called the retailer. 

The Pyrex dish is clear. The consumer emailed the firm today to inform them of what happened and has not gotten a response. The consumer felt it was imperative to report this issue to the CPSC. The product has no signs of damage prior to the incident. The size of the dish was just smaller than a 9X13 and was clear. At the time of the incident she did not have the dish lined with aluminum foil.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, causing glass shards to embed in the floor, but no one was injured.

incident_description: Dishwasher GE Profile Model PDW9980L00SS, SN RL860782B about 5 years old malfunctioned.  Heating element kicked on and did not shut off.  Was detected by my husband who was up late that night when he smelled burning plastic.  It had been on for about 3 hours.  When discovered we left the door ajar and the next day the cleaners closed it and it started overheating again.  Thank God my oldest son came home about 2 hours later and again the insides were melting more.  The lower water sprayer that goes around completely melted into the lower element.  If it had not been detected I am sure the house would have burned down.
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused significant damage and posed a serious fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
While baking apple crisp in the baking dish set on 45 minutes when the glass dish exploded within 40 minutes in the oven the range is electric. The apple crisp and dish were both placed in the oven while they were both at room temperature. 

The glass sides exploded into  little pieces while the bottom of the dish  exploded in six large shards of glass. There were no injuries reported.

 She estimates using the pan at least once a month. She has not contacted the firm but plans on doing so.


She would like to see the firm place a warning label on their products to prevent any injuries with it exploded.
justification: The glass dish exploded but no injuries were reported, making it an incident without injury. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the monthly usage and the unexpected nature of the event.

incident_description: The coffee maker (47214) brews coffee and after it comes out the bottom. My grandaughter was here at my house and it did that and her hand got a lil burned nothing major cuz I was able to pull her but coffee gets extremely hot enough to burn someone. Not safe at all. It's happened before but didn't really worry me until my granddaughter was here. Plus I went online and saw a lot of people with the same problem. I've tried contacting Hamilton beach at 1-800-672-5872   and no luck getting to a representative.
justification: The coffee maker caused a minor burn to the grandaughter, which is an injury but not a death or serious injury.

incident_description:
consumer sent 3 letter to manufacturer about gas Jenn-Air cooktop.
December 13,2009
Jenn-Air Brand
Home Appliances
553 Benson Road
Benton Harbor, MI 49022-2692
Dear Jenn-Air,
Last year we finished a major refurbishing of our home here in Helena, Montana. As part of the updating, my wife decided to covert from an electric Jenn-Air to a gas unit, which all of her friends said was more cook friendly. The new gas Genn-Air looks nice, and works fine, but I do think you have a major and serious safety design flaw in the unit. In my opinion, the igniters should start operating as soon as the control knob is turned, as opposed to having to go a full counter clockwise
turn to get to the "ignite" position. We have had a few circumstances where the knob was turned on, but not turned enough to the ignite position (fast enough) to avoid some very burnt eyelashes. I do sincerely consider this a serious design safety flaw, which can be very easily taken care of by having ignitors come on prior to gas being released. Is there a kit available to

incident_description:
This incident occured at my mother's home on December 9th, 2011.  She had a large countertop microwave which sits in a built in wall unit.   I, Her daughter, was visiting her for dinner, we had started cooking and my mother placed a microwaveable baking potato into her microwave.   This potato was purchased at her local grocery, individually wrapped in a plastic for the specific purpose to be placed in a microwave.  My mother placed the potato into the microwave and set the cooking time as indicated on the potato's label.  
After a short time I, her daughter, smelled an odor, thinking it was just the odor of the plastic baking in the microwave.  A few more minutes went by when I glanced over to the microwave I noticed smoke lifting off of the top of the microwave which had a strong electrical odor.  The microwave outside walls were too hot to touch and at that time I pulled the plug from the wall, noticing that the plug and the wall were not hot, which indicated to me there was not a problem with the outlet or cord.
I needed to get this microwave out of the house.  Since the microwave was too hot to touch I ran to the basement to get something to cover it with, I found a blanket.  I covered the microwave with the blanket and carried it to the garage to get the strong odors out of the house.  In thinking again I needed to get this out of the house completely and asked my mother to open the garage door.  As she was doing that she is telling me she sees fire inside the microwave as I was holding it.  I carried it outside and placed it in the her gravel driveway.  The moment I set it down and removed the blanket the microwave burst into flames.  Once I realized it was faraway from the house and posed no problem to the house or us we returned to the kitchen to find a small fire burning into the shelf.  That was easily put out with a wet dish cloth, but it did burn down about 1/4 inch into the shelf.  
I then took a pitcher of water outside and slowly doused the flames.  The microwave was left outside and is still outside.
Evaluating the situation it scared both of us.  If I a 60 year old healthy daughter had not been there and this happened when my 83 year old mother was alone she would have a terrible incident on her hands and had her home on fire.  This microwave was too heavy for her to move.
justification: The incident involved a microwave fire causing property damage but no injuries, and such events are unlikely but possible with improper use or malfunction.

incident_description:
Kenmore 790 range went into very unsafe full heating mode following about an hour of operation at 325F setting.  The oven lower element stuck on in full heating mode and the oven began to get very hot (some cookies were scorched at very beginning of event).  A minute or two later, the control panel began to beep and an error code of F1 was displayed.  The lower element was fully on (very red), my brownies had turned completely black, and some food debris/ash on the bottom was near ignition.  Control panel did not respond.  Immediately cut power at the breaker.  Smoke filled the kitchen and other rooms of the house, but no damage was done.

Oven should have a shutdown rather than a error code display during a runaway heating event.  With 5kW of heating, the oven and surroundings could have easily caught fire, with very bad property damage or injury to my family.

Similar incidents are described on various internet bulletin boards including Mysears boards, it does not appear that Sears has recalled this item or initiated any informal repair.  Considering the danger of fire with this type of failure, this is quite disturbing, I do not plan to use this appliance again.

Oven is visibly scorched at the vent locations at the door.

Oven remains very hot after an hour.

Model 790.95204103 purchased about 5 years ago at Sears.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction that could have led to fire or injury, but no actual injury or property damage occurred. Similar incidents reported online suggest this is a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: My wife returned home from work on Friday, December 16 to the smell of smoke in the house.  She searched the home for the location of the smell and was unable to pinpoint exactly where it was coming from.  When I came home I immediately received a strong smoke/burning odor when I walked in the door.  The smell was strongest in our kitchen.  I searched the kitchen and pulled the refrigerator out and saw ash and a burn mark on our kitchen tile.  I immediately unplugged the refrigerator.  I called the fire department to come over to take a report as it appeared the fire was out.  I pulled the back cover off the refrigerator and found more ash, burned wires and burned electronics mounted to the compressor.  I used a spray bottle to spray everything down with water.  The fire department took information from the refrigerator for their report and left.  I am glad that we had a ceramic tile floor because any other type of flooring may have ignited and caused a house fire.  I did some research and found that this is a common problem with Whirlpool, Kenmore, and Maytag refrigerators of this vintage.  It appears that a recall was issued for the Maytags and possibly the Whirlpools, but not the Kenmore.  Sears may want look at recalls on these units, because it very easily could have been a house fire.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual fire or injury, but the situation could have escalated under different conditions.

incident_description:
Hello,
I would like to start out by stating that I am now aware of the hazard of heating soda lime glass bakeware directly on the stove, and openly admit that I did, in fact, attempt to heat my glass bakeware in this manner today.  

HOWEVER, I have many Pyrex baking dishes that I've inherited, which I have used dozens of times both in the oven and on the stovetop with no issues.  Today, however, I removed a meatloaf from the oven at 350 degrees, intending to remove the meat and make a pan-gravy in a relatively new Pyrex dish.  I allowed the pan to cool so I could remove the meat, and then reheated the drippings, added flour and seasoning, and then began to whisk in some broth.  After a few minutes of whisking, the pan suddenly shattered all over my oven, counter, and floor.  I can only attribute my not getting hot gravy or glass on myself to my being able to jump backwards while the explosion occurred in the opposite direction from me.

I visited the Pyrex website after the incident, where I saw a new safety campaign led by [REDACTED] to highlight the precautions to take while using their glassware.  This is in fact rather new.  The last time I researched Pyrex pieces on their website, no such campaign was being advertised, and I did not know that Pyrex started using Soda Lime Glass rather than the far-superior Borosilicate glass.  I am tremendously disappointed that consumers were not informed of this switch and the new safety campaign regarding the Soda Lime Glass.  As someone who watches both local and national news every single day, I am disappointed that this information was not made available by Pyrex or the CPSC, or even by Consumer Reports, who tested many types of glass bakeware.  Perhaps even a shared effort to mail a postcard to "Resident" at every address in the US would have been helpful, as consumers such as myself who have been using Pyrex for years would not think to check their website to see if they have changed the type of glass they use.

I implore the CPSC to look into this issue further, encourage the manufacturers of glass bakeware to use the safer, far-superior Borosilicate glass, and actively attempt to inform ALL consumers (not just via internet) of the NEW dangers with their products now being made of Soda Lime Glass and not Borosilicate Glass.  Remember that those consumers who have used Borosilicate for years, such as myself, were not aware that Soda Lime was substituted and it is more likely to shatter during the same activities where Borosilicate glass does NOT shatter.

Thank you for your time.
justification: The incident involved the shattering of glass bakeware but no injury occurred, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as similar incidents have been reported but are not extremely common.
