incident_description: I have had numerous problems with this range. The most recent incidents are the most disturbing. This range is a safety hazard and should NOT be on the market.  On Thanksgiving 2011 I put my turkey in the oven at 350 degrees - after 45 minutes there was a series of beeps, and when I got to the kitchen it was filled with smoke and my turkey was on fire. The oven was flashing a code F10 which I know to be a runaway temperature code as this is not the first time I have seen this code.  This is, however, the first time I had food in the oven when the temperature has 'runaway'.  Immediately I turned the oven off, however, it would NOT go off.  My husband had to turn it off at the breaker to get the oven to go off.  Thank goodness we were home at the time - or this would have burned our home down. Of course, our dinner was ruined as a result and I will not use the oven again after this incident.  A few days later I was using the stove top to make a marinara sauce. I went to turn the marinara down and put it on simmer select. As soon as I pushed the simmer select button there was a loud pop and flash. Sauce shot through the air and was all over everything - including the ceiling and me which caused burns on my arms.  I am thankful I was not touching the pot at the time - as it had to be an electrical shock to cause the sauce to explode out of the pot and all over my kitchen.  If someone were touching the pot they would have been electrocuted.  On several occasions I have been burned by this oven as the entire oven gets blistering hot when using it. Additionally, the handle to the oven door is poorly designed as it has fallen off the door on several occasions. This is a safety hazard as well - especially when you are trying to open the oven door at the time the handle fails. Prior to purchasing this oven we had owned a Kenmore for 20+ years and were very happy with it - I am familiar with how a Kenmore oven should behave.  This appliance is a danger to everyone and should not be allowed on the market.  Sears needs to recognize this fact and remedy this dangerous situation.  I would like for Sears to pick up this oven and reimburse me.
justification: The incident describes multiple injuries (burns from sauce explosion and hot oven) and a high risk of electrocution, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated occurrences of safety hazards suggest a likelihood of 4 (likely).

A catastrophic failure of a Cook TekÃÂ®, Magna WaveÃÂ, Induction, Single Position, Drop In-Cook Top stove, model MCD 3500 occurred on 10/07/2011 at [REDACTED].

Furthermore, the manufacturer speculated that something heavy must have been placed on the surface or that someone may have stepped on the cook top causing it to break.

After going to the emergency room and being immediately referred to a hand surgeon, I found out I had severed a tendon in my wrist.   I had to have surgery to repair the severed tendon.  This occurred in my Arizona home while down there for the winter.  

This glass was made by Libbey.   It has a very, very thick base.   I know several other people with the same glasses.   They have reported similar breakages, even having the bottom fall off when ice is dropped into the glass.  (Actually, this happened to me a few days before my accident but I was unaware of other breakages at the time so I continued to use the glasses.)   We have emails describing instances of breakage that others have experienced.   We received these emails after others heard of my accident.  I can forward the emails to you if you'd like.

Although I did not purchase it through Amazon.com, I have since found very similar looking Libbey glasses on the Amazon.com website.   There are several reviews (1 and 2 stars) that describe sudden breakages.  

In addition, my husband visited a restaurant on the east coast and was shocked to have the waiter set down a glass of water in the SAME style glass.   My husband inquired about the manufacturer and the restaurant's experience.  The waiter laughed and said "They break all the time.   Sometimes we set the glass on the table and it breaks in two pieces and water is all over."  We have this gentleman's business card (i.e. contact information) if you would like.

Last, but not least, a Libbey glass bowl was recalled last month.  It is on your website, along with a picture.   It has the SAME thick base as the glass that I am reporting to you.

I still have the broken glass (and a couple unbroken glasses) if you need them to test.  These glasses are an EXTREME laceration hazard.

incident_description: Dishwasher smelled of burned rubber or plastic about 6 months ago.  In the last few weeks it has been running for an extremely long time - maybe 4-6 hours for a cycle.  Did some online research and found a common problem of burned circuit boards for Bosch dishwashers.  Opened the unit up and found wires melted into plastic parts.  Opened up circuit board holder and found a burned solder joint on the board just like the rest.  Unit is not part of the recall but had  exact  same problem as the recalled units.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning dishwasher with burned components, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My dishwasher caught fire during the late evening hours.  We had started the dishwasher close to 1130 pm.  At 12:30 am I was awoken from my sleep to a very bad smell of smoke in the house.  I went down stairs to find the dishwasher was warm and charred around the upper right hand corner.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke and charring, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Running the dishwasher and was ready to walk out the door.  Heard a noise -- opened the dishwasher and water was squirting out all over... could not stop it..... smelled smoke.   Finally after hitting all the control buttons, finally stopped.   I am so fortunate that I was home when this happened.  

Called for service  and didn't try using the dishwasher at all.

Service man did inform me that the control panel of the dishwasher did smoke and burnt parts of the dishwasher.   Would cost me $777.43 to fix it.  Purchased the dishwasher from Sears in October, 2004.  Also was charged $129.00 for them to come out.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing water leakage and smoke, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: My 13x9 Pyrex baking dish exploded.  I was roasting carrots in the oven at 375 degrees.  When cooking was finished, I pulled out the dish and placed it on the stove top.  About 10 minutes later, I heard a loud crack sound from the living room.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but no injury was reported, making it an incident without harm. Such incidents are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description: My Frigidaire Model FEFL79FCB left front burner will on occasion not turn off.  The burner continues to heat and glow when the switch is turned off.  We need to turn off the power to the range at the breaker box to prevent overheating and possible house fire.
justification: The burner not turning off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Caller was referred by Lombard Fire Dept after he explained to them that new gas range purchased October 1st, 2011 from Grant's Appliances & Electronics in Downers Grove, [REDACTED] mgr & salesrep.

Range was delivered on October 3rd around 1:30 - 2:00.

Wife began cooking same day around 4:00pm October 3rd, 2011, after approximately 30 - 40 minutes when she called for her husband, asked him to touch the knobs on the range.

The knobs which were so hot that he had to withdraw his hands. 

Husband called Frigidaire who referred him to D&S, he called them, tech came out October 10th, 2011, tech said he had to leave but he returned around October 12th although techs paper shows the 10th only.  When he came out on the 12th, he wrote, " Ran for 40 minutes, 165 degrees behind the knobs, allowable 150 degrees".

Consumer contacted Frigidaire again and tech was sent for 3rd visit but this time tech came from Diamond Factory, he told wife that it was a flaw in the system of the design that he would not write that on the ticket and wrote only that the range could normally go up to 165 degrees & nothing they can do about it

Caller noted that if grandchildren were to touch the knobs at any time they could become burned.

Consumer had contacted Electrolux, spoke with [REDACTED] who told him that after 3 tech visits then range would be replaced.

Consumer called Electrolux again today, spoke [REDACTED]  who is going to "try" but she doesn't believe that there is anything they can do.

Caller is reporting as a safety hazard siting that user or any children nearby could be burned.

His wife is afraid to use the range and would request that the manufacturer replace range with a different model at manufacturer expense.
justification: The knobs on the gas range become dangerously hot during use, posing a burn risk, especially to children, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I purchased a Cuisinart coffee maker Model DCC 1200 (Serial #91204) approximately 1 year ago.  I brewed coffee yesterday and approximately 30 minutes after brewing the coffee, I heard a crackling sound coming from the coffee maker.  When I walked into the kitchen, I found the coffee maker was smoking and on fire and had a horrible burning electrical smell.  I immediately unplugged it and took it outside.  From reading other online reports, it sounds like this coffee maker needs to be recalled before someone dies in a fire.  I called Cuisinart and they told me that it had not been recalled.  They offered to replace it, but I do not want another one.  I purchased a different brand entirely.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without injury. Online reports suggest this is a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
Hotpoint Gas Range oven Model RGB745BEH7WH, Serial TH209904R

Unfortunately I am unsure of the age however I can say I have had the same issue since it was purchased. I will guess and say approximately 6 years ago this oven was purchased. 

When using the oven there is a very strong gas oder. A service tech told me it was fine and normal for a small oder. I called the gas company several times throughout the years of which they too told me it was "normal".

Upon completion of the gas company fixing a small gas leak from the instalation of a new meter I asked again if they would check my oven. I do not feel it is normal to have to air out a kitchen in order to use an oven.

This gas tech took her time and allowed the over to heat. She then measured and immediately shut off the oven stating it was at a gas leak level of explosion. I was advised to not use the over portion and to service immediately.

I have been unable to locate any recall information regarding this oven and in return am reporting this information to you.
justification: The gas leak level was at an explosion risk, posing a severe threat to life, and the issue persisted over years despite initial dismissals.

incident_description:
GE dishwasher caught fire in my home kitchen, it was part of a recall and it was repaired.

http://www.geappliances.com/products/recall/dishwasher_2010/
 
Model: ZBD6880K03SS
VG718562B
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: The top door micro switch for the GE model JKP85WoD1WW microwave caught on fire
justification: The microwave's door switch caught fire, indicating an incident but no reported injury.

incident_description: My GE oven (model # JBS55BK4BB) ignited in flames while broiling.  The upper broiling element was on fire.  After turning off the oven and extinguishing the flames, I noticed the broiling element was severed near the front right.  Now, both baking and broiling functions do not operate.
justification: The oven ignited in flames but was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
While reaching over the range to get into the cabinet his shirt got caught on the control knob and gas was released. The control knob was on halfway between off and ignition which allows gas to flow without igniting. 

He did not notice the failure until he left the home for an 1 ÃÂ½ before noticing the gas in the home. He opened all the windows in the home and left for a few hours. 

He contacted the firm via email on 10/21/2011 and was advised that his concerns would be forwarded to the product team and he would hear back from them. He received a case number REDACTED.
The firm was contacted via the phone on 10/26/2011 and he has a service technician scheduled to come out to the home on 11/4/2011.  CONSUMER ADDED:  On November 4, 2011 AC Service Rep came to service as requested by REDACTED GE Customer Rep stated nothing wrong, just the way they are made!  To add insult to almost fatal catasrophe had to charge me $87.50 because questions are not covered by warranty!  Told him not paying since REDACTED at GE Requested I have them come to Check out!  It is a manufactoring flaw!  Told I could buy child proof locks!  This is an accident waiting to happen!  Very poor engineering !!!  

It will be a shame if someone's house gets blown up or worse People Killed!  All Because to cheap to put a locking device on control shaft to lock in!!

He indicated that his concerns are with the knobs on the range any accidental turning of the knobs can cause gas to leak from the range. He indicated that it could potentially pose as a fire hazard.

A report was also filed by the REDACTED.  He uses the range on a  everyday basis but is extra carefully when using it and ensuring the knobs are powered in the off position.
justification: Gas was released but no injury or death occurred, making it an incident without injury. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) due to the potential for recurrence with the described design flaw.

incident_description:
Caller's have been trying to obtain some relief for problems with their gas range through Consumer Protection via the Vermont Attorney General's Office but were finally referred to CPSC to report  trouble with the broiler/oven.

Around September 11, 2011 caller's were preparing to cook, the oven/broiler did not heat properly so they decided to turn it off, however it would not turn off so caller went to the Propane Tank and turned it off. Two independent technicians have verified that the safety valves have failed.

Callers have had switch to oven/broiler disabled so that they can use the burners which is very inconvenient, caller states that they still at times smell gas.  Advised caller that use of range in this case could be very dangerous.

Caller believes this to be a severe safety hazard, would not like to have the same part as a previous one, he would like a replacement at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident caused a safety hazard with the gas range, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought a 1 quart Pyrex measuring cup from Bed, Bath and Beyond in July 2011. Yesterday I went to wash the measuring cup. It had been sitting at room temperature, approximately 65F and was submerged into 140F water. It exploded in my had - it was not bumped against the side of the sink or any other item. The explosion was enough to cause a small cut on my hand and send several sharp shards up to 3 feet away from where I was standing.
justification: The incident caused a small cut on the hand, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such occurrences are unlikely (likelihood 2) as Pyrex products are generally durable under normal use.

incident_description:
Radiant burner went to high heat while on simmer, and turning the dial to off did not turn off the burner.
While cooking chili, I turned the burner down to simmer since the chili required about 45 minutes of slow cooking, and I went upstairs.
After about 20 minutes I came back to the kitchen, and the burner was on high. The water had almost completely boiled off by then.
I confirmed the burner setting was on simmer (and the coils were still full on maximum as seen by the bright red color under the radiant top) and I then turned the burner off, making sure I felt the off indent of the dial. The burner remained on.
I fiddled with the burner and got it to turn off. I have instructed my wife not to use that burner until the issue is resolved.
The cooktop is 16 years old, and parts readily available, but this event is disturbing.
After researching on the web, and checking with Kenmore, I could find no existing recall.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that could not be turned off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My front, left burner will not turn off on my range. When I was using it one day, I turned the burner off, but it continued to stay on. Then, it will randomly turn on and off by itself and get extremely hot even when I have not used it for the day. I was concerned that this may happen while I am away and a fire could start, so I have to turn off the breaker. Now, Im afraid to even use the stove. When I try to turn the front, left burner on, it will make noises and will not put out the amount of heat the knob is set at. It seems as if is stuck on "high". Now, the burner wont turn on and my back, left burner is making the same noises. Im worried that this range is going to catch my house on fire. It is a shame.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no injury or fire has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Kenmore electice range with smoothtop, model 790.9611 serial vf72118411 

Front left burner stuck on high, only unplugging will make it go off. When plugged in, comes right back on. Extremely dangerous, can not believe there is not a recall for these models. There is a very similar model of kenmore, but its the elite, that has a recall. Was this ignored since its a builders level range?
justification: The burner stuck on high poses a significant burn or fire hazard, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description:
While using the oven at 325 degrees or any setting, after approximately 10 minutes the broiler turned on without physically enabling the switch for broil. It was impossible to tum the broiler off using the stove controls -the circuit breaker at the building fuse box had to be switched to the off position. \\'hen range is not in use, the circuit breaker is in off position. When turning circuit breaker on, broiler comes back on and won't tum off. Setting oven to pre-heat sometimes defeats the broiler -only to have it start on its own again. 

On 10/31/2011 after powering the circuit breaker in the on position the broiler switched in the on position without being switched on.  While doing some research online he noticed that the there was a recall  (see Release # 09-333) where one of the hazards were the element would  fail to turn off after being switched off.
He has not contacted the firm but indicates that he will contact them to see if any repairs could be made.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven broiler that turns on unexpectedly, posing a fire hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I got a call from my Au Pair who was panicking as she said our Dishwasher was sparking and caught fire.  I told her to open the dishwasher which would turn it off.  She got the fire and smoke to stop.  We looked at it and quickly realized that this dishwasher was dead.  I am writing this as if my Au Pair was not at home this dishwasher could have caught my house on fire.  These Dishwashers need to be recalled ASAP or else others may not be as lucky as us.
justification: The dishwasher sparked and caught fire, but the situation was controlled without injury. The incident highlights a potential hazard that could recur.

incident_description: on 12/11/2011, my Maytag Dishwasher Model# MDB5600AWB, sr. # 23621945ER, overheated during regulat wash cycle and heating element would not stop causing excessive heating and smoke. My daugher was home alone and almost got burned. even after turning off the dishwasher, after five hours the heating element would not stop causing excessive heating inside the dishwasher. This is extremely dangerous FIRE hazard. we tried to reach Maytag for help, but their service centers were closed. we left email message from their website for help.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and caused excessive heating, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Our Maytag 36" gas cooktop model:MGC55336BDS started spontaneously turning on the burner ignitor and would not stop until the unit was unplugged.  I had to do this a couple of times in the last few weeks.  But today the burner knob unit starting smoking and sparking.  Fortunately I was standing nearby and was able to unplug the unit.  I hate to think what would have happened if we had been away from the house.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning cooktop that sparked and smoked, but no injury occurred as the issue was promptly addressed.

incident_description:
I purchased a smaller lidded 2 qt pyrex bakeware dish 11/29/11 at my local grocery store.  I hand washed it and put it on the shelf to store.  Today, I decided to make a small lasagna in it.  I constructed the meal and put it in the oven to bake at 350' for 35 minutes.  When the timer went off after the 35 minutes, I slightly opened the oven door to look at the lasagna.  I decided it needed another 5 minutes to bake, so I closed the oven door, reset the timer and went to the living room to sit down.  Right after I sat down, there was a very loud glass-like noise that came from the kitchen - I thought maybe something had fallen out of the dish drain and had broken, but when I went into the kitchen, everything was fine.  I was perplexed and for some reason decided to look in the oven.  To my shock, the Pyrex dish had completely exploded - sharp chards of glass and boiling hot lasagna are everywhere!!  

I had heard the claims about this happening and how the company has been discrediting the complaints or saying that some had misused the bakeware, 'leading' to breakage, but I reporting this to ensure that folks know the claims are true.  I did absolutely nothing outside of the norm to this dish and I just purchased it this week.  I am completely freaked out right now and am shocked to learn that the claims are true.  Had I not chosen to leave it in the oven, it most definitely would have happened when I was handling it and I would have been seriously injured.   I am really upset and very concerned that this could happen to some one else - and possibly not with the same unharmed outcome.  

Please, please, please be sure these dishes are thoroughly investigated/tested, as I am very concerned about their safety.  I own so much Pyrex bakeware and dishes, as I do not like to bake in metal nor store items in plastic.  No more.  It is all going to the recycling center as I will never trust another of their products again.  

Thank you for your time and attention to this potentially dangerous bakeware.  

[REDACTED]
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, but no injury occurred as the user was not handling it at the time.

incident_description:
On 10/30/2011 while baking a pizza in the oven at 400 degrees for  approximately 15 minutes when he noticed a burning odor coming from the oven . He made an attempt to power the oven in the off position with the control panel and it would not power off which also caused the pizza to burn up. The circuit breaker was then pulled to cease power to the unit. 

The heating elemnet began to grow bright red when the failure occured and the temperature heated to another temperature that was not selected. 

On 10/31/2011 after powering the circuit breaker in the on position and placing the oven in the on position at 350 degrees they noticed the heating element was glowing bright red.

When making attempts to power the oven in the off position it would not power off and the circuit breaker was pulled again to cease power to the oven. No repairs have been made to the unit and the circuit breaker is still currently pulled to prevent any power to the range. 

Because consumer has to keep the breaker off she can't use the stove either/  If the breaker is on the oven heats automatically to extreme temps and cannot be turned off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: turn oven on to preheat 350 for baking//after 10 minutes heard an explosion went to kitchen bottom oven element was on fire. oven is exactly 13 months old.....called sears ...allthey wanted to do was sell us a maintenance contract.....told them it must be a defect since it is so new..was told it was past warranty and would have to pay to have it fixed....will never buy from them again.....could have been seriously hurt.......    [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven, which could have caused serious injury but did not, placing it at severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the age of the oven and the defect mentioned.

incident_description: My kenmore elite range smooth top turns on by itself. I have tried to get this replaced by Sears but they have been no help. I have researched their products online and there have been recalls for other elite smooth top ranges but the serial number on mine doesn't match any of the recall items. I am currently turning my range on and off at the main power source.
justification: The range turning on by itself is a safety hazard, but there is no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
When the front left burner was powered in the on position on the lowest setting she noticed that it would heat up to another temperature than selected. The burner would not power in the off position when being switched so the circuit breaker had to be powered off. A technician came out on 9/25/11.

August 26 of 2011 while using the front left burner on a low setting and the temperature changed to a higher temperature than select and caught fire to the food that was being cooked on the cook top.  

She attempted to use water to put the fire out but since it was a oil fire and most of the oil was gone the flames went died out by themselves. The burner was powered in the off position.

Her husband is a volunteer fire fighter so he contacted The former Fire chief whom bought out  a fan to suction the smoke out. They noticed that element was still powered in the on position but the control knob was positioned to off so the  circuit breaker was then pulled.

The hood above the stove was melted and the cabinets beside the range were burned.

The retailer was contacted and, on 9/13/2011, and 9/26/2011  two  different technicians came out to the home and the one on 9/13 reported to the retailer that the range should be replaced.

Pictures of the damages were taken by the technician on 9/26/2011 and provided to the retailer. She has also spoke with the insurance company in regards to the damages that were caused by the fire. 

She spoke with a representative at the retailer on 10/13/2011 who advised the consumer that that they were only offering to repair the appliance and not replace. The representative also checked for a recall since  she experienced two of the same hazards in Release #09-333 but her appliance was not included within the recall, or the recall done by Electrolux on Oct. 21, 2010, Release #11-016.

She then contacted the firm on 10/13/2011 and they were not willing to offer assistance with the stove and she has not used the appliance since the incident in August of 2011. The circuit breaker is currently powered in the off position to prevent any future hazards with the range.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to the stove and cabinets, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Several weeks ago my Kenmore Dishwasher, model 665.17053400 serial number 3901353 sent a large spark across my kitchen and then started smoking heavily.  Luckly my son saw it happen and called me and I was able to turn off the dishwasher and then the breaker immediately.  I called Kenmore they said said I would have to pay for repairs, I checked on cpsc and it seems to fall under recall (release #05-123).  Kenmore said it didn't.  I called cpsc, they said they would look into it and call me back, my case number [REDACTED].  I have not heard back from them and now I am forced to repair/replace this dangerous dishwasher on my own.
justification: The dishwasher emitted a large spark and heavy smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her electric range is a fire hazard. The consumer stated that she looked at the electric dials of the range, and at the dials of the digital display appear to show that the range is off. However, the front left burner is still on and very hot, the consumer states that the control panel does not indicate that the surface is hot. However, sometimes the control panel will indicate that the surface is hot.  The consumer stated the burner will not turn on spontaneously. The consumer stated that this problem happened about 6 months ago and has continued to happen about 6 times. The consumer had to go in the garage of her home and turn off the circuit breaker. The consumer didn't hear a crackling noise from the product or smell any type of burning. 

The consumer has the range burner set to medium to medium high normally. Two years ago, the consumer found that the front right burner would remain on after the consumer would shut off the range at the dials. The consumer called the retailer immediately after the incident happened. The consumer was informed that she had to pay at her expense to have the product serviced. The consumer's husband decided to fix the range himself and that particular burner has not had any problems since. The consumer did not call the firm about the right front burner. The consumer has a smooth top surface electric range.

The consumer did call Sears, where they purchased it, and they said there was nothing they could do.  They also called Kenmore and were told the same thing.  The consumer called the firm's recall hotline in release 09-333 today and was informed that her product was not on recall and was given the number to the CPSC. The consumer was informed by the CPSC that there was no recall currently for his range. 

The consumer found similar models in release 09-333 that have the same hazard as her range. The consumer has not continued to use the stove or the effected burner at all. The product appeared to show no signs of damage.  The product has not damaged the consumer's home. The consumer stated that no one has been hurt. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incidents.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range that poses a fire hazard, but no injuries or property damage have occurred.

incident_description:
The evening of 09/27/2011 caller was baking banana bread at 350 degree oven when after 10 minutes of putting bread in the electric range oven, the broiler had turned on by itself and the oven had become so hot that it burned the bread beyond the point of being able to be eaten.

Glass and Teflon Containers were also burned.

Caller immediately tried to turn both the oven and broiler off but neither could be turned off manually, caller ran to basement and flipped the breaker off.
No injuries 

The breaker remains off for fear of fire hazard.
Caller lives on a remote island in Alaska, called Retailer/Manufacturer on 09/27/2011, was told that a tech would be sent to look at range but hasn't heard back regarding date.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that burned food and containers, but no injuries occurred. The likelihood is considered possible due to the remote location and delayed response from the manufacturer.

incident_description:
We have had Breville 800ESXL Expresso Maker for the last year.  We kept smelling a burning odor coming from the machine.  Eventually, the odor was gone.  

Recently, the steamer option stopped working.  We initially thought it was the pump going.  When we open up the machine, we found many of the electrical connection with plastic covering had burned off, which explains the burning odor we have had.  Furthermore, some of the connections were sparking.

This expresso machine has a stainless body.  I am just gratefull that none of the us were elecuted.  I guess fire would of been another hazard.
justification: The incident involved electrical damage and sparking, posing a risk of injury or fire, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Thursday October 27, my son like any other day used the toaster to toast 2 pieces of bread,
and while he was waiting for the toaster he started to brush his teeth and getting ready for
school. He heard a popping noise and waled to the Kitchen and the toaster was on fire.

I called Rival, Rival gave me another number I called that number and was told to go to
Wall-mart, I went to Wallmart and they told me that it is not there issue. I contacted BBB
and found out the Rival has a F rating. I did make my complaint with them as well.

Can you provide any help with this issue we have the reminder of the toaster in our
possession and attached are the pictures of the toaster and the damages.

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
justification: The toaster was on fire, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her slow cooker had the glass shatter after she used it for 5  hours cooking ribs. The product is electric powered. The consumer is unsure of what setting is was on. The consumer feels that there is a design flaw of not enough venting that caused this to happen. The consumer feels that the gasket where the glass top is prevents the air to escape the cooker. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. 

The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident took place and the product did not damage her home. The product has not charring or cinge marks. The consumer called the firm about the issue today and was told that the firm would send her a new lid. The consumer was outside when the incident happened so was not present when it happened but there was glass all over her kitchen. The consumer has yet to call the retailer.
justification: The glass shattered but no injury or property damage occurred, and the consumer was not present during the incident.

incident_description: Dishwasher control panel fire within door panel.  Fire extended out of the door panel to the lower kitchen cabinets.
justification: The incident involved a fire extending to kitchen cabinets, indicating property damage but no mention of injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: Console "sparked" where digital display is. Now only partial display is shown.
justification: The console sparked and the display is partially affected, indicating an incident with no reported injury.

incident_description: The consumer says there was a strange noise coming from dishwasher.  He saw black smoke coming out of unit.  He cut off the circuit breaker to turn the dishwasher off.    He says that the control board flamed out and melted the components inside the dishwasher.  He contacted the manufacturer who told him they haven't heard of any issues with the unit.  He is concerned that a repair would not resolve the issue as he has read on numerous online reports.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flame from the dishwasher, but no injury was reported, and the consumer took immediate action to prevent further damage.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there was a an issue with the start relay of her double door refrigerator was smoking and has melted down. The consumer walked in to the kitchen and found smoking at the ceiling in his kitchen. The refrigerator also emitted a burning odor. The consumer pulled the refrigerator away from the wall and pulled the plug from the outlet in order to stop the smoking. The consumer called a service technician to inspect the refrigerator and replace the relay to the refrigerator at her expense 2 and half weeks ago. Since then the product was fixed it has not had any problems.

 The start relay is on the compressor and shows signs of burning. The relay also damaged the capacitor of the refrigerator. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. The product did not damage his house and on the exterior the refrigerator looks to be just fine. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident took place.  

The consumer called the firm about the issue on October told and was told that there is no current recall for her similar refrigerator. The consumer stated that her product is similar to other recalled models and the firm refuses to reimburse her for the service call to the repairman. The consumer has not called the retailer.
justification: The incident involved smoking and a burning odor from the refrigerator, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
On thanksgiving day, I was cooking stuffed artichokes in one of my brown glass 3 quart pyrex baking dish.  I took it out of the oven and placed it on my granite countertip.  I turned back to shut the oven door and when I turned back to my artichokes the glass pyrex exploded.  It scared the [REDACTED] out of me and my 85 year old mother who was standing next to me.  We were very lucky not to get cut by the flying glass, but it did ruin our thanksgiving dinner.  For fear of glass getting in our food we had to throw out our artichokes and 2 other dishes of food that was next to them on the counter.
I own a lot of pyrex and have always used them, but I am now afraid because I do not know what caused this to happened.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the exploding Pyrex dish caused property damage and disrupted the meal, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Burned my hand with these picking up a hot skillet that an old oven mitt could handle. There was a drop of water where I was burned. Too unsafe if it has to be moisture free.
justification: The description mentions a burn injury from handling a hot skillet, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I have a Cuisinart DCC1200 that I purchased about 1 1/2 years ago.  This morning the base of the maker caught fire.  A quick internet search and reviews on Consumer Report's site show that this appears to be a common problem.  I was standing next to the coffee maker when it caught fire.  The pot appeared to be brewing normally, but within seconds acrid smelling smoke began to pour out of the base.  I unplugged the maker and remove the carafe.  The heating element was bright red and extremely hot.  Had I not been standing there, the unit would have likely caused a large fire.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred as the user was present to unplug it.

incident_description:
Order Placed: December 15, 2010
Amazon.com order number: [REDACTED]

SENSEO Pod Coffee Maker.

incident_description:
Purchased Maytag electric range MET8885X directly from manufacturer, accepting delivery on 11/18/11.  With first oven use, the stove tripped the breaker.  Manual indicates to reset and retry, and second attempt also tripped the breaker.  Following MaytagÃÂs manual, we called an electrician to inspect electrical service.  Electrician review on 11/21 indicates no issues with electric service (note that this purchase replaced an existing working electric oven, which never had any issues).  He reset the breaker and the oven turned on without another trip.  
In subsequent days, however, oven safety quickly degraded.  It started with spotty temperature control and both ovens heating up when only one was in use.  Late in the afternoon of 11/27, we realized that even though all controls indicated the oven was off, the oven temperature was upwards of 300 degrees.  The oven had not been used that day.  The only way to shut off the oven was to unplug the range, or trip the breaker.
Call to Maytag customer service on 11/28 resulted in a transfer to their Safety Department.  [REDACTED] arranged for a technician to visit, and indicated that we should keep the breaker off and not use the range.  She would ask a supervisor to respond to our request for reimbursement for the electrician visit.  
My husband took a half-day off from work to meet with the technician on 12/1.  [REDACTED] from A&E Factory Service found a short in the lower baking element - the contacts had shorted to the back panel.  He repaired all exposed wiring by insulating with electrical tape.  his attempt to turn on the oven was not successful. he found that the computer controller was damaged ÃÂ he removed it, and indicated one of the relays was rattling internally.  He ordered new parts, and scheduled a return appointment for Monday 12/5 between 1-5 p.m.  
a supervisor in MaytagÃÂs Safety Department [REDACTED], also called that day indicating it would take 21 days if we wanted to request a replacement range.  He also offered us $100 ÃÂto make goodÃÂ for the repair.  
On Saturday, 12/3, we received a call from A&E indicating they needed to reschedule the appointment from the 5th to the 12th due to a part delay.   We indicated that was unsatisfactory, and inquired who we might speak with to expedite.  She indicated to call Maytag.
On Sunday, 12/4 we received a call indicating our appointment was scheduled for Monday.  Calls to A&E on Monday confirmed they would be out between 1-5.  Again, my husband needed to take off from work for a half-day to meet with the technician.  By 4:00 p.m., the part was delivered by UPS, however,  a call to A&E indicated they would not be able to make it on Monday.  The ÃÂgood newsÃÂ is that they would come out on Tuesday.  We declined and indicated we would follow up with Maytag.  My husband left a message indicating the circumstances, and that we would like Maytag to pick up the appliance and refund the purchase price.  His voice mail indicated he was out of the office for the day.
By 12:30 on  12/6, we still did not hear from Maytag.  Another call to [REDACTED] resulted in a voice mail indicating that he is again out of the office for the day.  I called the main number for the Safety Dept. at Maytag, and the consultant indicated she could not authorize an appliance pick up and refund.  I asked to speak with someone who could ÃÂ she indicated that [REDACTED] would call back.  No call was received from them by the end of the day.  
At 4 p.m. an A&E technician indicated he would be at our house within a half hour.  I indicated that the appointment was for yesterday, and no one would be available to meet with him.  Indicated we are working with Maytag to resolve this issue.
At this point, we have concerns regarding the safety of this appliance, as well as MaytagÃÂs customer service commitment.  The purchase contract to provide a working, quality product has been breached, and would like Maytag to pick up the appliance and refund the full purchase price as soon as possible.  We are now on our second week without a working stove.

incident_description:
While making Espresso, a loud whoosh was heard followed by a massive steam escape from the unit. No injuries.

Upon disassemble it was discovered the the four plastic (PBTP) mounting brackets that secure the boiler unit assembly to the appliance housing had cracked. The two halves of the boiler unit were separated by approximately 2mm.

The brackets are secured to the boiler assembly with the same screws that clamp the upper and lower halves of the boiler unit together. The brackets are approx 2mm thickness and over time deteriorated such that the bracket split and the material under the screw head broke away from the rest of the bracket on each of the four brackets. This resulted in the boiler unit not being secured to the chassis and being held in place by means not intended for that purpose. Once the material under the screw heads deteriorated further and fell away, there became a 2mm gap between the housing and screw head. Eventually the steam pressure inside the chamber during the boiling process caused the 2 halves of the boiler unit to separate by approx 2mm resulting in a massive steam escape and rendering the unit inoperable. 

The method of mounting the boiler unit to the chassis with a plastic bracket is not safe and should be designed with metal brackets.
justification: The incident involved a massive steam escape but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described deterioration over time and the unsafe design of the mounting brackets.

The control panel is $262.00 not including labor and Maytag is ignoring its consumers rather than accepting responsibility for the defective product. It is a fire hazard and since waking up at 2am with my oven on i have had to disconnect power to avoid an incident
justification: The oven's malfunctioning control panel poses a fire hazard and has caused the oven to turn on unexpectedly, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: It was Thanksgiving Day and I had preheated my oven to 350 to bake my dressing.  I mixed my dressing and put it in my Pyrex 9 x 13 3 qt. clear baking dish.  I put it in my oven, closed the oven door and took two steps to the counter, when a loud bang that rattle my stove happen.  I looked through the window of the stove and the Pyrex baking dish had exploded.  Shardes of glass were everywhere.  I immediately turned the oven off.  When the oven had cooled we took pictures of the inside of oven, broken glass everywhere.  We had to clean the inside of the oven with a shop vacumn.  I am not sure if there is any damage to  my oven.  It was a loud enough bang to make you be shaken for the rest of the day.  If it had exploded on a counter top it would have caused serious injury.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but no one was injured, though the incident caused significant shock and potential oven damage.

incident_description: Delonghi toaster oven timer does not turn off oven.  Set the timer to ten minutes and it runs for ten minutes and then still stays on. A fire hazard.   A brief search showed similar complaints on Amazon but no recall or fix
justification: The toaster oven timer malfunction poses a fire hazard, indicating an incident with potential for harm but no reported injuries. Similar complaints suggest the issue is likely to occur.

incident_description: My Kenmore dishwasher (yes it was old - I purchased it in 1988) burst into flames while I was sleeping.  I had set the delay start that evening, and went to bed. About 11pm, my parents who were sleeping downstairs came and woke me up to report my house was filling with smoke. When I came downstairs, there were flames coming form the control panel. I did try and put the fireout,realized it was useless, and got myself and my parents out of the house.  We were out of our house for 6 weeks while the kitchen was repaired and the house was cleaned to rid the smoke damage.  I expected an old dishwasher to fail by leaking water or not cleaning dishes. I did not expect it to ignite.
justification: The dishwasher burst into flames causing significant damage and requiring evacuation, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I OWN A FRIDGEDAIRE ELECTRIC STOVE, NO MORE THAN 5YRS.OLD
   I SMELT SMOKE    THE CORD FROM  THE STOVE  SPARKED & BURNT
THE STOVES  HEATING BOX.   I CALLED A PERSON WHO FIX`S STOVES

STOVE  THAT SITS IN MY KITCHEN & DOESNT  WORK,  JUST  WANTED TO LET 
 ANYONE  OUT THERE TO KNOW   IN CASE YOU ARE HAVING THIS PROBLEM,

incident_description: I was using a 9"x13" Pyrex glass baking dish to bake 8 sweet potatos. Per the manufacturers directions the oven was fully pre-heated to 325 deg. F, the bottom of the dish was fully covered with a liquid (Brown sugar sauce approximately .5" depth), and no direct flame or broiler in use. after baking for 23 minutes i heard an explosion and thick smoke began billowing out of my oven. After extinguishing a small fire inside the oven I realized that the baking dish shattered spilling oily sauce into the ovens lower shelf and into the burners causing the fire. Other than Destroying a good portion of my familys thanksgiving dinner, if nobody was nearby to hear the dish break or see the smoke this breaking dish could have burned my house down! My parents have Pyrex glass bakeware that has been in service for more than 25 years with no problems. After doing a little research I believe that the manufacturer has compromised the saftey of their product while attempting to save money in the manufacturing process.
justification: The incident involved a shattered baking dish causing a small fire, which could have led to significant property damage if unnoticed, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Elite initiated a fire inside while normal cooking was in process. Flames came out of the door. The same odor one has during self clean lingered for days. It locked itself so I cannot identify the model number. It was purchased in December 2006 from Sears.
It is a regular electric plus convection wall oven with all controls digital and recessed.
justification: Flames emerged from the oven during normal use, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a "Pro-Slicer," from Sam's Club on 11/13/2011 for my mother and I to use in our kitchen.  Since the purchase date, mother has used the device twice, resulting in deep lacerations to her hands.  The problem is that the device cuts deeply even when used as directed.  I fear that people could risk losing extremities (i.e. fingers, finger tips, et cetera).  I'm also worried about the housekeepers and those who wash their own dishes, and how this device can literally slice someone up in the process.  Please look into this device!!
justification: The device caused deep lacerations when used as directed, indicating a high risk of injury.

incident_description:
The left and right front burner spontaneously  go to high while using the burners  (amount of time using the burners vary) on the lowest settings without being switched. After powering the burners in the off position they continue to heat up.

The circuit breaker is then powered in the off position and powered back in the on position within five minutes and both burners power back on without being switched on and are on the highest setting. 

The consumer states that he usually make sure the burners are powered in the off position and while the burner is still heating up he powers the breaker in the off position waits for the burner to cool down for 10 minutes before powering the circuit breaker back into the on position and both burners would be powered off.

The consumer noticed online that there was a recall where similar model experienced the same hard (see Release #09-333) so he contacted the firm on 9/21/2011.

The representative (name was not provided) advised the consumer that his model number was not included in the recall but that they would like to schedule a technician to come out to the home to take a look at the range.

The consumer has not scheduled a date and time for the repairman to come out but indicated that he plans on doing so. 

He still currently uses the burner but states that the failure occurs intermittently but he is really careful not to leave the range unattended.
justification: The burners malfunction and heat up unexpectedly, posing a risk of fire or burns, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he has been experiencing problems with the Range for over 2 months with the control knobs not operating properly to turn off the large front burners.

Consumer said that after he had power off the range, the front right burner came back on by itself he had to switch it off from the circuit breaker.

The burners exhibit these features simultaneously and he feels that this product is a fire hazard, especially if no one is at home.

Consumer contacted the manufacturer but the center was not open as yet.

Consumer is concerned that this product is dangerous and should be reported.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning range that could pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
While operating the dishwasher on the normal wash and air dry after pressing the start button within five minutes there was an explosiive sound and black smoke and flames were shooting from the vent. 

While attempting to power the dishwasher in the off position he noticed that it would not power off. He opened the door to the dishwasher and made several more  attempts with the control panel. When that failed the circuit breaker was pulled to cease all power to the unit.


There is black soot  on the outside dishwasher door and a burnt plastic odor, but no other damages reported.  The firm was contacted on 10/30/2011 and she was advised that her model number was not affected by a recall. 

There was no final decision made on repairing the unit and the firm was not contacted since 10/30/2011 and the circuit breaker was pulled so there is no power to the unit and it has not been used.  Consumer posted incident in a Sears Forum and was contacted by Sears, who arranged for a service call and repair service was completed on 11/11/11
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries or damages were reported, and the issue was resolved without further incident.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while preheating the oven for approximately 15 mins at 350 degrees, she heard a beeping sound, when she got back to the oven she discovered that the oven had switched to broil on its own which caught her content on fire.  The temperature was not displayed on the control panel, this was first time the incident occur.  Consumer was unable to use the control panel to power off the unit, she had to remove it from the wall to unplug it.

Consumer stated that an hour later she attempted to turn on the unit and the incident re-occurred, she unplugged it and is awaiting to contact the retail store or manufacturer.

Consumer is concerned that she unable to use this oven due to the fire hazard.

justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My Kenmore (Whirlpool) side by side refrigerator model 106.52542101, Coldspot, serial number SL2244299,  has had the relay overload switch replaced 2 times now. the 2nd time, yesterday caused a smoke, smoldering fire while I was home so the house didn't burn down.  I began smelling smoke and couldn't locate the source.  I called the fire department and they sent a truck out.  Before they arrived I saw some smoke coming from beneath the refrigerator so I started to pull it away from the wall when the fireman knocked at the door.  They came in with their heat sensor and I waited outside.  Within a couple of minutes they came out and said it was the refrigerator.  The relay switch had melted, shorted out and started the cardboard backing to smoke.  I suppose it would have combusted at some point if we hadn't found it.  I called service repair as soon as possible because we had thanksgiving food in the refrigerator.  He came that day at 5pm.  It was the same repairman from 2 years ago, he had switched companies.  It took him two hours and $250 later it was running.  I noticed when he had finished, the burnt switch area was empty.  So Whirlpool had redesigned the relay kit and the location of the parts so it wouldn't cause the same problem again, but they made me pay for their bad design by not recalling the part and location.  The part is now located inside a cover mounted on the compressor.  I can not find a Whirlpool recall on this common failure and the Whirlpool complaint website has hundreds of people with the same problem, some with extensive fire and smoke damage. I am attaching the web site with these complaints for you to see. I think you should look into all the complaints on Whirlpool appliances and get them to cover the repairs and damage caused. http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/whirlpool_refrigerators.html
thanks
[REDACTED] (you can call me or email me if you have more questions)
justification: The incident involved a smoldering fire caused by a faulty relay switch, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:

We have been having problems with the refrigerator light staying on when the door is closed. This has caused not only food to spoil but the plastic to melt inside the unit. When we contacted Sears about this they were NO HELP AT all. This has to be a fire hazard as when you do open the door the plastic is extremely HOT to the touch. incident_description:
This is a quick sketch of what I have been going through with Sears in my attempts to get my stove repaired.

1. Kenmore Stove model 94472 purchased 3-18-09 for $960.49 with an extended warrenty for $249.99 which doesn't expire until 12-25-14. I also had to pay $19.52 for the electrical connection.

2. First service call from Sears was 11-24-09 as I had noticed that the right front element did not heat well and not evenly. The warmer drawer did not heat consistently. Service tech declared everything ok even though I have continued to have problems with this element.

3.  I decided to use the self clean element for the first time on 6-4-11 . I set it for the minimum 3 hours and the stove turned off by itself even though I don't know how long it actually ran. I didn't expect problems. ! immediately noticed that the front plastic pane! on the door (where the heat exhaust is) was discolored from white to a light brown. I began checking for other problems and noticed that the cabinet drawers on the right had been damaged from the heat.

4.  Called local retailer and talked with owner. He said he would call service center for me as I had not been able to get through. He said he would call me back.

5.  No call-back; I called Sears Service on 6-15-11 and was told that they had not been contacted. called assistant manager at retailer; she set up new service call for 6-24-11 ; no one showed up.

6.  Another service call set up for 7-1-11 . This service tech said that the cleaning temperatures are very high and that he has seen much worse damage than what I had! He looked at the oven door and said that he couldn't find anything wrong. He suggested I contact the searshomeservice.com. I did; I never received a reply.

7.  I contacted Consumer Reports magazine on 7-3-11 to seek help with this; I read about the CPSC on their website and decided to try that.

8.  Another tech arrived on 7 -22-11 ; he said he checked the door seal and the temperature (for about ten minutes); he said everything checked out ok. (He told me that if I wanted to use the self clean, I would just have to pull the stove out into the middle of the room.)

9. On 10-11-11 , I set oven on 250 degrees and put in some frozen egg rolls to thaw and heat slowly. About 15 minutes later, the kitchen alarms and stove alarms went off; the stove would not respond to the off button; finally the stove was pulled out and disconnected from the wall. The food was burned black; I put an oven thermometer inside and it quickly registered over 450 degrees. I didn't call Sears because their Service has been so slow and completely unhelpful.

10. On Nov.11, 2011, I set the "warm & hold" setting on oven to keep food warm for later. The maximum
temperature for this setting is supposed to be 170 degrees. Within minutes, the alarms went off and the
stove could not be turned off. Pulled stove out, discounted from the wall, and checked the oven temp. It
was over 400 degrees; an error code of F10 was blinking.

11 . Nov. 16, 2011, a representative from CPSC called and took my information about this dangerous
situation which I cannot seem to resolve with Sears.

12. Sears sent another service tech on 11-18-11, he asked if any of the other techs had checked the
main control panel; I said "no". He said he was amazed they had not because that has been the problem
all along.
He ordered a new control computer and told me It would be about two-three weeks before it would arrive.
I asked him if this was the cause of the top elements being so hard to regulate and he said "yes"
because this is the master control and controls everything and that it was the cause of the oven overheating.

13. About four days after the last tech visit on 11-18-11; I received the control panel at my home!
guess that means I'm supposed to install it although I know nothing about such things. The control panel
is marked "remanufactured" which I plan to refuse. I paid for a new stove and I deserve a new stove.
(Actually, I would rather have my money back because I will never get over being afraid of this stove.)
The stove still looks brand new; I've taken very good care of it but Sears is not even trying to resolve this
properly. This has always been a defective stove and it is dangerous. I intend to fight this as long as it
takes. Your assistance is deeply appreciated.
justification: The stove has caused multiple incidents of overheating and has not been properly repaired by Sears, posing a risk of injury or property damage.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool Gold Dishwasher, named Whirlpool Partner IV, Model GU1500XTKQO, serial number FM0720274 that started on fire. I purchased the dishwasher in August 2002, and had it installed in October 2002. In February 2009.  I phone Whirlpool stating I smelled something electrical from the dishwasher. A tech comes to my home for a service call. On Feb. 13, 2009 the heating element and soap dispenser were replaced, because the electrical smell could not be properly identified, so this was the easiest solution.
At about 7:30 PM Sept. 9, 2011 I started the above mentioned dishwasher. It made a crackly noise, that I first associated with the incoming water heating. Then I saw flames coming out of the control panel and thick black smoke. I immediately hit the door latch shutting off power supply. My husband turned off the dishwasher circuit.
September 12 , 2011  I phone Whirlpool and reported the incident. my dishwasher is 9 years old. I can accept that a 9 year old dishwasher may stop working and attribute it to normal use. However starting on fire, is an entirely different curve. Thank goodness we were home.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I was steaming two ears of corn in a steamer basket in my Farberware pot on medium high on my electric range, and just as the water boiled out, the bottom of the pot melted all over the burner.  There was melted aluminum everywhere.   From the Farberware website, I read that this is not covered by Farberware's lifetime warranty because the 2 digit code on the bottom of the pot is 'unreadable', yes, because it melted off, so this item is not covered by a warranty.   
In all my 50 years of cooking, I have never even heard of a pot melting just when the water boils off. The food did not even burn, and the inside of the pot just has a small haze from the boil off. 
It is most important that a consumer alert be issued that aluminum clad pots can and will MELT is water boils off!
justification: The incident involved a pot melting but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is rare given the user's 50 years of cooking experience without encountering this issue.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he opened up the refrigerator and discovered that the plastic casing around the light had melted and the sockets were discolored.  The temperature inside was extremely warm.  He was able to remove the damged plastic casing and the lights to prevent further damages.  This was the first time this incident had occurred.

Consumer stated that the refrigerator is operating without the light bulb at this time.

Consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer is concerned that this refrigerator poses a fire hazard and should be reported.

UPDATE: Consumer contacted LG at 800-243-0000 and explained the problem to its customer service representative.  They said the repair would be made at no cost to him- the service company is a home tech service at 570-822-2000.  He contacted them about 10/25 and they were aware of the problem but had not received authorization from LG to proceed.  After about 3-4 more phone calls, they received authorization  to proceed on the problem.  The first thing they have to do is order the parts.  As of 11/9/2011, they hadn't received the parts (he had made 4 phone calls to check on where the parts were).  (he just called again-recording on office hrs etc).

Once again, the parts aren't in and his appointment for repair hasn't been scheduled.  From the info on the internet, this seems to be a pretty common problem.  He is a retired enginerr from IBM where he had product responsibilities. It is very difficult for him to understand why this product wasn't recalled because of this serious problem.  If this occured while they were away, a fire could have easily happened that could have burned the house down.  I don't think LG takes this situation as seriously as they should under these circumstances.

Some of their design procedures are very questionable.  They solder a fuse intro a fuse holder on the control board.  If the  fuse blows, the replacement part is the entire control board and not the fuse.  This makes no sense at all- a fuse costs about $2 while the control board is probably $150 or so.
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator but no injury or death, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as the problem seems to be common but not certain.

incident_description:
November 22, 2011

To Whom It May Concern (Frigidaire),

In December of 2010 I ordered a Frigidaire Gallery Series gas range model #FGGF3054KFK, serial #VF05232575.  The unit was manufactured in January 2011, delivered and installed in February 2011. I purchased the unit from Bennies TV and Appliance in San Antonio, TX.

Over the course of the next 6 months I would smell gas while cooking or cleaning in the kitchen and would notice  the range knobs were turned slightly and emitting fumes into the air.  It was until recently that I realized while cooking, serving, or cleaning in and around the range that knobs were inadvertently turned on due to gentle bumping and light contact.  On most occasions, I was still at the range when I smelt gas and would turn the knobs off.  In mid-September of 2011 I was performing normal cleaning activities in and around the stove and stepped out of the kitchen.  When I returned the kitchen was thick with gas fumes. I checked the range knobs and found one slightly turned on.  I turned it off and opened the windows to thin out the air. I am now concerned for my safety.

I contacted the retailer and they promptly sent out a technician to inspect the range.  He reported that the range was operating as designed; gas emits from the burner before a spark is introduced. I was told by the retailer that I would have to contact the mfr if I had any further complaints.  I called Frigidaure on 9/20/11 and spoke with [REDACTED], a Cooking Warranty agent, he opened an account (#[REDACTED] and gave me the numbers of 3 appliance repair businesses and instructed me to call once and have them call the "Frigidaire tech line" while they are inspecting my range. As the first technician reported he stated that the range was operating as designed but did remark that the knobs were very sensitive.

I stayed in contact wuth [REDACTED] in hopes that Frigidaire would understand my concerns for my and my family's safety and work with me on a buyback or swap out for an electric range. I was contacted by [REDACTED] from Frigidaire on 11/4/11 stating that since the range was operating as designed, Frigidaire would take no further action.

I am not disputing that the operation of the range is working as designed but it is clear that the flaw with the range is in the design itself.  I should be able to perform normal kitchen tasks in and around my range without having concern for gas emitting from incidental contact with the range knobs.  As the 2nd technician reported back to Frigidaire the knobs were very sensitive.

I was disappointed in Frigidaire's 'No action" response and lack of concern for me and my family's safety.  Had I left the house that day in September instead of just leaving the room, it could have very easily had serious implications.  As I mentioned earlier I am concerned for myself and my family's safety and had no choice but to file a report with the Consumer Product Safety Council. I am writing this letter now in hopes that Frigidaire will consider working with me on a trade out for an all electric range of the same series.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage due to sensitive knobs, posing a safety risk but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his daughter's oven is a potential fire hazard as it shorted out and caused the circuit breaker in her home to trip. incident_description:
This incident occurred with a GE Dual-Fuel Range model j2b918sel2ss.   The range caught fire resulting in large flames shooting out from under the control panel.   The fire was extinguished by turning off the external gas feed to the appliance.   

Analysis after indicates that the control panel was destroyed, and all the internal wiring running down the side of the range was burned.   In addition, there's a large gas leak internally in the area where the wires and gas feed line run up the side of the range.

At the time of the incident, both the oven and cooktop were in use (The oven was in non-convection mode), and had been in use for approx 2 hours.  Turning off the burners on the cooktop did not extinguish the fire, and the food cooking in the oven was not affected by the fire (the fire was NOT in the oven)
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant damage to the range, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

phone:      [REDACTED]
email:       [REDACTED]

After 7 years of regular use in a 2-adult household, we have discovered a possible design flaw that allows the lower hinge pin to become unscrewed during normal use, ultimately resulting in the heavy door abruptly falling to the floor.  As a direct consequence, I incurred $143.44 in unreimbursed damages.  When contacted, the manufacturer (Amana) was not interested in inspecting the damage, offering instead to provide a service call at my expense.  The issuer of an extended warranty service (GE Service Protection Plus ) declared that the policy did not cover such events.   But more importantly, this event could have caused serious injury to small children or pets, had they been in the area.


DETAILS

Purchase:  On Jan 17, 2004, we bought the subject refrigerator/freezer from HH Gregg, at a cost of $2046.57, including delivery and installation.  Delivery and Installation appeared to come off without a hitch.  [When called about the accident in 2011, HH Gregg stated that they no longer carry Amana products.]

Accident:  On October 4, 2011, when the top door was opened wide (with hand on door to control its movement), to fully access the various drawers in the body, it suddenly and unexpectedly fell from its hinges onto the floor, breaking 3 of the plastic bins in the door, and destroying some of the contents housed in those bins.  I was stunned by the event, and simply stared at the door and mess on the floor for several seconds.  

Upon gathering my wits, I noticed that the bottom hinge pin was also on the floor with the door, having come unscrewed from the hinge mount on the refrigerator.  With difficulty, I was able to screw the pin back into the lower mount, the screw threads being undamaged, and re-mount the door.   The refrigeration function appears to be performing satisfactorily at this time.

I now routinely inspect the screw mounted lower hinge pin for any evidence of it unscrewing from its mount.  

Apparent cause:  I can only conclude that the lower pin had become unscrewed gradually during the time I owned the refrigerator and finally dislodged from its final friction position when the door was opened wide on that date.   I found the pin laying on the floor about 6 inches from the pin hole in the door, and there was no damage to the screw threads.  I picked it up, noted its likely function, and screwed it back into the hinge mount on the body of the refrigerator.  I then re-mounted the door, minus its contents.

Hazard:  Fortunately, there were no injuries from this incident.  However, had small children or pets been present in the vicinity, they could have been seriously injured when the door fell off its hinges, since the event was sudden and without warning.  Adults could have also been injured, most likely with broken bones in the feet.  Note that the door was full width and quite heavy.  

Damage and costs:  The door has a slight dent on the lower left corner in the vicinity of the hinge hole.  This appears to be largely cosmetic, since once remounted, the door appears to function normally on the restored lower pin.  Three bins were broken and had to be replaced at an unreimbursed cost to me of $ 98.09.  A number of small jars of food items were shattered and had to be replaced at an unreimbursed cost to me of $45.35.   I waited till now to report this, because the replacement bins took this long to arrive.

Respectfully, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator door falling unexpectedly, causing property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely as the issue was identified and mitigated by routine inspection.

Upon further investigation I found the broiler unit in the oven on.  I tried to shut it off using the touch switch (off/cancel) but the unit remained on.  The display did not indicate that either the oven, broiler, or clean had been turned on.  No matter what I did, the unit would not turn off and the oven and top front of the range were very hot.
