incident_description:
My wife returned home yesterday afternoon and noticed a burning smell in our house.  At first, she could not locate the origin of the smell, but after walking through the kitchen, she felt a lot of heat coming from the dishwasher.  She opened it up to find it excessively hot, and many plastic (but dishwasher safe) items were melted.  So many items were melted and dripping down into the bottom of the dishwasher that she was unable to pull out the bottom rack (it was fused to the bottom of the dishwasher with melted plastic).  She made sure it was turned off (it was already) and left it open to cool.

When I returned home a few hours later, I inspected it but noticed that it was still hot inside and the heating element appeared to be the source of the heat.  I turned off the circuit breaker and removed the dishes that I could.

I tried to contact GE but it was already after 10 PM ET (when their customer service line is closed).  I purchased this dishwasher just over 3 years ago (July of 2008) and it is unfathomable that an applicance could go this bad this early.  If my wife didn't arrive home early that day to notice this, it could have caused a fire.  I called GE this morning.  The first time I was on hold for 15-20 minutes and abandoned the effort.  The second time, I called while I was driving into work.  After about 30 minutes, I was able to speak to a representative.  He took down my information and then offered to send someone out to check it out.  Having been through this exercise before with other GE appliances at the same time, I advised him that I expected that person to bring a check for the amount that I paid for the dishwasher or a new dishwasher that doesn't act as an oven.  I am still awaiting a call back from them.

From looking online, I have noticed many similar stories with GE dishwashers burning up like mine did.  These do not appear to have been covered by this recall.  I am very concerned that this is a problem that is not yet fixed.  Please do something before someone gets hurt!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that caused melting of plastic items but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
After moving into a new apartment, we went to bake food in the relatively new oven (<5 years) that was installed with the former tenants (whom had no complaints). Upon our first use of the oven as new residents, there were major arcing and pops coming from behind the oven panels and subsequent breaker trip.

After fixing the breaker, we called the apartment's general maintenance man (not the retailer or manufacturer) and surprisingly, the oven worked fine in his presence. Naturally, when we went to use the oven later that evening, arcing and smoke was again observed, and the breaker tripped.

On the second trip by the apartment's general maintenance man, we removed the oven's rear access shield panel and discovered evidence of arcing across the bare metal panel (PN#5304465312) and the broiler element wire blade connector (PN#316203200). We also observed burning of the relay attached to the Electronic Oven Control panel's circuit board. 

During disassembly, we were disturbed to observe absolutely no usage of insulation on any of the high voltage blade connectors on the oven's wiring harness (PN#1056185) Additionally, we measured in some cases no more than 0.25 inch clearance between most of these high voltage connectors on the wiring harness and the rear shield.

It is our opinion that perhaps during the cleaning of the apartment between tenants the oven was removed and pushed back into the cabinetry, possibly too hard, resulting in contact between the rear shield panel and the broiler element connector on the wiring harness. It was noted that the 220V receptacle was recessed into the wall but the oven plug may have been the main contact point.

I believe that the ability for arcing to occur from this kind of handling is evidence of a significant design flaw present in this model oven. Images of replacement wiring harnesses and rear access cover panels available on the internet show that the use of uninsulated wire connectors or sheet insulation on these panels is common.  The problem is compounded with this particular model oven housing design that provides limited clearance between the connectors and the rear access cover panel or the lack of structural support that could prevent flexing of the rear panel. It should be noted that of the many warnings and notices on the handling and installation of this oven, no comments are made to highlight the additional attention and care needed to prevent contact pressure between the wall, plug, and oven rear access shield.
justification: The incident involved arcing and smoke but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recurring nature of the issue and the design flaw.

We found out after the incident, there was a recent article in the newspaper regarding Bosch Dishwasher fires - unfortunately we did not read it. We had not received any information regarding the recall.

incident_description: On 11/23/2011 my Maytag/Magic Chef side-by-side refrigerator w/in-door water and ice dispenser started to shoot out water all over my kitchen floor.  I moved the lever to the ice side to make it stop but ice started shooting out.  Then it started to smoke from the panel and a flame came out and we could smell burning plastic.  We pulled the unit away from the wall, unplugged it and shut off water supply.  My husband removed the front panel of the dispenser unit and the inside was melted and still smoking.  He disconnected the power to the dispenser.  I went to this site to look up if our fridge had been recalled and found that millions had been recalled for the exact same problem, but our Model and Serial Number were not included in the recall--but obviously they should be now.  I contacted Maytag and they said they would send out someone to "inspect" it but since it wasn't under warranty all "repairs" are our responsibility.  I don't care about the money and let them know that this model now needs to be included in the previous recall.  They didn't seem to interested in doing that.  If we were not home, our house could have burned down--we live in a rural area.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator malfunction causing water and ice discharge, smoke, and flames, posing a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I left my home on a trip 11/6/2011 and upon my return on 11/23/2011 (day before Thanksgiving), I discovered our Whirlpool refrigerator/freezer was not operating. Although the lights worked, the inside temperature was warm and the contents were spoiled and/or melted.
The designated Whirlpool technician arrived Friday, 11/25 and advised me the compressor relay had caught fire, resulting in the burning of the compressor as well. Per the rep, we were lucky that was all that had burned and waived the service fee. The safety feature on the relay should have turned it off, not set fire.  He suggested we call Whirlpool to determine whether or not they would assist in the repair of such a safety/fire hazard as the parts and labor were estimated to be $600-800.

When I contacted Whirlpool, they advised since the appliance was no longer under warranty (Jan., 2004 purchase), the responsibilty of repair fell on us.  Although I acknowledged such, I inquired further as this was not a part that just ceased operating or a normal wear and tear issue but rather, a part that was faulty, presenting a true hazard. Subsequently, I've learned that Whirlpool was aware of this issue since 2005 but did not issue a recall (as they did with their Maytag line) and is currently suing the manufacturer of the this particular component. 

A second call to Whirlpool resulted in a "there's nothing we can do about it" response. A product warranty that has expired is one thing but it has nothing to do with a product that has posed a threat and hazard to my home and family from the day it was purchased and I think everyone should be made aware of this danger and the fact that Whirlpool knows of it as well.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, and the issue was known but not widespread.

Foxboro, Massachuesetts

I have to wonder what the hold up is.

I contacted Sears on 11/28/2011 concerning my Kenmore Elite Range which has the same safety problems as those identified with other Kenmore Elite ranges (manufactured by Frigidaire).  I was told that my appliance is not covered by the recall. Referred tp this agency.

Purchase date: 7/1/2005
Model: 790.99122405
Serial: VF52527573
Problems:
1.  Used bridge and gridle on left side. Turned off, but "hot surface" light will not turn off.  Unplugged the appliance, left unplugged for > 8 hours, replugged.  "Hot surface" light comes on, will not turn off, although left side burners are off/not warm.
2.  Right front triple element burner. Various problems. (i) Will not turn off. (ii) Last used with 2 elements and heat could not be controlled (lowered).  Had to unplug to turn off.  (iii) When last used, turned heat to "LO", but temperature would not lower.  (iv) Unplugged to turn off, left unplugged for > 8 hours, replugged and triple element (all 3) heated without the burner being "turned on" with the switch, even though I had not used the 3-elements when last used.  Heat was on high.  Heat is uncontrolled.
3.  Oven does not heat up to temperature set.
4.  Convection oven will not turn on.

This particular unit is not on the recall list, but it appears to have the same problems.
justification: The incident involves uncontrolled heating and malfunctioning elements, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Frigidaire electric range new from Lowe's on 08-25-2002. About 2 weeks ago this range caught fire in a very catastrophic way. What caught fire was the Electronic Oven Control with Clock and Timer. Flames and sparkes were shooting out the back of the unit. The range was NOT in use at the time. Fortunately there was someone in the next room that heard the noise, came into the kitchen, saw what was happing and pulled the range away from the wall before the flames spead to the wall. That quick action prevented any damage to the house but had this happened while no one was home or at night it could have easly caught the house on fire.  With people asleep it have even been fatal. It concerns me that this product had the potential to fail in such a way. It seems to me that appliances should not just burst into flames like this.

The appliance is a Frigidaire electric range ES100 Control with coil surface elements.
Model Number: FEF326ASB
Serial Number: VF22615109
justification: The incident involved a fire with potential for severe damage, but no actual injury or death occurred, and the likelihood of such an event is unlikely based on the description.

My 13 year old was burned while trying to remove her toast.  I contacted Hamilton beach and they said this model was not recalled but they could send me out the same toaster for $19.95 shipping.
