incident_description:
Here is an excerpt from the email letter I sent to Kitchen Aid Consumer Dept.

"There is a problem with the Roll-Out Rack on my range.  It is very slick on the top of the shelf, as well as the roll-out rack itself.  There is no back stopper on the shelf, and food pans tend to slide backwards when I slide out the rack.  This has caused serious trouble, trying to retrieve the pans.  The latest incident was a sheet full of cookies.  The sheet slid backward as I pulled out the rack, and tipped the pan, dumping the whole batch into the rear of the oven!  This is a dangerous and frustrating situation.  According to the manual, this rack should have a tilted-up stopper, as the others in the range do.  I would like Kitchen Aid to send me the proper rack for my range and prevent further cooking disasters."  

model: KGRS505XSS01  serial: D10240130

This is a gas range that I purchased in January of 2011.  The range has two ovens.   The Roll-Out Rack I am concerned about is a safety issue.  The rack is a special feature, withball-bearings to facilitate removing pans.  But it has no back stopper to prevent the pans from sliding backwards off the slick rack, and tipping into the rear of the range cavity.  That is what happened to me.  In addition to the danger to persons using it (I burned my hand trying to retrieve the pan) it could constitute a fire hazard if the contents of a pan were dumped into the bottom of the oven, at the burner level.  I was lucky it was only a pan of cookies .Although they became a burned lump in the bottom of the oven, they did not catch fire thanks to the quick action of my grandson.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and poses a potential fire hazard, indicating a significant safety issue.

incident_description: I own a Rival Crock Pot Stone ware slow cooker. One handle fell off and the other handle has one end where the plastic is broken off and is loose at that end. While using the unit 11-17-2011, I almost dropped the whole unit and had a chance of getting scolded. I called the  phone number [REDACTED] on the unit 11-18-2011 and the person [REDACTED]told me he could do nothing about it because my model number 38601 is not part of the recall they had due to handles breaking. I feel this is a real safety hazard and the product should be recalled.
justification: The incident describes a near-miss with potential for scalding due to broken handles, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I placed some pork ribs in a 9 x 13 Pyrex baking dish, then placed the baking dish into a preheated 450 degree oven.  The Pyrex dish dates back to 2002, and it had no chips, dings, or large scratches that would have caused me to be concerned about the safety of the dish.  Fifteen minutes into the baking of the ribs, I heard a loud explosion come from my kitchen.  I looked in the oven and discovered the Pyrex dish had burst into hundreds of glass shards.  I was lucky that this happened while the dish was in the oven, because those shards combined with the force of that explosion could have caused me serious injuries otherwise.
I have read that Consumers Union expressed concerns about these products.  Why has nothing been addressed with Pyrex and other makers of such products?  Shower doors, car windows, and other glass products are required to be made so that they do not present a threat of serious injury; why are potentially explosive glass baking dishes being ignored?
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded but no injuries occurred, as the incident happened while the dish was in the oven.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore gas stove (white, 4 burner Plus).  It was purchased in 2000.  I was gently cleaning a spill off of the inside of the glass front with a damp paper towel, when it suddenly shattered into hundreds (thousand?) small pieces of glass.  The appliance was at room temperature at the time as I had not used the oven in approximately 36 hours.  I was holding the door at the time and it did not come in contact with any other item, just my hand supporting it and a damp paper towel wiping the glass.
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: My Sears Kenmore electric, smooth top range, model number beginning with 655, nearly burned down the house this weekend. The broiler came on by itself and superheated, filling the house with smoke and toxic fumes. Walls and adjacent counters also hot. Nothing appeared on the display. The cancel/off would not work. Stove had to be pulled out and unplugged to make it stop. Thank god I was home and heard the smoke alarms from outside. The house still smells like burned plastic and wiring. This is an extremely dangerous and scary malfunction.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and potential for injury, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: While using the self-cleaning cycle on my oven for the first time, the outer glass on the oven door shattered into a million tiny, boiling hot pieces.  The cycle had been running for approximately 1hr and 45 minutes.  Thankfully no one was in the kitchen at the time.  Pieces of glass were found several feet away in all directions.  Over one hour later the glass is still piping hot and popping and crackling.
justification: The oven door shattered, posing a significant hazard, but no one was injured as the kitchen was unoccupied.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Elite Refrigerator with 2 doors and the freezer on the bottom. Model #795.77554600. Manufacture date of 06/2006. The lights have been staying on with the doors closed. I opened it last night and found the top rack was really warm, lights were very hot, plastic cover covering the light bulbs was warped and the light bulb holders are scorched. I had to unscrew the light bulbs and need to get at least some of it repaired.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator with potential fire hazard due to overheating lights, but no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I had my wall oven set to 375 degrees an error occured on the screen "F10" and the oven would not turn off.  The gas continued to flow with the oven's flame.  I couldn't make the oven turn off. I had to go outside and turn the main gas off to the house. There were no injuries or damages.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that required turning off the main gas supply, but there were no injuries or damages.

incident_description:
My Kenmore dishwasher the control pannel was burning , there was smoke coming out, I saw 
spark,the smell was like burning rubberor cable,  after that the machine shut down, there is no power on the control panel.
justification: The incident involved smoke and sparks but no reported injury, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: I was cooking bread in the oven in glass pans.  The oven would not shut off.  If my children were cooking it could have been disaterous.  The oven broiler turned on and would not shut off.  The main breaker in our house has to be off or the stove turns on!
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury occurred, though there was potential for harm if children were involved.

incident_description: Our Kenmore oven door shattered all over the entire kitchen floor. We contacted Sears and they said that because the stove was slightly over 1 year old that we would be responsible for the repair. We had a repairman out and replaced the glass at OUR expense. @ $269 and time out of work!
justification: The oven door shattered, causing damage and inconvenience, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The front door of the dishwasher was shorted out. The dish washer was not on. Before I realized it the house was full of smoke and burnt electric smell. Before i could pull out the baseboard and the mounting screws the plastic on the door started to warp and melt. There was no fire but I am sure it was only a matter of time.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher and potential fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Sear Kenmore Elite French door refrigerato with bottom freezer Mod #795.77554600, SN 606KR0024 Purchased 12/06 $2400.00.

We gave ourselves a Christmas gift in 2006. We liked the refrigerator but after having it at home for a couple of weeks during the holidays and having a closer look at the unit found it lacking in Kenmore appearance and quality. It just seemed flimsy. 
About two years ago we opened the refrigerator doors and found the light cover melted. We thought we had left the doors open. Purchased a new light cover and though nothin of it.
Last night I opened the door and found the inside of the refrigerator hot about 70* even though the refrigerator was running. The lights were very hot and every thing inside  warm. Pressing both door switches simultaniously discovered the lights did not turn off. Figured I would remove the lights and see if the refrigerator would get cool. After a closer look I noticed the light sockets are brown. I though to myself this could have gooten much hotter and perhaps caused a fire!
I figured I could remove the lights and see if the refrigerator would cool. I wet a papet towel and grabbed one of the bulbs, as soon as I did that the light explded into small fragments striking me just below my eyes.
This morning I called Sears and after being transfeed around and hangin up and calling again, Finally found someone that said they would be out on Monday and fix the problem free of charge. Then tried slling me a one year warranty for $265. 
I am glad all they are fixing is my refrigerator,
justification: The incident resulted in injury from exploding light fragments, but the likelihood of such an event is unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: My Kenmore refrigerator, Model 106.53652300, manufacturered in February 2004 caught on fire.  I awoke at 2 a.m. in morning on November 22, 2011 to an arching noise and a smoke filled kitchen.  I was able to pull the refrigerator out from the wall and unplug the cord.  Fortunately, no one was injured and no property damage took place, except for the damage to the frigerator.  I was shocked at the number of similar complaints I found online and no recalls have occurred on this product.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire but no injuries or property damage occurred, fitting severity level 2. Online complaints suggest this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Several months ago, I received as a gift a Martha Stewart Enamel Teapot purchased at Macys in Providence, RI.

Even though I read the directions to use a potholder and that the handle was not heat resistant, I did forget one day and dropped the pot on my tile floor, dented the  floor and the teapot and spilled scalding hot water all over the floor.  Thankfully, I jumped out of the way and did not get burned.

This Model #107 is hazardous and should be taken off the market. I can't believe Martha Stewart, with all her emphasis on safety, would put out such a product.  

This item should be removed from the market as soon as possible as so not hurt anyone in the future.  

Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a dropped teapot and spilled hot water, but no injury occurred as the user jumped out of the way.

incident_description:
While I was heating food in my Westinghouse microwave, flames came out from behind the aluminum plate on the right inside wall.  We had no metal inside the oven.

The microwave is model WST 3501, manufactured in May of 2004.  The serial number is 5503500405 029589.
justification: Flames emerged from the microwave, indicating an incident, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Excess natural gas filled kitchen from malfunctioning gas oven ignitor. Malfunction occurred after oven reached operating temperature and into 20-30 minutes of operation. 

Range/oven is a Frigidaire Gallery model FGGF305MKFA purchased in 2009. After reporting this to Frigidaire and expressing our concerns about safety, the only reply is a form letter to have it serviced by one of their authorized service centers. The range/oven only carries a one year warranty.

Range is only two years old and oven is only used about 15 times a year. Online research reveals that a weak ignitor is the cause. The gas odor was quite strong raising our fears of an explosion.
justification: Excess natural gas filling the kitchen poses a significant risk of explosion, though no injury or death occurred in this incident.

incident_description: i was sitting watching tv and heard weird noise from the kitchen,it was coming from the kitchen,further invest. and  burning smell,it was coming from the dishwasher, the panel started on fire and the coil  heater on the bottom stayed on..the machine was not in use at time or on.i had to pull the fuse out to stop the coil from burning down the house.i took the panel off and thier was a huge burn hole. i called the company to see if thier was a recall and no thier wasnt,and they told me my warrenty was over and nothing they can do about it.i looked online and people had the same issue with the same dishwasher. so i filed a complaint to the bbb. i have the reciet and pictures of the burnt panel. i no longer have this dishwasher.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, which posed a significant risk but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: After making a pot of coffee the coffee maker was left on for somewhere between 30 and 45 minutes and after that it was turned off.  Approximately 20 minutes after it was turned off there was smoke coming out of it and the heating element under the pot was red.  At that point the maker was unplugged and carried outside.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a red-hot heating element but no reported injury or death, indicating a non-injury incident with possible fire risk.

incident_description: After brewing a pot of coffee we started to hear noises from the coffee maker.  The coffee was boiling in the carafe and smoke started coming out of the coffee maker.  We immediately unplugged the coffee maker and brought it outside where it continued to smoke.  The house smelled like burnt electrical wires.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker causing smoke and a burnt smell, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: EWave coffee maker model EWCM12BP2   When pouing coffeee the top part of the handle has separated from the caraffe causing a potential for burn injuries.
justification: The incident describes a potential for burn injuries due to a coffee maker handle separating, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: GE Profile Model PDW9200LOOBB serial ML912874B  Heat did not cut off.  Cut unit off and thought it was off.  Smelled burning wire and checked dishwasher.  Very hot and melted interior coatings.  Cut off at breaker.  Fire would have been imminent.  Purchased about 4-5 years ago.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that overheated and melted interior coatings, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I had a Pyrex baking dish EXPLODE in my oven on Thanksgiving.  The food had been in the dish overnight in the refrigerator.  I took it out of the refrigerator and let it set for half an hour to bring it to room temperature before placing it in the oven.  Had I been opening the oven to check on food at the time of the explosion, I ÃÂ or someone else in the kitchen- would have surely been seriously injured.  The food was obviously ruined because we were afraid of glass shards.  My husband cut himself while cleaning it up today, because there were so many tiny sharp pieces, and well as huge shards of glass.  As a footnote, I am not a beginner cook- this was the 33rd Thanksgiving dinner I have prepared.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (husband cut himself) and potential for serious injury if someone had been near the oven during the explosion.

incident_description:
LG Refrigerator LFX25960ST--interior light unit stayed on when refrigerator door was closed causing the unit to melt.  The smell of melting plastic alerted us to the problem. Cover of unit melted; light sockets blackened; roof of refrigerator above unit blistered.
Removed light bulbs, refrigerator now has no interior lighting.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator light staying on, causing melting and damage but no injury or death.

incident_description: LG refridgerator light melted housing and scorched the bulb holders.  Lights did not shut off.  The temperature control unit came off the mounting the ceiling of the refridgerator.  The extremely high heat caused by high wattage lightbulbs melted the housing and caused my Thanksgiving dinner to become unsafe due to the high temperature in the refridgerator.  My turkey had a temperature of 58 degrees F!  Model is not under warranty.
justification: The incident caused property damage and spoiled food but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
Came home from dinner to notice that my LG Fridge model LFC25760SB was warm inside and smelled of melting plastic. The two lights on the top of the fridge were extremely hot and had completely melted the housing that encloses them. The housing was hanging down almost 2 inches as the retaining screws had melted through the plastic holding it in. The plastic is turning brown from smoke and the entire surface of the top of the fridge is warped from the massive amount of heat generated. It is frightful to think that had I been gone longer there could have been a fire. 

There is a buzzer that warns you of an open door which was not in operation upon my return and the doors were shut. This is a very serious defect that could have cost someone their home or their life. After some research on the internet I found many others with similar problems.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Bosch dishwasher that runs so hot I have to open my drawers around it to try to cool the area and countertop. (This doesn't help.)
The control panel died and I paid to have someone replace it (350.00) a couple years ago.
A couple weeks ago I learned a friend's kitchen caught fire when his Bosch dishwasher overheated. His house is gone and they are living out of a motel for the next several months. 
I checked out the report by CBS2 and I see others have replaced the control panel in lieu of the dishwasher (the companies, that is).
I called Bosch. They said their dishwashers "run hot" and that is normal.
Then when I said I plan to follow up, Bosch said, "oh, we cant tell you if yours is fine. You have to determine that" (paraphrasing). I did determine that! I called them and already my panel had to be replaced once. I am concerned there is a problem that Bosch is not owning up to. I think Bosch should look into a recall of all their dishwashers with control panel and heating problems. My serial no. is SHU43C02UC/22. They said it is not part of their current recall, but clearly there is a problem since it runs so hot and since the control panel had to be replaced once so far at my expense. This is not right. Consumers should not be left to handle and/or "diagnose" their own fire hazards. We do not have access to their database that lists known problems and serial numbers reporting problems.

*Consumer update: I want to specific that problem occurs in the POWER SCRUB PLUS mode. I run the dishwasher in the regular mode with the drawers open because I am afraid to use it in the other mode. (That is when it gets so hot that the countertops and cabinets heat up.)
justification: The incident describes a dishwasher overheating to the point of causing a house fire, which resulted in death (friend's house destroyed). The likelihood is possible given the recurring issues reported by multiple users.

incident_description:
I have a Jenn-Air dishwasher and the heating element stayed on all night after we ran it - and melted some plastic dishes.  It heated up the counter and I am concerned that it could have caught our house on fire.

Model# - JDB1250AWP
Serial# - 36463971LG
justification: The heating element malfunction caused property damage (melted dishes and heated counter) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I was in my kitchen when I heard a popping noise come from my Whirlpool side by side refrigerator. After that, smoke started coming from the bottom of the refrigerator and it was progressively getting worse.  There was also a strong smell like that of an electrical fire.  My husband came downstairs, moved the refrigerator and unplugged it.  I am very thankful that we were home when this happened.  If not, I feel certain that it would have caught on fire.  

The technician recommended by my 2-10 Home Warranty company came to fix the refrigerator today.  The problem was the relay switch.  The switch is obviously burned.  I have saved the burned switch and some of the wires that he clipped from the refrigerator.

Please check into this.  I am afraid to leave my home.  I am not confident that this will not happen again.  The technician did tell me that the replacement relay switch has a cap that should smother the fire if that happened again.  This tells me that there is a known problem with this switch.  I do not find any recall information about this.

My refrigerator serial number is SM2926101

Thank You
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is considered possible (3) as the technician indicated a known issue with the relay switch.

incident_description:
We left for Thanksgiving for 5 days, came home and our dishwasher was extremely hot.....apparently the heating element had been going the entire time we had been gone.  Not only did this cost us an arm and a leg in electricity, I'm sure, but out entire house could have burned to the ground.  Even now, I'm still trying to figure out how to turn it off.  And, Maytag's customer hotline which says "call anytime" is apparently closed until Monday.  

It's a Maytag quietseries 300 and is apparently involved in a recent recall.

I'm thankful the house didn't burn down, but am really upset about this.  And I don't want my defective dishwasher repaired.....I want a new one.  $150-$250 rebate doesn't buy a new one, and I don't want a stainless steel front.
justification: The dishwasher was extremely hot, which could have caused a fire, but no one was injured.

incident_description: Oven overheats out of control and flashes F1 on display. Unable to turn applaince off except by unplugging from the wall. Stove top Range became extremely hot and unable to touch due to heat.
justification: The oven overheated and became dangerously hot, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Shortly after opening a can of pineapples her husband stepped on a fine piece of metal from the can- it was a 1/2 inch in length and the width of thread. She removed the can from the trash with the lid to it and was able to locate where  the shard of metal came from.  The shard itself was accidentally discarded.

The can opener is designed to remove the entire lid from the can.  The consumer indicated that her concerns were with the shard of metal that could have fallen into the food while opening it.

She has not contacted the firm or the retailer and will not contact them. She has discontinued the use of the can opener.
justification: No injury occurred, but a metal shard was found, indicating an incident. The likelihood is possible as the can opener design may occasionally leave metal fragments.

incident_description:
Last night we had our G.E. range model # JBP74MWW oven set to 450 degrees in order to cook a pizza. After about 15 minutes we heard a loud explosion and rushed to the kitchen, only to find glass all over the floor, the glass panel on the oven door had exploded in a million pieces. Luckily no one was in the kitchen at the time, and serious injury was avoided.
I did an internet search, and found out that this had happened before to other G.E. range owners.
I took pictures and can send them if needed!
justification: The oven door glass exploded, but no one was injured. Similar incidents have been reported by other G.E. range owners, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: While preheating my oven last night, I heard a buzzing noise and went back into the kitchen to see sparks and flames, shooting out of the back and top of the range. If it had not been for the quick actions of my husband, who knows what might have happened. He quickly shut off the breaker and gas line, as it is a dual fuel range. The back and top of the entire control panel was burned. This could have had disastrous consequeces!
justification: The incident involved sparks and flames, but no injury or death occurred due to quick actions.

incident_description: Control board caught fire
justification: A control board catching fire is an incident with potential for injury, but the description does not mention any harm.

incident_description: My wife was melting butter in a Anchor Hocking glass baking disk.  All of a sudden the dish exploded sending glass and melted butter all over.  Luckily my wife was not injured by the flying glass but she cold have been.  The explosion was so strong, she found pieces of shattered glass in the next room.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass dish causing a mess but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are possible but not common, hence likelihood 3.

incident_description:
During the first quarter of 2001 my wife and I purchased a Kenmore model XC K 49 19920 ÃÂMicrowave-Hood CombinationÃÂ appliance from SearsÃÂs retail store in New Hartford, NY.

On October 16, 2001 the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced a safety recall of microwave oven/exhaust fan hood combination units sold under the WhirlpoolÃÂ®, KitchenAidÃÂ®, and KenmoreÃÂ® brand names that had serial numbers beginning with XC due to the problem of overheating and catching fire.

For whatever reason my wife and I did not receive notice of the recall. (We assume it may have been sent to our physical, street address rather than our mailing, Post Office box address.)

In any event, in August 2010 our microwave/hood unit began ÃÂsparkingÃÂ and making a ÃÂgrindingÃÂ noise. 

We stopped using the unit and contacted Sears to arrange for repair. At that time we were advised the unit was subject to a CPSC recall and the repair would be made at no cost to us.

August 20, 2010 the Sears service technician came to our home to repair the unit. As part of the repair a ÃÂdiskÃÂ had to be sealed in place to ÃÂprevent steam or oil vapors from reaching the wave-guide.ÃÂ However, silicone sealant included in the technicianÃÂs ÃÂrepair kitÃÂ had hardened and was unusable. As a result, the technician attempted to make the repair with an alternate, construction grade silicone sealant.

The repair appeared to be effective and we resumed using the unit within several days.

In early October 2011 the unit began making the same sound as it had in August 2010. When we contacted Sears we were advised we would be responsible for the cost of repair ($129 plus parts) and that the previous repair was warranted for 3-months only. When I contacted Whirlpool (manufactured of the unit) I was told the CPSC file was closed and they offered no assistance other than to sell me a new unit for $259.

Since:

a) The unit contained an original manufacturing defect which was NOT corrected in August 2010 b) To use the unit poses a threat of overheating and fire 

We are dismayed at Sears and WhirlpoolÃÂs lack of concern and failure to act in a responsible manner to correct the problem once and for all.
justification: The microwave exhibited sparking and grinding noises, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore french door refrigerator-model #795.77302601.   The refrigerator light would not go off.   Light bulbs got very hot.  There was a smell of  hot plastic.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator light that got very hot and emitted a smell of hot plastic, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Range Model# 790.79834400 was purchased in December 2004.  It has always worked well and never gave any problems until tonight.  

Tonight my wife was using the oven at  425 degrees, baking some pizza bread.  The oven had been on about 35 to 45 minutes when we heard an "arcing or sparking" sound coming from the kitchen.  My son said he saw flashing occuring from somewhere near the display, at the top of the unit.  This may have come from behind the unit, a vent is immediately below the top.  It appears that there is a small amount "electric smoke" residue on the top. 

The breaker was tripped.  I unplugged the range and turned off the gas.  After doing a little investigation on the internet, it appears that this is a problem that has occurred with quite a few Kenmore/Frigidaire Dual Fuel ranges as well as other types.

I don't know if you can provide any feedback, but I'd like to know if there are any proceedings for this problem.

I talked to a Sears hotline guy on the 800 number and got a person who confirmed my information and was intending to send out a service man.  I declined to have one come out until I find out more information.

It appears that some people have had luck getting their units replaced with a newer or different model.  I'm not sure that I want this one repaired with what I've read about other incidents.

Any information or suggestions you can provide may be helpful.
justification: The incident involved electrical arcing and smoke but no injury or death, and similar issues have been reported with this model.

incident_description: Left front burner on a Frigidaire smooth top stove will not turn off. Must shut off the house circuit breaker for the stove to shut off the burner
justification: The burner not turning off is an incident with no injury, and such malfunctions are unlikely to occur frequently.

incident_description: In August 2011, we received the Cuisinart TOB-40 as a gift.  It worked great at first.  We used it for multiple methods, toasting and baking.  About two weeks ago, after using the baking setting, I turned the machine as usual by turning it to off as well as turning the temperature to the lowest setting. I walked away and few minutes later smelled a melting plastic type of smell.  I went back into the kitchen and saw the heating element was still going.  I unplugged everything and eventually and the machine cooled down.  I used it again this evening, and the same thing happened.  Without any power feeding the machine, it was still getting power somehow.  I researched other reviews about the machine and saw the same comments appearing.  I called Cuisinart and although they said they are sending a replacement of the machine, I do not trust this product will be safe to use.  Cuisinart said the unit shouldn't function like that and I have to agree.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning appliance that could potentially cause harm, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Item: GE Rotisserie Convection Oven
Model: 898691 53
UPC: 60538898691
Purchased: Wal Mart Kansas City, MO 64145
DOP: 11/05/2011

Used four time for toast only. Unit was plugged in and had not been in use for a minimum of 72 hours. Loud noise coming from the glass door of the unit exploding. Sending glass in small particles in the air throughout the kitchen. Blew handle off the glass door. No one injured. No heat associated with the unit at time of explosion. Electrical cord and unit not hot or warm to the touch. 

If a child was present, they would have been harmed by the flying glass. Informed Wal-Mart through their [REDACTED] number and email. Was told to return unit for store credit or another unit. Doesn't anyone have concerns as to why this happened? I do am following through with this until someone from the manufacturer would like the product back.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of the oven door, but no one was injured, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but are documented.

incident_description: Dishwasher did not work and called Maytag repair.They showed me both the control panel and wiring harness was totally melted and burnt.Said it would cost over 300 in parts alone to repair.Paid the 99 dollar service call and started calling Maytag customer service, as the machine was only months out of the 1 year warranty. I got nowhere with them.My wife, who is batteling lung cancer called coporate and broke down on the phone as we can not afford this right now because of medical bills, etc. They agreed to replace the panel and harness for just the service call finally. How do I know this will not happen again?After seeing reviews on the product, and tv reports they had to have known it was a defect in design.Replacing with the same parts will not fix the obvious problem
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with no reported injuries, but significant inconvenience and financial stress, especially given the context of medical bills.

incident_description: Kitchenaid Dishwasher Model # KUDP01FLSS6. My door retention cord broke allowing the very heavy  door to fly open and hit my elderly mother causing an open wound all down her shin with added bruising which was severe enough that it took her weeks to heal.  Separately, we also had to have the repairman out to replace and/or recalibrate the electrical panel at least 6 times, becoming expensive with costly repairs. Eventually, even though the dishwasher was only 3 years old at the time, the repairman said that it would keep happening and informed me to just buy a new dishwasher. This problem began only less than 2 years after purchasing the dishwasher, so didn't feel as though I should have to buy a new one.  We haven't been able to budget for a new dishwasher, therefore we have elected to just leave this lemon of a dishwasher sit in my kitchen for now.
justification: The dishwasher door caused an open wound and severe bruising to an elderly person, requiring weeks to heal, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The repeated electrical panel issues suggest a systemic problem, making recurrence likely (4).

incident_description: My KitchenAid dishwasher caught on fire in the middle of the night while not running.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Caller washed lid for large bowl, realized that it was loose, turned it upside down to slightly tighten it when it exploded in his hand sending glass shards downward and outward in a 8 to 10 foot radius in all directions.

Bowl was still slightly wet but was not hot or wet.

Caller describes lid as "going off like a bomb" stating also that the explosion of glass did not go upward at all.

Caller would like to report this product as a safety hazard to avoid anyone else from becoming injured.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of glass shards but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the event.

incident_description: Residents set the dishwasher to normal cycle with heated dry at about 1130 on 11/12/11 and left the home about 1145. They arrived home at about 0045 on 11/13/11 to find the dishwasher completely consumed by fire, which had spread to a cabinet and the trash and recycling containers next to it. The fire appears to have burned itself out. The residents state they have not had any issues with the dishwasher. They have only lived in the home about 2 weeks and have used it 3-4 times.They state they did not overload the dishwasher. The did have two plastic containers with lids on the top shelf of the dishwasher, however they would have been too large to fall through the spaces in the racks. The investigaion has placed the area of origin at the dishwasher. The cause remains undetermined. The electrical connection was intact and the circut breaker did trip.
justification: The incident involved a fire that caused property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but have been documented.

incident_description:
Dough-Nu-Matic by NOSTALGIA 
The device is a fire hazard and electrocution hazard. If the Flippers become out of alignment or jammed for any reason, including stuck food the scoop will make contact with an un insulated electrical connector for the heating tray element Causing Possible 120v shock, or an electrical fire witch heats the oil to its flash-point causing the fire to grow rapidly fueled by cooking oil
justification: The description indicates potential for electrocution and rapid fire growth, which could lead to death, hence severity level 4. The likelihood is possible (3) given the specific conditions required for the hazard to occur.

incident_description: I have a Whirlpool Microwave that caught on fire when it was not being used. We were packing for a trip in my home when my child yelled that the micro had smoke coming out of it. If this would have happened a day later, while away my entire house could of burnt down.
justification: The microwave caught fire but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such incidents are not common but possible.

incident_description: Microwave contines running when the door is closed and unit is off.
justification: The microwave running when it should be off is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: My Kitchen Aid dishwasher started on fire last night.  The control panel was sparking and black smoke was coming from either side.  The dishwasher was 3/4 through the cycle and began making a loud noise.  I tried to open the dishwasher door to stop the cycle but it would not.  I tried to 'Cancel' the cycle but it would not stop.  Only after turning off the circuit breaker did the dishwasher stop.  The burning and noise dissipated after 5 minutes.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and emitted black smoke, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: While baking a chicken in the wall oven, the inside glass of the double glass panel door exploded and shattered inward.  The oven can still be used but the area closest to the largest hole in the glass cooks a bit quicker than the remainder of the oven.  I have placed aluminum foil over the worst of the broken glass portion.  Also, this explosion was not caused because the door was hit with an object as Sears was alluding to.  This was not previously reported because my oven was past its initial warranty.  It has not yet been repaired due to shortaqge of funds.  Also, the oven was properly pre-heated before using.
justification: The glass door exploded but no injury was reported, and the oven remains functional with minor cooking inconsistencies.

incident_description:
Whirlpool double oven model# rbd275prb00

Glass doors electric in wall

Top oven door exploded with 3 people and a cat near by. The oven was not in use or being touched at the time. Just exploaded out of no where.
justification: The oven door exploded unexpectedly, but no injuries were reported to the people or cat nearby.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore Electric smooth top electric oven Model number #665.95794000.  We set the oven to 350 degrees to bake cookies.  The top element of the stove never turned off, so the cookies started to burn. We took the cookies out, and turned the oven off.  10 minutes later, I noticed the inside of the oven was glowing red, so I looked, and the top element was still on.  When I opened up the oven, a puff of black smoke came out of the oven.  I tried to turn the oven on and off several times, but it did not turn off.  I finally had to run downstairs and turn the breaker off.  My incident is similar to many on this post.

http://www.appliance.net/2009/recallfrigidaire-and-kenmore-smoothtop-electric-ranges-due-to-fire-hazard-1369
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred. Similar incidents have been reported, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Upon opening the refrigerator this evening, we noticed a burning, electrical smell. With some investigation, we discovered the two lights housed at the "roof" of the refrigerator were not going out when the door was closed or the buttons depressed.  We removed the housing, with gloves on, and it was warped and melted. We removed the bulbs...the area around them is brown and scorched.
Hard to know what would have happened if we hadn't discovered the problem when we did.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with visible damage, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
After using my Kenmore model 790.95300 Flat Top Range at 170 degrees, I turned the oven off. About a half hour later, my fire alarm went off. I ran downstairs and noticed a bunch of smoke in the kitchen. I opened my oven door and noticed that the heating elements were glowing extremely bright, as if my oven was on full heat. When I looked at the buttons, the oven was still showing as off. I turned the oven on and then back off again, but the element would not turn off. There was a bunch of smoke pouring from the oven. I then went and flipped the breaker outstide. 
I completed a search on the internet and noticed there were at least 25 other people complaining about this exact problem with this same model.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a malfunctioning oven, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We own a Sears Kenmore smooth top range oven, model #79096009601, serial # VF71649412. This oven is only 3 years old, installed new in a newly built home, and the front burners will turn on to high by themselves once turned off and get stuck in the high position. The rear left back burner now does not function as it turns on and then off repeatedly no matter what temperature, so cannot get a consistent cooking degree. We have woken up to our son informing us the stove burner was on, when it had previously been off, and my husband has burnt his hand, thinking the burner had been off and resulting in the pan getting so hot that when he grabbed it he sustained a burn to his hand. This is a fire hazard and is similar to what I am seeing online in another model that was recalled by Sears, similar make, etc. We cannot cook on any burners but one now, and this issue needs to be resolved, as I have lost complete faith in Sears/Kenmore products and will not recommend them to anyone I know professionally or personally.
justification: The incident involves a stove burner turning on by itself, causing a burn injury and posing a fire hazard, which aligns with severity level 3 due to the injury sustained.

incident_description:
At the time of the incident, the Kenmore Elite dishwasher was idle. The machine had been used and emptied the night before on 11/16/11. Around 5:30pm of 11/17, a smell of burning plastic was found to be coming from the kitchen. The electronic smell was strongest along the top of the dishwasher door. No smoke was seen. But there was a faint sizzling sound at the door panel. 

The power was shut off at the main breaker and the door panel was removed to inspect the instrumentation and control panel. There appears to be a burnt resister (see photos) at position R28. As well there is a capacitor at position C7 (see photos) that is bubbling or bulging at the top. No further damage can be seen on the electronic control panel board.

No one was harmed or injured.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and electrical component damage, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: We bought the Lollacup about 1 month ago on Amazon.com.  About two weeks ago, my 15 month old son was drinking from the Lollacup and he threw it off his highchair to the hardwood floor.  The plastic lid broke.  One of the "bumps" on top of the cup broke off at the lid, creating a small part about .5" x .5".  Since the broken part was the lid, I removed the lid and let him continue use the cup.  Today he dropped the cup and the "foot" broke off the handle/base creating another small part and a very sharp broken edge.  My son's throwing and dropping of the cup is just normal toddler behavior and I believe this cup does not meet safety standards.  It says on the package it is for babies 9 months and up.
justification: The incident involved the cup breaking into small parts with sharp edges, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
About 8 months ago, I was cooking dinner on the stove top and the lid to my pot just popped while I was cooking a pasta casserole. I thought maybe I had tapped the lid with my fork. Today the same thing happened while my wife was cooking our daughters dinner. The lid basically exploded, while she was heating up her food. The glass lid shattered into hundreds of pieces just as it did when i was cooking. The glass went into the food and onto the floor.  

We have a gas stove and the flame was not on its highest setting in either case.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but the glass lid shattered into hundreds of pieces, which is a safety hazard.

incident_description: EXPLODING glass door Black&Decker TOASTER OVEN Model T01420B. I was using it to toast bread. No one was hurt this time! But someone could have. I have not seen a recall. But there are a lot of people have had the same thing happen.
justification: The glass door exploded but no one was hurt, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as many people have reported the same issue.

incident_description: 175v sensor attached only to the burner indicator light detached when I closed the oven door, connected with the metal cover on the back of the unit and shorted out. There was a huge flash of blue light, the wiring melted, and burned the inside of the back cover. The entire range is no longer working, and there are no visible safety fuses in the unit wiring.
justification: The incident involved a significant electrical short causing damage to the oven but no reported injuries.

incident_description: My Cuisinart Fully Automatic Burr, Grind & Brew programable coffee maker model #DGB-700BC, serial #70810C was used to make coffee this morning.  After the coffee had brewed and was in the carafe, the hot plate surface the carafe sits on overheated to the point of turning red, started smoking and melting the plastic base of the appliance.  It was removed from the house for risk of fire.
justification: The coffee maker overheated, causing smoke and melting, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says that she was melting butter.  She heard a pop sound.  She went in the kitchen and saw a fire in the microwave.  It was set for one minute but it did not last a minute before the fire started.  She says there is a rack that goes on top of the unit.  She says one of the racks inside the microwave is melted.  She feels that their needs to be a recall on product. She says the unit still works.  This item needs to be recalled, melting butter should not cause a fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injury or death was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as fires in microwaves are not common but can happen under certain conditions.

incident_description: We have a Kitchen Aid Dishwasher. My husband smelled something burning from it while I was running a cycle. The machine is now non operable. When looking in in manual it states that the heating circuit is malfunctioning. I was made aware of the current issues that have been happening due to the heating elements catching on fire on the news and realized the potential danger these machines have been causing due to this issue. Unfortunatley my warranty is no longer valid.
justification: The dishwasher emitted a burning smell and became non-operable, indicating a malfunction without injury.

incident_description: I was baked a vegetarian shepherd's pie in an 9x13 Pyrex dish, and the dish exploded.  The dish was less than 3 months old and had never been cracked, dropped, broken, or cleaned with abrasive products.  It was purchased at Target in October 2011 as part of a set of 3 Pyrex dishes with lids.  For the dish, I placed room temperature filling into the dish and put the dish into a 350 degree oven.  It cooked for about 45 minutes, and I removed the pan to a wooden trivet.  Shortly after I removed the pan and placed it on the trivet, it shattered.  The small shards were all over our kitchen and in the food.  No injuries were sustained other than glass splinters in my fingers.
justification: Glass splinters in fingers indicate minor injuries, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common with proper use of Pyrex dishes.

incident_description: I was cooking pork loin in a new pyrex dish at 350 degrees.  It was placed in the oven at room temperature.  When I checked on it about 45 minutes later, the dish had exploded, and the oven was full of glass.  A photo can be provided upon request.  This was to be a meal  prepared for company, and it was ruined.  If I  would have moved the dish a little earlier, it could have exploded, and caused serious injury.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, causing damage but no injury, and the incident could have led to serious injury if handled differently.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore Elite Dishwasher - Model number 665.1626 purchased in 2004 filled our house with the smell of burnt plastic.  Upon taking apart the control panel we discover that the control panel caught fire and melted the housing and the control panel.

Further investigation of this incident has other dishwasher listed on the recall list for the exact same problem but our model is not listed on the recall list and should be!  Luckly we were home and prevented a fire.
justification: The dishwasher's control panel caught fire and melted, but no injury or death occurred. The incident was prevented from escalating due to the homeowners' presence.

incident_description: While cooking eggs at med high heat the rivet on this pan shot across the kitchen and bounced off the wall leaving an indention in the wall
justification: The incident involved a rivet shooting off a pan and causing damage to the wall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My GE microwave starts by itself and gets very hot! It does it in the middle of the night and during the day. I have to unplug it between use and am thinking it should be recalled. I've only had it 8 months. It's a Model JES1451.
justification: The microwave starting by itself and getting very hot poses a risk of fire or damage, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Microwave catches on fire and sparks near thin pad/mechanism on inside, upper right side wall of unit.  Very much an electrical type fire and arching.
justification: The microwave caught fire and sparked, indicating an electrical incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
New electric coffee percolator. Used according to manufacturer's instructions, which were read & followed.
First use: smoke and burning come out around plug on appliance. Loud spark (blue color) around plug on appliance. Circuit braker tripped. Black residue around plug. Black residue on bottom of appliance and on counter. Appliance had been plugged in for only about one and a half (1 1/2) minutes.
justification: The incident involved smoke, sparks, and circuit tripping but no reported injury.

incident_description: I was hand washing a tall drinking glass, and as I was washing the inside of the glass, a large chuck of the cup broke off. The broken edge cut my thumb and index finger knuckle before I could react, and the cuts were so deep I had to go to the ER to have my wounds addressed. I missed one day of work because I could not use my hand.
justification: The incident resulted in deep cuts requiring ER treatment and missed work, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: Electronics that control internal incandescent bulbs did not extinguish bulbs. Bulbs are 2x 60W (came as installed when new) and got very hot, melting plastic to the point that parts fell off, temp was close to igniting (but did not.) Food was heated.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting plastic, but no injury or ignition occurred.

incident_description: Bosch gas range. Oven door has either warped or spring to close it has worn out causing the oven door to not close properly. excessive heat escapes from the oven and has caused several burns to my and my wifes hands. upon studying the problem i have found many many complaints about this stove from other consumers.
justification: The incident describes burns to hands due to excessive heat escaping from the oven, indicating an injury (severity 3). The mention of many similar complaints suggests the issue is likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: Woke up this morning and walked into my kitchen. The room was filled with smoke.  The smoke was coming from my refirgerator.  I was able to pull it out and unplug it, but I'm glad I got there when I did because it was billowing out smoke and I'm glad my entire house did not burn down.  Unfortunately now my entire house smells like smoke.
justification: The incident involved significant smoke but no injury or death, and the likelihood is low as such events are not common.

incident_description: I bought my Macic Chef microwave 4 years ago and haven't had any issues with it untill earlier this year when it quit. I unplugged the machine and plugged it back in that seemed to help I used it for a month or so and then one day it just started to start by itself.  I have looked online and it seems that there are several people that have the same issue as me and theh company doesn't seem to want to fix the issue.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning by starting by itself is an incident with no reported injury, and the issue appears to be common based on online reports.

incident_description:
Kitchenaid Microwave Hood Combination Model KHMS155L beeps in an erratic pattern and then turns on by itself. The display alternates between a 3 minute countdown and the word "PAN". Only unplugging or opening the door makes it stop.

This is a potential fire hazard and there should be a recall on this item. I had a similar problem with my Kitchenaid stove earlier this year and had to pay to have it fixed.
justification: The microwave exhibits erratic behavior and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher control panel randomly caught fire not too long after we started a load of dishes, smoke came out of the front panel and filled the kitchen.  This dishwasher is a serious safety hazard, and I feel lucky that I was able to de-energize it before it got out of control.  The house still smells like smoke.  I took the front panel apart and found the circuit board and connectors melted and black.  I have no confidence in it being safe after repair.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and produced smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The incident was controlled before escalating.

incident_description: About 10 minutes into wash cycle, my family smelled burning plastic and smoke coming from our Kitchen Aid dishwasher, my husband quickly unplugged it, thankfully in time before anything bad could have happened.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning plastic smell, but no actual injury or damage occurred as the dishwasher was unplugged in time.

incident_description: 7 yr. old Whirlpool dishwasher stopped running during wash cycle. My wife said she had been smelling "hot electrical" components during washes in the past. After testing I found the thermal fuse had blown. After replacing the unit ran for a few washes then the smell got worse. Suddenly black smoke came out of the control panel. The fuse blew again and burned this time. I have also had problems with the machine leaking at the tub/door edges. The flexible splash guard is torn and the plastic door liner is warped. I'm done with this machine. Then I heard about the class action lawsuit on 11/17/11.
justification: The incident involved black smoke and electrical burning, but no injury or death was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurring issues and the mention of a class action lawsuit suggest a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
Master Cut 2 knife by Jesco.
When cutting a piece of cheese, the blade separated from the handle. My wife nicked her finger when this happened, but the failure of the product was so quick & sudden that much more serious damage was possible.
These knives have a lifetime warranty, supposedly. I have contacted customer support of the manufacturer, but they just advise returning the product where bought with the original receipt. Unfortunately, this is not possible at this time.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (nick on the finger) due to the blade separating from the handle, indicating a moderate severity. The likelihood is unlikely as such failures are not common but possible with defective products.

incident_description: 11-5-11 was washing dishes in warm water in kitchen sink.  heard a loud bang and the Dansk icecream scooper shot out of the sink and landed in the other side. Sounded like a gun shot. Couldn't hear out of left ear for two days. One part of the end of the scooper shot past my face hitting the refrigerator 8 feet away leaving a mark.  Another small piece ended up on the other side of kitchen table 10 feet away. Not sure where the fluid inside went. Close call to getting hit in the face with this. This was one of the most scarriest experiences I've had. Took my husband and I several minutes to figure out what happened. This could of been a tragedy if it hit me in the face. I am so lucky.  I wish I would of known about the recall sooner.  Thank God a child was not washing this and got seriously hurt.  I have always washed this in the sink. Not sure why now it decided to explode.
justification: The incident caused temporary hearing loss and a close call with potential serious injury, but no lasting harm occurred.

incident_description: Flour sifter handle cut my finger while I was drying it.
justification: The description states a finger was cut, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Range, model #665.95002102.  I was baking at 350 degrees to return to oven being extremely hot, food burned, 'F1' error code beeping on digital display.  Tried to turn the oven off, but it continued to stay glaring hot.  Heat was so intense it could be felt several feet away from oven.  We turned off breaker to get stove to turn off.  It was too hot to move to unplug.  We found instructions online for disconnecting the top broiler element so that we could continue to use the stove until we are able to have it repaired.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and became dangerously hot, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
microwave fan keeps running after it has timed out due to oil and steam vapors in and around wave guide. the consumer product safety commission has recalled 1.8 million microwave hood combinations but not the one i have. it is doing the same thing as the recalled ones. i have a kenmore hmc ultra model no 401.80086700 serial no 915mmo1443 manufactured april 2009 fcc id a31smh17cn
it gets very hot and i am afraid of a fire. it was purchased at sears on 06/05/09
justification: The microwave fan issue poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: The consumer says his wife was cooking bacon.  He says the paper plate went into flames.  He said the bacon was almost done but was not burned.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who sent out a technician.  The technician stated that the magnatron overheated.  A few weeks later the manufacturer determined the microwave was working just fine.  The consumer has seen many reports online about the same issue happening.  The consumer will not plug in this unit again.
justification: The incident involved a paper plate catching fire, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was investigated and deemed non-recurring by the manufacturer, though similar reports exist online.

incident_description: I have a GE Profile PS968S P1SS stainless steel electric range.  I feel the front knobs can be too easily activated.  Tonight I was replacing my counter top coffee maker.  I put the box on top of the electric range stove top.  After a while I smelled and saw smoke and realized that the weight of the box "turned" the fron two knobs and turned on the top burners.  This isn't the forst time when I realized the burners were accidentily activated but couldn't figure out how it happened.  Now I know. The knobs are raised and easily "turned on" if an object is plaxced on the cooking top and extends over the are, touching the knobs.  Thankfully we were still home and able to respond to smoke before a larger fire started.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire risk due to accidental activation of burners, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
A Frigidaire Gas Range, Model number FPGF3081KF, was turned on to start cooking, after several minutes while waiting for it to warm, we noticed the smell of gas.  The oven was warm so some of the burners were working.  I blew into the chamber and could hear that one of the burners then lit.

By this time our house was filled with gas.  Be that it is November in Chicago, the windows to our house were closed.  We opened them to clear out the gas.  The Fire Department was not called.

This expensive model was purchased slightly over one year ago, and the oven is perfectly clean.  We use the oven on average 3 times a week.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak that filled the house, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire department was not called.

incident_description:
The coffee maker has been used within the last 8 months 

When plugging the unit into the wall outlet and attempting to brew a cup off coffee the lights begin to flicker and the circuit breaker pops.  

While doing some research on the internet he came across a recall (see Release #10-238) where there was a different hazard with a similar coffee maker 

The firm was contacted on 11/1/2011 and was given a  reference number to show that he called he was advised to contact the retailer and see if it could be returned. 

Consumer was given reference number [REDACTED] to return this unit to Walmart.  Walmart in Chicoppee, MA would not take it back.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning coffee maker causing electrical issues, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Checking microwave for recall due to fire starting more than once at clips that hold shelf inside microwave, shoots up the sides of the microwave.
Around October 2010 caller was using the microwave to heat food, caller doesnt' remember temperature or time but states that she never uses microwave for more than Just to Heat up a plate, she heard a pop, returned to kitchen & saw fire inside the microwave, she opened it to turn it off and caused fire to dissipate.

Caller's husband contacted retailer, purchased and replaced clip.
October 27, 2011 caller was heating rice & beans on plate with napkin on top when she heard again a popping sound and saw fire in microwave again.

She called manufacturer who told her she couldn't help her and advised her to file a report w/CPSC caller would like the public to be made aware of this danger and would very much like to have her microwave replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved a fire starting inside the microwave twice, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Caller was watching television, dishwasher was running when he smelled burning odor.
He went into kitchen where he saw dishwasher door had smoke coming out of it.
He opened the door to the dishwasher thinking operation would stop but it didn't.
He was now trying to shut the door back with hot soapy water coming out of it and landing all over the floor.
He got door shut back and went to circuit box and threw circuit breaker off which is how it has remained.
He back to the dishwasher, opened the door, felt panel and found it to be extremey hot which is how he said he knew that was the problem.  Panel was not warped or melted because dishwasher had only been in use approximately one half hour.                                                                     
He called the manufacturer this morning who advised him that his dishwasher was recalled but not for the panel, it is recalled due to the motor causing fires.
He is reporting to CPSC in hopes to get this dishwasher recalled also recalled for the panel.
justification: The incident involved smoke and hot water but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the reported recall for similar fire hazards.

incident_description:
Caller came home from Church 11/2/2011 around 8pm to celebrate her daughter's birthday, smelled something burning, decided it may be from someone burning leaves or rubbish outside.

Around 9:00pm caller's husband went to the refrigerator to put something away and found that it was extremely hot with plastic melting the holder serving to holding the light bulbs in and the socket was brown and burned that the light bulbs screw into.

The double doors were shut, the light bulbs should have been off but had stayed on.

Callers removed the light bulbs because they do not feel safe when them in the refrigerator at this point.

Consumer contacted manufacturer this morning 11/03/2011, was told that all they could do was repair the refrigerator.  She declined stating she had read that others had opted for repair and had fire afterward.

She contacted a lawyer; Top Class Action.com/lawsuit-settlements/lawsuit-news/723-lg-refrigerator-class-action-lawsuit-  (973) 994-1700 and her local television station;www.mysuncoast.com ABC7, 1477 Tenth Street, Sarasota, FL 34236 (941) 923-NEWS

Caller states that if she and her husband had gone to bed she may not be speaking with me at this time.

She wants the refrigerator recalled and replaced at manufacturer expense citing extreme danger of fire.
Caller states that she informed manufacturer that she understands that they are trying to save money by repairing, however she doesn't want any LG Appliance in her home.
Her husband is a builder, has recommended LG appliances but will not recommend them in the future.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator overheating and melting parts, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Purchased a Kitchen Aide Dishwasher January 2011 for 800.00.
 I called them on Sept. 23 to tell them that the washer had stopped working. every time i called, i got a hangup, a transfer or someone who would say that they were not sure it was covered.

After two days on the phone I finally got an associate that scheduled an appointment for me with an A&E appliance repair. I was given a date of  Sept . 29  between 8am-5pm  and was told that the repair center would call me the day before to give me a more precise time.  

I waited for the call on September 28 and no call was received.  I called kitchen aide back on Sept 30 and got the same run around as before. Until I finally found an associate that said my area is serviced by a company called interstate appliance. She then made  an appointment for my service on October  19 which was the earliest she could do, she gave me the phone number to interstate appliance and said to contact them directly and see if I could get a better date for service as they may have can cancellations. 

I tried calling Interstate appliance  4 times leaving messages with my phone number however, I received no return phone call. I tried again to call  kitchen aide and again I was subjected to the same run-around. And each time, they were checking to see if my unit was still in warranty.  I was again rescheduled with interstate appliance and given a date of October 26. unfortunately our area had a sudden snow storm that week and many people and businesses were without power. I however was unaffected by the storm. Again I waited and no call or service was given. 

I called kitchen aide November 5, and was told that I was supposed to be serviced by A& E Appliance, however, she could not find a service call for me.  She then said I was to be serviced by Interstate appliance and the best date they could give me was November 23.   I said that was unacceptable and could they do better. They then told me they had Forrest appliance who could do me on November 16. I was not pleased, but accepted that as the best appointment I could get.  

I finally got through to Interstate appliance on November 5.  they told me that kitchen aide should have known that my town was not serviced on a Wednesday. But regardless, they were affected by the storm and many customers had to be rescheduled. I asked why I wasn't notified. I was told that I should have called them to see if they had any scheduling problems. They then rescheduled me to November   16...the same as Forrest appliance. I decided not to cancel any appointment and wait to see if any of the two that were scheduled that day would show up.

On November 15 I calked interstate appliance because I had heard noth8ing, I left  my phone number 2 times. I heard nothing from either service company .  On November 15 I called kitchen aide and they checked and said they couldnÃÂt get to the service company because it was after 5pm.  I was very heated and told the representative that the service was unacceptable and I would be filing a complaint with the BBB if I did not get service ob November 16.

I got a phone call from Forrest appliance on November 15 at 915pm. They scheduled me for 9am the following morning. They apparently had no idea about the service problems I was having.

When the service man arrived. He looked at  the unit and said, ÃÂwith these lights lit like this, it looks like some kind of  a  short circuit. He then took off the front panel and told me that the circuit board had burned and he would have to order new parts. I was told it would be about another week. 

I then read about other short circuit issues that cause d fires. I am hoping that this does not happen, but my unit definitely dis short curcit. And kitchen aide should have been able to tell me that was the issue instead of giving me  run around ad keep checking that I was still in warranty.  I kind of got the impression that they were waiting until I was out of warranty so they wouldn't have to take responsibility.  My unit is  dishwasher model  KUDS30IXBL1   serial number   F10206110 and was purchased at Lowes home center Leominster, Ma.
justification: The incident involves significant service delays and poor customer service, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: While baking with my Maytag electric stove the lower heating element started on fire.  It looked like a firecracker fuse while burning in the oven.  We quickly removed the baking goods, and then turned off the oven and pulled it out from the wall and unplugged it from the power box.  The lower element was still sparking and burning despite being unplugged from the power source.  Then while it was still burning inside the oven we sprayed the element directly with a fire extinguisher.  This did not put the fire out.  Leaving the oven door closed after spraying with the fire extinguisher into the oven compartment we pulled the stove out side where after 5-8 minutes the burning element finally went out.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but was successfully contained without injury, indicating a moderate severity with low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a saute pan from the Lincoln, Nebraska, T.J. Maxx store on November 6, 2011.  Last evening (after washing and "oiling" the pan according to directions) I attempted to use the pan on my gas kitchen stove.  THE HANDLE CAUGHT FIRE, NEXT TO THE CONNECTION TO THE BODY OF THE PAN!  Fortunately I was made aware of this by the smell and was able to keep damage to a minimum.

The pan information is as follows:

Brand:  IPAC
20 cm/ 8"
Green Ceramica
Made in China

It is my opinion that ANY pan or skillet made for consumer cooking should not ignite while being used for this purpose!
justification: The pan handle caught fire during use, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This is the second time that my Farberware coffee pot has had a catastrophic failure.  The first incident happened on January 30, 2009.  I plugged in my Farberware superfast fully automatic 12 cup coffee pot into a GFI protected circuit - the consequence of which was an electrical explosion. One of the male connectors in the base of the unit separated from its insulated mounting and was pressed back into the base. That caused the a direct short when plugged into my outlet.

This first incident was to was "Farberware Superfast Fully Automatic" model number FCP 280 with the date code of 97 1105.  I made an immediate report to the CPSC and initially retained the destroyed GFI and coffee pot.  

After some period of time, after not having heard from the CPSC, I packaged up the unit and sent to Underwriter Laboratories for  failure analysis.  The implication of their analysis was that the coffee pot had been submerged and was corroded as a consequence of having been underwater.  This was not the case as my spouse and I have been the sole owners and users of that coffee pot from the inception.  We NEVER immersed the coffee pot.  A visual examination of the insulation piece that separated male side of the plugs at the base of the pot had cracked and separated such that it no longer held one side of the pin.  That is, it was a mechanical failure that allowed for this direct short having nothing to do with the UL allegation that an immersion was involved.

After that incident, we purchased a replacement coffee pot model FCP number 412G.  This one has failed in much the same way.  It is marked "QC passed" and 102 EE is embossed on its base.  I do not see a date code on it.  However, there is a stamping on it that says 102 EE.

On November 4, 2011, this reaplacement coffee pot also tripped the GFI; however it did not explode like the first incident.  There is obviously a dead short in this one too.  

I suspect that the replacement Farberware Coffee Pot suffers from a similar defect in design as the original one.  This time I am not sending it to UL for their failure analysis but will hold onto it assuming that you would have an interest in examining it.
justification: The incident describes a repeated electrical failure in coffee pots causing a short circuit, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
My 7 yr old Whirlpool side by side model refrigerator ED5PHEXNB00 started smoking and caught fire.

I was in the living room when I heard a brief crackling noise coming from the kitchen.  When I went into the kitchen it smelled like something electrical was burning, however I could not figure out where it was coming from.  When I opened the refrigerator door, I heard the crackling sound again and smoke started pouring out from behind the refrigerator.  I pulled the refrigerator away from the wall and saw the smoke pouring out from the bottom, so I quickly unplugged it.  The crackling noise and smoke then stopped.  Yet enough smoke filled up my kitchen in that short amount of time that it took me 2 days to completely air out the electrical burn smell (with all windows open and fans going.)  I hesitate to think what would have happened if I was not home and right there.  Fortunately no one was injured.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire and produced significant smoke, but no one was injured.

The  indicator on the control panel turns red when the surface is hot . He noticed on two different occasion while walking by that the burner had powered in the on position. When leaving the home or the range is not being used it is unplugged from the wall outlet.
