incident_description: On December 24, 2010, while working in my kitchen, wiping down the counter and cabinetry,  I bumped the back of my hand on the corner of the stainless sell oven completely severing or lacerating the extensor tendon of my index finger. I was immediately taken to a nearby  hospital urgent care where the attending physician gave me a tetanus shot, splinted my hand and instructed me to return in one week for removal of the stitches. On 12/31/10, I returned to have the stitches removed and because I had loss strength in my index finger, I was referred to a hand surgeon and on in early January had surgery to repair the damage to the extensor tendon. The metal flashing around the opening of the oven and warming unit are not soldered and in an unfinished state with the corners simply bent.  My husband and I purchased this stove on November 16, 2010.  This unsafe condition is unapparent to a reasonable customer as he or she considers the stove for purchase as the main focus is the look, features, function and price. This incident was reported to Sears on January 8, 2011 by mail to the local store and by online report through its website. On January 17, 2011, I was called by the local Loss Prevention Manager who at the time was informed of my injury and surgery, promising to immediately remove the model from the floor and report the injury to the manufacturer, Electrolux. After surgery, my hand was completed immobilized to allow the tendon reconnection to heal. I wore a custom hand brace for weeks. I was finally released from the surgeon's care in March 2011. After hearing from no one in weeks, I contacted Sears again in March via its website and was again called by the Loss Prevention Manager and Store Manager. I was told that a claims adjuster from Sedgwick would contact me about my injury.  The adjuster Sedgwick took my report and several weeks later on April 14,2011, I was informed she would have to refer me to Electrolux and they would contact me. There was no contact from Electrolux and I reported the incident through their online site in May. I also had the Sedgwick adjuster to reach out to them again and in June 2011, I received copy of a letter from a claims adjuster form Electrolux Crawford & Co to investigate my claim for "personal injury". I was finally  visited by an adjuster from Crawford & Co in June at my home to investigate my claim, take photos of the stove, record my statement.  After slow progress, I contacted her in August and was informed my claim was referred to a new adjuster. After weeks of working with the new adjuster bringing him up to speed, I was informed that Electrolux had not yet accepted responsibility for my injury. In the mean time, I am still making payments for medical bills and catching up personally and professionally from lack of use of my hand for several months. I have been unable to replace the stove which is a safety hazard to everyone in my home.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring surgery and prolonged recovery, but such occurrences are unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Toaster Oven 100.8000990A. I have had the unit for approximately a year and I have used it regularly for toasting and baking which it is specified for. I used the broiler function for the first time today (11-12-11) and, about an hour later, the glass door exploded. Glass shards were sent flying half way across the kitchen.  The unit was completely cool to the touch and nothing had fallen on it to cause the glass to break. I began researching this product on line and found that several other people have had similar trouble with this toaster oven model. I even noticed that mine is not the first report submitted to this web site.  I am thankful that no one in my household was standing close to the unit when it exploded; however, I feel that this item should be recalled because of the potential danger it presents.
justification: The glass door exploded, sending shards across the kitchen, but no one was injured. Similar incidents have been reported by other users, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description:
On November 9, 2011 a Kenmore undercounter dishwasher manufactured by Frigidaire, while not set to operate, commenced smoking, with fumes emerging from the front of the machine.  Fortunately, the two tenants, watching television in the adjoining living room, smelled the smoke and one of them switched off the circuit breaker, thereby avoiding a fire in their residence.

CPSC has issued recalls for a substantial number of Frigidaire dishwashers due to corrosion of wiring from liquid detergent or timer hazards (Models starting with 587), but to the best of my knowledge, not this particular model.  

The dishwasher that started to burn and emit fumes, while in the off position, was sold by Sears, and carries a "Sears Kenmore, Hoffman Estates, IL 60179" nameplate.  

This is Frigidaire/Kenmore Model 587.15072201.
The serial number is TH31820117. 

The property at risk of fire from this dangerous dishwasher was built in 1692, but had all new wiring in 1990.  It is separately listed on the National Register of Historic Places (the Rea-Proctor Homestead), and should not be destroyed by a dangerous appliance.  Sears, when informed of the fire risk, failed to offer a free repair.  Instead, they offered a $129 site visit, charge for any parts, and offer only a 30 dayt warranty.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke but no injury or fire occurred, and the tenants took action to prevent further damage.

We were able to turn it off quickly & no one was hurt but this seems very dangerous to me. The cover was on, just not fully locked in for some reason, so the blade stayed contained.

incident_description:
Dishwasher completed its cycle with the heated dry option on.  I opened the dishwasher to help the dishes complete drying.  They were warm and some were a little damp.  About 30 minutes later, I closed the door to keep our toddler out of the dishes.  I then went to bed.  This was around 12 AM.  At 4 AM we were awakened by an awful smell and smoke in the house.  I was about to call the fire department because I could not locate the cause when I noticed that the kitchen counter above the dishwasher was very hot to the touch.  I opened the dishwasher to find a mess of melted plastic.  It appears that the heating element came again some time during the night.  The inside of the DW was as hot as an oven.

After a brief search on the web, we discovered multiple reports of similar problems with GE DW.  There is a recall for a model similar to ours, but not our model.  This is outrageous.  They should be forced to recall all of their DW with this feature.

We unplugged the unit, removed the crock and lifted the unit and saw that the plastic on the bottom of the unit was melted and the heating element had dropped.

incident_description:
We were shopping today (11/13/11) in a major grocery chain in central Texas (the incident has been reported to them at the time and followed up by a telephone call to management, recommending they remove the product from display). My wife asked me to pick up a 9-inch Pyrex pie plate from the display counter. As I began to lift the plate from a stack of about a half-dozen plates, the one I was holding completely shattered, causing minor cuts to two fingers on my left hand, and my thumb on my right hand. I had not even removed the plate from the stack. The incident was witnessed by another shopper; and he stated that his wife was similarly injured while using a casserole dish in their kitchen - the dish merely shattered. An associate from the store immediately arrived (he must have heard the audible POP when it shattered), and provided the necessary assistance, took a report, and cleaned-up from the incident. It was fortunate that no young children were in the area, or they too could have been injured, as the shattered glass material flew out from the shelf no less than 4-feet.
My wife then recalled reading in the October 2011 issue of Consumer Reports about the faulty products manufactured by [REDACTED]. When we got home, I recovered the magazine and read that [REDACTED] commented, "that most glass-product failures are caused by "consumer misuse, failure to follow the manufacturer's instructions, and supplier mishandling." I can assure you that I was merely trying to retrieve a plate from the display shelf when a loud POP occurred and the plate shattered in pieces. [REDACTED], later in the article, declined to comment on the  (previous) complaint, citing its policy on pending litigation.
I can only say that as a 75-year-old retired naval officer, I would be willing to stand before any judge and jury (or other adjudicator) and cite that the product I was trying to obtain for purchase is clearly an unsafe product, and it should be removed from the shelves of sales floors in the interest of public safety. I was not trying to pry the product from a stack, merely lifting it carefully with both hands when it shattered with a loud POP. 
Reading through the Consumer Reports article, it seems since Pyrex and [REDACTED] changed the materials utililzed for producing their bakeware products from borosilicate to soda lime glass (reportedly in the interest of less cost, thus more profits) they have subsequently placed profits higher on their agenda than public safety.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in minor cuts to multiple fingers, indicating an injury without long-term consequences.

incident_description:
My wife and I purchased a bought a top-of-the-line LG refrigerator--model No. LG-LFX21960ST refrigerator. We came home a couple weeks ago and discovered the interior light was on again. It was on so long that the inside of the refrigerator was HOT. The plastic light fixture actually melted. The area above the light fixture (the liner) began to melt and form drips. The liner also cracked. This makes this refrigerator run almost constantly, not very energy efficient. At first we blamed the kids for leaving the doors partially open. They insisted it they were closing the doors so I decided to do research and found this is a major issue with the LG Refrigerators. It has caused homes to catch fire! 

Pounds of butter have melted, [REDACTED] rolls containers popped. Entire packages of hot dogs have cooked! 

I contacted LG customer support. They sent a technician to my house to take pictures of the damage. The refrigerator has to be replaced. LG agrees and has offered a settlement of $787.50, a third of what we paid for the refrigerator. This is a manufacturer defect and is dangerous. LG has not issued a recall. They refuse to replace the refrigerator. We've had this thing for 4 1/2 years. I would expect 20 years out of a refrigerator. The refrigerator list price was $2,599. We paid less because it was part of a bulk purchase for a kitchen remodel. I want LG to replace the refrigerator at no cost to me with their current model similar to the on we purchased. We are not in a position to spend the additional $1,711.50 to replace an appliance that should last 20 years. I don't want money from LG. I want them to replace the refrigerator with a current model comparable to the one I purchased. I also want them to issue a recall to repair the refrigerators before more people come home to find their refrigerator has melted or caused a house fire.

I documented this incident. All calls and e-mail communication with LG.

LG Electronics has sold refrigerators with a major design flaw. These are dangerous and people need to know about it. [REDACTED] LG Easy Bake oven and you will see the many complaints about this refrigerator that cooks rather than cools your food. Our family has suffered unexplained upset stomachs, nausea and diarrhea. I now believe the food spoiled in the refrigerator then cooled to proper temperature.
justification: The incident caused property damage and potential health issues (upset stomachs, nausea, diarrhea) due to spoiled food, but no severe injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Maytag/Jenn-Air Dual-fuel oven/range

Manufacturer: Maytag Appliances
Model: JDR8895AAS
Serial No.: 13411627GP


Appliance was purchased in late 2005.  Appliance has had many minor problems, such as control knobs breaking off.  Approximately two years ago, the right front igniter on the range stopped working.  Every time I use the top broiler, an "electrical" smell emits from the appliance for approximately a day.  The plastic seals around the glass on bottom oven door appear to have melted over time.

On November 9, 2011.  I was simmering some taco meat and using the oven at 350 degrees.  Spontaneously, the igniters began rapidly clicking (approximately two times per second).  

After about 2 minutes of clicking, I heard a loud pop and sparks flew out of the back of the range, near the top.  Thirty seconds later, another loud pop and shower of sparks occurred.  Thirty seconds after that, a third loud pop and sparking occurred.  

After that, the igniters continued clicking, but a much slower rate (approximately once per second).  

At that point, I turned off the appliance's circuit on my circuit breaker.

This seems to be a well-known problem that has resulted in more than a few kitchen fires, as I have found several consumer reviews detailing the same or similar problems:

justification: The incident involved sparks and potential fire hazard but no injury or death, and similar issues are frequently reported by other users.

incident_description:
Kitchen Aid Dishwasher Model KUDP02CRBL2 SN# FT2801917

During use of the Dishwasher my wife and I noticed a slight burning odor; we were not sure where the burning odor was coming from.  After a week or so we found that the dishwasher had over flowed all over the kitchen floor.  After cleaning up the flood we used it again and thatÃÂs when the burning odor was discovered coming from the dishwasher itself. 

I contacted Kitchen Aid / Whirlpool customer service and explained the problem.  I was told that the Dishwasher was out of warranty and they would not do anything except to have their service agency come to my home to repair it at very high cost to me.

Being an electronic engineer and owner of [REDACTED] I decided to investigate the cause of this strong burning odor.  I found that the circuit board was the cause of the odor, and it was only burning when the dishwasher was being used with high temperature settings.  I also noticed that the wiring that went to the main power connections from the internal circuitry has melted.

Kitchen Aid / Whirlpool did nothing to address this reported problem and just said that it was out of warranty.  Knowing that reports of their dishwashers going on fire, they should have investigated this problem to prevent possible house fires and injury to occupants, but they just ignored the problem.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing a burning odor and overflow, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he turned off the power switch of his coffee maker after almost 45 minutes of use and the consumer could hear a boiling noise from another room in the house. The consumer stated that he found that the coffeemaker was smoking from the bottom of the coffee maker. The coffemaker is programmable and turns on at a timer as desired. The consumer stated that the coffee maker was set to make the full amount of 6 cups. The consumer unplugged the coffee maker to stop the smoking and placed it outside.  The consumer called the firm later that day and informed them of the incident. The consumer has not accepted the resolution and asked if the corporate office would give him a refund if the retailer will not refund the product. The consumer took the product back to the retailer that afternoon and was given a refund.
justification: The coffee maker emitted smoke and an electrical burning smell but caused no injury or property damage, fitting severity level 2. Similar incidents with this model suggest the occurrence likelihood is possible (3).

incident_description:
When attempting to move the Crockpot she noticed that the bottom was stuck to the counter top and after taking a closer look she noticed that the bottom was melted.  The unit was powered in the off position and she does not recall if it was plugged into the wall outlet. 

After she  was to remove it from the counter she noticed a few holes from the outside of the crock pot. She recalls using the crock pot last on 10/24/2011 for six hrs on high but does not recall noticing any holes are it melt then.

She has not contacted the firm on the retailer but plans to do so. She has discontinued the use of the product and may replace it.
justification: The incident involved a melted crockpot with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the commonality of such appliance malfunctions.

incident_description: Handle of slow cooker has cracked and pieces have broken off. Can't use or hold it.
justification: The handle is broken, making the slow cooker unusable, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: During use of the microwave, sparks and lightening would fly across the microwave.  It was similar to what would happen if there was metal in the microwave.
justification: The incident involved sparks and lightning in the microwave, indicating a malfunction, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Pfaltzgraff Catalina dinnerware are labeled microwave safe. When using the plates, bowls, or mugs in the microwave, the dinnerware gets exceedingly hot. Family members and guests have been burned when removing these items from the microwave. 
 
This is clearly a safety hazard. I spoke with Consumer Services at Pfaltzgraff (can provide employee name if needed) who denied that there was any issue with their dinnerware. They told me that microwave safe meant that it wouldn't hurt the microwave. I asked if there was an organization within the company that fields calls regarding safety issues. She refused to provide any contact information for me.
justification: Family members and guests have been burned when removing the dinnerware from the microwave, indicating an injury has occurred.

incident_description: Used large pyrex  15x 10x 2 pan. Baked 2 winter squash halves in 300 degree oven for 1 hour, poured in 1/4 c warm water while pan still on oven rack. . Pan gave off 2 separate explosions- 20 sec apart- sending sharp glass shards throughout kitchen.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex pan exploding, sending glass shards throughout the kitchen, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
RE: Sanyo 3.7 cu ft Refrigerator, Model: SR 3720M
Bought at Costco recently.  Had several soda cans in it setting of 4/5. Last week, one of the soda cans froze, so I turned it down to 3/5. The night before last, I opened the fridge to find one of the glass shelves had shattered. The glass particles were everywhere and many were small as dust. 3 more cans had tiny punctures from the broken glass and were leaking through these tiny punctures. The night of the indicent, I didn't think the broken glass would be in pieces so small, so I opened one of the cans and had a drink and immediately felt something sharp in my throat. I then closed the fridge and drank water to try to "get it down". I inspected the fridge yesterday morning and found that the glass pieces were from the size of dust particles up to 2 inches in diameter. It took hours to clean the fridge and the floor in front of it.  I feel the glass shelves are unecessary and unsafe. I've reported this to Costco also.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (glass particles in throat) but is unlikely to occur frequently given the specific circumstances of glass shelf shattering.

incident_description: left front burner will not turn off at times when knob is turned off
justification: The burner not turning off poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or incident is reported.

incident_description:
The oven/range have faulty wiring, which can melt and cause the oven to short circuit. The appliance can then stop working and pose a shock hazard to consumers.
the wires underneath the range melted wich caused all the burners to go out.
justification: The faulty wiring poses a shock hazard and can cause the appliance to stop working, indicating a potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description:
Large burners will fluctuate the temperature spontaneously without adjusting the gauge. When I turn the temperature gauge to decrease the temperature it does not respond. I need to turn off the burner and turn the burner back on to get the desired temperature. This option does not always work and is very unsafe. I cannot leave the room because the temperature can go out of control at any time. 
I have contacted the manufacturer several times regarding this matter to report this problem and they have not offered any help. They state this problem is unfamiliar to them and this issue with my specific product has not been reported before.
justification: The burner's temperature fluctuation and lack of control pose a safety risk, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire Glass Cooktop exploded.  After using one small back burner, it was turned off.
When my husband turned around to walk away, the cooktop exploded.
justification: The cooktop exploded, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: My microwave (Emerson model #MWG9115SL) randomly shuts off, and sometimes it will shoot sparks from the broiler unit in the roof of the microwave. It has been an ongoing problem, and Emerson doesn't seem to be very interested in the issue.
justification: The microwave sparks and shuts off randomly, posing a potential fire hazard but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
LG refrigerator model: LFC25760SB
Purchased new, delivered and installed on 10-MAY-2007.

Around November 2008, notice a burning plastic smell coming from fridge. Opening the fridge revealed melting plastic on the inside top of fridge. The lightbulbs were remaining on when the doors were closed, releasing tremendous heat over time.  Fridge was unplugged, and the bulbs removed. This is a FIRE HAZARD. Contacted LG, they said warranty was past, and would have to pay to have technician take a look at it.

With the bulbs removed, the fridge can cool the food. The plastic guard that covers the lights was partially melted and would not hold into place anymore. The entire 'microchip' area at the top of the fridge is sagging down a bit. The lightbulb sockets are now exposed (because the guard is broken), so now is an electotrocution hazard as an unwary person could put their finger in it accidentally.

From reading on the internet, the lights failing to turn off appears to be a common defect on these models. Take this off the market before someone gets killed.


The ice cube maker also broke, around JULY-2008 (right after the warranty period), but doesn't appear to pose a physical threat.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard and potential electrocution risk, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher control panel caught on fire!
justification: A fire in the dishwasher control panel is a significant incident that could lead to injury if not promptly addressed.

incident_description:
Today November 7, 2011 My wife called me into the kitchen to check out our Jenn-air gas
stove. She explained to me that she had tripped the circuit breaker to the stove because the burners had started sparking as if they were trying to lite. she said she tried turning the control knob and of course the burners lit and went out, but the sparking kept on going. Each time I reset the circuit breaker the sparks would get faster and louder and the control knobs start to pop and spark as if to short circuit. I eventually just unplug the stove and stop using it for safety reasons.  Also back in July of this year the oven on this stove would turn on by itself. The timer would beep and the panel would show the that the oven is heating up as if someone had turned it on. But of course no one had'nt. 

    I called Jenn-air customer service to see if they had any ideas or what could cause this. Their
only option was to call a repairman at my expense, no thanks.

    My stove is a Jenn-air double oven gas range (model JDR8895AAS). Purchase about July 2006.
justification: The stove exhibited dangerous electrical malfunctions including sparking and self-activation, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Smelled and saw smoke coming from dishwasher bottom heating element was so hot it almost caught fire. Melted anything plastic in dishwasher. had to throw out numerous items. This is the second time this has happened. Im really scared it is going to catch fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and near-fire conditions with property damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The interior lightbulbs at the top of the Kenmore French Door refrigerator remained on even though doors were closed.  They burned through the plastic shield and were extremely hot to the touch.  Repairman said other refrigerators of same brand/model have had that issue and some caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved overheating lightbulbs that could cause a fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Right front electric burner, on a glass top, sears kenmore oven and range, operates independently.  It will change temperature settings, turn on the power, when off, and not respond to off, on the dial.  It is a serious safety problem.  This has been happening for a few months, to a lesser degree..., now it will not turn off without unpluging the range.
justification: The burner operates independently and cannot be turned off without unplugging, posing a serious safety risk, though no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range, Model # 790.9371002, Serial # VF217126 began "beeping" and flashing an FI error on the screen while baking.  I removed whatever I was cooking in the oven (can't remember what it was) and tried to turn off the range by pressing the off button on the control screen. It would not turn off!  It continued to "beep" and flash the F1 error.  I noticed that the oven's lower burner element was getting increasingly hot, very hot and glowing red.  The range still would not turn off!   I went to the breaker box and flipped the breaker for the range "off".  I have not used the range since. I have not flipped the breaker back "on."

This appliance is a fire hazard!   I have seen other reports on the Internet in which the same type of incident happened.   I purchased my range new around July 2002 (approximate) from Sears. It seems the stove should last longer than nine years?   I have ordered a new range as I am too afraid to use this fire hazard of a cooking appliance.  The incident range will be removed on November 18, 2011, and replaced with a new one.
justification: The incident caused a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: When cooking dinner the left fron burner did not shut off when I turned it off.  I was burnned, dinner was burned, pot was burned.  The burner did this several more times when turned on.  I had to wiggle the knob a lot to get it to shut off.
justification: The burner malfunction caused a burn injury and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue recurred multiple times, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: kenmore elite dishwasher about 7 years old. Stainless steel. model 66517463300. circuit board caught fire and burned dishwasher up. all of the wires melted and burned up the unit and melted the front plastic panel.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing significant damage to the unit and its components, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: While waiting for our Sears Kenmore (Serial # 790.9611240D, Model #VF00561567) oven to preheat at 350 degrees we herd a loud popping noise and a blue flash of light. We ran to the kitchen and found the oven smoking and the back of the element on fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description: This is related to a Kenmore Elite Induction 30" cooktop.  Today, my husband and I were cooking 10 shrimps on the most right burner, and water on the 2nd burner from the left.  "BANG!" ( a big explosion) - a loud gunshot noise, and a lighting flash came out from the cooktop.  We were not able to turn on the cooktop since!  Besides my husband's ear was ringing for a very long period of time, and took us some time to recover from the incident, we were glad that no other physical damage to any of us.
justification: The incident caused ear ringing and required recovery time, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such explosions are rare for cooktops (likelihood 1).

incident_description: Refrigerator had an electrical fire on the box attached to the compressor.
justification: Electrical fire on a refrigerator is an incident but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Elite series 795 refrigerator. Defective electronics: interior lights do not turn off when doors are shut. Plastic in the electric-control unit melted (screw mounts) until enter unit fell down exposing wires and bulbs. Plastic light bulb sockets are burned. Metal panel inside control unit is warped. Control unit can not be reattached. Seals on doors were damaged from heat and where previously replaced. Unit is a fire hazard and known to be defective, with bulbs that are very hot and stay on for extended periods. Refrigerator also has to run more to keep food cold, and safety of food may be compromised.
justification: The description indicates a fire hazard and potential for injury due to melted and exposed wiring, burned components, and compromised food safety.

incident_description: I have twice brushed my hand accidentally against the top right corner of the oven door of my gas range, and suffered a serious cut on the end of my finger. The first time was the most serious as the sharp corner sliced off a chunk of flesh. Even though I am now aware of the hazard, it is difficult to always keep in mind as I move around quickly in the kitchen, as is obvious since I've done it twice now. I plan to use duct tape, but I don't think that is much of a fix.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious cut, indicating an injury, and the likelihood is high as it has happened twice despite awareness.

incident_description: Watching World Series, heard loud explosion coming from the kitchen.  I thought it was a gas explosion, but I do not have any gas.  I went and saw the front of the range had exploded outwardly into many thousands of small pieces all over the kitchen.  I have not have any help from Sears, at many different numbers.  One was customer solutions, and would not stand be hide the product because it was out of warranty.  They said it was an insurance problem.  Then they also said they had to document it.   I was charged a service call for them to come out and document it.  They would come out and replace the door at my cost.  I am afraid to replace the door and am planning on buying a stove somewhere else.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the range, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore glass cook top electric range model 790.96011407 s/n VF73049986, the left front element on two occasions would not turn off or down. I understand that there is a recall on other models, mine is not on the list. 
After much research, it appears that the manufacturer has selected a vendor for the element controls that is making a inferior product, and this problem is not isolated to just a few models, but the entire line of glass cook top ranges.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning cooktop element that fails to turn off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Unit was not running, door was closed.  We began smelling smoke and burning plastic.  Due to past experience with this dishwasher catching fire, immediately recognized source and cut power to unit.   Inspection reveals power supply board behind control panel had again caught fire melting some plastic components of door.  Contacted sears immediately who denied assistance as product is outside warranty period.  They also denied any previous reports of fire with this model despite the fact they repaired mine in 2007 due to same fire.
I purchased unit in 2005, then in 2007 the power supply board caught fire during cycle.  After filing complaints and dealing with Sears for nearly 3 months the finally honored their warranty and replaced power supply board.  This fire could have been disastrous if we had been asleep or not home.  Since first experience with kenmore dishwasher fire, I have not run dishwasher at night or while we were out.  This time it started while unit was off.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher, which could have been disastrous but was promptly addressed without injury.

incident_description: A Kenmore Elite (Manufactured by LG) bottom freezer Refrigerator and purchased in 2006 has had issues with the lights not coming on or going off when the doors open or close.  In one incident the lights did not go off and melted the light cover and housing.  It continues to be an issue and causes the refrigerator to heat up and cook the food on the top shelf (e.g. [REDACTED]).  This issue really worries me because it would tend to imply an electrical short or faulty electronics in the switches or elsewhere.  In looking up the product for service I could find several other people have had the exact same problem within the last year on an item they purchased about the same time as me.  Overall the quality of the product has been very poor.  One of the rollers on a drawer broke early on, both drawers pop out feature failed to lock on closing within a couple years,
justification: The incident involves a malfunction causing property damage (melted light cover) and potential food spoilage, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Coffee maker Cuisinart DCC-1200 serial # 91120 had finished brewing coffee and was an hour and a half into the "keep warm" stage when it made a loud noise and began smoking.  Immediately unplugged and took outside but the smell of an electrical fire remained in the house for quite sometime -- definitely an electrical fire.  Had I not been in the kitchen at the time I am sure there was a good possibility I would have had a house fire.
justification: The coffee maker caused an electrical fire but was promptly unplugged, preventing injury or death.

incident_description: I have a Bosch Model 300 diswasher. We were having problems with it and contacted Bosch. We were told about the recall on our Dishwasher and that a service technician would fix it. The diswasher was serviced and worked for about a year then we began having the same problems again. We contacted Bosch and again a technician came due to the recall. Now about a year after the second servicing of the dishasher, the problems are back.  We contacted Bosch again, but were told our warranty is up and they offered no help.  When I check the Bosch website, I see a note that the recall is indefinite. The recall also says to not use the dishwasher, since this problem can cause a fire. I'm just wondering how Bosch can walk away from the recall?
justification: The recall indicates a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue has recurred multiple times.

incident_description:
Our refrigerator was leaking water from the freezer. We found ice on the bottom and so decided to remove the interior shroud to see if indeed ice was building up and if the drain is clogged.

We discovered one side of the coils, is melted...interior plastic liner of the freezer is melted in one section  and discolored brownish...from what appears to be burning. I am concerned about this! Seems very unsafe...like a fire hazard!
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to melted coils and plastic, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: We suddenly smelled a strong burning smell and it there was smoke coming from our dishwasher. It was still running but I shut the power off. Then after the power was diconnected I opened up the front panel and found the board burnt up and the plastic enclosure for it melted. One of the line wires going to a connector to the board was burnt up and exposed the bare wire. We were glad we were home at the time of the incident because we were able to shut the power off to it.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries occurred as the power was shut off promptly.

incident_description: After having company leave I had started our dishwasher, went upstairs to put my child to bed when my husband yelled, telling me the dishwasher was smoking and throwing sparks from the face of the dishwasher where the control panel is located.  The dishwasher was still running when he had left the kitchen and gone to the basement.  (Electric and water do not mix).  He had gone to the basement to shut the breaker off which stopped the dishwasher and stopped the sparks and smoke.  Had we not been home our house could have been a total loss or worse case we could have died in the fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher causing smoke and sparks, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
After smelling electrical smoke in our kitchen and investigating, we found smoke pouring out of the start relay on
the compressor of our side-by-side Whirlpool refrigerator, model EDSPHAXMQOO, date of manufacture 10-03. The
68.00 part has been replaced ... part box has the following note:
***ATTENTION***
WHIRLPOOL MAY PAY FORTHIS REPAIR
Whirlpool Corporation may pay for this
replacement part and associated labor
costs for affected start relays.
Obviously this is a known problem that needs to be dealt with before extensive damage and/or death occurs.
Interesting note: This happened to my Mother-in-Iaw's Whirlpool a few months back ... actually caused a fire,
damaging wiring and other appliance components, the floor and the kitchen cabinets. Additionally, the house filled
with smoke and had to be cleaned, along with damage that the fire crews caused while trekking throughout the
house.
WE were lucky because we were home and caught it before more damaged occurred, but obviously others have not
been so lucky.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported in this specific case, though past incidents caused significant property damage.

incident_description: I partially fried chicken thighs before attending parent/teacher conferences and I placed the pra-cooked chicken in a glass Anchor Hocking baking dish. I was gone for approx 1 hour and 45 mins. Upon returning home, I preheated the oven to 300 degrees and started to prepare the side dishes.  Once the oven beeped to indicate that it was heated, I put the dish of chicken in the oven. After about 20 mins I reached into the oven, grabbed the dish and began to pull it from the oven.  As I lifted the dish off of the oven rack, it exploded.  I turned my face to avoid injury but I was hit in the chin and mouth with flying glass.  My upper lip was cut and my lower lip and chin are burned. I went to urgent care and was given a Rx for antibiotics and burn cream and received a tetanus shot.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts and burns requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury severity level. The likelihood is considered possible due to the specific circumstances of glass dish use and oven handling.

incident_description: I was pouring coffee and the handle fell off the pot. I burnt my leg.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

My name is[redacted] and I own the Frigidaire PLES389ECH s/n MFB1509160.  I have replaced the knobs on my range with your safety upgrade kit provided in the recall; however, I am continuing to have problems with the knobs.  

Before the recall, I had accidentally bumped the knobs on three separate occasions which have all resulted in a fire.  I have burned a backpack, a loaf of bread covered in plastic, a dishtowel and papers.  After the recall, I have continued to bump the knobs and they continue to become looser with use.  I am only 5ÃÂ1ÃÂ tall, so when I reach to the back of the range, I have a tendency to bump the knobs.  I have the same issue with my 8 year old son.   We have had two more small fires since the recall replacement fix.  We have been fortunate that we have not had major injuries or damage at this point. incident_description:
Over the past few years I noticed a sulfur smell on the first floor of my home in the morning. I searched for the source off and on during that time a decided that it may have been from and abundance of cardboard boxes in my basement or new drywall I had installed in my basement (this was at the time of the Chinese drywall recall) and figured it would eventually go away.

One day when my allergies were acting up and my nose was more sensitive than usual I went looking for the source again and found a loose gas fitting in my kitchen stove. I tightened the fitting and have not noticed the smell since. The fitting was not in the supply line but rather inside the stove at the block that the supply line fed into. I only had to turn the fitting on the tube about 1/4 turn to stop the leak.

I didn't immediately check the stove because it was only a mild sulfur smell not the thiol/mercaptan odor you get from a burner not lighting right away.

My stove is a GE Profile purchased from Sears in mid 2005.
model: J2B918CEK1CC 
s/n: GH203532P
justification: The incident involved a gas leak that was detected and fixed without any injury or harm occurring.

incident_description:
The item in question is a GE gas oven, model JGBP99WEH1WW.  The serial number is ZF274443P.

If the knobs on the gas oven are bumped or pushed from the right, the gas is often turned on, even if the knobs are not being pressed in.  In theory, it should be necessary to depress the knobs to turn them, but this takes very little pressure.  Designing the knobs so the igniter is triggered when the gas is turned on would be even smarter.

This has happened when opening cupboards above the stove, bumping into knobs, and even by nudging a knob with a pregnant belly.  The problem has been present as long as we've had the stove, but we normally remove the knobs to avoid the danger.  This has caused our home to fill with gas on one occasion, to the point where we had to leave until it dissipated.  This most recent incident was Sunday, when a bag of groceries was bumped into the stove, when the knobs had been left in place.

Interestingly enough, there's an example of this behavior at http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wlXiJHxCbQY  It's not my stove, or even the same model, and I am not the woman in the video, but this is not an isolated issue.
justification: The incident involves gas leakage due to easily triggered knobs, posing a significant hazard but no reported injuries.

incident_description: The burners on my Kenmore smoothtop range, Model 790.96011407, Serial #VF71052791, frequently do not turn off after the controls have been turned off.  Had I not been paying attention, this could easily have been a fire hazard.  By turning the controls back on and off a few times, after 10 minutes or so, I was eventually able to get the range to register that the controls had been turned to "off".  I see a recall on record for Kenmore Elite models with a similar number, but not for mine, but the problems we've encountered seem the same.
justification: The burners not turning off poses a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The large, front left burner was having troubles with heat control and was still on "high" when the knob was turned to the off position.  

In the days leading up to the burner not being able to be turned off, there were heat control issues.  Specifically, the burner would be on high heat instead of on medium or low heat, causing much of the food to burn and it actually damaged a skillet due to the excessive heat
justification: The burner malfunction caused property damage (damaged skillet) but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The issue persisted over days, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Ice maker unit malfunctioned causing water to flood both inside and outside of refrigerator unit and pool onto floor.  The refrigerator electronics/connections beneath the unit became saturated.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing water damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: At 5:30am, the dog was wimpering and scratching on the bedroom door, which he has never done before, so I got up, opened the bedroom door and immediately smelled toxic fumes in the air inside the house, similar to an electrical/plastic burning smell. The fire department was contacted. It was determined to be coming from the refrigerator.
justification: Toxic fumes were detected, posing a potential health hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Cooking on electric stove top made by Frigidaire I was burned with 3rd degree burns due to the fact that this stove top is extremely slippery and the pan that I was cooking in slid across the stove top and the hot grease splashed on my arm causing 3rd degree burns and now i am permanently scarred on my arm..Also it has no warning lights that the surface is hot even though it is turned off.  No where on the stove top are any warnings of slippery or hot surface.
justification: The incident resulted in 3rd degree burns and permanent scarring, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is possible (3) given the described conditions of the stove top.

incident_description:
Cusinart Grind and Brew Coffee Maker:  Only about a year old.

Set machine to make coffee.  Within ten minutes pot was boiling and front of machine appears melted - kitchen was filled with a toxic smelling smoke but no damage to anything other than the coffee maker only because we were right there and we were able to unplug and throw it outside.  It smoldered outside for 20 miniutes.

If we would have set the timer the night before like we often do to have the coffee ready when we woke up , this could have happened while we weren't in the room with disastrous results  The only reason there wasn't a bigger problem was becasue we were right there. 

Complete fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that produced toxic smoke and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to immediate action.

incident_description:
Oven was on without being turned on. 

 My wife walked into the house after work and noticed that the back burner was hot when she went to pick something up from the counter.  She noticed that the burner was in the off position and she turned it on and back off.  After about 10 minutes she walked back in the kitchen and heard a click from the range.  When she looked at the range she noticed the left rear burner turned red and then black again.  The knob was in the off position.  I did a search and noticed that others with this stove has had the same problem.  All of them stating that the burner turned on with the knob being in the off position.  I called sears who told me that this was not part of the recall.  I gave them the same info provided here and they did not ask for anymore information. 

Kenmore
Serial no. CF71649516
Model no. 790.96009601
justification: The incident involved an oven turning on by itself without injury, but with potential for harm.

incident_description:
On  09/07/2003 we purchased a KitchenAid Dishwasher Ser# FP3414140, Type 577-0, Model# KUDI01ILBL2. We did not experience any problems with the dishwasher until this past Sunday, 10/30/2011 when I turned the machine on and after about 5 minutes it started making a grinding noise and I saw flames and dirty gray smoke coming out of the right side of the dishwasher door. I hit the "cancel" button and this turned off the machine and the flames and smoke stopped. Nothing in my kitchen was damaged. We will be replacing the diswasher. I called KitchenAid at 1-800-422-1230 on Monday, 10/31/2011 and they asked me to allow a service tech to come to the house on this coming Friday, 11/04/2011 to check out the machine. The KitchenAid dishwasher will be taken away when the install on our new dishwasher is done on Saturday, 11/05/2011.

We purchased the KitchenAid Dishwasher from Sears at Golf MIll Center in Niles, IL 847-803-
7500.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or damage occurred, and the issue was resolved by turning off the machine.

incident_description: I placed an 8 oz block of cream cheese in my Anchor Hocking 8" glass cake dish and put it in the microwave for one minute.  I opened the microwave with a few seconds remaining and the dish shattered all over the microwave and kitchen.  Small pieces of glass struck me in the face.
justification: Small pieces of glass struck the person in the face, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: Pyrex baking dish shattered after removing it from the oven and placing it on the stovetop.  I was roasting squash, there was water in the pan, it had been baking on 425 for about 1 hour, broiler was turned on for last five minutes to glaze the top.
justification: The incident involved a shattered Pyrex dish but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. Thermal shock from rapid temperature change is a known risk with glass bakeware, making this occurrence likely.

incident_description:
We own a Frigidaire smooth top electric range, model number PLEFMZ99GCD, serial number VF84236960.  On Sunday, October 30, mid afternoon, the left front burner came on spontaneously while the rotary dial control was in the off position.  We were in another room, but were alerted when we heard the stove make beeping noises.  We could not turn off the burner with the rotary dial, and eventually turned off the circuit breaker to the stove.  
We tried turning the breaker back on.  At first, the rotary dial to the left front burner gave an "Er" code, but then came on again spontaneously and again would not turn off.  We again turned off the circuit breaker to shut off the stove.
We looked up Frigidaire recalls on the CPSC website, and found your recall notification of Frigidaire Smooth Top Electric Ranges with model numbers in our range.  However, when we called the Frigidaire Recall telephone number from your posting, we were told that our stove was not included in the recall.  We suggest that this is an error, since our stove clearly has the defect of spontaneously turning on.
No one was injured in this incident, and there was no property damage, since we were home when it occurred.  Luckily.
justification: The burner turned on spontaneously without injury or property damage, but required intervention to prevent potential harm.

incident_description:
My dishwasher failed, apparently due to the inability of the unit to heat the water.

I extracted the controller board from the door interior and discovered that a portion of the board exhibits evidence of overheating. A through-hole pin solder solder connection appears to have melted away, and the board material in the vicinity appears blackened and charred.

I discovered at the Bosch home appliance website, and the CPSC webiste that earlier serial numbers of this model were affected by a safety recall referring to an overheated component and possible fire hazard.

I am compelled to file this report to alert about the possible need to expand the above recall, if applicable, or the need to open a new investigation.
justification: The incident involves a dishwasher malfunction with evidence of overheating and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My range had been heating only intermittently for a few weeks. I needed to use it briefly one Sunday morning, so I heated a piece of toast for my son. Afterwards I pushed the "Cancel" button to turn off the oven. Thinking the oven was off, I left my son to eat his toast and got in the shower. Before I could take a shower the oven temperature rose rapidly to the extent that the house filled with smoke and my son went to get his dad. His dad couldn't get the oven to stop rising in temperature since the "Cancel" button was apparently not controlling the temperature rise. He had to unplug the range from the power source to get it to turn off. This was not just that the oven wouldn't turn off, but a case in which the temperature rose sharply and continued to rise. The temperature rose so rapidly and to such and extent in just those few minutes that the iron skillets in the oven had all of the coating burned off and left in a pile of ashes on the bottom of the oven.
I contacted the company to file a claim. I was asked to fill out a claim form and include the damaged items from the oven in my claim. I compiled all of the required information and sent it to the company. I received a letter from Whirlpool Corp. stating that my claim was denied because according to the users manual the oven was not to be used for storage. My response to them was to inquire about their plans for replacing or repairing the defective range. They did not respond. My last correspondence with them was on October 24, 2011 via email. My fear is that had I left the house after pressing the "Cancel" button and reasonably assuming that I had turned the oven off, the temperature may have continued to rise to the extent that a house fire would have been caused.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that rapidly overheated, causing smoke and damage but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Caller's wife was baking Apple Crisp at 350 degrees "bake", after approximately 30 minutes they began smelling a burning odor, went to kitchen, opened oven door, saw that the broiler had come on and that the Apple Crisp was burnt.
Caller took the Apple Crisp out of the oven, tried to turn the oven off but couldn't turn it off.
The oven heat continued escalating as the caller tried to turn the broiler off so he unplugged the range.
He plugged the range back in until after it cooled down, plugged it back in and the broiler came back on automatically.  He then plugged it in this morning 10/21/2011 with the same result.

Caller would like the public to be made aware of the fire hazard/danger for this particular model, said the broiler becomes so hot that the backslash & burners next to it may catch on fire if left too long.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: Started a load of dishes tonight in my Kenmore elite dishwasher Model #655,16052400 Serial #FR3702473 when I heard a lot of noises coming from the kitchen.  When I went in there smoke was pouring from it and there were snap, crackle and popping noise then flames broke out on the control panel right front.   I went and shut of the circuit breaker to the house.   House was filled with smoke and dishwasher was a total loss.  Nothing else was damaged though.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke and flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Several hours AFTER making coffee with our Cuisinart Automatic Grind and Brew Thermal Coffee Maker- model #: DDC590PC my husband and I smelled smoke coming from our kitchen.  Further inspection revealed a small flame and smoke emanating from the back of our coffee maker.   We are very surprised and dismayed by what happened.  Luckily we were home to catch the problem early before serious property damage occurred!! Our coffee maker does not have a hot plate.  The maker should turn off after coffee is done brewing (coffee stays hot is a thermal carafe).  Cuisinart stated that there is nothing they can do as the coffee maker is no longer under warranty.  Further investigation online revealed that this is not an isolated incident.  Link:  http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html
Someone should look into these incidents before lives are lost.
Thank you!
justification: The incident involved a small flame and smoke, but no injury or death occurred, and the problem was caught early. Online reports suggest this is not an isolated issue, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: This is the third failure of a Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker we have experienced.  The first one tuned itself on whenever it felt like it.  It was retuned and replaced under warrantee.  The second and third ones went up in smoke.  The third one is less then a year old.  I contacted Cuisinart customer service, and "[REDACTED]" apologized, and promised a replacement, and waived the ten dollar return shipping fee to us.  But this hardly addresses the over-arching issue.  A web search revealed many complaints identical to mine.
justification: The coffee maker failures resulted in property damage (smoke) but no reported injuries, and similar incidents are frequently reported online.

incident_description:
On Friday October 21, 2011at approximately 7 PM, my husband, [REDACTED], noted the smell he described as ÃÂburning candlesÃÂ in our kitchen.  At the time, we were unable to locate the source of the smell, but it persisted.  At approximately 8 PM, I went to get a soda from our LG Model Number LFC2570ST refrigerator.  The soda was on the top shelf.  Not only was the soda not cold, it was warm to the touch.   Some investigation revealed that some other items on the top shelf were also unusually warm.   Further, it appeared that the warmest items were located closed to the light/thermostat assembly in the top of the refrigerator unit.  

Further investigation revealed that the refrigerator light was not going off when the door was closed and considerable heat was coming from the light bulbs.  I decided to remove the light bulbs for the time being to correct the situation until we could have a service person look at the refrigerator. When I tried to pull the plastic cover off the bulbs, however, the entire thermostat assembly came down. I inspected the screw areas around the assembly and found that the plastic near the metal screws had melted.  After the assembly was down I was able to remove the light bulb cover. I found that the sockets holding the light bulbs were discolored and looked burned.  The light bulbs were too hot to remove even with gloves, so I unplugged the refrigerator and placed a container of ice underneath the bulbs and waited about ten minutes for the bulbs to cool down (one came out easily, but the other required significant force to remove).  I was unable to replace the thermostat assembly because of the melted screw holes, so I replaced the plastic cover for the light bulbs and used electriciansÃÂ tape to hold the assembly in place temporarily.

The next day my husband went on-line and found an account of an incident similar to ours that occurred with the same model LG refrigerator.  The web address for this account is:

http://wizbandit.wordpress.com/2008/08/01/lg-fridge-turns-into-easy-bake-oven-family-escapes-fire/

I am concerned because I believe that this situation, if undetected, could have resulted in a fire.  The inside of the refrigerator is all plastic and the fumes from even a small fire could have caused serious injury.  In addition, the problem was subtle: if I had not gotten a drink before going to bed, we would not have discovered the problem before the situation became worse.  We purchased a new refrigerator and had the old one removed, but I Have attached pictures of the burned sockets and melted plastic.

Thank you for any attention you can give this issue.  If you would like to contact me by phone, I can be reached at [REDACTED].
 
Sincerely,




[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I placed a 9x 13 pyrex over safe dish in  my over to bake augratin potatoes. Dish was not cold . The dish exploded in my oven within 15 minutes of cooking. Now....... so reluctant to buy glass dish ware. I am 57 years old and have used pyrex since I was a teenager.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no injury was reported, making it a minor incident with low likelihood based on the user's long-term experience with Pyrex.

incident_description:
Frigedaire model # FRS6LF7JBO serial # 4A81718146. Two major issues:

Prior to the last carafe cracking, I merely wiped some spilled coffee from the hot plate before replacing the carafe on the plate,  I contacted the Cuisinart customer service representative who stated that the carafes are made with tempered glass.  She denied any knowledge of other consumers having this type of problem or to replace these units.  SHe also reported that Cuisinart does not warrant the carafes.  

I have heard that some consumers have had "[REDACTED]" type glass crack under similar circumstances.  Based on my limited reading on the matter, it appears to have something to do with a change in the formulation in which the glass is made.

There were no injuries as a result of these incidents.  However, as a physician I believe that the glass carafes cracking with minor temperature changes constitutes a safety risk.

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes carafes cracking without causing injury, but indicates a potential safety risk due to minor temperature changes.

incident_description:
My Cuisinart Coffee Maker, Model DCC 1200 filled my kitchen with smoke this morning. We first heard a cracking and popping noise and then smelled electric burning.  If we had not been in the room my house would have been set on fire.  I quickly removed the maker and it continued to smoke outside.  

This was very dangerous and this product should have been recalled before.  I have read many reports of this same type of problem about this coffee maker.  

I have reported this to Cuisnart and am waiting for their reply.  This unit was purchased  in April 2010.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Reports of similar problems suggest this is a likely occurrence.

GE now wont repair it. They want it back. I have a Keurig B70 Coffee maker that is less than one year old that I have started to have problems with.  I contacted Keurig that said the problem was most likely caused by the K-Cups that I used, made by [REDACTED].  Because of that, they provided different use instruction from what the manual instructs. To avoid risk of injury, do not put your fingers in the K-Cup Assembly Housing." Case Numbers:
Keurig:  [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Our glass Pyrex baking dish shattered for no apparent reason right after removing it from the oven. Luckily, my husband was holding the dish over the stove when it broke, so the glass shards did not land on him, but it was a potentially dangerous situation.

233-R
A-10
for oven and microwave (no rangetop or broiler)

incident_description: The mechanism that turns the lights off in our LG Bottom Freezer Refrigerator malfunctioned and the 2 sixty watt bulbs (that came in the refrigerator) remained on even with the doors fully closed.  The shield over the bulbs started to melt and is all warped.  The sockets started to burn.  It hadn't been very long - maybe 1 hour, 45 minutes or less before the problem was found. There was a burning smell in the kitchen and I found the problem by following the smell.  The refrigerator was warm and even a loaf of bread on the top shelf was hard as if it had been toasted.  We removed both bulbs and have called someone in to repair it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing overheating and damage to the refrigerator, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The KitchenAid oven in our home is a built-in microwave and oven combination with a vent located at the bottom of the oven. The vent holes on the oven are at toddler eye level. ÃÂ Our 19 month old toddler was playing with magnets on the refrigerator, which is located next to the oven, when she noticed the vent holes on the oven. ÃÂ She proceeded to put her finger in one of the vent holes and when she tried pulling it out, it sliced her finger. ÃÂ We took her to the emergency room where she received seven stitches. ÃÂ 

We contacted KitchenAid requesting assistance. ÃÂ The customer service representative indicated that they could not assist because blocking the vent would cause the oven to combust while in use. ÃÂ We believe KitchenAid disregarded our concern. ÃÂ 

We think that a guard on the vent would be an easy and appropriate safety measure to address our concern.ÃÂ
justification: The toddler suffered an injury requiring stitches, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) as toddlers exploring appliances is common but not every instance leads to injury.

incident_description: Control for front burner on my electric stove was arcing and giving off a burning odor. Stove was immediately unplugged and considered a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved arcing and a burning odor, posing a fire hazard, but was promptly addressed without injury.

incident_description:
October 5, 2011: I noticed the refrigerater was warmer than normal. Food was warm because the interior lights would not shut-off.   The light assembly was beginning to burn so I hit the circuit breaker and removed the two light bulbs. I turned the circuit breaker back on and the refrigerator temperature stabilized. I contacted Sears and provided the model number (795.77543600) and Serial number (611KR00393). Sears did not tell me that they had issued a Service Flash (SF46-515) about this problem. 

The Sears Product Resolution Line (800-659-7026) has not been helpful.  The light parts have been on backorder. The my sears.com web site documents that other owners of this product have experienced multiple failures of the lighting unit (assembly 6621JK2003B) and that the problem may be centered at the main board (part# 6871JB1423N) which has been replaced in some instances.

[redacted]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light assembly causing warmth but no injury, and similar issues have been reported by other owners indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
We were baking apple pies.  Our 5-year old Kenmore oven (model # 790.94212409) was set at 350F.  The first two pies came out perfect.  We put the next two in the oven and left the kitchen to watch TV.  15 minutes later, the pies were on fire.  The digital clock on the oven was showing an error code of F10.  We were able to shut off the oven and prevent the house from burning down.  

We called Sears but their repair guy couldn't come until 1.5 week later so we found a local to try to figure out what was happening.  He told us that the control board of the oven had a short circuit that was kicking the self cleaning mode every time we turned the oven on.  He took of the control board as he mentioned that sometimes he's seen it start by itself even without human intervention.

We researched the web and realized that this happens often. See http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/kenmore-electric-range-c3796.html and other websites are available with similar types of horror stories.

This is a major fire hazard and will now have to get a new range because I'm not trusting that replacing the control board with another one from Sears will fix the issue.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to a faulty oven control board, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The issue is described as happening often, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
UPDATE: Both refrigerators have moisture problems.  Both cause property and health issues for my family.

Consumer stated that her refrigerator, (GE Monogram that costs $6,000.00) started leaking from the bottom about 2 months ago, this was a refrigerator that was replaced by the company approximately 2 years ago because the same problem.

"Black Mold" was behind this built in fridge. Consumer stated that the first refrigerator caused $50,000 worth of damages to her home which was renovated by the company, however the replacement is causing similar problems and she believes that this refrigerator is a safety hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involves property damage and potential health issues due to black mold, but no direct injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: The tab off the lid of my babies Nuby Take or Toss cup broke off and I found it in her mouth.  It broke off a half circle.  The cups are less than a month old.

incident_description: We purchased a set of Eggies from Bed Bath and Beyond on 10.22.11.  We first used them today and completely followed the directions.  13 minutes into boiling the 6 eggs one of the containers violently popped.  There is no steam release on this product so this will probably happen if used again.  Nobody was injured however, I am very concerned that this product has the potential to cause injury if someone is close to the boiling water.  Steam burns can be very painful and it is only a matter of time before somone is injured.
justification: The incident involved a violent pop with no injuries, but the potential for steam burns indicates a likely risk if used again.

Front right burner issues: cannot control temperature.  Temperature is often much hotter than selected knob setting.  Will boil water even on "Lo" setting.

The first time the front right burner would not turn off, it almost started a fire in my kitchen.  I now know to just not use this burner.  Instead I know I can only use the front right burner on the lowest setting, which is ridiculous.

Serial VF64666993
Model 79096020405
justification: The oven coil caught fire, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The Spring Lake Park-Blaine-Mounds View responded to a report of smoke coming from the refrigerator.  [REDACTED] arrived and found the house evacuated.  There was a light smoke in the house and a smell of burning electrical/plastic.  [REDACTED] attempted to locate the breakers to shut off the appliance however the panels were not marked for which unit they control.  Therefore [REDACTED] simply unplugged the unit. incident_description: I turned on my clean Kenmore oven.  The oven is four years old.  The bottom element caught fire and melted a large area of it.   I called Sears and they could not tell me why this would happen.   I looked online and found that many people have had the same problem with their Kenmore oven.  Some fires were worse than others.  I am afraid to replace the element and then have my house burn down because of this defect. It is a 940.9403.

incident_description: Investigated burning plastic smell from my Kenmore dishwasher and found wires from the control board melted into other plastic around the door. Searched online and found kitchenaidfire.com, thank god. There are about 400 reports of fires from Whirlpool made dishwashers manufactured around the same period, all starting from the control panel. Whirlpool denies any responsibility, so I guess they need a class action lawsuit going before they do anything.

incident_description:
Pressed bake (or POSSIBLY convection) button on front panel and flames and smoke immediately shot up from back above control panel. A strong odor of electrical fire. Control panel lights went out. Flames shot up on wall behind stove. Black smoke pouring up from back of control panel. It stopped then started again. incident_description: While I was pouring out boiling water into my cup the handle of the Capresso Electric Glass Kettle broke and the whole pot lunged towards my cup.
