justification: The incident caused property damage (melted dishwasher and dishes) but no injury or death, and such malfunctions are uncommon but not unheard of.

incident_description: Tried to cook chicken in the oven (electic) portion of the dual-fuel range, after about 20 minutes of baking at 350 degrees, the inside glass exploded. It covered the chicken with glass and destroyed the thermometer.
justification: The incident involved glass explosion causing property damage (destroyed thermometer) but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
The incident occurred on Friday 10/21/2011at 7:25p.m eastern time according to the Sparta Fire Department report.

The GE microwave oven caught on fire while not being in use.  I told my wife to run out of the house to call 911 as I grabbed a fire extinguisher and put out the fire.  Before we had a chance to call 911, the home's alarm went off and the alarm company contacted the fire department and police.  The entire house rapidly filled with black smoke debris and white powder from the fire extinguisher.  Extensive damage was experienced to the cabinets, floors, carpets, walls, ceilings and furniture.  In addition,  we have been exposed to a reasonable amount of chemicals, which we can still feel today in our lungs.  

The insurance company told us that we were very lucky as the fire could have rapidly spread to the entire house.  They told us that it seemed like it began in the electrical panel, but they will take the microwave unit into their labs for further examination.  

The initial estimated damages by the insurance company was put at $25,000-$35,000 and we have been told that the estimate will likely surpass that point due to the cleaning costs and other expenses.  I was further told by the insurance company (Travelers) that an investigation is currently going on, as many consumers have gone to the unfortunate experience with GE microwave ovens.  

Product Model Number: 164D5312G001
Product Serial Number: ZD94431S
MANUFACTURED in KOREA December 2002
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and exposure to chemicals, but no direct injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: We have a GE rangetop microwave. On 2 seperate occasions, the plastic clips that hold the metal shelf has sparked causing flames and melted the clips. We had to call GE to report each incidence and to obtain replacement clips on both occasions. The first occurance was over a year and a half ago, the most recent was the beginning of this year.
justification: The incident involved sparks and flames but no reported injuries, and it has occurred twice over a span of more than a year.

incident_description:
Three weeks ago,l installed my new Frigidaire range, however, I feel it is a fire hazard because the oven controller
has fallen out of its hole. Initially, the oven controller was glued in a rectangular slot inside the range, but the glue
was not nearly enough to stabilize this controller to function when pressed, after several weeks, the glue gave out,
and now the controller must be placed horizontally across the hole. Occasionally, the controller has a habit of falling
near the back burners, which could cause a fire immediately or an electrical flre, because the wiring that is
attached to the oven controller gets very hot when the oven is on.
justification: The oven controller falling near hot burners poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
We purchased an Avante Elite convection toaster oven by T-FAL on 3-2-2010. This oven has a glass door on the top, covering a warming tray. The glass door has a 4 inch black handle attached to lift the door. Below the warming section is the regular convection/toaster oven with a separate handle. The Avante Elite sits on top of a 14 inch high microwave oven on a wooden kids play table at the side of our kitchen. 

At noon on 10-23-2011, we used the toaster function of the toaster oven to toast 4 slices of bread. We removed the toast and sat at our kitchen table which is 6 feet from the front of the Avante oven. Approximately ten minutes later there was a loud explosion sound and glass and the handle from the upper door of the Avante exploded into our kitchen. No one was near the oven, it was off at the time, and nothing hit it or dropped on it.  It just exploded! Glass pieces hit me sitting in my wheelchair at our table but did not injure me. For a few minutes following the original explosion, pieces of glass continued to fly off. We took numerous pictures of the glass and oven to document this catastrophic failure.

We were shocked by this amazing event. Frequently, our four young grandchildren eat at the table below the Avante. Luckily, they were not at our house today. If they had been sitting at the table, they would surely have been seriously injured by the flying glass and flying handle which weighs over 4 ounces. My daughter also has this model Avante oven in her house but she will stop using it immediately. 

I called T-FAL and started a report file with them about this incident. This is a very serious, dangerous failure of a common product which we felt the CSPS should know about.
justification: The incident involved an explosion causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rare as such catastrophic failures are uncommon.

incident_description:
Kettle ceased functioning over a period of time and finally would not work at all.  Burnt plastic smell was also noticed.  Upon inspection of the base unit, it was noted that within the interior of the base, the cord was blackened from heat damage and had the odor of burnt plastic.

Within the black circular connection unit it was noted that the center electrical contact had melted into the plastic.  This plastic was also heat damaged.  See photographs.

Appears to pose a fire risk.
justification: The kettle malfunctioned with visible heat damage and a burnt smell, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased this toaster last year about this time of year from Wal Mart..it has gotten pretty warm at times but nothing we were alarmed about..Last night we'd gone to bed and within the hour our kitchen filled with smoke and the alarms went off..the smoke was so heavy going to celing we thought and the fireman thought it was our ceiling fan/light..

Nope, it was our toaster on fire..hadn't been used in 2 days so we never gave it a thought with the smoke up near ceiling..it melted stuff around it and a bag of rolls setting by it became part of it..

I've heard of appliances starting on their own but never experienced it..from now on every appliance not in use will be unplugged..But the makers of this DURABRAND TOASTER..Model #TS-5221..should recall and make sure what they are making in the future does not do this..we were lucky that it is only us..what if our children or grandchildren had been alone here..BE AWARE PLEASE
justification: The toaster caught fire without being used, causing smoke and melting nearby items, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: My LG Refrigerator Model # LFX21960ST  partially caught fire.After smelling and seeing smoke coming from my refrigerator, I was socked to see the upper lighting fixture had melted. I researched on the internet for potential occurrences to others . The search resulted in hundreds of occurrences.An investigation needs to be preformed.
justification: The refrigerator partially caught fire, causing damage but no reported injuries, and similar incidents are reported frequently online.

incident_description: Maytag microwave Model # mmv4184aab must be unpluged to be turned off.  If left pluged in it will comtinue to cook anyting that is left in the oven.
justification: The microwave's failure to turn off could lead to overcooking or fire, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: I ran my Whirlpool Dishwasher, model # DU1148xtpb1, on Sunday October 23, 2011 on a normal wash load cycle. During the drying portion of the cycle the control panel's circuit board got so hot that it melted a hole in the board. The smell and smoke of melted plastic was evident throughtout my house. I purchased this machine in January 2005.
justification: The incident involved a melted circuit board and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I turned on my dishwasher and left the room. My son (5) noticed a bad smell, so I started searching for this smell. When I went to my kitchen my dishwasher was on fire, and kitchen was full of smoke. Immediately, I removed the kids and pets from the house, cut power to the appliance and called 911. The fire company came and said that yes it was an electrical fire from the dishwasher. I replaced the entire kitchen appliances, as now I had a bad opinion of Whirlpool appliances, and honestly, afraid the others could catch fire too. I had no idea that there was a recall on these items, till now, 7 months later.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher fire causing smoke but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the known recall and electrical fire risk.

incident_description: Upon cooking stuffed squash in a relatively new Pyrex glass pie dish, I removed it from the oven and and set it onto an unused burner.... it shattered into many pieces all over the top of the stove.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: Within first use of the sippy cup water bottle, by 5 year old son bit off the spout, which he could have choked on.
justification: The child bit off the spout but did not choke, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I purchased these glasses for iced coffee/tea. The first glass actually exploded when I poured coffee (not very hot) on ice cubes. Fortunately it was in the sink so the glass was contained. The second glass exploded in the refrigerator after I put room temperature coffee in the glass to keep overnight. When I opened up the refrigerator, there was coffee and shards of glass all over the refrigerator and the floor. These glasses do not hold up and are very dangerous. They should be banned.
Fortunately the first incident caused me no harm but only because the sink acted as a buffer. Had I been holding the glass or had it on the sink shelf I would have been hit by flying shards (shrapnel). Think how risky it would have been if I had a child who opened the refrigerator and went to get something inside with all the shards around.
justification: The incident involved exploding glasses causing potential harm, but no actual injuries occurred.

incident_description:
I had a brand new Black & Decker model TRO355 toaster oven (an older model, circa 2006?) that was still in the original factory retail box.  This week (October 2011), I plugged in this toaster oven for the first time and used the toast function.  I could see through the front glass door that the upper and lower heating coils glowing red/orange.  But in about 1 or 2 minutes, there was a very loud explosion (louder than a firecracker)!  Fortunately, I was not looking through the glass door like I was doing just moments ago.  The front glass door blew open and there was smoke throughout the kitchen.  After yanking the power cord out of the AC outlet, I could see that the 2 bottom heating elements and 1 of the 2 top heating elements had exploded.  The metal sheath of each element was torn/twisted open and the coiled wire from inside the heating element was hanging out.  The white ceramic/porcelain insulators on the ends of each heating element had shattered.  There was white powder from those insulators everywhere inside the oven, on the kitchen counter, on the kitchen cabinets and on the floor.  There were small pieces of the white insulators in several places in the kitchen, up to about 4 feet away from the toaster oven.

This Black & Decker toaster oven was new and not tampered with or damaged in any way as far as I know.  I have looked on the internet and find at least a few other people who reported the exact same experience (explosion of the heating elements, white powder everywhere) and coincidentally was the same model:  TRO355.

I have had an older but very similar Black & Decker toaster oven that I used without any problems for over 10 years.  But this TRO355 was extremely dangerous and we are lucky that my spouse or I or my children were not injured by this incident.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion with no injuries, and similar incidents have been reported for the same model.

incident_description:
The Cuisinart DCC-1100 pot that we recently purchsed does not have a non- programmable auto shut off.This is
especially bad in case remaining coffee dries up.Pot can overheat and possibly catch fire.
I understand that the pot has a timed shut-down,but that does not address unit overheating. lt could be out of
product in 15 min and stay on 4 hrs.
If one does not choose to use timed shut down there is no protection. It is potential fire hazard.
justification: The incident describes a potential fire hazard due to lack of auto shut-off, which could lead to property damage but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Cuisinart DC-1100 coffee maker quit working and it smelled  hot and a heavy electrical smoke.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned with smoke, indicating an incident but no reported injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Ronco FD1005WHGEN 5-Tray Electric Food Dehydrator from AMAZON.com.

Upon the first use, one of the plastic parts melted and released an odor / smoke. We had retired for the nite, the smell woke us up. We unplugged it.

This product is a fire hazard and should be removed from the market.
justification: The incident involved a melted plastic part and smoke, but no injury or death occurred, warranting a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as it happened upon first use but may not be common for all units.

incident_description:
On October 25, 2011, we were unable to shut off the right front burner of our Frigidaire Electrolux glass top range, which was apparently set on high. We had been using the burner, and when my wife turned the burner down to simmer, she was surprised that the food was still boiling. She took the food off the burner and realized that it would not turn off. I tried several times to turn it off with the knob, without success. I then unplugged the range, and plugged it back in, hoping that it would reset, but the burner came back on at high. Finally, I unplugged the stove and had my dinner. After dinner, I tried some more things, and finally when I set the burner at its lowest temperature, I noticed that the burner seemed to be resetting at a lower temperature. When I turned the dial to off, the burner turned off. 

Although the stovetop may be working, we have left it unplugged since the incident. An unattended burner at a high temperature is a serious fire hazard.  

The Model number is PLEF398CCD. The serial number is VF42128366.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that posed a fire hazard but was successfully managed without injury.

incident_description:
My GE microwave (Model WES1450DN1BB) auto-started during the night, becoming extremely hot to the touch.  If this had occurred during the day, I'm certain it would have caused a fire.

I have since purchased a new microwave and will never use a GE microwave again.  From some on-line research, I understand that this is not an uncommon occurrence with these microwaves, so it is very troubling that GE is able to continue to manufacture these appliances.
justification: The microwave auto-started and became extremely hot, posing a fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer was baking biscuits in the oven on350 degrees  for approximately  minutes when they heard a popping noise but prior to the noise that was heard  the cook top was used but had been powered in the off position. 

He opened the oven door  and before  closing the door there was thick black smoke pouring from the behind the range and when the door was closed that was when he saw smoke coming from the same direction 

He attempted to use table salt on the fire but when that did not put the fire out the range was pulled from wall and unplugged from the wall outlet and placed outside where he was able to put the fire out with a nearby water house.

The retailer was contacted the date of the incident where the consumer was advised there was no warranty on the appliance and that there was also no recall.

The consumer still currently has the appliance located in the backyard on a concrete patio. She indicated that she does not feel safe with it being in the home and she is not sure if she will have the unit repaired.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injury or death was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) given the detailed description of the event and the consumer's ongoing concern.

incident_description:
I have a 4 year old Kenmore 790.9611340A Range and the burner won't turn off.  This is the second time this has happened in the last 2 months.  The first time we were able to get it to turn off by jiggling the switch.  We have used the stove many times since but now the eye won't turn off and we need to switch the circuit breaker to get it to turn off.  The condition is identical to Recall #09-333.  I have found numerous other cases of this model experiencing this condition online and believe my model should be added to the recall. I have talked to Sears Customer solutions and residential customer care and they are not willing to fix the issue because it is not on the recall list.

Had my wife not noticed the range glowing this could have burned our house down or easily burned her or one of my kids.
justification: The burner not turning off poses a fire hazard and potential injury risk, though no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Left front burner will not turn off or turn down but remains red hot
justification: The burner remaining red hot poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Caller turned dishwasher on but only approximately a minute later saw sparks coming from the handle, smoke and smelled a burning odor.

Because she had not walked away and was beside the dishwasher she was able to open the door.

The sparks stopped after she opened the door but the burning and the odor of burning continued for maybe 3 minutes.

Caller did not trip the breaker and said it didn't appear to be out of position, all breakers were o.k.

Caller states that dishwasher was in house when she and her husband purchased it in 1998.
She is calling manufacturer once we hang up from call.
That she would like to have dishwasher replaced at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and a burning odor, but no injury occurred as the caller was able to open the dishwasher door and stop the sparks.

incident_description: October 5, 2011 - it was late evening when we heard a strange noise coming from the kitchen. When we investigated, there was smoke coming from the dishwasher and spreading into the room. We tried to turn it off but without success, so we had to shut down the power to stop it. By then the burning smell permeated the area and we had to air out the house for hours to even make it breathable. When the repairman came the next day, he discovered the circuit board and associated wiring were completely burned, he took photos as he had never seen such severe damage (he could use them to train new technicians). He didn't know how far the damage would reach, his advice, put the money into a new dishwasher. We are contacting Kitchenaid as we loved the design and features of this dishwasher, however, the fire concern is real
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from a malfunctioning dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I had loaded a batch of dishes into my dishwasher and started it.  I went outside and was working in my yard around 4:00 pm.  My husband had picked up my daughter from school and brought her home.   At approximately 5:00 pm my husband and daughter arrived home.  I was still working in the yard.  My daughter went into the house and came running out asking me what was burning in the kitchen.  I told her that I was not cooking anything and I ran in the house.  The kitchen was filled with smoke and there was a terrible chemical smell in the air.  We checked all outlets, ovens, cooking appliances, etc.  My husband came in and was looking around as well.  We started opening up all the windows and covering our noses.  My husband went to the dishwasher and noticed that there was some brown markings on the top of the dishwasher and as we looked further, there was a bubbling of the plastic underneath the controls to the dishwasher.  The chemical smell and smoke was terrible.  I believe that if we had not caught this when we did, we would have been dealing with a fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a chemical smell but no injury or fire occurred, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description: The glass pyrex dish I used exploded in my oven.  In shattered in hundreds of tiny pieces.
justification: The pyrex dish exploded but there is no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
Insinkerator Disposal Air Switch / Model Number 71456 / 120 Volt / 12 Amp - Air actuator switch to turn garbage disposal on and off

My garbage disposal turned itself on I smelled burning wires.  I unplugged the Air Switch (Air Switch plugged into outlet and disposal plugged into Air Switch).  Air switch smelled like burning wires and I unscrewed the four screws that hold on the faceplate - upon inspection I saw burnt wires and smoke pattern on inside.

I called Insinkerator to discuss what happened and what I saw and explained that I was glad I was home when it happened as my fear was that it could have caught fire.  The customer service person at Insinkerator told me it was a known issue they had documentation on and that I could buy a new unit.  I was a bit surprised and when I reiterated that I'm glad I was home when it happened and concerned that this was a known issue - the support person then repeated that it was a known issue and that I could buy a new one.

My fear is that if this happened to my Air Switch, there could be one out there where this may happen to someone else that isn't home they might not be so lucky.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning air switch with burnt wires, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Stove top spontaneously turned on (with all dials off) at least twice in last week.

Fridgidaire: FEFB79GSA
S/N:            VF71625358

Electric range is very similar to, but not included, in voluntary recall listed in:
http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml09/09333.html
justification: The stove turning on spontaneously is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
One of the stovetop elemetns on my smoothtop electric oven/range activated by itself and will not turn off.  The burner visually appears to be on the highest setting (the element under the glass is bright red) but the dial is set to off.  The digital display shows "HE" which normally indicates a burner is off but remains hot.  If the burner were on, it would display a number to correspond to the setting.  The dial is also at a different distance from the surface of the range.

Other functions (timer, oven, other burners) appear to work normally.  The only way turn off the unit is to shut down the circuit breaker.

Product #: PLEF398CCD

This unit was previously repaired under a recall order for this specific problem.  The technician appeared to tape the control units for the burners to the back of the panel with a metallic tape.  It would seem that this taping job failed.
justification: The stovetop element activating by itself poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: I was manually brewing 6 cups of coffee in my Cuisinart DCC-1000 coffee maker. Approximately 30 minutes after the brewing was complete sparks and smoke began emitting underneath the coffee maker. Luckily I was present as this began to happen and I quickly unplugged the coffee maker and moved it outside and doused it with water. The only other issue I have had with this coffee maker is the clock would not keep accurate time.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no injury or death, and was quickly mitigated by the user.

incident_description: At 6am on Oct. 24, 2011, I made coffee with my Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker. The unit is roughly one-year-old. It shut itself off about an hour later via its "auto" off function. Around 9am, my dog perked up and growled at the kitchen. I could hear crackling sounds. I walked into the kitchen to find the coffee maker engulfed in smoke. There were no visible flames, but the unit was very hot and continued to smoke. It had an acrid electrical arcing odor. The unit was still plugged in. I unplugged it and moved it out of the house, where it continued to spew smoke.
justification: The incident involved a smoking coffee maker but no injury or flames, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common with standard appliances.

incident_description:
Kenmore Coldspot Refrigerator start relay and components attached to compressor burn up and smoking. Melted one of the three prongs on compressor so cannot even replace the burnt components.
Would need to replace compressor and components. Still have worry it might burn again and catch house on fire. Read reports on internet that this is a common problem with this model and many other brands with this compressor set up.

Kenmore Coldspot: Model: 106.53234300
Serial Number: SP2937306
justification: The incident involves a refrigerator component burning up and smoking, posing a fire hazard but no reported injury or death. Reports indicate this is a common problem with this model.

incident_description: I have a three year old Kenmore smooth top range that has been malfunctioning.  One of the burners won't turn off and sometimes randomly turns on and heats up.  Even if the knob is in the off position the burner will continue to heat up and may just come on at any time.  There was a large recall for this problem through Kenmore and Frigidaire, but my model is not on the list.  From the complaints online, this problem is much bigger than just the models they have listed.  Now I am stuck either paying a repair bill that will be about a third the price of just getting a new one, or just getting a new one (not a Kenmore!).
justification: The malfunctioning burner poses a fire hazard and potential injury risk, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: While beginning to run the dishwasher, the control board on Kitchenaid dishwasher started to burn.  This caused smoke to rise from the unit and the smell of electrical wires burning to permeate the house.  I turned the unit off and shut off the electrical breaker for the unit.  Unit is still in home, however I will need to get a new one.  It is still in place and available for inspection and analysis.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burning smell but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
KitchenAid Dual-Fuel Double-Oven Range, Model Number: kdrs505xss01

Yesterday, my husband walked into the kitchen and was overcome by the smell of natural gas.  I had been in the kitchen a few minutes earlier and apparently brushed by the range knobs and inadvertently engaged one ever-so-slightly to where it allowed gas to escape, but not far enough that the lighting mechanism "clicked" that we would have been forewarned.  This has happened on at least 5 separate occasions, but I have always smelled gas almost immediately and turned it off.  I have notified KitchenAid on at least three occasions, but have been universally dismissed.  

In my inexpert opinion, the stainless steel knobs are too heavy, which allows a minimal amount of pressure to press the knob past the catch mechanism.
justification: Gas leakage poses a significant risk of explosion or poisoning, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
About 1 year after we purchased the range, the safety valve was leaking and had to be replaced. A few weeks ago the electronic ignitions just started to go off and not stop until I unplugged the range.  When I called Magtag I was told that if the burners were wet or out of place that could cause that to happen. I expressed my concerns if this happened and no one was home, what could happen!  Well today, the ignitions did that again, they continued to keep clicking away.  I was in the other room, by the time I got to the kitchen there was a puff of smoke from one of the burners and then then a fire surrounding the dials.   This also blew the circuit breaker.  This could have been disasterous if I were not home to put out the fire and unplug the range.
Maytag Gemini  Model # MGR6875ADB  serial # 12764984GG
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have been disastrous if not for immediate intervention, indicating a high potential for severe outcomes.

incident_description: Three years ago I installed a new Viking side-by-side refrigerator, model number VCSB423DSS, manufactured January 29, 2008, and the lower hinge on the refrigeration door is bending from the weight of the door and is at risk of breaking.
justification: The incident involves a refrigerator door hinge bending, which poses a risk of breaking but has not yet caused injury or death.

incident_description: Pyrex glass baking dish exploded in oven at 350 degrees.  simply reheating a previously cooked chicken.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I have a Ge Profile gas cooktop. Approximate age is 7 years old. I was making spaghetti and had a large pot  boiling with water on the high output burner. The other two burners were also being used at the same time. I placed the spaghettti in pot and some water boiled over. I was standing at the cooktop and was just going to stir the spaghetti and all of sudden the entire cooktop shattered and made a loud bang noise, like it exploded!. The glass shattered and pieces of glass came off cooktop. Part of the cooktop collapsed. I panicked and removed the pans and inadvertinly burned the countertop. At the time I was very concerned the cooktop was going to fully collapse into the cabinet. The spaghett pot  tipped and some water spilled out and burned my  foot and dogs paws.

I was so shakin up that I called my neighbor whom is the  captain of the fire department.  He came over immediately  and turned off the gas and told me to contact GE, this was definitely a manufacturer defect. 

The next day I called Ge and spoke with a [REDACTED]. She told me she was sorry for the mishap and would like to send a GE repairmen to my house to evaluate the cooktop. They even paid for the GE rep to come to my home to inspectthe unit. He arrrived at my home the same day within 4 hours. He evaluate the cooktop and  I quote, He said  " This happens alot on the electric glass cooktops but he had never seen it on the gas cooktops." He then tells me," Don't worry the part to fix this is no longer available so GE   will  replace this cooktop." " That's what we do when the parts are no longer available and this happens." End quote..

The next day I call [REDACTED] and I am on hold for 30 minutes and then I am told she is not available. I leave a voice message. Then I call again on the next day, still no [REDACTED]so I talk to [REDACTED]. She informs me at this time accoding to the notes in the computer, GE  will send me a new cooktop, however, I will need to pay $759.00. I tell her this is not acceptable. She says she will see what she can do. I never hear from her again!

I then get a call from GE telling me that since they have not heard from me they are closing my case. I immediately call, and again I am on hold for 30 minutes and still it is somebody new! This time they tell me I can get a new cooktop for $689.00 That is what I need to pay. I again say this is not acceptable. I did nothing wrong to have the cooktop shatter the way it did. I explain how the GE rep told me it was a manufacturing problem They told me to take this offer or they would be closing the case. I again said not acceptable and asked to speak to a manager. I was on hold for another 20 minutes and was finally told the managers were in a meeting and the only additional thing they could do is to take off the shipping charges off the price of a new  cooktop Meaning I will be paying $639.00. Big deal!! I could buy the same cooktop on the internet with an additional 10 year warranty, and free shipping for $800.00.

As it stands today I am waiting to hear from a manager at GE!!
justification: The incident resulted in burns to the person and their dog, indicating an injury (severity 3). The GE repairman noted this is rare for gas cooktops, suggesting low likelihood (2).

incident_description: I had a pot of water simmering on my front right burner and then shut off the stove.  I didn't take the pot off and about 2 minutes later the water started to boil.  When I took the pot off the burner I saw that the burner was bright red as if it was on high.  I double checked and the knob was off. I tried turning the knob on and then off again but it would not go off.  I had to wait until my husband came home from work so he could move the stove to unplug it.  This happend yesterday, today we tried pluging it back in to see if it cleared itself up.  It was off and about 2 minutes later it turned itself back on.
justification: The stove turning itself on is a serious incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On 10/22/2011 I was cooking in my Frigidaire Electric range when the lower heating element began to spark & flame. I shut off the oven immediatly. I contacted Frigidaire about this right away. They say the stove is not recalled. If I had not been in the kitchen when this happened my house could have started on fire. This is a Frigidaire Electric Range Model # FEF364FSB Serial # VF63161033. If you could check into this I would appreciate it.
justification: The incident involved a sparking and flaming heating element, which could have led to a fire if not addressed, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says the oven was on and very hot and could not get it to shut off.  There was an F2 code on the digital display and a constant beeping.   She contacted the gas company who disconnected the unit.  She never had any issues with it before.  She says there was an electronic ignition installed on it a few years ago.  She tried to contact the manufacturer but was not able to reach anyone.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but was safely disconnected without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: My husband, 21 month old daughter, and I were on the way home in the dark from shopping.  My daughter said "Cup broke!" and we told her there was no way the cup could have broken.  She was persistent so my husband turned on the light and sure enough she had ripped a portion of the spout off the Mighty Grip sippy cup.  We could not find the piece and were worried she had swallowed it.  When we got home my dear husband scoured the car and located it.  My concern is that the torn piece was small enough to be a choking hazard as per the FDA brochure on choking and young children and I have no idea if it would have passed safely through her digestive system.  I do have pictures I took when I got home.
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard, but the piece was found and no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Moved into a new modular home retirement community home June 2010, she cooks a lot and uses her GE Range quite often.

When she uses the self cleaning option for the range there is a lot of smoke, like walking through a dense fog.  

The smoke sets off smoke alarms.   

Caller is very much afraid that the cupboards could become too hot and catch fire .                                                                                                                                    

She would like to know whether this range is smoking "Normally" and would like to file a report with CPSC
justification: The incident involves significant smoke and potential fire hazard, causing fear but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Toaster oven started emitting a smell and small amounts of smoke about a week before the main incident.  We though some food or other foreign material fell into one of the vents on top of the unit.  About a week later, my wife was using the unit to heat up some frozen waffles.  Smoke and flames were visible from the right side of the unit.  It was immediately unplugged and the flames were blown out.  I opened the case and discovered the fire was an electrical fire.  The main power lead enters the unit and is clamped to several smaller diameter wires.  One of these connections overheated and caught the plastic insulating cover over it on fire.  The main power lead was against the side of the metal case, so had the plastic totally melted away, it was possible the case of the unit could have become energized.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames from an electrical fire, but was promptly contained without injury, indicating a moderate likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description: I have owned the same toaster over since the late 1990s.  I have always unplugged my toaster oven after I am done using it.  Recently, my toaster oven will turn on automatically when I plug it in.  I cannot shut it off even if I turn the temperature to "off" or the toaster button to "off".  The previous toaster I had (same brand) failed in a similar manner.  I contacted the manufacturer after my first toaster oven failed and they asked me to send them the end of the power cord and they sent me a new toaster oven, which is the one that I have now.  I am submitting this report to bring awareness to the problem associated with this product.
justification: The toaster turns on automatically and cannot be shut off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
When opening either door to the refrigerator he noticed on some occasions the light bulbs would be powered in the on position with the door closed or open. 

On 10/6/2011 while retrieving some butter from a  top self located under the housing of the light bulb he noticed that the butter had melted
he unplugged the refrigerator and allowed it to cool down and opened the refrigerators door and when he attempted to remove the light bulb the housing that surrounds the light bulb is warped. 

On 10/6/2011 he contacted the retailer and was informed that they had a service flash for certain serial numbers (same model numbers) and he was advised to contact the CPSC. He has a technician schedule to come out on 10/10/2011 to take a look at the unit. 

The consumer indicated that  by the light bulb staying in the on position while the door is closed could potentially pose as a fire or electrical hazard and to prevent that he has removed both light bulbs from both sides.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light bulb causing melted butter and a warped housing, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was reported and is being addressed, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer attempted to turn the oven on and there was a crackle-pop sound and a flame shot up from the back of the unit.  The consumer has not seen an visible damage to her wall.  The consumer immediately turned the control back off.  Her husband unpluged the unit from the electrical outlet.  He also checked the circuit breaker for the range/oven and it did trip.

There were no injuries.  Damage was limited to the unit itself.


The consumer called the mfr. and their rep. indicated that there was no recall on the product and then gave her the number to the CPSC Hotline.

The consumer also searched the Internet and found other reports of problems with this manufacturer's product.
justification: The incident involved a flame and electrical issue with no injuries or visible damage, and similar reports were found online, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description: Blender began to smoke and sparks came out from the bottom of the blender.
justification: The blender smoking and sparking indicates an incident but no injury was reported, making severity level 2. Such electrical malfunctions are uncommon but not rare, hence likelihood 2.

incident_description:
While using the dishwasher on the normal setting with the high temperature scrub  for approximately 15 minutes when she detected a horrible burning electric odor. 

She noticed that the dishwasher had stopped operating  within 15 minutes after it was being started and she does not recall noticing any smoke coming from the appliance.

The cycle stopped directly in the midst  of the rinse cycle so she used a wet dry vacuum to get the water out of the machine, 

When she was able to take a closer look she noticed that the vent on located on the front of the dishwasher near the control panel had the electrical burning odor coming from it. 

 The consumerÃÂs husband is an electrician by trade and took the control panel a part and noticed that  circuit board had caught fire.

The firm has not been contacted but she plans on contacting them. She has not  used the dishwasher since the failure occurred and has unplugged the appliance from the wall outlet.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned with a burning odor and a circuit board fire, but no injuries or smoke were reported.

incident_description: The consumer stated that his refrigerator was smoking this morning. The consumer stated that the refrigerator was emitting a electrical burning smell and the consumer had to unplug the refrigerator in order to make the smoking subside. They style of the refrigerator is a side by door model. The consumer cannot see any outer damage to the refrigerator. The consumer stated that the product has not caused any property damage to his home. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident took place. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The consumer called the firm and was told that there is no recall for his product. The firm has offered to send a repairman but is not sure of who is to pay for the service. The consumer has not been harmed or injured by the product. The consumer suspects that the relay may be the cause of the smoking. The consumer was not injured by the product but did smell burning electrical components.
justification: The refrigerator was smoking and emitting an electrical burning smell, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description: My Kitchenaid Microwave Hood combination started sparking 2 years after purchase.  I had two repair companies look at it, and it is non-operable.  Kitchenaid said that due to arcing and melted tuning rods, it is a fire hazard.  It is not covered by any warrantly, just 2 years after purchase, and retail value is $1050.
justification: The microwave sparked and is a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The whirlpool microwave MH1150XMB-1 was not running. We warmed up some food about 15 minutes prior and the cook time was over. It was not running and nothing was going on.

I noticed a smell - a burning smell. We looked around and noticed a fire inside the microwave. It was the small gasket under the turntable plate was burning and the plate was cracked. We immediately opened the door to the microwave and tried to remove the plate. The plate was black and cracked, and the small gasket was blackened and burnt. After removing the plate and the gasket, we closed the door. Then unplugged the unit from power.

This is totally unacceptable quality of whirlpool. Luckily we were home and happened to notice the fire. If we had not been home, it would have been a major fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the microwave with no reported injuries, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but can occur with faulty equipment.

incident_description: I used an Anchor brand glass pie dish to bake some chopped sweet potatoes in the oven.  I baked them at 400 degrees for 40 minutes.  As I began to take the dish out of the oven, the dish cracked and broke in my hands.  Luckily I had oven mits on, so my hands were not injured, but glass shattered all over the inside of my oven.
justification: The glass dish broke but no injury occurred due to the use of oven mitts, though it caused a mess.

incident_description:
I have a 8 cup Faberwear electric coffee pot.  It is about 2 years old.  While cleaning it the handle fell off.  I don't understand how the handle was attached to the pot.  There is no hole where a screw goes into the body of the stainless steel pot.  The handle has a indent in which there is a screw that goes into a small plate, but the plate nor screw goes into the body of the pot.

I feel very fortunate that this happened while I was cleaning the pot and not when I was pouring a hot cup of coffee.

This is unbelievable to me...but then again not, after all it is made in China.
justification: The handle fell off during cleaning, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: On October 19th in the evening I was using the Magic Bullet to make my daughter some baby food.  I have used this blender many times (10-15) in the past month as she just started eating table food.  I cut up sweet potatoes into small squares and put in two tablespoons of water along with the sweet potatoes into the tall cup.  I attached the steamer lid and placed it in the microwave for three minutes.  When the timer went off I removed the lid stirred up the potatoes then place the cross blade onto the cup.  I then placed them on the base and blended the potatoes.  I noticed they needed some more water to get the right consistency so I removed the cup from the base.  I banged the cup on the counter to get the sweet potatoes to slide down the cup so I wouldn't make a mess when I opened the lid.  I started to unscrew the cross blade attachment and it was giving me a hard time and all of a sudden as I unscrewed the contents exploded in a six-feet radius around my kitchen and on myself.  My husband came in to see what happened and I started to feel my skin burning.  He rushed me to the sink to run cold water on my skin.  It felt like my skin was falling off the burn was so intense.  We read online what to do for a burn so we covered my arm with loose gauze.  I woke up the next day (today) and I have an appointment to see the doctor to find out what else we can do.  I have two burn marks on my left wrist and hand.  One on the top of my hand just below the thumb the size of a quarter, red with white bumps in the middle.  One on my wrist the size of a dime and deep red.  Both of them are extremely tender and feel like large bruises.  My hand is also stiff.
justification: The incident resulted in burns requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
WE own a GE Profile 30" dual fuel convection range model #J2B918SEK3ss, serial #LL202846P, PURCHASED 07/01/2006. The unit has a warming tray/oven below the regular oven. On September 27, 2011 we discovered that the dishwasher had been leaking and reported a claim to State Farm Insurance. State Farm sent the local Service Master firm to remove the damaged flooring. During this process I was called to the kitchen and shown the vinyl flooring under the above referenced range. The top layer of vinyl (aprox. 4 to 5 years old) had a dinner plate size burn under the area of the warming tray and the second layer of vinyl, much older, had a smaller burn through to the pine sub flooring.

I have both layers of the flooring. I have digital photos of the flooring as each layer was removed.

GE service techs said the range was installed correctly with a minimum of 1/4 inch clearance.

The company installing the new vinyl states they have never experienced this problem before.
The company that sold the top layer of the vinyl that was burned states they have never experienced this problem before.
Service Master states they have never experienced this problem before.

GE has not provided any assistance in correcting, repairing or replacing the range.

I feel that this product is a danger to our house and to our lives.

For the incident date I have used the discovery date.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned flooring) but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Light bulbs in refrigerator compartment did not turn off when door closed.   Melted plastic cover and scorched bulb sockets.  FIRE HAZARD!
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator and posed a fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My dishwasher caught on fire. I had started my dishwasher and had gone to bed. After about 15 minutes or so I heard a strange noise and got up and went into the kitchen. There was black smoke billowing out of the top vents on my dishwasher and it had a very distinctive burning smell. I immediately opened the dishwasher door believing this would shut off the dishwasher. I was drenched with hot water as the water did not shut off and the dishwasher continued to run and fling water throughout my kitchen. So I closed the door and the smoke continued to flow.  My husband went to the garage and turned off the circuit breaker and only then after a few minutes did the smoke dissipate.  
The plastic / electrical burn smell has stayed in our house for two days.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and caused significant smoke and water damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I own a Kenmore oven.  The model number is 790.92412102.  

While cooking a turkey (at 325 degrees) the other night, the bake element heated out of control.  It did not turn off when we tried to use the control buttons, and we had to turn off the breaker in order to force the oven to cool down.   

This is the third time that I have experienced this problem with this oven.  I feel fortunate that I have been standing in the kitchen each time that it has occurred and that I noticed the problem before my oven went up in flames.  The other times that the problem occurred, I "fixed" it by unscrewing the back cover, unplugging the wire from the "bake" control, plugging in the oven, unplugging the oven, reattaching the wire, then replugging in the oven.  The oven then made a little buzzing noise (like something electronic re-setting itself) and worked properly for some time (probably about a year).  This time, I have been unable to induce the oven to "reset" itself, and have therefore been obliged to leave the wire unplugged from the control, as the bake element begins to heat up of its own accord every time I plug it back in.  

The first time this occurred, I checked online and found dozens of complaints about the same issue.  This time (about two years later) I found even more.  It doesn't seem to me that this is an isolated issue.  This is a serious danger.  I have 5 children ages 12 and under.  When the oven decides to overheat like this, the exterior of the unit is always very hot by the time I've noticed what is going on (much hotter than it gets during normal usage).  One of my children could EASILY burn themselves on the exterior of the overheated oven.  The items inside the oven have  burned every time it goes out of control like this.  This time, the turkey bag enclosing the turkey breast melted and burned onto the pan, releasing VILE fumes into our house.  We aired the house as best we could, but it still STANK to high heaven all night long.  I believe I'm going to have to dispose of the pan, too, because I can't get the burned on turkey bag to come off, even with the flat edge of a razor.  

This is a manufacturer problem with the oven unit.  It is not an isolated issue.  The company should take some responsibility in correcting this problem.
justification: The oven's uncontrolled heating poses a burn risk to children and has caused property damage, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: Our Sears Kenmore dishwasher,(Mod 665.16052400), had a fire occur in the control panel.  Luckily I was home at the time and was able to shut off the circuit breaker providing power to the unit.  Black smoke was coming from  the front of the dishwasher and did not stop until the circuit breaker was tripped by me.  Have other consumers reported problems like this about this model dishwasher?  Are there any recalls on this product?  The dishwasher was purchased in 2005.   Considering the severity of the failure and the fact that the house circuit breaker did not trip, this could have ended in a house fire.   Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher control panel, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the potential for house fires if not addressed.

incident_description:
The consumer says the unit has leaked since he purchased product.  He called a repairman who told him the valve pump unit is defective.  He says that the underflooring of his kitchen is now damaged.  The leak had gotten on a junction box in his basement which poses a shock hazard.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and sent them the defective pump.  
They refused to test it because the bracket was removed and said that he tampered with it.  He noticed many reports about the same issue on complaint boards online.  The manufacturer also acknowledged that there have been complaints.  He says that the unit works fine with a third party pump installed on it.
justification: The incident involves property damage and a potential shock hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: KitchenAid dishwasher model KUDMO1FKSS, serial # FM2303399 was running when housekeeper heard popping sound and then saw smoke coming out of dishwasher.  She opened the dishwasher door and flames shot out.  She put out fire using spray nozzle from sink. The control panel appeared to be on fire.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, but no injury or death was reported, and the fire was quickly extinguished.

incident_description:
I have an Amana range model AOCS3040E
It failed and when we opened it up found a high voltage wire running lose and near the housing had touched the side and belew out (charing markes are redaly aparent as the wire welded to the housing). on further inspection realized there were 5 such wires floting in the air that could wiggle from shutting the door and short acainst the housing applying 120 volts to the housing that is commonly touched by the user and creating the potential for electricution and or fire. Common practice is to use insulated wiring for these high voltage lines to insure they can not short to something, but for some reason this unit was assembled with these wires exposed and with no insulation. The other wires in the oven are properly insulated but not these.
justification: The exposed high voltage wires pose a significant risk of electric shock or fire, which could lead to injury or death if the housing is touched.

incident_description: Can opener produced metal shavings that entered into food containers as it was being used. Purchaser was cut by a large shaving resulting in injury. When Customer Service was contacted to report the danger and incident, representative ignored the immediate problem and advised to return the product and packaging at customer expense and they would replace the unit.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from metal shavings, and the problem was ignored by customer service, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: GE Electric Range, model #JPB89SM2SS, Burner knob in off position, range stayed on. Found knob was made completely of plastic with no metal reinforcement where shaft entered knob. This is a burn and fire risk as the stove can be on even when the knob is in the off position.
justification: The incident describes a burn and fire risk due to a faulty knob, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We turned our oven on to bake at 400f.  The broiler came on during baking, overheated the oven and burned our dinner.  We attempted to turn off the broiler by turning the oven off and we tried turning the broiler on & off, but nothing would turn it off.  The only remedy was to unplug the oven entirely.

When the oven was plugged back in, the broiler immediately came back on and could not be turned off.

This oven is equipped with a delay start to allow users to begin cooking at a specified time.  Had we used this feature the oven could have ignited, causing a fire.  Fortunately, we were monitoring the oven when this happened and we were able to get the oven unplugged before a fire erupted.

The motherboard controller for the oven had to be replaced to fix the problem.

This is the second time this oven has had the exact same problem in our home.  We replaced the motherboard in 2010 and again just this week (Oct 2011).  In researching the issue, we see that this model has numerous complaints from other owners with the exact same problem.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned dinner) and posed a fire risk, but no injuries or deaths occurred. The problem is recurring and has been reported by multiple owners, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
At 9 PM on 10/17/11 our Bosch dishwasher caught on fire at the control panel. Flames were over a foot high and melted the control panel and front of the dishwasher. We used a fire extinguisher to to put out the file and the Moorestown Fire Company responded. The Bosch dishwasher is:
Model number SHU3307UC/14
Serial number FD8208 000468
Purchased around 2002.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was extinguished without further incident.

incident_description: Dishwasher was designed and manufactured with a water inlet on the left side of the unit that is open at the top allowing water to splash out of the unit when it runs.  The slow and steady flow of moisture soaks the sound insulating cloth on the outside of the unit which in turn transfers the moisture to nearby cabinets, flooring, drywall, etc.  The result over time is water damage to surrounding furnishing and development of hazardous mold.  The problem goes undetectable until the cabinets, flooring, and drywall become saturated with water at which time small pools of water begin to appear.
justification: The slow and steady flow of moisture causes water damage to surrounding furnishings and development of hazardous mold, which is an incident but does not cause injury.

incident_description:
We have a Maytag double wall oven, model MEW5630DDB, that we purchased 6 years ago. I was pulling a cobbler out of the oven when the oven rack fell off the rack ledge and crashed down, spilling the cobbler all over. It happened a week before, and can happen now by just moderately pressing on the rack. The rack is still in good condition and shape. The rack from the bottom oven fits snuggly in the bottom oven, but when placed in the top oven, falls the same thing as the other rack. The rest of the oven(s) operates normally.

I contacted Maytag today, explaining the situation and they told me I had to pay for a service man to come out. When I pressed them that this was a manufacturer's defect and a major safety issue that I could not have caused, they told me I was out of warranty and they would not do anything. I offered for them to come take measurements to problem solve their product quality but they continued on about the warranty. They asked if I was burned and when I said no (because I jumped back), they said there was nothing they would do.

Clearly, this is a major safety issue that Maytag wants to ignore. It is a certain fact that this would lead to injury. If my oven is faulty, surely many more are as well. I have children cooking in my house.
justification: The incident involves a rack falling, which could lead to spills or burns, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is high as it has happened multiple times and could easily recur.

incident_description: Kitchenaid Microwave overheated and caught on fire.
justification: The microwave caught fire, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Runaway / Uncontrollable Oven

I purchased a Kenmore Oven from Sears - Model # 790.92419102  Serial #  VF23607376

The electronic control failed and the oven ran at maximum heat and COULD NOT BE SHUT OFF.  The only way to stop this dangerous condition was to disconnect the power supply.

Any reasonable person would expect a failure to result in non-operation of the device; NOT an uncontrollable fire hazard.

Contact with officials from both Sears and Kenmore was made with no concern on their part. An Internet search search shows this has happened to numerous other consumers as well.
justification: The oven's uncontrollable operation poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. Internet reports suggest this issue is not isolated, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: During drying cycle smoke and flames starting coming out of the top right of the control panel. Opened door and extinguished flames, no injury or property damage other than the dishwasher.
justification: Smoke and flames indicate a significant incident, but no injury or property damage beyond the dishwasher occurred.

incident_description: Front right burner comes on and stays on unless entire oven is disconnected from electric source.  Fire started in kitchen which had to be put out with extinguisher.
justification: The fire started in the kitchen and had to be put out with extinguisher, but there was no injury.

incident_description: Toastmaster Toaster Oven/Broiler is just over one year old. When using yesterday to bake a sweet potato, the glass door shattered. The oven was set at 350 degrees and had been on about 20 minutes. The door was tempered glass and no glass shards were produced when it shattered but glass was all over my kitchen counter top in front of the toaster oven.
justification: The glass door shattered but no injuries occurred, only creating a mess on the countertop.

incident_description: Baking a meatloaf in the oven the baking dish exploded in the oven just prior to removal. The oven timer had just finished approx. one minute after a loud bang inside the oven. Oven was set to 350 degree for 35 minutes. Upon opening the door to the oven the glass baking dish was shattered, glass all over on the inside, meatloaf juices dripping to the oven bottom almost starting a fire. Luckily no one was hurt but a few seconds later would of meant totally different outcome
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, making it a severity level 2.

incident_description: Maytag built-in dishwasher began to smolder while in drying mode.  According to the fire department, an electrical short ignited some insulating material.  When the firefighters arrived, they removed a burning piece of insulation  from lower front area.  It was still glowing when they extinguished it.  The firefighters stated that it could have burned our house down had we not been home, not noticed the burning smell or seen the smoke.  We're very fortunate.
justification: The incident involved a smoldering dishwasher with potential for severe damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I bought a Kitchenaid double oven about 3 years ago. I had never used the self cleaning feature till last Saturday (10/15/2011). During the self cleaning the inside glass exploded with so much force that shattered glass came out of the closed oven and scattered around the oven sapce. Also the lower oven was filled with shattered glass. I have been cleaning the pieces of galss for the last two days. There are tiny pieces in every cornier and opening of the ovens. everytime I open the door more pieces fall out, in the lower oven or inside the oven. We were so lucky no one was standing infront of the oven when this happened.
When I called them, they said yes, that happens sometimes.!!!!!! I think they should not make an oven with self clenaing feature and sell it for so much more money, when this could happen and injure people. They won't take any responsibility.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (exploding glass) but no injury, and the manufacturer acknowledged it happens sometimes, indicating a possible likelihood.

incident_description: problem with light inside refrigerator which apparently stays on when the door is closed. the light bulb by design touchs the inside liner of the refrigerator and by staying in the on position melted into the liner causing burn damage to the liner and insulation of the unit.
justification: The incident caused damage to the refrigerator liner and insulation but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Oven  Model#665.95014100

Set oven for pre-heat 350 deg. Oven heated up higher than 350. It would not shut off using the STOP/OFF button.  Had to shut the circuit breaker off at the panel. The outside of this unit got so hot, it could not be handled to unplug the unit. I have been a Fire Fighter for 20 years and find this malfunction very,very dangerous!!!!!!
justification: The oven malfunctioned and overheated, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Burner was on low. Upon turning burning OFF the burner began heating to extremely hot. After attempting to turn burner off several times, unplugging and replugging the power cord, with no success, I had to unplug the range to turn it off.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but no injury or damage was reported, only an incident requiring intervention.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range

09/26/2011 caller was baking at 400 degrees for 45 minutes per instructions on pre-prepared food item purchased at Cosco.

Caller went away from the range, was on computer but when he came back to the range to check on food he saw odd symbols on the display area.

Caller said the 45 minutes was over so he tried to turn range off, however it didn't go off so he tried a few more times with the same result.

He opened the oven which was so very, very hot.

He went to the circuit breaker, turned it off.  Food was not burned but thermometer measured temperature at 125 degrees when it was supposed to be 140 degrees.

The next morning (09/27/2011) he turned breaker back on, turned oven on, let it heat up to 350 degrees, tried to turn it off but again it wouldn't go off again so he turned breaker off, allowed range to cool off then turned breaker on again to test range again to attempt to turn it off, however when he returned to the range it had turned itself on and was already heating up.

Caller believes this to be an extreme loss of control, dangerous situation and therefore wanted 
Caller has contacted repair & has an appointment for repair 10/08/2011
justification: The incident caused a loss of control, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Purchased a Nonstick Linked 4 loaf pan.  When I was washing it prior to its first use, I suffered a laceration on one of my fingers due to the edges of the pan not being properly finished during the manufacturing process.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I HAVE A FRIGIDAIRE STOVE MODEL NUMBER FES367DSA.  THE OVEN DOOR HAS GLASS ATTACHED AND WHEN YOU OPEN THE OVEN THE HANDLE MOVES ALLOWING THE GLASS TO COME UNATTACHED WHICH CAUSE IT TO HIT THE PERSON STANDING IN FRONT AND COULD EASILY FALL ON FOOT CAUSING A MAJOR CUT. THIS HAS BEEN HAPPENING FOR A COUPLE OF YEARS TO WHERE I WAS PUTTING TAPE AROUND IT AND I SHOULDNT HAVE TO PUT DUCT TAPE ON THE FRONT OF MY STOVE, I KNOW I CANT BE THE ONLY ONE WITH THIS PROBLEM.
justification: The description indicates the oven door glass could cause a major cut, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The issue has been recurring for years, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she had just finished cleaning the Range, the rear left burner came on spontaneously by itself, she was unable to power it off from the control panel, it had to be switched off from the Circuit breaker.  There was also a lot of smoke emitting from the front glass panel.

Consumer stated that this incident occurred 1 year ago and she had contacted the retailer and a service rep was sent out.

9/27/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that her model was part of the recall Release #11-016  and she would be provided with a repair kit.
Consumer feels that this problem with the Range cannot be repaired with a repair kit.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that emitted smoke but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: Our 6 year old daughter's arm came into contact with the outside of the waffle maker (Waring #WMK600) briefly, which resulted in a first/second degree burn.  The outside appears to be heated to an unsafe level during operation.
justification: The incident resulted in a first/second degree burn, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while using the toaster it burnt the toast and flames were emitting from it, he immediately blew out the flames from the toast. There was no damages.

Consumer feels that if he had not been at home it would have caused a house fire.

Consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer feels that this toaster is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved flames from the toaster but no damages or injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the consumer intervened to prevent further damage.

incident_description:
On October 16 2011 about 6:30 pm cst I was cooking marinated portobella mushrooms in my oven that was placed in a Pyrex dish. They had been marinated, then placed in the oven second row down and broiled on the lowest setting. I added cheese to the portobellas and then after approximately 3 minutes I took them out and placed them on some hot pads. The PYREX dish, that I had cooked them in, exploded in to several hundred small shards.  The explosion was so violent that it spread out to about 100 feet, caused me to have about 7 nicks on my leg area, burns on my legs, and several tiles on my floor have melted spots on them from the incident. As of now I have not received any medical attention to my injuries.
    I do not have any information about when I purchased the dish because it was a gift. I do know it was a Pyrex because it said Pyrex on it and the plastic cover,that came with it,has Pyrexware usa 233-PC MADE IN THE USA imprinted on it. The lid is also navy blue in color and is about 16x10 inches. The dish itself was a clear glass and said Pyrex on it as well. 
    I also would like to take note of the fact that I have several other Pyrex dishes that I have used to cook in the same manner and this has not occurred.

Approximately 10 minutes into the cooking process the baking dish literally exploded in the oven into small to medium sized pieces many of which had very sharp edges that could easily have injured someone.

incident_description:

incident_description:
We own a Maytag dishwasher Model # MDBH975AWS  Serial # 10500941JA. We noticed a lot of water coming out from underneath our dishwasher.  Upon further investigation,  we found that the water was coming out from the connection port area for the heating element. When we removed the heating element we found that the element itself had exploded. 

Having noticed for the past few days that the indicator lights for the sanitary option was no longer lighting up upon completion of a cycle we can only assume that the heating element explosion tripped a circuit but not one that would make the dishwasher inoperable. 

We are surprised that the dishwasher would keep on running after such an incident and highly believe that we could have had a fire.

Upon going to the Maytag site and checking for recalls we found a recall on Maytag dishwashers, plus others, for a faulty heating element that caused fires and damage. However, our model was not included in that recall.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction with potential fire risk but no actual injury or death occurred.
