incident_description:
Frame of stove and burner knobs get extreamly hot when using oven .Burner knobs eventually melt.
Burned thumb on control knob. Is an extream burn hazard for children. Have seen many complaints from others on-line with same problem.
justification: The incident describes a burn injury from hot stove knobs and mentions a burn hazard for children, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high due to multiple online complaints about the same issue.

incident_description: I was trying to preheat my oven/microwave combo to 350 degrees. It heated up and beeped letting me know it was ready stated placing potatoes in oven when the broiler and self cleaning heat lamps came on. F2 came up and said door locked, was also beeping, but door was not locked .My husband tried to shut down the oven it would not go off( by pressing the clear/off button). It got so hot that it craked the inside glass and the handle to open was so hot you had to use a mitt to open. My husband had to turn the oven off at the breaker box. Four hours latter he turned the breaker back on and the oven came back on with the F2 message and beeping noise. My husband turned the breaker back off. The next day around 5pm we turned the breaker back on and the oven broiler is still comming on. Our combo is a GE appliance with the modle number JKP86W0F1WW
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that became dangerously hot, cracked glass, and required intervention to prevent potential injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: We put water in the reservoir, started the brew, switched to steam the milk, but then when we switched back to brew, the filter holder and filter exploded off the coffee maker.  It shattered the carafe and sprayed hot water and grounds across our kitchen.  The filter holder was on tight so we do not know how it could have exploded off the coffee maker.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of hot water and grounds causing damage, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I came home from being out for a few hours and opened my refrigerator to see that the whole electrical unit which is called the Cool Sense Electronic Temperature Control System had fallen off the interior top wall of the refrigerator.  The bulbs remained on after it fell and were even burning the ceramic bulb holders to a dark brown.  All the food in the top of the shelves had become warm - eggs, etc. The plastic cover for the bulbs had melted and warped.  Apparently, the piece dropped off and the bulbs remained on and didn't automatically shut off as it should.  This exteme heat was very disconcerting as it could have caused a fire.  We had to disconnect the whole temperature unit to make sure the lights didn't stay on and start a fire while we slept that night.

We had not had any reason to believe this was a problem before this.  There were no indications that anything was wrong, and nothing had been done to harm the electrical unit prior to this incident.  

Concerned that this major issue could be more than the "regular" repair type issues, I looked on line to see if there were any recalls for this make and model.  I did find that there are other incidents reported of this exact nature in the same make and model, but did not find any recalls. This alarms me because having an electrical problem of this type that is happening to others makes me question the safety of this product overall since it is not a one time incident.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electrical unit that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer reported that she was cooking sauce on the front-left burner while using the "simmer select" option for approximately one hour when she hurd a "pop" sound and saw a blue flash come from the range.  She did know where on the range the blue flash came from since she was not looking directly at it. The consumer immediately shut off the unit.

A short time later she turned on the right front burner to see if it was still working and she heard another "pop" and the digital screen on the back of the unit went black.  The consumer also reported the smell of something electrical burning.  The complainant stated the circuit breaker to the unit tripped after the other burner was attempted to be turned on.  There were no injuries and no smoke alarm sounded.

The consumer previously had an incident which was investigated under [REDACTED] for the same range which involved the same front left burner heating up after it was shut off and causing the cooking surface to break.  The front left burner and a circuit board in the back of the unit were replaced by the manufacturer after the first incident.  The manufacturer told her those repairs were only guaranteed for 90 days and the unit was no longer under warrenty when the 2nd incident occurred.  She has already gotten rid of the unit and purchased a new one since she did not believe the incident unit to be safe, even if it was repaired.
justification: The incident involved electrical malfunctions and a burning smell but resulted in no injuries or smoke alarm activation.

incident_description:
The person is an investigator reporting an incident on behalf of a consumer. The consumer set her dishwasher and went to another room in her house. The consumer heard a pop sound 30 minutes later and returned to her kitchen to find that her dishwasher caught fire. The investigator is unsure what cycle the dishwasher was set to. The consumer called the fire department to extinguish the fire. The response time was 8 minutes and 42 seconds. The fire department extinguished the fire with an extinguisher. 

The dishwasher was purchased approximately in 1991. The product is portable so it didn't spread fire through her home. The dishwasher is burned and it is a total loss. The contents of the dishwasher are also totally lost and the product suffered extensive damage at the control panel. The investigator feels that the product is involved in recall 96-133. The consumer has yet to call the firm and the retailer. The consumer was not injured by the product.  The flooring was burnt and the house sustained extensive smoke damage.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) given the product's age and potential recall involvement.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his spouse had noticed heat on the countertop but had dismissed it, he discovered the following morning that the toaster came on by itself because no one had use it but the elements were red hot.  He unplugged it and then attempted to plug it in again it immediately came on without pushing the button on.  Consumer unplugged it to prevent further damages.

9/24/11 Consumer contacted the retailer and was advised that the toaster had not been recalled so he should report it to the Agency.

Consumer feels that this toaster is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The toaster malfunctioned by turning on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: the consumer says the stove made a "pop" sound.  There was a flame shooting out of the top part of the stove.  She pulled away the stove from the wall and unplugged it.  The flames went out after it was unplugged.  She contacted the retailer who told her to contact CPSC.  She says that if she was not home, it could have burned down their home.  If it had happened at night there could have been loss of life.
justification: The incident involved flames and potential danger, but no actual injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the description.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his dishwasher smokes posing a fire hazard. The consumer stated that his dishwasher was running on a normal cycle of about 30-45 minutes. The consumer stated that the front panel melted near the switch, the consumer is not sure if  plastic melted and the wires blackened. The consumer found that there was more damage outside of the machine. The model has a delay start and has concerns if something were to happen while she was asleep at night and the product was running. 

The consumer stated that the smoking timed out when the consumer's husband went downstairs to turn off the circuit breaker.  The consumer stated that his product has a digital interface. The consumer conducted that his product is similar to other models that were recalled but his model number is not listed in the recall. The consumer stated that she called the manufacturer today. She was informed that an appointment will be scheduled for repair at her expense. 

The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The consumer mentioned that the product has not caused any damage to his home. The consumer has not been injured by the product. The consumer stated that the product emitted a chemical burning. The consumer opted to not call the fire department after the incident happened.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and had melting parts, but no injury or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
The bake element of the GE electric range ( Model J BP78D0H2BB, Serial# Z F2 834430)  burst into flame and both ends of the element continued to burn until the stove was shoot off.  A seven inch portion of the element fell off . There were no food spills on the coil or on the inside of the oven.
Because the oven was shut down in time no damage occurred.
justification: The incident involved flames and a portion of the element falling off, but no damage or injuries occurred as the oven was shut down in time.

incident_description:
New GE Microwave Model PVM2070DM4WW   SN HV 302789B
about 2 week old.  Last night microwave started running all by its self.  I had to unplug from wall to clear it.  I cleaned selection screen with wet paper towel and dried.  This morning the unit did the same thing again.  I called GE customer care and they told me to open and close the door 3 times.  If unit still continues to start on it own, call repair.  What happens if it starts doing it when we are on vacation for 2 weeks next month?  Google has several GE's that are causing fires, 7 in Florida per what I read.  This microwave should be on a recall list or at least tell people about the problem before they buy one.
justification: The microwave malfunctioning poses a potential fire hazard, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual harm has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she had not used the oven for about three days.  She says she used one burner on medium.  She heard an explosion a few minutes later.  She says the front glass shattered and flew into two other rooms.  She says the burner on for about 10 minutes before the incident.  She says the burner had already been turned off before the explosion.  She never had any issues with the unit prior to the incident. 

Consumer added:  We had no idea that the oven door was painted glass.  It has been replaced with a painted glass panel with us paying 50% of costs.  A am aware every day that this could happen again and in a home with small children, it could be a bad situation.  Our little dog was covered with glass.  I think the Consumer should be made aware of what could possibly happen (warning).  I understand most self-cleaning ovens have glass doors, (panel) they should be metal.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and shattered glass, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is unlikely as the consumer had no prior issues with the unit.

incident_description:
HAMILTON BEACH TABLE TOPP OVEN, TYPE 027, MODEL NO. 31197R, SERIES A2890BW. WHEN IN USE, THE HARD WIRED ELECTRIC CORD GETS SO HOT YOU CANNOT TOUCH IT. YOU HAVE TO WAIT UNTIL THE OVEN IS TURNED OFF AND COOLS DOWN. I CALLED HAMILTON BEACH CUSTOMER SERVICE (1-800-851-8900) AND WAS TOLD THERE IS NO RECALL ON THIS UNIT BECAUSE OF A FAULTY CORD, BUT THE CUSTOMER SERVICE REP WAS KIND ENOUGH TO OFFER TO SEND ME A MAILING LABEL TO RETURN THE OVEN AND THAT THEY WOULD EVALUATE IT AND SEND ME A NEW UNIT. I EXPLAINED THAT IT WASN'T THE OVEN THAT WAS FAULTY, ONLY THE ELECTRIC CORD. AND THAT MOST LIKELY THE CORD HAD ONLY THE MINIMUM SIZE WIRE AND THAT'S WHY IT GETS SO HOT. IT CANNOT HANDLE THE 1500 WATTS. THE CUSTOMER SERVICE REP SAID THEY JUST DON'T CHANGE THE CORD. I INDICATED THAT IF THEY JUST SEND ME ANOTHER TABLE TOP OVEN, IT WOULD HAVE THE SAME TYPE ELECTRIC CORD, CORRECT? THE REP SAID, "YES".

AGAIN, THE PRODUCT IS GOOD, BUT THE ELECTRIC CORD IS BAD. SO BAD THAT IF LEFT PLUGGED INTO THE ELECTRIC OUTLET, IT COULD VERY WELL CAUSE A FIRE. HAMILTON BEACH'S ANSWER TO SIMPLY EXCHANGE THE OVEN, WHICH HAS THE SAME TYPE ELECTRIC CORD, IS NOT PRODUCT SAFETY OR THE ANSWER TO THIS DANGEROUS PROBLEM.
justification: The electric cord gets dangerously hot, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Caller reporting that the light within his Kenmore Refrigerator is staying lit causing the inside near it to become warm.

When he noticed this he searched online for any similarities, reporting of same incident and found many.

He took the lamps out of his refrigerator once he found the articles/reports of similar findings but also some where the overheating caused a potential for fire, smoke and food spoilage etc.

He wanted to report so that his incident would be counted as those among the disheartened.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but it could have caused food spoilage and a potential for fire.

incident_description: While preheating the Kenmore Built In Electric Oven the front glass door exploded shoot glass fragments accross the kitchen.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass fragments to scatter, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Oven would not shut off. Set at 350F to bake and when the smell of burning food was noticed the oven door was opened and the broiler burners were on not baking elements. We could not shut off the oven except by disconnecting the breaker. It will remain off as this is a serious fire hazard!! Someone without the knowledge to trip the breaker could have burned down there residence. There is no failsafe enginering in this product even though it is an older model.
Kenmore Model Ultra Bake 665 9580 9000
Serial Number RK1311349
justification: The oven malfunctioned and could not be shut off normally, posing a serious fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I own the Delonghi D895UX Deep Fryer as seen here:
http://www.amazon.com/DeLonghi-D895UX-Cool-Touch-Electric-2-Pound-Capacity/dp/B00004RGAW

This unit has a rubber drain hose that during normal operation is bent 90degrees upwards with a stopper in the end to keep oil from draining.  I have owned the unit approximately 5 years with minimal usage.  By design the rubber tube is bent, and at that bend the rubber tube has now cracked right at the bend.  I luckily noticed this when draining unit. But I am not sure when the crack started.  The problem that could easily occur is that while using the unit at temperatures up to 370 degrees F. the oil could start leaking out the bottom front onto ones counter top, floor... and on a person who tries to stop the flood of burning oil.  I can't imagine someones response to try and mitigate the leak would cause.
I contacted the company, they said that part was not allowed for consumer repair, and I would have to send the unit to them for repair at 100% my cost.  I told them that I believed this was a design flaw and a serious hazard, they did not offer to fix at their expense, stating that the warranty was over.
I believe this should be considered for a recall due to high potential for burn/fire hazard.  If you search about this fryer and leaking, it does bring up other reviews about this problem.
justification: The incident could lead to serious burns and fire hazards, but no injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description:
We purchased a Kitchenaid Dishwasher Model KUDP01ILBS2 Serial No. 029754274 from Lowes July 21, 2007.  On March 27, 2006 this dishwasher started to smell like an electrical fire, or burned wiring.  Mr. Appliance is an authorized repair service for Kitchenaid.  They found that the main control board melted and burned up.  They had to replace the control panel, board, wiring harness.  Just recently we had the same problem only this time there were flames and smoke coming from the area where the control panel is located.

This product is not safe and will cause a fire in your home.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke, indicating a significant fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We have a Cooks brand slow cooker model SC-702 purchased at [REDACTED] in Clearwater, Florida about a year ago.  The glass lid has a plastic handle attached to the top middle of the lid.  The plastic handle totally shattered into several pieces in my wife's hand while removing the lid from the hot pot. The lid fell to the kitchen floor and thankfully landed on a fatigue mat and did not break.  I searched the internet for a replacement handle and discovered that there are many accounts of this handle breaking in addition to the side handles breaking.  
We used this product according to manual directions and probably cooked a meal less than a dozen times.
justification: The plastic handle shattered but no injury occurred, and the incident aligns with multiple similar reports.

incident_description: Since Farberware changed their electric coffeepots to a 3 prong plug, it continuously pops my GFI breaker. I have exchanged the pots in the store 3 times and the manufacturer has sent me a new pot. I have had my GFI switch changed and it still happens. I bought a different brand of electric coffeepot, also with a 3 prong plug and it works fine. This has been going on over a year. I have given up on Farberware but I feel this is a serious defect and should be reported. My electrician says it is a problem with the coffeepot. I purchased the pots origionally at Bed Bath and Beyond and the manager there said they are getting alot of returns.
justification: The incident involves a recurring electrical issue with the coffeepot causing GFI breaker trips, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: My mother informed me that her stove burner would go on without turning on the burner knob. To determine if this was true she placed a tea kettle with water on the burner. When the burner  turn itself on eventually the kettle would go off. This burner would turn itself on without notice. i checked the recall list for Frigidaire and found the stove's model number on the recall list. i called the hotline and they sent us a repair kit and an authorization number for a service company to install the repair kit. However the tech said the burner and board needed to be replaced. This is the burner that kept turning itself on. It now has turned itself off permanently. Frigidaire gallery series Model# GLEFM97GPWA, serial number VF74258555. The parts that need to be replaced element:316419902, board 316442101. The authorization number given for the repair kit SF22-816B. The repair kit has only shut down the rear element from running altogeather. The other burners work fine, but did before. My Mom is 85 loves to cook. it's not fair to pick on an 85 year old. what gives with these people, need new engineer? Many qualified on the unemployement line. Please ding this company for another incident. If this is the only thing they understand then so be it! I also will follow up with the local store which sold the unit RALIN in Syracuse,N.Y I also will complain to the BBB the ATT.GEN of N.Y and our local broadcasting station Consumer Affairs. the purpose is to discourage people from purchasing this manufactures product even  though it is Electolux that does.They said I was frustrated, I wasn't just wanted those parts, we didn't break the stove they did!
justification: The stove burner turning on without notice is a safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The heating element of my GE dishwasher overheated during the night causing the plastic racks to melt and extreme heat to the surrounding counters/cabinets.  Luckily, I was woken up by my pet before a fire could start with this appliance.
justification: The overheating caused damage to the dishwasher and surrounding area but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore Smoothtop Range started spontaneously turning on the back left burner, but the switch shows off. Cannot "turn off" burner once this happens without flipping breaker to the range, or unplugging the range. This has happened 4 times in the past 4 weeks. incident_description: I bought a emerson Microwave Model 9115SL about a year ago and recently when using it it started sparking inside.  The unit has a grill element inside for browning and it apears the one of the srews must have had a coating on it that must have worn off. So I opened the dishwasher to add the fork. Only when I'd opened the dishwasher door smoking was coming out and I smelt something burning. incident_description: In May of 2011 my range went into clean mode while cooking causing the food to burn. I used it again and it did the same thing. I called Whirlpool and they said they would send out a repairman and pay for diagnostics, labor and I had to pay for parts. When the repair man couldn't figure out what was wrong whirlpool said they would not pay for labor. The repairman noted that the lock mode motor was burnt and had melted down to the next componit. He also stated that the range was useable. I contacted Whirlpool and they said it had out lived its use ability and they would give me $100 for it. I tried to use it as they said I could this time just the burners and it went into clean mode and would not shut off. I had to shut off the breaker. Two days later I turned on the breaker and it went into clean mode as soon as it got power. I have since unplugged it and have been without a stove since June. Whirlpool refuses to see the fire hazard and their responsability considering the service report says it is useable. I paid over $1000 for this unit and do not this it is fair that a company can get away with this kind of safety issue. How many more flat top stoves are having this problem? I know of a few because I have seen them on craigs list for sale stating that they might need a need heating eliment because they smelt something like wire burning. They should be recallled and Whirlpool be made to replace or reimburse for this faulty product. The range never tripped my breaker and it should have when it caught fire.

incident_description: Jenn-Air refrigerator model JSD2789DES had a relay switch burn causing a small fire. Switch controls compressor motor.

incident_description: After baking some chicken in the Pyrex dish I took it out of the oven when it just exploded.  Glass flew everywhere and even caused several burns on our solid wood floors!  Luckily no one was hurt, but dinner was ruined.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, causing glass to fly and damage floors, but no one was injured.

incident_description: While baking brownies at 350 degrees in my Pyrex dish in the oven, it suddenly exploded in the oven.  Luckily the only damage was to the dish  and brownies, there was no damage to the oven except for getting all the tiny shards of glass from the bottom of the oven.
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, but there was no injury or damage to the oven beyond glass shards.

incident_description: My daughters heard popping and crackling in the kitchen that was immediately followed by smoke. My mother in law and 2 daughters immediately went outside and called 911. The fire department concluded that there had been an elctrical fire in the bottom rear of our Kenmore Coldspot refrigerator (model # 106.52574202).
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire, which is a serious hazard, but no injuries were reported as everyone evacuated safely.

incident_description: We purchased our Kenmore Elite refrigerator in June 2007.  Within a month we started having issues with the model.  First the waterline was found to be leaking, it ruined the floor and cabinets behind the unit. Then about two months later we noticed that it was warm, and cold in the refrigerator. Upon closer inspection we realized the lights had melted the plastic housing and created massive warping and melting of the inside. The Sears store sent a repair service person, and they replaced the unit.  Now, 10/10/2011, the unit is doing the same now.  The light stays on, but only shuts off when it gets overheated.  We still have hot food.  We had to remove the bulbs today.  I really hope that Sears wises up and fixes this problem for good.  There needs to be a recall on this very dangerous appliance.
justification: The incident caused property damage (ruined floor and cabinets, melted plastic housing) but no reported injuries or deaths, and the recurrence suggests it is likely to happen again.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Oven overheated as Broiler turned on when using the ove and would not turn off unless turned off the breaker and almost started fire.
justification: The oven overheated and almost started a fire, but no injury or death occurred, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is possible given the description of the malfunction.

incident_description: Dishwasher was running.  White, acrid smoke started pouring out of the upper right corner.  Wife opened door trying to stop cycle.  Cycle did not stop, spraying water around kitchen.  Note additional smoke poured out of dishwasher.  It was not steam.  Note entire house smells from electrical burning.  She closed door to dishwasher and called me. I came in, and immediately shut down power to house at main breaker. I then disconnected wires to unit in base of unit. I then shut down breaker to unit.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical burning smell, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was quickly controlled by shutting down the power.

incident_description:
Kenmore Range model# 790,96113409:
Explosion inside of oven and top element caught fire. Nothing in oven at the time; oven turned on to broil.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and fire in the oven, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Left front electric range top burner will not shut off. Burner stays on high no matter what the control knob is set at. Initially I could fidget with the knob to get it to turn off. The last time it stayed on high for about 10 minutes with the knob in the off position. At that point, a good wack on the knob finally shut it off. After reading many similar complaints for this condition, (in addition to stoves turning on by themselves), I unplugged it all together. I am frustrated to hear that my stove does not fall under the recall, although it has the same problem as those listed.
justification: The burner staying on high despite attempts to turn it off poses a risk of fire or burns, but no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description: The dishwasher was started before going to bed, as usual. Approximately 5-10 minutes into the cycle, a strange noise was heard and 8-12" flames were coming out the top and right side of the dishwasher. The control panel was inoperative to shut the dishwasher down, but when the door was opened the flames died out. The Fire Department cut power upon arrival. no injuries, but the dishwasher was destroyed.
justification: Flames and inoperative control panel indicate a significant incident, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
Maytag Range - purchased in mid-2008 - has upper and lower ovens. Both ovens have turned on by itself at random time, thus creating a life-safety / fire hazzard. Called Maytag. They said they would send Flamingo Appliance out for an inspection and diagnosis, but I would have to pay for any part(s); further, they said it sounded like a control board issue. I asked what the approx. cost was and was told it would be about $212. I also asked about a warranty on that part and was told it was covered by a 1 yr warranty.

Flamingo Appliance showed up; told me the control board DID have to be replace. Said the cost was $262 + tax and that there was a THREE-MONTH warranty. Why would I pay almost 1/3 the TOTAL COST of the range with only a three-month warranty?  This should never have happened on a 3-yr-old expensive appliance...

Again, this is a life-safety issue and there have been numerous documented issues or prior instances of this same exact thing occurring. These other episodes can be located on the internet.  WHY HASN'T MAYTAG BEEN FORCED INTO A RECALL FOR THE LIFE-THREATENING SITUATION THEY HAVE CREATED?

It is unconscionable that they are aware of the fire hazzard their appliances are creating yet feel they are under no obligation to correct.
justification: The ovens turning on by themselves poses a fire hazard, which is a life-safety issue, but no injury or death has been reported in this specific incident.

incident_description: Appears to be A fire from a control board in the dishwasher. An Internet search revealed www.kitchenaidfire.com with similar issues.
justification: A fire incident occurred with no reported injury, and similar issues are documented online, indicating likelihood.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while using the dishwasher for approximately 30 mins there was an odor of burnt plastic and discovered that there was black smoke emitting from the unit.  The door was opened and she noticed that the plastic casing around the control panel had melted.  The was no other physical damage to the outer or inner parts of the dishwasher or the cabinets.  The unit was switched off from the control panel.

Consumer had not contcted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer feels that this unit is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved burnt plastic odor and smoke, but no injury or physical damage beyond the melted control panel casing.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she had used the toaster oven at 9:00 am earlier the morning on 8/15/2011 and she was down she had unplugged it from the wall outlet and powered it in the off position. 

At or around 1:00 pm she heard a loud crash noise and when she went into the kitchen she noticed that the glass from the oven door had shattered  and the glass was all over the counter top, floor and some inside of the oven.

She touched the oven to see if it was hot and it was not she also double check to make sure that the oven was powered in the off position and  unplugged from the wall outlet and it was.  

She found the handle to the oven door 12 inch away from the toaster oven on the counter top. She noticed that the pieces of glass varied in different sizes.

She contacted the firm but they only handled large appliances and since then she has not made any further attempts to contact the firm . She has packaged the toaster oven back into the same packaging it came in and plans to return it to the retailer on 8/24/2011.
justification: The incident involved the toaster oven's glass door shattering, but no injury was reported, and the oven was not in use at the time.

incident_description:
The consumer recalls using the back left burner earlier (approximately 5 pm) in the day time to prepare a meal  and approximately 8 pm  while cleaning the range she noticed that the burn was on but was not powered in  position by using the control knobs and that the knob was powered in the off position. 

The service light on the control panel indicated that the element was In the on position. The consumer turned the knob from the on position to the off position simultaneously  and the burner powered off. 

On 8/31/2011 while using the front left burner on setting number four for 15 minutes the back left burner powered in the on position without being switched on.  After trying to us the knob to switch back and forth from on and off to power the burner in the off position did not work the range was pulled from the wall and unplugged.

After allowing the range to cool off the range was plugged back into the wall and the back left burner powered in the on position again without being switched on. 

The firm was contacted on 9/1/2011 and the consumer indicated that  they were not willing to  offer any assistance in repairing it. So the consumer  is considering either hiring a third party company to take a look at the range and or replacing  the appliance. 

The consumer did some research online and noticed there was a recall for similar models (see release #09-333) that experienced the same hazard but she was already informed by the firm that her model number was not affected. 

The range is currently unplugged from the wall outlet and has not been used.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner that turned on unexpectedly, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says his wife was cooking and when she turned the top right burner off, it stayed on.  The consumer says he inspected it and he noticed the burner comes on by itself while the burner is in the off position.  the consumer says the only way to turn off the burner is by shutting off circuit breaker.  The consumer says he contacted manufacturer and they said the model is not under recall and offered to inspect the unit for a fee.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a 16 inch Presto electric skillet with a glass top 5 months ago. Yesterday, the glass skillet top shatterred in my dishwasher, leaving a million shards all over the dishwasher, and the floor. This was not the first time it had been put in the dishwasher. Fortunately my spouse did not get injured. He waited until I came home, and we had to use a shop vac to clean out the dishwasher.he was emptying the dishwasher of clean dishes.
justification: The glass top shattered, causing a mess but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as it happened once in 5 months of use.

incident_description: I was cooking on my Frigidaire Smoothtop stove on the large burner, I turned it off and the small inner burner remained hot and on. I tried to turn on and off, unplug it and it still remained on after I plugged it back in. If I had left my house and not doublechecked my stove my house could have burned down, I was going to work and would have been gone all day.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that remained on, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her smooth top range is a potential hazard The consumer stated that she owned one electric smooth top range with an oven. The range has a digital interface. The consumer was using the right front burner at high while she was boiling corn. The burner was in use for roughly 30 minutes when the consumer turned off the range. As the consumer walked to the sink and had her back turned, the consumer heard an explosion. The consumer was not injured during the incident. The consumer did not call the fire department at the time of the incident. 

At the time the range exploded, the oven was off. The damage was so extensive that the stove top could no longer be used. There was no damage to anything surrounding the range. The consumer purchased this range on April of 2007. The consumer opted not to call the fire department. The consumer never called the firm after the incident took place. The consumer called the retailer immediately after the incident took place and the company offered to exchange the range at no expense. 

The consumer had the company deliver her a new with the exact same model and serial number and July 10, 2011. The range is cited in release 11-016.The consumer stated that beginning in 2008 and 2009 (dates unknown) the consumer was experiencing on many occasions (about 3-4 times) that the back left burner once, rear right burner the other times. On all occurrences the consumer found the range on and found the rotary knob of the range in the on position. The consumer received a recall notice in the mail from Frigidaire the week of 12/14/2010.

 The consumer spoke with a representative that same week and told her they would FedEx her the parts that were needed and fix the range at their expense. The consumer was told that originally the serviceman would be there on 12/20/2010 but the consumer chose to reschedule. The consumer was informed to unplug the range or unplug the circuit breaker. At this point, the is still off. The consumer had the product fixed (date unknown) in January 2011. On September 2, 2011 the consumer came home found that the range was on and the knob was set to the on position.

 The consumer that were sitting on the front burner were burned. The fan over the stove came on automatically because of the heat. The consumer called the firm (date unknown) a few days afterward at the number for the firm's recall hotline. The consumer was offered by the firm that they will offer 70% cost of the range or repair the range at no expense. The consumer was unsure whether what she wanted to do and advised the firm that she will call them back. The consumer received a package on September 5th, 2011 with a seal kit to repair the range. 

The consumer is not happy with the firm's solution and no longer wants the product. This particular range on the right front burner has a chip on it from the excessive heat. The range did not damage her home or the surrounding appliances. The consumer never called the called the fire department about this range. The consumer was not harmed by this product. The consumer did not call the retailer about this range.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and repeated malfunctions, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says she walked in home and house was filled with smoke and was coming out from behind of range.  The consumer says it was on for roughly 10 minutes.  The consumer said she was able to turn it off by hitting the "clear" button.  She said that the same thing happened again a week later.  She says her walls our filled with black smoke.  She has been coughing for 3 days since the incident.  The consumer says she turned on the oven and stepped outside, she said that it was set to automatically shut off in two hours.  She says that if she hadn't forgotten something making her come back to the house, her house would have burned up.

Consumer believes the short resulted frrm her using the broiler a day earlier as she'd never used it before.  And the next time she turned the oven on, the electrical fire started.  This needs immediate attention- poeple's homes are in danger. If you look at the recall list and pictures of her range and model numbers are similar as ones that have been recalled.  She purchased this range 1 month after 1st recall. It looks exactly like the picture of the recalled range.  

You need to see consumeraffairs.com to see the horror stories with this company and their response to fire by their product.

incident_description:
Less than a year ago we purchased a Cuisinart coffeemaker model DCC-1100 in black.  This week it almost burned our house down!
 
Something malfunctioned in the heater plate.  It started making a clicking sound and the coffee in the pot was rapidly boiling.  You could smell burning electrical wires.  We immediately unplugged the unit before it caught fire.  It was just fortunate we were in the kitchen at the time and not in the shower as we frequently use the timer feature to wake up to a fresh brewed pot of coffee every morning.
justification: The coffeemaker malfunctioned, causing a near-fire incident with no injury or death.

incident_description: Fire department suppression personnel responded to a report of an oven fire.  Upon arrival they found the electric heating element inside the oven burning "like a fuse"  personnel isolated the electric source and the element stopped burning and cooled.

incident_description: Pyrex baking dish shattered while in oven.  Oven was set at 400 degrees.  No one was hurt.  The bakeware was put in the preheated oven.  It was in the oven approx. 20 minutes before the shattering occurred.
justification: The Pyrex dish shattered but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I was baking brownies at 300 degrees F in a glass Pyrex 9x13 pan.  The pan was new, purchased in the last few months.  We heard a "pop" noise and my son opened the oven enough to look inside.  The Pyrex pan had exploded into a thousand pieces which were scattered all over the oven.  I contacted Pyrex to find out about the pan.  The representative read off a list of "don'ts" and told me to collect all the pieces and save them until I received a replacement pan.  Since many of the pieces were stuck to the brownies, I used a plastic trash bag to contain the pieces.  Where the shards came in contact with the plastic bag, they sliced through the plastic.  I ended up putting the whole mess into a cardboard box.  I took great care in collecting the pieces but still ended up with a splinter in my foot.  There were so many pieces in the oven, I used my shopvac to collect them.

Although we had used the pan approximately two times before, we had not done any of the "don'ts" listed by the representative.  I have another Pyrex pan which is the same size but probably 20 or more years old.  I have never had any problems with this pan.  Even if Pyrex sends me a replacement pan, I will be hesitant to use it.  I have already purchased a metal pan as a replacement.

Interestingly, when I went online to google Pyrex, "Pyrex pan exploding" came up as a search option.  When I followed that search, I found many reports of exploding pans, so with associated injuries, including one poor woman who was blinded.  Talking to the Pyrex representative, I got the impression that she was trying to blame me for the pan explosion.  I assure you, this was not my fault.  I could do the exact same thing with my old Pyrex pan and not have a problem.  This is a product problem.
justification: The incident resulted in a splinter injury and potential for more severe injuries, as indicated by online reports. The occurrence likelihood is possible, given the reports of similar incidents.

incident_description:
On 9/1/11, I bought an 8" by 10" Pyrex Storage Plus baking dish (7212-PC) from Wal-Mart.  The label on the dish stated that it was "Freezer Safe," "Oven and Microwave Safe," and "Dishwasher Safe."  Before use, I washed the dish in the top of my dishwasher and stored it in my cabinet.
     I had this dish for 8 days and I never used it in the freezer, oven, or microwave.  I used it once, in my refrigerator, to store lettuce.  Afterwards, I loaded it into the top of the dishwasher in the evening, and turned the dishwasher on the next morning, so the dish was room temperature when washed.  After the washing cycle ended,  I opened the door of the dishwasher to allow my dishes to air-dry.  (I use "No heat rinse" and "No heat dry" to save energy.)  Almost three hours later, I heard an incredible explosion in my kitchen.  The cooled pyrex dish had violently shattered inside the opened-door dishwasher, sending razor-like shards of glass everywhere.  The dish did not crack and break --  it exploded!   Glass fragments were found as much as 9 foot 10 inches from the dishwasher.   Thankfully, no one was in the kitchen at the time. 

     I tried my best to provide the details you would need, but please do not hesitate to contact me if you need any more information.  Also, I have kept the glass shards if examining them would be helpful. This was a terrifying event.  Please, please, please investigate this product before someone is very seriously hurt!
justification: The Pyrex dish exploded, causing significant property damage but no injuries as no one was present in the kitchen at the time.

incident_description: Our 8-month-old Emerson microwave (model MW8999RD) started making a very loud hum and then began emitting smoke and an acrid, burning plastic smell. We tried contacting the company via the numerous toll-free numbers, but it only said all lines were busy and would disconnect us. When it became apparent that we would need a new microwave, we checked online and dozens of others have had this unit catch fire, sometimes while not in use. I guess we were lucky ours only required the house to be aired out, but this is a dangerous appliance.
justification: The microwave emitted smoke and a burning smell, indicating a hazardous incident, but no injury occurred. Reports of similar incidents suggest this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Returning home, I opened my refrigerator and noticed that the top shelf of food products were warm to the touch and the shelf was very hot.  I double checked that when both door light switches were depressed that the light remained on.  I confirmed my suspicions that the switches were bad by firmly closing both doors (side-by-side style) and returning 5 minutes later and that the shelf had not cooled in the least bit.  I unplugged the refrigerator and waited until the light fixture and bulbs were cool enough to handle and promptly removed both bulbs. 10/06/11

This is the 2nd major problem with this refrigerator. Although not a safety hazard, the water supply line to the icemaker would freeze because it was routed in front of the freezing cold air vent that cooled the refrigerator.  A Sears repairman came out and it worked for a very short while before it re-froze.  We have lived without the icemaker ever since.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning refrigerator with no reported injury or death, but it is a recurring issue affecting functionality.

incident_description: Opened Refrigerator door at 04:00 found light fixture had failed to turn off and had melted, lights were still on. Appears to be a very common problem from reports on the web where it's caused a few fires.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning refrigerator light that could potentially cause a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Bosch Dishwasher Model SHE65P02UC  After one year and 43 days of use, the dishwasher died mid-cycle, and wouldn't turn on the next day.  I opened up the junction box under the dishwasher, and the wires had burned and melted the plastic terminal strip.  The black wire was burned and carmalized.  There was black soot on the metal junction box.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing wire damage and soot, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Bosch SHE44C02UC/22 residential dishwasher stopped functioning. 

Appeared to be a power problem, as +120VAC present at on/off switch, w/ open neutral. 
Accessed installer access point to check connections. 

Noted installer used proper wire, 14AWG on a 15A circuit. Three wire nuts in use. 

Residence circuit breaker DID NOT trip. 

Neutral wire burned open, wire nut melted to bottom of box. Noted damage to wire nut on hot leg. 

Noted the wire that is manufacturer supplied for powering the unit is undersized at 16AWG. (clearly marked on outer jacket). It appears that the installer/end user has NOT modified the internal wiring in any way, as all three legs of the circuit are the same make/type/size wire. 

Several time over the lst few months we have smelled a burning smell when operating this appliance.  We thought it was the hot wash water, or food inside the washer, but can see now if was this wire melting.  

Posts on the web revealed others have noted the same problem. 

Damaged wire and parts will be retained for 90 days, should CPSC desire they be submitted for evaluation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with electrical damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I have a Samsung over the range microwave oven which is starting spontaneously on its own (empty) and runs continuously until I press the stop button.  Fortunately, I have been aware of its running and have been able to manually stop it.  I have observed that when it self starts it has been in the "Popcorn" mode according to the display.  I am concerned that it is a fire hazard.  I am indicating the "Incident Date" below as yesterday because it happened several times yesterday, but it has actually been happening regularly for several weeks.

I was heating a flour tortilla in a T-Fal stainless steel fry pan when I heard a bang, almost like a gun shot, and something flew to my left.

I found a small round, size of a pea, piece of stainless steel in my floor.  It was torn on one side.  On inspection of my skillet I found that it apparantenly popped off  the skillet where the handle is riveted on.  My husband said it is a rivet cover

Thankfully the handle was pointed away from anyone.  Someone could have been hurt seriously.

I did call your 800 number today and left a message so you will have a duplicate report.
justification: A piece of the skillet broke off but no one was injured, though there was potential for serious harm.

incident_description: I purchased a stainless steel 8'' pan from Macy's 5 years ago.  This morning I was cooking eggs over medium heat when I heard a terribly loud pop.  I covered my ears and stepped away from the pan.  When I looked back I realized that a steel bolt cover had popped off the pan, hit the ceiling and landed on the floor.  I or someone in my family could have sustained serious injury to the eye.  It's a wonder I wasn't injured.  This product poses a serious safety concern and should be recalled at once.  I took pictures of the pan and the bolt that popped off.
justification: The incident involved a loud pop and a bolt cover flying off, but no actual injury occurred, though there was potential for serious harm.

incident_description:
Shortly after plugging the popcorn popper into the wall outlet to allow it to run prior to use it  she powered it in the on position and powered it in the off position within three meant when she noticed the on/off switch had a spark in it. She unplugged it immediately and placed it back into the original packaging. On/Off switch sparks when turned OFF - every time!!

She contacted the firm and reported the incident with them. The representative that she spoke with (name was not provided) advised her that it might be an isolated incident and that she could return  it to the retailer or exchange it and if she got a new one and the same incident occurred to please call back.

On  9/10/2011 she exchanged it at the retailer for the same model. Following the first steps that were taken the day before she experienced the same failure. 

On 9/13/2011 She contacted the firm and was recommended to contact the retailer. She bought it to the attention of the manager that she had 2 popcorn poppers that had sparks flying from the on/off switch. The manager showed no interest and laughed at the consumer. Later that date  she returned the product to the retailer and received a full refund.  

On  9/15/2011 she contacted the firm again and wanted to know if there was a recall in affect and she was advised by the representative (name is unknown) that once they receive a certain number of reports and or a certain number of phone calls for a product for them to recall it. 

The consumer indicated that a person could seriously harm themselves with the product.
justification: The incident involved sparks from the on/off switch but no injury occurred, and the issue was reproducible with a second unit, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Purchased Samsung Side by Side refrigerator from Best Buy January 2009.  Model RS2530BBP.
Yesterday (10/06/2011) noticed burning-rubber-type smell in the kitchen but couldnt determine where the smell was coming from.  Later at night, my wife touches the exterior of the freezer side and it was too hot to touch.  Did some research online and noticed other samsung customers had identical problems with their refrigerators.  Repairmen I have spoken to have all said that it is unusual for this type of problem to occur when the fridge is less than 3 years old.  I have 3 children in the house and this posed a serious burn hazard.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and excessive heat posing a burn hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was cooking dinner and came into the kitchen and the oven was smoking.  I removed dinner from the oven and turned the stove off.  The light indicated that the stove was off but in fact it was not. It continued to get hotter. I tried several time to turn the oven off before I went and turned the breaker off.  I waited about 30 minutes and turned the breaker on again and the oven came on again by itself.  We have the breaker off. Everything on the oven and around the oven was very hot.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his electric oven range combo is a fire hazard. The consumer stated that he looked at the electric dials of the range, and at the dials of the digital display appear to show that the range is off. However, the front left burner is still on and very hot, the consumer states that the control panel does indicate that the surface is hot. The consumer stated that this problem happened about 6 months ago and has continued. The consumer had to  go downstairs to power off the circuit breaker to shut off the breaker.

 The consumer plugged in the circuit breaker again and the range front burner did not turn right back on its own. The consumer's wife was using the range to cook pasta and found that the burner would not shut off 3 minutes after she powered it off. The range was set to 3/4 heat capacity. The consumer was not using the oven at the time of the incident. The consumer has a smooth top surface. The consumer called the firm today after doing some independent online research and they stated that the product was not on recall. 

The firm gave him the number to the CPSC. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The consumer was informed by the CPSC that there was no recall currently for his range. The consumer found similar models in release 09-333 that have the same hazard as his range. The product is an oven range combo and has not experienced any issues with the oven. 

The consumer has continued to use the stove but has not used the effected burner. The consumer tried to use the left front burner and it still would not respond to a shut off. The product appeared to show no signs of damage.  The product has not damaged the consumer's home. The consumer stated that no one has been hurt. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner that poses a fire hazard but has not caused injury or damage, fitting severity level 2. The issue is recurring, making occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description: kenmore elite dishwasher model 665.16292401 started smoking from control panel
