incident_description:
I own a Kenmore smooth top range which in my house when I bought it August 2010.  The Model # is 790.96002601 and the Serial # is VF71831158.   The left front burner will remain on after being turned to OFF.  It also will come on to a low setting and even a very high RED setting ALL by itself.  I have to turn the stove off at the circuit breaker panel to ensure it doesn't come on by itself and burn the house down.

I understand that this particular model and serial number is not in the recall.  How am I supposed to pay for something that is very expensive to repair?  It apparently is happening all over the United States according to the information I found when googling "Kenmore range top turns on by itself" This is the manufacturers fault.  It didn't just happened to me.... many many many people have these KENMORE stovetops (and the ovens are cutting on by themselves too!!!!) that are cutting on by themselves and they are NOT in the recall!  I am a single mom with limited employment now and two kids to support.  I shouldn't have to pay for this stove when it is not my fault.    Read the below incerp from a website that I visited re: getting SEARS to accept responsibility and repair the product....

"When I saw the recall in Consumer Reports magazine, I immediately called Sears and was informed that this model was not on the recall list,but the operator did tell me she had received many phone calls exactly like mine from people experiencing the same problems whose stoves were not on the list. She suggested I report the problem to the C.P.S.C. which I did. The C.P.S.C. sent me a letter confirming the information and suggested I contact the manufacturer. I contacted Frigidaire/Electrolux via e-mail and was told by them that they could not help me and I needed to contact Sears Customer Care as that was the place of purchase. After an e-mail to Sears, I got a phone call from a customer care representative who said that Sears was willing to pay me back the $65.00 service fee if I would pay parts and labour for a technician to come ....."  

This lady's problem never got solved..... Why would you trust that an effective repair would be made with this type of problem occurring?  Why chance burning up your family or house in the middle of the night?

There needs to be a recall on ALL of the KENMORE electric range top products experiencing these issues!   SEARS should stand by their products! They should  give full coverage for REPLACEMENT.  
Please help us to get our stoves replaced!
Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: The stove turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, which could lead to property damage or injury, though no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: Cooking a pork roast in oven at 400 pork roast had been in oven for around 30 minutes pulled out rack and basted roast with meat juices from the pan when pan exploded. My husband was in the kitchen standing next to me. I had my arm straight out and jumped back pulling my arm back so fast that I dislocated my arm and ran the bone through my shoulder tearing my biceps muscle,the seal on my shoulder socket and tendons. Needless to say dinner was not at my house and my daughter came over and cleaned up the glass. My husband took me to the ER and I am still recovering.
justification: The incident resulted in a dislocated arm, torn biceps muscle, and other injuries requiring ER visit and ongoing recovery, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such severe injuries from basting a roast are not common.

incident_description: My 18 month son old son was playing with his toys on his belly in front of the dishwasher.  While playing, he lifted his foot and sliced it open on his right heel.  The injury was caused by an exposed stainless steel edge on the back side of the dishwasher's stainless steel front panel.  The injury required 7 stitches and still hasn't fully healed (not to mention the trauma his parents endured).  No doubt this is a manufacturer design flaw as this edge should have been beveled up to prevent an exposed edge.  This needs to be corrected immediately to prevent future injury.
justification: The injury required 7 stitches, indicating a significant injury (severity 3). The exposed edge suggests a possible recurrence if not corrected (likelihood 3).

incident_description: i try to use the oven and it will say f13. i'll hit clear to stop the beeping. the oven control panel will do a series of clicking then the oven will go on  by itself doing the last command that was attempted. example: if i tried to broil-then broil will come on whenever it feels like it. one time it happened when we werent home. I have contacted my warranty dept and they have replaced the thermostat and the control panel three times already and it is still happening.
justification: The oven malfunctioning poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
The oven electronic control panel spontaneously caught fire while baking one item at 450 degrees. The burners and lower oven were not on and had not been used previously that day.
Frigidaire range model # PLEFM399DCD
Serial # VF 52043472
Purchased June 2007 at Airport Appliance in Hayward, CA, for $1,200.

There was a crackling sound, then flames about 6" high shot out the back of the unit, then a loud pop sound and the fire went out.  There was a strong electrical fire smell the rest of the day.  It was a Sunday. The following morning I called Frigidaire to report the problem as was told the unit was under recall for a fire hazard; however, NOT for that hazard.  Apparently a different part also catches fire on this unit.  They were happy to sell me the replacement parts I needed for $250.
justification: The oven control panel caught fire but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident was unexpected and related to a known recall issue, suggesting an occurrence likelihood of 3.

incident_description:
failure of the electric Stove/Oven caused an apartment fire. Investigator partially remove the back panel of the stove revealing a wiring bundle approximately 4 inches from the top back that had substantial fire/heat damage consistent with an arching event. The fire/heat progressed to nearby combustibles: wiring insulation, top plastic components and light metals of the stove control panel, out the back of the stove to the paneling that was likely touching or very near the back of the stove. a smoke detector on the main level was not installed. the fire progressed to the cabinets to the south of the stove and contents on the counter top on the south. 6 residents, 4 adults & 2 kids, were in the aparment at time of the fire.
21 yof was hospitalized.
justification: A fire caused by electrical failure resulted in property damage and hospitalization of one individual, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
GE Refrigerator model PSI23SCRGSV, started to heat and cause interior plastic to melt. Whole house smelt like burnt plastic. The heat inside was so intense it melted not only the butter, but also the cheese.
The freezer side was intact and seem to work ok.
I think if we were not home at 7AM on 09/24/2011, I am afraid the kitchen would have caught on fire. 

I have notified GE. They only seem to be concern that it was out of warranty.
We bought the unit on 05/03/2008. We did however bought an extended warranty thru a 3rd party. We will see what happens on Monday 09/26.
justification: The refrigerator caused significant heating and melting, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
US CONSUMER SAFETY COMMISSION
4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814

Subject: Exploding Glass Oven Doors

In the interests of consumer safety and product reliability I would think you would address the countless reported incidents
of tempered glass oven door fronts literally exploding, and forcefully showering glass shards into the surrounding area .
... . See Google; "Exploding Glass Oven Doors".

The manufacturers are apparently refusing to acknowledge this design flaw, (similar to the [REDACTED] of the seventies).

In our case, the disconnected oven door had been lying on a counter top for further cleaning. When two hands grasped either side to pick it up it literally exploded! - sending shards of glass into adjacent rooms as far away as twenty or more feet. My hands received several cuts, but I shudder to think of my resultant bloodied face and eyes had the door been facing me.

I think that your organization should consider an investigation into this situation and publicly expose the phenomenon.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (cuts to hands) and could have caused more severe harm if the glass had hit the face or eyes. The description also mentions countless reported incidents, indicating a significant occurrence likelihood.

incident_description: "Oven safe" Pyrex glassware, first use, placed 9 x 9 glass pan in preheated oven with brownie mix, pan shattered after being inside of oven for 12 minutes
justification: The incident involved the shattering of a Pyrex pan in the oven, which is a material failure but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Sitting at kitchen table and heard an explosion in a kitchen cupboard. Started investigating and found a glass bowl shattered in a kitchen cupboard. Immediately looked at open window  and  screen to see if stray bullet had come into house. (No bullet hole found in screen, window, or cupboard door). This bowl was the top bowl in a stack of three. The bowl immediately below it was of the same type and size. The bottom bowl was larger and held the other two bowls. In addition the bottom bowl contained the majority of the shards. The event was so unusual that I took pictures and a few days later posted them on facebook.

Looked at damage and determined that a glass bowl had shattered on the top shelf throwing sharp shards as far away as the bottom shelf. The bowl that shattered primary use was for heating materials in the microwave. This bowl hadn't been used for a least a three days and sat undisturbed in the cupboard for that amount of time. 

The cupboard was room temperature and is not heated or cooled. The dish was approximately 2 years old. (We have several that were purchased in the same time frame and had no evidence of damage prior to the explosion.) It was manufactured by Anchor Ovenware and is a 20oz Casserole dish. 

After this event I remembered reading about breaking glassware somewhere. About a week later, I ran across the article in consumer's reports. The article though dealt with breakage during use. This dish however was not in use and the noise was loud like an explosion.
justification: The incident involved a glass bowl shattering unexpectedly, but no injuries or further damage occurred.

incident_description: Anchor Hocking glass pan shattered/exploded in mid air as it was lifted out of the oven.
justification: The glass shattered in mid-air, which could potentially cause injury from flying glass shards.

incident_description:
Our Maytag dishwasher caught fire.

We bought the unit new a number of years ago (we do not remember how many years ago that was). We had a load of wash running. The load was the usual si8ze (i.e., not overloaded). We heard a crackling and popping. We saw flames shooting from the lower right of the unit and smelled smoke. By the time we got out our fire extinguisher the fire had stopped, the smoke had mostly subsided, and we found later that the circuit breaker had tripped.

The model # is MDB5130AWW
The serial # is 27239658AC
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
I participated in the recall of Maytag dishwashers in July 2010 and the heating coil at the bottom of the dishwasher was replaced. Recently (in the last 3-6 months) I began using the Sanitizing and Heat Dry functions of the dishwasher. Two weeks ago I noticed that two spots on the dish rack directly above the heating coil were melted/burned through. In one of the spots, the tine that holds the dish in place had melted and fallen off the rack. In the other spot, the rack has melted through so that only the shell of coating remains at that spot on the dish rack. 

I contacted Maytag via their hotline and was told that the recall replacement had a 90-day warranty which is now expired so that any repairs going forward will be my responsibility.
In calling the CPSC hotline, I was told I could submit this report. The Release Number for this case is [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted dish rack) but no injury or death.

incident_description: I came in the house to find that the microwave was running by itself. I attempted to turn it off by using the key pad, but it wouldn't shut off. I had to open the door to stop it. The LED display was showing "PAD". I unplugged the microwave, and plugged it back in. Within seconds, it started running again. The interior of the microwave was extremely hot. So hot that I couldn't touch the glass rotisserie. I did a quick search on the internet to find that this is a common problem with this particular model. Whirlpool replaced the control board at no cost to me, but could not insure that the replacement board was any different than what was originally in the microwave. Hence, the issue may occur again at any time. KitchenAid model KHMS155LSS-3. Manufacture date Oct 05.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and ran by itself, posing a burn risk, but no injury occurred. The issue is known to recur with this model.

incident_description: Responded to a report of a fire in an oven.  Upon my arrival found that a small fire had occurred in a Whirlpool Model RF395LXED Serial RE3718609 240volt electric stove.  The home health aid reports that while cooking dinner for the resident the stove went into the self cleaning mode.  The door locked and caused the food in the oven to start on fire.  She was unable to open the oven and remove the burning material.  The fire department was contacted.  After a time they were able to get the oven to open and extinguished the small fire.  The home health aid reports that on 9/30 she also cooked in the oven.  She states that on that day, after the stove was turned off, the stove also went into self clean mode.  The stove was disconnected and she was told to no longer use the stove.  The stove was left at the residence.
justification: The incident involved a small fire in an oven with no reported injuries, but required fire department intervention.

incident_description:
Back left burner comes on by itself. Buttons to turn off burner are unresponsive and display on panel doesn't show the burner as being on at all when this happens. Fortunately there were no flammable items on top of the range when this happened and we were actually home to see it and turn off the power to the range. Currently have power off to the range when not in use. I have used the range since then and when the power is turned on to the range the burner will come on for maybe 30 seconds then go off. It will continually repeat this process. As stated above there is no indication on the display that the burner is on.

Have been in contact with Sears and they state that there is no recall on this range and that I would be charged to repair what I consider a defective product and a fire hazzard. Will be contacting Fridgidaire (the manufacturer) to see what they will do. There are many other ranges by the same manufacturer that have been recalled for the same problem.

I have made a video recording of the defective range with this condition happening.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred due to immediate action.

incident_description:
We purchased a Whirlpool 30" freestanding gas range - model WFG371LVB - from Sears in January 2011.  The range works properly but there is a design flaw that is very dangerous.

The four burner controls are on the front of the stove.  As one reaches over the stove to the back burners the control knobs can inadvertly turn slightly to the on position and release gas into the air but not far enough to ignite the burner.  THIS IS A SAFETY CONCERN.

This has happened to us on numerous occasions since we purchased the range.  The seriousness of this design flaw was evidenced the other evening when we unknowingly bumped the knob as we went to bed and found the house filled with gas in the morning.  Fortunately, we had the bedroom door closed so the gas did not enter the bedroom or we could have been asphixiated!
justification: The incident describes a near-fatal gas leak due to a design flaw, indicating a high severity (potential death) and moderate likelihood (happened multiple times but not always).

incident_description:
Kenmore Refridgerator model number 795.77312600 lights would not turn off even when doors were closed.  Lightbulbs overheated and scorched their sockets.  Melted Plastic Lightbulb housing. Inside of refrigerator was very warm.   We had to remove the bulbs with hotpads for fear of this causing a house fire.   We were forced to throw away all of the raw meat due to possible spoilage.  
There are many complaints of this happening on the internet and I hope it is taken seriously as the fire hazard that it is.   Please urge Kenmore to recall this fridge.
justification: The incident involved property damage and potential fire hazard without injury, and multiple complaints suggest it's a likely recurring issue.

incident_description:
My Kenmore oven door exploded and the oven was not even on. I looked into many stoves and bought this rather expensive stove a little over a year ago. I could not believe my eyes. I cried and called Sears they only passed me from one operator to the next saying it was not their problem. That evening I looked online only to find many exploding oven doors and yet nothing ever seems to come of it. I really hope you can shed some light on this and tell me you have dealt with this before. I am so sick to think my new oven is defective and others like it and no one is doing anything about it. If you can not help me I will be contacting news watch 16 to look into this someone has to deal with this problem before someone gets hurt. I am not out for a new oven  just a new door with less glass.
Thank you,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The oven door exploded, but no one was hurt, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 because it is not rare but not very common either.

incident_description: Our Kenmore electric oven (serial # 2M2025730 and model# 911.93601002) apparently did not shut off after the nobs were turned off. Therefore our oven temperature kept rising and rising for 10 hours while we were in and out of the house.  Finally we noticed that the stove was very hot and realized that it was still running despite being turned off 10 hrs ago.  We pulled the stove away from the wall and unplugged it.  This was an extremely dangerous situatuion for my husband, myself and my 3 young children.  In researching this on the internet, I can see that we are not alone in having this situation happen. When you turn something off you expect it to be off. Something must be done with this brand of oven.
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury occurred, though the situation was dangerous for the family.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was finished using the microwave for approximately half and hour, she heard a pop and cracking sound and she noticed that the center peice of glass exploded and shattered into several peices onto the countertop.

9/15/11 Consumer contacted the store and was advised that a service rep would be sent out at a cost to her.  The rep advised that the microwave part was no longer available.

Consumer feels that this unit is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The microwave glass exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The refrigerator comes with five glass shelves that sit on top of a plastic bracket that broke. The  plastic bracket  broke causing the two shelves at the top of the refrigerator to break and the .

The firm was contacted 5/2010 the firm was contacted and the consumer ordered the two shelves the brackets that are used to support the shelves are incased around the shelf.

On 9/5/2011 the top bracket  the second shelf and the lower shelf over the vegetable bin bracket  broke (not all within the same day). The firm was contacted  that same very week and the consumer ordered the replacement shelves.

The consumer indicated that in the event someone is opening the refrigerator and the plastic bracket break causing a shelf to fall someone could be possibly injured. 

The consumer was advised  when she spoke with the firm that she was washing the shelves in hot water causing the plastic bracket to weakened and fail. 

The consumer indicated that she only washed the shelf one time and with Luke warm water. No further information was provided.
justification: The incident involved broken shelves and brackets, but no injury was reported. The consumer raised a hypothetical risk of injury, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore stove Model 790.96612409 S/N VF63214170 failed in a hazardous state.  The following was written by my wife whom was apparently shocked by the stove.
 
"I was making BBQ meatballs on the stove, using the burning with the simmer select feature. The pot was boiling, I turned down the heat, then pushed the simmer select button. When I pushed the button, there was a loud popping sound and a white flash . The burner was still functional, the clock was still on.
 
About five minutes later I was putting a pot of water on the back right burner to make rice. I had my hand on the handle of the pot and turned the burner on. There was a loud popping sound, an orange flash, and the muscles in my left arm contracted. An orange flash appeared to be coming from the area of the knob I was turning. 

The display panel was still on after the 2nd incident, and as far as I could tell, the simmer select burner was still working."
 
My daughter and I also both heard the arc and saw the first arc flash from about 10' away with our backs to the stove.  Before the stove was disconnected I confirmed continuity from a copper water pipe to the stove chassis.  The stove was wired with separate nuetral and ground wires.  The stove has since been removed from the house and is being stored in a pole shed in case somebody would like to look into what is wrong with it.  
 
It is now 2 days after my wife was shocked, the pain in her arm has now subsided, but she is still having spasms in one finger which may be related to the shock.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock causing muscle contractions and ongoing spasms, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I was cooking chicken in a Pyrex glass casserole dish. I put it in the toaster oven on the broil setting. After 5 or 10 minutes I took it out, and turned to put it on the stove to cool, but before I set it down, it exploded in my hand, cleaving into several large chunks, and sending small shards of glass all over the kitchen.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no injury was mentioned, making it a severity level 2. Such incidents are unlikely but possible with improper use of glass cookware.

incident_description: 5yr 4mo old Jenn-Air free standing gas range caught fire.
justification: The gas range caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the dishwasher was placed on a normal cycle, he noticed that approximately 2 hours later it was still running, and then it automatically powered off  but the contents were not dried.  He also noticed that the heating element had overheated and had charred a small portion. The lights on the control panel kept blinking as well.

9/19/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that his model was not part of the recall and the dishwasher was out of warranty.

Consumer is concerned that his dishwasher is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and charred a small portion, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
My GE counter top micro wave oven, Model # JES 1139BL03, Ser # FT 912872B, Manu March 2010,
Made in Mayaysia, Sparks and Smokes internally, as if wires are burning.
[REDACTED]
justification: The microwave sparks and smokes internally, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Krups FBC 412, Ref 575.04 digital convection toaster oven purchased in December 2008 for regular household use has a small wire in the rear of the unit that shorted out, causing the heating elements to fail.  The unit was approximately 12 minutes into the convection baking cycle, with temperature set 400 degrees F when a flame and sparks shot out from the rear vent.  The unit continued to run (convection fan and timer) however, the heating elements were not working.  No further sparks or flame developed.  The failed heating elements and burned wire were not readily evident since the unit continued to run, even when turned off and turned back on.  I'm concerned if the defect had gone undetected a fire could have resulted. 

I researched product recalls and did not find any.  The unit has always been used according to manufacturer instructions.
justification: The incident involved sparks and flame but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the defect could recur but hasn't been widely reported.

incident_description: The dishwasher did not shut off when the cycle ended  therefore it melted everything that was plastic on the dishwasher and dishes and a skillet  the dishwasher was hot to the touch.  Had to unplug it and let cool for some time before I was able to remove the dishes.  I feel we were lucky that the house did not catch on fire
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused damage to items and posed a fire risk, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a Anchor Hocking glass casserole dish 1-2 yrs ago and have used it frequently (in the oven) without any problems. I am always careful with any glass product to not expose them to temperature extremes.
On Friday, 9/30/11, I used the dish to make lasagna. After cooking in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes, we ate some of the lasagna and  I placed the dish on cloth pads to cool for about 1 hour  at room temperature. After that, I put the dish with the remaining lasagna in the refrigerator.
On Saturday, 10/1/11, my family would dip some parts of the lasagna out of the dish and microwave it in a separate dish. The Anchor Hocking dish was just taken out of the refrigerator and then immediately put back after they took out a piece of lasagna.
On Sunday. 10/2/11, about midnight, I was working on a project on my computer when I heard what could best be described as a explosion from the inside of the refrigerator. When I opened the door, pieces of glass ranging from small slivers to 4 inch pieces (many had sharp edges) were in every space of my refrigerator. The only part of the dish not apart was where leftover lasagna was which was about 20% of the dish. Even this part of the dish had crack marks through every inch but they had not "flown" anywhere, unlike the rest of the dish. We spend a couple of hours cleaning, sweeping, and throwing out food due to being scared of small slivers of glass in stuff. We kept the pieces of the bottom that show the Anchor Hocking emblem. 
Thank goodness I was not leaning down to get something out of the refrigerator when this happened or there could have been serious injuries. I also took pictures of it before I moved any of the pieces. The dish had been in the refrigerator for about 50 hours at the same temperature except for 2-4 times of dipping out a piece of lasagna. There needs to be a recall before somebody's eyesight or in a worst case scenario, a lacerated carotid artery happens.  Thank you for listening.
justification: The incident involved a glass dish exploding in the refrigerator, causing no injuries but significant property damage and cleanup effort.

incident_description: I set my Martha Stewart CollectionÃÂ® Enameled Steel Tea Kettle on the stove on a high setting about half full of water.  I became distracted and returned about 30 minutes later to find the kettle miscolored, the red paint had adhered to the stove and the handle was deformed.  Upon researching the product, I realized it had been recalled last year for problems with the handle.
justification: The incident caused damage to the kettle and the stove, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: In summer of 2011, we noticed the "element on" light of our Frigidaire smoothtop cookstove was on but all of the switches were in the off position.   My husband turned each of the 5 switches on and back off multiple times. The light went out after one of them.  Within 5 minutes the light was back on.  He tried the switches again and this time a different switch triggered the light off.  We had been playing that game for several months with the switch and during that time there was no heat coming from any of the elements, so we didn't find it an emergency situation. However, on 3 October 2011, I noticed that while there was an element on a low temperature (#3) on the left rear side of the stove, the front right burner also felt warm. Neither my husband nor I had used that burner that day (it was not warm earlier in the day).  We are now concerend that the burners can now turn themselves on, wich is very scary.  The stove is not on recall with Frigidaire. The model number is FEFL77AQF
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove with burners turning on unexpectedly, posing a potential fire hazard but no injury or damage reported.

incident_description: Left front burner will not turn off or runs at a higher temperature then selected. Multiple attempts to turn off the burner failed and the burner continued to be energized as it's highest setting.  The setting would also not reduce to a lower setting.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Frigidaire electric oven, model PGEF3077KWB, with touch pad controls does not shut off.  Repeated pressing of the cancel button may finally get it shut down but on several occasions the circuit breaker had to be used to clear the problem.
justification: The oven's failure to shut off poses a potential hazard, but no injury or death is reported; the issue occurs frequently based on the description.

incident_description: i had bought a frigidaire stove from lowes on 07_19_2011 .first of all it was burning food at 200 degress.on morning i put my stove on self clean.it had caught fire.due to a default in the stove.it has been over a week and i still had not heard nothing back for frigidaire or lowes about it.i will make sure everyone knows to make sure if they buy these stoves to check a recall,.
justification: The stove caught fire due to a defect, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Our fridge started filling the room with smoke and a nasty burning smell. We unplugged it immediately. Later I opened the back panel, vacuumed out the dust and plugged it in again. I could see where it was sparking and igniting a small flame, probably burning the plastic housing near the wiring.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a small flame, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While I was using my crock pot on low setting yesterday, I noticed the smell of plastic melting, shut off crock pot, removed contents and noticed the plastic bottom had a melted area the size of a half dollar.  The heating element melted through bottom of crock pot, and another area where it was starting to melt, also. This did not result in any injuries but had I not been home or in the kitchen it could have resulted in the loss of our home and then possible injury or death to me,my fiancee, my other children ,one of which has a disability,  and is at a disadvantage to get out of home quick enough.
justification: The incident involved a melted crock pot but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for serious consequences if unnoticed.

incident_description: I purchased a whirlpool refrigerator. I used the top shelves for milk, water, juice etc.  There was no weight limit indicated, so I thought this was ok.  However, the white plastic cracked in several places, under pressure.  Due to this, the glass edges were exposed, that were once covered by the protective hard plastic. Im afraid that further cracking, or chipping can occur and cause the glass to shatter and seriously injur myself or my young son. In addition the wall of the freezer is splitting open.
justification: The incident involves potential for injury due to exposed glass edges and further cracking, posing a risk to the user and their child.

incident_description:
Every time the consumer turns on the front left hand burner (when facing the range), the electronic sparking does not stop.  The arcing continues, but no flame appears.  The consumer has left the burner on 10 seconds or longer, but the flame never appeared.  The consumer thought that the arcing would stop, but it would not.  

The consumer discontinued use of that burner.  The consumer went to the mfr's website and the advice was to discontinue the use of the burners until it has been repaired.

(9/2/11)  The cosnumer called the mfr. after reviewing information on the Internet (CA{P 05-050).  The mfr's rep. scheduled a tech. to come out on 9/9/11.  The consumer agreed to the offer, but not feel that she should have pay.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner with continuous arcing but no flame, posing a potential hazard but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: We bought a microwave oven I believe from either K-Mart or Target, in Moorhead, MN and had the unit for only two years. Last week we went to use the microwave and the inside part of the oven closest to the powersupply was burnt. We have never placed anything inside the unit that should have not been in there, such as metal forks, etc. The microwave still had the digits lit up on the display panel before we unplugged it. We did not smell smoke or see it start on fire. It must of happened after we left the house. I talked to an appliance tech and he said that seemed quite unusual for that to happen.  I do have photos if you need them.
justification: The microwave showed signs of internal burning but no injury or fire occurred, and the issue was identified before further damage.

incident_description:
I have a Cuisinart DCC-1200 Brew Central Programmable Coffeemaker which was purchased 10/14/2010 from Amazon.com. I use this coffee maker 4-5 times per week. Yesterday, about 10 minutes after starting the brew cycle, I heard a strange noise coming from the coffee maker, a bubbling, gurgling, hissing sound (which I later found out was due the coffee in the pot boiling and the hot plate burning). I checked the coffeemaker and saw smoke coming out from the hot plate. I removed the carafe and found the front half of the hot plate bright red. I immediately unplugged the coffee maker. Smoke continued to come out from around the hot plate along with a burning plastic smell. There was no damage to my countertop or any other surrounding appliances or the outlet. However, I feel if I had not been in the immediate vicinity this would not have been the case and quite likely could have led to a kitchen fire.
I called Cuisinart. They offered a replacement which I obviously didn't want. They refused to give me a refund.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer said that her wife set up the coffee maker  pour water and the coffee beans and press the bottom in the "on" position.  Consumer said that middle of the cycle the coffee maker started making a wire sound followed by strong plastic smell burned  (reason why unknown). 

Consumer stated that immediately unplugged the coffee maker and took to her back yard.  Consumer said that the smelling was so strong that they have to air the whole house.

Consumer feels that his coffee maker could pose a fire hazard
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker with a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as similar incidents are not uncommon.

incident_description:
Black and Decker "Smart Grind" Coffee mill, about 5 years old, sparked, sputtered and blew both the safety outlet in the kitchen and the circuit breaker in the garage.  At the point the wires emerge from the base, the insulation was melted and bare wires were visible.

The unit has never been used to gring anything except coffee beans and grains.  The cord has always been rewound into the base per the owners manual.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee mill causing electrical issues but no injury or death.

Consumer said that when she was having dinner with her husband she smelled something burning she went to the kitchen consumer inspected the range all the lights were ÃÂoffÃÂ and all knobs were in the ÃÂoffÃÂ position. 

Consumer opened the oven and found out that the heating element was ÃÂonÃÂ.

Consumer believes that her range/oven could pose a fire hazard.

incident_description: The consumer says when he sets the temperature on the front left burner, it goes to a higher temperature than indicated.  Also the burner does not switch off when turned off.  It also turns on without being turned on.  The consumer says that his unit is doing all three hazards indicated in 09-333 but his model is not listed in the recall.  The consumer says he has tried to unplug it for a few minutes but it happened again.  He unplugged it again and left it unplugged for a couple of days but it was having the same issue when turning it on.
justification: The burner malfunctions pose a hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I wasn't sure who to contact until today when I saw an article with the same problem.
It happened about a year ago, I had my family and their friends over for dinner. I was baking brownies and when I took the glass dish out of the oven and was about to set it down on the counter it popped and shattered into a million little pieces leaving cuts on mine and my mother's arms. We were all in shock, and we were very lucky that it didn't do permanent damage to our eyes. Unfortunely my parents little dog wasn't so lucky. She was standing in the kitchen when it happened. I could hear something sizzling and I looked at her and she had hot brownie batter on her back. We grabbed her and started washing it off when we noticed blood on our hands. A piece of glass had shot right into her leg. We took her to the vet right away as we sobbed our hearts out. The shard of glass had severed her tendons and veins in her leg and she had to have surgery at the cost of $1500. This might have been a freakish accident but it still happened when it shouldn't have at all. Whenever I tell my story there is always someone else who has their own story about the same problem. I do not cook with glass anymore even though I prefer to, it's to dangerous now.
justification: The incident caused injuries to humans and a dog, requiring veterinary surgery, but no permanent damage or death occurred.

incident_description: Frigidaire Side by side refrigerator model FRS6LR5EW6, serial number 4A70605549. Saturday, October 1, 2011, my husband started smelling something like electric burning or hot wires. After several hours we narrowed it down to the kitchen. We started checking first with the light fixture because it was put in last week.Then we checked the microwave and stove which is electric. We checked the attic. Finally we decided it was the small freezer of my mother in laws. We disconnected and emptied the small freezer. We went to bed. After about an hour I started coughing as I have lung issues.  I came into the kitchen area and the smell was strong.  So I sat down and watched the kitchen in the dark and within 5 minutes, I heard the refrigerator cycle on and a small light appeared... then it dimmed and came back very strong.  It appeared on the wall and floor as if it was a flame. The freezer was thawing towards the back of the freezer area.  We lost approximately $200 in food. The refrigerator was purchased at Lowe's in Tulsa, OK, on or after August 2007. I believe it was in the spring of 2008.  I have reported it to Frigidaire. And was told to contact their recall center at 888-360-8556.
justification: The incident involved a potential electrical fire hazard and food loss, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We purchased a gas range, Frigidaire model # FGGS3045KBA, serial #NF00324195, on February 10, 2010.  My husband and I are senior citizens and no children live in the home.  Therefore, we maintain our appliances and use them properly.  Just after the warranty expired, the handle on the oven fell off.  The screws holding it on have a very agressive thread design and only go into the handle about 3/16 to 1/4 inch.  Therefore, it is not a secure fit, very inadequate, and cannot be repaired since it is a design flaw.  It is extremely difficult to open a hot oven door without a handle.  

The control panel laminate is cracking and blistering.  This is not due to any cleaning chemicals since we use a microfiber cloth to clean it.  Soon the push button controls will be difficult or impossible to read and therefore, it could inadvertantly be set for self clean instead of turning oven off.

They were contacted and gave their condolences but do not agree there is any problem.  There is no fix to the shallow screw depth on the handle or the delamination of the control panel.
justification: The incident involves a faulty oven handle and deteriorating control panel, posing a risk of difficulty in operation but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Wine bottle opener manufactured by SUNBEAM PRODUCTS-  the wine bottle exploded while trying to open it. I suffered two cuts to my fingers, ruined my clothes, stained my table cover and stained the kitchen wall.
The bottle opener - Make- SUNBEAM-
Model  NBSKWA2600
justification: The incident resulted in two cuts to the fingers, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as bottle explosions are not common but can happen under certain conditions.

incident_description: Fire originated in GE Wall oven control module; resultant fire burned wooden cabinet in which the oven was mounted.  GE wall oven Model JKP17WVWW.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to property (wooden cabinet) but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Light fixture inside the fridge stayed on and the entire housing melted - noticed this when we began to smell an odor of melted plastic.  The bulb housing and plastic had browned and was completely warped.  Food on the top two shelves had 'cooked' under the intense heat of the two internal 60 watt bulbs.

Removed the fixture and bulbs to avoid any additional problems.  Will call vendor Monday.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted fixture and cooked food) but no reported injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: I baked some cornbread in an Anchor-Hocking Oven and Microwave Safe Glass Baking Dish and it exploded when I removed it from the oven. I received two black eyes and cuts to my face. It also burned my floor and counter top. I have doctor bills and pictures if needed.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (black eyes and cuts) and property damage, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the rarity of such incidents with proper use of oven-safe dishes.

incident_description:
In November 2005 I purchased a Kenmore Range Model 790.96213. In September 2011, I heated up my oven and went to open the door and the entire handle fell off and the stainless panel and glass fell down on me. I called Sears and talked with the initial customer service representative, then recall, and finally customer resolutions. All informed me that since my range was out of warranty that they could not do anything. I did a lot of research on the internet and found that others have experienced the same problem. Most said that the screws were too short. I measured the original screws in the oven door, which was 1 ÃÂ¾ÃÂ compared to 1 ÃÂ½ÃÂ door thickness. This left ÃÂ¼ÃÂ of the screw to attach to a plastic handle. Consequently, with only ÃÂ¼ÃÂ holding a handle on a door with a fairly heavy spring, the handle had a very high probability of coming off. My subsequent research showed that Sears recognized this problem and put longer screws on the later model ranges, hence, a manufacturerÃÂs defect.

The Recall Department implied that this was not a safety issue and there had been no recall. I personally do not see it that way as the panel could have dropped on a child and did burn one person (found on the internet). Had I been holding the door partway down, as I do many times, with my arm in the oven, I could have been severely burned from the door snapping back up on my arm. I was lucky that I was just opening the door when the handle came off.
justification: The incident involved the oven door handle falling off, which could have caused injury but did not in this specific case. The occurrence likelihood is high due to the manufacturer's defect and similar reports from other users.

incident_description: I have a kenmore smoothtop electric range that has 4 burners and two of them will not turn off unless I pull the breaker.  It is model # 79096009601
justification: The burners not turning off poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
I had made two Pumpkin Pies for Thanksgiving. One pie in a pyrex, one in a pie tin from France. 
When I took the pies from the oven, the Pyrex dish fell apart in my gloved hands..there was also an unusual smell in my oven....Not the delicious smell of my famous Pumkin Pies....I never bake in Pyrex anymore....I won't until I am assured of Quality control..maybe not even then!!! (My husband took a photo). [REDACTED]
justification: The Pyrex dish fell apart, but there was no mention of injury, only an unusual smell and a decision to avoid Pyrex in the future.

incident_description: Baking halibut in a 9X13 pyrex glass bakeware pan.  Oven temperature 400 degrees.  Pan shattered while in the oven, about 15 minutes into cooking.
justification: The pan shattered in the oven, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I cooked chicken in the oven in my 9x13 glass baking dish. When I took it out of the oven I set on my stove top as I have done many times before. The stove had not been on and was not hot. The dish shattered and pieces fell to the floor and some scattered about the kitchen. Fortunately, neither my daughter nor I were hurt at all. The dish had no visible damage prior to use. I have used this dish in the same manner previously, so I am uncetain as to the cause.
justification: The glass baking dish shattered, but no one was injured, classifying it as an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a set of 6 MJOD beer glasses from IKEA in East Palo Alto, CA approximately 1 month ago.  In the course of washing these glasses, 3 of them broke over the following weeks when placing the glass in the drying rack, usually because of a slight bump to another dish.  On 2 of these occasions, a piece of the top rim broke off, and until you used the glass to drink, you were not aware the glass was even cracked, because an entire top circular piece broke off, leaving a rough, dangerous new rim on top.  It appears that these glasses have glass that is much too thin to take any kind of regular consumer usage.

Then, last Sunday, September 18th, I was washing one of these glasses, with my left hand partially  inside the glass with a sponge cleaning the inside, when the entire glass exploded, severely cutting my thumb and releasing a large quantity of blood.  I rushed down to the Stanford Emergency Room, but because the wait was so long (and I was concerned whether my insurance would be excepted by them), I moved to the Palo Alto Medical Foundation Urgent Care.  There, I needed 5 stitches to close the wound.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring medical attention (5 stitches), and the description indicates a pattern of glass breakage suggesting a possible defect.

incident_description:
Laceration of the hand while removing a Farberware knife from its protective sheath. Laceration required emergency room visit, stitches. Long term nerve and tendon damage is not know as of this writing.

Farberware knife sheath is defective and allows knife cutting edge to be exposed when completely inserted in sheath. Each side of the knife sheath has a decorative, non-functional, opening running the length of the sheath through which the knife is easily inserted. This leaves the cutting edge of the knife exposed and unprotected.

Addionally, the knife blade and sheath are identical colors so it is difficult to determine if knife is inserted completely into the sheath and protected, or exposed and unproteted.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring emergency room treatment and stitches, indicating an injury (severity 3). The defective sheath design and poor visibility make such injuries likely to occur (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Around the seal of the freezer on the freezer door  has condensed water that  causes it to drop down onto the floor near the plug and is causing minor damages to the wooden floor that it sits on.

October of 2010 the seal was repaired by the firm  but she still currently experiences the failure with the unit. She learned that her model is the first model of that line and believes that it was poorly designed and could pose as a fire hazard.


On 7/10/2011 she heard arching near the chest freezer  which is located in her dining room. Her husband immediately powered off the circuit breaker  and unplugged it from the wall outlet.

On 7/11/2011 she contacted the firm and they only afforded to replace the seal once again. She does not want them to replace the seal again because it does not repair the problem but instead is considering replacing the unit. The unit is still currently unplugged from the wall outlet.
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with the freezer seal causing water damage and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
On Friday evening, Sept. 23, I received a call from my wife telling me that she heard grinding, screeching noises coming from our Kenmore dishwasher. She went downstairs to the kitchen and saw smoke and flames pouring from the upper right corner of the door. She opened the door (very brave) and, thankfully, the machine stopped and the flames/smoke subsided. I told her to shut off the breaker, which she did. 

I returned home Monday, Sept. 26, and called Sears - they dispatched a repair person on Wed., Sept. 28. The repair person said he had not seen this issue before, although he had seen what may have been a precursor on three previous calls. These involved heat damage in the control board area - the same area as that which burned in my dishwasher. He called his tech. people  and asked if anyone knew anything about what might be the cause and, apparently, got a "no comment" comment - which he appeared to think odd.

In any case, he mentioned repairing the machine, but could not tell me what had gone wrong. I told him that, since no one appears to know what caused the fire, there was every likelihood that it may burn again and that repair was not a satisfactory resolution.

I called Sears again this morning, after they had received the repair person's report, and was told, at first, that they were 'oh so sympathetic', but that they hadn't heard about this problem before and therefore would only be willing to grant a a partial discount on the parts for a repair. I reiterated that their product was a fire hazard, that there is ample evidence "out there" (including on this website) that this was no isolated incident and that their apparent lack of concern was endangering the public. They then upped the ante to offer a free repair. I told them that I would think about it, but I'm really not comfortable with a repair if they don't know the cause.

For anyone else who has had this problem, I suggest visiting www.kitcheaidfire.com to read the 200+ accounts of those who have posted there.

CPSC.... Get these things recalled!
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred. The repair person noted similar issues in previous calls, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
On September 29, 2011, a few minutes after turning on my KitchenAid dishwasher, I smelled burning from wires.  I opened the dishwasher and saw smoke. I checked inside the dishwasher for any items on the heating coil or for any visibly melted items. I turned it back on briefly.  I could smell the fire in the upper right hand corner of the dishwasher door.

After finding that there has been reports by googling the problem on the web, I called KitchenAid.  I wanted someone to come to see the problem, but they would only send a repairman at cost to me.  I told them I was not getting it repaired and wanted someone to just see that the dishwasher was a fire hazard.  They would not do that.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I HAVE A RIVAL CROCK POT AND I WAS TAKING THE LID OFF THE CROCK POT AND THE HANDLE FLEW OFF DROPPING THE GLASS LID  BREAKING ON THE FLOOR THEY HAVE TO MAKE THEIR HANDLES BETTER SO THEY DONT BREAK OFF THE CROCK POT PROBABLY IS NOT EVEN A YEAR OLD
justification: The incident involved a broken glass lid but no reported injury, indicating a non-injury incident with possible likelihood due to product design flaws.

incident_description:
We had an electrical fire in the door of our dishwasher. The control board burned, burning and melting the plastic housing.  The fire was contained in the metal door. 

This was a Fridgidaire Electronic Dishwasher model PLDB999cc0
justification: The fire was contained within the dishwasher door, causing no injuries, but it resulted in damage to the appliance.

incident_description: Microwave flashes dramatically (not sparking) when heating food, as if it is going to explode. Very frightening! Although it is probably off warranty (a little under 2 years old) this is not really a warranty issue as much as a safety issue. It belongs to my former spouse and she was continuing to use it, standing by to quickly hit the stop button. I was concerned for her safety, as well as our son's, so encouraged her to remove it ASAP and said I'd check to see if there was a recall on it and if there wasn't that I would report it.
justification: The microwave exhibited alarming behavior but no injury occurred, and the user took precautionary measures.

incident_description:
In late June earlier July I was in the process of moving.  I was in the new apartment when I decided to make spaghetti for my daughter and her friend.  I went to look for my pans and realized that they must had been left in my storage unit.  I took a tin cake pan and started to brown the hamburger and then started to look for something that I could boil the noodles in.  I chose a square Blue Pyrex dish that I had owned for a couple years.  I always thought they could withstand an abundance of heat especially since the dish could cook casseroles in the oven.   
I was standing about 2 feet away with my back towards the oven washing some dishes in the sink.  I started to turn my body to the left, thinking that the noodles should be almost done.  Right at that very exact moment, the dish with boiling water and noodles exploded!!!  I'm talking, it sounded like a bomb and blue Pyrex went flying everywhere!  I found bigger chunks about 7 feet away.  The kitchen was closed in on all four sides.  On the side with the sink that was facing was where, to the left, you would enter through an open entry way.  To the right was a wall that had a window opening that looked into the living room.  Kind of like a Diner effect where the waitress would put her ticket on a spinner.
I didn't think too much about if I was cut or hurt because I was so angry and hungry at the same time and the 2 girls needed to be fed.  I left the mess in the kitchen and checked over my body quick to make sure there were no gashes and I seemed to be okay!  I took the girls to eat and went on with the night.  After getting my daughter to bed that night I took a shower to try to relax myself.  After I got out, is when I kinda started to think that something more could have happened during the explosion!     
My skin started to feel, how do you describe it?, tight and tingly.  Like hair raising or growing when you get really cold or have goosebumps. (Closest description I can come up with).  I said to my room mate, humor me John, I think I have glass in my skin... what does the internet say to do to get it out?  The first thing we tried that night was soaking in ice cold water that had baking soda mixed in with it.  We filled a huge round laundry basket in the tub as I took turns putting a leg in at a time and then my arms.  We weren't for sure that it did anything or even if there was what seemed to be itty bitty slivers of glass in my skin.  
   So, the next day, my body temp going from warm to cold due to the fact that I was moving plus I cleaned apartments during the day...This is why I feel the shards in my fingers just got pressed further into my skin from scrubbing hard surfaces all day long with the tips of my fingers.  I was getting annoyed by the sensation of my skin tightening that I went to CVS/Walgreens to get PRID a suave that is suppose to pull things like this out of your body!  It smells horrible, but I started rubbing it on my legs and arms and sure enough small little dark pieces started appearing.  I would put Prid on my hands and then wrap them up and put gloves on so I wouldn't mess with them.       
(I would start to mess with my fingers by taking a tweezers or clippers to get what felt like little pieces of glass... I think all Ii did was break them off into more pieces and it would just go further down into my skin.???)    
After using the Prid I went over to my friends house because she had a steam shower/room.  We thought that this would bring some of the glass out also.  I would feel my face tightening up and doing the weird thing described above, so she had an up close mirror with a light around it.  When I put my face up to it and took a close look I couldn't even believe what I saw!!!  My whole face along with my neck had blue hairlike follicles everywhere!  I told her to look into the mirror because we all thought I was crazy thinking that this glass could be so tiny that it was hard to tell if it was glass or not!  She looked and said "OMG... Yep that's blue... What else could it be?"
  This incident happened in May and it is now September!  I feel like I am still having to remove hairlike follicles from my face and hands because these were the areas that i had more interaction with due to cleaning and then touching my face during daily routines of putting on make up and washing it!  I feel that the tiny microscopic shards in my hands have mostly migrated to the tips of my fingers where I have numbness and col-lased skin

I haven't gone to the doctor because I don't know what the could possibly do for me.  I have contemplated it though, due to the fact that some of my friends think I am crazy when I say I have glass in my skin from a Pyrex explosion.  If you would like to contact me about this you can reach me on my cell at [redacted].  I would like to know if something like this has ever happened to someone else because it has haunted me for almost 6 months now!  Any suggestions on what to do to find out if there are still pieces of it in my body I would gladly go and do to know what the deal is.
 
Thank you for listening,
[redacted]
justification: The incident resulted in injury from glass shards embedded in the skin, causing ongoing discomfort and minor medical issues, but no death or severe injury was reported.

incident_description:
Needing a 9x13 glass pan for a recipe, on Sunday, September 25, 2011, my husband and I purchased a new Pyrex pan at Target in Rockville, MD as part of a 6 piece set that included three pans and three storage covers called ÃÂPyrex Grip Rite Bake nÃÂ Store 6-pc. Value Pack.ÃÂ I do not have the model or serial number, as it would have been imprinted on the pan itself. I do not have the wrapping as I recycled it in my Tuesday pickup. The Target website lists the store item number as 070-02-1175.  Here is a link to the set I purchased: http://www.target.com/p/Pyrex-Grip-Rite-Bake-n-Store-6-pc-Value-Pack/-/A-10762124 which also shows the item number. I also have the receipt, the two other pans from the set and the three matching covers as proof of purchase. I attached a pdf of the website, the receipt, and a picture of the other items in the Pyrex set. 

On Sunday evening, I placed the Pyrex in the dishwasher, with the three glass pans on the bottom shelf and the three covers on the top shelf as directed by the Pyrex instructions. It was washed on a ÃÂnormalÃÂ setting. The pans sat in our cabinets from Monday evening, when my husband and I emptied the dishwasher, until last night, the first time we used the pan. 

I made noodle kugel ÃÂ a type of noodle pudding. I mixed in a separate bowl sugar, eggs, sour cream, cottage cheese, and crushed pineapple. The mixture sat on the counter while I cooked the noodles. I instructed my husband to make sure that our granite counter tops were completely dry before placing the Pyrex pan on the counter. Then my husband coated the bottom of the pan with corn flake crumbs, cinnamon and sugar, and added some pads of butter from a stick that had been sitting out for at least 10-15 minutes. My husband strained the noodles and I sprayed them down with cool water to prevent sticking and to prevent the noodles from cooking the mixture I created. We combined the noodles and mixture and coated the tops with more crumbs, cinnamon and sugar, and butter. I write all of this to demonstrate that room temperature contents were added to a Pyrex pan on a dry surface. 

At about 9:35pm, I place the pan into an oven set to 350 degrees. I emphasize that the oven was not in the preheat stage or broil, nor was the pan close to the heat source. The pan was placed on a rack in the middle of the 350 degree oven. After about 20 minutes (I know from the timer I set), my husband and I heard a loud boom that sounded like an explosion from the inside of our oven. I peaked in and found that my Pyrex pan had exploded. I have two pictures that are attached from the inside of my oven showing the pieces - a wide shot and a close up. My oven has since been cleaned. I saved the glass which is intermixed with the kugel and have a picture, also attached, of the pan in the paper bag we used to hold the glass pieces.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex pan exploding in the oven, but no injuries were reported, only property damage.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the dishwasher was in use for approximately 10 mins when she smelled an odor of burnt plastic and there was smoke emitting from the vent of the dishwasher, she immediately attempted to power it off but the control panel was inoperable, she had to switched it off from the circuit breaker.  This incident caused melting of the electronic components to the control panel. 

Consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting components, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Maytag MGT8885xw.  We have had less than a year.  It took us 9 months to figure out, we had an inherent problem with the regulator/ burner in the top oven.  It was not lighting the whole way during ignition, and as such was letting gas escape and fill up the house.  After filling up the house in less than 15 minutes, we reported to Maytag.  A service technician came out under the warranty, assessed the situation, and it took 2+ months to obtain the required parts and fix.  No parts were immediately available in the entire country.  (July to September 2011)  The second problem happend Sunday 9/25/11.  The exterior lower oven glass spontaneously exploded with the oven off.  Maytag sent out a technician to "assess problem" although we had provided a picture.  Part was not immediately available. The did find it in Louisville, KY.  Resolution is to reinstall glass.
justification: The incident involved gas leaks and glass explosion, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was making muffins tonight in my Kenmore oven Model # 665-95781000. The oven was set to 350degrees. The first batch of 12 came out perfect. The second batch came out darker and when I pulled them out they were a little smokey. I figured I would bake the last batch of only 10 minutes instead of 12 like the others. About 5 minutes later, I smelled this awful smell. I walked into the kitchen and saw a fire on the muffins. My first reaction was to turn the oven off, then I opened the oven door and put the fire out on the muffin. I noticed how hot the oven felt. I started a fan to get the smoke out of the house and my kids were all scared. My husband came in and noticed that the top heating element was still glowing orange and that it wasnt shutting off. The only way we could turn the oven off was to turn off the breaker. This was a very scary event.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, but it caused fear and required intervention to turn off the oven.

incident_description: The consumer said the dishwasher was in use.  His friend noticed smoke coming out of it.  They opened the door and saw flames inside of it.  The consumer turned it off by unplugging it and hasnt used it since.  The consumer said the unit may have been on roughly ten minutes.  He contacted the retailer about getting unit replaced but they transferred him around and he finally got to CPSC.  Product and hazard are similar to Release # 05-123.  The consumer's model is not listed is out of range of the recall.
justification: The incident involved flames inside the dishwasher, but no injury or death was reported, and the consumer took immediate action to unplug it.

incident_description: I filled a mug from this set with water, not even hot water, just water. I picked the mug up and the handle crumbled in my hand nearly requiring stitches in about an inch long cut on my little finger. After 4 days the cut on my finger is still having trouble staying closed - this is a very deep cut, not requiring actual medical care, but very close. I have read reviews of this product since and have discovered MANY others have had similar experiences so wanted to make sure it was reported. Sears was where I purchased this and they would not help me file a report and would not refund the purchase since it was plus 90 days.
justification: The incident caused a deep cut that took 4 days to heal, indicating a serious injury.

incident_description: Pr-cooked soup items (rice, beans, chicken, etc...) were placed in to a blender approximately 1/2L.  Lid was placed on to the container/blender and held with a hand; thereafter, switch was turned to position 1 (LO).  When the switch was turned to position 1 (LO) the pressure build and soup ejected out of the top and on to the user.  The user experienced minor burn injuries to the upper chest, neck, and chin.  We had this blender for about an year and had experienced similar problems with it but never where the soup came out at that pressure and rate.
justification: The user experienced minor burn injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident has occurred before, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
On Monday, July 4, 2011, at 4:50 a.m. I was awakened by the smell of smoke. Somehow my self-cleaning feature of my Frigidaire oven had come on. There was one plastic microwavable pan in the oven. This pan caught fire and filled my house with choking smoke. My oven has digital touch pad controls on it.

Tuesday, July 5, 2011. I went to work the next day and told a co-worker about this. She told me that the same thing had happened with her oven. That night I did some research on the Internet and found many accounts of similar incidents involving various brands with a similar digital touchpad that controls the oven, such as [REDACTED], Frigidaire, and others. I found a contact personÃÂs name and email address at Electrolux, which owns Frigidaire. The contactÃÂs name was [REDACTED]. 

I have been negotiating with [REDACTED] since July 9, 2011. I first asked him to replace my stove; he refused. Then, after I said I would report Electrolux to this and other agencies and also to take my story to the local TV stations, he agreed to replace the stove. I accepted delivery of a new unit on 9/24/11. However, I have not had the unit installed.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an oven malfunction, but there was no injury reported, only property damage and inconvenience.

incident_description: The consumer says that the unit did not complete and turn off.  She says during the heating cycle it stayed on heat and overheated.  In order to turn it off she had to cut off the circuit breaker.  The consumer says it melted the basket for knives and forks.  It also melted a heavy plastic glass.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told her the dishwasher was not under recall.  The consumer says a large spoon is glued to the heating element.  The product is similar in brand and hazard as listed in Release #11-022.  Her model and serial number are not included in the recall.
justification: The incident involved overheating and property damage (melted items), but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I reported the first exploding pie plate to Anchor Hocking about three years ago. I was using the pie plate for the first time for Thanksgiving Dinner. After removing the pie from the oven and letting it cool on a wire rack, my sister was moving the pie plate to a table for serving. Before she could set it down, it exploded all over the table. Glass was everywhere, including in the mouths of my curious two 4 month old miniature poodles. Other than worrying about glass in the food, my main concern at that time was to let Anchor Hocking know that there was a problem in the hope that it wouldn't happen to others. Anchor Hocking kindly forwarded me a replacement pie plate and a set of very nice drinking glasses after that report. At that time I assumed that this explosion was a fluke or manufacturing flaw. I haven't thought much about it since. 

Fast forward to two days ago. I had stored the replacement pie plate that was kindly sent to me by Anchor Hocking in a basket under my kitchen island with other specialty items that I rarely use. I had forgotten that it was there. About two weeks ago, I heard a loud crash in the night and went to investigate in case a picture had fallen off the wall. I couldn't find anything. The next day, I found my now three year old poodle chewing on a chunk of glass. I couldn't figure out where it had come from. Very mysterious. Then last night I was cleaning and opened the basket that contained the pie plate. I  have photographs to show what happened that are attached to this report. The bottom line is that it had exploded in the basket. 

What was so unusual about this is: (1) It's never been used and (2) It's been sitting undisturbed in a basket in an air conditioned house for about 2 years. Occasionally I have the windows open but I live near Washington D.C. and the temperature in the house never gets above about 80 degrees. If it's hotter, I put on the air conditioner. No one else lives in my house so no one was knocking the basket around or scratching the glass. My dogs only weigh about 8 pounds so they aren't knocking into it either. This was a spontaneous explosion. Very scary!
justification: The incident involved exploding pie plates causing glass to scatter, but no injuries were reported, only potential risk to pets and property.

incident_description: Last night I heard a noise , I thought was coming from the electrical fuse panel box area, and smelt a burning wire smell.  I have had off and on problems where the unit would beep and experience a power failure.  The unit is plugged into a surge protected outlet.  This morning, my adult son was microwaving a [REDACTED] pizza, when the unit let out a plume of smoke.  He immediately shut off the unit, but, also complained that his lungs felt like they were burning from the smoke.  After reading other owner problems, I checked the grill area of the unit, and found that the burner area is all burnt, with a black and brown color burnt appearance, along with a black burn area where the screw is at the white attachment that holds the grill at the top of the unit.
justification: The incident involved a plume of smoke causing lung irritation, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The recurring electrical issues and burning smell suggest this is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Maytag Dishwasher caught fire.  Smoke soot and heat came out the top of the door.
