incident_description:
All of the appliances I own are Whirlpool branded.  I have chosen each product based upon consumer reports and the long-standing reputation of these brands.  I depend upon the reliability and safety these products for my family and families that rent their housing from me.
In a triplex I own, I had a Magic Chef refrigerator in the middle unit.  This triplex is home to three young families, one of whom brought a baby home from the hospital last week.  On Sunday, my tenant called to let me know that he came home to find his refrigerator on fire.  Needless to say, he was alarmed and frightened but he was able to pull the refrigerator from the wall and unplug the unit which, luckily, extinguished the fire.
A responsible landlord, I replaced the refrigerator immediately.    Upon inspection of the damaged refrigerator, it is immediately apparent that the fire began in the relay that cycles the compressor on and off.  In an internet search to find a new relay, I came across CSPS Recall # 09-322.  The hazard prompting the recall is an electrical failure in this relay that can cause overheating with 23 reports of relay ignition. From the CSPC website:
Description: The recall includes certain MaytagÃÂ®, Magic ChefÃÂ®, Performa by MaytagÃÂ® and CrosleyÃÂ® brand side-by-side and top freezer refrigerators. The affected refrigerators were manufactured in black, bisque, white and stainless steel. They have model and serial numbers printed on a label located on the top middle or left upper side of the refrigerator liner and have the following model and serial number combinations:
 	Serial Numbers ENDING with	AND Model Numbers BEGINNING with
Side by Side
Refrigerators	CN, CP, YY, YZ	MZ
Top Freezer
Refrigerators	CA, CC, CE, CG, ZB, ZD, ZF, ZH	CT15G4, CTB152, CTL151, CTM152,
CTN151, MTB195, MTB215, MTB245,
MTF195, MTF215, PTB155, PTB175,
PTB195, PTB215

My model number is:  CTL1511GEW
My serial number is:  22887591CG

As you can see from the highlighted portions, I thought I could safely assume that my refrigerator was part of the expanded recall.   I called the recall hotline and was told that my refrigerator was NOT covered by the recall and that there was nothing that Maytag would do for me.  I was not satisfied with this answer and asked to speak with the safety department.  The customer service agent (I use this term loosely) was not only rude but defamatory towards my tenant, saying that it was hearsay that the refrigerator caught on fire.  Further, she claimed that this refrigerator was not covered under the recall and the minimum she would do is send a technician over to see if it was the relay that caught on fire.  If it was, they would review the claim but there would be no guarantee that they would fix it even if the relay was the ignition point of the fire.  

I find this completely unacceptable.  There are three families that are in close proximity to this refrigerator.  Had the tenant not come home when he did, the results could have been disastrous, families destroyed.  

I understand that products fail; this is a part of life.  What I do not understand, is how Maytag is unwilling to fix the part recalled voluntarily by its own corporation.  I did not ask for repair costs of the smoke damage.  I did not ask for replacement of the food lost in the refrigerator.  I only asked that the refrigerator be repaired.  

I have spent $600 to uphold the commitment I made to my tenants.  It seems only fair that Whirlpool uphold is promise to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator fire with no reported injuries, but potential for severe consequences if not promptly addressed.

incident_description:
I was making dinner in the oven of my Jenn-Air range. The circuit breaker flipped. I turned it back on and the oven appeared to be functioning. I then received an error message ID 11 which was not in the hand-book. I tried cancelling the oven and it would not shut-off. It not only would not shut-off it began to heat up beyond the 350 degrees it was set for. The oven appeared to be off as the display was blank. I only noticed it was not off because I could still see the flame in the bottom of the oven. I called the Fire Department. They shut off the gas and electricity  to the stove. My appliance serviceman said that the oven had a manufacturers defect. The ignitor wire had frayed and ground itself on the oven wall. He replaced the ignitor wire and turned the stove on. The problem still existed and he said the circuit board was fried as well. I had him disconnect the oven and I contacted Jenn-Air. They opened an investigation. I want you to be aware of this problem in case they do not do anything to warn people of the existence of this problem. If I had left the house or not checked the flame, my house would have been on fire. The model number of this range is JGS8750BDB, serial number is 13664615LR. I bought the range in 2007 so it is only 4 years old. 
Please contact me if you have any further questions. Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

The oven had been on 350 degrees.  Glass was all over the inside of the oven and oven door.  Despite trying to clean it up well, some thin shards must have fallen on the floor and the next day cut my foot.  As these pieces of glass were reddish tinged (they are cranberry colored) it was impossible for me to extract the shard, and necessitated my having it looked at by an EMT.  After looking on-line, it is clear that Corning Visions cookware should be pulled from every cabinet and shelf as I feel lucky to not have had shard shooting across the room lacerating my limbs.  This is horribly dangerous stuff.  I had to take my husband out to dinner as we had nothing left in the house and our dinner was ruined.  The bill came to $48.12.

incident_description:

incident_description:
I utilized the Westek mechanical electric timer for operating a resistive heater.  The Westek timer is Item #TM77DHB listed with the CSA certification lab on file #227259.  The timer has a mechanical on/off feature and is rated for 1875W restistive load (1250W tungsten load).  The timer was utilized with a Delonghi Heat machine with a maximum power consumption rating of 1500W electric.  

After about 6 months of regular use, I noticed one morning a smell of burning plastic.  The area of the timer near the prongs was beginning to melt.  The item was grossly overheated and had begun to melt onto the underlying power strip, a UL listed power strip rated at 1800W resistive load.  The item was almost too hot to touch, and the plastic left a melted/charred region around the prongs.  It appears a serious fire was narrowly averted.

The company has asked me to return the timer to them, but I am able to share it for examination with the CPSC before returning it.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting of the timer, narrowly averting a serious fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Last week, a huge "fire ball" - 3 to 4 inches large shot our of the electrical outlet while I had 2 appliances plugged in:  my coffee maker and my Capresso coffee grinder.  I switched outlets and continued making and grinding coffee.  I taped over the outlet from which the fireball came.

Two days later, I again had both appliances plugged in to another outlet.  The coffee maker was running. The grinder was not running, but it was plugged in.  A huge spark came out of the outlet and hit my jacket.  At that point, I pulled everything out of the outlet and we turned off the breakers.

I called the Scarsdale Fire Dept.  The Fire Dept examined the outlets and breakers and saw nothing unusual.  They questioned whether an applicance may have been at fault.

When the electrician came, he too examined the outlets and wiring.  He said everything was normal.  He thought there may have been an unusual power surge.  When he proceeded to test the 2 applicances:  the coffee maker and the coffee grinder, the grinder did not work in one outlet. He looked at the grinder and thought the plug may have been faulty.  At that point he saw that, at the point wheree the cord connects to the grinder, the rubber had worn away and the wiring was completely exposed.  

The cord is intended to be wrapped into a groove  at
 the base of the grinder and evidently, little by little the rubber wore away exposing the wires.  I think the grinder is about 2-3 years old. The electrician said that there should have been a piece of protective rubber at the point where the cord meets the unit

The Grinder is Capresso Model 503.
I emailed Capressor yesterday and have not received a response yet.
As I could have been seriously burned, or this could have started a fire, I am alerting you.
justification: The incident involved sparks and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The faulty grinder cord suggests possible recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description: Handle separated from coffee carafe during use.  Internal PLASTIC nut had broken into 3 pieces.
justification: The handle breaking is an incident but there is no mention of injury, fitting severity level 2. The high frequency suggests occurrence likelihood is almost certain.

incident_description: The consumer says the oven was off when she heard three loud popping sound.  The consumer said the glass exploded forward and outward in many large and small pieces.  The glass that exploded was the outside pane of the window on the oven door.  The consumer said the unit was off and she hadn't used it for nearly twenty hours.  The consumer says that she contacted the manufacturer's corporate office who only offered to send out a technician for a fee.  The consumer contacted the retailer who offered the same remedy.
justification: The oven glass exploded, but there was no mention of injury or death, only property damage.

incident_description:
While baking a dish on the rack inside of the oven the rack falls. The consumer indicated that no matter the size and or weight of the dish it falls.  She had a service technician from the form come out on 9/9/2011 who advised the consumer that the oven cavity had expanded and a new cavity is need.

The consumer indicated that the firm will not order the part unless she pays out of pocket because the appliance no longer falls under a warranty. The consumer indicated that the oven could potentially poses as a fire hazard if the rack does not hold the hold the dishes.

The consumer stated that it is both racks inside of the oven. She will not honor any repairs because it is a safety issue and she does not feel obligated to ay out of pocket. 

No repairs have been made and she has discontinued the use of the oven.
justification: The incident involves a rack falling in the oven, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the right hand front burner will turn itself from low to high.  He says that in order to shut if off he would have to push the knob in and turn it.  The consumer says that he has no other issues with the unit.  The hazard is similar to Release # 09-333.  The consumer's model number is out of range of the recall.  He says he has never had to cut off the circuit breaker to turn the unit off.
justification: The burner turning itself from low to high poses a potential hazard, but there is no report of injury or death, and the consumer can still control it by pushing the knob in.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was using one of the rear burners for approximately 3-4 mins on the Gas Range she noticed that the cap of the oven for the control panel started to melt.  She contacted the repair service and a technician was sent out to replaced the part but she noticed that the part was plastic, she visited the store and discovered that the caps were not steel as she thought.

Consumer stated that she is concerned that since this part is made from plastic it poses a potential risk of melting again and causing a fire.

Consumer feels that this is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a melting plastic part but no injury or fire occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The consumer says the front right burner will turn on without turning off.  The consumer says she has had the relay board replaced in May of 2010 by retailer.  She has had it replaced again in July of 2010.  The consumer says the problem still persists so she stopped using it.  The product and hazard are similar to recall 09-333 but her model and serial are out of range of the recall.
justification: The burner turns on without turning off, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I'm going to leave out the details that are not life threatening, seals and crisper covers breaking and falling off.  About 2 years ago, I opened the fridge to make breakfast, only to find the interior of the fridge EXTREMELY warm.  The unopened package of hot dogs were cooked through.  The roast, almost at the bottom of the fridge, was cooked through.  I found the two light bulbs on top were hot and melted their protective cover.  The casings around the bulbs were charred from the excesive heat.  It seems the lights were staying on even while the doors were closed.  I unscrewed them so they could not light up or get hot any more.  Since that time the fridge has been getting progressively worse.  Now it will stop working all together and the digital lights on the front will show 88 instead of the correct temperature.  Other times it will freeze everything in the fridge and will again show 88s across the board.  Each time it eithers tops working or gets super cold, it beeps.  The only way we can get it to stop and correct itself is by unplugging it for a while, then plugging it back in.  At first it didn't happen too often, but it has gotten progressively worse.  Now we have to unplug it several times a week and just recently had to start unplugging it several times a day.  I am not the only consumer who has had these problems.  I found the trick of unplugging and plugging back in on the internet, where many other LG owners were having the same problems and sharing.  LG has recalled many models, but this one does not seem to be on their list.  Even though, this fridge is just as bad, if not worse than the ones they have recalled.  Seems outrageous that they are not taking responsibility for selling a defective appliance, an appliance that is a fire hazard.

It worries me when I'm at work, not knowing if it's going to overheat while the house is empty.  Or when we are sleeping.
justification: The fridge overheating and melting components poses a fire hazard, which could lead to injury. The issue occurs frequently, requiring unplugging several times a day.

incident_description:
The consumer stated her toaster oven poses a fire hazard similar to the toaster oven cited in recall release 11-265. Her toaster has the same model but is from a different series number. The style is regular pop up toaster oven. The toaster oven has 2 slots for bread. The consumer stated that her toaster oven doesnÃÂt pop up on its own the consumer has to press cancel to make the toaster stop. This occurs every single time except if the toaster is on a light setting. The toaster was on for roughly a minute. 

The consumer was using both burners at the time of the incident. The product does not show any signs of damage. The consumer's home has not been damaged by the product. The consumer has yet to call the fire department about the product. The consumer still uses the product but has to monitor it more closely. The consumer called the firm and cannot reach them as the number does not seem to be working. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The consumer has not been harmed by the product.
justification: The toaster oven poses a fire hazard and malfunctions regularly, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description: On 9/17/2011 I used a Pyrex casserole dish to bake a ham at 325 degrees.  About one hour after the dish was removed from the oven I was loading it into the dishwasher.  As I was leaning down to put soap into the dishwasher the dish suddenly shattered near my face.  The shattering sent glass flying as far as 8 feet away.  Luckily no one was hurt.  I believe this shattering is the same type that has been in the news.  This dish could easily have been sitting on my table with my young children nearby when it shattered.  Please look into this matter promptly to keep consumers safe.  I feel this is an unsafe product that needs to be removed from the market.  I have also contacted Pyrex to let them about the incident.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex dish shattering near the user's face, but luckily no one was hurt. The potential for injury was high, especially with children nearby.

incident_description:
August 18, 2011, I was finishing up cleaning after dinner and I put my "wash by hand" wooden handle knives into the large 8 cup Pyrex Measuring Cup which I regualarly use as a mixing bowl or prep bowl which I had used earlier in the day. I put the knives into the cup point down, put a little liquid detergent, and filled with warm tap water. Then as I turned my back I heard an awful explosion sound and was totally astounded to see the cup had shattered in the sink. Fortunately, most of the shards were in the granite sink. The noise brought my husband out from another room and the 2 of us cleaned up the hundreds of pieces of glass (of course, not thinking to take a photo or save some glass....why would we?

For days I muttered about not understanding how that could happen and bemoaning the fact that for the second time I had lost the same favorite kitchen item. This one had replaced one I had for years "exactly" like it but had dropped a few years ago and it broke on impact. I used that measuring bowl several times a week for pancake batter, mixing meatloaf, making jam, itc. I would replace it again if I could.

Then two weeks after the incident my husband handed me the Consumer Reports and said, " Here, hon. You should read this." It was the article in the Oct. 2011 Consumer Reports page 40 titled "Shattered Glass." I was astounded that others had similar experiences! Then I got on the internet and did some more investigating. It seems the only way I can replace my favorite old measuring bowl made of borosilicate glass is to find one at a garage sale that is "pre" soda lime construction. My kitchen is full of Pyrex items, some 50 years old. I have never had any similar experience except for breakage upon impact. I was not injured but I feel this is a dangerous product  and people using it are taking a risk.
justification: The incident involved a Pyrex measuring cup shattering, but no injuries were reported, only property damage.

incident_description: Brand new GE gas range.  Several knobs on top burners will allow gas to flow without the igniter spark.  Had the range delivered September 12, 2011.  Had this problem.  Returned the range and a replacement was installed.  Same type of problem but with different burner locations.
justification: Gas flow without ignition poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Knob on GE Built in Cooktop made large popping noises. Went to see what the noise was. There were flames and black smoke coming from the last control knob on the cooktop. Had to call 911 and the fire department had to come out. The cooktop had not been used for at least 2 days. This happened on its OWN. No one had touched it. This is a major safety concern for anyone who has this cooktop. Luckily, I was home to call the fire department. It could have damaged my home or worse. It could have happened while my family, with 3 small children slept. I can't even image. Flames and smoke should NOT be coming out of a control knob! Especially by itself. This cooktop needs to be recalled right away.
This is Model # JGP328CEC2CC. Serial # is: FD778763Q
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the cooktop, posing a significant safety risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Our KitchenAid Dishwasher Model KUDS01FLSS5 purchased 11/2004 caught on fire while running. We heard some loud "popping" noises and went to the Kitchen to investigate. The dishwasher was smoking. Sparks and flames were coming from the upper right side of the door. We pressed the cancel button but the unit kept running and smoke/sparks/flames kept coming from the unit. We turned off the circuit breaker for the dishwasher and the unit shut down. Damage was limited to the dishwasher. A service technician was sent to our house and he determined that the units control panel circuit board had failed and caught on fire. This issue, to my surprise, DOES NOT appear to be isolated. Many cases are documented at kitchaidfire.com. This is a very dangerous situation.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing sparks and flames, but no injuries or deaths were reported. The issue is documented in multiple cases, indicating a recurring problem.

incident_description: toaster was on fire and the whole casing melted on kitchen counter while putting muffin to toast on4/25/11. I brought this to the product claim dept attention on 5/5/11, took me a while to get the dept who is responsible . they did not have good faith in accepting the claim and deny compensation to me.  on 8/9/11, i refile the claim to them continue the issue was never address and ignored.  this product if not watch out could set the place on fire and toaster was not suppose to be 'supervised' monitored while toasting items in there. if this product can't be used unattended, is not safe to be in the market.  if you wish to see the full claim supporting documents, please let me know how to give you the full detail of my claim.
justification: The toaster caught fire and melted, but no injury or death was reported. The incident suggests a possible risk if the product is used unattended.

incident_description: We had recently purchased a Frigidaire Gallery range.  My 10 months old son received 3rd degree burns by opening the storage drawer and reaching inside 30 minutes after the oven had been turned off.  The portion of the stove frame that the drawer face rests against was found the be extremely hot.  The drawer is not a "warming drawer," but rather a storage drawer that does not have a locking mechanism.
justification: The incident resulted in 3rd degree burns to a child, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the design flaw allowing access to hot surfaces without a locking mechanism.

incident_description: The consumer says that she was using crockpot when she went to lift up the lid.  She says the lid detached from the handle as she lifted it up.  It fell onto a cushion, so the glass didn't break.  The consumer says that it was also very hot and poses a significant safety issue.  She contacted the manufacturer who sent her a replacement lid but she is afraid to use it.  The consumer says that the manufacturer is very helpful but is concerned that they won't inform consumers of the issue.
justification: The lid detached but fell onto a cushion without causing injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her microwave is a potential fire hazard. The consumer was sitting about 9 feet from her microwave. When her husband removed a bowl of soup from the microwave after 45 seconds. Then consumer closed the door of the microwave and heard a humming as if the microwave was still on but the light inside of the microwave was off, giving no indication that the microwave was off. 

The consumer tried to turn off microwave by shutting it off with the digital touchpad would not respond to her command of turning it off. The consumer had to unplug it from the outlet to shut it off. The consumer stated that she has an above the range. The consumer has yet to call the retailer about this. The consumer called the firm today and was told that the product was not on recall and in order to have it fixed it would have to come at her expense, or company would pay 20% on a new Maytag microwave.  Consumer refused Maytag's offer.

The consumer stated that the that the product got so hot that it melted some chocolate candy that was in the cupboard next to the microwave. The product caused no apparent damage to her home. The consumer opted not to call the fire department at the time of the incident. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. Consumer is worried that her husband, who is hard-of-hearing, may not have hard or smelled microwave and gone to bed.  This would have put them both in jeopardy of death by fire.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned but caused no injury or damage, though it posed a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: The consumer says she smelled smoke, and saw flames coming out of the dishwasher.  Her husband cut off the circuit breaker.  The consumer says when she opened the door, water spread all over her kitchen floor.  The consumer says the unit was not on for more than five minutes before the incident.  The consumer says that when the unit caught fire, the dishwasher was still on.  She contacted the retailer who said they would send out a technician for a fee.  The consumer says that all the electrical components are completely burned.  The consumer's model number is just outside the range listed in Release # 05-123.
justification: The incident involved a fire and water damage but no reported injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the model number being just outside the recalled range, indicating a known issue.

incident_description: We purchased a Kenmore Electric Range(Model # 790.9422340C, Serial # Vf73781985 ) in October 16th, 2007 at Sears in Fresno, California.  The range is not a smooth top so it is not part of the recall for smooth tops, but it is a fire hazard just like the smooth tops because one particular burner(right rear back)burns at a high temperature even though it is set to a lower temperature.  Several times what I was cooking burned or cooked too fast until I noticed the bright red burner.  I believe that the first time this happened I just turned it off and the next time the burner was okay.  I believe this must  have happened about a year after we purchased the stove, because we didn't call Sears thinking that it would no longer be under  warranty.  The burner kept doing this on and off to this day and eventually I started avoiding using this burner.  I just lived with the situation until I read that the the Sears electric smooth tops were being recalled because they were a fire hazard.  When I read what the smooth top range was doing, it was the same problem as our stove.    We checked the recall list hoping that our range was there, but no luck.  I  called the CPSC  line  to check if they knew if our range was also being recalled and they said no.  When I talked to Sears, they told me that we would have to pay for repairs or purchase a maintenance agreement.  This smacks of blackmail to me.  I feel Sears should be the one putting pressure on their manufacturer to make sure that their products are safe, and it should be forced to remedy all ranges that show the fire hazard problem.
justification: The burner operates at a higher temperature than set, causing food to burn, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Kenmore electric glass top range /oven model 79097423901.   Purchased April 2010 from Sears.   Turned oven on to heat to 350 degrees.   Oven was still in process of rising in temperature to 350 when I heard a popping sound followed by a shattering sound hitting the floor.   Walked in to find outside glass panel on oven door shattered into a million pieces, mostly on the ground and shot out from the oven.   Some sections remained in the door frame, looking like they had been pushed from the inside out.   Nothing hit the door, the door was not hot; it seemed to just spontaneously explode.   Sears technical service said they've never heard of this and there are no recalls.   When I searched online, I found hundreds of reports of the same type incidents with Kenmore and [REDACTED] (I believe my model is actually made for Kenmore by [REDACTED]).   Sears will not repair, not investigate, nor do anything with this issue.
justification: The incident involved the oven door glass shattering, but no injuries were reported. Online reports indicate this is a known issue, suggesting a possible but not certain likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Kenmore refrigerator model # 106.41512101 was producing a smell of burning plastic and metal and woke us up on Saturday morning at 5 AM due to the odor. The refrigerator was unplugged and the back panel was removed to discover that the starter device to the compressor looked as if it had almost caught fire. The part was burnt and the contacts had welded themselves on to the compressor due to the heat generated. The capacitor contacts also showed signs of soot that plugs into this module but was not damaged. The problem I experienced is very similar to the one listed here: http://www.retrotechnology.com/aux/fridge.html
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and potential fire hazard, but no actual fire, injury, or death occurred.

incident_description: The broiler in our oven came on by itself and overheated the stove. (apparently from a short circuit in the control board).  I immediately flip the breaker off because the broiler would not turn off. If we had not have noticed when we did, it could possibly lead to a fire, and who knows what else? The range is a Kenmore, model 790.95661100; serial number VF1313131372 purchased at Sears outlet store Orlando, Florida on October 5, 2001.
justification: The broiler malfunctioned but was promptly addressed, posing no immediate injury or death, though it had potential for a fire.

incident_description: I have a Samsung refrigerator, model #RS2630SH.  I have owned this product for approximately 3 years.  Several months ago, the refrigerator started making a noise intermittently.  As time went on the noise started lasting longer. I noticed after opening the frezzer door that the magneted strip around the frezzer was holding heat and hot to the touch.  Last week my wife informed me she burnt her forearm while getting meat out of the frezzer.  I investigated and found the entire area surrounding the frezzer is very hot. I am concerned that this refrigerator may short out and start a fire.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the forearm, and there is a potential for further harm due to the overheating issue.

incident_description: I have a 2 family home.  In my tenants apartment I have a Jenn Air range which exhausts fumes via a blower in the range and ductwork below the range.  If the range burners are set to a very low flame the ranges exhaust fan is strong enough to blow out the flame -- resulting in unburned gas being emitted into the living space.  This is a potentially hazardous condition.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous condition with potential for gas emission, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The dishwasher was in the off position, when the consumer's wife noticed a burning odor.  The dishwasher had been used earlier in the day, but had been off for several hours at the time of the incident.  

The spray arm had melted as well as portions of the racks.  Some of the items that were washed also melted.  Damage was limited to the items inside of the dishwasher.

The consumer estimates that the dishwasher is used approximately 5 times a week.

The consumer has already replaced the dishwasher with a different brand.  The dishwasher was not listed in any of the CPSC recalls.
justification: The incident caused damage to the dishwasher and its contents but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Glass Cookware - 15"X10" - Anchor Ovenware Baking Dish

A few years ago I had a glass cooking dish EXPLODE in my kitchen. I had just finished removing a turkey from the oven. I placed the glassware between the four burners on the stove and lifted the bird out. The pan contained hot boiling juices so I placed the dish on the divider in the sink. I turned to get something to pour the liquid into when it sounded like a gunshot. The 15"X10" glass baking dish turned into small toothpick shards that covered my entire 10' X 4' kitchen. The pieces were extremely sharp and small. Fortunately, all the boiling liquid went down the sink and I had just stepped away so there were no injuries. I remember thinking how lucky I was that this did not occur as I was lifting the turkey out of the oven!

I mishandled the glassware - placing a heated bowl onto a cool sink can cause rapid cooling - BUT the glass exploded like no other glass I have ever seen. I bought the glassware after watching my mother cook with similar pans she bought in the 60's and she never had an issue ... in fact I use her glassware to cook with now.

I read Consumer Reports about the glass bakeware problem and I wanted to share my experience.
justification: The glassware exploded but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are rare but possible due to thermal shock.

incident_description: Two thick rubber type oven mittens or pot holders (red) bought at Costco in Sterling, VA.  The gloves cracked between thumb and finger when picking up a hot frying pan handle.  The hot handle slid into the crack and burn my skin between thumb and finger.  It hurt a lot and blistered the skin.  I dropped the pan and hot contents all over the kitchen floor, over my shoes, sock and pant leg.  A few months later, the same thing happened to the other glove.  I contacted Costco and the rep there said they had not received any other complaints about this product.
justification: The incident caused a burn injury with blistering, and the same issue recurred months later, indicating a potential product defect.

incident_description:
I was making chicken parmesan, frying the pieces of chicken  in a cast iron pan on top of the stove and then put the browned pieces of chicken in a 9x13 pyrex glass pan.  My oven was preheated to 350 degrees.
I then poured a jar of spagetti sauce over the chicken and topped with cheese and set it in the oven to heat and melt the cheese.  After about 5 minutes, I heard an explosion in my oven.
When I opened it, I found the pan had split into many pieces with shards of glass everwhere inside my oven.  I had to use my vacuum to get them all out.
justification: The incident involved a glass pan exploding in the oven, causing a mess but no reported injuries.

incident_description: A brand new 13x9 Pyrex soda lime glass pan was used to make eggplant parm.  The meal had finished cooking and was set next on a rack to cool when it burst into hundreds of pieces.  Some of the pieces of glass flew on my girlfriends feet who was standing a foot away from the "explosion."  I was in the next room with the television on when i heard the loud bang.  I heard the loud bang first and then a scream coming from the kitchen so I bolted up to see what had happened.  Upon entering the kitchen I noticed many pieces of glass scattered all over the counter top and floor, blood on my girlfriends feet and food all over the floor and counter.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (blood on girlfriend's feet) due to glass shattering, but no death occurred.

incident_description: My Whirlpool refrigerator (Model number ED25GWXFW00)(Ser# SK2331678) had smoke coming from the back bottom of the unit.  I unplugged the unit and removed the lower back panel to find the Start Relay was smoking.  After a while, when the part stopped smoking and the smoke dissipated, I removed the part to find there was a short inside the part.  I called an appliance parts and repair shop for a replacement part.  When I picked up the replacement part, the repairman informed me that this is a common problem with the Whirlpool Refrigerators with these older Start Relays, and that they have been known to catch fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric range model no. 790.93751, serial no. VF20512549  
I shut off the oven after use around 10pm last night, but oven continued to heat up.  Would not shut off even though displays were off.  Only way to shut off was to unplug the range.  
Serious risk of fire/hazard and could easily gone unnoticed because there was nothing on to indicate that the oven continued to heat.  I was very fortunate to have discovered the problem before it was too late.  It was after midnight and I happened to go down to the kitchen for some water when I felt extreme heat as I stood next to the range.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: While removing a 350 degree stoneware pan from the oven the handle broke off, the other handle was broken on one of two attachment locations.
justification: The handle broke off a hot pan, which could lead to burns or spills, but no injury was reported in the description.

incident_description:
GE Coffee and Spice Grinder model #111338

I bought this item in 09/2011 at Walmart. I only used it twice.  Once the second day I bought it and today on 09/20/2011 at approximately 7:00am.  After putting a small amount of coffee beans in the grinder top and pressing the pulse button I began to smell smoke after about 2 seconds.  After another second I actually began to SEE smoke.  I looked near the plug at the base (where the smoke was originating)  and plug connected to the machine began to smoke and burn.  

This is a NEW product and could have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and the product was new, suggesting a possible manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
My GE refrigerator caught on fire. Model Number GSH25JSRF SS. 

My husband woke up at 12:30 a.m. and smelled burning plastic. He looked at the back of the fridge and a two inch flame was coming from a part connected to the condenser. My husband says the fan was working fine. He unplugged the fridge and put out the fire. Thank the Lord my husband woke up. I'm having a baby in a week. We have a seven year old daughter, a cat, and a dog. We bought the fridge about 5-6 yrs ago. It was an expensive model. It was a good fridge then this just happened.
justification: The refrigerator caught fire, but the fire was extinguished without injury or death.

incident_description:
Purchased my range on 12-17-2007, and picked up in Jan. 2008 from Sears. Prior to 11-24-2008 the stove (eyes) started staying on at the highest temperature even when turned down. My husband called Frigidaire on this date and was told to turn the main breaker off and then back on. Upon doing this the stove worked correctly for several months, then started acting up again. I spoke with Frigidaire and Sears several times after this and was told "Sorry it is out of warrenty and you can pay to have fixed". On 10-16-2009 I reached E. Cooko unit 94.22 at Frigidaire and was told that Ace Appliance and Repair would fix at no charge, after waiting a week, I never heard back and contacted Ace and was told they were never contacted by Frigidaire. So I continued to call Frigidaire and was told nothing could be done, my last conversation was with [REDACTED]  on 10-23-09. My stove eyes continue to stay on high after using the stove to this day. I am able to turn the eye off and listen for a click and then it will start working correctly for a short time. My stove is a Frigidaire Gallery Series Model # GLEFS79DSL Seriel VF74969984. It was not on the recall list but is and has been posing the same fire hazard as the ones that were recalled. I do not understand how it could not have been covered under warrenty when Frigudaire was contacted prior to 1 year. Also do not understand why my Model was not recalled when it posed the same fire hazard as the ones recalled and this was told to Sears and Frigidaire. 
Contact dates : 11-24-08 to Frigidaire,  10-13-09 to Sears [REDACTED] 10-16-11 Sears Mgr.[REDACTED],  10-16-10 Customer Solutions [REDACTED], 10-23-09 Frigidaire [REDACTED] given [REDACTED],  10-23-09 One Source [REDACTED] and Sears. Spoke with [REDACTED] at One Source and she made a case [REDACTED]. I also do not know how that Sears was able to tell me over the phone without looking at my stove that parts and repair were going to cost $129.00. Seems to me that they already knew that this stove posed a problem. I finally gave up, hoping that one day it would be recalled also, since I told everyone of the people that I spoke with that it was a fire hazard.
justification: The stove malfunction poses a fire hazard but no actual fire or injury has been reported.

incident_description:
Stove controls on side of unit can be accidently turned on without notice, or ignition of flame, gas is then spread into home without detection. 

I left my house to go to the store at night, my mother and brother were sleeping. When I left there was NO odor of natural gas in the house. Upon returning, the entire home reaked of the rotten egg odor that is placed in natural gas. I immediately opened all the windows and doors then woke up my family to make sure everyone was safe.  Had I not gone to the store and went to bed this could have turned out very differently.
justification: The incident involved gas leakage without injury, but with potential for severe consequences if undetected.

incident_description: On September 14, 2011, I took out the carafe of the Cuisinart coffee maker  DTC 975BKN, after it finished brewing, the top plastic part separated from the metal base and the hot coffee fell unto my Right foot scorching it and causing second degree burns.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description: HOMEOWNER STARTED HER ASKO DISHWASHER, MODEL 1595, HEARD POPPING NOISES FROM KITCHEN, FIRE ALARM ACTIVATED IN THE HOUSE. HOMEOWNER WENT TO THE KITCHEN AND SAW SMOKE BILLOWING FROM THE TOP OF THE DISHWASHER THEN FLAMES BEGAN. HOMEOWNER USED A DRY CHEMICAL EXTINGUISHER TO EXTINGUISH THE FIRE.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was extinguished without injury, and dishwasher fires are uncommon.

incident_description:
On September 19, 2011, my GE Microwave Model EMO3000cbb02 sustained fire damage. The unit had been used for 30 seconds to heat a child's milk, and then sat idle for 5 minutes. At that time, there was multiple "popping" noises followed by a "buzzing" noise, multiple flashes, and then the area of the front plastic shelf support burst into flames. Luckily we were at home at the time. I am a former firefighter, and was able to disconnect the unit from it's power source, and the flame ceased. I immediately took a photo of the unit's damage with my cell phone. I believe this incident is similar to one that was reported to this office in June of this year report number 20110617-F3ABE-2147478129.
 
Subsequent photos taken of damage and manufacturer's label inside the unit.
justification: The microwave caught fire but was quickly extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no harm to people.

incident_description: I have a 6 month old wall oven, Bosch Model HBL5450UC/06, Seriel 900600424.  The very first time I turned on the self cleaning feature, I heard a cracking sound about 10 minutes after the start of the process.  I looked but did not see anything.  Ten minutes later, there was a very loud crashing sound.  When I looked into the oven through the door, I could see that  the interior glass of the oven had exploded into very small pieces, filling the floor of the oven.  A few pieces of the shattered glass somehow came out onto the kitchen floor in front of the oven. I called the manufacturer and followed their instructions to turn off the cleaning cycle and to turn off the power at the circuit breaker.
justification: The incident involved the oven glass shattering but no injury was reported, indicating a non-injury incident with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description: My Cuisinart Coffee Maker model DCC-1200 is about a year old.  On 9/17/11, after brewing a pot of coffee, it started smoking and giving off a heavy burning smell.  It got worse to the point I had to unplug it, put it in the sink and spray water on it and up under the bottom where the motor vents are.  It could have developed into a very dangerous situation if I had not been home.
justification: The incident involved smoking and a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was controlled without further escalation.

incident_description: Our Kenmore oven (9268) had a loud mini-explosive pop and there was a burning smell. Then the oven stopped working but the cooktop was OK. We purchased it around 2004. I'm sure you hear this all the time but our previous stove had lasted for over 20 years. The repairman showed us the burn marks around the part that went, and asked if we wanted to replace the stove with a new one. He said the repair would cost over $300 which was over half of the cost of the stove. We were wondering if this is the normal way a stove should act or if this is a hazard. Have you had other reports of this? Thanks for your consideration.
justification: The incident involved a loud pop, burning smell, and oven failure, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I bought the LGEF3043KF Frigidaire stove one year and 16 days ago. It has always heated very strange. Simmer will suddenly start burning on the top burners. Last night, the oven would not shut off. I started looking online, and there are a lot of reports about this. It sounds like a short in the circuit, but it does not kick the home breaker. It is a fire hazard. There are recalls on some earlier models. Mine is just over a year old, so maybe people are not yet seeing these problems. I'm glad I did not burn the house down. Frigidaire is putting people in danger with these stoves year after year that short out and won't turn off.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death was reported. Reports suggest this issue is common with this model.

incident_description: My 13 year old daughter was using the Target Chefmate Blender to make a smoothie, the plastic pitcher came off while the blender was in motion. She received lacerations to her hand from the metal blades which were still spinning.  The liquid from the pitcher drained down into the motor causing the motor to smoke and spark until she was able to unplug blender with her uninjured hand.  There was strawberry and blood splattered all over the kitchen.  My daughter had to get many stitches in her hand, she has a scar and some sensation affected, long recovery time.  Classmates have bullied her about the accident.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations requiring stitches and a long recovery time, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but can happen with improper use or equipment failure.

incident_description:
I have GE electrical range. Yesterday it stared fire on the coil. The fireball was about one feet with sparks. My mom was scared to death. She was near to the range while incident happen. She was slightly burned on the finger while removing pan. The fire burned the cooking pan too. I turned off the circuit breaker manually.  

After cooling down, I removed the damaged coil. After cleaning up the mess, I started the circuit breaker again. I saw the burner light does not off even though all the burner switches are off.  
After the incident, I did little research on the model number, I was able to find cpsc recall Alert #04-576. http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml04/04576.html?omni_key=Ranges_and_Wall_Ovens_Recall
 
My model number JBS03BH is listed in the recall notice. When I called on the toll free number, my serial number is not listed.

I have uploaded photos of the damaged burner and cooking pan: https://picasaweb.google.com/111355744807159860536/September182011#


I would greatly appreciate if you could take necessary action. I need to have the electric range fixed ASAP. 
GE model number: JBS03B H2WH
Serial number: ZF144951P

Thanks,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fireball and sparks, causing a slight burn injury to the person involved and damage to the cooking pan.

incident_description:
The gas burners on this range turn on extremely easily. They turn on sometimes just by brushing
against them with your body or a piece of clothing, which has happened to us many times.
Often, we wouldn't know until we smelt the gas (sometimes several minutes later), unless they
ignited and then we are at the risk of being burnt. One day, when no one was home, the burner
was turned on. We think our dog turned it on by hitting it when she put her paws and head on
the counter next to the range to get a plate of food that was left there. When we got home, the
burner on the highest setting. It had scorched the counter, which was smoldering, and I am sure
if we arrived any later it would have started a fire. Since then, we have been removing the burner
dials when we are not using the range.

This is an extremely dangerous situation. We could have been hurt or killed by either the gas
escaping or a fire. I am surprised this product has not been recalled already.
justification: The incident describes a high risk of death from gas leaks or fire, and the occurrence is likely as it has happened many times and even when no one was home.

incident_description: heating plate on the coffee maker began to spark and then smoke continued when element was turned off needed to be unplugged.

incident_description:
In 2009 I purchased a Kenmore Electric Range. On September 16th, 2011the exterior glass on the range door spontaneously exploded while making dinner. It shot out several feet. Luckily, no one was hurt. I called Sears and they did not seem to be in any rush to send over a tech. Meanwhile, there is still broken glass dangling from my stove door.

I'm not sure if these incidences are related but within a few months of having the stove I called Sears to complain that when the oven self-cleaned it seemed way too hot. In fact, it peeled the laminate end of my countertop and was extremely hot to touch anywhere on the stove. In fact, it radiated heat in such a way I was afraid it was going to burn my wall. Sears sent over a technician and said it was fine. Despite this I have always contended the stove is too hot and haven't used the self cleaning option since. A few days ago, prior to the door exploding, the oven caught fire while making a desert. There was a small amount of drippings caught in a sheet of tinfoil but the stove literally ignited in flames. We had to use a fire extinguisher to kill the flame. Thankfully, I was in the kitchen and we were able to put it out fairly quickly without the kitchen catching fire.

What concerns me, is the lack of concern Sears has over this. I found a consumer complaint site online where several people complain of the same incident happening to them and Sears not willing to pay for repairs or better yet, recall the stoves. I was told Sears Canada would not pay for the service call but fortunately my local Sears store has. However, they are not willing to pay for repair.

This really concerns me and upsets me Sears seems to be so lax in all this...
justification: The incident involved a stove door exploding and an oven catching fire, but no injuries were reported. Similar complaints suggest the issue is likely to occur.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore smooth top range Model# 911.95402000, I turned on the oven to preheat it, the next thing I notice bright white sparks in the oven, and smoke coming out of it....I turn off the oven on the dial and its still sparking...so I try to put it out, its burning so hot it will not go out...after a few minutes I decided to pull out the stove and unplug it...then it finally goes out. I feel this is a real safety hazard....if I had not been home I dont know if my wife or children would have known what to do. I looked for a recall on the internet and found none, But I did find alot of people having the same problems(complaintsboard.com)....I think something needs to be done before someones house burns down, or someone get hurt. Is there some kind of a recall?...
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore Refrigerator purchased 2007 from Sears
Model 79577306600
Serial 705 MREN00580
This evening I smelled a burning electrical smell in the kitchen.  I had last opened the refrigerator 3-4 hours before and noticed nothing.   I opened the refrigerator again to find the interior roof of the refrigerator compartment melted!  The interoir lighting/control panel had almost completely separated/melted from the housing which was also extremely hot.  There had been no recent services or repairs.  No problems prior to this. 
      I was very disturbed to find several complaints online of similar issues, some resulting in home fires.  There was even a recall of what appears to be the same refrigerators from 2002.  
I was very lucky to be home when this occured. I believe this would have resulted in a fire had I not unplugged as soon as I had.   I would not want this to happen to someone else who might not catch it in time.

incident_description:
Lights stayed on in the refrigerator with doors completely closed causing a burning smell, the light sockets to turn brown as they got too hot, and causing the clear light cover to partially melt falling off.  In addition, it heated up items in the refrigerator.  The doors were completely closed and the there was no door chime going off to warn if the doors were open, but the doors were closed.  Evidently this has happened to me a couple of times before, but the refrigerator was used at a quicker interval, so other than a slight burning smell, and the light cover coming off once, the cover was able to be reinstalled.  Previously, I had wondered whether the doors were open or not, but this time, I smelled something burning before I opened the refrigerator, and since I had problems before, I inspected the doors before I opened them and they were completely closed.  Upon opening the refrigerator doors, I noticed the light sockets had turned brown from heat, the light cover lying on the shelf, and the liquid items on the shelf were warm.  It reminded me of an [REDACTED]....in my refrigerator!!!  This is a serious problem that will at some point result in a fire.

This is a Kenmore Elite French (Trio) door Refrigerator
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted light cover, browned sockets) and could lead to a fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Dear Electrolux:
You will find enclosed the controlling circuit board from my dishwasher, along with the model numberserial
number sticker affixed to the appliance by Electrolux. (Model No. PLDB998CCO, Serial No.
TH34268305) The reason that I have enclosed the board is that last Wednesday evening, August 16,
2011, the circuit board shorted out and arced at the post labeled P5 on the board. Flames began to
shoot out of the door panel of the dishwasher, and had I not been in my kitchen at the time of the
incident, able to immediately extinguish the flames and cut off the power to the unit, the repercussions
could have been terrible.
Since the dishwasher is out of warranty, I cannot say that I am surprised that the appliance failed, for
that seems the state of manufacture these days -nothing is built to last anymore. However, there is
really no excuse in my mind for the circuitry to have caused a fire in the unit. I hope that you will have
the board evaluated to try to determine the cause of the fire, so that if there is a systemic problem, you
can alert other purchasers of this model and correct the issue. In the interest of protecting other
owners of this model, I am copying the Consumer Product Safety Commission, who can determine if this
problem is widespread or of particularly acute concern.

Since we own several other Electrolux appliances, from microwave, to range to fridge, to vacuum, I hope
that this problem was indeed an anomaly and not an indication of generally poor manufacturing
standards. I am, frankly terrified to think otherwise and hope that you will afford this matter the
attention that it deserves. My family has been loyal to the Electrolux brand for many years and you
should want to keep us that way.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a short circuit in the dishwasher, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

Consumer stated that his electric oven range combo is a fire hazard. The consumer stated that he powers off the range at the dials and the digital displays appear that the range is off.  The consumer called the firm about this issue today. The would not offer assistance except send out a repairman at the consumer's expense. incident_description: The consumer says the dishwasher was on for a few minutes, black smoke started coming out of it.  The consumer says that a spark shot out of it. incident_description: This incident involves a Better Homes and Gardens Die-Cast Stand Mixer (model # 145648) purchased at Walmart. While making biscotti and mixing the dough, a screw fell into the dough. The screw is there to attach the spindle to the mixer unit. I was unaware of the screw until my wife bit into a piece of biscotti and found the screw. She was uninjured.
justification: A screw fell into the dough and was ingested without injury.

incident_description: The Vent Grille at the top of the microwave fell off of the unit in the middle of the night. About 3am I heard a loud noise from the kitchen, and discovered that the Vent Grille had just fallen right off of the unit leaving two chips out of the hardwood floor. When I looked more closely in the morning, the two tabs that secure the Vent Grille to the main body of the microwave had just broken off leaving the tab part still behind under the screw that was intended to secure the Vent Grille. I thought, "good thing nobody was standing there cooking when this broke free." Upon searching for a replacement part I discovered lots of other customers who had experienced this same failure. The part itself doesn't seem to be a critical safety piece, but if someone were standing, or worse yet cooking when this happens, I could imagine that the injuries could get fairly serious. If this were to fall on a pan handle or something on a cook top below, a person could be seriously burned.
justification: The incident caused property damage (chips in the hardwood floor) but no injury, and there is evidence of similar failures among other customers indicating a possible design flaw.

Consumer stated that she had placed the dishwasher into the wash cycle, approximately 15mins later she noticed smoke emitting from the control panel towards the corners of the unit.  She immediately open the door but it was stiil making weird noises, so she powered it off from the circuit breaker to make sure it was off.  The incident caused the plastic around the circuit board to be melted and charred.  This was the first time that this incident had ever occurred.

Consumer has removed the dishwasher from the house into the driveway to prevent any fires.

Consumer had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer is concerned that this product is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting plastic, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the panel in his refrigerator, where the refrigerator light is very hot. The consumer believes that the light stays on when the refrigerator even when the door is closed.Consumer stated that his refrigerator has not been emitting a smell of burning plastic from his refrigerator.  The consumer stated that he is not sure of the light wattage. The consumer has not been injured by the product. The consumer has opened the refrigerator since inspecting the refrigerator but can see no signs of structural damage from the outside. The consumer stated that the panel has not melted. 

 The consumer stated the product has not damaged his home or called the local fire department to inspect his product. The consumer called the firm tody and was told that the product did not fall under their known recalls and offered no further assistance. 

The consumer did independent research and found that the product had numerous reports about his same issue with similar models in recall 05-213 not including his but feels that his hazard is just as severe. The consumer has called the retailer today and was told that they could send out a technician at his expense. The consumer still has the product currently plugged in.
justification: The consumer reports a potential hazard with the refrigerator light but no injury, damage, or immediate danger has occurred.

incident_description: General Electric Food processor's safety interlock system failed.  Fingers were cut badly requiring numerous stitches.
justification: The safety interlock failure led to severe finger injuries requiring stitches, indicating a significant injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the known failure rate.

incident_description: I have a set of 8 nesting glass bowls by Anchor Hocking.  They are approximately 6 years old.  In July of this year the largest bowl (the bottom one in which the others sit) shattered while in the cupboard.  None of the bowls had been used in at least a week.  They were not being moved.  They were in the cubboard with the door closed when I heard a crash from three rooms away.  I thought that something had fallen off another shelf.  When I opened the cupboard I realized that the bowl had not only shattered but appeared to have almost exploded as glass shards were everywhere in the cubboard, up to almost 12 inches away and inside other dishes about 10 inches away.
justification: The bowl shattered unexpectedly but no one was injured.

incident_description:
I heard the carafe rattling in the coffee maker.  I got up to investigate.  When I removed the carafe the heating plate started turning orange hot and smoke started coming out of seams in the plastic body.  Although the light was already out, I unplugged it.  It continued to smoke for about 5 minutes.
Thank goodness I hadn't already left for work!
justification: The incident caused smoke and heat, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Standard features are extremely dangerous.  New installation of a General Electric Hotpoint residential kitchen cooking stove, model RB526D PWW, there is a high tendancy to accidentally turn on the oven. The temperature dial can easily be rotated by brushing against it which silently starts the oven heating. In this case, the installation booklet cought fire and resulted in an employee being burned.
justification: An employee was burned due to the oven accidentally turning on, indicating injury (severity 3). The description notes a high tendency for accidental activation, making occurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Microwave oven performed an uncommanded start and began to heat up with no product inside.
The unit was shut down.  Shortly thereafter, the unit started again and began to quickly overheat until it threatened to burst into flames.  The plug was pulled and the unit abandoned from further use.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and overheated, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I own a Frigidaire refrigerator/freezer Model # FRS24ZGG with an ice dispenser in the freezer door.
Last evening I smelled smoke somewhere in my kitchen and realized it was coming from the refrigerator. Upon closer inspection, smoke was coming from the ice dispenser. I quickly disassembled the front cover on the ice dispenser and saw that a wire inside was on fire, but smoltering slowly. I am not sure if the wire had a bare spot and was touching the cabinet or just what had happened. I carefully pulled the wire out and taped  wire nuts to the ends and re-energized the refirg without further incidents. I feel that if I had not smelled the smoke, it could have resulted in a major fire.
justification: The incident involved a smoldering wire but was resolved without injury or further damage, indicating a minor incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The front burner powered in the on position without being switched on  and when she attempted to power it in the off potion it would not power off. The temperature of the burning begin to get higher and higher without the setting being changed. 

 She then pulled the range out from the wall to unplug it from the outlet. She waited 30 minutes before plugging it back into the wall outlet and when she did the same right front burner powered back into the on position. So she unplugged it from the wall outlet once.

The firm was contacted the same date of the incident and they did not offer any assistance. The consumer left the range unplugged from the wall outlet over night. On 8/30/2011 the consumer contacted the firm again and they offered  to send out a service technician but the consumer would be required to pay the cost of the range. 

While doing some research online she came across a recall (see Release #09-033 where the hazard was Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can: 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers. 

She noticed that her model number was not affected by the recall but she experienced one of the same hazards.The consumer indicated that she did not feel safe if any repairs were made because the same failure could possibly occur. 


The consumer is unaware of where the range was purchased from. The range was purchased by the builder of her home prior to her moving in and she moved in, in 2007.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning burner posing a fire and burn hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On July 5th, 2011 at 20: 13 the Black River Falls Fire Department was paged by the Jackson County Emergency Dispatch Center (EDC) for a house fire at [REDACTED] which is located in the City of Black River Falls and County of Jackson. At the time of the page out the caller, a neighbor was reporting that flames were coming from the structure.
Upon arrival the department found light smoke coming from the two story wood frame structure but no flames
could be seen at the time.
The department was able to confirm with the home owner, [REDACTED], who arrived at the address that no one
else was in the structure.
There is an estimated $12,000 in damage to the structure which is insured.
The department made an offensive attack on the fire which was contained to the kitchen area. The rest of the
structure does have smoke and heat damage.
There were two cats in the home at the time and both were located by firefighters in the basement area of the
structure. They both appeared to be scared but okay and were returned to the owner.
The cause of the fire is under investigation.
Sixteen firefighters were on the scene for two hours.
There were no reported injuries.
The Red Cross was contacted to assist the owner.
Other agencies that responded to and assisted at the scene were the Black River Falls Police Department,
Jackson County Sheriff's Department, We Energies, and Black River Falls Utilities.
justification: The incident involved a house fire with no injuries or deaths, but caused significant property damage.

incident_description: The consumer says the broiler burner turned on by itself and continued to get hotter.  The consumer says he had to go outside and turn off the circuit breaker.  He says they wont come off with the controls.  The consumer says it is only the broiler burner for the oven that comes on.  The consumer says that when he turns the circuit breaker back on the broiler burner also comes on.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him the unit is not on recall and to contact the CPSC.
justification: The consumer says the broiler burner turned on by itself and continued to get hotter, which is a hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
In August of 2011, took delivery from LOWES of four Fridgidare Professional Appliances including Smooth top electric range model FPES3085KFD at vacation home. This is "the top of the line". Manufacture date of June 2011.  Appliances were installed but have not been used.  In early September, entered empty house to find front right burner very hot with HE indicator on but all controls turned to "OFF". House had been empty for days.  When I turned the appropriate dial to try to get the burner "OFF", it blew the circuit breaker. Left circuit breaker off and called service number to report defect/safety issue but call center refered me to authorized representatives, "[REDACTED]" and "[REDACTED]" (I didn't make up these names).  Told the call center I had a confidence issue in the unused unit and needed it replaced for safety reasons, not repaired by [REDACTED].  They seemed not to appreciate the difference between a defective new product, a safety issue and a repair to a used product. 
Following Monday I contacted Lowes and my building contractor who had taken delivery of the appliances...they visited the house and were able to immediately replicate the problem by turning the circuit back on.  Both commented that the range needed to be removed immediately for safety reasons.  Unfortunately, because I had reported the problem directly to the manufacturer, they were refusing to allow LOWES to replace it without a visit from [REDACTED], who, I'm afraid , has a financial incentive to declare it repairable rather than replace it.
My confidence in Lowes has risen sharply and my confidence in Fridgidare, as a brand, has tanked.  Lowes has made a commitment to resolve the issue including the possibility of returning all the appliances with no questions asked while Fridgidare refuses to adopt any other stance than to make an appointment with [REDACTED].  Its ashame they don't understand the damage that can be done by the empowered consumer in a digital world.
justification: The incident involved a defective appliance that became dangerously hot while turned off, posing a safety risk but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Started my morning pot of coffee, went downstairs to get the newspaper. When I came back into the house there was a bad smell of something burning , went back inside the Kitchen and saw the Mr.Coffee Maker (Model:DRX5) (Date Code:D6 XO21) billowing smoke from the bottom of the maker, I unpluged the maker and it continued to smolder for a short time after. I have owned this maker for a few years and have had no problems with it until today. I just wanted to let you know what had happened.

Thank You
[REDACTED]

incident_description: KitchenAid Microwave/Range Hood (model KHMS155LSS-4), manufactured in April 2006 in PRC, suddenly and by itself started operating.  I happened to come home and noticed the microwave was on.  I suspect it had been on for some time because the machine was hot and there was a noticeable burnt smell in the kitchen.  When I hit the stop button, it would immediately come back on.  If I opened the door of the microwave, it would stop, but when I closed the door it would turn back on.  Only unplugging the microwave stopped it.  The read out on the display kept saying "PAN".  This is a serious fire hazard, and according to internet reports is common with the model.  The company knows about this defect because they agreed, at no cost, to send me a new part and pay for the repair.  I'm not sure this is good enough if there has been no recall/fix of ALL of these machines.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The issue is known to be common with this model.

incident_description: Microwave internal fire.

I grabbed a fire extinguisher and put it out then pulled the range away from the wall and ran downstairs and shut off the circuit breaker.I then opened the windows and door to help clear the smoke from the kitchen!The house smelled like burnt electronics and you can see the black flame marks on the top back of the range!

Consumer has medical appointment on 08/05/2011 to see his doctor and treat his burning sensation in his right arm.
