incident_description:
Kenmore Gas Range; Model 790.70502013 (purchased on 09/11/2011)

Oven continued heating for several hours after being turned off by keypad. Numerous attempts to "reset" the electronics (remove 110VAC cable from outlet for five minutes; per instructions in manual) have failed to make it stop doing this. Oven burner continues to burn at "full strength" until gas supply is removed (there is a shut-off valve on the regulator; found on the back of the range). No "error code" is shown on the LED display.

Steps taken to remedy the condition:
Turn off gas supply at regulator.
Unplug power cable from outlet for five minutes (last time; left it unplugged for an hour)
Turn on gas supply at regulator.
Plug power cable in to outlet.

Result:
Leaking gas can be smelled and heard; seems to be coming from the oven burner.
When oven is turned on, "excess" gas caused a small explosion within broiler compartment.
After oven reached set temperature, attempted to turn oven off with keypad.
Failure. Turned gas supply off at the regulator.

Obviously, this situation presents a number of dangers to life, limb, and property; from minor burns to carbon monoxide poisoning to a home-destroying explosion. How is it that a "brand new" appliance fails like this unless it was made with faulty parts?
justification: The incident involves a gas range malfunction that could lead to serious hazards like explosions or carbon monoxide poisoning, but no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Elite bottom freezer refrigerator in 2006 - LG is the manufacturer.
Approx. last year (June) we experienced the interior light had not shut off when the doors were shut. The lamp and bulbs severely overheated, ruining food and melting the lense cover and trim. Assuming that it was human error (i.e. doors not closed completely), I replaced the lense cover and trim. The same problem is now re-occurring. I removed the partially melted (replacement) lense and cover, again, 3 weeks ago. This morning we found the lights on (again) this morning and the interior temperatures were so hot that thawing, raw meat on the top was cooked!!! 

I am greatly concerned that this refrigerator is a severe fire hazard and "discovered" on an internet blog that LG and Sears are both aware of the problem and yet a product recall has not been issued. This is a SEVERE life safety concern!!! They have identified that the problem is in the main circuit board and switches. Sears at the very least is issuing a Service Flash Repair (if applicable to your model #) but only if you are a VERY well informed consumer and have researched the internet to find out just how big a problem this is. 

Additionally, a class action lawsuit vs LG was filed last year in New Jersey - fyi.
justification: The incident describes a recurring overheating issue that has damaged food and refrigerator components, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Was removing a cake from the oven: Had the oven door open and brushed my leg against the corner of the oven door which caused a large cut to my leg.. ( nine stiches to close cut) The corner of the door has a very sharp edge to it. It is made of very thin stainless steel.
justification: The incident resulted in a large cut requiring nine stitches, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The sharp edge of the oven door makes similar injuries likely if not addressed.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore side by side refrigerator model 106-53562200 purchased new on 5/11/2002.  Numerous problems just out of warranty with circuit boards going bad for ice maker and main unit not keeping cold.  Today, 9/12/2011, daughter was home and called me in a panic saying there was a burning smell in the kitchen and great room at 9:30AM.  I left work and headed home. Strong smell in house of electrical burning. Smell was coming from the back bottom of the refrigerator. Unit was plugged in to wall plug. Pushed refrigerator away from wall to gain access to back for a look. I removed the cardboard back access panel and the smell was strongest at the compressor. The fan motor was running but compressor was not. I unplugged the unit from the wall.  Used my flash light and didn't see anything out of the ordinary and nothing burned.  I plugged the unit back into wall plug and within 5 seconds the white box (with 3 wires going to it) attached to the side of the compressor began to crackle / sizzle then sparked and glowed red then smoke came out of the top.  I unplugged the unit, waited 5 minutes and did the process again with the same results.  The refrigerator is unplugged for fear of fire. DTE appliance service contract (Home protection Plus) will be here 9/13 for a diagnosis and possible repair. I, through internet researce discovered that the Start Device pn 8201786 is now superceeded to pn 8201786 which is on back order status according to Sears Parts Direct site.  I don't trust this appliance anymore, it's a danger and unreliable.
justification: The incident involved a strong electrical burning smell and visible sparks, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My wife had placed two trays of pasta in the oven so it could bake while we were at church so that it would be ready as soon as we got home. She set the temperature for 350 degrees.  Everything seemed fine / normal, so we left. This was at about 4:45pm. When we arrived back to our house around 5:50pm, we opened the door and immediately heard at least 2 of our smoke alarms beeping. The house was filled with smoke. We went in and found smoke pouring from the oven with fault code "F1" displayed on the screen. Pressing the off button did not turn the oven off. The surfaces of the oven were incredibly hot, so much so that we could not move the oven to unplug it. I went down to the breaker box in the basement and shut the power off that way.  Once it had cooled down, we inspected it. The inside is probably permanently damaged (scorched everywhere). The baking sheet's silcone grips were burnt to the point they turned into power. You can't even see through the door's glass anymore. We turned the power back on once it had cooled off, and it seemed like it was working normally again. However, we have now shut the power off at the breaker and will likely replace the oven completely as we simply do not trust it anymore. This is extremely dangerous; it could have easily started a fire in the house if we had been much later getting home. I have seen many complaints on the internet about this problem, and I find it amazing that there has not been a recall issued. This was scary and extremely dangerous. No oven should be allowed to heat out of control. There needs to be a fail-safe type of control to shut down power immediately if the oven starts to overheat.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused significant smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: I was baking chicken in my anchor hocking 13 X 9 glass baking dish at 350 degrees, about 20 minutes into cooking the chicken I heard a sound like marbles hitting a sheet of glass.  I looked in the oven and the dish had exploded into many pieces.  I turned the oven off and let it cool down completely before cleaning up the mess.  Luckily it happened inside the oven and did not break the glass oven door.  No one was hurt, but I have a 7 year old daughter that loves baked chicken - it could have been a lot worse.  I had the dish for about 5 years.
justification: The glass baking dish exploded but no one was injured, and the incident was contained within the oven.

incident_description:
A couple of burners on my "Frigidaire Gallery" cooktop are having the same problems as listed below on the recall units. 



I would please like to have my unit covered under this recall. My model # is FEC36S8HBA. 





Hazard: Liquids pooling under the control knob can cause the surface heating element to turn on unexpectedly, heat to temperatures other than expected and then not turn off, posing a risk of fire and burn hazards to consumers. 

Incidents/Injuries: Frigidaire has received 70 reports of incidents, including three reports of fires that resulted in property damage. Three minor burn injuries were also reported. 

Description: This recall involves Frigidaire electric smoothtop slide-in ranges and cooktops with rotary knobs and digital displays. 



Hazard: Depending on the model, the surface heating elements can 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to consumers.
justification: The description reports three minor burn injuries and 70 incidents, including fires causing property damage, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury) and a likelihood of 4 (likely) given the number of reports.

incident_description:
I have a Krups FMF5 coffee maker that is only a few weeks old.  It was fine in the beginning, but then it started to turn on spontaneously.  I would make a pot of coffee, the machine would turn off, but then a few minutes later it would start to heat up again with an empty water tank.  I noticed when I smelled an odd odor coming from the kitchen.  Unplugging the machine prevented a more serious issue.  
I verified this problem on 3 occasions, and also noted that the readout and the clock no longer worked.
I reported this to Krups, who were less than helpful in my request to have this machine replaced, even though they have already removed the machine from the market.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned by turning on spontaneously and emitting an odd odor, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
This dishwasher shorted out several times before.  Shortly after placing the dishwasher on the normal wash setting within a  matter  of minutes she noticed that the unit had powered in the off position without completing the cycle and when she attempted to power back in the on position. She reset the circuit breaker and it  still would not power in the on position.

She contacted an electrician (name not provided) and he attempted to look at the unit and he could not locate duplicate the failure. She then contacted the firm on 8/15/2011 and was advised that she would be required to pay for the parts and the labor if she wanted a technician come out. 

The consumer indicated that she believes the appliance might have short circuit.The consumer isn't sure if whether or not she wants to have the unit repaired or replace.

incident_description:
The dishwasher was powered in the on position on the normal cycle prior to the consumer going to bed and within a few hours she and her husband awoke to a strong plastic burning odor in the home. 

The consumers husband got up immediately  and went into the kitchen where he  noticed smoking and flames coming from the control panel of the dishwasher.

The consumerÃÂs husband used a fire extinguisher  that was close by to put the fire out but there were minor smoke damages inside of the dishwasher. He then powered the circuit breaker in the off position to cease all power to the dishwasher .

On 8/12/2011 the consumerÃÂs husband removed the control panel from the dishwasher and noticed that the wires were charred and melted together. The firm was contacted on 8/12/2011 and he advised  the representative that he spoke with (representative name is unknown) that he had removed the control panel and discovered the melting and burnt wires. 

The representative advised the consumer that he was not to remove the control panel and insisted that he have a technician come out to the home to service the appliance. incident_description: The consumer says as he was heating water the control panel caught fire.  The consumer says the fire was coming from the rear of the stove.  The consumer says he had to shut the main breaker off to turn off the oven.  The consumer says the unit was on for about 6 minutes prior to the incident.  the consumer says he saw melting plastic on the face of the control panel.  The consumer says he contacted the manufacturer and they filed a report but said they didnt know what caused it.

incident_description:
The consumer  noticed that the wash select cycle panel lost all power to it so he contacted  the firm (exact date is unknown) and a technician came out to repair it. 

Approximately three to four months later the same failure occurred and the  firm was contacted (date is unknown) and a technician came out to the home. 

The consumer was advised by the technician that there was bad insulation around the panel (which allows steam and/or condensation to innundate electrical control panel) and it the dishwasher were to fail again to try and unplug it from the wall outlet and allow to air dry prior to use. The technician was able to repair the unit. 

On or around 7/27/2011 the consumer attempted to use the dishwasher an notice there was no power to the control panel so he unplugged the unit from the wall outlet and waited for a week when he plugged it back in to determine if it would work. 

On 8/2/2011shortly after plugging the dishwasher back into the wall outlet and loading it he started it on the normal wash with sanitizer within a matter of minutes he noticed a plastic burning odor and went into the kitchen and there was smoke coming from the dishwasher. He opened the dishwasher door and noticed that the coil was charred brown and black. The dishwasher was unplugged and moved into the garage. 

The firm was contacted on 8/23/2011 and he spoke with a representative who filed a report. The consumer indicated that he isnÃÂt sure if he would like to have the appliance repaired. He has placed the dishwasher inside of the garage and it is still currently in the unplug position. 

The consumer indicated that the dishwasher poses as a fire hazard and does not want to risk losing his home by leaving the dishwasher in it.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a charred coil, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The consumer says that she turned the unit on when all of a sudden she smelled rubber burning.  The consumer says she didnt notice anything strange inside.  The consumer said that her husband inspected the dishwasher and noticed a hole to the right of the start and cancel button.  The consumer says that approximately 30 minutes had passed between her turning the unit on and her noticing the burning smell.  The consumer says that her kitchen was filled with smoke.  The consumer says her husband unplugged it.  She said that she tried to use it but the lights would not come on, thats when her husband noticed it.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said the unit is not on recall and offered to send out a service technician for a fee.   the consumer says that the motor was replaced on the unit 6 years ago.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is unlikely given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her gas range seems to have a surge of power on her gas range. The consumer was baking bread and muffins in May of 2011 when she thought something might be wrong with her range. The consumer had her product on already for about 90 minutes set to bake, when she placed a second batch of food it burned within minutes and her smoke detectors went off. The consumer shut off the oven and the smoke burned itself out. On another occasion today, the consumer's daughter had the range on for about an hour when she put a batch of cookies in the oven. The cookies burnt in minutes and her daughter turned off the oven. The consumer in another incident, tried to use the auto clean feature and it blew the thermostat of her range on August 10th and the oven door locked.

 The circuit burned itself out and the product shut itself off. The consumer's husband was by the stove and saw the digital interface shut off. The consumer stated that no one was harmed in any instance with the product. The consumer stated that her product is an oven range combo. The consumer is only experiencing an issue with the oven of the product. The consumer stated that the product surges after an hour of use. The oven was set to bake at 325 and 350 degrees respectively when this issue occurs. The consumer called the firm today and was told that the product was not on recall and they can send a serviceman at her expense . The consumer has called the retailer and was given the number to the manufacturer. 

The range shows no apparent signs of charring or discoloration.  The product has not caused to the structure of the consumer's home. The consumer opted not to call the fire department at the time of the respective incidents. The consumer was not harmed by the product. The range has a coil surface. 

Consumer update: replaced 2 grates due to paint cracking, replaced thermostat, and has another appointment for someone to look at the oven again.
justification: The incident involved multiple occurrences of the oven malfunctioning, leading to burnt food and smoke, but no injuries or structural damage were reported.

incident_description: Consumer is a fire investigator with the city of Hartford, CT.  Consumer was heating water in a coffee mug, and a fire started in the venting area near the microwave lamp. Interior of microwave was burning. The unit is not repairable.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) given the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description:
The refrigerator is located in a vacation home and the consumerÃÂs daughter and son in law went to the home and when they opened the refrigerator they noticed a horrible electrical/plastic burning odor.

After careful observation they noticed that the housing that surrounded the light bulb had melted around the light bulb and the light bulb was powered in the on position. 

The consumerÃÂs daughter used a drying towel to carefully removed the light bulb from the plastic melted housing.  The consumer indicated that he safely believes that the lights stayed powered in the on position while the refrigerator doors were closed.

The firm was contacted via email on 8/22/2011 and the consumer has not received a response at this current time. 

The consumer indicated that he isnÃÂt sure if he will allow any repairs to be made on the appliance and he  will continue to use the refrigerator without any light bulbs inside.
justification: The incident involved a melted light bulb housing and a burning odor, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says the first time he used it he noticed when unplugging it from the wall that the plug prongs were very hot.  The consumer says the next time he used it, it took a long time to toast and then he noticed sparks coming out of it.  He unplugged it and has not used it since.  He tried to contact the manufacturer but all he keeps getting is automated message and never a live person. Consumer says that the plug was so hot it burned his finger.
justification: The consumer experienced a burn injury from the hot plug, indicating a severity level of 3. The repeated issues with the toaster and the inability to contact the manufacturer suggest a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer states that her electric smooth top range is not included in the recall CAP for NR#09-333 (August 27, 2009), but CPSC should pursue an investigation on her model and serial number, because his range poses the exact same problem as the one on recall.

Consumer stated that when she turned "on" the right front burner to low setting the temperature increase to the high setting by itself while the burner was set to the "low" setting.

Consumer said that at the beginning of June the issues started in one burner, but now all the burners suddenly rise the temperature without being switching on.

Consumer called and explained incident to mfrÃÂs rep. (name unknown) who said that the product is not longer under warranty

No injury

Consumer feels that her electric range could pose a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range with potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
While baking in the oven at 350 degrees for 15 minutes then the setting was changed to 400 for an additional 15 minutes when she heard loud pop noise. 

When she got closer to the oven she saw flames coming from the back of the control panel they lonely lasted two seconds and the fire went out by themselves. 

The oven was then powered in the off position and her husband pulled the range from the wall outlet and they noticed that all power was lost to the control panel    (which is an all touch electric control panel) and when they removed the control panel the wires inside were blackened and melted. 

The firm was contacted on 8/22/2011 and the consumer was advised that her unit was not affected by any recent recalls and no assistance was offered to make any repairs to the unit.

The consumer is considering get the appliance repaired but has not yet made any repair appointments. She has not used the range since the failure occurred she contacted her local gas company and they shut the gas off to the range. The range is currently in the unplug position.
justification: The incident involved flames and electrical damage but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Consumer stated that his dishwasher is a potential fire hazard as he smelled an acrid smell of burning emitting from the appliance. The consumer stated that this has happened twice, 3 weeks ago and 2 days ago. The consumer stated that both time the product was on for a normal cycle. In both cases the consumer found no damage to his home or any visual damage to the product. The consumer opted not to call the fire department in both cases as the issue seemed to time itself out once the he opened the dishwasher door. The consumer has noticed numerous reports of a potential fire hazard online including similar models. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product and has yet to call the firm or retailer.
justification: The consumer reported a burning smell but no actual fire or damage occurred, and no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury. The issue has happened twice under normal use, suggesting a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
Caller was away on vacation when a friend came in to take her trash out and found herself sloshing through water in the kitchen. 
Friend contacted caller who contacted a friend who is professional in these types of repairs. 
Professional  found that the start relay had burned up in the refrigerator. 
Start relay was burned and scorched.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burned start relay) but no injuries or fatalities.

incident_description: The consumer says she used the self cleaning feature and now the outside top of her oven door is browned.  The consumer is concerned that the oven may pose a fire hazard.  She says that she has never used the self cleaning feature before.  The consumer contacted the retailer who offered to send out a service technician for a fee.  The consumer says it may have been on self cleaning mode for about 2 hours.  The consumer says the vent in the back of the stove was not venting well and caused puddles on the top of her stove due to poor condensation inside the oven.  This occured while the product was under warranty so it got repaired.  The consumer says also that when she first received the oven she hit the self cleaning feature by mistake, while she had food in the oven.  She pressed off and it would not go off.  She contacted the manufacturer who took her thru a process to get the self cleaning mode off.  The consumer says that there should not be a self cleaning button next to the off button.  The consumer is not happy that no one is willing to help her.  She just got a new floor installed in her kitchen, as well as a new dishwasher and the browning of the oven door mars the newer look of the kitchen.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven feature causing cosmetic damage and potential fire hazard concerns, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a set of glass storage/bakeware from Lock & Lock at QVC.  The item number is K34008, and it was a 6-pc. round and rectangular set.  One day I was putting together a recipe and had broken 4 eggs into one of these round glass containers.  I had beaten the eggs with a fork and left the container on the counter while I turned away to get more ingredients from the pantry when  I heard a crash and thought I had somehow knocked something off the counter.  What had happened is that the container had exploded on the counter leaving glass--and beaten eggs--all over the counter top and on the floor.  I tried to figure out if I had done something wrong but could think of nothing.  My husband gathered all the broken glass and looked it over carefully, looking for a flaw in the glass.  He said he saw a place that looked like it could've been a flaw that caused the explosion.  I didn't want to continue to use this set, so I e-mailed QVC, and they allowed me to return the set for a complete refund.  I had had this set for about one month and had hardly used it.  When I had used it, it was mostly for storage in the refrigerator.  I've read about this type of problem in Consumer Reports, so i wanted to report my experience.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not rare but not frequent either.

incident_description:
I purchased and installed a dishwasher several years ago. It is a Frigidaire Model FDB944CB0. Soon after installation, I began noticing a burning smell when using the heat dry option. I rarely use this option, but as time goes on the smell seems to get worse. After power outages, the unit seems to reset itself to include the activation of the Heat Dry option and we don't realize it until the burning takes place.
Last week, the dishwasher ran through its cycle, and upon entering the heat dry mode it started burning. My wife was the only one home, and she was upstairs. A neighbor came over to see if our kitchen was on fire...that is how bad the smell got.
During these episodes, we are forced to manually shut the dishwasher off and wait for the smoke to clear before removing the dishes and turning the heat dry option off so it does not happen the next time. With the heat dry option off, the dishwasher appears to run with no issues.
I have a repair issue with another unrelated appliance, and I thought i would enter in the information on the dishwasher to see if there was information on how to repair it. What I have found are numerous reports of fire and/or similar issues with heating elements burning the inside of the tub during high heat dry cycles. I decided to post this complaint in hopes that it will put the number over the threshold required for an investigation/ safety recall.
justification: The incident involves a burning smell and smoke, but no injury or death has been reported, fitting severity level 2. The issue occurs frequently during heat dry cycles, making it likely (4).

incident_description: Started dishwasher for a normal wash cycle at approximately 7:25 a.m.  Was getting ready for work and oldest daughter was waiting getting ready to leave for school.  When my daughter walked in the kitchen to get her last items for her school bag she began screaming MOM, MOM, the dishwasher is on fire.  I immediately ran to the kitchen and saw a thick black smoke and large frame exiting from the control panel at the top of the dishwasher.  Had the children go outside and immediately called the fire department.  Managed to open the dishwasher door letting it fall hoping it would stop the power supply.  Water was splashing out as the cycle was still running.  The smell of burning plastic was terrible.  The fire appears to have started in the electrical control panel/display.  This unit was serviced by A&E Factory Service on numerous occassions and this area was worked on in October 2010 replacing the console insert, board, panel-cntl., and act ovlay on an extended warranty.  There were no physical injuries only the emotional trama of the girls.  Thank goodness I hadn't left yet for work and learned a valuable lesson not to run appliances if I am not at home.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher fire with no physical injuries, only emotional trauma, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such electrical failures are not common but have been documented in this unit's service history.

incident_description: The GE Spectra oven was just previously self-cleaned and then wiped down thoroughly when just a few days later the bottom heating element burst into a flame and and continued to burn despite turning off oven and throwing some baking soda on it.  We ordered and installed a replacement part for this.  A week later the top one did the same thing!  I am trying to see if there has been any recalls on this but I can't find any.  I did read on the internet where someone had the same thing happen to them but that was in 2008.
justification: The incident involved flames in the oven but no injury or death was reported, and the issue was addressed by replacing the faulty parts.

incident_description:
We awoke this morning to our LG LFX25960ST refrigerator producing an overwhelming smell of burning plastic.  We opened the door and the refrigerator was actually HOT and the roof of the interior was literally melting and dripping plastic around the interior light fixture.  This problem appears to be well documented on the internet.  http://wizbandit.wordpress.com/2008/08/21/lg-i-want-a-refund-on-this-fridge/

All of our food is ruined in the fridge and we cannot even replace the light bulbs out of fear that an electrical fire could occur.
justification: The refrigerator malfunction caused property damage and food loss, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
This product was purchased last christmas 2010. It has a date code of  031X0.
The hinges on the unit keep breaking, even before I use the waffle maker.

I contacted Black & Decker through their web site and received a new set of hinges.

Then they broke so here is my second email to them...

"Hi, I received the replacement hinges a few days ago. I put them in, open and closed the unit a few times, it seemed fine.  Then I went to use the unit and a hinge  broke.
They do not seem to be able to support the weight of the top lid... or maybe they are getting caught on something inside and breaking.  i request some  more replacement hinges and better quality hinges!  If they keep breaking, then I will request a replacement with one that will not break. Thank you!"

This is my third and last email to them... i did not get a response or new hinges...

sent 3-29-2011

"I received the second set of hinges some time ago... By the time I went to use the waffle maker, the hinges were already broken. All the hinges are breaking in the same spot.  This is dangerous as the first time that I was able to use it,the hinges broke as I was using it, the top and bottom seperated and luckily I did not burn myself.  The new hinges just break before I am able to use the product.  The directions also say I am able to stand the unit upright, but the top and bottom open and then falls down.  Needless to say, better hinges are needed... maybe metal ones that will not break.  HELP !!!!  I would like to use the product !!!!   Are there any technicians that will research my problem?  Please send new hinges... again.... Regards, [REDACTED]"


I would like to report this problem and get the Belgian Waffle Make off the shelves until they get them fixed.
justification: The incident involves repeated hinge failures, with a near-miss burn injury reported, indicating potential for harm but no actual injury.

incident_description: While cooking a frozen pizza in my toaster oven the wires over heated and began smoking.  There was no fire in the oven itself.  The food was still partially frozen, nothing on the bottom was on fire or smoldering and the element was not burning, smoking or sparking.  The overheating/fire/smoke event was entirely contained to the portion of the toaster oven on the right hand side where the controls are located as well as the convection fan.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoking but no fire or injury, making it a minor operational issue.

incident_description:
Started diswasher and about 5 minutes into the cycle, the control panel started to smoke heavily and soon after flames were shooting out from the handle .
Quickly opened the door and disconnected the circuit breaker.
The flames stopped but smoking continued for several minutes, and the terrible burned out odor from the components lingered in house for more than one day till I decided to remove it from the house.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from the dishwasher, but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: My Kenmore Range Model 911.46556590 serial number 58271471 R caught on fire and wouldn't quit heating up. First, I saw a bright explosion in my oven. The bottom bake element had seemed to catch on fire. It wasn't a flame,however, it was a white light like magnesium burning. I turned the oven off, but the burning continued around the element like a sparkler. I turned the circuit breaker off but the burning still continued. I poured water on it (aprox. 2 cups) and it finally went out. I turned the breaker back on to continue cooking on the range - top. I noticed the surface and area getting very hot. the top element in the oven was red hot, I'd say over 600 degrees. The oven was not turned on! If I hadn't been in the kitchen, it would have set my house on fire. I don't see any product recalls. I am scared of this product and don't even know if I should try to have it fixed. It doesn't seem to have a safety cutoff when things go wrong.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction (fire and overheating) but no injury occurred. The likelihood is high given the described behavior and lack of safety cutoff.

incident_description:
Sears Kenmore smooth top range model number 79096009601 both front burners will stay on high after range has been turned down or off completely.  Burners will turn on spontaneously.  These are the same symptoms of Kenmore Elite and Frigidaire smooth top ranges recalled August 28th 2009.
See below:

About 200,000 Frigidaire and Kenmore Elite Smoothtop Electric Ranges have been recalled after 126 reports of problems with a defective heating elements, which could turn on spontaneously, fail to turn off or heat to different temperatures than what is selected. 
The U.S. Consumer Products Safety Commission announced the electric range recall on August 27, involving of several models of Frigidair, Frigidair Gallery, Frigidair Professional and Kenmore Elite smooth top ovens with rotary knobs and digital displays on the electric range.

At least four reports involving burns and two reports of property damage have been linked to the defective smooth-top ranges. Consumers have been urged to immediately stop using them until a free repair can be arranged.

All of the affected rangers were manufactured by Frigidaire, and sold at Sears and other stores throughout the United States between June 2001 and August 2009.

The recall affects Frigidaire models with serial numbers from VF 122xxxxx through VF831xxxxx and model numbers beginning with FEFBZ90GC, FEFLMC55GC, FEFLZ87GC, GLEF396AB, GLEF396AQ, GLEF396AS, GLEF396CQ, GLEF396CS, GLEFM397DB, GLEFM397DQ, GLEFM397DS, GLEFM97FPB, GLEFM97FPW, GLEFM97GPB, GLEFM97GPW, LEEFM389FE, PLEF398AC, PLEF398CC, PLEF398DC, PLEFM399DC, PLEFMZ99EC, PLEFMZ99GC, PLEFZ398EC, and PLEFZ398GC. The recall also affects Kenmore Elite models with serial numbers from VF122xxxxx through VF334xxxxx and model numbers beginning with 790.99012, 790.99013, 790.99014, and 790.99019.

NEED I SAY MORE???
justification: The incident involves burners turning on spontaneously, which has led to burns and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3 due to reported injuries.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range: 790.41023800

This is a smooth top range.  The right front burner can accommodate pans/pots for different sizes - there are three settings for pan size.  

Yesterday was the second time the burner (set on the largest size) did not turn off.  Two of the three rings were on.  The dial showed HE meaning the burner was hot but off.  The only way I have found to turn the burner off is to turn it on and then turn on the three burners and select a heat setting.
justification: The burner not turning off is an incident with no injury reported, but it poses a potential burn hazard.

incident_description: Kenmore Electric Range 665.95029101  - element would not turn off - had to unplug range.  After 2 hours plugged back in and the range element started heating again so unplugged.  What is the cause of this problem and what needs to be replaced on the range and what is the routine cost of repair.  Range is 8 year old.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning range element that poses a potential hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Yesterday evening (9/8/2011) I was using my Kenmore oven which is less than 1 1/2 years old (but was installed by previous homeowners when we purchased our home 1 year ago) to heat up chicken nuggets for my kids.  I set the oven to 425 and cooked them for 15 minutes.  After that I shut the oven off and removed them and then closed the door.  I turned around to walk back across the kitchen and feed my kids and as I got over to them there was a loud pop that sounded like a gunshot that came from the oven.  I went back over to the oven to open it and make sure there was nothing inside that could have exploded and when I did I saw that the center piece of glass in the oven door had completely shattered.  Fortunately no glass burst into the kitchen or into the oven, but I am afraid that if the center glass on a fairly new range could just shatter for no apparent reason, then the other glass on the door that they used in manufacturing could shatter as well.  In the meantime I can't cook in my oven and glass fragments and dust are coming out of the bottom of the door and falling into the warming drawer.  It is terrifying to think of what would have happened if the other panes shattered as well.  My children were all about 5 feet from the oven door.
justification: The incident involved a shattered oven door glass with no injuries, but potential for harm if other panes had shattered.

incident_description:
My refrigerator has had numerous problems but the latest one is dangerous, unexpected, and ridiculous.  The light bulbs inside did not shut off, make so much heat that it browned the bulb sockets, created smoke, melted the plastic housing and cooked the frozen chicken on the top shelf.

I am aware of similar models being recalled but when I called the Product Revolution line at Sears that handles the Recalls I was told by the rep, [REDACTED], that this model hasn't been recalled; its not on the list.  I asked for a supervisor and was told one would call be back.  That has yet to happen.

I have removed the bulbs but I'm fearful that others electrical problems will ensue. I'm also concenred that another consumer might not catch this in time and may suffer major fire property damage, worse. life damage.
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I continue to cut myself deeply when operating near and around my Electrolux freestanding electric range.  On the last occasion, the cut was so severe that I was forced to go to the emergency room for treatment, as my urgent care provider couldn't stitch the wound.

Upon close examination of this stove, I have found that there are RAZOR SHARP edges to the stainless steel trim pieces that line both sides of the oven door.  These edges are carried by the design all the way to the ground, and are EASILY reachable by children of all ages.  Based on the fact that I cannot seem to clean my cabinets around this oven without receiving serious cuts, it would seem to me that this product suffers from a design defect that poses a SERIOUS risk to ANY household with children.
justification: The description reports severe cuts requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is described as a design defect with razor-sharp edges, making occurrence likely (4) for anyone using or near the stove.

incident_description: I purchased a GE "Sensor Microwave Oven" on 4/10/2011 to replace my 7 yr. old  microwave (which still worked but not the carrousel).  My husband was died of cancer so the microwave was only used for occasionally reheating foods or veggies and melting chocolate/butter, etc.  Last evening I suddenly heard beeping & checked - my microwave was beeping & the digital readout said "keypad was shorted out".  (Note: I had not used the micro for 2-1/2 days - IT WAS SITTING IDLE!)  I opened the door and the insides were SCALDING HOT and smelled HOT too (a fire hazard in the making - thank goodness I was @ home!)!  I tried working the keypad but nothing worked so I unplugged it.  After leaving it cool down I plugged it in again & it told me to "set the clock", I did and it seemed ok (I was still hesitant).  Within 2 minutes, while I was standing there, it SUDDENLY STARTED on it's own!  Again, none of the keypad buttons worked so I unplugged it and it is STILL UNPLUGGED!  I will not use this appliance again.  I sent an electronic email to GE on their www.geappliances.com/service_and_support/contact/form_concern.htm last evening.  I received an auto-reply: "Thank you for contacting us through www.geappliances.com. We have received your eMail on 9/7/2011 at 09:50:00 PM EST.  We regret to inform you that we are currently experiencing longer than usual response times. A Consumer Specialist will respond to your inquiry as soon as possible. Sincerely, The Consumer e-Response Team GE Appliances" (they gave me a "reference number [REDACTED]).  I've searched the internet & find there ARE OTHER REFERENCES to people having the same problem with micro beeping suddenly, for no reason.  The micro is only 1 yr. and just under 5 mos. old + not used that often & NEVER used to cook a full meal (or frozen dinner either).  This is A FIRE HAZARD - thank goodness I was @ home!
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and became scalding hot, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: WARNING Kenmore Range model 790.96613409 has unpredictable fire danger flaw in control panel The other day we joined what we never knew was a large group and had a fire in our Kenmore Range caused by the electronic clock/timer, oven control. This Kenmore tagged range was built by Frigidaire for Sears and is model number 790.96613409. I loved this range and it cost us a lot of money. In fact I have been a Sears guy for 50 years! Our ordeal began when the Kenmore Range's electronic panel (with oven and clock/timer controls) shorted out suddenly in it's insides and then burst into flames! There was lots of smoke and a shower of sparks spraying up the wall behind and above the range, within the several long seconds it took for the houses main circuit breaker panel to trip off the ranges electricity! This was incredibly terrifying and you might imagine my ( I will be polite ) SURPRISE, to research the internet about the burnt to a crisp clock/timer oven control, only to discover that there have been an incredible number of these fires for several years and all over the country! AND the replacement timer control offered by Sears, still to this day...is...none other ...than part number 316418702, made by the company called ( now get this ) "SPITFIRE Controls Inc. This name couldn't have described my experience with this product any better. [REDACTED}
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by the range's control panel, resulting in significant property damage and terror, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
While cooking chicken in our Kenmore Electric Range, Model # 665.95829003, the oven started getting EXTREMELY hot.  The chicken was smouldering and I removed it--but the oven was so hot I needed full-hand mitts to retrieve the chicken.  I turned off the oven, but the top broiler elements remained on.  The oven was glowing orange and continued heating unchecked until I shut off the circuit breaker.  The display stated "F-1 F-3."  If we had not been inside (the oven was only set to bake, not broil--and 350 degrees) the oven could have caught the house on fire.

Appearantly, we are not the only ones this has happened to. Upon a Google search of the problem I found many like stories online at this website:   

http://www.mysears.com/Appliances/topics/My-oven-won-t-turn-off-/posts?page=7

It seems that a relay in the oven fuses, causing the broiler to remain on with no thermostatic control until the power is cut.
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high as similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
Consumer states that his electric smooth top range is not included in the recall CAP for NR#09-333 (August 27, 2009), but CPSC should pursue an investigation on his model and serial number, because his range poses the exact same problem as the one on recall.

Consumer stated that her electric range's oven turned "on" spontaneously without being switched on.  Consumer said that she had to turn 'off' from the circuit breaker.  Consumer said that she been having this issues with the range's oven for some time, but the last time on 08/01/2011 she could turn off the range's oven by turning the knobs in the "off" position.

No injury

Consumer called and explained incident to retail rep.  (Name unknown), who told consumer that is nothing that they can do for consumer because the warranty had expired. 

Consumer Added:  Having to worry about a dysfunctional range that turned on by the itself to an extreme heat and would not turn off when pushing the off button, was a scary situation; having to run down to the breaker box to get it to turn off.  Having no stove for five days and the safety of my home and the people and animals that live in the house was no concern of Frigidaire.  This was not the first time this had happened, it has occured several times in the past.  Called Frigidaire and same response to call technician of their choice and then it would be a recall, so this time I did as they wanted.  Then the wishes, washes started talking about warranty.  I didn't ask for warranty.  I am not happy with the way I was treated by Frigidaire employees, the way they gave me the run-around and lied, in the beginning of the phone call it says it was recorded, shouldn't it have been recorded?
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning electric range that turns on spontaneously, posing a safety risk but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My 1yr old Kenmore dishwasher overheated and caught fire from the control board and soap dispenser.

On 3 ocassions the door retention cord broke allowing the heavyweight door open and hit my wife causing a bruise on her right thigh area. incident_description: My whirlpool RF395LXE serial # rg5313780 range malfunctioned, resulting in the oven locking and turing on at a very high temperature, as though I had set the oven to clean.  However, this happened when the oven and stove were turned off and no one was in the room. Whirlpool (Safety unit) said I could either replace the circuit board or replace the stove.  I was alarmed that the circuit board could malfunction in such a way that the oven would unexpectedly turn on and, apparently, enter the cleaning cycle.
justification: The oven malfunctioned without causing injury, but the potential for harm exists if the issue recurs.

incident_description: My wife and I own a Whirlpool dishwasher Model #GU2548XTPQ3 and Serial #FS0101131. On 09-06-11 my wife started our dishwasher and went to bed. about 10 minutes later our son started screaming for us from the kitchen. As we ran into the kitchen there was smoke filling the room and there were sparks and flames coming from the top of the front latch and electrical panel. I touched the front panel at the start/stop button and tried to turn it off. although the light went out of the front of the panel it continued to spark and create a flame. I quickly ran out of the house and turned off my main control panel and went inside to find a flashlight. After learning which fuse was connected to my dishwasher I turned that one off and then turned my main back on. We then went into the kitchen and found our kitchen filled with smoke but the sparks and fire were out. We also thought it was strange that the door had popped open and water was on the floor.  This was obviously an electrical fire caused by the electrical panel having shorted out. I called whirlpool and they said that they would have a technician come out at no charge to look at and fix our dishwasher. I asked if we would be charged for the technician coming out and they said that they would not be charging for the house call or for the repair, but we would have to pay for the parts. My wife and I have a problem with this considering the fact that if our son had not been home at the time, our home could have been burned down or even worse, we could have been hurt or even killed.I feel that Whirlpool should be held accountable for any product that threatens it's customers lives.
justification: The incident caused smoke and flames, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Microwave Oven Model WMH1162XVQ-2, Serial Number TR Y 14 28532, manufactured April 2009.

When the stove-top light is selected on both the rear right quadrant of the lower surface of the interior oven compartment beneath the turntable as well as the wheeled turntable rack become blistering hot to the touch.  This occurs without the oven being in use, but only with the stove-top light turned on to either the high or low setting.  The white plastic wheel track in our microwave has become discolored (light brown), probably due to the heat build-up.  A factory recommended technician evaluated our oven and admitted that the design flaw lay in the close proximity of the bulb to the oven compartment.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing parts to become blistering hot, posing a burn risk, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: I have a Jenn-air dual fuel range/oven.  The oven is electric and the cook top is gas.  I purchased it in summer 2009.  This summer (2011) as I was broiling a cheese dish, I heard a noise and suddenly a huge amount of gas started spewing out of the unit.  I immediately turned off the oven.  Then I rushed around trying to figure out what to do.  I went out to the gas meter but couldn't figure out how to turn that off.  I called two neighbors for help, neither was home.  I ran down to another neighbor--not home.  I saw a man walking his dog.  I asked for help and he came to my house.  I gave him a wrench and he turned off the gas.  By this time probably 5-7 minutes had passed and the house was full of gas, I opened the windows and hoped the house didn't explode with me and my cats inside.  That was a very frightening experience.  I had the gas company come over and he said he never saw anything like it and red-tagged my unit.  He said there was a shocking amount of gas coming out.  He determined it was coming from the oven and not the gas line from the house.  The service person Jenn-air sent said the same thing...just a huge amount of gas and he couldn't tell where it was coming from in the oven but something inside was wrong.  They took the unit to the shop for repair.  I was without a range for weeks.  In the end I was told that the gas line wasn't installed properly and that every time I opened or closed the oven door it rubbed against the gas line until it was severed hence the large leak!!!  I am worried that if the factory installed the line improperly in my unit, others could face the same frightening and dangerous situation.  Here is the unit info:  Model JDS 9865BDP22  Jenn-air Dual-Fuel Modular Downdraft Slide-In Range Pro Style.  This was an expensive appliance that I regret buying and would never recommend to others.
justification: A large gas leak occurred, posing a significant risk of explosion, but no injury or death resulted.

incident_description:
I turned my oven on 350 to preheat for baking.  Within 3 minutes the lower burner was flaming - flames were 5-6 inches high.  Turned off the oven.  Burner kept flaming.  Had to turn off the power to the range at the breaker.  Burner finally burnt itself out after breaking into multiple pieces. Had I not been standing in the kitchen at the time, this event would have had disastrous consequences. There was nothing in the oven and it was clean. I have had burner elements quit working but have never had one flame the way this one did in over 45 years. 

This range was purchased and installed in February of 2002.  It is a GE Spectra Self-Cleaning Radiant Range, model # JBP67WOD1WW; Serial #DD269836Q.  Online research shows this range has NOT been recalled by GE.  Online research also shows there have been many reports of spontaneous burning of the elements in these models.  I contacted GE about this rather than just replacing the burner myself due to the numerous reports about this model flaming.  They waived the service call charge and sent a technician out.  All he did was replace the burner to the tune of $198.26 - something I could have done for $53.  There were NO diagnostics performed nor was anything else about the range checked. When I asked if he was going to check anything else, the technician's comment was that since the burner turned on properly after he installed it, that meant there was nothing else wrong with the unit. Really?  What a ridiculous statement. Do I trust this stove?  No way.  I will never again leave the kitchen when it is in use for any reason.  It will also be replaced with another model as soon as possible - and it won't be a GE!

This range should have been recalled when these flaming issues first came to light.  At the very least, it needs to be recalled now.  This model is a fire hazard and GE knows it.  That is why they were so quick to respond to my complaint and so quick to waive the 'home call charge' and send a technician.  The fact that all he did was replace the burner at a very high cost to me is a travesty. I had the option to say no when he gave me the cost - however, I thought he was going to really check the range over and make sure there were no electrical shorts or any other problem.  Otherwise I would have said no thanks and gone and bought my replacement burner for $53 and installed it myself.  What a waste. 

Recall these range models before anyone else gets hurt or worse.
justification: The incident involved a flaming oven burner with potential for disaster, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We recently moved to a newly built house by DR Horton on May 31, 2011. My wife was cooking rice and beans [in a pressure cooker] on August 18, 2011 at around 4 pm the burner that was on blew up with a very big noise. My son [REDACTED] who is 10 years old was in his room upstairs and felt the house shaking. The rice and beans flew all over the place. The grill on top of the burner shattered into pieces. The rest of the burners which were off came out of their base. The hot rice and beans stuck my wife's face, eyes, neck and hand causing 1st and 2nd degree burns. Luckily the hot grill pieces did not cause any injuries. We called the GE consumer representative and she said no one could come to look at the stove that day and sent a contractor from A&E the next day morning. On the same evening we called the Texas Gas Company and they did a thorough inspection and ruled out any leaks. The A&E technician came and just said the stove is beyond repair and needs to be replaced. That's it. After calling many times to GE insurance company and customer representatives, GE finally sent a independent forensic engineer from Houston and a insurance adjustor to look at the stove on August 30 but did not give any reason for the blow up. GE has agreed to replace the stove with a newer model. I want a report from GE for the cause of the blowup. I think this could have caused much greater damage and want to prevent further incidents.
justification: The incident caused 1st and 2nd degree burns to the wife, indicating an injury, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the gas range oven he purchased in 2002 has a history of its oven ignition breaking which leads to gas being released when the oven is turned on.  In 2004, he turned on the oven, set the temperature to 350 degrees. He then left the kitchen expecting the oven to light and heat up to the desired temperature, at which point, a single alarm is sounded.  After an extended period of time and not hearing the alarm, the caller returned to the oven and noticed that the temperature gauge noted "low" and there was the smell of gas.  Because it is difficult to see the actual oven flames he was unable to see whether the oven had lit or not.  Other than the "low" reading, there was no warning that ignition was not working and that gas is being released.  The caller turned off the oven.  He called the manufacturer who sent a repair tech the next day who replaced the oven ignition at no cost to the consumer.

In 2006-7 the ignition broke again and manufacturer paid for a repair person to install a new ignition.  In 2009 the ignition broke again.  This time, hoewever, the manufacturer said that as it was an old product, they were not responsible for it.  The caller responded that it was a dangerous situation caused by a dangerous product.  The manufacturer sent a repair technician the next day who replaced the ignition at no cost to the caller.

Most recently, on August 30, 2011, the situation repeated itself.  However this time the manufacturer showed great resistance to repairing the ignition.  After a couple of hours of discussion, the caller had to pay for the service tech to inspect the oven to verify the broken ignition.  After which the manufacturer agreed to pay for the part, but not the installation.  Caller believes this range has a serious life threatening defect.  It should have been recalled and replaced.
justification: The incident involves repeated gas release due to ignition failure, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On April 2,2011 I bought Toaster Oven Broiler from Sears.com. Unfortunately I didn't open package for another couple months. Sears has 90 days satisfaction warranty. In the end of August I tried to return the product because of safety issue, I burned my fingers twice and my wife three times. Sears refused to take product back, claiming expiration of 90 days, so under normal circumstances I wouldn't  dispute my fault with that. The problem is this product  is health hazard. Now here is the problem: on the front there is a handle that you grab to open up the door, right behind the handle there is a metal strip which is a part  of the door frame, this metal strip is about one inch wide and gets extremely hot, now space between the handle and the strip is about one inch. When you grab the handle you  will touch  this hot metal strip with your fingers (outside part between your knuckles and first joint) and burn yourself painfully. There is no way that normal size person can open that door without hurting itself. Now I went to Home Depot to see other models of toasters and amazingly I found  another model  made by the same company that looks almost identical and on the top that same metal strip there is plastic strip that provides insulation so you won't get burned. 
         I would like to add that during phone call conversation Sears.com was fully inform about this specific safety hazard yet as of today Sept. 6, 2011 it is still available on Sears.com.
         On Aug. 26, 2011 I received email from Sears Customer  Care, signed [REDACTED] that they won't take this product back because of 90 days policy, never mentioned or even thank for bringing  such as serious safety issue up.
justification: The description reports multiple instances of burns (injury) due to a design flaw in the toaster oven, indicating a clear safety hazard.

He tried turning on and off but then had to flip the breaker to stop power to the built in stove.

Caller's have had to keep the breaker turned off for fear of fire.
They don't believe that the oven is turning itself back on but do believe that the oven just isn't actually turning off when user turns it off.

incident_description:
We purchased a KitchenAid (Whirlpool) Dishwasher (Model: KUDS01FLSS6, Ser No: FR4614215) on April 19, 2005. 

On August 31, 2010, my wife and I heard a popping noise from our kitchen. It happened again and we smelled smoke. We rushed into the kitchen to find smoke billowing out of the dishwasher. I opened the door and the smoke was coming out of the right-side door vent. I pushed the Cancel button, left the door open, and aired out the kitchen.  Luckily we were home, as our kitchen cabinets would have caught fire.

We had a repairman come out and give us a $400 estimate to replace the control panel and accompanying fuse. I bought the parts online, instead, for $80 and installed them myself. The dishwasher tries to work now, but stops mid-cycle with the 7 blinking lights, showing a heat sensor malfunction. Another repairman came out twice (for $85) to fix it, said I had installed the parts correctly, and left shrugging his shoulders. He said there's nothing wrong with it...just doesn't work. Nice
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no one was injured, so the severity level is 2.

incident_description: This is a GE Profile Dish Washer Model #GSD4330Y73WW Serial#MS818751B.  On 9/3/2011 around 10 PM we started our dishwasher and then went to bed which we often do.  The next morning on 9/4 around 7 am my wife went to the kitchen and the dishwasher was still on heat dry!  The plastic utensils melted and dripped onto the heater.  The entire kitchen was hot and actually smelled hot from the dishwasher.  The dishes were so hot that you could not touch them without getting burned.  I am concerned that this could have caused a fire.  We sometimes start our dishwasher and go away for the day.  Obviously, we will not be doing this anymore.
