The cup was used periodically over the previous days to heat water for tea.  The cup was filled with 2 cups of water and heated for 3 minutes, then removed to the counter where tea bags were steeped to make the tea.  No problems occurred with that use.

The cup was noted as microwave safe.

After reading the October issue of Consumer Reports, I realized I should report this incident.
justification: The glass shattered in the microwave, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The occurrence likelihood is low as the cup was noted as microwave safe and similar incidents are not common.

incident_description:
I am writing to inform you about a serious safety problem.  On September 3, 2011 my wife put some food in our oven to warm it up.  While working in the kitchen she happened to look at the oven and notice light coming out of it.  She opened the oven door to discover the bottom heating element glowing white hot and sending out sparks.  She immediately turned off the oven and removed the food from the oven.  Even with the power turned off to the oven the element continued to glow white-hot and send out sparks like a Fourth of July sparkler.  I grabbed our fire extinguisher, which is rated for electrical fires, and sprayed the burning element.  I emptied the entire extinguisher and it made no difference ÃÂ the element continued to burn and send out sparks.  Since the fire was burning along the element I grabbed a cutter and cut the element.  When the fire reached the end of the cut it then stopped burning.

The stove is a Sears Kenmore Model # 911-95582990 about eleven years old.  The serial number is 9T1-2486420.

This incident is of concern because we could have put food in the oven to cook and not been watching the oven and a fire could have been produced that may have resulted in major damage or even loss of life.  We do not know how common this problem is but if there have been other incidents we believe there should be a recall/replacement of the oven heating elements for these models of Kenmore electric stoves.

I have attached photos of the stove.  The white material you see is from the fire extinguisher.  

Please assist us in informing the proper persons about this potentially serious problem.

Thank you for your assistance,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a dangerous oven malfunction with sparks and potential fire risk, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: Oven over heated to more than 500 degrees and was set to only 375 degrees.  Luckily there was no fire or damage but there very easily could have been
justification: The oven overheated but there was no fire or damage, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
Refrigerator light would not shut off after the door was properly closed. I discovered this after I noticed the light bulb housing in the refrigerator was melted and the refrigerator was hot inside. Caused food to spoil. Possible fire hazard. I purchased the refrigerator new on September 5, 2007 for $2070.56. It is a Kenmore Elite Trio bottom freezer refrigerator. The model #795.77542600 and serial #706KR00029.
Upon researching this appliance failure on the internet I discovered a huge amount of consumers that had the same hazard occur with the same refrigerator.
justification: The incident caused food spoilage and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: On 8/15/2011 my refrigerator door, unexpectedly the right door fell off and onto my wife. Two days later Sears Technician inspected and found the bottom guide pin broken. Reported number [REDACTED] as "Door Fell Off/Safety Report Filed" but no action as to repair or to replace it. I temporary lift the door back up and we are using it with very caution.
justification: The refrigerator door fell onto the wife, indicating an incident occurred, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her dishwasher was smoking. The consumer stated that her dishwasher was set to a heavy cycle and was on for 10 minutes before it started smoking. The consumer opened the door of the washer and it continue to operate. The consumer tried to press the cancel button and the product would not respond. The consumer had to turn off the product by disconnect the power from the circuit breaker.

 The product has a digital interface. The consumer stated that she did not any charring or discoloration to the unit. The consumer tried to operate it again 3 hours later and again the product began to smoke. The consumer stated that the product did not damage her home. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident occurred. There consumer did not see melted plastic by the dishwasher, but it was discolored.

 The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. The consumer called the retailer about the incident on August 4th, 2011. The consumer stated the firm offered to do nothing since it was out of warranty and they had no notes on the issue. The consumer was told by the firm that there was no recall of the product.  The consumer has yet to call the retailer.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking but there was no injury or damage to the home, and the consumer was not harmed.

incident_description: The consumer says that when she turns the oven off, it stays on.  The consumer says that she also gets an E2-F3 code on the digital display.  The consumer says that her husband ends up having to shut off the circuit breaker.  She says it is the only way to get the oven off.  The consumer says the broiler keeps going higher and higher and the entire oven gets hot to the touch.  The consumer has the same brand as listed in recall 09-333.  Her model and serial number not listed in the recall.
justification: The oven malfunction poses a risk of overheating and requires circuit breaker intervention, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: The consumer says that if she left the refrigerator open for more than a minute, she noticed it would smell hot and smelled a burning smell.  The consumer contacted the repair man who asked her to check if the light bulb was loose.  She unscrewed the light bulb out and found a great big hole where it melted the inside of the refrigerator above where the light bulb was.  The manufacturer offered her 30% discount towards a new unit or offered to repair the unit.  The consumer says her concern is that there is no shield to protect the unit from the bulb.  She asked the manufacturer what type of bulb she should have which is a 40 watt appliance bulb which is exactly what she had on it.  She is concerned that the unit may pose a fire hazard.  She says the longer the unit is open the stronger the burning smell coming from it.  A new offer by the manufacturer was 40% or repair.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and melting inside the refrigerator, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We have a wonderful popcorn machine that did a strange thing just tonight.  We had the light on (only), warming up some popcorn in our great popcorn machine that we purchased from you a couple of years ago (in 2008-2009 timeframe), and it nearly burnt our house down--a large fireball and a great deal of smoke that began to fill our house until the short completely burned the wire out and it disconnected.
After we successfully disconnected the machine from power and eliminated the fire hazard, I noted that the cable leading to the popping pot shorted somehow and melted inside the connector that is between the closed top of the unit and the inside of the glass area. I have the burner disconnected now, and have verified that the switches to the turner and the light are unaffected, and the lights and turner still operate.  So the problem was with the wire going from the wiring harness to the popping pot.  The Popcorn Machine was sold to us by Great American Popcorn company in late 2008 or early 2009.  The model number is UE40010.
justification: The incident involved a fireball and smoke but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was successfully contained.

incident_description: While using the self cleaning cycle on my Frigidaire ES340 CONTROL, SELF-CLEANING OVEN WITH CERAMIC COOKTOP, the outside glass in the oven door exploded spraying glass over the kitchen area.
justification: The oven door glass exploded, causing damage but no reported injury.

incident_description:
My Frigidaire refrigerator tripped our GFI outlet in the kitchen while I was away on a business trip.  My wife returned home to find the refrigerator off and everything in the kitchen not working.  I had her unplug everything in the kitchen to determine what was blowing the circuit.  The instant that she plugged the fridge back in the GFI outlet (a separate outlet near... not the same outlet as the fridge) tripped.  I'm very thankful for the protection that GFI outlet provided - without it my wife probably would have been seriously injured.  With the fridge unplugged she was able to have everything else in the kitchen work properly - the electrical wiring in the kitchen has not been modified any time recently and is working properly.

I'm very concerned that this could seriously shock one of my family members or even cause a fire.  We make a point not to run any appliances when we're not at home because a fire could start and kill our dog - we count on our refrigerator to be safe and operate safely while we are not in the home - I'm concerned for the safety of my family (and dog) due to the problems with this Frigidaire appliance.

Clearly there is a short in the wiring or a component of the fridge.  I called customer service and they didn't seem to care that this was a safety issue - they just wanted to sell me an extended warranty.

I'd recommend steering clear of Frigidaire products as they don't stand behind the safety of their products and have some quality issues.
justification: The GFI outlet prevented injury, but the fridge's electrical issue poses a potential shock or fire hazard.

incident_description:
In January 2011, the consumer preheated the oven and put in partially frozen food. A few
minutes later, the oven went into self dean mode, locked and started beeping. The
temperature sensor had gone out and was replaced thru the consumer's extended
warranty.

The consumer was baking cookies and set the timer. After a few minutes she smelled
something burning. She noticed the oven went into self cleaning mode and was beeping.
She says the oven door locked up so she was unable to open it. The cookies became
charred and the oven and kitchen filled with smoke. The consumer says that she had to
shut off the circuit breaker. She says the oven eventually cooled off to the point that she
could get the oven open. The oven interior was coated with black soot.
She contacted the manufacturer who said the unit was not under recall and it would need
to be repaired thru her extended warranty. The consumer also requested a phone number
for someone higher in the company to discuss if the oven could be replaced or repaired so
it would not lock up again if further parts went out. No numbers were provided. The
manufacturer said a complaint could be filed with a supervisor.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused smoke and charred food, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Control knobs on gas range soften or weaken during heavy use of burners and oven. This reaches a point where the flow of gas cannot be controlled leading to boil overs and extremely hot oil. On occasion it was necessary to run for pliers in order to shut off the gas flow.
This happens any time the stove is heavily used and would be a serious danger to children/young adults who might use the range.
My belief is that they are using a plastic with too low a temperature resistence.
Whirlpool Model WFG381LVB
Ser No RY5011690
justification: The incident involves a gas range control issue that could lead to uncontrolled gas flow and boil overs, posing a serious danger, especially to children, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was about to retire to bed she heard a clicking noise coming from the kitchen like the stove  was trying to power on by itself, her son went to investigate and discovered that the stove was emitting sparks from the control knobs.  The stove was disconnected from the gas for safety precaution.

7/11/11 Consumer stated that shetried contacting the manufacturer but each time she would get someone the phone got disconnected and was not able to report it to them.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The stove emitted sparks, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Consumer says that there was smoke was coming out of unit and there was still time left on the timer before it would even stop.  The consumer says that she contacted the manufacturer who told her that it was not there problem and that it is probably a bag issue.  She says there seems to be a problem with the preset buttons.  The consumer says she pushed the popcorn button and walked away for a moment.  She says it still had a bit more time on the timer when it began smoking.  Consumer says the inside of the micorwave is scorched inside and she cleaned it but it still has a strong odor.
justification: Smoke and scorching indicate a malfunction, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Refridgerator light stopped shutting off when doors are closed nor when you push the button that controls the light. Came down stairs this morning to the smell of burning plastic, opened the doors to fridge and it was extremely hot in there and in the freezer. The plastic around the bulbs, the light encasement as well as the liner of the fridge around the light are all brown and burned. The food in both the fridge and freezer were melted and spoiled. My husband had to unplug the it and wait a while before he was able to, with two sets of oven mitts, unscrew the bulbs. I contacted the store that I purchased the product from and they said we are not the first to complain and they gave me all the information that I needed to contact LG. I contacted LG and they said they would send out a service person to replace the parts, I said that wasn't good enough and I told them that the store told us we were not the first to complain and asked why the product was not recalled and the guy said he knows nothing about recalls. An outside service person contacted us to say that he is ordering parts, and when my husband questioned why he didn't need to come and see the fridge first to see what needed to be ordered his response was that they have been getting a ton of service calls on this and that the issue was the relay board, light assembly, etc. I think that if we weren't home we may have had a fire.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The consumer says that her husband was making meatloaf, when sparks and flames came out of the back of the control panel.  She said there was smoke all over her kitchen.  She says the unit may have been on for at least 15-20 minutes. They contacted the manufacturer who informed them that their particular model is not by the recall. They offered to send a technician for a fee.  The consumer said she has already had a burner replaced and something on the control panel about four years ago. The model and serial number fall just outside of the recall in release # 09-333
justification: Sparks and flames from the control panel caused smoke but no reported injuries, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: The past three times that we have run our Kenmore dishwasher it has produced a burning smell and white smoke during the wash part of the "smart wash" cycle.  The smell is coming from around the control panel and not from within the dishwasher.  Each time the smell and smoke got worse.  The last time we used it the smoke filled our kitchen.  We have stopped the dishwasher mid-cycle each time it has happened and are no longer using the dishwasher.  We have consulted a repairman who said this was a recurring problem with Kenmore dishwashers manufactured by Whirlpool during this time period and that we should discontinue use because it is a fire hazard.
justification: The dishwasher produces smoke and a burning smell, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Kenmore Ultra Bake Super Capacity Electric Glass Top Range.  While cooking a pork loin I walked into the kitchen and saw an error code on the electronic display.  The bake element had shut off but the broiling element was raging.  I left the door open and did a quick error code search.  Most suggested replacing the control board.  20 minutes later the broiler was still on so I flipped off the breaker.   Once cool I flipped it back on and same thing.  More research showed me this is a recurring proplem with many similar units but different serial numbers.  I haven't been able to find a recall notice.  I thank God I was home and cooking when it happened because several other people have mentioned not even using the range and realizing the broiler was raging.  My model number is 95792000 and serial number is RK0811206.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that could have led to a fire or injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Kenmore Convection range from sears in Feb 2009 for $1,000.  About a month ago when trying to make dinner I couldn't get the oven temperature  to heat up to 300 degrees. Today a repairman came out and found the clock assembly wires had melted and fried. After the last time I used the oven, we noticed what we thought smelled like burning rubber, but couldn't figure out where it was coming from. A new clock assembly will cost us $200.  I've been battling with Sears but getting nowhere.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven with melted wires but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
A few days ago, while I was removing my Anchor Hocking 5-quart glass baking dish from the cabinet where it was stored, the dish suddenly shattered in my hand, spreading large and small pieces of glass all over my kitchen floor, the cabinet where I had stored the dish, and other dishes in the cabinet. A couple of small shards cut my bare foot and fingers. I backed away from the debris field carefully to prevent more injury, put on shoes, and then photographed the damage before sweeping up the floor, emptying the cabinet, and cleaning out the rest of the cabinet dishes and stuff. I am attaching a couple of the photos for you to look at.

I threw the glass pieces into the garbage and then contacted the manufacturer on their website. When I received a reply from the company requesting I send them the broken glass I collected the broken glass from the garbage and placed it for safe keeping in a plastic bag in a box. I still have the box with the broken pieces of glass.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (cuts on foot and fingers), warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) as spontaneous glass shattering is not a common occurrence.

incident_description: I had an Anchor Hocking 9 x 13 baking dish explode.  I made 2 casseroles at the same time and each one went through the same process.  The older dish was fine and the newer one exploded.  This happened just minutes before my daughter's wedding.  I was planning on serving the casseroles for a brunch after the service.  Thankfully, nobody was injured.
justification: The baking dish exploded but no one was injured, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description: My mom got two fingers of her right hand burned with the copper resistor of an electric skillet. She was going to unplug the cable with the left hand, and grabbed the skillet from the side with the right hand and got burned. She said that the resistor is located underneath the skillet, by the handle, and since it is exposed, it represents a high risk for the user to get burned.
justification: The incident resulted in burns to two fingers, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The exposed resistor and user behavior suggest a likely recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
We have a KitchenAid Diswasher purchased in October of 2004.  It is listed with a model number of KUDS01FLSS. This past Monday evening (August 29, 2011) it started on fire, spontaneously emitting smoke and flames. 

The dishwasher had been turned on before retiring for bed and was running for about 40 minutes when I heard an unusual noise from the machine.  I went to check on it in the kitchen a few moments later, and there was an odd burning smell and a significant amount of smoke coming out from the right side of the door.  I quickly opened the door in a panic.  A lot of water sprayed out (as it appears that the machine was still running) and a flame shot out as well.  Thankfully, the water put out the flames quickly.  The smoke and flames stopped shortly after the door was opened and the machine stopped running.  We are assuming it was a hidden electronic panel in the door that melted or caught fire, but we cannot be sure.

My husband called KitchenAid the following day to report this, and the representative indicated they did not know anything about any problems with thier dishwashers. They did offer a 15% discount on another Kitchenaide machine, however, right now we are too frightened to buy another Kitchenaide dishwasher.  We have children, and are horrified to think what would have occurred had I not seen the problem quickly and shut the machine off.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, emitting smoke and flames, but no injuries were reported. The incident was contained quickly.

incident_description: I turned on my KitchenAid dishwasher, model# KUDS01IJBLO, and 7-10 minutes later it made a clicking sound and then a loud popping sound.  I went over to see what was wrong and it started pouring flames out of the top of the door over where the circuit board is located.  The display went out and I quickly opened the door to stop the cycle.  I grabbed a box of baking soda and doused the flames with it which did put them out.  Then very black thick smoke was pouring out of the top where the flames had been.  My son ran to the basement and cut the power to the dishwasher and the smoke continued to  pour out that I thought it would catch fire again.  My entire downstairs smelled of an electrical fire for days.  I found out that KitchenAid has known about this problem, but has made a conscious decision not to do anything about it.  My house could've easily burned down had I no been RIGHT THERE in the kitchen - it happened so fast.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required immediate presence to prevent escalation.

incident_description:
[REDACTED]
Kenmore smooth-top stove
Model # 790.96122400     Serial # VF71312364

My wife and I purchased a Kenmore stove on 02-18-07 as part of a kitchen remodeling project. It was delivered on 03-16-07. It worked adequately until last week, when my wife noticed that the right rear burner was coming on by itself [control knob was off]. After it happened a few times, we started turning the circuit breaker off in the basement, after using the stove each time. It is very inconvenient, but we could not take the chance that the stove would come on during the night or when we were out of the house.

I googled the stove problem and discovered that Sears and CPSC have an active recall concerning this problem. But, our stove's model and serial number are not included in the recall list. When I contacted Sears, they confirmed that our stove is not part of the recall. But, when I described the problem, they believed that it should be. They said they would pass the data along to CPSC and suggested that I initiate a CPSC report.

I initiated a report 2 days ago, but it got lost on the CPSC website [20110829-D60C2-2147475838]. I spoke to several people at CPSC, and they could not locate it. So, here is another one.

I believe that the problem with our stove is identical with the ones identified in the recall. I also believe that our model and/or serial number should be added to the recall list. We have just been lucky that the problem did not surface before now.

We are quite anxious to get this problem fixed as soon as possible for a variety of reasons - safety, wasted money on electricity, inconvenience, etc. Your efforts to resolve this issue as expeditiously as possible, would be appreciated.

Gratefully yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The stove turning on by itself poses a safety hazard but no injury has been reported yet, and the issue is known to occur based on the recall and user report.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the edge of her electric oven range stove has very sharp edged and no measures are taken to make the product safer. The product is located close to her sink and has to frequently come in close contact with the range. The consumer cut herself in her left leg while moving  passed the product. The cut was 4 inches across the calf muscle. The consumer has a permanent scar on her leg. The consumer placed pressure on the cut at the time of the incident and did not get any stitches nor did she see a doctor. The consumer went to the doctor in October of 2010, sometime after the incident and was given a shot to ensure she did not have an infection. Consumer called the firm immediately after the incident happened. The firm gave her a claim number and sent a contracted company that came to her home in October and file a report about the range and the incident. The consumer gave the investigator pictures of the incident. The consumer has not heard anything from the company since then. The product is a self standing smooth top oven with an electric range. 

Consumer contacted Sears, then Sears referred her to Electrolux, the manufacturer, and Electrolux referred her case to
Crawford & Company. She had contacted Electrolux and Crawford & Company on several occasions for a response. As of August 19,2011 there has not been a resolution for the injury.

Consumer is very disappointed that the company did not replace the dangerous oven for a safer one. The edges around the oven range door are extremly sharp. She is very disturbed that she will have a permanent scar on her leg (work in a professional business envirorunent where I wear skirts and dresses) and the company does not appear to have any concerns of preventing future injuries. More importantly, this unsafe product should not have been released for consumers to purchase. Just recently, her son received a minor cut on his finger just by opening the oven door.

She believes there should be a recall on these types of Kerunore Oven Range. This is a serious matter, and Electrolux needs to be held accountable for it.
justification: The consumer sustained a 4-inch cut with a permanent scar, and her son also received a minor cut, indicating repeated injuries from the product.

incident_description: I have a black and decker counter top oven and a fire started inside the coils.  There is no way to remove the coils to clean them.
justification: A fire started inside the coils, indicating an incident with no reported injury, and the inability to clean the coils suggests a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
While baking a dish inside of the oven on 350 degrees for approximately an hour the consumer noticed smoke pouring from inside of the oven and the food baking inside had caught fire. He attempted to power the oven in the off position but it would not power off and that was when he noticed that the setting had switched to broil without him changing it.

He then used a hand towel to put the fire out. The circuit breaker was then powered in the off position to power the range in the off position. He waited approximately ten minutes and powered the circuit breaker back into the on position and noticed that the oven also powered back into the on position on the broil setting without being switched on.


The firm was contacted on the same date of the incident and a service technician was scheduled to come out to the consumerÃÂs home on 8/4/2011. On 8/4/2011 a service technician came out to the home and indicated that the control modular needed to be replace and the consumer was provided with the price for the labor and parts. 

While the service technician was there the consumer contacted the firm again in reference to the price that he was going to be charged for the repairs. The representative that the consumer spoke with (name is unknown) advised the consumer that his appliance did not fall under any recalls and he would be required to pay out of pocket.

 The consumer declined on having the appliance required and has unplugged the range from the wall outlet and has not used it since the date of the failure. He did not indicate if he would make any repairs on the unit and or replace it.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, and the issue was resolved without further harm.

incident_description:
we are an apartment management company and have expirienced problems with GE dishwashers HDA2100R20CC

we just recently had a second dishwasher of this model burn a hole thru the front panel

We are scheduled to meet with GE later this week
justification: The incident involves a dishwasher burning a hole through the front panel, which is a property damage issue with no reported injuries.

incident_description: Purchased a Hamilton Beach microwave approx 4 months ago. I mailed in warranty card. Today while baking a potato on a microwaveable plate and the plate caught fire after approx 2 minutes. I contacted the company and was advised warranty cards do no matter, even though it is supposed to have a year warranty. When I questioned why the card was disregarded, the representative said they do not honor warranty on any microwave without all the original packaging and receipts, even when warranty registrations have been filed. I explained the danger of the microwave and the rep replied, 'you should have educated yourself about our policies, prior to purchasing our product. We will do nothing.'
justification: The microwave plate caught fire, but no injury was reported. The issue is possible but not frequent based on the description.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she turned on the bottom oven of her electric double wall oven into self cleaning mode and the glass door of the oven exploded. The consumer stated that this a convection oven and does not know if glass will blow into the food in her oven moving forward. The consumer set the oven to self cleaning mode at 500 degrees and left her kitchen. She was away from her kitchen for about 20 minutes when she heard the oven explode and returned to the kitchen. The product was installed in November of 2009. 

The consumer stated that hot pieces of glass were on the floor. They flew out through the bottom where the hinges are - while the door was closed.  The consumer found that there is no charring or discoloration to the product and has not caused damage to the structure of her home. Luckily, no one was harmed or injured by the product.  The consumer called the manufacturer on Friday August 5th and today. The firm offered to give her 50% off on a replacement part only. 

The firm has acknowledged this happening before. The consumer has done research and found similar reports on this before. The consumer called the retailer on August 5th and today. The retailer offered her no further assistance.
justification: The incident involved an oven door exploding, but no one was harmed or injured, fitting severity level 2. The firm acknowledged similar past incidents, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer had the home built and the builder purchased the dishwasher  in April  of 2003 but she is unaware of where it was purchased from.
The dishwasher was placed on the light and heated dry cycle and half way through the cycle  when she noticed black and brown smoke coming from the control panel  and there was a terrible plastic burning odor. 

Within in a matter of minutes the right hand side of the  control panel  caught fire. She attempted to power the unit in the off position but it would not power off. There was a toggle switch under the kitchen sink that was pulled to power the unit in the off position and the circuit breaker was also powered in the off position to cease all power.  Once the all power was ceased the flames went out and shortly after the smoke dissipated. 

On 8/9/2011 the consumerÃÂs husband removed the control panel and noticed that all the wires and circuit boards  were burned  and melted together. The same date the dishwasher was removed from the home by a retailer that the consumer purchased a new dishwasher from. The consumer kept the control panel and also has pictures of the unit. 

On 8/12/2011 the firm was contacted in regards to the fire that started inside of the dishwasher the representative  that the consumer spoke with [REDACTED] advised the consumer that they would have replace the dishwasher free at charge.

Kitchen Aid representative contacted consumer on Monday 8/15/2011 and offered consumer $100 towards purchase of a new [REDACTED] dishwasher. In return, they requested a copy of the Bill of Sale for the new machine and the Burnt Up Control Panel. Consumer has decided to keep the control panel in their possession until they hear from CPSC. They will keep this panel for at least the recommended 30 days.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
While opening the oven door on the stove the handle fell off and the oven door came apart in my hands.  It just sort of exploded out on me.  I had been roasting meat at 450 degrees when this occurred.  As the door fell down it hit me on the shin slicing my leg open.  

The cut looked deep and is approx. 2 - 21/2 inches long.  I went to the local Emergency room and received six stitches and a tetanus shot.

Prior to this incident I did not experience any problems with the door or the door handle.  

The oven is a self cleaning, convection range in a stainless steel finish.  The metal part of the door with the glass window in it separated from the interior door that keeps the heat in the oven.  The bolts that hold the handle on just fell on the floor.   Neither of the bolts appear to be broken or damaged.
 I had the oven on for approximately 1 hr. at 450 degrees. 

We cannot figure out why the door separated.  Had a child been in front of the door when that happened I believe the force could have done serious perhaps fatal damage.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut requiring stitches, indicating an injury, and the description suggests potential for more severe outcomes if a child had been involved.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his digital microwave would not turn off after the consumer opened the microwave door. The product is a over the counter. The consumer stated that his wife had placed a ceramic cup frozen vegetables in the microwave for roughly 8 minutes until they noticed that the food had caught fire in the microwave. The consumer opened the microwave door the and microwave was still on the consumer placed his hand in the microwave while it was operating and is unsure if he sustained any injury but otherwise had sustained no other injuries.

 The consumer to put out the fire had to first unplug the microwave from the outlet to power it off and shut the door of the microwave to put the fire out. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident. The consumer stated that there was smoke in his home after the incident but otherwise there is no damage to his home. The consumer reported that there is smoke residue in the microwave. The consumer stated he has not seen a physician after the incident. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer.
justification: The consumer sustained potential injury from placing his hand in the operating microwave, and the incident involved a fire, indicating a moderate severity with unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was using the dishwasher for approximately two hours, it was on the drying cycle when her son alerted her that he smelled smoke, she discovered that there was flames emitting from the door handle and the control panel.  Consumer had to use a fire extinquisher to put the flames out and called the fire department who advised that the control panel had malfunctioned and to call the company to see if it had been recalled.  A fire report was filed.

Consumer stated that the front of the dishwasher was charred but the inside remained intact.  There were no damages to the countertop or her cabinets.

Consumer experienced the same problems of Release #09-100.

8/1/11  Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that a representative would be sent out to take pictures of the damaged dishwasher, but no one came.
justification: The incident involved flames and required a fire extinguisher, but there were no injuries or damages beyond the dishwasher itself.

incident_description:
I had made coffee in my Cuisinart DCC-1200 electric coffee maker. I had poured myself a cup of coffee and left another couple of cups in the carafe on the coffee maker's heating element.  After some time I heard a strange sound from the direction of the coffee maker, as if something was bubbling.  I looked and saw that the coffee was boiling vigorously.  I ran to the coffee maker to turn it off and unplug it, and as I did so it began to smoke and release a smell as of burning plastic.  The bottom of the coffee maker was extremely hot, and the smoke appeared to be coming from the point where the cord enters the back of the machine.  Fearing that it might still burst into flame even though unplugged (and not wanting my kitchen to be filled with noxious fumes) I took it outside to cool off.

A searh of the internet revealed a number of other recent reports of identical problems with this and related models. See http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html (Ignore the first item about a popcorn maker.)
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning coffee maker that produced smoke and a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: LG refrigerator,french doors, bottom freezer, Model # LRFC25750ST, new in 2006.  Interior lights became so hot that they melted the plastic digital sensor control unit housing causing it to fall on to the shelf.  I assume this was caused by the lights not turning off when the door closes.  The unit is beyond repair and must be replaced. Real fire hazard if a fire can start inside a refrigerator.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard due to overheating lights, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I preheated my Kenmore range as usual, put in a cake and shortly ( about 5 minutes) began hearing it sizzle.  Looked in and it was starting to burn because the top element was on. It normally is not on during bake. Thinking I had hit broil by mistake, I turned it off and on again to bake.  When I opened it again, the top element was again heating, so I turned it completely off, but the burner kept heating!  I could not reach the plug, so I turned off the breaker.  A couple of hours later, when we turned the breaker back on, the stove element began to heat again even though the stove had not been turned on.  I read online of the same thing happening to others with Kenmore stoves.  As long as this stove is plugged in, the element will continue to heat without ever going off.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning stove that could lead to a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Kenmore electric built in oven, purchased and installed 3/24/10.  Turned oven on to 350 to preheat, oven door exploded sending glass flying in all directions.
justification: The oven door exploded, sending glass flying, which poses a significant risk of injury.

incident_description:
Home was built in 2007 and first occupied July 1, 2007.  The builder-provided (upgraded) GE Profile Dishwasher (Model PDW9980N00SS) in our $44,000 "French Kitchen" overheated during dry cycle, causing all plastic contents including utensils, silverware racks and water-distribution spindle arms to melt.  Several dishes were cracked with the heat, and the handles of several utensils melted to the point that they were unusable and had to be thrown away.

Heat was such that the 1" thick granite countertop above the dishwasher became too hot to touch, as did the solid cherry cabinetry surrounding the unit.  My wife sustained minor burns to her fingertips as she leaned on the countertop to open the unit and turn it off manually.
Unit would not turn off manually, and we had to rush and disconnect power at the breaker.

GE have told us that our unit is not covered under the 2 recalls, even though the recall dated October 26, 2010 (Release #11-022) shows an exact picture of our unit.  The GE agent told me on the phone "Well, because of the recall we changed the model numbers, and yours is newer and isn't covered."  I asked if the actual unit had been changed or modified to make it safer, and I was told "No, - it's the same and just the model number was changed."  GE declined all responsibility and refused any repair or replacement assistance.

Several weeks subsequent to the incident, after working on the electrical supply to a newly added outlet elsewhere in the house, the electrician unknowingly turned all the breakers back on when he restored power.  Unknown to anyone, the dishwasher unaccountably began to heat up again even though it was turned off, had not been touched, and the door was tied shut.  Again the heat was so intense that it almost caught fire, and we were only alerted because of the smell of scorching cabinetry and burning plastic.  Had nobody been home, the entire house could well have caught fire, incinerated our pets and belongings, and potentially burned to the ground. 

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident caused minor burns to the wife's fingertips and had the potential to cause a house fire, which could have led to more severe injuries or death.

incident_description: The consumer says he has had the same problem crop up three times.  He says the interior light stays on, even after closing the door.  The consumer says the plastic covering melts and there is a burning smell.  The consumer says the first two times this occurred, he removed the bulbs and left them out for 24-48 hours.  He says after putting them back in, they would once again work properly.  The consumer says the unit inside is very very warm.  The consumer says he has not had any problems with spoiled food as of yet.  He says that currently there are no bulbs in the unit.
justification: The incident involves a recurring electrical issue causing overheating and a burning smell, but no injury or property damage has occurred yet.

incident_description: Tonight, I cut inside of my mouth with a brand new soup spoon with a plastic handle, bought at a kitchen specialty store, "Genevieve Lethu" at 900 N Michigan Ave, Chicago, IL 60611, yesterday on 8-25-11. The spoon was made in France with engraved mark which says "INDX MADE IN FRANCE".  I was eating a bowl of soup with the spoon when I felt a sharp pain in my mouth. There was a cut, inside my cheek, like a cut made by razer blade - but it was the edge of the spoon made the cut. I looked at the spoon and realized that the edge of the spoon was coarse yet sharp. I intend to report the incident to the store tomorrow so that other people will not get hurt by buying and using the same type of spoon at the store. I am reporting the incident so that the store will act on this promptly and properly.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut inside the mouth, which qualifies as an injury, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) since the defect appears to be specific to this spoon rather than a widespread issue.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite Trio Refrigerator. I have noticed recently that my food was not staying cold. One morning I noticed that the light was still on, but the door was closed. Opening the door, the refrigerator was very hot, and the lights had melted the top of the refrigerator. In trying to remove the lightbulbs, I had burned myself slightly from accidentally touching the plastic, even though I was using a dish towel folded over a few times. I had to use an oven mitt because the lights were so hot, and it almost burned through the oven mitt, which had started smoking after just a couple seconds of contact. I looked online, and saw that this is a very common problem for these refrigerators. I am glad I found the problem before it caught fire -- this is a very dangerous issue.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burn) and potential for fire, indicating a significant hazard. Online reports suggest this is a common issue, increasing likelihood.

incident_description:
My Kenmore dishwasher on Sunday, August 28,2011 sounded like a transformer exploded.  When I looked to see what the noise was I saw a lot of smoke coming out of the front of the dishwasher..  The kitchen & family room filled with smoke.  Thank God I did not see flames.

My model # 665 15835792 
     Serial  # FH3201925 15835

I have read online about a lot of these Kenmore & Whirlpool dishwashers having the same problem, but they are different model #'s than mine.  I believe these model number and serial #'s need to be 
recalled also.  This was a very frightening experience.
justification: The incident involved smoke but no flames or injuries, and similar issues have been reported with other models, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore EliteTrio mfg by LG, that I bought in 2007, Model 795. 77564600.  Two weeks ago, I noticed the smell of burnt plastic and electrical wires.  After opening the food doors, the light housing was completely melted from its housing.  Minuplating the door switches had no effect, so I burnt my hands unscrewing the bulbs out.  One burst in my hands because of the heat and sprayed glass all over the referigator.  I ordered the parts myself hoping that replacement parts would fix the problem.  When the parts came in I had a refigerator repairman come out to insall them.  After he did, the problem still existed, the lights stayed on.  He said to order new switches for the doors and he would install them.  After he left, I did some extensive research on the internet, and found out there are hundreds of complaints of this nature, and the main cause of this problem was a faulty realy in the computer board. 
I emailed "Sears Cares", and wrote a letter to Sears Cares, with pictures and received no response whatsoever  I hate to think what might have happened if I was on a long vaction,etc, and It would not have been discovered early.
As a former Fire Chief, I find it incomprehensible that Sears has not addressed this FIRE HAZZARD!
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and minor injury (burnt hands), but no severe injury or death. The likelihood is high given the numerous similar complaints.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Trio #77309 . While upstairs, I smelled burning, like an electrical fire. I located the source in the downstairs kitchen.  It was coming from the Kenmore Trio.  I opened the door and realized the top shelf was warm.  Then I realized that the plastic housing around the lights had melted.
I could not touch the lights, they were too hot.  Also, the housing where the bulb screws in had turned brown and melted, making it very difficult to remove the lights.  Eventually, using a silicon pot holder I was able to remove the lights.  I think that had I not been home, and observant, this could have caused an electrical fire.  I have not put the lights back in, because I think it is too dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual fire or injury, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with current conditions.

incident_description:
I had my Pyrex 9x13 inch baking dish in the oven - baking at 375 degrees for 30 minutes with chicken and sauce.  I took it out of the oven and the dish exploded - sending large and small glass shards everywhere.  It was very dangerous - I got cut on my foot, leg and hand and the extremely hot chicken and sauce was hard to handle as well.  There was nothing unusual about it - I have cooked this dish many times.  No warning whatsoever - just a loud pop and glass shards went flying everywhere.  
I cleaned out the glass, but I still hurts.  I may have some glass embedded in my thigh.  I may need to see a doctor.  I had company over and couldn't leave to go to an emergency room.  I am so thankful that there were no children around.  
I found a bunch of similar complaints on consumeraffairs.com.  I will NEVER buy this type of product again.  It is very dangerous that the glass is so unstable and shatters without warning at a normal baking temperature.  Thank god nothing flew in my eyes or injured my children.  Very frightening.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring potential medical attention, and similar complaints suggest a recurring issue.

incident_description:
I ran my GE Dishwasher (Model = PDW7300N10WW Serial Number = MM723742B) during the afternoon.  The dishwasher completed its cycle and turned off.  The next morning (approximately 18 hours later), I awoke to find my kitchen countertop extremely hot.  When I opened the dishwasher, it was continuing to produce heat.  The dishes were too hot to touch and the heating coil at the bottom was turning white.  We turned off the circuit breaker and contacted GE Service.

The GE repairman indicated that the module control (Part#WD21X10372) was defective.  The part was ordered and replaced.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, producing excessive heat, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a dishwasher that was serviced due to a recall for fire hazard a year ago. This past weekend I smelled something burning when it was running and when I went to unplug it a big electrical arc occured. I tried to call Maytag but they were unhelpful.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and an electrical arc, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Control board on Kitchen Aid dishwasher is burnt/charred near the area of the thermal overload/fuse.  I'm assuming the board caught fire, or came very close, based on the damage to it in this area, but I was not home when it happened.
justification: The control board shows signs of fire damage, indicating an incident occurred, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I own a Whirlpool electric range which was purchased in 2009, model wfe301lvs 0 and serial number ry3141305.  I turned the unit on, heard a loud pop, and then smoke and flames were coming from the electrical panel where the knobs and settings are inputed.
justification: The incident involved smoke and flames from the electrical panel, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
We purchased a Fridgedaire Electric Smoothtop Stovetop in 2007.  

Model #FEC30S6ASF (which is not listed on the 2 existing Recall Lists Release #09-333 dated 8/27/09 & Release #11-016 dated 10/21/10).  

However, the Serial #NF71020590 is within the range of the S/Ns that were recalled and the stove top is experiencing the same issues:

1) Fails to turn off after being switched off 
2) Heats to different temperatures than selected and 
3) Recently started sparking and making a crackling noise beneath the stovetop as if it were going to catch on fire.
justification: The stove is malfunctioning and poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while her 2 1/2 year old grand daughter was drinking out of the Sippy cup her bottom lip was caught between the soft spout and the hard cup causing her to receive a minor laceration.  First aid was administered to the child.  Consumer stated that this was the second occurrence, the first incident did not leave a mark.

Consumer stated that the second incident she had to ease the child's lip from the cup.

Consumer attempted to contact the manufacturer and receive the voicemail but didnot leave a message.

Consumer feels that this product is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor laceration requiring first aid, and it was the second occurrence, indicating a pattern.

incident_description:
Dishwasher overheated, smoked and flames came out of button input area.

Whirlpool dishwasher Gold Quiet Partner III

MOD 
GU2500XTP81

SER
FR3801667
justification: The dishwasher overheated and produced smoke and flames, indicating an incident with potential for harm, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: relay burned on whirlpool side by side refrigerator.  melted and charred.  manufactured 2003. was not on the recall. model ED5TNXMQ, serial SP3060326.
justification: The relay burned and caused damage to the refrigerator, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
I moved to a 2 year old house that has a Thermador double oven model SMW272yp. Progressively the digital display got dimmer to the point that today you cannot see the numbers, thus cannot set the oven temperature, rendering the over pretty much unusable.  These ovens are expensive; I understand over $2000.
Upon consulting with an authorized technician for Thermador he said that this is a known problem and that many, if not all, displays suffer from this dimming issue. Thermador is aware of the problem but has never issued a recall.
I check on the web for ÃÂThermador dimming displayÃÂ and confirmed that there are hundreds of complaints from customers with the same problem.
I contacted Thermador Customer Service and they said that they can provide a new display kit that replaces the defective one but at a cost of $288.
I also found several cases on the web that mentioned that they have installed this new kit to find, within one or two years, that the display dims again.
I believe that this is a known design problem and the ovens should be recalled or at least Thermador should send the parts to the customers without cost and cover the repair service.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven display with no reported injuries or deaths, but it is a widespread issue affecting many customers.

incident_description:
Coffee for the evening was in the carafe for about 2 hours. I heard noise across the room and discovered the coffee
in the carafe was boiling, and smoke was coming from the bottom of the coffeemaker. I immediately unplugged
the coffeemaker and moved it next to the stove exhaust fan. If I had not been in the same room, I seriously believe
that a fire would have started. Fortunately, no injuries were sustained.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the clear potential for recurrence if left unattended.

incident_description: Overheating broiler element in Kenmore 665.95792000 range.
justification: Overheating broiler element is an incident that could lead to potential fire hazard, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: On August 24th, went to my kitchen and cooked a sausage in a little water for 2 mins. Sat down to eat my lunch and 10 minutes later, I heard a pop from my kitchen, I asked my husband if something fell upstairs, he stated no, as I was getting up from the couch and he started coming down the stairs and noticed smoke from the kitchen. The microwave touch pad was on fire. I turned the breaker switch off for that plug and he unplugged the microwave. He went and grabbed the fire extinguisher and put out the fire. He then grabbed the microwave using hot pad mittens and took it outside. I opened all the windows and doors. I purchased our Kenmore Microwave in 1999. I have never had a microwave do this before.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but was quickly contained without injury, and the microwave was old (purchased in 1999), suggesting such events are unlikely.

incident_description:
The microwave was in the home prior to the consumer moving into it. 

Shortly after placing a dish inside the microwave to heat up (the exact amount of time the microwave was placed on is unknown) within 10 seconds after the microwave was started she saw sparks flying from the metal rack that is located inside of the microwave. 

She opened the microwave door and the sparks went away. She currently still uses the microwave but has since then removed the metal rack to prevent any hazard. 

Prior to the incident occuring she contacted the firm because she leard from a home inspector that the microwave was once affected by a recall (unable to locate the exact recall reflecting the model number provided) she was advised by the representative from the firm that if the repairs were already made to the unit there would be a green sticker located near the model number. 

She did locate the sticker.  She tried again to contact the firm but only gets recordings which indicate the green sticker shows repairs were made.
justification: The incident involved sparks but no injury occurred, and the hazard was mitigated by removing the metal rack.

incident_description: We have a Kitchen AId cooktop (PN KGCT366GBL1).  During dinner the glass cooktop spontaneously exploded shooting bits of glass throughout our kitchen.  Luckily there was nothing on top of the cooktop or our children werent near.  One of my smaller children did suffer a minor cut on his foot from teh glass on the floor.  When we called Kitchen Aid, they had little concern about how dangerous the product was, but quickly had someone from their "safety" group try to get something on record so they wouldnt have any liability.  When I told them the danger of spontaneous exploding glass, they said they have heard of this before, but "that's what happens with glass".  If they know the danger of such an event this product and all of its kind should be recalled immediately.  Obviously they told me they wouldnt replace the stove nor pay for its repair.  They did send an authorized repair service ([REDACTED]) and they said it was conclusive the product exploded through no fault of my own, but this product is not very sturdy (although at the time we paid almost $1000 for the product) and that we would have no luck or support from Kitchen Aid (from his experience).  After looking at the web we saw many more instances (one example: http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/kit_stoves.html).  I request that Kitchen Aid either put a warning on all their glass cooktops for sale and immediately do a recall to protect consumers from any future injuries.
justification: A child suffered a minor cut from the glass, indicating an injury occurred. The company acknowledged previous similar incidents, suggesting a possible but not certain likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his dishwasher was smoking in the early hours of the morning while his family was asleep. The consumer stated that his wife was using the dishwasher in the afternoon the day and noticed that the washer was unusually hot after it ran it's normal cycle of 45 minutes. She left the door of the dishwasher open ajar so that the machine would be off and left the kitchen. The consumer stated that his family woke to find smoke had filled the kitchen. The consumer thinks the product apparently started a cycle on its own.

 The consumer's wife and her son and two daughters were not injured or harmed by the product but had to go shut off the circuit breaker to ensure the product was off. The dishwasher has melted plastic throughout the inside. Luckily, the damage did not spread to the structure of the consumer's home. The consumer's wife opted not to call the fire department. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer and since the product was originally in the home when he bought it he doesnÃÂt know the retailer. 

The consumer stated that the product has never been serviced. While doing some research, the consumer found that similar models like his were recalled in release 11-022 also for a fire hazard.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and caused damage but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the family was able to safely address the situation.

incident_description:
Samsung Microwave, Model SMH9187ST, Serial Number JALV7MZ400917H, Made April 10. Used microwave to heatup meatballs. Set it up where the glass tray inside would not go around. Had 55 seconds left - went into the other room and noticed a buring smell. Came back into the kitchen and the inside of the microswave was engulfed in flames. The fire burnt itself out - found that the pyrex glass dish containing the meatballs had melted into the microwaves' glass tray. Lifted the microwaves glass tray and noticed that 1/2 of the the roller guide ring's center holding up the glass tray was melted. 

Reported incident to Sears - but since it was 2-3 months past the 12 months warranty, they were of no real help. 

Wanted to let you know about the product. 

Never had a problem with the product before.
justification: The incident involved a fire inside the microwave but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Electric Range -model 790.99129405
Right front burner came on by itself and stays lit. Cannot use the stove top or oven. Must keep it unplugged.
It is a fire hazard!!
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
After using the range for dinner and turning it off i noticed a smell of smoke in the house, so I checked the range and the display indicated that is was off.  Later the smell got much worse andthis time I actually opened the oven door even though it indicated that it was off and I noticed the broiler elment red hot and the oven very hot.  I attemted to turn it off by pressing the oven button and on and then off and the broiler button on then off but it would not go off.  I turned the breaker off to the unit.  About an hour later and also the next day I cycle the breaker and even though the range display showed it being off the broiler came on.  

From a suggestion of a friend, I seached this site for a recall but none was found on this unit, however, there were multiple reports of the same or similar units with the same problem.  The following Incident numbers are from my search: 20110707-3571D-1190453, 20110708-596F0-2147477416, 20110709-70C32-2147477388, 20110510-F4A4E-2147479305, and 20110427-8582D-2147479723.  From my reseach these are all in the same model group and the model prefix of 665 indicates they were made by Whirlpool.  

I have been in touch with the Sears Kenmore Executive Customer Relations department and they are still in the process of reviewing my complaint.  It's my opinion that the problem is due to a defective manufacturing process of the control circuit board and repairing the product with a replacement board does not solve the problem of this being a dangerously defective device.  The product should be recalled and if an upgraded circuit board is not manufactured the the manufacturer and retailer need to compensate the product owners for the balance of the reasonable product lifespan.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning range that could potentially cause a fire, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer said that her tenant  called her on 08/04/2011 to report to that his refrigerator top freezer did not closed properly; therefore his food will spoiled. 

Consumer said that refrigerator had been served for 3 occasions for similar issues. On 07/31 was the last time that the refrigerator was served by the mfr. the issues that time was the refrigeratorÃÂs door had a gap and not let the door closed properly.

Consumer called and explained incident to mfrÃÂs rep. (name unknown) who said that the product is no longer under warranty.

Consumer feels that her refrigerator could pose an unsafe health issues.

No injury
justification: No injury reported, but the refrigerator malfunction could lead to food spoilage, posing potential health risks.

incident_description: The consumer says the glass oven door exploded overnight.  The consumer says this happened in the middle of the night and was not in use.  The consumer says the last time she used the range was two days prior to the incident.  The consumer says the outside glass shattered, but the inside glass is still in place.  The consumer contacted the retailer and told her that her warranty expired.  She contacted the manufacturer and they told her it was not on recall.
justification: The glass oven door exploded, but no injury was reported, and the oven was not in use at the time.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting overheating of GE Profile Dishwasher , 07/20/2011

She called GE, 07/25/2011 spoke with customer service, sent them pictures and report but no one advised her that there were recalls or that this incident had happened to other models before she purchased her dishwasher nor did the customer service rep advise her that there had been similar problems with other models.

Caller's dishwasher model is not recalled.

Caller and husband started dishwasher around 1:30PM, let it run it's cycle.
Around 7PM she was standing at sink and heard noise coming from dishwasher, opened and noted that it was running, all was excessively hot.  
She Physically turned dishwasher off.
She and her husband had dinner then went out for approximately one hour.
When she and her husband came home they noticed a strange odor and began trying to narrow down to a source by throwing away flowers that were wilting, checking trash etc. until they noticed that it was actually coming from the dishwasher running again.
When she opened it she noticed that at least most of the lights were on, all was so hot that they couldn't be touched.
She took a towel, pulled the racks out and left all to cool for at least ten minutes, she then took a towel and removed all her dishes. 
The racks themselves were not melted but plastic inside dishwasher is melted.
Neither caller or husband could get the dishwasher turned off, husband unplugged unit.
She called GE, 07/25/2011cShe called GE, 07/25/2011 spoke with customer service, sent them pictures and report but no one advised her that there were recalls or that this incident had happened to other models before she purchased her dishwasher nor did the customer service rep advise her that there had been similar problems with other models.

Around 9:30PM caller contacted number for appliance repair.
Appliance Center called her the next morning, after listening to scenario she advised caller that it most likely would not be cost effective to repair.
GE replaced, at no charge, the 2008 GE Profile dishwasher with a new one on 8/12/11.  The took the old one back.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and caused melting of plastic parts, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher shorted out - fried the power connections
justification: The dishwasher shorting out and frying power connections is an incident with no reported injury.

incident_description: G.E. Profile Dishwasher overheated. Smelled hot. Smoke filled our home. The dishwasher panel would not turn off. We were home and were able to disconnect appliance in electrical box as it would not turn off via the control panel.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and produced smoke, but no injuries were reported. The incident was resolved by disconnecting the appliance.

incident_description:
Tappan Microwave purchase one and a half years ago caught fire.
Microwave was on a discontinued or clearance table when purchased.

Caller kept smelling an odor like burning plastic throughout an approximate 10AM to 6PM day but couldn't narrow down to a source.

Around 6PM she noticed that the house was filling with smoke very quickly and then that her microwave had burst into flames.

Flames approximately one and a half to two inches high were coming from the vents on the side.

Caller had her 9 month old grandson and her 5yr old grandson who has Autism in the house so took them outside to get them away from the flames and calm the 5yr old while her husband smothered the flames.

Caller's husband said he believes that the electronic module is in front of the panel that caught fire may be the source.
justification: The microwave caught fire, but no injuries were reported; the incident was managed without harm to the occupants.

incident_description: I own a set of Healthcraft Cookware. Five days ago, on August 19, 2011,  I took the 2 qt. pot off the stove (it was full of hot cooked noodles and hot hot water) and was draining the water from it, the handle broke off into many fragments. I was able to drop the pan in the sink to avoid injury, but it could have been extremely dangeous and I or my children could have been severly burned.
justification: The incident was dangerous but did not cause any injury, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is not rare but not certain to occur.

incident_description:
Microwave repeatedly sparks, emits popping sounds while interior light flickers in and out sporadically when microwaving food. I tried checking for any remaining packing material inside the grill part of the microwave, cleaning the microwave and plugging the microwave in to a different plug, and none of that helped at all.

I've had this microwave for 4-5 months. It is not heavily used, mostly for reheating food for a few minutes.
justification: The microwave exhibits electrical issues but no injury or damage has occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore smoothtop range from approx. 2006, with model number 790.96009600.  At the end of May, the front left burner would not turn off after having been used for cooking.  A repairman from Sears came and replaced the infinite switch, and fixed it temporarily.  I was out of town almost all summer and only used it twice between the repair (May 20th) and the day the same thing happened again (August 20th).  The burner was only on for 3 minutes, and then would not turn off, so I cut power to it with the circuit breaker and unplugged it.  A repairman from Sears came again and put in a new part, but could not find anything to explain why the infinite switch broke again so quickly with such minimal use.  Since other Kenmore smoothtop ranges have been recalled, I thought I should report my concern.
Thanks.
justification: The burner malfunctioned but was safely turned off without injury, and similar incidents have been reported with minimal use.

incident_description:
LG Refrigerator Model LFC21760ST Purchased 2007

The lights inside of refrigerator failed to turn off when door was closed, remained on overnight, and overheated causing the light assembly and control unit to melt and fall from its mounting.  So much heat was generated that the top inside liner of the appliance bubbled and other plastic parts warped.  Eggs that were stored one shelf below were too hot to touch and all food had to be thrown away.  Had our daughter not discovered this before leaving the house the following morning I believe the unit would have caught on fire.

Even though it is no longer in warranty, LG is willing to provide limited repairs for what they deem to be a faulty light switch on the main circuit board.  They admitted that other consumers have experienced this same problem, yet we never did receive any notification from them of a potential hazard (we registered this appliance on their website immediately after purchase).

incident_description:

incident_description:
I just came in the house after spending about an hour and a half mowing the lawn. To my surprise, the KitchenAid Microwave (Model KHMS155LSS-3  Oct 2005) was running by itself. I tried to turn it off using the buttons, but none of them worked. I ended up opening the door and unplugging the unit to get it to stop running. 

The inside of the microwave was absolutely smoking hot! Before unplugging it, the digital display was indicating "PAN". I plugged the microwave back into the outlet, and "PAN" again appeared. Seconds later the microwave started to run by itself again, so I unplugged it. 

I called Whirlpool (800/331-7456), and they said it was most likely a control board problem, and that they would be mailing a new one to my house. They also scheduled a service call, which is a week and a half from today. 

This unit should have been recalled! A quick web search reveals that this has been a problem with countless others.

Thank God I was at home or we might not have a home (and pets) to come back to.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned and ran by itself, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The other morning we decided to cook something on the stove and make some biscuits in the oven. After cooking with the cooktop and preheating the oven, we placed the food in the oven an started to bake. We heard a loud pop a smoke came out of the top control panel. This oven/range has had other problems in the past and after closer inspection, the damage could have occured during a cleaning cycle. We followed all instructions in the guide to the letter. This was our first oven that had this feature.
We have had a total of three problems.
First: The handle kept falling off because the screws used weren't long enough. Solved with longer screws.
Second: The appliance bulb exploded while going through the cleaning cycle and damage to the mogul base was a result.  Solved by not ever running the cleaning cycle again. remove light base and replace light. =(
Third: The Control Board commonly referred to as the "Clock" arc'ed out sending 240 VAC into the 120 VAC components in the rest of the board. I would say this is because of a lack of proper spacers between the two boards that are sandwiched together in this unit and many others. The lack of proper spacers would have prevented this from happening, and the manufacture has issued a replacement part with no description why or even if they have addressed this issue. Also, speaking with a rep there has been no recall on these or any other units.

Result: Won't buy products from that manufacturer again. Have to out-source the control panel from a third party as the manufacturer won't replace a defective component and is charging too much for the part. Now upon closer inspection the light mogul base needs to be replaced as well. The only good news is the handle doesn't fall off after installing longer screws.

Conclusion: They should recall this product! It posses a fire hazard from the cleaning cycle and a defective design in their control board. They have switched part numbers from 316207509 to 316207529. What they changed. Who knows. They wouldn't disclose this to me over the phone.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing smoke and potential fire hazards, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I recently bought an Amana gas range, Model AGR5844VDW.  I've used it approximately 4 times.  The knobs on the front of the range are extremely easy to turn on inadvertently.  They protrude rather far from the surface of the stove, they are pointed so they can catch on things, and you only need to push it in very slightly to turn the knob. Out of the 4 times I've used the range, I've unknowingly turned the gas on 3 times while either removing things from the stove or cleaning the stovetop.  I didn't realize the gas was turned on until we smelled gas in the house.  Once it happened twice in one evening!  The last time it happened, we didn't realize it, and we woke up in the morning to our home filled with gas.  It had been running all night.  We also have a greyhound, who is the height of the stove knobs, so he could easily have bumped it with his nose and turned it on.  A small child could very easily reach up and slightly turn the knob to get the gas going.  We do not know how it got turned on the last time, but it could easily have blown up the house, it was that bad.  We were afraid to turn on any fans because we didn't want to create a spark and cause an explosion.  We had to open the doors and windows and evacuate until it cleared up a little.  The store we bought the appliance from (Frank's Appliance in Bradley, IL) said they had a similar complaint from another customer.  They called Amana and were told they made it that way because they got complaints from people with arthritis that it was too hard to turn the knobs, so they were standing by their product and would not do anything about it.  (I guess they think it's OK to take the risk of blowing up someone's house, though!)  While I was in the appliance store, I went with the owner to the floor model of the range, showed her how I had leaned slightly against the stove to clean the stovetop, and each time I did it in the store (4 to 5 times), it turned the burner on.  I tried it on all the other brands of ranges in the store, and this was the only model where I could turn the gas on just by leaning against the stove.  This is the MOST DANGEROUS thing I have ever had in my house, and it could very easily have killed the entire family, and Amana thinks it is not a problem.  Frank's Appliance agreed that it was a dangerous product and agreed to swap it out with a range made by another manufacturer.  I am not normally a complainer, but this stove is going to kill someone, and I would feel terrible if I neglected to report the problems I know are inherent to the product.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a high risk of gas leaks leading to potential explosions, which could result in death. The likelihood is high as the issue occurred multiple times in a short period and could easily happen again.
