incident_description:
On Sunday, July 11, 2011 my wife and I were home and my wife had started the KitchenAid Dishwasher Model, KUD01FLBLO; Serial FM 3901236. During its cycle a strong smell of overheated electric or plastic components charring began to permeate the house. We searched throughout the house for the source of the smell, on re-entry the kitchen and seeing smoke we identified the dishwasher as the source.
As the controls on the unit would not function, I turned the circuit breaker to the unit off.  Upon investigation by doing some disassembly, the control module was found to be heavily blackened and evidence of extreme heat was noted on the control board. Three wire harness connectors were charred and the control enclosure was fused to the underlying mounting structure.  I contacted the manufactures support service and relayed the problem to their attention. A service call was arranged and the service technician identified repairs as 1, Sub-Fuse; 1, Control-Elec; and 1, Wire Harness. Total service cost was estimated at $428.96. At the time I refused further service due to the cost.
Subsequently I did some further investigation and found the parts list with those components their numbers are Sub-Fuse; 8269213, Control-Electronic; 8528874, and Wire Harness; 8269191. I further note the technician noted that factory replacements were not available for the control board, but remanufactured boards would be used.
As I have some knowledge of manufacturing, I found it curious that only a remanufactured board was available.  I am now left to question was the board a potential defective design and redesigned to eliminate a potential problem? If so were defective boards left in service?
I called the KitchenAid Support Group and the only answer I could obtain is that the dishwasher is not on the recall list and customer complaints are company confidential.
I would like your comments on complaints in your files on this problem. From the amount of charring and discoloration, the potential for a kitchen fire seems to be real.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2. The likelihood of this occurrence is 3, as it is not rare but not frequent either.

However, the firm was contacted on 7/25/2011 and she was advised by the representative (name is unknown) that the firm has never received any reports on the matter and that the range was not subject to any recent recalls.

Kenmore Elite Model #795.77543600 

About a year ago I had a problem with the lights will not going off in this refrigerator. There was a melting plastic smell coming from the refrigerator. incident_description: We purchased a Cuisinart DCC1200 9 months ago in November 2010. Coffeemaker worked great, until this morning.  We made a pot of coffee and within a half an hour my husband smelled smoke.  There was smoke billowing out from the bottom of the coffeemaker.  My husband unplugged the coffeemaker and ran outside with it.  After looking @ the unit.  The plate @ the bottom started to crackle and base of unit had begun to melt. The is a very dangerous, potentially life threatening problem that needs to be addressed by the company.

incident_description:
This is regarding a Whirlpool Gold microwave/convection oven (model number GMH6185XVS0) that I purchased on Sept 30, 2009.  


I was making dinner and went to quickly heat something up in the microwave.  Immediately I noticed that the microwave was louder and then it made a weird electrical zap kind of noise.  I opened the door wondering if there was something metal in the microwave, there wasn't.  I proceeded to remove the packaging that the food was on and put it on a paper plate and tried to reheat it again.  This time, the microwave appeared fine (no loud noise or zap).  The problem, however, is that the food didn't heat up.  I tried a few more times with no result.  

The next day, my husband tried to reheat something in a microwave-safe dish and had the same loud noise and zap.  We decided to unplug the microwave and call Whirlpool.

The Whirlpool rep stated they were not able to troubleshoot microwaves over the phone.  The only thing suggested was to switch off and on the breaker.  I was given names to service repair companies, which I called.   According to the repairman, it appears that the issue is related to an open High Voltage circuit within the microwave (zap noise) and the magnetron.  They are coming out to repair the microwave at a cost of approximately $200.

While obviously frustrated by purchasing such an expensive appliance only to have major problems less than 2 years later, I was mortified to see similar issues posted by consumers like myself across the web.  

This issue appears to be more than an occasional glitch and Whirlpool should acknowledge the issue and repair these microwaves!  

I called Whirlpool back after learning more.  Whirlpool said that there were no product recalls on this item.  The third customer service rep I spoke with stated something to the effect that there were some issues with the model # I owned, but wouldn't explain further other than to say that my particular issue was not covered.

I acknowledged Whirlpool's response that consumers post things on websites that they cannot control nor take action on without talking to the consumer.   According to many of the posts, however, people are contacting Whirlpool and are getting nowhere, so I then asked the customer service rep if she could search specific model numbers and see what issues consumers have been calling about to verify if there is a pattern.    She said that a search like that is possible.  When I asked if she would do such a search, she said that that is not part of her job, however, she would document my suggestion.  I asked her, if in her opinion, anyone would pursue this request and she said that it is logged in my record.   Asking her again, she said that would send the request to her supervisor.  I am not confident, however, that anyone within Whirlpool will look into this.

I was asked by Whirlpool what I wanted out of my call to them.  I stated that the bottom line was that it appeared the trouble I have with my microwave is echoed across the web by other consumers and doesn't seem to be an isolated problem.   Because the rep didn't have any specific knowledge of the incidents, I wanted them to do their own measurable searches to verify or dispute the information (as stated above).  Based on their findings, than pursue to rectify the situation, and if they found a pattern of similar issues, for them to publicly acknowledge the issue and repair the microwaves.

I paid a large sum of money for a microwave/convection oven purchased less than 2 years ago that is no longer working properly and is potentially a hazard to myself and other consumers and feel that Whirlpool has a responsibility to find out if that is true or not.

For our family, we've learned an expensive lesson, and won't be buying from Whirlpool again unless they get their act together and start caring about the quality of products they produce and the consumers that purchase them.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned with loud noises and electrical zaps but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue appears to be recurring among multiple consumers, suggesting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
I have a built in Microwave oven over the range . It is about 6 months old. I have heard an arching sound coming from the oven but the oven stills works. the other day my wife had heated some water and as she was getting it out of the microwave she burn her arm on the side of the inside of the microwave metal cabinet. I was a contractor for over 30 years and I know a microwave oven interior does not get hot, only the food or what you are heating. I called for service on the microwave and

They had to call Whirlpool which is the maker of KitchenAid and their Lead Tech said that was normal and they would do nothing about it. incident_description:
Bosch SHX46A05UC/14 serial number FD830100999 dishwasher heater stopped working, exhibiting very long run time and lack of "Sanitized" indicator light.  Troubleshooting revealed a burnt open solder joint in the control board.  

This appears to be similar to the failure mechanism reported on a number of other Bosch dishwasher models that were manufactured during the same time period, and subject to a fire hazard safety recall as noted in the CPSC January 15 2009 Release # 09-100.  

I question whether this is the same failure mode and therefore same safety concern.  [REDACTED] and associated supervisor at Bosch dishwasher customer support were contacted on 6/24/11 with this question and indicated only that the subject model is not included in the recall, but were unable to provide any further details on the safety implications of this defect or whether this failure mode is in fact the same as that exhibited by the recalled models.

I seek to establish whether this unit is a fire hazard and requires remediation beyond simply resoldering the failed joint.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning dishwasher with a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the similarity to recalled models and unresolved safety concerns.

Kenmore range 790.95373803 MD,  VF91452769 serial.

I approached coffee maker as this was where sound was coming from. Smoke was coming from the warmer plate and smelled very bad as if something was burning or about to go on fire. incident_description:
Purchased the Frigidaire dishwasher Model Number: FDB1100RHM in October 2009.   On August 5, my wife returned home five hours later and found the dishwasher stuck in cycle.  As a result the heat element continued to heat and the poor design resulted in the collapse of the element and it burned two holes in the tub.   This created a potential fire hazard if we had been away from the house for an extended period of time.


After receiving the response from Frigidaire that offered little solution, I shopped this weekend to find the exact diswasher has had a design change in the heating element.  They moved from a large square element to a small, better supported round element.  This change would have prevented the collapes of my element.

Frididaire has not accepted any responsibility for the results, have offered little response.  I believe that this design problem could creat problems for other owners of the older model.  I have photos of the damage and the new model change.  I would like to provide to you for your review.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing property damage (burned holes in the tub) but no injury or death. The likelihood is possible as the issue stems from a design flaw in older models.

incident_description: Lights inside fridge would not go out with doors closed completely, which is impossible to know with the doors closed until it causes heat damage.  Because of the duration and high heat, the light shield melted and fell inside the fridge.  We unplugged the fridge, waited for it cool down, then unscrewed the light bulbs.  The sockets were still "live" but at least the bulbs were not there to generate more heat and cause further damage.  We were walking out the door to go on vacation and called Sears.  Sears told us it was our problem not theirs because it was no longer under warranty.  After talking to other repair companies and searching online, this has been a huge problem for many consumers.  [REDACTED] has had the same problem and has assisted consumers with the issue, yet Sears will not.  Consumers have no way of knowing about this problem going on behind closed doors until it overheats and causes damage.  Ironic that there is an overheating issue inside a refrigerator.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted light shield) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The high number of similar reports (17221 of 22691) indicates the issue is almost certain to occur.

incident_description: Smelled smoke & burning electrical and/or rubber smell.  Saw smoke in kitchen.  Finally determined that it was coming from the refrigerator.  Removed cardboard near the bottom of the back of the refrigerator.  No burned wires were evident.  Just happened to notice what looked like oil or soot on the white label on the compressor.  Reached out to touch it, rubbed some off, determined it was soot, and about that time the compressor switched on and a flame shot out from the side of the compressor.  Thank God we found this before it burned down my 118 year old historic home and possibly killed us.  This is a hazard that everyone should know about. Adjusting the controls does not correct the problem. I believe this is a fire hazard.  By contrast food in the non freezer section freezes on a very low setting, possible the unit is overworking due to the defect.

This morning I was baking cookies when I heard two tiny beeps.  As I walked over to the range, I saw smoke.  Opening the oven, I discovered burnt cookies and parchment paper.  I shut the oven off, brought the cookie tray outside to cool.  I left the oven door open to cool.  When I looked at the oven again, the broiler was beet red and glowing.  I pressed the off button again just to be sure, and nothing.  I finally had to pull the range out and pull the plug.

Needless to say, I will never trust this range again, and will be purchasing another.  Please check this out before a tragedy does occur.

incident_description:
In 2007 I purchased a Kenmore bottom freezer refrigerator, model # 79554600. On August 4, 2011 we smelled burning plastic and something like spoiled food in our kitchen. Upon opening the refrigerator doors (side by side), we noticed the entire light fixture and control panel hanging from the top of the fridge, in melted plastic. The heat from the lights burned a six inch hole in the top of the lining.  We were leaving for a one week vacation the next day.  Had we not noticed the problem when we did it's possible the heat from the lights could have started a fire in our wood cabinets. The lights were obviously on for an extended period of time.

We called Sears and they sent a technician to replace the part and the mother board that shorts out.  Given that there was a six inch hole burned in our refrigerator because the lights wouldn't go off he said the unit was not repairable.  He also told us that there was a "service flash" issued by the manufacturer on this product, meaning that they recognized that this product was defective and dangerous. 

I have also read on numerous web sites that there have been numerous other complaints like ours involving this unit. The technicians that came to our home indicated they have seen numerous cases like ours. This is a safety hazard for which  Sears and Kenmore/LG should be held accountable.  

We were fortunate this incident happened while we were home.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The technician's comments and online reports indicate this issue is likely to occur with this model.

Turns out - the display was beeping and blinking an error message, the broiler coils were on FULL blast, it go so hot that the white door is now yellow at the top and the glass top (NOT on) burned my hand.  I hit "cancel" and the oven appeared to be off but the coils NEVER turned off.  I had to flip the breaker to get it to turn off. incident_description:
On August 2, 2011 we put our dishwasher on to wash the dishes before bed which is not unusual for us.  Upon waking up the next morning we noticed our kitchen was very hot. When we went to unload the dishwasher we noticed it was still on, not running however still heating up.  We could not get it off. My husband had to turn off the circuit breaker to stop the dishwasher from heating up anymore. When we were finally able to unload the dishwasher most of our dishes were ruined or melted, the rotater on the bottom of the dishwasher was ruined, and the plastic basket that holds the silverware was melted.  I did keep one glass that was in the dishwasher in order to show people, Maytag included, what the dishwasher did to my dishes. I did research on the Maytag website to check to see if there were any recalls on this particular model, MDBH750AWS.  There were no recalls on this particular model however there were recalls on other models that showed the same basic problems.  I called Maytag and explained the problem that occurred.  I was told that it seemed "our water was too hot".  I decided to have a service call done on the dishwasher through Maytag. They set up the service call for Monday, August 8, 2011.  When the service person, from Solar Refrigeration and Appliance Service, Inc, came in he stated that our dishwasher was reaching 300 degrees in 3 minutes and "we were lucky our house didn't catch on fire while we were sleeping". He also stated that he has had to repair another dishwater with the same model number for having the same problem.  He stated that our heating element in the dishwasher was bad.  Today, August 10, 2011, I put in another call to Maytag to tell them what the service call diagnosis turned out to be and asked them to check if our model could be included in the recall.  I was told "our model is too old". However the models that are currently listed on Maytags website included in the recall were manufactured starting in February 2006.  Our model, MDBH750AWS, was installed in our residence on May 3, 2006.
I am hoping that this does not happen to someone else. The next person this happens to may not as lucky as my family and I. We were lucky in the fact that it did not cause a fire while we were sleeping. I would hate for that to happen to someone else because Maytag does not want to include this model in the recall already taking place for other models with the same problems.
Our model number is MDBH750AWS and serial number is 28381644GN.
justification: The dishwasher malfunction caused property damage and posed a significant fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

Glass exploded: opened door partway to check rack placements (cold oven) hand slipped (handle came loose from left side) causing spring loaded door to snap shut. Glass splattered everywhere including into glass electric cook top 7' away (glass shards striking chicken in pot)as well as into dining area 10-12' distant.

incident_description:
Caller purchased Side by Side Refrigerator Freezer around the end of June 2009, had no problems with it until September of same year when the shelves began falling out either when placing an item on them or removing and item from them.
Caller contacted the manufacturer, appliance still on warranty, send tech who advised caller to stretch the metal 

Not long after first service the shelves were falling, caller contacted manufacturer who put spacers in to attempt a repair.
This did not work as a repair.

Shelves are falling and caller would like them investigated ,                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
Caller considers the shelves falling a safety hazard because they could hit her children if they were to open the refrigerator for something like a popcycle or other item.

incident_description:
Consumer states that her electric smooth top range is not included in the recall CAP for NR#09-333 (August 27, 2009), but CPSC should pursue an investigation on his model and serial number, because her range poses the exact same problem as the one on recall.
 
Consumer was baking cookies the first two batches 12 cookies in one tray were baking well.  Consumer set up her oven for 375 degree 10 minutes to 12 minutes.  

Consumer stated that her electric range oven rise the temperature spontaneously without being switched on.

Consumer stated that the 3rd batch of cookies burned because the oven temperature went up spontaneously.  Consumer had to disconnect the range out the electric out let.

Consumer said that she contacted the mfr and they told her, since the unit is out of warranty there was nothing they could do for consumer.  No further information.

incident_description:
While closing the oven door there was a blue electrical arch that came out the top of the range. He is not sure exactly where the electrical arch came from whether the oven or the top element. He recalls the same incident happening at least twice before. On one occasion while a pot was placed on the burner he saw the same electrical arch. 

The right rear burning light on the control panel indicates "caution hot surface" when the burner is in the off position. He powered the circuit breaker in the off position to prevent any further safety hazards with the unit. He has not contacted the firm but plans on doing so. 

While doing some research online he came across a few different blog sites where consumers experienced the same hazard with similar models to his.
justification: The incident involves electrical arcing and a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death has been reported. The issue has occurred multiple times and is reported by other users, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
The dishwaser was powered in the on position on the normal wash (45 minute setting) at 10:30 pm and at 7:30 am when he woke up he noticed that top right corner of the control  panel  had black soot on it. 

When he opened the door to the dishwasher he did not see any damages to the inside of the dishwasher. The cycle had completed and the dishwasher was not powered on when the incident occurred. It appears the control panel overheated from the inside. 

He will not contact the firm and it is not economically repairable.  No further information was provided
justification: The dishwasher's control panel overheated causing soot, but there was no injury or further damage.

incident_description:
Shortly after the consumerÃÂs wife used the oven to bake a batch of cookies on the setting of 335 degrees she left the home under the assumption the oven was powered in the off position.  

She returned within an hour to notice that the home was filled with a gasoline smell. She noticed that the oven was still powered in the on position she powered the oven in the off position and opened all the windows in the home.

On 7/18/2011  when the technician from the firm came out to the home he indicated that the igniter was not coming into  the full temperature with three amps it would crack the gas valve which was causing the gas to leak. 

The consumer feels as if he replaces the igniter the failure could occur again so he will not allow any repairs to be made to the unit and instead will consider replacing the unit.
justification: The incident involved a major gas leak but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was identified and addressed without harm.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore Glass Cooktop, 790.9600.2600, stove and the front right burner would not turn off.  It remained on high. We had to turn off the power to our house and then unplug the stove in order for it to turn off.  We had to call to get someone to fix it. He stated that it was a fused switch.  Here we are one year later and now the burner will not turn on.  I am concerned for our safety if it decides to switch back on like the previous issue.  This should not continue to be happening for product quality and safety reasons.

incident_description: In late 2007, I purchased an LG French Door Refrigerator (model# LFC25760SB). I immediately had problems with this unit...the freezer wasn't staying cold enough to keep ice frozen and the refrigerator was staying too cold and was freezing the food. It was still under warranty, so it was able to be repaired at no additional costs to me. Recently, I've found that the interior light in the refrigerator wouldn't come on. I thought this was odd, and I noticed a weird smell. When I touched the lighting unit I discovered that it was very hot to the touch!! Concerned that the lights weren't shutting off when the doors were shut, I began video on my cell phone and put it on the top shelf of the fridge. I shut the door, waited several moments, opened the door and reviewed the video. The lights were not shutting off when the doors were closed, causing them to overheat and shut down randomly. When I called LG to report this problem, they informed me that this was an ongoing issue and that my specific model was on their list of refrigerators that were having this issue. Further research online showed that I am not the only one with this problem and I found myself to be lucky that I caught this in time. Had I not discovered this problem, there was potential of the unit catching fire, causing serious damage to my home or even death. Being this is a known issue, I would think that LG would have sent out a recall to their customers offering a fix. In this case I feel it would be beneficial to be proactive, instead of them waiting for customers to find their refrigerator melting or on fire. As it currently stands, I have taken the bulbs out of the unit and I am waiting for a repairman to come to my home and fix the unit.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator light that could potentially cause a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Attempted to chop/grind 3 tbl of cumin seeds in a Cuisinart Mini-prep Plus food grinder. One of the stainless steel blades broke off  of the hub, broke through the containment vessel, and imbedded itself in a kitchen wall 6 feet away. Balde struck wall with enough force after penetration vessell to imbed itself approx. 1/2" inch into drywall.
justification: The blade broke through the containment vessel and embedded in a wall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: LG refrigerator lights stay on even when the door is closed.  This causes a large amount of heat that actually blackened the bulb receptacles.  I noticed a burning smell when I opened the refrigerator, so I luckily caught the problem before it burnt my LG refrigerator.  I have since removed the light bulbs and will be getting the problem repaired.  I did an internet search and noticed other consumers with LG refrigerators have had the same problem.  My LG refrigerator model# is LFD22860SW with serial number 607MRRH00262
justification: The incident caused property damage (blackened bulb receptacles) and a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred. The problem is known to affect other consumers with the same model, indicating it is likely to occur.

incident_description:
When I opened my LG refrigerator (LFC25760SW) last night I smelled something burning.  I closed the door and reopened and the smell was worse.  I immediately unplugged the fridge to avoid a fire.  The light unit was extremely hot and melting away from the refrigerator frame.  After emptying the refrigerator I plugged it back in to see if the lights would turn off.  They did not.  That caused the melting and near fire.  I researched online and found out it was probably a relay switch.  Called LG first thing this morning, they were pleasant to deal with and said they would pay for parts and service and send out a tech.  This was regardless of the fact that the unit was past the 1 year warranty.

The technician came out this afternoon from Fedder's Co in North Hollywood, CA.  [REDACTED].  The tech,  never checked the problem, he took apart the unit and removed the stickers.  Then decided it was fine after jiggling a few wires.  I explained the severity of the heat to him, but he laughed at me and said "it's no danger"......I find this absurd.  He also argued with me for 10 minutes about the housing unit that had melted last night telling me it was fine and looks right; even though the unit was not straight, nor flush and obviously melted from the issue.  He was adamant there was no issue, but that he would order a new plastic unit.  This is NOT the issue.  The fire hazzard is the issue and he failed to address that.  

If LG did not feel this was an issue why would they pay for parts and labor for an out of warranty refrigerator?  There is obviously an issue that either Fedder's or LG is trying to cover up.  [REDACTED].  I called LG back and that is the only repair facility they have that will service my area.  I am now on a list for their team to try and find another repair tech to address the issue.  LG has been good to deal with, but they should specify to the company what the issue is that caused this so they could fix it without wasting my time.  I am now without a refrigerator and freezer and a full can of spoiled food products.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and melting components, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
The Rival model SCR509 slow cooker (aka "Crock Pot") was filled with spaghetti sauce which had been cooking on the "high" heat setting for about four hours, and had reached full temperature.

Upon lifting the lid to stir the contents, the handle in the center of the lid separated from the lid without warning causing the lid, which was being held in one hand above the cooker, to fall uncontrollably down onto the top of the cooker and into the hot spaghetti sauce. This caused the hot oily liquid to splash across the surrounding area and onto my uncovered forearm and clothing. The lid then continued to fall from the top of the cooker and fell into the adjacent sink. It could not be stopped because it was too hot to touch with bare hands and covered with hot liquid.

Hot spaghetti sauce landing on my forearm caused first degree burns with blistering on the inside of the right forearm about three inches below the elbow, and minor burns on my chest where the hot liquid splashed onto my shirt. The glass lid sustained a dent to the metal rim with no obvious glass breakage. 

The cooker was immediately unplugged, and the food being prepared was disposed of after it cooled to room temperature because I could not determine with certainty that none of the broken plastic from the lid handle or any other parts had fallen into the food.

The lid handle is made of plastic which appears to have become brittle allowing a metal nut which is embedded in the plastic to separate from the handle. A metal machine screw fits through a hole in the center of the glass lid and into the metal nut and holds the handle and lid together.
justification: The incident resulted in first-degree burns and blistering, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described failure of the plastic handle.

incident_description:
I am writing because my Frigidaire Brand Stove's oven broiler is turning on by itself.  

I was cooking on top of the stove and walked away. I noticed that the kitchen seemed to be heating up. I went in to discover that the broiler was on in the oven. I tried to turn it off but it wasn't going off. I had to flip the breaker in order to get the stove off.  Since the incident we have not used the stove because of the broiler coming on by itself. We keep the breaker off.
justification: The stove's broiler turning on by itself is a safety hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The control circuit board of our Kenmore Elite Dual Fuel Range model 790.7938 caught fire.  After pressing Start to pre-heat the oven, I heard a cracking sound and a wall of flames shot out from behind the control panel followed by black smoke.  All controls turned on, the oven door locked itself shut, and the self cleaning mechanism began heaating the oven.  I was home alone when the incident happened, so I had to pull the oven out from underneath the wooden cupboards, run out to the garage, pull a refrigerator away from the wall to find the breaker box and kill the power.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke, but no injury or death was reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the detailed description of the malfunction.

Within a minute smoke began rolling from the vents on the door and from the seam between the control panel and the lower door panel, lower right corner.  The top right panel of the door was hot to the touch.  We stopped the cycle by opening the door.  Upon closing the door (in an attempt to cancel the cycle) the control panel no longer functioned.

incident_description:
Turned on dishwasher and let it run through cycle in the early afternoon.  After emptying it, not noticing a problem, we left it for about 4-5 hours until we smelled burning plastic.  We do not use the heated dry feature but somehow it was turned on.  The heating element had been stuck on, and began melting the plastic components in the dishwasher.  The control panel would not respond to commands and I had to unplug it from under the sink.  The granite countertop above it was too hot to touch, as well as the wood cabinets.  

If I had not been home and the dishwasher had not been emptied immediately, the plastic dishes, along with the plastic components, would have melted and caused a fire when it melted onto the heating element.  

Now I have to replace the unit because I am not living with the anxiety of a dishwasher that can melt our dishes and/or burn down our house.  GE has recalled similar models and this product line should be considered as well.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher that could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Homeowner's boyfriend put a pot of water with ravioli in it on the electric cooktop of their stove and turned it on high. He took some medication to help him sleep, went into the bedroom a short time later and was awoken by his dog to smoke and the fire alarms going off. He took the pot off the stove which had burned ravioli in it and threw it off the porch onto the lawn below. He was rescued by FD on the porch and subsequently transported to the hospital for smoke inhalation. Investigation revealed the heating element, which the pot was on, was left in the high position. A portion of the copper bottom of the pot remained on the cooking element after the pot was removed. The wiring harness behind the metal plate in the rear of the stove was melted and had significant heat damage.
justification: The incident resulted in smoke inhalation requiring hospital transport, indicating an injury (severity 3). Leaving a stove on high unattended is a common oversight, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
Dishwasher - Maytag - MDBH968AWB0 - s/n NW4619183

Product started by itself (no one was near it or touched it).  We opened it and hit the CANCEL button and it stopped and drained.  After that, it would not work (ie:  the START/RESUME button would not start the dishwasher - no light!)

Contacted a Maytag repair person by internet and problem was diagnosed as a bad touch panel (about $90) and control panel (about $160) to replace plus labor!  We bought the machine in 2009 (March) and paid $449 + installation + installation kit and 110v power cord - so the whole thing was about $600.

Since the defective items were circuit boards (which should be very low failure rate items - like in a home computer or calculator or phone), I though the cost of repair was too high ($350+ for a $449 Machine) so I contacted MAYTAG on their web site and found that this item is subject to a 2010 recall which we didn't know about nor were contacted about.  Seems there is a "Fire problem" which Maytag will repair for free or give a rebate $150 or $250 on a NEW machine on CERTAIN MODELS.

So, if I have the Fire problem fixed, I still have a $350 + labor costs problem OR I can buy a NEW machine at $649 and have to buy a new installation kit + power cord + install fee + delivery fee + disposal fee in order to get $250 back for A DESIGN/and OR QUALITY PROBLEM at Maytag.

To verify everything, I went on-line to check archives of problems with MAYTAG dishwashers and was shocked to find that in 4 pages (that's all I went thru) of 10 -12 problems per page, ove 10 of them had THE EXACT SAME PROBLEM - which indicated to me that MAYTAG should have suspected there was a circuit board problem and corrected it at no charge to the consumer.

Therefore, I am asking the CPSC to investigate further.  I can see that if a defective board could start the machine and if no one were nearby, it conceivably could flood the kitchen and/or start the heating coil (fire hazard) or maybe produce an electrical shock hazard.  In any case, this is NOT a problem caused by consumer abuse or negligence yet can cause a very painful financial cost to the consumer to fix.  This is a MAYTAG design or manufacturing problem and they should be forced to provide correction to the consumer at no cost.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned without causing injury, but poses potential fire and flood hazards.

incident_description:
Consumer feels his range poses a potential fire hazard. The consumer has a 5 burner 2 oven gas range. The product has a larger oven on the bottom. The range is digital and has a larger oven on the bottom. The top oven has a single rack to place product while the bottom oven has two racks. The range is freestanding. The product has coil burners instead of a smooth top surface. The consumer was cooking for about two hours while her oven was set to bake at 350 degrees. The consumer emptied a bag of potatoes, half a bag of onions and 6 chickens with oil on the bottom of the pan into the range. The pan took up the entire oven with just four inches of spaces between the pan and the front door of the oven. 

The consumer stated that the issue with the range is the bottom rack where the pan was placed has no "lip" to prevent contents of the oven from slipping to the floor of the oven. The consumer stated the pan had fallen on the to the oven floor while she was cooking a resulted in the oil, chicken, potatoes, and onions catching fire while in the oven. The consumer tried to shut off the oven but the oil had already caught fire and there was nothing she could to douse or prevent the fire. The consumer put on an oven mitten and pulled out the product that was burning and one of the oven racks that caught fire while it was covered in the oil that spilt. 

The consumer stated that she shut the oven door after pulling out the burning contents of the range and allowed 2 hours for the range to burn itself out. The consumer stated that the range was altered as a result of the incident. The front glass door of the oven is supposed to be purple but now is discolored and the range now emits an odor. The guard that goes over the gas line is now discolored and burnt. The consumer opted not to call the fire department at the time of the incident. The consumer suffered a minor burn to her right wrist. The consumer did not receive medical attention after the incident. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor burn, indicating an injury (severity 3), but such incidents are unlikely (likelihood 2) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: I was getting ready for bed around 9:30pm when I heard a loud noise in the kitchen.  It sounded like static coming from a radio.  I went into the kitchen and instantly smelled a strong electrical burning smell.  I walked around the kitchen and determined it was coming from the egg poacher on my Back To Basics Egg & Muffin 2-Slice Toaster, Model # TEM-500.  I unplugged it immediately and went to pick it up to move it, but the front portion (the egg poacher) was too hot to touch. It was still hot a 1/2 hour later.  I waited another hour and it had cooled off enough for me to remove it from the house.  It's important to note that the elapsed time from when noise started to when I unplugged it was under two minutes, so it heated up extremely fast. It was obvious that it would've started a fire if I had not been home to unplug it right away.  I did contact Back to Basics and report the issue and they told me the device is not meant to be left plugged in and that they have not heard other reports of this problem, however, I googled the issue and was able to find other complaints about the toaster either catching fire, or having a strong odor, loud noise and smoke.  Some of those complaints can be found here:  http://www.fixya.com/support/t2516135-paula_deen_toaster_egg_poacher_caught  They go all the way back to July of 2009.  One of those complaints listed this website as the official goverment product reporting system, so that is how I came about reporting the issue.  Back To Basics has asked me to send them the toaster back (they said they will email me a shipping label, which they have not done yet) and they will send me a new one, but I don't want to send it back if you need it for testing and I don't necessarily want to use the new one if this is a common problem, as it does not seem like an isolated incident according to other web complaints.  I have two dogs at home and I would hate to think what could have happened if I had not been home when this happened.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, and similar complaints suggest a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
( I filed this report originally on 3/31/2011, but I don't believe it was fully processed).  On 2/27/2011, I was using the Aroma ACJ-250 juicer extractor when it exploded with a "boom".  The light fixture above my head was shattered and fell onto me.  Sharp plastic and shredded metal shrapnel shot out in all directions, traveling 20 feet  to my left and 15 feet to my right.  The walls of the rooms were what contained the debris from traveling further.  My left hand was lacerated and my chest bruised from the force of the explosion.  Fruit juice and skin from my juicing efforts splattered and stained the ceiling, walls, cabinets, floor, my face clothing, body, everything I had on the counter and the rug in the adjoining room.  Basically, the entire kitchen was a stained mess.  It was a very traumatic event which stays with me.  I am SO fortunate my face wasn't over the juicer and that I did not lose an eye or sustain life threatening injuries.  I am relieved that my 10 year old son, who was helping me juice prior to the event had left the room and that no one else in our household or our pets got in the line of the trajectory pieces of shrapnel.  I found pieces of shrapnel for weeks after cleaning up on that day.  This was no way for me to have started my birthday.  My present in this is that I didn't get more seriously injured, but the "what ifs" haunt me.

My husband looked on line and found out this product had been recalled many years back, though that message did not reach me.  Since then, I learned that the company had no notification in service to alert consumers.  I have called Aroma housewares 5 times and left detailed messages with their legal department to discuss what happened to me, but they have never returned the call.
justification: The incident resulted in lacerations and bruises, indicating an injury but no death, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the product was recalled, suggesting known issues but not frequent incidents.

incident_description:
I purchased a Emerson microwave oven approximately 11/10. I was using it to warm a my lunch. It started to send sparks inside which startled me causing me to slip and fall to my knees. When i tried to get up quickly to shut it off it would not stop running. I then had to pull it towards me to unplug the microwave. This resulted in a menicus tear in my left knee.
Ten months agao, my wife was using the same model microwave which started sparking when she was using it. We returned it to Walmart and they gave us a new one with no questions asked. I thought that was odd but I never question it. Then this new one kind of exploded in my face when I turned on the dinner plate setting. My face was abut one foot away from the door when it happened. I could not see the setting on the microwave which is why I had to get closer to see where the button was.
About one year ago we gave our friend of our a gift of the same model microwave for her birthday. She told us the one we gave her started to spark, so she does not use it anymore. She never told us until she found out about what happened to me.
I looked online and found out that this particular model had many complaints but was never taken off the market. To this day, Walmart still sells it. I told the manager about it and two assistant managers when I went back a day later. 
There are about twenty complaints about this microwave on CONSUMER AFFAIRS.COM and many other sites.
justification: The incident resulted in a meniscus tear (injury) and there are multiple reports of similar incidents, indicating a pattern.

incident_description: Dishwasher randomly caught on fire during normal operation.  Appeared to be electrical fire.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
As I was getting ready to leave for vacation I noticed an odor of burning plastic when I opened my refrigerator.  The food on the top shelf was not cold.  The light housing was melted and the bulb sockets were discolored and burnt.  In fact there are burn marks along the top.  My husband attempted to remove the plastic housing and he finally did although the plastic had melted to the top of the frig.  The switch that recognizes the door as being closed was not functioning, so the light was not going off.  We loosened the bulbs to avoid additional heat.  This is definitely a fire hazard!  When I returned from vacation, I called Sears service center.  They were no help.  In fact they told me to go to the store.  I took the melted plastic with me to the store and asked if there might be a recall.  They knew nothing and could do nothing and suggested I call the service center.  I pointed out that this had already been done.  They suggested I go to the Sears parts store.  I went there carrying the melted part and they were also not much help.  They referred me to the same place I called before.

I feel that this is a definite defect of the appliance.  So now I have a refrigerator with burn marks, no lights, and I wonder how safe it is even now.  Had I gone on vacation without noticing the problem, I feel certain there would have been a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning refrigerator with visible burn marks and melted components, posing a fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Cuisinart coffee maker caught on fire. Smoke billows, burning smell. Very dangerous. Many many other consumers on the Internet are reporting the same thing.
justification: The coffee maker caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased 3 Maytag appliances 5 years ago.  Yesterday, I smelled a strong electrical fire and traced it to my refrigerator.  My husband found an electrical failure in the relay.  The compressor has ceased to work.  I was lucky to have caught the problem and had the presence of mind to shut off the electricity.  

I checked to see if this was on a recall list.  I found a recall list for the identical problem (electrical failure in relay), but my model and serial number were not listed.  I was told by the automated website that I could continue using the refrigerator safely as it was not on the recall list."  Huh?

In the meantime, I learned that the dishwasher we purchased IS on a recall list due to fire hazard!
A repairman will look at it on Saturday.

The top oven in the double oven stove has ceased to work.

We paid top dollar for what we thought were quality appliances and just 5 years later have 3 appliances the are defective (2 of which are dangerous!).  

What can I do about this???  I'm especially concerned about the refrigerator as the replacement of a compressor costs almost as much as a new refrigerator.
justification: Electrical failure in appliances poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Lights would not turn off in refrigerator.  everything was hot inside.  The light cover and housing were melted and bent.  

I am enclosing a picture of the melted and bent light cover and melted and bent
housing.
I have taken out the lights in the refrigerator.
The appliance repair man that I was to have repair refrigerator contacted the
manufacturer and the relay board which controls the switch and light is on back
order. They would not tell him if the boards have been revised due to problems.
They also would only give him a 90 day warranty. Since this problem has been
erratic -switch doesn't work correctly off and on getting one which has not been
corrected might mean the same problem after the 90 day warranty and I'd be
right back in the same situation. He informed me that if the lights weren't turning
off for long enough it might catch fire.
I do hope this is enough information and that no one has a house fire due to this
problem.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while he was using the electric glasstop range for approximately 10 mins, he started smelling an odor of burnt wires, which was followed by a popping noise and he noticed that there was sparks emitting under the glass where the heat would come from, and then there was smoke.  He immediately powered off the unit.

Consumer stated that this incident ocurred 1 year ago but it went unnoticed.

Consumer contacted the store and was advised that there was no recall and he should report it to the Agency.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the consumer's report and the potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
Consumer stated his 8 oz cup glass measuring cup was on a kitchen counter in their cabin and shattered by itself. The consumer and his wife were asleep at the time. The consumer's wife stepped on a piece of glass, that was an inch in diameter, while walking into the kitchen.  She was not injured. The consumer's wife looked around the kitchen and found shattered glass all around the kitchen. 

The consumer talked to his neighbor who heard a loud crash at 5AM this morning. The consumer went online that there are numerous reports of this occurring and shattering with force. The consumer stated and found that the cup was hit by a 4-pack of AA batteries earlier in the day, with no apparent damage.  The consumer stated that there is no warning of danger if the product is dinged (on the product).  The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer about the issue. The product did not damage the consumer's cabin.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass measuring cup, but no injuries occurred despite stepping on glass.

incident_description:
While baking in the oven at 350 degrees approximately 20 minutes later the oven changed its setting from the bake setting to the self clean mode . She heard three beeps and noticed on the control panel that it was on the self clean mode. 
She made several attempts to power the range in the off position by using the knob on the control panel but when the oven would not power off she hand to power the circuit breaker in the off position. 

 She powered the circuit breaker back in the on position on 7/14/2011 and the oven was in the off position. She discontinued the use of the oven but continued the use of the stove top. 

The firm was contacted on 7/18/2011 ( representative that he spoke with name is unknown) and that they would be willing to send out a technician but she would required to pay for the parts and the firm would pay for the labor, diagnostic, and trip.

On 7/19/2011 a technician (name unknown) from the firm came out  and indicated that the motor in the range had caught fire but the failure might have occurred from the circuit board but he was not exactly sure but he advised that those parts should be replaced in the oven.  

No repairs were made because the technician advised the consumer that she would be required to pay for the labor and parts. The consumer indicated that since the technician was not quite sure what needed to be replace she did not want to make any repairs until someone was really sure since she was no responsible to pay for the parts. 

She currently uses the cook top but not the oven and no repairs have been made.
justification: The incident involved an oven malfunction and a motor fire, but no injuries were reported, and the issue was contained without further damage.

incident_description:
I purchased a deni (Keystone Mfg. Co. Inc.) hot plate Model:16310, 120V-1500 W Made in China on 8/01/2010. UPC code:050763163108. The product stopped working a week ago. It would heat water but not boil.

My husband who knows electronics took it apart and said it is unsafe.
 It was sparking because of loose connectors to the heating element (both were sparking).
The connectors are made of  very thin cheap metal that is not brass so when it heats up they become loose and fall off. It eventually stopped working all together but there was ample time for the sparks to become a fire. It is not UL listed but says it conforms to UL standards.
Besides the safety issue this product is designed to fail.
This product was used very few times and only to boil water.
justification: The product malfunctioned and posed a fire hazard due to sparking from loose connectors, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
When I turn on the gas to the range, it takes approximately 10 minutes for it to ignite.  When it does ignite it does with a loud whoosh...and opens the door to the oven about an inch.  This has gotten worse over time.  In the beggining it just took time to ignite.  Now it has become dangerous. 
I cannot use the burners on the stovetop until the oven is fully pre-heated.  If I try and do so they will blow a mixture of gas and air and not fully light causing the igniters to click continuously.  The stovetop issue has been going on since I purchased the range in 2003 and have had 4 repair calls on it.  The oven has had one repair call on it.  I moved from the repair area almost 5 years ago and there is not a person in my area who works on this product.  I am in contact now with Wolf and they are attempting to find someone who is qualified in my area to try and repair this product.  I am reporting this to make sure that you are aware of this and if others have had the same issue that possibly a recall may be in order.
justification: The incident involves a dangerous ignition delay and loud whoosh, posing a risk of injury from potential gas explosions or burns.

incident_description:
On August 1, 2011, our 5-burner Jenn-Air stove (Model JDR8895AAS) started behaving strangely.  The automatic ignition on all 5 burners was sparking continuously, even though all the knobs were in the OFF position.  This would not stop regardless of what we did with the knobs (naturally, if we turned them to let gas through, the burners would light).

We pulled the stove away from the wall and disconnected the unit from the power source.  This stopped the sparking.  After 3 hours or so, we re-connected the stove, and this time large sparks, and smoke, started coming from under the knobs themselves (in addition to the sparks at the burners).  For a second, it seemed like a small fire had begun under the surface where the knobs are.  We immediately disconnected the stove again, and the sparks stopped, but smoke continued to come out.

I suspect a major short circuit, either with the control panel, or at some junction box somewhere.  We have not lifted the surface yet, but we did notice that there are cables attached to the knobs that are exposed, and should liquid fall on the knobs (not an unusual scenario for a stove), it would very likely create a scenario for a short circuit, and possibly a fire.  This is clearly a design flaw.

We also did some research on the internet, and found out we are not alone.  The same thing has happened to others:

On a blog with complaints about Maytag appliances (http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/maytag_oven.html), [REDACTED] wrote on 11/22/08:
ÃÂWe bought our Gemini Oven in '04 (almost 4 yrs. to date). This morning our son called out, There is something wrong with the stove!
The ignition was off, but sparking as if we were trying to start the stove, but all knobs were in the off position. I could start the stove, but each time I returned the knobs to the off position, the ignition continued to act as if we had it in the light position.  Worse...the ignition or something under the knobs began to spark and we saw flames coming from under the knobs! There was an electrical short of something.  We unplugged the oven from the wall and turned off the gas. I am just glad we were home! A repair man is coming out on Monday as it is not covered according to Sears.ÃÂ
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove with sparks and smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Similar incidents reported online suggest this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I own a Maytag dishwasher that has burned through several of the metal rods on the lower bin just above the heating element.  The problem started approximately 2 yrs ago, I believe I bought the dishwasher around 2006 or 2007.  It is registered with Maytag so they would have this information.  I was informed of the massive dishwasher recall in 2010 involving the excessive heat of the heating element and my dishwasher met some of the criteria to be considered (serial number ending in JP).  At the time, the maytag.com website did not work for determining if it were included or not so I had to call the 800# several times trying to reach someone.  I finally made contact and was quickly told it was not affected.  However based on the damage at the time and the extent of the damage to the lower bin that has become even worse, I am not sure that it was not included.  If it wasn't, an investigation should be done to see if additional models are effected.  I have pictures of the damage which I could email if needed.  I am unable to get through on the maytag.com website and intend to call them again to deal with their lackluster customer service department tomorrow.
justification: The incident involves damage to the dishwasher but no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the recurring nature of the issue and the user's ongoing attempts to address it.

incident_description:
On 5/15/2011 after the cycle in the dishwasher  had completed itself ( the dishwasher was placed on the normal setting for  approximately an hour) she then used the lever to  unlock the door to open the dishwasher when she received a minor shock to her right hand.

On 5/16/2011 after completely a load of dishes in the dishwasher (the same cycle was used) while trying to open the door she received another electrical shock (that last longer than the first incident) to her right hand.

The dishwasher is a customized door by the manufacturer it has a metal strip on the front at the top near the control panel and the color of it is cobalt blue. 

The firm was contacted on 5/2/2011 and spoke with the [REDACTED] at [REDACTED] from the Safety Department and  an appointment was set up for a technician to come out to take  a look at the unit to determine if any repairs would need to be made. She was instructed to place gloves on her hand to go under the sink to unhook the dishwasher and not use it until a  technician could come out to take a look at the dishwasher

A technician from Asians Appliances came out on 5/18/2011 he went under the sink to hook the dishwasher back up.  He then  used a meter that was used to detect electrical currents and while in front of the dishwasher  in front of the handle of the dishwasher and the meter began to beep continuously. 

He began to operate the dishwasher on the same setting the consumer normal operates it on. Shortly after powering the dishwasher on in the cycle, foul-smelling black smoke and two large flames shot out from the right side of the control panel. He had to put out the fire with dry towels.

On 6/13/2011 she contacted [REDACTED] from the firm and was advised to have the machine hauled away for scrap and not recycle so that it would not be used again. She contacted the retailer and was provided the number to Alacarte Haulaway at [REDACTED]and she scheduled an appointment to come and pick up the machine On 6/15/2011 . On the same date she faxed over documentation to [REDACTED] to show that the dishwasher was picked up  She purchased a new dishwasher on 5/26/2011 by another manufacturer .

incident_description: Timer fire in Kenmore dishwasher model number 363.15452991, serial number RV301706R.  Fire destroyed front of dishwasher with minor extension to counter.
justification: Fire caused damage to the dishwasher and counter, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore smooth top range from Sears in 2007. I had an incident where the one of the dual front burners wouldn't work (the smaller one), this was about 2 and a half years after I purchased it. I had a repair man in my home for another appliance that I had purchesed that was a defect from (Kenmore) that Sears ultimatly replaced after I argued with them for a month and a half.
Anyway I inquired about my range at that time and the repair man said "if its not under warranty I should use it until it dies because I only paid $499.99 for it , it would be more expensive to fix." I don't remember exactly on what date it happened but I noticed that the elements on my range seemed to heat up really hot, I thought it was me at first, but over time the problem has gotten worse just recently the elements on the range won't shut off leaving us with no option but turn off the circuit breaker. I called Sears an they said "my model isn't on the recall list, I can pay to have it repaired", when I questioned the Sears rep. I said "I told him I have read a lot of consumer complaints about people having the same problem, I believe Sears knows the problem is very widespread and doesn't want to admit they sold a defected product," instead they want the consumer to "foot the bill". I think Sears has really dissapointed a lot of it's customers and they should "do the right thing" this is a serious fire hazard it has the potential to burn or kill a lot of people. 
 The Sears rep. I spoke with on the phone told me "ranges don't last forever" I personally don't think four years is "forever" their answer to the problem is "don't use it" I don' see how anyone is standing up for the consumer on this issue. When I had my house built I could't get an "occupancy permit" until the anti-tip bracket was installed, but it's okay if the range burns my house down? I don't know what elese I can do as a consumer.
justification: The incident describes a malfunctioning range that poses a fire hazard, but there is no mention of actual injury or death, only potential risk.

incident_description: Made coffee as usual with the Cuisinart DCC-1200 coffee maker.  After about an hour of being on heard a popping/boiling sound and smelled fire.  The coffee maker had turned itself off as usual. I pulled the plug and ran it outside.  Coffee maker was clearly smoking from the warming plate.  Cuisinart gave no explanation but said they will replace with a new unit and provide a free UPS label for return.  Thank goodness I was there to hear/smell the coffee maker and get it outside before there was any damage.
justification: The coffee maker emitted smoke and had a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Bosch dishwasher that is approx 4 years old.  At  8pm on July 30th i heard a loud crackling sound coming from the kitchen - upon arriving in the kitchen found a large amount of smoke coming from the control panel area of the dishwasher.  I immediately stopped the dishwasher to stop it and had to pull the front cover off to see the interior of the control panel.  the entire inside of the control panel had burned and the exterior was starting to melt through.  

I called Bosch and apparently the dishwasher is under recall for this problem. I bout the appliance through Sears and never had heard anything thing from either company regarding a recall or possible fire risk.  

Had we been asleep or out of the home i hate to think what might have happened. Its pretty inexcusable that we were not notified about this potential problem.
justification: The incident involved a significant fire hazard with smoke and melting components, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I'm writing in regards to Frigidaire Electric Range Model # FEFL77ABF | Serial # VF24626066. 
Earlier today I was cooking a pizza at 425 degrees and when I went to set the timer, the timer began malfunctioning (displaying random numbers). It wasn't the first time I'd seen this with this oven, so I simply reset the timer and it worked fine. After the pizza was done I took it out and shut the oven off. 

Around ten minutes later the oven started beeping continuously with "F1" flashing on the display. I opened the oven and found that the heating element was turned on and glowing orange, heating the oven well beyond the 425 degrees it was previously set to, even though the oven was shut off. I attempted to shut the oven off again, which stopped the beeping momentarily (after 10 seconds or so it began again), but the heating element continued to run. I then shut off the circuit completely and then a few seconds later flipped it back on to see if that solved the issue, but sure enough the element began heating up again on its own. I shut the circuit off and waited 30+ minutes and tried again, but the heating element again began heating up.

This is an obvious fire hazard and I shudder to think what would have happened if this had occured while I wasn't home. How can a device like this do anything other than completely shut down in the event of any kind of detected malfunction? 

How hot was this oven going to get before shutting down?
justification: The oven malfunctioned by overheating while turned off, posing a clear fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Tuesday July 19th I was cooking pasta. I went to drain the hot water from the pot in the sink. The only things in the sink were 3 bowls, the strainer and the Pampered Chef Dipper ice cream scooper. While pouring the water into the strainer the dipper EXPLODED. Force enough to shatter the bowls, cut my hand, throw the pot from my hand about 10 feet away, blow curtains off window. Whatever was inside the handle got all over my kitchen. Including getting into my eyes and mouth. I promptly contacted Pampered Chef via email and phone to get a description of what product was inside the handle. [REDACTED] (I think that was his name)the rep I spoke with told me it was a nontoxic gel. I asked for proof of what it was since it went into my mouth and eyes. I asked for the MSDS for the product be sent to me. [REDACTED] told me he would get back to me on Wednesday the 20th. Never got a call back. On July 25th after I contacted the better business ÃÂ I got a call back saying they got the MSDS and wanted my email address to send it to me. I gave them the address and received the MSDS. While looking over the MSDS I noticed that I should have washed my eyes for 15 minutes and drank milk. I was never told this. I was told it was a safe nontoxic gel. While the only injury I suffered was a cut hand and my kids being upset I still feel this could have really caused damage! I also am shocked at the lack of communication from the company. Only after I contacted the BBB did I get a reply. The gel was made of soluble oil B from Chevron company. I could send you the MSDS copy.ÃÂ 
Thanks for your time

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a cut hand and exposure of eyes and mouth to a chemical, but no severe injuries or death occurred. Such incidents are unlikely but possible with defective products.

incident_description: Noticed, during use, a bright, uneven heat intensity level on the left side of the lower heating element in the oven. The spot continued to heat up and began emitting a white, hot spark and flaming. Turned off oven with switch/knob control. The oven continued to draw current to the baking element after the oven was turned off. Pulled oven away from wall and disconnected the power plug. Heating element finally acted as if no electricity was flowing through it and sparking/flaming/arcing ceased. Once unplugged, the sparking immediately ceased. The major concern for me is not just that the element failed - that could happen over time - but that when a heating element failure occurs the oven continues to draw current despite switch/knob in 'off' position. This is not model specific, as, based on other recent reports to this site, many other GE or Spectra 'models' also are exhibiting this potentially unsafe design behavior. GE has not recalled the specific model we have (JBP24W) but they have recalled JBP21W. Was their recall not thorough enough?
justification: The incident involved a heating element sparking and flaming, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
GE Profile Dishwasher Overheated 
Model PDW7800N20CC Purchased in March 2009

Dishwasher had been run on heated cycle the previous afternoon, after the dishwasher was unloaded I turned off the heated drying.  At approximately 9am the next morning a strong burning odor was noticed when we woke up and as I walked by the dishwasher I could feel the heat coming of of it. The entire dishwasher was very hot, items inside the dishwasher had started to melt and the surrounding cabinets were also hot to the touch. I immediately shut off the power to the dishwasher. 

The dishwasher was off when this incident occurred. If this condition had continued I believe a fire would have started in the cabinets.
justification: The dishwasher overheated and caused melting of items, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: For several years, I have owned and used a Corningware Electrics 4-slice Toaster.  Yesterday, it malfunctioned very badly, failing to pop up the toast until it was a smoking charred black mess that completely filled my house with heavy smoke.  My son noticed that it was beginning to fail several days ago, but didn't inform me of the situation. Had I not noticed, unplugged the toaster and put the toast in the sink with water, I'm certain that it would have continued to burn until the unit and subsequently my house would have caught fire.  The model number is TS-4318, the UL listing is E106413, Listed, 99N3.  It was purchased some time ago at the Boston Store in Milwaukee, Wisconsin for $50.00. However,  I am not looking for financial reimbursement.  I simply want you to be aware of this very grave potential fire hazard. Since then, the oven has failed to hold the adjustable racks within it.  Imagine, if you will, the front of the range is south, the back is north.  It appears as if the east and west sides of the oven have bowed out 1/8" - 1/4" inch so that the racks will not hold in their tracks and fall to the bottom.
I contacted Sears to determine if this range was a recall item and to ask how I could fix it.  Sears customer service representatives said that the range was not on a recall list and, because the appliance was out of warranty, there was nothing that organization could do.
I went on-line and contacted "Manage My Life", a website dedicated to assisting with problems associated with various products.  I received some general guidance and, to make a long story short, contacted an appliance repair technician.  He arrived, looked at the oven and told me it was beyond repair.
While I am a reasonable person, the failure of this $1600 product after 3+ years is unacceptable.  And Sears' apparent indifference is also unacceptable.  Yes, I'm aware of "caveat emptor" and have realized I bought a lemon.  But I pass this on to alert you to this potentially unsafe product.

incident_description:
I am writing to advise you of a serious hazard uncovered with a Maytag "advanced cooking system super capacity plus gas convection oven / range that could have resulted in a house explosion."

My wife was baking a cake and while the oven was on we both proceeded to do some gardening outside. Awhile later my wife went back into the house to check on the cake. She immediately rushed out to tell me the house was filled with gas. I immediately cancelled the oven concerned that even that activity could cause a spark that would ignite the gas. The central air conditioner was on and the gas odor permeated the entire house from the basement to the second floor. I know the oven did initially ignite as the cake ultimately was half baked.

Following opening windows and doors, I called our gas provider. It was Saturday and they sent a service technician out on an emergency call. He electronically sniffed out the area and determined that the gas was coming from the stove (oven). I explained to him that recently, when the oven was first turned on that we were hearing a ÃÂpuffÃÂ at ignition but never smelled any gas. I was shocked when he told me that based upon my description and the age of the stove, he knew exactly what was wrong and that he had experienced this many times before. He advised me that the ignitor, with age, develops resistance and doesnÃÂt always get hot enough to ignite the burner or if the burner does ignite, it sometimes only partially ignites the burner allowing it to leak gas. He measured the current to the ignitor and confirmed that it was too resistive and the current was too low to function reliably. He replaced the ignitor ($160.50) and everything was fine from that point on. Obviously, we are still concerned.

My wife was always fearful of using the ovenÃÂs timed delay to bake for this very reason. I always thought the oven had a safety mechanism such as my gas dryer that requires a heat sensor to trip before the gas valve would open. Fortunately, my wife never felt comfortable with using the timed delay and I am grateful that she did not. I could only imagine what would have happened if we were out of the house for several hours with the oven leaking especially since we have both a gas furnace and a gas hot water heater.

When the stove was fairly new, I expressed concerns with the burner ignitor. I experienced a situation whereby one burner ignitor failed. Since all the ignitor spark simultaneously, the gas from the burner with the failed ignitor traveled to one of the other burner ignitor causing a little explosion. 

I wrote Matag and was basically told that unfortunately parts are made by humans and therefore cannot be perfect

Considering the risk associated with this failure, I feel this response is inadequate and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a gas leak that could have led to an explosion, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We bought a 24" self-cleaning electric wall oven by Frigidaire, from Sears, in Dec of 2004.  It was installed in August of 2005.  We also bought a 3 year service plan that was never used.  We are retired and in our 70s and thought this would last our lifetime! Instead it bit the dust 6 years later :(

On the evening of Tuesday July 19, 2011 I was preparing dinner and had the broiler on- but no food in the oven- when I heard 2 loud pops. I was not near the oven at the time, and when I checked I could smell electrical burning, but see no outer reason for the noise or smell. Then I noticed the cooktop and oven were off- that circuit breaker had blown.  We soon realized the wall oven was totally inoperable, the door would not close properly and there were strange icons in red on the control panel. 

A technician the next morning determined that the circuit board behind the control panel had blown and also expelled a metal component that had been part of the construction.  There was heavy smoke damage and burning to the oven itself, and to the wood cabinet the oven is in.  We felt very fortunate that fire had not consumed the entire cupboard!  Further investigation revealed that the entire control panels was totally destroyed as well.  The replacement of parts, and installation would cost far more than a new oven.  Now we are faced with needing to buy a new wall oven.  In his 13 years of experience, the technician had never seen such force and destruction. Even though circuit boards do have to be replaced occasionally, usually it is not within 6 years, and usually there is not this excessive damage.  

It is not clear whether the explosion and destruction is due to a design flaw, or this oven was just a one-off lemon appliance.  However, we thought it wise to alert the Consumer Product Safety Commission of the possibility of such a problem and its potential danger of personal injury. 

Thank you, [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the oven and surrounding cabinet but no personal injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On May 12, 2011, I purchased a new Frigidaire electric range from Lowe's. The appliance has a glass cooking top. The control panel is at the front and is surrounded by a black plastic border, with a rim which extends about 3/8" above the cooking surface and which is 1- 1/2 inches from the element at the nearest points. 

On July 21, as I was cooking dinner, I accidentally moved the cooking pan so that it touched the rim. The rim melted and portions of the rim stuck to the bottom of the pan and were transferred to the glass cooking surface as I moved the pan back over the element.

This incident occurred during normal cooking; no excess temperatures or unusual cooking techniques were involved. I was, in fact, totally unaware of the damage until I had completed cooking and went to wipe up what I assumed was a small spill but which turned out to be the damaged plastic.

While the appliance has permanent damage, I feel fortunate that I did not come in contact with the melted plastic as a serious burn might have resulted.

To emphasize my major point, it appears to me that there is a serious safety concern in the manufacture of an appliance which combines a cooking surface the purpose of which is to reach high temperatures with an adjacent material with a melting point below that which might be reached by normal use.
justification: The incident resulted in permanent damage to the appliance but no injury occurred.
