incident_description:
This is concerning a freezer I had bought.

Whirlpool Freezer
Model: EV161 NZRQ05
Serial: EWY1232166
Purchase date: 12-22-2009
Place of purchase : Menards - Muncie, Indiana

On 6/15/2011 I was driving back from taking my dog to the vet. I called my wife by cell phone and told her to go downstairs in the basement and make sure the dehumidifier was on because it was raining outside. She came back up and said the freezer was making a thumping or hitting type of noise. So I hurried home without stopping anywhere else.

When I got home I pulled about 200 Ibs of meat out and removed the racks and some screws form the freezer. The noise was coming from an air circulation fan behind a plastic cover. I looked at it and the fan blade had been backing up on the shaft and hitting the motor. This hitting was causing the fan to have gashes cut out in it by the motor. (See pictures)

I called Whirlpool service department and they said there was "no recalls" on this model number. (This info will be important later on in this letter.) They wanted to send a technician out to my house but it would cost me normal rates to work on the freezer. I declined. I then called CPSC. While on the phone I gave them the info they asked.  After talking to CPSC I hung up and looked on the internet for parts for this freezer. There was a fan blade on the website for searspartdirect.com. I had notice the fan blade (sears part no. 439012) had been replaced by another part no.(1-B0250-102} I got ahold of a sears parts technician on line. He said the part had been changed in 2010 by whirlpool.

So I called whirlpool back up and talked to their service department again and told them about the blade replacement. They told me they had problems with the blade as early as 2009. (This means the fan was bad when I bought the freezer and Whirlpool knew it. ... }1 asked them why they didn't let people know. They said their engineers didn't think it was important enough. I told them I had called earlier and no one had told me about the fan . Duh ... ??????? They didn't even offer to send me an updated fan .... 

I then reported this to CPSC by phone after I had talked to Whirlpool.

This fan blade has the possibilty to stop the motor and cause it to overheat. Then causing a short or fire ...

Sears price for the fan blade was $7.10 + shipping & handling of about $B.99 I ordered one thru a technician 15 miles away for $ 7.10 + tax.  I asked the technician if he's had the problem of the fan before. And he said "Alot more than you
might think."( A technician normally does not report problems to the CPSC, they just fix them so CPSC would not hear of the problem other than by a consumer)
justification: The incident involves a faulty freezer fan with potential to cause overheating or fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

Thank you for contacting Frigidaire.

We regret to hear that you are having difficulties with your Cooktop.  In cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Electrolux Home Products, Inc. is voluntarily recalling certain Frigidaire Electric Cooktops and Slide-in Ranges.  Liquids pooling under the control knob can cause the surface heating element to turn on unexpectedly, heat to temperatures other than expected and then not turn off, posing a risk of fire and burn hazards to our consumers.


Regrettably, your Model is listed under this recall; we ask that you stop using and unplug the recalled range or power off the cooktop at the circuit breaker.


Please call1-888-281-5310 between 8:00am to 10:00pm (EST) Monday through Saturday, to schedule a free service call.

Regards, [REDACTED]
Upon calling the number listed and speaking to a representative named [REDACTED] I was told this product was not recalled and that I had to start this process all over again tomorrow.

Clearly my model, although not yet recalled, has this same dangerous defect.

incident_description: I bought 24 "Eggies Hard-Boil Egg Cookers" which came in 4 packs of 6 each, on ebay ("cheryls-closeouts").  These are called "As seen on TV."  Each Eggie consists of an egg-shaped translucent white plastic base and top part, with an equatorial ring to hold the two together, and a little screw-in top cap closure.  Instructions were followed to wash first, then oil inside with any cooking oil.  Finally, you insert yolk and white in each through the top hole, then screw in the cap.  Then each filled Eggie is floated in warm water, then heat applied to bring to a boil, then wait about  20 minutes to achieve "hard boiled eggs."  About 15 minutes into the boiling, 3 of the Eggies exploded or suddenly came apart, even though the equatorial rings had be carefully tightened as well as the top caps.  The package warned of steam buildup upon user opening, but NOT the possibility of getting shot in the eye by a flying part.  I was just lucky that the top and caps missed my eyes.  There is NO steam outlet on an Eggie except for possible thread leakage.  Steam expands, or trys to expand, like in a steam engine.  I would say then that I observed a 3/24 failure rate in a sample of 24, or  1/8 failure rate, i.e. one in eight.  I was not hurt, but someone else, especially if leaning over the pans to watch, could be hurt, like lose an eye.  The ebay Seller does not accept returns on "opened packages or used items."   I am waiting for a reply from the Seller, who obviously does not know of any dangers.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (exploding Eggies) with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred. The failure rate observed was 1 in 8, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Summary: The left-front burner on my Frigidaire electric glass-top stove wouldn't turn off.

Details: When I started cooking, I set the burner to high for about a minute, then reduced the heat to 5.  After a couple of minutes I realized the heat was too high. The burner continued to glow brightly.  By this point the teflon pan was removed, but had already been ruined.  I shut off power to the stove at the circuit breaker.   When I restored power, all seemed normal again.
The next morning, my wife was cooking again and the same thing happened.  

The stove is now disconnected fearing fire and burn hazards.

incident_description: On July 15, 2011, I turned on my electric oven (GE Spectra Model #JBP26B0B1WH) and the heating element on the lower right side sparked, started burning, and sparks continued to fly from the flame. There was no food in the oven and there was no residue on the heating element, or other apparent causes for this spark. I turned off the oven, but there was still a visible electric current on the heating element, which began to melt, like when an insulated wire does when it shorts out and the plastic starts melting up the wire. We unplugged the oven and checked the breaker box to see if it had tripped, and within about 2 mins. the spark dissipated. The element was completely melted -- if we hadn't taken immediate action, it could have easily developed into a dangerous house fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to immediate action.

About 10 days ago, I was sitting at my computer, and we had a power
glitch. It was quite short, but enough to reset my computer. I started
rebooting the computer, and after a few minutes, I started to smell an
electrical fire. I rushed around the house to find it, and finally saw
an electrical fire inside our microwave, which was running. I quickly
pulled the plug, and opened the door. The glass tray inside had a 2-3
inch hole melted in it. The glass was red hot, and took many minutes to
cool enough to inspect. We were not cooking anything at the time, so the

microwave was empty.

I have been an electrical engineer for 45 years, and have developed many

products, some much higher power than this oven. It seems to me there
are a few problems with this whole incident. Firstly, a micro-controller

should be designed to not be sensitive to a short power interruption,
and certainly should not behave in an unpredictable behavior. Secondly,
the glass tray in the oven should not be able to be melted simply by
bombarding it with high energy microwaves. I don't know if the glass was

the fault, or the plastic rollers actually burned, but the glass has a
hole 'melted' in it. This may be due to a contamination in the glass. We

always keep the oven clean and well ventilated.

Thank God we were home at the time, as it could easily escalated into a
home fire. We have left our house often without unplugging the oven, and

have not had this problem before. We do have a lot of interruptions of
power, being very rural, but have not had this type of failure with any
other appliance. I am concerned that the safety of others may be
reflected in this incident. I also want Sears to repair or replace the
oven with, hopefully, a more reliable unit. I have the information all
documented, and will retain it all until I hear from you.

Thank you, respectfully,
[REDACTED]

incident_description: Fire crews responded to a reported residential structure fire. Upon arrival, fire crews located smoke and flames coming from the dishwasher. Fire crews proceeded to extinguish the fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire in a dishwasher, which was extinguished without reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I purchased Tommee Tippee Explora spill-proof water bottles on or about June 15, 2011.  Within weeks my 2 year old twins were able to chew the spout of the cup completely off of the cup. Had I not been sitting with my child, I feel he could have easily swallowed and possibly choked on the spout that had come off the bottle.  The product is marked for ages 18 months and up.  However, in light of the fact that my son was able to chew the spout off, I have no doubt that any child within the given age range would be able to do the same.  I would hate to have a child become injured because of this product
justification: The description indicates a potential choking hazard that could lead to injury, and the likelihood is high as the spout can be chewed off by children within the recommended age range.

incident_description: GE dishwasher model GLD 6860N10SS heating element failed to turn off at the end of cycle.  The element remained on all night.  Most plastic items were ruined or damaged.  Some plastic dishwasher parts sustained minor damage.
justification: The heating element failure caused property damage but no injuries.

justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is a significant incident, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description: Odor of burning electrical plastic in kitchen. Found to be coming from Amana refrigerator. Unit was then unplugged for safety. Appliance repair technician was called next day (7/15/11) and found the compressor starter relay had burnt. Visible charring and melting inside the relay which I have saved if needed for inspection. Checked with Amana but they report my model (ARB1917CC) is not listed in their recall of  refrigerators where this same part has caught fire. Identification number stampings on failed relay are 5SPD4T419PFM  21  R03R 419PFBYY -77 GAM3L
justification: The incident caused a burning odor and visible charring, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Fire loss in Whirlpool Model GU2400XPT3 s/n FS1406642 dishwasher.  Electrical damage to micro switch door latch part number FSP8269209.
justification: The incident describes a fire loss and electrical damage to a dishwasher component, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I was using my Frigidaire Electronic Wall Oven in Convection mode last night; it was set at 425 degrees and the glass door exploded and shattered into thousands of pieces.
justification: The glass door exploded, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: my frigidaire flat top oven/stove started smoking out of the vents in the back panel and the oven and the clock stopped working. When I pulled the back cover to investigate I found the control board had a 2" burn mark that completely burned the etching off the board. We live in Florida and lightning is always a concern but was not the case here as we were in the middle of a severe draught and had not had any storms in a month. The model number of the stove is FEF376ASL and the control board is a Spitfire SF5306 Rev. D
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the stove's control board but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have a Kenmore Elite Refrigerator Model # 795-77319600.  This morning I awoke to find the Master Control panel (on the ceiling of the fridge) hanging, melted, and hot.  The lights will not turn off.  This is a significant fire hazard.  After brief internet searches i was able to find a large number of customers who have had the same problem.  Sears expects me to maintain this fire hazard in my home for the next seven days (to wait for a part they are shipping after my call to them).  The certified repair company has the part and can resolve the issue today.  
I am significantly concerned regarding the lack of response, on the part of Sears, in dealing with this well-documented safety hazard.  I am also concerned that as an organization they are advising consumers to wait to repair appliances that pose safety risks.  

Below, please find just a few links to websites outlining this problem and the experiences of other customers.

http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/sears--kenmore-c107278.html
http://www.mysears.com/Refrigerators--3975/topics/Kenmore-Refrigerator-Light-Unit-SMOKING-/posts#post_221811
http://www.mysears.com/Refrigerators--3975/topics/Kenmore-Refrigerator-light-problems/posts


This issue warrants attention, please feel free to contact me.
justification: The incident involves a melted and hot control panel, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported. The likelihood is high given the documented cases from other customers.

incident_description:
Kenmore Elite Range Malfunction/Fire Hazard.
Stove was on when a loud popping began and sparks and black smoke came from the back of the stove.  Stove would not shut off or respond to keypad instructions... I had to flip breaker to shut stove down.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove with sparks and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
OUR COUNTERTOP BLACK&DECKER DIGITAL CONVECTION OVEN (MODEL CT06301) FAILED TO TURN OFF WHILE UNDER THE TWO YEAR WARRANT.

CALLED BLACK & DECKER WHO SENT US REPLACEMENT UNIT (MODEL CT067301) ON 3/24/2011 AND IT ALSO REFUSED TO SHUT DOWN TODAY JULY 12, 2011UNLESS WE UNPLUGGED FROM WALL.  WE HAVE CALLED BLACK AND DECKER TODAY, AND ARE AWAITING THEIR RETURN CALL.

AS THIS HAS HAPPED WITH 2 UNITS, THIS MAY BE A TRUE SAFETY ISSUE AS UNIT GETS EXTREMELY HOT IF IT DOES NOT STOP AT TIME TO QUIT.
justification: The oven failing to turn off poses a potential safety hazard due to extreme heat, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
On Monday, July 14th, I was baking 3 fish fillets. The fish is Swai, so they are larger, about half a pound per fillet. I baked them with a light coating of olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice.  After they had been baking about 15 minutes, 10 minutes at 400, about 5 more at 450, I opened the oven to remove the fish. 

When I started to lift the pan, moisture ran off the fish, and the bakeware shattered, though "exploded" is not an unreasonable description. Shards of glass were scattered throughout the oven with some on the floor around it. Fortunately, as oven door was only half open, no one was hit by the glass, and we were able eventually to remove sweep up all the tiny shards with only 1 or 2 minor pricks on fingers from tiny glass shards. 

The date was 9th, 10th, or 11th. Not sure right now.
justification: Minor pricks from glass shards indicate a minor injury, but no serious harm occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased our fridge in August of 2007 for $2000.00 @ Home Depot.  LFX25960ST.  On July 13th 2011, we noticed a strong electrical smell coming from our fridge.  When examining the odor we discovered that the lights in the fridge were not turning off and had melted the light housing, burned the bulb housings, and the plastic cover was so hot we needed potholders to remove the cover to get to the 2 bulbs to remove them.  The plastic around the light housing itself was so hot that I was able to push the melted plastic up with my fingers in a pot holder. 

I am glad that I found the problem as I was headed out for a week of vaca and Im positive this would have caught on fire.  The plastic cap on a food product that was under the light was also too hot to touch and remove. Thats how hot the entire light housing unit was. 

One month out of warranty on this fridge....Sept. 2008, the ice maker would work intermittently.  LG was no help what so ever.  Their customer service is horrible.   I will never purchase one of their products again.
justification: The incident involved a significant electrical malfunction that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: The glass on the interior of my 8year old GE electric oven shattered.  The oven was not being used.  I opened the door to cook a meal and found broken glass.
justification: The oven glass shattered without use, indicating an incident but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My GE Profile dishwasher caught fire this evening. I looked on line and then called GE. They stated there are similar units that are recalled for the same problem, but not my model #. Being a Professional Firefighter, I'm concerned that someone may have a more serious incident. Fortunately, I was home when this happened, because the outcome would have been different if I wasn't. We had our house built in 2004 so I believe the unit may be a 2004. The model # is PDW8800J03BB The serial # is SG776808B.

I hope this information is helpful to someone. I can be reached at [REDACTED] for further questions. My mailing address is [REDACTED]
Thank You for your time.

incident_description: The control panel of our dishwasher stopped working. When we took the cover off the dishwasher to make sure we ordered the correct part, we found that the two lines of the ribbon cable looked shorted and one line looked completed burned across. We researched recalls online for the dishwasher and at this point there are none, but multiple reports of fires. We have stopped using the dishwasher due to this evidence.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with evidence of a short circuit and burn marks, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My flat top range turns on spontaneously without being switched on and fails to turn off after being switched off, it also heats to a very high degree, unlike I have ever seen. I purchased a 4 year extended warranty, and this incident happened less than a month after it expired.
justification: The flat top range malfunctions by turning on and heating excessively, posing a hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We put our wall oven on cleaning cycle. The oven became extremely hot, we smelled fumes , we turned on exhaust on a separate range and turned on overhead fan in the den.
The insulation and/or seal on the door apparently melted, the seal inside the glass window melted steaking internally -- unable to clean between the glass lamination.
We fear that this excessive heat and "air leak" around the door seal could have been toxic and the extreme heat could have caused a fire in the house.
The wall oven was recently installed,, two technicians have said it can't be fixed, we are getting resistance from the Fridgidaire customer survice representatives.
The item is a Fridgedaire Single Wall Oven - item # FFEW3025LB A  Brand FR12M purchased from Wholesale Appliance Center , LLC in Summerville, SC. We purchased this OVEN in February this year , it was instaled at the end of March 2011.
Appliance Doctors of Ladson, SC have verified that this oven needs to be replaced.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that emitted fumes and had a melted seal, posing potential fire and toxicity risks, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My Kenmore electric range has a burner that on more than one occasion has not shut-off or when the temperature on the burner is turned down, the burner still remains hot on the high setting. Last evening the burner turned itself on by itself. Luckily I noticed this before I went to bed, the outcome may have caused a fire. There are several Kenmore electric ranges that have been recalled similar to my stove. My stove has not been recalled, but I believe it should. A burner that turns itself on is a danger, espcially with small children in my home.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred. The issue has happened multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Last night I opened my 3 year old Sears Kenmore 3 door refrigerator (model 795.7730, beginning SN 801) and saw that the 2 lights were out.  I reached up to the cover and it was too hot to touch and food nearby was warm.  I used oven mitts, and removed the cover and bulbs.  I read the owner's manual on replacing the bulbs and followed those directions, however, the lights did not come back on.

I went to CPSC.gov  and read many comments from other owners of a similar product and learned that I was very lucky in finding this problem before it melted the plastic around the sockets.  I also saw a mention of Sears Service Flash SF46-515R4 to use when calling Sears for service on this problem.  I spoke to [REDACTED] with Sears and she did some research for me and found out that this SF was for models with SN prior to my "801."  

This sounds like a very dangerous trend with this light problem and I wanted to share it with you.  I am going ahead with Sears repair to get this fixed, but it does seem like some that Sears needs to own up to.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous condition (overheating lights) but no injury occurred, and similar issues are reported by other owners, indicating likelihood.

incident_description: The compressor of our Kenmore Elite refrigerator became extremely hot and started to burn the surrounding wire/plastic parts. The burning smell had alerted us to the problem. There was also an intermittent clicking sound associated with this incident.  Thankfully, we unplugged the refrigerator before a fire started.
justification: The compressor overheated and caused burning, but no fire or injury occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: Bottom of a Paula Deen 3 quart stackable steamer pot (with copper bottom) melted into molten metal after the pot boiled dry on the stovetop.  When I picked the pot up to drain the vegetables inside, the bottom dripped hot metal over my countertop, floor, a rug and finally the sink where I left the pot.  The drippings burned dents into my countertop and sink, and set an area rug on fire.  I have contacted Meyer (the manufacturer) 4 times with no response.  I am seeking a refund for the product, as well as compensation for damage to my kitchen.  In addition, I want to ensure that this product is removed from the market so that others are not harmed.  The metal could have caused serious personal injury.
justification: The incident caused property damage and a fire, but no personal injury was reported.

incident_description: The refrigatrator is extremly hot on the metal front between the freezer and the frig.  Even the seal that keeps the doors from leaking air out is warm to the touch.  I am worried there is going to be a fire.  It has been making the food in the frig go bad, milk, butter etc.
justification: The refrigerator is overheating, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description: I was cleaning the interior of my IKEA Energisk B18 W refrigerator/freezer when I suffered a laceration on my middle and ring fingers. The compartments of the refrigerator door are sectioned off by metal bars, and the bars are constructed by folding the edges of a flat sheet of metal over approximately one inch on the top and bottom. The edges of the folded metal are extremely sharp, and cut through both the paper towel I was using to wipe the fridge and my skin. The laceration required emergency care, as it bled profusely and was jagged. The laceration on my middle finger required three sutures to repair.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring emergency care and sutures, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Maytag Dishwasher
Model MDB9150AWW
Ser# 27614890AL
While using this dishwasher, smoke, burning smell, and sound of electrical sparks came out from bottom of front door panel. I removed the inside cover and discovered the main wiring harness that goes between the control board to various electrical components (motor, relays, sensors) have shorted out with burnt marks and with couple of wires severed. There are exposed copper wires where the wire insulation is showing signs of cracks and openings. I believe the wiring harness is faulty due to the flexibility of the insulation to handle the opening and closing motion of the door. This fault can potentially cause house fire and/or cause electrical shocks to the consumers. Others have also reported having the same issue. Maytag was contacted but wasn't interested in looking further into this incident. I have pictures showing the problem wiring harness.
justification: The incident involves a faulty wiring harness causing smoke and sparks, posing a fire hazard and electrical shock risk, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: On 7/2/2011, went into the kitchen and smelled burning. Interior temperature of refrigerator had risen to about 90 degrees.  All of the food was spoiled and freezer contents had melted. We were very concerned the refrigerator would overheat and/or possibly start a fire, especially considering the burning smell we also had smelled. We have two very small children and were concerned for their safety and ours, so we unplugged the refrigerator for safety reasons. Immediately reported the burning to Maytag's automated customer service line which assigned a repair tech to come to our home on 7/5/2011. On 7/5/2011, repair technician came to the home and said that the compressor was defective/burned out. Same day called Maytag while repair tech was present in the home and explained incident and concerns but Maytag representatives didn't seem concerned at all. Also, they refused repair and/or warranty claim even though refrigerator had obviously burned up and was covered by warranty. Also representatives tried to claim 1 year warranty applied which was false and misleading since refrigeration components (including specifically compressors) are covered "through" the 5th year of the warranty.
justification: The incident involved a defective refrigerator with a burning smell and spoiled food, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says that when she bakes items in oven and pull the pan out the glass pan will explode.  The consumer says that this has happened 2 or 3 times.  The consumer says she cannot place anything on the bottom rack because it burns things really fast.  The consumer says her temperature is only set between 350-375 degrees.  She is concerned for her safety and has discontinued use of the range.  The consumer says also the burners cook things to hot and fast.

She tried to turn it down but the temperature just kept rising until she and her husband turned the stove off and then the circuit breaker off.
She contacted the manufacturer who advised her that there was no recall at this time. Consumer is unable to find out f there is a part to buy that will fix this.  
This happened possibly another five times (she doesn't remember the dates) until Sunday, June 19th she was cooking for Father's Day and the same burner repeated the same escalation of heat and the same steps were taken to alleviate the heat.
Caller views this as an extreme fire hazard, would like this range investigated and recalled.
(Caller did not contact manufacturer this date) siting they were of no assistance previous calls to them.
As of 7/10/11, consumer cannot  use the left large burner.

The product did not emit any smell at the time that it exploded. The product was used two days prior to the incident. The product did not cause any damage to the consumer's home. The consumer stated that no fire ensued after the explosion of the product.

incident_description:

About four hours later she heard a loud noise and discovered that the toaster oven glass door had exploded shattering glass peices over the countertop.

Consumer stated that the retailer store advised taht there was nothing they could do, she would have purchase another toaster oven they would not replace the defective brand.
Consumer believes that this product is a safety hazard and should be recalled.

incident_description:

She said that all glass pieces were every small when the broke.

incident_description:
The home we built and occupied on October 10, 2004 was furnished with a GE JBPWOH2WW electric range. About 2 years ago the upper element in the oven left a white powder after it burned. We had this element replaced. This week my wife was preheating the oven and heard a sizzling sound and looked down and found the bottom of the oven on fire. The fire grew around the coil. She closed the door and turned off the electricity. I had heard of this problem before and felt this report necessary to expose the potential for property damage and risk to life. I was doubly driven to do this as one of my children has a similar GE range of the same series that was installed in a home they built a few years before us. They had a fire exactly the same but more intense in March where they had the fire department responds as it was more stubborn to extinguish. In both ours and their case we felt it prudent not to attempt to fix but replace these products in the interest of safety considering it a possible design flaw or substandard part. The oven is cleaned frequently and no spills are left to build up in our effort to operate this product in a safe manner.
FYI: in information below we have had problems with other GE products installed at construction and the manufacture has stonewalled in these instances so I feel it would be not productive in attempting to fight with them. Additionally we do not have room for storage in our condo so it was hauled away by Lowes - I do have picture.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven with no reported injuries, but potential for property damage and risk to life.

incident_description: Baking in the oven and when time to turn off the oven it would not turn off.  This happened a couple times so now we do not use it.  We need to get it fixed but the cost is not in our budget with labor cost too.
justification: The oven not turning off is an incident but no injury or harm occurred, and it has happened multiple times before being taken out of use.

incident_description: I bought a Wirlpool gas range a few years back , the glass oven door gets extermly hot and well as the control knobs w2hen oven is in use, model # SF31opekwo serial # BVEL3207713 The handle and glass are attachech by a screww which the screw  is on the inner part of oven and it screws into a plastic peice on handle, it gets so hot that eventually it cracks and the oven door falls apart, i called Wirlpool and they said it was outta warrenty and i had to purchace a new hadle, here it is a year and half later it does same thing only this time catching my arm while it was in oven and burning me badly , i want  this reported it has now become a safety hazard , they should have looked into deeper the frist time when i told them it seemed unsafe. [REDACTED][REDACTED]
