incident_description: Oven keeps randomly coming on at the high broiler setting. Oven got so hot it discolored the outside of the oven door.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and got extremely hot, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description:
This letter and report are to urge you to issue a safety recall for Krups electric coffee  maker, model KT 4065 which I believe is a newly designed product. You can see from the receipt, I purchased this coffee-maker five months ago; I began using it approximately four months ago, Early in use, the coffeemaker spilled hot fluid all over our kitchen counter on two occaSions, but I dismissed it Recently, it has it done this on a fairly regular basis, Enclosed is the actual coffee maker so you may test and verify the safety design defect in this product. Also enclosed is my receipt and the product booklet with warranty. Although this item is still under warranty, the terms indicate that Krups would repair or replace the item. Since this item is a huge safety hazard, I am not interested in another one of these.

Defective design, This coffee maker overflows the carafe spilling scalding hot fluid onto the counter or table. For families with small children who reach onto the counter, this is particularly dangerous. From my inspection, it appears that either the plastic lid to the carafe or the cone filter chamber is the culprit. The lid has a small trap door and very small entry holes for the water. I am a foodie and purchase high end appliances, cutlery, kitchen devices and am well versed in how to use them. The cause of the chronic overflow problem is definitely not:

(1 ) Lack of cleanliness. There was no excessive debris or calcification because we clean our coffee makers with white vinegar every 2 months. When this second spillover happened, I performed an extra deep vinegar soak and clean of all parts to make sure this would not happen again. It functioned fine for two mornings, then three days later the overflow occurred again. 

(2) The grind or type of coffee. We grind our coffee by hand where it is not too course, not too fine as we have for the past 4 years. We primarily use [REDACTED] Decaf or Breakfast blend. This was the coffee in use during the overflow incidents.

(3) The type of filter. We use the same filters we have always used. Two previous coffeemakers over the years have used the same cone type which we get at the grocery store nearby. I enclosed a few of those so that you can see for yourself
should you decide to test this. 

(4) The centering of the carafe. I have made 100% certain the carafe is centered directly under the cone (in fa~ there is a crevice that guides the carafe to keep it centered) and that the lid is correctly tightened on top with the thumb tab aligned
correctly.

(5) The water level. I have made 100% certain that I only fill the coffee maker up to the 10 cup level.
justification: The coffee maker spills hot fluid regularly, posing a safety hazard, especially to small children, but no injury is reported.

incident_description: The consumer was baking a potato in microwave.  The consumer says they started smelling smoke.  He said the entire house was full of smoke.  His wife opened the microwave door and the unit was on fire from the inside.  He says the unit was charred.  the consumer contacted the manufacturer who told him the problem was with the baked potato because sometimes they have air pockets inside of them.  The consumer says he has never had this issue before in his life and he has been cooking baked potatoes all his life and he is 44 years old.  The consumer had a technician inspect the unit and he said that the cooking sensor was the problem.  The consumer contacted the technician thru the manufacturer's website.  The cosumer says also that they would not warranty the product because the consumer left it unattended.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such incidents are not common but have been documented.

incident_description:
Sharp microwave/convection oven, model R-8310, serial number 93870, manufacturered Aug., 1983.

Convection portion of oven failed.  Triac that controls heating element shorted, charred, and partially melted, activated smoke or fire alarm.  The thermistor that senses oven temperature (located elsewhere in product) developed a spot inside it (visible because thermistor is in clear glass package), possibly due to exposure to greatly excessive voltage or current.  I believe these failures may have been related to the convection temperature control shorting to the chassis, which could be a shock hazard if the oven is plugged into an ungrounded AC outlet.  This control is supposed to be electrically insulated from the chassis, as evidenced by the sheet of plastic (mylar?) between its metal body and the oven chassis and the use of plastic screws to attach it to the chassis.  One of those screws cracked, and that may have caused the failure.  This circuit is not isolated from high voltage with a transformer, and instead its power is derived by a 1-3 watt resistor that drops the high voltage to a much lower value.

The manufacturer was informed of this incident years ago but did not respond, except to recommend repair by an authorized service center (not possible due to parts, including the thermistor, no longer being available, not even from sources not authorized by manufacturer).  They did not seem to care or understand the electric shock hazard and were quite poorly trained.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and potential shock hazard, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the right front burner wont turn on unless it is on high.  She says when it is on sometimes it wont turn off.  The consumer says that the contact on the control between the glass top and the back where the knobs are started visibly arching, posing a fire hazard.  The consumer says the only way to turn off the burner is by cutting off the circuit breaker.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who said they would send out a technician for a fee.
justification: The burner malfunction and visible arcing pose a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the front right burner would cut on by itself.  He contacted the builder who replaced the whole unit.  The consumer says it worked okay for a while, but then if he turned on one burner a different one would turn on.  The consumer says the burners are also turning on spontaneously without being turned on.  The consumer says his unit is doing the exact same thing as listed in the recall.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who transferred him around to different departments and someone told him they would call him back, yet they never did.  The consumer says lastnight he cleaned the range and washed the dishes.  He stepped outside for a moment.  When he came back inside, the burner was on.  Consumer has same brand and product as listed in release # 09-333.  His model and serial # are not included in the recall.
justification: The consumer says the burners are turning on spontaneously, which could lead to a fire hazard, but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: The consumer says his wife turned the oven on to 250 degrees. She went to the next room & immediately heard a crackling & popping sound coming from the kitchen. She went back to the kitchen & saw flames & smoke coming out of the back, top portion, of the range. She turned the oven off & the fIre went out..The fIre & smoke blackened the wallpaper behind the range & it will not come clean ... The consumer opened the back of the range & noticed that the control board & modules ,along with some of the connecting wires were burned off. The plastic case supporting the controls had melted from the heat of the flIe. The consumer contacted SEARS, the retailer from whom the unit was purchased, & they wanted to send a technician out to look at the problem & charge the consumer $ 129.00
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke causing damage to the range and surrounding area, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
While lying in bed she heard a loud explosion she went into the kitchen and noticed that the glass from the toaster oven door had shattered onto the floor, counter and inside of the oven. The handle to the oven's door was laying on top of the counter near the toaster.

 She recalled using the oven about four and half hours prior to when the incident occurred. The toaster oven was in the unplug position from the wall outlet. When the glass shattered it was into a million little pieces. 

She contacted the firm on 6/23/2011 and was advised that there was not a recall involving the model number. She will also contact the retailer to determine if they will allow her to return the product.
justification: The incident involved a toaster oven glass shattering, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The oven was powered in the on position on bake at 250 degrees for two hours while the consumer and his family left the home. After returning he noticed that the home was filled with smoke and an electrical burning odor in the home. While opening the oven door he noticed that the food that was placed inside of the oven was not burned  but the heating element at the bottom of the oven was glowing bright red.  

There was an error code E@ or F2 on the control panel. Unable to power the range in the off position by using the proper switch the circuit breaker had to be powered in the off position. He went to the retailer and spoke with the store manager (name unknown) and he was the provided with the retailers service number. 

He contacted the service number and the representative that he spoke with recommended that he have a service technician come out to the home to take a look at it. He declined in having any repairs made to the unit in fear that the hazard would repeat itself and potential y pose as a fire hazard. He contacted the firm on 6/20/2011 and was advised that the there was no recall involving the model number and serial number of his unit. 

The range was still in the off posiiton due to the circuit breaker being powered off. On 6/21/2011 he powered the circuit breaker back into the on position and the oven powered back into the on position without being switched in the on position. He powered the circuit breaker back in the on off position. On 6/22/2011 he powered the circuit breaker back into the on position and the range powered on at the highest setting. He quickly powered the circuit breaker back into the off position in which it still currently remains.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical burning odor but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was contained by turning off the circuit breaker.

incident_description: The consumer says the heat shoots up to high even if the knob is on the lowest.  The consumer says this has happened several times.  She says all of the knobs are doing this.  She says there are no issues with the oven.  The consumer says her husband made repairs to oven about a year ago.  She says the only issue is with the burner knobs.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and told her there is no recall for it and there is nothing they can do about it.  The unit is having the same issue as in Release # 09-333.  She says it started with one burner and they all have gradually have been having this problem over the course of a few months.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner knob causing excessive heat, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
In September 2010, our (from Sears) Kenmore Elite model #665.1747 - 3300 caught FIRE.  At the time, the fire dept came out and was able to limit the damage to just the unit and the surrounding area.  Sears really didn't work with us very well.  They passed us to Kenmore who passed us to Sears and back and forth we went.  The Kenmore Elite IS part of a recall however, the ending digits are not - solely because we were told that the unit was top of the line and so expensive that they weren't including them.  Nice.  We hassled with this for weeks.  We didn't want to purchase a new one only to later be told that we would get a replacement and not reimbursed.  So we waited - and hand washed.  Until finally in Nov we broke down.  If it was a staring contest, we lost.  Kenmore and Sears won.  We purchased the Maytag using whatever credits we could get and in the end spent $851.98 for the new dishwasher.
Because this was really part of a recall and on a technicality it was not covered.  I am still upset this many months later.  
But I still feel VERY upset and burned, literally, that we had no dishwasher for 2 months, had to complain nearly daily, hassle with Kenmore, complain to Sears, get very upset which in the end upset my chronic health issues to the point, I had to stop the process, give up and give in.
What I would like is Kenmore to do the right thing and refund us the full cost of having to purchase a replacement since their unit caught fire - again, at no fault of our own - on a unit they fully knew had issues and was in their recall.
But that seems like that will never happen.
This isn't me trying to get a free ride or take advantage of Sears.  This is me trying to get justice.  To get really what is owed to me.
The cost of the Maytag we purchased was $851.98. (reg 949.99)I haven't gotten anywhere with Sears or Kenmore on the recall issue - I haven't gotten much anywhere with any of this.
We were/are a loyal customer to Sears and of Kenmore products,  who did nothing wrong except have their dishwasher catch fire in middle of the night, causing fire department to come and us to evacuate then spending 2 weeks getting the smell of burnt plastic and wiring out of the house.  We had the expense of staying elsewhere because the air was so thick it was hard to breathe.  All the horror we went through, blessed that the whole kitchen or worse, house didn't burn down.  The firemen said we were SO lucky that once it had started, it really could have taken off.  We also had damage to the surrounding area and tile work - all items we had to pay for.  Nothing got covered.
I would love the whole $850 refunded to me which was the cost of a new unit.  I know - I ask a lot.  But imagine yourself, asleep, 3am, kids and dogs in the home, and you smell something burning.  You find your high end dishwasher on fire.  And then no one helps you even though it is on the recall list.  You hand wash for weeks.  You give up.  You purchase a unit that doesn't come close to the one you had before and aren't 100% happy with but make do.  
The fire department reassured us we did nothing wrong.  The control electrical panel caught fire.  Something about how they are now using cheaper parts that can not handle the amount of volts going through the unit.  The fire department themselves has had TWO dishwashers catch fire in the last year.....both Kenmore.  
Our unit was the Kenmore Elite 665-1747 -3300 and I truly believe that ALL their units in that section was recalled EXCEPT ours and they really did say it was because it was the expensive line therefore not cost effective to them to add that to the recall because people with higher budgets tend to just pay to replace a unit than hassle with a recall process.  If they added it to the recall then they would be replacing units that might not have issues and the cost to Kenmore would be too high.  This offended me.  I guess it doesn't pay to buy high end.  Buy cheaper so they will replace it when it burns up?
Our house could have burned down.  Thankfully it didn't.  The local Sears admitted that one other unit the same model had caught fire recently as well.  Going online I am seeing this model has issues.  Our family could have been killed.  We are so thankful that at 3am we were able to smell it and get out of the house before too much damage was done.  In the end, we had a stinky house with a hole in the wall and hand washed for 2 months and didn't get reimbursed or compensated for this.  Not for the inconvenience, not for the clean up, not to have the wiring checked and replaced by an electrician, not the cost of the repair mans service call and repair to the melted freeze lines that were melted in the fire, not the worry it caused our kid to have to leave his home in middle of the night with firemen rushing through.......it was misery and in the end - we paid for it.  Completely.  This is NOT right.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher catching fire, causing property damage and significant inconvenience, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Oven was set to bake.  After preheating oven to 350, placed cookie sheet in with dough.  Approximately 3 minutes later, my brother noticed smoke coming out of the oven and looked inside.  The broiler burners had turned on and the cookies were on fire.  He said he saw a yellow error message on the instrument panel, but did not remember what it said.  He turned the oven off and pulled the cookie sheet out and took it outside to douse the flames with water.  This is at least the fifth time this has happened.

Sears carries the warranty on this appliance and has refused to acknowledge any problem.  The broiler does not turn on every time I bake and Sears technicians say have not been able to replicate the problem.  However, each time they come out, they can see that the bake feature "is not available."  The technician does something (I do not know what because I cannot see everything they are doing to the back of the oven) to reset the oven so the bake feature works again.  Then, they test the oven - 1 time - and tell me the oven is working properly.  They do not replace nor repair anything.

Eventually, there will be a more serious fire and my home will burn down.  So far, the only reason that has not happened is because I stay in my kitchen all the time while I am baking.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard with potential for serious consequences, but no injury or death has occurred yet. The problem is recurring and not adequately addressed by technicians.

incident_description: We purchased our fridge in the summer of 2006. Not only was it 3 weeks late and we had to live out of a cooler, but then the light unit caught on fire and burned out until we were able to unplug it and use oven mitts to take out the bulbs. We called sears and Kenmore but since we had the unit for about 20 months, they said we were out of warranty and would not do anything for us and even wanted to charge us to talk to someone on the phone. We saw the other people who had complained about this and heard it would be 500 to fix the problem and we don't have that kind of money to spend on a fridge we paid over 2300 for less than 2 years before. My parents also had a Kenmore and had the same thing happen to their fridge. Neither appliance had been recalled so we had no options. We have been living with the same fridge with no light. Not too big of a deal, but we have had to watch it carefully to be sure that it doesn't start burning again. I feel we were very lucky to catch the problem before it turned into a full fledge fire! I smelled something burning from upstairs and tracked it to the fridge.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the fridge light unit but was caught before causing injury or significant damage, indicating a no-injury incident with a low recurrence likelihood based on the description.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore 30" Electric Range, Model 790.9422240B, S/N: VF73249031, that has a "Simmer Select" feature that reduces the heat to the left front high heat burner to allow simmering of delicate foods or sauces.    This feature experienced two failures since ownership over the 3yr period due to electrical shortage or blowing of its fuse.  The result is not only does it not work, but the burner will unpredictably experience a flare-up or increase in heat when set at a low or medium setting which results in the coil becoming "red-hot" and for food potentially burning when not intended or expecting.   This is a potential fire hazard and risk for injury.   Sears wants to charge as much as a new stove to fix the problem.    We feel that there should be a recall on this stove because of this problem.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard and risk of injury, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: This is a kenmore oven. the oven will not sut off it gives F1 or F2 error and the item over heats and smokes. the power to the unit has to be shut off by way of circut breaker.
justification: The oven overheating and smoking poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
We have a Bosch dishwasher that is included in the 2009 recall.  Though we sent our registration card in, we were never notified by Bosch.  The dishwasher caught fire last week, and though all the wiring and control panel is blackened by the smoke and fire, Bosch wants to replace the board.  The authorized repair service says they cannot get the part for at least 3 weeks as well.  I'm furious.  I normally start the dishwasher and go to bed, or start the dishwasher and leave the house.  Luckily this time I was home.  I walked outside after starting the dishwasher and returned 10 minutes later to find my kitchen filled with smoke, so much smoke that the glasses in my upper cupboards had to be re- washed.  The smoke was coming from the dishwasher which was making a horrible popping and crackling noise.  Not thinking I opened the dishwasher to turn it off and burned (not badly) my hand in the process.  

So, first I want to report it, tho we were very lucky our home was not damaged.  Second, I want to complain about Bosch not handling this correctly.  They said I can have 200 dollars credit towards a new Bosch dishwasher or they can repair it.  The dishwasher was $800 and it's only 7 years old.  It should have lasted 20 years.  At the very least they should pro-rate the reimbursement.  I also strongly believe that a dishwasher that caught fire should not be repaired.  One quick search on the Internet will show you that, after repair, they are catching fire again.

Can you help us in any way?
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke damage and a minor burn injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the recall history and similar incidents reported online.

incident_description:
Magic Chef Microwave Model # MCO160UW
Serial #DJ07Yo3560
Nov 2007

Microwave turns itself on, keypad locks up and unit cannot be turned off. Open door, then close it press off/cancel and it comes on again. This has happened twice in the past couple of days when I happened to get up early in the morning and came downstairs to find the unit running and hot inside.
Another time, it turned itself on whilst I was using the stove to boil eggs and the steam was coming up into the exhaust vents under the unit.

I have no idea how often it comes on when I am not home or during the night. I am afraid of it now as it is a fire hazard. 

Upon looking, I found MANY reports of this online, why has this model not been recalled???
justification: The microwave turning itself on poses a fire hazard, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Whirlpool Gold side by side refrigerator model GS6SHAXLQ03 starter relay burned out. Upon disassembly, blackened plastic housing and melted contacts were discovered. While researching this on the web, I found multiple reports of fires arising from this type and model of refrigerator, which has been attributed to the starter relay. The starter relay is common to multiple refrigerators (including Maytag). I did not experience the fire but the fact it got hot to melt metal contacts disturbs me.
justification: The starter relay burned out and caused damage, but no fire or injury occurred. Multiple reports of fires indicate a significant risk.

incident_description: Burner was turned on level 4 and was hotter than should have been.  Griddle turned white it was so hot.  Also, when the HE went off the burner was still very warm, enough that you could not touch it.  This happens all the time.
justification: The burner was excessively hot, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported. The issue happens 'all the time', indicating it is almost certain to recur.

incident_description: stove is about 4 years old and about a 11/2 years ago when you turn the stove on bake, it somehow switches to broil and it burns what you have in it. If I would not of been paying attention my stove would of caught fire. It does not do this all the time, enough to upset me. I writing this to you now to see if anyone eles has been having the same problem. I spent alot money on this stove for it to be acting up already. I should of keep my 1970 stove that worked great, but didnt look good in my kitchen. With my old stove I could lay down and take a nap and not worry about my house catching on fire. This new stove I cant even go to the bathroom. Noone should have to worry about burning their house down everytime you cook dinner.
justification: The stove's malfunction poses a fire hazard but no actual injury or death has occurred, and the issue happens intermittently but not constantly.

incident_description:
My Kenmore Flat top electric range model # 790.95304103 sn# VF24137312, bake oven would not stop heating. The controls would not turn off the oven, and I had to turn off the power at the circuit breaker. If we hadn't noticed the oven getting hot, it could have easily burnt something or possibly dammaged the rest of the oven. This product should have an overriding thermal cutout similar to a dryer, to shut off the oven if the control fails. Very dangerous product. Several complaints about these Kenmore ovens have been reported at http://www.complaintsboard.com/complaints/kenmore-oven-c14186.html?sort=datea&page=1  
Thank you
justification: The oven was not able to turn off, which could have caused a fire or damage to the oven, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Smoothtop range spontaneously turn on burner.  Could not turn burner off, no controls were responsive.  Had to turn off circuit breaker to turn oven off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range with no reported injury, and such occurrences are uncommon but documented.

incident_description: When on vacation, the Kenmore electtic range turned on the broiler function and overheated.  The unit stayed on and caused the internal racks to melt.  Fortunately, we came home and found the unit on.  We could not approach it as it was emitting extreme heat.  All of the dials were off and there was no indication that the unit was on.  We turned off circuit breaker to range.  We cooled the unit down for 12 hours and then flipped the circuit breaker.  The oven immediately turned on the broiler unit.  All dials on the stove were off.  In discussion with appliance repair man, he inidcated he felt it would not be wise to repair unit as the reason for the failure could be many..
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted racks) but no injury or death, and the likelihood is possible given the unexpected malfunction.

incident_description: I opened the refrigerator door this morning and immediately noticed a hot electrical smell, like burning wires and plastic. I told my husband and it took us both a few minutes to realize it was the light inside the unit. The light was apparently on all night, even with the doors shut, and got extremely overheated, melting the plastic casing and emitting noxious plastic fumes. The plastic cover had started to drop down, which was beginning to expose the hot bulbs (there are 2 of them). The food close to the lights was overly warm, including milk, yogurt, sour cream.  My husband removed the cover with some difficulty because it was melted and deformed.  He then took a towel and unscrewed both light bulbs to make them go out.  I have not contacted Sears yet, but will be doing so today.  In the meantime, I got on the Internet this morning and found numerous complaints about this same problem, many of them from late in 2010.  I even found a warning from the Fire Marshal in Canada about this problem with Kenmore refrigerators. One person noted they were told the cause of this problem is a faulty circuit board that causes overheating. People that had it replaced said the new unit has an overheat switch that shuts the lights off if they get too hot. THERE NEEDS TO BE A RECALL ON THIS!!!  This could be a serious problem -- either a fire hazard or a problem with the noxious plastic fumes. I hope Sears will cover the cost to repair this, as it is ridiculous to expect the consumer to pay to replace this obviously faulty part. We've only had our unit for a few years. I don't know how I'm going to get that smell out of my refrigerator and I'm concerning about those fumes and the food in there.  As I said, there are a number of people on line with this same problem, but I don't know if they are reporting it here or not.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous electrical malfunction with potential fire risk and noxious fumes, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she was awaken by an explosion in the kitchen, she discovered that the glass door of the toaster oven had exploded and shattered glass peices on the countertop and the floor.

Consumer stated that the last time the unit was used was the evening before and it was not in use when this incident occurred.

5/17/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that there was nothing that could be done and she can file an incident report with the Agency.

Consumer feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and shattered glass, but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common based on the description.

incident_description:
I have a Bosch dual fuel range model # HDI7282U/03.  Our oven turns on when the power goes out and comes back on.  It has happened twice.  The first time I was sure I had turned the oven off, but blamed it on myself.  The second time was during a storm.  I had come down about 2 am to check the radar and no oven was on.  When my husband got up late about 5:30 because the power had gone off during the night, he found the oven on to 405 degrees.  

I have contacted the dealer and they suggested changing the panel, but I am afraid the same problem could happen again.  I have also contacted Bosch and they are reviewing what they can do for me.  It seemed like a serious problem that could lead to a fire.  I now turn my oven breaker off unless it is in use.
justification: The oven turning on unexpectedly poses a fire hazard, but no injury or damage has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Our Frigidaire dishwasher did not finish it's cycle and the heating element remained on overnight resulting in the bottom spray wand and dishes in the dishwasher melting.  The heating element did not turn off until we opened the dishwasher after smelling a burning smell.  Had we not been home, the incident could have ultimately resulted in a fire.  At the time of the incident the dishwasher was only 18 months old.  The model and serial number are as follows:

Model:  PLD4375RFC3
Serial #:TH85087214
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, causing the heating element to remain on, resulting in damage to the dishwasher and dishes, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Defective Gas, Kitchen Stove Jen-Air range model #JGR8875QDS  Serial #16463840JJ

This range has heat vents on top of the door, just under the knobs. The knobs get so hot that they have melted and it's necessary to warn anyone to stay away from the stove when it is on because they could easily be burned. Especially dangerous for small children.

I believe that this model is poorly designed and should be replaced. Two of the knobs have melted so badly that they can not be used.
justification: The knobs get extremely hot and have melted, posing a burn risk, especially to small children, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Maytag Built-In Dishwasher
Model: DWU9200BAB
Serial Number: 26379054MM

While the dishwasher was in use, a large flash appeared beside the base and the circuit breaker tripped.  Fortunately, no one was injured and damage was confined to the dishwasher unit.  

When the unit was inspected by a BGE Home repair tech, damaged wiring was discovered. An electrical wiring bundle located in the base of the unit shorted, causing the wiring insulation to blacken and melt.  The dishwasher has been disconnected and is awaiting removal.

I checked both CPSC.GOV and the MAYTAG website; I could not find where this model dishwasher had been recalled.  I called the MAYTAG Recall Hotline, was told that this dishwasher had not been recalled, and was invited to call Customer Service.  I attempted to call MAYTAG Customer Service, but the wait was excessive.

Bottom Line:  As the dishwasher was functioning as advertised until it failed due to an electical short, I suspect there are still units of this model in use and users may well be unaware of the danger associated with this model.
justification: The dishwasher was functioning as advertised until it failed due to an electrical short, causing no injury.

incident_description: I was hosting a party at my home which included making margaritas.  I purchased this blender at Wal-Mart 3 days earlier and successfully made 2 pitchers of margaritas (tequila, grand marnier, and ice).  On the third attempt, a large chunk of glass exploded from the bottom of the glass jar thowing glass shards and liquid all over my kitchen.  One large chunk of glass hit me in the stomach and several small slivers of glass were found on the floor, countertops, and bread basket.  There was a huge mess to clean up since liquid sprayed all over the floor, cabinets, and other kitchen appliances.  It was a great inconvenience and diappointment, not to mention a very scary and dangerous situation.  The party was interrupted to clean up the mess and we were no longer able to serve margaritas.
justification: A large chunk of glass hit the person in the stomach, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
Viking Electric Double Oven, Model DED0527TSS, Serial # 062907C00059972, Installed 7/31/2008.  Shortly after it was installed the upper door did not close firmly, leaving the light on inside, and preventing the oven from reaching the set temperature.  The company records warranty service September 29, 2008 for repair under warranty.  There were additional visits to this remote location, but the servicing agency, Kendall Distributing and Viking have no records, according to them.

Returning to this seasonal home in late June, we found the upper door did not close properly, remaining 8 mm ajar and not reaching set temperature: set to 375 degrees it reaches 240 to 325 degrees, and does not reach the set temperature in even several hours.

Viking claims that they have not encountered such problems in the past, but the professional repairman states to me it was a recurrent problem fixed by an established procedure.  Viking further informs me that they will not compensate me or the distributor or repairman for parts or labor.  

This is a serious safety problem, notwithstanding Vikings unwillingness to acknowledge the issue.  My fear is that others will not know how to deal with the faulty hinges on this and other Viking models, as the company claims to me in phone calls they recorded that there have been no recalls, bulletins or special actions over hinges or door closing issues.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning oven door that does not close properly, posing a potential safety hazard but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
We Purchased A Cuisinart Premier Coffee Maker Model # DCC-1100 Approximately 4 months ago.
On July 4th 2011 the Coffee Maker Developed an internal electrical short causing smoke to billow from the back of the unit. (Electrical Fire )
My Wife Smelled the burning elecrical wiring and saw the coffee maker smoking on the counter top My wife pulled the power cord from the elecric outlet. We Moved The Coffee Pot To A Safe Place as the Coffee Pot Continued To Smolder At The Back of the unit for some time.
The heat from the electrical fire was hot enough to blister the coating on the built in coffee pot heat plate. The potential for serious fire damage to our home from this defective product was deffinately there if this had happened while we were not at home.

After Doing Some Online Research We have Concluded that this is not an isolated issue with the Cuisinart coffee makers and the problem spans several models.

We have not contacted Cuisinart Customer Service yet. Based Upon Complaints about the Cuisinart Customer service lack of interest and concern about the problem and their warranty policy concerning this issue, We are not interested in a replacement Coffee Maker. at an additional cost to Us as the consumer.
Nor Will We Be Able To Trust Cuisinart to porvide us with a defect free replacement.

We Put Our Six Year Old Mr. Coffee Maker Back Into Service, Now We Feel Safer.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire with smoke and potential for serious damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
GE Profile Dishwasher PDW 7380 N 15 SS

The heating element does not shut off at the end of cycle.  

The specific incident: Ran dishwasher in late evening.  In the morning the counter-top and front of dishwasher were too hot to touch with bare hand.  The unit did not shut off when the door was opened; the breaker needed to be turned off to turn off the heating element.

Ran dishwasher a couple of days later with the same problem.

Notified GE at 800-386-1215 of this problem.
justification: The heating element not shutting off poses a burn risk and potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I writing to report an instance of shattering pyrex.  About 2 years ago I used a pyrex baking dish in an oven for about 30 minutes at 400F.  When I took the dish out of the oven and put it on the grills of my cooktop to cool it immediately shattered upon contact with the cooktop.  The baker broke into about 4 large pieces and a large number of very tiny pieces that flew accross my kitchen.  Some pieces flew as much as 6 - 8 feet.  It was extremely frightening and I consider myself very fortunate that neither I nor another member of my family was injured.
justification: The incident caused a shattering of the baking dish, but no one was injured, making it a level 2 severity.

incident_description: My Kenmore Elite Electric Range Slide-in model (Model No. 790.41023801 & Serial No. NF94819026) had an electrical fire inside of it appproximately 20-25 minutes after it was turned off.  The fire was contained and remained inside the oven b/c we were at home and present when there was a popping noise and we smelled the electrical fire.  We turned the breaker off and the fire ceased.  However, black smoke billowed out of it for about 3 minutes.  There was no damage to anything other than the range.  It is worth noting that this is a lemon replacement from Sears and the first Kenmore Elite Electric Slide-in (a model No. 790.4670) that we had was tripping the breaker and burned the motherboard on the back of the range.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire contained within the range, causing no injury or external damage, but indicating a potential recurring issue with the appliance model.

incident_description: dishwasher caught on fire
justification: The dishwasher catching fire is an incident with potential for harm, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: The two large burners on my Kenmore Smoothtop Range will spontaneously turn to HIGH and will not shut off until the power is turned off to the range at the breaker box. At first it seemed to reset and turn off but this last time even turning it off at the breaker will not allow it to turn off. After researching, I have found that the Kenmore Elite model has a recall but my model/serial number is NOT included in this recall.
justification: The burners turning to HIGH and not shutting off poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: While cooking in our over the range microwave for approximately 15 minutes the fan above the range turned on randomly.  I thought I accidentally touched the button so I tried shutting it off.  The fan would not shut off.  I let it go for about 5 more minutes.  I was done cooking but the fan was still running.  I went to unplug it so as to make the fan shut off and the plug was quite hot to the touch.  About 15 minutes later I plugged the microwave back in and immediately the fan turned on.  I didn't feel safe to keep the microwave plugged in (because of the warmth of the cord) so I left it unplugged.  I called the manufacturer (Goldstar/LG).  The gentleman, [REDACTED] (badge no 1215) started off very nice.  However after he found out that the microwave was manufactured March of 2002 all he had to offer was a technician to come out that I would have to pay for.  He told me that, although it may be a manufacturer's defect, they only warranty for 1 year.  I feel this would have very bad consequences if I were to leave our microwave plugged in.  We can now only have it plugged in when we are using it (as long as it is quick).  We will not use it freely anymore.  [REDACTED] did not care.  He did not care that this could have caused a fire in my house with my family.  He just wanted to charge me for a service call.   This microwave was in the remodeled kitchen of the house we purchased in 2004.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave fan and a hot plug, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
I bought this toaster oven on 6/23/2011. On 7/5/2011 I used the oven to toast 2 waffles. After they finished I removed the waffles. About 60 seconds later the entire glass door in the front of the toaster exploded. Glass was sprayed over the entire kitchen. Luckily no one was hurt but if someone was standing in front of the toaster they would have been sprayed in the face with hot broken glass.

This was a DeLonghi RO2058 Convection/Toaster Oven With Rotisserie.
justification: The incident involved a toaster oven door exploding, spraying glass, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
I have a GE Oven, and after only a couple years, the burner elements all stopped working.  I have had to replace them a couple times, and I realize the wiring underneath is MELTING or BURNING OUT!  Of course that needs to be replaced as well. 

I have by now invested in so many new parts, and I need to REINVEST because the burners I bought a year or so ago are not working again!

This oven is not good to own, I feel it is a danger.

I think it should be recalled.
I have called GE and they do nothing.  They sent a man out but he was not allowed to replace the parts unless I paid for them.  I got a better price if I replaced them myself.  

I also have made a copy of a webpage where other people have experienced the same thing.  The wiring melts !  

Here is the webpage. 
http://www.partselect.com/PS783534-GE-WB17T10006-Surface-Burner-Terminal-Block-Kit.htm?SourceCode=1&ModelNum=JBP24BB4WH

Thank you for your help.
justification: The description indicates repeated incidents of wiring melting or burning out, posing a potential danger, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: The refrigerator light switch on my two-year-old GE Profile counter depth side-by-side refrigerator/ freezer failed.  As a result, the interior lights in the refrigerator comparment remained on when the refrigerator door was closed and the two factory-installed 60 watt bulbs above the deli compartment melted their mountings and came into contact with surrounding plastic. From their new position, the bulbs, still lit, proceeded to melt the plastic light cover, the deli compartment lid and the refrigerator liner without tripping the breaker, the GFI, or a fuse in the unit.  There was no failsafe. The smell of burning plastic was our only warning. Switches fail, but the consequence of a predictable failure should not be an electrical fire.  Refrigerator model # pscs3vgxss, serial #gr400994.  Installed 6/19/2009.   GE part # wr23x10530 failed.
justification: The incident involved equipment failure and potential fire hazard but resulted in no injury or death.

incident_description:
Kenmore electric range 790.96009600 back right burner would not shut off and stayed hot to the touch until we unplugged the appliance. When we plugged it back in the burner came on even though the knob was in the off position. 

The reason I'm reporting it to the CPSC is because Kenmore is recalling a similar (but higher end) model for this very reason so I'm guessing this model should be included in the recall.
justification: The burner staying on poses a burn or fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported. The issue is likely to recur given the recall of a similar model.

incident_description:
I was baking chicken in the oven. When I opened the oven door and turned to get oven mitts to remove the chicken, my left leg brushed against the edge of the door. The door sliced through the outside of my left leg like a razor. The cut is quite deep and bled for a long time. Considered a trip to the emergency room but was able to stop the bleeding. The wound, however, is quite deep. I was unaware that the edge of my oven door was so sharp. I reached down to feel it with my fingers and was shocked to see how sharp and ragged the metal edge is. It is truly a safety hazard. If one of my grandchildren were to fall on the oven door when it is open, it could cause quite a severe injury. 

It is a Kenmore Elite gas range. There is a warning sticker on the inside of the oven door which warns to be cautious of 'tipping' but there is nothing warning of the sharp edges. They are ragged and extremely dangerous. This was considered one of the "top of the line" ranges.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut that bled significantly, indicating an injury, and the sharp edges pose a recurring hazard.

incident_description:
Kenmore Model #106.51582200 refrigerator caught on fire this morning.  I was awoken to the sound of popping and zapping sounds and immediately could see and smell smoke in the kitchen.  I pulled the fridge out unplugged it and called 911.  Fire Dept. determined yes it had caught on fire and have tagged it as an "Unsafe to Use" appliance.  My house had to be aired out with fire dept. fans and I was transported to the hospital for cardiac problems.   
From the looks of it the compressor caught on fire, it burned all the connecting wires and the insulation on the back and bottom of the fridge.  Soot on the wall behind the fridge.   
After doing some research online I have noticed that MANY others are having the same problem with this particular model refrigerator.   I purchased this item brand new from Sears in Sept. 2002.

This product needs to be recalled or taken off the market.  If I had not been home my home would have burned down!!
justification: The incident involved a fire causing injury (cardiac problems requiring hospital transport) and significant property damage, with evidence of a recurring issue for this model.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore refrigerator model number 253.57388601 and the light bulb has burnt out and burnt all the way through the top of the fridge. The light must be staying on all the time to be able to burn all the way through the top of the refridgerator. I removed the light bulb and there is a hole in the top of the refrigerator. There is no cover over the lightbulb on this model. This is a fire hazzard and should be fixed. I called Sears and was told I have to pay to have a technician to look at it and to replace the bulb.
justification: The incident describes a fire hazard due to a burnt-out light bulb causing damage to the refrigerator, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range
Model 790.96022404
Seriel VF60529534

The stove top does not go off even when the knob is is turned to "off". The stove had to be turned off from the circuit breaker. I was cooking soup and turned the knob off and walked away thinking that the stove was off. I came back about an hour later to find my soup burned to a crisp. The knob was "off", but the burner was still on red hot. If I had not come back in time, it could have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Product - Black and Decker 5-cup coffeemaker
Malfunction - Warming Plate overheated when electric current was not cut off by temp. regulating device. Note: Coffeemaker was sitting on a non-combustible surface.
Result - Medium fire, engaged building fire suppression system, resulting in $500,000+ in water/smoke damage.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries or fatalities, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the described malfunction and its consequences.

incident_description: I burned myself on the metal part of the toaster where the toast is inserted.  The burn was small and so I didn't think too much of it.  However last night my 11 year old grandson was by the counter when I was toasting some bread and he did the same thing by touching his arm on this part of toaster and he got a rather bad burn about 3 inches long.  I noticed that the metal part at the top of this toaster is higher than the surrounding plastic that doesn't heat up.  Because the rest of the toaster doesn't get hot it is easy not to realize how hot that top part is and get burned. Also, I noticed that my other similar toaster that is a different brand had same metal area but it is recessed down inside the plastic so the hazard is almost eliminated.  I've never burned myself on this one and I use it a lot.  The Hamilton beach model that we got burned on is the one I use occasionally when I want to toast 4 pieces at once.  I think the co. should have all the metal recessed in on plastic toasters.
justification: The burn was small and so I didn't think too much of it.  However last night my 11 year old grandson was by the counter when I was toasting some bread and he did the same thing by touching his arm on this part of toaster and he got a rather bad burn about 3 inches long.

incident_description:
I HAVE A GE MONOGRAM MODEL ZBD0700N0II.  RAN THE DISHWASHER AND WHEN IT FINISHED THE CYCLE IT BEEPED (SIGNALS IT IS OFF).  I WENT TO BED AND THE NEXT MORNING I COULD SMELL HEAT IN THE KITCHEN.  I OPENED THIS DISHWASHER AND IT SHOWED THE HEAT CYCLE STILL ON, THE PLASTIC COOKWARE IN SIDE HAD MELTED.  THE ONLY WAY I COULD GET THE DISHWASHER TO SHUT OFF WAS TO SHUT OFF THE CIRCUIT BREAKER.  THE DISHWASHER WAS PURCHASED AROUND JULY 2007.  I CHECKED GE'S RECALL LIST AND SOME MONOGRAM MODELS WERE LISTED BUT NOT THIS ONE HOWEVER, THIS IS APPARENTLY SIMILAR TO THE INCIDENT THAT THE RECAL MODELS HAD.  THE FOLLOWING IS FROM THE GE WEBSITE ON RECALLED DISHWASHERS:

GE has determined that water condensation can drip onto the electronic control board, causing a short circuit and resulting in an overheated connector. This poses a fire hazard to consumers. 

I WILL BE CALLING GE CONSUMER AFFAIRS TOMORROW AS SINCE TODAY IS JULY 4TH THERE IS NO ONE THERE TODAY
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, causing overheating and melting of plastic cookware, but no injury or death occurred. The issue is similar to recalled models, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description: On July 2 2011 my Maytag diswasher ,Model # MDB765AWQ AND SER # 23564894EG, heat element exploded.  The dishwasher was in the heated dry cycle with 27 minutes left in cleaning cycle when there was a loud pop followed by steam and smoke exiting from the dishwasher.  The event triggered the breaker immediately disrupting the power to the unit.  Upon opening the unit, there was black and brown metalic particles over all of the dishes.  When I removed the bottom rack the heat element was lying on the bottom of the washer tub in pieces with the coiled heat element exposed.  Maytag has reccommended discontinued use of the product until a service person can look at the damage.  The unit is inoperable.
justification: The dishwasher's heating element exploded, causing damage and making the unit inoperable, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The dishwasher caught fire while it was not being used.  It appears as if the fire was caused by an issue with the control panel on the front door.  It was a Whilrpool diswasher.  The model number was DU929PFGQ2.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but there was no mention of injury or death, indicating an incident with no harm to people.

incident_description: My mother was unloading the dishwasher and bumped her shin on the corner of the door, peeling off a large area of skin. She cleaned and bandaged the wound. Almost three weeks later, the wound became infected, and she went to a walk-in clinic, where she was given prescriptions for two oral antibiotics, and two antibiotic injections. Two or three days later, the infection appeared worse, so she went to the ER. They referred her to a wound clinic, where she was seen the next day. She is receiving ongoing treatment at the wound clinic.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury that required medical treatment, including antibiotics and ongoing wound care, but did not result in death.

incident_description: We own a Whirlpool electric cooktop Model RSC3014LSO and the unit has started to overheat. It has charred the wooden cabinet that supports it and the heat has cracked the surrounding Corian countertop.
justification: The cooktop overheated, causing damage to the cabinet and countertop, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Kitchenaid micorwave Model KHMS155LWH-3 SERIAL NO. TR T 17 11347. Unit comes on by itself and gets very hot possibly hot enough to cause a fire.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself and overheating poses a fire hazard, but there is no mention of actual injury or death.
