incident_description: Microwave keeps turning itself on!  Nearly caused fire by overheating.
justification: The microwave malfunction caused a near-fire incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Kenmore Dishwasher began to give off an electrical burning smell. When I went back into the kitchen it had white smoking coming out of it. I opened the dish washer and water was pooled into the bottom of it (hasn't drained). Front panel no longer lights up or works.
justification: The dishwasher exhibited electrical burning smell and smoke, indicating a malfunction, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I was cooking a pizza in my Kenmore stove when I heard a beeping alarm on the control panel.  When I opened the oven door my food was burning and the broiler was cherry red even though I didn't turn the broiler on.  I had my oven set at 400*, and it had only been on about 25 minutes.  
Model #665.95802000
Serial #RK4635321
I tried to turn it off, but finally had to pull the stove out and pull the plug.  After waiting for close to two hours I tried plugging it back in, and the broiler immediately started heating up again.  It is now unplugged.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning stove that caused burning food and required unplugging, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
While using self clean mode on upper oven I smelled what seemed to be electrical or rubber  burning. I immediately turned off the oven. When it cooled there was nothing inside that appeared affected. I turned the oven on to see if it was working, an error message displayed. On having the repairman out he showed me where a wiring harness above the top oven had burned and started to melt the attached wiring insulation. He told me this was not unusual in self cleaning ovens since the wiring lays directly on the metal roof of the oven with no insulation between the wiring and the oven. 
If I would have left my house during the cleaning period or not noticed the burning smell this could have caused a serious house fire. I am without an oven again since this is not the first time my ovens have had need of repair and I have been quoted a very large amount to repair this by an independant contractor ($700.). The independant service contractor had looked at my unit in the spring. After the contractor was unable to procure the correct parts he suggested I try thermador again.
Contacted thermador on 6/30/2011 they informed me that the product was not on recall and of course I could pay to have their repair people come and repair the unit. .
Thermador did not even offer to look at the problem to see if it was something they should be concerned about. They are willing to make the service call for the $100 and the $120 dollar an hour there after for the repair.
Even if it is repaired the problem will not be sovled by having wiring laying directly on the top of the metal box of the oven
justification: The incident involved a wiring harness burning and melting insulation, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: During normal use of toaster oven, realized that sometimes the timer would not "ding" (but still turn off oven when it reached zero). The bigger problem is that the timer then continues on PAST zero, all the way until it gets to "Stay On", at which point the oven turns itself back on again. Luckily, we happened to be in the kitchen when this started happening, and were able to catch that it was back ON, before it had the chance to cause any significant damage. However, it DID leave a scorch mark on the counter backsplash directly behind it. Sometimes the timer works as it should, sometimes not. The toaster oven itself works fine. We just are never sure if it's going to turn itself back on or not, so we try to remember to unplug it after each use. If left unchecked, this could have been a real disaster!
justification: The incident caused a scorch mark but no injury, and the issue occurs intermittently with potential for significant damage if unchecked.

incident_description: The grill coil of my Thermador oven exploded when set to broil (after about 8 minutes).  It was replaced by a new component installed by a Thermador service representative.  He told me I was lucky I did not have the door to the oven open at the time.  I have attempted to contact Thermador- including transmission of the picture attached.  Thermador has not responded.  If the coil had any faulty materials, owner of the ovens need to know.
justification: The grill coil exploded but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the incident happened but is not common.

incident_description: The consumer says his wife was using oven and set at 400 degrees.  When she went to take contents out, the handle flew open and the outside glass exploded while the inside glass stayed intact.  The outside glass shattered all over the kitchen, dining and living room.  The consumer says that the unit was only on for about 30-35 minutes.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who will send out a technician.  The product is under warranty.
justification: The incident involved glass shattering but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are uncommon but not rare, warranting a likelihood of 3.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that the left front burner on his Kenmore Elite electric range turns on by itself. The product is a oven/ range combo unit. The range also has a smooth top surface. The issue is isolated to the range and the oven works fine. The oven was on for roughly two hours before the left front burner turned on by itself. The consumer had the product modified 6 months ago as he had the front right burner would not turn off in a similar incident. The consumer called the retailer about the issue today and was told that they could examine the range at a charge of $125 at the consumer's expense. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer about this product. The consumer stated that similar models from 2006 have had the exact same issue and were recalled. The product is not damaged and does not show signs of discoloration or charring. The consumer was not injured by the product and shows no signs of structural damage to his home. However, the consumer felt it was imperative to report this issue to the CPSC.
justification: The product turned on by itself, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description: Glass shattered on the oven door I opened the door.
justification: Glass shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
We own a Kenmore Elite Trio Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Model 795.7754*
We have owned it just short of three years.  Over the weekend we opened the upper french-style doors and found both refrigerator lights out and smelled an odor of hot electrical burning.  We removed the light bulb cover and attempted to remove the bulbs.  They were too hot to touch.  After they cooled down, we removed the bulbs and observed the compartment that houses the light bulbs.  It is beginning to discolor.  Furthermore the glass bulbs were darkening and discoloring - but the filaments were still in tact.  After cooling, we placed the bulbs back in the sockets to see if they would once again illuminate.  They did but after several minutes, they became very hot again and again we smelled the odor of electrical burning.  We were able to determine that at least one of the two switches used to determine if the refrigerator doors are open or shut has gone bad - causing the scenario where the refrigerator senses that the door is open and thus keeps the light bulbs illuminated.  We have since removed the bulbs to open the circuit and prevent any fire hazard to our home.  We did an online search and found many other consumers who have experienced this problem.  Today we contacted Sears service center and were told that they knew nothing about the defect in their product.  Their only two solutions were to either purchase a one-year service agreement/warranty for a technician to make a service call and repair the refrigerator or schedule a service appointment without the agreement and pay for time and material.  Upon expressing our concern that this was a defect in their product and that it posed a fire hazard to our home and our family, we were simply told that they could do nothing about it.  The customer service representative couldn't understand why we didn't want to purchase a service agreement to remedy their defective product.  We are disappointed in Sears approach to resolving this issue and want to make others aware of the potential fire hazard they have in their homes.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard but no injury, making it a level 2 severity. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as it is a known issue with the product.

incident_description: Back in 2004, my husband and I were about to bake some chicken.  Our Anchor brand 9x13 glass baking dish was sitting on top of the stove (at the time, I had NO idea that my husband had just recently turned the burner off...this was an old coil burner stove and the coil was black...but apparently still somewhat hot).  The exact moment that I put a cold chicken breast into the pan, the pan sounded like it exploded.  Glass shattered into small pieces and went flying everywhere. Luckily I turned my head around quickly, or I would have had glass all over my face!
justification: The incident involved a glass baking dish shattering, which could have caused injury but luckily did not.

incident_description:
Coffee Maker from Walmart Model# 47374 SN = D1690GN Hamilton Beach Brew Station returned to Walmart & replaced 3 times since original purchase around November 26, 2010.

Leaks hot coffee when sitting falling on counter where wires and plug is located.  DOM2009

They clean regularly as instructed.

Most recently replaced coffee maker is about 6 months old but caller is not pleased to find that it may have been manufactured in 2009.

Walmart Rep most recently spoken with stated that she was evening manager, could be reached at [REDACTED] advised caller that he should not have spoken with the manufacturer.

Caller is on disability, manufacturer wants him to pay for shipping this time but Walmart is willing to replace again.

Caller does not want to replace again, he is stating that replacement does not remove the potential for electrocution should the leaking coffee hit the plug or wiring incorrectly.
justification: The coffee maker leaks hot coffee near electrical components, posing a potential electrocution risk, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Nuby brand sold by Stop & Shop Baby CUP
The baby dropped the cup from his highchair and the handle penetrated the cup causing a piece of plastic to enter the water. The plastic was not immediately discovered until the baby tried drinking and water came out of the hole and onto his hand.  If I was not there watching the baby could have swallowed the small piece of plastic that entered the cup.
justification: The baby could have swallowed a small piece of plastic, but no injury occurred as the incident was noticed in time.

incident_description:
At about 7:20 AM the woman that was house/dog sitting for us smelled smoke. Went down stairs to discover that the microwave was on and that the food that was placed in there for storage was on fire.

The microwave started on it's own. 

Kitchenaid KHMS 155LSS purchased on November 12, 2005
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a malfunctioning microwave, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Stove burner was set on 'low' setting to simmer a pot. Burner control system failed causing much power to go to burner. Burner and stove top became very hot. Heat intensity was enough to damage a heavy aluminum pot and discolor paint on the stove control unit.

Power was cut to the stove at the circuit breaker. Stove cooled.

After stove cooled to room temperature, it was noted that the 'hot top' indicator light stayed on and would not turn off.

No fire or injuries were caused by this incident. Burner has not been used since this incident.

Stove was examined for alphanumeric model and serial number information. None was readily visible.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries or fire, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such failures are not common but possible.

incident_description: I used a new Pyrex mixing bowl to cook polenta in the microwave (corn meal, room temp water, salt).  The bowl exploded into tiny shards all over my microwave, just moments before I was going to open the door to check on it.  I cut myself several times cleaning up the shards and very sharp glass from all over the microwave.  If it'd opened the door a moment sooner, it would have exploded all over me.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts from cleaning up glass shards, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: My Cuisinart model DCC-1100 automatic coffee maker, serial numer 00223, started smoking about an hour after use. I noticed a burnt plastic smell and noticed the smoke rolling out of the unit. It was very hot when I removed it from the house. Fortunately, we noticed the problem before anything else was damaged.
justification: The coffee maker started smoking and emitted a burnt plastic smell, but no injury or damage occurred beyond the unit itself.

incident_description:
During the brewing process our Cuisinart DC 1200 (Serial number 98324 h), purchased from Amazon in late November or early December of 2009 began to billow smoke and give off a sharp plastic smell. 
We unplugged it immediately.

The smoke was considerable and it is clear from the odor that plastic parts were hot enough to melt inside. Fortunately my husband was in the kitchen when the meltdown occurred and could unplug it before it damaged the countertop or started a fire. We have never had a problem like this with an appliance.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting plastic but was promptly addressed without injury or fire, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description:
Saturday June 18th at [REDACTED]

Home caught fire due to Kenmore dishwasher manufactured in 1998.  It was one the original Kenmore appliances they came with our home when we had it built by Suburban Homes.  Houston Fire dept determined it was the timer/control panel had a short which caught fire and damaged my entire home.
justification: The incident involved a home fire caused by a dishwasher, resulting in property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Stove burner will come on by itself full high, and will not turn off unless you turn off breaker
justification: The stove burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard and potential injury risk, but no injury is mentioned.

incident_description: The interior light on Model 795.77562600 Kenmore Elite (LG) fails to go off when the door closes.  The light creates so much heat it melts the interior plastic light housing.  If left for an extended period of time it could cause a fire.  Numerous complaints can be found on the internet describing the same issue noted above.
justification: The incident involves a potential fire hazard due to a malfunctioning light, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My Slow Cooker feet broke, spilling the food and burning my hand. 6-quart unit has model number 106851, the series code is E and does not fall into the recall that is out right now.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, and similar incidents are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description: I was washing the item after having used it for the first time, when my hand brushed along the top edge it was cut.  It wasn't deep so I continued to wash the item when I was cut a second time, even deeper.  Both cuts were shallow but deep enough to bleed.  The item is not intended to cut anything and the top edge should not be so sharp as to easily cut through my skin with little to no pressure.
justification: The incident resulted in shallow cuts that bled, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Terrible chemical smell coming from new Frigidaire electric wall oven (model number FEB24S2ABE) after it heats up.  More noticeable on HI BROIL setting or on BAKE at high temperatures.  I have now had this issue on two different units (see below).

The chemical smell is very difficult to describe in comparison to other known odors.  It is NOT a burning plastic smell.  It is NOT the smell of the manufacturing oils that burn off in the first few minutes of operating a new oven. 

The odor burns the lungs and eyes.  It requires airing out the entire house.  I am very concerned that the chemicals may be dangerous.

Frigidiare honored the warranty and replaced the original unit manufactured in November 2010 with another unit manufactured in December 2010, presumably at the same plant.  The new oven has the same odor issue as the first model,  suggesting this issue is probably impacting other consumers.

The two appliance repair technicians servicing the unit indicated that they have never encountered a similar odor in all of their years working on ovens.  They needed to leave the house after the odor made them feel ill.

During the ordeal with the two ovens, Frigidaire customer service required that I try a number of things including:
- Cleaning the entire inside of the oven with diswashing soap (twice).
- Operating the oven at high temperatures (multiple times totalling more than 10 hours).  The odor does not have a self cleaning feature, so it was run on HI broil or at 450 - 500 degrees.
- Leaving ammonia in a bowl overnight to "soak up" any odors.
- Having a technician dismantle the unit to look for mice droppings, insects or burnt wires (none found).

Despite all of the obvious signs that there is something wrong with the manufacturing of these units, and that the smell isn't going to just "go away", the appliance repairmen were asked by Frigidaire's technician hotline to AGAIN run the oven at high temperatures for 3 more hours, releasing more of this unknown chemical into my home.

Needless to say, it didn't work.  Frigidiare has not admitted to any known issues from consumers with new ovens.  It's hard to believe that this is true given that I've now been given two defective ovens.  

I would like some answers as to what chemical is responsible for the odor, and whether it is a health hazard to humans and/or pets.
justification: The chemical smell causes burning in the lungs and eyes, and made technicians feel ill, indicating injury. The issue occurred in two units, suggesting it's not isolated but still uncommon.

incident_description: On Sathurday we were cooking pizza in a Frigidaire FGF 328 oven. 20 minutes after we turned off the oven we sensed a awful burning smell wich caused us to start coughing and irritated our eyes and nose. Ten minutes later we sensed it was coming from the oven and saw smoke coming out from under the burner plates. It grew steadily larger and then we decided to open the top of the stove wich had the burners and saw that the insulation was burning. We opened all the windows and doors to ventilate our apartment. We poured water on the insulation to stop it from catching fire, but in 15 minutes it started to burn again. I have two children, one 2 year old and one 11 year old witch were also present at the incident. The horrible smell still lingers and we cannot use the stove/oven.
justification: The incident caused coughing and irritation to eyes and nose, indicating minor injuries, and posed a significant fire hazard.

incident_description: Hello, I have the Warring Belgium Waffle maker wwm200ssa, which has worked for me well for the last few years. Recently the top element stopped working and overheated the machine.  Had I not been with the appliance, it may have caused a fire. As it is, the screws got so hot they melted away from the plastic parts.  The reason the top element stopped working was because the positive wire came loose from the connector and was arcing. Instead of the appliance automatically shutting down, all the power was routed directly to the bottom element, giving it twice the power it was supposed to have.  While I understand this is out of warranty, it represents a significant product safety issue and design flaw. I am not seeking remuneration/replacement, the product is otherwise good quality. I just want to make sure this issue is brought up. thanks for looking out for us.
justification: The incident involved overheating and potential fire hazard due to a design flaw, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We bought a new GE Profile QuietPower 7 Dishwasher Model # PDW 9980N00SS approx. three (3)  years ago that recently started to melt all hard plastic dishware and is getting extremely hot to the point that it is causing the very thick granite that it is under to not be touchable. We only use the "Heated Dry" cycle and have never used the "Added Heat" cycle. Also we only use dry tablet detergent and have never used liquid detergent in this new model, so I think GE has a much bigger dishwasher problem than they are letting on, by trying to blame it on liquid detergent. Also this is a new model that has not been on any prior list of overheating problems.
justification: The dishwasher is overheating and melting plastic dishware, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: GE Profile dishwasher had a recall to correct fires that started in units like mine.  My unit was part of the recall and was fixed.  My control circuit caught fire and melted the wireharness before the thermal detector turned the power off.  The recall was only to install the thermal overload device, not to replace the underlying cause of the fires.  The thermal protection device did its job but only after the fire started.  The damage involves the control panel, wireharness, the thermal protection device, and the control board (not sure if the smoke caused any damage.)
justification: The incident involved a fire that caused damage to the dishwasher components but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
GE Profile Radiant Downdraft glass cooktop: 
Model Number J P989B0D2BB
Serial Number MD701159C
Front right burner came on, on HIGH, by itself at random times, twice, until we disconnected it.
justification: The burner turning on by itself poses a fire hazard but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On March 5, 2011, I was trying to chop a few cubes of ice in the processor (something which I did easily on my older one made by another company.)  I closed the lid, turned on the processor, and the blade got out of place: ice got underneath the blade.  I removed the lid with the intent of pushing the blade out of place.  Apparently, my other hand was on the ÃÂLowÃÂ or ÃÂHighÃÂ button, because the machine started to run.  I emphasize the lid was completely off, and, as I knew it was a common safety feature that such a processor does not run until the lid is locked, I was caught completely by surprise when it began operating.  I jerked my hand out as soon as possible. My right index finger was bleeding profusely.  When I emptied the ice, I found a piece of my finger inside the bowl.   This was a sheer slice, much like a piece of deli meat.   It included a piece of tissue and a piece of the nail as well.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury with a piece of the finger being sliced off, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is moderate as such incidents are not common but possible with improper use.

incident_description: I am writing to report a problem with exploding Pyrex. When removing a roast that I was cooking in a Pyrex dish, the pyrex exploded right in my hands.  Glass flew in all directions throughout my kitchen hitting myself, my wife, and our 3-year-old daughter.  This is the 2nd time this occurred.  The first time was back in 1988-89. At that time, I assumed it was a fluke.  This time, I'm convinced that this is a very dangerous product.  Luckily, we only received small cuts and ruined expensive dinners.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts to multiple family members, indicating an injury severity level. The recurrence of the issue suggests a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
On the date listed below, the Kenmore Dishwasher was turned on in the pots and pans cycle. About 15 minutes into the wash I returned to the kitchen and found the dishwasher billowing out a large amount of smoke. I tried to turn the unit off first by opening the door but the unit kept running. I then tried to turn it off with the off button, this also would not turn the unit off. I then shut the circuit breaker off to kill the power to the unit. Once the power was eliminated the smoke dissipated. 

If I had left my house or been gone for a period of time, the dishwasher and the house would have caught on fire.

We looked up the model number 665.17379300 and serial number FP3901937 for recalls. We only found that the same model number was listed but a different serial number sequence 

I then contacted Sears and informed them of the problem. They gave me a case number and sent a Sears Technician to inspect the unit. He stated, the control panel was burnt & would need to be replaced. We chose instead to purchase a new dishwasher, rather than take a chance on this happening again.

Being an Aircraft Technician I took the unit apart and found the circuit card burnt through as well as the wiring harness melted and the plastic case melting and showing signs of preliminary ignition. Assembly Whirlpool p/n 8539379 REL. circuit card number R4MOWYMA. I have pictures and the circuit card assembly in hand.
justification: The dishwasher emitted smoke and showed signs of potential fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On evening of June 9, 2011 the outer glass  of my Sears Kenmore oven door exploded violently.  At the time, the oven was off and the door was partially open.  Shattered glass particles were scattered up to 20  feet, and covered the entire kitchen floor.  No one was in the direct line of the explosive force, but this could have been a potentially very dangerous incident if there had been a child present, or of someone had been facing the oven door at the time.  

The appliance was a Kenmore Wall oven Model 790.47849403  Serial number NF54807281
The design of the tempered glass front and handle is flawed and potentially dangerous. I can explain why if you don't already know.  Short of a recall and redesign, there should at least be a WARNING included in the owners' documentation to minimize the possibility of a dangerous accident.
justification: The oven door exploded violently, but no one was injured. The potential for injury was high if someone had been nearby.

incident_description: I have a sears kenmore Elite  slide in gas oven, purchased in 2009.  I preheated the oven to 350 and put a cookie sheet inside.  Within minutes the entire glass front door popped and shattered.  There was enough of an explosion to throw pieces of glass 6 feet away! Some were thrown hard enough to bounce off the cabinets and fly into the next room. This is a dangerous product.  I checked reviews online and found this is a common problem with sears!  Why is this not a recalled product?
justification: The incident involved the oven door shattering violently, but no injury was reported. Online reviews indicate this is a common problem, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Series no. WY1252537,   Model no. KP26M1XBS, THE Kitchenaid PROFESSIONAL 60 SERIES STAND MIXER.

We used it to make a 1lbs dough at the speed of 4 for about 10 minutes, and it fell off the kitchen counter. It was very dangerous especially for kids. From a engineer perspective, I think the manufacturer should add a part to make this machine mechanically fastened.
justification: The mixer fell off the counter, which was dangerous, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have a Maytag dishwasher that isn't on the recall list, but the unit burned out and will no longer work.  I can't see any burn marks but smelled wiring burning then it stopped working in mid cycle. 
This is a Maytag E71195 Type 777-0 Model MDBH945AWB3 serial # NY3512148. I bought this at Famous Tate and they will not take it back even though it's been purchased within a year. They said Maytag has law suits against them and we need to take it up with them. I want my unit replaced or my money refunded.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned (burned out wiring) but caused no injury or visible damage, making it an incident without harm.

incident_description:
We purchased a GE coffee pot 12 cup model 169209 from walmart about 9 months ago.  yesterday it started smoking from the rear in billows.  It would have burnt down the house if we were not home.  They are still selling them at Walmart cuz we went a bought a different one today.
I'm concerned about house fires with this pot.
justification: The coffee pot started smoking, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says she put the electric oven on a 2 hour self cleaning, and she heard a pop towards the end of the cleaning.  She turned it off and had to wait for the oven to cool and unlock itself.  She says the glass from the inside of the door it busted and cracked.  The consumer tried to contact the manufacturer and they told her she is no longer under warranty.
justification: The incident involved a cracked oven door glass but no injury or further damage, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are possible but not highly frequent, warranting a likelihood of 3.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that his Kenmore electric range is dangerous. The unit is a self standing oven stove combo. He stated in some the element light on the stove wont turn off. The range is a smoothe top range. In one incident the oven turned itself on or in other cases it wont turn off after an hour of use. Consumer pointed out that the oven also malfunctions and cooks at a temperature different from the one desired. He noticed that his oven is similar to models that were recalled by frigidaire and Kenmore elite for a heating element issue dating back to November of 2009.He has yet to call the retailer or manufacturer.The products is not damaged or charred on the inside of the stove. However, he felt it was imperative to report this to the CPSC.
justification: The malfunctioning stove poses a clear hazard (e.g., overheating, unintended operation), but no injury or damage has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she discovered that the bulb inside the refrigerator was overheating, it melted the plastic housing on the bulb and temperature of the unit became extremely hot.
Consumer stated that she had to remove ther bulb in order for the unit to be functional.

Around 4/20/11 she contacted the manufacturer and was informed that a thermostat replacement would be done, however, the problem is not the thermostat because she unplugged the bulb and the refrigerator works.  The manufacturer has not responded in sending out anyone for service.

Consumer feels that this bulb within the refrigerator poses a fire hazard and needs to be investigated.
justification: The bulb overheating and melting plastic housing indicates a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Around January 2011 caller noticed that the temperature of left front burner of her electric range was difficult to control.
As time went on she began realizing that whenever she used this burner with temperature turned on high to begin cooking that when she turned the temperature down it didn't actually turn down but stayed on high.
Whenever she would turn the same left front burner off it would remain on high until she turned it back & forth from high to low and then to off but even that would not always turn it off.
She does not use this left front burner at all anymore due to fear of fire.
She would like her electric range repaired at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning burner with potential fire risk but no actual injury or fire reported.

incident_description: I was using my Breadman Ultimate Plus breadmaking machine, and it rocked itself off the counter and came crashing down to the floor while in its first kneading cycle.
justification: The breadmaker fell but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: My husband made coffee this morning as usual.  When he returned to get a cup he found the coffee to be boiling in the carafe and the unit to be smoking. It is a Cuisinart 12 cup DCC-1100 series.  I did a quick search of this on the internet and found this is happening to alot of people.  Had we used the feature to program auto brew we may not have discovered this until it burst into flames and caught our house on fire.  This is a SERIOUS safety hazard and it appears that until someone dies nothing is going to be done.  It is clear from all of the reports that the maufacturer is aware of this.  I also understand that this has been reported to this agency many times.  I add my complaint to the stack in hopes that someone will take this seriously
justification: The incident describes a malfunction causing boiling and smoking, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. Reports indicate this is a recurring issue.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the dishwasher was in use he smelled smoke, he was able to turn it off and noticed that the electrical wiring had melted and there was black soot inside the unit.
The unit is now inoperable.

4/27/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that the unit would electrical components would be replaced but the labour would be a cost to him.  Consumer is experiencing similar problems of Release #09-100.

Consumer is concerned that this unit is fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melted wiring but no injury or death, and the unit is now inoperable.

incident_description:
This evening our kitchen filled with smoke, we called the fire department. The fireman determined that
our 7 year old Whirpool Gold side by side refrigerator caught fire. The condenser overheated and the
surrounding wiring and plastic ignited. The Whirpool side by side model number is GS5SHGXLS01. After
the incident, I searched on-line and saw that our refrigerator fire was not the first. There were at least
34 outer incidents reported and there was even severals youtube videos showing a fire in this model.

Please protect the public and have this refrigerator recalled and require the manufacturer to replace the
faulty product. Also, make sure that the manufacturer does not sell dangerous products and once they
become aware of a problem they take immediate action to resolve the problem and protect the public
health.

Please let me know what the Consumer Product Safety Commission is doing or will do about this
dangerous Whirpool product.
justification: The incident involved a refrigerator fire with no reported injuries, and there are multiple similar incidents reported, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Consumer stated that a dishwasher she owned prior had caught fire in her home. She stated that at the time of the incident her husband and her son were in the home. They initially smelled a strong odor in the air of smoke and plastic which they ignored. When the smell persisted they discovered that their dishwasher had caught fire. The product was on for about 30 minutes on medium before the incident occurred. The consumer was not able to contact the manufacturer or the retailer at the time due to other proceedings at the time but did mention that this issue is eerily similar to the incidents occurring with dishwashers included in release 10-255. The consumer said the product was burned and badly melted. The consumer also mentioned that the damage did not spread to the structure of her home. The consumer's husband put out the fire using water. The consumer opted not to call the fire department and luckily was not harmed.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing damage to the product but no injuries or structural damage to the home.

incident_description:
New Jenn-Air wall oven installed in new construction home February 2011. Turned on oven in March 2011 to test.  I noticed an odor when the oven was on, that smelled like plastic burning.  I had read in the instruction manual that came with the oven, that the oven may have an odor for the first few times of use. The oven was not turned on again until June 14, 2011.  While baking, after preheating, I noticed a smell coming from the oven that smelled like plastic burning.  When I opened the oven door, a large cloud of smoke came out the oven door.  The oven was on for only 17 minutes at 350 degrees.  In the rear of the oven I noticed a yellow substance dripping down onto the oven liner floor.  Once the oven cooled, I touched the yellow substance and found it was as hard as stone.  The burning of this substance has caused a sticky film on the oven door that occurred when I opened the oven door and the smoke came out. This could be dangerous also as it could very well be residue from the yellow sticky substance and could be flammable.

Jenn-Air has not offered any resolution to this problem, except for the Jenn-Air Service Tech to clean it up.  It cannot be cleaned as it is baked on the oven liner and has charred the porcelin oven interior.  This substance has caused damage to the oven and is very toxic to smell.  I am afraid if I use the oven again, this would cause a fire.  The smell of the substance is overwhelming, and my smoke alarm went off, I had to open up my house to let the smoke out.

I feel this is a potentially dangerous situation and this product is unsafe.  I did find another consumer, on-line at www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/jenn-air_wall_ovens.html that had the same problem, with no resolution from Jenn-Air.
justification: The incident involves a potentially dangerous situation with smoke and toxic odors, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
She noticed that the light bulb went out and had melted through its plastic housing and through the insulation of the top of the refrigerator. She removed the bulb from the refrigerator and now the wiring is exposed. She fears that it could potentially statr a fire so she refuses to put the bulb back inside of the refrigerator. 

She contacted the firm the week of May 8,2011 and the retailer offered a $65.00 credit towards a repair and she will contact third party repair company to see what the fees are involved and have it repaired.  Consumer stated that Frigidaire would not repay her for the service call required to prove the defect. They would give her a 40% discount to purchase another freezer/refrigerator or 40% on the origibal purchase price from years ago. Consumer purchased all her appliances to replace those ruined during Hurricane Katrina.
justification: The incident involved a melted light bulb and exposed wiring, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while the oven was in use for broiling the oven door was open she heard a rattling noise, she noticed that the noise was coming from the vent, and then their was a flash of flame that started blazing and then the unit powered off but the fire was still blazing, her spouse switched off the circuit breaker for the flames to dissolve.

3/18/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that the unit was not recalled or under warranty but as a 'goodwill ' gesture they would sent out a service representative which would be a charge to her.

Consumer believes that this oven is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a flash of flame and a fire, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that for the past 2 weeks he has been experiencing problems with his dishwasher whenever it started the wash mode, then it would stop and make a buzzing sound, which is followed by a odor of burnt wires.  He then turns it off with the concern that it could start a fire. 

Consumer stated his most recent incident occurred on 5/30/11.  He stated that he feels that he is experiencing problems of release# 05-123 -An electrical defect within the dishwashers' wash motor wiring poses a risk of the motor overheating and possibly catching fire.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard  and should be investigated.
justification: The dishwasher exhibits signs of electrical malfunction (buzzing sound, burnt wire odor) but no fire or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: The consumer says she ran a regular wash cycle.  She left her house and came back 6 hours later.  When she came back the heating element never turned off.  Consumer says steam was coming from unit.   She unplugged unit.  She plugged it back on .  she hit the drain button, and the heating element came on and was burning hot again and would not turn off without unplugging the unit.   Consumer says she contacted manufacturer, who sent someone out.  Technician ran diagnostic with rep from manufacturer on the phone, who concluded there was nothing wrong with the unit.
justification: The heating element malfunctioned, posing a burn risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have the Kenmore Elite Trio Fridge Model # 795.77559600 and smelled something burning.  I opened the refridgerator to find that the entire lighting unit on the top was charred and had melted from the top of the fridge itself.  The entire inside was so hot and the bulbs were too hot to touch even with oven mitts.  This could have started a serious fire had we not been home or smelled the burning.  This is a problem that needs to be repaired before someone is seriously hurt or even killed.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and charred lighting unit, posing a fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Oven set to bake at 425 as I have done many times. This time, burritos were set on fire because only top element came on and stayed on. Bake is supposed to turn on only bottom element. Unplugged reset clock and bake still only turns on top element which now will not turn off until I unplug unit. Seems like a dangerous fire hazard.
justification: The oven malfunction caused a fire hazard but no injury occurred, indicating an incident with no injury. The issue is likely to recur given the described behavior.

incident_description:
I have a Kitchen Aid 14-Cup Coffee Maker (model# KCM222CU) that I started using on 2/3/11. This morning (6/22/11), my husband set the timer to turn on at 5:30 AM, and then I went to get coffee from the maker at 7:45 AM.  I noticed that the coffee was abnormally hot, and then noticed that the maker had an error message on the screen.  Following the manufacturer's instructions, I turned off the machine, and the error message disappeared.  About an hour later I heard the coffee maker make a noise, and realized that although the unit was off the heating element under the carafe was still heating (much, much hotter than normal). I unplugged the unit several times, but each time I would plug it back in it would immediately heat up again (the unit was turned off the entire time).  Apparently the unit had gotten so hot that it had burned the carafe a bit around the metal ring on the glass portion. Sears never disclosed at the time of purchase that this product had been recalled.  Water leaked from the motor area.  Due to the product malfunctioning we decided to replace this product as we went to remove we discovered it had been leaking from the motor area.

My family has sustained great financial and physical damage to our home due to the neglect of Sears & Whirlpool by not disclosing a product recall when purchasing this product at their retail store. Our Kitchen cabinets and whole floor has to be replaced due to the recall of this product and as well the mold due to the leaking of this product. We are currently in the process dealing with homeowners insurance and several contractors to determine the told physical damage and cosmetic to the house which could include structural damage. If Sears had not sold us this recalled dishwasher we would not be in this situation with damage to our home and the health risks associated with water and mold damage.

I smelled burning plastic smoke and came downstairs to find smoke emanating from behind the electronic controls on the top of the washer door. My wife turned off the circuit breaker and I removed the dishwasher front panel and plastic cover to find the circuit board charred and the wiring scorched along with melting of the plastic that covered the circuit board. I feel extremely fortunate that this occurred in the evening before my family went to sleep, otherwise the results could have been catastrophic if a fire started at night while everyone was asleep. I was surprised that the smoke from the burned circuit board and melted plastic cover continued for several minutes after we turned off the power at the breaker.  I still have a headache from breathing the fumes more than an hour ago.  I have spent the last hour looking online to see if my dishwasher model has been recalled.  I could not find any recall info, but I found many reports from other consumers who have experienced the same problem. It seems that there is a severe safety hazard with these Frigidaire dishwashers and a recall seems appropriate to me if there have been multiple reports of actual damage.

I followed all the directions on the labeling for the non stick cookware use and care before using.  When I used it last night to stir fry pork and vegetables, per my usual recipe, it immediately started smoking very heavily and gave off a chemical smell.  It turned out that the inside of the pan was burned and lost some coating.  However, the worst was that the pan had melted on my induction stove and lost some of the coating on the bottom of the pan.  It was scary!  My induction stove-top was in pristine condition before using this pan.  It took over 45 minutes to get the coating removed from the induction stove.  This item should be immediately removed from the stores and Xylan non stick coating banned.

The machine has been removed from my house and is in storage. It can be used for investigation if necessary. If I had not been home, then the machine certainly would have caught the house on fire. Below is the full details of the letter that I sent to GE.

GE Company
Appliance Park
Building 6, Room 129
Louisville, KY 40225 


May 7, 2011

Dear Sirs:


I have a GE Spacemaker Model Number EMO3000CBB02 over range microwave that caught on fire. The Microwave caught on fire without being used. Fortunately, I was home at the time and was able to switch the dedicated fuse and unplug the unit before my house caught on fire.

I would hate to see people lose their life, pets, or homes to such a tragic malfunction.

Please let me know where this unit can be sent for investigation, or if GE will pick up this unit at my home.  Or if GE would rather have me contact the US Consumer Product Safety Commission, then I can follow through with them if I do not hear from GE by the May 31, 2011.

Sincerely,

incident_description:
This electric oven/range was purchased new and professionally installed by Sears in 2008, and had been operating normally prior to the incident.  On May 25, 2011, the large rear burner on the electric range was on 'high', boiling a 2-quart pot (copper-clad stainless) of salted water (for pasta).  No other elements were being used at the time of the incident.  Suddenly, a bright white light flashed, a loud buzzing noise began, and sparks began to fly out from under the pot.  The drip pan melted and eventually (approximately 30 seconds later) the element exploded, sending a piece of element approximately 1-1/2" long shooting out, as well as molten metal (presumably from the drip pan) which sprayed out and landed on the countertop approximately 16" from the burner.  The molten metal was so hot that it burned holes into the countertop (formica) where it landed.  I was unable to turn off the dial for the burner as it was directly above the sparking element.  I grabbed a fire extinguisher and prepared to put out the fire.  By the time I got the fire extinguisher, the noise and molten metal spray had stopped.  The fire/sound/light ceased when a piece of the previously-mentioned element broke free.  Once I saw that there was no fire, I ran outside and cut the power to the stove (which is on a dedicated circuit breaker).

If I had been touching the pot when the short occurred, I would have been electrocuted.  If I had been standing over the stove when the short occurred, I would have been burned by the metal spray.  In other words, this incident had the potential to cause severe injury or death.

I called Sears on May 26, 2011 to have a technician inspect the stove.  They sent out a repair person on June 3, 2011.  He wrote up the ticket as "element failed", and ordered a new element, drip pan, and switch.  The technician said he did not know the cause of the failure, and said sometimes elements "just do that".  He charged me $253.83 for the parts and labor, and said that Sears was not responsible for the damage/failure because the product was only under warranty for one year from the purchase date.  

By replacing burned/molten parts, the technician is addressing the symptoms of the problem, but not the CAUSE.  I am afraid to operate the appliance since the cause of the short was not identified.  I am concerned that other consumers may have similar problems with this appliance.  

I went on line to speak to a "Blue Crew" representative about this issue on June 3, 2011.  I corresponded (via Instant Messenger) with a representative who said his name was [REDACTED].  I asked him if other consumers had experienced a similar product failure.  He told me, "we do not keep record of the problems with the appliances".  I saved a transcript of our IM chat which I have not attached, but can supply later if you need it.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction with potential for severe injury or death, but no actual injuries occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as such severe malfunctions are not common.

When she was finished with her shower, and opened the bathroom door, she smelled a strong odor of something burning.  She went downstairs, and noticed that the dishwasher's display was blank, there was a black smoke mark on the front edge of our countertop directly above the dishwasher's door, and the front top of the dishwasher's door (i.e. the console assembly cover) was burnt.  Upon further inspection, she noticed that the plastic faceplate was distorted, and the gasket between the plastic faceplate and the stainless steel dishwasher door was burnt and melted.  When I got home that evening, I removed the front cover of the dishwasher's door to see what was wrong.  I discovered that the circuit board behind the console assembly cover was charred, there were several burnt components, a fair amount of melted plastic, and even some of the wiring harnesses were burnt.  There was also black soot deposited on the inside of the plastic cover, and part of the cover itself was burnt.

My wife did a brief search on the internet, and discovered a lot of postings about a possible design defect with this particular model of KitchenAid dishwasher causing similar problems.  As an electrical engineer and circuit designer myself, given the fairly large number of reported problems, I do believe that there is likely some latent design or component defect that's causing these issues.  When I opened the cover, there was no trace of any water leaking in; although it's possible that water may have initiated this problem and the heat from the ensuing burning components & plastic caused it to evaporate.  The damage to the dishwasher was fairly extensive, so much so that we will have to replace it.

The reason I'm submitting this report is that I believe that this particular product could well be dangerous.  We were lucky that my wife was at home at the time and the burning was contained to just the dishwasher itself.  However, we often turn the dishwasher on late at night before going to bed.  Given the extent of the damage inside the dishwasher and the size of the burn mark on our kitchen counter, I could imagine similar instances of dishwasher failures causing a fire, particularly if there happened to be anything flamable on the countertop directly above the middle of the dishwasher door.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

#R11 014805, was delivered & installed on 4/1. We first lit the oven on 412 and the sides & top became "extremely"

incident_description:

The bulbs became extremely hot and melted the entire light fixture and top of the fridge itself.  All the food on the top shelf was extremely hot.  In order to remove the bulbs, an oven mitt was required.  I am certain that this would have caused a house fire if not discovered.  

This is an intermittent problem.  I plugged the light assembly back in and shut the doors and the bulbs did once again turn off.

Looking online after this occurred I researched this issue online.  This is a common problem with the model fridge.  Individuals online have also indicated this is an intermittent problem.

incident_description:
I had purchased a Hamilton Beach Food Processor (10 cup, DPCI: 072-04-0943) from Target, because it claims that it can be used to grate cheese.  

The food processor has a large blade at the top of the processor that spins very rapidly, and above that there's a locking plastic lid that contains a feeding tube.  When you put food down the tube, it's supposed to be processed by the blade.  The food processor will not start unless the lid is locked into place.  There's maybe a half-inch or so gap between the blade and the lid.

When I used it to grate cheese, I put the large disk on the motor and locked the lid into place.  I started the food processor and proceeded to put a block of cheese into the tube.  After about two spins of the blade (I did get a tiny amount of grated cheese, so it wasn't immediately), the cheese I had put into the tube was sucked down extremely quickly between the blade and the lid, in that 1/2 inch gap.  The block of cheese was about 2 or 3 inches wide, which caused the lid's locking mechanism to crack and the lid to fly off, hitting me.  The cheese flew across the room.  The most alarming thing is that the blade did not stop spinning after the lid was ripped off.  

I was not injured at all during this, just extremely shocked.  However, with the sharp, metal blade spinning exposed, it's entirely possible that someone using this machine could be injured.  I almost caught one of my fingers on the spinning blade.  Grating cheese is an approved use of this machine.  

I called Hamilton Beach to let them know what had happened with their product, left a detailed message with my name and number, and did not hear back from them.  I returned the product to Target and got a full refund.
justification: The incident involved a malfunction causing the lid to fly off, but no injury occurred. The exposed spinning blade poses a potential injury risk, making future occurrences likely if not addressed.

incident_description: I had some slices of bread cooking in the oven which had been previously preheated to 425.  The timer was set for 5 minutes.  After a few minutes, the oven beeped but it was a different sound that the timer going off.  I looked at it and thought the display looked funny so I went over to the oven and on the display, the left side which normally has the oven temperature displayed said  LOC and I don't recall what was on the other side which normally shows the time, but under where the time would be were the words "locked".  I pulled on the door and it would not open.  I pressed on the "Off" button to hopefully turn the oven off.  I went to look for my owners manual.  When I returned to the kitchen a minute or 2 later, the broiler was on and the bread was black & smoking.  Fearfully that it would catch fire, I pulled on the oven door as hard as I could until I forced it open.  I removed the bread & pan to the sink.  I tried to use the buttons to see if it would turn off now with no success.  I then went to the breaker box and cut the power to the oven that way.

I called the company and was told that my model was not under the recall.  Despite having the same problem, I was told that they would do anything about it. incident_description:
Product is a Panasonic microwave oven, model # NN-S954WF;  serial number 6AO4280171; date of manufacture:  10/2004

Over the past years we have owned this microwave there has been problems with the electrical interlock that permits the microwave to operate when the door is closed and shuts off the unit when the door is opened.  

There has been a burning smell and the door interlock has malfunctioned.  Upon examination (after the warranty period), the wiring is burned and the connector melted connected to one of the door interlock switches.  When the unit is operating and the door is opened there is a spark coming out of the switch, which has burned the wiring, caused the burning smell, and melted the connector.  Even when wiring and connector were replaced, the wiring burned and connector became damaged and burning smell persisted.

Not wanting to use this unit any longer, we called the company to find out if the interlocking electrical system is currently used in their oven and their representative said the same mechanism is being used.

I was in living room watching a movie when i heard a loud bang come from the kitchen, when i went to kitchen saw nothing out of ordinary decided to check on roast when i opened door of oven, the pyrex 13x9 baking pan the roast was in had exploded and shards of glass covered the inside of my oven and in my roast.  ruined my roast and my pan had to throw dinner away and took me 2 hrs and a few burns later finally cleaned up the mess. Caller states that she has been baking for years and had never had these problems so she contacted retailer who sent repair tech out.
Repair tech said he had to obtain/order parts but then no one ever came back out again.

She called retailer in Fall of 2009 who sent tech out and who told caller that the range was fluctuating but at only 5 to 10 degrees off the set temperature & he didn't believe that this small variation was anything to worry about, caller states that she thought at that time that this was acceptable.
Sometime around May 9th or 10th, 2011 caller began noticing that whenever she uses the oven on this stove and the oven is set at 350 degrees to 375 degrees at the highest then her baked food is drying, burning and cooking much faster than it should be and that there is an odor in the air coming from the oven that smells like it is self cleaning.

incident_description:
On Saturday, June 11, 2011, at 5:30 AM my wife entered our kitchen to find all of the control panel lights illuminated and flashing on our Kenmore Elite double oven. The oven had been turned off the previous evening and had not been turned on. As she attempted to turn the oven off to stop the flashing light, there were two popping sounds, followed by smoke and a strong electrical fire odor. The oven would not turn off. She call the Sears emergency number, but the technician who answered was unable to provide instruction that would successfully turn the oven off. My wife then called the Albuquerque Fire Department. The firemen were able to turn electricity off at the circuit breaker and disabled the oven. A Sears repairman came to our home that afternoon and examined the oven we had purchased in March 2009. The main control board, wiring harnesses, and convection fans were charred rendering the oven a total loss. 

If my wife had not gone downstairs into the kitchen early that morning, it is very likely that we would have suffered a major fire caused by an appliance that was turned off.   
 
Kenmore Elite Oven
Model: 79048123800
Serial # NF90924254

That burner was mistakenly turned on.  After a short interval the plastic base on which the kettle rests and which contains the electric cord burst into flames. It seems to me that this part cannot be cleaned in a reasonably safe way, and therefore should not be used in a refigerator.

[REDACTED]

The plastic cover over the coffee basket and water well does not seal to prevent steam from escaping around this cover. incident_description:
Frigidaire/Electrolux Model: FRS6LR5EM2
Report of Burning Plastic Refrigerator Light Bulb Area

Our Frigidaire refrigerator began to catch fire as a result of either a possible defective intermittent door light switch and or door seal not allowing the light switch to shut off the interior light after the door is closed. The end result was that the interior light stayed on for an undetermined amount of time resulting in the interior plastic casing to overheat and catch fire.

On 5/23/2011 at approximately 10:57 p.m. while our children slept upstairs, my wife detected a burning smell in our house. We followed the burning smell to our kitchen refrigerator, the Frigidaire model as listed above. This unit was installed new in 2006 after our new house was built.

Opening the refrigerator right door, we observed smoke, charred plastic dripping from above the light bulb at the top of the enclosure. We immediately observed that the interior enclosure had burned through the interior shell into the exterior casing insulation. There was no flame visible to us at this point. We did not reinstall the light bulb into the socket and continued to check for heat around the refrigerator. Nothing further was found. We also removed the freezer light bulb.

We contacted Frigidaire explaining the problem, was directed to their Liability Department who called us back. Per their instructions, we contracted with an authorized service tech who documented the damage and paid a fee of $89.04. We asked Frigidaire/Electrolux for a replacement refrigerator with a safer light assembly.. They responded thus far that maybe a buy back would be in order but is yet to be determined.

The technician and I recommended to Electrolux b=via my enclosed email that either a heat shield to dissipate the heat be designed for use above the light bulb, a thermal limiter be placed in the interior in to prevent light bulb fires and or the door switch be redesigned with a fail safe device. This is a serious fire hazard that must be eliminated.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with visible smoke and charred plastic, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

I discovered this problem late one night before going to bed, due to smelling the burn smell. incident_description:
My household possessed a Cuisinart DCC-755 coffeemaker.  Approximately a week ago, it began not wanting to turn on, or would run and turn off.  It gave up entirely today.  Upon opening it (removing 4 readily available screws on bottom that releases a base not attached to any function-related components), I was met with a burning smell and a fairly thick coat of white powder strewn about the inside of the unit.  The origin of the white powder is unclear, but it may be coming from a wire near the heating element for under the carafe.  Looking at one of the circuit boards, I also discovered scorch marks across an area of the board containing two large resistors and one small one.  Photographs were taken, but the webpage dialog for submitting them does not seem to be functionig properly on your site.

Investigating this on the web, I discovered that this failure seems to be the exact same syndrome (abrupt failure, burning, powder)  from others who have purchased this exact (and perhaps closely related) unit, some of whom had more dramatic burning, melted plastic, smoke, and the like.  Looking at the dates, it appears that the timing on many is similar as well, indicating that this may be an ongoing problem.  Thus, while we were relatively lucky with our unit, we seem to have dodged a bullet.  More importantly, as this was likely a popular unit due to being sold at Costo, it may represent an acute and ongoing concern for others, some of whom may be more unlucky than we were, perhaps much more.

Website of particular relevance to this:
http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html

incident_description:
We recently bought a new Jenn-Air indoor grilling cartridge to insert into our existing Jenn-Air electric downdraft cooktop.  We cooked chicken skewers on the new grill unit using a layer of aluminum foil beneath the raw meat, by placing this foil on top of the grill grates, as we had done with our former Jenn-Air indoor grilling unit to avoid flare-ups from dripping fat or marinade.  This time, however, within ten or fifteen minutes, a fire had started inside the grilling cartridge.  We saw flames coming out from the portion of the grill grates that was not covered with aluminum foil.  (Again, this was an electric unit, not a gas unit, so there should have been no flames of any kind.)  There was also smoke with a chemical odor.

When we turned off the grill and removed the chicken skewers and foil, we discovered that the fire had melted the metal grill grates.  We later discovered that these new grill grates were not made of solid metal, but of a sculpted "Excalibur" nonstick material with aluminum rods inside for support.  This Excalibur material appears to have physically melted off the aluminum bars, turning pale gray and ash-like, and slumping into the grill basin, onto the electric heating element.  (Since the different parts of the grill have melted together, and due to the chemical odor, we have not tried to remove the cartridge from the cooktop for closer inspection.  This is my best effort to describe what I have seen.)  There is now a hole several inches wide in the center of the grill grates, where the bars used to be.

In trying to investigate this problem, which we reported to Jenn-Air on the same night it took place, I have discovered that the user manual for a similar Jenn-Air cooktop warns users not to use aluminum foil on the grill grates, apparently due to a fire risk.  Yet there is no such warning in the user manual of the grill cartridge we bought and used.  Furthermore, there is at least one report online by a customer who had an identical meltdown on his indoor Jenn-Air grill with Excalibur grill grates, and he did *not* use aluminum foil; he cooked steaks directly on the grill grates, and the steaks must have covered enough of the grilling surface to cause the rise in temperature, melting the grates.
justification: The incident involved a fire and melting of grill grates but no injuries or deaths were reported.

They have refused to return it stating that we have not allowed them the chance to fix the machine. I told them that we did allow their technician to come fix the machine and they said it was unsafe. Sincerely,
[REDACTED]

incident_description:

We had the same problems as the recalled product, but complained to Maytag enough that we got a new stove because we felt as thought the one we had was a "lemon" and could not bear the time it took for anymore service calls....just to have the stove malfunction and break again.

Things went okay for a little while until I used the self clean and now something important keeps breaking/melting because of the heat that is produced when both ovens are on...or the self clean...or so they say.

Currently we have lived with only being able to use the lower oven and no self clean. We can not afford another service call only for it to break again. We read the recall and also decided not to get it fixed because it sounds extremely dangerous...and we have 3 little ones. We were hoping the recall would be expanded by now. I believe our original stove would be a recall...but this one is a little newer. 

The model number on the stove we have currently matches the recall...but the serial number ends in CE. So we have just missed it. But our stove is having all of the same symptoms. We are not willing to get it fixed only to potentially endanger our lives. I am writng this letter in hopes that your compiled information will lead to an expansion on the recall. This way we may be able to enjoy our product as we intended or a new one and anyone else that has the same stove will not get hurt.
justification: The stove has recurring malfunctions and poses a potential danger, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

I can no longer use this product as there is a hole melted through the bottom of the grease reservoir.

incident_description:
This incident involves Frigidaire smooth cooktop FEC30S6AB.  The first unit was purchased new from Grand Appliance on 2/23/08.  The kitchen was in process of being remodeled so the unit was installed approximately 1 month later.  Upon starting up one of the burners for the first time, a large electrical arc and loud pop came from the unit.  The burner went into thermal run-away and would not turn off.  For fear of burning down the house, I had to run down stairs to turn off the breaker to mitigate the catastrophic hazard.  

I immediately pulled the unit out and returned it to Grand Appliance as an out of box failure.  Grand Appliance exchanged the item for another new  Frigidaire smooth cooktop FEC30S6AB on 4/6/2008.  This unit lasted until 2010 then the lower right burner failed to turn off and began going into thermal run-away.  Again, I had to run down stairs to turn off the breaker to mitigate the catastrophic hazard.  The unit would intermittently reproduce this failure, with the last failure occurence on 2/5/2011.

I have isolated the failure on the second unit to the lower right burner on this unit and have not used this burner since.

With the wife now home with 2 little kids, the probablity of occurrence and severity present an unacceptable risk level.   Internet research has proven this to be a known frequent event by Frigidaire.  Frigidaire needs to be held liable for their products.  I seek reimbursement of the purchase price.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My mother purchased me a Frigidaire side by side refrigerator on 4-28-2011. The refrigerator began omitting strong, noxious fumes on 5-22-2011. It smelled like burnt plastic and we thought that there was an electrical fire. We soon determined that the smell was coming from the refrigerator, especially the freezer. We became nauseated, disoriented, lightheaded, and experienced a sensation that is similar to exposure to paint fumes without ventilation. The next day food, water, and ice we consumed had an unnatural metallic, burnt taste and we had to stop using the refrigerator. We called to schedule a service repair with Conn's Service. They did not inform us that we had the option of going straight to Frigidaire for service and they did not tell us that we could get food loss reimbursed by them sending out a form. (These facts would come out over the next several days.) They scheduled a service date for two days later, however, the tech called to cancel and we were rescheduled for 5-31-2011. During that time we waited, seven days, and we were constantly exposed to the fumes and odor. We also had to purchase food and drinks on a daily basis, unable to use the refrigerator. I called Sand K Appliance Repair and was advised that we would likely need a new product, as it would be almost impossible to get the smell out of it. When [redacted], the tech came over, I advised him of this. I called Conn's and spoke to the manager,[redacted]. he told me that the tech could submit the product for exchange. He then spoke to him on the phone. [redacted] advised him that he was required to contact the manufacturer and follow their directions. He did so and he was told that the likely source of the fumes was melting Styrofoam blocks within the freezer paneling that the defrosting heater was melting. He checked and found that this was the case. He was then advised to move the melted styrofoam over and to tell me to use baking soda to remove the smell. I told him that we were not comfortable with this as a solution and were not satisfied. He told me to call the service department. I did so and left a message with manager [redacted], with whom I've dealt with extensively and has not been forthcoming, honest, or helpful. She told me that ["redacted"]would call me back.I then called Conn's and left a message for [redacted] to call me. Neither called me, so I called Customer Resolutions for Conn's. I was advised to call Frigidaire. I did so, but they were closed, so I left an online complaint. I received a message from them stating that there policy is to make three repairs before replacement review. The suggested I call Conn's and ask [redacted] to replace the unit. I called Frigidaire and I was advised by the person I spoke to that this is a manufacturer defect where the defrost heater becomes hotter than it should and spreads heat further up than it should. She said that the tech should have been advised to replace the heater and styrofoam and dispose of both. I asked her if she or Frigidaire could tell me that the product is safe and safe to contain food. She said she could not. I advised her that the day before I had became ill for a few hours after the tech had the refrigerator  open to service it. She told me that she would have to send me the parts and a service tech and they had to try to fix it three times before submitting it for an exchange. I advised her that this policy does not take into account what should happen if a design flaw deems the product unsafe. Styrofoam omits toxic fumes, benzine gas, and carcinogens when burnt and there are even special procedures to follow when disposing of melted Styrofoam. To suggest that a product that had contained melting styrofoam for over a week would be safe for human use after putting baking soda in it, was absurd and risky. Furthermore, the manufacturers of baking soda do not make claims that their product absorbs toxic fumes, residue from burning hazardous material, or decontaminates food services that were exposed to such chemicals. After making the call I was surprised to learn that my mother was told by [redacted] that "We would not leave an unsafe product in your home. Two of my technicians told me it would be safe after cleaning...." At this point I am waiting to hear back from Conn's Customer Resolutions or to see if the service company that comes out deems the refrigerator unrepairable. I have multiple emails documenting my correspondence with Conn's.
justification: The incident caused nausea, disorientation, and lightheadedness, indicating injury from toxic fumes.
