incident_description:
About 15 minutes after starting the dishwasher, a Bosch SHX43C05UC / 43 with serial number FD870100284, I heard a popping sound and noticed the dishwasher stopped working.

I opened the front door and did not see any lights. I pulled the dishwasher out from the wall and inspected the back. There is a black hard plastic coating the dishwasher, and in a few locations, this black plastic had severely melted.

After I did some searches online, I found other people had a similar experience. I also noticed that there was a recall for a similar problem on other models, but not this one.

I would like to submit that something had shorted, or overheated in this dishwasher, in order for this damage to occur.

This dishwasher is on its own circuit and there does not seem to be any other power issues.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned with visible damage but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. Similar incidents reported online suggest occurrence likelihood is likely (4).

incident_description:
I have a new KitchenAid tea kettle - about 7-8  inches in max diameter. .
The design of the spout is low on the kettle.  The handle is not in cnter but also off to the side of the spout. Not centered as other tea kettles.

This design has two problems.

When starting to pour after whistle starts - boiling -  the water comes out with an explosive force.  At least a half cup before you can back off the pour.  IT IS VERY UNEXPECTED.  I have done it several times knowing it may happen.

Secondly,  the handle puts your hand over the spout when pouring - the steam coming out of the spout rises to your hand and you must quickly stop pouring or burn yourself. 

I believe that this product is dangerous.  especially to the person using it the first time.
justification: The description indicates a risk of burns from steam and unexpected forceful pouring, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
We have a Maytag over-the-range microwave model No. MMV4205BAW.  We were using the microwave's 30-second feature to heat a cup of coffee.  The microwave beeped three times when the timer ran out.  The fan and light clicked off; but the microwaving itself continued to run without the fan and light.  It took us a minute or so to figure out what was going on.  We couldn't stop the microwave by pushing the stop button.  Finally, we pushed the start button and then the stop button to stop the microwave.  The cup and coffee were extremely hot and steaming profusely.  We left it in the microwave for a while before attempting to remove it.

This reminded us of when we first ordered the Microwave from Home Depot a couple years ago.  After installing the first microwave we received, it came on and ran after we just closed the door.  We immediately removed the microwave and took it back.  Home Depot ordered a replacement unit.  We just thought only the first microwave had a defect.  However, now that we've had this recent incident, we are wondering if there is a design flaw in the units.

Aside from our frustration over the waste of money and the cost to replace the microwave, we were startled over the safety risk it posed.  Had we left the room or not been aware of what was happening at the time, serious injuries or fire could have occurred.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning microwave without any reported injuries, but with potential safety risks if unnoticed.

incident_description:
I have a Whirlpool wall oven that while cooking today the top heating element turned on and would not turn off.  We could not control it from the front panel and had to turn the oven off at the house breaker.  When we turned the breaker back on the oven was still in an always on state.

The oven beeped once and displayed a couple of characters in the display  a 2 and a 3.

Model RBD245PDT12
Serial XM3400298
justification: The oven malfunctioned but no injury occurred, requiring intervention to prevent potential hazards.

incident_description:
The Maytag Performa Refrigerator (Serial #PTB1949GR), caused a fire in my home resulting in extensive damage to the interior.  If I had not been up at that time, I could not have saved my children.  The following is from the recall website - "An electrical failure in the relay, the component that turns on the refrigerator's compressor, can cause overheating and pose a serious fire hazard."

I never received a recall notice in the mail, so I was not aware of this.

State Farm Insurance is handling the claim, but I want to sue Maytag/Whirlpool for all my pain and suffering.  I am now living in a hotel until the interior of my home is reconstructed. I have also lost many memorable personal items that cannot be replaced.  My children and I are missing our home, not to mention that our lives have been turned upside down.
justification: The incident caused extensive property damage and emotional distress, but no physical injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Caller & family came home around March 25, 2011, smelled burning odor and narrowed it down to his refrigerator.
He is reporting that the lightbulbs in his refrigerator were not turning off when refrigerator is closed and the plastic coverings were melting and posing a fire safety hazard.
Food placed anywhere near the lights was warm, never getting cool and thereby spoiling especially any milk placed nearby.
Caller tried to unscrew the bulb but burned his thumb, index & middle fingers on his right hand so left alone at that time.
Feeling of no fingertips remains.
Caller has an electrician friend who came to his house, unplugged the refrigerator, let all cool and then removed bulbs so that caller & family can use refrigerator without fear.
Caller contacted manufacturer/retailer who referred him to distributor after telling him they could charge him for parts and labor if he wanted repair.
He is calling them again but would like to request that the CPSC recall these refrigerators, that manufacturer be required to repair refrigerators involved at manufacturer expense and if already repaired at caller's expense that manufactuere be reqeired to reimburse.
It took more than a few days to rid his house of the smell.
justification: The caller suffered burns to multiple fingers and has lasting numbness, indicating an injury. The incident involved a fire hazard and spoiled food, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
The large front right burner  was powered in the on position at a medium high setting for a couple of minutes when the coil began to glow bright red.

She went to power the burner in the off position when she noticed a huge flame the blew up fromt he coil and then the coil exploded and shot the burning metal  through out the kitchen.
The firme as contacted and they stated that it is no longer under warranty. The part as not available  and she ordered it from  Glenwood Appliance Center and she has plugged the part back in.

She expereinced the same failure a few years prior with a different range by the same manafacturer. The heating element in the oven also experienced the same failure.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of the burner coil, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was using the oven, she only had it on for a few minutes when it started overheating to a temperature of 600 degrees, the four burners came on and the broiler and the error flashed on the control panel as F1 and would not turn off, by attempting to turn off the stove she received minor burns to her arms, she had to power it off from the Circuit breaker.  Consumer didnot seek medical attention, she administered first aid.

Consumer eventually unplugged the stove to prevent further damages.  

5/2/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that the unit was not under warranty so there was nothing that could be done.

Consumer feels that this range is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The consumer received minor burns while attempting to turn off the malfunctioning oven, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says was using dishware.  Consumer said unit was not hot or cold, when she says that a small 5 oz bottle of hot sauce fell and hit the side of the bowl.  The consumer says the glassware shattered into a million pieces, while the bottle of hot sauce did not break.  The consumer says she had not used dishware yet she was just getting it ready.
justification: The incident involved glassware shattering but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description:
After brewing a cup of coffee he went to remove the coffee pot to from the base and the brew basket became detached. The hot water then burned his right hand. He received a minor burn mark to the right hand in which later turned in to a hard blister. He ran cold water on it and placed ice on it. He then did some research online about other incidents happening with the same model as he owns. 

The brew basket is only snapped it to place and is not sealed on. He is going to return the product to the retailer. He has not contacted the manafacturer but plans on doing so.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor burn and blister, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported with the same model.

incident_description:
Our Kenmore  oven  door exploded ( exterior Glass panel ) sending glass across the kitchen.  The oven was not on and and had not been on for 3 days!
Model #  970-94223403
Purchased in 2004
Sears in Dalton, Ga.
justification: The oven door exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was popping popcorn in the microwave when there was a flash and a crackling sound. There is a screw inside the microwave that holds the heating element and it was arcing. Unpluged and wiped out and tried again, same thing. It is an Emerson model #MWG9115SL. I have had this microwave since 3/16/10, just a little over a year. This could be very dangerous.
justification: The incident involved arcing inside the microwave, which is dangerous but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: I was holding the coffee pot of the electric coffee maker by the handle. Without warning, the pot fell off the handle, leaving the consumer holding only the handle.
justification: The coffee pot fell off the handle but no injury was reported, indicating a minor incident.

incident_description: On Sunday May 22, we were running our Bosch SHU43C02UC/14 dishwasher (serial #FD8306 02184) when I heard a popping sound coming from it.  When I investigated, plumes of black smoke was exiting from the control panel area.  I immediately turned off the power from the front on/off pushbutton on the dishwasher and then turned off the power at the breaker.  I was able to turn off power within 30 seconds of when I heard the popping noise.  I am very concerned that 1) the dishwasher appeared to catch fire, 2) the breaker did not trip, 3) if I wasn't sitting 15 feet away, my kitchen/house may have caught fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and potential fire risk, but no injury or death occurred, and the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
I have a range hood Kitchenaid microwave KHMS155LSS-4 that I purchased about 5 years ago.  About 6 months ago, my microwave started up itself during the night giving off a beeping sound.  I could not stop it except to unplug it.  I did not have it occur again until more recently.  Thank goodness, I was at home.  It will now start up by itself more often, so I unplug it when I am not using it.  I did some research on the internet and see that this is a frequent problem.  See http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/kitchenaid_microwave_rangehood.html

I called Kitchenaid and they are to send a part and have it replaced in a couple of weeks.  I am fearful that this won't work and it will happen again when I am not at home.  Kitchenaid needs to recall this product.  It is extremely dangerous!  Whoever imagined that a microwave can start up by itself!  Some of the on-line reports indicate that the repair does not cure the problem.
justification: The microwave starting by itself poses a potential hazard but no injury or death has been reported in the description.

incident_description: Dishwasher caught fire while running.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Recently our Samsung Microwave oven has started turning on by itself. I am concerned that this posses a fire hazard if the unit were to be left plugged in.
justification: The microwave turning on by itself poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Toaster oven worked as described for approximately 3 months.  Then, noticed strong burning smell and smoke when using - discovered that heating elements were not turning off with set temperature - basically the oven elements were on all the time.

Outer case became extremely hot and dangerous.

Once unit was unplugged and cooled down, heating elements would not come on at all now.

Significant burn hazard and/or fire hazard.
justification: The toaster oven malfunctioned, creating a significant burn and fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an under-the-counter Black and Decker toaster oven to replace the one I already had on May 30, 2010. It is model TROS1000. I was skeptical about buying it, in that there were quite a few reviews on amazon.com saying that people had trouble with the mounting system, and many said that the oven kept falling off the cabinet and they sent the oven back. But since some hadn't had that problem, and I liked my previous Black & Decker toaster oven, I decided to try it out. Well, I DID have problems with the mount and it DID fall down. There are two flimsy clips on the front of the mount to keep it in place. So I sent it back to Amazon.com and they sent me a replacement. I had the same problem with the second one, but was finally able to bend the clips so that the unit stayed in place. However, after some time, it began falling again. 

This is really quite dangerous because if the oven is hot, it can burn you or fall on something that's underneath it and possibly start a fire. 

So I contacted B&D via email and went back and forth with them on it. They ended up sending me a replacement oven, a $20 cheaper model (with no electronic controls) stating that they could substitute it out based on their warranty. So I asked for it to be escalated to management. They have finally said that they will refund my money, but frankly, I'm really concerned that they don't seem to care that people are having safety issues with this oven. 

On amazon.com alone, out of 301 customer reviews, 155 are 3 stars or less (out of 5 stars maximum), with many people talking about problems with the mount. This model has an identical mounting system to model TROS1500. 63 fall in the 1 star category.

Because it is an item that can get very hot, I feel that  even when the clips are working properly, the chance of bumping the unit and it falling are great. This is NOT the same mounting system I had on my previous B&D oven. 

I am going to return this and get my money back, but I hope you look into this matter. I hope a terrible accident doesn't have to happen before you make them fix this problem.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with the toaster oven falling, which could lead to burns or fire, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: The homeowner called the N. Andover Fire Dept after they had preheated their Kenmore electric oven to cook in. The control panel overheated and caught fire with active flames coming out of it at the time of the call. The FD unplugged the unit, however the fire was out prior to FD arrival. I was called to investigate this incident by [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved an oven fire, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description:
On Sunday, May 22, 2011 I bought a KitchenAid 12" countertop toaster-oven from Target in Peoria, IL.  Got it home, set it up, plugged it in and set it for 350 degree Bake.  Less than 4 minutes later, I noticed a strong burning smell.  When I looked through the window into the oven I saw that it was ON FIRE!!!!  My husband came into the kitchen when I screamed.  He quickly unplugged the oven and took it outside of our home, setting it on a brick walkway.  It was several moments before the flames were extinguished.
We planned to return it to the store immediately, but it was too hot to safely put into our car.  30 minutes later it was still hot to the touch.  My husband noted that the hottest spot was not where we saw the initial flames.  The flames originated on the upper rear element, but the hot spot then appeared to be closer to the top front, as if the fire had spread.
The next day we returned it to the Target store where we bought it for a refund.  The only note made during the return was that the product was "defective".
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: The consumer says unit gave her an eletrical shock for 15 seconds.  The consumer said she felt the pain, the unit stopped the electrical current to come thru and that is when she was able to release her hand from the handle.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer and they said there are no safety concerns with this product and to contact CPSC.
justification: The consumer experienced pain from an electrical shock, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
When brewing coffee, the coffeemaker started smoking and smelling like an electrical fire.  It was purchased on April 12, 2010 from Amazon.com.  It is a Cuisinart model DCC-1200, serial # 91223H.
This was a very close call for us, and I think a year old coffee maker that does this is obviously defective.
justification: The coffeemaker started smoking, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Electrical short in dishwasher started small fire within it.  No damage outside of dishwasher.  I'm the second owner of this house and don't remember receiving a notice.  I moved in in 2005.  Found the following recall notice, issued in 2007:

http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml07/07190.html

My dishwasher is on the list.
justification: The incident involved a small fire contained within the dishwasher with no external damage or injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recall notice suggests a known issue, making recurrence likely.

incident_description:
Smoke started coming out of my dishwasher.

After further investigation, I found that the smoke was coming from inside the door.  Upon taking the screws out and looking inside - there are wires that started melting together.

LUCKILY - I was home when this happened!
justification: Smoke and melting wires indicate a fire hazard, but no injury occurred as the issue was caught in time.

incident_description: Last night the microwave WHILE NOT IN USE had an apparent electrical short. The short was in the wiring connected to the mother board. As we neared the microwave we saw smoke coming from the oven then we saw flames. The house filled with smoke quickly. We unplugged the oven and took the panel loose. The fire was still burning.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Kenmore Range 790.96123409

Smooth Top Stove - Electric Burner turns on randomly to high by itself!  Sometime when on low it will turn to high and not able to turn down or shut off.  It turned on to high by itself 4 times in 30 minutes.
justification: The stove turning on randomly poses a potential hazard but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Turned off oven and the broiler came on and almost caught fire! The panel indicated everything was off. Had to turn off the circuit breaker to get it to turn off.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that almost caught fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Purchased DeLonghi EO2058 Electric Counter Oven. The rotating timer switch is either defective or improperly designed. When timer is manually rotated to the OFF position, it is very easy to go by the OFF position, and the power comes on, with no warning. Very dangerous, because you can walk away, thinking you turned it off, but the device comes on and overheats. This switch should have a hard stop when you get to the OFF position,
justification: The defect can lead to the device overheating, posing a danger, but the description does not mention any actual injury or death.

incident_description: Control module on Bosch SHE45M06UC dishwasher caught fire.  The electrical fire burned out the control module, wiring harness, and motor of the dishwasher.  Other than inhalation of noxious fumes, there was no bodily injury to me or further fire damage to my home related to the incident.  Although several Bosch dishwashers have been recalled because of this fire hazard, this particular model is not currently listed on the recall list.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing damage to the dishwasher but no bodily injury or further property damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the known fire hazard in similar models.

incident_description:
my KitchenAid Convection Microwave Oven keep beeping, then has mind of its own, getting all different number entered by itself to the oven.  It may start running with unlimited time without stopping....it is unsafe and dangerous.....it may cause the house to burn down....

I have it fixed by KitchenAid service and it happened again right after it was fixed...i think there is design fraud on the keypad design...

I called KitchenAid and they claimed that is the isolated problem but i found out that many consumers have similar problem with the products...

Like to know what is the latest update on this product.  Thanks.

My Kitchenaid model number is: kbmc140hss0
justification: The microwave's malfunctioning behavior poses a potential fire hazard, which is unsafe and dangerous, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: Dishwasher smelt like burnt plastic
justification: The smell of burnt plastic indicates an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
We bought an Amana range in 10/2009.  Model number AER5830VAB0.  Serial number RY3816920.  We heard an electrical popping sound coming from behind the knob of a burner.  When we had a service person come out today, he said that he has seen this problem before with this type of range and that if he replaced it he would be replacing it with the same part.  He said that 2 of our 4 burners have shorted out and that another one looks like it will in the future.  To use the burners as they are is a fire hazard. 

How can I have him repair the parts with the same part that broke and could cause a fire?  Also, if he did the repair, it would cost almost as much as we paid for the range in the first place.  I called the company, and they won't do anything because our warrantee is up.  How can they use parts that break so easily?  I am furious that they have put my family in danger.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard due to electrical issues in the range, but no actual fire or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that for over the past 4 years he has been experiencing similiar problems of Release # 09-333.  He has contacted the dealer  and several services has been administered to the unit but those services did not resolve the problems.

Consumer stated that his most recent occurred approximately 2 weeks ago.

Consumer is concerned that this unit is a fire hazard and should be recalled
justification: The consumer reports recurring problems and concerns about fire hazard, indicating an incident without injury but with potential for harm.

incident_description: Hazard:  The surface heating elements can 1) turn on spontaneously without being switched on; 2) fail to turn off after being switched off; or, 3) heat to different temperatures than selected. This poses a fire and burn hazard to our family and other consumers.
justification: The hazard involves potential fire and burn risks, which could lead to incidents without immediate injury but pose significant danger.

incident_description: Bottom of Walmart/GE slow cooker 168945 melted and caused countertop to become extremely hot.  There might have been a fire had I not been home at the time.  Countertop had melted plastic on it.  I now see that this product has been recalled but I was not notified.
justification: The incident involved a melted slow cooker and hot countertop, but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the product recall and potential for fire if unattended.

incident_description:
In April 2005 I purchased a KitchenAid electic range model#KERA807PWW00.  On May 18, 2005 for no apparent reason and while not in use the oven started displaying a message, "enter probe temp or remove probe"  I had no idea how or why this happened and tried to clear it.  The oven "bake" kicked on and I could not shut it off.  The off button would not work.  I pulled it out from the wall and unplugged it.  I then contacted KitchenAid who referred me over to the Safety Division of Whirlpool.  After explaining my issue again, I was asked a series of questions such as, "were there any personal injuries or property damages"?  They said this is a safety issue and to leave it unplugged until someone could come out.  They made arrangements for a repair service to come out the next day, May 19.  They told me they would cover labor and I would have to pay for the parts if any were needed.  The repair service came out and I explained again to him what it was doing.  I helped him pull it out away from the wall so I could plug it in for him.
The unit immediately went into "self clean", the door locked and the smell was horrible.  He also could not get the off button to work.  He entered time to time it out.  He then went over to his laptop, entered some information and told me I needed a new computer membrane which costs $220.00.  I asked him how long this was covered for.  He did not know any warranty information.  I then called the Whirlpool Safety Division and spoke with the woman I talked to the day before.  I asked her about the warranty which she stated 90 days.  I explained my concern of of wanting to know if this could happen again.  I wanted to know if it was possible for this unit to come on and cause a fire.  I wanted to know who would take responsibility should this oven come on while we were sleeping or away from home.  She could not tell me what could or would happen after the 90 days.  Nor could she gaurantee me that when these computer membranes go these ovens won't have a mind of thier own to cause serious damage or death.  My issue was not paying $220.00 for a repair.  My issue is the consumer needs to know the hazzard involved with an appliance that has a "brain" that can do what it wants to do when it wants to do it without human direction.  This is way more than a computer "glich".  The models that have these type of computer membranes need to be recalled.  At best an awareness letter needs to be mailed to the consumer.  I paid $1,085.00 for this oven and I would have invested $220.00 to repair it if I could be gauranteed my family, my pets and my home were not in danger.  It is also obvious to Whirlpool that the hazard is there or I would not have been told to leave it unplugged.  The general public needs to be made aware of this so they have the opportunity to trade in there computerized oven for one that will not think on it's own.  A dead consumer does not need help from a consumer protection agency.  We need your help now.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that could not be turned off, posing a potential safety hazard, but no injuries or property damage were reported.

incident_description:
8:30 AM last Friday (April 29) when consumer tried to unloaded the clean dishes from the previous night.  Consumer found out that the dishwasher was in the dry cycle the entire night. Consumer tried to turned "off" but the turned off bottom did not work so consumer have to turned 'off' his circuit breaker

Consumer called an independent repair tech who said that the relay switch is malfunctioning and the whole panel needs to be change.

Consumer called and explained incident to mfr  rep. (name unknown) who said that the product is not longer under warranty.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher and circuit breaker, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer wanted to report that her Kenmore Elite electric range doesnt turn on to the desired setting on low it exceeds itself to high. The unit is a smooth top range and this applies to the left side of the stove. The product is a stove and oven. The right front burner only works sometimes as it occasionally wont turn on. The left burners will turn off but they wont turn to anything but high immediately when turn on even if she sets the burner at low or medium. She called the manufacturer in April of 2009 because the oven wouldn't work for baking. The manufacturer told her that they would fix it at her expense. They replaced the motherboard control that controlled the baking element for the oven. 

She has noticed that Sears has similar models that were recalled for similar issues with the heating element. Later that year, the manufacturer came to fix the same issue with the stove's malfunctioning baking feature. Her father who is repairman in 2010 serviced the unit for problem with oven's front touch panel so that she may turn the oven on. In March of 2010 the issue with her left burner's began. In this instance she chose not to call the manufacturer or the retailer. Presently, the stove and oven are not charred or discolored. No damage has spread to the structure of her home. Her father provided with several numbers to call and after speaking to the manufacturer regarding similar recalled units, she felt it was imperative to report this issue to the CPSC.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove with no reported injuries or property damage, but the recurring issues and recalls suggest a likely occurrence.

incident_description: black plastic handle on carafe of the 5 CUP electric COFFEEMAKER broke off while consumer was washing it. consumer stated that handle is secured to carafe by metal screw held secure by cheap plastic nut. The nut in carafe was in 6 pieces & carafe fell off into his other hand.
justification: The incident involved a broken handle causing the carafe to fall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says she turned on the unit and she stepped away.  She says she heard a big grinding noise.  Consumer runs into the kitchen when she noticed the unit was making noise when she noticed fire burst out of the back.  

Consumer says she shut off the circuit breaker and she unplugged the unit.  Consumer says the unit behind the wall is blackened.  Consumer says that the unit was on not even 5 minutes.  Consumer contacted the manufacturer and they offered no assistance and explained to her that she should have gotten the extended warranty.  She also says they told her to contact CPSC.  

Consumer says she is dissapointed in retailer and manufacturer for not providing any assistance.
justification: The incident involved a fire and property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: About a month ago, I put a microwavable bowl in microwave to heat up food.  I placed a paper towel over it as I used to do frequently in my previous microwave.  Within seconds, the towel caught fire.  I unplugged microwave and took care of it.  I assumed it was the paper towel or that you shouldn't use paper towels in microwave and have not done it since.  However, the past three times that I have made microwave popcorn, the bag ends up burning, the kernels fly all over the microwave and about a quarter of the bag pops into popcorn.  I don't understand why a microwavable bag of popcorn burns in the microwave and just to be clear, this has not been the same brand of popcorn so it has to be an issue with the microwave.  I feel this is very dangerous and should be investigated.
justification: The incident involves repeated burning of popcorn and a previous paper towel fire, indicating a potential microwave malfunction, but no injuries have been reported.

incident_description: I was baking some cookies in my GE range oven at 350 degrees.  I turned the oven off and went about cleaning the kitchen.  My 11 month old son pulled himself to a standing position using the oven door to brace himself.  He screamed and cried and dropped to the floor.  I picked him up and when trying to figure out what happened, I realized there was a lot of heat next to me.  I placed my hand on the window portion of my oven door and it was so hot to the touch that if you left your hand on there for more than a couple of seconds you would burn your hand badly.  My son's hand was red, but thankfully, he was okay and did not have any continuing issues.  I went to Sears where I purchased the oven and they referred me to call GE directly.  A GE technician came out and after turning the oven on for a few minutes, taking the door apart, his solution was :  the door gets hot, keep the kiddies away.  I bought this oven to replace my previous GE range and never had any problems in the past.  I feel this is a very serious issue and that it should be addressed.  I would never have bought this oven if I had thought it could be a safety issue for my children.  I also feel that I should not have to shoo my children out of the kitchen ( a kitchen I feel is safe & childproofed except for the now hot oven door ) while I am cooking and baking.  I have always been able to have my children with me in the kitchen within reason.  I was under the impression that a tempered glass oven door should shield some heat and not allow the door to get to levels that could potentially cause serious injury.  I have talked to several other mothers and none of them have ever noticed this as being a problem in their kitchens.  I have 4 children, a 5 year old, a 3 year old, and 11 month old twins and I believe that if this had been a problem in the past, I would have noticed it long before now.  We purchased this oven in February 2010.  I feel in this day and age with safety at the forefront of our minds and homes, an oven door should not be a burn hazard in my home, especially a new oven.
justification: The child suffered a burn injury from the hot oven door, which constitutes an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as it happened once but may not be frequent.

incident_description: Range was purchased July 13, 2009.  Customer says the white plastic knobs that control burners on top of the glass top range have multiple temperature settings on each knob printed in a charcoal color on the white plastic knobs.  After a bit of use the printed settings start coming off, thus eventually making the settings completely unreadable on all 4 knobs.  This puts the electric glass top range in the same category as a [REDACTED] camp stove- just guess at your temperature.  Customer says she contacted manufacturer and that they told her they have no reports of this issue and that it is a cosmetic issue for which they are not liable.  The customer feels this is a safety issue as three burners are dual burners; therefore three knobs have both dual and single burner settings on each, showing low to high settings plus simmer (3 settings) and low medium, high settings for each of the fore-mentioned settings. The fourth burner is a standard burner with warm, melt, simmer (3 settings) low to high each with low, medium, high indicated for each setting.  With the print rubbed or wiped off, she can only guess the settings.  This could result in a kitchen fire (possibly grease getting too hot) or even bodily injury (something spattering from having too much heat).
justification: The incident describes a potential safety hazard due to unreadable temperature settings, which could lead to bodily injury or kitchen fires.

incident_description: The consumer says she was sitting next to unit when black smoke and sparks started coming out of unit.  She pulled the plug from unit and it stopped.  Consumer said the unit was running for only about 5-7 minutes before sparking.  Consumer also noticed strong odor.  Consumer says the circuit board melted.  She contacted the manufacturer and they did not seem concerned with it stating that they havent had any problems.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the unit malfunctioning shortly after use.

incident_description: We put the dishwasher on last night before we went to bed, as we usually do, and this morning when we got up, we went to empty it and the items were hot to the touch and you could smell a burnt smell.  It appears that the heater was on all night.  There were some plastics, on the bottom and top racks that were partially melted and the cutlery basket also has some melted parts.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted plastics and cutlery basket) but no reported injuries, making it a severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but can occur with faulty appliances.

incident_description: I have a KitchAid Microwave with hood combo microwave oven Model # KHMS155LSS-4 Serial # TRT 02 11042.  Five days ago, the microwave started beeping, the lights started flashing, and the microwave oven turned on all by itself.  It appears that the microwave oven went into auto cook mode.  I got up immediately and pushed the cancel button to stop the cooking.  About 20 minutes later, the microwave oven did the exact same thing. incident_description:
We have installed a Jenn-Air Model JJGC1430ADS 30" Gas Cooktop as part of a kitchen renovation.  The controls for each burner are in the following positions: "Off" at the 6 o'clock position, "Start" or "Ignite" at the 4 o'clock position, "High" at the 3 o'clock position, "Medium" at noon and "Low" at the 9 o'clock position.

Having had other gas cooktops our experience has been that there is a stop or indent of some sort at the "Start" point where the gas ignites.  On this cooktop the indent is at the "High" or 3 o'clock position.  This means that it is very easy to turn the control knob past "Ignite" to "High" if you are not looking closely.  This results in the free flow of raw gas into the home that is NOT burning.  Our installer and we ourselves have already experienced this free flow of gas and it would be very easy for someone cooking or a child to turn the controls past the start point creating a very unsafe condition as, once you pass the start position the igniters do not function.

Though we understand the advantage of having gas flow and being able to light the cooktop on a manual basis should power to the home fail, we do NOT understand why Jenn-Air would design a product where the ignition of the gas is subject to such easy failure caused by what we believe is simply having the indent in what appears to be an incorrect location.

Last, we have already contacted Jenn-Air regarding our concerns and have been advised this the configuratin is in fact what they designed.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw leading to potential gas leaks, which is hazardous but no injury or death has been reported yet.

Had someone been standing in front of the oven, especially a child at counter height, there could have been serious bodily injury.  Needless to say, the glass oven door is defective and not properly tempered.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion of the oven door, posing potential for serious injury but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Frigidaire free standing range Model FEFL79GCA.  Purchase date 7/30/2007.  Serial number VF72250055.
Burner is not turning off when knob is in off position; not cooking at temperature set at; and turning back on from off position.
We have extended warranty.  Called Frigidaire and explained problem.  They sent service technician; he ordered parts and installed.  The burner continues to not cut off; and cook at much higher temperature than set.
We looked on line to see if any recalls had been issued and noted many models for same reason.  We did not see our model listed, however, it is doing the same thing as the recalled models.
Has this model also been noted to have the same issue and please advise on how we proceed with Frigidaire.
justification: The burner not turning off poses a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage is reported.

incident_description: Consumer reports that the electric pressure cooker poses a fire hazard. Consumer states that within a short time, the heating coil increases its temperature so much that the coating on the pot goes off, and at some point may cause a fire.
justification: The description indicates a potential fire hazard, which is an incident with no reported injury, and the likelihood is high given the consumer's report of the heating issue.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore ceramic cooktop that sometimes it failed to turn off after being switched off. It had happened many time and the only way I can turn it off is to throw the breaker. It just happened again today 5/14/2011. Luckily, nobody got hurt.
justification: The cooktop fails to turn off, requiring breaker intervention, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I bought a kenmore stove serial #vf40376266 flat top stove and I really like it but for the last 2-3 years i have had a problem with the stove there is a metal lip between where the flat top ends and where the stove door opens up this gets extreamly hot the service guy said between 100 and 150 degrees and that was very normal. the problem my daughter and I have both got burned on this metal bar bad enough it has blistered and had a nasty red place for about a week. It happens if your shirt comes up on your stomach or if you are waring something light. I really worry about it when we have people over I am worried someone is going to get burned very bad and we are going to get sued for something that is not our fault at all. We bought the kenmore in feb 05. I have contacted sears and the mail sears headquarters and have just got the run around I thought the customer service guy was really helpful when it just explained that it is just old and needs to be replaced there was nothing they could do. I really would like some help in this matter. [REDACTED]
justification: The description reports burns resulting in blisters and prolonged redness, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue has occurred multiple times and is a concern during gatherings, suggesting a likely recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Electric Range was not in use but callers noticed that the center burner was getting red then black then red again indicating that it was in use, off then in use again.
Caller checked the electronic control panel on front of unit and there were no codes warning that there was a hot burner at any time.
He assured that the sensa cook button was not on, then he turned the element on then off again but this did not solve the problem either.
They followed the same steps a few times after which the caller turned the on button to "high" then off again.
Once the button was turned to high then off the control panel showed HE to indicate hot burner, went off and hasn't come back on again.
Caller turned his circuit breaker off.
Caller contacted retailer he purchased the electric range from on 04/11/2011, spoke with rep who told him that the range was not on recall but they could send a tech out if he made an appointment but at his expense.
He explained what the range was doing, that it is a safety hazard, that ranges recalled on release# 09-333 are recalled for the same thing & that repair should be at their expense.
Called manufacturer he was led to believe was the producer of this range, they identified the actual manufacturer.
He called retailer customer service 04/11/2011, spoke with [redacted] who told him that she couldn't tell him who the manufacturer is, it is not recalled.
The model is made by the same manufacturer as cuted in recall notice 09-333, where other models were cited as having the same malfunction.  
Subsequently, the retailer made a number of service calls and replaced the same circuit board as was replaced to remedy the issue under recall notice 09-333.  The issue has not reocurred since the repairs have been made.
He would like this model recalled for the safety of all in the public.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range with potential safety hazards, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Bosch dishwasher Model # SHU43C05UC/14, Serial # FD830701395, purchased in 2003, suffered a small explosion from the control panel and caught fire on May 14, 2011.  Two plastic control buttons burst from the door of the unit, and in flames, landed on the floor of the kitchen, scorching the wood floor.  Fortunately, we were home and were able to cut power to the dishwasher (the failure did not trip the circuit breaker) and extinguish the fire both inside the dishwasher panel and on the floor.  

We purchased the dishwasher at an Expo Design Center store.  These stores, although owned by The Home Depot, are now closed.  We have learned today that many of these Bosch dishwashers were recalled. We were never notified of the recall, and believe the closure of the Expo store probably contributed to that notification failure.  

If we had not been home at the time, this failure would have resulted in far greater property damage due to the fires both within the dishwasher (built into wooden cabinets) and the burning plastic buttons which landed on the wood floor.
justification: The incident involved a fire and property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the recall and potential for similar failures in other units.

incident_description: I have recently owned a Siemens SL34A FD8503. I did not know about the recall, however I was on the website trying to find out if I could get a brochure but was unsuccessful. My dishwasher was smelling of something burning and found out that the water would not drain out. I called two times over the phone to see if there was a recall on it and both times the operators said "no". So I just purchased another dishwasher of a different brand. Can I receive any compensation for my loss?
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dishwasher with no reported injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) based on the frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description:
We bought a new home October 2010.  The Maytag oven storage drawer has a very sharp edge where you reach into the lower drawer.  Three members of the family have been cut on this edge.  We reported it to Maytag, but it was not fixed.

We have looked at other new homes in our neighborhood, and the edge of the drawer now seems less sharp.

The model number is MES5752BAS16, the serial number is D01320827

The company did send someone out, and sent a replacement part.  It was just as sharp as the first one.  They denied the part was defective, and then we were contacted by their attorneys.  We got tired of the phone calls and said forget everything.

WE do not think ours is the only drawer with a sharp edge, and someone may get seriously injured.  The edge is sharp like a knife blade.
justification: Three family members were cut by the sharp edge, indicating injury, and the issue persists despite replacement parts.

incident_description: Whirlpool Microwave model # GH5184XPQ-3   serial # TRT 0811655 -4.5 years old -did spark inside-smell of burning wire and now does not work/heat. Contacted Whirlpool Supervisor  [REDACTED]/customer service /MI office. [REDACTED] did not care about how unsafe there product was, only that I was out of WARRANTY and that Whirlpool  would not repair or replace product.
justification: The microwave sparked and emitted a burning smell but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: While my Whirlpool Refrigerator with Bottom Drawer Freezer (model #GB2SHDXTS) was running normally, it began to smell heavily outside of the fridge of burning/melting plastic.  Upon further inspection, a plastic covering on the temperature control board had melted including some of the plastic wall panels of the fridge.  There are burn marks on the ceiling and on the temperature control panel.  After removing the temp control panel, the smell still persisted.  Completely removed the temp control panel to outside of the house and the internal portion of the refrigerator still smelled of melted plastic.  After at least two hours of leaving the temp control panel outside of the fridge and airing it out, the fridge still smells of burnt plastic.  It makes us concerned about putting food back in the fridge because of the toxins that may be in the air inside of the fridge.  I have found no other complaints about this phenomenon with this model, so I am submitting this report to hopefully help others.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and burn marks, posing a potential health risk but no reported injury or death.

incident_description: I've been having many problems with drainage with respect to my Maytag Dishwasher, Model No. MDBD820AWW.  Water drains on the floor not thru hoses.  The motor also sparks when in use and it has a burning smell.  I'm afraid t use it!
justification: The dishwasher has a drainage issue and sparks with a burning smell, posing a risk of property damage and potential injury if used.

incident_description:
I contacted Comsuner Product Safety Commission last year because I was very concerned about the safety of my electric range. The oven door is not flush against the oven causing a 9/16" gap from top of door to top of oven and a 11/16th gap at the side of the door. This seems to get worse when the oven is being used. If something in the oven caught on fire, it would not be confined and could cause a fire in the kitchen/house. I first contacted Whirlpool on 1/13/09 complaining I was unable to use auto clean and the code F5EO came up. They told me this indicated the door and switches do not agree and to follow directions indicated in the manual. This worked for a while but then I noticed the over door seemed to be dropping away from the oven itself. I contacted Whirlpool again on10/12/10 with my concern about the safety of the oven door not being flush against the oven to the point where the oven light comes on even with the door closed. Since I did not purchase the extended warranty, the were not concerned.
In  my opinion, this is a manufacture design default and seems to center on the hinges of the oven door. The only way the oven light goes off when the oven is being used is to pull the oven door up and push the oven door in, but the door drops down again and the oven light comes on after a short time. I am sure I am not the only one having this problem with this electric range!
justification: The description indicates a potential safety hazard with the oven door not sealing properly, which could lead to a fire, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
First of all I saw the Black Jenn-Air cooktop on the Internet, but could not find a dealer locally that had the product in stock.  So I ordered the cook top unseen from a dealer in Dallas, TX.  The internet page showed the grid somewhat better than it really is. 
However, you are unable to see the grid that is on the cook top that tells you what level of power, i.e.lo, hi, and number, that you are cooking on.  The grid is grey on black when I think it should be white on black, based on other black cook tops that I have seen.  You can barely see the grid only if you look at it in an awkward way, i.e. standing directly over the grid, or turning your head in an un-normal position.
My wife has misused the cook top several times due to not being on the right power level. This has resulted in what she is cooking boiling over or burning.  She is only 5' tall, so it is very awkward for her to use. I consider this cook top a safety hazard because, 1) you cannot be sure of the level of power you are cooking on, 2) something boiling over could get into the controls, because the controls are flat on the surface of the cook top, which I think could possibly cause a fire, or an electrical short, or destroy the controls.
I have worked with the dealer, Jenn-Air customer service, & the corporate office for the past year.  The final results from the corporate office, is that this is the way the cook top is designed & nothing can be done about it.
justification: The incident involves misuse of the cooktop leading to boiling over or burning, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
the microwave oven started to operate without being programmed. consumer cancelled operation. 
the unit was hot.
justification: The microwave operated unexpectedly but was stopped without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: I noticed my GE coffee maker not pulling water through and when I examined the pot, the plastic under the water heating mechanism was melted and the maker was extremely hot.
justification: The coffee maker malfunctioned, causing melting and excessive heat, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Whirlpool Single wall oven
Model:  RBS305PD12

while cooking french fries the oven switched from cooking mode into cleaning the oven and locked and would not unlock.  We had to shut the circuit breaker off.  After turning the circuit breaker back on the oven automatically started up again in cleaning mode.  We could not shut off except by the ciruit breaker.
justification: The oven malfunctioned and locked in cleaning mode, requiring circuit breaker intervention, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Sears Oven/When you pull rack from oven out, the rack falls.

Gas range was purchased March 2008 & no problems were had with it until Thanksgiving 2010.
Callers were pulling 12 lb turkey out of oven when the rack dropped.
Caller's contributed this first incident with possible user error and not to any range issues.
Believes that they may have cleaned the oven using self cleaning mode before Thanksgiving but isn't positive.
Caller was able to save turkey.
SinceThanksgiving they have noticed that if they use the self cleaning mode then afterward the racks drop out when user is attempting to retrieve food.
The most recent incident this caller has had was 04/24/2011 when he was baking scalloped potatoes and ham, pulled rack out to retrieve food and rack dropped.
Although caller was able to save meals with all incidents he is aware that he or his wife could have been scalded.
This last time the caller inspected the oven and noted that if he pushed the rack to one side it would just fall out posing a severe burn hazard if not caught.
Oven has three racks, they have been using only two so he grabbed the rack that they have NOT been using to see if the racks themselves were adjusting in size but the 3rd rack also fell.
Caller would like this gas range inspected and recalled before there is a senseless and possibly severe burn hazard to one or more consumers.
He would like his range replaced by manufacturer at manufacturer expense.
Caller has investigated online and states there appears to be an ongoing problem.
justification: The incident involves a rack falling out of the oven, posing a severe burn hazard, though no injuries have occurred yet. The issue is recurring after self-cleaning, indicating a likely and ongoing risk.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Elite range with a flat cooktop. The left front burner turns itself on and off. This has happenend multiple times. I called and there is a recall for this problem but not on my model.
justification: The burner turning on and off unexpectedly is an incident with no reported injury, and it has happened multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: The light bulbs in my refrigerator failed to turn off.  The bulb housing melted and sagged, the roof of the refrigerator has bubbled, and the bulb sockets appear scorched.  It appears the manufacturer is aware of this problem, but did not notify me.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted housing, bubbled roof, scorched sockets) but no injury or death, and the manufacturer's awareness suggests it is a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
Toaster oven is about 1 year old in good, clean condition. Turned oven on, like always, rotating the control timer knob to approx 20 minute position. After 3-5 min the oven began to arc internally behind the control panel area. Smoke and fire could be seen coming from the unit. I noticed immediately and unplugged unit from wall but fire persisted internally behind the control panel. 

Removed unit from house and fire eventually extinguished itself inside the unit.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the toaster oven but was promptly addressed without injury or death.

incident_description: the lights on the inside of the fridge did not turn off causing the inside to become very hot and melting the plastic light housing and the top of the fridge
justification: The incident caused damage to the fridge and its components but no injury or death was reported.

They said they were aware of the issue and that the authorized repair people could fix the problem. I hope that this wiring issue has not resulted in any fires or injuries to others. I have an authorized repairman coming tomorrow to fix the issue with my appliance. Thanks

Cuisinart 12-Cup Coffee Maker DCC-1200 Serial #00624 h

The coffee maker had recently finished brewing and was plugged in. It started crackling and popping with smoke rising out the back and bottom. It smelled like burning plastic. I unplugged it and ran it outside where I doused it in water to cool it.

I was completly shocked by what happened after all I thought this stuff was made for baking!

incident_description: GE microwave went on fire. this is the second one to do this. GE replaced the first one, but the same thing happend with the same model,  a metal plate on the side of the microwave went on fire.  then it started to make a loud noise like it was going to blow up.

incident_description:
We have a GE Profile dishwasher which caught on fire May 4th. We immediately cut off the circuit breaker. The house was filled with white toxic smoke and electrical fire smell  that took two  and half or three days to get out even with the windows open, and fans on.  The top of the dishwasher is black, gray and yellowish brown from all the smoke.  

GE sent someone over Friday, May 6th. He took off the backside of the dishwasher door and he said the wires were corroded due to us living on the Intracoastal Waterway. (We live in the Charleston, SC area)and there is salt in the air.  He also said that if it gets above 76 degrees in the house that could cause humidity which could be the cause as well.  He said he could repair it, but not replace it.   Inside,the area behind the control panel looks like the hollowed out portion of half a coconut without the white part in it.  The front panel also has a yellowish brown melted in spot on the exterior of the machine where the controls are, in addition to the black gray and yellowish brown area all over the top of the dishwasher door. 

One would think that instead of the area of the country we live in being the problem, loose seals on the dishwasher door around the electrical area would be the probable source  of the problem. Also, I noticed on line that [REDACTED} sells a salt product for consumers to put in their dishwashers to soften the water. How GE's competitor  could put salt directly into their dishwasher, and yet living  on the coast is a safety hazard according to GE is beyond me.  

Also, in regards to the humidity, how hot and humid is it inside a dishwasher? 

We feel unsettled having an appliance that has caught on fire "fixed". We believe they should replace it.  After all, this appliance has already had one fire.

I have received a run around from GE. The repairman said that only the Customer Service could authorize a replacement, and they will not do so.  The Customer service person I spoke to said she could not order a replacement either, and I have yet to speak to someone who can. 

GE is suggesting popping in  a new circuit board into this  dishwasher instead of replacing it. Is that an acceptable and safe remedy?
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing toxic smoke and damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: A new GE Dishwasher turns the heat element on by its self.  The first time we unplugged it and called the service as it was under warrenty.  They replaced a module in the door and said it should be fine.  Two nights later it turned on again and I smelled something like some one was cooking at 4:00 AM.  I got up to check and the dishwasher had turned on again and was hot enough to melt a nylon cutting board that was on the bottom rack.  I unplugged the washer and called the GE service department.  They are sending a service man out to check what went wrong.  If we had not been here I am afraid that it would have caused a fire.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned and caused damage to a cutting board, but no injury or fire occurred. The issue has happened twice, indicating a possible recurring problem.

incident_description:
KitchenAid dishwasher MODEL # KUDP01FLBT5
In service for approximately 5 years with no problems prior to this incident.

Black smoke and burning plastic smell filled house. Upon returning home within a half an hour after dishwasher was started, we found smoke and arcing coming from dishwasher control panel. I immediately turned off the dedicated circuit breaker.  After opening the windows to clear the smoke, I disassembled the front panel and found the electronic control assembly AP3775964 badly burned, wire connectors to this board melted, and plastic housing burned and partly melted.  Also, the user interface AP3177796 was blackened and partly burned along with the fuseable link.  

My question is: Why didn't the fuseable link within the dishwasher disconnect the power upon this severe electronic failure?

I looked at replacement parts costs, totaling more that $175, and found that Whirlpool (maker of KitchenAid) replaced the fuseable link with a "fuse kit" AP3178588. This kit has the installer relocate the fuseable link to lower location in the dishwasher.  Was this a known problem with this unit that caused my incident?
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the dishwasher and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Our Kitchenaide Over the range microwave (Model# KHMS155LSS-4) turned on by itself !!! I returned from work today to find our microwave running by itself with nothing in it.....A MAJOR FIRE HAZARD!!!!  The keypad was unresponsive and the only way to stop it was to open the door and unplug it from the power source.  I quickly went online to discover that hundreds, if not thousands of others have reported this same problem.  I then checked if there were any recalls issued for this product, and there were not any that I could find.

*** Then I talked to Whirlpool (the parent company of Kitchenaide), and they were very responsive, admitted to being aware of the problem, and agreed to parts and labor at no charge.  In fact, the repair is scheduled for only 4 days from now and the part is being FedEx'ed directly to me.

*****Most important, they indicated that it is NOT a fire hazard, since there is a built-in auto-shutoff feature that will trigger if the unit becomes too hot.  I would not personally want to test this capability in my home, but it offers some degree of re-assurance.

Call Whirlpool Safety Department in Michigan at [redacted]
justification: The microwave turned on by itself, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred. The manufacturer acknowledges the issue and has safety measures in place.

incident_description: Kitchen Aid slide in gas range model # KGSA906ps won't turn off...needs a new switch membrane.  After troubleshooting this online, it is extremely common for Kitchen Aid and Maytag ranges to have this problem yet they take no initiative in recalling the product or making changes to the switch membrane.
