incident_description: KitchenAid Double Gas Range Model #KGRS505XSS01, Serial # D10949212 was purchased in February 2011.  Burner knobs are located on front panel of range and do not have a push in to turn feature.  With the slightest motion, lean up to use microwave, even walking past, knobs turn on letting gas escape.  This has occurred at least a dozen times already.   Today I returned home to a gas filled home after several hours and realized 2 of the knobs were turned AGAIN.  I hate to think of the explosion that could have occured had a light switch been turned on there was a spark.  Upon looking on-line, there are numerous complaints of same hazardous problem.  I contacted KitchenAid this afternoon and was told "most ranges are made that way today, it can not be fixed, it is how the range was manufactured."  This is an unacceptable response from KitchenAid and a horrific danger.  I have older children who are always in the kitchen and have instructed them to stay away from the range, I can not imagine what could happen with very small children in the house.  There is absolutely no lock feature for the knobs.  Can you please help me?
justification: The incident has caused gas leaks, which could lead to explosions, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
We have, well HAD an 18 pc. set of Cutco knives. We've had them for at least 8 years and never had a problem like we just experienced. In fact, they are/were seemingly great (although pricey) kitchen knives, durable, did a great job, etc.
Two days ago, they inexplicably went up in flames. My husband lit a [REDACTED] candle (small, votive) near the knife set and placed the candle on the counter about 4 inches away from said knife set. He went upstairs and no more than a few minutes later, the fire alarm went off. Our six month old baby was asleep in her swing not far from the kitchen. My husband runs downstairs to see what is going on and the knife set is in a full on blaze. He was able to pick it up with some towels and throw it out into the yard, burning one of his fingers in the process. Once he was sure the baby was fine and nothing else was on fire, he went back outside and extinguished the fire with the water hose. Afterward, we immediately saw that the counter as well as one nearby cabinet were scorched/bubbled, thus ruined. 
I called the Cutco corporation this morning to tell them what happened. They said there is no way that a votive candle burning a few inches away could have caused that. I said yeah I know, there is NO logical explanation, which is what really scares us and why I called. [REDACTED] I told them if that were the case and there was a logical explanation as to why it happened, I wouldn't have called. I was calling because they seemed to have caught on fire for no reason whatsoever. I also told them I Googled "Cutco flammable" and found several websites that noted the following:
[REDACTED]
I mentioned this to the rep, saying of course I take what I read on the internet with a grain of salt unless from an absolutely reliable source, but the fact that this verbiage was mentioned on so many websites, well... I felt it was worth mentioning. She said she has never heard of such a thing and likely the postings of disgruntled consumers. (Uh, maybe a consumer whose knives caught on fire?)
She then said if we file an insurance claim and send them the paperwork, they'll be glad to sell us another set at 50% off retail. Wow. I told her I'm not looking for free or discounted knives (especially flammable ones), I simply felt I needed to report this to them because it could have had a MUCH worse ending than it did and (I thought) they needed to know. Thank God no one was badly hurt. We have a gas stove and I think of all the times I've used the turning/carving forks while cooking - yikes.
She didn't even ask me for my contact information and ultimately referred to the situation as a probable "user error". I was dumbfounded.
My guess: The candle "spit" if you will and a very small but hot particle landed somewhere on one of the knife handles, starting the fire. There is absolutely no other logical explanation and if that is in fact what caused it (which we'll probably never know) I hope someone takes a closer look at what these handles are made of. Very frightening.
Thanks for your time.
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (burned finger) and property damage, but no severe harm or death. The occurrence likelihood is rare given the unusual and unexplained nature of the event.

incident_description:
While fixing dinner today 5/10/11, I was using my Kenmore Self-Cleaning Electric Range model #665.9502210, Ser#RL1110117. I used the oven, set at 350. After 10 minutes I noted the food was burning, removed it, and turned the oven off. I prepared other items, we had dinner, then prepared to leave for soccer practice. My 9 yr old daughter brushed against the front door of the range and told me it was hot. The entire stove was blister hot to the touch and the top broiler element inside the oven was glowing red. The oven was off and had been for an hour. I wrapped wet towels around the oven door handle and pulled the device away from the wall. The sides and back of the range were also blister hot. I unplugged the power and the oven took nearly 3 hours to cool down. I tried to plug it back in and with the oven still off, the elements was glowing red hot again in under 5 minutes. I unplugged the device. Had not my daughter been burned, I have no doubt that we would have experienced a house fire had we gone on to soccer practice.

I checked for recalls or other related incidents on the web and noted that this model electric range was not included on any current recall. SEARS has a serious problem here and needs to expand the product recall to include all electric ranges.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that caused burns to a child and posed a significant fire hazard, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: The CPSC recall 09-333 should be expanded to include our Kenmore electric stove, model 790.9401 2600, purchased new from Sears in late 2006.  As with the smoothtop stoves in the recall, two of this model's four heating elements turn themselves all the way up to MAX after about five minutes regardless of how low you set the dial, which renders them useless for cooking (they burn everything), as well as a potential fire hazard.  This has been a problem since a year or two into our ownership.
justification: The stove's heating elements malfunctioning poses a potential fire hazard and renders them useless for cooking, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Dear Consumer Commission,  I purchased a GE Hotpoint Range Serial Number RB757BH5WH in Greenville South Carolina for my Mother in Law in November 2009.   The warranty has expired, but two days ago the glass door exploded and cause bodily injury to my Mother in Law.  She had to be treated at emergency center at a local hospital.   The range was purchase at Home Depot, my concern is not have this product repaired but totally replaced in lieu of the warranty expiration.   This is not a wear and tear issue but a life safety issue based on what appears to be faulty appliances, please advise what can we do?   I reported the incident to GE and they have agreed to send a technical representative to inspect the oven range and repair if possible and/or completely replace it.    I personally feel that this product should be totally replaced, it has already exploded and replacing the oven door does not address the reason for the previous combustion.
justification: The glass door exploded causing bodily injury requiring emergency treatment, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) based on the description of the incident as a rare event.

incident_description: I was called to investigate a fire in my capacity of Code Enforcement Officer for my Town.  I found that a dishwasher had caught fire while in use.  The damage to the home was minor, but the dishwasher was substantially destroyed.  There was no harm to any of the residents.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire causing minor damage to the home and substantial destruction to the dishwasher, but no harm to residents.

incident_description:
Kenmore Electric Range - Model Number 790.9656.9602, S/N VF73538269
The stove top came on without the switch being on and caused a fire.  I called Sears and they refused to fix it as they claim my serial number is not covered by the recall: http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml09/09333.html

Please keep in mind this is the exact same problem as described in the recall, but not a listed model and serial number.  This is a huge fire/safety hazard as the stove top is hot with the switch off.
justification: The stove top turning on without the switch being on caused a fire, which is a significant safety hazard, though no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Cooking on a Kenmore Elite Range Model # 790.97473805 - Turned on the right eye on the stovetop and the right and left eye came on.    Later the same day 2 more incidents - right eye came on without being turned on and all eyes were on cooking and suddenly the stovetop cut off and all the lights began flashing a code.  Worried about the fire hazard so cut off the breaker to the stove.
justification: The stove malfunctioned multiple times, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
A Sears Kenmore Elite Refrigerator Model 795.77543600 that I installed about 2 years ago.
The interior lights could not be turned off by the door switches and burned the plastic light sockets and housing.  The lights generated enough heat to warm up the refrigerator and spoil the food.  There was a burning smell in the refrigerator.   I did a quick search on the internet and found this is a common problem.  Sears apparently will not make this right since the warentee has expired.  I believe this to be a safety issue as it may have caused a fire.  A very poor design.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burned plastic, spoiled food) and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a product called the Luau Food Tent at Dollar Tree.  It is like a small square umbrella, made of mesh, used to cover plates of food outside.  It opens and closes with a mechanism similar to an umbrella.  My son, who is nine, opened the tent with the inside facing him.  The metal broke where one of the struts was connected another metal wire inside, and the strut popped out scratching him across the nose and cheek.  The tent had only been used once before.  He was not handling it roughly.  The scratch was deep enough to develop a scab.  It could easily have hit him in the eye.  This is why I am reporting this product.  I knew they were not sturdy and that I would only be able to use them a few times - but the metal actually snaps and does so while under tension.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep scratch that developed a scab, indicating an injury, and the product's failure could have caused more severe harm.

incident_description:
A cup of coffee in a to go cup from Flying Star resteraunt was placed in the microwave to reheat. The cup started on fire. Luckily it was caught before major damage was done.

The cups should either be microwavable or marked not to use in the microwave.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was caught before major damage or injury occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with proper labeling.

incident_description:
I purchased a Black & Decker Countertop Oven, Model # TR0480BS on 7/5/10 from Sears in North Attleboro, MA. In 8/10, while cooking a piece of dry toast, the oven burst into flames. If someone had not been in the immediate area, we would have had a serious house fire. The unit was replaced on 8/25/10 by Black & Decker at no charge.

On 2/23/11, the replaced unit, Model # TR0480BS once again burst into fire while cooking dry toast. The Black & Decker representative said they would replace the unit with a $70 more expensive unit without hesitation. They told me it would take 3 to 4 weeks to receive the new unit. I received the new unit, Model #TR04075B on 2/26/11.
I would like to demand an investigation to see if a recall of the Black & Decker Countertop Oven, Model # TR0480BS is warranted before someone has a serious fire which results in possible loss of life. I believe these countertop ovens appear to be a serious fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved the oven bursting into flames, which could have led to a serious house fire if not for immediate intervention, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Consumer was using microwave to melt butter.  Unit started arcing, making a sound like an electrocution.  Butter in dish caught fire
justification: The incident involved arcing and a small fire in the microwave, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Just bought a new gas range from GE (model # JGBS19DENWW) over the internet, but when it was delivered, we discovered that the dials that control the top burners have a gap between "low" and "off" where the flame goes out. I don't know if gas is coming out in that zone, but even if it isn't, if you don't know that you've accidentally turned the dial even slightly below "low", you might turn the dial up a bit to, for example, simmer something, and unintentionally start a serious gas leak.

This could have a relatively simple solution---just put a stop at "low" that you'd have to click through to turn the burner off. 

However, I talked with a couple of people at GE who I'm sure have nothing to do with product design or fixes; don't know if my complaint will ever be heard where it would make a difference.

We're going to try to return the stove and buy another one; this kind of detail can't be seen on the internet. But this stove is, in our opinion, a safety hazard, and an unnecessary one (we've used gas ranges for 20 years and this is just the result of exceedingly poor design).
justification: The issue involves a potential safety hazard with the gas range design, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
After running the dishwasher in the evening, I discovered that it was still very hot inside 8 hours later. I closed it (making sure it was not turned on) and went on to doing other things.  About 5 hours later I noticed that it was still very hot inside.

The heating coil appears to still be putting out heat despite the fact the the front panel indicates that the dishwasher is off.

I am concerned because this model (Maytag mdbh965aww) was the subject of a recall notice last year (heating coil causing fires). While this particular unit was repaired by Maytag last year under the recall program, the overheating of the coil is a problem
justification: The dishwasher is overheating despite being off, which is a known issue from a previous recall, posing a fire hazard but no immediate injury.

incident_description: Yesterday (5/10) our Maytag MDB9100 dishwasher (Serial # 25419461ZH) caught on fire while no one was home.  The dishwasher was not turned on when I left the house.  My husband came home to smell acrid smoke in the house and evidence of smoke and fire on the front panel of the dishwasher (where the latch hooks into the door).  This is not one of the dishwashers that was part of Maytag's recent product recalls.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, causing smoke damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Consumer reports glass bakeware dish exploded while in use in the oven.  a female & her grangdaughter, age 5 were not injured.
justification: The glass bakeware exploded, but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My Kenmore model # 911.93712021 Oven range caught fire.  It was in the preheat mode with nothing in the oven and the oven was completely clean.  I turned around to find the burner/coil on fire inside the oven.  I had to use a fire extinguisher and call the fire dept to put out the fire.  I have found many complaints online about this same exact incident with the kenmore electric ovens.  They need to be recalled.  My house would have burned to the ground if I hadn't had a fire extinguisher.
justification: The oven caught fire, requiring a fire extinguisher and fire department intervention, indicating a significant hazard.

incident_description:
Bought new appliances from Sears for delivery to my n.y. condo. They where delivered december 30
2009. On november 5,2010 we used the self cleaning feature of the oven. After cleaning we found
that the exterior of the stove got so hot it melted the side of the cabinet next to it. I called sears the 
next day and they said they would send someone out.After much dancing around we where re-assigned to a adjuster, then re-assigned to Electrolux (which is the manufacturer), who then re-assigned us to their adjuster.After many months of run around,the claim was denied.
My questions are many. Number one why wasn't the stove replaced uder warranty? Numbertwo
why do we allow american companies to import far inferior products that are a definite safety
hazard.Obviously this stove is not safe and should be replaced.My claim is fair for all I want is
a new stove and the cabinet replaced.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted cabinet) but no injury or death.

incident_description: While warming dog's dinner, microwave started emitting much smoke.  Smoke had the characteristics of an electrical fire (I am a retired Navy officer with substantial engineering and damage control experience).  Disconnected power and moved microwave to the driveway.  Checked the electrical socket with a meter to ensure the problem was with the oven and not the house power.
justification: The incident involved smoke emission from a microwave, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The circular unit in the top center of the microwave caught on fire while in use.  The microwave had been on less than a minute.  The circular unit melted on the right side, dripping the plastic onto the bottom of the microwave.  After putting out the fire you can see mettle exposed.  Whirlpool has been contacted and they said it was our fault, due to the popcorn that was being popped.  I am very concerned with there answer.  If I was not downstairs and if I did not hear a weird, loud popping noise who knows how much damage would have been caused to my house or family.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the microwave with no reported injuries, but potential for significant damage if unnoticed.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while she was in the kitchen she heard a loud explosion and she noticed that there was smoke coming from the rear of refrigerator, her spouse immediately powered it off from the circuit breaker, it was removed from the wall to unplug it and she noticed that the plug was charred. The refrigerator was unplugged to prevent further damages.

4/8/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised that it was not a part of the recall.

Consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a loud explosion and smoke from the refrigerator, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I have a Samsung refrigerator RS2630SH.

Originally a loud noise was coming from the back of the refrigerator on an irregular basis.
The refrigerator stopped making the loud noise but the dividing wall heats up to extremely hot temp. Also the freezer side outside wall is very hot to touch. Ice maker does not work as well. 

I am afraid the unit is going to catch on fire and burn the house down.  Upon moving the unit, it has water standing behind it, causing the flooring to lift.
justification: The refrigerator's overheating and potential fire hazard pose a risk of injury or property damage, though no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: lights in top of refrigerator will not turn off even when refrigerator is closed.  lights burned all day. when we returned to home in the afternoon, smelled burning smell.  found it was coming from refrigerator.  lights were so hot, they had melted the plastic cover surrounding them and light sockets had turned brown.  top shelf of refrigerator was so hot, all food on it had to be thrown away. called Sears and spoke to [REDACTED]. [REDACTED] stated I would have to pay a service charge just for a technican to come out to see if my refrigerator is involved in a recall.  I commented that Sears has manufactured a product that is unsafe; the defect in these refrigerators can cause a fire and injure/kill someone.  I asked does Sears not "care about its customers".  [REDACTED] replied Sears is a corporation; it doesn't have feelings.  Sears is not going to do anything about this problem unless it is mandated to.  I urge everyone affected to report this unsafe product.
justification: The incident caused property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Cuisinart Griddler GR-4N has removable top and botom grill plates.  After pre-heating per the manufacturer directions, when I opened the lid the upper grill plate fell off.  The clips, which appear to be some sort of plastic, had melted.   The grill plate,which was now extremely hot,fell out of the unit onto the the kitchen counter.  Fortunately, neither I nor the counter top were hurt nor burnt by the falling grill plate. 

When I contacted Conair Corporation regarding this product failure, they seemed completely disinterested.  This product comes with a three-year warranty but was only in use for eight months.   They were willing to look at the unit, and maybe send me a new one, if I paid for shipping both ways.  Until this incident, I was unaware that Conair Corporation, the manufacturer of Cuisinart and many other household products had such a complete disregard for consumer safety.
justification: The incident involved a hot grill plate falling but no injuries or damage occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the product's design flaw and manufacturer's disregard for safety.

incident_description:
We purchased a Cuisinart Classic 12-Cup Programmable Coffee maker Model DCC-1100 Series in June of 2008.  This Coffee maker came with a three year guarantee. In January of 2011 the Coffee maker stopped working, so we contacted Cuisinart and paid $10.00 (plus an additional $14 for postage) to have the unit replaced. We received this new (?) unit on January 24, 2011. Last night, May 4, 2011, we ate dinner, then made a fresh pot of coffee. Within about a half an hour or so my granddaughter said she smelled something burning - it was mild for a few seconds, we immediately told her to go outside, and my husband and I looked for the source of the burning odor which was getting stronger by the seconds. As we got near the coffee maker it was clear that was the problem. My husband turned it off and immediately, unplugged the unit then took it out of the house. The coffee in the pot was close to boiling temperature. Thank God that we were in the next room and our granddaughter smelled it immediately or we would have had a serious fire. The strong burning odor in our home took over six hours to dissipate - with windows open, a ceiling fan and an exhaust fan running. I called the company and will deal with them as to replacing this with something safer, but I feel that the U S Consumer Product Safety Commission needs to look into this problem and possibly have the company recall the DCC-1100 Series Coffee makers. After talking with a company representative I looked online and was appalled at how many other consumers had the very same problem with this unit. (Actually consumers were complaining about some of CuisinartÃÂs other models as well - all with the heating plates - but the DCC-1100 was the one that had the most complaints) I am not satisfied at all dealing with their customer service supervisor and will pursue that, but the top priority is to have the USCPSC look into this and stop this company from just replacing units and not addressing the problem of this unsafe coffee maker. Peoples lives are in danger.  If we would not have been right there, if say my husband was sleeping and I took a shower, we would have had a fire! This happened last night at approximately 7:15 PM, and as IÃÂm writing this at 12:21 PM today I still have a sore throat from the strong burning smell.  Please, please address this problem because the next family may not be as lucky as we were. Thank you so much for your time. We look forward to hearing from you.


At this time the company is willing to replace the item. They have told me they would be calling me back this evening, May 5, 2011, 7:00 PM.  I would, however, like to be assured that this safety issue is investigated.  This is a definite safety hazard that must be addressed. 

I am not alone in having the problems with this fire hazard. The following is a web site that lists many complaints about the very same problem with the Cuisinart Model DCC 1100.

http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/cuisinart.html
justification: The incident involved a strong burning odor and potential fire hazard, causing a sore throat but no serious injury. Online complaints indicate this is a recurring issue with the product.

incident_description: The consumer says on 2 occasions an electrical burning smell has come out of unit and it stopped working.  The consumer says he contacted the manufacturer and they sent a technician who told him he needs replacement of control board, which was burnt in one area.  The consumer says that they offered no other remedy since the unit is not under warranty.  He also says the technician did not mention a safety concern with the product and just said eventually the unit would stop working if repair was not done.  The consumer says the website kitchenaidfire.com has numerous reports of units catching fire and pictures of hazardous dishwashers.  The consumer contacted the retailer and they also did not offer remedy.  Consumer is upset with manufacturer and retailer who have provided no assistance.  Consumer feels this product should be recalled and consumers should be offered a remedy.
justification: The incident involves a burnt control board and reports of potential fire hazards, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: Skybar wine opener exploded bottle while using to remove cork
justification: The explosion of a bottle while removing a cork can cause injury, but such incidents are relatively uncommon.

incident_description:
Spitfire Controls
451 Maple Avenue
Carpentersville, IL 60110-1939

Frigidaire Inc.
P.O. Box 212378
Martinez, GA 30917

Subject: Frigidaire Electric Kitchen Range Model FEFL78CQA Ser. No. VF3389120

I am writing to inform you of a defect in the above referenced Electric Range ÃÂ more specifically with the Spitfire Control SF5306 Rev D Model 316207509.

We were baking in our electric range oven on Feb. 13, 2011 when the circuit breaker blew.  Wondering why ÃÂ I reset it.  The range readout was normal ÃÂ said it was still baking.  We baked for  another 20 minutes and served dinner ÃÂ the readout said it was still heating.  When we next tried to use the oven on Feb. 15, 2011 ÃÂ the readout said the oven was preheating and we assumed all was well.  After about 10 minutes, we opened the oven door and it was cold.  Neither the baking element or the broiling element would heat.  I checked the voltage input to both elements and it read zero.  I used  an ohm meter and the elements were continuous.  I turned off the power ÃÂ opened up the back of the stove and removed the electronic oven control.  The enclosed pictures show the damage from the shorted board in the control.  The board on the left is clean because I rubbed it with my finger to see what caused the damage.  The damage on the right hand board is as produced by the short spraying material upon it.  

I was tempted to just repair the stove ÃÂ thought better of it and just bought a new one.  I checked your web site and our range has not been recalled.

It would appear to me that this control poses a significant risk of producing a fire.  I believe you owe it to the public and your customers to correct this situation immediately!


						Sincerely,
						
						[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range that could pose a fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: 2nd to 3rd degree burns from steam-pressured coffee pot that blew up.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd to 3rd degree burns, indicating an injury, but such occurrences are relatively uncommon.

incident_description:
cooking on range today and after turned it off indicator displayed HE but was apparent by red glow and tremendous heat that range was still on. had to turn unit off at breaker. several hours later flipped breaker on and element turned on again with control knob still in off position.

unit was serviced for recall approximately 18 months ago wherein serviceman came and placed electrical-looking tape on what we assume to have been a sensor.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that remained on despite being turned off, posing a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she filed a report about the electric range light staying approximatey 6 months ago, however, about 1 month ago the oven caught fire.  While she was using the oven at 350, she heard a beeping a noise and discovered that the broiler came on she could not turn off the unit and had to power it off from the circuit breaker. 
 
Consumer discard the unit because she felt that it pose a fire hazard.  She has not contacted the manufacturer because in her previous report about the light staying on she was assured by the manufacturer that there was no danger with that defect.
justification: The oven caught fire, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she opened the refrigerator and there was an odor of burnt plastic, then she noticed the plastic housing around the bulb had fallen down and was scorched.  

The light bulb was removed but she is not sure what could have caused this incident.  The refrigerator was left plugged in.

Consumer is concern that this is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a burnt plastic odor and scorched housing, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Amana self cleaning oven Model #ACF3325AS, Serial # 11928527CN, purchased in 2003.
I've used the self cleaning feature 3 times. The first time the oven igniter broke, (after 1 year) the last two times, (in 2008 & 2011) the plastic gasket inside the oven door melted emitting a terrible gas odor lasting for days. 
When the igniter broke I called the Maytag consumer safety department and was told they would cover the cost of the technician and labor but not the part, I paid $150 for the part.  The second time I called in 2008 to say the gasket melted to the oven door and I was very concrned that the odor was a health hazard. They said it was not. I asked if other consumers reported similar issues and was told no, no one reported anything like this. The oven was not on recall and they could not do anything for me since it was out of warranty.  Concerned, I repeated I felt this was a safety issue, they said it was not. Cost of the gasket $70.  When the technician arrived he said Amana was sold to Maytag and they wouldn't back the product. I asked if he heard of this happening before, he said yes and suggested next time using a shorter cleaning cycle.
I cleaned the oven last week, running a shorter cycle and again the gasket melted emitting the same odor which took a few days with windows open to clear out. I've ordered the part again but decided to contact your agency becuase I really feel this is a problem.  It can't be good for people and pets to be breathing this in. Also, why should a part break every time a feature is used on the oven ?
Thanks so much for your consideration, appreciate any help you can offer.
justification: The incident involves a recurring issue with the oven's self-cleaning feature causing a melted gasket and gas odor, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
On Friday 22 April 2011 there was a fire in our Whirlpool dishwasher. I was in the kitchen when I noted smoke coming from the machine. I immediately opened the door of the washer and the smoke generation ceased. There was a strong and persistent odor of burned plastic and/or insulation in he area. 

I found the product literature that came with the machine, and as directed in the literature I telephoned [REDACTED]. I talked with a representative named "[REDACTED]" who took information on the situation and then transferred me to a person named "[REDACTED]" (who later gave me his direct line as [REDACTED])

I gave both [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] the details on the dishwasher:
Whirlpool Gold
Model:  GU1200XTKQO
Serial:    FM2047879
purchased June 2002

[REDACTED] pointed out that the machine was out of warranty, but agreed to pay for a repairman to inspect the machine. He arranged for a person from Quaker City Service Co in Philadelphia [REDACTED] to call on me the next business day (25 April 2011). The repairman, called "[REDACTED]", examined the machine and reported that there had been a fire in the touchpad. To quote from [REDACTED]'s report, "needs touchpad and control due to fire in D/W".  [REDACTED] estimated the repair at $300+. I stated that I would not have the machine repaired because of my concern about the fire. He replaced the controls, wrote up his report (referenced above), and left after about 40 minutes.

[REDACTED] called my home on 26 April, but I missed him. We connected on 28 April and discussed the implications of the fire. He pointed out that the machine was out of warranty, and stated that there was no obligation on the part of Whirlpool to do anything further. He did admit that he would not expect a dishwasher to burst into flame even if out of warranty. I offered to remove and send the failed part to him, but he declined the offer. I subsequently did remove the fire damaged hardware for possible future inspection by other interested parties.

I am mystified by the unconcern shown by [REDACTED] about the potentially deadly situation of a dishwasher catching fire. I cannot believe that burning up in place is an acceptable failure mode for a Whirlpool appliance. In defense of [REDACTED], I want to point out that he was always courteous, and he did arrange for the inspection of the equipment at his expense. My sense is that he has been instructed to stonewall complaints of this sort.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the dishwasher with no reported injuries, and such events are unlikely but not impossible.

incident_description:
We have made multiple complaints about our range handle getting dangerously hot. We have had three service technicians come out. All have indicated that the range in question does not have appropriate insulation but the handle is allowed to get to approximately 170 degrees and be acceptable. We do not agree and find this temperature excessive.

In addition, the technicians have verified side wall temperatures of the stove in excess of 130 degrees. We are concerned with a potential for damage or fire on the adjoining cabinets. 

Finally, Whirlpool has advised that they will not be doing anything to mitigate the concern even though the range is within the warranty period. 

We believe the range to be of inferior design and the dangers of burns to children or even unsuspecting adults is unacceptable.
justification: The description indicates a potential for burns (injury) due to excessively hot range handles and side walls, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Shortly after plugging the toaster into the wall outlet she placed the setting on the highest setting which was 7 then the two levers to lower the slots that would hold the toast was pressed. Within a matter of seconds the toaster got extremely hot to the touch.

She released the levers and allowed the unit to cool off. When it finally did she repackaged the toaster and placed it back into the box it came in. The toaster appears to be made out of stainless steel.

She did not attempt to use the toaster to prepare toast but was actually testing it out since it was going to be placed in an office setting. She has not contacted the manufacturer but will return it back to the retailer.
justification: The toaster got extremely hot but no injury occurred, and the issue was resolved by allowing it to cool and returning it.

incident_description:
March 30th, 2011 caller had been cooking soup with temperature for left front burner being used set at 8 for the initial first 5 minutes to bring water to a boil, turned knob to simmer once water was boiling but temperature did not go down, she turned knob to off but it wouldn't go off, temperature kept rising..

Caller's husband turned breaker off to turn range off & left it off for approximately 5 minutes to allow range to cool down, when breaker was turned back on the range began heating up again with knob still on off position, caller's husband turned breaker back off, waited about 5 minutes but still range heated up.
The third time that caller's husband turned the breaker off, the range stopped heating up while turned being off when he turned breaker back on.

They avoided using the left front burner after this incident.

Friday, April 8, 2011 around 1:00PM although range had not been used at all that day, caller was sitting at her kitchen table reading when she noticed that her range was making a tiny popping/hissing sound.

She walked over to the range felt heat on the left front burner noticing that it was not so hot that she couldn't just touch but if she had laid her hand on it she knows that it would have burned her hand.
She looked at the controls on the back of the range, the "hot surface" light was on. 
Caller's husband turned the breaker off, pulled the range out, removed the wires to the left front burner so that range could be used without fear.

Friday, April 16th, 2011 caller contacted the manufacturer after being advised by her sister that she should call to inquire whether her range was recalled, was informed  that it was not but that manufacturer rep would call a repair shop for her to obtain repair at caller's expense.  (She didn't obtain name of the manufacturer rep).

Caller would like to have this range investigated, recalled and would request that she obtain repair at manufacturer expense or reimbursement for repair if she had already paid for it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning range that could have caused burns but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that her self standing electric Kenmore range is unsafe. She has a selfstanding glasstop stove that the left front burner will not turn itself or when turned on at a desired setting it exceeds that setting. When it wouldn't turn off the stove was on for 20 seconds. The indicator light for the stove that exhibits a burner in use was off eventhough the burner was clearly on. She had the front two burners on at the time; set at medium. She spoke to the manufacturer yesterday, spoke to representative and was informed that there were recalls on similar models but not hers. They then offered her the number to CPSC. She has yet to call the retailer and noticed no damage to the product with the exception to the left front switch. The issue is limited to the range. She had the switch for the left front burner replaced yesterday. The part number was 316436001. She wanted to express her experience with this product.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning stove burner that could pose a safety risk, but no injury or damage was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stopped using his dishwasher because the heating element was overheating melting the bottom of the racks and started to smoked.
Consumer said that his dishwasher is not under any recall, but CPSC should pursue an investigation on his model and serial number, because his dishwasher poses the exact same problem as the one on recall.
Consumer called and explained incident to mfrÃÂs rep., (name unknown), who arranged to have service technician visit consumerÃÂs home at consumerÃÂs expense.  Consumer did not accept the offer.
Mr. Mfr. also refer consumer to report to issues to CPSC.

Consumer feels that his dishwasher could pose a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved overheating and smoking, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the issue is similar to a recalled model.

incident_description: We have had a Sears Kenmore Refrigerator for several years and it has function flawlessly.   The model # is 10653632300, serial # SP3361010.  On 2/28/2011, the refrigerator starting making a loud buzzing sound which was quickly followed by billowing electrical/burnt plastic smelling smoke filling up our kitchen and then the rest of our 1st floor.  I rushed the kids out of the house, grabbed a fire extinguisher and tried to pull the fridge out of the wall and pull the plug on it.  I was successful and could see charred bottom layer on the back of the unit.  After the plug was pulled, the fridge stopped smoking and we opened all doors and windows to air out the house. We called Sears immediately and they transferred to me to multiple persons who were less than helpful. They did schedule to have a technician come out on 3/2/2011 who indicated that the source of the fire was that the relay shorted and melted to the compressor. I have pictures if needed. I called Kitchen Aid, was on the phone for over an hour and was told I could have their repair service fix the glass but would be at my cost because the oven is out of warranty.  No concern from them regarding the fact that this is an extremely unsafe situation.  I'm very concerned in the safety now of using this oven because there are vents under the oven and glass "powder" and chips have gotten into that space.  The oven has a circulating fan that comes on and I'm not able to clean this area without taking the oven apart and my concern is that this glass could be circulated throughout the oven when I use it.  Reading online there are many entries from people that this has happened to and some people have been injured.  This company has to be forced to come up with a better design and material to use, seems to me the glass isn't able to withstand the high temperatures of the cleaning cycle.  There also is nothing in the manual that indicates this could be a problem.  Is it going to take somebody loosing an eye or God forbid a small child getting hurt before this situation gets the attention of someone?  If I had known of the potential dangerous situation here, I would have used Easy-Off oven cleaner.

incident_description:
I purchased a Sharp R420LK microwave oven from Amazon in May 2010 to replace a malfunctioning Sharp microwave oven that I had for over 5 years.
The 420 model oven is made with a mica waveguide cover on the inner surface of the oven that covers the microwave generator. This cover is the major weak point of this oven.
There is a warning on page 8 of the oven's manual that states: Keep the waveguide cover clean. Food residue can cause arcing and/or fires.
At some point when the family was using the oven, some food spatter landed on the waveguide cover and was not noticed by anyone.  Subsequent uses of the oven caused the spot of food spatter to burn a hole in the waveguide cover so that the next use of the oven resulted in much sparking in the oven.
I took the oven to a Sharp authorized servicing facility on 1/3/11 and it took Sharp two months to tell me that they would replace that oven with a refurbished same model.  I picked up the refurbished model on March 1, 2011.
Last night, I heated up two frozen Teriyaki Chicken Breasts for dinner in an open Pyrex dish without any cover.  Evidently, during the cooking cycle, a spatter landed on the waveguide cover unbeknown to us.  Later, my daughter placed a snack pack of popcorn in the oven to cook it & the oven started shooting electricla discharges inside the oven - sort of like seeing discharges of lightning occur.  The cooking was stopped & a spatter was noticed on the waveguide cover plate.  It was cleaned and then the oven performed normally.

I have owned various makes of microwave ovens for 35 years.  The original lasted for 15 years before it was replaced.  Later models also worked for several years before being replaced.  This Sharp unit (R420LK) is the first one, and the only brand, that I have found to have a mica waveguide cover.  I have never had any problems with arcing or waveguide covers in all my previous experiences with microwave ovens.  I have used microwave ovens at various worksites that had not been cleaned in awhile and they did not do any arcing inside the oven.

I believe that the mica cover that Sharp uses make the oven a definite safety hazard unless the oven is kept very clean to remove any food spatters that might land on the cover.  They also use the same material on other model waveguide covers.  This is the last Sharp microwave oven I will ever purchase because of the use of an inferior material inside the oven as a cover over the waveguide.
justification: The incident involved electrical discharges and potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
A few weeks ago I loaded my Kenmore elite dishwasher, filled the tray with detergent, closed the door and pushed the "smart wash" cycle. The dishwasher turned on and began washing. I walked out of the kitchen and down the hall to visit with my husband. We had been talking for 5 or 10 minutes, when I heard a strange clicking noise coming from the kitchen. I walked back toward the kitchen to check out the sound and the kitchen was filling with smoke. As I got close to the dishwasher I could see sparks coming out of the side of the front control panel. I yelled for my husband and he came running. He opened the door to the dishwasher hoping that would stop the dishwasher from running. It did not. The dishwasher continued to run and sprayed water all over the floor. He closed the door to the dishwasher. The unit continued to smoke and spark. I began looking for the fire extinguisher and he ran out to the garage. The dishwasher began to flame. I was pretty panicked. [REDACTED] found the breaker to the dishwasher in the electrical panel in the garage and flipped the switch off. As soon as he did that the dishwasher stopped running and the flame, spark and smoke stopped. We were so relieved. We wondered what would have happened to our home if we had started the dishwasher and then left. Would our house have caught fire? 

The next day we were scheduled to leave out of town on a spring break vacation trip to Texas. Upon arriving back home I called Sears to report the problems with the dishwasher. They seem less than concerned. I asked if there was a "product safety department" within Sears that I could talk to about my experience. They said there was not.

Sears initially told me that  my dishwasher was under a "recall" and that I should have received notice of that. I had not been notified. I have since learned that this particular model is not under recall, but a similar model with a plastic tub liner is. (My dishwasher has a stainless steel tub). We have learned that there is a "service flash" #22-754R2 for this dishwasher due to problems with the control panel and the heating element. 

Further inspection of the unit reveals that there is a "thermal fuse" built into the control panel in case of overheating, but this units fuse never did blow, even though the unit caught fire. I believe this dishwasher is hazardous.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher malfunction causing smoke and sparks, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

While serving, we realized all burners were on even though we had not used all of the burners.  Then smoke began coming out of the knobs at the back of the cooktop. incident_description:
Kitchen Aid Dishwasher:

ModelÃÂ  KUDSO1FLSS1

SNÃÂ ÃÂ ÃÂ  FP1919207

ÃÂ PURCHASED top of the line inÃÂ  2003

At American TV in Appleton, Wisconsin


http://www.kitchenaidfire.com/


http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVl02Tz7_AA&feature=player_embedded#at=38




ÃÂ My Narrative:

Our dishwasher was finishing a normal cycle.ÃÂ  We began to smell the smoke of hot insulation.ÃÂ  The door of the dishwasher was opened to access the control panel.ÃÂ  The cancel button (thus, the stop button) was pressed and the door was shut.ÃÂ  However, the machine would NOT shut off.ÃÂ  The washer continued to run and continued to over heat and smell.

ÃÂ The power was cut off to the Dishwasher at the fuse box.

ÃÂ The Dishwasher was mounted under a counter top with wood on all sides.ÃÂ  The Dishwasher was removed on to a breezeway for inspection. Turning the Dishwasher upside down showed the area of over heating was the heating coil on the bottom of the Dishwasher used to heat the water to wash the dishes.ÃÂ  The bottom of the dishwasher has as layer of asphalt type material on the bottom.ÃÂ  The asphalt material had heated to the point that there were bubbles, as if the material was boiling.

By the time the Dishwasher was inspected, the material was warm, but not hot.ÃÂ  Nevertheless, there was the smell of burning insulation.  The specific location of the oder could not be determined.  However, something somewhere on the dishwasher had been hot enough to cause smoke and a burning smell.  There were no flames to be observed.

ÃÂ Nevertheless, it seems the control panel had failed.ÃÂ  Therefore, it too could have been a dangerous fire hazard.ÃÂ  However, it seems the heating unit continued to heat even though there was no water left in the boiler pan to heat.ÃÂ  Thus, if that were the case, the heater was heating ÃÂan empty boilerÃÂ.ÃÂ  The container, normally for water, had no water and the heating coil stayed on.ÃÂ  Since there was no short in the system, there seemed to be no working safety system, which monitored over heating of the pan with the heating coil.ÃÂ  Had we had not been home and the power not been shut off the to Dishwasher, it seems the asphalt bottom might well have caught on fire.ÃÂ  With wood on four sides of the area, the house may well have gone up in flames.ÃÂ  Of course, our dog also.

ÃÂ In addition to the over heating, it was evident the water pump on the bottom of the Dishwasher had been leaking for years.ÃÂ  This judgment is made, due to the very large build up of calcium/magnesium deposits all over the pump and below the pump.ÃÂ ÃÂ  

ÃÂ After, inspecting the faulty Dishwasher and feeling very lucky we were at home when the Dishwasher failed, I called Kitchen Aid the next day to report what I considered a serious safety issue.

1-800-422-1230.

ÃÂ Kitchen Aid seemed to be concerned that the safety issue was that, the Dishwasher could not be cut off by opening the door and pressing the cancel button.ÃÂ  Kitchen Aid rejected the idea the Dishwasher was a fire hazard. Though as one can see from above, there are a number of control panel fires, which have been reported.

ÃÂ I did not argue the point with Kitchen Aid.ÃÂ  However, I feel that normal house wiring is such that it will continue to supply the current without interruption to the heating coil.ÃÂ  I contend the heating coil or other parts over heated due to the fact of a control failure.   Control panel failure may have allowed the heating coil to stay on after all the water had been pumped out of the boiler pan of the Dishwasher and thus, over heat.  In any event, if one smells burning insulation from any source, one is sure the dishwasher is unsafe

ÃÂ Had there been a heat limit switch for protection from the coil's over heating that worked, the Dishwasher's heating coil would have shut off.ÃÂ  It did not shut off.ÃÂ  The question is whether the Dishwasher will cause a fire in the asphalt on the bottom of the machine.ÃÂ  If a fire will result due to over heating of the empty water boiler container, then the Dishwasher is a very serious hazard to life and property.ÃÂ  If the control panel was not functioning properly, there could have been a fire there, as others have reported.  Also, had there not been a place for the leaking water to drain away to the crawl space where the dishwasher was placed, there would have been serious damange to the floor under the dishwasher.  Needless to say, my dishwasher, while and expensive unit, was not a quality, safe product.

In looking up parts, I found that virtually all dishwashers use many of the same parts and the bulk of the dishwashers are made by the same company, regardless of the name on the dishwasher.
KitchenAid, Jennaire, Maytag, Ammana, Sears Kenmore, Whirlpool dishwashers are all manufactured by Whirlpool and have interchangeable parts.ÃÂ  Therefore, changing brands may not help in getting a safe one.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned, causing overheating and smoke, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is high given the described failure and potential for fire.

incident_description:
I have a maytag refrigerator model#mff2258ve, serial#ky3027730 which I purchased at Sears on 
8/9/09.  I started having problems with it shortly after the 1 year warranty expired.  The refrigerator would not stay cold and the freezer would go into overdrive with heavy frost building up and the blower constantly running.  I checked on-line to see if this was a problem with this model and found that others were having the same problem -- lots of others.  I unplugged the unit and removed everything for about a day to let it defrost completely and had to purchase a thermometer to keep check on the refrigerator temperature.  This seemed to work for about 2 months.  The same problem started again this past week and I basically went through the same process and again the temperature improved.  I checked the freezer yesterday morning and the panel to the rear looked clear (this is the area that would be covered with frost when the refrigerator temp would raise.)  About 2 hours later a member of my family entered the kitchen and could detect a very strong odor (she said it smelled like someone burned something in the microwave.)  She opened the refrigerator and it was filled with smoke.  She thought it seemed to be coming out of the top area of the refrigerator and said it was blowing out of the area where the light bulbs are located.  Needless to say she immediately called for help and someone unplugged the refrigerator and our kitchen filled with smoke.  Everything in the unit smelled like it had been through a fire. I did not see this unit on the recall list, but considering others have had the same initial problem I experienced, I am assuming this is a potential disaster waiting to happen.  If this had happened while we were sleeping it surely would have turned into a fire.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The problem is recurring and widespread among similar models, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: i shifted a cabinet beside a ge range. this resulted in an electrical shock and a noticeable spark coming from the range .this caused the circuit to shut down. On inspection i noticed that the problem was caused by an electrical wire that ran between the side panel and   a sharp inner edge , acting like a knife and cutting through the insulation of the wire. There is certainly a safety problem as the electrical shock could have caused serious injury and was frightening . The members of the household are afraid of using the range. There is a design flaw in this product in terms of the location of these electrical wires, also if the group of wires were bundled together or had had a sheath around them, size would have rendered it impossible for the wires to get wedged between the side panel. The site where the wire shorted is located at the top left  left  side panel where the wires lead to the controls.I have reported this incident to GE and they have arranged for a technician to look at the range tomorrow which is a quick response.
justification: The incident involved an electrical shock and a spark, which could have caused serious injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the design flaw and the immediate danger posed by the exposed wires.
