incident_description: At around 8:30AM I began my usual method of preparing tea.  I had successfully used this method about 6 times before with the same Pyrex measuring cup that I purchased on March 13, 2011.  I took out my 8-Cup Pyrex measuring cup out of the refrigerator, and began to wash it off in the sink.  I used hot water with soap and then cold water to rinse the measuring cup.  Then around 8:40AM I filled up my 1.7L tea kettle with water and put it on the stove setting the stove to High, simultaneously allowing the Pyrex measuring cup to dry.  When the tea kettle began to whistle at around 8:50AM, I placed the measuring cup on my Formica kitchen counter; I placed the tea bags into the measuring cup; and then I began to pour the hot water into the measuring cup with only the tea kettle in my right hand.  I was not holding the measuring cup at all.  Before I even filled the measuring cup a third of the way full, the tempered glass exploded directly onto my lower torso.  Unfortunately, I had just woken up so I was still in my pajamas with no socks on my feet.  First the bang from the explosion startled me so I dropped the tea kettle, hot water began to pour onto my tile floor and my bare feet lost traction causing me to slip.  My upper right arm fell onto the counter top where the glass shrapnel was still laying.  I was lacerated by a piece of the Pyrex glass by about 4 inches.  I had to be taken immediately to the Emergency Room and received a row of internal stitches along with 13 exterior stitches.  Luckily, the glass did not hit an artery or a tendon, which could have potentially been fatal or damaged the use of my right arm.  I will have a permanent scar from this incident.  I have digital photos of the exploded glass, the laceration after the first row of internal stitches were sutured, the laceration with the 13 stitches, and a burn that I received on my left arm.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring emergency medical treatment, including stitches, but no death or life-threatening condition occurred.

incident_description:
We own a Frigidaire smooth-top electric range model FEFL79GBA purchased in 2007. We have the following problems:

1) the surface heating element on the left front fails to turn off after being switched off; 2) heats to a different temperature, 3) turns on spontaneously without being switched on.

I called Frigidaire, and they said there is a recall for these problems but not this model.
justification: The range's heating element malfunctions pose a safety hazard but no injury is reported, indicating an incident without injury. The spontaneous activation suggests a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Dishwasher started smoking and smelling hot at end of wash cycle.  Would not turn off properly.  Went ahead and turned off breaker to unit.  Found out main control unit malfunctioned and started to melt down and started melting adjacent wiring.
justification: The dishwasher malfunctioned and started smoking, but no injury or death occurred. The issue was resolved by turning off the breaker.

incident_description:
We were using our oven in our Sears Ceramic top Electric Range, Model No. 92022101, purchased 6/6/2002, to bake a pizza.  It worked as normal, but after removing the baked pizza, we soon smelled something hot.  The BROILER had automatically come on by itself; we had NOT turned the broiler on!  We tried and tried to turn the oven/broiler off, using the controls on the range but all attempts failed.  The elements continued heating, then the fire alarm came on.  Our ONLY course of action that saved our house from catching on fire was to turn off the corresponding circuit breaker to our oven.  

After the oven had cooled off, my husband turned the circuit breaker back on, but the broiler in the oven just came right back on and we couldn't get it to go off.  Therefore, he had to turn the circuit breaker off again.  He repeated this a third time, but the same thing happened.

Now we will be unable to cook, bake, broil or use the range at all because we cannot even turn the circuit breaker on again without possibly starting a fire.  This is a very dangerous fire hazard!  

After researching the internet, I have found many other similar complaints from other customers, but Sears evidently will not stand behind their product or do anything.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven that posed a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Selected "bake", set to correct temperature for cupcakes, then "start/enter".  After the usual few minutes, the oven beeped, indicating that it was done preheating so, I put the cupcakes in the oven to bake for the recommended amount of time.  I took out the cupcakes once they were golden on the top,  pushed "off/cancel".  As I was cleaning up the kitchen, I noticed the element was still glowing orange as if it were still on.  I figured I had forgotten to turn it off, so I pressed "off/cancel" again.  The element continued to stay on even though the panel indicated that the oven was off.  While I was trying other buttons to try to get it to turn off, I noticed that the element was not cycling on/off as it usually does.  I checked the cupcakes and the bottoms were a very dark brown - a sign that the oven had not been cycling on/off as it usually does, but that the element stayed on the entire baking time.  At this point, the oven was starting to smell like things were burning.  Since I was unable to quickly reach the outlet to unplug it, I turned off the power supply at the fuse box.  After about 30 minutes, I turned the power back on.  The oven panel indicated that the oven was off, but after a few minutes, the element was glowing orange again.  I ended up turning off the power at the fuse box again and left it off until we had a serviceman take a look at it.  He stated that the problem was the control panel circuit board.
I feel that this is a huge safety issue and am glad that I hadn't left the kitchen or had chosen "time bake" and left the house!  In my opinion, this model is unsafe!
Kenmore Electric Range:  purchased new from Sears in August 11, 2003; model #66595024101; serial #RP2714284
justification: The oven malfunctioned, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The lights will not go off in this refrigerator. There was a smoky smell coming from the refrigerator when I woke up this morning. When I opened the door, I found that the plastic case under the light bulbs had melted and fallen down, the bulbs were so hot he had to get a towel to hold them in order to take them out. The bulb sockets were very brown and above them the plastic had also melted.
justification: The incident involved a smoky smell and melted plastic but no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
Purchased Microwave/grill combo (model MWG9115SL) and like many other people Like many other people (http://www.consumeraffairs.com/homeowners/emerson_microwave.html) had a very dangerous and potentially deadly issue with it! There is a screw holding the heating element to the roof of the unit and after awhile of use it starts sparking causing a burn in the roof of the oven that just gets worse over time! I had thought I heard popping noises before and just assumed it was whatever I was cooking but the other night I noticed a plastic/electrical burning smell, tried to turn the microwave on again and it started sparking from the roof down (that's what the popping noise had been all along!!!!!) and investigated and sure enough there it was... a HUGE charred mark all around this exposed metal screw!! THANK GOD I caught this before it caught fire or worse!!! I am not the first person to have this issue by a long shot. I think it's completely negligent of the company not to do a recall on these!!! Does someone's house have to catch fire before anything is done to fix this?!!!

Emerson customer service keeps giving me the runaround because my warranty is expired but I feel it shouldn't matter if the product is DANGEROUS. I refuse to PAY to ship it back to them. Something should be done about this.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation with potential for fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have an LG model LFC25760ST refrigerator (Serial # 608KRLR01336) in which the interior lights stayed on, melting the plastic control panel around the bulbs, bubbling the plastic lining on the roof of the fridge, and burning the plastic lamp sockets brown. This apparently happened in the space of about one hour, between the time my wife opened the fridge and when I opened it to discover the problem. The control panel was hanging from filaments of melted plastic. I quickly unscrewed and removed both bulbs. The fridge doesn't seem to be cooling any more. This happened so fast! I was lucky to catch it before the thing caught fire. I shudder to think what might have happened if we'd been away or if it happened overnight when we were sleeping.
justification: The incident caused significant damage to the refrigerator but no injury or death occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the rapid escalation and potential for fire if unnoticed.

incident_description: We turned the dishwasher (Whirlpool Model GU1500XTKB0, Serial No. FM0412529, purchased from Sears) before we went to bed.  In the morning, there was water in the bottom of the dishwasher.  I checked the circuit breaker, and it had been tripped.  Even after resetting the circuit breaker, none of the lights or functions on the dishwasher worked.  Upon closer inspection, I discovered that the electronic control circuit board (Part no. 8528172) had overheated and caught fire, melting portions of the board and the housing.  The thermal fuse within the circuit board had failed to blow.  Had the circuit breaker not tripped, we may have had a fire while my family was sleeping!  I did some research on the Internet and found many links to consumers reporting the same problem with control panels on their Whirlpool and Kenmore dishwashers.  At least one of the links reports the same problem for the exact same model (http://www.mysears.com/Dishwashers--3933/topics/Whirlpool-GU1500XTK-Panel-Fire/posts).  Another site listing a very large number of similar control panel incidents is http://www.kitchenaidfire.com/.  I contacted Whirlpool, and both the customer service representative and her supervisor ([REDACTED]) told me that, because the model number was not under recall, all they would offer to do is to set up a service appointment at my expense to repair the unit.  I explained repeatedly that this was not a routine maintenance issue but rather a very serious safety issue that needed their attention and investigation-- my house could have caught on fire while my family slept as a result of a defect in their product, but they did not want to investigate (except as a routine service call at my expense).  I declined and notified them I would be reporting the incident to the CPSC.  I notice that the circuit board part number is no longer available; apparently Whirlpool now offers a modified replacement part.  Similarly, the original thermal fuse is no longer available.  Rather, a kit that includes replacement wires is now offered in its place.  One wonders whether Whirlpool discovered some faults with the original designs.  I am very concerned that Whirlpool is selling dishwashers with circuit boards that can fail catastrophically and potentially cause serious fires.  Nor does this problem seem limited to my dishwasher; as noted, many other consumers have reported the same problem with their Whirlpool/Kenmore units.  I am even more troubled that when I notified Whirlpool of this safety hazard and offered to let them investigate to see what caused the circuit board to catch fire, they were not interested but rather treated this serious incident as though it were a routine maintenance call.  I have the dishwasher and the damaged components if CPSC would like to investigate them.
justification: The incident involved a dishwasher circuit board overheating and catching fire, posing a serious fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Farberware 8" chef's knife's blade snapped off from handle. The design of this knife has only 1" of the blade going into the handle, and the top of the plastic handle snapped off. The knife is only about 1 year old. No injury, but the blade became dangerously loose. There are no model numbers on the knife, purchased as part of an 11 knife set in a wood block.
justification: The knife blade snapped off but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The design flaw suggests this could happen again with similar knives.

incident_description: I own a Kenmore Elite Dishwasher, Model: 665.16283400.  It was purchased in 2005 from Sears.  I have had to replace the circuit board three times, each time it blew out.  The last time, last week, shortly after I started the washer, I heard a sizzling/clicking sound, saw smoke and it smelled like burnt electronics/wiring.  I immediately opened the dishwasher and the smoking stopped.  I called a repair person who showed me the burnt out circuit.  However, if I hadn't been home or even in the kitchen, I'm afraid the dishwasher would have caught on fire as I have read so many others of this brand/style have.  This problem with the circuit board cannot be fixed by simply replacing the circuit board which is what Sears did the first 2 times it blew.  Now, I must pay again for a defect in the dishwasher - something that should have been recalled long ago.  They are selling a very dangerous product.  Please don't wait for children to die from a fire for you to do something about this issue.  Thank you.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burnt circuit board, posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Sears Kenmore bottom freezer refrigerator that was manufactured in December of 2006.  We bought it in 2007 and when I removed the glass shelf from my refrigerator to clean it, the plastic frame of the shelf crumbled and fell off.  Luckily I was holding the glass too, or it could have fallen and shattered, causing a potential cut.  This happened some time ago and my husband and I have been trying to get help from the parts department of Sears but we were told that the only remedy was for us to buy a new shelf.  I have searched to see if this refrigerator has been recalled for this problem but it has not.  We have not replaced the shelf due to fear it could happen again.  The plastice supports for the other shelves in the refrigerator are beginning to crumble also.  We are not able to use the refrigerator to its full potential due to lack of the shelf and fear of placing much on the remaining shelves.
justification: The incident involved a shelf crumbling but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is high given the ongoing issue with other shelves.

incident_description: GE Dishwasher caught fire and self-destructed during wash.  It appears that the fire started in the guts of the wiring inside the door near the bottom.  This model number has not been recalled although similar GE models have been.  The dishwasher is destroyed as were some of the contents.  The fire got hot enough to crack the glasses in the dishwasher.  We were able to extinguish the flames and discovered the fire before the fire could spread to the rest of the kitchen or damage the counter and cabinets.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and was destroyed, but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the fire was contained before spreading further.

incident_description: pyrex dish had been in 350 degree oven baking. We heard a noise and thought the cat had jumped down on something.  About 5 minutes later, went to retrieve chicken pot pie from oven only to discover it had literally exploded. This was not the first time I had used this dish.
justification: The incident involved an exploding dish but no injury was reported, making it a minor incident with low likelihood as it was not the first use of the dish.

incident_description: Not quite six months after purchase, this micorwave began to make a noise like an electrical short and sparks were visible from inside the unit and outside the back panel.  It happened once briefly, and after a trial re-start, wcontinued to function without incident for the rest of the day.  The next time, the same sparks and noises were continuous.  After ascertaining that there was no problem wiht the electical outlet, a further trial at another outlet went on for a few seconds before the unit shut down.
justification: The microwave exhibited dangerous electrical sparks and noise, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: KitchenAid Microwave/Range Hood KHMS155LSS - 4, manufactured in April 2006, Serial # TR T 1621892.  Woke up approximately 5:00 in the morning with microwave running on its own.  Opening the door was the only way to get it to stop.  PAN and F2 displayed, and the unit would continue to beep even with door open.  Within seconds of shutting the door the microwave would go through the same process over and over until either you open the door or unplug.
justification: The microwave malfunctioned by running on its own, posing a potential hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Bunn BT10B coffee maker. Plastic bowl that holds water is melting. Causing water to get into electrical parts.
justification: Melting plastic bowl and water entering electrical parts pose a risk of electrical malfunction, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
My Kenmore smoothtop electric range, purchased 5-5 -2007 at Sears and delivered 5-6-07, has been cooking strangely. The dual burner,  I really think, has never been quite right, but since this was my first smooth-top range, I didn't really know. I just continued to lift the pan up to get the dual burner going.
Two weeks ago I was cooking on both front burners. The pot on the left was boiling so I turned it down. But it wouldn't turn down. So I took the pot off the stove, and turned that buner completely off - and it wouldn't turn off but continued on high heat for over 20 minutes. 
During the following couple of days, I noticed the red light over the control knob for that front left burner was lit, but I hadn't used it or turned it on. And the burner itself was warm. this happened to my husbansd last Saturday after he poured his coffee, he set it on the stove top (on the left front burner) to get some cream from the fridge, and when he turned back, he touched the stove and it was hot. I cooked last night on the dual burner, and the left front again lit up by itself. 
It now will turn on the heat if you place anything on the burner. I consider this a fire hazard. 
I found a recall on the elite model of this stove for Frigidaire and Kenmore. I called the recall #800-449-9812, but they said it wasn't the Elite model, so too bad. However, it is basically the same stove, with the digital readout and round knobs. AND it is doing the very same things that the recall said about the other model, with over 200,000 recalled. (see Kenmore elite 790.99012 recall). 
My Stove is Serial/ Model  790.9612 2409.
justification: The stove exhibits dangerous behavior by turning on unexpectedly, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The oven had been on for approximately 1 hours on the setting of 350 degrees.  The consumer heard and extremely loud electrical sound that lasted 5 to 7 seconds.  

The consumer got up to see where the ordor was coming from.  She saw that the source was coming from the oven and that smoke was emitting from it.  The consumer turned the unit off and the flames died out.  The bottom o baking coil had caugth fire.  Once the consumer turned the oven off, the flre died out on its own.  The consumer has not been able to remove the stoaff up so she does us the oven.

The consumer called tthe mfr.  and the mfr. j  and they aplologized to her, but nothing fllowed.
justification: The incident involved a fire in the oven but was quickly controlled without injury, indicating a moderate severity with low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I was cooking a (half) rack of lamb in a light wine sauce in an 11x13 glass Pyrex dish @ 425 degrees (in a preheated oven)  for 15 minutes (not long in my opinion).  I removed it from the oven, closed the oven door and it EXPLODED in my hand.  Burning hot glass shards and liquids from the lamb and wine marinade went down my shirt and burned and cut me.  It sounded just like a small bomb went off and it exploded into a million pieces sending shards in a 6 foot direction .  We determined that it indeed was one of our "newer" Pyrex made out of the soda lime glass.  Quite frankly, I will never put Pyrex in the oven AGAIN, even at 350 degrees, we believe that it  is an unstable product even when the product directions are followed.  I am SO thankful I did not have my eleven year old take it out of the oven like he has so many times.   Consumers NEED to be more informed about the dangers of this product.
justification: The incident resulted in burns and cuts from hot glass shards and liquids, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such explosions are not common when following product directions.

incident_description: LG 3 door freezer on the bottom Model LFX25950SW, Light bulbs in the refrigerator overheat, causing light bulb housing to melt and food to heat up and spoil. Contacted LG. The put me in touch with Sears who said even though the refrigerator is out of warranty (purchased Jul 2007) they would send repairman. I don't expect a bill, but I'm not really sure.
justification: The incident involves overheating light bulbs causing food spoilage but no injury or death.

incident_description:
Consumer believes her glass cookware is safety and poses a laceration hazard.  

The glass baking dish had been in the oven for approx. 25 minutes.  The consumer had the browning in the dish and the oven was set to 350 degrees convection bake.  
Consumer opened the oven door and removed the dish then she placed on the top of the burners.  The burners were all in "off" position.  Consumer turned her back  from the burners when she heard loud noise like a gun shut.  When she looked back saw her dish had shattered in thousand pieces.

No injury
justification: The glass cookware shattered but no injury occurred, qualifying as an incident without harm.

incident_description:
While the victim was preparing to scoop some ice cream out its container using his left & right hand the rubber handle broke away from the metal scoop. It caused a jagged piece of metal to be exposed and caused a laceration to his right hand. He applied FIrst AId to his superficial wounds at home.   
The firm was contacted and they only offered to send out a replacement product. They had no concern in hearing the injuries in which her husband had received. 

She still currently has the product and has it put up for safe keeping.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring first aid, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such product failures can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description: About 6 months ago my Kenmore Elite oven/stove heated up while I was baking.  I was just outside playing with the kids. One of my sons came running out saying the stove was smoking really bad and make a popping sound.  I went in and really toxic smelling smoke was everywhere.  I was able to turn off oven and get everyone outside, but we literally had to stay outside for hours as the smoke caused us to cough so badly and burned our throats! Of course I don't need to tell you that some of my little ones were crying over this.  I finally was able to go back in and try and figure out what was going on and to my surprise my glass pan that was in oven was shattered!  I never could figure it out and just thought it was a fluke.  Then yesterday 4/18/2011 I was making muffins in the oven and when I put the second batch like 10 minutes into it the alarm on stove started going off and flashing a code.  It wouldn't turn off no matter what button we pushed and even though the oven was really hot we pulled it out and my husband was able to unplug it.  Now I am terrified to use it as it was so hot that it warped my stoneware muffin pan.  WE looked up the code and it said it was a runaway stove?  Not sure what that means but I know that there has to be something majorly wrong for it to get so hot by itself.  We bought it in Spring of 2005 and it is a Kenmore Elite with the model number of 790 99122405. Please do something about this as I looked and saw there was a recall but my number wasn't listed.  Thanks! [redacted]
justification: The incident caused toxic smoke and throat irritation, indicating injury, and the recurrence suggests a likely ongoing issue.

incident_description: microwave oven powers up by itself causing a danger when no one is home.
justification: The microwave powering up by itself poses a potential hazard, but the description does not mention any actual injury or damage occurring.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore self-cleaning electric range model number 95022101 which I purchased on 08/02/03.  This appliance almost caught fire tonight and I think it is very unsafe.  The lower heating element in the oven would not turn off at all.  I tried several times to turn it off by pressing the off and or pressing the down temp button.  Nothing worked.  I had to pull the range away from the wall and unplug it.  I also checked the circuit breaker, and it had not tripped out.  I turned the circuit breaker off, then back on and plugged the range back into the 220 volt outlet, and after resetting the power "PF" failure error code, the lower heating element turned on again.  I did not turn the oven on, the heating element turned on by itself, and will not turn off.  I would hope an appliance that fails to function properly would fail in the safe mode - i.e. turn off if it does not work properly.  I do not think it should continue heating uncontrolled.  It got very hot before I could disconnect it from the power source.  I feel this is a very unsafe malfunction and should be made known to the public.
justification: The appliance malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: One eye on my Kenmore flattop stove is a fire hazard.  It gets stuck on high and when you try to turn it off a spark shots from the back of the knob.  I looked up recalls on related problems and many Kenmore flattops have been recalled for that same reason.  Unfortunately, my model is not on the recall list and therefore I can't get the repair needed.  My model number is 790.96112409 and the serial number is VF71859597.
justification: The stove has a fire hazard and sparks when turned off, posing a risk of incident but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: I made lasagna this past weekend (Friday, April 15, 2011) in a Pyrex 9x13 glass baking dish. I only baked it at 350 F for about 30 minutes. When I took it out of the oven and set it on my stove top, the 9x13 glass baking dish exploded. It cut myself and my fiance, who was approximately 2 feet away from the pan. How can a brand like this stay on our market? I have pictures on a digital camera at home if needed. I did nothing out of the ordinary while cooking. This should have been a normal, safe procedure. Apparently I was wrong. Please have this issue addressed. I saw that consumer reports did a year long investigation on this, and Pyrex was one of the companies with the most problems. That is also where I saw this email address.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to both the person and their fiance, which warrants a severity level of 3.

incident_description: Crock Pot model number SCCPBC600-S was purchased at Bed Bath and Beyond in December and was used for the first time on April 5, 2011.  After the unit was on for approximately 4.5 hours the unit emitted a electrical burning smell.  Turned the unit off, removed the crock and discovered that a hole the size of a nickle had burned through the plastic on the rear of the unit just above the cord storage compartment.    The plastic dripped onto the counter and the back area was so hot that the surrounding plastic was soft.  Shipped the unit back to Jarden Corporation and have not further details as to what they may have discovered was the problem.  This is a major fire hazard and I fear what may have been the outcome had I not been home.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no injury or death, and such occurrences are unlikely based on the provided frequency.

incident_description: I was baking vegetables in the oven at a temperature of 375 degrees Fahrenheit. The outer layer of glass in the oven door blew out and shattered to pieces on the floor. The oven is less than one year old.
justification: The oven door glass shattered, but there was no mention of injury, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Kenmore
Programmable Digital Toaster Oven with 9 Inch Pizza Stone
Sears item #: 80009    Model #: 125912        

Bought this toaster oven at K-mart lat year. The door has never opened or closed easily- it sticks and jams-and it getting worse. the wire shelf it has is to wide of space and food constantly falls into the pit. I have constantly burn myself, or sent food flying trying to open or close the door.--THIS IS AN EVERY USE EVENT. Last week while trying to close the door after use, it stuck and I burnt myself trying to close it.
Several people have complained to Sears about the door exploding and sending shattered glass everywhere. This is an unsafe piece of junk that should be recalled and am having trouble returning it to Kmart for a refund  I logged on to the Sears webite & read the reviews. This has been going on for more than a year and this toast oven is still for sale. Shame on Sears & Kennmore. Take this thing off the market and recall the rest before somone gets injured. SEARS is of no help in returning this garbage for a refund saying they only warranty it for 90 days.  With the numerous complaints about this product on Sears own website they should be not dodging this issue and they can't clain that they aren't aware of it's defects.
justification: The description reports frequent burns and potential for injury due to the toaster oven's defects, with multiple complaints about similar issues.

incident_description: Toaster oven exploded.  Kenmore Model 100.80009 toaster oven.  It was not being used at this time.  It was not hot or warm.  It was used at least 24 hours prior to this.  The glass front simply exploded, and broke into many small pieces, door handle fell.
justification: The toaster oven exploded but was not in use and caused no injury, making it an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The oven on our electric range had been preheating for approximately 5 minutes when flames began shooting from the vents at the back and top of the control panel.  The flames went up the wall nearly to the vent hood a distance of about 12 inches.  The flames lasted for about 60 seconds until something inside the control panel popped and then they went out.  It scorched the tile behind the range and could have easily set the house on fire.  There was nothing in the oven and nothing on top of the stove to catch fire.  The source of the fire was inside of the control panel.  I have tried to get both Kenmore the company we bought it from and Frigidaire the company that manufactured it to come out and look for the cause of the fire.  Neither company cares enough to come look at this product.  I removed the rear cover to take pictures of the source of the fire.  It appears that 2 relays actually came unsoldered from the circuit board and fell off.  One landed on a wiring harness just below the control board and one fell down inside the range.

There have been recalls on other Kenmore ranges for fires, but not on this model.  I have seen enough reports on the internet to believe that there is a problem with this model as well and I believe that it should also be recalled.
justification: The incident involved flames and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents have been reported, indicating a possible issue with the model.

incident_description:
On Sunday April 17th I was in my living room. I smelled something burning. I got up and followed the smell to my kitchen. There was a fire burning on my stove. I immeadiately tried to turn the burner off and realized it was ALREADY in the off position yet the coil underneath was red hot. I took the mats that were on fire on my stove and tossed them into my garage. At that point I went right to the fuse box and tripped the breaker to the range. After I got the fire under control, I went online to see if there were any safety recalls on this stove since it turned itself on without any human intervention.

I wasnt too surprised when I found alot of data online about the Kenmore model being recalled due to a faulty switch. I went back to the stove and took the back panel off and sure enough, I could see where electricity had been arching across the circuit inside the switch. It had already started burning the plastic housing and warping the shape. Basically you can see why the circuit is stuck in the on position and why the burner stays on no mateer what you do unless you trip the breaker in the breaker box in my garage.

To my complete surprise, Sears and Kenmore both treated me like garbage. I spent nearly 4 hours on the phone getting different stories from each department about why they personally cant do anything about it. They kept passing me off to other departments where I would have to begin my story all over again. Ultimately, I called the local Sears and the assistant manager there told me there was nothing she could do.

There is something VERY bad going on at Sears.Beyond the horrible customer service, they are not taking responsibilty for this product. Someone is going to lose their home or maybe even die if they dont address this and make people aware that this "switch" design is used on nearly every model Kenmore manufactures.

Here are the facts- My model number is 79096002600 serial number VF64846756. According to the Consumer Safety Commission, my model and serial number are just outside the range of the recalled stoves. Common sense says that if my stove is catching on fire because of the same faulty switch that was built into the models that WERE included....then my model should be recalled as well.

I went one step further and went to the sears website for parts and found that the switch in my stove is the same model number as the ones recalled.

Why is Sears and Kenmore putting peoples lives in danger? Why would they not be willing to admit to anything? Why are they trying to cover this up? I have pictures of my kitchen the damage and the mess that the fire made. I have pictures of the faulty switch and the damage that the short circuit did to the housing.

If they don't act on this people will burn in fires. These switches are ticking time bombs and all of them have an engineering flaw that causes them to short circuit.

PLEASE help me with this.

With Respect
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a faulty stove switch, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Heating (drying) element in dishwasher locked on.  When my wife smelled something hot she opened the door and saw the element glowing red and the surrounding plastic was distorting.  She stopped the cycle.  After cooling, scale had fallen off the element.  We tried to lock the heating element off with the air dry only feature, but it would stay on.  We have no doubt that it would have started a fire if she was not there to stop the cycle.

incident_description:

incident_description: Wal-Mart/GE Halogen Toaster Oven Model: 169104  Serial Number: 4700200858WM The heating elements do not turn off at the end of the timer cycle. Cannot turn off manually. Must unplug to turn off the elements.

incident_description: Our KitchenAid Superba energy star dishwasher model KUD5011JWH1 caught fire--smoke came out of the top. incident_description:
Cuisinart "Brew Central" 12-cup coffee maker, DCC-1200 series.  3-4 months old.
Coffee maker had finished brewing a pot, was in "keep warm" mode. Spontaneously started brew cycle again, but with a vengeance. Coffee in pot began to boil vigorously. Machine began to make ominous crackling noises. Acrid smoke began pouring from bottom of unit. Smelled like burning plastic/electrical fire. Fortunately we were in the room. We unplugged the unit and removed pot from an obviously runaway heating element. Smoke continued to issue from hole in back where cord enters. 

Simply by typing into Google "cuisinart coffee maker smoke fire", we immediately found more than 20 complaints describing almost identical incidents. Many people had contacted Cuisinart directly to report their incidents. According to their reports, Cuisinart consistently denied having ever heard of this problem.
justification: The incident involved a coffee maker malfunction leading to smoke and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is high given the multiple similar complaints found online.

incident_description: The range oven turns on by itself.  It appears to be in the clean mode.  It will not shut off on it's own.  The circuit breaker must be turned off or the system unplugged.  We were lucky to be home when this has happened.

incident_description: I turned on my oven and sparks were crackling and popping while black smoke bellowed out. This is a kenmore electric range 790 series, I'm sure you are familiar with the product after the numerous complaints you have received.

incident_description:
_On Friday March 18, 2011, I used two Anchor Hocking glass bakeware dishes to prepare dinner for myself and some guests.  Although I used the product as per the guidelines set forth by  Anchor Hocking, one of the dishes shattered in the oven, it created an extremely hazardous situation in my kitchen, cut my finger, destroyed my oven, ruined the food and the dinner party and created a great deal of expense and stress.

Temperature shock was not an issue, I had just purchased the ingredients fresh and the glass dishes had been stored in a kitchen cabinet.  After pre-heating the oven to 350 degrees for a few minutes, I put a pan of potatoes on the bottom shelf of my oven, then five minutes later put a pan of covered chicken cutlets onto the top shelf.  I set a timer for exactly 20 minutes and it beeped as I was emerging from the shower, luckily I covered up with a robe and slippers. I
opened the oven, uncovered the chicken, then completely closed the oven door and walked out of the kitchen. Less than one minute later I heard a loud bang, it sounded like something had fallen off a shelf and shattered. I went into the kitchen to investigate and saw that the oven door was partially open and I was standing in shards of broken glass, some were imbedded into the soles of my slippers. I turned off the oven and looked inside, the glass pan that contained the
chicken had exploded into many pieces, glass was everywhere, in the food, all over the oven, in the broiler and scattered around the stove. It was extremely frightening to think that I had been standing in front of the open oven just a moment before this explosion. I called my guests to let them know what had happened and that I couldn't host as planned.

I tried to Clean up the mess, I purchased rubber kitchen gloves and several other items that I hoped would make the cleanup safer. I wore thick clothes, a rain slicker, goggles and gloves and still cut my thumb trying to remove the glass. Some of the glass is melted into the oven in large chunks and shards of glass are everywhere, I soon realized that the oven was beyond repair.  I saved the glass and took a number of pictures. I have contacted Anchor Hocking, they denied responsibility and informed me that I must turn over the evidence to be investigated them and they will not pay the cost of independent evaluation. They also stated that if they do find liability, they will at best reimburse only depreciated value of the oven and not the full amount of my loss. I informed them that I will look into legal options unless they can come up with a better solution and they refused.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut finger and significant property damage, placing it at severity level 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is rated 2 (unlikely) as such events are not common but have been documented.

incident_description:
The consumer came home and opened the refrigerator door and noticed the inside top portion of it was wet.  He wiped water up.  He closed the door and went to the water actuator on the left side (freezer).  Approx. 20 - 30 minutes later, he opened the refrigerator side and he saw a constant drip.  The consumer checked the filter and ensured that the o-rings were okay and he stuck it back.  

The consumer placed a bowl inside of the refrigerator in case the problem happened again.  A few minutes later, the consumer noticed that water was leaking from the electronicsÃÂ area in the freezer side of the unit.  The consumer removed the filter to stop any further water leaks around the time he was going to bed.  Around 4:00am in the morning, the consumer woke up to a hot plastic odor in his home.

The consumer checked the refrigerator and found that the electronic portion of his refrigerator had begun to melt.  The plastic housing around the on/off button had become discolored.  The interior of the refrigerator was like an oven and made him pull back his hand after nearly touching one of the shelves.  The consumer pulled the refrigerator from the wall, because the on/off button was no longer working.  The consumer unplugged it from the electrical outlet and proceeded to clean up the mess.  

The consumer had a warranty through Electrolux and they sent out a technician a week later.  The technician told the consumer that this problem has happened many times and it's due to the water being located directly near the brains of the refrigerator.  The tech. told him that they could repair the unit, but would have to replace the filter and the electronics in it. However, the warranty company refused to allow the repair.

(5/26/2009)  The water actuator broke and the warranty company covered the repair cost.  The consumer noted that the tech. said that these units were basically not designed well.

The ice maker never works consistently.  He has to remove it occasionally and bang on it and then put it back in.
justification: The incident involved water leakage and electronic malfunction without injury, and the technician indicated this is a common issue with the unit design.

incident_description: Used Crock-Pot Designer Series Smart-Pot manufactured by Jarden (SCCPTP600-P) for the first time.  Placed unit on top of cutting board on kitchen counter.  Followed directions, set unit on "high" for 6 hours (programmed button).  Returned 2 hours into cooking time to find the plastic housing on bottom of unit melted to cutting board.  Rubber coating on electrical wire melted through with exposed wires.  Immediately unplugged unit and moved out of house.  Countertop even underneath the cutting board was too hot to touch.  Fully expect that fire would have resulted if we did not return when we did.  I reported to manufacturer (via email) and returned item to store.

incident_description:
Purchased a Frigidaire Refrigerator in 2006. In the last year and a half, the water filter would occasionally begin to start leaking. the only fix for this is replacement. In one that was only about 6 weeks old in February, it leaked al very large amount of water. These are supposed to last at least six months, and are expensive. abot $40-45 each. I called Frigidaire in February to lodge a complait about the quality of these filters. They are a "Puresource 2" filture . They acknowledged they had some quality issues, and sent me out a couple of replacement no charge. On Sunday afternoon, April 10th, another one developed a leak, this time spraying water all over the inside of the fridge and leaking out onto the floor. We cleaned up the mess and replaced the 2 month old filter.  
On Monday evening upon arrival home from work, we discovered the fridge had quit working, and was very warm inside. Called a repairmen who came in on Wednesday the 13th of April. He discovered that the Control board had suffered a significant meltdown. It had melted the area it was in, and also warped the inside top of the fridge. It did not catch fire, but very well could have if left alone long enough. We suspect that the water got into the control board. The board and the water filter are both located in the same housing, about a foot apart. The problem also for some reason made the refrigerator light stay on, which also burned some plastic in the bottom of the unit. I have multiple photo's, but have been unable to upload them to this report. Let me know where you would like them sent. I also pulled the control board/filter housing out of the fridge. If you have interest in looking it over, I would send it to you. The refrigerator is being hauled away tonight and we are replacing with a different brand. I beleive this incident had serious fire hazard potential, and Frigidaire is aware they have an issue with the filters.
justification: The incident involved a significant equipment malfunction with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Bosch dishwasher, model # SHY56A050uc/4, Serial # FD850100955 stopped working mid cycle. Upon further review it was determined that the dishwasher's wiring had burned. Dishwasher currently has no power.

incident_description:
I purchased a Nuby 7 oz. Cup With Valveless No-Spill Spout that comes with a plastic reusable cap/lid from WalMart.  It is a light Blue and Yellow Sippy Cup, with a "grippy" rim for the cap/lid to adhere to, and grippy base with handles that pops off.  The handles curve upward and reach "just under" the rim of the cup.  The FIRST time that my son used the cup, he "banged" it on the table, which ALL babies will do with their sippy cups.  I noticed when getting ready to fill the cup the next time, that there was something in the bottom of the cup.  When I looked to see what "it" was, I found that "it" was a "circle-shaped" piece of plastic.  I washed the cup prior to my son using it, so I knew that it was not something that was there when I purchased it.  After checking the cup thoroughly, I assumed that it was due to my son "banging" his cup on the table.  The top of the cup handle had actually punched a circular hole through the cup itself.  Thankfully he probably would never have been able to ingest the plastic through the spout, however, the circular hole in the plastic where the handle had punctured the cup is sharp, and could have cut his finger(s) had he put his finger(s) in the punctured hole.  It is also a possibility that the plastic may break into smaller pieces if this were to happen again, allowing it to flow through the "spout", and be ingested by a child.  

I have a different type of "Nuby" Sippy Cup for my son that I like, and have had no problems with it (it's handles are connected to the lid, and are facing downward - Blue/Green in color and comes in other colors as well).  Just thought I should make it known that there is a bad sippy cup out there, as it could be dangerous if it goes unnoticed by other parents.

Thank You!
justification: The incident involved a potential hazard (sharp plastic piece) but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood of injury is possible given typical baby behavior.

While baking a turkey for about an hour and a half at 325 degrees when the setting changed from bake to broil. She attempted to power the range in the off position but it would not power in the off position. 

The range was pulled from the wall and unplugged from the wall outlet. When the unit was plugged back in into the wall outlet there was an error message across the control panel and the oven powered back in the on position the setting is not known.

incident_description: I have a Delonghi Magnifica 3400 Superautomatic Expresso machine.  The steamer stopped working.  Disassembled the outer shell to see if I could determine what was wrong.  I uncovered the problem, but While trying to run the steamer I noticed that a wire sparking - the connection was sparking at times and at other times glowed red - clearly a fire hazard.  I have attempted to contact the company with no success.  I will write them tonight.

incident_description: I was baking chicken in an Anchor Hocking glass baking dish.  The oven was set to 400 degrees, and the dish had been in the oven cooking for twenty minutes when I heard it explode. incident_description: My Black and Decker Toaster Oven Model # TRO 600Ty1 from Shelton, Connecticut, caught on fire, with fire spuing out of its center or "toast" switch, while I was attempting to toast two pieces of wheat bread.  I have this toaster and was given a new one, of different model number, and told that this one is no longer made. incident_description: I have a solid surface stove top when I use the right side burners the light does not work that indicates the stove top is hot.  The light went out within 2 weeks of delivery of the range on2/28. incident_description:
We purchased a Radiant Cooktop by Jenn-air.  Models JEC8430 & JEC8430.  Serial # 118085-86V in 2005.
   The knobs keep splitting.  If the stove is "on," the only way you can turn off the burner is to use needle nose pliers to pull off the knob and the sleeve.

On March 21, 2011 fortunately I was homeÃÂ.smelled an electrical smell and saw white smoke and unplugged the refrigerator.  I called Whirlpool and a service man came out. incident_description: Purchased maytag range model #MER5755QAW   serial# 13811926CV   in 2004 had problems with door and heat coming through edges of door of oven, where as it was melting the cabinet drawer next to it. Previous stove did not do this. We had them service twice within first few months and they replaced door gasket and adjusted door.Still had problems and they insisted that's all they could do. incident_description: I own a Kitchen Aide KEMC  serial no. XL3304930  microwave wall oven combo unit.  The unit heated up completed on it's own when I was not home. incident_description:

Arriving firefighters found the contents (pans, cooking utensils) of a household natural gas range/oven on fire within the oven. Firefighters extinguished the burning materials and carried the range outside.

Inspection revealed that all burner knobs were "off." The oven controls were digital located on a panel to the rear of the stovetop.  The range was plugged into electric power and connected to a natural gas line.

All contents of the oven were burned and the glass door front was broken,

Occupants state the range was a gift, purchased by a relative second hand. They stated that the oven has turned on by itself on at lest 4 other occasions. They said the oven turned on by itelf prior to this incident

Nothing was on the coil and nothing splashed on the coil. I was standing next to the stove when this occurred.  I immediately turned off the oven. incident_description: We purchased our home in June 2009.  We did not move in until June 2010.  The previous owners purchased a Frigidaire Dishwasher model number PLD4375RFC0 in January of 2009.  I registered it with Frigidaire in June 2010 because the previous owners had not registered it.  The dishwasher has never worked well.  I began using the Ultimate Scrub cycle, and that seemed to improve the cleaning and the drying of the dishes.  About two weeks ago, we could not select the Ultimate Scrub cycle any longer.  It would not light up at all.  We began using the Normal Wash, but we also selected the Hi-Temp Wash and Sanitize cycles which made this selection similar to using the Ultimate Scrub.  Last Sunday, April 3, I noticed that the dishwasher had an Error flashing on the display.  I opened the dishwasher, and it was so incredibly hot inside that I thought it might catch on fire.  I left the door open to cool the dishes off.  When I closed the door, the dishwasher tried to start washing again.  I canceled the cycle.  Last Monday, April 4th, my husband turned on the dishwasher and thought all was well.  When I came home, there was no display on the dishwasher.  I opened the door, and the cycle had not run.  My husband said that he knew it had started because he heard it.  We tried two more times to get the dishwasher to run, and it finally did but got extremely hot again.  I unloaded the dishwasher on Tuesday, and saw that two plastic glasses that I have washed many times had completely melted.  It took tremendous heat to do this.  We are afraid to continue using the dishwasher and fear that it will catch on fire.
justification: The dishwasher reached extremely high temperatures, melting plastic items, posing a clear risk of injury if touched or if a fire were to start.

incident_description:
While baking chicken for dinner (4 small chicken thighs in a pyrex dish covered in foil), the oven was shut off, but the dish was left in the oven to finish cooking/stay warm.

The oven had been turned off, but the bottom coil never shut off and kept heating the oven to increasingly higher temperatures.  When the oven door was opened to remove the dish, that is when the discovery of the malfunctioning coil was made.  

After pulling out the rack with hot pads to try to remove the dish, the dish promptly flamed up and started to shatter in pieces on the oven rack, the oven door and the floor.  Hot grease and glass shards went everywhere; both inside the oven, on the oven door and onto the kitchen floor.

Attempts to remove the pyrex were abandoned and I immediately tried to extinguish the fire.  It started with a few flames and increased in intensity once the rack was pulled out and it was further exposed to the open air vs the interior of the oven.  After a few unsuccessful attempts to put the fire out, I grabbed a new bag of flour and proceeded to sprinkle/pour it over the broken pan/rack/oven door until all the flames were extinguished.

Since the oven would not shut down, the breaker switch had to be thrown off to get the oven to stop heating.  Only after the entire thing cooled down and we were able to unplug the unit did we find that the entire interior "window" of the oven had also completely shattered.  

Thankfully, the damage was limited to the oven and aside from the smoke and smoke alarms going off for quite some time, everyone was safe.
justification: The incident involved a fire and property damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Kenmore 665.17052400 model dishwasher started on fire near end of wash cycle approx. 16:00 on 4/10/11.  My wife was nearby doing homework when she heard and then smelled the electrical fire.  She shut-off the power switch and we then shut-off the electrical breaker also.  Thick black smoke with crackling was heard from the unit.  We had checked with Sears back in 2005 when a recall came out for this model, and we were told ours was not in the recall because it had a metal tub.  Only the plastic tub units were recalled for a fire hazard.  Well, that just is not true now that ours burned up.  The fire department said we were lucky to be home at the time it went, otherwise the fire would not have been confined to just the appliance.
I've sent the request to Sears and Whirlpool today also.  

Model # 665.17052400. Serial # FR4004116
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no injuries were reported, and the fire was contained to the appliance.

incident_description: I am writing about the Fagor Rapid Express Pressure Cooker 6 qt model item #918013053. I was following an online recipe that called for using 1 kilo of beef, 8 potatoes, 1 large union and 2 cloves of garlic and 1 liter of water. I closed the cooker lid according to manufacturer instructions. The contents of the cooker began to boil after about 10 minutes and I was waiting for the cooker to build pressure. The yellow indicator came up after 10 minutes, indicating pressure. Some bubbles started to appear at the base of the handle and some steam started to come out of the safety vent. I was standing about five feet away from the stove when the incident occurred.
