justification: The incident involves a defective dishwasher control board with an electrical short, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or damage reported.

incident_description:
Caller was cooking with her oven set around 350 degrees, dish had been oven around 30 minutes when the timer went off to alert completion of cooking.
Caller opened oven door and saw that the knob that she saw glass all over the oven.
She noted that the knob handle on top of the glass lid had exploded.
Caller did not keep any of the glass, she thought it to be an isolated incident until seeing other reports of explosians
She is reporting, noting that she is 77 yrs old and if she had opened the oven she could have been cut very badly.
justification: The incident caused no injury, but there was a risk of injury if the caller had opened the oven door.

incident_description: I have a Maytag electric range, model MER5751BAS.  I smelled a meltig plastic smell and saw smoke coming from the vent under the clock.  Then the electricity to the range failed.  I switched off the breaker and looked behind the stove to find the elecric cord melted through at the point where it connects to the range.  The outlet was unaffected, and there is no additional singe damage anywhere else on the stove.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a melted power cord but no injury or further damage, indicating a non-injury incident with low likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
We have a Hotpoint kitchen range, Model # RB5250J2A0, Serial # AZ116089H. It is probably about 20 years old, but we have just moved into the home, so it is new to us. When using the oven for baking or broiling, the outside top surface and the outside front surface of the door get very hot. It is so hot that if I forget about the very hot condition and rest a hand on one of these surfaces, I can easily burn myself. It is also necessary to keep our small child out of the kitchen while baking, for example, when baking cookies, as she might easily be burned by touching one of these surfaces.

I got a surface thermometer to see how hot the top surface should  get. I found that it gets above 205 degrees F when I use the broiler. I checked with General Electric-Hotpoint by phone and was told that the maximum temperature of the top surface should not be above 191 degrees F.
justification: The oven surfaces get dangerously hot, posing a burn risk to users and small children, with documented temperatures exceeding safe limits.

incident_description: I bought a microwave in February 2010.An Emerson MW8998B.I lost the receipt for this microwave.The microwave has recently started sparking with weird buzzing noises and a burnt smell comes from it.There is  a black burnt mark on the splash panel that seems to be getting bigger.I called their customer service but they said they couldn't do anything because i no longer had the receipt and my one year warranty had likely expired.I went online and Emerson seems to have the same complaint from several consumers.This item should be recalled.It is a fire and safety hazard.
justification: The microwave is sparking and has a burnt smell, which is a fire and safety hazard, but no injury has occurred.

incident_description:
We have a Kenmore Dishwasher Model 665.17032402 Serial No. FS3201092. When we turn on the dishwasher on a 'Normal Wash' cycle it automatically sets the 'Heated Dry' cycle. Normally we un-click the 'Heated Dry' cycle button to safe the energy on drying the dishes. But if we forget to do it, it will be automatically scheduled to dry on a Heated Dry cycle.
Few months ago we turned on the dishwasher to run when we were not at home. When we came back we smelled a smoke in the house. We identified that the smoke smell was coming out from the dishwasher. Next time we decided to check if the smoke is definitely related to the 'Heated Dry' cycle. We turned the dishwasher on and as soon as it switched to the 'Heated Dry', it started to smell like a smoke. We immediately turned off the dishwasher and when we opened its door the smoke was coming out from it. For now on we are just using it for the washing cycle but we are afraid that it has a danger of a fire hazardous condition.
We checked CPSC's web site for recalls of this specific model of Kenmore dishwashers. We didn't find our model but it seems that a lot of Kenmore dishwashers were recalled for similar problems.
justification: The incident involves smoke emission from the dishwasher during the 'Heated Dry' cycle, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On or about mid to late April 2010, my mother and step father were in their living room.  They had just put on a second pot of coffee for the morning.  They heard an explosion and saw a fire ball.  They both ran to the kitchen approximately 12 feet from their living room, they saw the Hamilton Beach 12 cup, programmable, coffee maker (model #49464) on fire on the counter.  They both stated that the cord had already been burned in half.  My step father grabbed the cord and unplugged it from the electrical socket.  My mother grabbed a kettle of water to throw on the fire.  My mother burned her hand while trying to remove the pot from the burner and extinguish the fire.  A peice of the melted plastic stuck to the top of her right hand.  This caused her hand to blister in a 2" x 1" area.  The coffee pot was placed on the back porch and then they poured more water to make sure the fire was completely out.  They had used the coffee pot for approximately a year and a half prior to the explosion.  My mother stated that there was no indication that the coffee maker had any problems.  The coffee maker was purchased from Kohls Department Store in Waldorf, MD, the price was approximately $29.00.  There was soot from the fire on the bottoms of the cabinets above where the coffee maker had exploded.  There was damage to the counter top in which a 6" x10" are of formica completely burned away, exposing the wood in which the formica was adhered to.  The area around the burn hole is bubbled up (Approximately 14" a 19".)  There is an area on their vinyl flooring that was burned by dripping plastic from the coffee maker (Approx 2" x 3").
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the mother's hand, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the lack of prior indications of problems with the coffee maker and the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: Ran my dishwasher on the normal cycle with normal items after cycle there was scoot on a pot and some of the prongs on the lower tray were seared into.
justification: The incident describes damage to items in the dishwasher but no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: We have a Frigidaire slide in, smooth top range Model Number FEF365ASD and one burner seems to stay on "high" no matter where the dial is set.  The burner is a small back burner that we seldom used except for a tea kettle.  We had an incident just this week where a pot of potatoes boiled dry and almost caught on fire after just a few minutes on "low" or simmer.  When we lifted the lid on the pot, smoke filled the kitchen.  I saw the recall for ranges like this but the web site says our range does not fit the recall.
justification: The incident involved a pot boiling dry and smoke filling the kitchen, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the burner malfunction is recurring but not constant.

incident_description: I was microwaving dinner in my new Panosonic microwave when sparks started flying.  There were loud pops which terrified the dog.  There was fire and smoke before I could turn off the microwave and I was only about 8 steps away.
justification: The incident involved sparks, fire, and smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the dishwasher started smoking so she flipped the circuit breaker.  Consumer said the unit caught fire and melted the plastic and burned the control panel.  Consumer contacted manufacturer and they told her that her unit model number matches the recall but the serial number is not within range.  Consumer's unit is similar to recall under release # 93-042
justification: The dishwasher caught fire and caused damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
This involves a past recall on the Black & Decker Spacemaker coffee maker(my model is#ODC440B) for hot fluids leaking from the edge of basket. When I ordered the new basket for my coffeemaker (has been at least six months ago), I read some reviews that said that replacing the basket did NOT solve the problem. I am finding that to be true!! I know better than to stick my hand under it and should have stopped using it months ago!! These coffee makers need to be recalled ALTOGETHER, since there seems to be something in the design of it that makes this happen. IT IS AN UNSAFE PRODUCT!!!

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves hot fluids leaking, posing a burn risk, but no injury is reported. The problem persists despite replacement, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Kenmore smoothtop range model 790.95202100

Oven burner will not turn off.  Certainly would have caused a fire if we had not been home.
justification: The incident involved an oven burner that would not turn off, posing a fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description: Oven heating element fails to turn off after being switched off and heats to a different temperature than selected.
justification: The oven heating element failing to turn off is an incident that could lead to overheating, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Within 5 to 10 minutes after the diswasher started, smoke was pouring from the top of the dishwasher and there was an electrical burning smell in the home. The unit was placed on a normal wash setting.

He noticed that there was no power to the unit so he safely assumed the fuse was blown to the unit 
A technician from the firm was sent out to the home on 10/15/2010 and he removed the control panel. 

The electrical board was burned up completely. The dishwasher could not be repaired.
justification: The incident involved smoke and electrical burning smell, but no injury or death occurred. The occurrence likelihood is possible as electrical faults can happen but are not extremely common.

incident_description: My Maytag dishwasher was part of the recall last year for a faulty heating element that continues to run and could cause a fire risk.  We never had an issue with the dishwasher heating element continuing to run, however, we still had the part fixed under the recall.  Now almost one year later, we have the exact issue with the heating element continuing to run.  My wife has called Maytag, however, they are stating that the dishwasher was fixed and the recall has been satisfied and refuses to cover the repair.
justification: The faulty heating element poses a fire risk, but no actual fire or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
several weeks ago I set the top oven of my maytag gemini oven to the 3-hour clean.  About 2 hours into the process I started to smell something electrical burning.  I could not stop the process and the system ended up tripping a circuit breaker.  I reset the breaker and the oven continued until the time was up.  My son looked at it the next day and all the insulation was burned off the wiring in the top oven.  There was smoke on the panel on the outside of the top of the stove.

My son called Maytag and after waiting for over an hour for a response on the phone, he was eventually told that this make and model was not a part of a previous recall.  Sorry--there is nothing we can do.

This was an extremely dangerous situation and one that I think should be covered.  It is an expensive repair for me to make.

Over and above the danger, I was not happy with the response from Maytag and their customer service.
justification: The incident involved electrical burning and damage to the oven, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: Consumer says the unit switch was sparking and smoking.  Consumer unplugged the unit to stop the smoking.  Consumer contacted manufacturer and they told him it is out of warranty and they offered no further assistance.  Consumer says has noticed many online complaints with other consumers having similar issues.
justification: The incident involved sparking and smoking, but no injury was reported. The mention of similar online complaints suggests the issue is likely to recur.

incident_description:
Last fall we purchased a Frigidaire electric slide in range. Model FGES3065KBB, Ser. NF01423539.  It is a smooth top electric range with a warming drawer.  We needed the slide in range because of an opening to the living room behind it.

Since that time, the top burners have been turned on ACCIDENTALLY several times with only a slight bump of the controls.  It was never noticed until someone looked on the stovetop and found a burner on, or found something actually being burned.  It burned a pot holder one time.  A dish rag was barely touching the edge of the oven and it caught on fire.  The outside of an expensive pan was damaged, but fortunately I was close by and kept the kitchen from burning down.  In 30 years of cooking, I have NEVER had problems with a kitchen fire or an oven accidentally being turned on before.  I have three children and am worried about their risk if I am not home as well.

The controls take VERY LITTLE effort to turn them on.  some of them have the HIGH control right next to the off. This means that a little movement puts them in the riskiest position.  Our old range had taller stems to the controllers and it needed a little more of a push to turn on the controls.  I even purchased a little rubber disk to slide under the controls so that a child couldn't turn on the controls even if he wanted to.  These controls fit much more closely and I cannot use that extra safety on this new range.

Please check this model and others for this risky setup for the controls.  I am afraid this could easily start some house fires if it is not corrected.

We purchased the oven from Metro Builders supply on Mingo Ave., in Tulsa.  I did call and report this to a salesperson, who said they would report it to a Frigidaire rep.  I did not receive a callback from the manufacturing company.
justification: The incident involves actual fires and property damage, indicating injury risk, and the controls are easily activated, making recurrence likely.

incident_description:
Appliance fire on a builth-in dishwasher.
control panel overheating, smoking during use.
Kenmore Model 16519200: S/N FM4108418
Fire contained to control panel area.
justification: The fire was contained to the control panel area with no reported injuries, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Purchased Frigidarie Gallery Range on November 30 2009 from Admark Products.  This Electric Range is manufactured by Electrolux

Serial Number: VF92447335
Model Number: FGEF3056KFA

We started having problems after 6 months of usage.  We noticed that the surface burners could not be turned off or down using the touch screen controls on this Range.  In addition the oven became an issue with similar problems. We could not shut the oven off once it was turned on.  The problem seemed to resolve itself after the oven was cleaned.  This happened 4 times.  On April 2, 2011, we began our evening preparations for dinner.  We were utilizing the two front burners to boil water and simmer Veggies.  We noticed a strong smell of burning plastic.  We began searching our first floor for the impeding electrical fire that seemed to be taking place.  We discovered that there was a white smoke pouring out the back of the stove.  I ran into the basement and shut off the Circuit Breaker to the Oven which stopped the stove from shorting out and burning.  I pulled the stove away from the wall and it reeked of an electrical fire.  We now have no Range and cannot cook for our family.  I've called Electrolux and Frigidaire.  Have been bounced back and fourth to decide who will deal with this issue. I'm ready to call my attorney.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric range that emitted smoke and had potential fire hazards, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Re: Kenmore Smooth to electric range Model# 95802000, serial# RK 1316768.
Broiler was hot and smoking red within 2 minutes, even when the oven was not turned on. Had to switch of the breaker. Tried to switch on the breaker but brolier become hot and red in less than 2 minutes. Please help! This is a disaster waiting to happen. The kitchen and house was hot within 5 minutes. 
I hope you can help us.
Sincerely,
[REDACTETD]
justification: The broiler heating up without being turned on poses a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: The heating portion of the Slow Cooker melted through the bottom plastic.
justification: The incident involved the melting of plastic but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Yesterday, I was baking a meatloaf in the oven in a square Pyrex dish.  Towards the end of the baking time, I poured a little water directly on the meatloaf to keep it moist.  As soon as I did that, the dish exploded.  Broken glass hit the walls of the oven and fell into the bottom all around the heating element, into the drawer below and onto the floor along with juice from the meatloaf.  Luckily, I was not injured, but it was a mess to say the least and dinner was completely ruined!

The Pyrex dish was not that old (maybe a few years) and I have used it many times to bake casseroles and meatloaf.  This sort of thing never happened to me before.  However, after mentioning this to some friends, I was told this has been an ongoing problem.  After searching on Google, it is very disturbing to see that this continues to happen.
justification: The incident involved property damage and a mess but no injuries, and similar incidents are reported but not extremely common.

incident_description:
I was roasting a chicken in my oven in an Anchor bakeware pan at 350 degrees for about a half an hour and I then turned the temperature up to 425 degrees.  About 10 or 15 minutes later the pan exploded in the oven into millions of glass shards.  If this would have happened with the oven door open I believe a serious injury could have resulted.

I did some research online and consumer reports stated that these incidents are quite common. I think these supposedly oven safe dishes are a safety hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the potential for serious injury was noted if the oven door had been open. Online research indicates such incidents are common.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that her Black and Decker toaster oven had caught fire while she was cooking chicken nuggets and set itself to the broil setting. The unit has a glass front The unit was off and it turned on by itself. The machine caught sparks from the orange light indicator. The toaster is powered by electricity. The toaster was on for 15 minutes before she turned it off. The unit set off her smoke alarm. She has called the manufacturer but it was not the desired department. She has not called the retailer. The toaster is 4-5 years old. The unit is now partially charred. She allowed the sparks to burn themselves out. She feels that this unit is very unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The toaster oven caught fire and caused sparks, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The control panel is warped and does not have a seal on it.  Consumer says product should never have passed inspection.  While cooking beans on the front right there was a spillage causing the liquid to drip into the control panel. It should have gone to the right and left side as it is designed for that; as the tech told consumer.  The liquid also leaked inside of the oven glass door, between both glasses, and to the bottom drawer.   

A technician came out to the home and removed the control panel and saw that the liquid went everywhere because of the defect. She isn't sure if damage was done to the wires that control the oven because she has not used the oven since the incident. She hasn't made any repairs to the unit. The first tech person she spoke with what the consumer wants them to do, consumer said she wanted a replacement range because hers is unsafe, and she's concerned about a fire.  The tech agreed, but they have since declined on the offer. 

She believes that the unit may potentially start a fire and could shorten out.  Manufacturer also said there were safety concerns.
justification: The incident involves a defective control panel and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: Recreational Vehicle Fire.
justification: The description mentions a fire, which is an incident, but there is no mention of injuries or death.

incident_description: I ordered Temp-tations cookware from QVC. It is handpainted in China. I tested it for lead paint and the result was positive. I conducted the test several times.
justification: The presence of lead paint is a serious issue, but the description does not mention any injury or death, only the detection of lead.

incident_description:
My wife purchased two sets of the Better Homes and Gardens brand 20-piece flatware sets from Wal-Mart in Lacey Washington on 19 January 2011.  Each set contains 4-each salad forks, dinner forks, teaspoons, soup spoons and knives.  The product UPC is 19978-95154. The first time we used the new utensils was on March 20th.  I was eating ice cream with one of the teaspoons and was cut on the inside corner of the left side of my mouth by the sharp edge on the tip of the spoon.  The cut was about 1/4" wide and deep enough to bleed for about 20 minutes.  I did not think I needed to see a doctor because it quit bleeding.  When we examined the other spoons in both sets we found that all the spoons, both the teaspoons and the soup spoons had varying degrees of sharpness.  
A few days later my wife was able to find the boxes they came from the store in and called the 1-800-890-3366 number that was listed for customer service of the distributor, Cambidge Siversmiths.  She made three attempts to call the 800 number and each time it was answered by the voice mail.  About a week later Cambridge Silversmiths left a message with a number to call back to.  My wife called the new number and spoke to {redacted}.  She asked that we ship back to her only the spoons and that the company would pay for the shipping.   She agreed to ship us a replacement carton (3-Sets) of flatware and that the warehouse would inspect all the spoons before shipping them.  The cartons arrived on March 30th.  Again, every spoon had varying degrees of sharpness just like the first set we purchased. 
My wife called  and requested a refund for the products instead of replacing them.  [REDACTED] said she could not approve a refund and would have to check with her supervisor.
In the last three days my wife and I looked at many of the same brand and style of Better Homes and Gardens flatware sets at two different stores and found them to also have varying degrees of sharpness.  Not every spoon by this manufacture is sharp enough to cut the user like I was, but many were as sharp as or sharper than the one that cut me.  In my opinion this products need to be recalled and all the spoons inspected for sharp edges.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut that bled for 20 minutes, indicating an injury, and multiple spoons from different sets were found to have sharp edges, suggesting a recurring issue.

incident_description: I  have some Gibson dinnerware and some of it, especially the cups, get so hot when put in the microwave that you cannot touch them when they used to reheat or heat fluids.  The handles get so hot they burn your finger so badly.  Several times they have gotten so hot I have dropped the cup and broken them as have the plates been dropped.  I am concerned that the dinnerware may be high  in metal content.
justification: The dinnerware gets extremely hot in the microwave, causing burns and breakage, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description: Purchased a Kenmore Electric Range Model #790-97453804 11 months ago. Glass on the oven door shattered while nobody was even near it. Called Sears they were not helpful, disconnected twice, and was told I could replace it for $400 with cost of service technician. I have seen many, many similar reports on Kenmnore oven doors with hundreds of the same complaints. Extremely annoyed. We barely use this oven.
justification: The glass on the oven door shattered without causing injury, and there are many similar complaints reported.

incident_description:
We were cooking two pizzas in the oven and watching television in the other room, when we heard a a popping noise and a loud electrical buzzing noise.
We ran into the kitchen, and there were flames and sparks inside of the oven.
My husband tried to shut the oven off, but the controls would not work.
He ran downstairs and turned off the breaker.  It was after that, that the fire finally stopped.  Upon inspection after the oven and cool down.  We saw that the lower burner element was melted, and there was residue spattered throughout the oven.
It is a Kenmore electric oven.
Model number 790.  94112400.
Serial number, VF 43622911.
Date of purchase: 09/04/04.

On the Internet, we found webpage at: http://www.cpsc.gov/CPSCPUB/PREREL/prhtml09/09333.html
It concerns the recall of Kenmore and Frigidaire electric ovens.
We noted that our serial number falls into the range mentioned.  However, our model number was not listed.  We are therefore uncertain if our oven was recalled.  We never received any information from Sears.
We would like to confirm if our oven was part of the recall.
We are still very shaken after this incident, and we would appreciate any help, you can give us.
justification: The incident involved flames and sparks in the oven, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore Electric Range model # 790.96010405 purchased 5/5/06.  The right front burner sometimes heats at maximum though it is set only at 2 or low ("hi" is after "8").  I have also turned the burner off completely yet it continued to heat at maximum for over a minute with the power shut off.  I am afraid to use that burner and am afraid it could come on by itself.  I see that Sears has issued recalls for the same issue, however with different models.  I have also seen on line that many people have the same issue with the right front burner of models that have not as yet had recalls issued.  This is a very dangerous situation and would appreciate any help or advice you could provide.
justification: The burner malfunctions and heats at maximum despite being turned off, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: At 11am this morning i placed a potatoe in my microwave and pressed the bake potato button on the key pad approx. 3 min later my entire microwave was engolfed in flames. My house was filling with smoke flames were shooting out of the microwave door my hudsband opened the door and threw a bucket of water on the entire wall over my stove. I called 911 and they assessed the microwave and did testing with a heat devise on the wall behind and above cuboards to make sure fire was out and informed me that heat level was extremly high and good thing i was right there to put out fire. My entire house smells like burnt charcoal ,my kitchen diningroom greatroom and nook has smoke damage. I called several different phone numbers to kenmore sears and whirlpool and was pushed off to the next dept with absolutly no help what so ever. I was told by all 3 companys that there in fact had not been a recall on this product and for me to contact their legal dept if unsatisfied with their service. They also informed me that if a product is recalled it is only warrantied for 90 days. I asked so if my house burns down because of one of your products that has been recalled over 90 days ago you are not liable for that? They then told me to contact their legal dept they couldnt help me with this matter...
justification: The incident involved a microwave fire causing significant smoke damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: When taking a Pyrex 9x12 baking dish from the oven, it actually blew up in my wifes hands.  The dish had been in the oven for 15 minutes at 400 degrees.  It contained 4 pieces of baked fish that had marinated for 20 minutes in the refrigerator.  The explosion was so violent that we found pieces of glass over 40 feet away.  The dish shattered into thousands of small pieces.  There were very few pieces over 6 inches long.  My wife was wearing jeans and closed shoes.  She did not get injured even though she was hit with many, many pieces of shrapnel.  It took over two hours to clean up the mess off of cabinets, appliances, counter tops, and the floor.  Only through the grace of God did my wife not get severely burned or cut.  Two of my grandchildren had been in the kitchen just the day before helping with supper.  I cannot even think how severely these two young children would have been injured if this had happened the day before.  I have read since this happened that this is not the first or even hundredth time that this has happened.  I have found no evidence that your agency has done anything to investigate the Pyrex problem. I nor my wife can gain any benefit from this incident.  However, if this incident will protect future users of this product, then our lost time and food will be well worth it.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion of a Pyrex dish causing significant damage but no injuries, as the wife was not harmed despite being hit by shrapnel.

incident_description: Belgique anodized cookware w/silicone handles  - the handles get extremely hot after several weeks of use
justification: The handles getting extremely hot poses a burn risk, but no injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
Frigidare Gallery drop in electric range model # FGES3065KBB.

We have experienced two fires with this range caused by inadvertent operation of stove top controls.
The controls are mounted on the front top edge of the range and are very easy to bump and turn on accidentally. 

The controls are supposed to require a push and turn to operate.  However, just a slight bump or touch will move the controls from the OFF position.  The position next to OFF is HIGH so that if the control is moved from OFF it turns the the heating unit to full hot and has started two fires because there were flammable items on or near the heating elements.
justification: The fires have caused property damage but no injuries, so the severity level is 2. The controls are very easy to bump, making the occurrence likelihood 4.

incident_description:
General Electric Company Dishwasher 
Model: GHDA654L00BG
Serial: LL716580B
GE Repairman came out in mid January to repair a dark circuit board on our machine. Within 30 days, the circuit board caught fire and flamed up. Had I not been home or turned the machine on delay for a few hours and gone to bed, the house would've surely burned more severely. Luckily, I smelled the burning 'plastic' smell, saw the flames and smoke, and turned the machine off. The fire department came and tripped the breakers and secured the electrical connections to make them safe. 

GE sent another repairman and he told us the unit was a goner. And we might want to contact an attorney. Since then, GE has replaced the unit and tried like heck to get the old unit back. I still have it and have uncovered a recall on several GE units that had the same problem. Mine was not in the recall - though it should've been in my opinion.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but no injury or death occurred, and similar incidents are documented but not extremely common.

incident_description: I purchased a new Black & Decker toaster oven model TRO420.  When using it for toasting it sometimes will not turn off.  One must turn the dial past 10 minutes & then back to the toast darkness one desires to get it to turn off when finished.  Guest at my house will not know this. The heating elements cycle on & off so you can see that the toaster oven is still on.  After hours of being on all surfaces gets very hot.  One is easily burned.
justification: The toaster oven does not turn off properly, which can lead to overheating and potential burns, but there is no injury reported.

incident_description:
LG Model LFC25760ST Bottom Freezer Refrigerator -- Interior lights did not shut off even though the doors were firmly closed.  
Unit S/N 604KRMK00251, Manufacture Date 2006
Underwriter Labs number 656U
The heat from the bulbs melted the plastic in the light assembly, warped the assembly which now hangs down top of the unit., and charred the light bulb sockets.  Subsequent testing showed the open door alarm worked was working properly.  The heat from the lights also damage food contained inside at the time of the incident.

The only reason the damage was limited was due to early discovery.  Otherwise, I cannot estimate the hazard had the unit continued to heat up and melt.  Fire is a likely possibility.
justification: The incident caused property damage (melted plastic, charred sockets, and damaged food) but no injury or death. The likelihood is possible given the early discovery limited further damage.

incident_description: We  bought a Wolf gas cook top model CT36G/S in November of 2006.  Two and a half years ago we contacted Wolf's customer service department notifying them that when the large dual burner was on simmer the burner would detonate and the cook top would actually lift off the counter slightly.  There would also be a slight odor of gas in the cabinet below.  The gas plumbing was throughly checked and there were no leaks and we never found a gas odor except under these special circumstances.  Wolf told us to call a repair man and ignored this problem even after my husband discovered that it could be fixed by tightening a 7/8 inch brass fitting under the burner which loosens over time.  We believe this to be a manufacturing defect.  We now have discovered that we have to tighten this fitting every month instead of every 6 months and that the red gaskets and "O" rings have deteriorated as well.  We contacted Wolf and again they continue to ignore this serious problem.  We have been on line and found out that we are not alone with this problem. incident_description:
COFFEEMAKER FIRE HAZARD

While brewing a pot of coffee one recent morning, my CUISINART Model No. DC-1100 began to produce smoke from the underside and/or rear of the unit. It also produced a strong odor of an electrical fire and/or smoldering.

When I noticed the smoke/odor, I immediately unplugged the appliance. As I did this, I heard a "whoosh" sound, the kind of noise that is made when something catches fire. I saw no flame, however. The coffeemaker continued to smoke and produce an strong odor.

I threw out the coffeemaker on the next garbage day. I now regret this, however, since cursory online research suggests Cuisinart coffeemakers (other models, too) are the target of more than a few fire-related consumer complaints. Several Websites I read included consumer remarks that, when contacted, Cuisinart customer service representatives said they had no previous such reports. But if the incidents are as plentiful as the Internet suggests, this would doubtless fall under the "known problem" category.

My coffeemaker was less than one year old. I have not informed Cuisinart of this incident because I cannot find the original receipt. However, I may yet contact the company, if only to (hopefully) cause an internal report with the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a strong odor of an electrical fire, but no actual flames or injuries occurred.

incident_description:
To Whom This May Concern:

On September 8th, 2010 at approximately 1:15pm, my wife noticed the lights in the house begin to flicker.  We found out later that there was a power surge related to trees brushing against power lines.  After a few seconds she heard a loud bang and saw a red glow on the Oster 6212 2-Slice Extra Wide Slot Metal Toaster, Brushed Stainless Steel and it burst into flames.  She quickly unplugged the toaster and doused the fire.  Had she not been present, the toaster would have set the cabinets and subsequently the house on fire. 

The toaster was plugged in, but was not turned on or in use.  Nor had it been in use for several hours.  The outlet is on a circuit with four other outlets.  There was a toaster oven plugged into the same outlet that suffered no damage. A coffee maker was also connected to this circuit and received no damage.  The only other damage in the entire house was one light bulb which burned out.  No other appliances were affected, leading us to believe the toaster was faulty.  

We contacted the utility company, Atmos Energy, and they determined they were not responsible for the fire.  I have contacted Oster and sent in the defect product along with the incident report. I am contacting the CPSC in order to ensure that Oster is indeed following through with their obligation to ensure this does not happen again.

While I can understand an appliance breaking during a power surge, it is unacceptable for an appliance to catch on fire, especially when not even turned on.  Had my wife been in the other room or away from the house it could have easily caused serious damage and injury.  

Sincerely, 



[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a toaster catching fire due to a power surge, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Bosch SHE44C05UC/22 residential dishwasher stopped functioning.

Appeared to be a power problem, as +120VAC present at on/off switch, w/ open neutral.
Accessed installer access point to check connections.

Noted installer used proper wire, 14AWG on a 15A circuit. Three wire nuts in use.

Residence circuit breaker DID NOT trip.

Neutral wire burned open, wire nut melted to bottom of box. Noted damage to wire nut on hot leg.

Noted the wire that is manufacturer supplied for powering the unit is undersized at 16AWG. (clearly marked on outer jacket). It appears that the installer/end user has NOT modified the internal wiring in any way, as all three legs of the circuit are the same make/type/size wire. 

Posts on the web revealed others have noted the same problem.

It is my opinion as a former mil. spec. wireman, solder tech. aerospace assembler, and current professional firefighter that Bosch has created an emanate hazard with under designed wiring. 

Damaged wire and parts will be retained for 90 days, should CPSC desire they be submitted for evaluation.

incident_description: While cooking with Frigidaire Flat Top Stove Model # GLEF379DSG Serial# VF60346637 the front right burner caught on fire. At the time the back two burners were the only ones turned on, and the back burners were only set to half heat. When I walked into the kitchen the fire was coming from the front right burner and got soot on the ceiling/walls/and burned the vent a hood. I turned off the back burners and poured water on the stove top. The fire went out but the stovetop (from the edge) leached out soap of the type used to clean the top for the last several years. A few hours later I turned off the breaker supplying power and scrapped away the soap. To my amazement the stove appeared to have no damage. There was no carbon in the debris I scraped away and the soot was all ever the vent a hood, walls and ceiling. The soap had turned a little brown around the burner but was still white on the burner itself and could have been used for cleaning. I had 2 small children in the house and the fire alarm saved lives that day. [REDACTED] I can see no way of making a product like this safe because the soap used to clean the top is absolutely necessary  to keep the top clean enough to work. The soap used was always ÃÂ[REDACTED] glass cook top cleanerÃÂ since the day the stove was bought new. The edges of the stove always appeared to be water tight until the fire heated up the top to an extreme temperature. One of my principle concerns over this incident is the fact that the stove did turn off the front burner when the back burners were turned off. The front burner was never turned on through the whole fire. As strange as the soap part of the fire is, the cause must be a control issue with the knobs that turn on the burners. On this model of stove the knobs are located above and behind the burners. Those knobs have never been wet or been exposed to steam. My oven only gets occasional use for small items. A few turkeys have been cooked during holidays. Since the top burners are controlled directly from the knobs and are not affiliated with the computer, I have zero faith in this product from this point on.

incident_description:
Since we have owned the stove/oven, which came with our new home in 2001, the hot surface light will stay lit for days, even when the stove has not been used at all.  We were not very concerned about that as we assumed that maybe there was just a short in the light itself because the stove surface did not feel hot when the light would stay on.  
About 3 years ago, the oven and stove stopped working and lost power all together and when my husband and father-in-law pulled the oven away from the wall to inspect it, they noticed that the electrical cord had melted.  We replaced the cord and the oven worked fine for a while, thought the hot surface light continued to stay lit often.  In the fall of 2010, I had preheated the oven for dinner and walked into the kitchen and noticed a smell like that of burned wiring and there was smoke in the kitchen, though I had put no food in the oven.  I pulled out the drawer at the bottom and could see that the cord had caught fire and there were flames shooting out of the outlet itself.  At that time, I flipped the main breaker to the house to stop the flames.  We then replaced the cord again and the outlet itself.  When I called Kenmore, they told me that I was the only one who had experienced such a problem and that it must be my wiring.  Two weeks ago, I turned the oven on LO BROIL and was prepping pork chops to put in.  When I opened the oven, a piece of the upper heating element was laying on the oven rack and the element at the top was on fire.  I immediately turned the oven off.  About 1 minute later, I heard a pop inside the oven and another piece had broken off and the flames were bigger.  Within about 5 minutes, about 5 more pieces had broken off of the element and the entire oven was engulfed in flames.  My husband came in from work and flipped the main breaker and we extinguished the fire.  We both sustained minor burns, but it could have been so much worse, I have taken showers or baths on occasion while dinner was cooking, what if I had not been right there when that oven went up in flames.  And why did the heating element not stop heating up after I turned the oven off?  Kenmore reps have told me that they can do nothing for us because my model number is not on their recall.  Yet I have found 9+ pages of complaints about the same exact incident on ComplaintsBoard.com as well as numerous complaints on this site.  They (Kenmore) offered to send someone to my house to inspect the oven at a charge of 167 dollars just to look at it.  How generous when they are lucky that my family did not burn up and die because of this oven.  I have always believed in Kenmore appliances and my house has nothing but Kenmore, but I have owned ovens my entire life and have NEVER had these types of problems with any other oven that I have ever owned.  By the way, the Kenmore vent hood microwave that is in my house was also recalled as a fire hazard and a rep came out years ago and put a recall kit in the microwave and it stopped working shortly after and has not worked in years.  What is Kenmore trying to do to people and what happened to the quality that their named used to stand for??
justification: The incident involved multiple instances of fire and minor burns, indicating injury (severity 3), and the recurring nature of the problem suggests a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Interior light on my refrigerator does not turn off. The heat from the light melted the plastic housing causing it to melt. Some parts were discolored from the heat. If this continued a while longer a fire was a definite possibilty. The bulbs were too hot to touch and all the food on the top shelf was hot. A milk container was even starting to melt.

Kenmore Elite Model # 795.77563600
S/N 612KR00174
justification: The incident involved property damage and a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Our Kennmore Elite dishwasher Model 66515972992 serial number FK0407749 began smoking. It smelled like an electrical issue. I was concerned it may catch on fire. After doing some research on the internet I have found that is a possibility. I have turned off the circuit breaker. It has also had some start up issues prior to the smoking.
justification: The dishwasher was smoking and had electrical issues, posing a fire risk, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We bought a Kenmore dishwasher made by Whirlpool in January of 2005.  There was a recall on  that model and similar ones but ours did not fit into the serial number list.  In January of 2011 the dishwasher caught fire while it was running.  Luckily my husband and I were home and in the kitchen when it happened.  There have been many times I would turn it on and go to bed.  Flames and smoke started comming out of the front panel.  We tried to shut it by opening the door but the water kept running and the dishwasher kept going.  We turned the water off and ran to turn off the fusebox.  We contacted Sears who has been trying to get a refund or something for the appliance but I am so upset and shocked that my family was in danger for so long and we did not know it.  I will always register an appliance now but the problem here is the unit had the problem but was not listed in the recall serial number list.  

Whirlpool decided that there was no property damage so they would do nothing but Sears is still going to try to get a partial refund.  It is the point of SAFETY that upsets me MORE than getting another dishwasher.  Truthfully I do better washing the dishes each night, but it would be nice to have a working one for large meals and such.
justification: The dishwasher caught fire, but no one was injured, so the severity level is 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 because fires are not very common but can happen.

incident_description: 3- 23-11. I have a GE dishwasher PDW9280N00SS. I have had it for about 4.5 years with no problems. Then Wednesday morning around 3:45 am I awoke to the smell of smoke. I ran thru the house to see where it was coming from and found the added heat light on the dishwasher. I opened the door and smoke rolled out and everything in it was melted. The counter top was really hot and the smell was awful. I turned the added heat button off but it continued to heat up. I switched it off at the cicuit box and then unhooked the dishwasher and took it to the garage and had to keep the house open two days to get the smell out. I contacted GE and they are sending a technician out to look at it and see if it can be repaired. I understand that they need to check but I don't think any repair will give me back my peace of mind. Also it seems to me that there would be a notice to all consumers that had GE dishwashers that this could happen. What if I had not been home? I hope this is handled in a professional manor and resolved to my satisfaction. The customer service rep, [REDACTED] was very friendly and helpful but informed me that my model was not in the recall, even though it is exactly the same thing that is happening in the other reports I have read about.
justification: The incident involved smoke and melting inside the dishwasher, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I was baking dinner in my Kenmore Electric Range Model #790.61752.  The broiler came on, on its own, and I could not get the oven to shut off by pressing the off button.  I had to turn it off at the breaker.  Had I not been monitoring the stove, this could have been a dangerous situation.

I believe that this has the potential for serious injury from any resulting fire.
justification: The incident involved the oven not turning off, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred.

incident_description: I use outlet timers to cycle the lights on terrariums for my reptiles.  I purchased a Utilitech TE06WHBL Digital 2-Outlet Timer, from Lowes, for this purpose.  It has a batttery backup in case of power outage or when it is unplugged to program, etc.  I programmed the timer and then plugged in two lights, one a 100 watt "Daylight" bulb and the other a Repti-Glo compact fluorescent.  A couple of days later I noticed the lights were still on when they were supposed to be off.  I went to unplug the timer to check the program and noticed the display was blank.  I also noted there was a rattle when I moved the timer.  At first I thought it was dropped or hit by mistake but it was set up behind a dresser and you could not reach it unless you moved the dresser.  I opened the timer to see what the rattle was and noticed two black discs about 1/4" in diameter, inside the case.  There was also the presence of a fine black powder towards the bottom of the timer.  When I took a closer look I noticed the tabs for the battery were splayed apart and realized what had happened, the battery had exploded.  The only other time I have seen something like this is when a battery was overheated due to improper soldering tehchniques or because it was installed incorrectly (polarity reversed).  I say no indication of any damaged outside of the case, everything was contained within the case.
justification: The battery explosion was contained within the timer case with no external damage or injury, indicating an incident without harm. Such occurrences are unlikely given proper usage and handling.

incident_description: In 2008, we purchased a Maytag Gas-Precision Touch Control 700 gas range Model#MGR5775QDB, Serial#29315825LY. On many occasions over the years, the gas has been turned on without anyone knowing it. The safety mechanism on the gas knobs that is supposed to prevent the knobs from being turned on accidentally does not work properly. Knobs can be turned on accidentally if someone brushes into one, such as when reaching over the stove top to remove an item from the cabinet above, or just reaching across to stir something at the back of the stove. Today I was in the living room and suddenly noticed a very bad smell. When I recognized the smell of gas, I quickly went into the kitchen and the room was filled with the odor of gas! My husband had accidentally brushed up against the stove, unknowingly turning the knob nearly halfway on, and then went into the basement where he never smelled the gas. I had to open the kitchen door and windows for several minutes to clear the air! If I had not been here, the outcome could have been catastrophic! I was wondering if anyone else had complained of this problem. I'm worried that the next time it happens, I won't be here to intervene. This is a very dangerous situation; we should have complained long ago.
justification: The incident describes a gas leak due to a faulty safety mechanism, which could lead to a catastrophic outcome if undetected, but no injury or death occurred this time.

incident_description:
I'm in the middle of making cupcakes to have for dessert and I decided to check the microwave timer (which I always use) to see how much time is left.  Well, the timer was blank.  I checked the oven and it was still on, so we didn't lose power.  Hmm, I push some buttons and nothing happens.  I pull open the door and stick my hand inside.  It's hotter than an oven inside.  I accidentally touched the glass turntable and burned my fingers.  Fortunately, the burns weren't bad.  It turns out the outside of the microwave (all that great plastic) is hot as well.   

Because our microwave doesn't plug in (it's wired in) we had to remove the microwave from the wall.  Even though the microwave appeared to have no power, it was raging hot.  We had to to kill the power with the circuit breaker and detach the wires from the wall.

It was very scary and if I didn't happen to be using the timer on the microwave and noticed how hot it was getting, I think it would have just continued to get hotter and hotter and eventually caught our kitchen on fire.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns, indicating an injury, and the potential for a kitchen fire suggests a high likelihood of recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description: I have a Samsung refrigerator, model #RS2630SH.  A few months ago, the refrigerator started making a noise intermittently.  Then the noise started lasting longer.  We then started having some problems with out ice maker, however; now the divider between the freezer & refrigerator is burning hot.  Also, the outside of the refrigerator, where the freezer is, is extremely hot to the touch.  I have almost burned myself getting things out of the refrigerator.  I have children also, and they have also almost been burned.  I am concerned that someone will burn themselves or that it may cause a fire.

incident_description: After using our range to cook one evening the burner was turned off.  After a few minutes of being off the burner was again red-hot.  The burner was turned on and off again via the dial and the burner on indicator light went off and the burner appeared to turn off.  After another minute or so the burner was again red-hot and the burner-on indicator light never came on.  After going through this cycle several times the only way to get the burner to stop heating up was to unplug the unit from the wall.
justification: The burner malfunction poses a fire hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I was using the MainStays Non-Stick 17" x 11" Cookie Sheet (UPC 072867250850). This item is dangerous! While using it to bake chicken in a 350 degree oven, I heard a "pop" sound. I soon found out that the pan had warped/bent while in the oven. When I went to remove the chicken from the oven, the pan "popped" back into original form right in my hand (with an oven mit on of course). It is a very good thing I was wearing long sleeves, because some of the chicken juices jumped from the pan as it "popped" and could have easily burned my arm (or even my face if the juices had jumped high enough). I "tested" the second exact same pan I had purchased, by putting it in the oven without any food items on it and the same thing happened.

incident_description: We have a Kenmore stove model 95802000, today the oven showed an error message and then the broiler came on and wouldn't turn off, getting hotter and hotter.  Note we didn't turn the broiler on, we turned the oven on to 350 and it burnt my food the oven got so hot.  Also the burner on the top of the stove was set on 5 but went extremely hot also. If this stove can come on by itself and possibly in the middle of the night it could burn my house down.  This is very much a fire hazard.

I turned off the oven and it didn't work so I tried to put it out with my electrical fire extinguisher and it didn't work.  While my family notified the FD, I pulled the stove away from the wall and unplugged it.  That worked...FD arrived, annotated what took place and documented model/ser # for this stove. I will document the fact that I have notified the U.S. CPSC about this incident and the fact that numerous other individuals have complained about similar incidents with their Kenmore ranges...different models, but the same problems...fire, couldn't turn off the oven, had to isolate the oven from it's power source (unplugged/breaker off).

incident_description: I was in the process of making Jello. I heated the 2 cups of water on the stove and poured the hot water into a PYREX casserole container (12" round) I started to mix the jello. incident_description: We have a Kenmore Elite Smoothtop Electric Range, model # 790.990102, serial # VF323304806 purchased 6/03.  In 6/09 we had an incident where the large burner would not turn off and we had to cut the power to the stove by using the circuit breaker.  On 7/01/09 a Sears service technician replaced the relay board at our expense which we thought had fixed the problem.  In 8/09 we received a recall notice from Sears about this issue and after great difficulty and much time on the phone were able to get Sears to re-imburse us for our expense replacing the relay board in July.  There were no further incidents until 3/11/11 when again the same burner would not turn off and we had to cut the power to it.  Obviously this is still a fire hazard.  I contacted Sears and spent over an hour on the phone trying to resolve this.  I was told that the warranty on the recall was 90 days and I would have to repair the stove at my expense.  At this point I do not trust another repair since the first one was defective and poses a serious fire hazard.

incident_description:
Made pizza for dinner in the oven, turned off oven controls and noted heating element still glowing red and oven temperature increasing.  I could feel the heat increasing on the outside of the oven after only a few minutes.  Tried to turn it back on and off in the hopes that it would reset, but this didn't work.  Oven was too hot to move so I turned off the power at the breaker and let unit cool.  Later I restored power and within minutes the oven was once again hot to the touch, disconnected power again and notified Sears.  

No doubt that if this was left unchecked that the oven would have been destroyed and possibly my house damaged or destroyed.  There is a recall for many models of Kenmore electric smoothtop ranges to correct this very issue, yet my oven which is experiencing the same issue and contains the same flawed control systems is not covered by this recall.  I find this outrageous.

incident_description:
After cleaning the oven the oven never turned off. It was hot 14 hours later. I had to use the circuit breaker to stop it from heating. (The controls were set properly and the circuit board indicated that the oven was off -- but it really was not.)
After cooking in the oven the oven remaines hot for many hours after pushing off on the control board and usually can  only be completely turned off by flipping the circuit breaker or by leaving the oven door open. (Not a very good thing to have to do with young children around.) 
Very occassionally the oven will stop heating in a reasonable amount of time after the oven has been turned off but since it happens so eratically the only way I can be sure it is off completely is by flipping the circuit breaker.
This same thing happened several years ago and the main circuit board was replaced. The same thing as before is happening again now.
I feel that this is a definite safety hazzard and possiby a fire hazzard
justification: The oven remains hot and fails to turn off properly, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: oven door does not close tight enough to keep the heat in and over heats the control knobs on the front of the stove, i am afraid to operate the self cleaning mode as i know hot hot that gets. i need ot prop the door closed when i use the oven or the heat escapes. bosch has not recogtnized this as a problem and i see it as a safety concern and a design flaw on a product that costs over $2000. several other complaints have been noted on blog and web sites so i know that i am not the only one that has this problem. seems others think it is a faulty hinge or a hinge that is not heavy duty enough.

incident_description:
GE Profile dishwasher PDW9280L purchased October 2005 for $850.00.
NOTE:  I am unsure if it is related, but there is a recall on PDW9280J.  I actually ordered this model and the L version was received. 
ÃÂHazard: Water condensation can drip onto the electronic control board, causing a short circuit and resulting in an overheated connector. This poses a fire hazard to consumers.
Incidents/Injuries: GE has received five reports of fires, four of which caused minor damage to the kitchen countertops where the dishwashers were installed and one caused minor damage to adjacent cabinets and smoke damage to the home. No injuries have been reported.ÃÂ

 Repaired twice in 2010.  (Pump stopped working and dishwasher not cleaning well.  Spent over $300 on 2 service calls.)  Earlier this month, March 2011, we went to bed.  The dishwasher was NOT on or running.  My 12 year old son was sleeping in the living room because he was sick.  At 2AM he woke up to a terrible smell and woke me.  I discovered the dishwasher was very hot, as was the surrounding counter.  I opened dishwasher.  Very strong smell of burnt plastic.  No water or moisture in dishwasher.  All plastic, including dishwasher parts such as cleaning are and racks had melted.  Tupperware, utensils, bacon cooker, painted glasses, were all melted and ruined. 
I am glad that my son woke us up, averting a fire.  There are several similar incidents on www.consumeraffairs.com.   4 of them involve the PDW9280 with a letter after the J recalled model number.  There are similar stories for several other GE dishwashers.    
Below is one of the postings:
ÃÂ Purchased a GE Profile dishwasher Model No.:PDW9900NWW; Serial No.:VL726731B in 12/2006 ($812.81). On Sunday 10/10/2010, I did a load of dishes and after the cycle ended I went to sleep. I woke up to an apt. filled with smoke. Called the Fire Dept. They pulled out the dishwasher and turned off the circuit breaker. It appeared that the heater from the dishwasher turned itself on and keep cooking all night long until every bit of plastic melted causing the fire. 
This included some platic utensils, containers and the racks in the diswasher itself to melt and burn. 
The super had to disconnect the unit as it was hard wired. The windows had to be kept open for a week from the smell. I contacted the GE Hotline at 800-626-2005 and spoke with ***, who connected me to Consumer Relations:800-386-1215 and ***. 
I filed a Claim No.:11323141. They sent out an inspector who called it "a runaway heater." They are replacing the diswasher with a comparable model, installing it and taking out the old unit.
*** of Howard Beach, NY Oct. 24, 2010ÃÂ

I reported the incident to GE.  I am very concerned about safety of the unit for other consumers.  GE sent a service technician who said the unit was not repairable.  He seemed concerned at what he saw.  I was surprised that GE did not seem to take a safety report.  ([REDACTED])  I noticed on consumeraffirs.com, if the fire department was called, GE picked up the defective unit, as well as replacing at no cost.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no injuries reported, but significant property damage and potential for harm.

incident_description: I was making soup (cooked vegtables in broth) in my Cuisinart "Original" model DLC-10C when the underside of the metal blade broke off. This machine has never been subjected to hard use.

incident_description: The blender was being used by my girlfriend on low power to make milkshakes. During use, the metal blade at the bottom detached, shredding the surrounding plastic into shards, and blending them into the milkshake. Some plastic was ingested before we realized what had happened.

incident_description: Sears Kenmore Elite gas stove model 790.36603604.  Since I used the self-clean feature for the first (and only time), the oven liner warped and now the racks fall down.  I can only use the top and bottom rack positions and the bottom rack can't be slid out or the rack will fall down.  Several times I have spilled hot liquids when the rack suddenly fell. The common opinion seems to be that they used steel that was too thin for the sides of the oven and they warp.  When the oven is heating up, it makes several loud banging sounds that sound just like the metal is warping and unwarping.

incident_description: We were using our Kenmore built in microwave (5yrs old)  yesterday afternoon when it started making a grinding noise. Within a few seconds it started smoking and caught fire inside the ventialtion system. We were able to pull the vent off and access the internal control panel. Luckily, we were able to extinguish the fire before it spread to our cabinetry.

incident_description: I have a Kenmore stove in one of my homes and the burner on the stove spontaniously turns on. The turn knob on the stove will not turn the stove off. This is a safety hazards as it could potentially start a fire or burn a small child who may place their hand on the stove.

justification: The oven overheated and emitted an odor but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Frigidair Smoothtop Electric Range Model FEF362MXESD, Serial VF71233051. 1) surface heating element turned on spontaneously without being switched on, 2)failed to turn off after being switched off.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning heating element, which poses a potential hazard but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I am currently experiencing the same problems on our diswasher that was under a recall by GE. The recall number was released on 10-26-10, #11-022.  Our problems were similiar in that the steam from the interior of the dishwasher caused the plastic covering the control panel housing to "blister" and crack and separate from the top of the inner door. She would like this investigate because she believes it to be a sever fire hazard as others are recealled with the same problem that have been recalled. Other models of the same brands have been recalled for the same problem.

incident_description: I was rinsing the glass lid of a cooking pot with lukewarm water after taking it off of the pot. The glass exploded in my hand and went flying onto the floor, the counter and in the sink. I luckily escaped with only a few scratches. It scared *** me.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (scratches) from the glass exploding, indicating a moderate severity level, and such occurrences are relatively uncommon.

incident_description:
I am writing to let you know of the following situation that happened to me on Saturday, March 19, 2011. At approximately 9:50am I turned my oven (Kenmore Range Model#665.92023101) on to preheat at 350 degrees. About 10 minutes later I put in a pan of spicy chicken dip that I had prepared to take to my daughter's college softball tailgate party. It was a triple recipe which usually takes at least 60 minutes to cook. At about 10:40am my step-daughter alerted me that the kitchen and living room where really getting filled with smoke. So when I went to the kitchen I could see smoke come from inside the oven, the bottom element was bright orange and the food smelled like it was burned. I took the chicken dip out of the oven to try and salvage it but the top layer was black and burned. I have cooked this many times in the past and have never had any problems so i wasn't sure what had happened. But, then I pushed the off button on the digital display to turn the oven off and noticed an error code but didn't pay attention to it while trying to turn it off. About 30 minutes later as we were about to leave we noticed smoke still coming from inside the oven, the element was still bright red and everyplace on the outside of the range was extremely hot to touch. The temperature was definetely way higher than 350 degrees. We thought that turning the oven off and waiting a minute or two and turning it back on and then off again would reset it, but that did not work. The oven would not go off and the entire range front of oven door, top control ppanel and sides were hot to the touch. We had to pull the oven out from the wall and unplug it to get it to turn off. I am just thankful that I didn't leave to go to the softball game right away and was still home to realize the oven did not turn off or I may not of had a house to come home to. 

 

I tried researching the problem online and see where some ranges have been recalled for this problem so i called the Sears recall line and was told that my model number was not recalled and would have to be repaired at my expense. I do not feel comfortable having this range repaired as i fear for the safety and well-being of my family.THIS KENMORE RANGE IS A SAFETY CONCERN AND A FIRE HAZZARD and I emailed them and requested a refund of the total purchase price I paid for this range plus reimbursement for ruined food and aggrevation. I will take a picture of the range so that you know I still have it before I purchase a new one as I will not subject my family to those circumstances of what might have happened. I believe I purchased this range in 2003.

 

Please call me with any questions at ***
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning oven causing smoke and burned food, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
Dear Sir,

In February 2010 I purchased a Viking VGSU1636BWH cooktop from Appliance Connection in Woodbridge Va.  After using the cooktop for approximately 6 months the corner of my corian countertop cracked and needed repair.  During the repair process, the workman observed that the counter cracked due to excessive heat from the cooktop.  The edge of the cooktop had scorched the counter in that particular location.  I also noticed that the porcelain top gets so hot over use that one cannot touch it without getting burned.  Both due to excessive heat.

The next incident occurred in Dec 2010 when I noticed that the back edge of the cooktop had sagged about 1/2 inch.  The back center was about 1/2 inched lower than the sides.  This particular unit has a rear downdraft (Viking VIPR161SS) so there is no counter support along the back edge of the cooktop. In addition the stainless steel vent filters on the downdraft also show scorch marks due to excessive heat.  Again due to excessive heat (my opinion)

I contacted Viking and reported these issues, and they claimed that none of this should be happening.  They are replacing the sagging porcelain top,  but claim that the filter scorch marks are from normal use.  They also said that the unit is rated to be used with a wooden counter top and do not believe that the unit caused the counter to crack.   I feel that root cause has not be determined for any of these issues. The new top will sag with use, the vent filters will continue to darken from the heat and the top will still keep getting excessively hot to the touch. 

In closing I believe that this is a heat related issue and something is wrong with this particular model or at least my particular unit.  I am worried that over time this may cause a serious incident.
justification: The incident describes property damage (cracked countertop, scorched filters) and potential for burns, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: On 2/22/11 at 6pm our refrigerator interior lights failed to turn off with the doors closed.  This melted the plastic around the light unit and scorched the light sockets.  The control unit fell due to the melting and was too hot to touch.  Food on the top shelf was very warm.  This problem (heating and melting) occurred between noon and 6 pm.  There was an odor of burnt plastic.  We unplugged the refrigerator and called a local repairman who said he knew of this problem with Sears Kenmore Refrigiratores (model 795.773004600).  He said that we would have to call Sears and have them fix the problem.  We called Sears.  They offered to come for a $75 service call and a one year service plan for $250, if we agreed to the plan BEFORE they came out.  They would not estimate the cost of the repair without coming out and the service plan was not an option once the service call had been made.  We requested to be put in touch with someone who dealt with recalls and complaints.  After a half hour run around only to return where I had started, we gave up.  We then went to the Consumers Affair web site and found a number of similar complaints from people with refrigerators the style and age (3 years) of ours.  We contacted Sears Live Chat on line to see if there had been a recall on this model.  We received no satisfaction, only a repeat of the service call information.  It is frightening to think of what could have happened had this occurred when we were asleep or out of town.  Because of our concern about the possibilty of a fire we chose not to fix our 3 year old Kenmore nad purchased a different brand from a different store.
justification: The incident involved significant damage to the refrigerator and potential fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Black & Decker Toast-R-Oven Model TRO490W

Was heating up some crackers in my toaster oven.  Set the timer to a very low setting (right at the indicator for the lowest toast setting), and wandered off to do something.  I heard the timer ticking.  After a brief while, I noted that the ticking stopped, but the bell didn't chime.  I guessed that I hadn't moved the dial far enough to arm the chime.  A minute later, I noticed smoke filling the kitchen, and ran to the toaster oven, which was still on, even though the dial was clearly in the off position.

I opened the door to see what was going on, and to try to get the contents to stop burning, and flames shot out.  I tried adjusting the dial to get the heating element to turn off, but since the toaster was already in the off position, nothing happened.  I eventually got it to turn off by moving the dial up to a higher toast setting than I originally used, and then moving it back down to the off position.  I left the oven door closed until the fire inside starved due to lack of oxygen.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On Sunday evening March 13, 2011, I returned to my home and I noticed a burning smell in my dining room and kitchen area.  I immediately thought of electrical fire somewhere, so I began searching for source of burn smell.  I didn't immediately identify source of smell, until I opened my Kenmore Coldspot Side-by-side refrigerator model# 106.54586400, Serial # SR1151713, manufactured March, 2004.  I saw the my frozen items were thawed and my ice chest was dripping water from melted ice.  The lights and the fan were operational on the refrigerator, but I noticed the burning smell even more, once I opened my freezer side of refrigerator.  I turned off the power to the refrigerator and pulled the fridge from the wall.  I opened the cardboard backing and checked the relay switch and condenser area to find a badly burned out relay switch, plugs and condenser.  The relay switch was badly burned.

I called Sears home service phone line and scheduled tech support.  The tech arrived at my home, opened the back area of refrigerator, saw the burned parts and told me that it was great that I noticed the issue and turned off the unit, or worse problems could have occurred....especially with a cardboard backing (fire-hazard).  The tech told me that the repair would cost around $700 to fix.  I held out for the service, because even if I get this repaired, this product is a major fire hazard and next time I may be out of time if this happens again, to find my condo burned down.

I have searched blogs regarding this issue and many consumers have this same issue with the Kenmore series of refrigerators starting with model# 106.########.
justification: The incident involved a burned-out relay switch posing a fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred. The issue is described as common among similar refrigerator models, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a teakettle.  I liked it because it had a whistling spout.  About 6 months ago, one of the screws from the lid came loose and fell into the kettle.  I discovered it because when I removed the lid, the lid came apart slightly on that side.  I retrieved the screw (thankfully, I hadn't poured it into a cup of tea) and screwed it back into the lid, thinking all the while that it was a stupid design for a lid, having a screw on the bottom!
Last week, I discovered the screw again had fallen out, but this time I couldn't put it back together because the 'bakelight' had cracked and a piece had either disintegrated or fallen into the kettle (I never found the piece[s]).  I filled the kettle anyway and heated water.  However, when I poured from the kettle, hot steam billowed up around the lid and my hand became quite hot.  Fortunately, I have a high tolerance for heat on my hands, so I merely placed my hand under some cool water after I had gotten it too hot from the steam.  I twisted the lid to keep the steam coming out the side of the hole, rather than up near the heel of my hand, but decided this was not satisfactory, since I could burn myself at any time with the steam, if I should forget that the lid had this problem, so I stopped using the kettle.
Another person could easily have dropped the kettle, spilling boiling water over themselves, or gotten quite badly burned on the hand and arm from the steam.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injury (hand becoming quite hot from steam) but no severe burns or further harm, and the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the design flaw.

The technician inspected the refrigerator and advised that the defroster motor dislodged from its clips and fell to the pan and burned the pan.  I am concerned about this product since it runs 24/7 and could possibly cause a fire in the kitchen and possibly burn the house.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burned pan but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for recurrence given the unit's continuous operation.
