incident_description:
I own a electric range. This range is used for normal preparation of meals in the home on most days for at least breakfast and dinner.  

I attempted to bake bisquits on a termerature of 500 F for nine minutes.  After five minutes, I noticed smoke coming from the oven and also noticed that the broiler (upper element) was the element doing the heating insted of the lower element.  I assumed I had incorrectly selected "broil" instead of "bake" and proceeded to prepare another batch of bisquits.  

I placed this new batch in the oven at the same settings of "bake", 500F and nine minutes.  Within five minutes smoke was again coming from the oven.  I turned the oven off and let it cool.  After letting the oven cool for 30 aapproximately one hour, I again started the oven on "bake" 500F.  The upper element or the "broiler" element again heated up.

It appears to me that if I had left my home to attend to other business there is a significant chance a house fire would have resulted.  I believe this is a defective product and am not willing to operate it in my home unless someone is there to monitor it, so I am not having it repaired and will purchase another brand this week at a significant increase over the cost of paying for repairs to this one.

incident_description: We purchased a Maytag (MORXEMMWW) refrigerator.  The store had the refrigerator delivered.  The delivery agent from the store reversed the hinges as agreed in the purchase.  The agent failed to put all the bolts in the center hinge.  The design of the center hinge has two open claw foot bolt holes on the left side and one solid bolt hole on the right.  The agent failed to put the right side bolt in the hinge.  Because of the design, without the bolt in the solid right side bolt hole, the weight of the doors eventually pulls the center hinge from under the open left side claw foot holes. incident_description:

Then I looked at the burner itself and it looked bad also. The clay?/ceramic? base that the element was supposed to be stuck in was cracked and briddle and the element was loose in places. The outside of the burner was also rusted. 
I thought the switch may have stuck on and caused the burner to overheat. But I could not account for the rust untill I was looking for parts online and came across the recall notice about the kenmore/ frigidair glass top ranges doing the same thing. The people that reported all said it was a front burner switch (which is different than the rear switch says sears) and some also mentioned moisture/rust problems.
I know this model is not included in the recall, but I hope you will check into it.
Thank you.

incident_description:
Danby propane refrigerator being used at a cabin.  Refrigerator was operational for approximately 2 years.  It began to emit carbon monoxide into the cabin killing my 10 year old son, and nearly killing my wife and 8 year old daughter.
The refrigerator uses propane as an energy source to operate the refrigeration cycle.  the burner uses a small flame a little bigger than a candle.  We had done light maintenance on the unit, but it seems that in the course of running out of propane a few times the burner started to create soot.  A piece of soot fell down onto the top of the burner, causing it to burn incorrectly and emit CO.  
The unit is certified to operate inside an occupied residence.  The design is such that it does not require flue gas venting to the exterior.  There are no safety devises to shut the unit down or alert the occupants if the flame begins to burn incorrectly, as in my case.
We have found that there have been 20 or more deaths linked to propane refrigerators in Canada, and that Canada requires the unit to come with a CO detector.  This is not a requirement in the united states.  
There is a state of [REDACTED] police report as well as media reports on the incident.
I did not have a CO detector installed in the cabin.  If I had one, it is very likely this incident would have been avoided.
justification: The incident resulted in a death and near-fatal injuries, indicating the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is high given the lack of safety devices and previous similar incidents.
